en:
Muhammad ibn Abu Bakr was a grandson of Ali ibn Haditha, of the Al Ali branch of the Al Fadl, the Bedouin house that held the office of amir al-ʿarab under the Mamluks. In 1279 Sultan Qalawun punished Isa ibn Muhanna for joining a revolt and named Muhammad in his place, though only nominal.

In 1293 al-Ashraf Khalil imprisoned Muhanna in Cairo, and Muhammad led the Bedouin until Muhanna was restored in 1295. He received the post again in 1320, when an-Nasir Muhammad banished Muhanna.

穆罕默德·本·阿布·伯克尔是阿里·伊本·哈迪塞之孙，出身法德勒部族的阿里支系；该部族在马穆鲁克治下世袭“阿拉伯人埃米尔”一职。1279年，嘉拉温苏丹惩罚参与叛乱的伊萨·本·穆汉纳，改任穆罕默德接替其职，但任命只是名义上的。

1293年，阿什拉夫·哈利勒将穆哈纳囚于开罗，穆罕默德统领贝都因诸部，直到1295年穆哈纳复职。1320年纳西尔·穆罕默德放逐穆哈纳，他再度获任此职。

en:
Abaqa Khan (1234–1282), second Ilkhan of Iran, succeeded his father Hulagu in 1265. He fixed the capital at Tabriz and married Maria Palaiologina, daughter of the Byzantine emperor Michael VIII.

His reign was spent warring with the Golden Horde and the Chagatai Khanate and raiding Syria, where the Mamluks defeated him at the Second Battle of Homs in 1281. He died at Hamadan in 1282 and was succeeded by his brother Tekuder; his own sons Arghun and Gaykhatu later ruled.

zh:
阿八哈（1234—1282）是伊儿汗国第二任伊儿汗，1265年继其父旭烈兀即位。他定都大不里士，并迎娶拜占庭皇帝米哈伊尔八世之女玛丽亚·巴列奥略。

他在位期间不断与金帐汗国、察合台汗国交战，并攻略叙利亚，1281年在第二次霍姆斯战役中被马穆鲁克击败。1282年他死于哈马丹，弟贴古迭儿继位；其子阿鲁浑、海合都后来也都成为伊儿汗。

en:
Abu Sa'id Bahadur Khan (1305–1335) was the ninth Ilkhan of Persia, succeeding his father Öljaitü in 1317 as a boy. The emir Chupan long ruled in his name; in 1319 they crushed a revolt and repelled Özbeg of the Golden Horde, earning him the title Bahadur.

In 1327 he overthrew Chupan, who was strangled at Herat, and married his daughter Baghdad Khatun. Marching against another Özbeg invasion, he died at Karabakh in December 1335 without an heir, and the Ilkhanate fell apart.

en:
Acciaiolo Acciaiuoli (died 1349) was a Florentine banker and politician of the Acciaiuoli family, the illegitimate son of Niccolò Acciaiuoli il Vecchio and father of Niccolò Acciaiuoli, the future grand seneschal of Naples. He took the family bank south, founding branches at Naples and in Greece, the Levant and Barbary; the Naples branch proved especially important to the family's fortune.

He lent large sums to King Robert of Naples, who named him chamberlain and counsellor in 1333, and from 1335 until his death he was the Angevin king's perpetual vicar at Prato.

In Florence he was twice prior of liberty, served among the war magistrates in 1336, and commanded the fortress of Pistoia in 1339. He died in Florence in 1349.

阿恰约洛·阿恰约利（？—1349）是佛罗伦萨阿恰约利家族的银行家、政治家，老尼科洛·阿恰约利的私生子，也是后来的那不勒斯大总管尼科洛·阿恰约利之父。他把家族银行的生意带向南方，在那不勒斯、希腊、黎凡特和柏柏尔开设分号，其中那不勒斯分号对家族的发迹尤为重要。

他向那不勒斯国王罗贝托贷出巨款，后者于1333年任命他为侍从长兼顾问；1335年至去世，他担任安茹国王驻普拉托的终身代理人。

在佛罗伦萨本城，他曾两度出任自由长官，1336年进入战争六署，1339年出任皮斯托亚堡垒长官。他于1349年在佛罗伦萨去世。

en:
Leone Acciaiuoli (c. 1220–1300), born at Ortona, was a knight and politician of the Florentine Acciaioli family. He sat in the magistracy of the Quattordici Buonomini in 1280 and served as capitano del popolo at Pistoia in 1296.

Abruzzese tradition remembers him as the sea captain who, sailing for King Manfred, on 6 September 1258 brought the relics of Saint Thomas back to Ortona Cathedral. He died in Florence in 1300.

en:
Anthony le Flamenc, a Frankish knight of Flemish descent, was lord of Karditsa in Boeotia in the Duchy of Athens. He is first mentioned in 1303, when Duke Guy II de la Roche named him deputy over Thessaly; Guy had taken its young ruler John II Doukas under his tutelage after the death of John's father.

In 1308 Venice accused him and others of plotting to seize its colony of Negroponte. He remained loyal to Matilda of Hainaut and attended her betrothal to Charles of Taranto at Thebes on 2 April 1309.

At Halmyros on 15 March 1311 he fought the Catalan Company and was among the few survivors, but was captured and held for ransom. After his return he built Saint George church at Karditsa, which bears a donor's inscription.

安托内·勒弗拉芒是一位有佛兰德血统的法兰克骑士，任雅典公国维奥蒂亚地区卡尔迪察的领主。1303年，雅典公爵居伊二世·德拉罗什任命他为色萨利的代理人，这是他首次见于史料；色萨利年幼的统治者约翰二世·杜卡斯在父亲去世后受居伊监护。

1308年，威尼斯指控安托内等人密谋夺取其殖民地内格罗蓬特。他忠于埃诺的玛蒂尔达，1309年4月2日在底比斯出席了她与塔兰托的查理的订婚。

1311年3月15日，他在哈尔米罗斯战役中迎战加泰罗尼亚公司，是为数不多的幸存者之一，但被俘并被扣押索取赎金。回国后，他在卡尔迪察建造圣乔治教堂，教堂留有捐建者的题铭。

en:
Catherine of Valois-Courtenay (c. 1303–1346) was a Latin empress without an empire. Eldest daughter of Charles of Valois and Catherine of Courtenay, she inherited her mother's claim to Constantinople in 1307, though the city had fallen to the Empire of Nicaea in 1261; in exile she held authority only over the Crusader states in Greece.

In 1313 she married Philip I of Taranto. After Philip's death in 1332, their son Robert received Achaea in 1333 from his uncle, and Catherine governed it for him until 1341.

In 1338 she went to Achaea, where she sheltered Nikephoros II Orsini of Epirus and backed his bid against the Byzantine emperor Andronikos III. In 1341 she became governor of Cephalonia and held it until her death at Naples in 1346.

瓦卢瓦-库尔特内的凯瑟琳（约1303—1346）是一位没有帝国的拉丁女皇。她是瓦卢瓦伯爵查理与库尔特内的凯瑟琳的长女，1307年继承母亲对君士坦丁堡的皇位主张，但该城1261年已落入尼西亚帝国之手；流亡中，她的权力只及于希腊的十字军国家。

1313年，她嫁给塔兰托亲王菲利波一世。1332年菲利波去世后，儿子罗伯特于1333年从叔父手中获得亚该亚，凯瑟琳代他治理至1341年。

1338年她前往亚该亚，在那里庇护伊庇鲁斯的尼基弗鲁斯二世·奥尔西尼，支持他对抗拜占庭皇帝安德罗尼卡三世。1341年她出任凯法洛尼亚总督，直至1346年在那不勒斯去世。

en:
Centurione I Zaccaria (1336–1382) was one of the most powerful barons of the Frankish Principality of Achaea, the eldest son of Martino Zaccaria and Jacqueline de la Roche. After his father's death in 1345 he held the Barony of Damala and half of Chalandritsa, acquiring the other half in 1359.

Around 1370 he became Grand Constable of Achaea and received the Barony of Estamira. He married Asenina, daughter of Andronikos Asen, in a Greek Orthodox ceremony, and their son Andronikos, named for his Greek grandfather, held Chalandritsa and Arcadia.

He served three times as bailli, or viceroy, for the Angevin overlords and died in 1382 during his third term. His daughter Maria was regent of Achaea in 1402–1404, and his grandson Centurione II ruled as prince from 1404 to 1432.

琴图廖内一世·扎卡里亚（1336—1382）是法兰克人的亚该亚亲王国最有权势的贵族之一，为马蒂诺·扎卡里亚与雅克丽娜·德拉罗什的长子。1345年父亲死后，他领有达马拉男爵领地和哈兰德里察的一半，1359年取得另一半。

约1370年，他成为亚该亚大统帅，受封埃斯塔米拉男爵领地。他按希腊正教仪式迎娶安德洛尼卡·阿森之女阿塞尼娜，儿子以希腊外祖父之名取名安德罗尼科斯，后来领有哈兰德里察和阿卡迪亚。

他三次担任安茹宗主的巴伊（副王），1382年在第三任内去世。女儿玛丽亚于1402—1404年摄政亚该亚，孙子琴图廖内二世于1404—1432年任亚该亚亲王。

en:
Florent of Hainaut (c. 1255–1297), son of Count John I of Hainaut and Adelaide of Holland, held the stadholdership of Zeeland before leaving the Low Countries to serve Charles II of Naples as constable.

In 1289 he married Isabella of Villehardouin, heiress of Achaea, and ruled the principality in her right, negotiating the Treaty of Glarentsa with Byzantium in 1290. When the Greeks retook Kalamata in 1293 he protested rather than reopen the war. He died in 1297 besieging Saint George castle in Arcadia, leaving his daughter Matilda as heir.

埃诺的弗洛朗（约1255—1297）是埃诺伯爵约翰一世与荷兰的阿德莱德之子。他从父亲手中获得泽兰省督之职，随后离开低地，效力于那不勒斯国王卡洛二世，担任大元帅。

1289年，他与亚该亚女继承人维拉杜安的伊莎贝拉结婚，以其丈夫身份统治亚该亚侯国，1290年与拜占庭签订格拉伦察条约。1293年希腊人夺回卡拉马塔后，他选择抗议而未重开战端。1297年，他在围攻阿卡狄亚的圣乔治城堡时去世，由女儿玛蒂尔达继承。

Giovanni Orsini (c. 1321–?), also called Tsafas, was the son of Guido Apostolico Orsini, count palatine of the Principality of Achaea, who died in 1336. He inherited the lordship of Leucadia, but later lost it and withdrew to the family fief at Nocera in the Kingdom of Naples.

In 1361 Simeon Palaiologos, self-styled emperor of the Greeks and Serbs, confirmed him as an imperial prince. He later married Beatrice Griffi and was buried in Naples.

乔瓦尼·奥尔西尼（约1321年生），又称查法斯，是亚该亚侯国帕拉丁伯爵圭多·奥尔西尼之子，父亲卒于1336年。他继承了莱夫卡达的领主之位，后来失去该地，退居那不勒斯王国诺切拉的家族封地。

1361年，自称希腊人与塞尔维亚人皇帝的西门·帕莱奥洛格确认他为帝国亲王。他后来娶比阿特丽丝·格里菲为妻，死后葬于那不勒斯。

en:
Guido Orsini, also called Guy, was the third son of John I Orsini, count palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos, and Maria Komnene Doukaina, daughter of the Despot of Epirus Nikephoros I. While his elder brothers Nicholas and John II made themselves despots of Epirus in 1318–1335, Guido was constable of the Principality of Achaea, to which his family's island county owed vassalage, and is attested in documents down to 1326.

His possible son John III, called Tsaphas, bore the title of count of Leucas and in 1361 served the Serbian ruler Simeon Uroš as megas konostaulos, or grand constable. Later family genealogies give Guido the Orsini estates in Italy and date his death to 1336.

圭多·奥尔西尼（一译居伊）是凯法洛尼亚与扎金索斯宫廷伯爵约翰一世·奥尔西尼与伊庇鲁斯专制君主尼基弗鲁斯一世之女玛丽亚·科穆宁·杜卡伊娜的第三子。两位兄长尼古拉与约翰二世在1318至1335年间先后成为伊庇鲁斯专制君主，圭多则在亚该亚侯国担任总管，奥尔西尼家族的岛屿伯国正是该侯国的附庸；1326年的文书中仍有他的记载。

他可能有一子约翰三世，绰号“察法斯”，自称莱夫卡斯伯爵，1361年出任塞尔维亚君主西美翁·乌罗什的“大总管”（梅加斯·科诺斯塔夫洛斯）。后世家谱称圭多分家时取得奥尔西尼家族在意大利的领地，卒于1336年。

William I of Champlitte (1160s–1209) was a French knight, the second son of Odo I, viscount of Dijon. He married Elisabeth of Mount-Saint-Jean, but they divorced in 1199.

He joined the Fourth Crusade, and in April 1203 he was among the leaders who signed a letter to Pope Innocent III after the capture of Zara. He became the first prince of Achaea in 1205 and held the title until his death in 1209.

en:
Louis of Burgundy (1297–1316) was a younger son of Duke Robert II of Burgundy and Agnes of France. In 1313 he married Matilda of Hainaut, heir to the Villehardouin claims on Achaea, and ruled the principality jointly with her. He gave up his claims to the family lands in Burgundy to his elder brother Hugh for the claim to the Kingdom of Thessalonica, then travelled to Greece by way of Venice seeking aid.

He defeated Ferdinand of Majorca at Manolada in July 1316 but died about four weeks later. Accounts of his death disagree: the Chronicle of the Morea blames a fever, while a Catalan source accuses John of Cephalonia of poisoning him.

路易·德勃艮第（1297—1316）是勃艮第公爵罗贝尔二世与法兰西的阿格妮丝的幼子之一。1313年，他与埃诺的玛蒂尔达结婚，与妻子共同统治亚该亚侯国。他把对勃艮第领地的权利让给兄长于格，换得塞萨洛尼卡王国的主张，随后经威尼斯前往希腊求援。

1316年7月，他在马诺拉达战役中击败马略卡的费尔南多，但约四周后便去世。关于死因记载不一：《莫雷亚编年史》称是热病，一份加泰罗尼亚文献则指控凯法洛尼亚的约翰下毒。

en:
Martino Zaccaria was the Genoese lord of Chios from 1314 to 1329 and a scourge of Turkish corsairs in the Aegean. In 1319 he brought seven ships to a Hospitaller fleet that crushed an Aydinid fleet, and Gregoras called him the terror of the Turks of Asia Minor.

The titular Latin emperor Philip II gave him the mostly symbolic title ‘King and Despot of Asia Minor’ in 1325, and he held Achaean baronies too. In 1329 Andronikos III attacked Chios with 105 ships; Martino held the citadel with 800 men until his brother yielded a fort, then remained prisoner in Constantinople until 1337.

He later became Genoese envoy to the Holy See and in 1343 commanded the papal galleys in the crusade that stormed Smyrna, where Turks killed him on 17 January 1345 during mass in the old cathedral.

马蒂诺·扎卡里亚是热那亚人，1314年至1329年任希俄斯领主，也是爱琴海上土耳其海盗的克星。1319年，他率七艘船加入医院骑士团舰队，大败艾登舰队，格里高拉斯称他是小亚细亚土耳其人的恐怖。

1325年，拉丁名义皇帝腓力二世授予他“亚细亚王与专制公”的头衔，多半只是象征；他还在亚该亚持有男爵领地。1329年，安德罗尼卡三世率105艘船进攻希俄斯；马蒂诺率800人固守城堡，直到兄弟交出要塞，此后被囚于君士坦丁堡，直至1337年。

后来他出任热那亚驻教廷使节，1343年指挥教皇桨帆船队，参与攻占士麦那的十字军。1345年1月17日，土耳其人在城内旧主教座堂的弥撒中袭击，他因此丧生。

en:
Matilda of Hainaut (1293–1331), only child of Florent of Hainaut and Isabella of Villehardouin, claimed Achaea in vain in 1307 after Charles II of Naples revoked her mother's rights. In 1313 she married Louis of Burgundy, with whom she received the principality.

They landed in Achaea in early 1316 and secured it after Ferdinand of Majorca fell at Manolada. After Louis died that year, Robert of Naples had her abducted to Naples in 1318 and forced a ceremony with his brother John of Gravina, which she refused to recognise.

In 1321 she refused the pope's order to marry John, admitting a secret marriage to the knight Hugh de la Palisse. Robert revoked her rights to Achaea and imprisoned her at Naples and then Aversa, where she died in 1331.

They landed in Achaea in early 1316 and secured it after #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('mll_ferdinand_mallorca').GetID],X #L Ferdinand of Majorca#!#! fell at Manolada. After Louis died that year, #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('nap_robert_i_anjou').GetID],X #L Robert of Naples#!#! had her abducted to Naples in 1318 and forced a ceremony with his brother John of Gravina, which she refused to recognise.

In 1321 she refused the pope's order to marry John, admitting a secret marriage to the knight Hugh de la Palisse. Robert revoked her rights to Achaea and imprisoned her at Naples and then Aversa, where she died in 1331.
zh:
埃诺的玛蒂尔达（1293—1331）是埃诺的弗洛朗与维拉杜安的伊莎贝拉的独生女。1307年，那不勒斯的卡洛二世剥夺她母亲对亚该亚的权利，她提出继承要求但未获接受；1313年她与路易·德勃艮第结婚，二人一同获封亚该亚侯国。

1316年初他们在亚该亚登陆，马略卡的费尔南多在马诺拉达战败身亡后，二人取得侯国控制权。路易于同年去世。1318年，国王罗贝托将她劫往那不勒斯，逼她与其弟格拉维纳的乔凡尼举行婚礼，她拒不承认。

1321年，她拒绝教皇要她嫁给乔凡尼的命令，并承认与骑士于格·德拉帕利斯秘密结婚。罗贝托剥夺她对亚该亚的权利并将她囚禁，先在那不勒斯，后转阿韦尔萨，她于1331年死于囚禁之中。

en:
Robert of Taranto (1319 or 1326–1364), of the Capetian House of Anjou, was the eldest surviving son of Philip I of Taranto and Catherine of Valois. In 1332 his uncle John of Durazzo arranged his acquisition of Achaea in exchange for his claims to Albania.

As he was still a boy, his mother governed Achaea until her death in 1346, when he inherited the Latin imperial title and was recognised as Emperor Robert II by the Latin states of Greece, though his real power rested on Achaea alone.

His 1347 marriage to Marie of Bourbon at Naples was childless. He died in Naples in September 1364, and though his widow tried to keep Achaea for herself and her son by an earlier marriage, his brother Philip II succeeded him.

zh:
塔兰托的罗伯特（1319或1326—1364）出身卡佩王朝的安茹家族，是塔兰托亲王菲利波一世与瓦卢瓦的凯瑟琳在世诸子中的长子。1332年，叔父杜拉佐的乔凡尼安排他接管亚该亚，条件是他放弃对阿尔巴尼亚的权利。

罗伯特当时年幼，亚该亚由母亲以他的名义主政，直至1346年凯瑟琳去世。同年他继承拉丁皇帝头衔，被希腊的拉丁各国承认为皇帝罗伯特二世，但实际权力仍只在亚该亚。

1347年，他在那不勒斯迎娶波旁的玛丽，二人无子；1364年9月他在那不勒斯去世。遗孀试图为自己和前夫之子保住亚该亚，但继位的是他的弟弟菲利波二世。

en:
Baramaraja, a mixed Mon–Chinese prince, was one of the princes produced by a marriage alliance between the Siamese dynasty of Ayodhya and the Mon house of Haripuñjaya at Chaliang. He was first a prince of Si Satchanalai before he took the throne of Ayodhya.

In 1344 his son Ramathibodi I succeeded him. In 1351 Ramathibodi founded Ayutthaya on an island in the Chao Phraya River.

en:
Phra Chao Luang won the throne of Ayodhya in the two-year war of succession after the childless King Narai died in 1087. He had no son and married his only daughter to Sai Nam Peung, a prince of Chaliang descent.

Through that marriage the line known as the Uthong dynasty came to hold Ayodhya, and its descendants ruled there until Ayutthaya was founded in 1351.

1087年无嗣的那莱国王去世后，阿逾陀爆发为期两年的王位之争，銮王在内战中获胜登位。他没有儿子，把独生女嫁给出身柴立王族的赛南蓬。

Narai was king of Lavo in the late 11th century. In the 1080s he moved the royal seat from Lavapura (Lopburi) to Ayodhya on the lower Chao Phraya, a move the chronicles credit to him.

In 1087 Pagan invaded Lavo but the dispute ended in negotiation; Narai died that year without an heir. The nobles of Ayodhya then fought a two-year civil war, won by Phra Chao Luang.

en:
Ramathibodi I (1314–1369), also known as Uthong, was the founder and first king of Ayutthaya, reigning from 1351 to 1369. He was the son of Baramaraja, a former prince of Si Satchanalai who became king of Ayodhya, and he succeeded his father in 1344.

In 1351 he founded Ayutthaya on an island in the Chao Phraya River, uniting Lopburi and Suphan Buri under one state. He also codified laws from Tai customs. After his death in 1369, the throne passed repeatedly between his son and his Suphannaphum brother-in-law.

en:
Sai Nam Peung was a 12th-century king of Ayodhya, the son of Kesariraja and son-in-law of Phra Chao Luang, whose only daughter he married. Before taking Ayodhya he ruled Si Satchanalai from 1106, and he is dated as king of Ayodhya from 1111 to 1165.

The Northern Chronicle makes him the hero of a famous tale: he took a Chinese princess, Soi Dok Mak, as his queen. His son Dhammikaraja founded Wat Dhammikaraja.

Agha Muhammad Khan Qajar (1742–1797) founded Iran's Qajar dynasty. Born to a Qajar tribal chieftain, he was captured and castrated by Adel Shah, then held hostage for sixteen years at Karim Khan's court before escaping in 1779.

He fought his brothers and rival Zand claimants to reunify Iran and made Tehran his capital in 1786. In 1794 he defeated Lotf Ali Khan and devastated Kerman; after sacking Tbilisi in 1795 he was crowned shahanshah in 1796, and in 1797 he was assassinated and succeeded by his nephew Fath-Ali Shah.

阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔（1742—1797）是伊朗卡扎尔王朝的开国之君。他出身卡扎尔部首领家族，被阿德尔沙俘获并阉割，随后在卡里姆汗宫廷中当了十六年人质，1779年逃脱。

他与兄弟和赞德王位争夺者交战以重新统一伊朗，1786年定德黑兰为都。1794年击败卢特夫·阿里汗并摧毁克尔曼，1795年洗劫第比利斯后于1796年加冕为沙汗沙，1797年遇刺身亡，由侄子法塔赫·阿里沙继位。

en:
Agostino Barelli (1627–c. 1697) was an Italian High Baroque architect, born in Bologna, who helped introduce Italian Baroque architecture to Bavaria. In 1662 Electress Henriette Adelaide of Savoy summoned him to Munich to design the Theatinerkirche, one of the first High Baroque churches north of the Alps.

In 1664 he also drafted the plans for Nymphenburg Palace. After clashing with the Theatine supervisor, he was replaced in 1674 by Enrico Zuccalli and returned to Bologna, serving as city architect from 1676.

阿戈斯蒂诺·巴雷利（1627—约1697）是意大利鼎盛巴洛克风格建筑师，生于博洛尼亚，曾协助将意大利巴洛克建筑引入巴伐利亚。1662年，选帝侯夫人萨伏依的亨丽埃特·阿德莱德召他前往慕尼黑设计剧院教堂，该堂是阿尔卑斯山以北最早的鼎盛巴洛克教堂之一。

1664年他还绘制了宁芬堡宫的设计图。施工期间他与工程监督发生冲突，1674年被恩里科·祖卡利取代，随后返回博洛尼亚，1676年出任该市官方建筑师。

Aqruqchi (died soon after 1306), a son of Kublai Khan, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping in 1269. In 1272 he led Mongol princes and Tibetan tribal troops against the Jiandu tribes on the Tibetan border, capturing their chiefs and taking their surrender in 1273.

In 1275 he campaigned into Tibet, and in 1285 he fought the rebel Chagatai khan Duwa without success, marching against him again in 1293. He died shortly after 1306, leaving a son, Temür Buqa.

en:
Ahmed Tekuder (c. 1246–1284), son of Hulagu and brother of Abaqa, was Ilkhan of Iran from 1282 to 1284. Baptized a Nestorian as Nicholas in childhood, he had converted to Islam by his accession and ruled as Sultan Ahmad. He reversed Abaqa's pro-Christian policies and sought an alliance with the Mamluk sultan.

His purges drove his nephew Arghun into revolt. Arghun surrendered in 1284 but was freed; Tekuder was captured and executed on 10 August, and Arghun took the throne.

艾哈迈德·贴古迭儿（约1246—1284）是旭烈兀之子、阿八哈之弟，1282至1284年任伊儿汗。他幼年受景教洗礼、教名尼古拉，即位前已改宗伊斯兰教，以“算端艾哈迈德”之名统治，一改阿八哈亲基督教的政策，谋求与马穆鲁克结盟。

他的整肃迫使侄子阿鲁浑起兵。1284年阿鲁浑投降后获释，贴古迭儿被捕，于8月10日被处死，阿鲁浑随即继承伊儿汗位。

Sukhaangphaa was the fourth swargadeo, or king, of the Ahom kingdom, eldest son of King Subinphaa. He came to the throne in 1293, and around 1324 began his realm's first major war, invading the Kamata kingdom of King Durlabh Narayan.

The long struggle had no clear winner: Durlabh Narayan sued for peace and gave his daughter Rajani in marriage to seal a truce. After a thirty-nine-year reign, Sukhaangphaa died in 1332.

苏汉法是阿豪姆王国第四任国王（斯瓦尔加德奥），老国王苏宾法的长子，1293年即位。约1324年，他发动阿豪姆人对邻邦的第一场大战，入侵卡马塔国王杜尔拉布·纳拉扬的国土。

这场持久战未分胜负：杜尔拉布·纳拉扬求和，把女儿拉贾尼嫁给苏汉法，双方缔结盟约。苏汉法在位39年，于1332年去世。

en:
Sukhrangpha, also called Tao Shukhampha, was king of the Ahom kingdom from 1332 to 1364. Early in his reign his youngest brother Chao Pulai plotted against him and fled to Kamata, whose king, their uncle, sent troops to back him. Sukhrangpha avoided battle and reconciled with his brother by naming him Charing Raja, the heir apparent's post.

The rest of his reign was peaceful. He died in 1364, and some historians hold that the throne then stood vacant until 1369.

Sutuphaa, a younger brother of Sukhrangpha, was king of the Ahom kingdom from 1369 to 1376 after an interregnum. He wanted to expand his kingdom, and his reign was marked by frequent conflict with the neighbouring Sutiya kingdom.

In 1376 the Sutiya king invited him to a regatta on the Safrai river, lured him onto his own barge without attendants, and had him murdered there. The Ahom escort returned with the news.

He was dominated by his elder queen, who had his favourite younger queen falsely accused and condemned; ministers set the younger woman adrift on the Brahmaputra instead. The nobles later had him assassinated, and the elder queen was put to death as well.

en:
Kamal al-Din al-Damiri (1341–1405) was a Shafi'i Sunni scholar of Cairo, trained in jurisprudence, hadith and theology at al-Azhar. After working in his father's sewing shop in his youth, he taught at al-Azhar and other Cairo schools.

Known as an ascetic Sufi, he made the pilgrimage to Mecca more than six times. Around 1371 he completed the Ḥayāt al-ḥayawān al-kubrā, the first systematic Arabic work on zoology, combining animal lore with law, proverbs and medicine.

en:
Taqi al-Din al-Maqrizi (1364–1442) was the leading Egyptian historian of the Mamluk age, born in Cairo of Damascene origin and a direct student of Ibn Khaldun. After serving as a secretary, he became inspector of markets for Cairo and northern Egypt in 1399 and took a lectureship in Damascus in 1408.

In 1430 he went on pilgrimage with his family and travelled for some five years, afterwards devoting himself to historical and biographical works, particularly on the Fatimid era and earlier Egyptian history.

en:
Agnes of Périgord (died 1345) married John of Gravina, Duke of Durazzo and brother of King Robert of Naples, who arranged the 1321 match to win papal and French support for his designs in northern Italy. Her brother Hélie de Talleyrand-Périgord became a cardinal and a major figure of the Avignon papacy, and she bore three sons, Charles, Louis and Robert.

Widowed in 1335, she became a court political force, and after Robert's death in 1343 married her eldest son Charles to his granddaughter Maria of Calabria, to draw the Durazzo line nearer the throne.

Her meddling in papal diplomacy in 1345 turned Queen Joanna against her, and she died that May, reportedly poisoned by Joanna's ladies, though the tale may be fiction. Charles was executed in 1348, but her grandson Charles of Durazzo seized the crown in 1382.

佩里戈尔的阿格妮丝（?—1345）是杜拉佐公爵、格拉维纳的乔凡尼之妻，乔凡尼为那不勒斯国王罗贝托之弟。1321年罗贝托撮合这门亲事，想借此争取教廷与法国支持其意大利经营。她的兄弟埃利·德·塔列朗-佩里戈尔后来升任枢机，为阿维尼翁教廷头面人物；她生下查理、路易吉、罗贝托三个儿子。

1335年守寡后，她成为宫廷政治力量；1343年国王罗贝托驾崩，她安排长子查理迎娶老王的孙女卡拉布里亚的玛丽亚，让杜拉佐一系更接近王位。

1345年她插手教廷外交，使乔万娜女王对她更为不满；同年5月她去世，传为乔万娜身边女眷毒杀，惟此说可能出于虚构。查理于1348年被处死，但她的孙子杜拉佐的查理在1382年夺取了王位。

en:
Charles of Durazzo (1323–1348), eldest son of John, Duke of Durazzo, and Agnes of Périgord, led the Anjou-Durazzo faction against his cousin Queen Joanna I of Naples, and succeeded his father as Duke of Durazzo and Count of Gravina in 1336.

In April 1343 he and his mother abducted Maria of Calabria, Joanna's sister, once meant for Louis I of Hungary or John of France, and married her at Naples to move closer to the throne.

He kept aloof from the plot that killed Joanna's husband Andrew, but opposed the queen and Louis of Taranto and sought Hungarian support. When Louis of Hungary invaded in 1348 and Joanna fled, the Hungarians seized and beheaded him at Aversa. His daughter Margaret later married Charles III of Naples.

杜拉佐公爵卡洛（1323—1348）是杜拉佐公爵乔凡尼与佩里戈尔的阿格妮丝的长子，领导安茹—杜拉佐一系对抗堂亲、那不勒斯女王乔万娜一世。1336年父亲死后，他继任杜拉佐公爵和格拉维纳伯爵。

1343年4月，他与母亲劫持乔万娜的妹妹、卡拉布里亚的玛丽亚——她原本被许配给匈牙利的拉约什一世或法国的让——并在那不勒斯娶她为妻，借此更接近王位。

乔万娜之夫安德拉什遇害的阴谋，他小心置身事外，却反对女王与塔兰托的路易吉，并向匈牙利宫廷寻求支持。1348年匈牙利国王拉约什一世入侵、乔万娜出逃时，他被匈牙利人抓住，在阿韦尔萨斩首。女儿玛格丽塔后来嫁给了那不勒斯国王卡洛三世。

en:
Philip I of Taranto (1278–1331), younger son of Charles II of Naples, became Prince of Taranto in 1294. He married Thamar, daughter of Nikephoros, Despot of Epirus, receiving Achaea and Albania, and around 1297 claimed Epirus. The Aragonese captured him at La Falconara in 1299 but later freed him.

After divorcing Thamar in 1309, he married the titular Latin empress Catherine of Valois in 1313 and claimed Constantinople through her. He granted Achaea first to Matilda of Hainaut and in 1318 to his brother John of Gravina, dying in 1331.

en:
John of Gravina (1294–1336), youngest son of Charles II of Naples, was a prince of the Capetian House of Anjou. In 1315 he succeeded his brother Peter, killed at Montecatini, as Count of Gravina. In 1318 his brother Philip I of Taranto forced Matilda of Hainaut to marry him; when she refused to surrender her rights and secretly married Hugh de La Palice, Philip stripped her of Achaea, gave it to John, and annulled the marriage.

His 1325 Morea expedition failed to retake Skorta from Byzantium, and in 1332, unwilling to swear fealty to his nephew Robert of Taranto, he exchanged Achaea for claims to Albania and ruled as Duke of Durazzo until his death in April 1336.

杜拉佐的乔凡尼（1294—1336）是那不勒斯国王卡洛二世的幼子，出身卡佩安茹家族。1315年，其兄皮耶特罗在蒙特卡蒂尼被杀，他继任格拉维纳伯爵。1318年，其兄塔兰托的菲利波一世强迫埃诺的玛蒂尔达嫁给他。玛蒂尔达拒绝交出权利并秘密嫁给于格·德·拉帕利斯，菲利波便剥夺她的亚该亚领地转赐乔凡尼，两人的婚姻也被废除。

1325年他远征摩里亚，未能从拜占庭手中夺回斯科塔。1332年，他不愿向侄子塔兰托的罗伯特宣誓效忠，以亚该亚换取对阿尔巴尼亚的权利，此后以杜拉佐公爵身份统治，直至1336年4月去世。

Thamar Angelina Komnene (died c. 1311), daughter of Nikephoros I Komnenos Doukas, Despot of Epirus, married Philip I of Taranto, son of Charles II of Naples, in August 1294, bringing four Epirote castles as her dowry. When the Aragonese captured Philip in 1299, she pawned her coronet to raise his ransom.

Despite the terms she was forced to convert to Catholicism. In 1309 Philip accused her of adultery and divorced her; she died around 1311, either as a nun or in prison.

en:
Aldus Manutius (c. 1449–1515) was an Italian humanist and printer, born near Rome. After studying in Rome and Ferrara, he settled in Venice in 1490 and founded the Aldine Press, devoting it to editions of Greek and Latin classics.

Greek texts had rarely been printed, but his editions appeared in the original language. He commissioned the first italic typeface, helped standardize the comma and semicolon, and issued cheap pocket-sized octavos under his dolphin-and-anchor mark, pioneering the portable book.

en:
Amaury III de Craon (c. 1280–1333), lord of Craon, Créon, Mareuil and Sablé, served the English crown as Seneschal of Gascony in 1313–1316 and again in 1320–1322, and in 1315 obtained leave from Edward II to found the bastide of Créon.

He held the hereditary seneschalties of Anjou, Maine and Touraine, which the French crown bought back in 1323 and 1331. By Isabelle de Sainte-Maure he had a son, Maurice VII, and by his second wife Béatrice de Roucy more children, among them Jean III, Archbishop of Reims. Amaury died in 1333 and was buried at the Cordeliers convent in Angers.

Amaury IV de Craon (1326–1373) was a powerful baron of Anjou, son of Maurice VII de Craon and Marguerite de Mello. In 1345 he married Péronnelle, viscountess of Thouars. Captured at the Battle of Poitiers in 1356, he became one of Charles V's leading captains.

As vicomte consort of Thouars he later defected to the English, leading the Anglo-Poitevin coalition against Bertrand du Guesclin. Besieged at Thouars in 1372, he surrendered and swore fealty to Charles V. He died in 1373 and was buried at Angers.

en:
Charles II, called the Magnanimous (1297–1346), Count of Alençon and Perche, was the second son of Charles of Valois and younger brother of Philip VI, who took the French throne in 1328. He first fought in Guyenne under his father, inheriting Alençon on his death in December 1325.

He fought at Cassel in 1328, and when Edward III challenged Philip's crown and refused homage, the king made him lieutenant general of the kingdom and sent him against an English-stirred revolt at Saintes, where he retook several strongholds.

In the Breton succession war Philip gave him L'Aigle, confiscated from Jean de Montfort. At Crécy on 26 August 1346 he commanded the vanguard and was killed; his eldest son Charles III succeeded him in Alençon.

查理二世绰号“宽宏者”（1297—1346），是阿朗松伯爵兼佩尔什伯爵，瓦卢瓦的查理的次子，也是1328年登上法国王位的腓力六世之弟。他早年随父亲在吉耶讷作战；1325年12月父亲去世，他继承阿朗松等领地。

1328年他参加卡塞尔战役。英王爱德华三世挑战腓力的王位并拒绝行臣服礼，国王便任命查理为王国中将，派他镇压英国人煽动的桑特叛乱，他夺回数处要塞。

布列塔尼继承战争爆发后，腓力把从让·德·蒙福尔手中没收的莱格勒交给他。1346年8月26日，他在克雷西战役中率领前锋战死，长子查理三世继承阿朗松。

en:
Charles III of Alençon (1337–1375) inherited Alençon and Perche as a boy after his father Charles II fell at Crécy in 1346. In 1361 he renounced his titles, entered the Dominican convent in Paris, and with John II's approval left Alençon to his brother Peter and Perche to Robert. At the insistence of his kinsman King Charles V, he became archbishop of Lyon on 13 July 1365; the cathedral chapter, defending its right to elect independently, accepted him only after three rounds of voting.

As primate he fiercely defended the see's rights; when a royal official tried to seize his temporal power in 1372, he imposed an interdict that lasted until his death on 5 July 1375.

en:
Guillaume I de Craon, called the Great (c. 1318–1388), second son of Amaury III de Craon by Béatrice de Roucy, founded the Châteaudun branch of his house. Around 1337 he traded his one-sixth share of Château-du-Loir to his cousin Pierre de Dreux for Domart-en-Ponthieu and Bernaville.

On 4 May 1341 he married Marguerite of Flanders-Termonde, Viscountess of Châteaudun, holding the viscounty through her. In 1345 he inherited La Ferté-Bernard from his brother-in-law Ingelger of Amboise, and served as a royal chamberlain.

In early 1361 he rode with Bertrand du Guesclin against Hugh Calveley at Juigné-sur-Sarthe, but midway through the battle he and eighty men-at-arms fled, leaving Du Guesclin to be captured. Of his eight children, sons Guillaume II, Pierre and Jean I continued the Châteaudun line.

纪尧姆一世·德·克朗，号称“伟大者”（约1318—1388），是阿马尔里克三世·德·克朗与贝阿特丽丝·德·鲁西的次子，沙托丹支系的始祖。约1337年，他以继承的沙托迪卢瓦六分之一份额，与表亲皮埃尔·德·德勒交换多马尔昂蓬蒂约和贝尔纳维尔。

1341年5月4日，他娶沙托丹女子爵玛格丽特·德·佛兰德-泰尔蒙德为妻，凭妻权领有沙托丹子国。1345年他从姻兄昂布瓦斯的英热尔热继承拉费泰贝尔纳，曾任王室侍从。

1361年初，他与贝特朗·杜·盖克兰在于尼耶苏尔萨尔特迎战休·卡尔弗利，战斗正酣时他带着八十名重装骑兵临阵逃走，丢下杜·盖克兰被俘。八个子女中，儿子纪尧姆二世、皮埃尔和让一世延续了沙托丹支系。

en:
Isabeau de Craon (c. 1330–1394), daughter of Maurice VII de Craon and Marguerite de Mello, was the sister and sole heiress of Amaury IV de Craon, inheriting the barony of Craon in 1373. Betrothed as a child to Guy XI de Laval in 1339, she received dower lands at Acquigny after his death in 1348, although it is uncertain whether the marriage ever took place.

She then married Louis de Sully, an English partisan, and in 1376 sought the protection of Louis I, Duke of Anjou, against him. Her daughter Marie de Sully inherited Craon. Isabeau died in February 1394 and was buried at Angers.

Jean III de Craon (1329–26 March 1373) was a French prelate, the son of Amaury III de Craon. He became Bishop of Le Mans in 1350 and in 1355 was promoted Archbishop of Reims, the see whose archbishops crowned the kings of France.

With his brother Pierre I de Craon and Boucicaut he negotiated the Treaty of Guérande, ending the Breton Succession War in favour of the House of Montfort.

Jeanne de Craon, also called Aliénor (c. 1330–c. 1385), was the younger daughter of Maurice VII de Craon. Her father died before his own father in 1330, and she married Renaud de Montbazon, lord of Montbazon.

Her daughter Jeanne de Montbazon married her cousin Guillaume II de Craon in 1372; her brother Amaury IV and sister Isabeau ceded the couple Jarnac and other family lands, reuniting much of the Craon inheritance.

In 1341 she married Guillaume I de Craon, known as Guillaume le Grand, carrying the viscounty of Châteaudun into the Craon family. They had eight children, among them Guillaume II de Craon and Pierre de Craon, called le Grand.

María de la Cerda y de Lara (1319–1375) was a Castilian noblewoman, the youngest daughter of Fernando de la Cerda and Juana Núñez de Lara. In 1335 she married Charles d'Évreux; he died in 1336, leaving her with twin sons.

Three months later she married Charles II, Count of Alençon. Her second husband was killed at the Battle of Crécy in 1346. She died in Paris in 1375 and was buried in the Couvent des Jacobins.

Maurice VII de Craon (c. 1304–8 August 1330) was the only son of Amaury III de Craon and his first wife Isabelle de Sainte-Maure.

His mother's death in December 1310 made him lord of Sainte-Maure and Marcillac, and through his marriage to Marguerite de Mello in 1323 he also held her other fiefs. Maurice predeceased his father, dying on 8 August 1330, so he never ruled Craon itself; his son Amaury IV succeeded Amaury III as lord in 1333. He was buried in the family chapel at Angers.

Peter I of Alençon (1251–1283) was a son of Louis IX of France and Margaret of Provence, born at Château Pèlerin during the Seventh Crusade. In 1268 his father gave him Alençon and Perche, and in 1270 he joined the Eighth Crusade to Tunis.

His marriage to Joan of Châtillon in 1272 brought him Blois, Chartres and Guise. After the Sicilian Vespers he aided his uncle Charles I of Anjou, and died at Salerno in 1283 without surviving sons, so Alençon reverted to the crown.

en:
Pierre I de Craon (c. 1315–1376) was the elder son of Amaury III de Craon by Béatrice de Roucy. He fought for Charles de Blois in the Breton Succession War.

At the siege of La Roche-Derrien in 1350, his men lacking ardour, he hung his purse from a pole, promising it to the first soldier into the town, which fell. In 1356 he held Romorantin with Boucicaut against the Black Prince; the town held out until English engineers set up cannon, the first use of artillery in a French siege, and Craon surrendered.

Taken at Poitiers that year, he was among the hostages Edward III demanded for King John II's ransom. With his brother, Archbishop Jean III, and Boucicaut he later negotiated the Treaty of Guérande, which recognised Montfort as Duke of Brittany.

皮埃尔一世·德·克朗（约1315—1376）是阿马尔里克三世·德·克朗与贝阿特丽丝·德·鲁西的长子，在布列塔尼继承战争中为夏尔·德·布卢瓦效力。

1350年围攻拉罗什德里安时，士兵士气低落，他把钱袋挂在杆子上，许诺赏给第一个入城的人，城随即被攻下。1356年，他与布锡考特在罗莫朗坦抵挡黑太子；守军一直坚持到英军工兵架起火炮——这是火炮首次用于法兰西的围城战——才投降。

同年他在普瓦捷战役中被俘，成为爱德华三世为抵偿约翰二世赎金而要求交出的人质之一。后来他与兄弟、兰斯大主教让三世和布锡考特一同谈判达成《盖朗德条约》，承认蒙福尔为布列塔尼公爵。

Ahmad ibn Abi Dabbus was an Almohad prince descended from Abu Dabbus Idris II, the last Almohad caliph, killed at Marrakesh in 1269. After his family's failed bid for the Hafsid throne brought exile in Egypt in 1344, he returned to Ifriqiya and settled in Tozeur as a tailor.

In 1348, as Arab rebels defeated the Marinid sultan, the Ku'ub found the tailor and proclaimed him sultan. With Ibn Tafragin he besieged Tunis, but his allies deserted him; he was handed to the Marinid sultan and later went to Spain.

en:
Berthold von Buchegg, who ruled as Berthold II, came from the comital family of Buchegg near Solothurn, the son of Count Heinrich. A Teutonic Order commander and opponent of Louis the Bavarian, he became Pope John XXII's candidate when the see of Speyer fell vacant on Emich of Leiningen's death in April 1328.

The canons ignored a papal warning and elected Walram von Veldenz, a supporter of the Wittelsbachs; Berthold failed to prevail even by force and soon yielded the see. A papal bid to make him archbishop of Mainz after his brother Matthias died that September also failed.

Berthold was then installed at Strasbourg, where he was bishop from 1328 until his death. In 1329 he took the chronicler Matthias von Neuenburg into his service. He died at Molsheim on 25 November 1353.

贝特霍尔德·冯·布赫格（教名贝特霍尔德二世）出身于索洛图恩附近的布赫格伯爵家族，是伯爵海因里希之子。他曾任条顿骑士团指挥官，反对巴伐利亚的路德维希；1328年4月莱宁根的埃米希去世、施派尔主教之位出缺时，他成了教皇约翰二十二世属意的人选。

参事会无视教皇的警告，选出维特尔斯巴赫家族的支持者瓦尔拉姆·冯·韦尔登茨；贝特霍尔德诉诸武力仍未能取胜，不久便让出主教领地。同年9月其兄弟马蒂亚斯去世后，教皇让他继任美因茨大主教的尝试同样失败。

en:
Lamprecht von Brunn, in French Lambert de Buren, was born around 1320–1330 into a lower noble family of northern Alsace and owed his career to his own ability rather than his family's standing. From 1354 he was abbot of Gengenbach, then bishop in turn of Brixen, Speyer and Strasbourg.

In 1374 he moved to Bamberg as prince-bishop, became a close adviser of Emperor Charles IV and later chancellor of King Wenceslaus. He founded Nuremberg's Carthusian monastery in 1381, and in 1390 ended the Giechburg inheritance dispute, the last major enlargement of the Bamberg bishopric.

His beer tax, the Bierpfennig, was known as the Lambertiner for centuries. In 1395 he founded a hospital at Scheßlitz and gave it his library. He resigned in January 1399 and died at Forchheim on 17 July.

兰普雷希特·冯·布龙（法语称朗贝尔·德·比伦）约于1320至1330年间生于阿尔萨斯北部的下层贵族家庭，仕途靠个人能力而非家族声望。他自1354年起任根根巴赫修道院院长，此后先后担任布里克森、施派尔和斯特拉斯堡主教。

1374年他调任班贝格采邑主教，成为皇帝查理四世的亲信顾问，后任国王文策尔的掌玺大臣。他于1381年在纽伦堡建立加尔都西会修道院，1390年了结吉希堡继承纠纷，这是班贝格主教区最后一次明显扩张。

他开征的啤酒税“啤酒芬尼”此后数百年一直被称为“兰贝蒂纳”。1395年，他在舍斯利茨创办医院并捐出藏书。1399年1月辞职，同年7月17日卒于福希海姆。

en:
Ala al-Din bin Yusuf was the second bey of the Alaiye beylik, succeeding his father Yusuf, its founder, around the 1350s. His reign was dominated by the coastal campaigns of Peter I of Cyprus, who seized Korikos in 1360 and Antalya in 1361.

Ala al-Din joined the Teke bey Mehmet and other rulers against the Cypriots, at one point acknowledging Peter's overlordship. He died in 1364 and was entombed in Alanya's Gülevşen Mosque; his son Mahmud succeeded him.

en:
Hüsameddin Mahmud bin Ala al-Din ruled the Alaiye beylik from 1364 until at least 1374, succeeding his father. His reign was spent fighting Peter I of Cyprus: in 1364 Cypriot forces raided Alanya and stormed its harbor, whereupon Mahmud retaliated by landing on Cyprus and carrying off many captives.

In 1366 Peter attacked Alanya with twenty-two ships but was repulsed by Turkmen archers. After the reconquest of Antalya in 1373, Mahmud built Alanya's Gülevşen Mosque in 1374 to mark it.

en:
Yusuf Bey was the founder of the Turkmen beylik of Alaiye, at modern Alanya on the southern Anatolian coast, and a prince of Karamanid descent. Alanya had been conquered from the Franks in 1293 by Bedreddin Mahmud Bey, under whom Yusuf governed the city.

When Ibn Battuta visited him, he ruled as an independent bey, his reign dated 1330–1337. He was the father of Alâeddin bin Yusuf, who held Alaiye from the 1350s until 1364.

en:
Arnaud Odon (died between 1264 and 1267) was Viscount of Lomagne and, by marriage, Count of Armagnac and Fézensac. He wed his cousin Mascarose I, succeeding her brother Bernard V in 1243. A cousin, Géraud of Fézensaguet, denied women could inherit and made war with Toulouse's backing, while Henry III of England backed Arnaud Odon. After Mascarose died in 1246 he ruled the counties as regent for their daughter Mascarose II until she married.

The dispute ended with her childless death in 1254. By his second wife Escarone he fathered Vezian III, later Viscount of Lomagne; a third marriage produced a daughter, Philippa.

en:
Bernard I (died 995), called the Cross-Eyed, was the first Count of Armagnac and the second son of William Garcés of Fézensac. When his father died in 960, his lands were divided: his elder brother Odo received Fézensac while Bernard received Armagnac.

To atone for his misdeeds Bernard vowed a pilgrimage to Jerusalem but never undertook it, founding instead the basilica of Saint Orens at Auch. He was succeeded by his son Gerald I Trancaléon and died in Normandy in 995.

en:
Bernard of Fézensaguet (c. 1155–c. 1191), also called Bernard de Lomagne, was the eldest son of Odon de Lomagne, lord of Firmacon, and Mascarose, daughter of Count Géraud III of Armagnac. In 1184 his uncle Count Bernard IV adopted him, named him heir to Armagnac and Fézensac should he have no children, and enfeoffed him with Fézensaguet.

Bernard IV was succeeded by his own son Géraud IV, but Bernard's son Géraud V inherited the counties in 1215 and began the second House of Armagnac.

en:
Bernard II Tumapaler (c. 1020 – 1064/1090) succeeded his father Girard I Trancaleon as Count of Armagnac around 1020, and through his grandmother Prisca was recognised Duke of Gascony in 1039. His authority probably extended mainly over the south.

His uncle Guy Geoffrey disputed the duchy and defeated him at the Battle of La Castelle, after which Bernard surrendered Gascony for fifteen thousand sous in 1052. He also warred on the archbishop of Auch and abdicated Armagnac by 1061, possibly entering a monastery. In May 1063 he led a Gascon baronial revolt against Guy Geoffrey, now Duke of Aquitaine, and was again defeated; Gascony was firmly bound to Aquitaine.

伯纳德二世·图马帕勒（约1020年生，1064至1090年间卒）约于1020年继承父亲热拉尔一世·特兰卡莱翁的阿马尼亚克伯爵之位，并凭借祖母普里斯卡的血统，于1039年被承认为加斯科涅公爵。他的权威可能主要限于南部。

叔父居伊·若弗鲁瓦争夺公国，在拉卡斯泰勒战役中将他击败，他被迫于1052年以15000苏的代价让出加斯科涅。他还与欧什大主教交战，1061年前退离阿马尼亚克，可能进了修道院。1063年5月，他率领加斯科涅贵族反抗已成为阿基坦公爵的居伊·若弗鲁瓦，再度兵败；加斯科涅从此牢牢归属于阿基坦。

en:
Bernard III (c. 1071–1110) succeeded his father Géraud II as Count of Armagnac around 1103. In 1090 he confirmed his family's grants to Saint-Mont priory, and he followed Duke William IX of Aquitaine to La Réole in 1103 before subscribing the Truce of God proclaimed after the Lateran council in 1104.

With his wife Alpais of Turenne he donated to Auch cathedral in August 1110; he died later that year and was succeeded by his son Géraud III.

Bernard IV (1136–1193) succeeded his father Géraud III as Count of Armagnac and Fézensac in 1160, and his rule was marked by conflict with Géraud de la Barthe, archbishop of Auch.

He designated his nephew Bernard de Lomagne as heir in case he had no children and in 1184 gave him the viscounty of Fézensaguet. His son Géraud IV succeeded when Bernard died in 1193.

en:
Bernard V (c. 1212–1245) was Count of Armagnac and Fézensac from 1242, when he succeeded his brother Pierre-Géraud. In 1242 he joined Henry III of England's coalition against Alphonse of Poitiers, but the coalition was defeated.

He died in 1245 without children by his wife Agnes. His sister Mascarose, wife of Arnaud Odon of Lomagne, inherited the county, at once claimed by their cousin Géraud of Fézensaguet.

Bernard VI (c. 1270–1319), Count of Armagnac and Fezensac from 1285, was the son of Géraud VI and Mathe de Béarn. His first wife was Isabella d'Albret, and through that marriage Bernard held the title of lord of Albret until her death in 1294.

In 1298 he married Cecilia de Rodez, heiress of Count Henri II of Rodez. Their children included his successor John I and a daughter Mathe, who married a lord of Albret.

en:
Gaston d'Armagnac (c. 1275–1320) was the younger son of Count Géraud VI of Armagnac and Mathe de Béarn. When his elder brother Bernard VI inherited the family counties in 1285, Gaston received Fézensaguet as his share and became the founder of its junior viscomital branch.

His first marriage remained childless and ended in repudiation; in 1298 he married Valpurge de Rodez, who bore his heir Géraud III in 1299. Gaston died in 1320 and was succeeded in Fézensaguet by Géraud III.

Géraud I, called Trancaléon (c. 958–c. 1020), was the only recorded son of Bernard I le Louche and Emerina, and he succeeded his father as Count of Armagnac in 995, the second ruler of that Gascon county.

en:
Géraud II (died 1095) was Count of Armagnac from 1063, the son of Bernard II Tumapaler and Ermengarde. His father, defeated in rebellion in 1063, abdicated and retired to Cluny, leaving Géraud to rule under the overlordship of William VIII of Aquitaine.

From 1072 his brother Arnaud-Bernard apparently shared rule of the county, and in 1073 the brothers fought Centule, viscount of Lescar. His wife Azivelle de Lomagne had earlier been married to the lord of Aubeissan; she bore him his successor Bernard III and two other sons, and after her death he married Sancha, widow of the viscount of Corneillan.

Géraud III (c. 1096–1160) succeeded his father Bernard III as Count of Armagnac in 1110 and ruled for half a century. In 1119 he married Anicelle, Countess of Fézensac; when her father died in 1140, Géraud added Fézensac, joining the two counties after two centuries.

By Anicelle he had a son, Bernard IV, who succeeded him, and a daughter, Mascarose, who married Odon de Lomagne and became ancestress of the second House of Armagnac.

en:
Géraud IV, nicknamed Trencaléon (c. 1170–1215), was Count of Armagnac and Fézensac from 1193, the long-awaited son of Bernard IV. In 1202 King John of England granted him lands in Gascony. During the Albigensian Crusade he did homage to Simon de Montfort for his counties and in 1213 joined the siege of Toulouse.

He died childless in 1215, having adopted his cousin Géraud V de Lomagne, who succeeded him and began the second House of Armagnac.

en:
Géraud V d'Armagnac (c. 1150–1219), son of Bernard of Fezensaguet, unexpectedly inherited the counties of Armagnac and Fezensac in 1215 when his childless kinsman Géraud IV Trenqueléon died. During the Albigensian Crusade, on 8 June 1215 he submitted to Simon de Montfort to avoid the fate of Raymond VI of Toulouse.

In 1217 Toulouse rose against Montfort; Géraud answered the summons to its siege and was entrusted with L'Isle-Jourdain. Montfort was killed in the siege, and his claims passed to the future Louis VIII, making the French crown suzerain of Armagnac. Géraud died on 30 September 1219, leaving the counties to his son Pierre-Gérard.

en:
Géraud VI (1235–1285), son of Roger I of Fézensaguet and Pincelle d'Albret, was Viscount of Fézensaguet before becoming Count of Armagnac and Fézensac. From 1246 he warred on Arnaud Odon of Lomagne; captured and ransomed though backed by Raymond VII of Toulouse, he secured them only in 1256 after Mascarose II died childless.

In 1260 he married Mathe de Béarn. After two years' imprisonment for quarrels with the seneschal, he did homage to Edward I of England and died in 1285.

en:
Jean I of Armagnac (1306–1373) succeeded his father Bernard VI in 1319 as Count of Armagnac, Fezensac and Rodez, the last through his mother Cécile, heiress of Rodez. His 1327 marriage to Béatrice de Clermont brought Charolais.

On 28 July 1340 he destroyed Robert III of Artois's Anglo-Flemish army near Saint-Omer, but in 1355, as the Black Prince raided the south, he held Toulouse and avoided battle. The 1360 Treaty of Brétigny handed Rouergue to England. On 5 December 1362 Gaston Fébus of Foix, his old rival, captured him at Launac, and he paid three hundred thousand gold florins for his freedom.

English troops held Rodez until he beat them at Mondalazac in January 1369. He died on 16 May 1373 and left the county to his son John II.

en:
Jean II, called the Hunchback (c. 1333–1384), was the son and heir of Jean I of Armagnac. He held Charolais from 1364, administered Lomagne as an appanage, and later inherited Armagnac, Fezensac and Rodez.

He fought in the Hundred Years' War from 1351. He was the first and long the only lord to back his father's appeal to Charles V against the Black Prince, which in the end freed Gascony from English rule, and was put in charge of Languedoc.

In 1379 he ended an eighty-nine-year feud between the two most powerful families of the Midi by marrying his daughter Béatrix to the son of Gaston Fébus of Foix. In 1380 he supported a revolt by the nobles of Comminges and seized their countess. Summoned to Paris on charges of plotting with England, he died at Avignon on 26 May 1384 before trial.

约翰二世绰号“驼背”（约1333年生，1384年卒），是约翰一世·德·阿马尼亚克的儿子和继承人。他自1364年起领有沙罗莱，受封洛马涅管理，后来继承了阿马尼亚克、弗藏萨克和罗德斯。

en:
Mascarose I (c. 1214–before 25 March 1246) was suo jure Countess of Armagnac and Fézensac in 1245–1246, the daughter of Count Géraud V. She married her cousin Arnaud Odon of Lomagne, by whom she had a daughter, Mascarose II.

When her brother Bernard V died in 1245 she inherited the counties, but their cousin Géraud of Fézensaguet claimed women could not inherit and warred on the couple, backed by Raymond VII of Toulouse while Henry III of England supported Mascarose.

zh:
玛斯卡罗斯一世（约1214—1246年3月25日前）于1245至1246年以自身权利任阿马尼亚克与费藏萨克女伯爵，是伯爵热罗五世之女。她嫁给堂亲、洛马涅的阿尔诺·奥东，生女玛斯卡罗斯二世。

1245年其兄弟贝尔纳五世去世，她继承两个伯国，但费藏萨盖的堂弟热罗声称女子不能领有伯国，向夫妇二人开战：图卢兹的雷蒙七世支持热罗，英王亨利三世则支持玛斯卡罗斯。

en:
Mascarose II (died 1254) ruled Armagnac and Fézensac as countess in her own right from 1246. The daughter of Arnaud Odon, Viscount of Lomagne, and Countess Mascarose I, she received the two counties from her father on her marriage to Eschivat de Chabanais.

Their cousin Géraud, Viscount of Fézensaguet, contested the succession, arguing the counties could not pass through women. She died childless in 1254, and Géraud succeeded as Géraud VI.

en:
Pierre-Géraud (c. 1210–c. 1242) was Count of Armagnac and Fézensac from 1219, the eldest son of Count Géraud V. A child at his accession, he was guarded by his uncle Arnaud-Bernard, who usurped the comital title and ruled as count from 1222.

Pierre-Géraud recovered his counties only in 1226. He married Mascarose de La Barthe but died without legitimate children around 1242, and the county passed to his younger brother Bernard V.

Roger I of Fézensaguet (c. 1190–22 March 1245) was Viscount of Fézensaguet in Gascony, the son of Bernard I, Viscount of Fézensaguet and Lomagne. He married Pincelle d'Albret, daughter of Amanieu IV, Lord of Albret.

Their eldest son, Géraud, born in 1235, succeeded him in Fézensaguet and became Count Géraud VI of Armagnac in 1256. Roger died on 22 March 1245.

en:
Shihab al-Din Ahmad ibn Hajji (c. 1235–1282) was emir of the Al Mira, the dominant Bedouin tribe of the Hauran. He challenged the Mamluk-backed amir al-arab Isa ibn Muhanna and drove the rival Al Fadl out of the Hauran, after which Sultan Baybars recognized his tribe as practically independent.

In the late 1260s he raided Najd and the Hejaz, extorting thousands of camels from Medina, which he restored under sultanic order in 1268. After backing the rebel Sunqur al-Ashqar, he rejoined the Mamluks with some four thousand horsemen at Homs in 1281.

希哈卜丁·艾哈迈德·本·哈吉（约1235—1282）是豪兰地区最强大的贝都因部落米拉的埃米尔。他挑战马穆鲁克册封的“阿拉伯人埃米尔”伊萨·本·穆汉纳，将敌对的法德勒部落逐出豪兰，拜巴尔苏丹随后承认米拉部落实际独立。

1260年代末，他劫掠内志与汉志，向麦地那强索数千峰骆驼，1268年奉苏丹之命归还。他曾支持叛将孙库尔·艾什盖尔，1281年又率约四千骑兵在霍姆斯重归马穆鲁克阵营。

en:
Anqa ibn Shati was a Bedouin emir of the Al Mira, the tribe that dominated the Hauran in southern Syria under Mamluk rule. Around 1389, as emir, he joined Nu'ayr ibn Hayar of the Al Fadl in backing the rebel Mamluk emir Mintash against Sultan Barquq.

The rebel allies besieged Aleppo but were driven off by Barquq's forces. In 1390 or 1391 Anqa was killed by the Assassins, after which the Al Mira returned to the sultan's allegiance.

安卡·伊本·沙提是米拉部的贝都因埃米尔；马穆鲁克统治时期，米拉部称雄叙利亚南部的豪兰地区。约1389年，身为埃米尔的他与法德勒部的努艾尔·伊本·哈亚尔联手支持叛乱的马穆鲁克埃米尔明塔什，对抗苏丹拜尔古格。

en:
Ludwig of Arnsberg (c. 1245–1313) ruled the County of Arnsberg from 1282, after years as co-ruler with his father Gottfried III. By his wife Petronella of Jülich he had thirteen children, and his son William succeeded him. He compromised with the expansionist archbishops of Cologne, avoiding open war.

His main work was internal: he exchanged outlying estates, recovered alienated lands and founded Sundern and Hagen through forest clearance. He died on 2 May 1313.

阿恩斯贝格的路德维希（约1245—1313）自1282年起统治阿恩斯贝格伯国，此前曾与父亲戈特弗里德三世共同执政多年。他与妻子于利希的佩特罗内拉育有十三个子女，儿子威廉继位。对外，他对扩张中的科隆大主教采取妥协，避免公开交战。

他主要致力于内部经营：交换边远领地、收回此前封出的地产，并通过开垦森林建立了松德恩、哈根等村庄。1313年5月2日，路德维希去世。

en:
William of Arnsberg (c. 1277–1338) succeeded his father Louis as count of Arnsberg in 1313. A settlement mediated by his uncle Gerhard of Jülich confirmed him as sole heir, and he then held a court registering 261 fiefs. He backed Louis of Bavaria for the German crown, gaining Soest's advocacy and ducal rights in his county.

In advanced age he joined John of Luxembourg's campaign with the Teutonic Order against the Lithuanians, founding Arensburg on Ösel in 1337. He died in 1338.

阿恩斯贝格的威廉（约1277—1338）于1313年继其父路德维希之后成为阿恩斯贝格伯爵。叔父于利希的格哈德调解达成继承协议，确认他为唯一继承人；随后他召开封臣会议，登记了261处封地。他支持巴伐利亚的路德维希争夺德意志王位，由此获得索斯特的监护权以及伯国境内的公爵权利。

晚年他随卢森堡的约翰参加条顿骑士团对立陶宛人的远征，于1337年在厄塞尔岛建立阿伦斯堡，1338年去世。

en:
André-Hercule de Fleury (1653–1743) was a French cardinal and chief minister to Louis XV. Born in Lodève, he became bishop of Fréjus in 1698 and tutor to Louis XV in 1715, and in 1726 he ousted the duke of Bourbon and took power.

For seventeen years his ministry stabilized currency and restored finances, though he harshly enforced the anti-Jansenist bull Unigenitus, and his road-building relied on forced peasant labour. He sought peace, but France entered the wars of the Polish and Austrian successions, dying in office in 1743.

安德烈·埃居尔·德·弗勒里（1653—1743）是法国枢机主教、路易十五的首席大臣。他生于洛代沃，1698年任弗雷瑞斯主教，1715年成为路易十五的教师，1726年逐走波旁公爵、亲自掌权。

en:
Albert I (c. 1258–1316) of the House of Ascania was the second Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst, ruling after his father Siegfried's abdication in 1290 and formally from 1298. In 1293 he abolished Polabian as a court language, and from 1295 he was the first Ascanian prince to reside at Köthen Castle.

Around 1307 he secured the Brandenburg-held part of Zerbst as a fief. After King Albert I's murder in 1308, Margrave Waldemar of Brandenburg proposed him as King of the Romans, in vain.

Beatrix of Saxe-Wittenberg (died after 26 February 1345) was an Ascanian princess, the daughter of Duke and Elector Rudolf I of Saxe-Wittenberg and Jutta of Brandenburg. In 1337 she became the second wife of Albert II, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst, while her sister Elisabeth married his brother and co-ruler Waldemar I.

The couple had five children, among them Albert III and John II, who both ruled Anhalt-Zerbst. Beatrix died at Coswig convent after February 1345.

en:
Henry I (c. 1170–1252), of the House of Ascania, was Count of Anhalt from 1212 and its first ruling prince from 1218. On his father Bernhard's death in 1212 he received the old Ascanian lands in the Schwabengau, while his brother Albert took the Saxon ducal title. He styled himself prince from about 1215 and was raised to princely rank by Emperor Frederick II.

He backed Frederick against the rebel King Henry (VII) in 1234. Around 1245 he retired and divided Anhalt among his sons Henry II, Bernhard and Siegfried.

en:
Siegfried I (c. 1230–1298) was the youngest son of Prince Henry I of Anhalt. In 1247 he joined the War of the Thuringian Succession, but later surrendered his claim to Margrave Henry III of Meissen. When the brothers divided Anhalt in 1252, he became the first Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst, receiving its eastern estates.

In 1273 he stood for the German crown, which instead went to Rudolf of Habsburg. In 1290 he abdicated to enter the Dominican Order, leaving rule to his son Albert I, and died at Köthen Castle in 1298.

en:
Waldemar I (died in 1368) was an Ascanian prince of Anhalt-Zerbst, youngest son of Albert I and Agnes of Brandenburg. After his father died in 1316, he and his brother Albert II were raised by their maternal uncle, Margrave Waldemar of Brandenburg, and on coming of age ruled the principality jointly, Waldemar holding his court at Dessau.

In 1344 he married Elisabeth of Saxe-Wittenberg. When Albert II died in 1362, Waldemar continued as co-ruler with his nephew John II. At his death he was succeeded by his son Waldemar II.

en:
Geoffrey V (24 August 1113 – 7 September 1151), called the Fair or Plantagenet, was Count of Anjou and Maine from 1129 and Duke of Normandy from 1144. The elder son of Fulk V and Ermengarde of Maine, he was knighted in 1128 by Henry I of England and married his daughter, the Empress Matilda.

Matilda returned to her father's court after a few months, but Henry intervened and she went back to Geoffrey. During the ensuing civil war he conquered Normandy and entered Rouen in 1144. His son by Matilda became Henry II of England, founder of the Plantagenet dynasty named from Geoffrey's broom-plant byname. Geoffrey died of fever at Château-du-Loir and was buried at Le Mans.

若弗鲁瓦五世（1113年8月24日—1151年9月7日），绰号“美男子”或“金雀花”，自1129年起任安茹与曼恩伯爵，1144年起任诺曼底公爵。他是富尔克五世与曼恩的埃芒加德的长子，1128年由英格兰国王亨利一世册封为骑士，并迎娶国王之女玛蒂尔达皇后。

几个月后玛蒂尔达回到父亲的宫廷，亨利出面干预，她才回到若弗鲁瓦身边。此后的内战年间，他攻取诺曼底，于1144年进入鲁昂。他与玛蒂尔达之子后来成为英格兰国王亨利二世，开创金雀花王朝——王朝名便得自若弗鲁瓦的金雀花绰号。他在卢瓦堡染热病去世，葬于勒芒。

en:
Robert the Strong (c. 830 – 2 July 866) was a Frankish noble and ancestor of the Capetian dynasty. He was made missus dominicus over Maine and Anjou by Charles the Bald in 853, to defend Neustria against Viking and Breton raids.

He rebelled with the Bretons in 858, was reconciled and named Count of Anjou in 861, and later lay abbot of Saint Martin at Tours. In 866 he fought a Breton-Viking force at Brissarthe. The Viking commander took refuge in a church, and Robert removed his armour to begin a siege; the Vikings then attacked by surprise and killed him. His sons Odo and Robert I became kings of West Francia, and his great-grandson was Hugh Capet.

Arnau de Llordà (died 1346) was a Catalan cleric who became bishop of Urgell in 1326, and with that see the fourth episcopal co-prince of Andorra.

His years at La Seu d'Urgell saw renewed quarrels with the counts of Foix over jurisdiction in Andorra, and he was forced to withdraw from the diocese for several years. Transferred to Tortosa in 1341, he held a synod there in 1343 and died in 1346.

en:
Anna von Schlüsselberg (died 1379), daughter of Konrad II, was abbess of Schlüsselau Abbey from 1339. After her father fell in 1347 as the last male Schlüsselberg, she used the family settlement to win further estates for the abbey and completed its church.

In 1356 she secured an imperial charter of protection from Charles IV, confirming its rights and high jurisdiction. Remembered as Schlüsselau's most important abbess, she gave the house a sound economic and legal basis and died in 1379.

en:
Berthold von Zollern (1320–1365) was the second son of Burgrave Frederick IV of Nuremberg and Margaret of Görz. He joined the Teutonic Order at thirteen in 1333 and rose to Landkomtur.

In 1351 Pope Clement VI named him Prince-Bishop of Eichstätt before he was even ordained; he received minor orders, the diaconate and priesthood within three weeks. Bishop Albrecht of Hohenfels still held the see, so the two divided the work until Albrecht resigned in 1353.

Berthold enlarged the bishopric's lands and began the Willibaldsburg, moving in during 1355; his successors lived there until 1725. A councillor of Emperor Charles IV, he went with him to Avignon in 1365, fell ill on the way home, and died that September at Eichstätt. He was buried at Heilsbronn Abbey.

贝特霍尔德·冯·措伦（1320—1365）是纽伦堡城堡伯爵腓特烈四世与格尔茨的玛格丽特的次子。他13岁时的1333年加入条顿骑士团，后升任地区长官。

1351年，教皇克雷芒六世在他尚未受圣职时就任命他为艾希施泰特亲王主教，他在三周内先后领受低级圣职、执事和司铎圣职。当时霍恩费尔斯的阿尔布雷希特仍在位，二人分工共治，直至阿尔布雷希特于1353年逊位。

贝特霍尔德扩充了主教区的领地，主持修建维利巴茨堡，1355年迁入，其后继者在此居住到1725年。作为皇帝查理四世的顾问，他于1365年随皇帝前往阿维尼翁，归途中染病，同年9月在艾希施泰特病逝，葬于海尔斯布隆修道院。

Elisabeth of Henneberg (c. 1318 – 6 December 1377), also called Elsbeth, was a German countess and burgravine of Nuremberg. She was the daughter of Berthold VII, Count of Henneberg-Schleusingen, and Adelheid of Hesse. She married John II the Acquirer, the Hohenzollern Burgrave of Nuremberg, and bore his only son, Frederick V, who succeeded as burgrave in 1357.

Two of their daughters, Anna and Adelheid, became abbesses of Birkenfeld Abbey. Elisabeth died in 1377, surviving her husband by twenty years.

亨讷贝格的伊丽莎白（约1318年—1377年12月6日），又称埃尔斯贝特，是德意志女伯爵、纽伦堡城堡伯爵夫人。她是亨讷贝格-施莱辛根伯爵贝特霍尔德七世与黑森的阿德尔海德之女。她嫁给霍亨索伦家族的纽伦堡城堡伯爵、绰号“整合者”的约翰二世，为他生下独子腓特烈五世；约翰二世1357年去世后，腓特烈五世继任城堡伯爵。

Frederick I (c. 1139–1201), born Frederick III of Zollern, was a younger son of Count Frederick II of Zollern and the first Hohenzollern to hold Nuremberg. From 1171 he was a partisan of the Hohenstaufen, serving Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, including the 1180 campaign against Henry the Lion.

Around 1184 he married Sophie of Raabs, heiress of the Nuremberg burgraviate, and Henry VI enfeoffed him with it around 1191. He founded the Franconian line of the Hohenzollern; his sons Conrad I and Frederick IV took the Franconian and Swabian inheritances.

腓特烈一世（约1139—1201），即索伦伯爵腓特烈三世，是索伦伯爵腓特烈二世的幼子，也是霍亨索伦家族首任纽伦堡城堡伯爵。自1171年起，他追随霍亨斯陶芬家族，在皇帝腓特烈·巴巴罗萨麾下效力，包括1180年讨伐狮子亨利的行动。

en:
Frederick III (c. 1220 – 14 August 1297) was Burgrave of Nuremberg, son of Conrad I and Adelheid of Frontenhausen. He held the western Hohenzollern lands around Cadolzburg and in 1248 received Bayreuth through the Meranian inheritance. He succeeded his father in 1261.

In 1273 his deciding vote elected Rudolf of Habsburg King of the Romans, and Rudolf made him Prince-Elector and entrusted him with the royal district court of Franconia. Frederick fought at Dürnkrut against Ottokar of Bohemia in 1278, gaining Wunsiedel and Erlangen. By his second wife Helene of Saxony he fathered his successor Frederick IV.

en:
Frederick IV (c. 1287 – 19 May 1332) was Burgrave of Nuremberg from 1300, succeeding his elder brother John I; he was the younger son of Frederick III and Helene of Saxony. In 1307 he and King Albert I led an imperial army against the Wettin margraves, but were defeated at Lucka.

In 1322 he fought for Louis the Bavarian at Mühldorf and helped capture the Habsburg claimant Frederick the Fair. In 1331 he bought Ansbach, nucleus of the later Hohenzollern principality. His wife Margaret of Görz-Tyrol bore him many children, including his successor John II. Frederick died in 1332.

Frederick V (before 3 March 1333 – 21 January 1398) was the elder son of Burgrave John II of Nuremberg and Elisabeth of Henneberg. Succeeding in 1357, he guarded the imperial castle of Nuremberg and served Emperor Charles IV, who in 1363 made him the first burgrave of princely rank.

He married Elisabeth of Meissen in 1356; their daughters wed Rupert, King of the Romans, and Duke Albert III of Austria. After his death in 1398 his sons divided his lands, and Frederick VI, who received Ansbach, later became the first Hohenzollern Elector of Brandenburg.

en:
Frederick of Zollern, born before 1325, was Prince-Bishop of Regensburg from 1340 to 1365, a son of Burgrave Frederick IV of Nuremberg and Margaret of Görz-Tyrol. His brothers John and Berthold became burgrave and Bishop of Eichstätt.

After Bishop Nicholas of Ybbs died, most of the chapter chose Frederick, but Emperor Louis the Bavarian backed a rival, Heinrich of Stein. Both claimants pledged castles and borrowed heavily, and the bishopric was left deeply in debt. Heinrich withdrew in 1345 and the emperor accepted Frederick.

He later gave Donaustauf Castle to Emperor Charles IV, over the chapter's protests, and in 1349 saw plague empty villages across his diocese. He resigned in 1365 and died before February 1368.

索伦的腓特烈（1325年前生）于1340年至1365年任雷根斯堡采邑主教，是纽伦堡城堡伯爵腓特烈四世与戈里齐亚-蒂罗尔的玛格丽特之子。兄弟约翰任城堡伯爵、贝特霍尔德任艾希施泰特主教。

伊布斯的尼古拉主教去世后，多数教士选他继任，但皇帝巴伐利亚人路德维希支持对立主教施泰因的海因里希。两位主教都靠抵押城堡、举债来争夺地盘，主教区因此债台高筑。1345年海因里希放弃，皇帝转而接受腓特烈。

此后他把多瑙施陶夫城堡转给皇帝查理四世，教士会为此大为不满；1349年黑死病使教区内许多村庄人口死绝。他于1365年辞职，1368年2月前去世。

John I (c. 1279–1300) was a Hohenzollern burgrave of Nuremberg, the elder son of Burgrave Frederick III and Helen of Saxony. On his father's death in 1297 he succeeded to the burgraviate and ruled it jointly with his younger brother Frederick IV, and in the same year married Agnes of Hesse.

He died childless in 1300 after a reign of only three years. His brother Frederick IV was left to rule the burgraviate alone.

en:
John II (c. 1309 – 1357), called the Acquirer, was Burgrave of Nuremberg and elder son of Frederick IV. Succeeding in 1332, he earned his byname by enlarging the Hohenzollern lands in Franconia, notably through an inheritance treaty that brought him Plassenburg Castle and Kulmbach in 1340, when the counts of Orlamünde died out.

In 1345 he briefly governed the March of Brandenburg for the Wittelsbach margrave Louis. When plague reached Nuremberg in his time, the city's Jews were massacred and the burgrave did not intervene.

By Elisabeth of Henneberg he left an only son, Frederick V, who succeeded him. His two daughters became abbesses of Birkenfeld.

en:
Catherine of Nuremberg (c. 1323 – after 1373) was a Hohenzollern princess, daughter of Frederick IV and Margaret of Görz-Tyrol. In 1331 her father bought the town of Ansbach, the seed of the later Hohenzollern principality there.

Catherine was betrothed at Würzburg on 29 June 1335 and married before June 1338 Eberhard I, son of Count Rudolf IV of Wertheim. As countess she bore at least thirteen children.

They included John I, who succeeded as count, and Albert, bishop of Bamberg from 1398. Two of her brothers also became bishops: Frederick of Regensburg and Berthold of Eichstätt. She is last recorded alive on 11 March 1373.

en:
Conrad I (c. 1186 – 1261) was a Hohenzollern Burgrave of Nuremberg and elder son of Burgrave Frederick I. He received the Franconian lands and burgraviate in a family partition of 1218. A loyal Hohenstaufen partisan, he backed Emperor Frederick II and in 1219 took military protection of Nuremberg after its freedom charter.

In 1237–1239 he administered Austria. He enlarged his lands with the Rangau and Ansbach, controlled major trade routes to Nuremberg and fought marauding knights. He died in 1261 and was succeeded by his son Frederick III.

en:
Konrad II von Schlüsselberg (c. 1277–1347) was the most powerful and last lord of the Franconian noble house of Schlüsselberg. As Reichssturmfähnrich he held the imperial battle-standard fief from 1322 to 1336.

He enlarged his domains and held seventeen castles. A feud in 1347 with the bishops of Würzburg and Bamberg ended when a catapult stone killed him at the siege of Neideck on 14 September. His lands were divided among the victors, as he left no son.

Margaret of Görz-Tyrol (c. 1291–1348) was the daughter of Albert II of Gorizia-Tyrol and Agnes of Hohenberg, and a granddaughter of Meinhard, Duke of Carinthia. Before August 1307 she married Frederick IV, Burgrave of Nuremberg.

She was the mother of his ten children, among them John II, who succeeded as burgrave in 1332, Frederick, bishop of Regensburg, and Berthold, bishop of Eichstätt. Margaret herself died in 1348.

en:
Antonello da Messina (c. 1425–1430 – 1479) was a Sicilian painter of the Early Renaissance, born in Messina. Around 1450 he trained in Naples under Niccolò Colantonio, where he absorbed Netherlandish oil technique. He became a master painter at Messina, and his early paintings combined Flemish influences with Italian attention to the volume of figures.

In Venice from 1475 to 1476, he painted the San Cassiano Altarpiece and the Condottiero, passing oil technique to Giovanni Bellini and the Venetian school. He died at Messina in 1479.

安东内洛·达·梅西纳（约1425—1430年生，1479年卒）是文艺复兴早期的西西里画家，生于墨西拿。约1450年他在那不勒斯师从尼科洛·科兰托尼奥，并在那里掌握了尼德兰油画技法。他在墨西拿成为画师，早期作品融合佛兰德斯影响与意大利画家对人物体积的重视。

1475至1476年居留威尼斯期间，他创作《圣卡夏诺祭坛画》和《佣兵队长肖像》，把油画技法传给乔瓦尼·贝利尼和威尼斯画派，1479年在墨西拿去世。

en:
António Fernandes (died 1520) was a Portuguese carpenter turned explorer, the first European known to have entered the Zimbabwean interior. Condemned to death, his sentence was commuted to African exile; he arrived on the East African coast in 1501 and settled at Sofala in 1504.

From 1511 to 1514 he explored the Zambezi and the inland, reaching the court of the Mwenemutapa ruler. In 1515–1516 he explored the Buzi River, and he died at Sofala in 1520.

en:
Amanieu VII d'Albret (died 1326), one of the most powerful lords in Gascony, held the lordship of Albret from 1298. A kinsman of the Plantagenets and Pope Martin IV, he sat on the English King's Council under Edward I and Edward II.

In 1286 he ended a private war with the English seneschal of Gascony for a payment from Edward I. In 1302 he negotiated the Treaty of Paris that restored Gascony to England.

He then courted both crowns, taking his quarrels to the Parlement of Paris and in 1324 joining the French in the War of Saint-Sardos. His son Bernard Ezi V succeeded him.

阿马尼厄七世·德·阿尔布雷（1326年卒）是加斯科涅最有权势的领主之一，自1298年起统治阿尔布雷领地。他与金雀花王室和教皇马丁四世都有亲谊，在英格兰国王爱德华一世、爱德华二世两朝出任国王会议成员。

1286年，他接受爱德华一世的赔款，结束了与英方加斯科涅总督的私人战争。1302年，他获任谈判代表，商议使加斯科涅归还英格兰的《巴黎条约》。

此后他周旋于两顶王冠之间：把争端上诉到巴黎高等法院，更在1324年的圣萨尔多战争中倒向法兰西。其子贝尔纳·埃齐五世继立。

en:
Bernard Ezi V d'Albret (c. 1290–1358), son of Amanieu VII, was Lord of Albret from 1324 and one of the Gascon barons who stood by the English crown. In 1321 he married Mathe of Armagnac, and they had twelve children.

In 1330 he tried to marry his heir Arnaud Amanieu to a daughter of Edmund of Woodstock, and the plan failed, though he still gained money and lands. In 1337 Edward III made him joint lieutenant of Aquitaine with Oliver Ingham, and he refused Philip VI's bribes.

In 1340 he received Auribat and other lands in exchange for Montendre and Blaye. A 1351 betrothal of his son Bernard to Edward's daughter Isabella came to nothing. Arnaud Amanieu succeeded him.

贝尔纳·埃齐五世·德·阿尔布雷（约1290—1358）是阿马尼厄七世之子，1324年起任阿尔布雷领主，是始终站在英格兰一边的加斯科涅男爵之一。1321年他娶阿马尼亚克的玛特为妻，育有十二个子女。

1330年，他试图为继承人阿尔诺·阿马尼厄求娶伍德斯托克的埃德蒙之女，婚事未成，他却由此得到了钱财和土地。1337年，爱德华三世任命他与奥利弗·英厄姆共同出任阿基坦公国副长官，他拒绝了腓力六世的贿赂。

1340年，他以蒙唐德尔和布莱换得奥里巴等领地。1351年，其子贝尔纳与爱德华三世之女伊莎贝拉订婚，但婚约最终取消。他死后由阿尔诺·阿马尼厄继位。

en:
Hugh, called le Brun (the Brown), was a Poitevin baron of the Lusignan family, eldest son of Hugh VIII of Lusignan and elder brother of Aimery and Guy, later kings of Jerusalem and Cyprus. He helped administer the family estates and appears as lord of Lusignan while his father was on crusade after 1163.

In the Aquitanian revolt of 1168 Henry II Plantagenet took and dismantled Lusignan castle, which the brothers rebuilt. Hugh died before his father in April 1169, leaving by Aurengarde of Exoudun three underage children, including Hugh IX.

于格，绰号“棕发者”，是吕西尼昂家族的普瓦图男爵，吕西尼昂的于格八世的长子，也是后来成为耶路撒冷和塞浦路斯国王的艾默里与居伊的兄长。他协助管理家族产业，1163年父亲东征期间，以吕西尼昂领主的身份出现在特许状中。

1168年阿基坦诸侯叛乱期间，英格兰的亨利二世攻占并拆毁吕西尼昂城堡，吕西尼昂兄弟随后将其重建。1169年4月，于格先于父亲去世，与埃克苏丹的奥朗加德留下三个年幼子女，其中包括于格九世。

en:
Hugh VIII, called the Old, of Lusignan was a Poitevin baron, eldest son of Hugh VII of Lusignan. On his father's death in 1151 he inherited Lusignan, Couhé and Château-Larcher, and through his wife Burgundia of Rancon he gained further castles in Poitou and Saintonge.

He took the cross in 1163 and led a crusader contingent to the Holy Land. In 1164 his troops joined a surprise attack on Nur ad-Din's camp, and on 11 August 1164 Nur ad-Din captured him at the Battle of Harim and took him to Aleppo. His sons Guy and Aimery later ruled Jerusalem and Cyprus.

吕西尼昂的于格八世，世称“老者”，是普瓦图贵族，吕西尼昂的于格七世之子。1151年父亲去世后，他继承吕西尼昂、库埃和夏特拉尔谢等领地，又通过妻子朗孔的勃艮第，在普瓦图和圣通日掌握更多城堡。

1163年他领取十字，率一支十字军前往圣地。1164年，他的部队参与突袭努尔丁的营地，同年8月11日他在哈里姆之战中被俘，押往阿勒颇。他的儿子居伊和艾默里后来成为耶路撒冷与塞浦路斯的统治者。

Jeanne d'Albret (c. 1333 – 1359 or before) was the eldest daughter of Bernard Ezi V, Lord of Albret. By a marriage contract of 8 July 1350 she married Jean-Jourdain I, Count of L'Isle-Jourdain in Gascony.

She bore two sons. Bernard Ezi died young, and Bertrand II succeeded as count in 1365 and died without issue in 1369, whereupon the county passed to his great-uncle Jean-Jourdain II. Jeanne died before 15 July 1359.

Mathe d'Armagnac (1302–1364) was the daughter of Bernard VI, Count of Armagnac, and Cécile de Rodez. In 1321 she married Bernard Ezi V, lord of Albret, as his second wife. He was a Gascon baron faithful to Edward III of England and in 1337 was named lieutenant of Aquitaine.

The marriage produced twelve children, including Arnaud-Amanieu, who inherited Albret, and Jeanne and Rose, married in 1350 to the count of L'Isle and Jean III de Grailly.

en:
Bertrand of Saint-Geniès (c. 1260 – 6 June 1350), a Gascon law professor and papal chaplain, became Patriarch of Aquileia in 1334. Though already old, he came to Friuli with a programme of reform.

Allied with Venice and Austria, he defeated Rizzardo da Camino in 1335 and recovered the Cadore in 1347. He and the abbot of Moggio once celebrated Christmas mass in armour, a scene Udine re-enacted until 1848. He curbed the Friulian feudal lords and founded the university of Cividale in 1344.

The nobles allied against him in 1348, and in 1350, in his nineties, he was ambushed and killed at San Giorgio della Richinvelda. The Church venerates him as a blessed martyr.

圣热涅的贝特朗（约1260—1350年6月6日）是加斯科涅出身的法学家、教皇司铎。1334年出任阿奎莱亚牧首时他已年事很高，却带着一整套改革方案来到弗留利。

他联合威尼斯与奥地利公爵，1335年击败里扎尔多·达·卡米诺，1347年收复卡多雷。他与摩焦修道院院长曾披甲主持一次圣诞弥撒，乌迪内直到1848年仍重演这一幕。他压制弗留利的封建领主，并于1344年创办奇维达莱大学。

1348年贵族们结盟反对他；1350年6月6日，年过九旬的他在圣乔治-德拉里金韦尔达遭伏击身亡。天主教会尊他为真福殉道者。

en:
Carlevario della Torre was a Lombard nobleman of the Veronese branch of the Torriani, son of Giovanni della Torre and Orsina Mandelli. His line made its career in Friuli around the patriarchs of Aquileia.

An instrument drawn up at Udine on 28 September 1344 names his son Luigi among the witnesses before Patriarch Bertrando. He married first Caterina of the counts of Collalto and then Giovanna di Zucco. His daughter Leonardina was married as a child to Tolberto IV da Camino in 1330 and later wed Ludovico di Cucagna.

卡莱瓦里奥·德拉·托雷是米兰托里亚尼家族维罗纳支的伦巴第贵族，乔瓦尼·德拉·托雷与奥尔西娜·曼代利之子。他这一支在弗留利围绕阿奎莱亚牧首发展。

Cassone della Torre, or Gastone (c. 1269–1318), was a Torriani churchman, son of Corrado 'Mosca' della Torre. He returned to Milan in 1302 and became archbishop in 1308. Driven out by his cousin Guido in 1309, he returned to crown Henry VII as King of Italy in January 1311.

Forced to leave Milan again in 1311, he excommunicated Matteo I Visconti in 1314 and was made Patriarch of Aquileia by John XXII in 1316. He died in a fall from his horse at Florence on 20 August 1318 and was buried in Santa Croce.

Febo I della Torre, called Febosino (c. 1261–1329), was a Milanese nobleman of the Torriani, son of Lombardo della Torre, who perished in Baradello prison after Desio. In 1274 he settled on the Tagliamento under his great-uncle Raimondo, Patriarch of Aquileia, and with his brother Raimondo held Flambro.

As castellan of Tolmino he was captured by Cividale through treason in 1292. Freed, he became the patriarch's vicedominus in 1298, and was podestà of Treviso in 1321 and of Trieste in 1328–1329.

费博一世·德拉·托雷，绰号小费博（约1261—1329），米兰托里亚尼家族贵族，伦巴多·德拉·托雷之子，其父在代西奥战败后死于巴拉德罗监狱。1274年，他在叔祖父、阿奎莱亚牧首雷蒙多的庇护下定居塔利亚门托河畔，并与兄弟雷蒙多一同受封弗拉姆布罗。

Giovanni della Torre, known as Gian Furiano (c. 1291–1345), was the only son of Febo I della Torre and the first of his line born in Friuli, which gave him his nickname. He followed Patriarch Pagano della Torre in the wars against the Visconti of Milan and was defeated at Vaprio in 1324.

Back in Friuli after Pagano's death, he joined the enemies of the new patriarch Bertrando, backing Rizzardo da Camino's invasion and feuding with the Savorgnano. After a clash near Flambro, the patriarch had the stronghold dismantled and the Torriani stripped of their fiefs.

Gian Furiano still grew in power through gifts from the counts of Gorizia, who made him captain of Latisana. He died in 1345, before the league against Bertrando ended in the patriarch's murder.

詹·富里亚诺仍靠戈里齐亚伯爵的赠予壮大势力，被任命为拉蒂萨纳统领。他于1345年去世，没有看到反对贝尔特兰多的同盟以牧首被害收场。

Ludovico della Torre (died 30 July 1365) was a son of Raimondo II della Torre. He became bishop of Trieste in 1346, and Innocent VI named him Patriarch of Aquileia on 10 May 1359.

In June 1361 Duke Rudolf IV of Austria invaded; Aquileia fell almost without a fight, and Ludovico was taken hostage to Vienna. Freed in 1362, he faced a second invasion in 1363, but won the backing of his old enemy Charles IV, who wanted a trade route from Venice to Prague through Friuli.

Rudolf's forces were beaten in 1364. Ludovico died of a sudden fever at Soffumbergo on 30 July 1365, three days after Rudolf died in Milan.

卢多维科·德拉·托雷（？—1365年7月30日）出身托里亚尼家族，是雷蒙多二世·德拉·托雷之子。1346年他任的里雅斯特主教，1359年5月10日被教皇英诺森六世任命为阿奎莱亚牧首。

1361年6月奥地利公爵鲁道夫四世入侵，阿奎莱亚几乎不战而降，卢多维科被掳往维也纳为人质。1362年获释后，1363年哈布斯堡军队再度来犯，这次他得到昔日对手查理四世的支持，后者想借弗留利打通从威尼斯到布拉格的商路。

1364年，鲁道夫的军队被击败。1365年7月30日，卢多维科在索丰贝戈死于急性热病，三天前鲁道夫刚在米兰去世。

Pagano della Torre (died 18 December 1332) was a prelate of the Milanese della Torre family, which had settled in Friuli after the Visconti drove them from Milan. He became Bishop of Padua in 1302 and Patriarch of Aquileia in 1319.

He joined the della Torre crusade against the Visconti, but was beaten at Bassignana in 1322 and Vaprio in 1324, abandoning hopes of retaking Milan. War debts forced him to sell his mitre and library, and heavy taxes pushed Istrian towns such as Rovigno and Pola to surrender to Venice. He died in 1332, soon after Pope John XXII mediated peace.

Raimondo della Torre (c. 1230 – 23 February 1299) was a cleric of the Guelph della Torre family, son of Pagano I of Milan. As bishop of Como he was captured in 1269 and publicly displayed in a cage at Sondalo in the Valtellina until della Torre troops freed him in 1273.

As Patriarch of Aquileia from 1273 he sheltered kinsmen exiled after Desio and fought Venice for Capodistria and Trieste, annexing Trieste by the 1291 Peace of Treviso. He crushed revolts by his vassals and was buried in Aquileia Basilica.

en:
Raimondo II della Torre (c. 1267–1323) was a Milanese Torriani nobleman, son of Lombardo della Torre and Caterina Pirovano. With his brother Febo he settled in Friuli under their great-uncle Raimondo, Patriarch of Aquileia, and held the fief of Flambro from Count Henry of Gorizia.

His long feud with the Savorgnano family became notorious. He married Anfonisia, daughter of Ludovico of the lords of Villalta; his sons included Ermacora I and Ludovico, Patriarch of Aquileia from 1359. On 16 January 1340 his children were granted Venetian nobility, but his line died out in the fourteenth century.

en:
Alfonso II (1157–1196), called the Chaste, was the first king of Aragon to rule as count of Barcelona. His father Ramon Berenguer IV died in 1162; his mother Petronilla abdicated the Aragonese throne in his favour in 1164 and acted as his regent.

He allied with Castile by marrying Sancha, sister of Alfonso VIII, in 1174, and pushed the Reconquista south in 1171; the Treaty of Cazorla in 1179 fixed Aragon's southern claims. He ceded Provence to his brother in 1173 and added Cerdanya and Roussillon. A patron of troubadours, he died at Perpignan in 1196.

en:
Alfonso III the Liberal (4 November 1265 – 18 June 1291), son of Peter III and Constance of Sicily, became King of Aragon in 1285.

He moved at once against his uncle James II of Majorca, taking Majorca in 1285 and Menorca on 17 January 1287. At home he was forced to grant the Privilege of the Union to the Aragonese nobility, surrendering important royal powers.

He initially backed his brother James's claim to Sicily, but withdrew that support shortly before his death and sought peace with the papacy and France. Betrothed to Eleanor, daughter of Edward I of England, he died in Barcelona on 18 June 1291 before the marriage, aged 25.

阿方索三世（慷慨者）（1265年11月4日—1291年6月18日）是佩德罗三世与西西里的科斯坦察之子，1285年即位为阿拉贡国王。

他随即出兵征讨其叔马略卡国王海梅二世：1285年攻占马略卡，1287年1月17日攻克梅诺卡。在国内，他被迫向阿拉贡贵族颁布《联盟特权令》，让出多项重要王权。

他起初支持弟弟海梅对西西里的主张，临终前却撤回支持，寻求与教廷和法国议和。他与英格兰国王爱德华一世之女埃莉诺订有婚约，却于1291年6月18日在巴塞罗那未婚而卒，年仅25岁。

en:
Alfonso de Aragón y Foix, called the Old (1332–1412), was the eldest son of Count Peter of Ribagorza and Joanna of Foix, a grandson of James II of Aragon and a cousin of Peter IV.

He married Violante Díaz de Arenós in 1355, the year he became Count of Dénia. He added Ribagorza in 1361 and was made the first Duke of Gandía in 1399.

His chance came in 1410, when King Martin died childless and left the Crown of Aragon without a direct heir. As the senior male-line descendant of James II, Alfonso put in a claim, but he died at Gandía in March 1412, before the Compromise of Caspe settled the succession. His brother Juan inherited the claim, and his son Alfonso inherited Gandía, Ribagorza and Dénia.

en:
Alfonso I, called the Battler (c. 1073–1134), ruled as king of Aragon and Navarre from 1104, succeeding his brother Peter I. Raised at the monastery of Siresa, he learned letters and military arts.

In 1109 he married Urraca, queen of Castile and León, and claimed the title Emperor of Spain, but the marriage collapsed into years of civil war. His greatest success in the Reconquista was the capture of Zaragoza in 1118.

He died after his defeat at Fraga in 1134, leaving his kingdoms to the military orders, a will his nobility rejected. Aragon and Navarre chose separate kings.

en:
Alfonso IV the Kind (2 November 1299 – 24 January 1336) was born in Naples, the second son of James II and Blanche of Anjou. In 1314 he married Teresa d'Entença, heiress to the County of Urgell, which thereby joined the Crown lands.

He became heir when his elder brother James renounced the throne in 1319, led the conquest of Sardinia in 1323–1324 and succeeded as king in November 1327. A long war with Genoa began in 1329.

That year he married Eleanor of Castile; his grants of land to their sons divided the court and provoked opposition in Valencia. He died aged 36, leaving the crown to his son Peter IV.
