阿方索四世（友善者）（1299年11月2日—1336年1月24日）出生于那不勒斯，是海梅二世与安茹的布朗什的次子。1314年，他与乌尔赫尔伯国的女继承人特蕾莎·德·恩滕萨结婚，乌尔赫尔由此并入阿拉贡王室领地。

同年他迎娶卡斯蒂利亚的埃莉诺，为二人的儿子分封土地，引发宫廷分裂和巴伦西亚人的反对。他36岁时去世，王位传给其子佩德罗四世。

en:
Antonio Beccadelli (1394–1471), known as Il Panormita from his native Palermo, was an Italian humanist poet and canon lawyer. He taught eloquence at Pavia and served as court poet to the Visconti duke of Milan. In 1425 he published Hermaphroditus, a Latin collection of erotic epigrams that made his name.

From 1442 he served Alfonso V of Aragon at Naples, and in 1448 founded the humanist academy Porticus Antoniana. He died at Naples in 1471.

安东尼奥·贝卡代利（1394—1471），人称“帕诺尔米塔”，意为“巴勒莫人”，是意大利人文主义诗人、教会法学家。他在帕维亚教授雄辩术，并担任米兰维斯孔蒂公爵的宫廷诗人。1425年出版拉丁语艳情警诗集《赫耳玛佛洛狄托斯》，由此成名。

1442年起他在那不勒斯效力于阿拉贡的阿方索五世，1448年创办人文主义学园“安东尼门廊”，1471年在那不勒斯去世。

en:
Bahya ben Asher ibn Halawa (1255–c. 1340) was a rabbi and biblical commentator in Zaragoza, in the Crown of Aragon. A pupil of Solomon ibn Aderet, the Rashba, he served his native city as a darshan, an expounder of scripture.

He belonged to the circle of Kabbalists of Girona and is counted among the most distinguished Hebrew Bible exegetes of medieval Spain. Unlike his master, he wrote no Talmud commentary and devoted himself to interpreting the Torah.

en:
Blanche of Anjou (1280–1310), also called Blanche of Naples, was the daughter of Charles II of Naples and Mary of Hungary, and queen of Aragon as the second wife of James II. She married James at Vilabertran on 29 October 1295 under the Treaty of Anagni, negotiated by Pope Boniface VIII between Aragon and Naples.

Blanche of Taranto (1309–1337) was the daughter of Philip I of Anjou, prince of Taranto and Achaea, by his first wife Thamar Angelina Komnene. In 1327 she married her first cousin Ramon Berenguer of Aragon, count of Prades, who later exchanged Prades for the County of Empúries.

en:
Cécile de Comminges (c. 1320–1384) was the eldest daughter of Bernard VIII, Count of Comminges. In 1336 she married James I, Count of Urgell, and from 1339, when her little brother Jean died, she held the viscounty of Turenne in her own right.

Her uncle Pierre-Raymond denied that women could inherit Comminges; a settlement gave him the county and her Turenne. At Avignon she became a friend and adviser of Pope Clement VI, so close that rumour made her his mistress, and Petrarch called her ‘Semiramis with her quiver’.

Widowed in 1347, she was regent of Urgell for her young son Peter II until 1360. In 1349 she sold Turenne to the pope for 145,000 gold florins, to pay her husband's debts and build a church at Balaguer. She died at Balaguer Castle on 16 June 1384.

塞西尔·德·科曼日（约1320—1384）是科曼日伯爵贝尔纳八世的长女。1336年，她嫁给乌拉尔伯爵海梅一世；1339年幼弟让夭折后，她以本人身份领有蒂雷纳子爵领。

她的叔父皮埃尔-雷蒙以女性不能继承科曼日为由与她争夺继承权，最终叔父取得科曼日，她取得蒂雷纳。她在阿维尼翁成为教皇克雷芒六世的密友与顾问，亲近到传出她是教皇情妇的流言，彼特拉克称她为“带着箭袋的塞米拉米斯”。

1347年丈夫去世后，她为年幼的儿子彼得二世摄政乌拉尔伯国，直到1360年。1349年，她以145,000金弗罗林将蒂雷纳卖给教皇，用来偿还丈夫的债务并在巴拉格尔兴建一座教堂。1384年6月16日，她在巴拉格尔城堡去世。

en:
Francesc Eiximenis (c. 1330–1409) was a Catalan Franciscan writer, probably born at Girona. He studied at Paris and took his theology doctorate at Toulouse in 1374.

From 1382 to 1408 he lived in Valencia; his works, above all Lo Crestià, were widely read, making him one of the most successful medieval Catalan writers, and Peter IV, John I and Martin I of Aragon and the Avignon pope Benedict XIII all read him. In 1408 Benedict XIII made him patriarch of Jerusalem, and he died at Perpignan in 1409.

en:
Ferdinand of Aragon (11 December 1329 – 16 July 1363) was the elder son of Alfonso IV and his second wife Eleanor of Castile, and half-brother of Peter IV. Alfonso's plan to grant him Valencian lands angered the heir and the Valencians and was dropped.

In 1335 Eleanor fled with her sons to Castile. After James of Urgell died in 1347, Ferdinand took over the Valencian opposition to the king, but he was wounded, defeated and captured at Epila in 1348, and freed at Castile's request.

In 1357 Peter made him lieutenant general and later gave him command of his army. The king then suspected treason. On 16 July 1363, after dining with Peter at Burriana, Ferdinand refused arrest, drew his sword and was killed.

zh:
阿拉贡的费尔南多（1329年12月11日—1363年7月16日）是阿方索四世与第二任妻子卡斯蒂利亚的埃莉诺的长子，佩德罗四世的异母弟。阿方索打算把巴伦西亚的部分领地分给他，王储与巴伦西亚人都为此不满，计划作罢。

1335年，埃莉诺带着两个儿子逃往卡斯蒂利亚。1347年乌赫尔的海梅去世后，费尔南多接过巴伦西亚反对国王的旗帜，但1348年在埃皮拉之战中受伤兵败被俘，应卡斯蒂利亚之请获释。

1357年佩德罗授他副将军之职，后来又让他统率军队，随后却渐起疑心，认为他通敌。1363年7月16日，费尔南多在布里亚纳与国王共进晚餐后拒绝被捕，拔剑抵抗，被杀。

en:
Baltasar Gracián (1601–1658) was a Spanish Jesuit, Baroque writer and philosopher, born at Belmonte in Aragon. Ordained in 1627, he became a noted preacher and rector of the Jesuit college at Tarragona, and served as an army chaplain at the 1646 siege of Lleida.

His works on courtly conduct include The Hero and The Art of Worldly Wisdom (1647), while his allegorical novel El Criticón appeared 1651–1657. Publishing without his order's leave, he was exiled to Graus and died at Tarazona in 1658.

巴尔塔沙·葛拉西安（1601—1658）是西班牙耶稣会士、巴洛克作家与哲学家，生于阿拉贡的贝尔蒙特。1627年晋铎，他以讲道闻名，后任塔拉戈纳耶稣会学院院长，1646年莱里达围城战期间曾任随军神父。

他著有《英雄》《智慧书》（1647）等探讨宫廷立身之道的作品，寓言小说《批评大师》于1651至1657年问世。因未经修会许可出书，他1658年被流放格劳斯并卒于塔拉索纳。

en:
James I the Conqueror (2 February 1208 – 27 July 1276) succeeded his father Peter II as King of Aragon in 1213. After Peter fell at Muret, Simon de Montfort held the young king until Pope Innocent III demanded his release in 1214, and he was then raised by the Knights Templar at Monzón.

Taking power in 1227, he led the Crown of Aragon southwards: he conquered Majorca in 1229, then captured Valencia in 1238 after a five-year campaign.

With the Treaty of Corbeil in 1258, Louis IX of France gave up all claims over the Catalan counties. He sponsored Catalan letters and dictated the chronicle of his reign, the Llibre dels fets.

海梅一世（征服者）（1208年2月2日—1276年7月27日）于1213年继其父佩德罗二世为阿拉贡国王。佩德罗在米雷阵亡后，年幼的海梅受到西蒙·德·蒙特福特控制，直到1214年教宗诺森三世要求蒙特福特交还他，他随后由圣殿骑士团在蒙松抚养。

1227年亲政后，他率领阿拉贡联合王国向南扩张：1229年征服马略卡岛；经过五年征战，于1238年攻取巴伦西亚。

1258年，他与法兰西国王路易九世签订《科尔贝条约》，使法王放弃对加泰罗尼亚诸伯国的一切宗主权。他扶持加泰罗尼亚语文学，口授了记述自身统治的《海梅一世编年史》。

en:
James I (1321–1347), infante of Aragon and count of Urgell, was born in Zaragoza, a son of King Alfonso IV of Aragon and Teresa d'Entença, countess of Urgell. He inherited the County of Urgell after his father renounced it.

In 1336 he married Cecilia, daughter of Bernard VIII of Comminges; they had a son, Peter, who succeeded him. His brother Peter IV had no son, which made James heir presumptive. When the king tried to put his own daughter in James's place, James fled to Zaragoza and won over nobles eager to reassert their power, and Peter had to restore him as procurator general.

James died suddenly in Barcelona on 15 November 1347, widely believed poisoned on Peter's orders. Without him the Union of Aragon was crushed at Epila in 1348.

乌赫尔伯爵海梅一世（1321—1347）是阿拉贡亲王，生于萨拉戈萨，为阿拉贡国王阿方索四世与乌赫尔女伯爵特蕾莎·德·恩滕萨之子。父亲放弃继承权后，海梅继承乌赫尔伯国。

1336年，他与科曼日伯爵贝尔纳八世之女塞西尔结婚，两人育有儿子佩德罗，佩德罗后来继袭爵位。兄长佩德罗四世没有儿子，海梅因此成为王位的推定继承人。国王想让自己的女儿取代他时，海梅逃往萨拉戈萨，争取到想重振权力的贵族，佩德罗被迫让步，恢复他的总代理官之职。

1347年11月15日海梅在巴塞罗那突然去世，普遍认为他是被兄长下令毒杀。失去首领的阿拉贡联盟，1348年在埃皮拉被击溃。

James II the Just (10 April 1267 – 2 November 1327), second son of Peter III and Constance II of Sicily, was crowned King of Sicily in 1286 and in 1291 succeeded his brother Alfonso III as King of Aragon.

By the Treaty of Anagni in 1295 he gave up Sicily to the papacy and restored the Balearics to his uncle James II of Majorca; the Sicilians instead placed his brother Frederick on the island's throne. Pope Boniface VIII also granted him rights to Sardinia and Corsica, and James conquered Sardinia in 1324.

海梅二世（公正者）（1267年4月10日—1327年11月2日）是佩德罗三世与西西里的科斯坦察的次子，1286年加冕为西西里国王，1291年继其兄阿方索三世为阿拉贡国王。

John of Aragon and Foix (Joan de Prades, 1335–1414) was a younger son of Peter IV of Ribagorza and Joanna of Foix, and a grandson of James II of Aragon. In 1358 he became Count of Prades and served as seneschal of Catalonia.

After Martin I's death he was one of the claimants to the Aragonese throne, but at the Compromise of Caspe he won little support. In 1412 he recognized Ferdinand of Antequera as Ferdinand I.

Joana of Empúries (1330–1395) was the elder daughter of Ramon Berenguer I, Count of Empúries, and Blanche of Taranto, and a granddaughter of King James II of Aragon.

In 1346 she married Fernando Manuel, son of the Castilian writer Juan Manuel, at Castelló d'Empúries; he died in 1351. Their daughter Blanca Manuel, born in 1348, inherited his lordships of Escalona, Villena and Peñafiel but died in 1361. Joana herself died at Toledo in 1395.

en:
Violant of Hungary (c. 1215–1251), also called Yolanda, was queen of Aragon and the only child of King Andrew II of Hungary and Yolanda of Courtenay. She married King James I of Aragon in 1235 as his second wife, his first marriage having been annulled in 1229.

She became his trusted advisor and accompanied him on campaign. Of her ten children, Peter III inherited Aragon and James II received Majorca, while daughters Violant and Isabella became queens of Castile and France. She died in 1251 and was buried at Vallbona Abbey.

She became his trusted advisor and accompanied him on campaign. Of her ten children, #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('ara_pere_iii_arago').GetID],X #L Peter III#!#! inherited Aragon and #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('mll_jacme_ii_mallorca').GetID],X #L James II#!#! received Majorca, while daughters Violant and Isabella became queens of [GetCountry('CAS').GetName] and [GetCountry('FRA').GetName]. zh:
匈牙利的维奥朗（约1215—1251），亦名约朗德，是阿拉贡王后，匈牙利国王安德烈二世与库尔特奈的约兰德的独女。1235年，她作为第二位妻子嫁给阿拉贡国王海梅一世，海梅的前一次婚姻于1229年被撤销。

她成为丈夫信任的顾问并随军出征。她生有十个子女，其中佩德罗三世继承阿拉贡，海梅二世获得马略卡，女儿维奥朗和伊莎贝拉分别成为卡斯蒂利亚和法兰西的王后。1251年她去世，葬于巴尔沃纳修道院。

John of Aragon (1330–1358) was an infante of Aragon, the younger son of King Alfonso IV and Eleanor of Castile. After his father's death his half-brother Peter IV seized his inheritance, but restored the lordship of Elche to him in 1338.

In 1354 Peter I of Castile married him to Isabel Díaz de Haro, heiress of Biscay. He served Peter as standard-bearer in the War of the Two Peters, until Peter had him killed at Bilbao in 1358.

胡安·德·阿拉贡（1330—1358）是阿拉贡国王阿方索四世与卡斯蒂利亚的埃莉诺的幼子。父亲去世后，异母兄佩德罗四世没收了他的产业，但在1338年把埃尔切领地归还给他。

1354年卡斯蒂利亚国王佩德罗一世安排他迎娶比斯开女继承人伊莎贝尔·迪亚斯·德·阿罗。他在“两佩德罗战争”中担任佩德罗一世的掌旗官，1358年被后者派人杀死于毕尔巴鄂。

Eleanor of Castile (1307–1359) was the eldest daughter of Ferdinand IV of Castile and Constance of Portugal. Her first marriage, to the Aragonese heir James, was annulled after he took holy orders; in 1329 she married his brother, King Alfonso IV of Aragon, and was queen until his death in 1336.

She was the mother of the infantes Ferdinand and John. Back in Castile, she was killed at Castrojeriz in 1359 on the order of her nephew, King Peter I of Castile.

en:
Ausiàs March (c. 1400–1459) was a Valencian poet and knight from Gandia, born into a noble family of poets. On his father's death in 1413 he became head of the family. Knighted young, he joined Alfonso the Magnanimous on Mediterranean expeditions in 1420–1425, then settled at Gandia.

He was twice married, and in 1450 he moved to Valencia, where he died in 1459. A leading poet of the Valencian Golden Century, he wrote in Valencian rather than Occitan; 128 of his poems survive, on love, death and morality.

奥西亚斯·马尔希（约1400—1459）是甘迪亚出身的巴伦西亚诗人、骑士，生于一个爱好诗歌的贵族家庭。1413年父亲去世后他成为家族之主，很年轻时受封骑士，1420至1425年间随宽宏的阿方索远征地中海，之后定居甘迪亚。

他两度结婚，1450年迁居巴伦西亚，1459年在当地去世。他是巴伦西亚文学黄金世纪最重要的诗人之一，不用奥克语而用巴伦西亚语写作，现存128首诗，主题围绕爱情、死亡与道德。

Nissim ben Reuven of Gerona (c. 1315–1376), known by the Hebrew acronym the RaN, was a Catalan rabbi, talmudist and authority on Jewish law, born in Barcelona. He earned his living as a physician.

He served the Barcelona community as judge and teacher and founded a yeshiva there; after criticizing its wealthy leaders he was slandered and imprisoned for five months before being cleared. His pupils included Isaac ben Sheshet and Hasdai Crescas.

Peter I (c. 1068–1104), eldest son of Sancho Ramírez and Isabella of Urgell, ruled Sobrarbe and Ribagorza as a sub-king from 1085 before succeeding his father as king of Aragon and Pamplona in 1094.

He pressed the Reconquista south, routing the Taifa of Zaragoza at Alcoraz and capturing Huesca in 1095. Beside El Cid he defeated an Almoravid army at Bairén in 1096. He died on 28 December 1104, and his brother Alfonso the Battler succeeded him.

en:
Pere de Thous (c. 1295–1374) was a Valencian friar of the Order of Montesa, born at Peñíscola, who became its third grand master in 1327. The order was a young one, founded in 1317 by James II of Aragon.

In August 1330, during the War of the Strait, he and Arnau d'Alós led the heavy cavalry on a raid launched from Lorca into Granada. He remained loyal to Peter IV of Aragon in the War of the Union, when much of the Maestrat rose against him.

A notable builder, he fortified San Mateo, founded the Dominican convent there in 1360, and promoted works at the order's castles until his death in 1374.

en:
Peter II the Catholic (1178–1213) was King of Aragon and Count of Barcelona from 1196, the eldest son of Alfonso II. He married Marie of Montpellier in 1204, who bore him his heir James I.

In 1205 he was crowned in Rome by Pope Innocent III, the first Aragonese king to receive papal coronation, and placed Aragon under the Holy See. He fought at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212, then intervened against Simon de Montfort's Albigensian Crusade to protect his vassal Raymond VI of Toulouse, and was killed at Muret on 12 September 1213.

zh:
佩德罗二世（1178—1213），1196年起为阿拉贡国王兼巴塞罗那伯爵。他是阿方索二世的长子，1204年迎娶蒙彼利埃的玛丽，二人的儿子海梅是他的继承人。

1205年，他在罗马由教宗诺森三世加冕，成为首位由教宗加冕的阿拉贡国王，并将阿拉贡置于教廷治下。1212年他参加拉斯纳瓦斯·德·托洛萨会战，随后出兵对抗西蒙·德·蒙特福特率领的阿尔比十字军，以庇护附庸图卢兹伯爵雷蒙六世，最终于1213年9月12日在米雷之战中阵亡。

en:
Peter III the Great (c. 1240–1285), son of James I and Yolande of Hungary, ruled as King of Aragon and Count of Barcelona from 1276. In 1280 he defeated a Catalan noble revolt.

After the Sicilian Vespers uprising in 1282, he invaded Sicily on the Hohenstaufen claim of his wife Constance II, drove out Charles I of Anjou and was crowned king of the island. In 1283 he was forced to grant the General Privilege to the Aragonese Union.

Pope Martin IV thereupon proclaimed an Aragonese Crusade, and the French invasion of Catalonia in 1285 collapsed by land and sea. Peter died in 1285.

zh:
佩德罗三世（伟大者）（约1240—1285）是海梅一世与匈牙利的维奥朗之子，1276年起为阿拉贡国王兼巴塞罗那伯爵。1280年，他平定了加泰罗尼亚贵族的叛乱。

1282年西西里晚祷起义爆发后，他凭借妻子科斯坦察二世的霍亨斯陶芬家族继承权进军西西里，驱逐安茹的查理一世并加冕为西西里国王。1283年，他被迫向阿拉贡联盟颁布《大特权令》。

教宗马丁四世随即宣布发动阿拉贡十字军，1285年法兰西军队入侵加泰罗尼亚，在海陆两线均告溃败。佩德罗于1285年去世。

en:
Peter of Aragon and Anjou (1305 – 4 November 1381), son of James II and Blanche of Anjou, was an infante of Aragon who served three kings as soldier, diplomat and counsellor. He was Count of Ribagorza from 1322.

In 1343 he joined Peter IV's Majorca expedition. He was chief counsellor of Alfonso IV and Peter IV, and regent during Peter IV's absence in 1354–1356. In 1358 he gave up his counties and entered the Franciscans, advocating an end to the Avignon papacy in a prophetic tract.

His son Alfonso became duke of Gandia, John was a candidate for the Aragonese crown before the Compromise of Caspe, and James rose to cardinal. Peter died at Pisa in 1381.

zh:
佩德罗·德·阿拉贡-安茹（1305—1381年11月4日）是阿拉贡王子，海梅二世与安茹的布朗什之子，历事三位国王，是军人、外交官和谋臣。他于1322年受封里瓦戈萨伯爵。

1343年他参加佩德罗四世的马略卡远征。他是阿方索四世与佩德罗四世两朝的首席谋臣，1354—1356年佩德罗四世离境期间摄政。1358年他放弃伯爵领，加入方济各会，主张结束阿维尼翁教廷，并为此写了一部预言性的论著。

其子阿方索成为甘迪亚公爵，胡安在卡斯佩妥协之前是阿拉贡王位的候选人，海梅升任枢机。1381年佩德罗在比萨去世。

en:
Peter IV the Ceremonious (1319–1387), son of Alfonso IV and Teresa d'Entença, ruled the Crown of Aragon from 1336 and spent his reign fighting the noble unions that limited the crown. In 1344 he deposed James III of Majorca and took over his kingdom.

With no son, Peter tried to name his daughter Constance heir over his brother James of Urgell; when James died suddenly in 1347, many suspected poison. The Valencian Union held Peter under guard until he escaped in 1348. On 21 July 1348 he crushed the unionists at Epila, and had the Union's meeting bell melted down and poured down its leaders' throats.

From 1356 to 1375 he fought Castile in the War of the Two Peters, which ended without a winner, and in 1381 became Duke of Athens and Neopatria. He died in Barcelona, aged 67.

zh:
佩德罗四世，绰号“守礼者”（1319—1387），是阿方索四世与特蕾莎·德·恩滕萨之子，1336年起统治阿拉贡联合王国，在位期间一直与限制王权的贵族联盟周旋。1344年他废黜马略卡国王海梅三世并接管其王国。

佩德罗没有儿子，想立女儿康斯坦萨为继承人，取代弟弟乌赫尔的海梅；1347年海梅突然去世，许多人怀疑是毒杀。随后巴伦西亚联盟将佩德罗置于看管之下，直到1348年他才趁乱逃脱。1348年7月21日，他在埃皮拉之战中击溃联盟，并熔毁联盟用来召集会议的钟，把铜汁灌进联盟首领的喉咙。

1356至1375年，他与卡斯蒂利亚进行双佩德罗战争，未分胜负；1381年又成为雅典与新帕特里亚公爵。他在巴塞罗那去世，终年67岁。

en:
Petronilla (1136–1173), queen of Aragon, was the only child of King Ramiro II and Agnes of Aquitaine. Her father had taken the throne after his brother Alfonso I died childless in 1134, leaving his kingdom to military orders.

In August 1137, when little over a year old, she was betrothed at Barbastro to Count Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona, joining Aragon and the County of Barcelona into the Crown of Aragon.

After her husband died in 1162 and she abdicated in 1164, she ruled as regent for her young son Alfonso II until her death, and was the last ruler of Aragon's Jiménez dynasty.

阿拉贡女王佩德罗尼拉（1136—1173）是国王拉米罗二世与阿基坦的艾格尼丝的独女。1134年，她的伯父阿方索一世去世，没有子嗣，将王国留给军事修会，此后拉米罗继位。

1137年8月，刚满周岁的她在巴尔瓦斯特罗与巴塞罗那伯爵拉蒙·贝伦格尔四世订婚，这桩婚姻把阿拉贡和巴塞罗那伯国合并为阿拉贡联合王国。

1162年丈夫去世、1164年她退位后，以摄政身份为年幼的儿子阿方索二世主持国政，直至1173年去世。她是阿拉贡希梅纳王朝最后一位统治者。

en:
Ramiro I (before 1007–1063) was the illegitimate son of King Sancho III of Pamplona. When Sancho III divided his realm in 1035, Ramiro received the county of Aragon and ruled it as its first king, though he styled himself only son of King Sancho.

He challenged his half-brother García of Navarre and, despite defeat at Tafalla, gained territory including Sangüesa. In 1043 he annexed Sobrarbe and Ribagorza and fixed his capital at Jaca.

He married Ermesinda of Bigorre, and their son Sancho Ramírez succeeded him. Ramiro was killed attacking Graus on 8 May 1063 and was buried at San Juan de la Peña.

拉米罗一世（1007年前—1063）是潘普洛纳国王桑乔三世的私生子。1035年桑乔三世分封领地时，拉米罗得到阿拉贡伯国，成为阿拉贡的第一代国王，尽管他在文书中只自称“国王桑乔之子”。

他向同父异母兄弟纳瓦拉国王加西亚发起挑战，虽在塔法利亚战败，仍获得了包括桑圭萨在内的领地。1043年，他兼并索夫拉韦和里瓦戈萨，定都哈卡。

他娶比戈尔的埃尔梅辛达为妻，儿子桑乔·拉米雷斯继位。1063年5月8日，他在攻打格劳斯时战死，葬于圣胡安-德拉佩尼亚修道院。

en:
Ramiro II, called the Monk (1086–1157), was a son of King Sancho Ramírez of Aragon and Felicia of Roucy who became a monk and abbot. His brother Alfonso the Battler blocked his election as bishop of Burgos.

When Alfonso died in 1134, the Aragonese nobility took Ramiro from the cloister and made him king, while Navarre chose García Ramírez, separating the two realms. He had a daughter, Petronilla, who was betrothed in 1137 to Count Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona, uniting Aragon and Catalonia. He withdrew to a monastery soon after, keeping the royal title until his death.

拉米罗二世，绰号“修士”（1086—1157），是阿拉贡国王桑乔·拉米雷斯与鲁西的费利西亚之子，出家为僧，后任修道院院长。其兄阿方索一世曾阻止他当选布尔戈斯主教。

1134年阿方索去世，阿拉贡贵族把拉米罗从修道院请出立为国王，纳瓦拉则选出加西亚·拉米雷斯，两国从此分立。拉米罗之女佩德罗尼拉于1137年与巴塞罗那伯爵拉蒙·贝伦格尔四世订婚，阿拉贡与加泰罗尼亚由此联合。此后不久他退回修道院，直至去世仍保留国王头衔。

en:
Ramiro Sánchez of Monzón (c. 1070–1129/1130) was a Navarrese noble, the son of Sancho Garcés, an illegitimate son of King García Sánchez III of Navarre. After his uncle Sancho IV was killed in 1076 and Navarre was partitioned between Castile and Aragon, he was raised at the Aragonese court.

As a royal tenente he held Monzón and Tudela between 1104 and 1129. Around 1098 he married Cristina Rodríguez, a daughter of El Cid, and in 1099 escorted the Cid's body to Cardeña. His son García Ramírez succeeded him at Monzón and became king of Navarre.

蒙松的拉米罗·桑切斯（约1070—1129/1130）是纳瓦拉贵族，为纳瓦拉国王加西亚·桑切斯三世的私生子桑乔·加尔塞斯之子。1076年他的叔父桑乔四世被杀，纳瓦拉被卡斯蒂利亚与阿拉贡瓜分，他便在阿拉贡宫廷长大。

作为王室封臣，他在1104至1129年间领有蒙松和图德拉。约1098年，他与熙德的女儿克里斯蒂娜·罗德里格斯结婚，1099年护送熙德的灵柩前往卡尔德尼亚。他的儿子加西亚·拉米雷斯继承蒙松，后来成为纳瓦拉国王。

en:
Ramon Berenguer of Aragon (1308 – c. 1366) was the youngest son of James II and Blanche of Anjou. He received the County of Prades and the barony of Entença from his father in 1324. In 1334 his brother Alfonso IV gave him Elche.

In 1341 he exchanged Prades with his brother Peter for the County of Empúries. He first quarrelled with his nephew Peter IV, but Peter's mediation made him one of the king's closest men. He helped put down the Valencian revolts of 1347–1348, went to Pope Innocent VI in 1356 as envoy over Sardinia, and in 1363 defended Valencia against Peter of Castile.

In 1364 he gave Empúries to his son John, who forced him into the Dominican order. He died at Barcelona around 1366.

zh:
阿拉贡的拉蒙·贝伦格尔（1308—约1366）是海梅二世与安茹的布朗什的幼子。1324年，他从父亲手中得到普拉德斯伯爵领和恩滕萨男爵领。1334年，兄长阿方索四世把埃尔切赐给他。

1341年，他与兄长佩德罗交换领地，改任安普里亚斯伯爵。他起初与侄子佩德罗四世不睦，经兄长佩德罗调解，成为国王最亲近的臣属之一。他协助佩德罗四世平定1347—1348年的巴伦西亚叛乱，1356年作为使节前往教皇英诺森六世处商议撒丁岛事务，1363年又抵御卡斯蒂利亚国王佩德罗对巴伦西亚的进攻。

1364年，他把安普里亚斯让给儿子胡安，却被胡安强迫加入多明我会。他约1366年在巴塞罗那去世。

en:
Roger Bernard III of Foix-Castelbon (1310–1350) was the younger son of Count Gaston I of Foix and Joan of Artois. In 1315 the County of Foix passed to his elder brother Gaston II, while Roger Bernard received the Catalan viscounty of Castelbon, holding it as his brother's vassal.

By his wife Constance de Luna he fathered Roger Bernard IV and founded the Foix-Castelbon line, from which sprang the later counts Matthew and Isabella of Foix.

罗歇-贝尔纳三世·德·富瓦-卡斯泰尔邦（1310—1350）是富瓦伯爵加斯东一世与阿图瓦的让娜年纪较小的儿子。1315年，富瓦伯国传给其兄加斯东二世，罗歇-贝尔纳则得到加泰罗尼亚的卡斯泰尔邦子国，并作为兄长的封臣持有该土地。

他与卢纳的康斯坦丝结婚，生下罗歇-贝尔纳四世，开创了富瓦-卡斯泰尔邦支系，后来的富瓦伯爵马蒂厄与伊莎贝尔即出自该支。

en:
Roger Bernard IV of Foix-Castelbon (c. 1333–1381) inherited the viscounty of Castelbon from his father, Roger Bernard III, and like him held it as vassal of the ruling counts of Foix. He married Géraude de Navailles, who bore him a son, Matthew, and a daughter, Isabella.

Long overshadowed by the senior Foix line, his children inherited the County of Foix itself: Matthew succeeded Count Gaston III Fébus in 1391, and Isabella followed her brother as countess.

罗歇-贝尔纳四世·德·富瓦-卡斯泰尔邦（约1333—1381）从父亲罗歇-贝尔纳三世手中继承了卡斯泰尔邦子国，并与父亲一样作为富瓦执政伯爵的封臣持有该土地。他娶热罗德·德·纳瓦耶为妻，生子马蒂厄、女伊莎贝尔。

en:
Sancho Ramírez (c. 1042–1094) succeeded his father Ramiro I as king of Aragon in 1063. In 1067–1068 he and Sancho IV of Navarre lost to Sancho II of Castile. After Sancho IV was murdered by his siblings in 1076, Sancho Ramírez became king of Pamplona as well, ceding Navarre's western lands to Alfonso VI of Castile.

He took Barbastro, Graus and Monzón, but was routed by El Cid near Morella. He fell besieging Huesca on 4 June 1094, leaving the crown to his son Peter I.

zh:
桑乔·拉米雷斯（约1042—1094）于1063年继父亲拉米罗一世之后成为阿拉贡国王。1067至1068年，他与纳瓦拉的桑乔四世联手，却负于卡斯蒂利亚的桑乔二世。1076年，桑乔四世被自己的兄弟谋杀，桑乔·拉米雷斯兼任潘普洛纳国王，并把纳瓦拉西部领地让给卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索六世。

他攻取了巴尔瓦斯特罗、格劳斯和蒙松，却在莫雷利亚附近被熙德击败。1094年6月4日，他在围攻韦斯卡时阵亡，王位传给儿子佩德罗一世。

en:
Teresa d'Entença (c. 1300–1327) was countess of Urgell in her own right. When her granduncle Ermengol X, count of Urgell, lay dying without children, he named the infante Alfonso of Aragon his heir, on condition that Alfonso marry Teresa as his rightful successor.

The wedding was celebrated at Lleida in 1314. She died at Zaragoza on 20 October 1327 giving birth to her son Sancho, only days before her husband ascended the throne as Alfonso IV. Her son Peter IV later ruled Aragon, while James inherited Urgell.

特蕾莎·德·恩滕萨（约1300—1327）本人即拥有乌赫尔伯国的继承权。她的叔祖父、乌赫尔伯爵埃尔蒙戈尔十世无嗣，临终前立阿拉贡王子阿方索为继承人，条件是阿方索必须迎娶自己的合法继承人特蕾莎。

两人于1314年在莱里达举行婚礼。1327年10月20日，她在萨拉戈萨生下儿子桑乔时离世，距丈夫以阿方索四世之名登基只有几天。她的儿子佩德罗四世后来成为阿拉贡国王，海梅则继承了乌赫尔伯国。

en:
Vincent Ferrer (1350–1419) was a Dominican friar, ordained in 1379. During the Western Schism he backed the Avignon antipope Benedict XIII. After a vision in 1398 he preached itinerantly for two decades; his missions converted many Jews, sometimes through coercion.

In 1412 he was decisive at the Compromise of Caspe, placing Ferdinand of Antequera on the throne of Aragon. He died at Vannes in 1419 and was canonized in 1455.

文森特·费雷尔（1350—1419）是多明我会修士，1379年受任神父。西方教会大分裂期间，他支持阿维尼翁的对立教宗本笃十三世。1398年一次神视之后，他二十年间四处巡回布道；他的传教使许多犹太人改宗，其中不乏胁迫之举。

1412年，他在决定阿拉贡王位的卡斯佩妥协中起了关键作用，使安特克拉的费尔南多当选。1419年他在瓦讷去世，1455年被封圣。

en:
Violante of Aragon (October 1310–1353), born in Barcelona, was the youngest daughter of King James II of Aragon and Blanche of Anjou, who died after giving her birth. In 1328 she married Philip of Anjou, despot of Romania, a son of the prince of Taranto.

After Philip was assassinated in 1330 she returned to Catalonia. In 1339 she married Lope de Luna, lord of Segorbe, becoming countess of Luna, and died at Pedrola in 1353.

薇尔兰特·德·阿拉贡（1310年10月—1353）生于巴塞罗那，是阿拉贡国王海梅二世与安茹的布朗什的幼女，母亲在生下她后去世。1328年，她嫁给塔兰托亲王之子、罗马专制君主腓力·德·安茹。

1330年腓力遇刺后，她返回加泰罗尼亚。1339年，她改嫁塞戈尔韦领主洛佩·德·卢纳，成为卢纳伯爵夫人，1353年在佩德罗拉去世。

en:
Andreotto of Arborea (died 1308) was the elder illegitimate son of Judge John of Arborea and his mistress Vera Cappai. On his father's death in 1304 he succeeded as Judge of Arborea, ruling jointly with his brother Marianus III but holding supremacy.

In 1308, shortly before he died, he bought the castles of Serravalle di Bosa, Planargia and Costaville from the Malaspina family, and their revenues financed the administration of the giudicato's demesne.

en:
Brancaleone Doria (1337–1409), a Genoese Doria born illegitimate in Sardinia, was caught between Aragon and Arborea. In 1357 Peter IV of Aragon legitimised him and granted him his ancestral lands, including Castelgenovese and Monteleone. In 1376 he married Eleanor of Arborea, sister of Hugh III, in a political match.

After Hugh's murder in 1383, Eleanor ruled for their son Frederick, while Brancaleone went to Barcelona to negotiate peace, but was arrested and held at Cagliari until 1390.

Freed, he turned against Aragon: in 1391 he and his son Mariano took Sassari and Osilo, and in February 1392 announced that all territory held in 1388 was recovered. After Mariano died in 1407 he withdrew to Castelgenovese, where he was killed in 1409, before the Battle of Sanluri.

布兰卡莱奥内·多里亚（1337—1409）是热那亚多里亚家族的私生子，生于撒丁岛，夹在阿拉贡与阿尔博雷阿之间。1357年，阿拉贡国王佩德罗四世承认他的合法身份，并授予他祖传领地，包括卡斯特尔真诺韦塞和蒙泰莱奥内。1376年，他娶乌戈三世之妹埃莱奥诺拉，结成政治联姻。

1383年乌戈遇刺后，埃莱奥诺拉以儿子费德里科的名义摄政，布兰卡莱奥内前往巴塞罗那议和，却被捕，囚于卡利亚里直到1390年。

获释后他转而与阿拉贡为敌：1391年与儿子马里亚诺攻占萨萨里和奥西洛，1392年2月宣布已收复1388年全部领土。1407年马里亚诺去世后，他退回卡斯特尔真诺韦塞，1409年圣卢里战役前在那里被杀。

en:
Constance of Saluzzo (1314–1348), also called Costanza Del Vasto, was the daughter of Philip of Saluzzo, first governor-general of Aragonese Sardinia and Corsica, and Sibilla of Peralta. In 1328 she married Peter, eldest son of Judge Hugh II of Arborea, and when Hugh died in 1335 she became giudicessa of Arborea at her husband's side.

A devout woman, she founded the convent of Santa Chiara at Oristano, retired there after Peter III's death in 1347, and died in 1348.

科斯坦扎·迪·萨卢佐（1314—1348），又称德尔·瓦斯托，是阿拉贡治下撒丁与科西嘉首任总督萨卢佐的菲利波与佩拉尔塔的西比拉之女。1328年，她嫁给阿尔博雷阿执政官乌戈内二世的长子彼得罗；1335年乌戈内去世后，她随丈夫成为阿尔博雷阿执政官夫人。

en:
Philip of Saluzzo (c. 1266–1324) was a son of Thomas I, Marquess of Saluzzo, and Luisa of Ceva. He married Sibilla of Peralta, who bore him Constance and Raymond.

After the Aragonese conquest of 1323–1324 he became the first Governor General of the Kingdom of Sardinia and Corsica for the Crown of Aragon. His daughter Constance married the future Judge Peter III of Arborea, allying his house with the giudicato's ruling family. Philip died in 1324, the year of his appointment.

en:
John, called Chiano (died 23 March 1304), was Judge of Arborea from 1297, succeeding his father Marianus II. In 1287 he married Giacomina, daughter of the Pisan noble Ugolino della Gherardesca.

After Gallura fell in 1288, Arborea was the only giudicato left on Sardinia. Pope Boniface VIII created the Kingdom of Sardinia and Corsica for James II of Aragon. Preparing to resist, John ceded to Pisa in 1300 his third of Cagliari, the silver mines and part of the royal demesne.

Alienating public land provoked a popular revolt, and rebels killed and mutilated him. His sons Andrew and Marianus, born of his relationship with Vera Cappai, succeeded him.

乔瓦尼，绰号“基亚诺”（?—1304年3月23日），自1297年起任阿尔博雷亚执政官，继其父马里亚努斯二世之位。1287年，他迎娶比萨贵族乌戈利诺·德拉·盖拉尔代斯卡之女贾科米娜。

1288年加卢拉被废后，阿尔博雷亚成为撒丁岛仅存的判官领。教皇卜尼法斯八世设立撒丁与科西嘉王国，将其封给阿拉贡的海梅二世。为备战，乔瓦尼于1300年把治下三分之一的卡利亚里、银矿和部分王领割让给比萨。

出让公地激起民变，叛乱者将他杀死并肢解。他与维拉·卡帕伊所生的儿子安德鲁和马里亚努斯继位。

en:
John of Arborea, Giovanni de Serra Bas (1320–1376), was a younger son of Judge Hugh II of Arborea and Benedetta, raised at the Barcelona court of Alfonso IV of Aragon. In 1338 Peter IV of Aragon enfeoffed him with Bosa and Monteacuto.

Through purchases he built up an estate in Gallura and traded in grain, becoming the kingdom's wealthiest feudatory outside his ruling brother. His quarrels with Judge Marianus IV proved fatal: he was imprisoned in 1349 and died in captivity in 1376.

阿尔博雷亚的乔瓦尼（全名乔瓦尼·德·塞拉巴斯，1320—1376）是阿尔博雷亚执政官乌戈内二世与贝内代塔年纪较小的儿子，在阿拉贡国王阿方索四世的巴塞罗那宫廷长大。1338年，阿拉贡国王佩德罗四世将博萨和蒙泰阿库托封给他。

他购入加卢拉的大片地产，又经营粮食贸易，成为王国内仅次于执政官兄长的最富封臣。他与马里亚诺四世反目，1349年被囚禁，1376年死于狱中。

en:
Guido Cattaneo (died by 1339) was a Dominican, probably of Tuscan origin, who was archbishop of Arborea from 1312. Pope John XXII empowered him to pursue clergy withholding tithes, even by excommunication.

In 1322 he went to Avignon as Hugh II's ambassador and pledged backing for James II of Aragon's conquest of Pisan Sardinia, on condition that Arborea keep its sovereignty as an Aragonese vassal paying 3000 florins a year. In 1328 he took Hugh's son Peter to Zaragoza to swear vassalage to Alfonso IV. When Peter became judge in 1335, Guido served as his chancellor.

His one known writing, a treatise defending the pope's line on evangelical poverty, is the judgeship's only surviving 14th-century work. He last appears in Hugh II's will of 1335 and was dead by 1339.

圭多·卡塔内奥（1339年前去世）是可能出身托斯卡纳的多明我会修士，自1312年起任阿尔博雷阿大主教。教皇约翰二十二世授权他追缴神职人员拖欠的什一税，必要时可处以绝罚。

1322年，他作为法官乌戈内二世的使节前往阿维尼翁，承诺支持海梅二世征服比萨人控制的撒丁岛，条件是阿尔博雷阿作为阿拉贡封臣、每年缴纳3000枚弗罗林，但保有主权。1328年，他带着乌戈内二世的儿子彼得前往萨拉戈萨，向阿方索四世宣誓效忠。1335年彼得继位为法官后，他出任宰相。

他仅存的著作是一本为教皇的福音清贫主张辩护的小册子，也是阿尔博雷阿14世纪唯一传世的作品。他最后见于1335年乌戈内二世的遗嘱，1339年前已经去世。

en:
Marianus II (died 1297) was Judge of Arborea from 1241, succeeding his father Peter II as a child under the regency of William of Capraia. After William died in 1264, Marianus shared power with his son Nicholas; in 1270 he imprisoned Nicholas, and had him killed in 1274.

From 1274 he campaigned in Cagliari and Logudoro. A Pisan citizen from 1265, he nevertheless called in Peter III of Aragon against Cagliari in 1284. He was wounded at the siege of Villa di Chiesa and died in 1297, succeeded by his son John.

马里亚努斯二世（?—1297）自1241年起任阿尔博雷亚执政官，父亲彼得二世去世时他年幼，由卡普拉亚的威廉摄政。1264年威廉去世后，他与威廉之子尼古拉共治；1270年他囚禁尼古拉，并于1274年将其杀死。

自1274年起，他连年征战卡利亚里和洛古多罗。他自1265年起拥有比萨公民权，却在1284年召请阿拉贡的佩德罗三世出兵对付卡利亚里。他在围攻基耶萨镇时负伤，1297年去世，其子约翰继位。

en:
Marianus III (died 1321) was Judge of Arborea, an illegitimate son of Judge John and Vera Cappai. He co-ruled with his elder brother Andreotto from 1304, ruling alone from about 1310. In 1312 Pisa forced him to buy his succession rights from the Emperor Henry VII and to marry Constance of Montalcino by proxy; he never did, and lived instead with Padulesa de Serra, who bore him six children, including his successor Hugh II.

In 1314 he sought Aragonese aid against Pisa. He restored roads and bridges and completed the walls and towers of Oristano.

马里亚诺三世·迪·阿尔博雷阿（？—1321）是阿尔博雷阿法官，为法官乔瓦尼与薇拉·卡帕伊的私生子。1304年起他与兄长安德烈奥托共同执政，约1310年起单独统治。1312年，比萨共和国迫使他向皇帝亨利七世购买继承权，并要他与蒙塔尔奇诺的科斯坦察订立代理婚姻；他始终未娶她，而与帕杜莱萨·德·塞拉同居，育有六个孩子，包括继承人雨果二世。

1314年他向阿拉贡王冠求援以对抗比萨，又修复道路与桥梁，主持完成奥里斯塔诺的城墙与塔楼。

en:
Marianus IV (1317–1375), called the Great, was the second son of Judge Hugh II of Arborea and Benedetta. He married Timbora of Rocabertí in 1336, and in 1339 Peter IV made him count of Goceano and Marmilla. There he repopulated Burgos and issued the rural code later absorbed into his daughter Eleanor's Carta de Logu.

Proclaimed judge in 1347 after his brother Peter III died, he went to war with the Catalans. Peter IV sent nearly twelve thousand men in 1354 and gained little, and peace came at Sanluri in 1355.

When fighting resumed in 1365 Marianus besieged Cagliari and took Villa di Chiesa; in 1368 he and his son Hugh destroyed a Catalan army at Oristano. When he died in May 1375, nearly all Sardinia was Arborea's.

马里亚诺四世（1317—1375），人称“伟大者”，是阿尔博雷阿法官乌戈内二世与贝内代塔的次子。1336年他娶罗卡贝尔蒂的廷博尔为妻，1339年被佩德罗四世封为戈切阿诺和马尔米拉伯爵。他在当地让布尔戈斯重新有人定居，并颁布乡村法典，后来被女儿埃莱奥诺拉的《洛古宪章》吸收。

1347年兄长彼得三世去世后，他被立为法官，随即与加泰罗尼亚人开战。1354年佩德罗四世派来近一万二千人，收效甚微，双方于1355年在圣卢里议和。

1365年战事重启，马里亚诺围攻卡利亚里，攻占基耶萨镇；1368年他与儿子乌戈在奥里斯塔诺城下围歼一支加泰罗尼亚军队。1375年5月他去世时，撒丁岛几乎全归阿尔博雷阿所有。

en:
Peter II (died 1241) was Judge of Arborea, the son of Judge Hugh I and Preziosa of the Massa family of Cagliari. He inherited the throne as a child in 1211 and was compelled by Ubaldo Visconti to marry his daughter Diana. In 1228 rivals William II of Cagliari and Marianus II of Torres defeated him and forced him to share his giudicato, though he later regained full control.

In 1237 he became a vassal of the papacy, promising an annual tribute and the castle of Giripala in return for papal recognition of his sovereignty. He died in 1241, leaving young Marianus II as heir.

en:
Peter III (c. 1314–1347), eldest son of Hugh II and Benedetta of the Serra-Bas house, became Judge of Arborea in 1335. Around 1326 Peter married Constance, daughter of Philip of Saluzzo, the first Aragonese governor of Sardinia.

His reign was uneventful and run by his chancellor Guido Cattaneo, Archbishop of Arborea. In 1336 his brother Marianus did homage to Peter IV of Aragon on his behalf and received the County of Goceano.

In 1343 Pope Clement VI allowed Peter to found a convent of Poor Clares at Oristano. He died in 1347 with Constance childless, and Marianus succeeded him.

彼得三世·迪·阿尔博雷阿（约1314—1347）是塞拉-巴斯家族的乌戈内二世与贝内代塔的长子，1335年起任阿尔博雷阿法官。约1326年，彼得娶了撒丁首任阿拉贡总督萨卢佐的菲利波之女科斯坦察。

他在位期间事迹平淡，国政由宰相兼阿尔博雷阿大主教圭多·卡塔内奥主持。1336年，其弟马里亚诺代他向阿拉贡的佩德罗四世行臣服礼，受封戈切阿诺伯爵领。

en:
Timbor of Rocabertí (1318–1364) was a Catalan noblewoman who sided with Sardinia against her own countrymen. Daughter of Viscount Dalmau VII of Rocabertí, she married Marianus of Arborea in 1336 at the Aragonese court in Barcelona; the couple lived at Molins de Rei, where Hugh III and Eleanor of Arborea were born.

When Marianus became judge in 1347 she moved to Oristano and backed his war against Aragon without reserve. He often made her regent during campaigns and sent her as ambassadress, and at Alghero she mediated with her kinsman, the Aragonese admiral Bernat de Cabrera.

She gave generously to the monastery of Santa Chiara, and Pope Innocent VI let her and her daughters enter its cloister seven times a year. She died in 1364, before her son and daughter came to power.

廷博尔·德·罗卡韦蒂（1318—1364）是加泰罗尼亚贵族女子，却站在撒丁一边，对抗自己的同胞。她是罗卡韦蒂子爵达尔马乌七世之女。1336年她在巴塞罗那的阿拉贡宫廷嫁给阿尔博雷阿的马里亚诺，夫妻住在莫林斯德雷，乌戈内三世和埃莱奥诺拉就在那里出生。

1347年马里亚诺继任法官后，她迁居奥里斯塔诺，毫无保留地支持丈夫对阿拉贡的战争。丈夫出征时常让她摄政，也派她出使；在阿尔盖罗，她与亲戚、阿拉贡海军统帅贝尔纳特·德·卡夫雷拉斡旋调停。

她慷慨资助圣基亚拉修院，教皇英诺森六世准许她和女儿们每年七次进入修院的内院。1364年她去世，没能看到儿子和女儿掌权。

Ugone I (1178–1211) was giudice of Arborea, son of Sinispella and Hugh Ponç, viscount of Bas. In 1185, aged seven, he succeeded his grandfather under the regency of Ramon de Torroja. A compromise at Oristano in 1192 made Peter di Serra co-judge, but William I of Cagliari invaded in 1195 and captured Peter, forcing Ugone to make peace and cede Arborea.

He reclaimed Bas in 1198 and married William's daughter Preziosa in 1206. He styled himself king of Sardinia. He died at Oristano in 1211, succeeded by his son Peter II.

en:
Ugone II (died 1335) was Judge of Arborea from 1321, the illegitimate son of Marianus III and Padulesa de Serra. He became vassal of James II of Aragon, whom the pope had invested with Sardinia and Corsica in exchange for renouncing Sicily, hoping to rule the island as the Catalan crown's governor. In 1323–1324 he aided the future Alfonso IV's conquest, which expelled Pisa from Sardinia.

With his wife Benedetta he had nine children. He died of illness at Sardara on 5 April 1335 and was succeeded by his son Peter III.

Hugh III of Arborea (c. 1337–1383) was the eldest son of Judge Marianus IV. He succeeded his father in 1375 as judge of Arborea and count of Goceano, and continued Marianus's wars against Peter IV of Aragon, allying in 1377 with Louis I of Anjou.

A praised lawgiver, he helped complete the Carta de Logu. In 1383 he and his heiress Benedetta were murdered in a revolt at Oristano; his sister Eleanor then took power as regent for his nephew Frederick.

en:
Walter VI of Brienne (c. 1304–1356), called the Duke of Athens, was heir to a duchy he never ruled. When his father Walter V fell at Halmyros in 1311, he inherited Brienne, Lecce and Conversano, but the Catalan Company had overrun the Duchy of Athens, leaving him only Argos and Nauplia.

In 1330 Pope John XXII issued a crusading bull for him. His expedition of 1331–1332 seized Leucas and Vonitsa, but the Catalans refused battle and withdrew behind the walls of Thebes and Athens, and he returned deeper in debt.

In 1342, amid a severe economic crisis, the Florentines made him signore, but a conspiracy ended his harsh rule after ten months. As Constable of France he fell at Poitiers on 19 September 1356; his sister's sons inherited his titles.

en:
Isabella of Brienne (c. 1305–1360), called the Beautiful Helen, was the daughter of Walter V of Brienne, Duke of Athens. After her father was killed by Catalan mercenaries in 1311, her mother fled with her to France. About 1321 she married Walter III of Enghien and bore him thirteen children; she was widowed in 1345.

When her brother Walter VI fell at Poitiers in 1356, she succeeded as countess of Brienne and titular duchess of Athens. She divided her inheritance among her children; Sohier received Brienne, and she died in 1360.

布里耶纳的伊莎贝尔（约1305—1360），绰号“俊美的海伦”，是雅典公爵戈蒂埃五世·德·布里耶纳之女。1311年，她的父亲被加泰罗尼亚佣兵杀死，母亲带着她逃回法国。约1321年，她嫁给戈蒂埃三世·德·昂吉安，育有十三个子女，1345年丧夫。

1356年，她的兄长戈蒂埃六世在普瓦捷战役阵亡，她遂承袭为布里耶纳女伯爵和名义上的雅典女公爵。她生前将继承的财产分给子女，西热获得布里耶纳；她于1360年去世。

en:
John of Enghien (died 1380) was the third son of Walter III of Enghien and Isabella of Brienne. In 1356 he inherited from his uncle Walter VI the county of Lecce and the Greek lordships of Vonitsa and Lefkada, lost to Leonardo Tocco by 1373.

After his brother Sohier was executed in 1364 he waged a revenge war against Albert of Bavaria until peace in 1367. In 1370 he and his brother Louis planned to retake Athens from the Catalans, but Venice refused aid and the expedition never sailed. He died in 1380.

让·德·昂吉安（？—1380）是戈蒂埃三世·德·昂吉安与伊莎贝尔·德·布里耶纳的第三子。1356年，他从舅父戈蒂埃六世手中继承了莱切伯国以及希腊的沃尼察和莱夫卡扎领地，到1373年这两处领地已被莱奥纳尔多·托科夺取。

en:
Louis of Enghien (died 1394), a son of Walter III of Enghien and Isabella of Brienne, received Conversano when his mother divided Walter VI of Brienne's inheritance. In 1370–1371 Philip II of Taranto made him bailli of the Principality of Achaea; he vainly asked Venice for help retaking Athens from the Catalan Company.

In 1381 his childless nephew's death made him Count of Brienne, Lord of Enghien and titular Duke of Athens. He helped found Charles III's Order of the Ship and died at Conversano in 1394, leaving daughters.

路易·德·昂吉安（？—1394）是戈蒂埃三世·德·昂吉安与伊莎贝尔·德·布里耶纳之子。母亲分配其舅戈蒂埃六世·德布里耶纳的遗产时，他得到了普利亚的孔韦尔萨诺。1370—1371年，塔兰托亲王菲利波二世任命他为亚该亚侯国摄政；他曾请求威尼斯出兵，协助从加泰罗尼亚佣兵团手中收复雅典，但没有结果。

1381年，他无嗣的侄子去世，他由此成为布里耶纳伯爵、昂吉安领主和名义上的雅典公爵。他是查理三世创立的船舰骑士团创始骑士之一，1394年于孔韦尔萨诺去世，身后只留下女儿。

en:
Beatrice of Taranto (1305–1340) was a daughter of Philip I of Anjou, prince of Taranto, by his wife Thamar Angelina Komnene of Epirus. In 1325 she married Walter VI of Brienne, titular duke of Athens.

Her claims in Epirus helped finance Walter's anti-Catalan crusade of 1331 to 1332, which seized Leucas and Vonitsa but failed against Athens. As his wife she held the lordship of Argos. Their young son died in childhood, and Beatrice died in 1340.

塔兰托的贝阿特丽切（1305—1340）是塔兰托亲王安茹的菲利波一世与原配伊庇鲁斯的塔玛尔·安杰利娜·科穆宁之女。1325年，她嫁给名义上的雅典公爵戈蒂埃六世·德布里耶纳。

en:
Sohier of Enghien (1324–1364), son of Walter III of Enghien and Isabella of Brienne, became lord of Enghien in 1345. When his mother divided the inheritance of her brother Walter VI of Brienne, he received the counties of Brienne and Conversano and the titular duchy of Athens, and succeeded Walter as constable of France.

Captured amid the feuds of Hainaut, he was beheaded without trial at Le Quesnoy on 21 March 1364 on the orders of Albert of Bavaria.

en:
Walter III of Enghien (1302–1345) was a Brabançon knight, lord of Enghien in Hainaut, son of Walter II and Yolande of Flanders. In January 1321 he married Isabella of Brienne, heiress to the Brienne claims in Frankish Greece.

He campaigned in Scotland as an ally of Edward III of England against Robert Bruce, and in 1343 attended the festivities founding the Order of the Garter. He died on 16 October 1345, leaving many children, among them Sohier and Louis.

戈蒂埃三世·德·昂吉安（1302—1345）是布拉班特骑士、埃诺的昂吉安领主，戈蒂埃二世与佛兰德的约兰德之子。1321年1月，他迎娶布里耶纳家族在法兰克希腊领地主张的女继承人伊莎贝尔·德·布里耶纳。

en:
Arghun (1258–10 March 1291), son of Abaqa, was the fourth Ilkhan of Persia, ruling from 1284, when he overthrew his uncle Ahmad Tekuder. A Buddhist tolerant of Christians, between 1285 and 1290 he sent embassies to the Pope and to France and England, seeking in vain a joint campaign against the Mamluks.

In 1289 he executed the all-powerful Buqa and made the Jewish physician Sa'ad al-Dawla his vizier. After taking an alchemical sulphur-and-mercury elixir he fell ill and died in March 1291. His sons Ghazan and Öljeitü later reigned.

阿鲁浑（1258—1291年3月10日）是阿八哈之子，1284年推翻叔父阿合马·帖古迭儿后继任伊儿汗国第四代君主。他笃信佛教，对基督教徒宽容，1285至1290年间多次遣使觐见教皇以及法国、英格兰国王，徒劳地谋求结盟共讨马穆鲁克。

en:
Ariq Böke (c. 1219–1266) was the youngest son of Tolui and Sorghaghtani Beki, grandson of Genghis Khan. After Möngke died in August 1259, Ariq Böke guarded the Mongol capital Karakorum, and in April 1260 he was proclaimed great khan there, weeks after Kublai's enthronement at Kaiping.

The rival elections opened the Toluid Civil War, pitting steppe traditionalists behind him against Kublai's North Chinese princes. Driven into the Ili valley, he surrendered to Kublai in August 1264, was pardoned, and died at Karakorum in 1266.

en:
Min Hti (c. 1270s–c. 1373/1374) was king of Launggyet Arakan, credited by the chronicles with a reign of 106 years, the longest reputed in history; modern scholars allow about 95 or fewer. The chronicles say his father Min Bilu, hearing prophecies about the boy, had him thrown into the Lemro River, but fishermen rescued him.

After Min Bilu was murdered by the usurper Sithabin I, ministers executed the usurper and in about 1279 acclaimed the nine-year-old Min Hti. He repelled the Shans in 1294, and in 1334 sent an army over the Arakan Mountains to take Thayet, founding the town of Ann around 1335 on the way home.

He died without a legitimate heir and an illegitimate son succeeded; the line of his son Thinhse later produced Min Saw Mon, founder of Mrauk U.

敏梯（约1270年代—约1373/1374）是隆邑时期的若开国王，编年史称他在位106年，为传说中史上在位最久的君主，现代学者则认为至多约95年。据编年史，父亲敏比卢听闻关于这孩子的预言，下令把他抛进莱穆罗河，渔民却把他救起。

敏比卢被篡位者悉达宾一世杀害后，大臣们处死篡位者，约1279年拥立九岁的敏梯为王。他于1294年击退掸人；1334年他派军越过若开山脉袭取德耶，回师途中于约1335年兴建安城。

他死后无嫡子，一名私生子继位；其子提恩塞这一支后来出了妙乌城的奠基者明绍蒙。

en:
Avag Zakarian, son of Ivane I, succeeded his father as atabeg in 1227 and was later raised to amirspasalar, ruling Georgia's eastern lands. During the Mongol invasion of 1238–1239 he was besieged at the fortress of Kayan and became the first Caucasian prince to surrender, paying tribute and joining his troops to the Mongol army; Ani fell soon after.

In 1243 he arranged Queen Rusudan's submission to the Great Khan, and in 1245–1250 he commanded one of Georgia's eight Mongol districts. He died in 1250, leaving a daughter, Khoshak.

Ivane I Zakarian was the younger brother of Zakare II and, as atabeg, the highest officer of Queen Tamar's Georgia. With Zakare he took Dvin in 1193 and Ani around 1199, and around 1200 adopted the Chalcedonian faith.

Captured at Ahlat in 1208, he was freed after a ransom and the surrender of his daughter Tamta to the Ayyubids. After Zakare's death in 1212 he declined the amirspasalar title. Defeated at Garni in 1225, he died in 1227 and was succeeded by his son Avag.

Ivane II Zakarian was a 13th-century Zakarid noble and mandaturtukhutsesi, the chief mandator of the Georgian court, and a son of Shahnshah I of Ani. When David VII rose against the Mongols in 1260, Ivane took the Khan's side.

Around 1271–1272 he accompanied Demetrius II to the Ilkhan court for coronation, and in 1288 he campaigned with Demetrius against Arghun Khan. His decree freeing the peasants of Koshi from taxes is inscribed on the church near Yerevan.

Jacob II (Hakob II Anavarzetsi, died 1359) was Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church from 1327 to 1341 and again from 1355 to 1359. A nephew of Gregory VII, he clashed with King Leo IV during a Mamluk invasion; when he threatened the king with the church's vengeance, Leo had him deposed and Mukhitar elected.

In 1347 Constantine II sent him to the pope in Avignon. Restored after Mukhitar's death in 1355, he died four years later.

Shahnshah I Zakarian was born in 1197, the son of Zakare II, from whom he inherited Ani in 1212. Raised by his uncle Ivane I and converted to the Chalcedonian faith, he ruled Ani as amirspasalar.

He defended Ani against the Mongols in 1238–1239. In 1255 William of Rubruck found him ruling fifteen cities, and he later campaigned with the Mongols at Mayyafariqin. In 1261 his son Zakare III was executed by the Mongols; ransomed, he died the same year and was buried at Kobayr.

Shahnshah II Zakarian was the son of Ivane II and grandson of Shahnshah I, and was atabeg and amirspasalar of Georgia. He joined the Mongol punitive expedition against King David VIII, and was sent as envoy to Beka I Jaqeli of Samtskhe to arrange the upbringing of Prince George, later George V.

He died in 1320: in an inscription at Ani's Church of the Holy Apostles his widow Kuandze mourns him and, with their son Zakare IV, records a tax remission.

en: Zakare I Zakarian was an Armenian landholder in the Kingdom of Georgia during the reign of King Demetrius I (1125–1156). He belonged to the Zakarid-Mkhargrdzeli line, held estates in Lower Kartli as a vassal of the powerful Orbeli family, and was the chief patron of the Haghpat Monastery. His son Sargis became amirspasalar, commander-in-chief of the Georgian army.

en:
Zakare II Zakarian was amirspasalar, commander-in-chief of the Georgian army under Queen Tamar, and elder son of Sargis Zakarian. He fought for George III against the Orbeli revolt of 1177.

With his brother Ivane he took Dvin in 1193, won Shamkor in 1195 and Basian in 1203, and captured Ani from the Shaddadids around 1199. In 1210 he raided Iran as far as Qazvin. He died in 1212, leaving Ani to his son Shahanshah.

扎卡列二世·扎卡良是塔玛尔女王麾下的阿米尔拉斯帕萨拉尔，即格鲁吉亚军队总司令，也是萨尔吉斯·扎卡良的长子。1177年，他为吉奥尔基三世征讨奥尔贝利家族叛乱。

en:
Zakare III Zakarian was amirspasalar of Georgia under King David VII and the eldest son of Shahnshah I, ruler of Ani. He was a leading architect of Georgia's alliance with Hulegu Khan and fought in the Mongol siege and sack of Baghdad in 1258.

When David VII rebelled in 1260 rather than march against the Mamluks, Zakare left without the Mongol general's knowledge to visit his wife, who was with her rebel father. Hulegu had him put in chains, and he was executed in 1261.

扎卡列三世·扎卡良是格鲁吉亚国王大卫七世麾下的阿米尔拉斯帕萨拉尔，也是阿尼统治者沙罕沙一世的长子。他是格鲁吉亚与旭烈兀汗结盟的主要促成者之一，并于1258年参加蒙古围攻、洗劫巴格达之役。

en:
Zakare IV Zakarian was the Zakarid prince who ruled Ani from 1320 to 1333 under Il-Khanid suzerainty. He was the son of Shahnshah II and his wife Kuandze, and held the Georgian rank of amirspasalar.

In 1320 he and his widowed mother set up an inscription at Ani's Church of the Holy Apostles, waiving the counting of cows and donkeys and the entry permits on their estate for his dead father's salvation.

en:
Arpa Ke'un (died 1336) ruled Persia as Ilkhan from 1335 to 1336. A descendant of Hulagu's brother Ariq Böke, he was placed on the throne by vizier Ghiyas al-Din after Abu Sa'id died heirless.

He defeated an invasion by Özbeg of the Golden Horde, executed Abu Sa'id's former wife Baghdad Khatun, and married his sister Sati Beg. Preferring Genghis Khan's Yasa to Islam, he was challenged by Ali Padshah, whose puppet Musa defeated him in 1336; Arpa was captured and killed on 15 May 1336.

阿儿巴（？—1336）于1335至1336年统治波斯，称伊儿汗。他是旭烈兀之弟阿里不哥的后裔，在不赛因无嗣而死后由宰相吉亚斯丁扶上汗位。

他击退钦察汗国月即别的入侵，处死不赛因的前妻巴格达·哈敦，又娶不赛因之妹撒迪别。他推崇成吉思汗的《大札撒》而不重伊斯兰法，后遭阿里·帕沙挑战，后者所立的傀儡木撒于1336年将其击败。阿儿巴被俘，于5月15日被杀。

en:
Amicie de Courtenay (1250–1275) was a French noblewoman of the Capetian House of Courtenay. Her father Peter of Courtenay fell at the Battle of Mansurah in 1250 during the Seventh Crusade.

She married Robert II, Count of Artois, and bore three children, Mahaut, Philip and Robert, the last of whom died in infancy. Amicie died in 1275, aged twenty-five, and her estates, including Conches, passed to her son Philip of Artois.

Blanche of Brittany (c. 1270/1271 – 1328) was the daughter of Duke John II of Brittany and Beatrice of England, granddaughter of Henry III. In 1281 she married Philip of Artois, the Artois heir. Her seven children included Margaret, Robert III of Artois, Joan and Marie.

Philip died in 1298 of wounds received at Furnes, and Artois went to his sister Mahaut rather than to Blanche's son Robert. Her long widowhood was spent at the French court, and she died at Vincennes in 1328.

en:
Gerard de Dainville (c. 1328–1378) was a prelate of the Empire from a noble Artois family; his brother Jean served the French kings John II and Charles V. He became bishop of Arras in 1361, moved to Thérouanne in 1369 and to Cambrai in 1371, entering the city solemnly on 8 May 1372.

There he invested Albert of Bavaria with the county of Hainaut on Emperor Charles IV's authority. In December 1377 he received Charles IV at Cambrai; Charles V did not want him to celebrate Christmas publicly in France, so he kept it in Gerard's cathedral. In 1378 Gerard promised obedience to the archbishop of Reims, but died that June before he could make good.

热拉尔·德·丹维尔（约1328—1378）是神圣罗马帝国境内的高级教士，出身阿图瓦的贵族家庭，其兄让·德·丹维尔曾侍奉法王约翰二世与查理五世。他1361年任阿拉斯主教，1369年改任泰鲁阿讷主教，1371年调任康布雷主教，1372年5月8日举行隆重入城礼。

在康布雷，他奉皇帝查理四世之命，为巴伐利亚的阿尔布雷希特行埃诺伯爵册封礼。1377年12月，他在康布雷迎接查理四世；法王查理五世不愿皇帝在法国公开过圣诞节，皇帝便在热拉尔的座堂里过节。1378年，热拉尔向兰斯大主教表示服从，却在同年6月去世，未及兑现。

en:
Mahaut of Artois (1268–1329), also called Mathilda, was the daughter of Count Robert II of Artois and in 1291 married Otto IV, Count of Burgundy. On her father's death in 1302 she inherited Artois by proximity of blood and ruled it for twenty-seven years against the claims of her nephew Robert III.

The Parlement of Paris repeatedly upheld her rights, and she crushed noble revolts. She governed the County of Burgundy as regent for her daughter Joan II from 1303 to 1315.

Her daughters Joan and Blanche married kings Philip V and Charles IV of France, and in 1316 she was accused of poisoning Louis X. She died on 27 November 1329.

阿图瓦的玛奥（1268—1329），又名玛蒂尔德，是阿图瓦伯爵罗贝尔二世之女，1291年嫁给勃艮第伯爵奥东四世。1302年父亲去世后，她凭近亲继承权取得阿图瓦，统治二十七年，屡次挫败侄儿罗贝尔三世提出的继承要求。

巴黎高等法院多次维护她的权利，她也平定了贵族的叛乱。1303至1315年，她代女儿让娜二世摄政勃艮第伯国。

她的两个女儿让娜和布朗什分别嫁给法王腓力五世和查理四世；1316年她被指控毒杀路易十世。她于1329年11月27日去世。

en:
Philip of Artois (1269–1298), lord of Conches, Nonancourt and Domfront, was the elder son of Count Robert II of Artois and Amicie de Courtenay. In November 1281 he married Blanche of Brittany, and in August 1284 he was knighted alongside the future King Philip IV.

He inherited his mother's Norman estates and disputed their division with his sister Mahaut until their father intervened in 1296. In 1291 a court granted him a share of John de Sully's estate.

During the Franco-Flemish War he was wounded at Bulskamp near Furnes on 20 August 1297 and nearly captured until his father rescued him. He never recovered and died on 11 September 1298.

阿图瓦的菲利普（1269—1298）是阿图瓦伯爵罗贝尔二世与阿米西·德·库特奈的长子，领有孔什、诺南库尔和栋弗龙。1281年11月，他迎娶布列塔尼的布朗什；1284年8月，他与后来的法王腓力四世一同受封骑士。

他继承了母亲在诺曼底的地产，并与姐姐玛奥就其分配长期争执，直至1296年父亲出面调解。1291年，法庭将让·德·苏利的一份遗产判给菲利普。

佛兰德斯战争期间，他于1297年8月20日在弗尔讷附近的布尔斯坎普之战中身负重伤、险些被俘，幸由父亲救出。他始终未能痊愈，于1298年9月11日去世。

Robert I of Artois (25 September 1216 – 8 February 1250) was the first Count of Artois, a younger son of Louis VIII of France. He received Artois as his appanage in 1237 and married Matilda of Brabant.

In 1240 Pope Gregory IX offered him the imperial crown against Frederick II, but he refused. On the Seventh Crusade with his brother Louis IX, he charged into Mansourah with Templars and English troops without the king's knowledge; on 8 February 1250 he was trapped in the narrow streets and killed. His posthumous son Robert II succeeded.

阿图瓦伯爵罗贝尔一世（1216年9月25日—1250年2月8日）是法王路易八世较年幼的儿子，阿图瓦首任伯爵。1237年他领有阿图瓦作为封邑，并娶布拉班特的玛蒂尔德为妻。

en:
Robert II (September 1250 – 11 July 1302), posthumous son of Robert I, was Count of Artois and a trusted commander under his cousin Philip III of France and Philip IV. In 1285 he served as regent of Angevin Naples during the War of the Sicilian Vespers, while Charles II was an Aragonese prisoner, and he rebuilt the treasury and the navy.

Sent against a Flemish revolt, he led French cavalry at the Battle of the Golden Spurs on 11 July 1302; his knights bogged down in the marshes and he was killed. His daughter Mahaut inherited Artois.

罗贝尔二世（1250年9月—1302年7月11日）是罗贝尔一世的遗腹子、阿图瓦伯爵，也是堂兄法王腓力三世及其子腓力四世倚重的将领。1285年，西西里晚祷战争期间，那不勒斯的查理二世被阿拉贡囚禁，他出任安茹家族那不勒斯王国摄政，并重建国库与海军。

1302年他奉命镇压佛兰德斯起义，7月11日率法国骑兵投入金马刺战役；骑士陷入沼泽，他本人战死，阿图瓦由其女玛奥继承。

Tommaso I Malaspina was an Italian noble of the Spino Secco branch of the Malaspina family, the son of Federico I Malaspina of Villafranca and Agnese del Bosco, an heiress of the Aleramic dynasty.

From his mother's inheritance he held the Monferrato fief of Cremolino and a co-lordship over Ovada, and he founded the Malaspina di Cremolino line. Tommaso died in 1309 and was succeeded by his son Isnardo I.

Amanieu d'Astarac (died c. 1326) was heir to Astarac but never ruled it. A younger son of Bernard V and Mathe de Foix, he was destined for the Church, receiving a Valenciennes canonry and archdeaconry from Clement V in 1311. In 1317 he married Cécile de Comminges.

In 1320 a brawl at Mirande brought reprisals on the town, and Amanieu sought Pope John XXII's intercession. He died in Cyprus c. 1326 before his father; his son Centule IV inherited the county.

en:
Arnold I, also called Arnaud-Garcia and nicknamed Nonnat, was the first Count of Astarac. The youngest son of Duke García II Sánchez of Gascony, he received Astarac when his father's duchy was divided around 920, while his brothers took Gascony and Fézensac.

His county lay between Fézensac and Bigorre and included Pardiac and Magnoac. He is attested in charters as count from 920 to 952 and was dead by 960, when his son Garcia Arnaud succeeded him.

阿尔诺一世（又名阿尔诺-加西亚，绰号“诺纳”）是第一代阿斯塔拉克伯爵。他是加斯科涅公爵加西亚二世·桑切斯的幼子，约在920年父亲的公国被诸子瓜分时分得阿斯塔拉克，他的兄弟们分别得到加斯科涅和弗藏萨克。

en:
Arnaud II (died c. 1023) was the second count of Astarac in Gascony, the son and successor of Count Garsie-Arnaud, called Arnaud I. His line descended from Garcie II the Bent, who had received the Astarac district as an appanage around 920. Arnaud married Talaise, who bore him seven children.

His eldest son William succeeded him as count around 1023. Another son, Odon, became archbishop of Auch, while Bernard held the county of Pardiac.

长子纪尧姆约于1023年继位。另一子奥东出任欧什大主教，贝尔纳则领有帕尔迪亚克伯国。

Bernard I was count of Astarac in Gascony and younger son of Count Sancho I, succeeding his father or elder brother William II. In 1130 he rebuilt fire-damaged Simorre and founded Boulaur monastery. Around 1137 he and his son Sancho founded the Cistercian abbey of Berdoues.

Late in 1141, with his other sons' consent, he gave his middle son Bernard the seigneury of Saint-Martin-du-Gôt. Bernard probably died soon after, in late 1141 or 1142.

Bernard IV (died c. 1291) was Count of Astarac from 1249, when his brother Centule II died without children. A younger son of Centule I and Séguine d'Armagnac, he founded three Gascon bastides, the most important being Mirande in 1281, which became the county's capital at the end of the century.

He also founded Seissan in 1266 and Masseube in 1274. He had four sons, among them Centule III, who succeeded him, and Arnaud.

en:
Bernard V (1279–1328 or 1329) was Count of Astarac, ruling from his father Centule III's retirement in 1294 and in his own right from 1301. In 1294 he married Mathe de Foix, who bore him Bernard and Amanieu. He later married Tiburge de L'Isle-Jourdain, widow of Gautier du Fossat.

His eldest son Bernard predeceased him; Bernard V last appeared in documents in 1328 and died that year or the next, leaving the succession to his grandson Centule IV.

en:
Bohemond (died in or after 1176) was Count of Astarac by 1153. The eldest son of Count Bernard I by his second wife Longuebrune, he helped rebuild fire-ravaged Simorre before 1141 and succeeded his brother or nephew. In 1153 his mother, prioress of Bolauc, bribed Bernard de Marestaing to spare Simorre.

He married Rouge de Marsan, and in 1172 donated to Berdoues Abbey. His last recorded act dates to 1175; his daughter Marquese succeeded him.

en:
Centule I (died 1230 or 1233) was Count of Astarac, first named as count in a charter of 1211. A son of Countess Beatrice, he was named by troubadour Bertran de Born among the lords allied against Richard the Lionheart in 1183.

He fought at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212 and in 1219 defended Marmande against the Albigensian Crusaders; he was captured when Prince Louis arrived but soon exchanged. In 1229 he did homage to Louis IX. His sons Centule II and Bernard IV succeeded.

en:
Centule III (c. 1245–c. 1301) was Count of Astarac from 1291. In 1278 he married Assalide d'Albret, who bore him Bernard V and Bohémond. When he succeeded his father Bernard IV, his younger brother Arnaud received Mézamat.

He acknowledged Simorre Abbey's authority and lost the direct vassalage of Sauveterre, Gaujac and Sabailan to the French crown. In 1294 he married his heir Bernard to Mathe de Foix, and on 31 October retired on a pension of 2000 livres tournois, keeping several lordships for life.

en:
Centule IV (1315–1362) was count of Astarac in Gascony from 1330, first under the regency of his mother Cécile de Comminges. In the Hundred Years' War he served Philip VI and held Agen for France in 1342 and 1346.

The Black Prince overran Astarac in 1355, and the Treaty of Brétigny let him recover it in 1360. In 1362 he fought for Foix against Armagnac at Launac, made his will on 7 December and died within the month.

Garcia Arnaud was Count of Astarac from c. 960, second son of Arnold I Garcia Nonnat. His eldest brother William had died before their father, so Garcia inherited the county, while Magnoac had been detached for his younger brother Arnaud of Or.

He is named in the Códice de Roda and in charters granting churches to the abbeys of Auch and Simorre. He died before 975, leaving a son, Arnaud II, who ruled under the regency of his uncle Arnaud of Or.

en:
William I was count of Astarac in Gascony from 1022 or 1023, the eldest son of Count Arnold II and Talesa. When Arnold died, William took Astarac while his brother Bernard Pelagus received Pardiac. He made several grants of monasteries to Simorre Abbey and backed his brother Otto's restoration of Saramon.

His marriage to a kinswoman breached church rules and was validated only after penance. His last surviving charter is dated 1060, and his only son, Sancho I, succeeded him.

Sancho I was count of Astarac in Gascony from about 1060, the only son of William I, whose full county he inherited. His eldest son William died before him; his second son Bernard became heir, while the youngest, Odo, became a monk at Simorre.

Sancho reorganized the monasteries of Astarac, granting several houses to Simorre and other abbeys. Between 1100 and 1110 he and Bernard donated land at Fonsorbes to the Holy Sepulchre and the Hospital of Saint John in Jerusalem.

Sancho II was count of Astarac in Gascony from about 1144, the eldest son of Count Bernard I. After their father's death he divided the inheritance with his brothers: Bernard received the seigneury of Saint-Martin-du-Gôt, while Bohemond took eastern Astarac.

Charters from 1144 to 1162 name Sancho and Bohemond together, each bearing the comital title. From 1162 Bohemond appears as sole ruler; Sancho perhaps retired or went to the Holy Land, and he died in 1168.

en:
Walter V of Brienne (c. 1275–1311) was the only son of Hugh of Brienne and Isabella de la Roche, heir to Brienne and Lecce. As a boy he was a hostage for years in Augusta, and he was captured again in Sicily in 1299, freed by the Treaty of Caltabellotta in 1302.

He succeeded his cousin Guy II as duke of Athens in 1308, after a court rejected the claim of another cousin, Eschiva of Ibelin. He hired the Catalan Company against Thessaly, but withheld their pay; they defeated and killed him at Halmyros on 15 March 1311 and seized the duchy.

en:
Manfred (1306–1317) was the second son of Frederick III of Sicily and Eleanor of Anjou, born at Catania. After the Catalan Company defeated Walter V of Brienne and conquered Athens in 1311, it offered the duchy to King Frederick, who in 1312 invested the young Manfred as duke instead, sending a regent to govern in his name.

Manfred never visited his duchy. In November 1317, aged about eleven, he died after a fall from a horse at Trapani. Athens then passed to his younger brother William.

en:
William II (1312–1338), Duke of Athens, was the third son of Frederick III of Sicily and Eleanor of Anjou. When his brother Manfred died in 1317, William inherited the Catalan-ruled duchy while still a child.

His illegitimate half-brother Alfonso Fadrique governed the Greek lands for him and in 1319 added the Duchy of Neopatria; when Alfonso returned in 1330, William gave him Malta and Gozo. In 1335 he married María Álvarez de Jérica without papal dispensation, since the popes sought to check his father's power.

In 1337 Frederick left him Taranto, to pass to him after Eleanor's death, but William died first, in 1338. He was buried in Palermo cathedral and left his library to the city's Dominicans.

同父异母的私生子兄长阿方索·法德里克代他治理希腊领地，于1319年攻取新帕特雷公国；1330年阿方索自希腊返回，古列尔莫把马耳他和戈佐让给他。1335年，他未经教皇特许便娶玛丽亚·阿尔瓦雷斯·德·赫里卡为妻，因为教皇想遏制其父的势力。

en:
Anselmo, called il Molle (the Soft; c. 1178 – after 1213), was a son of William I, the first marquis of Ceva. A charter of 1197 already shows him acting in his own right.

In 1200, when the bishop of Asti and William stormed the newly founded free commune of Mons Regalis, he served as its podestà under the name Monteregale, almost certainly installed there by the bishop. He is last found alive in 1213, and he probably died before his father.

en:
Al-Mansur Najm al-Din Ghazi II was the Artuqid ruler of Mardin from 1294 to 1312, succeeding his brother Shams al-Din Dawud I. A son of Kara Arslan, he reigned as a vassal of the Mongol Il-khans, to whom Mardin had submitted after Hulagu's siege of 1260.

Coins struck at Mardin in his time bore sun and lion-and-sun imagery. On his death in 1312 his two sons, Ali Alpi II and Shams al-Din Mahmud, succeeded him in turn.

As-Salih Shams al-Din Mahmud was an Artuqid emir of Mardin and a son of Ghazi II. In 1312, after the brief reign of his brother, he succeeded to the Mardin throne and ruled for more than half a century, until 1364.

His son Ahmad ruled from 1364 to 1367, after which Mahmud briefly returned to power. Another son, Dawud II, then reigned until 1376.

en:
Ulrich II of Schönegg (before 1288–1337) was bishop of Augsburg from 1331 until his death. Born to the Swabian Reichsministerialis lords of Schönegg, he was elected under Emperor Louis IV's pressure, defeating Nicholas of Frauenfeld, Pope John XXII's candidate.

In 1334 he began rebuilding Augsburg Cathedral, and in 1336–37 served as Reichskanzler. He died in July 1337 and was buried there, succeeded by his brother Henry III.

乌尔里希二世·冯·舍内格（1288年前—1337）于1331年起任奥格斯堡主教，直至去世。他出身施瓦本的帝国侍役贵族舍内格家族，在皇帝路德维希四世的压力下当选，战胜了教皇约翰二十二世任命的尼古拉·冯·弗劳恩费尔德。

Blanche of Ponthieu (1322–1387) was the elder daughter of John II, Count of Aumale, and Catherine of Artois. When her father died in January 1340 without sons, she inherited Aumale as suo jure countess.

She married John V, Count of Harcourt, a leading Norman baron, and bore him seven children, including John VI, who later held both Harcourt and Aumale. She died in 1387.

Catherine of Artois (1296–1368) was a daughter of Philip of Artois and Blanche of Brittany, and a sister of Robert III of Artois; her father died in 1298. Before 1320 she married John II of Ponthieu, Count of Aumale, and bore him two daughters.

John of Aumale died in January 1340, and Catherine outlived him by almost thirty years, dying in 1368.

en:
Stephen of Aumale (c. 1070–1127), count of Aumale and lord of Holderness, was the only son of Odo of Champagne and Adelaide, sister of William the Conqueror, and thus cousin to William II and Henry I of England. He succeeded his mother as count before 1089.

In 1095 rebels under Robert de Mowbray planned to put him on the English throne, but the plot failed and his father lost their English lands. Stephen joined the First Crusade in 1096 and recovered Holderness in 1102. He supported Henry against Robert in 1104, backed William Clito's revolt in 1118 and submitted in 1119. He died in 1127.

欧马勒的斯蒂芬（约1070—1127），欧马勒伯爵兼霍尔德内斯领主，是香槟的厄德与征服者威廉的姐妹阿德莱德的独子，与英王威廉二世、亨利一世是表兄弟。他在1089年之前继承母亲的伯爵领。

1095年，以罗贝尔·德·莫布雷为首的叛党密谋拥立他为英格兰国王，事败后他父亲被剥夺在英格兰的领地。1096年斯蒂芬参加第一次十字军东征，1102年收回霍尔德内斯。1104年他支持亨利对抗罗贝尔，1118年又支持威廉·克利托反叛，1119年臣服。他于1127年去世。

en:
Odo of Champagne (c. 1040–1115), also Eudes II of Troyes, was the son of Count Stephen II of Troyes and Meaux and ruled Troyes and Meaux from 1047. His uncle Theobald III of Blois governed as regent during his minority.

In 1060 he married Adelaide of Normandy, sister of William the Conqueror and heiress of Aumale, and became count of Aumale through her. He accompanied William in the conquest of England in 1066, while Theobald seized his Champagne counties.

In 1095 he was imprisoned and lost his English lands for joining a plot to put his son Stephen on the English throne. He died in 1115.

1060年他娶诺曼底的阿德莱德为妻，她是征服者威廉的姐妹、欧马勒的女继承人，厄德凭妻权成为欧马勒伯爵。1066年他随威廉征服英格兰，蒂博则夺取了他在香槟的伯国。

1095年，他因参与拥立儿子斯蒂芬登上英格兰王位的阴谋而入狱，丧失了在英格兰的领地。他于1115年去世。

en:
Ferdinand of Castile (1238–c. 1260) was an infante of Castile, the elder son of King Ferdinand III and Joan, Countess of Ponthieu, and an elder brother of Eleanor of Castile, queen of England.

After his father's death at Seville in 1252, he went with his mother to France and inherited the County of Aumale. He married Laure de Montfort. Their son John I succeeded him as count and fell at the Battle of the Golden Spurs in 1302.

en:
John II, Count of Aumale (1293–1343), was the son of John I of Aumale and Ida de Meulan. His father was killed at Courtrai in July 1302, and John inherited Aumale and his other lands.

By 1319 he married Catherine d'Artois. In 1339 he served Philip VI at the siege of Cambrai. His daughters were Blanche, later Countess of Aumale, and Joan, who married the Count of Vendôme.

en:
John I of Ponthieu (c. 1255–1302), Count of Aumale, was the son of Count Ferdinand II and Laura of Montfort, and a grandson of King Ferdinand III of Castile. After his father died in 1260 he inherited Aumale and Ponthieu, ruling with his grandmother until 1279. Edward I then claimed Ponthieu; John resisted until bought off in 1293, keeping Aumale.

By his wife Ida of Meulan he left his heir John II. He was killed fighting for France at the Battle of the Golden Spurs in 1302.

en:
John I of Brienne (c. 1250–1294) was Count of Eu in Normandy. The eldest son of Alphonse of Brienne and Marie of Lusignan, the heiress of Eu, he inherited the county on his mother's death in 1260 and ruled under his father's tutelage until 1270. Through his father he was a grandson of John of Brienne, king of Jerusalem.

He married Beatrice, daughter of Guy III, Count of Saint-Pol, who bore him his heir John II and a daughter Mahaut. He died in 1294.

John II of Brienne (c. 1274–1302), called Jean III in French, succeeded his father John I as count of Eu in 1294. He married Jeanne, heiress of Guînes, and pressed her claim before the Parlement of Paris.

Her grandfather had been forced to sell Guînes to Philip III in 1282. In February 1295 Philip IV restored the County of Guînes to the couple. On 11 July 1302 he was killed among the French chivalry at the Battle of the Golden Spurs near Kortrijk. His son Raoul succeeded to Eu.

en:
Joan of Dammartin (c. 1220–1279), queen of Castile and countess of Ponthieu, was the eldest daughter of Simon of Dammartin and Marie of Ponthieu. In 1234 she was promised to Henry III of England, but the pope forbade the match on grounds of kinship.

In 1237 Joan married Ferdinand III of Castile; her daughter Eleanor married Edward I of England. Widowed in 1252, she ruled Ponthieu and from 1263 Aumale, then married Jean de Nesle, running up substantial debts. She died at Abbeville in 1279, leaving Ponthieu to Eleanor and Aumale to her grandson John I.

Jeanne de Mello (died 1351), lady of Lormes and Château-Chinon, was the daughter and heiress of Dreux VI de Mello of a Burgundian baronial house. In 1315 she married Raoul I of Brienne, Count of Eu and Guînes, who became Constable of France and was killed at a Paris tournament in January 1344.

Her son Raoul II succeeded as count but was beheaded in 1350; her daughter Jeanne married Walter VI of Brienne. Jeanne de Mello died in 1351.

让娜·德·梅洛（？—1351），洛尔姆与沙托希农的女领主，是勃艮第男爵家族德勒六世·德·梅洛的女儿和继承人。1315年她嫁给厄镇与吉讷伯爵拉乌尔一世·德·布里耶纳；拉乌尔后来出任法兰西王室统帅，1344年1月在巴黎的比武大会上身亡。

其子拉乌尔二世继位，1350年被斩首；女儿让娜嫁给戈蒂埃六世·德布里耶纳。让娜·德·梅洛卒于1351年。

en:
Joan of Ponthieu (before 1336–1376), younger daughter of John II, Count of Aumale, and Catherine of Artois, inherited Épernon from her father. In 1344 she married John VI, Count of Vendôme, and bore Bouchard VII.

In 1362 raiders seized Vendôme and held her for ransom. After Bouchard died in 1371, she ruled Vendôme as regent for her infant granddaughter Joan, who died months later.

蓬蒂约的让娜（1336年前—1376）是欧马勒伯爵约翰二世与阿图瓦的卡特琳的幼女，从父亲那里继承埃佩尔农领地。1344年，她嫁给旺多姆伯爵约翰六世，生下布夏七世。

1362年，武装团伙攻占旺多姆，将她扣押勒索赎金。1371年布夏死后，她为尚在襁褓中的孙女让娜摄政旺多姆，但这个孩子数月后便夭折。

en:
Philip Hurepel (1200–1234) was a son of King Philip II Augustus of France and Agnes of Merania. In 1216 he married Matilda II, Countess of Boulogne, and ruled Boulogne and Aumale in her right; in 1218 he received Clermont-en-Beauvaisis.

He joined Louis VIII on the Albigensian Crusade in 1226 and carried the sword at Louis IX's coronation. In 1229 he joined the barons' revolt against the regent Blanche of Castile, later winning pardon. He died at Corbie in 1234, supposedly killed after slaying Count Floris IV of Holland in a tournament.

zh:
腓力·于雷佩尔（1200—1234）是法王腓力二世·奥古斯都与梅拉涅的阿涅丝之子。1216年他迎娶布洛涅女伯爵玛蒂尔达二世，凭妻权统治布洛涅和欧马勒，1218年受封克莱蒙。

1226年他随路易八世参加阿尔比十字军，在路易九世的加冕礼上捧持御剑。1229年他参与贵族反对摄政卡斯蒂利亚的布兰卡的叛乱，后来获赦。1234年他卒于科尔比，相传此前他在比武大会上杀死荷兰伯爵弗洛里斯四世，随后也被杀死。

Raoul I of Brienne (died 1344) was the son of John II of Brienne, Count of Eu, and Jeanne of Guînes. He succeeded to Eu in 1302 and Guînes in 1332. In 1315 he married Jeanne de Mello, heiress of Château-Chinon.

Named Constable of France in 1329, he led French armies in the Hundred Years' War. Killed at a tournament in Paris, he was succeeded by his son Raoul II.

Raoul II of Brienne (1315–1350) succeeded his father Raoul I in 1344 as Count of Eu and Guînes and as Constable of France. In 1340 he married Catherine, daughter of Louis II of Vaud.

He was captured at Caen in 1346 and held prisoner in England. Allowed back to France in 1350 to raise his ransom, he was seized and beheaded without trial on John II's orders; rumour said he had pledged Guînes to the English.

en:
Simon of Dammartin (c. 1180–1239) was count of Aumale and Ponthieu. He received Aumale from Philip II Augustus in 1206 and married Marie, heiress of Ponthieu. He joined King John of England and fought at Bouvines in 1214; defeated, he fled into exile and his lands went to Philip Hurepel.

In 1223 he seized Abbeville to reconquer Ponthieu, but Louis VIII drove him out. His wife obtained Ponthieu's restoration on harsh terms, including the surrender of Doullens and Saint-Riquier. Simon accepted these terms in 1230 and recovered Aumale in 1234. He died in 1239.

西蒙·德·达马尔坦（约1180—1239）是欧马勒和蓬蒂约伯爵。1206年他获腓力二世·奥古斯都册封欧马勒伯国，并迎娶蓬蒂约女继承人玛丽。他转投英格兰国王约翰，1214年战于布汶；兵败后他流亡海外，领地被转封给腓力·于雷佩尔。

Béraud I (c. 1315–1356), eldest son of Dauphin John I, married Marie de La Vie de Villemur at Avignon on 14 June 1333. Lord of Mercœur from 1340, in 1350 he attended Clement VI's jubilee in Rome and saw the Veil of Veronica.

He succeeded as Dauphin in March 1351, made his testament on 9 August 1356, and died on 27 August, leaving lands to his son Béraud II.

en:
Béraud II the Great (1333–1399) became the eighth Dauphin of Auvergne in August 1356 and fought at Poitiers three weeks later. In 1357 he married the heiress Jeanne de Forez. Under the 1360 Treaty of Brétigny he was sent to England as a hostage for the released John II and stayed over ten years.

He served Charles VI in the 1382 Flanders campaign, and in 1390 sailed on the Barbary Crusade. He died in January 1399, succeeded by Béraud III.

en:
Guy of Boulogne (1313–1373) was the third son of Count Robert VII of Auvergne and Boulogne. Destined for the Church, he studied theology and was elected Archbishop of Lyon in 1340. Pope Clement VI made him a cardinal in 1342, and he left Lyon for Avignon.

As a papal legate he negotiated truces in Hungary, Italy and Spain and headed efforts to end the Hundred Years' War; his niece Joan married the future John II of France. He later became cardinal-bishop of Porto and dean of the College of Cardinals, and helped choose Popes Urban V and Gregory XI.

He died at Lleida in 1373 on a diplomatic mission, probably poisoned, though the suspicion cast on Charles II of Navarre was later cleared. Petrarch's letters mention him often.

居伊·德·布洛涅（1313—1373）是奥弗涅与布洛涅伯爵罗贝尔七世的第三子。他被安排投身教会，攻读神学，1340年当选里昂大主教。1342年，教皇克雷芒六世将他擢升为枢机，他离开里昂，迁往阿维尼翁。

作为教皇特使，他曾赴匈牙利、意大利和西班牙斡旋停战，并主持结束百年战争的谈判；他的侄女让娜后来嫁给了日后的法王约翰二世。他后来出任波尔图枢机主教和枢机团团长，参与选出乌尔班五世与格列高利十一世两位教皇。

1373年，他在执行外交使命期间于莱里达去世，多半死于毒杀，对纳瓦拉的卡洛斯二世的怀疑后来得到澄清。彼特拉克的书信里也屡屡提到他。

en:
Guy I of Auvergne was viscount of Auvergne in the later tenth century and the first to rule it as count. He became viscount after his brother Robert III. After Count William Tête d'Étoupe died around 963, the viscounts filled the vacant county, and by the 980s charters styled Guy count.

He married Ausenda. In 985 he attacked Mende in Gévaudan; a later bishop's account claims he was killed by a lance before the city gates. He died around 989 and his brother William IV succeeded him.

en:
Guy II (1165–1222), son of Robert IV of Auvergne and Matilda of Burgundy, became count in 1195. His marriage to Péronnelle de Chambon added the barony of Combrailles. After Richard I dropped his claim to overlordship in 1196, Guy stayed in the Plantagenet camp against Philip Augustus.

He feuded for years with his brother Robert, bishop of Clermont, before a truce in 1207. Philip's armies took Riom in 1212 and stormed Tournoël in 1213, annexing most of Auvergne; Guy kept only the Comté around Vic-le-Comte. He died in 1222, leaving his son William X.

en:
William IV (c. 950–1016) became count of Auvergne in 989, when his brother Guy I died without children. A son of Viscount Robert II of Clermont and Engelberga, he first appears in charters as the count's brother, countersigning gifts to Brioude and Sauxillanges.

Around 1000 he and his wife Umberga made donations for the souls of their children. Of these, Robert I succeeded as count, Stephen became bishop of Clermont, and Ermengarde married Count Odo II of Blois in 1005.

en:
William VI (c. 1069–1136) succeeded his father Robert II as count of Auvergne. He joined the First Crusade and in 1102 led Auvergne's nobles to the Holy Land, besieging Tripoli with Raymond of Saint-Gilles. He founded the fortified town of Montferrand to overawe the bishop's city of Clermont.

His attacks on the Clermont clergy brought Louis VI's army south in 1122, forcing him to return what he had seized. In 1126 the king besieged Montferrand until the Duke of Aquitaine, William's overlord, intervened. By Emma of Sicily, his sons were Robert III and William VIII, both later counts.

William VII, called the Young (c. 1130–1169), became the legitimate count of Auvergne when his father Robert III died on crusade in 1147. He married Marquise d'Albon of Viennois, whose family's Dauphin title passed to his heirs.

After a long feud his uncle William VIII the Old seized the county around 1155, but William retained part of it, including Montferrand. Louis VII once imprisoned both rival counts, who were released only in 1164. William died in 1169, and his son Robert IV founded the Dauphin line of Auvergne.

en:
William VIII, called the Old (c. 1100–1182), was count of Auvergne, a son of Count William VI and brother of Robert III. In 1155, after a long quarrel with his nephew William VII the Young, he seized part of the county and ruled from Clermont.

Louis VII imprisoned both claimants briefly and freed them in 1164. When Henry II arbitrated in 1167, William VIII refused his judgment and did homage to Louis VII instead, while his nephew paid homage to Henry. He married Anne of Nevers and died in 1182, leaving the county to his son Robert IV.

en:
William X (c. 1195–1247), count of Auvergne, was the son of Count Guy II and Péronnelle de Chambon. At eighteen he helped defend Tournoël, Auvergne's last free fortress, against Philip Augustus in 1213. He was taken in a failed sortie, and the castle's commander then surrendered.

He succeeded his father in 1222 as count of the remnant of Auvergne, and in 1229 or 1230 Louis IX restored several of his father's lordships to him. He married Adelaide of Brabant and died in 1247, leaving the county to his son Robert V.

William XII (c. 1300–6 August 1332) succeeded his father Robert VII as count of Auvergne and Boulogne in 1325. His mother was Blanche of Clermont, daughter of the Capetian prince Robert, count of Clermont. In 1325 he married Margaret of Évreux, daughter of Louis, count of Évreux.

William died on 6 August 1332, leaving a single child, Joan, who succeeded as countess of Auvergne and Boulogne and later became queen of France through her marriage to John II.

John I, called Dauphinet (c. 1280–1351), was the sixth Dauphin of Auvergne and Count of Clermont, ruling from 1324. He was the son of Robert IV Dauphin and Alix of Mercœur, and in 1313 married Anne of Poitiers-Valentinois.

In 1340, after making his testament in favour of his eldest son Béraud, he followed Philip VI to Flanders, governed Saint-Omer and defeated the Flemings there. He died in 1351.

en:
Joan I of Auvergne (8 May 1326 – 29 September 1360) inherited the counties of Auvergne and Boulogne as a child, when her father William XII died in 1332. Her first husband, Philip of Burgundy, fell at Aiguillon in 1346; their infant son Philip inherited the Duchy of Burgundy in 1349 under her regency.

In February 1350 she married John, Duke of Normandy. His first wife had died of the Black Death leaving eight children, so there was little pressure on Joan to produce an heir. When John succeeded as John II that August, she became queen of France.

Her three children with him died young, and her son Philip became a ward of the king. She died at the Château d'Argilly in 1360. Philip inherited her counties but died the next year, aged fifteen.

1350年2月她改嫁诺曼底公爵约翰。约翰的前妻死于黑死病，留下八个孩子，因此让娜并不承受生下继承人的压力。同年8月约翰即位为法王约翰二世，她随之成为法国王后。

她与约翰所生的三个孩子都早夭，儿子菲利普则成为国王的被监护人。1360年她在阿尔日伊城堡去世，两个伯国由菲利普继承，而他次年便夭折，年仅十五岁。
