en:
Margaret of Évreux (c. 1307–1350) was a Capetian princess, daughter of Louis, Count of Évreux, and Margaret of Artois, and sister of Philip III of Navarre.

In 1325, at the castle of Busséol, she married William XII, Count of Auvergne and Boulogne. She was countess of both until 1332. Their daughter Joan I, born in 1326, inherited the two counties.

en:
Robert, called the Young, was viscount of Auvergne in the mid-tenth century, the son of Viscount Robert I. In 936 he appears with his father among the founders of Chanteuges Abbey. Charters style him viscount from 947, and he succeeded his father around 950.

Cartularies of Brioude and Sauxillanges show him acting beside his brother Stephen, bishop of Clermont, and later beside his sons. He died between 970 and 980, and his son Guy succeeded him.

en:
Robert I (c. 970–c. 1032) succeeded his father William IV as count of Auvergne around 1016, the year he subscribed the foundation of the church of Saint-Genès. His piety did not stop him seizing the property of the church of Aydat, which he was forced to restore in 1022.

He married Ermengarde of Arles, daughter of William I of Provence. Their son William V succeeded to the county, while their daughter Ermengarde married Odo II, count of Blois.

en:
Robert II was count of Auvergne from about 1060, succeeding his father William V. By his first marriage to Bertha, daughter of Hugh, count of Rouergue and Gévaudan, he ruled Rouergue jure uxoris. After Bertha died childless around 1065 he lost Rouergue but kept Gévaudan.

He last appears in a Cluny charter of 1095 and died around that year. By his second wife Judith of Melgueil he left a son, William VI, who succeeded him in Auvergne.

Robert III was count of Auvergne from about 1136, succeeding his father William VI. His dispute with the church of Brioude was settled by a treaty involving the archbishops of Bourges and Lyon.

He joined Louis VII of France on the Second Crusade, perhaps to atone for his wrongs against the church, entrusting his possessions to his brother William the Elder. Robert died on the expedition around 1147, and his brother seized the county as William VIII.

en:
Robert IV (c. 1130–1194), count of Auvergne from 1182, was the son of William VIII the Old and Anne of Nevers. In 1183 Brabançon mercenaries raided Auvergne, and Robert gathered the nobility and destroyed the raiders.

In 1192 he founded the Cistercian abbey of Bouschet-Vauluisant as his dynasty's burial church. His sons by his wife Matilda of Burgundy included Guy II, who succeeded him as count, and Robert, bishop of Clermont and later archbishop of Lyon.

en:
Robert V (c. 1225–1277) succeeded his father William X as count of Auvergne in 1247, ruling the reduced county. Through his mother Adelaide of Brabant he received Boulogne in 1260. After he imprisoned a monk over Saint-Germain-Lembron abbey, Pope Alexander IV excommunicated him.

In 1253 the bishops of Auvergne called in Alphonse of Poitiers against him. Robert sent a noble embassy to protest the royal investigations, then accepted a mediated settlement in 1254. He made his will on 11 January 1277 and died days later, leaving Auvergne and Boulogne to his elder son William XI.

Robert VI (1250–1314) inherited the lordship of Combrailles under his father Robert V's will of 1277 and succeeded his brother William XI as count of Auvergne and Boulogne in 1280. Before 1282 he married Beatrice of Montgascon, who bore him his heir Robert VII.

en:
Robert VII of Auvergne (c. 1282–1325) was count of Auvergne and Boulogne from 1317 until his death. In 1297 he served under King Philip IV of France and his father Robert VI in the Franco-Flemish War, fighting at Courtrai in 1302 and at Mons-en-Pévèle in 1304.

He married Blanche of Clermont in 1303 and, after her death, Marie of Dampierre. In 1314 his father named his wife Beatrice of Montgascon sole heir, and she later named Robert her heir. He died in 1325 and was succeeded by his son William.

en:
Alix of Burgundy, also called Adelaide (c. 1251–1290), was ruling countess of Auxerre. She was the daughter of Odo of Burgundy and Matilda II of Bourbon.

After her father died on crusade in 1266, a Parlement of Paris ruling in 1273 gave Auxerre to Alix, dividing his lands among his three daughters. In 1268 she married John I of Chalon, lord of Rochefort, and their son William succeeded her in Auxerre.

William of Chalon, called the Great (c. 1270–1304), was count of Auxerre and Tonnerre and lord of Rochefort. The only son of John I of Chalon and the heiress Alix of Burgundy, he succeeded his mother in Auxerre, and in 1292 his aunt Margaret of Burgundy granted him part of her rights over Tonnerre.

In 1302 he attended Philip IV's first Estates General and married Eleanor, daughter of Count Amadeus V of Savoy. He fought in Philip IV's Flemish war and fell at the battle of Mons-en-Pévèle on 18 July 1304, leaving a minor son, John II.

en:
John I of Chalon (c. 1243–1309), lord of Rochefort in the county of Burgundy, became count of Auxerre through his marriage to its heiress Alix of Burgundy, confirmed by a Parlement of Paris ruling in 1273. In 1293 he also took the title of count of Tonnerre.

From 1294 to 1301 he led Comtois barons resisting Philip IV, who had bought the county from Otto IV. After his son William fell at Mons-en-Pévèle in 1304, William's widow guarded their son John II until her remarriage in 1308; John I then guarded his grandson until his own death in October 1309.

en:
John II of Chalon (1292–c. 1362), son of William the Great, was a count who kept minting his own coin against the wishes of the French crown. He became count of Auxerre on his father's death in 1304, inherited Tonnerre in 1308 and ruled in his own right from 1314.

After the royal ordinance of 1315 ended his minting rights in those two counties, he is said to have struck coin at Orgelet instead, and the archbishop of Besançon excommunicated him. He minted again at Châtelbelin in 1343. The emperor lifted the excommunication in 1351 and, two years later, granted him the right to mint at Orgelet in perpetuity.

In the Hundred Years' War he was a prisoner in London in 1346 and still in captivity in 1357. His second wife Alix of Burgundy bore his successor John III.

John III of Chalon, called the White Knight (c. 1318–1379), was Count of Auxerre and Tonnerre. He served as grand butler of France and was captured in 1356 shortly before Poitiers, freed by the Treaty of Brétigny in 1360.

He inherited Tonnerre in 1360 and Auxerre in 1361. Broken by captivity, he sold Auxerre to King Charles V and died in 1379 under his children's guardianship.

沙隆的让三世，绰号“白衣骑士”（约1318—1379），是欧塞尔与托内尔伯爵。他曾任法兰西大酒政，1356年在普瓦捷战役前不久被俘，直到1360年《布雷蒂尼条约》签订后才获释。

他于1360年继承托内尔、1361年继承欧塞尔。囚禁生涯使其心智衰退，他后来把欧塞尔伯国卖给法王查理五世，1379年在子女的监护下离世。

en:
Peter of Courtenay (c. 1218–1250), lord of Conches and Mehun, was the eldest son of Robert I of Courtenay, lord of Champignelles, and Mahaut of Mehun. He ruled his Norman and Berry lordships from 1239, and on 25 August 1248 sailed from Aigues-Mortes with his cousin Louis IX on the Seventh Crusade to Egypt.

Most historians place his death at Mansurah on 8 February 1250, when Robert I of Artois led a vanguard into a Mamluk trap. His daughter Amicia by Pétronille of Joigny married Robert II of Artois.

库尔特奈的皮埃尔（约1218—1250）是孔什与默安领主，尚皮涅勒领主库尔特奈的罗贝尔一世与默安的玛奥的长子。他1239年起统治在诺曼底与贝里的领地，1248年8月25日随表兄路易九世从艾格莫尔特登船，参加远征埃及的第七次十字军。

en:
Robert I of Courtenay (c. 1168–1239), lord of Champignelles, was a grandson of King Louis VI and a trusted knight of Philip II Augustus. He fought at the siege of Château-Gaillard in 1204 and was rewarded with the lordships of Conches and Nonancourt.

He served on the Albigensian Crusade in 1209, and Louis VIII made him grand butler of France in 1223. He later joined the Barons' Crusade and died at Acre in 1239.

en:
Chimpu Orma appears in Sarmiento de Gamboa's 1572 chronicle as a woman of Anta, daughter of its sinchi and concubine of the Ayarmaca ruler Tocay Cápac. Her position let her visit Tocay's captive, the Inca prince Titu Cusi Hualpa.

She brought him food and arranged his escape during a boys' race. Her kinsmen beat back the pursuers and hid the prince in Anta for a year. After Inca Roca learned his heir lived, he recognized the Antas as kin of Cuzco's orejones.

琴普·奥尔马见于萨米恩托·德·甘博亚1572年编年史，她是安塔辛奇之女，也是阿亚尔马卡统治者托凯·卡帕克的妾。她因此能探望被托凯囚禁的印加王子蒂图·库西·瓦尔帕。

In the Spanish chronicles, Curi Hilpay, also spelled Ccuri-hilpay, was the woman whose marriage linked an Ayarmaca lord to Cápac Yupanqui, ruler of Cusco.

Sarmiento de Gamboa says a wealthy Ayarmaca sinchi presented her from fear, while another account made her a native of Cusco. The marriage belonged to the diplomacy between Cusco and the Ayarmaca as Chanca power expanded; Sarmiento names her as the mother of Inca Roca.

en:
In the Spanish chronicles, Tocay Cápac was the sinchi, or war leader, of the Ayarmaca people around Cusco. When the Huallacanes gave Mama Micay to Inca Roca after first promising her to Tocay, he felt insulted and conspired with them to seize her young son Titu Cusi Hualpa.

Legend says the boy wept blood and was spared; he later became known as Yáhuar Huácac, the one who weeps blood. Around 1350 peace was sealed when Inca Roca sent him his daughter Curi Ocllo, and Tocay's own daughter Mama Chiquia married the Inca prince.

en:
Khidr Beg (died c. 1360) was the third ruler of the Aydınid beylik in Anatolia. He succeeded his brother Umur Beg in 1348, after Umur died at Smyrna in the Latin crusade.

That year he was forced to accept a Latin treaty, surrendering half the customs revenue and opening his ports to Christian ships. He soon recovered, making agreements with the Hospitallers, Genoa and, in 1353, Venice and Crete. He died around 1360 and was followed by İsa Bey.

希兹尔·贝伊（约1360年卒）是安纳托利亚艾登王朝的第三位统治者。1348年其兄乌穆尔贝伊在士麦那死于拉丁人的十字军，他随即继位。

en:
Mubariz al-Din Gazi Mehmed Bey (died 1334) was the founder of the Aydınid principality in western Anatolia. A Turkish commander serving the Germiyan ruler Yakub Bey, he seized the Aydın lands for himself in 1308 and made Birgi his capital.

He took Ayasuluk and other towns, built a fleet there, and captured the harbour of Smyrna in 1328–1329. On his death in 1334 his son Umur succeeded him.

en:
Umur Ghazi (c. 1309–1348), called Umur the Lion, was the second bey of Aydın, a Turkish beylik on the Aegean coast of Anatolia, ruling from 1334. His power was his navy: at its height Aydın had 350 ships and 15000 men. His raids on Christian shipping led Pope Clement VI to proclaim the Smyrniote Crusade against him in 1343.

He was a loyal friend of the Byzantine emperor John VI Cantacuzenus in the civil war of 1341–1347, and sent up to 380 ships and 28000 men to his aid.

In 1348 a Venetian, Hospitaller and Cypriot fleet destroyed his navy, and Umur was killed by arrows while climbing the walls of Smyrna castle in an attempt to retake it. John mourned him, and Umur's elder brother Hızır succeeded him.

加齐·乌穆尔（约1309—1348）人称“狮子乌穆尔”，是安纳托利亚爱琴海沿岸土耳其人的艾登侯国第二任贝伊，自1334年起统治。他的力量在海军：鼎盛时艾登拥有350艘战船和15000名士兵，他对基督教船只的袭掠促使教宗克雷芒六世于1343年发动士麦那十字军。

1341—1347年拜占庭内战期间，他是皇帝约翰六世（坎塔库泽努斯）的忠实朋友，派出多达380艘船和28000人相助。

1348年，威尼斯、医院骑士团与塞浦路斯的联合舰队摧毁了他的海军，乌穆尔在攀登士麦那城堡城墙、试图夺回该城时中箭身亡。约翰为他哀悼，继位的是他的兄长赫兹尔。

en:
Aylangir was a 13th-century Mongol amir of the Barlas tribe in the Chagatai Khanate, the son of Ichil and father of Burgul. Yazdi's Zafarnama relates that Aylangir took over Ichil's duties in the khanate after his father moved to Persia; Hafiz-i Abru instead says that Ichil's other son Qutlugh Qiya moved there.

Both writers say the khanate flourished under Aylangir. Through Burgul, father of Taraghai, he was the great-grandfather of Timur, the future conqueror.

en:
Ayurbarwada (1285–1320), titled Buyantu Khan and Emperor Renzong of Yuan, was the second son of Darmabala and a pupil of the Confucian Li Meng. He helped his brother Khayishan seize power in 1307, became crown prince and succeeded in 1311.

He reversed his brother's free-spending ways and in 1313 restored the Confucian civil service examinations, first held in 1315. He fought Chagatai khan Esen Buqa until the latter's death in 1318, and died in 1320, leaving the throne to his son Shidibala.

en:
Acamapichtli was the first tlatoani of the Mexica of Tenochtitlan and founder of its royal dynasty. His mother was Atotoztli I, princess of Culhuacan. The elders chose him for his Culhua, and hence Toltec, bloodline, and he entered the island city as its ruler in the 1370s after marrying Ilancueitl.

Tenochtitlan paid tribute to the Tepanec city of Azcapotzalco and fought its wars before being allowed its own. Acamapichtli preferred alliances to war and paid what was demanded: when Tezozomoc asked for a chinampa of beautiful flowers, the Mexica planted one and floated it across the lake to him.

He extended the chinampa fields, divided the city into four calpullis and issued its first laws. Crowned at Huitzilopochtli's altar in 1382, he died in 1395 and his son Huitzilihuitl succeeded him.

阿卡马皮奇特利是墨西加人在特诺奇蒂特兰的首任特拉托阿尼，也是当地王朝的奠基者。母亲是库瓦坎公主阿托托斯特利一世。长老们因他的库瓦坎血统（库瓦坎贵族自称托尔特克人后裔）选中他，他娶伊兰奎特尔为妻，于1370年代进入这座岛城执政。

特诺奇蒂特兰先向特帕内克城市阿斯卡波察尔科纳贡并为其征战，后来才获准自行征战。阿卡马皮奇特利宁可结盟也不轻启战端，对索要的贡赋照付：特索索莫克想要一块种满鲜花的奇南帕田，墨西加人就种出一块，从湖面上浮送过去。

在城内，他扩展奇南帕田、将城市划为四个卡尔普里，并颁布首批法律。1382年他在维齐洛波奇特利祭坛前加冕，1395年去世，其子维齐利维特尔继位。

en:
Atotoztli I was a Colhua princess of Culhuacan, a daughter of King Coxcoxtli and sister of King Huehue Acamapichtli. She married Opochtli Iztahuatzin, a Mexica leader, in one of the unions between the two peoples at Tizaapan. The Colhua nobility claimed descent from the Toltecs of Tula.

After Tenoch's death, the Mexica elders sought a ruler who could strengthen their new city's ties to powerful neighbours. They chose her son Acamapichtli, who became the first tlatoani of Tenochtitlan and founded its royal dynasty. The Codex Aubin dates his accession to 1376, while other chronicles differ.

阿托托斯特利一世是库尔瓦坎的科尔瓦公主，国王科什科什特利之女、国王韦韦·阿卡马皮奇特利的姐妹。她嫁给墨西卡首领奥波奇特利·伊斯塔瓦钦，是两族在蒂萨潘交往时通婚的例子之一。科尔瓦贵族自称是图拉的托尔特克人的后裔。

en:
Tenoch (c. 1299–1363) was the Mexica war leader, or cuauhtlahtoani, raised to power by the council of elders. His people were then in Azcapotzalco's grip: they paid heavier tribute and from 1318 had to fight in Tepanec campaigns.

In 1344, with Azcapotzalco's support, he made Culhuacan the Mexica's first tributary, and he rose to Huitznahuatl, the highest military rank open to a priest. After Ilancueitl's death in 1347 he was chosen as leader; he replaced Culhuacan's ruler with the more loyal Nauhyotl, and in 1351 he led the first New Fire ceremony at the Hill of the Star.

He reorganized the island settlement in Lake Texcoco and began its central sacred precinct, laying the ground for a lasting royal line. He died in 1363; one account says Acamapichtli renamed the city Tenochtitlan in his honour in 1376.

特诺奇（约1299—1363）是墨西卡人的军事首领“夸乌特拉托阿尼”，由长老会议推举掌权。当时墨西卡人受制于阿斯卡波察尔科：贡赋加重，自1318年起还要参加特帕内克人的战争。

1344年，他在阿斯卡波察尔科支持下使库尔瓦坎成为墨西卡的首个纳贡城邦，并晋升为祭司所能达到的最高军职“威兹纳瓦特尔”。1347年伊兰奎特尔去世后，他被推举为首领，在库尔瓦坎以更忠于墨西卡的瑙约特尔取代原有统治者，1351年又在星之山主持首次新火典礼。

他整顿特斯科科湖中的岛城，开始营建城中心的祭祀区，为日后稳固的王室世系打下基础。他于1363年去世；一种记载称，阿卡马皮奇特利于1376年为纪念他将该城改名为特诺奇蒂特兰。

en:
Tlacaelel (1397–1487) was the chief architect of the Aztec Empire, son of the Mexica ruler Huitzilihuitl and brother of Moctezuma I. In the late 1420s war against the Tepanecs he became cihuacoatl and held the office under four successive tlatoque.

He recast the Mexica as a chosen people, raised Huitzilopochtli to the head of the pantheon, used the flower wars against Tlaxcala to take sacrificial captives, imposed sumptuary laws and burned the histories of conquered peoples.

He first rose under his uncle Itzcoatl. He dedicated the seventh rebuilding of the Templo Mayor at Tenochtitlan in 1484 and died in 1487.

特拉卡埃莱尔（1397—1487）是阿兹特克帝国的主要缔造者，为墨西加统治者维齐利维特尔之子、蒙特苏马一世的兄弟。1420年代末对特帕内克人的战争中，他出任西瓦科瓦特尔，并连续辅佐四代特拉托阿尼。

他把墨西加人塑造为神选之民，将维齐洛波奇特利抬到众神之首；发动对特拉斯卡拉的荣冠战争以获取献祭俘虏，颁布奢侈禁令，并焚毁被征服民族的史书。

他早年在叔父伊茨科亚特尔麾下崛起。1484年他主持特诺奇蒂特兰大神庙第七次重建的落成典礼，1487年去世。

en:
Leopold II of Egloffstein (died 27 June 1343), born into the knightly family of Egloffstein in Franconian Switzerland, served as prince-bishop of Bamberg from 1335 until his death.

Appointed under Pope Benedict XII and Emperor Louis IV, he inherited a deeply indebted bishopric yet still acquired the castles of Marloffstein, Theisenort and Greifenstein. In 1340 he confirmed Bamberg's new Poor Clares convent, the first religious foundation endowed by a patrician family of the city.

Beatrice of Bar (1310–1350) was a French noblewoman of the house of Montbéliard, the third child of Count Edward I of Bar and Mary of Burgundy. She married Guido Gonzaga as his third wife. Guido (1290–1369) was a condottiero of the Gonzaga family that ruled Mantua.

In 1360, at seventy, he became second capitano del popolo. Beatrice died in 1350, ten years before he took that office; their son Ludovico II took over Mantua's government after Guido's death in 1369.

巴尔的贝亚特丽切（1310—1350）是蒙贝利亚尔家族的法国贵族女子，巴尔伯爵爱德华一世与勃艮第的玛丽的第三个孩子。她嫁给圭多·贡扎加，是他的第三任妻子。圭多（1290—1369）是统治曼托瓦的贡扎加家族的雇佣兵首领。

en:
Edward I (c. 1295–1336) became count of Bar in 1302 on the death of his father Henry III, and his uncles were regents until his 1310 marriage to Mary of Burgundy. Captured by Frederick IV of Lorraine at Frouard in 1313, he was freed in 1314 after a ransom of ninety thousand livres was agreed.

In 1324 he joined the War of the Four Lords against Metz, seeking to cancel the debts from his ransom and assert his seigneurial rights. He died at Famagusta in November 1336 while on crusade, and his son Henry IV succeeded him.

en:
Eleanor of England (1269–1298) was the eldest surviving daughter of King Edward I and Eleanor of Castile. For years she was betrothed to Alfonso III of Aragon, but Edward I withheld her while Alfonso's parents were under papal interdict over their claim to Sicily, and Alfonso died before the wedding.

In September 1293 she instead married Count Henry III of Bar, bearing him two children, Edward I of Bar and Joan, later Countess of Surrey. She died at Ghent on 29 August 1298 and was buried in Westminster Abbey.

Gillette de Bar was a daughter of Pierre I of Bar and Jeanne de Vienne. Before January 1334 she married Johann of Saarbrücken, who became Count John II of Saarbrücken in 1341.

In 1352 she and her husband certified an older charter of privileges granted to Commercy. Her daughter Joan married John I of Nassau-Weilburg in 1353 and carried the Commercy inheritance into that German comital line. Gillette died between April 1356 and September 1362.

Henry I (1158–1190) was count of Bar and lord of Mousson from 1170. Succeeding his father Reginald II as a minor, he ruled under the regency of his mother Agnes of Champagne, whose 1172 claim to Verdun led her to ravage its diocese; both were excommunicated and submitted in 1177.

A first cousin of Philip II Augustus, he attended the king's coronation at Reims in 1179. He joined the Third Crusade after Jerusalem fell in 1187, and at Acre he was mortally wounded fighting Saladin's army on 4 October 1190, dying later that month.

en:
Henry II (1190–1239) was count of Bar from 1214, son of Theobald I. He fought for Philip II Augustus at Bouvines and supported Count Theobald IV in the Champagne war of 1216–1221. In 1227 he rose with Theobald IV against the regent Blanche of Castile, then submitted; after quarrelling with Theobald, he raided Lorraine in 1230.

By his 1219 marriage to Philippa of Dreux he fathered his successor Theobald II and Margaret, wife of Henry V of Luxembourg. He took the cross in 1239 and was killed at Gaza on 13 November.

en:
Henry III (1259–1302) was count of Bar from 1291. To balance the power of France on his border, in 1293 he married Eleanor, daughter of Edward I of England. Pressed by Edward to invade Champagne, he was defeated and captured by the lord of Châtillon.

He only regained freedom under the Treaty of Bruges in 1301, surrendering fortresses, doing homage to Philip IV for the western Barrois and pledging to crusade. At Naples he helped Charles II against Frederick II of Sicily, was mortally wounded in battle, and died in 1302.

zh:
亨利三世（1259—1302）自1291年起任巴尔伯爵。为制衡边境上日益强大的法国，他于1293年迎娶英格兰国王爱德华一世之女埃莉诺。爱德华敦促他入侵香槟，他却被沙蒂永领主击败俘虏。

他直到1301年依《布鲁日条约》才获释，条件是割让数座堡垒，为西部巴鲁瓦向法王腓力四世行臣服礼，并立誓参加十字军。他在那不勒斯协助查理二世抵御西西里的腓特烈二世时受致命伤，1302年死于当地。

en:
Henry of Bar (c. 1316–1380), lord of Pierrefort, was a son of Peter I of Bar and a captain of the king of France. In 1342 he married Isabella of Vergy.

In 1353 he arrested Philip of Navarre, new husband of the regent Yolande, who thereupon gave up the regency. In 1369 he supported his son Peter when the Lorrains and Messins besieged Pierrefort, forcing them to raise the siege. He died early in 1380.

Henry IV (c. 1315–1344) became count of Bar in 1336, succeeding his father Edward I, while his aunt Joan of Bar governed during his minority. In 1337 he warred with Duke Raoul of Lorraine until Philip VI of France arbitrated, and in 1339–1340 served Philip against Edward III of England.

He married Yolande of Dampierre; their sons Edward II and Robert I later ruled Bar. In 1344 he joined an embassy to Pope Clement VI, fell ill and died on 24 December.

Hugh of Bar (1318–1361) was a son of Peter I, lord of Pierrefort, and a grandson of Count Theobald II of Bar. In 1329 he became a canon of Verdun Cathedral, and in 1351 was appointed bishop of Verdun, consecrated the next year.

He kept good relations with the Holy See throughout his episcopate. In 1361 he set out on pilgrimage to the Holy Land, but died in the Sinai on 13 August before returning.

en:
Yolande of Dampierre (1326–1395), also called Yolande of Flanders, was the daughter of Robert of Cassel and a great-granddaughter of Count Guy. She inherited Cassel after her brother John's death in 1332, and in 1338 married Henry IV, Count of Bar.

After Henry died in 1344 she was left with two small sons and took the regency of Bar for Edward II. The Pierrepont lords claimed it too; she made them back down by allying with Philip VI of France and the Duke of Lorraine, and Edward was declared of age in 1349.

He died in 1352, and Yolande kept the regency for her younger son Robert. King John II forced her out in 1353; his capture at Poitiers in 1356 removed Joan of Bar's royal backing, and Yolande ruled again until Robert came of age in 1359. She died in 1395.

约朗德·德·当皮埃尔（1326—1395），又称佛兰德的约朗德，是罗贝尔·德·卡塞勒之女、伯爵居伊的曾孙女。1332年兄长让去世后，她继承卡塞勒，1338年嫁给巴尔伯爵亨利四世。

1344年亨利去世，留下两个年幼的儿子，她出任巴尔摄政，辅佐爱德华二世。皮埃尔蓬家族的领主也主张摄政权，她与法兰西国王腓力六世、洛林公爵结盟，迫使二人退让；1349年爱德华被宣布成年。

1352年爱德华去世，约朗德继续为幼子罗贝尔摄政。1353年国王让二世迫使她交出摄政权；1356年让二世在普瓦捷被俘，竞争者巴尔的让娜失去王室支持，约朗德重新执政，直到1359年罗贝尔成年。她于1395年去世。

Marie of Burgundy (c. 1298–1323/1336) was the youngest daughter of Robert II, Duke of Burgundy, and Agnes of France, daughter of Louis IX. On 11 February 1310 she married Edward I, Count of Bar, becoming countess of Bar.

Her children included Henry IV, who succeeded as count of Bar, and Eleanor, who married Duke Rudolph of Lorraine in 1330. She was last recorded in 1323 and was buried at Saint-Maxe in Bar-le-Duc.

en:
Peter I of Bar (c. 1272–1347), lord of Pierrefort, was a younger son of Count Theobald II and founder of the Pierrefort branch of his house. He married Joan of Vienne, and his children included Henry and Hugh.

After Count Henry IV died in 1344, Peter and a kinsman claimed seats on the regency council for the young Edward II, but the regent Yolande of Flanders, allied with King Philip VI, confined them to minor roles. Peter died on 30 November 1347.

皮尔福领主皮埃尔一世·德·巴尔（约1272—1347）是巴尔伯爵蒂博二世之子，巴尔家族皮尔福支的始祖。他娶维埃纳的让娜为妻，子女中包括亨利与于格。

1344年巴尔伯爵亨利四世去世后，他与一名族人要求参加年幼的爱德华二世的摄政会议，但摄政佛兰德的约兰德联合法王腓力六世，把他们排挤到次要位置。皮埃尔于1347年11月30日去世。

en:
Reginald I, called the One-Eyed (c. 1080–1149), ruled as count of Bar from 1105, inheriting Bar and Mousson from his father. In the Investiture Controversy he sided with the pope, and in 1113 Emperor Henry V stormed Bar castle and held him prisoner until he swore homage.

In 1134 he stormed Bouillon, claiming it as an heir of its former lord, but had to return it to the bishop of Liège in 1140. He joined the Second Crusade with his sons and drowned in the Mediterranean on the voyage home, before 10 March 1149.

雷诺一世（约1080—1149）绰号“独眼”，1105年起任巴尔伯爵，从父亲手中继承巴尔与穆松。在主教叙任权之争中他站在教宗一方；1113年皇帝亨利五世攻占巴尔城堡，将他囚禁，直到他宣誓效忠才获释。

1134年他强攻布永，以布永原领主继承人的身份主张此地，攻占后却于1140年被迫归还列日主教。他与诸子参加第二次十字军东征，归国途中溺亡于地中海，时为1149年3月10日之前。

en:
Reginald II (c. 1122–1170) was count of Bar and lord of Mousson from 1149, succeeding his father Reginald I, with whom he had gone on the Second Crusade in 1147. He resumed Bar's feud with the duke of Lorraine and the bishop of Metz.

In 1152 he attacked the abbey of Saint-Mihiel and was excommunicated, making public amends to be absolved. By his marriage in 1155 to Agnes of Champagne, daughter of Count Theobald of Blois and Champagne, he fathered Henry I and Theobald I, who each in turn ruled Bar. He died on 25 July 1170.

en:
Theobald I (c. 1158–1214) became count of Bar in 1190 after his brother Henry I died at the siege of Acre. Through his third marriage in 1197 to Ermesinde, heiress of Luxembourg, he also ruled Luxembourg; with Philip of Swabia's approval, he besieged Namur. The Treaty of Dinant confirmed the settlement in 1199.

In June 1211 he led troops to reinforce Simon de Montfort at the siege of Toulouse during the Albigensian Crusade. He died on 13 February 1214 and was buried at Saint-Mihiel, leaving Bar to his son Henry II.

en:
Theobald II (c. 1221–1291) became count of Bar in 1239 after his father Henry II died on the Barons' Crusade, with his mother Philippa of Dreux acting as regent until 1242. In 1245 he made peace with Matthew II of Lorraine, beginning decades of peace between their lands.

Fighting for his brother-in-law Guy of Dampierre in the Flanders succession war, he was captured at Westkapelle in 1253 and ransomed in September 1254, composing poetry while imprisoned. By charter on 21 April 1261 he founded the town of Pont-à-Mousson. He died in October 1291 and was succeeded by his son Henry III.

en:
Baraq, who on converting to Islam took the name Ghiyas-ud-din, was a great-grandson of Chagatai Khan and the father of Duwa. Raised at Kublai Khan's court, he seized the Chagatai throne by deposing Mubarak Shah in September 1266 and soon rejected Kublai's overlordship.

He defeated Kaidu but lost near Khujand, then made peace at Talas in 1269, receiving two-thirds of Transoxiana. Invading the Ilkhanate, he won in Khurasan but was routed by Abaqa near Herat on 22 July 1270. He died at Bukhara on 9 August 1271.

en:
Bartan Baghatur was a Mongol prince of the Borjigin in the twelfth century, the second son of Khabul Khan, founder of the Khamag Mongol. He never held the khanship: after Khabul died in 1148 it passed first to his cousin Ambaghai and then to his son Hotula.

Bartan remained chief of the Khiyad clan, bearing the warrior title baghatur. His son Yesugei was the father of Genghis Khan, making Bartan the great conqueror's grandfather.

en:
Gerhard von Wippingen (c. 1262–1325) was a cleric from the Vuippens nobility near Fribourg, whose uncle Otton de Grandson brought him to the English court. After serving Edward I on diplomatic missions, he became bishop of Lausanne in 1302 and bishop of Basel by papal appointment in 1309.

He ruled the see from Delémont, prosecuting beguines in Basel in 1320 and losing the lordship of Pfirt to Habsburg in 1324. He died on 17 March 1325 and was buried in Basel Minster.

He ruled the see from Delémont, prosecuting beguines in Basel in 1320 and losing the lordship of Pfirt to Habsburg in 1324. He died on 17 March 1325 and was buried in Basel Minster.

格哈德·冯·维平根（约1262—1325）出身弗里堡附近的维庞贵族家庭，叔父格朗松的奥托把他引荐到英格兰宫廷。他受爱德华一世派遣承担外交使命，1302年成为洛桑主教，1309年被教皇任命为巴塞尔主教。

他主要在德莱蒙城堡理政，1320年在巴塞尔追查贝居安派异端，1324年把费雷特的宗主权丢给哈布斯堡。1325年3月17日去世，葬于巴塞尔大教堂。

en:
William of Grandson, called the Great (died 1386), was a Vaudois knight and the younger son of Peter II of Grandson and Blanche of Savoy. He succeeded his father in 1348 as lord of Sainte-Croix, Cudrefin and Grandcour, and became one of the favourites and councillors of Count Amadeus VI.

In 1364 he was among the first fifteen knights of the Order of the Collar, which the count had just created, and in 1365 he gained rights over Aubonne and Coppet. He served in Savoyard campaigns in the Valais and Italy, and in 1366–1367 went with the count to Greece and Bulgaria.

In 1383 he was an executor of Amadeus VI's will, and in 1384 he knighted the young Amadeus VII at the siege of Sion, two years before his death in 1386.

纪尧姆·德·格朗松，绰号“伟大者”，是沃地区骑士，皮埃尔二世·德·格朗松与萨伏依的布朗什之幼子。1348年他继承父亲的圣克鲁瓦、屈德勒凡和格朗库尔领地，成为萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥六世身边的近臣与顾问。

1364年，他是伯爵新创的项圈骑士团最早的十五名骑士之一；1365年取得奥博讷与科佩的领地权利。他随萨伏依军队在瓦莱和意大利作战，1366至1367年又随伯爵远征希腊与保加利亚。

1383年，他是阿梅迪奥六世遗嘱的执行人之一；1384年，他在锡永围城战中为年轻的阿梅代七世授予骑士衔，两年后的1386年去世。

Hartung Münch von Landskron (c. 1265–1332) was a Basel cleric from one of the city's leading ministerial families, the son of mayor Heinrich I Münch. He held canonries at Basel and Strasbourg and became archdeacon of Basel in 1321.

After Gerhard von Wippingen died, the chapter elected him bishop on 22 March 1325. He resigned the see in 1328 and died on 25 October 1332, buried in the minster chapel he had founded.

Jacques de Grandson (died 1381) was the son of Othon II de Grandson and Jeanne de Pesmes, through whom he inherited the lordship of Pesmes in the Franche-Comté on her death in 1349.

His career was less distinguished than his father's: he was captured by the free companies and was remembered for plundering the treasury of Vergy. After his death in 1381, his widow had the Saint-Jean-Baptiste chapel built at Pesmes.

John of Chalon-Arlay (c. 1300–1335) was a Burgundian churchman of the Chalon-Arlay line, son of Lord John I of Arlay. He was appointed bishop of Basel by Pope John XXII on 30 March 1325, overriding the chapter's election of Hartung Münch.

Backed by Philip of Valois, he won the see only in 1328 after Hartung resigned, becoming bishop of Langres and administrator of Basel. He first entered Basel in 1330 and died in May or June 1335.

Johann II Senn von Münsingen (c. 1308–1365), trained in canon law, was elected bishop of Basel by its chapter in 1335. He rebuilt a diocese ruined by his predecessors' wars.

In 1337 he admitted craftsmen to the city council, in a charter that first mentioned Basel's guilds. Charles IV's visit in 1347 ended the interdict on Basel. His rule also saw the plague of 1348 and the great earthquake of 1356, and he died on 30 June 1365 and was buried in Basel Minster.

en:
Othon II of Grandson (c. 1305–1374) was a Vaudois knight. He became lord of Pesmes in 1327 through his wife Joan of Pesmes.

In 1336 he stayed loyal to Duke Odo IV when the leading Franche-Comté barons rebelled. He became a chief councillor of Odo and of his successor Philip of Rouvres, and inherited Grandson and Belmont in 1343.

After Philip of Rouvres died in 1361 he refused to serve Philip the Bold and took Edward III of England as his lord, doing homage for Belmont in 1362; only in 1366 did he return to Burgundy. In 1367 he freed the people of Suchy from mortmain. He died in autumn 1374, and his son Hugues succeeded him.

In 1328 he inherited all the Vaudois estates of his uncle Otto I and was enfeoffed with them by the count of Savoy the next year. He died around 1342 and was buried in the Franciscan church at Grandson.

en:
Batu Khan (c. 1205–1255), a son of Jochi and officially a grandson of Genghis Khan, founded the Golden Horde, which ruled the western steppe and Rus' lands. After Jochi's death Genghis made him head of the Jochid ulus.

In 1235 Ögedei named him head of the princes in the eldest sons' campaign, though a quarrel with Güyük never healed. His armies crushed the Cumans and Volga Bulgaria, took Ryazan in 1237 and Kiev in 1240, and in 1241 beat the Poles at Legnica and the Hungarians at Mohi, turning back in 1242 at Ögedei's death.

Batu made his court at Sarai on the lower Volga, and in 1251 backed Möngke for great khan. The Mongols called him Sain Khan, the good khan, for his leniency to his men. He died in 1255; his son Sartaq soon followed, and his brother Berke inherited the Horde.

拔都（约1205—1255）是术赤之子、名义上的成吉思汗之孙，创建了金帐汗国，这个蒙古国家统治西部草原和罗斯诸地。术赤死后，成吉思汗立他为术赤兀鲁思之主。

1235年，窝阔台任命他为长子西征的全体宗王之首，但他与贵由的嫌隙再未弥合。他的大军击溃钦察人和伏尔加保加利亚，1237年攻陷梁赞，1240年攻陷基辅，1241年在莱格尼察击败波兰人、在赛约河击败匈牙利人；1242年窝阔台死讯传来，大军撤回。

拔都在伏尔加河下游的萨莱建立汗廷，1251年支持蒙哥当选大汗。蒙古人因他宽待部下而称他赛因汗，意为善良的汗。1255年他去世，其子撒里答不久也去世，弟弟别儿哥继承汗位。

en:
Agnes of the Palatinate (1201–1267) was a daughter of the Welf Count Palatine Henry V and Agnes of Hohenstaufen. In 1222 she married Otto II Wittelsbach, a marriage through which the Wittelsbachs inherited the Palatinate and adopted the Palatine lion.

When Louis I died in 1231 she became duchess of Bavaria. Her five children included Louis II, father of Emperor Louis IV, Henry XIII and Elizabeth, wife of King Conrad IV. Agnes died in 1267 and was buried at Scheyern Abbey.

普法尔茨的阿格尼丝（1201—1267年）是韦尔夫家族的莱茵行宫伯爵海因里希五世与霍亨斯陶芬的阿格尼丝之女。1222年，她嫁给奥托二世·冯·维特尔斯巴赫；凭借这场婚姻，维特尔斯巴赫家族继承了普法尔茨，并采用普法尔茨之狮纹章。

1231年路德维希一世去世，她成为巴伐利亚公爵夫人。她生有五个子女，包括皇帝路德维希四世之父路德维希二世、亨利十三世，以及嫁给国王康拉德四世的伊丽莎白。1267年她去世，葬于沙伊恩修道院。

Elisabeth of Gorizia-Tyrol (c. 1262–1312) was the eldest daughter of Count Meinhard of Gorizia-Tyrol and Elisabeth of Bavaria, and half-sister of Conradin. In 1274 she married Albert of Habsburg, becoming duchess of Austria in 1282 and queen of Germany in 1298.

She bore him at least twelve children, including Frederick the Fair and Albert II. After Albert was murdered by his nephew John Parricida in 1308, she founded the monastery of Königsfelden on the spot, where she died and was buried in 1312.

en:
Henry IX the Black (c. 1075–1126), second son of Duke Welf I of Bavaria, gained Billung lands around Lüneburg through his marriage to Wulfhilde of Saxony around 1095. In 1106 he sought to succeed his father-in-law as Duke of Saxony, but King Henry V granted the duchy to Lothair of Supplinburg.

He succeeded his childless brother Welf II as duke in 1120 and helped bring about the Concordat of Worms in 1122. In the 1125 royal election he backed Lothair of Saxony over his own Hohenstaufen son-in-law. Abdicating in 1126 for his son Henry the Proud, he retired to Weingarten Abbey and died there on 13 December.

“黑者”亨利九世（约1075—1126）是巴伐利亚公爵韦尔夫一世的次子，约1095年娶萨克森的武尔夫希尔德为妻，由此获得吕讷堡一带的比隆家族领地。1106年他谋求继承岳父的萨克森公爵位，国王亨利五世却将公爵领封给了叙普林堡的洛泰尔。

1120年他继无嗣的兄长韦尔夫二世成为公爵，并促成1122年的《沃尔姆斯宗教协定》。1125年国王选举中，他转而支持萨克森公爵洛泰尔，没有支持自己的霍亨斯陶芬家族女婿。1126年他让位给儿子“骄傲者”亨利，退隐魏恩加滕修道院，同年12月13日死于那里。

Louis I Wittelsbach (1173–1231), called the Kelheimer, ruled as Duke of Bavaria from 1183 and, from 1214, as Count Palatine of the Rhine. He was the only surviving son of Duke Otto I and inherited as a child. He backed the Hohenstaufen emperors and accompanied Henry VI to Sicily in 1194.

Frederick II rewarded him with the Rhenish Palatinate in 1214, and his son Otto's marriage to Agnes of the Palatinate secured the electorate for the Wittelsbach. In 1221 he joined the Fifth Crusade at Damietta and was held hostage after the defeat at Mansurah. He was murdered on a bridge at Kelheim in 1231.

en:
Otto I Wittelsbach (c. 1117–1183), called the Redhead, was the first Wittelsbach Duke of Bavaria. Son of Count Palatine Otto IV of Wittelsbach, he succeeded his father as Count Palatine of Bavaria in 1156 and became a trusted military ally of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa. In 1155 he captured a position above a defile near Verona, securing the imperial army's return across the Alps.

After Henry the Lion was deposed, Barbarossa enfeoffed Otto with Bavaria at Altenburg in 1180. He died suddenly at Pfullendorf in 1183, after the Peace of Constance. His son Louis succeeded him.

en:
Otto IV of Scheyern (c. 1083–1156), second son of Count Eckhard I of Scheyern, accompanied Henry V on his Italian campaign of 1110–1111 and took part in the seizure of Pope Paschal II to force him to crown Henry emperor, for which Otto was excommunicated.

After his family moved its seat to Wittelsbach Castle near Aichach, he styled himself Otto of Wittelsbach from 1116, giving the dynasty its name. He became Count Palatine of Bavaria in 1120 and founded Indersdorf Abbey to atone for the papal kidnapping. His son Otto the Redhead became the first Wittelsbach Duke of Bavaria.

家族将居城迁到艾夏附近的维特尔斯巴赫城堡后，他从1116年起自称“冯·维特尔斯巴赫”，这个王朝由此得名。1120年他成为巴伐利亚行宫伯爵，并兴建因德斯多夫修道院，为劫持教皇一事赎罪。他的儿子“红发”奥托成为维特尔斯巴赫家族的首任巴伐利亚公爵。

en:
Welf I (c. 1035/1040–1101) was the son of Albert Azzo II of Este and Kunigunde of Altdorf, and founder of the younger House of Welf. He was made Duke of Bavaria by Emperor Henry IV in 1070.

In the Investiture Controversy he backed Pope Gregory VII and the anti-king Rudolf of Rheinfelden. Henry IV declared him deposed in 1077, but Welf kept his position with Bavarian and Italian support. He reconciled with Henry in 1095 and was confirmed as duke. By Judith of Flanders he fathered Welf II and Henry IX. His Bavarians were ambushed in Anatolia during the Crusade of 1101; Welf escaped but died on Cyprus while returning.

韦尔夫一世（约1035/1040—1101）是阿尔贝托·阿佐二世·德斯特与阿尔特多夫的库尼贡德之子，小韦尔夫家族的始祖。1070年，他被皇帝亨利四世封为巴伐利亚公爵。

主教叙任权之争中，他支持教皇格列高利七世和对立国王莱茵费尔登的鲁道夫。亨利四世于1077年宣布剥夺他的公爵领地，但韦尔夫在巴伐利亚人和意大利方面的支持下保住了地位。1095年他与亨利和解，公爵地位得到确认。他与佛兰德的朱迪丝生下韦尔夫二世和亨利九世。1101年十字军东征时，他的巴伐利亚军队在安纳托利亚遭伏击；韦尔夫逃脱，却在归途中死于塞浦路斯。

en:
Welf II the Fat (1072–1120), son of Duke Welf I of Bavaria and Judith of Flanders, married the much older Countess Matilda of Tuscany as a teenager in 1088 or 1089, binding his family to the papal side in the Investiture Controversy.

He fought Henry IV in Italy in 1090, then separated from Matilda around 1095 and made peace with the emperor. He succeeded as duke in 1101 and remained married to Matilda until her death in 1115. He died childless at Kaufering on 24 September 1120.

“胖子”韦尔夫二世（1072—1120）是巴伐利亚公爵韦尔夫一世与佛兰德的朱迪丝之子。他少年时便在1088或1089年娶了年长二十多岁的托斯卡纳女伯爵玛蒂尔达，借此在主教叙任权之争中把家族与教皇阵营绑在一起。

1090年他在意大利与亨利四世作战，约1095年与玛蒂尔达分居，并与皇帝和解。1101年他继位为公爵，与玛蒂尔达的婚姻维持到1115年她去世为止。1120年9月24日他无嗣而终于考弗灵。

en:
Albert II of Regenstein (c. 1293–1349), son of Count Ulrich III, became regent of the county in 1310. His feud with the bishop of Halberstadt turned violent in 1336, when he raided Quedlinburg's lands and seized its new town; captured that July, legend keeps him for twenty months in a wooden chest in Quedlinburg's town hall.

The 1338 peace made him accept the bishop as the town's protector. In 1349 he was murdered by assassins hired by Bishop Albert II of Halberstadt.

阿尔布雷希特二世·冯·雷根施泰因（约1293—1349）是伯爵乌尔里希三世之子，1310年成为伯国摄政。他与哈尔伯施塔特主教结仇，1336年冲突激化：他洗劫奎德林堡乡野并占据新城，同年7月被俘。相传他被关在奎德林堡市政厅的一个木箱里长达二十个月。

1338年双方和解，他承认主教为该城保护者。1349年，他被哈尔伯施塔特主教阿尔布雷希特二世雇凶刺杀。

en:
Ulrich III of Regenstein-Heimburg (c. 1287–1322/23) was a count of the Regenstein line in the Harz, holding the county of Heimburg and the lordship of Derenburg. He was the son of Count Albert I of Regenstein and Sophie of Lippe.

In 1308 he married Sophie of Anhalt-Aschersleben. Their marriage produced sixteen children, including his successors Bernhard I and Albert II of Regenstein, and he died around 1322–1323.

Johannes I Pfefferhard (born before 1300, died 23 May 1331), a cleric from a wealthy Konstanz patrician family, served as bishop of Chur from 1325 until his death. He studied at Bologna and held church posts at Steffisburg, Chur, Konstanz and Würzburg.

He sided with the pope against Emperor Louis IV. Consecrated at Avignon in 1330, he was seized on his way home by the barons of Grünenberg and held in a castle called Tüfelsruggen; he died in captivity and was buried at Binzen.

en:
Rudolf III of Montfort (born 1260–1275, died March 1334) was a Swabian count's son who became bishop of Chur and Konstanz. A canon and later provost at Chur, he was elected its bishop in 1322, but Pope John XXII made him bishop of Konstanz, while he administered Chur until 1325.

He backed the Habsburgs but sided with the pope against Emperor Louis IV, whose regalia he accepted in 1332. The pope excommunicated him in 1333, and he died at Arbon in 1334, buried in unconsecrated ground.

鲁道夫三世·冯·蒙特福特（生于1260至1275年间，卒于1334年3月）是施瓦本伯爵之子，后成为库尔与康斯坦茨主教。他曾任库尔的法政牧师和座堂主任司铎，1322年当选库尔主教，但教皇约翰二十二世任命他为康斯坦茨主教，他仍代管库尔教区至1325年。

en:
Ulrich of Lenzburg, also called Ulrich Ribi (died 25 March 1355), was an Augustinian hermit in Mainz before becoming bishop of Chur in 1331. As a papal penitentiary he had opposed Emperor Louis IV, and in 1338 he was sent to Avignon to mediate with Benedict XII.

In the wars over Tyrol he allied with Charles IV of Bohemia; in 1347 Louis of Brandenburg captured him and seized Chur's Tyrolean lands. In 1352 and 1354 he backed Albert II of Austria against the Swiss.

en:
Frederick II of Baden (died 22 June 1333) ruled as margrave from 1291, when his father Herman VII died, until his own death. He first governed jointly with his brother Rudolf IV; after the margraviate was partitioned, Frederick held Baden-Baden and Eberstein while Rudolf kept Pforzheim.

He married Agnes of Weinsberg before 1312 and, after her death in 1320, Margaret of Vaihingen. His son by the first marriage, Herman IX, succeeded him in Eberstein.

巴登的腓特烈二世（卒于1333年6月22日）自1291年父亲赫尔曼七世去世后担任巴登藩侯，统治直至本人去世。他起初与兄弟鲁道夫四世共同执政，后来藩侯国分家，腓特烈分得巴登-巴登和埃伯施泰因，鲁道夫分得普福尔茨海姆。

1312年前他娶魏因斯贝格的阿格尼丝，后者1320年去世后又娶法伊欣根的玛格丽特。第一次婚姻所生之子赫尔曼九世在埃伯施泰因继其位。

en:
Frederick III, called the Peaceful (1327 – 2 September 1353), was Margrave of Baden from 1348 until his death. The elder son of Margrave Rudolf IV and Marie, he and his brother Rudolf V took power together after their father's death and divided the inheritance: Frederick made Baden-Baden his residence while Rudolf ruled Baden-Pforzheim.

Around 1345 he married Margareta, daughter of Margrave Rudolf Hesso of Baden-Baden; their son Rudolf VI later reunited the margraviate. Frederick died on 2 September 1353.

巴登藩侯腓特烈三世（1327—1353年9月2日），绰号“和平者”，1348年起任藩侯直至去世。他是藩侯鲁道夫四世与玛丽亚的长子，1348年父亲死后与弟弟鲁道夫五世共同掌权并分割遗产：他以巴登-巴登为驻地，鲁道夫五世统治巴登-普福尔茨海姆。

en:
Herman V (c. 1180–16 January 1243) was Margrave of Baden from 1190, making Pforzheim the margraviate's seat in 1219. The son of Margrave Herman IV, he married Countess Palatine Irmengard of the Rhine in 1217 and became a loyal follower of Emperor Frederick II.

He joined the Fifth Crusade, where he was captured in Egypt in 1221. He founded Stuttgart, Backnang and Pforzheim and fought the Mongols at Liegnitz in 1241.

zh:
赫尔曼五世（约1180—1243年1月）自1190年起任巴登藩侯，1219年将普福尔茨海姆定为藩侯国治所。他是藩侯赫尔曼四世之子，1217年娶莱茵行宫伯爵之女伊尔门加德，后来成为皇帝腓特烈二世的忠实追随者。

他参加第五次十字军东征，于1221年在埃及被俘。他建立了斯图加特、巴克南和普福尔茨海姆，并于1241年在莱格尼察抗击蒙古人。

en:
Hermann IX of Baden-Eberstein (died 13 April 1353) was the son of Margrave Frederick II of Baden-Eberstein and Agnes of Weinsberg. On his father's death in 1333 he succeeded to the Eberstein share of the margraviate.

In 1344 he gave the Iburg to his uncle Rudolf IV of Baden-Pforzheim, but in 1350 King Charles IV enfeoffed him with it again. In 1341 he married Matilda of Vaihingen; their son Frederick IV died before him, so when Hermann died in 1353 his cousin Rudolf VI inherited Eberstein.

巴登-埃伯施泰因藩侯赫尔曼九世（1353年4月13日卒）是巴登-埃伯施泰因藩侯腓特烈二世与阿格妮丝·冯·魏因斯贝格之子。1333年父亲去世后，他继承藩侯领地中的埃伯施泰因部分。

en:
Herman VII of Baden, called the Rouser (1266–12 July 1291), ruled as Margrave of Baden from 1288 until his early death. The son of Margrave Rudolf I and Kunigunde of Eberstein, he married Agnes of Truhendingen before October 1278, and their children included Frederick II, Rudolf IV and Herman VIII.

In 1291 he acquired Weißenburg Monastery lands around Bietigheim. He died on 12 July 1291 and was buried in Lichtenthal Abbey, leaving the margraviate to his young sons.

en:
Kunigunde of Zollern (died 1381) was the daughter of Count Frederick VI of Zollern and Kunigunde of Baden, herself a daughter of Margrave Rudolf I of Baden. She became a Cistercian nun at Lichtenthal Abbey near Baden-Baden and served as its abbess from 1367 until her death.

She is last attested in October 1380, and the convent's necrology records her death on 12 August, placed in 1381. An older abbess list that credited her with office in 1295–1310 confuses her with her mother of the same name.

en:
Rudolf IV of Baden-Pforzheim (died 1348) was a younger son of Margrave Hermann VII of Baden. Destined for the church, he served as a canon at Speyer until his father's death in 1291, when the margraviate was divided and he received Baden-Pforzheim, ruling first with his brother Hermann VIII and alone after 1300.

He later left Duke Leopold I of Austria for Emperor Louis IV, and in 1335 inherited Baden-Baden from his cousin Rudolf Hesso. His sons Frederick III and Rudolf V divided his lands.

en:
Rudolf V of Baden-Pforzheim (died 28 August 1361) was a younger son of Margrave Rudolf IV. In 1348 he succeeded his father in Baden-Pforzheim while his brother Frederick III took Baden-Baden.

Emperor Charles IV could not redeem the Ortenau lands pledged to his father, so Rudolf kept them. In 1347 he married Adelaide; the marriage was childless, so in 1356 he made his nephew Rudolf VI his heir. On his death in 1361 Baden-Pforzheim passed to Baden-Baden, reuniting Baden.

en:
Rudolf I (1230–19 November 1288), son of Margrave Herman V of Baden, acted as regent for his nephew Margrave Frederick I from 1250 to 1267 and ruled Baden as margrave from 1268 until his death. After his brother Herman VI married into the Austrian ducal family, Rudolf ruled Baden-Baden alone.

In 1257 he married Kunigunde of Eberstein, through whom he acquired Eberstein Castle, and in 1250 he began building Hohenbaden Castle. He patronized churches and abbeys and was buried at Lichtenthal Abbey.

Fakhr al-Dawla Shah-Ghazi was the Baduspanid ustandar of Rustamdar who succeeded his brother Jalal al-Dawla Iskandar in 1360 and ruled until his death in 1379. As a prince he had held Natelrustaq under Iskandar.

As ruler he is chiefly remembered for patronising the scholar Awliya Allah Amuli, who at his request composed the Tarikh-i Ruyan, a chronicle of Ruyan and its Baduspanid rulers. He died in 1379 and was succeeded by his son Adud al-Dawla Qubad.

法赫尔·道拉·沙阿·加齐是巴杜斯潘王朝统治鲁斯塔姆达尔的乌斯坦达尔，1360年继兄长贾拉勒·道拉·伊斯坎达尔之位，统治至1379年去世。他身为王子时曾受伊斯坎达尔委任管辖纳特尔鲁斯塔克。

在位时他最知名的事迹是资助学者奥利亚·安拉·阿穆利，后者奉他之命撰写《鲁扬史》，记述鲁扬地区与巴杜斯潘历代君主。他于1379年去世，其子阿杜德·道拉·库巴德继位。

en:
Jalal al-Dawla Iskandar was ustandar of the Baduspanids of Rustamdar from 1333 to 1360. A son of Taj al-Dawla Ziyar, he secured his father's accession by murdering their uncle Nasir al-Din Shahriyar, and received Kalarrustaq to rule.

Exploiting the Ilkhanate's collapse after 1335, he expanded deep into the southern Alborz; in 1344 he and the Bavandid Hasan II destroyed a Sarbadar army. He founded Kojur in 1346 and conquered Daylam. In 1360 his bodyguard fatally wounded him at a drinking party, and his brother Fakhr al-Dawla Shah-Ghazi succeeded him.

贾拉勒·道拉·伊斯坎达尔是1333至1360年统治鲁斯塔姆达尔的巴杜斯潘王朝乌斯坦达尔，即君主。他是塔季·道拉·齐亚尔之子，因亲手杀死叔父纳西尔丁·沙赫里亚尔而帮助父亲夺得王位，受封统治卡拉尔鲁斯塔克。

他乘1335年后伊利汗国崩溃之机，向厄尔布尔士山脉南麓大举扩张；1344年与巴文德王朝的哈桑二世联手歼灭萨尔巴达尔军队。1346年他兴建科朱尔城并征服德莱木。1360年他在酒宴上被侍卫刺成致命伤，其弟法赫尔·道拉·沙阿·加齐继位。

en:
Taj al-Dawla Ziyar was the Baduspanid ustandar of Rustamdar and Ruyan from 1325 until his death, and the first of his line to take the title Malik. In 1325 he seized the throne after instigating his son Iskandar to murder his brother Nasir al-Din Shahriyar.

When another brother, Izz al-Dawla, challenged him with the Ilkhan's support, Ziyar defeated him and consolidated his rule over Ruyan. He died at Kavir in 1333, leaving sons including Jalal al-Dawla Iskandar and Fakhr al-Dawla Shah-Ghazi.

塔季·道莱·齐亚尔是巴杜斯潘王朝鲁斯塔姆达尔与鲁扬的乌斯坦达尔，1325年至去世为止在位，也是家族中第一个采用“马利克”称号的统治者。1325年，他指使儿子伊斯坎达尔谋杀兄长纳西尔丁·沙赫里亚尔，随即夺取王位。

另一个兄弟伊兹·道莱在伊利汗支持下起兵争位，被他击败，齐亚尔由此巩固了对鲁扬的统治。他于1333年卒于卡维尔，儿子包括贾拉勒·道拉·伊斯坎达尔和法赫尔·道拉·沙阿·加齐。

en:
Awang Alak Betatar, who as Sultan Muhammad Shah (died c. 1402) founded the Sultanate of Brunei, was, in Brunei tradition, a son of Dewa Emas Kayangan. Ruling first as raja from Kota Batu with his brothers, he cast off Majapahit overlordship and campaigned against the Melanau lands.

In 1363 or 1368 he converted to Islam and took the name Muhammad Shah, becoming Brunei's first sultan, and in 1371 he received a Ming embassy from the Hongwu Emperor. He died around 1402.

阿旺·阿拉克·贝塔塔尔即苏丹马合谟沙（约1402年卒），相传为德瓦·埃马斯·卡扬安之子，是文莱苏丹国的创立者。他最初以拉者身份在哥打巴都与诸兄弟共同执政，摆脱满者伯夷的宗主权，并出兵攻打马兰诺人地区。

1363或1368年他皈依伊斯兰教，改名马合谟沙，成为文莱第一位苏丹；1371年他接见了明朝洪武帝派来的使团。约1402年他去世。

The Brunei epic Syair Awang Semaun presents Awang Semaun as the half-brother of Awang Alak Betatar, founder and first sultan of Brunei, and as one of the fourteen children of Dewa Emas Kayangan. Tradition places him among the new raja's chief ministers, holding Kota Batu.

He marched with Alak Betatar and the raja's ministers against the Melanau stronghold of Igan during Brunei's early conquests. The Malay poem recounting Brunei's founding bears his name.

Brunei tradition, preserved in the epic Syair Awang Semaun, names Dewa Emas Kayangan as the father of fourteen siblings. His sons included Awang Alak Betatar, the first sultan Muhammad Shah, Awang Semaun and Pateh Berbai, later Sultan Ahmad.

The tale makes him set out to find tembadau wild cattle for his pregnant wife; after finding the animal he ascended to the sky, where he was called Batara Kala di Kayangan.

en:
Berke Khan (c. 1208–1266), a son of Jochi and grandson of Genghis Khan, ruled the Golden Horde from 1257 and was the first Mongol ruler to establish Islam officially in a khanate; his name means ‘stubborn’. After Batu's successors Sartaq and Ulaghchi died he governed until confirmed as khan in 1257.

His conversion, begun in Batu's lifetime, was probably political, aimed at the merchants of Volga Bulgaria and Central Asia, and he built mosques. He quarrelled with his cousin Hulagu over Azerbaijan and the 1258 sack of Baghdad and killing of the caliph; allied with Mamluk sultan Baibars, he fought Hulagu in the Caucasus from late 1262.

An Egyptian envoy in 1263 described his thin beard, jewelled gold earring and bad leg. Berke died in 1266 or 1267 crossing the Kura against Hulagu's son Abaqa; his grandnephew Mengu-Timur succeeded him and kept the Mamluk alliance.

别儿哥（约1208—1266）是术赤之子、成吉思汗之孙，1257年起统治金帐汗国，也是第一位在汗国正式确立伊斯兰教的蒙古统治者；名字在蒙古语中意为“顽固”。拔都的继承人撒里答、乌剌黑赤相继去世后代为执政，1257年受封。

他在拔都生前已皈依，这多半是政治之举，意在争取伏尔加保加尔和中亚商人，并兴建清真寺。他与堂兄弟旭烈兀因阿塞拜疆及1258年巴格达遭洗劫、哈里发被杀交恶，遂与马穆鲁克苏丹拜巴尔斯结盟，1262年末起在高加索交战。

1263年埃及使者描绘他胡须稀疏，耳戴镶宝石的金环，腿脚有疾。1266或1267年，他在渡库拉河攻打旭烈兀之子阿八哈时去世，堂侄孙忙哥帖木儿继位并延续同盟。

en:
Bernt Notke (c. 1440–1509) was the leading late Gothic sculptor and painter of the Baltic region. He possibly trained in Flanders before settling in Lübeck in the 1460s, where he ran an altarpiece and sculpture workshop.

His works include Lübeck Cathedral's triumphal cross and a Saint George and the Dragon, commissioned by Sten Sture after Brunkeberg and unveiled in 1489. He lived in Stockholm in 1491–1497, serving as Sweden's mint master, and died in Lübeck in 1509.

伯恩特·诺特克（约1440—1509）是波罗的海地区最重要的晚期哥特式雕塑家兼画家。他早年可能在佛兰德学艺，1460年代定居吕贝克，经营制作祭坛与木雕的作坊。

代表作包括吕贝克主教座堂的凯旋十字架，以及斯滕·斯图雷在布伦克贝格之战后委托、1489年揭幕的《圣乔治与龙》。1491至1497年他居于斯德哥尔摩，其间担任瑞典铸币官，1509年在吕贝克去世。

en:
Bertrand du Guesclin (c. 1320–1380) was a Breton knight, nicknamed the Eagle of Brittany. He defended Rennes against the English in 1356–1357 and was captured at Auray in 1364.

In 1366 he led free companies to Castile for Henry of Trastámara. Defeated and captured at Nájera in 1367, he was ransomed and helped him seize the throne at Montiel in 1369.

Appointed constable of France by Charles V in 1370, he avoided pitched battles while reconquering Poitou and Saintonge. He died at Châteauneuf-de-Randon in 1380 and was buried at Saint-Denis.

贝特朗·杜·盖克兰（约1320—1380）是布列塔尼骑士，绰号“布列塔尼之鹰”。他在1356—1357年坚守雷恩、抵御英军，1364年在欧赖战役被俘。

1366年他率自由佣兵团赴卡斯蒂利亚，支持特拉斯塔马拉的恩里克；1367年在纳赫拉战败被俘，获赎后于1369年在蒙铁尔帮助恩里克夺得王位。

1370年他被查理五世任命为法兰西王室统帅，力避正面会战，逐步收复普瓦图和圣通日。1380年他病逝于朗东新堡，葬于圣但尼。

Ualgarg Mór Ó Ruairc (died 1346), a son of Domhnall Carrach, ruled the kingdom of West Breifne from 1316. Inaugurated with the backing of Fedlim Ó Conchobair of Connacht, he fought beside him at the Second Battle of Athenry.

He backed Toirdelbach Ó Conchobair's claim to Connacht in 1318 and expelled the Clan Muircheartaigh from Breifne in 1343. He was killed in a sudden fight at Calry in 1346. His thirty-year reign restored Ó Ruairc power, and the rival O'Rourke branches that emerged in the 15th century traced their descent to him.

Eustace IV (c. 1129–1153) was the eldest son of King Stephen of England and Matilda I of Boulogne, and ruled the County of Boulogne from 1146. After his father took the English throne in 1135, he was heir apparent through the Anarchy, the civil war in which Empress Matilda also claimed the crown.

In 1137 he did homage for Normandy to King Louis VII of France, and in 1140 he married Louis's sister Constance. He died suddenly on 17 August 1153 while raiding church lands near Bury St Edmunds, clearing the way for Henry Plantagenet's succession, and was buried at Faversham Abbey.

en:
William I of Boulogne (c. 1137–1159), was the second son of King Stephen of England and Matilda I of Boulogne. In 1148 he married Isabel de Warenne, Countess of Surrey. In 1153 Stephen agreed to recognize Henry Plantagenet as his heir instead of William's brother Eustace IV. After Eustace died, the Treaty of Wallingford ending the Anarchy left William Boulogne and the lands intended for both brothers.

Henry II initially allowed him to keep the earldom of Surrey through his wife. William was suspected of knowing of a Flemish plot to kill Henry and fled to Normandy. He died of disease near Toulouse on 11 October 1159, childless, and his sister Marie I succeeded him.

纪尧姆一世（约1137—1159），是英格兰国王斯蒂芬与布洛涅女伯爵玛蒂尔达一世的次子。1148年他娶萨里女伯爵伊莎贝尔·德·瓦伦。1153年斯蒂芬同意让亨利·金雀花作为继承人，取代纪尧姆的兄长尤斯塔斯四世。尤斯塔斯死后，结束“无政府时期”的《沃灵福德条约》将布洛涅和原定由兄弟二人继承的领地留给纪尧姆。

亨利二世起初允许他凭妻子的权利保有萨里伯爵领。纪尧姆涉嫌事先知晓佛兰德人刺杀国王的阴谋，逃往诺曼底。1159年10月11日他在图卢兹附近染病去世，无嗣，由姐妹玛丽一世继位。

Ida of Boulogne (c. 1160–1216) ruled the county of Boulogne in her own right from 1173, when her father Matthew of Alsace died, until her death. The elder daughter of Matthew and Countess Marie I, she was twice widowed before 1190.

In 1190 Count Reginald I of Dammartin abducted her; she became his wife and bore the future Countess Matilda II of Boulogne. Ida died in 1216.

en:
Marie of Boulogne (1136–1182), also called Mary of Blois, was the youngest daughter of King Stephen of England and Matilda of Boulogne. Dedicated to the Church as a child, she became abbess of Romsey in the late 1150s.

When her brother William died in 1159, she inherited the County of Boulogne. In 1160 Matthew of Alsace removed her from her abbey and married her; the Church forced them to separate in 1169. She then returned to religious life, leaving two daughters, Ida and Matilda.

en:
Matthew of Alsace (c. 1137–1173) was a younger son of Thierry of Flanders and Sibylla of Anjou. In 1160 Henry II of England arranged his marriage to Mary of Blois, abbess of Romsey and heiress of Boulogne, making him count of Boulogne; because Mary was a nun, he was excommunicated.

Henry's refusal to cede Mortain led Matthew to ally with Louis VII of France. Separated from Mary in 1170, he ruled through their daughters Ida and Matilda. In 1173 he joined Henry the Young King's revolt and, invading Normandy with his brother Philip of Flanders, was mortally wounded by a crossbow at Driencourt on 25 July.

阿尔萨斯的马修（约1137—1173）是佛兰德伯爵蒂埃里与安茹的西比拉之幼子。1160年，英格兰国王亨利二世安排他娶了罗姆西修道院女院长、布洛涅女继承人布卢瓦的玛丽，他就此成为布洛涅伯爵；因玛丽是修女，他被开除教籍。

亨利拒绝交出莫尔坦，促使马修与法王路易七世结盟。1170年他与玛丽分居，以两个女儿伊达和玛蒂尔达的名义统治。1173年他参加幼王亨利的叛乱，与兄长佛兰德伯爵菲利普一世一同入侵诺曼底，7月25日在德朗库尔被弩箭重伤，随后去世。

en:
Matilda II of Dammartin (1202–1259) inherited Boulogne from her mother Ida in 1216. In 1223 she married Philip Hurepel, son of Philip II of France, and reigned with him as co-ruler until he died in 1234. In 1238 she married the Portuguese infante Afonso, who became Afonso III in 1248, renounced Boulogne and made her queen of Portugal.

They had no surviving children, and she reportedly was not allowed to follow him to Portugal. They divorced in 1253. In 1258 she charged Afonso with bigamy before Pope Alexander IV over his marriage to Beatrice of Castile. She died in January 1259.

达马尔坦的玛蒂尔达二世（1202—1259）1216年从母亲伊达手中继承布洛涅。1223年她嫁给法国国王腓力二世之子腓力·于雷佩尔，他作为共同执政者与她一同统治，直至1234年去世。1238年她改嫁葡萄牙王子阿方索，阿方索于1248年即位为阿方索三世，放弃布洛涅，她成为葡萄牙王后。

两人没有存活的子女，据记载她未获准随丈夫前往葡萄牙。两人于1253年离婚。1258年因阿方索另娶卡斯蒂利亚的比阿特丽斯，她向教皇亚历山大四世控告他重婚。1259年1月她去世。

en:
Renaud of Dammartin (c. 1165–1227) was the eldest son of Alberic III of Dammartin and a childhood friend of Philip Augustus. In 1191 his father abducted Ida, Countess of Boulogne, and had Renaud marry her, making him count of Boulogne. In 1203 he and Ida granted a charter to the merchants of Boulogne.

In 1212, after Philip seized his lands, Renaud allied with King John at Lambeth and joined the 1214 invasion of France. He commanded the Brabançons at Bouvines, where he was captured, and spent the rest of his life chained at Péronne, dying in 1227. His daughter Matilda II inherited Boulogne.

雷诺·德·达马尔坦（约1165—1227）是阿尔贝里克三世·德·达马尔坦之长子，与腓力·奥古斯都自幼交好。1191年，父亲绑架布洛涅女伯爵伊达并让雷诺娶她，他因而成为布洛涅伯爵。1203年雷诺与伊达向布洛涅商人颁发特许状。

1212年腓力没收其领地后，雷诺在兰贝斯与英格兰国王约翰结盟，加入1214年入侵法国的联军。他在布汶战役中指挥布拉班特人，被俘后一直被锁链锁在佩罗讷，1227年死于狱中。其女玛蒂尔达二世继承了布洛涅伯国。

en:
Belgutei (c. 1161–c. 1271) was a son of Yesugei and a half-brother of Genghis Khan. After his brother Begter was killed by Temujin in youth, Belgutei became his loyal follower.

As a general and envoy he once dissuaded Temujin from pursuing the man who slashed his arm at a banquet. After the empire was proclaimed in 1206, he was enfeoffed as prince with three thousand households. Tradition credits him with longevity.

en:
Kumun Buqa was a Borjigin prince, the second son of Belgutei and a nephew of Genghis Khan. He campaigned against the Jin with Ögedei Khan, and in spring 1232 crossed the Yellow River to join Tolui's army at the Battle of Sanfengshan, where the Mongols destroyed the pick of the Jin forces and captured General Yila Pu'a.

From 1235 he led armies against the Southern Song, taking several cities including Zaoyang and Huangzhou. Chinese literati praised him as a disciplined commander who spared the populace.

en:
Bhanji Jethwa was the Jethwa Rajput rana of Ghumli, the last Jethwa ruler to hold the ancient capital. In 1309 he repulsed an attack on Ghumli by Jam Unad of the Jadeja clan.

In 1313 Unad's son Jam Barmaniya stormed Ghumli and drove him out; he fled to Ranpur, and the city was left in ruins. Bardic tradition blamed the fall on the curse of the sati Sone, whose lover he had killed. His widow Rani Kalabai later retook lands as far as Ranpur.

班吉·杰特瓦是古姆利的杰特瓦拉杰普特拉纳，也是最后一位据守该古都的杰特瓦君主。1309年，他击退了贾德贾氏族首领贾姆·乌纳德对古姆利的进攻。

1313年，乌纳德之子贾姆·巴尔马尼亚攻破城池，班吉出逃，退往兰布尔，古姆利沦为废墟。诗人传说将城破归因于萨蒂索妮的诅咒——他曾害死她的情郎。他的遗孀卡拉巴伊后来起兵收复土地，兵锋直至兰布尔。

en:
'Izz al-Din Ahmad al-Bukhti was emir of the Bohtan principality, ruling from its centre at Jazirat ibn Umar, modern Cizre. In 1336 his tribesmen seized the city with the help of al-Ashraf, emir of Hisn Kayfa, whose daughter he married.

Bohtan consolidated its rule and developed Cizre. 'Izz al-Din reigned from 1335 to 1362, when its rulers still followed Yazidism, and was succeeded by his son Sayf al-Din Isa.

en:
Engelbert von Dolen was a Baltic German churchman from a vassal family long settled in Livonia. First documented in 1323 as provost of Dorpat cathedral, he was elected bishop of Dorpat that year and won papal confirmation at Avignon.

In 1336 he crowned King Magnus Eriksson of Sweden. A consistent opponent of the Teutonic Order, he was transferred to the archbishopric of Riga in 1341 and stayed at the papal court in Avignon, where he died on 3 September 1347.

zh:
恩格尔贝特·冯·多伦是波罗的海德意志教士，出身于久居利沃尼亚的封臣家族。1323年，他首次见于记载，时任多尔帕特座堂主任，同年当选多尔帕特主教，在阿维尼翁获得教皇确认。

1336年，他为瑞典国王马格努斯·埃里克松加冕。他一贯与条顿骑士团为敌，1341年调任里加大主教，此后留在阿维尼翁教廷，1347年9月3日在当地去世。

en:
Jakob (died 1337) was bishop of Ösel-Wiek from 1322, when Pope John XXII appointed him at Avignon. A former scholasticus of the Tartu cathedral chapter, he paid 1300 florins for his confirmation, almost as much as the other bishops combined, marking him as perhaps the richest man in Livonia.

In 1323 he fixed the bounds of Haapsalu's town territory with the vassals of Läänemaa, and in 1326 he fell into dispute with the archbishop of Riga. He died at Lübeck in 1337.

雅各布（？—1337）自1322年起担任厄塞尔-维克主教，当年由教宗约翰二十二世在阿维尼翁任命。他原是塔尔图主教座堂的掌校司铎，为确认任职向教廷缴纳1300弗罗林，几乎相当于利沃尼亚其他主教所缴之和，可能是利沃尼亚最富有的人。

1323年，他与莱内马的封臣划定哈普萨卢城镇辖地边界；1326年与里加大主教发生争执。1337年，他在吕贝克去世。

en:
ʿAlam al-Din, son of Siraj al-Din Umar, is known from a marriage contract in the Kanz documentary corpus. In 734 AH/1334 CE he married Umm al-Khayr, daughter of Rukn al-Din al-Husayn and niece of Kanz al-Dawla Abu Abdallah Muhammad, the Muslim Kanz leader who had ruled at Dongola.

The contract reflects marriage alliances within the Kanz elite strung between Aswan and Nubia. No narrative chronicle records his birth, death, offices or later life.

en:
Rukn al-Din al-Husayn was a member of the Kanz elite, known from two marriage contracts from the Aswan region. In 734 AH/1334 CE his daughter Umm al-Khayr married ʿAlam al-Din, son of Siraj al-Din Umar; in 742 AH/1341 she married ʿIzz al-Din Afrun.

Robin Seignobos identifies Umm al-Khayr as a niece of Kanz al-Dawla Abu Abdallah Muhammad, the Kanz leader who had seized power at Dongola, placing Rukn in the same Kanz family network.

en:
Sayf al-Din Abu Abdallah Muhammad, known as Kanz al-Dawla, was emir of the Banu Kanz of Aswan and a son of Shuja al-Din Nasr. In 1316 his uncle Karanbas, ruler of Nubia, proposed him as successor, but the Mamluk sultan detained him and sent Barshanbu to take the throne.

Released after Karanbas fell, Muhammad won Nubian support and Barshanbu was killed in 1317. After his uncle Abram arrested him and died soon afterwards, he was crowned king in 1318. He still claimed the throne in a marriage contract of 1333.

赛夫丁·阿布·阿卜杜拉·穆罕默德号坎兹·道拉，是阿斯旺巴努-坎兹的埃米尔、舒贾丁·纳斯尔之子。1316年，他的舅父、努比亚统治者克兰巴斯提名他为继承人，但马穆鲁克苏丹扣留了他，派巴尔尚布夺取王位。

克兰巴斯失势后，穆罕默德获释南行，赢得努比亚人的支持，巴尔尚布在1317年的争斗中被杀。舅父阿布拉姆拘捕他后不久去世，他于1318年被拥立加冕。在1333年的一份婚约中，他仍主张王位。

Umm al-Khayr was a daughter of the Kanz emir Rukn al-Din al-Husayn and a niece of Kanz al-Dawla Muhammad, the Muslim king of Dongola. She appears in a family archive of Arabic legal documents from Aswan.

A marriage contract records her wedding in 1334 to ʿAlam al-Din, son of Siraj al-Din Umar, and after his death another contract records her remarriage in 1341 to ʿIzz al-Din Afrun. A contract of 1343 records the marriage of her female slave Maliha.

en:
Stefan II (died 1345) was bishop of Lebus from 1316, though his position was confirmed by the pope only in 1326 during a stay at Avignon. In 1326 his episcopal seat at Göritz was destroyed by Brandenburg troops, so he sought the protection of the Polish kings, whose coronation he attended in 1333.

Driven from his diocese in 1339, he became suffragan bishop at Wrocław and sat as a papal commissioner in the Warsaw trial against the Teutonic Order. He died at Wrocław in 1345.

en:
Alidosio Alidosi, known as Alidosio della Massa, founded the Castel del Rio branch of the Alidosi, the dynasty that ruled Imola. He was the first signore of Castel del Rio, then called the Massa di Sant'Ambrogio, a fief granted his ancestors by Emperor Otto IV.

In 1304 he served the Florentine Republic as capitano del popolo. He died after 1304 and was succeeded by his son Gentile; another son, Guido, carried on the line.

阿利多西奥·阿利多西，人称阿利多西奥·德拉马萨，是统治伊莫拉的阿利多西家族卡斯泰尔德尔里奥支系的始祖。他是卡斯泰尔德尔里奥的第一任领主——该地当时称圣安布罗焦马萨，由皇帝奥托四世封授给他的先人。

1304年，他出任佛罗伦萨共和国的人民领袖。他于1304年后去世，其子真蒂莱继任领主，另一个儿子圭多延续了这一支系。

Andrea Pepoli (born c. 1294) was a Bolognese noble, a son of the banker Romeo Pepoli and a brother of Signore Taddeo. He married Ricciarda da Camino, daughter of Rizzardo VI da Camino, lord of Treviso, and of Verde della Scala, tying the Pepoli to the Scaliger-led houses of the Veneto.

安德烈亚·佩波利（约1294年生）是博洛尼亚贵族，银行家罗梅奥·佩波利之子、领主塔代奥之弟。他娶特雷维索领主里扎尔多六世·达·卡米诺与维尔德·德拉·斯卡拉之女里恰尔达为妻，使佩波利家族与斯卡拉家族主导的威尼托诸望族联姻。

en:
Bornio Samaritani was a Bolognese politician and diplomat and a leader of the Scacchesi, the Guelph faction around the Pepoli. In 1306 he and the banker Romeo Pepoli led a piazza rising against the moderate Guelph government; it failed and Romeo was briefly imprisoned. In 1308 his sister married Romeo's son Taddeo.

The papal legate Bertrando del Poggetto denied the city self-government, and in December 1332 jailed Bornio, Taddeo and Brandelisio Gozzadini in the Castel Galliera; a popular revolt forced him to free them within hours. The legate was driven out in 1334.

In May 1336 Bornio sat with Taddeo and Brandelisio on the extraordinary balìa that governed the city, and Taddeo became lord of Bologna in 1337.

博尔尼奥·萨马里塔尼是博洛尼亚政治家、外交家，也是以佩波利家族为核心的圭尔夫派系斯卡凯西派的首领之一。1306年，他与银行家罗梅奥·佩波利共同领导广场起义，反抗温和派圭尔夫政府；起义失败，罗梅奥一度下狱。1308年，他的妹妹嫁给罗梅奥之子塔代奥。

教皇特使贝尔特拉多·德尔·波杰托剥夺城市自治，1332年12月把博尔尼奥、塔代奥和布兰达利西奥·戈扎迪尼囚禁于加列拉城堡，民众暴动迫使他在数小时内放人。1334年特使被逐。

1336年5月，博尔尼奥与塔代奥、布兰达利西奥同在治理全城的非常市政委员会任职，塔代奥于1337年成为博洛尼亚领主。

en:
Brandelisio Gozzadini was chief of the Gozzadini, a leading Guelph house of Bologna, and for years an ally of Taddeo Pepoli against the papal legate. In December 1332 Bertrando del Poggetto had him jailed in the Castel Galliera with Taddeo and Bornio Samaritani, until a revolt freed them within hours.

In 1334 Brandelisio led the rising that forced the legate to barricade himself in Galliera until Florentine troops escorted him out of Bologna. He also helped drive out the rival Maltraversi.

Where Taddeo relied on law, diplomacy and money, Brandelisio relied on force, and their rivalry ended on 7 July 1337: after street fighting he was talked into disarming, then attacked in his own palace and driven out. A plot of March 1338 to hand Bologna to him was crushed.

布兰达利西奥·戈扎迪尼是博洛尼亚圭尔夫望族戈扎迪尼家族的首领，多年来与塔代奥·佩波利联手对抗教皇特使。1332年12月，特使贝尔特拉多·德尔·波杰托把他和塔代奥、博尔尼奥·萨马里塔尼一同关进加列拉城堡，民众暴动在数小时内迫使特使放人。

1334年，布兰达利西奥领导起义，特使被迫困守加列拉城堡，直到佛罗伦萨军队护送他出城。他还协助驱逐敌对的马尔特拉韦尔西派。

塔代奥靠法律、外交和钱财，布兰达利西奥靠武力，二人的对立终结于1337年7月7日：巷战之后他被劝说解除武装，随即在自己的宅邸遇袭出逃。1338年3月，一场要把博洛尼亚交给他的阴谋被粉碎。

en:
Giacomo Pepoli (c. 1315–1367), third son of Signore Taddeo, was the family's fighter and its man of property. In 1336, after a violent quarrel with Bologna's bishop over a parish, he came back at the head of his men, wrecked the bishop's palace and drove the bishop out.

He led a campaign in the Ravenna country in 1338 and held the Apennine border against the Great Company in 1342. From 1338 he also ran the family estates, buying Castiglione dei Gatti castle in 1340.

He ruled Bologna jointly with his brother Giovanni from 1347, until on 16 October 1350 they sold the signoria to Giovanni Visconti for 170,000 florins. Accused in 1351 of plotting with Florence, he was jailed in Milan until pardoned in 1354, and died at Forlì on 23 September 1367.

贾科莫·佩波利（约1315—1367）是领主塔代奥的第三子，家族里能打仗的人，也是管产业的人。1336年，他因一座堂区教堂的任命与博洛尼亚主教大吵一场，随即率人闯回，捣毁主教宫，逼得主教出逃。

1338年他率军远征拉文纳一带，1342年据守亚平宁边境抵御大佣兵团。1338年起他还打理家族产业，1340年买下卡斯蒂廖内德加蒂城堡。

1347年起他与兄长乔瓦尼共同统治博洛尼亚，1350年10月16日兄弟二人以170,000弗罗林将领主权卖给乔瓦尼·维斯孔蒂。1351年他被控与佛罗伦萨密谋，囚于米兰，1354年获赦，1367年9月23日在弗利去世。

en:
Giovanni Pepoli (c. 1310–1367), eldest son of Signore Taddeo, was the family's envoy. When Taddeo died in September 1347, Giovanni and his brother Giacomo inherited a signoria already tied to the Visconti.

Pope Clement VI asked the brothers to back his rector Astorgio di Durfort against Visconti expansion; their answer was lukewarm, and in July 1350 the rector lured Giovanni into a trap at Solarolo and captured him. Freed, he fled to Milan.

The talks there ended on 16 October 1350 with the sale of Bologna to Giovanni Visconti for 170,000 gold florins, the family keeping its castles. Unlike Giacomo, jailed in 1351, Giovanni entered Visconti service and died as their vicar at Pavia on 28 August 1367.

乔瓦尼·佩波利（约1310—1367）是领主塔代奥的长子，家族的外交使者。1347年9月塔代奥去世，乔瓦尼与弟弟贾科莫继承了一个已与维斯孔蒂家族结盟的领主国。

教皇克雷芒六世要兄弟二人支持辖区长官阿斯托尔焦·迪迪尔福尔，遏制维斯孔蒂的扩张，二人反应冷淡；1350年7月，长官在索拉罗洛设下圈套俘获了乔瓦尼。获释后他逃往米兰。

谈判于1350年10月16日以博洛尼亚卖给乔瓦尼·维斯孔蒂告终，价格170,000金弗罗林，家族保留了自己的城堡。1351年贾科莫入狱，乔瓦尼却转而效力维斯孔蒂家族，作为其在帕维亚的代理人于1367年8月28日去世。

en:
Giovanni Pepoli (born c. 1290) was a Bolognese banker, a son of Romeo Pepoli and younger brother of Taddeo. Romeo had been the real master of Bologna since 1307, until the rival Maltraversi drove the family out on 17 July 1321.

They took refuge in Ferrara and Romagna. In 1323 the papal legate Bertrando del Poggetto captured Giovanni together with Taddeo, but the two brothers escaped.

In 1325 Giovanni fought beside the Modenese at Zappolino, where the exiles tried to force their way home. The attempt failed, and the Pepoli were readmitted in March 1328, when the legate let many exiles return.

乔瓦尼·佩波利（约1290年生）是博洛尼亚银行家，罗梅奥·佩波利之子、塔代奥之弟。罗梅奥自1307年起实际掌控博洛尼亚，直到敌对的马尔特拉韦尔西派于1321年7月17日把全家逐出城。

全家先到费拉拉避难，再转往罗马涅。1323年，教皇特使贝尔特拉多·德尔·波杰托俘获乔瓦尼和塔代奥，兄弟二人后来逃脱。

1325年，流亡者试图武力打回博洛尼亚，乔瓦尼随摩德纳人在扎波利诺作战。这次尝试终归失败，1328年3月特使允许众多流亡者返回，佩波利家族得以归乡。

en:
By Tasso family tradition, Lamoral Torriani, also called Lamorale della Torre, was a son of Guido della Torre, the Guelph lord of Milan. After Guido was driven from Milan in 1311, Lamoral took refuge in 1313 in the Brembana valley, at a place named Monte Tasso for its badgers, where he was buried at Cornello.

Early-modern genealogists claimed him as ancestor of the Tasso family of Thurn und Taxis. The tale first appeared in 1645, and no document records his existence.

按塔索家族的谱系传说，拉莫拉尔·托里亚尼（又称拉莫拉莱·德拉·托雷）是米兰圭尔夫派僭主圭多·德拉·托雷之子。圭多于1311年被逐出米兰；拉莫拉尔于1313年避居布伦巴纳河谷，在一处因獾群得名塔索山的地方生活，身后葬于科尔内洛。

近代早期的谱系学家把他奉为塔索家族的始祖，即后来的图恩和塔克西斯亲王家族。这一说法1645年才首次刊印，其生平并无文献可考。

Ricciarda da Camino (born c. 1320) was the daughter of Rizzardo VI da Camino, lord of Treviso, and Verde della Scala, daughter of Alboino I della Scala of Verona. Ricciarda married the Bolognese noble Andrea Pepoli, while her sister Beatrice married Aldobrandino III d'Este.

里恰尔达·达·卡米诺（约1320年生）是特雷维索领主里扎尔多六世·达·卡米诺与维尔德·德拉·斯卡拉之女，其母为维罗纳的阿尔博伊诺一世·德拉·斯卡拉之女。里恰尔达嫁给博洛尼亚贵族安德烈亚·佩波利，她的姐妹贝阿特丽切则嫁给阿尔多布兰迪诺三世·埃斯特。

1368年5月，她在米兰的维斯孔蒂宫廷与另外八十名身着猩红礼服的贵妇一起，迎接前来迎娶维奥兰特·维斯孔蒂的安特卫普的莱昂内尔。

en:
Romeo Pepoli (c. 1250–1322) was a Bolognese banker whose financial dealings made him the wealthiest private individual in fourteenth-century Italy. He married Azzolina Tettalasini in 1280 and placed his children in both Guelph and Ghibelline houses.

His estates grew from 200 hectares in 1296 to over 2600 by 1315, making him Bologna's greatest landowner and its de facto signore. A July 1321 revolt drove him into exile, and he died at Avignon in 1322, summoned before Pope John XXII.

en:
Taddeo Pepoli (1285/1290–1347), son of the Bolognese banker Romeo, was a jurist who became the first open signore of Bologna. His lavish degree celebrations of 1320 aroused suspicion, and the family was driven out in 1321. He returned in 1328, and in 1334 helped drive the legate out.

After crushing the rival Gozzadini, he had his men occupy the main square without bloodshed on 28 August 1337, and the People's Council named him perpetual conservator and governor. Pope Benedict XII excommunicated him and laid Bologna under interdict in 1338, until a 1340 settlement made him papal vicar.

His rule gave Bologna a rare decade of peace at the cost of the commune's independence. He died on 29 September 1347, leaving power to his sons Giacomo and Giovanni.

塔代奥·佩波利（1285/1290—1347）是博洛尼亚银行家罗梅奥之子，法学家出身，成为博洛尼亚第一位公开的领主。1320年他获学位时庆典铺张，引起猜疑，1321年家族被逐。1328年他返回博洛尼亚，1334年又协助把使节赶出了城。

击败对手戈扎迪尼家族后，他于1337年8月28日派人兵不血刃占领主广场，人民会议任命他为终身守护者兼总督。教皇本笃十二世将他绝罚，1338年又对博洛尼亚下达禁令，直到1340年达成和解，他被任命为教皇代理人。

他的统治给博洛尼亚带来少有的和平，代价是公社失去独立。1347年9月29日他去世，权力传给儿子贾科莫与乔瓦尼。

en:
Francesco Pepoli, called Tarlato (born c. 1293), was a Bolognese banker, a son of Romeo Pepoli and brother of Taddeo. He married Besia Galluzzi, whose family stood with the Pepoli in exile.

When a revolt drove the Pepoli out of Bologna in 1321 they took refuge in Ferrara and then Romagna, and in those years Tarlato seized a castle in the city's contado to harry the commune.

In 1325 the exiles again tried to force their way home, fighting at Zappolino, where the Modenese crushed Bologna's army; the attempt failed, and the Pepoli were readmitted in March 1328.

弗朗切斯科·佩波利，绰号塔拉托（约1293年生），是博洛尼亚银行家，罗梅奥·佩波利之子、塔代奥之弟。他娶贝西娅·加卢齐为妻，加卢齐家族在佩波利家族流亡期间与他们站在一起。

1321年起义将佩波利家族逐出博洛尼亚，他们先到费拉拉避难，后转往罗马涅；流亡期间，塔拉托夺取博洛尼亚辖区内的一座城堡，在乡间牵制公社。

1325年流亡者再度尝试武力返城，在扎波利诺作战，摩德纳人大败博洛尼亚军队；尝试终归失败，佩波利家族于1328年3月获准返回。

en:
Zerra Pepoli (c. 1289–?) was a Bolognese banker, son of Romeo Pepoli and younger brother of Taddeo, who would make himself lord of Bologna. While Taddeo managed politics, Zerra ran the family's finances and spent its fortune for the Scacchesi.

Driven out in 1321 and readmitted in 1328, the family was soon back at the centre of power: in May 1336 Zerra sat on the extraordinary balìa that governed the city.

On 7 July 1337, when Scacchese militias fought the Gozzadini in the piazza, the brothers made peace and escorted Brandelisio Gozzadini home. On 28 August Pepoli troops took the piazza and Taddeo became lord of Bologna.

泽拉·佩波利（约1289—？）是博洛尼亚银行家，罗梅奥·佩波利之子，也是后来自立为博洛尼亚领主的塔代奥之弟。塔代奥主理政治，泽拉掌管家族财务，并为斯卡凯西派动用家产。

佩波利家族1321年被逐，1328年获准返回，不久重回权力中心：1336年5月，泽拉进入治理全城的非常市政委员会。

1337年7月7日，斯卡凯西派民兵与戈扎迪尼家族在广场开战，兄弟二人出面劝和，护送布兰达利西奥·戈扎迪尼回府。8月28日，佩波利家族的军队占领广场，塔代奥成为博洛尼亚领主。

en:
Mongondow tradition makes Mokodoludut the first ruler of Bolaang, the maritime kingdom of the Mongondow people of northern Sulawesi. In the thirteenth century the bogani, local warrior chiefs, united and in a bakid council agreed to raise Mokodoludut, a bogani of Molantud, as their king under the title Punu.

Local king lists date his reign from 1280 to 1376, with his seat at Dumoga in the Mongondow highlands, naming him king at Manado and ruler of nine territories.

Fyodor Romanovich was appanage prince of Beloozero from 1339 until his death, the elder son of Roman Mikhailovich. He married Feodosia, a daughter of Ivan Kalita of Moscow, while his younger brother Vasily took Sugorsky.

In 1375 he joined Dmitry Donskoy against Tver. In 1380 he fought in the vanguard at the Battle of Kulikovo and was killed together with his son Ivan; Beloozero then passed to his nephew Yury Vasilyevich.

Fyodor Mikhailovich (c. 1286–1314) was prince of Beloozero from 1293, succeeding his father Mikhail Glebovich. His mother was a daughter of Prince Fyodor the Black of Yaroslavl.

In 1302 he married in the Golden Horde a daughter of a certain Velblasmysh, possibly Ilbasmysh, son of Khan Toqta. In 1314 he took a second wife, a daughter of Dmitry Zhidimirich, thought to be a Novgorod boyar. Most genealogies make him childless.

en:
Mikhail Glebovich (1263–1293) was prince of Beloozero, the son of Prince Gleb Vasilkovich and a daughter of the Mongol khan Sartak. In 1277 he campaigned with Mengu-Timur against the Alans, and in 1278 married a daughter of Prince Fyodor of Yaroslavl.

He inherited Beloozero that year, but his cousin Dmitry of Rostov seized it in 1279; he recovered it only in 1286. In 1293 he went to the Golden Horde to accuse Grand Prince Dmitry, and died that summer.

In 1277 he campaigned with #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('mongke_temur_borjigin').GetID],X #L Mengu-Timur#!#! against the Alans, and in 1278 married a daughter of Prince Fyodor of [ShowLocationName('yaroslavl')].

zh:
米哈伊尔·格列布维奇（1263—1293）是别洛奥泽罗王公，别洛奥泽罗与罗斯托夫王公格列布·瓦西里科维奇之子，母亲是蒙古汗撒里答的女儿。1277年，他随忙哥帖木儿汗出征高加索的阿兰人；1278年娶雅罗斯拉夫尔王公费奥多尔之女。

他同年继位，1279年罗斯托夫堂兄德米特里·鲍里索维奇夺去封邑，直到1286年才收回别洛奥泽罗。1293年，他前往金帐汗国控告大公德米特里，同年夏在汗国去世。

en:
Roman Mikhailovich, nicknamed Romanchuk, was appanage prince of Beloozero from 1314 to about 1339, the younger son of Mikhail Glebovich. He received it only in mature age, after his elder brother Fyodor's death.

In 1339 he and a prince of Yaroslavl travelled to the Horde to complain to Öz Beg Khan of Ivan Kalita's encroachments, and probably perished. His sons Fyodor and Vasily succeeded to a Beloozero that soon began to split; Fyodor fell at Kulikovo in 1380.

罗曼·米哈伊洛维奇，绰号罗曼丘克，是别洛奥泽罗的封邑王公，1314年至约1339年在位，为米哈伊尔·格列布维奇的幼子。他成年后才在兄长费奥多尔去世后领有该公国。

1339年，他与雅罗斯拉夫尔的一位王公同赴金帐汗廷，向月即别汗控告伊凡·卡利塔侵夺土地，很可能就死在那里。他的两个儿子费奥多尔和瓦西里继位后，别洛奥泽罗开始分裂，费奥多尔后来于1380年在库里科沃战役中阵亡。

en:
Vasily Romanovich, called Sugorsky, was a Rurikid prince of Beloozero and the younger son of Roman Mikhailovich. When his father died in 1339 the Beloozero principality was divided: his elder brother Fyodor kept the western part around Belozersk, while Vasily received the eastern appanage that became the Sugorsky principality.

He founded the Sugorsky line of princes. His son Yury Vasilyevich inherited Belozersk after Fyodor fell at Kulikovo in 1380 and became its last appanage prince.

en:
Adela (c. 1067–1137), a daughter of William the Conqueror, married Count Stephen-Henry of Blois around 1083. She ruled Blois and Chartres as regent during the First Crusade, and after Stephen fell at Ramla in 1102 continued ruling for her son Theobald until 1107.

In 1105 she helped arrange a truce between Henry I of England and Pope Paschal II, and from 1107 governed jointly with Theobald until retiring.

Her son Stephen, raised at her brother's court, seized the English crown in 1135. She retired to Marcigny Priory around 1120 and died there on 8 March 1137.

阿德拉（约1067—1137）是征服者威廉之女，约1083年嫁给布卢瓦伯爵艾蒂安-亨利。第一次十字军期间，她以摄政身份统治布卢瓦和沙特尔；1102年斯蒂芬在拉姆拉战死后，她继续为儿子蒂博执政至1107年。

1105年，她帮助亨利一世与教皇帕斯卡尔二世达成休战，1107年起与蒂博共同治理伯国，直至退隐。

她的儿子斯蒂芬在兄长的宫廷长大，于1135年夺取英格兰王位。她约1120年退隐马尔西尼修道院，1137年3月8日在那里去世。

en:
Alix of Brittany (6 June 1243 – 2 August 1288), dame de Pontarcy in her own right, was the eldest daughter of John I, duke of Brittany, and Blanche of Navarre. She married John I of Châtillon, count of Blois, bringing Pontarcy and Brie-Comte-Robert as her dowry; their daughter was Joan, later countess of Blois.

With her husband she founded La Guiche Abbey near Blois in 1277. Widowed in 1279, she travelled to the Holy Land in 1287 and built two towers at Acre, dying in 1288.

en:
Stephen Henry (c. 1045–1102) was Count of Blois and Chartres from 1089 and a leader of the First Crusade. He commanded a crusader army and directed the siege of Antioch, but on 2 June 1098 he retreated and persuaded Emperor Alexios I Komnenos to turn back rather than relieve the city.

Disgraced and urged on by his wife Adela, he took the cross again in 1101 and reached Jerusalem. In 1102 he fought for Baldwin I at the Second Battle of Ramla, was captured, and executed on 19 May, probably at Ascalon.

艾蒂安二世（约1045—1102）自1089年起任布卢瓦与沙特尔伯爵，是第一次十字军东征的领袖之一。他指挥一支十字军，主持安条克围城战，却在1098年6月2日临阵撤退，还劝说拜占庭皇帝阿历克塞一世回师、不要救援该城。

en:
Odo I (c. 950–996) succeeded his father Theobald the Trickster around 977 as count of Blois and Chartres, and was made count palatine by King Lothair. In the 970s he subjugated Rennes in Brittany, and in 987 supported Charles of Lorraine against Hugh Capet.

In June 991 he seized Melun, soon retaken by a royal coalition, and later warred on Fulk Nerra of Anjou. While besieging Langeais in the winter of 995–996 he fell ill and died at Marmoutier Abbey near Tours on 12 March 996. By Bertha of Burgundy he left his successors Theobald II and Odo II.

en:
Guy I of Châtillon (c. 1298–1342) succeeded his father Hugh II in 1307 as count of Blois, Dunois and Fréteval and lord of Avesnes. In 1310 he married Margaret of Valois, sister of the future Philip VI, tying his house to the Valois.

Their son Charles of Blois would later fight in the Breton War of Succession. Guy campaigned with Louis X against the Flemings in 1315, ceded his coinage rights to Philip VI in 1328 and became lord of Château-Renault in 1332.

From 1336 he backed the French crown against Edward III as the Hundred Years' War began. He died on 12 August 1342 and was buried at La Guiche Abbey near Blois.

居伊一世·德·沙蒂永（约1298—1342）1307年继承父亲于格二世，成为布卢瓦、迪努瓦和弗雷特勒瓦尔伯爵及阿韦讷领主。1310年他娶后来的腓力六世之妹瓦卢瓦的玛格丽特，使家族与瓦卢瓦王室结成姻亲。

儿子布卢瓦的夏尔日后参加布列塔尼继承战争。1315年他随路易十世出征佛兰德，1328年把铸币权让予腓力六世，1332年成为沙托雷诺领主。

1336年起，他在百年战争伊始支持法兰西王室对抗爱德华三世。1342年8月12日他去世，葬于布卢瓦附近的拉吉什修道院。
