en:
Hugh I of Châtillon (c. 1198–1248), son of Walter III of Châtillon and Elisabeth, heiress of Saint-Pol, became count of Saint-Pol in 1226. In 1226 he married Marie of Avesnes, heiress of the old line of Blois counts, and ruled Blois jure uxoris from 1230 until 1241, founding the Châtillon dynasty there.

He founded Cistercian nunneries at Pont-aux-Dames and L'Amour-Dieu in Troissy. His sons included John I, his successor in Blois, and Guy III of Saint-Pol. He planned to join Louis IX's Seventh Crusade but died on 9 April 1248.

于格一世·德·沙蒂永（约1198—1248）是沙蒂永的戈谢三世与圣波勒女继承人伊丽莎白之子，1226年成为圣波勒伯爵。同年他娶布卢瓦旧朝伯爵世系的女继承人、阿韦讷的玛丽为妻，1230年至1241年妻权统治布卢瓦伯国，开创沙蒂永王朝。

他创建了蓬托达姆和特鲁瓦西“天主之爱”两座西多会女修院。其子包括布卢瓦继承人让一世和圣波勒的居伊三世。他本打算参加路易九世的第七次十字军，却于1248年4月9日去世。

Hugh II of Châtillon (9 April 1258–1307) was the son of Guy III, count of Saint-Pol, and Matilda of Brabant. On his father's death in 1289 he succeeded as count of Saint-Pol, but in 1292 he inherited Blois from his cousin Joan and surrendered Saint-Pol to his younger brother Guy.

He ruled Blois until his death in 1307 and was buried at La Guiche Abbey near Blois. Around 1287 he married Beatrice of Dampierre; their son Guy I succeeded them.

en:
John I of Châtillon (c. 1225–1279) inherited Blois and Dunois from his mother Marie of Avesnes in 1241 and his father Hugh I's lordships in 1248. In 1254 he married Alix of Brittany, and in 1256 the will of his cousin Matilda of Amboise reunited the County of Chartres with Blois.

In 1260 he granted the parish of Chouzy the right to hold a ball game at Whitsun, and Louis IX named him lieutenant general of France in 1270.

His daughter Joan married Peter of France, count of Alençon. He passed his lands to her before his death at Chambord in 1279.

en:
Jeanne de Beaumont, also called Jeanne of Hainault (1323–1350), was ruling countess of Soissons from 1344, daughter of John of Beaumont and Margaret of Soissons. In 1340 she married Louis of Châtillon, heir to Blois; her three sons all later became counts of Blois, two of them also holding Soissons.

Louis was killed at Crécy in 1346, after which Jeanne remarried William I, Marquis of Namur; they had no children. She ruled Soissons until she died of the Black Death in December 1350.

en:
Joan of Châtillon (c. 1253–1292) was countess of Blois, Chartres and Châteaudun, the daughter of Count John I of Blois and Alix of Brittany. She married Peter of Alençon, son of King Louis IX, in 1272 and was widowed in 1283 with no surviving children. In 1286 she sold the county of Chartres to Philip IV of France.

She is remembered for opening hunting to all inhabitants. She died at Blois on 29 January 1292, leaving Blois to her cousin Hugh II of Châtillon.

Louis I of Blois (1172–1205), son of Theobald V and Alix of France, was count from 1191 and fought on the Third Crusade. He married Catherine of Clermont, bearing his heir Theobald VI; in 1196 he freed his serfs.

At Écry on 28 November 1199 he and his cousin Theobald III became the first nobles to take the cross for the Fourth Crusade. He commanded a division at Constantinople in 1203, but fever kept him from its 1204 sack. Pursuing Kaloyan's Cumans too far at Adrianople, he was killed on 14 April 1205.

路易一世（1172—1205）是蒂博五世与法兰西的艾莉克丝之子，1191年继位为布卢瓦伯爵，曾参加第三次十字军东征。他娶克莱蒙的卡特琳娜，生下继承人蒂博六世；1196年，他解放了自己的农奴。

Louis of Châtillon, numbered Louis I of Blois-Châtillon, was the eldest son of Count Guy I of Blois and Margaret of Valois, Philip VI's sister. In 1340 he married Jeanne of Avesnes, Countess of Soissons, and from 1342 he ruled Blois and Dunois, holding Soissons through his wife.

In the Breton succession war from 1341, he backed his brother Charles of Blois and helped take Rennes in 1342. He was killed at Crécy on 26 August 1346.

Margaret of Blois (1170–1230) was the daughter of Count Theobald V and Alix of France. She married first Hugh III of Oisy and then, in 1190, Otto I, count of Burgundy. Widowed in 1200, she ruled Burgundy as regent for her daughters until 1208; Joan I and Beatrice II both succeeded her.

Her third husband was Walter II of Avesnes. In 1218 her nephew Theobald VI died and she became countess of Blois and Châteaudun, succeeded in 1230 by her daughter Mary.

en:
Margaret of Valois (1295–1342) was a French princess of the Valois line, daughter of Charles, Count of Valois, and Margaret of Anjou, and elder sister of King Philip VI. In 1311 she married Guy I de Châtillon, Count of Blois, tying the Blois comital house to the Valois royal line.

Her children were Louis, who succeeded as Count of Blois and fell at Crécy in 1346, Charles of Blois, the beatified duke of Brittany, and Marie, who married Rudolf, Duke of Lorraine.

en:
Mary of Avesnes (c. 1200–1241), countess of Blois, was the only child of Walter II d'Avesnes and Margaret of Blois. In 1225 she married Hugh I of Châtillon; the couple founded the nunnery of Pont-aux-Dames.

On her mother's death in 1230 she inherited the County of Blois, holding also lands including Avesnes and Guise as her parents' sole heiress; Hugh ruled Blois with her. She died in 1241, and Blois passed to her eldest son John I. Her son Guy became count of Saint-Pol.

en:
Theobald I, called the Trickster, was the son of Theobald the Elder and founder of the comital House of Blois. Around 940 he became count of Blois, Tours and Chartres, chief lieutenant of Hugh the Great, and about 944 married Luitgarde of Vermandois.

In 945 he held the captured King Louis IV in his custody. After Hugh's death in 956, Theobald exercised a near regency during the minority of Hugh Capet. From 960 he warred on the Normans until they burned Chartres and killed his eldest son in 962.

After Hugh Capet disapproved of the war, Theobald sought the support of King Lothair, and by his death around 977 ruled a vast Loire principality.

蒂博一世，绰号“欺诈者”，是蒂博·老大人之子，也是布卢瓦伯爵家族的奠基者。约940年，他成为伟大的于格最得力的封臣，领有布卢瓦、图尔和沙特尔；约944年，他娶韦尔芒杜瓦的留特加德为妻。

945年，被俘的国王路德维希四世曾交由他看管。956年伟大的于格去世后，蒂博在于格·卡佩未成年时近乎摄政。960年起他与诺曼人交战，962年诺曼人焚毁沙特尔并杀死他的长子。

于格·卡佩反对这场战争，蒂博转而寻求国王洛泰尔的支持；到约977年去世时，他已在卢瓦尔河流域建立起幅员辽阔的领地。

Theobald II (c. 983–1004) was the eldest son of Count Odo I of Blois and Bertha of Burgundy. When his father died in 996 he succeeded as count of Blois and Chartres, ruling under the regency of his mother, who had married King Robert II of France.

Theobald died of exhaustion on his way back from Rome on 11 July 1004, leaving no heir. His lands passed to his younger brother Odo II.

en:
Theobald V the Good (1130–1191) was Count of Blois and Chartres from 1151, second son of Theobald the Great and Matilda of Carinthia; his elder brother Henry took Champagne. In 1164 he married Alix of France, daughter of Louis VII and Eleanor of Aquitaine, who bore his heir Louis I.

In 1171 he staged the first blood-libel trial in continental Europe, burning thirty Jews. After opposing the young Philip II he reconciled with him, joined the Third Crusade in 1190, and died at the siege of Acre on 20 January 1191.

He campaigned against the Muslims in Spain, where he contracted leprosy, and afterwards lived withdrawn in his castle at La Ferté-Villeneuil. He died childless in April 1218, leaving Blois to his aunt Margaret and Chartres to his aunt Isabelle, while Clermont was sold to the French crown.

Withego II of Colditz (died 1342) was bishop of Meissen from 1312 until his death. A nephew of the preceding bishop Albert III of Leisnig, he had been a canon of Meissen Cathedral.

In 1258 he married Sophie, daughter of King Abel of Denmark. Their sons included John I, who succeeded him, and Bernhard II.

en:
Bernhard II (c. 1260–after 1323) was the third son of Bernhard I and Sophie of Denmark. He succeeded in 1287 and ruled jointly with his elder brother John I until John died in 1291, then reigned alone. In 1300 he took the title count of Bernburg.

When the Anhalt-Aschersleben line died out in 1315 he inherited its princely title, though the bishopric of Halberstadt took the lands for Prince Otto's debts. In 1320 he was made count palatine of Saxony. In 1302 he married Helene of Rügen; their son Bernhard III succeeded.

Bernhard III (died 1348) was a German prince of the House of Ascania who ruled Anhalt-Bernburg from 1323, when he succeeded his father Bernhard II. His two younger brothers renounced their claims to enter the Church, leaving him sole ruler.

In 1328 he married Agnes, daughter of Elector Rudolph I of Saxony, who bore him five children, including his successors Bernhard IV and Henry IV; after her death in 1338 he married twice more.

Bernhard IV (died 1354) was a German prince of the House of Ascania and ruler of Anhalt-Bernburg. The eldest son of Bernhard III and Agnes of Saxe-Wittenberg, he succeeded his father as sole ruler in 1348.

He also styled himself Margrave of Landsberg, although the Wettins had bought it back in 1347. Betrothed to Beatrix, daughter of the Margrave of Meissen, but never married, he died in 1354 and was succeeded by his brother Henry.

en:
Henry IV (died 7 July 1374) was a German prince of the House of Ascania who ruled Anhalt-Bernburg from 1354. The second son of Bernhard III and Agnes of Saxe-Wittenberg, he was bypassed by his elder brother Bernhard IV, taking power only when Bernhard died without issue.

By his wife Sophie he left three children, including Bernhard V and Rudolf, later bishop of Halberstadt. On his death in 1374 he was succeeded by his half-brother Otto.

Helena of Rügen (c. 1270/1272 – 1315) was the daughter of Wizlaw II, Prince of Rügen, and Agnes of Brunswick-Lüneburg. In November 1288 she married John III, Lord of Mecklenburg; their daughter Luitgard was born around 1289, but John drowned near Poel in May 1289 after only seven months of marriage.

In December 1302 she married Bernhard II, Prince of Anhalt-Bernburg. She bore him three sons, including his successor Bernhard III, and died in 1315.

en:
Catherine of Anhalt-Bernburg (c. 1330–1390) was a princess of the House of Ascania, the daughter of Bernhard III of Anhalt-Bernburg and Agnes of Saxe-Wittenberg. In 1356 she married Magnus II, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg, and bore him numerous children, including three future dukes of Brunswick.

Magnus lost Lüneburg to Albert of Saxe-Wittenberg in 1370 and fell in battle in 1373 in the war that followed. In 1374 Catherine married his rival Albert, Duke of Lüneburg, and died in 1390.

en:
John II (c. 1283–1333) was Count of Bentheim, succeeding his father Eckbert I. In 1305 he allied with Simon I, Lord of Lippe, and married Simon's daughter Mechthild, who bore him five children, among them his successors Simon I and Otto III.

To guard the trade road from Münster to Amsterdam, he founded the town of Neuenhaus around Dinkelrode Castle in 1317. He died in 1333.

Simon I (c. 1310–1344) was Count of Bentheim from 1333 until his death. The eldest son of Count John II and Mechthild of Lippe, he succeeded on his father's death in 1333.

He allied with Tecklenburg and waged feuds against the Bishopric of Münster. He married Catherine, daughter of Count Ludolf VI of Steinfurt, but had no children, so on his death in 1344 the county passed to his younger brother Otto III.

en:
Albert Pallavicini was the fifth marquess of Bodonitsa, succeeding his father Thomas. He married the Venetian noblewoman Maria dalle Carceri and through her held a sixth of Euboea. He loyally served the princes of Achaea and attended their parliaments on the Isthmus of Corinth.

In 1311 he followed Walter V of Brienne against the Catalan Company at the Battle of Halmyros and was killed. By the Assizes of Romania his widow and daughter Guglielma inherited Bodonitsa.

阿尔贝托·帕拉维奇尼是博多尼察第五代侯爵，在父亲托马斯死后继位。他娶威尼斯贵族女子玛丽亚·达莱·卡尔切里为妻，并通过她占有埃维亚岛六分之一的份额。他忠心侍奉亚该亚诸亲王，曾出席他们在科林斯地峡召开的议会。

Bartolomeo Zaccaria (c. 1305–1334) was the eldest son of Martino Zaccaria, of the Genoese Zaccaria family that ruled Chios. In 1327 he married Guglielma Pallavicini, Marchioness of Bodonitsa, and ruled her march as her consort, also holding the Barony of Damala.

During a Catalan invasion he was seized and imprisoned in Sicily, winning release only through the intercession of Pope John XXII. He died young in 1334, leaving one daughter, Marulla.

en:
Francis Zorzi, called Marchesotto (1337–1388), was a Zorzi marquess of Bodonitsa, a Venetian march in Central Greece. The son of Guglielma Pallavicini and Niccolò Zorzi, he became his mother's co-ruler in 1354 and ruled alone from 1358.

As a tribute-paying vassal of the Catalan Duchy of Athens he nonetheless kept his independence and backed Maria of Sicily against Peter IV of Aragon. He died around 1388, leaving Bodonitsa to his young son Jacob under the regency of his widow Euphrosyne Sommaripa.

en:
Guglielma Pallavicini (c. 1300–1358), the Lady of Thermopylae, was the last Pallavicini ruler of the March of Bodonitsa in Frankish Greece. On her father Albert's death in 1311 she inherited the march, at first ruling with her mother and later with her stepfather Andrea Cornaro.

In 1327 she married the Genoese Bartolomeo Zaccaria; widowed in 1334, she married the Venetian Niccolò Zorzi, with whom her long quarrel over Larena Castle drew in Venice and the Catalans. After Zorzi's death in 1354 she ruled with their son Francis until 1358.

en:
Guy Pallavicini (died 1237), a Lombard noble, joined the Fourth Crusade in 1203. In 1204 Boniface of Montferrat made him warden of Thermopylae, and Guy made Bodonitsa his seat as its first marquess, building a castle on an ancient acropolis.

In 1208–1209 he joined the Lombard barons' revolt against King Demetrius of Thessalonica, but by 1221 he was the kingdom's bailli and defended Thessalonica until he surrendered it to the Epirotes in 1224. Released, he returned to Bodonitsa, made his will in 1237, and died soon after, leaving the mark to his son Ubertino.

en:
Isabella Pallavicini (died 1286) was sovereign marchioness of Bodonitsa, a Frankish lordship in Greece. A daughter of the first margrave Guy, she succeeded her brother Ubertino in 1278.

Already old when she inherited, Isabella was summoned that year by her overlord Charles of Anjou to do homage to his bailli. She refused, and her absence was the chief reason the other Achaean barons also refused homage. She died childless in 1286, and William I of Athens arbitrated the succession in favour of her cousin Albert.

en:
Nicholas I Zorzi was the first Venetian of the Zorzi family to rule Bodonitsa, a Frankish march in Greece guarding the pass of Thermopylae. In 1335 he married its heiress Guglielma Pallavicini and ruled jointly with her.

The neighbouring Duchy of Athens was governed by the Catalan Company; Nicholas stayed on good terms with it but objected to its annual tribute of four war horses. He held the march until his death in 1345. His three sons, Francis, James and Nicholas, each ruled it in turn, and the Zorzi kept it until the Ottomans conquered it in 1414.

尼科洛一世·佐尔齐是威尼斯佐尔齐家族中第一个统治博多尼察的人。博多尼察是守卫温泉关隘口的希腊法兰克人侯国。1335年，他娶侯国继承人古列尔玛·帕拉维奇尼为妻，与她共同统治。

邻近的雅典公国由加泰罗尼亚公司执掌，尼科洛与其大体保持友好，却不肯接受它索要的每年四匹战马的贡赋。他统治侯国直到1345年去世。他的三个儿子弗朗切斯科、贾科莫和尼科洛先后统治侯国，佐尔齐家族一直守到1414年奥斯曼人攻占此地。

en:
Rubino Pallavicini was a Lombard noble and younger brother of Guy, the first marquess of Bodonitsa. He followed Boniface of Montferrat to Greece on the Fourth Crusade and is named with Guy at the long siege of Acrocorinth.

After Boniface's death in 1207, the brothers joined the Lombard revolt against the young king Demetrius, holding out at Thebes before submitting to the Latin emperor Henry in 1209. Rubino's line inherited Bodonitsa: his grandson Tommaso made good his claim to the march after the death of the marchioness Isabella in 1286.

鲁比诺·帕拉维奇尼是伦巴第贵族，首任博多尼察侯爵圭多的弟弟。他随蒙费拉的博尼法斯参加第四次十字军东征前往希腊，史料记载他与圭多一同参与了对阿克罗科林斯的长期围攻。

1207年博尼法斯死后，兄弟二人加入伦巴第叛乱，反对幼王德米特里，据守底比斯，直至1209年向拉丁皇帝亨利投降。博多尼察侯爵之位后来转入鲁比诺一系：1286年女侯爵伊莎贝拉去世后，他的孙子托马索争得侯国。

en:
Thomas Pallavicini was marquess of Bodonitsa and founder of its second ruling line, a grandson of Rubino, younger brother of the first margrave. When his kinswoman Marchioness Isabella died childless in 1286, Thomas claimed the marquisate against her widower.

While the feudal court of Achaea delayed its verdict, Thomas seized the castle of Bodonitsa and installed himself. He ruled unchallenged and passed the march to his son Albert.

托马斯·帕拉维奇尼是博多尼察侯国侯爵，也是该领地第二统治支系的开创者，是第一代侯爵之弟鲁比诺的孙子。1286年，同族女侯爵伊莎贝拉无嗣而终，托马斯与她的鳏夫争夺侯国继承权。

en:
Ubertino Pallavicini (c. 1210–1278) succeeded his father Guy as marquess of Bodonitsa in 1237. Although Bodonitsa was a vassal of Achaea, he aided his cousin Guy I de la Roche of Athens against Prince William II of Villehardouin, fighting at Karydi in 1258.

In 1259 he joined William and Michael II against Nicaea and was defeated at Pelagonia, and in 1263 he campaigned with his Achaean liege against the Morea. Pirates based on Atalanta disrupted his people's food supplies. In 1264 he inherited estates near Parma from his sister, and when he died in 1278 the mark passed to his sister Isabella.

乌贝蒂诺·帕拉维奇尼（约1210—1278）1237年继承父亲圭多，成为博多尼察侯爵。博多尼察本是亚该亚公国的附庸，他却援助表亲雅典公爵居伊一世·德·拉罗什，对抗亚该亚亲王威廉二世·德·维尔阿杜安，1258年参加卡里迪战役。

en:
Anne of Bohemia (1323–1338), also called Anna of Luxembourg, was a daughter of John of Bohemia and his wife Elizabeth of Bohemia, born at Cham during her mother’s exile, and a younger sister of Emperor Charles IV. Two earlier betrothals came to nothing.

In 1335 she was married at Znojmo to Otto the Merry, Duke of Austria, Styria and Carinthia, becoming stepmother to his sons. She died childless on 3 September 1338, aged fifteen, and was buried at Neuberg Abbey.

en:
Anne of Bohemia (1290–1313) was the eldest daughter of Wenceslaus II and Judith of Habsburg, sister of Wenceslaus III. In 1306 she married Henry of Carinthia, who was elected king of Bohemia after her brother's murder, but the couple were driven out by Rudolf of Habsburg and fled to Carinthia.

Henry recovered the throne after Rudolf's death in 1307 but lost it again in 1310, when John of Luxembourg and Anne's sister Elizabeth seized Prague. Anne died in exile at Ljubljana in 1313, aged twenty-two and childless.

en:
Beatrice of Bourbon (1320–1383), daughter of Louis I, Duke of Bourbon, married King John of Bohemia in December 1334 and reached Prague in 1335. Her only son, Wenceslaus, was born there in 1337, and she was crowned queen that May; but alienated from Bohemia, she withdrew to Luxembourg.

Widowed when John fell at Crécy in 1346, she married Eudes II, Lord of Grancey, in 1347. She died in Paris on 23 December 1383, outliving her son.

en:
Blanche of Valois (1317–1348) was the youngest daughter of Charles of Valois and a sister of Philip VI of France. In 1323 she was betrothed to Charles, eldest son of John of Bohemia, who had been educated at the French court. They married at Prague in May 1329.

The couple lived apart until 1334, when she entered Prague with her French household as Margravine of Moravia. She learned Czech and German and stayed on in Bohemia when Charles travelled, proving more popular than John's second wife, Beatrice of Bourbon. With no living son, she came under pressure from John and moved to Brno in 1337; her two daughters were Margaret and Katherine.

John fell at Crécy in 1346, and she became queen of Bohemia. She died on 1 August 1348 and was buried in St Vitus Cathedral; Charles became emperor seven years later.

瓦卢瓦的布朗歇（1317—1348）是瓦卢瓦的查理最小的女儿，法王腓力六世的妹妹。1323年，她与波希米亚国王约翰的长子查理订婚；这位王子在法国宫廷长大，两人1329年5月在布拉格成婚。

婚后两人分居，直到1334年布朗歇带着法国随从进入布拉格，成为摩拉维亚藩侯夫人。她学会了捷克语和德语，丈夫出国时仍留在波希米亚，比约翰的第二任妻子波旁的比阿特丽斯更得人心。因没有在世的儿子，她受到约翰施压，1337年迁居布尔诺；两个女儿是玛格丽特和凯瑟琳。

en:
Charles IV (1316–1378), born Wenceslaus at Prague, was King of Bohemia and Holy Roman Emperor. Son of John of Bohemia and Přemyslid Elizabeth, he took the name Charles at the French court, spoke five languages, governed Bohemian lands from 1333 and became Margrave of Moravia in 1334.

In 1346 electors backed by Pope Clement VI made him King of the Romans; rivals mocked him as the ‘Priests' King’. His father fell at Crécy, where Charles was wounded, leaving him Bohemia and Luxembourg. Louis IV died in 1347; defeating Günther von Schwarzburg, he was re-elected in 1349. He made Prague his capital and in 1348 founded its university and built Karlštejn Castle.

A 1350 jousting accident left him hunchbacked. Crowned emperor at Rome in 1355, he issued the Golden Bull in 1356, the Empire's basic law until 1806. Brandenburg passed to his son Wenceslaus in 1373, succeeding him in Bohemia in 1378.

查理四世（1316—1378）原名瓦茨拉夫，生于布拉格，是波希米亚国王兼神圣罗马皇帝。他是波希米亚国王约翰与普热米斯尔的伊丽莎白之子，在法国宫廷取名查理，通晓五种语言；1333年起治理波希米亚领地，1334年受封摩拉维亚藩侯。

1346年，在教宗克雷芒六世支持下，选帝侯推举他为罗马人的国王，对手讥他为“教士之王”。父亲在克雷西战死，查理亦负伤离开，继承波希米亚与卢森堡。1347年路德维希四世去世；他击败京特尔·冯·施瓦茨堡，1349年再度当选。他定都布拉格，1348年创办大学并修建卡尔施泰因城堡。

1350年一场马上比武使他驼背。1355年他在罗马加冕为皇帝，1356年颁布《金玺诏书》，为帝国基本法直至1806年。1373年勃兰登堡归其子瓦茨拉夫，瓦茨拉夫于1378年继位波希米亚。

Elizabeth of Bohemia, in Czech Eliška (1292–1330), was a daughter of Wenceslaus II and Judith of Habsburg. She married John of Luxembourg, son of Emperor Henry VII, in 1310; John later took Prague, driving her sister Anne into exile. Her son Charles, the future Emperor Charles IV, was born in 1316.

After an alleged plot against John in 1319 she lost custody of her children, endured exile in Bavaria, and returned to Bohemia in 1325. She died of tuberculosis in 1330, aged thirty-eight.

Judith of Habsburg, in Czech Guta (1271–1297), was the youngest daughter of King Rudolf I of Germany and Gertrude of Hohenberg. Betrothed as a child to Wenceslaus II of Bohemia to seal her father's peace with King Ottokar II, she married him at Cheb in January 1285, becoming queen of Bohemia.

She bore Wenceslaus ten children, among them Wenceslaus III, Anna and Elizabeth, and died in May 1297 giving birth to her last daughter; only four of the children reached adulthood.

Henry I of Rosenberg (c. 1262–1310), Wok I's son, was a Vítkovci noble. After backing Záviš of Falkenstein he made his peace with Wenceslaus II, becoming Supreme Chamberlain of Bohemia in 1301. When the Krumlov line of the Vítkovci died out c. 1302, the king granted him Český Krumlov, seat of his descendants for three centuries.

He supported Rudolf of Habsburg's claim to the crown in 1306 and died at Prague Castle in July 1310, succeeded by his son Peter I.

Hynek Berka of Dubá (died 1348) was a Bohemian nobleman of the Ronovci clan and founder of the Berka of Dubá family. He joined the revolt against King John as one of seven hostages for the settlement, but later became his trusted servant.

He served as supreme burgrave of Prague from c. 1319 until his death. After 1333 he founded Hradčany below Prague Castle, and by his wife Agnes left two sons, who began the two branches of his house.

en:
John IV of Dražice (c. 1260–1343) was Bishop of Prague from 1301 until his death. A Prague canon from a noble Bohemian family, in 1310 he backed John of Luxembourg's seizure of the Bohemian crown with troops and money.

In 1318 Pope John XXII suspended him on Dominican charges; he spent eleven years at Avignon before being restored in 1329. He then became a lavish builder, founding an Augustinian monastery and a stone bridge over the Elbe at Roudnice nad Labem, and died in 1343, buried at St Vitus.

en:
Jan Hus (c. 1370–1415) was a Czech theologian and the leading voice of the Bohemian Reformation. Born at Husinec (hus means ‘goose’ in Czech), in 1402 he became preacher at the Bethlehem Chapel, denouncing clerical and even papal failings. Influenced by John Wycliffe, he held that Scripture outranked the pope.

In 1409 he became rector of Charles University. Excommunicated in 1410, he attacked indulgences in 1412, then left Prague under interdict and spent two years preaching and writing in the countryside.

In 1414 he went to the Council of Constance under Sigismund's safe conduct, but was jailed. He refused to recant unless shown wrong from the Bible, and on 6 July 1415 he was burned at the stake, his ashes thrown into the Rhine. Bohemia's Hussites beat five papal crusades between 1420 and 1431; the Basel Compacts then allowed a reformed church in Bohemia, a century before Luther.

扬·胡斯（约1370—1415）是捷克神学家、波希米亚宗教改革领袖。他生于胡西内茨，“胡斯”在捷克语中意为“鹅”。1402年任伯利恒礼拜堂传道人，痛斥教士乃至教宗堕落；受威克里夫影响，主张《圣经》高于教宗。

1409年他出任布拉格查理大学校长。1410年被逐出教会后，他于1412年抨击赎罪券，随后离开布拉格，两年间在乡间以捷克语传教写作。

1414年他持安全通行令赴康斯坦茨会议，却被关押；受审时拒绝撤回主张，除非依《圣经》证明他有误。1415年7月6日被处火刑，骨灰被抛入莱茵河。波希米亚的胡斯派在1420至1431年间击败五次教宗十字军；《巴塞尔协约》随后允许波希米亚保有改革教会，比路德早了近一个世纪。

John I of Rosenberg was the youngest son of Peter I of Rosenberg and Catherine of Vartenberk, of a leading Bohemian noble house. After his father died in 1347 his elder brothers ruled the family lands.

In 1367 the brothers founded an Augustinian monastery at Třeboň, and when the estates were divided in 1374 John took over their administration, residing at Třeboň and Český Krumlov. He died childless on 1 September 1389, never becoming regent.

Jan Volek (c. 1290–1351) was the illegitimate son of King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia and the last male Přemyslid. Before ordination he was a canon at Prague and Olomouc, and from 1319 served as provost of Vyšehrad and chancellor to King John of Luxembourg.

In 1334 Pope John XXII named him Bishop of Olomouc and he was ordained a priest. He was a councillor to his half-sister Queen Elizabeth and deputy governor of Moravia under his nephew Charles IV. He died at Olomouc on 27 September 1351.

Jindřich Berka z Dubé, called the One-Eyed (died 1404), was a Bohemian nobleman and the younger son of Supreme Burgrave Hynek Berka z Dubé. After 1352, when the estates were divided, his share included Dubá, Kuřívody, Houska and Mšeno, and Charles IV later redeemed Mšeno from his pledge.

He bought Jablonné and built the castles Milčany, Hrádek and Čáp. His seven sons founded the Kuřívody branch of the Berka family.

en:
George of Poděbrady (1420–1471) led the moderate Utraquist party. He seized Prague in 1448, and in 1451 Frederick III made him administrator of Bohemia; in 1458 the estates unanimously elected him king.

Ruling tolerantly under the Compacta of Prague, he was called the King of two peoples. When Pope Pius II declared the Compacta void in 1462, George rejected it, and in 1464 he proposed common European institutions in his peace treaty against the Turks.

Excommunicated by Pope Paul II in 1466, he fought Matthias Corvinus, who occupied much of Moravia and was elected rival king in 1469. George died in Prague in 1471.

en:
John of Luxembourg (1296–1346), called the Blind, was the eldest son of Emperor Henry VII and Margaret of Brabant. In 1310 he married Elizabeth of Bohemia, drove Henry of Carinthia from Prague, and was crowned king in 1311; from 1313 he also held Luxembourg. The Czech nobility saw an ‘alien king’, and he was often abroad.

He backed Louis IV at Mühldorf in 1322 and received the Egerland, and in 1335 sold his claim to the Polish crown to Casimir III. Crusading in Lithuania, he lost his sight to ophthalmia in 1336. When the Hundred Years' War began he joined Philip VI.

At Crécy in 1346 he commanded the French vanguard; Froissart tells how his knights tied their bridles together and led him into the English line, where he struck several blows before he was killed. His son Charles IV succeeded him in Bohemia.

Catherine of Vartenberk (died 1355), traditionally of the Vartenberk family, was the second wife of the Bohemian lord Peter I of Rosenberg, whom she married in 1318. She bore him five sons and three daughters, three of whom became lords of Rosenberg.

In 1347 she helped her husband found a hospital and was widowed. In 1350 she and her sons founded Franciscan monasteries at Krumlov, and she later donated vestments she had made to Vyšší Brod Abbey, where she was buried.

en:
Margaret of Bohemia (1335–1349), also called Margaret of Luxembourg, was the second child of Charles IV, later Holy Roman Emperor, and his first wife Blanche of Valois. In 1338 she was betrothed at age two to Amadeus VI, Count of Savoy, but the contract was broken.

In 1342, aged seven, she married Louis I of Hungary and became his queen. The marriage produced no children, and she died in 1349 at about fourteen, probably buried at Székesfehérvár.

Oldřich I of Rosenberg (died 1390) was the fourth son of Peter I of Rosenberg and Kateřina of Vartenberk. As a young man he helped endow the Minorite monastery in Český Krumlov.

When his brother Jošt died in 1369 he became head of the family, but kept out of public life because of the Rosenbergs' quarrel with the crown. In 1381–1382 he and his brothers aided Jindřich of Schaunberg against Duke Albert III of Austria.

en:
Ottokar II of Bohemia (c. 1233–1278), the Iron and Golden King, was elected Duke of Austria in 1251 and became king of Bohemia in 1253. He defeated Béla IV of Hungary at Kressenbrunn in 1260, securing Styria, and inherited Carinthia and Carniola in 1269, raising Bohemia to the height of its power.

Rudolf of Habsburg, elected German king in 1273, forced him to surrender the Alpine lands in 1276; Ottokar fell fighting to regain them at the Battle on the Marchfeld in 1278.

Peter II of Rosenberg (1326–1384) was a Bohemian churchman, the second son of Peter I of Rosenberg and Kateřina of Vartenberk. He held several canonries, and from 1355 served until his death as provost of All Saints' College at Prague Castle.

In 1384 Pope Urban VI offered him a cardinal's hat, which he refused, apparently aware that his death was near. He died at Vyšší Brod on 16 November 1384.

en:
Peter I of Rosenberg (c. 1282–1347) was a Bohemian nobleman who inherited the office of Supreme Chamberlain on his father Jindřich's death in 1310. He married Viola of Teschen, widow of King Wenceslas III, and later Kateřina of Vartenberk, who bore him five sons.

He joined the baronial revolt against John of Luxembourg in 1317, losing his office from 1319 to 1325. His name is linked to the Rosenberg Book, the oldest record of Czech land law.

en:
Rudolf I of Habsburg (c. 1281–1307), called the Good, was the eldest son of King Albert I of Germany and Elizabeth of Gorizia-Tyrol. From 1298 he ruled the Austrian and Styrian duchies as his father's co-ruler and acted as regent for his younger brothers.

His first wife Blanche of France died in 1305, after their two children had died young. After King Wenceslaus III of Bohemia was murdered in August 1306, Albert seized Bohemia and had Rudolf crowned king, marrying him to Elizabeth Richeza, widow of Wenceslaus II.

Many Bohemian nobles rejected him and rose in favour of Henry of Carinthia. While besieging the rebel castle of Horažďovice, Rudolf died of dysentery in July 1307, leaving no heir.

鲁道夫一世（约1281—1307），绰号“好人”，是罗马人的国王阿尔布雷希特一世与戈里茨-蒂罗尔的伊丽莎白的长子。1298年起，他作为父亲的共治者统治奥地利与施蒂利亚公国，并为年幼的弟弟们摄政。

他的第一任妻子法国的布朗歇于1305年去世，两人的一对子女也早夭。1306年8月，波希米亚国王瓦茨拉夫三世遇刺，阿尔布雷希特占领波希米亚，将鲁道夫立为国王，并让他迎娶瓦茨拉夫二世的遗孀伊丽莎白·里基莎。

许多波希米亚贵族拒不承认他，转而拥立克恩滕的亨利。鲁道夫在围攻叛军城堡霍拉日焦维采时染上痢疾，于1307年7月死在当地，身后无嗣。

en:
Rudolf II of Habsburg (c. 1270–1290), called the Debonair, was the youngest son of King Rudolf I of Germany. In 1282 his father enfeoffed him and his elder brother Albert with Austria and Styria jointly, but under the Treaty of Rheinfelden in 1283 Rudolf surrendered his share to Albert, receiving instead the honorific title Duke of Swabia.

In 1289 he married Agnes, daughter of King Ottokar II of Bohemia. He died in May 1290, aged twenty; his son John Parricida later murdered Albert in 1308.

Vilém z Landštejna (died 1356) was one of the most powerful Bohemian lords under King John of Luxembourg and later a loyal supporter of Emperor Charles IV. The son of Vítek z Landštejna, he inherited Třeboň and Landštejn and enlarged his domains.

He ended his career as Supreme Burgrave of Bohemia (1351–1356), and died of wounds from a duel with his kinsman Jindřich of Hradec over a trade route.

威廉·兹·兰德施泰因（逝于1356年）是卢森堡的约翰国王治下最有权势的捷克大贵族之一，后来成为查理四世的忠实支柱。他是维特克·兹·兰德施泰因之子，继承了特热博尼和兰德施泰因，并不断扩大领地。

他官至波希米亚最高城堡长官（1351—1356），最终因商路争执在与亲属因德日赫·兹·赫拉代茨的决斗中伤重而死。

en:
Vítek z Landštejna (died 1312) was a Bohemian nobleman of the Landštejn branch of the Vítkovci clan, son of Ojíř z Lomnice. Czech sources remember him and his father as fearless warriors. He held Landštejn Castle from about 1302 until 1311, together with the Třeboň estate.

After his death in 1312 his lands were divided between his sons Smil, who received Ledenice, and Vilém, who inherited Třeboň and Landštejn.

en:
Wenceslaus II (1271–1305), son of Ottokar II of Bohemia, inherited the crown when his father fell at the Battle on the Marchfeld in 1278. After years under Brandenburg regency he returned to Prague in 1283, married Judith of Habsburg in 1285, and took power in person after executing his stepfather Záviš of Falkenstein in 1290.

Wealth from the Kutná Hora silver mines produced the Prague groschen. Crowned king of Poland at Gniezno in 1300, he accepted the Hungarian crown for his son after the Árpád male line died out in 1301.

In 1304 he marched to Buda and brought his son and the crown back to Bohemia. He died in 1305, aged thirty-three.

1304年，他率军前往布达，将儿子和王冠带回波希米亚。1305年他去世，年仅33岁。

en:
Wenceslaus III (1289–1306) was the last ruler of Bohemia's Přemyslid dynasty, the son of Wenceslaus II and Judith of Habsburg. He was crowned king of Hungary in 1301, but his rule there was nominal and his father brought him home in 1304.

Succeeding to Bohemia and Poland in 1305, he ceded his Hungarian claim to Otto III of Bavaria. After Władysław Łokietek took Kraków in 1306, Wenceslaus prepared a Polish campaign, but was stabbed to death at Olomouc the same year, his assassin never identified.

en:
Wenceslaus I (1337–1383), first Duke of Luxembourg, was the son of John the Blind of Bohemia and Beatrice of Bourbon. In 1352 he married Joanna, heiress of Brabant, and in 1353 his half-brother Charles IV made him Count of Luxembourg; it became a duchy in 1354.

After Joanna inherited Brabant in 1355 he confirmed its liberties. Captured at Baesweiler in 1371, he spent eleven months a prisoner. He died in 1383; a poet himself, he left seventy-nine poems.

温塞斯拉斯一世（1337—1383）是第一代卢森堡公爵，波希米亚国王盲人约翰与波旁的比阿特丽斯之子。1352年，他与布拉班特女继承人让娜结婚；1353年，异母兄查理四世将卢森堡伯国交给他，该地于1354年升为公国。

1355年让娜继承布拉班特后，他确认了当地的自由特权。1371年他在巴斯韦勒被俘，囚禁十一个月。1383年去世；他本人是诗人，留有诗作79首。

en:
Wok I of Rosenberg (c. 1210–1262) was a Bohemian nobleman of the Vítkovci clan and the first of his line to style himself after Rožmberk Castle. He was made court marshal by King Ottokar II in 1255 and accompanied the king's Prussian crusade.

He fought in the victory at Kressenbrunn over Hungary in 1260, receiving the Raabs lordship, and founded Vyšší Brod Monastery in 1259. Wok died at Graz in 1262 and was buried there; his son Jindřich succeeded him.

en:
Bolot was a Yuan imperial prince, son of Esen Temür and younger brother of Tughluq. During the Zhizheng reign of Toghon Temür he succeeded as Prince of Yunnan.

In 1346, when Si Kefa of Luchuan broke away, Bolot campaigned against him and presented captives at the capital Dadu in 1347. In 1355 he was raised to Prince of Liang for his merits. His son was Basalawarmi, the last Yuan ruler of Yunnan.

en:
Jelena Šubić (died c. 1378) was the daughter of George II Šubić, Count of Klis. In late 1337 or early 1338 she married Vladislav, brother of Ban Stephen II of Bosnia, sealing her brother Mladen III's alliance with Bosnia against the Hungarian king.

When Stephen died in autumn 1353, her son Tvrtko, about fifteen, became ban. Jelena and Vladislav, the latter excluded from the succession, ruled for him; Vladislav died within a year, and she ruled alone until 1357. She first visited her overlord Louis I of Hungary to win his consent.

At a Mile assembly she confirmed noble privileges, and in 1355 marched to Duvno to settle the Šubić inheritance dispute. In 1374 she arranged Tvrtko's wedding to Dorothea of Bulgaria; three years later he was crowned king.

耶莱娜·舒比奇（约1378年卒）是克利什伯爵尤拉伊二世·舒比奇之女。1337年底或1338年初，她嫁给波斯尼亚班斯特凡二世之弟弗拉迪斯拉夫，巩固了姆拉登三世与波斯尼亚对抗匈牙利国王的同盟。

1353年秋斯特凡去世，她约十五岁的儿子特夫尔特科继任班。耶莱娜与被排除在继承之外的弗拉迪斯拉夫以少主名义执政；一年内弗拉迪斯拉夫去世，她独自执政至1357年。她先赴宗主匈牙利国王拉约什一世的宫廷，请求认可儿子继位。

en:
Catherine of Bosnia (Katarina Kotromanić, born c. 1336) was a Kotromanić princess, generally held to be a daughter of Ban Stephen II. In 1361 she married Hermann I, Count of Celje. Her elder son Hans died young; Hermann II succeeded as count and in 1427 was recognized as heir presumptive to the Bosnian throne.

Through Hermann’s daughter Barbara, wife of Emperor Sigismund, Catherine was an ancestress of later European royal houses. She died after 1400.

波斯尼亚的卡塔琳娜（卡塔琳娜·科特罗马尼奇，约1336年生）是科特罗马尼奇王朝的公主，一般认为是波斯尼亚班斯蒂芬二世之女。1361年，她嫁给采列伯爵赫尔曼一世。长子汉斯早夭，赫尔曼二世后来承袭伯爵，并于1427年被认定为波斯尼亚王位的推定继承人。

凭借赫尔曼二世之女、皇帝西吉斯蒙德之妻芭芭拉，卡塔琳娜成为后世欧洲各王室的祖先。她于1400年后去世。

Catherine Kotromanić was a Bosnian princess, daughter of Ban Stephen I of Bosnia and Elizabeth Nemanjić and sister of Ban Stephen II. Born around 1294, about 1310 she married Nicholas, the župan of Hum, and made her home at Blagaj, bearing him two sons, Vladislav and Bogiša.

Some accounts say that after Nicholas died around 1340 she remarried and became mother of the vojvoda Hrvoje. She died at Birbir in 1355.

Kotroman, called the Goth in Ragusan writings, is the legendary forefather of the Bosnian Kotromanić dynasty. In 1432 the Ragusan government described him as a knight, a kinsman of the Hungarian king, who came from Hungary and took possession of the banate of Bosnia.

The chronicler Mavro Orbini presents him as a warrior appointed ban after the death of Ban Kulin about 1204. Genealogical reconstructions make him the grandfather of Bans Matej Ninoslav and Prijezda I.

en:
Maria of Bosnia (Marija Kotromanić, born after 1333, died 27 April 1403) was a Kotromanić princess, likely a younger daughter of Ban Stephen II. In 1352 Emperor Charles IV arranged her marriage to Ulrich V, Count of Helfenstein, and she travelled to Passau for the wedding. A supporter of the emperor, she bore six sons and three daughters.

Widowed when Ulrich was killed in 1372, she spent her later years at Bühringen. She founded a hospital in Swabia and was probably buried at Überkingen.

en:
Matej Ninoslav (died 1250) was ban of Bosnia from 1232, when he replaced Stjepan Kulinić with the backing of the Bosnian Church. In 1233 he swore to Pope Gregory IX to remain a Catholic, while his cousin Prijezda gave his son as a hostage to seal his conversion.

Gregory nonetheless proclaimed the Bosnian Crusade in 1234, and the Hungarian king granted Ninoslav's title to Coloman. Hungarian armies overran the country for years; after the Mongol invasion of 1241 Ninoslav restored his rule.

He served as prince of Split from 1242 to 1244 and issued trade charters to Ragusa. On his death in 1250 his cousin Prijezda succeeded him.

马特伊·尼诺斯拉夫（？—1250）自1232年起任波斯尼亚班，在波斯尼亚教会支持下取代了斯捷潘·库利尼奇。1233年，他向教宗格列高利九世宣誓继续信奉天主教；他的堂亲普里耶兹达交出儿子作为人质，为自己改宗作保。

尽管如此，格列高利九世仍于1234年宣布发动波斯尼亚十字军，匈牙利国王也将尼诺斯拉夫的头衔授予科洛曼。匈牙利军队连年攻占波斯尼亚；1241年蒙古人入侵后，尼诺斯拉夫恢复了统治。

1242至1244年他出任斯普利特的领主，并向拉古萨颁发贸易特许状。1250年他去世，堂亲普里耶兹达继位。

en:
Mladen II Šubić of Bribir (c. 1270–c. 1341) was the eldest son of Paul I Šubić, the most powerful Croatian noble of his day, who named him Ban of Bosnia in 1305. When Paul died in 1312, Mladen inherited a dominion covering Croatia, Bosnia and the Dalmatian cities.

He ruled Bosnia through Stephen Kotromanić as his vassal, and in 1313 returned Zadar to Venice in return for autonomy. In 1315 he backed the exiles of Trogir and demanded that the city send him a blank sheet on which he would write his terms, settling for a heavy fine.

After risings at Šibenik and Trogir in 1321–1322, Dalmatian cities and Croatian nobles turned on him, and King Charles Robert of Hungary, whom the Šubići had helped to his throne, defeated him at Bliska. Taken to Hungary, he died in prison around 1341; the family lost Bosnia and its dominance.

布里比尔的姆拉登二世·舒比奇（约1270—约1341）是帕瓦奥一世·舒比奇的长子，其父是当时克罗地亚最有权势的贵族，1305年立他为波斯尼亚班。1312年保罗去世，他继承囊括克罗地亚、波斯尼亚和达尔马提亚的领地。

他通过封臣斯特凡·科特罗马尼奇统治波斯尼亚，1313年扎达尔以自治为条件回归威尼斯。1315年他支持特罗吉尔流亡者，要求该城送来一张白纸由他写下条件，最终以重罚了结。

Ninoslav Kotromanić, also called Miroslav, was a Bosnian prince born at Jajce around 1288, son of Ban Stephen I of Bosnia and Elizabeth Nemanjić and brother of Ban Stephen II. When his father died around 1314 and the Šubić seized power, the chronicler Orbini records that he and his brother Vladislav took refuge at Medvedgrad in Croatia.

He died before the autumn of 1353, leaving illegitimate sons barred from succession. Later tradition names Maria of Helfenstein and King Stephen Dabiša as his children.

en:
Paul I Šubić of Bribir (c. 1245–1312), head of the leading Croatian noble house, became Ban of Croatia in 1275. With his brothers he brought most Dalmatian coastal cities under his rule and fought Venice until peace in 1294.

During the succession crisis he was the chief ally of the Angevins against the Árpáds, and escorted Charles Robert to Zagreb in 1300. He conquered the Banate of Bosnia in 1299 and Hum in 1301, and in 1304 quelled a Bosnian rebellion after his brother Mladen was killed and made his son Mladen ban. He took Zadar from Venice in 1311 and died on 1 May 1312, leaving his domains to his son Mladen II.

在王位继承危机中，他是安茹家族对抗阿帕德王朝的首要盟友，1300年护送查理·罗伯特前往萨格勒布。1299年他征服波斯尼亚班领地，1301年又攻取胡姆；1304年兄弟姆拉登被杀后，他平定波斯尼亚叛乱，任命儿子姆拉登为班。1311年他从威尼斯手中夺取扎达尔，1312年5月1日去世，领地传给儿子姆拉登二世。

en:
Prijezda I Kotromanić (fl. 1233–1287) was ban of Bosnia. His origins are disputed, though some historians regard him as the first known member of the Kotromanić dynasty. A kinsman of Ban Matej Ninoslav, he appears in 1233 as his vice-ban, newly returned to Catholicism from the Bosnian Church.

By 1240 he had sided with Hungary against Ninoslav. With Hungarian backing he secured the banate by 1255, when King Béla IV granted him Bosnia proper, and he campaigned against Bohemia in 1260. In 1284 his son Stephen married a daughter of the Serbian king Stefan Dragutin, and in 1287 he died in office.

en:
Prijezda II Kotromanić (1242–1290) was a son of Ban Prijezda I of Bosnia. In 1287 the old ban granted a district in the Donji Kraji with his sons' consent.

When Prijezda I died that year, the brothers divided Bosnia: Prijezda II took the western lands while Stephen I, called Kotroman, held the east. In 1290 the pope addressed the two brothers as joint bans of Bosnia. Prijezda II died later that year, and his lands passed to his brother.

en:
Stephen II Kotromanić (c. 1292–1353), Ban of Bosnia from 1314, was the son of Ban Stephen I and Elizabeth Nemanjić. After his father died the family fled to Ragusa, until the Croatian magnate Mladen II Šubić, who dominated Bosnia, installed him as a vassal.

Stephen turned on Mladen with King Charles I of Hungary, whose victory in 1322 left him ruling in person. He annexed Usora and Soli in 1324, took Hum from Serbia, and ceded Ston and Pelješac to Ragusa in 1333. Playing Hungary and Venice against each other, in 1340 he persuaded the pope of his Catholic loyalty.

In 1350 Stefan Dušan invaded with a far larger army; Stephen held Bobovac, and when Dušan gave up he retook the lost lands. His daughter Elizabeth went to Hungary to marry Louis I, but Stephen, ill, missed the wedding and died in September 1353. His young nephew Tvrtko succeeded.

en:
Stephen I Kotromanić, called Kotroman (1242–1314), was ban of Bosnia and father of Ban Stephen II. He ruled eastern Bosnia jointly with his brother Prijezda II from 1287, and alone from 1290. In 1284 he married Elizabeth, daughter of Stefan Dragutin of Syrmia.

Amid Hungary's succession wars the Croatian Šubić family overran most of his lands: by 1302 Mladen I Šubić held nearly all of Bosnia, and in 1305 Paul Šubić claimed the whole country.

Mladen's persecution of the Bosnian Church drove some of its adherents to Kotroman's side. Kotroman nonetheless held out, but died in 1314 before he could recover his realm.

Vladislav Kotromanić (1295–1354) was a younger son of Ban Stephen I of Bosnia and Elizabeth of Serbia, and younger brother of Ban Stephen II. As a child he fled the Šubić takeover for Medvedgrad in Croatia. From 1326 he jointly issued his brother’s charters.

In 1337 or 1338 he married Jelena and had two sons, Tvrtko and Vuk. When Stephen II died in 1353 the title of Ban passed to the young Tvrtko, and Vladislav ruled Bosnia as regent until his own death in 1354.

In 1337 or 1338 he married #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('ser_jelena').GetID],X #L Jelena#!#! and had two sons, Tvrtko and Vuk. When Stephen II died in 1353 the title of Ban passed to the young Tvrtko, and Vladislav ruled Bosnia as regent until his own death in 1354.
zh:
弗拉迪斯拉夫·科特罗马尼奇（1295—1354）是波斯尼亚班斯蒂芬一世与塞尔维亚的伊丽莎白之子、波斯尼亚班斯蒂芬二世之弟。幼年时为躲避舒比奇家族夺权，流亡到克罗地亚的梅德韦德格勒。1326年起，他与兄长联合签发文书。

1337或1338年，他娶耶莱娜为妻，生有特弗尔特科和武克两子。1353年斯蒂芬二世去世，班位传给年幼的特弗尔特科，弗拉迪斯拉夫以摄政身份统治波斯尼亚，直至1354年去世。

en:
Archambaud IX, called the Young (1212–1249), was seigneur of Bourbon and son of Archambaud VIII and Beatrice of Montluçon. He married Yolande I, Countess of Nevers; their daughters were Matilda II, Countess of Nevers, and Agnes, lady of Bourbon.

In 1242 he revised the town taxes of Moulins, remitting its annual rent for a citizenship levy graded by wealth. In 1248 he joined Louis IX's Seventh Crusade, but an epidemic at the fleet's Cyprus stopover carried him off; he died there in January 1249.

en:
Archambaud VIII, called the Great (c. 1189–1242), was seigneur of Bourbon from 1216, succeeding his father Guy II of Dampierre; his mother was Mathilde I, heiress of the lordship. After Philip II Augustus confiscated Auvergne in 1213, he was made its guardian and in 1223 constable of Auvergne. About 1215 he married Beatrice of Montluçon, mother of his heir Archambaud IX.

In 1232 he granted a charter of liberties to Moulins, supplementing earlier privileges, in return for an annual payment of 200 livres. He died at the Battle of Taillebourg in 1242.

Beatrice of Burgundy (1257–1310) was ruling Lady of Bourbon suo jure from 1288, when she inherited the Bourbon estates through her mother, Agnes of Dampierre. Her father was John of Burgundy, a son of Duke Hugh IV of Burgundy.

In 1272 she married Robert, Count of Clermont. Their eldest son, Louis I, called the Lame, became the first Duke of Bourbon. Beatrice died in 1310.

en:
Isabella of Valois (1313–1383) was the daughter of Charles of Valois and half-sister of King Philip VI. In 1336 she married Peter I, Duke of Bourbon, and bore eight children, including Louis II, Duke of Bourbon, and Joanna, who married the future King Charles V in 1350.

After Peter was killed at Poitiers in 1356 she took the veil. In 1369 mercenaries seized her at Belleperche Castle and Charles V ransomed her in 1372. She died in Paris in 1383.

en:
James I of Bourbon (1319–1362), son of Duke Louis I, was Count of La Marche from 1341 and founder of the line that, seven generations on, gave France Henry IV. He fought for Charles de Blois in Brittany.

Closeness to King John II brought him the county of Ponthieu in 1351 and the office of Constable of France. At Poitiers in 1356 he was wounded and captured. The 1360 Treaty of Brétigny freed him but cost him Ponthieu, returned to the English.

When the Free Companies of discharged mercenaries ravaged the countryside, John ordered him to raise an army against them. On 6 April 1362 the companies surprised and routed it at Brignais; James and his eldest son died of their wounds at Lyon.

波旁的雅各一世（1319—1362）是波旁公爵路易一世之子，1341年起封拉马什伯爵，他开创的这一支传了七代后出了法王亨利四世。他曾在布列塔尼为夏尔·德·布卢瓦作战。

他与国王约翰二世关系亲近，1351年得到蓬蒂厄伯爵领，又出任法兰西统帅。1356年在普瓦捷负伤并被俘。1360年《布雷蒂尼条约》使他获释，蓬蒂厄却被归还给英国人。

被遣散的佣兵组成自由佣兵团，劫掠乡村，约翰二世命他集军讨伐。1362年4月6日，佣兵团在布里涅突袭并击溃这支军队，雅各与长子负伤，死于里昂。

en:
Louis I, called the Lame (1279–1341), was the first Duke of Bourbon and a grandson of King Louis IX. Through his mother Beatrix of Burgundy he inherited Bourbon. He fought at the Golden Spurs and Mons-en-Pévèle and became Grand Chamberlain of France in 1310.

Crusading was his cause: he took the cross in 1316 and was to lead an expedition until Genoa destroyed the assembling fleet in 1319. A second crusade plan was cancelled in 1336 as war with England loomed.

In 1327 Charles IV took Clermont from him, gave him La Marche, and raised Bourbon to a duchy-peerage; his support for Philip VI's claim won Clermont back in 1331. Chroniclers report spells of severe mental infirmity, which some historians trace through his granddaughter Joanna to her son Charles VI. He died in 1341 and his son Peter succeeded him.

路易一世，绰号“跛子”（1279—1341），是第一代波旁公爵，法王路易九世之孙。他通过母亲勃艮第的比阿特丽斯继承波旁领地，参加过金马刺战役和蒙桑佩韦勒战役，1310年出任法国宫廷总管。

十字军是他一生的事业：1316年他立下十字军誓约，原定由他统领远征，但集结中的舰队于1319年被热那亚人摧毁。随着英法战争迫近，另一项十字军计划于1336年取消。

1327年，查理四世从他手中收回克莱蒙，改封拉马什，并把波旁升格为公爵兼法兰西贵族领；他支持腓力六世继承王位，国王于1331年将克莱蒙归还给他。编年史家记载他曾有严重的精神失常，一些史家认为这一病症经孙女让娜传到她的儿子查理六世身上。1341年他去世，儿子皮埃尔继位。

Mary of Avesnes (1280–1354), also called Marie of Hainaut, was a daughter of John II, Count of Holland and Hainaut, and Philippa of Luxembourg. In 1310 she married Louis I, Duke of Bourbon, and bore him eight children.

Among them were Peter I, Duke of Bourbon, and James I, Count of La Marche, both killed in battle after her death, and Beatrice, who in 1334 married King John of Bohemia. Through her brother William I of Hainaut she was aunt to Philippa of Hainault, queen of England.

阿韦讷的玛丽（1280—1354），又称埃诺的玛丽，是荷兰与埃诺伯爵约翰二世和卢森堡的菲莉帕之女。1310年她嫁给波旁公爵路易一世，共育有八名子女。

其中包括波旁公爵皮埃尔一世和拉马尔什伯爵詹姆斯一世，二人都在她去世后战死；还有1334年嫁给波希米亚国王约翰的比阿特丽丝。经由兄长埃诺伯爵威廉一世，她是英格兰王后埃诺的菲利帕的姑母。

en:
Marie de Bourbon (c. 1315–1387) was a daughter of Louis I, Duke of Bourbon and Mary of Avesnes. In 1329 she reached Cyprus to marry Guy of Lusignan, titular Prince of Galilee; they wed in 1330 and their son Hugh was born around 1335.

Left a widow in 1343, she was forbidden by her father-in-law to leave Cyprus until 1346. In 1347 she married Robert of Taranto, Prince of Achaea and titular Latin Emperor. When Robert died childless in 1364 she refused to accept his brother Philip II as heir.

Holding sixteen castles in Achaea, she kept the title of princess and put forward Hugh, who invaded the Peloponnese in 1366 with 12,000 mercenaries. The war ended in 1370, when she sold her rights to Philip for 6,000 gold pieces and kept only Kalamata. She named her nephew Louis II of Bourbon her heir.

玛丽·德·波旁（约1315—1387）是波旁公爵路易一世与阿韦讷的玛丽之女。1329年她抵达塞浦路斯，嫁给名义上的加利利亲王吕西尼昂的居伊；1330年成婚，儿子于格约生于1335年。

1343年居伊去世后，公公禁止她离开塞浦路斯，直到1346年才准许。1347年，她改嫁亚该亚亲王、名义上的拉丁帝国皇帝塔兰托的罗伯特。1364年罗伯特无嗣而终，她拒不承认其弟腓力二世继位。

她凭借在亚该亚拥有的十六座城堡，保留亲王头衔，推举于格争位；于格1366年率一万两千名雇佣兵入侵伯罗奔尼撒。战争于1370年结束，她以六千金币把权利卖给腓力，只保留卡拉马塔。她指定侄子波旁公爵路易二世为继承人。

en:
Matilda II of Bourbon (1234–1262), also called Mahaut of Dampierre, was countess of Nevers, Auxerre and Tonnerre, and the elder daughter of Archambaud IX, lord of Bourbon, and Yolande of Châtillon. In 1248 she married Odo of Burgundy, eldest son of Duke Hugh IV.

On the death of her great-grandmother Matilda of Courtenay in 1257 she entered into the three counties. She died in 1262 aged 28, and they were divided among her daughters Yolande, Margaret and Alix.

玛蒂尔德二世·德·波旁（1234—1262），一称当皮埃尔的玛霍，是讷韦尔、欧塞尔和托内尔女伯爵，也是波旁领主阿尔尚博九世与沙蒂永的约兰德的长女。1248年，她嫁给勃艮第公爵于格四世的长子厄德。

1257年外曾祖母库特奈的玛蒂尔德去世后，她取得讷韦尔、欧塞尔和托内尔三个伯国。1262年她去世，年仅28岁，三个伯国由女儿约兰德、玛格丽特和阿莉克斯瓜分。

en:
Pierre d'André (c. 1300–1368), born at Clermont, rose from Keeper of the Seals of France and bishop of Noyon in 1339 to the sees of Clermont in 1342 and Cambrai in 1350.

At Clermont he was fined in 1347 for setting up a market without royal authority. At Cambrai his vicar general was Guillaume de Grimoard, the future Pope Urban V, and he is credited with building the palace clock and establishing the feast of Saint Martial. He died at Cambrai on 13 September 1368.

zh:
皮埃尔·德·安德烈（约1300—1368）生于克莱蒙，1339年出任法国掌玺大臣兼努瓦永主教，1342年调任克莱蒙主教，1350年调任康布雷主教。

在克莱蒙，他于1347年因未经国王许可设立集市而被罚款。在康布雷，他的副主教是后来成为教皇乌尔班五世的纪尧姆·德·格里马尔；他还被认为主持修建了主教宫时钟，并设立了圣马夏尔节。1368年9月13日，他卒于康布雷。

en:
Peter I (1311–1356) was the second Duke of Bourbon, succeeding his father Louis I in 1342 as duke and Grand Chamberlain of France. In 1336 he married Isabella of Valois, sister of Philip VI. He fought in Brittany in 1341, helping the French claimant Charles de Blois take possession of the duchy.

In August 1345 he was made lieutenant in Languedoc against Henry of Derby. Peter raised a new army, but Derby defeated it at Auberoche that October, and Peter was wounded at Crécy in August 1346.

From 1347 he led peace embassies, all fruitless. On 19 September 1356 he was killed at Poitiers, shielding King John II with his body; his daughters Joanna and Blanche had married Charles V of France and Peter the Cruel of Castile.

zh:
皮埃尔一世（1311—1356）是第二代波旁公爵，1342年继承父亲路易一世的公爵之位，并接任法国宫廷总管。1336年他娶腓力六世之妹瓦卢瓦的伊莎贝拉为妻。1341年，他在布列塔尼作战，协助法方继承人夏尔·德·布卢瓦接管公国。

1345年8月，他被任命为朗格多克督军，对手是德比的亨利。皮埃尔募集新军，但德比10月在欧贝罗什将其击败；1346年8月，他又在克雷西负伤。

1347年起他多次率团进行和谈，均无结果。1356年9月19日，他在普瓦捷战役中为护卫国王约翰二世而阵亡；他的女儿让娜和布朗什分别嫁给了法王查理五世与卡斯蒂利亚的残忍者佩德罗。

Robert, Count of Clermont (1256–1317), was the youngest son of King Louis IX of France, created count in 1268. A head injury in youth left him handicapped, so he played little part in public affairs. In 1272 he married Beatrice of Burgundy, heiress to the lordship of Bourbon.

Through their son Louis I, the first Duke of Bourbon, Robert became the founder of the House of Bourbon, which inherited the French throne in 1589. He died on 7 February 1317.

en:
Yolande of Châtillon (c. 1221–1254) was daughter of Guy II of Saint-Pol and Agnes II of Donzy, heiress of Nevers, Tonnerre and Auxerre. Her mother died in 1225 and her father was killed at the siege of Avignon in 1226; her grandmother raised her.

She married Archambaud IX, lord of Bourbon, and in 1248 followed him on the Seventh Crusade; he died in an epidemic in Cyprus in 1249. When her brother Gaucher died in 1250 she inherited three counties; at her death in 1254 they went to her daughter Matilda and Bourbon to Agnes.

Atula Dewi (born 1266), personal name Min Hla Myat, was chief queen consort of Thihathu, Viceroy of Prome. She was the youngest and only sister of the three brothers who founded the Myinsaing Kingdom after the collapse of Pagan.

In 1287 her husband murdered his father, King Narathihapate, and was killed at Pegu in 1288 before seizing the throne. Her daughter Shin Myat Hla became the mother of King Swa Saw Ke of Ava, who came to the throne in 1367.

en:
Min Shin Saw was governor of Thayet, a vassal state of the Pinya Kingdom in Upper Burma. A son of King Kyawswa of Pagan, he married Shin Myat Hla. In 1334 Arakanese raiders sacked Thayet and carried his family off to the Arakanese capital Launggyet.

Held for nearly a decade, they returned in 1343 or 1344 and he was reappointed governor. His sons included Swa Saw Ke, founder of the Ava Kingdom, and Saw Yan Naung of Prome.

A son of King #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('pin_kyawswa_pagan').GetID],X #L Kyawswa of Pagan#!#!, he married #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('bpr_shin_myat_hla').GetID],X #L Shin Myat Hla#!#!. zh:
敏欣绍是上缅甸彬牙王国属邦德耶的总督，为蒲甘国王觉苏瓦之子，娶欣妙拉为妻。1334年，若开军队劫掠德耶，将全家掳往若开都城隆邑。

一家人被扣押近十年，1343或1344年返回，他重新被任命为德耶总督。他的儿子中有阿瓦王朝的实际奠基人明基苏瓦绍盖，以及卑谬总督绍扬南。

en:
Saw Myat (born 1332) was a daughter of Min Shin Saw of Thayet and younger sister of King Swa Saw Ke of Ava. Still an infant, she was carried off with her family to the Arakanese capital Launggyet after the 1334 sack of Thayet, returning in 1343 or 1344.

From the 1360s to the 1390s she was duchess of Sagu. She was the grandmother of Shin Bo-Me, who became a principal queen of Ava.

en:
Saw Omma (born c. 1333), originally named Ommadanti, was the youngest child of Min Shin Saw of Thayet and sister of King Swa Saw Ke of Ava. She spent her childhood in Arakanese captivity at Launggyet after the 1334 sack of Thayet, returning around 1343.

Her beauty made her chief queen to the last three kings of Pinya and then to Thado Minbya of Ava. After Thado Minbya died in 1367, she and a commander failed to seize the throne, and her brother pardoned her.

绍翁玛（约1333年生），原名翁玛丹蒂，是德耶的敏欣绍最小的孩子、阿瓦国王明基苏瓦绍盖的妹妹。1334年德耶陷落后，她的童年在阿腊干隆邑的扣留岁月中度过，约1343年返回。

凭借美貌，她先后成为彬牙末代三位国王和阿瓦的德多明帕耶的首席王后。1367年德多明帕耶死后，她与一名禁军统领图谋篡位失败，其兄赦免了她。

en:
Saw Pale (born 1331) was a daughter of Governor Min Shin Saw of Thayet and Shin Myat Hla, and the eldest sister of King Swa Saw Ke of Ava. She was carried to Arakan in the 1334 sack of Thayet and returned in 1343 or 1344.

She married Thilawa, governor of Yamethin, who in 1367 declined the Ava throne and recommended her brother as king. She was mother of Queen Min Hla Myat and maternal grandmother of King Kale Kye-Taung Nyo.

en:
Saw Yan Naung (1323/24–1377/78) held Prome, on the Irrawaddy, for over three decades. A grandson of King Kyawswa of Pagan and son of Governor Min Shin Saw of Thayet, he was carried off to Launggyet with his family by Arakanese raiders in 1334 and held until his release around 1344.

Kyawswa I of Pinya then made him governor of Prome. As Pinya's authority collapsed in the late 1350s he ruled like a sovereign, though he never declared independence as Toungoo did. In 1367–1368 he joined his brother Swa Saw Ke, new king of Ava.

In 1375 Swa enlisted him against Pyanchi I, viceroy of Toungoo, allied with Hanthawaddy. He proposed a marriage between his daughter and Pyanchi's son, to be held at Prome; Pyanchi came with a small force and was ambushed and killed. Swa made his brother viceroy, and he died in 1377 or 1378.

zh:
绍扬南（1323/24—1377/78）在三十余年间执掌伊洛瓦底江畔的卑谬。他是蒲甘国王觉苏瓦之孙、德耶总督敏欣绍之子；1334年若开人将他全家掳往隆吉，直到约1344年才获释。

彬牙国王觉苏瓦一世随即任命他为卑谬总督。1350年代末彬牙中央权力崩塌，他像独立君主般统治卑谬，却不曾像东吁那样正式宣布独立。1367至1368年，他投奔弟弟、阿瓦新王明基苏瓦绍盖。

1375年，苏瓦让他对付已与汉达瓦底结盟的东吁副王般师一世。绍扬南提议让自己的女儿与般师之子联姻，婚礼在卑谬举行；般师率小队人马前来，被伏击身亡。苏瓦因此将兄长升为副王；他于1377或1378年去世。

en:
Shin Myat Hla was a Pagan princess born around 1288, the only daughter of Viceroy Thihathu of Prome and Atula Dewi, herself sister of the three founders of the Myinsaing Kingdom. Through her father she was a granddaughter of King Narathihapate.

She married Min Shin Saw, governor of Thayet, and in 1334 was carried off with her family to the Arakanese capital Launggyet; they returned in 1343 or 1344. Her six children included King Swa Saw Ke of Ava and Queen Saw Omma of Pinya.

en:
Shwe Nan Shin (born 1322) was the eldest child of Governor Min Shin Saw of Thayet, and elder brother of King Swa Saw Ke of Ava. In 1334 Arakanese raiders sacked Thayet and carried him and his family to Launggyet in Arakan, where they were held until 1343 or 1344.

The family was treated well and the children were taught by an Arakanese monk. After their return, his father was reappointed at Thayet, while he and his brother Saw Yan Naung became governors of Myinsaing and Prome.

en:
Mingyi Swa Saw Ke (1330–1400) ruled Ava from 1367 to 1400 and founded its power. A son of Min Shin Saw of Thayet, he spent his youth in Arakanese captivity after the 1334 sack of Thayet, then governed Yamethin. Chosen to succeed Thado Minbya, he reunified Upper Burma and in 1373 placed his nominee on the Arakanese throne.

His invasions of Pegu from 1385 opened the Forty Years' War, ending in a 1391 truce. He died in 1400, succeeded by his son Tarabya.

明基苏瓦绍盖（1330—1400）是阿瓦王朝实际的奠基人，1367—1400年在位。他是德耶的敏欣绍之子，1334年德耶被阿腊干军队攻破后自幼在隆邑为质，其后受封央米丁。被群臣推举继德多明帕耶之后即位后，他重新统一上缅甸，并于1373年把属意的人选扶上阿腊干王位。

1385年起他多次南征勃固，开启阿瓦与勃固的四十年战争，最终于1391年停战。1400年驾崩，其子德勒帕耶继位。

en:
Thihathu (d. 1288) was a son of King Narathihapate, the last sovereign ruler of the Pagan Empire, and served as viceroy of Prome from 1275. During the Mongol invasion his father fled Pagan and submitted to the Mongols in 1287; when the king passed through Prome, Thihathu seized him in 1287 and forced him to swallow poison.

He then murdered a rival half-brother and marched on Dala and Pegu, where in 1288 he accidentally killed himself with his own crossbow bolt.

梯诃都（？—1288）是蒲甘帝国末代国王那腊底哈勃德之子，1275年起任卑谬总督。蒙古入侵期间，其父逃离蒲甘，并于1287年向蒙古称臣；国王途经卑谬时，梯诃都于1287年将他拘捕，逼他服毒自尽。

随后他杀害了与自己争位的异母兄弟，又进军达拉和勃固，1288年在勃固被自己的弩箭误杀身亡。

en:
Fayid ibn Muqaddam was an Arab amir of the Banu Hayb, a branch of the Banu Sulaym that dominated Barqa in modern Libya under Mamluk overlordship. During the third reign of Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad he was the recognized muqaddam, or chief, of the Arabs of Barqa.

In 1319 he and Sulayman, both of the Banu Muqaddam, led tribal auxiliaries from al-Buhayra in the sultan's expedition against the rebel amir Ja'far ibn Umar of the Ja'afira.

法伊德·本·穆卡丹是巴努海卜部的阿拉伯埃米尔；该部是巴努苏莱姆人的分支，在马穆鲁克宗主权下据有今利比亚的拜尔盖。在苏丹纳西尔·穆罕默德第三次在位期间，他是拜尔盖阿拉伯人公认的首领（阿拉伯语称穆卡丹）。

1319年，他与同属巴努穆卡丹部的苏莱曼一起，率领来自布海拉的部落辅助军，参加苏丹征讨贾法拉部反叛埃米尔贾法尔·本·欧麦尔的战役。

en:
Agnes of Bavaria (1276–1345) was a daughter of Duke Louis II of Upper Bavaria and Matilda of Habsburg. In 1290 she married Henry the Younger of Hesse, son of Landgrave Henry I, and had a daughter Agnes. After Henry's death in 1298, she married Margrave Henry I of Brandenburg-Stendal of the House of Ascania in 1303.

This marriage produced Henry II and two daughters, Sophia and Judith, who married into the Brunswick ducal house. She died in 1345.

巴伐利亚的阿格尼丝（1276—1345）是上巴伐利亚公爵路德维希二世与哈布斯堡的玛蒂尔达之女。1290年她嫁给黑森领地伯爵亨利一世之子“小亨利”，生有一女阿格尼丝。1298年丈夫去世后，她于1303年改嫁阿斯坎尼家族的勃兰登堡-施滕达尔藩侯亨利一世。

en:
Albert the Bear (c. 1100–1170), son of Count Otto of Ballenstedt, was the first margrave of Brandenburg and founder of Ascanian rule in the mark. King Lothair enfeoffed him with the Northern March in 1134, and he briefly held the Duchy of Saxony from 1138 to 1142.

He joined the Wendish Crusade in 1147 and in 1150 inherited Brandenburg from the Wendish prince Pribislav-Henry, founding the Margraviate of Brandenburg in 1157. He promoted Dutch and German settlement east of the Elbe, and died in 1170.

Albert II (c. 1177–1220), youngest son of Margrave Otto I, ruled Brandenburg from 1205 as the fourth Ascanian margrave. He joined the German Crusade of 1197 and attended the Teutonic Knights' founding in 1198.

At first he supported Philip of Swabia, but after Philip's murder in 1208 he turned to Emperor Otto IV, who confirmed the margraviate in 1212. He secured Teltow, Prignitz and parts of the Uckermark. When he died in 1220 his young sons John I and Otto III succeeded under a regency.

en:
Albert III (c. 1250–1300) was an Ascanian margrave of Brandenburg-Salzwedel, son of Margrave Otto III and Beatrice of Bohemia. He was a co-ruler while his cousin Otto IV 'with the Arrow' held power, and administered Stargard, serving as lord of Stargard and Lychen from 1284.

After his sons died around 1299, he sold Stargard to his son-in-law Henry II of Mecklenburg, who held it as a Brandenburg fief under the 1304 Treaty of Vietmannsdorf. In 1299 he founded the Coeli Porta monastery at Lychen. After his death in 1300 he was buried at Lehnin Abbey.

阿尔布雷希特三世（约1250—1300）是阿斯坎尼家族勃兰登堡-萨尔茨韦德尔支系的边境侯爵，为奥托三世侯爵与波希米亚的贝阿特丽切之子。他仅为共治者，实权掌握在堂兄“持箭者”奥托四世手中，管理施塔加德领地，1284年起成为施塔加德和利兴的领主。

诸子约于1299年死后，他把施塔加德卖给女婿梅克伦堡的海因里希二世；1304年的《菲特曼斯多夫条约》确认海因里希以勃兰登堡采邑的形式持有该地。1299年他在利兴创立“天门”修道院。1300年死后葬于莱宁修道院。

Anna of Austria (1275/1280–1327) was born in Vienna, a daughter of Albert I of Germany and Elisabeth of Tirol. In 1295 she married Herman, Margrave of Brandenburg-Salzwedel, and bore him four children, including his heir John.

Herman died in 1308 and their son succeeded him; when John died in 1317, the Brandenburg-Salzwedel line of the Ascanians became extinct. In 1310 Anna married Henry VI the Good, Duke of Wrocław. She died at Legnica in 1327.

en:
Frederick I (1371–1440) was a Hohenzollern prince who ruled Nuremberg as Burgrave Frederick VI. A trusted servant of King Sigismund, he fought at Nicopolis in 1396 and represented him in the disputed 1410 imperial election. In 1411 Sigismund made him administrator of Brandenburg, where he crushed the rebellious nobility. At the Council of Constance in 1415 Sigismund made him Margrave and Elector of Brandenburg, with formal enfeoffment in 1417, founding Hohenzollern rule there.

Frederick withdrew to Cadolzburg in 1425 and transferred the regency of Brandenburg to his son John in 1426, remaining elector until his death in 1440.

腓特烈一世（1371—1440）是霍亨索伦家族王公，在纽伦堡称伯爵腓特烈六世。他深受国王西吉斯蒙德信任，1396年参加尼科波利斯之战，1410年在有争议的帝国选举中代表西吉斯蒙德投票。1411年西吉斯蒙德任命他为勃兰登堡摄政，他镇压了叛乱贵族。1415年西吉斯蒙德在康斯坦茨会议上封他为勃兰登堡藩侯兼选帝侯，1417年正式授封，开创霍亨索伦家族在勃兰登堡的统治。

1425年腓特烈退居卡多尔茨堡，1426年将勃兰登堡摄政权交给儿子约翰，仍保有选帝侯之位，直至1440年去世。

Henry I, called Lackland (1256–1318), was an Ascanian margrave of Brandenburg-Stendal, a younger son of Margrave John I. Long excluded from government by his older brothers, he only received Delitzsch as his seat in 1294.

He lost the County Palatine of Saxony to Duke Rudolf I in 1311. His nephew Waldemar proposed him as King of the Romans, but Henry declined and in 1314 voted for Louis IV of Bavaria. By Agnes of Bavaria he fathered Henry II, Brandenburg's last Ascanian margrave.

亨利一世，绰号“无地者”（1256—1318），阿斯坎尼家族的勃兰登堡-施滕达尔边境侯爵，是约翰一世侯爵的幼子。他长期被兄长们排除在统治之外，直到1294年才得到德利奇作为自己的驻地。

en:
Henry II, called the Child (c. 1308 – July 1320), was Brandenburg's last Ascanian margrave, the son of Margrave Henry I Lackland and Agnes of Bavaria. In 1319, aged eleven, he succeeded his childless cousin Waldemar.

Duke Wartislaw IV of Pomerania seized the regency until King Louis IV declared Henry of age without enfeoffing him. He died in July 1320 before ruling in person, ending Ascanian rule; in 1323 Louis IV enfeoffed his son Louis V with Brandenburg.

Herman, called the Tall (the Long) (c. 1275 – 1 February 1308), was an Ascanian margrave of Brandenburg-Salzwedel, son of Margrave Otto V. From 1299 he ruled Brandenburg jointly with his cousin Otto IV.

In 1308 Brandenburg fought Mecklenburg in the North German Margrave War; Herman died on 1 February while besieging Lübz. Buried at Lehnin Abbey, he left by his wife Anne of Austria, daughter of King Albert I, a son and successor, John V.

en:
Alexander von Humboldt (1769–1859), younger brother of Wilhelm, was a Prussian polymath and naturalist, regarded with Carl Ritter as a founder of modern geography. As a boy he collected and labelled plants, shells and insects, earning the nickname the little apothecary, and he trained as a scientific explorer at Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen and Freiberg.

In Paris he met the botanist Aimé Bonpland, and from 1799 to 1804 the two travelled across the Spanish Americas with the permission of the Spanish crown. They covered thousands of miles, tracing the source of the Orinoco, and in 1802 Humboldt climbed Mount Chimborazo to a record altitude for a Westerner.

His quantitative work on plant distribution by altitude and climate founded biogeography, and he described human-caused climate change as early as 1800. His multi-volume Kosmos presented nature as one interacting whole. He died in Berlin in 1859 and was buried at Tegel.

亚历山大·冯·洪堡（1769—1859）是普鲁士博学家、博物学家，威廉·冯·洪堡之弟，与卡尔·李特尔同为现代地理学奠基人。他少年时收集并标注植物、贝壳和昆虫，得了“小药剂师”的绰号，后在奥得河畔法兰克福、哥廷根和弗莱贝格求学。

他在巴黎结识植物学家埃梅·邦普兰，1799至1804年两人经西班牙王室许可游历西属美洲，行程数千英里，探查到奥里诺科河源头；1802年他登上钦博拉索山，创下当时西方人登山高度的最高纪录。

他对植物随海拔气候分布的定量研究奠定生物地理学基础，早在1800年便论述人类活动造成的气候变化；多卷本《宇宙》将自然界描绘为相互联系的整体。1859年在柏林去世，葬于泰格尔。

en:
John I (c. 1213–1266) was the elder son of Margrave Albert II and ruled Brandenburg jointly with his brother Otto III from 1220, in person after 1225. Their reign enlarged the margraviate with the Uckermark, Stargard, the Lubusz Land and the first Neumark lands beyond the Oder, and they promoted Cölln and Berlin.

In 1230 he married Sophie, daughter of King Valdemar II of Denmark, and between 1261 and 1264 held King Eric V of Denmark prisoner. In 1266 the brothers founded Chorin Abbey.

John II (1237–1281) was the eldest son of Margrave John I and Sophie of Denmark, and from 1266 co-ruler of the Brandenburg-Stendal line alongside his brothers Otto IV and Conrad I, politically overshadowed by Otto IV. In 1269 he co-signed the Treaty of Arnswalde with Duke Mestwin II of Pomerelia.

His record centres on Chorin Abbey, the Cistercian house founded by his father: in 1273 the three brothers confirmed moving it from Mariensee to Chorin, where John was buried on his death in 1281.

John V, called Illustris (1302 – 26 March 1317), was an Ascanian margrave of Brandenburg-Salzwedel, the son of Margrave Herman the Tall and Anne of Austria. Six years old when his father died besieging Lübz in 1308, he succeeded him as margrave and co-ruler of Brandenburg.

He married Catherine, daughter of Duke Henry III of Glogau, but died on 26 March 1317 as a teenager. With his early death the Brandenburg-Salzwedel Ascanian line became extinct, and his cousin Waldemar ruled the margraviate alone.

en:
Louis V, called the Brandenburger (1315–1361), was the eldest son of Emperor Louis IV, who set him over Brandenburg as a boy. In 1323 the eight-year-old was enfeoffed with the march, ending the Brandenburg Interregnum. Defeat at Kremmer Damm in 1332 forced him to give up Pomerania.

In 1342 he married the Tyrolean heiress Margaret before her first marriage was dissolved, winning Tyrol but drawing excommunication. In 1347, while he was away in Prussia, Margaret beat back Charles IV's attack on Schloss Tirol, and that year he inherited Upper Bavaria.

In 1351, at odds with Brandenburg's nobles, he ceded the march to his half-brothers by the Treaty of Luckau. The Golden Bull of 1356 gave his Bavarian line no electoral vote. He died at Zorneding in 1361.

路德维希五世绰号“勃兰登堡人”（1315—1361），是皇帝路德维希四世的长子，少年时就被父亲派去治理勃兰登堡。1323年，年仅八岁的他受封勃兰登堡藩侯领地，结束了勃兰登堡空位期。1332年克雷门堤战败，他被迫放弃对波美拉尼亚的主张。

1342年，他在蒂罗尔女继承人玛格丽特的第一段婚姻尚未解除时便与她成婚，因而取得蒂罗尔，却被开除教籍。1347年他远赴普鲁士时，玛格丽特击退了查理四世对蒂罗尔城堡的进攻；同年他继承上巴伐利亚。

1351年，他与勃兰登堡贵族不睦，依《卢考条约》把勃兰登堡让给异母弟弟。1356年的金玺诏书没有把选侯资格授予他的巴伐利亚支系。1361年他卒于措内丁。

en:
Margaret of Denmark (c. 1305–1340) was the eldest daughter of King Christopher II of Denmark and Euphemia of Pomerania. To ally with the German king Louis IV, Christopher married her in December 1324 to his son Louis V, whom Louis IV had enfeoffed with Brandenburg, promising a dowry of 12000 silver marks.

The dowry was never paid, and the claim was eventually settled when her brother King Valdemar IV offered Danish Estonia to Brandenburg instead. Margaret died in 1340.

丹麦的玛格丽特（约1305—1340）是丹麦国王克里斯托弗二世与波美拉尼亚的欧菲米娅的长女。为与德意志国王路德维希四世结盟，克里斯托弗于1324年12月将她嫁给已受封勃兰登堡藩侯国的路德维希五世，许以12000马克白银的嫁妆。

这笔嫁妆始终没有支付，最终由她的弟弟瓦尔德马四世国王以把丹麦属爱沙尼亚让予勃兰登堡的方式了结。玛格丽特于1340年去世。

en:
Otto I (c. 1128–1184) was the second Margrave of Brandenburg, ruling from 1170 as the eldest son of Albert the Bear, who had founded the margraviate in 1157. Already active in his father's government by 1144, after 1157 the two shaped Ascanian policy together.

Around 1148 he married Judith, daughter of Polish duke Bolesław III. As margrave he focused on settling and securing the territory rather than expanding it, and was buried at Lehnin Abbey.

奥托一世（约1128—1184）是阿斯坎尼王朝第二代勃兰登堡藩侯，1170年继位。他是1157年建立勃兰登堡藩侯国的“大熊”阿尔布雷希特一世的长子，早在1144年便已参与父亲领地的事务，1157年后父子二人共同奠定了阿斯坎尼家族的治国方针。

约1148年，他娶波兰公爵波列斯瓦夫三世之女朱迪斯为妻。在位期间他注重移民垦殖、稳固领地，而非对外扩张，死后葬于莱宁修道院。

en:
Otto II (after 1147–1205), called the Generous, was the third Margrave of Brandenburg, succeeding his father Otto I in 1184. He strengthened its settlement and defences and campaigned against the Slavs and King Canute VI of Denmark, ravaging Danish-held Pomerania in the winter of 1198–1199.

From 1200 he backed the Hohenstaufen Philip of Swabia against Otto IV. His marriage to his stepmother Ada of Holland was childless, so his half-brother Albert II succeeded him in 1205.

奥托二世（1147年后—1205），绰号“慷慨者”，1184年继承父亲奥托一世之位，为阿斯坎尼王朝第三代勃兰登堡藩侯。他加强了藩侯国的防务与垦殖，并对斯拉夫人和丹麦克努特六世作战；1198至1199年冬天，他蹂躏了丹麦占据的波美拉尼亚。

1200年起，他支持霍亨斯陶芬王朝士瓦本的菲利普对抗奥托四世。他娶继母荷兰的爱达为妻却无子嗣，1205年死后由异母弟阿尔布雷希特二世继位。

en:
Otto III the Pious (1215–1267), younger son of Margrave Albert II, ruled Brandenburg jointly with his elder brother John I from 1225 until John died in 1266, and then alone for a year. Together they won the Uckermark and carried Ascanian rule beyond the Oder into the Neumark.

In 1255 he joined King Ottokar II of Bohemia on the Prussian Crusade and helped found Königsberg, and in 1256 he was a candidate for King of the Romans.

en:
Otto IV (c. 1238–1308), called Otto with the Arrow, was the foremost of the three sons of John I ruling Brandenburg-Stendal jointly from 1266. The 1269 Treaty of Arnswalde made Duke Mestwin of Pomerelia their vassal.

Feuding with Magdeburg, he was captured and caged at the Battle of Fohse and freed for four thousand pounds of silver; an arrow wound at Staßfurt in 1280 gave him his nickname. As elector he backed Adolf of Nassau in 1292.

en:
Otto V the Tall (c. 1246–1298) was a son of Otto III the Pious, and from 1267 margrave of the Brandenburg-Salzwedel line, ruling jointly with his cousin Otto IV. He spent years at the Prague court of his uncle Ottokar II, and after the king fell at the Marchfeld in 1278 he became regent for the seven-year-old Wenceslaus II.

He outmaneuvered the Bohemian nobles and made Wenceslaus renounce Upper Lusatia. He married Judith of Henneberg, and his son Herman succeeded him in 1298.

en:
Waldemar the Great (c. 1280 – 14 August 1319), son of Margrave Conrad, was Brandenburg's last effective Ascanian margrave, ruling from 1308 and alone from 1317. By the 1309 Treaty of Soldin he sold his Pomerelian claims to the Teutonic Order, and in 1312 he captured Frederick I of Meissen, gaining Lusatia.

After defeat in 1316 he ceded Stargard to Mecklenburg by the 1317 Treaty of Templin. His marriage to Agnes was childless, and his ward Henry II died in 1320, ending Ascanian rule.

瓦尔德马大帝（约1280—1319年8月14日）是康拉德侯爵之子，勃兰登堡最后一位真正掌权的阿斯坎尼家族边境侯爵，1308年起执政，1317年起独掌大权。根据1309年的《索尔丁条约》，他把对波美雷利亚的权利卖给条顿骑士团；1312年俘获迈森侯爵腓特烈一世，取得卢萨蒂亚。

Samuel von Cocceji (1679–1755) was a Prussian jurist born in Heidelberg. He took his doctorate in 1699, became a law professor at Frankfurt an der Oder in 1702, and by 1731 was president of Prussia's highest court of appeal in Berlin.

As Grand Chancellor from 1747 under Frederick II, he reorganised justice first in Silesia and then across all Prussia, clearing court backlogs, requiring trained judges, and issuing the Codex Fridericianus Pomeranicus in 1747 and the Codex Fridericianus Marchicus in 1748.

Georg Wenzeslaus von Knobelsdorff (1699–1753) was a Prussian officer turned architect and the favourite builder of Frederick the Great. He left the army as a captain in 1729, trained as a painter, and from 1732 advised Crown Prince Frederick on art and architecture, enlarging Rheinsberg Palace and helping to shape the Frederician Rococo style.

In 1740, after Frederick took the Prussian throne, he travelled to Paris and Italy to study architecture. He designed the Berlin Opera House and the palace of Sanssouci at Potsdam, begun in 1745. Dismissed in 1746, he died in Berlin in 1753.

en:
Carl von Clausewitz (1780–1831) was a Prussian officer and military theorist, author of the unfinished treatise On War. Born near Magdeburg, he joined the army at twelve and entered the Berlin War Academy in 1801. Captured at Jena-Auerstedt in 1806 and held until 1808, he returned to help Scharnhorst reform the army.

Unwilling to support Napoleon's war on Russia, in 1812 he entered Russian service, fought at Borodino and helped arrange the Convention of Tauroggen; branded a deserter, he was taken back only in 1814. In 1815 his outnumbered corps delayed Waterloo-bound reinforcements at Wavre.

From 1818 he directed the Berlin War Academy, though he was not allowed to teach. In 1831, when Gneisenau died of cholera on the Polish border, he took over and died of the same disease. His widow Marie published it from 1832; its best-known line calls war the continuation of policy by other means.

卡尔·冯·克劳塞维茨（1780—1831）是普鲁士军官、军事理论家，未完成的《战争论》的作者。生于马格德堡附近，十二岁入伍，1801年进入柏林军官学校。1806年在耶拿-奥尔施泰特战役被俘，被关至1808年，回国后协助沙恩霍斯特改革军队。

他不愿支持拿破仑攻俄，1812年转入俄军，参加鲍罗金诺战役并促成《陶罗根协定》；国王斥他为逃兵，直到1814年才许他回国。1815年在瓦夫尔，所部以少敌多，拖住开往滑铁卢的援军。

1818年起他主持柏林军官学校，却不许授课。1831年在波兰边境，格奈泽瑙染霍乱死后他接掌军队，亦死于霍乱。遗孀玛丽自1832年起出版《战争论》，书中名言称战争是政治以其他手段的延续。

Adelaide of Burgundy (c. 1233 – 23 October 1273), daughter of Hugh IV of Burgundy, married Henry III, Duke of Brabant, in 1251. After his death in 1261 she ruled as regent for their young son Henry, despite opposition from a cousin of her husband.

In 1262 she founded Val-Duchesse, the Low Countries' first Dominican priory for women. When her eldest son proved unfit to rule, she replaced him in 1267 with her second son John, handing over power in 1268. She died in 1273.

Godfrey of Brabant was the youngest son of John III, Duke of Brabant, and Marie of Évreux. In 1346 his father made him Lord of Aarschot, and in 1347 he was betrothed at Paris to a daughter of Peter I, Duke of Bourbon.

The match never became a marriage: he died young soon after 1352 and was buried at Tervuren. As his brothers John and Henry had already died, the ducal throne passed in 1355 to his elder sister Joan.

Henry I, called the Courageous (c. 1165–1235), son of Count Godfrey III of Leuven, became the first Duke of Brabant in 1183, a rank confirmed by King Henry VI in 1190. He joined the emperor's crusade in 1197, helping to retake Beirut and serving as regent in Acre.

In the German throne quarrel he switched sides between Otto IV and Philip of Swabia, fighting at Bouvines in 1214. He took part in the Fifth Crusade in 1217–1218. He died at Cologne in 1235 escorting Isabella of England to Emperor Frederick II.

Henry II of Brabant (1207–1248), called the Magnanimous, succeeded Henry I as duke in 1235. He intervened in disputes between the bishop of Liège and his towns and gained the County of Dalhem in 1244 through his alliance with Emperor Frederick II.

In 1247 he refused the German kingship in favour of his nephew William II of Holland. His son by Sophie of Thuringia, Henry the Child, founded the House of Hesse. In January 1248 he granted Brabant its first land charter to ease the succession of his young son Henry III, and died weeks later at Leuven.

en:
Henry III of Brabant (c. 1231–1261) succeeded his father Henry II as duke in 1248, and in 1251 married Adelaide of Burgundy. He backed Alfonso X of Castile for the German crown, who named him imperial vicar in 1257 and granted him disputed Lothier.

Himself a trouvère, he kept the poet Adenet le Roi at court. He died at Leuven in 1261, after issuing a charter to ease his under-age sons' succession; his will threatened to banish Jews who kept moneylending, but Adelaide did not enforce it as regent. His children included John I and Maria, wife of Philip III of France.

zh:
亨利三世（约1231—1261）于1248年继父亲亨利二世成为布拉班特公爵，1251年迎娶勃艮第的阿德莱德。他支持卡斯蒂利亚的阿方索十世竞选德意志国王，阿方索于1257年任命他为帝国代理官，并把有争议的洛捷领地封给他。

他本人是游吟诗人，在宫中供养诗人阿德内·勒鲁瓦。1261年他卒于鲁汶，死前颁下特权状，为年幼诸子的继位铺平道路。他的遗嘱威胁驱逐坚持放贷收息的犹太人，但阿德莱德摄政时并未执行。子女包括约翰一世，以及嫁给腓力三世的玛丽亚。

en:
Henry IV of Brabant (1251/1252 – after 1272) became duke in 1261 as the eldest son of Henry III and Adelaide of Burgundy, succeeding at about the age of ten. He was judged infirm, and in 1267 he was deposed in favour of his younger brother John I.

He then became a novice at Saint Bénigne Abbey. Nothing certain is recorded after April 1272, and the date of death is unknown.

en:
Jacques de Châtillon (15 May 1256–11 July 1302), lord of Leuze and Condé, was a son of Guy III, Count of Saint-Pol, and Matilda of Brabant. After imprisoning Count Guy of Dampierre, Philip IV of France made him governor of Flanders in 1300 to press the French annexation.

Heavy taxes and extortion by pro-French nobles angered the townspeople. On 18 May 1302 they massacred the French garrison in the Bruges Matins, part of the Flemish uprising. Jacques escaped, but was killed less than two months later at the Battle of the Golden Spurs.

沙蒂永的雅克（1256年5月15日—1302年7月11日）是勒兹和孔代的领主，圣波勒伯爵居伊三世与布拉班特的玛蒂尔德之子。法王腓力四世囚禁佛兰德伯爵当皮埃尔的居伊后，于1300年任命他为佛兰德总督，以推进兼并。

重税和亲法贵族的勒索激怒了当地市民。1302年5月18日，市民在“布鲁日晨祷”中屠杀法国驻军，这是佛兰德起事的一部分。雅克逃出布鲁日，但不到两个月便在金马刺战役中被杀。
