en:
John I, called the Victorious (1252/1253–1294), became Duke of Brabant in 1267 after his infirm brother Henry IV was set aside. His first wife, a daughter of Louis IX, died young with their infant son; in 1273 he married Margaret of Flanders, mother of his successor John II.

In the War of the Limburg Succession he defeated Rainald I of Guelders and the archbishop of Cologne at Worringen in 1288, winning Limburg for Brabant. A famed patron of poets, he was mortally wounded in May 1294 in a melee at the wedding feasts of Bar-le-Duc.

en:
Jan II Berthout van Berlaer (1280–1328) was a Brabantine nobleman of a wealthy Mechelen family and lord of Helmond from 1314 until his death. On 13 July 1314 he received Helmond in fief from the fourteen-year-old Duke John III of Brabant.

He also held Berlaar, near Lier. His son by Elisabeth van den Berghe, Lodewijk III, succeeded him when he died in 1328, and he was buried at Binderen Abbey.

en:
John II, called the Peaceful (1275–1312), succeeded John I as Duke of Brabant in 1294. He put down early revolts and, with Edward I of England and the Count of Flanders, formed an anti-French league that broke up in 1300. In 1309 his army crushed the Crusade of the Poor, which had besieged Genappe castle where Jews sheltered.

Suffering from kidney stones and seeking a peaceful succession for his son, he granted the Charter of Kortenberg, Brabant's constitution, on his deathbed in 1312. Married to Margaret of England in 1290, he died at Tervuren, leaving the duchy to John III.

en:
John III (1300–1355) was Duke of Brabant and Limburg from 1312, the last man of his line to rule them. He inherited heavy debts: the towns would pay them only if he honoured the Charter of Kortenberg and granted new privileges. He married Marie of Évreux in 1311.

As Brabant's trade clashed with France's wish to isolate Flanders, he backed Edward III at the start of the Hundred Years' War. Philip VI answered by seizing Brabantine goods in France; Brussels rose against its duke, and John put the revolt down and had a ringleader beheaded.

From 1340 he turned to France, marrying his daughters to the rulers of Luxembourg, Flanders and Guelders. All three sons died before him, so he named his daughter Joanna heiress. His death in 1355 brought a succession crisis.

zh:
让三世（1300—1355）自1312年起担任布拉班特与林堡公爵，是这个家系最后一位统治这两块领地的男性。他继承的是一个负债的公国：各城市答应偿还公爵的债务，条件是他遵守《科滕贝格宪章》并给予新的特权。1311年他迎娶埃夫勒的玛丽。

布拉班特的商业利益与法国孤立佛兰德的企图相冲突，百年战争初期他站到英格兰国王爱德华三世一边。腓力六世以扣押布拉班特人在法国的财产作为报复，布鲁塞尔市民起而反抗；让三世平息了暴动，并砍下一名领袖的头。

en:
Joan of Argies (1290–1334) was a French noblewoman, daughter of the lord of Dargies in Picardy. Her first husband was Hugh of Soissons, by whom she had a daughter Margaret. She then married John of Charolais, son of Robert of Clermont; their daughters were Beatrice, lady of Charolais, and Joan, lady of Saint-Just.

Widowed in 1316, she later took a third husband, Hugh of Châtillon, by whom she had a daughter Joan. She died in 1334.

en:
Joanna of Brabant (1322–1406), daughter of Duke John III of Brabant, inherited the duchy in 1355 and faced invasion within a year. In 1334 she married William II of Hainaut, who was killed fighting the Frisians in 1345. Her second husband was Wenceslaus of Luxembourg.

In January 1356 she granted the Joyous Entry charter, limiting ducal power and settling the succession on her sisters. That year Louis II of Flanders, claiming Brabant through his wife Margaret, overran the duchy and forced the humiliating Treaty of Ath, which ceded Mechelen and Antwerp.

Emperor Charles IV later had parts of the charter annulled to satisfy the Luxembourgs, and in 1371 Wenceslaus was captured at Baesweiler. On Joanna's death in 1406 Brabant passed to her great-nephew Anthony of Burgundy.

布拉班特的让娜（1322—1406）是布拉班特公爵让三世之女，1355年继承公国，一年之内就遭到入侵。1334年她嫁给埃诺的威廉二世，威廉于1345年在与弗里斯兰人作战时阵亡。她的第二任丈夫是卢森堡的文策尔。

1356年1月，她颁布《欢乐入口》宪章，限制公爵权力，并确定由她的姐妹继承公国。同年，佛兰德伯爵路易二世以妻子玛格丽特的名义主张布拉班特，侵占公国，迫使她签下屈辱的《阿特条约》，割让梅赫伦和安特卫普。

皇帝查理四世后来废除了宪章的部分条款以满足卢森堡家族，1371年文策尔在巴斯韦勒战败被俘。1406年让娜去世后，布拉班特传给她的甥外孙勃艮第的安托万。

en:
Lodewijk III Berthout van Berlaer (1310–1346) was a Brabantine nobleman, the son of Jan II Berthout van Berlaer and Elisabeth van den Berghe. He succeeded his father as lord of Helmond in 1328 and ruled until his death, having married Johanna van Dinther, who bore him his heir Walraven.

He was probably the founder of Helmond Castle, and raised a loan on the security of the castle to pay for its building. He died in 1346 and was buried at Roosendaal.

Margaret of England (1275 – after 1333) was a daughter of King Edward I and Eleanor of Castile, born at Windsor Castle. In 1290 she married John II, Duke of Brabant, becoming duchess consort of Brabant; their only son was the future John III.

Her husband issued the Charter of Kortenberg in 1312 and died later that year, but Margaret was excluded from the regency for the minor John III, which was led by Louis of Évreux. She died in Brabant.

Mary of Brabant (1325–1399) was the third daughter of Duke John III of Brabant and Mary of Évreux. In 1347 she married Reginald III the Fat, Duke of Guelders. When her brother-in-law Edward seized Guelders and imprisoned Reginald in 1361, she settled at her dower castle of Turnhout; Reginald was freed in 1371 but died soon afterwards.

Mary founded Corsendonk Priory in 1395. Her claims to Brabant were settled by the Peace of Ath, and she died at Turnhout in 1399.

en:
Marie of Évreux (1303–1335) was the eldest child of Louis of Évreux and Margaret of Artois, and sister of Philip III of Navarre and Jeanne d'Évreux, queen of France. In 1311 she married John III, Duke of Brabant, sealing Brabant's rapprochement with the French crown.

She was the mother of Joanna of Brabant and of Margaret, who married Louis II of Flanders, along with three sons who all died before their father. Marie died on 31 October 1335, aged about thirty-two.

Walraven Berthout van Berlaer (1330–1361) was lord of Helmond and Keerbergen in the Duchy of Brabant, the son of Lodewijk III Berthout van Berlaer and Johanna van Dinther. He succeeded his father in 1346, and around 1348 married Elisabeth van Utenhove, through whom he gained the lordship of Herlaar at Herenthout.

Their son Jan was born in 1350 and succeeded him as Jan III in 1361. Walraven died at Helmond in 1361.

en:
Henry IV (d. 1351) was provost of the Augustinian foundation of Berchtesgaden from 1333 until his death. He drew the provostry closer to the Habsburgs and enjoyed free production and export of Schellenberg salt through the territory of the Archbishopric of Salzburg.

In his last months he contested the advocacies of Jettenstetten and Weidenbach, a suit referred by Pope Clement VI to the Abbot of Tegernsee in October 1350. Henry died before 1 April 1351, before judgement gave the advocacies to his church.

Andrea di Gualtieri de' Bardi (c. 1300–1368) was a Florentine merchant, knight and statesman of the Bardi banking family. He fought against John of Bohemia and the Scaligeri and held offices in Florentine service.

In 1332 he bought the county of Mangona, which Florence forced him to surrender in 1341 after the magnate conspiracy led by his brother Pietro failed. He helped Walter of Brienne seize power in 1342 and helped expel him in 1343, and later served as ambassador to Avignon.

Piero di Gualtieri de' Bardi (c. 1290–1345) was a Florentine knight, magnate and partner in the Bardi banking company. He bought the county of Vernio in 1332.

He led the magnate conspiracy against Florence's popular government, uncovered in 1340; denounced by his brother Andrea, he was exiled and condemned to death, and the Republic bought Vernio in 1341. Restored under Walter of Brienne in 1342, he helped expel the Duke in 1343, then fled to Vernio, where he died suddenly in 1345.

en:
Burchard Grelle (c. 1260–1344) was Archbishop of Bremen from 1327 until his death. Born into a Bremen citizen family, he studied at the University of Paris and represented the archdiocese at the papal court before Pope John XXII appointed him to Bremen in 1327 after the death of Archbishop Jens Grand.

One of only two commoners ever to hold the see, Grelle maintained unusually good relations between the city and the archbishopric, and politically aligned himself with the Curia against Emperor Louis IV.

en:
Henry of Berg, called Heinrich von Windeck (before 1247 – probably 1298), was a younger son of Count Adolf VII of Berg. From 1271 to 1281 he served his brother Count Adolf VIII as stadholder, later holding Windeck Castle.

He backed John I of Brabant in the War of the Limburg Succession and fought at the Battle of Worringen in 1288. By his wife Agnes of the Mark he fathered Count Adolf IX of Berg and Margaret; he is buried at Altenberg Cathedral.

en:
Alix of Thouars (1200–1221) became duchess of Brittany as an infant in 1203, after her captive half-brother Arthur disappeared in John of England's prisons and Breton barons set aside her half-sister Eleanor's claim. Her father Guy of Thouars ruled as regent until 1206, when Philip II of France took over and in 1213 married her to his cousin Peter of Dreux, called Mauclerc.

Peter governed the duchy in her name. Alix died in 1221, leaving the duchy to her infant son John I.

图阿尔的阿丽丝（1200—1221）于1203年在襁褓中成为布列塔尼女公爵：此前她被囚禁的同母异父兄长阿蒂尔一世在英格兰国王约翰的牢中失踪，布列塔尼贵族便排除了其姐埃莉诺的继承权。其父图阿尔的居伊先任摄政，1206年法王腓力二世接管摄政权，并于1213年将她嫁给皮埃尔·德勒（人称‘莫克莱尔’）。

en:
Arthur II (1261–1312) was Duke of Brittany from 1305, eldest son of John II and Beatrice of England. In 1275 he married Marie, who bore his heir John III; after her death he married Yolande of Dreux in 1292, and this marriage produced John of Montfort, future claimant to the duchy.

Arthur kept Brittany independent of the French crown, divided it into eight military districts, and in 1309 summoned the first Estates of Brittany, the first French assembly including the third estate. He died on 27 August 1312 and was buried in the Cordeliers convent at Vannes.

阿蒂尔二世（1261—1312）于1305年起任布列塔尼公爵，是约翰二世与英格兰的贝阿特丽丝的长子。1275年他娶玛丽为妻，生下继承人约翰三世；玛丽去世后，他于1292年再娶德勒的约朗德，生下日后争夺公国继承权的蒙福尔的让。

Béatrix of Brittany (1295–1384), Lady of Laval, Vitré and Hédé, was a daughter of Arthur II, Duke of Brittany, and Yolande of Dreux. In 1315 she married Guy X de Laval; their three children included Guy XII de Laval and Catherine.

Her husband was killed and her son captured at the battle of La Roche-Derrien in 1347, and Béatrix raised the large ransom that freed him. She died in 1384 and was buried in Clermont Abbey.

Blanche of Navarre, also called Blanche of Champagne (1226–1283), was the daughter of Theobald I, King of Navarre and Count of Champagne. In 1236 she married John I, Duke of Brittany, a match that briefly made John heir to the throne of Navarre.

She bore eight children, of whom only John II, Peter and Alix reached adulthood. In 1270 she founded the Abbey of La Joie near Hennebont, where she was buried after her death in 1283.

Catherine de Laval (c. 1329 – before 1378) was the daughter of Guy X de Laval and Beatrice of Brittany, herself a daughter of Duke Arthur II. About 1370 she married the Breton captain Olivier V de Clisson, a match that made him cousin to both claimants to Brittany.

She bore two daughters, Marguerite and Béatrix, who married into the houses of Châtillon and Rohan. While her husband campaigned, she ran his estates from Josselin Castle.

en:
Charles of Blois-Châtillon (1319–1364), called the Saint, was nephew of King Philip VI of France. In 1337 he married Joan of Penthièvre, heiress of John III of Brittany, and on the duke's death in 1341 claimed the duchy, fighting John of Montfort with French backing in the Breton War of Succession.

A devout ascetic who is said to have put pebbles in his shoes and worn a hairshirt under his armour, he still ordered the massacre of 1,400 civilians after Quimper. Captured by the English in 1347, he spent nine years in captivity and was released in 1356 for a ransom of about half a million écus.

He resumed the war and was killed at Auray on 29 September 1364, a defeat that ended the war for the Montforts. He was beatified in 1904.

夏尔·德·布卢瓦-沙蒂永（1319—1364），人称“圣人”，是法王腓力六世的外甥。1337年，他迎娶布列塔尼公爵约翰三世的继承人让娜·德·庞蒂耶夫尔，1341年约翰三世去世后主张公国继承权，在法国王室支持下与让·德·蒙福尔展开布列塔尼继承战争。

他虔诚苦修，相传在鞋里放小石子，铠甲下穿苦衣，却仍在坎佩尔一役后下令屠杀1,400名平民。1347年他被英军俘虏，囚禁九年，1356年交付约五十万埃居赎金获释。

他重启战事，1364年9月29日在欧赖战死，这场失败使战争以蒙福尔家获胜告终。他于1904年被宣福。

en:
Guy of Thouars (died 13 April 1213) was a noble of the House of Thouars and the third husband of Constance, Duchess of Brittany, whom he married in 1199. He ruled as duke until Constance died giving birth to twin daughters in 1201. After her son Arthur I disappeared in English captivity in 1203, Guy served as regent for his own daughter Alix until 1206.

In 1204 he besieged and burned Mont Saint-Michel. In 1206 Philip II of France took the regency himself. Guy died at Chemillé in 1213 and was buried beside Constance at Villeneuve Abbey.

en:
Guy de Bretagne, also Guy VII of Limoges (1287–1331), was the second son of Duke Arthur II of Brittany and Marie of Limoges. In 1314 his brother John III invested him with the viscounty of Limoges, but in 1317 the duke's wife Isabella recovered it, and Guy was compensated with the county of Penthièvre.

In 1318 he married Jeanne d'Avaugour; their daughter Jeanne de Penthièvre inherited his claims. He died suddenly on 27 March 1331 and was buried at Guingamp.

Guy X de Laval (c. 1300–1347) was a Breton baron, lord of Laval and Vitré. In 1315 he married Béatrix of Brittany, daughter of Duke Arthur II, which made Duke John III his brother-in-law. Their children included Guy XI, Jean, later Guy XII, and Catherine, who in 1361 married the constable Olivier de Clisson.

On 18 June 1347 he fought at La Roche-Derrien in the Breton War of Succession, the battle in which Charles of Blois was taken prisoner. Guy X was killed there, and his son Guy XI, fighting beside him, was captured.

en:
Guy XI de Laval (c. 1316–1348), eldest son of Guy X and Béatrix of Brittany, held his inheritance for little more than a year. In 1338 his father married him to Isabeau, heiress of Craon.

On 18 June 1347 he fought beside his father at La Roche-Derrien, where Guy X was killed and Charles of Blois was taken; Guy XI was captured by the English as well, and his mother arranged the ransom.

He died at the Château de Vitré on 22 September 1348, never having recovered from his wounds, and was buried beside his father. He left no children, and his brother succeeded him as Guy XII.

en:
Guy XII de Laval (c. 1327–1412), second son of Guy X and Béatrix of Brittany, was baptised Jean and took the name Guy only in 1348, when he succeeded his brother Guy XI as lord of Laval and Vitré. He stood close to Bertrand du Guesclin and to Olivier de Clisson, his brother-in-law from 1361.

After Auray in 1364, du Guesclin was captured and his ransom set at 100,000 livres; Charles V raised 40,000 and Guy paid the rest. In 1370 he was among the commanders who beat Robert Knolles' English at Pontvallain.

He helped broker the second Treaty of Guérande in 1381. In 1384 he married du Guesclin's widow, Jeanne de Laval; their daughter Anne inherited Laval and Vitré when he died in 1412.

Joan of Penthièvre (c. 1319–1384), called Joan the Lame, was the only child of Guy of Penthièvre, younger brother of John III of Brittany. In 1337 she married Charles of Blois, and on her uncle's death in 1341 the couple claimed Brittany, fighting the House of Montfort in the Breton War of Succession.

After Charles was killed at Auray in 1364, the Treaty of Guérande in 1365 left her Countess of Penthièvre with a life right to the ducal title.

Joan of Savoy (c. 1310–1344) was the only child of Edward, Count of Savoy, and Blanche of Burgundy. In 1329 she married John III, Duke of Brittany. When her father died the same year, she claimed Savoy, but her uncle Aymon, backed by the nobility under semi-Salic law, succeeded instead.

She pressed her claim until 1339, when she renounced it for a pension of 6000 livres. Her childless marriage left the Breton succession disputed when John III died in 1341, and she died in 1344.

en:
Peter I of Brittany, called Peter Mauclerc (c. 1187–1250), was a younger son of Robert II of Dreux. In 1213 Philip II of France chose him as betrothed of Alix of Thouars, and Peter married the Duchess of Brittany in 1214. He ruled at her side and then served as regent for his son John I until 1237, and as Earl of Richmond from 1218 he led the barons opposing Blanche of Castile before submitting in 1234.

He joined the Barons' Crusade in 1239 and Louis IX's Seventh Crusade in 1249. Wounded and captured at Mansourah in 1250, he died at sea returning home and was buried at Braine.

布列塔尼的皮埃尔一世，绰号“恶教士”莫克莱尔（约1187—1250），是德勒的罗贝尔二世的幼子之一。1213年，法王腓力二世选他与阿丽丝·德·图阿尔订婚，他于1214年迎娶这位布列塔尼女公爵。他先与妻子共同治国，之后为儿子约翰一世摄政至1237年；自1218年成为里士满伯爵后，他曾领导贵族对抗卡斯蒂利亚的布兰卡，1234年归顺朝廷。

他参加了1239年的男爵十字军和1249年路易九世发起的第七次十字军。1250年他在曼苏拉受伤被俘，于归国途中死于海上，葬于布赖讷。

en:
John I the Red (c. 1217–1286), named for the colour of his beard, was Duke of Brittany from 1221, under the regency of his father Peter Mauclerc until 1237. In 1236 he married Blanche, daughter of King Theobald I of Navarre, who bore his successor John II.

In 1240 he expelled the Jews from the duchy and cancelled debts owed to them. Henry III made him Earl of Richmond in 1268, and he joined Louis IX on the Eighth Crusade in 1270, surviving the plague that killed the king. He died on 8 October 1286.

en:
John II (1239–1305), eldest son of John I the Red, was Duke of Brittany from 1286 and Earl of Richmond. In 1260 he married Beatrice, daughter of Henry III of England, and in 1271 joined Edward I on the Ninth Crusade. In the 1294 Gascon War he first aided Edward, but after English troops sacked Saint-Mathieu Abbey in 1296 he turned to Philip IV of France, who made him a peer of France in 1297, whereupon Edward deprived him of Richmond.

He fought at Mons-en-Pévèle, and in 1305 attended Clement V's coronation at Lyon, where a collapsing wall crushed him. He died on 18 November.

en:
John III the Good (1286–1341), son of Arthur II, became Duke of Brittany in 1312 and ruled through nearly thirty years of peace and prosperity. He was a loyal ally of the French crown: he fought for Philip VI at Cassel in 1328, and in 1340 his fleet was destroyed with the French at Sluys.

Yet as Earl of Richmond from 1334 he had also sworn homage to Edward III, so when the Hundred Years' War began he held land under both kings. He resented his stepmother Yolande and her son John of Montfort, whom he would not accept as heir.

His marriages were childless, and he considered leaving the duchy to the French crown. He died on 30 April 1341, and his death opened the Breton War of Succession.

zh:
“好人”约翰三世（1286—1341）是阿蒂尔二世之子，1312年成为布列塔尼公爵，在位近三十年，公国安定繁荣。他是法国王室的忠实盟友：1328年随腓力六世出征卡塞尔；1340年他的舰队在斯勒伊斯与法军一同被英军摧毁。

可是1334年起他兼任里士满伯爵，曾向英王爱德华三世宣誓效忠，百年战争爆发时，他在两位国王名下都有领地。他厌恶继母约兰德及其子蒙福尔的让，不肯接受后者做继承人。

他的婚姻都没有子嗣，曾考虑把公国留给法国王室。1341年4月30日他去世，随即引发布列塔尼继承战争。

en:
Arnaud-Guilhem de Béarn (c. 1330–c. 1391) was the illegitimate son of Gaston II, Count of Foix. Born shortly before his half-brother Gaston III Fébus, he became Fébus's closest collaborator, and by 1353 he was lieutenant-general of Béarn, left with wide powers whenever the count was away.

Through Fébus's reign he led the armies and directed the fortifications. In 1362 Fébus charged him with repudiating Agnes of Navarre, just after she had borne the heir.

He married the heiress of Morlanne, and the Château de Morlanne was built there to complete Fébus's defensive system. He died around 1390, shortly before Fébus.

阿尔诺·吉耶姆·德·贝阿恩（约1330—约1391）是富瓦伯爵加斯东二世的私生子。他比异母弟加斯东三世·费比斯略早出生，后来成为费比斯最亲近的帮手；1353年他已是贝阿恩的副摄政王，费比斯外出时由他全权代理。

费比斯在位期间，他统领军队、主持要塞修筑。1362年，费比斯在王妃纳瓦拉的阿涅丝刚生下继承人后，命他将其休弃。

他娶了莫尔拉讷领地的女继承人，莫尔拉讷城堡也修建于此，用来补全费比斯的防御体系。他约在1390年去世，略早于费比斯。

en:
Albert II, called the Fat (c. 1268–1318), was the second son of Duke Albert I of Brunswick-Lüneburg and Adelaide of Montferrat. The brothers ruled jointly after their father's death in 1279, and in 1284 Albert married Rixa of Werle. When the inheritance was divided in 1286, he received Göttingen and the lands around Hanover.

After his brother William died in 1292, a seven-year dispute with his brother Henry ended in Albert's favour, with Brunswick's support; Henry kept his principality of Grubenhagen.

en:
Ernest I (c. 1305–24 April 1367) was a son of Albert II the Fat of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel and Rixa of Werle. When his childless brother Otto the Mild died in 1344, he and Magnus I divided the Welf lands, and Ernest took the Principality of Göttingen, the poorest of the Welf domains, formed from the old Northeim holdings. The split parted Göttingen from Brunswick for a long time, though the city of Brunswick itself stayed with the whole house.

Ernest ruled Göttingen until his death. In 1339 he married Elizabeth, daughter of Landgrave Henry II the Iron of Hesse; she bore him six children, including his successor Otto I.

He is believed to have fought alongside local cities against the robber barons around Göttingen, and in 1364 he joined a regional coalition in a war on the Bishopric of Hildesheim.

恩斯特一世（约1305—1367年4月24日）是不伦瑞克-沃尔芬比特尔的“胖子”阿尔布雷希特二世与韦尔勒的里克莎之子。1344年，无嗣的兄长“温和者”奥托去世，他与马格努斯一世瓜分韦尔夫家族领地，恩斯特分得哥廷根亲王国，那是韦尔夫诸领地中最贫瘠的一块，由诺特海姆家族的旧产构成。这次分割使哥廷根与不伦瑞克长期分离，不伦瑞克城本身仍归全家族共有。

en:
Jutta of Hesse (c. 1289–1317) was the youngest daughter of Henry I, the first Landgrave of Hesse and founder of the Hessian princely house, and Mechthild of Cleves. In 1311 she married Duke Otto of Brunswick-Göttingen, known as Otto the Mild.

Jutta died in 1317, the year her only child, Agnes, was born, and was buried in Brunswick Cathedral. In 1329 the widowed Otto endowed an altar in Göttingen where masses were to be said for her.

en:
Magnus I, called the Pious (1304–1369), was a Welf prince and the first duke to rule Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel as a principality of its own. The son of Duke Albert the Fat, he came under his brother Otto's guardianship in 1318. His wife Sophia of Brandenburg was a niece of Emperor Louis IV, who in 1333 made Magnus margrave of Landsberg.

When Otto died childless in 1344, Magnus and Ernest divided the Welf lands; Magnus took Wolfenbüttel in 1345. War with the Archbishop of Magdeburg forced him in 1347 to sell Landsberg and cede territory, and the ruined duke could not stop towns, Brunswick above all, from winning more rights.

His claims to Lüneburg helped spark the Lüneburg Succession War. In 1367 he plundered the lands of the Bishop of Hildesheim, was beaten and captured at Dinklar, and died in 1369 after paying ransom.

马格努斯一世，绰号“虔诚者”（1304—1369），是韦尔夫家族王公，也是第一位把不伦瑞克-沃尔芬比特尔作为独立公国统治的公爵。他是公爵“胖子”阿尔布雷希特之子，1318年起由兄长奥托监护。妻子勃兰登堡的索菲是皇帝路德维希四世的侄女，1333年路德维希封他为兰茨贝格藩侯。

1344年奥托无嗣而终，他与恩斯特瓜分家族领地，1345年分得沃尔芬比特尔。1347年与马格德堡大主教的战争迫使他卖掉兰茨贝格并割地；财政破产的他无力阻止城镇，尤其是不伦瑞克城，取得更多权利。

他对吕讷堡的继承权主张促成吕讷堡继承战争。1367年他劫掠希尔德斯海姆主教的领地，在丁克拉尔兵败被俘，缴纳赎金后于1369年去世。

en:
Magnus II, called Torquatus or Magnus of the Silver Chain (1328–25 July 1373), was the Welf duke of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel and, briefly, Lüneburg. The eldest son of Magnus the Pious, he inherited Wolfenbüttel in 1369. Within months Duke William II of Lüneburg died too, having named Magnus his heir, a claim backed by Welf house law.

Emperor Charles IV instead treated Lüneburg as a vacant imperial fief and granted it to the Ascanian duke Albert of Saxe-Wittenberg, igniting the Lüneburg Succession War. Magnus's repeated demands for money drove the town of Lüneburg to side with his rivals, and his attempt to take it failed.

On 25 July 1373 he died of a wound received in a duel with his brother-in-law Count Otto I of Schaumburg at the Battle of Leveste.

马格努斯二世，绰号“佩银链者”托尔夸图斯（1328—1373年7月25日），是韦尔夫家族的不伦瑞克-沃尔芬比特尔公爵，并曾短暂领有吕讷堡。他是“虔诚者”马格努斯的长子，1369年继承沃尔芬比特尔。数月之内，吕讷堡公爵威廉二世也去世，此前已指定马格努斯为继承人，韦尔夫家族家法支持这一主张。

但皇帝查理四世视吕讷堡为空置的帝国采邑，转封给阿斯坎尼家族的萨克森-维滕贝格公爵阿尔贝特，吕讷堡继承战争由此爆发。马格努斯反复征款，致使吕讷堡城倒向他的对手，他试图攻占该城却告失败。

1373年7月25日，他在莱韦斯泰战役中与姻亲绍姆堡伯爵奥托一世决斗，受伤致死。

en:
Otto I, called the Child (c. 1204–1252), was the only son of William of Winchester and Helena, daughter of King Valdemar I of Denmark. He inherited the Welf estates around Lüneburg as a minor in 1213. When Emperor Frederick II tried to seize Brunswick after his uncle's death, Otto, backed by the town and the estates, drove the imperial forces out.

In 1235 Frederick enfeoffed him as first duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg. He died in 1252 and was buried in Brunswick Cathedral.

Otto the Mild (1292–1344), Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg, was the eldest son of Albert II and Rixa of Werle. He succeeded his father in 1318. In 1311 he married Jutta of Hesse, and in 1319, after her death, Agnes of Brandenburg, through whom he claimed the Altmark.

Unable to master the Brandenburg nobility, he sold his rights there for 3000 marks in 1343. He died at Göttingen in 1344; his brothers Ernest and Magnus split the duchy into Göttingen and Wolfenbüttel.

Rixa of Werle (c. 1270–26 November 1317) was the daughter of Henry I, Prince of Werle, and Rikissa Birgersdotter. Rixa was a granddaughter of the Swedish jarl Birger Magnusson of Bjälbo. On 10 January 1284 she married Albert II, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg, founder of the Göttingen line.

She bore Albert thirteen children, among them Otto the Mild, Magnus I of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel and Ernest I of Göttingen. Rixa died in 1317, ten months before her husband.

韦尔勒的里克莎（约1270—1317年11月26日）是韦尔勒亲王海因里希一世与里基莎·比耶尔斯多塔之女，也是瑞典雅尔、比耶博的比尔耶·马格努松的外孙女。1284年1月10日，她嫁给不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公爵阿尔布雷希特二世，即哥廷根支系的开创者。

en:
William I (1270–1292) was the third son of Duke Albert I of Brunswick and Adelaide of Montferrat. In the 1286 partition after their father's death, William received Brunswick itself and its surrounding lands, while Henry and Albert took Grubenhagen and Göttingen; open war between the brothers followed in 1288.

He married Elisabeth, daughter of Landgrave Henry I of Hesse, probably without children. William died at Brunswick in 1292, his lands passing to Albert after an inheritance dispute with Henry.

en:
Dmitry Romanovich (c. 1290–after 1352), a Rurikid prince, ruled Bryansk from about 1314. In 1333 he marched with Tatar forces against Smolensk, but sabotaged the campaign and made peace with its prince, whereupon Moscow's Ivan Kalita had him replaced by Gleb Sviatoslavich.

After the Bryansk veche killed Gleb in 1340, Dmitry regained his throne and in 1341 married his daughter Fedosia to Ivan II of Moscow. Around 1352 he was deposed again and is said to have died of plague soon after.

德米特里·罗曼诺维奇（约1290—1352年后）是出身留里克家族的王公，约1314年起统治布良斯克。1333年，他随鞑靼军队出征斯摩棱斯克，却虚与周旋，同斯摩棱斯克王公议和，莫斯科的伊凡·卡利塔随即将他排挤下台，扶植格列布·斯维亚托斯拉维奇。

1340年布良斯克市民在维彻上杀死格列布，德米特里复位，并于1341年将女儿费多西娅嫁给莫斯科的伊凡二世。约1352年他再度被废，相传不久死于瘟疫。

en:
Gleb Svyatoslavich (died 6 December 1340) was a Rurikid prince of the Smolensk branch and son of Svyatoslav Glebovich, Prince of Bryansk. In 1333 the Smolensk prince Ivan Alexandrovich secured his installation on the Bryansk throne, although the townspeople of Bryansk disliked both Gleb and his father.

He ruled Bryansk for at least seven years. In 1340, after the death of Ivan I of Moscow, the citizens gathered in veche and killed him, ignoring the warnings of Metropolitan Theognostus.

格列布·斯维亚托斯拉维奇（1340年12月6日卒）是斯摩棱斯克支系的留里克王公，布良斯克王公斯维亚托斯拉夫·格列博维奇之子。1333年，经斯摩棱斯克王公伊凡·亚历山德罗维奇运作，他被扶上布良斯克公位，但布良斯克市民对他和他的父亲都心怀敌意。

en:
Oleg Romanovich, later revered as Saint Oleg of Bryansk, was the younger son of Roman the Old and succeeded him as prince of Bryansk and grand prince of Chernigov after 1288.

The Galician-Volhynian Chronicle names him in 1274 among the princes taking part in the campaign against Lithuania, and in 1285 he joined his father's unsuccessful attack on Smolensk. He died in 1290 or 1307. Canonised by the Russian Orthodox Church, his feast is 20 September.

《加里西亚-沃伦编年史》在1274年条下提到他参加了对立陶宛的征战；1285年他又随父亲出征斯摩棱斯克，无果而返。他于1290年或1307年去世。俄罗斯正教会将他尊为圣徒王公，纪念日为9月20日。

en:
Roman Mikhailovich, called the Old, was prince of Bryansk and, from 1263, grand prince of Chernigov, a son of Mikhail Vsevolodovich of Chernigov. When Lithuanians seized Chernigov in 1263, he retook it and was wounded defeating troops sent by King Mindaugas.

In 1274–1275 he joined the campaign against Lithuania under Mongol khan Mengu-Timur, and in 1285 he led an unsuccessful attack on Smolensk. He died after 1288 and was succeeded at Bryansk by his son Oleg.

en:
Svyatoslav Glebovich (died 1310) was the youngest son of Gleb Rostislavich of Smolensk and held Mozhaysk until 1303, when Daniil of Moscow absorbed the principality. In 1309 he expelled his nephew Vasily, whom the Smolensk prince had installed on the Bryansk throne, and seized the town himself.

In 1310 Vasily returned and stormed Bryansk, a Golden Horde detachment accompanying him. The Bryansk regiment hung back and Svyatoslav was defeated and killed, only his own retinue fighting to the end. His sons Gleb and Fyodor later held Bryansk and Rzhev respectively.

en:
Vasily Alexandrovich (died 1314) was prince of Bryansk, traditionally held to be a son of Alexander Glebovich of Smolensk. In 1309 his uncle Sviatoslav Glebovich, formerly of Mozhaysk, expelled him and took Bryansk.

In 1310 Vasily returned with a Golden Horde detachment and stormed the town; the Bryansk regiment fought reluctantly and Sviatoslav was killed. That same year he and his Tatars overran Karachev and killed its prince. He died in 1314, and his brother Dmitry eventually succeeded at Bryansk.

en:
Annam Deo, also called Annamaraja, was a Telugu warrior traditionally described as a member of the Kakatiya house of Warangal and a brother of its last king, Prataparudra II. Chronicles say that after anointing Prataparudra's son as king he left Warangal for the north-eastern forests.

Around 1324 he founded a kingdom at Bastar, placing it under the goddess Danteshwari. Ruler lists give his reign as 1313 to 1358 and name Hamir Deo his successor.

en:
Adelheid of Hanau (born 1311–1313, died after 1378) was a daughter of Ulrich II, Lord of Hanau, and Agnes of Hohenlohe. She was first married to Count Eberhard II of Katzenelnbogen, who died soon after the wedding in 1329 leaving no children.

In July 1332 she was betrothed to Henry II of Isenburg-Büdingen, her dowry handed over that September; among their children were John I of Isenburg-Büdingen and Adelheid, abbess of Quedlinburg. She was buried at Arnsburg Abbey.

en:
Henry II of Isenburg-Büdingen (c. 1300–1378/1379) was a lord of the Büdingen line of the Isenburg family, the son of Lothar of Isenburg-Cleeberg. In 1332 he was betrothed to Adelheid of Hanau, and around 1340 he succeeded to his father's lands.

He ruled at Büdingen until 1378, securing his house's inherited claims to the lordship. His son John I succeeded him, while his daughter Adelheid became abbess of Quedlinburg.

en:
Chwa I Nabakka was the second Kabaka, or king, of Buganda, ruling in the mid-fourteenth century after the death of his father, Kato Kintu, the kingdom's first Kabaka. He established his capital at Bigo Hill.

He married Naabakyaala Nakku and Nakiwala of the Ngonge clan, who bore him Prince Kalemeera. After him the kingdom was ruled by regents Walusimbi and Sebwaana until 1374.

他娶纳巴基亚拉·纳库与恩贡盖氏族的纳基瓦拉，纳基瓦拉为他生下王子卡莱梅拉。他之后王国由瓦卢辛比和塞布瓦纳两位摄政治理，直至1374年。

en:
Prince Kalemeera was the son of Kabaka Chwa I Nabakka of Buganda by Nakiwala of the Ngonge clan. Ganda tradition relates that his father drove him out of Buganda, and he took refuge in Bunyoro at the court of his uncle, Omukama Winyi I.

There he had an affair with Wannyana, his uncle's chief wife, who bore him a son, Kimera Walusimbi. The boy was raised in Bunyoro and in 1374 returned to Buganda to become its third Kabaka, while Kalemeera remained in exile.

卡莱梅拉王子是布干达卡巴卡奇瓦一世·纳巴卡与恩贡盖氏族纳基瓦拉之子。布干达口传传统称，他被父亲逐出布干达，前往布尼奥罗，投奔他的叔伯或舅父、奥穆卡马温尼一世。

en:
Kato Kintu Kakulukuku (fl. c. 1300), called Kato Kimera in Bunyoro, was the first Kabaka, or king, of the Kingdom of Buganda. Born at Bukasa in the Ssese Islands on Lake Nalubaale, he adopted the by-name Kintu after the first man in Ganda mythology.

He set his capital at Nnono in Busujju County and fathered three children. Ganda oral tradition holds that he died at thirty; his son Chwa I succeeded him.

en:
Aldimir, also called Eltimir, was a Bulgarian noble of Cuman origin, a younger brother of Tsar George Terter I and despot of Kran. After George abdicated in 1292 he took refuge with the Golden Horde, returning in 1298 as ally of the regent Smiltsena, whose daughter Marina he married.

In 1300 he captured and blinded the pretender Radoslav, submitting to his nephew Tsar Theodore Svetoslav. When he defected to Byzantium in 1305, Theodore Svetoslav overran Kran; Aldimir is not recorded thereafter and may have been killed.

en:
Alexander Asen was the second son of Tsar Ivan Asen I and Empress Elena, and younger brother of Ivan Asen II. After the usurper Boril seized power in 1207, he fled with his brother abroad and returned in 1217. In 1218, after Rus' mercenaries toppled Boril, Ivan Asen II made Alexander sebastokrator with Sofia as his appanage.

In 1233 he defeated the Hungarians near Vidin and at Braničevo, restoring Bulgarian control over the occupied lands. His son Kaliman Asen II briefly held the throne in 1256.

亚历山大·阿森是保加利亚沙皇伊凡·阿森一世与皇后叶莲娜的次子、伊凡·阿森二世之弟。1207年僭主博里尔夺权后，他随兄长流亡国外，1217年回国。1218年罗斯雇佣兵推翻博里尔，伊凡·阿森二世封他为至尊者，以索非亚为封地。

1233年他在维丁附近和布拉尼切沃连挫匈军，收复失地。其子卡里曼·阿森二世曾于1256年短暂在位。

en:
Balik (fl. c. 1320, died 1347) was a Bulgarian noble who built the Principality of Karvuna into a virtually independent state in the region later called Dobrudja, ruling from the fortress of Kaliakra.

In the Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347 he backed the regent Anna of Savoy against John VI Kantakouzenos. He died in 1347, either in the Black Death or in a retaliatory campaign by the Turkish emir Umur Beg that destroyed Dobrudja's seaports. His brother Dobrotitsa succeeded him after recapturing Karvuna in 1354.

巴利克（约1320年前后在世，1347年卒）是保加利亚贵族，他以卡利阿克拉要塞为据点，把卡尔武纳公国经营成后世称为多布罗加地区的实际独立政权。

1341—1347年拜占庭内战期间，他支持摄政萨伏依的安娜，对抗约翰六世·坎塔库泽努斯。他于1347年去世，或死于黑死病，或死于土耳其埃米尔乌穆尔贝伊的报复性远征；这次远征摧毁了多布罗加的海港。其弟多布罗蒂察于1354年收复卡尔武纳后继立。

en:
Boril was tsar of Bulgaria from 1207 to 1218. A nephew of Kaloyan through a sister of the three Asen brothers, he seized the throne after Kaloyan died besieging Thessaloniki in October 1207 and married his Cuman widow. His cousin Ivan Asen fled abroad while other kinsmen rebelled.

In July 1208 the Latin emperor Henry defeated him near Philippopolis. In early 1211 Boril held a church council at Tarnovo that condemned the Bogomils, and with Hungarian aid crushed a revolt at Vidin. In 1218 Ivan Asen returned, captured him at Tarnovo and blinded him.

博里尔（1207—1218年在位）是保加利亚沙皇，其母是彼得二世、伊凡·阿森一世与卡洛扬三兄弟的姐妹。1207年10月卡洛扬围攻塞萨洛尼基时暴卒，博里尔夺取皇位并娶其库曼遗孀。表亲伊凡·阿森出逃国外，其他亲属则举兵反叛。

1208年7月，拉丁帝国皇帝亨利在腓力波波利附近将他击败。1211年初，他在特尔诺沃召开宗教会议谴责波格米勒派，又借匈牙利援军镇压维丁叛乱。1218年伊凡·阿森归国，在特尔诺沃擒获博里尔并将其弄瞎。

en:
Chaka (died 1300) was a Mongol prince, son of the Golden Horde strongman Nogai Khan. In the late 1290s he fought with his father against Khan Toqta, who defeated and killed Nogai in 1299. Chaka then led his followers into Bulgaria, drove out Ivan II's regency, and ruled at Tarnovo in 1299–1300.

Toqta's army pursued him and besieged the capital; his brother-in-law Theodore Svetoslav plotted against him, had him strangled in prison, and sent his head to the khan.

恰卡（1300年卒）是蒙古宗王，金帐汗国权臣那海汗之子。1290年代末，他随父亲与脱脱汗交战，那海于1299年兵败被杀。恰卡随即率部众进入保加利亚，驱逐伊凡二世的摄政势力，于1299—1300年统治特尔诺沃。

en:
Constantine Tih Asen was a wealthy Bulgarian boyar with estates around Skopje. Elected tsar at Tarnovo in 1257 on the Asen dynasty's extinction, he married Irene Laskarina, daughter of the Nicaean emperor, and took the name Asen.

He fought Hungary for Vidin and seized Philippopolis in 1262, only to lose it to Michael VIII Palaiologos. Paralyzed in a riding accident, he left government to his wife. In 1277 the swineherd Ivaylo rebelled; Constantine marched against him and was killed in his chariot.

君士坦丁·提赫·阿森是斯科普里一带有封地的富有保加利亚贵族。1257年阿森王朝男系绝嗣，他在特尔诺沃被推举为沙皇，娶尼西亚皇帝之女伊琳娜·拉斯卡丽娜，并改用阿森之名。

en:
George Terter I (died 1308 or 1309), a Bulgarian boyar of Cuman descent, was tsar from 1280 to 1292. Ivan Asen III made him despot and he divorced his wife to marry the emperor's sister; his first wife and their son Theodore Svetoslav were sent as hostages to Byzantium.

When Ivan Asen fled in 1280, George seized the throne, but Mongol raids under Nogai Khan weakened his rule. After Nogai attacked Bulgaria around 1292, George was deposed and went into exile in Byzantium, where he lived in want.

In 1301 his son Theodore Svetoslav, now tsar, ransomed him for thirteen captured Byzantine officers. George ended his days in Bulgaria.

en:
George Terter II was the son of Tsar Theodore Svetoslav and reigned as tsar of Bulgaria from 1322 to 1323. Succeeding his father in 1322, he exploited the Byzantine civil war to invade Thrace and capture Philippopolis, installing a garrison there.

Later that year he reduced several fortresses around Adrianople, but Andronikos III rallied and drove the Bulgarians back. As the Byzantines prepared a counter-invasion, George died young, apparently of natural causes, leaving no known heir; Michael Shishman succeeded him.

en:
Irene Palaiologina was the eldest daughter of Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos and Empress Theodora. In 1277 or 1278 her father married her to the Bulgarian exile Ivan Asen III and sent armies to place him on the throne at Tarnovo during Ivaylo's revolt. Irene was crowned empress in 1279, but in 1280 the couple fled Tarnovo and returned to Constantinople.

In 1305 she plotted against her brother Andronikos II to avenge her son-in-law. The plot failed and she was placed under house arrest.

en:
Irene Palaiologina (1327 – c. 1399), born Maria, was a Byzantine princess, daughter of Emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos and Anna of Savoy, and an elder sister of Emperor John V. Her betrothal to the Bulgarian heir Michael Asen sealed the peace after the Battle of Rusokastro; they married in 1336, and she took the name Irene as a pledge of peace between the two realms.

In 1355 Michael Asen IV was killed fighting the Ottoman Turks near Sofia. His widow returned briefly to Constantinople, then settled at Mesembria, where she became a nun under the name Mataisa. She spent the rest of her life in the town's monastery and was buried there around 1399.

en:
Ivan Alexander (died 17 February 1371), nephew of Michael Shishman, was tsar of Bulgaria from 1331 to 1371. He fought at Velbazhd in 1330, where Serbia crushed Bulgaria; defeat and invasion sparked a coup in 1331 that ousted Ivan Stefan and put him on the throne.

He retook northeastern Thrace and secured the Serbian border by marrying his sister Helena to Stefan Dušan in 1332. That summer he caught Andronikos III at Rusokastro and, reinforced by Mongol cavalry, overwhelmed the Byzantine army. Around 1332 he crowned his eldest son Michael Asen IV co-emperor.

His long reign brought economic recovery and a cultural and religious revival, but Ottoman raids and the Black Death wore Bulgaria down. He divided the realm among his sons, leaving it split when the Ottomans advanced.

伊凡·亚历山大（1371年2月17日卒）是米哈伊尔·希什曼的外甥，1331—1371年任保加利亚沙皇。他参加了1330年塞尔维亚大败保加利亚的维尔巴日德战役；战败与入侵引发1331年政变，驱逐伊凡·斯特凡，把他推上皇位。

他收复色雷斯东北部，1332年把妹妹海伦娜嫁给斯特凡·杜尚，稳住了与塞尔维亚的边界。同年夏天，他在鲁索卡斯特罗追上安德洛尼卡三世，借助蒙古骑兵击溃拜占庭军队。约1332年，他为长子米哈伊尔·阿森四世加冕为共治皇帝。

漫长的统治带来经济复苏与文化、宗教复兴，但奥斯曼人袭扰和黑死病拖垮了保加利亚。他把国土分封给诸子，致使国家在奥斯曼人推进时已陷于分裂。

en:
Ivan Asen IV (c. 1326 – 1349) was a Bulgarian prince, the third son of Tsar Ivan Alexander and Theodora of Wallachia. In 1349 he led Bulgarian forces against an Ottoman army under Süleyman in a fierce battle near Sofia.

Both sides suffered heavy losses and Ivan Asen was killed in the fighting; the Bulgarians appear to have beaten off the raid, as the next Ottoman incursion came only in 1355. He had married a Wallachian princess of the Basarab dynasty and left two daughters.

en:
Ivan Asen I (died 1196), a founder of the Second Bulgarian Empire, ruled as tsar from 1187 or 1188, at first with his elder brother Peter II. In 1185, after Emperor Isaac II Angelos refused and humiliated their demand for Balkan lands, Asen and Peter roused the Bulgarians and Vlachs to revolt, and Peter was crowned that year.

Defeated in 1186, they fled across the Danube and returned with Cuman allies, taking Paristrion. Asen received Tarnovo when the realm was divided around 1192 and extended Bulgarian rule to the Struma valley. The boyar Ivanko stabbed him to death in 1196.

en:
Ivan Asen II (1190s–1241), son of Ivan Asen I, was tsar of Bulgaria from 1218 to 1241. He fled to Rus' after Boril usurped the throne in 1207, but returned in 1218, took Tarnovo and blinded Boril. At Klokotnitsa in 1230 he crushed Theodore Komnenos Doukas and took Macedonia, Thessaly and much of Thrace.

He controlled the Via Egnatia and minted gold at Ohrid. In 1235 his alliance with Nicaean emperor John III Vatatzes restored the Bulgarian patriarchate. After jointly attacking Constantinople, he broke with Nicaea in 1237. He died in 1241, leaving the throne to his young son Kaliman.

en:
Ivan Asen III (c. 1259–1303), son of Tsar Mitso Asen and a daughter of Ivan Asen II, claimed Bulgaria with Byzantine backing. In 1277 or 1278 Michael VIII Palaiologos made him despotēs and married him to his daughter Irene Palaiologina.

While Ivaylo's rebels were blockaded at Silistra, a Byzantine army besieged Tarnovo; hearing a rumour of Ivaylo's death, the nobles surrendered and accepted Ivan Asen as emperor in 1279. He married his sister Maria to George Terter. Ivaylo returned and routed two relief armies; in 1280 the tsar fled the capital with the palace treasure and sailed to Constantinople, where he sought Nogai Khan's aid in vain. He died on his Troad estates in 1303.

en:
Ivan II Smilets (born c. 1290, died before 1330) reigned as tsar of Bulgaria from 1298 to 1299. A child when he succeeded his father Smilets at Tarnovo, he ruled under the regency of his mother Smiltsena, who defeated the claims of Smilets' brothers.

In 1299 the Mongol prince Chaka seized Tarnovo, and Ivan fled into exile, eventually settling in Byzantium. He became a monk as Joasaph and died in exile before 1330.

伊凡二世·斯米列茨（约1290年生，1330年前卒）于1298至1299年任保加利亚沙皇。他在特尔诺沃继父斯米列茨之位时年幼，由母亲斯米尔察娜摄政，她曾挫败斯米列茨诸兄弟的夺位企图。

1299年蒙古宗王恰卡攻占特尔诺沃，伊凡流亡国外，最终定居拜占庭。他后来出家，教名约阿萨夫，1330年以前在流亡中去世。

en:
Ivan Asen III (c. 1259–1303), son of Tsar Mitso Asen and a daughter of Ivan Asen II, claimed Bulgaria with Byzantine backing. In 1277 or 1278 Michael VIII Palaiologos married him to his daughter Irene Palaiologina. While Ivaylo was blockaded at Silistra, a Byzantine army took Tarnovo and enthroned him in 1279.

Ivaylo returned and routed the Byzantine relief armies; in 1280 Ivan fled with the palace treasure to Constantinople. He sought Nogai Khan's aid in vain and died on his Troad estates in 1303.

伊凡·阿森三世（约1259—1303）是沙皇米措·阿森与伊凡·阿森二世之女的儿子，在拜占庭支持下争夺保加利亚皇位。1277或1278年，米海尔八世·巴列奥略将女儿伊琳娜·巴列奥略吉娜嫁给他。趁伊瓦伊洛被围困在锡利斯特拉之机，拜占庭军队攻克特尔诺沃，于1279年拥立他为沙皇。

en:
Ivan Sratsimir (1324 or 1325 – c. 1397) was a son of Tsar Ivan Alexander of Bulgaria and Theodora of Wallachia. Proclaimed co-emperor in 1337 with Vidin as his appanage, he was disinherited in favour of his half-brother Ivan Shishman and in 1356 declared himself emperor at Vidin.

After 1371 he broke with Tarnovo. He joined King Sigismund's crusade against the Ottomans, but after Nicopolis in 1396 they seized Vidin and took him to Bursa, where he was probably strangled, the last ruler of medieval Bulgaria.

伊凡·斯拉齐米尔（1324或1325—约1397）是保加利亚沙皇伊凡·亚历山大与瓦拉几亚的狄奥多拉之子。1337年他被宣布为共治皇帝，领有维丁作为封地；后来被剥夺继承权，其父改立同父异母弟伊凡·希什曼为储君，他遂于1356年在维丁自立为帝。

1371年后他与特尔诺沃决裂。他参加了匈牙利国王西吉斯蒙德讨伐奥斯曼人的十字军，但1396年尼科波利斯战败后，奥斯曼人攻占维丁，把他押往布尔萨，可能遭绞杀，是中世纪保加利亚最后的统治者。

en:
Ivan Stefan was the eldest surviving son of Tsar Michael Asen III Shishman of Bulgaria and Ana-Neda, daughter of King Stefan Uroš II Milutin of Serbia. After his father died of wounds at Velbazhd in 1330, he was placed on the throne at Tarnovo, ruling only eight months while his mother governed in his name.

In March 1331 a palace coup overthrew them and raised his cousin Ivan Alexander to power. Ivan Stefan fled into exile at Dubrovnik, where he was recorded with his mother in 1332; he was dead by 1357.

伊凡·斯特凡是保加利亚沙皇米哈伊尔·阿森三世·希什曼与塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·乌罗什二世·米卢廷之女安娜-内达幸存的长子。1330年父亲在维尔巴日德伤重而死后，他即位于特尔诺沃，仅在位八个月，由母亲以他的名义执政。

en:
Ivaylo (died 1281), nicknamed Lakhanas or ‘the Cabbage’, was a rebel who ruled Bulgaria as tsar in 1278–1279. In 1277 he led a peasant uprising and forced the nobility to accept him. He married the widowed empress and was recognized as emperor in 1278, winning the Battle of Devina.

In 1279 Mongol forces blockaded him at Silistra and Tarnovo accepted Ivan Asen III. After George Terter I seized the throne, Ivaylo sought Nogai Khan's aid, but Nogai had him killed in 1281.

en:
Kaliman Asen I (1234–1246) was tsar of Bulgaria from 1241, succeeding his father Ivan Asen II at seven; his mother was Anna Maria of Hungary. Regents ruled during his minority, and early in his reign Bulgaria, the Latin Empire and Nicaea made a two-year truce.

In March 1242 the Mongol prince Kadan invaded, destroying Tarnovo and other fortresses; Bulgaria later paid an annual tribute. In 1245 Pope Innocent IV urged him to unite the Bulgarian Church with Rome. Kaliman died at twelve in August or September 1246, amid rumors of poisoning.

en:
Kaliman Asen II ruled as tsar of Bulgaria for a few months in 1256. The son of Alexander, younger brother of Ivan Asen II, he murdered his cousin Tsar Michael II Asen at a hunting party near Tarnovo, seized the throne and married the dead tsar's widow.

Her father Rostislav then marched on Tarnovo and forced him to flee. Mitso Asen took the throne, and Kaliman was murdered after his supporters deserted him.

en:
Kaloyan the Roman-Slayer (c. 1170–October 1207), youngest of the Asen brothers, was tsar of restored Bulgaria from 1197. Once a hostage in Constantinople, he seized sole power when Asen and Peter were murdered in 1196–1197. After capturing Varna in 1201 he styled himself the Roman-Slayer, in imitation of Basil II the Bulgar-Slayer.

He sought an imperial title from Pope Innocent III, offering to acknowledge papal primacy. A papal legate crowned him king at Tarnovo in 1204. In 1205 he captured the Latin Emperor Baldwin I at Adrianople. He died in October 1207 while besieging Thessalonica.

en:
Keratsa Petritsa (born c. 1280) was a Bulgarian noblewoman, a daughter of Despot Shishman of Vidin and sister of Tsar Michael Shishman. Around 1300 she married the sebastokrator Sratsimir, lord of Kran or Karvuna, and through her mother traced descent from Tsar Ivan Asen II.

Her children included Ivan Alexander, who seized the Bulgarian throne in 1331, and Helena, who married the Serbian king Stefan Dušan in 1332. Late in life she returned to Orthodoxy and took the veil as Theophana.

en:
Maria Asenina (born between 1238 and 1241) was a Bulgarian princess, daughter of Emperor Ivan Asen II and his third wife Irene Komnene Doukaina. She was the full sister of Emperor Michael Asen.

Bulgarian historiography traditionally identifies her as the wife of Emperor Mitso Asen, who ruled in 1256–1257, making her briefly empress consort. On that view she was the mother of Emperor Ivan Asen III and ancestress of the Byzantine branch of the Asen dynasty.

en:
Michael II Asen (c. 1239–1256/1257), son of Ivan Asen II, was tsar of Bulgaria from 1246, succeeding his half-brother Kaliman I at the age of seven. Early in his minority Nicaea and Epirus overran the Vardar valley and western Macedonia.

In 1254 he allied with Ragusa against Serbia and marched against her without gaining territory. After John III Vatatzes died, Michael retook most of the lost Macedonian lands with local support, but Theodore II Laskaris counter-attacked in 1255 and forced peace. Shortly afterward discontented boyars murdered him, and his cousin Kaliman II seized the throne.

en:
Michael Tih, also called Michael Asen II, was the son of Tsar Constantine Tih and Maria Palaiologina Kantakouzene, born around 1270. He became emperor in 1277, when his father fell fighting Ivaylo's rebels, and ruled under his mother's regency.

In spring 1278 his mother married Ivaylo, who reigned as his co-emperor. When the city nobles admitted the Byzantines in February 1279, Michael was dethroned and taken captive to Byzantium. Around 1302 or 1303 a boyar faction backed his return, but he failed and vanishes from the sources.

en:
Michael Shishman (c. 1286–1330), son of the Vidin despot Shishman, ruled Bulgaria as tsar from 1323 and founded the Shishman dynasty, the last dynasty of the Second Bulgarian Empire. On accession he took the name Asen, linking himself to the earlier Asenids.

He pursued an aggressive, shifting diplomacy against Byzantium and Serbia and was the last Bulgarian ruler to attempt the capture of Constantinople. On 28 July 1330 King Stefan Dečanski defeated him at Velbazhd; Michael died shortly afterward. His son Ivan Stephen and later his nephew Ivan Alexander succeeded him.

米哈伊尔·希什曼（约1286—1330）是维丁专制公希什曼之子，1323年起任保加利亚沙皇，建立了第二帝国最后一个王朝——希什曼王朝。即位后他改用“阿森”之名，以标榜自己与阿森王朝的联系。

en:
Michael Asen IV (c. 1322–1355) was the eldest son of Tsar Ivan Alexander of Bulgaria and Theodora of Wallachia. Soon after his father took the throne in 1331, the boy was crowned co-emperor and designated heir.

In 1339 he married Maria, renamed Irene, daughter of the Byzantine emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos. When the Ottomans invaded Bulgaria in 1354–1355, heading for Plovdiv and Sofia, Michael gathered the Bulgarians and met the Turks near Sofia.

An anonymous Bulgarian chronicle records heavy Bulgarian losses, Michael among the dead. The Ottomans took neither city and left Bulgaria alone until 1370, and folklore remembers the emperor's son as one of the brave who fell.

米哈伊尔·阿森四世（约1322—1355）是保加利亚沙皇伊凡·亚历山大与瓦拉几亚的狄奥多拉的长子。父亲1331年即位后不久，他便被加冕为共治皇帝、立为储君。

1339年，他娶拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡三世·巴列奥略之女玛丽亚（婚后改名伊琳娜）为妻。1354—1355年，奥斯曼人入侵保加利亚，直取普罗夫迪夫和索非亚，米哈伊尔集结保加利亚人，在索非亚附近迎战土耳其人。

一部佚名的保加利亚编年史记载，保加利亚军伤亡惨重，米哈伊尔本人也在阵亡者之中。奥斯曼人没有攻下两城，直到1370年都未再进犯保加利亚，民间传说也把这位皇帝之子记作阵亡勇士中的一员。

en:
Mitso Asen was tsar of Bulgaria from 1256 to 1257, taking the throne through his marriage to a daughter of Tsar Ivan Asen II. After Kaliman Asen II was murdered in 1256 he claimed the crown, but the nobility opposed him and a failed campaign against Nicaea cost him his support.

When Constantine Asen I was proclaimed in 1257, he fled the capital and resisted from Preslav and then Mesembria, which around 1263 he surrendered to Michael VIII Palaiologos. His son Ivan Asen III later claimed the Bulgarian throne.

en:
Sarah-Theodora was the second wife of Tsar Ivan Alexander of Bulgaria, who ruled from 1331 to 1371. Said to come from a Jewish family of Tarnovo, she converted to Eastern Orthodoxy, took the name Theodora, and married the tsar in the late 1340s after he divorced Theodora of Wallachia.

A fierce patron of her adopted faith, she instigated a church council against the Jews and founded monasteries. She pressed the claim of her son Ivan Shishman over the elder Ivan Sratsimir; after the tsar died in 1371, Shishman succeeded at Tarnovo while Sratsimir declared Vidin a separate empire.

萨拉·狄奥多拉是保加利亚沙皇伊凡·亚历山大（1331—1371年在位）的第二任皇后。相传她出身特尔诺沃的犹太家庭，皈依东正教后改名狄奥多拉，在1340年代末沙皇与瓦拉几亚的狄奥多拉离婚后成为皇后。

她热忱护持皈依的信仰，发起针对犹太人的宗教会议，又兴建修道院。她力主自己的儿子伊凡·希什曼优先于年长的伊凡·斯拉齐米尔继位。1371年沙皇去世后，希什曼在特尔诺沃继位，斯拉齐米尔则宣布维丁为独立帝国。

en:
Shishman (fl. from the 1270s, died before 1313) was a Cuman boyar in Bulgaria who ruled a semi-independent realm from the Danubian fortress of Vidin. He was made despot by Tsar George Terter I. In 1291 he accepted Golden Horde suzerainty, and in 1292 he led an unsuccessful invasion of Serbia.

The Serbs retaliated by taking Vidin, but he was restored as a Serbian vassal and kept his lands effectively independent until his death. Through his son Michael Shishman, who seized the Bulgarian throne in 1323, he was the progenitor of the Shishman dynasty.

希什曼（1270年代起在世，1313年前卒）是保加利亚的库曼裔贵族，以多瑙河畔的维丁要塞为中心，统治一个半独立政权。他获沙皇乔治·捷尔捷尔一世封为专制公。1291年他接受金帐汗国的宗主权；1292年率军入侵塞尔维亚失利。

塞尔维亚人反攻夺取维丁，他后来复位成为塞尔维亚的附庸，却始终保持实际独立直至去世。其子米哈伊尔·希什曼于1323年登上保加利亚皇位，希什曼也因此成为希什曼王朝的始祖。

en:
Smilets was tsar of Bulgaria from 1292 to 1298. His boyar clan held broad lands, and he replaced George Terter I with the backing of Nogai Khan; his reign is seen as the height of Mongol overlordship over Bulgaria.

Early on he fought an unsuccessful war against Byzantium, and around 1296 or 1297 married his daughter Theodora to the future Serbian king Stefan Dečanski. In 1298, during Chaka's invasion, Smilets vanishes from the records, perhaps killed; his young son Ivan II briefly succeeded him.

Sratsimir was a Bulgarian magnate who held the title of despot, ruling either Kran in the Balkan Mountains or the coastal region of Karvuna. Possibly of the Terter house, he already held his lands before his son Ivan Alexander seized the Bulgarian throne in 1331.

He married Keratsa Petritsa, sister of Tsar Michael Shishman, and founded the Sratsimir dynasty. Their children included Ivan Alexander and Helena, who married the Serbian king Stefan Dušan in 1332.

en:
Theodora of Wallachia was a daughter of Basarab I, prince of Wallachia from 1310 to 1352. Her father fought beside her husband Ivan Alexander at Velbazhd in 1330, the year before Ivan Alexander took the Bulgarian throne. As his first wife she bore him four children.

In 1345 Ivan Alexander divorced her and had her shut in a monastery, where she took the nun's name Teofana. She is counted the first nun known in Romanian history, and the Romanian Orthodox Church canonised her in 2022.

en:
Theodora was a Bulgarian princess, the daughter of Despot Sratsimir of Kran and a sister of Tsar Ivan Alexander. First recorded at the Serbian court in 1352, she was to marry Emperor John V Palaiologos under Stefan Dušan's plan to split him from John VI Kantakouzenos, but the scheme fell through.

After Dušan's death the Epirote ruler Nikephoros II Orsini meant to put aside his wife and marry her, but abandoned the plan before he was killed in 1359, after which she vanishes from the record.

en:
Theodor-Peter Asen, who ruled as Tsar Peter IV (died 1197), was the eldest of the Asen brothers who restored Bulgaria. In 1185 the Byzantine emperor Isaac II Angelos refused his and Asen's request for land in the Balkan Mountains, and the emperor's uncle John Doukas ordered Asen struck. The brothers roused the Bulgarians and Vlachs to revolt, and Peter was crowned tsar before year's end.

Defeated in 1186, he fled to the Cumans and returned with Cuman troops. He took Preslav in the brothers' partition around 1192; after Asen's murder in 1196 he made Kaloyan co-ruler, but was himself killed in 1197.

en:
Theodora Palaiologina (fl. 1308–1330) was a Byzantine princess, daughter of Emperor Michael IX and sister of Andronikos III. In spring 1308 she married Tsar Theodore Svetoslav of Bulgaria to seal the peace ending his war with Byzantium.

Widowed in 1321, she stayed at Tarnovo and in 1324 married the new tsar Michael Shishman after he set aside his first wife. When Michael fell at Velbazhd in July 1330 and his ex-wife returned, Theodora left for Constantinople, where she became a nun named Theodosia.

en:
Theodosius II was Patriarch of Bulgaria, with his see at Tarnovo, from 1348 to 1363, during the Second Bulgarian Empire. A monk of the Zografou Monastery on Mount Athos before his election, he led the Bulgarian Church under Tsar Ivan Alexander.

He took part in two church councils convened at Tarnovo, in 1350 and in 1359–1360, which condemned the Messalian, Bogomil and Adamite heresies. He died in 1363 and was succeeded by Joannicius II.

狄奥多西二世是第二保加利亚帝国时期的保加利亚牧首，1348至1363年间驻节特尔诺沃。当选牧首前，他是阿索斯山佐格拉夫修道院的修士，在沙皇伊凡·亚历山大治下主持保加利亚教会。

他参加了分别于1350年和1359—1360年在特尔诺沃召开的两次宗教会议，会议谴责梅萨利安派、博格米尔派和亚当派异端。他于1363年去世，约安尼基二世继任牧首。

en:
Theodore Svetoslav, son of Tsar George Terter I, spent his youth as a hostage in Byzantium and the Golden Horde. After his father divorced his mother, they were sent to Nicaea; Patriarch Joachim III arranged Theodore's release in 1285.

In 1299 he backed the Mongol prince Chaka's seizure of Tarnovo, but in 1300 he strangled Chaka and seized the crown. As tsar he ended Mongol suzerainty, executed Patriarch Joachim III for treason, captured Mesembria and Anchialos in 1304, and routed Michael IX Palaiologos.

The peace of 1307 was sealed by his marriage to Theodora, Michael IX's daughter. He died in 1322, leaving the throne to his son George Terter II.

托多·斯维托斯拉夫是沙皇格奥尔基·捷尔捷尔一世之子，早年曾在拜占庭和金帐汗国充当人质。父母离异后，他和母亲被送往尼西亚；1285年，牧首约阿基姆三世促成他获释。

1299年，他支持蒙古宗王恰卡攻占特尔诺沃，却于1300年废黜并缢杀恰卡，自立为保加利亚沙皇。在位期间，他摆脱了蒙古的宗主权，以叛国罪处死牧首约阿基姆三世，1304年夺取梅塞姆布里亚和安希亚洛斯，并击溃米海尔九世·巴列奥略率领的拜占庭军。

1307年双方议和，他迎娶米海尔九世之女狄奥多拉以巩固和约。他于1322年去世，王位由儿子格奥尔基·捷尔捷尔二世继承。

en:
Agnes of Dampierre (1237–1288) was Lady of Bourbon in her own right, the younger daughter of Lord Archambaud IX of Bourbon and Yolande of Châtillon. In 1248 she married John of Burgundy, a younger son of Duke Hugh IV.

When her elder sister Mahaut died in 1262, Agnes inherited the lordship of Bourbon. Her only child, Beatrice, married Robert, Count of Clermont, son of Louis IX, in 1272. After John's death she remarried Robert II, Count of Artois, in 1277.

en:
Agnes of France (1260 – 19 December 1325) was the youngest daughter of King Louis IX of France and Margaret of Provence. Betrothed to Duke Robert II of Burgundy, she married him in 1279 and became duchess.

On Robert's death in 1306 she ruled Burgundy as regent for her under-age son Hugh V until 1311; on the king's orders she confiscated Jewish property during her regency. She arranged prestigious marriages for her children, among them Margaret, wife of Louis X, and Joan, wife of Philip VI.

In 1316 she defended her granddaughter Joan's claim to the French throne. She died in 1325 and was buried at Cîteaux Abbey.

法兰西的阿格妮丝（1260年—1325年12月19日）是法王路易九世与普罗旺斯的玛格丽特最小的女儿。她被许配给勃艮第公爵罗贝尔二世，1279年成婚，成为公爵夫人。

1306年罗贝尔去世后，她为年幼的儿子于格五世摄政勃艮第，直到1311年；摄政期间她奉国王之命没收犹太人的财产。她为子女安排显贵联姻，其中女儿玛格丽特嫁给路易十世，约娜嫁给后来的腓力六世。

1316年，她维护外孙女让娜对法国王位的继承权。她于1325年去世，葬于西多修道院。

en:
Blanche of Burgundy (1288 – July 1348), daughter of Duke Robert II of Burgundy and Agnes of France, was married in 1307 to Edward, heir to Savoy. Her mother arranged the match, signed at the French king's Paris court, and the wedding followed at the Château de Montbard.

After Edward became count in 1323, she commissioned the Hours of Savoy, a book of hours now kept at Yale. He died in 1329, and Blanche bargained with his brother and successor Aymon over her dower until 1330, when she received lands in Bresse.

In 1346–1347 she used her influence at the court of her nephew Amadeus VI to draw Savoy closer to Burgundy, which led to his brief engagement to Joan of Burgundy. She died in 1348, perhaps of the Black Death.

勃艮第的布朗什（1288年—1348年7月）是勃艮第公爵罗贝尔二世与法兰西的阿格妮丝之女，1307年嫁给萨伏依继承人爱德华。婚事由母亲一手安排，在她舅父法王的巴黎宫廷签约，婚礼随后在蒙巴尔城堡举行。

1323年爱德华继位为伯爵后，她订制了《萨伏依时祷书》，今藏耶鲁大学。1329年爱德华去世，布朗什与继位的小叔艾蒙谈判寡妇产，1330年获封布雷斯的封地。

1346—1347年，她利用自己在侄子阿梅迪奥六世宫廷中的影响力，推动萨伏依向勃艮第靠拢，促成他与勃艮第的让娜短暂订婚。她于1348年去世，可能死于黑死病。

en:
Odo of Burgundy (1230–1266), count of Nevers, Auxerre and Tonnerre, was the eldest son of Duke Hugh IV of Burgundy and Yolande of Dreux. In 1265 he was among the last European barons to lead a crusading force to the Holy Land.

At Acre he helped defend the city when Sultan Baybars I harassed it in June 1266. He died at Acre that August, leaving his wealth to his followers and hospitals; the Templar of Tyre called him a holy man.

en:
Henry I, called the Great or Odo-Henry (946 – 15 October 1002), was a younger son of Hugh the Great and the younger brother of Hugh Capet. He entered the church young and was a cleric when, in 965, he was elected Duke of Burgundy after his brother Otto's death, taking the name Henry. His marriage in 972 to Gerberga brought him Nevers and a stepson, Otto-William, whom he adopted.

In 978 he joined the invasion of Lotharingia. He died in 1002 without a legitimate heir, sparking a succession war between Otto-William and his nephew King Robert II.

Odo I Borel, called the Red (c. 1058–1103), was the second son of Henry of Burgundy and became duke in 1079 when his elder brother Hugh I retired to Cluny. Chroniclers call him a violent brigand who ransomed travelers through his lands, and he campaigned against the Moors in Spain in 1087.

In 1098 he granted land for the founding of Cîteaux Abbey. He joined the Crusade of 1101 and died at Tarsus in Cilicia on 23 March 1103, leaving the duchy to his son Hugh II. His body was brought back to Cîteaux for burial.

Odo II (1118–27 June 1162), eldest son of Duke Hugh II the Pacific, ruled Burgundy from 1143. He is said to have fought the Moors in Portugal, but earned a name as a plundering lord, and at the accession of Louis VII in 1137 he refused the king homage until a ruling of Pope Adrian IV compelled him.

To atone for his violence he set out on pilgrimage to the Holy Land and died on the journey. In 1145 he married Marie of Champagne. Their son Hugh III succeeded him.

en:
Odo III (1166 – 6 July 1218) was Duke of Burgundy from 1192. Unlike his father he was a loyal ally of Philip II, fighting King John of England and Emperor Otto IV; at the Battle of Bouvines in 1214 chroniclers record two horses killed beneath him. He led the 1209 Albigensian campaign against the Cathar strongholds after Philip refused to join, and pledged a castle and village to the Templars.

He repudiated his first wife Theresa of Portugal in 1195, and in 1199 married Alice of Vergy, who bore his heir Hugh IV in 1213. He died in 1218.

en:
Odo IV (1295 – 3 April 1349), second son of Robert II and Agnes of France, became Duke of Burgundy in 1315, succeeding his brother Hugh V. In 1316 he defended his niece Joan's rights against her uncle Philip the Tall, and in 1318 he married Philip's eldest daughter, Joan III, Countess of Burgundy.

When she inherited Artois and the County of Burgundy in 1330, Robert of Artois, a friend of Philip VI, contested Artois until his claim was found to rest on documents forged on his orders. Odo was one of Philip VI's trusted advisers: wounded at Cassel in 1328, he held Saint-Omer against Robert in July 1340, sallying out and barely regaining the walls before the Flemings broke.

A patron of artists and the church, he died of plague in 1349; his son Philip had died in 1346, so a four-year-old grandson succeeded as Philip I.

厄德四世（1295年—1349年4月3日）是罗贝尔二世与法兰西的阿格妮丝的次子，1315年继兄于格五世成为勃艮第公爵。1316年他维护外甥女让娜的继承权，对抗她的叔父高个子腓力，1318年娶腓力的长女、勃艮第女伯爵让娜三世。

1330年让娜继承阿图瓦和勃艮第伯国，腓力六世的好友阿图瓦的罗贝尔争夺阿图瓦，直到其宣称所依据的文件被查出是奉他之命伪造的。厄德是腓力六世信任的谋臣：1328年在卡塞尔负伤，1340年7月坚守圣奥梅尔抵御罗贝尔，曾冲出城外，险些没能退回城墙之内，随后佛兰德军溃逃。

他赞助艺术家与教会，1349年死于瘟疫；儿子腓力已在1346年去世，年仅四岁的孙子继位为腓力一世。

Henry of Burgundy, called the Gallant (c. 1035–1070/1074), was the eldest surviving son of Duke Robert I the Old and Helie of Semur, and heir to the Duchy of Burgundy. He died before his father and never ruled as duke.

The duchy passed first to his son Hugh I and then to his second son Odo I. Another son, Henry, became count of Portugal in 1093 and fathered Afonso I, the first king of Portugal.

en:
Hugh of Vaucemain (died 1341) was a Burgundian Dominican elected Master General of the Order of Preachers in 1333. His tenure was marked by a quarrel with Pope Benedict XII, a Cistercian who set out to reform the religious orders.

Hugh did not oppose reform, but feared it would undermine the position of the mendicant orders, and he resisted. A census in 1337 put the Dominicans at roughly twelve thousand members. He remained Master General until his death in 1341.

en:
Hugh I (1057–1093) was duke of Burgundy from 1076 to 1079, the son of Henry of Burgundy and grandson of Duke Robert I, from whom he inherited after his father's early death. With Sancho I of Aragon he campaigned against the Moors in the Iberian Peninsula.

Worn by wounds and illness, in 1079 he abdicated in favor of his brother Odo I and entered Cluny Abbey. He later became prior of Cluny and died there on 29 August 1093.

en:
Hugh II, called the Pacific (c. 1085–1143), was the eldest son of Duke Odo I Borel and Sibylle of Burgundy. Regent when his father left on crusade in 1100, he inherited the duchy in 1103.

He fought for King Louis VI against Henry I of England in 1109 and commanded the vanguard against Emperor Henry V's invasion of Champagne in 1124. His reign was otherwise largely peaceful, earning his nickname; he even pardoned a subject condemned for insulting him.

Around 1116 he married Matilda of Mayenne, who bore his successor Odo II. He donated property to Cîteaux Abbey in 1119 and died in February 1143.

Hugh III (c. 1142–1192) was Duke of Burgundy from 1162, succeeding his father Odo II with his mother Marie of Champagne as regent. His reign ended Burgundy's long years of peace.

He fought Louis VII and Philip II of France; in 1186 Philip captured Châtillon and his heir Odo, forcing him to abandon his claims on French lands. In 1187 he moved the capital to Dijon and fostered trade.

He joined the Third Crusade and led the French after Philip sailed home. He fought at Arsuf and died at Acre in 1192.

en:
Hugh IV (9 March 1213 – 27 October 1272) was Duke of Burgundy from 1218, succeeding his father Odo III, and titular King of Thessalonica from 1266. In 1229 he attacked Theobald IV of Champagne against Blanche of Castile's regency, but was countered. In 1237 he acquired the counties of Chalon and Auxonne from John of Chalon, expanding the duchy along the wine trade.

He crusaded in the Holy Land in 1238–1241, then joined Louis IX's Seventh Crusade, commanding a division at Mansurah in 1250 and sharing the king's captivity that year. Emperor Baldwin II granted him the Thessalonican claim in 1266.

en:
Hugh V (1294–1315) was Duke of Burgundy and titular King of Thessalonica, the eldest surviving son of Duke Robert II and Agnes of France, a daughter of King Louis IX. He succeeded his father in 1306 while still a child and ruled under his mother's regency.

Betrothed young to Catherine of Valois-Courtenay, he renounced the match in 1312, and in 1313 sold his Thessalonican claim to his brother Louis. He died in May 1315 and was succeeded by his brother Odo IV.

John of Burgundy (1231–1268) was Count of Charolais and a younger son of Duke Hugh IV of Burgundy and Yolande of Dreux. In 1248 he married Agnes of Dampierre, daughter of Lord Archambaud IX of Bourbon.

In 1262 Agnes inherited Bourbon after the death of her sister Mathilde. The couple had one daughter, Beatrice, who in 1272 married Robert, Count of Clermont, a son of King Louis IX; the Capetian House of Bourbon descends from her.

en:
John of Charolais (1283 – 1316), also called John of Clermont, was a French baron, younger brother of Louis I, Duke of Bourbon, and son of Robert, Count of Clermont, and Beatrice of Burgundy, Lady of Bourbon. He held Charolais and fought the Flemings under Philip IV the Fair, including at Mons-en-Pévèle in 1304.

Around 1309 he married Joanna of Dargies and Catheux; their daughter Beatrice succeeded him in Charolais and married John I, Count of Armagnac. He died in 1316 while preparing to crusade in the Holy Land.

John II of Noyers was a Burgundian lord of the Maisey branch of the House of Noyers, son and heir of John I and Margaret of Durnay. After 1302 he went to Frankish Greece, and in 1307 married Beatrice da Verona, widow of Grappola dalle Carceri and heiress of the southern third of Euboea.

en:
Otto of Burgundy (c. 945–965) was Duke of Burgundy and Count of Auxerre, the second son of Hugh the Great and Hedwig of Saxony, sister of Emperor Otto I. Before Easter 955 his father married him to Liutgarde, heiress of Gilbert of Chalon, and on Gilbert's death in 956 Otto succeeded him.

King Lothair challenged his rule during his minority by occupying Dijon, but recognized him as duke in 960. Otto died in February 965 without children; his brother Henry succeeded him.

勃艮第的奥东（约945—965）是勃艮第公爵兼欧塞尔伯爵，伟大的于格与萨克森的哈德维希的次子，母亲是皇帝奥托一世的姐妹。955年复活节前，父亲安排他娶沙隆的吉尔贝尔之女、女继承人柳特加德为妻，956年吉尔贝尔死后奥东接掌勃艮第。

法兰西国王洛泰尔趁他年幼侵占第戎，直到960年才承认他的公爵地位。965年2月奥东无嗣而终，弟弟亨利继位。

en:
Philip of Burgundy (1323–1346) was the only surviving son and heir of Duke Odo IV of Burgundy and Joan III, Countess of Burgundy. Around 1338 he married Joan I, Countess of Auvergne and Boulogne, and held those counties in her right.

He campaigned with the Duke of Normandy in the Hundred Years' War and in August 1346 died at the siege of Aiguillon after falling from his horse, leaving his infant son Philip to inherit Burgundy.

勃艮第的菲利普（1323—1346）是勃艮第公爵厄德四世与勃艮第女伯爵让娜三世唯一长大成人的儿子和继承人。约1338年，他娶奥弗涅与布洛涅女伯爵让娜一世，以妻子的权利领有这两个伯国。

他随诺曼底公爵参加百年战争，1346年8月在艾吉永围城战中坠马身亡，年幼的儿子菲利普随后继承勃艮第。

en:
Robert I the Old (1011–1076) was the third son of King Robert II of France and Constance of Arles. After rebelling against Henry I in 1031 with his mother's support, he received the Duchy of Burgundy in 1032, founding the ducal House of Burgundy.

His long reign was marked by violence: he plundered Church lands around Autun and Dijon and the abbey of Saint-Germain at Auxerre. In 1048 he repudiated his wife Helie of Semur and killed her father Lord Dalmas with his own hands.

Both his sons, Hugh and Henry, died before him. On his death in 1076 he was therefore succeeded by his grandson Hugh I.

罗贝尔一世“老者”（1011—1076）是法兰西国王罗贝尔二世与阿尔勒的康斯坦丝的第三子。1031年他在母亲支持下起兵反叛国王亨利一世，1032年受封勃艮第公国，由此开创勃艮第公爵支系。

他统治残暴，长期劫掠欧坦和第戎一带的教会地产以及欧塞尔的圣日耳曼修道院。1048年他休弃妻子瑟米尔的埃莉，并亲手杀死岳父达尔马爵士。

他的儿子于格和亨利都先他而死。1076年他去世后，由孙子于格一世继位。

en:
Robert II (1248 – 21 March 1306) was Duke of Burgundy from 1272 and titular King of Thessalonica, succeeding his father Hugh IV. In 1279 he married Agnes, daughter of Louis IX of France; their son Odo IV inherited the duchy.

In 1284 his brother-in-law Rudolf I of Germany invested him with the Dauphiné, but two years of war ended when Philip IV bought his claim. He helped negotiate the 1303 Treaty of Paris ending the Gascon War, and ended the partition of the duchy by imposing primogeniture.

zh:
罗贝尔二世（1248年—1306年3月21日）1272年继父于格四世成为勃艮第公爵，也是名义上的塞萨洛尼卡国王。1279年，他娶法王路易九世之女艾格妮丝，儿子厄德四世后来继承公国。

1284年，他的妹夫德意志国王鲁道夫一世把多菲内封赐给他，随后爆发两年战争，最终腓力四世买下他的宣称，战事方告结束。他参与谈判1303年结束加斯科涅战争的《巴黎条约》，并终止分割公国的做法，确立长子继承制。

Yolande of Dreux (c. 1212–1248) was Duchess of Burgundy as the first wife of Duke Hugh IV. The daughter of Count Robert III of Dreux and Aénor, Lady of Saint-Valery, she married Hugh in 1229.

Her children included Odo, Count of Nevers and Auxerre, and Robert II, later Duke of Burgundy. She died on 30 October 1248 while Hugh was away on crusade in the Holy Land, and was buried at Cîteaux Abbey.

en:
Matthäus an der Gassen (c. 1300–1363) was Prince-Bishop of Brixen from 1336 until his death. Born near Meran into a Tyrolean ministerialis family, he was a Brixen canon when the future Emperor Charles IV arranged his election in November 1336.

In the Luxemburg–Wittelsbach war over Tyrol he trod cautiously, accepting a 1353 treaty that made Brixen part of the County of Tyrol. When Tyrol passed to Rudolf IV in 1363, he went over to the Habsburgs, dying at Brixen on 27 October 1363.

马特乌斯·安·德·加森（约1300—1363）1336年至去世任布里克森采邑主教。他出身梅拉诺附近的蒂罗尔家臣家族，本是布里克森大教堂参事；1336年11月，经后来的皇帝查理四世安排，获主教座堂选举为主教。

卢森堡家族与维特尔斯巴赫家族争夺蒂罗尔期间，他行事审慎，1353年接受条约，使布里克森成为蒂罗尔伯国的一部分。1363年蒂罗尔归属鲁道夫四世后，他转投哈布斯堡家族，同年10月27日在布里克森去世。

en:
Bolesław of Bytom (1330–1355) was a Silesian Piast, Duke of Koźle from 1347 and of Bytom from 1352. The eldest son of Władysław of Bytom, he succeeded his half-brother Casimir at Koźle in 1347 and inherited Bytom on his father's death in 1352.

In 1354 he accompanied King Charles of Bohemia to Rome for the imperial coronation. He died late in 1355, leaving no son, so the Bytom–Koźle Piast line ended with him; Oleśnica and Cieszyn divided his lands in 1357.

比托姆的波列斯瓦夫（1330—1355）是西里西亚皮亚斯特家族公爵，1347年起任科兹莱公爵，1352年起任比托姆公爵。他是比托姆的瓦迪斯瓦夫的长子，1347年继异母兄卡齐米日领有科兹莱，1352年父亲去世后又得到比托姆。

1354年他随波希米亚国王查理前往罗马参加皇帝加冕。1355年末他去世，没有儿子，比托姆—科兹莱一系的皮亚斯特男系就此断绝，其领地于1357年由奥莱希尼察与切申的公爵瓜分。

Casimir of Bytom (1253/1257–1312) was a Silesian Piast, the second son of Duke Władysław of Opole-Racibórz. After their father's death in 1282 he ruled Opole jointly with his brother Bolko I until 1284, when he took Bytom, Koźle and other lands and founded the Bytom line of the Piasts.

In January 1289 he became the first Silesian duke to pay homage at Prague to King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia. In 1306 he married his daughter Maria to Charles Robert of Hungary, and he died on 10 March 1312.

zh:
比托姆的卡齐米日（1253/1257—1312）是西里西亚皮亚斯特家族成员，奥波莱-拉齐布日公爵瓦迪斯瓦夫的次子。1282年父亲死后，他与兄长波尔科一世共同统治奥波莱，直到1284年分家，取得比托姆、科兹莱等地，开创皮亚斯特家族的比托姆支系。

Casimir of Koźle (c. 1312–1347) was Duke of Koźle in Upper Silesia from 1336 until his death. The eldest son of Władysław of Bytom and Beatrix of Brandenburg, he received the district from his father in 1336.

Burdened by heavy debts, he stopped paying Peter's Pence, for which the Church excommunicated him. He died unmarried and childless in 1347, and Koźle passed to his younger brother Bolesław.

en:
Ludgarda of Mecklenburg (c. 1310 – between 1362 and 1369) was Duchess of Bytom and Koźle, wife of the Piast duke Władysław of Bytom. She was probably a daughter of Henry II of Mecklenburg and Anna of Saxe-Wittenberg.

In 1328 she married Władysław, a match likely promoted by King Władysław I Łokietek of Poland, who was then drawing closer to the princes of western Pomerania and Mecklenburg. She bore Władysław five children, among them Bolesław, who succeeded his father in 1352.

Widowed that year, she kept her duchess's title and lived on, respected, in Bytom. She is last recorded alive in 1362 and was dead by 1369.

梅克伦堡的卢德加尔达（约1310年—1362年至1369年间）是比托姆和科兹莱公爵夫人，皮雅斯特公爵比托姆的瓦迪斯瓦夫之妻。她多半是梅克伦堡的海因里希二世与萨克森-维滕贝格的安娜之女。

1328年她嫁给瓦迪斯瓦夫，婚事可能由绰号“矮子”的波兰国王瓦迪斯瓦夫一世促成，当时这位国王正与西波美拉尼亚和梅克伦堡的诸侯走近。她为瓦迪斯瓦夫生下五个子女，其中波列斯瓦夫在1352年继承父亲的爵位。

她同年守寡，保留公爵夫人头衔，在比托姆受人尊敬地度过余生。她最后一次见于记载是1362年，1369年前已去世。

Władysław of Bytom (1277/83–1352) was a Silesian Piast duke who ruled Koźle from 1303 and Bytom from 1316. The second son of Casimir I, he reunited his father's scattered lands, but money troubles forced him to sell Siewierz in 1337 and pledge Koźle to Racibórz.

In 1327 he did homage to King John of Bohemia at Opava, but during the Polish–Bohemian war of 1345–1348 he fought on Poland's side. He died in 1352, leaving Bytom to his son Bolesław.

en:
Alexander (870–913), third son of Basil I, was Byzantine emperor from May 912 after his brother Leo VI's death, ruling jointly with his young nephew Constantine VII. He had been co-emperor since 879.

He dismissed Leo's advisers and shut Constantine's mother Zoe Karbonopsina in a nunnery. He also restored Nicholas Mystikos, the patriarch Leo had removed.

In the east he faced attacks by the Abbasid caliph al-Muqtadir, and by refusing the customary tribute he provoked Simeon I of Bulgaria to war. He died in June 913, reportedly from gluttony and drink, leaving Constantine VII under Nicholas Mystikos's regency amid a Bulgarian invasion.

亚历山大（870—913）是巴西尔一世的第三子，912年5月兄长利奥六世去世后继任拜占庭皇帝，与年幼的侄子君士坦丁七世共治。他自879年起即为共治皇帝。

他斥退利奥六世的近臣，把君士坦丁的生母佐伊·卡波诺普西娜关进修道院，并恢复被利奥罢黜的牧首尼古拉·米斯蒂科斯的职位。

东线他遭到阿拔斯哈里发穆克塔迪尔进攻，又因拒绝按惯例纳贡而招致保加利亚的西美昂一世开战。913年6月他死去，据称死于暴食酗酒，把处于保加利亚入侵威胁下的君士坦丁七世留给尼古拉·米斯蒂科斯摄政。

en:
Severus Alexander (208–235) was Roman emperor from 222, the last of the Severan dynasty and, at thirteen, the empire's youngest sole emperor. A grandson of Julia Maesa, he was adopted by his unpopular cousin Elagabalus; she then arranged Elagabalus's murder, and the guards hailed him that March.

He relied on Maesa until her death in 224, and thereafter on his mother Julia Mamaea, from whom he got the nickname Mamaeas. His senatorial council included the jurist Ulpian, but the praetorians murdered him before Alexander could intervene.

After Ardashir founded the Sassanid dynasty, he checked raids by the Persians in Mesopotamia. When Germanic tribes crossed the Rhine and Danube he camped at Mainz and tried bribing them into peace, enraging soldiers who wanted loot. In March 235 they killed him and Mamaea, probably in a mutiny led by the Thracian officer Maximinus, who took the throne; decades of crisis followed.

亚历山大·塞维鲁（208—235）自222年起为罗马皇帝，是塞维鲁王朝末代皇帝，十三岁登基，为统一帝国最年轻的独自在位皇帝。他是尤利亚·玛伊莎之孙，被表兄、不得人心的埃拉伽巴路斯收为养子；玛伊莎随后策划杀害埃拉伽巴路斯，222年3月禁卫军拥立亚历山大为帝。

224年玛伊莎去世前他倚重祖母，此后倚重母亲尤利亚·玛麦亚，绰号“玛麦亚之子”即由此而来。他的元老顾问团中有法学家乌尔比安，禁卫军却杀死了乌尔比安，亚历山大无力相救。

阿尔达希尔建立萨珊王朝后，亚历山大遏制了波斯人对美索不达米亚的侵扰。日耳曼部落渡过莱茵河和多瑙河时，他驻军美因茨，试图以金钱买和，激怒了想要战利品的士兵。235年3月，士兵杀死他和玛麦亚，兵变大概由色雷斯军官马克西米努斯领导，他随即夺位，此后数十年危机不断。

en:
Alexios Apokaukos (c. 1295–1345) was born humble in Bithynia and rose through the tax offices. He joined John Kantakouzenos in the plot that raised Andronikos III to the throne, and when Andronikos became sole emperor in 1328 he was given charge of state finances.

Early in 1341 he became megas doux, head of the navy, and re-equipped the fleet with his own money. When Andronikos died that year, he turned on his patron and, with Patriarch John XIV Kalekas and the dowager empress Anna of Savoy, led the regency for John V in the civil war of 1341–1347.

As city prefect he championed the townsmen against Kantakouzenos and his aristocrats. In June 1345, inspecting a new prison for his political prisoners without a bodyguard, he was lynched by them. Kantakouzenos entered Constantinople in 1347.

阿历克塞·阿波考寇斯（约1295—1345）出身比提尼亚的卑微之家，以税务官起家。他参与约翰·坎塔库泽努斯的密谋，扶助安德洛尼卡三世上台，1328年安德洛尼卡成为唯一皇帝后，他掌管国家财政。

1341年初他出任大都督，统率海军，并自掏腰包重新装备舰队。同年安德洛尼卡三世死后，他背离恩主，与普世牧首约翰十四世·卡莱卡斯及皇太后萨伏依的安娜共同主持约翰五世的摄政政府，在1341—1347年的内战中对抗坎塔库泽努斯。

他任首都行政长官，成为市民对抗坎塔库泽努斯及其贵族的旗手。1345年6月，他未带卫队便去视察关押政治犯的新监狱，被囚犯私刑处死。1347年坎塔库泽努斯进入君士坦丁堡。

en:
Alexios I Komnenos (c. 1057–1118) was Byzantine emperor from 1081 to 1118 and architect of the Komnenian restoration. A nephew of Isaac I, he seized the throne from Nikephoros III in 1081.

Defeated at first by Robert Guiscard's Normans, he allied with Emperor Henry IV and checked the invasion by 1085. He crushed the Pechenegs at Levounion in 1091 with Cuman help.

In 1095 his envoys appealed to Pope Urban II against the Seljuks, helping trigger the First Crusade and recover much of western Anatolia. He died in 1118, succeeded by his son John II; his daughter Anna Komnene wrote the Alexiad.

阿历克塞一世·科穆宁（约1057—1118）1081至1118年任拜占庭皇帝，是“科穆宁中兴”的缔造者。他是伊萨克一世的侄子，1081年从尼基弗鲁斯三世手中夺取皇位。

他初败于罗贝尔·吉斯卡尔的诺曼人，随后与皇帝亨利四世结盟，到1085年遏制了入侵。1091年他借库曼人之力在莱翁尼翁歼灭佩切涅格人。

1095年他的使节向教皇乌尔班二世求援以对抗塞尔柱人，促成第一次十字军东征，帝国得以收复小亚细亚西部大片土地。1118年他去世，其子约翰二世继位；女儿安娜·科穆宁娜撰写了《阿历克塞传》。

Alexios II Komnenos (1169–1183), the only son of Emperor Manuel I and Maria of Antioch, was born in the purple at Constantinople. He married Agnes, daughter of King Louis VII of France, in March 1180 and succeeded his father that September aged eleven.

His mother and Alexios Komnenos ruled as regents, draining the treasury while Hungary and the Seljuks raided the borders. In 1182 Andronikos Komnenos seized the capital, and in September 1183 he had Alexios strangled with a bowstring and thrown into the Bosporos.

en:
Alexios III Angelos (c. 1153–1211) was Byzantine emperor from 1195 to 1203. His brother Isaac II made him sebastokrator, but in 1195 Alexios seized Isaac, blinded and imprisoned him.

His reign saw lavish gifts that emptied the treasury and plundered imperial tombs for tribute. Turkish and Bulgarian raids went unchecked.

When the Fourth Crusade stormed Constantinople for Alexios IV in July 1203, he fled by night. He blinded Alexios V, fell captive to Boniface of Montferrat, and in 1211 was taken fighting his son-in-law Theodore I Laskaris; he died in a Nicaean monastery.

阿历克塞三世·安格洛斯（约1153—1211）于1195—1203年任拜占庭皇帝。其弟伊萨克二世封他为至尊者，他却在1195年擒获伊萨克，刺瞎双目后囚禁。

他在位时滥施赏赐耗尽国库，为凑贡金甚至盗掘皇陵。突厥人与保加利亚人的侵扰无人遏制。

1203年7月，第四次十字军为拥立阿历克塞四世猛攻君士坦丁堡，他连夜出逃。他刺瞎阿历克塞五世，随后被蒙费拉托的博尼法乔俘获；1211年他与女婿狄奥多尔一世·拉斯卡里斯作战时被擒，最终死于尼西亚的一所修道院。
