提比略二世·君士坦丁（约535—582）出身色雷斯，曾任执盾军统领，是查士丁二世信赖的挚友。574年，精神失常的查士丁收他为养子、立为凯撒。

提比略与索菲亚皇后共同理政；578年9月，弥留之际的查士丁加冕他为奥古斯都，10月4日查士丁去世后他独掌大权。他以慷慨闻名，散发数千磅黄金，并停止迫害基督一性论派。

将领莫里斯深入波斯作战，但582年阿瓦尔人夺取锡尔米乌姆，斯拉夫人涌入巴尔干。临终时，他于582年8月13日立莫里斯为共治皇帝，次日去世。

en:
Tiberius III, born Apsimar, a droungarios in the Cibyrrhaeot Theme, served in the failed expedition sent by Leontius to recover Carthage from the Umayyads in 696. On Crete the mutineers killed their commander John and hailed him emperor; he sailed to Constantinople and deposed Leontius in 698.

He repaired the sea walls, reorganized the naval themes, and let his brother Heraclius raid Cilicia and Syria, winning a victory at Sisium in 704. In 705 Justinian II returned with a Bulgar and Slav army and retook the city. Tiberius was captured in Bithynia and beheaded with Leontius on 15 February 706.

提比略三世本名阿普西玛尔，是基比拉奥特军区的舰队指挥官，696年参加利昂提奥斯收复迦太基的远征，行动失败。退守克里特岛时，哗变官兵杀死指挥官约翰，拥立他为帝；他率舰队驶往君士坦丁堡，于698年推翻利昂提奥斯。

他修复海墙、整顿海军军区，并派弟弟希拉克略深入奇里乞亚与叙利亚袭扰，704年在西西乌姆取胜。705年，查士丁尼二世率保加利亚人与斯拉夫人的军队返回，夺回都城。提比略在比提尼亚被俘，706年2月15日与利昂提奥斯一同被斩首。

en:
Titus (AD 39–81), eldest son of Vespasian, was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 and the first to succeed his father. In 66 the Jews of Judaea rose against Rome, and he joined his father's army there; when the legions proclaimed Vespasian emperor in 69, Titus was left to finish the war.

In 70 he besieged Jerusalem, breached the walls and burned the Second Temple, and his soldiers hailed him imperator. In 71 he rode in triumph through Rome with his father and brother; the Arch of Titus marks the victory. His love for the Jewish queen Berenice shocked Romans, and he sent her away.

Succeeding on 23 June 79, he completed and dedicated the Colosseum and relieved sufferers of the Vesuvius eruption. Suetonius called him ‘the delight and darling of the human race’. He died of fever on 13 September 81, and his brother Domitian succeeded him.

提图斯（39—81）是韦斯巴芗的长子，79年至81年任罗马皇帝，也是第一位继承父亲皇位的罗马皇帝。66年犹太人起义反抗罗马，他随父亲出征；69年军团拥立韦斯巴芗为帝后，提图斯留下来结束这场战争。

70年，他围攻耶路撒冷，攻破城墙后烧毁第二圣殿，士兵们欢呼他为“统帅”。71年，他与父亲、弟弟一同凯旋进入罗马；提图斯凯旋门便是为纪念这场胜利而建。他与犹太女王贝勒尼基的恋情令罗马人震惊，他把她送走。

79年6月23日继位后，他完成并为罗马斗兽场举行落成典礼，还救济了维苏威火山喷发的灾民。苏埃托尼乌斯称他为“人类的宠儿”。他于81年9月13日死于热病，皇位由其弟图密善继承。

en:
Trajan (53–117), born Marcus Ulpius Traianus at Italica in Hispania Baetica, was Roman emperor from 98 to 117 and the second of the Five Good Emperors; the Senate gave him the title optimus princeps, 'the best ruler'. He rose as a general under Domitian, and after a Praetorian revolt the childless Nerva adopted him in 97.

In Rome he expanded the alimenta welfare scheme and built Trajan's Forum and Column. His armies conquered Dacia in 101–106, annexed Nabataea in 106, and after 115 made Armenia, Mesopotamia and Assyria provinces at the expense of Parthia, carrying the empire to its greatest extent.

Taken ill on the voyage home, he died at Selinus shortly before 11 August 117. His cousin Hadrian, whom he had helped to raise as a ward, succeeded him. Tradition places his ashes in a small chamber beneath the Column.

图拉真（53—117）原名马库斯·乌尔皮乌斯·图拉真，生于贝提卡行省的意大利迦，98—117年为罗马皇帝，是五贤帝中的第二位，元老院授予他“最佳元首”的称号。他在图密善治下凭军功升迁，近卫军叛乱后，无嗣的涅尔瓦于97年收他为继承人。

在罗马，他扩大“养育金”福利制度，修建图拉真广场与图拉真纪功柱。他的军队于101—106年征服达契亚，106年吞并纳巴泰，115年后又从帕提亚手中夺取亚美尼亚、美索不达米亚和亚述，设为行省，使帝国版图达到极盛。

归途中他病倒，117年8月11日前不久死于塞利努斯。曾由他参与监护抚养的表亲哈德良继位为帝。依传统，他的骨灰安放在纪功柱下的小室里。

en:
Trebonianus Gallus (c. 206–253), from a senatorial family, was governing Moesia Superior when Decius fell at Abritus in June 251, whereupon his army proclaimed him emperor. He recognized Decius' surviving son Hostilian as co-emperor and bought peace from the Goths with an annual subsidy. When Hostilian died of plague, Gallus made his son Volusian his colleague.

In 253 Shapur I destroyed a Roman army at Barbalissos and sacked Antioch. Aemilianus was proclaimed emperor and marched on Italy. Gallus summoned Valerian with reinforcements, but he did not arrive in time; Gallus and Volusian were killed at Interamna in August 253.

特雷伯尼阿努斯·加卢斯（约206—253）出身元老家族，251年6月正出任上梅西亚总督，德西乌斯在阿伯里图斯阵亡后，他的军队随即拥立他为帝。他承认德西乌斯在世的儿子霍斯蒂利安为共治皇帝，又以每年向哥特人支付补助金为代价换取和约。霍斯蒂利安死于瘟疫后，加卢斯改立自己的儿子沃鲁西安努斯为共治皇帝。

253年，沙普尔一世在巴尔巴利苏斯歼灭一支罗马军队并洗劫安条克。埃米利亚努斯被拥立为帝，进军意大利。加卢斯召瓦勒良率援军前来，却未及抵达；253年8月，加卢斯与沃鲁西安努斯在因特兰纳遇害。

en:
Valens (328–378) ruled the eastern Roman Empire as augustus from 364, when his brother Valentinian I made him co-emperor at Constantinople. He suppressed the usurpation of Procopius in 366 and twice campaigned across the Danube against the Goths, before spending years on the Persian frontier in Armenia.

After he allowed fleeing Goths to cross the Danube in 376, their mismanaged settlement in the Balkans led to war. Valens returned from the east to fight them, but failed to coordinate with his nephew Gratian, the western emperor. At Adrianople on 9 August 378, Valens and much of his army perished.

en:
Valentinian I (321–375), born at Cibalae in Pannonia to an Illyro-Roman military family, rose in rank under Constantius II, Julian and Jovian, and after Jovian's death was proclaimed emperor in February 364. Weeks later he made his brother Valens co-emperor at Constantinople, keeping the Western provinces for himself.

He campaigned successfully against the Alamanni, Quadi and Sarmatians and strengthened the Rhine and Danube frontiers. On 17 November 375, enraged by Quadi envoys at Brigetio, he died of a stroke; his sons Gratian and Valentinian II succeeded him.

瓦伦提尼安一世（321—375）出生于潘诺尼亚的齐巴莱，属伊利里亚—罗马军人家庭，在君士坦提乌斯二世、尤利安与约维安麾下逐级升迁，约维安死后于364年2月被拥立为帝。数周后，他在君士坦丁堡立弟弟瓦伦斯为共治皇帝，自己管辖西部诸行省。

他屡次击败阿勒曼尼人、夸迪人与萨尔马提亚人，加固莱茵河与多瑙河边防。375年11月17日，他在布里格提奥怒斥夸迪使者时中风而死，其子格拉提安与瓦伦提尼安二世继位。

en:
Valerian (c. 199–260 or 264), from a noble senatorial family, was a senior general under Decius and Trebonianus Gallus. In 253 Gallus summoned him against the rebel Aemilianus, but was killed before he arrived; Valerian's soldiers proclaimed him emperor. He at once made his son Gallienus co-emperor, dividing the frontier with his son.

He recovered Antioch from the Persians and in 257–258 issued edicts persecuting the Christians. After plague weakened his army at Edessa, Shapur I of Persia defeated and captured him in 260, the first Roman emperor taken prisoner. He died in Persian captivity.

瓦勒良（约199—260或264）出身显贵的元老家族，在德西乌斯和特雷伯尼阿努斯·加卢斯麾下为大将。253年加卢斯召他讨伐叛将埃米利亚努斯，却在他抵达前被杀，瓦勒良的士兵随即拥立他为帝。他随即立儿子加里恩努斯为共治皇帝，父子分掌东西边防。

en:
Vespasian (AD 9–79) was Roman emperor from 69 to 79, the general who ended the civil war of the Year of the Four Emperors and founded the Flavian dynasty. Born at Falacrinae near Rome to an undistinguished equestrian family, he is said to have earned the nickname muleteer by trading in mules. In 66 he was appointed to crush the Jewish revolt in Judaea.

After Nero's suicide in 68 and the deaths of Galba and Otho, the legions of Egypt and Judaea proclaimed him emperor on 1 July 69. His armies defeated Vitellius that December, and the Senate confirmed him emperor. He rebuilt state finances and began the Flavian Amphitheatre, the Colosseum.

A famous story has him taxing urine collection and telling his son Titus that money has no smell. He died on 23 June 79, and Titus succeeded him, the first Roman emperor followed by his natural son.

韦斯巴芗（9—79）69年至79年任罗马皇帝，结束了四帝之年的内战，开创弗拉维王朝。他生于罗马附近的法拉奎奈，出身并不显赫的骑士阶层，相传靠贩骡得了“骡夫”的绰号。66年他受命镇压犹地亚的犹太人起义。

68年尼禄自杀，伽尔巴和奥托又接连死去，埃及与犹地亚的军团于69年7月1日拥立他称帝。他的军队于当年12月击败维特里乌斯，元老院随即承认他为皇帝。他整顿国家财政，动工兴建弗拉维圆形剧场，即罗马斗兽场。

相传他对收集尿液征税，还对儿子提图斯说钱没有气味。79年6月23日他去世，提图斯继位，是首位由亲生儿子继承的罗马皇帝。

en:
Vitellius (AD 15–69) was Roman emperor for eight months in 69, the third of the four in the Year of the Four Emperors, and the first emperor not born into a senatorial house. In 68 Galba sent him to command the army of Germania Inferior, and he won over the soldiers. In January 69 the Rhine legions refused to swear loyalty to Galba and acclaimed him.

His generals marched on Italy and beat Otho at the first Battle of Bedriacum on 14 April, after which Otho killed himself. He let his troops riot in Rome, while the sources accuse him of gluttony and cruelty.

The eastern legions declared for Vespasian, and Antonius Primus crushed Vitellius at the second Battle of Bedriacum. Vespasian's troops fought their way into Rome, and Vitellius was dragged from hiding and killed on the Gemonian stairs on 20 December 69. Vespasian founded the Flavian dynasty.

维特里乌斯（15—69）于69年在位八个月，是“四帝之年”中相继称帝的四人里的第三位，是第一位并非生于元老世家的皇帝。68年加尔巴任命他统帅下日耳曼尼亚军队，他赢得了士兵的拥戴。69年1月，莱茵军团拒绝向加尔巴宣誓效忠，拥戴他称帝。

东方军团拥立韦斯巴芗，安东尼·普里姆斯在第二次贝德里亚库姆战役中击溃维特里乌斯。韦斯巴芗的军队杀入罗马，维特里乌斯被人从藏身处拖出，69年12月20日死在盖莫尼亚阶梯上，韦斯巴芗由此开创弗拉维王朝。

en:
Zeno (c. 425–491), born Tarasicodissa in Isauria, was Eastern Roman emperor in 474–475 and again from 476. In 466 he married Leo I's daughter Ariadne; their son Leo II made him emperor but died within months. Driven out by Basiliscus in 475, he retook Constantinople in 476 after the general Illus defected.

Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus, sending the Western regalia to Zeno and gaining recognition in Italy. Zeno directed Theodoric the Great against Odoacer, and his 482 Henotikon failed to heal the Chalcedonian rift, provoking the Acacian schism. He died in April 491; Ariadne then chose Anastasius I.

芝诺（约425—491）是东罗马帝国皇帝，474年至475年首次在位，476年复辟。他生于伊苏利亚，原名塔拉西科迪萨，466年娶利奥一世之女阿里阿德涅；二人之子利奥二世使他成为皇帝，但孩子数月后夭折。475年他被巴西利斯库斯逐走，476年因将领伊卢斯倒戈而收复君士坦丁堡。

同年奥多亚塞废黜罗慕路斯·奥古斯图卢斯，把西罗马帝徽送往芝诺处，芝诺则承认其在意大利的统治。他派狄奥多里克大王前去对付奥多亚塞；482年颁布的《合一诏书》未能平息迦克墩派争端，反而引发阿卡西乌分裂。491年4月他去世，阿里阿德涅选定阿纳斯塔修斯一世继位。

en:
Zoe Porphyrogenita (c. 978–1050) was a Macedonian-dynasty Byzantine empress, the second daughter of Constantine VIII. She spent decades confined to the palace women's quarters until 1028, when her dying father married her to Romanos III Argyros. When Romanos was found dead in his bath in 1034, she wed Michael IV the same day.

Michael V, whom she had adopted, later exiled her. A popular rising against him in 1042 placed Zoe and her sister Theodora on the throne as joint empresses; two months later she married Constantine IX Monomachos and remained Augusta until her death.

en:
Cesare Borgia (1475–1507) was the illegitimate son of Cardinal Rodrigo Borgia, later Pope Alexander VI. Made archbishop of Valencia in 1492 and cardinal in 1493, he resigned in 1498 after his brother's murder and became Duke of Valentinois under Louis XII of France.

Commanding papal armies, he became Duke of Romagna in 1501 and seized Urbino in 1502 before executing his condottieri at Senigallia. His father's death in 1503 exposed him to Pope Julius II; imprisoned in Spain, he escaped to Navarre and was killed at Viana in 1507. His career inspired Machiavelli's The Prince.

切萨雷·波吉亚（1475—1507）是枢机罗德里戈·波吉亚（后来的教宗亚历山大六世）的私生子。他1492年出任瓦伦西亚大主教，1493年升为枢机，1498年在兄长遇刺后辞职，被法王路易十二封为瓦伦蒂诺公爵。

他统率教皇军队，1501年受封罗马涅公爵，1502年用计夺取乌尔比诺，随后在塞尼加利亚处死谋反的雇佣军首领。1503年父亲去世后，他失势于教宗儒略二世，被囚于西班牙，后逃到纳瓦拉，1507年在比亚纳被杀。他的经历启发了马基雅维利写作《君主论》。

en:
Guy de Lévis de Ventadour (c. 1302–1352) was a French prelate from a family rich in bishops. He became bishop of Cambrai in 1342 and found a diocese in crisis, where many priests ignored the duty to reside in their parishes and left poorly trained substitutes, called deservitors, in their place.

In 1345 he issued a statute ordering the deservitors to present themselves to him on pain of excommunication, and allowing priests to leave their parishes only with his permission. The reform did not last.

Transferred to the see of Vabres in 1349, he soon saw the Cambrai chapter undo his measures. He remained bishop of Vabres until his death in 1352.

居伊·德·勒维·德·旺塔杜尔（约1302—1352）是法国高级教士，出自一个多出主教的家族。1342年他出任康布雷主教，接手的教区陷入危机：许多神父不履行驻堂义务，把教务交给被称为“代牧”的训练不足者顶替。

1345年他颁布规章，勒令代牧到主教面前报到，违者处以绝罚，神父离开教区须获主教许可。这些改革没能持久。

1349年他调任瓦布尔主教，康布雷教士团很快废除了他的措施。他一直担任瓦布尔主教，直至1352年去世。

en:
Guillaume d'Avesnes (1254–1296) was a French prelate and bishop of Cambrai, a son of John I of Avesnes, Count of Hainaut. Provost of Cambrai when he was elected bishop in 1286, he quarrelled bitterly with his cathedral chapter, which was at war with his brother John II, Count of Hainaut.

In 1288 Guillaume disputed the village of Blarignies with John, and the count recovered the village. In 1291 he helped John put down the townsmen's revolt at Valenciennes. He died in 1296 while journeying to Jerusalem.

纪尧姆·德·阿韦讷（1254—1296）是法国高级教士、康布雷主教，为埃诺伯爵约翰一世·德·阿韦讷之子。1286年他以康布雷教务长的身份当选主教，与主教座堂教士团关系恶劣，教士团当时正与他的兄长、埃诺伯爵约翰二世交战。

1288年，纪尧姆因布拉里尼村与约翰发生争执，伯爵最终收回了村庄。1291年，他协助约翰镇压了瓦朗谢讷市民的起义。1296年，他在前往耶路撒冷的途中去世。

en:
William II d'Auxonne was a French prelate born at Avesnes. A canon of Paris, he was made bishop of Cambrai in 1336, taking over a border city that both Edward III and Philip VI wanted once the Hundred Years' War began. He sided with France.

Edward's siege failed in 1339, but his army devastated the Cambrésis on its retreat and left a garrison whose raids drove the citizens to appeal to the Duke of Normandy. William secured papal intervention, and in January 1339 Pope Benedict XII annulled the proceedings Edward had begun against him.

Leaving the ravaged Cambrésis, William moved to the see of Autun in August 1342. He helped found the Collège de Cambrai in Paris with two other prelates, and died at Autun on 30 March 1344 or 1345.

纪尧姆二世·多克松是14世纪的法国高级教士，生于阿韦讷。他本是巴黎教堂的咏礼司铎，1336年出任康布雷主教，接手的是一座百年战争爆发后英王爱德华三世与法王腓力六世都想夺取的边境城市。他倒向法国。

1339年爱德华攻城不克，撤军时蹂躏了康布雷西斯，留下驻军，其劫掠逼得康布雷居民向诺曼底公爵求援。纪尧姆争取教宗干预，1339年1月教宗本笃十二世下诏撤销爱德华对他提起的诉讼。

1342年8月，他离开残破的康布雷西斯，改任欧坦主教。他还与另外两位高级教士在巴黎创办了康布雷学院，1344或1345年3月30日卒于欧坦。

en:
Jules Mazarin, born Giulio Mazzarino (1602–1661), was an Italian cardinal who ruled France as chief minister to Louis XIII and Louis XIV. He entered Richelieu's service in 1640, became a cardinal in 1641 and succeeded him as first minister in 1642, governing for Regent Anne of Austria from 1643.

His ministry saw victory in the Thirty Years' War and the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, then the Fronde revolt led by his former ally Condé; Mazarin fled Paris, returning in 1653 after Turenne's victory. The Treaty of the Pyrenees followed in 1659, adding three provinces, and in 1660 arranged Louis XIV's marriage to Maria Theresa of Spain.

He brought Italian opera to Paris and founded France's first public library, the Bibliothèque Mazarine. Told he had two months to live, he answered, ‘That's enough.’ He died at Vincennes in 1661, leaving the bequest that founded the Collège des Quatre-Nations.

儒勒·马萨林，本名朱利奥·马扎里诺（1602—1661），意大利籍枢机，以首席大臣执掌路易十三与路易十四治下的法国。他1640年投入黎塞留门下，1641年升枢机，1642年接任首席大臣，1643年起辅佐摄政奥地利的安妮。

他执政初期促成三十年战争胜利与1648年《威斯特伐利亚和约》。同年投石党运动爆发，后期由旧盟友孔代亲王领导；马萨林逃离巴黎，1653年蒂雷纳获胜后才返回。1659年《比利牛斯条约》为法国增添三省，1660年安排路易十四迎娶西班牙的玛丽亚·特蕾莎。

他将意大利歌剧引入巴黎，创办法国首座公共图书馆马萨林图书馆。医生告知只剩两月时，答：“够了。”1661年卒于万塞讷，遗赠创办四国学院。

en:
Armand Jean du Plessis, Cardinal Richelieu (1585–1642), was the French statesman who ruled France as chief minister of Louis XIII. Born in Paris into the lesser nobility of Poitou, a sickly child who lost his father at five, he became Bishop of Luçon in 1607.

Named chief minister in 1624, he set out to make the crown supreme: he curbed the great nobles and broke Huguenot power at the siege of La Rochelle (1627–1628), leaving them freedom of worship. He survived the Day of the Dupes in 1630, and in 1635 brought France into the Thirty Years' War against the Habsburgs.

His Capuchin confidant Father Joseph was nicknamed the Grey Eminence. He founded the Académie Française in 1635 and ran a network of spies and censorship. He died in Paris on 4 December 1642 and Mazarin took his place; Louis XIV later built absolute monarchy on his work.

阿尔芒·让·迪普莱西，即红衣主教黎塞留（1585—1642），是法国政治家，以路易十三首席大臣身份执掌朝政。他生于巴黎，出身普瓦图小贵族，自幼体弱，五岁丧父，1607年成为吕松主教。

1624年他出任首席大臣，一心抬高王权：压制大贵族，通过1627至1628年的拉罗谢尔围城战摧毁胡格诺派的政治势力，只留给他们信仰自由。1630年愚人日危机中他保住权位，1635年推动法国加入三十年战争、对抗哈布斯堡家族。

其心腹嘉布遣会士约瑟夫神父人称“灰衣主教”。他1635年创立法兰西学院，并布下密探网络、检查出版物。1642年12月4日他在巴黎去世，马萨林接掌其位；路易十四后来在他打下的基础上建成绝对君主制。

Alfonso de la Cerda, called the Disinherited (1270–1333), was the elder son of Ferdinand de la Cerda, heir of Alfonso X. When his father died in 1275 his uncle Sancho IV seized the succession. Taken to Aragon by his grandmother Violant, he was kept in the fortress of Xàtiva for thirteen years.

Proclaimed king by Alfonso III of Aragon in 1288, he struggled in vain for the crown. Under the 1304 Treaty of Torrellas he gave up his claim to León in return for scattered possessions.

Charles IV of France later made him Baron of Lunel. He swore fealty to Alfonso XI in 1331 and died at Ávila in 1333.

阿方索·德·拉·塞尔达，绰号“被废嗣者”（1270—1333），是阿方索十世的继承人费尔南多·德·拉·塞尔达的长子。1275年父亲死后，他的王位继承权被叔父桑乔四世夺走。祖母维奥兰特把他带往阿拉贡，他在哈蒂瓦城堡被看管了十三年。

1288年他被阿拉贡国王阿方索三世拥立为国王，此后为夺回王位徒劳征战。依照1304年《托雷利亚斯条约》，他放弃莱昂王位主张，换得若干分散的领地。

后来法王查理四世封他为吕内尔男爵。1331年他向阿方索十一世宣誓效忠，1333年卒于阿维拉。

en:
Alfonso of Molina (1202–1272) was an infante of León, son of Alfonso IX and younger brother of Ferdinand III. In 1230 he waived his claim to León in favour of Ferdinand.

He fought for his brother in the Reconquista, helping take Córdoba in 1236 and Seville in 1248, where he seized the Torre de Oro. Through his marriage to Mafalda González de Lara he became lord of Molina in 1243; his daughter María de Molina married Sancho IV. He died in 1272.

en:
Alfonso VII, called the Emperor (1105–1157), was the son of Queen Urraca of León and Raymond of Burgundy, and the first king of the Castilian House of Burgundy. He succeeded Urraca in León and Castile in 1126.

In 1135 he was crowned Emperor of All Spain in León Cathedral, asserting his claim to authority across the peninsula. He took Almería in 1147, though Portugal's independence was recognized at Zamora in 1143.

In 1151 he agreed with Ramon Berenguer IV on their zones of conquest. He died in 1157 returning from an expedition against the Almohads, leaving Castile to Sancho III and León to Ferdinand II.

zh:
阿方索七世，人称“皇帝”（1105—1157），是莱昂女王乌拉卡与勃艮第的雷蒙之子，也是卡斯蒂利亚勃艮第王朝的开国君主。1126年他继承母亲的莱昂与卡斯蒂利亚王位。

1135年，他在莱昂大教堂加冕为“全西班牙皇帝”，宣示对整个半岛的权威。他于1147年攻取阿尔梅里亚，但葡萄牙的独立也在1143年的《萨莫拉条约》中得到承认。

1151年，他与拉蒙·贝伦格尔四世划定各自的征服区域。1157年他在征讨穆瓦希德人的归途中去世，卡斯蒂利亚传给桑乔三世，莱昂传给斐迪南二世。

en:
Alfonso VIII, called the Noble (1155–1214), became king of Castile at the age of two in 1158; during his minority his uncle Sancho VI of Navarre seized much of La Rioja. In 1170 he married Eleanor of England. In 1176 Henry II arbitrated the disputed Navarrese border, and Alfonso recovered much of the lost territory.

After defeat by the Almohads at Alarcos in 1195, he led the Christian coalition that broke Almohad power at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212, turning the tide of the Reconquista. He founded Spain's first university at Palencia and was succeeded by his young son Henry I.

en:
Alfonso X, called the Wise (1221–1284), ruled Castile, León and Galicia from 1252. In the 1240s he helped his father conquer Muslim strongholds including Murcia. Through his Hohenstaufen mother he claimed the German crown and was elected king of the Romans in 1257, though he never went to Germany and abandoned the claim in 1275.

A patron of learning, he sponsored the astronomical Alfonsine Tables, introduced the vernacular law code Siete Partidas, and founded the Mesta sheep-owners' guild. His later reign was torn by civil war with his son Sancho, who succeeded him as Sancho IV.

en:
Alfonso XI (1311–1350), called the Avenger, was king of Castile and León. Born at Salamanca to Ferdinand IV, he inherited the throne as an infant in 1312, while regents and nobles divided a kingdom the Moors raided. The Vega disaster of 1319 killed two regents; the last, his grandmother María de Molina, died in 1321.

Declared of age at the Cortes of Valladolid in 1325, he set about breaking the nobles; in 1326 he lured Juan the One-eyed to Toro and had him killed. His victory over the Marinid invasion at Río Salado in 1340 and the conquest of Algeciras in 1344 carried Castile to the Strait of Gibraltar.

He neglected Maria of Portugal for Eleanor of Guzmán, who bore him ten children, including the future Henry II. He died of plague besieging Gibraltar in 1350, and Granada's Yusuf I spared his funeral procession. His son Peter succeeded him.

阿方索十一世（1311—1350），绰号“复仇者”，是卡斯蒂利亚与莱昂国王。他生于萨拉曼卡，为斐迪南四世之子，1312年襁褓中即位，摄政者和贵族在摩尔人劫掠中瓜分王国。1319年韦加惨败，两位摄政战死；最后一位摄政、祖母玛丽亚·德·莫利纳于1321年去世。

1325年他在巴利亚多利德议会被宣布成年，随即着手压制贵族；1326年他把“独眼”胡安诱至托罗杀害。1340年，他在里奥萨拉多击败马林王朝的入侵，1344年攻克阿尔赫西拉斯，把卡斯蒂利亚的疆界推到直布罗陀海峡。

他冷落王后葡萄牙的玛丽亚，宠爱埃莉诺·德·古斯曼，后者为他生了十个子女，其中就有日后的恩里克二世。1350年他在围攻直布罗陀时染鼠疫去世，格拉纳达的优素福一世下令不得袭击送葬队伍。其子佩德罗继位。

en:
Gabriel Alonso de Herrera (1470–1539) was a Spanish agronomist and cleric, born at Talavera de la Reina, who became chaplain to Cardinal Cisneros. After studying in Granada, where he ran praised market gardens as early as 1502, he travelled through Italy and France gathering agricultural knowledge.

Commissioned by Cisneros, his Obra de Agricultura was printed at Alcalá de Henares in 1513, blending classical authorities such as Columella and Palladius with Muslim farming practices he had learned in Granada. It covered crops, livestock, veterinary medicine and weather, ran through many editions and remained a standard handbook into the twentieth century.

加夫列尔·阿隆索·德·埃雷拉（1470—1539）是西班牙农学家、教士，生于塔拉韦拉·德拉雷纳，后来成为西斯内罗斯枢机的小堂神父。他在格拉纳达求学，1502年便因经营的菜园广受赞誉，此后游历意大利和法国搜集农耕知识。

en:
Asher ben Jehiel (c. 1250–1327), known by the Hebrew acronym Rosh, was a German-born Talmudist who became rabbi of Toledo. He studied under Meir of Rothenburg; after Meir was imprisoned in 1286 Asher raised the ransom he refused and succeeded him in Worms.

Driven into exile by official extortion, he settled in Toledo. His concise abstract of Talmudic law became a cornerstone of halakhah; his son Jacob wrote the Arba'ah Turim. Opposed to Greek philosophy, Asher died in poverty in 1327.

亚设·本·耶希埃尔（约1250—1327）是生于德意志的塔木德学者，后来出任托莱多拉比，常以希伯来语缩写‘罗什’为人所知。他师从罗滕堡的迈尔；1286年迈尔被囚后，他筹措赎金却被恩师拒绝，随后接任其沃尔姆斯的拉比之职。

en:
Martín de Azpilcueta (1492–1586), called Doctor Navarrus, was a Navarrese canonist, theologian and economist, born at Barásoain into a noble family. After studies at Alcalá and Toulouse, he held canon-law chairs at Salamanca from 1524 and taught at Coimbra from 1538 to 1555.

With Francisco de Vitoria and Domingo de Soto he was a leading light of the School of Salamanca, and in 1556 he first formulated the quantity theory of money. Philip II entrusted him with the defence of Archbishop Bartolomé Carranza before the Inquisition, and he ended his years in Rome as counsellor of the Apostolic Penitentiary under Pope Pius V.

马丁·德·阿斯皮利奎塔（1492—1586），人称“纳瓦鲁斯博士”，是纳瓦拉的教会法学家、神学家和经济学家，生于巴拉斯奥因的贵族家庭。他在阿尔卡拉和图卢兹求学后，自1524年起在萨拉曼卡担任教会法教席，1538至1555年在科英布拉任教。

他与维多利亚、索托同为萨拉曼卡学派的核心人物，1556年率先提出货币数量论。腓力二世委托他为宗教裁判所面前的巴托洛梅·卡兰萨大主教辩护，他晚年居留罗马，被教皇庇护五世任命为使徒忏悔院顾问。

Domingo Báñez (1528–1604) was a Dominican theologian of the later School of Salamanca and its foremost defender of strict Thomism. Born at Valladolid, he entered the Dominicans at Salamanca in 1547, studied under Melchor Cano, and in 1581 became its first professor of theology. He was confessor to Teresa of Ávila.

In 1582 a public disputation with a Jesuit grew into a debate over free will and predestination. In 1588 he censured the Jesuit Luis de Molina's Concordia on grace and free will, and led the Dominicans until it reached Rome's Congregation of Auxiliis. He died at Medina del Campo.

en:
Elisabeth of Swabia, known in Castile as Beatrice (1205–1235), was a Hohenstaufen princess, daughter of the German king Philip of Swabia and Irene Angelina. After her father's murder and her mother's death in 1208, she came under the guardianship of her cousin Frederick, who arranged her marriage to Ferdinand III of Castile in 1219. She became queen of Castile and, in 1230, of León.

She bore ten children, including Alfonso X the Wise and Manuel. She died in 1235, probably in childbirth; first buried at Las Huelgas, she was later moved by Alfonso X to Seville Cathedral.

Berengaria (1179 or 1180—1246), called the Great, was the eldest daughter of Alfonso VIII and Eleanor of England. Betrothed to Conrad of Swabia, she married her cousin Alfonso IX of León in 1197; Pope Innocent III annulled the union after five children, including the future Ferdinand III. She served as regent for her young brother Henry I after their father's death.

When Henry died in 1217, she succeeded as queen of Castile but within months abdicated in favor of her son. In 1230 she secured his accession to León, reuniting Castile and León, and remained his chief counselor until her death.

en:
Pedro Berruguete (c. 1450–c. 1504) was a Castilian painter, born at Paredes de Nava near Palencia, whose work bridges the Gothic and Renaissance styles in Spain. Around 1480 he is thought to have worked in Urbino for Duke Federico da Montefeltro, absorbing Italian Renaissance forms and Flemish technique.

Back in Castile by 1483, he painted in Toledo and Ávila, producing altarpieces and scenes of the early Inquisition for churches such as Santo Tomás in Ávila, and may have established a studio there in the 1490s. Called the first Renaissance painter of Spain, he was the father of sculptor Alonso Berruguete.

Blanca de la Cerda (1311–1347), also Blanca Núñez de Lara, was a Castilian noblewoman, daughter of Fernando de la Cerda and Juana Núñez de Lara, la Palomilla. Through her father she was great-granddaughter of Alfonso X and descendant of Louis IX, and in January 1329 she became the third wife of Juan Manuel, Prince of Villena, author of El conde Lucanor.

Their son Fernando Manuel de Villena, born in 1332, inherited Escalona, Peñafiel and Villena and served as adelantado mayor of Murcia. Their daughter Juana Manuel married Henry II in 1350 and became Castile's queen.

en:
Blanche of France (1253–c. 1320) was a daughter of Louis IX of France and Margaret of Provence, born at Jaffa during her father's Seventh Crusade. In 1268 she married Ferdinand de la Cerda, heir of Alfonso X of Castile, and bore him two sons, Alfonso and Ferdinand. After Ferdinand died in 1275, her sons were displaced in the succession and exiled.

The dispute drew in France: her brother Philip III launched an expedition in 1276, but his army turned back before crossing the Pyrenees. Blanche returned to France and later instigated a biography of Saint Louis. She retired near a convent in Paris, where she died around 1320.

法兰西的布朗什（1253—约1320）是法兰西国王路易九世与普罗旺斯的玛格丽特之女，在父亲发动第七次十字军东征期间生于雅法。1268年，她嫁给卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索十世的继承人费尔南多·德·拉·塞尔达，生有阿方索、费尔南多二子。1275年丈夫去世后，她的儿子被剥夺继承权并流亡。

继承争端引来法兰西介入：她的兄长腓力三世于1276年发动远征，但法军未越过比利牛斯山便折返。布朗什返回法兰西，晚年推动撰写圣路易传记。她隐居在巴黎一座修道院附近，约1320年在巴黎去世。

Melchor Cano (c. 1509–1560) was a Dominican theologian and a central figure of the School of Salamanca. Born at Tarancón, he entered the Salamanca Dominicans in 1523 as a pupil of Francisco de Vitoria and succeeded Vitoria in the chair of theology at Salamanca.

His rivalry with fellow Dominican Bartolomé Carranza divided the university, and Cano took part in his condemnation for heresy. At the Council of Trent he debated the Eucharist and indulgences. In 1552 his Jesuit opponents had him made bishop of the Canary Islands to remove him from Spain; he resigned a year later. His De locis theologicis appeared posthumously in 1563.

梅尔希奥·卡诺（约1509—1560）是多明我会神学家、萨拉曼卡学派的核心人物。他生于塔兰孔，1523年在萨拉曼卡进入多明我会，师从弗朗西斯科·德·维多利亚，后来接替维多利亚出任萨拉曼卡神学教授。

他与同会的巴托洛梅·卡兰萨彼此争斗，使大学分成两派，还参与了对卡兰萨的异端定罪。特伦托公会议上，他参与圣体与赎罪券之争。1552年，敌对的耶稣会士推他出任加那利群岛主教，把他排挤出西班牙，一年后他便辞职。其《神学论题》于1563年在他身后出版。

Francisco Jiménez de Cisneros (1436–1517) was a Franciscan friar who became Queen Isabella I's confessor in 1492 and Archbishop of Toledo in 1495, the richest see in Spain. He reformed the religious orders, founded the University of Alcalá in 1499, and financed the Complutensian Polyglot Bible.

Made cardinal and Grand Inquisitor in 1507, he led the 1509 conquest of Oran in North Africa. He twice governed Castile as regent, in 1506–1507 and after Ferdinand II's death in 1516, and died at Roa in November 1517 as Charles I arrived from Flanders.

弗朗西斯科·希梅内斯·德·西斯内罗斯（1436—1517）原为方济各会修士，1492年成为卡斯蒂利亚女王伊莎贝拉一世的忏悔神父，1495年出任西班牙最富庶的托莱多总教区总主教。他改革各修会，1499年创办阿尔卡拉大学，并出资刊印《康普鲁顿合参本圣经》。

1507年他成为枢机兼宗教裁判所大裁判长，1509年亲自领军远征北非、攻取奥兰。他两度以摄政身份治理卡斯蒂利亚：1506—1507年，以及1516年斐迪南二世去世之后；1517年11月查理一世从佛兰德抵达之际，他在罗阿病逝。

Pedro González de Mendoza (1428–1495), fifth son of Castile's powerful Mendoza house, was a cardinal, statesman and soldier. He studied civil and canon law at Salamanca and became bishop of Calahorra in 1453 and of Sigüenza in 1468.

In 1473 he became cardinal and chancellor of Castile. Backing Isabella, he fought at Toro in 1476 and became archbishop of Toledo and Primate of Spain in 1482. For twenty years he led the royal council and funded the Granada war, entering Granada in 1492; his sway over the Catholic Monarchs earned him the name the Third King. He died at Guadalajara in 1495.

佩德罗·冈萨雷斯·德·门多萨（1428—1495）是卡斯蒂利亚权门门多萨家族的第五子，集枢机主教、政治家与军人于一身。他在萨拉曼卡学习民法与教会法，1453年任卡拉奥拉主教，1468年任锡古恩萨主教。

1473年他成为枢机主教兼卡斯蒂利亚首相。他支持伊莎贝拉，1476年参加托罗战役，1482年出任托莱多大主教、西班牙首主教。他主持御前会议长达二十年，资助格拉纳达战争并于1492年进入攻陷的格拉纳达城。他在天主教双王朝中权势极盛，被称为“第三位国王”，1495年卒于瓜达拉哈拉。

Constance of Portugal (1290–1313) was queen of Castile and León as the wife of Ferdinand IV. Eldest child of Denis of Portugal and Elizabeth of Aragon, she married Ferdinand at Valladolid in January 1302.

Her children included Eleanor, later queen of Aragon, and Alfonso XI, born in 1311. When Ferdinand died at Jaén in September 1312, she escorted his body to Córdoba for burial amid regency quarrels over her infant son. She died at Sahagún in November 1313, aged twenty-three.

Constanza Manuel (c. 1318–1345/1349) was the daughter of the Castilian magnate and writer Juan Manuel and Constance of Aragon. In 1325 her father wedded her to Alfonso XI, who repudiated her in 1327 to marry Maria of Portugal.

Betrothed in 1335 to the Portuguese heir Pedro, she was imprisoned by Alfonso in Toro to block the match; the proxy wedding nonetheless took place at Évora on 28 February 1336. Once in Portugal, she bore Pedro a daughter, Maria, in 1342, and the future Ferdinand I in 1345, before dying in childbirth.

Hernán Cortés (c. 1485–1547) was the Spanish conquistador who overthrew the Aztec Empire. Born at Medellín in Extremadura, he sailed for Hispaniola in 1504 and joined Velázquez in Cuba. Appointed to lead an expedition to Mexico in 1518, he sailed in 1519 after Velázquez revoked his commission.

His men took Veracruz and he scuttled his ships to end thought of retreat. With interpreter Doña Marina and native allies he marched inland; Moctezuma II received him at Tenochtitlan in November 1519 and was taken hostage. A massacre sparked revolt, and after Moctezuma died in July 1520 the Spaniards fled in the Noche Triste.

Cortés rebuilt his force and besieged the city until Cuauhtémoc was captured in August 1521. In 1529 Charles V made him Marquis of Oaxaca but never restored him as governor. He explored Baja California and died in debt in 1547; his son Martín inherited the title.

埃尔南·科尔特斯（约1485—1547）是推翻阿兹特克帝国的西班牙征服者。生于埃斯特雷马杜拉的麦德林，1504年赴伊斯帕尼奥拉岛，后在古巴投奔贝拉斯克斯。1518年受命率墨西哥远征队，贝拉斯克斯撤销委任后仍于1519年出航。

部下接管韦拉克鲁斯后，他凿船断念，带译员堂娜·玛琳娜联合土著盟友进军，1519年11月在特诺奇蒂特兰受蒙特祖马二世接见，将其扣为人质。一场西班牙人制造的屠杀引发暴动，1520年7月蒙特祖马死后，西班牙人在“悲痛之夜”出逃。

科尔特斯重整兵力围城，1521年8月擒获库奥特莫克。1529年查理五世封他瓦哈卡侯爵，未恢复其总督职。后探索下加利福尼亚，1547年负债而死，子马丁袭爵。

Diego de Covarrubias y Leyva (1512–1577) was a jurist and prelate of the School of Salamanca, born in Toledo. He studied under Azpilcueta, Vitoria and Soto, and at twenty-one held a canon-law chair at Salamanca, where he was hailed as the Bartolus of Spain.

As bishop of Ciudad Rodrigo from 1560, he attended the Council of Trent and drafted its decrees on reform. He became bishop of Segovia in 1564 and president of the Council of Castile in 1572, and died in Madrid in 1577 shortly after nomination as bishop of Cuenca.

迭戈·德·科瓦鲁维亚斯（1512—1577）是萨拉曼卡学派的法学家与高级教士，生于托莱多。他师从阿斯皮利奎塔、维多利亚和索托，二十一岁便在萨拉曼卡担任教会法教席，时人称他为“西班牙的巴尔多鲁”。

Juan de Herrera (1530–1597) was a Spanish architect, mathematician and geometrician, and the foremost architect of the Spanish Renaissance under Philip II. After serving Charles V on campaign, he turned to architecture and from 1563 worked under Juan Bautista de Toledo at El Escorial. On Toledo's death in 1567 he took charge of the works, building the western façade and central basilica.

He gave the monastery-palace its sober granite façades and saw it completed in 1584. His austere manner became known as the Herrerian style.

Juan de la Cosa (c. 1450–1510) was a Castilian navigator and cartographer from Santoña. He owned and sailed the Santa María, Columbus's flagship on the first voyage of 1492. In 1499 he was chief pilot with Alonso de Ojeda on the South American coast, and around 1500 he drew the earliest surviving European world map showing the New World.

He later joined Rodrigo de Bastidas's voyage. In 1509 he returned with Ojeda to Colombia and was killed by poison arrows near Cartagena in February 1510.

Garcilaso de la Vega (c. 1501–1536) was a Toledo-born soldier and poet, the son of a courtier of the Catholic Monarchs. He entered Charles V's guard in 1520 and fought in the emperor's campaigns in Italy, Tunis and France. In 1532 he was briefly exiled to an island in the Danube, and in 1536 he died at Nice of a wound received at Le Muy in Provence.

He naturalized Italian Renaissance verse forms in Castilian through his sonnets and eclogues. His friend Juan Boscán published his poetry posthumously in 1543.

Luis de León (1527–1591) was an Augustinian friar, theologian and lyric poet of the School of Salamanca. He entered the Augustinians as a youth and from 1561 held theology chairs at Salamanca, where his Spanish version of the Song of Songs angered Dominican rivals.

In 1572 the Inquisition imprisoned him at Valladolid; acquitted in 1576, he returned to his lecture hall and, as tradition has it, began: ‘As I was saying the other day…’

His treatise The Names of Christ appeared from 1583, and in 1588 he published the first collected edition of Teresa of Ávila's writings. He died in 1591.

Bartolomé de Medina was a Spanish Dominican theologian of the School of Salamanca. Born at Medina de Rioseco in 1527, he joined the Dominicans and studied at Salamanca under Francisco de Vitoria and Domingo de Soto. He spent most of his teaching career there, winning its principal chair of theology.

His theological writings were chiefly commentaries on Aquinas's Summa Theologica, in which he formulated probabilism, which permits following a solidly probable opinion even when the contrary seems more probable. He died at Salamanca around 1580.

Domingo de Soto (1494–1560) was a Dominican theologian born in Segovia and a founder of the School of Salamanca. He joined the Dominicans at Burgos in 1524 and took a theology chair at Salamanca in 1532. Charles V sent him as imperial theologian to the Council of Trent, where he defended Catholic tradition on original sin and justification.

At the Valladolid debate of 1550 he condemned the enslavement of Native Americans against Sepúlveda. His De iustitia et iure (1553) shaped later theories of international law.

en:
Francisco de Vitoria (c. 1483–1546) was a Dominican theologian and jurist, born in Burgos, who founded the School of Salamanca. Educated in Paris, he held Salamanca's prima chair of theology from 1524 until his death.

His posthumous Relectiones Theologicae, above all De Indis and De iure belli of 1539, argued that the American peoples were true owners of their lands and could be fought only under strict just-war conditions.

His theory of the law of nations earned him the title father of international law. He published nothing himself and died at Salamanca in 1546.

Juan Sebastián Elcano (c. 1486–1526) was a Basque sailor from Getaria who completed the first circumnavigation of the globe. He joined Magellan's expedition in 1519, and after Magellan was killed in the Philippines in April 1521 the crew elected him captain. Elcano chose to sail west across the Indian Ocean, and brought the sole surviving ship, the Victoria, home to Sanlúcar de Barrameda in September 1522.

Charles V granted him a globe crest with the motto Primus circumdedisti me. In 1525 he sailed as chief pilot of the Loaísa expedition and died of scurvy in the Pacific in 1526.

en:
Henry II of Castile (1334–1379), called the Fratricidal, was an illegitimate son of Alfonso XI and Leonor de Guzmán. His father made him Count of Trastámara, and favour shown to Leonor's sons angered María of Portugal and Peter. When Alfonso died in 1350, Henry and his brothers rebelled against Peter the Cruel.

Leonor was executed in 1351 and Henry fled to Portugal, later entering French service and fighting for Aragon against Castile. With Aragonese and French support he was proclaimed king at Burgos in 1366, and the titles he handed allies earned him the nickname ‘of the favours’.

Defeated at Nájera by the Black Prince in 1367, he returned with Bertrand du Guesclin's companies, won Montiel in 1369 and killed Peter himself, founding the Trastámara dynasty. He fought Portugal in the Fernandine Wars and backed France against England, and died in 1379, succeeded by his son John I.

zh:
恩里克二世（1334—1379），绰号“弑兄者”，是阿方索十一世与莱昂诺尔·德·古斯曼的私生子。父亲封他为特拉斯塔马拉伯爵；国王对莱昂诺尔诸子的厚待，激怒了葡萄牙的玛丽亚和佩德罗。1350年阿方索去世后，恩里克兄弟起兵反叛“残忍者”佩德罗。

1351年母亲被处死，恩里克逃往葡萄牙，后来为法兰西效力，又随阿拉贡对抗卡斯蒂利亚。1366年，他在阿拉贡与法兰西支持下于布尔戈斯被拥立为王，因大封盟友，得了“施恩者”的外号。

1367年他在纳赫拉败于黑太子，后借贝特朗·杜·盖克兰的雇佣兵团之力卷土重来，1369年赢得蒙铁尔战役，亲手杀死佩德罗，建立特拉斯塔马拉王朝。他在费尔南多战争中与葡萄牙交战，并联合法兰西对抗英格兰，1379年去世，其子胡安一世继位。

en:
Fadrique Alfonso of Castile (1334–1358) was an illegitimate son of Alfonso XI and Eleanor of Guzmán and twin brother of Henry of Trastámara. While still a child in 1342 he succeeded his maternal uncle as master of the Order of Santiago. He held Haro and served as adelantado mayor of the Andalusian frontier.

In 1353 he escorted Peter I's bride Blanche of Bourbon back from France, and gossip later said he had been too close to her on the road. Joining his half-brothers' revolt in the war with Aragon, he was murdered at Seville in 1358 on Peter's orders.

Chroniclers later gave him the story of being thrown from a window, which really belongs to another victim, Prince John of Aragon. The Enríquez admirals descended from him.

法德里克·阿方索·德·卡斯蒂利亚（1334—1358）是阿方索十一世与埃莉诺·德·古斯曼的私生子、特拉斯塔马拉的恩里克的孪生兄弟。1342年他尚在幼年，便继任舅父成为圣地亚哥骑士团团长，还领有阿罗，任安达卢西亚边境的边防总长。

1353年他赴法国，将佩德罗一世的新娘波旁的布朗什护送回国，后来坊间传言他在路上与她过从太近。他在对阿拉贡战争中加入异母兄弟的叛乱，1358年在塞维利亚奉佩德罗之命被杀。

后世编年史家又把被抛出窗外的故事安在他头上，那其实是另一位受害者、阿拉贡亲王胡安的下场。恩里克斯家族的历代海军统帅皆为其后裔。

Fernando Alfonso of Castile (1334–1350) was an illegitimate son of Alfonso XI and Eleanor de Guzmán, born after his half-brother Peter I in 1334. From 1335 he confirmed royal charters as the king's son, and in 1338 his father gave him Ledesma and the estates of his half-brother Sancho Alfonso.

In 1342 he received Haro on Fadrique Alfonso becoming master of Santiago, but in 1344 the king transferred Ledesma to his younger brother Juan Alfonso. A planned Aragonese marriage in 1348 came to nothing; he died unmarried in 1350.

en:
Fernando de Herrera (c. 1534–1597), known as El Divino, was a Sevillian poet of Spain's Golden Age. An admirer of Italian poetry, the classics and the Bible, he found inspiration in the verse of Garcilaso de la Vega. From around 1559 he frequented the literary circle of the Count of Gelves, whose wife Leonor de Milán inspired his Petrarchan love poetry.

His patriotic canciones celebrated contemporary Spanish commanders and campaigns, and he published an influential commentary on Garcilaso's verse. After Leonor's death in 1581 he turned to prose works until his death in 1597.

Ferdinand III, called the Saint (1199 or 1201–1252), was the son of Alfonso IX of León and Berengaria of Castile. After his parents' marriage was annulled in 1204, his mother took him to the Castilian court. In 1217 his mother abdicated in his favor, and he fought his father and rebellious nobles.

In 1230 he inherited León, uniting the two crowns. Exploiting Muslim disarray, he led Castile's greatest southward expansion, conquering Córdoba, Jaén and Seville.

He married Elisabeth of Swabia in 1219 and was succeeded by his son Alfonso X. Canonized in 1671, he is buried in Seville Cathedral.

en:
Ferdinand IV, called the Summoned (1285–1312), became king of Castile and León in 1295, aged nine. His mother María de Molina held the regency, defending his throne against revolts led by his uncle John of Castile and other nobles. The Pope legitimized him in 1301, when he came of age.

In 1302 he married Constance of Portugal. Continuing the Reconquista, he failed before Algeciras in 1309 but captured Gibraltar that year and took Alcaudete in 1312.

In 1312 he promoted judicial reform to strengthen royal authority. He died in September 1312, aged 26, leaving the crown to his infant son Alfonso XI.

Ferdinand de la Cerda (1255–1275), eldest son of Alfonso X of Castile and Violant of Aragon, was heir apparent to the Castilian throne. His name de la Cerda meant “of the bristle”. In 1268 he married Blanche, daughter of Louis IX of France; their two sons, Alfonso and Fernando, began the Infantes de la Cerda line.

He ruled Castile as regent from 1274 while his father pursued the German crown. In 1275 Marinid troops invaded; Ferdinand raised troops and marched south but died at Villa Real. His brother Sancho seized the throne, disinheriting his sons.

en:
Fernando de la Cerda (1275–1322) was the younger son of Castilian heir Ferdinand de la Cerda and Blanche of France, a grandson of Alfonso X of Castile and Louis IX. Born after his father's death in 1275, he grew up while his elder brother Alfonso, called the Disinherited, pressed the family's claim to the Castilian throne. Fernando served Alfonso XI as mayordomo mayor, or high steward.

By his marriage to Juana Núñez de Lara, known as la Palomilla, he was lord consort of Lara. Of their children, their daughter Blanche married the prince and writer Juan Manuel.

He served at the 1350 siege of Gibraltar and became adelantado of Murcia under Peter I, but he fled the court, was dismissed in February 1351 and died later that year, aged nineteen, leaving a daughter, Blanca Manuel.

Alonso III de Fonseca (c. 1475–1534) was a Galician churchman and statesman, son of Archbishop Alonso II. He became Archbishop of Santiago de Compostela in 1507, and Charles V later appointed him to the royal council.

A Renaissance humanist in touch with Erasmus, he made the University of Santiago de Compostela a major center of learning and founded the college named for him. In 1523 he was promoted to Archbishop of Toledo, primate of Spain, and in 1527 he baptized the future Philip II. He died at Alcalá de Henares in 1534.

en:
Nuño Freire de Andrade, called the Bad (el Malo), was a Galician noble of the late Middle Ages, born around 1374. He held wide lordships in the kingdom of Galicia. His harsh rule so enraged his vassals that in 1431 they banded together as the Mad Brotherhood, the first Irmandiño revolt.

Led by the hidalgo Roi Xordo, the rising spread across the bishoprics of Lugo, Mondoñedo and Santiago. Nuño died in 1431, the year of the rising, and was succeeded by his son Pedro Fernández de Andrade II.

Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba, called El Gran Capitán (1453–1515), was a Castilian general born at Montilla near Córdoba. He served Isabella the Catholic in the Castilian succession war and fought in the Granada War of 1482–1492, then led Spanish armies in Italy.

Reforming infantry around pikes and arquebuses, he defeated the French at Cerignola in April 1503 and on the Garigliano that December, conquering Naples and becoming its viceroy. He died at Granada in 1515, and his reforms inspired the later tercios.

Defying a royal summons, he fled to Valencia de Alcántara and offered the Order's border towns to Portugal's king. Abandoned by his companions, he was captured, condemned as a traitor, and executed in 1340.

Gonzalo Núñez de Lara (c. 1165 – after 1230) was a Castilian-Leonese count, third son of Count Nuño Pérez de Lara and stepson of Ferdinand II of León. Made count in 1215, he supported his brother Álvaro's regency, then submitted to Ferdinand III after the Laras' defeat. By María Díaz de Haro he fathered Nuño González ‘the Good’.

en:
Henry of Burgundy (c. 1066–1112), Count of Portugal, was a younger son of Burgundy's ducal house. He came to Iberia to fight the Almoravids for Alfonso VI and married the king's illegitimate daughter Teresa around 1095, receiving the county of Portugal.

He made a pact with his kinsman Raymond of Burgundy to share power after Alfonso's death. After Alfonso's death he exploited the wars between Queen Urraca and Alfonso I of Aragon to enlarge his lands.

He died of wounds at the siege of Astorga in 1112 and was buried at Braga. His son Afonso Henriques became Portugal's first king.

He came to Iberia to fight the Almoravids for #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('lon_alfonso_vi_jimena').GetID],X #L Alfonso VI#!#! and married the king's illegitimate daughter Teresa around 1095, receiving the county of Portugal.

He made a pact with his kinsman #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('glc_raymond_burgundy').GetID],X #L Raymond of Burgundy#!#! to share power after Alfonso's death. After Alfonso's death he exploited the wars between Queen Urraca and Alfonso I of [GetCountry('ARA').GetName] to enlarge his lands.

He died of wounds at the siege of [ShowLocationName('astorga')] in 1112 and was buried at [ShowLocationName('braga')]. His son Afonso Henriques became Portugal's first king.

勃艮第的亨利（约1066—1112）是葡萄牙伯爵，为勃艮第公爵家族的幼子。他前往伊比利亚，为阿方索六世与穆拉比特人作战，约1095年娶国王的私生女特蕾莎为妻，受封葡萄牙伯国。

他与亲属勃艮第的雷蒙订约，约定在阿方索死后分享权力。阿方索死后，他利用女王乌拉卡与阿拉贡的阿方索一世之间的战争扩张领地。

1112年，他在阿斯托尔加之围中伤重而死，葬于布拉加。他的儿子阿方索·恩里克斯后来成为葡萄牙第一位国王。

en:
Inês de Castro (c. 1320–1355) was a Galician noblewoman, natural daughter of Pedro Fernández de Castro. In the household of Constance of Castile, she became the lover of Constance's husband Infante Pedro, heir to Afonso IV of Portugal. After Constance died in 1349 she lived openly with him and bore four children; Pedro refused the new marriages his father proposed.

Her brothers' influence over the prince threatened Portugal's neutrality in the Castilian civil war; Afonso IV ordered her killed. She was beheaded at Coimbra on 7 January 1355. Pedro rebelled but was beaten within a year.

As king from 1357 he hunted her killers, who had fled to Castile, and had two executed; in 1360 he declared that he had married her secretly in 1353. The tale that he crowned her exhumed corpse is probably a myth.

伊内斯·德·卡斯特罗（约1320—1355）是加利西亚贵族女子，佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·卡斯特罗的私生女。她侍奉卡斯蒂利亚的康斯坦萨，成为康斯坦萨之夫、葡萄牙王储佩德罗的爱人。1349年康斯坦萨去世后，与佩德罗公开同居，生下四个子女；佩德罗拒绝了父亲提出的新婚事。

她的兄弟对王子的影响与日俱增，威胁到葡萄牙在卡斯蒂利亚内战中的中立，阿方索四世遂下令杀她。1355年1月7日，她在科英布拉被斩首。佩德罗起兵反父，不到一年即告失败。

1357年即位后，他追捕逃往卡斯蒂利亚的凶手，处决了其中两人，并于1360年宣称自己早在1353年就与她秘密成婚。相传他还掘出她的遗体为其加冕，这个故事很可能出于后人编造。

Jacob ben Asher (c. 1269–1340), called Ba'al ha-Turim, was a German-born rabbinic authority active in Castile. Third son of the rabbi Asher ben Jehiel, the Rosh, he was born at Cologne and in 1303 moved to Toledo after his father fled persecution in Germany. Schooled by his father, he lived in poverty.

His legal code Arba'ah Turim, the Four Columns, arranged Jewish law in four parts and gave him his byname. He died about 1340, at Toledo, or on a journey at Chios.

雅各·本·亚设（约1269—1340），绰号“《图林》作者”，是生于德意志、活跃于卡斯蒂利亚的拉比律法权威。他是拉比亚设·本·耶希埃尔（“罗什”）的第三子，生于科隆；1303年父亲为躲避迫害而出走，他随全家迁居托莱多，主要师从父亲，一生清贫。

所著律法汇编《四列》把犹太律法分为四部分，他也由此得绰号。约1340年他卒于托莱多，一说卒于旅途中的希俄斯岛。

en:
Don Juan Manuel (1282–1348), Prince of Villena, was a grandson of Ferdinand III and nephew of Alfonso X of Castile. One of the richest and most powerful men of his time, he coined his own money like a king, negotiated with Aragon's James II for Queen Mother María de Molina in 1304, and later tutored the young Alfonso XI.

When Alfonso imprisoned his daughter Constanza at Toro, he rebelled, allying with Granada and Aragon. He escaped the siege at Garci-Nuñez in 1336 and fought on from exile until 1338. A reconciliation brokered by the pope was complete only in 1340, when he fought beside the king at Río Salado and Algeciras.

He retired to write El conde Lucanor, a celebrated story collection that some thought beneath his rank. He died in 1348.

堂胡安·曼努埃尔（1282—1348），比列纳亲王，是卡斯蒂利亚国王斐迪南三世之孙、阿方索十世之侄。他是当时最富有、最有权势的人物之一，像国王一样自铸钱币；1304年，王太后玛丽亚·德·莫利纳委托他与阿拉贡的海梅二世谈判，后来他又担任年幼的阿方索十一世的导师。

阿方索把他的女儿康斯坦莎囚禁在托罗，他随即起兵反叛，联合格拉纳达与阿拉贡对抗国王。1336年他从加尔西·努涅斯的围攻中逃脱，流亡在外继续作战，直到1338年。在教皇斡旋下，双方直到1340年才完全和解，他随后与国王并肩参加里奥萨拉多战役和攻取阿尔赫西拉斯之役。

他退隐后写成著名故事集《卢卡诺尔伯爵》，当时有人认为这与他的身份不相称。他于1348年去世。

Juan Núñez de Prado (died 1355) was an illegitimate son of Infanta Blanche of Portugal and a Portuguese nobleman, and a knight of the Order of Calatrava. He joined a revolt against Master Garci López de Padilla, whom the rebels charged with fleeing the field at Baena and abandoning his friars. They defeated Garci at Malas Tardes.

In 1325 they brought charges against him to Alfonso XI at Valladolid, and the king backed Núñez de Prado as Master, though a long dispute followed.

Under Peter the Cruel he opposed the crown. Peter had him arrested at Almagro in 1355; he did not resist, though he had men enough to fight. Diego García de Padilla replaced him, and Núñez de Prado was sent to Maqueda Castle and murdered there.

胡安·努涅斯·德·普拉多（?—1355）是葡萄牙公主布兰卡与一名葡萄牙贵族的私生子，卡拉特拉瓦骑士团骑士。他参加了反对团长加尔西·洛佩斯·德·帕迪利亚的起事，指控后者在巴埃纳战场丢下修士逃走。他们在马拉斯塔德斯击败加尔西。

1325年，他们到巴利亚多利德向阿方索十一世控诉，国王支持推举努涅斯·德·普拉多为团长，但争议持续了很久。

到“暴君”佩德罗在位时，他反对王室。1355年他在阿尔马格罗被捕，虽有足够人手却没有抵抗。迭戈·加西亚·德·帕迪利亚接替了团长一职，努涅斯·德·普拉多被押往马克达城堡遇害。

Juan Núñez I de Lara, called el Gordo (died 1294), headed the noble House of Lara in Castile. Son of Nuño González de Lara el Bueno, he joined Louis IX of France on the Eighth Crusade at Tunis in 1270.

In the revolts of 1272–1273 against Alfonso X he followed his father into exile. Under Sancho IV he rebelled again, fled to France in 1292, and was captured by the infante John. Sent to the Andalucían frontier against Granada, he died at Córdoba in April 1294.

胡安·努涅斯一世·德·拉腊，绰号“胖子”（？—1294），是卡斯蒂利亚拉腊家族的族长。他是努诺·冈萨雷斯·德·拉腊“好人”之子，1270年随法兰西国王路易九世参加第八次十字军东征，兵至突尼斯。

Juana de Castro, called the Unloved (died 1374), was the second wife of Peter I of Castile and half-sister of Inês de Castro. Her father was Pedro Fernández de Castro, and she was a great-granddaughter of Sancho IV. She had a son with her first husband Diego López de Haro.

After his death she met Peter; she demanded he have his marriage to Blanche of Bourbon annulled before she would marry him. Peter complied, and they wed in 1354, but he abandoned her the day after the wedding, leaving her only the castle of Dueñas.

There she gave birth to their son John. She died at Dueñas in 1374 and was buried at Santiago de Compostela.

胡安娜·德·卡斯特罗，人称“不被爱者”（?—1374），是卡斯蒂利亚国王佩德罗一世的第二任王后，也是伊内斯·德·卡斯特罗的同父异母姐妹。她的父亲是佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·卡斯特罗，本人是桑乔四世的曾孙女。她与第一任丈夫迭戈·洛佩斯·德·阿罗育有一子。

丈夫去世后她结识佩德罗；她要求佩德罗先宣布他与波旁的布朗什的婚姻无效，才肯嫁给他。佩德罗照办，两人于1354年成婚，他却在次日便将她抛弃，只留给她杜埃尼亚斯城堡。

她在那里生下他们的儿子胡安。1374年她于杜埃尼亚斯去世，葬于圣地亚哥—德孔波斯特拉。

Juana Núñez de Lara, called la Palomilla (1286–1351), was the daughter of Juan Núñez de Lara the Fat and Teresa Díaz de Haro, heiress of Biscay. Her first husband, Infante Henry of Castile, a son of Ferdinand III, died in 1304 without children and left her a young widow. She then married Fernando de la Cerda, a grandson of Alfonso X; he died in 1322.

Their children included Juan Núñez III de Lara; Blanche, who married the prince and writer Juan Manuel; and María, wife of Charles II of Alençon. Juana died at Palencia in 1351.

Judah ben Asher (1270–1349) was a German Talmudist and later rabbi of Toledo, son of the rabbi Asher ben Jehiel, the Rosh. He left Germany for Spain in 1283, reached Toledo in 1285, and in 1305 preceded his father to Castile.

After the Rosh died in 1321 or 1328, Toledo made him its rabbi. After a quarrel he planned to move to Seville, but his congregation doubled his salary; he nevertheless urged his sons to return to Germany. He died at Toledo in 1349.

Eleanor de Guzmán (1310–1351) was a Castilian noblewoman who outshone the queen at the court of Alfonso XI. Her husband Juan de Velasco died in 1328, and soon afterwards she met the king at Seville. She became his long-term mistress and bore him ten children, among them the future Henry II and Fadrique Alfonso.

After his son Peter was born in 1334, Alfonso left his queen Maria of Portugal and lived with Eleanor. He gave her large estates and set up her household at Seville, where she heard political matters.

When Alfonso died in 1350, Maria, regent for her son Peter, had Eleanor imprisoned and in 1351 executed at Talavera de la Reina. The killing widened the rift: Henry and Peter fought for Castile until Henry won the crown.

埃莉诺·德·古斯曼（1310—1351）是卡斯蒂利亚贵妇，在阿方索十一世的宫廷里风头盖过王后。1328年丈夫胡安·德·贝拉斯科去世后不久，她在塞维利亚结识国王，成为他长期的情妇，为他生下十个子女，包括后来的恩里克二世和法德里克·阿方索。

1334年儿子佩德罗出生后，阿方索便离开王后葡萄牙的玛丽亚，与埃莉诺同住。他赐她大片地产，并在塞维利亚为她设立府邸，让她在那里听取政务。

1350年阿方索去世后，为儿子佩德罗摄政的玛丽亚将埃莉诺囚禁，并于1351年在塔拉韦拉-德拉雷纳将她处死。这一杀戮加深了王室的裂痕：恩里克与佩德罗争夺卡斯蒂利亚，最终恩里克夺得王位。

Pedro López de Ayala (1332–1407), born at Vitoria, was a statesman and chronicler of Castile. He served Pedro I, then defected to Henry of Trastámara and fought at Nájera in 1367, where the Black Prince captured him. In 1378 he negotiated a French alliance.

Captured by Portugal at Aljubarrota in 1385, in his iron prison he wrote a falconry treatise and part of his satirical Rimado de Palacio. Ransomed around 1388, he resumed diplomacy in France, became grand chancellor under Henry III and chronicled four Castilian kings. He died at Calahorra in 1407.

佩德罗·洛佩斯·德·阿亚拉（1332—1407）生于维多利亚，是卡斯蒂利亚的政治家与编年史家。他先效力于国王佩德罗一世，后来转投特拉斯塔马拉的恩里克，1367年在纳赫拉战役中被黑太子俘虏。1378年他出使法国，谈判促成结盟。

After Sancho III died in 1158 he held the regency for the child Alfonso VIII, waged civil war against the Castro family, and was killed by Fernando Rodríguez de Castro at the Battle of Huete.

en:
María de Molina (c. 1265–1321), lady of Molina from 1292, was queen of Castile as the wife of Sancho IV. As the couple lacked a papal dispensation, their children were at first deemed illegitimate. On Sancho's death in 1295 she became regent for her nine-year-old son Ferdinand IV, defending his crown against his uncle John and rival claimants; in 1301 the Pope legitimized the marriage.

In 1302 nobles accused her of misusing royal funds, but her accounts showed she had spent her own income on the monarchy. After Ferdinand died in 1312 she again held the regency for her grandson Alfonso XI, until her death in 1321.

en:
Maria of Portugal (1313–1357), eldest daughter of Afonso IV, became queen of Castile in 1328 by marrying Alfonso XI. The marriage was unhappy from the start: Alfonso kept Leonor de Guzmán, who bore him ten children, and Maria spent long periods secluded in a monastery in Seville.

Her father demanded that Alfonso give Leonor up. In 1340 Alfonso promised to send Leonor to a convent, winning Portuguese support at Río Salado, but returned to her afterwards.

After Alfonso died in 1350, Maria used her influence over her son Peter's council to have Leonor killed in 1351. She joined the revolt against Peter in 1354; in 1356 he killed several nobles of her household at Toro, and she returned to Portugal. She died at Évora in 1357.

en:
Luis de Molina (1535–1600) was a Spanish Jesuit theologian of the School of Salamanca. Born in Cuenca, he encountered Ignatius of Loyola's Spiritual Exercises and joined the Society of Jesus in 1553. He later taught philosophy and theology at Coimbra and Évora.

In 1588 he published the Concordia, arguing through his theory of middle knowledge that divine foreknowledge leaves human free will intact; this system became known as Molinism. Dominicans denounced him to the Inquisition, and Rome examined the dispute from 1597.

路易斯·德·莫林纳（1535—1600）是萨拉曼卡学派的西班牙耶稣会神学家。他生于昆卡，接触伊尼戈·德·洛约拉的《神操》后，于1553年加入耶稣会，后来在科英布拉与埃武拉教授哲学和神学。

en:
Nuño González de Lara, called el Bueno ‘the Good’ (c. 1220 – 8 September 1275), head of the House of Lara, was the closest friend of Alfonso X of Castile.

He defeated the rebellious infante Henry near Lebrija in 1255, suppressed Mudéjar revolts at Jerez and Écija, and became the first castellan of Jerez in 1261.

In 1272 he led the nobles' revolt and fled to Granada, but was reconciled in 1273 and granted Écija. He fell defending it against the Marinids in 1275; his recovered head was buried with his body at Palencia.

en:
Nuño Pérez de Lara (died 3 August 1177) was a Castilian nobleman, son of Count Pedro González de Lara. Alfonso VII made him alférez in 1145; he was probably captured at Montoro against the Almohads in 1156 and ransomed in 1157, then captured again by the Castros at Lobregal in 1160.

He became count by 1162 and guardian of Alfonso VIII. After his brother Manrique died in 1164, Nuño held the regency until 1169. He promoted the cult of Thomas Becket in Spain and was killed at Cuenca in 1177.

Pedro de Aguilar (1331–1338) was an illegitimate son of Alfonso XI of Castile and his mistress Eleanor de Guzmán, born at Valladolid amid public celebrations. In 1332 the king granted the infant the vast lordships formerly held by Infante Pedro, including Aguilar de Campoo.

From 1333 he confirmed royal charters as son of the king and lord of Aguilar, and in May 1335 Alfonso made him chancellor mayor of Castile. He died at Guadalajara in 1338, still a child.

Pedro Fernández de Castro, called o da Guerra (c. 1290–1342), was a Galician noble and mayordomo mayor of Alfonso XI of Castile. After his father was killed in battle in 1304, he was raised at the Portuguese court, returning to Galicia about 1319, when the king restored his family lands.

He led the assault at Teba in 1330 and refused to fight the Portuguese king when he invaded Castile in 1334. He died in an epidemic at the siege of Algeciras in 1342.

Pedro González de Lara (died 16 October 1130) was a Castilian magnate and the first to call himself de Lara. First recorded as royal alférez in 1088 under Alfonso VI, he may have joined the First Crusade, earning the nickname el Romero.

Under Queen Urraca, whose lover he became, he was Castile's most powerful subject. He resisted Alfonso VII's accession and rebelled in 1130, seizing Palencia; captured and exiled, he was killed in a duel with Alfonso Jordan of Toulouse.

en:
Peter I (1334–1369), called the Cruel or the Just, was king of Castile and León from 1350, the last ruler of the senior House of Ivrea. Born at Burgos to Alfonso XI and Maria of Portugal, he lost his intended bride Joan of England to plague in 1348. He came to the throne at almost sixteen, married Blanche of Bourbon in 1353 but left her within days for María de Padilla.

His long feud with half-brother Henry of Trastámara plunged Castile into civil war; he took refuge with the Black Prince, who restored him after Nájera in 1367. Henry returned in 1368 and defeated Peter at Montiel in 1369.

Du Guesclin led Peter into his tent, where Henry himself killed him and left the body unburied for three days. Chronicler Ayala, later a Trastámara servant, called him a tyrant, but the English remembered him and Chaucer lamented his fall.

佩德罗一世（1334—1369），绰号“残酷者”或“公正者”，1350年起为卡斯蒂利亚与莱昂国王，也是伊夫雷亚家族主支的最后一位君主。他生于布尔戈斯，为阿方索十一世与葡萄牙的玛丽亚之子。1348年，他原定的新娘英格兰的琼染疫而亡。他近十六岁即位，1353年迎娶波旁的布朗什，没过几天便抛下王后，转投玛丽亚·德·帕迪利亚。

他与异母兄特拉斯塔马拉的恩里克长期反目，使卡斯蒂利亚陷入内战；他投奔黑太子，后者于1367年在纳赫拉战役后助他复位。恩里克于1368年返回，1369年在蒙铁尔击败佩德罗。

en:
Pedro Manrique de Lara (c. 1140–1202), second lord of Molina, was the leading Castilian magnate of the House of Lara under Alfonso VIII. Son of Count Manrique Pérez de Lara and Ermessende of Narbonne, he is first documented in 1158 and helped guard the young king.

He defended Toledo and Extremadura against the Almohads, briefly served Ferdinand II of León in 1185–1186, and from 1192 held the viscounty of Narbonne by inheritance. The first Spanish noble whose seal survives, he died in January 1202, leaving a son Aimerico by his wife Sancha Garcés of Navarre.

佩德罗·曼里克·德·拉腊（约1140—1202），第二代莫利纳领主，是阿方索八世朝拉腊家族的首席权贵。他是伯爵曼里克·佩雷斯·德·拉腊与纳博讷的埃尔梅森德之子，1158年首次见于特许状，曾参与守护年幼的国王。

他抵御穆瓦希德王朝，保卫托莱多与埃斯特雷马杜拉，1185—1186年曾短暂效力莱昂国王斐迪南二世，1192年起凭继承权领有纳博讷子爵领。他是现存印章最早的西班牙贵族，1202年1月去世，留下与纳瓦拉的桑查·加塞斯所生的儿子艾默里。

Pedro Núñez de Guzmán (born c. 1250) was a Leonese-Castilian noble, lord of Puebla de Asturias, Cangas and Tineo. Son of Álvaro Pérez de Guzmán, alcaide of Seville, and María Girón, he served Ferdinand IV as steward major of the royal household and as adelantado mayor of the Andalusia and Galicia frontiers.

By his wife Juana Ponce de León he fathered Alonso Meléndez de Guzmán, master of the Order of Santiago, and Eleanor de Guzmán, who became Alfonso XI's all-powerful mistress. He had died before 1324.

佩德罗·努涅斯·德·古斯曼（约1250年生）是莱昂—卡斯蒂利亚贵族，领有普埃夫拉-德阿斯图里亚斯、坎加斯和蒂内奥。他是塞维利亚城防长官阿尔瓦罗·佩雷斯·德·古斯曼与玛丽亚·希龙之子，曾任斐迪南四世的宫廷总管，并担任安达卢西亚与加利西亚边境的边防总长。

en:
Francisco Pizarro (c. 1478–1541), a conquistador from Trujillo, led the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire. He grew up illiterate and sailed to the New World in 1509, and in 1513 accompanied Balboa across Panama. Later he arrested Balboa, who was beheaded in 1519, and was made mayor of Panama City. After two failed expeditions toward Peru, he obtained the Crown's permission in 1529 to conquer it.

At Cajamarca in November 1532 he captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa. Atahualpa filled a room with gold as ransom, but Pizarro had him garrotted in July 1533. That year he entered Cuzco. He founded Lima in 1535 and was made Marquess of the Conquest in 1537.

Caught in the power struggles among the conquerors, he was assassinated in Lima on 26 June 1541. The Inca state was destroyed, and Pizarro has been reviled for killing Atahualpa after the ransom was paid.

弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗（约1478—1541）是出身特鲁希略的征服者，主持了西班牙对印加帝国的征服。他一辈子不识字，1509年前往新大陆，1513年随巴尔沃亚穿越巴拿马。后来他逮捕巴尔沃亚，后者于1519年被斩首，皮萨罗因此得到巴拿马城市长之职。两次远征秘鲁失败后，他于1529年获得王室批准去征服秘鲁。

1532年11月，他在卡哈马卡俘获印加皇帝阿塔瓦尔帕。阿塔瓦尔帕以黄金堆满一间屋子作赎金，皮萨罗却于1533年7月将他绞死。同年他进入库斯科。1535年他建立利马城，1537年受封征服侯爵。

1541年6月26日，他在征服者内部的权力斗争中于利马遇刺身亡。印加国家被摧毁，皮萨罗因在赎金付清后仍杀害阿塔瓦尔帕而遭唾骂。

en:
Ruy, or Rodrigo, Pérez Maldonado was a Castilian knight who became Grand Master of the Order of Alcántara in 1335, succeeding his brother Suero Pérez Maldonado.

His election came during a schism in which rival bands of the order proclaimed their own masters, until King Alfonso XI intervened with force and secured Ruy's recognition.

In 1336 the king ordered him to reinforce the relief army for Badajoz, then besieged by the Portuguese; after their defeat at Villanueva de Barcarrota the retreating troops ravaged the order's lands, and the Crónica de Alfonso XI blames Ruy for a faint-hearted defence. He resigned the maestrazgo on 26 May 1337, when Gonzalo Martínez de Oviedo took office.

鲁伊（即罗德里戈）·佩雷斯·马尔多纳多是卡斯蒂利亚骑士，1335年继其兄苏埃罗·佩雷斯·马尔多纳多出任阿尔坎塔拉骑士团大团长。

他当选时骑士团正陷入分裂，各派纷纷拥立自己的大团长，国王阿方索十一世以武力介入，才确立了鲁伊的地位。

1336年，国王命他率军驰援被葡萄牙军围困的巴达霍斯；葡军在巴尔卡罗塔新镇战败后，撤退途中蹂躏骑士团领地，《阿方索十一世编年史》指责鲁伊防御怯懦。1337年5月26日他辞去团长之职，由贡萨洛·马丁内斯·德·奥维耶多接任。

en:
Bernardino de Sahagún (c. 1499–1590) was a Franciscan friar and pioneering ethnographer born at Sahagún in León. He reached New Spain in 1529, mastered Nahuatl, and spent more than fifty years documenting Aztec religion, society and history with native assistants, developing methods to collect and check the information he gathered.

He compiled the General History of the Things of New Spain, preserved as the bilingual and richly illustrated Florentine Codex, whose twelfth book recounts the fall of Tenochtitlan from the Aztec point of view. His methods later earned him the title of first anthropologist of America.

贝尔纳迪诺·德萨阿贡（约1499—1590）是方济各会修士、开创性的民族志学者，生于莱昂的萨阿贡。他于1529年抵达新西班牙，掌握纳瓦特尔语，与本土助手一道用五十多年时间记录阿兹特克人的宗教、社会与历史，并发展出收集和核验资料的方法。

en:
Samuel ha-Levi Abulafia (c. 1320–1360), born at Úbeda into the powerful Abulafia family, was treasurer to Peter the Cruel of Castile. He began as administrator to Juan Alfonso de Alburquerque, then rose at Peter's court from chamberlain to almojarife and judge.

When Henry of Trastámara's supporters staged a pogrom against Toledo's Jews and seized the royal treasures, Samuel went with the king to Toro to demand them back, then helped him reclaim Toledo and make peace with Portugal at Évora in 1358.

With the wealth Peter gave him he founded the Synagogue of El Tránsito in Toledo between 1355 and 1357, its Hebrew and Arabic inscriptions and Moorish features echoing the king's palace in Seville. In 1360, suspected of embezzlement, he was imprisoned and tortured, and died under torture.

塞缪尔·哈列维·阿布拉菲亚（约1320—1360）生于乌韦达，出身显赫的阿布拉菲亚家族，是卡斯蒂利亚国王“暴君”佩德罗的财政大臣。他先为胡安·阿方索·德·阿尔布开克管理事务，后在佩德罗的宫廷中由宫廷长升任阿尔莫哈里费和法官。

特拉斯塔马拉的恩里克的支持者袭击托莱多犹太人并夺走王室财宝后，塞缪尔随国王赶往托罗索还，之后又协助国王收复托莱多，并促成1358年与葡萄牙在埃武拉缔约。

他用国王赐予的财富，于1355至1357年间在托莱多修建埃尔特兰西托犹太会堂，会堂刻有希伯来文和阿拉伯文铭文，带有与国王塞维利亚宫殿相近的摩尔式特征。1360年，他因涉嫌侵吞公款被捕受刑，死于酷刑之下。

他用国王赐予的财富，于1355至1357年间在托莱多修建埃尔特兰西托犹太会堂，会堂刻有希伯来文和阿拉伯文铭文，带有与国王[ShowLocationName('sevilla')]宫殿相近的摩尔式特征。1360年，他因涉嫌侵吞公款被捕受刑，死于酷刑之下。

en:
Sancho Alfonso of Castile, called the Mute (Valladolid, c. 1332–1342), was one of the ten children Alfonso XI had with his mistress Eleanor of Guzmán, a brother of Henry II of Castile and a half-brother of Peter I. Described as mute and feeble-minded, he nonetheless held several lordships, including Ledesma and Béjar, and served briefly as the king's standard-bearer.

He died about 1342, still a boy. A younger brother of the same name, born in 1343, later became Count of Alburquerque.

桑乔·阿方索·德·卡斯蒂利亚，绰号“哑巴”（约1332—1342，巴利亚多利德），是阿方索十一世与情妇埃莉诺·德·古斯曼所生十个子女之一，恩里克二世的兄弟，佩德罗一世的异母兄弟。史籍称他又哑又愚钝，却仍领有莱德斯马、贝哈尔等多处领地，并曾短暂担任国王的执旗官。

他约于1342年夭折，仍是个孩子。1343年出生的同名幼弟日后成为阿尔布开克伯爵。

en:
Sancho II the Strong (1036/1038–1072), born at Zamora, was the eldest son of Ferdinand the Great and Sancha of León. On Ferdinand's death in 1065 Castile passed to Sancho, León to Alfonso and Galicia to García; Sancho was also assigned the tribute of the taifa of Zaragoza.

In 1068 he won the War of the Three Sanchos against Navarre and Aragon, gaining several border territories, then defeated Alfonso at Llantada. With his alférez El Cid he beat Alfonso again at Golpejera in January 1072 and united the three kingdoms.

He took his sister Elvira's city of Toro, but while besieging Urraca at Zamora he was murdered by Vellido Adolfo, and Alfonso recovered the throne.

桑乔二世，绰号“强者”（1036/1038—1072），出生于萨莫拉，是斐迪南大帝与莱昂的桑查的长子。1065年斐迪南死后，卡斯蒂利亚归桑乔，莱昂归阿方索，加利西亚归加西亚；桑乔还获得了萨拉戈萨泰法的贡赋。

他夺取了姐妹埃尔维拉的托罗城，却在萨莫拉围攻乌拉卡时被贝利多·阿道尔夫刺杀，阿方索重登王位。

en:
Sancho III, called the Desired (c. 1134–1158), ruled Castile and Toledo from 1157 until his death. The eldest son of Alfonso VII of León and Castile and Berengaria of Barcelona, he received Castile while his brother Ferdinand II took León under their father's will. His nickname reflected his birth after eight years of childless marriage.

In May 1158 the brothers signed the Treaty of Sahagún, partitioning their conquests against al-Andalus. Sancho granted the castle of Calatrava to the monk Raymond of Fitero, giving rise to the Order of Calatrava. He married Blanche of Navarre in 1151 and was succeeded by their son Alfonso VIII.

zh:
桑乔三世（约1134—1158），绰号“渴望者”，1157年起统治卡斯蒂利亚与托莱多，直至去世。他是莱昂兼卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索七世与巴塞罗那的贝伦加利亚的长子；依父亲遗嘱，卡斯蒂利亚归他，莱昂归弟弟斐迪南二世。他的绰号源于父母婚后八年无子，直到他出生。

1158年5月，兄弟二人签订《萨阿贡条约》，划分了对安达卢斯的征服范围。桑乔把卡拉特拉瓦城堡交给修士菲特罗的雷蒙驻守，卡拉特拉瓦骑士团由此诞生。他于1151年娶纳瓦拉的布兰卡，死后由其子阿方索八世继位。

en:
Sancho IV, called the Brave (1258–1295), was the second son of Alfonso X of Castile. After his elder brother Ferdinand de la Cerda died in 1275, Sancho contested the succession against Ferdinand's infant son Alfonso; backed by nobles, he rebelled in 1282 and was crowned at Toledo after his father's death in 1284.

He married María de Molina in 1282 without papal dispensation. He crushed repeated revolts, executing the lord of Biscay, Lope Díaz de Haro, and imprisoning his brother John.

After his release, John rebelled again and brought in the Marinids; in 1291 Sancho relieved Tarifa, where Guzmán the Good had resisted their siege. He died in 1295, leaving María as regent for his nine-year-old son Ferdinand IV.

桑乔四世（1258—1295），绰号“勇敢者”，是阿方索十世的次子。1275年兄长费尔南多·德·拉·塞尔达死后，他与费尔南多年幼之子阿方索争夺继承权，在贵族支持下于1282年举兵反叛，1284年父亲去世后在托莱多加冕。

他于1282年迎娶玛丽亚·德·莫利纳，却未取得教皇特许。他不断镇压叛乱，处死比斯开领主洛佩·迪亚斯·德·阿罗，囚禁弟弟胡安。

胡安获释后再次叛乱，引来马林王朝军队；1291年桑乔解塔里法之围，好人古斯曼此前在那里死守。1295年桑乔去世，遗命玛丽亚为九岁的儿子斐迪南四世摄政。

Sancho Manuel de Villena (1320–1347) was a Castilian nobleman, the natural son of the prince and writer Juan Manuel by Inés de Castañeda. His father made him first lord of Carcelén and Montealegre, and through his wife María de Castañeda he held Coy and Celdá.

A ricohombre of Castile, he served as warden of Lorca and adelantado mayor of the kingdom of Murcia. He left four children, including Constanza Manuel, and died in 1347.

en:
Michael Servetus (1509 or 1511–1553) was an Aragonese theologian, physician and Renaissance humanist, born at Villanueva de Sigena. He took part in the Protestant Reformation and rejected the doctrine of the Trinity. He studied medicine in France, and his Restoration of Christianity (1553) contained the first correct European description of pulmonary circulation.

Arrested by the Catholic Inquisition in April 1553, he escaped to Geneva, where John Calvin denounced him; the city council condemned him and burned him at the stake on 27 October 1553.

米格尔·塞尔韦特（1509或1511—1553）是阿拉贡的神学家、医生与文艺复兴人文主义者，生于比利亚努埃瓦-德锡赫纳。他参与了新教改革，反对三位一体教义。他在法国学医，所著《基督教的复兴》（1553年）包含欧洲人对肺循环的首次正确描述。

en:
Francisco Suárez (1548–1617) was a Spanish Jesuit philosopher and theologian, a leading figure of the School of Salamanca. Born at Granada, he entered the Society of Jesus in 1564 and began teaching philosophy in 1570, later teaching theology at Valladolid. He taught at Rome, Alcalá and Salamanca before taking the principal chair of theology at Coimbra in 1597.

His Disputationes metaphysicae were read across seventeenth-century Europe, while his treatises on law and church and state earned him the title godfather of international law. Doctor Eximius, he influenced Grotius and Leibniz.

Vasco Rodríguez de Coronado was a Galician-born Castilian knight who became Grand Master of the Order of Santiago in 1327. In that year he marched with King Alfonso XI from Mérida in the campaign against Granada that took Olvera, Pruna and other strongholds, and the king made him adelantado mayor de la Frontera.

On 27 December 1327 Violante Sánchez, illegitimate daughter of King Sancho IV, made over to him and the order the lordships of Ucero and Vilamartín de Valdeorras together with her Galician and Castilian estates.

He died in 1337 or 1338. The order first elected his nephew Vasco López, who was deposed within the year.

瓦斯科·罗德里格斯·德·科罗纳多是出身加利西亚的卡斯蒂利亚骑士，1327年出任圣地亚哥骑士团大团长。同年他随国王阿方索十一世从梅里达出征格拉纳达，连克奥韦拉、普鲁纳等要塞，国王任命他为边疆先遣长官。

1327年12月27日，国王桑乔四世的私生女比奥兰特·桑切斯将乌塞罗、比利亚马丁·德·巴莱德拉斯等领地，连同她在加利西亚和卡斯蒂利亚的全部产业移交给他和骑士团。

他于1337或1338年去世。骑士团先选出他的侄子瓦斯科·洛佩斯，后者在同年即被废黜。

Gabriel Vásquez (1549 or 1551–1604), called Bellomontanus, was a Spanish Jesuit scholastic theologian, born near Belmonte in Cuenca. At Alcalá he began studying law before turning to philosophy under Domingo Báñez, and entered the Society of Jesus in 1569.

After teaching theology at Ocaña, Madrid and Alcalá, he was summoned to Rome in 1585 to succeed Francisco Suárez in the Roman College's theology chair, returning to Alcalá in 1591. He became Suárez's foremost academic critic, disputing his accounts of natural law and the jus gentium, and his disciples carried on a famous school until his death in 1604.

加布里埃尔·巴斯克斯（1549或1551—1604），人称贝洛蒙塔努斯，是西班牙耶稣会经院神学家，生于昆卡省贝尔蒙特附近。他在阿尔卡拉先学法律，后转学哲学，师从多明戈·巴涅斯，1569年加入耶稣会。

他先后在奥卡尼亚、马德里和阿尔卡拉教授神学，1585年奉召前往罗马，接替弗朗西斯科·苏亚雷斯出任罗马学院神学教授，1591年返回阿尔卡拉。他成为苏亚雷斯最主要的学术论敌，就自然法与万民法问题与他反复辩难，其弟子形成的学派名噪一时，直至他1604年去世。

Violant of Aragon (8 June 1236–1301) was queen of Castile and León as the wife of Alfonso X the Wise, whom she married at Burgos in January 1249. A daughter of James I of Aragon and Violant of Hungary, she founded the convent of San Pablo in Valladolid in 1276.

After her eldest son Ferdinand de la Cerda died in 1275, Alfonso named their second son Sancho as heir, but Violant defended the rights of Ferdinand's sons, placing them under the protection of her brother Peter III at Játiva in Aragon. She later lived mostly in Aragon and died at Roncesvalles in 1301 while returning from Rome.

阿拉贡的比奥兰特（1236年6月8日—1301）是卡斯蒂利亚—莱昂王后，1249年1月在布尔戈斯嫁给“贤者”阿方索十世。她是阿拉贡国王海梅一世与匈牙利的比奥兰特之女，1276年在巴利亚多利德创建圣巴勃罗修道院。

1275年长子费尔南多·德·拉·塞尔达早逝后，阿方索立次子桑乔为继承人，比奥兰特却维护费尔南多诸子的权利，把他们托付给兄长阿拉贡国王佩德罗三世，安置在哈蒂瓦。她后来长居阿拉贡，1301年从罗马返回途中在龙塞斯瓦列斯去世。

Roi Xordo (died 1437) was a Galician hidalgo from the lands of the House of Andrade, by tradition a native of Ferrol or A Coruña. In 1431 he led the Irmandade Fusquenlla, or Mad Brotherhood, in revolt against the harsh lord Nuno Freire de Andrade, called the Evil One.

Rising between Pontedeume and Betanzos, his followers took the castle of Moeche and attacked other strongholds as far as Santiago de Compostela, in the first of the Irmandiño revolts. The brotherhood was defeated at Pontedeume in 1437, where Roi Xordo was killed.

en:
César-François Cassini de Thury (1714–1784), known as Cassini III, was a French astronomer and cartographer. Born at Thury-sous-Clermont, he was the second son of Jacques Cassini and grandson of Giovanni Domenico Cassini, founder of the Paris Observatory. He entered the Academy of Sciences in 1739.

In 1744 he began a trigonometric survey of France, which produced the 180-sheet Cassini map, the kingdom's first complete topographical map, completed by his son in 1793. Appointed the Paris Observatory's first director in 1771, he proposed a survey linking it with the Greenwich observatory and died of smallpox in 1784.

塞萨尔-弗朗索瓦·卡西尼·德·蒂里（1714—1784），又称卡西尼三世，是法国天文学家、地图学家。他生于蒂里苏克莱蒙，是雅克·卡西尼的次子、巴黎天文台创立者乔瓦尼·多梅尼科·卡西尼之孙。1739年他进入法兰西科学院。

1744年，他开始以三角测量绘制法国全图，最终成果是180幅图版的“卡西尼地图”——法国第一幅完整的全国地形图，由他的儿子于1793年完成。1771年他被任命为巴黎天文台首任台长，后来提议开展连接巴黎与格林尼治天文台的测量，1784年因天花去世。

Berenguer Ramon I, called the Hunchback (c. 1005–1035), inherited the counties of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona in 1018, son of Ramon Borrell and Ermesinde of Carcassonne. A minor until 1023, he long ruled beside his forceful mother.

His reign was peaceful: he brought the count of Urgell to heel, befriended the neighbouring Catalan counts, accepted the suzerainty of Sancho the Great of Navarre and made a pilgrimage to Rome in 1032. His peace with the Muslim taifas angered the nobility. He died in 1035 and was buried at Ripoll, leaving his counties divided among his sons.

贝伦格尔·拉蒙一世，绰号“驼背”（约1005—1035），是拉蒙·博雷利与卡尔卡松的埃尔梅辛德之子，1018年继承巴塞罗那、赫罗纳和奥索纳三个伯国。1023年之前他因年幼，长期与强势的母亲共同执政。

en:
Berenguer Ramon II (c. 1053–1097/1099), called the Fratricide, was count of Barcelona from 1076. Son of Ramon Berenguer I, he first ruled jointly with his twin brother Ramon Berenguer II. Pope Gregory VII appealed for reconciliation in 1079, but the twins partitioned Catalonia against their father's will and alternated palaces.

After Ramon Berenguer II was killed hunting in 1082, murder suspicions sparked civil war, weakening Barcelona's authority over Carcassonne and Razès. A settlement in 1086 made Berenguer Ramon regent for his young nephew Ramon Berenguer III. Twice captured by El Cid, he resigned in 1097 for Jerusalem, possibly dying on the First Crusade.

贝伦格尔·拉蒙二世（约1053—1097/1099），绰号“弑亲者”，1076年起任巴塞罗那伯爵。他是拉蒙·贝伦格尔一世之子，起初与孪生兄长拉蒙·贝伦格尔二世共同统治。1079年教皇格列高利七世呼吁两人和解，但兄弟俩违背父亲遗愿瓜分加泰罗尼亚，轮流居住巴塞罗那宫殿。

en:
Borrell II (927/928–993) was count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 947 and added Urgell in 948, ruling alone after his brother's death in 966. More diplomat than soldier, he exchanged embassies with Córdoba's caliph in 950, did homage to al-Hakam II in 966, and invited Gerbert of Aurillac, later Pope Sylvester II, to Catalonia.

In 970 he and Bishop Ató went to Rome for a separate Catalan church province; the pope approved, but Ató's murder soon ended the plan.

In 985 Almanzor sacked Barcelona after defeating Borrell at Rovirans. His Frankish appeals unanswered, in 988 he refused homage to Hugh Capet, leaving his counties de facto independent.

zh:
博雷尔二世（927/928—993）947年起任巴塞罗那、赫罗纳和奥索纳伯爵，948年又领有乌赫尔，966年兄弟死后独自统治。他外交重于武功：950年与科尔多瓦哈里发互派使节，966年向哈卡姆二世称臣，还邀请欧里亚克的热贝尔（即后来的教皇西尔维斯特二世）来加泰罗尼亚。

970年他与主教阿托赴罗马争取独立的加泰罗尼亚教省；教皇批准，但阿托遇刺，计划落空。

en:
Wilfred the Hairy (Catalan Guifré el Pilós; died 11 August 897) built the fortunes of the early House of Barcelona. He held Urgell and Cerdanya from 870, received Barcelona, Girona and Besalú in 878, and added the frontier county of Ausona in 886. He repopulated the deserted lands around Vic, restored its bishopric and founded the monastery of Santa Maria de Ripoll.

His southern castles provoked the Muslim lords of Lleida; after a failed assault on Lleida he fell defending Barcelona against Lubb ibn Muhammad in 897. He was buried at Ripoll, and his counties passed to his son Wilfred Borrell.

en:
Wilfred II Borrell (Catalan Guifré II Borrell; c. 874 – 26 April 911) succeeded his father Wilfred the Hairy in 897 as count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona. His father's lands were divided among his sons, and Wilfred governed his three counties with his younger brother Sunyer, who was then a minor under his guardianship.

He was the last Catalan count to swear vassalage to a Frankish king. In 898 he married Gersenda, daughter of Odo of Toulouse, by whom he left a daughter but no son.

He founded the monastery of Sant Pau del Camp in Barcelona and was buried there after his death in 911, when his counties passed to Sunyer.

他在巴塞罗那创立圣保德尔坎普修道院，911年去世后葬于该院，诸伯国传给苏涅尔。

en:
Miro (926–966) was count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 947, jointly with his brother Borrell II after their father Sunyer retired to monastic life. The brothers divided the work: Borrell handled military and foreign affairs while Miro took charge of domestic government and the city of Barcelona.

He made grants to the monasteries of Sant Cugat del Vallès and Ripoll, and the Rec Comtal canal, which carried water from the Besòs river to the city, is thought to have been built under him. He died at Barcelona in 966.

en:
Pau Claris i Casademunt (1586–1641) was a Catalan lawyer and churchman from Barcelona who became the 94th president of the Deputation of the General of Catalonia. A doctor of civil and canon law, he was made a canon of Urgell in 1612 and represented the church arm at the Catalan parliament of 1626, where resistance gathered against Philip IV's taxes.

Elected ecclesiastical deputy in July 1638, he led Catalonia through the Reapers' Revolt and, on 16 January 1641, proclaimed the Catalan Republic under French protection. He died in Barcelona the following month, on 27 February 1641.

en:
Ramon Berenguer I, called the Old (c. 1023–1076), succeeded his father Berenguer Ramon I as Count of Barcelona in 1035. He campaigned against the Muslim taifas, raiding as far as Barbastro and drawing tributes that brought Catalonia its first prosperity, and built Catalan sea power in the western Mediterranean. He acquired Carcassonne and Razès beyond the Pyrenees and began codifying the Usages of Barcelona.

He scandalised the papacy by marrying Almodis de la Marche, wife of the Count of Toulouse, and both were excommunicated; together they founded the Romanesque cathedral of Barcelona. He died in 1076, leaving twin heirs.

en:
Ramon Berenguer II, called the Towhead for his thick fair hair (1053/1054–1082), was a twin son of Ramon Berenguer I of Barcelona and Almodis de la Marche. On their father's death in 1076 he and his twin Berenguer Ramon II ruled jointly, but they soon quarrelled and partitioned the counties against their late father's will.

In December 1082 he was murdered while hunting in the woods; public opinion blamed his brother, who ruled alone and became known as the Fratricide. His son by Mahalta of Apulia later ruled as Ramon Berenguer III.
