en:
Ramon Berenguer III the Great (1082–1131) was count of Barcelona from 1086, at first under his uncle Berenguer Ramon II and ruling alone from 1097. In 1102 he counter-attacked the Almoravids but was defeated at Mollerussa.

He absorbed Besalú in 1111 and Cerdanya in 1117, and by marrying Douce, heiress of Provence, in 1112 carried Catalan power east as far as Nice. With a Pisan fleet he raided Muslim Mallorca in 1114 and 1115 and freed Christian captives.

In 1116 he sought papal support for a crusade to Tarragona, which he retook and rebuilt by 1118 as the seat of Catalonia's restored archbishopric. He died in 1131, leaving Barcelona to his son Ramon Berenguer IV and Provence to Berenguer Ramon.

拉蒙·贝伦格尔三世（1082—1131），绰号“伟大者”，1086年起任巴塞罗那伯爵，最初由叔父贝伦格尔·拉蒙二世共同执政，1097年开始独自统治。1102年他反击阿尔摩拉维德人，却在莫列鲁萨战败。

他于1111年并吞贝萨卢、1117年并吞塞尔达尼亚，又在1112年迎娶普罗旺斯女继承人杜丝，使加泰罗尼亚势力向东延伸至尼斯。1114至1115年，他联合比萨舰队袭击穆斯林统治的马略卡岛，解救基督教囚徒。

1116年他请求教皇支持远征塔拉戈纳，至1118年收复并重建该城，成为恢复的加泰罗尼亚大主教区驻地。1131年他去世，巴塞罗那传给儿子拉蒙·贝伦格尔四世，普罗旺斯传给贝伦格尔·拉蒙。

en:
Ramon Berenguer IV (c. 1114–1162), sometimes called the Saint, inherited the county of Barcelona from his father Ramon Berenguer III in 1131. In August 1137 he was betrothed to Petronilla, the infant heiress of Aragon.

When her father Ramiro II withdrew to a monastery that November, Ramon Berenguer took charge of Aragon as prince, forging the dynastic union of Barcelona and Aragon that became the Crown of Aragon. He styled himself count of Barcelona and prince of the Aragonese.

The two lands retained their own laws and institutions. He died in Piedmont in August 1162, leaving his son Alfonso II to inherit both Aragon and Barcelona.

zh:
拉蒙·贝伦格尔四世（约1114—1162），有时被称为“圣人”，1131年从父亲拉蒙·贝伦格尔三世手中继承巴塞罗那伯国。1137年8月，他与尚在襁褓的阿拉贡女继承人佩德罗尼拉订婚。

同年11月佩德罗尼拉之父拉米罗二世退隐修道院，拉蒙·贝伦格尔遂以亲王身份执掌阿拉贡，促成巴塞罗那与阿拉贡的王朝联合，即后来的阿拉贡联合王国。他通常使用巴塞罗那伯爵和阿拉贡人亲王的头衔。

两地保留各自的法律和制度。1162年8月他死于皮埃蒙特，其子阿方索二世后来同时继承阿拉贡与巴塞罗那。

en:
Ramon Borrell (972–1017), son of Borrell II, was count of Barcelona from 992. Surviving Almanzor's last raids, he counter-raided Lleida in 1003.

In 1010, during the civil war in the Caliphate of Córdoba, he joined Muhammad II to defeat Caliph Sulayman II and sack Córdoba. Later raids reached the Ebro and Segre in 1015–1016, and their wealth helped him maintain his barons' loyalty. He repopulated the Camp de Tarragona and was the first Catalan count to mint coinage. He died in 1017, leaving his son Berenguer Ramon to the regency of his wife Ermesinde of Carcassonne.

en:
Sunyer (c. 890–950), the youngest son of Wilfred the Hairy, was count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 911 to 947. He took the offensive against the Muslims of Lleida: in 912 the wali Muhammad al-Tawil routed his army near Tàrrega, but a counter-raid in 914 killed him.

With the count of Empúries he raided Tortosa and Valencia in 936, killing the qadi of Valencia and forcing Tortosa to pay tribute, and he acknowledged Louis IV of France as his overlord. From 929 he repopulated the Penedès south to Olèrdola. He abdicated in 947 and died three years later.

苏涅尔（约890—950）是“多毛者”威尔弗雷德的幼子，911年至947年任巴塞罗那、赫罗纳和奥索纳伯爵。他对莱里达的穆斯林转取攻势：912年，莱里达总督穆罕默德·塔维勒在塔雷加附近击败他的军队，但914年的反击将其击杀。

en:
He Zhen (1321–1388) was a Yuan commander from Dongguan who became the effective ruler of Guangdong. He left office to raise militia against bandits, seized Huizhou and Xunzhou in 1354 and rose to Guangdong's top military post.

In 1362 he retook the provincial capital Guangzhou from the strongman Shao Zongyu. Shao besieged Guangzhou again in 1365 and forced He Zhen out, but he rallied his troops and retook the city the following year.

When the Ming general Liao Yongzhong marched south in 1368, He Zhen surrendered, helped him defeat Shao and served the new dynasty as a provincial administrator. Ennobled as Count of Dongguan in 1387, he died in 1388 and was posthumously named Zhongjing.

何真（1321—1388）是元末实际据有广东的元朝将领，东莞人。他弃官回乡组织乡兵抵御盗寇，1354年攻取惠州、循州，升任广东最高军职。

1362年，他从豪强邵宗愚手中收复省府广州。1365年邵宗愚再围广州，迫使何真突围；次年何真重整兵马，夺回广州。

1368年，明将廖永忠南下，何真归顺并助他消灭邵宗愚，此后在新朝出任数省地方长官。1387年他受封东莞伯，1388年病逝，谥号忠靖。

en:
John I Orsini (Italian Giovanni, died 1317) succeeded his father Richard as count palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos in 1303/1304. In 1292 he married Maria, daughter of Despot Nikephoros I of Epirus, and spent a decade at the Epirote court.

As an Achaean vassal he joined the failed siege of Arta in 1304 and the unsuccessful invasion of Epirus in 1307, when disease struck the Latin troops.

At Manolada in 1316 he led the loyalist first line against Ferdinand of Majorca, who was routed and killed. John died in 1317; a year later his son Nicholas murdered Despot Thomas and seized Epirus.

en:
John II Orsini, also John Komnenos Doukas (died 1335), was the second son of Count John I Orsini of Cephalonia. In 1323 he murdered his brother Nicholas, who had seized Epirus five years earlier, and succeeded him as count palatine and despot.

In 1324 John of Gravina annexed Cephalonia, so John submitted to Emperor Andronikos II, adopted Orthodoxy and married Anna Palaiologina. The emperor granted him the title of despot.

In 1332 he annexed Thessaly, but Emperor Andronikos III soon took its eastern part. John died suddenly in 1335, perhaps poisoned by Anna.

en:
Maio I Orsini, also called Matthew de Monopoli, was count palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos after the Fourth Crusade. Probably an Apulian from Monopoli, he made himself master of the Ionian islands around 1206.

The partition of Byzantine lands had assigned them to Venice; Maio placed his domains under Pope Innocent III in 1207, at times acknowledging Venetian suzerainty, before turning to the Latin Empire.

In 1227 he married a sister of the Epirote ruler Theodore Komnenos Doukas, and after Theodore's defeat at Klokotnitsa in 1230 became a vassal of Achaea in 1236. He is last attested in 1238, when Pope Gregory IX urged him to defend Constantinople.

马约一世·奥尔西尼，又称莫诺波利的马修，是第四次十字军东征后凯法利尼亚与扎金索斯的行宫伯爵。他很可能是出身莫诺波利的普利亚人，约1206年成为伊奥尼亚群岛的主人。

瓜分拜占庭领土时，群岛被划给威尼斯；马约于1207年将领地置于教皇英诺森三世保护之下，一度承认威尼斯的宗主权，后来转投拉丁帝国。

1227年，他娶伊庇鲁斯统治者狄奥多尔·科穆宁·杜卡斯的姐妹为妻；1230年狄奥多尔在克洛科特尼察战败后，他于1236年成为亚该亚侯国的封臣。1238年，教皇格列高利九世敦促他出兵保卫君士坦丁堡，这是关于他最后的记载。

en:
Maio II Orsini (c. 1228–c. 1260) may be identified with Count Theodore, a little-documented count palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos whom a historian places between Maio I and Richard. In this reconstruction, he was likely the son of Maio I and a sister of the Epirote ruler Theodore Komnenos Doukas.

A Greek church document of 1264 mentions a count Theodore, apparently after his death. He is thought to have died around 1260; in 1262 William II of Villehardouin, prince of Achaea, became guardian of Richard, identified in this reconstruction as his underage son.

zh:
马约二世·奥尔西尼（约1228—约1260）可能就是狄奥多尔伯爵，一位记载稀少的凯法洛尼亚和扎金索斯宫廷伯爵；一位史家认为他统治于马约一世与里卡尔多之间。按照这一推断，他可能是马约一世与伊庇鲁斯君主狄奥多尔·科穆宁·杜卡斯的姊妹所生之子。

1264年的一份希腊教会文书提到狄奥多尔伯爵，当时他似乎已经去世。他被认为约于1260年去世；1262年，亚该亚亲王威廉二世·维尔阿杜安成为里卡尔多的监护人，而这一推断认为里卡尔多是他的幼子。

en:
Maria Komnene Doukaina was an Epirote princess, the only child of Despot Nikephoros I Komnenos Doukas of Epirus and his wife Maria Laskaris, daughter of the Nicaean emperor Theodore II Laskaris. In 1291 her father sent her as hostage to Count Richard Orsini of Cephalonia.

In 1292 Richard married her to his son John I without Nikephoros' leave; the despot forgave them only in 1295. She became countess palatine when John succeeded in 1303 or 1304. Her sons Nicholas and John II ruled Epirus.

玛丽亚·科穆宁·杜卡伊娜是伊庇鲁斯公主，伊庇鲁斯专制君主尼基弗鲁斯一世·科穆宁·杜卡斯与妻子玛丽亚·拉斯卡丽丝（尼西亚皇帝狄奥多尔二世·拉斯卡里斯之女）的独女。1291年父亲将她送往凯法洛尼亚伯爵理查·奥尔西尼处为质。

1292年，理查未经尼基弗鲁斯同意便将她嫁给其子乔瓦尼一世；专制君主直到1295年才予宽恕。1303或1304年乔瓦尼继位，她成为宫廷伯爵夫人。她的儿子尼古拉斯和乔瓦尼二世后来统治伊庇鲁斯。

en:
Maria Laskaris Vatatzaina was a Nicaean princess, the daughter of Emperor Theodore II Laskaris and Elena Asenina of Bulgaria. Around 1249 her family betrothed her at Pegai to Nikephoros, son of Despot Michael II of Epirus, on whom John III conferred the title of despotes.

The wedding was celebrated at Thessalonica in October 1256, sealing Nicaea's alliance with Epirus. Maria died in 1258, leaving a daughter, Maria Komnene Doukaina, later countess of Cephalonia.

玛丽亚·拉斯卡里斯·瓦塔泽娜是尼西亚公主，皇帝狄奥多尔二世·拉斯卡里斯与保加利亚的埃列娜·阿森妮娜之女。约1249年，双方在佩盖将她许配给伊庇鲁斯专制君主米海尔二世之子尼基弗鲁斯，约翰三世并授予他专制君主之衔。

婚礼于1256年10月在塞萨洛尼基举行，缔结了尼西亚与伊庇鲁斯的同盟。她于1258年去世，留下女儿玛丽亚·科穆宁·杜卡伊娜，即后来的凯法洛尼亚宫廷伯爵夫人。

en:
Richard I Orsini (1165–1197) was an Italian nobleman and the forefather of the Apostolico Orsini, later called the Orsini of Epirus to distinguish them from their Roman cousins. From 1194 he was count of Cephalonia and Zakynthos, ruling the islands through the dowry of his wife, a daughter of the Norman admiral Margaritus of Brindisi.

Emperor Henry VI also enfeoffed him at Nocera in 1194. He died at Cephalonia in 1197 and was succeeded by his son Maio I.

en:
Richard Orsini (Italian Riccardo, died 1303/1304) ruled as count palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos from before 1260. Around 1262, while he was still a minor, William II of Villehardouin acted as regent.

As an Angevin vassal he served as captain-general of Corfu and as bailli of the Principality of Achaea in 1297–1300. In 1291/1292 he aided Despot Nikephoros I of Epirus against the Byzantine forces besieging Ioannina, and married his heir John I to the despot's daughter Maria without consulting her father, paving the way for the Orsini takeover of Epirus. He was accidentally killed by one of his own knights.

en:
Francesco II Ordelaffi (c. 1310–1374), called the Great, was Ghibelline lord of Forlì from 1331. Driven out by a papal army in 1332, he re-established his rule the next year and gained Cesena.

In 1337 he imprisoned the archbishop of Ravenna and was excommunicated, yet the pope then made him papal vicar for an annual payment. To escape the tribute he sided with Emperor Louis IV as imperial vicar. His refusal to submit later brought on Cardinal Albornoz and a crusade preached against him in 1355–1356.

Cesena fell despite the resistance of his wife Cia and son Ludovico, and Forlì fell in July 1359, leaving him only Forlimpopoli and Castrocaro. He died in Venice in 1374; his son Sinibaldo succeeded him.

弗朗切斯科二世·奥尔德拉菲（约1310—1374），绰号“伟大者”，自1331年起任弗利的吉伯林派领主。1332年他被教皇军队驱逐，次年重建统治，并获得切塞纳。

1337年他囚禁拉文纳大主教，被处以绝罚，随后教皇任命他为教皇代理人，条件是每年缴款。为逃避贡赋，他转而支持皇帝路德维希四世，成为帝国代理人。他拒不臣服，引来枢机主教阿尔沃诺斯，教会还在1355—1356年发起针对他的十字军。

尽管他的妻子奇娅和儿子卢多维科奋力抵抗，切塞纳仍告陷落；1359年7月弗利也陷落，他只保住福利姆波波利和卡斯特罗卡罗。他1374年死于威尼斯，儿子西尼巴尔多继位。

en:
Giovanni II Malatesta (died 20 September 1299), first count of Sogliano, was the son of Ramberto di Giovanni Malatesta. He belonged to the Ghibelline Malatesta branch that opposed Malatesta da Verucchio's hold on Rimini, and served as podestà of Rimini in 1276.

In 1287 he made peace with Verucchio, but the Romagna rector Pietro Stefaneschi, unable to capture Verucchio, seized Giovanni and held him at Cesena. Released in 1288, he followed the Malatesta into exile, and after the 1290 peace returned home still hostile to his kinsmen. He died in 1299.

乔瓦尼二世·马拉泰斯塔（1299年9月20日卒）是首任索利亚诺伯爵，父亲是兰贝托·迪·乔瓦尼·马拉泰斯塔。他属马拉泰斯塔家族的吉伯林支派，反对马拉泰斯塔·达·韦鲁基奥控制里米尼，1276年任里米尼最高行政官。

1287年他与韦鲁基奥和解，但罗马涅督主教彼得罗·斯特凡内斯基未能抓住韦鲁基奥，便将乔瓦尼拘捕、押往切塞纳。他于1288年获释，随后随马拉泰斯塔家族流亡，1290年和议后返乡，仍敌视同族，1299年去世。

Giovanni Malatesta, also called Gianne, was an Italian noble of the Sogliano branch of the Malatesta, the son of Malatestino da Sogliano. He made his home in Rimini, where in 1352 he renewed leases on two houses, one in the city and one at Monte San Giuliano.

He married Margherita and died around 1358, leaving as his heir his son Malatesta; he also had a son Ramberto.

Malatesta II Malatesta of Sogliano (died c. 1380) was the son of Giovanni Malatesta, called Gianne, and Margherita. With his brother Ramberto II he ruled as sovereign count of Sogliano from 1358, holding castles including Verucchio and Roncofreddo.

Still a minor under his mother's regency, he saw Count Lando's mercenary company storm Sogliano in November 1358. He married Agnesina Faetani, leaving five children.

en:
Malatestino Malatesta, known as Malatestino da Sogliano, was an Italian condottiero of the Ghibelline Malatesta branch and a son of Giovanni II Malatesta, first count of Sogliano. Orphaned in 1299, in 1305 he bought Strigara castle with his brothers. In 1317 the Guelph Malatesta of Rimini took Sogliano, after which he took refuge with his cousin Ramberto of Giaggiolo; together they occupied Forlì.

In 1334, with Ramberto and Malatesta Guastafamiglia, he retook Sogliano and rebuilt its walls. Last documented in 1334, he left a son Giovanni, attested in 1352.

en:
Cia Ordelaffi, born Marzia degli Ubaldini (1317–1381), was the daughter of Vanni Ubaldini and in 1334 married Francesco II Ordelaffi, Ghibelline lord of Forlì. In May 1351 her intervention to relieve her son Ludovico decided the Battle of Dovadola.

In 1357, with a papal crusade preached against the Forlivesi, her husband entrusted Cesena to her. She held out against Cardinal Gil de Albornoz until, on her father's advice, she surrendered on 21 June; Villani records that she asked safe passage for her soldiers and nothing for herself. She was imprisoned at Ancona and only released in July 1359, when Forlì fell.

She died at Forlì in 1381 and was buried beside her husband. She is remembered as one of Italy's best-known women warriors.

奇娅·奥尔德拉菲本名马尔齐娅·德利·乌巴尔迪尼（1317—1381），是万尼·乌巴尔迪尼之女，1334年嫁给弗利的吉伯林派领主弗朗切斯科二世。1351年5月，她出兵援救儿子卢多维科，对多瓦多拉战役的胜利起了决定性作用。

1357年，教皇方面对弗利人发动十字军，丈夫把切塞纳托付给她。她抵抗枢机主教希尔·德·阿尔沃诺斯，最终听从父亲劝告，于6月21日投降；据维拉尼记载，她只为部下请求安全通行，自己别无所求。她被关押在安科纳，1359年7月弗利陷落后才获释。

1381年她在弗利去世，与丈夫合葬。她是意大利最著名的女战士之一。

en:
Niccolò I Malatesta (died 1374) was a condottiere, son of Ramberto I Malatesta and Cassandra della Faggiola. In 1355 he fought for the Church, helping take Santarcangelo and Verucchio. In 1356 he fought Francesco Ordelaffi, but was captured near Cesena and held in a harsh prison for over two years, until Count Lando freed him.

Hired by Florence during the Pisan war, he in 1363 recovered castles including Sambuceto usurped by the people of Cesena. In 1367 his father gave him the county of Ghiaggiolo; he is thought to have died in 1374.

en:
Paolo Malatesta, known as il Bello (c. 1246–c. 1284), was the third son of Malatesta da Verucchio, lord of Rimini. In 1269 he married Orabile Beatrice, heiress of the counts of Ghiaggiolo, founding the Malatesta di Giaggiolo line.

In March 1282 Pope Martin IV made him Captain of the People in Florence. He is famous for his affair with Francesca da Polenta, wife of his brother Gianciotto, whom he had represented at her proxy wedding. The lovers were slain by Gianciotto around 1284, traditionally at Gradara, an episode Dante immortalized in Inferno, Canto V.

保罗·马拉泰斯塔，绰号美男子（约1246—约1284），是里米尼领主马拉泰斯塔·达·韦鲁基奥的第三子。1269年，他娶贾焦洛伯爵家族的女继承人奥拉比莱·贝阿特丽丝，开创马拉泰斯塔·迪·贾焦洛支系。

1282年3月，教皇马丁四世任命他为佛罗伦萨人民长官。他最著名的事迹是与兄长詹乔托之妻弗朗切斯卡·达·波伦塔的恋情——当初他曾代表兄长出席她的代理婚礼。约1284年，两人被詹乔托杀死，相传遇害地点在格拉达拉；但丁在《神曲·地狱篇》第五章中使这段故事不朽。

en:
Ramberto I Malatesta (1302–1367), son of Uberto, count of Giaggiolo, belonged to the Giaggiolo branch of the Malatesta and spent his life in arms, always trying to harm his kinsmen in Rimini. Small of stature, he was called il contino di Ghiaggiolo.

Beaten under the walls of Ferrara in 1333, he escaped by swimming the Po. He helped the Ordelaffi retake Forlì, then raised Cesena in revolt and became its podestà, which set him against Francesco Ordelaffi for good. He later served Cardinal Albornoz against the Ordelaffi, until in 1356 Francesco's wife Cia caught him on the road toward Cesena and put him to flight.

In 1360 his own sons shut him in a dungeon. He died there in 1367, having given Giaggiolo to his son Niccolò.

兰贝托一世·马拉泰斯塔（1302—1367）是贾焦洛伯爵乌贝托之子，属于马拉泰斯塔家族的贾焦洛支系，一生戎马，总想着给里米尼的族亲添乱。他身材矮小，人称贾焦洛小伯爵。

1333年在费拉拉城下战败，泅渡波河逃生。他帮助奥尔德拉菲家族收复弗利，又策动切塞纳叛乱并出任其最高行政官，从此与弗朗切斯科·奥尔德拉菲势不两立。后来他为枢机主教阿尔沃诺斯攻打奥尔德拉菲家族，1356年，弗朗切斯科之妻奇娅在他进军切塞纳途中突袭，将他击溃。

1360年，亲生儿子们把他关进地牢。他于1367年死于狱中，死前把贾焦洛封邑授予儿子尼科洛。

en:
Ramberto II Malatesta was an Italian condottiero of the Ghibelline branch of the Malatesta and a son of Giovanni II Malatesta, first count of Sogliano, by Sofia Silighini, whose dowry had brought the family the Sogliano lands in 1255. In 1305 he bought Strigara castle with his brothers.

In 1334 he and Malatestino retook Sogliano with the help of Malatesta Guastafamiglia and rebuilt its walls. Ramberto died in 1348.

en:
Sinibaldo I Ordelaffi (1336–1386), son of Francesco II Ordelaffi and the warrior Cia degli Ubaldini, was Ghibelline lord of Forlì. In January 1376 he exploited the city's revolt against papal rule to recover the seigniory.

In 1379 Pope Urban VI made him papal vicar of Forlì, Forlimpopoli and Castrocaro. In December 1385 his nephews Pino and Cecco imprisoned him in Ravaldino castle, where he died the next year, possibly poisoned.

西尼巴尔多一世·奥尔德拉菲（1336—1386）是弗朗切斯科二世·奥尔德拉菲与女战士奇娅·德利·乌巴尔迪尼之子，吉伯林派的弗利领主。1376年1月，他趁弗利起兵反抗教皇统治之机重建领主政权。

en:
Uberto Malatesta (c. 1270–1324), count of Giaggiolo, was the eldest son of Paolo il Bello and Orabile Beatrice, raised at Rimini by his uncle Gianciotto, who had murdered his father. In 1297 he fled to the Ghibellines and became their captain-general in Romagna, and in 1300 he seized Cesena from his uncle Malatestino.

He became podestà of Cesena in 1303, only to be expelled for authoritarian rule. Tradition says he killed Gianciotto in 1313 to avenge his father. In 1324 his cousin Ramberto betrayed his plot against Pandolfo I, who had Uberto slain at a banquet.

乌贝托·马拉泰斯塔（约1270—1324）是贾焦洛伯爵、保罗·美男子与奥拉比莱·贝阿特丽丝的长子，由杀害其父的伯父詹乔托在里米尼抚养成人。1297年他投奔吉伯林派，成为该派在罗马涅的总司令，1300年从伯父马拉泰斯蒂诺手中夺取切塞纳。

1303年他出任切塞纳最高行政官，不久便因专横被市民驱逐。相传他在1313年杀死詹乔托，为父报仇。1324年，他的堂兄弟兰贝托出卖了他反对潘多尔福一世的密谋，潘多尔福设下宴席将他杀死。

en:
Anselmo of Ceva was a son of Bonifacio del Vasto, lord of Savona and western Liguria, and Agnes de Vermandois. His father's testament of 1125 named him among the sons sharing the family patrimony in southern Piedmont.

Anselmo was associated with Ceva and Clavesana, which his sons later held separately: Guglielmo I became the first documented marchese of Ceva, and Bonifacio the first marchese of Clavesana. Anselmo died in 1178.

安塞尔莫·迪·切瓦是萨沃纳及西利古里亚之主博尼法乔·德尔·瓦斯托与阿涅丝·德·韦芒杜瓦之子。1125年父亲立遗嘱时，把他列入共享皮埃蒙特南部家族领地的诸子之中。

安塞尔莫与切瓦和克拉韦萨纳两地有关，他的儿子后来分别领有两地：古列尔莫一世成为第一位有文书可考的切瓦侯爵，博尼法乔则成为首位克拉韦萨纳侯爵。安塞尔莫于1178年去世。

Bonifacio di Ceva was a marquis of Ceva from 1324 to 1326, the son of Giorgio III di Ceva and a grandson of Marquis Giorgio II il Nano. His father died before his grandfather.

On 29 June 1324 Bonifacio and his brother Oddone appear among the Ceva lords who concluded a convention with the Scarelli of Pornasio. He died after 22 April 1328.

en:
Federico di Ceva was a son of Guglielmo IV of the Aleramici marquises of Ceva. On 30 December 1329 Arnaldo, bishop of Asti, invested him and his brother Emerico with the shares held by their family in the feuds of Lesegno, Mombasiglio and Montegrosso.

In May 1349 he swore fealty to bishop Baldracco Malabayla of Asti, receiving in fee a quarter of Lesegno and Montegrosso and an eighth of Mombasiglio.

费代里科·迪·切瓦是切瓦阿勒拉米奇家族侯爵古列尔莫四世之子。1329年12月30日，阿斯蒂主教阿尔纳尔多把家族世代持有的莱塞尼奥、蒙巴锡利奥和蒙特格罗索封地的相应份额封授给他与兄弟埃梅里科。

en:
Giorgio II di Ceva, called il Nano (before 1268 – shortly after 29 June 1324), was marquis of Ceva; after his death the marquisate gradually fragmented in the fourteenth century. He consistently backed Asti against Charles of Anjou and joined the peace of 1282.

On 22 October 1295 he sold Ceva and all his lands to Asti for a hundred thousand lire, receiving them back as a fief. He defeated his cousin Guglielmo IV and in 1309 aided Asti against the Ghibellines.

乔治二世·迪·切瓦，绰号“侏儒”（1268年前—1324年6月29日后不久），是切瓦侯爵；他死后，侯国在14世纪逐渐分裂。他始终支持阿斯蒂对抗安茹的查理，并参与了1282年的和约。

1295年10月22日，他以十万阿斯蒂里拉把切瓦及全部领地卖给阿斯蒂，再以封臣身份领回。他击败了堂亲古列尔莫四世，并于1309年协助阿斯蒂对抗吉伯林派。

en:
Giorgio III di Ceva was the eldest son of the marquis Giorgio II “the Dwarf” of Ceva. He is first documented in 1268, when Marquis Tommaso I of Saluzzo granted him and his descendants free passage through his lands.

When his father sold all his lands to the commune of Asti in 1295, Asti invested Giorgio and his brother Guglielmo with them as fiefs, and in 1296 both brothers ratified the sale. Early in the fourteenth century he disputed lands at Garessio with the Certosa di Casotto, which his father renounced to the monastery in 1308.

He died before his father, before 19 November 1324. His sons Bonifacio and Oddone divided the marquisate with their uncle Guglielmo V in May 1326.

乔治三世·迪·切瓦是切瓦侯爵“矮子”乔治二世的长子。1268年，萨卢佐侯爵托马索一世特许他及其后代自由通行其领地，这是史料对他的最早记载。

1295年，其父将全部领地出售给阿斯蒂公社，阿斯蒂随即将这些领地作为采邑册封给乔治与其弟古列尔莫，1296年兄弟二人共同追认了这笔出售。14世纪初，他与卡索托加尔都西会修道院就加雷西奥的地产发生争讼，其父于1308年将相关权利让予修道院。

他先于父亲去世，卒于1324年11月19日之前。他的儿子博尼法乔与奥多内于1326年5月与叔父古列尔莫五世瓜分了侯爵领地。

en:
Guglielmo V of Ceva was a son of Giorgio II “the Dwarf”, marchese of Ceva. In February 1296 he and his brother Giorgio III joined their father in ratifying the sale of Ceva to the commune of Asti.

When Giorgio II died in 1324, Guglielmo's elder brother had already predeceased him, leaving the young nephews Bonifacio and Oddone. In 1326 the heirs partitioned the marquisate: Guglielmo took Priero and other lands, while his nephews received Battifollo and neighbouring lordships.

en:
Guglielmo I of Ceva (before 1170–before 1222) was the first marquess of Ceva and founder of the Ceva line of the Aleramici, son of Anselmo and grandson of Bonifacio del Vasto; his brother Bonifacio founded the Clavesana branch. In 1188 he swore the cittadinatico oath at Savona.

In 1190 Asti forced him to surrender Montezemolo and Murialdo, returned as fiefs, and in 1191 he was podestà of Asti. He died before 1222, succeeded by his sons under Guglielmo II.

切瓦的古列尔莫一世（1170年前—1222年前）是第一代切瓦侯爵、阿莱拉米奇家族切瓦支系的始祖，安塞尔莫之子、博尼法乔·德尔瓦斯托之孙；其弟博尼法乔开创了克拉韦萨纳支系。1188年他在萨沃纳作市民宣誓。

en:
Guglielmo II di Ceva (died after 25 November 1228) ruled the marquisate of Ceva jointly with his brothers after their father Guglielmo I died around 1224. In 1218 he was sent to Alba to swear a stricter citizenship pact, binding the family to serve the city with ten knights and two hundred foot soldiers.

In the War of Capraia he switched from Genoa to Asti in 1227, helping cut Alba and Alessandria off from Liguria. He married a daughter of Manfredo II of Saluzzo.

en:
Guglielmo IV di Ceva was a Ceva marquis who contested control of the marquisate with his kinsman Giorgio II il Nano in the 1290s, in a war that devastated the family lands. Allied with the commune of Mondovì and Emanuele di Clavesana, he tried to supplant Giorgio, who seized Nucetto from Guglielmo's son Bonifacio.

The dispute ended in defeat: in 1297 Mondovì agreed to exile him and his Clavesana allies, while Ceva itself had been sold to Asti in 1295.

en:
Leone di Ceva was a son of Guglielmo I and one of the Ceva marquises ruling jointly with his brother Guglielmo II. In 1221 he joined Guglielmo II in renewing the family's citizenship pact with Alba, and in 1227 both brothers switched from Genoa to Asti, fielding a hundred knights against Alba and Alessandria.

In 1243 he served as imperially appointed podestà of Alba. He died before 1252, leaving four young sons, including Andrea, under the guardianship of their uncle Giorgio.

en:
Fang Guozhen (1319–1374), a native of Huangyan in Zhejiang, was the leading coastal rebel of the late Yuan. In 1348 he formed a pirate band among the offshore islands and preyed on the grain ships feeding the Yuan capital Dadu. Yuan forces failed to defeat him, and official titles secured only his nominal submission.

By 1356 he ruled the coastal prefectures of Qingyuan, Taizhou and Wenzhou with a thousand-ship fleet, and from 1357 he helped Zhang Shicheng ship grain north to Dadu. Zhu Yuanzhang's generals seized his ports in 1367 and Fang surrendered that December; Zhu needed his fleet and granted him favorable terms. Fang died in Nanjing in 1374.

方国珍（1319—1374），浙江黄岩人，是元末东南沿海最有势力的海上叛首。1348年，他在沿海岛屿聚众为盗，劫掠供给元朝都城大都的粮船。元军未能击败他，以官爵招抚也只换来名义上的归顺。

到1356年，他已据有庆元、台州、温州三路沿海州郡，部众拥有上千艘船只；1357年起，他又替张士诚向大都海运粮食。1367年，朱元璋的部将连下他的港口，方国珍于同年十二月投降。朱元璋需要他的船队，给予他优厚条件；1374年方国珍在南京去世。

en:
Guo Zixing (1302–1355) was a wealthy White Lotus notable from Dingyuan and an early Red Turban rebel leader. In February 1352 he and his allies seized Haozhou with several thousand followers. The young Zhu Yuanzhang joined him that April and rose quickly; Guo gave him his adopted daughter, the future Empress Ma, in marriage.

Feuds divided the Haozhou commanders, and Zhu rescued Guo after the faction of Sun Deya and Zhao Junyong seized him; Guo later joined Zhu at Chuzhou. After Guo died in 1355, Han Lin'er confirmed his son and brother-in-law as successors, while Zhu gradually consolidated his leadership. In 1370 Zhu posthumously named Guo Prince of Chuyang.

郭子兴（1302—1355）是濠州定远的富豪、白莲教首领，也是早期红巾军起事者之一。1352年二月，他与同盟率数千人袭取濠州。年轻的朱元璋于同年四月投奔其麾下，迅速得到提拔；郭子兴把养女、后来的马皇后许配给他。

濠州诸将争斗不止，郭子兴被孙德崖、赵均用一派扣押后，朱元璋将他救出。郭子兴后来在滁州与朱元璋会合。1355年他去世后，韩林儿确认其子和妻弟继承其地位，朱元璋则逐渐巩固了领导权。1370年，朱元璋追封郭子兴为滁阳王。

en:
Indravarman V, originally named Harideva, was a king of Champa. In 1257 he assassinated his uncle Jaya Indravarman VI, but waited until 1266 for his coronation. He refused Kublai Khan's demand of personal submission.

In 1282–1283 Sogetu's Yuan army seized Vijaya, driving Indravarman and his son Harijit into the mountains. Disease and supply shortages wore the invaders down, and after Sogetu fell in battle in 1285, Champa was delivered. He died in 1288, succeeded by Harijit, the future Chế Mân.

Jamo, called Chế Mỗ in Vietnamese annals (制某), was a Cham prince and the son of King Jaya Ananda of Champa. His father invested him with the rank of Bố điền, or great king, as royal heir, and appointed his son-in-law Maha Sawa as minister.

When Jaya Ananda died in May 1342, Maha Sawa drove Jamo out and seized the throne. Jamo fled to Trần-ruled Đại Việt.

en:
Jaya Ananda founded the thirteenth dynasty of Champa and ruled from 1318 to 1342. Born in the southern marches of Đại Việt, he was a commander under the Cham king Chế Năng, whom the Trần dynasty drove into exile in Java in 1318, when the Vietnamese installed Jaya Ananda as a vassal king.

Cham tradition expected the five-state alliance's leader to come from the Areca or Coconut tribe, which he did not, so nobles opposed him from 1323 to 1326. In 1323 he sent tribute to the Yuan court to seek recognition.

Emperor Trần Minh Tông invaded in 1326 but was repelled, and Champa stood independent thereafter. On his death in 1342 his son-in-law Maha Sawa seized the throne from his heir Jamo, who fled to Vietnam.

zh:
制阿难（？—1342）是占城第十三王朝的建立者，1318—1342年在位。他出生于大越南部边陲，原为占城国王制能麾下将领；1318年陈朝迫使制能流亡爪哇，越人立制阿难为附庸国王。

按占城传统，五国联盟的首领应出自槟榔或椰子部族，他并不符合，因此1323年至1326年间一直受到贵族反对。1323年他遣使向元朝进贡，以求得到承认。

陈明宗于1326年出兵进攻，却被击退，此后占城保持独立。1342年他去世后，女婿茶和布底从继承人制某手中夺取王位，制某逃往安南。

#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('dai_manh').GetID],X #L 陈明宗#!#!于1326年出兵进攻，却被击退，此后占城保持独立。1342年他去世后，女婿茶和布底从继承人制某手中夺取王位，制某逃往安南。

en:
Jaya Simhavarman III (Chế Mân), son of Indravarman V, ruled Champa from 1288 to 1307. As crown prince Harijit he led Cham resistance to the Mongol invasion of 1282–1283 before fleeing with his father into the mountains.

A patron of Hindu temples, he endowed Po Klaung Garai and built Yang Prong Tower. In 1306 he married Princess Huyền Trân of Đại Việt, ceding the provinces of Ô and Lý as bride price. He died in 1307, and her refusal of sati kindled war with the Vietnamese.

他崇奉印度教，赞助波克朗加莱塔，并主持修建扬普龙塔。1306年，他迎娶大越陈朝的玄珍公主，以乌、里二州为聘礼；1307年他去世，玄珍拒绝按萨蒂习俗殉葬而归国，由此引发占越之间的战争。

en:
Jaya Simhavarman IV (Chế Chí), son of Chế Mân and his first queen Bhaskaradevi, was born in 1284 and ruled Champa from 1307 to 1312. Resenting the loss of the provinces of Ô and Lý ceded to Đại Việt, he stirred the Cham of Thuận and Hóa to revolt.

In 1312 Trần Anh Tông invaded with three armies; Chế Chí surrendered and was carried off to the Trần court, where he died in 1313. His brother Chế Năng replaced him under Annamese control.

Maha Sawa, whose title Bố Để renders the Cham word for chancellor, was king of Champa from 1342 to 1360. A son-in-law of King Jaya Ananda, he seized the throne when the old king died in 1342, driving out the legitimate heir Jamo, who fled to the Trần dynasty of Đại Việt.

In 1353 a large Trần army came to put Jamo on the throne, and Maha Sawa defeated it. In later years he repeatedly raided the Vietnamese borderlands. He died in 1360 and was succeeded by Po Binasuor.

Po Binasuor (Chế Bồng Nga; died 1390) was the last powerful king of Champa, ruling from about 1360. He united the Cham lands and repeatedly attacked Đại Việt, sacking Thăng Long in 1371, 1377 and 1383 and killing King Trần Duệ Tông before Vijaya in 1377.

In 1378 he wed his daughter to prince Trần Húc. Stopped by Hồ Quý Ly after 1380, he fell to a firearms volley on his barge in 1390; Ko Cheng seized the throne and his sons fled to Đại Việt.

Simhavarman, better known as Chế Năng, was a son of Chế Mân by the Javanese queen Tapasi and the last king of Champa's twelfth dynasty. After the Annamese captured his half-brother Chế Chí in 1312, the Trần court installed him as a vassal ruler.

He tried to recover the lost provinces of Ô and Lý. In 1318 Trần generals routed his army; Chế Năng fled to Java, opening the way for the Annamese-backed Chế A Nan.

en:
Chagatai (c. 1183–1242), second son of Genghis Khan and Börte, founded the Chagatai Khanate and was famed for his knowledge of Mongol law and his harsh temper. He never accepted his elder brother Jochi as legitimate.

At Gurganj he quarrelled with Jochi and was reprimanded; when Genghis told him his favourite son Mutukan had died at Bamiyan and forbade him to mourn, Chagatai wept only when alone. He applied the Yasa strictly—a code Genghis is said to have entrusted to him—and was excluded from the succession as too inflexible.

After Genghis died in 1227 he held to his will and in 1229 helped crown Ögedei; he made Ögedei limit his drinking, and the khan found a very large cup. After Ögedei died his backing gave Töregene the regency. He died in 1242, and his descendants converted to Islam more slowly than the other Mongol khanates.

察合台（约1183—1242）是成吉思汗与孛儿帖的次子，察合台汗国的开创者，以精通蒙古法律和性情严苛闻名。他始终不承认哥哥术赤的合法地位。

围攻玉龙杰赤时他与术赤争吵，受到父亲斥责；成吉思汗告知他最爱的儿子木阿秃干死于范延，禁止他哀伤，他直到独处时才痛哭。他执法极严，相传成吉思汗曾把《札撒》交给他执行；成吉思汗嫌他过于执拗，把他排除在继承人之外。

1227年成吉思汗去世后，他坚守遗愿，1229年促成窝阔台登基。他要窝阔台少喝酒，窝阔台便换了一只特大的杯子。窝阔台去世后，他支持脱列哥那摄政。1242年他去世，子孙皈依伊斯兰教比其他蒙古汗国慢得多。

en:
Charles-François de Broglie, marquis de Ruffec (1719–1781), was a French general and diplomat, second son of the first duc de Broglie. He fought in the War of the Austrian Succession and the Seven Years' War.

As ambassador to Poland from 1752 he secretly sought to place the prince de Conti on the Polish throne, but the Anglo-Prussian alliance of 1756 overturned his plans. From 1767 he headed Louis XV's private intelligence network, the Secret du Roi. Exiled to Ruffec in 1771, he continued to advise the king in secret.

With Beaumarchais he organized covert French aid to the American insurgents, helping finance La Fayette's voyage in 1777. He died in 1781 and was buried in Angoulême Cathedral.

夏尔-弗朗索瓦·德·布罗伊，吕费克侯爵（1719—1781），是法国将领与外交家，第一代布罗伊公爵的次子。他参加过奥地利王位继承战争和七年战争。

1752年起他出任驻波兰大使，暗中谋划让孔蒂亲王登上波兰王位，但1756年英普结盟打乱了他的计划。1767年起，他主管路易十五的私人情报网“国王密档”。1771年被流放至吕费克后，他仍秘密向国王献策。

他与博马舍合作，组织法国对美洲起义者的秘密援助，并于1777年资助拉法耶特渡海赴美洲。1781年他去世，葬于昂古莱姆大教堂。

en:
Amir Chupan (c. 1262–1327) was a Mongol of the Sulduz clan who became commander-in-chief and power behind the Ilkhanid throne, founder of the Chupanid dynasty. After quelling Gilan in 1307 he was made amir al-umara by Il-Khan Öljeitü, whose daughter he married. Under Abu Sa'id he crushed Amir Irinjin's revolt in 1319 and married the Il-Khan's sister Sati Beg.

In August 1327 Abu Sa'id killed his son Demasq Kaja; his army deserted and he fled to Herat, where the Kartid ruler had him strangled that November.

en:
Demasq Kaja (c. 1300–1327), third son of Amir Chupan, was born during Ghazan's siege of Damascus, which gave him his name. He became viceroy of Azerbaijan and Iraq, and from 1325 he wielded the vizier's authority, effectively ruling the Ilkhanid capital Sultaniya while Chupan campaigned in Khurasan.

Abu Sa'id used Demasq's affair with a former concubine of the late Öljeitü as a pretext to move against him. He was captured and killed on 25 August 1327, the first Chupanid to fall.

德马什克·火者（约1300—1327）是埃米尔·出班的第三子，生于合赞汗围攻大马士革期间，并以该城得名。他受任阿塞拜疆与伊拉克总督，1325年起掌握维齐尔大权，在出班远征呼罗珊时实际主持伊儿汗都城苏丹尼耶。

不赛因汗以他与完者都的旧妾私通为借口动手。1327年8月25日，他被俘处死，是第一个倒下的出班家族成员。

en:
Hasan Kuchak (c. 1319–1343), ‘the Little’, was a Chupanid prince who rebuilt his family's power from the wreck of the Ilkhanate. His father Timurtash had been executed by the Mamluks in 1328, while Hasan Buzurg's Jalayirids held western Persia behind a puppet Ilkhan. He reunited the Chupanids by claiming his father was still alive and presenting a slave as Timurtash, even marrying him to the dead man's widows.

On 16 July 1338 he defeated Hasan Buzurg near Van and, aged nineteen, took Tabriz. As kingmaker he raised Sati Beg to the throne, then installed Suleiman Khan and forced her to marry the new khan.

He defeated the Jalayirids again near Maraga in 1340. His wife Izzat Malik murdered him in December 1343. He left no heir, and the Chupanid lands were divided.

哈桑·库楚克（约1319—1343），绰号“小哈桑”，是出班家族王公，在伊利汗国的废墟上重建了家族势力。父亲帖木儿塔什于1328年被马穆鲁克人处死，而谢赫·大哈散的札剌亦儿人则扶植傀儡伊利汗，掌控波斯西部。哈桑声称父亲仍在人世，让一名奴隶假扮帖木儿塔什，甚至让他迎娶亡父的遗孀，借此重新团结出班宗室。

1338年7月16日，他在凡城附近击败谢赫·大哈散，十九岁便夺取大不里士。他拥立撒迪别为汗，随后改立速来蛮，并迫使撒迪别嫁给速来蛮。

1340年他在马拉盖附近再败札剌亦儿人。1343年12月，妻子伊扎特·马利克将他杀害。他没有继承人，出班家族的领地被瓜分。

en:
Malek Ashraf (c. 1318–1357) was the second son of the Chobanid Timurtash and the last Chobanid to hold power in the Ilkhanate. After his brother Hasan Kucek's death in 1343 he defeated his uncles, had Yagi Basti murdered in 1344, and raised Anushirwan as a puppet Ilkhan before marching to Tabriz in 1346.

A harsh and suspicious ruler, he failed to take Baghdad in 1347 and Isfahan in 1350. His rule ended in 1357, when the Golden Horde khan Jani Beg conquered Tabriz.

马立克·阿什拉夫（约1318—1357）是楚邦系将领帖木儿塔什的次子，也是伊儿汗国境内最后一位掌有实权的楚邦系统治者。1343年其兄小哈桑死后，他击败两位叔父，于1344年杀死亚吉·巴斯提，拥立阿努失儿万为傀儡伊儿汗，随后于1346年进军大不里士。

他为政残暴多疑，1347年攻取巴格达失败，1350年又未能拿下伊斯法罕。1357年金帐汗札尼别攻陷大不里士，他的统治随之终结。

Sati Beg (fl. 1316–1345) was an Ilkhanid princess, daughter of Il-Khan Öljaitü and sister of Abu Sa'id. In 1319 she married the powerful amir Chupan, executed after falling out with her brother in 1327. After Abu Sa'id's death she married in turn the il-khans Arpa and then Suleiman Khan.

In 1338 the Chobanid leader Hasan Kucek set her on the Ilkhanid throne as a puppet queen, and she struck coins in her own name as sultan. Deposed by 1339, she vanishes from the records after 1345.

Suleiman Khan (birth name Ilyas; died c. 1345) was a Genghisid prince descended from the Ilkhan Hülegü. In 1339 the Chobanid Hasan Kucek enthroned him as a puppet Ilkhan, and he married Sati Beg.

In 1340 he fought against the Jalayirid Hasan Buzurg at the Jaghatu, and he was later defeated by Eretna near Sivas. After Hasan Kucek's murder in 1343 he fled to Diyarbakir, where coins were still struck in his name until 1345.

Surgan (c. 1320–1345) was a Chobanid prince, son of Amir Chupan and the princess Sati Beg. As governor of Karabakh he backed his nephew Hasan Kucek against the Jalayirids in campaigns of 1338 and 1340, receiving the government of Persian Iraq.

Angry at Hasan Kucek's treatment of his mother, he defected to Hasan Buzurg, but was defeated and imprisoned in Anatolia in 1341. Released after Hasan Kucek's murder in 1343, he fought Malek Ashraf for the Chobanid lands, lost in 1345, and was executed after fleeing to Baghdad.

en:
Ala al-Din Timurtash (c. 1298–1328) was the second son of Amir Chupan and governor of Anatolia from 1319. In 1321–1322 he declared independence and allied with the Mamluks, but submitted when his father marched against him. From 1324 he attacked the Anatolian beyliks, killing Dündar and, around 1326, Süleyman II, whose body he threw into Lake Beyşehir.

After Chupan's fall in 1327 he fled to Mamluk Egypt, where Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad welcomed him, then had him executed on 12 August 1328 and sent his head to Abu Sa'id.

en:
Chen Youliang (1320–1363) founded the Chen Han regime on the middle Yangtze and was the strongest rival of Zhu Yuanzhang. Born to a fishing family in Mianyang, Hubei, he joined the Red Turban movement under Ni Wenjun. In 1357 he killed Ni Wenjun, who was plotting against Xu Shouhui, then overran Jiangxi, Anhui and Fujian.

In 1359 he seized Xu and made himself King of Han at Jiangzhou, and in 1360 had Xu murdered and proclaimed himself emperor. That year he attacked Zhu's base at Yingtian, but Zhu ambushed him at Longwan and he fled to Jiangzhou.

In 1363 he returned with a fleet reported at 600,000 men and fought Zhu on Lake Poyang. Zhu's smaller fleet won with fire attacks after three days, and a month later Chen was killed by an arrow breaking out of a blockade. His second son Chen Li surrendered in 1364.

陈友谅（1320—1363）是长江中游陈汉政权的建立者，也是朱元璋最强劲的对手。他出身湖北沔阳的渔家，后来投入红巾军倪文俊麾下。1357年，他杀死图谋对付徐寿辉的倪文俊，随后席卷江西、安徽和福建。

1359年他挟持徐寿辉迁往江州，自称汉王；1360年又刺杀徐寿辉，登基称帝。同年他进逼朱元璋的根据地应天，朱元璋在龙湾设伏，陈友谅败回江州。

1363年他率据称六十万水军再战，与朱元璋在鄱阳湖交锋。朱元璋的船队较小，借助火攻，激战三天后获胜；一个月后，陈友谅在突破封锁时中箭而死。次子陈理于1364年投降。

en:
Alghu (died 1266) was a son of Baidar and a grandson of Chagatai Khan. In 1260, during the Toluid civil war, Ariq Böke made him ruler of the Chagatai ulus against Mubarak Shah, and Alghu married Mubarak Shah's mother Orghana. He seized Transoxiana.

He turned against Ariq Böke in 1262, killing his general Qara Buqa before Ariq Böke ravaged the Ili valley and drove him south. In 1263 he submitted to Kublai and defeated Kaidu near Otrar. He died in 1266 and was buried at Almaliq.

zh:
阿鲁忽（？—1266年）是拜答儿之子、察合台之孙。1260年拖雷家族内战时，阿里不哥扶立他为察合台汗国之汗，与木八剌沙及其母兀鲁忽乃对抗，他随后娶兀鲁忽乃为妻。他掌控河中地区。

他于1262年起兵反叛阿里不哥，斩杀其大将哈剌不花；阿里不哥随即洗劫伊犁河流域，把他逼退到南方。1263年他归附忽必烈，又与海都交战，在讹答剌附近取胜。1266年他去世，葬于阿力麻里。

en:
Ali Khalil, better known as Ali-Sultan, was a descendant of Kadan and thus of the house of Ögedei. In 1339 he attacked the camp of the Chagatai khan Yesun Temur and seized the throne at Almalik, the only Ögedeid restoration over the Chagatai ulus since Kaidu's day.

A Muslim ruler, he pressed Islam on the Chagatai Mongols and persecuted other faiths, ordering six Franciscan friars put to death at Almalik in 1339. He reigned until about 1342.

阿里·哈利勒，通称阿里算端，是合丹的后裔，属窝阔台一系。1339年，他攻打察合台汗也孙帖木儿的斡耳朵，在阿力麻里夺取汗位，这是海都时代以后窝阔台系唯一一次复辟察合台兀鲁思。

他以穆斯林君主的身份在察合台蒙古人中强力推行伊斯兰教，迫害其他信仰，并于1339年下令在阿力麻里处死六名方济各会修士。他约在1342年之前在位。

en:
Baidar, also called Peta, was the sixth son of Chagatai Khan and a grandson of Genghis Khan. From 1235 to 1241 he joined the Mongol campaign into Europe alongside his nephew Büri, commanding the detachment sent into Poland with Kadan.

His troops crossed the frozen Vistula in February 1241, sacked Kraków, and on 9 April crushed an army under Duke Henry II the Pious at Legnica, where Henry was killed. After ravaging Moravia he rode south to join Batu in Hungary. His son Alghu later ruled the Chagatai ulus.

zh:

1241年2月，蒙古军渡过冰封的维斯瓦河，洗劫克拉科夫；4月9日在列格尼卡战役击溃联军，公爵亨里克二世阵亡。此后他纵兵蹂躏摩拉维亚，再南下匈牙利与拔都的主力会合。他的儿子阿鲁忽后来成为察合台汗。

en:
Bayan Qulï (died 1358), a grandson of Duwa Khan, was the puppet khan of the Western Chagatai ulus from 1348 to 1358. In 1348 the Qara'unas amir Qazaghan, effective master of Transoxiana, raised him to the throne after executing Danishmendji, and for a decade he reigned without real authority.

When Qazaghan was assassinated in 1358 his son 'Abdullah succeeded him and soon had Bayan Qulï killed. A pious Muslim and disciple of the sheikh Saif ed-Din Boharsi, he was buried opposite his teacher's grave at Bukhara, where a mausoleum was raised over him that same year.

1358年加兹罕遇刺，其子阿卜杜拉继位，不久便将拜延忽里杀死。他是虔诚的穆斯林，师从谢赫赛夫丁·巴哈尔兹，死后葬于布哈拉的谢赫墓对面，同年墓上建起陵寝。

en:
Buqa Temür was a great-great-grandson of Chagatai Khan and a son of Qadaqchi. Around 1272 he killed Negübei, who had rebelled against Kaidu, and Kaidu rewarded him with the Chagatai throne.

Soon after his enthronement he fell seriously ill and never made his authority effective, proving helpless against raids by the sons of Alghu and Baraq. In 1282 the descendants of Alghu and Baraq overthrew him, and Baraq's son Duwa succeeded him.

en:
Büri (died 1252) was a son of Mutukan and a grandson of Chagatai Khan, who raised him after Mutukan was killed at Bamyan in 1221; his Turkic name means wolf. Brave, hot-tempered and quarrelsome in drink, he joined Batu's western campaign from 1236, but he and Güyük mocked Batu, and Ögedei recalled him in disgrace.

In 1241 he ravaged Wallachia and Transylvania, and later settled German miners on his appanage near Talas. After backing the regent Oghul Qaimish against Möngke, he was handed to Batu and executed in 1252.

en:
Buzan (died c. 1335), the son of Duwa Temür, was briefly khan of the Chagatai Khanate in 1334–1335. In 1334 he rose against his uncle Tarmashirin, whose conversion to Islam and settlement in Transoxiana had alienated the Mongol princes, and killed him.

Buzan then took the throne; sources call him a Muslim himself, yet he ruled in favour of the traditional Mongol Yassa. His reign lasted less than a year before his cousin Changshi overthrew him.

en:
Changshi (r. 1335–1338) was one of the last effective khans of the Chagatai Khanate, a grandson of Khan Duwa through his father Ebugen. In 1335 he seized the throne from Buzan and reasserted the importance of Almaliq.

Favourably disposed toward Nestorian Christians, he allowed missionaries to preach and granted land for a friary, earning a letter of thanks from Pope Benedict XII in 1338. He also sent the Yuan emperor Toghon Temür 170 Russian captives as tribute. Chinese accounts say he was murdered in 1338 by his younger brother Yesun Temur, who succeeded him.

As the first khan of the Western Chagatai ulus set up by the tribal amirs, he ruled only as Qazaghan's puppet from his seat in Transoxiana. He was executed by Qazaghan in 1348 and replaced by Bayan Qulï.

他是西察合台兀鲁思第一位由部落异密拥立的汗，实权尽归加兹罕。他于1348年被加兹罕处死，汗位由#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('chg_bayan_quli_borjigin').GetID],X #L 拜延忽里#!#!继承。

en:
Duwa Temür (died c. 1331), a son of Duwa, was khan of the Chagatai Khanate in 1329–1330. In 1313, during Esen Buqa I's revolt against the Yuan, he surrendered to Yuan forces, and in 1329 he seized power by overthrowing his brother Eljigidey.

He was still ruling in 1330, when with the khans of the Golden Horde and the Ilkhanate he presented a map of his realm to the Yuan court. Muslim writers claim his brother Tarmashirin soon deposed him.

zh:
笃来帖木儿（？—约1331）是察合台汗笃哇之子，1329至1330年为察合台汗国大汗。1313年也先不花起兵反抗元朝时，他曾向元军投降；1329年他推翻兄弟燕只吉台夺取汗位。

他1330年仍在位，曾与钦察汗国、伊儿汗国的大汗一同向元朝进献本藩地图。穆斯林史家称他不久即被兄弟答儿麻失里废黜。

en:
Eljigidey (died 1329), a son of Duwa, succeeded his brother Kebek as khan of the Chagatai Khanate in 1326. During the Yuan succession struggle of 1328–1329 he backed his ally Kusala, who was enthroned at the Yuan court in 1329 but died in suspicious circumstances within months.

The new Yuan emperor, Tugh Temür, sent an envoy with an imperial seal to appease him. Eljigidey's brief reign ended in 1329 when another brother, Duwa Temür, overthrew him.

zh:
燕只吉台（？—1329）是察合台汗笃哇之子，1326年其兄怯别去世后继位为察合台汗国大汗。在1328至1329年元朝皇位之争中，他支持盟友和世㻋；和世㻋于1329年登基为元明宗，数月后便蹊跷死去。

新帝元文宗图帖睦尔派使者携印玺前往安抚。1329年，他的另一个兄弟笃来帖木儿将他推翻，短暂统治就此结束。

en:
Esen Buqa I (died c. 1318), a son of Duwa, spent his early years at the Yuan capital of Dadu. After his brother Kebek overthrew Taliqu in 1308 or 1309, a quriltai in 1310 proclaimed him Chagatai khan.

He began on good terms with the Yuan and sent tribute, but border quarrels brought war in 1314 with both the Yuan and the Ilkhan. Yuan forces defeated him in 1315, and he died around 1318, after which Kebek returned to the throne.

en:
Kadan was a son of Ögedei Khan by a concubine and a grandson of Genghis Khan, raised in Chagatai's ordo. He campaigned west with Batu, and in 1241 led a diversionary army through Poland, helping defeat the Silesians at Legnica.

He then ravaged Moravia and Hungary, sacking Buda and pursuing Béla IV into Croatia and Dalmatia until Ögedei's death recalled the Mongols in 1242. He backed Möngke's election in 1251 and later supported Kublai against Ariq Böke, holding his appanage around Beshbalik.

zh:
合丹是窝阔台汗庶出之子、成吉思汗之孙，幼年在察合台的宫帐中长大。他早年随拔都西征，1241年率领偏师攻入波兰，参与了在莱格尼察击破西里西亚军队的战役。

此后他纵掠摩拉维亚与匈牙利，焚破布达，并追击匈牙利王贝拉四世至克罗地亚和达尔马提亚，直至1242年窝阔台死讯传来才随军东返。1251年他拥戴蒙哥即位，后来又支持忽必烈对抗阿里不哥，其封地在别失八里一带。

en:
Kaidu (c. 1235–1301), a posthumous son of Qashi and grandson of Ögedei Khan, led the House of Ögedei. In 1252 Möngke enfeoffed him at Qayaliq. He defeated the Chagatai khan Baraq and divided Transoxiana with him at the Talas kurultai of 1269, and in 1271 became ruler of the reconstituted Ulus of Ögedei.

From 1282 he controlled the Chagatai khan Duwa and waged decades of war against Kublai's Yuan dynasty. Wounded fighting Qayishan at Mount Tiejiangu in September 1301, he died late that year.

zh:
海都（约1235—1301）是窝阔台汗之孙、合失的遗腹子，后来成为窝阔台家族的领袖。1252年蒙哥将海押立封给他。他击败察合台汗八剌，并于1269年塔拉斯忽里勒台与八剌瓜分河中地区，1271年被拥立为重建的窝阔台兀鲁思之主。

1282年起，他扶立都哇为察合台汗并加以控制，同忽必烈的元朝进行了数十年战争。1301年9月，他在帖坚古山与海山作战时负伤，同年年底死去。

en:
Kebek, a son of Duwa, overthrew Taliqu in 1308 or 1309 and became Chagatai khan. Near Almaliq he defeated the invading sons of Kaidu, ending the Ögedeid threat, but at a quriltai in 1310 he yielded the throne to his brother Esen Buqa.

When Esen Buqa died around 1320, Kebek ruled again and killed the rebel prince Yasa'ur. He kept peace with the Yuan, standardized the coinage, promoted agriculture, and built Qarshi as his capital. He died around 1326, succeeded by his brother Eljigidey.

zh:
怯别是笃哇之子。1308或1309年他推翻塔里忽，成为察合台汗，在阿力麻里附近击败来犯的海都诸子，终结了窝阔台系复国的威胁。1310年他在忽里台大会上把汗位让给兄长也先不花。

约1320年也先不花死后，怯别再度执政，于1320年攻杀反叛宗王牙撒吾儿。他与元朝保持和平，统一币制、扶持农业，并营建卡尔希作为定居都城。他约于1326年去世，弟燕只吉台继位。

en:
Khabul Shah was the nominal khan of the Western Chagatai ulus from about 1364, a Chagatai prince descended from Khan Eljigidey. Before his enthronement he lived as a Sufi dervish in a mountain cave and wrote poetry.

In 1364 the emirs Husayn and Timur, having seized Transoxiana, raised him from his dervish's rags to the throne in a ceremony built around the royal cup. He ruled as Amir Husayn's puppet and perished as Timur took power, either deposed in 1366 or executed in 1370.

合不勒沙是约1364年起的西察合台兀鲁思名义可汗，为察合台汗燕只吉台的后裔。即位之前，他是隐居山洞的苏菲派托钵僧，还擅长写诗。

1364年，攻占河中地区的异密忽辛与帖木儿把他从托钵僧的破衣烂衫中扶出，在以授予御杯为核心的仪式上将他立为汗。他只是异密忽辛的傀儡，在帖木儿掌权之际丧命，一说1366年被废，一说1370年被处死。

en:
Khashin (c. 1215–c. 1236) was the fifth son of Ögedei Khan and a grandson of Genghis Khan. His name came from Hexi, the Mongol name for the Tangut kingdom of Western Xia, against which Genghis was campaigning at his birth.

Like his father he was a heavy drinker and died young while Ögedei still lived; after his death his name became taboo and the Hexi lands were called only Tangut. His son Kaidu later led the House of Ögedei in its long wars against Kublai.

合失（约1215—约1236）是窝阔台大汗第五子、成吉思汗之孙。他出生时正值成吉思汗出征西夏，其名便来自蒙古人对西夏的称呼“河西”（音近合失）。

他与父亲一样嗜酒，年少而亡，时窝阔台仍在位；他死后名字成为忌讳，河西之地只改称唐兀。其子海都后来统领窝阔台一系，长期与忽必烈争战。

en:
Könchek (died 1308), a son of Duwa, succeeded his father as khan of the Chagatai Khanate in 1307 with the recognition of the Yuan court. He kept the peace with the Yuan after decades of war, and in 1308 his envoys presented the Great Khan with census registers of his cities and three years' tribute in token of submission.

During his short reign the Delhi Sultanate recovered Lahore. He ruled little more than a year and died in 1308, after which Taliqu seized the throne.

宽阇（？—1308）是笃哇之子，1307年父亲死后经元朝册封继位为察合台汗。他与元朝结束数十年战端、保持友好，1308年向元朝进献户口清册，并请以三年贡赋上交，以示恭顺。

他在位期间，德里苏丹国收复了拉合尔。宽阇在位仅一年有余，于1308年去世，此后塔里忽夺取了汗位。

en:
Mubarak Shah (died 1276), son of Qara Hülegü and Orghana, was the first Chagatai khan to convert to Islam. He succeeded his father in 1252 under his mother's regency, until Ariq Böke replaced him with Alghu in 1260. After Alghu's death Orghana restored him in 1266 without Kublai Khan's approval; Kublai backed Baraq, who won over the army and drove him from the throne that September.

He later supported Kaidu against Baraq in 1271, then defected to the Ilkhan Abaqa and led the Qara'unas, dying on campaign in Persia in 1276.

zh:
木八剌沙（？—1276）是哈剌旭烈与兀鲁忽乃之子，也是第一位皈依伊斯兰教的察合台汗。1252年父亲去世后他幼年继位，由母亲摄政，1260年阿里不哥改立阿鲁忽而被取代。阿鲁忽死后，兀鲁忽乃于1266年未经忽必烈同意将他重新扶上汗位；忽必烈转而支持八剌，八剌收买军队，在当年9月逼他退位。

1271年他先助海都攻打八剌，随后转投伊儿汗阿八哈，统领合剌乌纳思人，1276年在波斯征战时死于军中。

en:
Muhammad ibn Pulad was a khan of the Chagatai Khanate who reigned in 1342–1343. A Chinggisid prince of the Chagatai line, he was a grandson of the former khan Könchek through his son Pulad.

The genealogical chronicle Shajrat ul Atrak credits him with trying to halt the political dissolution of the ulus during his brief reign. Apparently a Muslim, judging by his name, he was succeeded by Qazan ibn Yasaur.

麻哈没的（穆罕默德·伊本·不剌）是1342—1343年在位的察合台汗。他是察合台系的成吉思汗后裔，为前汗宽阇之孙、不剌之子。

谱系编年史《突厥世系》记载，他在短暂的统治期间力图遏止兀鲁思的政治瓦解。从名字判断他应是穆斯林，继他之后登上汗位的是牙撒吾儿之子合赞。

en:
Negübei was a grandson of Chagatai Khan and a son of Sarban, installed as khan of the Chagatai Khanate by Kaidu in 1271 after the death of Baraq. Unwilling to rule as Kaidu's puppet, he rebelled within a year.

Kaidu sent an army against him and defeated his forces. Negübei fled eastward but was killed late in 1271 or in 1272, and Kaidu replaced him with Buqa Temür.

zh:
聂古伯是察合台汗之孙、撒儿班之子。1271年八剌死后，海都拥立他为察合台汗国可汗。他不愿充当海都的傀儡，即位不到一年便起兵反叛。

海都发兵讨伐，将其击败。聂古伯东逃后于1271年底或1272年被杀，海都随后改立不合帖木儿为汗。

en:
Ögedei Khan (c. 1186–11 December 1241), third son of Genghis Khan, was the second khan of the Mongol Empire, extending Mongol conquests into northern China and Europe. At Gurganj in 1221 Genghis made him sole commander; later quarrels among his brothers confirmed him as heir. After Genghis's 1227 death and Tolui's regency, he was elected khan in 1229.

He destroyed the Jin in 1234; in 1233 Yelü Chucai talked him out of Subutai's plan to sack Kaifeng. With Yelü he fixed taxation and founded Karakorum; his armies beat Poles and Hungarians in 1241.

A notorious drinker, he let Chagatai set a watcher over his cups, and the story goes he had cups made twice the size. He died at dawn on 11 December 1241 after a night's drinking, nobles blaming his lack of self-control. His widow Töregene ruled as regent for five years before his son Güyük was elected.

zh:
窝阔台汗（约1186—1241年12月11日）是成吉思汗第三子、大蒙古国第二位大汗，将父亲的征服推向华北和欧洲。1221年玉龙杰赤之战，成吉思汗令他独掌全军；兄长们后来再起争执，他被确认为继承人。1227年成吉思汗去世，经拖雷监国，他于1229年被推举为大汗。

他1234年灭金；1233年耶律楚材劝阻了速不台洗劫汴京的计划。他与耶律楚材确立赋税，营建哈剌和林；1241年蒙古军击败波兰人和匈牙利人。

他嗜酒出名：察合台派官员盯着他的酒杯，传说他就让人做了大一倍的酒杯。1241年12月11日黎明，他在一夜狂饮后去世，贵族认定他死于缺乏节制。遗孀脱列哥那摄政五年，之后其子贵由当选大汗。

en:
Qadaqchi, also called Qadaqai Setsen, was a Chagataid prince whom the genealogies identify as the eldest son of Büri and great-grandson of Chagatai Khan. He served the Great Khan Möngke, who once ordered him to shave his head in the manner of a cleric.

He later accompanied Möngke's campaign against the Southern Song and died on the march. His sons Buqa Temür and Taliqu both later occupied the Chagatai throne, reigning in 1272–1282 and 1308–1309.

合答乞（又称合答乞·薛禅）是察合台系宗王，诸谱系认为他是不里的长子、察合台的曾孙。他效力于大汗蒙哥，曾奉蒙哥之命像僧侣一样剃发。

en:
Qara Hülegü (died 1252) was the youngest son of Mutukan and the heir chosen by Chagatai for the Chagatai ulus in 1242. His mother governed as regent during his youth. In 1246 Güyük, favouring his friend Yesü Möngke, deposed Qara Hülegü and gave the throne to his uncle.

He then backed Möngke Khan against the Ögedeids, and after Möngke's election in 1251 was restored. He died on the road in 1252, leaving his widow Orghana to rule as regent for their son Mubarak Shah.

哈剌旭烈（？—1252年）是木阿秃干的幼子，1242年由察合台本人生前指定为察合台汗国继承人。因他年纪尚轻，由母亲临朝摄政。1246年，大汗贵由偏宠亲信也速蒙哥，废黜哈剌旭烈，把汗位交给了这位叔父。

此后他支持蒙哥对抗窝阔台系；1251年蒙哥即位后恢复他的汗位。1252年他在途中去世，遗孀兀鲁忽乃为儿子木八剌沙摄政。

en:
Qazan (died 1346), son of the Chagatayid prince Yasa'ur, was khan of the Chagatai ulus from about 1343. He moved to curb the Turkic nobility of Transoxiana, who rallied behind the Qara'unas amir Qazaghan. In a battle of 1345 north of the Iron Gates, Qazan routed Qazaghan and put out one of his eyes, but then withdrew to winter at Qarshi instead of pursuing.

Qazaghan rebuilt his forces, counterattacked in 1346 and killed Qazan. With his death the Chagatai khans lost real power in Transoxiana and the ulus split in two.

zh:
合赞（？—1346），又称合赞算端，是察合台宗王牙撒吾儿之子，约1343年成为察合台兀鲁思的汗。他着手压制河中地区的突厥贵族，贵族们便聚集在合剌乌纳思部异密加兹罕周围。1345年在铁门以北的会战中，合赞击溃加兹罕并射瞎他一只眼睛，却没有乘胜追击，而是返回卡尔施过冬。

加兹罕重整军力，于1346年反攻并杀死合赞。他死后，察合台汗在河中地区丧失实权，兀鲁思分裂为东西两部。

en:
Sarban was a son of Chagatai Khan and a grandson of Genghis Khan, born to a mother whose name and rank are unrecorded. Most manuscripts of Rashid al-Din's Jami' al-tawarikh place him fourth among Chagatai's sons, ahead of Yesü Möngke and Baidar.

His son Negübei briefly headed the Chagatai ulus in 1271–1272 and was killed after rebelling against Kaidu. Another son, Qushqi, served on Möngke Khan's campaign against the Southern Song.

撒儿班（《新元史》作撒巴）是察合台之子、成吉思汗之孙，生母的名位均不见于记载。拉施德丁《史集》多数写本把他列为察合台第四子，排在也速蒙哥、拜答儿之前。

en:
Shah Temur was a son of the Chagatai khan Yesun Temur and a descendant of Genghis Khan through Chagatai. In 1358 the amir 'Abdullah, son of Qazaghan, murdered the reigning puppet khan Bayan Quli in Transoxiana and raised Shah Temur to the throne of the western Chagatai Khanate.

'Abdullah's rule was weak, and tribal chiefs Hajji Beg of the Barlas and Buyan Suldus rose against him, drove him out, and killed Shah Temur later that same year, leaving the western khanate without a khan.

en:
Taliqu was a grandson of Büri and a son of Qadaqchi and a princess of Kerman. After Könchek died in 1308, he seized the Chagatai throne.

A Muslim, he pressed Islam on his Mongol subjects, and his rule was resented both for this and because he was not a descendant of Duwa. The sons of Duwa revolted and chose Kebek as khan, and Taliqu was killed in 1309, reportedly assassinated at a banquet.

塔里忽是不里之孙、合答乞之子，母亲是起儿漫的公主。1308年宽阇死后，他夺取了察合台汗位。

他信奉伊斯兰教，极力向蒙古部众推行，加之他并非笃哇的后裔，统治遭到笃哇一系的仇视。笃哇诸子起兵反叛，拥立怯别为汗。塔里忽于1309年被杀，据传是在宴会上遇刺。

en:
Ala-ad-din Tarmashirin (died 1334), a son of Duwa, ruled the Chagatai Khanate from 1331. Before his enthronement he led a plundering raid into the Delhi Sultanate in 1327 and sacked Lahore in 1329. One of the first Chagatai khans to embrace Islam, his faith and preference for the cities of Transoxiana angered his traditionalist nobles, who charged him with abandoning the Yassa.

He was deposed at a kurultai and overtaken near Samarkand. There, in 1334, the eastern princes under Buzan killed him.

答儿麻失里（？—1334）是察合台汗笃哇之子，1331年起统治察合台汗国。继位前，他于1327年对德里苏丹国发动大规模掠夺性远征，1329年洗劫拉合尔。他是最早皈依伊斯兰教的察合台汗之一，但他的信仰和偏爱河中城市的做法引起守旧蒙古宗王不满，被指背弃《大扎撒》。

en:
Taraghai (c. 1290–1360) was a minor emir of the Turkified Mongol Barlas confederation in Transoxiana, serving the khans of the Chagatai Khanate around Kish. Unlike his militarised kinsmen he lived as a pious Muslim drawn to Sufism and the Naqshbandi order.

By his wife Tekina Khatun, held by Timurid tradition to descend from Genghis Khan, he fathered several children, including Timur, born near Kish in 1336. He died on 12 March 1360, and the Zafarnama records Timur returning home to settle his estate.

塔剌海（约1290—1360）是河中地区突厥化蒙古巴鲁剌思部落的小埃米尔，在渴石一带臣事察合台汗国的汗。与尚武的同族不同，他是虔诚的穆斯林，倾心苏非主义和纳克什班迪教团。

他的妻子特金娜·可敦据帖木儿朝传统说是成吉思汗的后裔；子女众多，1336年在渴石附近生下帖木儿。塔剌海于1360年3月12日去世，《帖木儿武功记》记载帖木儿当时返乡料理父亲的遗产。

en:
Timur (1336–1405) was a Turco-Mongol conqueror from Transoxiana who founded the Timurid Empire. He was born near Kesh into the Turkified Mongol Barlas tribe. Around 1363 arrows wounded his leg and right hand, in one account while stealing a sheep, laming him: the Persian Temur-i Lang, Timur the Lame, inspired the name Tamerlane.

Not Genghis Khan's descendant, he ruled as emir behind a puppet Chagatai khan. By 1370 he held the western Chagatai Khanate, and from Samarkand conquered Persia, defeated Tokhtamysh in 1395, sacked Delhi in 1398 and crushed the Ottomans at Ankara in 1402, capturing Bayezid. Scholars estimate his wars killed millions.

In December 1404 he marched against Ming China, fell ill beyond the Syr Darya and died at Farab in February 1405, and was buried at Gur-e-Amir. The empire fragmented; his grandson Ulugh Beg ruled in 1411–1449 and his descendant Babur founded the Mughal Empire.

帖木儿（1336—1405）是出身河中地区的突厥—蒙古征服者，帖木儿帝国的建立者。他生于渴石附近，属于已经突厥化的蒙古巴鲁剌思部落。约1363年，他的腿和右手各中一箭，有一种说法是在偷羊时中箭，从此跛足：波斯语的“帖木儿·朗”即跛子帖木儿，是“塔梅尔兰”一名的由来。

由于不是成吉思汗的后裔，他以埃米尔的身份，奉一位傀儡察合台汗之名执政。到1370年他已掌控西察合台汗国，此后以撒马尔罕为基地征服波斯，1395年击败脱脱迷失，1398年洗劫德里，1402年在安卡拉击溃奥斯曼军队，俘获巴耶济德。学者估计，他的战争夺去了数百万人的生命。

1404年12月，他出兵攻明，在锡尔河对岸病倒，1405年2月死于法拉卜，葬于古尔·埃米尔陵。帝国分裂，其孙兀鲁伯于1411至1449年统治，其后裔巴布尔则建立了莫卧儿帝国。

en:
Tughlugh Timur (1312/13–1363) was the first khan of the Eastern Chagatai khanate, or Moghulistan. In 1347–1348 the Dughlat amir Bulaji brought the young Chagatai prince to power at Almalik, after more than a decade without a khan. Persuaded by the khoja Jamal ad-Din, he embraced Islam and in 1353 made his faith public, with one hundred and sixty thousand Moghuls said to convert with him.

Seeking to reunite the ulus, he invaded Transoxiana in 1360 and again in 1361, and in 1362 left his son Ilyas Khoja as viceroy there. He died in 1363 and the reunification collapsed.

秃忽鲁帖木儿（1312/13—1363）是东察合台汗国（蒙兀儿斯坦）第一代可汗。汗位空悬十余年后，杜格拉特部异密播鲁只于1347—1348年在阿力麻里拥立这位年轻的察合台宗王即位。他受和卓札马鲁丁感召皈依伊斯兰教，1353年公开宣布入教，相传十六万蒙兀儿人随他一同入教。

为重新统一兀鲁思，他于1360年和1361年两度进兵河中，1362年留其子也里牙思火者为河中总督。他于1363年去世，汗国的统一随即瓦解。

en:
Yasa'ur (died 1320) was a Chagatai prince, the son of Chübei and father of the future khan Qazan. In 1314 he campaigned against the Ilkhanate with Kebek, defeating an Ilkhan army before Esen Buqa recalled the forces. Accused by Kebek of colluding with the enemy, he defected to Ilkhan Öljeitü, who settled him in the Badghis pastures.

After Öljeitü's death he rebelled against Abu Sa'id in 1319, raiding Mazandaran. Driven back from Herat, he was killed in 1320 by Kebek, now khan.

牙撒吾儿（？—1320）是察合台宗王，出伯之子，后来的可汗合赞之父。1314年，他与怯别一同出征伊儿汗国，击败伊儿汗军队，随后也先不花将察合台军队召回。他被怯别指控通敌，遂投奔伊儿汗完者都，获准在巴德吉斯草原游牧。

完者都死后，他于1319年起兵反叛不赛因，攻掠马赞达兰，在赫拉特被击退。1320年，已成为察合台汗的怯别将他杀死。

Yesü Möngke (died 1252) was the fifth son of Chagatai Khan and the third ruler of the Chagatai ulus. Around 1246 his friend Güyük deposed the chosen heir Qara Hülëgü and made him khan instead. He gave himself up to drink, leaving affairs to his wife and vizier.

After Güyük's death he backed the Ögedeid princes against Möngke and boycotted the quriltai that elected him in 1251. Möngke then restored Qara Hülëgü, who died on the journey; his widow Orghana seized power and had him executed in 1252.

Yesun Temur (r. 1338–1339) was khan of the Chagatai Khanate, a son of Prince Ebugen and younger brother of Changshi Khan. He came to power after Changshi's death, whose circumstances remain unclear.

Chinese annals say he murdered his brother, was rebuked by his mother and drank heavily thereafter. His short reign was marked by strife between traditional Mongol factions and the spread of Islam. In 1339 he was overthrown by Ali-Sultan, a prince of the House of Ogedei.

Chen Zuyi (died 1407) was a Chinese pirate chief from Chaozhou in Guangdong. During the Hongwu reign his family fled the Ming sea ban and settled in Palembang in Sumatra, the old Srivijaya, where he became a local strongman who plundered every passing ship and dominated the Strait of Malacca.

On Zheng He's first treasure voyage, Chen feigned surrender while plotting to seize the Ming fleet. In 1407 Zheng He destroyed his pirate band, captured him at Palembang and took him back to China, where he was beheaded.

陈祖义（？—1407），广东潮州人，明初海盗首领。洪武年间，他全家为避海禁逃到苏门答腊的旧港，即三佛齐故地，在那里成为地方豪强，凡有船只经过即行劫掠，称雄马六甲海峡。

en:
Han Yong (1422–1478) was a Ming dynasty official born in Changzhou County, Suzhou. He became a jinshi in 1442 and served as a censor, and as provincial inspector of Jiangxi from 1452 he rebuilt the famous Tengwang Pavilion at Nanchang.

After he impeached the Prince of Ning, the prince retaliated and Han was imprisoned and dismissed in 1457. Restored to office, he became governor of Xuanfu and Datong in 1460.

In 1465, as military inspector, he took part in Zhao Fu's campaign against the Miao and Yao rising at Datengxia in Guangxi; the leader Hou Dagou was captured and killed, and Han was appointed Viceroy of Liangguang, stationed at Wuzhou. Attacks by subordinates and colleagues forced him into retirement in 1473, and he died in 1478.

韩雍（1422—1478）是明代大臣，生于南直隶苏州府长洲县。他于1442年考中进士，任监察御史，1452年起巡抚江西，在南昌重建名楼滕王阁。

他弹劾宁王后遭到报复，于1457年被下狱夺官，复职后于1460年巡抚宣府、大同。

1465年，他以赞理军务的身份随赵辅出征广西大藤峡，镇压瑶、苗等族起事，擒杀起事首领侯大苟，随后出任两广总督，驻扎梧州。1473年，他因下属和同僚攻讦被迫辞官，1478年去世。

en:
Li Zicheng (1606–1645) was the peasant rebel leader who overthrew the Ming dynasty and founded the short-lived Shun. Born to a poor family in Shaanxi, he was a post-station attendant from Mizhi until Ming courier cuts cost him his post, and he joined the revolts in 1629.

After his uncle Gao Yingxiang was executed, Li inherited the title Dashing King and built an army in Henan promising equal land and no taxes. He proclaimed the Shun at Xi'an in early 1644 and entered Beijing that April, driving the Chongzhen Emperor to suicide. Defeated at Shanhai Pass by Qing forces, he retreated and died in Hubei in 1645.

李自成（1606—1645）是推翻明朝、建立短命政权大顺的明末农民军领袖。他出身陕西贫苦人家，本是米脂驿卒，明朝裁撤驿站后失业，于1629年投身起义。

舅父“闯王”高迎祥被杀后，他袭称闯王，在河南以“均田免赋”号召饥民、壮大兵力。1644年初他在西安称帝，国号大顺，同年4月攻入北京，崇祯帝自缢，明朝灭亡。不久他在山海关被清军击败，一路撤退，1645年死于湖北。

en:
Peng Yingyu (died 1353), called the Monk Peng, was a Yuan rebel preacher from Yuanzhou, Jiangxi, founder of the southern Red Turbans. A monk at Cihua Temple, he took up Maitreya worship and wandered healing the poor as he preached.

In 1338 he and his disciple Zhou Ziwang raised more than five thousand followers, writing Buddha on their backs in the belief that it would protect them from weapons. He made Zhou a king, but the rising failed and Zhou was killed; Peng fled to Huaixi and continued preaching.

In August 1351 he joined Zou Pusheng and cloth peddler Xu Shouhui in the Qizhou rising, enthroning Xu as Tianwan emperor. He died fighting the Yuan when Qishui fell in 1353.

彭莹玉（?—1353），人称彭和尚，江西袁州人，是元末民变领袖、南派红巾军的开山始祖。他本在慈化寺出家，后改信弥勒教，四方行走，免费为人治病传教。

1338年，他与弟子周子旺在袁州聚众五千余人起事，命士兵背心皆书“佛”字，以为可避刀兵。他扶周子旺称王，起义失败、周子旺被杀后，彭莹玉逃亡淮西，继续传教。

1351年八月，他联合邹普胜与布贩徐寿辉在蕲州起兵，扶徐寿辉称帝、建立天完政权；1353年蕲水失陷时，他在与元军作战中战死。

en:
Yu Qian (1398–1457), courtesy name Tingyi, was the Ming minister who held Beijing against the Mongols in 1449. Born in Qiantang, Hangzhou, he passed the jinshi examination in 1421. In 1426 he so sternly listed the rebel Zhu Gaoxu's crimes that the prince trembled on the ground. As Grand Coordinator of Shanxi and Henan he strengthened the Yellow River dikes and petitioned for relief.

He offended the eunuch Wang Zhen and was sentenced to death, later freed. In 1449 the Oirat leader Esen captured Yingzong at Tumu. As Minister of War Yu said those proposing to flee south should be beheaded, posted 220,000 men outside Beijing's nine gates, and in October repulsed Esen.

For eight years Yu led the Jingtai Emperor's government. In 1457 Yingzong retook the throne in a coup and Yu was executed for treason. Later rehabilitated, he was given the posthumous name Zhongsu.

于谦（1398—1457），字廷益，是1449年在北京城下挡住蒙古军队的明朝大臣。他生于杭州钱塘，1421年考中进士。1426年他奉命历数叛王朱高煦的罪状，言辞严厉，朱高煦伏地发抖。此后他出任山西、河南巡抚，加固黄河堤防，遇水旱灾害即奏请赈济。

他得罪宦官王振，被判死罪，后获释。1449年土木堡之变，瓦剌首领也先俘获英宗，兵部尚书于谦驳斥南迁之议，称主张南迁者应当斩首，又集兵二十二万陈于北京九门之外，十月击退也先。

八年间，于谦是景泰帝朝廷的核心人物。1457年英宗发动政变复辟，于谦以谋反罪被处死，后来获得平反，谥号忠肃。

en:
Zheng He (1371–1433), born Ma He into a Muslim family of Kunyang in Yunnan, was the eunuch admiral who led the Ming treasure fleets across the Indian Ocean. When Ming forces took Yunnan in 1381, the ten-year-old boy was carried off to Nanjing, castrated and given to Zhu Di, Prince of Yan. He served Zhu Di in the Jingnan Campaign, and after he became the Yongle Emperor was given the surname Zheng in 1404.

Between 1405 and 1433 he commanded seven treasure voyages for Yongle and his successor Xuande, reaching Southeast Asia, India, Arabia and the East African coast. The fleet projected power across the Indian Ocean.

The Hongxi Emperor ended the voyages in 1424, but Xuande sent him on a seventh and last voyage in 1430. He died in 1433, probably at Calicut; the voyages were played down until Liang Qichao revived his fame in 1904.

郑和（1371—1433），原姓马，生于云南昆阳的穆斯林家庭，是统率明朝宝船船队横渡印度洋的宦官航海家。1381年明军攻占云南，十岁的他被掳往南京受宫刑，分给燕王朱棣。靖难之役中他追随燕王，永乐帝即位后于1404年赐姓郑。

1405至1433年间，他为永乐帝及其继位者宣德帝七次率领宝船船队远航，遍历东南亚、印度、阿拉伯直至东非沿岸。这支舰队向印度洋投射武力。

1424年洪熙帝终止远航；1430年宣德帝派他第七次、也是最后一次远航。他于1433年去世，可能逝于古里。这些航行后来被史书淡化，直到1904年梁启超才使他重新闻名。

Chosbal was a Yuan imperial prince, a great-grandson of Kublai and son of Temür Buqa, whom he succeeded in 1297 as Prince Zhenxi Wujing, holding Tibet as his hereditary appanage. He led a large army into Ü-Tsang and defeated west Mongol troops below Gyantse during the Drikung disturbances, and in 1306 moved against revolts across Tibet.

He campaigned against the Chagatai prince Kebek in 1319. In 1330 he helped crush Tughan's rebellion in Yunnan and died soon afterwards.

en:
Blanche of Navarre (c. 1177–1229), daughter of King Sancho VI and Sancha of Castile, married Count Theobald III of Champagne in 1199. Widowed in 1201 while pregnant, she bore Theobald IV days later and ruled Champagne as regent until 1222. She at once paid homage to Philip II at Sens, the first countess to do so, securing her son's rights.

In 1212 she established procedures allowing daughters to inherit castles without a son. In 1215 Philippa of Champagne and Erard of Brienne-Ramerupt made war on her claim; backed by Pope Innocent III, Blanche forced them to renounce it by 1222. She died in 1229.

en:
Érard II of Brienne (c. 1130–1191), son of Count Gautier II and Humbeline de Baudement, ruled the county of Brienne from 1161. He accompanied his father on the Second Crusade, staying in the Holy Land until 1151.

In 1188 he and his brother André took the cross with Henry II of Champagne and reached the Siege of Acre by September 1189, ahead of the Third Crusade.

André fell that October, and Érard died at the siege on 8 February 1191, probably of famine or disease. His son Walter III succeeded him; another son, John, later governed Brienne during his nephew's minority and became king of Jerusalem.

1188年，他与弟弟安德烈随香槟伯爵亨利二世领取十字，1189年9月便抵达阿卡围城战场，早于第三次十字军的主力。

en:
Odo II (c. 985–1037), son of Count Odo I of Blois and Bertha of Burgundy, ruled Blois and Chartres from 1004. Defeated by Fulk Nerra of Anjou at Pontlevoy in 1016, he seized Troyes, Meaux and Champagne without royal approval when his cousin Stephen I died heirless around 1020, uniting Blois and Champagne under one lord.

He was later offered the Lombard crown and invaded Burgundy in 1032, but withdrew before an imperial and French royal coalition. In 1037 he attacked Lorraine and fell on 15 November at the Battle of Bar-le-Duc against Duke Gothelo. His sons by Ermengarde of Auvergne were Theobald and Stephen.

Odo, called Eudes III of Troyes (c. 1062–c. 1093), was a son of Count Theobald III of Blois and Adele of Valois. On his father's death in 1089 the inheritance was divided: his half-brother Stephen-Henry took Blois and Chartres while Odo received the county of Troyes.

During his brief rule he proved a generous patron, granting lands to local abbeys and priories. He died around 1093, apparently unmarried, and Troyes passed to his younger brother Hugh.

Henry I (1127–1181), called the Liberal, ruled Champagne from 1152 as the eldest son of Count Theobald II and Matilda of Carinthia. He joined Louis VII on the Second Crusade.

On his father's death he kept Champagne, leaving Blois and Chartres to his brothers. Under his protection the Champagne Fairs became a centre of European trade, and his court at Troyes became known for literature. In 1164 he married Marie of France, who bore Henry II and Theobald III.

In 1179 he was captured in Anatolia returning from Jerusalem and ransomed by the Byzantine emperor. He died in 1181.

en:
Hugh I (c. 1074–after 1130), a younger son of Count Theobald III of Blois and Adele of Valois, inherited Troyes from his brother Odo in 1093 and added Bar-sur-Aube and Vitry, becoming the first count of Champagne. He journeyed several times to the Holy Land, where his vassal Hugh de Payns founded the Knights Templar.

In 1125, leaving his pregnant wife and refusing to acknowledge her child, he abdicated to his nephew Theobald and joined the Templars, dying in the East after 1130.

en:
Jean II de Châteauvillain (born after 1285, died 1312) was lord of Châteauvillain, Arc-en-Barrois and Pleurs in Champagne. Eldest son of Simon II de Châteauvillain and Marie de Dampierre, he succeeded his father in 1306, his grandfather Jean I, called the Blind, being still alive. That year he married Marie de Roucy, who bore him Jean and Guillaume.

He died in 1312 leaving two young children and appointed Simon de Choiseul their guardian. At the request of relatives, Philip the Fair instead named other guardians in March 1313.

Jean II de Trie (c. 1225–1302), son of Mathieu I de Trie and Marsilie de Montmorency, succeeded his father in 1272 as Count of Dammartin and lord of Trie and Mouchy. He married first Ermengarde, then Yolande, daughter of John I, Count of Dreux; by Yolande his children were Renaud, his heir, and Mahaut.

He is also identified with the trouvère Jehan de Trie, to whom two surviving courtly chansons are attributed. Fighting for Philip the Fair against the Flemings, he was killed on 11 July 1302 at the Battle of the Golden Spurs.

Mathieu I de Trie (c. 1192–1272) was a French baron, son of Jean I de Trie, lord of Trie and Mouchy, and Aélis de Dammartin. He held the lordships of Trie and Mouchy. His mother's family gave him a claim to Dammartin.

When his cousin Matilda, Countess of Dammartin, died without children, the Parlement of Paris settled the disputed succession in his favour in 1262, making him Count of Dammartin. He married Marsilie de Montmorency and was succeeded at his death in 1272 by his son Jean II.

Theobald III (c. 1019–1089), also called Theobald I of Champagne, succeeded his father Odo II in 1037 as count of Blois, Meaux and Troyes. In 1044 he was defeated and captured at Nouy by Geoffrey Martel of Anjou, who freed him only in exchange for the county of Touraine.

Theobald used his nephew's involvement in the Norman invasion of England to strengthen his authority in Champagne. After his death at Épernay on 30 September 1089, following a fifty-two-year rule, King Philip I arranged the division of Blois and Champagne between his sons Stephen, Odo and Hugh.

Theobald the Great (1090–10 January 1152) was the son of Count Stephen-Henry of Blois and Adela of Normandy, and brother of King Stephen of England. He succeeded to Blois and Chartres in 1102. In 1123 he married Matilda of Carinthia; their children included Henry I of Champagne and Adela, wife of King Louis VII. When his uncle Hugh abdicated in 1125, Theobald added Champagne and Brie, reuniting the family lands.

War over his sister Eleanor's marriage in 1142–1144 saw royal troops burn Vitry-en-Perthois, where hundreds died in the burning church. Theobald died on 10 January 1152.

Theobald III (1179–1201), younger son of Count Henry I of Champagne and Marie of France, became count in 1197 after his brother Henry II died in the Holy Land. He worked closely with his suzerain Philip II of France. In 1199 he married Blanche of Navarre at Chartres.

At a tournament at Écry on 28 November 1199, Fulk of Neuilly preached the Fourth Crusade; the nobles present took the cross and elected Theobald their leader. He died on 24 May 1201 before the crusade sailed, succeeded by a posthumous son, Theobald IV, whose mother Blanche ruled Champagne as regent.

en:
Christopher Columbus (1451–1506) was a Genoese navigator who crossed the Atlantic four times for the Catholic Monarchs and opened the Americas to Europe. The son of a Genoese weaver, he went to sea and settled in Lisbon after a 1476 shipwreck. His westward plan to reach the East Indies was rejected in Portugal, but after lobbying in Castile, Isabella and Ferdinand sponsored him.

In 1492 he sailed with three ships and landed on a Bahamian island called Guanahani, then reached Cuba and Hispaniola. Three more voyages reached the Lesser Antilles, the South American coast and Central America. He died believing he had reached the Far East; Amerigo Vespucci recognized the new continent that mapmakers named America after him.

As governor he was accused of brutality and arrested on Hispaniola in 1500. He died in 1506; no important place carried his name until Colombia was named for him in 1819.

Christopher Columbus (1451–1506) was a Genoese navigator who crossed the Atlantic four times for the Catholic Monarchs and opened the Americas to Europe. The son of a Genoese weaver, he went to sea and settled in Lisbon after a 1476 shipwreck. His westward plan to reach the East Indies was rejected in [GetCountry('POR').GetName], but after lobbying in [GetCountry('CAS').GetName], Isabella and Ferdinand sponsored him.

In 1492 he sailed with three ships and landed on a Bahamian island called [ShowLocationName('guanahani')], then reached Cuba and Hispaniola. Three more voyages reached the [ShowLocationName('lesser_antilles_wastelands')], the South American coast and Central America. He died believing he had reached the Far East; Amerigo Vespucci recognized the new continent that mapmakers named America after him.

As governor he was accused of brutality and arrested on Hispaniola in 1500. He died in 1506; no important place carried his name until Colombia was named for him in 1819.
zh:
克里斯托弗·哥伦布（1451—1506）是热那亚航海家，四次受天主教双王派遣横渡大西洋，为欧洲打开美洲之门。他是热那亚织工之子，1476年遇海难后定居里斯本。他西航前往东印度群岛的计划被葡萄牙否定，在卡斯蒂利亚游说后，伊莎贝拉与斐迪南才同意资助。

1492年他率三艘船启航，在巴哈马瓜纳哈尼岛登陆，随后抵达古巴和伊斯帕尼奥拉岛。此后三次远航，到达小安的列斯群岛、南美海岸和中美洲。他至死以为到达了远东；亚美利哥·韦斯普奇认出那是新大陆，制图师便以他的名字命名美洲。

任总督时他被指控残暴，1500年在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛被捕。1506年去世，1819年才有重要地名以他命名，即哥伦比亚。

Christophe de Longueil (1488 or 1490–1522), Latin name Christophorus Longolius, was a humanist born at Mechelen in Brabant and raised in France. He studied law at Valence, became a lawyer in 1511 and held office in Paris from 1513, and also tutored the young King Francis I.

Moving to Rome in 1517, he joined the Ciceronian circle of Pietro Bembo and Jacopo Sadoleto and obtained Roman citizenship in 1519, despite a campaign against him over an early speech praising the Franks above the Romans. Harassed, he withdrew to Venice and Padua, where he died on 11 September 1522.

克里斯托夫·德·隆格伊（1488或1490—1522），拉丁名作克里斯托弗鲁斯·隆戈利乌斯，是生于布拉班特梅赫伦、长于法国的人文主义者。他在瓦朗斯学习法律，1511年成为律师，自1513年起在巴黎任职，还曾教导年轻的国王弗朗索瓦一世。

1517年他移居罗马，加入彼得罗·本博和雅各布·萨多莱托的西塞罗派圈子，1519年获罗马公民权；此前他因一篇称颂法兰克人胜过罗马人的旧演说遭到攻讦。备受排挤的他退往威尼斯，再赴帕多瓦，1522年9月11日在当地去世。

en:
Seii (1328–1349), fifth and last king of the Eiso dynasty of Chūzan, is known from the Ryukyuan royal chronicles. He succeeded his father Tamagusuku in 1337 at about ten years of age, and his mother ran the government in his name. The chronicles condemn her rule in a line: the hen crows in place of the cock.

Meanwhile Satto, the aji of Urasoe, won standing among the aji for his virtue. When Seii died in 1349, the regional lords set aside his heir and enthroned Satto, ending Eiso rule.

西威（1328—1349）是琉球中山英祖王朝第五代、也是末代国王，事迹见于琉球王室史书。1337年他继承父亲玉城之位，年仅约十岁，朝政由母后执掌。史书中以一句话斥责这段朝政：牝鸡乱政。

与此同时，浦添按司察度因德行著称，在各地按司中渐有威望。1349年西威去世，诸按司废黜他的世子，拥立察度为王，英祖王朝就此灭亡。

en:
Tamagusuku (1296–1336), recorded in the Ryukyu chronicles as the fourth king of the Eiso dynasty from 1314, was the third son of King Eiji and succeeded at Urasoe. He could not command the loyalty of the territorial lords, the anji.

During his reign the lord of Ōzato withdrew south to found the kingdom of Nanzan and the lord of Nakijin proclaimed Hokuzan in the north, leaving Tamagusuku ruler of Chūzan and opening the Three Kingdoms era. He died of illness on 22 April 1336, leaving his son Seii as the last Eiso king.

玉城（1296—1336），据琉球史书记载，是英祖王朝第四代国王，1314年即位。他是前代国王英慈的第三子，在浦添继位，无法使各地按司臣服。

他在位期间，大里按司南下建立南山国，今归仁的领主在北方自立北山国，玉城仅保有中山，三山时代由此开始。1336年4月22日他病逝，其子西威继位，是英祖王朝末代国王。

en:
Alice of Korikos (c. 1305–1329) was queen of Armenian Cilicia and the only daughter of Oshin of Korikos, regent for the young King Leo IV. To secure his hold on power, Oshin forced Alice to marry Leo IV around the end of 1320.

She bore Leo one son, Hethum, who died young. When Leo took power in 1329, he had Oshin and his brother Constantine killed and ordered Alice murdered as well.

科里科斯的艾丽斯（约1305—1329）是奇里乞亚亚美尼亚王后，摄政奥辛·科里科斯的独女。为巩固权势，奥辛强迫艾丽斯在1320年底前后嫁给年幼的国王莱翁四世。

她为莱翁生下一子海屯，幼年夭折。1329年莱翁亲政，处死奥辛及其弟君士坦丁，并下令将艾丽斯一并杀害。

en:
Bohemond of Lusignan (1307/1309–1344) was a Cypriot royal prince, the son of Amalric of Lusignan, Lord of Tyre, and the Armenian princess Isabella. After his father's murder in 1310 he grew up in Cilician Armenia, where he became Lord of Korikos in 1336. In 1340 he married Euphemia of Neghir, who bore him Barthelemy, later regent of Armenia.

He was the brother of King Constantine II and uncle of the future King Leo V. Bohemond was murdered by Armenian barons at Adana on 17 November 1344.

吕西尼昂的博希蒙德（1307/1309—1344）是塞浦路斯王室成员，父亲为提尔领主阿马尔里克，母亲为亚美尼亚公主伊莎贝拉。1310年父亲遇刺后，他在奇里乞亚亚美尼亚长大，1336年成为科里科斯领主。1340年他娶内吉尔的尤菲米娅为妻，生子巴泰勒米，后者后来出任亚美尼亚摄政。

en:
Baldwin (died 12 December 1336) was an Armenian noble of the Hetumid house, lord of Neghir and Pertzerpert in the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia. The son of Constantine of Neghir, he rose to the kingdom's highest military rank, the sparapet, or commander-in-chief.

Baldwin did not live to wear a crown, but after his death his son was chosen king as Constantine III in 1344, while his daughter Euphemia became lady of Korikos.

en:
Euphemia of Neghir (7 May 1325 – after 1381) was the daughter of Baldwin, lord of Neghir and marshal of Armenia, and sister of King Constantine III. In 1340 a papal dispensation allowed her to marry Bohemond of Lusignan, lord of Korikos; he was murdered in 1344, leaving her a childless widow.

On the coronation day of Leo V in September 1374 she married her second husband, Sohier Doulçart, whom the king made lord of Korikos. She later died in Jerusalem.

内吉尔的尤菲米娅（1325年5月7日—1381年后）是内吉尔领主、亚美尼亚统帅鲍德温之女，国王君士坦丁三世的妹妹。1340年，教皇特许她嫁给科里科斯领主、吕西尼昂家族的博希蒙德；1344年博希蒙德遇刺，她无子守寡。

en:
Joan of Taranto (died 1323) was a daughter of Philip I of Taranto and Thamar Angelina Komnene. In February 1316 she married King Oshin of Cilician Armenia, taking the name Eirene, and bore him a son, George.

Widowed in July 1320, when Oshin died amid rumours of poison, she was forced to marry his cousin Oshin of Korikos, who had seized the regency. She died in March 1323, leaving a daughter Maria who later married two Armenian kings.

en:
Hethum I (1213–1270) founded the Hethumid dynasty of Cilician Armenia. His father, Constantine of Baberon, was regent for Queen Isabella and arranged the removal of her first husband Philip. In 1226 Constantine forced Isabella to marry Hethum, making them co-rulers.

Hethum accepted Mongol suzerainty, and in 1254–1255 travelled through Central Asia to the Great Khan's court at Karakorum. He joined the Mongols in war against the Mamluks, who in 1266 killed his son Thoros at the Battle of Mari. In 1270 he abdicated in favour of his son Leo and died on 21 October.

海屯一世（1213—1270）是奇里乞亚亚美尼亚海屯王朝的开创者。其父巴巴伦的康斯坦丁曾任女王伊莎贝拉的摄政，安排除掉了她的首任丈夫腓力。1226年，康斯坦丁逼迫伊莎贝拉嫁给海屯，使二人成为共治君主。

海屯接受蒙古的宗主权，并于1254—1255年经中亚前往哈拉和林的大汗宫廷。他联合蒙古对抗马穆鲁克，1266年其子多罗斯在马里战役中战死。1270年他禅位于儿子莱翁，同年10月21日去世。

en:
Hethum II (1266–1307), son of Leo II and Keran, was three times king of Armenian Cilicia. After the Mamluks sacked Hromgla in 1292 he ceded border towns, then abdicated in 1293 to join the Franciscans. Restored in 1295, his brother Sempad seized the throne, partially blinded him, and had Thoros III killed.

Freed in 1299, he joined Ilkhan Ghazan's victory at Wadi al-Khazandar. Abdicating again, he ruled as regent for his nephew Leo III, until Mongol Bilarghu murdered them both in 1307.
