海屯二世（1266—1307）是莱翁二世与克兰之子，曾三度登上奇里乞亚亚美尼亚王位。1292年马穆鲁克军队攻陷赫罗姆格拉，他割让边境城镇，1293年退位加入方济各会。1295年他复位后，遭兄弟斯姆巴特篡位、灼伤眼睛而部分失明，多罗斯三世也被杀害。

en:
Hethum of Korikos, called the Historian (c. 1240–c. 1310), was an Armenian nobleman and chronicler of the Hethumid house. The son of Oshin, prince of Korikos, he governed that city until he conspired against King Hethum II and was exiled in 1294. In 1299 he made a pilgrimage to Paris, and in 1305 entered the Premonstratensian order at Bellapais Abbey in Cyprus.

In 1307, as prior at Poitiers, he dictated his Flower of the Histories of the East at Pope Clement V's request, an influential account of the Mongols and the East. After Hethum II's murder he returned to Armenia as constable, last recorded alive in 1309.

en:
John of Lusignan (c. 1306–1343) was a Poitiers-Lusignan prince who served the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia as constable and then regent. He was a son of Amalric, Lord of Tyre, and the Armenian princess Isabella. When the barons murdered Leo IV, the last Hethumid king, in 1341, the crown was offered to John, who urged his elder brother Guy to accept it; Guy reigned as King Constantine II.

He was murdered in Cilicia on 7 August 1343, eight months before Guy was killed in an uprising. His son Leo, born in 1342, became the last Lusignan king of Armenian Cilicia, reigning in 1374–1375.

吕西尼昂的约翰（约1306—1343）是普瓦捷-吕西尼昂家族的亲王，在奇里乞亚亚美尼亚王国历任统帅与摄政。他是提尔领主阿马尔里克与亚美尼亚公主伊莎贝拉之子。1341年，贵族杀害末代海屯王朝国王莱翁四世，王冠被送到约翰面前，他却劝兄长居伊接受，居伊遂以康斯坦丁二世之名为王。

en:
Guy de Lusignan, who reigned as Constantine II, was elected the first Latin king of Armenian Cilicia. Son of Amalric, Lord of Tyre, and Isabella of Armenia, he governed Serres from 1328 to 1341. In 1341 the barons murdered his cousin Leo IV, the last Hethumid king, and the crown was offered to Guy's younger brother John, who urged Guy to take it instead.

Guy was reluctant: the regent Oshin of Corycos had murdered his mother and two of his brothers. He accepted in 1342 and took the name Constantine. He was killed in an uprising on 17 April 1344, and Constantine III succeeded him.

en:
Constantine of Baberon (died c. 1263), called the Grand Baron, was a powerful noble of the Hethumid house in Cilician Armenia. As guardian of Queen Isabella, he engineered the murder in 1226 of her husband, Philip of Antioch.

He tricked Philip's father Bohemond IV into looking for his son at Amouda while Philip was held at Sis, then forced the Frankish garrison at Silifke to surrender the queen and married her to his own son Hethum I, founding the Hethumid royal line. By his third wife Biatr he fathered Constantine, lord of Neghir, ancestor of later Armenian kings.

腓力被囚于锡斯时，康斯坦丁诱使其父博希蒙德四世前往阿穆达寻找儿子，随后逼迫锡利夫凯城堡的法兰克守军交出女王，将她嫁给自己的儿子海屯一世，由此开创海屯王朝。他与第三任妻子比亚特生有内吉尔领主小康斯坦丁，即后来几位亚美尼亚国王的祖先。

Constantine I (1278–c. 1310) was a son of Leo II of Cilician Armenia and Keran of Lampron. In 1296 he helped his brother Sempad seize the throne from Hethum II.

After their brother Thoros was murdered in July 1298, he turned on Sempad and took the crown while Hethum recovered. When Hethum resumed the throne in 1299, Constantine plotted to restore Sempad, and both were imprisoned for life.

en:
Constantine III (1313–1362), son of Baldwin, Lord of Neghir, was king of Armenian Cilicia from 1344. The main Hethumid line had ended with the murder of Leo IV in 1341; his successor Constantine II fell to an uprising in 1344, and Constantine III took the crown.

He tried to wipe out rival claimants, ordering the deaths of Constantine II's nephews Bemon and Leo, but the boys escaped to Cyprus. Under Mamluk pressure his realm shrank: they seized Ajazzo in 1347, then Tarsus and Adana in 1359, leaving the kingdom little more than Sis.

He married Maria, daughter of Oshin of Corycos. Both his sons died before him, and when he died of natural causes the crown passed to his cousin Constantine IV.

康斯坦丁三世（1313—1362）是内吉尔领主鲍德温之子，自1344年起为奇里乞亚亚美尼亚国王。1341年莱翁四世被杀，海屯王朝的正支就此断绝；继位的康斯坦丁二世在1344年的叛乱中被杀，康斯坦丁三世登上王位。

他试图铲除王位竞争者，下令处死康斯坦丁二世的侄儿贝蒙和莱翁，但两个少年逃到了塞浦路斯。在马穆鲁克人的压力下王国不断缩小：1347年阿亚斯陷落，1359年塔尔苏斯和阿达纳也被攻占，疆域只剩西斯一带。

他娶了科里科斯的奥辛之女玛丽亚。他的两个儿子都先他而死，他自然死亡后，王位传给亲族康斯坦丁四世。

en:
Constantine IV (1324–1373), son of Hethum of Neghir, inherited the throne of Armenian Cilicia in December 1362 from his cousin Constantine III, whose widow Maria, daughter of Oshin of Corycos, he married. The Mamluks had already taken Ajazzo, Tarsus and Adana.

He allied with Peter I of Cyprus and gave him Corycus; after Peter's death in 1369 he turned to the sultan and sought a treaty. His barons feared annexation and murdered him in March 1373. His cousin Leo V, of the Poitiers-Lusignan line, succeeded and became the last king of Armenian Cilicia.

康斯坦丁四世（1324—1373）是内吉尔的海屯之子。1362年12月，亲族康斯坦丁三世去世，他继承奇里乞亚亚美尼亚王位，并娶了寡后、科里科斯的奥辛之女玛丽亚。此时阿亚斯、塔尔苏斯和阿达纳已落入马穆鲁克人之手。

Constantine (died 1308) was lord of Neghir and Partzerpert in Cilician Armenia, youngest son of the Grand Baron Constantine of Baberon by his third wife Biatr. About 1285 he married Isabelle of Lusignan, daughter of King Hugh III of Cyprus, who after his death married King Oshin of Armenia.

His sons were Baldwin, marshal of Armenia, murdered at Aleppo in 1336; Vacahk, lord of Gantschi, who died in 1328; and Hethum, lord of Neghir, who died in 1356.

en:
Leo II (c. 1236–1289), eldest son of Hethum I and Isabella, ruled Cilician Armenia from 1269 to 1289. In 1266 he fought the Mamluks at the Battle of Mari, where his brother Thoros was killed and Leo captured; Sis was sacked. His father later ransomed him, and Leo took the throne when Hethum abdicated in 1269.

He fostered Italian and Catalan trade and upheld the Mongol alliance, but defeat with the Mongols at Homs in 1281 forced a ten-year truce and territorial concessions in 1285. He died of arsenic poisoning in 1289 and was succeeded by his son Hethum II.

en:
Leo III (1289–1307) was king of Armenian Cilicia, the son of Thoros III and Margaret of Lusignan. Crowned in 1303 while still a minor, he ruled with his uncle Hethum II, who acted as regent.

In 1305 the two led the Armenian army to defeat a Mamluk force near Bagras. On 17 November 1307, the Mongol general Bilarghu had Leo and Hethum massacred at a banquet in Anazarbus. He left no children, and his uncle Oshin succeeded him.

en:
Leo IV (1309–1341), son of King Oshin, was the last Hethumid king of Armenian Cilicia. He came to the throne in 1320 under the regency of Oshin of Corycos, who in 1321 forced him to marry his daughter Alice and killed several royals.

In 1329 Leo answered in kind: Oshin, Oshin's brother Constantine and Alice were killed, Oshin's head sent to the Il-Khan and Constantine's to the Mamluk sultan. His pro-Western policy and 1331 marriage to Constance of Sicily enraged the barons.

After the Mamluks took Ayas in 1337 he bought a humiliating truce with territory and a large indemnity, and spent his last years in the citadel at Sis waiting for Western aid that never came. His barons murdered him on 28 August 1341 and chose his cousin Constantine II as successor.

莱翁四世（1309—1341）是国王奥辛之子，奇里乞亚亚美尼亚的末代海屯王朝国王。他1320年即位，由科里科斯的奥辛摄政；奥辛1321年逼他娶自己的女儿艾丽斯，并杀害数名王室成员。

1329年莱翁以牙还牙：奥辛、奥辛之兄君士坦丁和艾丽斯都被处死，奥辛的首级送往伊儿汗，君士坦丁的首级送往马穆鲁克苏丹。他的亲西方政策以及1331年与西西里的康斯坦丝的联姻激怒了贵族。

1337年马穆鲁克人攻占阿亚斯后，他以割地和巨额赔款换来屈辱的休战，晚年困守西斯城堡，等待始终没有到来的西方援军。1341年8月28日，贵族将他杀害，改立他的堂兄弟康斯坦丁二世继位。

1337年马穆鲁克人攻占[ShowLocationName('ayas')]后，他以割地和巨额赔款换来屈辱的休战，晚年困守西斯城堡，等待始终没有到来的西方援军。1341年8月28日，贵族将他杀害，改立他的堂兄弟康斯坦丁二世继位。

en:
Leo I, called the Magnificent (1150–1219), was the tenth Roupenid lord of Armenian Cilicia and its first crowned king. After his father Stephen was murdered in 1165, Leo and his brother Roupen lived with their uncle. He succeeded Roupen III in 1187 and warred against Aleppo and Damascus, drawing Muslim forces away from the Crusader states.

He aided the Third Crusade with provisions and guides, extended his rule over Isauria, and was consecrated king at Tarsus in 1199. He died on 2 May 1219, leaving the crown to his young daughter Isabella.

zh:
被誉为“宏伟者”的莱翁（1150—1219）是鲁本王朝第十任奇里乞亚亚美尼亚领主，也是第一位加冕的国王。1165年父亲斯捷潘遇害后，莱翁与兄弟鲁本投靠了舅父。1187年他继鲁本三世之后成为领主，随即与阿勒颇和大马士革的统治者交战，牵制穆斯林兵力，减轻十字军国家承受的压力。

他以粮草和向导支援第三次十字军，将统治拓展到伊苏利亚，并于1199年在塔尔苏斯加冕为王。1219年5月2日他去世，王位传给年幼的女儿伊莎贝拉。

en:
Margaret of Poitiers-Lusignan (1276–1296) was a Cypriot princess of the Lusignan dynasty who became queen of Cilician Armenia. She was a daughter of King Hugh III of Cyprus and Isabella of Ibelin, and a sister of the Cypriot kings John I and Henry II. In 1288 she married Thoros, son of King Leo II of Armenia, who became king as Thoros III in 1293.

She left two sons, Leo III, who later wore the Armenian crown, and Bohemond, whose later fate is unknown. Margaret died in 1296 after three years as queen.

吕西尼昂的玛格丽特（1276—1296）是吕西尼昂家族的塞浦路斯公主，后成为奇里乞亚亚美尼亚王后。她是塞浦路斯国王于格三世与伊贝林的伊莎贝拉之女，塞浦路斯国王约翰一世与亨利二世的姐妹。1288年她嫁给亚美尼亚国王莱翁二世之子多罗斯，后者于1293年即位为多罗斯三世。

en:
Marie of Korikos (1321 – before 1405) was the daughter of Oshin of Korikos, regent of Cilician Armenia, and Joan of Taranto. In 1340 she married her cousin Constantine III and became queen when he ascended the throne in 1344; her two sons died in childhood.

After Constantine died in 1362, she married his successor, her cousin Constantine IV, and was again queen until his murder in 1373. From April 1373 she governed the shrunken kingdom as regent until Leo V of Lusignan was crowned in September 1374.

科里科斯的玛丽（1321—1405年前）是奇里乞亚亚美尼亚摄政科里科斯的奥辛与塔兰托的乔万娜之女。1340年，她嫁给表亲君士坦丁三世，在他于1344年登基后成为王后；两个儿子都幼年夭折。

en:
Oshin (1282–1320), a son of Leo II of Armenia, seized the Cilician crown after the Mongol Bilarghu murdered his brother Hethum II and nephew Leo III in November 1307. He defeated Bilarghu and drove him out, while the Ilkhan Öljeitü confirmed his kingship and had the killer executed.

His pro-Roman church-union policy stirred discontent. By Isabel of Korikos he had Leo IV, and in 1316 married Joan of Taranto. He died on 20 July 1320, widely believed poisoned by Oshin of Corycos.

奥辛（1282—1320）是亚美尼亚国王莱翁二世之子。1307年11月蒙古人比拉尔古杀害他的兄长海屯二世和侄儿莱翁三世后，他夺取奇里乞亚王位，击败并逐走比拉尔古；伊儿汗完者都承认他的王位，并处死了凶手。

他推动与罗马教会合一，招致民间不满。他与科里科斯的伊莎贝尔生有莱翁四世，1316年娶塔兰托的乔万娜。他于1320年7月20日去世，时人普遍认为他是被科里科斯的奥辛毒杀的。

Oshin of Korikos (died 1329), son of the historian Hayton of Corycus, became regent for the young Leo IV after King Oshin died in July 1320, a death he was rumoured to have poisoned. He probably had the king's sister Isabella and two of her sons murdered as rivals.

He married first Margaret d'Ibelin, whose daughter Alice became Leo IV's queen, then King Oshin's widow Joan of Anjou. When Leo came of age, the king had both Oshin and Alice killed in 1329.

en:
Sempad (1277 – c. 1310), a son of Leo II of Armenia, usurped the Cilician throne in 1296 while his brothers Hethum II and Thoros escorted their sister to Constantinople. In 1297 he won Mongol recognition and a Mongol bride at the Ilkhan Ghazan's court.

Sempad had the returning Hethum partially blinded and imprisoned at Partzerpert, where Thoros was strangled on his orders in July 1298. Their brother Constantine then freed Hethum, who overthrew Sempad. After another plot with Constantine, Sempad was imprisoned for life, dying around 1310.

Sibylla of Cyprus (1198–c. 1230) was the elder daughter of Aimery of Lusignan, king of Cyprus and Jerusalem, and Queen Isabella I of Jerusalem. Orphaned in 1205, in 1210 or 1211 her half-brother King Hugh I married her to the aged Leo I, King of Cilician Armenia.

She was queen until Leo died in 1219 and was the mother of his sole heir, Queen Isabella I of Armenia. She also held a claim to the throne of Jerusalem, which she never pursued.

zh:
塞浦路斯的西比拉（1198—约1230）是塞浦路斯与耶路撒冷国王艾默里·德·吕西尼昂与耶路撒冷女王伊莎贝拉一世的长女。1205年父母双亡后，1210或1211年异母兄长于格一世将她嫁给年迈的奇里乞亚亚美尼亚国王莱翁一世。

1219年莱翁去世前她身为亚美尼亚王后，是他唯一继承人亚美尼亚女王伊莎贝拉一世的母亲。她本人也拥有耶路撒冷王位的继承权，但从未主张。

en:
Thoros III (c. 1271–1298), a son of Leo II of Armenia, became king of Armenian Cilicia when his brother Hethum II abdicated in 1293. In 1288 he married Margaret of Lusignan; their son Leo III later inherited the crown. In 1295 he recalled Hethum as co-ruler.

In 1296 the brothers took their sister Rita to Constantinople to marry Michael IX Palaiologos, only to find Sempad had seized the throne. Imprisoned at Bardzrberd, he was strangled there on 23 July 1298 on Sempad's orders.

zh:
多罗斯三世（约1271—1298）是亚美尼亚国王莱翁二世之子，1293年其兄海屯二世退位后继任奇里乞亚亚美尼亚国王。1288年他娶吕西尼昂的玛格丽特，二人之子莱翁三世后来继承王位。1295年他召回海屯共治。

1296年，兄弟二人护送妹妹丽塔前往君士坦丁堡嫁给米海尔九世·巴列奥略，回来时斯姆巴特已篡夺王位。多罗斯被囚于巴兹尔伯德，1298年7月23日奉斯姆巴特之命被绞死。

en:
Isabella of Armenia (c. 1280–1323), also called Zabel, was a daughter of Leo II and Keran and the twin sister of King Sempad. In 1292 or 1293 she married Amalric of Cyprus, Lord of Tyre, and bore him six children, including Guy, later Constantine II of Cilicia, and Maria, who married Leo IV.

When Oshin of Corycos ruled as regent for Leo IV, he sought to remove rival claimants: he imprisoned and murdered Isabella and her son Henry before April 1323. Isabella was reportedly poisoned.

亚美尼亚的伊莎贝拉（约1280—1323），又名扎贝尔，是莱翁二世与克兰之女、斯姆巴德国王的孪生妹妹。1292至1293年间，她嫁给提尔领主、塞浦路斯的阿马尔里克，生下六个子女，其中包括后来在奇里乞亚称康斯坦丁二世的居伊，以及嫁给莱翁四世的玛丽亚。

科里科斯的奥辛为莱翁四世摄政时，决意铲除王位竞争者：他在1323年4月之前将伊莎贝拉和儿子亨利囚禁并杀害。据传伊莎贝拉是被毒杀的。

en:
Isabella, also called Zabel (c. 1216–1252), was queen regnant of Armenian Cilicia from 1219 until her death. Only child of Leo I and Sibylla of Cyprus, she succeeded at about three; the rival Raymond-Roupen was defeated and executed. Her regent Adam of Baghras was assassinated and Constantine of Baberon became her guardian.

Constantine married her to Philip of Antioch in 1222, but Philip plundered the palace and was poisoned at Sis. Constantine then forced her to marry his son Hethum I, who ruled with her and founded the Hethumid dynasty. She died on 23 January 1252.

zh:
伊莎贝拉，又译扎贝尔（约1216—1252），自1219年起为奇里乞亚亚美尼亚女王，直至去世。她是莱翁一世与塞浦路斯的西比拉唯一的孩子，约三岁时继位；竞争者雷蒙-鲁本战败后遭处决。摄政巴格拉斯的亚当遇刺后，巴巴伦的康斯坦丁接任监护人。

康斯坦丁于1222年安排她嫁给安条克的腓力，但腓力劫掠王宫，在锡斯遭毒杀。康斯坦丁随后逼她改嫁自己的儿子海屯一世，二人共同统治，开创海屯王朝。1252年1月23日，伊莎贝拉去世。

en:
Jan I van Cuijk (c. 1230 – 13 July 1308) was a Brabantine noble, knight and diplomat, and lord of Cuijk. In 1288 he fought for the Duke of Brabant at the Battle of Worringen, where he was praised as one of the bravest knights.

In 1294 King Adolf of Nassau sent him as envoy to Edward I of England to negotiate an alliance, and in 1296 he led the baronial conspiracy that overthrew Count Floris V of Holland. His son Jan II succeeded him.

扬一世·范·克伊克（约1230—1308年7月13日）是布拉班特的贵族、骑士与外交家，克伊克领主。1288年，他随布拉班特公爵征战沃林根战役，被誉为最英勇的骑士之一。

1294年，德意志国王拿骚的阿道夫派他出使英格兰，与爱德华一世谈判结盟；1296年，他领导贵族密谋，推翻了荷兰伯爵弗洛里斯五世。他死后由儿子扬二世继位。

en:
Otto van Cuijk (1270–1350) was a nobleman of the Duchy of Brabant, a son of Jan I van Cuijk and Jutta of Nassau. When his brother Jan II, lord of Cuijk, died in 1319 without lawful children and his other brothers had already died, Otto succeeded to the lordship of Cuijk; he also held Mierlo and Asten.

He married three times, and his only known child, Adelise, was born of the second marriage. His nephew Jan III succeeded him in 1350.

Köke Temür (d. 1375), also called Wang Baobao, was the foremost commander of the late Yuan and pillar of the Northern Yuan. In 1362 he inherited the army of his adoptive father Chaghan Temür after his assassination, storming Yidu to avenge him.

In the struggle at the Yuan court he supported the crown prince against the general Bolad Temür, and was made Prince of Henan in 1365. He resisted the Ming, but Xu Da defeated him at Taiyuan in 1368 and Shen'er Gorge in 1370, driving him north.

In 1372 he crushed Xu Da's army near Karakorum, halting the Ming conquest of the steppe. He spurned every Ming surrender offer; Zhu Yuanzhang called him the extraordinary man of his age.

扩廓帖木儿（？—1375），汉名王保保，是元末最杰出的统帅，也是北元朝廷的支柱。1362年，其养父察罕帖木儿遇刺，他接管养父的军队，攻破益都为其报仇。

在元廷的权力斗争中，他支持太子对抗将领孛罗帖木儿，1365年受封河南王。他抵抗明军，却先后于1368年在太原、1370年在沈儿峪被徐达击败，被迫退往漠北。

1372年，他在哈拉和林附近大败徐达的军队，阻止了明朝对草原的征服。他拒绝明朝的一切劝降，朱元璋称他为“天下奇男子”。

Henry O'Neill (Irish: Anrí Ó Néill; d. 1347), son of Brian O'Neill and grandson of Hugh Boy O'Neill, succeeded his kinsman Donnell O'Neill as king of Tyrone in 1325. In 1338 a peace treaty granted him war-ravaged lands in southern Antrim, where his descendants built up the lordship of Clandeboye.

In 1345 the justiciar Ralph de Ufford deposed him for joining the rising against William Donn de Burgh, Earl of Ulster, and installed Áed Remar O'Neill instead. Henry died in 1347 and his son Muirchertach Ceannfada succeeded him in Clandeboye.

en:
Duan Guang, also called Duan Xinguang, was the ninth hereditary zongguan of Dali under the Mongol Yuan dynasty, succeeding in 1333. His general Gao Peng routed rebel tribal troops at Hewei Pass near Xiaguan in a battle so bloody the river was said to run red.

He fought the Mongol prince of Liang over their border and in 1343 defeated the prince's invading army at Kunmi Mountain, after which they divided the region at Luona Pass, the Duan ruling the south. He died in 1344 and was succeeded by his brother Duan Gong.

段光（？—1344），又称段信苴光，是元朝治下第九位世袭大理总管，1333年袭职。他派大将高蓬在河尾关（今下关）大破作乱的蕃兵，战况惨烈，史书称“河水尽赤，为之不流”。

en:
Frederick I (c. 1300–1359), born lord of Žovnek in the Savinja Valley, founded the house that would dominate Slovenian and Croatian history in the early fifteenth century. In 1322 the Counts of Heunburg died out in the male line, and he inherited their castles in Carinthia, Carniola and Styria, among them Celje.

His cousin Ulrich V of Pfannberg and Countess Elizabeth contested the inheritance, but with his brother-in-law Ulrich of Walsee's help he held nearly all of it by 1333. Loyal to the Habsburgs like his father, he served as their captain of Carniola and the Windic March, smoothed their takeover of 1335 and fought Charles of Luxembourg's forces in Carinthia.

In April 1341 Emperor Louis IV made him first Count of Celje. By Diemut of Wallsee he left sons Ulrich and Hermann.

en:
Hermann I (c. 1333–1385), Count of Celje, was the second son of Frederick I and Diemut of Wallsee. From his father's death in 1359 he ruled jointly with his elder brother Ulrich I, and alone after Ulrich's death in 1368, guarding the inheritance of his young nephew William.

His marriage to Catherine Kotromanić of Bosnia linked the counts of Celje to the Hungarian and Bosnian royal houses. He died in 1385, the greatest landowner in Slovenia, succeeded by his son Hermann II.

en:
Ulrich I (c. 1331–1368), eldest son of Frederick I of Celje and Diemut of Wallsee, was a condottiere from his teens. He first saw war in 1346 at Louis the Great of Hungary's unsuccessful siege of Zadar, then fought for Emperor Charles IV on his Italian expedition of 1354 and for Louis against Venice at Treviso in 1354–1355.

From 1359 he headed the house with his brother Hermann. In 1362–1363 he fought for the Habsburg duke Rudolf IV in Friuli and Tyrol and received Kamnik, Žalec and Vojnik in pledge; from 1362 he also served as Habsburg governor of Carniola.

His generalship is usually credited with bringing the Counts of Celje into the high nobility of Central Europe, and his son William, by Adelaide of Ortenburg, married Anna, daughter of Casimir III of Poland, tying the house to royalty.

He first saw war in 1346 at Louis the Great of [GetCountry('HUN').GetName]'s unsuccessful siege of Zadar, then fought for Emperor Charles IV on his Italian expedition of 1354 and for Louis against Venice at Treviso in 1354–1355.

From 1359 he headed the house with his brother Hermann. In 1362–1363 he fought for the Habsburg duke Rudolf IV in Friuli and [GetCountry('TIR').GetName] and received Kamnik, Žalec and Vojnik in pledge; from 1362 he also served as Habsburg governor of [GetCountry('CAR').GetName].

His generalship is usually credited with bringing the Counts of Celje into the high nobility of Central Europe, and his son William, by Adelaide of Ortenburg, married Anna, daughter of Casimir III of [GetCountry('POL').GetName], tying the house to royalty.
zh:
乌尔里希一世（约1331—1368）是采列的腓特烈一世与瓦勒塞的迪穆特的长子。他少年时即成为雇佣军首领，1346年随匈牙利国王路易大王围攻扎达尔，未能攻克；此后他为皇帝查理四世在意大利作战，1354—1355年又为匈牙利的路易在特雷维索对抗威尼斯。

1359年起，他与弟弟赫尔曼共同掌管家族。1362—1363年，他在弗留利和蒂罗尔为哈布斯堡公爵鲁道夫四世作战，得到卡姆尼克、扎莱茨和沃伊尼克作为抵押；1362年起，他还出任哈布斯堡治下的卡尼奥拉总督。

一般认为，正是他的统兵才能让采列伯爵家族进入了中欧的高级贵族圈。他与奥滕堡的阿德莱德之子威廉娶波兰国王卡齐米日三世之女安娜，使这个家族与王室联姻。

en:
Ulrich of Sanneck (c. 1255–1316) was a free noble and Lord of Žovnek in the March of Savinja. The son of Conrad I of Sanneck, he inherited the estates. In 1278 he fought at the Battle of Marchfeld beside King Rudolf I.

In 1308 he surrendered his lands to the Habsburg dukes and received them back as a fief, bringing the Savinja Valley into Habsburg Styria. His marriage gave their son Frederick the inheritance including Celje Castle and founded the House of Celje.

en:
Sir Uilleag, or Ulick, de Burgh, also called Ulick Burke of Annaghkeen, was an Anglo-Irish chieftain in County Galway. After the young Earl of Ulster was murdered at Carrickfergus in 1333, he led one of the three Burke factions in the civil war that followed, ruling south Connacht from Annaghkeen.

By 1340 his branch had made itself the independent Clanricarde, or Upper Mac William lordship. He died in 1343 or 1353 and was succeeded by his son Richard Óg.

en:
Mao Gui (died 1359) was a leading general of the northern Red Turban Song state. After helping take Huai'an in 1356, he was driven back by Yuan forces and sailed north from Haizhou to Shandong in 1357. He seized Yidu and Jinan, overran most of the peninsula, and at Yidu set up civil administration and founded 360 military-farming colonies.

In 1358 Liu Futong sent him against the Yuan capital Dadu; his force neared the capital and panicked the court before being repulsed. In 1359 his nominal superior Zhao Junyong murdered him and seized Shandong, and Mao's officers killed Zhao in revenge three months later, infighting that helped Yuan forces retake the peninsula.

毛贵（？—1359年）是北方红巾军韩宋政权的重要将领。1356年他参与攻克淮安，随后被元军击退，于1357年从海州乘船北上山东。他攻占益都、济南，控制了山东大半，在益都建立民政，设立360处屯田。

1358年，刘福通派他北伐元朝都城大都，所部一度逼近大都、震动元廷，最终被击退。1359年，名义上地位更高的赵均用杀害毛贵、吞并其地；三个月后，毛贵的部将为他报仇，杀死赵均用。这场内斗有利于元军收复山东。

en:
Berardo I da Varano (d. 1329) was the second lord of Camerino, ruling from his father Gentile I's death in 1284, jointly with his brother Rodolfo until 1316. A Guelph condottiere, he fought for Perugia against Foligno in 1288 and served as capitano del popolo of several cities before entering Pope Boniface VIII's service in 1297.

He was elected podestà of San Ginesio in 1300. In 1319 Pope John XXII named him Marquis of Ancona to defend the Papal States in the Marche.

He helped capture Recanati in 1322 but was defeated by the Ghibellines outside Osimo. The jurist and poet Cino da Pistoia took refuge at his court.

贝拉尔多一世·达瓦拉诺（？—1329）是卡梅里诺的第二代领主，1284年父亲真蒂莱一世死后继位，与兄弟鲁道夫共同统治至1316年。作为圭尔夫派雇佣军首领，他于1288年助佩鲁贾攻打福利尼奥，曾在数座城市出任人民统领，1297年转而为教皇卜尼法斯八世效力。

1300年他当选圣吉内西奥行政长官。1319年教皇约翰二十二世封他为安科纳侯爵，以捍卫教会国在马尔凯的领地。

1322年他参与攻取雷卡纳蒂，却在奥西莫城下被吉伯林派击败。法学家兼诗人奇诺·达皮斯托亚曾在他的宫廷避难。

en:
Berardo II da Varano was an Italian condottiere and lord of Camerino, a son of Gentile II da Varano. A Guelph like his father, he served the papal cause alongside him in the wars of Umbria and the March of Ancona against the Ghibellines.

He held the lordship of Camerino from 1335 to 1341. By his wife Bellafiore he had a son, Gentile III. Berardo died at Camerino in 1350, predeceasing his father.

en:
Gentile I da Varano (d. 1284), a Guelph leader, was the first lord of Camerino in the Marche. When the mercenary Percivalle Doria, vicar of King Manfred of Sicily, sacked the town, Gentile fled with its people and obtained help from Pope Alexander IV.

In 1259 he recovered Camerino and was proclaimed its lord. He repelled a second attack by Doria in 1264, and two years later was named podestà of Camerino and Rocca Contrada.

en:
Gentile II da Varano (d. 1355), fourth lord of Camerino, was the son of Berardo I. His family held the rocca of Varano, which controlled a pass between Umbria and the Marche. A Guelph, he was podestà of Florence in 1312 and fought alongside his father against the Ghibellines of Umbria and the March of Ancona. He stormed Matelica for Pope John XXII in 1322.

When Emperor Louis the Bavarian came down into Italy to support the Ghibellines, he offered Gentile the imperial vicariate, but was declined; Pope Clement VI then made him vicar of the Church for Camerino.

He received Cardinal Gil de Albornoz with full honours. His son Berardo predeceased him, and Rodolfo II took over Camerino in 1355.

Gentile III da Varano was an Italian condottiero, son of Berardo II da Varano, who ruled Camerino from 1385 until his death in 1399. Pope Urban V named him senator of Rome in 1368.

Loyal to Pope Gregory XI, he was confirmed in Tolentino and San Ginesio in 1377, the year his brother Rodolfo drove him out of Camerino. As lord he expelled his brother Venanzio's sons and captured a papal commander, so Pope Boniface IX granted the Da Varano the vicariate of Camerino.

Giovanni I da Varano was an Italian condottiero and lord of Camerino, a son of Berardo II da Varano. While his brothers Rodolfo and Venanzio joined the 1375 league against Pope Gregory XI, Giovanni stayed loyal to the Church and took part in the unsuccessful defence of Fabriano.

When Gregory XI returned to Rome in 1377, he confirmed Giovanni and his brother Gentile in possession of Tolentino and San Ginesio. Giovanni built the rocca Varano and ruled Camerino from 1384 until his death in 1385.

1377年格列高利十一世返回罗马后，将托伦蒂诺与圣杰内肖的领有权确认给乔瓦尼及其兄弟真蒂莱。他修建了瓦拉诺要塞，1384年起统治卡梅里诺，1385年去世。

en:
Rodolfo I da Varano (d. 1316), son of Gentile I, ruled Camerino jointly with his brother Berardo I from their father's death in 1284. A Guelph, he was capitano del popolo of Lucca in 1284, podestà of San Ginesio in 1299, and from 1301 capitano del popolo of Perugia.

He attended the June 1305 Perugia conclave that elected Pope Clement V. He enriched himself with property confiscated from Ghibellines, and on his death in 1316 the signoria passed to Berardo alone.

en:
Rodolfo II da Varano (d. 1384), lord of Camerino, was the son of Berardo and succeeded Gentile II in 1355. He had already made his name at the Christian capture of Smyrna in 1344.

In 1355 he defeated Galeotto Malatesta near Paderno, seized Recanati and captured him at Castelfidardo; the peace was sealed by Galeotto's marriage to his daughter Elisabetta. As papal gonfaloniere he reconquered Rimini, Fano and Pesaro for the Church.

In 1377 Pope Gregory XI made him commander-in-chief against Florence, and the Florentines painted him on a public building as a traitor, hanging upside down from a gallows. He died at Tolentino in 1384.

鲁道夫二世·达瓦拉诺（？—1384）是卡梅里诺领主，贝拉尔多之子，1355年继真蒂莱二世之位。1344年基督徒夺取士麦那之战中，他已凭战功成名。

1355年，他在帕代尔诺附近击败加莱奥托·马拉泰斯塔，攻占雷卡纳蒂，又在卡斯泰尔菲达尔多将其俘获；和约以加莱奥托迎娶他的女儿伊丽莎白为凭。他任教皇旗官时，为教会收复里米尼、法诺和佩萨罗。

1377年教皇格列高利十一世任命他为对抗佛罗伦萨的总司令，佛罗伦萨人便把他画成叛徒，倒吊在绞架上，绘在一座公共建筑的墙上。1384年他卒于托伦蒂诺。

en:
Naghachu (d. 1388) was a Mongol general of the Northern Yuan who held out in Liaodong after the Yuan collapse. A descendant of Muqali and a myriarch at Taiping, he was captured in 1355, refused to defect to Zhu Yuanzhang and was freed.

As grand commandant he gathered Mongol forces in the northeast, holding Jinshan with some two hundred thousand men and raiding the Ming frontier, his influence extending over much of Rehe and Liaoning.

In 1387 a two-hundred-thousand-strong Ming army under Feng Sheng and Fu Youde advanced, and he surrendered. Made Marquis of Haixi, he died at Wuchang in 1388 on the Yunnan campaign, reportedly from overdrinking.

纳哈出（？—1388）是北元蒙古将领，元朝灭亡后坚守辽东。他是名将木华黎的后裔，任太平路万户时于1355年被俘，拒绝归顺朱元璋而被释放。

官至太尉后，他在东北聚集蒙古部众，拥众二十万据守金山一带，屡次进犯明朝边境，势力遍及热河和辽宁大部。

1387年，冯胜、傅友德率二十万明军进逼，纳哈出投降，受封海西侯。1388年他随军征讨云南，途中在武昌去世，相传因饮酒过度而死。

Gülçiçek Hatun was a Greek woman from Bithynia who entered the Ottoman palace and became a concubine of Sultan Murad I around 1359. She bore him the future Sultan Bayezid I, later called Yıldırım.

As the mother of a sultan she founded a pious establishment whose revenues paid for a mosque at Bursa, the first built by an Ottoman concubine, and for her own tomb. She died around 1400 and was buried in that tomb.

居尔奇切克哈屯是出身比提尼亚的希腊女子，进入奥斯曼宫廷后，约于1359年成为苏丹穆拉德一世的妃嫔。她为穆拉德生下后来的苏丹、绰号‘闪电’的巴耶济德一世。

作为苏丹之母，她设立宗教慈善基金会，以其收入在布尔萨修建清真寺——她是第一位修建清真寺的奥斯曼妃嫔——并为自己修建陵墓。她约于1400年去世，葬于该陵墓。

Ghiyath al-Din İbrahim I was bey of Candar from 1341 until his death around 1345, the eldest son of Süleyman I Pasha. His father first entrusted him with governing Sinop, annexed in 1322, but later named İbrahim's youngest brother Çoban heir, so around 1340 İbrahim rebelled and took Kastamonu.

In 1341 he captured about ten Genoese vessels in a clash over Genoa's trading post near Sinop. In 1346 his cousin Adil came to the throne.

en:
Süleyman I Pasha was the second bey of Candar, succeeding his father Şemseddin Yaman Candar. In 1309 he seized Kastamonu, killed Mahmud of the Chobanids and made the city his capital. He ruled under Ilkhanid suzerainty until Abu Sa'id's death, took control of Sinop in 1322, declared independence in 1327 and minted coins from 1335.

At peace with his neighbours, he continued raiding Byzantium. When he named his youngest son Çoban heir, his son İbrahim revolted and took Kastamonu; Süleyman died in 1340, aged over eighty.

苏莱曼一世·帕夏是詹达尔王朝第二代贝伊，继其父谢姆塞丁·亚曼·詹达尔而立。1309年，他攻取卡斯塔莫努，杀死丘班王朝的马哈茂德，并定该城为都。他先在伊利汗国宗主权下统治，直至大汗不赛因去世；1322年接管锡诺普，1327年宣布独立，1335年起自铸钱币。

他与邻邦相安，却继续袭掠拜占庭。他原想立幼子丘班为继承人，儿子易卜拉欣便起兵夺取卡斯塔莫努。苏莱曼于1340年去世，享年八十余岁。

en:
Şemseddin Yaman Candar was a Turkish commander of the Kayı Oghuz line and the founder of the Candar principality in northern Anatolia. He was rewarded with the Eflani region for distinguished service to Sultan Mesud II of Rum.

He established himself there as an independent bey, founding the Candaroğulları dynasty. He ruled until his death in 1309 and was succeeded by his son Süleyman I.

Aedh mac Tairdelbach Ó Conchobair, a son of Toirdelbach Ó Conchobair, claimed the kingship of Connacht after his father's death in 1345. His reign was spent warring with his cousin Aedh mac Feidlimid.

In 1350 MacWilliam Burke and the lords of Connacht deposed him, but he returned in 1351 and retook the kingship by force in 1352. In 1356 he was killed at Balloughdacker by Donnchad Carrach Ó Cellaig.

艾德·麦克·泰尔代尔巴赫·奥康诺尔是泰尔代尔巴赫·奥康诺尔之子，1345年父亲死后争得康诺特王位。他在位期间一直与堂亲艾德·麦克·费德利米德交战。

Ruaidrí Ua Conchobair (c. 1116–1198), anglicised Rory O'Conor, succeeded his father Tairrdelbach as king of Connacht in 1156 and was inaugurated High King of Ireland in 1166, the first to rule without opposition. He expelled Diarmait Mac Murchada, but the exiled king's Norman allies invaded from 1169.

He united the Irish kings, besieged Dublin in 1171 and won at Thurles, but could not stop the invasion. The 1175 Treaty of Windsor made him Henry II's subordinate king; he abdicated in 1183 and died in 1198, the last High King of Ireland.

Toirdelbach Ó Conchobair was a king of Connacht and a son of Aedh mac Eogain Ó Conchobair. In 1317, after the Second Battle of Athenry, he displaced Ruaidri na Fed and seized the kingship, only to be deposed by Cathal mac Domnaill in 1318.

He won back Connacht in 1324, lost it in 1342 and recovered it in 1343. On 15 October 1345 he was killed by an arrow fighting the Clan Murtagh Ó Conchobair, after a longer reign than any Connacht king of his generation.

Tairrdelbach Mór Ua Conchobair (1088–1156) became king of Connacht in 1106 after deposing his brother Domnall, and was recognised as High King of Ireland from about 1120. He broke the power of the Ua Briain dynasty of Munster by partitioning the province and crushing its army at the Battle of Móin Mór in 1151.

He campaigned across Ireland and died in 1156 after a reign of fifty years. His son Ruaidrí succeeded him in Connacht and later became High King.

en:
Chen Youding (d. 1368) was a Yuan loyalist general who held Fujian during the dynasty's collapse. Orphaned and impoverished, he worked as a farm labourer and in a salt shop before enlisting as a postal soldier.

He won promotion from 1352 by crushing revolts and defeated Chen Youliang's general Deng Keming. In 1364 he lured Zhu Yuanzhang's officer Hu Shen into an ambush and killed him. He suppressed the Ispah rebellion in coastal Fujian and rose to Pingzhang, the province's highest official.

When Ming armies took his stronghold Yanping in 1367, he attempted suicide, was captured and taken to Nanjing, refused to submit, and was executed in 1368.

Palladio Avogadro came from Vercelli's noble Avogadro family, which supplied many bishops to the Piedmontese church. In 1326 he became bishop of Ivrea, the diocese covering the Canavese.

The episcopal castle of Albiano d'Ivrea had belonged to his see since Emperor Otto III granted it in 1000; Palladio invested it to Philip I of Savoy-Acaia. After wars in the Canavese later in the century, the castle returned to the bishops.

In 1329 he toured his diocese. On 25 August he described San Michele at Parella as in good repair but poorly adorned, and also visited San Costanzo at Pont Canavese. He remained bishop until his death around 1346.

en:
Cola di Rienzo (1313–1354) was a Roman notary who championed the Roman people against the city's barons. A nobleman had killed his brother, sharpening his desire to restore order in Rome. A mission to Pope Clement VI at Avignon in 1343 won him papal favour, and in 1347 he led a rising and took the title of tribune.

He reformed justice, cleared robbers from the roads and summoned Italian cities to federate, but was driven from power within months. After years of imprisonment in Prague and Avignon he returned to Rome in 1354 as papal senator, only to be murdered by a mob.

en:
Aliénor de Comminges (1329–1402) was the fourth daughter of Count Bernard VIII of Comminges. Clement VI bought the viscounty of Turenne from her sister Cécile as a wedding gift for his nephew Guillaume III Roger de Beaufort; they married in 1349–1350.

As viscountess of Turenne and lady of Meyrargues in Provence, Aliénor held the strong castle of Meyrargues and exercised justice there from 1370. Mother of the mercenary captain Raymond de Turenne, she backed his private war against the Anjou rulers of Provence and the Avignon papacy.

In 1385 she sent a barge across the Durance to supply Marie of Blois's opponents at Aix, and she reportedly forced fishmongers carrying Angevin banners as passes to swallow them. She submitted to Marie in 1388 only after a siege, was seized by Marshal Boucicaut in 1399 and held at Aix until 1401. She died in 1402 and was buried there.

阿莉埃诺·德·科曼日（1329—1402）是科曼日伯爵贝尔纳八世的第四个女儿。教皇克雷芒六世从她姐姐塞西尔手中买下蒂雷纳子爵领，作为侄子纪尧姆三世·罗歇·德·博福尔的结婚礼物；两人于1349—1350年间成婚。

作为蒂雷纳子爵夫人兼普罗旺斯的梅拉尔格女领主，她坐镇坚固的梅拉尔格城堡，自1370年起在当地行使司法权。她是雇佣军首领蒂雷纳的雷蒙之母，支持儿子对统治普罗旺斯的安茹家族和阿维尼翁教廷发动私战。

1385年，她派驳船横渡杜朗斯河，向艾克斯的布卢瓦的玛丽之敌运送补给；相传她还逼迫举着安茹旗帜当通行证的鱼贩把旗帜吞下去。1388年她在遭围攻后才向玛丽臣服，1399年被布锡考元帅俘获，在艾克斯关到1401年。她于1402年去世，葬于艾克斯。

Arnaud I (c. 900–957) was count of Comminges and Couserans from about 940. Modern genealogists regard him as a son of Count Aznar III. He and his brother Roger I ruled the two counties jointly.

He appears with his wife Arsinde in donation charters to the abbeys of Lézat in 944 and Montolieu in 949. He died before 27 November 957, when a charter names only his widow and sons, and his lands were divided among his sons Roger, Eudes and Raymond.

en:
Aznar III (died 940) was count of Comminges, the son of Loup Aznar. He bore the title of viscount of Comminges during his father's lifetime and succeeded as count after his death. In 915, returning from a pilgrimage to Rome, he founded the monastery of Peyrisse.

Arnaud I and Roger I, thought to have been his sons, divided the county between them. Roger's line kept Comminges and ruled it until the fourteenth century.

en:
Bernard I (d. between 1145 and 1154) was the first great count of Comminges, succeeding his father Roger III before 1105. He joined the Aragonese Reconquista, fighting at the capture of Tudela in 1114 and at the taking of Zaragoza in 1118.

Around 1120 he married Dias de Samatan, heiress of Muret and Samatan, drawing Comminges into the orbit of Toulouse. He later contested the Val d'Aran with Aragon.

In 1134 Bernard met Alfonso VII of Castile at Zaragoza, probably seeking support, and in 1143 sought an agreement with the Count of Barcelona, apparently securing the valley by 1144.

贝尔纳一世（1145—1154年间卒）是科曼日第一位强权伯爵，1105年前继其父罗歇三世之位。他投身阿拉贡的收复失地运动，1114年参加攻取图德拉，1118年参加攻占萨拉戈萨。

约1120年，他娶米雷与萨马唐的女继承人迪亚斯·德·萨马唐，使科曼日进入图卢兹的势力圈，后来又为阿兰山谷与阿拉贡争执。

Bernard II of Comminges (died between 1149 and 1153) was the eldest son of Count Bernard I and Dias. He succeeded his father after 1145 and ruled only briefly.

In 1149–1150 he granted lands to the young Cistercian abbey of Bonnefont. He probably died young and childless, the first count known to be buried there, and his brother Dodon succeeded him as Bernard III.

en:
Bernard III of Comminges, born Dodon de Samatan (c. 1120–1176/1183), was a son of Count Bernard I. When his brother Bernard II died around 1153, Dodon inherited the county and took the name Bernard. He enlarged Muret and built its church of Saint-Jacques.

In 1176 he abdicated, granting Couserans to his son Roger and Saves to his son Guy. He married Laurence, and his heir was Bernard IV.

en:
Bernard IV (died 22 February 1225) succeeded his father Bernard III Dodon as count of Comminges in 1176, sharing the family lands with his brother Roger, who received the viscounty of Couserans. From 1180 to 1195 he occupied Saint-Lizier and expelled successive bishops until the pope intervened.

He later joined Count Raymond VI of Toulouse against Simon de Montfort in the Albigensian Crusade. Montfort occupied Comminges in 1212, but the Fourth Lateran Council restored the county to him in 1216, on condition that his daughter Pétronille marry Guy de Montfort; he made peace in 1220.

Bernard V (1196–30 November 1241) was the son of Count Bernard IV of Comminges. During the Albigensian Crusade he fought beside his father against Simon de Montfort, and in 1212 was sent to Aragon to persuade King Peter II to aid the southern lords against the crusaders.

In 1224 he married Cécile, daughter of the Count of Foix, and succeeded his father in 1225. He died at Lanta on 30 November 1241, leaving the county to his only son Bernard VI.

Bernard VI (c. 1224–before March 1300) was the only son of Count Bernard V of Comminges and Cécile de Foix. He succeeded his father in 1241 and did homage to Count Raymond VII of Toulouse a few days later. His reign of more than fifty years was marked by the foundation of numerous comital bastides.

In 1295 he retired, donating his lands at Muret to his eldest son Bernard VII and asking King Philip IV the Fair in writing to approve the transfer and receive his successor's homage.

en:
Bernard VIII (1280–1336) ruled Comminges from 1312, succeeding his father Bernard VII. Through his marriage in 1305 to Marguerite, only daughter of Viscount Raymond VII of Turenne, he became viscount of Turenne, retaining it under her will after Marguerite and their infant daughter died in 1314.

In 1335 he married his daughter Cécile to the Count of Urgell, brother of Peter IV of Aragon. He died in 1336 leaving only daughters; a posthumous son, Jean I, succeeded but died in infancy.

en:
Jean I of Comminges (May 1336–1339) was the posthumous only son of Count Bernard VIII and Mathe de l'Isle-Jourdain. Under his father's will he was recognized from birth as count of Comminges and viscount of Turenne, under his mother's guardianship.

He died in early 1339. His death opened a violent succession dispute between his mother and sisters and his uncle Pierre-Raymond, who denied women the right to inherit.

After months of war and years of legal disputes, Pierre-Raymond secured Comminges. His sister Cécile was instead recognized as viscountess of Turenne.

en:
Jeanne de Comminges (c. 1332–1398) was a daughter of Count Bernard VIII of Comminges and Mathe de l'Isle-Jourdain. After her cousin Pierre-Raymond II inherited the county in 1341, she claimed Comminges, and the quarrel ended in 1350 with her marriage to her rival.

When he died around 1376 she ruled the county as regent for their daughters. Gaston Fébus, Count of Foix, then claimed Comminges as a relative, but renounced his claim under the peace of 1379. Their elder daughter Éléonore died before her mother, so the younger, Marguerite, became countess. Jeanne died in 1398.

Laure de Montfort (c. 1262–1300) was the second daughter of Philippe II de Montfort, lord of Castres, and Jeanne de Lévis. After 1277 she married Bernard VII, count of Comminges.

In May 1290 she and her siblings divided their parents' inheritance, with Bernard representing her in the Albigeois. She died before 1 December 1300, leaving at least eight children, including Bernard VIII and the cardinal Jean-Raymond.

en:
Mathe de L'Isle-Jourdain (died 1352), a daughter of Bernard IV of L'Isle-Jourdain, married Count Bernard VIII of Comminges in 1315. When he died in 1336 she was pregnant; per his will the county passed to her posthumous son Jean, and Mathe ruled as regent from 1336 to 1339.

Jean died at age three, and the inheritance passed to her daughter Cécile, wife of James I of Aragon, Count of Urgell.

en:
Pierre-Raimond I (c. 1295–1341), the second son of Count Bernard VII of Comminges, inherited the lordship of Serrières. When his nephew, the child count Jean, died in 1339, the boy's sisters claimed Comminges; Pierre-Raimond denied that women could inherit the county, won the French king's backing, and made himself count.

The quarrel also aimed to keep Comminges from the Crown of Aragon, as the elder claimant Cécile had married the Count of Urgell. He fell gravely ill and died in April 1341, shortly after taking power.

en:
Pierre-Raimond II (died 1375) was Count of Comminges and Viscount of Serrières from 1341, succeeding his father Pierre-Raimond I. His cousin Jeanne contested the county, and the quarrel was settled by their marriage in 1350.

He fought for the king of France in the Hundred Years' War. His will was made in October 1375, and he died soon after, leaving the county first to his widow as regent and then to his daughter Marguerite.

Roger I (c. 930–1012) was a son of Count Arnaud I of Comminges and Arsinde of Carcassonne. From 957 he was associated with the rule of Comminges; in 983 he inherited Couserans on his father's death, and around 1000 he also received Carcassonne from his mother, uniting three counties in the Pyrenean foothills.

In 969 he married Adelaide of Rouergue; their daughter Ermesinde married Count Ramon Borrell of Barcelona, and their son Bernard-Roger became Count of Bigorre. He died in 1012 and was succeeded by his nephew William I of Carcassonne.

罗歇一世（约930—1012）是科曼日伯爵阿尔诺一世与卡尔卡松的阿尔桑德之子。957年起他参与治理科曼日，983年父亲去世后继承库瑟朗，约1000年又从母亲处获得卡尔卡松伯国，身兼比利牛斯山北麓三个伯国。

969年他娶鲁埃格的阿德莱德为妻，女儿埃尔梅辛迪嫁给巴塞罗那伯爵拉蒙·博雷利，儿子贝尔纳—罗歇成为比戈尔伯爵。他于1012年去世，由侄子卡尔卡松的纪尧姆一世继承。

en:
Corfitz Ulfeldt (1606–1664) was Denmark's most notorious traitor. The son of Chancellor Jacob Ulfeldt, he married Christian IV's daughter Leonora Christina in 1636 and became steward of the realm in 1643.

Suspected of embezzlement after Frederick III's accession, he fled to Sweden in 1651, and in the war of 1657–1658 guided Charles X Gustav's army across the frozen Belts and negotiated for Sweden the Treaty of Roskilde. Later condemned by Sweden too, he died a hunted fugitive in 1664; his wife then spent twenty-two years in Copenhagen's Blue Tower.

科尔费茨·乌尔费尔特（1606—1664）被后世视为丹麦最臭名昭著的叛国者。他是首相雅各布·乌尔费尔特之子，1636年迎娶克里斯蒂安四世之女莱奥诺拉·克里斯蒂娜，1643年出任王国宫廷总管。

腓特烈三世即位后，他因涉嫌贪渎在1651年逃奔瑞典；1657—1658年战争中，他引导卡尔十世·古斯塔夫的军队越过冰封的贝尔特海峡，并代表瑞典谈成《罗斯基勒条约》。后来他又被瑞典定罪，1664年作为被追捕的逃客死去；他的妻子随后在哥本哈根的蓝塔被囚禁了二十二年。

en:
Bartolomeo Casali (c. 1315–1363) succeeded his father Ranieri II as signore of Cortona in 1351. In 1352, serving Giovanni Visconti of Milan, he invaded Perugian territory and seized the fortress of Bettona by bribing its podestà; besieged by Perugia, Siena and Florence, he escaped in disguise, and in February 1353 publicly begged Perugia's pardon with a rope around his neck.

Emperor Charles IV confirmed him as imperial vicar in 1355. Perugia besieged Cortona in 1357, and in 1358 Bartolomeo allied with Siena; he died of plague in 1363 and was succeeded by his son Francesco I.

巴尔托洛梅奥·卡萨利（约1315—1363）于1351年继承父亲拉涅里二世，成为科尔托纳领主。1352年他效力于米兰的乔瓦尼·维斯孔蒂，入侵佩鲁贾领地，收买行政长官夺取贝托纳要塞；遭佩鲁贾、锡耶纳和佛罗伦萨联兵围困后他乔装逃走，1353年2月又颈系绳索，当众向佩鲁贾请罪求和。

1355年，皇帝查理四世确认他为帝国代理人。1357年佩鲁贾围攻科尔托纳，1358年他与锡耶纳结盟。1363年他死于瘟疫，儿子弗朗切斯科一世继位。

en:
Ranieri II Casali (c. 1280–22 January 1351) was a condottiero and the first signore of Cortona, founder of the Casali lordship that held the city until 1409. In 1324 he drove out the counts of Petrella when they tried to seize Cortona, and as one of the Three Consuls became its de facto lord in 1325.

In 1332 his brother Uguccio stormed the town hall to kill him, his son Bartolomeo and the bishop and hand the city to the Tarlati of Arezzo. Ranieri fought them off and then allied with Florence.

In 1336, backed by Perugia and with Bartolomeo beside him, he laid waste the country up to the walls of Arezzo. He died in 1351, and Bartolomeo succeeded him.

拉涅里二世·卡萨利（约1280—1351年1月22日）是雇佣兵首领、科尔托纳的首任领主，开创了统治该城直到1409年的卡萨利领主家系。1324年彼得雷拉伯爵企图夺取科尔托纳，被他赶出城去；1325年他作为“三执政官”之一成为事实上的统治者。

1332年，他的弟弟乌乔攻入市政厅，要杀死他、儿子巴尔托洛梅奥和主教，把城市献给阿雷佐的塔尔拉蒂家族。拉涅里奋力抵抗，将叛军逐出，随后与佛罗伦萨结盟。

1336年，他在佩鲁贾支持下与儿子巴尔托洛梅奥并肩，把阿雷佐城下的乡野劫掠一空。1351年他去世，巴尔托洛梅奥继位。

en:
Local tradition remembers Kriznook as a Kalasha ruler in southern Chitral in the early fourteenth century. He commanded the valleys of Shishi Kuh, Drosh and Urtsun, and Chitrali accounts also place several valleys of Bashgal under his rule, ranking him above the northern Kalasha chief Bulasing in power.

Around 1320 Shah Nadir Rais, founder of the Rais dynasty, killed Bulasing and overran upper Chitral; he raided Kriznook's lands too, but could not take them.

en:
Guido della Torre (27 September 1259 – summer 1312) was the Guelph lord of Milan from 1302 to 1312. After his father was killed in the Visconti victory at Desio in 1277, he was captured with his uncle Napoleone and spent seven years imprisoned in the Baradello castle near Como before escaping in 1284.

In 1302 a Guelph coalition drove the Visconti from Milan, ending twenty-five years of exile, and in 1307 he became capitano del popolo and then perpetual captain in 1308. After a failed rising against Emperor Henry VII in 1311, he fled to Cremona, where he died.

圭多·德拉·托雷（1259年9月27日—1312年夏）是1302至1312年间的米兰圭尔夫派领主。1277年维斯孔蒂家族在代西奥战役中取胜，他的父亲战死，他与叔父纳波莱奥内一同被俘，在科莫附近的巴拉德罗城堡被囚禁七年，1284年逃脱。

en:
Gregory V Šubić of Bribir (Grgur, c. 1300–c. 1374) was a son of Ban Paul I Šubić. In 1312 he received Šibenik and the family seat of Bribir.

Appointed guardian of his underage nephew George III after Paul II's death in 1346, he in 1347 surrendered Ostrovica and the county of Luka to King Louis I, receiving in exchange the fortress of Zrin and its neighbourhood. He settled at Zrin with his nephew, founding the Zrinski branch.

en:
George II Šubić of Bribir (c. 1290–1328) was a Croatian magnate, the second son of Ban Paul I Šubić. In 1303 he inherited his uncle's Dalmatian towns.

When his brother Mladen II fell in 1322, George became head of the Šubić clan. His forces were defeated near Knin in 1324, and Duke Nelipac captured him after the battle; his wife Lelka held his lands until his release in 1326.

He died at Klis on 15 December 1328. His daughter Jelena was the mother of King Tvrtko I of Bosnia.

布里比尔的尤拉伊二世·舒比奇（约1290—1328）是克罗地亚大贵族，巴昂帕瓦奥一世·舒比奇的次子。1303年，他继承叔父的达尔马提亚诸城。

1328年12月15日，他卒于克利斯。女儿耶莱娜是波斯尼亚国王特夫尔特科一世的母亲。

en:
George I Zrinski, also numbered George III Šubić of Bribir (c. 1330–1361), was a Croatian count and the founder of the Zrinski family. He was the son of Paul II Šubić.

Underage at his father's death in 1346, he and his guardian, his uncle Gregory, in 1347 gave Ostrovica and the county of Luka to King Louis I and received instead the fortress of Zrin; he was the first to call himself Zrinski, and was succeeded by his son Paul I.

en:
Charles Martel of Anjou (1271–1295) was the eldest son of Charles II of Naples and Maria of Hungary. After his uncle Ladislaus IV was killed in 1290, Pope Nicholas IV backed him as titular King of Hungary against Andrew III.

He won recognition in Croatia but never ruled Hungary itself, and he was acquainted with Dante, who portrayed a meeting with his spirit in the Heaven of Venus in the Divine Comedy.

By his wife Clemence of Habsburg he left a son, Charles Robert, who later won the Hungarian crown as Charles I. He died of plague at Naples in 1295.

en:
Mladen III Šubić (c. 1315–1348) was a grandson of Pavao I, the most powerful Croatian noble of his age; by his time he was almost the last man left to defend the family. From Klis Fortress he held Klis, Omiš and Skradin, his mother Lelka ruling the lands until he came of age in 1332.

He fought the coalition of Split, Trogir and Šibenik under Venice and the nobles led by Ivan Nelipić, forcing the return of Ostrovica in 1335, and by 1344 was the chief opponent of the Hungarian king. Against Louis I he allied with Bosnia in 1338.

In 1348 he took the title Marquess of Slavonia, aiming to end Louis's rule in Croatia, but plague killed him that May. He was buried in Trogir Cathedral, where his epitaph called him the Shield of the Croats.

姆拉登三世·舒比奇（约1315—1348年）是克罗地亚最有权势的贵族帕沃一世之孙；到他这一代，家族几乎只剩他一人撑持。他以克利斯要塞为中心，统治克利斯、奥米什和斯克拉丁，1332年成年前由母亲莱尔卡掌管领地。

他击败威尼斯支持下的斯普利特、特罗吉尔、希贝尼克三城联军和伊万·内利皮奇率领的贵族，1335年迫使对方归还奥斯特罗维察，到1344年已是匈牙利国王的主要对手。为对抗拉约什一世，他于1338年与波斯尼亚结盟。

1348年他起用斯拉沃尼亚侯爵称号，意在推翻拉约什在克罗地亚的统治，却在当年5月死于瘟疫。他葬于特罗吉尔主教座堂，墓志称他为“克罗地亚人之盾”。

Paul II Šubić of Bribir (c. 1295–1346) was the third son of Paul I Šubić, Ban of Croatia. He held Trogir and Skradin, and joined Croatian nobles in rebelling against his eldest brother Mladen II, defeated at Bliska in 1322.

Afterwards he supported his brother George II against Duke Nelipac II, receiving Ostrovica for his aid. He died there in August 1346, leaving the fortress to his underage son George III, ancestor of the Zrinski counts, under the guardianship of his brother Gregory.

en:
Antonio I del Carretto (1260–1313), marquess of Finale, was the son of Giacomo del Carretto and Caterina da Marano, Frederick II's natural daughter. As a minor he divided the family lands with his brothers, keeping Finale.

A Ghibelline, he made peace with Charles of Anjou in 1270. His refusal in 1280 to swear an oath to Genoa opened a long war with the republic, to which he submitted in 1292. He issued statutes for Finale in 1311 and died in 1313.

安东尼奥一世·德尔·卡雷托（1260—1313）是菲纳莱侯爵，贾科莫·德尔·卡雷托与腓特烈二世私生女卡泰丽娜·达·马拉诺之子。他幼年继位，与诸弟瓜分家族领地，自己领有菲纳莱。

en:
Antonio II del Carretto (1284–1321), younger son of the marquess of Finale Antonio del Carretto and Leonora Fieschi, settled in Sicily early in the fourteenth century. In 1307 he married Costanza Chiaromonte, daughter of a leader of the Sicilian Ghibellines, and through her held the baronies of Calatabiano and Siculiana; Racalmuto later passed to their son.

He drew little profit from his claims to Finale, then caught in Genoese internal struggles. He died in Palermo in 1321, leaving a Sicilian line that lasted until the eighteenth century.

安东尼奥二世·德尔·卡雷托（1284—1321）是菲纳莱侯爵安东尼奥与莱奥诺拉·菲耶斯基的幼子，14世纪初迁居西西里。1307年，他迎娶西西里吉伯林派领袖之女科斯坦扎·迪·基亚罗蒙特，凭借她领有卡拉塔比亚诺和锡库利亚纳男爵领；拉卡尔穆托后来传给他们的儿子。

他对菲纳莱的继承权所获甚微，当时菲纳莱卷入热那亚的内部斗争。他于1321年卒于巴勒莫，留下的西西里支系一直延续到18世纪。

en:
Beatrice del Monferrato (c. 1142–1228), daughter of William V, Marquess of Montferrat, and Judith of Babenberg, married in 1155 Guigues V, Count of Albon, who died in 1162.

Around 1165 her cousin Frederick Barbarossa gave the widow to Enrico I del Carretto, called il Guercio, marquess of Savona; their children included Ottone and Enrico II. Widowed again in 1185, she returned to Montferrat, where around 1197 the troubadour Raimbaut de Vaqueiras made her the subject of several songs. She died in 1228.

贝亚特丽切·迪·蒙费拉托（约1142—1228）是蒙费拉托侯爵古列尔莫五世与巴本贝格的尤蒂特之女。1155年，她嫁给阿尔邦伯爵吉格五世，丈夫于1162年去世。

Carlo I del Carretto was a son of Giorgio del Carretto and founder of the Zuccarello branch of his house. Under the family settlement of 1385, after he ceded his share of Finale to his brother Lazzarino I in 1390, Carlo kept the Clavesana lands around Zuccarello.

A close ally of Gian Galeazzo Visconti, he was in 1397 invested as the first marquis of Zuccarello. By Pomellina Adorno he fathered Ilaria, who in 1403 married Paolo Guinigi of Lucca; her tomb there was carved by Jacopo della Quercia.

Costanza Chiaramonte was the only daughter of Federico Chiaramonte, lord of Sutera, and sister of Manfredi I, Count of Modica. In 1296 her father received the barony of Siculiana from King Frederick III of Sicily and built the Castello di Chiaramonte there; on his death in 1311 she inherited the barony.

She first married Antonio del Carretto, margrave of Finale. Widowed, she married the Genoese nobleman Brancaleone Doria, governor of Sardinia. Her son Antonio del Carretto Chiaramonte later inherited Siculiana.

en:
Enrico I del Carretto, also called il Guercio (died 1185), was an Aleramici nobleman and marquess of Savona, the son of Bonifacio del Vasto. He earned his nickname on the Second Crusade and later fought alongside Frederick Barbarossa, who confirmed his fiefs in 1162.

As the communes of Savona and Noli gained autonomy, Enrico consolidated his family's remaining position at Finale. As imperial chancellor he negotiated the Peace of Constance with the Lombard League in 1183.

In 1179 he founded a hospital at Cosseria. From his son Ottone sprang the del Carretto line, which later made Finalborgo its seat.

恩里科一世·德尔·卡雷托（卒于1185年），绰号“圭尔乔”，是阿莱拉米奇家族贵族、萨沃纳侯爵，博尼法乔·德尔·瓦斯托之子。他在第二次十字军东征中得到绰号，后来随腓特烈一世作战，后者于1162年确认了他的封地。

1179年他在科塞里亚创立一座医院。其子奥托内一支发展为德尔·卡雷托家族，后来以菲纳尔博尔戈为治所。

en:
Enrico II del Carretto (c. 1170–1231), marquess of Savona, was the second son of Enrico il Guercio and Beatrice del Monferrat. Succeeding around 1185, he divided the family lands with his brother Ottone, taking the western portion around Finale. In 1188 he founded the Burgus Finarii, later Finalborgo.

He married Simona Guercio. He backed Otto IV before siding with Frederick II, who in 1226 confirmed his rights to the march, but defeat at Savona in 1227 forced him to swear fealty to Genoa.

他迎娶西莫娜·圭尔乔。他先支持奥托四世，后倒向腓特烈二世，后者于1226年确认他对侯爵领地的权利；1227年萨沃纳战败后，他被迫向热那亚宣誓效忠。

en:
Giacomo del Carretto (c. 1215–1268) was marquess of Finale, succeeding his father Enrico II around 1233. A loyal Ghibelline of his kinsman Frederick II, he fought Genoa and led the defence of Savona in 1243. In 1247 he married Caterina da Marano, a natural daughter of Frederick II, and became imperial vicar north of Asti.

After the emperor's death he made peace with Genoa at Varazze in 1251, surrendering Segno but keeping Finale. He died in 1268, when his lands were divided among his sons.

贾科莫·德尔·卡雷托（约1215—1268年）是菲纳莱侯爵，约1233年继其父恩里科二世之位。作为亲属腓特烈二世的忠实吉伯林派，他与热那亚作战，1243年指挥萨沃纳保卫战。1247年，他迎娶腓特烈二世的私生女卡泰丽娜·达·马拉诺，并成为阿斯蒂以北地区的帝国代理人。

皇帝死后，他于1251年在瓦拉泽与热那亚议和，交出塞尼奥但保住了菲纳莱。他于1268年去世，领地由诸子瓜分。

en:
Giorgio del Carretto (1280–c. 1359) was marquis of Finale in Liguria, eldest son of Antonio del Carretto. A leader of the Ghibelline exiles, he reduced the Guelph stronghold of Noli in 1322.

After he ravaged the territory of Albenga in 1341, the Genoese doge Simone Boccanegra seized him under a safe conduct and confined him in a wooden cage until his escape at Christmas 1344. He made peace with Genoa in 1345 and received imperial investiture from Charles IV in 1355.

乔治·德尔·卡雷托（1280—约1359）是利古里亚的菲纳莱侯爵，安东尼奥·德尔·卡雷托的长子。作为流亡的皇帝派领袖，他于1322年攻克教皇派据点诺利。

1341年他劫掠阿尔本加一带后，热那亚总督西蒙·博卡内格拉背信将他拘捕，关入木笼，直到1344年圣诞节他才越狱逃脱。1345年他与热那亚议和，1355年获皇帝查理四世正式封授领地。

en:
Lazzarino I del Carretto (died 1392), son of Giorgio del Carretto, inherited the marquisate of Finale and its long feud with Genoa. In 1385 Genoa demanded he do vassal homage; he refused, invoking his house's imperial investitures. Doge Antoniotto Adorno's troops occupied Finale and forced him to swear fealty.

In 1390 his brother Carlo ceded him his share, and Lazzarino lifted old bans on settling by the coast. He left a successor, his son Lazzarino II.

en:
Albertino Morosini (c. 1240–1305) was a Venetian nobleman and statesman. He served as Count of Zara and later as bailo in Acre, where he concluded a treaty with Tyre restoring Venetian privileges there.

As podestà of Pisa he commanded its fleet against Genoa and was wounded and captured at the Battle of Meloria in 1284. He became Duke of Crete in 1287, facing the revolt of Alexios Kallergis.

After his nephew Andrew III became king of Hungary, Morosini was made Duke of Slavonia in 1297. He returned to Venice after Andrew's death in 1301 and died there in 1305.

阿尔贝蒂诺·莫罗西尼（约1240—1305年）是威尼斯贵族与政治家。他曾任扎拉伯爵，后任威尼斯驻阿卡代表，在任上与提尔签订条约，恢复威尼斯人在当地的特权。

担任比萨执政官时，他率比萨舰队与热那亚作战，1284年在梅洛里亚海战中负伤被俘。1287年他出任干地亚公爵，任内面对阿莱克修斯·卡莱尔吉斯起义。

外甥安德拉什三世成为匈牙利国王后，莫罗西尼于1297年受封斯拉沃尼亚公爵。1301年安德拉什三世去世后，他返回威尼斯并于1305年在该地去世。

Iacopo II Barozzi (died 1308) was a Venetian colonial administrator and the first Barozzi lord of Santorini. He served as Duke of Candia from 1301 to 1303, and Venice's 1302 treaty with Emperor Andronikos II recognized his seizure of Santorini; he acknowledged only the Republic as his suzerain.

William I Sanudo, Duke of Naxos, captured him in transit, until Venice's Great Council forced his release. Barozzi retired to Candia in 1308 and died there.

Marco Venier (died 1311) was a Venetian noble of the Venier family and Lord of Cerigo, the island of Kythera off the southern Greek coast. He was born to a daughter of Nikolaos Evdaimogiannis, the Greek lord of Kythera.

In 1310 the Venetians and the Venier clan retook the island, which Byzantium had held since 1269. Marco died in 1311, and his son Pietro Venier continued the line of Cerigo governors.

en:
Michel Vitali was a Venetian nobleman who served as Duke of Candia for the Republic in 1299. That year he signed the Peace of Alexios Kallergis with the leaders of the great Cretan rebellion that had broken out in 1282.

Its articles proclaimed a general amnesty, restored confiscated lands and privileges, and lifted the ban on mixed Cretan–Venetian marriages. The treaty ended seventeen years of war and left Alexios Kallergis as the recognized head of the Orthodox Cretans.

en:
Tito Venier was a Venetian feudatory on Crete and a leader of the 1363 Revolt of Saint Titus, the first Cretan rising in which Venice's own Latin colonists took part. When the Senate pressed new taxes on Crete, the Venier and Gradenigo families led the revolt.

They arrested the Duke of Candia, set up the Commune of Crete and raised the banner of Saint Titus. Venice sent an army which retook Candia in May 1364.

Proscribed with his brother Teodorello, Tito renewed the rising in western Crete that August. When the other rebel chiefs were captured and tortured to death after the famine of 1365, Tito alone escaped by leaving the island.

蒂托·韦涅尔是克里特岛上的威尼斯封臣，也是1363年圣提多起义的领袖之一，这是克里特第一次有威尼斯自己的拉丁殖民者参加的起义。元老院向克里特加征新税后，韦涅尔与格拉德尼戈两家领头发难。

他们逮捕干地亚公爵，建立克里特公社，举起主保圣人圣提多的旗帜。威尼斯出兵于1364年5月收复干地亚。

被通缉后，蒂托与兄弟泰奥多雷洛于当年8月在克里特西部重新起事。1365年饥荒过后，其余叛党首领均被捕并处以酷刑而死，唯有蒂托离岛逃脱。

en:
Teodorello Venier was a Venetian feudal noble on Crete and brother of Tito Venier. In 1363 he was among the leaders of the revolt of Saint Titus against Venice, which overthrew the island's government and set up the rebel Republic of Saint Titus.

After a Venetian army under Luchino dal Verme retook Candia in May 1364, Teodorello and Tito carried on the rising from western Crete. The last rebel leaders were taken through treason and killed in 1366; only Tito escaped the island.

en:
Viago Zeno was a Venetian noble of the Zeno family who served as Duke of Crete (Candia) in 1333. That year he ordered new taxes to build more galleys against the piracy spreading along the Cretan coasts.

The exactions broke the Peace of Alexios Kallergis of 1299, and by September 1333 western Crete had risen under Vardas Kallergis. With the help of Cretan allies the Venetians suppressed the uprising in 1334; its leaders were executed and their families exiled.

en:
Li Siqi (1323–1374) was a Yuan warlord from Luoshan in Henan who ruled Shaanxi. He raised militia with Chaghan Temur against the Red Turbans, and after clearing Shaanxi of rebels in 1357 built his own power base there. After Chaghan's death in 1362, Li refused orders to obey his son Köke Temür and held Chang'an against Köke's attacks.

He surrendered to the Ming in 1369. The Hongwu Emperor later sent him to win over Köke Temür; Köke's horsemen demanded an arm as a parting gift, and Li Siqi died of the wound in 1374.

李思齐（1323—1374），河南罗山人，是元末据有陕西的军阀。他起初与察罕帖木儿组织武装镇压红巾军，1357年协同把红巾军逐出陕西后，便在当地建立自己的势力。1362年察罕帖木儿死后，李思齐拒绝服从其子扩廓帖木儿，固守长安击退扩廓的进攻。

1369年他投降明朝。后来洪武帝派他去招降扩廓帖木儿，对方的骑兵要他留下一只手臂作为告别之物；李思齐断臂交给骑士，回去不久便在1374年因伤重而死。

en:
Liu Futong (1321–1363) was the dominant leader of the Northern Red Turbans in the late Yuan uprisings. In 1351 he and White Lotus preacher Han Shantong rebelled among Yellow River labourers. After Han was executed, Liu fought on and in 1355 installed Han's son Han Lin'er at Bozhou as emperor of a restored Song.

Han's claim helped unite the northern rebels. Liu's men took the old Song capital Kaifeng in 1358, but Yuan forces under Chaghan Temur retook it in 1359, forcing Liu back to Anfeng. In 1363 Zhang Shicheng's troops captured Anfeng and killed Liu there. Zhu Yuanzhang then rescued Han Lin'er.

刘福通（1321—1363）是元末北方红巾军的主要领袖。1351年，他与白莲教首领韩山童在治河民夫中起兵。韩山童被捕杀后，刘福通继续率部作战，于1355年在亳州拥立韩山童之子韩林儿为帝，国号宋。

韩林儿的帝号有助于凝聚北方红巾军。1358年，刘福通攻取北宋故都汴梁，但1359年元将察罕帖木儿反攻夺回汴梁，刘福通退守安丰。1363年，张士诚所部攻破安丰，刘福通被杀。朱元璋随后救出了韩林儿。

en:
Han Lin'er (1339–1367), son of the executed White Lotus rebel Han Shantong, was the nominal emperor of the late-Yuan Red Turban movement. After his father's arrest he went into hiding. In 1355 Liu Futong enthroned him as emperor of a restored Song.

Liu held real power at his court. Red Turban forces seized Kaifeng as their capital in 1358 but lost it in 1359.

In 1363 Zhu Yuanzhang rescued him from the siege of Anfeng and installed him at Chuzhou. In 1367, while being escorted to Zhu's domains, he drowned crossing the Yangtze at Guabu, perhaps murdered on Zhu's orders.

韩林儿（1339—1367）是元末红巾军拥立的皇帝，白莲教首领韩山童之子。父亲被捕后，他一度躲藏。1355年刘福通奉他为帝，国号“宋”。

刘福通掌握朝政。红巾军于1358年攻取汴梁定为都城，1359年又兵败弃城。

1363年，朱元璋在安丰之围中将他救出，安置于滁州。1367年，他在被迎往朱元璋辖地途中，于瓜步渡长江时溺死，或说系朱元璋授意谋害。

en:
Han Shantong (died 1351) was a White Lotus preacher and a founder of the Red Turban rebellion against the Yuan dynasty. He taught that the Maitreya Buddha and the King of Light would soon appear and claimed descent from the Song emperors.

In 1351, when the Yuan conscripted labourers to repair Yellow River dikes, he and Liu Futong buried a one-eyed stone man there and plotted revolt. The plot was discovered and Han was captured and executed. Liu continued to lead the rebellion, while Han's son Han Lin'er became its figurehead, the Young King of Ming.

韩山童（？—1351）是元末白莲教首领、红巾军起义的发起人之一。他宣扬“弥勒佛降生、明王出世”，自称是宋朝皇室后裔。

1351年，元朝强征民夫修筑黄河堤坝，他与刘福通在工地埋下一尊独眼石人，筹划起义。计划败露后，他被俘遇害。刘福通继续领导起义，其子韩林儿成为运动的象征，称“小明王”。

Chronicles record Curu Yaya as a daughter of the early Inca ruler Lluq'i Yupanki of Cuzco and a sister of Mayta Qhapaq.

They relate that Mayta Qhapaq formed a union with her in his youth — whether she was his concubine is uncertain — and that their son was Qhapaq Yupanki, the fifth ruler of Cuzco and the last of the Hurin dynasty.

Chronicles describe Cusi Chimbo as a daughter of an Ayarmaca lord, given to the Sapa Inca Cápac Yupanqui as a concubine who became his second wife. She was the mother of Inca Roca.

Around 1350, the same chronicles relate, she poisoned Cápac Yupanqui at Cusco: his death let her son's Hanan Cusco faction storm the Inticancha palace, overthrow the Hurin dynasty and place Inca Roca on the throne, founding the Hanan dynasty.

en:
Inca Roca (Inka Ruq'a, c. 1330–1380) is presented in the chronicles as the sixth ruler of Cusco and the first Sapa Inca of the Hanan Cusco dynasty, who reached the throne by a coup. After Cápac Yupanqui's death the Hanan faction rebelled, killed the designated heir Quispe Yupanki and placed Inca Roca on the throne.

The old order was not swept away: a Hurin chief stayed at the Inticancha as high priest of the Sun while the Hanan took secular power. Chronicles credit him with founding the Yachaywasi, the school where Inca noble boys learned Quechua, religion, quipus and warfare.

Legend gives him victories over the Chancas, who kept troubling his successors, though he more reliably seems to have improved the irrigation works around Cusco. His younger son Yáhuar Huácac succeeded him.

After #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('csu_qhapaq_yupanki').GetID],X #L Cápac Yupanqui#!#!'s death the Hanan faction rebelled, killed the designated heir Quispe Yupanki and placed Inca Roca on the throne.

The old order was not swept away: a Hurin chief stayed at the Inticancha as high priest of the Sun while the Hanan took secular power. Chronicles credit him with founding the Yachaywasi, the school where Inca noble boys learned Quechua, religion, quipus and warfare.

Legend gives him victories over the Chancas, who kept troubling his successors, though he more reliably seems to have improved the irrigation works around Cusco. His younger son Yáhuar Huácac succeeded him.

编年史中的印卡·罗卡（约1330—1380年）是库斯科的第六位统治者，也是哈南·库斯科王朝的第一位萨帕·印卡，靠一场政变登上王位。卡帕克·尤潘基死后，哈南派反叛，杀死指定继承人基斯佩·尤潘基，拥立印卡·罗卡。

旧秩序并未被一扫而空：一名乌兰首领留驻印蒂坎查担任太阳最高祭司，哈南一派执掌世俗权力。编年史把创办‘雅奇瓦西’归于他：贵族少年在这所学校学习克丘亚语、宗教、奇普与军事。

传说他战胜了昌卡人，但昌卡人仍不断困扰他的继任者；不过较为可信的是，他似乎改善了库斯科周边的灌溉工程。他去世后，较年幼的儿子亚瓦尔·瓦卡克继位。

Lluq'i Yupanki (c. 1260–c. 1290) was the third Sapa Inca of the Kingdom of Cusco and a member of the Hurin dynasty, succeeding his father Sinchi Roca; chronicles call him the first Inca ruler born in Cusco itself.

His reign brought almost no territorial expansion, as the Incas fought constantly to keep their hold on the Cusco valley. He is credited with establishing the market in Cusco and building the Acllahuasi, the house of chosen women. His son Mayta Qhapaq succeeded him.

en:
Manco Qhapaq (Manco Cápac; died c. 1230) is remembered as founder and first ruler of Cusco and ancestor of the Inca dynasty, although whether he really lived is uncertain. Tradition says he was born at Tamputoco, son of Apu Tambo, and on his father's death led the group into the Cusco valley.

There he defeated three small tribes and settled on ground between two streams that later became Cusco's main plaza. The larger tribes regarded the newcomers as invaders and attacked them often, so Manco and later his son had to defend the town.

His wife and sister Mama Uqllu bore his successor Sinchi Ruq'a, and he is named patriarch of the Qhapaq Ayllu royal lineage, branches Hurin and Hanan. He died naturally; his mummified body stayed in Cusco until Pachacuti moved it to the Temple of the Sun on the Isla del Sol, only his statue remaining there.

曼科·卡帕克（约1230年卒）相传是库斯科的建立者、首任统治者，也是印加王朝的始祖，不过他是否确有其人尚无定论。相传他生于坦普托科，是阿普·坦博之子，父亲去世后率领族人进入库斯科河谷。

他在河谷击败三个小部落，在后来成为库斯科主广场的两条小溪之间定居。大部落视新来者为入侵者，频频进攻，曼科和后来的儿子都得保卫城镇。

他的妻子兼姐妹玛玛·奥克略生下继承人辛奇·罗卡，他被奉为卡帕克·艾柳王族世系的始祖，该世系分乌林和哈南两支。他寿终正寝，木乃伊一直留在库斯科，直到帕查库提下令迁往太阳岛的太阳神殿，城中只留下他的一尊雕像。

en:
Mayta Qhapaq (Mayta Cápac, c. 1290–c. 1320) was the fourth ruler of the early Inca polity of Cuzco and a member of the Hurin dynasty, succeeding his father Lluq'i Yupanki. Spanish chronicles record that he was still a child at his accession, so his uncle governed as regent until he came of age.

He was remembered as a reformer of the calendar and is said to have subdued the Alcabisa and Culunchima peoples near Cuzco. His heir was Qhapaq Yupanki.

en:
Cápac Yupanqui (Quechua Qhapaq Yupanki, c. 1320–1350) was the fifth Sapa Inca of the Kingdom of Cusco and the last ruler of the Hurin dynasty, succeeding his father Mayta Cápac. His chief wife, Mama Cusi Hilpay, was the daughter of the lord of Anta, formerly a great enemy of the Incas.

In legend he was a conqueror, the first Inca to take land beyond the valley of Cusco, where he subdued the Cuyumarca and Ancasmarca peoples. He is also credited with new buildings, bridges, roads and aqueducts.

His death in 1350 brought the Hurin line down with it: the Hanan faction rebelled, killed his designated heir Quispe Yupanki, and gave the throne to Inca Roca, his son by another wife.

卡帕克·尤潘基（约1320—1350）是库斯科王国的第五位萨帕·印卡，也是乌林王朝末代君主，继承父亲迈塔·卡帕克之位。他的正妻玛玛·库西·希尔佩是安塔首领之女，安塔此前曾是印卡人的大敌。

传说中他是一位征服者，是第一位夺取库斯科河谷以外土地的印卡，降服了库尤马卡和安卡斯马卡人。他还被记在城中兴建了许多建筑、桥梁、道路和引水渠。

1350年他去世，乌林王朝也随之终结：哈南派起而反叛，杀死他指定的继承人基斯佩·尤潘基，把王位交给他与另一位妻子所生的印卡·罗卡。

He is credited with dividing the land into districts, holding the first Inca census, and ordering ear-piercing as a mark of nobility. He was succeeded by his son Lluq'i Yupanki.

en:
Tarco Huamán (fl. c. 1320) was a short-reigned Inca ruler of Cusco, the favorite son of Mayta Qhapaq and Mama Tancaray. He succeeded his father around 1320 but was overthrown by his cousin Qhapaq Yupanki, who killed nine of Tarco's brothers; he is absent from the official list of Sapa Incas.

After Qhapaq Yupanki conquered Cuyumarca near Cusco, he appointed Tarco its kuraka, or governor, charging him with a yearly tribute of a thousand cages of birds.

en:
Chitrali tradition remembers Shah Nadir Rais as the founder of the Rais dynasty that ruled Chitral in the Hindu Kush. The Nai Tarikh-i-Chitral relates that he was a foreign chief, presumably from Turkestan, who arrived in 1320 and brought the pre-Islamic Kafir period to an end.

The later Tarikh-i-Gilgit instead makes him a prince of the Trakhan dynasty of Gilgit. He is counted as the first of nine Rais rulers, a line later displaced by the Kator dynasty.

en:
Zou Pusheng was a blacksmith from Macheng in Hubei who became a chief leader of the southern Red Turbans. In 1351 the cloth peddler Xu Shouhui brought iron to him and asked him to make implements. Zou replied that the world needed a sword rather than farm tools, and the two planned a revolt under the sign of the red turban.

They rose at Qizhou, and when Xu was enthroned as Tianwan emperor late in 1351, Zou became Grand Preceptor. He kept the title after Chen Youliang seized power; his later fate is unknown.

邹普胜是湖北麻城人，以炼铁为生，后成为南派红巾军的主要首领之一。1351年，布贩徐寿辉携铁上门，请他打造器具；邹普胜答称天下需要的是剑而非锄锹，二人遂以红巾为号共谋起兵。

他们在蕲州起兵，1351年末徐寿辉称帝、建立天完政权，邹普胜受封太师。陈友谅夺权后他仍保有太师头衔，此后下落不明。

en:
Xu Shouhui (1320–1360) was a cloth peddler from Luotian in Hubei who became emperor of the southern Red Turbans. In August 1351 he joined the rising at Qizhou, which rallied followers with the promise of Maitreya's coming. That October, after Qishui was taken, he was proclaimed emperor of the Tianwan regime.

Yuan troops destroyed Qishui in 1353, but his forces recovered Jiangxi and Hunan and moved the capital to Hanyang in 1356. His minister Ni Wenjun held real power and attempted to kill him in 1357; Chen Youliang killed Ni and took control. Chen later held Xu captive and murdered him at Caishi in 1360.

zh:
徐寿辉（1320—1360），湖北罗田人，原是布贩，后来成为南方红巾军拥立的皇帝。1351年八月，他参加蕲州起事，起义军以弥勒降生号召群众。同年十月蕲水攻克后，他被拥立为帝，该政权后世多称天完。

1353年元军攻破蕲水，但所部后来收复江西、湖南，并于1356年迁都汉阳。丞相倪文俊把持实权，1357年谋杀徐寿辉未遂；陈友谅杀死倪文俊，夺取实权，后来挟持徐寿辉，于1360年在采石将他杀死。

en:
Ni Wenjun (died September 1357), nicknamed Manzi, was a fisherman from Hubei who became a top commander of the southern Red Turbans. Joining Xu Shouhui's rising, he rose to Grand Commandant of the Tianwan court.

In 1355 he destroyed at Hanchuan the river fleet of the Yuan Prince of Weishun, and retook Mianyang in 1356, where Chen Youliang entered his service. In September 1357, after his plot to murder Xu Shouhui failed, he fled to Huangzhou and was killed by Chen Youliang.

倪文俊（?—1357），号蛮子，湖北人，以捕鱼为业，是南派红巾军的重要将领。他随徐寿辉起兵，天完建国后受封太尉。

1355年，他在汉川大破元朝威顺王的水军；1356年攻占沔阳，陈友谅于此时投入他麾下。1357年九月，他谋害徐寿辉未成，逃奔黄州，被陈友谅袭杀。

en:
Achitomecatl Teomecatl II was tlatoani of Culhuacan from 1336 to 1347. The Anales de Cuauhtitlan record that in 1336 he killed tlatoani Huehue Acamapichtli, last lord of the old Chichimec dynasty, and enthroned himself; the dead lord's widow Ilancueitl and Acamapichtli fled to Cohuatlinchan.

Ilancueitl rejected his rule and attacked him in 1344, and Culhuacan became the Mexica's first tributary town. In 1347 the Mexica leader Tenoch replaced him with Nauhyotl Teuctli, or Nauhyotzin III.

zh:
阿奇托梅卡特·特奥梅卡尔二世于1336至1347年任库尔瓦坎的特拉托阿尼。据《夸乌蒂特兰编年史》记载，1336年他杀害在位君主、旧奇奇梅克王朝末代领主韦韦·阿卡马皮奇特利，随即自立为王；遗孀伊兰奎特尔与阿卡马皮奇特利逃往科瓦特林钱。

伊兰奎特尔不承认他的统治，于1344年出兵攻打，库尔瓦坎由此成为墨西哥人第一个纳贡属邦。1347年，墨西哥人首领特诺奇以纳乌约特尔·特乌克特利（即纳乌约钦三世）取代他。

en:
Coxcoxtli was tlatoani of Culhuacan from 1281 to 1307, the sixteenth lord of the Colhua. The Codex Boturini depicts him seated on his throne in 2-reed, 1299, after the Culhua and their Nahua allies drove the Mexica from Chapultepec: the captured Mexica leader Huehue Huitzilihuitl and his daughter were brought before him and sacrificed when he refused mercy.

In 1301 he settled the subjected Mexica at Tizaapan and later sent them against the Xochimilca, from whom they returned victorious. His son Huehue Acamapichtli and daughter Atotoztli I were ancestors of Acamapichtli, the first tlatoani of Tenochtitlan.

zh:
科什科什特利是库尔瓦坎的特拉托阿尼，据奇马尔帕因记载于1281至1307年在位，是科尔瓦人的第十六代首领。《博图里尼古抄本》描绘了1299年（2-芦苇年）他端坐王位的情景：此前库尔瓦人与纳瓦诸城邦结盟，将墨西哥人逐出查普尔特佩克，被俘的墨西哥人首领韦韦·维特西利维特尔及其女儿被押到他面前，他拒绝施恩，下令将二人献祭。

1301年（4-房屋年），他把臣服的墨西哥人安置在蒂萨潘，后来又征调他们攻打索奇米尔卡人，墨西哥人得胜而归。其子韦韦·阿卡马皮奇特利与女儿阿托托斯特利一世都是特诺奇蒂特兰第一代特拉托阿尼阿卡马皮奇特利的祖辈。

en:
Huehue Acamapichtli (Nahuatl for Acamapichtli the Elder, c. 1300–1336) was tlatoani, or king, of Culhuacan and the last ruler of its Chichimeca dynasty, succeeding his father Coxcoxtli.

The Anales de Cuauhtitlan place his enthronement in 1324, and his relative Acamapichtli later became the first tlatoani of Tenochtitlan. In 1336 he was killed by Achitomecatl, who at once seized the throne of Culhuacan, whereupon the young Acamapichtli fled with Ilancueitl to Cohuatlinchan.

en:
Risdeard O'Reilly (Risderd Ó Raghallaigh) was king of East Breifne, the O'Reilly kingdom in what is now County Cavan, from about 1328 until his death around 1349. He was the second son of Giolla Iosa Ruaidh, who had established the O'Reilly seat at Cavan.

When Risdeard's elder brother Maelseachleann died in 1328, after briefly being counted as king, Risdeard took the kingship. His long reign brought decades of stable O'Reilly succession, and when he died his brother Cu Chonnacht succeeded him.

里斯德阿德·奥赖利是东布雷夫讷的国王；东布雷夫讷是奥赖利家族的王国，位于今卡文郡一带，他约1328年继位，约1349年去世。他是吉奥拉·伊萨·鲁艾什的次子，其父把奥赖利家族的驻地设在卡文。

兄长梅尔谢赫莱恩于1328年去世，此前曾短暂被认作国王，里斯德阿德随后继位。他在位长久，奥赖利家族的继承在此后数十年保持稳定；他死后，兄弟库·乔赫纳赫特继位。

en:
Sir Edmond de Burgh (1298–1338), also called Edmond of Clanwilliam, was an Anglo-Irish knight and a son of Richard Óg de Burgh, second Earl of Ulster, and Margery de Burgh. He married Sláine O'Brien and was ancestor of the Burkes of Clanwilliam.

In 1338, while visiting the Augustinian friars at Ballinrobe, he was seized at the friary by his cousin Edmond Albanach Burke and his men, carried to Earls Island, and drowned in Lough Mask with a stone fastened to his neck.

埃德蒙·德·伯格爵士（1298—1338），又称克兰威廉的埃德蒙，是盎格鲁—爱尔兰骑士，第二代阿尔斯特伯爵理查德·奥格·德·伯格与妻子马杰里之子。他娶斯兰妮·奥布赖恩为妻，是克兰威廉伯克家族的始祖。

1338年，他前往巴林罗布拜访奥斯定会修士时，堂兄弟埃德蒙·阿尔巴纳赫·伯克率人闯入修道院将他擒获，押到伯爵岛，在他脖子上拴了一块石头，把他溺死在马斯克湖中。

en:
Ming Yuzhen (1328–1366) was a Red Turban rebel who founded the Xia state in Sichuan during the Yuan collapse. He joined Xu Shouhui's Tianwan Red Turban army around 1352.

In 1357 he led troops into Sichuan through the Wu Gorges, seized Chongqing, and subdued Yuan forces across Sichuan. After Chen Youliang killed Xu in 1360, Ming refused allegiance, took the title King of Longshu in 1361, and in 1363 enthroned himself in Chongqing as emperor of Great Xia. On his death in 1366 his son Ming Sheng succeeded; Xia fell to the Ming in 1371.

zh:
明玉珍（1328—1366）是元末红巾军将领，在四川建立大夏政权。1352年前后他加入徐寿辉的天完红巾军。

1357年，他率军经巫峡入蜀，攻占重庆，又平定川内元军。1360年陈友谅杀害徐寿辉后，他拒不归附，1361年自称陇蜀王，1363年在重庆称帝，国号大夏。他于1366年病逝，子明昇继位，大夏于1371年被明朝攻灭。

en:
Alice of Ibelin (1304/1306–after 1386) was the only child of Guy of Ibelin, Lord of Nicosia, and Isabella of Ibelin, orphaned before she was eleven. In 1318 she married Hugh of Lusignan.

When Hugh became King Hugh IV in 1324, she was crowned queen in Nicosia's Saint Sophia Cathedral. Two of her sons, Peter I and James I, later wore the Cypriot crown. After Hugh's death she married Philip of Brunswick-Grubenhagen in 1368, only to be widowed again in 1369.

伊贝林的爱丽丝（1304/1306—1386年后）是尼科西亚领主居伊·德·伊贝林与伊贝林的伊莎贝尔唯一的孩子，十一岁前便父母双亡。1318年，她嫁给吕西尼昂的于格。

1324年于格成为于格四世，她在尼科西亚的圣索菲亚大教堂加冕为王后。她的两个儿子彼得一世与雅克一世后来相继成为塞浦路斯国王。于格死后，她于1368年改嫁不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根的菲利普，1369年即再度守寡。

en:
Amalric of Lusignan (c. 1272–1310), Lord of Tyre, was a younger son of King Hugh III of Cyprus. He fought at the fall of Tripoli in 1289 and commanded the Accursed Tower at Acre in 1291, escaping.

In 1300 he sought to coordinate an attack on the Mamluks with Ghazan's Mongols and occupied Ruad, but the Mongols never arrived. In 1306, backed by the Templars and barons, he deposed his epileptic brother Henry II and governed Cyprus as regent.

A rising for Henry failed in 1308, and in 1310 Amalric exiled him to Armenia. He was murdered at Nicosia the same year, after which Henry regained the throne.

吕西尼昂的阿马尔里克（约1272—1310）是塞浦路斯国王于格三世较年幼的儿子，受封提尔领主。他参加了1289年的的黎波里陷落之战，1291年在阿卡指挥“诅咒之塔”，城破时逃出。

1300年，他试图与合赞的蒙古军协同进攻马穆鲁克，占据鲁阿德岛，但蒙古军未到。1306年，他在圣殿骑士团和贵族支持下废黜患有癫痫的兄长亨利二世，以摄政身份统治塞浦路斯。

1308年一场拥护亨利的起事失败，1310年阿马尔里克将亨利流放亚美尼亚。同年他在尼科西亚遇刺，亨利随后复位。

en:
Balian of Ibelin (1240–1302) was seneschal of the Kingdom of Cyprus. A son of Guy of Ibelin, constable of Cyprus, and Philippa Berlais, he married Alice of Lampron, of the Armenian Hetumid dynasty and a granddaughter of Raymond-Roupen. Their son Guy, born in 1286, became lord of Nicosia.

Of their daughters, Maria married Rupen of Montfort in 1299, Isabelle married John, titular lord of Arsuf, and Margaret married Oshin of Korikos. Balian died in 1302.

伊贝林的巴利安（1240—1302）任塞浦路斯王国宫廷长。他是塞浦路斯统帅伊贝林的居伊与菲利帕·贝尔莱之子，娶出身亚美尼亚赫图米德王朝兰普龙家族的爱丽丝为妻，她是雷蒙-鲁本的外孙女。两人的儿子居伊生于1286年，后成为尼科西亚领主。

en:
Baldwin of Ibelin (c. 1211–1267) was the fourth son of John of Ibelin, the Old Lord of Beirut, and Melisende of Arsuf. At the Battle of Agridi in 1232 he commanded the third division.

In 1246 he became seneschal of Cyprus, and in 1250 he was taken prisoner at Mansurah in Egypt on Louis IX of France’s crusade. His sons included Philip, later constable of Cyprus, and Hugh, regent of Cyprus in 1306. Baldwin died in 1267.

Eschiva of Ibelin (1253–1312), daughter of John II of Beirut and Alice de la Roche, inherited the lordship of Beirut when her sister Isabella died in 1282, though after the Mamluk conquest of 1291 she held it in name only.

In 1274 she married Humphrey de Montfort, lord of Tyre, who died in 1284. In 1291 she married Guy of Lusignan, constable of Cyprus; their son became King Hugh IV. She died in 1312.

en:
Eschive de Lusignan (died 1363) was the eldest daughter of King Hugh IV of Cyprus and his second wife Alice of Ibelin. She married Ferdinand of Majorca, Viscount of Omélas. After a violent quarrel Hugh IV expelled Ferdinand from Cyprus and held Eschive captive at court, accusing Ferdinand's mother Isabella of Ibelin of sorcery.

Eschive was still captive when her only child, Alice, was born in 1341; Ferdinand died in exile at Omélas before 1347. Eschive died during an outbreak of plague in 1363.

en:
Guy of Lusignan (1316–1343) was the eldest son of King Hugh IV of Cyprus and his first wife Maria of Ibelin. Around 1320 he inherited the titular principality of Galilee from his mother's family, and in 1324 his father took the Cypriot crown. In 1330 he married Maria of Bourbon in Nicosia's Saint Sophia Cathedral.

Appointed constable of Cyprus in 1338, he died in the summer of 1343, leaving one son, Hugh, later titular prince of Galilee and prince of Achaea.
