en:
Guy of Lusignan (c. 1150–1194), a Poitevin knight and youngest son of Hugh VIII, married Sibylla, sister of Jerusalem's King Baldwin IV, in 1180. Baldwin made him regent in 1183 but resumed power that year; in 1186 Sibylla became queen and crowned Guy beside her.

At Hattin in 1187 his army was destroyed and Saladin captured him; Jerusalem fell three months later. Released in 1188, he began the siege of Acre in 1189. Deprived of the Jerusalem crown in 1192, he received Cyprus from Richard I of England and ruled until his death in 1194, succeeded by his brother Aimery.

zh:
吕西尼昂的居伊（约1150—1194）是普瓦图骑士、于格八世的幼子，于1180年娶耶路撒冷国王鲍德温四世之姐西比拉为妻。鲍德温于1183年任命他为摄政，同年又收回权力；1186年西比拉成为女王，让居伊与她一同加冕为王。

1187年他在哈丁战役中惨败，本人被萨拉丁俘虏，三个月后耶路撒冷陷落。1188年获释后，他于1189年发起阿卡围城战。1192年他失去耶路撒冷王位，英格兰国王理查一世将塞浦路斯补偿给他；他统治该岛至1194年去世，由其兄艾默里继位。

en:
Guy of Ibelin (1215/1218 – after 1255) was the fifth son of John of Ibelin and Melisende of Arsuf. He served King Henry I as marshal and then constable of Cyprus.

With his brother Baldwin he led Cypriot knights at the 1249 siege of Damietta on Louis IX’s crusade; Joinville called him one of the finest knights of his age and recounted their capture alongside him.

He married Philippa Barlais; their daughter Isabella married King Hugh III, while their sons Balian and Philip each became seneschal of Cyprus. He founded the Ibelins’ Cypriot branch and died after May 1255.

zh:
伊贝林的居伊（1215/1218—1255年后）是约翰·德·伊贝林与阿尔苏夫的梅利桑德的第五子。他在国王亨利一世麾下历任塞浦路斯马政官与统帅。

1249年，他与兄长鲍德温率领塞浦路斯骑士参加路易九世十字军的达米埃塔围城战；编年史家茹安维尔称他是当时最出色的骑士之一，并记载了他们与自己一同被俘的经历。

他娶巴莱的菲利帕为妻，女儿伊莎贝拉嫁给于格三世国王，儿子巴利安和腓力则先后出任塞浦路斯宫廷总管。他开创了伊贝林家族的塞浦路斯支系，于1255年5月之后去世。

en:
Guy of Ibelin (1286–1308) was lord of Nicosia in Cyprus. The son of Seneschal Balian of Ibelin and Alice of Lampron, he obtained a papal dispensation in 1303 to marry his cousin Isabella, daughter of Baldwin of Ibelin.

Their daughter Alix became the second wife of King Hugh IV of Cyprus, while another daughter, Margaret, married Guy of Ibelin. Guy died in 1308 and was buried at Bellapais Abbey near Kyrenia.

en:
Guy of Ibelin (1250–1304) became count of Jaffa and Ascalon after his brother James died in 1276, though Baibars had conquered Jaffa in 1268, leaving him count in name only. In 1299 he seized Byblos, and in 1301 he met a Mongol commander to plan against the Mamluks.

Pirates captured Guy at Episcopia in Cyprus in 1302. He died in 1304 and was buried, at his own wish, in a pauper's grave in Nicosia.

Guy of Poitiers-Lusignan (1275–1303) was the youngest son of King Hugh III of Cyprus and Isabella of Ibelin. He held the office of constable of Cyprus from 1291 and married Eschiva of Ibelin, lady of Beirut.

In 1303 he joined a conspiracy against his brother King Henry II; the plot was uncovered and Guy was executed that same year. His son by Eschiva later inherited the crown as Hugh IV in 1324.

en:
Henry I of Cyprus, called the Fat (1217–1253), succeeded his father Hugh I as king in 1218 as an infant. During his minority his mother Alice of Champagne was regent and the Ibelin lords held power.

Emperor Frederick II also claimed the right to govern Cyprus, leading to war with the Ibelins, whose 1232 victory at Agridi secured his throne; he came of age that year.

In 1246 he became regent of Jerusalem for King Conrad II. He joined Louis IX's Seventh Crusade in 1248 but soon returned to Cyprus, dying in 1253; his infant son Hugh II succeeded him.

en:
Henry II (1270–1324) was a son of Hugh III and succeeded his brother John I as king of Cyprus in 1285. That year he retook Acre from the Angevins and in 1286 was crowned king of Jerusalem at Tyre, the last such coronation.

During the Mamluk siege of Acre in 1291 he fled to Cyprus; the city fell, ending the mainland kingdom. He later sought Mongol ruler Ghazan's cooperation and twice asked the pope for a new crusade.

In Cyprus he had the High Court keep written records. Epileptic, he was deposed in 1306 by his brother Amalric and exiled to Armenia, returning in 1310 after Amalric's murder. Childless, he was succeeded by his nephew Hugh IV.

亨利二世（1270—1324）是于格三世之子，1285年继兄长约翰一世之后成为塞浦路斯国王。同年他从安茹家族手中收复阿卡，并于1286年在提尔加冕为耶路撒冷国王，这是最后一次该加冕礼。

1291年马穆鲁克围攻阿卡时，他逃回塞浦路斯；城池陷落，大陆王国就此终结。他后来寻求蒙古统治者合赞的配合，并两次请求教皇发动新的十字军。

在塞浦路斯，他命高等法院保存书面记录。他患有癫痫，1306年被弟弟阿马尔里克废黜并流放亚美尼亚，1310年阿马尔里克遇刺后回国复位。他没有子嗣，由侄子于格四世继位。

en:
Hugh I of Cyprus (1195–1218) succeeded his father Aimery as king in 1205 aged nine; his brother-in-law Walter of Montbéliard governed as regent. He married Alice of Champagne and took personal power in 1210.

Hugh fell out with Walter, who fled to Jerusalem, and reversed his policies, making peace with the Seljuqs of Rum and backing the Armenians in the War of the Antiochene Succession.

Hugh joined the Fifth Crusade in 1217 but fell ill and died at Tripoli on 10 January 1218, leaving the crown to his infant son Henry I under Alice's regency.

zh:
塞浦路斯的于格一世（1195—1218）于1205年九岁时继承父亲艾默里的王位，由姐夫蒙贝利亚尔的沃尔特摄政。他娶香槟的阿丽丝为妻，1210年亲政。

于格与沃尔特失和，后者逃往耶路撒冷；于格改变了他的政策，与罗姆塞尔柱人讲和，并在安条克继承战争中支持亚美尼亚人。

1217年末于格加入第五次十字军东征，却染病于1218年1月10日在的黎波里去世，王位传给幼子亨利一世，由阿丽丝摄政。

en:
Hugh II (c. 1252–1267) became king of Cyprus as an infant when his father Henry I died, his mother Plaisance of Antioch governing as regent. In 1258 the barons recognized him as heir presumptive to Conrad III of Jerusalem, and after Plaisance's death in 1261 his cousin Hugh of Antioch became regent.

A marriage to Isabella of Ibelin was arranged in 1265, but Hugh died before reaching his majority in 1267, ending the first Lusignan line; Hugh of Antioch succeeded him.

于格二世（约1252—1267）在父亲亨利一世去世时还是襁褓中的婴儿，就此成为塞浦路斯国王，由母亲安条克的普莱桑斯摄政。1258年，贵族们承认他为耶路撒冷的康拉丁的推定继承人；1261年普莱桑斯去世后，表兄安条克的于格接任摄政。

en:
Hugh III (c. 1235–1284) was the son of Henry of Antioch and Isabella of Lusignan. He governed Cyprus as regent for the young Hugh II and succeeded him in 1267.

After Conrad III was executed in 1268, Hugh claimed Jerusalem too. He tried to rebuild royal authority and check the Mamluks. Marriage alliances secured Ibelin loyalty, but the Templars and Venetian merchants opposed him.

His aunt Maria of Antioch sold her claim to Charles I of Anjou, who seized Acre in 1277. Hugh twice failed to recover the city and died at Tyre in 1284, succeeded by his son John I.

于格三世（约1235—1284）是安条克的亨利与吕西尼昂的伊莎贝拉之子。他先以摄政身份代年轻的于格二世治理塞浦路斯，并于1267年继位。

1268年康拉丁被处死后，他又取得耶路撒冷王位。他力图重振王权、遏制马穆鲁克；联姻为他赢得伊贝林家族的忠诚，但圣殿骑士团和威尼斯商人反对他。

姨母安条克的玛丽把继承权卖给安茹的查理，后者于1277年攻占阿卡。于格两次收复阿卡未果，于1284年死于提尔，其子约翰一世继位。

en:
Hugh IV (1293/1296–1359) was the son of Constable Guy of Cyprus and Eschiva of Ibelin. He succeeded his father as constable in 1318, and in March 1324 inherited the Cypriot throne from his uncle Henry II; he also claimed the title of king of Jerusalem.

He seems to have been content with Cyprus and prevented his son Peter from going to western Europe to seek help to reconquer Jerusalem. In 1344 he joined the Venetians and Hospitallers in capturing Smyrna. Cyprus reached its peak of power and prosperity under him.

When his eldest son Guy died leaving a son, Hugh passed over his grandson and in November 1358 had his second son Peter crowned, the first Cypriot king to crown his successor in his lifetime. He died in 1359.

zh:
于格四世（1293/1296—1359）是塞浦路斯统帅居伊与伊贝林的埃希芙之子。1318年他继任统帅，1324年3月又从叔父亨利二世手中继承塞浦路斯王位，同时自称耶路撒冷国王。

他似乎满足于守住塞浦路斯，阻止儿子彼得前往西欧寻求援助、收复耶路撒冷。1344年，他与威尼斯人和医院骑士团联手夺取士麦那。塞浦路斯的国力与富庶在他治下达到顶峰。

长子居伊死后留下一子，于格越过孙子，于1358年11月为次子彼得加冕，成为第一位生前为继承人加冕的塞浦路斯国王。他于1359年去世。

en:
Hugh of Lusignan (c. 1335–1385?) was the only son of Guy of Lusignan and Marie of Bourbon. When Guy died in 1343, Hugh became his grandfather Hugh IV's designated heir to the throne of Cyprus. His mother, estranged from the king, wanted to take him west, and after papal pressure they left in 1347.

In 1358 the old king crowned his younger son Peter instead. Hugh appealed to the pope and served as senator of Rome in 1361. In 1362 Peter I bought his renunciation with a pension of 50,000 bezants, making him the richest lord after the king.

Hugh fought at Alexandria in 1365, where Peter named him prince of Galilee; after campaigning in Achaea, he and his mother ceded their claim to Philip of Taranto in 1370. He died childless in Cyprus.

于格·德吕西尼昂（约1335—约1385）是居伊·德·吕西尼昂与波旁的玛丽的独子。1343年居伊去世后，于格成为祖父于格四世指定的塞浦路斯王位继承人。他的母亲与国王交恶，想带他回西方，经教皇施压，母子于1347年离岛。

1358年，老国王却为自己较年幼的儿子彼得加冕。于格向教皇申诉，1361年任罗马元老。1362年，彼得一世以50,000拜占特的年金换取他放弃权利，使他成为仅次于国王的富有领主。

1365年于格参加亚历山大之役，彼得封他为加利利亲王；他在亚该亚作战多年后，于1370年与母亲把当地的权利让予塔兰托的腓力。他死于塞浦路斯，没有子嗣。

en:
Isabella of Ibelin (1241–1324) was queen of Cyprus and Jerusalem by marriage to Hugh III. The daughter of Guy d'Ibelin, constable of Cyprus, she wed Hugh of Antioch in 1255; her kinsmen helped him succeed the childless Hugh II in 1267.

Widowed in 1284, she saw her sons John I and Henry II crowned. When Amalric deposed Henry in 1306, she and her brother Philip backed the king; after Amalric's murder in 1310 she secured Henry's restoration.

en:
Isabella of Cyprus (before 1216–1264), daughter of King Hugh I of Cyprus and Alice of Champagne, in 1233 married Henry of Antioch, son of Prince Bohemond IV; their son Hugh later ruled Cyprus and Jerusalem as Hugh III.

While her nephew Hugh II was king, she was Cyprus's heir presumptive but yielded the regency to her son. In 1263 she claimed the regency of Jerusalem, but its High Court granted her limited powers. She returned to Cyprus in 1264, died later that year and was buried in Nicosia.

en:
James I of Lusignan (1334–1398) was a younger son of King Hugh IV of Cyprus and Alice of Ibelin. When the Genoese invaded Cyprus in 1373 he successfully defended Kyrenia; the next year he left the island under a treaty and was captured at Rhodes and taken to Genoa, where his son Janus was born.

Chosen king after his nephew Peter II died in 1382, he accepted Genoese release terms in 1383, but opposition in Cyprus sent him back into captivity.

He returned and was crowned at Nicosia in 1385, later adding the titles of King of Jerusalem and King of Armenia. He died at Nicosia in 1398 and Janus succeeded him.

John of Lusignan (1329–1375), a son of King Hugh IV of Cyprus and Alice of Ibelin, married Constance of Sicily in 1343 and Alice of Ibelin in 1350. He became titular Prince of Antioch in 1345 and later served as constable and regent of Cyprus.

In 1369 he led the Cypriot fleet against Mamluk ports, sacking Botron and Tartus and raiding as far as Alexandria. Implicated in the murder of his brother King Peter I, he was killed in Nicosia in 1375 at the urging of Queen Eleanor and the Genoese.

John I (c. 1268–1285) was the eldest surviving son of King Hugh III of Cyprus and Isabella of Ibelin. When his father died in 1284 he succeeded to the crowns of Cyprus and Jerusalem and was crowned in Nicosia, aged about seventeen.

On the mainland only Tyre and Beirut recognized him; Acre still favored Charles I of Anjou. John died in 1285, barely a year after his coronation, and his younger brother Henry II succeeded him.

en:
John of Ibelin (1215–1266), count of Jaffa and Ascalon, was the son of Philip of Ibelin, bailli of Cyprus, and Alice of Montbéliard. He fled Cyprus in 1229 after Frederick II seized the Ibelin fiefs, and fought at Casal Imbert in 1232.

Around 1240 he married Maria of Barbaron, sister of Armenia's King Hethum I, and helped take Tyre in 1242. He became count of Jaffa in 1246, joined Louis IX’s crusade at the taking of Damietta in 1249, and as bailli of Jerusalem repulsed an Egyptian attack on Jaffa.

In the War of Saint Sabas he backed Venice. He wrote the Livre des assises de Jérusalem, the crusader kingdom’s longest surviving legal treatise, and died in 1266.

圣萨巴斯战争中他支持威尼斯。他撰写的《耶路撒冷法令集》是这个十字军王国留存最长的法学著作，于1266年去世。

吕西尼昂的玛丽（1215—1251）是塞浦路斯国王于格一世与香槟的阿丽丝的长女，也是耶路撒冷女王伊莎贝拉一世的外孙女。1229年，她与布列塔尼公爵皮埃尔一世的婚约被取消；1233年她嫁给布里耶纳伯爵戈蒂埃四世。

1244年10月，戈蒂埃在拉佛比战败被俘，在开罗遇害，遗下儿子约翰和于格。玛丽此后长居塞浦路斯宫廷，于1251年去世。

en:
Philip of Ibelin (1253–1318) was seneschal of the Kingdom of Cyprus from 1302 and also held the seneschalcy of Jerusalem. A son of Constable Guy of Ibelin and Philippa Barlais, he married Maria of Hamousse; the marriage was childless, and around 1295 he married Maria Embriaco, lady of Gibelet.

His son Guy by the second marriage succeeded him as seneschal, his daughter Isabella married Ferdinand of Majorca in 1315, and his daughter Helvis married Henry II of Brunswick-Grubenhagen in 1330. He died at Nicosia on 25 November 1318.

Philip of Ibelin (c. 1233–1304) was constable of the crusader Kingdom of Cyprus. The son of Baldwin of Ibelin, the kingdom's seneschal, and Alice of Bethsan, he married around 1253 Simone of Montbéliard, whose mother held the principality of Galilee.

Their son Balian bore the titular title prince of Galilee until his death in 1315, and their daughter Maria married Guy of Ibelin, count of Jaffa. Philip died in 1304.

en:
Philip of Ibelin (1180–1227) was a son of Balian of Ibelin and Maria Komnene, widow of King Amalric. In 1206 he escorted his niece Alice to Cyprus to marry King Hugh I, settling on the island with his brother John of Beirut before 1217.

When Hugh I died in 1218, Philip became regent for the infant Henry I and built Ibelin power on the island. By his wife Alice of Montbéliard he fathered John, the future count of Jaffa, and died in 1227.

en:
Peter I (1328–1369) was king of Cyprus and spent his reign trying to raise a crusade for Jerusalem. The son of Hugh IV and Alice of Ibelin, he was made titular count of Tripoli in 1346 and, after his elder brother Guy died, was crowned in 1358 in his father’s lifetime.

He was crowned titular king of Jerusalem in 1360 and in 1361 took Attaleia from the Turks. In 1363 he went to Avignon and persuaded the leaders of a new crusade to aim at Alexandria. His fleet of 165 ships took the city in 1365 and plundered it for a week before withdrawing.

His quarrels with the nobles ended on 17 January 1369, when three knights killed him at Nicosia. His son Peter II succeeded him.

彼得一世（1328—1369）是塞浦路斯国王，在位期间一直奔走筹划夺回耶路撒冷的十字军。他是于格四世与伊贝林的爱丽丝之子，1346年受封名义上的的黎波里伯爵；兄长居伊去世后，他于1358年在父亲生前加冕。

1360年，他加冕为名义上的耶路撒冷国王，1361年从突厥人手中夺取安塔利亚。1363年他前往阿维尼翁，说服新十字军的首脑把目标定在亚历山大。1365年，他的165艘战船攻占该城，洗劫一周后撤军。

他与贵族积怨甚深，1369年1月17日，三名骑士在尼科西亚将他杀害。其子彼得二世继位。

Bolesław II (c. 1253–1313), younger son of Siemowit I of Masovia, ruled Masovia with his brother Konrad II after 1262 and received Płock in 1275. In 1279 he married Sophia.

After Leszek II the Black died in 1288 he seized Kraków and Sandomierz and claimed the senioral throne, but withdrew after the Battle of Siewierz in 1289. On Konrad II's death in 1294 he reunited all Masovia, later promoted Warsaw, and in 1310 enfeoffed his sons with Warsaw and Czersk.

en:
Casimir I of Warsaw (1329/1331 – November/December 1355) was a Piast prince, traditionally the youngest son of Trojden I of Czersk and Maria of Galicia. After Trojden's death in 1341 he ruled Czersk jointly with his brother Siemowit III, and the brothers inherited Rawa in 1345.

In 1349 Casimir received Warsaw as his own duchy, and in 1351 he gained Sochaczew and did homage to Casimir III of Poland. He died unmarried in 1355 and was buried in Płock Cathedral, whereupon Warsaw reverted to the Polish crown.

加利奇的玛丽亚（1293年前—1341年1月11日）是留里克王朝公主，加利奇-沃伦国王尤里一世与库亚维的尤菲米娅之女。1310年之前，她嫁给马佐夫舍公爵特洛杰登一世，传统记载两人生有尤里二世·波列斯瓦夫、尤菲米娅、谢莫维特三世和华沙的卡齐米日一世四个子女。

1323年她的兄弟安德烈和列夫二世战死，她与侄女尤菲米娅继承了他们的权利，后来她辅佐儿子尤里二世·波列斯瓦夫统治加利奇。她于1341年1月去世，比丈夫早两个月。

en:
Siemowit I (c. 1215–1262) was a Piast prince, a son of Konrad I of Masovia. He inherited Masovia from his brother Bolesław I in 1248. To counter Baltic raiders he allied with Daniel of Halych, married his daughter, joined campaigns against the Yotvingians and backed the Teutonic Order.

In 1262 Lithuania and Rus' invaded under Mindaugas. On 23 June 1262 the fortress of Jazdów fell through betrayal and Siemowit was killed, while his son Konrad II was taken captive.

谢莫维特一世（约1215—1262）是皮亚斯特王朝王公，马佐夫舍的康拉德一世之子，1248年继承兄长波列斯瓦夫一世的马佐夫舍。为抵御波罗的海部族袭扰，他与加利奇的达尼洛夫结盟并娶其女，参加征讨约特温吉亚人的战事，同时支持条顿骑士团。

en:
Siemowit III (c. 1320 – 16 June 1381) was a Piast duke of Masovia, the second son of Trojden I and Maria of Galicia. In 1341 he and his brother Casimir inherited Czersk, adding Rawa in 1345; in 1349 he kept Czersk, Liw and Rawa while Casimir took Warsaw.

In 1351 the brothers recognized Casimir III of Poland as suzerain, and in 1355 the king granted him Warsaw. When Casimir III died in 1370, Masovia regained its independence; Siemowit issued a customary law code in 1377 and reformed its coinage. He died in 1381.

Trojden I (1284/1286 – 13 March 1341) was a Piast duke who ruled Czersk from 1310 and, after his father Bolesław II of Płock died in 1313, Warsaw and Liw as well, giving him all of eastern Masovia. Around 1310 he married Maria, daughter of Yuri I of Halych-Volhynia.

When the Rurikid line ended in 1323, he placed his son Bolesław on the Ruthenian throne as Yuri II. He maneuvered between Poland and the Teutonic Order, joining the Order in 1326, and in 1340 sold his Ruthenian claim to Casimir III after Yuri II was poisoned.

Anh Tư, posthumously honoured as Consort Dowager Minh Từ (died 1365), was a consort of Emperor Trần Minh Tông and the mother of two emperors. Born of the Lê clan, she was titled Anh Tư Nguyên phi.

She bore two sons: Trần Vượng in 1319, who took the throne in 1329 as Hiến Tông, and Trần Phủ in 1321, the future Nghệ Tông. When Hiến Tông died in 1341, Minh Tông instead enthroned his empress Hiến Từ's son, Dụ Tông.

She was the aunt of Hồ Quý Ly and died in 1365; after Nghệ Tông took the throne in 1370, he honoured her posthumously in 1371.

en:
Trần Thái Tông (Trần Cảnh; 1218–1277) was the founding emperor of the Trần dynasty. In 1226 his uncle Trần Thủ Độ arranged his marriage to the last Lý ruler, Lý Chiêu Hoàng, who abdicated to him.

In 1257 Mongol envoys demanded passage through Đại Việt; after they were imprisoned, Uriyangkhadai invaded. The emperor led his army from an elephant but was defeated. Uriyangkhadai forced the court to abandon Thăng Long and held the capital nine days before withdrawing, after which Thái Tông agreed to tribute.

A learned Buddhist, he authored the Khóa Hư Lục. He abdicated in 1258 for his son Trần Hoảng and died as retired emperor.

陈太宗，名陈煚（1218—1277），是越南陈朝的开国皇帝。1226年，叔父陈守度安排他迎娶李朝末代君主李昭皇，李昭皇随即禅位，陈朝由此建立。

1257年蒙古使者要求借道大越，使者被囚后，兀良合台率军入侵。陈煚骑象领兵却遭战败，蒙古军队迫使朝廷撤离升龙，占领都城九天后撤兵，陈煚此后同意纳贡。

他精通佛学，著有《课虚录》。1258年他禅位给儿子陈晃，以太上皇身份去世。

en:
Trần Dụ Tông (Trần Hạo, 1336–1369) was the seventh Trần emperor of Đại Việt, reigning from 1341 to 1369. A son of Trần Minh Tông, he was only five when chosen after his brother Hiến Tông died without an heir, and his father ruled as retired emperor until 1357.

Once he governed himself, Dụ Tông was keen on affairs of state but fonder of pleasure: he built palaces, gambled and kept exotic birds and beasts.

He died without a son in 1369, and his will named as successor Trần Nhật Lễ, adopted son of his late brother Prince Cung Túc. When Nhật Lễ tried to take the surname Dương, he was overthrown by Minh Tông’s third son, Trần Phủ.

en:
Empress Hiến Từ (1299–1369), also called the Lệ Thánh empress, was the chief consort of Trần Minh Tông and mother of Emperor Trần Dụ Tông. At court she was known for kindness and tact, and was praised as ‘a Yao and Shun among women’.

Made empress in 1323, she became empress dowager in 1342 and bore two princes, Trần Nguyên Dục and Trần Hạo. After Minh Tông died in 1357, she followed his wish and withdrew from court.

After Dụ Tông died in 1369, she supported the accession of his adopted heir Dương Nhật Lễ. When she came to regret it, Nhật Lễ had her poisoned.

en:
Hồ Quý Ly (1336–?) was a Trần-dynasty official and general from Thanh Hóa who founded Vietnam's short-lived Hồ dynasty. He rose through royal marriages and command in the wars against Champa, becoming chief minister in 1387.

In 1388, after a court plot against him was exposed, he persuaded the senior king to depose Trần Phế Đế. His reforms reshaped the examinations and currency.

In 1400 he deposed the last Trần ruler and took the throne, then abdicated to his son Hồ Hán Thương in 1401. The Ming invasion of 1406–1407 overthrew him; he was captured and exiled to China.

胡季犛（1336—？）是越南陈朝的大臣与将领，清化人，后建立短命的胡朝。他凭借与王室联姻和对占城战争中的军功崛起，1387年受命辅政。

1388年，朝中谋除他的计划泄露后，他说服上皇废黜陈废帝。他还推行改革，改订科举、发行纸币。

1400年他废黜陈朝末帝自立，1401年传位于儿子胡汉苍。1406—1407年明朝出兵攻灭胡朝，他被俘后押送中国。

en:
Trần Thánh Tông (Trần Hoảng; 1240–1290) was the second emperor of the Trần dynasty, ruling Đại Việt from 1258 to 1278. As crown prince he witnessed the Mongol invasion of 1257, after which his father Thái Tông enthroned him and governed as retired emperor until 1277.

He abdicated in 1278 for his son Trần Khâm (Nhân Tông), and as retired emperor the two were supreme commanders against the two Yuan invasions.

After defeats in 1285 they won at Hàm Tử and Chương Dương and retook Thăng Long, and in 1288 the Yuan fleet was destroyed at Bạch Đằng. He died in 1290.

陈圣宗，名陈晃（1240—1290），陈朝第二位皇帝，1258年至1278年统治大越。1257年蒙古入侵时他还是太子，战后父亲太宗将皇位传给他，并以太上皇身份共同治理，直至1277年。

1278年，圣宗禅位给儿子陈昑（仁宗），成为太上皇后与儿子同为最高统帅，抵御后来的两次元朝入侵。

1285年越军先败后胜，在咸子关和章阳获胜、收复升龙；1288年元朝水师在白藤江覆灭。他于1290年去世。

en:
Trần Nhân Tông (Trần Khâm; 1258–1308), the third Trần emperor, ruled Đại Việt from 1278 to 1293. As the Yuan threat grew, he and retired emperor Thánh Tông gathered the court in 1282 to discuss war and appointed Trần Quốc Tuấn commander-in-chief in 1283.

They led resistance to the Yuan invasions: after defeats in 1285, their forces won at Hàm Tử and Chương Dương and retook Thăng Long, and in 1288 Trần Quốc Tuấn destroyed the Yuan fleet at Bạch Đằng.

After abdicating to his son Trần Thuyên in 1293 he became a monk in 1295 and founded the Trúc Lâm school. In 1306 his daughter Huyền Trân married the Champa king for two provinces.

陈仁宗（陈昑；1258—1308）是陈朝第三位皇帝，1278年至1293年统治大越。元朝威胁日增，他与太上皇圣宗于1282年召集朝臣议战，1283年任命陈国峻为统帅。

他们一同指挥抗元战争：1285年越军先败后胜，在咸子关和章阳获胜、重返升龙；1288年陈国峻在白藤江歼灭元朝水师。

1293年他禅位给儿子陈烇，1295年出家，创立竹林禅派。1306年，他将女儿玄珍公主嫁给占城国王，换得两处州郡。

en:
Lê Văn Hưu (1230–1322) was a Trần-dynasty official and historian from Thanh Hóa. Placing second in the 1247 civil service examination, he rose to minister of war and head of the national history office.

In 1272 he presented the Đại Việt sử ký, a history modeled on the Spring and Autumn Annals and Vietnam's first official history. Though lost, its text survives in Ngô Sĩ Liên's Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư and later works.

黎文休（1230—1322）是越南陈朝官员、史学家，清化人。1247年科举及第高中榜眼，后官至兵部尚书、国史院监修。

en:
Trần Minh Tông (Trần Mạnh, 1300–1357) was the fifth Trần emperor of Đại Việt, reigning at the dynasty's height. The fourth son of Trần Anh Tông, he was named crown prince in 1305 and enthroned at fourteen in 1314.

Chronicles praise him for trusting able Confucian officials; he kept Đại Việt prosperous and at peace with the Yuan, although Champa shook off his overlordship in 1326. In 1329 he abdicated to his son Trần Vượng (Hiến Tông) but as retired emperor still settled court affairs.

When Hiến Tông died in 1341 he placed another son, Trần Hạo (Dụ Tông), on the throne, and spent years driving back raids on the western frontier. He wrote poetry but ordered most of it burned as he lay dying in 1357.

陈明宗（讳奣，1300—1357）是大越陈朝第五位皇帝，在位时正值陈朝鼎盛期。他是陈英宗第四子，1305年被立为皇太子，1314年年方十四岁登基。

史书称赞他重用有才干的儒臣，维持了国内兴盛，与元朝保持稳定关系，但占城于1326年摆脱了大越的臣属地位。1329年他禅位给儿子陈旺（宪宗），以太上皇身份继续裁断朝政。

1341年宪宗去世，他又立另一子陈暭（裕宗）为帝，并花多年工夫抵御西部边境的入侵。他也写诗，1357年临终时却下令烧毁大部分诗稿。

en:
Princess Ngọc Tha, titled Princess Thiên Ninh, was a daughter of Emperor Trần Minh Tông and Empress Hiến Từ and a sister of Emperor Trần Dụ Tông. She received the title in 1342 and married Trần Kham.

After Dương Nhật Lễ took the throne, he killed her mother. In 1370 her two sons joined a failed attempt by Trần kinsmen to kill Nhật Lễ and were killed; the following month she met her half-brother Trần Phủ and urged him to raise an army against Nhật Lễ. She helped bring about his fall and her brother's accession as Trần Nghệ Tông.

Lady Nguyễn (Nguyễn Phu nhân) was a daughter of the scholar Nguyễn Thánh Huấn, who tutored Emperor Trần Nhân Tông while he was crown prince. She became the wife of the prince Trần Quốc Chẩn and bore him a daughter, Huy Thánh.

In 1323 Huy Thánh married Emperor Trần Minh Tông and became his Lệ Thánh empress, honoured as Empress Dowager Hiến Từ. Lady Nguyễn's daughter by a later marriage into the Lê family was Anh Tư Nguyên Phi, mother of the emperors Trần Hiến Tông and Trần Nghệ Tông.

Trần Nguyên Dục (died 1364), titled Prince Cung Túc, was the eldest son of Emperor Trần Minh Tông and Empress Hiến Từ and an elder brother of Emperor Trần Dụ Tông. His extravagance displeased his father, who passed him over for the throne when Hiến Tông died.

He took an entertainer's wife as a concubine and adopted her son Dương Nhật Lễ, raising him in the palace. When Dụ Tông died without an heir in 1369, his will gave the throne to Nhật Lễ, who ruled little more than a year before the Trần clan overthrew him in 1370.

en:
Trần Nguyên Trác (1319–1370), titled Prince Cung Tĩnh, was a son of Emperor Trần Minh Tông. After the childless Dụ Tông died in 1369 and Dương Nhật Lễ took the throne, Nhật Lễ made Nguyên Trác his thái tể in charge of the court's troops.

When the new ruler moved to restore the imperial surname Dương, Nguyên Trác and his son Trần Nguyên Tiết plotted to kill him. Exposed, both were executed in 1370. His brother Trần Phủ withdrew and gathered forces; two months after the failed plot, Phủ overthrew Nhật Lễ and restored the Trần.

杨日礼企图恢复杨姓，元晫便与儿子陈元节密谋将其刺杀。密谋败露，父子二人于1370年被杀。其弟陈暊退走聚集力量；密谋失败两个月后，陈暊推翻杨日礼，复兴陈朝。

en:
Trần Nghệ Tông (Trần Phủ, 1321–1395) was the ninth Trần emperor of Đại Việt. A son of Trần Minh Tông and the consort Anh Tư, he was Prince Cung Định and a minister under Dương Nhật Lễ, who meant to restore the surname Dương.

In 1370 a plot by Trần princes against Nhật Lễ failed, and Phủ withdrew to raise forces. His half-sister Princess Thiên Ninh urged him on and joined his march; within two months Nhật Lễ was deposed, imprisoned and beaten to death, and Phủ took the throne.

He abdicated in 1372, yet as retired emperor ruled through three successors for over twenty years. His favour to his maternal kinsman Hồ Quý Ly let him build the power that destroyed the Trần in 1400.

zh:
陈艺宗（讳暊，1321—1395）是大越陈朝第九位皇帝。他是陈明宗与英姿元妃之子，原封恭定王，在企图恢复杨姓的杨日礼朝中任大臣。

1370年，陈朝宗室谋杀日礼失败，陈暊退走聚集力量。异母妹妹天宁公主劝他起兵，并与他一同进军京城；两个月内，杨日礼被废黜、囚禁，随后被打死，陈暊登基。

他1372年便禅位，却以太上皇身份历经三任君主、执掌朝政二十余年。他重用外戚胡季犛，使其势力坐大，最终在1400年灭亡陈朝。

en:
Trần Quốc Chẩn (1281–1328), titled Huệ Vũ đại vương, was a Trần general and the second son of Emperor Nhân Tông. In 1318 Anh Tông sent him to campaign against Champa. His daughter married his nephew Emperor Minh Tông as the Hiến Từ empress, making him the emperor's uncle and father-in-law.

In 1328, when he opposed naming a crown prince before his grandson was born, a bribed retainer accused him of treason, and Minh Tông had him imprisoned without food until he died.

陈国瑱（1281—1328），封号惠武大王，是陈朝大将、陈仁宗次子。1318年，陈英宗派他出征占城。他的女儿嫁给侄子陈明宗，即宪慈宣圣皇后，他因此身兼明宗的叔父与岳父。

1328年，他反对外孙出生前另立太子，被受贿的家臣诬告谋反，明宗将他囚禁、断绝饮食，他最终饿死。

en:
Trần Anh Tông (Trần Thuyên; 1276–1320) was the fourth emperor of the Trần dynasty, ruling Đại Việt from 1293 to 1314. Made crown prince in 1292, he succeeded his father Nhân Tông and kept peace with the Yuan, while his general defeated western border raiders.

Once, too drunk to receive his visiting father, he sought scholar Đoàn Nhữ Hài's help in writing a petition for forgiveness, then appointed Đoàn a counselor and gave up drinking.

He mounted campaigns against Champa, and his sister Huyền Trân married the Champa king, extending Đại Việt southward. In 1314 he abdicated to his son Trần Mạnh (Minh Tông) and remained retired emperor until his death.

zh:
陈英宗（陈烇；1276—1320）是陈朝第四位皇帝，1293年至1314年统治大越。他于1292年被立为太子，次年继承父亲仁宗的皇位，对元朝长期维持和平，手下将领击败了西部入犯者。

有一次，他因醉酒未能迎接来访的父亲，便请士人段汝谐代拟请罪表；事后他任命段汝谐为谏官，并戒了酒。

他数次对占城用兵，妹妹玄珍公主嫁给占城国王，大越南疆向南拓展。1314年他禅位给儿子陈奣（陈明宗），以太上皇身份度过余生，直至去世。

en:
Trần Hiến Tông (Trần Vượng, 1319–1341) was the sixth Trần emperor of Đại Việt, reigning from 1329 to 1341. A son of Trần Minh Tông and the consort Anh Tư, he was put on the throne at ten when his father abdicated, but ruled in name only: the retired emperor settled every matter of state.

It was Minh Tông who took the field against rebels and drove back raiders on the western frontier. Hiến Tông died in 1341 aged twenty-two without an heir, and his father raised his younger brother Trần Hạo, a boy of five, to the throne and kept control of the court.

陈宪宗（讳旺，1319—1341）是大越陈朝第六位皇帝，1329—1341年在位。他是陈明宗与英姿元妃之子，1329年父亲禅位时年仅十岁登基，却只是名义上的君主，朝政大事都由太上皇裁决。

出兵镇压叛乱、击退西部边境入犯者的，正是明宗本人。1341年宪宗以二十二岁之龄无嗣而终，父亲随即立他五岁的幼弟陈暭为帝，朝政仍握在自己手中。

Abel Valdemarsen (c. 1218–1252), son of Valdemar II, became Duke of Schleswig in 1232. As duke he fought a long civil war against his brother Eric IV, and after Eric's murder in 1250 Abel cleared himself by a public oath and was elected king.

After only eighteen months he campaigned against tax-rebelling Frisian peasants and was killed on Husum Bridge in 1252 by a wheelwright named Henner. His son was held hostage in Cologne, and his brother Christopher I succeeded him.

阿贝尔·瓦尔德马森（约1218—1252）是瓦尔德马二世之子，1232年受封石勒苏益格公爵。他任公爵时与兄长埃里克四世长期内战；1250年埃里克四世遇害后，阿贝尔发誓洗清嫌疑，被拥立为王。

Adelaide of Holstein-Rendsburg (c. 1299–January 1350) was the daughter of Count Henry I of Holstein-Rendsburg and Helwig of Bronckhorst. In 1313 she married Duke Eric II of Schleswig, who died in 1325, and after his death she married Count Dietrich V of Hohnstein-Heringen.

By Eric she was the mother of Valdemar III, king of Denmark from 1326 to 1329 and later duke of Schleswig, and of Helvig, who married King Valdemar IV in 1340; both her son and her son-in-law therefore wore the Danish crown.

荷尔斯泰因-伦茨堡的阿德莱德（约1299—1350年1月）是荷尔斯泰因-伦茨堡伯爵亨利一世与布龙克霍斯特的海尔维希之女。1313年她嫁给石勒苏益格公爵埃里克二世（1325年卒），丈夫死后改嫁霍恩施泰因-黑林根伯爵迪特里希五世。

en:
Buris Henriksen (c. 1130–c. 1167) was a son of Prince Henrik Skadelår. During the Danish civil war he and his brother Canute backed Canute V before going over to Valdemar the Great after the Bloodfeast of Roskilde in 1157. In 1162 he inherited his brother's Duchy of Southern Jutland and accompanied Valdemar to Frederick Barbarossa's court.

In 1167 Valdemar had him imprisoned at Søborg Castle on charges of conspiring with a Norwegian earl to seize the throne. His fate thereafter is unknown, though he may not have survived long in captivity.

en:
Tycho Brahe (1546–1601) was a Danish nobleman and the greatest astronomer of the age before the telescope. The solar eclipse of 1560 turned him to the stars. In 1566 a duel at Rostock cost him the bridge of his nose, and he wore a metal prosthesis thereafter.

In 1572 he saw a new star in Cassiopeia and found it lay beyond the Moon; he published De nova stella in 1573. Frederick II gave him the island of Hven, where he built Uraniborg and compiled the most accurate star catalogue yet made. He devised the Tychonic system, with the planets orbiting the Sun and the Sun orbiting the Earth.

In 1597 Christian IV forced him out of Denmark, and he became imperial astronomer in Prague. He died there in 1601, asking Johannes Kepler to finish the Rudolphine Tables; Kepler used his data to derive the laws of planetary motion.

第谷·布拉赫（1546—1601）是丹麦贵族，也是望远镜发明之前最伟大的天文学家。1560年的日食让他转向星空。1566年他在罗斯托克的决斗中失去鼻梁，余生佩戴金属假鼻。

1572年，他在仙后座看到一颗新星，发现它位于月球之外，并于1573年出版《论新星》。腓特烈二世把汶岛赐给他，他在岛上建造天堡，编出当时最精确的恒星位置表，还提出第谷体系：行星绕太阳运行，太阳绕地球运行。

1597年克里斯蒂安四世迫使他离开丹麦，他前往布拉格出任御用天文学家。1601年他在布拉格去世，临终请约翰内斯·开普勒完成《鲁道夫星表》；开普勒后来用他的数据推导出行星运动定律。

en:
Canute Henriksen (c. 1110–1162) was a son of Prince Henrik Skadelår. During the civil war he fought for Canute V and helped drive Sweyn Grathe and Valdemar out of Schleswig. After Canute V was murdered at the Bloodfeast of Roskilde in 1157, he and his brother Buris switched sides, helping Valdemar win at Grathe Heath and become sole king.

Rewarded with the Duchy of Schleswig, Canute ruled it until his sudden death in 1162. He left no children and was succeeded by Buris.

en:
Canute IV, later called the Holy (c. 1042–1086), a son of Sweyn II Estridsson, was king of Denmark from 1080. He had led raids on England and married Adela of Flanders. As king he enforced tithes, enriched Lund Cathedral in 1085 and tightened royal law over nobles and peasants.

In 1085 he gathered a fleet to invade England, but it never sailed. A peasant revolt drove him to Odense, where rebels slew him in St. Alban's Priory on 10 July 1086. Canonized in 1101, he became Denmark's patron saint.

en:
Canute Lavard (1096–1131) was the only legitimate son of Eric I of Denmark. In 1115 his uncle King Niels enfeoffed him with Schleswig to defend the border against Slavic raiders. He pacified it and became Duke of Holstein and a vassal of the emperor, who recognized him as lord over the Wends.

His standing made him a possible successor to Niels but alarmed Niels's son Magnus the Strong, who in 1131 trapped and slew him in Haraldsted Forest. His posthumous son Valdemar I secured his canonization in 1170.

en:
Canute V Magnussen (c. 1129–1157) was the son of Magnus the Strong. After Eric III abdicated in 1146, Jutland's magnates proclaimed Canute king while Zealand and Scania crowned Sweyn III, opening years of civil war. Canute joined Sweyn on the Wendish Crusade in 1147 but was defeated by him in Jutland in 1150 and fled to Sweden.

A 1152 settlement left him Sweyn's inferior co-ruler, and a 1157 tripartition gave him Zealand; Sweyn's men killed him at the Bloodfeast of Roskilde later that year.

en:
Canute VI (1163–1202), eldest son of Valdemar the Great, was made co-king in 1170 and ruled Denmark alone from 1182. When Emperor Frederick Barbarossa demanded homage in 1184, Canute defied him; Absalon's fleet shattered the invasion fleet of Bogislaw I of Pomerania, and by 1185 Bogislaw acknowledged Canute as overlord, after which Danish kings bore the title King of the Wends.

Canute crusaded against the pagan Estonians in 1197. He died childless in 1202 and the crown passed to his brother Valdemar II.

en:
Christopher II (1276–1332), a son of Eric V, was elected king in 1320 after Eric VI died, but only by accepting a charter stripping the crown of taxation and patronage. When he tried to rule without it and warred in Germany, Gerhard III of Holstein drove him into exile in 1326 and set Valdemar III on the throne.

Restored in 1329, he found most of Denmark mortgaged to German counts. He died in 1332 with the kingdom dissolved; his son Valdemar IV became king in 1340 and reunited Denmark.

After Jaromar II of Rügen invaded Zealand and took Copenhagen in 1259, Christopher died suddenly at Ribe, rumoured poisoned at mass. His son Eric V succeeded him.

en:
Jens Dinesen Jersin (1588–1634) was a Danish Lutheran bishop. Educated at Herlufsholm and Wittenberg, he served as tutor to Christian IV's illegitimate sons and held teaching and parish posts in Copenhagen before becoming bishop of Ribe.

A Ramist, he issued Latin grammars that explained Latin partly in Danish, though his teaching method met fierce opposition from professors and schoolmen. As bishop he fought superstition, publishing in 1631 the first Danish work to argue that many reported wonders were imagination or fraud.

A Ramist, he issued Latin grammars that explained Latin partly in Danish, though his teaching method met fierce opposition from professors and schoolmen. As bishop he fought superstition, publishing in 1631 the first Danish work to argue that many reported wonders were imagination or fraud.

延斯·迪内森·耶尔辛（1588—1634）是丹麦路德宗主教。他在海卢夫斯霍尔姆和维滕贝格求学，曾任克里斯蒂安四世私生子的教师，并在哥本哈根担任教职与教区牧师，后来成为里伯主教。

他信奉拉米斯学说，出版的拉丁文语法书部分用丹麦语解释语法，教学方法却遭到教授和学校人士的激烈反对。任主教期间他抵制迷信，1631年出版丹麦第一部主张许多所谓奇事多出于想象或骗局的著作。

en:
Eric Christoffersen (c. 1307–1332), eldest son of Christopher II of Denmark, was elected king in 1321 and crowned beside his father in 1324 as junior co-ruler. In 1325, sent against the Holstein counts, he was deserted by his troops and captured at Haderslev.

Released in 1330 after marrying the sister of Gerhard III, he fought again when war resumed. Defeated at the Danevirke in 1331, he escaped wounded to Kiel and died soon after, and was later buried at St Bendt's Church in Ringsted.

埃里克·克里斯托弗森（约1307—1332）是丹麦国王克里斯托弗二世的长子，1321年被选为国王，1324年与父亲一同加冕，为共治的幼王。1325年他被派去抵御荷尔斯泰因诸伯爵，却被部下抛弃，在哈泽斯莱乌被俘。

en:
Eric I, called the Good (c. 1056–1103), a son of Sweyn II Estridsson, was king of Denmark from 1095. He backed Canute IV, fled the 1086 rising into Scania, and was elected at the landsting assemblies after Olaf Hunger's death as the long famines ended.

Popular and diplomatic, he secured from the Pope Canute's canonization in 1101 and an independent archbishopric at Lund. In 1103 he set out on pilgrimage to Jerusalem, but died at Paphos in Cyprus in July.

en:
Eric II the Memorable (c. 1090–1137) was an illegitimate son of Eric I and a jarl. After his half-brother Canute Lavard was murdered in 1131, he rose against King Niels and was proclaimed antiking in Scania. Mocked as Harefoot after early defeats, he returned in 1134 and, with German mounted mercenaries, crushed Niels at Fotevik.

He killed his rival Harald Kesja and in 1136 crusaded against pagan Rügen, forcing Arkona to surrender by cutting off its water. In 1137 a nobleman slew him with a spear at the Urnehoved assembly.

“难忘者”埃里克二世（约1090—1137）是埃里克一世的私生子，曾任雅尔。1131年异母兄克努特·拉瓦德遇害后，他起兵反抗尼尔斯国王，在斯科讷被拥立为对立国王。他曾因撤退被讥为“兔足”，但1134年卷土重来，依靠德意志雇佣骑兵在福泰维克战役击溃尼尔斯。

Eric II Valdemarsen (c. 1288–1325) was Duke of Schleswig from 1312 until his death, the only legitimate son of Duke Valdemar IV. He already ruled jointly with his father before succeeding him, and in 1313 he married Adelaide of Holstein-Rendsburg.

Their son Valdemar was underage when Eric died in 1325, later ruling Schleswig and serving as king of Denmark in 1326–1329; their daughter Helvig married King Valdemar IV. Eric was buried in Schleswig Cathedral.

en:
Eric III Lamb (c. 1120–1146) was the son of Ragnhild, a daughter of Eric I. He fought for his uncle Eric II at Fotevik in 1134 and took the throne after his murder in 1137. His cousin Olaf Haraldsen seized Scania in 1139, but Eric defeated and slew him near Helsingborg in 1141.

Wendish raids went largely unanswered under him, while he richly favoured the Church, especially Odense's St Canute's Abbey. In 1146 he became the first Danish king to abdicate voluntarily, retiring to the abbey, where he died.

en:
Eric IV, called Plovpenning (c. 1216–1250), son of Valdemar II, was Duke of Schleswig and crowned co-king in 1232, succeeding his father in 1241. His reign was consumed by civil war with his brother Abel of Schleswig and by a Scanian peasant revolt against his plough tax, which earned him his nickname.

On 10 August 1250, while Abel's guest at Gottorf, he was seized by Abel's steward, beheaded and thrown into the Schlei. Abel succeeded him after swearing his innocence before twenty-four nobles.

Eric I Abelsøn (c. 1241–1272), second son of Abel, claimed Schleswig after his brother Valdemar III's death in 1257, but his uncle Christopher I withheld the duchy. In 1259 he joined the bishop and Jaromar II of Rügen in taking Copenhagen. Made duke in 1260, he defeated Regent Margaret Sambiria at Lohede in 1261, capturing Eric V.

The 1264 peace granted him all crown lands in Schleswig and Als. He died in 1272, leaving Gottorp and the duchy to his son Valdemar IV.

en:
Eric V Klipping (1249–1286) became king of Denmark in 1259 on his father Christopher I's death; his mother Margaret Sambiria acted as regent until 1266. Captured by the Holsteiners in 1261, he was held at the Brandenburg court, and in 1273 married Agnes of Brandenburg. He curbed the church but antagonised the nobles, who in 1282 forced him to accept Denmark's first coronation charter limiting royal power.

In 1286 he was hacked to death in a barn at Finderup; Stig Andersen Hvide and other magnates were outlawed.

埃里克五世（削剪王，1249—1286）在父亲克里斯托弗一世去世后于1259年成为丹麦国王，由母亲玛格丽特·桑比利亚摄政至1266年。1261年他被荷尔斯泰因人俘获，曾被软禁在勃兰登堡宫廷，1273年与勃兰登堡的阿格尼丝成婚。亲政后他压制教会，却激怒了贵族，1282年被迫接受限制王权的丹麦第一部加冕约章。

en:
Eric VI Menved (1274–1319) succeeded his murdered father Eric V as king of Denmark in 1286, aged twelve, with his mother Agnes as regent until 1294. Arresting Archbishop Jens Grand in 1294 brought a papal interdict lifted only after his submission in 1303.

Lavish tournaments and foreign wars drained the treasury, forcing him to mortgage royal lands; famine and taxation then provoked revolts on Zealand and in Jutland, crushed with German mercenaries. All his children died before him, so on his death in 1319 his brother Christopher II inherited a bankrupt kingdom.

en:
Estrid Svendsdatter (born c. 990, died after 1057) was a Danish princess, daughter of Sweyn Forkbeard and half-sister of Cnut the Great. She married Ulf Jarl, who ruled Denmark until Cnut had him killed in 1026. Her son Sweyn Estridsson became king in 1047 and gave the Estridsen dynasty her name.

She held great estates across Denmark and was one of the North's richest women; tradition says she replaced Roskilde's timber church with its first stone church, where she was buried.

en:
Gorm the Old (born before 900, died c. 958) was the first ruler recognised as king of all Denmark, reigning from Jelling from about 936. He married Queen Thyra, whom tradition credits with strengthening the Danevirke rampart, and raised the older Jelling Stone and a burial mound in her honour, calling her Denmark's salvation.

Gorm remained a pagan; Denmark converted only under his son Harald Bluetooth. Tree-ring dating places his death in the winter of 958–959.

老戈姆（900年之前出生，约958年去世）是第一位被公认为全丹麦之王的统治者，约936年起以耶灵为都统治。他娶提拉王后为妻，传统认为她主持加固了边境工事丹麦墙；戈姆为她立起较早的耶灵石，还修建坟冢，铭文称她为“丹麦的拯救者”。

en:
Peder Griffenfeld (1635–1699), born Peder Schumacher into a wealthy Copenhagen trading family, was the leading Danish statesman of his age. After years of study abroad, he returned in 1662 and helped draft the absolutist King's Law of 1665.

From Christian V's accession in 1670 he was the king's chief minister, and in 1673 he became Chancellor of Denmark and a count. Arrested in 1676 on a treason charge now considered false, he spent 22 years in prison, mostly at Munkholmen in Norway.

佩德·格里芬费尔德（1635—1699），原名佩德·舒马赫，生于哥本哈根一个富商家庭，是那个时代丹麦最有权势的政治家。他在国外游学多年，1662年回国，并参与起草1665年确立专制王权的《国王法》。

en:
Harald Bluetooth Gormsson (died c. 985/86), son of Gorm the Old, ruled Denmark from about 958. Around 965 he raised the larger Jelling Stone, whose inscription boasts that he unified Denmark and made the Danes Christian. He backed conversion with a wave of building, expanding the Danevirke, raising ring fortresses, and issuing Denmark's first coinage.

He briefly held power in Norway and fought the German emperors. Deposed by his son Sweyn Forkbeard, he died of his wounds around 986 and was buried at Roskilde.

Harald II Svensen (c. 997–1018) was king of Denmark from 1014 until his death. A younger son of Sweyn Forkbeard, he ruled Denmark as regent while his father campaigned in England.

After Sweyn died in 1014, the Danes elected Harald their king, while his brother Cnut led the army in England and took the English throne in 1016. Harald died around 1018, and Cnut succeeded him in Denmark, uniting the two kingdoms.

Harald III, called Hen (c. 1040–1080), an illegitimate son of Sweyn II Estridsson, was king of Denmark from 1076. He joined his father's 1069 English raid and was elected king after promising to uphold the law.

A peaceful ruler, he standardized Danish coinage with royal mints and sought to reform trial by combat and hot-iron ordeals by introducing sworn oath-helpers after English custom. He died on 17 April 1080 and was buried at Dalby in Scania, leaving no heirs; Canute IV succeeded him.

en:
Christian Frederik Hansen (1756–1845), known as C. F. Hansen, was the leading Danish architect of his age, called Denmark's Palladio for the austere neoclassicism of his buildings. Trained at the Royal Danish Academy under Harsdorff, he studied Roman architecture in Italy in 1782–1784, then spent eighteen years in Altona as regional architect for Schleswig and Holstein.

Recalled to Copenhagen in 1804 and made Chief Building Director in 1808, he built the City Hall and Courthouse on Nytorv, rebuilt the Church of Our Lady after the British bombardment of 1807, and reconstructed Christiansborg Palace.

en:
Hans Christian Andersen (1805–1875) was Denmark's most famous writer, born in Odense the son of a shoemaker and an illiterate washerwoman. At fourteen he went to Copenhagen to become an actor. At the Royal Danish Theatre he lost his singing voice; Jonas Collin arranged for his schooling.

A travel grant in 1833 began years of travel across Europe, and his first novel The Improvisatore succeeded in 1835. The same year he published the first of his Fairy Tales Told for Children. Critics disliked their chatty style, but The Little Mermaid made his name, and in The Emperor's New Clothes a child cries out that the emperor wears nothing.

His 156 tales, among them The Ugly Duckling and The Snow Queen, have been translated into more than 125 languages. He died in 1875, having asked that the funeral march keep time with little steps, since most mourners would be children.

汉斯·克里斯蒂安·安徒生（1805—1875）是丹麦最著名的作家，生于欧登塞，父亲是鞋匠，母亲是不识字的洗衣妇。十四岁时他前往哥本哈根想当演员，进入丹麦皇家剧院后嗓音变声，院长约纳斯·科林安排他入学读书。

1833年一笔旅行津贴开启了他遍游欧洲的旅程，1835年第一部小说《即兴诗人》获得成功，同年出版《讲给孩子们听的童话》第一集。评论家不喜欢闲谈式的文风，但《海的女儿》让他成名；《皇帝的新装》以一个孩子喊出皇帝什么也没穿作结。

他的156篇童话包括《丑小鸭》和《白雪皇后》，已被译成125种以上的语言。1875年他去世，生前要求葬礼乐曲踩着小步子的节拍，因为跟在后面的多半是孩子。

Helvig of Schleswig (c. 1320–1374), daughter of Eric II, Duke of Schleswig, was queen of Denmark as the wife of Valdemar IV Atterdag, and her marriage was a piece of politics. Her brother Valdemar V had once ruled Denmark as their uncle Gerhard III's ward.

In the late 1330s he allied with Christopher II's son Valdemar against Gerhard and sealed the pact by giving Helvig to him. They wed in 1340, and she brought the pawned province of Nørrejylland as her dowry. She bore Margaret, the future Margaret I, in 1353, after which she no longer lived with the king.

She spent her last years at Esrum Abbey, where she died in 1374 as a lay sister and was buried. A year later her daughter became regent of Denmark.

石勒苏益格的黑尔维希（约1320—1374）是石勒苏益格公爵埃里克二世之女，丹麦国王瓦尔德马四世·阿道戴的王后，她的婚姻是一桩政治安排。她的兄长瓦尔德马五世曾做过丹麦国王，受舅父格哈德三世监护。

1330年代末，兄长与克里斯托弗二世之子瓦尔德马结盟对抗格哈德，并把黑尔维希许配给他以巩固盟约。两人1340年成婚，她带来被抵押的北日德兰领地作为嫁妆。1353年她生下后来的玛格丽特一世，此后便不再与国王同住。

她晚年住在埃斯鲁姆修道院，1374年以世俗修女身份在院中去世并安葬。一年后，她的女儿成为丹麦摄政。

Henrik Skadelår, or Henrik the Lame (c. 1090–1134), was a Danish prince, the son of Svend Tronkræver and grandson of Sweyn II Estridsson. Through Queen Margaret Fredkulla he married Ingrid Ragnvaldsdotter, granddaughter of King Inge I of Sweden.

After his cousin Canute Lavard was killed in 1131, Henrik was put forward as a possible king of Denmark. He never pressed the claim: on 4 June 1134 he fell at the Battle of Fotevik fighting for King Niels. His sons included Magnus Henriksen, briefly king of Sweden, among others.

en:
Poul Laxmand (c. 1450–1502), the greatest Danish landowner of his age, served as rigshofmester from 1489. He belonged to the group of high nobles who held royal power in check, and his estates, mostly in Skåne, comprised about 900 tenant farms. In 1487 he helped negotiate Gotland's surrender to Denmark.

After taking part in King Hans's failed relief of Stockholm in 1502, he was stabbed to death on the Højbro bridge in Copenhagen on 22 June. The crown then condemned him for treason and seized his lands.

Ludvig Holberg (1684–1754) was a Danish-Norwegian writer, historian and playwright, born in Bergen and active in Copenhagen. He brought Enlightenment thought to Denmark-Norway and is regarded as the founder of modern Danish and Norwegian literature, publishing works of history, law, geography and philosophy.

He is best known for the comedies written in 1722–1723 for Copenhagen's Lille Grønnegade Theatre, including Jeppe on the Hill and Erasmus Montanus, whose characters became archetypes in Danish. In 1747 he founded the Barony of Holberg on his estates and died in Copenhagen in 1754.

路维·郝尔拜（1684—1754）是丹麦-挪威作家、历史学家与剧作家，生于卑尔根，主要活动于哥本哈根。他把启蒙思想引入丹麦-挪威，被视为现代丹麦与挪威文学的奠基人，著作遍及历史、法学、地理和哲学。

Magnus Olafsson, called the Good (1024–1047), was the illegitimate son of St. Olaf of Norway. When Cnut the Great deposed his father in 1028, he took refuge at the court of Yaroslav the Wise in Kiev, returning in 1035 to be crowned king of Norway at eleven.

In 1042 he also became king of Denmark and fought Sven Estridsson for the kingdom. In 1046 he accepted his uncle Harald Hardrada as co-king of Norway. Magnus died in Denmark on 25 October 1047, and the two crowns passed to Harald and Sven.

en:
Niels (c. 1063–1134), youngest son of Sweyn II Estridsson, was elected king of Denmark in 1104 after his brother Eric Evergood died on pilgrimage. In 1105 he married Margaret Fredkulla, daughter of King Inge I of Sweden, who held strong influence at court. He backed the canonization of Canute IV the Holy and ruled with the clergy's support.

After his son Magnus murdered the popular prince Canute Lavard in 1131, Niels supported him, sparking civil war. Defeated at Fotevik in 1134, he fled to Schleswig and was killed there on 25 June.

en:
Niels Juel (1629–1697) was a Dano-Norwegian admiral born in Christiania. He learned seamanship in the Dutch navy during the First Anglo-Dutch War, joined Danish service, and became an admiral in 1657, helping defend Copenhagen in 1658–1660.

Given supreme command in the Scanian War after Cort Adeler's death in 1675, he fought at Jasmund and Öland, then defeated the Swedes at Møn and at Køge Bay in 1677; Køge Bay was the greatest victory in Danish naval history.

Juel regained supreme command in 1678. From 1683 he headed the admiralty and expanded the fleet into a blue-water navy.

他于1678年重新获得最高指挥权。1683年起他主管海军部，将舰队扩建为一支远洋海军。

en:
Peter Wessel Tordenskiold (1690–1720) was a Norwegian-born vice-admiral in the Dano-Norwegian navy and a daring raider of the Great Northern War. He moved from Trondheim to Copenhagen in 1704 and joined the navy.

In 1714, when his ammunition ran low during a fight with a Swedish privateer, he asked his opponent for more. Frederick IV ordered a court-martial over his recklessness, but he was acquitted after citing the naval code and promoted.

Ennobled as Tordenskiold in 1716, he destroyed most of the Swedish transport fleet at Dynekilen, forcing Charles XII to abandon Norway, and in 1719 took Marstrand and Carlsten fortress. In November 1720 he was killed in a duel near Hanover.

彼得·韦塞尔·托登肖尔（1690—1720）是出生于挪威的丹挪海军中将，也是大北方战争中大胆的海上袭击者。1704年他从特隆赫姆前往哥本哈根，加入海军。

1714年他与一艘瑞典私掠舰交战，弹药不足时竟向对方索取弹药。腓特烈四世因他的鲁莽下令军事审判；他援引海军法典为自己辩护，最终无罪开释并获晋升。

1716年他受封贵族、得姓托登肖尔，随后在迪内基伦摧毁大部分瑞典运输船，迫使卡尔十二世放弃挪威，1719年又攻克马斯特兰德和卡尔斯滕要塞。1720年11月，他在汉诺威附近的一场决斗中身亡。

en:
Olaf I Hunger (c. 1050–1095), a son of Sweyn II Estridsson, was king of Denmark from 1086. In 1085, as spokesman of the fleet mustered against England, he drew Canute IV's suspicion, was chained and exiled to Flanders. After Canute was killed, Olaf was proclaimed king.

His reign brought harvest failures and famine, whence his nickname, widely seen as punishment for Canute's murder. Royal power ebbed to the magnates. He died in 1095 and was succeeded by Eric the Good.

奥拉夫一世，绰号“饥饿者”（约1050—1095），是斯文二世·埃斯特里德森之子，1086年起为丹麦国王。1085年，他作为征英舰队的代言人遭克努特四世猜忌，被戴上镣铐流放佛兰德斯。克努特被杀后，他被拥立为王。

他在位时连年歉收、饥荒蔓延，由此得到“饥饿者”的绰号，时人视之为弑杀克努特的天谴，王权也旁落于大贵族之手。1095年他去世，由“好人”埃里克继位。

en:
Otte Rud (1520–1565) was a Danish fleet commander in the Northern Seven Years' War. As a young man he served abroad, fighting for Saxony against Brunswick, then returned home in 1543 and in 1549 married Pernille Oxe, Peder Oxe's sister.

In 1563 he won fame on land at Mared and then at sea, helping to destroy the Swedish flagship Makalös off Gotland in May 1564. He succeeded Herluf Trolle as fleet commander in 1565, was taken by a stronger Swedish fleet off Bornholm, and died of plague in captivity at Svartsjö on 11 October 1565.

奥特·鲁德（1520—1565）是北方七年战争中的丹麦舰队司令。他年轻时在国外从军，曾为萨克森对不伦瑞克作战，1543年回国，1549年娶佩德·奥克塞之妹佩妮莱·奥克塞。

en:
Otto of Denmark, Otto Christoffersen (c. 1310 – after 1346), was the second son of King Christopher II and Euphemia of Pomerania, created Duke of Lolland and Estonia. When Christopher died in 1332 after his elder brother Eric, Otto claimed the crown, but Count Gerhard III of Holstein defeated and captured him near Viborg in October 1334; he was imprisoned at Segeberg.

Released after his younger brother Valdemar IV took the throne in 1340, Otto renounced his claim, went to Germany and joined the Teutonic Order in 1346, which bought his duchy that year.

en:
Peder Oxe (1520–1575) was Denmark's leading financier of the century. He joined the rigsråd in 1552, governed Copenhagen in 1554 and shared charge of the treasury.

In 1557 he quarrelled with the king over a property exchange and in 1558 fled to Germany, where he intrigued against Frederick II. Financial difficulties during the Northern Seven Years' War led Frederick to recall him in 1566 and restore his estates.

As rigshofmester he raised the Sound Dues, reformed the coinage, cut the national debt, redeemed crown lands and promoted trade and agriculture, dying the wealthiest landowner in Denmark on 24 October 1575.

佩德·奥克塞（1520—1575）是那个世纪丹麦首屈一指的理财家。他1552年进入国务会议，1554年任哥本哈根长官并与人共同掌管国库。

1557年他与国王因地产交换发生争执，1558年逃往德意志，在那里密谋反对腓特烈二世。北方七年战争期间的财政困难促使腓特烈于1566年将他召回并归还其地产。

任里格斯霍夫梅斯特期间，他提高松德海峡税、改革币制、削减国债、赎回王室土地并推动商贸与农业，1575年10月24日去世时是丹麦最富有的地主。

en:
Saxo Grammaticus (c. 1150–c. 1220) was a Danish historian and cleric, born on Zealand and probably educated outside Denmark. He served Archbishop Absalon of Lund, chief adviser to Valdemar I, as clerk and secretary.

Under Absalon's patronage he composed the Gesta Danorum, a Latin history of the Danes in sixteen books, from their earliest legends to his own day. It is the first full history of Denmark, and its tale of Amleth later inspired Shakespeare's Hamlet.

萨克索·格拉玛提库斯（约1150—约1220）是丹麦史学家、教士，生于西兰岛，可能曾在丹麦以外受教育。他担任隆德大主教、瓦尔德马一世首席顾问阿布萨隆的文书与秘书。

在阿布萨隆庇护下，他以拉丁文写成《丹麦人的事迹》，共十六卷，自丹麦人最古老的传说叙述到他所处的时代，是丹麦第一部完整通史；书中阿姆雷特的故事后来启发了莎士比亚的《哈姆雷特》。

en:
Anders Sørensen Vedel (1542–1616) was a Danish priest and historian. Born in Vejle, in 1562 he accompanied Tycho Brahe on his European tour as tutor, and became priest at Copenhagen Castle in 1568.

Encouraged by Peder Oxe, he translated Saxo Grammaticus's Latin chronicle Gesta Danorum into Danish, publishing Den danske Krønicke in 1575. Appointed royal historian in 1584, he failed to complete a continuation of Saxo, but his Hundredvisebogen of 1591, a hundred Danish ballads, preserved the older Danish tradition. He died at Ribe on 13 February 1616.

安诺斯·瑟伦森·韦泽尔（1542—1616）是丹麦牧师、历史学家。他生于瓦埃勒，1562年作为第谷·布拉赫的导师陪其游历欧洲，1568年任哥本哈根城堡牧师。

Svend Tronkræver, or Svend Svendsen (died 1104), was an illegitimate son of King Sweyn II Estridsson of Denmark. When Eric Evergood died in 1103, Svend claimed the crown. Traveling to the royal election at Viborg he fell ill, yet pressed on lest rivals arrive first, and died of the hardships in 1104.

His younger brother Niels was elected king instead. His son was Henrik Skadelår, and his grandson Magnus Henriksen ruled briefly as king of Sweden.

en:
Sweyn II Estridsson (c. 1019–1076), born in England to Ulf and Estrid, sister of Canute the Great, ruled Denmark from 1047. He fought wars against Magnus I of Norway and Harald Hardrada, who defeated him at Niså in 1062 before recognizing him in 1064.

In 1069 he allied with Edgar Ætheling and sent a force to England that took York, then accepted payment from William the Conqueror to abandon him. He organized the Danish church into bishoprics and died in 1076; five of his sons followed him on the throne.

zh:
斯文二世·埃斯特里德森（约1019—1076）生于英格兰，是乌尔夫与克努特大帝之妹埃斯特丽德之子，1047年起为丹麦国王。他同挪威国王马格努斯一世和哈拉尔·哈德拉达作战，1062年在尼萨战败，1064年哈拉尔才承认他的王位。

1069年，他与显贵者埃德加结盟，派兵入侵英格兰并攻占约克，随后收受征服者威廉的钱款抛弃了埃德加。他将丹麦教会划分为多个主教区，1076年去世；他有五个儿子先后登上丹麦王位。

en:
Sweyn III Grathe (c. 1125–1157) was the illegitimate son of Eric II the Memorable. When Eric III abdicated in 1146, Zealand's magnates elected Sweyn king while Jutland's crowned Canute V, opening a civil war. Sweyn held on through shifting alliances with Canute V and his cousin Valdemar.

In 1157 the three agreed to partition Denmark, but at a banquet in Roskilde Sweyn's men murdered Canute V while Valdemar escaped. Valdemar raised an army and defeated Sweyn at the Battle of Grathe Heath in 1157, and Sweyn was killed after it.

“格拉特”斯文三世（约1125—1157）是“难忘者”埃里克二世的私生子。1146年埃里克三世退位后，西兰岛的贵族拥立斯文为王，日德兰半岛的贵族则加冕克努特五世，丹麦由此陷入内战。斯文在与克努特五世、堂亲瓦尔德马反复离合的同盟中维持王位。

1157年三人同意瓜分丹麦，但在罗斯基勒的晚宴上，斯文的手下杀死克努特五世，瓦尔德马逃脱。瓦尔德马随即起兵，于同年在格拉特希夫战役击败斯文，斯文在战后被杀。

en:
Bertel Thorvaldsen (1770–1844) was Denmark's first internationally celebrated sculptor, born in Copenhagen to an Icelandic wood-carver. He won a Royal Danish Academy gold medal in 1793 and reached Rome on its stipend in 1797, working there for forty-one years.

His Jason of 1801, praised by Antonio Canova, established him as Canova's heir in heroic neoclassicism; his monuments include the Copernicus statue in Warsaw and the tomb of Pope Pius VII in St Peter's. When he returned in 1838 he was hailed as a national hero, and the Thorvaldsen Museum was built beside Christiansborg to house his work.

贝特尔·托瓦尔森（1770—1844）是第一位享誉国际的丹麦雕塑家，生于哥本哈根，父亲是冰岛籍木雕工匠。他1793年获得丹麦皇家美术学院金奖，1797年凭津贴赴罗马，在那里创作了四十一年。

他1801年的《伊阿宋》受到安东尼奥·卡诺瓦赞赏，使他成为卡诺瓦在英雄式新古典主义领域的传人；作品包括华沙的哥白尼雕像和圣彼得大教堂里的庇护七世墓。1838年回国时他被当作民族英雄受到欢迎，人们在克里斯蒂安堡旁修建托瓦尔森博物馆收藏他的作品。

en:
Valdemar IV, called Atterdag for the lands he gradually won back (c. 1320–1375), grew up at Louis IV's court while Count Gerhard III ruled a Denmark pledged away in pieces. After Gerhard was killed in 1340, Valdemar was acclaimed king at Viborg.

He redeemed the pawned lands and taxed hard, even through the Black Death of 1349–1350, and uprisings followed. In 1361 he conquered Gotland and, at Visby, ordered three beer barrels filled with gold and silver within three days or the town would be pillaged; they were full before the first night.

In 1362 the Hanseatic towns, Sweden and Norway allied against him, and they forced him abroad in 1368. The Treaty of Stralsund in 1370 gave the Hansa trading rights and let him return. He died in 1375; his daughter was Margaret I.

瓦尔德马四世，绰号“阿道戴”，因逐步收回失地而得名（约1320—1375）。他在路德维希四世的宫廷长大，此时格哈德三世统治着被一块块抵押出去的丹麦。1340年格哈德被杀后，瓦尔德马在维堡被拥立为王。

他赎回被抵押的土地，并不断加税，1349—1350年黑死病期间也不松手，随后起义四起。1361年他征服哥得兰岛，在维斯比下令三天内用金银装满三只啤酒桶，否则纵兵洗劫，结果第一天夜里桶就满了。

1362年汉萨诸城与瑞典、挪威结盟对抗他，1368年他被迫离开丹麦。1370年订立《施特拉尔松德条约》，汉萨同盟取得贸易权利，他得以返国。1375年他去世，其女即后来的玛格丽特一世。

en:
Valdemar I, called the Great (1131–1182), was the son of the murdered prince Canute Lavard. After Eric III abdicated in 1146 he fought a ten-year civil war against rivals Sweyn III and Canute V. When Sweyn murdered Canute at Roskilde in 1157, Valdemar avenged his kinsman, defeating and killing Sweyn at Grathe Heath and uniting Denmark.

Aided by Bishop Absalon, he rebuilt the kingdom and warred down the Wends. In 1168 he stormed Arkona on Rügen, imposing Christianity and Danish overlordship.

en:
Valdemar II, called the Victorious (1170–1241), succeeded his brother Canute VI as king of Denmark in 1202, conquering Holstein and Lübeck. In 1219 his army defeated the Estonians at Lindanise, where legend says the Dannebrog fell from the sky.

In 1223 he and his son were seized on Lyø by Count Henry of Schwerin and freed only for a ransom; his defeat at Bornhöved in 1227 lost Denmark's German lands. His Code of Jutland was enacted in 1241, shortly before he died.

en:
Valdemar III (1314–1364), son of Duke Eric II of Schleswig and Adelaide of Holstein, was placed on the Danish throne in 1326 when Holstein and Danish nobles deposed Christopher II; as he was only eleven, his maternal uncle Gerhard III of Holstein ruled as regent. The Constitutio Valdemariana barred any one man from holding Denmark and Schleswig together, so Valdemar enfeoffed Schleswig to his uncle.

Peasant revolts in Zealand and Jutland weakened the regime, and in 1329 Christopher II returned to the throne while Valdemar resumed rule as Duke of Schleswig until his death.

en:
Valdemar III Abelsøn (1238–1257) was the eldest son of King Abel and Matilda and Duke of Schleswig from 1253. When Abel was killed in 1252, Valdemar was a hostage in Cologne and could not claim it, so his uncle Christopher I became king.

Freed by his mother's Holstein kinsmen, he was invested with Schleswig in 1253, and his short rule was spent warring against the king. He died in 1257, leaving it to his brother Eric.

en:
Valdemar IV Eriksøn (c. 1262–1312) was Duke of Schleswig from 1283, the eldest son of Duke Eric I and Margaret. When his father died in 1272 Valdemar was only about ten, and Eric V of Denmark withheld the duchy for a decade until the Danehof meeting forced his installation in 1283.

The next year he granted city rights to Flensburg. He died in 1312 and was buried in Schleswig Cathedral, succeeded by his heir Eric II.

en:
Valdemar the Young (c. 1209–1231) was the only child of King Valdemar II of Denmark and his first queen, Dagmar of Bohemia. In 1215 he was made co-king beside his father, entrenching the new hereditary kingship, though he never reigned alone.

In 1223 he was seized together with his father by Count Henry of Schwerin during the hunt on Lyø and shared his captivity. On 28 November 1231 he was accidentally killed by an arrow while hunting at Refsnæs, dying before his father.

en:
Darmabala (1264–1292) was the second son of Crown Prince Zhenjin and grandson of Kublai Khan, wedded to Dagi. After Zhenjin's death in 1286 Kublai made him a likely heir with a command, though Marco Polo called him rickety. In 1291 Kublai sent him to govern Huaizhou, but he fell ill on the way, returned to Khanbaliq and died in 1292.

His sons Khayishan and Ayurbarwada both became Yuan emperors; Khayishan's accession in 1307 brought Darmabala posthumous honour as Emperor Shunzong.

答剌麻八剌（1264—1292）是太子真金的次子、忽必烈之孙，娶答己为妃。1286年真金死后，忽必烈视他为可能的继承人，授以兵权，马可·波罗却称他体弱。1291年，忽必烈派他出镇怀州，他途中病倒，返回大都后于1292年病逝。

他的两个儿子海山和爱育黎拔力八达后来都成为元朝皇帝；1307年海山即位，追尊答剌麻八剌为顺宗皇帝。

en:
Andrew Guigues (1184–1237), born André of Burgundy, was a son of Duke Hugh III of Burgundy and Béatrice of Albon, through whom he inherited the Dauphiné of Viennois in 1228, ruling as Dauphin Guigues VI. He enlarged his lands chiefly by diplomacy and patronage rather than war, founding the collegiate church of Saint-André in Grenoble, where he was buried.

He married Beatrice of Sabran in 1202 and divorced her in 1215. By his second wife, Beatrice of Montferrat, married in 1219, he left a son and heir, Guigues VII.

安德鲁·吉格（1184—1237）本名勃艮第的安德烈，是勃艮第公爵于格三世与贝娅特丽克丝·德·阿尔邦之子。他通过母系于1228年继承维埃努瓦多芬领地，称多芬吉格六世。他扩张领地主要依靠外交和庇护而非战争，并在格勒诺布尔创建圣安德烈协同教堂，身后即葬于此。

en:
Anne of Viennois (died 1299) was countess of Albon and Viennois, the daughter of Dauphin Guigues VII of Viennois. In 1273 she married Humbert, baron of La Tour-du-Pin.

When her brother John I died in a riding accident in 1282, Anne inherited the Dauphiné, which passed through her marriage to the House of La Tour-du-Pin, rulers of the Dauphiné for the next century. She bore nine children, including Dauphin John II, and was buried at Salette.

Beatrice of Montferrat (c. 1210–1274) was the eldest daughter of William VI, Marquess of Montferrat, and younger sister of Boniface II. In 1219, aged about nine, she married Guigues VI of Viennois, more than twenty years her senior.

When Guigues died in March 1237 she became regent for their young son Guigues VII, guiding his reign until 1243. The troubadour Gauseran de Saint-Leidier made her the idealised lady of his love songs.

en:
Béatrice of Albon (1161–1228) inherited Albon, Grenoble and the Dauphiné of Viennois as an infant on the death of her father Guigues V in 1162, with her grandmother Margaret acting as regent. Aged three she was married to Albéric Taillefer of Toulouse, who died without issue in 1183.

That year she married Hugh III, Duke of Burgundy, who ruled her lands and joined the Third Crusade, dying at Acre in 1192. Her son by Hugh, André, succeeded as Dauphin Guigues VI. She later married Hugh of Coligny and died at Vizille in 1228.

en:
Beatrice of Hungary (1290 – 1343 or 1354) was the elder daughter of Charles Martel of Anjou, titular King of Hungary, and Clemence of Habsburg, and sister of Charles I of Hungary. In 1296, aged six, she was married at Naples to the ten-years-older John II of Viennois, Dauphin of Viennois. She bore him two sons, Guigues VIII and Humbert II, both later dauphins.

After John died in 1319 she became a nun at Cîteaux, moving in 1340 to Saint-Just-de-Claix Abbey, which her son Humbert had founded for her. She died there in 1343 or 1354.

en:
Guigues I, called the Old (c.995–1070), was a minor noble of the Kingdom of Arles who founded the line of the counts of Albon, the future dauphins of Viennois. From lands first attested at Moirans in 1016, he built a domain between the Rhône and the Alps, later holding Oisans, Grésivaudan and the Briançonnais. His lands lay in the Kingdom of Arles, incorporated into the Holy Roman Empire in 1033.

He placed kinsmen in the bishoprics of Grenoble and Valence. With his wife Adelaide he had a son, Guigues II, and died a monk at Cluny about 1070.

吉格一世绰号“老者”（约995—约1070），是阿尔勒王国的小贵族，开创了阿尔邦伯爵家族，即后来维埃努瓦多芬的世系。1016年的特许状已记载他在穆瓦朗拥有地产；此后他在罗讷河与阿尔卑斯山之间建立领地，后来据有瓦桑、格雷西沃当和布里扬索内等地。他的领地位于阿尔勒王国境内，该国于1033年并入神圣罗马帝国。

他把亲族安插进格勒诺布尔和瓦朗斯的主教区。他与妻子阿德莱德生有一子吉格二世，最后在克吕尼出家为修士，约1070年卒于该地。

en:
Guigues II d'Albon, called the Fat (c. 1025–c. 1079), was a noble of the Kingdom of Arles and the son of Count Guigues I and Adelaide. Before 1052 he married Pétronille, who bore his heir Guigues III. His scattered estates ran from Albon and the Grésivaudan around Grenoble to the Briançonnais.

From 1070 he was styled count in the Grésivaudan and Briançonnais. He is first styled count of Albon in 1079 and died soon after.

en:
Guigues III, called the Old (c. 1050–1133), ruled as count of Albon from 1079, when the County of Vienne was split between him and Humbert I of Savoy. From the Grésivaudan north of Grenoble he long disputed church estates with Hugh of Châteauneuf, bishop of Grenoble. An accord in 1099 had Guigues return church lands, while Hugh recognised the count's authority around the city.

In 1095 he married Matilda. The 1129 partition of the Viennois with Amadeus III of Savoy enlarged his lands, and on his death in 1133 his son Guigues IV inherited the county.

en:
Guigues IV, called le Dauphin, was count of Albon from 1133. The eldest son of Guigues III and Matilda, he was the first of his family to bear the name Dauphin, which became the title of the Viennois rulers. He married Margaret, daughter of Count Stephen I of Burgundy.

In 1140 the first war broke out between Albon and Savoy, probably over his sister's dowry. Guigues invaded Savoy and besieged Montmélian, but was ambushed and wounded near La Buissière, dying on 28 June 1142. His son Guigues V succeeded him.

en:
Guigues V (c.1125–1162), count of Albon and Grenoble from 1142, was the first to take the title Dauphin du Viennois. He succeeded his father Guigues IV as a minor under his mother Margaret's regency until 1153.

Seeking to avenge his father, killed besieging Montmélian, he renewed the war with Savoy until Humbert III's relief army drove him off. In 1155 at Rivoli he did homage to Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, who confirmed his lands.

The emperor also granted him minting rights at Râme and Cesana. He died at Vizille on 29 July 1162, leaving a daughter, Beatrice.

Guigues VII (1225–1269) succeeded his father Andrew Guigues VI as dauphin of Viennois in 1237, initially under the guidance of his mother Beatrice of Montferrat.

He disputed the counties of Embrun and Gap, the dowry of his father's first wife, with Charles of Anjou until a compromise left him Embrun while Charles took Gap.

In 1253 he married Beatrice of Savoy, whose dowry brought him Faucigny, an enclave bordering Savoy that drew his successors into repeated wars. He was succeeded by his son John I, then by his daughter Anne, wife of Humbert de la Tour du Pin.

en:
Guigues VIII (1309–1333) succeeded his father John II as dauphin of Viennois in 1318, under the regency of his uncle Henri, bishop-elect of Metz, until 1323. In 1323 he married Isabelle, daughter of Philip V of France, strengthening French influence in his lands.

A bold soldier, Guigues won a victory over the Savoyards at the Battle of Varey in 1325, and in 1328 fought under Philip VI at the Battle of Cassel against the Flemings. He was killed in 1333 besieging the Savoyard castle of La Perrière, and was buried in Grenoble, leaving the Dauphiné to his brother Humbert II.

en:
Henri de la Tour du Pin (1296–1328), also called Henri Dauphin, was the fourth son of Humbert I, Dauphin of Viennois, and Anne of Burgundy. Destined for the church but never ordained a priest, he became bishop of Passau in 1317 and was named bishop of Metz by Pope John XXII in 1319. From 1319 to 1323 he ruled the Dauphiné as regent for his nephew Guigues VIII.

His constant demands for money angered the people of Metz, and in 1325 he resigned his see, returned to lay life, and died in 1328.

en:
Humbert I (c.1240–1307), baron of La Tour-du-Pin, married Anne, daughter of Dauphin Guigues VII, in 1273, and from 1282 ruled the Dauphiné of Viennois in her right.

The union cut the Savoyard lands in two and brought war with Count Philip I of Savoy. He later ambushed and routed Amadeus V near Barraux.

In 1294 he became a vassal of King Philip IV of France in exchange for an annual pension, preparing the later French annexation of the Dauphiné. He died in April 1307, leaving the Dauphiné to his son John II.

en:
Humbert II (1312–1355), the last dauphin of Viennois, was abroad in Hungary and Naples when he was recalled in 1333 to replace his brother Guigues VIII, killed assaulting a castle. His lavish court outran his means, yet he was a notable administrator: the Conseil delphinal in 1337, Grenoble University in 1339, and in 1343 the Charter of the Escartons, which gave the Briançonnais self-rule.

After his only son André died in 1335 he tried to sell his lands, and in 1345 led a papal crusade to relieve Smyrna, beating the Turks before returning ruined in 1347.

By the Treaty of Romans in 1349 he sold the Dauphiné to Philip VI and invested the king's grandson Charles, the first French dauphin. Humbert became a Dominican and Latin patriarch of Alexandria, and died in 1355.

安贝尔二世（1312—1355）是末代维埃努瓦多芬。1333年，他还在匈牙利和那不勒斯游历时就被召回，接替攻城时阵亡的兄长吉格八世。他的奢华宫廷入不敷出，却是出色的行政者：1337年设立多芬会议，1339年创办格勒诺布尔大学，1343年颁布《埃斯卡尔通宪章》，授予布里扬索内自治权。

1349年，他通过《罗芒条约》将多菲内卖给法王腓力六世，并为法王的孙子查理授封，查理成为第一位法国多芬。此后安贝尔加入多明我会，任拉丁礼亚历山大宗主教，1355年去世。

John I (1264–1282) was dauphin of Viennois and count of Albon from 1269, succeeding his father Guigues VII when he was only five. His mother Béatrice of Faucigny ruled as regent, and a 1270 convention named Duke Robert II of Burgundy as his tutor.

When his mother married Gaston VII of Béarn in 1273, Robert became regent of the Dauphiné. John died in 1282 after a fall from his horse, aged eighteen and without an heir, so his lands passed to his sister Anne.

en:
John II (1280–1319) succeeded his father Humbert I as dauphin of Viennois in 1306. In 1296 he married Beatrice of Hungary, daughter of Charles Martel, titular king of Hungary; their sons Guigues VIII and Humbert II both became dauphin.

His reign was dominated by rivalry with the counts of Savoy: he secured the frontier by chartering walled towns at La Buissière and Avalon, offering settlers land and rights in return for maintaining walls. He made peace with Count Amadeus V in 1314, but war resumed in 1318. John died on 5 March 1319 at Pont de Sorgues near Avignon, returning from the papal court.

en:
David Hume (1711–1776) was a Scottish philosopher, historian and essayist, born David Home in Edinburgh, whose empiricism and scepticism reshaped European thought. At twenty-five he went to La Flèche in Anjou and wrote A Treatise of Human Nature in the Jesuit college's library (1739–1740).

It argued that all ideas derive from impressions and causal belief rests on custom. In 1745 an atheism petition by Edinburgh ministers cost him a university chair. He recast his arguments in two Enquiries (1748, 1751), and from 1752 wrote the six-volume History of England (1754–1762), which became the standard English history for decades.

After serving as embassy secretary in Paris in 1763–1765, he brought Rousseau to England in 1766, where they quarrelled and parted. Kant said Hume had woken him from his dogmatic slumbers. Hume died of abdominal cancer in 1776.

大卫·休谟（1711—1776）是苏格兰哲学家、历史学家和散文家，原姓霍姆，生于爱丁堡，他的经验主义和怀疑论重塑了欧洲思想。二十五岁时他前往安茹的拉弗莱什，在耶稣会学院的藏书室里写成《人性论》（1739—1740年出版）。

该书主张一切观念来自印象、因果信念建立在习惯之上。1745年爱丁堡牧师指控他无神论的请愿使他丢掉大学教席。他把论点改写为两部《研究》（1748、1751年），1752年起写成六卷本《英格兰史》（1754—1762年），此后几十年一直是英国史的标准读本。

1763至1765年他在巴黎大使馆任秘书，1766年他陪卢梭前往英国，两人在那里争吵失和。康德称休谟把自己从教条主义的迷梦中唤醒。休谟1776年死于腹部癌症。

en:
Vijayabahu V, also called Savulu Vijayabahu, was the last king of Dambadeniya in fourteenth-century Sri Lanka. A son of Chandrabhanu, he succeeded Bhuvanaikabahu III in 1325 or 1326 and kept his capital at Kurunegala.

His reign ended in 1344 or 1345, when Bhuvanaikabahu IV succeeded him and the seat of power moved to Gampola. The Arab traveller Ibn Battuta visited the island's northern port of Puttalam either late in his predecessor's reign or early in his own.

维阇耶巴忽五世（别称萨乌鲁·维阇耶巴忽）是14世纪斯里兰卡丹巴德尼亚王国的末代国王，旃陀罗巴忽之子。他于1325/1326年继布伐奈迦巴忽三世即位，定都库鲁内加拉。

1344/1345年他的统治结束，布伐奈迦巴忽四世继位，权力中心随之转到甘波罗。阿拉伯旅行家伊本·白图泰在其前任统治末年或其本人统治初年到访岛屿北部的普塔勒姆港。

Ahmed Shihabuddine was Sultan of the Maldives from 1341 to 1347, succeeding his father Sultan Omar I. His reign ended in 1347 when his elder sister Khadijah deposed him and seized the throne.

He was banished to Haddhunmathi Atoll, where he was assassinated. With him gone, Khadijah became the first woman to rule the Theemuge dynasty and held power for most of the next thirty years.

艾哈迈德·希哈卜丁是马尔代夫苏丹，1341年继承父亲奥马尔一世之位，统治至1347年。他在位末期，姐姐哈迪杰将他废黜并夺取王位。

他被流放至哈敦马蒂环礁，并在那里遇刺身亡。他死后，哈迪杰成为提穆格王朝第一位女性统治者，并在此后近三十年间大体掌握政权。

en:
Khadijah (died 1379 or 1380) was Sultana regnant of the Maldives and the eldest daughter of Sultan Omar I. In 1347 she deposed and had her brother Sultan Ahmed Shihabuddine assassinated and seized the throne, the first woman to rule the Theemuge dynasty.

Deposed by her vizier-husband Muhammad el-Jameel around 1363, she soon had him killed and ruled again, then lost power to a second husband, Abdullah I, before assassinating him in 1376 and beginning her third reign. She ruled for nearly thirty years. She was succeeded by her sister Raadhafathi.

哈迪杰（？—1379或1380年）是马尔代夫女苏丹，奥马尔一世的长女。1347年，她废黜并派人刺杀兄长艾哈迈德·希哈卜丁苏丹，自立为王，成为提穆格王朝第一位女性统治者。

en:
Omar I was Sultan of the Maldives from 1306 until his death in 1341, succeeding his father Sultan Salis. The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta records that Salis was a Bengali who founded a new ruling dynasty.

Omar ruled the islands for thirty-five years and was succeeded on his death by his son Ahmed Shihabuddine. His two daughters, Khadijah and Raadhafathi, also later took the throne, so that all three of his children ruled the Maldives.

奥马尔一世（？—1341）是马尔代夫苏丹，1306年继承父亲苏丹萨利斯之位。摩洛哥旅行家伊本·白图泰记载，萨利斯来自孟加拉，开创了新的统治王朝。

奥马尔统治群岛三十五年，1341年去世后由儿子艾哈迈德·希哈卜丁继位。他的两个女儿哈迪杰和拉达法蒂后来也相继登位，三个子女都成了马尔代夫的君主。

en:
Raadhafathi was Sultana regnant of the Maldives from 1379 or 1380 to 1383, the third daughter of Sultan Omar I and a younger sister of the long-ruling Khadijah.

She ascended after Khadijah's death, and her husband Mohamed of Maakurath directed affairs as her vizier. On her death in 1383 Mohamed took the throne himself, succeeding his wife as ruler of the islands.

en:
Devapaladeva, also called Deda or Dedu, was a Guhila Maharawal of the Vagad region, ruling from Baroda, the early capital of the Dungarpur line, known in Sanskrit as Vatapadraka.

A Sanskrit inscription dated 1287 from his successor Virasimhadeva names him as the previous maharajakula of Vatapadraka and records a grant of land made for the spiritual welfare of the dead Devapaladeva.

德奥帕利·提乌（梵语作提婆波罗提婆，又名德达或德杜）是婆迦尔地区的古希拉罗瓦尔，以栋格尔布尔支系的早期都城巴罗达（梵语称瓦塔帕德拉卡）为治所。

继任者维尔辛哈·提乌在1287年的一篇梵语铭文中称他为瓦塔帕德拉卡的前任罗瓦尔，并记载了为已故的德奥帕利祈求冥福而施舍土地之事。

en:
Samantasimha was a Guhila ruler of Mewar in the later twelfth century, succeeding his father Kshemasimha. After the death of the Chaulukya king Kumarapala of Gujarat he invaded Gujarat, but the Chahamana chief Kirtipala drove him from Mewar.

He withdrew to Vagad and founded a new Guhila principality there in 1177, with its seat at Baroda, the nucleus of Dungarpur. He later joined Prithviraja III of Ajmer and may have fallen fighting at the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192.

萨曼塔辛哈是12世纪后期梅瓦尔的古希拉首领，继父亲克谢马辛哈之位。古吉拉特的乔卢基国王库马拉波罗死后，他入侵古吉拉特，随后被查哈马纳首领基尔蒂波罗逐出梅瓦尔。

他退入婆迦尔，于1177年在当地建立新的古希拉政权，都城设在巴罗达，成为栋格尔布尔的雏形。后来他投奔阿杰梅尔的普利色毗罗阇三世，可能在1192年的第二次塔拉因战役中阵亡。

Sinhat Deo, recorded in inscriptions as Sihadadeva, was a Rawal of Vagad in the thirteenth century. An inscription at Jagat bears his name in 1220.

Another, dated 1234, records that Vaja, son of Mahilana, rebuilt a temple of the goddess Vindhyavasini at Vinjhalpur while Sihadadeva ruled at Vatapadraka, or Baroda. His son Jayasimghadeva is named in an inscription of 1249.

en:
Virasimhadeva was a Guhila Maharawal of Vagad in the Dungarpur line, ruling from its early capital Baroda. Sanskrit inscriptions style him maharajakula of Vatapadraka; the earliest, dated 1287, records a land grant for his predecessor Devapaladeva, and the last is dated 1302.

Later tradition holds that he killed Dungaria, an independent Bhil chieftain, and founded the town named after him, Dungarpur. His grandson Dungarasimha, who gave the state its name, succeeded him as Rawal.

en:
Al-Mughith ibn al-Faiz was a sultan of Dhofar and a kinsman of the ruler of Yemen. His father al-Faiz had governed Dhofar on the Yemeni ruler’s behalf and sent him a yearly gift, but Al-Mughith ruled in his own right and stopped sending it. The ruler of Yemen planned to fight him, but abandoned the attempt after his appointed commander was killed by a falling wall.

His palace stood opposite the great mosque. Musicians played at its gate each afternoon, and troops assembled twice a week.

穆吉斯·本·法伊兹是佐法尔苏丹，也是也门统治者的堂亲。他的父亲法伊兹曾代表也门统治者治理佐法尔，每年向其进献礼物；穆吉斯自行统治后停止了进献。也门统治者打算征讨他，但所任命的统帅被倒塌的墙压死后，便放弃了计划。

他的宫殿位于大清真寺对面。每天下午，乐师在宫门前演奏，军队每周两次在门前集结。

en:
Al-Wathiq Ibrahim, formally Abu'l-Muzaffar Ibrahim Nur al-Din, was a Rasulid prince of Yemen, a son of Sultan al-Muzaffar Yusuf I. Born in 1261, he studied Islamic jurisprudence and grammar. In 1284 his father made him governor of Sanaa, and he was later posted to Fashal.

In 1293 the sultan enfeoffed him with Dhofar in southern Arabia, where he settled and ruled the frankincense-producing region until his death in 1311 or 1312. His sons kept Dhofar as a hereditary appanage.

瓦西格·易卜拉欣，全名阿布·穆扎法尔·易卜拉欣·努尔丁，是也门拉苏勒王朝苏丹穆扎法尔·优素福一世之子。他生于1261年，曾研习伊斯兰教法与语法。1284年，父亲任命他为萨那总督，后来又出镇费沙勒。

en:
Richard de Bury (1287–1345), born Richard Aungerville near Bury St Edmunds, was an English churchman, royal servant and book collector. He tutored the future Edward III and, after Edward's accession, rose to be Lord Privy Seal and twice ambassador to the papal court at Avignon, where he met Petrarch in 1330.

In 1333 he was made Bishop of Durham, and later served as Lord Chancellor. His Latin treatise Philobiblon, completed before his death in 1345, celebrates the love and care of books.

理查德·德·伯里（1287—1345），生于贝里圣埃德蒙兹附近，本名理查德·昂格维尔，是英格兰教士、王室官员与藏书家。他曾任后来的爱德华三世的师傅，爱德华三世上台后官至掌玺大臣，并两度出使阿维尼翁教廷，1330年在那里结识彼特拉克。

1333年他被任命为达勒姆主教，后又出任大法官。他用拉丁文写成的《书之爱》在1345年去世前夕完成，通篇畅谈对书籍的热爱与护惜。
