en:
Gerhard VI (c. 1298–1343) was Count of Diez, a small county in the Lahn valley known to contemporaries as the Golden County. The son of Count Gottfried III, who was judged unfit to rule, he governed Diez from 1332 during his father's long incapacity.

He married Jutta of Nassau-Hadamar, who bore his successor Gerhard VII. Gerhard was killed on 17 October 1343 in a feud against the nearby city of Limburg, and was the penultimate count of the Diez line.

en:
Gerhard VII was the last Count of Diez, succeeding his father Gerhard VI after the latter was killed fighting Limburg in 1343. His family's influence had declined since the fall of the Hohenstaufen dynasty, and by Gerhard's time the once Golden County had been heavily pledged to creditors to settle debts.

He married Gertrud of Westerburg, and their daughter Jutta became his heiress. When Gerhard died in 1388 without a male heir, the County of Diez passed through Jutta to her husband, Adolf I, Count of Nassau-Siegen, ending Diez rule.

en:
Firuz Shah Tughlaq (1309–1388) became sultan of Delhi in 1351 after the death of his cousin Muhammad bin Tughluq. The son of Sipahsalar Rajab and a Punjabi Hindu princess, he had been raised by his uncle Ghiyath al-Din.

His long reign brought campaigns in Bengal, Odisha, Kangra and Thatta, but he is best remembered as a builder: he founded Hisar, Fatehabad, Firozabad and Jaunpur and dug irrigation canals. He abdicated in 1387 and died in 1388 after a rule of thirty-seven years.

菲鲁兹沙·图格鲁克（1309—1388）在1351年堂兄穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克死后成为德里苏丹。他是军元帅拉杰卜与旁遮普印度教公主之子，由伯父吉亚斯丁抚养。

他长期在位，曾出征孟加拉、奥里萨、坎格拉和特达，但最以营建闻名：兴建希萨尔、法塔哈巴德、菲罗扎巴德和江布尔，并开凿灌溉渠。他于1387年退位，1388年去世，在位37年。

en:
Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, born Ghazi Malik, was the founder and first sultan of the Tughluq dynasty, ruling Delhi from 1320 until his death. Of humble Qara'unas origin, he rose under the Khaljis and helped defeat the Mongols at Amroha in 1305. After the Khalji collapse he took Delhi in 1320 and built the fortress city of Tughlaqabad.

His son Muhammad overthrew the Kakatiyas of Warangal in 1323, and the 1324 Bengal campaign made West Bengal tributary and annexed the east. In February 1325 a pavilion collapsed on him at Kara; Ibn Battuta suspected murder.

吉亚斯丁·图格鲁克原名加齐·马利克，是图格鲁克王朝的开创者与第一代苏丹，1320年起统治德里直至去世。他出身卑微的喀喇乌那斯部族，在卡尔吉王朝下发迹，1305年参与在阿姆罗哈击败蒙古人。卡尔吉王朝崩溃后，他于1320年夺取德里，兴建城堡城市图格鲁克巴德。

1323年，其子穆罕默德攻灭瓦朗加尔的卡卡蒂亚王朝；1324年的孟加拉之役使西孟加拉称臣、东孟加拉被吞并。1325年2月，他在卡拉因一座亭子坍塌而死，伊本·白图泰怀疑他是被谋害的。

en:
Razia Sultana (c. 1205–1240) was the only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate and the first female Muslim ruler of the subcontinent. Eldest daughter of Iltutmish, a Turkic slave, she governed Delhi in 1231–1232 while he campaigned at Gwalior. A chronicler says he named her his heir, but the nobles raised her half-brother Ruknuddin Firuz instead, whose mother Shah Turkan ruled in his name.

In 1236, as Ruknuddin marched against rebels and Shah Turkan plotted her death, Razia roused the people at prayer; a mob seized the palace and the army placed her on the throne. She put down a Shia rising and retook Gwalior, but Turkic nobles resented her non-Turkic officers.

In April 1240 they deposed her and rebel Altunia arrested her. She married him in September and marched on Delhi, but on 14 October was defeated by her half-brother Muizuddin Bahram and killed by her captors.

拉齐娅苏丹（约1205—1240）是德里苏丹国唯一的女性统治者，也是南亚第一位穆斯林女君主。她是伊勒杜迷失（突厥奴隶出身）的长女，1231至1232年父亲远征瓜廖尔期间主持德里政务。有史家记载伊勒杜迷失指定她为继承人，但贵族们拥立异母兄弟鲁克丁·菲鲁兹，其母沙·图尔坎代为掌权。

1236年鲁克丁平叛，沙·图尔坎图谋处死她，拉齐娅在聚礼祈祷中鼓动民众，暴民攻占王宫，军队推她上位。她镇压了一场什叶派起事并收复瓜廖尔，但突厥贵族不满她重用非突厥裔官员。

1240年4月贵族将她废黜，起兵的阿尔图尼亚将她俘获。她9月嫁给阿尔图尼亚并进军德里，10月14日被异母兄弟穆伊兹丁·巴赫拉姆击败，被俘遇害。

en:
Muhammad bin Tughluq (1290–1351) was Sultan of Delhi from 1325, eldest son of Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, founder of the Tughlaq dynasty. Sent to the Deccan, he took the Kakatiya capital Warangal in 1323, ending that dynasty.

As sultan he moved the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad in 1327 to rule from a safer central place; many of those ordered south died on the road, and after a revolt and plague he moved it back to Delhi in 1335. In 1330 he issued brass and copper tokens valued as silver, but forgers flooded the markets and the scheme collapsed, while a 1333 campaign into Kumaon lost nearly all its 100,000 men.

Versed in philosophy, mathematics and medicine as well as a calligrapher, he was later nicknamed the Wisest Fool. Under him the sultanate fell apart as Vijayanagara and the Bahmani Sultanate broke away in the south. He died in 1351 on campaign in Sindh.

穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克（1290—1351）1325年起为德里苏丹，是王朝创建者吉亚斯丁·图格鲁克的长子。他被派往德干，1323年攻陷卡卡提亚王朝都城瓦朗加尔，灭亡该王朝。

即位后，他于1327年把首都从德里迁往道拉塔巴德，以便居中统辖南北、躲避劫掠；许多被命令南迁的人死在路上，经历叛乱和瘟疫后于1335年迁回德里。1330年他发行与银币等值的黄铜和铜质代用币，却因私铸成风、假币充斥而失败；1333年库马盎一役，十万大军几乎全军覆没。

他精通哲学、数学和医学，还是书法家，后世称他为“最聪明的蠢人”。他治下苏丹国开始崩解，南方先后出现毗奢耶那伽罗和巴赫马尼苏丹国。1351年，他在信德征战途中去世。

en:
Qutb ud-Din Aibak (c. 1150–1210) was a Turkic slave-general of the Ghurid sultan Muhammad of Ghor who laid the foundations of the Delhi Sultanate. Sold young to a qazi in Nishapur, he was resold to Muhammad at Ghazni and became stable-master.

After victory over Prithviraja III at Tarain in 1192, he took charge of Indian lands. He took Delhi that year, deposed its local vassal in 1193 and forced Kalinjar fortress to terms in 1202.

After Muhammad's assassination in 1206, Lahore called him to power, and in 1208–1209 Mahmud recognised him as ruler of Hindustan. His generosity earned him the epithet lakh-bakhsh, and he founded the Qutb Minar in Delhi. In 1210 he died at Lahore after a fall at polo, the saddle pommel piercing his ribs. He named no heir; his former slave and son-in-law Iltutmish took the throne and made the Ghurid lands the Delhi Sultanate.

库特布丁·艾伊拜克（约1150—1210）是古尔苏丹穆罕默德麾下的突厥裔奴隶将领，也是德里苏丹国的奠基人。他幼年在尼沙布尔被卡迪买下，后转卖给加兹尼的穆罕默德，升任马厩长。

1192年塔拉因战役战胜普利特维拉贾三世后，穆罕默德委他统管印度领地。他当年攻占德里，1193年废黜当地附庸，1202年迫使坎林杰尔要塞议和。

1206年穆罕默德遇刺后，拉合尔请他执政；1208—1209年马哈茂德承认他为印度斯坦统治者。他因慷慨得号“拉克巴赫什”，并兴建德里的顾特卜塔。1210年他在拉合尔打马球坠马，鞍桥刺穿肋骨而死。他未指定继承人，从前的奴隶兼女婿伊勒图特米什随后继位，建立德里苏丹国。

Boris Davydovich was a Rurikid prince, a son of Davyd Konstantinovich of Galich and Dmitrov and grandnephew of Alexander Nevsky. In 1280, after his uncle Vasily Konstantinovich died, the family principality was divided: his elder brother Fyodor took Galich and Boris received Dmitrov as his appanage.

He ruled Dmitrov for more than half a century and died in the Golden Horde in 1334, after which his son Dmitry probably succeeded him.

鲍里斯·达维多维奇是留里克家族王公，加利奇-德米特罗夫王公达维德·康斯坦丁诺维奇之子、亚历山大·涅夫斯基的侄孙。1280年叔父瓦西里·康斯坦丁诺维奇去世后，家族公国被瓜分：兄长费奥多尔分得加利奇，鲍里斯分得德米特罗夫为封邑。

他统治德米特罗夫半个多世纪，1334年死于金帐汗国，此后可能由其子德米特里继位。

en:
Dmitry Borisovich was the second prince of Dmitrov, succeeding his father Boris, the first known prince of the town, after 1334. Around 1360 Moscow absorbed Dmitrov, but the Golden Horde secured him the throne of Galich.

In 1363 he supported Dmitry Konstantinovich of Suzdal against Dmitry Ivanovich of Moscow in their struggle for the grand principality of Vladimir. That same year the prince of Galich was expelled from his inheritance, and Moscow annexed the town and its surrounding lands.

en:
John FitzThomas, 1st Baron Desmond (died 1261), was a Norman-Irish magnate and head of the Desmond line of the FitzGerald dynasty, the son of Thomas FitzMaurice. In 1259 he received a royal grant of Desmond and west Waterford, provoking Fineen MacCarthy, King of Desmond, who gathered the Gaelic clans against him.

At the Battle of Callann in July 1261 the Gaelic army routed the Normans, and John was killed together with his son Maurice FitzJohn. His infant grandson Thomas inherited the barony.

Maurice FitzThomas FitzGerald, called Maurice the Great (1293–1356), was an Anglo-Irish magnate who succeeded as Baron Desmond in 1307 and was created 1st Earl of Desmond in 1329. In 1331 the Crown imprisoned him amid rumours that he meant to make himself king of Ireland.

In 1345 he led an open rebellion of Anglo-Irish lords until he surrendered and forfeited his lands. Pardoned in 1349, he was made Lord Justice of Ireland for life in July 1355 and died in Dublin Castle the following January.

Maurice FitzMaurice FitzGerald, called Maurice Óg or young Maurice (died 1358), was the only son of Maurice FitzGerald, 1st Earl of Desmond, by his first wife Catherine de Burgh. He succeeded his father as 2nd Earl of Desmond in January 1356.

He married Beatrice de Stafford but left no male heirs. He died at Castle Maine in 1358 and was buried at Tralee Abbey, the earldom passing to his half-brother Gerald, called the Poet.

Thomas FitzGerald, 2nd Baron Desmond (c. 1261–1298), inherited the title in infancy after his father Maurice FitzJohn and grandfather John FitzThomas were killed at the Battle of Callann in 1261; only after a long minority did he enter his lands in 1282.

Family legend nicknamed him Thomas an-Apa, the ape, after an ape carried the baby along the battlements of Traly monastery and brought him safely back. In 1294 he served as deputy justiciar of Ireland and in 1295 was summoned to Parliament. He died in 1298 and was buried at North Abbey in Youghal.

en:
Domenico Ghirlandaio (1448–1494), born Domenico Bigordi in Florence, was a leading painter of the Florentine Renaissance. His early fame came from the Santa Fina chapel frescoes at San Gimignano (1477–1478), and in 1481 Pope Sixtus IV summoned him to Rome to paint the Vocation of the Apostles in the new Sistine Chapel.

Back in Florence he completed the Sassetti Chapel cycle in Santa Trinita (1482–1485) and the Tornabuoni Chapel in Santa Maria Novella (1485–1490), crowded with portraits of Medici Florence. His large workshop trained Michelangelo, and he died of pestilential fever in January 1494.

多梅尼科·吉兰达约（1448—1494）出生于佛罗伦萨，原名多梅尼科·比戈尔迪，是佛罗伦萨文艺复兴的重要画家。他早年因1477至1478年在圣吉米尼亚诺绘制圣菲纳礼拜堂湿壁画成名，1481年教宗西斯都四世召他前往罗马，在新建的西斯廷礼拜堂绘制《使徒蒙召》。

回到佛罗伦萨后，他于1482至1485年完成圣三一教堂萨塞蒂礼拜堂的壁画组画，又在1485至1490年完成新圣母教堂托尔纳布奥尼礼拜堂的壁画，其中画满了美第奇时代佛罗伦萨名流的肖像。他的庞大作坊培养出了米开朗琪罗，1494年1月死于瘟疫般的热病。

Jutta of Oldenburg-Delmenhorst, born before 1291, was a daughter of Count Otto II of Oldenburg-Delmenhorst and his wife Oda, called countess of Sternberg. Before 1321 she married Rudolf III, Lord of Diepholz, and is last documented alive in 1331.

She bore Rudolf six children: her eldest son Conrad VI succeeded as lord of Diepholz and died in 1379; two other sons held cathedral canonries, and her daughters Adelheid and Mechthild both entered religious life.

Conrad V, numbered Conrad I in some genealogies, was Lord of Diepholz, the son of Lord John I of Diepholz and Hedwig of Roden and grandson of Kuno III. He married Hedwig of Rietberg, daughter of Count Conrad I of Rietberg.

On 15 September 1298 their daughter Hedwig married Count John II of Oldenburg. Their son Rudolf III, born around 1300, succeeded as Lord of Diepholz and was still alive after 1350. Conrad died after 1302.

The expedition stopped in Cyprus, and John died there at Nicosia before reaching the fighting. In 1240 he had married Marie of Bourbon, daughter of Archambaud VIII of Bourbon; their son Robert IV succeeded him.

en:
John II of Dreux, called the Good (1265–1309), succeeded his father Robert IV as Count of Dreux in 1282. Under Philip IV the Fair he served in the long Flemish wars: he took Furnes, Cassel and Lille in 1297, survived Courtrai in 1302, and fought at Mons-en-Pévèle and the siege of Lille in 1304, then helped negotiate peace with Flanders.

In 1292 he married Jeanne of Beaujeu, lady of Montpensier. She bore him three successive counts, Robert V, John III and Peter I.

Peter I of Dreux (1298–1345) was the youngest son of Count John II and Jeanne of Beaujeu, and inherited her lordship of Montpensier. In 1328 he fought for Philip VI against the Flemish rebels at Cassel. The county of Dreux came to him only in 1331, after his elder brothers Robert V and John III had both died without heirs.

In 1341 he married Isabeau of Melun. He died on 3 November 1345; his infant daughter Joan died the next year, and the county passed to his sister Joan II.

en:
Robert I of Dreux, called the Great (c. 1123–1188), was the fifth son of King Louis VI of France and Adelaide of Savoy. In 1137 his brother Louis VII granted him the county of Dreux as an appanage. He joined the Second Crusade in 1147, fighting at the failed siege of Damascus, then returned early and plotted against Louis VII, a conspiracy checked by Abbot Suger.

In 1152 his marriage to Agnes of Baudement brought him Braine and other lordships. He chartered Dreux in 1180, founded Brie-Comte-Robert, and ceded his county to his son in 1184.

en:
Robert II of Dreux, called the Young (c. 1154–1218), succeeded his father Robert I as Count of Dreux in 1184. He took the cross with Philip Augustus in 1190 and fought at the siege of Acre and the battle of Arsuf on the Third Crusade. Back in France he campaigned against the English and in Normandy.

He joined the Albigensian Crusade in 1209, serving at the siege of Termes, and commanded the left wing of the army at the victory of Bouvines in 1214. By his wife Yolande of Coucy he left sons Robert III and Peter Mauclerc, later Duke of Brittany.

罗贝尔二世（约1154—1218），绰号“年轻者”，1184年继父罗贝尔一世成为德勒伯爵。1190年他随腓力·奥古斯都参加第三次十字军东征，参与阿卡围城战和阿尔苏夫战役。回国后他与英格兰人作战、转战诺曼底。

en:
Robert III of Dreux, called Gasteblé or Wheat-Spoiler (1185–1234), was Count of Dreux and Braine and the eldest son of Robert II and Yolande of Coucy. His nickname came from a youthful hunt when he destroyed a field of wheat. In 1212 he fought under Prince Louis against the English, defending Nantes until he was captured; after Bouvines he was exchanged for the Earl of Salisbury.

He joined the Albigensian Crusade at the siege of Avignon in 1226. He was buried in the family necropolis at Braine in 1234.

罗贝尔三世（1185—1234），绰号“毁麦者”，是德勒和布赖讷伯爵，也是罗贝尔二世与库西的约兰德的长子。他的绰号来自年轻时一次狩猎：他毁坏了一片麦田。1212年，他在路易王子麾下与英格兰人作战，守卫南特时被俘；布汶战役后，他以索尔兹伯里伯爵为交换获释。

1226年他参加阿尔比十字军，围攻阿维尼翁。1234年，他被安葬在布赖讷的家族墓地。

Robert IV of Dreux (1241–1282), son of John I and Marie of Bourbon, held the counties of Dreux and Braine and, through his wife, Montfort-l'Amaury. In 1260 he married Beatrice, heiress of Count John I of Montfort, joining the Montfort inheritance to his own lands.

He campaigned with King Philip III the Bold in Languedoc in 1272. His daughter Yolande married King Alexander III of Scotland, and on his death in 1282 his son John II succeeded him as count.

zh:
罗贝尔四世（1241—1282）是约翰一世与波旁的玛丽之子，领有德勒、布赖讷伯国，并因妻子而领有蒙福尔拉莫里。1260年，他娶蒙福尔伯爵约翰一世的女继承人比阿特丽丝，把蒙福尔的遗产并入自己的领地。

1272年，他随国王腓力三世（勇敢者）出征朗格多克。其女约朗德嫁给苏格兰国王亚历山大三世；1282年罗贝尔去世后，其子约翰二世继位为伯爵。

en:
Robert V (1293–1329) was Count of Dreux and Braine, the eldest son of Count John II of Dreux and Jeanne of Beaujeu, lady of Montpensier. He succeeded his father in 1309 and supported King Philip V of France.

In April 1321 he married Marie, daughter of Walter II, lord of Enghien. Robert died at Braine without children, and his brother John III succeeded him as count.

en:
Simon de Dreux (c. 1300 – after 1326) was a younger son of John II, Count of Dreux, and Jeanne de Beaujeu, Lady of Montpensier. He entered the Church and became sub-dean of Chartres Cathedral, a title recorded for him in a charter of 1326.

Family settlement charters of 1318 and 1320 name him with his brothers Robert, John and Peter, and he was still living in 1326. He held no share of the county, while his three brothers succeeded one another as counts of Dreux.

en:
Bhuvanasimha was a Rana of the junior Guhila branch holding the village of Sisoda in Mewar, named in the genealogy preserved by the 1652 Eklingji inscription. A later inscription of Rana Kumbhakarna hails him as the conqueror of Sultan Alauddin Khalji.

Around 1299, when the Delhi army crossed Mewar on its march against Gujarat, a column raiding Guhila lands met fierce resistance, which Bhuvanasimha may have led as a feudatory of the Rawal Samarasimha. He was an ancestor of Maharana Hammir Singh.

en:
Lakhanasimha, also called Rana Laksha or Lakshman Singh, was Thakur of the village of Sisoda near Nathdwara in Mewar and a chief of the Guhila Rana branch, the son of Jayasimha.

When Alauddin Khalji besieged Chittorgarh in 1303, he led his sons into the garrison and died fighting to defend the fort after Rawal Ratnasimha abandoned the field. He and seven sons perished in the final saka while their women perished in jauhar. Through his son Arisimha he was grandfather of Hammir Singh.

zh:
拉卡纳辛哈又称拉纳·拉克沙或拉克什曼·辛格，是梅瓦尔纳特德瓦拉附近西索达村的塔库尔，也是古希罗拉纳支系的首领，为贾亚辛哈之子。

1303年阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉围攻奇托尔堡时，他率诸子加入守军；拉瓦尔·拉特纳辛哈离开战场后，拉卡纳辛哈战死守城。他与七个儿子在最后的萨卡殉死中阵亡，家中女眷则行乔哈尔自焚。其子阿里辛哈是哈米尔·辛格之父。

en:
Rahapa was the second son of Ranasimha, the Guhila rawal of Mewar, and founder of the dynasty's junior Rana branch. Around 1168, when the Guhila lands were divided between Ranasimha's sons, he established his base at the village of Sisoda near Nathdwara, after which his descendants were called Sisodias.

His son Narapati succeeded him. Through this line Rahapa was the ancestor of Hammir Singh, who re-established the dynasty's rule over Mewar in 1326.

拉哈帕是梅瓦尔古希拉拉瓦拉拉纳西姆哈的次子，也是古希拉拉纳幼支的开创者。约1168年古希拉领地在拉纳西姆哈诸子间分立时，他在纳特德瓦拉附近的锡索达村建立据点，后人遂以西索迪亚为姓。

en:
Ranasimha, also called Karna, was a Guhila rawal of Mewar during the later twelfth century. Succeeding his father Vikramsimha, he ruled from Chittor in about 1158–1168.

After his death his son Kshemasimha carried on the senior Rawal line, while his second son Rahapa founded the junior Rana branch from the village of Sisoda. From Rahapa descended the later Sisodia maharanas, and Ranasimha's name became the hereditary title Rana borne by that branch.

zh:
拉纳西姆哈又名卡尔纳，是12世纪后期梅瓦尔的古希拉拉瓦尔。他继承父亲维克拉姆辛哈之位，约1158—1168年以奇陶尔加尔为都。

他死后，其子克谢马辛哈延续拉瓦尔长支，次子拉哈帕则从锡索达村起家，另立拉纳幼支。后世的西索迪亚马哈拉那均出自拉哈帕一系，而拉纳西姆哈的名字也成为该支世代袭用的“拉纳”称号。

en:
Boris was prince of Drutsk from the 1180s until at least 1196, a ruler of the Polotsk branch of the Rurikids, possibly a son of Vseslav Rogvolodich.

In 1196 he joined the Chernigov princes and Prince Vasilko Volodarevich in a campaign against Vitebsk, then subject to Smolensk. In the battle that routed the Smolensk army, Boris struck from the rear, captured their commander Mstislav Romanovich, and handed him over to the ruler of Chernigov.

鲍里斯于1180年代至不早于1196年担任德鲁茨克王公，属留里克王朝波洛茨克支系，可能是弗谢斯拉夫·罗格沃洛多维奇之子。

1196年，他联合切尔尼戈夫诸王公与瓦西里科·沃洛达列维奇王公，出征当时依附斯摩棱斯克的维捷布斯克。在击溃斯摩棱斯克军队的战役中，鲍里斯自后方突袭，俘虏斯摩棱斯克统帅姆斯季斯拉夫·罗曼诺维奇，并将其交给切尔尼戈夫王公。

en:
Davyd Vseslavich (born between 1047 and 1057, died after 1129) was a son of Vseslav Briachislavich and prince of Polotsk in 1128–1129; he may also have ruled there in 1101–1127. In 1103 he joined Vladimir Monomakh in defeating the Polovtsians at Suteni.

In 1127 the Polotsk veche drove him out in favour of his nephew Rogvolod. After he refused Mstislav the Great's summons to a Polovtsian campaign in 1129, Mstislav's governors seized him; in 1130 he was exiled with his family to Byzantium, where he may have died.

达维德·弗谢斯拉维奇（生于1047—1057年间，1129年后卒）是弗谢斯拉夫·布里亚奇斯拉维奇之子，1128—1129年担任波洛茨克王公，也可能曾于1101—1127年统治该地。1103年，他随弗拉基米尔·莫诺马赫在苏捷尼击败波洛伏齐人。

1127年，波洛茨克市民大会将他驱逐，改立其侄罗格沃洛德。1129年他拒绝奉姆斯季斯拉夫大帝之召参加对波洛伏齐人的征战，姆斯季斯拉夫的将领随即将他擒获；1130年他合家被流放拜占庭，可能客死于该地。

Gleb Rogvolodich (died c. 1186) was a prince of Drutsk from the Polotsk branch of the Rurikids, son of Prince Rogvolod Borisovich, and may have ruled Drutsk as early as 1144–1151 and again in the 1170s and 1180s.

In 1180 he allied with Smolensk prince Davyd Rostislavich against the Chernigov princes. In 1181 Yaroslav Vsevolodovich and Igor Sviatoslavich besieged Davyd in Drutsk; after Davyd fled to Smolensk the attackers burned the outer town, and Gleb may have lost his throne.

1180年他与斯摩棱斯克王公达维德·罗斯季斯拉维奇结盟，对抗切尔尼戈夫诸王公。1181年，雅罗斯拉夫·弗谢沃洛多维奇与伊戈尔·斯维亚托斯拉维奇将达维德围困于德鲁茨克；达维德逃奔斯摩棱斯克后，联军焚毁外城，格列布可能因此失去公位。

en:
Gleb Rostislavich was the son of Rostislav Glebovich, prince of Minsk, and Sofia of Turov. When the Polotsk townsmen deposed Rogvolod Borisovich in 1151 and made his father prince of Polotsk, Gleb was installed in Rogvolod's ancestral town of Drutsk.

He ruled there until 1158, when pro-Rogvolod citizens drove him out as Rogvolod returned with an army granted in Chernigov, and his father's attempt to retake the town failed.

格列布·罗斯季斯拉维奇是明斯克王公罗斯季斯拉夫·格列波维奇与图罗夫的索菲娅之子。1151年波洛茨克市民驱逐罗格沃洛德·鲍里索维奇、迎立其父后，格列布被安插在罗格沃洛德的祖地德鲁茨克。

en:
Rogvolod, baptised Vasily and also called Rogvolod Borisovich (c. 1110 – after 1171), was the son of Rogvolod-Boris Vseslavich of the Drutsk line. He may have first received Drutsk in 1127, shared his family's exile to Byzantium after 1129, and returned in 1140.

He held Polotsk in 1144–1151 until the townsmen handed him to Rostislav of Minsk, regained Drutsk in 1158 and Polotsk in 1159, but lost the city after his defeat at Gorodets in 1162. The Rogvolod Stone of 1171 near Orsha preserves his name, and his son Gleb later ruled Drutsk.

en:
Roman Vseslavich (died c. 1114 or 1116) was a son of Vseslav Briachislavich, prince of Polotsk. After his father's death in 1101 he held an appanage in the Polotsk land, possibly Drutsk, which later genealogies name as his seat and where legend makes him the first prince.

He may have lost his domain in a family feud and died in exile, at Ryazan in 1114 or Murom in 1116. He died childless, and his widow took the veil in Polotsk, copying books and aiding the poor.

罗曼·弗谢斯拉维奇（约1114或1116年卒）是波洛茨克王公弗谢斯拉夫·布里亚奇斯拉维奇之子。1101年父亲死后，他在波洛茨克领地领有封邑，可能即德鲁茨克——后世的德鲁茨克王公谱系将他奉为当地首任王公。

他可能在家族内讧中失去封地，死于流亡途中，于1114年卒于梁赞或1116年卒于穆罗姆。他身后无嗣，遗孀在波洛茨克出家，以抄书济贫度日。

Qaim Khan was the son of Motay Rao Chauhan, Rajput ruler of Dadrewa. Around 1353 he and his brothers embraced Islam during the reign of Firuz Shah Tughlaq, and in 1359 the Sultan appointed him governor of Hisar Feroza with the title Khan-i Jahan.

He held the post under Mahmud Shah Tughlaq and the Sayyid ruler Khizr Khan. In 1419 Khizr Khan had him seized by treachery and killed on the banks of the Yamuna.

en:
Ghars al-Din Khalil Beg (d. 1386) was the second ruler of the Dulkadirid Turkoman principality, reigning from 1353. As a prince he took Elbistan from the rival chief Taraqlu and fought the Mamluks beside his father Qaraja.

He retook Harpoot in 1378 and allied with Kadi Burhan al-Din of Sivas. He married his heir Mehmed to Burhan al-Din's daughter. His raids around Aleppo prompted Sultan Barquq to incite Khalil's brother Ibrahim against him; he was killed in an ambush in April 1386 and succeeded by his brother Suli.

en:
Zayn al-Din Qaraja Beg (c. 1279–1353) was the Turkoman chieftain who founded the Dulkadirid principality in southern Anatolia. After his father's death he led the Bozok tribal confederation on the Mamluk frontier, and his rivalry with Taraqlu ended when Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad recognized him as client ruler of the Marash–Elbistan region in 1337.

As Mamluk power faltered he expanded and declared independence in 1348. The Mamluks captured and executed him in 1353. His son Khalil succeeded him.

As Mamluk power faltered he expanded and declared independence in 1348. The Mamluks captured and executed him in 1353. His son Khalil succeeded him.

Wirich II von Daun (c. 1251 – 14 April 1299) was a German nobleman of the Daun-Oberstein branch, lord of Nanstein and Oberstein-Landstuhl near Idar-Oberstein.

He married Kunigunde, daughter of Raugraf Heinrich I of Neuenbaumburg and sister of Emich I, bishop of Worms. Their son Heinrich III was elected bishop of Worms in 1318, while another son, Wirich III, carried on the family line.

en:
Duwa (died 1307), second son of Baraq, was made Chagatai khan by Kaidu in 1282 and became the khanate's longest-reigning ruler. For decades he joined Kaidu's wars against the Yuan, besieging Qocho in 1275 and taking Karakorum in 1289. In 1297 he sacked Lahore and installed his son Qutlugh Khwaja there.

Paralyzed by an arrow wound in 1301, he set Kaidu's son Chapar over the Ögedeids, made peace with the Yuan in 1303, and with Yuan support crushed Chapar by 1306, recovering lost lands. He died in 1307, and his son Könchek succeeded him.

en:
Heinrich V Schenk von Reicheneck (d. 1344) was Prince-Bishop of Eichstätt from 1329 to 1344. A canon of Regensburg, he fought for Frederick the Fair before Pope John XXII, whose loyal partisan he was, appointed him to Eichstätt in 1329.

He reconciled with Emperor Lewis the Bavarian in 1330 and received the regalia from him in 1334. For this the Pope excommunicated him. He reduced the bishopric's debts, and around 1340 walled the town of Herrieden. He died at Nuremberg in 1344 and was buried at Engelthal Abbey.

Abraham Darby (1677–1717) was an English Quaker ironmaster, born near Dudley in Staffordshire. After an apprenticeship in Birmingham, he settled in Bristol in 1699 and developed casting iron pots in sand moulds.

In 1709, at his Coalbrookdale furnace in Shropshire, he became the first to smelt pig iron successfully using coke instead of charcoal, a breakthrough that supplied cheap iron for the machinery, engines and bridges of the Industrial Revolution. He died at Madeley in 1717.

亚伯拉罕·达比（1677—1717）是英格兰贵格会的炼铁厂主，生于斯塔福德郡达德利附近。他在伯明翰学徒出师后，于1699年定居布里斯托尔，研发出以砂模铸造铁锅的工艺。

Sir Aymer de Strathbogie, also recorded as Adomar de Atholl, was the second son of David II Strathbogie, Earl of Atholl, and Joan Comyn. His father had rebelled against Robert the Bruce in 1307, lost his Scottish lands, and been compensated in England, where he became warden of Northumberland.

In 1324 his mother became co-heiress of her uncle Aymer de Valence, Earl of Pembroke, bringing Northumberland manors into the family. While his elder brother David upheld the claim to the earldom of Atholl as a leading supporter of Edward Balliol, Aymer made his life in England, holding Jesmond, Ponteland and Felton, and in 1381 was returned to parliament as Knight of the Shire for Northumberland.

He married Mary, said to be a daughter of Walter the Steward, and the couple were buried together in the chancel of St Andrew's church in Newcastle upon Tyne. He died on 14 April 1402.

艾马尔·德·斯特拉斯博吉爵士，史书又作阿多马尔·德·阿瑟尔，是阿瑟尔伯爵大卫二世·斯特拉斯博吉与琼·科明的次子。其父1307年起兵反抗罗伯特·布鲁斯，失去苏格兰的领地，在英格兰得到补偿，后来出任诺森伯兰守卫官。

1324年，其母与人共同继承舅父彭布罗克伯爵艾马尔·德·瓦朗斯的遗产，诺森伯兰若干地产由此归入家族。长兄大卫作为爱德华·巴里奥的主要支持者，继续坚持对阿瑟尔伯爵位的主张；艾马尔则在英格兰安身，领有杰斯蒙德、庞特兰和费尔顿，1381年作为诺森伯兰的郡骑士被选入议会。

他娶玛丽为妻，玛丽据称是总管沃尔特之女；夫妇合葬于泰恩河畔纽卡斯尔的圣安德鲁教堂圣坛。他卒于1402年4月14日。

Agnes FitzAlan (1298 – 3 November 1348), also called Matilda, was the elder daughter and co-heiress of Bryan FitzAlan, Lord FitzAlan of Bedale in Yorkshire, by Maud de Balliol, sister of King John Balliol of Scotland.

On 10 May 1306, weeks before her father's death, the eight-year-old Agnes had her marriage granted to Sir Gilbert Stapleton. With her sister Katherine she inherited the FitzAlan estates, including Bedale, and her husband died in 1321.

Her son Sir Miles Stapleton of Bedale was one of the founding Knights of the Garter in 1348, and another son, Sir Bryan Stapleton, received the Garter in 1382.

阿格尼丝·菲茨艾伦（1298—1348年11月3日，又名莫德）是约克郡比代尔的菲茨艾伦勋爵布莱恩·菲茨艾伦与苏格兰国王约翰·巴里奥之妹莫德·德·巴里奥的长女，也是共同继承人之一。

1306年5月10日，即父亲去世前几周，八岁的阿格尼丝被许配给吉尔伯特·斯特普尔顿爵士。她与妹妹凯瑟琳共同继承了包括比代尔在内的菲茨艾伦家产，丈夫于1321年去世。

她的儿子比代尔的迈尔斯·斯特普尔顿爵士是1348年嘉德骑士团的创始骑士之一，另一个儿子布莱恩·斯特普尔顿爵士于1382年获授嘉德勋章。

Agnes Mortimer, Countess of Pembroke (1317–25 July 1368), was a daughter of Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March, and Joan de Geneville. In 1328 or 1329 she married Laurence Hastings, the future Earl of Pembroke and her father's ward.

Her only surviving son, the 2nd Earl of Pembroke, was born in August 1347, and Laurence died the next year. Agnes then married John de Hakelut. She died in July 1368 and was buried at the Minoresses convent outside Aldgate in London.

en:
Alfred the Great (c. 849–899) was King of the West Saxons from 871 and King of the Anglo-Saxons from 886, the only English monarch called ‘the Great’. He and his brother Æthelred fought the Great Heathen Army; on Æthelred’s death in April 871 he took the Wessex throne and after defeat at Wilton made peace with the Danes.

In January 878 the Danes struck Chippenham; he fled to Athelney and fortified it, Wessex the sole resisting kingdom. In May he beat Guthrum at Edington, who accepted baptism and withdrew, splitting England between Alfred and the Danelaw. After taking London in 886 he styled himself King of the Anglo-Saxons.

He reformed army and law, founded a court school, and translated Latin works. In 868 he married Ealhswith of Mercia; his son Edward the Elder succeeded him. Asser’s life of Alfred, written at his command, portrayed a learned and merciful king.

阿尔弗雷德大帝（约849—899）自871年起为西撒克逊国王，886年起为盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王，是唯一称“大帝”的英格兰君主。他与兄长埃塞尔雷德并肩对抗“大异教徒军队”，871年4月兄长去世后继承威塞克斯王位，威尔顿战败后与丹麦人议和。

878年1月丹麦人突袭奇彭纳姆；他逃到阿瑟尔尼筑垒坚守，此时威塞克斯是仅存的抵抗王国。5月他在埃丁顿击败古思伦，古思伦受洗礼退兵，英格兰分为他的领地与丹麦法区。886年收复伦敦后，他自称盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王。

他整顿军备与法律，开办宫廷学校，翻译拉丁文著作。868年他娶埃尔斯威斯，生子长者爱德华继位。主教阿瑟奉他之命作传，塑造了他博学仁慈的形象。

Alice of Norfolk (c. 1324–1352) was the younger daughter of Thomas of Brotherton, Earl of Norfolk and eldest son of Edward I. After her father's death in 1338, Edward III in 1339 ordered her share of his lands delivered to her and her husband Edward Montagu, 1st Baron Montagu.

Her husband fought at Crécy in 1346. Alice died at Bungay in Suffolk shortly before 30 January 1352 after being assaulted by Montagu, who was indicted for her death.

Alice de Lusignan (c. 1229 – 9 February 1256) was Countess of Surrey and a uterine half-sister of Henry III: her mother was Isabella of Angoulême, King John's widow, by Hugh X of Lusignan, Count of La Marche. In 1247 she followed her Lusignan brothers to England, where Henry III married her to John de Warenne, 6th Earl of Surrey.

Of her children, Isabella married King John Balliol of Scotland and William was born in 1256. She died in Sussex on 9 February 1256 after giving birth to William.

Amaury IV of Évreux, also numbered Amaury VI de Montfort, was Count of Évreux in Normandy and later Earl of Gloucester in England. The son of Count Amaury III and Mabel, he inherited Évreux after his father died on the Third Crusade, and in 1198, still a minor, inherited his mother's claim to Gloucester.

In 1199 Philip II of France overran Évreux, and by the Treaty of Le Goulet in 1200 King John ceded it to France; Amaury surrendered it and was compensated with the earldom of Gloucester. He supported John when war resumed in 1202, but revolted the next year, and died around 1213.

en:
Anne Boleyn (c. 1501 or 1507–1536) was the second wife of Henry VIII and queen of England in 1533–1536; her rise and fall helped start the English Reformation. After serving at courts abroad, she returned to England as maid of honour to Catherine of Aragon.

From 1526 Henry pursued her, but she refused to become his mistress; his wish to annul the marriage led him to break the Church's power in England. They married secretly; Cranmer declared the marriage to Catherine void, Anne was crowned in June, and that September gave birth to the future Elizabeth I.

After three miscarriages, Henry was courting Jane Seymour by March 1536. Tried at the Tower, she was convicted of adultery, incest and plotting the king's death, charges most historians dispute, and was beheaded with a single stroke on 19 May 1536. Her daughter's reign after 1558 made her a Protestant martyr.

安妮·博林（约1501或1507—1536）是亨利八世的第二任王后，1533至1536年在位；她的崛起与覆灭推动了英格兰宗教改革。她曾在尼德兰和法国的宫廷侍奉，后回到英格兰，成为阿拉贡的凯瑟琳的宫廷侍女。

亨利八世自1526年起追求她，她却不肯做国王的情妇；国王为废除婚姻、改娶她，着手瓦解教会在英格兰的势力。两人随后秘密成婚，克兰麦宣布原有婚姻无效，安妮6月加冕，9月生下日后的伊丽莎白一世。

Anthony Babington (1561–1586) was a Derbyshire Catholic gentleman who had served as a page in the household of the Earl of Shrewsbury, keeper of the imprisoned Mary, Queen of Scots. Around 1580 he met Thomas Morgan, who persuaded him to carry letters to Mary.

In 1586 he led young Catholic conspirators planning to murder Elizabeth I and free Mary; their letters to Mary, smuggled in beer barrels, were intercepted by Sir Francis Walsingham's agents. Babington was arrested in August and hanged, drawn and quartered on 20 September 1586, and his plot supplied the treason charge that led to Mary's execution the following year.

Anton van den Wyngaerde (c. 1525–1571) was a Flemish topographical artist, born in Antwerp, who made panoramic views of cities across northern Europe. Around 1544 he produced a fourteen-sheet panorama of London, including a plan of Whitehall Palace drawn for Henry VIII, and he later recorded the sieges of Saint-Quentin and Ham during Philip II's 1557 campaign.

He visited England in 1558–1559 to draw Dover, London and the royal palaces, then from about 1562 worked in Spain, where Philip II commissioned at least sixty-two city views, among them Barcelona, Seville, Toledo and Madrid. He died in Madrid on 7 May 1571.

en:
Sir Anthony van Dyck (1599–1641) was the Flemish Baroque painter who became the leading court painter of Charles I's England. Born in Antwerp, he trained under Rubens, who called him his best pupil, and after seeing Titian's work in London spent 1621 to 1627 in Italy, mostly in Genoa, developing tall full-length portraits, and painted the Saint Rosalia series.

Back in Flanders he made the Iconography, etchings of contemporaries. In 1632 Charles I knighted him in London as principal painter and gave him a Blackfriars house, with a causeway built for their visits.

Though the king was a hard sitter under five feet tall, van Dyck painted him forty times and Queen Henrietta Maria thirty. Their relaxed elegance dominated English portraiture until the late eighteenth century, and the Van Dyke beard is named after his sitters' styles. He died at Blackfriars on 9 December 1641, his daughter's baptism day.

安东尼·范戴克爵士（1599—1641）是佛兰德巴洛克画家，后成为查理一世治下英格兰的首席宫廷画师。他生于安特卫普，师从鲁本斯，被鲁本斯称为最好的学生；在伦敦见到提香的作品后，于1621至1627年旅居意大利，主要住在热那亚，发展出修长的全身肖像，并创作了圣罗莎莉亚系列。

回到佛兰德后，他创作了蚀刻同时代名人的《肖像集》。1632年查理一世在伦敦封他为爵士、任首席画师，赐他布莱克弗赖尔斯的住宅，还为国王夫妇到访修了一条堤道。

国王身高不到五英尺、很难画好，范戴克仍为他画了四十幅肖像，为亨利埃塔·玛丽亚王后画了三十幅。其松弛优雅的格调主导英国肖像画直到十八世纪末，范戴克式胡须也以他笔下人物的装束命名。1641年12月9日他卒于布莱克弗赖尔斯，当天正是女儿受洗之日。

Aphra Behn (baptised 1640–1689) was an English playwright, poet and prose writer of the Restoration era, and one of the first English women to earn a living by writing. Charles II employed her as a spy in Antwerp, and after returning to London she was probably briefly imprisoned for debt and then turned to the stage.

Under the pastoral pen name Astrea she found fame with the comedy The Rover and later the short novel Oroonoko, or the Royal Slave. During the Exclusion Crisis, a prologue and an epilogue brought her legal trouble, after which she devoted most of her writing to prose.

A loyal Stuart supporter, she refused to write a poem welcoming William III. She died in April 1689 and was buried in Westminster Abbey.

Æthelstan (c. 894 – 27 October 939), son of Edward the Elder, became king of the Anglo-Saxons in 924 and was crowned in September 925. In 927 he conquered the Viking kingdom of York, becoming the first ruler of a united England, and in 934 he invaded Scotland and received Constantine II's submission.

When Scots and Vikings invaded together in 937 he crushed them at Brunanburh, a victory famed across Europe. A pious lawmaker who founded churches, he died childless in 939 and was succeeded by his half-brother Edmund.

Albéric de Clermont (1222–1284) was Count of Clermont-en-Beauvaisis from 1234 to 1252. The son of Philip Hurepel and Matilda II of Boulogne, he was a grandson of King Philip II Augustus of France.

In 1252 he surrendered all his lands to his sister Joan, Countess of Boulogne, and settled in England. When Joan died later that year, Clermont escheated to the French crown, and Louis IX granted it to his son Robert of Clermont. Albéric died in 1284.

Under Edward III he served until his death as constable of Dover Castle and warden of the Cinque Ports, undertook embassies to France and Avignon, and went to Gascony. Named a guardian of the realm in 1355, he died at Dover that August.

Bartholomew Burghersh, 2nd Baron Burghersh (before 1329–1369), called the younger, was an English soldier, son of Bartholomew Burghersh the elder. He fought at Crécy in 1346 and at Calais, and in 1348 was among the first Knights of the Garter.

After a 1354 pilgrimage to Jerusalem, he played a leading part at Poitiers in 1356 under the Black Prince, and joined Edward III's 1359 campaign that ended with the Treaty of Brétigny. He died in 1369 and was buried at Walsingham Abbey.

en:
Blanche of Lancaster (1342–1368) was the younger daughter of Henry of Grosmont, 1st Duke of Lancaster. In 1359 she married John of Gaunt, son of Edward III; the great Lancaster inheritance she brought him became the foundation of his power and of the Duchy of Lancaster, and she bore seven children, including the future Henry IV.

She died at Tutbury Castle on 12 September 1368, probably of the Black Death, while Gaunt was overseas. He held annual commemorations of her death and in 1374 commissioned a joint tomb for them at St Paul's Cathedral, and Geoffrey Chaucer's The Book of the Duchess is generally thought to have been written in her memory.

兰开斯特的布兰奇（1342—1368）是第一代兰开斯特公爵格罗斯蒙特的亨利的小女儿。1359年她嫁给爱德华三世之子冈特的约翰；她带来的巨额兰开斯特遗产成为冈特的约翰权势的根基，也奠定了兰开斯特公国的基础，她共生育七个子女，其中包括日后的亨利四世。

Sir Bryan Stapleton (c. 1322–1394) was a Yorkshire knight, third son of Sir Gilbert Stapleton of Bedale and Agnes FitzAlan. His wars began at Tournai in 1340, and by his own account he fought in all the great battles of Edward III's reign, among them Crécy and the siege of Calais in 1346–1347.

He joined the force sent in 1369 to relieve the Black Prince in Aquitaine, and in 1373 sailed to raid the Breton coast and helped defend Brest. Captain of Calais Castle from 1380 and of Guînes from 1381, he became a Knight of the Garter in 1382, and in 1383 escorted Richard II's young bride, Anne of Bohemia, to Calais.

He bought Wighill in 1376 and died there in 1394, asking in his will to be buried beside his wife at Helaugh Priory.

1376年他买下威格尔，1394年卒于此地，遗嘱要求葬在赫劳修道院，与亡妻相伴。

en:
Bryan FitzAlan, Lord FitzAlan, was a Yorkshire landowner, lord of Bedale and other manors, and the son of Sir Alan FitzBryan. In 1290 he founded a chantry at Bedale for prayers for his parents, his first wife Muriel and their three sons; Muriel and the three sons had died by then.

In 1291 he received licence to crenellate his house at Killerby and was appointed one of the guardians of Scotland. By his second wife Maud de Balliol, sister of King John Balliol, he was the Scottish king's brother-in-law. He died on 1 June 1306 and was buried at Bedale, his estates passing to his daughters and co-heiresses Agnes and Katherine.

en:
Catherine of Aragon (1485–1536) was Queen of England in 1509–1533 as the first wife of Henry VIII; her lack of a surviving son triggered England's break with Rome. The youngest child of Ferdinand and Isabella, she married Arthur, Prince of Wales, in 1501 and, after his death, Henry VIII in 1509; in 1507 she became the first known female ambassador in European history.

In 1513, while Henry campaigned in France, she was regent for six months and England won at Flodden. Of six pregnancies only her daughter Mary, born in 1516, survived.

By 1526 Henry, infatuated with Anne Boleyn, wanted an annulment; when the Pope refused, he took supremacy over the English church and married Anne. She refused every title but queen and denied Henry's church supremacy, and died at Kimbolton Castle on 7 January 1536. Cromwell said, but for her sex, she could have defied history's heroes.

阿拉贡的凯瑟琳（1485—1536）是亨利八世的第一任妻子，1509至1533年任英格兰王后；她无子存活，引发英格兰与罗马决裂。她是费尔南多与伊莎贝拉最小的孩子，1501年嫁给威尔士亲王亚瑟，亚瑟早逝后于1509年改嫁亨利八世；1507年成为欧洲已知的第一位女大使。

1513年亨利远征法国，她摄政半年，其间英格兰在弗洛登击败苏格兰。六次怀孕中只有1516年出生的女儿玛丽存活。

1526年亨利迷恋安妮·博林，要求废除婚姻；教皇拒绝后，他自任英格兰教会最高首脑，迎娶安妮。她拒绝王后以外的称号，不承认亨利为教会首脑，1536年1月7日在金博尔顿城堡去世。克伦威尔说，若非性别所限，她足以挑战历史上的英雄。

1513年亨利远征法国，她摄政半年，其间英格兰在弗洛登击败[GetCountry('SCO').GetName]。六次怀孕中只有1516年出生的女儿玛丽存活。

1526年亨利迷恋安妮·博林，要求废除婚姻；教皇拒绝后，他自任英格兰教会最高首脑，迎娶安妮。她拒绝王后以外的称号，不承认亨利为教会首脑，1536年1月7日在金博尔顿城堡去世。克伦威尔说，若非性别所限，她足以挑战历史上的英雄。

en:
Catherine of Braganza (1638–1705), daughter of John IV of Portugal, married Charles II of England in 1662. Her dowry brought England Tangier, Bombay and trading privileges in the Portuguese Indies, sealing an alliance backing Portugal's independence from Spain. She suffered at least three miscarriages and bore no surviving children, placing her position under strain.

A Catholic, she was accused of treason during the Popish Plot of 1678–1679, but Charles defended her and she was never tried. After his death she returned to Portugal and twice served as regent for her brother Peter II, in 1701 and 1704–1705. She died in Lisbon, credited with popularising tea in England.

布拉干萨的凯瑟琳（1638—1705）是葡萄牙国王若昂四世之女，1662年嫁给英格兰国王查理二世。她的嫁妆把丹吉尔、孟买以及葡属印度的贸易特权带给英格兰，巩固了支持葡萄牙脱离西班牙独立的同盟。她至少流产三次，没有留下存活的子嗣，地位因此受到压力。

作为天主教徒，她在1678—1679年的“教皇阴谋”中被控叛国，但查理二世力保于她，最终未受审判。丈夫死后她返回葡萄牙，于1701年和1704—1705年两度为弟弟佩德罗二世摄政，最后在里斯本去世，相传饮茶在英格兰的流行也得益于她。

en:
Charles Beauclerk, 1st Duke of St Albans (1670–1726), was the elder son of Charles II and the actress Nell Gwyn. Created Earl of Burford in 1676 and Duke of St Albans in 1684, he became a cavalry colonel in 1687 and served Emperor Leopold I at the siege of Belgrade in 1688. In 1694 he married Lady Diana de Vere, heiress of the 20th Earl of Oxford, and had twelve children.

William III made him a gentleman of the bedchamber in 1697. A Whig out of favour under Queen Anne, he regained favour under George I, received the Garter in 1718 and died at Bath in 1726.

第一代圣奥尔本斯公爵查尔斯·博克莱尔（1670—1726）是查理二世与女演员内尔·格温的长子。1676年他被封为伯福德伯爵，1684年晋封圣奥尔本斯公爵。1687年他出任骑兵团上校，1688年随皇帝利奥波德一世的军队参加贝尔格莱德围城战。1694年他娶第二十代牛津伯爵的继承人黛安娜·德维尔为妻，育有十二个子女。

1697年威廉三世任命他为寝宫内侍。他身为辉格党人，在安妮女王一朝失势，乔治一世即位后重新受宠，1718年获授嘉德勋章，1726年在巴斯去世。

Charles Brandon, Duke of Suffolk (c. 1484–1545), was Henry VIII's closest friend and a leading commander. His father died carrying Henry Tudor's standard at Bosworth in 1485, and Brandon was raised at court. He fought at Thérouanne and Tournai in 1513, became Master of the Horse, and was made a duke in March 1514. In 1515 he secretly married Henry's sister Mary Tudor, dowager queen of France, but was forgiven.

In 1523 he led an English army into northern France before withdrawing. He became Earl Marshal in 1524, helped dismiss Wolsey in 1529, led the 1544 invasion of France, and died on 22 August 1545.

1523年，他率英军进入法国北部后撤退。他1524年任宫廷典礼大臣，1529年参与罢黜沃尔西，1544年率军入侵法国，1545年8月22日去世。

Charles Neville, 6th Earl of Westmorland (1542–1601), was a Catholic nobleman of the Neville family of northern England. Allied to the Catholic Howards, he opposed Elizabeth I's Protestant policies.

In November 1569 he and the Earl of Northumberland led the Rising of the North: the rebels seized Durham, celebrated mass, and marched to free Mary, Queen of Scots, before royal forces scattered them. Neville fled to Scotland and was attainted in 1571, forfeiting his estates.

In 1572, fearing betrayal after Northumberland's capture, he went into exile in the Spanish Netherlands, living on a pension from Philip II. In 1588 he mustered English Catholic exiles in Flanders for the Armada invasion, and he died in poverty on 16 November 1601.

第六代威斯特摩兰伯爵查尔斯·内维尔（1542—1601）是英格兰北方内维尔家族的天主教贵族。他与天主教霍华德家族结盟，反对伊丽莎白一世的新教政策。

1569年11月，他与诺森伯兰伯爵共同领导北方起义：起义者夺取达勒姆、举行弥撒，并进军解救被囚的苏格兰女王玛丽，最终被王军击溃。内维尔逃到苏格兰，1571年被褫夺公权，家产尽失。

1572年诺森伯兰被捕后，内维尔担心遭到出卖，逃往西属尼德兰，靠西班牙国王腓力二世的津贴度日。1588年，他在佛兰德召集英格兰天主教流亡者，准备配合无敌舰队入侵，1601年11月16日在贫困中客死他乡。

en:
Christopher Marlowe (baptised 1564–1593), called Kit, was the English playwright ranked London's foremost dramatist just before Shakespeare. A Canterbury shoemaker's son educated at Corpus Christi, Cambridge, he was blocked from his master's degree in 1587 until the Privy Council intervened, praising his unnamed ‘good service’; scholars still debate whether he was a government agent.

His Tamburlaine (1587) was the first English play in blank verse, the age's standard form, and Doctor Faustus, The Jew of Malta and Edward II followed. In May 1593 Thomas Kyd, under torture, called a heretical tract found in his papers Marlowe's, and he was ordered to attend the Privy Council daily.

On 30 May, at a widow's house in Deptford, he quarrelled over the bill with Ingram Frizer, one of the Walsinghams' men, and was stabbed to death. Frizer was pardoned within a month, and Marlowe lies in an unmarked grave at Deptford.

克里斯托弗·马洛（1564年受洗—1593），人称基特，学者视他为莎士比亚之前伦敦首屈一指的剧作家。坎特伯雷鞋匠之子，就读剑桥大学基督圣体学院；1587年校方拒授硕士学位，枢密院称他为女王效力“有功”而不言明其事，学者至今争论他是否做过政府密探。

《帖木儿》（1587年）是首部无韵诗体英语戏剧，此诗体后成时代标准，随后又有《浮士德博士》《马耳他的犹太人》和《爱德华二世》。1593年5月，托马斯·基德受刑后称所持异端文字出自马洛，他被责令每日向枢密院报到。

5月30日在德特福德一寡妇家，他与受雇于沃尔辛厄姆家族的英格拉姆·弗里泽因账单争吵，被刺身亡。弗里泽一月内便获赦，马洛葬在德特福德一处无碑墓中。

en:
Sir Christopher Wren (1632–1723) was the English scientist who became the architect of rebuilt London. A sickly child who lived past ninety, he taught in London, where the circle around his lectures grew into the Royal Society in 1660, and was its president in 1680–1682. An orbit problem he set Halley and Hooke sent Halley to Newton, producing the Principia.

In 1665 he designed a dome for old St Paul's, accepted a week before the Great Fire of 1666 destroyed two-thirds of the City. His plan was never adopted, but as Surveyor of the King's Works from 1669 he oversaw more than fifty rebuilt churches, and he was knighted in 1673.

St Paul's took thirty-six years and was declared complete by Parliament in 1711. He died in his sleep in 1723 and was buried in the crypt, where his inscription tells seekers of his monument to look around.

克里斯托弗·雷恩爵士（1632—1723）是由科学家转身成为重建伦敦的建筑师的英格兰人。他幼时体弱却活过九十岁。他在伦敦讲学，讲座圈子1660年发展为皇家学会，1680至1682年任会长。他向哈雷和胡克提出的行星轨道问题，促使哈雷请教牛顿，催生《自然哲学的数学原理》。

1665年他为旧圣保罗大教堂设计穹顶，设计获通过一周后，1666年伦敦大火便烧毁城中三分之二区域。重建伦敦规划始终未被采纳，但1669年起他任王室工程总监，重建五十多座教堂，1673年受封爵士。

圣保罗大教堂历时三十六年建成，1711年议会宣布竣工。1723年他在睡梦中去世，葬于教堂地穴，墓志铭让寻找纪念碑的读者环顾四周。

Cnut, called the Great (c. 995–1035), was the younger son of Swein Forkbeard. He invaded England in 1015, defeated Edmund Ironside at Assandun in October 1016, and became king on Edmund's death weeks later. In 1017 he married Æthelred's widow Emma of Normandy, inheriting Denmark in 1018.

He defeated Norwegian and Swedish rivals at the Helgeå in 1026 and took Norway in 1028. Ruler of England, Denmark and Norway, the core of the North Sea Empire, he died at Shaftesbury on 12 November 1035 and was buried at Winchester.

克努特，世称“大帝”（约995—1035），是八字胡斯文的幼子。他于1015年入侵英格兰，1016年10月在阿桑顿击败刚勇者埃德蒙，几周后埃德蒙去世，他成为全英格兰国王。1017年他迎娶埃塞尔雷德的遗孀诺曼底的爱玛，1018年继承丹麦王位。

en:
Cornelis Drebbel (1572–1633) was a Dutch engineer and inventor born in Alkmaar. In 1598 he obtained a patent for a water-supply system and a perpetual clockwork. Around 1604 he moved to England, where he astonished the court with hydraulic automata and optical instruments.

In 1610 he entered Emperor Rudolf II's service in Prague, where he was imprisoned after the emperor's fall. He returned to London in 1613, and on a second stay in Prague was captured when the city fell in 1620. He built the first navigable submarine that same year and died in London in 1633.

en:
Daniel Defoe (c. 1660–1731) was an English writer and government agent, author of Robinson Crusoe and one of the earliest proponents of the English novel. Born Daniel Foe in London, he lived through the Great Plague of 1665 and the Great Fire of 1666, which left only three houses standing in his neighbourhood. He later added the grand-sounding De to his name.

He was rarely out of debt and went bankrupt in 1692. He had joined Monmouth's rebellion in 1685 and escaped the Bloody Assizes by pardon, and under William III he served as a secret agent. His political tracts cost him a period in prison.

Robinson Crusoe (1719) ran through four editions before the year ended, and its name now defines the Robinsonade genre; Moll Flanders and Roxana followed. He died in 1731, probably in hiding from his creditors.

丹尼尔·笛福（约1660—1731）是英国作家兼政府密探，《鲁滨逊漂流记》的作者，也是英国小说最早的倡导者之一。他生于伦敦，原名丹尼尔·福，经历了1665年的伦敦大瘟疫和1666年的伦敦大火，大火中他所在街区只剩三栋房子。后来他给姓氏加上听来显贵的前缀“德”。

他很少不欠债，1692年宣告破产。他曾在1685年参加蒙茅斯叛乱，靠赦免躲过血腥巡回审判，威廉三世在位时担任密探。政论小册子还让他一度入狱。

《鲁滨逊漂流记》（1719）在当年内连印四版，书名后来成了“鲁滨逊式故事”这一体裁的名称，《摩尔·弗兰德斯》《罗克萨娜》等小说随后问世。1731年他去世，当时多半在躲避债主。

en:
Eadred (c. 923 – 23 November 955), younger son of Edward the Elder, became king in 946, when his brother Edmund I was killed leaving the young princes Eadwig and Edgar. His reign was dominated by the long struggle with Viking York, and in 954 the York magnates expelled their last king, Erik Bloodaxe, bringing all Northumbria under his rule.

A friend of Dunstan of Glastonbury, he supported the early English Benedictine reform. He died unmarried in his early thirties in 955, and Eadwig and Edgar succeeded him in turn.

en:
Eadwig (c. 940–959), called All-Fair, was the elder son of King Edmund I and became king of England in November 955 after his uncle Eadred died. Crowned in January 956, he soon quarrelled with Dunstan, Abbot of Glastonbury, and drove him into exile in Flanders.

In 957 his brother Edgar was made king north of the Thames, leaving Eadwig with only Wessex and the south. In 958 his marriage to Ælfgifu was annulled because they were too closely related. Eadwig died on 1 October 959, aged about nineteen, and Edgar reunited the kingdom.

Edgar, known as the Peaceful (c. 943–975), was the younger son of King Edmund I. In 957 the Mercians and Northumbrians made him king north of the Thames, and on Eadwig's death in 959 he took the throne of all England.

His reign saw no Viking attacks; he backed Dunstan's Benedictine Reform and standardised the coinage. In 973 he was crowned at Bath and received homage from neighbouring rulers at Chester. He died on 8 July 975, leaving the crown to his son Edward.

Sir Edmund FitzAlan (c. 1327/1329–1382), also called Edmund de Arundel, was the only son of Richard FitzAlan, Earl of Arundel, and Isabel le Despenser, and a great-great-grandson of Edward I. He was heir to the earldom until his parents' marriage was annulled in 1344 and he was declared illegitimate.

Knighted in 1352, he served as a soldier and envoy: he fought in France in 1359–1360, carried Pope Urban V's report to Edward III in 1368, and fought under the Black Prince at Pontvallain in 1369–1370.

After his father died in 1376 he quarrelled with his half-brother Richard over the earldom, was held in the Tower of London in 1377, and never won it back. He sailed for Gascony in 1381 and was dead by February 1382; his three daughters by Sybil Montagu later sued their half-uncle the Earl of Arundel and failed.

Edmund Crouchback (1245–1296) was the second surviving son of Henry III and founder of the House of Lancaster. In 1254 his father accepted a papal grant naming him king of Sicily, but the scheme collapsed for lack of funds. He fought in the Second Barons' War and after Evesham in 1265 received Simon de Montfort's confiscated lands, becoming Earl of Lancaster.

Through his marriage to Blanche of Artois he governed Champagne from 1276. He died at Bayonne in 1296 while campaigning in Gascony against Philip IV.

Edmund FitzAlan, Earl of Arundel (1285–1326), succeeded his father Richard in 1302 as a ward of the Earl of Surrey, whose granddaughter Alice he married. Knighted by Edward I in 1306, he fought in the Scottish wars.

In 1311 he joined the Lords Ordainers against Edward II and, with Thomas of Lancaster, helped bring about Piers Gaveston's death in 1312. Later reconciled with the king, he supported the suppression of Mortimer's and Lancaster's rebellions.

Captured during Isabella and Roger Mortimer's invasion, he was beheaded at Hereford in November 1326. His title and lands were forfeited, but his son Richard recovered them in 1331.

en:
Edmund II, known as Ironside (c. 990–1016), was a son of King Æthelred the Unready. In 1015, after Sigeferth was executed, he defied Æthelred, married Sigeferth's widow and made himself master of the Five Boroughs.

On Æthelred's death in April 1016 he was elected king and led resistance to Cnut's Danish army, before defeat at Assandun, where Eadric Streona's flight was decisive. He divided the kingdom with Cnut at Alney, keeping Wessex, but died on 30 November 1016 after seven months as king.

埃德蒙二世，世称“刚勇者”（约990—1016），是国王决策无方者埃塞尔雷德之子。1015年贵族西格弗斯被处死后，他起兵对抗埃塞尔雷德，娶其遗孀为妻，控制了丹麦法区的五座重镇。

Sir Edmund Mortimer (1302/1303 – 16 December 1331), eldest son of Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March, married Elizabeth de Badlesmere in July 1316, when he was fourteen and she was three. During his father's exile he was imprisoned in the Tower of London and knighted by Edward III in February 1327.

After the Earl was attainted and hanged in 1330, Edmund recovered the Wigmore estates in October 1331 but died of fever on 16 December, leaving his son Roger, later 2nd Earl of March.

Edmund, 2nd Earl of Kent (c. 1326–1331), was the eldest son of Edmund of Woodstock, Edward I's son, by Margaret Wake. His father was executed for treason in March 1330.

After Edward III overthrew Roger Mortimer later that year the attainder was reversed and the infant Edmund was recognised as Earl of Kent. He died on 5 October 1331, aged about five, and the earldom passed to his baby brother John.

Edmund of Woodstock (1301–1330), 1st Earl of Kent, was a younger son of Edward I and half-brother of Edward II. He was made Earl of Kent in 1321 and helped put down a baronial revolt.

In 1326 he joined Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer in deposing the king, but soon fell out with their regime. In 1330 he was convicted of plotting to free Edward II and beheaded at Winchester. Edward III annulled the charges, and Kent passed to his son.

en:
Edmund I (920/921 – 26 May 946), elder son of Edward the Elder, succeeded his half-brother Æthelstan as king in 939. At first he lost the north to the Viking king Anlaf Guthfrithson, but after Anlaf's death in 941 he recovered the Five Boroughs and expelled the Viking kings of York in 944, reuniting England.

In 945 he ravaged Strathclyde and ceded it to Malcolm I of Scotland. Edmund was killed in a brawl at Pucklechurch in 946, and was succeeded by his brother Eadred.

en:
Edward I (1239–1307), called Longshanks and later the Hammer of the Scots, was King of England from 1272 to 1307. The eldest son of Henry III, he joined the Ninth Crusade in 1270 and was crowned in 1274. At 6 ft 2 in he towered over his contemporaries.

War overtook his legal reforms. After risings in 1276–1277 and 1282–1283 he conquered Wales, and the Statute of Rhuddlan of 1284 brought it under English administration. When Eleanor of Castile died in 1290, he raised twelve crosses where her procession stopped each night, and that year expelled England's Jews.

Asked to arbitrate the Scottish succession, he claimed overlordship of Scotland and invaded, beating William Wallace at Falkirk in 1298. When Robert the Bruce was crowned in 1306, the ill king marched north and died of dysentery at Burgh by Sands on 7 July 1307. The war outlived him.

爱德华一世（1239—1307）绰号“长腿”，后世又称“苏格兰之锤”，1272至1307年任英格兰国王。他是亨利三世的长子，1270年参加第九次十字军东征，1274年加冕。他身高六英尺二英寸，在同代人中鹤立鸡群。

受请裁决苏格兰王位继承之争时，他宣称拥有宗主权并出兵入侵，1298年在福尔柯克击败威廉·华莱士。1306年罗伯特·布鲁斯加冕为苏格兰王，抱病的国王再次北上，1307年7月7日在伯格拜桑兹死于痢疾。这场战争在他身后仍在继续。

en:
Edward II (1284–1327), Edward of Caernarfon, succeeded his father Edward I in 1307 and in 1308 married Isabella, daughter of Philip IV of France. Barons led by his cousin Thomas of Lancaster killed his favourite Piers Gaveston in 1312. In 1314 Robert the Bruce routed him at Bannockburn, ending English hopes in Scotland.

He later ruled through the Despenser family and executed Lancaster in 1322. In 1326 Isabella and her lover Roger Mortimer invaded and forced him to abdicate in January 1327 in favour of his son Edward III. He died that year at Berkeley Castle, probably murdered on the orders of the new regime.

en:
Edward III (1312–1377), king of England from 1327, was fourteen when Isabella and Roger Mortimer deposed Edward II. In 1330 he seized Mortimer at Nottingham and ruled. When Philip VI seized Gascony in 1337, Edward claimed the French crown, opening the Hundred Years' War.

He won at Sluys in 1340 and beat the French at Crécy in 1346; Calais fell in 1347, before the Black Death of 1348 killed a third of the English. In 1356 the Black Prince took King John II at Poitiers, and the 1360 Treaty of Brétigny secured Edward's French lands.

He founded the Order of the Garter around 1348 and used Parliament for taxes, strengthening the Commons. Froissart wrote his like had not been seen since King Arthur. War resumed in 1369; by 1375 Edward held only the Calais Pale. The Black Prince predeceased him, and Edward died in 1377, succeeded by grandson Richard II.

爱德华三世（1312—1377）1327年十四岁即位为英格兰国王，当时伊莎贝拉与罗杰·莫蒂默逼迫爱德华二世退位。1330年他在诺丁汉拿下莫蒂默，开始亲政。1337年腓力六世没收加斯科涅，爱德华便主张法国王位，百年战争由此开始。

1340年他在斯勒伊斯海战取胜，1346年在克雷西击败法军，1347年加来陷落；随后1348年的黑死病夺去了三分之一英格兰人的生命。1356年黑太子在普瓦捷俘虏法王约翰二世，1360年《布雷蒂尼条约》保住了他在法国的领地。

约1348年他创立嘉德骑士团，并依靠议会征税，下议院由此壮大。傅华萨写道，自亚瑟王以来再无人能与他相比。1369年战争重启，到1375年他只剩加来周边地区。黑太子先他去世，爱德华于1377年去世，孙子理查二世继位。

en:
Edward, 2nd Duke of York (c. 1373–1415), known as Edward of Norwich, was the eldest son of Edmund of Langley and a grandson of Edward III. Richard II made him Earl of Rutland in 1390 and appointed him admiral of the northern fleet in 1391. He accompanied Richard on campaign in Ireland and became Duke of Aumale in 1397, yet in 1399 he abandoned Richard for Henry Bolingbroke.

He succeeded his father as Duke of York in 1402 and translated the hunting book The Master of Game. He died commanding the right wing at Agincourt in October 1415.

Edward of Norfolk (c. 1313–1334) was the only son of Thomas of Brotherton, 1st Earl of Norfolk, and a grandson of Edward I. In 1328 he married Beatrice Mortimer, daughter of Roger Mortimer, in a double wedding attended by Edward III and Queen Isabella. The marriage produced no children.

He died before 9 August 1334, predeceasing his father, so when Thomas of Brotherton died in 1338 the Norfolk earldom passed to Edward's elder sister Margaret.

Edward of Woodstock, the Black Prince (1330–1376), was Edward III's eldest son and heir. Created Duke of Cornwall in 1337 and Prince of Wales in 1343, he commanded the English vanguard at Crécy in 1346, aged sixteen.

His chevauchées of 1355–1356 sacked Narbonne and ravaged Auvergne and Limousin, and at Poitiers in 1356 his army routed the French and captured King John II. English contemporaries saw him as chivalry's model; French sources remember his brutality. He negotiated the Treaty of Brétigny in 1360 and ruled Aquitaine as prince from 1362.

In 1367 he defeated Henry of Trastámara, Peter of Castile's rival, at Nájera, but Peter never repaid the debt, and a hearth tax he secured in 1368 alienated Aquitanian nobles. In failing health he returned to England in 1371 and died in June 1376; his son Richard II succeeded Edward III.

Edward the Confessor (c. 1003 – 5 January 1066) ruled as king of the English from 1042, the son of Æthelred the Unready and Emma of Normandy. After spending much of his youth in Norman exile, he succeeded his half-brother Harthacnut.

His later reign saw the rise of Earl Godwin's family. Edward rebuilt Westminster Abbey, and when he died childless in January 1066 Harold Godwinson took the throne, paving the way for the Norman Conquest. He was canonised in 1161.

Edward the Elder (c. 874 – 17 July 924), elder son of Alfred the Great, ruled as king of the Anglo-Saxons from 899. He first defeated a bid for the crown by his cousin Æthelwold, and in 910 his army crushed the Northumbrian Vikings.

With his sister Æthelflæd he then conquered Viking-held eastern and southern England, and in 918 imposed direct rule on Mercia. After putting down a Mercian and Welsh revolt at Chester in 924, he died at Farndon and was succeeded by his son Æthelstan.

en:
Edward, later called the Martyr (c. 962–978), was the eldest son of King Edgar and ruled the English from July 975. On Edgar's death his claim was disputed against his young half-brother Æthelred, but Archbishop Dunstan secured his succession. His short reign saw an anti-monastic reaction, as nobles seized back lands granted to monasteries.

On 18 March 978 he was murdered at Corfe while visiting Æthelred's household; later tradition blamed Æthelred's mother. His body was translated to Shaftesbury Abbey in 979, and he was venerated as a saint.

en:
Eleanor FitzAlan (c. 1284 – July or August 1328) was a daughter of Richard FitzAlan, 1st Earl of Arundel, and Alice of Saluzzo. In 1294 she married Henry de Percy, the future 1st Baron Percy, a match documented by a 1300 recognizance for a 2000-mark debt her father owed Percy. Her husband, who bought Alnwick Castle in 1309, died in 1314 after serving through the Scottish wars.

By him she had two sons, Henry, born in 1301, who succeeded as 2nd Baron Percy, and William. She was styled a kinswoman of Edward II, through descent from the counts of Savoy, and her tomb displayed the FitzAlan arms.

埃莉诺·菲茨艾伦（约1284—1328年7、8月间）是第一代阿伦德尔伯爵理查德·菲茨艾伦与萨卢佐的阿洛伊西亚之女。1294年，她嫁给后来的第一代珀西男爵亨利·德·珀西；这门婚事有1300年的一份债务确认书为证，内容是她父亲为欠珀西的2000马克债务作保。丈夫1309年购入阿尼克城堡，长年转战苏格兰战争，1314年去世。

她生有两子：1301年出生的亨利后来袭封第二代珀西男爵，以及威廉。她经萨伏依伯爵家族一系被记为爱德华二世的亲属，墓上刻有菲茨艾伦家族的纹章。

en:
Eleanor ‘Nell’ Gwyn (1650–1687) was one of the first actresses on the English stage and the best-known mistress of Charles II. Raised in a London slum, she sold oranges in a King's Company playhouse before becoming an actress. Samuel Pepys praised her comic parts and called her ‘pretty, witty Nell’, and she won acclaim in a breeches role in 1667.

She became the king's long-standing mistress and bore him two sons; the elder, Charles, was later made Earl of Burford and Duke of St Albans. Struck by two strokes in 1687, she died that November.

埃莉诺·“奈尔”·圭恩（1650—1687）是英国舞台上最早的女演员之一，也是查理二世最著名的情妇。她自幼在伦敦贫民窟长大，先在国王剧团的剧院卖橙子，随后登台演戏。塞缪尔·佩皮斯称赞她的喜剧表演，称她为“美丽机智的奈尔”，1667年她女扮男装的角色尤受好评。

后来她成为查理二世的长期情妇，为他生下两个儿子，长子查尔斯后来受封伯福德伯爵和圣奥尔本斯公爵。1687年她两度中风，同年11月去世。

en:
Eleanor of Lancaster (1318–1372) was the fifth daughter of Henry, 3rd Earl of Lancaster, and Maud de Chaworth. In 1330 she married John de Beaumont, 2nd Baron Beaumont, killed at a tournament in 1342. As lady-in-waiting to Queen Philippa she pilgrimaged to Santiago de Compostela.

In 1345 she married Richard Fitzalan, 3rd Earl of Arundel, after his marriage was annulled; Edward III attended. Her children included the 4th Earl of Arundel and Thomas Arundel, Archbishop of Canterbury. Eleanor died in January 1372.

en:
Elizabeth Montagu, née Robinson (1718–1800), was a British salon hostess, literary critic, writer and social reformer, born in Yorkshire. In 1742 she married Edward Montagu, a wealthy Northumberland coal-owner, and used his fortune to patronise English and Scottish literature and relieve the poor.

From the 1750s her London literary breakfasts, and after 1760 her evening assemblies where cards and strong drink were banned, formed the core of the Blue Stockings Society. By 1770 her Hill Street house was London's leading salon. She died in August 1800.

伊莉莎白·蒙塔古（1718—1800），本姓鲁宾逊，是英国沙龙女主人、文学评论家、作家与社会改革家，生于约克郡。1742年她嫁给拥有诺森伯兰大片煤矿的爱德华·蒙塔古，以其财富资助英格兰与苏格兰文学、赈济穷人。

en:
Eleanor of Woodstock (1318–1355), an English princess and Countess of Guelders, was a daughter of Edward II and Isabella of France and younger sister of Edward III. In 1332 she married Reginald II, Count of Guelders.

Legend says in 1338 she was driven from court on a false charge of leprosy, disproving it at Nijmegen when her husband sought an annulment. After Reginald's death in 1343 she ruled Guelders as regent for her son Reginald III, but was forced from office the next year. She died at Deventer in 1355.

en:
Elizabeth Raffald, née Whitaker (1733–1781), was an English cookery writer and entrepreneur, born at Doncaster in Yorkshire. After fifteen years in service she became housekeeper at Arley Hall, Cheshire, then married the head gardener, John Raffald, in 1763 and settled in Manchester, where she ran a servants' register office, a cookery school and a confectionery business.

In 1769 she published The Experienced English Housekeeper, with the earliest recognisable recipe for a modern wedding cake, and in 1772 issued Manchester's first trade directory. She died suddenly in 1781.

en:
Elizabeth Woodville (c. 1437–1492) was queen of England as the wife of Edward IV. Her first husband, the Lancastrian John Grey, died at the Second Battle of St Albans in 1461. Her secret marriage to Edward IV in 1464 became a cause célèbre. Her relatives' advancement drove Warwick to rebellion, and in 1469 he had her father and brother executed.

After Edward IV's death in 1483, her son Edward V was deposed by Richard III and disappeared. Elizabeth helped secure Henry VII's accession in 1485, and her daughter Elizabeth of York married Henry in 1486.

Æthelred II, called the Unready (c. 968–1016), a son of King Edgar, became king in March 978 after the murder of his half-brother Edward the Martyr. Viking raids resumed, and after defeat at Maldon in 991 he bought off the Danes with tribute.

A massacre of Danes in 1002 provoked retaliation, and in December 1013 Swein Forkbeard drove him into exile in Normandy. He returned in 1014 after Swein's death and died on 23 April 1016, leaving the war against Cnut to his son Edmund Ironside.

en:
Sir Francis Drake (c. 1540–1596) was a Devon-born seaman who made the second circumnavigation of the globe and became the terror of Spanish America. After a Spanish fleet destroyed most of John Hawkins's ships at San Juan de Ulúa in 1568, he took to raiding Spanish possessions, leading his first independent expedition to the Spanish Main in 1572.

From 1577 he sailed the Golden Hind around the globe, plundering Spanish ports and ships along the Pacific coast, and returned in 1580. Elizabeth I knighted him in 1581, and the Spanish called him El Draque, the Dragon. In 1588 he was vice admiral repulsing the Armada.

After the 1589 English Armada failed, he had no command until a failed 1595 expedition. Drake died of dysentery on 28 January 1596, aged about 56, off Portobelo; asking to be dressed in full armour, he was buried at sea in a lead-lined coffin.

弗朗西斯·德雷克爵士（约1540—1596）生于德文郡，完成了人类历史上第二次环球航行，也是西属美洲闻风丧胆的英国私掠船长。1568年西班牙舰队在圣胡安-德乌卢阿击毁约翰·霍金斯的大部分船只后，德雷克便一心袭击西班牙海外领地，1572年首次率队独立远征西班牙大陆沿岸。

1577年他乘“金鹿号”出航，沿太平洋沿岸劫掠西班牙港口和船只，1580年完成环球航行后返回。1581年伊丽莎白一世封他为爵士，西班牙人称他为“埃尔·德拉克”，意为“龙”。1588年他以副司令身份参加击退无敌舰队之战。

1589年他率“英格兰无敌舰队”远征，未能消灭残余的西班牙舰队，此后直到1595年才再获指挥权，那次远征也告失败。1596年1月28日，德雷克在波多贝洛外海死于痢疾，终年约56岁；他临终要求穿上全副铠甲，被安葬入海，棺木衬铅。

en:
Sir Francis Walsingham (c. 1532–1590) was Queen Elizabeth I's principal secretary from 1573 until his death, her spymaster. A committed Protestant exiled in Switzerland and Italy under Mary I, he later served as ambassador in Paris, where he witnessed the St Bartholomew's Day massacre of 1572.

As secretary he built a network of agents across Europe that penetrated Spanish Armada preparations, exposed the Babington Plot against Elizabeth and gathered evidence that sent Mary, Queen of Scots to the block in 1587. He also supported the English navy and worked to bring England and Scotland closer together. He died in 1590.

en:
Geoffrey Chaucer (c. 1343–1400), son of a London wine merchant, was the poet who made Middle English a literary language. A royal page from 1357, he moved in court circles. Taken prisoner at the siege of Reims in 1360, he was ransomed by the king for £16, and around 1366 he married Philippa Roet, whose sister married John of Gaunt.

Italian missions introduced him to poetry he later drew on. From 1374 he controlled London's customs and sat for Kent in Parliament in 1386. In the early 1380s he began The Canterbury Tales, framed as pilgrims' tales to Becket's shrine; it remained unfinished.

Clerk of the King's Works from 1389, he took a house in Westminster Abbey's close in 1399 and died in 1400. The poet Thomas Hoccleve called him the first finder of English poetry, and in 1556 his remains were moved to Poets' Corner, its first writer.

杰弗里·乔叟（约1343—1400）是伦敦酒商之子，也是让中古英语成为文学语言的诗人。1357年他成为王室侍童，从此出入宫廷圈。1360年兰斯围城战被俘，国王出资16镑将他赎回；约1366年娶菲莉帕·罗伊特，其妻姐后来嫁给冈特的约翰。

出使意大利让他接触到日后借鉴的意大利诗歌。1374年起他掌管伦敦关税，1386年代表肯特郡出席议会。1380年代初他开始写《坎特伯雷故事集》，以朝圣者赴贝克特圣陵讲故事为框架，全书未能完成。

1389年起任国王工程书记官，1399年住进威斯敏斯特教堂辖区，1400年去世。诗人托马斯·霍克利夫称他为英语诗歌的第一位发现者；1556年遗骨迁入诗人角，他是葬在那里的第一位作家。

en:
Sir Godfrey Kneller (1646–1723), born Gottfried Kniller in Lübeck, was the leading portrait painter in England under the later Stuarts and George I. After studying under Rembrandt in Amsterdam and working in Rome and Venice, he settled in London in 1676 and painted Charles II; after Peter Lely died in 1680 he became a Principal Painter in Ordinary.

His studio produced portraits on a vast scale, using sketches of faces and a formula for the remaining details. His Hampton Court Beauties of 1690–1691 earned him a knighthood in 1692; he later painted the forty-eight Kit-Cat Club portraits and was created a baronet in 1715.

en:
William le Gros, or William of Aumale (died 20 August 1179), was Count of Aumale and Earl of York, the eldest son of Count Stephen of Aumale and Hawise de Mortimer. He fought for King Stephen at the Battle of the Standard in 1138 and was made Earl of York, then shared the king's defeat at Lincoln in 1141.

He founded Thornton and Meaux abbeys. Henry II seized his Scarborough Castle, built without permission during the Anarchy, and his wife Cicely, Lady of Skipton, brought him estates at Harewood. He left a daughter, Hawise, who inherited Aumale, and was buried at Thornton Abbey.

威廉·勒格罗，又称欧马勒的威廉（1179年8月20日卒），身兼欧马勒伯爵与约克伯爵，是欧马勒伯爵斯蒂芬与哈维丝·德·莫蒂默的长子。1138年他在军旗之战中为斯蒂芬国王作战，受封约克伯爵，1141年又随国王在林肯战败。

他创建了桑顿修道院和莫修道院。亨利二世没收了他在无政府时期未经许可修建的斯卡伯勒城堡，妻子斯基普顿女领主塞西莉为他带来哈伍德的地产。他留下女儿哈维丝，由她继承欧马勒；他本人葬于桑顿修道院。

Guy I of Thouars (1183–1242) was a Poitevin nobleman of the house of Thouars, the second son of Viscount Aimery VII. He became lord of Vihiers in 1227 and in 1234 succeeded his uncle Raymond I as the twenty-first viscount of Thouars.

In the struggles between the English and French crowns in western France, Guy stayed loyal to Henry III of England, whom he supported in Poitou. He died at the beginning of April 1242, as Hugh X of Lusignan, count of La Marche, rose in revolt against Capetian rule, and was succeeded by his brother Aimery VIII.

图阿尔的居伊一世（1183—1242）是13世纪上半叶的普瓦图贵族，出自图阿尔家族，为图阿尔子爵艾默里克七世的次子。他于1227年成为维耶领主，1234年继叔父雷蒙一世之后任第二十一任图阿尔子爵。

在英、法两国王室于法兰西西部的争夺中，居伊始终效忠英格兰国王亨利三世，在普瓦图支持英王。1242年4月初，拉马什伯爵于格十世·德·吕西尼昂起兵反叛卡佩王朝，居伊在叛乱爆发之际去世，其弟艾默里八世继任子爵。

Hans Holbein the Younger (c. 1497–1543) was a German painter and printmaker, born in Augsburg and trained in Basel, where his portraits of Erasmus made his name. As the Reformation reached Basel he worked for reformist and traditional religious patrons. He first reached England in 1526 with Erasmus's recommendation and worked in Thomas More's humanist circle, then settled there from 1532 under Thomas Cromwell's patronage.

By 1535 he was King's Painter to Henry VIII, portraying the court and designing royal jewellery and decorations. He died in London late in 1543, leaving the defining image of the Tudor age.

小汉斯·霍尔拜因（约1497—1543）是德国画家与版画家，生于奥格斯堡，在巴塞尔学艺，为伊拉斯谟绘制的肖像令他声名远播。宗教改革传到巴塞尔后，他既为改革派委托人工作，也为传统宗教赞助人效力。1526年他持伊拉斯谟的推荐信首次前往英格兰，进入托马斯·莫尔的人文主义圈子，1532年起在托马斯·克伦威尔的庇护下定居英格兰。

1535年他已成为亨利八世的御前画师，为宫廷人物绘制肖像，并设计王室珠宝与装饰。1543年末他在伦敦去世，为都铎时代留下了最具代表性的图像记录。

en:
Harold Godwinson (c. 1022–1066), son of Earl Godwin of Wessex, became the most powerful noble in England and succeeded his childless brother-in-law Edward the Confessor, crowned king on 6 January 1066. His reign opened with invasion: his brother Tostig joined Harald Hardrada of Norway, whom Harold defeated and killed at Stamford Bridge on 25 September 1066 after a forced march north.

He then hurried south to face William of Normandy. At Hastings on 14 October he fell, the last crowned Anglo-Saxon king of England.

哈罗德·戈德温森（约1022—1066）是威塞克斯伯爵戈德温之子，后成为英格兰最有权势的贵族；无嗣的内兄忏悔者爱德华去世后，他于1066年1月6日加冕为英格兰国王。他即位之初便遭遇入侵：弟弟托斯蒂格联合挪威国王哈拉尔·哈德拉达来犯，哈罗德急行军北上，于9月25日在斯坦福桥战役中将其击败击杀。

Harold I, called Harefoot (c. 1016–1040), was a son of Cnut the Great. When Cnut died in 1035 he became regent for his half-brother Harthacnut, detained in Denmark, ruling north of the Thames. In 1036 the returning ætheling Alfred was seized, blinded and killed by Harold's followers.

Harold was proclaimed king at Oxford in 1037, and Queen Emma was exiled to Flanders. He died at Oxford on 17 March 1040; Harthacnut succeeded him and had his body dug up and thrown into a fen.

en:
Harthacnut (c. 1018–1042), son of Cnut the Great and Emma of Normandy, became king of Denmark in 1035. Detained in Denmark, he saw England pass to his half-brother Harold Harefoot, but after Harold's death in March 1040 he returned to England as king.

He had Harold's body thrown into a fen, and a heavy fleet tax caused a rising at Worcester in 1041. On 8 June 1042 he collapsed and died while drinking at a wedding, the last Dane to rule England; Edward the Confessor succeeded him.

en:
Hawise (c. 1160 – 1214) was ruling Countess of Aumale, the daughter and heiress of William le Gros. In 1180 she married William de Mandeville, Earl of Essex, who held Aumale until his death in 1189.

Richard I then gave the wealthy widow to the crusader William de Forz, a match she opposed. They had an heir, William de Forz, later Earl of Albemarle, and after her husband died in 1195 she supported their son. Her third husband was Baldwin de Béthune.

After Philip Augustus seized Aumale in 1196 and Baldwin's death, she agreed to pay King John five thousand marks to keep her inheritance and avoid a forced marriage. She died in March 1214.

哈维丝（约1160—1214）是欧马勒女伯爵，威廉·勒格罗的女儿和继承人。1180年她嫁给埃塞克斯伯爵威廉·德·曼德维尔，后者在1189年去世前一直执掌欧马勒。

随后理查一世将这位富有的寡妇改嫁给十字军军人威廉·德·福尔兹，她曾反对这门婚事。两人生下继承人威廉·德·福尔兹，即后来的阿尔伯马尔伯爵；丈夫于1195年去世后，她支持儿子。她的第三任丈夫是博杜安·德·贝蒂讷。

1196年腓力·奥古斯特夺取欧马勒，博杜安死后，她同意向约翰王缴纳五千马克，以保住继承地产并免遭强迫改嫁。她于1214年3月去世。

Henry of Grosmont (c. 1310–1361), only son of Henry, 3rd Earl of Lancaster, and Maud Chaworth, was Edward III's leading captain in the early Hundred Years' War. Created Earl of Derby in 1337, he won a victory at Auberoche in 1345.

He was a founding knight of the Order of the Garter in 1348 and in 1351 became Duke of Lancaster. He wrote Livre de Seyntz Medicines and died in 1361, leaving Maud and Blanche.

格罗斯蒙特的亨利（约1310—1361）是第三代兰开斯特伯爵亨利与莫德·德·查沃思唯一的儿子，也是百年战争初期爱德华三世麾下最得力的统帅。他1337年受封德比伯爵，1345年在欧贝罗什战役取胜。

1348年他成为嘉德骑士团的创始骑士之一，1351年受封兰开斯特公爵。他著有《圣药书》，1361年去世，留下莫德和布兰奇两个女儿。

en:
Henry Hudson (c. 1565–disappeared 1611) was an English navigator who in 1607 and 1608 twice sought a Northeast Passage above Russia. In 1609, sailing for the Dutch East India Company, he crossed the Atlantic and sailed up the river later named after him, opening it to Dutch settlement.

On his final expedition, seeking a Northwest Passage, he became the first European to see Hudson Strait and Hudson Bay. After wintering in James Bay, the crew mutinied in June 1611 and cast him, his son and six others adrift in an open boat; they vanished without trace.

亨利·哈得孙（约1565—1611年失踪）是英格兰航海家，1607和1608年两度试图开辟绕过俄罗斯北方的东北航道。1609年他受雇于荷兰东印度公司，横渡大西洋，沿后来以他命名的哈得孙河上溯，为荷兰人在这一地区的殖民开辟了道路。

最后一次航行中，他寻找西北航道，成为第一个见到哈得孙海峡和哈得孙湾的欧洲人。船队在詹姆斯湾过冬后，船员于1611年6月哗变，把他和儿子及另外六人放到一条敞篷船上任其漂流，他们从此下落不明。

Henry I (c. 1068–1 December 1135), later called Beauclerc, was king of England from 1100 and youngest son of William the Conqueror. On 2 August 1100 his brother William Rufus was killed by an arrow while hunting; Henry seized the Winchester treasury and was crowned three days later, issuing a charter ending his brother's abuses.

Robert Curthose invaded in 1101 and withdrew after negotiations, but in 1105–1106 Henry conquered Normandy and captured him at Tinchebray, holding him for life. In England he built a royal exchequer and itinerant justices; contemporaries thought him harsh but effective.

His only legitimate son William drowned in the White Ship disaster of 1120. Henry named Matilda heir and married her to Geoffrey of Anjou, but died on 1 December 1135 at Lyons-la-Forêt, reportedly from a surfeit of lampreys. His nephew Stephen seized the crown, and the civil war called the Anarchy followed.

亨利一世（后世称博克莱尔，约1068年—1135年12月1日）自1100年起为英格兰国王，是征服者威廉最小的儿子。1100年8月2日，他的兄长威廉·鲁弗斯在狩猎时中箭身亡；亨利夺取温彻斯特国库，三天后加冕，并颁布宪章承诺废除兄长的暴政。

兄长罗贝尔·柯索斯于1101年入侵，经谈判议和后退兵；但1105至1106年亨利征服诺曼底，在坦什布赖俘虏罗贝尔，将他囚禁终身。在英格兰，他设立王室财政署和巡回法官；时人认为他严酷而有效。

他唯一的合法儿子威廉于1120年死于白船海难。亨利立玛蒂尔达为继承人，把她嫁给安茹的若弗鲁瓦，自己于1135年12月1日在利翁斯拉福雷去世，一说因贪吃七鳃鳗而死。外甥斯蒂芬夺取王位，随即爆发史称“无政府时期”的内战。

en:
Henry II (1133–1189) was King of England from 1154 and ruler of the Angevin Empire. He held Normandy and Anjou, gaining Aquitaine by marrying Eleanor, and in 1153 forced Stephen to name him heir. His short Angevin cloak earned the nickname Curtmantle.

He widened royal justice through the Assize of Clarendon of 1166, travelling justices and use of juries, regarded as the foundation of English Common Law. His wish to try criminal clergy in royal courts led to a quarrel with his former friend Thomas Becket, which ended when four knights killed Becket at Canterbury on 29 December 1170.

In 1173 his sons, joined by Eleanor and backed by France, rose against him; he crushed the revolt the next year. In 1189 Richard and Philip II defeated him, and he died at Chinon on 6 July. Richard succeeded him, and the empire broke up under his son John.

zh:
亨利二世（1133—1189）1154年起为英格兰国王，统治安茹帝国。他原已据有诺曼底和安茹，又因迎娶埃莉诺取得阿基坦，1153年迫使斯蒂芬立他为继承人。他偏爱安茹人的短斗篷，因而得绰号“短斗篷”。

他通过1166年的《克拉伦登法令》、巡回法官和使用陪审团扩大王室司法，被视为英格兰普通法的基础。他要求在王室法庭审理犯罪的教士，与昔日好友托马斯·贝克特争执，最终四名骑士于1170年12月29日在坎特伯雷杀死贝克特。

1173年，他的儿子们在埃莉诺加入和法兰西支持下起兵叛乱，被他于次年平定。1189年理查与腓力二世联手击败他，他于7月6日死于希农。理查继位，帝国在他的儿子约翰手中瓦解。

en:
Henry III (1207–1272), son of King John, became king in 1216 during the First Barons' War; William Marshal's victory at Lincoln in 1217 secured his crown. He rebuilt Westminster Abbey honouring Edward the Confessor.

Defeat at Taillebourg in 1242 ended his French reconquests. In 1258 Simon de Montfort's barons imposed the Provisions of Oxford; Henry was captured at Lewes in 1264, but Edward freed him after victory at Evesham in 1265. He died in 1272.

zh:
亨利三世（1207—1272）是约翰国王之子，1216年第一次男爵战争期间即位；1217年威廉·马歇尔在林肯取胜，保住了他的王位。他为纪念忏悔者爱德华而重建威斯敏斯特教堂。

1242年塔耶堡之败终结了他收复法兰西失地的尝试。1258年，西蒙·德·蒙福尔为首的贵族迫使他接受《牛津条例》；1264年他在刘易斯被俘，爱德华在1265年伊夫舍姆获胜后将他救出。他于1272年去世。

Henry, 3rd Earl of Lancaster (c. 1281–1345), younger son of Edmund Crouchback, was summoned to Parliament in 1299. When his brother Earl Thomas was executed in 1322, he recovered Leicester in 1324 and Lancaster in 1327.

In 1326 he joined Isabella's invasion and captured Edward II near Neath, and in 1330 he helped Edward III overthrow Mortimer. Blind from about 1330, he retired to Leicester, founded the Newarke hospital, and died in September 1345, succeeded by his son Henry of Grosmont.

第三代兰开斯特伯爵亨利（约1281—1345）是埃德蒙·克罗奇贝克较年幼的儿子，1299年奉召出席议会。兄长托马斯伯爵于1322年被处死后，他于1324年收回莱斯特伯爵领，1327年收回兰开斯特伯爵领。

1326年，他加入伊莎贝拉的入侵行动，在尼思附近擒获爱德华二世；1330年又协助爱德华三世推翻莫蒂默。约1330年他双目失明，退居莱斯特，创立纽瓦克济贫院，1345年9月去世，由儿子格罗斯蒙特的亨利继位。

en:
Henry de Percy, 1st Baron Percy of Alnwick (1273–1314), was an English magnate who fought for Edward I in Wales and Scotland, earning large Scottish grants that Robert Bruce later reconquered. He acquired Alnwick Castle, making the Percys a dynasty of northern warlords. He married Eleanor FitzAlan, daughter of the Earl of Arundel, and had two sons, Henry and William.

Under Edward II he joined the barons against the king's favourite Piers Gaveston and was imprisoned. He then refused to serve at Bannockburn in 1314, remaining at Alnwick, where he died that October, leaving Henry to succeed him as 2nd baron.

阿尼克的第一代珀西男爵亨利·德·珀西（1273—1314）是英格兰大贵族，曾随爱德华一世征战威尔士和苏格兰，获封大片苏格兰土地，后被罗伯特·布鲁斯夺回。他购得阿尼克城堡，使珀西家族成为镇守北方的军阀世家。他娶阿伦德尔伯爵之女埃莉诺·菲茨艾伦为妻，育有亨利和威廉两个儿子。

爱德华二世在位时，他联合贵族反对国王的宠臣皮尔斯·加韦斯顿，因而被囚禁。后来他拒绝赴1314年的班诺克本战役，留在阿尼克，同年10月在此去世，其子亨利继任第二代男爵。
