en:
Henry Percy, 2nd Baron Percy (1301–1352), was thirteen when his father died in 1314 and left him the Alnwick barony, first held in custody by John de Felton. In 1316 Edward II granted him lands in Northumberland, and in 1322 made him governor of Pickering and Scarborough castles.

He joined the barons who removed the king's favourites, the Despensers. After a disastrous war with the Scots, he and William Zouche negotiated the Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton, so unpopular in England that the peace lasted only five years.

A member of Edward III's council from 1327, he received Skipton and then Warkworth Castle in 1328. He fought at Halidon Hill, and at Neville's Cross in 1346 commanded the English right wing. He married Idonia Clifford and was buried at Alnwick in 1352.

第二代珀西男爵亨利·珀西（1301—1352）十三岁时父亲于1314年去世，他继承阿尼克男爵领地，初由王室交约翰·德·费尔顿代管。1316年，爱德华二世赐予他诺森伯兰的土地，1322年又任命他为皮克林和斯卡伯勒城堡守官。

他参加了贵族们除去国王宠臣德斯潘塞父子的行动。对苏格兰的战争惨败后，他与威廉·祖什一同出面谈判，签订《爱丁堡—北安普顿条约》；这份条约在英格兰极不得人心，和平只维持了五年。

Henry Percy, 3rd Baron Percy of Alnwick (c. 1321–1368), eldest son of the 2nd Baron and Idonia Clifford, was the father of two earls. He married Mary of Lancaster, daughter of Henry, 3rd Earl of Lancaster, and their sons were Henry, later 1st Earl of Northumberland, and Thomas, later 1st Earl of Worcester.

After Mary died in 1362 he married Joan, daughter and sole heiress of John, Lord Orreby. He served as High Sheriff of Northumberland and died around 18 May 1368, probably at Alnwick Castle, and was buried in Alnwick Abbey. His eldest son Henry succeeded him.

en:
Henry Stafford, 2nd Duke of Buckingham (1455–1483), inherited the dukedom in 1460 at the age of four on his grandfather's death. In 1466 he married Katherine Woodville, sister of Edward IV's queen.

In 1483 he supported Gloucester's seizure of the crown as Richard III, but within months turned against him. With Margaret Beaufort he raised a rising across southern England and Wales in Henry Tudor's name.

Flooding of the Severn scattered the army he had gathered on his Welsh estates, and a retainer betrayed him. Richard III had him beheaded without trial in November 1483; the plot is remembered as Buckingham's Rebellion.

en:
Henry VII (1457–1509), born Henry Tudor, was the first Tudor king of England. Through his mother Margaret Beaufort, a great-granddaughter of John of Gaunt, he held a Lancastrian claim. He spent fourteen years exiled in Brittany and in 1483 pledged to marry Elizabeth of York.

In 1485 he landed in Wales and met Richard III at Bosworth. He won when the Stanleys changed sides; Richard was killed, and Henry became the last king to win his crown in battle. Crowned in 1485, he married Elizabeth in 1486, uniting Lancaster and York. Simnel was set to kitchen work and Warbeck executed.

The Star Chamber curbed the nobility, and he married his son Arthur to Catherine of Aragon and his daughter Margaret to James IV of Scotland. Arthur died in 1502, Queen Elizabeth in 1503; Henry died of tuberculosis in 1509, and Henry VIII executed his tax collectors Empson and Dudley.

亨利七世（1457—1509），原名亨利·都铎，是英格兰第一位都铎国王。母亲玛格丽特·博福特是冈特的约翰的曾孙女，因而拥有兰开斯特继承权。他在布列塔尼流亡十四年，1483年宣誓迎娶约克的伊丽莎白。

1485年他在威尔士登陆，与理查三世战于博斯沃思。斯坦利家族倒戈，他得以获胜，理查战死，他成为最后一位战场夺冕的国王。1485年加冕、1486年迎娶伊丽莎白，兰开斯特与约克合流。西姆内尔被罚做厨房杂役，沃贝克被处死。

以星室法庭约束贵族，让亚瑟迎娶阿拉贡的凯瑟琳，玛格丽特嫁给苏格兰的詹姆斯四世。亚瑟死于1502年，伊丽莎白王后死于1503年，他1509年死于肺结核，亨利八世随后处决其税吏埃普森和达德利。

Henry Yevele (c. 1320–1400) was England's royal master mason from 1360 until his death, serving Edward III and Richard II. Probably born in Derbyshire, he may have learned the trade from his father, who may have been a mason; he refaced Westminster Hall at the Palace of Westminster and built the Bloody Tower at the Tower of London.

His greatest surviving works are the naves of Westminster Abbey, begun in 1362, and Canterbury Cathedral, built from 1377 in an early Perpendicular Gothic style and finished only in 1400. He died that year.

en:
Thomas Hobbes (1588–1679) was an English philosopher whose Leviathan (1651) gave social contract theory its most influential form, making him a founder of modern political philosophy. Raised by a wealthy uncle and educated at Oxford and Cambridge, he tutored the Cavendish family.

In 1640, his Elements of Law circulating, he fled to Paris for eleven years. Among royalist exiles he wrote Leviathan, picturing the state as a giant made of men and arguing that only an undivided sovereign could end the war of all against all. Its secular spirit broke his royalist ties, and he fled to London in 1651.

After the Restoration Charles II gave him a £100 pension and shielded him from an atheism bill naming Leviathan in 1666, but he could publish nothing on human conduct afterwards. He translated Homer and died at Hardwick Hall aged 91, reportedly saying 'a great leap in the dark'.

托马斯·霍布斯（1588—1679）是哲学家，1651年的《利维坦》使社会契约论获得最具影响力的形态，他也被视为现代政治哲学的奠基人之一。他由富有的伯父抚养，先后在牛津和剑桥受教育，长期担任卡文迪许家族的家庭教师和秘书。

1640年，他因《法律要旨》流传而逃往巴黎，一住十一年。在流亡的保王党人中，他写成《利维坦》，把国家比作由人组成的巨人，主张只有不可分割的主权者才能终结一切人对一切人的战争。该书的世俗精神使他与保王党人决裂，1651年逃回伦敦。

王政复辟后，查理二世给他100镑年金，并在1666年点名《利维坦》的反无神论法案中庇护了他；此后他不能出版有关人类行为的著作。他翻译了荷马，最终在哈德威克庄园去世，终年91岁，相传临终说的是“一次黑暗中的大跳跃”。

en:
Horatio Nelson (1758–1805) was the British admiral whose victories in the Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars made him the Royal Navy's greatest hero. He joined the navy in 1771, suffered lifelong seasickness and won his first command in 1778. In 1794 he partly lost his right-eye sight; at Cape St. Vincent in 1797 he broke from the line to board enemy ships, and lost his right arm at Tenerife later that year.

In 1798 he destroyed the French fleet at the Battle of the Nile. His affair with Emma Hamilton damaged his standing, and in 1801 he beat the Danish fleet at Copenhagen.

At Trafalgar on 21 October he signalled that England expected every man to do his duty and crushed the combined fleet. A French marksman shot him on HMS Victory; he died three hours later, aged 47. He received a state funeral.

霍雷肖·纳尔逊（1758—1805）是英国海军将领，在法国革命战争和拿破仑战争中屡建战功，成为皇家海军最伟大的英雄。他1771年加入海军，终生晕船，1778年首次获得指挥权。1794年右眼视力部分丧失；1797年在圣文森特角脱离战列线跳上敌舰，同年在特内里费失去右臂。

1798年他在尼罗河口海战中歼灭法国舰队。他与艾玛·汉密尔顿的私情损害了声望，1801年在哥本哈根击败丹麦舰队。

en:
Hugh le Despenser (c. 1308–1349), Lord of Glamorgan, was the son of Hugh Despenser the Younger. From 1326 he held Caerphilly Castle for Edward II against Isabella's forces, surrendering in 1327 on promise of his life, and was imprisoned until 1331.

Restored under Edward III, he inherited Glamorgan in 1337 and was summoned to Parliament as Baron le Despenser in 1338. He fought at Sluys, Morlaix and Crécy, joined the siege of Calais, and died in 1349 without issue.

Hugh le Despenser the Elder (1261–1326) served Edward I and was made a baron in 1295. Loyal to Edward II in the Piers Gaveston crisis, he became the king's chief administrator after Gaveston's execution in 1312.

Hatred of him and his son Hugh the Younger drove both into exile in 1321, but Edward recalled them and made the elder Despenser Earl of Winchester in 1322. When Isabella and Roger Mortimer invaded in 1326, he was captured at Bristol and hanged in his armour on 27 October.

en:
Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone (c. 1550–1616), was the leading Gaelic Irish lord in the Nine Years' War against Elizabeth I. Raised in the English Pale, he built up power in Ulster, secretly backing rebellion in the 1590s. He adopted firearms and continental tactics before his 1595 revolt, storming the Blackwater Fort.

Victory at the Yellow Ford in 1598 won him much of Ulster, but Spanish aid ended in defeat at Kinsale in 1601, and he submitted under the Treaty of Mellifont in 1603. He fled in the 1607 Flight of the Earls and died in Rome in 1616.

Humphrey de Bohun, fourth earl of Hereford (c. 1276–1322), succeeded his father in 1298 as earl of Hereford and Essex. In 1302 he married Edward I's daughter Elizabeth of Rhuddlan. He fought in the Scottish wars and was captured at Bannockburn in 1314, later exchanged for Robert Bruce's queen.

A leader of the Ordainers who imposed the Ordinances of 1311 on Edward II, he later turned against the Despensers and joined the earl of Lancaster's revolt. He was killed leading the rebel assault at Boroughbridge on 16 March 1322.

Idonia de Clifford (c. 1300 – 24 August 1365) was a daughter of Robert de Clifford, 1st Baron Clifford, killed at Bannockburn in 1314, and Maud de Clare. In that same year she married Henry de Percy, who as 2nd Baron Percy of Alnwick became one of Edward III's chief wardens of the Scottish marches.

She bore him six sons and four daughters, among them Henry, who succeeded as 3rd Baron Percy, Thomas, bishop of Norwich, and daughters Margaret, Maud and Eleanor, who married into the Ferrers, Neville and FitzWalter families.

Her daughter Isabel married William de Aton. Her husband died in February 1352 and was buried at Alnwick, and Idonia survived him by thirteen years.

en:
Inigo Jones (1573–1652), an English architect, first made his name designing court masques for Queen Anne of Denmark from 1605, introducing movable scenery and the proscenium arch to the English stage.

In 1613 he toured Italy, studying the villas of Andrea Palladio, his chief influence. He became Surveyor of the King's Works in 1615 and introduced classical architecture to England. His buildings include the Queen's House at Greenwich and the Banqueting House at Whitehall.

Captured when Basing House fell in 1645 during the Civil War, he was later released and fined. He died in London in 1652.

en:
Sir Isaac Newton (1643–1727) was an English mathematician and physicist, a central figure of the Scientific Revolution. Born prematurely at Woolsthorpe Manor, he was so small his mother said he could fit in a quart mug. After an attempt to make him a farmer, he entered Trinity College, Cambridge, in 1661. After his bachelor's degree he developed his theories of calculus, optics and gravitation.

In 1669 he became Lucasian Professor at twenty-six. His Principia of 1687 set out laws of motion and universal gravitation, uniting terrestrial and celestial motion. Opticks (1704) gathered his work on light, built on the prism splitting white light into colours.

He privately rejected the Trinity and pursued alchemy. From 1696 he served at the Royal Mint, hunting counterfeiters during the Great Recoinage. President of the Royal Society from 1703 and knighted in 1705, he died in 1727, the first scientist buried in Westminster Abbey.

艾萨克·牛顿爵士（1643—1727）是英国数学家、物理学家，科学革命的核心人物。他生于伍尔索普庄园，为早产儿，母亲说他小得能装进夸脱量杯。家人本想让他务农，1661年他入剑桥大学三一学院，毕业后发展出微积分、光学与引力理论。

1669年，二十六岁的他任卢卡斯数学教授。1687年《自然哲学的数学原理》提出运动定律与万有引力定律，统一天上与地上的运动。1704年的《光学》汇集其光学研究，基于棱镜将白光分解为各色光。

他私下否定三位一体，潜心研究炼金术。1696年起任职皇家造币厂，大重铸币期间追究伪币犯。1703年起任皇家学会会长，1705年封爵，1727年去世，成为首位入葬威斯敏斯特教堂的科学家。

他私下否定三位一体，潜心研究炼金术。1696年起任职皇家造币厂，大重铸币期间追究伪币犯。1703年起任皇家学会会长，1705年封爵，1727年去世，成为首位入葬威斯敏斯特教堂的科学家。

Isabel of Beaumont (c. 1318–1361), youngest daughter of Henry de Beaumont, Earl of Buchan, married Henry of Grosmont in 1330. She accompanied him on embassies, and when he was made Duke of Lancaster in 1351 she became the first Englishwoman to bear the title of duchess.

Her daughters Maud and Blanche married William V of Hainaut and John of Gaunt respectively, making her grandmother of Henry IV. She died of the plague at Leicester Castle in 1361, the same year as her husband.

en:
Isabel le Despenser (born c. 1312) was the eldest daughter of Edward II's favourite Hugh le Despenser the Younger. Her betrothal sealed an alliance between her father and Edmund FitzAlan, Earl of Arundel, and in February 1321, aged about eight, she married Edmund's seven-year-old heir Richard.

When her father was executed for treason in November 1326, the marriage saved her: of his daughters, only Isabel and her youngest sister escaped confinement in a nunnery, Isabel because she was already a wife.

Richard became earl in 1331 but later repudiated her. The marriage was annulled and their son Edmund was declared illegitimate, losing his claim to the earldom. Isabel was still living in 1356 and had died by 1375.

伊莎贝尔·德斯潘塞（约1312年生）是爱德华二世宠臣小休·德斯潘塞的长女。她的婚约巩固了父亲与阿伦德尔伯爵埃德蒙·菲查伦之间的联盟，1321年2月，年仅约八岁的她嫁给埃德蒙七岁的继承人理查德。

1326年11月父亲因叛国罪被处决时，这桩婚姻保住了她：他的女儿中，只有伊莎贝尔和最小的妹妹免于被关进修道院，伊莎贝尔是因为已经嫁人。

理查德于1331年袭伯爵位，后来却休弃她：婚姻被宣告无效，两人之子埃德蒙被定为私生子，失去伯爵爵位的继承权。伊莎贝尔1356年仍在世，1375年前去世。

Isabel de Percy (died before 25 May 1368) was a daughter of Henry de Percy, 2nd Baron Percy of Alnwick, and Idonia de Clifford. Before 1327 she married Sir William Aton of West Ayton in Yorkshire, a knight who served twice as High Sheriff of Yorkshire and was sometimes accounted 2nd Baron Aton.

Her son Sir William Aton died childless before June 1384 and the barony lapsed; her three daughters Anastasia, Katherine and Elizabeth became co-heiresses, marrying into the St John, Euer and Conyers families.

en:
Isabella of France (c. 1295–1358), later called the She-Wolf of France, was the daughter of Philip IV. She married Edward II in 1308 but could not tolerate his favourite Hugh Despenser the Younger, and by 1325 the marriage was at breaking point.

Sent to France on a diplomatic mission, she joined the exiled baron Roger Mortimer, and in 1326 landed in England with a small mercenary army while the king's forces deserted him. Edward II was deposed in January 1327 and died at Berkeley Castle that September. As regent for her son Edward III she made an unpopular but successful peace with Scotland.

On 19 October 1330 Edward III's men entered Nottingham Castle through a secret tunnel and seized Mortimer, who was executed at Tyburn. Isabella was held under house arrest for two years, then lived richly at Castle Rising until her death in 1358 as a Poor Clare.

法兰西的伊莎贝拉（约1295—1358），后世称为“法兰西母狼”，是法王腓力四世之女。1308年她嫁给爱德华二世，却无法容忍宠臣小休·德斯潘塞，到1325年婚姻已濒临破裂。

她以外交使命赴法，与流亡贵族罗杰·莫蒂默结盟，1326年率一支雇佣军登陆英格兰，国王的军队纷纷弃他而去。爱德华二世于1327年1月被废，同年9月死于伯克利城堡。她以儿子爱德华三世的名义摄政，缔结了不得人心却成功的对苏格兰和约。

1330年10月19日，爱德华三世的人马经一条秘密地道进入诺丁汉城堡，抓获莫蒂默，他后来在泰伯恩被处决。伊莎贝拉被软禁两年，此后迁居卡斯尔赖辛，生活富足，1358年以贫穷克拉拉会修女的身份去世。

Isabella of England (1332–1379/1382) was the eldest daughter of Edward III and Philippa of Hainault, born at Woodstock Palace. In 1365 she married Enguerrand de Coucy, a French nobleman held hostage after Brétigny.

De Coucy became Earl of Bedford, and her daughters were Marie and Philippa. She was made a Lady of the Garter in 1376. When de Coucy renounced England in 1377, she stayed and petitioned Richard II's Parliament as a deserted wife.

en:
Jack Sharp (died 1431), whose real name was William Perkins, was a weaver and town bailiff of Abingdon. In the spring of 1431 he put himself at the head of the Lollards of the southern midlands, circulating handbills as Jack Sharp of Wigmoreland that revived a scheme of 1410 to divert church endowments to secular uses.

The council offered a reward for his capture, and the regent Humphrey, Duke of Gloucester, suppressed the movement. Sharp was seized at Oxford on 17 May 1431 and executed five days later, his head being set on London Bridge.

James Audley, 2nd Baron Audley (1312/13–1386), lord of Heighley Castle, was an English peer and Marcher lord. He succeeded his father Nicholas Audley, 1st Baron Audley, and through his mother Joan Martin inherited the barony of Barnstaple and the Marcher lordship of Kemes.

In 1330 he married Joan Mortimer, daughter of Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March, who bore him his heir Nicholas and three children. After her death he married Isabel LeStrange in 1351.

James Cook (1728–1779) was a British Royal Navy officer, explorer and cartographer who led three voyages into the Pacific and Southern Oceans. A farm labourer's son from Yorkshire, he joined the Royal Navy in 1755; his Newfoundland surveys drew the Admiralty's attention. In 1768 his Endeavour sailed to observe the transit of Venus at Tahiti, then under sealed orders sought the southern continent, circumnavigating New Zealand and charting Australia's east coast.

His second voyage (1772–1775) took him three times across the Antarctic Circle without finding it. His third voyage (1776–1779), seeking a Northwest Passage, reached Hawaii, North America's northwest coast and the Bering Strait. His scurvy prevention earned the Royal Society's Copley Medal.

Back at Kealakekua Bay in the Resolution in February 1779 to repair a foremast, Cook tried to take the king hostage after a cutter was stolen, and fell with four marines on 14 February.

詹姆斯·库克（1728—1779）是英国皇家海军军官、探险家与制图师，三度率船远航太平洋和南大洋。他是约克郡农场工人之子，1755年加入皇家海军；他在纽芬兰的测绘工作引起海军部注意。1768年他乘“奋进号”前往塔希提观测金星凌日，随后依密令寻找南方大陆，环航新西兰并测绘澳大利亚东海岸。

第二次远航（1772—1775）中，他三次越过南极圈，始终没有找到南方大陆。第三次远航（1776—1779）为寻找西北航道，他抵达夏威夷、北美西北海岸并驶过白令海峡。他预防坏血病的措施为他赢得皇家学会的科普利奖章。

1779年2月，“决心号”因前桅折断折回凯阿拉凯夸湾修理，一艘小艇被偷后，库克试图劫持国王为人质，2月14日他与四名海军陆战队员在冲突中被杀。

Sir James Lancaster (c. 1554–1618) was an English privateer and pioneer of the East India trade. Raised in Portugal as a merchant, he returned to England in 1587 and fought the Spanish Armada in 1588.

In 1591 he led England's first voyage to the East Indies, reaching Penang; only twenty-five survived the return. After the East India Company was chartered in 1600, he commanded its first fleet to Bantam, where he founded its first factory, and was knighted by James I in 1603.

On that voyage he showed that daily lemon juice prevented scurvy. He remained a chief director of the company until his death.

詹姆斯·兰开斯特爵士（约1554—1618）是英格兰私掠船长，也是东印度贸易的先驱。他在葡萄牙长大，1587年返回英格兰，1588年参加抗击西班牙无敌舰队的战斗。

1591年他率领英格兰第一支东印度远航船队，抵达槟城，返航时仅25人生还。1600年东印度公司获特许成立后，他指挥公司首支船队驶往万丹，在当地建立第一个商馆，1603年被詹姆斯一世封为爵士。

这次航行中，他证明每日服用柠檬汁可以预防坏血病。此后他一直担任公司主要董事，直至去世。

Jane Austen (1775–1817) was an English novelist whose six novels comment wryly on the late-eighteenth-century landed gentry. Born at Steventon, Hampshire, a rector's daughter, she wrote stories for her family from about eleven. An early novel was declined by a publisher in 1797; another, sold in 1803 and never printed, she bought back in 1816.

She was thirty-five when Sense and Sensibility appeared anonymously in 1811, followed by Pride and Prejudice (1813), Mansfield Park (1814) and Emma (1815). They were moderate successes that brought her no fame, and explore women's dependence on marriage for security.

She rewrote the ending of Persuasion in 1816 and began Sanditon in 1817, stopping after twelve chapters. Taken to Winchester for treatment, she died on 18 July 1817, aged forty-one; her cathedral epitaph praises her character but never mentions her books. Northanger Abbey and Persuasion were published after her death.

简·奥斯汀（1775—1817）是英国小说家，六部小说以讽刺笔调评说18世纪末乡绅阶层。她生于斯蒂文顿，为教区长之女，十一岁便写家庭故事。一部早期小说1797年被退稿；另一部1803年售出未印，1816年才赎回版权。

1811年，三十五岁的她匿名出版《理智与情感》，随后是《傲慢与偏见》（1813）、《曼斯菲尔德庄园》（1814）与《爱玛》（1815）。销量尚可却未带来声名，探讨女性靠婚姻获得保障的处境。

1816年她重写《劝导》结尾，1817年开写《桑迪顿》，十二章后搁笔。她赴温切斯特求医，1817年7月18日病逝，年四十一；大教堂墓志铭称颂其品德，却不提她的作品。《诺桑觉寺》与《劝导》身后出版。

Lady Jane Grey (1536/1537–12 February 1554), the Nine Days' Queen, was a great-granddaughter of Henry VII through his daughter Mary Tudor, proclaimed queen at sixteen or seventeen. The Duke of Suffolk's eldest daughter, educated in Latin and Greek, married Northumberland's son Lord Guildford Dudley in May 1553.

As Edward VI lay dying, Northumberland feared Catholic Mary would undo the Reformation, so the king's will named Jane heir over Mary and Elizabeth. After Edward's death on 6 July, Jane was proclaimed on 10 July and entered the Tower, where she refused Guildford kingship, offering only a dukedom. Support for Mary grew, and on 19 July the Privy Council made her queen.

Northumberland was executed within a month; Jane was convicted of treason in November. Mary spared her until her father joined Wyatt's rebellion against the Spanish marriage; Jane and Guildford were beheaded at the Tower on 12 February 1554.

简·格雷郡主（1536/1537—1554年2月12日）世称“九日女王”，是亨利七世之女玛丽·都铎的外孙女，十六七岁时被宣布为女王。她是萨福克公爵的长女，受过拉丁文、希腊文教育。1553年5月，她嫁给诺森伯兰公爵之子吉尔福德·达德利勋爵。

爱德华六世病危时，诺森伯兰担心信奉天主教的玛丽会推翻宗教改革，国王的遗嘱便绕过玛丽和伊丽莎白，指定简继位。爱德华于1553年7月6日去世后，简在7月10日被宣布为女王并进入伦敦塔；在塔里她拒绝吉尔福德称王，只肯封他为公爵。支持玛丽的力量壮大，7月19日枢密院宣布玛丽为女王。

诺森伯兰不到一个月后被处决，简在11月被判叛国罪。玛丽本来饶她一命，直到她父亲参加反对女王西班牙婚姻的怀亚特叛乱；1554年2月12日，简与吉尔福德在伦敦塔被斩首。

Joan of Bar (c. 1295–1361), daughter of Henry III, Count of Bar, and Eleanor, was a niece of Edward II. In 1306 she married John de Warenne, 7th Earl of Surrey, who from 1313 vainly sought a divorce while keeping a mistress; Edward II lodged her at the Tower of London.

In 1352 John II made her regent of Bar for her great-nephew Robert. She ruled until 1356, when defeat at Poitiers lost her support, then returned to England and died in 1361.

Joan of Lancaster (c. 1312–1349) was the third daughter of Henry, 3rd Earl of Lancaster, and Maud de Chaworth. In 1327 she married John de Mowbray, 3rd Baron Mowbray; their children included John de Mowbray, 4th Baron Mowbray.

Her brother Henry of Grosmont was father of Blanche of Lancaster, wife of John of Gaunt and mother of Henry IV. Joan died of the plague in Yorkshire in 1349 and was buried at Byland Abbey.

Joan Mortimer (1311 or 1312 – between 1337 and 1351) was an English noblewoman, probably third daughter of Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March. Betrothed in childhood to James Audley, she was arrested after Mortimer fled into exile in 1323, and confined at Sempringham Priory on twelve pence a week.

Freed after her father seized power with Queen Isabella in 1326, she married Audley in 1328 or 1329 at a double wedding. Her children included Nicholas Audley, later Baron Audley.

Joan of England (1333/1334–1348) was a daughter of Edward III and Philippa of Hainault, born in the Tower of London. Betrothed in 1336 to the Duke of Austria's son, she lived at the imperial court until Edward III ended the match in 1340.

Joan of Kent (c. 1328–1385), the Fair Maid of Kent, was the daughter of Edmund of Woodstock, 1st Earl of Kent. In 1340 she secretly married Thomas Holland, but while he campaigned in France her family married her to William Montagu, Earl of Salisbury, annulled by the Pope in 1349.

She inherited Kent in 1352, and after Holland's death married Edward the Black Prince in 1361. Their younger son, born at Bordeaux in 1367, became Richard II. She died at Wallingford in 1385.

Joan of the Tower (1321–1362), youngest daughter of Edward II of England and Isabella of France, was born in the Tower of London. In July 1328 she married David, son of Robert the Bruce, and became queen of Scots when David II succeeded in 1329.

After Edward III won at Halidon Hill in 1333, the couple took refuge at the French court until 1341. David was captured at Neville's Cross in 1346 and held in England eleven years. Joan died childless at Hertford Castle in 1362, long estranged from him.

John I, called John of Aviz (1357–1433), was the illegitimate son of Peter I of Portugal, made master of the Order of Aviz in 1364. When his half-brother Ferdinand I died in 1383 without a male heir, Beatrice's claim threatened Castilian annexation, triggering the 1383–1385 interregnum. John led the revolt, was acclaimed king at Coimbra in 1385, and won the Battle of Aljubarrota on 14 August 1385.

He founded the Aviz dynasty, married Philippa of Lancaster in 1387, and conquered Ceuta in 1415, beginning Portugal's overseas expansion.

en:
John Cabot, born Giovanni Caboto (c. 1450–c. 1499), was an Italian navigator who sailed for England. A Venetian citizen, he traded in the Mediterranean before debts drove him from Venice in 1488, reaching London in 1495.

In 1496 Henry VII granted him letters patent to seek new lands. Sailing from Bristol on 2 May 1497, he made landfall in North America, probably Newfoundland, on 24 June and claimed it for England.

In 1498 he sailed with five ships; one reached Ireland after a storm, the others continuing. His fate and the expedition's outcome remain unknown.

John Capgrave (1393–1464) was an Augustinian friar, theologian and historian, born at Lynn in Norfolk. Ordained priest about 1417, he later headed the Austin friary at Lynn, where he received Henry VI in 1446, and became provincial of the Augustinians in England.

A prolific writer of biblical commentaries and saints' lives, he is best remembered for his English works: a metrical Life of St Katharine and a Chronicle of England running from the Creation to 1417. Humphrey, Duke of Gloucester, was his chief patron, and he died at Lynn on 12 August 1464.

John de Bohun, fifth earl of Hereford (1306–1336), was the eldest son of the fourth earl and Elizabeth of Rhuddlan, Edward I's daughter. His father's attainder after Boroughbridge in 1322 cost the family its lands, and John recovered the earldoms of Hereford and Essex after the Despensers' fall in 1326.

In 1325 he married Alice FitzAlan, and after her death Margaret Basset. Frail and largely inactive, he died on 20 January 1336, his titles passing to his brother Humphrey.

John Charlton, 1st Baron Charlton of Powys (1268–1353), rose from a Shropshire landowning family in Edward II's household. In 1309 he married Hawys Gadarn, heiress of the Welsh lordship of Powys, gaining Welshpool and laying the foundations of Powis Castle. In 1313 he was summoned to Parliament as Lord Charlton.

He fought the Scots, joined Lancaster's revolt against the Despensers in 1321, and in 1326 executed the Earl of Arundel on Queen Isabella's orders. He served as Justiciar of Ireland and died in 1353.

en:
John Charlton, 3rd Baron Charlton (c. 1336–1374), was the son of the 2nd baron and Maud Mortimer. In 1343 his grandfather arranged his marriage to Joan de Stafford, and he succeeded his father as baron in 1360.

Muster rolls for 1372 record him as a banneret leading 22 archers and men-at-arms on a naval expedition under Edward III. His sons John and Edward later became the 4th and 5th barons Charlton.

约翰·查尔顿（约1336—1374）为第三代查尔顿男爵，是第二代男爵与莫德·莫蒂默之子。1343年，祖父安排了他与琼·德·斯塔福德的婚事；1360年，他承袭父爵。

1372年的兵员名册记载，他以方旗骑士身份率二十二名弓箭手和披甲武士参加爱德华三世麾下的一次海上远征。他的儿子约翰和爱德华后来成为第四代、第五代查尔顿男爵。

en:
John of Padua (active 1543–1557) was an Italian architect and musician employed at the courts of Henry VIII and Edward VI, one of the foreign craftsmen who brought Renaissance architecture to England. His name first appears in the royal Treasury accounts on 30 January 1544, and between 1543 and 1557 the Exchequer paid him fees and a pension.

A Murano glassmaker's will made in London in 1551 describes him as architect and servant of the king. He disappears from the records after 1557.

约翰·迪·帕多瓦（活跃于1543—1557年）是效力于亨利八世与爱德华六世宫廷的意大利建筑师兼音乐家，也是把文艺复兴建筑带入英格兰的外来工匠之一。1544年1月30日，他的名字首次出现在王室财政账簿上；1543至1557年间，财政署向他支付酬金与年金。

John FitzAlan (born 1287) was the second son of Richard FitzAlan, 1st Earl of Arundel, and Alice of Saluzzo. While his elder brother Edmund succeeded to the earldom in 1302, John entered the Church as a priest.

He lived to a great age: the will of his nephew Richard FitzAlan, Earl of Arundel and Surrey, dated 5 December 1375, names him among its beneficiaries as my uncle John Arundell.

en:
John de Grey, first Baron Grey of Rotherfield (1300–1359), was an English soldier and courtier, the son of Sir John de Grey. He began soldiering in 1321, serving in Scotland and Gascony.

He wanted to marry Eleanor de Clare, widow of Hugh le Despenser the Younger, but lost her to William la Zouche after a quarrel that briefly put both men in prison. Summoned to parliament from 1338, he was one of the founding Knights of the Garter in 1348 and from 1349 served as Lord Steward of Edward III's household almost until his death.

He married first Katherine FitzAlan of Bedale and then Avice Marmion, and died in September 1359; his son John by Katherine succeeded as second baron.

他先娶比代尔的凯瑟琳·菲茨艾伦，再娶阿维斯·马米恩，1359年9月去世；凯瑟琳所生之子约翰继位为第二代男爵。

en:
John de Grey, second Baron Grey of Rotherfield (1319–1375), was the eldest son of the first baron, a founding Knight of the Garter, and Katherine FitzAlan. Born at Rotherfield in Oxfordshire, he succeeded his father in 1359, inheriting lands chiefly in Oxfordshire and Yorkshire, and married Maud de Burghersh, daughter of Bartholomew Burghersh.

His son John died before him. When John died at Rotherfield in June 1375 the barony passed to his grandson Bartholomew.

en:
Sir John Hawkins (1532–1595) was a Plymouth sea captain and naval administrator, born to a shipbuilding family. He worked in shipping and privateering until about 1559.

In the 1560s his voyages carried enslaved Africans to Spanish colonies in the Caribbean, making him the first English merchant to profit from the Atlantic slave trade.

As Treasurer of the Navy he rebuilt Elizabeth's fleet for speed and firepower, and in 1588 he served as vice-admiral against the Spanish Armada and was knighted for the victory. After his son's capture by the Spanish, he and Drake raised a fleet against the Spanish West Indies, and he died at sea off Puerto Rico on 12 November 1595.

约翰·霍金斯爵士（1532—1595）是普利茅斯的船长与海军事务官，出身造船家族，约1559年前从事航运与私掠事业。

1560年代，他的船队把被掳的非洲人贩运到加勒比海的西班牙殖民地，成为第一个从大西洋奴隶贸易中获利的英格兰商人。

任海军财务官期间，他改造伊丽莎白一世的舰队，使船只更快、火力更强；1588年他以副海军上将身份迎战西班牙无敌舰队，因战功受封骑士。儿子被西班牙人俘虏后，他与德雷克筹组舰队出击西属西印度群岛，1595年11月12日在波多黎各附近海上去世。

en:
John Holland, 1st Duke of Exeter and Earl of Huntingdon (c. 1352–1400), was Richard II's half-brother and loyal supporter. Made a Knight of the Garter in 1381, he killed Ralph Stafford during the 1385 Scottish expedition, forfeiting his lands, restored in 1386.

In 1386 he married Elizabeth, daughter of John of Gaunt. He became Earl of Huntingdon in 1388. After helping arrest the Duke of Gloucester in 1397 he became Duke of Exeter, losing the title when Henry IV took the throne in 1399.

In January 1400 he joined the Epiphany Rising to restore Richard; on its failure he was captured in Essex and beheaded on 16 January 1400.

en:
John (1166–1216), nicknamed Lackland, was the youngest son of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine, not expected to inherit much land. Made Lord of Ireland in 1177, he failed in a rebellion against Richard I's officials while the king was on crusade. He became king in 1199.

When war resumed in 1202, his forces captured rebel leaders including his nephew Arthur, whom historians believe John had murdered. The scandal undermined his rule, and Normandy and most of his French lands were lost by 1204. His judicial reforms raised revenue and shaped English common law.

His dispute with Pope Innocent III brought an interdict on England and his own excommunication. After defeat at Bouvines in 1214, barons forced him to agree to Magna Carta in 1215. Civil war followed, and John died of dysentery on 19 October 1216; his son Henry III's supporters won the next year.

约翰（1166—1216）绰号“无地王”，是亨利二世与阿基坦的埃莉诺的幼子，本不被指望继承多少土地。1177年他被封为爱尔兰领主，趁兄长理查一世参加十字军期间起兵反抗其官员，未能成功。1199年他即位为王。

1202年战事重启，他的军队俘获叛军首领，其中有他的侄子亚瑟，史家认为亚瑟是奉约翰之命被害。这桩丑闻动摇了他的统治，到1204年诺曼底和法国的大部分领地相继丧失。他的司法改革增加了收入，也影响了英格兰普通法。

他与教皇英诺森三世争执，英格兰被施以禁罚，他本人也被革除教籍。1214年布汶战败后，男爵们于1215年迫使他同意《大宪章》。内战随即爆发，1216年10月19日约翰死于痢疾；他的儿子亨利三世的支持者于次年获胜。

他与教皇英诺森三世争执，英格兰被施以禁罚，他本人也被革除教籍。1214年布汶战败后，男爵们于1215年迫使他同意《大宪章》。内战随即爆发，1216年10月19日约翰死于痢疾；他的儿子#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('eng_henry_iii').GetID],X #L 亨利三世#!#!的支持者于次年获胜。

en:
John de Grey, called John Marmion, was the elder son of John de Grey, first Baron Grey of Rotherfield, by Avice Marmion, through whom the Marmion estates at West Tanfield had come to the Greys.

Knighted, he married Elizabeth, a daughter and co-heiress of Sir Herbert St Quintin. A retainer of John of Gaunt, he sailed with the duke's 1386 campaign to press his claim to Castile and died in Spain in 1387, leaving no children.

His niece Elizabeth, daughter of his brother Robert, inherited the Marmion lands; his widow lies with him beneath the alabaster effigies in West Tanfield church.

约翰·德·格雷又称约翰·马米恩，是第一代罗瑟菲尔德的格雷男爵约翰·德·格雷与阿维斯·马米恩的长子；母亲一方把马米恩家族在西坦菲尔德的产业带入格雷家。

他受封骑士，娶赫伯特·圣昆廷爵士的女儿及共同继承人之一伊丽莎白为妻。作为冈特的约翰的随从，他1386年随公爵出征，为其卡斯蒂利亚王位主张作战，1387年死于西班牙，没有子嗣。

马米恩家族的产业由弟弟罗伯特之女、他的侄女伊丽莎白继承；他的遗孀与他合葬于西坦菲尔德教堂，墓上的夫妇雪花石膏墓像保存至今。

en:
John Milton (1608–1674) was an English poet and republican polemicist, remembered above all for the epic Paradise Lost. At Christ's College, Cambridge, his fair complexion earned him the nickname the Lady of Christ's College. Before the Civil War he wrote pamphlets against bishops. When his young wife left him in 1642 he published divorce tracts; the outcry prompted Areopagitica (1644), against censorship.

After the regicide he defended the people's right to call rulers to account, and in 1649 became Secretary for Foreign Tongues, handling the Commonwealth's Latin letters. By 1652 he was totally blind, dictating to helpers. His writings against the 1660 Restoration led to arrest, imprisonment and the burning of his books.

In retirement he dictated Paradise Lost (1667), on Adam and Eve's temptation and fall, followed by Paradise Regained and Samson Agonistes (1671). He died in November 1674, poor and marginal but famous across Europe.

约翰·弥尔顿（1608—1674）是英格兰诗人和共和派政论家，以史诗《失乐园》闻名。他就读剑桥大学基督学院，因肤色白皙得绰号“基督学院小姐”。内战前夕他撰文抨击主教；1642年年轻妻子离去后，他发表离婚小册子，招来的敌意促使他写成《论出版自由》（1644），抨击事前审查。

弑君后他为人民追究统治者的权利辩护，1649年任外文事务秘书，负责共和国拉丁文文书。1652年他完全失明，靠助手笔录。他反对1660年王政复辟，被捕入狱，著作遭焚。

晚年他口述《失乐园》（1667），讲述亚当和夏娃受诱惑而堕落，1671年又成《复乐园》与《力士参孙》。1674年11月去世，贫困潦倒、身处边缘，却已名满欧洲。

John Montagu, 3rd Earl of Salisbury (c. 1350–1400), was an English nobleman and one of the firmest partisans of Richard II. A prominent Lollard, he succeeded his uncle as Earl of Salisbury in 1397, helped overthrow the Duke of Gloucester, and became a Knight of the Garter.

He accompanied Richard's last expedition to Ireland and was sent to Wales against Henry Bolingbroke, but his men deserted. Henry IV imprisoned him in the Tower after seizing the throne.

Released, he joined the Epiphany Rising of January 1400 to restore Richard; he was captured by townspeople at Cirencester and beheaded without trial on 7 January 1400.

第三代索尔兹伯里伯爵约翰·蒙塔古（约1350—1400）是英格兰贵族，也是理查二世最坚定的支持者之一。他是著名的罗拉德派信徒，1397年继承叔父的索尔兹伯里伯爵之位，参与扳倒格洛斯特公爵，后来成为嘉德骑士。

他随理查参加最后一次爱尔兰远征，奉命赴威尔士对抗亨利·博林布鲁克，但部众溃散。亨利四世夺位后将他囚于伦敦塔。

获释后，他于1400年1月参与意在复辟理查的主显节起义，在赛伦塞斯特被市民俘获，未经审判即于1月7日被斩首。

John de Montagu, 1st Baron Montagu (c. 1330–c. 1390), was a younger son of William Montagu, 1st Earl of Salisbury, and Catherine Grandison, and brother of the 2nd earl. Froissart records him at the Siege of Calais in 1349, and in 1357 he was summoned to parliament as Baron Montagu.

He married Margaret de Monthermer, heiress of Thomas, 2nd Baron Monthermer; their son John inherited the earldom of Salisbury from his uncle in 1397 and became the 3rd earl.

John de Mowbray, 3rd Baron Mowbray (1310–1361), was the son of the 2nd Baron, who was hanged after the Battle of Boroughbridge in 1322 for opposing Edward II; he and his mother were held in the Tower until 1327. Restored, he married Joan, daughter of Henry, 3rd Earl of Lancaster.

He served at the sieges of Nantes and Aiguillon and fought at Neville's Cross in 1346. He died of plague at York in 1361.

John of Eltham (1316–1336), Earl of Cornwall, was the second son of Edward II and Isabella of France and younger brother of Edward III. Created earl in 1328, he served as Guardian of the Realm during Edward III's absences.

In 1333 he was a leading commander at Halidon Hill, where the Scots were crushingly defeated, and he later led troops in south-western Scotland. He died at Perth, probably of fever, just after turning twenty and was buried in Westminster Abbey.

John, 3rd Earl of Kent (1330–1352), was the posthumous son of Edmund of Woodstock, 1st Earl of Kent, executed three weeks before his birth. When his elder brother Edmund died in 1331, John succeeded to the earldom. He took part in the 1346 Crécy campaign and received his inheritance from Edward III in 1347.

In 1348 he married Isabella of Jülich, and in 1349 inherited the Wake estates. He died childless at Woking in 1352, his titles passing to his sister Joan of Kent.

en:
Sir John Oldcastle (c. 1370–1417) was a Herefordshire knight and Lollard leader. He fought against Owain Glyndŵr in Wales. Sheriff of Herefordshire in 1406–1407, he married the Cobham heiress in 1408 and sat in parliament as Lord Cobham. A trusted soldier of Henry V, he was convicted of heresy in 1413 and escaped from the Tower of London.

In January 1414 he led a Lollard rising scattered at St Giles's Fields. Captured in Wales in November 1417, he was hanged and burnt in London on 14 December.

John de Stratford (c. 1275–1348) was a civil lawyer from Stratford-on-Avon who became Bishop of Winchester in 1323 and Archbishop of Canterbury in 1333. In 1326 he joined Queen Isabella against Edward II and urged the king to abdicate at Kenilworth. Under Edward III he was three times chancellor and the king's leading councillor.

His quarrel with Edward in 1340 helped establish that peers should be tried only in parliament. Reconciled, he died at Mayfield in 1348.

John Thornton of Coventry (fl. 1405–1433) was the leading English stained-glass painter of the early fifteenth century. In 1405 he contracted with the dean of York Minster to glaze the choir east window.

He completed the Great East Window three years later; at 1680 square feet, it is the largest expanse of medieval stained glass in the world. Thornton designed its histories and images, became a freeman of York in 1410, and was again paid by York Minster in 1433. His workshop spread the International Gothic style across northern England and the Midlands.

John de Warenne, 6th Earl of Surrey (1231–1304), was an English commander under Henry III and Edward I. In 1247 he married Henry III's half-sister Alice of Lusignan. In the Second Barons' War he changed sides twice, fighting for the king at Lewes in 1264 and Evesham in 1265; after Lewes he fled to the Continent before his confiscated estates were restored.

After the Welsh campaigns of 1277–1283, Edward I made him warden of Scotland. He commanded at Dunbar in 1296 but was routed by William Wallace at Stirling Bridge in 1297 and fought at Falkirk in 1298. He died on 27 September 1304, leaving the earldom to his grandson.

en:
John de Warenne, 7th Earl of Surrey (1286–1347), was the last Warenne earl of Surrey. A minor when his grandfather died in 1304, he became a royal ward and in 1306 received his lands and married Edward I’s granddaughter Joan of Bar. The marriage was childless and his attempts at divorce failed.

In 1312 he helped capture Edward II’s favourite Piers Gaveston. A private war with Thomas, Earl of Lancaster, cost him much of his estates; after sitting in judgment on Lancaster in 1322, he recovered his Yorkshire lands in 1326. One of the last earls loyal to Edward II, he went over to Queen Isabella after Arundel's execution and urged the king's abdication in 1327.

As guardian of Edward Balliol he joined his Scottish campaign and was named earl of Strathearn. He died at Conisbrough Castle in 1347, the earldom passing to his nephew Richard FitzAlan.

en:
John Wycliffe (c. 1328–1384) was an Oxford theologian and priest whose attack on the wealth and authority of the Church made him the forerunner of the English Reformation. He became Master of Balliol College in 1361 and took his doctorate in 1372. In 1374 he negotiated with papal envoys at Bruges and received the living of Lutterworth.

His book On Civil Dominion argued that the Church should surrender its property and the clergy live in poverty. John of Gaunt took his side, but after rejecting transubstantiation in 1380, Wycliffe lost Gaunt's support. Itinerant poor priests carried his teaching across England, and his followers became known as Lollards.

He is traditionally linked with an English Bible. He withdrew to Lutterworth and died after a stroke in 1384. His writings shaped the Czech reformer Jan Hus, and in 1428 his remains were dug up, burned and cast into the River Swift.

约翰·威克里夫（约1328—1384）是牛津大学神学家和神父，他对教会财富与权威的攻击使他成为英国宗教改革的先驱。他1361年任巴利奥尔学院院长，1372年获神学博士学位，1374年在布鲁日与教皇使节谈判，并获得拉特沃思的教区俸禄。

他在《论世俗统治》中主张教会应交出财产、神职人员安于清贫。冈特的约翰一度站在他一边，但1380年后他否定化质说，因此失去冈特的支持。云游的贫穷教士把他的主张传遍英格兰，追随者被称为罗拉德派。

传统认为他与一部英文圣经有关。他退居拉特沃思，1384年中风去世。他的著作影响了捷克改革家扬·胡斯，1428年他的遗骨被掘出焚毁，骨灰撒入斯威夫特河。

Sir Joshua Reynolds (1723–1792) was the leading English portrait painter of the 18th century and theorist of the Grand Style, which sought to idealise the imperfect. Born at Plympton in Devon, he apprenticed to a portraitist in 1740 and in 1749 spent two years in Rome studying the Old Masters.

His prolific London studio produced more than two thousand paintings. In 1768 he became the first president of the Royal Academy of Arts, was knighted by George III in 1769 and delivered his influential Discourses. He died in February 1792 and was buried in St Paul's Cathedral.

Julian of Norwich (c. 1343–after 1416) was an English anchoress enclosed at St Julian's Church, Norwich. On 8 May 1373, gravely ill at thirty, she received sixteen visions of Christ's Passion; recovering on 13 May, she wrote them first in a Short Text and, decades later, in the Long Text Revelations of Divine Love, the earliest surviving book in English by a woman.

Her longer work explored the meaning of her visions after years of reflection. She counselled the pilgrim Margery Kempe, and the Long Text stayed in manuscript until 1670, long after her death.

诺里奇的朱利安（约1343—1416年后）是英格兰女隐修者，隐居于诺里奇圣朱利安教堂的隐修室。1373年5月8日，年约三十、病危的她见到基督受难的十六次异象；5月13日痊愈后，她先写成短本，数十年后又扩充为长本《神圣之爱的启示》，这是现存最早由女性撰写的英语著作。

长本是她多年反思后对异象意义的探讨。她曾为朝圣者玛格丽·肯佩提供灵性指导，长本以抄本流传，直到她去世多年后的1670年才首次刊印。

Sir Edmund Mortimer (1302/1303 – 16 December 1331) was the eldest son of Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March. He married Elizabeth de Badlesmere in 1316, and during his father's exile was imprisoned in the Tower of London from 1326; Edward III knighted him in 1327.

His father was executed in 1330 and the family lands forfeited. Edmund regained them at Wigmore in October 1331, but died of fever that December, leaving a young son, Roger.

Laurence Hastings, 1st Earl of Pembroke (1319–1348), born at Allesley in Warwickshire, was the son of John Hastings, 2nd Baron Hastings. Succeeding as Baron Hastings in 1325, he inherited Valence lands and in 1339 Edward III made him Earl of Pembroke.

In the Hundred Years' War he fought in Brittany and Aquitaine, took Bergerac in 1345, defended Aiguillon in 1346 and joined the Calais siege in 1347. He married Agnes Mortimer and died at Abergavenny in 1348, leaving his son John as heir.

Eleanor of Castile (1241–1290), daughter of Ferdinand III of Castile and Joan of Ponthieu, married the future Edward I near Burgos in 1254, a match to secure English rule over Gascony. During the Second Barons' War, Simon de Montfort's government imprisoned her at Westminster Palace.

She joined Edward's Ninth Crusade in 1270–1271 and was at Acre when an assassin wounded him. From 1279 she held Ponthieu in her own right and amassed large estates in England, which made her unpopular.

She died at Harby near Lincoln in November 1290. The grieving Edward erected memorial crosses, later called the Eleanor crosses, at every stop of her cortège to London.

1290年11月她逝于林肯附近的哈比；悲痛的爱德华在她灵柩运往伦敦途中的每一处停灵点竖立纪念十字架，后世称为“埃莉诺十字”。

Luisa Carvajal y Mendoza (1566–1614) was a Spanish noblewoman born in Extremadura. Orphaned young, she was raised by her uncle the Marquis of Almazán, studied literature and theology, and in 1598 took a vow of martyrdom.

In late 1605 she reached London to join the Catholic underground, teaching and visiting imprisoned priests. She was jailed in 1608 after preaching in Cheapside, and again in October 1613, when the archbishop charged her with founding a convent. Ordered expelled, she died of fever at the embassy on 2 January 1614.

en:
Lady Margaret Beaufort (1443–1509) was an English noblewoman of the Wars of the Roses and mother of Henry VII, founder of the Tudor dynasty. Daughter of John Beaufort, she inherited a claim to the throne, married Edmund Tudor, and in 1457, aged thirteen, bore her only child, the future Henry VII.

She conspired against Richard III, and her husband Thomas Stanley helped win Bosworth Field in 1485. Under her son she wielded great influence and patronised printing and learning.

She founded Christ's College, Cambridge, in 1505, and also began St John's College, completed by her executors in 1511. She died on 29 June 1509.

玛格丽特·博福特女领主（1443—1509）是玫瑰战争时期的英格兰贵族女性，也是都铎王朝开国君主亨利七世的母亲。她是约翰·博福特之女，继承了王位宣称，嫁给埃德蒙·都铎，1457年年仅十三岁时生下独子，即后来的亨利七世。

她密谋反对理查三世，1485年博斯沃思原野战役中，她的丈夫托马斯·斯坦利帮助奠定胜局。儿子在位期间她权势很大，奖掖印书与学术。

1505年她创办剑桥大学基督学院，还着手创办圣约翰学院，该学院由遗嘱执行人于1511年完成。她于1509年6月29日去世。

Margaret of Norfolk (c. 1322–1399) was the daughter of Thomas of Brotherton, Earl of Norfolk. After her brother Edward died childless in 1334, she and her sister Alice became heirs; in 1338 Margaret succeeded to the earldom of Norfolk and the office of Earl Marshal.

In 1335 she married John de Segrave. She sought an annulment in 1350 and crossed the Channel in disguise against the king's prohibition. After Segrave's death in 1353 she married Walter Manny, and in 1397 Richard II created her Duchess of Norfolk.

Margaret Percy (born c.1318, died 1375) was a daughter of Henry Percy, 2nd Baron Percy of Alnwick, by Idonia Clifford. By a marriage licence of January 1340 she married Sir Robert d'Umfraville, only son of the Earl of Angus, who died without issue before 1368. Before May that year she married, as his second wife, William Ferrers, 3rd Baron Ferrers of Groby; this marriage too was childless.

Her will as Ferrers's widow was dated 26 April 1374. She died in Essex on 2 September 1375 and was buried in the Dominican friars' church at Chelmsford.

因财政原因，她从未举行加冕礼。她于1300年生下布劳瑟顿的托马斯、1301年生下伍德斯托克的埃德蒙、1306年生下埃莉诺；1307年爱德华一世去世后她没有再嫁，1318年去世。

en:
Maud de Balliol (born 1257, alive in 1340) was a daughter of John de Balliol and Dervorguilla of Galloway, and a sister of John Balliol, king of Scots from 1292. Before July 1297 she became the second wife of Bryan FitzAlan of Bedale, a guardian of Scotland and her brother's close ally.

By him she had two daughters, Agnes and Katherine, who after his death in 1306 became his co-heiresses: Agnes married Sir Gilbert Stapleton, while Katherine married John de Grey, first Baron Grey of Rotherfield.

Long a widow, Maud was still living in April 1340, when she granted church lands to Egglestone Abbey for masses for herself and her dead kin; she was later buried in the Black Friars' church at York.

莫德·德·巴里奥（1257年生，1340年仍在世）是约翰·德·巴利奥尔与加洛韦的德沃尔吉拉之女，1292年即位为苏格兰国王的约翰·巴里奥之妹。1297年7月之前，她嫁给比代尔的布莱恩·菲茨艾伦为续弦，他是苏格兰护国者之一，也是其兄的亲信。

两人生有阿格尼丝与凯瑟琳两女；1306年丈夫死后，两女成为共同继承人，阿格尼丝嫁给吉尔伯特·斯特普尔顿爵士，凯瑟琳嫁给第一代罗瑟菲尔德的格雷男爵约翰·德·格雷。

莫德长年寡居，1340年4月仍在世，当时她把教会土地授予埃格尔斯通修道院，为自己和已故亲人的灵魂举行弥撒；身后葬于约克的黑衣修士教堂。

Maud de Chaworth (1282–1322) was the only child of Patrick de Chaworth, lord of Kidwelly. Her father died in 1283, leaving her a wealthy heiress and ward of Queen Eleanor; in 1286 her mother married Hugh Despenser the Elder, making Hugh Despenser the Younger her half-brother.

In 1292 Edward I granted her marriage to Edmund Crouchback, and in 1297 she married Edmund's son Henry, later Earl of Lancaster. She bore seven children, including Henry of Grosmont.

en:
Maud of Lancaster (c. 1310–1377) was a daughter of Henry, 3rd Earl of Lancaster, and Maud Chaworth. In 1327 she married William de Burgh, Earl of Ulster, and lived in Ireland, where their daughter Elizabeth was born. After William was murdered near Carrickfergus in 1333, she fled with her daughter to Edward III's court.

Her second husband, Ralph de Ufford, was Justiciar of Ireland until his death in 1346. Widowed again, she became a canoness at Campsey Priory, later a Poor Clare at Bruisyard Abbey, where she died in 1377.

Maud Mortimer (c. 1307–after 1345) was an English noblewoman, probably a daughter of Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March, and Joan de Geneville. Before 1319 she married John Charlton, heir to the 1st Baron Charlton of Powys.

en:
Sir Miles Stapleton of Bedale (c. 1316–1364), eldest son of Sir Gilbert Stapleton and Agnes FitzAlan, was an English knight and a founder Knight of the Garter. Through his father he was a great-grandson of Dervorguilla of Galloway, mother of King John Balliol.

He served at the siege of Tournai in 1340, fought in the Breton War of Succession and was probably at Calais in 1347. In 1348 he took a stall in the new Order of the Garter. In 1354 he joined an embassy to Pope Innocent VI seeking aid in the Anglo-French war.

In 1361 the crown granted him a £100 annuity for his unwearied labours. He probably joined a Prussian crusade in 1363 and died in December 1364, perhaps of wounds from Auray.

en:
Nicholas of Hereford (died 1420) was an Oxford theologian and a leading follower of John Wycliffe. Ordained in 1370, he became a Doctor of Theology and briefly chancellor of Oxford University in 1382. He criticised the Church's luxury, defended lay Bible reading, and helped produce Wycliffe's English Bible, translating much of the Old Testament.

Condemned for heresy in 1382, he appealed to the pope in Rome and was imprisoned before escaping in 1385. Back in England he was jailed again but recanted in 1391 and later held church office; he died a Carthusian in Coventry in 1420.

en:
Oliver Cromwell (1599–1658) was the Parliamentarian commander who defeated Charles I, ended the English monarchy and ruled the British Isles as Lord Protector. After years of failure he joined the Parliamentarian army, leading the New Model Army's cavalry from 1645, earning the nickname Old Ironsides. He pressed for Charles I's execution in 1649, then conquered Ireland with a brutality that still divides opinion, and invaded Scotland in 1650–1651.

In April 1653 he forcibly dissolved the Rump Parliament, becoming Lord Protector that December. In 1657, after six weeks' deliberation, he refused Parliament's offer of the crown, saying he would not rebuild Jericho. He died at Whitehall on 3 September 1658.

His son Richard resigned in 1659, and Charles II returned in 1660. On 30 January 1661, anniversary of Charles I's execution, Cromwell's corpse was dug up and hanged at Tyburn; his displayed head was buried at Cambridge in 1960.

奥利弗·克伦威尔（1599—1658）是击败查理一世、终结英格兰君主制，并以护国公身份统治不列颠诸岛的议会军统帅。早年屡遭挫折后，他加入议会军，1645年起指挥新模范军骑兵，得到“老铁骑军”的绰号。1649年他力主处死查理一世，随后征服爱尔兰，其残酷至今仍引起争议，又在1650—1651年入侵苏格兰。

1653年4月他以武力解散残缺议会，同年12月就任护国公。1657年，他对议会献上的王冠思虑六周后拒绝，称自己不愿重建耶利哥。1658年9月3日他在白厅去世。

其子理查1659年辞职，1660年查理二世复位。1661年1月30日，即查理一世被处决的周年，克伦威尔的遗体被掘出，在泰伯恩处以绞刑；他的头颅被示众，最终于1960年安葬在剑桥。

Owain ap Thomas ap Rhodri, called Owain Lawgoch, ‘red-handed Owain’ (c. 1330–1378), was a Welsh soldier and the last male-line heir of the princely House of Aberffraw, a descendant of Llywelyn the Great and claimant to the title of Prince of Wales. As captain of a largely Welsh free company, he fought the English for Charles V, who knew him as Yvain de Galles.

He lost his English lands in 1369. In a treaty with Charles he declared English kings had slain or driven out his ancestors and wrongly held Wales, and the king promised men and ships to win it back. The invasion never landed: after he attacked Guernsey, Charles ordered him to seek ships in Castile.

At Soubise he defeated an English and Gascon force and captured Thomas Percy and Jean de Grailly. An English agent assassinated him at the siege of Mortagne in July 1378.

欧文·阿普·托马斯·阿普·罗德里，人称欧文·劳戈赫，意为‘红手欧文’（约1330—1378），是威尔士军人，也是阿伯弗劳王公家族最后的男系继承人，为大卢埃林的后裔，并以威尔士亲王头衔的继承人自居。他率一支以威尔士人为主的自由兵团，为法王查理五世对英作战，被法国人称作‘伊万·德·加勒斯’。

1369年他失去英格兰的土地。他在与查理的条约中宣称，英格兰诸王杀害或驱逐他的先祖、非法占据威尔士，法王许以人马舰船助他夺回。入侵始终未能登陆：欧文进攻根西岛后，查理命他赴卡斯蒂利亚寻找船只。

在苏比斯他击败英格兰与加斯科涅联军，俘虏托马斯·珀西和让·德·格赖伊。1378年7月围攻莫尔塔涅时，他被英格兰刺客暗杀。

en:
Philippa of Hainault (c. 1310–1369), daughter of William I, Count of Hainaut, and Joan of Valois, was engaged in 1326 to Edward, Prince of Wales, and married him at York Minster in January 1328, months after his accession.

As queen she turned Edward's attention to England's commercial expansion, accompanied him on campaign and served as regent in 1346, when she was present at the victory of Neville's Cross. In 1347 she persuaded him to spare the Burghers of Calais, a mercy that won her the affection of the English.

She died at Windsor Castle in August 1369 after a happy forty-year marriage and was buried in Westminster Abbey, where Edward was laid beside her eight years later. She left thirteen children, whose descendants' rivalry later brought on the Wars of the Roses.

埃诺的菲利帕（约1310—1369）是埃诺伯爵威廉一世与瓦卢瓦的让娜之女。1326年她与威尔士亲王爱德华订婚，1328年1月在爱德华登基数月之后，两人于约克大教堂成婚。

作为王后，她促使丈夫关注英格兰的商业扩张，随他出征，并在1346年出任摄政，亲临内维尔十字之战的胜利。1347年，她说服国王赦免加来义民，这份怜悯使她深得英格兰人的爱戴。

1369年8月她病逝于温莎城堡，结束了四十年美满的婚姻，葬于威斯敏斯特教堂，八年后爱德华也安葬在她身旁。她留下十三个子女，后裔之间的争夺后来引发了玫瑰战争。

Ralph Neville, 2nd Baron Neville of Raby (c. 1291–1367), son of the first Lord Neville, was a leading soldier of the English north. In 1326 he married Alice de Audley, who bore him thirteen children including his heir John. He served as warden of the Scottish marches.

His greatest feat came in 1346, when he led the English army to a crushing victory over a Scottish invasion at the Battle of Neville's Cross near Durham and captured King David II. He died in 1367.

Pocahontas (c. 1596–1617), later baptized Rebecca, was the daughter of Powhatan, leader of Virginia's Powhatan Confederacy. After the English founded Jamestown she became linked with the colony, and John Smith made their encounters famous. Seized for ransom by the colonists in 1613, she converted to Christianity and in 1614 married John Rolfe; their son Thomas was born in 1615.

They travelled to London in 1616, where she was presented to English society to encourage investment in Jamestown and fêted at court. She died at Gravesend in March 1617, about to return to Virginia.

宝嘉康蒂（约1596—1617），受洗后取名丽贝卡，是弗吉尼亚波瓦坦联盟首领波瓦坦之女。英格兰人建立詹姆斯敦后，她与殖民地产生关联，约翰·史密斯让两人的交往广为人知。1613年她被殖民者掳走勒索赎金，其间皈依基督教，1614年嫁给约翰·罗尔夫，儿子托马斯于1615年出生。

1616年夫妇二人前往伦敦，她被介绍给英格兰社会以吸引对詹姆斯敦的投资，并在宫廷受到款待。1617年3月，即将返回弗吉尼亚之际，她在格雷夫森德去世。

Sir Richard Arkwright (1732–1792) was an English inventor and industrialist of the early Industrial Revolution, born at Preston. Starting as a barber and wig-maker, he used income from a waterproof wig dye to fund his machinery work. He turned to cotton spinning, and in 1769 he patented the spinning frame, later called the water frame, which produced strong warp thread.

In 1771 he built a water-powered mill at Cromford in Derbyshire, combining mechanised carding and spinning and creating the model for the factory system. His patents were overturned in court in 1785, but he was knighted in 1786 and died in 1792.

理查德·阿克莱特爵士（1732—1792）是英国工业革命早期的发明家与实业家，生于普雷斯顿。他早年做过理发师和假发匠，用防水假发染料的收入资助机械研制。他后来转而研究棉纺，1769年取得纺纱机（后称水力纺纱机）的专利，机器能纺出坚韧的经纱棉线。

1771年，他在德比郡克罗姆福德建成水力纺纱厂，把机械化的梳棉与纺纱集中在一处，开创了现代工厂制度的范本。他的专利于1785年被法庭推翻，但他在1786年受封爵士，1792年去世。

Richard Chancellor (c. 1521–1556) was a Bristol-born navigator who opened England's trade with Russia. In 1553 he sailed as second-in-command of Hugh Willoughby's expedition in search of a north-east passage to Asia. Separated by storms, his ship reached the White Sea, and he travelled by sleigh to Moscow, where Tsar Ivan IV granted English merchants trading privileges.

Chancellor returned in 1554 and helped form the Muscovy Company, revisiting Russia in 1555. Sailing home with Russia's first ambassador to England, he was drowned when his ship was wrecked off the Scottish coast on 10 November 1556.

Richard FitzAlan, Earl of Arundel (1267–1302), inherited the earldom and the Welsh Marcher lordships of Clun and Oswestry from his father John in 1272. Knighted by Edward I in 1289, he fought through the Welsh wars of 1288–1294 and led a force to relieve Castell y Bere when Madog ap Llywelyn besieged it.

His opposition to the king in the 1295 crisis left him heavily indebted and cost him part of his lands. He later campaigned in Gascony and in Edward I's Scottish wars. Before 1285 he married Alice of Saluzzo; their son Edmund succeeded him.

en:
Richard Fitzalan, earl of Arundel (c. 1313–1376), was the son of Edmund Fitzalan and Alice de Warenne. His father backed the Despensers, and Richard was married as a boy to Hugh the Younger’s daughter Isabel; the father was executed in 1326, and Richard inherited neither title nor estates.

By 1330 politics had shifted, and he gradually recovered the earldom and his family's lands. He became a trusted commander of Edward III and justiciar of North Wales in 1334. As Admiral of the West he fought at Sluys in 1340 and was one of three principal commanders at Crécy in 1346, guarding the Black Prince in the rearguard.

In 1344 the pope annulled his underage, unwilling Despenser marriage; in 1345 he married Eleanor of Lancaster, the king attending. He died at Arundel Castle on 24 January 1376, leaving sixty thousand pounds in cash.

en:
Richard I (1157–1199), called the Lionheart, was King of England from 1189. A younger son of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine, he became heir only after his elder brothers died. Sent to subdue the rebellious Aquitanian barons, he won his nickname in that fighting.

His reign was spent on crusade, in captivity or defending his French lands. In 1191 he took Acre and led the crusade after Philip II of France went home, beating Saladin at Arsuf. He never took Jerusalem, and in 1192 signed a three-year truce with Saladin.

Seized shortly before Christmas 1192, he was handed to Emperor Henry VI, who demanded 150,000 marks. He was freed in 1194; Philip is said to have warned John that the devil was loose. In 1199 a crossbow bolt struck him at a siege; he died after forgiving his killer, leaving no legitimate heir, and John succeeded him.

Richard of Cornwall (1209–1272), second son of King John, was made Earl of Cornwall by his brother Henry III in 1225, and his Cornish revenues made him among Europe's richest men. He rebelled against Henry three times. In 1231 he married Isabel Marshal of a family often opposed to the king. He joined the Barons' Crusade in 1240, freeing prisoners and refortifying Ascalon.

In 1257 he bought election as King of the Romans for twenty-eight thousand marks and was crowned at Aachen. Captured in a windmill after Lewes in 1264, he was held until September 1265 and died at Berkhamsted on 2 April 1272.

en:
Robert Aske (c. 1500–1537) was a Yorkshire barrister who led the Pilgrimage of Grace, the rising of 1536 against Henry VIII's dissolution of the monasteries. Returning from London when rebellion broke out, he took up the rebels' cause as it spread across the northern counties. As chief captain he led nine thousand insurgents who occupied York and restored expelled monks and nuns.

In November he negotiated with the Duke of Norfolk and went to London, where the king promised redress. When fighting resumed, Henry had him seized; Aske was convicted of treason and executed at York on 12 July 1537.

Robert Blake (1598–1657) was an English naval commander born in Somerset. He fought for Parliament in the Civil War, holding Lyme Regis in 1644 and Taunton in 1645. Made a general at sea in 1649, he pursued Prince Rupert's fleet from Ireland to the Mediterranean, and fought the Dutch at Dungeness (1652) and the Gabbard (1653).

The Fighting Instructions he issued with fellow commanders in 1653 codified the line-ahead formation. He burned the corsair fleet at Porto Farina in 1655 and destroyed the Spanish treasure fleet at Santa Cruz de Tenerife in April 1657, and died off Plymouth in August 1657.

en:
Robert Boyle (1627–1691) was an Anglo-Irish natural philosopher, regarded as the first modern chemist and a pioneer of the experimental method. Born at Lismore Castle, son of the Earl of Cork, he was sent to Eton and in 1641 studied Galileo's writings in Florence before returning in 1644.

He joined the Invisible College circle and in 1654 moved to Oxford. After reading of Otto von Guericke's vacuum pump, he and Robert Hooke improved it into the machina Boyleana by 1659. In 1662 he stated that the volume of a gas varies inversely with pressure, the rule known as Boyle's law.

His Sceptical Chymist (1661) is a cornerstone of chemistry. When the circle became the Royal Society in 1663 he joined its council, later declining the presidency. From 1668 he lived in London with his sister Katherine; he died on 31 December 1691, and his will endowed the Boyle Lectures.

罗伯特·波义耳（1627—1691）是英裔爱尔兰自然哲学家，被视为第一位现代化学家和实验方法的先驱。他生于利斯莫尔城堡，是科克伯爵之子，后入伊顿公学，1641年在佛罗伦萨研读伽利略的著作，1644年回国。

他加入研讨新哲学的“无形学院”，1654年迁往牛津。读到奥托·冯·格里克的真空泵后，他与罗伯特·胡克把它改进成“波义耳机”，1659年完成。1662年他提出气体体积与压强成反比，这就是波义耳定律。

1661年出版的《怀疑派化学家》是化学史上的基石。1663年该团体改组为皇家学会，他进入理事会，后来又辞谢了会长一职。1668年起他在伦敦与姐姐凯瑟琳同住，1691年12月31日去世，遗嘱设立了波义耳讲座。

Robert III of Artois (1287–1342) was the claimant whose lawsuit over the County of Artois helped push France and England into the Hundred Years' War. After his grandfather Robert II fell at Courtrai in 1302, the county went to his aunt Mahaut. In 1328 Philip VI compensated him with Beaumont-le-Roger, but after Mahaut died in 1329 Robert reopened the claim.

In 1331 he was convicted of using his father's forged will, backed by false depositions and a document from Jeanne de Divion, who was burned. Sentenced in absentia in 1332, he fled through Namur and Brabant to Edward III, whose council he joined with his knowledge of the French court.

Philip cited Edward's refusal to expel him when confiscating Guyenne in 1337. Robert commanded an Anglo-Flemish army at Saint-Omer in 1340 and died of dysentery after the retreat from Vannes in 1342.

Sentenced in absentia in 1332, he fled through [ShowLocationName('namur')] and [GetCountry('BRB').GetName] to #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('eng_edward_iii').GetID],X #L Edward III#!#!, whose council he joined with his knowledge of the French court.

Philip cited Edward's refusal to expel him when confiscating Guyenne in 1337. Robert commanded an Anglo-Flemish army at [ShowLocationName('saint_omer')] in 1340 and died of dysentery after the retreat from [ShowLocationName('vannes')] in 1342.

阿图瓦的罗贝尔三世（1287—1342）是为争夺阿图瓦伯国而打官司、把法英两国推向百年战争的人。1302年祖父罗贝尔二世在科特赖克阵亡，伯国由姑母马奥继承。1328年腓力六世把博蒙勒罗歇封给他作补偿，但1329年马奥去世后，罗贝尔又重提继承之争。

1331年，他因使用伪造的父亲遗嘱被判有罪，伪证和让娜·德·迪维翁伪造的文书支撑了这份遗嘱，让娜后来被烧死。1332年他被缺席判处放逐，经那慕尔、布拉班特逃亡，最后投奔英格兰国王爱德华三世，进入其会议，把法国宫廷的底细告诉他。

1337年腓力没收吉耶讷，理由是爱德华不肯驱逐罗贝尔。罗贝尔于1340年在圣奥梅尔指挥英佛联军，1342年自瓦讷撤退后死于痢疾。

en:
Robert Kett (c. 1492–1549) was a landowner of Wymondham in Norfolk, thought to have been a tanner, who led Kett's Rebellion against the enclosure of common lands during the Duke of Somerset's protectorate. After riots in July 1549 he gathered some sixteen thousand followers on Mousehold Heath, enforced camp discipline, and presented demands to the crown to limit the gentry's power and protect communal resources.

His men took Norwich on 1 August, but he rejected a royal pardon. On 27 August John Dudley, Earl of Warwick, crushed the rebels at Dussindale. Kett was convicted of treason and hanged from Norwich Castle on 7 December 1549.

罗伯特·凯特（约1492—1549）是诺福克郡温登姆的地主，据信曾是制革匠，在萨默塞特公爵护政期间领导了反对圈占公地的凯特起义。1549年7月骚乱后，他在毛斯霍尔德荒野集结约一万六千人，整肃营规，并向王室提出诉求，要求限制乡绅权力、保护公共资源。

8月1日，起义者攻占诺里奇，凯特拒绝了王室赦免。8月27日，沃里克伯爵约翰·达德利在杜辛德尔击溃起义军。凯特以叛国罪被定罪，于1549年12月7日被吊死于诺里奇城堡。

Robert de Grey, called Robert Marmion, was the younger son of John de Grey, first Baron Grey of Rotherfield, by Avice Marmion. He married Lora, younger daughter and co-heiress of Sir Herbert St Quintin, and had by her one daughter, Elizabeth.

Robert died before November 1367, in his elder brother's lifetime. When his brother John Marmion died without children in 1387, Robert's daughter Elizabeth, by then the wife of Sir Henry FitzHugh, inherited the Marmion estates.

en:
Robert Shirley (c. 1581–1628) was an English traveller and adventurer. In 1598 he accompanied his brother Anthony to Safavid Persia, where he trained Shah Abbas I's army and reformed its artillery on English lines, helping Persia hold its own in the Ottoman war of 1603–1612. In 1607 he married the Circassian Sampsonia, later Lady Teresa.

From 1608 Abbas sent him to European courts seeking an alliance against the Ottomans; in Poland and Rome the emperor and pope made him a count. In 1627 his third journey to Persia with the English ambassador ended in his death at Qazvin in 1628.

en:
Robert Walpole, 1st Earl of Orford (1676–1745), a Norfolk Whig, is regarded as Britain's first prime minister and held office longer than any successor. Born at Houghton, he entered Parliament in 1701. In 1712 he was impeached for corruption and spent six months in the Tower, returning to office in 1714.

After the South Sea Bubble collapse, he became First Lord of the Treasury and Chancellor of the Exchequer in 1721. For twenty years, an era later dubbed the Robinocracy, he kept Britain out of European wars, held taxes low and encouraged trade, though he had to withdraw his 1733 excise scheme amid protest.

Pushed by king and Commons, he reluctantly went to war with Spain in 1739. After a narrow defeat in Parliament in 1742 he resigned and became Earl of Orford. He rebuilt Houghton Hall and filled it with Old Master paintings, dying on 18 March 1745.

第一代奥福德伯爵罗伯特·沃波尔（1676—1745）是诺福克乡绅出身的辉格党人，被视为英国第一位首相，任期之长无人超过。他生于霍顿，1701年进入议会。1712年他因贪腐指控被弹劾，在伦敦塔被关了六个月，1714年重返政坛。

南海泡沫破灭后，他于1721年出任第一财政大臣兼财政大臣。此后二十年，后人称这一时期为“罗宾政治”，他使英国置身于欧洲战争之外，保持低税，鼓励贸易，不过他1733年的消费税计划遭反对而被迫撤回。

1739年，在国王和下议院的压力下，他不情愿地对西班牙开战。1742年他在议会险败后辞职，受封奥福德伯爵。他重建了霍顿堂，收藏大量古典大师画作，1745年3月18日去世。

en:
Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March (1287–1330), was a marcher lord. His 1301 marriage to Joan de Geneville won him Welsh March and Irish lands, and he became Lord Lieutenant of Ireland in 1316. He led the marcher lords against Edward II and was imprisoned in the Tower in 1322, but escaped to France.

He allied with Queen Isabella; their 1326 invasion deposed Edward, whose murder at Berkeley Castle Mortimer allegedly arranged. He ruled in young Edward III's name until seized at Nottingham in 1330 and hanged at Tyburn.

en:
Roger Mortimer, 2nd Earl of March (1328–1360), was grandson of the man who had ruled England in the name of the boy Edward III. That first earl was seized at Nottingham Castle in October 1330 and executed, and the family estates were confiscated.

Roger recovered the Mortimer lands and title and distinguished himself in the wars in France. The Black Prince knighted him at La Hogue in 1346, and he fought at Crécy. In 1348 he was among the founding knights of the Order of the Garter.

He married Philippa, daughter of William Montagu, Earl of Salisbury, the companion who had helped Edward III seize his grandfather. Roger died in 1360, leaving his son Edmund as third earl.

Samuel Pepys (1633–1703) was a London-born naval administrator and diarist. He became Clerk of the Acts to the Navy Board in 1660 and later rose to Chief Secretary to the Admiralty, helping professionalise the Royal Navy.

From 1660–1669 he kept a diary recording the Restoration court, the Second Anglo-Dutch War, the Great Plague of 1665 and the Great Fire of 1666, until failing eyesight stopped him. He was President of the Royal Society from 1684 to 1686.

塞缪尔·皮普斯（1633—1703）是生于伦敦的海军官员与日记作家。他于1660年出任海军委员会文书官，后来官至海军部首席秘书，推动了皇家海军的专业化。

1660至1669年间，他坚持撰写私人日记，记录了王政复辟时期的宫廷、第二次英荷战争、1665年伦敦大瘟疫和1666年伦敦大火，后因视力衰退而停笔。1684至1686年，他担任皇家学会会长。

en:
Simon Sudbury (c. 1316–1381) was Bishop of London from 1361 and Archbishop of Canterbury from 1375. He crowned Richard II at Westminster Abbey in July 1377, and in January 1380 became Lord Chancellor of England.

Held responsible for the third poll tax, he was targeted in the Peasants' Revolt: rebels who had freed John Ball stormed the Tower of London, dragged Sudbury to Tower Hill and beheaded him on 14 June 1381. His body was buried at Canterbury Cathedral.

西蒙·萨德伯里（约1316—1381）自1361年任伦敦主教，1375年起任坎特伯雷大主教。1377年7月，他在威斯敏斯特教堂为理查二世加冕，1380年1月出任英格兰大法官。

他被认为是第三次人头税的主要推手，因而在1381年农民起义中成为目标：释放了约翰·鲍尔的起义者冲入伦敦塔，把他拖到塔山，于6月14日斩首。他的遗体葬于坎特伯雷大教堂。

en:
Stephen of Blois (c. 1096 – 1154), a nephew of Henry I, was king of England from 1135. He held vast English estates through his wife Matilda of Boulogne, and the White Ship disaster of 1120, in which Henry's heir drowned, left the succession open to challenge.

On Henry's death in 1135 Stephen seized the throne, breaking his oath to support his daughter, the Empress Matilda. Her 1139 invasion opened the long civil war known as the Anarchy; Stephen was captured at Lincoln in 1141 but later freed. After his own son Eustace died, he recognised Matilda's son Henry as heir by the 1153 Treaty of Winchester, and died in October 1154.

布卢瓦的斯蒂芬（约1096—1154）是亨利一世的外甥，自1135年起为英格兰国王。他凭借妻子布洛涅的玛蒂尔德在英格兰拥有大片地产；1120年亨利的继承人溺死于白船海难，王位继承因此面临争议。

1135年亨利一世去世后，斯蒂芬违背支持其女玛蒂尔达皇后的誓言，夺取王位。1139年玛蒂尔达入侵，开启史称‘无政府时期’的长期内战；1141年斯蒂芬在林肯被俘，后来获释。其子尤斯塔斯死后，他于1153年签订《温彻斯特条约》，承认玛蒂尔达之子亨利为继承人，1154年10月去世。

en:
Swein Forkbeard (died 1014), son of Harald Bluetooth, seized the Danish throne from his father in 986. In 994 he joined Olaf Tryggvason raiding England until the English paid sixteen thousand pounds in tribute, and around 1000 defeated and killed Olaf at the Battle of Svold, making himself overlord of Norway.

In 1013 he invaded England to conquer it; by December the English accepted him as king and Æthelred fled to Normandy. He ruled only weeks, dying on 3 February 1014 and leaving the claim to his son Cnut.

en:
Thomas de Beauchamp, 12th Earl of Warwick (1338–1401), was an English nobleman and chief opponent of Richard II. He campaigned in France with John of Gaunt and became a Knight of the Garter, and in the parliaments of 1376 and 1377 was appointed to supervise government reform.

In 1387 he was one of the Lords Appellant moving against the king's favourites. Lured to London in 1397, he was attainted and held in the Tower and on the Isle of Man. Freed when Henry Bolingbroke seized the throne in 1399, he was restored to his earldom and died in 1401.

第十二代沃里克伯爵托马斯·德·比彻姆（1338—1401）是英格兰贵族，也是理查二世的主要反对者之一。他曾随冈特的约翰出征法国，后成为嘉德骑士，1376年和1377年的议会任命他监督政府改革。

1387年，他作为“上诉贵族”之一，起兵反对国王的宠臣。1397年他被诱捕至伦敦，剥夺爵位与财产，先后囚禁于伦敦塔和曼岛。1399年亨利·博林布鲁克夺取王位后他获释，恢复伯爵爵位，1401年去世。

en:
Thomas Cromwell (c. 1485–1540), a tradesman's son from Putney, rose through Cardinal Wolsey's service to become Henry VIII's chief minister from 1534. He helped annul Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon after the pope refused, and Parliament endorsed the king's claim to be Supreme Head of the Church of England.

As royal vicar general he directed the dissolution of the monasteries and reformed administration. He helped bring down Anne Boleyn in 1536 and was made Earl of Essex in 1540, but the failed match with Anne of Cleves destroyed him. He was beheaded on Tower Hill on 28 July 1540.

en:
Sir Thomas Gresham (c. 1519–1579) was a London merchant and royal financier to Edward VI, Mary I and Elizabeth I. Appointed the crown's agent in Antwerp in 1551, he negotiated royal loans abroad and worked to support the pound after the Henrician debasements. Knighted in 1559, he served as envoy in the Netherlands until unrest forced him to leave Antwerp in 1567.

From London he continued his business and in 1565 founded the Royal Exchange, opened by the queen in 1571; his bequest established Gresham College. He died on 21 November 1579, and Gresham's law is named for him.

托马斯·格雷沙姆爵士（约1519—1579）是伦敦商人兼王室金融家，历仕爱德华六世、玛丽一世与伊丽莎白一世三朝。1551年，他被任命为王室驻安特卫普代表，在海外为王室筹措贷款，并在亨利八世时代货币贬值之后设法支撑英镑币值。1559年他受封骑士，出任驻尼德兰使节，1567年动荡迫使他离开安特卫普。

Thomas Harriot (c. 1560–1621) was an Oxford-educated mathematician, astronomer and navigator employed by Sir Walter Raleigh as his mathematics tutor. He joined the 1585 expedition to Roanoke, learned the local Algonquian language, and in 1588 published A Briefe and True Report of the New Found Land of Virginia, his only printed work.

Under the Earl of Northumberland's patronage he was credited with discovering the law of refraction and devised binary arithmetic decades before Leibniz. On 5 August 1609 he made the first known drawing of the Moon through a telescope, preceding Galileo. He died in 1621, leaving most of his work unpublished.

托马斯·哈里奥特（约1560—1621）是牛津出身的数学家、天文学家和航海专家，受雇于沃尔特·罗利并教授他数学。他参加1585年的罗阿诺克远征，学会当地的阿尔冈昆语，并于1588年出版《弗吉尼亚新大陆见闻实录》，这是他生前唯一付印的著作。

en:
Sir Thomas More (1478–1535) was an English lawyer, humanist and statesman, author of Utopia and Henry VIII's Lord Chancellor, who went to the scaffold rather than accept the king as head of the Church. After Oxford and legal training in London, he was called to the bar in 1502 and considered monastic life before choosing the world. His Utopia (1516), about an imaginary island, made him famous across Europe.

Lord Chancellor from 1529 to 1532 after Wolsey's fall, he refused to acknowledge Henry as supreme head of the Church or the annulment of his marriage to Catherine.

Convicted of treason on what he said was false evidence, he was beheaded at Tower Hill on 6 July 1535, reportedly saying he died the king's good servant, and God's first. Erasmus called his character purer than snow. The Church canonised More in 1935.

托马斯·莫尔爵士（1478—1535）是英格兰律师、人文主义者和政治家，《乌托邦》的作者，亨利八世的大法官，最终宁可走上断头台，也不承认国王是教会领袖。他在牛津受教后到伦敦学习法律，1502年取得律师资格，曾一度考虑做修士，最终选择俗世生活。1516年的《乌托邦》描绘了一个虚构岛国，使他名扬欧洲。

沃尔西倒台后，他在1529至1532年任大法官，但拒绝承认亨利是教会最高领袖，也不接受国王与凯瑟琳的婚姻被判无效。

他依据在他看来是伪证的证词被判叛国罪，1535年7月6日在塔山被斩首，相传临终说他是国王的忠臣，但首先是上帝的忠臣。好友伊拉斯谟称他品格比雪还纯净。1935年，教会封他为圣徒。

Thomas of Brotherton (1300–1338) was an English prince and Earl of Norfolk, the fifth son of Edward I and his second queen Margaret of France, and half-brother of Edward II. Created Earl of Norfolk in 1312 and Earl Marshal in 1316, he was despoiled of lands by the Despensers and joined Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer in 1326.

He sat in judgment on the Despensers and, as Lord Marshal, commanded the right wing at Halidon Hill in 1333. He died in 1338, his titles passing to his daughter Margaret.

布劳瑟顿的托马斯（1300—1338）是英格兰王子、诺福克伯爵，爱德华一世第五子，由第二任王后法兰西的玛格丽特所生，是爱德华二世的异母弟。1312年他受封诺福克伯爵，1316年出任英格兰司礼官；德斯潘塞父子侵夺他的土地，他遂于1326年加入伊莎贝拉王后与罗杰·莫蒂默一方。

Thomas Paine (1737–1809) was an English-born political writer and revolutionary from Thetford in Norfolk. He reached Philadelphia in 1774 with Franklin's recommendation. Common Sense (January 1776), signed only 'by an Englishman', blamed George III and argued for separation plainly.

His American Crisis papers, opening 'These are the times that try men's souls', were read to Washington's troops. Back in England, his Rights of Man (1791) answered Edmund Burke's attack on the French Revolution; threatened with arrest, he fled to France in September 1792 and was convicted of seditious libel in absentia.

Elected to the National Convention despite no French, he was jailed by the Montagnards in December 1793 until James Monroe freed him in November 1794. His deist Age of Reason made him notorious, and in America after 1802 he was widely shunned. He died in New York on 8 June 1809; only six mourners attended his funeral.

托马斯·潘恩（1737—1809）是出生于英国的政治作家与革命者，来自诺福克郡塞特福德。1774年他带着富兰克林的推荐信抵达费城。1776年1月出版的《常识》只署名“一个英国人”，以浅白语言把责任归于国王乔治三世并主张脱离英国。

他的《美国危机》开篇写道“这是考验人类灵魂的时刻”，华盛顿曾下令向军队宣读。回到英国后，他1791年出版《人的权利》，回应埃德蒙·柏克对法国大革命的攻击；面对逮捕威胁，他1792年9月逃往法国，被缺席判处煽动诽谤罪。

他不会说法语仍被选入国民公会，但1793年12月被山岳派投入监狱，1794年11月由詹姆斯·门罗救出。他主张自然神论的《理性时代》使他声名狼藉，1802年返回美国后广受冷落。1809年6月8日他在纽约去世，葬礼只有六人出席。

Thomas Percy (c. 1332–1369) was a younger son of Henry Percy, 2nd Baron Percy of Alnwick, commander of the English right wing at Neville's Cross. While his elder brother carried on the barony, he entered the Church.

Nominated Bishop of Norwich in 1355 and consecrated the next year, he held the East Anglian see until his death in August 1369, a little over a year after his brother, the 3rd Baron Percy.

Thomas Percy, 7th Earl of Northumberland (1528–1572), was an English Catholic nobleman whose father was executed after the Pilgrimage of Grace. Restored to his lands under Mary I, he retook Scarborough Castle in 1557 and was created earl, later warden of the northern marches.

In 1569 northern Catholics planned to free Mary, Queen of Scots and win freedom of worship. That November Percy joined Westmorland in the Rising of the North, occupying Durham and hearing Mass. He fled to Scotland, was captured and sold to the crown for two thousand pounds, and was beheaded at York on 22 August 1572 rather than renounce his faith. He was beatified in 1895.

Thomas Farnolls Pritchard (baptised 1723–1777) was an English architect and interior decorator born in Shrewsbury. Trained as a joiner, he designed provincial churches and houses, created rococo interiors such as the ballroom at Powis Castle, and specialised in chimney-pieces and funerary monuments.

After moving to Eyton on Severn in 1769 he farmed while continuing his architectural work, and adapted timber-bridge principles to design a cast-iron arch over the Severn at Coalbrookdale. Cast in 1777–1779, the Iron Bridge was the world's first cast-iron bridge, but Pritchard died in December 1777 before its completion.

托马斯·法诺尔斯·普里查德（1723年受洗—1777）是英国建筑师与室内装饰师，生于什鲁斯伯里。他早年学做细木工，在地方上设计教堂与宅邸，创作了波伊斯城堡舞厅等洛可可室内装饰，擅长壁炉饰件和墓碑。

1769年他迁居塞文河畔艾顿，一边务农一边继续建筑工作，又将木桥原理用于设计横跨科尔布鲁克代尔塞文河的铸铁拱桥。该桥于1777至1779年浇铸，即世界上第一座铸铁桥“铁桥”，但普里查德已于1777年12月去世，未能见到它完工。

Thomas Savery (c. 1650–1715) was an English military engineer and inventor from Devon, who held the rank of captain. On 2 July 1698 he patented the first commercially used steam-powered machine, a steam pump for draining mines and supplying towns with water, demonstrated to the Royal Society and described in his treatise The Miner's Friend.

Its condensing steam created a partial vacuum to draw water up, but the pump wasted heat and could not work effectively in deep mines. Parliament extended his patent in 1699, and his work in Dartmouth probably brought him into contact with Thomas Newcomen.

托马斯·塞维利（约1650—1715）是英国德文郡出身的军事工程师与发明家，获上尉军衔。1698年7月2日，他为第一台投入商业使用的蒸汽动力装置——用于矿井排水和城镇供水的蒸汽泵——取得专利，曾向皇家学会演示，并在专著《矿工之友》中加以说明。

蒸汽冷凝形成局部真空将水吸上，但该泵浪费热量，在深矿中难以有效使用。议会于1699年延长其专利，他在达特茅斯的工作可能使他结识了托马斯·纽科门。

Sir Thomas Shirley (c. 1542–1612), of Wiston in Sussex, was an English landowner, Member of Parliament and courtier under Elizabeth I. From 1586 he served as Treasurer-at-War with the English forces in the Netherlands, but speculation with army funds left him deep in debt to the Crown, and his estate was sequestered in 1602.

Arrested for debt in 1604 despite claiming parliamentary privilege, he was imprisoned in the Fleet; the House of Commons secured his release, and Parliament then passed an act confirming members' freedom from arrest. He was the father of the adventurers Anthony and Robert Shirley, who both served Shah Abbas I of Persia.

Thomas Tallis (c. 1505–1585) was an English composer who served the Chapel Royal under Henry VIII, Edward VI, Mary I and Elizabeth I. After posts at Dover Priory, Waltham Abbey—where he received forty shillings when it was dissolved in 1540—and Canterbury Cathedral, he joined the Chapel Royal around 1543 and shaped Tudor church music through decades of religious change.

In 1575 Elizabeth I granted him and his pupil William Byrd a monopoly on printing music, and they published the Cantiones sacrae. His works include the forty-voice motet Spem in alium and settings of the Lamentations. He died at Greenwich in November 1585.

托马斯·塔利斯（约1505—1585）是英格兰作曲家，先后在亨利八世、爱德华六世、玛丽一世与伊丽莎白一世的王室礼拜堂供职。他早年历任多佛尔修道院、沃尔瑟姆修道院（1540年解散时领到四十先令）与坎特伯雷大教堂的乐职，约1543年进入王室礼拜堂，在数十年宗教更迭中塑造了都铎教堂音乐。

1575年伊丽莎白一世授予他与学生威廉·伯德印制乐谱的垄断权，两人同年出版了一部宗教经文歌集。他的作品包括一首四十声部经文歌和为《耶利米哀歌》谱写的乐曲，1585年11月在格林尼治去世。

Thomas Wake, second Baron Wake of Liddell (1297–1349), inherited his barony as an infant in 1300; Piers Gaveston and Henry, Earl of Lancaster, were his guardians, and before 1317 he married Lancaster's daughter Blanche. Opposed to Edward II's favourites, he joined Queen Isabella's invasion in 1326.

He turned against Roger Mortimer and fled to France in 1330 after the Earl of Kent's execution. Restored under Edward III, he governed the Channel Islands and aided Edward Balliol's invasion of Scotland, dying childless in 1349.
