Thomas Wolsey (c. 1473–1530) was Henry VIII's chief minister and a cardinal. Son of an Ipswich butcher, he rose to become Archbishop of York in 1514, then cardinal and Lord Chancellor in 1515. As papal legate he directed policy and organised the Field of the Cloth of Gold in 1520.

He founded Cardinal College, but after failing to secure the king's annulment from Catherine of Aragon he fell from power in 1529, and died at Leicester Abbey on 29 November 1530 on his way to London to face a treason charge.

Thomas of Woodstock, Duke of Gloucester (1355–1397), was the youngest son of Edward III, born at Woodstock Palace. Created Earl of Buckingham in 1377 and Duke of Gloucester in 1385, he campaigned in France before turning on his nephew Richard II.

As leader of the Lords Appellant he defeated the king's favourite Robert de Vere at Radcot Bridge in December 1387 and dominated the Merciless Parliament of 1388, which purged Richard's circle. In 1397 Richard had him arrested and imprisoned at Calais, where he was smothered in September, probably on the king's orders.

Thomas Holland, Duke of Surrey and 3rd Earl of Kent (1372–1400), was an English nobleman and a nephew of Richard II. He succeeded his father as Earl of Kent in 1397, arrested his uncle the Earl of Arundel in the purge of the Lords Appellant, and was created Duke of Surrey that September.

After Henry IV deposed Richard in 1399 he lost the dukedom. He was a ringleader of the Epiphany Rising in January 1400, plotting to kill Henry and restore Richard; the rising failed and he was captured at Cirencester and beheaded without trial on 7 January 1400.

Tomas ap Rhodri, or Thomas Rothery (c. 1300–c. 1363), was the only son of Rhodri ap Gruffudd, youngest brother of the Welsh princes Llywelyn and Dafydd ap Gruffudd. He inherited his father's estates in Cheshire and Surrey, later exchanging the Cheshire lands for holdings in Gloucestershire and Powys.

As Owain Goch's closest male heir he made an unsuccessful claim to the lordship of Llŷn. By his wife Cecilia he fathered Owain Lawgoch, who proclaimed himself Prince of Wales in 1369.

Sir Walter Raleigh (c. 1552–1618) was a Devon-born courtier, explorer and writer, and a favourite of Elizabeth I. Knighted in 1585, he received a royal patent to colonise North America and sponsored the Roanoke settlements, naming the territory Virginia.

His secret marriage in 1591 to Elizabeth Throckmorton cost him the queen's favour and the Tower. In 1595 he sailed to Guiana in search of El Dorado. Imprisoned under James I from 1603 for involvement in the Main Plot, he was released in 1616 for a second Guiana voyage; after his men attacked a Spanish outpost, he was executed in 1618.

Wat Tyler (1341–1381) was the Kentish leader of England's Peasants' Revolt. In June 1381, angered by the third poll tax, he led rebels from Canterbury to London demanding reforms; they burned the Savoy Palace, stormed the Tower and executed the chancellor.

After Richard II granted the rebels' demands at Mile End, Tyler parleyed with him at Smithfield the next day, where the Lord Mayor Walworth slashed him down; he was beheaded and his head displayed on London Bridge. Richard revoked them and the revolt collapsed.

William Caxton (c. 1422–c. 1491) was an English merchant who introduced printing to England. Settled in Bruges, he learned the craft in Cologne and set up a press with Colard Mansion, and in 1473 printed his translation of the Recuyell of the Historyes of Troye, the first book printed in English. Margaret of York, Duchess of Burgundy, had encouraged him to complete the translation.

In 1476 he established England's first press at Westminster, issuing Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur in 1485, and many translations of his own. He died in 1491.

William Cecil, 1st Baron Burghley (1520–1598), was the chief minister of Queen Elizabeth I for almost the whole of her reign. He first became Secretary of State under Edward VI in 1550 and returned to the office at Elizabeth's accession in 1558; created Baron Burghley in 1571, he became Lord High Treasurer the following year.

He sought a Protestant British Isles through control of Ireland and alliance with Scotland, and strengthened the navy. In 1587 he persuaded the queen to execute Mary, Queen of Scots, implicated in a plot against Elizabeth. He died in 1598, and his son Robert Cecil succeeded to his power.

William Gilbert (1544–1603) was a Colchester-born physician and natural philosopher educated at St John's College, Cambridge. He became president of the Royal College of Physicians in 1600 and served as physician to Elizabeth I from 1601, later retained by James I.

His six-volume De Magnete (1600) described experiments with his terrella, a spherical lodestone model, and argued that the Earth itself is a great magnet, explaining why compasses point north. He also argued that the Earth rotates daily. He also studied static electricity from amber, used the word electricus for attractive properties, and invented the versorium, the first electrical instrument.

His six-volume De Magnete (1600) described experiments with his terrella, a spherical lodestone model, and argued that the Earth itself is a great magnet, explaining why compasses point north. He also argued that the Earth rotates daily. He also studied static electricity from amber, used the word electricus for attractive properties, and invented the versorium, the first electrical instrument.

威廉·吉尔伯特（1544—1603）生于科尔切斯特，是就读于剑桥大学圣约翰学院的医生与自然哲学家。他1600年出任皇家内科医学院院长，1601年起担任伊丽莎白一世的御医，詹姆斯一世继位后继续留用。

en:
William II Rufus (c. 1057 – 2 August 1100), third son of William the Conqueror, ruled England from 1087. He crushed the 1088 revolt led by Bishop Odo, forced homage from Malcolm III of Scotland, built Carlisle Castle and saw Malcolm killed at Alnwick in 1093. His quarrel with Archbishop Anselm ended in Anselm's exile in 1097.

From 1096 he held Normandy in pledge while Robert Curthose went on crusade. On 2 August 1100 an arrow killed him hunting in the New Forest, and his brother Henry seized the crown.

威廉二世（绰号鲁弗斯，约1057年—1100年8月2日）是征服者威廉的第三子，自1087年起统治英格兰。他镇压了1088年主教奥多领导的叛乱，迫使苏格兰国王马尔科姆三世称臣，修建卡莱尔城堡，1093年马尔科姆在阿尼克毙命。他与大主教安瑟伦长期冲突，安瑟伦最终于1097年流亡。

1096年起，罗贝尔·柯索斯参加十字军，诺曼底抵押给他管辖。1100年8月2日，他在新森林狩猎时中箭身亡，其弟亨利随即夺取王位。

William Montagu, 1st Earl of Salisbury (1301–1344), born at Cassington, was the closest companion of Edward III. In 1330 he helped the king overthrow Roger Mortimer at Nottingham. He fought in the Scottish Wars, received the Isle of Man and ruled it as king, and in 1337 was created Earl of Salisbury.

Captured by the French in 1340, he promised never to fight in France again. He died in 1344 of wounds sustained at a tournament.

William Montagu, 2nd Earl of Salisbury (1328–1397), born at Donyatt, succeeded his father as earl and King of Mann in 1344 and was a founder knight of the Garter. He married Joan of Kent, whose secret marriage to Thomas Holland was upheld; the pope annulled Montagu's marriage in 1349.

He fought at Poitiers in 1356 and negotiated the Treaty of Bretigny in 1360. He supported Richard II against Wat Tyler's revolt and sold the Isle of Man in 1393.

en:
William Pitt the Elder, 1st Earl of Chatham (1708–1778), was the British Whig statesman called the Great Commoner for his long refusal to accept a title. He won fame through his House of Commons oratory in the 1730s, denouncing corruption and royal subsidies.

As effective leader of the ministry from 1756 to 1761, he directed Britain's effort in the Seven Years' War, securing the conquest of Canada and dominance in India. He accepted an earldom in 1766 and served as prime minister until 1768, later defending the American colonies against coercion. He died in May 1778.

en:
William Shakespeare (1564–1616) was an English playwright, poet and actor, remembered as England's national poet. From Stratford-upon-Avon, he married Anne Hathaway at eighteen; his life in 1585–1592 is almost undocumented. By 1592 he was established in London, where Robert Greene called him an upstart crow.

From 1594 he wrote for and part-owned the Lord Chamberlain's Men, who built the Globe in 1599 and became the King's Men in 1603. From about 1589 he moved from histories and comedies to tragedies Hamlet, Othello, King Lear and Macbeth, and romances such as The Tempest.

He retired to Stratford around 1613 and died on 23 April 1616, leaving his wife his second best bed. His daughter Susanna inherited; his granddaughter Elizabeth died childless in 1670, ending his direct line. In 1623 fellow actors published the First Folio of 36 plays; Ben Jonson hailed him as for all time.

威廉·莎士比亚（1564—1616）是英格兰剧作家、诗人和演员，被后世称为英格兰的民族诗人。他是斯特拉特福人，十八岁与安妮·海瑟薇结婚；1585至1592年间他的生活几乎没有记载。到1592年他已在伦敦立足，罗伯特·格林曾骂他是暴发的乌鸦。

1594年起，他为宫内大臣剧团写戏并参股，该剧团1599年建成环球剧场，1603年改称国王剧团。约1589年起，他从历史剧和喜剧写到《哈姆雷特》《奥赛罗》《李尔王》《麦克白》等悲剧，又写《暴风雨》等传奇剧。

约1613年他退居斯特拉特福，1616年4月23日去世，遗嘱留给妻子“第二好的床”。女儿苏珊娜继承家产，外孙女伊丽莎白1670年去世时无子女，他的直系后代就此断绝。1623年，演员同事们出版收入36部剧作的《第一对开本》，本·琼森称他属于所有时代。

en:
William the Conqueror (c. 1028–1087) was Duke of Normandy from 1035 and King of England from 1066, the first Norman to rule England. Born at Falaise, the illegitimate son of Robert I, he inherited the duchy as a child amid warring nobles. He put down a rebellion in 1047, married Matilda of Flanders, and by 1060 held Normandy firmly.

When Edward the Confessor died childless, William claimed the throne had been promised him and that Harold had sworn to support him. He invaded in 1066, killed Harold at Hastings, and was crowned at Westminster on Christmas Day.

Revolts followed, and in 1069–70 he devastated northern England. He raised castles, among them the Tower of London, settled a new Norman nobility, and in 1086 ordered the Domesday survey. He died at Rouen in 1087 and was buried at Caen, leaving Normandy to Robert and England to William Rufus.

征服者威廉（约1028—1087）自1035年起为诺曼底公爵，1066年起为英格兰国王，是第一位统治英格兰的诺曼君主。他生于法莱斯，是罗贝尔一世的私生子，年幼袭位，诺曼贵族彼此争战。1047年他平定叛乱，娶佛兰德的玛蒂尔达，约1060年稳固了诺曼底的统治。

忏悔者爱德华无嗣而终，威廉声称王位曾被许诺给他，哈罗德也曾发誓支持他。1066年他入侵英格兰，在黑斯廷斯杀死哈罗德，圣诞节在威斯敏斯特加冕。

此后叛乱不断，1069至1070年他纵兵焚掠英格兰北部。他广建城堡，包括伦敦塔，安插诺曼贵族，1086年下令开展末日审判调查。1087年他死于鲁昂，葬在卡昂，诺曼底传给罗贝尔，英格兰传给威廉·鲁夫斯。

en:
William de Warenne (1256–1286) was the only son of John de Warenne, 6th Earl of Surrey, and Alice de Lusignan, half-sister of King Henry III. He married Joan, daughter of Robert de Vere, 5th Earl of Oxford, who bore him a son, John, later 7th Earl of Surrey, and a daughter Alice.

In 1286 William was killed in a tournament at Croydon, predeceasing his father, and it was later suggested that his enemies had planned his death as murder.

William Zouche (1299–1352) was an English cleric and royal administrator who became Archbishop of York. Educated at Oxford, he served Edward III as Keeper of the Wardrobe, Lord Privy Seal and Lord Treasurer. In 1340 the canons of York elected him archbishop against the king's wishes, and he was consecrated at Avignon in 1342.

As Warden of the Marches he led troops against the Scots at Neville's Cross in 1346. He died at Cawood in 1352 and was buried in York Minster.

Anna Komnene Doukaina Palaiologina Asanina was a Byzantine noblewoman of the early fourteenth century, a daughter of the protostrator Theodore Synadenos and Eudokia Doukaina Komnene. In December 1321, at Adrianople, she married Manuel Komnenos Raoul Asanes, grandson of the Bulgarian tsar Ivan Asen III and brother-in-law of John VI Kantakouzenos.

She is portrayed beside her husband in a family miniature in the typikon of the Constantinople convent of Bebaia Elpis, founded by her grandmother Theodora Synadene. Her son Andronikos Asanes, raised by Kantakouzenos, later became sebastokrator.

安娜·科穆宁·杜卡伊娜·巴列奥略吉娜·阿萨尼娜是14世纪初的拜占庭贵族女子，为“普罗托斯特拉托”狄奥多尔·西纳德诺斯与欧多基娅·杜卡伊娜·科穆宁之女。1321年12月，她在阿德里安堡嫁给曼努埃尔·科穆宁·拉乌尔·阿森；后者是保加利亚沙皇伊凡·阿森三世之孙、约翰六世·坎塔库泽努斯的内弟。

在祖母塞奥多拉·西纳齐娜于君士坦丁堡创办的“坚定希望”修道院的规章手抄本中，绘有她与丈夫并立的家族细密画。她的儿子安德洛尼卡·阿萨尼斯由坎塔库泽努斯夫妇抚养，后来受封“塞瓦斯托克拉托”。

Anna Palaiologina was the daughter of the Byzantine aristocrat Andronikos Angelos Palaiologos, a grandson of Emperor Michael VIII. Around 1323 she married John II Orsini, Despot of Epirus, and bore him Nikephoros and Thomais. When John died suddenly in 1335, believed poisoned by Anna, she ruled as regent for the young Nikephoros.

In 1338 Andronikos III annexed Epirus and imprisoned her at Thessalonica; escaping in 1341, she was confined at Arta by John Angelos. Freed after the Serbian conquest c. 1347, she married John Komnenos Asen, lord of Valona, around 1350, and later went to live with her daughter Thomais at Trikala.

安娜·巴列奥略娜是拜占庭贵族安德洛尼卡·安格洛斯·巴列奥略之女，其父是皇帝米海尔八世的外孙。约1323年，她嫁给伊庇鲁斯专制公约翰二世·奥尔西尼，生下尼基弗鲁斯和托马伊斯。1335年约翰暴卒，时人多认为系安娜毒杀，她遂为年幼的尼基弗鲁斯摄政。

1338年，安德洛尼卡三世吞并伊庇鲁斯，将她押往塞萨洛尼基囚禁；1341年她逃脱，抵达阿尔塔后又被约翰·安格洛斯软禁。约1347年塞尔维亚人征服伊庇鲁斯后她获释，约1350年改嫁发罗拉领主约翰·科穆宁·阿森，晚年退居特里卡拉，与女儿托马伊斯一同生活。

John Komnenos Angelos Doukas Synadenos was a Byzantine noble who held the rank of megas stratopedarches under Michael VIII and Andronikos II. First attested in 1276/77, he and Michael Kaballarios led an army against the independent ruler of Thessaly, John I Doukas.

Routed at Pharsalus, Synadenos was captured while Kaballarios was killed attempting to escape; Synadenos later regained his freedom. He fought in the victory over the Angevins at Berat in 1281 and campaigned against Thessaly again in 1283. He ended his life as the monk Joachim, dying between 1310 and 1328, and left children by Theodora Palaiologina, niece of Michael VIII.

en:
Michael I Komnenos Doukas (c. 1170–1215), illegitimate son of the sebastokrator John Doukas and cousin of the Angeloi emperors, founded the Despotate of Epirus. A hostage to the Third Crusade in 1190, he later rebelled against Alexios III and fled to the Seljuks.

After the Fourth Crusade sacked Constantinople in 1204, he first served Boniface of Montferrat, then made Epirus a centre of Greek resistance to the Latins. He made treaties with the Latin Empire and Venice, conquered most of Thessaly in 1212 and recovered Dyrrhachium and Corfu in 1213–1214. He was assassinated in his sleep in 1214/15 and succeeded by his half-brother Theodore.

米海尔一世·科穆宁·杜卡斯（约1170—1215）是至尊者约翰·杜卡斯的私生子，与安格洛斯王朝的皇帝们是表亲，也是伊庇鲁斯专制国的开创者。1190年他曾作第三次十字军的人质，后来反叛阿历克塞三世，失败后逃往塞尔柱人处。

en:
Michael II Komnenos Doukas (c. 1206–1268), illegitimate son of Michael I, ruled the Despotate of Epirus from 1230. Exiled after his father's murder in 1215, he returned after his uncle Theodore's defeat by Bulgaria at Klokotnitsa and married Theodora Petraliphaina, later Saint Theodora. He took Corfu by 1236, occupied Thessaly after Manuel's death in 1241 and in 1249 received the despot title from John III Vatatzes.

In 1259 his alliance with Manfred of Sicily and Achaea was routed at Pelagonia after his bastard John deserted. He recovered Epirus and accepted Michael VIII's suzerainty in 1264; on his death Epirus went to Nikephoros and Thessaly to John.

Nikephoros I Komnenos Doukas (c. 1240–c. 1297), son of Michael II and Saint Theodora of Arta, ruled Epirus from 1267/8. The Nicaean emperor John III Vatatzes made him despot around 1249, and he later married Anna Kantakouzene, niece of Michael VIII.

He swung between Constantinople and the Angevin kings, becoming vassal of Charles I in 1279 until the Sicilian Vespers of 1282 broke Angevin power. In 1294 he wed his daughter Thamar to Charles II's son Philip of Taranto, with coastal fortresses as her dowry. He died c. 1297, leaving his young son Thomas under Anna's regency.

en:
Nikephoros II Orsini (c. 1328–1359) was the child ruler of Epirus, a Greek despotate the Byzantine emperor meant to swallow. His father John Orsini died in 1335, allegedly poisoned by his mother Anna Palaiologina, who governed as regent for the seven-year-old.

Emperor Andronikos III annexed the Epirote part of Thessaly in 1336 and in 1338 kept Anna hostage. Nobles smuggled Nikephoros to the titular Latin empress Catherine of Valois, at whose urging Arta rose in his name. John Kantakouzenos crushed the revolt, married Nikephoros to his daughter Maria and took him to Constantinople; when Kantakouzenos became emperor in 1347, Nikephoros was made despot.

In 1356 he seized Thessaly and drove Simeon Uroš out of Arta. He was killed fighting Albanian clans at the Battle of Achelous in 1359.

尼基弗鲁斯二世·奥尔西尼（约1328—1359）是伊庇鲁斯的幼年统治者，这个希腊专制公国正是拜占庭皇帝急于吞并的对象。1335年，其父约翰·奥尔西尼去世，据称是被母亲安娜·帕莱奥洛吉娜毒死，七岁的他继位，由安娜摄政。

1336年，安德罗尼卡三世吞并伊庇鲁斯在色萨利的领地，1338年又扣留安娜。贵族把他偷偷送给名义上的拉丁女皇瓦卢瓦的凯瑟琳，在她的鼓动下阿尔塔以他的名义起义。坎塔库泽诺斯平定叛乱，把女儿玛丽亚嫁给他，带他前往君士坦丁堡；1347年坎塔库泽诺斯称帝，尼基弗鲁斯获授专制公头衔。

1356年，他夺取色萨利，逐走阿尔塔的西美翁·乌罗什。1359年，他在阿凯洛奥斯战役中与阿尔巴尼亚部族作战时阵亡。

en:
Nicholas Orsini (Italian Nicolò, died 1323), eldest son of Count John I Orsini of Cephalonia, succeeded his father as count palatine in 1317. In 1318 he murdered his childless uncle, Despot Thomas Komnenos Doukas, seized Arta and southern Epirus, adopted Orthodoxy and married Thomas's widow Anna Palaiologina, daughter of Emperor Michael IX.

In 1319 he refused to pay homage to the Angevins as ruler of Epirus. The Byzantines kept Ioannina, recognizing him only as despot in 1319/1320, and his later siege of the city failed when its citizens joined the defence. In 1323 he was killed by his own brother, the future John II.

尼古拉斯·奥尔西尼（意大利语名尼科洛，卒于1323年）是凯法洛尼亚宫廷伯爵约翰一世的长子，1317年继承父位。1318年，他杀害无嗣的舅父、专制公托马斯·科穆宁·杜卡斯，夺取阿尔塔和伊庇鲁斯南部，皈依东正教，并娶舅父的遗孀、皇帝米海尔九世之女安娜·帕莱奥洛吉娜。

Theodora Palaiologina Synadene was a Byzantine noblewoman, daughter of Constantine Palaiologos and a half-niece of Emperor Michael VIII, who became her guardian after she was orphaned and died in 1282. She married John Synadenos and bore him three children, among them the cavalry commander Theodore Synadenos and a daughter, Euphrosyne, who became a nun.

After her husband's death she founded the convent of Bebaia Elpis in Constantinople, entered it with Euphrosyne, and composed its typikon, a rule for its organization and monastic life.

en:
Theodore Synadenos (c. 1277–1346), son of the megas stratopedarches John Synadenos, was one of the first and most committed supporters of the young Andronikos III against his grandfather Andronikos II. On Easter night 1321 he fled Constantinople with Andronikos and John Kantakouzenos to begin the revolt, and in 1328 the three took the capital without a fight through a gate whose guard had been bribed.

As protostrator he governed Constantinople, then Mesembria and Epirus from 1336. Rebels for Nikephoros II Orsini captured him at Arta in 1338 and held him until 1340.

In the civil war of 1341 he tried, as governor of Thessalonica, to hand the city to his friend Kantakouzenos, but the Zealots drove him out. He made terms with the regency, was given a high rank and put under house arrest, and died impoverished in 1345 or 1346.

en:
Thomas I Komnenos Doukas (c. 1285–1318) was the son of Nikephoros I of Epirus and Anna Kantakouzene. In 1290 Andronikos II made him despot, and after his father's death around 1297 he inherited Epirus under his mother's regency, which thwarted the claim of his sister Thamar and her Angevin husband Philip of Taranto.

A new Angevin invasion in 1307 ended in a compromise that ceded many recovered fortresses back to Philip. Thomas later married Anna Palaiologina, daughter of Emperor Michael IX, and a quarrel with Byzantium brought a raid on Arta in 1315. In 1318 he was murdered by his nephew, Nicholas Orsini of Cephalonia.

en:
Thomais Komnene Angelina, better known as Thomais Orsini (c. 1330 – before 1385), was the daughter of John II Orsini, Despot of Epirus, and Anna Palaiologina. In 1335 her father died of poison, and in 1338 Emperor Andronikos III annexed Epirus, driving her family from Arta.

Around 1348 she married the Serbian governor Simeon Uroš, half-brother of Stefan Dušan. After her brother Nikephoros II died in 1359, Simeon ruled both Epirus and Thessaly. Her children included John Uroš of Thessaly and Maria, wife of Thomas II Preljubović.

托马伊斯·奥尔西尼，本名托马伊斯·科穆宁·安杰利娜（约1330—1385年前），是伊庇鲁斯专制君主约翰二世·奥尔西尼与安娜·巴列奥略之女。1335年父亲被毒杀，1338年安德洛尼卡三世吞并伊庇鲁斯，她一家被逐出阿尔塔。

约1348年，她嫁给塞尔维亚君主斯特凡·杜尚的异母弟、当地总督西美翁·乌罗什。1359年其兄尼基弗鲁斯二世战死后，西美翁统治伊庇鲁斯和色萨利。她的子女包括色萨利统治者约翰·乌罗什，以及嫁给托马斯二世·普雷柳博维奇的玛丽亚。

en:
Desiderius Erasmus (c. 1466–1536), known as Erasmus of Rotterdam, was the Dutch humanist who became the most influential scholar of the Northern Renaissance. Orphaned by plague about 1483, he entered an Augustinian canonry and took his vows in 1488. A pupil brought him to England in 1499, where Thomas More became his lifelong friend.

He compiled the Adagia. His Praise of Folly, written in More's house, appeared in 1511 and became a best-seller. In 1516 he published his scholarly Greek and Latin New Testament, which ended the Vulgate's untouchable status and fed the Reformation.

He neither broke with Rome nor joined Luther, and in 1524 attacked Luther on free will, leaving both camps resentful. Paris theologians censured his works in 1531. He returned to Basel in 1535 and died there on 12 July 1536; the Protestant city allowed a Catholic requiem at his funeral.

德西德里乌斯·伊拉斯谟（约1466—1536），通称鹿特丹的伊拉斯谟，是尼德兰人文主义者，北方文艺复兴影响最大的学者。约1483年瘟疫使他成为孤儿，他进入奥古斯丁修会，1488年发愿。1499年随学生赴英，与托马斯·莫尔结为挚友。

他编纂了《箴言集》。《愚人颂》在莫尔家中写成，1511年问世后畅销。1516年他出版希腊文与拉丁文《新约》，打破拉丁文通行本的独尊地位，滋养了宗教改革。

他既不与罗马决裂也不追随路德，1524年就自由意志问题抨击路德，两派皆怨。1531年巴黎神学家公开谴责其著作。他1535年回到巴塞尔，1536年7月12日在那里去世；这座新教城市准许为他举行天主教安魂弥撒。

Eberhard V von Erbach-Erbach (born before 1277, died before 1303) was Schenk, or hereditary cup-bearer and lord, of Erbach in the Odenwald, serving the Electors Palatine. His father was Konrad I, and he married Agnes Reiz von Breuberg.

Their son Konrad III inherited the Erbach lordship, while another son, Gerlach, became a cathedral canon and was elected bishop of Worms by the chapter in 1329, though the pope had already appointed a rival candidate.

埃伯哈德五世·冯·埃尔巴赫-埃尔巴赫（1277年前生，1303年前卒）是奥登林山埃尔巴赫的申克，即世袭掌酒官兼领主，效命于普法尔茨选侯。他的父亲是康拉德一世，娶阿格妮斯·赖茨·冯·布罗伊贝格为妻。

其子康拉德三世继承埃尔巴赫领地；另一个儿子格拉赫成为法政牧师，1329年被教区参议选为沃尔姆斯主教，但教皇此前已任命了他人。

Eberhard VIII von Erbach (before 1341 – 3 September 1373) was Schenk, the hereditary cup-bearer of Erbach in the Odenwald, and a son of Schenk Konrad III and Ida von Steinach. He is recorded as a knight in 1341 and in 1347 married Countess Elisabeth von Katzenelnbogen.

Their children included Eberhard X, Ida and Margarethe. He died on 3 September 1373, while Elisabeth lived on until 1385.

Konrad III von Erbach (before 1296 – 5 June 1363) was Schenk, the hereditary cup-bearer and lord of Erbach in the Odenwald. He succeeded his father Eberhard V after the latter's death in 1303; his mother was Agnes von Breuberg.

By his wife Ida von Steinach he left the sons Konrad V and Eberhard VIII, who carried on the Erbach-Erbach line. He died on 5 June 1363.

Kadi Ahmad Burhan al-Din (1345–c. 1398) was a Turcoman judge, poet and ruler born at Kayseri. Trained in Islamic law in Damascus and Cairo, he became qadi of Kayseri in 1364 and later vizier to the Eretnid rulers. In 1381 he seized the Eretnid lands around Sivas and took the title sultan.

For eighteen years he fought off the Ottomans, Mamluks and other neighbours. In 1398 the Aq Qoyunlu chief Qara Yuluk Osman captured and executed him, and the Ottomans then occupied Sivas. His Turkic collection is counted the first divan in the language; he also wrote in Persian and Arabic.

卡迪·艾哈迈德·布尔汉丁（1345—约1398）是出生于开塞利的土库曼法官、诗人与统治者。他曾在大马士革和开罗学习伊斯兰教法，1364年出任开塞利卡迪，后来成为埃雷特纳朝的维齐尔。1381年，他夺取锡瓦斯一带的埃雷特纳领地，自称苏丹。

十八年间，他先后击退奥斯曼、马穆鲁克及周边诸势力。1398年，白羊部首领卡拉·尤卢克·奥斯曼将他俘获处决，锡瓦斯随后被奥斯曼占领。他的突厥语诗集被视为该语言的第一部《迪万》，也用波斯语和阿拉伯语写作。

Ala al-Din Eretna (died 1352), of Uyghur origin, founded the Eretnid sultanate in central and eastern Anatolia. An officer under the Ilkhanid commander Timurtash, he came to govern Anatolia for the Jalayirid leader Hasan Buzurg and balanced between Mamluk and Mongol overlords. In 1343 he declared himself sultan.

In 1350 he seized Konya from the Karamanids. His realm stretched from Konya to Ankara and Erzurum, ruled from Kayseri. Known as Köse Peyghamber, 'the beardless prophet', for restoring order, he died in 1352.

阿拉丁·埃雷特纳（1352年卒）是维吾尔血统的安纳托利亚中东部埃雷特纳苏丹国的建立者。他本在伊儿汗国将领帖木儿塔什麾下任职，后替札剌亦儿部首领谢赫·大哈散治理安纳托利亚，在马穆鲁克与蒙古宗主之间周旋。1343年他自立为苏丹。

1350年他从卡拉曼人手中攻取科尼亚。他的国家从科尼亚延伸到安卡拉和埃尔祖鲁姆，以开塞利为都。他因恢复秩序而被称为“无髭先知”（克瑟·佩甘贝尔），1352年去世。

en:
Izz al-Din Jafar was a son of the Eretnid founder Ala al-Din Eretna and briefly ruled as the dynasty's sultan. On Eretna's death in 1352 his younger brother Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad took the throne at Kayseri and imprisoned Jafar, who escaped to Mamluk Egypt.

In 1354 the Eretnid emirs deposed the incompetent Muhammad and raised Jafar to the throne. He reigned for less than a year: in April 1355 Muhammad defeated and killed him at the Battle of Yalnızgöz and recovered the sultanate.

伊兹丁·贾法尔是埃雷特纳王朝建立者阿拉丁·埃雷特纳之子，曾短暂君临该王朝。1352年埃雷特纳去世，其弟吉亚斯丁·穆罕默德在开塞利继位，将贾法尔囚禁，贾法尔后来逃往马穆鲁克埃及。

1354年，埃雷特纳的埃米尔们废黜施政无能的穆罕默德，拥立贾法尔登基。他在位不足一年：1355年4月，穆罕默德在耶尔讷兹格兹战役中将他击败并处死，夺回苏丹之位。

en:
Kaluyan, called Kaluyan al-Qunawi in Arabic sources, was an architect active in medieval central Anatolia. His name appears on the Köşkmedrese near Kayseri, the khanqah built in 1339 by Eretna in memory of his consort Suli Pasha; he may have been Armenian.

Turkish tradition also credits him with major Seljuk buildings, including the Gök Medrese at Sivas. He is said to have been born a Christian and a follower of the Sufi poet Rumi before converting to Islam.

卡卢扬在阿拉伯文献中被称为卡卢扬·库纳维，是中世纪活跃于安纳托利亚中部的建筑师。开塞利附近的科什克梅德雷斯留有他的名字：这座修行院由埃雷特纳于1339年为纪念王妃苏利帕夏而建，他可能是亚美尼亚人。

土耳其传统还把多座塞尔柱重要建筑归于他名下，包括锡瓦斯的格克经学院。相传他本是基督徒，曾追随苏菲派诗人鲁米，后来改宗伊斯兰教。

en:
Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad I was the second sultan of the Eretnids, ruling in Anatolia from his father Eretna's death in 1352 until his murder. Enthroned young at Kayseri, he was deposed by his emirs in 1354 in favor of his brother Jafar, but killed Jafar at the Battle of Yalnızgöz in April 1355 and restored his rule.

He lost Ankara to the Ottoman sultan Murad I in 1361. In October 1365, after suppressing a revolt by his vizier, he was murdered by his emirs at Kayseri, who placed his young son Ali on the throne.

吉亚斯丁·穆罕默德一世是埃雷特纳王朝第二代苏丹，自1352年父亲埃雷特纳去世起在安纳托利亚执政，直到遇害。他少年时在开塞利登基，1354年被手下埃米尔废黜，改立其兄贾法尔；1355年4月，他在耶尔讷兹格兹战役杀死贾法尔，复辟成功。

Suli Pasha Khatun (died 1339) was a consort of Ala al-Din Eretna, founder of the Eretnid sultanate in central Anatolia. After her death in 1339, Eretna built the Köşkmedrese on Mount Köşk southeast of Kayseri in her memory.

Originally a Sufi khanqah, it became her tomb. Eretna, his son Muhammad I and his grandson Ala al-Din Ali were later buried there as well.

苏利·帕夏·哈屯（1339年卒）是安纳托利亚中部埃雷特纳苏丹国建立者阿拉丁·埃雷特纳的配偶。1339年她去世后，埃雷特纳在开塞利东南的克什克山为纪念她修建克什克麦德雷斯。

en:
Hermann of Prague (c. 1280–1349) was a Bohemian canon lawyer who became prince-bishop of Warmia. Educated at Bologna, he served at Avignon from 1327 as papal chaplain and auditor of the Rota. In December 1337 Pope Benedict XII named him bishop of Warmia against the Teutonic Order's wishes, but the cathedral chapter barred him until 1340.

He then settled the bishopric's borders, founded some seventy-five towns and villages and held the first diocesan synod at Frauenburg in 1343. He died on 31 December 1349 and was buried at Frauenburg.

布拉格的赫尔曼（约1280—1349）是波希米亚教会法学者，后来成为瓦尔米亚采邑主教。他曾在博洛尼亚求学，1327年起在阿维尼翁担任教宗司铎与圣轮法院审计员。1337年12月，教宗本笃十二世不顾条顿骑士团的反对任命他为瓦尔米亚主教，但主教座堂参事会拒绝他入境，直到1340年才得以就任。

此后他划定教区边界，建立约七十五座城镇和村庄，1343年在弗龙堡召开首届教区会议。他于1349年12月31日去世，葬于弗龙堡。

Erumduli Barlas was a twelfth-century Mongol prince of the Borjigin and a military commander, holding the ranks of noyan and darughachi under the khans of the Khamag Mongol. He was a son of Khaduli Barlas and nephew of Khabul Khan.

He served under Khabul, who died in 1148, and later under Ambaghai and Hotula. His own son Suqu Sechen was also an officer of the confederation.

en:
Esen-Temür (died 29 February 1332) was a Mongol prince, the son of Hügechi and grandson of Kublai Khan. After his father's murder he was made Prince of Yunnan only in 1280. From 1285 he led campaigns into Burma, sacking Pagan in 1287 and conquering the country's north.

In 1290 the senior title Prince of Liang passed to Zhenjin's line, and in 1308 Esen-Temür became Prince of Ying. He backed the losing Shangdu faction in the 1328 civil war, lost his seal, and died in 1332.

也先帖木儿（1332年2月29日卒）是蒙古宗王，忽哥赤之子、忽必烈之孙。父亲被毒杀后，迟至1280年他才受封云南王。1285年起他率军征讨缅甸，1287年攻破蒲甘，征服缅甸北部。

en:
Katharina von der Mark (1310–1360) was princess-abbess of the Imperial abbey of Essen from 1337 until her death. A daughter of Count Engelbert II of the Mark, she was elected through her brother Count Adolf II, the abbey's advocate, and installed on 11 August 1337 after an age dispensation from Pope Benedict XII.

In 1338 she renounced the Kurmud, her right to a dead peasant's horse and weapons. She died on 27 September 1360 and was buried in Essen Minster.

卡塔琳娜·冯·德马克（1310—1360）自1337年至去世担任埃森帝国直辖女修道院的采邑女院长。她是马克伯爵恩格尔贝特二世之女，借助身兼修道院护持官的兄长阿道夫二世当选，1337年8月11日在获教宗本笃十二世特许免除年龄限制后正式就职。

en:
Charles d'Évreux (1306–1336) was a Capetian prince, son of Louis, Count of Évreux, and Margaret of Artois, and brother of Philip III of Navarre. His father granted him Étampes, raised to a county by King Charles IV in 1327; his uncle Charles of Valois acted as regent.

In 1328 he was among the first peers to back Philip of Valois against Edward III. He married Maria de la Cerda in 1335 and died on 5 September 1336, leaving the infant Louis I to succeed him.

en:
Louis I, Count of Étampes (1336–1400), was a French prince of the blood, the elder son of Charles d'Évreux and Maria de La Cerda. He fought at Poitiers in 1356, where he was captured and later ransomed. He married Jeanne de Brienne in 1358, and in 1360 he was one of four princely hostages handed to Edward III to guarantee the Treaty of Brétigny.

Charles V later gave him the lordship of Lunel and sent him on a mission to Pope Urban V. He had no children and died in Paris on 6 May 1400.

en:
Amda Seyon I, whose Ge'ez name means Pillar of Zion and whose throne name was Gebre Mesqel, ruled Ethiopia as Negusä Nägäst from 1314 to 1344 and made the Solomonic dynasty a power in the Horn of Africa. A son of Emperor Wedem Arad, he married his father's concubine Jan Mogassa; monks led by Basalota Mika'el accused him of incest and threatened excommunication, and he beat one accuser and exiled the rest.

In 1316–1317 he campaigned against Damot, Hadiya and Gojjam, exiling the conquered peoples. His fame rests on 1332–1333, when he crushed Sabr ad-Din of Ifat's rebellion and overran the Muslim sultanates to the southeast, wars celebrated in the Ge'ez chronicle The Glorious Victories.

He had no fixed capital and spent most of his time on campaign, answering every refusal of tribute with a punitive march. He died in 1344 and his son Newaya Krestos succeeded him.

zh:
安达·塞永一世的吉兹语名意为“锡安之柱”，王号加布雷·梅斯克尔，1314年至1344年为埃塞俄比亚万王之王，使所罗门王朝成为非洲之角的强权。他是皇帝韦德姆·阿拉德之子，却迎娶父亲的妾詹·莫加萨；以巴萨洛塔·米卡埃尔为首的修士指责他乱伦，威胁将他逐出教会，他殴打其中一人，把其余教士流放。

1316至1317年，他征讨达莫特、哈迪亚和戈贾姆，将被征服人口迁往异地。他的声名系于1332至1333年：他平定伊法特萨布尔丁的叛乱，席卷东南方的穆斯林苏丹国，这些战事见于吉兹语编年史《辉煌的胜利》。

他没有固定都城，多半时间随部队在外征战，凡拒绝纳贡者必遭讨伐。他于1344年去世，其子内瓦亚·克雷斯托斯继位。

Asay, known in church tradition as Abba Yasay, was a son of the fourteenth-century Emperor Amda Seyon I (r. 1314–1344) and the fifth of five princes in the traditional Solomonic genealogy. He entered the Church, and local tradition of the Dembiya country, recorded on the northern shore of Lake Tana, makes him the founder of the church of Mandaba Madhane Alem.

He has also been identified with a king's brother who lived as a monk at the monastery of Saint Abba Aron under the Emperor Newaya Krestos.

en:
Bahr-Sagad, also called Bahir-Sagad, was the eldest son of the Emperor Amda Seyon I by his queen Bilen-Saba, as the Solomonic genealogies name him. After the suppression of the rebellion of Ya'ibika-Igzi in Tigray, the emperor first gave Inderta to the queen to govern.

Then, in 1328, he placed Bahr-Sagad at the head of a centralized administration over Tigray and the maritime provinces, where he held the title Ma'ikala-Bahr. His government covered the country between the Marab river and the Red Sea, a command which became the precursor of the office of Bahri Negash.

en:
Ewostatewos (1273–1352) was an Ethiopian Orthodox monk and religious leader born near Mekelle in Enderta. Educated by his uncle Abba Daniel, he founded a monastery in Serae, where he taught that Christians should keep both Saturday, the Old Testament Sabbath, and Sunday as days of rest.

When Abuna Yaqob rejected his teaching around 1337, Ewostatewos went into exile with his disciples, travelling through Sudan and Cairo, where he defended his views before the Coptic patriarch, and then Jerusalem. He died in Cilician Armenia in 1352, and his disciples, the Ewostathians, spread his Sabbath teaching across Ethiopia.

埃沃斯塔特沃斯（1273—1352）是埃塞俄比亚正教会修士与宗教领袖，生于恩德尔塔的默克莱附近。他受教于叔父阿巴·但尼尔，后在塞拉埃修建修道院，宣讲基督徒应同时以星期六，即《旧约》中的安息日，和星期日为安息之日。

约1337年大主教雅各布否定其教义，他遂率门徒流亡，经苏丹抵达开罗，向科普特牧首申辩，随后前往耶路撒冷。1352年他在奇里乞亚亚美尼亚去世，门徒即埃沃斯塔特派信徒，将其安息日教义传遍埃塞俄比亚。

Hezba Asgad was later remembered as the second son of Emperor Yagbe'u Seyon of Ethiopia and the second of five brothers to occupy the throne after their father's death in 1294. He ruled as Negusä Nägäst for a single year, from 1295 to 1296, taking the crown from his elder brother Senfa Ared IV and being succeeded in turn by his brother Qedma Asgad.

Chroniclers disagree whether the brothers reigned by annual rotation or fought through a dynastic crisis. In 1299 Wedem Arad seized the throne.

Jin Asgad was later remembered as the fourth son of Emperor Yagbe'u Seyon and the fourth of five brothers to rule Ethiopia in the troubled years after 1294. He reigned as Negusä Nägäst from 1297 to 1298.

A tradition recorded by E. A. Wallis Budge credits him with first using Amba Geshen as a royal mountain prison: he confined his treacherous brother Saba Asgad there, along with his other brothers and his own sons. In 1299 Wedem Arad seized the throne and ended the brothers' succession.

en:
Mateus, called Matthew the Armenian (died 1520), was the ambassador sent by Queen Eleni, regent of Ethiopia, to King Manuel I of Portugal and to the Pope, seeking allies against the growing influence of Muslim powers in the region.

He reached Goa in 1512 and Lisbon in 1514, then returned with a Portuguese embassy that included the priest Francisco Álvares. Mateus died in May 1520, just before the embassy reached the new emperor's court.

en:
Newaya Krestos, throne name Sayfa Ar'ed (sword of terror), was the eldest son of Amda Seyon I and ruled Ethiopia as Negusä Nägäst from 1344 to 1372, inheriting an empire held together largely by force and his father's unfinished quarrel with the clergy. At his accession he promised Abuna Yaqob to recall the exiled monks and live monogamously, then broke his word by marrying three women; when the clergy protested he sent the abuna back to Egypt and exiled the monks south.

He crushed Ali ibn Sabr ad-Din's revolt in Ifat and Adal, ending Ifat's independence, and imprisoned Ali and his sons except Ahmad, whom he made governor of Ifat.

He is credited with rebuilding the church of Debre Igziabher above Lake Hayq. Late in life he pressed Mamluk Egypt to free the imprisoned Patriarch Mark IV of Alexandria, jailing Egyptian merchants and, by tradition, marching toward Egypt.

内瓦亚·克雷斯托斯王号赛义夫·阿雷德，意为“恐怖之剑”，是安达·塞永一世的长子，1344年至1372年为埃塞俄比亚万王之王，接手的是一个主要靠武力维系的帝国，以及父亲留下的与教会的纠纷。即位之初他向大主教亚各布承诺召回被流放的修士并坚持一夫一妻，随后却食言娶了三位妻子；教士抗议时，他把大主教遣返埃及，并把修士流放南方。

他在伊法特和阿达尔平定阿里·伊本·萨布尔丁的叛乱，终结了伊法特的独立，囚禁阿里及其诸子，只留下艾哈迈德任伊法特总督。

相传他重建了哈伊克湖畔的德布勒伊吉亚布赫尔教堂。晚年他向马穆鲁克埃及施压，要求释放被囚禁的亚历山大牧首马可四世，为此囚禁境内的埃及商人，相传还率军向埃及进发。

en:
Saf-Asgid, also called Saf-Sagad, was a son of the Emperor Amda Seyon I; the Solomonic genealogies make him the second son borne to the emperor by Queen Bilen-Saba. The royal chronicle of his father's wars against Ifat and Adal names him among the five horsemen who followed Amda Seyon when he charged the army of Adal at the Battle of Das in 1329.

He took part in the Adal wars and the genealogical tradition records him as still living after 1332, while his brother Newaya Krestos succeeded to the throne as Saifa Arad in 1344.

1294年耶格贝·齐翁去世，相传他临终命五个儿子依次各在位一年；森法·阿拉德首先登基，称万王之王，至1295年由其弟赫兹巴·阿瑟格德继位。五人的短暂统治于1299年韦德姆·阿拉德夺取政权时告终。

en:
Wedem Arad (died 1314), a son of Yekuno Amlak and brother of Yagbe'u Seyon, seized the Ethiopian throne from his nephews around 1299. In his first year he foiled a jihad proclaimed by the sheikh Abu-Abdallah: his agents won over most of the rebel's followers, forcing him to make peace.

In 1306 he sent thirty envoys to Europe seeking an anti-Muslim alliance; they visited Rome, Avignon and Genoa. At Genoa a geographer interviewed them, and a later summary of his lost account first linked Ethiopia with the legend of Prester John.

韦德姆·阿拉德（1314年卒）是耶库诺·阿姆拉克之子、耶格贝·齐翁之弟，约1299年从侄子手中夺取埃塞俄比亚皇位。即位第一年，他挫败了谢赫阿布·阿卜杜拉发起的圣战：他的密使争取到叛军大部倒戈，迫使对方讲和。

en:
Yagbe'u Seyon (throne name Salomon; died 1294) succeeded his father Yekuno Amlak as Ethiopian emperor in June 1285, after years as co-ruler. With his father he had given vestments and utensils to the monastery on Lake Hayq.

He courted his Muslim neighbours and in 1289 wrote to the Mamluk sultan of Egypt over the treatment of Christians, but failed to secure an Abuna from Alexandria.

Marco Polo records that in 1288 the sultan of Aden seized and circumcised an Ethiopian prince's bishop, whereupon the prince captured his capital; some historians identify the prince as Yagbe'u. He crushed a revolt, and when he died in 1294 his sons disputed the throne.

en:
Yekuno Amlak (throne name Tesfa Iyasus; died 19 June 1285), a ruler of Bete Amhara, overthrew the last Zagwe king and in 1270 founded Ethiopia's Solomonic dynasty. Tradition associates his rise with Lake Hayq monastery and the monk Tekle Haymanot.

He campaigned south against Damot, founded the capital of Ankober, and exchanged letters with the Byzantine emperor Michael VIII, to whom he sent giraffes. In 1273 he asked the Mamluk sultan Baibars for a new Abuna for the Ethiopian Church; when none arrived, he blamed the sultan of Yemen. His son Yagbe'u Seyon succeeded him.

耶库诺·阿姆拉克（即位后改名特斯法·伊亚苏斯，1285年6月19日卒）原是贝特阿姆哈拉的统治者，他推翻末代扎格维国王，于1270年建立埃塞俄比亚所罗门王朝。相传他的崛起与海格湖修道院及修士特克勒·海马诺特有关。

en:
Étienne de Vesc (c. 1445–1501) was a Provençal courtier whom Louis XI appointed in 1470 to govern the household of the Dauphin Charles at Amboise; the chivalric education he gave the boy shaped the future Charles VIII. He undertook embassies as far as Spain and sat on the regency council in 1483.

A keen advocate of invading Italy, he prepared the 1494 campaign and entered Naples with Charles in February 1495, receiving the duchy of Nola and command of Gaeta. He organized the French evacuation from Naples in 1496, and kept at court by Louis XII, he died in 1501.

en:
Étienne Marcel (c. 1302–1358), born into a wealthy Parisian family of cloth merchants, became provost of the merchants of Paris in 1354. As provost he defended the interests of the city's craftsmen and guildsmen.

As a leader of the Third Estate at the Estates-General of 1355 he demanded oversight of royal finances. After John II was captured at Poitiers in 1356, Marcel led a reform movement that forced the Great Ordinance of 1357 on the Dauphin Charles.

During the Jacquerie he backed Charles the Bad of Navarre against the dauphin, and on 31 July 1358 was killed while trying to open Paris's gates to Navarrese mercenaries.

Amaury IV de Montfort (died 1140), a son of Amaury III and Agnes of Garlande, succeeded his father as Count of Évreux in 1137, while the family lordship of Montfort-l'Amaury passed to his brother Simon III. The split reflected their two overlords: the king of France for Montfort and the duke of Normandy, king of England, for Évreux.

Amaury survived his father by only three years, dying unmarried and without children, so Évreux reverted to Simon III, reuniting the family titles.

en:
Amaury V de Montfort (c.1150–1182), known in Normandy as Amaury III of Évreux, was the eldest son of Count Simon III and Matilda. On his father's death in 1181 the Montfort inheritance was divided: Amaury kept the County of Évreux and the family's English lands, while his younger brother Simon IV received Montfort-l'Amaury.

Around 1170 he married Mabel, heiress of William fitz Robert; their son Amaury VI later claimed the Gloucester earldom through her. He died on 13 March 1182, only months after taking power.

en:
Louis of Évreux (1276–1319), son of King Philip III of France, was a half-brother of Philip IV, who in 1298 granted him the county of Évreux. He fought in Flanders and distinguished himself at Mons-en-Pévèle in 1304, but won greater note as a diplomat, negotiating the treaties of Paris (1303) and Athis-sur-Orge (1305).

In 1316 he backed his nephew Philip V's regency, after which Évreux was raised into the peerage. By Margaret of Artois he fathered Philip III of Navarre and Joan, and he died at Longpont Abbey.

en:
Margaret of Artois (1285–1311), eldest child of Philip of Artois and Blanche of Brittany, married Louis, Count of Évreux and half-brother of King Philip IV, in 1301, becoming countess of Évreux.

After her death, her son Philip married Joan II of Navarre and ruled the kingdom as Philip III from 1328, while her daughter Jeanne married Charles IV of France in 1324 and became queen. Margaret died in Paris in 1311 and was buried in the Dominican church of the Jacobins.

en:
Alberghetto I Chiavelli was a leading member of the Ghibelline Chiavelli dynasty of Fabriano in the Marche, and son of Gualtiero di Ruggero Chiavelli, who is believed to have founded the Augustinian convent of Sant'Agostino in 1216 and was buried there in 1258.

Early in the fourteenth century Alberghetto brought that convent inside the city walls, and he funded the completion of the Benedictine church and convent of San Nicolò, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1266. He died around 1304, before his family became formal lords of Fabriano.

阿尔贝盖托一世·基亚韦利是马尔凯地区法布里亚诺吉伯林派基亚韦利家族的首领，瓜尔蒂耶罗·迪·鲁杰罗·基亚韦利之子；据信其父于1216年创建圣奥古斯丁修道院，1258年葬于该处。

en:
Alberghetto II Chiavelli (c. 1295–c. 1376) was a Ghibelline condottiero and lord of Fabriano in the Marche, son of Tommaso I. In 1317 he returned from exile by night with three hundred knights and began the city's second circuit of walls, finished in 1330.

He founded a hospital outside the walls in 1321 and set up his signoria the next year, but his grip slipped and in 1338 he was expelled. In 1344 he retook Fabriano with the help of Nolfo da Montefeltro, exiling his opponents and confiscating their property.

In 1351 he rebuilt the Sturinalto fountain and had a new town bell cast with his arms. Jailed by the pope in 1363 for plotting for Giovanni Visconti, he was released and died among his family at Genga castle around 1376.

阿尔贝盖托二世·基亚韦利（约1295—约1376）是马尔凯地区法布里亚诺的吉伯林派雇佣军首领与领主，托马索一世之子。1317年，他率三百骑士乘夜返乡，随后动工修建城市第二道城墙，1330年完工。

1321年他在城墙外兴建医院，次年建立领主统治；此后权势滑落，1338年被逐。1344年他借诺尔弗·达·蒙特费尔特罗之力夺回法布里亚诺，流放对手并没收其财产。

1351年，他重建斯图里纳托喷泉，并铸造了一口带有自家徽记的新市钟。1363年他因替乔瓦尼·维斯孔蒂密谋而被教皇囚禁，获释后约1376年在真加堡家人身边去世。

en:
Giovanni Chiavelli was a soldier of Fabriano, son of Tommaso I Chiavelli and a brother of Alberghetto II. His father had made the family a power in the city: in 1325, with Montefeltro backing, Tommaso took office as gonfalonier and defender of the people, and the next year he captured Rocca Contrada.

In 1347 and 1348 Giovanni served with his brother Alberghetto in the fighting in the Kingdom of Naples. In 1364 he was granted the Rocca d'Appennino by a local lord. He died without children, leaving his estate to the church of Santa Caterina in Fabriano, which his nephew Guido enlarged in 1378–1382 and where Guido was buried.

Guido Chiavelli, called Napolitano (c. 1325–1404), was a soldier and lord of Fabriano, a son of Alberghetto II, whose Neapolitan campaigns gave Guido his nickname. He was a businessman as much as a soldier: from 1359 he ran paper mills outside the city and pushed its manufacturing and trade, paper above all.

On 24 June 1378 he entered Fabriano with seven hundred knights and drove out the Da Varano garrison holding it for the pope. He first feigned an attack on the castle of Belvedere to draw off part of the garrison, entered by night, and when the rest were penned in the fortress had their cisterns drained until they surrendered.

Acclaimed defensor populi and apostolic vicar, he had the latter office confirmed by Pope Boniface IX in 1393. He enlarged the church of Santa Caterina, where he was later buried.

圭多·基亚韦利，人称“纳波利塔诺”（约1325—1404），是法布里亚诺的军人与领主，阿尔贝盖托二世之子，绰号得自随父参加的那不勒斯战争。他经商不亚于带兵：1359年起经营城郊的造纸作坊，大力扶持当地制造业与贸易，尤以造纸为重。

1378年6月24日，他率七百骑士进入法布里亚诺，驱逐替教皇占据该城的达瓦拉诺守军。他先佯攻贝尔韦代雷城堡，引开部分守军，乘夜入城，待余下的守军退入要塞，便排空他们的蓄水池，迫使其投降。

他被拥戴为“人民保卫者”和使徒代理，教皇卜尼法斯九世于1393年正式确认了后一职务。他扩建了圣卡泰里娜教堂，身后即葬于此。

en:
Tommaso I Chiavelli (c. 1262–c. 1330) was the head of the Ghibelline Chiavelli dynasty of Fabriano in the early fourteenth century, the son of Alberghetto I and father of Alberghetto II. In 1288 a papal bull, rewarding his family's defence of the Church, granted him the castle of Domo and other lands and styled him gonfaloniere of Fabriano.

In 1306 the city's conservatori della libertà drove him into exile in Naples, but he returned the next year. Banished again in 1316, he re-entered Fabriano in 1317 with his son and three hundred horsemen.

Backed by the Montefeltro, in 1325 he took office as gonfaloniere and defender of the people, and in 1326 he captured Rocca Contrada. He died around 1330.

托马索一世·基亚韦利（约1262—约1330）是14世纪初法布里亚诺吉伯林派基亚韦利家族的首领，阿尔贝盖托一世之子、阿尔贝盖托二世之父。1288年，为酬谢其家族保卫教会，教皇诏书将多莫城堡及其他领地封赐给他，并称他为法布里亚诺旗官。

1306年他被“自由维护者”驱逐，流亡那不勒斯，次年返回。1316年他再次被放逐，1317年率儿子和三百名骑兵重返法布里亚诺。

在蒙特费尔特罗家族支持下，他于1325年就任旗官兼人民保卫者，1326年攻取罗卡孔特拉达。他约于1330年去世。

Vagnino Chiavelli, born Aldebrandino and known by the nickname Vagnino, was a nobleman of Fabriano and a son of Alberghetto I Chiavelli. After 1303 he acted for the Fabriano commune in buying feudal estates in its contado: in 1305 it paid twenty thousand pounds for the lands of the count of Rovellone's widow.

The purchases sparked a war with Jesi that ended in 1308 with the Peace of Fermo, which assigned the disputed fiefs, including Castelletta, to Fabriano. Vagnino died around 1310.

瓦尼诺·基亚韦利原名阿尔德布兰迪诺，瓦尼诺是他的昵称；他是法布里亚诺贵族，阿尔贝盖托一世·基亚韦利之子。1303年后，他代表法布里亚诺城邦收购周边封地，1305年城邦以两万镑从罗韦洛内伯爵遗孀手中购得其产业。

收购引发对耶西的战争，1308年以《费尔莫和约》告终，包括卡斯特莱塔在内的争议封地判归法布里亚诺。瓦尼诺约于1310年去世。

Alberghettino II Manfredi (c.1285 – 18 November 1329) was the second signore of Faenza. The son of Francesco I Manfredi, he first tried to overthrow his father in 1326 and fled when the plot was discovered. In 1327, urged on by rival families, he entered Faenza and proclaimed himself signore.

In 1328 the papal legate besieged him; Alberghettino resisted for twenty-five days before surrendering the city. He then plotted to give Bologna to the Emperor Louis the Bavarian in return for the vicariate of Faenza. Discovered and imprisoned, he was tortured and beheaded in Bologna on 18 November 1329, after ten months in prison.

阿尔贝盖蒂诺二世·曼弗雷迪（约1285—1329年11月18日）是法恩扎的第二任统治者。他是弗朗切斯科一世·曼弗雷迪之子，1326年首次图谋推翻父亲，事泄后出逃。1327年，在敌对家族怂恿下，他进入法恩扎，自立为统治者。

1328年教皇使节围攻该城，阿尔贝盖蒂诺抵抗25天后投降。此后他密谋将博洛尼亚交给皇帝路德维希四世（巴伐利亚人），以换取法恩扎的代治权。事泄后他被捕入狱并受酷刑，关押十个月后于1329年11月18日在博洛尼亚被斩首。

en:
Francesco I Manfredi (c.1260 – 29 May 1343) founded the Manfredi lordship of Faenza and lived to see it taken from him by his own son. A Guelph leader in Romagna, he inherited family lands in 1309, became capitano del popolo of Faenza in 1313 and of Imola in 1314, and by 1319 was absolute lord of both.

His son Alberghettino failed to seize Faenza in 1326, but took it in 1327 with the Ordelaffi's backing, and Francesco lost both offices. The papal legate besieged it in 1328 with Francesco's other son Ricciardo at his side, and Alberghettino was beheaded the next year.

Francesco won Faenza back only in 1340, governing for his underage grandson Giovanni, and died there in 1343. His wife Rengarda Malatesta, daughter of Malatesta da Verucchio of Rimini, bore both sons.

弗朗切斯科一世·曼弗雷迪（约1260—1343年5月29日）开创了曼弗雷迪家族对法恩扎的统治，却眼看它被自己的儿子夺走。他是罗马涅圭尔夫派领袖，1309年继承家族领地，1313年出任法恩扎人民统领，1314年又兼任伊莫拉人民统领，1319年成为两城的专制统治者。

其子阿尔贝盖蒂诺1326年夺取法恩扎未遂，1327年在奥尔德拉菲家族支持下得手，弗朗切斯科被免去两处职务。1328年教皇使节围攻法恩扎，他的另一个儿子里恰尔多随使节参战，阿尔贝盖蒂诺次年被斩首。

弗朗切斯科直到1340年才夺回法恩扎，替年幼的孙子乔瓦尼执政，1343年在城中去世。他的妻子是里米尼的马拉泰斯塔·达·韦鲁基奥之女伦加尔达·马拉泰斯塔，两个儿子都是她所生。

en:
Giovanni Manfredi (1324–1373) was the Manfredi who lost Faenza to the Church. Born in Imola, an illegitimate son of Riccardo Manfredi, he was lord of Faenza from 1341 to 1356.

In 1351 he took Bernabò Visconti's pay in his war against Bologna and the Papacy, for which he was excommunicated in 1352. In 1356 a crusade was proclaimed against him and his ally of Forlì.

After a long resistance he surrendered Faenza to the papal commander, Cardinal Albornoz. In 1361 he rebelled again, but his plans to take Faenza and Imola were discovered, and he died at Pistoia in 1373.

乔瓦尼·曼弗雷迪（1324—1373）是丢掉法恩扎、让它回到教会手中的那位曼弗雷迪。他生于伊莫拉，是里卡尔多·曼弗雷迪的私生子，1341年至1356年任法恩扎领主。

1351年他受雇于贝尔纳博·维斯孔蒂，参与其对博洛尼亚和教廷军队的战争，1352年因此被处以绝罚。1356年，教廷向他和弗利的盟友宣布十字军。

他长期抵抗后，把法恩扎交给了教廷统帅阿尔沃诺斯枢机。1361年他再度起事，但夺取法恩扎和伊莫拉的计划败露，1373年死于皮斯托亚。

en:
Giovanni Manfredi was the son of Alberghettino II Manfredi, second signore of Faenza, who seized the city from his own father in 1327, surrendered it to the papal legate after a siege in 1328, and was beheaded at Bologna in 1329 for plotting to give that city to Emperor Louis the Bavarian.

Giovanni held the Romagna Apennine lordships, and in 1339 his uncle Ricciardo Manfredi, third signore of Faenza, knighted him. He married twice; his first wife Lisa Sanvitale bore him a son, Almerico. He died in 1389.

en:
Guglielmo Manfredi (1327 – c. 1367) was born in Imola, the natural son of Riccardo Manfredi, third signore of Faenza, and his mistress Zeffirina Nordigli, and was later legitimised. His father knighted him on 21 August 1340, two days before his own death, and he became lord of Fontanamoneta and co-lord of Bagnacavallo in Romagna.

He was also co-lord of Gambaraldo, Castiglionchio, Gattaia and Calamello, but his cousin Giovanni d'Alberghetto Manfredi took those from him. He died around 1367.

古列尔莫·曼弗雷迪（1327—约1367）生于伊莫拉，是法恩扎第三任统治者里卡尔多·曼弗雷迪与情妇泽菲里娜·诺尔迪利所生的私生子，后获合法化。1340年8月21日，父亲将他册封为骑士，两天后父亲便去世；他成为丰塔纳莫内塔领主和罗马涅巴尼亚卡瓦洛的共主。

他还是甘巴腊尔多、卡斯蒂利翁基奥、加塔亚和卡拉梅洛的共主，但这些领地被表亲乔瓦尼·达尔贝盖托·曼弗雷迪夺走。他约于1367年去世。

Rengarda Malatesta was the eldest daughter of Malatesta da Verucchio, founder of the Malatesta lordship of Rimini and the leading Guelph commander in Romagna; her mother was probably his first wife Concordia dei Pandolfini.

She married Francesco I Manfredi, later lord of Faenza, binding the two chief Guelph dynasties of Romagna together. Rengarda died before 1312, predeceasing her father, who died that year at the age of about a hundred.

Ricciardo Manfredi (c.1285 – 23 August 1340), condottiere and third signore of Faenza, was a son of Francesco I. King Robert of Naples knighted him in 1316. In 1327 his brother Alberghettino seized Faenza and moved on Imola, telling the Imolesi that Ricciardo meant to give the city to the papal delegate. Ricciardo, backed by Bolognese knights, took up arms against him, and Imola passed to the papal legate.

He followed the legate to Bologna and joined the long siege that retook Faenza in 1328, and later fought the Ordelaffi of Forlì and joined the siege of Verona in 1333.

That year he led the legate's army against the Este of Ferrara and was heavily defeated. He left a son, Giovanni, the fourth signore, and died in 1340, possibly poisoned.

里恰尔多·曼弗雷迪（约1285—1340年8月23日）是雇佣兵首领、法恩扎第三任统治者，弗朗切斯科一世之子。1316年由那不勒斯国王罗贝托册封为骑士。1327年，其兄阿尔贝盖蒂诺夺取法恩扎后进犯伊莫拉，还向伊莫拉人散布说里恰尔多要把城市交给教皇使节。里恰尔多得博洛尼亚骑士支持，起兵对抗兄长，伊莫拉随后归于教皇使节。

他随使节前往博洛尼亚，参加1328年收复法恩扎的长期围城战，此后又参加讨伐弗利奥尔德拉菲家族的战争和1333年的维罗纳围城战。

同年他率使节的军队进攻费拉拉的埃斯特家族，遭到重败。他留下一子乔瓦尼，即后来的第四任法恩扎统治者，1340年去世，传为被毒杀。

en:
The False Waldemar (died 1356) was an impostor who claimed to be Waldemar, Margrave of Brandenburg, buried in 1319. After the apparent extinction of Brandenburg's Ascanians, Emperor Louis the Bavarian had given the march to his own son.

In the summer of 1348 an elderly man presented himself to the Archbishop of Magdeburg, declaring the funeral staged and himself a pilgrim returned from the Holy Land; chroniclers guessed he was a journeyman miller named Jacob Rehbuck. Backed by opponents of Wittelsbach rule, he won support across much of the march and was invested with it by Emperor Charles IV in October 1348.

Charles deposed him in April 1350 after an agreement with the Wittelsbachs. He then kept an honorary Ascanian court at Anhalt-Dessau until his death in 1356.

伪瓦尔德马（1356年卒）是一名冒充者，自称是1319年下葬的勃兰登堡藩侯瓦尔德马。勃兰登堡的阿斯卡尼家族看似绝嗣后，皇帝巴伐利亚的路德维希将藩侯领地赐给了自己的儿子。

1348年夏，一名老者向马格德堡大主教现身，声称当年的葬礼是假办，自己是从圣地归来的朝圣者；据编年史作家猜测，他可能是名叫雅各布·雷布克的磨坊帮工。在反对维特尔斯巴赫家族统治的势力支持下，他赢得藩侯领地大部分地区的拥护，皇帝查理四世于1348年10月将该地封给他。

1350年4月，查理与维特尔斯巴赫家族达成协议，将他废黜。此后他在安哈尔特-德绍保有阿斯卡尼家族的名誉宫廷，直至1356年去世。

Fath-Ali Shah Qajar (1772–1834) was the second shah of Qajar Iran, reigning from 1797. Born in Damghan and originally called Baba Khan, he was the elder son of Hossein Qoli Khan. As a boy he was held hostage at the Zand court in Shiraz alongside his uncle Agha Muhammad Khan, who later made him heir to his throne.

His reign saw a flowering of Persian painting and portraiture; he commissioned portraits and rock reliefs near those of the ancient Sasanians to glorify his rule.

Two wars with Russia ended in the Treaties of Gulistan (1813) and Turkmenchay (1828), which stripped Iran of Georgia, Derbent and much of Armenia and Azerbaijan. After his son Abbas Mirza predeceased him, he died in 1834 and was buried at Qom.

法特赫-阿里沙·卡扎尔（1772—1834）是伊朗卡扎尔王朝第二任沙阿，1797年即位。他生于达姆甘，原名巴巴汗，是侯赛因·库里汗的长子。幼年他与叔父阿迦·穆罕默德汗一同在设拉子的赞德宫廷为人质，后来叔父立他为王位继承人。

他在位期间波斯绘画与肖像画艺术盛极一时；他委托绘制肖像，还在古代萨珊王朝的浮雕旁开凿岩石浮雕，以彰显自己的统治。

两场与俄国的战争以1813年的《古利斯坦条约》和1828年的《土库曼恰伊条约》告终，伊朗割让了格鲁吉亚、杰尔宾特以及亚美尼亚和阿塞拜疆的大片土地。其子阿巴斯·米尔扎先他而逝，他本人于1834年去世，葬于库姆。

Egino II (c. 1263–1318) was Count of Freiburg from 1271, succeeding his father Conrad I and ruling jointly with his brother Henry. He defied King Rudolf I, who sought the return of imperial lands Egino had withheld and favoured towns against their lords. His brother Henry supported the king.

His feud with Freiburg led him to call in the troops of Bishop Conrad of Lichtenberg, who was killed in the fighting. Warlike and spendthrift, Egino sold and mortgaged his lands until in 1315 his son Conrad III, backed by Emperor Louis IV, imprisoned him in his own castle and forced him to surrender the county.

埃吉诺二世（约1263—1318）自1271年起任弗赖堡伯爵，在父亲康拉德一世死后与兄弟亨利共治。他同国王鲁道夫一世对抗：国王追索他扣留的帝国领地，并支持城镇对抗领主。埃吉诺的兄弟亨利支持国王。

在与弗赖堡城的争斗中，他召来利希滕贝格主教康拉德的军队，主教却战死。埃吉诺好战挥霍，不断变卖、抵押领地，1315年，其子康拉德三世在皇帝路德维希四世支持下把他囚禁在自己的城堡中，迫使他交出伯国。

Egino III (died 1385) was a son of Count Konrad II of Freiburg. When his half-brother Frederick died in 1356 leaving only a daughter, Klara, Egino won his claim from Emperor Charles IV and took power in 1358 against the city's will.

In 1366 he tried to storm Freiburg by night, but a beggar warned the citizens; his castle was destroyed and his army defeated the Freiburgers at Endingen. In 1368 he sold the lordship to the city for twenty thousand marks of silver and obtained Badenweiler, where he died on 23 August 1385.

en:
Frederick, count of Freiburg (1316–9 November 1356), was the son of Count Konrad II and Catherine of Lorraine, succeeding his father in 1350. In 1351 the bishop of Basel settled his feud with his stepbrother Egino over hunting rights and mines in the Breisgau, awarding Egino half.

He ran up debts like his forebears, until in 1353 the city council forbade further pledges and placed his seal under joint custody. He left no son, so on his death the city accepted his daughter Klara as its lady under an old succession rule.

en:
Klara of Freiburg (born 1321) was the daughter of Count Frederick and Anna of Hachberg. When her father died on 9 November 1356 without a son, the city of Freiburg accepted her as its lady under an old charter giving the eldest daughter the succession.

Her uncle Egino, enfeoffed by Emperor Charles IV, contested her rule, and in June 1358 she sold him the lordship for 3820 marks of silver. Unable to pay, Egino left her the use of Lichteneck, which became her property in 1368. She was married to Count Palatine Gottfried of Tübingen, who died in 1369.

en:
Konrad II, count of Freiburg (died 10 July 1350), was the eldest son of Count Egino II. In March 1316, when his father sold estate after estate to clear his debts, Konrad had him confined in Freiburg Castle and took over the county.

He too pawned lands and rights, until in 1327 the city bought a charter for 4000 marks of silver barring him from selling property or waging war without the council. On 30 January 1349, during the Black Death persecutions, the Jews of Freiburg were burned under his rule.

Adelaide of Merania (died 8 March 1279) inherited the County of Burgundy from her brother Otto III in 1248 and reigned as countess until her death. A daughter of Otto I of Merania, she married Hugh of Chalon around 1239; he ruled at her side until his death in 1266, and their children included Otto IV and Reginald of Montbéliard.

In 1267 she married Philip I of Savoy and became Countess of Savoy and Bresse by marriage. Her reign was marked by conflict with King Rudolf I, and she died at Évian.

Amadeus III of Montfaucon (c. 1207–1280) was lord of Montfaucon, Orbe and Échallens, son of Count Richard III of Montbéliard and Agnes of Burgundy. After the Zähringers died out in 1218 he expanded his lands and succeeded his father around 1230. In 1247 he married Matilda, Countess of Saarbrücken.

In 1255 Hugh of Chalon granted him Orbe's other half in exchange for other rights; Amadeus enclosed Orbe with walls. He disputed rights at Yverdon with Peter II of Savoy but sold them to Peter in 1260. He died on 15 January 1280.

Beatrice II (1193–1231) ruled as countess palatine of Burgundy from 1205 until her death. The younger daughter of Count Otto I of Burgundy and Margaret of Blois, she succeeded her sister Joan I as a child, after her uncle Philip of Swabia had secured the county for her.

In 1208 she married Duke Otto I of Merania, who ruled Burgundy at her side. Her son Otto III inherited the county when she died on 7 May 1231, and her daughter Adelaide later held it too.

Stephen I of Auxonne (died after 22 July 1173) was a count of the House of Ivrea, called Stephen II within his family. A son of William IV of Burgundy and Poncette, heiress of Traves, he and his brother Gerard succeeded their father in 1156: Gerard took Mâcon and Vienne, while Stephen received Auxonne and Traves.

About 1170 he married Judith, daughter of Matthias I, Duke of Lorraine. He died in 1173, leaving his young son, the future Stephen II, to Gerard's guardianship.

艾蒂安一世（1065—1102），绰号“鲁莽者”，自1097年起任勃艮第、马孔和维埃纳伯爵，继承死于第一次十字军东征的兄长雷诺二世。他是威廉一世“伟人”之子，娶洛林公爵格拉尔之女贝亚特丽丝。

en:
Stephen II of Auxonne (1172–1241) was a count of the House of Ivrea. After his father died in 1173 his uncle Gerard, count of Vienne and Mâcon, guarded his minority; Stephen then led the senior family branch as count of Burgundy and Auxonne. About 1186 he married Beatrice of Thiers, Countess of Chalon.

Their children included John of Chalon, called the Old, and a daughter married to the lord of Montfaucon. Stephen also had a son, Stephen of Oiselay. After divorcing Beatrice he married Agnes of Dreux in 1214, and he died on 16 March 1241.

zh:
欧索讷的艾蒂安二世（1172—1241）是伊夫雷亚家族的伯爵。父亲于1173年去世后，他的叔父维埃纳与马孔伯爵热拉尔在他未成年时摄政；其后他统领家族长支，领勃艮第与欧索讷伯爵头衔。约1186年，他与沙隆女伯爵蒂耶尔的贝阿特丽丝结婚。

他们的子女包括“长者”沙隆的约翰，以及嫁给蒙福孔领主的一个女儿。艾蒂安还生有一子，即瓦兹莱的艾蒂安。他与贝阿特丽丝离婚后，于1214年娶德勒的阿涅丝，1241年3月16日去世。

en:
Odo I of Champlitte (1123–1187), called the Champenois, was the unrecognised son of Hugh, Count of Champagne, and Isabella of Burgundy; Hugh entered the Temple in 1125 and left the county to his nephew Theobald II. Reared by his mother's family, Odo became lord of Champlitte and Viscount of Dijon.

Odo claimed Champagne, and in 1143 King Louis VII, at war with Theobald, captured Vitry and gave it to him, but peace forced Odo to surrender the city. In 1171 he made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land, and his son William became the first Prince of Achaea.

en:
Walter II of Montfaucon (c. 1250–1309) was a lord of the Montfaucon family in Franche-Comté, holding Montfaucon and Vuillafans as well as Orbe and Échallens in the Vaud country. He continued his father's work of making Échallens a castellany.

In May 1304 Count Reginald of Burgundy granted him the town of Goumois on the Doubs in reward for his service, and Walter built the castle of Franquemont there. When his brother John I died without children in 1306, he inherited the Montfaucon estates.

By his wife Mahaut of Chaussin he left sons John II, Henry, later Count of Montbéliard, and Girard. He died in May 1309.

戈捷二世·德·蒙福孔（约1250—1309）是弗朗什孔泰的蒙福孔家族领主，领有蒙福孔、维拉方以及沃地区的奥尔布与埃沙朗。他继续父亲的事业，将埃沙朗建为堡区。

1304年5月，勃艮第伯爵雷诺为酬谢他的效力，将杜河畔的古穆瓦镇封赐给他，戈捷随即在当地修建弗朗克蒙城堡。1306年，其兄让一世无嗣而终，蒙福孔领地由他继承。

他与妻子绍桑的玛奥生有让二世、日后成为蒙贝利亚尔伯爵的亨利，以及日拉尔。他于1309年5月去世。

en:
Girard de Montfaucon (died 1353), a son of Walter II, was lord of Orbe and Échallens in the Vaud; his brother Henry held Montfaucon and became Count of Montbéliard. Girard inherited Orbe, Échallens and Montagny, and added Vuillafans and Montgesoye when his mother died.

When a feud broke out between the bishop of Lausanne and the lords of Montagny, he sided with the bishop alongside Pierre de Grandson, whose daughter he would marry, until Edward of Savoy imposed a truce in 1327. He also served Count Philip I of Burgundy as lieutenant.

In 1351 he and his wife Jacquette of Grandson granted franchises to Orbe and Échallens to repopulate their villages. He died in February 1353 and was buried in the Lady chapel of Lausanne Cathedral; his son John III succeeded him.

日拉尔·德·蒙福孔（卒于1353年）是戈捷二世之子，领有沃地区的奥尔布与埃沙朗；他的兄长亨利执掌蒙福孔，后来成为蒙贝利亚尔伯爵。日拉尔继承了奥尔布、埃沙朗与蒙塔尼，母亲去世后又并入维拉方和蒙热苏瓦。

洛桑主教与蒙塔尼领主起了争端，他与皮埃尔·德·格朗松一同站在主教一边——皮埃尔日后成了他的岳父——直到1327年萨伏依的爱德华强制双方休战。他还曾任勃艮第伯爵腓力一世的副将。

1351年，他与妻子格朗松的雅凯特向奥尔布和埃沙朗居民颁授自由特许状，以招徕人丁、复兴村镇。1353年2月他去世，葬于洛桑大教堂的圣母礼拜堂，其子让三世继位。

en:
William I (1020–1087), called the Great, ruled the County of Burgundy from 1057 and the County of Mâcon from 1078. Son of Reginald I and Alice of Normandy, he married Étiennette, whose origin is uncertain.

His county was under imperial suzerainty after the Burgundian succession war of 1032–1034. In 1078 his cousin Guy II of Mâcon ceded Mâcon to him on entering Cluny Abbey.

One son, Guy, was elected pope as Callixtus II in 1119. William died at Besançon on 12 November 1087, and his sons Reginald II and Stephen I succeeded him.

en:
William II of Burgundy (c. 1075–1125), called the German, was Count of Burgundy, Mâcon and Vienne. The only son of Reginald II, he was raised by his maternal grandfather Count Conon in the Alemannic lands around Bern, which gave him his nickname.

When his father died on the First Crusade in 1097 he succeeded jointly with his uncle Stephen I. In 1125 he was killed in a plot by his own barons, and his young son William III was assassinated two years later.

William II de Champlitte (died 1271/1273) was a French knight of the thirteenth century, the son of William I, first prince of Achaea, and his third wife Eustachie de Courtenay. He succeeded his uncle Odo II as viscount of Dijon and held the lordships of Champlitte and Pontailler.

In 1224 he and his brother Odo III confirmed gifts made to the abbey of Cîteaux. He married Éléonore de Pontailler, who died before 1241, and then Catherine, and was buried at Notre-Dame de Pontailler.

William III of Burgundy (c. 1110–1127), called the Child, was Count Palatine of Burgundy and Mâcon from 1125. The only son of William II the German and Agnes of Zähringen, he succeeded after his father was killed in a barons' plot.

He founded a Cluniac priory on the island of Saint-Pierre, but while still an adolescent was murdered on 1 March 1127 in the abbey church of Payerne. Renaud III, son of his great-uncle Stephen I, then took the county.

He founded a Cluniac priory on the island of Saint-Pierre, but while still an adolescent was murdered on 1 March 1127 in the abbey church of Payerne. Renaud III, son of his great-uncle Stephen I, then took the county.

威廉三世（约1110—1127），绰号“孩童”，自1125年起任勃艮第行宫伯爵兼马孔伯爵。他是“日耳曼人”威廉二世与采林根的阿涅丝的独子，父亲死于男爵们的阴谋后继位。

他曾在圣皮埃尔岛建立一座克吕尼派小修道院，但仍在少年时，便于1127年3月1日在帕耶讷修道院教堂遇刺。叔祖艾蒂安一世之子雷诺三世随后取得伯国。

en:
William IV of Burgundy, also called William III of Mâcon (c. 1088–1155), was a younger son of Count Stephen I. From 1102 he co-held Mâcon with his brother Reginald III, later adding Auxonne and Vienne.

After Reginald's death he ruled the county of Burgundy for his niece Beatrice, but kept her captive and won recognition from Frederick Barbarossa by 1152. He died on 27 September 1155, after which Frederick married Beatrice and took the county.

en:
Guy II of Pontailler (c. 1335–1392), also called Guy de Champlitte, was a Burgundian noble, son of Hugh of Pontailler. His house, Champlitte-Pontailler, descended from William of Champlitte, prince of Achaea after the Fourth Crusade, and long held a leading place in the duchy of Burgundy.

In January 1364, with free companies keeping the duchy in constant insecurity, Duke Philip the Bold named Guy marshal of Burgundy, an office he held until his death. He administered the duke's army and rode out himself to deal with the mercenaries; by his own account nobody else dared go to them.

He also fought the English and in 1384 was made governor of Flanders. He greatly enlarged his lands across the Saône, and he died in 1392.

蓬塔耶的居伊二世（约1335—1392），又称尚普利特的居伊，是勃艮第贵族，蓬塔耶的于格之子。尚普利特-蓬塔耶家族是第四次十字军东征后成为亚该亚亲王的尚普利特的纪尧姆的后裔，长期在勃艮第公国地位显赫。

1364年1月，自由佣兵团使公国长期不得安宁，公爵“大胆的腓力”任命居伊为勃艮第元帅，他任此职直至去世。他管理公爵的军队，亲自出面同这些佣兵周旋；照他自己的说法，除了他没人敢去找他们。

他还同英军作战，1384年被任命为佛兰德总督。他大幅扩展了索恩河对岸的领地，于1392年去世。

Hugh of Chalon (c.1220–1266) was the son of John I of Chalon the Wise and Matilda of Burgundy. In 1237 his father exchanged the County of Chalon for Salins with Duke Hugh IV, and later designated Hugh to inherit Salins.

In 1236 he married Countess Adelaide I of Burgundy, ending the feud between the palatine branches; after her brother Otto III died in 1248 he ruled the county at her side. Hugh died on 12 November 1266 and was buried at Cherlieu Abbey.

en:
John of Chalon (1190–1267), called the Old, was the son of Stephen III of Auxonne and Beatrice, Countess of Chalon, and held Auxonne and Chalon-sur-Saône in his own right.

In 1237 he exchanged them with Duke Hugh IV of Burgundy for Salins and other Jura lordships; the salt works of Salins made him among the richest nobles of the County of Burgundy. He built castles to guard the trade routes and granted charters to towns.

He resided chiefly at Nozeroy and acted as regent for his son Hugh III, who became Count of Burgundy by his marriage to Adelaide I.

en:
John III of Montfaucon (c. 1333–1372) was lord of Orbe and Échallens in the Vaud, son of Girard de Montfaucon and Jacquette of Grandson. In 1354 he sided with his uncle Henry, Count of Montbéliard, in a feud with Louis of Neuchâtel over Jeanne's inheritance; the war spread through the mountains of the Doubs until Philip of Burgundy stepped in.

In 1366 he followed Amadeus VI of Savoy on the expedition to rescue the Byzantine emperor John V Palaiologos. Six years later he rode with Amadeus again, to help Pope Gregory XI against the Visconti, and died at the Battle of Asti in September 1372.

His body was carried on a shield to the count's lodging, to the displeasure of all the lords. He left no legitimate heir, and his cousin Stephen inherited his lands.

His body was carried on a shield to the count's lodging, to the displeasure of all the lords. He left no legitimate heir, and his cousin Stephen inherited his lands.
zh:
让三世·德·蒙福孔（约1333—1372）是沃地区奥尔布与埃沙朗的领主，日拉尔·德·蒙福孔与格朗松的雅凯特之子。1354年，他站到叔父、蒙贝利亚尔伯爵亨利一边，同路易·德·纳沙泰尔争夺让娜的遗产，战火蔓延到杜河沿岸的山区，直到勃艮第的腓力出面调停。

1366年，他随萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥六世远征，营救拜占庭皇帝约翰五世·巴列奥略。六年后，他再度追随阿梅迪奥，协助教皇格列高利十一世对抗维斯孔蒂家族，1372年9月在阿斯蒂战役中阵亡。

他的遗体被抬在盾牌上送回伯爵的营帐，诸位领主都大为不快。他没有嫡嗣，堂兄艾蒂安继承了他的领地。

en:
Joan I (1191–1205), also called Joanna of Hohenstaufen, was ruling countess of Burgundy from 1200, when her father Otto I was assassinated at Besançon, until her death in 1205. She was the elder daughter of Otto I and Margaret of Blois.

A child throughout her reign, she died at about fourteen without issue, and her younger sister Beatrice II succeeded her as countess of Burgundy.

en:
Marguerite de Mello (died 24 December 1350) was a Burgundian noblewoman, daughter of Dreux de Mello, lord of Château-Chinon, and Éléonore of Savoy. First married to Maurice VII de Craon, she was left a widow.

Before 1332 she became the first wife of Jean II de Chalon-Arlay, lord of Arlay, bringing him the lordships of Jarnac and Châteauneuf. Her sons included Hugues II and Louis I de Chalon-Arlay, and her daughter Marguerite married Étienne de Montfaucon, later count of Montbéliard.

1332年之前，她改嫁阿尔莱领主让二世·德·沙隆-阿尔莱并成为其第一任妻子，还带来雅尔纳克与沙托讷夫两处领地。她的儿子包括于格二世与路易一世·德·沙隆-阿尔莱，女儿玛格丽特则嫁给后来成为蒙贝利亚尔伯爵的艾蒂安·德·蒙福孔。

Marguerite de Noyers-Maisey was a Burgundian heiress, lady of Maisey, daughter of Jean I de Noyers, lord of Maisey and Courgis, and Marguerite de Durnay.

She married Philippe III de Chauvirey, lord of Bétoncourt and bailli of Mâcon, to whom she bore Odette, later the wife of Erard du Châtelet. Long after her husband’s death, in 1375, Marguerite sold her lordship of Maisey. She died sometime after that date.

Matilda of Burgundy (1190–1242) was the daughter of Duke Hugh III of Burgundy and Beatrice of Albon, countess-dauphine of Viennois. In 1214 she married John of Chalon, called the Wise, count of Chalon and later lord of Salins.

Her children included Hugh of Chalon, who married Countess Adelaide I of Burgundy and fathered Count Otto IV. Matilda died on 26 March 1242.

en:
Otto-William (c. 958–1026), son of King Adalbert of Italy and Gerberga of Chalon, was adopted by his stepfather Henry I, Duke of Burgundy, as a possible heir to the duchy. Around 982 he married Ermentrude of Roucy, gaining the County of Mâcon, and around Dole he built up the lands that became the Free County of Burgundy.

King Robert II of France annexed the duchy in 1005. In 1016 Otto-William revolted against Emperor Henry II. He died on 21 September 1026 and was buried at Saint-Bénigne in Dijon, succeeded by his son Reginald I.

en:
Otto IV of Burgundy (c. 1248–1303), son of Hugh of Chalon and Countess Adelaide I, became Count of Chalon in 1267 and inherited the County of Burgundy in 1279, though he made good his authority only in 1295.

Otto married Philippa of Bar in 1271 and Mahaut of Artois in 1285. His daughters Joan II and Blanche both married kings of France. He died at Melun on 17 March 1303, and Joan II succeeded him; the county later passed as her dowry on her marriage to Philip, the future king of France.

en:
Otto I (born 1167–1171, died 1200), fourth son of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa and Beatrice I of Burgundy, received the County of Burgundy after his mother's death in 1184 and ruled as count palatine from 1190. He feuded with the lords of Auxonne and Mâcon and with Duke Berthold V of Zähringen.

In 1195 he killed Count Amadeus II of Montfaucon during negotiations. He supported his brother Philip's royal election in 1198 and was assassinated at Besançon in 1200. His daughters Joanna I and Beatrice II succeeded him, with their mother Margaret acting as regent for Joanna.

en:
Otto I of Merania (c. 1180–1234), eldest son of Berthold IV of Andechs, succeeded his father as Duke of Merania in 1204. By his marriage to Beatrice II of Hohenstaufen in 1208 he ruled the County of Burgundy as Otto II.

At their wedding King Philip was murdered, weakening the Andechs family's position. The counts of Auxonne long contested Otto's rule in Burgundy.

He joined the Fifth Crusade in 1217 and inherited Istria and Carniola in 1228. When Beatrice died in 1231, their son Otto III succeeded in Burgundy, and Otto died on 7 May 1234.

梅拉尼亚的奥托一世（约1180—1234）是安代克斯的贝特霍尔德四世的长子，1204年袭任梅拉尼亚公爵。1208年，他与霍亨斯陶芬家族的贝亚特丽丝二世结婚，由此以奥托二世的身份统治勃艮第伯国。

婚礼上国王腓力遇刺，安代克斯家族的地位受到削弱。欧索讷伯爵长期同奥托争夺勃艮第。

1217年他参加第五次十字军东征，1228年继承伊斯特拉和卡尼奥拉边区。1231年贝亚特丽丝去世后，其子奥托三世继为勃艮第伯爵，奥托本人则于1234年5月7日去世。

en:
Otto III (c.1218–19 June 1248), only son of Otto I of Merania and Beatrice II of Burgundy, succeeded as Count of Burgundy in 1231 and as last Duke of Merania in 1234. He married Elizabeth, daughter of Count Albert IV of Tyrol, but died childless.

Fighting the Wittelsbachs in Bavaria, he left Franche-Comté to King Theobald I of Navarre, raised Innsbruck to a town in 1239 and pawned the county to Duke Hugh IV of Burgundy in 1242. Opposing Emperor Frederick II earned him an imperial ban. Buried at Langheim Abbey, he left Burgundy to his sister Adelaide.

勃艮第的奥托三世（约1218—1248年6月19日）是梅拉尼亚的奥托一世与贝亚特丽丝二世的独子，1231年继母亲成为勃艮第伯爵，1234年继父亲成为末代梅拉尼亚公爵（称奥托二世）。他娶蒂罗尔伯爵阿尔贝特四世之女伊丽莎白为妻，婚姻无嗣。

他把弗朗什孔泰交给纳瓦拉国王特奥巴尔多一世管理，自己在巴伐利亚同维特尔斯巴赫家族争斗，1239年将因斯布鲁克升格为城镇，1242年把弗朗什孔泰抵押给勃艮第公爵于格四世。因在皇帝腓特烈二世与教皇的冲突中反对皇帝，他被处以帝国褫夺令。1248年他去世，葬于朗海姆修道院，梅拉尼亚公国就此终结，勃艮第伯国由其姐阿德莱德继承。

en:
Philippe III de Chauvirey (1295–1347) was a knight of the county of Burgundy, lord of Chauvirey, Château-Dessous and Bétoncourt. The son of Gérard de Chauvirey and Agnès de Châteauneuf, he entered French royal service as bailli of Mâcon from 1332 to 1342 and captain-warden of Lyon from August 1333.

He married Marguerite de Noyers-Maisey, lady of Maisey, allying his house with the Noyers lineage of northern Burgundy. He died in 1346 or 1347.

菲利普三世·德·肖维雷（1295—1347）是勃艮第伯国骑士，领有肖维雷、沙托德苏和贝通库尔。他是热拉尔·德·肖维雷与阿涅丝·德·沙托讷夫之子，后入仕法兰西王室，1332至1342年任马孔邑督，1333年8月起兼任里昂守备长官。

他娶迈塞女领主玛格丽特·德·努瓦耶-迈塞为妻，使肖维雷家族与勃艮第北部的努瓦耶家族联姻。他于1346或1347年去世。

en:
Reginald I (986–1057), second Count of Burgundy, was the son of Otto-William and Ermentrude of Roucy. In 1016 he married Alice of Normandy and succeeded his father in 1026. In 1027 the bishop-count of Auxerre captured him at Chalon; his father-in-law's Norman troops freed him.

In the succession war of 1032–1034 he backed Odo II of Blois against Emperor Conrad II, and defeat left the county under imperial suzerainty. The salt pans of Salins and Jura trade routes enriched his rule. He died in 1057, succeeded by his son William I.

雷诺一世（986—1057）是勃艮第自由伯国第二任伯爵，奥特-威廉与鲁西的埃芒特吕德之子。1016年，他与诺曼底的爱丽丝成婚，1026年继承父位。1027年，他在沙隆被欧塞尔的主教伯爵俘获，后由岳父派来的诺曼军队救出。

en:
Reginald II (c. 1056–c. 1097) was Count of Burgundy, Mâcon, Vienne and Oltingen, the eldest son of William I the Great and Étiennette, and elder brother of Pope Callixtus II. He succeeded his father in 1087 alongside his brother Stephen I in Burgundy and Mâcon.

By his marriage to Regina of Oltingen, heiress of Count Conon in the region of Bern, Reginald gained the County of Oltingen; their son was William II, later called the German. Reginald died around 1097 on the First Crusade, and his brother Stephen I succeeded him in Burgundy.

en:
Reginald III (c. 1093–1148), son of Count Stephen I, held Mâcon jointly with his brother William IV from 1102 and became Count of Burgundy in 1127 after his cousin William III was murdered.

He rebelled against Emperor Conrad III, but was defeated by the duke of Zähringen and lost all his lands east of the Jura. His stand earned him the nickname franc-compte, free count, from which Franche-Comté takes its name. He died in 1148, leaving a young daughter, Beatrice. She married Emperor Frederick Barbarossa in 1156.

en:
Richard II of Montfaucon (c. 1110–1162) was a lord in the County of Burgundy, the son of Amadeus I of Montfaucon. By his marriage to Sophie, Countess of Montbéliard and daughter of Count Thierry II, he allied his house with the counts of Montbéliard and raised it to princely standing; their son Amadeus II inherited both the lordship and the county.

He founded and endowed several monasteries in Franche-Comté, notably Lucelle Abbey, to which he gave a large estate. He died in 1162.

蒙福孔的理查二世（约1110—1162）是勃艮第伯国的领主，蒙福孔的阿马多伊斯一世之子。他通过与蒙贝利亚尔女伯爵索菲——伯爵蒂埃里二世之女——的婚姻，使家族与蒙贝利亚尔伯爵家族联姻，跻身诸侯之列；其子阿梅代二世后来同时继承了领地与伯国。

en:
Sophie (died 1148) was the daughter of Count Thierry II of Montbéliard and heiress to his county. In 1128 she married Richard II, Count of Montfaucon in Franche-Comté, joining the House of Scarpone to the rising Montfaucon lords.

She and Richard had a son, Amadeus II. Sophie died before her father, who lived until 1163, so on his death Amadeus II inherited the County of Montbéliard, uniting it with the Montfaucon lands.

蒙贝利亚尔的索菲（卒于1148年）是蒙贝利亚尔伯爵蒂埃里二世之女、伯国的女继承人。1128年她嫁给弗朗什孔泰的蒙福孔伯爵理查二世，使斯卡蓬家族与崛起中的蒙福孔领主家族联姻。

她与理查育有一子阿梅代二世。索菲先于1163年才去世的父亲而亡，因此父亲死后，阿梅代二世继承蒙贝利亚尔伯国，将它与蒙福孔领地合而为一。

en:
Ali ibn Haditha was an Al Fadl emir, a son of the first amir al-arab Haditha ibn Ghudayya and brother of Mani. After their father died Sultan al-Kamil divided the office between Ali, Mani and their kinsman Ghannam, but soon dismissed Ali and Ghannam; Ali founded the Al Ali branch.

Some years later the Ayyubids of Aleppo gave the office to Ali or his son Abu Bakr, and one of them held it until the Mamluks took Syria in 1260. When Baybars fled into exile in Syria in the 1250s, Ali refused him refuge.

阿里·伊本·哈迪塞是法德勒部族埃米尔，首任阿拉伯人埃米尔哈迪塞·伊本·古戴耶之子、马尼的兄弟。父亲死后，苏丹卡米勒把职位分给阿里、马尼和族人加南，旋即又罢黜阿里与加南；阿里创立了阿里支系。

数年后，阿勒颇的阿尤布政权将职位授予阿里或其子阿布·伯克尔，两人之一保有该职直至1260年马穆鲁克攻占叙利亚。1250年代拜巴尔斯流亡叙利亚时，阿里曾拒绝庇护他。

en:
Fadl ibn Isa, called Fadl II, was a prince of the Al Fadl Bedouin dynasty and amir al-arab, commander of the Bedouin of northern Syria for the Mamluk sultanate. A son of Isa ibn Muhanna, he took the office in 1311 after his brother Muhanna defected to the Mongol Ilkhanate, holding it until 1317; the brothers secretly played the Mamluks and Ilkhanids against each other.

Appointed again in 1322, he served until Muhanna’s restoration in 1330. Fadl died around 1334, and his sons later held the office.

法德勒·伊本·伊萨（又称法德勒二世）是法德勒贝都因王朝的王公，曾任阿拉伯人埃米尔，代表马穆鲁克苏丹国统辖叙利亚北部的贝都因部落。他是伊萨·本·穆汉纳之子，1311年其兄穆海纳叛投蒙古伊儿汗国后接任此职，至1317年；两兄弟暗中联手，让马穆鲁克与伊儿汗国相互牵制。

1322年他再度受任，在任至1330年穆海纳复位。法德勒约于1334年去世，他的儿子们后来也担任该职。

en:
Haditha ibn Ghudayya was an emir of the Al Fadl clan of the Banu Rabi'ah and a grandson of Fadl ibn Rabi'ah. Sultan al-Adil, Saladin's brother, founded the office of amir al-arab and named Haditha its first holder, placing the Bedouin of Damascus and Hama under his command.

The Kilab were later brought under him too, so that all the Bedouin tribes of northern Syria answered to him. He died around 1220, and Sultan al-Kamil divided the emirate between his sons Mani and Ali and their kinsman Ghannam.

en:
Husam ad-Din Muhanna ibn Isa (died 1335) was the Al Fadl emir, lord of Palmyra and amir al-arab of the Syrian Bedouin under the Mamluks, succeeding his father Isa in 1284. The sultan imprisoned him in 1293, but he was released two years later and commanded a wing at the Third Battle of Homs in 1300.

He then played the Mamluks off against the Mongol Ilkhanate, defecting to Öljaitü in 1312 and being exiled by an-Nasir Muhammad before reconciling in 1330. His son Musa succeeded him in 1335.

侯萨姆丁·穆汉纳·本·伊萨（？—1335）是法德勒家族埃米尔、泰德穆尔领主，也是马穆鲁克治下叙利亚贝都因人的阿拉伯人埃米尔，1284年继承父职。1293年他被苏丹囚禁，两年后获释；1300年第三次霍姆斯战役中，他指挥军队一翼。

Mani ibn Haditha was an Al Fadl emir and a son of Haditha ibn Ghudayya, the first amir al-arab. When his father died around 1220 Sultan al-Kamil at first divided the Bedouin emirate between Mani, his brother Ali and their kinsman Ghannam.

en:
Muzaffar ad-Din Musa ibn Muhanna (died November 1341) was amir al-arab and lord of Salamiyah and Palmyra under the Mamluk sultanate. Son of Muhanna ibn Isa, he stayed loyal to Sultan an-Nasir Muhammad when his father defected to the Mongol Ilkhanate in 1311, and succeeded as amir al-arab in 1335.

He won back his clan’s confiscated fiefs by threatening revolt, and at the sultan’s request helped force the Syrian viceroy Tankiz to surrender in 1340. He died in November 1341; his son Umar later held the office.
