Sharaf ad-Din Isa ibn Muhanna (died 1284) was an emir of the Al Fadl Bedouin dynasty. After the Mamluk conquest of Syria in 1260, Sultan Baybars made him amir al-arab, commander of the Syrian Bedouin, and he campaigned repeatedly against the Mongol Ilkhanate.

In 1279 he joined a revolt against Qalawun but was restored by 1280. At the Second Battle of Homs in 1281 he led the Mamluk right flank to victory and was made lord of Palmyra. He died in May 1284 and was succeeded by his son Muhanna.

en:
Demetrios was the first known prince of Theodoro, the Greek-ruled Crimean Gothic state with its capital at Mangup, and the traditional ancestor of its Gabras dynasty. Theodoro paid tribute to the Golden Horde to the north and was in constant strife with the Genoese colonies to the south over the coast and its harbour trade.

Scholars following Alexander Vasiliev identify him with ‘Dmitry’, one of three Golden Horde princes at the Battle of Blue Waters in 1362–1363, when Grand Duke Algirdas of Lithuania defeated the Horde.

Prince Stephen, known in Russian sources as Khovra, went to Moscow with his son Gregory, who founded the Simonov Monastery there; the Khovrin and Golovin families claimed descent from them.

德米特里是狄奥多罗——都城设在曼古普、由希腊人统治的克里木哥特人国家——见于记载的第一位王公，被后世奉为加夫拉斯王朝的始祖。狄奥多罗向北方的金帐汗国纳贡，又因沿海地带与港口贸易，与南面的热那亚殖民地纷争不断。

沿袭瓦西里耶夫说法的学者认为，他就是1362—1363年蓝水之战中金帐汗国三位王公之一“德米特里”，此战立陶宛大公阿尔吉尔达斯击败了金帐汗国。

王公斯捷潘在俄罗斯史料中称霍夫拉，带着儿子格里高利前往莫斯科，格里高利在那里创建了西蒙诺夫修道院；霍夫林家族与戈洛温家族自称是他们的后裔。

en:
Alda d'Este (18 July 1333 – 26 September 1381) was born in Ferrara, a daughter of Obizzo III d'Este and Lippa Ariosti. On 16 February 1356 she married Ludovico II Gonzaga, who in 1369 became the third capitano del popolo and lord of Mantua.

Her son Francesco I later ruled Mantua as its fourth capitano, while her daughter Elisabetta wed Carlo I Malatesta, lord of Rimini. Alda died at Mantua in 1381, and Ludovico raised her tomb in the church of San Francesco.

阿尔达·埃斯特（1333年7月18日—1381年9月26日）生于费拉拉，是奥比佐三世·埃斯特与莉帕·阿里奥斯蒂之女。1356年2月16日，她嫁给卢多维科二世·贡扎加；后者于1369年成为曼托瓦第三任人民首领兼领主。

儿子弗朗切斯科一世后来成为曼托瓦第四任人民首领，女儿埃莉莎贝塔嫁给里米尼领主卡洛一世·马拉泰斯塔。1381年阿尔达在曼托瓦去世，卢多维科为她在圣方济各教堂修建了陵墓。

en:
Aldobrandino d'Este (1325–1381) was an illegitimate son of Rinaldo II d'Este, lord of Ferrara. He entered the Church in 1344 and was elected bishop of Adria in 1348, later holding the sees of Modena and Ferrara.

As bishop of Modena he backed the Este against the Visconti, and his refusal to pay anti-Ghibelline clerical taxes earned him repeated excommunication. He devoted himself to aiding the poor, and after his death on 30 October 1381 he was venerated as a beatus.

en:
Aldobrandino I d'Este (c. 1190–1215) succeeded his father Azzo VI in 1212 as Marquis of Este and lord of Ferrara. He backed Pope Innocent III and Frederick II against Otto IV.

War with Padua cost him Este and Montagnana in 1213, and after a surrender he returned to Ferrara and reached a compromise with the powerful Salinguerra family. At Innocent's bidding he campaigned in the March of Ancona against the Celano counts, initially defeating them.

He died at Ancona in October 1215, aged twenty-five, perhaps poisoned. His posthumous son Contardo was venerated as a saint, and his daughter Beatrice married Andrew II of Hungary.

阿尔多布兰迪诺一世·埃斯特（约1190—1215）是阿佐六世之子，1212年继其父为埃斯特侯爵兼费拉拉领主。他支持教皇英诺森三世和腓特烈二世，反对奥托四世。

在与帕多瓦的战争中，他于1213年失去埃斯特和蒙塔尼亚纳；投降后返回费拉拉，与强大的萨林圭拉家族达成妥协。他又奉英诺森之命进军安科纳边区，讨伐切拉诺伯爵，初期将其击败。

1215年10月他死于安科纳，年仅25岁，一说遭毒杀。遗腹子孔塔尔多后来被尊为圣徒，女儿贝阿特丽切嫁给匈牙利国王安德烈二世。

en:
Aldobrandino II d'Este (c. 1267–1326) was a son of Obizzo II, and in 1289 married Alda Rangoni. When his brother Azzo VIII died in January 1308 he claimed the marquisate, but the succession struggle let papal forces seize Ferrara, and the Este went into exile for nearly nine years, dropping claims to Modena and Reggio.

The ensuing war ended in 1313 with Venice recognizing Ferrara as papal territory. In 1317 Aldobrandino returned with his sons and recovered the lordship of Ferrara, ruling until his death at Bologna on 26 July 1326. His sons succeeded him, sharing the city until Obizzo III made himself sole lord.

阿尔多布兰迪诺二世·埃斯特（约1267—1326）是奥比佐二世之子，1289年娶阿尔达·兰戈尼。1308年1月其兄阿佐八世去世，他宣称继承侯爵之位，但继承权之争使教皇军队趁机夺取费拉拉，埃斯特家族流亡近九年，他也放弃了对摩德纳和雷焦的权利。

随后的战争于1313年结束，威尼斯承认费拉拉属于教皇。1317年，阿尔多布兰迪诺率诸子返回费拉拉，恢复领主统治，直到1326年7月26日在博洛尼亚去世。其子们共同继位，共治城市，最终由奥比佐三世独掌大权。

en:
Aldobrandino III d'Este (14 September 1335 – 3 November 1361) was the eldest son of Obizzo III d'Este and Lippa Ariosti, born before his parents married and legitimized by a bull of Pope Clement VI. In 1352 he succeeded his father as lord of Ferrara and Modena.

In 1355 he was among the first Italian lords to accompany Charles IV on his march to Rome for the imperial coronation, a loyalty that won his state wide privileges. He died on 3 November 1361, leaving a five-year-old son, Obizzo, who did not inherit; power passed instead to his brother Niccolò II.

阿尔多布兰迪诺三世·埃斯特（1335年9月14日—1361年11月3日）是奥比佐三世·埃斯特与莉帕·阿里奥斯蒂的长子，生于父母成婚之前，由教皇克雷芒六世颁布诏书合法化。1352年，他继其父成为费拉拉和摩德纳领主。

en:
Azzo VI d'Este (1170–1212), called Azzolino, became Marquis of Este on his father Azzo V's death in 1190. A leading Guelph captain in Lombardy, he served as podestà of several cities in Lombardy.

He waged a long feud with the Ghibelline Salinguerra Torelli, taking his stronghold of Fratta in 1205. Salinguerra and his ally Ezzelino da Romano drove him away, but Azzo retook Fratta in 1206. Emperor Otto IV reconciled the rivals when he came to Italy.

In 1208 Azzo was made Marquis of Ancona, and Ferrara chose him as its first lord. In 1212 Ezzelino defeated him near Vicenza; he died at Verona that November.

阿佐六世·埃斯特（1170—1212），又名阿佐利诺，1190年父亲阿佐五世去世后袭为埃斯特侯爵。他是伦巴第圭尔夫派的重要军事领袖，曾出任伦巴第数座城市的波德斯塔。

他与吉伯林派的萨林圭拉·托雷利长期交战，1205年攻克其弗拉塔据点。他被萨林圭拉与其盟友埃泽利诺·达·罗马诺逐走后，于1206年夺回弗拉塔。皇帝奥托四世来到意大利后促成两人和解。

1208年，阿佐被封为安科纳侯爵，同年费拉拉人推举他为城市的第一任领主。1212年，他在维琴察附近被埃泽利诺击败，同年11月死于维罗纳。

en:
Azzo VII d'Este, called Novello (c. 1205–1264), inherited the Este titles as a boy in 1215 after his half-brother Aldobrandino I died; his mother ransomed him from Florentine bankers. He led the Guelphs of the March of Treviso and held several podestà posts before, in 1240, driving the Ghibelline Salinguerra Torelli out of Ferrara and becoming its lord.

His troops helped capture Ezzelino da Romano at Cassano d'Adda in 1259. His only son Rinaldo died a hostage of Frederick II in Apulia; when Azzo died in February 1264, his grandson Obizzo II succeeded him.

en:
Azzo VIII d'Este (c. 1263–1308) succeeded his father Obizzo II, whom Dante says he murdered, as lord of Ferrara in February 1293. In 1305 he paid Charles II of Naples a great sum to marry his daughter Beatrice, a bargain Dante denounced as slave-trading.

The agreement imposed primogeniture, excluding his brother Francesco, who joined a league against him. When Azzo promised Modena and Reggio to Beatrice, both cities rebelled and fell to the league in 1306. He died in January 1308, and his will in favour of Fresco's young son Folco sparked the first War of Ferrara.

Beatrice d'Este (18 September 1332 – 1387) was a daughter of Obizzo III d'Este, lord of Ferrara and Modena, by his long-time mistress Lippa Ariosti; a papal bull legitimized their children in 1346, and the couple married the next year.

In 1365 she became the second wife of Waldemar I, the Ascani prince of Anhalt-Zerbst, whose residence was Dessau. The marriage was childless, and after Waldemar died in 1368 she lived as a widow until her own death in 1387.

Costanza della Scala (c. 1263–1306) was the daughter of Alberto I della Scala, lord of Verona. In 1289 she married Obizzo II d'Este, lord of Ferrara. When Obizzo was killed in 1293, probably by his son Azzo VIII, Azzo drove her out of Ferrara in 1294; her father then made war on the Este and defeated them.

In 1299 her brother Cangrande I married her to Guido Bonacolsi, lord of Mantua, sealing the Verona-Mantua alliance. She died at Ferrara in 1306, leaving no sons.

Elisa d'Este (1337 – 12 August 1402) was a Ferrarese noblewoman, daughter of Obizzo III d'Este, lord of Ferrara, and Lippa Ariosti. In 1350 she married Guido III da Polenta, who ruled Ravenna for thirty peaceful years after 1359 and was named the city's papal vicar in 1364.

Her daughters included Leta and Beatrice. In 1389 Guido was seized and imprisoned by his own sons and died in their custody that December, while Elisa lived on until 1402.

en:
Folco II d'Este (born c. 1300) was the designated heir to the lordship of Ferrara. The son of Fresco d'Este, he was named to succeed his grandfather Azzo VIII in his will. When Azzo died in 1308 his father ruled as his guardian, but his great-uncles contested the succession and appealed to Pope Clement V.

Ferrara rose against Fresco, who withdrew and sought Venetian help. A papal army seized Ferrara in 1309, and the city remained under direct papal control for years. Fresco and Folco took refuge in Venice, where both died in exile.

费拉拉民众起而反对弗雷斯科，他被迫撤退并向威尼斯求援。1309年教皇军队攻占费拉拉，该城此后由教皇国直接统治多年。弗雷斯科和福尔科逃往威尼斯，父子二人最终客死异乡。

en:
Francesco d'Este (died 23 August 1312) was a son of Obizzo II d'Este and founder of the Este cadet branch of the Marchesi d'Este. He helped his brother Azzo VIII rule Ferrara, but in 1305 opposed Azzo's Angevin marriage over its implications for the succession, and in 1306 joined a Modena–Reggio league against him.

In 1308 he appealed to Pope Clement V when his nephew Fresco held Ferrara. Siding with the papacy against Emperor Henry VII, he was killed at Ferrara's gates on 23 August 1312 by followers of the King of Naples.

en:
Francesco d'Este (1325–1384), born at Ferrara, was the son of Bertoldo I d'Este and Domenica Pio. Knighted in 1333, he was made governor of Parma by his cousin Obizzo III. When Obizzo died in 1352, Francesco claimed a share in ruling Ferrara and later tried to seize the Este lands with Malatesta, Gonzaga and Carraresi aid, but was defeated.

He then served the Visconti of Milan, campaigning against Modena and Bologna in 1359. He married Caterina Visconti and Taddea di Barbiano, and died at Pavia in 1384; his son Azzo X d'Este became a condottiere.

弗朗切斯科·埃斯特（1325—1384）生于费拉拉，是贝特霍尔德一世·埃斯特与多梅妮卡·皮奥之子。1333年受封骑士，被堂兄奥比佐三世任命为帕尔马总督。1352年奥比佐三世去世后，他要求参与费拉拉的统治，后来又在马拉泰斯塔、贡扎加和卡拉雷西家族支援下试图夺取埃斯特领地，却被击败。

en:
Fresco d'Este (c. 1280–1312) was an illegitimate son of Azzo VIII d'Este, lord of Ferrara. In 1308, the people of Ferrara appointed him guardian of his son Folco, whom Azzo had named his heir. His uncles Aldobrandino and Francesco challenged the succession and appealed to Pope Clement V.

When Ferrara rebelled against him, Fresco sought Venetian aid and then retired to Venice. In 1309 papal troops defeated the Venetian army and took Ferrara for the Papal States. Fresco remained in Venice with Folco until his death in 1312.

Giacoma Pepoli (c. 1296 – 3 March 1341) was a daughter of Romeo Pepoli, the Bolognese banker who made his family the wealthiest in Italy and became de facto signore of Bologna, and of Azzolina Tettalasini.

In May 1317 she married Obizzo III d'Este in the year the Este seized power in Ferrara, becoming lady consort of the city. Her daughter Violante d'Este married the condottiere Malatesta Ungaro in 1344. Giacoma died on 3 March 1341, leaving only one child.

en:
Filippa Ariosti, known as Lippa and called la Bella (died 27 November 1347), was the daughter of the Bolognese noble Iacopo Ariosti. She met Obizzo III d'Este while he was exiled in Bologna after quarreling with Pope John XXII, and became his mistress; when he was reconciled with the papacy in 1329 she followed him to Ferrara. She bore him ten children, including Aldobrandino III and Niccolò II.

Obizzo married her on her deathbed, and a papal bull legitimated their children. Ariosto praised the beautiful Lippa of Bologna in Orlando Furioso.

菲利帕·阿里奥斯蒂，通称莉帕，人称“美人”（1347年11月27日卒），是博洛尼亚贵族雅各布·阿里奥斯蒂之女。奥比佐三世·埃斯特因与教皇约翰二十二世冲突而流亡博洛尼亚期间与她相识，她成了他的情妇；1329年他与教廷和解后，她随他前往费拉拉。她为他生下十个子女，包括后来的领主阿尔多布兰迪诺三世和尼科洛二世。

她临终之际，奥比佐与她成婚，教皇诏书则使他们的子女获得合法地位。阿里奥斯托在《疯狂的罗兰》中称颂这位博洛尼亚美人莉帕。

en:
Obizzo II d'Este (c. 1247–1293) was the illegitimate son of Rinaldo d'Este and grandson of Marquis Azzo VII. Banished with his mother, he grew up at Ravenna, and after his father died a hostage in Apulia, Azzo VII fought to have him recognized as his heir. Pope Innocent IV legitimated him in 1252.

In 1264 the Ferrarese proclaimed him their lifelong lord; he added Modena in 1288 and Reggio in 1289, founding the Este signoria over Ferrara. Dante places him in the Seventh Circle of Hell; he was probably murdered in February 1293, reputedly by his son Azzo VIII.

奥比佐二世·埃斯特（约1247—1293）是里纳尔多·埃斯特的私生子，阿佐七世侯爵的孙子。他自幼随母亲被逐，在拉文纳长大；父亲作为人质死于普利亚后，阿佐七世努力争取承认他的继承权。1252年，教皇英诺森四世将他合法化。

1264年，费拉拉人宣布他为终身领主；他又于1288年取得摩德纳、1289年取得雷焦，开创了埃斯特家族在费拉拉的领主政权。但丁把他放在《神曲·地狱篇》第七圈中；他很可能于1293年2月遇害，据称凶手是其子阿佐八世。

en:
Obizzo III d'Este (14 July 1294 – 20 March 1352) ruled Ferrara for thirty-five years. A son of Aldobrandino II d'Este, he took power in 1317 jointly with his brothers and cousin, and ended as sole lord.

Modena's general council restored Este rule in 1336, and he bought Parma in 1344 but held it only two years. His marriage gave him no children; his heirs came from his long-time mistress Lippa Ariosti, known as la Bella.

She bore his successors Aldobrandino III and Niccolò II and several daughters. He married her in November 1347, shortly before her death, to legitimize them.

奥比佐三世·埃斯特（1294年7月14日—1352年3月20日）统治费拉拉三十五年。他是阿尔多布兰迪诺二世·埃斯特之子，1317年起与兄弟和堂兄共同执政，最后成为唯一的领主。

1336年，摩德纳大议事会重新拥立埃斯特家族；1344年他购得帕尔马，但仅统治两年。他的婚姻没有子女，继承人来自他的长期情妇、人称“美人”的莉帕·阿里奥斯蒂。

莉帕生下了继承人阿尔多布兰迪诺三世和尼科洛二世以及几个女儿。1347年11月，莉帕临终前，他与她成婚，使子女获得合法地位。

en:
Rinaldo II d'Este (c. 1290–1335) was a son of Aldobrandino II d'Este. In July 1317 Ferrara's people expelled the Angevin rulers, acclaimed the Este and gave Rinaldo power. Pope John XXII excommunicated him, and after he received investiture from Louis the Bavarian in 1324, the pope launched a crusade against the Este.

Rinaldo later reconciled with the papacy and in 1329 received Ferrara as a papal vicariate with his brothers. In 1333 he routed a Bolognese army besieging Ferrara, and in June 1335 he conquered Modena, but died on 31 December 1335 before receiving its investiture.

里纳尔多二世·埃斯特（约1290—1335）是阿尔多布兰迪诺二世·埃斯特之子。1317年7月，费拉拉民众驱逐安茹统治者，拥立埃斯特家族，由里纳尔多掌权。教皇约翰二十二世将他开除教籍；1324年他接受巴伐利亚的路德维希的册封，教皇遂对埃斯特家族发动十字军。

en:
Ferdinand of Portugal (1188–1233), fourth son of King Sancho I of Portugal, was born at Coimbra and became count of Flanders and Hainaut jure uxoris by marrying Countess Joan in Paris in 1212. Seized en route by Prince Louis of France over the Artois dowry, he was freed after concessions and joined the enemies of France.

Captured at the Battle of Bouvines in July 1214, he spent twelve years in French prisons while Joan ruled alone. Released by Blanche of Castile in 1226, he died at Noyon in 1233.

en:
William II of Dampierre (1196–1231), the second son of Guy II, constable of Champagne, and Mathilde of Bourbon, held the lordship of Dampierre from 1216. In 1223 he married Margaret, later Countess Margaret II of Flanders and Hainault.

Their Dampierre sons later pressed her claim against the children of her first marriage in the War of the Succession of Flanders and Hainault. With Margaret he founded Cistercian nunneries, including one at Saint-Dizier in 1226; he died in 1231 and was buried there.

en:
William III of Dampierre (1224–1251), lord of Dampierre from 1231, was the eldest son of William II of Dampierre and Countess Margaret II of Flanders. When Margaret inherited Flanders and Hainault in 1244, a succession war pitted William against the Avesnes sons of her marriage. Louis IX of France awarded him Flanders in 1246, and Margaret invested him as count in 1247.

After peace with the Avesnes in May 1250, he was killed at a tournament in Trazegnies on 6 June 1251. His brother Guy succeeded him.

en:
William of Termonde (1248–1311), second son of Count Guy of Flanders, held the lordship of Termonde and other Flemish lands. In 1270 he joined his father on the Eighth Crusade, and two years later led a mission asking Edward I of England to intercede with the French king over the embargo on Flemish trade.

Linked to the French crown by marriage, he stayed neutral in Guy's wars with Philip IV. After the Flemish defeat at Furnes in 1297, his family's lands were threatened. He was captured with his father in 1300 and returned to Flanders after four years; William died in 1311.

en:
Guy of Dampierre (c. 1226–1305), son of William II of Dampierre and Margaret II, ruled Flanders as count from 1251. In 1294 he arranged a marriage between his daughter Philippa and the English prince Edward, but Philip IV of France imprisoned him and forced him to cancel it.

Defying Philip, Guy allied with Edward I of England, but French forces conquered Flanders and took him prisoner in 1300. Flemish townsmen crushed a French army at the Golden Spurs in 1302 while he was captive; he was briefly released, returned to prison after defeat in 1304, and died there in March 1305.

Isabelle of Luxembourg (c. 1247–1298) was the daughter of Henry V of Luxembourg and Margaret of Bar. In 1265 she married Guy of Dampierre, Count of Flanders, as his second wife, settling her family's dispute with Guy over Namur. Her children included John I, Marquis of Namur, and a daughter Philippa.

Guy's plan to wed Philippa to Edward, Prince of Wales was crushed by Philip IV of France, who imprisoned her in Paris. Isabelle died in September 1298; Philippa remained captive until her own death in 1306.

卢森堡的伊莎贝尔（约1247—1298）是卢森堡伯爵亨利五世与巴尔的玛格丽特之女。1265年她嫁给佛兰德伯爵当皮埃尔的居伊，为其第二任妻子，这桩婚事了结了两家围绕那慕尔伯国的争端。她的子女包括那慕尔侯爵约翰一世和女儿菲莉帕。

en:
Jacob van Artevelde (c. 1290–1345), called the Wise Man, was a wealthy Ghent cloth merchant who became the leader of Flanders when the Hundred Years' War threatened the wool trade on which the Flemish towns depended. Fearing war would ruin Ghent, he entered politics in 1337 and bound the chief towns into an alliance for neutrality.

He took control of the revolt against Count Louis I, who fled to France, and ruled Ghent as captain general until his death. In 1340 he persuaded the towns to recognize Edward III as king of France and overlord of Flanders, and trade flourished under his near-dictatorial rule.

In 1345 rumours that he meant to make the Black Prince count, suspicion of embezzlement and his excommunication provoked an uprising in Ghent, and a mob killed him in July.

雅各布·范阿特费尔德（约1290—1345），人称“智者”，是根特的富裕呢绒商。百年战争威胁到佛兰德诸城赖以生存的羊毛贸易时，他成为当地的领袖。他担心战争毁掉根特的繁荣，于1337年投身政治，把诸城结成同盟以维持中立。

他掌握了反对伯爵路易一世的起义，路易逃往法国；此后他以总司令身份统治根特，直至去世。1340年，他说服诸城承认爱德华三世为法兰西国王和佛兰德的宗主，在他近乎独裁的统治下，贸易一度兴旺。

1345年，他打算拥立黑太子为伯爵的传言、贪污嫌疑及遭开除教籍引发根特民变，他在7月被暴动民众杀死。

en:
Jeanne de Bretagne (1296 – 24 May 1364) was a Breton princess, daughter of Arthur II, Duke of Brittany, and Yolande de Dreux, countess of Montfort. With a papal dispensation, she married in 1324 Robert de Cassel, lord of Marle and Cassel and second son of Count Robert III of Flanders.

Her daughter Yolande married Henry IV, Count of Bar, while her young son Jean died in 1332. After Robert's death in 1331, Jeanne lived on to 1364, dying at Ypres.

en:
Louis I (c. 1304–1346), Louis of Nevers, was Count of Flanders and Nevers from 1322. Raised in France, he married Margaret, daughter of King Philip V, in 1320 and tied his county to the French crown. His refusal of an English alliance clashed with the interests of Flanders' cloth industry.

Town revolts marked his rule: after Philip VI crushed the rebels at Cassel in 1328, Louis repressed the towns harshly and restricted their liberties. In 1338 Jacob van Artevelde's Ghent uprising drove him into exile. He was killed fighting for Philip VI at Crécy on 26 August 1346 and succeeded by his son Louis II.

en:
Louis II (1330–1384), called Louis of Male, succeeded his father as Count of Flanders after Crécy in 1346, abandoning his father's pro-French line. Ghent's weavers sought to impose an English marriage on him, but he escaped their control under cover of a falcon hunt in 1347 and married Margaret of Brabant.

He signed neutrality with England in 1348, giving Flanders three decades of recovery. The White Hoods revolt of 1379 overwhelmed him until French forces crushed it at Roosebeke in 1382. He died in 1384, leaving Flanders to his daughter Margaret, wife of Philip the Bold.

en:
Margaret I (1310 – 9 May 1382) was a Capetian princess, a daughter of King Philip V of France and Joan II of Burgundy. In 1320 she married Louis I of Flanders, binding his county to the French crown, and when Louis fell at Crécy in 1346 she served as regent of Flanders for her son Louis II.

After Duke Philip I of Burgundy died childless in 1361, Margaret inherited Artois and the county of Burgundy and ruled them suo jure. She promoted the 1369 marriage of her granddaughter Margaret III to Philip the Bold.

en:
Margaret of Alsace (c. 1145–1194), daughter of Count Thierry, inherited the county in 1191 after the childless death of her brother Philip of Alsace. In 1160 she married Ralph II of Vermandois, but his leprosy prevented the marriage from being consummated, and he died in 1167.

In 1169 she married Count Baldwin V of Hainaut, who ruled Flanders at her side. Their daughter Isabella married Philip II of France, while their sons Baldwin IX and Henry both became Latin emperors of Constantinople. Margaret ruled as countess suo jure until her death in 1194.

阿尔萨斯的玛格丽特（约1145—1194）是伯爵蒂埃里之女，1191年其兄阿尔萨斯的菲利普无嗣而亡，她由此继承佛兰德伯国。1160年她嫁给韦芒杜瓦伯爵拉乌尔二世，但因丈夫患麻风病而未能圆房，拉乌尔于1167年去世。

1169年她改嫁埃诺伯爵博杜安五世，后者与她共同统治佛兰德。他们的女儿伊莎贝拉嫁给法王腓力二世，儿子博杜安九世与亨利后来都成为君士坦丁堡的拉丁皇帝。玛格丽特以本人的继承权担任女伯爵，直至1194年去世。

en:
Philip of Alsace (1143–1191) ruled Flanders, first as co-count with his crusader father Thierry from 1157, then alone from 1168. His marriage to Elisabeth brought him Vermandois and the Amiénois, and in 1167 they inherited the county of Vermandois. Flemish clothmaking depended on English wool, and he renewed a treaty with England in 1163. He once arbitrated between the kings of France and England, but war with the French crown later cost him Vermandois.

He died of disease at the siege of Acre in 1191 during the Third Crusade. Under his patronage Chrétien de Troyes wrote the unfinished Perceval.

阿尔萨斯的菲利普（1143—1191）是佛兰德伯爵：1157年参加十字军的父亲蒂埃里外出期间，他以协理伯爵身份理政，1168年起独自统治。他与韦芒杜瓦的伊丽莎白成婚，获得韦芒杜瓦和亚眠领地，1167年两人继承韦芒杜瓦伯国。佛兰德的毛纺业依赖英国羊毛，他于1163年同英格兰续订条约。他曾在法王与英王之间调停，但后来与法国王室交战，丧失韦芒杜瓦。

1191年第三次十字军期间，他病逝于阿卡围城战。诗人克雷蒂安·德·特鲁瓦在他的赞助下创作了未完成的《珀西瓦尔》。

en:
Robert of Cassel (c. 1278–1331), second son of Count Robert III of Flanders, held Cassel and Dunkirk, receiving maritime Flanders as an apanage in 1320. Unlike his elder brother Louis of Nevers, he backed his father in the wars with Philip IV. He built a castle at Dunkirk around 1322, but it was demolished during a Flemish revolt.

After the rebels were crushed at the Battle of Cassel in 1328, he fined them heavily, restoring Dunkirk's customs and rights a year later. He died at Warneton in 1331, leaving young children.

en:
Robert III of Béthune, the Lion of Flanders (1249–1322), was the eldest son of Count Guy of Dampierre. He fought for Charles I of Sicily at Benevento in 1266 and joined the Eighth Crusade in 1270. Through his second wife Yolande of Nevers he became count of Nevers in 1273.

From 1297 Robert led Flemish resistance to Philip IV. Captured in 1300, he was still in a French prison when the Flemings won the Golden Spurs in 1302. He succeeded Guy in 1305 under the harsh Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge, resumed the struggle in 1310, and died at Ypres in 1322.

en:
Thierry of Alsace (c. 1099–1168), son of Theodoric II of Lorraine and Gertrude of Flanders, claimed the county after Charles the Good's murder in 1127. The Flemish towns backed him against King Louis VI's candidate William Clito, whose death in July 1128 left Thierry sole count.

He submitted to Louis in 1132, checked Baldwin IV of Hainaut, and gave Flanders forty years of stable rule, in which agriculture and commerce developed.

Four times he campaigned in the East, joining the Second Crusade and the 1164 invasion of Egypt. By Sibylla of Anjou he left sons Philip and Matthew and daughter Margaret I.

阿尔萨斯的蒂埃里（约1099—1168）是洛林的狄奥多里克二世与佛兰德的格特鲁德之子。1127年“好人”查理遇刺后，他声索佛兰德伯国；各城市支持他对抗法王路易六世扶植的威廉·克利托，1128年7月威廉之死使蒂埃里成为唯一的伯爵。

他于1132年向路易六世臣服，遏制了埃诺的博杜安四世，为佛兰德带来四十年的稳定统治，其间农业和商业均有发展。

他四次赴东方作战，参加过第二次十字军东征和1164年入侵埃及的行动。他与安茹的西比拉生有菲利普、马修两个儿子和女儿玛格丽特一世。

en:
Heinrich VI of Hohenberg (1277–1353) ruled the Imperial Abbey of Fulda as prince-abbot from 1315 until his death. When he built a second castle inside the town in 1319–1320, the citizens, helped by the abbey's high advocate Count Johann I of Ziegenhain, stormed and destroyed it. He fled to Emperor Louis the Bavarian, who outlawed the town and the count.

In 1326 Heinrich raised the city's annual tax from 100 to 800 pounds for seven years. When he tried again in 1330 and met resistance, he imprisoned wealthy citizens and demanded 9500 pounds for their release.

The citizens rose in 1331, but his ministeriales crushed them. In the peace mediated by Archbishop Baldwin of Trier, the citizens rebuilt the castle and paid heavy fines, the revolt's leaders were executed, and Fulda received a council and a mayor.

霍亨贝格的海因里希六世（1277—1353）自1315年起担任富尔达帝国修道院的亲王修道院长，直至去世。1319至1320年，他在富尔达城内修建第二座城堡，市民在修道院高级保护人齐根海因伯爵约翰一世的协助下攻陷并拆毁了它。他逃到皇帝路德维希（巴伐利亚人）处控诉，城市与伯爵被宣布剥夺法律保护。

1326年，海因里希把城市年税从100磅提高到800磅，为期七年；1330年他试图再次加税，遭到抵制，便拘禁富裕市民，索取9500磅保释金。

市民于1331年起义，被他的家臣骑士镇压。经特里尔大主教巴尔杜因调停议和，市民重建城堡并缴纳巨额罚金，起义首领被处决，富尔达则获准设立市议会与市长。

en:
Philip VI of Falkenstein (c. 1320 – 1373), called the Elder, was a Hessian noble with his seat at Königstein Castle. Around 1335 he and his kinsman Philip V inherited the imperial chamberlainship from the extinct elder line. In 1352 he was granted town rights at Hofheim, but lost it to Mainz in 1366 after an imperial war.

Dogged by debt, he fell from his horse while fleeing the lords of Reifenberg's siege of Königstein and was captured, dying after eight days in captivity. His son Werner became Archbishop and Elector of Trier in 1388.

菲利普六世·冯法尔肯施泰因（约1320—1373年），人称“长者”，是黑森贵族，驻地在柯尼希施泰因城堡。约1335年，他与族人菲利普五世从绝嗣的长支继承帝国宫廷总管之职。1352年他获得在霍夫海姆设市筑堡的特权，但在一场帝国战争中战败，1366年霍夫海姆落入美因茨大主教区之手。

他债台高筑，赖芬贝格领主围攻柯尼希施泰因时出逃坠马被俘，囚禁八天后死去。其子维尔纳于1388年成为特里尔大主教兼选帝侯。

en:
Gugliarello Acciaiuoli, known as Acciaiolo, was the earliest known ancestor of the Acciaioli of Florence. A Guelph born at Brescia, he fled political feuds and settled in Florence around 1160, where he enrolled in the money-changers' guild.

He probably traded in steel, which gave him the nickname Acciaiolo, and his family adopted the Brescian coat of arms. By his wife Ghisella he left sons Riccomanno and Leone, a doctor of law.

en:
Angelo Acciaiuoli (born c. 1319) was a member of the Florentine Acciaioli family, the son of the politician Donato Acciaiuoli il Vecchio and Taggia Biliotti. His father served several terms as a prior of Florence and died in the city in 1335, and his brother Jacopo Acciaiuoli was Gonfaloniere of Florence in 1341.

In 1350 Angelo represented the Republic of Florence. He negotiated with the king of Naples over the sale of Prato to the Florentine republic.

en:
Angelo Acciaioli (1298–1357), called the Elder, was a Dominican friar of the Florentine Acciaioli family and a bishop who ended up governing a city. Bishop of Aquila from 1328, he became bishop of Florence in 1342 and early in his tenure led the plot against the tyrannical Duke of Athens, heading the Balìa of Fourteen after the duke was driven out in 1343.

A skilled diplomat, he went three times as the republic's envoy to the papal court at Avignon, in 1344, 1348 and 1351, and in 1349 Queen Joanna I made him chancellor of the kingdom of Naples.

He helped found the Studio Fiorentino and, with his cousin Niccolò, the Florence Charterhouse. In 1355 he gave up his diocese to become abbot of Monte Cassino, and he died in Naples in 1357.

安杰洛·阿恰约利（1298—1357），人称“长者”，出身佛罗伦萨阿恰约利家族，是多明我会修士，也是一位最终执掌一城政务的主教。他1328年起任阿奎拉主教，1342年转任佛罗伦萨主教，任内之初就领头密谋推翻暴虐的雅典公爵，公爵被逐后于1343年主持十四人巴利亚政务会。

他长于外交，1344、1348和1351年三次受共和国派遣出使阿维尼翁教廷；1349年乔万娜女王任命他为那不勒斯王国宰相。

他还参与创办佛罗伦萨大学的前身“佛罗伦萨学堂”，并与堂亲尼科洛一同创建佛罗伦萨卡尔特修道院。1355年他辞去主教职务，出任卡西诺山修道院院长，1357年在那不勒斯去世。

Averardo de' Medici (1320–1363), called Bicci, was a Florentine politician, the son of Salvestro de' Medici and Lisa Donati. His son Giovanni di Bicci became the first historically significant Medici and founded the Medici Bank.

Through Giovanni, Averardo was the ancestor of the Medici lords of Florence and the grand dukes of Tuscany. His name came from the legendary knight Averardo, from whom the family claimed descent.

en:
Averardo de' Medici (c. 1270–1318) was a Florentine merchant and politician and a contemporary of Dante. Elected prior in 1309, he acquired half the patronage of Florence's church of San Tommaso in 1311 and became Gonfaloniere of Justice in 1314.

In the war against the Ghibelline leader Uguccione della Faggiola, he was made captain-general of the Guelph party in Tuscany and Romagna by Peter of Anjou, count of Gravina.

He was one of the first Medici to amass wealth in trade. His sons founded the Filii Averardi bank, recorded until 1330.

他是最早靠经商积累财富的美第奇成员之一。他的儿子们后来创办了“阿韦拉尔多之子”银行商号，有关商号的记载延续至1330年。

en:
Filippo Brunelleschi (1377–1446) was a Florentine goldsmith turned architect and engineer. The son of a notary, he trained as a goldsmith and became a master in 1398. After losing the 1401 competition for the Florence Baptistery's bronze doors to Lorenzo Ghiberti, he studied Roman ruins with Donatello and turned to architecture. Around 1415 his painted panels established the mathematical rules of linear perspective.

From 1420 he built Florence Cathedral's great dome, completed in 1436 without timber centering through ingenious machines and self-supporting masonry; in 1421 he received the first recorded patent in Europe, for a river barge. He died in Florence in 1446, regarded as a founding father of Renaissance architecture.

菲利波·布鲁内莱斯基（1377—1446）是佛罗伦萨金匠出身的建筑师与工程师。他是公证人之子，受训成为金匠，1398年取得大师资格。1401年，他在佛罗伦萨洗礼堂青铜大门的竞标中负于洛伦佐·吉贝尔蒂，随后与多纳泰罗一同考察罗马古迹，转而投身建筑。约1415年，他以画板实验确立了线性透视的数学法则。

Coluccio Salutati (1331–1406), born near Pistoia, studied in Bologna and worked as a notary in papal and city service before becoming chancellor of Florence in 1375.

For thirty years his Ciceronian official letters carried the republic through its war with Pope Gregory XI and the two wars against Gian Galeazzo Visconti, who said one Salutati letter did more damage than a thousand horsemen.

As a humanist he found Cicero's lost Letters to Friends, amassed some eight hundred books, and in 1397 brought Manuel Chrysoloras to Florence to teach Greek.

科卢乔·萨卢塔蒂（1331—1406）生于皮斯托亚附近，曾在博洛尼亚求学并担任公证人，在教廷和多个城邦任职后，于1375年出任佛罗伦萨国务秘书。

此后三十年，他那西塞罗式的官方信函伴随共和国经历与教皇格列高利十一世的战争，以及同吉安·加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂的两场战争；维斯孔蒂曾说，萨卢塔蒂的一封信比一千名骑兵更具杀伤力。

作为人文主义者，他寻获西塞罗失传的《致友人书信》，聚书约八百卷，并于1397年把曼努埃尔·赫里索洛拉斯请到佛罗伦萨教授希腊语。

en:
Donato di Niccolò di Betto Bardi, known as Donatello (c. 1386–1466), was a Florentine sculptor who helped create the Early Renaissance style. The son of a wool-stretcher, he studied ancient remains in Rome with Filippo Brunelleschi after 1402, and from 1404 worked in Ghiberti's workshop on the Baptistery doors, carving prophets and saints for the cathedral and Orsanmichele.

His bronze David, about 1440, probably made for Cosimo de' Medici, was the first free-standing nude male statue since antiquity. In 1443 he left for Padua and stayed ten years; his equestrian monument of the condottiere Gattamelata, completed in 1453, became the model for later monuments.

All accounts call him amiable but careless about money: he is said to have hung a basket of coins from his workshop ceiling for his assistants to take from. He died in Florence in 1466 and was buried in San Lorenzo near Cosimo de' Medici.

多纳托·迪·尼科洛·迪·贝托·巴尔迪，即多那太罗（约1386—1466），是佛罗伦萨雕刻家，文艺复兴初期风格的开创者之一。他是拉毛工人之子，1402年后与布鲁内莱斯基同赴罗马考察古代遗迹，1404年起在吉贝尔蒂的作坊参与洗礼堂铜门制作，为大教堂和奥尔桑米凯莱教堂雕刻先知与圣徒像。

约1440年的青铜《大卫》很可能是为科西莫·德·美第奇所作，是古典时代以来第一尊独立裸体男性雕像。1443年他前往帕多瓦并在那里住了十年，所作加塔梅拉塔青铜骑马像1453年完工，成为后世同类纪念像的样板。

各种记载都说他和气却不善理财，相传他在作坊天花板上吊一只装钱的篮子，让助手随用随取。他于1466年在佛罗伦萨去世，葬于圣老楞佐圣殿，邻近科西莫·德·美第奇之墓。

en:
Donato Acciaiuoli, called il Vecchio to distinguish him from a later namesake, was a Florentine statesman and son of Tommaso Acciaiuoli. He served repeatedly as a priore di Libertà, as a councillor of merchants and among the Dodici Buonomini, and in 1325 was captain of the Florentine militia and an envoy to Naples.

In 1331 he was gonfaloniere di compagnia, and in 1328 he helped reorganise Florence's government. He went on further embassies to Bologna in 1332 and Naples in 1333.

He died in 1335 and was buried in Santi Apostoli. By Taggia Biliotti he left sons Jacopo, Gherardo and Angelo.

他于1335年去世，葬于圣宗徒教堂。他与塔贾·比利奥蒂生有雅各布、杰拉尔多和安杰洛。

Filippo degli Albizzi (c. 1286–after 1329) was a Florentine of the Black Guelph Albizzi family, the son of Orlando degli Albizzi and Ghisola de' Pazzi. He married Contessa di Sinibaldo Donati.

He rose through the republic's highest magistracies, sitting as a prior in 1317, serving as Gonfaloniere of Justice in 1327–1328 and as one of the Twelve Good Men in 1329. His sons included Piero degli Albizzi, the Guelph leader beheaded in 1379, and Luca, who died in 1348.

Francesco Acciaiuoli (died c. 1355) was a Florentine politician, a son of Monte Acciaiuoli and grandson of Tommaso Acciaiuoli, and a brother of Angelo, the bishop.

Over more than thirty years he repeatedly held the republic's senior offices, including priore di Libertà, gonfaloniere of the Republic, one of the Dodici Buonomini and capitano del popolo at Pistoia. In 1342, while gonfaloniere, he went to Avignon as Florence's ambassador to Pope Clement VI. He died around 1355.

en:
Francesco Castracani degli Antelminelli was a Lucchese nobleman and cousin of the lord Castruccio Castracani. After Castruccio's death in 1328, his son Arrigo succeeded him, but in 1329 Emperor Louis the Bavarian deposed Arrigo and sold Lucca to Francesco.

A month later Marco Visconti's mercenaries seized the city and recalled Arrigo. In 1333 King John of Bohemia granted Francesco the vicariate of Coreglia and Ghivizzano.

He commanded a Pisan force at the battle of the Serchio in 1341. In 1355 Emperor Charles IV made Coreglia a county under his rule, and days later Castruccio's sons Arrigo and Vallerano murdered him on the road from Pisa to Lucca.

Francesco de' Medici was the youngest son of Giovenco de' Medici, one of the six Medici brothers who founded the family's Florentine bank, the compagnia filii Averardi. He married Francesca di Gregorio Dati, and their son Tommaso continued the line.

His descendants formed the patrician branch called the Medici di Lungarno, which died out in the male line in 1793 and in the female line in 1859, and from which the Florentine Lenzoni family descended through the female line.

en:
Poggio Bracciolini (1380–1459), known as Poggio, was a humanist and manuscript hunter born near Arezzo. Recommended by Salutati and Bruni, he became a cardinal's secretary in 1403 and joined the Roman Curia a few months later, eventually serving seven popes.

Searching German, Swiss and French monastic libraries, he recovered forgotten classics—Lucretius' De rerum natura, Quintilian's Institutio Oratoria and lost speeches of Cicero; his elegant book hand shaped the new humanist script.

After five years in England (1418–1423), he returned to Florence in 1453 as chancellor, succeeding Carlo Marsuppini. He died in Florence in 1459, leaving the satirical Facetiae and an unfinished history of Florence.

波焦·布拉乔利尼（1380—1459）常被单称为波焦，是生于阿雷佐附近的人文主义者和抄本搜寻者。经萨卢塔蒂与布鲁尼推荐，他于1403年担任一位枢机的秘书，数月后进入罗马教廷，先后侍奉七位教皇。

他在德意志、瑞士和法兰西的修道院图书馆中搜寻，找回了卢克莱修的《物性论》、昆体良的《雄辩术原理》以及西塞罗散佚演说等被遗忘的古典著作；他优雅的抄写书体也促成了新的人文主义字体。

他在英格兰度过五年（1418—1423），1453年回到佛罗伦萨，接替卡洛·马苏皮尼出任秘书长。1459年他在佛罗伦萨去世，留下讽刺故事集《诙谐集》和一部未完成的佛罗伦萨史。

en:
Joanna of Gallura (1291–1339) held the title of judge of a Sardinian realm she never ruled. The only child of Nino Visconti, last ruling judge of Gallura, and Beatrice d'Este, she inherited his titles in 1296, but Pisa occupied and administered Gallura directly.

What she did own was Visconti family property, including the fortresses around Civita. She moved to Milan in 1300, when her mother married its lord Galeazzo I Visconti, and in 1309 she married Rizzardo II da Camino, lord of Treviso, being widowed in 1312.

From 1323 she lived in Florence on a pension from the Guelphs. She sold her rights to Gallura to her half-brother Azzone Visconti, lord of Milan, and Dante names Joanna and her mother in Purgatorio VIII, the canto that honours her father.

焦万娜·维斯孔蒂（1291—1339）顶着撒丁岛一个法官辖地的头衔，却从未统治过它。她是加卢拉末代实际统治者尼诺·维斯孔蒂与贝阿特丽切·德斯特的独女，1296年继承了父亲的头衔，但加卢拉被比萨直接占领管理。

她真正拥有的是维斯孔蒂家族的产业，包括奇维塔周围的堡垒。1300年母亲改嫁米兰领主加莱亚佐一世·维斯孔蒂，她随母迁往米兰；1309年她嫁给特雷维索领主里扎尔多二世·达·卡米诺，1312年守寡。

1323年起她靠圭尔夫派发给的年金住在佛罗伦萨。她把对加卢拉的权利卖给同母异父的兄弟、米兰领主阿佐内·维斯孔蒂。但丁在《神曲·炼狱篇》第八章写到了她和母亲，这一章也称颂了她的父亲。

Giovanni Villani (c. 1276–1348) was a Florentine banker, official and chronicler. A shareholder of the Peruzzi bank from 1300, he visited Rome for the jubilee that year and began his year-by-year Nuova Cronica, a history of Florence rich in economic and statistical detail.

He served as prior and, from 1316, as master of the mint, and was present at the defeat by Castruccio Castracani at Altopascio in 1325. After the Buonaccorsi company he co-directed collapsed, he was imprisoned. He died of the Black Death in 1348; his brother Matteo and nephew continued the work.

乔瓦尼·维拉尼（约1276—1348）是佛罗伦萨的银行家、官员与编年史家。他自1300年起成为佩鲁齐银行的股东，同年前往罗马参加禧年庆典，受感召开始逐年撰写记载佛罗伦萨历史的《新编年史》，其中包含大量经济与统计细节。

他曾任佛罗伦萨执政官，1316年起主管铸币厂，并在1325年亲历了佛罗伦萨在阿尔托帕肖被卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼击败的战役。在他参与执掌的博纳科尔西公司破产后，他一度入狱。1348年他死于黑死病，《新编年史》由其弟马泰奥与侄子续成。

Guglielmo da Fogliano, called Guglielmino (c. 1279–1341), was a condottiero of the Reggio da Fogliano house, a son of Niccolò da Fogliano and Caterina della Scala. Early in the fourteenth century he and his brothers were invested with the fief of Carpineti.

He later served the Scaliger lords of Verona: on 2 October 1341, as captain of Mastino II della Scala's troops, he led the Scaliger vanguard at the battle of San Pietro a Vico near Lucca against the Pisans, and he died later that year.

en:
Jacopo Acciaiuoli (died 1356) was a Florentine politician of the banking house of Acciaiuoli, a son of Donato the Elder and Taggia Biliotti. He held a string of the republic's offices, and in 1341 was one of the Assunti di Lucca and gonfaloniere of Florence.

With his wife Bartolomea Ricasoli he had eight children, and his sons carried the family far beyond Tuscany. The second son, Neri I, drove the Catalans from Athens and ruled it until his death in 1394, invested as duke by King Ladislaus of Naples, while another son, Angelo, became bishop of Florence and later a cardinal.

雅各布·阿恰约利（卒于1356年）是佛罗伦萨银行家族阿恰约利家的政治家，老者多纳托·阿恰约利与塔贾·比利奥蒂之子。他历任共和国多项职务，1341年担任卢卡事务专员并出任佛罗伦萨旗官。

他与妻子巴托洛梅亚·里卡索利共有八名子女，儿子们把家族带到了托斯卡纳之外。次子内里一世把加泰罗尼亚人逐出雅典，统治该地直至1394年去世，并获那不勒斯国王拉迪斯劳册封为公爵；另一子安杰洛后来任佛罗伦萨主教，并成为枢机。

en:
Leonardo Bruni (c. 1370–1444), called Aretino from his native Arezzo, was a Florentine humanist historian and statesman. A pupil of Salutati and Manuel Chrysoloras, he was papal secretary to four popes in 1405–1414 and twice Chancellor of Florence, succeeding Salutati. His years as chancellor were marked by war, and his power was limited beside that of the Albizzi and Medici families.

His twelve-book History of the Florentine People pioneered humanist historiography, and his division of the past into ancient, medieval and modern periods earned him the title of first modern historian. He also wrote lives of Dante and Petrarch, translated Aristotle, and died in Florence in 1444, buried in Santa Croce.

列奥纳多·布鲁尼（约1370—1444）因出生地阿雷佐又被称为“阿雷蒂诺”，是佛罗伦萨人文主义历史学家和政治家。他师从萨卢塔蒂与曼努埃尔·赫里索洛拉斯，1405—1414年间担任教皇秘书，先后侍奉四位教皇；又两度出任佛罗伦萨秘书长，接替萨卢塔蒂的职位。他任秘书长期间战争不断，与阿尔比齐和美第奇家族相比，他的权力有限。

他所著十二卷《佛罗伦萨人民史》开创了人文主义史学，还最早把历史分为古代、中世纪和近代三个时期，因而被称为“第一位近代历史学家”。他还写过但丁和彼特拉克的传记、翻译亚里士多德著作，1444年在佛罗伦萨去世，葬于圣十字教堂。

en:
Niccolò Machiavelli (1469–1527) was a Florentine diplomat, historian and political writer whose name became shorthand for unscrupulous statecraft. In 1498 he became secretary of Florence's council for diplomacy and war, sent on missions to Louis XII's court, Rome and Italian lords. He observed Cesare Borgia closely, and was at Sinigaglia in December 1502 when Borgia killed his rebellious captains.

Distrusting mercenaries, he raised a Florentine citizen militia, which took Pisa in 1509. In 1512 Spanish troops backed by the Medici and Pope Julius II beat the Florentines at Prato; the Republic fell and he lost his post. Suspected of conspiracy in 1513, he was tortured but denied everything, then freed under Pope Leo X's amnesty.

On his farm near San Casciano he wrote The Prince around 1513, followed by the Discourses on Livy and The Mandrake. He died in Florence in 1527; The Prince was not printed until 1532.

尼科洛·马基雅维利（1469—1527）是佛罗伦萨外交官、历史学家和政治著作家，他的名字后来成了不择手段的权术的代名词。1498年他出任佛罗伦萨分管外交与战争的委员会秘书，先后出使路易十二的宫廷、罗马和意大利各地领主。他近距离观察切萨雷·博尔贾，1502年12月在塞尼加利亚目睹博尔贾杀害叛变的部将。

由于不信任雇佣兵，他组建佛罗伦萨公民民兵，1509年攻下比萨。1512年，在美第奇家族和教皇尤利乌斯二世支持下，西班牙军队在普拉托击败佛罗伦萨人，共和国垮台，马基雅维利丢官。1513年他被怀疑参与阴谋，遭拷打却始终否认，最后凭教皇利奥十世的大赦获释。

他退居圣卡夏诺附近的农庄，约1513年写成《君主论》，此后又写了《论李维》和《曼陀罗》。1527年他在佛罗伦萨去世，《君主论》直到1532年才付印。

en:
Manuel Chrysoloras (c. 1350–1415) was a Byzantine Greek scholar born in Constantinople, who reached Italy in 1390 on an embassy for Emperor Manuel II, seeking aid against the Ottomans.

Invited by Coluccio Salutati in 1396, he taught Greek in Florence from 1397 to 1400, numbering Leonardo Bruni, Niccolò Niccoli and Guarino da Verona among his pupils, and later taught in Bologna, Venice and Rome. He translated Homer and Plato into Latin, and his Erotemata was the first Greek grammar printed in the West.

In 1408 he went to Paris on an imperial mission, and in 1413 to Germany to help choose a site for a church council. He died at Constance in 1415, on his way to the council as a Greek Church representative.

曼努埃尔·赫里索洛拉斯（约1350—1415）是生于君士坦丁堡的拜占庭希腊学者。1390年他来到意大利，为皇帝曼努埃尔二世出使，寻求援助以抵御奥斯曼人。

应科卢乔·萨卢塔蒂于1396年发出的邀请，他于1397—1400年在佛罗伦萨教授希腊语，列奥纳多·布鲁尼、尼科洛·尼科利和瓜里诺·达·维罗纳都出自他门下；此后他又在博洛尼亚、威尼斯和罗马任教。他把荷马与柏拉图的著作译为拉丁文，所著《问答集》是西方第一部刊印的希腊语语法书。

1408年，他奉皇帝之命赴巴黎；1413年又赴德意志，协助为教会公会议选址。1415年，他以希腊教会代表身份前往公会议，途中在康斯坦茨去世。

en:
Niccolò Acciaiuoli, called il Vecchio, was a thirteenth-century Florentine judge, son of Guidalotto Acciaiuoli and brother of Tommaso. He served as priore di Libertà in 1289, 1294 and 1298, and in 1297 was officer in charge of tax assessments.

He and Baldo d'Agugliano were convicted over false testimony and sentenced to fines and banishment. By Pera Manzuoli he fathered Acciaiolo Acciaiuoli, whose son Niccolò became grand seneschal of Naples.

尼科洛·阿恰约利，人称老者，是13世纪佛罗伦萨法官，圭达洛托·阿恰约利之子、托马索的兄弟。他于1289、1294和1298年担任自由执政官，1297年主持税额评定。

en:
Niccolò Niccoli (1365–1437) was a Florentine humanist, bibliophile and copyist. He studied Greek with Manuel Chrysoloras from 1397 in Coluccio Salutati's circle.

Financed by Cosimo de' Medici and guided by Poggio Bracciolini, he built one of the age's greatest libraries, collating classical manuscripts and copying them in a refined Carolingian minuscule; his cursive hand became the model for italic type.

He published nothing himself, quarrelled with Bruni and Guarino, and openly scorned vernacular writers such as Dante. At his death in 1437 he left eight hundred manuscripts, which Cosimo gave to the library of San Marco.

尼科洛·尼科利（1365—1437）是佛罗伦萨人文主义者、藏书家和抄本师。他自1397年起在科卢乔·萨卢塔蒂的圈子里跟随曼努埃尔·赫里索洛拉斯学习希腊语。

在科西莫·德·美第奇资助和波焦·布拉乔利尼指导下，他建起当时最宏大的藏书之一：校勘古典抄本，用典雅的加洛林小写体抄写；他的草体后来成为意大利斜体字的范本。

他本人没有著作行世，与布鲁尼、瓜里诺争吵不和，还公开鄙薄但丁等俗语作家。1437年他去世时留下八百部抄本，由科西莫赠给圣马可修道院图书馆。

en:
Piero degli Albizzi (died 1379) was a leading Guelph politician in fourteenth-century Florence. He was prior in 1349–1350, and in 1358 the commissioner charged with defending Florentine land against the raids of the mercenary Count Lando.

In 1370, at the height of his career, he persuaded the councils to move against the Visconti. His feud with the Ricci, led by Uguccione, ended in 1372 with both men barred from office and exiled; Piero took refuge at Queen Joanna I's Naples court and returned in 1377 to the Guelph leadership.

In July 1378 the Ciompi revolt burned the Albizzi houses, and he fled to Venice. Arrested in Florence on 20 December 1379 on a charge of plotting against the popular regime, he was beheaded in the Palazzo della Signoria three days later.

皮耶罗·德利·阿尔比齐（?—1379）是14世纪佛罗伦萨圭尔夫派的领袖人物。1349—1350年他任执政官，1358年受任专员，保卫佛罗伦萨领土免遭佣兵首领兰多伯爵的袭扰。

1370年，仕途正处顶点的他说服各议会对维斯孔蒂家族采取行动。他与乌古乔内领导的里奇家族政争不断，1372年两人都被禁任公职并遭流放；皮耶罗投奔那不勒斯女王乔万娜一世的宫廷，1377年回到佛罗伦萨，重返圭尔夫派领导层。

1378年7月，梳毛工起义的民众烧毁了阿尔比齐家族的宅邸，他逃往威尼斯。1379年12月20日，他在佛罗伦萨以密谋反对平民政权的罪名被捕，三天后在领主宫被斩首。

Piero Soderini (1451–1522) was a Florentine statesman who served the republic after the fall of the Medici and Savonarola. Already ambassador to France in 1493, he was elected gonfaloniere of justice for life in 1502 to give the restored republic stable government.

Under his rule Florence replaced foreign mercenaries with a citizen militia and finally captured Pisa in 1509; Niccolò Machiavelli served as his second chancellor. Soderini also maintained an alliance with France.

In 1512 a Spanish army restored the Medici, deposed Soderini and drove him into exile in Dalmatia. Pope Leo X later summoned him to Rome, where he spent his remaining years and died in 1522, never having been allowed to return to Florence.

皮耶罗·索德里尼（1451—1522）是佛罗伦萨政治家，在美第奇家族倒台、萨伏那洛拉死后为共和国效力。他1493年已出任驻法兰西大使，1502年当选为终身正义旗手，以求为重建的共和国提供稳定统治。

他执政期间以公民民兵取代外国雇佣军，并于1509年攻占比萨；尼科洛·马基雅维利曾担任他的第二国务秘书。他还与法国保持同盟。

1512年，西班牙军队帮助美第奇家族复辟，索德里尼被废黜，流亡达尔马提亚。教皇利奥十世后来召他到罗马，他在那里度过余生，于1522年去世，始终未获准返回佛罗伦萨。

Salvestro de' Medici, called Chiarissimo (fl. first half of the fourteenth century), was a Florentine politician, the son of Averardo de' Medici. With his brothers he founded the family banking company, the Filii Averardi, documented until 1330, and in 1336 he served the republic as ambassador to Venice.

By his wife Lisa Donati he had three sons, including Averardo, known as Bicci (1320–1363). Through Averardo Bicci he was grandfather of Giovanni di Bicci and ancestor of the grand-ducal Medici line.

en:
Sandro Botticelli (c. 1445–1510) was a Florentine painter of the Early Renaissance, best known for Primavera and The Birth of Venus. The son of a tanner in the Ognissanti quarter, he took his nickname, 'little barrel', from his round-bodied brother Giovanni. Apprenticed to Fra Filippo Lippi from about 1461, he had his own workshop by 1469.

His Adoration of the Magi (c. 1475), with portraits of the Medici and of himself, spread his name. He worked on the Sistine Chapel in Rome in 1481–1482, and in the 1480s, his best decade, finished large mythological paintings for the Medici circle and many Madonnas.

By the 1490s his work returned to an archaic, Gothic manner. He never married and died in Florence on 17 May 1510, buried in Ognissanti at the foot of Simonetta Vespucci's tomb. His reputation stayed eclipsed until the Pre-Raphaelites rediscovered him in the late 19th century.

桑德罗·波提切利（约1445—1510）是文艺复兴早期的佛罗伦萨画家，以《春》和《维纳斯的诞生》闻名。他是制革匠之子，“波提切利”意为“小桶”，源自哥哥乔瓦尼的绰号。他约1461年师从菲利普·利皮修士，1469年已有自己的作坊。

约1475年的《三博士来朝》因画中美第奇家族和他本人的肖像使他成名。1481至1482年他赴罗马绘制西斯廷礼拜堂壁画；1480年代是他最成功的十年，他为美第奇圈子完成大型神话画和许多圣母像。

1490年代他的作品回归古旧的哥特式风格。他终身未婚，1510年5月17日去世，葬于诸圣教堂西莫内塔·韦斯普奇墓脚下。他的声名长期被埋没，19世纪末才由前拉斐尔派重新发现。

en:
Girolamo Savonarola (1452–1498) was an ascetic Dominican friar from Ferrara whose prophecies made him the dominant voice in Florence. He gave up medicine to enter the Dominican friary in Bologna in 1475. After Pico della Mirandola helped bring him back to San Marco in 1490, his sermons on Revelation drew such crowds that he moved to the cathedral.

When Charles VIII crossed the Alps in 1494, many saw his prophecy fulfilled; the Florentines drove out Piero de' Medici and set up a Great Council; he preached that Florence would be the New Jerusalem. On 7 February 1497 a bonfire of the vanities burned paintings, jewels and clothes.

He ignored Pope Alexander VI's summons and was excommunicated on 12 May 1497. A rain-cancelled trial by fire in April 1498 turned the crowd against him; arrested and tortured, he was hanged with two friars on 23 May 1498, their bodies burned.

He ignored Pope Alexander VI's summons and was excommunicated on 12 May 1497. A rain-cancelled trial by fire in April 1498 turned the crowd against him; arrested and tortured, he was hanged with two friars on 23 May 1498, their bodies burned.

吉罗拉莫·萨伏那洛拉（1452—1498）是来自费拉拉的苦行多明我会修士，凭预言成为佛罗伦萨最有影响力的声音。他放弃学医，1475年进入博洛尼亚的多明我会修道院。1490年皮科·德拉·米兰多拉帮助他回到圣马可修道院后，他讲解《启示录》的布道吸引了大批听众，以致移到大教堂举行。

1494年查理八世越过阿尔卑斯山，许多人视为预言应验。佛罗伦萨人赶走皮耶罗·德·美第奇，设立大议会；他宣讲佛罗伦萨将成为新耶路撒冷。1497年2月7日的“虚荣之火”烧掉了画作、珠宝和华美衣物。

他无视教皇亚历山大六世的召令，1497年5月12日被处绝罚。1498年4月一场因雨取消的火焰神判使群众倒戈；他被捕受刑，5月23日与两名修士同被绞死，遗体遭焚。

Tommaso Acciaiuoli, often called Mannino, was a Florentine politician of the later thirteenth century, son of Guidalotto Acciaiuoli and brother of Niccolò il Vecchio. He served the commune in a string of senior offices, as priore di Libertà and gonfaloniere, and in 1290 fought in the war against the Ghibellines of Arezzo.

en:
Fyodor Krasny, called the Red, was born around 1300 as the eldest son of Prince Konstantin Yuryevich of Fomin, and ruled the Rurikid appanages of Fomin and Berezuysk jointly with his brothers. The chronicles name him as a commander in Ivan Kalita's 1340 campaign against Smolensk.

In late 1345 he married Yevpraksia, widow of the Muscovite grand prince Simeon the Proud. Genealogies credit him with four sons, ancestors of several Muscovite serving clans. He died in old age in Moscow on 5 March 1387, taking the monastic name Simeon.

en:
Eleanor of Comminges (born before 1300, died c. 1369) was the mother of Gaston III of Foix, later famous as Fébus. A daughter of Bernard VII, Count of Comminges, she seemed destined to stay unmarried or enter a convent until her uncle arranged her marriage in 1324 to Gaston II, Count of Foix, then fourteen; she was about twice his age. After several children died young, she bore Gaston III in 1331.

Gaston II died in 1343 at the siege of Algeciras, and Eleanor became tutor and regent of Foix-Béarn, lands owing homage to both the French and English kings.

She led her twelve-year-old son on a tour of 126 places to introduce him to his subjects. He came of age in 1345, but she kept managing his property until he turned twenty-one, and died near Le Mas-d'Azil.

科曼日的埃莉诺（1300年前生，约1369年卒）是富瓦伯爵加斯东三世，即后来的腓比斯的母亲。她是科曼日伯爵贝尔纳七世之女，似乎原本注定终身不嫁或进入修道院，直到叔父出面，于1324年安排她嫁给富瓦伯爵加斯东二世。丈夫当时年仅14岁，她的年龄约为他的两倍。几个孩子夭折后，她于1331年生下加斯东三世。

1343年，加斯东二世在阿尔赫西拉斯围城战中身亡，埃莉诺随即成为儿子的监护人，并摄政治理富瓦—贝阿恩；这片领地同时向法王和英王效忠。

她带着十二岁的儿子巡行126个地方，让他认识自己的臣民。1345年儿子成年，但她仍继续代管其产业至他21岁，约1369年在勒马斯达济勒附近去世。

en:
Bernard Roger (born before 981, died around 1034), a younger son of Count Roger I the Old of Carcassonne, received Couserans and the lands around Foix when his father divided his counties. From about 1012 he ruled as the first Count of Foix, and married Garsenda, heiress of Bigorre, through whom he held Bigorre from 1032.

He built the square keep of Foix castle and made the site his chief seat, around which the town of Foix grew. His sons divided the lands: Bernard took Bigorre, Peter Couserans, Roger Foix. His daughter Ermesinda married Ramiro I of Aragon.

贝尔纳·罗歇（981年前生，约1034年卒）是卡尔卡松伯爵罗歇一世（“老者”）较年幼的儿子之一。父亲分割诸伯国时，他分得库瑟朗和富瓦城一带的土地，约自1012年起成为第一代富瓦伯爵。他娶比戈尔女继承人加尔森德为妻，于1032年凭借她领有比戈尔。

他修建了富瓦城堡的方形主塔，将该地作为统治中心，富瓦城镇由此发展起来。诸子分地：贝尔纳取得比戈尔，皮埃尔取得库瑟朗，罗歇取得富瓦。女儿埃尔梅辛达嫁给了阿拉贡国王拉米罗一世。

en:
Gaston I (1287–1315) succeeded his father Roger-Bernard III in 1302 as Count of Foix and Viscount of Béarn, ruling first under his mother Margaret's regency. In 1301 he had married Joan of Artois. He fought for France at Mons-en-Pévèle in 1304, but backed his towns against royal tax collectors, for which the crown briefly seized Foix.

In 1308 he warred on the Count of Armagnac against royal orders, was captured and jailed in Paris's Châtelet, and freed only for a ransom of thirty-six thousand livres. He later claimed Urgell without success. Returning from the Flemish wars, he died at Maubuisson Abbey near Pontoise.

加斯东一世（1287—1315）于1302年继其父罗歇-贝尔纳三世为富瓦伯爵兼贝阿恩子爵，起初由母亲玛格丽特摄政。1301年他娶阿图瓦的让娜为妻。1304年他随法军战于蒙桑佩韦勒，但因支持本邦城镇对抗王室税吏，富瓦一度被王室没收。

1308年他违令攻打阿马尼亚克伯爵，兵败被俘，囚于巴黎夏特莱，后以3.6万锂赎金获释。他后来曾主张乌赫尔伯国的继承权而未果。从佛兰德战场返回途中，他殁于蓬图瓦兹附近的莫比松修道院。

en:
Gaston II (1308–1343) inherited Foix and Béarn in 1315 aged seven. His mother Joan of Artois ruled as regent until her rule angered the local nobility, who had the Parlement of Paris strip her of her offices in 1317; Gaston later imprisoned her. His lands lay between two crowns: Foix was held of France, Béarn of England.

Coming of age around 1325, he renewed the war with the Counts of Armagnac, who contested Béarn, until peace was made in 1329. In the Hundred Years' War he still took France's side against the pro-English Gascon lords.

He also fought in Spain and was at the siege of Algeciras; he died at Seville on 26 September 1343. He had married his cousin Eleanor of Comminges, who brought rights to Bigorre, and their son Gaston III Fébus inherited Foix.

加斯东二世（1308—1343）于1315年以七岁冲龄继承富瓦与贝阿恩。母亲阿图瓦的让娜起初摄政，却惹恼当地贵族，1317年巴黎高等法院应贵族之请解除了她的职权；后来加斯东还将她囚禁。他的领地夹在两个王权之间：富瓦臣属法国，贝阿恩臣属英格兰。

约1325年成年后，他与争夺贝阿恩的阿马尼亚克伯爵们重启战端，1329年双方议和。百年战争中，他仍站在法国一边，攻打亲英的加斯科涅诸侯。

他还在西班牙作战，并参加阿尔赫西拉斯围城战，1343年9月26日殁于塞维利亚。他娶表亲科曼日的埃莉诺为妻，她带来比戈尔的权利；独子加斯东三世·费比斯继承了富瓦。

en:
Gaston Phoebus (30 April 1331 – 1 August 1391) was count of Foix and viscount of Béarn. He succeeded his father Gaston II in 1343 and began his personal rule in 1345. He claimed sovereignty over Béarn in 1347 and, playing England and France off against each other, made himself master of the Pyrenean foothills, crushing the House of Armagnac at Launac in 1362 though outnumbered.

His only legitimate son died in 1380 after a poison plot against him. He dictated the hunting treatise Livre de chasse and died in 1391.

en:
Joan of Artois (1289–after 1350), countess of Foix and viscountess of Béarn, was the sister of Robert III. She lost her father Philip of Artois in 1298. Her marriage to Gaston, eldest son of Count Roger Bernard III of Foix, was agreed with Philip IV in 1299 and contracted at Senlis in 1301, and when Gaston succeeded in 1302 she became countess.

Her influence over her husband brought repeated clashes with the Foix nobility, who in 1317 petitioned the Parlement to remove her from the care of her children, accusing her of extravagance and dissolute living.

In 1331 Philip VI let her son Gaston II imprison her, at Foix and then Orthez. She was freed in 1347 at the request of her son Robert, bishop of Lavaur, and retired to Carbonne.

zh:
阿图瓦的让娜（1289—1350年后），富瓦伯爵夫人、贝阿恩子爵夫人，是罗贝尔三世的妹妹。1298年，她的父亲阿图瓦的菲利普去世。1299年，国王腓力四世记录了她与富瓦伯爵罗歇·贝尔纳三世的长子加斯东的婚事协议，1301年婚约在桑利斯签订；1302年加斯东继位，她成为伯爵夫人。

她对丈夫的影响引发与富瓦贵族的屡次冲突，贵族们于1317年向高等法院请愿，要求夺去她对子女的监护，指控她挥霍无度、生活放荡。

1331年，腓力六世准许她的儿子加斯东二世将她囚禁，先在富瓦，后转至奥尔泰兹。1347年，应儿子、拉沃尔主教罗贝尔的请求，她获释，退居卡尔邦讷。

en:
Peter Bernard, in French Pierre Bernard (died 1074), was the third son of Count Bernard-Roger and Garsende of Bigorre. After his father's death the lands were divided: Bernard took Bigorre, Roger Foix, and Peter Bernard Couserans, which he ruled as count.

When Roger I died childless in 1064, charters show Peter Bernard ruling Foix as well. His claim to Carcassonne came to nothing, and at his death the counties passed to his son Roger II.

皮埃尔·贝尔纳（卒于1074年）是贝尔纳·罗歇伯爵与比戈尔的加尔森德的第三子。父亲去世后诸子分地：贝尔纳得比戈尔，罗歇得富瓦，皮埃尔·贝尔纳得库瑟朗，并任该地伯爵。

1064年罗歇一世无嗣而终，特许状显示皮埃尔·贝尔纳同时统治富瓦。他对卡尔卡松的权利主张落空，死后诸伯国由其子罗歇二世继承。

en:
Raymond Roger (1152 – 3 April 1223) was Count of Foix from 1188, the son of Roger Bernard I and Cécile Trencavel. He went on crusade with Philip Augustus in 1191, fighting at Acre. In 1196 he raided Upper Urgell and Cerdagne with Arnaud of Castelbon in pursuit of Andorra; both were imprisoned for several months in 1203.

Though a Catholic, he was close to Catharism through his wife Philippa, and attended the Catholic-Cathar debate at Pamiers in 1207. During the Albigensian Crusade he fought for Toulouse against Simon de Montfort, winning at Montgey in 1211. He submitted in 1214, but later joined the siege of Toulouse in 1217–1218. He died while besieging Mirepoix.

富瓦的雷蒙·罗歇（1152—1223年4月3日）自1188年起任富瓦伯爵，是罗歇·贝尔纳一世与塞西尔·特伦卡韦勒之子。1191年他随腓力·奥古斯特参加十字军，在阿卡作战。1196年，他与卡斯特尔邦的阿尔诺为夺取安道尔而劫掠上乌赫尔和塞尔达尼亚；两人于1203年被囚禁数月。

en:
Roger Bernard I, called the Fat (c. 1130 – November 1188), was Count of Foix from 1148, the son of Roger III and Jimena of Barcelona, granddaughter of the Cid. Breaking with his family's long attachment to Toulouse, he joined a coalition against Count Raymond V in 1151; after its defeat in 1153 he drew back from such leagues.

He worked to settle disputes between his county and the Church, returning property to the church of Saint-Antonin at Pamiers and donating to Boulbonne Abbey.

In 1185 he warred on Toulouse again with Aragon and England, after which Alfonso II of Aragon made him governor of Provence. He was buried at Boulbonne.

富瓦的罗歇·贝尔纳一世，绰号“胖子”（约1130—1188年11月），自1148年起任富瓦伯爵，是罗歇三世与熙德的孙女希梅娜·德·巴塞罗那之子。他一改家族长期亲图卢兹的立场，于1151年加入反对雷蒙五世伯爵的联盟；1153年联盟战败后，他便不再参与这类结盟。

他致力于化解伯国与教会的争端，向帕米耶的圣安托南教堂归还财产，并向布尔博讷修道院捐赠。

en:
Roger Bernard II, called the Great (1195 – 26 May 1241), Count of Foix from 1223, was the son of Raymond Roger and Philippa. His 1203 marriage to Ermessinde of Castelbon, lady of Andorra, brought his son Roger IV Castelbon and Andorra. In 1217 he held Montgailhard castle for six weeks against Simon de Montfort and fought at the siege of Toulouse.

As count he helped Raymond VII of Toulouse take Carcassonne in 1224. Louis VIII rejected his embassy seeking peace in 1226, and he resisted the king's invasion of Languedoc in 1226–1227. Excommunicated, he made peace after the 1229 Treaty of Meaux, renouncing Mirepoix.

en:
Roger-Bernard III (1243–1302) became Count of Foix in 1265, succeeding his father Roger IV. Philip III of France took Foix in 1272 after wars among vassals and imprisoned him at Carcassonne. In 1278 his treaty with the bishop of Urgell set up joint rule of Andorra. Captured by Peter III of Aragon at Balaguer in 1280, he was held until 1284.

In 1290 he seized Béarn through his wife Margaret of Montcada. Her nephew Bernard VI of Armagnac contested the inheritance, beginning a long struggle between the houses. He led French troops against the English at Saint-Sever and Bonnegarde, died at Tarascon, and was a troubadour.

en:
Roger I of Foix (died 1064), a younger son of Count Bernard-Roger, succeeded his father around 1034 as the first ruler to call himself count of Foix, while Couserans went to his brother Peter Bernard.

In 1034 he made a mutual inheritance pact with his uncle Peter Roger, bishop of Girona, who held Carcassonne; when the bishop died in 1050 Roger added Carcassonne to his lands. He left no children, so Foix passed to his brother Peter Bernard.

en:
Roger II (died 1124) was Count of Foix from 1064, the son of Peter Bernard of Foix. He claimed Carcassonne after its comital line ended but failed to take the city by force, and a treaty of 1095 confirmed its cession to the Trencavels against a large payment. The money helped finance his participation in the First Crusade.

He joined Raymond of Saint-Gilles' host, but delayed his departure so long that the pope excommunicated him. He reached the Holy Land after the fall of Jerusalem and returned in 1105. He then built a castle near Foix and founded the town of Pamiers, which he named after Apamea in Syria.

en:
Roger III (died 1148) was Count of Foix from 1124, the son of Roger II. In 1117 he married Jimena of Barcelona, granddaughter of the Cid. He backed Bernard Aton IV Trencavel's claims to the viscounty of Carcassonne against Raymond Berengar III of Barcelona, and took Bernard Aton's children under his protection after his death in 1129.

In 1134 he helped his suzerain Alphonse Jourdain of Toulouse broker peace between the kings of Castile and Aragon. In the Baussenque wars over Provence, he remained loyal to Toulouse, unlike many other lords.

en:
Roger IV (died 24 February 1265) succeeded his mother Ermessinde as Viscount of Castelbon in 1237, and his father Roger Bernard II as Count of Foix in 1241. After the failed 1242 revolt of Pyrenean lords against Alphonse of Poitiers, he submitted, but the Count of Toulouse seized Saverdun from him.

Roger sought royal aid in 1243, became a direct crown vassal and recovered Saverdun. In 1245 he issued measures abolishing serfdom in Foix. Unlike his father he was a loyal Catholic who favoured the Inquisition, which nevertheless suspected him.

He founded Mazères in 1251 and several other bastides. His dispute over Andorra with the bishop of Urgell was settled by his son in 1278.

en:
Aimery VII of Thouars (c. 1152–1226), eighteenth viscount of Thouars from 1173, was the eldest son of Geoffroy IV. He served as seneschal of Anjou and then of Poitou, and stood close to Eleanor of Aquitaine and her son Richard the Lionheart.

After the Poitevin barons rose against John of England and Arthur of Brittany was killed in 1203, Philip Augustus made his seneschalcy hereditary in his favor. His son by Sibylle, Guy I, became viscount in 1234; Aimery died in 1226.

en:
Alfonso of Brienne, called Alphonse d'Acre (c. 1227–1270), was the eldest son of John of Brienne, king of Jerusalem and Latin emperor of Constantinople, and Berengaria of León, born at Acre. He spent his career at the court of Louis IX. By marrying Marie of Exoudun, heiress of Eu, he became count of Eu and served as Grand Chamberlain of France.

In 1258 he represented Louis in negotiations with Henry III of England's envoys for the Treaty of Paris. Widowed in 1260, he governed Eu for his young son.

In 1265 he aided Alfonso X of Castile against the Moors. He joined the Eighth Crusade and died of dysentery at Tunis on 25 August 1270, the same day as Louis IX.

en:
Blanche of Castile (1188–1252) was a daughter of Alfonso VIII of Castile and Eleanor of England, and in 1200 married the future Louis VIII of France. Her English ancestry helped bring Louis an offer of the English crown, and she backed his invasion of England in 1216, organizing reinforcements from Calais.

Left a widow in 1226, she ruled as regent for the young Louis IX, putting down the revolts of the great nobles and forcing the Treaty of Paris on Raymond VII of Toulouse in 1229, which ended the Albigensian Crusade. She held a second regency from 1248 while Louis crusaded, dying at Melun in 1252.

en:
Blanche of France (1 April 1328 – 8 February 1393) was the posthumous daughter of Charles IV and Joan of Évreux, born two months after her father's death; as the last direct Capetian, her birth allowed Philip VI of Valois to claim the throne. In 1345 she married Philip, Duke of Orléans; the match was childless.

While Philip was held captive in England after Poitiers in 1356, Blanche administered his lands. She died at Vincennes in 1393 and was buried at Saint-Denis.

en:
Carloman II (c. 866–884), second son of Louis the Stammerer, succeeded to West Francia in 879 and ruled with his brother Louis. In 880 they divided their father's realm, Carloman taking Aquitaine, and in August 881 routed Viking raiders at Saucourt-en-Vimeu.

After Louis's death in 882 Carloman ruled alone, facing Viking raids. In December 884, while hunting, he was stabbed in the leg by his servant during a boar attack and died days later. His cousin Charles the Fat inherited his kingdom.

en:
Catherine of Courtenay (1274–1307) was the heiress of Philip of Courtenay, titular Latin emperor of Constantinople. On her father's death in 1283 she inherited his claim to the Latin Empire, lost to the Greeks in 1261, and was recognized as empress.

After several failed betrothals she married Charles of Valois in February 1301, who then held the imperial title in her right. She died in Paris in 1307, leaving her claim to her daughter Catherine of Valois-Courtenay.

en:
Charlemagne (747/748–814), eldest son of Pepin the Short, was King of the Franks and Lombards and the first emperor recognised in the West since Rome fell. He ruled from 768, alone after his brother Carloman died in 771, and took the Lombard crown in 774. His Saxon Wars of 772–804 subdued and converted the Saxons.

He subdued Bavaria and the Avars and received Pope Leo III after an attack in 799; on Christmas Day 800 the Pope crowned him emperor in Rome. Caliph Harun al-Rashid sent him an elephant, which reached Aachen in 802, where he ruled from 801.

His court saw the Carolingian Renaissance. In 806 he divided the realm among his sons, but by 811 only Louis survived. He died of pleurisy on 28 January 814 and was buried at Aachen; Louis's sons later split the empire at Verdun into West and East Francia.

他征服巴伐利亚和阿瓦尔人，在799年教宗利奥三世遇袭后接待了他；800年圣诞节，教宗在罗马为他加冕。哈里发哈伦·拉希德赠他一头大象，802年运抵亚琛，他自801年起在该城理政。

他的宫廷迎来加洛林文艺复兴。806年他把王国分给儿子们，但到811年只剩路易在世。814年1月28日他死于胸膜炎，葬于亚琛；路易的儿子们后来在凡尔登把帝国分为西法兰克与东法兰克。

en:
Charles of Artois (1328–1385), count of Pézenas, was the youngest son of Robert III of Artois and Joan of Valois. In 1334 his uncle Philip VI shut him and his brothers in Château-Gaillard; John II freed him on his accession in 1350 and made him a councillor. In 1356 he received Longueville, confiscated from Philip of Navarre, and helped take Évreux and Breteuil from Charles the Bad.

Captured at Poitiers, he spent four years in London. Longueville was taken back in 1360, and in 1362 Pézenas was raised to a county as compensation. Hoping to win Artois, he joined the Prince of Wales's companies in 1367; his exactions led Charles V to confiscate his property.

Reconciled in 1375, he stirred up trouble again, and the Duke of Anjou arrested him at Agde. He died in 1385.

en:
Charles the Bald (823–877) was the first king of the West Franks, whose realm later became France. The youngest son of Louis the Pious and a grandson of Charlemagne, his nickname may have been a joke at his lack of land. After Louis died in 840 he warred with Emperor Lothair I, and the Treaty of Verdun in 843 gave him the western kingdom.

His reign was a long fight on every border. The Vikings sacked Paris in 845 and he paid dearly for their retreat, while his Edict of Pistres in 864 ordered fortified river bridges.

After Emperor Louis II died in 875, Pope John VIII crowned Charles emperor in Rome on 25 December. Ill and abandoned by his nobles, he died crossing the Alps in October 877; his bearers could not endure the stench and buried him hastily. His son Louis the Stammerer succeeded him.

秃头查理（823—877）是西法兰克的第一位国王，他的国家后来演变为法国。他是虔诚者路易的幼子、查理曼之孙，他的绰号也许是对他没有领地的玩笑。840年路易去世后，他与皇帝洛泰尔一世交战，843年的《凡尔登条约》把西部王国划给了他。

875年皇帝路易二世去世后，教宗若望八世于12月25日在罗马为查理加冕称帝。他带病出征，被贵族抛弃，877年10月翻越阿尔卑斯山时去世；抬柩的人受不了恶臭，匆匆将他下葬。他的儿子口吃者路易继位。

en:
Charles III the Simple (879–929), posthumous son of Louis the Stammerer, was only five when nobles gave his crown to Charles the Fat in 884; after Odo of Paris died he was at last recognized as king in 898. In 911 he enfeoffed the Viking leader Rollo with lands around Rouen, the seed of Normandy, and annexed Lotharingia.

Revolting nobles proclaimed Robert I king in 922; although Robert was killed at Soissons in 923, Charles was defeated. He was captured by Herbert II of Vermandois and died imprisoned at Péronne in 929. His son by Eadgifu of Wessex became Louis IV.

en:
Charles IV, called the Fair (1294–1328), third son of Philip IV, ruled France and Navarre from 1322, the last king of the direct Capetian line. His first wife Blanche of Burgundy was disgraced in the Tour de Nesle affair of 1314 and their marriage was annulled. In 1324 his bid for the imperial crown failed.

That year his troops overran English-held Guyenne in the War of Saint-Sardos. Edward II then did homage and paid a fine to recover a reduced Guyenne. Charles died in 1328 leaving no son; France passed to his cousin Philip of Valois and Navarre to his niece Joan II. The succession dispute fed the Hundred Years' War.

“美男子”查理四世（1294—1328）是腓力四世第三子，1322年起统治法兰西与纳瓦拉，也是卡佩嫡系的末代国王。他的第一任妻子勃艮第的布朗奇卷入1314年的内斯勒塔事件，二人婚姻被废除。1324年他竞选神圣罗马帝位失败。

同年，他的军队在圣萨尔多战争中攻占英格兰人据有的吉耶讷公国。爱德华二世随后向他效忠并缴纳罚金，换回领土缩小的吉耶讷。1328年查理去世时没有留下男嗣，法兰西王位传给堂弟瓦卢瓦的腓力，纳瓦拉王位归侄女胡安娜二世。这场继承纠纷后来成为百年战争的导火索。

en:
Charles de la Cerda (1327–1354), known as Charles of Spain, was a Franco-Castilian nobleman, a distant cousin and boyhood favourite of John II of France. In 1350 he commanded the Castilian galleys at L'Espagnols-sur-Mer off Winchelsea, where Edward III of England defeated him. Once John was king, Charles succeeded the executed Raoul II of Eu as Constable of France and was made Count of Angoulême.

Charles the Bad, king of Navarre, also claimed Angoulême and bitterly resented the favourite's rise. In 1351 Charles married Marguerite, daughter of the Duke of Brittany.

After a quarrel with Philippe, the Navarrese king's brother, he was killed in an inn at L'Aigle in Normandy on 8 January 1354 by a henchman of the king of Navarre. The murder left France unsettled until Charles V came to the throne in 1364.

zh:
夏尔·德·拉·塞尔达（1327—1354），人称“西班牙的夏尔”，是法兰西—卡斯蒂利亚血统的贵族，法王约翰二世的远亲，也是他自幼的宠臣。1350年，他率卡斯蒂利亚桨帆船队在温切尔西外海的“西班牙人海战”中被英王爱德华三世击败。约翰即位后，他接替被处决的欧伯爵拉乌尔二世出任法兰西王室统帅，并受封昂古莱姆伯爵。

纳瓦拉国王“恶人”查理也主张拥有昂古莱姆，对这位宠臣的得势极为怨恨。1351年，夏尔迎娶布列塔尼公爵之女玛格丽特。

1354年1月8日，他同纳瓦拉国王之弟菲利普争吵后，在诺曼底莱格勒的一家客栈被纳瓦拉国王的亲信杀死。此案使法国局势动荡，直到1364年查理五世即位才告平息。

en:
Charles of Valois (1270–1325), fourth son of Philip III and Isabella of Aragon, founded the House of Valois. The 1285 Aragonese Crusade gave him a short-lived paper crown as king of Aragon. He became count of Anjou and Maine by his 1290 marriage to Margaret of Anjou.

He led a papal army into Italy in 1301–1302 and claimed the Latin Empire through Catherine of Courtenay. His Sicilian campaign ended in the Peace of Caltabellotta in 1302. In 1324 he overran Guyenne against Edward II. He died in 1325, three years before his son Philip VI took the French throne.

瓦卢瓦的查理（1270—1325）是腓力三世与阿拉贡的伊莎贝拉的第四子，瓦卢瓦王朝的开创者。1285年阿拉贡十字军曾给他一顶有名无实的阿拉贡王冠，不久便放弃。1290年他与安茹的玛格丽特结婚，成为安茹和曼恩伯爵。

Eleanor of Savoy (c. 1280–1324) was a daughter of Count Amadeus V of Savoy. In 1292 she married William of Chalon, Count of Auxerre and Tonnerre, who was killed fighting for Philip IV at Mons-en-Pévèle in 1304.

In 1305 she married Dreux IV de Mello, lord of Sainte-Hermine, and after his death in 1317 took a third husband, John I, Count of Forez. Her children by William included John II and Joan.

en:
Isabella of Aragon (c. 1247–1271) was the youngest daughter of King James I of Aragon. Betrothed to Philip, second son of Louis IX, under the Treaty of Corbeil of 1258, she married him in 1262.

She joined the Eighth Crusade in 1270 and became queen of France when Louis IX died in August. On the journey home she fell from her horse while six months pregnant, gave birth prematurely, and died at Cosenza on 28 January 1271. Her sons included Philip IV and Charles of Valois.

en:
Élisabeth de Courtenay (1140–1205) was the daughter of Renaud de Courtenay. In 1150 she married Pierre de France, a son of King Louis VI, who through the wedding acquired the lordship of Courtenay; their descendants founded the Capetian House of Courtenay.

Her son Pierre II was crowned Latin emperor of Constantinople in 1217, and her daughter Alix was the mother of Isabelle of Angoulême, queen of England. Élisabeth died in 1205.

en:
Enguerrand V de Coucy (1243–after 1321), second son of Arnould III, Count of Guînes, sought fortune abroad after his father sold Guînes to France. In Scotland he married Christiana Lindsay, John Balliol's niece, their wedding arranged by their cousin Alexander III. He served Edward I of England from 1283 and sat in parliament as Lord Ghisnes.

When his uncle Enguerrand IV died heirless in 1311, he inherited the barony of Coucy. He died after 1321 and was buried at Prémontré Abbey.

昂盖朗五世·德·库西（1243—1321年后）是吉讷伯爵阿尔努三世的次子。父亲把吉讷伯国卖给法国王室后，他赴海外自谋前程，在苏格兰娶了约翰·巴里奥的外甥女克里斯蒂娜·德·林赛，婚事由表兄亚历山大三世安排。1283年起他效力于英格兰国王爱德华一世，并以“吉讷勋爵”身份出席议会。

1311年舅父昂盖朗四世无嗣而终，他继承了库西男爵领。他在1321年后去世，葬于普雷蒙特雷修道院。

en:
Enguerrand VI de Coucy (1313–1346) succeeded his father in 1335 as lord of Coucy and spent his short rule in Philip VI's war against Edward III of England. In 1338 he married Catherine of Austria, daughter of Duke Leopold I, a match arranged to draw the Habsburgs to the French side.

In 1339 his men held the castle of Oisy against Edward III's ally Jean de Beaumont, and in January 1346 he fought in the Duke of Normandy's Gascon campaign.

That August he was killed in a skirmish just before Crécy. His young son Enguerrand VII succeeded him and in 1360, after Poitiers, was a hostage for King John II's freedom.

zh:
昂盖朗六世·德·库西（1313—1346）于1335年继承父亲之位成为库西领主，短暂的一生都在腓力六世对英王爱德华三世的战争中度过。1338年，他娶奥地利公爵利奥波德一世之女凯瑟琳为妻，这门亲事意在拉拢哈布斯堡家族站到法兰西一边。

1339年，他的部下守住瓦西城堡，抵御爱德华三世的盟友让·德·博蒙；1346年1月，他又参加诺曼底公爵的加斯科涅远征。

同年8月，他在克雷西战役前夕的交战中阵亡。幼子昂盖朗七世继领其地，1360年普瓦捷战役之后作为人质换取国王约翰二世的自由。

en:
Eschivat IV of Chabanais (died 1283), son of Alix de Montfort, countess of Bigorre, inherited Bigorre from his mother in 1255. A quarrel with his aunt Martha, wife of Gaston VII of Béarn, brought Gaston's invasion; in 1256 Eschivat married Inès, daughter of Roger IV of Foix.

In 1258 he entrusted Bigorre to Simon de Montfort, who kept it and soon rebelled, after which Eschivat and Gaston reconquered the county. After his death, his aunt and his sister Laura disputed Bigorre.

沙巴内的埃希瓦特四世（卒于1283年）是比戈尔女伯爵阿丽克斯·德·蒙福尔之子，1255年继承母亲的比戈尔伯国。他与姨妈——贝阿恩子爵加斯东七世之妻玛特——发生争执，招致加斯东入侵；1256年他娶富瓦的罗歇四世之女伊内丝为妻。

1258年他把比戈尔托付给西蒙·德·蒙福尔，西蒙却据为己有并很快起兵反叛，埃希瓦特遂与加斯东联手收复伯国。他死后，姨妈与姊妹洛尔又为比戈尔争执不休。

en:
François-Marie Arouet, known as Voltaire (1694–1778), was the leading French writer of the Enlightenment. After eleven months in the Bastille for a satire on the Regent, he took the name Voltaire in 1718, when his Œdipe made his name. After a 1726 clash with the Rohan family, he exiled himself to England, admiring its constitutional monarchy.

His English Letters (1733), burned as the French Lettres philosophiques, sent him to Cirey with his companion Émilie du Châtelet. Frederick the Great made him a Potsdam chamberlain in 1750, but a quarrel led to his 1753 detention at Frankfurt. In 1758 he bought Ferney by the Swiss border.

There he published Candide (1759) and the Dictionnaire philosophique (1764), and campaigned for Jean Calas, executed in 1762 and cleared in 1765. Barred from Paris for decades, he returned in 1778 and died on 30 May. His remains reached the Panthéon in 1791.

弗朗索瓦-马里·阿鲁埃，笔名伏尔泰（1694—1778），是法国启蒙时代最具代表性的作家。他因讽刺摄政王的诗被囚巴士底狱十一个月，1718年获释后改用伏尔泰为名，同年悲剧《俄狄浦斯王》使他成名。1726年与罗昂家族冲突后，他流亡英国，钦佩英国的君主立宪。

他的《英国书简》（1733）以法文《哲学通信》之名刊行后被焚毁，他躲到西雷，与伴侣埃米莉·迪·夏特莱同住。1750年腓特烈大帝在波茨坦封他为侍从官，但一场争执以他1753年在法兰克福被扣押告终。1758年他买下瑞士边境的费尔奈。

他在此发表《老实人》（1759）和《哲学辞典》（1764），并为让·卡拉斯奔走，卡拉斯1762年被处死、1765年获平反。被禁入巴黎数十年后，他1778年返回，5月30日去世。1791年他的遗骸被迁入先贤祠。

en:
Gaucher V de Châtillon (c. 1249–1329), count of Porcien, was named constable of Champagne by Philip III in 1284 and helped free Charles II of Naples from Aragonese captivity. In 1291 he drove the Count of Bar's army out of Champagne.

He fought in Flanders in 1302, surviving the defeat at Courtrai, after which Philip IV made him constable of France. In 1316 he backed Philip of Poitiers' regency and moved that women be barred from the crown. Still campaigning at eighty, he fought at Cassel in 1328 and died the next year.

戈谢五世·德·沙蒂永（约1249—1329）是波尔西安伯爵，1284年被腓力三世任命为香槟统帅，并曾促成那不勒斯的卡洛二世脱离阿拉贡的囚禁。1291年，他将巴尔伯爵的军队逐出香槟。

1302年他在佛兰德作战，从科特赖克惨败中脱身，战后腓力四世升他为法兰西王室统帅。1316年他支持普瓦捷的腓力摄政，并提议禁止女性继承王位。年届八旬时他仍在1328年的卡塞尔战役中出战，次年去世。

en:
Gaucher VIII de Châtillon (died 1377) was the eldest son of Jean II de Châtillon and Éléonore de Roye. A contract of September 1323 betrothed him while still a child to Jeanne de Guines. He succeeded his mother in La Ferté-en-Ponthieu and his father in Châtillon and Troissy.

After 1344 he married, as her fourth husband, Allemande Flotte de Revel, daughter of the chancellor of France and widow of Enguerrand de Coucy; their children were Jean, Gaucher and Jeanne. His will, made on 7 September 1377, was proved before the royal council on 15 December.

戈谢八世·德·沙蒂永（?—1377）是让二世·德·沙蒂永与埃莱奥诺尔·德·鲁瓦的长子。1323年9月的婚约在他还是孩童时将他许配给让娜·德·吉讷。母亲死后他继承拉费尔泰-昂蓬蒂厄，父亲死后继承沙蒂永与特鲁瓦西。

1344年后，他作为阿勒芒德·弗洛特·德·勒韦勒的第四任丈夫与她成婚；她是法兰西掌玺大臣之女、昂盖朗·德·库西的遗孀。两人生有让、戈谢、让娜三子。他1377年9月7日立下的遗嘱于12月15日呈交御前会议。

en:
William of Cremona (Guglielmo Amidano, c. 1270–1356) was an Italian Augustinian theologian born at Cremona. In 1326 he became Prior General of the Augustinian order, heading it for sixteen years.

In 1342 Pope Clement VI made him Bishop of Novara. As bishop he reorganised his diocese's estates and recorded them in a Latin register, the Consignationes, preserved in the cathedral archives. He died at Novara on 29 January 1356 and was buried in Pavia.

克雷莫纳的威廉（约1270—1356）是意大利奥斯定会神学家，生于克雷莫纳。他1326年出任圣奥斯定隐修会总会长，主持修会十六年。

1342年，教皇克雷芒六世任命他为诺瓦拉主教。任内他整顿教区产业，并以拉丁文登记造册，这份《产业录》保存在大教堂档案中。1356年1月29日他卒于诺瓦拉，葬于帕维亚。

Guillaume II Roger (1290–1380) was a Limousin nobleman, born at Rosiers-d'Égletons and elder brother of Pope Clement VI. He received the fief of Chambon through his first wife Marie de Chambon and was ennobled in 1332.

Clement's election in 1342 brought him Beaufort, raised into a county in 1347, and he inherited the county of Alès in 1362. By Marie he fathered the future Pope Gregory XI, and he died at Cornillon in 1380.

纪尧姆二世·罗歇（1290—1380）是利穆赞贵族，生于罗西耶-代格莱通，为教皇克雷芒六世之兄。他因首任妻子玛丽·德·尚邦获得尚邦领地，1332年受封贵族。

1342年克雷芒当选教皇后，他得到博福尔领地，该领地于1347年升为伯国，1362年他又继承阿莱斯伯国。他与玛丽之子后来成为教皇格里高利十一世。1380年他卒于科尔尼永。

en:
Guillaume III Roger de Beaufort (1332–1395), vicomte de Turenne, was nephew of Clement VI and brother of Gregory XI, two Avignon popes.

On 7 February 1350 he married Aliénor de Comminges, and Clement VI gave the couple the vicomté of Turenne as a wedding gift. In 1351 Joanna I of Naples named him Grand Chamberlain. The Treaty of Brétigny made Turenne English, and in 1361 he paid homage to the English king, though he remained loyal to the Valois.

He crusaded at Alexandria in 1365 and represented Gregory XI at the Bruges conference in 1375. In 1383 he presided over the assembly at Alès that ended the Tuchin revolt. He died in Paris on 28 March 1395 and was buried in Notre-Dame.

纪尧姆三世·罗歇·德·博福尔（1332—1395）是蒂雷纳子爵，也是阿维尼翁两位教宗克雷芒六世的侄子、格里高利十一世的弟弟。

1350年2月7日，他与阿莉埃诺·德·科曼日成婚，克雷芒六世将蒂雷纳子爵领地作为新婚礼物赐给夫妇二人。1351年，那不勒斯女王乔万娜一世任命他为王国宫廷大总管。《布勒丁尼条约》将蒂雷纳划归英格兰后，他于1361年向英王行臣服礼，却始终效忠瓦卢瓦王室。

1365年他参加远征亚历山大港的十字军，1375年代表格里高利十一世出席布鲁日和谈。1383年，他主持阿莱斯会议，会上缔结的和约平息了图钦人的起事。1395年3月28日，他在巴黎去世，葬于巴黎圣母院。

en:
William the Simple (c. 1085–c. 1150) was the eldest son of Count Stephen of Blois and Adela of Normandy, daughter of William the Conqueror. Designated Count of Blois and Chartres in 1102, he intervened in his mother's dispute with the cathedral chapter, bursting into the church to demand an oath against its canons. Around 1107 his mother set him aside in favour of his brother Theobald.

He married Agnes, heiress of Sully-sur-Loire, and retired to her Sully estates. Though the Conqueror's eldest legitimate grandson, he was never advanced for the English crown; King Stephen was his brother and Eudes Archambaud his son.

纪尧姆（天真者，约1085—约1150）是布卢瓦伯爵艾蒂安与“征服者”威廉之女诺曼底的阿德拉的长子。1102年他被指定为布卢瓦与沙特尔伯爵；母亲与主教座堂教士发生争端时，他闯入教堂，要求众人宣誓对付教士。约1107年，母亲阿德拉废黜他，改立其弟蒂博。

他娶卢瓦尔河畔叙利的女继承人阿涅丝，退居叙利领地。他是征服者威廉最年长的合法外孙，却从未被推为英格兰王位候选人；他的弟弟是英格兰国王斯蒂芬，儿子为叙利的厄德·阿尔尚博。

Guillaume de Châteauvillain (c. 1310 – 17 April 1352) was the younger son of Jean II de Châteauvillain and Marie de Pierrepont. When the family lands were divided he received the lordships of Pleurs and Courcelles.

In 1342, after a quarrel, he and his elder brother Jean III marched armed onto the lands of the bishop of Langres and had to beg his pardon. He married Blanche de Châtillon-en-Bazois, and their daughter Marie inherited Courcelles.
