Guillaume I de Coucy (1288–1335) was a Picard baron, lord of Coucy and Oisy. The son of Enguerrand V de Coucy and Christine Lindsay, a niece of King John of Scotland, he married Isabelle de Châtillon in 1311.

He held Oisy through the marriage and succeeded his father at Coucy around 1323. Jeanne of Flanders, widow of Enguerrand IV, disputed both lands. His claim was upheld in April 1329, when Philip VI settled the long family suit in his favour. He died in 1335 and was buried at Prémontré Abbey.

en:
Guy II of Thouars (1246/1249–1308), son of Aimery IX and Marguerite of Lusignan, joined his uncle Savary IV and other Poitevin barons in a 1269 agreement with Alphonse of Poitiers. Around 1274 he succeeded Savary as viscount of Thouars under Poitou's viage custom, by which fiefs passed first through the late lord's brothers; the custom was abolished soon afterward.

He then faced claims from kinswomen over pensions and lands, and the Parlement of Paris ordered him to pay his aunt Eleanor of Soissons an annuity in return for her landed rights.

In 1304 Philip IV summoned him for the Flanders war. He died on 21 September 1308, leaving the viscounty to his son Jean I.

居伊二世·德·图阿尔（1246/1249—1308）是艾默里克九世与吕西尼昂的玛格丽特之子。1269年，他与叔父萨瓦里四世及其他普瓦图男爵同普瓦捷的阿方斯达成协议。约1274年，他依普瓦图的“回归”惯例继萨瓦里为图阿尔子爵：按此惯例，封邑先传给已故领主的诸弟；该惯例不久后被废除。

此后他面对女性亲族关于年金与土地的索求，巴黎高等法院判令他向婶母苏瓦松的埃莱奥诺尔支付年金，以换取她的土地权利。

1304年腓力四世征召他参加佛兰德战争。他于1308年9月21日去世，子爵之位传给儿子让一世。

Guy VI was Viscount of Limoges from 1230 until his death in 1263. The son of Viscount Guy V and Ermengarde, he succeeded his father as a child in 1230, and his mother governed as regent until he took power in the late 1230s.

Around 1258 he married Margaret of Burgundy, daughter of Duke Hugh IV. In 1263, after besieging Bourdeilles Castle in vain, he died at Brantôme Abbey and was buried at Saint-Martial in Limoges. His three-year-old daughter Marie succeeded him.

en:
Guy VII de Mauvoisin (born c. 1307, died after 1360) was baron of Rosny-sur-Seine and the eldest son of Guy VI de Mauvoisin and Laure de Ponthieu. Around 1328 he married Roberte de Beaumetz, châtelaine of Bapaume, whose Artois lordships passed to their daughters.

The marriage produced three daughters, Laure, Béatrix and Marguerite, but no son. After Guy's death his brother Amaury sold Rosny to his daughter Béatrix in 1365.

en:
Henry I (1008–1060) was king of the Franks from 1031. Born to King Robert II and Constance of Arles, he was crowned co-king in 1027. He settled his brother Robert's revolt by granting him the Duchy of Burgundy in 1032.

In 1047 he helped the young William of Normandy win at Val-ès-Dunes, but later invaded Normandy twice, losing at Mortemer in 1054 and Varaville in 1057. In 1051 he married Anne of Kiev, mother of his heir. The royal demesne reached its smallest extent during his reign. He died at Vitry-en-Brie while besieging Thimert, and was buried at Saint-Denis.

亨利一世（1008—1060）自1031年起为法兰克人之王，为罗贝尔二世与阿尔勒的康斯坦丝之子，1027年被加冕为共治国王。1032年他以封赐勃艮第公国平息了弟弟罗贝尔的叛乱。

1047年他协助年轻的诺曼底公爵纪尧姆在瓦勒迪恩获胜，后来却两度入侵诺曼底，先后于1054年在莫特梅、1057年在瓦拉维尔战败。1051年他娶基辅的安娜为妻，生下继承人。王室领地在他统治期间缩至最小。他在围攻蒂梅尔时死于维特里昂布里，葬于圣但尼。

Henri III de Sully (died 1285) became lord of Sully-sur-Loire in 1269 and served as butler of France under Philip III. In 1282 he married Marguerite de Bommiers, lady of Brion and Châteaumeillant.

Their children included Henri IV, later grand treasurer, and Péronelle, wife of Count John II of Dreux. Henri died in 1285 during Philip III's campaign in Aragon, and his son Henri succeeded him as lord of Sully.

en:
Henri IV de Sully (1282–1336), lord of Sully-sur-Loire, was a councillor of Philip IV. He backed Philip of Poitiers's rise to the regency and the throne in 1316, becoming grand butler of France in 1317.

Under Philip V he served as grand treasurer, reorganizing the royal treasury and presiding over the Chamber of Accounts founded in 1320. Charles IV replaced him as treasurer in 1322.

He became governor of Navarre in 1329, took part in plans for a crusade against Granada that came to nothing, led Navarre's defense against Aragon in 1335, and died in office in 1336.

en:
Hugh of Blois (died 985/86) was a French prelate and archbishop of Bourges. The second son of Count Theobald I the Trickster of Blois and Liutgarde of Vermandois, he was the elder brother of Count Odo I.

Destined for the church while the comital inheritance passed to Odo, Hugh held charges attached to the abbey of Coulombs in the 950s and in 969 succeeded his uncle Richard as archbishop of Bourges. A rare recorded act of his episcopate, dated 983, was his seizure of the chapel of Saint-Sulpice. He died in 985 or 986.

en:
Hugh Capet (c. 941–996) was duke of the Franks and, from 987, king of the Franks, the first of the Capetian line. Son of Hugh the Great and Hedwige of Saxony. When Louis V, last of his line, died in 987, Archbishop Adalberon of Reims backed Hugh, who was acclaimed at Senlis and crowned; he had his son Robert the Pious anointed at Orléans.

Charles of Lorraine seized Laon in 988 and Hugh besieged it twice in vain. His appointee as archbishop of Reims, Arnoul, then opened Reims to Charles. In 991 Bishop Adalberon of Laon seized both men in their sleep and handed them to Hugh.

The nickname Capet may allude to the abbatial cape; Hugh was lay abbot of Saint-Martin of Tours. He died in 996, perhaps of smallpox, and was buried at Saint-Denis. His line held the throne until 1328, and its cadet branches until 1848.

于格·卡佩（约941—996）是法兰克人的公爵，987年起为法兰克国王，是卡佩家族的第一位国王。他是伟大的于格与萨克森的海德维希之子。末代加洛林国王路易五世于987年死后，兰斯大主教阿达尔贝隆支持于格，他在桑利斯被拥戴并加冕，又让儿子“虔诚者”罗贝尔在奥尔良受膏。

洛林的查理于988年夺取拉昂，于格两次围城不克。他任命的兰斯大主教阿尔努尔却把兰斯献给查理。991年，拉昂主教阿达尔贝隆趁二人熟睡将他们擒获，交给于格。

“卡佩”这一绰号可能指修道院长的披肩，于格是图尔圣马丁教堂的世俗院长。他于996年去世，可能死于天花，葬在圣但尼。他的这一系保有王位到1328年，旁系延续到1848年。

洛林的查理于988年夺取[ShowLocationName('laon')]，于格两次围城不克。他任命的兰斯大主教阿尔努尔却把兰斯献给查理。991年，拉昂主教阿达尔贝隆趁二人熟睡将他们擒获，交给于格。

“卡佩”这一绰号可能指修道院长的披肩，于格是[ShowLocationName('tours')]圣马丁教堂的世俗院长。他于996年去世，可能死于天花，葬在圣但尼。他的这一系保有王位到1328年，旁系延续到1848年。

en:
Hugh the Great (c. 898–956), duke of the Franks, was the son of King Robert I and father of Hugh Capet. When his father fell at Soissons in 923 he let the crown pass to his brother-in-law Rudolph.

The strongest magnate in West Francia, he recalled Louis IV in 936 and married Hedwig of Saxony, sister of Otto the Great, in 937.

He later warred against Louis, holding him captive in 945–946 until he surrendered Laon. Excommunicated by a council in 948, he made peace with Louis and the church in 953. He supported the succession of Louis's son Lothair and died in 956.

zh:
伟大的于格（约898—956）为法兰克人公爵，是罗贝尔一世之子，也是于格·卡佩的父亲。923年父亲在苏瓦松战死后，他没有自行称王，而让王位传给姐夫拉乌尔。

作为西法兰克最有权势的大贵族，他于936年迎回路德维希四世，又在937年迎娶奥托大帝之妹萨克森的海德薇希。

后来他与路德维希四世交战，于945至946年间将其囚禁，直到对方交出拉昂才放人。948年教会会议将他绝罚，953年他与路易和教会和解。他支持路易之子洛泰尔继位，956年去世。

Ide de Mauvoisin (before 1318–1375) was the daughter of Guy Mauvoisin and Laure de Ponthieu. Around 1329 she married John III, Count of Dreux, and was widowed childless in 1331, afterwards holding the lands of Saint-Valery in dower for forty-two years.

On 2 September 1332 she married Mathieu III de Trie, Marshal of France, who died on 26 November 1344. A charter of 1344 records her dower dispute with his sisters. She died in 1375.

伊德·德·莫瓦桑（1318年前—1375）是居伊·莫瓦桑与劳拉·德·蓬蒂约之女。约1329年，她嫁给德勒伯爵让三世，1331年丧夫且无子嗣，此后以寡妇产名义领有圣瓦勒里之地达四十二年。

Isabeau de Châtillon (c. 1295 – 19 May 1360) was the daughter of Guy IV, Count of Saint-Pol, and Marie of Brittany. As lady of Encre she married in 1311 at Pontoise, before Philip the Fair, the Picard baron Guillaume I de Coucy.

Her children included Enguerrand VI, killed at Crécy in 1346, and Raoul. Widowed in 1335, she kept Oisy as her dower and was styled its lady in 1351.

Isabeau de Thouars (died 1397) was a daughter of Louis I, Viscount of Thouars, and Joan II, Countess of Dreux. Her first husband, the marshal of France Guy II de Clermont-Nesle, was killed at Mauron in 1352. In 1356 she married Ingelger I d'Amboise, by whom she had two sons, Pierre II and Ingelger II.

Her third husband was Guillaume d'Harcourt. When her sister Péronnelle died in 1397, Isabeau's Amboise sons carried on the Thouars succession, with Pierre II ruling the viscounty until 1426.

James of Artois (1325–after 1347) was the third son of Robert III of Artois and Joan of Valois, sister of King Philip VI. After his father was convicted of forgery and driven into English exile, the king had his nephews taken into custody.

James was confined at Nemours in 1342 and then moved with his mother and brother Robert to Château Gaillard. He died in prison after 1347, probably a victim of the Black Death, without posterity.

en:
John of Artois (1321–1387), called Sans-Terre (the Landless), was the son of the disgraced Robert III of Artois and Joan of Valois, Philip VI's sister. His father's treason cost the family its lands, and in 1334 Philip shut John and his family in Château-Gaillard.

John II freed him in 1350 and in February 1351 gave him the County of Eu, recovered after Constable Raoul de Brienne's execution; the Artois family thereby joined the royal party against the Navarrese. As royal lieutenant in Normandy he helped seize the King of Navarre's lands there.

He was at Bordeaux when the king was captured at Poitiers in 1356, and in 1357 carried truce letters to Paris. He served Charles V and led the rearguard at Roosebeke in 1382.

阿图瓦的让（1321—1387），绰号“无地者”，是失势的罗贝尔三世·德·阿图瓦与腓力六世之妹瓦卢瓦的让娜之子。因父亲的背叛，家族丧失了领地，1334年腓力把让及其家人关进加亚尔堡。

1350年让二世释放了他，1351年2月又把厄镇伯国封给他；王室处决大元帅拉乌尔·德·布里耶纳后收回了这块领地。阿图瓦家族由此站到王室一边，对抗纳瓦拉派。他任国王在诺曼底的副将，协助夺取纳瓦拉国王在当地的领地。

1356年法王在普瓦捷被俘时，他身在波尔多；1357年他把停战文书送往巴黎。他后来效力于查理五世，1382年在罗斯贝克战役中指挥后军。

en:
John of Beaumont (1288–1356), born John of Hainaut, was the fourth son of Count John II of Hainaut and brother of Count William III of Holland. He became count of Soissons by marriage and often governed Holland for his brother.

In 1326, when Queen Isabella sought refuge at William's court, John led an expedition to England that helped her and Mortimer depose Edward II. In 1340 he was regent of Holland and Zeeland for his nephew William IV, who was killed at Warns in 1345 while John escaped.

His claim to the succession lost to his niece Margaret, and he left for France. He sided with Philip VI in 1346 and at Crécy pulled the king out of the rout. He died at Valenciennes in March 1356.

en:
Jean de Châtillon (1283–1363), second son of Gaucher V de Châtillon, Constable of France, and Isabeau de Dreux, was lord of Châtillon-sur-Marne and Gandelu, and held La Ferté-en-Ponthieu through his wife Éléonore de Roye. As grand queux of France he served Philip the Fair, who named him an executor of his will in 1314.

When war with England came, he went to Flanders with John, Duke of Normandy, in 1340 and defended Tournai against the English siege in 1341. Appointed grand maître de France in 1350, he was present at Poitiers in 1356. He died in 1363, very old, and was buried at Cerfroy near Gandelu.

en:
John I, called the Posthumous (15–19 November 1316), was king of France and Navarre for the four days of his life. The posthumous son of Louis X and Clemence of Anjou, he was born king and died in his cradle on 19 November, while his uncle Philip of Poitiers held the regency.

Buried at Saint-Denis, he was the youngest French king and the only one to reign from birth. His death broke three centuries of father-to-son Capetian succession, and Philip took the crown as Philip V. The dispute over Philip's legitimacy led to the reaffirmation of the exclusion of women from the French succession.

“遗腹子”约翰一世（1316年11月15—19日）在世上仅活了四天，这四天里他都是法兰西与纳瓦拉国王。他是路易十世与安茹的克莱门斯的遗腹子，出生即为王，11月19日夭折于襁褓之中，由叔父普瓦捷的腓力摄政。

John I of Thouars (born after 1284, died 1332) was the twenty-seventh viscount of Thouars, son of Guy II and Margaret of Brienne-Eu. In 1307 he married Blanche of Brabant, lady of Rochecorbon, younger daughter of Godfrey of Brabant. He succeeded his father in 1308 and ruled until he died.

Blanche died in 1330, leaving three sons. Louis I succeeded as viscount, John was lord of La Cheze-le-Vicomte, and Guy died in 1354.

Jean I de Trie (c. 1179–before 1237) was châtelain of Trie in the Vexin, son of Enguerrand II Aiguillon de Trie. In 1190 he confirmed his father's donation to Valle Sainte-Marie abbey, and in the same year married Alix de Dammartin, daughter of Count Aubry II of Dammartin.

Through this marriage his descendants inherited the county of Dammartin: their son Mathieu de Trie became count in 1259, while another son, Renaud, was seigneur de Fontenay.

John II, called the Good (26 April 1319 – 8 April 1364), was the eldest son of Philip VI of France and Joan of Burgundy, made duke of Normandy and count of Anjou in 1332. He married Bonne of Luxembourg the same year and succeeded his father as king in 1350.

en:
John III of Châteauvillain (c. 1310–1355) was lord of Châteauvillain in Champagne, eldest son of John II of Châteauvillain and Marie of Roucy, and spent much of his career in the service of the duke of Burgundy. Left fatherless in 1312, he received guardians named by Philip the Fair in 1313.

In 1326 he granted a charter of liberties to the people of Arc, which Duke Odo IV confirmed two years later, and in 1337 he sold his castle of Brémur to the duke. In 1342 he and his brother Guillaume entered the bishop of Langres's lands in arms, then admitted their fault and won his pardon.

A member of the duke's council, he was one of his eight testamentary executors in 1346. He died in 1355 and was succeeded by his son John IV.

Jean IV de Châteauvillain (born after 1326 – 19 September 1356) was the eldest son of Jean III de Châteauvillain and Marguerite de Noyers. He succeeded his father as lord of Châteauvillain, Arc-en-Barrois and Nully in 1355.

en:
Jean-Jacques Rousseau (1712–1778) was a Genevan philosophe whose works shaped modern political thought. Born in Calvinist Geneva, he lost his mother as an infant and ran away at fifteen, converting to Catholicism in Savoy under Madame de Warens. In Paris he befriended Diderot and wrote for the Encyclopédie; his Discourse on the Arts and Sciences won the Dijon prize in 1750.

His Discourse on Inequality (1755) argued that private property was the source of social inequality. In 1762 came The Social Contract, founding legitimate government on the people's general will, and Émile, a treatise on education. Both were condemned and burned, and an arrest warrant drove him out of France.

In England in 1766 his quarrel with David Hume became a public scandal. He finished his Confessions in 1770 and died at Ermenonville in 1778; published in 1782, they preceded his 1794 reburial in the Panthéon near Voltaire.

让-雅克·卢梭（1712—1778）是日内瓦启蒙哲士，其思想深刻影响了现代政治学说。他生于加尔文派的日内瓦，出生不久母亲去世，十五岁时逃离，在萨伏依受华伦夫人庇护改宗天主教。在巴黎他与狄德罗结交并为《百科全书》撰稿，《论科学与艺术》于1750年获第戎征文奖。

他的《论人类不平等的起源和基础》（1755）认为私有财产是社会不平等的根源。1762年他出版《社会契约论》，把合法统治建立在人民的“公意”之上，同年又出版论教育的《爱弥儿》。两部书都遭谴责焚毁，一纸逮捕令迫使他离开法国。

1766年在英国，他与大卫·休谟的争吵成了公开丑闻。他1770年写完《忏悔录》，1778年在埃尔默农维尔去世；《忏悔录》1782年刊行，1794年他的遗骸迁入先贤祠，安放在伏尔泰近旁。

Jean de Louvres was a French master mason of the fourteenth century, probably from the Paris region. From 1342 to 1351 he was master of the works at the papal palace of Avignon.

Under Clement VI he built the Great Chapel, the Great Audience hall and several towers of the Palais Neuf. He also served the pope as a serjeant-at-arms from 1345, settled in Avignon and died in 1357 or 1358.

Joan of Burgundy, called Joan the Lame (c. 1293–1349), was the daughter of Duke Robert II of Burgundy and Agnes of France. Promised to Philip of Valois in 1303, she married him in July 1313, and when he was crowned Philip VI in 1328 she became the first queen of the House of Valois.

The Hundred Years' War kept the king on campaign, and she governed France as regent several times. The role earned her a bad reputation, sharpened by her lameness, which some took for a curse.

A learned bibliophile, she commissioned French translations such as the Miroir historial. She died on 12 December 1349, probably of the plague, a few months before her son John II became king; her heart was buried at Cîteaux, resting place of the dukes of Burgundy.

勃艮第的让娜，世称“跛子让娜”（约1293—1349），是勃艮第公爵罗贝尔二世与法兰西的阿格妮丝之女。1303年她被许配给瓦卢瓦的腓力，1313年7月完婚；1328年腓力加冕为腓力六世，她成为瓦卢瓦王朝第一位王后。

en:
Jeanne de Châteauvillain (c. 1330 – c. 1389), elder daughter of Jean III de Châteauvillain and Marguerite de Noyers, inherited Châteauvillain after her brother Jean IV fell at Poitiers in 1356, while her sister Marie received Arc-en-Barrois and Nully. She married five times, her husbands including the Constable of Burgundy Jean I de Thil and the routier captain Arnaud de Cervole, called the Archpriest.

In 1373 she recovered her late sister's lands. When she died, Châteauvillain passed to her eldest son Jean V de Thil-Châteauvillain.

en:
Joanna of Châtillon (c. 1285–1354), daughter of the Constable Gaucher V de Châtillon, married Walter V of Brienne in 1305 and became Duchess of Athens in 1308.

Her rule there lasted three years: Walter was killed fighting the Catalan Company at Halmyros on 15 March 1311, and after perhaps trying to hold the Acropolis she surrendered it and returned to France with her infant son Walter VI.

By constant petitions to Naples, France and the papacy she kept her son's claim to Athens alive until he was old enough to press it himself. In 1321 that son sued her over his father's debts in a suit mediated by Philip V of France. She kept her ducal title until her death, and her tomb at Troyes was inscribed Duchesse d'Athènes.

Joan of Évreux (1310–1371), daughter of Louis, Count of Évreux, and Margaret of Artois, became the third wife of her cousin Charles IV of France in 1324. She bore three daughters but no son, and Salic law barred the daughters from the throne, so when Charles died in 1328 the direct Capetian line ended and the crown passed to the Valois.

Her book of hours, illuminated by Jean Pucelle, and her silver-gilt Virgin and Child are masterpieces of French Gothic art; Joan left the statue to the abbey of Saint-Denis. She died on 4 March 1371 at her château of Brie-Comte-Robert and was buried at Saint-Denis.

埃夫勒的让娜（1310—1371）是埃夫勒伯爵路易与阿图瓦的玛格丽特之女，1324年嫁给堂兄法王查理四世，成为他的第三任王后。她生下三个女儿却没有儿子，而萨利克法使女儿不能继承王位，因此1328年查理去世后，卡佩直系绝嗣，王位转入瓦卢瓦支系。

她的日课经由让·皮塞勒手抄彩绘，另有一尊银鎏金圣母圣婴像，二者都是法国哥特艺术的杰作；让娜将圣像留给了圣德尼修道院。1371年3月4日她在布里-孔特-罗贝尔的城堡去世，葬于圣德尼圣殿。

en:
Joan I (1273–1305) inherited Navarre and Champagne as an infant in 1274, married the future Philip IV in 1284 and became queen of France in 1285. Born at Bar-sur-Seine to Henry I of Navarre and Blanche of Artois, she never visited Navarre, which French governors ruled in her name.

She governed Champagne directly: in 1297 she raised an army against an invasion by Henry III of Bar and took the count prisoner. Her three sons all became kings of France and her daughter Isabella married Edward II. She founded the College of Navarre in Paris in 1305, the year she died.

zh:
胡安娜一世（1273—1305）于1274年幼年继承纳瓦拉王位与香槟伯国，1284年嫁给未来的腓力四世，1285年成为法兰西王后。她生于塞纳河畔巴尔，父亲是纳瓦拉国王恩里克一世，母亲是阿图瓦的布朗什。她从未到过纳瓦拉，当地由法兰西总督以她的名义治理。

en:
Joan II of Burgundy (c. 1291–1330), eldest daughter of Count Otto IV of Burgundy and Mahaut of Artois, inherited the County of Burgundy in 1303 and married the future Philip V of France in 1307.

In the Tour de Nesle scandal of 1314 she was accused of covering for her sister and sister-in-law and imprisoned at Dourdan until the Parlement acquitted her. She became queen in 1316.

After Philip's death she returned to Burgundy and inherited Artois in 1329. A patron of letters, she commissioned the Ovide moralisé. She died at Roye in 1330.

zh:
勃艮第的让娜二世（约1291—1330）是勃艮第伯爵奥东四世与阿图瓦的玛奥的长女，1303年继承勃艮第伯国，1307年嫁给后来的法兰西国王腓力五世。

腓力去世后她回到勃艮第，1329年继承阿图瓦伯国。她雅好文艺，命人编写《奥维德道德释义》。1330年，她卒于鲁瓦。

en:
Joan II of Dreux (1309–1355) was the daughter of John II, Count of Dreux, and Péronnelle de Sully. In 1330 she married Louis I, Viscount of Thouars. When her half-brother Peter, the last male heir, died in 1345, Joan inherited the county and ruled it as countess until her death.

Her son Simon de Thouars succeeded her as count but died in 1365. The county then passed to her three daughters, Péronnelle, Isabeau and Marguerite.

en:
Joan of Valois (1304–1363), known as Madame d'Artois, was the daughter of Charles, Count of Valois, and Catherine I of Courtenay, and half-sister of King Philip VI. About 1320 she married Robert III of Artois, who claimed Artois.

After Robert used forged documents and fled in 1331, Joan and her children were seized and confined at Château Gaillard. Her husband died in England in 1342, but she remained a prisoner for years; she died in July 1363 and was buried in Paris.

en:
Jean Roger de Beaufort was a son of Guillaume II Roger, Count of Beaufort, nephew of Pope Clement VI and brother of Pope Gregory XI. He became Bishop of Rieux in 1353 and was transferred to Carpentras in 1357, where he authorized the city's Jews to build a synagogue in 1361 and later a cemetery.

After his brother's election as pope he was made Archbishop of Auch in 1371 and of Narbonne in 1375. He died in 1391, loyal to the Avignon obedience during the Western Schism.

en:
Bonne of Luxembourg, born Jutta (20 May 1315 – 11 September 1349), was a daughter of John the Blind of Bohemia and Elisabeth of the Přemyslid dynasty. On 28 July 1332 she married the thirteen-year-old John, the future John II of France.

She never became queen: she died of the Black Death at Maubuisson Abbey in 1349, a year before John became king. Her children included Charles V of France and Philip the Bold, duke of Burgundy, and she patronised Guillaume de Machaut.

Catherine of Austria (1320–1349) was the elder daughter of Leopold I, Duke of Austria, and Catherine of Savoy. In 1338 her marriage to Enguerrand VI, Lord of Coucy, was contracted at Vincennes. Their son Enguerrand, the future Enguerrand VII, was born around 1340.

Enguerrand VI was killed in the fighting before Crécy in 1346. Catherine married Konrad von Hardeck in 1348, and both died of the Black Death in 1349, she three days after her husband; she was buried at Königsfelden.

奥地利的凯瑟琳（1320—1349）是奥地利公爵利奥波德一世与萨伏依的卡特琳的长女。1338年，她与库西领主昂盖朗六世在万塞讷订立婚约。她的儿子昂盖朗，即后来的昂盖朗七世，约生于1340年。

1346年，昂盖朗六世在克雷西战役前的战事中阵亡。1348年凯瑟琳改嫁康拉德·冯·哈德克，1349年夫妇二人先后死于黑死病，凯瑟琳比丈夫晚三天离世，葬于柯尼希斯费尔登修道院。

en:
Clementia of Hungary (1293–1328), daughter of Charles Martel of Anjou and his Habsburg wife Clemence, was raised at Naples but styled a Hungarian princess. On 19 August 1315 she married Louis X of France and was crowned at Reims.

Widowed in June 1316, she gave birth in November to John I, king from birth, who lived only five days before her brother-in-law took the crown as Philip V.

After disputing her dower with Philip she withdrew to Aix-en-Provence, returned to Paris in 1321, and died there on 13 October 1328, a patron of illuminated manuscripts.

匈牙利的克莱门西娅（1293—1328）是安茹的卡洛·马特罗与哈布斯堡家族的克莱门斯之女，生养于那不勒斯，却被视为匈牙利公主。1315年8月19日她嫁给法王路易十世，在兰斯加冕为后。

1316年6月路易十世去世，她于11月生下约翰一世：孩子出生即为王，仅存活五天，王位便由她的小叔腓力五世取得。

她与腓力争执寡妇产后退居普罗旺斯地区艾克斯，1321年回到巴黎，1328年10月13日在巴黎去世，以赞助泥金手抄本闻名。

Laure de Mauvoisin (born c. 1329) was the elder daughter of Guy VII de Mauvoisin, baron of Rosny, and Roberte de Beaumetz. From her mother she inherited the châtellenie of Bapaume and other Artois lordships, lands considered more valuable than Rosny itself.

She married Robert de Beaussart, seigneur of Wingles and constable of Flanders. Their daughters were Ide, who married Jean de Saquainville, and Béatrix, who married twice, her second husband being Hugues de Melun, burgrave of Ghent.

en:
Lothair (941–986), son of Louis IV and Gerberga, succeeded his father at thirteen in 954, crowned at Reims under the guardianship of Hugh the Great.

In 978 he raided Lotharingia, nearly catching Otto II at Aachen; Otto ravaged to the walls of Paris, and by the 980 treaty of Margut Lothair renounced Lotharingia. His son Louis V was crowned co-king in 979, and after Otto II's death in 983 he claimed guardianship of the young Otto III. He died at Laon in March 986, planning to attack Cambrai.

en:
Louis the Pious (778–840) was the Carolingian emperor who inherited all Charlemagne's realm and saw his sons tear it apart. Crowned King of Aquitaine in 781, he took Barcelona in 801. After his brothers died, he was crowned co-emperor at Aachen in 813 and became sole ruler in 814.

In 817, after a gallery collapsed beneath him, he issued a plan naming Lothair co-emperor and Pepin and Louis sub-kings. The birth of his son Charles in 823 upset the plan, and from 829 his elder sons rose against him.

In 833 his army melted away at the Field of Lies; deposed and made to do public penance, he was restored in 834. In 839 he divided the empire between Lothair and Charles. He died in June 840 on a Rhine island; his sons fought on until the 843 Treaty of Verdun split it into West, East and Middle Francia.

zh:
虔诚者路易（778—840）是继承了查理曼全部疆域、却眼看儿子们将其撕裂的加洛林皇帝。他781年被封为阿基坦国王，801年夺取巴塞罗那。兄弟们相继去世后，他813年在亚琛加冕为共治皇帝，814年成为唯一统治者。

817年一条回廊在他脚下坍塌后，他颁布继承方案，立洛泰尔为共治皇帝，丕平与路易为附属国王。823年儿子查理出生，打乱这一方案，从829年起年长的儿子们接连起兵反对他。

833年，他的军队在“谎言之野”溃散；他被废黜并当众忏悔，834年复位。839年他把帝国分给洛泰尔和查理。840年6月他在莱茵河一座岛上去世，儿子们继续争战，直到843年《凡尔登条约》把帝国分为西法兰克、东法兰克与中法兰克。

en:
Louis I de Sully succeeded his father Jean II as lord of Sully-sur-Loire about 1343. He married Isabeau de Craon, and from 1373 held the barony of Craon in her right.

In the Hundred Years' War he sided with the English, and in 1376 his wife sought the protection of the Duke of Anjou against him. He died in 1382, leaving a single daughter, Marie, who brought Sully and Craon to the La Trémoïlle family.

en:
Louis I of Thouars (c. 1310–1370), son of Jean I and Blanche of Brabant, succeeded his uncle Hugh II as viscount in 1333. In 1330 he married Joan II of Dreux, holding Dreux in her right from 1345 to 1355.

An ally of Philip VI, he served as a banneret against Edward III and stood beside John the Good when the king was beaten at Poitiers in 1356.

The Treaty of Brétigny in 1360 placed Thouars under English control, and John Chandos took possession of the town in 1361. Louis died at Talmont on 7 April 1370. Both his sons were dead, Simon at a tournament on his wedding day in 1365, so the viscounty passed to his daughter Péronnelle.

路易一世·德·图阿尔（约1310—1370）是让一世与布拉班特的布朗什之子，1333年继叔父于格二世之后任图阿尔子爵。1330年他娶德勒的让娜二世，1345至1355年凭妻权领有德勒伯国。

他始终是腓力六世的盟友，作为方旗骑士对英王爱德华三世作战；1356年好人约翰兵败普瓦捷，他就在国王身旁。

en:
Louis the Stammerer (846–879), eldest son of Charles the Bald, was nicknamed for his stammer. In 866 he succeeded his brother as king of Aquitaine, and in 877 his father's death brought him the West Frankish throne, crowned at Compiègne.

Pope John VIII crowned him again at Troyes in 878 and may have offered him the imperial crown, which he declined. He died at Compiègne in 879 marching against Viking raiders, leaving the realm to his sons Louis III and Carloman II.

en:
Louis III (863/865–882), eldest son of Louis the Stammerer, became king of West Francia in 879, his legitimacy disputed. In 880 he and his brother Carloman II divided the kingdom at Amiens, Louis taking Neustria, and by the Treaty of Ribemont ceded western Lotharingia to East Francia.

He failed to take Vienne from Boso of Provence, but in August 881 he and Carloman crushed Viking raiders at Saucourt-en-Vimeu, a victory praised in the Ludwigslied. In August 882 he died at Saint-Denis after striking his head on a low lintel while chasing a girl on horseback.

en:
Louis IV (920–954), called d'Outremer, was the son of Charles the Simple. After his father's capture in 923 he was raised in England, until Hugh the Great recalled him and he was crowned at Laon in 936.

In 939 he married Gerberga of Saxony. Captured by Normans in 945, he was handed to Hugh the Great and released in 946 after surrendering Laon. He died at Reims in 954 after falling from his horse while chasing a wolf, and his son Lothair succeeded him.

en:
Louis IX (1214–1270), called Saint Louis, was Capetian king of France from 1226 and the only king the Catholic Church has canonised. Crowned at twelve under his mother Blanche of Castile’s regency, he defeated Henry III at Taillebourg. The 1259 Treaty of Paris settled his borders.

His justice was the lasting part of his reign: he abolished trial by ordeal, banned private wars and let subjects appeal to the crown. He vowed to go on crusade: he took Damietta in 1249, but was captured at Fariskur in 1250 and freed for four hundred thousand bezants. He spent four years fortifying Acre, Caesarea, Jaffa.

He consecrated the Sainte-Chapelle for the crown of thorns. His piety had a harsh side: the burning of the Talmud. In 1270 he sailed for Tunis on the Eighth Crusade and died of dysentery. His son Philip III succeeded him; Boniface VIII canonised him in 1297.

zh:
路易九世（1214—1270），世称圣路易，自1226年起为卡佩王朝的法兰西国王，也是天主教会封圣的唯一一位国王。他十二岁加冕，由母亲卡斯蒂利亚的布兰卡摄政，在塔耶堡击败亨利三世。1259年的《巴黎条约》划定了他的边界。

他朝中最持久的成就是司法：废除神判法，禁止私战，允许臣民向王室上诉。他立誓参加十字军：1249年攻占杜姆亚特，1250年在法里斯库尔被俘，付出四十万拜占特赎金才获释，随后又用四年加固阿卡、凯撒利亚和雅法的防务。

他为安放荆棘冠冕祝圣了圣礼拜堂。他的虔诚也有严厉的一面：焚烧《塔木德》。1270年他率第八次十字军远征突尼斯，死于痢疾，其子腓力三世继位，1297年教宗博尼法斯八世将他封圣。

en:
Louis V (c. 967–987), called the Do-Nothing, was the son of Lothair. Crowned co-king in 979, he married Adelaide-Blanche of Anjou, a widow twice his age, in 982, but the childless marriage soon collapsed. He reigned alone after his father's death in March 986.

Louis died in May 987 after a hunting fall near Senlis. Dying without heirs, he ended the Carolingian line: Adalberon of Reims crowned Hugh Capet, elected king in his place.

en:
Louis VI (1081–1137), called the Fat, ruled as King of the Franks from 1108, succeeding his father Philip I. Much of his reign was spent campaigning against the lawless robber barons of the Île-de-France and fighting Henry I of England for control of Normandy.

He granted town charters to win urban support, was the first Capetian to issue kingdom-wide ordonnances, and strengthened royal justice with the counsel of Abbot Suger of Saint-Denis. In 1115 he married Adelaide of Maurienne; their eldest son Philip died after a fall from his horse in 1131, and Louis was succeeded in 1137 by their son Louis VII.

en:
Louis VII (1120–1180), called the Young, became King of France in 1137, when his father Louis VI died days after marrying him to Eleanor, heiress of Aquitaine, briefly extending Capetian power to the Pyrenees.

In 1147 he joined the Second Crusade and the failed siege of Damascus, returning in 1149. His marriage to Eleanor was annulled in 1152; she then wed Henry II of England, carrying Aquitaine into the Angevin Empire.

His third wife Adela of Champagne bore Philip II Augustus in 1165. His reign saw the rise of the University of Paris and the building of Notre-Dame.

Louis VIII (1187–1226), called the Lion, son of Philip II Augustus and Isabella of Hainault, married Blanche of Castile in 1200. As prince he invaded England in 1216 and was proclaimed king by rebel barons in London, though never crowned; after King John's death he was defeated and withdrew.

He fought in the Albigensian Crusade and, as king from 1223, seized western lands from the Angevins, leaving them only Gascony. In 1226 he led another crusade into Languedoc and died of dysentery on the campaign, leaving the crown to the young Louis IX.

Louis X (1289–1316), called the Quarrelsome, was the eldest son of Philip IV and Joan I of Navarre, inheriting Navarre in 1305 and ruling France from 1314. His reign saw noble tensions over his father's reforms; he let serfs buy their freedom and readmitted the Jews.

His queen Margaret of Burgundy was convicted of adultery in the 1314 Tour de Nesle affair and died imprisoned, and he then wed Clementia of Hungary. Louis died in 1316 after a game of real tennis, leaving Clementia pregnant. Their posthumous son John I lived only five days, and after a disputed succession Louis's brother became Philip V.

Margaret of Anjou (1273–1299) was countess of Anjou and Maine in her own right. A daughter of Charles II of Naples, she married Charles of Valois, son of King Philip III of France, at Corbeil in August 1290; her father ceded Anjou and Maine to Charles as her dowry.

Her children included Philip VI, the first Valois king of France, and Charles II of Alençon, killed at Crécy in 1346, long after her death on 31 December 1299.

en:
Margaret of Burgundy (1290–1315) was the daughter of Duke Robert II of Burgundy and Agnes of France. In 1305 she married Louis, king of Navarre and future Louis X; their daughter Joan became Joan II of Navarre.

Early in 1314 she was accused of adultery in the Tour de Nesle affair and imprisoned at Château Gaillard. When Louis inherited the French crown that November she became queen but stayed in prison, uncrowned. She died there on 30 April 1315, possibly strangled.

Margaret of Burgundy (c. 1231–1277) was the daughter of Duke Hugh IV of Burgundy and Yolande of Dreux. First married to the lord of Mont-Saint-Jean, she was widowed in 1256 and around 1258 married Guy VI, viscount of Limoges.

en:
Marie of Brabant (1254–1322), a daughter of Duke Henry III of Brabant, married Philip III of France in 1274 and was crowned queen in 1275. After the heir Louis died in 1276, she and the chamberlain Pierre de La Brosse accused each other in the ensuing court conflict; at her request Philip had him condemned and executed without trial.

After the Sicilian Vespers of 1282 she pushed Philip to intervene for Charles I of Anjou, helping launch the Aragón Crusade. Widowed in 1285, she lived retired at Les Mureaux until her death. Her children included Louis, Count of Évreux, and Margaret, who married Edward I of England.

布拉班特的玛丽（1254—1322）是布拉班特公爵亨利三世之女，1274年嫁给法王腓力三世，1275年加冕为王后。1276年王位继承人路易死后，她与宫廷侍从长皮埃尔·德·拉·布罗斯在宫廷纷争中相互指责；应她的请求，腓力未经审判便将他处决。

en:
Marie of France (October 1326 – 6 October 1341) was a Capetian princess, the second daughter of King Charles IV and Joan of Évreux. When Charles died in 1328, her mother was pregnant with Blanche, whose birth ended the direct Capetian line and let Philip VI of Valois take the crown.

Their mother nonetheless pressed the sisters' claims to Navarre, negotiating a buy-out with Queen Joan II. Marie died unmarried in Paris on 6 October 1341, aged about fifteen, before the dispute ended.

法兰西的玛丽（1326年10月—1341年10月6日）是卡佩王朝公主，法兰西国王查理四世与埃夫勒的让娜的次女。1328年查理四世去世时，其母正怀着布朗歇；这个遗腹女的出生意味着卡佩直系绝嗣，瓦卢瓦的腓力得以继位，称腓力六世。

en:
Marie de Châteauvillain (c. 1330 – 1366 or 1367) was the younger daughter of Jean III de Châteauvillain and Marguerite de Noyers. Unmarried at her father's death in 1355, she inherited Arc-en-Barrois and Nully when her brother Jean IV was killed at Poitiers in 1356; her sister Jeanne took Châteauvillain.

Marie married Jean II de Bourgogne and became lady of Montaigu. She made her will in October 1366, and her son Jean, born soon afterwards, died in infancy. Leaving no surviving children, she left Arc and Nully to Jeanne and was buried at Arc-en-Barrois.

en:
Mathieu III de Trie (d. 26 November 1344), lord of Araines and Vaumain, was marshal of France as the Valois came to the throne and war with England began. Eldest son of Renaud de Trie, he led a battalion at Courtrai in 1302, where his father fell, and succeeded Jean de Beaumont as marshal around 1320.

He accompanied Charles of Valois in the conquest of Guyenne in 1324 and commanded troops against the Flemings in 1325. In 1328 his brother Guillaume, archbishop of Reims, crowned Philip VI, and in 1339 Mathieu offered the king an army for the invasion of England.

In the Flanders campaign of 1340 he commanded under the king, then shut himself in Tournai, which Edward III was besieging, until the siege ended. He died childless in 1344, full of honours.

马蒂厄三世·德·特里（1344年11月26日卒）是阿莱讷与沃曼的领主，在瓦卢瓦家登上王位、对英战争爆发的年头担任法兰西元帅。他是雷诺·德·特里的长子，1302年率一个军阵参加科特赖克之战，父亲在此役阵亡，约1320年继让·德·博蒙之后出任元帅。

1324年他随瓦卢瓦的查理征服吉耶讷，1325年统军对抗佛兰德人。1328年，他的兄弟、兰斯大主教纪尧姆为腓力六世加冕；1339年，马蒂厄向国王提出出兵征服英格兰。

1340年的佛兰德战役中，他在国王麾下统军，后退守被爱德华三世围攻的图尔奈，直到围城结束。1344年他去世，无嗣，身后荣誉满身。

en:
Napoleon Bonaparte (1769–1821) was a French general who rose to First Consul and then Emperor of the French. He became an artillery officer in 1785, won notice at Toulon in 1793 and crushed a Paris royalist rising in 1795. After beating the Austrians and Italian allies in 1796, he invaded Egypt in 1798, but Nelson destroyed the French fleet at the Nile. Back in France he overthrew the Directory in 1799.

His Civil Code of 1804 reshaped French law, and that December he crowned himself emperor at Notre Dame with a replica of Charlemagne's crown. He won at Austerlitz, Jena and Friedland (1807).

The Peninsular War from 1808 and the Moscow retreat of 1812, costing about sixty thousand men, wore his armies down. After Leipzig he abdicated to Elba in 1814, escaped for the Hundred Days and lost at Waterloo in 1815. He died on Saint Helena in 1821.

拿破仑·波拿巴（1769—1821）是法国将领，后来成为第一执政和法兰西人的皇帝。1785年成为炮兵军官，1793年在土伦成名，1795年炮轰巴黎王党起事。1796年击败奥地利人及其意大利盟友后，1798年远征埃及，但纳尔逊在尼罗河口歼灭法国舰队。1799年11月回国推翻督政府。

1804年《民法典》重塑了法国法律；同年12月2日他在巴黎圣母院戴仿制的查理曼王冠自行加冕，他在奥斯特里茨、耶拿和弗里德兰（1807）取胜。

1808年起的半岛战争和1812年莫斯科撤退（损兵约6万）拖垮了他的军队。莱比锡战败后1814年退位，流放厄尔巴岛后逃回开始百日统治，1815年败于滑铁卢，1821年死于圣赫勒拿。

Nicolas Roger de Beaufort (1340–1415) was a son of Guillaume II Roger and Marie de Chambon and a brother of Pope Gregory XI. First destined for the church, he took up arms after his father was captured at Poitiers in 1356.

In 1371 he joined the papal league against the Visconti of Milan, campaigning with John Hawkwood and fighting at Montichiari in 1373. He married Marguerite de Galard around 1370 and Marthe de Montaut in 1396, after his first wife's death.

尼古拉·罗歇·德·博福尔（1340—1415）是纪尧姆二世·罗歇与玛丽·德·尚邦之子，教皇格里高利十一世之弟。他本准备出任神职，1356年父亲在普瓦捷战役被俘后转而从军。

en:
Odo (c. 857–898), called Odo of Paris, was the eldest son of Robert the Strong and Count of Paris from 882. When Vikings besieged Paris in 885 and 886, he defended the city and broke out to seek aid.

After the emperor Charles the Fat was deposed in 887, the West Frankish nobles chose Odo as king and crowned him in February 888, the first ruler of the Robertian dynasty. He defeated a Viking army at Montfaucon, and died on 1 January 898, leaving the crown to the Carolingian Charles the Simple.

en:
Pepin the Short (c. 714–768), son of Charles Martel, was the first Carolingian king of the Franks, the mayor of the palace who ended the Merovingian line. From Charles Martel's death in 741 he ruled with his brother Carloman, who withdrew to a monastery in 747, leaving Pepin alone.

He consulted Pope Zachary, who ruled the holder of power should bear the king's title. In 751 he deposed the figurehead Childeric III, had him tonsured and sent to a monastery, and was chosen king at Soissons. The cities he won in Italy became the Donation of Pepin to the papacy, the legal basis of the Papal States.

He took Narbonne in 759, ending Muslim rule in Septimania. His nickname, first recorded in the ninth century, is thought to mean he was short. He died in 768 and was buried at Saint-Denis; his sons Charlemagne and Carloman divided the kingdom.

矮子丕平（约714—768）是查理·马特之子，第一位加洛林王朝的法兰克国王，由宫相终结了墨洛温王朝世系。741年查理·马特去世后他与兄长卡洛曼共同治国；747年卡洛曼进修道院，丕平从此独掌大权。

他请教皇扎迦利裁定，对方答以掌握权力的人应当拥有国王的称号。751年，他废黜傀儡国王希尔德里克三世，将其剃发送入修道院，自己在苏瓦松被推举为王。他把在意大利夺得的城市献给教皇，史称“丕平献土”，是教皇国的法律依据。

759年他攻占纳博讷，结束了穆斯林对塞蒂曼尼亚的统治。这个绰号最早见于九世纪的记载，一般认为指他身材矮小。他于768年去世，葬在圣但尼，王国由儿子查理曼和卡洛曼分治。

Péronnelle de Thouars (c. 1330–1397), daughter of Louis I, Viscount of Thouars, and Joan II of Dreux, inherited Dreux in 1365 and Thouars in 1370 after her heirless brothers died. In 1345 she married Amaury IV de Craon, who ruled Thouars jure uxoris until 1373.

In 1378 she ceded Dreux to Charles V in exchange for Benon. She died at Puybéliard on 30 October 1397, ending the five-century rule of the elder House of Thouars.

佩罗内勒·德·图阿尔（约1330—1397）是图阿尔子爵路易一世与德勒的让娜二世之女，兄弟二人无嗣而亡后，她于1365年继承德勒伯国，1370年继承图阿尔子爵领。1345年她嫁给阿马尔里克四世·德·克朗，后者凭妻权统治图阿尔直至1373年。

1378年，她以德勒伯国与查理五世交换伯南领地。1397年10月30日她死于皮贝利雅尔，统治图阿尔五百余年的图阿尔家族长支就此断绝。

en:
Philip of Valois (1336–1375), born in Paris, was the younger son of King Philip VI and Joan of Burgundy. In 1344 his father made him Duke of Orléans with Valois as his apanage, and in 1345 he married Blanche, daughter of Charles IV; the marriage was childless.

He fought beside John II at Poitiers in 1356 but fled the field, then went as a hostage to England under the 1360 Treaty of Brétigny, freed in 1365. He died suddenly in 1375, and his apanage reverted to the crown.

en:
Philip VI of France (1293–1350), called the Fortunate, was the first Valois king. In 1328, when the last Capetian, Charles IV, died, the nobility preferred Charles's paternal cousin Philip to his nephew through his sister, Edward III of England. Philip opened with victory at Cassel the same year, restoring the Count of Flanders.

Relations with Edward soured over Gascony, and in 1337 Philip declared it forfeit. Edward answered by claiming the French crown: the Hundred Years' War had begun. His fleet was destroyed at Sluys in 1340; at Crécy in 1346 he ordered a general attack as evening fell, and barely escaped as his army was annihilated. Calais fell in 1347.

The Black Death then killed Queen Joan and a third of the population. Philip bought the Dauphiné in 1349 and died on 22 August 1350, leaving a divided kingdom to his son John II.

腓力六世（1293—1350），绰号幸运者，是瓦卢瓦王朝的第一位国王。1328年末代卡佩国王查理四世去世，法国贵族选择了查理的父系堂兄腓力，而不是查理的外甥英王爱德华三世。他即位之初在卡塞尔大胜，使佛兰德伯爵复位。

他与爱德华因加斯科涅问题日渐交恶，1337年腓力宣布将其没收，爱德华以主张法兰西王位作为回应，百年战争由此爆发。他的舰队于1340年在斯勒伊斯覆灭；1346年在克雷西，他在傍晚下令全军进攻，军队被歼灭，他本人勉强脱身。加来于1347年陷落。

随后黑死病夺走了王后让娜和三分之一的人口。他于1349年购得多菲内，1350年8月22日去世，把一个分裂的王国留给儿子约翰二世。

en:
Philip I, called the Amorous (c. 1052–1108), was king of the Franks from 1060, son of Henry I and Anne of Kiev, and first ruled under the regency of Baldwin V of Flanders. In 1076 he relieved Dol-de-Bretagne, forcing William the Conqueror to make peace, and he enlarged the royal demesne with the Vexin and Bourges.

In 1092 he repudiated his queen Bertha of Holland and married Bertrada of Montfort, wife of Count Fulk IV of Anjou, for which he was repeatedly excommunicated. He received absolution after public penance in 1104 and died at Melun on 29 July 1108.

en:
Philip II (1165–1223), called Augustus, was the only son of Louis VII and Adela of Champagne. He ruled France from 1180, and that year married Isabella of Hainault, who brought Artois as her dowry; from 1190 he was the first monarch to style himself King of France rather than King of the Franks. He joined the Third Crusade before returning to France.

After years of war with the Plantagenets, his victory at Bouvines in 1214 broke the Angevin Empire and left royal authority unchallenged. He walled Paris and stabilized the crown's finances, dying in 1223.

腓力二世（1165—1223），绰号奥古斯特，是路易七世与香槟的阿黛勒的独子，1180年起统治法兰西。同年他娶埃诺的伊莎贝拉，后者以阿图瓦为嫁妆；自1190年起，他率先自称“法兰西国王”，而非“法兰克人之王”。他参加第三次十字军东征，随后返回法国。

en:
Philip III (1245–1285), called the Bold, was the second son of Louis IX and Margaret of Provence, becoming heir after his elder brother died in 1260. He was beside Louis IX when he died at Tunis in 1270 and was crowned the next year. In 1271 his uncle Alphonse of Poitiers died childless, and Philip annexed the County of Toulouse to the royal domain.

Urged by his uncle Charles of Naples, he led the Aragonese Crusade until disease shattered his army and forced a retreat; he died of dysentery at Perpignan in 1285, succeeded by his son Philip IV.

en:
Philip IV (1268–1314), called the Fair for his looks and the Iron King for his temper, ruled France from 1285. In 1284 he married Joan I of Navarre.

In 1294 he declared Edward I's Gascony forfeit, beginning a war that ended in 1303. Flanders rebelled, and in 1302 its town militia destroyed the French knights at the Battle of the Golden Spurs, though Philip won in the end. In 1307 he had Templars arrested; their Grand Master Jacques de Molay was burned in March 1314.

His taxing of the clergy brought a clash with Boniface VIII and Nogaret's raid on the pope at Anagni in 1303; Boniface died soon after and the papacy moved to Avignon under Clement V. Philip died in November 1314. His sons reigned as Louis X, Philip V and Charles IV, none leaving a surviving son; the Capetian crisis led to the Hundred Years' War.

zh:
腓力四世（1268—1314）因容貌俊美得绰号“美男子”，又因性格刚硬被称“铁国王”，1285年起统治法兰西。1284年他迎娶纳瓦拉的胡安娜一世。

1294年，他宣布英王爱德华一世丧失加斯科涅，战争于1303年结束。佛兰德反叛，1302年城镇民兵在金马刺战役中全歼法国骑士，腓力最终仍取胜。1307年他下令逮捕圣殿骑士，大团长雅克·德·莫莱于1314年3月被烧死。

他向教士征税，引发与卜尼法斯八世冲突，诺加雷1303年在阿纳尼袭击教皇；卜尼法斯不久去世，教廷在克雷芒五世治下迁至阿维尼翁。腓力于1314年11月去世，三个儿子先后即位为路易十世、腓力五世和查理四世，均无存活子嗣，卡佩继承危机最终引发百年战争。

en:
Philip V (c. 1291–1322), called the Tall, was the second son of Philip IV and Joan I of Navarre. After Louis X died in 1316 he took the regency; the posthumous John I lived only days, and Philip had himself crowned. He set aside the claim of Louis's daughter Joan after the Estates General excluded women from the succession, fixing the precedent of the Salic law.

His reforms created an independent Court of Finances, standard weights and measures, and a single currency. He died of dysentery in 1322 leaving only daughters, succeeded by his brother Charles IV.

Peter I of Courtenay (c. 1126–1183) was the sixth son of King Louis VI and Adelaide of Maurienne. He joined his brother Louis VII on the Second Crusade in 1147, and was the only brother to stay loyal during the revolt of 1149–1150.

Around 1150 he married Elizabeth de Courtenay, heiress to the lordships of Courtenay and Montargis, founding the Capetian House of Courtenay. He took the cross again in 1179, died in the Holy Land, and left a son who became Latin Emperor of Constantinople.

Pierre de Mauvoisin, called de Rosny, was a cleric from the Rosny line of the Mauvoisin family of the Île-de-France. He became archdeacon of Brie in the church of Paris in 1343 and, from 1346, a canon of Notre-Dame; he also served as a master of requests in the royal Hôtel.

With his brother Amaury, likewise a Paris canon, he donated family lands to their niece Yde de Beausart and her husband Jean de Saquainville. Pierre died in 1397.

Renaud II de Trie (c. 1260–1316), count of Dammartin, was the son of Count John I of Dammartin. Like his father he served Philip IV in the Flemish wars: at the Battle of the Golden Spurs near Courtrai in 1302 his father was killed while Renaud escaped.

At the victorious Battle of Mons-en-Pévèle in 1304 he killed William of Jülich to avenge his father, and was said to have beheaded him as he fled. He left two sons, Renaud III and John III, who succeeded in turn as counts of Dammartin.

en:
Renaud de Trie was lord of Vaumain and Fontenay-en-Vexin in the Vexin. He married Jeanne de Houdenc and campaigned in Flanders with the royal army, where he was killed at the Battle of the Golden Spurs near Courtrai on 11 July 1302.

His children rose high in church and state. His eldest son Mathieu III became a marshal of France around 1320, his second son Guillaume rose from bishop of Bayeux to archbishop of Reims and, as former preceptor of Philip of Valois, crowned Philip VI at Reims in 1328, and a daughter, Agnès, also called Anne, became abbess of Port-Royal.

他的子女在教会与国家都身登高位：长子马蒂厄三世约于1320年成为法兰西元帅；次子纪尧姆历任贝叶主教与兰斯大主教，曾是腓力·德·瓦卢瓦的导师，1328年在兰斯为瓦卢瓦王朝开国君主腓力六世加冕；女儿阿涅丝（安妮）成为皇港修道院院长。

en:
René Descartes (1596–1650) was a French philosopher and mathematician, born at La Haye, whose method of systematic doubt marks the beginning of modern philosophy. Educated by the Jesuits at La Flèche, he joined the Dutch army at Breda in 1618. In November 1619, in a heated room at Neuburg, three dreams gave him analytic geometry and the idea of applying mathematics to philosophy.

From 1628 he lived in the Dutch Republic. After Galileo's condemnation in 1633 he abandoned his Treatise on the World, and in 1637 published the Discourse on the Method, whose La Géométrie joined algebra to geometry and which set out cogito, ergo sum. The Meditations followed in 1641.

His young daughter Francine died in 1640, and he wept openly. In 1649 Queen Christina of Sweden called him to Stockholm, where early-morning lessons in a cold castle gave him pneumonia; he died on 11 February 1650.

勒内·笛卡儿（1596—1650）是法国哲学家和数学家，生于拉海，他的怀疑方法标志着近代哲学的开端。他在拉弗莱什受耶稣会教育，1618年加入布雷达的荷兰军队。1619年11月他在纽堡一间暖屋里做了三个梦，由此构想出解析几何和把数学用于哲学的想法。

1628年起他定居荷兰。1633年伽利略被定罪后，他放弃出版《世界论》，1637年出版《谈谈方法》，其中《几何学》把代数与几何结合，书中提出“我思故我在”。《第一哲学沉思集》1641年问世。

1640年年幼的女儿弗朗辛去世，他为她公开落泪。1649年瑞典女王克里斯蒂娜召他赴斯德哥尔摩，他在寒冷宫堡里清晨授课，染上肺炎，1650年2月11日去世。

en:
Robert I (c. 860–923), younger son of Robert the Strong, ruled the county of Paris and the March of Neustria under his brother King Odo. He helped defend Paris against the Vikings in 885 and fought them for decades.

In 898 he recognised the Carolingian Charles the Simple as king. When Charles granted Chelles Abbey to his favourite in 922, Robert and the magnates revolted and crowned him king at Reims.

On 15 June 923 Robert's army defeated Charles at Soissons, though Robert himself fell in the fighting. The nobles then elected his son-in-law Rudolph of Burgundy king.

罗贝尔一世（约860—923）是强者罗贝尔的幼子，在兄长厄德国王治下领有巴黎伯国与纽斯特里亚边疆。他于885年参与防守巴黎、抵抗维京人，此后数十年间持续与维京人作战。

898年，他承认加洛林王朝的糊涂查理为王。922年查理把谢勒修道院赐给宠臣，罗贝尔遂与大贵族起兵反叛，在兰斯加冕为王。

Robert of Artois (1326–after 1347) was the fourth son of Robert III of Artois and Joan of Valois, King Philip VI's sister. When his father was condemned for forged documents and fled to England in 1334, the royal government seized his children.

Robert was imprisoned in 1342 and later transferred with his mother and brother James to Château Gaillard. He died in captivity after 1347, probably during the Black Death, leaving no descendants.

en:
Robert II, called the Pious (c. 972–1031), the only son of Hugh Capet, was crowned co-king in 987 and ruled alone from 996 as the second Capetian king of the Franks. Educated by Gerbert of Aurillac, he put aside his first wife Rozala, while his second marriage to his kinswoman Bertha ended after church opposition.

As sole king he maintained alliances with Normandy and Anjou against Odo II of Blois. After a long war against Otto-William he secured the Duchy of Burgundy in 1005, and in 1022 he had heretics burned at Orléans, the first such execution recorded in medieval France. His last years were shaken by the revolts of his sons Henry and Robert from 1025.

“虔诚者”罗贝尔二世（约972—1031）是于格·卡佩的独子，987年被加冕为共治国王，996年起亲政，是卡佩王朝第二位法兰克人之王。他师从欧里亚克的热尔贝，抛弃了第一任妻子罗萨拉；与亲属贝尔特的第二次婚姻则在教会反对后结束。

独自统治后，他维持与诺曼底和安茹的联盟，遏制布卢瓦的厄德二世。经过与奥托-威廉的长期战争，他于1005年取得勃艮第公国；1022年又在奥尔良下令火刑处死异端，这是中世纪法国见于记载的首例此类处决。1025年起，他的儿子亨利与罗贝尔起兵叛乱，动摇了他的晚年统治。

Robert de Foix was a younger son of Gaston I, Count of Foix, and Joan of Artois, and a brother of Count Gaston II. Destined for the Church, he became bishop of Lavaur in 1338 and held the diocese until his death.

His mother had been imprisoned by Gaston II at Foix in 1331. In 1347 Robert secured her release, and she withdrew to Carbonne; he died the next year, in 1348.

en:
Maximilien de Robespierre (1758–1794) was a lawyer from Arras and a leader of the Jacobins, remembered above all for the Reign of Terror. A scholarship took him to the Collège Louis-le-Grand in 1769, where he admired Rousseau. As a lawyer he made his name in the lightning-rod case of 1783.

Elected to the Estates-General in 1789 and the Convention in 1792, he campaigned for male suffrage and against the slave trade, gaining the nickname Incorruptible. He helped justify the execution of Louis XVI in 1793 and joined the Committee of Public Safety. In February 1794 he declared terror to be prompt, severe and inflexible justice.

The Hébertists were guillotined in March and Danton and Desmoulins in April. The Law of 22 Prairial stripped the Revolutionary Tribunal of defence counsel. On 27 July 1794 (9 Thermidor) the Convention turned against him; he was guillotined without trial the next day.

zh:
马克西米连·罗伯斯庇尔（1758—1794）是阿拉斯律师、雅各宾派的领袖人物，以恐怖统治闻名。1769年他靠奖学金进入路易大帝中学，在校推崇卢梭，后来在阿拉斯当律师，因1783年的避雷针案出名。

他1789年入选三级会议，1792年入选国民公会，争取男性选举权、反对奴隶贸易，赢得“不可腐蚀者”的绰号。他参与推动1793年处死路易十六，随后加入公共安全委员会。1794年2月他宣称恐怖就是迅速、严厉、不可动摇的正义。

埃贝尔派3月被处死，丹东和德穆兰4月也被送上断头台。牧月二十二日法令取消了革命法庭的辩护人。1794年7月27日（热月9日）国民公会转而反对他，他次日未经审判便被处决。

Roger d'Armagnac (c. 1277–1339) was a churchman of the comital house of Armagnac: son of Count Géraud VI and Marthe of Béarn, and nephew of Archbishop Amanieu II of Auch. As archdeacon of Agen he was named by Pope John XXII in 1317 the first bishop of the newly created diocese of Lavaur.

In 1319, after his brother Count Bernard VI died, the pope allowed Roger to act as guardian of Bernard's minor children. At Lavaur he enlarged the canons' cloister, consecrated the cathedral's high altar and joined Notre-Dame de Péchaudier to the provostship. He was translated to Laon in 1336 and died in 1339.

罗歇·德·阿马尼亚克（约1277—1339）是阿马尼亚克伯爵家中的教士，为伯爵热罗六世与贝阿恩的玛尔特之子，欧什大主教阿马尼厄二世的外甥。1317年，教皇约翰二十二世任命时任阿让总执事的他为新设拉沃尔教区的首任主教。

en:
Roger I of Blois (died 24 June 1024) was royal chancellor and bishop of Beauvais, the city's first count-bishop. Probably the son of Archbishop Hugh of Blois of Bourges, he recovered the abbey of Coulombs after 986, became chancellor to Hugh Capet and Robert the Pious in 988, and succeeded as bishop of Beauvais around 999.

In 1015 an agreement with Count Odo II of Blois restored to him part of the comital rights over Beauvais, which he then donated to the bishop's church, paving the way for the later prince-bishopric.

Rudolph (c. 890–936) was elected king of West Francia in 923, succeeding his father-in-law Robert I, and spent his reign defending the realm. In 925 Henry the Fowler of East Francia annexed Lotharingia.

From 924 Viking and Norman raiders ravaged the Loire valley and Burgundy; the Normans ambushed and wounded him before he defeated the Vikings. In 933 he granted the Channel Islands to William Longsword, and in 935 drove invading Magyars from Burgundy. He died in January 936, leaving no sons.

拉乌尔（约890—936）于923年被推举为西法兰克国王，继承岳父罗贝尔一世的王位，在位期间始终忙于抵御外敌。925年，东法兰克国王捕鸟者亨利吞并洛泰尔尼亚。

Simon of Thouars (1331–1365) was the second son of Louis I, Viscount of Thouars, and Jeanne II of Dreux, through whom he held the county of Dreux. In 1365 he married Jeanne of Artois, but on his wedding day he was killed in a tournament.

He was buried in the chapel at Eu. After his death Dreux was divided between his sisters Péronnelle and Marguerite, and Péronnelle inherited Thouars when their father died in 1370.

Yolanda of Lusignan (1257–1314), Countess of La Marche, was the daughter of Hugh XII of Lusignan and Jeanne de Fougères. Her father died on Louis IX's Eighth Crusade in 1270, and she inherited Fougères and Porhoët from her mother.

In 1308 she succeeded her brother Guy as countess of La Marche and lady of Lusignan, after the male line of the house had died out. After her death Philip the Fair annexed the county to the crown.

Francis Xavier (1506–1552), a Navarrese cleric, was one of the founders of the Society of Jesus and the first great Jesuit missionary in Asia. In Paris his roommate Ignatius of Loyola turned him from ambition, and in August 1534 they vowed with five others at Montmartre. At the Portuguese king's request he left Rome in 1540, reached Goa in 1542 and preached in India and the Maluku Islands.

At Malacca he met a Japanese samurai who urged him to go to Japan. He landed at Kagoshima in 1549, failed to reach the Kyoto emperor in 1551 but won leave to preach at Yamaguchi, where an abandoned temple became Japan's first lasting church.

Believing China was the key to Japan, he sailed in 1552 but was stopped on Shangchuan Island, dying there on 3 December aged forty-six. Scholars estimate he converted some thirty thousand people. He was canonized in 1622.

方济各·沙勿略（1506—1552）是纳瓦拉的神职人员，耶稣会创始人之一，也是该会在亚洲的第一位伟大传教士。在巴黎，室友依纳爵·罗耀拉扭转了他的世俗野心，1534年8月，两人与另外五人在蒙马特立誓。应葡萄牙国王之请，他1540年离开罗马，1542年抵达果阿，此后在印度和摩鹿加群岛传教。

在马六甲，他遇到一名劝他前往日本的日本武士。1549年他在鹿儿岛登陆，1551年在京都未能见到天皇后，获得在山口传教的许可，一座废弃寺院成为日本第一座长期使用的教堂。

他相信中国是打开日本的关键，1552年启程前往，却被阻在上川岛，12月3日病逝，终年四十六岁。现代学者估计他使约三万人皈依。1622年他被封圣。

en:
Franciscus Gomarus (1563–1641) was a strict Calvinist theologian, born at Bruges to parents who fled the Habsburg Netherlands for the Palatinate in 1578. He studied at Strasbourg, Cambridge and Heidelberg, and from 1587 pastored a Dutch Reformed congregation in Frankfurt until persecution dispersed it in 1593.

In 1594 he took the theology chair at Leiden, where after 1603 he led the opposition to Jacobus Arminius, defending unconditional predestination against the Remonstrants. At the Synod of Dort of 1618–1619 he was the foremost champion of orthodox Calvinism, and he remained an active theologian until his death in 1641.

François de Moulins de Rochefort (c. 1470–1526), born into Poitevin nobility, became a canon in 1500 and later abbot of Saint-Mesmin de Micy. He served as tutor and almoner to the young Francis of Angoulême, schooling the future Francis I in Renaissance learning, and around 1510 composed an illuminated Treatise on the Cardinal Virtues for Louise of Savoy.

After Francis took the crown in 1515 he remained a royal councillor, and in 1519 was appointed grand almoner of France, holding that office until his death in 1526.

弗朗索瓦·德·穆兰·德·罗什福尔（约1470—1526）出身普瓦图贵族，1500年成为议事司铎，后任圣梅曼·德·米西修道院院长。他担任少年昂古莱姆的弗朗索瓦的教师兼施赈神父，以文艺复兴学问塑造了后来的弗朗索瓦一世；约1510年，他为萨伏依的路易丝撰写了带彩绘插图的《枢德论》。

1515年弗朗索瓦即位后他继续担任国王顾问，1519年出任法兰西大施赈官，在任直至1526年去世。

en:
François Martin de Vitré (1575–1631) was a French apothecary and surgeon from Vitré in Brittany. In May 1601 he sailed as surgeon aboard the Croissant, one of two ships equipped by Saint-Malo, Vitré and Laval merchants for the East Indies. After her consort was wrecked in the Maldives, the Croissant traded at Aceh in Sumatra and called at Surat in Gujarat.

On the return voyage in 1603 she was intercepted by the Dutch and Martin was put ashore in England. At Henry IV's bidding he published at Rennes in 1604 the first French account of the East Indies.

弗朗索瓦·马丁·德·维特雷（1575—1631）是布列塔尼维特雷的法国药剂师兼外科医生。1601年5月，他作为外科医生登上‘新月号’，与另一艘由圣马洛、维特雷和拉瓦勒商人装备的船一同驶往东印度。姊妹船在马尔代夫失事后，‘新月号’在苏门答腊的亚齐贸易，并停靠古吉拉特的苏拉特。

1603年返航途中该船被荷兰人拦截，马丁被送上英格兰海岸。应亨利四世要求，他于1604年在雷恩出版了法国人撰写的第一部东印度行记。

en:
Friedrich Schiller (1759–1805) was a German playwright, poet, historian and philosopher, the great dramatist of the Sturm und Drang and, with Goethe, of Weimar Classicism. Born at Marbach in Württemberg and trained in medicine at the duke's Karlsschule, he wrote The Robbers. After leaving his post for its Mannheim premiere in 1782, he was jailed and banned, fleeing Stuttgart that September. In 1785 he wrote the Ode to Joy.

He became Jena's history professor in 1789; a January 1791 collapse, probably tuberculosis, made him a lifelong invalid. From 1794 he grew close to Goethe, once his rival, and they founded the Weimar Theater. Persuaded back to the stage, he wrote Wallenstein, Maria Stuart and William Tell.

France made him an honorary citizen in 1792, and the Duke of Saxe-Weimar ennobled him in 1802. He died at Weimar on 9 May 1805, aged 45; his dramas became German theatre standards.

弗里德里希·席勒（1759—1805）是德国剧作家、诗人、历史学家与哲学家，既是狂飙突进运动的大剧作家，也与歌德一起代表魏玛古典主义。他生于符腾堡的马尔巴赫，在公爵的卡尔学校学医，在校期间写出《强盗》。1782年他擅离职守去看该剧在曼海姆的首演，被关押并遭禁令，当年9月逃离斯图加特。1785年他写下《欢乐颂》。

1789年他出任耶拿大学历史学教授；1791年1月他突然病倒，可能是肺结核，此后终身多病。1794年起他与曾视他为对手的歌德日益亲近，共同创办魏玛剧院。在歌德劝说下他重回戏剧，写出《华伦斯坦》《玛丽亚·斯图亚特》和《威廉·退尔》。

1792年法国授予他荣誉公民称号，1802年萨克森-魏玛公爵封他为贵族。1805年5月9日他在魏玛去世，年仅45岁，他的戏剧成为德国剧院的常演剧目。

en:
Mercenario da Monteverde (c. 1275–1340) was a Ghibelline commander who became tyrant of Fermo in the March of Ancona. He began fighting in 1318, raiding towns around Macerata, and in 1323 defeated the Guelphs under Berardo II da Varano of Camerino at the battle of Osimo.

In September 1328 he took part at Fermo in preliminary peace terms with the papal rector. In 1331 he seized Fermo by a coup and ruled there for ten years, ignoring the repeated demands of Pope Benedict XII that he submit to the Church.

In February 1340 conspirators set on him as he rode with seven companions and killed him. Chroniclers remembered him as a wicked tyrant and enemy of the Church.

梅尔切纳里奥·达·蒙泰韦尔德（约1275—1340）是吉伯林派将领，后来成为安科纳边区费尔莫的暴君。他于1318年开始征战，劫掠马切拉塔一带的城镇；1323年在奥西莫战役中击败卡梅里诺的贝拉尔多二世·达·瓦拉诺率领的圭尔夫派。

1328年9月，他在费尔莫参与了与教廷边区总督的初步和约。1331年，他发动政变夺取费尔莫，统治该城十年，对教皇本笃十二世要求他归顺教会的一再呼吁置之不理。

1340年2月，他与七名同伴骑马出行时遭谋反者袭击身亡。编年史家称他为邪恶的暴君、教会之敌。

en:
Rinaldo da Monteverde, called Rinalduccio (died 1380), was a condottiere and possibly the illegitimate son of the tyrant Mercenario da Monteverde. After his father's murder in 1340 he took refuge in Milan with the Visconti. In 1373 he returned to Fermo with Visconti backing, and in 1376 had himself proclaimed captain of the people.

In 1377 he repeatedly attacked Sant'Elpidio, home of one of his father's killers. His despotic rule was hated, and in 1379 Fermo rose against him. He fled, hired three thousand men and besieged the city, but was repulsed.

He was seized by conspirators who tricked their way into Montefalcone castle on 31 May 1380. On 2 June he and his sons were beheaded in Fermo's main square, where a column carved with the severed heads stood until it was removed in 1419.

里纳尔多·达·蒙泰韦尔德，人称小里纳尔多（？—1380），是雇佣兵首领，可能是暴君梅尔切纳里奥·达·蒙泰韦尔德的非婚生子。1340年父亲遇刺后，他逃往米兰投靠维斯孔蒂家族。1373年，他借维斯孔蒂家族之力返回费尔莫，1376年让人拥立自己为人民长官。

1377年，他多次进攻圣埃尔皮迪奥，那里是刺杀其父的一名谋反者的故乡。费尔莫人痛恨他的专制统治，1379年市民起事反抗。他逃走后雇佣三千人围攻费尔莫，却遭击退。

1380年5月31日，谋反者诈开蒙泰法尔科内城堡将他俘获。6月2日，他和儿子们在费尔莫的公共广场上被斩首；广场上随后立起一根刻着斩首头颅的石柱，直到1419年才被撤去。

Joanna of Burgundy, called Jeanne de Montbéliard (c. 1292–1349), was the eldest daughter of Reginald, Count of Montbéliard, and Guillemette of Neufchâtel. Around 1303 she married Ulrich III, Count of Ferrette, by whom she had two daughters, Joanna and Ursula.

Widowed in 1324, she betrothed Joanna to Albert II of Austria, carrying the County of Ferrette to the Habsburgs, and later married twice more. Inheriting Belfort and Héricourt, she founded a collegiate church and a hospice, and was remembered as the Good Lady of Belfort.

勃艮第的让娜（一称蒙贝利亚尔的让娜，约1292—1349）是蒙贝利亚尔伯爵勃艮第的雷诺与讷沙泰勒的吉耶梅特的长女。约1303年她嫁给费雷特伯爵乌尔里希三世，生有让娜和乌尔苏拉两女。

1324年守寡后，她将女儿让娜许配给奥地利的阿尔布雷希特二世，费雷特伯国由此转入哈布斯堡家族，此后她又两度改嫁。她继承了贝尔福和埃里库尔，创立参事会教堂和济贫院，被称为“贝尔福的好夫人”。

en:
Joanna of Pfirt (c. 1300–1351) was heiress of Count Ulrich III of Pfirt. When her father died in 1324, she inherited his Sundgau lands. By the treaty of Thann she ceded her lands to the Habsburgs, giving them a contiguous territory in southern Alsace, and married Albert II of Austria.

She became Duchess of Austria in 1330, the year polyarthritis began to cripple her husband. Travel pained him, so he sent her on diplomatic missions; in 1336 she mediated peace between the Habsburgs and the House of Luxembourg over the Carinthian inheritance.

After years without a child, she bore Rudolf IV in 1339, aged thirty-nine. Six of her children survived, among them Leopold III, whose birth in 1351 cost her her life.

费雷特的约翰娜（约1300—1351）是费雷特伯爵乌尔里希三世的女继承人。1324年父亲去世后，她继承了桑德戈领地。依照《塔恩条约》，她把领地让与哈布斯堡家族，使其在南阿尔萨斯获得连片土地，并嫁给奥地利的阿尔布雷希特二世。

1330年她成为奥地利公爵夫人，也正是这一年，多发性关节炎开始使她的丈夫行动不便。他出行痛苦，便派她出使；1336年她为哈布斯堡家族与卢森堡家族调解克恩滕遗产争端，促成和约。

多年没有孩子后，1339年三十九岁的她生下鲁道夫四世。她的子女中有六人存活，包括利奥波德三世，1351年生下他后她便去世。

en:
Theobald I of Ferrette (c. 1250 – 1310/11) ruled the County of Pfirt in Upper Alsace from 1275. A younger son of Count Ulrich II, he inherited because the sons of his elder brothers were still underage.

He backed King Adolf of Nassau, who named him imperial advocate in Alsace against Albert of Austria, though after Adolf's defeat his position grew difficult. He left a son, Ulrich III, who succeeded him on his death in 1310 or 1311.

费雷特的蒂博（约1250—1310/1311）自1275年起统治上阿尔萨斯的普菲尔特伯国。他是乌尔里希二世伯爵的幼子，因两位兄长之子尚未成年而继承伯国。

他支持拿骚的阿道夫国王，阿道夫任命他为阿尔萨斯的帝国福格特，与奥地利的阿尔布雷希特对抗；阿道夫战败后，他的处境日益艰难。他留下儿子乌尔里希三世，于1310至1311年间去世后由其子继位。

en:
Ulrich III of Ferrette (c. 1280–1324) succeeded his father Theobald as Count of Pfirt in 1311. He broke with his family's earlier policy and backed the Habsburg Frederick the Fair against Louis of Bavaria in the imperial succession, and Frederick made him provincial advocate of Alsace in 1315.

Dying without a son in 1324, he left his county to his daughters; his widow wed the eldest, Joanna, to Albert II of Austria, and Pfirt passed to the Habsburgs.

费雷特的乌尔里希三世（约1280—1324）于1311年继其父蒂博成为普菲尔特伯爵。他一改家族此前的立场，在帝位之争中支持哈布斯堡的美男子腓特烈、反对巴伐利亚的路德维希，1315年腓特烈任命他为阿尔萨斯的地方福格特。

1324年他去世，没有儿子，伯国由女儿们继承；其遗孀将长女让娜嫁给奥地利的阿尔布雷希特二世，普菲尔特伯国由此并入哈布斯堡家族。

Guigues I of Forez (died after 1137) was the first count of Forez and Lyon from the House of Albon, the son of Guigues-Raymond d'Albon and Ide of Forez, through whom he inherited the county in 1107.

Around 1134 he married Sibylle, lady of Beaujeu, daughter of Lord Guichard III of Beaujeu. In 1137 he donated to Cluny Abbey for his parents' souls; he died after 1137, and his son Guigues II succeeded him.

en:
Guigues II of Forez (1130–1206) was the son of Count Guigues I and Sibylle de Beaujeu. Raised at the court of King Louis VII, he succeeded as count of Lyon and Forez in 1138.

Frederick Barbarossa's Golden Bull stripped him of his rights over Lyon. Restored in 1167 with the backing of Louis VII and Pope Alexander III, he ceded his Lyonnais lands in 1173. He married Guillelmine, and in 1198 he abdicated in favour of their son Guigues III. He died on 6 December 1206.

腓特烈一世的金玺诏书剥夺了他对里昂的权利。1167年在路易七世和教皇亚历山大三世支持下他恢复权利，最终于1173年让出里昂内的领地。他娶吉耶尔米娜为妻，1198年退位，传位于其子吉格三世，于1206年12月6日去世。

en:
Guigues III of Forez (1160–1203), nicknamed Branda, was count of Forez from 1199, when his father Guigues II retired to a monastery. His short reign was spent fighting the lords of Beaujeu.

In 1202 he took the cross for the Fourth Crusade, but instead of following the main army to Constantinople he sailed from Marseille straight for the Holy Land with a company of knights and sergeants. He reached Acre early in 1203 and died shortly afterwards.

Guigues IV of Forez (c. 1199–1241) inherited the county as a child in 1203, when his father Guigues III died on the Fourth Crusade; his uncle Renaud, archbishop of Lyon, acted as regent until 1218. He granted Montbrison a charter in 1223 and founded a collegiate church there the next year.

His marriage in 1226 to Matilda of Courtenay, countess of Nevers, made him count of Nevers. He joined the Barons' Crusade in 1239 and died at Castellaneta in Italy on his way home in 1241.

Guigues VII (c. 1299–1358), from a cadet branch of the house of Albon and a grandson of Humbert I of Viennois through his mother, became count of Forez in 1333 and kept up his father John I's administrative reforms as the Hundred Years' War began.

He stayed loyal to Philip VI of Valois against Edward III in the Flemish campaigns of 1338–1340, and the king's trust brought him command of royal armies in the Midi from 1345 to 1349 and the post of lieutenant-general in western France. In 1349, after France bought the province, he did homage to the Dauphin for his mother's Viennois fiefs.

In 1357, after the Black Prince's raids, he led 400 lances against Robert Knolles's English to help the hard-pressed Béraud II of Auvergne. He died in 1358, and the pillaging reached the heart of Forez; his eldest son Louis I succeeded.

zh:
维戈七世（约1299—1358）出自阿尔邦家族的旁支，外祖父是维埃努瓦的安贝尔一世。1333年他继父亲让一世任福雷伯爵，延续其行政改革，此时百年战争刚刚拉开。

1338至1340年的佛兰德战役中，他始终效忠瓦卢瓦的腓力六世，对抗英格兰的爱德华三世；凭着国王的信任，他于1345至1349年统率王家军队在法兰西南部作战，并出任国王在西部诸省的代理官。1349年法国购得维埃努瓦后，他就母亲一方继承的采邑向王太子宣誓效忠。

1357年黑太子劫掠之后，他亲率400枪骑兵对抗罗伯特·诺尔斯统领的英军，援助陷入困境的奥弗涅的贝罗二世。他于1358年去世，劫掠随即蔓延到福雷腹地，长子路易一世继位。

en:
John I (c. 1275 – 3 July 1333) was count of Forez from 1278, succeeding his father Guigues VI under the regency of his mother, Joan of Montfort. In 1296 he married Alix de la Tour-du-Pin.

He helped bring Lyon under the French crown through the treaty of Vienne in 1312, and organised the Lyon conclave that elected Pope John XXII. From 1317 he sat on the royal council and established a chambre des comptes at Montbrison. His son Guigues VII succeeded him.

en:
Renaud I (1226–1270) was count of Forez from about 1260, succeeding his childless elder brother Guigues V. He was the younger son of Count Guigues IV and Matilda of Courtenay, and in 1247 he married Isabelle of Beaujeu, a widow whose dower brought him several lands.

After Guichard V of Beaujeu died in 1265 he claimed Beaujeu in his wife's name. Other lords contested the succession, which was settled only in 1269, when King Louis IX recognised Isabelle's rights. His eldest son Guigues VI succeeded him in Forez; another son, Louis, inherited Beaujeu.

勒诺一世（1226—1270）约在1260年继无嗣的兄长维戈五世之后成为福雷伯爵，是维戈四世与库特奈的玛蒂尔达的小儿子。1247年，他迎娶博若莱的伊莎贝尔，她是一名寡妇，随嫁妆给他带来多处领地。

en:
John Visconti (c. 1229 – May 1275) was judge of Gallura from 1238. The son of Ubaldo I Visconti of Cagliari, he inherited Gallura under his cousin Ubaldo II's will of 1237 and recovered it from Ubaldo's widow Adelasia and her second husband.

In 1254 he joined Pisa against the judge of Cagliari, and when that giudicato was partitioned in 1258 he annexed a third of its lands. He later fought in the Guelph-Ghibelline wars.

In 1275 Pisa expelled him for joining the Guelphs, and he joined forces with Lucca and Florence to take Montopoli castle. He died at San Miniato the same year, and his son Nino succeeded him.

乔瓦尼·维斯孔蒂（约1229—1275年5月）自1238年起任加卢拉审判官。他是卡利亚里的乌巴尔多一世·维斯孔蒂之子，依堂兄乌巴尔多二世1237年的遗嘱继承加卢拉，并从乌巴尔多的遗孀阿德拉西娅及其第二任丈夫手中夺回领地。

1254年，他随比萨进攻卡利亚里审判官；1258年比萨瓜分该审判官国后，他吞并了其中三分之一的土地。后来他投身圭尔夫派与吉伯林派的战争。

1275年，他因加入圭尔夫派而被比萨驱逐，随后联合卢卡和佛罗伦萨攻占蒙托波利城堡。同年他在圣米尼亚托去世，儿子尼诺继位。

en:
Lamberto Visconti (died 1225) was a Pisan nobleman of the Visconti family and the first of his dynasty to rule in Sardinia. Elena, heiress of the giudicato of Gallura and last of the Lacon-Gunale, chose him as her husband despite Pope Innocent III, her overlord, having planned another match.

In 1209 he and his Pisan allies drove out Comita III of Torres, who had invaded Gallura. In 1215 he landed an army at Cagliari and left his brother Ubaldo to conquer the rest. After Elena died in 1218 he ruled Gallura alone. In 1220 he married Benedetta of Cagliari; he died in 1225 and his son Ubaldo II succeeded him.

en:
Ugolino Visconti, known as Nino (c. 1265 – August 1296), was judge of Gallura from 1275, succeeding his father John. Exiled with his father in 1274, he later returned to Pisa and became a leader of its Guelph party, serving the city as capitano del popolo and podestà.

In 1288 his grandfather Count Ugolino and Archbishop Ruggieri turned against him; Ruggieri drove him into exile and seized his giudicato. Nino fought back with Genoa, Lucca and Florence. He married Beatrice d'Este, his daughter Joanna inherited Gallura, and his friend Dante places him in Purgatorio.

1288年，他的外祖父乌戈利诺伯爵与大主教鲁杰里联手对付他，鲁杰里将他流放并夺取了他的审判官国。尼诺联合热那亚、[ShowLocationName('lucca')]和佛罗伦萨反击。他娶埃斯特的贝阿特丽切为妻，女儿乔万娜后来继承了加卢拉。他的友人但丁在《神曲·炼狱篇》中写到了他。

en:
Ubaldo I Visconti (died 1230) was a Pisan nobleman, son of the patrician Eldizio Visconti and brother of Lamberto. In 1214 he and Lamberto attacked Cagliari and Arborea, and the next year their forces seized the hill overlooking Cagliari, the future Castel di Castro.

By 1217 Ubaldo had forced the judge Benedetta to cede her giudicato and hold it as Pisa's vassal. In 1220 he arranged Lamberto's marriage to the widowed Benedetta and governed Cagliari on his brother's behalf. He died in 1230; his son John later inherited Gallura.

zh:
乌巴尔多一世·维斯孔蒂（1230年卒）是比萨贵族，城市长老埃尔迪齐奥·维斯孔蒂之子、兰贝托的兄弟。1214年，他与兰贝托进攻卡利亚里和阿尔博雷亚，次年军队攻占俯瞰卡利亚里的山丘，即后来的卡斯特罗堡。

到1217年，他已迫使女审判官贝内黛塔割让审判官国，再以比萨封臣的身份领回。1220年，他促成兰贝托与守寡的贝内黛塔成婚，并代表兄弟治理卡利亚里。他于1230年去世，儿子乔瓦尼后来继承了加卢拉。

en:
Ubaldo II (1207–1238) was judge of Gallura from 1225, the son of Lamberto Visconti and Elena of Gallura, last heiress of the Lacon-Gunale. In 1219, when both were twelve, he married Adelasia of Torres under a Pisan alliance that Pope Honorius III tried in vain to annul.

On his uncle Ubaldo I's death in 1230 he seized Cagliari, and in 1236 his influence helped secure Adelasia's election as judge of Torres, which he ruled as her consort. He died of fever at Siligo in 1238, leaving Gallura by will to his cousin John Visconti.

乌巴尔多二世（1207—1238）自1225年起任加卢拉审判官，是兰贝托·维斯孔蒂与加卢拉女审判官、拉孔-古纳莱家族最后的埃莱娜之子。1219年，年仅十二岁的他与托雷斯的阿德拉西娅成婚，这桩服务于比萨结盟的婚事遭到教皇洪诺留三世阻挠，却未能被废除。

1230年叔父乌巴尔多一世去世后，他进占卡利亚里；1236年，他的影响力促成阿德拉西娅当选托雷斯审判官，他也以其夫君的身份统治当地。1238年，他在锡利戈因热病去世，遗嘱将加卢拉传给堂弟乔瓦尼·维斯孔蒂。

en:
Galileo Galilei (1564–1642) was an Italian astronomer, physicist and mathematician. He taught mathematics at Pisa and Padua from 1589 to 1610. In 1609, after hearing of the Dutch spyglass, he built a telescope, and in January 1610 he discovered four moons circling Jupiter, named them the Medicean stars and reported them in his Starry Messenger, and saw Venus's phases, which favoured Copernicus.

In 1616 an Inquisitorial commission declared heliocentrism formally heretical. When his friend Maffeo Barberini became Pope Urban VIII in 1623, he took up the subject again, and his Dialogue of 1632 made its Aristotelian speaker look a fool, seeming to mock the pope.

Summoned to Rome, he was tried in 1633, forced to recant and sentenced to life house arrest. At Arcetri he wrote Two New Sciences (1638) and he died on 8 January 1642. In 1992 Pope John Paul II acknowledged that the Inquisition had erred.

伽利略·伽利莱（1564—1642）是意大利天文学家、物理学家和数学家。他1589年起在比萨、帕多瓦讲授数学，直到1610年。1609年他听闻荷兰望远镜后自制望远镜，1610年1月发现木星的四颗卫星，把它们命名为美第奇星，载于《星际信使》；又观察到金星盈亏，支持哥白尼学说。

1616年，宗教裁判所委员会宣布日心说在形式上属于异端。1623年其友巴尔贝里尼任教宗乌尔班八世后，他重提此说，1632年的《对话》把亚里士多德派发言人写得很可笑，似在嘲弄教宗。

他被召到罗马，1633年受审，被迫撤回主张，判终身软禁。在阿切特里写成1638年出版的《关于两门新科学的对话》，1642年1月8日去世。1992年教宗约翰·保罗二世承认裁判所判错。

en:
Gammala (1263–1302), son of Zhenjin and grandson of Kublai Khan, was raised by Empress Chabi. He guarded the northern border, where rebel princes submitted on his approach and rival envoys sued for peace.

In 1290 Kublai made him Prince of Liang and sent him to govern Yunnan; in 1292 he became Prince of Jin in Mongolia, commanding the Mongol homeland. His son Yesün Temür later took the throne and in 1324 honoured him as Emperor Xianzong.

甘麻剌（1263—1302）是真金之子、忽必烈之孙，由察必皇后抚养。他出镇帝国北境，叛王闻其到来便望风请降，敌对诸王也遣使求和，边境得以安宁。

1290年，忽必烈封他为梁王，派他出镇云南；1292年改封晋王，移镇漠北，统领蒙古本土。其子也孙铁木儿后来登基为泰定帝，1324年追尊他为显宗皇帝。

en:
Alī Mubārak, who ruled as Alauddin Ali Shah (c. 1290–1342), was an independent sultan of Lakhnauti in Bengal. After serving at Delhi, he fell out of favour and went east as army minister to Qadar Khan, the Tughluq governor there. When Qadar Khan died in 1339, Ali killed his deputy and seized the province and took the throne.

He then fought a triangular war with the rulers of Sonargaon and Satgaon, until in 1342 Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah defeated and killed him and took Lakhnauti.

阿拉丁·阿里·沙（约1290—1342），原名阿里·穆巴拉克，是孟加拉拉克瑙蒂的独立苏丹。他早年在德里效力，失势后东赴孟加拉，担任拉克瑙蒂总督卡达尔汗的军政长官。1339年卡达尔汗死后，他杀死副督夺取拉克瑙蒂，自立为王。

此后他与索纳尔冈和萨特冈的统治者三足鼎立、连年交战。1342年，沙姆斯丁·伊利亚斯·沙阿击败并杀死他，夺取了拉克瑙蒂。

en:
Gaykhatu (c. 1259–1295) was the fifth Ilkhan of Persia and a son of Abaqa, governing Anatolia under his brother Arghun before his election as Ilkhan in 1291. A Buddhist with the Tibetan name Rinchendorje, he was generous to Christians.

In 1294 his vizier persuaded him to issue Chinese-style paper money; merchants refused the notes, bazaars shut and trade collapsed, forcing him to withdraw the experiment. In March 1295 his cousin Baydu rose in revolt and Gaykhatu was captured and strangled with a bowstring.

海合都（约1259—1295）是伊儿汗国第五代君主、阿八哈之子，在兄长阿鲁浑在位时总督安纳托利亚，1291年被推举为伊儿汗。他信奉佛教，取藏名仁钦多吉，对基督教徒也十分慷慨。

1294年，在宰相建议下，他仿效元朝发行纸钞，却因商民拒用、市集停闭、贸易瘫痪而被迫废止。1295年3月，堂兄弟拜都起兵反叛，海合都被俘，被弓弦勒死。

Agnes of Meissen (c. 1264–after 1332) was the daughter of Albert II, Margrave of Meissen, by Margaret of Sicily, daughter of Emperor Frederick II. In 1282 she married Henry I the Marvelous, Duke of Brunswick-Grubenhagen, and bore him sixteen children.

Of her daughters, Adelaide married Henry of Bohemia and Adelheid, renamed Irene, married the Byzantine emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos. Her sons each later ruled in Grubenhagen. She died after September 1332.

zh:
迈森的阿格妮丝（约1264—1332年后）是迈森藩侯阿尔布雷希特二世与西西里的玛格丽塔之女，其母是皇帝腓特烈二世的女儿。1282年，她嫁给不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根公爵、号称“奇才”的海因里希一世，为他生育了十六个子女。

女儿阿德莱德嫁给波希米亚国王亨利，另一女儿阿德尔海德改名伊琳娜，嫁给拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡三世·巴列奥略。她的儿子们先后在格鲁本哈根执政。她于1332年9月之后去世。

en:
Albert I, called the Tall (1236–15 August 1279), was the eldest son of Otto the Child, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg, and Matilda of Brandenburg, succeeding his father in 1252. In 1260–1261 his troops fought the Danes in Schleswig for Queen Margaret Sambiria of Denmark, and in 1263 he intervened in the Thuringian Succession War in support of Sophie of Brabant.

In 1269 he divided the Welf lands with his brother John, and when John died in 1277 he became guardian of his young nephew Otto. He backed Ottokar II of Bohemia, defeated at the Marchfeld in 1278. Albert died in 1279 and was buried in Brunswick Cathedral.

zh:
阿尔布雷希特一世，绰号“高个子”（1236—1279年8月15日），是不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公爵“孩童”奥托与勃兰登堡的玛蒂尔德之长子，1252年继父位。1260—1261年，他应丹麦的玛格丽特·桑比里亚女王之请出兵，在石勒苏益格与丹麦人交战；1263年又介入图林根继承战争，支持布拉班特的索菲的诉求。

1269年，他与弟弟约翰瓜分韦尔夫家族领地。约翰于1277年去世后，阿尔布雷希特成为年幼侄子奥托的监护人。他支持波希米亚国王奥托卡二世，后者于1278年在马希费尔德战败。阿尔布雷希特于1279年去世，葬于不伦瑞克大教堂。

Adelaide, called Alessia (c. 1242–1285), was a daughter of Boniface II, Marquess of Montferrat, and Margaret of Savoy. About 1263 she became the second wife of Albert I, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg.

Her sons Henry, Albert and William succeeded their father, and Luther became Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights in 1331. Widowed in 1279, she married Count Gerhard I of Holstein-Itzehoe and died in February 1285.

阿德莱德，又称阿莱西娅（约1242—1285），是蒙费拉托侯爵波尼法乔二世与萨伏依的玛格丽特之女。约1263年，她成为不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公爵阿尔布雷希特一世的第二任妻子。

en:
Balthazar of Brunswick-Grubenhagen (c. 1336 – 1384 or 1385) was a son of Duke Henry II and his second wife Helvis of Ibelin. Following his brothers to the Latin East, he went to the Morea and briefly bore the title Despot of Romania, tied to Angevin claims in Albania and southern Greece.

He married Giacobella Caetani of the Caetani barons of Fondi, in the Kingdom of Naples. He died after 14 January 1384.

不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根的巴尔塔扎尔（约1336—1384/1385年）是格鲁本哈根公爵海因里希二世与第二任妻子伊贝林的海尔维丝之子。他追随诸兄弟前往拉丁东方，在摩里亚短期保有“罗马尼亚专制君主”头衔，该头衔与安茹家族在阿尔巴尼亚和希腊南部的领地主张相连。

他娶了那不勒斯王国丰迪卡埃塔尼男爵家族的雅各贝拉，于1384年1月14日之后去世。

en:
Ernest I of Brunswick-Grubenhagen (c. 1297 – 9 March 1361) was a younger son of Duke Henry I the Admirable, who founded the principality of Grubenhagen in 1291 and left eight sons and eight daughters. Destined for the Church, Ernest after his father's death in 1322 ruled jointly with his brothers Henry II and William.

A pact of 1324 soon gave way to partition: Ernest received the area around Einbeck, Grubenhagen Castle and Osterode, while several towns stayed under joint rule. Henry II withdrew in 1342 and died in 1351, and when William died childless in 1360 Ernest ruled the whole principality.

He had made his son Albert I co-regent in 1359, and when he died on 9 March 1361 Albert succeeded him.

不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根的恩斯特一世（约1297—1361年3月9日）是公爵海因里希一世（“令人敬仰者”）的幼子之一。海因里希一世在1291年建立了格鲁本哈根侯国，留下八个儿子和八个女儿要安置。恩斯特原本准备走教会道路，1322年父亲去世后，他与兄弟海因里希二世、威廉共同统治。

1324年的协议很快变为分家：恩斯特分得艾恩贝克、格鲁本哈根城堡和奥斯特罗德周边地区，部分城镇仍由兄弟共同统治。海因里希二世于1342年退出权力，1351年去世；威廉1360年无嗣去世后，恩斯特统治了整个侯国。

他在1359年立儿子阿尔布雷希特一世为共治者，1361年3月9日去世后，阿尔布雷希特继位。

en:
Henry I, called the Admirable (1267–1322), was a Welf duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg and the first ruler of the principality of Grubenhagen. The eldest son of Duke Albert the Tall, he governed Wolfenbüttel with his brothers until the 1291 partition, when Henry received Grubenhagen, with Einbeck and Osterode, and made Einbeck his residence.

He quarrelled with his brother Albert over their inheritance, but Albert prevailed and Henry withdrew to Grubenhagen. In 1320 the emperor named him Count Palatine of Saxony, and on his death in 1322 his sons divided Grubenhagen among themselves.

海因里希一世，绰号“可敬者”（1267—1322），是韦尔夫家族的不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公爵，也是格鲁本哈根侯国的第一位统治者。他是高个子公爵阿尔布雷希特的长子，起初与兄弟共同治理沃尔芬比特尔；1291年瓜分遗产时，他分得格鲁本哈根，领有艾恩贝克和奥斯特罗德，并以艾恩贝克为驻地。
