en:
Henry II of Brunswick-Grubenhagen (before 1296 – after 1351), called de Graecia, “of Greece”, was the eldest son of Duke Henry I. The principality of Grubenhagen, founded in 1291, could not support Henry I's eight sons and eight daughters. After their father died in 1322 the brothers divided the government, and Henry was left with little, chiefly administering their common property.

In 1327 he joined Emperor Louis IV's coronation journey to Rome, then travelled on to Constantinople and made a pilgrimage to Jerusalem. On Cyprus he met his second wife, Heloise of Ibelin, and returned home in 1331 laden with relics.

He withdrew from rule in 1342 for an annuity, handing his lands to the Archbishop of Mainz. He died at Grubenhagen Castle; his son Otto became the last husband of Joanna I of Naples.

zh:
不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根的海因里希二世（1296年前—1351年后），人称“希腊人”，是公爵海因里希一世的长子。格鲁本哈根是1291年建立的小侯国，养不起海因里希一世的八个儿子和八个女儿。1322年父亲去世后，兄弟几人分割了治权，海因里希所得无几，主要管理兄弟的共有财产。

1327年，他随皇帝路德维希四世前往罗马参加加冕，又继续前往君士坦丁堡，并去耶路撒冷朝圣。他在塞浦路斯结识第二任妻子伊贝林的海尔维丝，1331年携圣物归国。

1342年他放弃统治换取年金，把自己的领地份额交给美因茨大主教。他死于格鲁本哈根城堡；儿子奥托后来成为那不勒斯女王乔万娜一世的最后一任丈夫。

en:
John I of Brunswick-Grubenhagen (c. 1304 – 23 May 1367) was a younger son of Duke Henry I the Miraculous and Agnes of Meissen. Destined for the church, he entered the Mainz cathedral chapter in 1320 and in 1325 surrendered his inheritance to his brothers Henry II, Ernest I and William for a pension of thirty marks a year.

He held church dignities at Hildesheim, Osnabrück and Münster, was cathedral provost of Halberstadt from 1341, and later provost of St. Alexandri in Einbeck, where he died and was buried in 1367.

不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根的约翰一世（约1304—1367年5月23日）是公爵海因里希一世（绰号“怪人”）与迈森的阿格妮丝的幼子。他投身教会，1320年进入美因茨主教座堂参事会；1325年，他以每年30马克的年金为条件，把应继家产让给兄长海因里希二世、恩斯特一世和威廉。

他先后在希尔德斯海姆、奥斯纳布吕克和明斯特担任神职，1341年起任哈尔伯施塔特主教座堂教长，后任艾恩贝克圣亚历山德里修院教长，1367年在艾恩贝克去世安葬。

en:
Otto of Brunswick-Grubenhagen (c. 1320–1399), called the Tarantine, was the eldest son of Duke Henry II. With little to inherit, he became a bold condottiere. His marriage to Violante of Vilaragut, widow of James III of Majorca, made him the richest member of his family.

In 1376 he married Queen Joanna I of Naples, her fourth husband, and became Prince of Taranto, though not king. The couple backed the Avignon pope, and when Charles of Durazzo took Naples in 1381, Otto was captured trying to free the queen; she was strangled in prison in 1382.

Freed in 1384, he won Naples back for Louis II of Anjou in 1387, but, passed over for command, joined the Durazzo side. He died at Foggia in 1399, having rarely seen Grubenhagen again.

zh:
不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根的奥托（约1320—1399），人称“塔兰托人”，是公爵海因里希二世的长子。家里能继承的东西太少，他成了一名大胆的雇佣兵队长。他娶马略卡国王海梅三世的遗孀维拉古特的维奥兰特，由此成为这个贫穷家族中最富有的人。

1376年，他与那不勒斯女王乔万娜一世结婚，这是女王的第四任丈夫；他没有得到王位，却成为塔兰托亲王。夫妇二人支持阿维尼翁教皇，1381年杜拉佐的查理攻占那不勒斯，奥托试图营救女王时被俘，乔万娜于1382年在狱中被勒死。

奥托1384年获释，1387年为安茹的路易二世夺回那不勒斯，却因没被任命为王国总司令，转投杜拉佐一方。他于1399年卒于福贾，此后几乎再没见过格鲁本哈根。

en:
Philip of Brunswick-Grubenhagen (c. 1332 – 1369/70) was a younger son of Duke Henry II, called de Graecia, and his Cypriot wife Helvis of Ibelin. He made his career in the Latin East like his brothers and became Constable of Jerusalem.

By his first wife Helisia de Dampierre he had a daughter Helvis, wife of King James I of Cyprus, and a son John, later Admiral of Cyprus. His second marriage to Alix of Ibelin, widow of King Hugh IV of Cyprus, required a papal dispensation. He died on 4 August 1369 or 1370.

zh:
不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根的菲利普（约1332—1369/1370年）是绰号“希腊人”的格鲁本哈根公爵海因里希二世与塞浦路斯妻子伊贝林的海尔维丝所生之子。他和诸兄弟一样在拉丁东方谋生，官至耶路撒冷统帅。

他与首任妻子埃利萨·德·当皮埃尔生女海尔维丝，后嫁塞浦路斯国王雅克一世；生子约翰，后任塞浦路斯舰队司令。他续娶塞浦路斯国王于格四世的遗孀伊贝林的爱丽丝，这场婚姻需教皇特准。他于1369或1370年8月4日去世。

en:
William of Brunswick-Grubenhagen (c. 1298–1360) was the third son of Henry I the Miraculous and Agnes of Meissen. On his father's death in 1322 he ruled the Principality of Grubenhagen with his brothers Henry II and Ernest I.

The brothers soon divided most of the land, though a 1324 pact kept their chief towns in common. William reigned until his death in 1360; childless, he was succeeded by his brother Ernest I, who united the whole principality.

不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根的威廉（约1298—1360）是海因里希一世（绰号“怪人”）与迈森的阿格妮丝的第三子。1322年父亲去世后，他与兄长海因里希二世、恩斯特一世共同统治狭小的格鲁本哈根亲王国。

en:
Adam Smith (1723–1790) was a Scottish philosopher and economist and the author of The Wealth of Nations. Born at Kirkcaldy and raised by his mother, he studied under Francis Hutcheson at Glasgow and then at Oxford, leaving in 1746.

Edinburgh lectures from 1748 brought him David Hume's friendship, and in 1751 he took a Glasgow chair, later teaching moral philosophy. His Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759) grounded morality in sympathy. In 1764 he resigned to tutor the Duke of Buccleuch in France, meeting Voltaire, then spent nearly a decade writing The Wealth of Nations, published in 1776.

Against mercantilism, it argued that national wealth came from labour, the division of labour and competition rather than gold and silver. From 1778 Smith served as a customs commissioner in Edinburgh, where he died on 17 July 1790; his executors destroyed papers unfit for publication.

亚当·斯密（1723—1790）是哲学家、经济学家，著有《国富论》。他生于柯科迪，由母亲抚养长大，在格拉斯哥大学师从弗朗西斯·哈奇森，后入牛津大学，1746年离开。

1748年起他在爱丁堡讲学，由此结识大卫·休谟；1751年他获得格拉斯哥大学教职，后来讲授道德哲学。1759年的《道德情操论》把道德建立在同情之上。1764年他辞职担任巴克卢公爵的导师同游法国，见到伏尔泰，随后用近十年写成1776年出版的《国富论》。

针对重商主义，他提出国民财富来自劳动、分工与竞争，而非金银。1778年起他在爱丁堡任海关专员，1790年7月17日去世；遗嘱执行人销毁了不宜出版的文稿。

Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Makki (c. 1300 – 1364 or 1365) was the Amazigh head of the Banu Makki dynasty of Gabès, under Hafsid overlordship. When Genoese raiders seized Tripoli in 1354 and demanded fifty thousand gold mithqals for its release, Ahmad negotiated its liberation and paid the ransom himself after the Hafsid sultan sent no help.

The sultan then made him governor of Tripoli. He ruled there until his death, when his son Abd al-Rahman succeeded him.

艾布·阿拔斯·艾哈迈德·伊本·马基（约1300—1364或1365年）是柏柏尔人马基家族的首领、哈夫斯王朝宗主权下的加贝斯统治者。1354年热那亚人攻占的黎波里，索取五万金米斯卡尔赎金；哈夫斯苏丹未发援兵，他出面谈判并自掏家财凑齐赎金，使的黎波里光复。

哈夫斯苏丹随后任命他为的黎波里长官。他在任上去世，其子阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼继位。

en:
Edward of Guelders (1336–1371) was the youngest son of Duke Reginald II and Eleanor of Woodstock. In 1350, aged fourteen and encouraged by his mother, he rose against his elder brother Reginald III at the head of the Bronkhorst faction, and eleven years later his victory at Tiel captured his brother and made Edward duke.

He governed forcefully, allying with Jülich, Cleves and the bishop of Liège. In 1371 he joined his brother-in-law William II of Jülich against Luxembourg at the Battle of Baesweiler.

William won, but Edward was mortally wounded and died in 1371, and Reginald was restored. With neither brother leaving children, the duchy went in 1377 to William of Jülich, son of their half-sister Maria.

海尔雷的爱德华（1336—1371）是公爵雷诺二世与伍德斯托克的埃莉诺的幼子。1350年，年仅十四岁的他在母亲鼓励下，率领布龙克霍斯特派起兵反对兄长雷诺三世；十一年后，他在蒂尔击败支持雷诺的一派，俘获兄长，成为公爵。

他治理有力，与于利希、克莱沃及列日主教结盟。1371年，他随姻兄弟于利希的威廉二世在巴斯韦勒战役中对抗卢森堡一方。

威廉获胜，爱德华却受致命伤，于1371年死去，雷诺三世复位。两兄弟均无子嗣，1377年公国传给他们同父异母姐妹玛丽亚之子于利希的威廉。

Eleanor of Woodstock (1318–1355) was a daughter of Edward II of England and Isabella of France, and a sister of Edward III. In 1332 she married Reginald II of Guelders and became duchess of Guelders. In 1338 her husband expelled her from court, claiming she had leprosy.

Widowed in 1343, she was regent for her son Reginald III until 1344 and later took the veil. She died in 1355 and was buried in the Franciscan church at Deventer; her sons Reginald III and Edward both later ruled Guelders.

Mechteld of Guelders (c. 1324 – 21 September 1384) was the second daughter of Duke Reginald II and Sophia Berthout. She married Godfrey of Loon-Heinsberg in 1336 and, widowed, John, Count of Cleves, in 1348; both marriages were childless.

en:
Reginald I (1255–1326) ruled as Count of Guelders and Zutphen from 1271. In 1276 he married Ermengarde, heiress of Limburg, and ruled that duchy in her right, but she died childless in 1283 and his claim ended with his capture at the Battle of Woeringen in 1288.

In 1286 he married Margaret of Flanders, daughter of Count Guy of Dampierre. Debt after Woeringen left Guelders under Flemish influence. In 1320 his son Reginald II imprisoned him in Montfort Castle, where he died in 1326.

en:
Reginald II of Guelders, called the Black (c. 1295–1343), took power by imprisoning his own father. The son of Count Reginald I, he acted as regent from 1316, locked his father away in 1318 and governed as ‘son of the count’ until succeeding as Count of Guelders in 1326.

In 1332 he married Eleanor of Woodstock, sister of Edward III, and in the early Hundred Years' War became the English king's closest ally among the German princes. In 1338 he excluded Eleanor from court, claiming she had leprosy, and Guelders was raised to a duchy the next year.

He died at Arnhem after a fall from his horse, leaving sons Reginald III and Edward, whose quarrel later split the duchy.

海尔雷的雷诺二世（约1295—1343），绰号“黑人”，靠囚禁生父夺得实权。他是海尔雷伯爵雷诺一世之子，自1316年起摄政，1318年将父亲囚禁，以“伯爵之子”的名义执政，1326年正式继位为海尔雷伯爵。

1332年，他迎娶英格兰国王爱德华三世的妹妹伍德斯托克的埃莉诺；百年战争初期，他是爱德华三世在德意志诸侯中最亲密的盟友。1338年，他声称埃莉诺患有麻风病，将她逐出宫廷；次年海尔雷升格为公国。

他在阿纳姆坠马而死，留下儿子雷诺三世和爱德华，兄弟之争后来撕裂了公国。

en:
Reginald III of Guelders, called the Fat (1333–1371), was the elder son of Reginald II and Eleanor, and his reign was shaped by his younger brother's rebellion. He succeeded as duke in 1343, with his mother acting as regent, and from 1350 his brother Edward contested the duchy.

In 1361 he was beaten at Tiel and shut in Nijenbeek Castle, where he grew so stout that he could not have left even through an open door; legend says the walls had to be cut away to free him.

After Edward was mortally wounded at the Battle of Baesweiler in 1371, Reginald was released and restored, but he died that December without a legitimate heir. His half-sisters then fought the War of the Succession of Guelders.

en:
Alberto Fieschi (c. 1210–c. 1279) was a Genoese Guelph noble, count of Lavagna and a son of Tedisio Fieschi. In 1244 he helped escort his uncle Pope Innocent IV to safety in Genoa, and in 1254 Innocent appointed him captain general of the Church's armies in the kingdom of Sicily, but the campaign failed and his army dispersed.

Exiled during the factional fighting of 1271–1272, he joined his own sons and allies in an attack on Chiavari in 1278. The Genoese soon recovered the town and took Arcola from him.

en:
Ambrogio Boccanegra (c. 1333–1374), nephew of Doge Simone of Genoa, rose to command the fleet of Castile. His father Egidio, admiral of Castile, brought a fleet to Alfonso XI in 1341, and Ambrogio settled at Palma del Río. When Peter the Cruel executed Egidio in 1367 for favouring his rival Henry of Trastámara, Ambrogio fled to Henry's exiled court in France.

After Henry took the throne in 1369 he recovered Palma. As admiral he beat the Portuguese at the Guadalquivir in 1371, and in 1372 destroyed the English fleet off La Rochelle and captured the Earl of Pembroke. In 1373 he struck at Lisbon and forced Portugal to yield. He died in 1374.

安布罗焦·博卡内格拉（约1333—1374）是热那亚总督西蒙内之侄，后来执掌卡斯蒂利亚舰队。他的父亲、卡斯蒂利亚海军统帅埃吉迪奥于1341年率舰队投奔国王阿方索十一世，他随之定居帕尔马-德尔里奥。1367年，“暴君”佩德罗因埃吉迪奥倾向自己的对手特拉斯塔马拉的恩里克而将其处死，安布罗焦逃往法国，投奔恩里克流亡的宫廷。

1369年恩里克登上王位，他收回帕尔马。1371年他出任海军元帅，在瓜达尔基维尔河口击败葡萄牙人；1372年又在拉罗谢尔海战中歼灭英格兰舰队并俘虏彭布罗克伯爵。1373年他进攻里斯本，迫使葡萄牙屈服。他于1374年去世。

en:
Andrea Doria (1466–1560), Prince of Melfi, was born at Oneglia into an old Genoese noble family. Orphaned young, he became a mercenary in the papal guard and then a naval commander fighting Turks and Barbary corsairs for France.

In 1528 he entered Charles V's service, drove the French from Genoa and restored the Republic, refusing the dogeship for the title Father of the Fatherland. His reforms made the doge a two-year office and narrowed rule to the patrician councils, a settlement that survived until 1797. His fleet helped secure the imperial sea routes between Spain and Italy. He died at Genoa in 1560.

安德烈亚·多里亚（1466—1560），梅尔菲亲王，出生于奥内利亚一个古老的热那亚贵族家庭。他幼年丧亲，先在教皇卫队当雇佣兵，后成为海军将领，为法国与土耳其人和柏柏尔海盗作战。

en:
Anselm II of Savona was a noble of the Frankish Aleramici dynasty and margrave of Savona and Tortona. A son of Margrave Anselm I and Gisla of Milan, he and his brothers jointly ruled the Aleramic mark after their father died before 999. In 1014 Emperor Henry II named him and his brother Oberto in imperial diplomas.

He married his cousin Adela of Milan; their sons included Otto, called Teuto, who married Bertha of Turin. He was dead by 1055, when his widow named him as deceased.

en:
Benedetto II Zaccaria (died c. 1330) was a Genoese noble of the Zaccaria house and co-lord of Chios. When his kinsman Paleologo Zaccaria died in 1314 he ruled Chios and other Aegean islands jointly with his brother Martino. After Martino forced him into retirement around 1325, he appealed to the Byzantine emperor Andronikos III.

An imperial fleet seized Chios and captured Martino in 1329, and Benedetto returned as imperial prefect. He married Ginevra Doria and died childless about 1330, after which the island was annexed to the empire.

贝内代托二世·扎卡里亚（约1330年卒）是热那亚扎卡里亚家族的贵族、希俄斯共同领主。1314年亲族帕莱奥洛戈·扎卡里亚死后，他与兄长马蒂诺共同统治希俄斯和爱琴海上的其他岛屿。约1325年，马蒂诺迫使他退隐，他便向拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡三世求援。

en:
Bernabò Doria (c. 1255–1325), also called Bernabino, was a Genoese statesman, lord of Sassello and Logudoro, son of Branca Doria and Caterina Zanche. In 1275 he married Eleonora Fieschi, tying the Ghibelline Doria to the Guelph Fieschi. He managed his family's Sardinian estates, concluding truces with Arborea and Sassari. After Opizzino Spinola's 1306 rising he briefly shared rule in Genoa, and in 1311 welcomed Henry VII to Italy.

Exiled when the Guelphs seized Genoa in 1317, he joined the Aragonese siege of Villa di Chiesa in 1323 and mediated Pisa's surrender at Cagliari in 1324.

贝尔纳博·多里亚（约1255—1325年8月前），又称贝尔纳比诺，是热那亚政治家、萨塞洛与洛古多罗领主，布兰卡·多里亚与卡泰丽娜·赞凯之子。1275年他娶埃莱奥诺拉·菲耶斯基，使吉伯林派多里亚家族与圭尔夫派菲耶斯基家族联姻。他掌管家族在撒丁岛的产业，与阿尔博雷阿和萨萨里订立休战协定。1306年奥比齐诺·斯皮诺拉起义后，他一度在热那亚共同执政；1311年他迎接亨利七世南下意大利。

1317年圭尔夫派夺取热那亚后他被迫流亡，1323年加入阿拉贡军队围攻基耶萨镇，1324年又在卡利亚里斡旋比萨受降事宜。

en:
Boarello (or Bovarello) Grimaldi was a Genoese nobleman of the Guelph party, son of Ingo Grimaldi and brother of Luca Grimaldi. After the Savona revolt of 1248–1251 the two brothers took control of the castles of Stella and Andora. In 1252 Boarello served as Genoese ambassador to Charles I of Provence.

In 1269 Charles, by then king of Naples, charged him and Luca with receiving the ambassadors of the Abbasid caliph Al-Hakim I at Genoa. A Genoese document of April 1275 already names him as dead.

en:
Boniface del Vasto (c. 1055–c. 1125) was margrave of Savona and Western Liguria and founder of the del Vasto branch of the Aleramici. He took power after his brothers died in battle and confirmed Savonese privileges in 1084.

After Adelaide of Susa died in 1091, he fought Humbert II of Savoy for the Turin mark and seized Alba, Asti and Turin. In his 1125 will he left his extensive lands to his sons.

The chronicler Geoffrey Malaterra called him the most famous marquis in Italy, and by Agnes of Vermandois he fathered Manfred of Saluzzo and Henry, ancestor of the Del Carretto.

博尼法乔·德尔·瓦斯托（约1055—约1125）是萨沃纳与西利古里亚侯爵，阿莱拉米奇王朝德尔·瓦斯托支系的开创者。他在兄弟们战死后掌权，于1084年确认萨沃纳人的特权。

1091年苏萨的阿德莱德去世后，他与萨伏依的翁贝托二世争夺都灵边区，夺取阿尔巴、阿斯蒂和都灵。1125年的遗嘱中，他将广阔领地留给儿子们。

编年史学家杰弗里·马拉特拉称他为“意大利最负盛名的侯爵”；他与韦芒杜瓦的阿格尼丝生下萨卢佐的曼弗雷德和德尔·卡雷托家族的祖先亨利。

en:
Branca Doria (c. 1233–1325) was a Genoese patrician with lands and offices in Sardinian Logudoro. By marrying Caterina, daughter of Michele Zanche, governor of Logudoro, he claimed the region, and around 1275 he had his father-in-law murdered at a banquet in the Nurra and seized his power.

Dante places his soul in Hell while still alive, in the Ptolomaea of Inferno Canto XXXIII, for betraying a guest. When the Ghibellines were expelled from Genoa in 1317 he directed his politics from Savona, and he may have been killed in Sardinia in 1325 as Aragonese power grew.

布兰卡·多里亚（约1233—1325）是热那亚多里亚家族贵族，在撒丁岛卢古多罗拥有领地和官职。他迎娶卢古多罗统治者米凯莱·赞凯之女卡泰丽娜以取得对该地区的权利，约1275年在努拉的一次宴会上背信杀害岳父并夺权。

但丁在《神曲·地狱篇》第三十三歌中把尚未去世的他直接投入第九圈托勒密环，与背叛宾客者同列。1317年吉伯林派被逐出热那亚后，他在萨沃纳主持政治活动；1325年，随着阿拉贡势力扩张，他可能在撒丁岛被杀。

但丁在《神曲·地狱篇》第三十三歌中把尚未去世的他直接投入第九圈托勒密环，与背叛宾客者同列。1317年吉伯林派被逐出热那亚后，他在萨沃纳主持政治活动；1325年，随着阿拉贡势力扩张，他可能在撒丁岛被杀。

en:
Brancaleone Doria was a Genoese nobleman, the son of Bernabò Doria and Eleonora Fieschi and grandson of Branca Doria. In 1305 his father emancipated him and arranged his marriage to Isotta Malaspina, reuniting the two halves of the Apennine lordship of Molare, whose castle was made over to him.

Isotta died in 1310. He later pursued the family's interests in Sicily and Sardinia, marrying the heiress Costanza Chiaramonte, and in 1335 was appointed governor of Sardinia.

布兰卡莱奥内·多里亚是热那亚贵族，贝尔纳博·多里亚与埃莱奥诺拉·菲耶斯基之子、布兰卡·多里亚之孙。1305年父亲为他解除监护，安排他迎娶伊索塔·马拉斯皮纳，借此把亚平宁山区莫拉雷领地的两半合为一体，莫拉雷城堡也转交给他。

伊索塔于1310年去世。后来他在西西里和撒丁岛经营家族利益，娶了女继承人科斯坦扎·迪·基亚罗蒙特，并于1335年被任命为撒丁岛总督。

en:
Carlo Fieschi (c. 1269–after 1329) was a Genoese Guelph statesman of the counts of Lavagna, son of Nicolò Fieschi and Leonora and a counselor of Charles I of Anjou. In 1311 he attended Emperor Henry VII in Genoa and received imperial confirmation of Pontremoli with his brothers. From 1314 to 1319 he fought Franceschino Malaspina of Mulazzo.

In December 1317, with Gaspare Grimaldi, he took power in Genoa as capitano del popolo, placing the republic under Pope John XXII and Robert of Naples and forcing the Ghibelline exiles to surrender in February 1319.

卡洛·菲耶斯基（约1269—1329年后）是拉瓦尼亚伯爵支系的热那亚圭尔夫派政治家，尼科洛·菲耶斯基与莱奥诺拉之子，曾任安茹的查理的顾问。1311年他在热那亚觐见皇帝亨利七世，与兄弟们获皇帝确认蓬特雷莫利的领有权。1314至1319年，他与穆拉佐侯爵弗兰切斯基诺·马拉斯皮纳交战。

1317年12月，他与加斯帕雷·格里马尔迪一同出任平民首领，在热那亚掌权，将共和国置于教皇约翰二十二世和那不勒斯国王罗贝托的保护之下，并于1319年2月迫使吉伯林派流亡者投降。

en:
Corrado Doria (1250–1322) was a Genoese nobleman of the Ghibelline Doria dynasty, son of the capitano del popolo Oberto Doria and Niccolosia Cybo. He served in the Genoese fleet that crushed Pisa at the battle of Meloria in 1284.

From his father he inherited the county of Loano on the Ligurian coast, which Oberto had acquired in 1263, ruling as Corrado I, first Doria lord of Loano and founder of the Loano branch of the family.

Corrado Spinola was a Genoese Ghibelline noble of the Spinola family and the son of Oberto Spinola, co-ruler of Genoa. In 1284 he fought in the Battle of Meloria, where the Genoese fleet destroyed Pisan sea power at the height of Genoa's political power.

Continuing the Spinola-Doria diarchy, Corrado served as capitano del popolo of Genoa from 1295 to 1299, first with Corrado Doria and later with Lamba Doria. He died in 1304, and his son Opizzino was elected captain of the people in 1306.

en:
Domenico Fregoso (1325–1390) was the first doge of the Fregoso family, a merchant and financier who sat on the republic's First Council from 1355 and led the fight against the Fieschi. In 1370, as one of the two vicars of the people, he gathered the crowd against Doge Gabriele Adorno's new taxes; Adorno was deposed and Domenico made doge the same day.

His brother Pietro's fleet seized Famagusta from the kingdom of Cyprus, a port Genoa then held for over a century. In 1378, with the people roused again by Antoniotto Adorno, he was deposed and exiled, and he fought Venice in the War of Chioggia.

When his son Giacomo became doge in 1390, he returned to Genoa after twelve years of exile. He died there later that same year.

多梅尼科·弗雷戈索（1325—1390）是弗雷戈索家族的首任总督，出身商人与金融家，1355年起进入共和国首要会议，带头对抗菲耶斯基家族。1370年，他作为两名人民副使之一召集民众，反对总督加布里埃莱·阿多尔诺新开的税；阿多尔诺当天被废，多梅尼科同日就任总督。

其弟彼得罗的舰队从塞浦路斯王国手中夺取法马古斯塔，这座港口此后被热那亚占据一个多世纪。1378年，民众在安东尼奥托·阿多尔诺的鼓动下再度聚集，他被废黜并遭放逐，流亡期间在基奥贾战争中对抗威尼斯。

1390年其子贾科莫出任总督，他在流亡十二年后返回热那亚，并于同年去世。

Dorino I Doria was a Genoese patrician of the Doria family and lord of Loano, a small fief on the Ligurian coast enclosed within Genoese territory.

He was the son of Corrado Doria, one of the captains of liberty who overthrew Guelph rule in Genoa and fought beside his father at the naval victory of Meloria in 1284. His son Dorino II also became lord of Loano.

Oberto Doria, known as Dorino II, was a Genoese nobleman of the Doria branch of Loano and the son of Dorino I Doria and Ginevra. He succeeded his father as lord of Loano in 1350 and ruled the coastal lordship until 1375, jointly with his kinsmen Pietro I and Dorino III.

He married Violante Doria, who after his death married Luca Doria. Their daughter Valentina married Francesco II Gattilusio, lord of Lesbos, and their son Pietro died before February 1390, leaving a son named Corrado.

en:
Egidio Boccanegra, called Barbanera (c. 1300–1367), was a Genoese admiral and brother of Simone Boccanegra, Genoa's first doge. In 1340 he brought three galleys to Philip VI's fleet at Sluys and warned the French commanders that their packed lines left no room to manoeuvre; they ignored him, the English won, and he was one of the few captains to escape.

That year the Marinids wrecked Castile's fleet, and Alfonso XI hired Genoese galleys and made him admiral. In 1342 Egidio beat the Marinid squadrons, then blockaded Algeciras until it surrendered in 1344.

He later fought for Peter I against Aragon, but in 1366 he went over to Henry of Trastámara and seized the king's treasure. After Peter regained Castile at Nájera in 1367, Egidio was arrested and publicly executed at Seville.

埃吉迪奥·博卡内格拉，绰号“黑胡子”（约1300—1367），是热那亚海军将领，也是热那亚首任总督西蒙·博卡内格拉之弟。1340年，他率三艘桨帆船加入法王腓力六世的斯勒伊斯舰队，警告法军密集阵形没有周旋余地；对方不听，英军大胜，他是少数脱身的指挥官之一。

同年马林王朝全歼卡斯蒂利亚舰队，阿方索十一世遂雇用热那亚桨帆船，并任命他为海军元帅。1342年，埃吉迪奥击败马林舰队，随后封锁阿尔赫西拉斯，至1344年该城投降。

他后来在对阿拉贡的战争中为佩德罗一世效力，1366年却转投特拉斯塔马拉的恩里克，截获了国王的财宝。1367年佩德罗在纳赫拉战役后重掌卡斯蒂利亚，埃吉迪奥被捕，并在塞维利亚被公开处决。

Eleonora Fieschi, also called Eliana (c. 1254–1337), was a Genoese noblewoman of the counts of Lavagna, daughter of Federico Fieschi and niece of Cardinal Ottobono, the future Pope Adrian V.

In 1275 she married Bernabò Doria, eldest son of Branca Doria, a match Branca arranged soon after he murdered Michele Zanche, reconciling the Guelph Fieschi with the Ghibelline Doria. Her father's will of 1303 named her his heiress, and she was still alive as Bernabò's widow in 1325.

en:
Federico da Pagana was born in Genoa in 1315, the son of Nicolò da Pagana. A Ghibelline merchant tied to the common people, at twenty-five he was among the electors of the first doge, Simone Boccanegra, and he later served the republic as ambassador to Italian courts and as envoy to Emperor Charles IV in Vienna.

In April 1383 Doge Domenico Fregoso fled the city, and almost by popular acclaim Federico was elected the ninth doge on 7 April. He was deposed the very same day, and Leonardo Montaldo took his place. Federico returned to trade and lived out his life as a merchant, dying in Genoa in 1406.

Federico Fieschi (c. 1232–1303) was a Genoese nobleman of the counts of Lavagna, a son of Tedisio Fieschi and Simona della Volta and a brother of Pope Adrian V. He married Chiara, and through his daughter Eleonora's marriage in 1275 to Bernabò Doria he tied the Guelph Fieschi house to the Ghibelline Doria dynasty.

In 1303, at Sarzana, he made his will, naming Eleonora his heiress; he was later buried in Genoa at San Francesco di Castelletto.

en:
Francesco Giustiniani Garibaldo (Genoa, 1336–1408) was a Genoese merchant whose family business reached across the Maona of Chios and the eastern Mediterranean. In July 1393 the dogeship changed hands almost by the hour: Pietro Fregoso forced Antonio Montaldo to abdicate and was himself quickly displaced by Clemente Promontorio, who in turn gave way the next day.

The noble and popular factions then compromised on Francesco, seen as acceptable to all, and elected him doge on 16 July. He ruled for fourteen days before the Montaldo faction returned on 30 July and put Antonio back in office. Francesco left the ducal palace without protest, a sign historians read as proof he had not sought the post.

He went back to the family business. He later served as podestà of Savona and procurator of the Banco di San Giorgio.

弗朗切斯科·朱斯蒂尼亚尼·加里巴尔多（1336—1408）是热那亚商人，其家族的生意遍及希俄斯马奥纳和地中海东部。1393年7月，总督之位几乎按小时易手：彼得罗·弗雷戈索逼安东尼奥·蒙塔尔多退位，自己很快又被克莱门特·普罗蒙托里奥取代，普罗蒙托里奥次日也被迫让位。

贵族派与平民派最终妥协，选定各方都能接受的弗朗切斯科，于7月16日推举他出任总督。他只在任十四天，7月30日蒙塔尔多派重新得势，安东尼奥复位。弗朗切斯科毫无异议地离开总督府，史家据此认为他本无意于此位。

他回去打理家族生意。后来他担任过萨沃纳行政长官和圣乔治银行的代理人。

en:
Gabriele Adorno (c. 1320–1383) was the fifth doge of Genoa, a Ghibelline from a Genoese merchant family. Elected doge on 14 March 1363 after Simone Boccanegra's death, he shared offices evenly between Guelfs and Ghibellines and exiled the Boccanegra heirs for good.

With the Visconti pressing on Genoa, he sent his brother Giannotto to Avignon to seek the pope's support. His treaty of 1365 with Peter I of Cyprus opened the way to Genoese rule on the island; Genoa also occupied Soldaia in Crimea and made trade treaties with Aragon and Portugal. Taxes wore down his standing even after he became imperial vicar in 1368.

On 13 August 1370 Domenico Fregoso turned a public assembly against him, and Adorno fled; Fregoso was elected doge that same day. Adorno was later held at Voltaggio and died in 1383.

加布里埃莱·阿多尔诺（约1320—1383）是热那亚第五任总督，吉伯林派，出身热那亚商人家庭。1363年3月14日，西蒙·博卡内格拉去世后，他当选总督，在归尔甫与吉伯林两派间均分官职，并将博卡内格拉后裔永久流放。

面对维斯孔蒂家族的压力，他派弟兄詹诺托赴阿维尼翁，向教皇求援。1365年，他与塞浦路斯的彼得一世订约，为热那亚统治该岛开路；热那亚还占领了克里米亚的索尔达亚，又与阿拉贡和葡萄牙立约。1368年他取得皇帝代理人头衔，税负仍消磨他的威望。

1370年8月13日，多梅尼科·弗雷戈索在集会上煽动民众反对他，阿多尔诺出逃，弗雷戈索当天当选总督。阿多尔诺后被囚于沃尔塔焦，1383年去世。

en:
Gabriele Grimaldi (born c. 1302) was a Genoese nobleman, son of Gaspare Grimaldi, capitano del popolo of Genoa in 1317, and brother of Antonio Grimaldi of Antibes. King Robert of Anjou enfeoffed him and Antonio with the Calabrian fief of Policastro, confiscated from the Ruffo family.

He served the Angevin crown as grand justiciar of the Kingdom of Naples and viceroy of Abruzzo. In 1338 he joined Antonio in buying lands and houses at Monaco.

加布里埃尔·格里马尔迪（约1302年生）是热那亚贵族，1317年热那亚平民长官加斯帕雷·格里马尔迪之子，昂蒂布的安东尼奥·格里马尔迪的兄弟。那不勒斯国王安茹的罗贝尔将抄没自鲁福家族的卡拉布里亚波利卡斯特罗封邑授予他与安东尼奥。

en:
Galeotto Adorno was a Genoese merchant of the Adorno house, a family at the centre of Genoese politics in the fourteenth century; Gabriele Adorno of the same house was elected doge of Genoa in 1363.

Around 1343 Galeotto joined a trading venture to Cathay, carrying eight hundred silver sommi invested in precious goods, among them a crown, a necklace and pearls. At Khanbaliq he gathered the effects left by Luchino Malrasi, a Piacentine merchant who had died in the Chinese capital, and on his return to Genoa handed them to Malrasi's mother and settled with his backers, restoring their capital together with a share of the profits.

A Genoese notarial instrument of 10 July 1343 records him bequeathing a hundred lire to his sister Marinetta, widow of Antonio Embrone, towards a new marriage.

加莱奥托·阿多尔诺是热那亚商人，出自阿多尔诺家族，该家族在14世纪的热那亚政坛身居核心，同家族的加布里埃莱·阿多尔诺于1363年当选热那亚总督。

约1343年，他加入一支前往中国的商队，携带八百枚投资于珍宝的银索姆，其中包括一顶王冠、一条项链和若干珍珠。在汗八里，他收殓了皮亚琴察商人卢基诺·马尔拉西遗留在这座中国都城的遗物，返回热那亚后将其交还死者的母亲，并与出资人结清账目，在本金之外添上一份利润。

1343年7月10日的一份热那亚公证文书记载，他留给已是安东尼奥·恩布罗内遗孀的妹妹玛丽内塔一百里拉，以充再嫁之资。

Galeotto Spinola (born c. 1284) was a Genoese nobleman of the Spinola di Luccoli branch, son of Odoardo Spinola, grand admiral of the Kingdom of Sicily. Around 1310 he raided shipping from the castle of Monaco.

In 1335, after the Ghibellines overthrew Angevin rule in Genoa, he was elected capitano del popolo alongside Raffaele Doria, holding office until the 1339 rising that made Simone Boccanegra the first doge. He founded Spinola lines including that of Tassarolo.

en:
Gaspare Grimaldi was a Genoese Guelph leader, son of Gabriele Grimaldi, lord of the castle of Stella. In 1296 he was expelled from Genoa by the Ghibelline captains and his goods confiscated, returning after the peace of 1302. In 1310 he helped defeat Opizzino Spinola at Sestri Ponente.

In 1317 he and Carlo Fieschi were elected captains of the people, ending decades of Ghibelline rule, and in 1318 they handed power to Robert of Anjou, from whom Gaspare received fiefs in the kingdom of Naples. He was still alive in 1331.

en:
Giovanna Novella Malaspina, called Franceschina (Fosdinovo, c. 1320 – Mantua, c. 1385), was the daughter of the condottiero Spinetta Malaspina, known as il Grande, lord of Fosdinovo, and of Beatrice Visconti. She married the Genoese nobleman Lucemburgo Spinola, by whom she had a son.

In 1340 she became the third wife of Luigi I Gonzaga, the seventy-two-year-old first capitano del popolo of Mantua, and bore him five children.

en:
Giovanni da Valente (Genoa, c. 1280–1360) was a banker's son from the merchants and bankers who stood against the Genoese nobility. When Giovanni da Murta died of plague, electors proclaimed him the third doge on 9 January 1350.

The war he inherited was a hard one: Aragon and Venice allied against Genoa in January 1351, and a Bosphorus battle in February 1352 left both fleets bloodied. He answered with an alliance with Louis I of Hungary. Then in August 1353 Antonio Grimaldi's fleet was shattered off Alghero, and Genoa lost its hold on the Tyrrhenian Sea.

On 8 October Giovanni resigned. Squeezed between sea and mountains, the Republic submitted to the Visconti of Milan, and he lived out his days in private.

zh:
乔万尼·达·瓦伦特（约1280—约1360）生于热那亚，是银行家之子，属于与热那亚贵族相对立的商人和银行家阶层。乔瓦尼·达·穆尔塔死于瘟疫后，选举人于1350年1月9日宣布他为第三任总督。

他接手的是一场硬仗：1351年1月阿拉贡与威尼斯结盟对付热那亚，1352年2月博斯普鲁斯海峡一战，双方舰队都损失惨重。他随后与匈牙利国王拉约什一世结盟。1353年8月，安东尼奥·格里马尔迪的舰队在阿尔盖罗海外覆没，热那亚失去对第勒尼安海的控制。

乔万尼于10月8日辞职。共和国被夹在海与山之间，随后臣服于米兰的维斯孔蒂家族，他此后过着私人生活。

en:
Giovanni da Murta was born in the village of Murta in the Polcevera valley near Genoa to a wealthy commoner family. A banker, he was elected the second doge of Genoa on 25 December 1345, after Simone Boccanegra stepped down, as a man backed by no faction amid feuds among the noble houses.

Against the Grimaldi he had a private Maona equip a fleet of twenty-five to twenty-nine galleys under Simone Vignoso, and they fled to Marseille. He then sent the fleet to retake Chios. When Vignoso came home without the payment promised him, Giovanni gave him and his Maona partners the right to administer the island.

He also worked to strengthen Genoese rule in Corsica, and chose not to put his own initials on the coinage. Plague killed him on 6 January 1350, and he was buried in San Lorenzo.

zh:
乔瓦尼·达·穆尔塔生于热那亚附近波尔切韦拉河谷的穆尔塔村，出身富裕平民家庭。他本是银行家，1345年12月25日西蒙·博卡内格拉退位后，作为不属于任何派系的人选当选热那亚第二任总督，当时贵族家族之间纷争不断。

为对付格里马尔迪家族，他让一个私人马奥纳出资装备了二十五至二十九艘桨帆船的舰队，交给西蒙内·维尼奥索指挥，格里马尔迪家族逃往马赛；随后他又派这支舰队去收复希俄斯岛。维尼奥索归来后未获约定的报酬，乔瓦尼遂将岛屿经营权授予他和马奥纳的合伙人。

他还着力巩固热那亚在科西嘉的统治，并选择不在钱币上铸自己姓名的首字母。1350年1月6日，他死于鼠疫，葬于圣洛伦佐大教堂。

en:
Giovanni Fieschi was a Genoese cleric of the noble Fieschi family, counts of Lavagna. A papal chaplain and auditor of the Roman Rota, he was elected bishop of Vercelli in 1348, defending his church's rights against Galeazzo Visconti.

In 1377 the count of Savoy arrested him and held him at Biella. Pope Urban VI made him a cardinal priest in September 1378. He died at Rome in 1384.

乔瓦尼·菲耶斯基是出身拉瓦尼亚伯爵菲耶斯基家族的热那亚教士。他曾任教宗专职神父与罗马圣轮法院审计员，1348年当选韦尔切利主教，任内为维护教会权益与加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂相争。

1377年，他被萨伏依伯爵拘捕，囚禁于比耶拉。1378年9月，教宗乌尔班六世立他为司铎级枢机。1384年，他在罗马去世。

en:
Guglielmo Spinola was a Genoese nobleman, son of the consul Oberto Spinola, and the founder of the Spinola di Luccoli branch. He held the consulate of Genoa in 1208, 1212 and 1216.

As a Ghibelline and imperial feudatory he held Busalla in the upper Scrivia valley and allied with Emperor Frederick II Hohenstaufen. In 1242 the Genoese Guelphs besieged the fief of Busalla, conquering the whole district and forcing him into exile.

en:
Guido Spinola was a Genoese noble of the Spinola di San Luca branch, son of Giovanni Spinola and Giacoma di San Genesio. In 1251, as a leading councillor, he approved Genoa's agreements with Savona, Florence and Pavia; in 1252 he sat among the Eight Nobles in charge of public finances. In July 1261 he ratified the Treaty of Nymphaeum with the Byzantine emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos.

In 1263 he led an embassy to Pope Urban IV. After the failure of Oberto Spinola's rising, he held the podestà with Nicolò Doria from 1265 to 1266.

圭多·斯皮诺拉是热那亚贵族，出身斯皮诺拉家族圣卢卡支系，乔瓦尼·斯皮诺拉与亚科帕·迪·圣杰内西奥之子。1251年，他作为核心议事官参与批准热那亚与萨沃纳、佛罗伦萨和帕维亚的协议；1252年，他进入掌管公共财政的八贵族团。1261年7月，他参与批准与拜占庭皇帝米海尔八世·帕里奥洛加斯签订的《尼姆法伊翁条约》。

1263年他率使团觐见教皇乌尔巴诺四世。奥贝托·斯皮诺拉起事失败后，他于1265至1266年与尼科洛·多里亚一同担任最高行政长官。

en:
Lamba Doria (1245–1323) was one of Genoa's greatest admirals, brother of Oberto Doria. He first won fame escorting convoys to Constantinople with five galleys and defended trade routes around Corsica and Sardinia. He repeatedly beat the Pisans, notably at the Battle of Meloria in August 1284.

His greatest triumph came in 1298 at the Battle of Curzola, where he destroyed the Venetian fleet, capturing admiral Andrea Dandolo, who killed himself in despair, and, by tradition, Marco Polo. Genoa gave him a palace and lands, proclaimed him capitano del popolo, and Emperor Henry VII later named him imperial admiral.

兰巴·多里亚（1245—1323）是热那亚最杰出的海军将领之一，名将奥贝托·多里亚的兄弟。他早年以五艘桨帆船护航君士坦丁堡贸易船队而成名，又保卫科西嘉和撒丁岛一带的航线。他屡次击败比萨人，尤以1284年8月的梅洛里亚海战著称。

他最辉煌的胜利是1298年的库尔佐拉海战：热那亚舰队歼灭威尼斯舰队，俘虏威尼斯统帅安德烈亚·丹多洛（后者绝望自杀），相传马可·波罗也在此役被俘。热那亚赐他宫殿与地产，推举他为平民长官；后来皇帝亨利七世任命他为帝国海军元帅。

Lanfranco Adorno (fl. 1261) was a Genoese commoner, a son of the founder Barisone Adorno. He is the first member of the Adorno house recorded in public office: in 1261 he was elected anziano, one of the elders who shared in governing the Republic.

From his marriage to Benvenuta da Serino was born Daniele, whose son Gabriele Adorno became doge of Genoa in 1363, the first of the Adorno doges.

兰弗兰克·阿多尔诺（活跃于1261年）是热那亚平民，家族始祖巴里索内·阿多尔诺之子。他是阿多尔诺家族中最早见于公职记载者：1261年当选为“长老”，即参与治理共和国的元老之一。

他娶本韦努塔·达塞里诺，生子达尼埃莱；达尼埃莱之子加布里埃莱·阿多尔诺于1363年成为热那亚总督，是阿多尔诺家的第一位总督。

en:
Lanfranco Spinola was a Genoese nobleman and naval commander. In 1263, in Genoa's war against Venice, he and Pietro Avvocato led the fourteen galleys that engaged a Venetian fleet off the Greek island of Settepozzi.

The Genoese were defeated with heavy losses and Avvocato was killed. A Genoese court of inquiry afterward condemned the surviving admirals, Spinola among them, to exile for their conduct. By his wife Sibilla Zaccaria he left a son, Ingo Spinola.

兰弗朗科·斯皮诺拉是热那亚贵族、海军将领。1263年热那亚与威尼斯交战期间，他与彼得罗·阿沃卡托率领十四艘桨帆船，在希腊岛屿塞特波齐附近迎战威尼斯舰队。

en:
Leonardo Montaldo (1319–1384) was the son of Paolo Montaldo, a close ally of the first doge, Simone Boccanegra. He later served as captain general of Genoese Romania, where Emperor John V Palaiologos gave him a linen bearing the face of Christ, later kept in San Bartolomeo degli Armeni.

Two failed coups against Doge Gabriele Adorno, in 1365 and 1366, sent him into exile until 1371. He helped negotiate the 1381 peace of Turin with Venice. In April 1383 a commission of forty chose him as doge over Antoniotto Adorno, on his promise to rule only six months.

He freed King James I of Cyprus on terms that tightened Genoa's grip on the island, and died of plague on 14 June 1384. His son Antonio became doge in 1392.

莱奥纳尔多·蒙塔尔多（1319—1384）是保罗·蒙塔尔多之子，父亲是初代总督西蒙·博卡内格拉的盟友。他出任热那亚罗马尼亚领地的总司令，拜占庭皇帝约翰五世·巴列奥略赠他一方印有基督面容的亚麻布，后存放于亚美尼亚人圣巴托洛梅奥教堂。

1365年和1366年，他两次反对总督加布里埃莱·阿多尔诺的政变失败，被迫流亡，1371年才返回。1381年他参与与威尼斯的都灵和约。1383年4月，四十人委员会选他而非安托尼奥托·阿多尔诺为总督，条件是他只执政半年。

他释放塞浦路斯国王雅克一世，条件使热那亚对该岛的控制更牢，1384年6月14日死于鼠疫。其子安东尼奥于1392年出任总督。

en:
Luca Grimaldi (early 13th century – 18 April 1275) was a Genoese nobleman and diplomat of the Guelph party, son of Ingo Grimaldi. First recorded in 1239 in Genoa's alliance with Milan against Emperor Frederick II, he and his brother Boarello took control of the castles of Stella and Andora after the Savona revolt of 1248–1251.

He was podestà of Florence in 1257 and Genoese ambassador to Pope Alexander IV in 1258. When the Ghibellines under Oberto Doria and Oberto Spinola took Genoa in 1271, he was exiled to Stella and died in 1275.

en:
Niccolò Doria (c. 1150, died between 1224 and 1226) was a Genoese nobleman of the Doria family and a son of the admiral Simone Doria. He sat among the consuls of Genoa's ruling magistracy. He married Giacomettina della Volta, and their sons Emmanuele, Lanfranco and Ingo carried on the line.

On 3 July 1237 Emmanuele and Lanfranco bought an undivided half of the castle and vill of Andora, on the western Riviera, from the marquess Bonifacio Tagliaferro. After Lanfranco and Ingo had died, Emmanuele and Ingo's son Lanfranchino sold the castle of Andora to the commune of Genoa by charter of 15 June 1252.

en:
Nicolò Doria (died January 1276) was a Genoese politician and soldier of the Doria branch with interests in Logudoro, northern Sardinia, son of Manuele Doria. Around 1231 he married Preziosa, daughter of Judge Mariano II of Torres. He attended the signing of the Treaty of Nymphaeum in 1261 and, after losing his lands to Pisan interference, recovered them around 1264.

After Oberto Doria's failed coup in 1265 he was made capitano del popolo, leaving office the following year. In 1271–1272 he led the campaign that stormed the Grimaldi castle at Stella.

en:
Niccolò Fieschi (c. 1230–c. 1309) was a Genoese Guelph noble, count of Lavagna and Torriglia, brother of Pope Adrian V and nephew of Pope Innocent IV. In 1251 he joined the magistracy of the Eight Nobles.

Backed by Innocent IV, he built a wide lordship in the Ligurian Levant and Lunigiana, centred on La Spezia, where he built a palace in 1252. His expansion brought him into conflict with the bishop of Luni and the Genoese republic.

After the Ghibellines seized Genoa in 1270, Oberto Doria's forces took La Spezia in 1273 and ended his lordship, and in 1276 he sold his estates to the republic.

尼科洛·菲耶斯基（约1230—约1309）是热那亚圭尔夫派贵族，拉瓦尼亚与托里利亚伯爵，教皇阿德里安五世之弟、教皇英诺森四世之侄。1251年，他进入“八贵族”执政机构。

依仗英诺森四世的支持，他在利古里亚东部和卢尼贾纳建立起广阔的私人领地，以拉斯佩齐亚为中心，1252年在当地修建宫邸。他的扩张使他与卢尼主教及热那亚共和国发生冲突。

en:
Nicolò Guarco (c. 1325–c. 1385) was a Genoese Ghibelline, the son of a merchant, who climbed through embassies and offices and governed Famagusta for Genoa. In June 1378 a popular rising drove out Doge Domenico Fregoso. Antoniotto Adorno had himself proclaimed doge but gave up the title the same evening, and Guarco was elected.

He banished the Fregoso and on 22 September 1378 readmitted the exiled noble houses to public office, a power-sharing formula that lasted until Andrea Doria's reform of 1528. His rule was dominated by the War of Chioggia against Venice: Genoa took Chioggia in August 1379, surrendered it in June 1380, and made peace at Turin in 1381.

New taxes turned the people against him, and in April 1383 he was forced out. He died a prisoner at Lerici; two of his sons later became doges.

尼科洛·瓜尔科（约1325—约1385）是热那亚的吉伯林派人物，商人之子，靠出使和任官一步步上升，曾代表热那亚管理法马古斯塔。1378年6月，民众起事赶走总督多梅尼科·弗雷戈索。安托尼奥托·阿多尔诺自立为总督，却在当晚让位，尼科洛随即当选。

他驱逐弗雷戈索家族，并在1378年9月22日让流亡的贵族家族重回公职，这一分权办法一直沿用到1528年安德烈亚·多里亚改革。他任内的大事是对威尼斯的基奥贾战争：1379年8月热那亚攻占基奥贾，1380年6月又将其放弃，1381年在都灵缔结和约。

新增税赋使民众转而反对他，1383年4月他被迫下台，后来作为囚徒死于莱里奇；他的两个儿子日后也出任总督。

en:
Oberto Doria (before 1230–1306) was a Genoese admiral and capitano del popolo and brother of Lamba Doria. A merchant in his youth, he traded from France to North Africa. In 1266, after a Genoese defeat at Trapani, he took his first fleet command and raided Canea. In 1270 he and Oberto Spinola seized power as joint captains of the people, opening a fifteen-year Genoese golden age; in 1273 he stormed La Spezia against the Fieschi.

As admiral he crushed the Pisans at the Battle of Meloria on 6 August 1284, crippling their sea power. He retired in 1285 and helped make peace with Pisa in 1288.

zh:
奥贝托·多里亚（1230年前—1306）是热那亚海军将领与平民长官，兰巴·多里亚之兄。他年轻时从事贸易，生意遍及法国和北非。1266年热那亚舰队在特拉帕尼失利后，他首次受命指挥舰队，劫掠干尼亚。1270年他与奥贝托·斯皮诺拉共同就任平民长官，开启热那亚十五年的黄金时代；1273年他攻克菲耶斯基家族的拉斯佩齐亚。

作为海军统帅，他在1284年8月6日的梅洛里亚海战中大败比萨人，摧毁其海上霸权。他于1285年引退，1288年促成与比萨的和约。

Oberto Spinola was a late twelfth-century Genoese statesman, son of the consul Guido Spinola and Alda, and several times consul himself.

In October 1188 he and his sons founded the church of San Luca in the Maddalena quarter, on land belonging to his son-in-law Oberto Grimaldi; tradition dates its consecration to 1191. The San Luca branch of the Spinola descended from his line.

en:
Oberto Spinola was a Ghibelline leader of the Republic of Genoa and head of the Spinola family. In 1270 he and Oberto Doria, the so-called diarchy of the two Oberti, took power as consuls and governed Genoa together for twenty years. In 1275 he served as capitano del popolo at Asti. He directed construction of San Damiano d'Asti, a new town built by the people of Asti in place of their destroyed rival Astixio.

His son Corrado fought in the great naval victory over Pisa at Meloria in 1284. In 1291 Spinola and Doria began building Genoa's Ducal Palace.

Odoardo Spinola was a Genoese noble of the Spinola di Luccoli branch, son of Oberto Spinola. In May 1301 he subscribed Genoa's alliance with Charles II of Anjou, who in 1308 named him grand admiral of Sicily.

In November 1308 he arrested Bernabò Doria, letting his nephew Opizzino Spinola take sole power, and took charge of Monaco castle, from which his son Galeotto raided shipping. He returned to Genoa with Emperor Henry VII in 1311 and died in 1313.

en:
Opizzino Spinola was a wealthy Genoese merchant of the Spinola family. In 1306 he was elected capitano del popolo with Bernabò Doria, and that year married his daughter Argentina to Theodore Palaiologos, helping him win Montferrat. In 1308 he imprisoned Bernabò and made himself sole perpetual captain, seeking personal rule over Genoa.

After defeat at Sestri Ponente in 1309 he was banished, but his attacks on Montaldo and Voltaggio forced the Genoese to negotiate. He returned with Emperor Henry VII in 1311 and received Oltregiogo fiefs in 1313. Expelled once more, he died of fever at Serravalle Scrivia in 1317.

Paleologo Zaccaria was a Genoese admiral and lord of Chios, Phocaea and other Aegean islands. His baptismal name is unrecorded; he was called Paleologo because his mother was a Palaiologina, sister of Emperor Michael VIII, and his father was Benedetto I Zaccaria.

en:
Pietro Fregoso (1330–1404) was a Genoese lawyer, merchant and admiral, brother of Doge Domenico. Active in the eastern colonies, he was made admiral for Genoa's expedition against Cyprus, where he captured Famagusta and King Peter II. After Domenico's deposition in 1378, Pietro was imprisoned, escaped and went into exile.

Back in Genoa, he became doge on 15 July 1393, in a summer when doges changed within days or hours; he held office only a few hours before Clemente Promontorio forced him out.

In August 1394 he joined Antonio Guarco in storming the ducal palace to overthrow Doge Nicolò Zoagli. Guarco took the office, but only for a few weeks. Pietro died in Genoa on 22 April 1404.

彼得罗·弗雷戈索（1330—1404）是热那亚法律家、商人兼海军将领，总督多梅尼科之弟。他活跃于东方殖民地，后受命为海军司令远征塞浦路斯，攻取法马古斯塔并俘虏国王彼得二世。1378年多梅尼科被废后，彼得罗遭到囚禁，逃脱后流亡。

回到热那亚后，他于1393年7月15日出任总督，那个夏天总督数日甚至数小时一换；他在位仅数小时，便被克莱门特·普罗蒙托里奥逼退。

1394年8月，他与安东尼奥·瓜尔科联手围攻总督府，推翻总督尼科洛·佐阿利，但执政之位落到瓜尔科手里，也只坐了几周。1404年4月22日，彼得罗在热那亚去世。

en:
Raffaele Doria (born c. 1277) was a Genoese Ghibelline nobleman of the Doria family. In 1335, after years of Guelph dominance, the Ghibellines retook Genoa and Doria was elected one of its two captains of the people, ruling alongside a Spinola.

To face the exiled Guelph nobles and Catalan naval pressure the captains assumed full powers, but they lost popular backing, and in December 1339 the people acclaimed Simone Boccanegra as the republic's first doge, ending their government.

en:
Simone Boccanegra (c. 1301–1363) was a merchant with no political career until 1339, when the people of Genoa, tired of the Ghibelline captains, acclaimed him first doge for life on 23 December. The city's finances were exhausted and its Riviera lands in rebel hands; he shut the aristocratic factions out of power and brought the Rivieras back under Genoese control.

In 1341 he renewed peace with Pisa. Constant conspiracies forced him to resign in December 1345, and Genoa submitted to the Visconti of Milan.

When the city rose against them on 14 November 1356 he returned from exile, rallied the commoners at San Siro and was restored as doge. He died suddenly in March 1363, the day after a banquet for Peter I of Cyprus, amid rumours of poison; Gabriele Adorno replaced him.

1356年11月14日，热那亚起义反抗维斯孔蒂，他从流亡中返回，在圣西罗教堂争取平民支持，重任总督。1363年3月，他在宴请塞浦路斯国王彼得一世的次日暴卒，外界盛传他是被毒死的；加布里埃莱·阿多尔诺取代了他。

Simone Doria (born c. 1135) was a Genoese merchant, politician and admiral of the Doria family. A Ghibelline, he was elected consul of Genoa six times between 1175 and 1188. Chosen admiral in 1189, he led a fleet in support of Philip Augustus's troops at the Siege of Acre in 1190.

en:
Tommaso da Murta was a son of Giovanni da Murta, the second doge of Genoa. When his father died of the plague on 6 January 1350, the late doge's patrician partisans put Tommaso forward as his successor, while the popolani backed Luchino Fieschi.

Three days later, on 9 January, the electors gathered in the church of San Giorgio chose neither and proclaimed the elderly banker Giovanni II Valente doge as a compromise candidate, and Tommaso's bid for the dogeship came to nothing.

en:
Ugo Fieschi (c. 1150–1211) was count of Lavagna and head of the Guelph Fieschi dynasty on the Ligurian Levante. With his wife Beatrice Grillo he fathered Tedisio and Sinibaldo, the future Pope Innocent IV, who led the Church through its struggle with Emperor Frederick II.

In 1209–1210 Ugo replaced the old wooden crossing of the Entella between Lavagna and Chiavari with a thirteen-arch stone bridge, the Ponte della Maddalena, whose tolls remained in Fieschi hands until the mid-fifteenth century.

乌戈·菲耶斯基（约1150—1211）是拉瓦尼亚伯爵，利古里亚东部圭尔夫派菲耶斯基家族的宗主。他与妻子贝阿特丽切·格里洛生下泰迪西奥和西尼巴尔多，后者后来成为教皇英诺森四世，在任内领导教会与皇帝腓特烈二世相争。

Violante of Saluzzo (1270–1315) was an Italian noblewoman of the Aleramici dynasty, the fourth daughter of Thomas I, Marquis of Saluzzo, and Aloisia di Ceva. She first married Opizzino Spinola, the wealthy Captain of the People of Genoa; their daughter Argentina Spinola married Theodore I Palaiologos, Marquis of Montferrat.

After Spinola's death, Violante married Luchino Visconti, later lord of Milan, in 1315, but she died in Milan later that same year. Her daughter by Visconti, Caterina, later married Francesco d'Este.

维奥兰特·迪·萨卢佐（1270—1315）是阿莱拉米奇家族的意大利贵族女性，为萨卢佐侯爵托马索一世与阿洛伊西亚·迪·切瓦的第四女。她先嫁给热那亚豪门、热那亚人民领袖奥比齐诺·斯皮诺拉，两人的女儿阿尔真蒂娜·斯皮诺拉后来嫁给蒙费拉托侯爵泰奥多罗一世·巴列奥略。

en:
Genghis Khan (c. 1162–1227), born Temüjin, founded the Mongol Empire, history's largest contiguous empire. At eight his father, chieftain Yesugei, died and the tribe abandoned his family.

He broke Kerait ruler Toghrul in 1203 and executed Jamukha to become sole steppe ruler, taking the title Genghis Khan at a kurultai in 1206. He reorganised the Mongols into decimal military units. The Western Xia submitted in 1209–1210, and when a Jin envoy demanded tribute he spat and rode away; his armies took the Jin capital Zhongdu in 1215.

After Khwarazm killed his envoys he invaded in 1219, taking Bukhara and Samarkand in 1220. He died in August 1227 after a hunting fall during a Western Xia siege and was buried near Burkhan Khaldun. His son Ögedei succeeded him in 1229; his sons' appanages became the Golden Horde and Chagatai Khanate.

成吉思汗（约1162—1227），本名铁木真，创建了历史上疆域最连续的大蒙古国。八岁时父亲、首领也速该去世，家人被部落抛弃。

1203年他击溃克烈部首领脱斡邻勒、处死札木合，成为草原唯一的统治者，1206年在忽里勒台上称成吉思汗。他把蒙古人编成十进制军事单位。西夏于1209至1210年臣服；金朝使者索要贡赋时他啐了一口拨马而去，1215年军队攻占金朝都城中都。

花剌子模处死其使者后，他于1219年出兵，1220年攻克不花剌和撒马尔罕。1227年8月他在狩猎坠马后、围攻西夏期间去世，葬于不儿罕山附近。1229年其子窝阔台继位，诸子封地成为金帐汗国和察合台汗国。

en:
Bagrat III (c. 963–1014), called the Unifier, was the son of Gurgen of Iberia and an Abkhazian princess. Adopted heir of David III Kuropalates of Tao, he became king of Abkhazia in 978, displacing his uncle Theodosius the Blind.

He curbed the nobles, crushing their revolts. When Gurgen died in 1008, he united Iberia with Abkhazia as the first king of a single Georgia, later extending his power to Kakheti. He died on 7 May 1014.

巴格拉特三世（约963—1014），人称“统一者”，是伊比利亚王古尔根与阿布哈兹王族之女的儿子。他被陶的大卫三世·库罗帕拉特斯收为继承人，978年成为阿布哈兹国王，取代其舅“盲人”狄奥多西。

他压制贵族，粉碎了贵族的叛乱。1008年古尔根去世后，他将伊比利亚与阿布哈兹合二为一，成为统一格鲁吉亚的第一位国王，后来还把势力扩展到卡赫季。1014年5月7日他去世。

en:
Bagrat IV (1018–1072) ruled Georgia from 1027. After his father George I's defeat by Byzantium in 1022, he was held hostage in Constantinople for three years before succeeding to the throne aged eight.

Once ruling in person, he curbed the great nobles, defeating the Liparitid family, and reduced the rulers of Kakheti and the Muslim emir of Tbilisi to vassalage. Caught between Byzantium and the rising Seljuk Turks, he balanced both powers. His daughter Maria of Alania married two Byzantine emperors.

en:
Bagrat V the Great (died 1393) of the Bagrationi dynasty was the son of David IX. He ruled as co-king from 1355 and was crowned at Kutaisi after succeeding his father in 1360, winning fame as a soldier and archer.

His 1385 alliance with Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde brought war with Timur, who sacked Tbilisi and captured him in 1386. Feigning conversion to Islam, Bagrat was freed and promptly destroyed his Timurid escort with his sons. He died in 1393, leaving the crown to George VII.

zh:
巴格拉特五世绰号“大帝”（？—1393），是巴格拉季昂王朝成员，大卫九世之子。他自1355年起担任共治国王，1360年父亲去世后在库塔伊西加冕，以善战善射闻名。

1385年他与金帐汗脱脱迷失结盟，招来帖木儿的战争；1386年第比利斯在长期围攻后陷落，巴格拉特被俘。他假装皈依伊斯兰教获释，随即与诸子歼灭随行的帖木儿军队。1393年他去世，王位传给吉奥尔基七世。

en:
Basil V was Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia in the middle of the fourteenth century, heading the Georgian Orthodox Church during the reigns of George V the Brilliant and David IX.

The son of Ivane, a Georgian noble who bore the Byzantine court title of Grand Patrikios, he occupied the patriarchal see from the 1340s until his death in 1349. Dorotheos I succeeded him, appearing as patriarch in sources of the 1360s.

巴西尔五世是14世纪中叶的全格鲁吉亚卡托利科斯-宗主教，在“辉煌者”吉奥尔基五世与大卫九世在位期间主持格鲁吉亚正教会。

他是拥有拜占庭宫廷头衔“大帕特里基奥斯”的格鲁吉亚贵族伊瓦涅之子，自1340年代起出任牧首，直至1349年去世。他之后由多罗特奥一世接任，后者在1360年代的文献中以卡托利科斯身份出现。

en:
David IV, called the Builder (1073–1125), became king of Georgia in 1089 when his father George II abdicated. He reformed the army and administration, settling Kipchak families to supply troops, and retook Samshvilde and Rustavi from the Seljuk Turks.

In 1121 he routed a vast Muslim coalition at the Battle of Didgori, and in 1122 captured Tbilisi, ending its emirate of nearly five centuries. He opened Georgia's Golden Age and was canonized by the Georgian Orthodox Church.

zh:
大卫四世，号称“建造者”（1073—1125），1089年因父亲吉奥尔基二世退位而登基。他改革军政，把钦察人部众安置在国内以提供兵源，并从塞尔柱突厥手中收复萨姆什维尔德与鲁斯塔维。

1121年他在迪德戈里战役击溃庞大的穆斯林联军；1122年攻占第比利斯，终结了当地近五个世纪的埃米尔统治。他开启了格鲁吉亚的黄金时代，被格鲁吉亚正教会封圣。

en:
David IX (died 1360), son of George V the Brilliant, ruled Georgia from 1346 until his death. The Black Death struck in 1348, and his reign brought heavy foreign pressure: he lost the Laz lands to Trebizond and in 1349–1350 paid the Ilkhan Anushirwan four hundred thousand dinars a year.

He repaired the walls of Tmogvi in 1350 and restored church lands seized under Mongol rule. By his queen Sindukhtar he fathered Bagrat V. He died in 1360 and was buried at Gelati.

大卫九世（？—1360）是“辉煌者”吉奥尔基五世之子，1346年至1360年为格鲁吉亚国王。1348年黑死病肆虐，他在位期间外患沉重：拉兹地区被特拉比松帝国夺取，1349—1350年他每年向伊儿汗努失儿完缴纳40万第纳尔贡金。

他于1350年修缮蒂姆戈维堡垒的城墙，把蒙古统治时期遭侵占的教会土地归还原主。他娶辛杜克塔尔为后，生下巴格拉特五世。1360年他去世，葬于格拉特修道院。

en:
David V (c. 1113–1155) was the eldest son of Demetrius I and grandson of David IV the Builder. After Demetrius disinherited him in favour of his younger brother George, David's first coup failed around 1150, but in 1154 he overthrew his father, forced him into a monastery, and took the throne.

He appointed a new commander-in-chief, alienating the Orbeli brothers. After six months as king he died, reportedly poisoned by them. His son Demna was passed over in favour of his uncle George III.

大卫五世（约1113—1155）是德米特里一世的长子、大卫四世（建造者）之孙。德米特里废长立幼，改立幼子吉奥尔基为继承人；他约1150年首次发动政变失败，1154年终于推翻父亲，将其送入修道院后登上王位。

en:
David VI Narin (1225–1293), the Younger, was son of Queen Rusudan and her Seljuk husband. Crowned at Kutaisi in 1230, he was recognized in 1246 as junior king to his cousin David VII.

In 1259 he rebelled against the Mongols and fell back to Kutaisi, where he founded the independent Kingdom of Western Georgia, ruling it as David I. He sheltered his cousin in 1261 and repulsed Ilkhanate attacks. He died at Kutaisi in 1293, succeeded by his son Constantine I.

en:
David VII, called Ulu or the Elder (1215–1270), the son of George IV, ruled Georgia from 1246, jointly with his cousin David VI under Mongol suzerainty. He led Georgian troops in Hulegu Khan's 1258 siege of Baghdad.

After David VI seceded in 1259, David rebelled in 1260, was defeated near Akhaldaba and fled to Imereti; his wife Gvantsa was killed. He submitted in 1262 and died in 1270, succeeded by his son Demetrius II.

en:
David VIII (1273–1311), son of Demetrius II, was enthroned by the Ilkhan Gaykhatu in 1292. After backing Baydu against Ghazan in 1295, he refused a summons to Tabriz and was driven into the Mtiuleti mountains, where he defeated a Mongol force.

Ghazan raised his brothers George V and Vakhtang III against him, but David eventually made terms as joint sovereign. In 1305 he regained Jerusalem's Monastery of the Cross for the Georgian Church. He died in 1311, succeeded by his son George VI.

大卫八世（1273—1311）是德米特里二世之子，1292年被伊利汗海合都立为格鲁吉亚国王。1295年他支持拜都反对合赞汗，事后拒绝前往大不里士觐见，被逼退入姆季乌列季山区，在那里击败一支蒙古军。

en:
Demetrius I (c. 1093–1156), eldest son of David IV the Builder, ruled Georgia in 1125–1154 and again from 1155. As king he raided Ganja in 1139, carrying its iron gate to Gelati Monastery, and captured Emir Saltuk II at Ani in 1154.

Deposed by his son David V and tonsured as Damian, he returned after David's sudden death. He wrote the hymn Thou Art a Vineyard and is venerated as a saint.

德米特里一世（约1093—1156）是大卫四世（建造者）的长子，1125—1154年及1155年起两度统治格鲁吉亚。1139年他劫掠占贾，把该城的铁门运到格拉特修道院；1154年在阿尼俘获埃米尔萨尔图克二世。

他被儿子大卫五世废黜、剃度为修士，取教名达米安；大卫突然死后他复位。他创作了圣诗《你是葡萄园》，被尊为圣徒。

en:
Demetrius II, called the Devoted (1259–1289), succeeded his father David VII as king of eastern Georgia in 1270, under a regent. In 1288, on Arghun Khan's orders, he crushed Derbent's revolt.

That year a plot by the Ilkhan's minister Buqa was exposed; Demetrius was suspected of complicity and summoned to the Mongol court. Against his nobles' advice he went, was imprisoned, and beheaded at Movakan on 12 March 1289. He was canonized by the Georgian Church.

德米特里二世（1259—1289），绰号“虔信者”，1270年继其父大卫七世为东格鲁吉亚国王，由摄政王辅政。1288年，他奉阿鲁浑汗之命平定杰尔宾特的叛乱。

同年伊利汗权臣不哈的阴谋败露，德米特里被疑参与阴谋，受召前往蒙古宫廷。他不顾贵族劝阻前去，随即下狱，1289年3月12日在莫瓦坎被斩首，后被格鲁吉亚正教会封圣。

en:
George I (c. 1000–1027), son of Bagrat III, succeeded in 1014 as second king of a unified Georgia. He had to recognize Kakhetian independence, but his reign was dominated by war with Byzantium: claiming Tao, he fought Emperor Basil II and was defeated at Shirimni in 1021.

He backed a revolt of Byzantine generals in 1022, then lost again at Basiani. Peace terms sent his son Bagrat hostage to Constantinople and cost him Tao and fourteen fortresses. He died on 16 August 1027.

George II (c. 1050–1112), of the Bagrationi dynasty, succeeded his father Bagrat IV as king of Georgia in 1072. In 1070 he led a Georgian-Alan army to defeat the Shaddadid emir Fadl II near Ganja.

His reign was overwhelmed by Seljuk attacks and internal problems. After a 1088 earthquake, his nobles forced him in 1089 to abdicate in favour of his sixteen-year-old son David IV the Builder; he remained a nominal co-ruler until his death.

en:
George III (died 1184), younger son of Demetrius I, ruled Georgia from 1156. He campaigned against Armenia's Muslim rulers, seizing Ani in 1161 and sacking Dvin in 1162.

Defeated by a Muslim coalition in 1163, he gave Ani back before reoccupying it in 1174. In 1177 he crushed a noble revolt led by Ivane Orbeli in favour of his nephew Demna, who was blinded and died in prison. In 1178 he crowned his daughter Tamar co-ruler; she succeeded him in 1184.

en:
George IV, called Lasha Giorgi (1191–1223), son of Tamar the Great and David Soslan, was made co-ruler in 1207 and ruled Georgia from 1213. He reasserted suzerainty over Ganja and in 1219 forced Erzurum and other neighbouring rulers to pay tribute.

His plans to join the Fifth Crusade ended when the first Mongol incursion into the Caucasus routed the Georgians twice in 1221–1222 and wounded him. He died of the wound in January 1223, aged thirty-one. Rusudan succeeded him; his son by a commoner later ruled as David VII.

en:
George V the Brilliant (c. 1286–1346) of the Bagrationi dynasty worked to reunite Georgia as the Ilkhanate declined. The Ilkhan Ghazan installed him in 1299 against his rebel brother David VIII, but his authority reached little beyond Tbilisi, earning him the name Shadow King of Tbilisi; in 1302 his brother Vakhtang III replaced him. He returned as regent for his nephew George VI and was crowned in 1318, ruling as ally of Ilkhan Abu Sa'id and his minister Chupan.

Chupan's execution in 1327 was his opening: he halted tribute, expelled the Mongol troops, subdued Imereti and the western nobles, and in 1334 peacefully drew Samtskhe back. He issued two law codes between 1325 and 1338 and recovered Georgian monasteries in Palestine from the Mamluks.

To Philip VI of France he offered thirty thousand soldiers for a crusade. He died in 1346 and his son David IX succeeded him.

辉煌者吉奥尔基五世（约1286—1346）出身巴格拉季昂尼王朝，在伊儿汗国衰落时重新整合格鲁吉亚。1299年伊儿汗合赞扶他上台，对抗反叛的兄长大卫八世，但权力几乎出不了第比利斯，人称“第比利斯的影子国王”；1302年被兄长瓦赫坦三世取代。他后为侄儿乔治六世摄政，1318年加冕，作为伊儿汗不赛因和重臣出班的盟友治国。

他向法王腓力六世表示愿为十字军出兵三万。1346年去世，其子大卫九世继位。

George VI, called the Little (1303/1304–1318), was a son of David VIII. After the death of Vakhtang III in 1308, the Ilkhan Öljaitü made the boy king of eastern Georgia and appointed his uncle as regent.

When David VIII died in 1311, two kings coexisted until Öljaitü confirmed George VI. His reign remained nominal, overshadowed by Mongol-backed rivals, and he died while still a child in 1318.

en:
Giovanni da Firenze was an Italian Dominican friar who worked as a missionary in the Caucasus. He was one of the companions of Bartolomeo il Piccolo, bishop of Maragheh and founder of the United Armenian Dominicans.

Pope John XXII erected the Latin diocese of Tiflis, today's Tbilisi, in 1329, and in 1330 appointed Giovanni its first bishop. He held the missionary see until his death; his successor was appointed only in 1349, and the residential diocese did not survive the fourteenth century.

en:
Mirian III (c. 258/277–361) founded the Chosroid dynasty and ruled Iberia, or Kartli, in Georgia. As a Sasanian Persian vassal he fought in Shah Narseh's war against Rome in 297–298, but after Persia's defeat he drew his kingdom toward Rome.

Through the preaching of Nino, a Cappadocian woman, Mirian became the first Christian king of Iberia and around 337 made Christianity the kingdom's state religion. The Georgian Orthodox Church venerates him as Saint Equal to the Apostles.

米利安三世（约258/277—361）是格鲁吉亚伊比利亚（卡尔特利）科斯罗埃斯王朝的开国君主。作为萨珊波斯附庸，他曾参加297—298年沙纳尔塞斯对罗马的战争；波斯战败后，他使王国转而亲近罗马。

在卡帕多细亚女子尼诺的传道下，米利安成为伊比利亚第一位信奉基督教的国王，并于约337年将基督教立为国教。格鲁吉亚正教会尊他为“使徒同等者”圣徒。

en:
Rusudan (1194–1245), daughter of Queen Tamar and David Soslan, succeeded her brother George IV as queen in 1223. In 1225 the Khwarazmshah Jalal al-Din defeated the Georgians and sacked Tbilisi in 1226, killing more than a hundred thousand inhabitants.

Her alliance with the Seljuks of Rum ended in rout in 1228. As the Mongols overran Georgia, Rusudan submitted in 1239, accepting a tribute of fifty thousand gold pieces. She died in 1245, waiting for her son David to return from the Mongol court.

鲁速丹（1194—1245）是塔玛尔女王与达维特·索斯兰之女，1223年继其兄乔治四世之后成为女王。1225年，花剌子模沙札兰丁击败格鲁吉亚军队，又于1226年洗劫第比利斯，逾十万居民遇难。

en:
Saint Nino (c. 280–c. 332) was a Cappadocian woman who brought Christianity to Iberia, or Kartli. Fleeing Diocletian's persecution, she alone of her company escaped death in Armenia and reached Kartli. Tradition holds that the Virgin Mary gave her a grapevine cross and sent her to preach.

Nino healed and converted Queen Nana, then King Mirian III, after which Christianity became Iberia's state religion. She died at Bodbe in Kakheti, and the grapevine cross became the symbol of Georgian Christianity.

圣尼诺（约280—约332）是把基督教传入伊比利亚（即卡尔特利）的卡帕多细亚女子。为逃避戴克里先的迫害，她同行的人在亚美尼亚悉数殉道，只有她一人逃到卡尔特利。相传圣母赠予她葡萄藤十字架，命她前去传教。

尼诺行神迹治愈并归化了娜娜王后，又使国王米利安三世皈依，基督教由此成为伊比利亚国教。她在卡赫季的博德贝去世，葡萄藤十字架也成为格鲁吉亚基督教的标志。

en:
Tamar the Great (c. 1160–1213), daughter of George III, was Georgia's first ruling queen, styled mepe, or king, from 1184. She overcame aristocratic opposition, divorced Yury Bogolyubsky of Vladimir, and in 1191 married the Alan prince David Soslan.

Her armies defeated the Eldiguzids at Shamkor in 1195 and the Seljuk sultan of Rum at Basian around 1202. Her reign was the peak of the Georgian Golden Age, her empire spanning the Black Sea to the Caspian, when Shota Rustaveli composed The Knight in the Panther's Skin.

塔玛尔大王（约1160—1213）是吉奥尔基三世之女，格鲁吉亚第一位以本人名义执政的女性，1184年起以“梅佩”（意为国王）的尊号统治。她压服贵族反对势力，与弗拉基米尔的尤里·博戈柳布斯基离婚，又于1191年嫁给阿兰王公大卫·索斯兰。

格军1195年在沙姆科尔击败埃尔德古兹王朝，约1202年在巴西安击溃鲁姆的塞尔柱苏丹。她在位时是格鲁吉亚黄金时代的顶峰，帝国横跨黑海至里海，绍塔·鲁斯塔韦利也在这一时期创作了《虎皮武士》。

en:
Vakhtang II (died 1292), son of David VI Narin of western Georgia, was placed on the throne of eastern Georgia by the Ilkhan Arghun in 1289, after the execution of Demetrius II, to unite both Georgian realms under Mongol rule. Arghun gave him his sister Oljath in marriage.

Vakhtang ruled firmly and twice defeated the intrigues of his atabeg Khutlubuga, who backed Demetrius's son David. He died in 1292 after a reign of barely three years and was buried at Gelati, whereupon David succeeded him and married his widow.

en:
Vakhtang III (1275–1308), son of Demetrius II, was named king of Georgia by the Ilkhan Ghazan in 1302 as a counterweight to his rebel brother David VIII.

His power scarcely ran beyond Tbilisi, and after an unsuccessful campaign against David's mountain guerrillas the brothers agreed to rule jointly. Most of his reign was spent leading Georgian and Armenian auxiliaries in Mongol wars, notably the march on Damascus in 1303. He died in 1308, leaving sons Demetrius and George.

en:
Georg von Peuerbach (1423–1461), born at Peuerbach in Upper Austria, studied at the University of Vienna from 1446 and became its leading astronomer. After observing the Moon occult Jupiter in 1451, he lectured in Italy, where Bologna and Padua offered him chairs, before returning to Vienna in 1453.

In 1454 he became court astrologer to King Ladislas V and later imperial astronomer to Frederick III. His lectures on Ptolemaic planetary theory were attended by the young Regiomontanus, who became his pupil and collaborator, and were later printed as the Theoricae Novae Planetarum. He died in 1461.

格奥尔格·冯·波伊尔巴赫（1423—1461）生于上奥地利的波伊尔巴赫，1446年起在维也纳大学求学，后成为该校最重要的天文学家。1451年观测月掩木星后，他前往意大利讲学，博洛尼亚和帕多瓦大学都曾聘他任教，1453年返回维也纳。

1454年他任国王拉斯洛五世的宫廷占星师，后来成为腓特烈三世的皇家天文学家。他讲授托勒密行星理论时，年轻的雷格蒙塔努斯曾在座听讲，后来成为他的学生与合作者；其讲稿后来以《新行星理论》为名刊印。他于1461年去世。

en:
Rajput bardic accounts make Mokhadaji Gohil a Gohil chief of Saurashtra, ruling from 1309 until his death in 1347. Son of Ranoji, he seized lands from the Vala Rajputs and the Kolis and took the port of Ghogha.

He then conquered Piram Island from the Baria Kolis and made it a base for piracy. His sea raids drew Delhi Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq, in Gujarat to quell a rebellion; in 1347, after hard fighting, Tughluq captured Ghogha and Piram and killed him.

His sea raids drew Delhi Sultan #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('dlh_muhammad_bin_tughluq').GetID],X #L Muhammad bin Tughluq#!#!, in Gujarat to quell a rebellion; in 1347, after hard fighting, Tughluq captured Ghogha and Piram and killed him.
zh:
据拉杰普特吟游传统记载，莫克达吉·戈希尔是索拉什特拉的戈希拉拉杰普特首领，1309年起在位，直至1347年战死。他是拉诺吉之子，先后从瓦拉拉杰普特人和科利人手中夺取土地，并攻占港口戈加。

接着他从巴里亚科利人手中征服皮拉姆岛，将其作为海盗据点。他的海上劫掠引来正在古吉拉特平叛的德里苏丹穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克；1347年经过激战，图格鲁克攻占戈加与皮拉姆，将其斩杀。

en:
Ranoji Gohil (r. c. 1254–1309) was a Gohil Rajput chief in Saurashtra, reckoned in tradition as a son or grandson of the migrant leader Sejakji. He founded Ranpur, named after himself, and moved his capital there.

With Koli levies from Dhanmer he captured Vala, the ancient Vallabhipur, and extended Gohil power on the Saurashtra coast. His son Mokhadaji succeeded him and held Piram Island until 1347.

en:
Gian Giacomo Trivulzio (1440 or 1441–1518) was a Milanese nobleman and condottiero from the ancient House of Trivulzio. After fighting for the Sforza dukes, he entered French service under Charles VIII in 1483 and later served Naples; as commander of the Neapolitan army he negotiated peace with Charles, who then employed him.

Commanding Louis XII's army, he forced Ludovico Sforza from Milan in 1499 and was made a marshal of France and governor of the city. He later fought at Agnadello in 1509 and Marignano in 1515 and defended Milan against Emperor Maximilian I in 1516. Falling into disgrace, he died at Arpajon in 1518.

吉安·贾科莫·特里武尔齐奥（1440或1441—1518）是米兰古老贵族特里武尔齐奥家族出身的雇佣军首领。他早年为斯福尔扎公爵作战，1483年转投法王查理八世，后来又进入那不勒斯服役；作为那不勒斯军队的统帅，他与查理议定和约，随后受查理雇用。

他统领路易十二的军队，1499年将卢多维科·斯福尔扎逐出米兰，受封法兰西元帅并出任米兰总督。他还参加了1509年阿尼亚德洛战役和1515年马里尼亚诺战役，1516年击退皇帝马克西米利安一世对米兰的进攻。他后来失宠遭贬，1518年死于法国的阿尔帕容。

en:
Giuseppe Briati (1686–1772) was the leading Venetian artistic glassmaker of the eighteenth century, born on Murano. To meet competition from the new Bohemian crystal, he developed a glass type called uso cristallo and invented fresh decorative techniques.

In 1739 he opened his own furnace in Venice, producing mirrors, tableware, wall lamps and elaborate chandeliers, including pagoda or Chinese-style pieces whose arms were adorned with multicoloured glass flowers. He died in Venice on 18 January 1772.

朱塞佩·布里亚蒂（1686—1772）是18世纪威尼斯首屈一指的艺术玻璃匠，生于穆拉诺岛。为应对新兴波希米亚水晶的竞争，他研制出名为“仿水晶”的新玻璃品种，并发明了新的装饰技法。

1739年他在威尼斯自开窑厂，产品包括镜子、餐具、壁灯和精美的枝形吊灯，其中有以彩色玻璃花装饰灯臂的“宝塔式”或“中国式”吊灯。1772年1月18日他在威尼斯去世。

en:
Frederick VI of Schönburg (died 1328) was a younger son of Frederick III of Schönburg, the royal Bohemian land judge in the Pleissenland who divided the family estates around 1300.

Frederick and his brothers each received one of the house's three lordships of Pürstein, Glauchau and Hassenstein. He is attested in charters between 1310 and 1327 and served the Bohemian crown as sub-chamberlain in 1317 and 1318.

en:
García II (1041/1043–1090), youngest son of Ferdinand I of León-Castile and Sancha, received Galicia in the 1065 partition, with Portugal south to the Mondego. In early 1071 he killed the rebel Portuguese count Nuno Mendes at Pedroso, but his brothers' invasions drove him into exile in Seville.

After Sancho II's murder at Zamora in 1072, Alfonso VI lured him to a parley in 1073 and chained him in Luna Castle. He died there on 22 March 1090, asking to be buried in fetters at San Isidoro de León.

加西亚二世（1041或1043—1090）是莱昂与卡斯蒂利亚国王斐迪南一世与桑查最小的儿子。1065年父王分封诸子，他得到加利西亚，疆土包括向南直到蒙德古河的葡萄牙地区。1071年初，他在佩德罗索击杀叛乱的葡萄牙伯爵努诺·门德斯，但两个兄弟相继入侵，迫使他流亡塞维利亚。

1072年桑乔二世在萨莫拉遇刺后，阿方索六世于1073年诱他赴会将其擒获，锁入卢纳城堡。1090年3月22日他死于囚所，遗嘱要求戴着镣铐葬入莱昂的圣伊西德罗教堂。

en:
Raymond of Burgundy (c. 1070–1107) was the fourth son of Count William I of Burgundy. He came to Iberia around 1087 with a Burgundian army aiding Alfonso VI of León.

Raymond married the king's heiress Urraca, receiving the government of the Kingdom of Galicia, then including the counties of Portugal and Coimbra. In 1095 Alfonso detached those two counties and granted them to Raymond's kinsman Henry of Burgundy.

Raymond ruled Galicia with near-royal authority, using count and prince titles, until his death on 24 May 1107. His son by Urraca, Alfonso VII, later ruled León and Castile, and his brother became Pope Callixtus II.

雷蒙娶国王的女继承人乌拉卡为妻，受命统治加利西亚王国，当时该地还包括葡萄牙和科英布拉两个伯国。1095年，阿方索把这两个伯国划出，封给雷蒙的亲属勃艮第的亨利。

雷蒙以近乎君王的权威统治加利西亚，使用伯爵、亲王等头衔，直到1107年5月24日去世。他与乌拉卡所生的儿子阿方索七世后来统治莱昂与卡斯蒂利亚，他的兄弟则成为教皇加里斯都二世。

en:
Sancho Ordóñez (c. 895–929) was the eldest son of King Ordoño II of León and Elvira Menéndez. After his uncle Froila II died in 925, he briefly seized León before his brother Alfonso IV, backed by the Leonese nobility and his father-in-law the king of Pamplona, drove him out.

In 926 Sancho was crowned king of Galicia at Santiago de Compostela, ruling with Galician noble backing and styling himself Prince of Galicia in charters. At Christmas 927 he and Alfonso jointly held an assembly, confirming restoration of Santa María de Loio monastery. He married Goto Muñiz and died in 929, whereupon Alfonso inherited Galicia.

en:
Henry III of Głogów (1251/1260–1309), son of Konrad I, fought on the Marchfeld in 1278, where Ottokar II of Bohemia fell. In 1290 Henry IV Probus made him heir of Wrocław, but its burghers drove him out for Henry V the Fat, starting years of war.

From 1301 styling himself heir of Poland, he conquered most of Greater Poland in 1306–1307. His reign brought monetary reforms and a dozen towns. He married Matilda of Brunswick-Lüneburg in 1291 and died in December 1309, leaving five sons including Przemko II.

zh:
格沃古夫的亨里克三世（1251/1260—1309）是康拉德一世之子，1278年参加马希费尔德之战，波希米亚国王奥托卡二世在此役阵亡。1290年弗罗茨瓦夫的亨里克四世（公正者）立他为继承人，但弗罗茨瓦夫市民很快将他赶走、迎立胖子亨里克五世，由此引发连年战争。

1301年起他自称波兰王国王位继承人，1306—1307年征服大波兰大部。他治下推行货币改革、新建十余座城镇。1291年娶不伦瑞克-吕讷堡的玛蒂尔达，1309年12月去世，留下五个儿子，普热姆科二世即其中之一。

en:
Konrad I of Głogów (c. 1228–1274) was a Silesian Piast, son of Henry II the Pious. Destined for the Church and sent to study in Paris, he returned in 1248 to claim his inheritance. Backed by the people of Głogów, he forced his brother Bolesław II in 1251 to cede him Głogów and Żagań.

He promoted German settlement, granted Głogów Magdeburg town law in 1253, and after about 1260 attached himself to King Ottokar II of Bohemia. He died in August 1273 or 1274, leaving Głogów to his son Henry III.

格沃古夫的康拉德一世（约1228—1274）是西里西亚皮亚斯特家族王公，虔敬者亨里克二世之子。他原本被安排走教会道路、送往巴黎求学，却在1248年回国要求分得遗产。在格沃古夫市民的支持下，他于1251年迫使兄长波列斯瓦夫二世割让格沃古夫和萨根。

en:
Mechthild of Brunswick-Lüneburg (1276–1318) was the only daughter of Albert I of Brunswick-Lüneburg and Alessia of Montferrat. In 1291 she married Henry III of Głogów, allying the Welf and Piast dynasties against Henry V the Fat of Legnica, and bore him nine children.

When Henry died in 1309 she regented his Silesian duchies until 1312, although their eldest son Henry IV was already of age. Under his will Głogów was hers as a dower. She died on 26 April 1318, and Głogów passed jointly to her sons Henry IV and Przemko II.

zh:
不伦瑞克-吕讷堡的玛蒂尔达（1276—1318）是不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公爵阿尔布雷希特一世与蒙费拉托的阿德莱德唯一的女儿。1291年她嫁给格沃古夫公爵亨里克三世，韦尔夫家族与皮雅斯特家族因此结盟，共同对付莱格尼察的胖子亨里克五世；她为亨里克生下九个子女。

1309年丈夫去世后，尽管长子亨里克四世已成年，她仍摄政统治西里西亚诸公国直至1312年。依丈夫遗嘱，格沃古夫作为寡妇产由她持有。她于1318年4月26日去世，格沃古夫由儿子亨里克四世和普热姆科二世共同继承。

en:
Przemko II of Głogów (c. 1305–1331), youngest son of Henry III and Matilda of Brunswick-Lüneburg, ruled jointly with his brothers after 1309, receiving Głogów in 1318 and ruling alone from 1321.

After 1329 he was the only one of Henry III's sons to refuse homage to King John of Bohemia, saying he would rather lose his inheritance than serve a foreign ruler; his brothers deposed him. He died suddenly on 11 January 1331, reportedly poisoned by his own vassals, and that autumn John of Bohemia seized Głogów.

en:
Berdi Beg (c. 1310–1359) was khan of the Golden Horde from 1357. When his father Jani Beg conquered Azerbaijan in 1357, Berdi was left viceroy in Tabriz; recalled in his father's final illness, he succeeded amid rumors of patricide. He secured his throne by executing at least twelve kinsmen, even killing an infant brother himself.

He signed a trade treaty with Venice in 1358 and restored the Russian Church's privileges. He died in 1359, possibly murdered, opening two decades of civil war, and later accounts held the line of Batu ended with him.

zh:
别儿迪别（约1310—1359年）自1357年起为金帐汗国可汗。1357年其父札尼别征服阿塞拜疆后，他以副王身份留守大不里士；父亲病危时被召回继位，时人怀疑是他策划了父亲之死。他为巩固汗位处死至少十二名亲族，甚至亲手杀死襁褓中的幼弟。

1358年他与威尼斯签订通商条约，并恢复罗斯教会的特权。1359年他死去，可能遇弑，金帐汗国随之陷入长达二十年的内乱。后世记载认为拔都一脉随他的去世而绝嗣。

en:
Öz Beg (1282–1341), whose Muslim name was Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad, ruled the Golden Horde from 1313, longer than any other khan, at its zenith. His father Toghrilcha was executed by Toqta, who exiled the boy; a Bukharan sheikh is said to have converted him to Islam there. When Toqta died in 1313 he took the throne with his vizier's help.

He divided the realm into seventy tumens and abolished the baskak system, leaving princes to collect the tribute. He built New Sarai, whose bazaars and broad streets Ibn Battuta later praised. He repeatedly attacked Ilkhanid Azerbaijan and favoured Moscow in the princes' quarrels.

In 1331 he made Ivan I Kalita grand prince. A Russian proverb, ‘Near the tsar, near death,’ is thought to date from his reign. He died in 1341, and his sons Tini Beg and then Jani Beg followed him.

zh:
月即别（1282—1341），教名吉亚斯丁·穆罕默德，1313年起统治金帐汗国，在位最久，国势达到鼎盛。其父秃黑里勒察被脱脱处死，他自幼被流放，相传由一位布哈拉谢赫引入伊斯兰教。1313年脱脱去世，他在宰相协助下夺得汗位。

他把汗国分为七十个万户，废除达鲁花赤制度，由王公自行征收贡赋。他修建新萨莱城，其集市与宽阔街道后来受伊本·白图泰称赞。他屡次进攻伊儿汗国治下的阿塞拜疆，又在王公纷争中偏袒莫斯科。

1331年他册立伊凡一世·卡利塔为大公。俄罗斯谚语“近沙皇，近死亡”相传出自他的时代。他于1341年去世，其子迪尼别与继之的札尼别先后继位。

en:
Jani Beg (died 1357) was khan of the Golden Horde from 1342. A son of Öz Beg Khan, he eliminated his elder brother Tini Beg and was elected with his mother Taydula Khatun's support. He intervened in the Russian principalities, backing Moscow's princes, and Russian chroniclers called him 'the good tsar'.

His quarrel with the Italian colonies led to the long siege of Kaffa, traditionally linked to the Black Death's arrival in Europe. In 1357 he took Tabriz and died on the way home; contemporaries suspected that his son Berdi Beg ordered his murder.

In 1357 he took Tabriz and died on the way home; contemporaries suspected that his son #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('glh_berdi_beg_borjigin').GetID],X #L Berdi Beg#!#! ordered his murder.
zh:
札尼别（？—1357年）自1342年起为金帐汗国可汗。他是月即别汗之子，除掉长兄迪尼别后，在母亲泰都拉王后支持下经库里勒台当选。他介入罗斯诸公国事务，扶植莫斯科王公，罗斯编年史称他为“善良的沙皇”。

他与意大利殖民地的冲突导致卡法遭长期围攻，此事在传统说法中与黑死病传入欧洲有关。1357年他攻取大不里士，回师途中去世，时人怀疑其子别儿迪别下令弑父。

en:
Tini Beg (died 1342) was briefly khan of the Golden Horde in 1341–1342. A son of Öz Beg Khan and Taydula Khatun, he was his father's designated heir and governed the White Horde from about 1328. When Öz Beg died in 1341, Tini Beg was fighting Chagatai raiders while his brother Jani Beg held Sarai.

On his way back in 1342 he was killed at Saray-Jük by emirs incited by his mother, who favored Jani Beg. Pope Benedict XII had once written urging him to convert to Christianity.

Davyd Konstantinovich (died 1280) was the second prince of the Galich-Dmitrov principality, succeeding his father Konstantin Yaroslavich at Galich and Dmitrov in 1255. In 1276 he married the eldest daughter of Prince Fyodor Rostislavich the Black of Yaroslavl.

The chronicles record his death as Prince Davyd, grandson of Yaroslav, prince of Galich and Dmitrov. He was the last ruler known to hold both towns together, and after his death in 1280 his brother Vasily Konstantinovich became prince of Galich.

en:
Fyodor Davydovich was prince of Galich-Mersky, a son of Davyd Konstantinovich of Galich-Dmitrov by his marriage to a daughter of Prince Fyodor Rostislavich the Black of Yaroslavl. After his uncle Vasily's death, the family lands may have passed to his nephews and been divided: Fyodor received Galich-Mersky and Boris took Dmitrov.

Nothing is recorded of his rule, though genealogies claim he sold half of Galich to Ivan Kalita of Moscow. A prince Fyodor whose death the Nikon Chronicle records in 1335 has been identified as him. He left a single son, Ivan.

费奥多尔·达维多维奇是加利奇-梅尔斯基王公，加利奇-德米特罗夫王公达维德·康斯坦丁诺维奇与雅罗斯拉夫尔王公费奥多尔·罗斯季斯拉维奇‘黑者’之女所生之子。叔父瓦西里死后，家族领地可能由侄辈继承并瓜分：费奥多尔得到加利奇-梅尔斯基，鲍里斯分得德米特罗夫。

Konstantin Yaroslavich (died 1255) was the first appanage prince of Galich-Mersky and Dmitrov, a son of Grand Prince Yaroslav Vsevolodovich of Vladimir and brother of Alexander Nevsky. The chronicles first name him in 1238 among the princes who survived Batu's invasion.

In 1243 he went to Karakorum while his father visited Batu, and he remained with the Mongols until 1245. After Yaroslav's death he received Galich and Dmitrov as his appanage. He died in 1255, leaving two sons, Davyd and Vasily.

en:
Ernst II of Gleichen-Harburg (c. 1152 – 1170) was a son of Count Ernst I of Tonna. From 1152 he ruled with his brother Erwin II as count of Gleichenstein, holding Harburg Castle in the Eichsfeld and the advocacy of Gerode Abbey. In 1162 he founded the Cistercian Reifenstein Abbey at Kleinbartloff.

His castles of Harburg and Rusteberg were destroyed in 1165 during wars between the archbishops of Mainz and the Thuringian landgraves, who captured him and had him beheaded in 1170.

en:
Ernst III von Gleichen, called zu Velseck (died 1230), was a son of Count Erwin II of Gleichen-Tonna and a brother of Lambert II. The family's castle of Velsecke in the Eichsfeld was first documented in 1180 and later rebuilt as Gleichenstein.

He married Berta of Lohra. Lambert's sons divided the comital house into the Gleichen and Gleichenstein branches. Ernst died in 1230.

en:
Ernst IV von Gleichen (1198–16 May 1277) was a son of Count Lambert II and Sophie of Weimar-Orlamünde, and after the family partition he headed the Gleichen line of the comital house. A knight as well as a count, he married two Danish noblewomen in succession, Ingeborg Pedersdatter and Margrete Olufsdatter.

His sons included Erwin III and Heinrich IV, who served as a knight and royal councillor in Sweden; under Heinrich's grandsons this line later split into the Blankenhain and Tonna branches.

en:
Erwin I (c. 1040 – c. 1116) is the earliest known member of the comital house of Gleichen in Thuringia. He first appears in charters in 1099 as count at Tonna and is named count in Thuringia in 1114. Late in life he became a monk at Reinhardsbrunn Abbey.

By his wife Helinburg, daughter of Count Beringer I of Lohra, he left two sons who carried the line forward, Ernst I of Tonna and Lambert I.

Erwin II (c. 1124 – 7 September 1192) was the son of Count Ernst I of Tonna. He appears in 1154 as count of Tonna and Vogt of Gerode Abbey, and in 1162 he is the first of his line to style himself count of Gleichen, the name his dynasty afterwards bore.

He died on 7 September 1192 and was buried in the Peterskloster in Erfurt. His sons, among them Lambert II and Ernst III, divided the inheritance.

en:
Heinrich I von Gleichenstein (c.1202–1257) was a son of Count Lambert II of Gleichen. On the division of his father's inheritance he took the Eichsfeld lands.

After Velsecke Castle was destroyed in war in 1234, he rebuilt it in 1241–1246 as Gleichenstein and took the castle's name for his line. He ruled as count of Gleichenstein until his death on 20 January 1257; his wife was Mechtild of Schwerin.

Heinrich III von Gleichenstein (died 1299) was the last count of the Gleichenstein branch in the Eichsfeld. His comital house had fallen deep into debt.

en:
Lambert II, also numbered III, von Gleichen-Tonna (died 14 September 1227) was a Saxon count and, from 1193, archiepiscopal Vogt of Erfurt and its Peterskloster. He married Sophie of Weimar-Orlamünde.

His sons Ernst IV and Heinrich I founded the two comital lines of Gleichen and Gleichenstein, while another son, Hermann, became bishop of Cammin. Lambert's grave slab, which later became linked to the legend of the count with two wives, survives in Erfurt Cathedral.

en:
Alan of Galloway (before 1199–1234) was hereditary Lord of Galloway and Constable of Scotland. Succeeding his father Roland in 1200, he led the Scottish crown's forces and advised King John over Magna Carta.

His intervention in the Norse kingdom of the Isles drew a retaliatory fleet from the king of Norway, and Norse sagas ranked him among the great warriors of his age. He died in February 1234 leaving daughters as heirs. Alexander II partitioned Galloway among them, ending the native line of rulers.

加洛韦的艾伦（1199年前—1234）是世袭加洛韦领主兼苏格兰统帅。他于1200年继承父亲罗兰之位，统领苏格兰王室军队，曾在《大宪章》时期为英王约翰献策。
