en:
Dervorguilla of Galloway (c. 1210–1290) was a Scottish heiress, daughter of Alan, Lord of Galloway and Margaret of Huntingdon, descended through her mother from King David I. She married John de Balliol in 1223 and became one of her father's heirs on his death in 1234; her royal descent underpinned her son John Balliol's claim to Scotland's throne.

After her husband's death in 1269 she kept his embalmed heart in an ivory casket, and in 1273 founded the Cistercian Sweetheart Abbey near Dumfries. In 1282 she endowed and gave statutes to Balliol College, Oxford. She died on 28 January 1290 and was buried at the abbey.

加洛韦的德沃尔吉拉（约1210—1290）是苏格兰女继承人，加洛韦领主艾伦与亨廷顿的玛格丽特之女，随母系为大卫一世后裔。1223年她嫁给约翰·德·巴利奥尔，1234年父亲去世后成为继承人之一；其王室血统成为儿子约翰·巴里奥日后争夺苏格兰王位的依据。

1269年丈夫死后，她将丈夫的心脏防腐保存在象牙匣中；1273年在邓弗里斯附近创建西多会的斯威特哈特修道院。1282年，她为牛津大学贝利奥尔学院设立永久基金并颁行章程。1290年1月28日去世，葬于该修道院。

en:
Helen of Galloway (b. c. 1215, fl. thirteenth century) was a daughter and co-heiress of Alan, Lord of Galloway, by his first wife, a daughter of Roger de Lacy, Constable of Chester. She became the first wife of Roger de Quincy, Earl of Winchester, who died in 1264, and was the mother of his three daughters.

Through them her Galloway inheritance reached leading Anglo-Scottish houses: Margaret married William de Ferrers, Elizabeth married Alexander Comyn, and Helen married Alan de la Zouche.

en:
Adolf II (c. 1300–1347) ruled the County of the Mark from the death of his father Engelbert II in 1328. His first marriage, to Irmgard of Cleves, was dissolved in 1324, and a papal dispensation allowed him to wed Margaret of Cleves, through whom his sons later inherited Cleves.

He died at Fröndenberg in October 1347 and was succeeded by his eldest son Engelbert III; his younger son Adolf became Count of Cleves in 1368.

Adolf III of the Mark (c. 1334–1394), second son of Adolf II and Margaret of Cleves, was made Bishop of Münster in 1357 and briefly served as Archbishop-Elector of Cologne in 1363, resigning to pursue the Cleves inheritance. He succeeded the childless Count John of Cleves in 1368.

In 1369 he married Margaret of Jülich. After his brother Engelbert III died without heirs in 1391, he inherited the Mark also and gave it to his son Dietrich in 1393.

Dietrich I of the Mark (1336–1406) was the third son of Count Adolf II of the Mark and Margaret of Cleves. He became provost of Cologne Cathedral, but after being elected Bishop of Liège he declined the see and returned to secular life.

When his brother Adolf secured Cleves in 1368, Dietrich received most of the Cleves lands on the right bank of the Rhine, ruling there as lord until his death.

Eberhard I of the Marck-Arenberg (c. 1305–1387), a younger son of Count Engelbert II of the Mark, was first trained as a cleric. He studied canon law at Orléans and in 1339 became provost of Münster Cathedral, later a canon and cantor at Cologne.

In 1351 he left the Church to marry Maria of Looz, through whom he gained Peer and Neufchâteau in the Ardennes, and inherited Arenberg from his mother, founding the Mark-Arenberg line.

en:
Eberhard I von der Mark (c.1255–4 July 1308) became count in 1277, after his father Engelbert I, abducted by Count Herman of Lohn, died imprisoned at Bredevoort; in 1278 Eberhard stormed the castle in revenge.

From 1281 he allied with neighbouring counts against the Archbishops of Cologne and fought at Worringen in 1288, where victory freed the County of Mark from Cologne's overlordship. By his wife Irmgard of Berg he fathered his successor, Engelbert II.

1281年起，他与邻近诸伯爵结盟对抗科隆大主教，1288年战于沃林根并获胜，此役使马克伯国摆脱科隆的宗主权。妻子贝格的伊尔姆加德为他生下继承人恩格尔贝特二世。

en:
Engelbert II (1275–1328) ruled the County of Mark from 1308, succeeding his father Eberhard I, and through his 1299 marriage to Mechtilde of Arenberg also held Arenberg. He fought the bishops of Münster and Cologne, capturing Bishop Ludwig of Münster when he marched into Hamm in 1323 and freeing him only after payment of five thousand silver marks.

In the throne dispute between Frederick the Fair and Ludwig IV, he backed Ludwig. On his death his sons Adolf II and Eberhard inherited Mark and Arenberg.

zh:
恩格尔贝特二世（1275—1328）于1308年继父亲埃伯哈德一世之后成为马克伯爵；1299年他与阿伦贝格的梅希蒂尔德成婚，由此兼领阿伦贝格。他与明斯特和科隆的主教对抗：1323年明斯特主教路德维希进军哈姆时被他俘获，支付五千马克白银的赎金后才获释。

在美男子腓特烈与路德维希四世争夺德意志王位期间，他支持路德维希四世。他去世后，儿子阿道夫二世与埃伯哈德分别继承马克和阿伦贝格。

en:
Engelbert III of the Mark (1333–1391), eldest son of Adolf II and Margaret of Cleves, succeeded as Count of the Mark in 1347. When his brother Adolf inherited Cleves in 1368, Engelbert received its lands east of the Rhine.

He allied with Cologne against the Count of Arnsberg, then fought Cologne again in 1376–1377 after Arnsberg was sold to the archbishopric. He married twice but left no son, and after dying of plague at Wetter in December 1391 was succeeded by Adolf.

en:
Engelbert III of the Mark (1304–1368), second son of Count Engelbert II, became provost of Liège in 1332 and its Prince-Bishop in 1345. He at once faced a city revolt: defeated in 1346, he beat the rebels in 1347 and ended the unrest with concessions.

He lost the Cologne see to his nephew Adolf in 1362, but Pope Urban V made him Archbishop and Elector of Cologne in 1364 after Adolf resigned. Ailing, he appointed a coadjutor in 1366 and died in August 1368.

Margaret of the Mark (died 1409) was a daughter of Count Adolf II of the Mark and Margaret of Cleves. Betrothed as a child to the future John I of Nassau-Siegen in 1343, she married him in 1357. The marriage brought John revenues in the County of the Mark and claims to Cleves.

She bore four sons, Adolf I, John II, Engelbert I and John III. They jointly succeeded their father as counts of Nassau-Siegen in 1416.

en:
Margaret of Cleves (c. 1310 – after 1348) was a daughter of Count Dietrich VIII of Cleves and Margaret of Guelders. In 1332 she married Count Adolf II of the Marck, bearing him seven children, among them Engelbert III and Adolf III.

In 1333 her father issued an inheritance law settling Cleves on Margaret and her sisters, but his brother John had it repealed in 1338. After Adolf and Dietrich both died in 1347, Margaret pressed her claim against John, who prevailed; her son Adolf finally secured the county in 1368.

克莱沃的玛格丽特（约1310—1348年后）是克莱沃伯爵迪特里希八世与海尔德的玛格丽特之女。1332年，她嫁给马克伯爵阿道夫二世，生下恩格尔贝特三世、阿道夫三世等七个子女。

1333年她的父亲颁布继承法，规定克莱沃由玛格丽特姐妹继承，但叔父约翰于1338年促成废除该法。阿道夫二世与迪特里希八世于1347年相继去世后，玛格丽特向约翰主张继承权未果；她的儿子阿道夫最终于1368年取得克莱沃伯国。

Agnes of Chalon (died after October 1350) was the daughter of Count John I of Chalon. In 1285 she married Count Amadeus II of Geneva, allying him with her brother John of Chalon-Arlay and his Habsburg connections. She bore five children, among them William III, who succeeded his father.

Amadeus's will of 1306 named her regent, but on his death in 1308 the adult William claimed power; her brother mediated a settlement in 1311. She made her will in October 1350 and chose Geneva's Franciscan church as her burial place.

Agnes of Savoy (1286–1322) was a daughter of Count Amadeus V of Savoy. In 1297, amid the wars between Geneva and Savoy, she was contracted to marry William, heir to the County of Geneva, who became Count William III in 1308.

Their son Amadeus, the future Amadeus III of Geneva, was born in 1311, and they also had two daughters. William died in 1320, leaving Agnes her dowry and Genevois lands. She died on 4 October 1322 and was buried at Hautecombe Abbey.

en:
Amadeus II (died 22 May 1308) was Count of Geneva from 1280, succeeding his brother Aymon II. A son of Count Rudolf of Geneva and Marie de Coligny, he inherited a county burdened by debt and surrounded by the expanding lands of Savoy.

From 1282 he fought Amadeus V of Savoy in coalitions, but by 1287 had to do homage at Annemasse. Renewing the war in 1304, he built the fortress of Gaillard near Geneva and accepted papal arbitration in 1306.

He married Agnes of Chalon in 1285 and died near Vuache castle in 1308. Geneva passed to his son William III.

From 1282 he fought #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('sav_amedee_v_savoy').GetID],X #L Amadeus V of Savoy#!#! in coalitions, but by 1287 had to do homage at Annemasse. Renewing the war in 1304, he built the fortress of Gaillard near Geneva and accepted papal arbitration in 1306.

He married #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('gnv_agnes_chalon').GetID],X #L Agnes of Chalon#!#! in 1285 and died near Vuache castle in 1308. Geneva passed to his son #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('gnv_guillaume_iii_geneve').GetID],X #L William III#!#!.
zh:
阿梅迪奥二世（1308年5月22日卒）自1280年起任日内瓦伯爵，继承兄长艾蒙二世。他是日内瓦伯爵鲁道夫与玛丽·德·科利尼之子，接手的伯国债务沉重，四周被扩张中的萨伏依领地包围。

1282年起他加入反萨伏依同盟，与萨伏依的阿梅迪奥五世作战，但到1287年被迫在阿讷马斯宣誓效忠。1304年战事再起，他在日内瓦附近修建加亚尔堡垒，1306年接受教皇仲裁。

1285年他娶沙隆的阿涅丝为妻，1308年死于维阿什城堡附近。日内瓦由其子纪尧姆三世继承。

en:
Amadeus III of Geneva (1311–1367) succeeded his father William III as count in 1320, under the regency of his grandmother Agnes of Chalon and mother Agnes of Savoy until 1325. He ruled the Genevois but not the city of Geneva. Caught between Savoy and the Dauphin of Viennois, he fought at Varey in 1325 against his uncle Count Edward of Savoy, then in 1329 did homage to Count Aymon of Savoy, ending nearly a century of conflict.

From 1343 he shared the regency of Savoy with Louis II of Vaud for the boy count Amadeus VI. In 1355 he had to admit defeat as Savoy swept its neighbours, leaving his county enclosed by Savoyard lands.

In 1358 Charles IV took him under imperial protection, outside Savoyard jurisdiction. He died in 1367. Five sons succeeded him in turn, the last becoming the Avignon antipope Clement VII.

阿梅迪奥三世（1311—1367）1320年继承父亲纪尧姆三世为日内瓦伯爵，1325年前由祖母沙隆的阿涅丝与母亲萨伏依的阿涅丝摄政。他统治日内瓦伯领，但不包括日内瓦城。在萨伏依与维埃诺王太子的旧怨中，他1325年在瓦雷战役中对阵舅父萨伏依伯爵爱德华，1329年又向萨伏依伯爵艾蒙行臣服礼，结束近百年的冲突。

1343年起，他与沃男爵路易二世共同为年幼的萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥六世摄政。1355年萨伏依大举进攻邻国，他被迫认输，伯国从此被萨伏依领地包围。

1358年皇帝查理四世将他置于帝国保护之下，使他脱离萨伏依管辖。他于1367年去世，五个儿子相继继位，幼子后来成为阿维尼翁对立教宗克雷芒七世。

en:
Amadeus IV of Geneva (died 4 December 1369) was the second son of Amadeus III and Mathilde d'Auvergne, and one of five brothers who held the county in turn. In 1367 he succeeded his childless elder brother Aymon III, and that year confirmed the franchises of Annecy.

His father and brother had kept close to Savoy; he reversed that policy and backed the bishops of Lausanne and Geneva against his cousin Count Amadeus VI of Savoy, yet on 13 May 1368 did homage to Amadeus for the county. He then joined Amadeus's Italian campaign against Philip II of Piedmont and attended Philip's trial at Rivoli, possibly hoping to speak with the Emperor.

In February 1369 Charles IV revoked the Savoyard count's vicariate and declared Geneva an immediate imperial fief. Amadeus died that December.

阿梅迪奥四世（？—1369年12月4日）是阿梅迪奥三世与玛蒂尔达·德·奥弗涅的次子，也是先后执掌伯国的五兄弟之一。1367年无嗣的兄长艾蒙三世去世，他继任日内瓦伯爵，同年确认阿讷西的城市特许状。

父亲和兄长一向亲近萨伏依，他却反其道而行，支持洛桑和日内瓦主教对抗表兄萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥六世，但1368年5月13日仍为伯国向阿梅迪奥六世行臣服礼。随后他参加征讨皮埃蒙特的腓力二世的意大利战事，并在里沃利出席审判，或许想借机面见皇帝。

1369年2月，皇帝查理四世撤销萨伏依伯爵的帝国代理权，宣布日内瓦为帝国直领封地。同年12月阿梅迪奥去世。

en:
Eleanor of Joinville was the daughter of William of Joinville, seigneur of Gex, and Joan of Savoy. On the death of her brother Hugh, the last of the Joinville-Gex line, she inherited the barony of Gex. In 1351 she married Hugh of Geneva, who held Gex through her and refused homage to Count Amadeus VI of Savoy.

Savoyard troops seized Gex in 1354, and the treaty of Paris in 1355 assigned the Pays de Gex to Savoy. Her marriage was childless.

埃莉诺·德·茹安维尔是热克斯领主纪尧姆·德·茹安维尔与让娜·德·萨伏依的女儿。其兄于格——茹安维尔-热克斯家族最后一位领主——去世后，她继承了热克斯男爵领。1351年，她嫁给于格·德·日内瓦，后者凭她的身份领有热克斯，并拒绝向萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥六世效忠。

en:
William III of Geneva (1280–1320) was count of Geneva from 1308, when he succeeded his father Amadeus II. A 1291 treaty with Savoy first betrothed him to Beatrice of Savoy, and after its annulment he married her sister Agnes, daughter of Count Amadeus V, in 1297.

His succession brought a dispute with his mother Agnes of Chalon, settled by agreement in 1308. That October he made perpetual peace with Savoy, acknowledging several castles as its fiefs, and in 1316 he did homage to the dauphin of Viennois.

His children with Agnes included Amadeus III, born in 1311, who succeeded him. He made his will at Annecy in April 1319 and died the following year.

en:
Mathilde d'Auvergne (c. 1318 – 24 October 1399) was a daughter of Count Robert VII of Auvergne and Boulogne. In 1334 she married Count Amadeus III of Geneva and bore him ten children, five sons and five daughters. The five sons succeeded to Geneva in turn, and the youngest, Robert, became the Avignon antipope Clement VII.

As pope he left the government of the county to his mother and named his nephew Humbert of Villars as heir. When Robert died in 1394 she and her daughters contested Humbert's succession, claiming usufruct of the county in a 1395 suit.

She made her will at Rumilly in 1396 and died in 1399. Her surviving daughters Blanche and Catherine inherited her goods and rights, and Blanche took the title of countess of Geneva.

玛蒂尔达·德·奥弗涅（约1318—1399年10月24日）是奥弗涅与布洛涅伯爵罗贝尔七世之女。1334年她嫁给日内瓦伯爵阿梅迪奥三世，生有五子五女。五个儿子相继继承日内瓦，幼子罗贝尔成为阿维尼翁对立教宗克雷芒七世。

他以教宗之身把伯国政务交给母亲，并指定外甥安贝尔·德·维拉尔为继承人。1394年罗贝尔去世后，守寡的伯爵夫人与女儿们对安贝尔的继承提出异议；她在1395年开始的诉讼中要求取得伯国的用益权。

她1396年在吕米伊立下遗嘱，1399年去世。幸存的女儿布朗什与卡特琳继承她的财产和权利，布朗什还承袭日内瓦女伯爵头衔。

en:
Gonçalo da Silveira (1526–1561) was a Portuguese Jesuit born at Almeirim, the tenth child of the first count of Sortelha. He joined the Society of Jesus at Coimbra and from 1555 served as provincial superior of the Jesuits in India. In 1560 he sailed for south-east Africa, and in 1561 reached the court of the Mwenemutapa Negomo.

He refused the king's gifts and gave him a painting of the Virgin Mary, then instructed and baptised the king, his mother and hundreds of Shona nobles. A traditional account relates that rivals accused him of witchcraft and spying, and he was strangled on 15–16 March 1561 and thrown into the Musengezi River.

贡萨洛·达·西尔韦拉（1526—1561）是葡萄牙耶稣会传教士，生于阿尔梅林，为第一代索尔特利亚伯爵的第十个孩子。他在科英布拉加入耶稣会，1555年起任耶稣会印度省会长。1560年他前往非洲东南部，1561年抵达姆韦尼穆塔帕内戈莫的宫廷。

他拒收国王的馈赠，赠予国王一幅圣母像，随后教导国王与王母并为他们及数百名绍纳贵族施洗。按传统说法，政敌指控他行巫术、充当间谍，1561年3月15至16日他被勒死，尸体抛入穆森盖济河。

en:
Albert I of Gorizia (c. 1240 – 1 April 1304) was the younger son of Count Meinhard III and Adelaide of Tyrol. After their father was defeated by Carinthian and Salzburg forces, Albert and his brother Meinhard IV were held hostage at Hohenwerfen Castle from 1253 until their release in 1262. The brothers ruled jointly until dividing their inheritance in 1271, when Albert kept the County of Gorizia and lands in Friuli, Istria and Carniola.

He fought the Venetians alongside the patriarchs of Aquileia and backed Rudolf I against Ottokar II of Bohemia. His sons Henry III and Albert II succeeded him in turn.

zh:
阿尔贝一世（约1240—1304年4月1日）是戈里齐亚—蒂罗尔伯爵迈因哈德三世与蒂罗尔的阿德尔海德的幼子。父亲被克恩滕与萨尔茨堡军队击败后，他和兄长迈因哈德四世1253年起被扣在霍恩韦尔芬城堡为人质，1262年获释。兄弟二人共同统治，1271年瓜分领地，阿尔贝获得戈里齐亚伯国及弗留利、伊斯特拉、卡尼奥拉等地的领地。

他联合阿奎莱亚牧首与威尼斯作战，并支持鲁道夫一世对抗波希米亚国王奥托卡二世。他的儿子亨利三世和阿尔贝二世相继继位。

Albert II of Gorizia (died 1327 at Lienz) was a son of Count Albert I by his second wife Euphemia and the younger half-brother of Count Henry II. After Albert I partitioned the county in 1303, the Lienz treaties of 1307 assigned him the Anterior County, ruled from Bruck Castle near Lienz.

He built the Lienz town wall in 1311 and in April 1327 licensed a Jewish bank there. His wife Euphemia of Matsch bore the future counts Albert III, Henry III and Meinhard VI.

阿尔贝二世（1327年卒于利恩茨）是阿尔贝一世伯爵与第二任妻子奥伊菲米娅所生的儿子，海因里希二世伯爵的同父异母弟弟。阿尔贝一世1303年瓜分伯国后，1307年的《利恩茨分割条约》把后来所称的“前伯国”分给他，他在利恩茨附近的布吕克城堡统治。

他于1311年修筑利恩茨城墙，1327年4月批准在当地开设一家犹太银行。妻子马奇的奥伊菲米娅生下后来的伯爵阿尔贝三世、海因里希三世和迈因哈德六世。

en:
Albert III of Gorizia (died 1374) was the eldest son of Count Albert II and Elizabeth of Hesse. He governed Gorizia, Friuli and Istria as regent for his minor cousin John Henry IV until 1338, when the brothers inherited the county and ruled jointly.

In 1339 Albert became sole count palatine of Carinthia, and in 1342 he waived his share of Gorizia for Istria, the Windic March and Metlika. His two marriages, to Helen and Catherine of Celje, were both childless.

阿尔贝三世（1374年卒）是戈里齐亚伯爵阿尔贝二世与黑森的伊丽莎白的长子。1338年之前，他代年幼的堂弟约翰·亨利四世管理戈里齐亚、弗留利和伊斯特拉；1338年兄弟几人共同继承伯国。

en:
Anne of Austria (1318–1343) was the youngest daughter of Frederick the Fair, King of the Romans, and Isabella of Aragon. After her father's reconciliation with Emperor Louis IV, she married Duke Henry XV of Lower Bavaria in 1328; the union was childless and Henry died in 1333.

In 1336 she married Count John Henry IV of Gorizia and was widowed a second time in 1338. She returned to Vienna, joined the Poor Clares and from 1341 served as abbess of their convent, where she died aged twenty-five.

en:
Beatrix of Lower Bavaria (1302–1360) was a Wittelsbach princess, the daughter of Duke Stephen I of Lower Bavaria and Jutta of Schweidnitz. In 1322 she married Count Henry III of Gorizia and bore him John Henry IV. When Henry died in 1323, the infant succeeded to the county and Beatrix served as co-regent of the Gorizia lands.

After Patriarch Pagano of Aquileia died in 1332, she took over its secular government. In 1333 the Friulian parliament named her captain general of Friuli.

en:
Engelbert I (died 14 December 1122) was an early count of the Meinhardiner dynasty and the elder brother of Count Meinhard I of Gorizia. After the Aribonid count Rapoto V died in 1099, Engelbert received the Bavarian count palatinate, and in 1102–1104 inherited further Aribonid lands, including the advocacy of Millstatt Abbey.

He ruled the Gorizia lands in the upper Puster Valley jointly with his brother Meinhard I, and in 1122 he ceded the Millstatt advocacy to the Holy See.

en:
Engelbert II (died 1 April 1191) was a younger son of Count Meinhard I of Gorizia and Elisabeth of Schwarzenburg. First mentioned in 1137 as advocate of Millstatt Abbey, he was made Count Palatine of Carinthia about 1145, and in 1150 inherited Gorizia from his elder brother Henry II, ruling it until his death.

A loyal Hohenstaufen supporter, he rivalled the Andechs dukes of Merania in Istria. By his wife Adelaide of Scheyern he fathered Engelbert III and Meinhard II.

The son of Count Engelbert II, he inherited the county jointly with his brother Meinhard II on their father's death, and during his reign held the advocacies of Aquileia and Millstatt Abbey.

In 1183 he married Matilda, Countess of Pisino, and in 1190 remarried Matilda of Andechs. The second Matilda bore his successor, Meinhard III.

en:
Euphemia of Matsch (died around 1353) was the daughter of Ulrich II, bailiff of Matsch. She became the second wife of Albert II of Gorizia, who ruled the county as regent for his nephew John Henry IV from 1323 until his death in 1327.

Her sons Henry V and Meinhard VI and their half-brother Albert III succeeded as counts after John Henry IV died in 1338. In 1349 she and her sons founded the Carmelite monastery at Lienz, built for twelve friars. She is last documented around 1353.

en:
Henry III of Gorizia (c. 1263 – April 1323) was the elder son of Count Albert I and Euphemia of Głogów. In 1295–1299 he joined his father's invasion of Istria against Aquileia, taking several towns before a patriarchal army forced them to withdraw. He succeeded as count in 1304, inheriting the family's fiefs in Friuli, Istria, Carniola and Carinthia.

He first fought the patriarch alongside Rizzardo IV da Camino, then changed sides in 1310 to become the patriarchate's captain general and drive Treviso's troops from Friuli, and was podestà of Trieste in 1311. By Beatrix da Camino he had Meinhard V, and by Beatrix of Lower Bavaria John Henry IV.

戈里齐亚伯爵亨利三世（约1263—1323年4月）是阿尔贝一世与格沃古夫的奥伊菲米娅的长子。1295至1299年，他随父亲入侵伊斯特拉、进攻阿奎莱亚牧首区，攻占数座城镇后因牧首军队到来而撤退。1304年他继位为伯爵，继承家族在弗留利、伊斯特拉、卡尼奥拉和克恩滕的封地。

他起初联合里扎尔多四世·达·卡米诺与牧首作战，1310年倒戈成为牧首区统帅，将特雷维索军队逐出弗留利，1311年出任的里雅斯特长官。第一任妻子贝阿特丽丝·达·卡米诺生下迈因哈德五世；第二任妻子下巴伐利亚的贝娅特丽克丝生下约翰·亨利四世。

en:
John Henry IV of Gorizia (1322–1338), the only son of Count Henry III and Beatrix of Lower Bavaria, succeeded his father in 1323 as an infant. His mother, uncle Albert II and, after 1329, cousin Albert III acted as regents. In 1332, aged nine, Trieste elected him its podestà against Venetian expansion.

His betrothal to Beatrice of Sicily was cancelled in 1335; by the treaty of Ljubljana he married Anna of Habsburg, daughter of anti-king Frederick the Fair, in a childless marriage. He died in 1338 and was buried at Rosazzo Abbey, succeeded by Albert II's sons.

en:
Meinhard VI of Gorizia (died 1385) was the son of Count Albert II and Euphemia of Matsch. In 1338 he inherited Gorizia with his brothers Albert III and Henry V, and ruled alone from 1365. His claim to Tyrol failed when Countess Margaret ceded the county to Rudolf IV of Austria in 1363.

He weakened the patriarchate of Aquileia, but Venice gained most; his debts forced him to mortgage Gorizia estates and withdraw to Schloss Bruck in Lienz. He married twice, and his son Henry VI succeeded him after his death in 1385.

zh:
迈因哈德六世（1385年卒）是戈里齐亚伯爵阿尔贝二世与曼德沙伊德的奥伊菲米娅之子。1338年，他与兄弟阿尔贝三世、亨利五世共同继承戈里齐亚，1365年起独自统治。他对蒂罗尔的继承权落空：1363年女伯爵玛格丽特将蒂罗尔让给奥地利公爵鲁道夫四世。

他削弱了阿奎莱亚牧首区，最大受益者却是威尼斯；债务迫使他抵押戈里齐亚地产，退居利恩茨的布鲁克城堡。他两次婚姻，1385年去世后由儿子亨利六世继位。

en:
Meinhard I (died 1142) of the Meinhardiner dynasty was advocate of the Patriarchate of Aquileia and the first of his house documented as Count of Gorizia. He first appears in an Aquileia charter in 1120–1121; around 1120 he and his brother Engelbert I joined a patriarchal donation to a church of Saint John.

In 1139 the patriarchate's villages complained about his ruthless tax collectors. In January 1142 he witnessed for King Conrad III at Regensburg; dying, he granted three vineyards to Saint Peter's Abbey, Salzburg.

The Aquileia and Millstatt necrologies date his death to 14 September 1142. His wife Elissa of Schwarzenburg bore him the future counts Engelbert II and Henry II.

zh:
迈因哈德一世（1142年卒）是迈因哈德家族成员，任阿奎莱亚宗主教区护院官，也是家族中第一个有文献记载的戈里齐亚伯爵。1120—1121年，他首次出现在阿奎莱亚的文书中；约1120年，他与兄弟恩格尔贝特一世参与了宗主教向一座圣约翰教堂的捐赠。

1139年，宗主教区的村庄控诉他的税吏横征暴敛。1142年1月，他在雷根斯堡为国王康拉德三世作证，临终前把三处葡萄园赠给萨尔茨堡的圣彼得修道院。

阿奎莱亚和米尔施塔特的亡者名录把他的卒日定于1142年9月14日。妻子施瓦岑堡的伊丽莎白为他生下后来的伯爵恩格尔贝特二世和海因里希二世。

en:
Meinhard II, called the Elder (c. 1163 – 1231), was a younger son of Count Engelbert II of Gorizia and Vogt (reeve) of the Patriarchate of Aquileia. In 1192 he tried to seize Richard the Lionheart, shipwrecked near Aquileia returning from crusade, but the king escaped into Austria. He joined Emperor Henry VI's crusade of 1197.

Quarrels with the patriarchal church earned him temporary excommunication around 1216. In 1220 he succeeded his brother Engelbert III as count of Gorizia. Meinhard married three times, but none of his children survived childhood; his nephew Meinhard III succeeded him.

迈因哈德二世，绰号“长者”（约1163—1231），是戈里齐亚伯爵恩格尔贝特二世的幼子，曾任阿奎莱亚牧首区的福格特（行政代管人）。1192年，英王狮心王理查十字军东征归途在阿奎莱亚附近遇险，迈因哈德企图将他擒获，但理查逃入奥地利。他还参加了皇帝亨利六世1197年发动的十字军。

他与牧首区教会的争执使他在约1216年被短暂处以绝罚。1220年他继兄长恩格尔贝特三世任戈里齐亚伯爵。他结过三次婚，但子女都夭折，死后由侄子迈因哈德三世继位。

en:
Meinhard III (c.1200–1258) was Count of Gorizia from 1231 and, jure uxoris, Count of Tyrol as Meinhard I from 1253. An ally of Emperor Frederick II against Pope Innocent IV, he governed Styria, Carniola and Austria as imperial governor after 1246, until Ottokar II expelled him in 1251.

Defeated at Greifenburg in September 1252, he surrendered his sons as hostages under the Peace of Lieserhofen, then secured southern Tyrol in 1253. He died on 22 July 1258, leaving sons Meinhard II and Albert I.

zh:
迈因哈德三世（约1200—1258）1231年起任戈里齐亚伯爵，1253年又凭借妻权成为蒂罗尔伯爵（称迈因哈德一世）。作为皇帝腓特烈二世反对教皇英诺森四世的盟友，1246年后他以帝国总督身份治理施蒂利亚、卡尼奥拉和奥地利，1251年被奥托卡二世驱逐。

1252年9月他在格赖芬堡战败，被迫按《利瑟霍芬和约》交出儿子作为人质，1253年取得南蒂罗尔。1258年7月22日他去世，留下儿子迈因哈德二世和阿尔贝一世。

en:
Meinhard V of Gorizia (born after 1297, died after 1318) was a son of Count Henry III and his first wife Beatrix da Camino. Little is recorded of his life, but he probably ruled jointly with his father.

Around 1314 Henry III negotiated his marriage to a daughter of King James II of Aragon. Meinhard died before his father, and in 1323 the county passed to his younger half-brother John Henry IV.

en:
Abu Said Faraj ibn Ismail (1248–1320) was a Nasrid prince, nephew of Muhammad I and trusted adviser to Sultans Muhammad II and Muhammad III. Brought to court after his father's death, he befriended the future Muhammad II and later married his daughter Fatima.

In 1279 he became governor of Málaga, the emirate's chief port. He restored the city's economy, built up the Granadan navy and in 1306 led the conquest of Ceuta.

In 1311 he rebelled against Sultan Nasr to place his son Ismail on the throne, but his forces failed to besiege the capital. When he tried to surrender Málaga to the Marinids, Ismail deposed and imprisoned him; he died in 1320.

zh:
阿布·赛义德·法拉杰·本·伊斯玛仪（1248—1320）是奈斯尔王朝宗室，穆罕默德一世之侄，也是穆罕默德二世和穆罕默德三世两任素丹信赖的顾问。父亲去世后他被带入宫廷，与日后的穆罕默德二世结为朋友，后来娶其女法蒂玛为妻。

1279年他出任马拉加总督，马拉加是埃米尔国最重要的港口。他恢复当地经济、造船充实格拉纳达海军，1306年率军攻占休达。

1311年他起兵反对素丹纳斯尔，企图拥立儿子伊斯玛仪登基，但军队未能围攻首都。后来他试图把马拉加献给马林王朝，被伊斯玛仪废黜囚禁，1320年死于狱中。

en:
Bahar was a woman of Christian origin who became an umm walad, a freed concubine, of Sultan Ismail I of Granada. Her only child was Ismail's third son Yusuf, born in the Alhambra on 29 June 1318; he lived in her house until 1333, when at fifteen he took the throne as Yusuf I after his brother Muhammad IV was assassinated. His reign and his son's were later seen as Granada's golden age.

The vizier Ibn al-Khatib praised her good deeds, chastity and equanimity. In 1350, with Yusuf sick, she gave Ibn Battuta money for his stay when he sought an audience.

zh:
巴赫是基督教地区出身的女子，成为格拉纳达素丹伊斯梅尔一世的“乌姆·瓦莱德”，即生子后获释的妾。她唯一的孩子是伊斯玛仪的第三子优素福，1318年6月29日生于阿兰布拉宫。优素福一直住在她的住所，1333年其兄穆罕默德四世遇刺，十五岁的他继位，称优素福一世；他和儿子的统治后来被视为格拉纳达的黄金时代。

维齐尔伊本·哈提卜称赞她乐善好施、持身贞静、性情平和。1350年伊本·白图泰到格拉纳达请求觐见，适逢优素福病中，巴赫赠给他停留期间所需的钱财。

en:
Fatima bint al-Ahmar (c. 1260–1349) was the Nasrid princess who held her dynasty together through a run of coups and boy sultans. A daughter of Sultan Muhammad II of Granada, she was trained in the barnamaj, the biobibliographies of Islamic scholars, and married her father's cousin and adviser Abu Said Faraj, governor of Málaga.

When her half-brother Nasr grew unpopular she joined the factions against him: her husband rebelled in 1311, and in 1314 their son Ismail deposed Nasr and reigned as Ismail I, the first Nasrid to inherit the throne through the female line. She helped him govern.

She served as guardian when Muhammad IV took the throne at ten and later Yusuf I at fifteen, and Ibn al-Khatib called her 'the Sultan's Grandmother'. She died in 1349; his elegy for her is the only one ever written for a Nasrid princess.

法蒂玛·宾特·艾哈迈尔（约1260—1349）是在接连政变和幼主继位中撑住奈斯尔王朝的公主。她是格拉纳达素丹穆罕默德二世之女，精通“巴尔纳马吉”之学，即伊斯兰学者传记目录学；她嫁给父亲的堂亲兼顾问、马拉加总督阿布·赛义德·法拉杰。

异母弟纳斯尔渐失人心时，她与谋求推翻他的派系结盟：丈夫1311年起兵，1314年其子伊斯玛仪推翻纳斯尔，登基为伊斯梅尔一世，成为首位经由母系继承王位的奈斯尔君主。她协助儿子治国。

穆罕默德四世十岁继位、后来优素福一世十五岁继位时，法蒂玛都担任监护人，伊本·哈提卜称她为“素丹的祖母”。她1349年去世，伊本·哈提卜为她写的挽歌是奈斯尔王朝唯一献给公主的挽歌。

en:
Abu Abdallah ibn al-Hakim al-Rundi (1261 – 14 March 1309) was a Ronda-born scholar and poet of the Banu al-Hakim, a branch of the Abbadid dynasty. After studying in the east from 1284 he entered Sultan Muhammad II's chancery in 1287 as a secretary.

Under Muhammad III he became sole vizier in 1303 with the title dhu al-wizaratayn. He made peace with Castile and seized Ceuta from the Marinids, provoking a triple alliance of Castile, Aragon and the Marinids, and his policies and extravagant life angered the people of Granada.

On 14 March 1309 a mob sacked his palace. Muhammad III was deposed and Abu Abdallah was killed by his rival Atiq ibn al-Mawl.

阿布·阿卜杜拉·伊本·哈基姆·伦迪（1261—1309年3月14日）出生于龙达，是学者兼诗人，出身阿拔德王朝支系巴努·哈基姆家族。1284年他赴东方求学，1287年进入苏丹穆罕默德二世的中书省任秘书。

穆罕默德三世在位时，他1303年成为唯一的维齐尔，获得“两府维齐尔”尊号。他与卡斯蒂利亚议和，又从马林王朝手中夺取休达，招致卡斯蒂利亚、阿拉贡与马林王朝三方结盟；他的政策和奢侈生活激怒了格拉纳达民众。

1309年3月14日，暴民洗劫他的府邸。穆罕默德三世被废，阿布·阿卜杜拉被政敌阿提格·伊本·毛勒杀死。

en:
Lisan al-Din Ibn al-Khatib (16 November 1313 – 1374) was the great polymath of Nasrid Granada: poet, historian, physician, philosopher and, for much of his life, vizier. Born at Loja, he lost his father and brother at the Battle of Río Salado in 1340, then served his teacher Ibn al-Jayyab, Yusuf I's vizier, succeeding him when he died of plague.

The coup of 1359 put him in prison; the Marinid sultan secured his release, and he spent three years in Moroccan exile before returning in 1362 when Muhammad regained the throne. His verses decorate the Alhambra, and his history of Granada, al-Ihata, was written in 1369.

In 1371, with Muhammad V grown wary of him and the Grand Qadi al-Nubahi branding his Sufi writings heretical, he left Granada again. Tried for heresy at Fes, he was strangled in 1374, and his enemies had his body dug up and burned.

利桑丁·伊本·哈提卜（1313年11月16日—1374）是奈斯尔王朝格拉纳达的全才学者，身兼诗人、史家、医生、哲学家，大半生任维齐尔。他生于洛哈，1340年父兄在萨拉多河战役中战死，此后在老师、优素福一世的维齐尔伊本·贾亚布手下任秘书，伊本·贾亚布死于鼠疫后接任维齐尔。

1359年政变后他被捕入狱，马林苏丹出面将他救出，他流亡摩洛哥三年，1362年穆罕默德复位后返回。他的诗句装饰着阿兰布拉宫，所著《格拉纳达全史》1369年成书。

1371年穆罕默德五世对他心生戒备，大法官努巴希又斥他的苏非著作为异端，他再次离开格拉纳达。1374年他在非斯以异端罪名受审，被缢死，仇敌还掘出他的遗体焚烧。

en:
Ismail I ibn Faraj (1279–1325), fifth Nasrid sultan of Granada from 1314, was a grandson of Muhammad II. After his father Abu Said Faraj's rebellion against Sultan Nasr failed, Ismail resumed the revolt and forced Nasr to abdicate in 1314.

At the Battle of the Vega on 25 June 1319 his forces routed Castile, killing both royal regents, and Castile ended its support for Nasr. In 1324–1325 he took a string of towns including Baza and Martos, using cannons in a siege for the first time in Iberia. He enlarged the Alhambra and Generalife. In July 1325 a kinsman assassinated him.

伊斯梅尔一世·本·法拉杰（1279—1325）是格拉纳达奈斯尔王朝第五任素丹，1314年起在位，穆罕默德二世的外孙。其父阿布·赛义德·法拉杰反对素丹纳斯尔的叛乱失败后，他继续起兵，于1314年迫使纳斯尔退位。

1319年6月25日的维加战役中，他的军队大败卡斯蒂利亚军，击毙两位摄政亲王，卡斯蒂利亚随后停止支持纳斯尔。1324年至1325年，他连克巴萨、马托斯等城，并在围城战中首次于伊比利亚半岛使用火炮。他为阿尔罕布拉宫和赫内拉利费宫增建了建筑。1325年7月，他被一名宗室亲属刺杀。

en:
Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn Nasr (c. 1195–1273), called Ibn al-Ahmar, was founder of the Nasrid dynasty and first emir of Granada, the last independent Muslim state on the Iberian Peninsula. He seized his native Arjona in 1232 and entered Granada in 1237.

In 1246 he surrendered Jaén to Ferdinand III of Castile and became his vassal, even aiding the Christian capture of Seville in 1248. In 1264 he turned against Castile and supported an unsuccessful Muslim rebellion; two years later his former allies rebelled against him. He began building the Alhambra. He died in 1273 after a fall from his horse.

穆罕默德·本·优素福·本·奈斯尔（约1195—1273），别号伊本·艾哈迈尔，是奈斯尔王朝的缔造者、格拉纳达埃米尔国第一任埃米尔——该国是伊比利亚半岛最后一个独立穆斯林政权。1232年他在故乡阿尔霍纳起兵，1237年入主格拉纳达。

1246年，他将哈恩交给卡斯蒂利亚国王斐迪南三世并向其称臣，甚至在1248年协助基督徒攻占塞维利亚。1264年他转而反对卡斯蒂利亚，支持一场失败的穆斯林起义；两年后，他的旧盟友也起兵反对他。他动工修建阿尔罕布拉宫。1273年，他坠马后去世。

en:
Muhammad ibn Faraj was a Nasrid prince, younger son of the Málaga governor Abu Said Faraj and brother of Sultan Ismail I. During his nephew Muhammad IV's minority, the commander Uthman ibn Abi al-Ula rose against the vizier and in 1327 proclaimed Muhammad rival sultan at Andarax, with backing from Castile.

Muhammad IV called in Marinid troops, but the war stalemated. In 1328 the young sultan reconciled with Uthman and ordered the vizier killed; the pretender was captured and exiled to North Africa.

穆罕默德·本·法拉杰是奈斯尔王朝宗室，马拉加总督阿布·赛义德·法拉杰的幼子，素丹伊斯梅尔一世之弟。侄子穆罕默德四世年幼在位时，大将奥斯曼·本·阿比·乌拉起兵反对宰相，于1327年在安达拉斯拥立穆罕默德为对立素丹，并得到卡斯蒂利亚支持。

穆罕默德四世召来马林王朝军队，内战却陷入僵局。1328年，年轻的素丹与奥斯曼和解并下令杀死宰相；这位僭位者被俘，流放北非。

en:
Muhammad II (c. 1235–1302), called al-Faqih, the canon lawyer, succeeded his father Muhammad I as the second Nasrid emir of Granada in 1273. He maneuvered between Castile and the Marinids of Morocco, suppressing the Banu Ashqilula revolt and recovering Málaga in 1279.

In 1292 he helped Castile seize Tarifa, then switched sides when Sancho IV kept the town; after Sancho's death in 1295 his forces took Quesada and Alcaudete. A patron of scholars and poets, he organized the Volunteers of the Faith, expanded the Alhambra and promoted trade.

zh:
穆罕默德二世（约1235—1302），别号“法基赫”（教法学家），1273年继承父亲穆罕默德一世，成为格拉纳达奈斯尔王朝的第二任埃米尔。他在卡斯蒂利亚与摩洛哥马林王朝之间纵横捭阖，镇压巴努·阿什基卢拉家族的叛乱，于1279年收复马拉加。

1292年他协助卡斯蒂利亚夺取塔里法，桑乔四世拒绝交出该城后便转与马林王朝结盟。1295年桑乔死后，格拉纳达军队攻占克萨达和阿尔考德特。他优待学者和诗人，组建“信仰志愿军”，扩建阿尔罕布拉宫，并发展贸易。

en:
Muhammad III (1257–1314), called al-Makhlu, the Deposed, ruled the Nasrid Emirate of Granada from 1302. He captured Bedmar from Castile in 1303 and became Ferdinand IV's vassal in 1304. In 1306 he seized Ceuta from the Marinids, driving Castile, the Marinids and Aragon into coalition.

Nearly blind and dominated by vizier Ibn al-Hakim, he was deposed in 1309 in favour of his half-brother Nasr. After two restoration plots, he was drowned in an Alhambra pool in 1314. A poet, he built the Partal Palace and the Alhambra's Great Mosque.

穆罕默德三世（1257—1314），别号“迈赫卢”（被废黜者），1302年起统治格拉纳达埃米尔国。1303年他从卡斯蒂利亚手中夺取贝德马尔，1304年向斐迪南四世称臣。1306年他从马林王朝手中夺取休达，促使卡斯蒂利亚、马林王朝和阿拉贡结盟反对格拉纳达。

他晚年几乎失明，大权旁落于维齐尔伊本·哈基姆，1309年在宫廷政变中被异母弟纳斯尔取代。两度复位图谋失败后，他于1314年被溺死在阿尔罕布拉宫的水池中。他善于作诗，修建了帕尔塔尔宫和阿尔罕布拉大寺。

en:
Muhammad IV (1315–1333), son of Ismail I and Alwa, became sixth Nasrid sultan of Granada in 1325 after his father's assassination. Civil war followed between vizier Ibn al-Mahruq and Uthman ibn Abi al-Ula, who with Castilian backing proclaimed his uncle sultan.

He ceded Ronda, Marbella and Algeciras to the Marinids, probably in exchange for their aid, then in 1328 took power, reconciling Uthman and killing the vizier. In 1333 he helped the Marinids capture Gibraltar and made peace with Castile; the day after the truce he was assassinated on the orders of Uthman's sons, and his brother Yusuf I succeeded.

穆罕默德四世（1315—1333）是伊斯梅尔一世与阿勒瓦之子，1325年父亲遇刺后，他成为格拉纳达奈斯尔王朝第六任素丹。即位不久爆发内战：维齐尔伊本·马赫鲁克与乌斯曼·伊本·阿比·乌拉相争，后者得到卡斯蒂利亚支持，拥立他的叔父为对立素丹。

en:
Muhammad VI (1333–1362), nicknamed el Bermejo, the Red One, was the tenth Nasrid sultan of Granada. In August 1359 he led a coup that deposed Muhammad V and installed Ismail II, whom he executed in 1360 to seize the throne.

In the War of the Two Peters he allied with Aragon against Castile, but after Aragon made a separate peace in 1361, Peter I of Castile and the returning Muhammad V overwhelmed him. He fled and surrendered at Seville in 1362, where Peter killed him with a lance and sent his head to Granada.

en:
Nasr (1287–1322), fourth Nasrid sultan of Granada, was enthroned in 1309 when a palace revolution deposed his brother Muhammad III. He inherited a three-front war against Castile, Aragon and the Marinids, buying peace with territorial cessions.

Suspected of pro-Christian sympathies and mocked for his astronomy, he repulsed an initial revolt in 1311. A renewed rebellion forced him to abdicate to his nephew Ismail I in 1314. He then ruled Guadix as a vassal and sought Castilian help. He died without heirs in 1322.

纳斯尔（1287—1322）是格拉纳达奈斯尔王朝第四任素丹。1309年，一场宫廷政变废黜了他的兄长穆罕默德三世，将他推上王位。他接手的是与卡斯蒂利亚、阿拉贡和马林王朝三面作战的局面，只能以割地换取和平。

他被怀疑亲基督教，又因沉迷天文学而遭讥议。1311年他击退了一场首次叛乱，但叛乱再起后，他于1314年被迫向外甥伊斯梅尔一世退位。此后他以附庸身份统治瓜迪克斯，寻求卡斯蒂利亚帮助。1322年，他无嗣而终。

en:
Yusuf I (1318–1354), seventh Nasrid sultan of Granada, came to the throne at fifteen in 1333 after his brother Muhammad IV was murdered, at first ruling in name only under his grandmother Fatima. In 1334 his envoys secured a four-year peace with Castile and the Marinids.

When it lapsed he allied with the Marinids against Alfonso XI of Castile, and the allies were crushed at the Río Salado in 1340; Algeciras fell in 1344. When Alfonso died of the Black Death outside Gibraltar in 1350, Yusuf ordered his commanders not to attack the Castilians carrying their king's body home, then made peace with Peter I.

Granada lost ground yet flourished under him: he founded the Madrasa Yusufiyya and enlarged the Comares Palace, with Ibn al-Khatib as his vizier. He was stabbed while praying in the Great Mosque on Eid al-Fitr in 1354, and his son Muhammad V succeeded him.

优素福一世（1318—1354）是格拉纳达奈斯尔王朝第七任苏丹。1333年其兄穆罕默德四世遇刺，十五岁的他继位，起初在祖母法蒂玛监护下徒有其名。1334年，他的使者与卡斯蒂利亚及马林王朝议定四年和约。

和约期满后，他与马林王朝联手对抗卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索十一世，却在1340年萨拉多河战役中惨败，阿尔赫西拉斯于1344年陷落。1350年阿方索在直布罗陀城下死于黑死病，优素福下令不得攻击护送国王遗体的卡斯蒂利亚人，随后与佩德罗一世议和。

战场屡有失地，格拉纳达却文教兴盛：他创办优素福经学院，扩建科马雷斯宫，伊本·哈提卜曾任他的维齐尔。1354年开斋节，他在大清真寺礼拜时遇刺，其子穆罕默德五世继位。

en:
Johann I von Hals (died 1347) was count of the imperial county of Hals, seated at Castle Hals on the Ilz near Passau in Lower Bavaria. The only son of Count Albert VII, he belonged to the von Kamm lineage, which had styled itself von Hals since 1160. In 1337 he married Margareta of Leuchtenberg.

A pious donor, he gave a holding at Stiegelheim to Aldersbach monastery in 1341. Their son Leopold became the last count of Hals.

约翰一世·冯·哈尔斯（1347年卒）是直辖于神圣罗马帝国的哈尔斯伯国伯爵，治所为下巴伐利亚帕绍附近伊尔茨河畔的哈尔斯城堡。他是阿尔布雷希特七世伯爵的独子，属于自1160年起以冯·哈尔斯为姓的卡姆家族，1337年娶洛伊希滕贝格的玛格丽特为妻。

Leopold von Hals (died 1370) was the last count of the imperial county of Hals, seated at Castle Hals on the Ilz near Passau in Lower Bavaria. The son of Count Johann I, he married Anna of Magdeburg in 1360, but the marriage remained childless.

With his death the male line of the von Kamm counts of Hals ended, and his lands became the object of a long inheritance dispute between Leuchtenberg and Ortenburg.

en:
Togha Temür (died 1353) was the last strong claimant to the Ilkhanate from the house of Genghis Khan, and the only one from eastern Iran. A descendant of Genghis's brother Qasar, he led the nomadic Chete, and his power rested on Gorgan and western Khorasan.

When the Ilkhan Abu Sa'id died heirless in 1335 and the realm fell apart, eastern amirs backed him. His march west in 1337 took the capital Soltaniyeh, but the Jalayirid Hasan Buzurg defeated him and sent him home; in 1338 Hasan made him Ilkhan in return for help, though the alliance soon soured.

He never reunited the Ilkhanate, spending his last years fighting the Sarbadars of western Khorasan without subduing them. In December 1353 their leader came to his camp and killed him and his household, and most of his lands passed to the Sarbadars.

zh:
脱合帖木儿（？—1353）是成吉思汗家族最后一位有实力问鼎伊儿汗位的宗王，也是其中唯一出自伊朗东部的一位。他是成吉思汗之弟合撒儿的后裔，统领游牧切特部，势力根基在戈尔甘和呼罗珊西部。

1335年伊儿汗不赛因无嗣而终，汗国四分五裂，东部异密们拥立他为伊儿汗。1337年他西征占领都城苏丹尼耶，却被札剌亦儿王朝的大哈散击败退回；1338年大哈散以立他为伊儿汗为条件求援，双方很快反目。

他始终未能重统伊儿汗国，晚年长期与呼罗珊西部的萨尔巴达尔人作战而无法征服。1353年12月，萨尔巴达尔首领来到他的军营，将他和家族杀害，他的大部分领地落入萨尔巴达尔人之手。

en:
Mehmed Chakhshadan was Bey of Germiyan from 1340 to 1361, succeeding his father Yakub I at Kütahya. His nickname Chakhshadan meant the fighter or warrior.

His forces retook Kula and Angir, modern Simav, from the Catalan Company. Yet Germiyan lost its former dominance, for the Aydınid beylik became independent in his reign. He died in 1361 and was succeeded by his elder son Suleiman Shah.

Suleiman Shah, known as Shah Chelebi (died 1387), was Bey of Germiyan from 1361, succeeding his father Mehmed Chakhshadan at Kütahya. After backing the Hamidids against the Karamanids, he sought Ottoman protection and in 1381 married his daughter Devletşah Hatun to Murad I's son Bayezid.

The dowry surrendered several towns, including Kütahya, to the Ottomans, so Suleiman withdrew to Kula, where he died in 1387. A generous patron of letters, he had Persian works such as the Kabus-name translated into Turkish.

en:
Yakub I (died c. 1340) founded the Germiyan beylik in western Anatolia, centered on Kütahya. After submitting to the Sultanate of Rum, he became independent as the Seljuk state collapsed, and his domains stretched east to Ankara.

The contemporary al-Umari called him the most powerful Turkish emir, suzerain of his neighbours, with Byzantium paying him one hundred thousand gold pieces a year. The Catalan Company destroyed his army in 1304, and he twice besieged Philadelphia, which finally agreed to tribute around 1311. He died around 1340. He left a prosperous realm to his son Mehmed.

雅库布一世（约1340年卒）在安纳托利亚西部建立了以屈塔希亚为中心的盖尔米扬贝伊国。他起初臣服于鲁姆苏丹国，塞尔柱国家瓦解后获得独立，疆土向东远达安卡拉。

en:
William II of Gruyères (fl. first half of the twelfth century) was the first count to bear the title count of Gruyères, appearing as Willelmus comes de Grueria in 1144. The eldest son of Count William I, he and his brother Radbod were co-lords of Marsens.

The brothers were among the donors who founded Humilimont Abbey near Marsens. His wife's name is unknown, and he was succeeded by his son Rudolf I.

en:
Peter I of Gruyères (c. 1162 – after 1200) was a younger son of Count Rudolf I and Agnes of Glâne. He first appears as count in an 1197 charter beside his brother Rudolf II, renouncing rights in favour of Hauterive Abbey with the consent of their mother Agnes.

A charter of 1200 again names both brothers as counts, when they were forced to surrender Riaz and Albeuve to the bishopric of Lausanne. Peter died without issue, and the county passed to Rudolf II.

en:
Peter II, called the Elder (1224–c. 1304), was count of Gruyère, the eldest son of Rodolphe III and Colombe of Belmont. He served as avoué of Vevey and had shared in ruling the county with his father since 1264.

His heir, his eldest son Peter the Younger, died before him in 1283. The young man's widow, Guillemette of Grandson, then ran much of the county and used the title countess from 1291. Peter died around 1304 and his grandson Peter III followed him as count.

彼得二世，绰号‘年长者’（1224—约1304），格吕耶尔伯爵，鲁道夫三世与贝尔蒙的科隆布之长子。他出任沃韦的护尉，自1264年起便与父亲共同治理伯国。

en:
Peter III of Gruyères (1279–1342), grandson of Count Peter II, was the younger son of Peter the Younger. He first assisted his grandfather as lord of Gruyères before succeeding as count, when he left the lordships of Montsalvens and Le Vanel to his nephews. In 1307 he and his wife founded the Part-Dieu Charterhouse.

He added Les Ormonts and several castles to his domains, became avoyer of Fribourg in 1330, and promoted cattle trading and cheese production. He died late in 1342 and was buried at Part-Dieu.

en:
Peter IV of Gruyères, also called Perrod (c. 1280–1365), was the son of Rodolphe of Gruyères and nephew of Count Peter III, who raised him and his brother John after they were orphaned young. Knighted around 1327, he was made bailiff of the Pays de Vaud in 1329, and in 1342 he succeeded his uncle as count, ruling jointly with his brother John.

In 1352 he joined the confederacy of Bern and Fribourg, and in 1359 he granted Gruyères its charter of liberties. His second wife Catherine de la Tour-Châtillon bore his successor Rodolphe IV.

en:
Rodolphe II of Gruyère (c. 1170–1224) was a count of Gruyère, a younger son of Count Rodolphe I and Agnès of Glâne. Destined for the church, he was called the cleric in an 1173 charter, but in 1197 he married Gertrude, probably of Montagny.

He tried to revive the market of Gruyères, which his father had surrendered in 1195 to please the bishop of Lausanne, until Bishop Berthold of Neuchâtel forced him to desist. His son Rodolphe III succeeded him.

zh:
鲁道夫二世（约1170—1224）是格吕耶尔的伯爵，为伯爵鲁道夫一世与格拉讷的阿涅丝之幼子。他本被安排投身教会，1173年的一份特许状称他为‘教士’；1197年，他迎娶很可能出身蒙塔尼家族的格特鲁德。

他试图恢复格吕耶尔集市——其父已于1195年为迁就洛桑主教将其废止——但主教纳沙泰尔的贝特霍尔德迫使他作罢。死后由儿子鲁道夫三世继位。

en:
Rodolphe III, called the Younger (c. 1200–1269/1270), was count of Gruyère and the eldest son of Rodolphe II and Gertrude of Montagny. He had to surrender the estate of Ogens, his wife Colombe of Belmont's dower land, to William of Ecublens, bishop of Lausanne.

On 19 April 1244, under pressure from Count Peter II of Savoy, he yielded Gruyères Castle as freehold; the fief was regranted to his son William. His son Peter II succeeded him.

鲁道夫三世，绰号‘年轻人’（约1200—1269/1270），格吕耶尔伯爵，是鲁道夫二世与蒙塔尼的格特鲁德的长子。他被迫把妻子贝尔蒙的科隆布作为嫁资带来的奥让领地交给洛桑主教埃屈布朗的纪尧姆。

en:
Bernard I (c. 1245–c. 1286), a son of Nicholas I of Werle and Jutta of Anhalt, first appears in a charter in 1273. From 1277 he ruled Werle jointly with his brothers Henry I and John I, and when the lands were divided in 1281 he received Prisannewitz.

He last appears in 1282; by 1288 his nephew Nicholas II called him dead, and 1286 is considered his likely death year. He was buried at Doberan Minster, leaving no documented heirs.

Henry I (c. 1245–1291) ruled Werle from 1277, first jointly with his brothers John I and Bernard I after the death of their father Nicholas I, and from the partition of 1281 as lord of Werle-Güstrow.

In 1291 his sons Henry and Nicholas, fearing for their inheritance after his second marriage to Matilda of Brunswick-Lüneburg, struck him down during a hunt near Saal. They were soon ousted by Henry's nephew Nicholas II, who reunited Werle.

en:
Henry II of Werle (born after 1262, died after 1308) was a son of Henry I, Lord of Werle-Güstrow, and Rikissa Birgersdotter. With his brother Nicholas he murdered their father during a hunt near Saal, fearing his second marriage would threaten their inheritance.

Henry then held the lordship of Penzlin into the Margrave's War, while his cousin Nicholas II seized the succession. He disappears from charters after the patricide.

His wife was a daughter of Duke Barnim I of Pomerania. Their son Barnim became a canon at Cammin and their daughter Mechthild a prioress at Pyritz.

zh:
维尔勒的海因里希二世（1262年后生，1308年后卒）是维尔勒-居斯特罗领主海因里希一世与里基莎·比耶格斯多塔之子。他担心父亲再婚会危及继承权，便与兄弟尼古拉在萨尔附近的狩猎中杀死父亲。

此后他占据彭茨林领地，一直撑到藩侯战争时期，但继承权落入堂兄尼古拉二世之手。弑父之后，特许状中便不再出现他的名字。

他的妻子是波美拉尼亚公爵巴尔宁一世之女。两人的儿子巴尔尼姆成为卡明的座堂参事，女儿梅希蒂尔德成为皮里茨的女修院院长。

He married Sophia, daughter of Count Gunther of Lindow-Ruppin, and was buried in Doberan Minster. His son Nicholas II later reunited the Werle lands.

en:
John II, called the Bald (born after 1250, died 1337), was the second son of John I of Werle. From 1309 he shared Werle with his brother Nicholas II, who withdrew from government after travelling to Montpellier in 1311 in hope of a cure for leprosy.

When Nicholas died in 1316, Werle was divided again: John took Werle-Güstrow and his nephew John III took Werle-Goldberg. In 1326 Christopher II of Denmark promised him the Rügen estates, but his claims could not be enforced in the War of the Rügen Succession.

Burdened with debt, John cleared it through host-desecration trials against Jews in Güstrow. He died in 1337 and was buried in Doberan Minster.

约翰二世，绰号“秃头”（1250年后生，1337年卒），是维尔勒的约翰一世的次子。自1309年起，他与兄长尼古拉二世共同统治维尔勒；1311年尼古拉前往蒙彼利埃希望治好麻风病，此后退出政务。

1316年尼古拉去世，维尔勒再度分家：约翰得到维尔勒-居斯特罗，侄子约翰三世得到维尔勒-戈尔德贝格。1326年，丹麦国王克里斯托弗二世许诺把吕根的地产封给他，但这些要求在吕根继承战争中无法兑现。

约翰负债累累，靠在居斯特罗对犹太人提起的亵渎圣体审判还清债务。他于1337年去世，葬于多贝兰大教堂。

en:
John III, called John van Ruoden (before 1300–1352), took Werle-Goldberg in the 1316 partition after his father Nicholas II died, while his uncle John II kept Werle-Güstrow. In 1317 he married Mechtild, daughter of Duke Otto I of Pomerania.

The Rügen War of Succession broke his finances. In 1326 Christopher II of Denmark promised Rügen to John and Henry II of Mecklenburg, though he had already pledged it to Pomerania; under the eventual peace Pomerania kept Rügen, and John won only a pledge on Tribsees, which Pomerania then conquered.

To pay his war contractors he pledged Laage, Malchin, Stavenhagen and Malchow, most of his land. From 1350 he left rule to his son Nicholas IV. He was gravely ill in 1352 and was probably buried at Malchow Abbey.

约翰三世，绰号“约翰·范·鲁登”（1300年前—1352），1316年父亲尼古拉二世去世、维尔勒分家后得到维尔勒-戈尔德贝格，叔父约翰二世保有维尔勒-居斯特罗。1317年他娶波美拉尼亚公爵奥托一世之女梅希蒂尔德。

吕根继承战争拖垮了他的财政。1326年丹麦国王克里斯托弗二世许诺把吕根封给他和梅克伦堡公爵海因里希二世，却早已把它许给波美拉尼亚；最终和约让波美拉尼亚保住吕根，约翰只得到特里布泽斯的抵押权，该地最终也被波美拉尼亚攻占。

为偿付战争承包商，他把拉格、马尔欣、施塔文哈根和马尔肖等地抵押出去，押掉了大半领地。1350年起他把统治权交给儿子尼古拉四世；1352年他病重，死后可能葬于马尔肖修道院。

en:
Mechtild of Werle-Goldberg (c. 1329–1361) was a daughter of John III, Lord of Werle-Goldberg, and his first wife Mechtild, daughter of Duke Otto I of Pomerania. She married Count Otto I of Schwerin, who ruled the reunited County of Schwerin from 1344 until his death in 1357.

Their daughter Richardis was betrothed to Albert of Mecklenburg and became queen of Sweden when Albert took the Swedish throne, dying as queen in 1377. Mechtild herself died in 1361.

en:
Nicholas I (c. 1210–1277) was a younger son of the Mecklenburg prince Henry Borwin II and ruled as Lord of Rostock from 1229 to 1234, administering it as regent for his younger brother Henry Borwin III. In the 1234 Mecklenburg partition he received Werle.

Fighting with Duke Barnim I of Pomerania against Brandenburg, he lost Perleberg, Wesenberg and Penzlin but secured Parchim, Plau and Goldberg after his brother Pribislaw died. He founded the towns of Penzlin and Röbel. In 1275 he mediated a quarrel between his sons. After his death they divided Werle between them.

zh:
尼古拉一世（约1210—1277）是梅克伦堡诸侯海因里希·鲍尔温二世年纪较小的儿子，1229年至1234年任罗斯托克领主，代弟弟海因里希·博尔温三世执掌罗斯托克。1234年梅克伦堡分封时，他获得维尔勒领地。

他与波美拉尼亚公爵巴尔宁一世联兵对抗勃兰登堡，丧失佩尔莱贝格、韦森贝格和彭茨林，但在兄弟普里比斯拉夫去世后取得帕尔希姆、普劳和戈尔德贝格。他建立了彭茨林和勒伯尔两座城镇。1275年他调解了诸子之争。他去世后，儿子们瓜分了维尔勒。

en:
Nicholas II (before 1275 – 1316) ruled Werle-Parchim from 1283 and, after 1292, the reunited lordship of Werle. When his cousins murdered his uncle Henry I in 1291, Nicholas waged a long war against them and their allies, finally reuniting Werle-Parchim with Werle-Güstrow.

In 1311 he journeyed to Montpellier's famous school of medicine seeking a cure for leprosy. Treatment only slowed the disease, so he withdrew from government and retired to an estate near Güstrow.

His long retreat ended with his death in 1316. Werle was then divided between his son John III and his brother John II.

zh:
尼古拉二世（1275年前—1316）自1283年起统治维尔勒-帕尔希姆，1292年后统治重新统一的维尔勒领地。1291年堂兄弟们杀死叔父海因里希一世后，他与堂兄及其盟友长期作战，最终将维尔勒-帕尔希姆与维尔勒-居斯特罗重新合为一体。

1311年，他前往名医云集的蒙彼利埃求医，希望治愈麻风病。治疗只延缓了病情，他于是退出政务，退居居斯特罗附近的一处庄园。

1316年他在退居中去世。他死后，维尔勒被儿子约翰三世与弟弟约翰二世瓜分。

en:
Nicholas III, called Staveleke (born after 1311, died 1360–1361), was the eldest son of John II, Lord of Werle-Güstrow, and Matilda of Brunswick-Grubenhagen. When his father died in 1337 he ruled alone, and from 1339 jointly with his brother Bernard. In the 1347 partition Bernard received Werle-Waren while Nicholas kept Werle-Güstrow.

In 1338 he married Agnes of Mecklenburg, who bore him Lorenz and John V; his second wife was Mechtild of Holstein-Kiel, mother of his daughter Catherine. He is last attested in 1360.

en:
Nicholas IV, nicknamed Poogenoge or Pig's Eyes (before 1331–1354), son of John III and Mechtild of Pomerania, ruled Werle-Goldberg from 1350 until his death. He inherited a lordship ruined by his father's Rügen war, its chief towns pledged beyond redemption.

He governed jointly with his father at first and alone once John withdrew in 1350. The nickname was said to come from the shape and expression of his eyes.

In 1354 he concluded a regional peace pact, dying later that year. His son John IV succeeded him, while his wife Agnes afterwards married John I of Mecklenburg-Stargard.

en:
Nicholas of Werle-Güstrow (c. 1263–1298) was a son of Henry I, Lord of Werle-Güstrow, and his first wife Rikissa Birgersdotter. Fearing that their father's second marriage would cost them their inheritance, Nicholas and his brother Henry II murdered Henry I during a hunt near Saal on 8 October 1291 and succeeded him in Güstrow.

Their rule was short: their cousin Nicholas II of Werle-Parchim overthrew and persecuted the brothers and reunited Werle. Nicholas died in 1298.

en:
Guarino da Verona (1374–1460) was an Italian Renaissance humanist and a pioneer of Greek studies in Italy. Born in Verona, he spent five years in Constantinople learning Greek under Manuel Chrysoloras, returning in 1408 with Greek manuscripts; it was said that losing one case of them in a shipwreck turned his hair grey overnight.

He taught Greek in Verona, Venice and Florence before becoming professor at Ferrara in 1436 under Marquis Leonello d'Este. He interpreted for Byzantine envoys at the councils of Ferrara and Florence, translated Strabo and some of Plutarch's Lives, and compiled a Greek grammar.

维罗纳的瓜里诺（1374—1460）是意大利文艺复兴人文主义者、意大利希腊学研究的先驱。他生于维罗纳，曾在君士坦丁堡师从赫里索洛拉斯攻读希腊文五年，1408年携希腊文手稿回国。相传一箱手稿在海难中丢失，使他一夜白头。

他先后在维罗纳、威尼斯、佛罗伦萨讲授希腊文，1436年在莱昂内洛·德埃斯特侯爵资助下出任费拉拉的希腊文教授。他曾在费拉拉和佛罗伦萨的公会议上为拜占庭使节担任口译，译有斯特拉波的作品和普鲁塔克的部分传记，还编写了一部希腊语法纲要。

en:
Bino Gabrielli was a Guelph nobleman of Gubbio and a son of Pietro di Gabriello, brother of Cante Gabrielli, the Florentine podestà who condemned Dante to exile.

Bino served as podestà of Lucca in 1300 and Orvieto in 1303. In the first half of 1306 he became podestà of Florence and commanded its troops against Pistoia, taking possession of the city after its surrender. On his return to Florence, knights honored him with a golden canopy. His descendants became the first lords of Carbonana Castle.

en:
Cante dei Gabrielli di Gubbio (c. 1260–c. 1335) was an Italian condottiero from a leading Guelph family of Gubbio. Driven out by the Ghibellines in 1300, he returned among men disguised as pilgrims during the feast of St John and took control of the city, becoming its de facto lord.

Entering Florence with Charles of Valois in 1301, he became podestà and in 1302 sentenced Dante Alighieri to lifelong exile. He served repeatedly as podestà of Florence, Siena and other cities.

In 1317 Pope John XXII made him captain general of the Guelph League. He took Assisi in 1321 and later Urbino, and died in Gubbio around 1335.

en:
Gabriello Gabrielli was a Gubbio prelate who became bishop and ruler of his native city. In 1376 he seized the consular offices during a revolt against papal rule. Appointed bishop in 1377, he restored Gubbio to papal authority, and in 1380 returned with cavalry to crush a revolt.

By 1381 he governed the city and received the papal vicariate. Pope Urban VI revoked it in 1383, and Gabriello relinquished his authority over Gubbio. He retired to Cantiano, where he died of plague that autumn.

加布里埃洛·加布里埃利是古比奥的高级教士，后来成为故乡的主教和统治者。1376年，他趁反抗教皇统治的起义掌握了执政官职位。1377年他获任主教，随后使古比奥重归教皇权威，1380年又率骑兵返回镇压起事。

至1381年，他已统治该城，并获教皇任命为代理。1383年教皇乌尔班六世撤销其代理职务，加布里埃洛放弃了对古比奥的权力。他退往坎蒂亚诺，当年秋天死于瘟疫。

en:
Giovanni di Cantuccio Gabrielli, count of Borgovalle, was a Gubbio nobleman who in August 1350 made himself signore of Gubbio, ending Guelph communal rule. That year he razed the castle of Camporeggiano.

In 1351 his troops devastated Fratta during the wars between Perugia and the Visconti. Besieged in 1354 by Cardinal Albornoz, he surrendered Gubbio to the Church, and in 1355 he was imprisoned at Montefalco with his cousin Jacopo Gabrielli.

乔瓦尼·迪·坎图乔·加布里埃利是博尔戈瓦莱伯爵、古比奥贵族。1350年8月，他自立为古比奥领主，结束了圭尔夫派的公社统治，同年夷平坎波雷贾诺城堡。

1351年佩鲁贾与维斯孔蒂家族交战期间，他的军队劫掠了弗拉塔。1354年枢机主教阿尔沃诺斯围攻古比奥，他将城市交给教会；1355年他与表亲雅各波·加布里埃利一同被囚于蒙特法尔科。

en:
Jacopo de' Gabrielli da Gubbio (1295–1363) was born at Gubbio, son of Cante Gabrielli, who as podestà of Florence sentenced Dante to exile. He became podestà of Bologna in 1327 but left rather than swear obedience to the cardinal who was making himself master of the city.

As Siena's war captain he subdued Grosseto and Massa Marittima. Florence made him Conservatore in 1335, and in 1337 he took Arezzo. His harsh and arbitrary rule won him the name of tyrant of Florence, and he was later said to have prepared the way for the Duke of Athens, who seized the city in 1342.

As Senator of Rome in 1338–1339 he restored the Milvian Bridge and other works wrecked by factional fighting. Cardinal Albornoz imprisoned him in 1355 after he refused to surrender a town; reconciled, he became governor of Faenza and Todi, and died in 1363.

雅各布·德·加布里埃利·达·古比奥（1295—1363）生于古比奥，是坎特·加布里埃利之子，其父任佛罗伦萨长官时判处但丁流放。1327年他出任博洛尼亚最高行政长官，却不愿向正在把该城攥进手里的枢机宣誓服从，宁可离职。

他为锡耶纳统兵，先后征服格罗塞托和马萨马里蒂马。1335年佛罗伦萨任命他为国家执政官，1337年他接收了阿雷佐。他行事严酷专断，得了“佛罗伦萨暴君”之名，后人还说他为1342年夺取该城的雅典公爵铺了路。

他于1338—1339年任罗马元老，重修米尔维奥桥等毁于派系争斗的工程。1355年他因拒绝交出城镇遭阿尔沃诺斯枢机囚禁；和解后出任枢机治下的法恩扎和托迪总督，1363年去世。

Rosso Gabrielli was a Gubbio nobleman of the Guelph Gabrielli family and a son of Pietro di Gabriello. He served as podestà of Fossombrone in 1287 and later of Florence.

There, after the battle of Campaldino, he led operations against the castles of Anghiari and Poppi and the lands of Count Guido Novello. He held office at Roccacontrada in 1291–1292 and 1294, and at Siena in 1293.

en:
Guillaume Budé (1467–1540) was France's leading humanist. After studying law at Orléans, he devoted himself to Latin and Greek in his twenties, and won fame with the Annotationes in Pandectas (1508), which applied philology to Roman law, and De Asse (1514), on ancient coins and measures.

Sent as ambassador to Rome under Louis XII and made master of requests under Francis I, he persuaded Francis to found the Collège des Trois Langues, later the Collège de France, and the royal library at Fontainebleau, whose books began the Bibliothèque nationale. In 1533 he helped dissuade the king from banning printing. He died in Paris on 20 August 1540.

纪尧姆·比代（1467—1540）是法国首屈一指的人文主义者。他曾在奥尔良学习法律，二十多岁时潜心研习拉丁语和希腊语，1508年出版以文献学方法研究罗马法的《〈学说汇纂〉评注》，1514年又写成论述古代钱币与度量衡的《论阿司》，由此享誉欧洲。

他在路易十二朝出使罗马，在弗朗索瓦一世朝任请愿官，并推动弗朗索瓦一世创立三语学院（即后来的法兰西公学院）和枫丹白露王室图书馆，后者构成法国国家图书馆的雏形。1533年，他促成国王放弃查禁印刷术。1540年8月20日，他在巴黎去世。

Guru Amar Das (1479–1574) was the third Sikh guru. Born at Basarke, he followed the Vaishnava tradition and made repeated pilgrimages to Haridwar. About sixty when he heard Bibi Amro, daughter of Guru Angad, sing a Nanak hymn in 1539, he became Angad's disciple and succeeded him on 26 March 1552.

From Goindwal he organised the community through the Manji system, appointing representatives to spread the faith, and a Peerah system for women. He gathered its hymns into a pothi that fed into the Adi Granth, banned sati and permitted widow remarriage. He died on 1 September 1574, naming his son-in-law Jetha as Guru Ram Das.

古鲁·阿摩罗·达斯（1479—1574）是锡克教第三任古鲁。他出生于巴萨尔凯，早年信奉毗湿奴派，多次前往赫尔德瓦尔朝圣。1539年，年约六十的他听到古鲁·安加德之女比比·阿姆罗吟唱那纳克的赞美诗，遂成为安加德的弟子，并于1552年3月26日继其位。

他以戈因德瓦尔为中心，通过“曼吉”制度组织教团，委派代表到各地传教，还设立面向女性的“皮拉”制度。他把教团的赞美诗汇编成一部波提，后来成为《阿迪·格兰特》的基础；他还禁止萨蒂、允许寡妇再嫁。他于1574年9月1日去世，临终前立女婿杰塔为继任者，即古鲁·拉姆·达斯。

en:
Guru Angad (1504–1552), born Lehna at Matte-di-Sarai, was the second of the Sikh gurus. His family fled their ancestral village for Khadur in fear of Babur's armies. A priest of the goddess Durga there, he met Guru Nanak at Kartarpur in his late twenties and served him devotedly for six or seven years; on 7 September 1539 Nanak renamed him Angad and installed him as successor.

He led the community from Khadur Sahib on the Beas, adopted and formalised the Gurmukhi alphabet for the Sikh scriptures, and began collecting Nanak's hymns, adding sixty-two or sixty-three saloks of his own. He died on 29 March 1552, having chosen his disciple Amar Das as the third guru.

古鲁·安加德（1504—1552），原名勒希那，出生于马泰迪萨赖，是锡克教第二位古鲁。他的家人因惧怕巴布尔的军队入侵，离开祖居的村庄迁往卡杜尔。他原是卡杜尔供奉难近母女神的祭司，年近三十时在卡尔塔普尔遇见古鲁·那纳克，随后忠心侍奉六七年；1539年9月7日，那纳克为他改名“安加德”，立他为继任者。

他在贝阿斯河畔的卡杜尔萨希卜领导教团，采用并规范了书写锡克教经典的古木基字母，开始收集那纳克的赞美诗，并加入自己所作的六十二或六十三首短诗。他于1552年3月29日去世，临终前选定弟子阿摩罗·达斯为第三任古鲁。

en:
Guru Arjan (1563–1606), the fifth Sikh Guru, succeeded his father Guru Ram Das in 1581. He completed the Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar, where his father had founded the town and built a sacred pool.

He compiled the Adi Granth, collecting the hymns of earlier Gurus and other saints into one scripture installed in the temple, and reorganized the Masand system, urging Sikhs to give one-tenth of their income to fund gurdwaras and communal kitchens.

Arrested on the orders of the Mughal emperor Jahangir for backing the rebel prince Khusrau Mirza, he refused to convert and was put to death in 1606, becoming the first Sikh martyr.

古鲁·阿尔琼（1563—1606）是第五位锡克古鲁，1581年继其父古鲁·拉姆·达斯之位。他建成了阿姆利则的哈曼迪尔·萨希卜庙；他的父亲此前已在那里创建城镇并修建圣池。

他编纂《阿迪·格兰特》，将此前历代古鲁和其他圣徒的颂诗汇成一部圣典安奉于庙中，还整顿马桑德制度，号召锡克人捐出十分之一收入，用于兴建谒师所和公共食堂。

他因支持叛乱王子胡斯劳·米尔扎，被莫卧儿皇帝贾汉吉尔下令逮捕，因拒绝改宗于1606年遇害，成为第一位锡克教殉道者。

en:
Guru Gobind Singh (1666–1708), born Gobind Das in Patna, became the tenth Sikh Guru in 1675 after his father Guru Tegh Bahadur was beheaded on Aurangzeb's orders.

A warrior, poet and philosopher, he fought twenty-one battles against Mughal armies and the hill rajas of the Sivaliks. On Vaisakhi 1699 at Anandpur he founded the Khalsa, a Sikh warrior community, and introduced the Five Ks.

Two of his sons died in battle and two were executed by the Mughal administrator Wazir Khan. He completed the Guru Granth Sahib and named it the eternal Guru, ending the line of human Gurus before his death in October 1708.

古鲁·戈宾德·辛格（1666—1708）原名戈宾德·达斯，生于巴特那，1675年其父古鲁·得格·巴哈杜尔被奥朗则布下令处斩后继任为第十代锡克古鲁。

他集武士、诗人与哲人于一身，与莫卧儿军队及西瓦利克山的土邦主交战二十一次。1699年维萨基节，他在阿南德普尔创立锡克武士团体卡尔萨，并提出“五K”戒律。

他的两个儿子战死，另两个被莫卧儿官员瓦齐尔汗处决。他最终编定《古鲁·格兰特·萨希卜》，宣布这部经典为永恒的古鲁，结束了人代代任古鲁的传承，于1708年10月去世。

en:
Guru Har Krishan (1656–1664) was the eighth Sikh Guru and its youngest, placed on the gaddi at the age of five in 1661 after his father Guru Har Rai disowned his elder son Ram Rai for altering scripture to please Aurangzeb.

In 1664 the emperor summoned the child through Raja Jai Singh to Delhi, apparently intending to replace him with Ram Rai. Har Krishan contracted smallpox there and the meeting was cancelled; he died on 30 March, before his eighth birthday. His last words, Baba Bakala, guided the Sikhs to his grand-uncle Guru Tegh Bahadur as the ninth Guru.

古鲁·哈尔·克利香（1656—1664）是第八位锡克古鲁，也是最年幼的一位：1661年其父古鲁·哈尔·拉伊因长子拉姆·拉伊为讨好奥朗则布篡改经文而与他断绝关系，年仅五岁的克利香遂登古鲁之位。

1664年皇帝通过拉贾斋·辛格把这位幼童召往德里，似有意以拉姆·拉伊取而代之。克利香在德里染上天花，会面因此取消；他于3月30日夭折，未满八岁。他临终留下“巴巴在巴卡拉”的遗言，指引锡克人找到他的叔祖古鲁·得格·巴哈杜尔，是为第九代古鲁。

en:
Guru Har Rai (1630–1661) became the seventh Sikh Guru in 1644, aged fourteen, succeeding his grandfather Guru Hargobind. Though he kept the army Hargobind had built, he avoided war, devoting himself to preaching and care for all living things.

In the Mughal succession war he backed the tolerant prince Dara Shikoh against Aurangzeb and provided him with medical care. Summoned to court in 1660 to explain this support, he sent his elder son Ram Rai, who altered a line of the Adi Granth to please Aurangzeb.

Har Rai disowned Ram Rai and named his younger son Har Krishan his successor. He died in 1661, aged thirty-one.

古鲁·哈尔·拉伊（1630—1661）于1644年成为第七位锡克古鲁，年十四岁，继其祖父古鲁·哈尔戈宾德之位。他保留了祖父建立的军队，却避免战争，致力于传教和爱护众生。

莫卧儿皇位继承战争中，他支持宽厚的王子达拉·舒科，反对奥朗则布，还为达拉提供医疗照护。1660年，他被召入宫廷解释此事，遂派长子拉姆·拉伊前往；后者为讨好奥朗则布而篡改《阿迪·格兰特》中的一句经文。

哈尔·拉伊遂与拉姆·拉伊断绝关系，指定幼子哈尔·克利香继位。他于1661年去世，年仅三十一岁。

en:
Guru Hargobind (1595–1644) became the sixth Sikh Guru in 1606, aged eleven, after his father Guru Arjan was executed on Jahangir's orders. He armed the Sikh community, wore two swords symbolising temporal and spiritual authority, miri and piri, founded its first army, the Akal Sena, and built the Akal Takht at Amritsar.

In 1609 Jahangir jailed him in Gwalior Fort; released around 1612, he is said to have freed fifty-two imprisoned Rajput rajas, remembered as Bandi Chhor Divas. He later fought four campaigns against Shah Jahan's armies and died at Kiratpur in 1644.

1609年贾汉吉尔将他囚禁于瓜廖尔堡，约1612年获释时，相传他使被关押的五十二名拉杰普特土邦主一同获释，此事被纪念为班迪·乔尔·迪瓦斯。他后来与沙贾汗的军队四次交战，1644年在基拉特布尔去世。

en:
Guru Nanak (1469–1539) was the Punjabi mystic and poet honoured as the founder of Sikhism and the first of its ten gurus. Born at Talwandi into a Hindu family, he worked at a storehouse in Sultanpur and married in 1487. Around 1496, tradition says, he vanished in the Bein river and was given up for drowned; days later he returned saying only, ‘There is no Hindu, there is no Muslim.’

He left his post and travelled for seventeen years on tours reaching Varanasi, Assam, Sri Lanka, Tibet, Mecca and Baghdad. He taught Ik Onkar, one God dwelling in all creation, and rejected caste.

He later settled at Kartarpur, where followers ate together at the common kitchen, the langar. His 974 hymns stand in the Guru Granth Sahib. Passing over his own sons, he named Bhai Lehna as Guru Angad, and died at Kartarpur on 22 September 1539.

古鲁·那纳克（1469—1539）是旁遮普的神秘主义者与诗人，被尊为锡克教创始人、十位古鲁中的第一位。他生于塔尔万迪的印度教家庭，后来在苏丹布尔的官仓任职，1487年成婚。约1496年，据传他在贝因河中消失，人们以为他已溺亡；几天后他重新出现，只说：“没有印度教徒，也没有穆斯林。”

他辞去公职，游历约十七年，足迹远至瓦拉纳西、阿萨姆、斯里兰卡、西藏、麦加和巴格达。他传讲“伊克·昂卡尔”，即寓于一切造物之中的独一真神，并反对种姓制度。

后来他在卡尔塔普尔定居，追随者在公共食堂“朗加”共餐。他的974首赞美诗收入《古鲁·格兰特·萨希卜》。他没有传位给儿子，而是指定巴伊·勒希那为古鲁·安加德，于1539年9月22日在卡尔塔普尔去世。

en:
Guru Ram Das (1534–1581), born Jetha in Lahore, was the fourth Sikh guru. Orphaned at seven, he moved to Goindwal at twelve and served Guru Amar Das, marrying his daughter in 1553; in 1574 Amar Das chose him over his sons as successor.

Facing their hostility, he moved the community to Guru-ka-Chak and founded Ramdaspur, later Amritsar, Sikhism's holiest city, where he dug the Amrit Sarovar and invited merchants. He expanded the manji system and composed 638 hymns, about a tenth of the Guru Granth Sahib. He died at Goindwal on 1 September 1581, succeeded by his son Arjan.

古鲁·拉姆·达斯（1534—1581），原名杰塔，出生于拉合尔，是锡克教第四任古鲁。他七岁成孤，十二岁迁至戈因德瓦尔侍奉古鲁·阿摩罗·达斯，1553年娶其女为妻；1574年，阿摩罗·达斯越过诸子选他为继任者。

面对他们的敌意，他把教团中心迁往古鲁卡恰克，建立了后来改名阿姆利则的拉姆达斯布尔，即锡克教最神圣的城市；他在当地挖掘了“阿姆利特萨罗瓦尔”圣池，并招徕商人。他扩充了曼吉制度，创作638首赞美诗，约占《古鲁·格兰特·萨希卜》的十分之一。他于1581年9月1日在戈因德瓦尔去世，由儿子阿尔琼继任。

面对他们的敌意，他把教团中心迁往古鲁卡恰克，建立了后来改名阿姆利则的拉姆达斯布尔，即锡克教最神圣的城市；他在当地挖掘了“阿姆利特萨罗瓦尔”圣池，并招徕商人。他扩充了曼吉制度，创作638首赞美诗，约占《古鲁·格兰特·萨希卜》的十分之一。他于1581年9月1日在戈因德瓦尔去世，由儿子阿尔琼继任。

en:
Guru Tegh Bahadur (1621–1675), born Tyag Mal in Amritsar, was the youngest son of Guru Hargobind, who renamed him for bravery in the Battle of Kartarpur. He lived in retreat at Bakala until 1664.

That year the dying words of Guru Har Krishan led the Sikhs to acclaim him ninth Guru; Sikh tradition tells how the merchant Makhan Shah recognised him through a secret vow. He founded Anandpur Sahib and left 115 hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib.

Sikh accounts say he defended Kashmiri Brahmins facing forced conversion under Aurangzeb; he was taken to Delhi and beheaded on the emperor's orders in November 1675.

古鲁·得格·巴哈杜尔（1621—1675）原名提亚格·马尔，生于阿姆利则，是古鲁·哈尔戈宾德的幼子，因在卡尔塔布尔之战中表现英勇而得今名。他长年隐居巴卡拉，直到1664年。

这一年，古鲁·哈尔·克利香临终遗言指引锡克人奉他为第九代古鲁；锡克传说记载，商人马克汉·沙阿凭一个暗许的誓愿认出他才是真正的古鲁。他建立阿南德普尔·萨希卜城，有115首颂诗被收入《古鲁·格兰特·萨希卜》。

锡克记载称他为遭奥朗则布逼迫改宗的克什米尔婆罗门仗义执言；他被押往德里，于1675年11月奉皇帝之命斩首。

en:
Virsingh Dev (Virasimha-deva) was the first Tomara raja of Gwalior. A feudatory of the Tughluq sultans of Delhi, he rebelled in 1391 and was defeated by Islam Khan.

Later chronicles relate that while serving as a palace watchman in Delhi his vigilance during a rainstorm moved Sultan Ala ud-din Sikandar Shah to grant him Gwalior Fort in 1394; Virsingh took it by surprising the governor at a banquet. Muslim chroniclers instead date the seizure to the confusion of Timur's 1398 invasion. He ruled Gwalior until about 1400 and was succeeded by Uddharana Dev.

维尔辛格·德夫是瓜廖尔的初代都摩罗罗阇。他本是德里图格鲁克苏丹的封臣，1391年起兵反叛，被伊斯兰汗击败。

后世编年史记载，他在德里王宫充当守门人时，因在暴雨中坚守岗位感动了阿拉丁·西坎达尔沙苏丹，遂于1394年获赐瓜廖尔堡垒；维尔辛格在宴会上突袭总督夺取堡垒。穆斯林编年史家则把夺城归于1398年帖木儿入侵造成的乱局。他统治瓜廖尔至约1400年，由乌达拉纳·德夫继位。

en:
Agnes of Nuremberg (before 1326 – after 1363) was a Hohenzollern, the daughter of Burgrave Frederick IV of Nuremberg and Margaret of Görz. In 1336 she married Count Berthold V of Neuffen, one of Emperor Louis the Bavarian's closest counselors.

In 1341 she renounced her inheritance in favor of her brother Burgrave John. After Berthold's death in 1342 she married in 1343 or 1344 Count Albert II of Werdenberg-Heiligenberg, who died in 1373.

Her sons by him held the Werdenberg lordships of Bludenz, Rheineck and Heiligenberg, and her daughter Catherine married Count Diethelm of Toggenburg. Agnes is last documented in 1363.

阿格内丝·冯·纽伦堡（1326年前—1363年后）出身霍亨索伦家族，是纽伦堡城伯腓特烈四世与戈里齐亚的玛格丽特之女。1336年，她嫁给诺伊芬伯爵贝托尔德五世，即皇帝路德维希四世最倚重的顾问之一。

1341年她放弃对父母遗产的继承权，让与其兄城伯约翰。贝托尔德1342年死后，她于1343或1344年改嫁韦登贝格-海利根贝格伯爵阿尔布雷希特二世（1373年卒）。

她所生的儿子们分掌韦登贝格家族的布卢登茨、莱茵埃克和海利根贝格领地，女儿卡塔琳娜嫁给托根堡伯爵迪特黑尔姆。1363年之后她再无记载。

en:
Albert I of Habsburg (1255–1308), eldest son of Rudolf I, received Austria and Styria from his father in 1282, gaining sole government of them in 1283.

Passed over by the electors in 1291, he defeated King Adolf of Nassau at the Battle of Göllheim in 1298, where Adolf was killed, and was elected King of the Romans and crowned at Aachen. Pope Boniface VIII recognized him only in 1303.

In 1306 he placed his son Rudolf on the Bohemian throne, but defeat at Lucka in 1307 checked him. In 1308 his nephew John Parricida murdered him.

阿尔布雷希特一世（1255—1308）是鲁道夫一世的长子，1282年从父亲手中获得奥地利与施蒂利亚，1283年起单独统治两地。

1291年选帝侯们没有选他，他便于1298年在格尔海姆战役击败拿骚的阿道夫，后者在战斗中身亡；他随后当选罗马人的国王，在亚琛加冕。教皇卜尼法斯八世迟至1303年才承认他。

1306年他把儿子鲁道夫扶上波希米亚王位，但1307年在卢卡战败受挫。1308年，他被侄子“弑亲者”约翰杀害。

en:
Albert II the Wise or the Lame (1298–1358), a younger son of Albert I, was elected Bishop of Passau in 1313 while still a minor but gave up the see in 1317. His marriage to Joanna of Pfirt in 1324 brought him that county, and in 1330 he succeeded Frederick the Fair as duke of Austria and Styria.

When Henry of Carinthia died without a male heir, Albert pressed his claim against John of Bohemia, and on 2 May 1335 Emperor Louis IV enfeoffed him and Otto with Carinthia and Carniola. Probably polyarthritis gradually crippled him, yet he kept governing.

He gave Styria its constitution, the Bergbüchel, resumed the Gothic choir of St Stephen's Cathedral in Vienna, and issued the Albertinian House Rule on succession. After he died in 1358 his sons ruled jointly, until the 1379 Treaty of Neuberg split the house into two lines.

“智者”阿尔布雷希特二世（1298—1358），又称“跛者”，是阿尔布雷希特一世的幼子之一。1313年他尚未成年便被选为帕绍主教，1317年放弃该职；1324年他与费雷特的约翰娜成婚，获得费雷特伯国，1330年继美男子腓特烈之后成为奥地利和施蒂利亚公爵。

克恩滕的亨利去世后无男性继承人，阿尔布雷希特向波希米亚的约翰争夺继承权，1335年5月2日皇帝路德维希四世把克恩滕和卡尼奥拉封赐给他和奥托。他大概因多发性关节炎而行动不便，却仍然亲政。

他为施蒂利亚制定宪章《贝格比歇尔》，主持续建维也纳圣斯蒂芬大教堂的哥特式唱诗班席，并颁布《阿尔布雷希特家法》规定继承。1358年他去世后诸子共同执政，直到1379年《新堡条约》把家族分成两支。

en:
Gabriel Bethlen (1580–1629) was a Calvinist Hungarian nobleman who ruled Transylvania as prince from 1613, installed with Ottoman backing and recognised by Matthias in 1615. He was wounded at the Battle of Sellenberk in 1599.

In the Thirty Years' War he invaded Royal Hungary in 1619, took Kassa and Pressburg and menaced Vienna, and on 20 August 1620 the diet elected him king of Hungary.

At the Peace of Nikolsburg of 31 December 1621 he surrendered the crown in return for seven counties and guaranteed religious freedom for Hungarian Protestants. After two more campaigns he made peace in 1624 and 1626, and died in 1629.

拜特伦·加博尔（1580—1629）是匈牙利加尔文宗贵族，1613年在奥斯曼支持下成为特兰西瓦尼亚亲王，1615年获皇帝马蒂亚斯承认。1599年，他在塞伦贝克战役中受伤。

三十年战争中，他于1619年攻入匈牙利王室领地，连克科希策与普雷斯堡，兵临维也纳；1620年8月20日，议会推举他为匈牙利国王。

1621年12月31日签订《尼科尔斯堡和约》，他放弃王位，换取七个州以及匈牙利新教徒宗教自由的保障。此后他又两度用兵，分别于1624年和1626年议和，1629年去世。

en:
Stephen Bocskai (1557–1606) was a Hungarian Calvinist nobleman born at Kolozsvár in Transylvania. He spent his youth at Emperor Maximilian's court and became captain of Várad in 1592. As councillor to Prince Sigismund Báthory, he signed Transylvania's alliance with the Holy League in 1595 and led its troops to victory at Giurgiu.

Hounded by Rudolf II's anti-Protestant officials, he rose in revolt in 1604 with Hajdú soldiers and was elected Prince of Transylvania in February 1605 and Prince of Hungary in April. The Treaty of Vienna of June 1606 secured Transylvania's autonomy and religious freedom; he died that December.

伯茨凯·伊什特万（1557—1606）是生于特兰西瓦尼亚科洛日瓦尔的匈牙利加尔文宗贵族。他少年时在皇帝马克西米利安的宫廷度过，1592年出任瓦拉德统领。他作为亲王巴托里·齐格蒙德的顾问，于1595年签署特兰西瓦尼亚加入神圣同盟的条约，又率军在久尔久之役取胜。

因遭皇帝鲁道夫二世反新教官员的逼迫，他于1604年率豪伊杜士兵起事，1605年2月当选特兰西瓦尼亚亲王，4月又当选匈牙利亲王。1606年6月的《维也纳条约》确立了特兰西瓦尼亚的自治和信仰自由；他于同年12月去世。

Catherine of Savoy (c. 1298–1336) was a daughter of Count Amadeus V of Savoy and Maria of Brabant. In 1315 she married Leopold I, Duke of Austria and Styria, at Basel, a match tied to Habsburg rapprochement with the House of Luxembourg.

She took an active part in the Habsburgs' efforts to recover the imperial crown after 1308 and corresponded directly with Pope John XXII. Widowed in 1326, Catherine died at Rheinfelden in 1336 and was buried at Königsfelden Monastery.

en:
Isabella of Aragon (1302–1330) was a daughter of James II of Aragon and Blanche of Anjou. She married Frederick I of Austria in 1315. Frederick had been elected German king in 1314 in rivalry with Louis IV of Bavaria, so Isabella became queen of a divided Germany.

The rivals made peace in 1325 and ruled jointly until Frederick retired to Austria and died in 1330. Blind for her last six years, Isabella died that July and was buried at the Franciscan church in Vienna.

Elizabeth of Bavaria (c. 1305–1330) was born at Landshut, a daughter of Stephen I, Duke of Lower Bavaria, and Jutta of Schweidnitz. In 1325 she married Otto of Habsburg, younger brother of Duke Frederick the Fair.

She bore two sons, Frederick and Leopold, both of whom later briefly ruled Austria as dukes. When Frederick the Fair died in 1330 her husband succeeded as Duke Otto IV, but Elizabeth died only two months later the same year.

en:
Frederick the Fair (1289–1330), second son of Albert I, ruled Austria and Styria from 1308. After Henry VII died in 1313, the electors chose Frederick and his cousin Louis of Bavaria as rival kings in 1314. In 1315 he married Isabella, daughter of James II of Aragon.

Defeated and captured at the Battle of Mühldorf in 1322, he was held prisoner for three years. The 1325 Treaty of Munich made him Louis's co-king, though he never held real power. He died at Gutenstein in 1330, succeeded by his brothers Albert II and Otto.

en:
Frederick II of Habsburg (1327–1344) was the elder son of Otto the Merry, Duke of Austria, and Elizabeth of Lower Bavaria. After Otto's death in 1339 he and his brother Leopold were titular dukes under the guardianship of their uncle Albert II. That year Frederick claimed Lower Bavaria as his mother's inheritance, but Emperor Louis IV rejected his suit.

He held the Further Austrian lands. A marriage to a daughter of Edward III was planned but never came about. He died suddenly at Neuberg in December 1344, amid suspicions of poisoning.

en:
Gabriel von Salamanca (1489–1539) came from a merchant family of Burgos in Castile and was already a chancellor under Emperor Maximilian I by 1514.

When Archduke Ferdinand took over Austria in 1521, Salamanca became his general treasurer and archchancellor, opening the dynasty access to Fugger loans. He was enfeoffed with the County of Ortenburg in Carinthia in 1524. His measures and alleged self-serving conduct met fierce opposition from the nobility, and he was forced out in 1526.

He remained Ferdinand's adviser and retained his fiefs. In 1533 he began building a palace at Spittal an der Drau; he died at Ensisheim in 1539 before its completion.

en:
Michael Gaismair (1490–1532), born at Sterzing in the County of Tyrol, was secretary to the bishop of Brixen before leading miners and peasants in revolt during the German Peasants' War of 1525.

Summoned to the Innsbruck diet by Archduke Ferdinand, he was arrested for treason but escaped after two months to Switzerland. In May 1526 he drafted a constitution for an egalitarian, democratic Christian Tyrol; his plans abolished noble titles and nationalized land and mines.

He then joined the Salzburg rising. Defeated, he fled to Venice and was murdered at Padua on 15 April 1532 by soldiers collecting Ferdinand's bounty.

Gertrude of Hohenberg (c. 1225–1281), daughter of Count Burkhard V of Hohenberg, married Count Rudolf of Habsburg around 1253 and bore him eleven children, including the future King Albert I.

When Rudolf was elected King of the Romans in 1273 and crowned at Aachen, she was crowned beside him and afterwards styled herself Queen Anne. She kept out of politics and died in Vienna in 1281.

By her own wish she was buried at Basel Minster, which let Rudolf mend ties with the city's citizens after conflicts with its bishops; through her children she became ancestress of the Austrian Habsburgs.

霍恩贝格的格特鲁德（约1225—1281）是霍恩贝格伯爵伯克哈特五世之女。约1253年她嫁给哈布斯堡伯爵鲁道夫，为他生下十一个子女，其中包括后来的国王阿尔布雷希特一世。

1273年鲁道夫当选罗马人的国王并在亚琛加冕，她在丈夫身旁一同加冕，此后自称“安妮王后”。她不干预政事，1281年卒于维也纳。

按她本人遗愿，她被安葬在巴塞尔主教座堂，使鲁道夫得以在与当地主教冲突后修复与市民的关系；凭借子女，她成为奥地利哈布斯堡家族的先祖。

Gregor Erhart (c. 1465–1540), born at Ulm the son of sculptor Michel Erhart, was a leading wood and stone sculptor spanning Late Gothic and Renaissance. He worked in his father's workshop before settling in Augsburg in 1494.

In the imperial city patronised by the Fugger, he gained master's rights in 1496 and married Anna Mair, a kinswoman of Hans Holbein the Elder.

His works include the Marian altar at Kaisheim Abbey (1502), a painted Magdalen now in the Louvre, and the seated Schutzmantelmadonna of about 1510. He handed his Augsburg workshop to his son Paul in 1531 and died in 1540.

格雷戈里·埃哈特（约1465—1540）生于乌尔姆，父亲是雕刻家米夏埃尔·埃哈特，是晚期哥特风格向文艺复兴过渡时期重要的木石雕刻家。他早年在父亲的作坊工作，1494年定居奥格斯堡。

在这座受富格尔家族资助的帝国城市，他于1496年取得师傅资格，娶安娜·迈尔为妻，与老汉斯·荷尔拜因有姻亲关系。

他的作品包括1502年为凯斯海姆修道院创作的圣母祭坛、今藏卢浮宫的彩绘《抹大拉的马利亚》，以及约1510年的坐式《护佑圣母》。1531年他把奥格斯堡的作坊交给儿子保罗，1540年去世。

Gundakar of Liechtenstein (1580–1658), born at Lednice, was the youngest son of Baron Hartmann II and brother of Princes Karl I and Maximilian. In 1606 the brothers agreed that the first-born of the eldest line would head the house, and in 1618 he married Elizabeth Lucretia, Duchess of Cieszyn.

He served the Habsburgs as soldier, diplomat and imperial Obersthofmeister through the Thirty Years' War. In the White Mountain confiscations he acquired Moravian lordships, and in 1623 he and Maximilian became imperial princes; in 1633 his estates were styled the Principality of Liechtenstein. He founded the family's younger Gundakar line.

列支敦士登的贡达克尔（1580—1658）生于莱德尼采，是哈特曼二世男爵的幼子、卡尔一世和马克西米利安两位亲王的弟弟。1606年，兄弟三人约定由现存最年长支系的长子担任家族首领；1618年，贡达克尔迎娶切申女公爵伊丽莎白·卢克蕾齐娅。

三十年战争期间，他以军人、外交官和帝国宫廷总管的身份效力哈布斯堡王朝。白山战役后的抄没中，他获得多处摩拉维亚领地，1623年他与兄长马克西米利安受封帝国亲王；1633年，他的领地被定名为列支敦士登亲王国。他开创了家族的幼支——贡达克尔支系。

Lorenz Leopold Haschka (1749–1827) was an Austrian poet born in Vienna, where he also died. He joined the Jesuits young, but after the order's 1773 suppression turned to secular poetry and, under Josephinism, became a freemason. After Joseph II's death he returned to Catholicism.

In 1797 he was chosen to write the words of the patriotic anthem Gott erhalte Franz den Kaiser, set to music by Joseph Haydn and first sung on 12 February for Francis II's birthday. He later taught aesthetics at Vienna's Theresianum and worked at its university library, retiring in 1824.

Joseph Haydn (1732–1809) was an Austrian composer, called the father of the symphony and string quartet. Born at Rohrau, he sang in the choir of St. Stephen’s Cathedral from 1740 until his voice broke in 1749, when he was dismissed.

In 1761 he joined the Esterházy family as vice-Kapellmeister, rising to Kapellmeister in 1766, and for nearly thirty years led his orchestra, mostly at remote Eszterháza. Cut off from other composers, he said, he was ‘forced to become original’. By 1790 he was Europe’s leading composer; he befriended Mozart and taught the young Beethoven.

Two London visits produced his twelve London symphonies. Back in Vienna he wrote the oratorios The Creation and The Seasons and the Emperor’s Hymn. When French shells hit his neighbourhood in 1809, he reportedly told his servants that no harm could reach them where Haydn was. He died on 31 May.

约瑟夫·海顿（1732—1809）是奥地利作曲家，被称为交响曲之父和弦乐四重奏之父。他生于罗劳，1740年起在圣斯蒂芬大教堂唱诗班歌唱，1749年变声后被解职。

1761年他加入埃施特哈齐家族，任副乐长，1766年升任乐长，近三十年里带领乐队，大多在偏远的埃施特哈扎宫。他说，由于与其他作曲家隔绝，他“被迫变得有独创性”。到1790年他已是欧洲首屈一指的作曲家，与莫扎特结为朋友，也教过年轻的贝多芬。

他两度访问伦敦，写出十二部《伦敦交响曲》。回到维也纳后，他写下清唱剧《创世纪》《四季》和《皇帝颂》。1809年法军炮弹落到他住的街区，相传他对仆人说，有海顿在的地方，没有灾祸能够降临。他于5月31日去世。

Johann Lukas von Hildebrandt (1668–1745) was a defining architect of the Austrian High Baroque. Born in Genoa, he studied in Rome under Carlo Fontana, built fortresses for Prince Eugene of Savoy in 1695–1696, then settled in Vienna.

He became court engineer in 1700, head of the court building department in 1711 and court architect in 1723. Competing with the Fischer von Erlach architects, he built his reputation on commissions from prominent Viennese families.

For Prince Eugene he designed the Lower and Upper Belvedere (1714–1722); his other works include St. Peter's Church and the Palais Kinsky.

约翰·卢卡斯·冯·希尔德布兰特（1668—1745）是奥地利巴洛克鼎盛时期最具代表性的建筑师。他生于热那亚，早年在罗马师从卡洛·丰塔纳，1695至1696年为萨伏依的欧根亲王修筑要塞，随后定居维也纳。

他于1700年任宫廷工程师，1711年任宫廷营造部门主管，1723年成为宫廷建筑师。他与费舍尔·冯·埃尔拉赫父子竞争，凭借为维也纳显贵家族承接工程建立声誉。

他为欧根亲王设计了下美景宫与上美景宫（1714—1722），其他作品还有维也纳圣彼得教堂和金斯基宫。

Johann Sigismund Hubert (1736–1792) was an Austrian hydraulic and cameral engineer who made the first attempts to shield Vienna from the Danube. In 1771 he raised a protection dam almost six metres high below the city, but floods breached it again and again.

In 1785–1786, by order of Emperor Joseph II, he built a left-bank embankment at Floridsdorf to protect the Marchfeld, later named the Hubertusdamm after him. The first large-scale regulation at Vienna followed only in the 1870s.
