Karl I of Liechtenstein (1569–1627) was the elder son of Baron Hartmann II and the first prince of his house. He converted to Catholicism in 1599 and served Rudolf II as Obersthofmeister until 1607, but in the Habsburg succession quarrel he backed Archduke Matthias against the emperor and helped him seize power; a grateful Matthias made him a hereditary prince in 1608.

He acquired the Silesian duchies of Troppau and Jägerndorf. For supporting Ferdinand II at the White Mountain he became vice-regent of Bohemia in 1622, rewarded with confiscated rebel estates. He died in Prague in 1627.

Leopold I the Glorious (c. 1290–1326), third son of Albert I, was co-duke of Austria and Styria with his brother Frederick the Fair from 1308. He administered Further Austria, pursued his father's murderers, and backed Frederick's claim to the German crown in the 1314 double election.

In 1315 his knights were routed by the Swiss Confederates at the Battle of Morgarten. After Frederick was captured at Mühldorf in 1322, Leopold fought on and surrendered the imperial regalia in a failed bid for his release. He died at Strasbourg in 1326.

“荣耀者”利奥波德一世（约1290—1326）是阿尔布雷希特一世第三子，1308年起与兄长美男子腓特烈共治奥地利和施蒂利亚。他管理前奥地利，追讨杀害父亲的凶手，并在1314年的双重选举中支持腓特烈争夺德意志王位。

1315年，他的骑兵在莫尔加滕战役被瑞士同盟军队击溃。1322年腓特烈在米尔多夫被俘后，利奥波德继续作战，甚至交出帝国御用器以换取兄长获释，但谈判失败。1326年他卒于斯特拉斯堡。

Leopold II of Habsburg (1328–1344) was the younger son of Duke Otto the Merry of Austria and Elizabeth of Lower Bavaria. He lost his mother at age two and his father at eleven; afterwards he and his elder brother Frederick II were titular dukes under uncle Albert II's guardianship.

Leopold died suddenly in August 1344, aged sixteen, and Frederick died just as suddenly four months later. Contemporaries suspected poisoning, and Albert II continued to rule Austria.

Ludwig van Beethoven (1770–1827) was a German composer, born in Bonn, whose works carried music from the Classical style toward the Romantic. After early training in Bonn, he moved to Vienna in 1792 and studied under Haydn. A virtuoso pianist, he won noble patrons; his First Symphony premiered in 1800.

By 1798 his hearing had begun to fail, and in 1802 at Heiligenstadt he wrote an unsent letter to his brothers admitting thoughts of suicide and resolving to live for his art. He first titled the Third Symphony, the Eroica, after Bonaparte, then scratched out the name when Napoleon made himself emperor in 1804.

In 1824 his Ninth Symphony, the first major choral symphony, was performed to great acclaim, with the nearly deaf composer beside the conductor. He died in Vienna on 26 March 1827, and ten thousand people followed his funeral procession, with Franz Schubert among the torchbearers.

路德维希·范·贝多芬（1770—1827）是德国作曲家，生于波恩，他的作品把音乐从古典风格推向浪漫主义。他早年在波恩学乐，1792年迁居维也纳，跟随海顿学习。他是技艺高超的钢琴家，赢得贵族赞助，第一交响曲于1800年首演。

1798年起他的听力开始衰退，1802年在海利根施塔特写下一封从未寄出的给兄弟的信，坦言有过自杀的念头，并决心为艺术而活。他最初把第三交响曲《英雄》题献给波拿巴，1804年拿破仑称帝后划去了这个名字。

1824年，他的第九交响曲这部首个重要的合唱交响曲演出大获成功，已近乎全聋的作曲家站在指挥身旁。他1827年3月26日在维也纳去世，一万人跟随他的送葬队伍，舒伯特是持火炬者之一。

Martin Siebenbürger (c. 1475–1522), born Mert Kapp in Hermannstadt in Transylvania, followed his uncle to Vienna, where he taught law at the university and became the city's judge in 1512. His relentless prosecution of corruption among municipal officials in the Lauffner affair earned him powerful enemies, who denounced him to Emperor Maximilian I.

In 1520 the city council made him mayor of Vienna. He sought to preserve the city's autonomy, but after Archduke Ferdinand took over Austria, he was tried with five former councillors at the Wiener Neustadt blood court, condemned, and beheaded on 11 August 1522.

Maximilian of Liechtenstein (1578–1643) was a Moravian nobleman and younger brother of Prince Karl I. A career soldier in Habsburg service, he fought at the White Mountain in 1620 and rose to field marshal in the imperial army. Through his marriage to Catherine Šemberová, heiress of the Boskovice lords, he inherited large Moravian estates and was raised to imperial prince in 1623.

From 1627 to 1632 he guarded his nephew Karl Eusebius and enforced the Counter-Reformation in the family lands. In 1638 he took command of the fortress of Győr, strengthened its defences and died there.

en:
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791) was a composer born in Salzburg. His father Leopold trained him; by five he played instruments and had begun to compose, and the family toured Europe's courts with him as a prodigy.

Back in Salzburg he served Prince-Archbishop Colloredo, but resigned in 1777 and travelled seeking a post without success. In 1781 Colloredo summoned him to Vienna and dismissed him after a quarrel; he stayed in Vienna for the rest of his life. Die Entführung aus dem Serail in 1782 made his name, and he became a friend of Haydn.

With Da Ponte he wrote Le nozze di Figaro and Don Giovanni (1787); that December Joseph II appointed him chamber composer. His last year brought Die Zauberflöte. He fell ill on 20 November 1791 and died at 35, leaving the Requiem largely unfinished, and was buried in a common grave.

沃尔夫冈·阿马多伊斯·莫扎特（1756—1791）是作曲家，生于萨尔茨堡。他由父亲利奥波德培养，五岁时已能演奏乐器并开始作曲；一家人巡游欧洲各国宫廷，他作为神童登台演出。

回到萨尔茨堡后，他效力于大主教科洛雷多，1777年辞职外出谋职却一无所获。1781年科洛雷多召他去维也纳，两人争执激化，莫扎特被解雇，此后一直留在维也纳。1782年的《后宫诱逃》使他成名，他还与海顿结为朋友。

他与达·蓬特合作写出《费加罗的婚礼》和《唐·乔万尼》（1787年）；当年12月约瑟夫二世任命他为宫廷室内作曲家。最后一年里他完成了《魔笛》。1791年11月20日他病倒，35岁去世，《安魂曲》大部分未完成，葬在普通墓穴里。

Otto the Merry (1301–1339), youngest son of Albert I, married Elizabeth of Bavaria, a Wittelsbach, in the reconciliation after the Habsburgs lost the German throne at Mühldorf in 1322. In 1327 he founded Neuberg Abbey in Styria on the birth of his first son, and from 1330 he ruled the Habsburg duchies with his brother Albert II.

In 1335 he married Anna of Bohemia, daughter of John the Blind. After their maternal uncle Henry of Carinthia died without male heirs, Emperor Louis IV enfeoffed the brothers with Carinthia and Carniola on 2 May 1335; Otto was enthroned as duke on the Zollfeld in the ancient Carantanian rite and thereafter governed Carinthia.

His nickname recalls the festive air of his court. He died at Neuberg in 1339, aged 37; his two sons died in 1344, presumably poisoned, and his line ended.

“欢乐者”奥托（1301—1339）是阿尔布雷希特一世的幼子。1322年哈布斯堡在米尔多夫败北、输掉德意志王位之争后两家和解，他娶了维特尔斯巴赫家族的巴伐利亚的伊丽莎白。1327年为庆祝长子出生，他在施蒂利亚创建新堡修道院；1330年起与兄长阿尔布雷希特二世共治哈布斯堡诸公国。

1335年他娶约翰“盲人”之女波希米亚的安娜。舅父克恩滕公爵亨利去世时没有男性继承人，皇帝路德维希四世于1335年5月2日将克恩滕和卡尼奥拉封赐兄弟二人；奥托在措尔费尔德按古老的卡兰塔尼亚仪式即位为公爵，此后主要治理克恩滕。

“欢乐者”的绰号来自他宫廷里的欢庆气氛。1339年他卒于新堡修道院，终年37岁；两个儿子于1344年先后去世，据推测死于毒杀，他这一支就此绝嗣。

en:
Francis II Rákóczi (1676–1735), born at Borsi in Zemplén County, was the wealthiest magnate in Hungary. After a secret appeal to France against Habsburg rule was exposed, he was condemned to death but escaped to Poland.

Returning in 1703, he led the Kuruc rising known as his War of Independence: elected Prince of Transylvania in 1704, he was named Ruling Prince of Hungary at Szécsény in 1705, yet refused the royal crown. Defeats at Zsibó (1705) and Trencsén (1708) and the Peace of Szatmár (1711) ended the revolt. He died in Ottoman exile at Rodosto in 1735.

zh:
拉科齐·费伦茨二世（1676—1735）生于泽姆普林州的波尔希，是匈牙利最富有的大贵族。他因秘密向法国求助、反抗哈布斯堡统治事泄而被判死刑，却越狱逃往波兰。

1703年他回国领导库伦茨军起事，即拉科齐独立战争：1704年他当选特兰西瓦尼亚大公，1705年在塞切尼议会上被推举为匈牙利邦联大公，但他拒绝了王冠。1705年日博乌之役和1708年特伦钦之役接连战败，1711年《萨图马雷和约》结束了起事。1735年他在奥斯曼帝国流亡地罗多斯托去世。

en:
Rudolf I of Habsburg (1218–1291) was a Swabian count who, in 1273, became the first member of his house elected King of the Romans, ending the Great Interregnum. After his father's death in 1240 he took over the main Habsburg line and married Gertrude of Hohenberg.

He defeated and killed his rival Ottokar II of Bohemia at the Battle on the Marchfeld in 1278, securing Austria, Styria and Carinthia for his dynasty and laying the foundations of Habsburg power on the Danube. His efforts to make the crown hereditary failed, and he died at Speyer in 1291, never having been crowned emperor.

zh:
鲁道夫一世（1218—1291）原是施瓦本伯爵，1273年成为哈布斯堡家族首位当选的罗马人的国王，结束了大空位时代。1240年父亲去世后，他接掌哈布斯堡家族主支，迎娶霍恩贝格的格特鲁德。

1278年，他在马希菲尔德战役击败并击杀对手波希米亚国王奥托卡二世，为家族夺得奥地利、施蒂利亚和克恩滕，奠定哈布斯堡在多瑙河流域的权势基础。他使王位世袭的努力失败，1291年卒于施派尔，终生未加冕为皇帝。

en:
Samson Wertheimer (1658–1724) was the leading court Jew and financier to the Habsburg emperor Leopold I. Born in Worms, he settled in Vienna, where he supplied the imperial armies and, with Samuel Oppenheimer, helped finance the Habsburg war effort in the War of the Spanish Succession. He was also chief rabbi of Hungary and Moravia.

A scholar and patron of scholars, he paid for the Frankfurt printing of the Babylonian Talmud (1712–1722). His wealth and influence earned him the nickname Judenkaiser, the ‘Jewish emperor’; ten imperial soldiers guarded his house.

萨姆松·韦特海默（1658—1724）是哈布斯堡皇帝利奥波德一世麾下最重要的宫廷犹太人与银行家。他生于沃尔姆斯，后定居维也纳，为帝国军队提供军需，并与塞缪尔·奥本海默一同资助哈布斯堡王朝在西班牙王位继承战争中的战事。他还担任匈牙利与摩拉维亚的大拉比。

他本人是学者，也资助学者，于1712至1722年出资在法兰克福印制《巴比伦塔木德》。他的财富与权势为他赢得“犹太皇帝”的绰号，十名帝国士兵守卫着他的宅邸。

en:
Samuel Oppenheimer (1630–1703) was the court Jew and military financier of Emperor Leopold I in Vienna. Born at Heidelberg, he funded the Habsburg armies in the Great Turkish War and became the emperor's Oberfaktor.

Though Vienna's Jews had been expelled in 1670, Leopold let him settle there; he founded synagogues and schools and ransomed Jewish captives of the Turkish wars. Contemporaries called him the Judenkaiser, and he undertook delicate diplomatic missions for the emperor.

Around 1700 rioters looted his house. When he died in 1703, the state repudiated its debts to his heir Emanuel, bankrupting the firm and triggering a credit crisis.

塞缪尔·奥本海默（1630—1703）是皇帝利奥波德一世在维也纳的宫廷犹太人与军费筹措人。他出生于海德堡，为哈布斯堡军队进行大土耳其战争提供资金，成为皇帝的首席宫廷代理人。

1670年维也纳犹太人遭驱逐后，利奥波德仍准许他在当地定居；他修建犹太会堂和学校，还为土耳其战争中被俘的犹太人赎身。同时代人称他为“犹太人皇帝”，他还为皇帝承担过微妙的外交使命。

约1700年，他的住宅遭暴乱者洗劫。1703年他去世后，国家拒绝向继承人埃马努埃尔清偿债务，致使其商号破产，并引发信贷危机。

Georg Tannstetter (1482–1535), also called Collimitius, was born at Rain am Lech in Bavaria and studied at Ingolstadt before Conrad Celtis called him to the University of Vienna in 1503 to teach mathematics. One of the leading Viennese humanists, he became personal physician to Emperor Maximilian I in 1510 and was ennobled in 1516.

He edited the map of Hungary known as Tabula Hungariae from a manuscript by Lazarus Secretarius; printed in 1528, it included a scale and details of some 1300 settlements. His lives of Vienna's mathematicians, Viri Mathematici, pioneered the history of science.

格奥尔格·坦施泰特（1482—1535）人称科利米提乌斯，生于巴伐利亚的莱希河畔赖因，曾在因戈尔施塔特求学，1503年应康拉德·策尔蒂斯之邀到维也纳大学教授数学，是维也纳最重要的人文主义者之一。1510年他成为皇帝马克西米利安一世的御医，1516年受封贵族。

他依据拉扎鲁斯·塞克雷塔里乌斯的手稿编订《匈牙利地图》，于1528年印行，图上附有比例尺和约1300处聚落的细节。所著《数学家列传》记述维也纳数学家的生平，被视为科学史的先驱之作。

Bernhard von Cles (1485–1539) was born at Cles Castle in the Prince-Bishopric of Trent and studied law at Bologna. He became Prince-Bishop of Trent in 1514 and led the diocese through the peasant rising of 1525, in which his brother was killed.

A fierce opponent of Luther, he became president of Archduke Ferdinand's Privy Council in 1527 and pressed the Protestant estates at the Diet of Speyer in 1529. Made a cardinal in 1530, he helped prepare the Council of Trent.

He rebuilt Trento as a Renaissance city, rebuilding Santa Maria Maggiore and enlarging Buonconsiglio Castle. He died at Brixen in 1539.

伯恩哈德·冯·克勒斯（1485—1539）生于特伦托采邑主教区的克莱斯城堡，曾在博洛尼亚攻读法律。1514年他出任特伦托采邑主教，在1525年的农民起义中守住教区，他的兄弟在动乱中丧命。

作为路德的死敌，他自1527年任斐迪南枢密院主席，1529年在施派尔帝国会议上对新教诸侯施压。1530年他升任枢机，为特伦托会议铺路。

他把特伦托改建为文艺复兴式城市，重建圣母大殿，扩建博恩孔西利奥城堡。1539年他卒于布里克森。

Joseph Wenzel I of Liechtenstein (1696–1772), born in Prague, was twice Prince of Liechtenstein (1712–1718 and 1748–1772) and regent from 1732 to 1745. A professional soldier from his first campaign under Prince Eugene in 1717, he became a field marshal in 1745 and, as generalissimo in Italy, defeated the French and Spanish at Piacenza in 1746.

Appointed director general of artillery in 1744, he spent his own money rebuilding the service; his 1753 Liechtenstein artillery system made Austrian gunners the best in Europe during the Seven Years' War.

约瑟夫·文策尔一世（1696—1772）生于布拉格，两度担任列支敦士登亲王（1712—1718、1748—1772），1732至1745年任摄政。他自1717年随欧根亲王出征起成为职业军人，1745年晋升陆军元帅，任意大利方向大元帅时于1746年在皮亚琴察击败法国与西班牙联军。

1744年他出任炮兵总监，自掏腰包重整炮兵；他于1753年推行的“列支敦士登炮兵体系”使奥地利炮兵在七年战争中成为欧洲之冠。

Hachiun (born c. 1166), also called Hachiun Alchi, was the third son of Yesugei and Hö'elün and a full brother of Genghis Khan. The Secret History of the Mongols mentions him far less often than his brothers Qasar and Temüge, suggesting he may have died young.

He was still alive in 1207, when Genghis Khan apportioned lands and ranked him seventh. His son Eljigidey inherited his house and was later enfeoffed as prince of Jinan.

合赤温（1166年生），又称合赤温额勒赤，是也速该与诃额仑的第三子、成吉思汗的同母三弟。《蒙古秘史》中关于他的记载远少于兄长合撒儿和幼弟铁木哥，因此有人认为他可能早逝。

1207年他仍在世，成吉思汗分封土地时他位列第七。其子按赤台承袭家业，后来受封济南王。

en:
Baldwin of Avesnes (1219–1295), younger son of Bouchard IV of Avesnes and Margaret II of Flanders, was declared legitimate by the pope in 1246 and received Beaumont as his apanage; his parents' marriage had been ruled illegal because his father had received minor orders.

He spent decades fighting beside his brother John I against their Dampierre half-brothers, and was blamed for the Trazegnies tournament accident that killed William III of Dampierre. After John's death he reconciled with his mother and led her expedition against Namur. In 1287 he sold Dunkirk and Warneton to Guy of Flanders. He also compiled a universal chronicle.

阿韦讷的博杜安（1219—1295）是布沙尔四世与佛兰德的玛格丽特二世的幼子。因父亲曾领低级圣职，父母的婚姻被判非法；1246年他被教皇承认为合法子嗣，受封博蒙作为封禄。

他数十年间随兄长约翰一世与同母异父的丹皮尔家族兄弟作战，并被认为要对特拉泽尼比武会上导致当皮埃尔的威廉三世身亡的意外负责。约翰死后他与母亲和解，奉母命出征那慕尔。1287年他将敦刻尔克和瓦尔讷通卖给佛兰德伯爵居伊。他还编纂过一部世界编年史。

en:
Bouchard IV of Avesnes (1182–1244), son of James of Avesnes, began his career as a cantor and subdeacon at Laon. He became bailiff of Hainaut in 1212 and married his ward Margaret, the ten-year-old daughter of Baldwin VI of Hainaut, without her family's consent. He fought for Flanders at Bouvines in 1214, and Pope Innocent III declared the marriage unlawful and excommunicated him in 1216.

Bouchard and Margaret took refuge in Luxembourg. Captured in 1219 and held at Ghent for two years, he was freed after Margaret accepted the dissolution. He was finally beheaded at Rupelmonde on Countess Joanna's orders.

阿韦讷的布沙尔四世（1182—1244）是阿韦讷的雅克之子，早年在拉昂教会担任歌咏长和副执事。1212年他出任埃诺邑督，未经家属同意便娶了受他监护的埃诺的鲍德温六世之女、年仅十岁的玛格丽特。1214年他在布汶为佛兰德一方作战，1216年教皇英诺森三世宣布这桩婚姻非法并将他绝罚。

布沙尔与玛格丽特避往卢森堡。1219年他被俘，在根特关押两年，直到玛格丽特同意解除婚姻才获释。最终他被女伯爵让娜下令在吕佩尔蒙德斩首。

en:
Walter II of Avesnes (c. 1170–1244), eldest son of the crusader James of Avesnes, held lordships in Hainaut and became count of Blois and Chartres through his marriage to Countess Margaret. He fought at Bouvines in 1214, then went to the Holy Land; captured and ransomed by the Templars, he donated 1,000 bezants towards building Château Pèlerin in 1218.

Using income from Guise, he modernized his castles and built one at Englancourt to control the road through Hainaut, and later helped free Count Ferdinand of Flanders.

戈蒂埃二世·德·阿韦讷（约1170—1244）是十字军将领阿韦讷的雅克的长子，在埃诺领有多处领地，并因迎娶布卢瓦女伯爵玛格丽特而成为布卢瓦与沙特尔伯爵。他参加了1214年的布汶战役，随后前往圣地；被俘后由圣殿骑士团赎回，1218年捐出一千拜占特金币协助修建朝圣者城堡。

他用吉斯的收入改建自己的城堡，并在昂格朗库尔筑城控制穿过埃诺的道路，后来还帮助佛兰德伯爵费朗恢复自由。

en:
William I, called the Good (c. 1286–1337), was never meant to rule: after his brothers died in 1302–1303, he became count of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland in 1304. That year Guy of Namur beat him at Duiveland and, with Brabant, overran most of Zeeland and Holland, but William recovered the lands and fought Flanders until the Peace of Paris in 1323, when Flanders renounced Zeeland and he gave up his claim to Imperial Flanders.

He occupied much of the Utrecht bishopric and annexed Amsterdam to Holland. In 1305 he married Joan of Valois, sister of the future Philip VI.

In 1326 he backed Queen Isabella's expedition against Edward II, and his daughter Philippa was betrothed to the future Edward III. In 1337 he joined Edward and others in a coalition against Philip VI, but died that year, succeeded by William II.

威廉一世（绰号好人，约1286—1337）本来轮不到继承：兄长们于1302至1303年间先后死去，1304年他成为埃诺、荷兰与泽兰伯爵。当年他在德伊夫兰岛被那慕尔的居伊击败，居伊与布拉班特联手夺取泽兰和荷兰大部；威廉收复失地，与佛兰德作战直到1323年的巴黎和约，佛兰德放弃对泽兰的要求，他则放弃对帝国佛兰德的要求。

1326年，他支持王后伊莎贝拉远征英格兰对付爱德华二世，女儿菲利帕与王储（即后来的爱德华三世）订婚。1337年，他与爱德华等人结成反对腓力六世的同盟，却于同年去世，由威廉二世继位。

en:
William II of Hainaut (1307–1345), later called the Bold, found himself between France and the Empire. As a young man he made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land and fought the Moors in Spain. In 1337 he succeeded his father William the Good as count of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland, holding part of his lands from the French king and part from Emperor Louis IV.

Trying to please both, he angered both, and out of resentment at Philip VI he joined the English. As Edward III's brother-in-law he fought at the 1339 siege of Cambrai and the 1340 siege of Tournai.

In 1345 he took Utrecht, checking its bishop's bid for independence, then turned on a Frisian revolt and was killed at the Battle of Warns, leaving no heir. His sister Margaret, Emperor Louis IV's wife, inherited his counties.

埃诺的威廉二世（1307—1345），后来得绰号“勇敢者”，夹在法兰西与帝国之间。他年轻时曾前往圣地朝圣，并在西班牙与摩尔人作战。1337年，他继承其父好人威廉，成为埃诺、荷兰和泽兰伯爵，一部分领地向法王称臣，另一部分向皇帝路德维希四世称臣。

他想两头讨好，结果两头得罪，终因不满腓力六世而加入英格兰一方。作为爱德华三世的姻亲，他参加了1339年的康布雷围城战和1340年的图尔奈围城战。

1345年，他夺取乌得勒支，阻止当地主教谋求独立，随后回师镇压弗里斯兰人的起义，在瓦恩斯战役中战死，没有留下继承人。他的姐姐、皇帝路德维希四世之妻玛格丽特继承了这些伯国。

en:
James of Avesnes (1152–1191), son of Nicholas d'Oisy, Lord of Avesnes, was lord of Avesnes, Condé and Leuze from 1171. He took the cross in 1187 and led French, Flemish and Frisian crusaders by ship to the Holy Land, reaching the siege of Acre in 1189.

At the Battle of Arsuf in 1191 James was unhorsed and cut down after slaying fifteen enemy warriors. Hospitallers and Templars found his body the next day and buried it at Arsuf in the presence of Richard the Lionheart and Guy of Lusignan.

en:
John I of Avesnes (1218–1257) was the eldest son of Bouchard IV of Avesnes and Margaret II of Flanders, whose papally dissolved marriage left him considered illegitimate until Frederick II recognised his legitimacy. When Margaret inherited Flanders and Hainaut in 1244 and favoured her Dampierre sons, fighting followed; Louis IX's 1246 arbitration awarded John Hainaut, but Margaret refused to surrender it.

He defeated Guy of Dampierre at Walcheren in 1253, taking him prisoner, and secured the county with the backing of William II of Holland. Guy relinquished his claim to Hainaut in 1257. John died at Valenciennes in 1257, leaving the future John II.

en:
John II of Avesnes (1247–1304), son of Count John I of Hainaut and Adelaide of Holland, became count of Hainaut in 1280 on his grandmother Margaret's death and inherited Holland and Zeeland in 1299, uniting the three counties. Backed by France, he fought Count Guy of Flanders for Imperial Flanders.

His eldest son was killed fighting for France at the Golden Spurs in 1302. John's enemies overran much of Holland and Zeeland, and Guy of Namur defeated his son William at Duiveland, until the Franco-Holland fleet defeated Guy off Zierikzee in 1304. He died later that year, succeeded by his son William I.

zh:
阿韦讷的约翰二世（1247—1304）是埃诺伯爵约翰一世与荷兰的阿德莱德之子，1280年祖母玛格丽特去世后继任埃诺伯爵，1299年又继承荷兰与泽兰，将三地合为一体。他在法兰西支持下为帝国佛兰德与佛兰德伯爵居伊交战。

1302年他的长子在金马刺战役中为法兰西作战时阵亡。约翰的敌人攻占荷兰与泽兰大部，那慕尔的居伊在德伊夫兰岛击败他的儿子威廉，直到1304年法兰西—荷兰联合舰队在济里克泽海战击败居伊。他于同年去世，由儿子威廉一世继位。

en:
Joan of Valois (c. 1294–1352) stood where the French and English crowns met. Daughter of Charles of Valois and sister of Philip VI of France, she married William I of Avesnes, Count of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland, and governed Hainaut as regent whenever he was away.

Her daughter Philippa married Edward III of England, which made Joan mother-in-law to one king and sister to the other. After William died in 1337 she took the veil at Fontenelle Abbey, but kept her chancellery and staff.

In 1340, after Edward beat Philip at Sluys and besieged Tournai without money to carry on, Pope Benedict XII asked her to mediate. She begged her brother for peace, then went to Edward's tent and begged him too; on 23 September the two kings agreed a truce without loss of face. In 1345 she mediated a quarrel in Tournai. She died at Fontenelle in 1352.

zh:
让娜·德·瓦卢瓦（约1294—1352）所处的位置，正是法兰西与英格兰两顶王冠的交汇处。她是瓦卢瓦的查理之女、法王腓力六世之妹，嫁与威廉一世·德·阿韦讷，成为埃诺、荷兰与泽兰伯爵夫人，丈夫外出时由她以摄政身份治理埃诺。

她的女儿菲利帕嫁给英王爱德华三世，让娜因此既是一位国王的岳母，又是另一位国王的妹妹。1337年威廉去世后，她入丰特奈勒修道院为修女，却保留自己的文书机构和侍从。

1340年，爱德华在斯勒伊斯击败腓力后围攻图尔奈，却无力继续作战，教皇本笃十二世请让娜调停。她先向兄长求和，再到爱德华的帐中向他求和；9月23日，两位国王休战，双方都保住了颜面。1345年，她又调解了图尔奈城内的一场争端，1352年在丰特奈勒修道院去世。

en:
Philippa of Luxembourg (1252–1311) was a daughter of Count Henry V of Luxembourg and Margaret of Bar. She married John II, Count of Holland and Hainaut, of the House of Avesnes, and her many children linked the chief courts of western Europe.

Her son William succeeded as Count of Hainaut and Holland and fathered Queen Philippa of England; another son, John of Beaumont, married the Countess of Soissons. She died on 6 April 1311.

卢森堡的菲莉帕（1252—1311）是卢森堡伯爵亨利五世与巴尔的玛格丽特之女。她嫁给阿韦讷家族的荷兰与埃诺伯爵约翰二世，众多子女把西欧各主要宫廷联结起来。

儿子威廉继承父位成为埃诺与荷兰伯爵，是英格兰王后菲莉帕的父亲；另一个儿子博蒙领主让娶了苏瓦松女伯爵。她于1311年4月6日去世。

en:
Boris Vyacheslavich (c. 1056–1078) was the son of Vyacheslav Yaroslavich, prince of Smolensk, and a grandson of Yaroslav the Wise. Left an izgoi prince excluded from his inheritance after 1057, he vanishes from the chronicles until 4 May 1077, when he seized Chernigov while its prince Vsevolod was away; he held it only eight days before fleeing to Tmutarakan.

In summer 1078, with Oleg Svyatoslavich's backing, he defeated Vsevolod and retook Chernigov. On 3 October 1078 he fell fighting Vsevolod and Grand Prince Izyaslav near Chernigov.

鲍里斯·维亚切斯拉维奇（约1056—1078）是斯摩棱斯克王公维亚切斯拉夫·雅罗斯拉维奇之子、智者雅罗斯拉夫之孙。1057年父亲死后，他成为被剥夺继承权的“伊兹戈伊”王公，直到1077年才在编年史中出现。是年5月4日，他趁切尔尼戈夫王公弗谢沃洛德外出之机夺取公位，但仅统治约八天便逃往特穆塔拉干。

1078年夏，他在奥列格·斯维亚托斯拉维奇支持下击败弗谢沃洛德，再据切尔尼戈夫。1078年10月3日，他在切尔尼戈夫附近与弗谢沃洛德及基辅大公伊贾斯拉夫的激战中阵亡。

en:
Ivan Vasilkovich (died 1141), also called Igor, was a Rurikid prince, son of Vasilko Rostislavich of Terebovlia. When Vasilko died in 1124, Ivan received Halych while his brother Rostislav took Terebovlia.

In 1125 he and his brother joined Mstislav of Kiev in the feud between their cousins Vladimir Volodarevich of Zvenigorod and Rostislav Volodarevich of Peremyshl, supporting the latter. He died childless at Halych in 1141, and Vladimir then united the southwestern Rus lands under Halych.

伊凡·瓦西里科维奇（？—1141），一称伊戈尔，是留里克王朝王公、捷列博夫利王公瓦西里科·罗斯季斯拉维奇之子。1124年父亲去世后，他领有加利奇，其兄弟罗斯季斯拉夫继承捷列博夫利。

1125年，他与兄弟随同基辅大公姆斯季斯拉夫介入堂兄弟兹韦尼哥罗德王公弗拉基米尔·沃洛达列维奇与普热梅希尔王公罗斯季斯拉夫·沃洛达列维奇之争，支持后者。1141年他在加利奇无嗣而终，弗拉基米尔随即将西南罗斯诸地统一于加利奇。

en:
Oleg Yaroslavich, called Nastasich (died 1188), was the illegitimate son of the Halych prince Yaroslav Osmomysl by his mistress Anastasia Charg. In 1170 Yaroslav put aside his wife Olga, who fled with her son Vladimir, while Yaroslav favored Oleg.

In 1187 he left Halych to Oleg, giving Vladimir only Peremyshl, but the boyars drove Oleg out. He fled to Rurik Rostislavich, then joined the Polish king Casimir II, who restored him in Halych. Oleg was soon poisoned, and the boyars invited Roman Mstislavich.

奥列格·雅罗斯拉维奇，绰号“纳斯塔西奇”（？—1188），是加利奇王公雅罗斯拉夫·奥斯莫梅斯尔与情妇阿纳斯塔西娅·恰尔格的私生子。1170年，雅罗斯拉夫遗弃妻子奥尔加，奥尔加带着儿子弗拉基米尔出逃，雅罗斯拉夫却偏爱奥列格。

1187年雅罗斯拉夫遗命将加利奇传给奥列格，只把普热梅希尔分给弗拉基米尔，但波雅尔贵族随即将奥列格驱逐。他先投奔留里克·罗斯季斯拉维奇，又投靠波兰国王卡齐米日二世，后者助他重返加利奇。奥列格不久即被毒杀，波雅尔贵族遂迎立罗曼·姆斯季斯拉维奇。

en:
Rostislav Vasilkovich, baptized Gregory (died before 1141), was a Rurikid prince, son of Vasilko Rostislavich of Terebovlia. On his father's death in 1124 he became prince of Terebovlia while his brother Ivan took Halych.

In 1125 and 1126 he and Ivan joined Mstislav of Kiev in backing their cousin Rostislav Volodarevich of Peremyshl against Vladimir Volodarevich of Zvenigorod, who was supported by the king of Hungary. He died before 1141, and Terebovlia then passed to Ivan.

zh:
罗斯季斯拉夫·瓦西里科维奇（教名格里戈里，1141年前卒）是留里克王朝王公、捷列博夫利王公瓦西里科·罗斯季斯拉维奇之子。1124年父亲去世后，他成为捷列博夫利王公，兄弟伊凡领有加利奇。

1125至1126年，他与伊凡随同基辅大公姆斯季斯拉夫，支持堂兄弟普热梅希尔王公罗斯季斯拉夫·沃洛达列维奇，对抗得到匈牙利国王支持的兹韦尼哥罗德王公弗拉基米尔·沃洛达列维奇。他于1141年前去世，捷列博夫利随后并入伊凡的领地。

en:
Rostislav Volodarevich (died 1128) was the eldest son of Volodar Rostislavich of Peremyshl and ruled as prince of Zvenigorod from 1092 and of Peremyshl from 1124. In 1122 he was held hostage in Kraków in place of his father against a ransom of eight thousand grivnas.

After Volodar died in 1124 he defended Peremyshl against a Polish army, and in 1125–1126 against his younger brother Vladimir of Zvenigorod, aided by the king of Hungary. On his death Vladimir took Peremyshl, while Zvenigorod went to his son Ivan Berladnik.

en:
Rurik Rostislavich (d. 1092) was the eldest son of Rostislav Vladimirovich of Tmutarakan and a great-grandson of Yaroslav the Wise. After his father's death he and his brothers Volodar and Vasilko grew up dispossessed at Vladimir-Volynsky.

In 1084 the brothers fled to the Cherven cities, raised an army and occupied Vladimir in Volhynia. Rurik established himself as prince of Peremyshl, securing the southwestern Rus lands for his dynasty, and died childless in 1092; his brothers Volodar and Vasilko kept his lands.

zh:
留里克·罗斯季斯拉维奇（?—1092）是特穆塔拉干王公罗斯季斯拉夫·弗拉基米罗维奇的长子、智者雅罗斯拉夫的曾孙。父亲死后，他与弟弟沃洛达尔、瓦西里科作为被夺位的王公在弗拉基米尔-沃伦斯基长大。

1084年，三兄弟逃往切尔文诸城，募兵占领了沃伦的弗拉基米尔。留里克随后成为普热梅希尔王公，为家族保住了罗斯西南的土地。他于1092年去世，无子嗣，领地由弟弟沃洛达尔和瓦西里科继承。

en:
Vasilko Rostislavich (c. 1066–1124) was the third son of Rostislav Vladimirovich of Tmutarakan and Lanka, daughter of King Béla I of Hungary. With his elder brothers Rurik and Volodar he secured the Cherven cities and became the first prince of Terebovlia in 1092.

In 1097, after the council at Liubech, Grand Prince Sviatopolk II lured him to Kiev, where David Igorevich of Volhynia seized and blinded him. This blinding, almost unheard of among the Rurikids, shattered the Liubech settlement and reopened civil war. He held Terebovlia until his death in 1124.

瓦西里科·罗斯季斯拉维奇（约1066—1124）是特穆塔拉干王公罗斯季斯拉夫·弗拉基米罗维奇与匈牙利国王贝拉一世之女兰卡的第三子。他与兄长留里克、沃洛达尔一起守住切尔文诸城，1092年成为第一位捷列博夫利王公。

1097年柳别奇会议之后，基辅大公斯维亚托波尔克二世把他诱骗到基辅，沃伦王公达维德·伊戈列维奇将他逮捕并刺瞎双眼。这种酷刑在留里克王朝极为罕见，柳别奇协议由此破裂，内战再度爆发。他此后仍领有捷列博夫利，直至1124年去世。

en:
Vladimir Yaroslavich (1151–1199), the legitimate son of Yaroslav Osmomysl, was the last Rostislavichi prince of Halych. In 1187 his father left the throne to his illegitimate son Oleg; Vladimir seized Halych with boyar support, only to be driven out, and the struggle drew Hungary and Poland into civil war.

He fled to King Béla III of Hungary, who jailed him and gave Halych to his son Andrew. He escaped to Germany and returned in 1189 with backing from Emperor Frederick Barbarossa; his uncle Vsevolod the Big Nest's protection brought stability. He ruled until his death in 1199, after which Roman the Great of Volhynia seized Halych.

弗拉基米尔·雅罗斯拉维奇（1151—1199）是雅罗斯拉夫·奥斯莫梅斯尔的嫡子，也是哈利奇末代罗斯季斯拉夫系王公。1187年父亲遗命传位给庶子奥列格，弗拉基米尔在贵族支持下夺取哈利奇，却很快被逐，继承之争将匈牙利和波兰卷入内战。

他逃奔匈牙利国王贝拉三世，贝拉却将他囚禁，把哈利奇交给自己的儿子安德烈。弗拉基米尔逃往德意志，1189年在皇帝腓特烈一世支持下返国复位，舅父弗谢沃洛德·大窝的庇护为他带来稳定。他统治至1199年去世，此后沃伦的罗曼大帝夺取哈利奇。

en:
Volodymyrko Volodarovych (1104–1153), younger son of Volodar Rostislavich, was the first prince of a united Halych. He received Zvenyhorod in 1124, failed to take Peremyshl from his brother in 1125–1126 before inheriting it in 1128, and after adding Terebovlia and Halych made Halych his capital in 1141, defending the new principality against Kiev.

Allied with Yuri Dolgorukiy, he defeated the Kievan prince Izyaslav Mstislavich. In alliance with Emperor Manuel Komnenos against Hungary, he made peace with King Géza in 1152. He died in 1153 and was succeeded by Yaroslav Osmomysl.

弗拉基米尔科·沃洛达列维奇（1104—1153）是沃洛达尔·罗斯季斯拉维奇的幼子，也是统一的哈利奇公国第一位王公。1124年他领有兹韦尼哥罗德，1125至1126年未能从兄长手中夺取普热梅希尔，但于1128年继领该城；兼并捷列博夫利亚与哈利奇后，他于1141年定哈利奇为都城，并抵御基辅方面的进攻。

en:
Volodar Rostislavich (died 1124) was a Rurikid prince, son of Rostislav of Tmutarakan and, chronicles say, a daughter of King Béla I of Hungary. Expelled from Tmutarakan after 1067, he and his brothers seized lands in the Carpathian foothills. The Council of Liubech (1097) confirmed Peremyshl to him; in 1099 the brothers defeated Kiev at Rozhne Pole and repelled a Hungarian invasion.

Captured in Poland in 1122, he was ransomed by the blinded Vasilko for two thousand grivnas of silver. He died on 19 March 1124, counted with his brothers among the founders of Halych.

沃洛达尔·罗斯季斯拉维奇（？—1124）是留里克王朝王公，特穆塔拉干王公罗斯季斯拉夫·弗拉基米罗维奇之子；据后世史书记载，其母为匈牙利国王贝拉一世之女。1067年父亲死后，他与兄弟被逐出特穆塔拉干，随后在喀尔巴阡山麓夺取领地。1097年柳别奇会议确认普热梅希尔归他所有；1099年兄弟二人在罗日涅原野击败基辅军队，并击退匈牙利人的入侵。

en:
Yaroslav Osmomysl (c. 1135–1187) ruled Halych from 1153, son of Volodymyrko and a daughter of King Coloman of Hungary. He leant on Hungary and Poland against Kiev, which backed his rival cousin Ivan Berladnic; after years of war, Yaroslav secured Ivan's expulsion to Byzantium.

In 1172 he put aside his wife Olga of Suzdal for the concubine Anastasia, whom the Halych boyars burned at the stake. Forced to swear to live peacefully with Olga, he expelled her the next year. He died in 1187, bequeathing the throne to his natural son Oleg. His epithet Osmomysl, meaning 'Eight-Minded', was made famous by The Tale of Igor's Campaign.

zh:
雅罗斯拉夫·奥斯莫梅斯尔（约1135—1187）自1153年起为哈利奇王公，是弗拉基米尔科与匈牙利国王卡尔曼之女所生之子。外交上他依靠匈牙利和波兰对抗基辅，基辅支持与他争位的堂兄伊凡·贝尔拉德尼克；多年战争后，雅罗斯拉夫迫使伊凡流亡拜占庭。

1172年，他为宠姬阿纳斯塔西娅休弃妻子、苏兹达尔的奥尔加，哈利奇贵族愤而将阿纳斯塔西娅处以火刑。他被迫起誓与奥尔加和睦相处，却在次年将她逐走。1187年他去世，遗命传位给私生子奥列格。其绰号“奥斯莫梅斯尔”意为“八智”，因史诗《伊戈尔远征记》而闻名。

en:
Dündar Beg, called Felek al-Din (died 1324 or 1326), ruled the Hamidid beylik of southwestern Anatolia from about 1300. He moved his capital from Uluborlu to Eğirdir, rebuilt the city as Felekabad, and founded the Grand Mosque of Burdur.

Expanding during Ilkhanid internal strife, he seized Antalya and granted it to his brother Yunus, founder of the Teke branch. In 1321 he dropped Ilkhanid overlordship from his coins and took the title sultan. The Ilkhanid governor Timurtash later took Felekabad; Dündar fled to Antalya, was handed over by his nephew Mahmud, and was executed.

zh:
丁达尔贝伊，称号法莱克丁（卒于1324或1326年），约1300年起统治安纳托利亚西南部的哈米德侯国。他将都城从乌卢博尔卢迁至埃伊尔迪尔，重建该城并改名法莱克阿巴德，还修建了布尔杜尔大清真寺。

他趁伊儿汗内乱扩张，夺取安塔利亚，封给弟弟尤努斯，即泰克支系的始祖。1321年，他在钱币上取消伊儿汗的宗主署名，自称苏丹。后来伊儿汗异密帖木儿塔什攻占法莱克阿巴德，丁达尔逃往安塔利亚，被侄子马哈茂德交出，最终被处死。

en:
Hamid Beg was the eponymous ancestor of the Hamidid dynasty of southwestern Anatolia. His Turkmen tribe, originally settled in northern Syria, migrated into Anatolia, where he served the Sultanate of Rum and trained the children and army of Sultan Kayqubad I. In 1240 Sultan Kaykhusraw II granted him frontier lands around Isparta and Burdur.

He is said to have declared independence after the deposition of the Rum sultan Mesud II, ruling Isparta, Burdur and Eğirdir from his capital Uluborlu, though he may already have been dead by then; his death is placed in the late thirteenth century.

en:
Hızır Bey was a son of Dündar Bey, founder of the Hamidid beylik around Uluborlu in southwestern Anatolia. The Ilkhanid governor Timurtash seized Eğirdir and had Dündar killed at Antalya; Hızır later held the beylik together after its disruption.

He ruled around 1327–1328 and restored the damaged great mosque at Eğirdir, which took his name. In 1328 his brother İshak Bey returned from Mamluk Egypt and took over the beylik. Hızır's son Muizeddin İbrahim later held Şuhut.

en:
Kahaʻimaoeleʻa, also called Kahai IV, was a Hawaiian high chief, aliʻi nui of the island of Hawaiʻi, from 1285 to 1315. He was the son of Chief Kalapana and the chiefess Malamaʻihanaʻae, and succeeded his father after Kalapana died around 1285.

He was the first ruler to keep his royal residence in Waipiʻo Valley. By his half-sister Kapo-a-Kauluhailea he fathered Kalaunuiohua, who followed him on the island's throne.

Kalapana, also called Kalapanakuʻioʻiomoa, was a Hawaiian high chief of the island of Hawaiʻi. Tradition makes him possibly the son of Prince Kanaloa and his sister Makoʻani, children of Chief Kanipahu and Hualani of Molokai.

en:
Kalaunuiohua (fl. c. 1300) was a high chief of the island of Hawaiʻi in the Pili line, who succeeded his father Kahaimoelea. Chants remember him as a great warrior chief. He invaded Maui, Molokaʻi and Oʻahu, defeating each island's chief and carrying all three rulers off captive.

He next sailed against Kauaʻi, but was routed and taken prisoner by its sovereign Kukona. Freed after several years, he never made war again.

卡劳努伊奥胡阿（约1300年前后在世）是夏威夷岛的高级酋长，属皮利世系，继其父卡海莫埃莱阿之位。古代吟诵传说把他记为勇武善战的酋长：他入侵茂宜岛、莫洛凯岛和瓦胡岛，击败各岛酋长，将三位酋长全部掳走。

随后他进军考爱岛，却被考爱君主库科纳击溃并俘虏。被囚数年后获释，从此再未兴兵。

en:
Malamaʻihanaʻae was a Hawaiian high chiefess of the island of Hawaiʻi, born to Piʻikalani and his consort Kalamea. She married Kalapana, who came to rule the island after Kamaiole was murdered. Their son Kahaʻimaoeleʻa succeeded as chief after Kalapana died around 1285.

She later married the priest Haunaʻakamahala, who had a heiau temple built. Their daughter Kapo-a-Kauluhailea married Kahaʻimaoeleʻa and became the mother of Kalaunuiohua.

en:
Albert II of Brunswick-Lüneburg (c. 1294–1358), son of Duke Albert the Fat of Brunswick-Göttingen, was bishop of Halberstadt from 1325 to 1358 and spent most of it in feuds. In the 1324 chapter election he won only five votes, but Archbishop Matthias of Mainz chose him, although Pope John XXII had granted the see to Giseko of Holstein.

In 1325 he took Guntekenburg from the counts of Regenstein, and in 1326 Quedlinburg's guardianship passed to his church. His own chapter then allied with the city's collegiate chapters against him. When he closed the cathedral and the Liebfrauenkirche, Halberstadt rose, several of his envoys were killed and he had to flee; peace came in 1338.

In the 1350s Pope Innocent VI excommunicated him and forced his resignation. He died in 1358 and was buried at St Blasius in Brunswick.

阿尔布雷希特二世·冯·不伦瑞克-吕讷堡（约1294—1358）是不伦瑞克-哥廷根公爵“胖子”阿尔布雷希特之子，1325至1358年任哈尔伯施塔特主教，任内大半时间都在争斗。1324年的参事会选举中他只得五票，美因茨大主教马蒂亚斯却选定了他，尽管教皇约翰二十二世已把该主教区封给荷尔斯泰因的吉塞科。

1325年他从雷根施泰因伯爵手中攻取贡特肯堡，1326年奎德林堡的庇护权转归他的教会。随后，他自己的参事会与城中的教士会联合起来反对他。他关闭主教座堂和圣母教堂，哈尔伯施塔特市民随即暴动，他的几名使者被杀，本人被迫出逃；直到1338年才恢复和平。

1350年代，教皇英诺森六世将他逐出教会，迫使他辞去主教职位。他于1358年去世，葬于不伦瑞克的圣布拉修斯教堂。

en:
Bayram was the first bey of the Hacıemiroğulları, a Çepni Turkmen lordship on the Black Sea coast of northeastern Anatolia. Subject first to the Mongols and then to Eretna, the region saw Bayram make himself independent during the Mongol civil war of 1335–1336.

He fought the Empire of Trebizond, and in 1348 joined a league of beys besieging Trebizond, only to be defeated. His death date is unknown; by 1357 his son Hacı Emir had succeeded him.

巴伊拉姆是哈吉埃米尔贝伊国的第一代贝伊，这是安纳托利亚东北黑海沿岸的切普尼土库曼人领地。该地区先臣服于蒙古人、后臣服于埃雷特纳，巴伊拉姆在1335—1336年蒙古内战期间自立为政。

他与特拉布宗帝国交战，1348年联合众贝伊围攻特拉布宗城，却遭败绩。其卒年不详，到1357年其子哈吉埃米尔已经继位。

en:
Hacı Emir İbrahim Beg was the son of Bayram and ruler of the Black Sea beylik later named Hacıemiroğulları after him. By 1357 he was raiding Trebizond's lands around Maçka, and in 1358 sealed peace by marrying Theodora, daughter of Emperor Basil.

A Giresun campaign failed in 1361, but backed by his ally Kadı Burhaneddin he took Cotyora (Ordu) in 1380 and moved his capital to nearby Eskipazar.

en:
Eljigidei, also called Alchidai, was a Borjigin prince, the son of Hachiun, a full brother of Genghis Khan. Hachiun died young, so Eljigidei headed the family. In 1203 he warned Temüjin of an impending attack by Toghrul, the Kereit khan, and fought when the Kereit were destroyed. In the 1206 appanage grants he received his father's share as a left-wing prince.

Campaigning under Ögedei, he helped destroy the Jin field army at Sanfeng Mountain in 1232 and captured Puxian Wannu of Eastern Xia in 1233. In 1251 he helped enthrone Möngke as khan.

按赤台（又译阿勒赤台、额勒只吉歹）是孛儿只斤氏宗王，成吉思汗同母弟合赤温之子。合赤温早卒，由按赤台掌理家族。1203年，他侦知克烈部王罕将要来袭，先行告知铁木真，随后在攻灭克烈部的战事中从军作战。1206年蒙古帝国分封时，他作为左翼宗王领受父亲一系的份额。

他随窝阔台征战，1232年在三峰山之战参与歼灭金朝野战主力，1233年擒获东夏的蒲鲜万奴。1251年，他参与拥戴蒙哥即汗位。

Henry III of Brunswick-Lüneburg (c. 1296–1363) was a Welf prince who held the bishopric of Hildesheim from 1331 against the will of the pope. Son of Duke Albert II of Brunswick-Göttingen, he was elected by the cathedral chapter in August 1331, but his predecessor had placed the bishopric in papal hands before dying, so confirmation was doubtful.

Pope John XXII appointed Count Erich of Holstein-Schaumburg instead and placed Henry, who refused to yield, under ban and interdict. With the chapter, the Brunswick dukes and the local nobility behind him, Henry controlled most of the bishopric, while Erich held little beyond the city and its monasteries. The schism lasted until about 1350.

In 1346–1349 he built the water castle of Marienburg near Hildesheim. He died in Hildesheim on 6 February 1363.

海因里希三世·冯·不伦瑞克-吕讷堡（约1296—1363）是韦尔夫家族的亲王，1331年起违抗教皇的意愿据有希尔德斯海姆主教区。他是不伦瑞克-哥廷根公爵阿尔布雷希特二世之子，1331年8月由主教座堂参事会选举继位，但前任主教临终前已把主教区交到教皇手中，确认因而悬而未决。

教皇约翰二十二世改任荷尔斯泰因-绍恩堡伯爵埃里希为主教，不肯让步的海因里希被处以绝罚和禁罚。在参事会、不伦瑞克公爵和当地贵族支持下，他控制了主教区大部分地方，埃里希则基本只有城市和修道院。分裂局面持续到约1350年。

1346至1349年，他在希尔德斯海姆附近修建水堡马林堡。1363年2月6日，他在希尔德斯海姆去世。

en:
Otto I of Brunswick (c. 1247–1279), a Welf and son of Duke Otto the Child, was bishop of Hildesheim from 1260 until his death. Elected while still under age, he was confirmed by the pope in 1264 and consecrated in 1274. He enlarged his church's lands, buying the county of Wohldenberg in 1275.

A feud with his brother Duke Albert followed an arbitration awarding Albert five Salzgau villages. After their brother John, who had supported Otto, died, the war went badly: Albert took Campen and marched on Hildesheim. Otto died with the town under threat on 4 July 1279, aged thirty-two.

奥托一世·冯·不伦瑞克-吕讷堡（约1247—1279）是韦尔夫家族成员，公爵“孩童”奥托之子，1260年至去世任希尔德斯海姆主教。他尚在幼年便被选出，1264年获教皇确认，1274年才正式祝圣。他扩张教会领地，1275年购得沃尔登贝格伯国。

一项裁决将萨尔茨高的五个村庄判给兄长阿尔布雷希特公爵后，两人交战。最初支持奥托的兄长约翰死后，战事不利：1279年阿尔布雷希特攻占坎彭，进军希尔德斯海姆。1279年7月4日，在城池告急之际奥托去世，年仅32岁。

en:
Amano was the Garad, or king, of the Muslim Hadiya state south of Shewa in the early fourteenth century. Hadiya lay on trade routes that Emperor Amda Seyon I meant to take from the Muslim sultanates.

Amano refused to visit the emperor and pay tribute, urged on by a Muslim called Bel'am, whom the royal chronicle denounces as a prophet of darkness. Amda Seyon invaded Hadiya, put many to the sword, enslaved the rest and took Amano prisoner, while Bel'am escaped to Ifat. Hadiya was soon absorbed. By 1332 it was supplying troops for the emperor's campaign against Ifat.

阿玛诺是14世纪初绍阿以南穆斯林政权哈迪亚的国王，称号加拉德。哈迪亚地处商路上，皇帝安达·塞永一世正想从穆斯林苏丹国手中夺取这些商路。

阿玛诺拒绝觐见皇帝并缴纳贡赋，怂恿他的是一个名叫贝拉阿姆的穆斯林，皇帝的编年史斥其为‘黑暗的先知’。安达·塞永于是入侵哈迪亚，以利剑屠戮许多居民，将其余人掳为奴隶，并俘虏了阿玛诺，贝拉阿姆则逃往伊法特。哈迪亚随后被并入帝国。到1332年，它已为皇帝征讨伊法特的战事提供兵员。

en:
Heinrich Kramer (c. 1430–1505), Latinized as Henricus Institoris, was a German Dominican friar and inquisitor born at Schlettstadt in Alsace. Before 1474 he was made inquisitor for the Tyrol and Salzburg.

Pope Innocent VIII's bull of 1484 affirmed his authority to prosecute witches, but his witch trial at Innsbruck in 1485 was halted by the bishop of Brixen, who expelled him.

In Cologne he wrote the Malleus Maleficarum, first printed in 1487; condemned by the Cologne theological faculty, it yet became the most influential text of the European witch trials. In 1500 Pope Alexander VI assigned him to Bohemia and Moravia.

海因里希·克雷默（约1430—1505），拉丁名为亨利克斯·因斯蒂托里斯，是德意志多明我会修士、宗教裁判官，生于阿尔萨斯的施莱茨塔特。1474年前，他受命在蒂罗尔和萨尔茨堡主持异端审判。

1484年教宗英诺森八世发布诏书，确认他有权追猎女巫；但1485年他在因斯布鲁克主持的女巫审判被布里克森主教叫停，本人也遭驱逐。

他在科隆写成《女巫之槌》，1487年首次刊印。这部猎巫手册虽遭科隆神学家谴责，却成为欧洲女巫审判中影响最大的文本。1500年教宗亚历山大六世将他派往波希米亚和摩拉维亚。

en:
Enrico Zuccalli (c. 1642–1724) was a Swiss architect from Roveredo in the Three Leagues who shaped Bavarian High Baroque. He served the Wittelsbach rulers of Bavaria and Cologne and helped introduce Italian Baroque architecture to Germany. Trained in Bernini's circle in Rome, he settled in Munich in 1669 as court architect.

He completed the Theatinerkirche and Nymphenburg Palace, built Lustheim Palace and began the New Palace at Schleißheim. The Austrian occupation of 1706 cost him his offices; he then rebuilt Ettal Abbey church and died in Munich in 1724.

恩里科·祖卡利（约1642—1724）是瑞士建筑师，生于三同盟的罗韦雷多，塑造了巴伐利亚的鼎盛巴洛克风貌。他为巴伐利亚和科隆的维特尔斯巴赫统治者服务，推动意大利巴洛克建筑传入德意志。他曾在罗马的贝尔尼尼圈子中受训，1669年定居慕尼黑，出任宫廷建筑师。

他完成了剧院教堂与宁芬堡宫，修建卢斯特海姆宫，又开建施莱斯海姆新宫。1706年奥地利占领巴伐利亚后他被免去一切职务，随后主持改建埃塔尔修道院教堂，1724年在慕尼黑去世。

en:
Adelaide of Hesse (after 1323–after 1371) was the eldest daughter of Landgrave Henry II of Hesse and Elisabeth of Thuringia. In September 1341 she married King Casimir III of Poland and was crowned queen consort.

The marriage was unhappy; Casimir soon lived apart from her while Adelaide resided at Żarnowiec castle. He separated from her in 1356 to marry another, and the church annulled Adelaide's marriage only in 1368. She returned to Hesse and, after Casimir's death, won Pope Gregory XI's support for the return of her property.

黑森的阿德海德（1323年后—1371年后）是黑森方伯海因里希二世与图林根的伊丽莎白的长女。1341年9月，她嫁给波兰国王卡齐米日三世，并加冕为王后。

这段婚姻并不幸福，卡齐米日很快便与她分居，阿德海德主要居住在扎尔诺维茨城堡。1356年国王离弃她另娶，教会迟至1368年才宣布废除她的婚姻。她返回黑森，并在卡齐米日死后争取到教皇格列高利十一世的支持，要求归还自己的财产。

Adelheid of Ravensberg (c. 1270–1338) was the daughter of Count Otto III of Ravensberg and Hedwig of Lippe. In 1297 she married Otto I, Landgrave of Hesse, becoming landgravine when he inherited Hesse in 1308.

Her children included Henry II, called the Iron, who ruled Hesse from 1328, and Otto, who became Archbishop of Magdeburg in 1331. She survived her husband by ten years and died at Marburg, where she was buried in the Church of St. Elizabeth.

Eberhard I of Eppstein (c. 1337–1391) was a nobleman of the younger line of the House of Eppstein, son of Gottfried V and Liutgard of Breuberg. He married three times, his last wife being Luitgard of Falkenstein.

That marriage gave his sons Gottfried VII and Eberhard II a claim to the Falkenstein inheritance, from which in 1419 they received the Butzbach third, including Königstein and Kransberg. Eberhard died between May and October 1391.

埃伯哈德一世·冯·埃普施泰因（约1337—1391）出身埃普施泰因家族幼支，是戈特弗里德五世与布罗伊贝格的柳特加德之子。他三次成婚，最后一任妻子是法尔肯施泰因的柳特加德。

这次婚姻使他的儿子戈特弗里德七世与埃伯哈德二世取得法尔肯施泰因遗产的继承权，两人于1419年分得其中的“布茨巴赫三分之一”，包括柯尼希施泰因和克兰斯贝格。埃伯哈德卒于1391年5月至10月之间。

Elisabeth of Hesse (c. 1320–1390) was a daughter of Landgrave Henry II the Iron of Hesse and Elisabeth of Thuringia. In 1341 she married Duke Ernest I of Brunswick-Göttingen.

She bore at least six children, including Otto I, who succeeded his father in Göttingen in 1367. Widowed that year, Elisabeth died at Göttingen on 7 March 1390 and was buried in Hannover.

Elisabeth of Meissen (c. 1306–1367) was the daughter of Margrave Frederick I of Meissen. In 1321 she married Henry II, Landgrave of Hesse, later called the Iron.

She bore him five children, including Otto the Younger, his co-ruler from 1339, and Adelaide, who married King Casimir III of Poland in 1341. After Henry accused her of adultery in 1339, Elisabeth withdrew to Eisenach under her brother's protection, and she died there in 1367.

Gottfried V of Eppstein (c. 1318–1341) was a nobleman of the younger line of the House of Eppstein. The son of Gottfried IV and Loretta of Daun, he married Liutgard of Breuberg in 1328.

As an heiress she brought into the marriage an eighth of the lordship of Breuberg. Their sons were Gottfried VI and Eberhard I, who continued the Eppstein line. Gottfried died between 1336 and 1341.

en:
Henry I, called the Child (1244–1308), was the first landgrave of Hesse and founder of the ruling dynasty, son of Henry II of Brabant and Sophie of Thuringia. When the Ludowingian line died out in 1247, his mother fought the Thuringian succession war and secured Hesse for him; the 1265 Treaty of Langsdorf confirmed him as landgrave under Mainz.

Outlawed in 1274, he regained King Rudolf I's favour against Ottokar II of Bohemia, defeated Mainz at Fritzlar in 1290, and in 1292 became a prince of the realm. He died at Marburg amid a succession war among his sons.

海因里希一世，绰号“小孩”（1244年6月24日—1308年12月21日），是第一代黑森伯爵、黑森王朝的始祖，布拉班特公爵亨利二世与图林根的索菲之子。1247年路德温格家族绝嗣，他的母亲在图林根继承战争中为他保住黑森，1265年的《兰格斯多夫条约》确认他为隶属于美因茨的黑森伯爵。

en:
Henry II of Hesse, called the Iron (before 1302–1376), was Landgrave of Hesse from 1328, having ruled as co-regent with his father Otto I since 1320. In 1321 he married Elisabeth of Thuringia. He won two feuds against Abbot Henry VII of Fulda in 1356 and 1361.

When his only son Otto died in 1366, Henry made his nephew Hermann co-regent, provoking war with Duke Otto of Brunswick; to fund it he taxed all imported goods. He died on 3 June 1376 and Hermann succeeded him.

en:
Hermann I the Elder of Hesse (after 1305–1368/1370) was the youngest son of Landgrave Otto I of Hesse and Adelheid of Ravensberg. In 1326 he was offered a church prebend at Avignon, but renounced an ecclesiastical career. When his brother Henry II succeeded in 1328, he received Nordeck Castle as his apanage, adding Grebenstein Castle in 1349.

After his nephew Otto the Younger died in 1366, he did not claim the landgraviate. He died between July 1368 and July 1370, leaving no issue.

en:
Otto I (c. 1272–1328) was landgrave of Upper Hesse from 1308 and reunited the landgraviate by inheriting Lower Hesse in 1311 after his half-brother John's death. A son of Henry I the Child, he held Marburg and Giessen and ruled from Kassel.

He waged a long feud with Archbishop Matthias of Mainz, losing Giessen briefly in 1327 before its citizens restored it to him, and won a victory at Wetzlar, after which King John of Luxembourg mediated a settlement in 1328. He died at Kassel and was buried in Ahnaberg monastery.

Otto the Younger of Hesse, called Otto the Marksman (before 1322–1366), was the only son of Landgrave Henry II of Hesse and Elisabeth of Thuringia. In 1338 he married Elisabeth of Cleves; the marriage was childless. From 1339 he was co-regent with his father and imperial governor in Mühlhausen.

He fought in his father's victorious feuds against Abbot Henry VII of Fulda, ravaging Hausen in 1356 and Hünfeld in 1361. He died suddenly at Spangenberg in December 1366, rumoured poisoned by the Fulda abbot.

In 1338 he married Elisabeth of [GetCountry('KLE').GetName]; the marriage was childless. From 1339 he was co-regent with his father and imperial governor in [ShowLocationName('muhlhausen')].

He fought in his father's victorious feuds against Abbot Henry VII of [ShowLocationName('fulda')], ravaging Hausen in 1356 and [ShowLocationName('hunfeld')] in 1361. He died suddenly at Spangenberg in December 1366, rumoured poisoned by the Fulda abbot.

奥托（1322年前—1366），绰号“射手”，是黑森方伯海因里希二世与图林根的伊丽莎白的独子。1338年他娶克莱沃的伊丽莎白为妻，婚姻无子嗣。1339年起，他与父亲共同摄政，并担任帝国在米尔豪森的总督。

他参加了父亲对富尔达修道院长亨利七世的获胜家族仇争：1356年洗劫豪森，1361年劫掠欣费尔德。1366年12月他猝死于施潘根贝格，传言称他是被富尔达修道院长毒杀。

en:
Sophie of Thuringia (20 March 1224–29 May 1275), duchess of Brabant, was the daughter of Landgrave Louis IV of Thuringia and Saint Elisabeth of Hungary, born at Wartburg Castle. In 1241 she married Henry II of Brabant, and their son Henry the Child founded the Hessian dynasty.

When her uncle Henry Raspe died heirless in 1247, she fought the War of the Thuringian Succession against the Meissen margraves and Mainz, retaining Hesse for her son; the 1264 settlement gave him Hesse while Meissen took Thuringia. She died at Marburg and was buried at Villers Abbey.

图林根的索菲（1224年3月20日—1275年5月29日），布拉班特公爵夫人，是图林根伯爵路德维希四世与匈牙利的圣伊丽莎白之女，生于瓦尔特堡城堡。1241年她嫁给布拉班特公爵亨利二世，所生之子“小孩”海因里希后来成为黑森王朝的开创者。

1247年叔父海因里希·拉斯佩无嗣而终，她遂投身图林根继承战争，对抗迈森藩侯和美因茨，为儿子保住黑森；1264年的分割协定使他获得黑森，图林根则归迈森。她死于马尔堡，葬于维莱尔修道院。

en:
Agnes of Hohenberg (died 5 June 1366) was a Swabian noblewoman of the counts of Hohenberg, kinsmen of the Habsburgs, and daughter of Count Rudolf II and Margareta of Nassau-Hadamar. In 1349 she married Duke Konrad IV of Teck.

In June 1352 the couple and Konrad's cousin Friedrich III bound themselves to keep open several Tyrolean castles of the margrave of Brandenburg. On 4 September 1352 Konrad was murdered in Munich, leaving Agnes a childless widow. Friedrich still owed her 5000 guilders in 1356.

With her mother she founded the St Ursula benefice at Ehingen. She died on 5 June 1366 and was buried in the collegiate church of St Moriz in Rottenburg, where a yearly memorial for her and Konrad was kept.

阿格尼丝·冯·霍恩贝格（？—1366年6月5日）是施瓦本贵族女子，出身与哈布斯堡有亲的霍恩贝格伯爵家，是伯爵鲁道夫二世与拿骚-哈达玛的玛格丽特之女。1349年，她嫁给泰克公爵康拉德四世。

1352年6月，夫妇二人与康拉德的堂弟腓特烈三世一同承诺，为勃兰登堡藩侯开放其在蒂罗尔的数座城堡。同年9月4日，康拉德在慕尼黑遇刺，阿格尼丝成为没有子嗣的寡妇。1356年腓特烈仍欠她5000弗罗林。

她与母亲一同在埃英根创立了圣乌尔苏拉俸职。她于1366年6月5日去世，葬于罗滕堡的圣莫里茨修道院教堂，教堂每年在这一天为她和康拉德举行追思。

en:
Agnes of Schaunberg (died after 24 June 1348) was a daughter of Count Henry V of Schaunberg (d. 1351) and his wife Anna of Truhendingen. Before 25 June 1337 she married Count Henry of Hohenberg-Rotenburg, a son of Count Rudolf I of Hohenberg.

Her husband was killed in battle on 12 May 1352. Their only recorded child, a son named Rudolf, died before 1379. Agnes herself is last documented alive on 24 June 1348.

Albert II of Hohenberg-Rotenburg (c. 1235–1298) inherited his family's lands from his father Burchard V in 1253 and refounded Rotenburg as his seat around 1280. A follower of his brother-in-law King Rudolf I of Habsburg, he served as imperial governor of Lower Swabia, charged with recovering lost imperial and former Staufen lands. In 1280 he defeated and imprisoned Count Hartmann of Grüningen.

After Rudolf's death he backed Albert of Austria against King Adolf of Nassau. On 17 April 1298 he was killed near his castle of Leinstetten. Two song stanzas attributed to him as 'Albert of Haigerloch' survive in the Codex Manesse.

阿尔布雷希特二世·冯·霍恩贝格-罗滕堡（约1235—1298）于1253年从父亲布尔夏德五世手中继承家族领地，约1280年重建罗滕堡作为统治中心。他追随姐夫哈布斯堡的鲁道夫一世，任下施瓦本帝国地方长官，奉命收回失去的帝国领地和施陶芬旧领。1280年他击败并囚禁格吕宁根伯爵哈特曼。

鲁道夫死后他支持奥地利的阿尔布雷希特对抗国王拿骚的阿道夫。1298年4月17日，他在自己的莱恩施泰滕城堡附近战死。《马内塞手抄本》保存了两节署名“海格洛赫的阿尔布雷希特”、被认为是他的歌词。

en:
Burchard II of Zollern-Hohenberg (c. 1096–1150/1155) was a Swabian count and the ancestor of the Hohenberg line of the Hohenzollern family. The second son of Count Frederick I of Zollern and Udilhild of Urach, he saw his elder brother Frederick II inherit Zollern after their father died in 1125, while he founded the Zollern-Hohenberg branch, named for Hohenberg Castle near Schorzingen.

He married Helmburgis of Schala-Burghausen, and his sons Burchard III and Frederick held the county of Hohenberg. His great-great-granddaughter Gertrude married Rudolf of Habsburg, the future king of the Romans.

en:
Burchard III of Zollern-Hohenberg (died after 4 July 1193) was a Swabian count of the line that split from the House of Hohenzollern in the twelfth century, the son of Count Burchard II and Helmburgis of Schala-Burghausen. He is attested as count of Zollern in 1163 and as count of Hohenberg from 1179.

With his brother Frederick he witnessed charters of Emperor Frederick I and Duke Frederick of Swabia. He married Kunigunde of Grünberg and was the father of Burchard IV, who succeeded him.

en:
Burchard IV of Zollern-Hohenberg (died before 1225) was a Swabian count, the son of Count Burchard III and Kunigunde of Grünberg. In 1207 he and his brother Albert, as counts of Zollern, witnessed a charter of King Philip of Swabia at Strasbourg.

He is attested as count of Hohenberg from 1213, when he appeared at Constance and Überlingen, and in 1216–1217 he attended proceedings of King Frederick II in Constance and Rottweil.

He married Wilipirg of Aichelberg, who bore him his successor Burchard V and a daughter Kunigunde. His granddaughter Gertrud Anna married Rudolf of Habsburg, the later German king.

en:
Burchard V of Hohenberg (died 14 July 1253) was Count of Hohenberg and Haigerloch, the only son of Burchard IV and Wilipirg of Aichelberg. In 1233 he married Mechthild, an heiress of the Counts Palatine of Tübingen, bringing the dynasty lands around Nagold and Wildberg.

His daughter Gertrud Anna married Rudolf of Habsburg in 1245 and became German queen after his election as king in 1273. His other children included the minstrel Albert II and Burchard VI. On his death the main county passed to Albert, while Nagold and Wildberg went to Burchard VI, founder of a junior line.

Rudolf I of Hohenberg (died 11 January 1336) was Count of Hohenberg and lord of Triberg, the son of the minstrel-count Albert II and Margaret of Fürstenberg. In 1335 Emperor Louis the Bavarian named him imperial governor in Alsace and Lower Swabia.

By his first wife Agnes of Werdenberg he had four sons, Albert, Rudolf II, Hugo and Henry, along with a daughter; his two later marriages were childless. He died in Austria in January 1336 and was buried in the family vault at Ehingen.

en:
Rudolf III of Hohenberg (died 1389) was a Swabian count of Hohenberg, succeeding his father Rudolf II around 1336. His kinswoman Gertrud of Hohenberg was the wife of King Rudolf of Habsburg. Rudolf married Ida of Toggenburg, who bore him a daughter but no son, and he was deep in debt.

On 26 October 1381 he sold the entire county of Hohenberg for 66000 gold gulden to Duke Leopold III of Austria, and comital rule in his line ended. He died before 30 November 1389, the last male of the Hohenberg-Rotenburg branch.

Ursula of Pfirt (died after 5 May 1367) was the daughter of Count Ulrich III of Pfirt, and a younger sister of Joanna of Pfirt, wife of Duke Albert II of Austria. In 1333 she and her husband Count Hugo I of Hohenberg-Rotenburg renounced their rights to the County of Ferrette, and between 1347 and 1351 she held the lordships of Belfort and Rougemont.

After Hugo died on 26 May 1354 she married Count William II of Montfort-Bregenz. Her daughter, also named Ursula, married William's son Count William III and later Eberhard IV of Lupfen.

en:
Haniji (died 1395) was the founder and first king of Hokuzan, the northernmost of the three Ryukyu kingdoms, which he broke away from a Chūzan weakened under King Tamagusuku.

Songs preserved in the Omoro Sōshi relate that Haniji destroyed the lord of Nakijin, a cousin's son, and took Nakijin Castle; then in 1322 he threw off Tamagusuku's rule and called himself king of Hokuzan. He held northern Okinawa and its neighbouring islands, and in 1383 he sent tribute to the Ming court of China.

The Chūzan Seifu gives his son Min as his successor. A reign of nearly seventy years leads some scholars to think Haniji was several rulers of the same name in succession, since repeating a name across generations was common in Ryukyu.

zh:
怕尼芝（？—1395）是琉球三山时代北山王国的建立者和初代国王，他趁中山在玉城治下国力衰弱，另立北山。

据《思草纸》中的琉歌记载，他攻灭了今归仁按司（其堂兄弟之子），夺取今归仁城；1322年他宣布脱离玉城的统治，自称北山王，领有冲绳本岛北部及附近岛屿。1383年，他向中国明朝朝贡。

据《中山世谱》记载，他死后由儿子珉继位。因在位近七十年，部分学者认为“怕尼芝”可能指数代同名的君主，当时琉球父子数代同名十分常见。

en:
Baydu (died 4 October 1295) was the sixth Ilkhan of Persia, a grandson of Hulagu and son of Taraqai. After serving as viceroy in the Jazira, he overthrew his cousin Gaykhatu, who was strangled on 21 March 1295, and was enthroned at Tabriz.

An easygoing ruler sympathetic to Christianity, he wore a cross and allowed churches in his ordo while the victorious amirs partitioned the realm. Arghun's son Ghazan, backed by Amir Nawruz, then revolted from Khorasan; Baydu's army melted away, he was caught near Nakhchivan and executed on 4 October 1295, after a seven-month reign.

拜都性情温和、易于摆布，本人同情基督教，佩戴十字架，允许在自己的斡耳朵内设置礼拜堂，而国土尽被参与政变的异密瓜分。阿鲁浑之子合赞在异密捏兀鲁思支持下从呼罗珊举兵，拜都的军队纷纷倒戈；他逃往格鲁吉亚途中在纳希切万附近被俘，1295年10月4日被处死，在位仅约七个月。

en:
Musa Khan was a Borjigid prince and a grandson of Ilkhan Baydu. In April 1336 his patron Ali Padshah of Baghdad defeated Ilkhan Arpa Ke'un at the Battle of Jaghatu; Arpa was captured and killed at Soltaniyeh, and Musa was enthroned as a figurehead Ilkhan.

Within months Jalayirid leader Hasan Buzurg defeated them at Qara Darra and executed Ali; Musa fled. In June 1337 he joined Togha Temür and reoccupied Soltaniyeh, but Emir Qara Hasan captured and killed him in July 1337.

木撒是孛儿只斤氏宗王，伊儿汗拜都之孙。1336年4月，拥立他的巴格达的阿里在察哈图之战中击败伊儿汗阿儿巴；阿儿巴不久在苏丹尼耶被擒杀，木撒随后被扶立为伊儿汗，实为阿里的傀儡。

数月后，札剌亦儿部首领大哈散在喀拉·达拉击败二人，阿里被处死，木撒出逃。1337年6月，他投奔争位者脱合帖木儿，合兵再占苏丹尼耶，却被异密哈喇·哈散擒获，于1337年7月被杀。

en:
Adelaide of Nassau (c. 1311 – 8 August 1344) was a countess of the Walram line of Nassau, the daughter of Count Gerlach I of Nassau and Agnes of Hesse. In or after 1327 she married Ulrich III, who became Lord of Hanau in 1346.

She bore him at least five children, including his heir Ulrich IV. Adelaide died on 8 August 1344. She was buried in Arnsburg Abbey, where her gravestone survives.

Agnes of Hohenlohe (before 1295 – 29 November 1346) was the daughter of Kraft I of Hohenlohe-Weikersheim. In 1310 she married Ulrich II, Lord of Hanau, and bore him ten children.

Her eldest son Ulrich III succeeded as Lord of Hanau, while another son, Conrad, became prince-abbot of Fulda before he was killed in 1383. Her daughters married into the families of Falkenstein and Isenburg or entered convents at Patershausen and Gerlachsheim. Agnes died on 29 November 1346.

en:
Elisabeth von Rieneck (c. 1260 – c. 1300) was the daughter of Count Louis III of Rieneck. The peace of 1271, which ended the long conflict with the Archbishops of Mainz over the western Spessart, stipulated her marriage to Ulrich I of Hanau. Betrothed in 1272 while both were still children, they were to marry six years later.

Her rich dowry, including the town of Steinau an der Straße, greatly strengthened the young Lordship of Hanau. Her son Ulrich II later succeeded as lord, and she was buried at Arnsburg Abbey.

她的嫁妆丰厚，包括施泰瑙安德施特拉瑟城，大大增强了新兴哈瑙领地的实力。她的儿子乌尔里希二世后来继位，她本人葬于阿恩斯堡修道院。

她的嫁妆丰厚，包括施泰瑙安德施特拉瑟城，大大增强了新兴哈瑙领地的实力。她的儿子乌尔里希二世后来继位，她本人葬于阿恩斯堡修道院。

en:
Reinhard of Hanau (born between 1330 and 1340, died after 1400) was a younger son of Lord Ulrich III and Adelaide of Nassau. As Hanau followed primogeniture, his elder brother Ulrich IV inherited and Reinhard was steered into the Church.

He became rector of Wertheim church in 1386 and held canonries at Würzburg, where he was archdeacon, and at Mainz. In 1400 he exchanged his Würzburg posts with the Schwarzburg family, the last year he is documented.

zh:
赖因哈德·冯·哈瑙（1330至1340年间生，1400年后卒）是哈瑙领主乌尔里希三世与拿骚的阿德尔海德较年幼的儿子之一。由于哈瑙实行长子继承制，领主权归兄长乌尔里希四世，赖因哈德被安排走教会之路。

他1386年任韦尔特海姆教堂教区长，后在维尔茨堡大教堂任执事长和教士会成员，并任美因茨大教堂教士会成员。1400年，他把维尔茨堡的职位与施瓦茨堡家族交换，这也是文献中最后一次记载他在世。

en:
Ulrich I (c. 1255/1260 – late 1305 or early 1306) was Lord of Hanau from 1281, when he succeeded his father Reinhard I. Through his mother he inherited a sixth share of the wealthy Münzenberg inheritance.

In 1292 his feud with the Archbishop of Mainz ended in defeat and imprisonment at Bingen. A loyal follower of the kings of Germany, he was appointed Landvogt of the Wetterau in 1300, and King Albert granted Hanau its city charter in 1303.

乌尔里希一世（约1255/1260—1305年末或1306年初）自1281年父亲赖因哈德一世去世后担任哈瑙领主。他凭借母亲一方继承了富饶的明岑贝格遗产的六分之一。

en:
Ulrich II (c. 1288–1346) was Lord of Hanau from 1305/1306. In 1314 he attended Emperor Louis IV's election in Frankfurt, afterwards helping to pacify the Wetterau by settling noble feuds in courts.

He enlarged his lordship by buying judicial rights over Brandenstein and half of Schlüchtern, holding Bornheimerberg as an imperial mortgage, and gaining extensive Rieneck lands after an inheritance dispute in 1333. In 1339 he decreed primogeniture in Hanau, among the earliest such laws in Germany. He died on 23 September 1346.

乌尔里希二世（约1288—1346）自1305/1306年起担任哈瑙领主。1314年他在法兰克福出席皇帝路德维希四世的选举，此后推动以法庭而非私战解决韦特劳贵族的纠纷。

他不断扩张领地：购得布兰登施泰因的司法权及施吕希滕一半司法权，以帝国抵押的形式领有博恩海默贝格，1333年又在继承争议中取得大片林埃克领地。1339年，他在哈瑙颁布长子继承法，是德国最早的同类法令之一。他于1346年9月23日去世。

en:
Ulrich III (c. 1310–1369/1370) was Lord of Hanau from 1346 and imperial governor in the Wetterau. He lent to Emperor Charles IV and from 1349 received Frankfurt offices as security; with Bornheimerberg these posts encircled the city, whose guild disputes he mediated from 1358.

He attended the Metz and Nuremberg diets of 1356 that issued the Golden Bull. His wife was Adelaide of Nassau, mother of his successor Ulrich IV.

乌尔里希三世（约1310—1369/1370）自1346年起任哈瑙领主，并兼任韦特劳的帝国长官。他曾向皇帝查理四世放贷，1349年起取得法兰克福的若干职位作为抵押；加上博恩海默贝格领地，这些职位形成对法兰克福的包围，1358年起他还出面调解城中的行会纷争。

1356年他出席颁布金玺诏书的梅斯与纽伦堡帝国会议。他的妻子是拿骚的阿德尔海德，即继承人乌尔里希四世的母亲。

en:
Ulrich IV (c. 1330/1340–1380), son of Ulrich III, was Lord of Hanau from 1369/1370. He joined the Star League against Hesse and killed the Hessian ally Frowin of Hutten; Frowin's relatives captured him, and his uncle, the Bishop of Speyer, won his release for a 7500-guilder ransom.

In 1372 he sold Babenhausen to the Bohemian crown and received it back as a fief; in 1375 he finalized the Hanau primogeniture decree. He died in 1380 and was buried in Arnsburg Abbey.

乌尔里希四世（约1330/1340—1380）是乌尔里希三世之子，1369/1370年起任哈瑙领主。他加入对抗黑森的“星辰同盟”，杀死黑森的盟友胡滕的弗罗温；弗罗温的亲属将他俘获，其叔父施派尔主教出面调解，他以7500盾赎金获释。

en:
Berthold VII of Henneberg-Schleusingen, called the Wise (1272–1340), ruled as count for fifty-six years from 1284 and rose from local count to imperial prince. In 1309 King Henry VII pledged him the imperial city of Schweinfurt, and on 25 July 1310 raised him to imperial prince at the Frankfurt Diet.

In 1312 the marriage of Berthold's son Henry VIII to Jutta of Brandenburg brought the Coburg domain back to Henneberg, practically doubling his territory. He was governor of the Kingdom of Bohemia in 1313 and became one of Emperor Louis IV's most influential advisers.

From 1323 to 1330 he was guardian of the emperor's eldest son. He died at Schleusingen on 13 April 1340, and Henry VIII succeeded him.

亨讷贝格-施莱辛根伯爵贝特霍尔德七世（1272—1340），人称“智者”，1284年继位，在位五十六年，由地方伯爵升为帝国王侯。1309年国王亨利七世把帝国城市施韦因富特抵押给他，1310年7月25日又在法兰克福帝国会议上将他升为帝国王侯。

1312年，他借儿子亨利八世与勃兰登堡的尤塔联姻，使科堡领地重归亨讷贝格家族，领地实际上扩大了近一倍。他1313年出任波希米亚王国摄政，后来成为皇帝路德维希四世最有影响的顾问之一。

1323至1330年，他担任皇帝长子的监护人。1340年4月13日他卒于施莱辛根，亨利八世继位。

en:
Henry VIII of Henneberg (c. 1288 – 10 September 1347) succeeded his father Berthold VII the Wise as Count of Henneberg-Schleusingen in 1340, in whose reign the house ran short of sons. In 1312 his marriage to Jutta of Brandenburg restored the Coburg domain to Henneberg, practically doubling its territory.

But the marriage produced only surviving daughters. In 1339 his younger brother John reserved his right to inherit the county, and in 1340 Emperor Louis IV confirmed it.

Shortly before his death in 1347 Henry settled the succession. The southern New Lordship, largely Jutta's dowry, went to his widow and his three unprovided daughters, while the old northern Henneberg lands passed to John I, so the enlarged county was split again.

亨讷贝格的亨利八世（约1288—1347年9月10日）于1340年继承父亲“智者”贝特霍尔德七世，任亨讷贝格-施莱辛根伯爵，在他任内家族男嗣不足。1312年，他与勃兰登堡的尤塔结婚，使科堡领地重归亨讷贝格，领地实际上扩大了近一倍。

1347年临终前，亨利安排继承事宜：南部的“新领地”多为尤塔的嫁妆，分给遗孀和三个尚未安顿的女儿，北部古老的亨讷贝格土地则传给约翰一世，扩大后的伯国就此再度分裂。

en:
John I of Henneberg-Schleusingen (1289 – 2 May 1359) was a younger son of Berthold VII the Wise. Years in his father's retinue gave him court contacts, and in 1334 he negotiated the release of Prince Otto, captured after the battle of Viborg, though on terms so heavy that the Danes resented him.

When his brother Henry VIII died in 1347 leaving only daughters, John inherited the reduced northern part of the county, which left him weak against the bishopric of Würzburg, the old Henneberg rival. In 1348 he took the Würzburg burgraviate from Bishop Albert II as a fief, together with the hereditary marshal's office.

In 1349 he married Elisabeth of Leuchtenberg, and in 1356 Charles IV named him imperial councillor at the Nuremberg Diet. Debts and his own extravagance forced him to pawn castles and towns throughout his reign.

约翰一世（1289—1359年5月2日）是“智者”贝特霍尔德七世较年幼的儿子。他早年随侍父亲，在各地宫廷都有门路；1334年他通过谈判促成奥托王子获释，王子在维堡之战后被俘，但条件苛刻，丹麦人因此怨恨他。

1347年兄长亨利八世去世且只留下女儿后，约翰继承了缩小的北部领地，面对老对手维尔茨堡主教区时处境虚弱。1348年，他从主教阿尔布雷希特二世手中以封臣身份领回维尔茨堡城堡伯爵职，并获得世袭元帅职。

en:
Jamal al-Din Muhammad was the Nawayath Muslim sultan of Hunnur, modern Honnavar, and son of the merchant-founder Hasan Nakhuda. His fleet made him a coastal power: the king of Malabar paid him annual tribute, and in 1338 Hoysala king Vira Ballala III stationed an army at Barkur against him.

About 1340 he accepted the suzerainty of Harihara of Gersoppa. When Ibn Battuta visited in 1343, he sailed with the sultan's fleet of 52 ships that captured Sindapur; a counter-attack in 1344 then clouded the sultanate's fate.

Tradition calls him Shah Khan, or Ayasho I, the founder of the Ayasho dynasty of Hunza. He was a grandson of the earlier ruler Shah Thum, and the vizier Chosay Boto fetched him back from Afghanistan. In Hunza he married Nur Bibi, daughter of Girkis ruler Sahib Khan, whom the Hunza people had enthroned after her father's death.

Through this marriage he took power and founded the line that by tradition ruled Hunza from 874 to 1974 under the Burushaski title of Thum.

In Burusho tradition, Nur Bibi was the daughter of Sahib Khan, called Girkis, last ruler of Hunza's Girkis line. When her father was killed while hunting in Nagar, the Hunza people placed her on the throne with the title Thum.

She then married Shah Khan, a prince the vizier Chosay Boto had fetched from Afghanistan. Their marriage founded the Ayasho dynasty, which by tradition ruled Hunza from 874 to 1974.

Burkhard I (died 1061), lord of Zollern in Swabia, is the first reliably documented member of the Hohenzollern dynasty. The annals of the Reichenau monk Berthold record that in 1061 a Burchardus and a Wezil de Zolorin were killed, apparently in a feud.

The next documented Zollern was Count Frederick I, probably his son or grandson. He was the ancestor of the later Prussian kings.

en:
Frederick I, Count of Zollern, nicknamed Maute, was a powerful Swabian count and a loyal supporter of Emperor Henry V. A son or grandson of Count Burkhard I, he married Udilhild of Urach and fathered at least eight children; his eldest son succeeded him as Frederick II, while a younger son, Burkhard, founded the Zollern-Hohenberg line that lasted until 1486.

Frederick was the first advocate of Alpirsbach Abbey. Henry V sent him on a diplomatic mission to France, and he accompanied the emperor's Italian expedition of 1110–1111 to claim the imperial crown in Rome. He died before 1125.

en:
Frederick II, Count of Zollern (died 1142 or after 1145), was the eldest son of Frederick I, succeeding him around 1125. He backed Emperor Lothar III against the Hohenstaufen until Lothar's death in 1137, then after 1138 supported the Hohenstaufen king Conrad III against the Welfs.

During his rule the Zollern counts enlarged their lands and castles in southwestern Germany as far as the Rhine and upper Danube. He fell in battle, and his son became Burgrave Frederick I of Nuremberg.

en:
Frederick IV of Zollern (c. 1188–c. 1255), also numbered Frederick II as Burgrave of Nuremberg, was a son of Frederick I of Nuremberg and the younger brother of Conrad I. After his father's death around 1204 he succeeded as Burgrave of Nuremberg.

In 1218 the brothers divided their inheritance: Conrad took the Franconian lands and the Nuremberg burgraviate, while Frederick received the ancestral County of Zollern in Swabia and founded the Swabian line of the Hohenzollern. His son Frederick V succeeded him.

en:
Frederick IX of Hohenzollern, called the Old or the Black Count, was the second son of Count Frederick VIII. In 1339 he succeeded his elder brother Fritzli II and ruled as Count of Hohenzollern until his death between 1377 and 1379. In 1341 he married Adelheid of Hohenberg-Wildenberg.

In 1342 he agreed with the Zollern-Schalksburg line that the senior of the two counts should decide who inherited the original Zollern fief. He became a captain of the Lion League, an association of Swabian nobles.

In 1344 he divided the lands with his younger brother Frederick of Strasbourg and founded the Black Count line. It died out in 1412 with his son Frederick X, and the Strasbourg line inherited the county, later producing the princes of Hohenzollern.

Frederick V of Zollern succeeded his father Frederick IV as Count of Zollern around 1255 and died at Hohenzollern Castle on 24 May 1289. As reeve of Beuron Archabbey he founded Stetten Abbey in 1259, and with his wife Udilhild of Dillingen expanded it in 1267 with a crypt for the Zollern family.

His long feud with the Counts of Hohenberg ended through the mediation of King Rudolf I in 1286. The County of Zollern reached its greatest influence under him, and after his death was partitioned among his sons and lost importance. His son Frederick of Merkenberg founded the Schalksburg line, and Udilhild died as a nun at Stetten.

en:
Frederick VI of Zollern, called the Knight, succeeded his father Frederick V as Count of Zollern around 1289 and died on 4 May 1298. In the year of his succession he divided the family lands with his younger brother Frederick the Younger, who received Schalksburg and founded a cadet line.

Frederick kept the ancestral county around Hohenzollern Castle. In 1281 he married Kunigunde, daughter of Margrave Rudolf I of Baden. His son Frederick VII succeeded him.

en:
Frederick VII of Zollern was the elder son of Count Frederick VI and Kunigunde, and ruled the County of Zollern from 1298 until his death. Also in 1298 he married Euphemia, daughter of Count Albert II of Hohenberg; the match, promoted by King Rudolf I, ended the long rivalry between the Swabian houses of Zollern and Hohenberg.

He and Euphemia had two sons, Fritzli and Albert. Frederick died after 6 October 1309, and the county passed to his younger brother Frederick VIII.

en:
Frederick VIII of Zollern, called Easter Sunday (died 1333), was a count of Hohenzollern and the younger son of Count Frederick VI. When his elder brother Frederick VII died in 1309 he came to rule, jointly with his nephew Fritz I until the latter's death around 1313, and then alone.

In the factional wars he first backed Austria and later stood with Emperor Louis IV. Letters call him cheerful and kindly, yet a resolute man of war.

en:
Frederick of Hohenzollern, called the Strasbourg One, was the younger son of Count Frederick VIII of Zollern. He became a Strasbourg canon in 1333, but returned to secular life in 1342 and married Margaret of Hohenberg in 1343.

In 1344 he and his elder brother Frederick IX divided their inheritance, and Frederick founded the Strasbourg line, ancestor of the later Hohenzollern-Hechingen and Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen lines. He died after 9 March 1365, before his brother, leaving a son, Frederick XI.

en:
Dietrich von Dalwigk (died 1359) was a Corvey monk from a Waldeck ministerial family, admitted through King John of Bohemia's influence. Elected prince-abbot of Corvey in 1336, he enfeoffed Count Bernard V of Lippe with part of Schwalenberg in 1345 and in 1349 settled the Lichtenfels Castle feud with Count Otto II of Waldeck.

Emperor Charles IV confirmed Corvey's vehmic court rights in 1349, and in 1356 he allowed Höxter to raise a town wall. He died in 1359 after 23 years' rule.

en:
Gerhard II (c. 1260 – 18 October 1312 or 1313) was count of Hoya, son of Count Henry II. Destined for the church, he served as a canon at Verden and Bremen before leaving the clergy when his elder brother died in 1279. From 1281 he ruled with his father, and after 1290 with his brother Otto II.

Peaceable and on good terms with his neighbors, he encouraged trade. In 1302 the brothers received Drakenburg from their kinsman Duke Otto of Brunswick-Lüneburg. Married twice, he died childless.

en:
Gerhard III of Hoya (died 1383) ruled the County of Hoya from 1324, first jointly with his brother John after their father Otto II died. In 1345 the brothers divided the county, Gerhard taking the Lower County around Hoya and John the Upper County around Nienburg.

His long reign was spent in feuds: he fought the Hoya Feud of 1351–1359 against Bremen, and in 1370 joined Welf duke Magnus II in the Lüneburg War of Succession. He died in 1383.

zh:
霍亚的格哈德三世（1383年去世）自1324年起统治霍亚伯国：父亲奥托二世死后，他先与兄弟约翰共同执政。1345年兄弟二人瓜分伯国，格哈德取得霍亚一带的下伯国，约翰取得尼恩堡一带的上伯国。

他漫长的统治充斥着封建私战：1351—1359年与不来梅等势力展开霍亚战争，1370年又投奔韦尔夫家族的公爵马格努斯二世一方，参加吕讷堡继承战争。他于1383年去世。

en:
Henry I (died 1235) was the first documented count of Hoya, ruling from 1202. His father, a Frisian from Rüstringen, had settled at Hoya with the Bremen archbishops' support. Henry bought the county of Stumpenhusen in 1202 and adopted its name and seal, and acquired the county of Nienburg in 1215.

A Staufer partisan in the German throne conflict, he aided Archbishop Gerhard of Bremen against the Stedinger, defeating them at Hilgermissen in 1213. He was buried at Bücken and succeeded by his son Henry II.

海因里希一世（？—1235）是第一位有文献记载的霍亚伯爵，1202年起在位。他的父亲是来自吕斯特林根的弗里斯兰人，在不来梅大主教支持下定居霍亚。海因里希于1202年买下施图彭豪森伯国并改用其姓氏与印章，1215年取得尼恩堡伯国。

在德意志王位之争中他支持霍亨斯陶芬家族，并协助不来梅大主教格哈德进攻施特丁根人，1213年在希尔格米森将其击败。他葬于比肯，由儿子海因里希二世继位。

en:
Henry II, called Henry with the Axe, was count of Hoya from 1235, when he succeeded his father Henry I, until his death on 25 January 1290. Chronicles gave him his nickname for the brutal violence of his warfare.

He chiefly pressed south against the bishops of Minden and secured the new frontier with castles at Liebenau and Steyerberg. With Jutta of Ravensberg he is said to have fathered twenty-five children, at least eight of whom reached adulthood, including his successors Gerhard II and Otto II.

海因里希二世（？—1290年1月25日），绰号“持斧者”，1235年继承父亲海因里希一世成为霍亚伯爵，统治至去世。据当时编年史记载，他因作战凶狠残暴而得此绰号。

他主要向南对付明登主教，扩张领地，并在利伯瑙和施泰尔贝格修建城堡，拱卫新边界。相传他与拉文斯贝格的尤塔育有25个子女，其中至少8人长大成人，继任者格哈德二世与奥托二世都是他的儿子。

en:
Otto II (1271–1324) was count of Hoya from 1313, when he succeeded his childless elder brother Gerhard II, until his death. A younger son of Count Henry II, he married Ermengard of Holstein and had four children.

During his short reign he allied with neighboring princes, including the dukes of Brunswick-Lüneburg and the archbishopric of Bremen. He had already agreed that his sons Gerhard and John should divide the county, which they did in 1345.

奥托二世（1271—1324）是霍亚伯爵，1313年无子女的兄长格哈德二世死后继位，统治至1324年。他是海因里希二世年纪较小的儿子，娶荷尔斯泰因的埃尔门加德，育有四个子女。

他在位时间不长，与不伦瑞克-吕讷堡诸公爵、不来梅大主教区等邻邦诸侯结盟。他生前已商定由儿子格哈德和约翰瓜分伯国，两人最终于1345年分家。

en:
Gerard I van Horne (1270–1331) was a nobleman of the House of Horne, son of William II. He held several lordships, buying Herlaar in 1315. In 1302 he married Johanna of Leuven-Gaasbeek, who bore his heir William IV in 1305; after her death he married Irmgard of Cleves in 1316, by whom he had Dirk.

In 1318 he hosted the nobles mediating between the count of Holland and the duke of Brabant over the Land of Heusden. He was buried in the Carmelite church in Brussels.

赫拉德一世·范霍恩（1270—1331）是霍恩家族贵族，威廉二世·范霍恩之子。他领有数处领地，1315年购入海尔拉尔。1302年他娶勒芬-哈斯贝克的约翰娜，1305年生下继承人威廉四世；丧妻后于1316年续娶克莱沃的伊尔姆加德，生子迪尔克。

en:
Gerard II of Horne (1324–1345), son of Willem IV of Horne and Oda of Putten, was made lord of Heeze and Leende in 1342 and in 1343 succeeded his father as lord of Horne and Altena.

In 1345 he joined Count William IV of Holland's invasion of Friesland. That September he was killed with the count at the Battle of Warns, where nearly the whole invasion army was destroyed. He died unmarried, and his lordships were divided between his sister Johanna and his half-brothers.

en:
Johanna of Horne (1320–1356), daughter of Willem IV of Horne and Oda of Putten, inherited Horne, Altena and her other lordships in 1345 after her brother Gerard II fell at the Battle of Stavoren. She married Gijsbrecht III of Abcoude, who governed her lands iure uxoris.

In 1353 she granted Herstal to her eldest son Zweder, and on her death in 1356 the rest of her domains followed, though her half-siblings challenged the succession until arbitration in 1357.

Willem IV of Horne (c. 1302–1343), son of Gerard I, was lord of Horne, Altena, Weert and Heeze. He took charge of Altena in 1321, but the count of Kleve refused to invest him, favouring his half-brother Dirk; Count William III of Holland guaranteed his position in 1327.

He married Oda of Putten by 1316 and Elisabeth of Kleve-Hülchrath in 1336, with eleven children. He granted Heeze to Gerard II in 1342 and died in 1343.

en:
Willem V of Horne (c. 1337–1357) was the eldest son of Willem IV of Horne. After his half-brother Gerard II fell at Warns in 1345, his uncle Dirk of Perwez secured him the lordships of Horne, Kortessem and Weert as fifth lord of Horne, while his half-sister Johanna took the Brabant lands. Holland granted him the fief of Altena in 1347.

In 1349 he married Machteld, daughter of John IV of Arkel. He was dead by April 1357, when Altena passed to his brother Dirk Loef.

en:
Ludwig II of Mansbach (c. 1280–1343) was the forty-ninth abbot of the Imperial Abbey of Hersfeld from 1324 to his death. His rule saw the abbey's continuing decline: in 1328 he began a castle outside the town, and that November was forced by the town and convent to accept guardians and to grant the city self-rule over its crafts.

In 1332 he sold the abbey's rights at Arnstadt to the counts of Schwarzburg, and from 1336 headed the Johannesberg provostry as well. He died in Hersfeld in 1343.

en:
Ereyanga (r. 1098–1102), son of the Hoysala king Vinayaditya, was made crown prince, or yuvaraja, in 1062 and waited more than thirty years to reign. A Jain who took the title Vira Ganga, he served the Western Chalukyas as a senior commander, helping Someshvara II crush rebellions and fighting in their wars.

His own rule lasted only four years. By Echala Devi he left three sons, Ballala, Bitti Deva and Udayaditya; Bitti Deva became King Vishnuvardhana.

en:
Narasimha I (r. 1152–1173) succeeded his father Vishnuvardhana as Hoysala king. His great achievement was victory over his own overlord, the Western Chalukya king Tailapa III, a blow that paved the way to Hoysala independence. He fared less well against Bijjala II, the Kalachuri feudatory who had seized the Chalukya capital Kalyani.

His generals kept up the dynasty's Jain patronage, building the Bhandara Basadi at Shravanabelgola in 1159. His reign ended when his own son Veera Ballala II displaced him.

那罗辛哈一世（1152—1173年在位）继父亲毗湿奴伐弹那之后成为曷萨拉国王。他最大的武功是击败了自己的宗主西遮娄其国王泰拉帕三世，这一胜利为曷萨拉独立铺平了道路。但他抵挡不住夺取遮娄其都城迦罗尼的迦罗珠利封臣比贾拉二世。

他的将领延续了王朝对耆那教的护持，于1159年在什拉瓦纳贝拉戈拉建成班达拉寺。他最终被自己的儿子毗罗·巴拉拉二世推翻。

en: Nripa Kama II ruled the early Hoysala realm from about 1026 until his death in 1047. A chief of the dynasty's Malnad hill country in Karnataka, he was possibly a vassal of the Western Ganga kings and fought repeated wars against the expanding Cholas. He kept hold over several districts in the Malnad. His son Vinayaditya succeeded him.

Veera Ballala I (r. 1102–1108), eldest son of Ereyanga, succeeded as Hoysala king with his capital at Belur. A Jain, he subdued the restive Chengalva and Santhara chiefs of the Malnad, but his short reign was otherwise uneventful.

He tried more than once to throw off the overlordship of the Western Chalukyas, only to be brought to heel by the powerful Chalukya Vikramaditya VI. On his death his younger brother Bitti Deva succeeded as Vishnuvardhana.

毗罗·巴拉拉一世（1102—1108年在位）是埃雷扬加的长子，继位为曷萨拉国王，定都贝鲁尔。他信奉耆那教，在位期间平定了马尔纳德不驯服的琴加尔瓦人和桑塔拉人，此外统治短暂而平静。

他曾数次试图摆脱西遮娄其王朝的宗主权，却被强势的遮娄其国王维克拉马迪亚六世压制。他死后由幼弟比蒂·提婆继位，即毗湿奴伐弹那。

en:
Veera Ballala II (r. 1173–1220), who displaced his father Narasimha I, carried the Hoysalas to the height of their power. He defeated the Yadavas, Kalachuris and Pandyas, humbled the fading Western Chalukyas and made the Cholas of Tanjore his clients; by 1200 his conquests had made the Hoysalas the strongest power in the Deccan.

He married the Chola princess Cholamahadevi and gave his daughter Somaladevi to Kulothunga Chola III. His son Vira Narasimha II and queen Umadevi led his armies.

zh:
毗罗·巴拉拉二世（1173—1220年在位）推翻父亲那罗辛哈一世自立，把曷萨拉王朝带到国力的顶峰。他先后击败雅达瓦、迦罗珠利和潘地亚等王朝，压服日趋衰微的西遮娄其，使坦焦尔的朱罗王朝承认其宗主权；到1200年前后，曷萨拉已凭他的征服成为德干最强的势力。

他娶朱罗公主朱罗玛哈黛薇为后，又把女儿索玛拉黛薇嫁给朱罗国王库洛通加三世。他的儿子毗罗·那罗辛哈二世与王后乌玛黛薇替他统军理政。

en:
Veera Ballala III (c. 1262–1342), son of Narasimha III, was the last great king of the Hoysala dynasty, ruling from Dwarasamudra. He warred with the Yadavas of Devagiri and the Pandyas of Madurai. In 1311 Malik Kafur, general of the Delhi sultan Alauddin Khalji, sacked Dwarasamudra and forced Ballala to pay tribute; a second Delhi invasion plundered the capital around 1327.

He later built a new capital on the Tungabhadra. In 1342 he was defeated, captured and killed at Kannanur by the sultan of Madurai.

维拉·巴拉拉三世（约1262—1342）是那罗辛哈三世之子，曷萨拉王朝最后一位伟大国王，以德瓦拉萨穆德拉为都。他与德瓦吉里的雅达瓦王朝、马杜赖的潘地亚王朝交战。1311年，德里苏丹阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉的将领马利克·卡富尔洗劫德瓦拉萨穆德拉，迫使他纳贡称臣；约1327年德里军队再度劫掠都城。

此后他在栋格珀德拉河畔另建新都。1342年，他在甘纳努尔被马杜赖苏丹击败俘杀。
