en:
Vinayaditya (r. 1047–1098) was a Jain king of the Hoysala dynasty and an able feudatory of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani. From his Malnad base he brought the Kongalvas, Chengalvas, Santharas of Humcha and Kadambas of Bayalnadu under Hoysala control, and after the Western Gangas fell to Chola occupation he seized parts of Gangavadi.

He ruled South Kanara and Mysore and was a noted builder of towns, linked by marriage to Chalukya Someshvara I. His son was Ereyanga.

毗那耶阿迭多（1047—1098年在位）是曷萨拉王朝的耆那教国王，也是迦罗尼西遮娄其王朝得力的封臣。他以马尔纳德为根基，降服孔加尔瓦人、琴加尔瓦人、胡姆查的桑塔拉人和巴亚尔纳德的迦丹巴人等地方小酋长；西恒伽王朝在朱罗占领根加瓦迪后覆亡，他乘机夺取根加瓦迪的部分土地。

en:
Vira Narasimha II (r. 1220–1234) succeeded his father Veera Ballala II as Hoysala king. He pushed Hoysala power into the Tamil country: he defeated the Kadavas and the Pandyas of Madurai and levied tribute on them, and he backed his ally Rajaraja Chola III against Pandya raids.

To oversee the south he set up a second capital at Kannanur Kuppam near Srirangam, and in a later campaign he fought for the Cholas again and marched as far south as Rameswaram.

en:
Vishnuvardhana (r. 1108–1152), born Bitti Deva, took the Hoysala throne after his elder brother Veera Ballala I. Originally a Jain, he won his fame against the Cholas: near Talakadu he routed the Chola general Adiyamma, recovered lost territory and took the title Talakadugonda, endowing Jain temples.

Later, influenced by Ramanuja, he turned to Vaishnavism and adopted the name Vishnuvardhana, though his queen Shantala Devi remained Jain. His victories made the Hoysalas a true kingdom, crowned by the Chennakesava Temple at Belur and the Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu.

毗湿奴伐弹那（1108—1152年在位）原名比蒂·提婆，兄长毗罗·巴拉拉一世死后登上曷萨拉王位。他本为耆那教徒，靠对朱罗的战争成名：在塔拉卡杜附近击溃朱罗将领阿迪亚马，收复失地，获得“塔拉卡杜贡达”的称号，并向耆那教寺院广施土地。

en:
Hügechi (died 1271) was the fifth son of Kublai Khan and the first Mongol prince enfeoffed in Yunnan. On 12 September 1267 he was made Prince of Yunnan with a silver seal and sent southwest to govern Dali, Kunming and the Gold Teeth lands, appointing darughachi governors.

His rule angered Baoheding, the local commander of the thirty-seven tribes, who in 1271 poisoned him at a banquet. After a secret report by his tutor Zhang Lidao reached Kublai, the emperor sent investigators and Baoheding was executed. His son Esen-Temür later became Prince of Yunnan.

忽哥赤（？—1271年）是元世祖忽必烈第五子，也是首位受封出镇云南的蒙古宗王。1267年9月12日，他被封为云南王，获赐银印，奉命出镇大理、鄯阐（今昆明）和金齿等地，设置达鲁花赤。

en:
Hulegu (c. 1217–1265), grandson of Genghis Khan and son of Tolui and Sorghaghtani Beki, conquered much of West Asia and founded Persia's Ilkhanate. In 1252–1253 Möngke sent him west with a fifth of the empire's army.

He destroyed the Nizari Assassins in 1256, the year he was named il-khan. When the Abbasid caliph al-Musta'sim refused to surrender, Hulegu took Baghdad on 10 February 1258; a week of massacre followed, the caliph was killed, and the Abbasid caliphate ended. In 1260 his armies took Aleppo and Damascus, but news of Möngke's death drew him east with most of his troops.

The small force left behind was beaten by the Mamluks at Ain Jalut that September, stopping Mongol expansion westward. He died in February 1265 and was buried on Shahi Island in Lake Urmia, the only Ilkhan whose funeral included human sacrifice; his son Abaqa succeeded him.

zh:
旭烈兀（约1217—1265）是成吉思汗之孙，拖雷与唆鲁禾帖尼之子，征服了西亚大片土地，建立波斯伊儿汗国。1252至1253年，蒙哥派他率帝国五分之一的军队西征。

1256年他灭亡阿萨辛派，同年受封伊儿汗。阿拔斯哈里发穆斯台绥木拒不投降，旭烈兀于1258年2月10日攻占巴格达，随后屠城一周，哈里发被处死，阿拔斯哈里发国就此灭亡。1260年他的军队攻占阿勒颇和大马士革，但蒙哥的死讯促使他率主力东归。

留守的少量兵力当年9月在阿音札鲁特败于马木留克，蒙古向西的扩张就此止步。他于1265年2月去世，葬在乌尔米亚湖的沙希岛，是历代伊儿汗中唯一葬礼用活人殉葬的，其子阿八哈继位。

en:
Agnes of Austria (1281–1364) was a daughter of King Albert I of Germany and Elisabeth of Tirol. In 1296 she married Andrew III of Hungary, and with her father's backing the king put down baronial revolts. Small of stature, she wore dresses her sisters had outgrown.

Andrew's death in 1301 ended the male line of the Árpád dynasty; a contemporary, Stephen Ákos, called him its last golden twig. Agnes, a childless widow of nineteen, never remarried. She became patron of Königsfelden Monastery and lived nearby with her stepdaughter Elizabeth.

Her good name made her a sought-after mediator: in 1333 she arranged a treaty between Austria and Swiss towns, and in 1351 she settled a dispute between Duke Albert II and the Swiss Confederacy. She died at Königsfelden in 1364.

zh:
奥地利的阿格尼丝（1281—1364）是德意志国王阿尔布雷希特一世与蒂罗尔的伊丽莎白之女。1296年她嫁给匈牙利国王安德拉什三世，国王在岳父的支持下镇压了贵族叛乱。她身材矮小，常穿姐妹们不要的旧衣裙。

1301年安德拉什去世，阿尔帕德王朝的男性世系断绝；同时代的斯蒂芬·阿卡什称他是这个家族“最后一根金枝”。年仅十九岁、没有子女的寡后阿格尼丝再未改嫁。她资助柯尼希斯费尔登修道院，与继女伊丽莎白住在附近。

良好的名声使她常被请去调解：1333年她促成奥地利与瑞士城镇的和约，1351年又解决了阿尔布雷希特二世公爵与瑞士邦联的争端。她于1364年在柯尼希斯费尔登去世。

en:
Andrew of Hungary (1327–1345), Duke of Calabria, was a son of Charles I of Hungary. His family felt cheated of Naples, whose crown Charles II had left to Robert rather than to Andrew's father. In 1333 Andrew was betrothed at the age of six to Joanna, heir of Robert the Wise.

Raised in Naples, the soldierly boy never fitted the refined court, and the marriage was unhappy. When Robert died in 1343 and left the crown to Joanna alone, Andrew was kept from power. His mother Elizabeth sought papal approval for his coronation, but Pope Clement VI would crown him only as an honorary consort.

Conspirators strangled him at Aversa after a hunt on 18 September 1345. His brother Louis I of Hungary twice invaded the kingdom to avenge him.

匈牙利的安德拉什（1327—1345），卡拉布里亚公爵，是匈牙利国王查理一世之子。他的家族觉得那不勒斯被人夺走了：查理二世把王位传给罗贝托，而不是安德拉什的父亲。1333年，六岁的安德拉什与智者罗贝托的继承人乔万娜订婚。

他在那不勒斯长大，这个尚武的孩子始终融不进精致的宫廷，婚姻并不幸福。1343年罗贝托去世，把王位只留给乔万娜，安德拉什被排斥在权力之外。其母伊丽莎白为他争取教皇批准加冕，但教皇克雷芒六世只愿把他作为名义上的王夫加冕。

1345年9月18日，密谋者趁他狩猎之后在阿韦尔萨将他勒死。其兄匈牙利的拉约什一世两度入侵那不勒斯为他复仇。

en:
Andrew II (c. 1177–1235), a younger son of Béla III, held Croatia and Dalmatia under his brother Emeric before becoming king of Hungary and Croatia in 1205. His lavish grants of royal estates to his supporters weakened crown revenues.

He repeatedly fought to seize Halych and Lodomeria but was repelled. His queen Gertrude of Merania was murdered by discontented lords in 1213. He joined the Fifth Crusade in 1217–1218 but achieved little.

In 1222 he was forced to issue the Golden Bull, and in 1224 the Diploma Andreanum granted privileges to the Transylvanian Saxons. He died in 1235; his daughter by Gertrude was Saint Elizabeth of Hungary.

en:
Andrew III (c. 1265–1301), called the Venetian, was a grandson of Andrew II, born in Venice to Stephen the Posthumous and Tomasina Morosini. In 1278 a rebellious lord invited him to Hungary against Ladislaus IV, but it failed.

As the last male Árpád he was elected king after Ladislaus IV's murder in 1290. He issued the first Hungarian coronation diploma, but great baronial houses ruled their lands independently and rebelled repeatedly.

Albert of Austria and Mary of Hungary also claimed his throne; Andrew forced Albert to make peace. He died on 14 January 1301, leaving his queen Agnes of Austria, and the Árpád dynasty died with him.

en:
Béla IV (1206–1270), eldest son of Andrew II, governed Slavonia and Transylvania before succeeding as king in 1235. In 1241 the Mongols destroyed his army at Mohi and chased him to the Adriatic coast; Hungary was devastated before withdrawing in 1242.

Béla encouraged stone fortresses and fortified towns, and settled thousands of colonists on depopulated lands, earning the name second founder of Hungary. He occupied Styria in 1254 but lost it in 1260, fought civil war against his son Stephen, and died in 1270 as a Franciscan tertiary.

en:
Elizabeth the Cuman (1240–1290/1295) was queen consort of Stephen V of Hungary and regent for her son Ladislaus IV. A Cuman chieftain's daughter, traditionally held to be Khan Köten, she was betrothed to Stephen, eldest son of Béla IV, sealing an agreement that gave the Cumans asylum in return for conversion and loyalty.

When Stephen V died in 1272, she ruled Hungary as regent during Ladislaus IV's minority until 1277. Her daughters Anna and Maria married Andronikos II and Charles II of Naples.

库曼人伊丽莎白（1240—1290/1295）是匈牙利国王伊什特万五世的王后，并在儿子拉斯洛四世未成年时摄政。她是库曼酋长之女，传统说法认为其父是忽滩汗。她与贝拉四世的长子伊什特万订婚，婚约保证库曼人以皈依和效忠换取庇护。

1272年伊什特万五世去世后，她在拉斯洛四世成年前以摄政身份统治匈牙利，直至1277年。女儿安娜和玛丽亚分别嫁给拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡二世与那不勒斯国王卡洛二世。

en:
Stephen of Anjou (1332–1354), Hungarian István, was the youngest surviving son of Charles I of Hungary and Elizabeth of Poland. Styled Duke of Slavonia as a child, he took no part in governing it. In 1349 his brother Louis gave him his own household and made him Duke of Transylvania.

As his childless brother's heir, he and his mother governed during Louis's Neapolitan campaign in 1350. Late that year he married Margaret of Bavaria, daughter of Emperor Louis IV, despite Pope Clement VI's sharp opposition.

The match made him unpopular in Poland, whose nobles accepted Louis as Casimir III's heir in 1351 only on condition that Stephen be kept from office. Later given Croatia and Dalmatia, he died in 1354 returning from a campaign against Serbia; his infant son John inherited his duchy.

安茹的斯蒂芬，匈牙利语名伊什特万（1332—1354），是查理一世与波兰的伊丽莎白最小的活过童年的儿子。他幼年挂名斯拉沃尼亚公爵，却不参与治理。1349年，兄长拉约什给他自己的家政班底，同年封他为特兰西瓦尼亚公爵。

作为无子嗣兄长的继承人，他在1350年拉约什远征那不勒斯期间与母亲共同执掌国政。同年年末，他迎娶皇帝路德维希四世之女巴伐利亚的玛格丽特，教皇克雷芒六世强烈反对。

这桩婚事使他在波兰不得人心，1351年波兰贵族承认拉约什为卡齐米日三世的继承人，条件是不让他参与波兰政务。他后来受命管辖克罗地亚和达尔马提亚。1354年，他在征伐塞尔维亚的归途中去世，幼子约翰继领其地。

en:
John Hunyadi (c. 1406–1456) was Hungary's foremost commander against the Ottomans. He learned warfare on Hungary's southern frontier. Made Voivode of Transylvania in 1441, he routed Ottoman raiders in 1442 and led the Long Campaign across the Balkans in 1443–1444, before defeat at Varna in 1444. He ruled as regent of Hungary for Ladislaus V from 1446 to 1453.

In 1456 he repelled Sultan Mehmed II's assault on Belgrade, then died of plague in the camp weeks later. His son became King Matthias Corvinus.

匈雅提·亚诺什（约1406—1456）是匈牙利抗击奥斯曼人的头号统帅。他在匈牙利南部边境磨练军技。1441年他出任特兰西瓦尼亚总督，1442年击溃奥斯曼劫掠军，1443至1444年率军远征巴尔干，1444年在瓦尔纳兵败。1446至1453年，他在拉斯洛五世治下担任匈牙利摄政。

1456年，他击退苏丹穆罕默德二世对贝尔格莱德的围攻，几周后却在营地死于瘟疫。他的儿子后来成为国王马加什·科尔温。

en:
John Angelos, called Kaloiōannēs or Good John (c. 1193 – before 1250), was a Byzantine prince, the son of Emperor Isaac II Angelos and Margaret of Hungary. After the Latin sack of Constantinople in 1204 he fled with his mother to Thessalonica and around 1220 to the Hungarian court of his uncle King Andrew II, who made him governor of Syrmia.

In 1225 he took 200 silver marks from the Archbishop of Kalocsa for the Bosnian Crusade but never campaigned. He was dead by July 1250, when his wife Matilda is recorded as his widow.

约翰·安杰洛斯，人称“卡洛伊奥安尼斯”，意为“好人约翰”（约1193—1250年前卒），是拜占庭皇子，皇帝伊萨克二世·安杰洛斯与匈牙利的玛格丽特之子。1204年君士坦丁堡遭拉丁人洗劫后，他随母亲逃往塞萨洛尼基，约1220年又投奔舅父匈牙利国王安德烈二世的宫廷，受任管辖西尔米乌姆。

1225年，他收下考洛乔总主教为波斯尼亚十字军提供的200银马克，却始终没有出兵。至1250年7月他已去世，妻子玛蒂尔达在文书中被记作他的遗孀。

en:
Coloman (c. 1317–1375) was the illegitimate son of King Charles I of Hungary, born to a concubine on Csepel Island. Destined for the Church, he became bishop of Győr by papal bull in 1337, aged about twenty.

He accompanied his half-brother Louis I on the Neapolitan campaign of 1350, but was imprisoned in 1353, accused of conspiring against the king. Freed by 1359 and restored to his see, he remained bishop of Győr until his death.

en:
Charles I of Hungary, called Charles Robert (1288–1342), was the Angevin prince who put a shattered kingdom back together. Grandson of Charles II of Naples and Mary of Hungary, he landed at Split aged twelve in 1300 and was crowned in 1301 with a provisional crown.

Hungary had split into provinces under oligarchs, and most refused him. Proclaimed king in 1308, he was crowned with the Holy Crown in 1310. His victory at Rozgony in 1312 and the death of Matthew Csák in 1321 made him master of nearly the whole kingdom.

He granted office fiefs instead of perpetual estates and opened gold mines that made Hungary Europe's largest gold producer. The defeat at Posada in 1330 did not stop Wallachia from becoming independent. His son Louis the Great inherited the rebuilt kingdom.

查理一世，一称查理·罗伯特（1288—1342），是把四分五裂的王国重新拼合起来的安茹王子。他是那不勒斯的卡洛二世与匈牙利的玛丽亚之孙，1300年十二岁时在斯普利特登陆，1301年以临时王冠加冕。

当时匈牙利已分裂为寡头把持的省份，多数人拒绝承认他。1308年他被拥立为王，1310年以圣冠再次加冕。1312年罗兹戈尼之战获胜，1321年寡头马特·恰克去世，他成为几乎整个王国的主人。

他改用任职期间才有效的“官职采邑”取代永久封地，并开采金矿，使匈牙利成为欧洲最大的黄金产地。1330年他在波萨达战败，没能阻止瓦拉几亚走向独立。儿子拉约什大王继承了这个重整后的王国。

en:
Catherine of Hungary (c. 1315–1355) was a daughter of King Charles I of Hungary, probably by Maria of Bytom. In 1338 she married Henry II, Duke of Świdnica. After Henry died between 1343 and 1345, she raised their only daughter Anna at Visegrád.

In 1353 Anna married Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor, while Catherine's brother Louis I of Hungary renounced his claims to Świdnica in favour of the House of Luxembourg. Catherine died in 1355.

匈牙利的卡特琳（约1315—1355）是匈牙利国王查理一世之女，母亲可能是比托姆的玛丽亚。1338年，她嫁给希维德尼察公爵亨里克二世。亨里克于1343至1345年间去世后，她带着独女安娜在维舍格勒生活。

en:
Catherine of Hungary (c. 1256 – after 1316) was a Hungarian princess of the Árpád dynasty, the second daughter of King Stephen V and Elizabeth the Cuman. In 1268 she married the Serbian heir Stefan Dragutin as part of the peace ending their war, and she was queen of Serbia during his reign from 1276 to 1282.

Her children included Stefan Vladislav II, later lord of Syrmia, and the monk Urošica. She outlived Dragutin, who died in 1316.

zh:
匈牙利的卡塔琳（约1256—1316年后）是阿帕德王朝的匈牙利公主，国王伊什特万五世与库曼人伊丽莎白的次女。1268年，作为两国战争结束后的和议一环，她嫁给塞尔维亚王储斯特凡·德拉古廷，1276至1282年丈夫在位期间为塞尔维亚王后。

她的子女包括后来的斯雷姆领主斯特凡·弗拉迪斯拉夫二世和出家为僧的乌罗什察。她比1316年去世的德拉古廷长寿。

en:
Clemence of Austria (1262–February 1293 or 1295), daughter of King Rudolf I of Germany and Gertrude of Hohenberg, married Charles Martel of Anjou, titular King of Hungary, in 1281.

Their son Charles I won the Hungarian crown in 1308 after her death; they also had two daughters, Beatrice and Clemence, the latter the second wife of King Louis X of France. Clemence died in Naples, probably in 1293 after the birth of her youngest daughter, though 1295 is also argued.

哈布斯堡的克莱芒丝（1262—1293年2月，一说1295年）是德意志国王鲁道夫一世与霍恩贝格的格特鲁德之女。1281年，她嫁给名义上的匈牙利国王安茹的卡洛·马特罗。

两人的儿子查理一世在她死后于1308年夺得匈牙利王位，另有贝娅特丽克丝、克莱门西娅两个女儿，后者成为法兰西国王路易十世的第二任王后。克莱芒丝在那不勒斯去世，可能是在1293年幼女出生后，亦有1295年之说。

en:
Ladislaus IV (1262–1290), called the Cuman for his mother's Cuman origin, inherited the throne at nine in 1272, his father Stephen V dying while rebels held him captive. Baronial factions ruled until he came of age in 1277. Allied with Rudolf I of Germany, he helped defeat Ottokar II of Bohemia at the Marchfeld in 1278.

His defence of pagan Cumans against a papal legate earned him excommunication; he routed a Cuman invasion in 1282 and survived a Mongol raid in 1285. In his last years he could no longer control the great lords and bishops, and three Cuman assassins murdered him in 1290.

zh:
拉斯洛四世（1262—1290）因母亲的库曼血统而被称为“库曼人”。1272年其父伊什特万五世去世时他年仅9岁，且正被叛乱贵族拘押，他随后继承王位。贵族派系在他成年前把持国政，1277年他亲政。他与鲁道夫一世结盟，在1278年的马希费尔德之战中协助击败波希米亚的奥托卡二世。

他庇护信奉异教的库曼人、对抗教皇使节，因此被开除教籍；1282年击退库曼人入侵，1285年又扛过蒙古人的袭击。晚年他已无法控制最有权势的贵族与主教，1290年被三名库曼人刺杀。

en:
Louis I, called the Great (1326–1382), succeeded his father Charles I as King of Hungary and Croatia in 1342, inheriting a centralised kingdom; his mother Elizabeth of Poland long acted as co-regent. When his brother Andrew was murdered at Naples in 1345, he accused Queen Joanna, and punishing her became the aim of his foreign policy: he invaded twice between 1347 and 1350, but the papacy never recognised his claim and he withdrew in 1351.

In 1358 he forced Venice to give up the Dalmatian towns. Under a treaty of 1338 he inherited Poland from his maternal uncle Casimir III in 1370.

With no son, he issued the Privilege of Koszyce in 1374 to win acceptance for his daughters as heirs. Hungarian historians long counted him their most powerful king.

zh:
拉约什一世，即拉约什大王（1326—1382），1342年继承父亲查理一世的匈牙利和克罗地亚王位，接手一个中央集权的王国，其母波兰的伊丽莎白长期形同共同摄政。1345年弟弟安德拉什在那不勒斯遇害，他指控乔万娜女王，惩罚她成了对外政策的主轴：1347至1350年间他两度出兵，但教廷始终不承认他的主张，1351年他撤军。

1358年他迫使威尼斯放弃达尔马提亚诸城镇。根据1338年的条约，他于1370年从舅父卡齐米日三世手中继承波兰。

因膝下无子，他在1374年颁布科希策特权，为女儿们的继承权争取承认。匈牙利史家长期视他为本国最强大的国王。

en:
Maria of Bytom (before 1295–1317) was queen of Hungary as the wife of Charles I Robert and the only daughter of Casimir, Piast duke of Bytom, by Helena. In 1306 she married Charles and was crowned at Székesfehérvár.

The marriage, probably promoted by Władysław I the Elbow-high, drew Hungary and the Silesian Piasts together against Bohemia. The marriage is now considered childless, though older historians gave her two daughters. She died on 15 December 1317.

zh:
比托姆的玛丽亚（1295年前—1317）是匈牙利国王查理一世·罗贝尔的王后，皮亚斯特家族比托姆公爵卡齐米日与海莱娜的独女。1306年她嫁给查理，并在塞克什白堡加冕。

这桩联姻可能由“矮子”瓦迪斯瓦夫一世促成，使匈牙利与西里西亚皮亚斯特系联手对抗波希米亚。现代研究认为二人没有子女，旧说则称她生有两女。1317年12月15日她去世。

en:
Maria Laskarina (c. 1206–1270) was queen consort of Hungary as the wife of Béla IV, and a daughter of Theodore I Laskaris, founder of the Nicaean Empire. In 1218 she married Prince Béla, son of Andrew II, converting from Orthodoxy to Catholicism to seal the Nicaean-Hungarian alliance. She became queen on Béla's accession in 1235.

During the Mongol invasion she fled with her children, and in the 1260s she supported Béla against their son Stephen. She died on 24 June 1270, weeks after her husband.

en:
Elizabeth of Hungary (1207–1231) was the daughter of King Andrew II and Gertrude of Merania, sent as a child to the Thuringian court and married in 1221 to Louis IV, Landgrave of Thuringia. In 1226, while Louis attended an imperial diet, she managed affairs and distributed alms during a famine.

Louis died on crusade in 1227, leaving her widowed at twenty; she founded a hospital at Marburg and served the sick herself. She died in 1231 aged twenty-four, and Gregory IX canonised her in 1235 after reports of healings at her grave. She is patroness of the Third Order of Saint Francis.

en:
Stephen V (1239–1272) was the eldest son of Béla IV, married to Elizabeth, daughter of a Cuman chieftain. He governed Transylvania from 1257 and Styria from 1258.

Styrian nobles rebelled with Ottokar II's support, and Ottokar routed Stephen and his father at Kressenbrunn in 1260. He forced Béla to cede lands east of the Danube as junior king in 1262 and fought him until peace in 1266.

Stephen succeeded to the throne in 1270 and repelled Ottokar's invasion of Hungary in 1271. After his son Ladislaus was seized by rebels, he died on 6 August 1272.

Stephen succeeded to the throne in 1270 and repelled Ottokar's invasion of [GetCountry('HUN').GetName] in 1271. After his son Ladislaus was seized by rebels, he died on 6 August 1272.
zh:
伊什特万五世（1239—1272）是贝拉四世的长子，娶库曼人酋长之女伊丽莎白为妻。他1257年起治理特兰西瓦尼亚，1258年起治理施蒂利亚。

施蒂利亚贵族在奥托卡二世支持下反叛，1260年奥托卡在克雷森布伦击败伊什特万父子的军队。1262年他迫使贝拉割让多瑙河以东土地，受封小国王，并与父亲交战至1266年议和。

1270年他继位为王，1271年击退奥托卡二世对匈牙利的入侵。儿子拉斯洛被叛乱贵族劫持后不久，他于1272年8月6日去世。

en:
Tomasina Morosini (c. 1250–c. 1297) was a Venetian noblewoman of the powerful Morosini family. Around 1264 she married Stephen the Posthumous, an exiled Árpád prince claiming the Hungarian throne, bringing him Venetian wealth and backing. Their only son, the future Andrew III, was born around 1265. Stephen died in 1271, having named Tomasina's relatives as Andrew's guardians.

She remained in Venice, but when Andrew became King of Hungary she followed him in 1292 and ruled as Duchess of Slavonia. She died in 1296 or early 1297, amid rumours of poison; her son was the last Árpád king.

en:
Yolanda of Courtenay (c. 1197–1233) was Queen of Hungary as the second wife of Andrew II. Daughter of Peter II of Courtenay, Latin Emperor of Constantinople, and Yolanda of Flanders, she was a niece of Emperor Henry I, who arranged the marriage. In February 1215 she was crowned at Székesfehérvár.

After Henry I died in 1216 her father, not Andrew II, was chosen Latin emperor. As queen she granted land to citizens, and around 1230 she helped arrange her niece Matilda's marriage to John Angelos. She kept good relations with her stepchildren, and her daughter Yolanda married James I of Aragon.

库尔特奈的约兰德（约1197—1233）是匈牙利国王安德烈二世的第二任王后。她是君士坦丁堡拉丁皇帝皮埃尔二世·德·库尔特奈与佛兰德的约兰德之女、拉丁皇帝亨利一世的外甥女，这桩婚事正是由亨利一世安排。1215年2月，她在塞克什白堡加冕为后。

en:
Dietrich (died after 1341) was a Premonstratensian canon and former provost of Havelberg Cathedral who became its bishop in 1324 or 1325. In 1327 he issued an edict against those who plundered or burned church property. He consecrated the cathedral's high altar in 1330 and enlarged its library.

In 1336 and 1338 the pope entrusted him with lifting the interdict on Halle after the murder of Archbishop Burchard III of Magdeburg. He is last attested in 1341.

狄奥多里克（1341年后卒）是普雷蒙特雷修会教士，曾任座堂教长，1324或1325年出任哈弗尔贝格主教。1327年，他颁布法令惩处劫掠、焚毁教会财物者。1330年，他为座堂大祭坛祝圣，并扩充座堂藏书。

Muzaffar al-Din Afrasiab II became ruler of the Hazaraspid dynasty of Great Lorestan about 1340, succeeding his father Yusuf Shah II at Idhaj in the Zagros.

During his reign the Ilkhanate collapsed, so that the atabegs of Lorestan no longer answered to a Mongol overlord, while the Muzaffarids of Fars under Mubariz al-Din Muhammad rose as a new danger. Afrasiab was succeeded by his son Nawr-al-Ward.

Rukn al-Din Yusuf Shah II was the Hazaraspid atabeg of Great Lorestan, ruling from his capital Idhaj, now Izeh, in the Zagros from about 1330 to 1339 or 1340. He succeeded his father Nusrat al-Din Ahmad and was likewise remembered as a benevolent ruler.

He died at Shushtar aged about forty-three and was followed by his son Muzaffar al-Din Afrasiab II as the Ilkhanate began to break apart.

en:
Muhammad ibn Iyas (1448–c.1523) was an Egyptian historian of the late Mamluk age, born and educated in Cairo and trained in Hanafi law. He belonged to a Mamluk military family.

His major work, Bada'i al-zuhur fi waqa'i al-duhur, is a universal history of Egypt that he carried down to 1522. As an eyewitness to the Ottoman invasion of 1517 and the fall of the Mamluk sultanate, he recorded the conquest in dated entries, making his chronicle a principal source for Egypt's transition from Mamluk to Ottoman rule.

穆罕默德·伊本·伊亚斯（1448—约1523）是马穆鲁克晚期的埃及史家，生于开罗并在当地求学，修习哈乃斐法。他出身马穆鲁克军人家族。

他的主要著作《百花奇观：历代大事记》是一部埃及通史，记事一直延续到1522年。他亲身经历了1517年奥斯曼入侵和马穆鲁克苏丹国覆灭，在书中以系日笔法记录这场征服，使这部编年史成为了解埃及从马穆鲁克转入奥斯曼统治的首要史料。

en:
Ibn Khaldun (1332–1406) was an Arab historian and thinker, born in Tunis. For two decades he moved between the courts of North Africa, at times as chief minister, at times in prison. His skill with Berber tribes made him useful to every ruler, but in 1375 he tired of changing sides and withdrew to western Algeria, where a tribe sheltered him for three years.

There he wrote the Muqaddimah, introduction to his universal history Kitab al-Ibar. It describes how group solidarity (asabiyya) wins a dynasty its throne, and why the conquerors of a refined civilization are in turn softened and overthrown.

From 1382 he was in Cairo, where Sultan Barquq made him Maliki grand qadi in 1384, an office he held six times. At the siege of Damascus he was lowered over the wall by ropes to negotiate with Timur. He died in Cairo in 1406.

伊本·赫勒敦（1332—1406）是阿拉伯史学家与思想家，生于突尼斯。此后二十年他辗转于北非各地宫廷，时而任首相，时而入狱。他善于与柏柏尔部落打交道，因此各国君主都用他；1375年他厌倦了改换门庭，退居阿尔及利亚西部，部落庇护了他三年。

他在那里写成《历史绪论》，即其通史《殷鉴书》的导言。书中讲群体凝聚力（阿萨比亚）如何让一个王朝夺得王位，也讲征服了精致文明的人如何被同化而又被推翻。

1382年起他在开罗，1384年苏丹巴尔库克任命他为马立克派大法官，此职他先后六次出任。大马士革被围时，他被人用绳子从城墙上缒下去与帖木儿谈判。1406年他在开罗去世。

en:
Ichil was a 13th-century Mongol amir of the Barlas tribe in the Chagatai Khanate and an ancestor of Timur, succeeding his father Qarachar. Timurid works expanded on his career.

The Shajarat al-atrak makes him generalissimo serving the Chagatai khans Alghu and Mubarak Shah, while Yazdi's Zafarnama says he joined Prince Teguder after the enthronement of Khan Baraq. A 1317 manuscript of Rashid al-Din's Jami' al-tawarikh also calls him a great amir under the Ilkhan Abaqa, though scholars suspect that passage may be a later insertion.

亦连吉儿是13世纪察合台汗国巴鲁剌思部的蒙古埃米尔，帖木儿的先祖，继其父哈剌察儿任职。帖木儿朝著作对他的事迹多有铺陈。

《突厥世系》称他担任全军统帅，臣事察合台汗阿鲁忽和木八剌沙；耶兹德《帖木儿武功记》则说他在八剌汗即位典礼后投奔宗王特古迭儿。1317年的拉施特丁《史集》抄本也称他是伊儿汗阿八哈帐下的大埃米尔，但有学者怀疑这段文字为后人添入。

en:
Rao Sonag, also called Sonangji, was a Rathore Rajput chief and the founder of Idar State. A younger son of Rao Sheoji, he first held the fief of Sametra from the Chaulukya ruler.

In 1257 he and his brother Rao Asthan seized Idar, overthrowing the Koli chieftain Samalio Sora by a ruse: Rathore warriors hidden in carriages struck him down at a feast. As Idar's first Rao he founded the Idariya Rathore line and died in 1275.

zh:
拉奥·索纳格，又称索南吉，是罗怙罗族拉杰普特首领，伊德尔土邦的建立者。他是拉奥·谢奥吉较年幼的儿子之一，最初从遮娄其统治者那里受封萨梅特拉采邑。

1257年，他与兄弟拉奥·阿斯唐合力攻取伊德尔，以计推翻科利酋长萨马利奥·索拉：罗怙罗武士藏在马车里，在宴会上将其击杀。索纳格成为第一代伊德尔拉奥，开创“伊达里亚·罗怙罗”世系，于1275年去世。

en:
Jamal ad-Din I was Muslim governor of Ifat in the mid-fourteenth century, son of Nahwi ibn Mansur Walashma and brother of Sultans Haqq ad-Din I and Sabr ad-Din I. He owed his post to the Ethiopian emperor: in 1332, after Sabr ad-Din's revolt failed, Amda Seyon I released him from prison and made him governor.

The royal chronicle claims he joined Salih's Muslim alliance, defeated at the Battle of Das, and later refused to hand over Christian converts to Islam, though he did produce his brother's son.

Amda Seyon ravaged Ifat and replaced him with his brother Nasr ad-Din. The historian Taddesse Tamrat doubts Jamal ever rebelled, holding that he was imprisoned again on the pretext of the converts.

zh:
贾迈勒丁一世是14世纪中叶伊法特的穆斯林统治者，纳赫维·伊本·曼苏尔·瓦拉什马之子，哈格丁一世、萨布尔丁一世的兄弟。他的位置得自埃塞俄比亚皇帝：1332年萨布尔丁叛乱失败后，安达·塞永一世将他从狱中释放，任命为伊法特统治者。

皇家编年史称，他加入萨利赫的穆斯林联盟，在达斯之战中被击败，后来又拒绝交出皈依伊斯兰教的基督徒，只交出了兄弟的儿子。

安达·塞永蹂躏伊法特，由其兄弟纳斯尔丁接替他。历史学家塔德塞·塔姆拉特则认为贾迈勒丁并未走到叛乱那一步，而是以改宗者为借口被再次囚禁。

en:
Nahwi ibn Mansur was a prince of the Walashma dynasty of the Muslim Sultanate of Ifat, son of Mansur and grandson of its founder Umar ibn Dunya-hawz; the chronicle History of the Walashma shows the laqab Nahwi borne by several Walashma princes.

After Emperor Amda Seyon's Ethiopian campaigns against Ifat began in 1328, four of Nahwi's sons ruled in turn: Haqq ad-Din I, killed fighting the emperor, Sabr ad-Din I, Jamal ad-Din I and Nasr ad-Din.

纳赫维·伊本·曼苏尔是穆斯林伊法特苏丹国瓦拉什马王朝的王公，曼苏尔之子、开国君主乌马尔·伊本·敦亚豪兹之孙；编年史《瓦拉什马史》记载，“纳赫维”是该王朝多位王公共用的称号。

1328年埃塞俄比亚皇帝阿姆达·塞永对伊法特开战后，他的四个儿子相继在位：与皇帝作战被杀的哈格丁一世，以及萨布尔丁一世、贾迈勒丁一世和纳斯尔丁。

en:
Sabr ad-Din I was sultan of the Muslim Sultanate of Ifat in the early fourteenth century, a son of Nahwi ibn Mansur Walashma and younger brother of Sultan Haqq ad-Din I. By then Amda Seyon I of Ethiopia had been absorbing the Muslim borderlands and their inland trade. Early in 1332 he rallied the Muslims of the Horn against him, attacking garrisons, burning churches, enslaving people and forcing conversions.

Amda Seyon defeated him in battle and then overran Dawaro and Bale. Captured and imprisoned, he was replaced as ruler of Ifat by his brother Jamal ad-Din I. The campaign ended the independence of Ifat and its neighbouring Muslim states.

zh:
萨布尔丁一世是14世纪初穆斯林伊法特苏丹国的苏丹，纳赫维·伊本·曼苏尔·瓦拉什马之子、苏丹哈格丁一世之弟。其时埃塞俄比亚的安达·塞永一世正不断吞并穆斯林边地和这些地方的内陆贸易。1332年初，他召集非洲之角的穆斯林起兵对抗，进攻驻军、焚毁教堂、奴役民众、强迫改宗。

安达·塞永将其击败，继而攻陷达瓦罗和巴莱。他被俘下狱后，其弟贾迈勒丁一世被改立为伊法特之主。这场战事终结了伊法特及邻近穆斯林政权的独立。

en:
Bernard II Jordan (c. 1181–1228) was lord of L'Isle-Jourdain in Gascony from 1205. He was the eldest son of Jourdain III and Esclarmonde of Foix, called the Great Esclarmonde, who received the Cathar consolamentum in 1204 and became a central figure of Catharism.

He married Indie, an illegitimate daughter of Count Raymond V of Toulouse, and his rule spanned most of the Albigensian Crusade. On his death in 1228 his sons Bernard III and Jourdain IV succeeded him in turn; another son, Bertrand, later became bishop of Toulouse.

贝尔纳二世·茹尔丹（约1181—1228）自1205年起任加斯科涅的利勒茹尔丹领主。他是茹尔丹三世与富瓦的埃斯克拉蒙德——人称“大埃斯克拉蒙德”——的长子，其母于1204年接受卡特里派的慰藉礼，成为卡特里派的核心人物。

贝尔纳娶图卢兹伯爵雷蒙五世的私生女安迪为妻，统治岁月大半处于阿尔比十字军时期。他于1228年去世后，儿子贝尔纳三世、茹尔丹四世相继继位，另一子贝尔特朗后来成为图卢兹主教。

en:
Bernard IV Jordan (died 1340) was Lord of L'Isle-Jourdain in Gascony. In 1291 he married Marguerite de Foix, daughter of Count Roger-Bernard III, and kept up the alliance. He succeeded his father Jordan V in 1303 or 1304 and served Philip IV of France as seneschal of Languedoc until 1309.

In 1319 Pope John XXII wrote complaining of the Ghibelline advance in Lombardy. Between 1328 and 1331 he planned to join Philip VI on a crusade against Granada, though the expedition never set out. His eldest son Bertrand succeeded him.

贝尔纳四世·茹尔丹（1340年卒）是加斯科涅的利勒茹尔丹领主。1291年，他娶富瓦伯爵罗歇-贝尔纳三世之女玛格丽特·德·富瓦，此后一直维系着这一联盟。1303或1304年，他继承父亲茹尔丹五世之位，并在1309年之前为法王腓力四世出任朗格多克司法总管。

1319年，教皇约翰二十二世写信向他抱怨吉伯林派在伦巴第的得势。1328至1331年间，他计划随腓力六世远征格拉纳达，却终未成行。他死后由长子贝尔特朗继位。

en:
Bertrand I (died c. 1349) was the first Count of L'Isle-Jourdain in Gascony. In 1340 Philip VI of France raised his lordship to a county, and in 1344 named him the king's lieutenant and commander-in-chief in Guyenne.

He was captured at the Battle of Auberoche on 21 October 1345 by the Earl of Derby's Anglo-Gascon force. He married Isabelle de Lévis in 1328, was last attested on 26 June 1348, and was succeeded by his son Jean Jourdain I.

贝尔特朗一世（约1349年卒）是加斯科涅利勒茹尔丹的第一代伯爵。1340年，法王腓力六世将其领地升格为伯国；1344年，又任命他为国王在吉耶讷的副将兼最高指挥官。

1345年，他于10月21日的欧贝罗什之战中被德比伯爵麾下的英加联军俘虏。他于1328年娶伊莎贝尔·德·勒维，1348年6月26日最后一次见于记载，死后由子让·茹尔丹一世继位。

en:
Jordan III (c. 1150–1200) was Lord of L'Isle-Jourdain, succeeding his father Jordan II in 1196. In 1175 he married Esclarmonde of Foix, daughter of Count Roger-Bernard I of Foix; the marriage produced six children, among them his heir Bernard Jordan.

He warred with Bernard of Comminges until the count of Toulouse made them lay down arms at Verdun-sur-Garonne. He was dead by October 1200, when his widow turned to Catharism and became a leading Perfect.

en:
Jordan IV (c. 1220–1288) was Lord of L'Isle-Jourdain in Gascony, son of Bernard II and Indie of Toulouse. Around 1260 he joined a troubadour debate, a torneyamen, with Guiraut Riquier and others. A crusader in the Guelph wars of Italy, he took knights and crossbowmen to Charles of Anjou in 1266 and was enfeoffed in Calabria.

He soon returned to Gascony, but Charles threatened to confiscate his fiefs unless he returned. He lingered until 1282, when he returned with fresh soldiers. In 1285 he joined Philip III's Aragonese Crusade.

en:
Bagrat I, called the Minor (died 1372) of the Bagrationi dynasty, succeeded his father Michael as king of Imereti in 1329 while still a child. Rival noble factions carved up the provinces, and he could do little from his capital Kutaisi.

In 1330 his relative George V the Brilliant of Georgia crossed the Likhi Range, annexed Imereti and reunited the Georgian kingdom; Bagrat was left as eristavi (duke) of Imereti. In 1358 he married Natela, daughter of Qvarqvare I Jaqeli of Samtskhe, and fathered three kings, Alexander, George and Constantine.

巴格拉特一世绰号“年幼者”（？—1372），是巴格拉季昂王朝成员，1329年父亲米哈埃里去世后继任伊梅雷蒂国王，当时尚是孩童。贵族派系瓜分各省，他困守库塔伊西而无所作为。

1330年，他的亲戚、格鲁吉亚国王“辉煌者”吉奥尔基五世越过苏拉姆山脉征服伊梅雷蒂，重新统一格鲁吉亚王国；巴格拉特被降为伊梅雷蒂公爵（埃里斯塔维）。1358年他娶萨姆茨赫王公克瓦克瓦雷一世·贾克利之女纳特拉为妻，生下后来相继称王的亚历山大、吉奥尔基和君士坦丁。

en:
Constantine I (died 1327) of the Bagrationi dynasty ruled Imereti, or Western Georgia, as king from 1293, when he succeeded his father David VI Narin. His younger brother Michael disputed the crown and seized the northern provinces, and the brothers' civil war lasted until Constantine's death.

The Dadiani, Sharvashidze and Gurieli princes exploited the chaos to make their lands virtually independent principalities. He died in 1327 without an heir, and Michael took the throne.

君士坦丁一世（？—1327年）出身巴格拉季昂王朝，1293年继承父亲大卫六世·纳林的王位，成为伊梅雷蒂（西格鲁吉亚）国王。他的弟弟米哈埃里争夺王位，占据北方省份，兄弟内战一直持续到他去世。

达迪亚尼、沙尔瓦希泽和古里耶利等王公趁机作乱，使自己的领地成为近乎独立的公国。他于1327年去世，无子嗣，王位由米哈埃里继承。

en:
Michael I (died 1329) of the Bagrationi dynasty was a younger son of David VI Narin of Imereti. When his brother Constantine I took the throne in 1293, Michael rebelled and held the northern provinces through nearly thirty-five years of civil war, while western nobles won their independence.

He reached the throne only in 1327, after the childless Constantine died. As king he failed to subdue the Dadiani, Gurieli and other princes, and died in 1329, leaving his young son Bagrat I as heir.

en:
Alidosio Alidosi was an Italian nobleman of the Alidosi family of Imola. From 1278 to 1288 he governed the city as prefect and captain of the people. In 1290 he again became captain of the people at Imola with his brother.

In 1291 he commanded nearby Forlì, but a popular rising in 1292 drove the Alidosi out of Imola. He held the captaincy for the last time in 1302 and is last recorded alive in 1311.

en:
Azzo Alidosi (died 1372), a son of Roberto Alidosi, was an Italian condottiero who succeeded his father as papal vicar and lord of Imola in 1362. Serving Cardinal Gil de Albornoz, he entered Bologna for the pope in 1360 and then took possession of Fermo, ceded in exchange for Bologna.

His rule was troubled: in 1363 a revolt led by his brother Bertrando ended with both brothers carried to Bologna by papal forces, and he was jailed there again in 1366. He married Rengarda Manfredi of Faenza and died in 1372.

阿佐·阿利多西（？—1372）是罗伯托·阿利多西之子，意大利佣兵首领，1362年父亲死后成为伊莫拉的教廷代牧兼领主。他在枢机主教吉尔·德·阿尔沃诺斯麾下效力，1360年代表教皇进入博洛尼亚，随后接管费尔莫，该城曾被用来换回博洛尼亚。

en:
Bertrando Alidosi (died 1391), son of Roberto Alidosi, was an Italian condottiero who ruled Imola as papal vicar from 1372 until his death. Pope Urban V had associated him with his brother Azzo, whom he succeeded, and in 1365 he received several lordships.

Like Azzo he was twice imprisoned at Bologna by papal forces in 1366, and in 1371 a revolt drove him to Avignon, where Pope Gregory XI sheltered him. He died at Imola in 1391, succeeded by his son Luigi, called Ludovico, the last Alidosi lord of the city.

贝特朗多·阿利多西（？—1391）是罗伯托·阿利多西之子，意大利佣兵首领。教皇乌尔班五世命他协助兄长阿佐共同执政，1372年阿佐死后，他继任伊莫拉的教廷代牧兼领主，直至去世。1365年，他受封数处领地。

1366年他与阿佐两度被教廷军队囚禁于博洛尼亚；1371年又因叛乱被迫逃往阿维尼翁，受到教皇格里高利十一世庇护。1391年他死于伊莫拉，其子路易（卢多维科）继位，是阿利多西家族在伊莫拉的最后一位领主。

en:
Carlo Alidosi (died 1354) was a son of Lippo II Alidosi, lord of Imola, and became bishop of his native city while still a cathedral canon, appointed by Pope Clement VI.

In 1346 he held Imola's first diocesan synod, and he had the church of Sant'Agostino built and worked to recover Church estates seized in the wars. Shortly before his death in 1354, Cardinal Gil de Albornoz asked him to publish the excommunication of the lords of Forlì and Faenza.

en:
Cianghella della Tosa (c. 1290–1339) was a Florentine noblewoman, daughter of Arrigo della Tosa. She became the second wife of Lippo II Alidosi, who seized Imola in 1334 and became its papal vicar in 1336.

Reputedly proud and quarrelsome, she separated from him and returned to Florence, where she was said to live scandalously. Dante's ancestor Cacciaguida names her in canto fifteen of Paradiso as a byword for the city's later corruption. She died in Florence on 19 March 1339.

Lippo I Alidosi was de facto lord of Imola from 1278 to 1288, ruling as captain of the people with the title Defensor Pupuli Imole et Capitaneus Civitatis Imole.

The papal inquisitor of Romagna imprisoned him together with his nephew Lippo II Alidosi. In 1317 he plotted to reconquer Imola and make himself master of the city again, but he died shortly afterwards.

en:
Lippo II Alidosi (died 1350), also called Litto, was the first Alidosi lord of Imola. A son of Alidosio Alidosi, he fought the Este in 1333 while they warred with the Church, was captured, and later released.

When Bologna expelled its papal legate in 1334, governments fell across the region and Lippo seized power in Imola. He served the new free commune of Bologna as podestà, and Pope Benedict XII named him papal vicar of Imola in 1336. He joined the 1340 league formed to check the Visconti and ruled Imola until his death.

İshak Bey was the last bey of the İnançid principality of Lâdik around Denizli, succeeding his father Murad Arslan Bey, who died before 1362. A patron of learning like his father, he built a madrasa in Denizli that still bore his name in the sixteenth century.

Around 1368 his small beylik, hard pressed by the Germiyan dynasty, accepted Germiyan overlordship. He was still alive in 1391, when he sold part of his estates to the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I during the latter's campaign at Denizli.

伊沙克贝伊是以代尼兹利为中心的伊南奇（拉迪克）侯国末代贝伊，在1362年前继父亲穆拉德·阿尔斯兰贝伊而立。他和父亲一样扶持学术，在代尼兹利修建了以自己名字命名的经学院，该建筑到16世纪仍然存在。

Murad Arslan Bey was ruler of the İnançid beylik of Lâdik, the Turkmen principality centered on Denizli in southwestern Anatolia. Succeeding his father İnanç Mehmed Bey in 1336, he kept his house's close ties with neighbouring rulers such as the Germiyan and Aydın beys.

A patron of learning, he promoted scholarly work and encouraged the writing of books in Turkish. He died before 1362 and was succeeded by his son İshak Bey, under whom the beylik accepted Germiyan rule around 1368.

Ghiyath al-Din Kai-Khusrau, son of Sharaf al-Din Mahmud Shah, the Injuid governor of Fars for the Ilkhans, was his father's deputy in Shiraz. In 1327 he joined the Muzaffarid ruler Mubariz al-Din Muhammad to drive Haji Shah from Yazd. After Abu Sa'id's death in 1335 he expelled the replacement governor and ruled Fars as an independent amir.

When his elder brother Mas'ud Shah entered Shiraz in 1338, Kai-Khusrau refused him submission, was defeated in the ensuing war, and died in his brother's prison.

吉亚斯丁·凯霍斯鲁是伊儿汗国法尔斯总督、因珠人沙拉夫·丁·马哈茂德·沙阿之子，代父镇守设拉子。1327年他与穆扎法尔王朝的穆巴里兹·丁·穆罕默德联手，把哈吉沙赶出亚兹德。1335年伊儿汗不赛因死后，他驱逐伊儿汗国派来接替的总督，以独立埃米尔身份统治法尔斯。

1338年，长兄马苏德沙进入设拉子，凯霍斯鲁拒绝臣服，战败后死在兄长的狱中。

en:
Jalal al-Din Mas'ud Shah was a son of Sharaf al-Din Mahmud Shah. After his father was executed by the Ilkhan Arpa Ke'un in 1335, he fled to the Jalayirid Hasan Buzurg; when Arpa was later captured by rebels, Mas'ud Shah had him killed.

He served as vizier to the Jalayirid puppet Ilkhan Muhammad Khan, then contested Shiraz with his brother Kai-Khusrau until the latter died in 1338/39. Driven out by the Chobanids, he allied with Yagi Basti, who murdered him in 1342.

贾拉勒丁·马苏德沙阿是谢拉夫丁·马哈茂德沙阿之子。1335年父亲被伊儿汗阿儿巴处死之后，他投奔札剌亦儿部的谢赫·大哈散；后来阿儿巴被叛军俘获，马苏德沙阿将其处死。

他曾任札剌亦儿人拥立的傀儡伊儿汗麻合马的维齐尔，随后在设拉子与兄弟凯霍斯鲁争夺统治权，直到后者于1338/39年去世。他被楚邦王朝逐出后与亚吉·巴斯提结盟，却于1342年被后者杀害。

en:
Abu Ishaq Inju (1321–1357), born Jamal al-Din, was the last Injuid ruler and the youngest son of Sharaf al-Din Mahmud Shah. In March 1343 he seized Shiraz from the Chobanid Yagi Basti and for about twelve years ruled Fars, Isfahan and Luristan from Shiraz.

His repeated wars against the Muzaffarids ended when Mubariz al-Din Muhammad took Shiraz in 1356 and captured him in Isfahan in 1357; Abu Ishaq was sent back to Shiraz and executed.

阿布·伊沙克·因朱（1321—1357），原名贾马勒丁，是因朱王朝末代统治者，谢拉夫丁·马哈茂德沙阿的幼子。1343年3月他从楚邦王朝的亚吉·巴斯提手中夺取设拉子，以设拉子为中心统治法尔斯、伊斯法罕和洛雷斯坦约十二年。

他连年与穆扎法尔王朝交战，1356年穆巴里兹·丁·穆罕默德攻占设拉子，1357年又在伊斯法罕俘获他；阿布·伊沙克被押回设拉子处死。

en:
Sharaf al-Din Mahmud Shah was the founder of the Injuid dynasty of Fars. Around 1304 the Ilkhan Öljeitü sent him to Shiraz to administer the royal estates known as inju; by 1325 he held nearly absolute power in Fars and was named its governor.

His power alarmed Ilkhan Abu Sa'id, who dismissed him and, after a failed revolt, imprisoned him at Tabriz. After Abu Sa'id died in 1335, Arpa Khan had him executed, and his sons then fought each other over Shiraz.

沙拉夫·丁·马哈茂德·沙阿是法尔斯因朱王朝的开创者。约1304年，伊儿汗完者都派他前往设拉子，管理名为“因朱”的汗室私产；到1325年，他已在法尔斯几乎独揽大权，并被任命为当地长官。

他的坐大令伊儿汗不赛因不安，遂将他罢免；他起兵反抗失败后被囚于大不里士。1335年不赛因死后，阿儿巴汗继位并下令处死沙拉夫·丁，他的儿子们随后为争夺设拉子彼此攻杀。

Kan Ekʼ, or Ajaw Kan Ekʼ, was the name borne by every Itza Maya king at the island capital of Nojpetén in Lake Petén Itzá; in Itza it meant serpent star and joined the royal maternal and paternal lineage names.

The title is attested in Maya inscriptions from the 8th century and was still held by the last independent Itza king, captured when the Spanish took Nojpetén in 1697.

Jakob Fugger the Elder (1398–1469) was an Augsburg merchant, master weaver and town councillor who founded a branch of the Fugger trading family. His father Hans had moved to Augsburg in 1367 and built a fortune in weaving and textiles.

After Hans died in 1408, his mother Elisabeth continued the business, assisted by her sons. The family prospered in the following decades.

He separated from the family business in 1454 and by 1461 ranked among Augsburg's twelve richest citizens. His son Jakob the Rich later expanded the firm across Europe.

老雅各布·富格尔（1398—1469）是奥格斯堡商人、织工师傅和市议员，创立了富格尔商人家族的一个支系。他的父亲汉斯于1367年迁到奥格斯堡，靠织造和纺织品贸易积累财富。

汉斯于1408年去世后，母亲伊丽莎白继续经营生意，儿子们从旁协助。此后几十年间家族日渐兴旺。

1454年他从家族生意中分出独立经营，到1461年已跻身奥格斯堡十二位最富有的市民之列。他的儿子“富翁”雅各布后来将商号扩展到欧洲各地。

Jacobus Arminius (1560–1609), born Jakob Hermanszoon at Oudewater, was a Dutch Reformed minister and theologian. His father died when he was young, and his mother was killed in the Spanish massacre at Oudewater in 1575. He studied at Leiden, where he became a professor of theology in 1603.

Tasked with defending Calvinist predestination against its critics, he came instead to teach a grace sufficient for all who believed, and his disputes split the Dutch Reformed Church. He died at Leiden in 1609, a year before his followers issued the Remonstrance.

雅各布斯·阿民念（1560—1609），原名雅各布·赫尔曼松，生于奥德瓦特，是荷兰归正会的牧师与神学家。他幼年丧父，母亲在1575年西班牙军队对奥德瓦特的屠杀中遇害。他进入莱顿大学求学，于1603年成为该校神学教授。

他受命为加尔文派预定论辩护、驳斥批评者，却转而主张上帝的恩典足以使一切信者得救，他的论争使荷兰归正会分裂。他于1609年在莱顿去世，一年后追随者提出《抗辩书》。

Jacques Cartier (1491–1557) was a Breton pilot from Saint-Malo who made three voyages into the Saint Lawrence and was the first European to record the name Canada. Commissioned by Francis I to find a western passage to Asia, he reached Newfoundland in 1534 and raised a cross at Gaspé for France.

In 1535 he sailed upriver with two sons of chief Donnacona, passed Stadacona and reached Hochelaga, beside a hill he named Mont Royal. His men wintered at Quebec, where scurvy killed 25 of his 110 men before a local fir-bark cure saved the rest; in spring he carried Donnacona off to France.

On his third voyage (1541–1542), he built a fort and sent home supposed gold and diamonds that proved to be pyrite and quartz. He retired to Saint-Malo, dying in 1557; his voyages, none losing a ship, became the basis of France's claim to New France.

雅克·卡蒂埃（1491—1557）是圣马洛的布列塔尼领航员，三次航行圣劳伦斯河，第一个记录“加拿大”一名的欧洲人。受弗朗索瓦一世派遣寻找通往亚洲的航路，1534年抵达纽芬兰，在加斯佩竖起十字架，为法王宣示主权。

1535年，他带着首领多纳科纳的两个儿子沿河而上，经过斯塔达科纳，抵达霍切拉加，旁侧山丘被他命名为皇家山。人马在魁北克过冬，坏血病夺去110人中的25人，靠当地人的冷杉树皮煎剂才治愈余人；开春后他把多纳科纳带回法国。

第三次航行（1541—1542）时，他建起堡垒，运回的黄金钻石实为黄铁矿和石英。他退居圣马洛，1557年去世；三次航行未损失一艘船，成为法国主张新法兰西的依据。

Jacques Cœur (c. 1395–1456), a merchant born at Bourges, opened regular French trade with the Levant after buying goods at Damascus in 1432, running his operations from Montpellier.

Summoned to Paris by Charles VII in 1436, he became steward of royal expenditure and was ennobled in 1441; his loans funded the reconquest of Normandy.

In 1451 he was arrested on a fabricated charge of poisoning Agnès Sorel, and in 1453 sentenced to confiscation and exile. Escaping in 1455, he found refuge with the pope in Rome and died on Chios in 1456 while leading a papal fleet to relieve Rhodes.

雅克·柯尔（约1395—1456）是布尔日商人之子。1432年他在大马士革采购东方货物，以蒙彼利埃为基地，开通法国与黎凡特之间的常规贸易。

1436年查理七世召他入巴黎，他后来掌管王室开支，1441年受封贵族，他的借款资助了诺曼底收复战。

1451年，他被诬陷毒死国王情妇阿涅丝·索蕾而遭逮捕，1453年被判没收财产并流放。1455年他越狱出逃，在罗马受到教皇庇护；1456年奉教皇之命率舰队驰援罗得岛，途中在希俄斯岛病逝。

1451年，他被诬陷毒死国王情妇阿涅丝·索蕾而遭逮捕，1453年被判没收财产并流放。1455年他越狱出逃，在[ShowLocationName('rome')]受到教皇庇护；1456年奉教皇之命率舰队驰援罗得岛，途中在希俄斯岛病逝。

en:
Jacques Necker (1732–1804) was a Genevan banker who served as finance minister to Louis XVI. He moved to Paris in 1748 as a bank clerk and made his fortune there.

Appointed director of the royal treasury in 1776, he financed France's part in the American War of Independence by loans from 1777. In 1781 he published the Compte rendu, the first public account of the royal budget, and was dismissed months later.

Recalled in 1788, his dismissal on 11 July 1789 helped provoke the storming of the Bastille. Recalled again, he faced opposition to tax reform and resigned in 1790; he died in 1804.

雅克·内克尔（1732—1804）是日内瓦银行家，后任法王路易十六的财政总监。1748年他到巴黎做银行职员，在当地发迹。

1776年他被任命为皇家金库主管，1777年起以举债支持法国参与美国独立战争。1781年他公布《财政报告书》，首次公开王室账目，数月后即被解职。

1788年他被召回；1789年7月11日再度被免，成为攻占巴士底狱的导火索之一。他再次获召，税制改革却遭到反对，于1790年辞职，1804年去世。

en:
Al-Hariri (c. 1054–1122) was an Arab poet and scholar of the Bedouin Banu Harram tribe, who spent most of his life in Basra. After studying jurisprudence he became an official writer, moving between Basra's business affairs and Baghdad's literary circles.

His fame rests on the Maqamat al-Hariri, fifty anecdotes in rhymed prose ranked among the most admired works of Arabic literature. He also wrote a long grammar poem and died in Basra in 1122.

哈里里（约1054—1122）是贝都因巴努·哈兰部落出身的阿拉伯诗人与学者，大半生在巴士拉度过。他修习伊斯兰教法后担任官方文书，往返于巴士拉的产业与巴格达的文学圈之间。

他以《玛卡梅集》闻名，五十篇故事以押韵散文写成，是阿拉伯文学史上最受推崇的作品之一。他还著有一部讨论语法的长诗，于1122年在巴士拉去世。

en:
Anbarchi was a Mongol prince of the Ilkhanate, a son of Möngke Temür and grandson of Hulagu. After Gaykhatu's accession in 1291 he became viceroy of the eastern provinces and led reinforcements to Ghazan in Khorasan against the rebel emir Nawruz, until famine forced him to retreat.

In 1292 the emir Taghachar's faction spread word that Gaykhatu was dead and urged Anbarchi to claim the throne; distrusting the news, he arrested the envoys instead. Later accused of revolt, he died on 24 September 1294 at Nakhchivan.

en:
Dilshad Khatun (died 1351) was a Chobanid princess, daughter of the amir Demasq Kaja. After her father's execution in 1327 she found refuge at the court of Il-Khan Abu Sa'id, who married her in 1333 after divorcing her aunt Baghdad Khatun.

Following Abu Sa'id's death she became the chief wife of the Jalayirid ruler Hasan Buzurg and mother of his successor Shaikh Awais. She died in 1351 and was buried at Najaf; contemporaries suspected Hasan Buzurg had her poisoned for sympathizing with the rival Chobanid Malek Ashraf.

en:
Hasan Buzurg (c. 1305–1356) founded Jalayirid rule in Iraq and Persia. A Jalayir amir, after the Ilkhanate collapsed in 1335 he became its kingmaker: in 1336 he defeated 'Ali Padshah and set up the child Muhammad Khan at Tabriz.

Defeated by the Chobanid Hasan Kucek in 1338 and 1340, he withdrew to Baghdad and built an independent state, ruling as ulus beg without taking the khan's title. He died in July 1356 and was succeeded by his son Shaikh Awais.

Möngke Temür (23 October 1256 – 26 April 1282) was the youngest son of the Ilkhan Hulagu by an Oirat wife. In 1266 Abaqa placed him on the Caucasus frontier against the Golden Horde. Betrothed at five to Abish Khatun of Shiraz, he married her in 1272 and helped govern Fars.

In 1281 he led an army against the Mamluk sultan Qalawun in Syria, was wounded, defeated, and fled to Mosul. Abaqa's chosen heir, he died suddenly in April 1282, days after his brother. His son Anbarchi was accused of revolt and died in 1294.

Muhammad Khan (died 1338), born Hussein, was a child claimant to the Ilkhanid throne. In 1336 the Jalayirid amir Hasan Buzurg raised him to power as Muhammad Khan.

In July 1336 they defeated 'Ali Padshah and the rival khan Musa at Qara Darra and installed him in Tabriz. He reigned only as a Jalayirid puppet: in July 1338 the Chobanids under Hasan Kucek defeated them, and Muhammad Khan was captured and executed.

en:
Jan Długosz (1415–1480) was a Polish canon, diplomat and chronicler, regarded as Poland's first historian. Educated at the Kraków Academy from 1428, he served Bishop Zbigniew Oleśnicki as secretary and chancellor, and was ordained a priest in 1436.

He undertook missions for Casimir IV, including peace negotiations in the Thirteen Years' War and the education of the king's sons from 1467. He is best known for his Latin Annals of the Famous Kingdom of Poland in twelve books, covering 965–1480. Nominated Archbishop of Lwów, he died in 1480 just before the pope confirmed his elevation.

扬·德乌戈什（1415—1480）是波兰神父、外交家和编年史家，被视为波兰第一位历史学家。1428年起他在克拉科夫学院求学，1436年晋铎后成为克拉科夫法政牧师，并任克拉科夫主教兹比格涅夫·奥莱希尼茨基的秘书长。

卡齐米日四世派他参与十三年战争（1454—1466）期间对条顿骑士团的谈判，1467年起又命他教导王子。代表作《波兰史》记载了波兰至1480年的历史，他在临终前获提名为利沃夫大主教，同年于克拉科夫去世。

en:
Jan Kochanowski (1530–1584), born at Sycyna near Radom, was the foremost poet of the Polish Renaissance. He wrote in Polish and Latin, adapting and popularizing forms of Polish verse.

Educated at Kraków and Padua, he travelled in Italy and France before returning to Poland in 1559. From 1564 he served as royal secretary to Sigismund II Augustus and attended the 1569 Sejm of Lublin.

After retiring to his Czarnolas estate he wrote The Dismissal of the Greek Envoys (1578), the first Polish tragedy, and the Laments (1580) mourning his daughter Urszula. He died at Lublin in 1584.

扬·科哈诺夫斯基（1530—1584），生于拉多姆附近的瑟齐纳，是波兰文艺复兴时期最杰出的诗人。他以波兰语和拉丁语写作，改造并推广了波兰语诗歌形式。

他曾在克拉科夫和帕多瓦求学，游历意大利与法国，1559年回到波兰。1564年起，他担任国王齐格蒙特二世·奥古斯特的王室秘书，出席了1569年的卢布林议会。

退居恰尔诺拉斯庄园后，他写下波兰第一部悲剧《希腊使节的辞别》（1578）和悼念亡女乌尔苏拉的《挽歌》（1580）。1584年他卒于卢布林。

en:
Jan Žižka of Trocnov (c. 1360–11 October 1424) was the Czech knight who led the Taborite Hussites against the crusades, undefeated. Born into Bohemia's lower nobility, he served at the royal court.

A follower of Jan Hus, he led the Hussite army to victory at Sudoměř and on Vítkov Hill in 1420 and against Sigismund's host at Kutná Hora in 1421.

He drilled townsmen and peasants to fight behind armoured wagon forts mounting cannon, using terrain and gunfire against cavalry charges. Wounded at Rabí in 1421, he lost his remaining eye but kept command until his death before Přibyslav on 11 October 1424.

特罗茨诺夫的扬·杰式卡（约1360—1424年10月11日）是率领塔博尔派胡斯军抗击十字军、一生未尝败绩的捷克骑士。他出身波希米亚下层贵族，曾在王室宫廷任职。

他追随扬·胡斯，1420年率胡斯军在苏多梅日和维特科夫山获胜，1421年又在库特纳霍拉大破西吉斯蒙德的大军。

他操练市民与农民，依托装有火炮的装甲“战车工事”作战，凭地形与火力克制骑兵冲锋。1421年他在围攻拉比城堡时负伤，仅存的一目也告失明，却仍坚持指挥，直到1424年10月11日在围攻普日比斯拉夫期间病逝军中。

en:
Aisu Tsunenobu was a head of the Aisu warrior clan of Kii Province in the Kamakura period. As jitō, steward of the Nambu, Mitsu and Akitsu manors, he built Kinugasa Castle on Mount Kinugasa. His castle overlooked the Nakahechi route of the Kumano road, Tanabe Bay and Akitsuno.

After the Hōji War in 1247 he resigned his stewardship and, in his later years, moved his residence from Nambu Hall to the castle, which became the seat of the Kii Aisu clan.

en:
Akamatsu Mitsunori (1320–1381), also called Shichijō Mitsunori, was a Nanbokuchō-era commander and shugo of Settsu Province. Eldest son of Akamatsu Norisuke, he inherited the Settsu post in 1351 after his father's death, while the clan headship and Harima passed to his uncle Sokuyū.

In 1352 he helped the Northern Court retake Kyoto and fought at the siege of Otokoyama. He lost the Settsu post to Sasaki Dōyō in 1360, regained it in 1363, and was replaced again in 1374.

en:
Akamatsu Norimura (1277–1350), also known by his dharma name Enshin, was the fourth head of the Akamatsu clan and shugo of Harima Province. In 1333 he answered Prince Morinaga's call and rose against the Hōjō, helping Ashikaga Takauji storm the Rokuhara headquarters.

After the Kenmu regime confiscated his governorship, he joined Takauji's 1335 revolt. In 1336 he held Shirohata Castle for fifty days against Nitta Yoshisada, enabling Takauji's victory at the Minato River. He died in Kyoto in 1350.

en:
Akamatsu Norisuke, also called Sokuyū (1314–1371), was a Nanbokuchō-era commander and sixth head of the Akamatsu clan, son of Akamatsu Norimura. Once a monk on Mount Hiei, in 1333 he carried Prince Morinaga's anti-shogunate order to his father.

He held Kanjōyama Castle against Nitta Yoshisada in 1336. In 1351 he succeeded his elder brother as clan head and shugo of Harima, adding Bizen in 1355. In 1361, after rebels seized Kyoto, he sheltered Ashikaga Yoshimitsu at Shirahata Castle. Appointed to the Zenritsugata in 1370, he died in Kyoto the next year.

In 1349 he built Himeyama Castle, the nucleus of later Himeji Castle. He held Mimasaka as shugo from 1356 until the bakufu replaced him in 1364.

1335年，他追随足利尊氏参加箱根·竹之下之战，后归附北朝，组织赤旗一揆。1349年他修筑姬山城，即日后姬路城的前身。1356年起出任美作国守护，1364年被幕府替换。

en:
Akamatsu Tomonori was a Nanbokuchō-era commander, a son of Akamatsu Norisuke and grandson of Norimura, though the Taiheiki names his uncle Sokuyū as his father. He fought consistently for Ashikaga Takauji through the Kannō Disturbance.

In 1351 he joined Sokuyū under Kō no Moronao to attack Ishidō Yorifusa at Kōmyōji. In 1355 he served Ashikaga Yoshiakira at the battle of Jinnan in Settsu, where he charged enemy general Yamana Morouji and scattered his troops, himself suffering severe wounds.

en:
Akamatsu Ujinori (1330–1386) was a Nanbokuchō-era commander, the fourth son of Akamatsu Norimura. A warrior famed for his strength, he quarreled with his three elder brothers and, unlike them, sided with the Southern Court in the Kannō Disturbance.

In 1355 he joined Yamana Tokiuji in briefly retaking Kyoto. In 1360 he joined Prince Akamatsu's rebellion, then surrendered to Sokuyū. He rose again in 1369 and 1386; after the last revolt, Hosokawa Yorimoto's forces trapped him and he killed himself at Kiyomizu-dera with over a hundred followers.

en:
Akizuki Tanemichi was a warrior of the Nanboku-cho period and the ninth head of the Akizuki clan of Chikuzen Province. In 1336 he fought on the loyalist Southern Court side under the Kikuchi at the Battle of Tatarahama against Ashikaga Takauji's army.

The Akizuki were routed and lost more than twenty of their clansmen. Tanemichi broke away and fled as far as Dazaifu, where pursuing troops surrounded him and killed him in the third month of 1336.

en:
Akizuki Tanekatsu, born Harada Tanekatsu, was a warrior of Chikuzen Province and the founder of the Akizuki clan. He lived at the castle of Harada Tanenao, usually described as his elder brother. His family served the Taira, and he fought for them when the Taira court fled to Kyushu in 1183.

After the Taira destruction at Dannoura in 1185 and Tanenao's capture, he went into hiding. Around 1203 the Kamakura shogunate granted him the Akizuki manor; he settled there, took the name Akizuki and built Mount Kosho castle, founding the line of Akizuki lords.

en:
Anayama Yoshitake, first named Norinobu, was a son of the Kai governor Takeda Nobutake and is counted as the founder of the Anayama clan. He settled at Anayama in Koma District of Kai Province and took the place name as his family name.

The Taiheiki records that in 1359 he accompanied the Zen monk Hatakeyama Dōsei up to Kyoto with his elder brother Takeda Nobunari. Having no son of his own, he was succeeded by his grandnephew Anayama Mitsuharu, born Takeda Nobumoto.

穴山义武，初名范信，是甲斐守护武田信武之子，被尊为穴山氏之祖。他以甲斐国巨摩郡穴山为据点，改称穴山姓。

《太平记》记载，1359年他随禅门畠山道誓上洛，同行者还有其兄武田信成。他没有亲生子嗣，由侄孙穴山满春（初名武田信元）作为养子继承穴山氏。

en:
Andō Iesue (fl. 1330–1338) was a Mutsu Province commander of the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō eras, Andō Morosue's younger brother and a traditional son of Andō Munesue. In 1333 he and his brother fought for the imperial court at Daikōji Castle.

They later switched to the Northern Court, and in 1336 Shiba Ienaga appointed Iesue Tsugaru battle magistrate, after which he attacked the Nanbu clan. Kitabatake Akiie's letters accuse him of seizing Tsugaru and Sotogahama. After 1338 he vanishes from the records, replaced by his brother.

zh:
安藤家季（活跃于1330—1338年）是镰仓末期至南北朝时代陆奥国的武将，安藤师季之弟，相传同为安藤宗季之子。1333年，他与兄长一同作为朝廷方参加大光寺城之战。

后来兄弟改投北朝，1336年斯波家长任命家季为津轻合战奉行，家季随即进攻南部氏。北畠显家的御教书指责他强占津轻与外滨。1338年以后，家季不见于史料，由其兄接替。

en:
Andō Morosue (fl. 1325–1341), first named Takasue, was a commander of Mutsu Province in the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō eras, said to be Andō Munesue's son. Deeds record him inheriting Hanawa District lands and western Tsugaru in 1325–1330.

He fought for the court at Daikōji Castle in 1333, and Kitabatake Akiie confirmed his lands in 1334–1335. In 1338 he replaced his brother Iesue as Tsugaru battle magistrate. He took a character from Kō no Moronao to form the name Morosue, and in 1341 briefly rejoined the Southern Court, playing both courts to protect his domain.

安藤师季（活跃于1325—1341年）是镰仓末期至南北朝时代陆奥国的武将，初名高季，相传为安藤宗季之子。让状记载，他在1325至1330年间相继继承鼻和郡与津轻西滨的领地。

1333年，他作为朝廷一方参加大光寺城之战，1334至1335年其领地得到北畠显家承认。1338年，他取代弟弟家季出任津轻合战奉行。他取执事高师直的偏讳改名师季，1341年又一度倒向南朝，在两朝之间周旋以保全领地。

en:
Ando Munesue was a late Kamakura warrior based in Hanawa district of Mutsu Province. Most scholars identify him with Ando Suehisa, who fought his kinsman Ando Suenaga over the Ezo deputy post from before 1318, sparking the Ando clan war. In 1322 the Hojo Tokuso heard the dispute, and in 1325 Munesue was named Ezo deputy and took that name.

Bakufu troops captured Suenaga in 1326 and a settlement followed in 1328. Deeds record grants to his son Inuhoshi in 1325 and to Takasue in 1330; Inuhoshi is thought to have been Morosue's childhood name.

安东宗季是镰仓时代末期的武将，据点在陆奥国鼻和郡。通说认为他即安东季久：1318年以前，他便与亲族安东季长争夺虾夷代官一职，引发安东氏之乱。1322年纠纷上交北条得宗裁决，1325年宗季被任命为虾夷代官并改用此名。

1326年幕府军擒获季长，1328年双方达成和议。让状记载他曾于1325年让地给儿子犬法师、1330年让地给高季；一种有力的观点认为犬法师是师季的幼名。

Anenokōji Ietsuna (died 1390) was a fourteenth-century court noble and head of the Anenokōji family, the son of Anenokōji Takamoto. An account names him among those captured with his nephew Tadatsuna fighting Northern Court forces in Etchū in 1371.

Ietsuna is the first member of his family recorded as governor of Hida Province. A court diary names him in that office on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month, 1378.

en:
Anenokōji Tadatsuna was a Southern Court noble and warrior of the Nanbokuchō era, the son of Anenokōji Yoritoki, titled master of the Left Capital Office. He settled at Furukawa in Hida Province and took the family name Furukawa.

In 1371 he was captured fighting Northern Court troops at Kurose in Etchū together with his uncle Ietsuna. In 1411 he raised arms at Furukawa Castle over disputed Yamashina family lands, resisting a bakufu army of the Kyōgoku, Shiba and Ogasawara clans; in the ninth month he was killed by Kyōgoku Takakazu in the later-named Hida Revolt.

姊小路尹纲是南北朝时代的南朝公卿、武将，姊小路赖时之子，官至左京大夫。他定居飞驒国古川乡，称古川氏。

1371年，他在越中国黑濑与北朝军交战，与伯父家纲一同被俘。1411年，因围绕山科家领地的争端，他在古川城举兵，抵抗幕府派出的京极、斯波、小笠原诸氏讨伐军，同年9月被京极高数攻杀，史称飞驒之乱。

en:
Anenokōji Takamoto (1297–1358) was a court noble from the late Kamakura era into the Nanbokuchō wars, the son of the courtier Fujiwara no Yorimoto. He reached Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade in 1309 and served as chamberlain until resigning in 1315, after which he held no recorded office for twenty years.

When Emperor Go-Daigo founded the Southern Court at Yoshino in 1336, Takamoto joined it as a lieutenant of the Left Imperial Guards, became master of the Palace Office in 1342, and reached Junior Third Rank in 1347. He died in 1358.

姊小路高基（1297—1358）是镰仓后期至南北朝时代的公卿，为朝臣藤原赖基之子。他于1309年叙从五位上，曾任侍从，1315年辞官，此后二十年间没有任官记录。

1336年后醍醐天皇在吉野开设南朝朝廷，高基出仕南朝，任左近卫少将，1342年任宫内卿，1347年升至从三位。他于1358年去世。

en:
Ankan (466–536), the 27th emperor of Japan, was the eldest son of Emperor Keitai by Menokohime. Born Prince Magari no Ōe, he ascended the throne in 531 after his father's death.

In a reign of fewer than five years he enlarged the Yamato court's economic power, ordering royal granaries called miyake and attached service households called nashiro to be set up across the provinces. He died in 536, and the throne passed to his younger brother, Emperor Senka.

zh:
安闲天皇（466—536）是日本传统世系中的第27代天皇，为继体天皇与目子媛所生的长子，本名勾大兄。531年父亲去世后即位。

在位不足五年，他着力扩充大和朝廷的经济实力，在各国广设屯仓，并配属称名代的服役民户。536年去世，皇位由其弟宣化天皇继承。

en:
Ano no Kinsuke (c. 1160–before 1226) was an early Kamakura court noble and founder of the Ano house. The son of Fujiwara no Narichika, he was adopted by Fujiwara no Sanekuni.

In 1185 he was moved from chamberlain to the Right Stables Office as a pro-shogunate noble. Slander cost him his court access in 1192, and he later went to Kamakura. He married a daughter of Yoritomo's half-brother Ano Zenjō; their son Sanenao took the Ano name.

阿野公佐（约1160—1226年前）是镰仓时代前期的公卿、阿野家的家祖。他本是藤原成亲之子，被藤原实国收为养子。

1185年，他作为亲幕府的公卿，由侍从转任右马权头。1192年，他因遭人谗言被停止升殿，后来还曾前往镰仓。他娶源赖朝异母弟阿野全成之女为妻，二人之子实直以阿野为姓。

en:
Ano Renshi (1301–1359) was a court lady and favoured consort of Emperor Go-Daigo, a daughter of the court noble Ano no Kinkado. She entered court service in 1319 and bore Go-Daigo Princes Tsuneyoshi, Nariyoshi and Noriyoshi, the future Emperor Go-Murakami.

Promoted to junior third rank in 1331, she followed the emperor into exile on Oki after the Genkō War and later went with him to Yoshino. As Go-Murakami's mother she became Southern Court empress dowager, received the ingō Shintaikemon-in in 1351, took Buddhist vows in 1357 and died at Kanshin-ji in Kawachi in 1359.

zh:
阿野廉子（1301—1359）是后醍醐天皇的女官与宠姬，为公家阿野公廉之女。1319年她入仕后宫，后来成为后醍醐的侧室，生下恒良亲王、成良亲王和后来成为后村上天皇的义良亲王。

1331年她叙从三位，元弘之乱后随驾流放隐岐，后又随赴吉野。作为后村上的生母，她成为南朝皇太后，1351年受院号“新待贤门院”，1357年落发出家，1359年在河内观心寺崩逝。

en:
Ano Sanenao (1209–1251) was an early Kamakura court noble of the Ano house, the son of Ano Kinsuke. In the twelfth month of 1221, aged thirteen, he was made a chamberlain.

He rose through the palace guards to lieutenant of the Right Inner Palace Guards and reached junior third rank in 1249. Reappointed chamberlain in 1251, he died in the ninth month that year; his son Kiminaka continued the family line.

阿野实直（1209—1251）是镰仓时代前期公卿、阿野公佐之子。1221年十二月，年仅十三岁的他担任侍从。

此后他在近卫府累迁至右近卫中将，1249年叙从三位，跻身公卿。1251年他再任侍从，同年九月去世，其子公仲延续了家族血脉。

en:
Antoku (1178–1185), son of Emperor Takakura and grandson of Taira no Kiyomori, was named crown prince at about a month old. He was enthroned in 1180, with Kiyomori ruling in his name.

When the Minamoto seized Kyoto in 1183, the Taira fled west with the boy, and the court enthroned Go-Toba. At the Battle of Dan-no-ura in April 1185 the Taira were destroyed; his grandmother clasped the six-year-old emperor and drowned with him in the Shimonoseki Straits, and the sacred sword was lost.

安德天皇（1178—1185）是高仓天皇之子、平清盛的外孙，出生约一个月即被立为太子，1180年登基，由清盛以他的名义执政。

1183年源氏攻占京都，平家带着幼帝西逃，朝廷另立后鸟羽天皇。1185年4月坛之浦海战中平家覆灭，祖母抱着六岁的安德天皇一同跳入下关海峡溺亡，神剑也随之沉入海中。

en:
Arima Sumiyo was a head of the Hizen-Arima clan, a warrior family of Hizen Province in Kyushu. In the Northern and Southern Courts wars the clan followed the Kikuchi and the Shoni.

In 1353 Sumiyo invited the Soto Zen master Daichi Sokei, who had studied in Yuan China and enjoyed the Kikuchi's patronage, to Kazusa in southern Hizen; there Daichi founded Suigetsusan Entsu-ji, where he died in 1367. Sumiyo was succeeded as clan head by his son Arima Mitsuzumi.

en:
Arima Tsunezumi was an early Kamakura-period warrior and the recorded founder of the Hizen-Arima clan. During the Kenpo era of 1213 to 1219 he was granted the jitō office of the Arima manor in Hizen Province and took the surname Arima.

During the same era he built Hinoe Castle on the Shimabara Peninsula. Clan tradition called him a descendant of the Heian pirate leader Fujiwara no Sumitomo.

en:
Asakura Hirokage (1254–1352) was a Nanboku-chō warrior and the first head of the Echizen Asakura clan, born in Asakuradani in Tajima Province. After the Kamakura shogunate fell, he took service under Ashikaga Takauji and followed Shiba Takatsune into Echizen.

He fought at the Battle of Fujishima against Nitta Yoshisada and was rewarded with Kuromaru Castle, where he took the name Kuromaru Uemon Nyūdō. In 1342 he founded Kōshō-ji. He died in 1352, aged about ninety-eight, and was succeeded by his son Takakage.

朝仓广景（1254—1352）是南北朝时代的武将，越前朝仓氏初代当主，生于但马国朝仓谷。镰仓幕府灭亡后，他投奔足利尊氏，随斯波高经进入越前。

他在藤岛之战中参加讨伐新田义贞，因战功受赐黑丸城，遂号黑丸右卫门入道。1342年，他建立弘祥寺。1352年，他以约九十八岁高龄去世，家督由其子高景继承。

en:
Asakura Takakage (1314–1372) was the second head of the Echizen Asakura clan, serving the Ashikaga shoguns as a retainer of the Shiba. In 1355 he helped defeat a thirty-thousand-strong Southern Court army at Tō-ji's southern gate in Kyoto, and in 1357 he was made steward of the Asuwa estate.

During the Jōji Disturbance of 1366 he joined the bakufu forces against his own lord Shiba Takatsune at Somayama Castle, receiving steward rights over seven Echizen estates and laying the clan's territorial foundation. He died in 1372 and was succeeded by his son Ujikage.

zh:
朝仓高景（1314—1372）是越前朝仓氏第二代当主，以斯波氏被官的身份侍奉足利氏。1355年，他在京都东寺南门参与击溃三万南朝大军；1357年被任命为足羽庄的预所。

1366年贞治之变中，他加入幕府军，在杣山城攻打自己的主君斯波高经，因此获封越前七处庄园的地头职，奠定了朝仓氏的领地基础。他于1372年去世，家督由其子氏景继承。

en:
Asayama Kagetsura, also called Asayama Jirozaemon-no-jo, was a warrior of the Asayama clan of Izumo Province who served Ashikaga Takauji at the time of the Kenmu Restoration. In 1335 he was appointed shugo of Bingo Province, holding the post until 1338, when Niki Yoshinaga succeeded him.

The Edo-period chronicle Bingo Kojoki records that he built the fort on Koyajima in 1335, the earliest fortification on the later Kannabe Castle site. Takauji granted him estates for his service in Aki. His son Yoshikage later served the Ashikaga shoguns.

zh:
朝山景连，通称朝山二郎左卫门尉，是出云国朝山氏的武将，在建武新政时期出仕足利尊氏。1335年他被任命为备后守护，在任至1338年，由仁木义长接任。

据《备后古城记》记载，他于1335年在古城山筑城，被视为后来神边城最早的城郭。他因在安艺国的军功受足利尊氏恩赏领地，其子朝山义景后来也出仕足利氏。

en:
Asayama Koretsuna was an official of Asayama district in Izumo Province and the elder brother of Mototsuna. His daughter married Nogi Mitsutsuna, a son of Sasaki Takatsuna who became steward of Nogi in the early Kamakura period.

Their son Takasada inherited Kizu Mishima from his mother. After the Jōkyū War of 1221, most of Koretsuna's family lost their standing, while his brother Mototsuna became head of the Katsube no Sukune lineage.

朝山惟纲是出云国朝山乡的乡司，也是元纲之兄。他的女儿嫁给野木光纲；光纲是佐佐木高纲之子，镰仓时代初期成为乃木保地头。

他们的儿子高定从母亲继承了木津御岛。1221年承久之乱后，惟纲一系大多没落，其弟元纲则成为胜部宿祢一族的惣领。

en:
Ashikaga Ietoki (1260–1284) was the sixth head of the Ashikaga house and a Kamakura gokenin. Succeeding young, in 1269 he set rules for the clan temple Banna-ji.

In 1282 he became Iyo no kami, the first warrior to hold it since Minamoto no Yoshitsune. After losing a land suit against a Kōya-san monk in 1279 he grew critical of the shogunate, and in 1284 took his own life at Kamakura, succeeded by his son Sadauji.

足利家时（约1260—1284）是镰仓幕府御家人、足利宗家第六代当主。他幼年继承父亲赖氏，1269年为氏寺鑁阿寺制定寺规。

1282年他补任伊予守，是自源义经以来第一位出任该职的武家。1279年，他在与高野山僧人争夺领地的诉讼中败诉，对幕府渐生不满，1284年在镰仓自尽，由儿子贞氏继嗣。

en:
Ashikaga Sadauji (1273–1331) was the seventh head of the Ashikaga house and a late Kamakura gokenin. Succeeding at about ten, he received his name from the regent Hōjō Sadatoki and restored the family temples.

He took vows around 1301 and later may have yielded the headship to his eldest son Takayoshi. Takayoshi died in 1317, whereupon Sadauji resumed rule. He died in 1331; his son Takauji inherited and overthrew the Hōjō in 1333.

足利贞氏（1273—1331）是镰仓时代后期御家人、足利宗家第七代当主。他约十岁继承家督，元服时得执权北条贞时赐偏讳“贞”字，还复兴了足利氏的菩提寺。

他约于1301年出家，后来可能把家督让给长子高义。高义于1317年早逝，贞氏再度主持家政。1331年他去世，儿子尊氏继承家督，并于1333年推翻北条氏、灭亡镰仓幕府。

en:
Ashikaga Tadafuyu (1327–c. 1400) was an illegitimate son of Shogun Ashikaga Takauji. Unacknowledged by his father and raised as a novice at the Tōshōji in Kamakura, he was adopted around 1345 by Takauji's brother Tadayoshi.

He won his first campaign against Southern Court forces in 1348 and became Nagato tandai by 1349. During the Kannō Disturbance he turned against Takauji and was briefly named Kyushu tandai in 1351.

His faction collapsed after Takauji's death in 1358. His last known letter dates to 1366, and later genealogies place his death in 1400.

zh:
足利直冬（1327—约1400）是日本南北朝时代武将，室町幕府初代将军足利尊氏的私生子。他自幼不被父亲承认，在镰仓东胜寺做小沙弥，约1345年被尊氏之弟直义收为养子。

1348年他在讨伐南朝势力的初阵中立下战功，1349年前后出任统领西国的长门探题。观应之乱中，他与尊氏反目，1351年一度被任命为九州探题。

尊氏1358年死后，其党羽瓦解；存世的最后一封文书作于1366年，后世系图记载他于1400年去世。

en:
Ashikaga Tadayoshi (1306–1352), younger brother of the shōgun Takauji, ran the Ashikaga regime's government while Takauji commanded its armies; the pair were called the two shōguns. After the Hōjō fell he governed Kamakura for Prince Nariyoshi, and when the Nakasendai rebellion overran the city in 1335, he killed the imprisoned Prince Moriyoshi and fled.

He shaped much of the 1336 Kenmu Shikimoku, and a disciple of Musō Soseki, he expanded the Five Mountains temples. In 1349 his feud with the steward Kō no Moronao broke into the Kannō disturbance, and he was forced to take Buddhist vows.

He joined the Southern Court in 1350 and beat Takauji in 1351, taking Kyoto and Kamakura; but Takauji made peace with the south and turned on him. Defeated and held in a Kamakura monastery, he died suddenly in 1352; the Taiheiki says he was poisoned.

zh:
足利直义（1306—1352）是征夷大将军足利尊氏之弟。尊氏掌管军队，直义主持足利政权的政务，时人称兄弟二人为“两将军”。北条氏覆灭后，他奉成良亲王前往镰仓治理当地；1335年中先代之乱攻陷镰仓时，他杀害了被幽禁的护良亲王，随后出逃。

1336年的《建武式目》多出自他的主张。他师从禅僧梦窗疏石，扩建了五山禅寺体系。1349年，他与执事高师直的积怨爆发为观应扰乱，被迫出家。

1350年他投奔南朝，1351年击败尊氏，攻占京都并进入镰仓；尊氏却转而与南朝讲和，出兵讨伐他。直义兵败后被幽禁于镰仓的寺院，1352年突然去世，《太平记》称他是被毒杀的。

en:
Ashikaga Takauji (1305–1358) founded the Ashikaga shogunate and split Japan into two imperial courts. In 1333 the Hōjō sent him against Emperor Go-Daigo's rising, holding his family hostage; he turned on them at Shinomura, and his allies took their Kyoto headquarters.

After the 1335 Nakasendai rebellion, unauthorized rewards to his followers had him declared a rebel. The Taiheiki says he cut his hair as a monk before riding out, and Kamakura's warriors copied him. Driven to Kyūshū, he returned to win at the Minatogawa in 1336 and enthrone Emperor Kōmyō, while Go-Daigo founded a Southern Court at Yoshino.

Made shōgun in 1338, he fell out with his brother and co-ruler Tadayoshi in the Kannō disturbance. A Zen master praised his calm and generosity, but later Confucian historians named him one of Japan's three great villains. He died of a back boil in 1358, succeeded by his son Yoshiakira.

Driven to Kyūshū, he returned to win at the Minatogawa in 1336 and enthrone #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('jap_koumyou_tenno').GetID],X #L Emperor Kōmyō#!#!, while Go-Daigo founded a Southern Court at [ShowLocationName('yoshino')].

Made shōgun in 1338, he fell out with his brother and co-ruler Tadayoshi in the Kannō disturbance. A Zen master praised his calm and generosity, but later Confucian historians named him one of Japan's three great villains. He died of a back boil in 1358, succeeded by his son Yoshiakira.
zh:
足利尊氏（1305—1358）创立室町幕府，也使日本分裂为南北两个朝廷。1333年，北条氏派他去镇压后醍醐天皇的举兵，把他的家人扣为人质；他在筿村倒戈反对北条氏，盟友随即攻占了北条氏设在京都的六波罗探题。

1335年平定中先代之乱后，他未经朝廷许可便向追随者论功行赏，被宣布为朝敌。《太平记》说，他出阵前曾剪发欲出家，镰仓的武士也都跟着剪了发。他从京都败退九州，又于1336年在凑川获胜，拥立光明天皇，后醍醐天皇则在吉野另立南朝。

1338年他就任征夷大将军，后来与共同执政的弟弟直义反目，爆发观应扰乱。禅僧称他临阵沉着、宽厚慷慨，后来的儒家史家却把他列为日本三大枭雄之一。1358年他因背上的肿疮去世，其子足利义诠继任。

en:
Ashikaga Takayoshi (1297–1317) was a gokenin of the late Kamakura shogunate and the eldest son of Ashikaga Sadauji. At his coming of age he took a character from the regent Hōjō Takatoki, using the Minamoto character yoshi rather than the customary uji.

In 1315, already acting as head, he confirmed a monk's office at Tsurugaoka Hachiman shrine. He died in 1317, aged twenty-one; his younger brother Takauji later won the shogunate.

en:
Ashikaga Yasuuji (1216–1270) was the fourth head of the Ashikaga house and a Kamakura gokenin. The legitimate son of Ashikaga Yoshiuji and a daughter of the regent Hōjō Yasutoki, he was named for Yasutoki.

In 1251 he took vows without the shogunate's leave; the regency seized his Hanabusa manor in Shimōsa and he retired to Ashikaga. His Tokusō-born son Yoriuji became heir after the elder son Ieuji was set aside and founded the Shiba line.

Ashikaga Yoriuji (1240–1262) was the fifth head of the Ashikaga house and a gokenin of the mid-Kamakura shogunate. A son of Ashikaga Yasuuji by a daughter of Hōjō Tokiuji of the Tokusō line, he was made heir over his elder brothers.

First named Toshiuji, in 1256 he was renamed Yoriuji with a character from the regent Hōjō Tokiyori. He died in 1262, aged twenty-three, and his young son Ietoki succeeded him.

en:
Ashikaga Yoshiakira (1330–1367), son of Takauji, was the second shōgun of the Ashikaga shogunate. As a child named Senjuō he was left in Kamakura as a Hōjō hostage in 1333, and when his father turned on the Hōjō, warriors storming the city rallied under his name.

Recalled to Kyoto during the Kannō disturbance to replace his uncle Tadayoshi, he fled in 1352 when Southern Court troops seized the capital and captured the Northern Court's imperial family. He retook it and enthroned Emperor Go-Kōgon without the imperial regalia, succeeding his father as shōgun in 1358.

In 1361 his steward Hosokawa Kiyouji defected to the south, which briefly held Kyoto. In 1367 he entrusted his young son Yoshimitsu to Hosokawa Yoriyuki and died, buried beside the Southern Court warrior Kusunoki Masatsura.

zh:
足利义诠（1330—1367）是足利尊氏之子，室町幕府第二代征夷大将军。他幼名千寿王，1333年被北条氏扣作人质留在镰仓；父亲倒戈后，攻袭镰仓的武士以他的名义集结。

观应扰乱期间，他被召回京都接替叔父足利直义主持政务；1352年南朝军队攻占京都、俘虏北朝皇室，他出逃后夺回京都，在没有三神器的情况下拥立后光严天皇。1358年他继任将军。

1361年，他的执事细川清氏投奔南朝，南朝借此短暂占据京都。1367年他把幼子足利义满托付给细川赖之后去世，葬在南朝武将楠木正行墓旁。

en:
Ashikaga Yoshikane (1154–1199) was the second head of the Ashikaga clan and a close vassal of Minamoto no Yoritomo, founder of the Kamakura shogunate. When Yoritomo rose in Izu in 1180, Yoshikane joined him in Kamakura, and in 1181 he married a younger sister of Hōjō Masako, becoming Yoritomo's brother-in-law.

He fought in the campaigns against the Taira and the northern Fujiwara, and in 1190 suppressed a revolt in Dewa. He took Buddhist vows at Tōdai-ji in 1195 and died at the family's Kabasaki temple in 1199.

en:
Ashikaga Yoshiuji (1189–1255) was the third head of the Ashikaga house and a gokenin of the early Kamakura shogunate. A son of Ashikaga Yoshikane by a daughter of Hōjō Tokimasa, he inherited the family leadership through his mother's Hōjō blood.

He supported the Hōjō regents in the Wada conflict of 1213 and the Jōkyū War of 1221, after which he became shugo of Mikawa Province. He took Buddhist vows in 1241 and died in 1255.

en:
Minamoto no Yoshiyasu, better known as Ashikaga no Yoshiyasu (c. 1125–1157), was a late Heian warrior and founder of the Ashikaga clan. The second son of Minamoto no Yoshikuni, he inherited the Ashikaga manor and took its name.

He served Retired Emperor Toba as a northern guard and became a kebiishi officer. In the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 he led over a hundred horsemen on the side of Emperor Go-Shirakawa. He died in 1157, little more than thirty years old.

Ashina Morikazu (c. 1285 – 4 September 1335), also known as Ashina Hōgan, was the sixth head of the Ashina clan of Aizu. In 1333 he marched on Kyoto with the Kamakura bakufu's army sent to subdue Emperor Go-Daigo, but was defeated.

In the seventh month of 1335 he answered Hōjō Tokiyuki's call in the Nakasendai Rebellion and made for Kamakura. The next month Ashikaga Takauji's counterattack caught him at the Battle of Katasegawa, where he was killed. The seventh head, Ashina Naomori, succeeded him.

In 1333 he marched on Kyoto with the [ShowLocationName('kamakura')] bakufu's army sent to subdue #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('jap_go_daigo_tenno').GetID],X #L Emperor Go-Daigo#!#!, but was defeated.

In the seventh month of 1335 he answered #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('jap_houjou_tokiyuki').GetID],X #L Hōjō Tokiyuki#!#!'s call in the Nakasendai Rebellion and made for Kamakura. The next month #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('jap_ashikaga_takauji').GetID],X #L Ashikaga Takauji#!#!'s counterattack caught him at the Battle of Katasegawa, where he was killed. The seventh head, #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('jap_ashina_naomori').GetID],X #L Ashina Naomori#!#!, succeeded him.
zh:
芦名盛员（约1285—1335年9月4日），通称芦名判官，是会津芦名氏第六代当主。1333年，他作为镰仓幕府军的一员上洛，追讨后醍醐天皇，却遭败北。

1335年7月北条时行发动中先代之乱，他响应起兵，赶往镰仓。同年8月，足利尊氏反攻，他在片濑川之战中战死。家督由第七代当主芦名直盛继承。

en:
Ashina Naomori was the seventh head of the Ashina clan in the Nanboku-chō period. In 1335 he succeeded after his father Morimune and his brothers died fighting in the Nakasendai Rebellion. He clashed with local lords and expanded his power from the Jōwa years.

In 1352 he abandoned Ashikaga Takauji for the Nitta side, then was driven back into Aizu. Tradition credits him with founding the Higashi-Kurokawa residence in 1384, the precursor of Kurokawa Castle.

芦名直盛是日本南北朝时代芦名氏第七代当主。1335年，父亲盛宗与兄弟在中先代之乱中战死，他继承家督。此后他与当地势力交锋，自贞和年间起扩张势力。

1352年他背离足利尊氏，倒向新田一方，随后败逃回会津。相传他于1384年修筑黑川城的前身东黑川馆，芦名氏正是在他这一代扎根会津。

en:
Ashina Yasumori was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Ashina family of Aizu, an offshoot of the Miura clan's Sahara line. A son of Sahara Mitsumori, he was the younger brother of Ashina Tsunemitsu, who became shugo of Hōki in 1272.

After Tsunemitsu lost the post and wandered the provinces, Yasumori overran his private estates and called him a beggar; the Kamakura bakufu found him guilty and restored the lands to his brother. Yet the later Ashina lords of Aizu descended from Yasumori's line.

芦名泰盛是镰仓时代武将，属三浦氏佐原流在会津分出的芦名氏。他是佐原光盛之子、芦名经光之弟；经光于1272年出任伯耆守护。

经光被解职、流浪各国期间，泰盛侵占其私领，还骂他是讨饭的；镰仓幕府判定泰盛有罪，把领地还给经光。然而后来在会津兴起的芦名氏，恰恰出自泰盛这一支。

en:
Uji Korenobu was the earliest historically attested head of the Aso family, the daiguji shrine house of Aso Shrine in Higo Province. By the first half of the twelfth century his line had formed a warrior band that ruled the country around Aso.

He is named in a formal report dated the twelfth month of 1142 and is the first verifiable figure in the Aso genealogy; the family still used the surname Uji in his lifetime. His successor was Uji Sukenaga.

宇治惟宣是肥后国阿苏神社大宫司家阿苏氏中，第一个能被史料证实的当主。12世纪上半叶，其族人已组成支配阿苏一带的武士团。

康治元年（1142年）12月的正式文书中可见其名，他也是阿苏氏系图里第一个能证实确有其人的人物，当时这一家仍以宇治为姓。继其之后的当主是宇治资永。

en:
Aso Koretoki was daiguji, chief priest and lord of Aso Shrine in Higo Province, appointed to the office by 1319. In 1333 he answered Emperor Go-Daigo's call against the shogunate and fought against Ashikaga Takauji, then retired in favour of his son Korenao.

After Korenao killed himself following defeat at Tatara Beach in 1336, Koretoki resumed the headship. Between 1349 and 1351 he switched between the Northern and Southern courts four times. In 1351 he adopted Koremura as heir, and he died in 1353.

阿苏惟时是肥后国阿苏神社的大宫司，至迟于1319年就任此职。1333年，他响应后醍醐天皇的讨幕纶旨，与足利尊氏作战，随后让位于长子惟直，退居幕后。

1336年惟直在多々良滨战败后自尽，惟时只得重管家督。1349至1351年间，他在北朝与南朝之间四次反复改换阵营。1351年，他收惟村为养子继承人，最终于1353年去世。

en:
Aso Koretsugu succeeded his father Koreyasu as daiguji, head priest of Aso Shrine in Higo Province. In 1196 Hōjō Tokimasa issued a warrant appointing him to the daiguji office, and in 1200 his father transferred the Nangō valley lands to him.

Tradition places in his time the move of the clan seat south beyond the caldera toward Yabe, and in 1222 he is said to have relocated the Tendai temple Aitōji and fortified its site.

en:
Aso Koreyasu was daiguji of Aso Shrine in Higo Province and the first of his line to call himself Aso instead of Uji. In 1180 he was made daiguji of the Aso and Kengun shrines, and in 1184 sponsored a branch Aso shrine at Nagoya.

Having taken the Taira side in Kyushu during the Genpei War, he was removed by the Kamakura shogunate, which placed the shrine under Hōjō Tokimasa. In 1196 Tokimasa named his son Koretsugu daiguji, and in 1200 Koreyasu handed over his holdings.

阿苏惟泰是肥后国阿苏神社的大宫司，也是家族中第一个放弃宇治旧姓、改称阿苏的当主。1180年，他被补任为阿苏、健军两座神社的大宫司，1184年在名越谷劝请阿苏神社分祀。

en:
Aso Korezumi (c.1309–1364) was a late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō warrior and the Southern Court daiguji of Aso Shrine. Of the disgraced Era branch, he was long called Era Korezumi. In 1333 he defected to Emperor Go-Daigo, and in 1336 fought Ashikaga Takauji at Tatara Beach.

He backed Prince Kanenaga in 1337 and in 1340 killed a Northern Court claimant at Nango Castle. Taking Dazaifu with the Kikuchi in 1361 won him recognition as daiguji, though a Northern Court rival split the clan. In 1364 he yielded office to his son Koremura, dying shortly after.

阿苏惟澄（约1309—1364）是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，南朝方的阿苏神社大宫司。他出身获罪的庶流惠良氏，长期自称惠良惟澄。1333年他倒向后醍醐天皇的官军，1336年参加多々良滨之战，对抗足利尊氏。

1337年，他在九州拥立怀良亲王；1340年攻落肥后南乡城，讨杀北朝方将领。1361年，他协助菊池氏攻占大宰府，被征西府承认为大宫司，但北朝另立竞争者，阿苏家再度分裂。1364年，他把大宫司之职让给儿子惟村，不久后去世。

1337年，他在九州拥立怀良亲王；1340年攻落肥后南乡城，讨杀北朝方将领。1361年，他协助[ShowDynastyName('kikuchi_dynasty')]氏攻占大宰府，被征西府承认为大宫司，但北朝另立竞争者，[ShowDynastyName('aso_dynasty')]家再度分裂。1364年，他把大宫司之职让给儿子惟村，不久后去世。

en:
Chikatsuna was a son of Asonuma Hirotsuna. He inherited Tōno manor in Hei District, Mutsu Province, and from 1213 to 1219 built Yokota Castle on Mount Gomadō as his seat of government.

For his service in the Jōkyū War of 1221 he was made jitō of Yano-Arayama manor in Aki Province, where he is credited with building Tokonoyama Castle and founding the Aki branch of the clan.

zh:
亲纲是阿曾沼广纲之子，继承了陆奥国闭伊郡的远野保。1213—1219年间，他在护摩堂山修筑横田城，作为统治中心。

1221年承久之乱时他立下军功，被补任为安艺国世能荒山庄的地头；相传他还在鸟笼山筑城，阿曾沼氏的安艺一支由此发端。
