en:
Togashi Yasuie was a late-Heian and early-Kamakura warrior, sixth head of the Togashi clan of Kaga. In 1183 he joined Minamoto no Yoshinaka against the Taira and fought at Kurikara Pass, where torches tied to oxen were driven burning into Taira no Koremori's camp.

After Yoshinaka's fall in 1184 he guarded the Ataka barrier as shugo of Kaga. In 1187, tradition holds, he recognized Yoshitsune disguised as a yamabushi but let him pass, moved by Benkei's kanjinchō; stripped of office, he took the name Shigezumi and ended his days at Nonoichi.

富㭴泰家是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将，加贺富㭴氏第六代当主。1183年，他投奔源义仲讨伐平氏，在俱利伽罗峠之战中命人把燃着的松明绑在牛角上，冲入平维盛的大营，大破平军。

en:
Toki Mitsuhira (died 1206) was a late-Heian warrior and Kamakura gokenin, the third son of Minamoto no Mitsunaga and effective founder of the Toki clan of Mino Province. Adopted by his uncle Mitsumoto, he held back when his father and elder brother died fighting with Kiso Yoshinaka in 1180, and only in 1184 led his kin to join Minamoto no Yoritomo.

Around 1201 he was made shugo of Mino Province. He died in 1206 and was succeeded by his son Mitsuyuki.

土岐光衡（卒于1206年）是平安末期至镰仓初期的武将、镰仓幕府御家人，源光长的第三子，也是美浓国土岐氏的实际始祖。他被伯父源光基收为养子，1180年父亲与兄长随木曾义仲起兵战死后他没有参战，直到1184年才率一族投奔源赖朝。

en:
Toki Mitsusada was a late Kamakura-period commander and head of the Toki clan, and fifth son of Toki Mitsuyuki. He married into the Hōjō Tokusō family and held a jitō post in Iyo Province, raising the Toki to leading gokenin standing in Mino.

He became governor of Oki Province after seizing an outlaw. Buddhist records credit him with fighting the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281. Late in life he took the tonsure as Teikō and died around 1281.

en:
Toki Mitsuyuki (died 1249) was the second head of the Toki clan, eldest son of Mitsuhira. A Kamakura gokenin, he served Retired Emperor Go-Toba in Kyoto as a Saimen warrior. In 1216, appointed Saemon-no-jo, he guarded Sanetomo's shogunal appointment ceremony and received a palace-forged sword from Go-Toba.

One account identifies him with the court warrior who in the Jokyu War of 1221 fought with a thousand men, was routed by Ashikaga Yoshiuji on the Kiso River, lost the Mino shugo office and escaped punishment through Chiba patronage. He later moved to Asano manor, took the name Asano Mitsuyuki, and died in 1249.

zh:
土岐光行（?—1249）是土岐氏第二代家督、土岐光衡的长子。他身为镰仓幕府御家人，与朝廷关系深厚，曾在京都担任后鸟羽上皇的西面武士。1216年他任左卫门尉，在源实朝的拜贺式上担任随兵，并获后鸟羽上皇下赐院中锻造的御刀。

一说认为他就是1221年承久之乱中率一千兵力加入京方的武士，在木曾川被足利义氏击败，失去美浓守护之职，靠千叶氏庇护免于问罪。后来他移居浅野馆，自称浅野光行，1249年去世。

en:
Toki Naouji (born c. 1331) was a Nanboku-chō warrior lord, a son of Toki Yorikiyo and younger brother of the shugo daimyō Yoriyasu. He was adopted by Ōno Naotoshi, also called Doi Naotoshi, of the Ōno clan in Iyo Province, and took the name Ōno or Doi Naouji.

His career unfolded mainly in Iyo on Shikoku, far from the main Toki lands in Mino. He later died of apoplexy at his residence in Kyoto.

zh:
土岐直氏（约1331年生）是南北朝时代的武将，土岐赖清之子、守护大名赖康的弟弟。他被伊予国大野氏的大野直利（又称土居直利）收为养子，改称大野直氏或土居直氏。

他主要在四国的伊予国活动，远离土岐氏本据的美浓，后来因中风在京都的宿所去世。

en:
Toki Yoriaki was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō periods, the youngest son of Toki Yorisada, the first Muromachi shugo of Mino Province. He first served the Hōjō regents alongside his father, then answered Emperor Go-Daigo's call and fought under Ashikaga Takauji.

After his elder brother Yoritō, the shugo of Mino, was executed in 1342, Yoriaki supported his nephew Yoriyasu and campaigned under Kō no Moronao. He was killed in 1348 at the Battle of Shijōnawate in Kawachi against Kusunoki Masatsura.

土岐赖明是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，为美浓国初代室町守护土岐赖贞最小的儿子。他起初随父亲侍奉北条得宗家，后响应后醍醐天皇举兵，投入足利尊氏麾下转战各地。

1342年，美浓守护兄长赖远被处死后，赖明辅佐继承家业的侄子赖康，跟随高师直转战。1348年，他在河内国四条畷与南朝方的楠木正行交战，战死沙场。

en:
Toki Yorikatsu was a Nanboku-chō warrior, a son of Toki Yorikiyo and a younger brother of Yoriyasu. When Yoriyasu based himself at Kawate Castle in Atsumi district, Yorikatsu established himself in Ibi district in western Mino; with his younger brother Yoritada he consolidated the Toki grip on western Mino.

He later called himself Ibi Yorikatsu and died in 1380. His son Yasuyuki was adopted by Yoriyasu and succeeded to the headship of the main Toki line.

土岐赖雄是南北朝时代的武将，土岐赖清之子、赖康之弟。兄长赖康在厚见郡筑革手城后，赖雄在美浓西部揖斐郡立足，与弟弟赖忠一起巩固了土岐氏在西美浓的根基。

他后来自称揖斐赖雄，于1380年去世。其子康行被赖康收为养子，后来继承了土岐氏本家的家督。

en:
Toki Yorikiyo was a commander and shugo daimyō of the late Kamakura and early Nanboku-chō period, son of Toki Yorisada, the first shugo of Mino. He made his home in Ikeda district of Mino Province, and under the Kenmu Restoration he was appointed shugo of Iyo.

He died on 4 July 1336, before his father. The Toki headship passed first to his younger brother Yoritō and later to his son Yoriyasu, who brought the clan to its height.

土岐赖清是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，初代美浓守护土岐赖贞之子，居于美浓国池田郡。建武新政时他被任命为伊予守护。

en:
Toki Yorisada (1271–1339), seventh son of Toki Mitsusada, built the Toki into the dominant warrior house of Mino Province. Suspected of joining the Shōchū plot against the Kamakura shogunate in 1324, he nevertheless survived to serve Ashikaga Takauji and became the Muromachi shogunate's first governor of Mino.

A friend of the Zen master Musō Soseki, he spread Rinzai Zen in the Toki district. He also left nearly ten poems in imperial anthologies, and died in 1339.

土岐赖贞（1271—1339）是土岐光定的第七子，他把土岐氏经营成美浓国最有权势的武士家族。1324年正中之变时，他被镰仓幕府怀疑参与倒幕密谋，却免于覆灭，其后出仕足利尊氏，成为室町幕府的初代美浓守护。

en:
Toki Yoritada (1323–1397) was a Nanboku-chō warrior, the sixth son of Toki Yorikiyo. Adopted young by his grandfather Yorisada after his father's early death, he held the Ikeda district of Mino and supported his eldest brother Yoriyasu.

When his nephew Yasuyuki rose against Shōgun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu in 1390, Yoritada and his second son Yorimasu joined the shogunal army to crush him. Appointed shugo of Mino after the revolt, he founded the Toki Nishi-Ikeda line, yielded the post to Yorimasu in 1395, and died in 1397.

en:
Toki Yoritō (d. 1342), seventh son of Toki Yorisada, was a basara daimyō and governor of Mino. He fought for Ashikaga Takauji, and in 1338 against Kitabatake Akiie at Aonogahara, where the Taiheiki credits his thousand picked horsemen with pinning the great loyalist army.

Succeeding his father in 1339, he kept harrying Southern Court forces. In 1342, drunk, he reviled and overturned Retired Emperor Kōgon's ox cart; on Ashikaga Tadayoshi's order he was beheaded that December.

en:
Tokunō Michitsuna was a commander of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō period and head of a warrior house holding the Tokunō estate in Iyo. In the leap second month of 1333 he rose for Emperor Go-Daigo, stormed Utsunomiya Sadamune's Fuchū castle, and drove Hōjō Tokinao from the province.

Under the Kenmu government he became governor of Bingo Province. He joined Nitta Yoshisada's Southern Court, fought at Teshimagawara and Minatogawa in 1336, and was killed in 1337 defending Kanagasaki Castle.

得能通纲是镰仓时代至南北朝时代武将，为领有伊予国得能庄的得能氏当主。1333年闰二月，他举兵响应后醍醐天皇，攻陷宇都宫贞宗的府中城，并将北条时直逐出伊予。

建武政权下叙任备后守。南北朝战乱中，他追随新田义贞加入南朝，1336年参加丰岛河原合战与凑川之战，1337年在金崎城之战中战死。

en:
Prince Tomohira (964–1009), the seventh son of Emperor Murakami, came of age in 977, served as minister of war and later minister of central affairs, and reached the second court rank in 1007. Contemporaries knew him as Go-Chūshō-ō or the Lord of Rokujō Palace.

A gifted poet in Chinese and Japanese verse, he has forty-one waka in imperial anthologies and helped compile the Wakanshōrōshū and Honchō monzui. His son Morofusa took the surname Minamoto, founding the Murakami Genji line.

zh:
具平亲王（964—1009）是村上天皇第七皇子，977年元服，历任兵部卿、中务卿，1007年升至二品，时人称他为后中书王、六条宫。

具平长于汉诗与和歌，敕撰和歌集共收录其和歌四十一首，并参与编纂《和汉朗咏集》与《本朝文粹》。其子师房获赐姓源氏，子孙称村上源氏。

en:
Prince Toneri (676–735), sixth son of Emperor Tenmu, was a leading imperial prince of the early Nara period. He supervised the compilation of the Nihon Shoki and presented the thirty-scroll chronicle to the court in 720.

After Fujiwara no Fuhito's death that year he headed the Council of State with Prince Nagaya, and in 729 interrogated Nagaya during the Nagaya Incident. He died in 735, and when his son Prince Ōi became Emperor Junnin, Toneri was posthumously titled Emperor Sudōjinkei.

zh:
舍人亲王（676—735）是天武天皇第六子，奈良时代前期皇族势力的核心人物之一。他主持《日本书纪》的编修，于720年将这部三十卷史书奏上朝廷。

同年藤原不比等去世后，他出任知太政官事，与长屋王共同执政，729年长屋王之变时负责审问长屋王。735年他去世，其子大炊王后来即位为淳仁天皇，他被追尊为崇道尽敬皇帝。

en:
Tōyama Kagefusa was a lord of Akechi Castle in Mino Province of the Akechi Tōyama lineage. In July 1331 the Kamakura shogunate confirmed his jitō rights over Akechi and neighboring Ena district holdings; in 1336 he fought for the Ashikaga at Minatogawa, earning two thirds of Ichijima gō in Gujō district.

In 1347 he won the suit over Tamuke gō for Tomokado against Nagai Sadayasu, and in March 1352 his military service earned him an estate in Awa Province. His son Yorikage became jitō in 1390.

远山景房是美浓国明知城主，属明知远山氏一系。1331年7月，镰仓幕府安堵他对惠那郡明知及周边领地的地头职；1336年他在凑川之战中从足利一方参战，因功获赐郡上郡市岛乡三分之二的地头职。

1347年朝廉与长井贞泰争夺手向乡时，他代朝廉一方胜诉；1352年3月又因军功受封安房国领地。1390年，其子赖景继任地头。

en:
Tōyama Kagenaga was a Kamakura-period warrior of Mino and the second head of the Akechi Tōyama, succeeding his father Kageshige at Akechi Castle.

The Azuma Kagami records him at the hōjō-e festival of Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine in 1261, and in 1263 accompanied Shogun Prince Munetaka to Kyoto. In 1272 the bakufu stripped him of his jitō post in favor of Nagai Tokihide. His son Tomokado succeeded him.

en:
Tōyama Kageshige, called Saburōhyōe, was a Kamakura-period warrior of Mino Province and the second son of Tōyama Kagetomo, founder of the Tōyama clan. He inherited the Awaki district, also called Tamuke, in the southern Tōyama manor, and in 1247 built Akechi Castle there.

From that seat he founded the Akechi Tōyama, one of the three leading Tōyama houses alongside the Iwamura and Naegi lines, and was succeeded by his son Kagenaga.

远山景重，通称三郎兵卫，是镰仓时代美浓国武将、远山氏初代景朝的次子。他领有远山庄南部的淡气乡（又称手向乡），于1247年在当地修筑明知城。

他以此为根基开创明知远山氏，与岩村、苗木两家并称远山氏的三大支系，后由其子景长继嗣。

en:
Tōyama Kagetomo was a Kamakura-period warrior and founder of the Tōyama clan in Mino. The eldest son of Yoritomo's retainer Katō Kagekado, he inherited the Tōyama manor, took the Tōyama name, and ruled from Iwamura Castle.

In 1203 he and his father killed Nitta Tadatsune after the Hiki purge. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he led the fifty-thousand-strong Tōsandō army to Kyoto, and on Hōjō Yasutoki's order beheaded Ichijō Nobuyoshi at Iwamura. Records last mention him in 1249–1256.

en:
Tōyama Tomokado was a lord of Akechi Castle in Ena district, Mino Province, and a head of the Akechi Tōyama lineage. In 1333 the court issued him an edict granting Tamuke gō, and in 1336 he took service under Ashikaga Takauji.

In March 1339 he received one half of Tamuke gō and in December the other half. In 1347 he disputed its possession with Nagai Sadayasu, and the suit ended in his favour through his kinsman Kagefusa.

zh:
远山朝廉是美浓国惠那郡明知城主、明知远山氏当主。1333年，朝廷下纶旨将手向乡宛行于他；1336年他投效足利尊氏。

1339年3月他领有手向乡的一半，同年12月又获宛行另一半。1347年，他与长井贞泰就手向乡的领有权发生争议，经同族景房代表诉讼，朝廉一方胜诉。

en:
Toshima Aritsune was a Kamakura-era warrior of the Musashi Toshima clan and provisional governor of Kii. In August 1184, serving under Minamoto no Yoshitsune, he occupied the Denbōin manor at Negoro-ji in Kii and levied troops and provisions on its peasants; the Kamakura regime had already made him Kii's military governor.

In 1189 he attended Yoritomo's service at Tsurugaoka Hachiman. In 1191 the bakufu ended his jitō rights over Mikami manor after a court suit, but gave him replacement land.

zh:
丰岛有经是镰仓时代武将，出身武藏国丰岛氏，官居纪伊权守。1184年8月，他随源义经进驻纪伊国根来寺的传法院领，向庄民征发兵役与粮米，镰仓政权此时已任命他为纪伊守护人。

1189年他供奉源赖朝参拜鹤冈八幡宫。1191年，因朝廷方面的诉讼，幕府停止了他对三上庄的地头职，但另给替地作为补偿。

en:
Toshima Kagemura was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Southern and Northern Courts period, lord of Shakujii Castle in Musashi Province. Genealogies record that after his elder brother Yasukage died he held the family headship while his nephew Tomoyasu was a child.

After the Nakasendai War of 1335 he is said to have sheltered Hōjō Tokiyuki and adopted his son Terutoki. Tradition makes him a Southern Court follower under Nitta Yoshisada who later returned the headship to Tomoyasu.

丰岛景村是镰仓后期至南北朝时代的武将，担任武藏国石神井城主。据丰岛氏系图记载，兄长泰景死后，因侄朝泰年幼，由他继任家督。

相传1335年中先代之乱后，他藏匿败逃的北条时行，并收时行之子辉时为养子。系图称他追随新田义贞效忠南朝，待朝泰成人后又归还家督。

en:
Toshima Kiyomoto was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods and head of the Toshima clan of Musashi, a house long in the Minamoto's service. In 1177 he donated a new main hall to Katori Shrine in Shimōsa.

After Minamoto no Yoritomo's defeat at Ishibashiyama in 1180, Kiyomoto and his son Kasai Kiyoshige joined Yoritomo's army and became gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate. In 1189 the pair fought in the Ōshū campaign against the Northern Fujiwara.

zh:
丰岛清元是平安末期至镰仓初期的武将、武藏国丰岛氏当主，其家族世代为源氏家人。1177年，他为下总国香取神社造进正神殿。

1180年源赖朝在石桥山之战败北后，清元与儿子葛西清重投奔赖朝，镰仓幕府开创后列为御家人。1189年，父子二人参加讨伐奥州藤原氏的奥州合战。

en:
Toshima Terutoki, first called Kotarō Kagehide, is a warrior of the Southern and Northern Courts period known only from the Toshima genealogy and a temple necrology. They make him a son of Hōjō Tokiyuki, sheltered by the Toshima after his defeat in 1335; the childless Kagemura adopted him as heir.

He is said to have held junior fifth rank, met the Kamakura kubō Ashikaga Motouji and received permission to inherit the headship, and founded Dōjōji as the Toshima family temple in 1372. Modern scholars doubt the story.

丰岛辉时（初名小太郎景秀）是南北朝时代的武将，事迹仅见于《泰盈本丰岛氏系图》和道场寺过去账。系图称他是北条时行之子：1335年时行在中先代之乱中败逃，受到丰岛景村庇护，无子的景村遂收他为养子以继家督。

相传他官至从五位下，后谒见镰仓公方足利基氏，获许继承家业，1372年创建道场寺作为丰岛氏菩提寺。近代学者多怀疑这一传说。

en:
Toshima Tomotsune, called Tarō, was an early Kamakura gokenin and heir of Toshima Kiyomoto, head of the Musashi Toshima clan. In July 1201 he was appointed shugo of Tosa Province, and Hōjō Tokimasa's letter orders him to enforce a jitō grant there.

In August 1203 he was replaced as shugo by Miura Yoshimura. That November he fought Enryaku-ji's warrior monks on Mount Hachiōji near Kyoto and fell in the shogunate assault of 20 November, one of three hundred dead the Azuma Kagami records.

丰岛朝经，通称太郎，是镰仓幕府初期的御家人、武藏豪族丰岛氏当主清元的嫡子。1201年7月，他出任土佐国守护，北条时政致他的文书命其在当地执行地头职的授封。

1203年8月，土佐守护之职由三浦义村接替。同年11月比叡山僧兵据守京都附近的八王子山，朝经在11月20日幕府军的攻打中战死，《吾妻镜》载此役共有三百人阵亡。

en:
Toshima Yasuie, known as Saburō, was a Heian-period local magnate of southern Musashi Province, from the Taira-surnamed Chichibu line that produced the Toshima clan. The son of Toshima Tsuneie, he took a daughter of Chichibu Shigehiro as wife for his son Kiyomoto, and when his daughter wed Fujiwara Tōkane he gave her part of Adachi District.

By the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 Kiyomoto led the clan for Minamoto no Yoshitomo. Yasuie is also named as founder of Seikōji temple.

丰岛康家（通称三郎）是平安时代武藏国南部的地方豪族，出自赐平姓的秩父氏一脉，即丰岛氏所属的家族。他是丰岛常家之子，为儿子清元娶了秩父重弘之女；女儿嫁给藤原远兼时，又把足立郡的一部分分给女儿。

到1156年保元之乱时，其子清元已率一族在源义朝麾下参战。此外，清光寺也有以他为开基祖的说法。

en:
Tō no Shigetane (1177–1247) was the second head of the Tō clan and a trusted attendant of Kamakura Shogun Minamoto no Sanetomo. He succeeded his father Taneyori around 1190, and in 1199 joined the sixty-six gokenin signing the impeachment of Kajiwara Kagetoki.

A waka poet, he joined Sanetomo's inner circle; in 1206 the shogun sent him poems urging his return from Higashi Manor to Kamakura. After Sanetomo's assassination in 1219 he took vows and yielded the headship to his son Taneyuki.

东重胤（1177—1247）是东氏第二代当主，镰仓幕府将军源实朝的侧近。他约在1190年前后从父亲胤赖手中继承家督，1199年梶原景时之变时，列名于六十六名御家人联名弹劾的状纸。

他身为歌人，得到实朝宠信，入为近习。1206年他回下总国东庄久居不归，实朝特意赠和歌催他返回镰仓。1219年实朝遇刺后，他出家为僧，把家督让给儿子胤行。

他身为歌人，得到实朝宠信，入为近习。1206年他回下总国东庄久居不归，实朝特意赠和歌催他返回[ShowLocationName('kamakura')]。1219年实朝遇刺后，他出家为僧，把家督让给儿子胤行。

en:
Tō no Taneyori (1155–1228), called Tō Rokurō Daibu, was the sixth son of Chiba Tsunetane and ancestor of the Tō and Endō houses. At Prince Mochihito's rising in 1180, serving as a capital guard, he brought word of it to Minamoto no Yoritomo in Izu.

In the Genpei War he urged his father to join Yoritomo and destroyed the Shimōsa deputy's force. He held Higashi Manor in Shimōsa, was famed for his waka, and ended as a disciple of Hōnen; in 1227 he helped guard the transfer of Hōnen's remains during the Karoku persecution.

zh:
东胤赖（1155—1228），通称东六郎大夫，是千叶常胤的第六子，东氏与远藤氏的始祖。1180年以仁王举兵时，他正在京都担任大番役，事后赶赴伊豆，把举兵的消息报给源赖朝。

治承·寿永之乱中，他力劝父亲投奔赖朝，并参与攻灭下总目代。他领有下总国东庄，以和歌见长；晚年拜在法然上人门下，1227年嘉禄法难时参加了护送法然遗骸移葬的行动。

en:
Tō no Taneyuki, also called Sosen, was the third head of the Tō clan and founder of its Gujō branch in Mino Province. A waka poet like his father Shigetane, he served four successive Kamakura shoguns and won Yamada Manor in Gujō for his Jōkyū War service in 1221.

In 1233 he visited Fujiwara no Teika, seeking in vain a place in the new imperial anthology. In the Hōji Conflict of 1247 he stormed Chiba Hidetane's stronghold in Kazusa and saved his maternal grandson.

东胤行，法名素暹，是东氏第三代当主，也是美浓国郡上东氏的开祖。他和父亲重胤一样是歌人，先后出仕四代镰仓将军，因1221年承久之乱的军功获封郡上的山田庄。

1233年，他拜访藤原定家，希望自己的和歌入选新的敕撰集，却被定家称病拒见。1247年宝治合战时，他参加攻打上总国千叶秀胤据点的战斗，并以战功换得自己外孙活命。

en:
Tō no Ujimura was the fourth head of the Tō clan of Gujō in Mino Province, a warrior house descended from the Chiba clan. His father Taneyuki had been enfeoffed with Yamada Manor in Gujō for his service in the Jōkyū War of 1221.

Early in the fourteenth century Ujimura moved the clan's seat from Achiba Castle, and the Yamato village history records that Shinowaki Castle was completed under him, becoming their residence. He died in 1377.

东氏村是美浓国郡上东氏的第四代当主，该族是出自千叶氏的武家。其父东胤行因1221年承久之乱的军功受封郡上的山田庄。

14世纪初，氏村把据点从阿千叶城迁出；据《大和村史》记载，筱胁城在他任内正式完工，成为一族居城。他于1377年去世。

en:
Akahashi Tōshi (1306–1365) was the legal wife of Ashikaga Takauji, founder of the Muromachi shogunate. Born into the Hōjō regent house of Akahashi, she married Takauji and bore their eldest son Yoshiakira in 1330. In 1333 she and the boy were held hostage in Kamakura and narrowly escaped when Nitta Yoshisada overthrew the Hōjō.

In 1340 she bore Takauji's son Motouji, the first Kamakura kubō. Widowed in 1358 she took the veil and died in 1365 aged sixty, posthumously granted junior first rank.

赤桥登子（1306—1365）是室町幕府开创者足利尊氏的正室。她出身把持镰仓幕府执权之职的北条氏赤桥流，嫁给尊氏，1330年生下嫡男义诠。1333年她与幼子作为人质留在镰仓，新田义贞攻灭北条氏时母子险些遇难，侥幸逃脱。

1340年她又生下后来的初代镰仓公方足利基氏。1358年尊氏去世后她落发出家，1365年去世，享年60岁，追赠从一位。

en:
Genealogies name Taira no Hidemori, later called Tozawa Hidemori, as founder of the Tozawa clan and a son of Taira no Michimasa of the Kammu Heike. He first served Kiso Yoshinaka, then withdrew to the Shizukuishi manor in Iwate district, Mutsu.

In 1185 he submitted to Minamoto no Yoritomo, fought at Yashima and in the Ōshū campaign, and was enfeoffed with lands in Shizukuishi, taking the name Tozawa from his settlement there. Modern scholars suspect he was really a local retainer of the Northern Fujiwara.

en:
The Hankanfu genealogy makes Tozawa no Kanemori the second head of the Tozawa clan and a son of the founder Hidemori. In 1206, pressed by the Nanbu clan, he left the Shizukuishi manor in Mutsu and withdrew west across the Ōu Mountains to Kadoya-kodate in Dewa.

In 1220 he moved his seat from Kadoya-kodate to Kadoya, and in 1228 built Kadoya Castle, planting the clan in Dewa, from which it later grew powerful around Kakunodate.

en:
Tsuchimikado (1196–1231), the eldest son of Emperor Go-Toba, was placed on the throne in 1198 at the age of two when his father abdicated; Go-Toba held real power. In 1210 Go-Toba made him yield the throne to his younger brother Juntoku, who favored overthrowing the shogunate.

He took no part in the Jōkyū War of 1221, yet after its failure he asked to share his father's punishment and was exiled to Tosa and then Awa. He died in Awa in 1231, aged thirty-five.

zh:
土御门天皇（1196—1231）是后鸟羽天皇的长子，1198年父亲让位时，年仅两岁的他登基，实权由后鸟羽上皇以院政掌握。1210年，后鸟羽偏爱更赞同倒幕的守成亲王，迫使他让位给弟弟顺德天皇。

en:
Nobue Tsuchimochi was a warrior of the Agata-Tsuchimochi house of northern Hyūga who fought for Ashikaga Takauji and the Northern Court in the Kenmu wars. In the twelfth month of 1335 his men stormed the Mukasa-in manor office, where Itō Sukihiro had barricaded himself.

His own battle report, the Tsuchimochi Nobue gunchūjō issued in 1336, is the first record of Mukasa Castle. In 1336 he defended Takauji's private fief of Mukasa-in against Sagara Yorihiro's attack.

土持宣荣是日向北部县土持氏的武士，在建武年间的战乱中为足利尊氏和北朝效力。1335年十二月，他率部攻打穆佐院政所，将据守于此的伊东祐广逐出。

en:
Tsuchimochi Nobutsuna, called Tarō, was head of the Tsuchimochi warrior family of northern Hyūga Province. Under him the clan, remembered as the Seven Tsuchimochi Heads, held sway over seven strongholds including Agata, Takarabe and Obi.

They strengthened ties with the Kusakabe, Hyūga's long-serving local officials, and acquired their offices and interests. As a Kamakura shogunate vassal he held steward rights over Usa Hachiman lands; the 1197 Hyūga cadastral register lists his holdings at 1436 chō.

土持宣纲（通称太郎）是日向国北部武士家族土持氏的当主。在他的时代，全族号称“土持七头”，在县、财部、饫肥等七处要地称雄。

土持氏加强与世代担任日向在国司的日下部氏的关系，取得其官职和权益。镰仓幕府时代他成为御家人，领有宇佐八幡宫庄园的地头职权，据1197年的《日向国图田帐》记载，其名下领地达1436町。

en:
Prince Tsuneyoshi (1325–1338?) was the eldest son of Emperor Go-Daigo by his favourite consort Ano Renshi. Named crown prince in 1334, he was escorted north by Nitta Yoshisada to Kanagasaki Castle in Echizen after Ashikaga Takauji's victory in 1336.

There he issued imperial commands, heading a short-lived Hokuriku court. The castle fell in 1337; the Taiheiki says he was captured and poisoned in Kyoto in May 1338, though he may have survived in the north until around 1346.

恒良亲王（1325—1338？）是后醍醐天皇与宠姬阿野廉子的长子，1334年被立为皇太子。1336年足利尊氏获胜后，新田义贞奉他北上，进入越前金崎城。

他在那里以天皇名义发布纶旨，主持短暂的“北陆朝廷”。1337年金崎城陷；《太平记》称他被俘，于1338年5月在京都被毒杀，但也有迹象表明他可能在北陆活到1346年前后。

en:
Emperor Uda (866–931), personal name Sadami, was Japan's 59th emperor, reigning from 887 to 897. The seventh son of Emperor Kōkō, he was demoted to commoner with the Minamoto surname in 884, then enthroned three years later by Fujiwara no Mototsune.

His attempt to curb Mototsune in the Akō controversy failed, but after 891 he ruled directly, promoted Sugawara no Michizane, and halted the missions to Tang China in 894. He abdicated to his son Emperor Daigo in 897 and died in 931.

zh:
宇多天皇（866—931），名定省，是日本第59代天皇，887年至897年在位。他是光孝天皇的第七子，884年被赐姓源氏、降为臣籍，三年后被藤原基经迎回拥立为帝。

他在阿衡事件中试图压制基经未成，891年起亲政，重用菅原道真，894年废止遣唐使。897年他让位于儿子醍醐天皇，931年去世。

en:
Ueno Giben, first named Yoshiari and called the Ueno Risshi, was a mid-Kamakura warrior and Buddhist monk and ancestor of the Ueno and Hanabusa clans. The eighth son of Ashikaga Yasuuji, he is said to have been adopted by his grandfather Ashikaga Yoshiuji and married a daughter of Kira Nagauji.

He held the jitō office of the Ueno manor, a Hachijō-in estate in Mikawa, giving him standing within the Ashikaga house. His son Hanabusa no Tomimichi died in 1316.

en:
Ueno Yorikane (died 1351) was a Northern and Southern Courts period general of the Ueno clan, a cadet branch of the Ashikaga. In 1336, during Ashikaga Takauji's retreat to Kyushu, he led the attack on Kuroki Castle in Chikugo. As shugo of Iwami he repeatedly fought Southern Court forces.

During the Kannō Disturbance he sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi, who made him shugo of Tajima and Tango in 1351. He followed Tadayoshi north and fell in battle that September.

en:
Nichijō was a monk of the Nichiren sect in the Northern and Southern Courts period, born in Suruga Province as a son of Uesugi Yorishige. His elder sister Kiyoko (c. 1270–1343) was the mother of Ashikaga Takauji, founder of the Muromachi shogunate, making Nichijō the shōgun's uncle.

He founded the sect's Rokujō lineage and wrote the Kamakura Denchū Mondō, recording his master Nichiin's debate victory over every other sect at the palace of the Kamakura shogunate.

zh:
日静是日本南北朝时代日莲宗的僧人，生于骏河国，为上杉赖重之子。其姐清子（约1270—1343）是室町幕府开创者足利尊氏的生母，因此日静是尊氏的舅父。

他开创了日莲宗的六条门流，并撰有《镰仓殿中问答》，记述其师日印在镰仓幕府殿中当众论破各宗派僧人的经过。

en:
Uesugi Noriaki (1306–1368) was a warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts era, founder of the Yamanouchi Uesugi line and the first Kantō kanrei. A cousin of Ashikaga Takauji, he served the Kamakura government and, after his father Norifusa fell in 1336, succeeded him as shugo of Kōzuke. From 1341 he also held Echigo, subduing local Southern Court risings.

He sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi in the Kannō Disturbance and was driven out in 1351. Pardoned in 1361, he became Kantō kanrei in 1363.

zh:
上杉宪显（1306—1368）是日本南北朝时代的武将，山内上杉氏之祖，首任关东管领。他与足利尊氏是表兄弟，早年供职于镰仓将军府；1336年父亲上杉宪房战死后，他继任上野国守护，1341年起又兼任越后国守护，镇压当地的南朝势力。

观应之扰乱中他追随足利直义，1351年失势流亡。1361年获赦，1363年就任关东管领。

en:
Uesugi Norifuji (1318–1338) was a warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts era, son of Uesugi Norifusa and maternal cousin of Ashikaga Takauji and Tadayoshi, and the ancestor of the Inukake Uesugi house. He served Takauji and in 1338 marched with him on Kyoto to stop the Southern Court general Kitabatake Akiie.

On 15 March 1338 he fell in the battle at Watanabe, aged twenty-one. His two infant sons were raised under protection and grew to lead the Inukake house.

上杉宪藤（1318—1338）是日本南北朝时代的武将，上杉宪房之子、足利尊氏与直义兄弟的表弟，犬悬上杉氏之祖。他出仕尊氏，1338年随尊氏上洛，阻击南朝大将北畠显家。

同年3月15日，他在渡边之战中奋战而死，年仅21岁。他留下两个幼子，由人保护长大，后来支撑起犬悬上杉氏一门。

en:
Uesugi Norifusa was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Southern and Northern Courts era, third head of the Uesugi clan and maternal uncle of Ashikaga Takauji. For helping overthrow the Kamakura shogunate he received a jitō post in Izu Province in 1333 and served the Kenmu government.

War resumed and he became shugo of Kōzuke Province to watch Nitta Yoshisada. He marched on Kyoto with Takauji and died fighting at Shijō Kawara on 10 March 1336, covering Takauji's flight to Kyushu. His sons Noriaki and Norifuji founded the Yamanouchi and Inukake Uesugi lines.

zh:
上杉宪房是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，上杉氏第三代当主，也是足利尊氏的母方伯父。他因倒幕有功，于1333年获封伊豆国的地头职，在建武政权供职。

战事再起后，他出任上野国守护，负责牵制新田义贞。宪房随尊氏进军京都，尊氏逃往九州，他于1336年3月10日在四条河原的战斗中为掩护尊氏脱逃而战死。其子宪显、宪藤分别成为山内上杉家与犬悬上杉家之祖。

en:
Uesugi Noriharu (died 1379) was a Nanboku-chō warrior, a son of Uesugi Noriaki who attended the Kamakura kubo Ashikaga Motouji and his son Ujimitsu. In 1368 he helped his brother Yoshinori crush a revolt, and in 1371 he became shugo of Kōzuke, the Yamanouchi Uesugi's home province. He succeeded Yoshinori as Kantō kanrei in 1378.

When Ujimitsu prepared to march on Kyoto during the 1379 Kōryaku Disturbance, Noriharu's remonstrances were ignored, and he killed himself at his Kamakura mansion; Ujimitsu then abandoned the campaign.

上杉宪春（？—1379）是日本南北朝时代的武将，上杉宪显之子，自幼近侍镰仓公方足利基氏、足利氏满父子。1368年他随兄长能宪镇压叛乱立功，1371年被任命为上野守护，即山内上杉氏的根本之地，1378年继任关东管领。

1379年康历政变时，氏满打算上洛，宪春苦苦谏止却不被采纳，遂在镰仓的宅邸自尽，氏满因此放弃出兵。

en:
Uesugi Norikata (1335–1394) was a Muromachi warrior, a son of Uesugi Noriaki, and the founder of the Yamanouchi Uesugi line. In 1376 his brother Yoshinori, dying, passed him the clan headship and the Izu shugo post, and in 1379 Norikata became Kantō kanrei to Ashikaga Ujimitsu.

During his term the kanrei's practice of issuing enforcement orders alongside the kubo's edicts became standard. He led campaigns against the 1380–1382 Oyama Yoshimasa revolt and founded Kamakura's Meigetsu-in temple. He died aged sixty.

zh:
上杉宪方（1335—1394）是日本室町时代初期的武将，上杉宪显之子，开创了山内上杉氏。1376年，兄长能宪在病榻上将山内家督与伊豆守护职传给他；1379年他出任镰仓公方足利氏满的关东管领。

在他任内，管领在公方御教书之外附发施行状的做法成为定例。1380至1382年小山义政之乱时，他曾任讨伐军大将，又是镰仓明月院的开基者。他去世时终年60岁。

en:
Uesugi Norimasa (died 1366) was a Nanboku-chō warrior and heir of his father Uesugi Noriaki. In the Kannō Disturbance he fought for Ashikaga Tadayoshi: he entered Echigo against the Northern Court in 1350, and in 1351 marched into Kai and destroyed Kō no Morofuyu.

Later that year he was defeated by Takauji's army at the Sattatōge Pass. He rose again in Echigo in 1355, then fought on in Shinano, and died in 1366, before his father.

上杉宪将（？—1366）是日本南北朝时代的武将，上杉宪显的嫡子。观应之乱中他为足利直义作战：1350年进入越后与北朝交锋，1351年进军甲斐国，攻灭高师冬。

en:
Uesugi Shigeaki (dates unknown) was a Kamakura-period warrior, the legitimate son of Uesugi Yorishige. Known as Sakon-shōgen and Shuri-daibu, he served a lady in the court of Emperor Fushimi, who reigned from 1287 to 1298.

His sister Kiyoko was the mother of Ashikaga Takauji, so the first Muromachi shōgun was his nephew. One of his waka poems entered the Gyokuyō Wakashū, and he is counted the ancestor of the Ōgigayatsu Uesugi line.

en:
Uesugi Shigefusa was a mid-Kamakura court noble turned warrior and the founder of the Uesugi clan. The second son of the minor Kyoto official Fujiwara no Kiyofusa, he went down to Kamakura in 1252 in the retinue of Shōgun Prince Munetaka and was granted the Uesugi manor in Tanba Province, from which he took his family name.

When the prince returned to Kyoto in 1266, Shigefusa stayed, took up arms in shogunal service, and later served Ashikaga Yasuuji. His daughter, or possibly his sister, married Ashikaga Yoriuji and bore the clan head Ietoki.

上杉重房是镰仓时代中期由公家转为武家的人物，为上杉氏之祖。他是京都下级官员藤原清房的次子，1252年随新任将军宗尊亲王东下镰仓，受领丹波国上杉庄，此后以上杉为姓。

en:
Uesugi Shigeyoshi (died 28 January 1350) was a late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts era warrior and a cousin of Ashikaga Takauji, adopted into the Uesugi from a court-noble family. The Taiheiki says he forged an imperial order to push a hesitant Takauji into battle in 1335, and followed him to Kyushu.

An aide to Ashikaga Tadayoshi, he opposed Kō no Moronao and, after their 1349 showdown, was exiled to Echizen and killed early in 1350. His descendants became the Takuma Uesugi.

zh:
上杉重能（？—1350年1月28日）是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，足利尊氏的表弟。他出身公卿之家，被上杉氏收养；《太平记》记载，1335年他伪造纶旨，促使犹豫不决的尊氏出阵，随后随尊氏西走九州。

en:
Uesugi Tomofusa (1335–c. 1391) was the second head of the Inukake Uesugi line and a Kantō kanrei. His father Uesugi Norifuji fell in 1338, so he and his brother were raised by a retainer under the guardianship of Uesugi Tomosada. Appointed shugo of Tajima, Kazusa and Shinano, he helped crush the Musashi Heikki rising in 1368.

He was made Kantō kanrei jointly with Uesugi Yoshinori to support Ashikaga Ujimitsu, and later campaigned in Shinano and against the Nitta. He then withdrew to Kyoto and died around 1391.

zh:
上杉朝房（1335—约1391）是日本南北朝时代的武将，犬悬上杉氏第二代当主，曾任关东管领。父亲上杉宪藤1338年战死后，他与弟弟由家臣抚育，由上杉朝定监护。他历任但马、上总、信浓三国守护，1368年协助平定武藏平一揆。

随后他与上杉能宪同任关东管领，辅佐镰仓公方足利氏满，又出兵信浓、与新田氏交战。他后退住京都，约1391年去世。

en:
Uesugi Tomomune (c. 1337–1414) was head of the Inukake Uesugi and Kantō kanrei to the Kamakura kubo Ashikaga Ujimitsu and Mitsukane. After his father Norifuji fell in 1338, he and his brother Tomofusa were raised by a clan retainer, and he led the Kamakura forces through the 1380–1382 Oyama Yoshimasa revolt.

In 1395 he became Kantō kanrei and Musashi shugo, resigning in 1405. After Mitsukane died in 1409 he retired to a temple in Kazusa, and died there in 1414 aged seventy-six.

zh:
上杉朝宗（约1337—1414）是南北朝至室町时代前期的武将，犬悬上杉氏当主，先后侍奉镰仓公方足利氏满、足利满兼两代。父亲上杉宪藤1338年战死后，他与兄长朝房由家臣抚育，1380至1382年小山义政之乱中他统率镰仓军出战。

1395年他就任关东管领兼武藏守护，1405年辞任。1409年满兼死后，他退住上总国的寺院，1414年去世，终年76岁。

en:
Uesugi Tomosada (1321–1352) headed the Uesugi clan's Futabashi branch and served as shugo of Tango. After his father Shigeaki died young, he was protected by his aunt Kiyoko, mother of Ashikaga Takauji, and served the brothers. In 1337, aged seventeen, he became Tango shugo, and in 1344 head of the Naidan board.

In the Kannō Disturbance he took Tadayoshi's side and acted as his envoy to Takauji in 1351. He died in 1352; his adopted heir Akisada founded the Ogigayatsu Uesugi line.

上杉朝定（1321—1352）是上杉氏二桥家的当主，曾任丹后国守护。父亲上杉重显早逝后，他由姑母清子（足利尊氏之母）庇护，出仕足利兄弟。1337年，17岁的他被任命为丹后守护，1344年又成为内谈方头人。

观应之乱中他站在直义一方，1351年作为直义的使者与尊氏交涉。1352年他去世，养子上杉显定后来开创扇谷上杉家。

en:
Uesugi Yorinari (died 1346) was a warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts era, a grandson of Uesugi Shigefusa, the clan's founder. He later served as shugodai of Sagami and Tango, and fought across the country in the following of his nephew Ashikaga Takauji.

In 1338 he helped drive Kitabatake Akiie's Southern Court army back from Nara. Through his many sons his bloodline passed into the Ōgigayatsu Uesugi, the Sanuki Nagao and the Hagiwara houses.

en:
Uesugi Yorishige was a mid-Kamakura warrior and the second head of the Uesugi clan, heir of Uesugi Shigefusa. He deepened his house's ties with the Ashikaga: Ashikaga Yoriuji gave him the character 'yori' for his name, and his daughter Kiyoko married Ashikaga Sadauji and became the mother of Takauji and Tadayoshi.

After the Ashikaga overthrew the Kamakura shogunate in 1333, Yorishige served as their house steward. His son Shigeaki founded the Ōgigayatsu line.

en:
Uesugi Yoshinori (1333–1378) was a Nanboku-chō warrior, son of Uesugi Noriaki and adopted heir of Uesugi Shigeyoshi. In the Kannō Disturbance he served Ashikaga Tadayoshi, raising troops in Hitachi. In 1368 he succeeded his father as head of the Yamanouchi Uesugi and shugo of Kōzuke, and with Uesugi Tomofusa served as Kantō kanrei, guiding the kubo Ujimitsu.

en:
Unno Nagauji (died 1243) was a Kamakura-period head of the Unno clan in Shinano Province, a son of Unno Yukiuji, and is named in genealogies among the ancestors of the Sanada clan. He is said to have served the third shogunal regent, Hōjō Yasutoki.

The Shigeno genealogy calls his son Yukiharu 'Sanada Shichirō', the first appearance of the Sanada name, and scholars identify him with the Unno Saemon Tarō named in the Azuma Kagami in 1241.

en:
Unno Yoriyuki was a warrior of the Unno clan, the main Shigeno line in Chiisagata, Shinano. An Edo-period genealogy gives him the title Shinano no Kami and calls him a great-great-grandson of Unno Yukiuji, with a son named Noriyuki. Modern scholars identify him, or perhaps Noriyuki, with the Unno leader Shinano-gon-no-kami Nyudō, who held lands at Aida in 1329.

Shigeno warriors joined Hōjō Tokiyuki's Nakasendai War of 1335, though Unno participation is conjectural. The same genealogy makes him an ancestor of the Sanada clan.

en:
Unno Yukichika (1142–1184) was a Shinano warrior of the Unno clan, the main line of the Shigeno family, and succeeded his elder brother Yukimichi as its head. In the Hōgen War of 1156 he led three hundred cavalry under Minamoto no Yoshitomo.

He joined Kiso Yoshinaka's rising in 1181, followed him to Kyoto, and fought at Mizushima in 1183, where his heir Yukihiro was killed. In early 1184 he fell at the Battle of Awazu with Yoshinaka, and their heads were exposed at Shichijōgawara.

海野幸亲（1142—1184）是信浓国武将、滋野氏嫡流海野氏的当主，继兄长幸通之后统领一族。1156年保元之乱时，他率三百骑兵投奔源义朝麾下。

1181年他响应木曾义仲举兵，随义仲上洛，1183年在水岛之战中嫡子幸广阵亡。1184年初，他与义仲一同战死于粟津之战，首级被悬于七条河原示众。

en:
Unno Yukiuji (born c. 1173), third son of Yukichika, was a Kamakura-period head of the Unno clan. In 1183 he accompanied Kiso Yoshinaka's heir Yoshitaka to Kamakura as a hostage, and when Yoshitaka fled execution the next year he served as his decoy; Yoritomo made him a retainer for his loyalty.

Ranked among the Four Kings of Bow and Horse, he fought in the Wada War of 1213 and the Jōkyū War of 1221, and in 1241 won a land suit against the Takeda in Kōzuke.

en:
Uno Norikage was an early Kamakura-period Murakami Genji warrior in Harima Province. Genealogies such as the Sonpi Bunmyaku relate that his ancestor Minamoto no Suefusa was exiled to Sayo Manor, where the family settled.

During the Kenkyū era of the 1190s Norikage married a daughter of Hōjō Yoshitoki and was appointed jitō of Akamatsu village in Sayo. His heir Ienori took the village's name as his family name and became the first to call himself Akamatsu.

en:
Utsunomiya Fuyutsuna, first named Takafusa, was a son of Utsunomiya Sadatsuna, reportedly adopted into the Buzen Utsunomiya line, and became the seventh head of the Kii clan in Kyushu. He fought for Ashikaga Takauji's Northern Court and was made shugo of Chikugo and Buzen in 1352.

He briefly submitted to the Southern Court in 1355, taking the name Fuyutsuna, then returned to the north. In 1359 he fought Kikuchi Takemitsu and was defeated, after which the Kii clan rapidly declined.

宇都宫冬纲初名高房，是宇都宫贞纲之子，相传被丰前宇都宫氏收为养子，后来成为九州城井氏第七代当主。他初随足利尊氏为北朝效力，1352年受任筑后、丰前守护。

en:
Utsunomiya Kagetsuna (1235–1298), seventh head of the Utsunomiya clan, was a gokenin in the mid-Kamakura shogunate. He served Shogun Prince Munetaka from 1252 and later rose to become governor of Shimotsuke and a member of the Hikitsuke and Hyōjō councils. In 1283 he issued the Utsunomiya house code, modeled on the Goseibai Shikimoku.

As a sworn brother of Adachi Yasumori, he was purged after the 1285 Shimotsuki incident, but returned to office when Taira no Yoritsuna fell in 1293. He died in 1298 aged sixty-four.

宇都宫景纲（1235—1298）是镰仓时代中期的幕府御家人、宇都宫氏第七代当主。1252年起侍奉将军宗尊亲王，后历任下野守、引付众与评定众。1283年，他依据《御成败式目》制定了《宇都宫家弘安式条》。

en:
Utsunomiya Kintsuna (1302–1356) was the ninth head of the Utsunomiya clan of Shimotsuke. In 1333, during the Genkō War, he led the Ki and Sei warrior leagues against Kusunoki Masashige at Shitennō-ji in Settsu, with neither side forcing a direct battle.

After the Kamakura shogunate fell he served Emperor Go-Daigo's Kenmu government, then fought Ashikaga Takauji at Takenoshita in 1335 and later campaigned for the Southern Court under Kitabatake Akiie. His waka poems were collected in the Shinsenzai Wakashū.

en:
Hatta Munetsuna (1086–1162) was a warrior of the late Heian period, counted as the second head of the Utsunomiya clan. Born after the death of his natural father Fujiwara no Kanenaka, he became heir of his mother's husband, the clan founder Fujiwara no Sōen.

Calling himself Hatta Gon no Kami, he held Hatta in Hitachi and drew the Haga clan of Moka under his sway, preparing the clan's advance toward Utsunomiya. He died in 1162 aged seventy-seven, and his heir Tomotsuna made Utsunomiya the clan seat.

en:
Utsunomiya Naritsuna (1156–1192) was the fourth head of the Utsunomiya clan in the early Kamakura period. In 1189 he joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's Ōshū campaign with his father Tomotsuna; by then his son Yoritsuna had been given as a foster son to Oyama Tomomitsu.

Another son, Tomonari, was adopted into the Shioya house and became the ancestor of that branch. Skilled in waka like his sons, Naritsuna died young in 1192, predeceasing his father.

en:
Utsunomiya Sadatsuna (1266–1316), eighth head of the Utsunomiya clan, was a general of the later Kamakura shogunate. He took his name from Hōjō Sadatoki. During the second Mongol invasion of 1281, the Kōan campaign, the regent Hōjō Tokimune named him commander of some sixty thousand gokenin of the Sanyō and San'in circuits, and he led them to Kyūshū.

In 1305 he helped destroy Hōjō Munekata in the Kagen disturbance, and in 1312 he dedicated a great iron stupa in his late mother's memory. He died in 1316 aged fifty-one.

en:
Fujiwara no Sōen (1033–1111) was a late Heian nobleman regarded as the founder of the Utsunomiya clan of Shimotsuke Province. Genealogies make him the second son of Fujiwara no Kanefusa and a great-grandson of the regent Michikane. He served Minamoto no Yoriyoshi and Yoshiie in the Earlier Nine Years' War, earning merit through prayers for victory.

In 1063 he was appointed protector of Shimotsuke and bettō of Futaarayama Shrine, the province's ichinomiya. Tradition credits him with building Utsunomiya Castle. He died in 1111, and Hatta Munetsuna succeeded him.

en:
Utsunomiya Tomotsuna (1122–1204) was the third head of the Utsunomiya clan and a warrior at the court of the retired emperors in Kyoto. After Minamoto no Yoritomo rose in 1180, Taira no Kiyomori detained him in the capital; only in 1184 was he allowed to join Yoritomo. In the 1189 Ōshū campaign he fought with his son Naritsuna, and Yoritomo praised him as the finest bowman in Bandō.

In 1194 the court ordered him placed in the custody of the Bungo provincial government for seizing public land; he was pardoned in 1196 and died in 1204 aged eighty-three.

en:
Utsunomiya Ujitsuna (1326–1370) was the tenth head of the Utsunomiya clan and the son of Kintsuna. Unlike his Southern Court father, he served Ashikaga Takauji: in the Kannō disturbance of 1351 he won victories at Naba and Ashigara, helping decide the Sattayama Pass victory. In 1352 he was made shugo of Kōzuke and Echigo.

After falling out with Kamakura kubō Motouji he lost both posts in 1362. He rebelled again during the Musashi uprising of 1368, surrendered, and died of illness on campaign in Kii in 1370.

en:
Utsunomiya Yasufuji (1302–1352) was a warrior of Shimotsuke Province, son of Mumo Tokitsuna, and a senior retainer of Nitta Yoshisada. In 1335 he fought Ashikaga Takauji at Yamazaki, and in 1336 he fled with Yoshisada to Echizen Province.

When Yoshisada was killed at Fujishima in 1338, Yasufuji wandered the country carrying his lord's severed head, then buried it and became a Lotus sect monk named Renjō in Mikawa Province, where he died in 1352.

en:
Utsunomiya Yasumune was a general of the later Kamakura period, a younger son of Utsunomiya Kagetsuna and brother of the clan head Sadatsuna. He first bore the name Morimune, the character given him by Adachi Yasumori, and is thought to have renamed himself after Yasumori's fall in the 1285 Shimotsuki incident.

When Sadatsuna led the shogunal army against the second Mongol invasion in 1281, Yasumune followed him to Kyūshū and held Ōki Castle in Setaka, Chikugo Province.

His son Tokitsuna inherited Mumo manor in Hitachi Province, while Sadayasu became a land steward in Iyo and laid the foundations of the Iyo and later Chikugo Utsunomiya houses.

His son Tokitsuna inherited Mumo manor in Hitachi Province, while Sadayasu became a land steward in [ShowLocationName('iyo')] and laid the foundations of the Iyo and later Chikugo [ShowDynastyName('utsunomiya_dynasty')] houses.
zh:
宇都宫泰宗是镰仓时代中后期的武将，宇都宫景纲之子、当主贞纲之弟。他初名盛宗，名字拜领自安达泰盛的一字，一般认为在1285年霜月骚动泰盛被诛后改名。

1281年第二次元寇弘安之役时，他随贞纲出征九州，以筑后国山门郡濑高的大木城为据点。

其子时纲领有常陆国武茂庄，贞泰前往伊予国担任地头，奠定了伊予宇都宫氏及后来筑后宇都宫氏的基础。

en:
Utsunomiya Yasutsuna (1202–1260), sixth head of the Utsunomiya clan, was a senior councillor of the Kamakura shogunate and a waka poet. The son of Yoritsuna by a daughter of Hōjō Tokimasa, he took his name from his cousin Hōjō Yasutoki. In 1238 he accompanied Shogun Kujō Yoritsune to Kyoto and became governor of Shimotsuke, and in 1243 he joined the Hyōjōshū council, on which he served until his death.

Fujiwara no Teika praised his verse, many of his poems entering the Gyokuyō Wakashū. He died in Kyoto in 1260, aged fifty-nine.

en:
Utsunomiya Yoritsuna (c. 1178–1259), fifth head of the Utsunomiya clan, was a Kamakura gokenin and noted waka poet. Fostered to Oyama Tomomitsu, he fought in the Ōshū campaign of 1189 and around 1204 became shugo of Iyo Province. In 1205, suspected in the Makishi plot against Shogun Sanetomo, he took vows as Rensei and retired to Ogura in Kyoto.

A close friend of Fujiwara no Teika, he married a daughter to Teika's son Tameie and made the Utsunomiya circle a third center of court poetry. He died in Kyoto in 1259 aged eighty-two.

宇都宫赖纲（约1178—1259）是宇都宫氏第五代当主、镰仓御家人，也是著名歌人。他成为小山政光的犹子，1189年参加奥州合战，约1204年出任伊予国守护。1205年，他因涉嫌卷入牧氏谋害将军源实朝的阴谋而出家，法名莲生，隐居京都小仓。

他与藤原定家交谊深厚，把女儿嫁给定家之子为家，使宇都宫歌坛成为与京都、镰仓并列的和歌中心。1259年在京都去世，享年82岁。

en:
Wachi no Morozane was a head of the Wachi clan, local warriors of Mitaki District in Bingo Province whose houses, with the Eda and other kindred families, were known as the Hirosawa-shū. During the Nanboku-chō wars the Wachi first served Ashikaga Tadafuyu when he based himself in Bingo.

In 1365 the shōgun Ashikaga Yoshiakira ordered Yamauchi Michitsugu and Yano to suppress Morozane at Hiramatsu Castle. By 1367 Yoshiakira had ordered Michitsugu to join Morozane against Yano and Ōta Bizen.

和智师实是备后国三谿郡国人领主和智氏的当主；和智氏与江田氏等同族诸家并称“广泽众”。南北朝动乱中，和智氏起初投身以备后为据点的足利直冬麾下。

1365年，将军足利义诠命山内通继与矢野镇压据守平松城的师实。到1367年，义诠已命通继与师实联手讨伐矢野及太田备前。

en:
Wachi no Sanenari was a Kamakura-period warrior of Bingo province, son of Hirosawa Sanemura, whose family held twelve villages of Mitaki District for service at the Battle of Fujito. He divided his father's lands equally with his elder brother Sanetsuna, took Wachi Manor as his share and adopted the name Wachi, while Sanetsuna's line became the Eda.

In Kangen 1 (1302) the former court lady Go-Fukakusain no Nijō, returning from a pilgrimage to Itsukushima, lodged first at Sanenari's house and then at his brother's, nearly driving the brothers to fight until their cousin Hirosawa Yukizane mediated.

和智实成是镰仓时代备后国的武士，广泽实村之子；其家因藤户之战的军功获赐三谿郡十二乡。他与兄长实纲平分父亲遗领，自取和智庄，遂以和智（和知）为苗字，实纲一脉则称江田氏。

乾元元年（1302年），已出宫的后深草院二条参拜严岛神社后归途中寄寓实成的居馆，随后又转往其兄实纲处，几乎引发兄弟交战，经堂兄广泽行实仲裁方告平息。

en:
Wachi no Sukesane was a head of the Wachi clan, local warriors of Mitaki District in Bingo Province. The clan descended from Kanto gokenin of the Hirosawa family, installed as jitō of Wachi Manor after the founding of the Kamakura shogunate, and took its name from the manor.

During the Nanboku-chō period, Sukesane moved his seat to Kisa, after which the clan made Nantenzan Castle on Mount Nanten above the town its seat.

en:
Wada Kenkai (died 1348), called Wada Shinbōchi in contemporary records, was a Southern Court warrior of the Wada family, a Kusunoki cadet house of Kawachi Province. Kusunoki genealogies make him a son of Kusunoki Masasue, younger brother of Kusunoki Masashige.

He may be the same man as Wada Masaoki, who attacked Tange and Matsubara castles in Ise in 1338. He later followed the Kusunoki leader Masatsura and fell at the Battle of Shijōnawate on 4 February 1348, dying beside his lord.

en:
Waga Yoshiyuki, first called Katta Saburō Saemonnojō, founded the Waga clan of Mutsu province. Oniyanagi genealogies make him the son of Karita Yoshisue, a Kamakura gokenin enfeoffed in Katta district, and the Azuma Kagami names him in 1232.

During the Jōkyū era of 1219 to 1222 he entered Waga district as jitō of half its lands, took the name Waga and seated his main line at Iwasaki in Kuroiwa, now Kitakami; his third son Kageyuki fathered the Susumago branch.

zh:
和贺义行初称刈田三郎左卫门尉，是陆奥国和贺氏的始祖。其庶流鬼柳家所传系图称，他是受封刈田郡的镰仓御家人苅田义季之子；《吾妻镜》1232年正月条载有其名。

承久年间（1219—1222年），他以半郡地头身份进入和贺郡，改称和贺氏，把宗家据点设在黑岩的岩崎，即今岩手县北上市；其三男景行为庶家须孙氏之祖。

en:
Nagahiro Washizu was a warlord and shugo lord of the late Kamakura and Southern and Northern Courts period, born to Ōuchi Hiroie. The Washizu house, a branch of the Ōuchi based at Washizu Manor in Suō Province, had no heir, so the nun Zen'ni adopted him as its successor.

In 1333 Emperor Go-Daigo appointed him shugo of Suō after the Kamakura shogunate fell. In February 1336 he fought for Ashikaga Takauji against the imperial army at Hyōgo, and ruled the Ōuchi as Buzen no Kami. After his death, his second son Hironao inherited the Suō shugo post.

鹫头长弘是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，本为大内弘家之子。鹫头氏是大内氏的分支，领有周防国鹫头庄；宗家后继无人，禅惠尼便收他为养子作为继承人。

en:
Watanabe no Tsuna (953–1025) was a mid-Heian warrior, descended from Emperor Saga through the Saga Genji. Born after his father Minamoto no Atsuru's death, he was adopted by Minamoto no Atsushi and settled at Watanabe in Settsu, taking that place as his surname and becoming ancestor of the Watanabe clan.

He served Minamoto no Yorimitsu as foremost of his Four Heavenly Kings, and in 1020 received the governorship of Tango. Tales credit him with helping slay Shuten-dōji and severing Ibaraki-dōji's arm at Kyoto's Modoribashi bridge with the blade Higekiri.

渡边纲（953—1025）是平安时代中期武将，出自嵯峨源氏，为嵯峨天皇后裔。他是源宛的遗腹子，被源敦收为养子，移居摄津国渡边，以渡边为姓，成为渡边氏之祖。

他出仕源赖光，位列赖光四天王之首，1020年任丹后守。相传他曾随源赖光剿灭酒吞童子，并在京都一条戻桥以名刀髭切斩下茨木童子的一臂。

en:
Yabe Zenni (1187–1256) was a daughter of Miura clan leader Yoshimura. Around 1200 she married Hōjō Yasutoki, future third regent of the Kamakura shogunate, and bore his heir Tokiuji before the couple divorced. She then married Sahara Moritsura and bore three sons; after his death she returned to her Yabe estate and took the religious name Zen'a, becoming known as Yabe Zenni.

Her grandson Hōjō Tokiyori became the fifth regent. In the Hōji Conflict of 1247 her sons sided with the Hōjō, and Moritoki later revived the Miura name. When she died in 1256, Tokiyori mourned fifty days.

矢部禅尼（1187—1256）是三浦氏当主三浦义村之女。约1200年她嫁给后来成为镰仓幕府第三代执权的北条泰时，生下继承人北条时氏，后与泰时离异，改嫁佐原盛连，生有三子。盛连死后她回到矢部乡出家，法名禅阿，称矢部禅尼。

en:
Yamana Masauji was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-cho periods, son of Yamana Yoshitoshi and head of a Yamana branch of the Nitta clan in Kozuke.

When Nitta Yoshisada marched against Ashikaga Takauji in 1335, Masauji refused to follow the Nitta main line and sided with the Ashikaga, his wife's kinsmen. After the Muromachi bakufu was founded in 1336 he went on serving Takauji. The family headship later passed to his son Yamana Tokiuji.

en:
Yamana Moroyoshi (1328–1376) was the eldest son of Yamana Tokiuji and shugo of Tango, Hoki and Tajima. He campaigned against Enya Takasada in 1341 and fought Kusunoki Masatsura in 1347.

When Tokiuji defected to the Southern Court during the Kanno disturbance, Moroyoshi stayed with the Northern Court, fighting at Yawata in 1352. He later rejoined his father, submitting with him in 1363 and inheriting Tango and Hoki.

He became clan head in 1371 and built Utsubuki-yama Castle in Hoki. He died in 1376; with his sons unable to succeed, his brother Tokiyoshi followed him, contributing to a Yamana family feud.

zh:
山名师义（1328—1376）是山名时氏的嫡男，丹后、伯耆、但马三国守护。他参加了1341年讨伐盐冶高贞之役，1347年又与楠木正行交战。

观应之扰乱中，父亲时氏转投南朝，师义却留在北朝，1352年在八幡之战中作战。后来他与父亲合流，1363年一同归顺幕府，领有丹后与伯耆。

1371年他继任家督，在伯耆修筑打吹山城。1376年他去世，因子嗣无力继位而由弟弟时义继任，成为山名一族内讧的原因之一。

en:
Yamana Shigekuni was an early Kamakura-period warrior and gokenin of the Yamana clan of Yamana township in Kōzuke Province, son of Yamana Yoshisada. In October 1185 he was among the mounted retainers who attended Minamoto no Yoritomo at the dedication of Shōchōju-in, taking sixth place in the seven ranks of attendants.

Shōchōju-in was the temple Yoritomo had founded to mourn his father Minamoto no Yoshitomo. His son Yamana Shigemura succeeded him as head of the family.

en:
Yamana Tokiuji (c. 1303–1371) was a Nanboku-cho shugo lord of the Yamana clan. He joined Ashikaga Takauji's break with Emperor Go-Daigo and fought at the Minatogawa in 1336, becoming shugo of Hoki in 1337 and winning further provinces after the 1341 campaign against Enya Takasada.

During the Kanno disturbance he changed sides repeatedly, even occupying Kyoto with Southern Court armies in 1353 and 1354. He submitted to the Muromachi bakufu in 1363 with his sons, receiving Hoki and Tamba. By his death in 1371 the Yamana held five provinces.

山名时氏（约1303—1371）是南北朝时代山名氏的守护大名。他追随足利尊氏与后醍醐天皇决裂，参加1336年的凑川之战，1337年就任伯耆守护，1341年讨伐盐冶高贞后又得到数国领地。

en:
Yamana Yoshinori (died 1219) was a Kamakura-period samurai lord and founder of the Yamana clan. A concubine's son of Nitta Yoshishige of the Seiwa Genji, he held Yamana township in Kōzuke Province, from which he took his name, and around 1175 founded the Yamana Hachiman shrine.

When Minamoto no Yoritomo rose in 1180 Yoshinori joined him, unlike his hesitant father. He fought in the Genpei War, served under Minamoto no Yoshitsune in 1184, was made governor of Izu Province in 1185, and joined the Ōshū campaign of 1189.

en:
Yamana Yoshitada (1337–c. 1408), second son of Yamana Tokiuji, was shugo of Mimasaka and Kii. He became shugo of Mimasaka in 1366 and in 1378 helped crush Hashimoto Shotoku's rising in Kii.

In 1391 his brother Ujikiyo and nephew Mitsuyuki rebelled against Ashikaga Yoshimitsu in the Meitoku War; Yoshitada gave only hesitant assent and never left Kii, yet after the defeat the shogun confiscated both his provinces.

In 1392 Ouchi Yoshihiro drove him to Yura harbour, where he took vows with seventeen kinsmen. Pardoned around 1406, he briefly served as shugo of Iwami.

山名义理（1337—约1408）是山名时氏的次子，美作、纪伊两国守护。1366年他任美作守护，1378年出兵镇压纪伊的桥本正督叛乱。

1391年明德之乱中，弟弟氏清与侄子满幸举兵反抗足利义满，义理虽被说服却始终没有从纪伊出兵；乱后两国仍被没收。

1392年大内义弘攻入纪伊，他逃到由良凑，与十七名族人一同出家。约1406年他获赦免，一度出任石见守护。

Yamashiro Hiroshi was a leader of the Yamashiro house, a branch of the Matsuura warrior bands of Hizen Province. In 1337 Ashikaga Tadayoshi confirmed his stewardship of Yamashiro and other lands in the Uno estate. In 1350 Hiroshi transferred lands including Yamashiro to his eldest son Tsutomu.

During the wars of the Northern and Southern Courts he took the Northern Court side with his kinsmen of the Matsuura party, and in 1359 he fought at the Battle of the Chikugo River in the army of Shōni Yorihisa.

en:
Yamashiro Kakoi was a warrior of the late Heian period and the founder of the Yamashiro house, a branch of the Matsuura bands of Hizen Province.

The sixth son of Matsuura Nao, who held the Mikuriya manor, he established his family at Yamashiro in Matsuura District, backing Minamoto no Mitsusue, steward of the Kanzaki manor. His son Gen'en inherited the Kamachi lands in Chikugo after 1221. Another son, Hiroshi, carried on the Yamashiro line.

zh:
山代围是平安时代末期的武将，肥前国松浦党支族山代氏的始祖。

他是领有御厨庄的松浦直之第六子，在松浦郡山代地方起家；源满末作为神埼庄庄官下向时，即以山代氏的武力为后盾。其子源圆于1221年承久之乱后继承筑后国蒲池氏的遗领，另一子山代广则延续山代氏一脉。

en:
Yamashiro Katashi, also recorded as Minamoto no Tsubura, was an early Kamakura warrior and the third son of Yamashiro Kakoi, founder of the Hizen Yamashiro.

After the Jōkyū War of 1221 he married a daughter of the Kamachi family of Chikugo Province and received its lands, becoming the ancestor of the Kamachi clan. He had no son of his own. The Yamashiro house therefore passed to his nephew and adopted heir Hiroshi.

en:
Yamashiro Sakai was a Hizen Province gokenin of the Yamashiro house, one of the Matsuura warrior bands of northern Kyūshū. In the Kōan campaign of the Mongol invasions in 1281, he fought in the Japanese assault on the Mongol Eastern Route Army on Iki Island, in a host of tens of thousands led by the Matsuura and allied bands.

He fought with distinction there. For his service he received a letter of commendation from Hōjō Tokisada, shugo of Hizen.

zh:
山代荣是肥前国御家人，出自九州北部松浦党的支族山代氏。1281年蒙古来袭弘安之役，日军以松浦党等数万之众，向占据壹岐岛的元军东路军发起总攻，山代荣在壹岐岛之战中奋战。

en:
Taira no Kiyomoto, known as Yoshida no Kiyomoto, was the second son of Taira no Shigemoto, head of the Hitachi Taira; genealogies style him Yoshida Jirō. He settled at Yoshida in Hitachi Province, taking the place name as his surname to found the Hitachi Yoshida house.

He married his daughter to Minamoto no Yoshinari, eldest son of Yoshimitsu, and she bore Satake Masayoshi, first head of the Satake. His descendants founded the Namekata, Kashima and other clans.

en:
Yoshimi Tameyori was a warrior of the early Kamakura period and the founder of the Yoshimi clan of Musashi Province. His grandfather Minamoto no Noriyori, a half-brother of Shōgun Minamoto no Yoritomo, was exiled after a vendetta of 1193 and disappeared.

Tameyori's father Han'en was spared through Hiki no Ama's intercession, took the tonsure, and was granted Yoshimi manor; Tameyori became a Kamakura gokenin, inherited it, and was the first to call himself Yoshimi.

en:
Yoshimi Ujiyori was a Nanboku-cho warrior and shugo of Noto. Around 1348 he succeeded his father Yoshimi Yoritaka in the post, and after a brief interruption he was restored in 1352, holding Noto until 1379. During the Kanno disturbance he followed Ashikaga Takauji.

As a Northern Court commander in Hokuriku he repeatedly fought the Southern Court general Momoi Naotsune in Noto and Etchu. In 1370 he replaced Imagawa Sadayo as head of the Muromachi bakufu's hikitsuke court.

Yoshimi Yoritaka was a Nanboku-cho warrior of the Noto Yoshimi, a branch of the Minamoto, and son of Yoshimi Yorimune. He served as shugo of Etchu from 1336 and in 1337 became shugo of Noto, holding the post until 1346.

In 1344 Inoue Toshikiyo, deposed shugo of Etchu allied with Southern Court forces in Echigo, fought Yoritaka fiercely in Noto until he surrendered in 1346. His son Ujiyori succeeded him around 1348.

en:
Yōmei (c. 540–587), the 31st emperor of Japan, was a son of Emperor Kinmei by Soga no Kitashihime, daughter of Soga no Iname, and thus stood close to the Soga clan. He succeeded his half-brother Bidatsu in 585 amid the feud between the pro-Buddhist Soga and the anti-Buddhist Mononobe, but reigned less than two years, dying in 587.

By his consort Princess Anahobe no Hashihito he fathered Prince Shōtoku, who became the great regent under Empress Suiko and a patron of Buddhism.

zh:
用明天皇（约540—587）是日本第31代天皇，钦明天皇与苏我稻目之女苏我坚盐媛所生之子，与苏我氏关系密切。585年异母兄敏达天皇去世后，他在苏我氏崇佛与物部氏排佛之争愈演愈烈之际即位，在位不足两年，587年病死。

en:
Emperor Yōzei (869–949) was the 57th emperor of Japan, reigning from 876 to 884. The eldest son of Emperor Seiwa, he was named crown prince in infancy and ascended at nine, with his uncle Fujiwara no Mototsune as regent.

In 883 a courtier was beaten to death in the palace amid rumours of his involvement, and in 884 Mototsune deposed him, presenting the abdication as voluntary on grounds of illness. Yōzei then lived sixty-five years as a retired emperor, the longest such retirement, and was known as a waka poet.

阳成天皇（869—949）是日本第57代天皇，876年至884年在位。他是清和天皇的长子，未满周岁即被立为太子，九岁即位，由舅父藤原基经担任摄政。

883年，一名近臣在宫中被殴打致死，坊间传言此事与他有关；884年基经将他废黜，对外称他因病自愿退位。此后阳成以上皇身份生活了六十五年，是有记载以来在任最久的太上皇，以和歌诗人闻名。

en:
Yuasa Munechika, known as Kusumoto Saemon-no-jō, was a late Kamakura gokenin and jitō, or estate steward, of Ategawa manor in Kii Province. In 1275 the manor's peasants submitted a petition accusing him of threatening to cut off their ears and slice off their noses.

Preserved in the Koyasan archives, the complaint is one of medieval Japan's best-known peasant suits. He was the second son of Yuasa Muneuji and father of Yuasa Munekuni.

en:
Yuasa Munefuji was a leader of the Yuasa warrior band of Kii Province, based at Ategawa, and an ally of Kusunoki Masashige. In 1331, on the Kamakura shogunate's orders, he stormed Masashige's castle of Shimo-Akasaka and was made its jitō steward, but in 1332 Masashige retook the castle and Munefuji surrendered.

He then fought for the imperial side in Settsu and Kawachi, crossed to Shikoku in 1340, and in 1352 escorted Emperor Go-Murakami to the Sumiyoshi Shrine. Later tradition numbers him among Masashige's eight chief retainers.

汤浅宗藤是纪伊国汤浅党的有力武士，本据在阿氐河庄，是楠木正成的盟友。1331年，他奉镰仓幕府之命攻打楠木正成据守的下赤坂城，获任命为地头；1332年正成反攻夺回赤坂城，他投降，此后在摄津、河内为朝廷一方作战。

1340年他渡海前往四国，1352年又随侍后村上天皇行幸住吉社。后世将他列为楠公八臣之一。

en:
Yuasa Munemitsu was a Kamakura warrior of Kii Province, seventh son of Yuasa Muneshige. In 1197 Mongaku transferred to him the office of local administrator of Atekawa manor; in 1210 the shogunate confirmed his hereditary office as its land steward. In 1219 suit by Kumano shrine men brought exile to Tsushima, but he was recalled in 1221 and confirmed land steward of Atekawa and other manors, after which he took the name Hota.

Though an illegitimate son, he made his line the leading branch of the Yuasa clan. He later took orders as Jōshin.

汤浅宗光是镰仓时代纪伊国武士，汤浅宗重的第七子。1197年，文觉将阿氐河庄的下司职让给他；1210年，幕府安堵其家族相传的地头职。1219年他被熊野神人控诉，流放对马，1221年被召还，阿氐河庄等地头职得到安堵，此后改称保田氏。

他虽是庶子，却奠定了自己这一支在汤浅一族中的主导地位。他后来出家，法号净心。

en:
Yuasa Muneshige was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods, said to be a son of Fujiwara Munenaga, and lord of Yuasa Castle in Kii Province. In 1143 he built the castle on his Yuasa manor. In 1159 he brought Taira no Kiyomori, on pilgrimage at Kumano, news of the Heiji Disturbance and went up to Kyoto, becoming a captain under him.

After Kiyomori's death he held Yuasa Castle for the Taira before surrendering to Minamoto no Yoritomo, who confirmed his lands in 1186; his following became the Yuasa war band.

汤浅宗重是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将，相传为藤原宗永之子，纪伊国汤浅城之主。1143年，他在汤浅庄修筑汤浅城。1159年平清盛在熊野参拜时，他向清盛报告平治之乱爆发的消息，并随清盛上洛，成为其麾下武将。

清盛死后，他据汤浅城支持平氏，后向源赖朝投降，1186年所领得到安堵；其势力后来被称为汤浅党。

Yuasa Muneuji, also called Ategawa Muneuji, was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Yuasa clan in Kii Province. The third son of Yuasa Munemitsu and grandson of Muneshige, he became jitō of Ategawa manor and founded the Yuasa Ategawa house.

After Myōe died, Muneuji found Kanki-ji in decline and invited Myōe's disciple Kikai to restore it. His son Munechika inherited the office of jitō in 1273.

en:
Yūki Akitomo was the third head of the Shirakawa Yūki clan of Mutsu Province. The eldest son of Yūki Chikatomo, founder of a Komine branch house, he succeeded his grandfather Munehiro as head of the Shirakawa line. He fought for the Northern Court: in 1346 against the Date and Tamura clans, and at Iwakiri Castle in 1351 with Kira Sadaie.

In 1353 Ashikaga Takauji named him magistrate over eight Ōshū districts including Shirakawa, and in 1367 he defeated the rebel Kira Haruie. In 1369 he passed the headship to his adopted heir Mitsutomo.

Yūki Chikatomo was the eldest son of Yūki Munehiro and a warrior of the Shirakawa Yūki clan in Mutsu Province. He fought with his father to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate in 1333 and held office in the Mutsu government under the Kenmu Restoration. In 1340 he built Komine Castle at Shirakawa and founded a Komine branch house.

Though he first served the Southern Court and fought for Kitabatake Chikafusa, in 1343 he defected to the Northern Court in exchange for guarantees of his lands. He died in 1347.

en:
Yūki Hirotsuna (1221–1278) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and the third head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan, succeeding his father Tomohiro in 1255. In 1257 he was appointed a Kebiishi officer in Kyoto, and in 1260 became assistant governor of Kōzuke Province.

Temple tradition calls him founder of the Chōraku-ji, where he devoted himself to the nenbutsu. He died in 1278 and was buried at the Shōmyō-ji in Yūki; his son Tokihiro succeeded him.

en:
Yūki Munehiro (1266–1339) was the second head of the Shirakawa Yūki clan of Mutsu Province. A Kamakura retainer, he answered Emperor Go-Daigo's call in 1333 and stormed Kamakura with Nitta Yoshisada, overthrowing the Hōjō. He then governed the Ōshū lands with Kitabatake Akiie, and in 1336 helped retake Kyoto from Ashikaga Takauji, receiving the sword Onimaru from Go-Daigo.

After Akiie fell in 1338, he sailed from Ise toward Ōshū escorting Prince Noriyoshi, but his ship was wrecked and he died in Ise in 1339.

结城宗广（1266—1339）是陆奥国白河结城氏的第二代当主。他本为镰仓幕府御家人，1333年响应后醍醐天皇的讨幕纶旨，与新田义贞一同攻入镰仓，攻灭北条幕府。建武新政时，他随北畠显家治理奥州，1336年又协助朝廷从足利尊氏手中夺回京都，受后醍醐天皇赐予宝刀鬼丸。

1338年北畠显家战死后，他护送义良亲王从伊势渡海前往奥州，途中遭遇海难，1339年在伊势病逝。

en:
Yūki Naomitsu (1330–1395) was the eighth head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan. He succeeded his brother Naotomo in 1343 at fourteen and served Ashikaga Takauji in the Kannō disturbance. In 1352 he fought the Nitta rising in Kōzuke, and in 1368 he joined Uesugi Noriaki against Nitta Yoshimune in Musashi.

Trusted by three successive shōguns, he expanded the clan into Hitachi and held Awa Province as shugo. He took Buddhist vows in 1358 and died in 1395, leaving the headship to his son Motomitsu; he is credited with writing the Gen'ishū.

结城直光（1330—1395）是下总结城氏的第八代当主，曾任安房国守护。1343年兄直朝战死后，他十四岁继承家督，观应扰乱时站在足利尊氏一方。1352年新田氏在上野国举兵，他加入尊氏方作战；1368年又随上杉宪显讨伐在武藏举兵的新田义宗。

他深受足利尊氏、义诠、义满三代将军信任，将势力扩入常陆，一度担任安房国守护。他于1358年出家，1395年去世，家督由其子基光继承；相传他还是军记《源威集》的作者。

Yūki Naotomo (1325–1343) was the seventh head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan. When his father Tomosuke fell at the Battle of Tatarahama in 1336, he inherited the clan at the age of twelve. He served the Northern Court against the Southern Court Shirakawa Yūki and Seki houses.

In 1343 he joined Kō no Morofuyu's siege of Seki Castle in Hitachi, held by Kitabatake Chikafusa, and on 3 April was mortally wounded in a sortie. He died aged nineteen, leaving no heir, and his younger brother Naomitsu succeeded him.

结城直朝（1325—1343）是下总结城氏的第七代当主。1336年父亲朝祐在多多良滨之战中战死，他以十二岁之龄继承家督，继续依附北朝，与南朝方的白河结城氏、关氏等对立。

en:
Yūki Sadahiro (1289–1309) was a late Kamakura warrior and the fifth head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan. His father Tokihiro died in 1290 when Sadahiro was not yet one year old, so he inherited as an infant and his mother administered the clan's affairs until he came of age.

During his headship the Yūki abandoned Jōdo Shinshū Buddhism and turned to Zen. He died in 1309, aged twenty-one, and his one-year-old son Tomosuke succeeded him.

en:
Yūki Sukehiro was a Kamakura-period warrior and founder of the Shirakawa branch of the Yūki clan. A younger son of Tomohiro, second head of the Shimōsa Yūki, he inherited Shirakawa estates in Mutsu Province, granted to his grandfather after the 1189 Ōshū campaign.

In 1289 he went down to Ōshū and built Shirakawa Castle, establishing his branch; he held only part of the Shirakawa lands, while the main Shimōsa house governed the rest through deputies. His son Munehiro succeeded him.

Yūki Tomohiro (1190–c. 1274), a Kamakura-period warrior, was the second head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan, succeeding his father Tomomitsu. In the 1221 Jōkyū War he commanded on the Hokuriku road and won distinction in Etchū Province, afterward becoming a guards captain.

He later served as a Kebiishi officer in Kyoto, and in 1242 was appointed assistant minister of the treasury. His long headship saw the heyday of the Yūki clan; his son Hirotsuna succeeded him.

Yūki Tomomitsu (1168–1254), third son of Shimotsuke chieftain Oyama Masamitsu, founded the Shimōsa Yūki clan. In 1180 his mother presented him to Minamoto no Yoritomo, who presided over his coming-of-age. He fought at Uji in 1184 and Dannoura in 1185, and in the 1189 Ōshū campaign slew enemy general Hidetsuna at Atsukashiyama, winning the three districts of Shirakawa.

In 1199 he led sixty-six gokenin in the petition overthrowing Kajiwara no Kagetoki, commanded in the 1221 Jōkyū War, and joined the shogunate Council of State in 1235, later taking vows.

en:
Yūki Tomosuke (1308–1336) was the sixth head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan, succeeding his father Sadahiro in 1309. As a Kamakura gokenin he first used the name Tomotaka, the character taka granted by Hōjō Takatoki, and served in the 1331 siege of Kasagi Castle under Ashikaga Takauji before turning against the Hōjō.

He then renamed himself Tomosuke, but the Kenmu government favored his Shirakawa kinsmen, so he joined Takauji's Northern Court. He fought at Hakone and Takenoshita in 1336, followed Takauji to Kyushu, and fell at Tatarahama.

en:
Beatrice of Brandenburg (c. 1270–before 1316) was a German princess of the Brandenburg Ascanians, the second daughter of Margrave Otto V the Tall and Judith of Henneberg. Her betrothal to Bolko I the Strict, Duke of Świdnica, was celebrated in 1279 and their church wedding followed in Berlin in 1284. She bore Bolko ten children.

After Bolko's death in 1301, either she acted as regent for their minor sons with the support of her brother Margrave Herman, or Herman acted as regent on their behalf. By 1308 she had remarried Duke Władysław of Koźle-Bytom-Siewierz, by whom she had two more children.

Bolesław II the Horned (c. 1220–1278) was a Silesian Piast, son of Henry II the Pious. He succeeded when his father fell fighting the Mongols at Legnica in 1241, but soon lost Kraków and other lands. In 1248 he divided Lower Silesia and took Legnica.

He was excommunicated for jailing the Bishop of Wrocław and did penance in 1261. In 1277, allied with Rudolf of Germany, he captured Henry IV of Wrocław and won at Stolec. He died in December 1278, leaving Henry V, Bolko I and Bernhard; his son Henry V succeeded him.

Bolko I the Strict (1252/1256–1301) was a Silesian Piast, second son of Bolesław II the Horned of Legnica. After his father died in 1278 he inherited Jawor and ruled it alone from 1281.

Excommunicated in 1294, he defended his towns against King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia in 1295 and made his duchy a papal fief in 1299. He promoted German settlement and founded the Cistercian Krzeszów Abbey, where he was buried after his death on 9 November 1301.

Henry I of Jawor (c. 1294–1346) was a Silesian Piast duke, the third son of Bolko I the Strict and Beatrice of Brandenburg. After his father's death in 1301 he ruled jointly with his brothers until the 1312 partition gave him Jawor and Lwówek.

In 1319, when the Brandenburg Ascanians died out, he occupied eastern Lusatia and married Agnes, daughter of King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia. In 1337 he exchanged his Lusatian lands for the Duchy of Głogów and did homage to John of Bohemia. He died in 1346 and was buried at Krzeszów Abbey.

Jean-Baptiste de Machault, comte d'Arnouville (1701–1794), was a French statesman born in Paris. He was appointed Controller-General of Finances in December 1745, when France was deep in debt from the War of the Austrian Succession.

In 1749 he proposed the vingtième, a tax of one twentieth to be paid by all landowners including the clergy and nobility, but privileged opposition forced the plan's failure. Dismissed in 1757 after moving to the Naval Ministry, he died in a Paris revolutionary prison in 1794, aged ninety-two.

Jean Bureau (c. 1390–1463), born in Champagne, trained as a lawyer in Paris before he and his brother Gaspard offered their services as gunners to Charles VII in 1434. By 1439 Jean was master gunner of French artillery, and their batteries shaped the Normandy campaign of 1449–1450, from the fall of Rouen to the victory at Formigny.

In 1453 Bureau deployed 300 guns at Castillon, where cannon fire destroyed John Talbot's army and effectively ended the Hundred Years' War, after which he forced Bordeaux to surrender. He was knighted in 1461.

en:
Jean-Baptiste Colbert (1619–1683) was a French statesman born in Reims to a merchant family. In 1652 he managed the affairs of the exiled Mazarin, to whom he reported that less than half the taxes paid reached the king.

Recommended to Louis XIV by Mazarin, he became intendant of finances in 1661, helped destroy Nicolas Fouquet, and was Controller-General of Finances from 1665 and Navy Secretary from 1669.

His mercantilist program, later called Colbertism, reformed taxation, set up royal manufactures, chartered the East India Company in 1664, and expanded France's navy and colonies. He founded the Academy of Sciences in 1666 and died in 1683.

en:
Juan de Beaumont (1419–1487) was prior of the Order of St John in Navarre and royal chancellor from 1434. From 1432 he was tutor and chief counsellor to Charles, Prince of Viana.

As leader of the Beaumont faction he backed Charles against the prince's father John II of Aragon in the Navarrese Civil War and was imprisoned after the defeat. He later joined the Catalan civil war, briefly ruling Catalonia as viceroy for Henry IV of Castile before defecting to the royalists in 1464, and died in 1487.

Jean de Fontaney (1643–1710) was a French Jesuit mathematician. At Louis XIV's request, following an appeal from the Beijing missionary Ferdinand Verbiest, he set out with five scientifically trained Jesuits.

One remained in Siam, while the other four accompanied him to China. They reached Beijing in February 1688 and were received by the Kangxi Emperor, who kept Bouvet and Gerbillon at court. He returned to France in 1703 and died at La Flèche in 1710.

Jean d'Orléans (1402–1468), called the Bastard of Orléans and later Jean de Dunois, was the illegitimate son of Louis I, Duke of Orléans. While his half-brother was held captive in England after Agincourt, he led the House of Orléans in the Dauphin's service.

He defended Orléans and relieved the city with Joan of Arc in 1429. He helped retake Paris in 1436 and led the reconquest of Normandy and Guienne in its final phase. He died in 1468, after joining the League of the Public Weal against Louis XI in 1465.

He defended Orléans and relieved the city with Joan of Arc in 1429. He helped retake [ShowLocationName('paris')] in 1436 and led the reconquest of [GetCountry('NRM').GetName] and Guienne in its final phase. He died in 1468, after joining the League of the Public Weal against Louis XI in 1465.
zh:
让·德·奥尔良（1402—1468），人称“奥尔良的私生子”，后称让·德·迪努瓦，是奥尔良公爵路易一世的私生子。同父异母的兄长在阿金库尔战役后被英军囚禁，他遂以王太子麾下奥尔良家族之首的身份参战。

他守卫奥尔良城，1429年与贞德合力为该城解围。1436年他协助收复巴黎，并在战争最后阶段率军收复诺曼底与吉耶讷。1465年他加入反对路易十一的“公益同盟”，1468年去世。

en:
Martanda Cinkaiariyan (r. 1325–1348) was an early Aryacakravarti king of Jaffna, taking the throne name Pararasasekaram III. He put down revolts by the Vanniyar chieftains of the kingdom's interior, promoted agriculture and learning, and kept Jaffna in prosperous commerce with Yemen.

Around 1344 the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta visited his court and recorded that the king accompanied him up the sacred peak of Sivanoli Padam Malai. Martanda left several inscriptions and was succeeded by his son Gunabhushana Cinkaiariyan.

马坦达·辛凯阿里扬（1325—1348年在位）是贾夫纳阿梨耶遮迦罗跋帝王朝早期国王，王号帕拉拉塞卡兰三世。他平定王国内地万尼耶酋长的叛乱，推动农业与学术，并维持贾夫纳与也门之间繁荣的贸易。

约1344年，摩洛哥旅行家伊本·白图泰到访其宫廷，记载国王陪同他登上西沃诺利帕达马莱圣山。马坦达留下数方铭文，死后由其子古纳布沙那·辛凯阿里扬继位。

en:
Arghun Shah was chief of the Ja'un-i Qurban tribe of Khurasan and the most powerful amir of the Ilkhanid claimant Togha Temür. In 1337 he abandoned Togha Temür's western campaign, captured and executed the governor Shaykh Ali Qushji, then reconciled with the khan and helped clear Khurasan of Jalayirid forces.

When the Sarbadars invaded in 1340 he was driven from Nishapur to Tus. He died in 1345 or 1346, after which his tribe abandoned Togha Temür's cause.

阿鲁浑·沙是呼罗珊札兀尼·库尔干部落的首领，也是伊利汗位争夺者脱合帖木儿麾下最有权势的异密。1337年，他退出脱合帖木儿的西征，擒杀呼罗珊长官谢赫·阿里·库什吉，随后与汗和解，协助把札剌亦儿势力逐出呼罗珊。

1340年萨尔巴达尔人来攻，他从内沙布尔退守图斯。他死于1345或1346年，此后札兀尼·库尔班便抛弃了脱合帖木儿的事业。

en:
Kanhadadeva (r. c. 1292–1311) was a Chahamana king who ruled Javalipura, modern Jalore in Rajasthan. From 1296 he shared power with his father Samantasimha, becoming sole ruler around 1305. In 1299 he refused Alauddin Khalji's army passage through his lands on its Gujarat campaign, and later bardic chronicles credit him with recovering the Somnath idol from the Delhi forces.

After Alauddin's conquests isolated Jalore, a strong Delhi army under Malik Kamaluddin Gurg stormed the fort in 1311 and killed Kanhadadeva. His son Viramadeva survived him only days.

坎哈达德瓦（约1292—1311年在位）是乔汉（查哈马纳）王朝国王，统治阇瓦利普拉，即今拉贾斯坦邦的贾洛尔。自1296年起他与父亲萨曼塔辛哈共同执政，约1305年独掌大权。1299年，他拒绝阿拉丁·卡尔吉出征古吉拉特的大军借道领地；后世吟游史书称他从德里军中夺回了索姆纳特神像。

阿拉丁的连年征服使贾洛尔陷入孤立，1311年马利克·卡马鲁丁·古尔格率德里大军攻陷城堡，斩杀坎哈达德瓦，其子毗罗摩提婆继位仅数日便死去。

en:
Adityawarman (c. 1294–c. 1375) was the last powerful ruler of the Mauli dynasty in central Sumatra. The Javanese chronicle Pararaton places his birth at Trowulan, capital of Majapahit; his father was the nobleman Adwayawarman and his mother Dara Jingga, a Malay princess of Dharmasraya.

As a senior minister of Majapahit, he helped direct its conquest of Sumatra's east coast, then in 1347 set up his own court at Malayapura near Pagaruyung and controlled the Minangkabau gold trade.

A patron of Tantric Buddhism, he last appears in an inscription of 1375 and was succeeded by his son Ananggawarman.

阿迪蒂亚瓦尔曼（约1294—约1375）是苏门答腊中部茂利王朝最后一位强有力的统治者。据爪哇古籍《君王记》记载，他出生于满者伯夷首都多乌兰，父亲是贵族阿德瓦亚瓦尔曼，母亲是达尔马斯拉耶的马来公主达拉·金佳。

他曾任满者伯夷重臣，参与征服苏门答腊东海岸，1347年在帕加鲁永附近的马来普拉建立朝廷，掌控米南加保的黄金贸易。

他崇奉密宗佛教，1375年最后一次见于铭文记载，之后由其子阿南加跋摩继位。

Adwayawarman was a Javanese nobleman of the late Singhasari and early Majapahit period, named in West Sumatran inscriptions as the father of King Adityawarman of Malayapura. The historian Slamet Muljana identified him with Adwayabrahma, the minister who in 1286 escorted the Amoghapasha statue to Dharmasraya on the Pamalayu expedition.

The Javanese chronicle Pararaton names Dewa as the husband of the Malay princess Dara Jingga, brought to Java from Sumatra; his identification with Adwayawarman remains conjectural.

en:
Akarendrawarman was a king of the Malay kingdom in Sumatra who succeeded Tribhuwanaraja Mauli Warmadewa in 1316 and ruled until 1347, when his nephew Adityawarman followed him. He is named in the Pagaruyung VII inscription with a long imperial title, and the inscription places his realm at Parhyangan on Mount Marapi.

The Suruaso inscription credits him with beginning an irrigation canal for the rice lands at Surawasa, a work completed by Adityawarman.

en:
Dara Jingga was a princess of the Malay kingdom of Dharmasraya in Sumatra, the daughter of King Tribhuwanaraja and elder sister of Dara Petak, who married the founder of Majapahit. After Singhasari's Pamalayu expedition of 1275–1293, she and her sister were taken to Java to be offered in marriage to King Kertanegara.

On Kertanegara's death her sister married his heir Raden Wijaya, while Dara Jingga married a nobleman called Dewa, conjecturally identified with Adwayawarman. She was the mother of Adityawarman, later ruler of Malay Sumatra, and her name means scarlet dove in old Malay.

达拉·金佳是苏门答腊末罗瑜达摩室利耶王国的公主，国王特里布瓦纳拉贾之女，也是嫁给满者伯夷开国君主的达拉·佩塔的姐姐。1275—1293年信诃沙里发动巴马拉尤远征后，她与妹妹被带往爪哇，原本要进献给国王克塔纳伽拉为妃。

克塔纳伽拉死后，妹妹嫁给继位的罗登·韦查耶，达拉·金佳则嫁给贵族德瓦，有人推测德瓦即阿德瓦亚瓦尔曼。她是后来统治苏门答腊末罗瑜的阿迪蒂亚瓦尔曼之母，其名在古马来语中意为“猩红色的鸽子”。

en:
Sri Maharaja Tribhuwanaraja Mauliwarmadewa was king of Dharmasraya in Bhumi Malayu, the Malay kingdom in Sumatra, and is named on the Padang Roco inscription of 1286. That year, after Singhasari's Pamalayu expedition reached Sumatra, he accepted a stone Amoghapasa statue from King Kertanegara of Java, a gift possibly affirming vassalage or friendship between the kingdoms.

Javanese chronicles make him the father of princesses Dara Jingga and Dara Petak; after Singhasari fell, Dara Petak married the Majapahit founder Raden Wijaya and bore King Jayanagara.

en:
Khengara (r. 1331–1351) was a Chudasama king of Saurashtra whose capital was Junagadh; he succeeded his father Mahipala I. He expelled the Muslim governors from Somnath and Prabhas Patan and restored the decayed Somnath temple.

After sheltering Taghan, a rebel against Delhi Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq, he saw Junagadh besieged and captured in 1350; he was taken prisoner but soon released. Inscriptions credit him with conquering eighteen coastal islands and patronizing music, and he died in 1351, followed by his son Jayasimha I.

肯伽罗（1331—1351年在位）是索拉什特拉的珠多娑摩国王，定都朱纳格特，继父亲摩希波罗一世即位。他将穆斯林长官逐出索姆纳特和帕巴斯帕坦，修复了破败的索姆纳特神庙。

他收容反叛德里苏丹穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克的塔甘后，朱纳格特于1350年遭到围攻并被攻陷；他本人被俘但很快获释。铭文称他征服了沿海十八岛，并热心赞助音乐。他于1351年去世，其子阇耶辛哈一世继位。

en:
Joan of Arc (c. 1412–1431) was a peasant girl from Domrémy who led French troops against the English in the Hundred Years' War, now a patron saint of France. From about 1425 she saw visions, and in February 1429 she set out in men's clothes to the Dauphin.

She announced she would lift the siege of Orléans and see Charles VII crowned at Reims. She reached Orléans in April 1429 carrying her banner, and the English abandoned the siege nine days later. She persuaded Charles to ride to Reims, where he was crowned with her beside him.

Burgundian troops captured her at Compiègne in 1430 and sold her to the English. Pierre Cauchon tried her for heresy at Rouen; she was burned in the Old Market on 30 May 1431, aged about nineteen. A court annulled the verdict in 1456, and Pope Benedict XV canonised her in 1920.

圣女贞德（约1412—1431）是栋雷米村的农家少女，在百年战争中率法军对抗英格兰人，如今是法国的主保圣人之一。约从1425年起她见到异象，1429年2月穿着男装上路去见王太子。

她宣告将解除奥尔良之围，并使查理七世在兰斯加冕。1429年4月她持旗抵达奥尔良，九天后英军撤围；她说服查理前往兰斯，加冕时她侍立身旁。

1430年勃艮第军队在贡比涅俘虏她，并把她卖给英格兰人。皮埃尔·科雄在鲁昂以异端罪审判她，1431年5月30日她在旧市场广场被烧死，年约十九岁。1456年复审法庭宣告原判无效，1920年教宗本笃十五世封她为圣徒。

en:
Jochi (c. 1182–c. 1225), eldest son of Genghis Khan and Börte, was ancestor of the Golden Horde khans. The Merkits carried Börte off before his birth, so his paternity was doubted; his name means ‘guest’. Genghis treated him as a son, Chagatai did not, and their quarrel cost both the succession.

In 1206 Genghis granted him nine thousand warriors and the westernmost lands. In the Khwarazmian war of 1219–1221 he quarrelled with Chagatai at Gurganj, the capital he hoped to keep intact for himself, and the siege ruined much of it.

He withheld Genghis's loot share and withdrew north, where some said he preferred hunting. Summoned around 1224, he pleaded illness, but a traveller saw him hunting; Genghis meant to act when his death was reported. A tale that Genghis had him poisoned is probably invented. His son Batu inherited lands that grew into the Golden Horde.

术赤（约1182—约1225）是成吉思汗与妻子孛儿帖的长子，金帐汗国诸汗的始祖。他出生前孛儿帖曾被蔑儿乞人掳走，生父因此存疑，名字的意思是“客人”。成吉思汗始终视他为亲子，察合台却不认，这场争执使兄弟二人都失去继承资格。

1206年成吉思汗给他九千名战士和最西面的领地。1219至1221年的花剌子模战争中，在他希望完好保住、日后归自己的都城玉龙杰赤，他与察合台争吵，围城使城市大半被毁。

战后他未把应得的战利品送给父亲，北返领地，有说法称他更爱打猎。约1224年被召见时他称病不去，却有旅人发现他在打猎；成吉思汗正打算处置他，就传来死讯。成吉思汗下令毒死他的说法多半是后人编造。儿子拔都继承领地，后来发展为金帐汗国。
