Johan Offesson was a Scanian magnate from southwestern Skåne when the province had recently come under Swedish rule. In 1338 he led an uprising against King Magnus Eriksson of Sweden, who had bought Skåne from its Holstein pledge-holders in 1332.

Defeated in 1339, he kept his life, but his stronghold Lindholmen at Svedala was razed to the ground and his family lost its estates in the Skytts and Oxie hundreds.

en:
Johann Sebastian Pfauser (c. 1520–1569), probably born at Constance, was a Lutheran theologian who became court preacher to Emperor Maximilian II in Vienna. Under his influence Maximilian read Protestant literature and refused communion under the Catholic rite, though he never formally converted.

Pfauser was in contact with Heinrich Bullinger in Zurich and faced Petrus Canisius in public disputations. Later superintendent at Lauingen in Swabia, he died there on 6 June 1569.

en:
Johann Tetzel (c. 1465–1519) was a German Dominican friar, born at Pirna in Saxony, who became grand commissioner for indulgences in Germany. He studied theology and philosophy at Leipzig before entering the order in 1489, preached the Jubilee indulgence from 1502 and was made inquisitor of Poland in 1509.

From January 1517 he sold indulgences for Archbishop Albrecht of Brandenburg, claiming the money would help rebuild St Peter's in Rome. His preaching moved Martin Luther to publish the Ninety-five Theses later that year. He died at Leipzig in August 1519.

Johann Tserclaes, Count of Tilly (1559–1632), led Catholic forces in the Thirty Years' War. Born at Tilly in the Spanish Netherlands and Jesuit-educated at Cologne, he served under Alexander Farnese against the Dutch.

In 1610 Maximilian of Bavaria made him commander of the Catholic League's army. He won at White Mountain in 1620, fought in the conquest of the Palatinate, and crushed the Danes at Lutter in 1626.

His sack of Magdeburg in 1631 killed some twenty thousand inhabitants. Routed by Gustavus Adolphus at Breitenfeld, he defeated the Swedes at Bamberg in 1632, was mortally wounded at Rain, and died at Ingolstadt on 30 April 1632.

让·采克拉斯，即蒂利伯爵（1559—1632），是三十年战争中天主教阵营的主要统帅。他生于西属尼德兰的蒂利城堡，在科隆接受耶稣会教育，早年随亚历山大·法尔内塞与荷兰人作战。

1610年，巴伐利亚公爵马克西米连任命他为天主教联盟军队司令。他1620年取得白山战役大捷，参与征服普法尔茨，1626年在卢特击溃丹麦军队。

1631年他洗劫马格德堡，造成约两万名居民死亡。此后他在布莱登菲尔德被古斯塔夫·阿道夫击败，1632年在班贝格击败瑞典军队，同年在雷恩之战中受致命伤，4月30日死于因戈尔施塔特。

John Barbour (c. 1320–1395) was a Scottish churchman and the first major poet to write in Scots. Educated at Oxford and Paris, he became archdeacon of Aberdeen in 1356 and later served in the household of his patron, Robert II.

For the king he composed The Brus, a verse chronicle of Robert the Bruce and the Scottish wars of independence, including the victory at Bannockburn. He died at Aberdeen in 1395, leaving The Brus as the founding epic of Scottish poetry.

John Calvin (1509–1564), born Jean Cauvin at Noyon in Picardy, was the French theologian and reformer of Geneva whose doctrine came to be called Calvinism. He broke with the Roman Catholic Church around 1530 and fled to Basel, where he published the Institutes of the Christian Religion in 1536.

In Geneva that year he meant to stay one night, but William Farel implored him to help reform the church there. A quarrel over Easter communion led the council to expel both men in 1538. Calvin spent three years in Strasbourg, and came back to Geneva in 1541; the Ecclesiastical Ordinances created the Consistory.

In 1553 he denounced Michael Servetus, burned at the stake. In 1559 he opened the Collège and sent over a hundred ministers to France. He died in 1564 and was buried in an unmarked grave. His followers took the doctrine to Scotland, the Netherlands and Hungary.

约翰·加尔文（1509—1564）原名让·科万，生于皮卡第的努瓦永，是法国神学家、日内瓦宗教改革家，其教义后称加尔文主义。他约1530年与罗马天主教会决裂，逃往巴塞尔，1536年在当地出版《基督教要义》。

同年他在日内瓦本想只住一夜，却被威廉·法雷尔恳求留下改革当地教会。因复活节圣餐引发争执，市议会于1538年驱逐两人；加尔文在斯特拉斯堡度过三年，1541年返回日内瓦，《教会条例》设立宗教事务法庭。

1553年他谴责米格尔·塞尔韦特，后者被处以火刑。1559年他创办学院，向法国派出一百多名牧师。1564年他去世，葬于无名墓；追随者把他的教义带到苏格兰、尼德兰和匈牙利。

John of Fordun (died c. 1384) was a Scottish priest and chronicler. Outraged that Edward III's armies had carried off or destroyed Scotland's old records, he travelled through England and Ireland gathering material for the first continuous history of his country.

Written in Latin and divided into five books, his Chronica Gentis Scotorum traced the Scottish kings back to the legendary Fergus I and ended with David I's death in 1153.

Though its early books cannot be verified, Walter Bower later continued the work as the Scotichronicon, and Fordun remained the foundation of Scottish historiography for centuries.

John Law (1671–1729) was a Scottish financier whose theories reshaped French finances under the Regency. Born in Edinburgh, he killed a man in a duel in 1694, escaped a death sentence, and made his way as a gambler across Europe.

In 1716 the regent Philippe d'Orléans let him found a note-issuing bank, nationalized as the Banque royale in 1718. His Mississippi Company (1717), created to develop Louisiana, drove the speculation of the Mississippi Bubble. Made controller-general of finances in 1720, he fled France when it collapsed and died impoverished in Venice in 1729.

Ndiadiane Ndiaye (also Njaajan Njaay) is the legendary founder of the Jolof Empire, remembered in Wolof and Serer lore; his reign dates are unknown. Tradition makes him the son of Fatoumata Sall, raised in the upper Senegal valley. After his mother remarried, he travelled down the Senegal River to Waalo, where his good judgments led the people to choose him as ruler.

After sixteen years there he founded the Jolof state by peaceful means. Tradition holds that the Wolof language took shape at his court from his subjects' Fula, Serer and Mandinka speech, and coronation baths recalled his emergence from the river. His son Sare Ndiadiane succeeded him, beginning the Ndiaye dynasty that ruled Jolof until the 19th century.

恩迪亚迪亚内·恩迪亚耶（又作恩贾詹·恩贾伊）是乔洛夫帝国传说中的建立者，留存于沃洛夫和塞雷尔人的口述历史中，在位年代不详。相传他是法图玛塔·萨尔之子，在上塞内加尔河谷长大。母亲改嫁后，他沿塞内加尔河来到瓦洛，因断事公允被当地人推举为首领。

统治瓦洛十六年后，他以和平方式建立了乔洛夫国家。传说沃洛夫语在他的宫廷里由臣民所说的富拉语、塞雷尔语和曼丁卡语混合而成，加冕礼上的王室沐浴则纪念他从河中走出。其子萨尔·恩迪亚迪亚内继位，开创的恩迪亚耶王朝统治乔洛夫直至19世纪。

Joseph-Ignace Guillotin (1738–1814) was a French physician and politician born at Saintes. His 1788 petition on the composition of the Estates-General brought him public support, and as a Paris deputy in 1789 he helped the locked-out National Assembly find the tennis court where members swore the Tennis Court Oath.

On 10 October 1789 he proposed that executions be carried out by a simple beheading machine, hoping a swifter, painless death would be a step toward abolishing capital punishment.

He neither designed nor built the device, but a mocking song attached his name to it. He died in Paris in 1814.

en:
Josetsu was a Zen painter-monk active in Kyoto in the early fifteenth century and one of the founders of suiboku ink painting in Japan. Resident at Shōkoku-ji, he is regarded as the teacher of Tenshō Shūbun, who carried his Chinese-derived landscape style into the Ashikaga painting academy.

His best-known work, Catching a Catfish with a Gourd, painted around 1413, depicts a comical fisherman against a winding river and a bamboo grove. It is thought to be inspired by a riddle posed by the Ashikaga shōgun, how to catch a catfish with a gourd, and reads as Zen humour or a visual kōan.

Jarwan ibn Nasser al-Maliki, called Jarwan I, founded the Jarwanid dynasty of Shiite Arabs in fourteenth-century Eastern Arabia. From the port of Qatif he seized power over the Bahrain region, driving out the forces of Sa'id ibn Mughamis, chief of the Muntafiq tribe based at Basra.

Contemporary authors describe the Jarwanids as rawafid, Shia who rejected the first three caliphs, and mosques under their rule followed the Shia form of prayer. The dynasty he founded fell to the Jabrids in the fifteenth century.

贾尔万·伊本·纳赛尔·马利基即贾尔万一世，是14世纪东阿拉伯什叶派阿拉伯政权贾尔万王朝的建立者。他以港口卡提夫为据点，夺取巴林地区的统治权，驱逐了以巴士拉为基地的蒙塔菲格部落酋长赛义德·伊本·穆加米斯的军队。

当时学者称贾尔万人为“拉斐德”，即拒绝承认前三任哈里发的什叶派；在其治下，清真寺按什叶派方式礼拜。他建立的王朝于15世纪被贾布尔王朝取代。

en:
Gerhard V of Jülich (before 1250–1328), son of Count William IV, succeeded his brother Walram as count in 1297. He fought for King Adolf at Göllheim in 1298 and, after Adolf's fall, submitted to Albert I, who confirmed his imperial fief.

In 1300 he aided Albert and secured Rhine tolls against the Archbishop of Cologne. In 1313 he backed Louis the Bavarian for the crown and allowed his Aachen coronation. He died on 29 July 1328, succeeded by his son William.

于利希的格哈德五世（1250年前—1328）是于利希伯爵威廉四世之子，1297年继兄长瓦尔拉姆之后袭爵。1298年他在格尔海姆之战中为国王阿道夫作战；阿道夫败死后，他向阿尔布雷希特一世臣服，后者确认了他的帝国采邑。

1300年他协助阿尔布雷希特，并从科隆大主教手中取得莱茵河关税。1313年他支持巴伐利亚人路德维希争夺王位，允许其在亚琛加冕。1328年7月29日去世，儿子威廉继位。

en:
Gerhard VI of Jülich (c. 1325–1360) was Count of Berg and Ravensberg, the eldest son of William I of Jülich and Joanna of Hainaut. About 1344 he married Margaret of Ravensberg, heiress of both Ravensberg and Berg; as her uncles died without issue between 1346 and 1348, both counties passed to the House of Jülich.

Gerhard opposed the Archbishop of Cologne and won places. He died at a tournament in Düsseldorf on 18 May 1360 and was buried at Altenberg Abbey; his son William succeeded in Berg.

于利希的格哈德六世（约1325—1360）是贝格与拉文斯贝格伯爵，为于利希的威廉一世与埃诺的让娜的长子。约1344年，他娶拉文斯贝格的玛格丽特——她同时拥有拉文斯贝格与贝格的继承权；1346至1348年间她的叔舅先后绝嗣，两个伯国遂并入于利希家族。

en:
Joanna of Hainaut (c. 1312–1374) became countess of Jülich through her marriage to William V of Jülich, celebrated in Cologne on 26 February 1324. She was the third daughter of William I the Good, Count of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland, and a younger sister of Philippa of Hainault, queen of Edward III of England.

Her children included William II, Duke of Jülich, and Gerhard VI, Count of Berg and Ravensberg, maternal grandfather of the Duke of Cleves.

埃诺的让娜（约1312—1374）于1324年2月26日在科隆与于利希的威廉五世成婚，成为于利希伯爵夫人。她是埃诺、荷兰与泽兰伯爵“好人”威廉一世的第三个女儿，也是英格兰国王爱德华三世之后埃诺的菲利帕的妹妹。

en:
William I (c. 1299–1361) ruled Jülich as count from 1328, margrave from 1336 and, from 1356, as its first duke. Eldest son of Count Gerhard V, he married Joanna of Hainaut in 1324, making him brother-in-law to Edward III of England. In 1337 he helped form the German-English alliance that opened the Hundred Years' War, later backing Charles IV, who raised him to duke.

His sons imprisoned him during a revolt of Jülich knights in 1349, but he was freed in 1351. He died in 1361 and was followed by his second son, William II.

Jayaba Mukne, also called Jayadev Rao Naik, was the founder and first raja of Jawhar in the northern Konkan. A chief of the Mahadev Koli people, he established the Mukne dynasty and the state of Jawhar in 1306.

He married Mohanadevi of the Sisodia Rajput house and was succeeded by his son Dhulba Rao, later the raja Nemshah Mukne, who in June 1343 received the title of shah from Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq.

en:
Vasily Mikhailovich (1304–1368), known as Vasily of Kashin, was the youngest son of Mikhail of Tver and Anna of Kashin. In 1319 he received Kashin as an appanage, and after the anti-Tatar uprising of 1327 he fled Tver for Ladoga.

In 1346 the khan Jani Beg granted the Tver patent to his nephew Vsevolod, but in 1349 Vsevolod surrendered the throne and Vasily became prince of Tver. He spent his reign feuding with his nephews and warring with Lithuania, and died at Kashin in July 1368.

瓦西里·米哈伊洛维奇（1304—1368），人称卡申的瓦西里，是特维尔王公米哈伊尔·雅罗斯拉维奇与卡申的安娜最小的儿子。1319年，他获得卡申作为采邑；1327年特维尔爆发反抗鞑靼人的起义，他逃往拉多加。

en:
Basir Onin succeeded his father Imaga, who in 1309 founded the Papuan kingdom of Sran later called Kaimana, becoming its second Rat Sran and ruling with the title Rat Sran Adi.

He moved the royal capital from Weri to Borombouw on Adi Island, judging it a strategic seat on the shipping and trade route to the Koiwai mainland. In later life he declared himself too old to rule and installed his son Woran as king.

en:
Imaga, who bore the title Rat Sran Nati Patimunin, was the founder of the Kingdom of Sran, later called Kaimana, on the Bomberai Peninsula of West Papua. Papuan oral tradition relates that he came from the Mbaham highlands of the Patimunin region.

He bound the scattered villages to himself by visits and marriage alliances, until in 1309 they raised him as their king. He set his capital at Weri on Tunasgain Bay in Fakfak and traded with merchants from Seram.

en:
Kanō Masanobu (1434–1530) was a Japanese painter who served the Ashikaga shogunate in Kyoto as its official painter and is counted the founder of the Kanō school. Working in the capital by 1463, he succeeded Sōtan as official painter to the shogunate, though his provincial origins and lack of court rank drew aristocratic criticism.

He painted in the Chinese-derived suiboku ink-wash tradition of Tenshō Shūbun, adding firmer, more clearly defined forms, and produced Zen subjects alongside Buddhist deities. Few works survive, among them Zhou Maoshu Appreciating Lotuses, and his son Kanō Motonobu built the family workshop into Japan's dominant painting school for four centuries.

狩野正信（1434—1530）是日本室町时代的绘师，在京都担任室町幕府的御用绘师，被奉为狩野派之祖。他1463年已在京都以画师身份活动，后来接替宗湛担任幕府御用绘师，只是地方出身和缺少朝廷品级招来贵族批评。

他承袭天章周文一脉源自中国的水墨画风，以更坚实明确的造型自成面貌，兼绘禅宗题材与佛像、菩萨。其存世作品极少，《周茂叔爱莲图》是其中代表；其子狩野元信后来把家族画派发展成统领日本画坛四百年的狩野派。

Alâeddin Halil Mirza was a son of the Karamanid ruler Mahmut Bey. He became bey of Karaman after his elder brothers Musa and İbrahim, when İbrahim I stepped down in his favour between 1332 and 1340.

Unlike them he undertook no military campaigns; his reign was devoted to pious building, and he commissioned mosques and other charitable foundations in Ermenek. He died in 1340, after which İbrahim took power again.

阿拉丁·哈利勒·米尔扎是卡拉曼统治者马哈茂德贝伊之子。1332至1340年间，其兄易卜拉欣一世让位，他登基为卡拉曼贝伊，在诸兄穆萨、易卜拉欣之后相继执政。

Fahreddin Ahmed, a son of the Karamanid bey İbrahim I, succeeded his father as the ninth ruler of Karaman. His reign was brief, lasting from about 1349 until his death on 18 January 1350.

Throughout those months he was at war with the Mongols and with the neighboring beylik of Eretna. He is said to have fallen in battle against the Mongols in 1350.

Bedreddin İbrahim was a son of the Karamanid ruler Mahmut Bey. After his elder brother Musa succeeded in 1312, İbrahim claimed the throne and rose in revolt in 1318, winning it with the backing of the Egyptian Mamluks; Ibn Battuta once served as his envoy to Cairo.

Between 1332 and 1340 he abdicated in favour of his brother Halil, but after Halil died in 1340 he resumed rule. He campaigned against the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia and was certainly still alive in 1343.

en:
Karim al-Din Karaman Bey (died c. 1262), son of Turkoman leader Nure Sofi, succeeded his father before 1256 as a Seljuk vassal in the Taurus. He built a semi-independent beylik in wars with Armenian Cilicia, taking several towns; Laranda was renamed Karaman after him.

In 1261, claiming to restore the exiled Sultan Kaykaus II, he marched on Konya but was routed by a Seljuk-Mongol army at Gevele and died soon after. His son Mehmet I succeeded him and revived the Karamanid state in 1276.

en:
Badr al-Din Mahmud Bey (c. 1250–1308), fourth Karamanid ruler, was a son of its founder Karaman Bey. In 1293 he drove Cypriot crusaders from Alanya, and in 1300 succeeded his brother Güneri at Laranda; he was the first Karamanid to style himself sultan.

He defeated an Ilkhanid army and, after Hethum II of Armenia died in 1307, raided Armenian Cilicia. In 1308 he won near Anamur but died of his wounds. His son Musa succeeded him.

Burhanettin Musa, a son of Mahmut Bey, became bey of Karaman in 1312. After the Mongol emir Çoban seized Konya, his brother İbrahim, backed by the Egyptian Mamluks, rebelled and took the capital Larende, so that when Ibn Battuta visited in 1332 Musa ruled only Ermenek.

In 1352, amid disorder in the beylik, he was invited back to Karaman and reigned until 1356. He campaigned against the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, seizing much of its territory, and died at Konya in 1356.

en:
Seyfeddin Süleyman was the elder son of the Karamanid bey Alâeddin Halil and governed Ermenek for his uncle Musa when Musa died in 1356 and he succeeded as bey. He appointed his brother Alâattin Ali governor of Ermenek; after Ali defeated a hostile coalition, its losers allied with Mehmet of the neighboring Eretna beylik against Süleyman.

In 1361, on his way to an old soldier’s funeral, Süleyman was assassinated. Turkish chroniclers remember him as a pious, kindly ruler, and his tomb stands in Konya.

en:
Kazimierz Siemienowicz (c. 1600–c. 1651) was a Polish–Lithuanian general of artillery, military engineer and a pioneer of rocketry, born in the Raseiniai region of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. He fought in the Smolensk War of 1632–1634, served Frederick Henry of Orange and took part in the Siege of Hulst in 1645.

He returned in 1646 as King Władysław IV gathered specialists, and became second-in-command of the Royal Artillery in 1648. Around 1649 he settled in Amsterdam, where in 1650 he published the treatise Artis Magnae Artilleriae on artillery, rockets and pyrotechnics, a standard handbook for two centuries.

卡齐米日·谢米耶诺维奇（约1600—约1651）是波兰—立陶宛的炮兵将领、军事工程师和火箭学先驱，生于立陶宛大公国的拉塞尼艾地区。他参加过1632—1634年的斯摩棱斯克战争，曾为奥兰治亲王弗雷德里克·亨德里克效力，参与1645年的许尔斯特围城战。

1646年国王瓦迪斯瓦夫四世招募专家时他返回国内，1648年出任王家炮兵副司令。约1649年他定居阿姆斯特丹，1650年在当地出版论著《伟大的炮兵艺术》，内容涵盖火炮、火箭与烟火制造，在此后两个世纪里一直是该领域的标准手册。

en:
Keykubad Bey was the second ruler of the Kubadids, a Turkmen principality on Anatolia's Black Sea coast, succeeding his father Tâceddin Altunbaş around 1357. He kept Ladik as his capital in the lands around Ladik and Kavak, while his tutor Emir Taşan broke away to found the neighboring Taşanoğulları beylik.

Under Keykubad the Kubadids became vassals of the Amasya rulers Hacı Şadgeldi and Emir Ahmed. His son Ali Bey campaigned against the neighboring Taceddinoğulları and won Samsun, then succeeded him.

凯库巴德贝伊是安纳托利亚黑海沿岸土库曼小邦库巴德贝伊国的第二代统治者，约1357年继其父塔杰丁·阿尔通巴什之位。他以拉迪克为都，领有拉迪克和卡瓦克一带，而他的导师埃米尔塔尚另立门户，建立了邻近的塔尚奥卢贝伊国。

凯库巴德在位时，库巴德臣服于阿马西亚统治者哈吉·沙德格尔迪与埃米尔艾哈迈德。其子阿里贝伊征讨邻近的塔杰丁奥卢贝伊国，夺取萨姆松，随后继承了他的位子。

en:
Tâceddin Altunbaş was a Seljuk prince, a son of Gıyaseddin Mesud II, the last Sultan of Rûm. After his father's death in 1308, the Mongol Ilkhan granted him Amasya and the lands around Samsun and Ladik, which he governed as a Mongol vassal.

In 1318, after his atabeg Emir Yeşbek was killed in Amasya during clashes with the Mongols, he withdrew north to Ladik and ruled independently, founding the Turkmen beylik of the Kubadids. He died around 1357 and was succeeded by his son Keykubad.

en:
Abdullah II, called Kademi (ʿAbdallāh bin Kade, died 1335), became mai of Kanem about 1311, succeeding his murdered cousin Ibrahim I Nikale. Avenging Ibrahim, he invited the killers to court on the pretext of ennobling them and had them executed, then crushed the rebels and established his power with a strong hand.

Remembered as a just ruler, he died a natural death at Njimi. His four sons succeeded him in turn and all fell fighting the Sao.

Biri Ibrahim (Biri bin Dunama), enumerated as Biri II and also recorded as Kashim Biri or Uthman (died 1296), was a son of mai Dunama II Dibalemi and ruled Kanem during the long succession war between Dunama's sons.

en:
Dawud, called Nikalemi, was a son of mai Ibrahim I Nikale and succeeded his half-brother Idris I as mai of Kanem in about 1353. Taking the throne over Idris's many sons provoked civil war, and the Sayfawa split into the Dawudid and Idrisid branches.

Dawud was the first mai to face the Bilala invading from the east; they defeated him, seized the capital Njimi and killed him at Melfala near Lake Fitri about 1363. His death began a centuries-long conflict between the Sayfawa and the Bilala. He was succeeded by his son Uthman I.

en:
Dunama II Dibalemi (Dunama bin ʿAbd al-Jalīl, died 1248) was mai of Kanem and one of its greatest warrior-rulers, succeeding his father Selema II around 1221. He built a large cavalry force, sometimes credited with bringing cavalry warfare to central Africa.

He waged jihad against his pagan neighbours: he seized the Fezzan, fought the Toubou for seven years, raided from a fleet on Lake Chad and drove the Sao south. He kept a pilgrim hostel in Cairo, and under him Kanem stood at the height of its strength.

al-Hajj Ibrahim I, called Nikale (Ibrahim bin Biri, died around 1315), was mai of Kanem and a grandson of Dunama II Dibalemi. He emerged from the long succession war between Dunama's sons, though strife continued: he once put one of his own sons to death, probably for revolt.

He made the pilgrimage to Mecca, earning the title al-Hajj. After about twenty years he was murdered at Dískama, his body thrown into the Wau River; his cousin Abdullah II Kademi succeeded him.

“哈吉”易卜拉欣一世，绰号尼卡莱（易卜拉欣·本·比里，约1315年卒）是加奈姆麦伊，杜纳马二世·迪巴拉米之孙。他从杜纳马诸子的长期继承权混战中崛起，但纷争并未止息：他在位期间曾处死一个亲生儿子，大概是因其谋反。

他曾前往麦加朝觐，因而得到“哈吉”称号。在位约二十年后，他在迪斯卡马遇害，尸体被抛入瓦乌河，堂兄弟阿卜杜拉二世·卡德米继位。

en:
al-Hajj Idris I, called Nikalemi, was a son of mai Ibrahim I Nikale and succeeded Muhammad I Kure as mai of Kanem in about 1329. His accession ended the line of Abdullah II, whose four sons had perished in wars against the Sao.

Idris ruled for twenty-four or twenty-five years, far longer than his predecessors, and at some point made the pilgrimage to Mecca. He died about 1353, probably at Damasak, perhaps while campaigning against the Sao. His half-brother Dawud succeeded over Idris's own sons, splitting the Sayfawa into rival Idrisid and Dawudid branches.

zh:
“哈吉”伊德里斯一世（绰号尼卡莱米）是麦伊易卜拉欣一世·尼卡莱之子，约1329年继穆罕默德一世·库里之位成为加奈姆麦伊。阿卜杜拉二世的四个儿子先后在对萨奥人的战争中丧命，伊德里斯的即位终结了该支系的统治。

他在位二十四或二十五年，远比此前的麦伊长久，并曾前往麦加朝觐。约1353年他去世，可能卒于达马萨克，或许是在征讨萨奥人期间。其异母弟达乌德越过他的儿子们继位，赛法瓦王朝由此分裂为伊德里斯系与达乌德系两个对立支派。

en:
Kade I, called Aujami (Kade bin Dunama, died 1277), succeeded his father Dunama II Dibalemi as mai of Kanem. His reign fell in the decades-long conflict in which Dunama's sons fought over the throne.

The exact order and dates of these mais are uncertain. Kade was the father of Abdullah II Kademi, who later restored order after the murder of Ibrahim I Nikale.

卡代一世，一称奥贾米（卡代·本·杜纳马，1277年卒）在父亲杜纳马二世·迪巴拉米死后继位，成为加奈姆麦伊。他在位时正值杜纳马诸子争夺王位的数十年混战。

en:
Kure I, called Gana (the Younger), was a son of mai Abdullah II Kademi of the Sayfawa dynasty. He succeeded his brother Selema III as mai of Kanem in about 1326, after Selema was killed fighting the Sao south of Lake Chad. Though younger than his brother Kure Kura, Kure Gana took the throne first.

His reign lasted little more than a year: he too was defeated and killed by the Sao at a place called Ghaliwa. He was succeeded by Kure Kura, who ruled as Kure II.

库里一世（绰号“小库里”）是赛法瓦王朝麦伊阿卜杜拉二世·卡德米之子。约1326年，其兄塞莱马三世在乍得湖以南与萨奥人作战时被杀，库里遂继兄位成为加奈姆麦伊。尽管比兄长库里·库拉年幼，他却先登王位。

他在位仅一年多，便同样在名为加利瓦的地方被萨奥人击败身亡。继位者是库里·库拉，即库里二世。

en:
Kure II, called Kura (the Elder), was a son of mai Abdullah II Kademi and the elder brother of Kure I Gana. In about 1327 he succeeded Kure I, who had been killed fighting the Sao of Bornu south of Lake Chad. Two of his brothers, Selema III and Kure I, had already died in the same rising.

After a short reign Kure II was also defeated and slain by the Sao at Ghaliwa, the very site where Kure I had fallen. He was succeeded by another brother, Muhammad I Kure.

en:
Muhammad I, also called Kure Muhammad, was a son of mai Abdullah II Kademi and his wife Kagala. In about 1328 he succeeded his brother Kure II Kura as mai of Kanem. Three of his brothers, Selema III, Kure I Gana and Kure II, had already been killed in quick succession in wars against the Sao of Bornu south of Lake Chad.

After a brief reign Muhammad suffered the same fate, slain by the Sao at Nanigham. With him the sons of Abdullah II were extinguished, and the throne passed to Idris I, son of Ibrahim I Nikale.

穆罕默德一世（又称库里·穆罕默德）是麦伊阿卜杜拉二世·卡德米与妻子卡加拉之子。约1328年，他继兄库里二世·库拉之位成为加奈姆麦伊。此前他的三个兄弟塞莱马三世、库里一世·加纳和库里二世已在乍得湖以南对博尔努萨奥人的战争中接连战死。

en:
Selema III, also called Salmama II (Sǝlǝma bin ʿAbdallāh, died around 1326), was mai of the Kanem Empire in the early fourteenth century, succeeding his father Abdullah II Kademi. His short reign, beginning around 1322, was dominated by the rising of the Sao peoples south of Lake Chad, whom earlier mais had weakened but never fully subdued.

Selema campaigned against them but was killed in battle at a site recorded as Yúsub or N'difu, and was succeeded by his brother Kure I Gana.

塞莱马三世，一称萨尔马马二世（萨莱马·本·阿卜杜拉，约1326年卒）是14世纪初加奈姆帝国的马伊，继其父阿卜杜拉二世·卡德米之位。他约于1322年登位，统治短暂，其间乍得湖以南的萨奥人起兵——历代马伊虽曾削弱萨奥人，却始终未能将其彻底征服。

萨尔马马出兵征讨，战死于记作尤苏卜或恩迪富之地，其弟库里一世·加纳继位。

en:
Andrei Mstislavich was a Rurikid prince, the fourth son of Mstislav Mikhailovich of Karachev and a brother of Panteleimon Mstislavich. He is described as prince of Kozelsk or of Zvenigorod, the latter title appearing in a sixteenth-century genealogy.

He appears just once in the sources: under 1339 the Voskresensk Chronicle reports that he was killed by his own nephew, Vasily Panteleimonovich, for reasons unrecorded. A later genealogy names his wife as Elena, possibly a daughter of Grand Prince Gediminas of Lithuania, and gives him two sons, Fyodor and Ivan.

安德烈·姆斯季斯拉维奇是留里克王公，卡拉切夫王公姆斯季斯拉夫·米哈伊洛维奇的第四子、潘捷列伊蒙·姆斯季斯拉维奇之弟。他的头衔有科泽利斯克王公和兹韦尼哥罗德王公两种说法，后者见于一部16世纪家谱。

en:
Mstislav Mikhailovich (1220–c. 1280) was a Rurikid prince, traditionally one of the younger sons of Mikhail Vsevolodovich of Chernigov and the founder of the Karachev branch of the Olgovichi.

Sixteenth-century genealogies assign him Karachev and Kozelsk, and he is counted as the first prince of Karachev, though many scholars regard Kozelsk as his actual seat. Genealogies name Svyatoslav, Tit and Andrei as his sons; Tit and Andrei also appear in chronicles.

zh:
姆斯季斯拉夫·米哈伊洛维奇（1220—约1280）是留里克王公，传统上被认为是切尔尼戈夫王公米哈伊尔·弗谢沃洛多维奇较年幼的儿子之一，也是奥列格维奇家族卡拉切夫支系的始祖。

按16世纪编成的家谱，他领有卡拉切夫和科泽利斯克，被视为第一代卡拉切夫王公，但不少学者认为科泽利斯克才是他的实际中心。家谱将斯维亚托斯拉夫、季特和安德烈列为他的儿子；季特和安德烈也见于编年史。

en:
Panteleimon Mstislavich was a Rurikid prince of the Karachev line, traditionally a grandson of Mikhail Vsevolodovich of Chernigov and the third son of Prince Mstislav Mikhailovich of Karachev. He is known almost entirely from later genealogies, and historians differ over whether he held Karachev or Zvenigorod.

His only mention in the chronicles is indirect: the Voskresensk Chronicle records that in 1339 his son Vasily Panteleimonovich killed Panteleimon's brother Andrei Mstislavich, prince of Kozelsk.

en:
Svyatoslav Mstislavich (died 1310) was a Rurikid prince of Karachev, the second son of Mstislav Mikhailovich, from whom he inherited Karachev. He appears in the sources only once: the Nikon Chronicle records that in 1310 Bryansk troops with a Golden Horde force seized Karachev, and Svyatoslav was killed.

He may have laid claim to Bryansk, by then held by the Smolensk branch of the Rurikids. He left no heirs.

斯维亚托斯拉夫·姆斯季斯拉维奇（1310年卒）是卡拉切夫的留里克王公，姆斯季斯拉夫·米哈伊洛维奇的次子，在父亲死后继承卡拉切夫。他在史料中只出现过一次：《尼康编年史》记载，1310年布良斯克军队联合金帐汗国兵马夺取卡拉切夫，斯维亚托斯拉夫兵败身死。

en:
Vasily Panteleimonovich was the son of Panteleimon Mstislavich, prince of Karachev, and grandson of Mstislav Mikhailovich. He is named only once in the chronicles: the Voskresensk Chronicle states that in 1339 he killed his uncle Andrei Mstislavich, prince of Kozelsk or Zvenigorod.

The motive is not recorded, though modern historians have suggested a quarrel over his father's appanage after Panteleimon's death. One scholar also proposed that Vasily was later killed by the Mongols of the Golden Horde.

en:
Ivane II, called Atabek-Ivane and the Great, was an Armenian prince of the Hasan-Jalalyan house who ruled Khachen in the second half of the fourteenth century. He was the son of Prince Jalal II and grandson of Ivane-Atabek I.

His own domains covered Lower Khachen, while he exercised suzerain rights over the entire Khachen principality. Sources name him as its prince from 1361. He was succeeded by his son Jalal III.

伊凡二世（又称阿塔贝克-伊凡，绰号“大帝”）是哈桑-贾拉良家族的亚美尼亚王公，于14世纪后半叶统治哈琴。他是贾拉勒二世之子、伊凡-阿塔贝克一世之孙。

他的直领之地为下哈琴，同时对整个哈琴公国保有宗主权。史料自1361年起称他为哈琴王公，其子贾拉勒三世继立。

en:
Sultan Ibrahim Shah, son of Sultan Mahmud Shah I and Tunku Aishah, was the sixth Sultan of Kedah and held the throne for fifty-two years. He succeeded his father in 1321 and first resided at Kota Sungai Mas, before moving his court to Kota Seputih in 1323 and making it his capital.

Malay chronicles credit him with fixing the ranks of his ministers and record that Kedah's population and trade grew during his reign. He died in 1373 and was buried at Kota Seputih, succeeded by his son Sulaiman Shah I.

苏丹伊布拉欣·沙是马哈茂德·沙一世与东古·艾莎之子，吉打第六任苏丹，在位52年。他1321年继承父位，先居双溪马士，1323年将宫廷迁往哥打士布爹并以此为都。

马来史籍记载，他厘定了大臣的等级次序；在他治下吉打人口增长、贸易兴盛。他于1373年去世，葬于哥打士布爹，其子苏莱曼·沙一世继位。

en:
Muhammad Shah, born Awang Alak Betatar, founded the Sultanate of Brunei and ruled as its first sultan from 1363 or 1368 until his death around 1402. Brunei royal genealogies divide over his origins: one tradition makes him a son of Sultan Ibrahim Shah of Kedah.

He ruled at Kota Batu as Raja Awang Alak Betatar until his conversion to Islam in the 14th century, when he took the name Muhammad Shah; tradition connects the conversion with his marriage to Princess Dayang Pingai, daughter of the ruler of Johor or Tumasik.

The Nagarakretagama lists Brunei among Majapahit's vassals in 1365, and in 1371 he sent envoys to the Ming dynasty, whose records name him Ma-ho-mo-sa. His daughter Princess Ratna Dewi married the Chinese settler Ong Sum Ping.

穆罕默德·沙原名阿旺·阿拉克·贝塔塔尔，创建文莱苏丹国并成为第一任苏丹，1363或1368年至约1402年在位。文莱王家世系对其出身说法不一：一说他是吉打苏丹伊布拉欣·沙之子。

他早年在哥打巴都以拉惹阿旺·阿拉克·贝塔塔尔之名执政，14世纪皈依伊斯兰教后改名穆罕默德·沙；相传皈依与迎娶柔佛（一说淡马锡）统治者之女达央·宾盖公主有关。

1365年的《爪哇史颂》把文莱列为满者伯夷的属国；1371年他遣使赴明朝朝贺，中国史籍以“马合谟沙”记载其名。其女拉特纳·德维公主嫁给华人移民黄森屏。

en:
Tunku Mala was the permaisuri, or queen consort, of Sultan Ibrahim Shah of Kedah, who reigned from 1321 to 1373. She was the mother of his successor Sultan Sulaiman Shah I, who ruled Kedah from 1373 to 1423, and of another son, Tunku Abdul Rahman.

A Brunei royal genealogical tradition also names her as the mother of Brunei's first sultan Muhammad Shah, born Awang Alak Betatar.

en:
Khabul Khan (died 1148) was the founder and first khan of the Khamag Mongol confederation, uniting the Mongol clans under Borjigin leadership. A son of Tumbinai Khan, he fought off Jurchen Jin invasions; summoned to the Jin court in 1135, he offended the emperor by pulling his beard and then led raids into Jin territory.

In 1147 the Jin recognized him as king of the Mongols. Although he had seven sons, he was succeeded by his cousin Ambaghai.

zh:
合不勒汗（1148年卒）是蒙兀国联盟的创建者和第一位可汗，把蒙古诸部团结在孛儿只斤氏之下。他是敦必乃之子，多次击退女真人金朝的进攻；1135年应召入朝时，他捋金太宗的胡须，触怒了皇帝，后来又率部袭扰金境。

1147年，金朝册封他为蒙兀国王。他虽有七子，临终却传位给从弟俺巴孩。

Khaduli Barlas was a Borjigin Mongol prince. The son of Tumbinai Khan, he was the twin brother of Khabul Khan, founder of the Khamag Mongol.

He served Khabul as a military commander, minister and adviser from about 1130 to 1148, and fought at his side in the campaigns against the Jurchen Jin dynasty. His son Erumduli and grandson Suqu Sechen both held commands under the confederation's khans.

en:
Srindrabhupesvarachuda (born c. 1250) was the eldest daughter of Khmer king Jayavarman VIII. She married Indravarman, and an inscription records the pair being crowned as heir and consort while her father still reigned.

She persuaded her father to set aside her brother, the intended crown prince, and stole the golden sword of office for her husband. Her brother had his toes cut off and was thrown into a dark dungeon, after which Indravarman III took the throne in 1295.

en:
Indrajayavarman (died 1327), also called Indravarman IV, ruled the Khmer Empire from 1308 to 1327; his tie to his predecessor Indravarman III is unknown. A devotee of Shiva, he renewed the persecution of Buddhists and encouraged the destruction of Buddha images.

His reign also brought fresh Siamese incursions, launched in the name of defending the Buddhist faith. His inscriptions are the last Sanskrit records at Angkor, and he was succeeded by his son Jayavarman IX.

因陀罗阇耶跋摩（？—1327），又称因陀罗跋摩四世，1308至1327年统治高棉帝国，与前任因陀罗跋摩三世的亲属关系不详。他是湿婆的虔诚信徒，在位时恢复迫害佛教徒，鼓励毁坏佛像。

en:
Indravarman II (died 1243), son of Jayavarman VII, ruled the Khmer Empire from about 1215. His reign is poorly documented, since his successor Jayavarman VIII may have destroyed the records; only one inscription gives his death year. A Buddhist, he enlarged several of his father's temples.

Under him the empire shrank: the Khmers lost control of Champa, and the newborn Sukhothai kingdom seized western territories. One historian sees him as a possible model for the Leper King of Khmer legend.

en:
Indravarman III (died 1308), also titled Srindravarman, ruled the Khmer Empire from 1295. As commander of the army he took the throne when his father-in-law Jayavarman VIII abdicated. The king's daughter stole the royal Sacred Sword for him; the crown prince was seized, mutilated and imprisoned.

After suppressing resistance, Indravarman was crowned and married the princess to legitimize his rule. A Theravada Buddhist, he made that school the state religion. In 1296 the Chinese envoy Zhou Daguan visited his Angkor court and later wrote the Customs of Cambodia, which records that a recent Siamese war had devastated the country.

因陀罗跋摩三世（？—1308），又号室利因陀罗跋摩，自1295年起统治高棉帝国。他原任军队统帅，在岳父阇耶跋摩八世逊位后取得王位。国王之女盗出王室圣剑交给他，王储则被逮捕、割去脚趾并囚禁。

Jayavarman IX (died 1336), also called Jayavarmadiparamesvara, ruled the Khmer Empire from 1327 to 1336, succeeding his father Indrajayavarman. A Shaivite like his father, he is the last Angkorean king named in temple inscriptions, and the last Sanskrit inscription in Cambodia is his.

The Cambodian Royal Chronicle, which names him Sihanouk, relates that in 1336 he was murdered by the royal gardener Trasak Paem, who married his daughter and seized the throne; that tale is probably legendary.

en:
Jayavarman VII (c. 1122–1218) was the most powerful king of the Khmer Empire. A son of Dharanindravarman II, he was already past fifty when the Chams sacked Angkor in 1177; he drove out the invaders and was crowned in 1181. His armies took the Cham capital Vijaya in 1190 and annexed Champa in 1203.

The first Khmer king devoted to Buddhism, he followed Mahayana; his queen Jayarajadevi and her sister Indradevi, whom he later married, are thought to have shaped his faith. He built Angkor Thom, the Bayon, Ta Prohm and Preah Khan, and founded 102 hospitals and 121 rest houses. His son Indravarman II succeeded him.

zh:
阇耶跋摩七世（约1122—1218）是高棉帝国国力最盛时的国王。他是陀罗尼因陀罗跋摩二世之子，1177年占城军队洗劫吴哥时，年过半百的他起兵驱逐入侵者，于1181年登基。他的军队1190年攻占占城首都毗阇耶，1203年吞并占城。

他是第一位虔信佛教的高棉国王，信奉大乘佛教；王后阇耶罗阇黛维与其妹因陀罗黛维被认为塑造了他的信仰，王后去世后他娶了因陀罗黛维。他修建了吴哥城、巴戎寺、塔布隆寺和圣剑寺，还创办102所医院、设立121处驿馆。他死后由其子因陀罗跋摩二世继位。

en:
Jayavarman VIII (born c. 1210) ruled the Khmer Empire from 1243 to 1295. A Shaivite, he reversed the Buddhism of his father Jayavarman VII, destroying Buddha images at Preah Khan, turning the Bayon into a temple of Shiva and casting its great Buddha statue into a well.

In 1281 he imprisoned Mongol envoys in Champa, and when Kublai Khan's armies invaded in 1283 he bought peace with tribute. In 1290 Lavo threw off Khmer overlordship, and a war with the Siamese devastated the kingdom. He endowed the Mangalartha shrine in 1295, shortly before his son-in-law Indravarman III forced him to abdicate.

阇耶跋摩八世（约1210年生）于1243至1295年统治高棉帝国。他信奉湿婆派印度教，一改其父阇耶跋摩七世的佛教政策：捣毁圣剑寺等地的佛像，将巴戎寺改为湿婆神庙，并把寺中的大佛像投入井底。

en:
Nippean Bat (Khmer Nibbanapada), personal name Ponhea Kreak, is named by the Cambodian Royal Chronicles as ruler of the Khmer Empire from 1340 to 1346. The eldest son of the gardener-king Trasak Paem and Candravati, he succeeded his father.

His six-year reign is remembered for a loss: the Thais rose in revolt, set up independent kingdoms and freed themselves from Khmer vassalage, and the empire lost all its Siamese dependencies. His younger brother Sithean Reachea followed him on the throne, and the crown passed to his own son Lompong Reachea.

尼皮安·巴特（高棉语称尼般那巴达），本名奔哈·克雷克，据柬埔寨王家编年史记载，于1340至1346年统治高棉帝国。他是“园丁国王”特罗萨克·帕埃姆与钱德拉瓦蒂的长子，继承父位。

编年史记住他的六年在位，是因为一次丧失：泰人起兵反叛，建立独立王国，摆脱高棉的宗主权，帝国失去了全部暹罗属地。他死后由弟弟悉提因·列谢继位，王位随后又传给他自己的儿子隆庞·列谢。

The Cambodian Royal Chronicles name Sithean Reachea (Khmer Siddhanaraja) as ruler of the Khmer Empire from 1346 to 1347. The younger son of Trasak Paem and Candravati, he succeeded his elder brother Nippean Bat but reigned only three or six months before abdicating in favor of his nephew Lompong Reachea.

After stepping down he bore the ceremonial title Maha Upayuvaraja, meaning retired great king. His date of death is unknown.

en:
Trasak Paem is the first Khmer ruler known only from the Cambodian Royal Chronicles, said to have died around 1340. The chronicles make him a royal gardener to a king identified with Jayavarman IX, so skilled at growing sweet cucumbers that his title means master of the tasty cucumber. The king gave him his own spear to guard the crop. One night when the king came to test his zeal, he mortally wounded him; the dying man cleared him of blame.

With no heir, a white elephant at the royal election passed over the nobles to choose the gardener from the crowd. Facing the dignitaries' hostility, he withdrew to Banteay Samré and ruled quietly only after eliminating his predecessor's loyalists.

He married the old king's daughter Candravati, and the chronicles name his sons Nippean Bat and Sithean Reachea. Historians judge him probably legendary.

特罗萨克·帕埃姆是仅见于柬埔寨王家编年史的最早一位高棉统治者，相传约卒于1340年。编年史说他本是被比定为阇耶跋摩九世的那位国王的王家园丁，擅长种甜黄瓜，名号意为“美味黄瓜之主”。国王把自己的长矛交给他看守瓜田，一天夜里国王前来试探他是否尽心，被他刺成致命伤，临终前却说他无罪。

国王没有子嗣，选王仪式上的白象越过群臣，从人群中选中了这位园丁。面对权贵的敌意，他退居班迭萨姆雷，直到清除了前朝旧臣，才开始平静的统治。

他娶了先王的女儿钱德拉瓦蒂，编年史载其二子为尼皮安·巴特和悉提因·列谢。史家多认为他是传说人物。

en:
Kʼokaibʼ was an early ahpop, “man of the mat”, as the Kʼicheʼ called their king, in the Guatemalan highlands. The Kʼicheʼ traced their rulers to invaders who entered the highlands around 1200 and founded three lineages: the ruling Nima Kʼicheʼ, the Tamub, and the warrior Ilokʼab.

Native king lists place Kʼokaibʼ at Pismachi, a new town with a large ritual center, around 1325–1350, after Ajkan and before Kʼonache.

Under these two kings the lineages began to quarrel, and the Ilokʼab left for Mukwitz Chilokʼab. The kingdom later moved its capital to Qʼumarkaj and dominated the highlands until the Spanish conquest of 1524.

zh:
科凯布是危地马拉高地基切人早期的“阿赫波普”，意为“席上之人”，即基切人对国王的称呼。基切人把统治者的来历追溯到约1200年进入高地的外来者，他们建立了三大支系：统治的尼马基切、塔穆布和武士支系伊洛克阿布。

据基切本土王名表，科凯布约于1325—1350年在皮斯马奇统治，介于阿赫坎与科纳切之间；皮斯马奇是建有大型礼仪中心的新城镇。

在这两位国王治下，各支系开始争执，伊洛克阿布迁居穆克维茨·奇洛克阿布。王国后来迁都库马尔卡赫，支配高地，直到1524年被西班牙征服。

en:
Gerald FitzMaurice (c. 1150–1204), first Lord of Offaly, was a Cambro-Norman nobleman and second son of Maurice FitzGerald. He came to Ireland in the Norman invasion of 1169–71 and distinguished himself fighting outside Dublin in 1171.

He built Maynooth Castle and campaigned in the conquest of Limerick in 1197. Through his marriage to Eve de Bermingham around 1193 he acquired the barony of Offaly. He died on 15 January 1204, leaving a son Maurice, ancestor of the Kildare earls.

杰拉尔德·菲茨莫里斯（约1150—1204年1月15日）是第一代奥法利领主、坎布罗诺曼贵族，莫里斯·菲茨杰拉德的次子。1169至1171年诺曼人入侵爱尔兰时他随父出征，1171年在都柏林城外迎战爱尔兰高王，表现英勇。

他修建梅努斯城堡，并在1197年参加征服利默里克。约1193年他迎娶伊芙·德·伯明翰，由此获得奥法利男爵领地。1204年1月15日去世，独子莫里斯是历代基尔代尔伯爵的祖先。

en:
John FitzThomas FitzGerald (c. 1250–1316), fourth Lord of Offaly and first Earl of Kildare, was an Anglo-Norman magnate. In 1291 he accused Justiciar William de Vesci of oppression before Edward I; when de Vesci fled trial, the king granted him Kildare.

In 1294–1295 he imprisoned Richard de Burgh, later marrying his heir Thomas to de Burgh's daughter. He fought in Edward I's Scottish wars and resisted Edward Bruce's invasion of 1315–16. Created earl on 14 May 1316, he died that September.

约翰·菲茨托马斯·菲茨杰拉德（约1250—1316年9月）是第四代奥法利领主、第一代基尔代尔伯爵，盎格鲁诺曼大贵族。1291年，他在爱德华一世面前控告爱尔兰政法官威廉·德·维西苛政扰民；德·维西拒绝比武审判、出逃国外，国王遂把基尔代尔判赐给他。

1294至1295年，他囚禁理查德·德·伯格，随后让继承人托马斯迎娶德·伯格之女。他参加爱德华一世的苏格兰战争，并抵抗1315至1316年爱德华·布鲁斯的入侵。1316年5月14日受封基尔代尔伯爵，同年9月去世。

en:
Maurice FitzThomas FitzGerald, 4th Earl of Kildare (1318–1390), was an Irish nobleman, the second son of Thomas FitzGerald, 2nd Earl of Kildare, and Joan de Burgh, daughter of the Earl of Ulster. He succeeded his brother Richard as earl in 1329.

In 1347 he served Edward III at the siege of Calais, where he was knighted, and in 1360 he was appointed Lord Justice of Ireland, taking office again in 1371 and 1375. In 1364 he led Irish nobles to England to protest the misgovernment of Ireland. He died in 1390 and was buried at Christ Church Cathedral, Dublin.

莫里斯·菲茨杰拉德，第四代基尔代尔伯爵（1318—1390），是爱尔兰贵族，第二代基尔代尔伯爵托马斯·菲茨杰拉德与阿尔斯特伯爵之女琼·德·伯格的次子。1329年幼兄第三代伯爵理查夭折，他遂袭爵。

Maurice FitzGerald (c. 1105–1176), Lord of Llanstephan in Wales, was a Cambro-Norman baron and a leader of the Norman invasion of Ireland. He fought at the Battle of Crug Mawr in 1136, and in 1146 lost Llansteffan Castle to the Welsh.

In 1169 he sailed to Ireland to back the exiled Leinster king Diarmait Mac Murchada, helping take Wexford and fighting in the storming of Dublin in 1171. He died around September 1176; his sons Thomas and Gerald founded the FitzGerald Desmond and Kildare lines.

en:
Maurice FitzGerald (c. 1194–1257), second Lord of Offaly, was an Anglo-Norman soldier who served as Justiciar of Ireland from 1232 to 1245. At the Curragh in 1234 he defeated Richard Marshal, who died of his wounds amid rumours of betrayal.

As justiciar he joined the subjugation of Connacht in 1235 and in 1247 invaded Tír Chonaill, winning the Battle of Ballyshannon. In 1257 he fought Gofraidh Ó Domhnaill in single combat at Credan; both were gravely wounded, and Maurice died of his injuries at Youghal on 20 May.

Thomas FitzJohn FitzGerald (died 1328), second Earl of Kildare, was the son and heir of the first earl, John FitzThomas. In 1312 he married Joan de Burgh, daughter of the Earl of Ulster. During Edward Bruce's invasion he commanded an army against the Scots in Ulster, until Bruce was defeated and killed in 1318.

He served twice as Lord Justice of Ireland, from 1318 to 1321 and again from 1326 until his death. He died at Maynooth on 9 April 1328, leaving sons Richard and Maurice, who succeeded in turn as earl.

Thomas FitzMaurice (died 1213), Lord of OConnello and Shanid in Munster, was the eldest son of Maurice FitzGerald, Lord of Llanstephan, and founder of the Desmond branch of the Geraldines.

In 1210 he led an Anglo-Norman army gathered in Munster into Connacht, forcing its king Cathal Crobhdearg to negotiate with the Justiciar. He married Ellinor de Marisco, and their son John became first Baron Desmond.

en:
Alexander Yaroslavich Nevsky (1221–1263) was prince of Novgorod and later grand prince of Vladimir, the Rurikid who fought crusaders in the west while submitting to the Mongols in the east. Second son of Yaroslav II, he became prince of Novgorod in 1236. In July 1240 he attacked Swedish forces on the Neva; Nevsky, meaning of the Neva, was given to him in the 15th century.

Recalled in 1241 after crusaders took Pskov, he retook it and on 5 April 1242 met Livonian cavalry on Lake Peipus in the Battle on the Ice, halting the Teutonic Order's eastward push. When his brother Andrey plotted against the Mongols and fled, Alexander became grand prince of Vladimir in 1252.

On 14 November 1263 he died at Gorodets. The chronicle records Metropolitan Cyril saying the sun of the Suzdalian land had set. Canonized in 1547, his youngest son Daniel became prince of Moscow.

亚历山大·雅罗斯拉维奇·涅夫斯基（1221—1263）曾任诺夫哥罗德王公，后为弗拉基米尔大公，他在西面抗击十字军，在东面臣服于蒙古人。他是雅罗斯拉夫二世的次子，1236年出任诺夫哥罗德王公。1240年7月他在涅瓦河袭击瑞典军；“涅夫斯基”意为涅瓦河的，这称号15世纪才有。

1241年十字军占据普斯科夫，他被召回并夺回，1242年4月5日在楚德湖冰上之战中迎战利沃尼亚骑兵，挡住条顿骑士团东进。兄长安德烈反蒙古出逃后，他于1252年成为弗拉基米尔大公。

1263年11月14日他病逝于戈罗杰茨。编年史载都主教基里尔说，苏兹达尔之地的太阳落了。1547年教会封他为圣徒，他最小的儿子丹尼尔后来成为莫斯科王公。

Algimantas, also called Olgimund, was a prince of the Lithuanian Holshany family. Late chronicles make him Gediminas's viceroy in Kyiv after the city fell in 1321 or 1324, say he was baptized as Fyodor, and call him either a son of Mindaugas Holshansky or of the legendary Holsha.

Otherwise his name survives only in the patronymic of his son Ivan, named in documents of 1385–1388 as Ivan Algimantaitis, who fought for Vytautas in the Lithuanian civil war of 1381–1384.

en:
Anton Losenko (1737–1773) was a Russian neoclassical painter, born at Hlukhiv. Orphaned, he sang in the court choir at Saint Petersburg until his voice broke, then trained under Ivan Argunov and entered the Imperial Academy of Arts in 1759. Sent to Paris in 1760, he studied under Jean Restout the Younger.

In 1766–1769 he worked in Rome, studying Raphael and painting Cain and Abel. Back in Russia, his canvas Vladimir and Rogneda won him the title of academician; in 1772 he became professor and director of the Academy. He died in 1773.

Gleb Yurievich (c. 1130–1171), a son of Yuri Dolgorukiy and brother of Andrei Bogolyubsky, held Kanev from 1149 and in 1155 received Pereyaslavl, which he kept after his father's death. After Bogolyubsky's army sacked Kiev in 1169, Gleb took the Kievan throne.

en:
Igor II Olgovich (c. 1096–1147), son of Oleg of Chernigov, held the Kievan throne for less than a fortnight in 1146. His brother Vsevolod II had named him heir, but the Kievans called in his kinsman Iziaslav II, whose army defeated and captured Igor and threw him into a pit.

Released deathly ill in autumn 1146, he became a monk in Kiev. In 1147 a mob suspecting him of plotting to regain the throne tore down his sheltering balcony and killed him; he was venerated as a martyr.

Igor (c. 877–945) was Prince of Kiev from 912 to 945 and, by tradition, the son of Rurik. Left an infant at his father's death in 879, he grew up under the regency of his kinsman Oleg, who seized Kiev by killing its rulers.

In 941 and 944 Igor led Rus' fleets against Constantinople; Greek fire broke the first attack, and in 945 he made a treaty with Emperor Constantine VII. That year the Drevlians murdered him while collecting tribute a second time, after which his widow Olga took vengeance and the regency.

His reign was dominated by war with his uncle Yuri Dolgorukiy of Suzdalia, who drove him from Kiev in 1149; Iziaslav recovered the capital in 1151 and held it until his death in 1154. He was among the first Rus princes called tsar in the chronicles and founded the Volhynian Iziaslavichi line.
zh:
伊贾斯拉夫二世·姆斯季斯拉维奇（约1096—1154）是基辅大公姆斯季斯拉夫一世之子、弗拉基米尔·莫诺马赫之孙，登上基辅大公之位前先后统治多处领地。

1146年他入主基辅，在位期间主要与叔父、苏兹达尔的尤里·多尔戈鲁基交战，1149年被逐走，1151年收复基辅并统治到1154年去世。他是编年史最早称以“沙皇”的罗斯王公之一，也是沃伦伊贾斯拉维奇一系的始祖。

en:
Iziaslav Davidovich (died 1161), a son of Davyd of Chernigov, was prince of Starodub and Chernigov before he thrice seized the Kievan throne. After Iziaslav Mstislavich died in 1154 he took Kiev with Cuman help, but yielded it to Yuri Dolgorukiy, returning as grand prince after Yuri's death in 1157.

Driven out in 1158 for sheltering a fugitive, he crossed the frozen Dnieper with Cumans and retook Kiev by surprise in February 1161, only to be mortally wounded besieging Rostislav at Belgorod. He died on 6 March 1161.

伊贾斯拉夫·达维多维奇（？—1161）是切尔尼戈夫王公达维德之子，先为斯塔罗杜布和切尔尼戈夫王公，其后三度占据基辅大公之位。1154年伊贾斯拉夫·姆斯季斯拉维奇死后，他借波洛韦茨人之助夺取基辅，却被迫让给尤里·多尔戈鲁基；1157年尤里死后他重登大公公位。

Iziaslav IV Vladimirovich (born 1186, last attested 1235–1236), son of Vladimir Igorevich of Galicia, was prince of Novgorod-Seversk before claiming Kiev. In 1233 he joined Daniel Romanovich's campaign against the Hungarians in Galicia, then defected and ravaged Daniel's lands.

In 1234 he brought Cuman allies from the steppe, routed Grand Prince Vladimir Rurikovich and Daniel near Torchesk and captured Vladimir. In 1235 he joined Michael of Chernigov in capturing Kiev and became grand prince, after which the chronicles lose sight of him; his death date is unknown.

en:
Iziaslav I Yaroslavich (1024–1078) was the eldest son of Yaroslav the Wise. His marriage to Gertrude, sister of the Polish king Casimir I, sealed their 1043 agreement. Prince of Turov from 1045, he became Grand Prince of Kiev in 1054, ruling with his brothers Sviatoslav and Vsevolod, and helped compose the law code of Yaroslav's descendants.

In 1067 the brothers defeated and seized Vseslav of Polotsk under a truce. After the Cumans defeated them at the Alta River in 1068, a Kiev uprising drove Iziaslav into Polish exile.

Restored in 1069, he was expelled again in 1073 and regained Kiev only in 1077. On 3 October 1078 he fell fighting Oleg Sviatoslavich, the only ruling Grand Prince killed in battle.

伊贾斯拉夫一世·雅罗斯拉维奇（1024—1078）是智者雅罗斯拉夫的长子。他与波兰国王卡齐米日一世的妹妹格特鲁德联姻，巩固了双方于1043年达成的协议。他自1045年起任图罗夫王公，1054年成为基辅大公，与兄弟斯维亚托斯拉夫、弗谢沃洛德共同执政，并参与编纂《雅罗斯拉夫诸子法典》。

1067年，三兄弟击败波洛茨克王公弗谢斯拉夫，并借停战之机将其诱捕。1068年，他们在阿尔塔河被波洛伏齐人击败，基辅市民起义，伊贾斯拉夫被迫流亡波兰。

他于1069年复位，1073年再度被逐，直到1077年才重登基辅公位。1078年10月3日，他在与奥列格·斯维亚托斯拉维奇作战时阵亡，是唯一战死沙场的在任大公。

en:
Michael Vsevolodovich of Chernigov (c. 1185 – 20 September 1246), son of Vsevolod the Red, ruled several principalities including Novgorod, Galicia and Chernigov, and became grand prince of Kiev in 1236. He fought the Mongols at the Kalka River in 1223 and long contested Galicia-Volhynia with Daniel of Galicia.

During the Mongol invasion in 1239 he fled to Hungary, then returned to seek a patent from Batu Khan. In 1246 Batu executed him and his boyar Theodore for refusing Mongol purification rites; the Orthodox Church venerates both as martyrs.

Mikhail Yuryevich, called Mikhalko (c. 1145–1176), was a son of Yuri Dolgorukiy and half-brother of Andrei Bogolyubsky, who expelled him from Suzdalia. Named to the Kievan throne after Gleb's death in 1171, he declined it and sent his brother Vsevolod instead.

After Bogolyubsky's murder he took Vladimir, was driven to Chernigov by the Rostov and Suzdal boyars, returned to defeat Yaropolk Rostislavich in 1175, and ruled Vladimir until his death on 20 June 1176.

en:
Mindaugas Holshansky was a Lithuanian prince of the Holshany family whom the late chronicles make a kinsman of the legendary founder Holsha. They relate that after Gediminas defeated the forces of Kyiv on the Irpin River and took the city in 1321 or 1324, he appointed Mindaugas his viceroy there.

The chronicles disagree over his tie to the next prince, Algimantas, calling him either his son or his brother. These later chronicles are the sole record of his life.

Mstislav II Iziaslavich (c. 1125–1170), son of Grand Prince Iziaslav II, fought beside his father against Yuri Dolgorukiy and the princes of Chernigov. He defeated the Cumans in 1153, and in 1155 Dolgorukiy drove him to Poland; returning in 1156, he beat his rival in Volhynia.

He held the Kievan throne in 1158–1159 and again from 1167, until Andrei Bogolyubsky's army sacked Kiev in 1169 and forced him back to Volhynia. He retook Kiev in 1170 but died on 19 August, leaving a son, Roman the Great of Galicia-Volhynia.

Mstislav Romanovich the Old (died 1223), son of Roman Rostislavich of Smolensk and baptized Boris, ruled Smolensk before becoming grand prince of Kiev in 1214. He joined the 1185 campaign against the Cumans and in 1221 drove off an invading Hungarian army.

In April 1223 he led the southern Rus' princes against the Mongols; after the catastrophe on the Kalka River he was trapped at a nearby palisade, captured, and executed, reportedly smothered under planking in vengeance for the slain envoys.

Mstislav Vladimirovich (1076–1132), called the Great, was the eldest son of Vladimir Monomakh. He ruled Novgorod from 1095 to 1117, served as his father's co-ruler, and succeeded him as grand prince of Kiev in 1125. In 1096 he defeated his father's cousin Oleg of Chernigov on the Koloksha river.

As grand prince he campaigned against Polotsk, the Cumans and Lithuanians. By his Swedish wife Christina his daughters married the kings of Norway and Denmark. When he died on 14 April 1132, the chronicler wrote, the land of Rus was torn apart.

Oleg Svyatoslavich (c. 1052–1115), a son of Grand Prince Sviatoslav II of Kiev, ruled Vladimir-Volynsk, Tmutarakan, Chernigov and Novgorod-Seversk. In 1078 he allied with the Cumans to seize Chernigov from his uncle Vsevolod, but defeat drove him back to Tmutarakan; he was handed to Byzantium and exiled to Rhodes.

Returning with Cuman aid, he retook Chernigov from Vladimir Monomakh in 1094, lost it in 1096, and from 1097 held Novgorod-Seversk. He founded the Olgovichi clan and never ruled Kiev.

Roman Rostislavich (c. 1132–1180), eldest son of Rostislav Mstislavich, joined Andrei Bogolyubsky's sack of Kiev in 1169, and in 1171 Andrei made him grand prince. Two years later Andrei forced him back to Smolensk for shielding boyars suspected of murdering Gleb.

en:
Rurik (died 879) was the Varangian chieftain whom Rus' tradition credits with founding the dynasty that ruled Kievan Rus'. The Primary Chronicle records that East Slavic and Finnic tribes drove the Varangians across the sea but then fell into conflict, and in 862 invited Rurik and his brothers to restore order.

Chronicle manuscripts place his first settlement at Novgorod or Ladoga. After his brothers died he absorbed their lands. On his deathbed he entrusted his young son Igor and his realm to his kinsman Oleg, who later seized Kiev and established Kievan Rus'.

en:
Rurik Rostislavich (c. 1140–1212), son of Rostislav Mstislavich of Kiev, led the Smolensk branch of the Rurikids for nearly forty years. Between 1173 and 1210 he seized the Kievan throne at least six times, and from 1181 to 1194 ruled Kiev jointly with Sviatoslav of Chernigov.

In 1203 he and his Cuman allies sacked Kiev; forced into a monastery in 1204 by Roman Mstislavich, he broke his vows and returned. Vsevolod the Red displaced him in 1210, and he died in Chernigov.

en:
Olga (c. 900–969) became regent of Kievan Rus' in 945, after the Drevlians killed her husband Igor, ruling for her young son Sviatoslav as the first woman to head the state. The Primary Chronicle recounts her revenge: Drevlian envoys were buried alive or burned, and in 946 she fired their capital Iskorosten by tying burning sulphur to birds.

She regularised tribute collection through posts called pogosti. Baptised around 955 and taking the name Elena, she was the first Christian Rurikid ruler, honoured as a saint Equal to the Apostles. She died on 11 July 969.

The Primary Chronicle recounts her revenge: Drevlian envoys were buried alive or burned, and in 946 she fired their capital [ShowLocationName('korosten')] by tying burning sulphur to birds.

She regularised tribute collection through posts called pogosti. Baptised around 955 and taking the name Elena, she was the first Christian Rurikid ruler, honoured as a saint Equal to the Apostles. She died on 11 July 969.

奥莉加（约900—969）于945年成为基辅罗斯摄政：当时德列夫利安人杀死了她的丈夫伊戈尔，她代幼子斯维亚托斯拉夫执政，是首位统治这个国家的女性。《往年纪事》记载了她的报复：德列夫利安使者被活埋或烧死；946年，她命人把系着燃硫布条的鸟放出，焚毁其都城伊斯科罗斯坚。

en:
The sixteenth-century Belarusian-Lithuanian chronicles make Stanislav the last Rurikid prince of Kyiv. They relate that the Lithuanian grand duke Gediminas invaded and in 1320 defeated him and his allies at the battle on the Irpin River, after which Stanislav fled to Bryansk and then to Ryazan.

In Ryazan the prince gave him his daughter Olga in marriage. These accounts were first written down two centuries after the events, and Stanislav has also been identified with the Kyivan prince Fyodor.

据16世纪的白俄罗斯-立陶宛编年史记载，斯坦尼斯拉夫是基辅的末代留里克王公。书中写道，立陶宛大公格迪米纳斯入侵他的领地，于1320年在伊尔平河之战中击败他与盟友的联军；斯坦尼斯拉夫先逃到布良斯克，再投奔梁赞。

Sviatopolk II Iziaslavich (1050–1113), baptized Michael, was the son of Iziaslav I of Kiev by a concubine. He held Polotsk from 1069, ruled Novgorod in 1078–1088 and Turov from 1088, before succeeding to Kiev in 1093 after Vsevolod's death. His reign was dominated by rivalry and shifting alliances with his cousin Vladimir Monomakh.

The Cumans routed their armies at the Stugna River in 1093, but together they defeated the Cumans at the Salnytsia River in 1111. Sviatopolk encouraged the embellishment of St Michael's Abbey in Kiev and died on 16 April 1113.

en:
Sviatopolk I Vladimirovich, called the Accursed (c. 979–1019), was made prince of Turov in 988 by Vladimir the Great, whose son or stepson he was, and married a daughter of Bolesław I of Poland. Encouraged by his wife and Bishop Reinbern, he prepared to fight Vladimir, who imprisoned them; Reinbern died in captivity.

After Vladimir died in 1015 he seized Kiev; chronicles accuse him of murdering his brothers Boris and Gleb, later venerated as saints. Yaroslav of Novgorod defeated him at Lyubech in 1016, but Sviatopolk returned in 1018 with Polish and Pecheneg help and retook Kiev, only to quarrel with Bolesław. In 1019 Yaroslav routed him on the Alta River, and Sviatopolk died fleeing west.

斯维亚托波尔克·弗拉基米罗维奇（约979—1019），绰号恶棍，988年被弗拉基米尔一世封为图罗夫王公——他可能是弗拉基米尔之子，也可能是其继子——并娶波兰公爵波列斯瓦夫一世之女。在妻子和主教赖恩伯恩的鼓动下，他准备对抗弗拉基米尔，后者将他们囚禁，赖恩伯恩死于狱中。

Sviatoslav II Yaroslavich (1027–1076), a younger son of Yaroslav the Wise, received Chernigov when his father divided Kievan Rus among his sons in 1054. With his brothers Iziaslav of Kiev and Vsevolod of Pereyaslav he formed a princely triumvirate.

The triumvirate defeated Vseslav of Polotsk in 1067 but was routed by the Cumans on the Alta in 1068. In 1073, backed by Vsevolod, he drove Iziaslav from Kiev and ruled as grand prince until his death on 27 December 1076.

Sviatoslav III Vsevolodovich (c. 1123–1194), eldest son of Vsevolod II Olgovich, took Chernigov in 1164 after holding several lesser principalities. He seized Kiev from Yaroslav II Iziaslavich and, after his long northern campaign of 1180–1181 against Vsevolod the Big Nest, ruled the city while Rurik Rostislavich held the surrounding Kievan land.

In the steppe he captured the Cuman khan Kobyak and defeated Khan Konchak. In 1185, after his kinsman Igor's defeat, he relieved Pereyaslavl, and he died on 27 July 1194.

Sviatoslav Olgovich (c. 1107–1164), son of Oleg of Chernigov, received Chernigov in 1154 after ruling lesser towns. Having helped his brother Vsevolod II seize Kiev in 1139, he was driven out after Vsevolod's death by Iziaslav II, who captured his brother Igor; a Kievan mob killed Igor in 1147.

Sviatoslav made common cause with Yuri Dolgorukiy; their meeting on the Moskva river in 1147 is Moscow's first appearance in the chronicles. He died on 14 February 1164, and his son Igor Sviatoslavich inspired The Tale of Igor's Campaign.

en:
Sviatoslav the Brave (c. 943–972) ruled Kiev from 945, under his mother Olga's regency until about 963. A lifelong pagan, he spent his reign on campaign. He subdued East Slavic tribes, and around 965 destroyed the Khazar strongholds of Sarkel and Atil, breaking Khazar power.

In 967 he invaded Bulgaria at Byzantine prompting, but refused to withdraw and in 969 moved his seat to Pereyaslavets on the Danube. In 970 he appointed his sons Yaropolk, Oleg and Vladimir to rule Kiev, Drelinia and Novgorod.

Emperor John Tzimiskes forced him out after the siege of Dorostolon in 971. In early 972 Pechenegs killed him at the Dnieper rapids, and Khan Kurya had his skull made into a drinking cup.

斯维亚托斯拉夫一世·伊戈列维奇（约943—972），绰号“勇敢者”，自945年起统治基辅，约963年以前由母亲奥莉加摄政。他终生信奉异教，亲政后连年征战。他征服东斯拉夫部族，约965年摧毁可萨人的萨克尔、阿的尔等要塞，击灭可萨汗国。

971年，拜占庭皇帝约翰·齐米斯西斯经多罗斯托隆围城战迫使他撤出。972年初，他在第聂伯河险滩被佩切涅格人袭杀，可汗库里亚将他的头盖骨制成酒杯。

en:
Fyodor (Teodoras; fl. 14th century) was the Orthodox prince of Kiev under Lithuanian overlordship. In the early 1320s Grand Duke Gediminas of Lithuania defeated Stanislav of Kiev on the Irpen River and brought the city under his control.

In 1331 Fyodor stopped Archbishop Vasily Kalika of Novgorod outside Kiev alongside a Tatar tax collector, showing that the city still paid tribute to the Golden Horde.

A property list of Metropolitan Theognostus, compiled in 1331, names a Fyodor as a brother of Gediminas; modern historians identify him with the prince of Kiev. After the Lithuanian victory at the Battle of Blue Waters in 1362, he was replaced by Vladimir, son of Algirdas.

费奥多尔（14世纪人）是立陶宛宗主权下信奉东正教的基辅王公。1320年代初，立陶宛大公格迪米纳斯在伊尔平河之战击败基辅王公斯坦尼斯拉夫，控制了基辅。

1331年，费奥多尔与一名鞑靼征税官在城外拦阻诺夫哥罗德大主教瓦西里·卡利卡，表明基辅仍向金帐汗国纳贡。

1331年编订的都主教费奥格诺斯特财物清单称一位费奥多尔为格迪米纳斯之弟；现代历史学家认为他就是基辅王公。1362年立陶宛在蓝水河之战获胜后，他被阿尔吉尔达斯之子弗拉基米尔取代。

Viacheslav Vladimirovich (1083–c. 1154/1155), a son of Vladimir Monomakh, held Smolensk from 1113. On 18 February 1139 he succeeded his brother Yaropolk II as grand prince of Kiev, but within weeks Vsevolod Olgovich of Chernigov drove him from the throne.

During the long struggle between Yuri Dolgorukiy and Iziaslav II for Kiev, Viacheslav twice allied with his nephew Iziaslav, ruling Kiev jointly with him from 1151 until his death c. 1154/1155. He was buried in Saint Sophia Cathedral.

Vladimir III Igorevich (1170–September 1211), eldest son of Igor Svyatoslavich of Novgorod-Seversk, ruled Galicia in 1206–1208 and 1210–1211. He joined his father's 1185 campaign against the Cumans and was captured by Khan Konchak; he returned in 1188 with Konchak's daughter Svoboda, whom he married.

After Roman Mstislavich fell in 1205 he and his brothers seized Halych, but their reprisals against the boyars brought a Hungarian and Polish invasion in 1211; his brothers were hanged and Vladimir died that September.

弗拉基米尔三世·伊戈列维奇（1170年—1211年9月）是诺夫哥罗德-谢韦尔斯基的勇者伊戈尔的长子，两度统治加利奇（1206—1208年，1210—1211年）。他年轻时随父亲参加1185年征讨库曼人的远征，被孔恰克汗俘虏；1188年他携孔恰克之女斯沃博达归来并与之成婚。

1205年罗曼·姆斯季斯拉维奇死后，他与诸弟攻占加利奇，但他们对波雅尔的迫害引来1211年匈牙利和波兰联军入侵，他的兄弟被绞死，弗拉基米尔本人也于当年9月死去。

Vladimir II Monomakh (1053–1125), son of Vsevolod I and a Greek princess possibly of the Monomachos family, ruled Smolensk, Chernigov and Pereyaslavl before taking Kiev. He convoked princely congresses, beginning with Lyubech in 1097, to unite the Rurikids, and routed the Cumans in 1111.

After the 1113 Kiev uprising he was invited to the throne, where he curbed usury and issued a statute added to Russkaya Pravda. His Instruction to his children survives. He died in 1125 and was succeeded by his son Mstislav.

弗拉基米尔·莫诺马赫（1053—1125）是基辅大公弗谢沃洛德一世与一位希腊公主之子，其母可能出自莫诺马赫家族。他登上基辅公位前先后统治斯摩棱斯克、切尔尼戈夫和佩列亚斯拉夫尔。他召集以1097年柳别奇大会为首的数次王公大会以团结留里克王公，又于1111年大败波洛韦茨人。

1113年基辅爆发民变后，他被迎立为大公，任内限制高利贷，所颁法令后被补入《罗斯真理》。他写给子女的《家训》流传至今。1125年去世，其子姆斯季斯拉夫继位。

Vladimir III Mstislavich (1132–1171), called Macheshich as the son of Mstislav the Great's second marriage, was a grandson of Vladimir Monomakh. A Volhynian prince, he held a string of Volhynian towns, and in 1150 married a daughter of the Serbian zupan Belos Vukanovic.

After Gleb of Kiev's death he occupied the Kievan throne in February 1171 but ruled only about three months, dying in May 1171; his short reign is omitted from some lists of Kievan princes.

Vladimir IV Rurikovich (1187–1239), second son of Rurik Rostislavich of Smolensk, held Pereyaslavl from 1206 and Smolensk from 1212. He fought the Mongols on the Kalka River in 1223, after which he succeeded Mstislav the Old as grand prince of Kyiv.

In 1235 he was defeated and captured by the Cumans, losing Kyiv to Iziaslav; ransomed, he briefly retook it before yielding it to Yaroslav Vsevolodovich in 1236. He died at Ovruch in 1239, on the day the Mongols stormed Pereyaslavl.

Vladimir-Ivan Ivanovich was a Rurikid prince of Putivl who held the Kyiv throne in the first quarter of the fourteenth century. He appears only in the Vvedensky Synodikon, which calls him a grandson of Ivan Romanovich of Putivl.

The synodikon records that he secured Kyiv with the backing of Tokhta, khan of the Golden Horde from 1291 to 1312. Historians identify Andrei of Ovruch and Fyodor of Kyiv as his possible brothers.

en:
Vladimir I Sviatoslavich, called the Great (c. 958–1015), was prince of Novgorod from 970 and grand prince of Kiev from 978, the ruler who turned Rus' to Christianity. After Yaropolk murdered their brother Oleg in 977, Vladimir fled abroad, gathered a Varangian army and deposed Yaropolk in 978.

A thorough pagan, said to keep eight hundred concubines, he raised a shrine in Kiev to six gods headed by Perun. He sent envoys to test the faiths; at Constantinople they reported knowing not whether they were in Heaven or on Earth. In 988 he accepted Byzantine Christianity, married Emperor Basil II's sister Anna, and Christianized Rus'.

He founded the Church of the Tithes and installed his twelve sons over his principalities. In 1014 his son Yaroslav stopped paying tribute; Vladimir was gathering troops against him when he died on 15 July 1015. Both the Catholic and Orthodox churches canonized him.

弗拉基米尔一世·斯维亚托斯拉维奇（约958—1015），称伟大者，自970年起统治诺夫哥罗德，978年起成为基辅大公，是使罗斯转向基督教的统治者。977年亚罗波尔克杀死奥列格后，他逃到海外召集瓦良格军队，于978年推翻亚罗波尔克。

他本是彻底的多神教徒，传说有八百名妾，并在基辅为佩伦等六位神灵立庙。他派使者考察各大宗教；使者在君士坦丁堡回报说，不知身在天上还是人间。988年他接受拜占庭基督教，迎娶皇帝巴西尔二世之妹安娜，使罗斯基督教化。

他创建什一教堂，并让十二个儿子分驻各属地。1014年雅罗斯拉夫停止纳贡，他正集结军队讨伐，却于1015年7月15日病逝。天主教与东正教会都封他为圣徒。

Vsevolod II Olgovich (c. 1094–1146), son of Oleg of Chernigov, ruled Chernigov from 1127 and Kiev from 1139. After years of strife with Yaropolk II, he drove Yaropolk's brother Viacheslav from Kiev and seized the throne in 1139.

Married to a daughter of Mstislav the Great, he made the Kievans swear the cross to his brother Igor as his heir. He died a monk named Gavriil on 1 August 1146, and Kiev rose against Igor.

Vsevolod III Yuryevich the Big Nest (1154–12 April 1212), son of Yuri Dolgorukiy, was born at Dmitrov, the town his father founded for his birth, and grew up at the Byzantine court. In 1173 Smolensk princes placed him on the Kievan throne, and in 1176 he succeeded his brother as grand prince of Vladimir.

He curbed the boyars of Rostov and Suzdal, raided Volga Bulgaria, and in 1207 burned Ryazan. He fathered at least fourteen children, earning his nickname, and four sons later ruled Vladimir.

Vsevolod Svyatoslavich the Red (died August 1212), eldest son of Sviatoslav Vsevolodovich of Kiev, was prince of Chernigov and held Kiev four times between 1203 and 1212. He campaigned against the Cumans in his youth, yet later allied with them in his wars for Kiev.

He seized Kiev in 1206 and 1208 but was twice driven out by Rurik Rostislavich, and in 1210 retook it with backing from Vsevolod the Big Nest of Vladimir. His son Michael of Chernigov later ruled Kiev.

Vsevolod I Yaroslavich (1030–1093), the fifth son of Yaroslav the Wise, received Pereyaslav when his father divided Kievan Rus in 1054. Around 1046 he married a Byzantine kinswoman who bore his eldest son, Vladimir Monomakh.

With his brothers Iziaslav and Sviatoslav he formed the triumvirate that codified the Russkaya Pravda, and he backed Sviatoslav's seizure of Kiev in 1073. After Iziaslav's death he took the Kievan throne in 1078. A man said to speak five languages, he died on 13 April 1093.

Yaropolk II Vladimirovich (1082–1139), a son of Vladimir Monomakh, was prince of Pereyaslavl from 1114 and grand prince of Kiev from 1132, succeeding his brother Mstislav the Great. His reign was consumed by strife among the Monomakhovichi: his half-brother Yuri Dolgorukiy and nephews contested Pereyaslavl, while Vsevolod Olgovich of Chernigov and his Cuman allies ravaged the Kiev lands.

Defeat in 1135 cost him Kursk. In 1139 he besieged Chernigov with Hungarian troops, forced Vsevolod to peace, and died on 18 February 1139.

en:
Yaropolk I Sviatoslavich (c. 958–978), eldest son of Sviatoslav Igorevich, became prince of Kiev after his father's death in 972. War soon broke out between him and his brothers Oleg and Vladimir. In 977 he defeated Oleg, who died in the fighting, and took Novgorod, forcing Vladimir to flee to Scandinavia.

Vladimir returned in 978 with Varangian mercenaries and seized Polotsk and Kiev. Yaropolk's adviser Blud betrayed him, urging him to flee to Rodnya, where Vladimir besieged him, and Yaropolk was murdered at a parley on 11 June 978. His Greek wife bore Sviatopolk the Accursed, whose father may have been Yaropolk or Vladimir.

Yaroslav II Vsevolodovich (1191–1246), a son of Vsevolod the Big Nest, was prince of Pereslavl-Zalessky from 1212 and repeatedly ruled Novgorod. In 1236 he took Kyiv.

After his brother Yuri fell against the Mongols at the Sit in 1238, he became grand prince of Vladimir, and in 1243 Batu Khan granted him the first Mongol patent over Kyiv. Summoned to Karakorum for Güyük's enthronement, he died there on 30 September 1246, reportedly poisoned by Töregene Khatun. His sons included Alexander Nevsky.

Yaroslav III Yaroslavich (1230–1271) was a younger son of Yaroslav II of Vladimir and a brother of Alexander Nevsky. In 1247 he received Tver, founding the Tver branch of the Rurikids, and he briefly held Novgorod in 1255.

After Alexander Nevsky died in 1263, he disputed the grand principality with his brother Andrey; the Golden Horde ruled in his favour and he held Vladimir until his death. He died on 9 September 1271 returning from Sarai, and his son Svyatoslav inherited Tver.

en:
Yaroslav I Vladimirovich, known as the Wise (c. 978–1054), was a son of Vladimir the Great who ruled Novgorod and withheld tribute from Kiev in 1014. From 1015 he warred with his brother Sviatopolk and took the Kievan throne in 1019.

Defeated by his brother Mstislav in 1024, he divided the land until 1036, when he began ruling alone. In 1030 he captured Tartu, and the next year he recovered the Cherven towns from Poland. He crushed the Pechenegs near Kiev in 1036, built Saint Sophia Cathedral, and issued the law code Russkaya Pravda.

He married Ingegerd of Sweden, and their daughters became queens of France, Norway and Hungary. He died in February 1054.

雅罗斯拉夫一世·弗拉基米罗维奇（约978—1054），人称智者，是弗拉基米尔一世之子，曾任诺夫哥罗德王公，1014年停止向基辅缴纳贡赋。1015年起他与兄弟斯维亚托波尔克交战，1019年夺得基辅大公公位。

1024年他被兄弟姆斯季斯拉夫击败，双方分治罗斯，直到1036年才独掌大权。1030年他攻占塔尔图，次年又从波兰夺回切尔文诸城。1036年他在基辅附近大败佩切涅格人，修建圣索菲亚大教堂，并颁行法典《罗斯真理》。

他娶瑞典的因吉尔达，三个女儿分别成为法国、挪威和匈牙利的王后。他于1054年2月去世。

en:
Yuri I Vladimirovich Dolgorukiy (c. 1099–1157), a son of Vladimir Monomakh, ruled Rostov and Suzdal from 1108 and built the northeastern backwater into Vladimir-Suzdal. After clashing with the Rostov boyars he moved his capital to Suzdal in 1121 and founded fortified towns including Pereslavl-Zalessky, Yuriev-Polsky and Dmitrov.

In 1147 he met his ally Sviatoslav Olgovich at Moscow, and in 1156 he fortified the settlement, earning the name founder of Moscow. He twice seized Kiev and died there, apparently poisoned, in May 1157.

尤里·弗拉基米罗维奇·多尔戈鲁基（约1099—1157）是弗拉基米尔·莫诺马赫之子，1108年起受封罗斯托夫和苏兹达尔，把东北边陲经营成弗拉基米尔—苏兹达尔公国。与罗斯托夫波雅尔冲突后，他于1121年将都城迁至苏兹达尔，又修建佩列亚斯拉夫尔—扎列斯基、尤里耶夫—波利斯基、德米特罗夫等设防城镇。

en:
Kim Il-son (1464–1498) was a Joseon scholar, censor and state historian of the Gimhae Kim clan. While drafting the Annals of King Seongjong, he entered into his private notes the Lament for the Righteous Emperor, an essay by his teacher Kim Chong-jik that obliquely condemned King Sejo's seizure of the throne.

Seongjong had favored the Sarim scholars to check the Hungu faction, bringing the two groups into conflict. In 1498 Hungu officials uncovered Kim Il-son's notes, and Yu Ja-gwang reported the essay to King Yeonsangun.

The king condemned it as treason: Kim Il-son was executed, his dead teacher's body was exhumed and mutilated, and Sarim followers were killed or banished in the first literati purge.

金馹孙（1464—1498），本贯金海金氏，是朝鲜的文臣、言官与史官。他在编修《成宗实录》时，把老师金宗直影射批判世祖篡位的《吊义帝文》写入自己的史草。

成宗曾重用士林派学者牵制勋旧派，两派因而冲突。1498年勋旧派大臣发现金馹孙的史草，柳子光将文章呈报燕山君。

燕山君定为叛逆：金馹孙被处死，已故的金宗直被剖棺戮尸，士林门人或死或流，史称戊午士祸，即第一次士祸。

en:
Bukuku is the last king of the legendary Tembuzi dynasty of Kitara in Nyoro tradition, and its only ruler not born of the Gabu clan: a Ranzi clansman and commoner who had served King Isaza as gatekeeper. After Isaza was trapped in the underworld, Bukuku seized power, but most chiefs rebelled and his rule shrank to the south-west.

Witch-doctors warned that his daughter Nyinamwiru's son would kill him, so he shut her away in a house entered only through his palace. Her son Karubumbi, later called Ndahura, killed him over a cattle-watering quarrel and founded the Chwezi dynasty.

布库库是尼奥罗口传传统中基塔拉传说时代滕布齐王朝的末代国王，也是唯一不出身加布氏族的统治者：他是兰齐氏族的平民，曾在国王伊萨扎身边任守门近臣。伊萨扎被困冥界后，布库库夺取权位，但多数郡的酋长起兵反叛，他的统治退缩到基塔拉西南一隅。

巫师警告他，女儿尼亚姆武鲁之子会取他性命，他便将女儿幽禁在一座只能经由王宫进入的屋中。后来尼亚姆武鲁之子基亚鲁邦比（后改名恩达胡拉）因饮牛用水的争执杀死布库库，建立巴契韦齐王朝。

en:
Ndahura, also called Karubumbi, is the semi-legendary founder and first king of the Chwezi dynasty of the Empire of Kitara in western Uganda. Kitara oral tradition tells that he was a grandson of the Tembuzi king Bukuku, whom he killed in a quarrel over watering cattle before seizing the throne.

He then subdued rebellious chiefs and led campaigns said to carry Kitara's power into neighbouring lands. Traditions disagree over his end: he vanished on campaign in Ihangiro or was swallowed into the underworld, and Wamara succeeded him.

en:
Nyinamwiru, whose name means ‘commoner mother’, is the only child of Bukuku, the last Tembuzi king of Kitara in Nyoro oral tradition. Witch-doctors warned Bukuku that his daughter's son would kill him, so he shut her away in a house accessible only through his palace; some accounts add that he maimed her to destroy her beauty.

While she was confined, Isimbwa, son of King Isaza, climbed into her room by a ladder and stayed with her for months before leaving. She bore a son, Karubumbi, later called Ndahura, who killed Bukuku and founded the Chwezi dynasty of Kitara.

被幽禁期间，国王伊萨扎之子伊辛布瓦顺梯子爬入她的房间，与她同居数月后离去。尼亚姆武鲁生下儿子基亚鲁邦比，即后来的恩达胡拉；他杀死布库库，建立了基塔拉的[ShowDynastyName('bachwezi_dynasty')]王朝。

en:
Aji Batara Agung Paduka Nira, titled Aji di Dalam Taju, was the second king of Kutai Kartanegara, the Hindu kingdom on the Mahakam River in eastern Borneo. In 1325 he succeeded his father Aji Batara Agung Dewa Sakti, who had founded the realm at Kutai Lama, and ruled there until 1360.

He married Perwati Dewi, daughter of Maharaja Guna Perana Tungga of Kutai Martapura, a marriage tie with the older Martapura dynasty. Their son Aji Maharaja Sultan succeeded him as the third king.

阿吉·巴塔拉·阿贡·帕杜卡·尼拉，称号阿吉·迪达兰·塔朱，是婆罗洲东部马哈坎河畔印度教王国古泰-卡塔内加拉的第二任国王。1325年，他继在古泰拉玛开国的父亲阿吉·巴塔拉·阿贡·德瓦·萨克蒂之后继位，统治至1360年。

他娶古泰-摩多补罗摩诃罗阇古纳·佩拉纳·通加之女佩尔瓦蒂·德维为妻，与老牌的摩多补罗王朝联姻。其子阿吉·摩诃罗阇·苏丹继位，为第三代国王。

en:
Dietrich VII (c. 1256–1305) ruled the County of Cleves from 1275. He kept Cleves neutral in the 1288 Battle of Worringen and was a trusted councillor of the kings of Germany. In 1290 King Rudolf of Habsburg granted him Duisburg.

He pushed dike-building and internal colonization and was buried at Bedburg abbey. By Margaret of Guelders he fathered Otto; his second wife Margaret von Neu-Kyburg, wed in 1290, bore the later counts Dietrich VIII and John.

zh:
迪特里希七世（约1256—1305）自1275年起统治克莱沃伯国。他在1288年的沃林根战役中保持中立，是德意志国王信赖的顾问。1290年，国王鲁道夫·冯·哈布斯堡将杜伊斯堡封赐给他。

他大力修筑堤坝、推动境内拓殖，死后葬于贝德堡修道院教堂。他与海尔德的玛格丽特生下奥托，1290年续娶的诺伊-基堡的玛格丽特则为他生下后来的伯爵迪特里希八世和约翰。

en:
Dietrich VIII (c. 1291–1347) ruled the County of Cleves from 1310, when he succeeded his half-brother Otto and defeated the claims of Otto's widow and her allies, among them the archbishop of Cologne. In 1318 he settled the succession with his younger brother John, who would inherit if Dietrich had no sons.

He married Margaret of Guelders in 1308 and Maria of Jülich in 1340. He encouraged internal colonization, raised Uedem and Sonsbeck to town status, and founded the collegiate church at Kleve. His brother John succeeded him.

克莱沃伯爵迪特里希八世（约1291—1347）于1310年继承异母兄奥托的爵位，并艰难挫败了奥托遗孀联合科隆大主教等人提出的争位要求。1318年，他与弟弟约翰商定继承安排：若自己没有儿子，伯爵之位由约翰继承。

他于1308年娶海尔德的玛格丽特，1340年续娶于利希的玛丽亚。他在境内推动拓殖，将于德姆和松斯贝克升格为城市，并创立了克莱沃修道院教堂。他死后由弟弟约翰继位。

en:
Elisabeth of Cleves (1307–1382) was a daughter of Count Dietrich VIII and Margaret of Guelders. She first married Gerard van Voorne, who died in 1337.

In 1338 she married Otto the Younger, only son of Landgrave Henry II of Hesse, famed in legend as Otto the Archer; the marriage was childless. Otto died suddenly at Spangenberg Castle in 1366, amid rumours of poison. Elisabeth survived him by sixteen years.

克莱沃的伊丽莎白（1307—1382）是克莱沃伯爵迪特里希八世与海尔德的玛格丽特之女。她先嫁给赫拉德·范福尔讷，丈夫于1337年去世。

1338年，她改嫁黑森领地伯爵海因里希二世的独子、传说中被称为“射手奥托”的小奥托，两人没有子女。奥托1366年在施潘根贝格城堡暴卒，传闻系中毒而亡。伊丽莎白比丈夫多活了十六年。

en:
Irmgard of Cleves (1307–1362) was the only daughter of Otto, Count of Cleves, and his wife Mechteld von Virneburg; her father died soon after her birth. In 1327 she married John IV, Lord of Arkel.

The couple had four children, Matilda, John, Otto and Elisabeth, and their son Otto succeeded John IV as Lord of Arkel. Irmgard died in 1362.

en:
John of Cleves (1293–1368) was the last count of Cleves of the old Cleves dynasty, ruling from 1347 to 1368. A younger son of Count Dietrich VII, he was trained for the church and served as dean of Cologne Cathedral before giving up his offices to succeed his sonless brother Dietrich VIII.

In 1348 he married Mechtild of Guelders, but the marriage was childless. He backed Rainald III in the Guelders civil war, and on his death Cleves passed to his nephew Adolf III of the Marck.

en:
Margareta von Neu-Kyburg (c. 1272–1333) was the second wife of Count Dietrich VII of Cleves. Daughter of Eberhard I of Habsburg-Laufenburg and Anna of Kyburg, she was kinswoman to the Habsburg kings. After Dietrich's first wife died, she married him in 1290; that year Rudolf granted Dietrich Duisburg.

When her stepson Otto succeeded his father in 1305, he faced claims from Margareta and her sons Dietrich and John. Both sons later ruled Cleves. Margareta died at Kleve in April 1333.

en:
Margaret of Guelders (1288–1333) was a daughter of Reginald I, Count of Guelders, and his wife Margaret of Dampierre. In 1297 she was betrothed to Dietrich of Cleves, the future Count Dietrich VIII, and the marriage was celebrated around 1308.

Her daughters included Margaret, who married Count Adolf II of the Marck in 1332, and Elisabeth, later the wife of Otto the Younger of Hesse. She died in 1333, and Dietrich then married Maria of Jülich.

Otto (c. 1278–1310) was Count of Cleves from 1305, when he succeeded his father Dietrich VII, until his early death at Horstmar five years later. As eldest son of Dietrich's first marriage, he faced claims from his stepmother Margareta von Neu-Kyburg and her sons.

His first wife Adelheid von der Mark died childless about 1301; in 1308 he married Mechtild von Virneburg. Their daughter Irmgard later married Adolf II of the Marck. Otto was succeeded by his half-brother Dietrich VIII.

en:
Arjun Pal was a raja of the Jadaun Rajputs. He recovered the Bayana fort and its surrounding lands from Muslim rule, then in 1348 founded a safer capital at Kalyanpuri in the Chambal valley; the city later became Karauli.

He subdued the local Mewati and Mina chieftains and consolidated Jadaun power there. Tradition dates his reign to 1327–1361.

en:
Durlabh Narayan was a mid-fourteenth-century king of the Kamata kingdom, ruling from its capital Kamatapur. After his father's cousin Dharma Narayan seized power following the king's death, Durlabh Narayan challenged the usurper and the two partitioned the kingdom, Durlabh Narayan keeping lands including Kamrup, Koch Bihar and Kamatapur.

His court poets Hema Saraswati and Harivara Vipra composed the earliest surviving works of Assamese literature. He was succeeded by his son Indra Narayan, whose reign was shaken by the invasion of Sikandar Shah of Bengal in 1357–1390.

杜尔拉布·纳拉扬是14世纪中叶卡玛塔王国的国王，以迦摩多城为都。其父波罗陀波德瓦杰王死后，父亲的堂兄弟达尔马·纳拉扬篡夺王位，他起兵相争，最终两人瓜分王国，杜尔拉布·纳拉扬得到迦摩缕波、库奇比哈尔和都城迦摩多城等地。

他宫廷中的诗人赫摩·娑罗室伐底与诃利婆罗·毗波罗创作了现存最早的阿萨姆语文学作品。其子因陀罗·纳拉扬继位后，王国在1357—1390年遭孟加拉的锡坎达尔沙入侵而衰落。

en:
Johann of Saxe-Lauenburg (c. 1318–1370) was the youngest son of Duke Eric I of Saxe-Lauenburg and Elisabeth of Pomerania. Destined for the church, he studied at Montpellier and held several benefices before Pope Clement VI appointed him bishop of Cammin in 1343.

He held a diocesan synod in 1352 and resisted Gniezno's claims in his exempt diocese. In 1356 a treaty with Bogislaw V placed the see under ducal protection. He died in 1370 and was buried in Cammin Cathedral.
