en:
Dharm Chand (r. 1321–1344) was a raja of the Chand dynasty of Kumaon in the lower Himalayas, ruling from Champawat. Kumaoni tradition credits him with defending the hill kingdom against the Delhi Sultanate.

During Muhammad bin Tughluq's Qarachil expedition of 1337–1338, a Delhi army under Khusrau Malik, said to number one hundred thousand men, was destroyed in the mountain terrain by his forces. He was succeeded as raja in 1344 by Abhay Chand.

en:
Friedrich von Zollern (c. 1316–1407) was the son of Count Friedrich VIII of Zollern, called Ostertag, and began as a churchman: promised an Augsburg canonry in 1327, he studied at Bologna and became a canon in 1346. He later gave that up to join the Hospitallers under Grand Master Dieudonné de Gozon, probably serving at Rhodes.

Back in Germany from 1361, he ran commanderies including Rohrdorf, Bubikon and Villingen. In 1382 he co-signed the Heimbach agreement, which gave the order's Brandenburg bailiwick wide autonomy, and in 1392 he became Prior of Germany.

At nearly eighty he joined King Sigismund's crusade against the Ottomans, and after the crushing defeat at Nicopolis in 1396 he covered the survivors' retreat down the Danube to the Black Sea. He resigned in 1398 and died at Rhodes in 1407, probably past ninety.

弗里德里希·冯·索伦（约1316—1407）是索伦伯爵弗里德里希八世之子，其父绰号复活节。他起初走教会路线：1327年获许诺奥格斯堡的一个教士禄位，后在博洛尼亚求学，1346年成为奥格斯堡大教堂法政牧师。后来他放弃圣职，在团长迪约多内·德·戈宗任内加入医院骑士团，可能曾在罗得岛服役。

1361年返回德意志后，他执掌罗尔多夫、布比孔、菲林根等骑士团辖区。1382年他共同签署海姆巴赫协议，使骑士团勃兰登堡辖区获得很大自治权；1392年升任德意志区修道长。

1396年年近八旬的他随西吉斯蒙德出征奥斯曼人，尼科波利斯惨败后掩护残军顺多瑙河撤向黑海。1398年辞职，1407年在罗得岛去世，或已年逾九旬。

en:
Hélion de Villeneuve (c. 1270–1346), a Provençal knight and commander of Manosque, led the Hospitallers from the papal court at Avignon for years before he ever reached Rhodes. In 1317 Pope John XXII split the vast priory of Saint-Gilles, as Templar property passed to the order, and made Hélion the first prior of Provence.

In 1319, after Foulques de Villaret gave up the office, the pope gathered the priors at Avignon and they chose Hélion as the order's 26th Grand Master; he kept Provence until 1330. To please the pope, a native of Cahors, he surrendered the order's Templar holdings there in 1320 for 2,000 florins.

Reaching Rhodes in 1332, he garrisoned castles in Cilician Armenia and, with Venice and Byzantium, defeated the Turks in the Gulf of Smyrna in 1334. He died on Rhodes on 27 May 1346.

埃利翁·德·维尔纳夫（约1270—1346）是普罗旺斯籍骑士，曾任马诺斯克辖区长官。他在阿维尼翁的教廷身边领导医院骑士团多年，才第一次抵达罗得岛。1317年，圣殿产业归入骑士团之际，教皇约翰二十二世分拆圣吉尔修道区，任命他为首任普罗旺斯修道长。

1319年富尔克·德·维拉雷卸任后，教皇召集各地修道长，选出他为骑士团第26任大教长；他兼任普罗旺斯修道长至1330年。为迎合出身卡奥尔的教皇，他于1320年以2000弗罗林让出骑士团在当地的圣殿产业。

1332年抵达罗得岛后，他进驻奇里乞亚亚美尼亚的城堡，并联合威尼斯和拜占庭，于1334年在士麦那湾击败土耳其人。1346年5月27日，他在罗得岛去世。

en:
Albrecht von Hohenberg (c. 1303–1359) spent his career between emperor and pope. A son of Count Rudolf I of Hohenberg, he was a canon of Konstanz trained in canon law at Paris. An imperial minority elected him bishop of Konstanz, but the pope backed another man, and he held the disputed see only in 1334–1335.

Louis the Bavarian made him chancellor and imperial governor in Alsace, where he stopped pogroms against the Jews in 1338 and 1340. In 1342 Clement VI won him to the papal side, yet his return to Konstanz lacked papal approval, and the 1356 election failed.

Clement gave him Freising in 1349, overriding the chapter's right to elect; consecrated at Brugg in 1351, he sold many estates to mend the diocese's finances. He died at Stein am Rhein on 25 April 1359.

阿尔布雷希特·冯·霍恩贝格（约1303—1359）一生都夹在皇帝与教皇之间。他是霍恩贝格伯爵鲁道夫一世之子，曾任康斯坦茨法政牧师，在巴黎攻读教会法。亲皇帝的少数派选他为康斯坦茨主教，教皇却支持另一人；他只在1334至1335年占有这个有争议的主教座。

巴伐利亚人路德维希任命他为总理大臣和阿尔萨斯帝国地方长官，他于1338和1340年两次制止迫害犹太人。1342年，教皇克莱孟六世把他拉到教皇一方；他再回康斯坦茨却未获教皇认可，1356年的选举又告失败。

克莱孟于1349年授予他弗赖辛主教之位，无视教士会选举权；1351年他在布鲁格受祝圣，靠售产整顿教区财政。1359年4月25日卒于莱茵河畔施泰因。

en:
Aimery of Lusignan (before 1155–1205), a younger son of Poitou's lord Hugh VIII, rose to constable of the Kingdom of Jerusalem around 1180 and fought at Hattin in 1187. After his brother Guy died in 1194 the Cypriot barons chose him as lord, and in 1197 he was crowned the first king of Cyprus.

He married Queen Isabella I and ruled Jerusalem as her king from 1198, concluding truces with the Ayyubid sultan al-Adil; a treaty of 1204 secured several coastal towns. He died at Acre in 1205, leaving Cyprus to his son Hugh I.

zh:
艾默里·德·吕西尼昂（1155年前—1205）是普瓦图领主于格八世较年幼的儿子之一，约1180年升任耶路撒冷王国统帅，1187年参加哈丁战役。1194年其弟居伊去世后，塞浦路斯贵族推举他为首领，1197年他加冕为塞浦路斯第一位国王。

此后他娶女王伊莎贝拉一世，自1198年起作为她的国王共治耶路撒冷，并与阿尤布王朝苏丹阿迪勒缔结休战协定；1204年的条约保住了数座沿海城镇。1205年他在阿卡去世，塞浦路斯传给其子于格一世。

en:
Amalric I (1136–1174), younger son of Fulk and Melisende, was made count of Jaffa and later Ascalon by his mother. In 1157 he married Agnes of Courtenay, who bore Sibylla and Baldwin; he separated from her to be accepted as king on his brother Baldwin III's death in 1163.

His reign was dominated by repeated invasions of Egypt between 1163 and 1169 against Shirkuh and Saladin, and by an alliance and marriage with Byzantine Emperor Manuel I's grandniece Maria. Nur al-Din exploited Amalric's expeditions to attack the crusader states.

In 1169 Amalric and Manuel invaded Egypt together, but their forces cooperated poorly and failed. He died of dysentery in July 1174 and was succeeded by the leprous Baldwin IV.

阿马尔里克一世（1136—1174）是富尔克与梅利桑德较年幼的儿子，被母亲封为雅法伯爵，后又领有阿斯卡隆。1157年他迎娶库特奈的阿格尼丝，生西比拉和鲍德温；1163年兄长鲍德温三世去世后，他被迫与阿格尼丝分离才得以继位。

他在位期间，于1163至1169年多次远征埃及，与谢尔库赫和萨拉丁作战，并与拜占庭皇帝曼努埃尔一世结盟，娶其侄孙女玛丽亚为后。努尔丁趁阿马尔里克远征之机进攻十字军国家。

1169年阿马尔里克与曼努埃尔联合入侵埃及，但两军配合不佳，最终失败。1174年7月他死于痢疾，由患麻风病的鲍德温四世继位。

en:
Baldwin IV (1161–1185), the Leper King, succeeded his father Amalric in 1174 at the age of thirteen and was tutored by William of Tyre, who first noticed his leprosy. Raymond III of Tripoli acted as regent until 1176.

In 1177 Baldwin routed Saladin at Montgisard. He had arranged his sister Sibylla's marriage to Guy of Lusignan in 1180, but Guy's conduct later cost him the king's trust.

Blinded and enfeebled by 1183, Baldwin had his nephew Baldwin V crowned co-king and was carried in a litter to relieve Kerak. He arranged for Raymond to be regent before dying in 1185; two years later Saladin defeated the kingdom's army at Hattin.

en:
Baldwin V (1177–1186) was the son of Sibylla of Jerusalem and William of Montferrat. His uncle, the leper-king Baldwin IV, sought an heir among his relatives, and in 1183 had the six-year-old boy crowned co-king to bar Sibylla's unpopular second husband, Guy of Lusignan, from the throne.

When Baldwin IV died in 1185, the child reigned alone under the regency of Raymond III of Tripoli. Baldwin V died of unknown causes in Acre in 1186, provoking another succession crisis. He was the last Latin king buried in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre; his mother Sibylla then succeeded him and crowned Guy.

en:
Balian of Ibelin (c. 1143–1193), youngest son of Barisan of Ibelin, received the castle of Ibelin from his brother Baldwin around 1170. After their elder brother Hugh died, Baldwin inherited Ibelin but chose to remain lord of Ramla and gave the castle to Balian.

In 1177 Balian married Maria Komnene, widow of King Amalric I, becoming a leading baron under his stepson Baldwin IV. He escaped the Frankish rout at Hattin in July 1187 and, when Saladin besieged Jerusalem, led the city's outnumbered defenders before surrendering it on 2 October 1187. He served through the Third Crusade and died in 1193, leaving sons John of Beirut and Philip of Ibelin.

zh:
伊贝林的巴利安（约1143—1193）是伊贝林的巴里桑幼子，约1170年从兄长鲍德温手中受封伊贝林城堡。长兄于格去世后，鲍德温继承伊贝林，却选择留在拉姆拉为领主，将城堡交给巴利安。

1177年巴利安迎娶国王阿莫里一世的遗孀玛丽亚·科穆宁，成为继子鲍德温四世麾下的首要贵族。1187年7月，他从哈丁的惨败中脱身；萨拉丁围攻耶路撒冷时，他率领寡不敌众的守军抵抗，最终于10月2日献城投降。此后他在第三次十字军东征中效力，1193年去世，遗下贝鲁特的约翰和伊贝林的腓力等子女。

en:
Balian III (c. 1209–1247), son of John of Ibelin, the Old Lord of Beirut, and Melisende of Arsuf, won early fame at the Battle of Agridi in Cyprus in 1232, defending a pass against the Lombard troops of Emperor Frederick II. Assigned to the rearguard with his father, he went to the front instead.

Succeeding his father as lord of Beirut in 1236, he led the baronial party in the War of the Lombards and in 1242 commanded the siege that took Tyre from its imperial garrison. He married Eschiva of Montbéliard and was succeeded by his son Hugh in 1247.

巴利安三世（约1209—1247）是贝鲁特老领主伊贝林的约翰与阿尔苏夫的梅利桑德之子。1232年塞浦路斯的阿格里迪战役中，他据守隘口阻击皇帝腓特烈二世的伦巴第军队，由此初立威名。他原本被安排与父亲留在后队，却主动去了前线。

1236年他袭父职成为贝鲁特领主，接掌伦巴第战争中贵族派的领导权，并于1242年率军围攻苏尔，从帝国守军手中夺取该城。他娶蒙贝利亚尔的埃希娃为妻，1247年去世后由儿子于格继位。

Conrad of Montferrat (c. 1146–1192), a son of Marquis William V of Montferrat, later won rank in Byzantium, where Emperor Isaac II Angelos made him Caesar. He reached Tyre after Saladin's victory at Hattin in 1187, fortified the city and repelled Saladin's siege.

In 1189 he barred the released King Guy from Tyre and then joined the siege of Acre. In November 1190 he married Queen Isabella I, becoming de facto king of Jerusalem, and inherited Montferrat in 1191. Elected king in April 1192, he was assassinated by Assassins at Tyre on 28 April.

蒙特费拉的康拉德（约1146—1192）是蒙费拉托侯爵古列尔莫五世之子。后来他在拜占庭从军从政，被皇帝伊萨克二世·安格洛斯授予凯撒头衔。1187年萨拉丁在哈丁获胜后，他抵达推罗，设防固守，击退萨拉丁的围攻。

1189年他拒绝获释的国王居伊进入推罗，随后参加阿卡围城战。1190年11月他娶女王伊莎贝拉一世，成为事实上的耶路撒冷国王，并于1191年继承蒙费拉托侯爵之位。1192年4月他正式当选国王，却在当月28日于推罗被阿萨辛派刺杀。

en:
Fulk (c. 1089–1143) ruled as Count Fulk V of Anjou from 1109 and held Maine through his wife Eremburga. In 1128 he married their son Geoffrey to the Empress Matilda, surrendered Anjou to Geoffrey and sailed east to wed Melisende, heir of King Baldwin II of Jerusalem. He was crowned king in 1131.

As king he defended the crusader states against Zengi, and after a 1134 rebellion shared power with Melisende. After losing Montferrand in 1137 he strengthened the kingdom's defences, especially its southern frontier. He died in a hunting accident in November 1143.

en:
Walter IV of Brienne (1205–1246), son of Walter III, was count of Brienne from birth. His father was killed after failing to claim the throne of Sicily, and Walter's inheritance in southern Italy was confiscated. He fought in the War of the Keys in 1228–1229 to recover it.

Sent young to Outremer, he married Maria, daughter of King Hugh I of Cyprus, in 1233 and received the County of Jaffa and Ascalon in 1235.

Captured on crusade in 1239, he later commanded the crusader army at La Forbie in 1244 and was imprisoned in Cairo. He was murdered in prison in 1246, leaving sons John and Hugh.

en:
William Longsword, Italian byname Spadalunga (1140s–April 1177), was the eldest son of Marquis William V of Montferrat. In 1176 the High Court of Jerusalem chose him to marry Sibylla, sister and heir presumptive of the leper king Baldwin IV. Landed at Sidon by a Genoese fleet that October, he wed Sibylla despite noble opposition and received Jaffa and Ascalon as the likely heir to the throne.

He died of illness at Ascalon only months later, in April 1177, leaving Sibylla pregnant with the future Baldwin V; rumor said he had been poisoned.

en:
Henry II of Champagne (1166–1197), son of Count Henry I and Marie of France, inherited Champagne in 1181. He joined the Third Crusade in 1190 at the siege of Acre, which fell in 1191. After Conrad of Montferrat was assassinated days after being elected king in April 1192, the barons chose Henry, and he married Conrad's widow, Queen Isabella I, ruling the restored kingdom from its coastal strip without ever being crowned.

He once imprisoned Aimery of Lusignan over a Pisan plot, but reconciled with him in 1197. That September he fell to his death from a palace window at Acre; Aimery married Isabella and succeeded him.

en:
John of Ibelin (c. 1179–1236), the Old Lord of Beirut, was the elder son of Balian of Ibelin and Queen Maria Komnene, and half-brother of Queen Isabella I. Constable of Jerusalem before 1198, he received Beirut around 1204 and rebuilt the city after Saladin's occupation, building the great Ibelin palace.

He was regent of Jerusalem for his niece Maria of Montferrat in 1205–1210 and of Cyprus for the young Henry I in 1228–1232, leading the barons against Emperor Frederick II's bids to seize Beirut. He resisted Frederick's ambitions in Cyprus and opposed imperial forces until Henry came of age.

en:
John II of Ibelin (1230–1264), son of Balian of Beirut and grandson of the famous Old Lord John I, inherited the lordship of Beirut in 1254. In the War of Saint Sabas he drew the Jerusalem feudatories to Venice against Genoa in 1258.

In 1261 he joined a Templar raid into Galilee and was captured near Tiberias by Turcomen, along with the Templar grand master; his ransom alone cost twenty thousand bezants. He married Alice de la Roche and was succeeded by his daughter Isabella.

Maria of Montferrat (1192–1212), called la Marquise, reigned as queen of Jerusalem from 1205. The posthumous daughter of Marquis Conrad of Montferrat and Queen Isabella I, she succeeded as a child under the regency of her half-uncle John of Ibelin.

In 1210 she wed John of Brienne, who was crowned with her at Tyre on 3 October. She died late in 1212 after giving birth to her only child, Isabella II, who inherited the crown under John's guardianship.

en:
Peter Bartholomew (c. 1075–1099) was a Provençal soldier and visionary in Raymond of Saint-Gilles' army on the First Crusade. During the 1097–1098 siege of Antioch he claimed Saint Andrew revealed the hiding place of the Holy Lance; after the city fell he unearthed it on 14 June 1098.

The relic heartened the crusaders while they were besieged in Antioch, though many called him a fraud. He underwent an ordeal by fire on 8 April 1099, was badly burned, and died on 20 April.

皮埃尔·巴泰勒米（约1075—1099）是第一次十字军东征时图卢兹的雷蒙麾下的普罗旺斯士兵，也是一名自称能见异象的人。1097至1098年围攻安条克期间，他声称圣安德烈向他显灵，指示了圣矛的藏处；城破后他于1098年6月14日挖出圣矛。

十字军被反围于安条克时，这件圣物鼓舞了军心，但许多人斥他为骗子。他于1099年4月8日接受火刑裁判，被严重烧伤，4月20日死去。

en:
Philip I of Montfort (c. 1206–1270), son of Guy of Montfort and Helvis of Ibelin, inherited Castres in 1228 after his father died in the Albigensian Crusade. In Outremer he joined his uncle John of Ibelin against Frederick II's officials, and as constable of Jerusalem survived the Frankish disaster at La Forbie in 1244.

Made lord of Tyre in 1246, he served Louis IX as envoy during the Seventh Crusade and expelled the Venetians from Tyre in 1256, helping spark the War of St Sabas. He lost Toron to Sultan Baibars in 1266, and in 1270 an Assassin killed him at Tyre, perhaps in Baibars' pay.

蒙福尔的菲利普一世（约1206—1270）是蒙福尔的居伊与伊贝林的埃尔维斯之子，1228年父亲在阿尔比派十字军期间阵亡，他继承了法国的卡斯特尔领地。在海外之地，他加入舅父伊贝林的约翰一方，对抗腓特烈二世的官吏；身为耶路撒冷统帅，他在1244年法兰克人惨败的拉福尔比战役中幸免于难。

1246年他受封苏尔领主，第七次十字军东征期间任法王路易九世的使者，1256年将威尼斯人逐出苏尔，间接引发圣萨巴斯战争。1266年他将托龙失于苏丹拜巴尔；1270年，一名阿萨辛刺客在苏尔将他刺杀，幕后主使可能是拜巴尔。

Sibylla (c. 1159–1190), eldest daughter of King Amalric of Jerusalem, was heir to her leprous brother Baldwin IV. Her first husband, William Longsword of Montferrat, died in 1177, leaving a son, the future Baldwin V. In 1180 she married Guy of Lusignan, splitting the barons.

After Baldwin IV and the boy Baldwin V died, she claimed the throne in 1186, crowning Guy herself. Saladin shattered the kingdom at Hattin in 1187; Sibylla secured Guy's release, then died with her daughters in an epidemic outside Acre in 1190.

西比拉（约1159—1190）是耶路撒冷国王阿马尔里克之女，因弟弟鲍德温四世身患麻风而成为王位继承人。她的首任丈夫蒙费拉的“长剑”威廉于1177年去世，留下遗腹子，即后来的鲍德温五世。1180年，她改嫁吕西尼昂的居伊，这桩婚事使王国贵族分裂。

鲍德温四世与幼王鲍德温五世相继死后，她于1186年夺取王位，亲自为居伊加冕。1187年萨拉丁在哈丁战役击垮王国，西比拉设法使被俘的居伊获释，最终于1190年在阿卡城外的瘟疫中与两个女儿一同病死。

en:
Walram of Jülich (c. 1304–1349) was Archbishop of Cologne from 1332 until his death, the third son of Count Gerhard V of Jülich. He was a Cologne canon when his brother William V secured his appointment by Pope John XXII.

He made peace with Jülich and fought a coalition including the County of the Mark, which defeated his forces at Recklinghausen in 1345; he also founded Cologne Charterhouse in 1334. Burdened by war debts, he withdrew from government in 1347 and died in Paris in 1349.

于利希的瓦尔拉姆（约1304—1349）自1332年起担任科隆大主教直至去世，是于利希伯爵格哈德五世的第三子。他担任科隆法政牧师时，其兄威廉五世促成教皇约翰二十二世任命他为大主教。

en:
Chunghye (1315–1344), personal name Wang Jeong, was the 28th king of Goryeo, son of Chungsuk and Queen Gongwon. He took the throne in 1330 when his father abdicated and married the Yuan princess Deoknyeong; Yuan recalled Chungsuk two years later. When Chungsuk died in 1339, Wang Go, whom chancellor Bayan favored, failed to win the crown after ministers petitioned for Chunghye.

The Goryeosa portrays him as a viciously licentious ruler who abducted, raped and killed women. After he raped Princess Gyeonghwa, his father's concubine, she reported him to a Yuan envoy, who arrested him for the Yuan court. Deposed and banished toward Guangdong, he died on the way in 1344, and his young son Chungmok by Deoknyeong succeeded.

忠惠王（1315—1344），名王祯，高丽第28代国王，忠肃王与恭元王后之子。1330年忠肃王禅位，他即位并娶元朝德宁公主为妃；两年后元朝召回忠肃王，忠肃王复位。1339年忠肃王去世后，元朝丞相伯颜属意王暠，高丽群臣却联名上书拥立忠惠王，王暠夺位未成。

《高丽史》称他荒淫暴虐，常有掳掠、奸淫乃至杀害妇女之事。他奸污父亲的嫔妃庆华公主，公主向元朝使者告发，使者将他逮捕押往元廷。他被废黜，流放广东，1344年死于途中，德宁公主所生的幼子忠穆王继位。

en:
Chungnyeol (3 April 1236 – 30 July 1308), personal name Wang Geo, was the 25th king of Goryeo, son of Wonjong, enthroned in 1274. As crown prince he married a daughter of Kublai Khan, Princess Jeguk, opening eighty years of Mongol alliances as the first Goryeo ruler titled only wang.

Goryeo supplied fleets for Kublai's failed Japan invasions of 1274 and 1281 at great cost. Chungnyeol recovered Dongnyeong and Tamna, secured Yuan garrison withdrawal, restored a body investigating nobles' illegal holdings, and promoted Confucian learning. He abdicated to his son Chungseon in 1298, was restored within the year, and died in 1308.

zh:
忠烈王（1236年4月3日—1308年7月30日），名王昛，高丽第25代国王，1274年继承父亲元宗即位。为世子时他便向元世祖忽必烈求娶公主，迎娶齐国大长公主忽都鲁揭里迷失，开启了此后八十余年高丽国王与蒙古宗室联姻的惯例；他也是第一位以王为号的高丽国王。

在位期间，高丽为忽必烈1274年和1281年两次东征日本建造船队，付出沉重代价。他收回东宁府与耽罗，促使元朝撤回驻军，重设机构清查贵族非法占有的土地和人口，并提倡儒学。1298年他一度禅位于儿子忠宣王，同年复位，1308年去世。

en:
Chungseon (1275–1325) was the 26th king of Goryeo and its first ruler of Mongol blood, grandson of Kublai Khan. He married the Yuan princess Budashiri in 1296 and ruled briefly in 1298 after his father Chungnyeol abdicated, returning the throne amid feud between his Mongol queen and Korean consorts.

He was made Prince of Shenyang in 1308, the year he regained the Goryeo throne. He tried to reform court politics but spent much of his time in Dadu, abdicated to his son Chungsuk in 1313, and was known for calligraphy and painting. Briefly exiled to Tibet after 1320, he died in 1325.

忠宣王（1275—1325），高丽第26代国王，是忽必烈的外孙，也是第一位有蒙古血统的高丽国王。1296年他迎娶元朝公主宝塔实怜，1298年忠烈王禅位后他短暂即位，因蒙古王妃与高丽嫔妃争斗激烈，很快还位给父亲。

en:
Chungsuk (1294–1339), born Wang To and later renamed Man, was the 27th king of Goryeo, son of Chungseon and the Mongol consort Yasokjin. He grew up in Dadu and became king in 1313 when his father abdicated.

After Chungseon was exiled to Tibet in 1320, Chungsuk organized petitions for his release, but his rival Wang Go intercepted them. In 1322 Wang Go's supporters had him summoned to Dadu, where he was held until 1323; returning in 1324, he dismissed the signatories.

He abdicated to his son Chunghye in 1330 and was restored in 1332 when Yuan deposed Chunghye, making peace with Wang Go the next year. He changed his name to Man in 1335 and died in 1339.

忠肃王（1294—1339），讳王焘，后改名王卍，高丽第27代国王，忠宣王与蒙古嫔妃也速真之子。他在大都长大，1313年忠宣王禅位，他即位为王。

1320年忠宣王被流放吐蕃，忠肃王组织群臣上书营救，却遭对手王暠截留。1322年王暠的党羽上书元朝请求改立，忠肃王被召至大都滞留，直到1323年才得以脱身；1324年回国后，他罢免了联名上书的大臣。

1330年他禅位于儿子忠惠王，1332年元朝废黜忠惠王，他复位，次年与王暠和解。1335年他改名为卍，1339年去世。

en:
Princess Deoknyeong (died 1375), born Borjigin Irinjinbala, was a great-granddaughter of Kublai Khan, one of the Yuan princesses who married into the Goryeo royal house. In 1330 she wed King Chunghye at the Yuan court and returned with him to Goryeo, bearing the future King Chungmok in 1337. When Chunghye was deposed in 1344, she became regent for her young son and directed state affairs.

After Chungmok's early death she remained active under King Chungjeong, stepping down in 1348 amid disturbances by powerful officials. Honored as queen mother by Gongmin, she took a Yuan title in 1367 and was buried at Gyeongneung.

德宁公主（？—1375），名亦怜真班，元世祖忽必烈的玄孙女，是嫁入高丽王室的元朝公主之一。1330年她在元朝嫁给高丽忠惠王并随他回到高丽，1337年生下后来的忠穆王。1344年忠惠王被废，年幼的忠穆王即位，她以母后身份摄政，代掌国事。

忠穆王早逝后她在忠定王时期仍参与政事，1348年因权臣扰乱而退出摄政。恭愍王即位后尊她为王太后，1367年元朝再授她公主封号，死后葬于顷陵。

en:
Gongmin (1330–1374) was the 31st king of Goryeo, second son of Chungsuk. A hostage at the Yuan court, he succeeded in 1351 as Yuan power crumbled. He purged pro-Yuan nobles and in 1356 recovered Ssangseong and Dongnyeong with the aid of defecting Goryeo generals. Red Turban armies invaded in 1359 and 1361, briefly occupying Gaegyeong before being driven out.

His land reforms met strong resistance. After Queen Noguk died in childbirth in 1365 he entrusted the state to the reforming monk Sin Don, executed in 1371. In 1374 his guards murdered him in his bedchamber, and young King U succeeded.

zh:
恭愍王（1330—1374），高丽第31代国王，忠肃王次子。他早年在元朝为人质，1351年元朝统治动摇之际即位。他清除亲元贵族，1356年出兵收复双城、东宁两处故地，归附的高丽将领从旁协助。红巾军于1359年和1361年两次入侵，一度占领开京，随后被收复。

他推行田制改革，遭到拥有土地的官员阻挠。1365年仁德王后（鲁国公主）难产而死后，他把国政托付给锐意改革的僧人辛盹，1371年又将辛盹处死。1374年，他在寝宫被自己的护卫弑杀，年幼的禑王继位。

en:
Queen Gongwon (1298–1380), born Lady Hong of the Namyang Hong clan, married King Chungsuk of Goryeo in 1313 and became Consort Deok. She was the mother of two kings, Chunghye and Gongmin.

Goryeo kings were expected to marry Yuan imperial women, so when a Yuan princess became Chungsuk's wife, Lady Hong moved to another residence. He later expelled her to her hometown, and she did not return to Gaegyeong until 1332.

As queen dowager she opposed Gongmin's radical reforms carried out with the monk Sin Don and reproached him for executing obstructive officials. In 1376 she had Banya, King U's slave-born mother, drowned in the Imjin River. She died in 1380 aged 81 and was buried at Yeongneung.

恭元王后（1298—1380），本贯南阳洪氏，1313年嫁给高丽忠肃王，封德妃，是忠惠王与恭愍王两位国王的生母。

高丽国王按惯例要迎娶元朝皇室女子，因此元朝公主成为忠肃王之妻后，洪氏迁居别处。后来国王将她逐回故乡，直到1332年她才返回开京。

为太后期间，她反对恭愍王倚靠僧人辛盹推行的激进改革，斥责国王诛杀阻碍新政的官员。1376年，她命人将禑王的奴婢出身生母般若沉入临津江。1380年她以81岁高龄去世，葬于令陵。

Wang Ja, enfeoffed as Duke Gangyang (died 1308), was the eldest son of King Chungnyeol of Goryeo by his first consort. Although the eldest son, he was barred from succession because his half-brother Chungseon was born to Qutugh Kelmysh, a daughter of Kublai Khan.

Sent to Dongsimsa temple in 1279, he was recalled only in 1283 and enfeoffed as Duke Gangyang. His sons included Wang Ko, Prince Yeonan. He died in 1308; in 1391 his great-grandson, King Gongyang, gave him the posthumous name Jeonggang.

王滋（封江阳公，？—1308）是高丽忠烈王与贞和宫主王氏的长子。他虽为长子，却因异母弟忠宣王是忽必烈之女忽都鲁揭里迷失所生而无法继承王位。

Queen Jangmok (1259–1297), born Borjigin Qutlugh Kelmysh and known as Princess Supreme Jeguk, was the youngest daughter of Kublai Khan. In 1274 she married Crown Prince Wang Geo of Goryeo, aged 39; when he ruled as King Chungnyeol she became his primary queen, the first Goryeo consort from Yuan, outranking his Korean first wife.

She kept her Mongol retinue and customs, spreading Yuan fashions at the Goryeo court, and urged Chungnyeol to hunt less and attend to state affairs. In 1275 she bore the future King Chungseon. She died in 1297 and received the posthumous name Queen Jangmok.

庄穆王后（1259—1297），孛儿只斤氏，名忽都鲁揭里迷失，即元朝齐国大长公主，元世祖忽必烈之女。1274年，她下嫁年已39岁的高丽世子王昛，即后来的忠烈王；忠烈王即位后立她为正妃，使她成为高丽第一位来自元朝的王妃，位次在忠烈王原配之上。

en:
Cho Kwang-jo (1482–1519) was the Sarim Neo-Confucian leader who drove the reforms of King Jungjong's reign. He entered court in 1515, when Jungjong was using Sarim scholars to counter the Hungu leaders who had placed him on the throne in 1506, and rose to inspector-general.

He abolished the Sogyok office in 1516, introduced the Hyŏllyang examination in 1518, and purged unworthy names from the 1506 merit roster, enraging the Hungu elite. His enemies answered with honey-written mulberry leaves reading Cho shall be king.

Jungjong turned against him: in the 1519 Gimyo purge Cho was exiled and forced to drink poison. He was rehabilitated under King Injong.

赵光祖（1482—1519）是朝鲜中宗朝主持改革的士林派性理学领袖。1506年勋旧派首领拥立中宗为王，中宗后来招揽士林学者牵制勋旧派；赵光祖1515年入朝，官至大司宪。

任内他于1516年促成废除道教机构昭格署，1518年开设以举荐取士的贤良科，并削去1506年功臣名册中冒滥之人的封号，激怒勋旧派。对手以蜜水在桑叶上写下“走肖为王”反击。

中宗转而反对他，1519年己卯士祸中赵光祖被流放，继而被赐毒自尽。仁宗即位后他获得平反。

Han Jong-yu (1287–1354), courtesy name Saga, art name Bokjae, was a Goryeo civil official of the Hanyang Han clan and maternal grandfather of the scholar Gwon Geun. He passed the civil service examination under King Chungnyeol and rose at court.

When Yuan officials seized the dissolute King Chunghye and carried him to Dadu, Han was among the ministers jailed there. Around 1343 to 1344 he held the post of Left Chancellor, and was enfeoffed as Internal Prince Hanyang, receiving the posthumous name Munjeol.

en:
Kim Chong-sŏ (1383–1453) was a Joseon general and scholar-official who served Kings Sejong, Munjong and Danjong. After passing the state examination in 1405, he built his career on the northern frontier.

In 1433, as governor of Hamgyeong, he defeated the Jurchen raiders and founded the Six Garrisons, securing Korea's frontier along the Tumen River.

As Right State Councilor he was named guardian of the young Danjong; his influence brought him into conflict with Grand Prince Suyang, the king's uncle. In the Gyeyu coup of November 1453, Suyang had him and his sons killed.

金宗瑞（1383—1453）是朝鲜王朝的将领与文臣，历事世宗、文宗、端宗三朝。他1405年文科及第，早年在北部边疆任职。

1433年出任咸镜道观察使，北征击败女真，开拓北疆六镇，巩固图们江一线的边界。

en:
Wang Ko (died 1345), Mongol name Oljeitu, was a Goryeo prince and Yuan-dynasty King of Shen, son of Duke Gangyang. In 1316 he received the Shen fief from his uncle King Chungseon.

After 1320 he twice intrigued at court to seize the Goryeo throne, securing Chungseon's exile to Tibet, but Emperor Yingzong's assassination in 1323 and Bayan's downfall in 1340 ruined his plans. He briefly acted as king after Chunghye's fall in 1343, returned to Goryeo and died there in 1345, when his grandson Toghtua Bukha inherited Shen.

Wang Ko (died 1345), Mongol name Oljeitu, was a Goryeo prince and Yuan-dynasty King of Shen, son of Duke Gangyang. In 1316 he received the Shen fief from his uncle King Chungseon.

After 1320 he twice intrigued at court to seize the Goryeo throne, securing Chungseon's exile to [GetCountry('TIB').GetName], but Emperor Yingzong's assassination in 1323 and Bayan's downfall in 1340 ruined his plans. He briefly acted as king after Chunghye's fall in 1343, returned to Goryeo and died there in 1345, when his grandson Toghtua Bukha inherited Shen.
zh:
王暠（？—1345年），蒙古名完泽秃，高丽宗室、元朝沈王，江阳公王滋之子。1316年，叔父忠宣王将沈地转封给他。

1320年后他两度在元廷活动谋夺高丽王位，曾促使忠宣王被流放吐蕃，但1323年元英宗遇刺、1340年伯颜倒台，两次图谋都告失败。1343年忠惠王被废后他一度权署国王，1345年返回高丽并于同年去世，其孙脱脱不花后来承袭沈王爵位。

en:
Yasokjin, known by her posthumous title Consort Ui, was a Mongol-born consort of King Chungseon of Goryeo. She was not from the Yuan imperial clan and probably married Chungseon while he was a crown prince at the Yuan court, before his wedding to a Yuan princess in 1296.

She bore two sons, Wang Gam and Wang Do, the future King Chungsuk. She died in Yuan in 1316, and her coffin was returned to Goryeo and buried at Yeolleung.

en:
Ajlan Bey was a prince of the Karasid Turkoman dynasty in northwestern Anatolia, described in Ottoman sources as a son of Karasi Bey. He died around 1335, leaving two sons, one of them Dursun.

After Ajlan's death, Dursun fled to the Ottoman Sultan Orhan. He offered him the Karasid domains, leading to their capture and his brother's surrender. The historian Claude Cahen suggested that Ajlan was another name for Karasi Bey himself, identifying the rival sons as Demir Khan and Yakhshi Khan.

zh:
阿吉兰贝伊是安纳托利亚西北部土库曼卡拉斯王朝的王子，奥斯曼史料称他为卡雷西贝伊之子。他约于1335年去世，留下两个儿子，其中一个名叫杜尔孙。

阿吉兰死后，杜尔孙投奔奥斯曼苏丹奥尔汗，将卡拉斯领地献给他，奥斯曼人随后夺取领地，其兄弟也投降了。历史学家克劳德·卡昂认为，阿吉兰可能就是卡雷西贝伊本人的别称，卷入王朝争斗的儿子是德米尔汗和亚赫希汗。

en:
Demir Khan ruled the Karasid beylik at Balıkesir, while his brother Yakhshi Khan held Bergama. With his Marmara fleet he raided the southern Balkan coasts until Emperor Andronikos III made a truce at Biga in 1328. In 1333 he received Ibn Battuta, who wrote that his people disliked him.

His commanders turned to his brother Dursun, supported by the Ottoman Orhan; Demir had Dursun killed, after which Orhan annexed the beylik and exiled Demir to Bursa, where he died of plague.

zh:
德米尔汗是卡拉斯王朝的贝伊，以巴勒克埃西尔为统治中心，其兄弟亚赫希汗则控制贝尔加马一带。他凭借驻扎在马尔马拉海的舰队劫掠巴尔干南部沿海，直到1328年拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡三世在比加与他订立和约。1333年，他接见了旅行家伊本·白图泰，后者记载德米尔汗不受臣民爱戴。

心怀不满的将领请来得到奥斯曼苏丹奥尔汗支持的兄弟杜尔孙夺取贝伊国，德米尔汗将杜尔孙射杀，奥尔汗随即吞并卡拉斯领地，把德米尔汗流放至布尔萨，他最终在那里死于瘟疫。

en:
Karasi Bey, also called Karasi Khan, was the eponymous founder of the Karasid beylik in northwestern Anatolia. He and his father Kalam seized the hinterland around Balıkesir under Seljuk rule and later claimed independence.

After the failed Byzantine campaigns of 1302–1308 he expanded to the borders of the Sarukhanids. He built up a fleet on the Marmara and Aegean coasts and died around 1328, leaving power to his son Demir Khan.

卡雷西贝伊又称卡雷西汗，是安纳托利亚西北部卡拉斯贝伊国的同名建国者。他与父亲卡拉姆在塞尔柱统治下夺取了巴勒克埃西尔一带的内陆，后来宣布独立。

1302—1308年拜占庭的攻势失败后，他扩张到与萨鲁汗王朝接壤。他在马尔马拉海和爱琴海沿岸建立舰队，约于1328年去世，权力交给儿子德米尔汗。

Shuja al-Din Yakhshi Khan was a son of Karasi Bey and a ruler of the Karasid Turkoman principality in Anatolia. After Karasi Bey died around 1328, the lands split: Yakhshi held Pergamon while his brother Demir Khan ruled from Balıkesir.

He reigned from about 1332 to 1341, and the Ottomans later acquired the Karasid lands. Cahen proposed identifying him with Dursun, the prince whose fall brought on that annexation.

舒贾丁·亚赫希汗是卡雷西贝伊之子，统辖安纳托利亚的土库曼卡拉斯侯国。约1328年卡雷西贝伊死后，领地一分为二：亚赫希占据帕加马，其兄弟德米尔汗以巴勒克埃西尔为都。

en:
Qutb al-Din Jahanshah Nikruz was the Mongol governor of Kirman when the Ilkhanate broke apart after Abu Sa'id died heirless in 1335. His brother Sultanshah Nikruz sided with the kingmaker Ali Padshah and fought at Qara Darra on 24 July 1336, where Ali Padshah's army was broken and he died.

With no overlord left, Kirman lay open to Mubariz al-Din Muhammad, founder of the Muzaffarid dynasty, who invaded in 1339 or 1340. Qutb al-Din briefly recovered the province with aid from the Kartids of Herat, but Mubariz al-Din retook it for good in late 1340.

库特卜丁·贾汉沙·尼库鲁兹是克尔曼的蒙古长官，1335年不赛因死后无嗣，伊尔汗国随之瓦解。他的兄弟苏丹沙·尼库鲁兹站在拥立君主的权臣阿里·帕迪沙一边，于1336年7月24日列阵卡拉达拉；阿里·帕迪沙的军队被击溃，本人身死。

宗主既失，克尔曼门户洞开，穆扎法尔王朝的建立者穆巴里兹·丁·穆罕默德于1339或1340年入侵。库特卜丁借助赫拉特卡尔提德王朝的援兵一度收复该省，但穆巴里兹·丁于1340年底将其永久占领。

en:
Mu'izz al-Din Husayn ibn Ghiyath al-Din was Kart malik of Herat, ruler of the Kart dynasty in Khorasan. He came to power around 1331 and expanded his principality after the Ilkhanate fragmented in 1335.

He allied with Togha Temür, defeated the Sarbadars at the Battle of Zava in 1342, and campaigned against the Chagatai Mongols, taking the young Timur into his service. In 1349 he ceased paying tribute and ruled independently as sultan until his death in 1370, when his son Pir Ali succeeded him.

穆伊兹丁·侯赛因·伊本·吉亚斯丁是赫拉特的马利克，统治呼罗珊的卡尔提德王朝。他约1331年即位，1335年伊儿汗国瓦解后扩张了自己的领地。

他与脱合帖木儿结盟，1342年在扎瓦战役击败萨尔巴达尔，又出征察合台蒙古人，并将年轻的帖木儿收为部下。1349年他停止纳贡，以苏丹身份独立统治，在位至1370年去世，其子皮儿·阿里继位。

en:
Kota Rani (died 1339) was the last Hindu ruler of Kashmir's Lohara dynasty. She married the Ladakhi prince Rinchan, who seized the throne in the 1320 Mongol invasion and ruled as Sultan Sadr al-Din until killed in 1323.

As regent for her son, she married Suhadeva's brother Udayanadeva and defeated a Turco-Mongol invasion. She ruled from 1338, but in 1339 Shah Mir overthrew her and she died in prison. Her Kute Kol canal saved Srinagar from floods.

zh:
俱陀·罗妮（？—1339）是克什米尔卢诃罗王朝末代印度教统治者。她嫁给拉达克王子仁钦；仁钦在1320年蒙古入侵期间夺取王位，以苏丹萨德尔丁之名统治，1323年遇刺身亡。

她作为儿子的摄政，又嫁给苏诃提婆之弟乌达亚那提婆，并率军击退一次突厥—蒙古入侵。1338年起她执政，但1339年沙阿·米尔将她推翻，她最终死于狱中。她开凿的库特渠使斯利那加免于水患。

en:
Suhadeva (r. 1301–1320) was the last effective Hindu king of the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir. During his reign Shah Mir entered Kashmiri service in 1313 and rose at court.

In 1320 a Turco-Mongol army under the chief Zulju invaded the valley; Suhadeva tried to buy Zulju off, failed to organize resistance, and fled while the invaders looted for eight months. His flight ended Lohara power: his general Ramachandra and then Rinchan held Srinagar, and after Suhadeva's death his brother Udayanadeva briefly restored the dynasty.

zh:
苏诃提婆（1301—1320年在位）是克什米尔卢诃罗王朝最后一位掌握实权的印度教国王。他在位期间，沙阿·米尔于1313年入仕克什米尔，在朝中渐居要职。

1320年，首领祖尔朱率突厥—蒙古军队入侵谷地；苏诃提婆试图以重金令其退兵，又未能组织抵抗，最终弃国出逃，听任入侵者劫掠八个月之久。他的出逃终结了卢诃罗政权：大将罗摩占陀罗、继而仁钦先后据有斯利那加，他死后其弟乌达亚那提婆曾短暂恢复王朝。

en:
Jayari Malla was the eighth Malla king of the Kathmandu Valley and a son of Ananta Malla. In 1320 Rudra Malla of Bhaktapur deposed Jayanandadeva and installed Jayari, who reigned until 1344 as a figurehead while Rudra Malla and later Devaladevi held real power.

His reign saw the flight of the Tirhut royal family into the valley in 1324 after Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq's invasion, and Khasa raids in 1328 and 1334, the latter burning Sankhu.

贾亚里·马拉是加德满都谷地第八位马拉国王，阿南塔·马拉之子。1320年，巴克塔普尔的鲁陀罗·马拉废黜阇耶阿南达提婆，改立贾亚里为王；他在位至1344年，只是名义君主，实权先后掌握在鲁陀罗·马拉和提婆罗提毗手中。

他在位期间，1324年吉亚斯丁·图格鲁克入侵，底尔胡特王族逃入谷地；1328年和1334年迦舍军队两度入掠，后一次焚毁了桑库。

Shahab al-Din, titled al-Malik al-Adil, was a Kurdish Ayyubid emir of Hisn Kayfa. One traditional list of the emirs dates his reign from 1328 to 1349.

In 1334 the Artuqids went to war with Hisn Kayfa over the lands on the left bank of the Tigris. In the 14th century the Ayyubids rebuilt the great castle above the town as their dynasty's stronghold.

en:
Kublai Khan (1215–1294) was a grandson of Genghis Khan who became Great Khan of the Mongols in 1260 and founded China's Yuan dynasty. When he was nine, Genghis is said to have praised his words after the boy's first hunt as full of wisdom. After Möngke died on campaign in 1259, Kublai was proclaimed khan at Kaiping in 1260; he took four years to defeat Ariq Böke, and the war split the empire into rival khanates.

In 1271 he took the dynastic name Great Yuan and made Dadu his capital. Xiangyang fell in 1273, and in 1279 the last Song loyalists were crushed at Yamen, making him the first non-Han ruler of all China. His Japan and Java invasions failed.

After his wife Chabi and heir Zhenjin died, he sank into gout and depression. He died on 18 February 1294, and his grandson Temür succeeded as second Yuan emperor.

zh:
元世祖忽必烈（1215—1294）是成吉思汗之孙，1260年成为蒙古大汗，并创立了中国的元朝。九岁首次随猎后，成吉思汗相传称赞他的话充满智慧。1259年蒙哥在征战途中去世，1260年忽必烈在开平被拥立为汗；他用四年击败阿里不哥，这场内战使蒙古帝国分裂成几个互相对立的汗国。

1271年他取国号“大元”，定都大都。襄阳于1273年陷落，1279年最后的宋朝抵抗力量在崖山覆灭，忽必烈成为首位统治全中国的非汉族君主。他远征日本和爪哇均告失败。

皇后察必和太子真金相继去世后，他陷入痛风与消沉。1294年2月18日他去世，孙子铁穆耳继位，是元朝第二位皇帝。

en:
Külüg Khan, born Khayishan (1281–1311), posthumously Emperor Wuzong of Yuan, was the eldest son of Darmabala and nephew of the heirless Temür Khan. He won fame commanding Yuan armies in Mongolia against Kaidu, who died of wounds in 1301, and he became Prince Huaining in 1304.

Enthroned in 1307, he named his brother Ayurbarwada crown prince, showered princes and Buddhist temples with gifts, and revived the Department of State Affairs amid fiscal trouble. He died in 1311.

曲律汗，本名海山（1281—1311），庙号武宗，答剌麻八剌长子，无嗣的成宗铁穆耳之侄。他以在蒙古统兵对抗海都成名，海都在1301年的战役后伤重而死；1304年他受封怀宁王。

1307年他即位，立弟爱育黎拔力八达为皇太子，对宗王和佛寺赏赐浩大，并在财政困局中重设尚书省理财。他于1311年去世。

en:
Eberhard I of Habsburg-Laufenburg (c. 1235–1284) was the fourth son of Count Rudolf I of Laufenburg. In 1271 he married Anna, heiress daughter of Count Hartmann V of Kyburg, which gave him Anna's Kyburg inheritance and founded the Neu-Kyburg line.

To clear heavy debts, he and Anna sold the town of Fribourg to King Rudolf in 1277 for 3040 marks of silver. His son Hartmann I succeeded him as count of Kyburg.

en:
Eberhard II von Kyburg (c. 1299–1357), younger son of Count Hartmann I, was trained for the Church, studying at Bologna. A feud with his elder brother Hartmann II ended at a feast at Thun Castle in 1322, when a brawl left Hartmann dead after a fall from a window.

Accused of murdering his brother, Eberhard kept Kyburg with Bernese backing against King Louis IV's confiscation, and in 1328 won minting rights. He fought Bern in the Gümmenenkrieg of 1331–1333 and died on 17 April 1357.

A feud with his elder brother #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('kyb_hartmann_ii_kyburg').GetID],X #L Hartmann II#!#! ended at a feast at Thun Castle in 1322, when a brawl left Hartmann dead after a fall from a window.

Accused of murdering his brother, Eberhard kept [GetCountry('KYB').GetName] with Bernese backing against King Louis IV's confiscation, and in 1328 won minting rights. He fought [ShowLocationName('bern')] in the Gümmenenkrieg of 1331–1333 and died on 17 April 1357.
zh:
埃伯哈德二世·冯·基堡（约1299—1357）是哈特曼一世伯爵的幼子，原本准备进入教会，曾在博洛尼亚求学。他与兄长哈特曼二世结仇；1322年，双方在图恩城堡的和解宴会上斗殴，哈特曼坠窗身亡。

埃伯哈德被控弑兄，却在伯尔尼支持下顶住国王路德维希四世没收领地的处置，保住基堡，并于1328年取得铸币权。1331—1333年，他参加对伯尔尼的居梅嫩战争，1357年4月17日去世。

en:
Hartmann II of Kyburg (c. 1299–1322) succeeded his father Hartmann I as count in 1301, as a child under guardianship. In 1319 he married Margaret of Neuchâtel, but the marriage was childless.

When his clerical younger brother Eberhard II demanded a share of the inheritance, Hartmann had him imprisoned. A reconciliation at Thun Castle on 31 October 1322 turned violent after drinking, and Hartmann fell from a window and died. Backed by Bern, Eberhard then seized the county.

en:
Hartmann III von Habsburg-Kyburg (c. 1330–1377) succeeded his father Eberhard II as count of Kyburg and landgrave of Burgundy, reversing Eberhard's pro-Bern course after the so-called brother-murder of Thun.

He leaned toward Habsburg Austria and pledged several towns to the Austrian dukes. In 1375 his son Rudolf II inherited the indebted county of Neuchâtel-Nidau, and Hartmann died on 29 March 1377.

en:
Hartmann I of Kyburg (c. 1275–1301) was a count of Kyburg of the Neu-Kyburg line, son of Eberhard I of Habsburg-Laufenburg and Anna, the Kyburg heiress. He succeeded his father in 1284 as a child, under his uncle Rudolf's guardianship until 1292. Hartmann was the first of his line to style himself simply count of Kyburg.

In 1298 he married Elisabeth of Freiburg, who bore him Hartmann II and Eberhard II. He died on 29 March 1301, leaving an underage heir.

en:
Titus Mstislavich (died after 1365) was a prince of Kozelsk from the Rurikid line of Karachev, a son of Prince Mstislav Mikhailovich. The chronicles name him only once, under 1365, when he helped Oleg of Ryazan and Vladimir of Pronsk defeat an army of the Golden Horde at Shishevsky Forest.

His sons Svyatoslav and Ivan held Karachev and Kozelsk. They married daughters of Algirdas of Lithuania and Oleg of Ryazan.

季特·姆斯季斯拉维奇（1365年后去世）是留里克王朝卡拉切夫支系的科泽利斯克王公，姆斯季斯拉夫·米哈伊洛维奇之子。编年史中他只在1365年被提到一次：他率部驰援梁赞王公奥列格和普龙斯克王公弗拉基米尔，在希舍夫斯基森林击败金帐汗国的军队。

他的儿子斯维亚托斯拉夫和伊凡分别领有卡拉切夫与科泽利斯克。两人分别娶立陶宛大公阿尔吉尔达斯和梁赞王公奥列格之女为妻。

en:
Baldwin II of Courtenay (1217–1273), the last Latin emperor of Constantinople, was a son of Peter of Courtenay. He succeeded his brother Robert in 1228, ruling first with his father-in-law John of Brienne, whose daughter Marie he married. His realm held little beyond Constantinople, and he repeatedly travelled west for aid. In 1238 his regency council pawned the Crown of Thorns to Venetian creditors, and he later pledged his son Philip to merchants.

In 1261 Constantinople was recaptured and Baldwin fled, eventually reaching Italy. After the 1267 Treaty of Viterbo with Charles of Anjou, he died in Naples in 1273.

库尔特奈的鲍德温二世（1217—1273）是拉丁帝国末代皇帝，为库尔特奈的彼得之子。他1228年继兄罗贝尔即位，先与岳父布里耶纳的约翰共治，娶约翰之女玛丽。他的帝国所余领土仅及君士坦丁堡附近，多次前往西欧寻求援助。1238年他的摄政会议把荆棘冠抵押给威尼斯债权人；他后来又将儿子菲利普押给商人。

en:
Berengaria of León (1204–1237) was the daughter of Alfonso IX of León and Berengaria of Castile, and a younger sister of Ferdinand III. In 1223 the twice-widowed John of Brienne, former king of Jerusalem, sought a bride among her family; he chose Berengaria and married her at Toledo in 1224. When John was elected Latin emperor in 1229 and crowned at Constantinople in 1231, she became empress of the Latin Empire.

Her daughter Marie married Baldwin II, while her sons served the kings of France. She died on 12 April 1237, within weeks of her husband.

莱昂的贝伦加利亚（1204—1237）是莱昂国王阿方索九世与卡斯蒂利亚的贝伦加丽娅之女、斐迪南三世之妹。1223年，两度丧妻的前耶路撒冷国王布里耶纳的约翰到她的家族中择妻，最终选中贝伦加丽娅，二人于1224年在托莱多成婚。1229年约翰当选拉丁皇帝、1231年于君士坦丁堡加冕，她遂成为拉丁帝国的皇后。

其女玛丽嫁给鲍德温二世，诸子则效力于法兰西国王。1237年4月12日，她在丈夫去世仅数周后离世。

en:
John of Brienne (c. 1170–1237), a younger son of the count of Brienne, married the heiress Maria and was crowned king of Jerusalem in 1210. After Maria's death he ruled as regent for their daughter Isabella and led the Fifth Crusade, which seized Damietta in 1219 before its collapse in 1221.

In 1225 he married Isabella to Emperor Frederick II, who took the kingdom from him. Elected Latin emperor in 1229 and crowned in 1231, he led the defense against Nicaea and Bulgaria in 1235–1236 and died as a Franciscan friar in 1237.

en:
Peter II of Courtenay (c. 1155–c. 1218), son of Peter I of Courtenay and cousin of King Philip II of France, took the cross on the Third Crusade in 1190 and later fought in the Albigensian Crusade and at Bouvines. Chosen Latin emperor after his brother-in-law Henry of Flanders died in 1216, he was crowned in Rome by Pope Honorius III in April 1217.

He borrowed Venetian ships, promising to capture Durazzo, but failed and continued overland. Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus captured him, and Peter died in captivity without ruling Constantinople, where his wife Yolanda governed for a time.

皮埃尔二世·德·库尔特奈（约1155—约1218）是皮埃尔一世·德·库尔特奈之子、法兰西国王腓力二世的堂亲。他1190年参加第三次十字军东征，后来又投身阿尔比十字军和布汶战役。1216年内兄佛兰德斯的亨利死后，他被选为拉丁皇帝，1217年4月在罗马由教宗洪诺留三世加冕。

en:
Robert of Courtenay (1201–1228) was Latin emperor of Constantinople from 1221 until his death, a younger son of Peter II of Courtenay and Yolanda of Flanders. After his brother renounced the claim, he was crowned on 25 March 1221.

His reign brought defeat: Thessalonica fell to Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus in 1224, and John III Vatatzes of Nicaea beat him at Poimanenos the same year. A Burgundian conspiracy drove him from Constantinople; he fled to Rome and died in the Morea early in 1228.

en:
Albert V of Saxe-Lauenburg (c. 1335–1370) was the second son of Duke Albert IV and Beata of Schwerin. In 1356 he succeeded his childless brother John III as duke of the Saxe-Bergedorf-Molln branch. Short of money, he sold Molln, a key stage on the salt route to Scandinavia, to Lubeck for 9737.5 marks.

With his cousin Eric II he plundered merchants near Hamburg until 1363, when Hamburg and its allies stormed Bergedorf castle. By 1366 he had married Catherine of Werle-Gustrow, but died without heirs in 1370, and his brother Eric III succeeded him.

Eric I of Saxe-Lauenburg (c. 1280–1360) was an Ascanian duke, the second son of Duke John I of Saxony and Ingeborg. When John I abdicated in 1282, Eric and his brothers succeeded under their uncle Albert II's guardianship, and Saxony was partitioned into Saxe-Lauenburg and Saxe-Wittenberg in 1296.

Eric held Bergedorf and Lauenburg, inherited his brother Albert III's Ratzeburg share after 1308, and ceded Bergedorf to John II in 1321. About 1317 he married Elisabeth of Pomerania. He abdicated in 1338 for his son Eric II and died in exile at Nienburg in 1360.

他与堂侄萨克森-贝格多夫-默尔恩的阿尔布雷希特五世一道劫掠途经其领地的商人，1363年汉堡及其盟军联手出兵，攻陷了阿尔布雷希特在贝格多夫的城堡。

en:
Eric III of Saxe-Bergedorf (c. 1335–1401), youngest son of Duke Albert IV of Saxe-Lauenburg and Beata of Schwerin, was initially destined for the clergy. After his brothers John III and Albert V died without heirs he left the church and in 1370 succeeded Albert as duke of the heavily indebted Saxe-Bergedorf-Molln branch.

He pawned Bergedorf, the Vierlande, his half of the Saxon Wood and Geesthacht to Lubeck for 16262.5 marks, keeping only a life tenancy. He died heirless in 1401, succeeded by his cousin Eric IV, under whom the two branch duchies reunited.

zh:
萨克森-贝格多夫的埃里希三世（约1335—1401）是萨克森-劳恩堡公爵阿尔布雷希特四世与什未林的碧雅特的幼子，本拟从事神职。两位兄长约翰三世和阿尔布雷希特五世先后无嗣而终后，他离开教会，于1370年继阿尔布雷希特之位，统治负债累累的萨克森-贝格多夫-默尔恩支系公国。

他以16262.5吕贝克马克把贝格多夫、菲尔兰德、萨克森森林的一半份额和盖斯特哈赫特典给吕贝克，仅保留终身用益权。1401年他无嗣而终，族亲埃里希四世继位，两个支系公国在其治下重新统一。

en:
John I (1249–1285) was Duke of Saxony from the House of Ascania. After his father Albert I died in 1260, he ruled jointly with his younger brother Albert II, gradually partitioning the three disconnected Saxon lands between them in 1269, 1272 and 1282.

In 1270 he married Ingeborg. In 1282 he resigned in favour of his three minor sons John II, Eric I and Albert III, and entered the Franciscan monastery at Wittenberg, where he died on 30 July 1285.

zh:
约翰一世（1249—1285）是阿斯坎尼家族的萨克森公爵。1260年父亲阿尔布雷希特一世去世后，他与弟弟阿尔布雷希特二世共同执政，并于1269、1272和1282年逐步瓜分三块互不相连的萨克森领地。

en:
John II of Saxe-Lauenburg (c. 1275–1322) was the eldest son of Duke John I. After his father resigned in 1282, he and his brothers were guarded by their uncle Albert II and later ruled jointly with him. In 1296 Saxony was divided into Saxe-Wittenberg and Saxe-Lauenburg; John held the Mölln portion and gained Bergedorf from his brother Eric I in 1321, his branch becoming Saxe-Bergedorf-Mölln.

Though blind from his youth, he claimed the disputed Saxon electoral vote and joined the 1314 imperial election that raised Louis IV of Bavaria to the German kingship. He died on 22 April 1322.

萨克森-劳恩堡的约翰二世（约1275—1322）是约翰一世公爵的长子。1282年父亲退位后，他与弟弟们先由叔父阿尔布雷希特二世监护，成年后与叔父共同执政。1296年萨克森被分为萨克森-维滕贝格与萨克森-劳恩堡两部分，约翰分得默尔恩一份，1321年又从弟弟埃里希一世手中获得贝格多夫，他的支系因此称萨克森-贝格多夫-默尔恩。

他虽自幼失明，仍主张存在争议的萨克森选侯票，并参加了1314年推举巴伐利亚人路德维希四世为德意志国王的选帝。1322年4月22日去世。

en:
Thai chronicles make Kraisornrat a Tai ruler of the northern city-state of Chaliang in the upper Chao Phraya valley. Lavo's court had moved from Lavapura to Ayodhya in the 1080s, and its former seat stood vacant from 1087 until Kraisornrat took it in 1106.

Chaliang then became a northern stronghold of Lavapura, held by the crown prince. Kraisornrat married Suladevi, a princess of Si Satchanalai, and the chronicles name Sai Nam Phueng among his children.

泰国编年史记载，克赖颂叻是湄南河上游泰人城邦差良的统治者。罗涡王廷在1080年代从拉瓦普拉迁往阿约提亚，旧都的王位自1087年起空缺，直到克赖颂叻于1106年进占该城。

en:
Chronicles present Sri Thammasokkarat as a Tai ruler of Si Satchanalai. In 1181, when the Khmer king Jayavarman VII moved to recover Lavapura, the former Lavo capital, and appointed a kinsman to govern it, Sri Thammasokkarat withdrew under this pressure to Nakhon Si Thammarat on the Malay Peninsula.

Later Thai tradition honours him as founder of that city and first king of the Sri Thammasokaraj dynasty, whose rulers governed the twelve peninsula cities.

en:
Heinrich II Bochholt (died 1 March 1341), son of a Lübeck councilman, was elected bishop of Lübeck in 1317, the first commoner to hold the Hanseatic city's see. His election ended the quarrel his predecessor Burkhard von Serkem had waged with the city council, and Pope John XXII lifted the interdict Serkem had imposed.

After seven years at the papal court in Avignon, Heinrich in 1329 resumed the stalled Gothic high choir of Lübeck Cathedral, endowing five side altars at his own cost. He died in March 1341, a month before the choir was consecrated.

en:
Henry XIII (1235–1290) was the younger son of Otto II of Bavaria. In 1254 he succeeded his father with his brother Louis II, and in 1255 the brothers partitioned the duchy, Henry taking Lower Bavaria in its first division.

The unlawful division angered the Bavarian bishops, who allied with Ottokar II of Bohemia. Henry made Landshut his residence, began Burghausen Castle, and in 1257 joined Louis to repel Ottokar's invasion. He later warred on Salzburg and Passau and shifted his allegiance between Rudolph I and Ottokar.

His peace ordinances imposed heavy penalties for carrying swords or daggers in Landshut. He died in 1290, leaving Lower Bavaria to his son Otto III.

亨利十三世（1235—1290）是巴伐利亚公爵奥托二世较年幼的儿子。1254年他与兄长路德维希二世共同继承父位，1255年兄弟瓜分公国，亨利分得下巴伐利亚，这是巴伐利亚的首次分裂。

瓜分违反法律，激怒了巴伐利亚主教，他们与波希米亚国王奥托卡二世结盟。亨利以兰茨胡特为居所，动工修建布格豪森城堡，1257年与路德维希联手击退奥托卡的入侵。此后他屡与萨尔茨堡和帕绍交战，在鲁道夫一世与奥托卡之间反复倒戈。

他颁行的治安条例对在兰茨胡特携带剑或匕首者处以重罚。他于1290年去世，下巴伐利亚传给儿子奥托三世。

en:
Henry XIV (1305–1339) was a son of Stephen I of Lower Bavaria. When their father died in 1310, he and his brother Otto IV held the duchy under the guardianship of their cousin Emperor Louis IV. In 1328 he married Margaret, daughter of John of Bohemia.

He backed Louis against Frederick the Fair and in 1333, when the emperor considered resigning, became a candidate for the German crown. A feud with Otto IV and their cousin Henry XV over the partition of Lower Bavaria strained his ties with Louis and pushed him toward his father-in-law John; in winter 1337 he joined John's crusade with the Teutonic Order in Prussia.

After reconciling with Louis IV in 1339, he died of leprosy that 1 September. Lower Bavaria passed to his son John I, who died in 1340, and by December Bavaria was reunited under Louis IV.

亨利十四世（1305—1339）是下巴伐利亚公爵斯特凡一世之子。1310年父亲去世后，他与弟弟奥托四世在堂兄皇帝路德维希四世监护下继承公国。1328年，他娶波希米亚国王约翰之女玛格丽特。

他支持路德维希对抗美男子腓特烈，1333年路德维希考虑暂时退位时，他成为德意志王位候选人。后来他因瓜分下巴伐利亚与奥托四世及堂兄亨利十五世反目，与皇帝关系恶化，转而靠向岳父约翰；1337年冬，他随约翰赴普鲁士参加条顿骑士团的十字军。

1339年他与路德维希四世和解，同年9月1日死于麻风病。下巴伐利亚传给儿子约翰一世，约翰一世于1340年去世，当年12月巴伐利亚重归路德维希四世统一。

Henry XV (1312–1333), called the Natternberger after his favourite Natternberg Castle, was a Wittelsbach Duke of Lower Bavaria, son of Duke Otto III, born shortly before his father's death. He grew up under the tutelage of his cousin Emperor Louis IV and ruled jointly with his cousins Henry XIV and Otto IV until the partition of 1331 gave him Deggendorf and the surrounding lands.

In 1327 he stood unsuccessfully as a candidate for the Hungarian crown. He married Anna of Austria and died childless at Natternberg on 18 June 1333.

John I of Bavaria (1329–1340), called John the Child, was the only son of Duke Henry XIV of Lower Bavaria and Margaret of Bohemia, daughter of King John the Blind. In 1339 he married Anna, daughter of Emperor Louis IV, in Munich, sealing peace between the Wittelsbach branches. When Henry died that September, the emperor became his guardian.

John ruled Lower Bavaria only a year, dying at Landshut aged eleven; with him the Lower Bavarian line ended and Louis IV reunited the duchy divided in 1255.

en:
Kunigunde von Orlamünde (1303–1382) was a German noblewoman, the eldest daughter of Ulrich I, Landgrave of Leuchtenberg. In 1321 she married Otto VI, Count of Weimar-Orlamünde; the pair had no children of their own and adopted a daughter, Podika von Schaumnerg. Widowed with a large inheritance in 1340, she endowed the Cistercian Convent of the Celestial Throne in Nuremberg in 1342.

She served there as abbess until her death. German folklore later made her the model for the White Lady (Weiße Frau) said to haunt the Hohenzollern castles.

en:
Louis III (1269–1296) was a younger son of Henry XIII of Lower Bavaria. After his father's death in 1290, Lower Bavaria was held by the three brothers Otto III, Louis and Stephen, though Louis and Stephen only became co-regents in summer 1294. In 1293 the brothers agreed on an ordinance to limit their courts, allowing each just twelve horses for his stable.

Louis nevertheless raised taxes to fund a lavish household. He married Isabelle, daughter of Frederick III of Lorraine, and died childless on 13 May 1296, his share falling to his brothers.

Margaret of Bohemia (1313–1341), also called Margaret of Luxembourg, was the eldest daughter of King John of Bohemia and the Přemyslid princess Elizabeth; her brother later became the Emperor Charles IV. In 1328 she married Henry XIV, Duke of Lower Bavaria, allying him with her father against the Emperor Louis IV.

Her son John I was born in 1329; a second son died young. When John I's death ended the Lower Bavarian line in 1340, Louis IV took the duchy and Margaret withdrew to Bohemia, dying in Prague in July 1341.

波希米亚的玛格丽特（1313—1341），又称卢森堡的玛格丽特，是波希米亚国王约翰与普热米斯尔王朝公主伊丽莎白的长女，弟弟后来成为皇帝查理四世。1328年她嫁给下巴伐利亚公爵亨利十四世，这桩婚事使亨利与她的父亲结盟，共同对抗皇帝路德维希四世。

en:
Otto III (1261–1312), eldest son of Henry XIII, succeeded his father in 1290 and ruled Lower Bavaria jointly with his brothers Louis III and Stephen I. A grandson of Béla IV of Hungary, he fought for King Adolf against the Habsburgs at Göllheim in 1298.

Offered the Hungarian crown in 1301, he accepted in 1305 after Wenceslaus III renounced his claim. Otto slipped into Buda disguised as a merchant and was crowned at Székesfehérvár in December. His rival Charles of Anjou seized fortresses and Buda, and Ladislaus Kán of Transylvania imprisoned him in 1307. Otto abdicated in 1308 and died at Landshut in 1312.

en:
Otto IV (1307–1334) was a Wittelsbach Duke of Lower Bavaria, son of Duke Stephen I. From his father's death in 1310 he ruled jointly with his brother Henry XIV and cousin Henry XV. The co-regents warred among themselves in 1322, and in 1331 Lower Bavaria was partitioned, Otto taking Burghausen and Traunstein.

Estranged from his brother, he named his cousin Emperor Louis IV his contracted heir. He married Richardis of Jülich and died in Munich on 14 December 1334.

en:
Stephen I (1271–1310), born in Landshut, was the youngest son of Henry XIII of Lower Bavaria and Elizabeth of Hungary. Destined for the church in Salzburg, he was blocked by Pope Nicholas IV, and from 1290 ruled Lower Bavaria jointly with his brothers Otto III and Louis III.

While Otto pursued the Hungarian crown from 1305 to 1308, Stephen governed the duchy alone. He died in 1310 fighting the Habsburgs under Frederick I of Austria, leaving sons Henry XIV and Otto IV.

en:
Franchino I Rusca (died 1339), of the Rusconi family, was the Ghibelline lord of Como and a son of Pietro, lord of the city. In October 1301 Matteo I Visconti of Milan gave him his daughter Zaccarina in marriage, allying Como with the Visconti.

In 1313 Franchino crushed the rival Guelph Vitani family and became captain and lord of Como, ruling from 1327 as imperial vicar over the city and its countryside. The Visconti, into whose house he had married, then took the city from him.

In 1335 the Rusca, besieged by Bishop Benedetto da Asinago and barely able to defend themselves, turned again to Azzone Visconti: Franchino offered him the lordship of Como in return for Bellinzona, and Azzone entered the city that July. Franchino kept Bellinzona until he died in 1339; the Visconti took it a year later.

弗兰基诺一世·鲁斯科尼（?—1339）出身科莫的鲁斯科尼家族，属吉伯林派，是科莫领主彼得罗之子，自己也成为科莫领主。1301年10月，米兰的马泰奥一世·维斯孔蒂把女儿扎卡丽娜嫁给他，使科莫与维斯孔蒂家族结盟。

1313年，弗兰基诺击败对头圭尔夫派的维塔尼家族，成为科莫的统领兼领主，1327年起以帝国代牧身份统治科莫城及其乡郊。后来，与他联姻的维斯孔蒂家族反而夺走了科莫。

1335年，鲁斯科尼家族被主教贝内代托·达西纳戈围攻，又向阿佐内·维斯孔蒂求援；弗兰基诺提出把科莫的统治权让给他，换取贝林佐纳，阿佐内当年7月进入科莫。弗兰基诺保住贝林佐纳直到1339年去世，一年后维斯孔蒂家族夺取该城。

en:
Loterio Rusca (c. 1225–1291) was a Ghibelline nobleman of the Rusconi family of Como and the city's first de facto lord. Already signore del popolo, in 1276 he moved to set up a signoria and forced the hostile bishop Giovanni degli Avvocati into exile.

In 1284 he and William VII of Montferrat freed the Guelph leader Guido della Torre from Castel Baradello. War between Como and Milan continued until the Peace of Lomazzo in 1286 recognized his supremacy over the city.

en:
Napoleone, called Napo, della Torre (c. 1201–16 August 1278) was the leading noble of the Guelph della Torre house and de facto lord of Milan from 1265. He succeeded his cousin Filippo as Anziano del Popolo of Milan.

In 1267 he commanded the Guelph league against Conradin. He later refused to support Charles of Anjou's expansion and in 1273 joined the imperial party to counter him, becoming imperial vicar in Lombardy in 1274.

On 21 January 1277 Archbishop Ottone Visconti defeated and captured him at Desio, ending della Torre rule in Milan. He died after nineteen months in a cage at Castel Baradello in Como.

拿波列奥内·德拉·托雷（约1201—1278年8月16日），绰号纳波，是圭尔夫派德拉·托雷家族的首要贵族，1265年起成为米兰的实际统治者。他接替堂兄菲利波出任米兰“人民长老”。

1267年，他统领圭尔夫联盟对抗康拉丁。此后他拒绝支持安茹的查理扩张，1273年转向皇帝阵营以抗衡查理，1274年出任伦巴第帝国代牧。

1277年1月21日，米兰大主教奥托内·维斯孔蒂在代西奥将他击败俘获，德拉·托雷家族在米兰的统治就此终结。他被囚于科莫巴拉德罗城堡的牢笼中十九个月后死去。

en:
Pietro Rusconi was a nobleman of the Ghibelline Rusconi family of Como and a younger son of the city's first lord, Loterio Rusca. In March 1286 he was one of four Como envoys who settled terms with Milan in the negotiations that produced the Peace of Lomazzo.

In 1291 he is recorded as podestà of Carasso near Bellinzona, a district then held by the Rusconi. He had died before 1302.

彼得罗·鲁斯科尼出身科莫的吉伯林派贵族鲁斯科尼家族，是科莫首任统治者洛泰里奥·鲁斯科尼的幼子之一。1286年3月，他作为科莫的四名谈判代表之一与米兰方面商定条款，最终促成《洛马佐和约》。

en:
Zaccarina Visconti (died c. 1322) was a daughter of Matteo I Visconti, lord of Milan. In 1300 her father promised her in marriage to Riccardo Langosco, on condition that his father Filippone expel the Beccaria family from Pavia.

Matteo nevertheless broke the engagement and in October 1301 married her instead to Franchino I Rusca, the Ghibelline lord of Como. She gave Franchino three sons, Lotario, Alberto and Ottone.

扎卡丽娜·维斯孔蒂（?—约1322）是米兰统治者马泰奥一世·维斯孔蒂之女。1300年，父亲将她许配给里卡尔多·兰戈斯科，条件是其父菲利波内把贝卡里亚家族逐出帕维亚。

en:
Malik Izz al-Din Husayn III was the sixteenth atabeg of the Khorshidi dynasty of Little Luristan, succeeding his murdered father Shuja al-Din Mahmud in 1349 or 1350 when he was about twelve. He allied with the Muzaffarids and the Jalayirids: in 1383 Shah Shuja married his daughter at Khorramabad and another daughter married Ahmad Jalayir.

Timur's armies ravaged Luristan in 1386 and razed the fortress of Khorramabad. Captured and exiled to Turkestan in 1388, he returned three years later, but around 1404 his severed head was displayed stuffed with straw.

马利克·伊兹丁·侯赛因三世是小洛雷斯坦霍什迪王朝第十六代阿塔伯克，1349或1350年父亲舒贾丁·马哈茂德被杀时，他年仅约十二岁便继位。他与穆扎法尔王朝和札剌亦儿王朝结盟：1383年，沙阿·舒贾在霍拉马巴德迎娶他的一个女儿，另一个女儿嫁给艾哈迈德·札剌亦儿。

en:
Shuja al-Din Mahmud Khorshidi was the fifteenth atabeg of the Khorshidi dynasty, which ruled Little Luristan from its capital Khorramabad. The son of Izz al-Din Husayn II, he succeeded his father in the 1330s and kept close to the camp of the Ilkhanids as Mongol power in Iran broke apart.

His reign ended in 1349 or 1350, when his own subjects killed him. He was succeeded by his twelve-year-old son Izz al-Din Husayn, the future Malik Izz al-Din Husayn III.

en:
Siemowit of Dobrzyń (c. 1262–1312) was a Piast prince, son of Casimir I of Kuyavia, who received the Dobrzyń district in the family division of around 1288. Captured by Lithuanian raiders in 1293, he spent two years in captivity while his brother Władysław I ruled the duchy. Around 1296 he married Anastasia.

He did homage to Wenceslaus II of Bohemia in 1300, was deposed in 1303 and restored in 1305, after which he backed Władysław. He died in 1312, leaving minor sons under the regency of his widow and brother.

en:
Władysław the Hunchback (c. 1303–1352) was a Piast prince, the son of Siemowit of Dobrzyń and Anastasia of Halych–Volhynia. He ruled Dobrzyń from 1312, and in 1327 exchanged it with his uncle Władysław I the Elbow-high for the Duchy of Łęczyca amid Teutonic Order pressure.

The 1343 Treaty of Kalisz returned Dobrzyń to him. Childless, he died in 1351 or 1352, and his lands reverted to the Polish crown.

She was the mother of Otto III, who later ruled Anhalt-Bernburg. Bernhard died in August 1348, and Matilda was still living on 28 June 1354.

不伦瑞克-沃尔芬比特尔的玛蒂尔达是不伦瑞克-沃尔芬比特尔公爵马格努斯一世与勃兰登堡-施滕达尔的索菲娅之女。约1343年，她成为安哈尔特-贝恩堡亲王伯恩哈德三世的第三任妻子，使韦尔夫家族与安哈尔特的阿斯坎尼王公联姻。

她的儿子奥托三世后来统治安哈尔特-贝恩堡。伯恩哈德于1348年8月去世，玛蒂尔达在1354年6月28日仍在世。

en:
Sophia of Brandenburg-Stendal (1300–1356) was the daughter of Margrave Henry I of Brandenburg-Stendal and Agnes of Bavaria, born into the Ascanian dynasty. In 1327 she married Magnus the Pious, Duke of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, linking the Askaniers to the Welfs.

She bore him several children who reached adulthood, including Magnus II with the Necklace, Albert, Prince-Archbishop of Bremen, and Matilda, wife of Bernhard III of Anhalt-Bernburg. Her daughters Agnes and Sophie married into the counts of Hohnstein.

勃兰登堡-施滕达尔的索菲娅（1300—1356）是勃兰登堡-施滕达尔藩侯亨利一世与巴伐利亚的阿格尼丝之女，出身阿斯坎尼家族。1327年，她嫁给不伦瑞克-沃尔芬比特尔公爵“虔诚者”马格努斯，使阿斯坎尼家族与韦尔夫家族联姻。

她所生并长大成人的子女包括“戴项链者”马格努斯二世、不来梅大主教阿尔贝特，以及嫁给安哈尔特-贝恩堡的伯恩哈德三世的玛蒂尔达；女儿阿格尼丝和索菲娅则嫁入霍恩施泰因伯爵家族。

en:
Yi Se-jwa (1445–1504), enfeoffed as Prince Kwangyang, was a civil official of early Joseon. In 1482, under King Seongjong, he carried the royal order that forced the deposed Queen Yun, mother of the future King Yeonsangun, to take poison.

During the literati purge of 1498 he urged the execution of Kim Chong-jik and his followers. After he accidentally spilled wine on Yeonsangun's robe at a banquet in 1503, the king exiled him on a charge of lèse-majesté.

His role in Queen Yun's death later caught up with him. In the purge of 1504 the king had him put to death.

zh:
李世佐（1445—1504），封广阳君，是朝鲜王朝前期的文臣。1482年成宗在位时，他奉命将被废的尹氏赐死，而尹氏正是后来燕山君的生母。

1498年戊午士祸时，他奏请处死金宗直及其门人。1503年的一次宴会上，他不慎把酒洒在燕山君的衣服上，被以凌上的罪名流放。

他曾参与赐死尹氏一事后来牵连到他。1504年甲子士祸中，燕山君将他处死。

en:
Diarmait mac Máel na mBó (died 7 February 1072) was King of Leinster and, with opposition, High King of Ireland. In 1042 he made himself king of Leinster and installed his son Murchad as king of Dublin. Allied with the king of Ulaid, he pressed the kingdoms of Mide and Brega.

After 1066 he sheltered the sons of King Harold Godwinson and lent them the Dublin fleet for invasions of England in 1068 and 1069. He was killed fighting Conchobar Ua Máel Sechlainn of Mide at the battle of Odhbha on 7 February 1072.

迪尔梅特·马克·梅尔·纳·姆博（?—1072年2月7日）是伦斯特国王，并在反对声中成为爱尔兰至高王。1042年，他自立为伦斯特国王，并立其子穆尔哈德为都柏林国王。他与乌拉德国王结盟，向米斯和布雷加两个王国施压。

en:
Domhnall mac Art mac Murchada Caomhánach was a king of Leinster from the Kavanagh dynasty, the Gaelic lineage that held out in the Wicklow highlands after the Norman invasion of Ireland. He succeeded his father Art mac Murchada, who had ruled from 1314, and reigned from 1323 to 1338.

He allied with Murchad O'Byrne against English settlers and may have been elected king at an assembly in 1328. Captured soon afterwards, he escaped from Dublin in January 1331, and in 1335 he campaigned in Scotland for Edward III. In 1338 he was succeeded by his son Domhnall mac Domhnall, who ruled Leinster until 1347.

多姆纳尔·麦克·阿特·麦克·穆尔哈达·卡瓦纳是卡瓦纳王朝的伦斯特国王；诺曼人入侵爱尔兰后，这一盖尔支系在威克洛高地坚持抵抗。他于1323年继承父亲阿特·麦克·穆尔哈达之位（其父自1314年起在位），统治至1338年。

他与穆尔哈德·奥伯恩结盟对抗英格兰殖民者，可能于1328年在一次集会上被推举为国王。不久他被俘，1331年1月从都柏林逃脱，1335年又为爱德华三世在苏格兰作战。1338年，其子多姆纳尔·麦克·多姆纳尔继位，统治伦斯特至1347年。

Anna of Nuremberg (c. 1314–1340), daughter of Burgrave Frederick IV of Nuremberg, married Ulrich I, Landgrave of Leuchtenberg, as his second wife on 23 April 1328.

Ulrich died in 1334 and Anna herself in 1340. Her children were Ulrich II and John I, who both became landgraves of Leuchtenberg, Margarethe, Elisabeth, who married John I of Henneberg-Schleusingen, and another Anna, who married Kraft III of Hohenlohe-Weikersheim.

en:
John I of Leuchtenberg (c. 1330–1407) was the second son of Landgrave Ulrich I of Leuchtenberg and Anna of Nuremberg. After his father died in 1334, he and his elder brother Ulrich II ruled jointly until 1366, when they divided the landgraviate: John received the eastern part and kept his seat at Pleystein, while the two brothers governed the south together.

In 1376 Emperor Charles IV raised him to landgrave of Leuchtenberg and count of Hals near Passau. He married Metze of Rožmberk and died on 2 December 1407.

en:
Ulrich II of Leuchtenberg (c. 1326–1378) was landgrave of Leuchtenberg from 1334, succeeding his father Ulrich I; his mother was Anna of Nuremberg, daughter of Burgrave Frederick IV. In 1366 he and his brother Johann divided the landgraviate, Ulrich taking the west and Johann the east.

He moved his residence from Leuchtenberg Castle to Pfreimd, which he raised to a town in 1372 with a six-year tax exemption to attract settlers. In 1376 Emperor Charles IV named him count of Hals. He married Margarete of Niemodlin.

en:
Ulrich I of Leuchtenberg (1293–23 November 1334) was landgrave of Leuchtenberg, succeeding his father Gebhard VI in 1293. In 1313 he fought at the Battle of Gammelsdorf for Louis the Bavarian. In 1332 he purchased the town of Pfreimd, which later became the landgraves' residence.

He died in the monastery of Walderbach on 23 November 1334. By his second wife Anna of Nuremberg he fathered his successors Ulrich II and John I.

洛伊希滕贝格的乌尔里希一世（1293—1334年11月23日）是洛伊希滕贝格方伯，1293年继父格布哈德六世之位。1313年，他在加梅尔斯多夫战役中站在巴伐利亚人路德维希一方作战。1332年，他购得普弗赖姆德镇，此地后来成为历代方伯的居所。

1334年11月23日，他在瓦尔德巴赫的修道院去世。第二任妻子纽伦堡的安娜为他生下继承人乌尔里希二世和约翰一世。

en:
Bolesław III the Generous (1291–1352), eldest son of Henry V the Fat, was Duke of Legnica, Brzeg and Wrocław from 1296. He married Margareta, daughter of Wenceslaus II of Bohemia, and after the Přemyslids died out in 1306 claimed the Bohemian crown: he took Opava in 1308 but renounced his claim at Olomouc in 1311.

The 1311 division left him Brzeg, and he could not retake Wrocław from his brothers. He became a Bohemian vassal in 1329, and in 1342 abdicated Legnica to his sons Wenceslaus I and Louis I, retiring to Brzeg.

zh:
“慷慨者”博莱斯瓦夫三世（1291—1352）是“胖子”亨里克五世的长子，自1296年起任莱格尼察、布热格和弗罗茨瓦夫公爵。他娶波希米亚国王瓦茨拉夫二世之女玛格丽特为妻；1306年普热米斯尔王朝绝嗣后，他宣称波希米亚王位，1308年夺取奥帕瓦，却于1311年在奥洛穆茨放弃了主张。

1311年的诸子分地使他只得到布热格，他也未能从兄弟手中夺回弗罗茨瓦夫。1329年他成为波希米亚附庸，1342年把莱格尼察让给儿子瓦茨瓦夫一世和路德维克一世，自己退居布热格。

en:
Henry V the Fat (c. 1248–22 February 1296), eldest son of Bolesław II of Legnica, held the duchies of Jawor from 1273, Legnica from 1278 and Wrocław from 1290. In 1277 his charge at Stolec turned his father's defeat into victory and captured two dukes.

Seized by Henry IV Probus in 1281, he was forced to recognize him as duke of Wrocław, though its citizens invited him to rule in 1290. In 1293 Henry III of Głogów imprisoned him for six months in an iron cage, and he died on 22 February 1296 leaving minor sons under his brother Bolko.

胖子亨里克五世（约1248—1296年2月22日）是莱格尼察公爵波列斯瓦夫二世的长子，1273年起任雅沃尔公爵，1278年起任莱格尼察公爵，1290年起任弗罗茨瓦夫公爵。1277年，他在斯托莱茨一役的冲锋扭转了父亲的败局，俘获两名公爵。

1281年，他被亨里克四世·普罗布斯扣押，被迫承认其为弗罗茨瓦夫公爵，但1290年弗罗茨瓦夫市民邀他统治。1293年，格沃古夫公爵亨里克三世把他囚禁在铁笼中达六个月；他于1296年2月22日去世，诸子年幼，由弟弟波尔科监护。

en:
Katarina Šubić (died 1358), daughter of Mladen II Šubić, Ban of Croatia, married Bolesław III the Generous, Duke of Legnica-Brzeg, in 1326, four years after his first wife's death; the marriage was childless. When Bolesław abdicated in 1342 she retired with him to Brzeg.

On his death in 1352 his will left her the Duchies of Brzeg and Oława as her dower, to rule in her own right for life. She reigned over Brzeg for six years, and after her death in 1358 the lands passed to her stepsons Wenceslaus I and Louis I.

en:
Louis I the Fair (c. 1321–1398), second son of Bolesław III the Generous of Legnica, won Brzeg and Chojnów after a six-year war against his brother Wenceslaus I, settled in 1359.

After Wenceslaus died in 1364 he ruled Legnica as regent for his underage nephews until 1373, repaired its finances and bought back Brzeg-Oława in 1368. A trusted imperial mediator, he promoted the cult of St Hedwig and was buried at Brzeg in 1398.

en:
Margaret of Bohemia (21 February 1296–8 April 1322) was a daughter of King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia. Betrothed by her father to Bolesław III the Generous, Duke of Legnica and Brzeg, she married him in 1308.

The match gave Bolesław a claim to the Bohemian crown after the Přemyslid dynasty died out in 1306, although the crown passed to John of Luxembourg. She died on 8 April 1322, one day after giving birth to her youngest son Nikolaus; her surviving sons were Wenceslaus I and Louis I the Fair.

en:
Wenceslaus I (c. 1318–1364), eldest son of Bolesław III the Generous of Legnica, ruled Legnica-Brzeg jointly with his brother Louis I after their father abdicated in 1342, dividing their rule in 1345.

A quarrel over the inheritance after their father's death in 1352 sparked a six-year civil war; defeated in 1359, Wenceslaus ceded Brzeg-Oława and Chojnów to Louis. A loyal supporter of Emperor Charles IV, he died excommunicated for unpaid debts and was buried in the Legnica church he had founded.

en:
Heinrich II von Lichtenberg (died before 9 February 1269) ruled as lord of Lichtenberg in Lower Alsace jointly with his brother Ludwig II, and like their father Ludwig I he held the advocacy (Vogt) of Strasbourg. Both brothers are first recorded in 1249, and under them the family built up its Alsatian estates.

After they died the dynasty split in 1271 into an elder and a younger line: Heinrich's descendants formed the elder branch, headed by his son Conrad I, while Ludwig II's heirs formed the younger.

海因里希二世·冯·利希滕贝格（？—1269）与兄弟路德维希二世共治下阿尔萨斯的利希滕贝格领地，并和父亲路德维希一世一样担任斯特拉斯堡的福格特（护尉官）。兄弟二人都始见于1249年的记载，在他们治下家族在阿尔萨斯积累地产。

en:
Johann I von Lichtenberg, called the Elder (first recorded 1281, died 22 August 1315), was lord of Lichtenberg and Vogt in Alsace, leading the younger branch created by the family partition of 1271. The second son of Ludwig II and Elisabeth of Baden, he inherited that line's estates and married Adelaide of Werdenberg.

When the elder branch's Conrad I died in 1294, Johann became guardian of Conrad's young son Johann II. His uncle Konrad III was bishop of Strasbourg.

1294年长支的康拉德一世去世后，他成为其年幼之子约翰二世的监护人。他的叔父康拉德三世曾任斯特拉斯堡主教。

en:
Johann II von Lichtenberg, called Hannemann (born before 1295, died 1366), was head of the elder line of the Lords of Lichtenberg in Alsace. His father Konrad I died when he was still a minor, and a younger-line kinsman acted as his guardian. In 1318 he married Johanna von Leiningen.

From 1330 treaties split the Lichtenberg lands between the two lines. In 1340 he failed in a dispute over Gottesheim with Count Palatine Rudolf II, and in 1341 had to acknowledge Electoral Palatinate's suzerainty.

约翰二世·冯·利希滕贝格，绰号“哈尼曼”（1295年前—1366），是阿尔萨斯利希滕贝格领主家族长支的族长。父亲康拉德一世早逝时他尚未成年，由家族幼支的亲属担任监护人。1318年他迎娶约翰娜·冯·莱宁根。

en:
Ludwig I von Lichtenberg (first attested 1206, died 1252) was an Alsatian nobleman. He was lord of Lichtenberg and Vogt of Neuweiler.

He was the father of Ludwig II and Heinrich II, who carried on the secular lordship, and of Conrad III and Friedrich I, who both became bishops of Strasbourg; his other sons also entered the church. The later Lichtenberg lords all descended from his line.

路德维希一世·冯·利希滕贝格（1206年首见记载，1252年卒）是阿尔萨斯贵族。他担任利希滕贝格领主和诺伊韦勒的地方代牧。

他的儿子路德维希二世和海因里希二世承续世俗领地；另两子康拉德三世和弗里德里希一世都官至斯特拉斯堡主教，其余诸子也都成为教士。后来的历代利希滕贝格领主都出自他这一支。

en:
Ludwig II von Lichtenberg (first recorded 1249, died 1271) ruled as lord of Lichtenberg jointly with his brother Heinrich II and served as Landvogt, the territorial advocate, in Alsace. A son of Ludwig I, he married Margravine Elisabeth of Baden.

Their sons included Johann I, later head of the younger Lichtenberg line, and Sigibodo, who became bishop of Speyer in 1302. After the two brothers' deaths the family estates were divided in 1271 into an elder and a younger branch.

en:
Adolf II von der Mark (1288–1344), third son of Eberhard I of the Mark, became Prince-Bishop of Liège in 1313 through King Philip IV. In 1316 resistance forced him to sign the Peace of Fexhe; after trying to revoke it he fled to Huy and put Liège under interdict.

He sold Mechelen to Flanders in 1333 and failed to annex Loon in 1336. The Tribunal of the XXII curbed his authority in 1343, a year before he died.

en:
Ibn al-Khatib (1313–1374) was an Arab-Andalusi poet, historian, physician and vizier of the Nasrid Emirate of Granada. After his father and brother died at the Battle of Río Salado in 1340, he became vizier to Yusuf I, later serving Muhammad V.

Arrested after a coup in 1359, he went into exile in Morocco, returning when Muhammad regained the throne in 1362. His poems adorn the Alhambra, and his history of Granada, al-Ihata, was completed in 1369.

Exiled to Morocco a second time, he was arrested on a heresy charge in 1374 and strangled in prison at Fes, where his body was burned.

zh:
伊本·哈提卜（1313—1374）是阿拉伯安达卢西亚的诗人、史家、医生，也是奈斯尔王朝格拉纳达埃米尔国的维齐尔。1340年父亲与兄长在萨拉多河战役中战死后，他成为优素福一世的维齐尔，后来又效力于穆罕默德五世。

1359年政变后他被捕，流亡摩洛哥，1362年穆罕默德复位后回国复职。他的诗作装饰着阿尔罕布拉宫，记述格拉纳达历史的《群书荟萃》于1369年成书。

第二次流亡摩洛哥后，他于1374年以异端罪名被捕，在非斯狱中被缢杀，尸体遭焚。

en:
Butigeidis (died 1290 or 1291) was Grand Duke of Lithuania from 1285 and the first undisputed Gediminid ruler, taking power after Daumantas' death. He fought the Teutonic Order, which had recently overrun Suvalkija. In 1289 he led about eight thousand men against a Teutonic stronghold in Sambia.

Butigeidis was the first grand duke to fortify the Nemunas with a chain of castles. With his brother Butvydas he ceded Vawkavysk to Volhynia under a peace treaty, and Butvydas succeeded.

布蒂盖迪斯（1290或1291年卒）自1285年起任立陶宛大公，是格迪米纳斯王朝第一位无可争议的统治者，在道曼塔斯死后掌权。他在位期间与刚征服苏瓦尔基亚的条顿骑士团作战。1289年，他率约八千人进攻骑士团在桑比亚的据点。

en:
Butvydas, also known as Pukuveras (died c. 1295), was Grand Duke of Lithuania from about 1290. First mentioned in 1289 making peace with Volhynia alongside his brother Grand Duke Butigeidis, he may have shared power before ruling alone after Butigeidis died.

His short reign was spent resisting annual Teutonic Order raids into Samogitia and fighting the Order's Polish allies in Masovia. He was the father of Grand Dukes Vytenis and Gediminas, who built Lithuania into a major power.

en:
Gediminas (c. 1275–1341) became grand duke of Lithuania around 1316 and made it a power between the Teutonic Knights and weakened Ruthenian principalities. Pressed by the Teutonic and Livonian orders, he allied with the Tatars in 1319 and wrote to the Pope in 1322 offering baptism. In 1323 he invited Hanseatic merchants and artisans to settle in his lands and made peace with the Livonian Order, but he backed out of baptism and stayed pagan.

In 1325 his daughter Aldona married Casimir, future king of Poland. In the east he took Belarusian and Ukrainian lands, seized Kiev after the battle on the Irpin, and brought Lithuania close to the Black Sea.

Legend says an iron wolf in a dream led him to found Vilnius. He died in 1341, probably killed in a coup, leaving the Gediminid dynasty; his son Jaunutis succeeded him but was deposed by Algirdas in 1345.

zh:
格迪米纳斯（约1275—1341）约1316年起任立陶宛大公，在条顿骑士团与衰弱的罗斯诸公国之间，把立陶宛经营成一方强权。面对条顿和利沃尼亚骑士团的压力，1319年他与鞑靼人结盟，1322年致信教皇表示愿意受洗。1323年，他邀请汉萨商人与工匠入境定居，并与利沃尼亚骑士团议和，但他在受洗一事上反悔，终身信奉异教。

1325年，他的女儿阿尔东娜嫁给后来的波兰国王卡齐米日。在东方，他吞并白俄罗斯和乌克兰的土地，在伊尔平河战役后夺取基辅，使立陶宛逼近黑海。

相传他梦见铁狼，因而建立维尔纽斯。他于1341年去世，据推测死于政变，留下格迪米纳斯王朝；儿子尧努蒂斯继位，1345年被阿尔吉尔达斯推翻。

en:
Jaunė (died c. 1344) was said to have been the third wife of Gediminas, Grand Duke of Lithuania; historian Józef Wolff identified her as a daughter of Prince Ivan of Polatsk. She appears only in the late Bychowiec Chronicle, and some historians doubt she ever lived, though she is said to have borne Gediminas Algirdas, Kęstutis and Liubartas.

After her death in 1344, her elder sons Algirdas and Kęstutis drove their brother Jaunutis, Gediminas's chosen heir, from Vilnius in 1345. Tradition also credits her with founding an Orthodox monastery.

zh:
雅乌拿（约1344年卒）相传是立陶宛大公格迪米纳斯的第三任妻子，历史学家约瑟夫·沃尔夫认为她是波洛茨克王公伊凡之女。她只见于成书较晚的《贝霍维茨编年史》，部分史学家怀疑她确有其人；相传她为格迪米纳斯生下阿尔吉尔达斯、科斯图提斯和柳巴尔塔斯。

1344年她死后，年长的儿子阿尔吉尔达斯与科斯图提斯于1345年把格迪米纳斯指定的继承人尧努蒂斯逐出维尔纽斯。相传她还创立了一座东正教修道院。

en:
Jaunutis (c. 1300–after 1366) succeeded his father Gediminas as Grand Duke of Lithuania in 1341. His peaceful rule ended in 1345, when his elder brothers Algirdas and Kęstutis deposed him: Kęstutis seized Vilnius and installed Algirdas.

Offered Zasłaŭje, Jaunutis resisted, was imprisoned, escaped to Moscow and was baptized as Ioann, but won no support. He later reconciled with Algirdas and ruled Zasłaŭje until 1366.

zh:
尧努蒂斯（约1300—1366年后）于1341年继父亲格迪米纳斯之后成为立陶宛大公。他治内大体平静，1345年兄长阿尔吉尔达斯和科斯图提斯合力将他废黜：科斯图提斯夺取维尔纽斯，拥立阿尔吉尔达斯。

尧努蒂斯拒绝接受扎斯拉夫耶，反抗失败后被囚，逃脱后前往莫斯科受洗改名约安，却未求得援助。他后来与阿尔吉尔达斯和解，领有扎斯拉夫耶，1366年最后见于记载。

en:
Kęstutis (c. 1297–1382), son of Grand Duke Gediminas, was Duke of Trakai and, from 1345, co-ruler with his brother Algirdas, ruling western Lithuania. He spent decades defending Lithuania against the Teutonic Knights, negotiating conversion with the pope and accepting a crown promise from the King of Hungary only to escape.

After Algirdas died in 1377 he seized Vilnius from his nephew Jogaila in 1381 and ruled alone, but Jogaila retook the city in 1382; Kęstutis was captured and died in Kreva Castle. His son by Birutė was Vytautas.

科斯图提斯（约1297—1382）是立陶宛大公格迪米纳斯之子，受封特拉凯公爵，1345年起与兄长阿尔吉尔达斯共同统治，主持立陶宛西部防务。他数十年间抵御条顿骑士团的进攻，曾与教皇谈判受洗封王，又接受匈牙利的王冠许诺后中途逃脱。

1377年阿尔吉尔达斯死后，他于1381年从侄子雅盖洛手中夺取维尔纽斯独自称大公；1382年雅盖洛夺回城市，科斯图提斯被俘，死于克雷瓦城堡。他与比鲁特所生之子即维陶塔斯。

en:
Liubartas (died c. 1385), youngest son of Grand Duke Gediminas of Lithuania, was the last ruler of Galicia–Volhynia. About 1321 he married Andrew of Galicia's daughter and received Lutsk. After Yuri II Boleslav was poisoned in 1340, rebel nobles invited him to rule.

In 1349 Casimir III took all but eastern Volhynia, and Liubartas was captured in 1351; the 1366 treaty left him eastern Volhynia, and after Casimir's death in 1370 he seized all of Volhynia. He backed Kęstutis against Jogaila and built Lutsk Castle.

zh:
柳巴尔塔斯（约1385年卒）是立陶宛大公格迪米纳斯的幼子，也是加利西亚－沃里尼亚的末代统治者。约1321年，他娶加利西亚的安德烈之女，获得卢茨克。1340年尤里二世·博莱斯瓦夫被毒杀后，贵族邀他前来统治。

1349年卡齐米日三世夺取其几乎全部领地，柳巴尔塔斯于1351年被俘；1366年的条约只留给他东沃里尼亚，1370年卡齐米日死后他攻占整个沃里尼亚。他支持兄长科斯图提斯对抗约盖拉，并修建了卢茨克城堡。

en:
Margiris or Margis (died 25 February 1336) was a Lithuanian prince remembered as the defender of Pilėnai. In early 1329, during the Teutonic crusade in which King John of Bohemia captured Medvėgalis, a Lithuanian challenged John to single combat and later paid a ransom.

In February 1336 a Teutonic army stormed Pilėnai, which held some four thousand people. When defense became hopeless Margiris killed his wife and guards and then himself, while the defenders burned the castle rather than surrender. He became a Lithuanian national hero.

en:
Skalmantas, also called Skolomend (born c. 1210, died after 1285), is the possible early ancestor of the Gediminid dynasty. He is known only from later sources: the late fourteenth-century Russian poem Zadonshchina has two sons of Algirdas call themselves great-grandsons of Skalmantas.

Scholars debate whether he was Gediminas's grandfather or father, and some identify him with the Sudovian (Yotvingian) leader Komantas. Tradition makes Butigeidis and Butvydas his sons.

斯卡尔曼塔斯，又名斯科洛缅德（约1210年生，1285年后卒），可能是格迪米纳斯王朝的早期祖先。他仅见于后世文献：14世纪末的罗斯史诗《扎顿什奇纳》中，阿尔吉尔达斯的两个儿子自称是斯卡尔曼塔斯的曾孙。

学界对他究竟是格迪米纳斯的祖父还是父亲存有争议，也有人认为他就是苏多维亚人（约特文吉人）首领科曼塔斯。传统世系把布蒂盖迪斯和布特维达斯列为他的儿子。

en:
Vytenis was Grand Duke of Lithuania from about 1295 to about 1316, the first Gediminid to enjoy a long reign. As grand duke he recovered Ruthenian lands lost after Mindaugas' death and took Pinsk and Turov. In 1298, allied with Riga, he defeated the Livonian Order at Turaida, killing Land Master Bruno, and around 1307 he annexed Polatsk.

He campaigned against the Teutonic Knights and was last recorded in September 1315 besieging Christmemel. He died soon after without an heir, and his brother Gediminas succeeded.

en:
Eberhard von Monheim (c. 1275–before 1362) was Landmeister of the Teutonic Order's Livonian branch from 1328 to 1340, and the man who brought Riga to heel. A former commander of Ventspils and Kuldīga, he took office as Livonia flared up: in 1328 the Letts burned the order's fortress at Daugavgrīva, and the Lithuanians joined the rising, raiding as far as Paistu in 1329.

After pushing them back he besieged Riga from September 1329. Severe famine struck the city, and it surrendered on 17 March 1330. He had part of its walls pulled down and began an order fortress outside the old city limits, the later Riga Castle.

A winter campaign against Lithuania failed in 1340 and he resigned in June. He later held a commandery in Cologne or Mechelen and was last recorded in 1360 as an official in Prussia.

埃伯哈德·冯·蒙海姆（约1275—1362年前）1328至1340年任条顿骑士团利沃尼亚分支的首领，正是他制服了里加。他此前曾指挥文茨皮尔斯和库尔迪加城堡，上任时利沃尼亚恰好陷入动荡：1328年拉脱维亚人烧毁骑士团在道加夫格里瓦的要塞，立陶宛人加入叛乱，1329年一路袭至派斯图。

他击退立陶宛人后，于1329年9月起围攻里加。城内发生严重饥荒，里加于1330年3月17日投降。他下令拆毁部分城墙，并在旧城界外动工修建骑士团要塞，即后来的里加城堡。

1340年讨伐立陶宛的冬季战事失败，他于6月辞职。此后他在科隆或梅赫伦担任骑士团指挥官，1360年最后一次见于记载，当时在普鲁士任职。
