en:
Phayu was king of the Lan Na kingdom in northern Thailand, succeeding his father Khamfu, who by legend died after being bitten by a mermaid or crocodile. A chronicle records that his ministers crowned him at Chiang Mai when he was twenty-eight. Khamfu had moved the court to Chiang Saen; Phayu moved the capital back to Chiang Mai.

Tradition portrays him as a righteous Buddhist ruler, under whom the kingdom knew peace and prosperity and Buddhism flourished. He died in 1355, and the ministers invited his son Kue Na, governor of Chiang Saen, to take the throne.

帕育是泰国北部兰纳王国的国王，继承父亲坎富的王位；相传坎富是被美人鱼或鳄鱼咬伤后死去的。史载大臣们在清迈为二十八岁的他举行加冕。坎富原把朝廷设在清盛，帕育则把都城迁回清迈。

传统说法称他是笃信佛教的贤明君主，治下国家和平安宁、佛教兴盛。他于1355年去世，大臣们迎请曾治理清盛的儿子古纳继位。

en:
Frederick IV (c. 1250–1316) was Count of Leiningen, son of Count Frederick III and Adelaide of Kyburg. He ruled the family lands jointly with his uncle Emicho IV and cousin Emicho V, and after Emicho V died around 1289 he inherited part of their estates, including Madenburg Castle.

From 1275 to 1301 he was landvogt of Speyergau under Emperor Rudolf of Habsburg, and in 1301 Emperor Albert I pledged him Falkenburg Castle. His sons Frederick V of Leiningen-Dagsburg and Godfrey of Leiningen-Hardenburg divided the inheritance in 1317.

en:
Frederick V (born c. 1269, died after 1327) was Count of Leiningen and lord of Leiningen-Dagsburg and Ormes, the eldest son of Count Frederick IV and Johanna of Sponheim-Kreuznach. When his father died in 1316, he and his half-brother Godfrey I of Leiningen-Hardenburg divided the family lands in 1317, Frederick taking Dagsburg and so founding the Leiningen-Dagsburg line.

He married Sophie of Freiburg and, after her death, Marie of Châtillon, and was succeeded by his son Frederick VI; the Dagsburg line died out in 1467.

en:
Frederick VI of Leiningen-Dagsburg (c. 1294–1342), also numbered Frederick V, ruled as count of Leiningen-Dagsburg in the Vosges. He was the only son of Count Frederick V and his first wife Sophie of Freiburg, and married Jutta of Isenburg-Limburg, who died in 1335.

Their sons included Frederick VII, who kept Dagsburg, Frederick VIII, ancestor of the Rixingen line, and Emich. Frederick died between 1 January and 21 July 1342, and his sons divided the inheritance in 1343.

en:
Godfrey, in German Joffrid I of Leiningen-Hardenburg (c. 1304–1344), was count of Leiningen-Hardenburg and lord of Rixingen. He was the son of Count Frederick IV and his second wife Jeanne d'Aspremont, and half-brother of Frederick V.

By his first wife Agnes of Ochsenstein he fathered Fritzmann, who married the Rixingen heiress and founded the Rixingen line; his second wife Matilda of Salm bore him Count Emich VI.

戈特弗里德，德语作戈特弗里德一世·冯·莱宁根－哈登堡（约1304—1344），是莱宁根－哈登堡伯爵，兼领里克辛根。他是莱宁根伯爵腓特烈四世与第二任妻子让娜·达斯普勒蒙之子，也是腓特烈五世的同父异母兄弟。

他与第一任妻子阿格妮丝·冯·奥克森施泰因生子弗里茨曼，后者娶里克辛根女继承人，开创里克辛根支系；第二任妻子萨尔姆的玛蒂尔德为他生下埃米希六世。

en:
Aonghus Óg Mac Domhnaill, or Angus Og MacDonald, was chief of Clann Domhnaill and Lord of Islay, a younger son of Aonghus Mór. He first backed Edward I of England against John Balliol and rival Clann Dubhghaill, but after Robert the Bruce killed John Comyn in 1306 and claimed the Scottish crown, Clann Domhnaill appears to have switched its support to Robert, and members of the clan sheltered him.

The Bruce records him fighting at Bannockburn in 1314, and he received former Clann Dubhghaill lands. He may have died between 1314 and 1318.

Henry Lee recorded that he died in 1330 at Finlaggan and was buried on Iona. His son Eóin became the first Lord of the Isles.

安格斯·奥格·麦克唐纳是麦克唐纳家族首领、艾莱领主，安格斯·莫尔的幼子。他起初支持英格兰国王爱德华一世，对抗约翰·巴里奥和敌对的麦克杜格尔家族；1306年罗伯特·布鲁斯杀死约翰·科明并自立为苏格兰国王后，麦克唐纳家族似乎转而支持罗伯特，家族成员收留了他。

《布鲁斯》记载他参加了1314年的班诺克本战役；他获封原属麦克杜格尔家族的土地。他可能于1314年至1318年间去世。

亨利·李记载他1330年卒于芬拉根，葬在爱奥那岛。其子约翰成为第一代群岛之王。

John of Islay (Eoin mac Aonghais; died 1386), son of Aonghus Óg Mac Domhnaill, became Clan Donald chief and Lord of the Isles from 1336. Edward Balliol granted him lands, and David II confirmed his holdings in 1343. Through his wife Amie mac Ruari he inherited Garmoran, gaining most of the Hebrides.

He later married Margaret Stewart, the future Robert II's daughter, and divorced Amie, then submitted to David II in 1369 and died in 1386.

艾拉的约翰（盖尔语名作埃文·麦克·安格斯，1386年去世）是安格斯·奥格·麦克唐纳之子，后成为麦克唐纳氏族族长，1336年起自称“群岛领主”。爱德华·巴里奥封赐他领地，1343年大卫二世确认了这些领地。他凭妻子埃米·麦克·鲁阿里继承加莫兰，势力遍及赫布里底群岛大部。

后来他与后来的罗伯特二世之女玛格丽特·斯图亚特结婚并与埃米离婚，1369年向大卫二世臣服，1386年去世。

en:
Iain Ciar MacLeod (1330 – c. 1392), eldest son of Malcolm, was the fourth chief of Clan MacLeod. The Bannatyne manuscript calls him the most tyrannical MacLeod chief, feared by his own family; his wife, an Irish O'Neill chieftain's daughter, was said to be as cruel, burying two daughters alive in Dunvegan's dungeon.

Around 1392, after a Harris hunt, he was ambushed and struck by an arrow; he died at Rodel and was buried on Iona. His surviving son William Cleireach succeeded him.

伊恩·西亚尔·麦克劳德（1330—约1392）是马尔科姆的长子，是麦克劳德氏族第四代族长。《班纳蒂恩手稿》称他是所有麦克劳德族长中最暴虐的一位，家人都惧怕他；他的妻子是爱尔兰奥尼尔酋长之女，相传同样残忍，将两个女儿活埋在邓韦根的地牢里。

约1392年，他在哈里斯岛狩猎后遭伏击，中箭受伤，死于罗德尔，葬于爱奥那岛。存活的儿子威廉·克莱雷赫继任族长。

Malcolm MacLeod (Gille Caluim MacLeòid; 1296–1370), son of Tormod and grandson of Leod, was the third chief of Clan MacLeod from about 1320. Around 1343 he appears in a David II charter, among the first MacLeod chiefs recorded.

Tradition calls him its greatest hero: he slew a bull at Glenelg with a dirk and carried its horn to Dunvegan, where it became Sir Rory Mor's Horn. Known as Good Fat Malcolm, he died at Stornoway and was buried on Iona, succeeded by Iain Ciar.

马尔科姆·麦克劳德（盖尔语名作吉勒·卡卢姆·麦克劳伊德，1296—1370）是托蒙德之子、氏族始祖利奥德之孙，是麦克劳德氏族第三代族长，约于1320年继任。1343年前后，他的名字出现在大卫二世的特许状中，是最早见于记载的麦克劳德族长之一。

传说称他为全族最伟大的英雄：相传他凭一把匕首在格伦埃尔格杀死一头野牛，将牛角带回邓韦根，后来成为“罗里·莫尔爵士之角”。晚年得号“好心的胖卡勒姆”，最终在斯托诺韦去世，葬于爱奥那岛，族长之位由伊恩·西亚尔继承。

Thomas de Rossy (died 20 September 1348) was a Scottish churchman who became Bishop of the Isles, the medieval see covering the Hebrides and Mann. In 1331, while a canon of Dunkeld Cathedral, he was provided to the see by Pope John XXII and consecrated at the curia.

The Chronicles of Mann call him the first bishop to levy twenty shillings of visitation dues on the Manx churches and tithes from parish rectors on visiting herring fishermen. After an eighteen-year episcopate he was buried at Scone.

托马斯·德·罗西（1348年9月20日卒）是苏格兰教士，出任群岛主教，该主教区中世纪时辖赫布里底群岛与马恩岛。1331年，他身为邓凯尔德大教堂的法政牧师，被教宗约翰二十二世任命出掌该主教区，并在教廷祝圣。

《马恩编年史》称他是第一位向马恩岛各教堂征收20先令巡视费、并向堂区神甫就外来鲱鱼渔民征收什一税的主教。担任主教18年后，他安葬于斯昆。

en:
Adosinda was queen consort of Asturias during the reign of her husband Silo, 774–783. A daughter of Alfonso I and Ermesinda and granddaughter of Pelagius, after her brother Fruela I was killed in 768 she sheltered her young nephew Alfonso at San Julián de Samos monastery. She chose Silo, a wealthy landowner of Pravia, as her husband.

When Silo died without heirs in 783 she secured the boy's election as Alfonso II, but her half-brother Mauregatus seized power, and she was forced to take the veil at San Juan de Pravia in 783 or 785.

阿多辛达是阿斯图里亚斯王后，其夫希罗于774年至783年在位。她是阿方索一世与埃尔梅辛达之女、佩拉约的外孙女。768年其兄弗鲁埃拉一世遇弑后，她把年幼的侄子阿方索送往萨莫斯的圣胡利安修道院庇护。她亲自挑选普拉维亚的富有地主希罗为夫。

783年希罗无嗣而终，她促成侄子被拥立为阿方索二世，但她的异母兄毛雷加图斯篡夺王位，她被迫于783年或785年在普拉维亚的圣胡安修道院出家为修女。

Alfonso Fróilaz, called the Hunchback, briefly held the united throne of Asturias, Galicia and León in 925. The eldest son of Fruela II, he succeeded in July 925 but within the year was driven from León by his cousins Sancho, Alfonso IV and Ramiro II.

After Alfonso IV seized power in 926, Alfonso Fróilaz was recognised as king in the northeast, where a charter of 927 still bears his name. In 932 Ramiro II had him and his cousins blinded in a single day and confined them in León's Ruiforco monastery.

阿方索·弗鲁伊拉斯，人称“驼背”，曾在925年短暂领有阿斯图里亚斯、加利西亚和莱昂的统一王位。他是弗鲁埃拉二世的长子，925年7月继位，但不出一年就被堂兄弟桑乔、阿方索四世和拉米罗二世逐出莱昂。

926年阿方索四世掌权后，阿方索·弗鲁伊拉斯在东北部被承认为国王，927年的一份特许状仍用他的名义。932年，拉米罗二世下令在一天之内刺瞎他和其他堂兄弟，把他们囚禁在莱昂的鲁伊福尔科修道院。

en:
Alfonso I, called the Catholic (c. 693–757), was the third king of Asturias, reigning from 739. Son of Duke Peter of Cantabria, he married Ermesinda, daughter of Pelagius, and succeeded her brother Favila.

Exploiting the Berber Revolt of 740, he reconquered Galicia, took León in 754 and raided as far as La Rioja. Lugo and Tui, never occupied by Muslim forces, joined his domain. Frontier populations withdrew north under him, creating the depopulated Desert of the Duero as a buffer against Muslim armies.

He founded the shrine of Covadonga in memory of his father-in-law's victory there and died at Cangas in 757. His sons Fruela and Mauregatus both later became kings.

zh:
阿方索一世，绰号“天主教徒”（约693—757），是阿斯图里亚斯第三位国王，739年即位。他是坎塔布里亚公爵佩德罗之子，娶佩拉约之女埃尔梅辛达为妻，并在她的兄弟法维拉死后继位。

他趁740年柏柏尔人起义之机收复加利西亚，754年攻取莱昂，兵锋远达拉里奥哈。未被穆斯林占领的卢戈和图伊也归入他的领地。在他治下边境居民北撤，形成荒无人烟的“杜罗荒漠”，作为抵御穆斯林军队的缓冲地带。

他修建科瓦东加圣祠，纪念岳父在那里取得的胜利，757年死于坎加斯。他的儿子弗鲁埃拉和毛雷加图斯后来都成为国王。

en:
Alfonso II (c. 760–842), called the Chaste, was the son of Fruela I. After his father's murder in 768, he was elected king in 783, but magnates raised his uncle Mauregatus instead. Alfonso fled to his mother's relatives in Álava and became king in 791 after Bermudo I abdicated.

He made Oviedo his capital and built several churches. After Cordoban raids in 794 he sent embassies to Charlemagne, who recognized him, and his troops sacked Lisbon in 798.

In 814 the tomb of Saint James was found at Compostela and he became its first pilgrim. His victories of 825 opened the repopulation of Galicia and León. He died in 842 after a fifty-year reign.

zh:
阿方索二世（约760—842），绰号“纯洁者”，是弗鲁埃拉一世之子。768年父亲遇刺后，他于783年被推举为王，但贵族转而拥立他的叔父毛雷加托。阿方索逃往阿拉瓦投奔母族，791年贝尔穆多一世退位后他继承王位。

他定都奥维耶多，修建了多座教堂。794年科尔多瓦军队入侵后，他遣使觐见查理曼并获得承认，798年其军队洗劫里斯本。

814年，圣雅各的陵墓在孔波斯特拉被发现，他成为第一位前往该地的朝圣者。825年的胜利开启了对加利西亚和莱昂的再移民。他在位约半个世纪，于842年去世。

en:
Alfonso III, called the Great (c. 848–910), succeeded his father Ordoño I as king of Asturias in 866. He fled the usurper Fruela of Galicia, returning after his murder. He crushed a Basque revolt in 867 and around 869 allied with Pamplona, strengthening the bond by marrying Jimena.

Continuing his father's frontier resettlement, his counts took Porto in 868 and Coimbra in 878, advancing the frontier to the Mondego. In 878 he defeated Salid ibn Ghanim's army at Polvoraria and the Córdoban prince al-Mundir at Valdemora, forcing the first truce from Córdoba.

His sons rebelled in 909. He died at Zamora on 20 December 910, and the kingdom was divided among them.

阿方索三世，绰号“伟大者”（约848—910），866年继承父亲奥多尼奥一世的阿斯图里亚斯王位。即位之初他被加利西亚的篡位者弗鲁埃拉逼走，弗鲁埃拉被杀后才返回。867年他平定巴斯克人叛乱，约869年与潘普洛纳结盟，并娶希梅娜以巩固盟约。

他继续父亲的边境移民政策，手下的伯爵们于868年攻取波尔图、878年攻取科英布拉，把边境推到蒙德古河。878年，他在波尔沃拉里亚击败萨利德·伊本·加尼姆的军队，随后在巴尔德莫拉击败科尔多瓦王子蒙迪尔，迫使科尔多瓦首次求和。

909年他的儿子们起兵反叛。910年12月20日他在萨莫拉去世，王国被儿子们瓜分。

en:
Alfonso IV (c. 890s–933), called the Monk, was a son of Ordoño II of León. After Fruela II died in 925, Alfonso and his brothers, backed by Jimeno Garcés of Pamplona, drove Alfonso Fróilaz into eastern Asturias: Alfonso took León, his brother Sancho took Galicia, and on Sancho's death in 929 he reunited both kingdoms.

In 931 he abdicated in favour of his brother Ramiro II and entered a monastery. A year later, regretting his retirement, he rebelled with Fruela's sons, was captured and blinded, and died at Sahagún in August 933. His son by Onneca Sánchez was Ordoño IV.

阿方索四世（约890年代—933），人称“修道士”，是莱昂国王奥多尼奥二世之子。925年弗鲁埃拉二世死后，他与兄弟们在潘普洛纳的希梅诺·加尔塞斯支持下将阿方索·弗鲁伊拉斯赶至阿斯图里亚斯东部：阿方索取得莱昂，兄长桑乔取得加利西亚；929年桑乔去世，他重新统一两国。

931年他让位给弟弟拉米罗二世，进入修道院。次年他后悔退隐，联合弗鲁埃拉的儿子们起兵，战败后被刺瞎双眼，于933年8月死在萨哈贡。他与欧妮卡生有奥多尼奥四世。

en:
Alfonso IX (1171–1230) was the son of Ferdinand II of León and Urraca of Portugal, and ruled León from 1188. Faced with protests over taxes, he summoned the Cortes of León, an assembly of nobles, clergy and town delegates regarded as an early parliament with urban representation.

His marriages to Theresa of Portugal in 1191 and Berengaria of Castile in 1197 were both annulled for consanguinity, and the second brought an interdict. He also invaded Castile with Muslim troops and was excommunicated.

He founded the University of Salamanca in 1218 and captured Mérida and Badajoz in 1230, the year of his death. His son Ferdinand III inherited León and united it with Castile.

zh:
阿方索九世（1171—1230）是莱昂国王斐迪南二世与葡萄牙的乌拉卡之子，1188年起统治莱昂。面对民众对税收的抗议，他同年召开由贵族、教士和城市代表组成的莱昂议会，被视为早期包含城市代表的议会之一。

他1191年娶葡萄牙的特蕾莎、1197年娶卡斯蒂利亚的贝伦加利亚，两次婚姻均因血亲关系被废除，第二次还招致禁罚。他还联合穆斯林军队入侵卡斯蒂利亚，受到绝罚。

1218年他创办萨拉曼卡大学，1230年即他去世的当年攻占梅里达和巴达霍斯。其子斐迪南三世继承莱昂，将其与卡斯蒂利亚合并。

en:
Alfonso V (c. 994–1028), called the Noble, succeeded his father Bermudo II as king of León in 999, aged five. His mother Elvira García and Count Menendo González served as regents until Menendo's death in 1008.

In 1013 Alfonso married Menendo's daughter Elvira Menéndez and used the title emperor of all Spain. He rebuilt the kingdom after years of civil war and Muslim ravaging, and in 1017 granted León its first charters of privileges.

After Elvira's death he married Urraca of Pamplona. On 7 August 1028 he was killed by an arrow while besieging Viseu, and his son Bermudo III succeeded him.

zh:
阿方索五世（约994—1028），人称“高贵者”，999年父王贝尔穆多二世去世时年仅五岁，便继位为莱昂国王。母亲埃尔维拉·加西亚与梅嫩多·冈萨雷斯伯爵共同摄政，至1008年梅嫩多去世后亲政。

1013年阿方索迎娶梅嫩多之女埃尔维拉·曼德斯，并使用全西班牙皇帝的称号。经历多年内战与穆斯林蹂躏后，他着手重建王国，1017年向莱昂城颁布首批特权特许状。

埃尔维拉死后，他娶潘普洛纳的乌拉卡为妻。1028年8月7日，他在围攻维塞乌时中箭身亡，王位传给儿子贝尔穆多三世。

en:
Alfonso VI (c. 1040–1109), called the Brave, was the second son of Ferdinand I of León. Inheriting León in 1065, he fought his brothers Sancho II and García; Sancho's murder at Zamora in 1072 and García's long imprisonment left him ruler of León, Castile and Galicia.

His greatest triumph was the capture of Toledo in 1085, after which he styled himself emperor of Spain. The conquest provoked an Almoravid invasion, which he resisted for the rest of his reign.

But defeat at Uclés in 1108 cost him his heir Sancho. He died in 1109 and was succeeded by his daughter Urraca.

阿方索六世（约1040—1109），绰号“勇敢者”，是莱昂国王斐迪南一世的次子。1065年他继承莱昂，与兄弟桑乔二世、加西亚交战；1072年桑乔在萨莫拉城外遇刺，加西亚遭到长期囚禁，他由此成为莱昂、卡斯蒂利亚和加利西亚的统治者。

他最大的功业是1085年攻占托莱多，此后自称“全西班牙皇帝”。这一征服促使阿尔摩拉维王朝入侵，他在余下的统治岁月中不断抵御。

但1108年乌克莱斯战役的失败使他失去继承人桑乔。1109年他去世，女儿乌拉卡继位。

en:
Aurelius (c. 740–774) was King of Asturias from 768 until his death. The son of Fruela of Cantabria and nephew of Alfonso I, he was chosen king by the Asturian nobility after his cousin Fruela I was assassinated.

His quiet six-year reign saw him put down a rebellion of serfs, the first anti-seignorial revolt recorded in the Iberian Peninsula; he may have negotiated peace with the Muslim south through exchanged brides. He died of natural causes in 774 and was succeeded by his cousin-in-law Silo; contemporary chronicles do not mention a wife or children.

zh:
奥勒留（约740—774）于768年被推举为阿斯图里亚斯国王，在位直至去世。他是坎塔布里亚的弗罗伊拉之子、阿方索一世的侄子；堂兄弗鲁埃拉一世遇刺后，阿斯图里亚斯贵族将他选为国王。

他在位六年，政局平静，史载的主要事件是他镇压了一场农奴起义——这是伊比利亚半岛有记载的第一次反领主起义；他可能以交换新娘的习俗与南方的穆斯林议和。774年他自然死亡，由堂姐夫西罗继位；同时代编年史未提及他的妻子或子女。

en:
Bermudo I, called the Deacon (c. 750–797), was King of Asturias from 788 or 789 until 791. A son of Fruela of Cantabria and brother of King Aurelius, he was elected by the palace nobility after Mauregatus died, probably to bar Alfonso II's succession.

In 791 an Arab-Berber army invaded Álava and Galicia and defeated him at the Burbia River. Bermudo then abdicated and Alfonso II took the crown; the Chronicle of Alfonso III attributed his abdication to his status as a deacon. Remembered as merciful and pious, he left a son by an unnamed wife who later reigned as Ramiro I.

贝尔穆多一世，人称“助祭”（约750—797），于788或789年至791年任阿斯图里亚斯国王。他是坎塔布里亚的弗罗伊拉之子、国王奥勒留之弟，在马雷加托死后由宫廷贵族推举继位，此举很可能是为了阻止阿方索二世继位。

en:
Bermudo II (c. 950–999), called the Gouty, was a son of Ordoño III of León. In 982 Galician nobles proclaimed him king in revolt against Ramiro III, and he was crowned at Santiago de Compostela. After Ramiro's death in 985 he ruled all León.

Though he sought Córdoba's protection, Almanzor's armies came as conquerors; Bermudo expelled them in 987. A noble revolt drove him out in 991, but he was soon restored, and Almanzor later sacked León.

Gout-crippled, Bermudo travelled by litter in his last year. He died in September 999, and his son Alfonso V succeeded him.

zh:
贝尔穆多二世（约950—999），人称“痛风者”，是莱昂国王奥多尼奥三世之子。982年加利西亚贵族拥立他为王，反抗拉米罗三世，他在圣地亚哥-德孔波斯特拉加冕；985年拉米罗死后，他统治整个莱昂。

贝尔穆多因痛风致残，最后一年乘轿出行，于999年9月去世，其子阿方索五世继位。

en:
Bermudo III (c. 1015–1037), son of Alfonso V of León and Elvira Menéndez, became king of León as a child in 1028 and was the last ruler of the line of Peter of Cantabria.

In 1034 Sancho III of Pamplona drove him from his kingdom and he fled to Galicia. He recovered León, but on 4 September 1037 he was defeated and killed at the Battle of Tamarón fighting his brother-in-law Ferdinand of Castile, who then annexed the kingdom.

en:
Ermesinda (born c. 720 or 730, date of death unknown) was queen consort of Asturias as the wife of Alfonso I. She was a daughter of King Pelagius and Queen Gaudiosa and sister of King Favila.

When Favila was killed by a bear in 739, her husband Alfonso, son of Duke Peter of Cantabria, took the crown through her claim. Her children were Fruela I, Vimarano, whom Fruela had killed in 765, and Adosinda, who married King Silo.

en:
Favila or Fafila (died 739) was the second king of Asturias, succeeding his father Pelagius in 737. The only known act of his short reign was the founding of the Church of Santa Cruz in his capital of Cangas de Onís, where he was later buried.

In 739 he was mauled to death by a bear during a royal hunt, for which later Asturian chroniclers blamed his frivolity. He was buried beside his wife Froiluba and succeeded by his brother-in-law Alfonso I.

en:
Ferdinand I (c. 1015–1065), called the Great, was a younger son of Sancho III of Pamplona. Count of Castile from 1029, he married Sancha of León and in 1037 killed Bermudo III at Tamarón, taking the crown of León in 1038.

He had acknowledged the supremacy of his elder brother García of Navarre, but in 1054 defeated him at Atapuerca, where García was killed. Tradition holds that Ferdinand was crowned emperor of Spain in 1056.

He extracted tribute from the Muslim taifas and took Coimbra in 1064. He died in December 1065, leaving Castile, León and Galicia to his sons Sancho, Alfonso and García.

斐迪南一世（约1015—1065），绰号“伟大者”，是潘普洛纳的桑乔三世较年幼的儿子。他1029年成为卡斯蒂利亚伯爵，娶莱昂的桑查为妻，1037年在塔马龙击杀贝尔穆多三世，1038年取得莱昂王位。

他曾承认兄长纳瓦拉国王加西亚的宗主地位，却于1054年在阿塔普埃尔卡击败兄长，加西亚在战役中阵亡。相传斐迪南于1056年加冕为“西班牙皇帝”。

他向穆斯林泰法国索取贡金，1064年攻占科英布拉。1065年12月他去世，把卡斯蒂利亚、莱昂和加利西亚分别留给儿子桑乔、阿方索和加西亚。

en:
Ferdinand II (c. 1137–1188), born in Toledo, was a younger son of Alfonso VII of León and Castile. When his father died in 1157 the realm was divided and Ferdinand received León and Galicia.

He warred with Castile, first under his brother Sancho III and later under his nephew Alfonso VIII, while campaigning south against the Almohads, taking Alcántara in 1164 and Cáceres in 1169 after capturing Afonso I of Portugal at Badajoz.

In 1170 he founded the Order of Santiago to protect pilgrims to Compostela. He made peace with Castile in 1180, and on his death in 1188 his son Alfonso IX succeeded him.

斐迪南二世（约1137—1188）出生于托莱多，是莱昂与卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索七世较年幼的儿子。1157年父亲去世后王国被瓜分，他分得莱昂和加利西亚。

他先后与兄长桑乔三世、侄子阿方索八世治下的卡斯蒂利亚交战，同时南下进攻穆瓦希德王朝：1164年夺取阿尔坎塔拉，1169年在巴达霍斯俘虏葡萄牙国王阿方索一世后取得卡塞雷斯。

1170年他创立圣地亚哥骑士团，以保护前往孔波斯特拉的朝圣者。1180年他与卡斯蒂利亚议和，1188年去世，其子阿方索九世继位。

en:
Fruela of Cantabria, also called Fruela Pérez (c. 708–c. 756), was the second son of Duke Peter of Cantabria and a younger brother of King Alfonso I of Asturias. He fought alongside Alfonso in campaigns against the Muslim rulers of the Iberian Peninsula, helping to take Lugo, Tui, Porto and Braga in the northwest.

Although he never wore a crown himself, his sons Aurelius and Bermudo I both succeeded to the Asturian throne, and his daughter married Lope, a noble of Álava.

坎塔布里亚的弗罗伊拉，又称弗罗伊拉·佩雷斯（约708—约756），是坎塔布里亚公爵佩德罗的次子、阿斯图里亚斯国王阿方索一世之弟。据《阿方索三世编年史》记载，他随阿方索出征伊比利亚半岛的穆斯林统治者，参与攻占西北部的卢戈、图伊、波尔图和布拉加诸城。

他本人从未称王，但两个儿子奥勒留和贝尔穆多一世先后登上阿斯图里亚斯王位；他还有一个女儿嫁给了阿拉瓦贵族洛佩。

en:
Fruela I (c. 722–768), called the Cruel, was the eldest son of Alfonso I of Asturias and Ermesinda, Pelayo's daughter, and ruled from 757. He suppressed Basque and Galician revolts and defeated a Cordoban army. In 761 the church from which Oviedo grew was founded in his reign.

He murdered his popular brother Vimarano, earning his nickname, and was assassinated at Cangas de Onís in 768. His cousin Aurelius succeeded him, while his son Alfonso later ruled as Alfonso II.

弗鲁埃拉一世（约722—768），绰号“残忍者”，是阿斯图里亚斯国王阿方索一世与佩拉约之女埃尔梅辛达的长子，757年起统治。他镇压巴斯克和加利西亚的起义，击败一支科尔多瓦军队。761年，后来发展为奥维耶多城的教堂在他在位时建立。

他杀害深得人心的弟弟比梅拉诺，因而得到“残忍者”的绰号，768年本人在坎加斯德奥尼斯遇刺。堂弟奥雷利欧继位，他的儿子阿方索后来成为阿方索二世。

en:
Fruela II (c. 874–925), youngest son of Alfonso III of Asturias, received Asturias when his brothers deposed their father and divided the kingdom in 910. His diminished kingdom remained subordinate to León.

He consolidated the region later called Castile, while acknowledging the hegemony of his brother Ordoño II of León. When Ordoño died in 924 the magnates ignored his young sons and elected Fruela king of León.

He alienated the nobles by putting two noble brothers to death, and after only fourteen months died of leprosy in August 925. His death opened a succession war between his sons and Ordoño's.

弗鲁埃拉二世（约874—925）是阿斯图里亚斯国王阿方索三世的幼子。910年兄弟们废黜父王并瓜分王国，他得到阿斯图里亚斯，他缩小了的王国仍从属于莱昂。

他巩固了后来称为卡斯蒂利亚的地区，同时承认兄长莱昂国王奥多尼奥二世的宗主地位。924年奥多尼奥去世，权贵们撇开其年幼的儿子，推举弗鲁埃拉为莱昂国王。

他处死两名贵族兄弟，招致贵族怨恨；在位仅十四个月，便于925年8月死于麻风病。他死后，他的儿子与奥多尼奥的儿子之间爆发继承战争。

en:
García I (c. 871–914), eldest son of Alfonso III of Asturias and Queen Jimena, ruled León from 910 until his death. Implicated in a court conspiracy in 909, he saw Alfonso abdicate and divide the realm among his three sons: García received León, Ordoño Galicia and Fruela Asturias.

He fortified the line of the Duero and resettled Roa, Osma, Clunia and San Esteban de Gormaz. García died at Zamora in 914 without an heir, and León passed to his brother Ordoño II.

加西亚一世（约871—914）是阿斯图里亚斯的阿方索三世与王后希梅娜的长子，910年起统治莱昂，直到去世。909年他卷入一场宫廷阴谋，阿方索随后退位，把王国分给三个儿子：加西亚得到莱昂，奥多尼奥得到加利西亚，弗鲁埃拉得到阿斯图里亚斯。

他在杜罗河一线修筑防御，向罗阿、奥斯马、克鲁尼亚和圣埃斯特万-德戈马斯重新移民。914年加西亚在萨莫拉去世，未留下继承人，莱昂传给弟弟奥多尼奥二世。

en:
Mauregatus, known as the Usurper, was an illegitimate son of Alfonso I of Asturias, said to be born to a Moorish servant woman. When King Silo died in 783, the nobility elected the young Alfonso II.

Mauregatus seized the throne and drove Alfonso II into exile in Álava. Folk tradition links him with the legendary Tribute of the Hundred Maidens paid to the Moors. He ruled until his natural death in 789 and was buried at Pravia, where Bermudo I succeeded him.

en:
Ordoño I (c. 821–866), son of Ramiro I, was born in Oviedo and governed Galicia for his father before succeeding him in 850 as the first Asturian king to take the crown without election.

He put down a Basque rebellion backed by the Banu Qasi of Zaragoza. Against the warlord Musa ibn Musa he divided his forces, besieging Albelda while attacking Musa at Monte Laturce; Musa's army was routed and he himself barely escaped.

Ordoño repopulated León, Astorga and other ruined towns. He died of gout at Oviedo on 27 May 866, leaving the throne to his son Alfonso III.

奥多尼奥一世（约821—866）是拉米罗一世之子，生于奥维耶多，曾代父亲治理加利西亚，850年继位，是第一位未经选举便登基的阿斯图里亚斯君主。

他镇压了得到萨拉戈萨的巴努·卡西家族支持的巴斯克人叛乱。对阵军阀穆萨·伊本·穆萨时，他分兵围攻阿尔韦尔达，并在拉图尔塞山迎战；穆萨的大军被击溃，本人仅以身免。

en:
Ordoño II (c. 873–924), second son of Alfonso III of Asturias, was educated at the Banu Qasi court in Zaragoza. He received Galicia when his father's kingdom was divided among three brothers in 910. In 914, after his brother García died childless at Zamora, he inherited León and made the city his royal seat.

He sacked Mérida and Évora, forcing the Muslim governor to buy his retreat. Allied with Sancho I of Pamplona, he routed the Muslims at San Esteban de Gormaz in 917. In 920 the emir Abd-ar-Rahman III defeated him at Valdejunquera. Ordoño died at León in June 924.

en:
Ordoño III (c. 926–956), eldest son of Ramiro II, succeeded his father as king of León in 951. He sought to continue his father's work of fortifying royal authority against the separatist Castilian count Fernán González.

His throne was disputed by his half-brother Sancho the Fat, backed by Navarre and Fernán, and he also faced rebellions and Muslim attacks. In 955 he raided as far as Lisbon, forcing the caliph Abd al-Rahman III to conclude a peace treaty.

He married Fernán's daughter Urraca and later repudiated her. Ordoño died at Zamora in 956, leaving a son, the future king Bermudo II.

他娶费尔南之女乌拉卡为妻，后来又将她休弃。奥多尼奥于956年在萨莫拉去世，留下儿子、后来的国王贝尔穆多二世。

en:
Ordoño IV (c. 926–c. 963), called the Bad, was the son of Alfonso IV of León and Onneca Sánchez of Pamplona. In 958 nobles weary of the obese Sancho I rebelled and placed Ordoño on the throne with the backing of his father-in-law, Count Fernán González of Castile.

In 960 a Navarrese and Córdoban alliance restored Sancho, and Ordoño fled, abandoning his wife at Burgos and losing Fernán's support. He sought aid at the caliph's court in Córdoba, but died in exile around 963, still dethroned.

en:
Peter (died 730) was the Visigothic duke of Cantabria at the time of the Muslim conquest of Spain, said by the Chronicle of Alfonso III to descend from the Visigothic kings. When Musa ibn Nusair sacked Amaya in 714, he led his people into the northern mountains.

He backed Pelayo of Asturias's revolt and may have sent his son Alfonso to Pelayo's court after Covadonga. Alfonso married Pelayo's daughter Ermesinda, uniting Cantabria with Asturias, and later reigned as King Alfonso I. Peter was also father of Fruela of Cantabria.

en:
Pelagius (Pelayo, c. 685–737) was a nobleman in the Asturias, whom the chronicles call the son of the Galician duke Favila and an exile from Toledo under Wittiza. After the Arab conquest of 711 he led a northern rebellion.

Elected princeps by the Asturian magnates with his capital at Cangas de Onís, he founded the Kingdom of Asturias in 718. At Covadonga, c. 722, his small force defeated and killed the Muslim commander Alkama, later seen as opening the Reconquista. He died in 737 and was succeeded by his son Favila; his daughter Ermesinda married Alfonso I.

佩拉约（拉丁语作佩拉吉乌斯，约685—737）是阿斯图里亚斯的贵族。编年史称他是加利西亚公爵法维拉之子，曾被维提萨逐出托莱多。711年阿拉伯人征服伊比利亚后，他在北方山区率众起义。

en:
Ramiro I (c. 790–850), son of Bermudo I, became king of Asturias in 842 after Alfonso II died without children, having chosen Ramiro as his successor. While he was away marrying, the palace count Nepotian seized power; Ramiro raised an army in Galicia, defeated him at the Bridge of Cornellana and had him blinded and confined in a monastery.

In 844 he routed Vikings who landed at Corunna and burned much of their fleet. His resettlement of León failed when Córdoban forces burned the city in 846.

Near Oviedo he built Santa María del Naranco, a gem of pre-Romanesque ramirense architecture. He died on 1 February 850.

en:
Ramiro II (c. 900–951), son of Ordoño II of León, took the crown in 931 after his brother Alfonso IV abdicated. His marriage to Urraca Sánchez secured an alliance with Pamplona.

A commander whom the Moors called the Devil for his ferocity, he led a León–Pamplona coalition to a decisive victory over the caliph Abd al-Rahman III at Simancas in 939, then pushed the frontier from the Duero to the Tormes and repopulated the border strongholds.

In his final years he lost Pamplona's support, and Count Fernán González of Castile briefly gained de facto independence. He died on 1 January 951, leaving his sons Ordoño III and Sancho I.

en:
Ramiro III (c. 961–985), son of Sancho the Fat, succeeded his father as king of León in 966, aged five. His aunt, the nun Elvira Ramírez, first held the regency and used the title of queen, followed by his mother Teresa Ansúrez.

His regents confirmed peace with the Caliph al-Hakam II. Ramiro married Sancha Gómez and tried to impose absolute rule, alienating the Galician and Castilian nobility.

Repeated routs by Almanzor's armies, including at San Esteban de Gormaz, led the Galicians to proclaim Bermudo II king in 982. Ramiro lost León in 984 and died on 26 June 985.

en:
Sancha of León (c. 1018–1067), daughter of King Alfonso V, married Ferdinand I of Castile in 1032, after her betrothed García Sánchez was killed before the wedding. When Ferdinand slew her brother Bermudo III at Tamarón in 1037, Sancha's claim brought him the crown of León.

Mother of Sancho II, Alfonso VI and García II, she after Ferdinand's death in 1065 strove in vain to reconcile her warring sons. She died on 8 November 1067 and was buried at León's San Isidoro, to which she and Ferdinand gave the crucifix bearing their names.

莱昂的桑查（约1018—1067）是莱昂国王阿方索五世之女。1032年，她嫁给卡斯蒂利亚的斐迪南一世；此前她的未婚夫加西亚·桑切斯在婚礼前被杀。1037年，斐迪南在塔马隆战役杀死她的兄长贝尔穆多三世，凭借桑查的继承权戴上莱昂王冠。

她是桑乔二世、阿方索六世和加西亚二世的母亲，1065年丈夫死后曾徒劳地调解互相攻战的儿子们。1067年11月8日她去世，葬于莱昂的圣伊西多罗教堂；她与斐迪南曾向该教堂供奉以二人名字命名的十字架。

en:
Sancho I (c. 932–966), called the Fat, was the son of Ramiro II of León. He took the throne after Ordoño III died in 956, but in 958 Count Fernán González and the nobles deposed him for his gross obesity and raised up Ordoño IV.

Fleeing to his grandmother Toda of Pamplona, Sancho promised the caliph Abd al-Rahman III lands along the Duero. In Córdoba he received treatment from the court physician; a Muslim and Pamplonian army restored him to León in 960.

He soon abandoned his agreement with the caliph. In 966 he was poisoned, leaving his young son Ramiro III to succeed him.

桑乔一世（约932—966），人称“胖子”，是莱昂国王拉米罗二世之子。956年奥多尼奥三世死后他登上王位，但958年费尔南·冈萨雷斯伯爵率领贵族以他过度肥胖为由将他废黜，另立奥多尼奥四世。

桑乔投奔外祖母托达，并向哈里发阿卜杜勒-拉赫曼三世许诺杜罗河沿岸的土地。他在科尔多瓦接受宫廷医生的治疗；穆斯林与潘普洛纳联军于960年攻取莱昂，助他复位。

他不久便抛弃与哈里发的协议，于966年被毒杀，幼子拉米罗三世继位。

en:
Silo ruled the kingdom of Asturias from 774 until his death in 783, winning the crown through his marriage to Adosinda, daughter of Alfonso I. He moved his court from Cangas de Onís to Pravia, which lay closer to the centre of his kingdom.

His reign saw no major fighting with the Umayyads of Córdoba, but when Galicia rebelled he defeated the rebel army at the Battle of Montecubeiro.

The Diploma of King Silo of 775 is the oldest surviving medieval document from the Iberian Peninsula; in it he granted land to monks to found a monastery. He died at Pravia in 783.

en:
Theresa (c. 1080–1130) was the illegitimate daughter of Alfonso VI of León. In 1093 she married the French nobleman Henry of Burgundy, receiving the County of Portugal from her father in 1096.

Widowed in 1112, she defended Coimbra and in 1116 was recognized queen by Pope Paschal II. War with her half-sister Queen Urraca ended with her capture at Lanhoso in 1121 and accepting vassalage to León, though she retained her royal title. Portuguese nobles and clergy supported her son Afonso Henriques, who defeated her at São Mamede in 1128 and exiled her; she died in 1130.

en:
Urraca (c. 1081–1126), called the Reckless, was the daughter of Alfonso VI of León. Her half-brother Sancho's death in battle in 1108 left her the heir, and in 1109 she inherited León, Castile and Galicia, western Europe's first queen regnant.

Widowed by Raymond of Burgundy, she married Alfonso I of Aragon late in 1109. His abuse drove her away by 1110, and the marriage was annulled in 1112. War with Aragon and rebel Galicia followed. She died at Saldaña in 1126, and her son Alfonso VII succeeded her.

en:
Diederik of Heinsberg (1300–1361), lord of Heinsberg, was the son of Matilda, Arnold V of Loon's daughter. When his uncle Louis IV died childless in 1336, he claimed Loon and Chiny.

An 1190 pact promised Loon to Liège, but his brother-in-law Prince-Bishop Adolph of La Marck secured him the counties and a later bishop lifted the threat of excommunication. He ruled until his death at Stokkem in 1361, which opened the War of the Loon Succession.

en:
Adalbert (c. 1000–1048) was the eldest son of Gerhard, Count of Metz. When Godfrey of Upper Lorraine rebelled against Emperor Henry III and was defeated, the emperor installed Adalbert as duke of Upper Lorraine in 1047.

Godfrey continued the war, however, and on 11 November 1048 Adalbert was killed fighting him at the Battle of Thuin. He left no son, and Henry III at once named his brother Gerhard duke in his stead.

en:
Elisabeth of Austria (c. 1285–1352), known in Lorraine as Isabelle, was a daughter of King Albert I of Germany and sister of Frederick the Fair. A proposed French marriage was cancelled, and in 1307 she married Frederick IV of Lorraine, which put the duchy behind her brother's claim to the empire.

At Mühldorf in 1322 her husband was captured fighting for Frederick, and the French king secured his release. Widowed in 1328, she became regent of Lorraine for her young son Rudolph.

The regency ended when Rudolph married Eleanor of Bar and power passed to Eleanor's father. Of her six children only Rudolph and Margaret grew up. She died at Nancy on 19 May 1352 and was buried at Königsfelden.

en:
Frederick I, called Ferry (c. 1143–1206), was the second son of Matthias I and Judith of Swabia. Favoured by his mother for the succession, he received Bitche from his elder brother Simon II in 1176, but revolted against him.

After three years of war, the Treaty of Ribemont in 1179 gave him the German-speaking northern half of Lorraine, while Simon kept the south.

When Simon abdicated to a monastery in 1205, Frederick inherited the whole duchy, but ruled barely a year before dying in 1206. His son Frederick II, by Ludmilla of Poland, succeeded him.

en:
Frederick II (c. 1165–1213), son of Frederick I and Ludmilla of Poland, reunited Lorraine in 1205–1206, when his uncle Simon II abdicated and his father died, ending the division made at Ribemont in 1179.

His 1188 marriage to Agnes of Bar brought him several fiefs, but he joined the bishop of Metz against her father, Count Theobald I. The count seized Prény and Frederick was captured in 1208.

In the German succession he switched backing from Philip of Swabia to Otto IV and then Frederick of Hohenstaufen. In 1213 he defeated an Alsatian lord and died on 10 October.

en:
Frederick III, called Ferry (1240–1303), only son of Matthias II and Catherine of Limburg, inherited Lorraine in 1251 aged eleven; his mother held the regency until 1255. That year he married Margaret of Champagne, daughter of King Theobald I of Navarre, tightening the duchy's ties to France. In the disputed royal election of 1257 he backed Alfonso X of Castile against Richard of Cornwall.

His quarrels with the bishops of Metz brought excommunication from Pope Clement IV in 1267 and an interdict on the duchy. He died on 31 December 1303 and was succeeded by his son Theobald.

Frederick IV, called the Fighter (1282–1328), succeeded his father Theobald II as Duke of Lorraine in 1312. Married to Elisabeth, daughter of Emperor Albert I, he backed his brother-in-law, the Habsburg claimant Frederick the Handsome, against Louis of Bavaria after the disputed election of 1314.

He fought beside Frederick at Mühldorf in 1322, where both were captured; the king of France secured his release in exchange for Lorraine's neutrality. He campaigned in Aquitaine in 1324 and in the War of Metz in 1325–1326, and was killed fighting for Philip VI at the Battle of Cassel in 1328.

en:
Gerard of Alsace (c. 1030–1070), the second son of the count of Metz, received Metz in 1047 when his elder brother Adalbert became Duke of Upper Lorraine under Emperor Henry III. After Adalbert fell fighting the deposed duke Godfrey III the next year, Henry invested Gerard with Lorraine.

Rebels imprisoned him, but Bishop Bruno of Toul, later Pope Leo IX, freed him in 1049. Gerard remained loyal to the imperial dynasty.

In 1053 he fought at the disastrous Battle of Civitate against the Normans. He founded the castle of Prény, the seed of Nancy, and died in 1070 suppressing a revolt.

en:
Marie de Châtillon (1323–1363) was Duchess of Lorraine by her marriage to Duke Rudolph the Valiant. She was the daughter of the Count of Blois and a niece of King Philip VI of France.

When Rudolph was killed at the Battle of Crécy in 1346, their young son John I inherited the duchy, and Marie served as regent until 1354, ruling jointly with the Count of Württemberg. In that year the king dispensed John from his minority, ending the regency.

en:
Matthias I (c. 1119–1176), eldest son of Simon I, ruled Upper Lorraine from 1138, when he married Judith, sister of Frederick Barbarossa, binding his house to the Hohenstaufen.

Like his forefathers he supported the German emperors, accompanying Barbarossa to his coronation in Rome in 1155 and serving in his wars against the papacy and neighbouring kings. He enlarged the ducal demesne at the expense of the bishop of Toul while founding churches and abbeys, and died in 1176.

en:
Matthias II (c. 1193–1251), son of Frederick II and Agnes of Bar, succeeded his brother Theobald I in 1220. He first yielded Nancy to his brother's widow, but it reverted to the duchy at her death in 1225.

He restored the alliance with the emperors, joining Frederick II on the Sixth Crusade in 1228 and helping crush his son Henry's revolt in 1235.

War with the Count of Bar, who had ravaged his lands in 1230, ended in peace in 1245, and in 1247 he joined the papal party against Frederick. He died on 9 February 1251, leaving a son who became Frederick III.

en:
Rudolph, called the Valiant (1320–1346), became Duke of Lorraine as a boy in 1328, under the regency of his Habsburg mother Elisabeth of Austria until 1334. He grew into a warrior prince who fought in four wars, in Lorraine, France, Brittany and Iberia.

In 1337 Count Henry IV of Bar refused homage for several lordships; Rudolph ravaged the Barrois until Philip VI intervened. Lorraine's ties to France grew stronger under him, and his second wife, Marie of Blois, was the king's niece.

In 1340 he joined Alfonso XI of Castile against the Moors of Granada and distinguished himself at the Battle of Gibraltar. He later backed his brother-in-law Charles of Brittany, and was killed beside Philip VI at Crécy in 1346, leaving the duchy to his infant son John I.

1340年，他投奔卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索十一世，攻打格拉纳达的摩尔人，在直布罗陀战役中表现出众。他后来援助妻兄布列塔尼的查理，1346年在克雷西与腓力六世并肩作战时阵亡，年幼的儿子约翰一世继承了公国。

en:
Simon I (1076–1139) ruled Upper Lorraine from 1115, succeeding his father Theodoric II. Through his mother he was a half-brother of Emperor Lothair III, and he continued the dynasty's alliance with the emperors, accompanying Henry V to the Diet of Worms in 1122 that settled the Investiture Controversy.

He clashed with the bishop of Metz and the archbishop of Trier, allies of the count of Bar. The archbishop excommunicated him until Pope Innocent II lifted the sentence.

A friend of Bernard of Clairvaux, he founded abbeys including Sturzelbronn in 1135, and was buried there. He was succeeded by his son Matthias.

en:
Simon II (1140–1207) succeeded his father Matthias I as Duke of Upper Lorraine in 1176. His mother favoured his younger brother Frederick, so Simon had an assembly of nobles confirm him and concede feudal privileges, creating the Estates of Lorraine.

Frederick, granted Bitche as an appanage, still revolted; after three years the Treaty of Ribemont split the duchy, leaving Simon the French-speaking south and Frederick the German-speaking north.

His marriage to Ida was childless, and he named his nephew Frederick his heir, although his brother ultimately succeeded him. He abdicated to a monastery in 1205 and died on 4 January 1207.

en:
Theobald I (c. 1191–1220), son of Frederick II and Agnes of Bar, ruled Lorraine from 1213. He stood by Emperor Otto IV and was captured at Bouvines in 1214, but soon released.

From 1216 he backed Erard of Brienne's claim to Champagne; Emperor Frederick II and the armies of Champagne, Burgundy and Bar invaded, burned Nancy and besieged him at Amance, where he surrendered by treaty in 1218 and gave up his support. He died in 1220 amid rumours of poison, and being childless was succeeded by his brother Matthias II.

en:
Theobald II (1263–1312) succeeded his father Frederick III as Duke of Lorraine in 1303. In 1298 he fought for Albert of Habsburg at Göllheim against King Adolf of Germany.

Allied with Philip IV of France, he and his son Frederick fought at the Battle of the Golden Spurs in 1302, where the Flemings defeated the French knights. He served in the later campaigns and joined the negotiations that made peace with Flanders.

In 1305 he attended the coronation of Pope Clement V at Lyon and collected the papal tenth despite resistance from the bishop of Metz. His son Frederick IV, by Isabelle de Rumigny, succeeded him.

en:
Theodoric II the Valiant (died 1115) succeeded his father Gerard as Duke of Upper Lorraine in 1070. A rival claimant contested the succession, but Theodoric won election by the nobles, granted the County of Vaudémont to his brother to bind his family, and was confirmed by Emperor Henry IV.

The duke remained loyal to the emperors, campaigning against the Saxons between 1070 and 1078 and opposing the reforming popes.

In 1095 he took the cross for the First Crusade but withdrew through ill health, sending his vassals east instead. Afterward he took little part in imperial affairs, and he died on 30 December 1115.

Adelaide of Waldeck (c. 1264 – c. 1339–1342) was a daughter of Henry III, Count of Waldeck, and Matilda of Arnsberg-Cuyk. On 24 November 1276 she married Simon I, Lord of Lippe, and bore him at least eleven children.

Her sons included Bernard, bishop of Paderborn from 1321, and Otto and Bernard V, who divided Lippe between them on Simon's death in 1344 and ruled at Lemgo and Rheda.

en:
Bernard IV (c. 1230–June 1275) was Lord of Lippe, eldest son of Bernard III and Sophie of Cuijck-Arnsberg. In 1254 he took charge of Rheda and in 1265 succeeded his father in Lippe, while his brother Herman III received Lippstadt.

In 1267 he and his uncle Simon I, bishop of Paderborn, fought the Duchy of Jülich at Zülpich, where Simon was captured; Bernard ransomed him in 1269, saddling his house with debt. He was buried at Marienfeld Abbey, leaving a son, Simon I, by Agnes of Cleves.

Otto ruled his share as Lord of Lippe-Lemgo until his death, residing in Lemgo. He married Irmgard, and their son Simon III was born about 1340.

Simon I, Lord of Lippe (c. 1261–1344), ruled Lippe from 1275, succeeding his father Bernard IV. In 1302 a coalition of bishops and nobles with Herford city took Enger Castle and held him eighteen months in Osnabrück, releasing him only on condition he raze it.

In 1323 he acquired Varenholz Castle, and under him Lippe reached its greatest extent. Married to Adelaide of Waldeck, he died in 1344, and his sons Otto and Bernard V divided the lordship between Lemgo and Rheda.

Jean de Rossillon, a cleric from the pays de Gex, served Savoy's count from 1297 as judge of the Chablais-Genevois bailliage. After becoming a Lausanne canon, he was elected bishop there in 1323 with Pope John XXII's confirmation.

As prince-bishop he fought the sons of Aymon III de Montagny, secured episcopal rights at Avenches in 1339, and in the Laupen war sided with Fribourg against Bern. He probably died on 15 April 1341 and was buried in Lausanne Cathedral.

en:
Othon de Champvent (died 19 April 1312) was prince-bishop of Lausanne from 1309. He came from the Champvent lords, a cadet branch of Grandson southwest of Lake Neuchâtel, and was a son of Henri of Champvent and brother of Bishop Guillaume. His cousin Othon I of Grandson helped his career, notably at Henry III's English court, where he appears to have been from 1259; he held prebends in England and France.

Already an old man, he was raised to the see by Pope Clement V in 1309, and in 1311 renewed his church's truce with Louis II of Savoy, baron of Vaud.

Pierre d'Oron (died 27 March 1323) was prince-bishop of Lausanne from 1313. Born to a Valais ministerial family serving the abbots of Saint-Maurice-d'Agaune, son of Vevey's co-lord, he was treasurer of Lausanne when a revolt broke out during the episcopal vacancy of 1313.

Pope Clement V appointed him bishop in 1313 after he helped restore order, and he created the office of episcopal bailli. In 1316 he fought Louis II of Vaud, who seized Gourze and Villarzel, before accepting Count Amadeus V of Savoy's mediation and protection.

皮埃尔·德·奥龙（1323年3月27日卒）自1313年起任洛桑采邑主教。他出身瓦莱、世代为圣莫里斯达戈讷修道院院长效劳的侍臣家族，是沃韦共领领主之子；1313年主教空缺、洛桑爆发叛乱时他正担任教会司库。

en:
Castracane di Ruggero di Castracane was a Lucchese merchant-banker of the Castracani degli Antelminelli and grandfather of Castruccio Castracani. With his brother Lutterio he inherited, shortly after mid-century, a fortune that included rural estates. His family lived in the Curtis Sancti Martini by the cathedral and participated in Lucca's iron and silver mining.

In his time the firm financed Lucchese spice merchants bound for North Africa in 1270 and grew into one of the great Lucchese banking houses. His son was Gerio, father of Castruccio.

卡斯特拉卡内·迪·鲁杰罗·迪·卡斯特拉卡内是卢卡商人银行家，属卡斯特拉卡尼·德利·安泰尔米内利家族，为卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼的祖父。13世纪中叶过后不久，他与兄弟卢泰里奥共同继承一笔家产，其中包括乡间地产。他的家族住在大教堂旁的圣马丁坊，并参与卢卡的铁银矿开采。

en:
Castruccio Castracani degli Antelminelli (1281–1328) was a Ghibelline condottiero and lord of Lucca. Exiled by the Black Guelphs in 1300, he soldiered in France and Lombardy before serving Uguccione della Faggiuola of Pisa, helping to take Lucca in 1314 and win the Battle of Montecatini in 1315.

Uguccione imprisoned him, but an uprising in Lucca expelled his master and freed him. Chosen lifelong lord of Lucca in 1316, he defeated the Florentines at Altopascio in 1325.

Emperor Louis the Bavarian made him duke of Lucca and neighbouring lands, and he seized Pisa in 1327. He died in 1328.

卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼·德利·安泰尔米内利（1281—1328）是吉伯林派的雇佣兵首领、卢卡之主。1300年他被圭尔夫派黑党放逐，曾在法国和伦巴第从军，随后效力于比萨之主乌古乔内·德拉·法焦拉，参与1314年夺取卢卡，并在1315年的蒙特卡蒂尼战役中取胜。

乌古乔内囚禁了他，但卢卡的起义驱逐了乌古乔内，使他重获自由。1316年他被选为卢卡终身统治者，1325年在阿尔托帕肖击败佛罗伦萨人。

皇帝巴伐利亚人路德维希封他为卢卡及周边之地的公爵，1327年他攻占比萨。他于1328年去世。

en:
Gerio, also called Ruggero, di Castracane degli Antelminelli was a Lucchese merchant-banker and father of Castruccio Castracani. His firm traded across France, Flanders and England, and in 1296 it still carried a large debt to the Ricciardi company; that year his son Castruccio was emancipated from him.

After the murder of the Guelph Obizo degli Obizi in 1300, the Castracani were outlawed. Gerio took refuge in Ancona on business and died there in 1301.

en:
Lucrezia Borgia (1480–1519) was the illegitimate daughter of Rodrigo Borgia, later Pope Alexander VI. Given a humanist education, she could read Latin and Greek.

In 1493 her father married her to Giovanni Sforza of Pesaro, a marriage annulled in 1497. Her second husband, Alfonso of Aragon, was murdered in 1500, reputedly on her brother Cesare's orders. In 1499 she had been appointed governor of Spoleto, the Papal States' first female governor.

Her third marriage, to Alfonso I d'Este, took her to Ferrara, where she ran the duchy twice as regent, patronized the poet Ariosto, and died after childbirth in 1519.

卢克雷齐娅·波吉亚（1480—1519）是罗德里戈·波吉亚（后来的教宗亚历山大六世）的私生女。她受过人文主义教育，能读拉丁语和希腊语。

1493年父亲将她嫁给佩萨罗的乔瓦尼·斯福尔扎，这桩婚姻于1497年被宣告无效。第二任丈夫阿拉贡的阿方索于1500年遇害，据传是她的兄长切萨雷下令所为。1499年她被任命为斯波莱托总督，是教皇国第一位女性总督。

第三任丈夫阿方索一世·德斯特将她带到费拉拉，她在那里两度担任摄政主政，赞助诗人阿里奥斯托，1519年因产后并发症去世。

en:
Lukeni lua Nsanze was a princess of Mbata, the daughter of its ruler Nsaku Lau. Around 1375, when Mbata forged an alliance with Nimi a Nzima, ruler of neighbouring Mpemba Kasi, she was given to him in marriage, and Kongo tradition presents this wedding as the founding act of the Kingdom of Kongo.

Her son Lukeni lua Nimi, born around 1380, took his given name from her. He led the conquests that built the kingdom and became its first king; the rulers who followed belonged to his Kilukeni lineage, which held power until 1567.

en:
Elisabeth of Brunswick-Lüneburg (c. 1330 – 17 April 1384) was the daughter of William II, Prince of Lüneburg, by his first wife Hedwig of Ravensberg. She married Duke Otto of Saxe-Wittenberg, who died in 1350.

Their son Albert was William's chosen heir to Lüneburg, a claim that helped trigger the Lüneburg War of Succession after 1369. Around 1354 she married Count Nicholas of Holstein-Rendsburg, to whom she bore a daughter, also named Elisabeth.

不伦瑞克-吕讷堡的伊丽莎白（约1330—1384年4月17日）是吕讷堡亲王威廉二世与第一任妻子拉文斯贝格的黑德维希之女。她先嫁萨克森-维滕堡公爵奥托，奥托于1350年去世。

二人的儿子阿尔布雷希特被威廉选为吕讷堡继承人，这一继承权在1369年后引发了吕讷堡继承战争。约1354年，她改嫁荷尔斯泰因-伦茨堡伯爵尼库劳斯，生下女儿伊丽莎白。

en:
Henry the Lion (1129/1131–1195), son of Henry the Proud, recovered Saxony in 1142. He helped his cousin Frederick Barbarossa win the German throne in 1152 and was restored to Bavaria in 1156.

He founded Munich in 1157 and Lübeck in 1159, and in 1166 erected the bronze lion before Dankwarderode Castle in Brunswick. In 1168 he married Matilda, daughter of Henry II of England.

After he refused troops for Barbarossa's Italian war, he was stripped of both duchies in 1180 and spent years exiled in England. He died at Brunswick in 1195, leaving sons including Emperor Otto IV.

zh:
狮子亨利（1129或1131—1195）是骄傲者亨利之子，1142年收复萨克森。他于1152年帮助表亲腓特烈一世夺得德意志王位，1156年重新得到巴伐利亚。

他于1157年建立慕尼黑、1159年建立吕贝克，1166年在不伦瑞克的丹克瓦德罗德城堡前竖起铜狮像。1168年他娶英格兰国王亨利二世之女玛蒂尔达。

他拒绝为腓特烈一世的意大利战争出兵后，于1180年被剥夺两个公国，长年流亡英格兰。他于1195年在不伦瑞克去世，留下的儿子中有皇帝奥托四世。

en:
John (c. 1242–1277) of the House of Welf ruled Brunswick-Lüneburg with his brother Albert after their father Otto the Child died in 1252. The brothers partitioned the duchy in 1267–1269: John took the northern estates around Lüneburg and Hanover, founding the Old Line of Lüneburg.

In a feud with Count Gunzelin of Schwerin he won Uelzen and granted it privileges in 1270. He failed to control the Lüneburg saltworks, then gave the citizens a salt-trade monopoly along the Old Salt Route to Lübeck. His son by Liutgard of Holstein succeeded him as Otto II the Strict, under his uncles' guardianship until 1282.

zh:
约翰（约1242—1277）出身韦尔夫家族，1252年父亲“孩童”奥托去世后，与兄长阿尔布雷希特共同统治不伦瑞克-吕讷堡。1267至1269年兄弟瓜分公国：约翰取得吕讷堡和汉诺威一带的北部领地，开创吕讷堡长系。

在与什未林伯爵贡策林的争斗中，他夺得于尔岑，并于1270年授予其城市特权。他试图控制吕讷堡盐场却未能成功，随后把沿古盐道通往吕贝克的盐业垄断权交给市民。他与荷尔斯泰因的柳特加德所生之子继位，即奥托二世（严厉者），由叔伯监护至1282年。

en:
Matilda of Mecklenburg (1293–1358), daughter of Henry II and Beatrix of Brandenburg, was the wife of Otto III, who ruled Lüneburg jointly with his brother William from 1330.

Her only son Otto drowned as a child in the Ilmenau near Emmendorf, so when Otto III died on 19 August 1352 he left no male heir and the principality passed to his brother. Her daughter Matilda (d. 1357) married Count Otto II of Waldeck; her other daughter Elisabeth died in 1386.

en:
Matilda of Bavaria (1275 – 28 March 1319) was a Wittelsbach princess, daughter of Duke Louis II of Upper Bavaria and Matilda of Habsburg. Her brother Louis IV was elected King of the Romans in 1314 and later became Holy Roman Emperor.

She married Duke Otto II of Brunswick-Lüneburg and bore him eight children, including Otto III and William II, both princes of Lüneburg, and Louis, bishop of Minden. She died in 1319 and was buried beside her husband in St. Michael's Abbey at Lüneburg.

zh:
巴伐利亚的玛蒂尔达（1275—1319年3月28日）是维特尔斯巴赫家族的公主，上巴伐利亚公爵路德维希二世与哈布斯堡的玛蒂尔达之女。她的弟弟路德维希四世于1314年当选罗马人的国王，后来成为神圣罗马皇帝。

en:
Otto II the Strict (c. 1266–1330) of the House of Welf was Prince of Lüneburg from 1277, ruling under his uncles' guardianship until 1282. His reign was filled with feuds over border and property disputes, financed by pledging estates; he curbed knightly rights and kept the peace.

He granted town rights to Dahlenburg in 1289 and Celle in 1292 and bought the County of Wölpe in 1302. After a disputed royal election, he allied with Louis of Bavaria, who granted him an imperial fief in 1315, and that year Otto issued a law of succession for his sons Otto and William. He died in 1330.

奥托二世（严厉者，约1266—1330）出身韦尔夫家族，1277年起任吕讷堡亲王，因年幼由叔伯摄政至1282年。他的统治充斥着围绕边界与产业的仇争，靠抵押领地筹措费用；他限制骑士权利、维持地方和平。

en:
Otto III (c. 1296–1352) of the House of Welf, the second son of Otto the Strict and Matilda of Bavaria, was Prince of Lüneburg from 1330. In 1315 his father arranged the succession of Otto and his brother William II, and from 1330 the brothers ruled the undivided land together.

They enlarged their estates around Gifhorn and backed the growing towns, making the Ilmenau navigable between Lüneburg and Uelzen, so that Lüneburg's trade flourished.

The Ilmenau also took Otto's only son, who drowned in it as a child. When Otto died in 1352 he left no male heir, leaving William to face the succession question that ended in war after William's death.

en:
William II (c. 1300–1369) of the House of Welf ruled Lüneburg from 1330 with his brother Otto III; together they expanded the estates around Gifhorn and made the Ilmenau navigable to Uelzen. After Otto died without a male heir in 1352, the succession became the problem of William's life.

He promoted his grandson Albert of Saxe-Wittenberg as heir, then changed his mind, fearing Albert's uncles' influence. In 1355 he married his younger daughter to her Brunswick cousin Ludwig, a match meant to reunite the Welf lands.

Emperor Charles IV, however, treated Lüneburg as an imperial fief falling vacant at William's death and had already enfeoffed Albert and his uncles, laying the groundwork for the Lüneburg War of Succession. Shortly before his death at Lüneburg in November 1369, William handed rule to Magnus of Brunswick.

en:
William of Winchester (1184–1213) was the youngest son of Duke Henry the Lion of Saxony and Matilda of England, born in Winchester during his father's exile. He probably grew up at his uncle King Richard I's court, and in 1194 he and his brother Otto were surrendered as hostages to secure Richard's ransom.

At the 1202 partition of the Welf lands he received Lüneburg and made it his residence, fostering its salt trade. Earlier that year he married Helena, sister of Canute VI of Denmark. Their only son, Otto the Child, became the first Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg in 1235.

en:
Henry V the Blond (1216–1281) inherited Arlon from his father Waleran III in 1226 and Luxembourg from his mother Ermesinde in 1247. His 1240 marriage to Margaret of Bar brought him Ligny, though a feud with Theobald of Bar over its suzerainty led to his capture in 1266 and release in 1268.

He seized Namur in 1256 while Margrave Baldwin II was in Constantinople; Baldwin sold his rights to Guy of Dampierre, who retook Namur. Henry joined Edward of England on the Ninth Crusade and returned after a truce with the Mamluks. He died in 1281; his sons fell at Worringen in 1288.

en:
Henry VI (c. 1240–1288) was Count of Luxembourg and Arlon, titles he inherited from his father Henry V the Blond. He took charge of government while his father accompanied Louis IX of France on crusade, and succeeded as count in 1281. He joined the Limburg succession war and was killed at the Battle of Worringen on 5 June 1288 by a knight of John I of Brabant.

Around 1261 he married Beatrice d'Avesnes; their sons Henry VII, later Holy Roman Emperor, and Baldwin, Archbishop of Trier, secured the rise of the House of Luxembourg.

en:
Henry VII (1278/79–1313), son of Count Henry VI of Luxembourg and Beatrice d'Avesnes, grew up at the French court and ruled Luxembourg from 1288. After King Albert I was murdered in 1308, his brother Baldwin, Archbishop of Trier, won over the electors, and Henry was elected King of the Romans on 27 November 1308 and crowned at Aachen in 1309.

He crossed the Alps in 1310 to revive imperial authority in Italy. He married his son John to Elizabeth of Bohemia, winning Bohemia's crown for his dynasty, and was crowned emperor in Rome on 29 June 1312, the first since Frederick II. He died at Buonconvento on 24 August 1313.

en:
Margaret of Brabant (1276–1311), daughter of Duke John I of Brabant, married Count Henry VII of Luxembourg in 1292. When Henry was elected King of the Romans in 1308 she became queen.

Her children included John the Blind, king of Bohemia and father of Emperor Charles IV, and daughters Maria and Beatrix, who married the kings of France and Hungary. She joined Henry's Italian campaign and fell ill at Brescia, then died at Genoa, where Henry commissioned Giovanni Pisano to carve her monument.

en:
Margaret of Courtenay (1194–1270) was the daughter of Peter II of Courtenay, Latin Emperor of Constantinople. In 1217 she married Henry I, Count of Vianden. When her brother Henry II died in 1229, she seized Namur and defended it against Ferrand of Flanders until 1232.

She ruled the margraviate until 1237, when her brother Baldwin II reclaimed it and she withdrew to Vianden. Widowed in 1252, she became a nun at Marienthal, dying on 17 July 1270. Her children included Philip, Count of Vianden, and Henry, bishop of Utrecht.

Margaret of Bar (c. 1225–1275) was the eldest daughter of Count Henry II of Bar. In 1240 she married Count Henry V of Luxembourg, bringing Ligny-en-Barrois as her dowry.

en:
Jalaluddin Ahsan Khan (died 1339), originally named Hasan Kaithali, was the first sultan of the Madurai Sultanate. In 1335 he declared Ma'bar independent of Delhi.

When Muhammad bin Tughluq sent an army against him, Ahsan Khan defeated it; the sultan of Delhi retaliated by executing Ahsan Khan's son Ibrahim, his imperial purse-bearer. The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta was his son-in-law. After about four years' rule Ahsan Khan was murdered by one of his nobles in 1339.

en:
Otto of Hesse (1301 – 30 April 1361) was Archbishop of Magdeburg from 1327 until his death. A son of Landgrave Otto I of Hesse and grandson of Saint Elizabeth of Thuringia, he was designated for the see by Pope John XXII.

He reconciled Magdeburg, under the imperial ban after citizens murdered his predecessor Burchard III in 1325, and in 1333 received the city's homage. He settled border disputes with Brandenburg and withstood a revolt of the nobility, dying at Wolmirstedt in 1361.

黑森的奥托（1301—1361年4月30日）1327年起任马格德堡大主教，直至去世。他是黑森伯爵奥托一世之子、图林根的圣伊丽莎白之孙，由教皇约翰二十二世选定出任该职。

1325年马格德堡市民杀害前任大主教布尔夏德三世，城市被处帝国禁令，奥托促成解除禁令，于1333年接受城市宣誓效忠。他还解决了与勃兰登堡的边界争端，顶住贵族叛乱，1361年卒于沃尔米施泰特。

en:
Mahmud Ghazan (1271–1304) was the seventh Ilkhan of Persia, who made Islam the Mongol court's faith in Iran and reformed its finances. Raised a Christian and taught by a Buddhist monk, from 1284 he governed Khorasan for his father Arghun against the Chagatai Mongols. After Baydu seized the throne in 1295, Ghazan became a Sunni Muslim on 16 June in exchange for Nawruz's army and had Baydu executed in October. He put Nawruz to death in 1297.

He made Rashid al-Din his vizier and had him write the Jami al-Tawarikh, a universal history. He defeated the Mamluks at Wadi al-Khazandar in 1299, taking Damascus. In January 1300 Ibn Taymiyya told him a self-declared Muslim had broken his promise by invading.

His April 1303 defeat at Marj al-Saffar ended major Mongolian invasions of Syria. He died near Qazvin in May 1304 with no son; his brother Öljaitü succeeded.

马哈茂德·合赞（1271—1304）是伊儿汗国第七代君主，他使伊斯兰教成为伊朗蒙古宫廷的信仰，并整顿财政。他自幼是基督徒，受教于佛教僧人，1284年起替父亲阿鲁浑镇守呼罗珊，抵御察合台蒙古人。1295年拜都夺位后，合赞于6月16日皈依逊尼派伊斯兰教，以此换取捏吾鲁兹出兵，10月将拜都处死。1297年他将捏吾鲁兹处死。

他任命拉施特为宰相，命他撰写通史《史集》。他1299年在瓦迪哈赞达尔击败马木留克人并占大马士革。1300年1月，伊本·泰米叶对他说，自称穆斯林的人却入侵他国，背弃了诺言。

1303年4月他在迈尔季萨法尔惨败，蒙古人攻叙利亚至此终结。1304年5月他卒于加兹温附近，无子，弟完者都继位。

en:
Henry III of Virneburg (c. 1295 – 21 December 1353) was Archbishop and Elector of Mainz. A son of Count Rupert II of Virneburg, he secured the see through Pope John XXII in 1328, although the chapter had elected Baldwin of Luxembourg and Henry was only accepted in 1336.

He backed Emperor Louis IV of Bavaria against the Curia. Deposed by Pope Clement VI in 1346 in favour of Gerlach of Nassau, he nevertheless kept his position in Mainz until his death in 1353.

维尔讷堡的亨利三世（约1295—1353年12月21日）是美因茨大主教兼选帝侯。他是维尔讷堡伯爵鲁普雷希特二世之子，靠教皇约翰二十二世于1328年得到美因茨大主教之位；但座堂议会另选了卢森堡的鲍德温，亨利直到1336年才被普遍接受。

en:
Conrad of Wittelsbach (c. 1120/1125–1200) was Archbishop of Mainz and a cardinal caught in the struggle between emperor and pope. The son of Count Otto IV of Wittelsbach, he was appointed archbishop by Frederick Barbarossa in 1161. Refusing to back the antipope Paschal III, he broke with the emperor in 1165 and fled to Rome, where Pope Alexander III made him a cardinal.

The 1177 Treaty of Venice gave him Salzburg, but in 1183 he returned to Mainz, rebuilt its walls and cathedral, and hosted the Pentecost feast of 1184.

He joined the 1197 crusade as papal legate, and in 1200 secured an armistice between the Hohenstaufen and Welf factions, dying later that year.

康拉德·冯·维特尔斯巴赫（约1120/1125—1200）是美因茨大主教和枢机主教，身处皇帝与教宗的争斗之中。他是维特尔斯巴赫伯爵奥托四世之子，1161年由腓特烈一世任命为大主教。他拒绝支持对立教宗帕斯加尔三世，于1165年与皇帝决裂、逃到罗马，教宗亚历山大三世将他立为枢机主教。

1177年的《威尼斯条约》把萨尔茨堡划给他；1183年他回到美因茨，重建城墙与主教座堂，并在1184年主持了五旬节庆典。

1197年他以教宗使节身份参加十字军。1200年，他促成霍亨斯陶芬派与韦尔夫派休战，同年去世。

Anusapati, also called Anushanatha, was the second king of Singhasari in East Java, ruling from 1227 to 1248. The Pararaton makes him the son of Ken Dedes and Tunggul Ametung of Tumapel, raised as Ken Arok's stepson after his father's murder.

In 1227 he avenged Tunggul Ametung by killing Ken Arok with the same cursed kris that Mpu Gandring had forged for the murder. He ruled for two decades until 1248, when his half-brother Panji Tohjaya killed him with that same blade.

阿努沙帕蒂，又名阿努沙纳塔，是东爪哇信诃沙里的第二任国王，1227年至1248年在位。《国王之书》记载，他是肯·蒂德丝与杜马佩尔首领通古尔·阿梅通之子，生父被杀后成为肯·阿罗克的继子。

Cakradhara, later titled Kertawardhana, Bhre Tumapel, was a Javanese nobleman and prince consort of Majapahit. After King Jayanegara died in 1328 he won the marriage contest and took Dyah Tya, who ruled as Queen Tribhuwana Wijayatunggadewi, as his wife.

As prince of Tumapel he ruled the old Singhasari heartland. The Nagarakretagama praises the couple as devout Buddhists and likens him to the dhyani Buddha Ratnasambhava. Their son, born in 1334, became King Hayam Wuruk, and their daughter Dyah Nertaja became princess of Pajang.

查克拉达拉后称克尔塔瓦尔达纳、封号图马佩尔亲王，是爪哇贵族、满者伯夷王夫。1328年国王查雅纳迦拉死后，他在择婿比试中获胜，娶了后来以特里布婆那·毗阇耶顿迦提毗之名执政的迪雅·特亚为妻。

作为图马佩尔亲王，他统治旧信诃沙里的核心地区。《爪哇史颂》称赞二人为虔诚的佛教徒，并把他比作五方佛中的宝生佛。他们的儿子生于1334年，即后来的哈亚·乌鲁克国王；女儿迪雅·涅尔塔贾成为帕章公主。

en:
Dara Petak, later called Indreswari, was a princess of the Malay kingdom of Dharmasraya in Sumatra, daughter of King Tribhuwanaraja. In 1275 Singhasari ruler Kertanegara sent the Pamalayu expedition to Sumatra; when it returned in 1293 it brought Dara Petak and her elder sister to Java.

Intended for the late Kertanegara, she married his heir Raden Wijaya, founder of Majapahit, becoming his only non-Javanese consort. Their son Jayanegara succeeded as the second Majapahit king in 1309. Her Malay name means white dove.

达拉·佩塔，后称因德雷斯瓦里，是苏门答腊马来王国达摩室利耶的公主，国王特里布瓦纳拉贾之女。1275年，信诃沙里君主克塔纳伽拉派帕马拉尤远征军出征苏门答腊；1293年回师的军队将达拉·佩塔与其姐带回爪哇。

en:
Gajah Mada (c. 1290–c. 1364), also called Jirnnodhara, was the general and chief minister who made Majapahit the dominant power in the Javanese world. He rose after helping King Jayanegara crush the Ra Kuti rebellion, and in 1334 Queen Tribhuwana made him mahapatih. He swore the Palapa Oath: he would take no rest or pleasure until he had united the Nusantara archipelago.

His rival Ra Kembar mocked the oath, and their quarrel ended in a queen-sanctioned duel in which Ra Kembar died. Decades of campaigns brought Majapahit to its peak under Hayam Wuruk.

After the Bubat massacre of 1357, officials blamed him for meaning to demand Sunda's submission. He died in obscurity in 1364; Hayam Wuruk, judging he held too much power, split his duties among four new ministers.

加查·马达（约1290—约1364），又名吉尔诺达拉，是使满者伯夷成为爪哇世界霸主的名将与首相。他因协助查雅纳迦拉王平定拉·库提叛乱而平步青云，1334年特里布瓦纳女王任命他为玛哈帕蒂。他立下帕拉帕誓言：在统一努山塔拉群岛之前绝不休憩享乐。

对手拉·肯巴尔出言嘲笑这一誓言，争执以一场经女王认可的决斗收场，拉·肯巴尔死于其中。此后数十年的征战，使满者伯夷在哈奄·武禄时期臻于鼎盛。

1357年布巴特惨案之后，朝臣因他原打算迫使巽他称臣而归咎于他。他于1364年默默去世；哈奄·武禄认为他权力过大，便把他的职权分给四位新任大臣。

en:
Gayatri Rajapatni (c. 1276–1350), youngest daughter of Kertanegara, last king of Singhasari, became chief queen of Kertarajasa, founder of Majapahit. When Kediri overran Singhasari in 1292 she escaped disguised as a servant, and after Wijaya founded Majapahit in 1293 she became his favourite consort, bearing two daughters.

She may have supported the rise of Gajah Mada before retiring as a Buddhist nun. After Jayanegara's death in 1328 she had Tribhuwana enthroned in 1329, and died in 1350, later portrayed as the bodhisattva Prajnaparamita.

en:
Hayam Wuruk (1334–1389), regnal name Rajasanagara, was the fourth ruler of Majapahit, under whom the Javanese empire reached its greatest power. Prapanca recorded his birth in the year Mount Kelud erupted, read as a sign that Shiva had taken human form. Raised by his mother Queen Tribhuwana, he came to the throne in 1350 at sixteen, and with Gajah Mada extended Majapahit's sway across the Nusantara archipelago.

In 1357 his planned marriage to Dyah Pitaloka, daughter of the Sundanese king, ended in the Bubat massacre, in which the princess and her party died; court officials blamed Gajah Mada, who had meant to demand Sunda's submission.

In 1365 Prapanca composed the Nagarakretagama in his praise. He sent embassies to China from 1370 to 1381 and died in 1389, after which a succession quarrel between Wikramawardhana and Wirabhumi pulled the empire into decline.

哈奄·武禄（1334—1389），王号罗阇沙纳加拉，是满者伯夷第四位君主，在他治下这个爪哇帝国臻于极盛。帕拉潘查记载，他出生那年克卢德火山喷发，被看作湿婆降世为人的征兆。他由母亲特里布瓦纳女王一手栽培，1350年年方十六岁即位，与加查·马达合力将满者伯夷的势力扩展到努山塔拉群岛。

1357年，他与巽他国王之女迪亚·皮塔洛卡的婚事以布巴特惨案收场，公主及随行者尽数遇难；朝臣归咎于加查·马达，因为他原打算迫使巽他称臣。

1365年，帕拉潘查撰成《爪哇史颂》称颂他。1370年至1381年间他多次遣使中国，1389年去世。此后维克拉马瓦尔达纳与维拉布米争夺继承权，帝国由盛转衰。

en:
Jayanegara (1294–1328) was the second emperor of Majapahit and the only son of its founder Raden Wijaya, succeeding in 1309. His troubled reign was shaken by barons' revolts: in 1319 Kuti seized the palace, forcing him to flee until Gajah Mada crushed the rebellion.

The chronicle Pararaton brands him a dissolute ruler, Kala Gemet, who desired his officers' wives and his own half-sisters. In 1328 his physician Tanca murdered him during an operation, and childless he was succeeded by his half-sister Tribhuwana.

查雅纳迦拉（1294—1328）是满者伯夷第二任君主、开国者罗登·韦查耶的独子，1309年继位。他在位时政局动荡，1319年库蒂攻占王宫，他被迫出逃，靠加查·马达平定叛乱才得以复位。

爪哇编年史《爪哇诸王志》给他“加拉·格梅特”的恶号，称他觊觎臣下的妻子乃至自己的异母妹妹。1328年他在一次手术中被御医坦察杀害，因无子嗣，王位由异母妹妹特里布瓦纳继承。

en:
Ken Arok, or Ken Angrok, titled Rajasa (died c. 1227), founded the East Javanese kingdom of Singhasari and the Rajasa dynasty. The Pararaton gives him humble beginnings: abandoned as an infant and raised by a thief, he became a notorious thief in Kediri.

The rishi Mpu Lohgawe reformed him and declared him an avatar of Vishnu. Serving Tunggul Ametung of Tumapel, he desired his master's wife Ken Dedes, whom Lohgawe said would bear a royal dynasty. He murdered Tunggul with the kris of Mpu Gandring, seized Ken Dedes, and built a kingdom centered on Singhasari.

To legitimize his rise, he claimed descent from Shiva. Around 1227 his stepson Anusapati killed him with the same cursed blade.

肯·阿罗克（一译肯·昂罗克），王号罗阇沙（约1227年卒），是东爪哇信诃沙里王国和罗阇沙王朝的建立者。《国王之书》记载，他出身贫寒，幼时被遗弃、由盗贼抚养，长大后在谏义里为盗、声名狼藉。

仙人姆普·洛加韦点化他改邪归正，并宣布他是毗湿奴的化身。他在杜马佩尔首领通古尔·阿梅通麾下效力时，爱上主人的妻子肯·蒂德丝——洛加韦预言她将孕育一个王朝。他用姆普·甘德灵铸造的格里斯剑刺杀通古尔，夺娶肯·蒂德丝，建立起以信诃沙里为中心的王国。

为使登位名正言顺，他自称湿婆的后裔。约1227年，继子阿努沙帕蒂用同一把受诅咒的剑将他杀死。

en:
The Pararaton portrays Ken Dedes as the daughter of the Buddhist monk Mpu Purwa, a woman famed across Java for her beauty. Tunggul Ametung, ruler of Tumapel, seized her as his wife while her father was away, and Mpu Purwa cursed him.

Ken Arok murdered Tunggul Ametung, took Ken Dedes as his queen and founded the kingdom of Singhasari in 1222. She was later revered as the ancestress of the Rajasa dynasty, which ruled Java from Singhasari into the Majapahit era.

据《国王之书》记载，肯·蒂德丝是佛教僧侣姆普·普尔瓦之女，美貌传遍爪哇。杜马佩尔的统治者通古尔·阿梅通趁她父亲外出修行时将她强娶为妻，普尔瓦为此诅咒他。

后来肯·阿罗克刺杀通古尔·阿梅通，于1222年建立信诃沙里王国，立她为后。她被后世尊为罗阇沙王朝的女始祖，该王朝从信诃沙里时代起直至满者伯夷时代统治爪哇。

en:
Kertanegara, also called Sivabuddha (died 1292), was the last king of Singhasari, ruling East Java from 1268; his father Wisnuwardhana had enthroned him in 1254. He was the first Javanese ruler to expand beyond Java: Bali submitted in 1284, and Madura and parts of Borneo acknowledged him.

When Kublai Khan's envoys demanded tribute in 1289, he had them branded, mutilated and expelled. In 1290 he sent his army to Sumatra, and in 1292, with it abroad, the rebel Jayakatwang stormed the palace and killed him, clearing the way for Raden Wijaya's Majapahit.

克塔纳伽拉，又名湿婆佛陀（1292年卒），是信诃沙里末代国王，1268年起统治东爪哇；其父毗湿奴伐弹那1254年便将他立为国王。他是第一位把势力扩张到爪哇岛以外的爪哇统治者：1284年巴厘臣服，马都拉和婆罗洲部分地区也向他归附。

1289年忽必烈遣使要求朝贡，他下令将使者烙印、施以残刑后驱逐出境。1290年他派军队远征苏门答腊；1292年大军在外，叛将贾亚卡旺攻占宫殿将他杀死，为罗登·韦查耶建立满者伯夷铺平了道路。

en:
Kudamerta, later known as Wijayarajasa, Bhre Wengker, was a noble of the Majapahit court in Java. After King Jayanegara died in 1328 he won a contest to marry the royal princesses and wed Dyah Wiyat, known as Rajadewi, younger sister of Queen Tribhuwana. A daughter of his by a concubine became the chief queen of Hayam Wuruk.

After Rajadewi died in the 1370s he proclaimed himself king at Pamotan as Bhatara Parameswara, heading the breakaway Eastern Court, and died in 1388. The Surawana temple was built around 1390 as his funerary monument.

库达梅尔塔，后称威查亚拉贾萨、温克尔王公，是爪哇满者伯夷宫廷的贵族。1328年国王查雅纳迦拉死后，他在择婿比试中胜出，迎娶女王特里布婆那的幼妹迪亚·维雅特，即拉贾德维。他与妾室所生的一个女儿后来成为哈亚·乌鲁克的王后。

1370年代拉贾德维去世后，他在帕莫坦自立为王，号称巴塔拉·巴拉梅斯瓦拉，统领分裂的东廷，最终于1388年去世。约1390年建成的苏拉瓦纳神庙便是他的陵庙。

en:
Dyah Lembu Tal, also called Sri Harsawijaya or Mahisa Tal, was a Javanese knight of the Singhasari kingdom, described in the Nagarakretagama as a ksatria yudha, or warrior noble. He was the son of Mahisa Campaka and a descendant of Ken Arok, founder of Singhasari, through Ken Dedes.

He is chiefly remembered as the father of Raden Wijaya, who in 1293 drove out Kublai Khan's Mongol expedition and founded the Majapahit kingdom.

en:
Mahisa Campaka, also called Narajaya and titled Bhatara Narasinghamurti (c. 1230–1269), was a Singhasari prince of the Rajasa line, the son of Mahisa Wong Ateleng. The Pararaton makes him the companion of Rangga Wuni, the future Wisnuwardhana: backed by the army of Tumapel, the two overthrew the usurper Panji Tohjaya in 1250.

The Nagarakretagama describes Narasinghamurti as supreme commander, or Ratu Anggabhaya, of Singhasari and ruler of seven islands beyond Java, and names him the father of Lembu Tal and grandfather of Raden Wijaya, the founder of Majapahit.

马希萨·占帕卡，又名纳拉查亚，称号巴塔拉·纳拉辛哈穆尔蒂（约1230—1269），是罗阇沙世系的信诃沙里王子，马希萨·翁·阿特伦之子。《国王之书》把他写成朗加·武尼——即后来的毗湿奴伐弹那——的伙伴：在杜马佩尔军队支持下，二人于1250年推翻篡位者潘吉·托查亚。

en:
Mahisa Wong Ateleng, also styled Sri Bhatara Parameswara, was a Javanese prince of the Rajasa dynasty, born to Ken Arok and Ken Dedes, the founder and first queen of Singhasari.

The Pararaton records him ruling Kediri under Tumapel's overlordship after Singhasari's foundation in 1222, and gives his wife as Ken Rimbi, daughter of Ken Umang. The Nagarakretagama traces the later Majapahit kings to his line; his recorded son was Mahisa Campaka.

马希萨·翁·阿特伦，又号室利·巴塔拉·帕拉梅斯瓦拉，是罗阇沙王朝的爪哇王子，为信诃沙里开国君主肯·阿罗克与第一位王后肯·蒂德丝所生。

《国王之书》记载，1222年信诃沙里建国之后，他在杜马佩尔的宗主权下统治谏义里，并娶肯·乌芒之女肯·伦比为妻。《爪哇史颂》把后来的满者伯夷诸王追溯为他的后裔；他见于记载的儿子是马希萨·占帕卡。

en:
Mpu Prapanca was a 14th-century Buddhist monk and poet at the Majapahit court in Java. In 1365 he composed the Nagarakretagama in Old Javanese as a eulogy to King Hayam Wuruk.

The epic portrays Majapahit at the height of its power, describing its capital, temples and vassal lands across the archipelago, and remains the chief source for the empire's history. He reportedly described himself as a former head of the kingdom's Buddhist clergy, a dharmadhyaksa kasogatan.

普拉班扎是14世纪爪哇满者伯夷宫廷的佛教僧侣兼诗人。1365年，他以古爪哇语写成《纳加拉克尔塔加玛》，作为对国王哈奄·武禄的颂词。

这部史诗描绘了鼎盛时期的满者伯夷，记述其都城、庙宇与横跨群岛的藩属，是研究该帝国历史的首要文献。相传他自称曾任王国佛教僧团首脑达玛迪亚克沙·卡索加坦。

en:
Raden Wijaya was the Javanese prince who founded the Majapahit kingdom and ruled it from 1293 until his death in 1309. When Kublai Khan's Mongol army landed in 1292 to avenge an insult by the dead Singhasari king Kertanegara, Wijaya enlisted it against Jayakatwang of Kediri, who had overthrown Singhasari.

After Jayakatwang fell in 1293, he turned on the Mongols and drove them from Java, then took the throne. To secure his claim, he married Kertanegara's daughters, including Gayatri Rajapatni, rewarded his ally Aria Wiraraja with Madura, and appointed Nambi prime minister. His son Jayanegara succeeded him.

zh:
罗登·韦查耶是爪哇王公，满者伯夷王国的创立者，1293年至1309年在位。1292年，忽必烈的元朝军队登陆，要为已死的信诃沙里国王克塔纳伽拉羞辱蒙古使臣一事复仇；韦查耶借元军之力攻打推翻信诃沙里的谏义里统治者贾亚卡特望。

1293年贾亚卡特望败亡后，他转而攻击元军，将其逐出爪哇，随后登基。为巩固法统，他娶了克塔纳伽拉的女儿们，其中包括加亚特里·拉贾帕特尼；他把马都拉赐给盟友阿里亚·维拉拉贾，又任命南比为首相。死后由其子查雅纳迦拉继位。

en:
Rajadewi, birth name Dyah Wiyat and titled Bhre Daha, was the younger daughter of Majapahit founder Kertarajasa and his chief queen Gayatri Rajapatni, and younger sister of Queen Tribhuwana. Her half-brother King Jayanegara wanted the two sisters as wives and confined them in the palace for years.

After Jayanegara's murder in 1328 a marriage contest was held, and Rajadewi wed the nobleman Kudamerta, later Wijayarajasa, Bhre Wengker. She died in the 1370s, after which her husband set up the breakaway Eastern Court at Pamotan.

拉贾德维，原名迪亚·维雅特，封号达哈公主，是满者伯夷开国君主格尔达拉查沙与王后加亚特里·拉贾帕特尼的幼女，特里布婆那女王之妹。她的异母兄长查雅纳迦拉国王欲纳她与姐姐为妃，将二人长年幽禁于深宫。

1328年查雅纳迦拉遇刺后，宫中举行择婿比试，拉贾德维嫁给贵族库达梅尔塔，即后来的温克尔王公威查亚拉贾萨。她于1370年代去世，此后丈夫便在帕莫坦建立起割据的东廷。

en:
Rangga Wuni, known by his reign name Wisnuwardhana (died 1270 or 1272), was the son of King Anusapati and, from 1248, king of Tumapel, the heart of Singhasari in East Java. He and his companion Mahisa Campaka, also called Narasinghamurti, overthrew the usurper Panji Tohjaya, and the two governed together as king and chief minister.

To secure the succession he had his young son Kertanegara enthroned in 1254. Wisnuwardhana ruled until 1268 and died at Singhasari in 1270 or 1272.

朗加·武尼以王号毗湿奴伐弹那闻名（1270或1272年卒），是阿努沙帕蒂王之子，1248年起统治东爪哇的杜马佩尔，即信诃沙里的核心之地。他与伙伴马希萨·占帕卡（又名纳拉辛哈穆尔蒂）合力推翻篡位者潘吉·托查亚，此后二人以国王与首相的身份共同治国。

为确保继承无虞，他在1254年立幼子克塔纳伽拉为王。毗湿奴伐弹那在位至1268年，1270或1272年于信诃沙里去世。

en:
Tribhuwana Wijayatunggadewi, born Dyah Tya, was the third monarch and first queen regnant of Majapahit, ruling from 1329 to 1350. Eldest daughter of the founder Raden Wijaya and Gayatri Rajapatni, she was shut away for years in the women's quarter by her half-brother Jayanegara, who wanted her as consort. After he was murdered in 1328, her mother, by then in a convent, placed her on the throne.

In 1331 she led the army herself against the rebellions of Sadeng and Keta. In 1334 she appointed Gajah Mada as Mahapatih; he swore the Palapa oath to carry Majapahit's power across the archipelago. Majapahit conquered Bali in 1343 and subdued Sumatra in 1347.

She ruled under Gayatri's auspices, so when Gayatri died in 1350 she gave the throne to her son Hayam Wuruk, and went on sitting in the council of royal elders.

特里布瓦纳·毗阇耶顿迦提毗（本名迪亚·特亚）是满者伯夷第三位君主、第一位执政女王，1329年至1350年在位。她是开国君主罗登·韦查耶与加亚特里·拉贾帕特尼的长女；异母兄长查雅纳迦拉想纳她为妃，把她在内宅关了多年。他于1328年遇刺后，已入庵修行的母亲让她登上王位。

1331年，她亲自率军平定萨登与克塔叛乱。1334年她任命加查·马达为玛哈帕蒂，他立下帕拉帕誓言，要把满者伯夷的势力推向整个群岛。满者伯夷于1343年征服巴厘，1347年平定苏门答腊。

她是在加亚特里庇护下执政，因此1350年加亚特里去世时，她把王位让给儿子哈奄·武禄，自己仍留在王室长老会议中。

en:
Al-Amir Abi Abdallah Kanz ad-Daula appears in modern Nubian king lists as a Muslim king of Makuria in 1333. The only document behind the name is a 1333 marriage contract, which records Kanz al-Dawla Abu Abd Allah Muhammad marrying his paternal cousin Bashariyya and styles him sovereign of Dongola, although the Christian king Siti still ruled the city that year.

Recent scholarship concludes that the contract names the long-reigning Kanz ad-Dawla Muhammad himself, still asserting his claim to Dongola after losing it, rather than a separate successor; nothing else is recorded of a ruler by this name.

阿米尔·阿比·阿卜杜拉·坎兹·道拉见于近人整理的努比亚国王列表，被列为1333年马库里亚的穆斯林国王。这个名字唯一的文献依据是一份1333年的婚书，记载坎兹·道拉·阿布·阿卜杜拉·穆罕默德娶堂妹巴沙里耶，并冠以栋古拉之主的头衔，而基督教国王西蒂当年仍统治该城。

en:
Saba Nol, called Weluda Ityopya in the Ge'ez Life of Ewostatewos, was a Christian king of Noba, the Nubian land south of the Fifth Nile Cataract, remembered only through Ethiopian hagiography.

Around 1337 he received the exiled Ethiopian monk Ewostatewos while facing a great revolt, and the hagiography credits the saint's prayers with his victory over the rebels. The gloss explaining his Arabic name as Ge'ez for son of Ethiopia may be a copyist's invention, and modern scholars suggest he could be a memory of the Makurian king Siti.

zh:
萨巴·诺尔是诺巴的基督教国王（诺巴位于尼罗河第五瀑布以南的努比亚地区），吉兹语《埃沃斯塔特沃斯行传》称他为韦卢达·伊特约皮亚，关于他的记载仅见于这部埃塞俄比亚圣徒传记。

约1337年，他在遭遇大规模叛乱时接待了流亡的埃塞俄比亚修士埃沃斯塔特沃斯，行传把他对叛军的胜利归功于圣徒的祈祷。传记把他的阿拉伯语名字解释为吉兹语的“埃塞俄比亚之子”，这一说法可能是抄经士的附会；现代学者推测，他可能是对马库里亚国王西蒂的一种追忆。

en:
Siti was a Christian king of the Nubian kingdom of Makuria, also called Dotawo, who ruled from about 1331 to at least December 1333. He is known only from Old Nubian documents and inscriptions that name him as king.

He appears to have seized power from the Muslim ruler Kanz ad-Dawla Muhammad, who had taken Dongola in the 1310s and regained power after a temporary overthrow, and restored Makuria as a Christian kingdom.

西蒂是努比亚基督教王国马库里亚（又称多塔沃）的国王，约1331年至1333年12月以后在位。他只在古努比亚语的文书与铭文中留下记载，这些材料称他为国王。

他似乎从穆斯林统治者坎兹·道拉·穆罕默德手中夺取了权力——后者于1310年代占据栋古拉，曾被暂时推翻，随后复位——并使马库里亚恢复为基督教王国。

en:
Mande Bori, also called Abu Bakr in Arabic, was a hero of Mande oral tradition and the brother and right-hand man of Sundiata Keita. He was raised by Sogolon Condé, shared the family's exile, and fought in the wars against the Sosso, including the Battle of Kirina in 1235.

After Sundiata founded the Mali Empire, he held the office of kankoro-sigui, or viceroy. He never reigned himself, but his grandsons Mansa Musa and Mansa Suleyman later ruled Mali.

zh:
曼德·博里，阿拉伯语名作阿布·伯克尔，是曼丁戈口述传统中的英雄，松迪亚塔·凯塔的兄弟与得力副手。他由索戈隆·孔德抚养，随家族一同流亡，并参加了对索索人的战争，包括1235年的基里纳战役。

松迪亚塔建立马里帝国后，他出任康科罗-西吉，即副王。他本人从未称曼萨，但孙辈曼萨·穆萨与曼萨·苏莱曼后来相继统治马里。

en:
Abu Ishaq al-Sahili, also called al-Tuwayjin (c. 1290–1346), was an Andalusi poet and legal scholar from Granada who became the most celebrated foreign scholar at the court of Mansa Musa of Mali. He left al-Andalus around 1321 and met Musa during the pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324, then returned with him to Mali.

He directed construction of an audience chamber in the capital, paid for in gold, and settled in Timbuktu. He died there on 15 October 1346; Ibn Battuta saw his tomb in the city in 1353.

阿布·伊沙克·萨希利，又称图韦金（约1290—1346），是格拉纳达出身的安达卢斯诗人兼教法学者，后成为马里曼萨·穆萨宫廷中最负盛名的外来学者。约1321年他离开安达卢斯，1324年在麦加朝觐时结识曼萨·穆萨，随后随他前往马里。

他主持修建了都城的觐见厅，获赐重金，后定居廷巴克图。1346年10月15日他在廷巴克图去世，伊本·白图泰1353年造访该城时曾见到他的坟墓。

en:
Abu Bakr, called Bata Mande Bori, was the fifth mansa of the Mali Empire, reigning after the tyrant Khalifa was overthrown around 1275. He was the son of a daughter of Sundiata Keita, making him the first mansa to succeed through the female line.

He was succeeded by Sakura, an enslaved court official who seized power in a coup. He is often confused with his namesake Abu Bakr, Sundiata's brother and the ancestor of Mansa Musa.

en:
Khalifa was the fourth mansa of the Mali Empire, known only from Ibn Khaldun's Kitāb al-ʻIbar. The chronicler makes him a son of Sundiata Keita, ruling late in the thirteenth century after his brothers Mansa Wali and Wati.

He describes Khalifa as insane and devoted to archery, shooting his subjects for sport, until they rose and killed him. The throne then passed to Abu Bakr, a grandson of Sundiata, and his brief reign is placed around 1273–1275.

哈利法是马里帝国第四位曼萨，生平仅见于伊本·赫勒敦的《教训书》。据这位史家记载，他是松迪亚塔·凯塔之子，于13世纪末在兄长曼萨·瓦利和瓦蒂之后即位。

en:
Maghan I (1280s–1341) was the tenth mansa of Mali and the eldest son of Kankan Musa I, better known as Mansa Musa. When Musa left on his pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324, Maghan was left in nominal charge of the empire. He took the throne when Musa died in 1337, but reigned for only four years. He died in 1341, reportedly of a heart attack, and the crown went to his uncle Sulayman.

One historian suggests Sulayman had been passed over for Maghan and may have deposed him. Maghan's son Jata in the end seized power in the civil war that followed Sulayman's death.

马甘一世（1280年代—1341）是马里第十位曼萨，即著名的曼萨·穆萨（坎坎·穆萨一世）的长子。1324年穆萨启程前往麦加朝觐时，他被留下名义上执掌国政。1337年穆萨去世后他继位，但实际统治仅四年。1341年他去世，据称死于心脏病，王位没有传给子嗣，而由其叔苏莱曼继承。

有史学家认为，苏莱曼当年被越过而让位于马甘，后来可能还废黜了他。苏莱曼死后马里陷入内战，最终夺得权力的是马甘之子贾塔。
