en:
Naré Maghann Konaté was a twelfth-century faama of the Mandinka chiefdom of Kiri and a figure of the Epic of Sundiata. A hunter-diviner foretold his heir would be born of an ugly woman, so he married the hunchbacked Sogolon Condé, who bore him Sundiata Keita.

He favoured Sundiata over his eldest son Dankaran Touman, but after his death around 1218 Dankaran Touman seized the throne and drove Sundiata into exile.

纳雷·马甘·科纳特是12世纪曼丁戈人小邦基里的法王，也是《松迪亚塔史诗》中的人物。一位猎占师预言他的继承人将由丑陋的女子所生，他于是娶了驼背的索戈隆·孔德，后者生下松迪亚塔·凯塔。

en:
Muhammad ibn Qu was the eighth mansa of the Mali Empire, succeeding his father Mansa Qu around 1305 as the immediate predecessor of Mansa Musa.

In 1324 Musa recounted that his predecessor fitted out 200 ships, and then 2000, to explore the limits of the Atlantic Ocean and never returned, leaving Musa to rule. The historian al-Umari recorded the story without naming him; several historians identify the predecessor as Muhammad. The voyage is often wrongly credited to an Abu Bakr II, a ruler who never reigned.

en:
Mansa Musa (c. 1280–c. 1337) was the ninth Mansa of Mali, under whom the empire reached its greatest extent. By his own account, he inherited power after his predecessor sailed into the Atlantic on a second expedition and never returned, leaving Musa to rule as deputy. Mali's wealth rested on the salt trade and on the gold of Bambuk and Bure.

In 1324 Musa went on pilgrimage to Mecca with an enormous retinue. In Cairo his lavish gifts pushed down the price of gold for years, and on the way home he had to borrow from Egyptian merchants at high interest. His fame reached Europe, where the 1375 Catalan Atlas showed a rich West African ruler.

Musa annexed Gao and Timbuktu, built ties with the Mamluk and Marinid sultanates, and made Timbuktu a centre of Islamic learning. He died around 1337, and his son Maghan succeeded him.

曼萨·穆萨（约1280—约1337）是马里第九位曼萨，帝国在他治下达到极盛。据他本人的说法，前任曼萨率第二次远征驶入大西洋，一去不回，留下穆萨代理朝政，他由此继承大权。马里的财富来自食盐贸易，以及邦布库和布雷的黄金。

1324年，穆萨率庞大的随从队伍前往麦加朝觐。他在开罗的豪阔馈赠使金价多年低迷，归途中又钱袋告罄，只得向埃及商人高息借款。他的名声传到欧洲，1375年的《加泰罗尼亚地图》上画出了一位富有的西非君主。

穆萨吞并了加奥和廷巴克图，与马穆鲁克苏丹国、马林苏丹国通好，使廷巴克图成为伊斯兰学术中心。他约于1337年去世，其子马甘继位。

en:
Qu was mansa of the Mali Empire from about 1300 to 1305. A son of Mansa Uli, he came to the throne after Sakura, the court slave who had seized power, was murdered returning from the pilgrimage to Mecca; Mande tradition says he killed Sakura himself with the help of Sakura's daughter.

His accession ended the succession disputes between the great council, the Gbara, and the hunter guilds. He died in 1305 and was succeeded by his son Muhammad.

en:
Sakura (died c. 1300) was a mansa of the Mali Empire, known chiefly from Ibn Khaldun. Born outside the Keita dynasty, possibly a royal slave, he seized the throne amid palace conflicts around 1285. He stabilized Mali and stretched its power from the Atlantic eastward beyond Gao.

He made the pilgrimage to Mecca, the first mansa to do so since Uli. Returning from the hajj, he was killed at Tajura near Tripoli; with his death the Keita line returned to power.

萨库拉（约1300年卒）是马里帝国的曼萨，事迹主要见于伊本·赫勒敦的记述。他并非凯塔王族，可能曾是宫廷奴隶，约1285年趁宫廷内乱篡夺王位。他稳定了马里政局，将势力从大西洋沿岸向东扩张到加奥以东。

他赴麦加朝觐，是乌利之后第一位朝觐的曼萨。归途中他在的黎波里附近的塔朱拉被杀，他死后凯塔家族重新掌权。

en:
Mansa Sulayman (d. c. 1360), brother of Mansa Musa, ruled Mali from about 1341 after Musa's son Maghan, and may have deposed Maghan, whom he had earlier been passed over for.

He kept up Musa's diplomacy with the Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan of Fez, and in 1348 or 1349 sent an embassy to congratulate him on his conquests. In 1352 the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta reached his court and left the fullest eyewitness account of Mali at its height, noting the land's security but finding Sulayman a miser beside Musa.

During Ibn Battuta's stay, Sulayman imprisoned his principal wife and cousin Qasa and accused her of conspiring against him, and the court condemned her. Sulayman died around 1360, the last great mansa. His son Qasa reigned nine months, and the civil war that followed ended Mali's golden age.

曼萨·苏莱曼（约1360年卒）是曼萨·穆萨的兄弟，约1341年继穆萨之子马甘之后统治马里；他早年曾被越过，后来可能废黜了马甘。

他延续穆萨的外交，与非斯的马林王朝苏丹阿布·哈桑往来，1348年或1349年遣使祝贺其开疆拓土。1352年，摩洛哥旅行家伊本·白图泰到访他的宫廷，留下了关于鼎盛时期马里最详尽的亲历记录；他称许当地治安良好，却认为苏莱曼远不如穆萨慷慨。

伊本·白图泰逗留期间，苏莱曼囚禁了身为堂亲的正妃卡萨，指控她谋反，宫廷判她有罪。苏莱曼约于1360年去世，是最后一位伟大的曼萨。其子卡萨在位九个月，随后爆发的内战终结了马里的黄金时代。

en:
Sundiata Keita (c. 1217–c. 1255), called the Lion of Mali, was the son of the Mandinka ruler Naré Maghann Konaté and the founder of the Mali Empire. Epic tradition tells that as a child he could not walk until he pulled himself up on a baobab branch; persecution after his father's death drove him into exile at Mema, and he returned to free his people from Soumaoro Kanté, king of Sosso.

Around 1235 Mandinka chiefs rallied to him and he defeated Soumaoro at Kirina. He became the first Mandinka ruler to take the title mansa, ruling from Niani over a federation controlling the goldfields and trade routes.

He died around 1255, traditionally drowned in the Sankarani River near Niani; Mandinka custom forbids naming great kings' burial places. His sons succeeded him in turn, and the empire he founded lasted until 1610, reaching its height under his great-nephew Mansa Musa.

zh:
松迪亚塔·凯塔（约1217—约1255）人称“马里之狮”，是曼丁戈首领纳雷·马甘·科纳特之子，马里帝国的创立者。史诗讲述，他幼年不会走路，抓着猴面包树的枝条才站了起来；父亲死后他遭迫害，流亡到梅马，后来返回家乡，将族人从苏苏国王苏曼古鲁·康德手中解放出来。

约1235年，曼丁戈各部首领归附于他，他在基里纳击败了苏曼古鲁。他成为第一位采用“曼萨”称号的曼丁戈君主，定都尼亚尼，统治着一个掌控金矿与商路的联邦。

他约于1255年去世，相传溺死于尼亚尼附近的桑卡拉尼河；曼丁戈习俗禁止说出伟大君王的葬地。他的儿子们先后做了曼萨，他创立的帝国延续到1610年，在他的侄孙曼萨·穆萨时达到极盛。

en:
Mansa Uli, also called Wali, was the second mansa of the Mali Empire and son and successor of Sundiata Keita. Remembered as one of Mali's greatest rulers, he consolidated the new empire and may have been the first mansa to bring Walata, Timbuktu and Gao under Mali's rule.

Between 1260 and 1277 he made the pilgrimage to Mecca. He was apparently succeeded by his brother Wati, while his son Qu later took the throne.

en:
Mansa Wati was the third mansa of the Mali Empire. Arab sources name him as a son, possibly adopted, of Sundiata Keita and place his short reign between those of his brother Mansa Uli and Khalifa, who was overthrown around 1275.

Mande oral tradition does not remember him. The reason given is its tendency to preserve only rulers who left descendants.

en:
Melik Temür (died 1307) was a Mongol prince, a son of Ariq Böke. In 1276 he joined Shiregi's revolt against Kublai and, during a dispute among the rebels, supported Sarban in replacing Shiregi; after the revolt failed he took refuge with Kaidu in Central Asia.

In 1306 he abandoned Kaidu's successor Chapar and surrendered to the Yuan prince Qayishan. After Chengzong's death he backed Ananda's failed bid for the throne; Qayishan, reigning as Wuzong, had him put to death at Shangdu in 1307. His great-grandson Arpa later briefly held the Ilkhanid throne.

明里帖木儿（？—1307）是蒙古宗王，阿里不哥之子。1276年，他随昔里吉起兵反抗忽必烈，叛军内讧时支持撒儿班取代昔里吉；事败后投奔中亚的海都。

1306年，他脱离海都的继承者察八儿，向元朝宗王海山投降。元成宗死后，他依附阿难答争夺帝位，事败后被已即位的海山（元武宗）赐死于上都。他的曾孙阿儿巴后来曾短暂登上伊儿汗之位。

en:
Kitbugha (died 1303) was a Mongol soldier in Hulagu's army until captured at the Battle of Homs in 1260. Bought and freed by Qalawun, he rose to emir. After al-Ashraf Khalil's murder in 1293 he ruled Egypt as regent for the young al-Nasir Muhammad, deposing him to take the throne in 1294.

His favor to Oirat refugees, with famine and plague, turned the emirs against him; in 1296 they overthrew him and raised up Lajin. He later governed Hama and died there in 1303.

怯的不花（？—1303）原为旭烈兀军中的蒙古士兵，1260年在霍姆斯战役中被俘，由嘉拉温买下获释后升至埃米尔。1293年阿什拉夫·哈利勒遇刺后，他以摄政身份为年幼的纳西尔·穆罕默德执掌埃及，1294年废黜幼主自立。

他厚待卫拉特难民，加上饥荒与瘟疫，令埃米尔们离心；1296年他们将他推翻，拥立拉金。他后来出镇哈马，1303年卒于当地。

en:
Al-Ashraf Ala al-Din Kujuk (1334–1345), a son of al-Nasir Muhammad and his Tatar wife Ardu, was made Mamluk sultan of Egypt in 1341, aged five or six, after the strongman Qawsun deposed and executed his half-brother al-Mansur Abu Bakr. Qawsun ruled as regent until a mamluk revolt overthrew him later that year.

Kujuk was deposed in 1342 and returned to his mother in the Cairo Citadel. In 1345 court rivals accused Ardu of sorcery and the eleven-year-old Kujuk was murdered.

阿什拉夫·阿拉丁·库朱克（1334—1345）是纳西尔·穆罕默德与鞑靼妃子阿尔杜之子。1341年，权臣盖松废并处死他的异母兄长曼苏尔·阿布·伯克尔后，把年仅五六岁的他立为埃及马穆鲁克苏丹，自己以摄政身份独揽大权，同年在马穆鲁克哗变中倒台。

Al-Mansur Abu Bakr (c. 1321–1341) was the Mamluk sultan who briefly ruled Egypt after his father, al-Nasir Muhammad, died in 1341. Born to the concubine Narjis, he trained from boyhood at the desert fortress of al-Karak and was named heir ahead of his brothers.

His reign lasted about two months: in 1341 the senior emir Qawsun deposed and arrested him, and two months later had him executed in Upper Egypt.

en:
Al-Nasir Hasan (1334/1335–1361), a son of al-Nasir Muhammad by his Tatar concubine Kuda, was Mamluk sultan of Egypt in two reigns, 1347–1351 and 1354–1361. Enthroned at twelve, he was a figurehead for senior emirs and was toppled in 1351 when he tried to rule in person.

Restored in 1354, he purged the senior emirs and staffed it with sons of mamluks. In 1361 he was killed by his own mamluk Yalbugha. His reign left Cairo the great Sultan Hasan Mosque-Madrasa.

Alaa al-Din Ali bin al-Imam was an Egyptian emir of the el-Emam family. He rose under Sultan al-Ashraf Qansuh al-Ghuri, gaining his trust and high office. In 1501 he became supervisor of the sultan's privy treasury, and in 1503 also of pious endowments.

He later held a string of senior posts, including secretary of state and supervisor of the armies. He was known as Abu al-Asitul, Father of the Fleet.

en:
Al-Nasir Shihab al-Din Ahmad (1316–1344), a son of Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, was Bahri Mamluk sultan of Egypt from January to June 1342. As a boy he was sent to the desert fortress of al-Karak to learn horsemanship, and he never stopped preferring it to Cairo.

After his father died in 1341, the strongman Qawsun ruled through a five-year-old puppet until emirs sympathetic to Ahmad ousted him; Ahmad still delayed his departure for Egypt. Two months into his reign he went back to al-Karak and governed through a deputy.

When he executed his own backers, his half-brother al-Salih Isma'il deposed him. The Mamluks repeatedly besieged al-Karak before Ahmad was captured in July 1344 and beheaded that month. Chroniclers judged him the worst of his father's sons.

他处死自己的支持者，异母弟萨利赫·伊斯玛仪便将他废黜。马穆鲁克军队多次围攻卡拉克，1344年7月艾哈迈德被俘，当月被斩首。史家称他是父亲诸子中最糟的一个。

en:
Al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (1285–1341) was the Bahri Mamluk sultan of Egypt and Syria, enthroned three times between 1293 and 1341 and the dynasty's longest-ruling sultan. Put on the throne at eight after his brother al-Ashraf Khalil's murder, he was ruler in name only: the emir Kitbugha deposed him in 1294, and in 1309 he withdrew to al-Karak rather than live under the emirs Baybars and Salar.

Egyptians clamoured for his return, and in 1310 he came back determined to rule alone, executing Baybars and arresting Salar, who died in prison. He abolished the emirs' surcharges on commoners, made peace with the Ilkhanids in 1322, and in 1330 sent away French envoys who had asked him for Jerusalem.

He rebuilt much of the Cairo Citadel and renovated over thirty mosques. He died in 1341; eight of his sons reigned.

纳西尔·穆罕默德·本·嘉拉温（1285—1341）是埃及与叙利亚的伯海里马穆鲁克苏丹，1293至1341年间三度在位，是该王朝在位最久的苏丹。兄长阿什拉夫·哈利勒遇刺后，年仅八岁的他被拥立为苏丹，却只是名义上的君主：1294年埃米尔怯的不花将他废黜；1309年，他不愿再受埃米尔拜巴尔与萨拉尔摆布，退居卡拉克。

埃及民众呼吁他回来，1310年他复位，决心独掌大权，处决了拜巴尔，又逮捕萨拉尔，后者死于狱中。他废除埃米尔向平民加征的杂税，1322年与伊儿汗国议和，1330年又把向他索要耶路撒冷的法国使节赶出埃及。

开罗城堡在他手里大加扩建，三十多座清真寺得到翻修。他于1341年去世，八个儿子后来相继登上王位。

en:
Ardu was a Tatar concubine of the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad and mother of the future sultan al-Ashraf Kujuk, born in 1334. When another Tatar concubine, Kuda, died, Ardu raised her infant son, the future sultan al-Nasir Hasan.

After al-Nasir Muhammad's death in 1341 she later married Sultan al-Kamil Sha'ban. A rival wife accused her of sorcery under Sultan as-Salih Isma'il, and in 1345 her eleven-year-old son Kujuk was murdered in the ensuing intrigues.

阿尔杜是马穆鲁克苏丹纳西尔·穆罕默德的鞑靼妃子，1334年生下后来的苏丹阿什拉夫·库朱克。另一位鞑靼妃子库达死后，阿尔杜收养了她襁褓中的儿子，即后来的苏丹纳西尔·哈桑。

纳西尔·穆罕默德1341年去世后，她改嫁苏丹卡米勒·沙班。萨利赫·伊斯玛仪在位期间，与她为敌的妃嫔指控她施行巫术；1345年，她十一岁的儿子库朱克在随之而来的宫廷倾轧中遇害。

en:
Sitt Ashlun Khatun was a Mongol noblewoman, daughter of the Ilkhanate commander Shaktay ibn Qarajin in Mamluk service. In 1282 she married the Mamluk sultan Qalawun, and in 1285 bore a son, Muhammad, the future sultan al-Nasir Muhammad. Ashlun raised him in Mongol fashion.

He was made sultan in 1293 after his half-brother al-Ashraf Khalil was murdered, and when Kitbugha deposed him in 1294 Ashlun went with her son into confinement at al-Karak, returning to Cairo with him when he was restored in 1299.

阿什伦·哈屯是蒙古贵族女子，父亲是投奔马穆鲁克的伊儿汗国将领沙克泰·伊本·卡拉金。1282年她嫁给马穆鲁克苏丹嘉拉温，1285年产下一子穆罕默德，即后来的苏丹纳西尔·穆罕默德。阿什伦按蒙古风俗将他抚养长大。

1293年异母兄长阿什拉夫·哈利勒遇刺后，穆罕默德被拥立为苏丹；1294年怯的不花将他废黜，阿什伦随儿子一同被幽禁于卡拉克，1299年儿子复位时又随他回到开罗。

en:
Barquq (c.1336–1399) was a Circassian brought to Egypt in 1364 as a mamluk of the amir Yalbugha al-Umari. Rising through the army, in 1382 he deposed the child sultan al-Salih Hajji and founded the Burji Mamluk dynasty.

Ousted in a revolt that restored Hajji in 1389, he retook the throne in 1390 and replaced almost all governors and senior officials with members of his own household.

After Timur took Baghdad in 1393 he allied with the Ottomans against him. He died in 1399, leaving the throne to his son Faraj.

赛夫丁·巴尔库克（约1336—1399）是切尔克斯人，约1364年被带到埃及，成为埃米尔耶勒卜加·乌马里的马穆鲁克。他在军中崛起，1382年废黜幼苏丹萨利赫·哈吉，建立布尔吉马穆鲁克王朝。

1389年叛乱贵族复立哈吉，他一度失位，但1390年夺回王位，用自家私属替换了几乎所有总督和高级官员。

1393年帖木儿攻占巴格达后，他与奥斯曼结盟对抗。1399年他去世，其子法拉吉继位。

en:
Baybars al-Jashankir (died 1310) was a Circassian mamluk of Qalawun who rose to be emir and jashankir, food taster. During al-Nasir Muhammad's reign he served as vice-sultan and, with Salar, dominated the young ruler. In 1302 he helped crush a Bedouin rebellion, and in 1303 commanded against the Mongols at the Battle of Shaqhab.

When al-Nasir withdrew in 1309, Salar and the Burji mamluks made him sultan. His short reign saw famine and unrest; in 1310 he abdicated, was captured, and executed on al-Nasir's orders.

拜巴尔·贾山基尔（？—1310）是嘉拉温麾下的切尔克斯马穆鲁克，累迁至埃米尔和尝食侍从“贾山基尔”。纳西尔·穆罕默德在位期间，他出任副苏丹，与萨拉尔一同挟制年幼的君主。1302年他参与平定贝都因人叛乱，1303年在舍盖卜战役中率军迎击蒙古人。

1309年纳西尔退隐后，萨拉尔与布尔吉马穆鲁克拥立他为苏丹。他在位短暂，饥荒与动荡不断；1310年退位后被捕，奉纳西尔之命处决。

en:
Benjamin II was the 82nd Coptic Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the See of St Mark, serving from 1327 to 1339. Born in Demicrat in southern Egypt, he lived as a hermit and monk before his election, and was consecrated in 1327.

Under him the Copts suffered fierce persecution under Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, with churches and monasteries destroyed; he rebuilt the ruined Monastery of Abba Bishoy in the Nitrian Desert. He died on 6 January 1339 and was later reburied there.

本雅明二世是第82任亚历山大教宗兼圣马可牧首，1327年至1339年在任。他生于埃及南部的德米克拉特，当选前长年隐居修道，于1327年祝圣继位。

他在任期间，苏丹纳西尔·穆罕默德治下的科普特人遭受严酷迫害，多处教堂与修道院被毁；他重建了尼特伦沙漠中残破的圣比绍伊修道院。他于1339年1月6日去世，后遗体迁葬该院。

en:
Khawand Toghay was the favourite wife of the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun, who reigned from 1293 to 1341. A Turkish slave girl bought by the sultan's governor in Syria, she entered the Cairo Citadel as his concubine; he freed her and married her in 1321.

After her manumission she was remembered for her kind heart and for personally attending to the needs of her own slaves. She bore the sultan a son, Prince Anuk, who died in 1340. She outlived her husband by some seven years and was buried in her own mausoleum in Cairo's Northern Cemetery.

哈万德·托盖是马穆鲁克苏丹纳西尔·穆罕默德·本·嘉拉温（1293—1341年在位）最宠爱的妻子。她是突厥人，原为奴婢，由苏丹派驻叙利亚的总督买来，进入开罗城堡成为苏丹的侍妾；1321年，苏丹释放她并娶她为妻。

获释之后，她以心地善良、亲自照料手下奴婢的需求而闻名。她为苏丹生下王子阿努克，阿努克于1340年去世。她比丈夫多活了约七年，葬在开罗北墓地为自己建的陵墓中。

en:
Lajin (died 1299) was a Mamluk of possibly Circassian origin, bought by Qalawun, whose daughter he married. He served as governor of Damascus from 1280 and took part in the assassination of Sultan al-Ashraf Khalil in 1293. He persuaded Kitbugha to seize the throne, then in 1296 forced him aside and became sultan.

Favoritism toward his mamluk Mankutumur, made atabeg over senior emirs, led to his murder with Mankutumur in Cairo in 1299, after which al-Nasir Muhammad returned.

zh:
拉金（？—1299）可能出身切尔克斯，被嘉拉温买下并娶其女为妻。1280年起任大马士革总督，1293年参与刺杀苏丹阿什拉夫·哈利勒。他先怂恿怯的不花篡位，又于1296年逼退怯的不花，自立为苏丹。

他提拔自己的马穆鲁克曼库图穆尔为阿塔贝格，位居老资格埃米尔之上，最终于1299年在开罗与曼库图穆尔一同被杀，纳西尔·穆罕默德随后复位。

en:
Qalawun (c. 1222–1290) was a Kipchak Turk sold as a mamluk for a thousand dinars, hence his nickname al-Alfi. Rising under Baybars, he became atabeg to the child sultan Solamish and in 1279 took the throne.

In 1280 he defeated Sunqur al-Ashqar, and in 1281 joined him to repel Abaqa at the Battle of Homs. Against the Crusaders he took Margat in 1285 and Tripoli in 1289. He died in Cairo in 1290 while besieging Acre, which his son al-Ashraf Khalil took in 1291.

zh:
嘉拉温（约1222—1290）是钦察突厥人，被卖为马穆鲁克时以一千第纳尔买下，故得绰号“阿尔菲”（千金之人）。他在拜巴尔斯麾下崛起，成为幼主索拉米什的阿塔贝格，1279年篡位自立。

1280年他击败孙库尔·阿什卡尔，1281年又与其联手，在霍姆斯战役击退阿八哈。对十字军方面，他1285年攻取麦尔盖卜，1289年攻陷的黎波里。1290年他在围攻阿卡期间卒于开罗，阿卡于1291年由其子阿什拉夫·哈利勒攻克。

en:
Sayf al-Din Anuk (8 April 1323 – 31 August 1340) was a son of the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad and his favorite wife, Khawand Toghay. Long his father's preferred heir, he accompanied the sultan on the departure for the Mecca hajj in 1332, meeting his half-brothers at al-Aqaba.

By July 1340 he had lost favor and been dropped from the succession. He died on 31 August 1340, months before his father, and was buried in his father's Cairo madrasa.

赛义夫丁·阿努克（1323年4月8日—1340年8月31日）是马穆鲁克苏丹纳西尔·穆罕默德与其宠妻哈万德·托盖之子。他长期是父亲属意的继承人；1332年曾随苏丹启程前往麦加朝觐，在亚喀巴与异母兄弟们会合。

en:
Agnese Pico (1303–1340) was an Italian noblewoman of the Pico della Mirandola family, daughter of Francesco I Pico, imperial vicar of Mirandola. In 1321 Rinaldo Bonacolsi of Mantua captured her father and brothers and had them starved in the castle of Castel d'Ario.

Agnese became the first wife of Guido Gonzaga, capitano del popolo of Mantua. Her two daughters married into the Este of Ferrara and the da Correggio family. She died at Mantua in 1340.

阿涅塞·皮科（1303—1340）是皮科·德拉·米兰多拉家族的意大利贵族女子，米兰多拉帝国代理人弗朗切斯科一世·皮科之女。1321年，曼托瓦统治者里纳尔多·博纳科尔西俘获她的父亲与兄弟，把他们关入卡斯泰尔达里奥城堡，任其饿死。

阿涅塞后来成为曼托瓦“人民首领”圭多·贡扎加的第一任妻子，两个女儿分别嫁入费拉拉埃斯特家族与达·科雷焦家族。她于1340年在曼托瓦去世。

en:
Anna Dovara (c. 1301–c. 1354) was an Italian noblewoman of the Dovara clan of Cremona and the wealthy lady of Isola Dovarese. In 1322 she married Filippino Gonzaga, son of Luigi I Gonzaga, Mantua's first capitano del popolo, in a lavish wedding, bringing rich Cremonese lands as her dowry.

The marriage gave the Gonzaga their first foothold in the Cremonese countryside. Her daughter Gigliola married Matteo II Visconti in 1342. Anna died in Mantua around 1354.

en:
Antonia da Correggio was an Italian noblewoman, the daughter of Guido IV da Correggio, signore of Correggio, and Guidaccia della Palù. In 1328 she married Feltrino Gonzaga, a son of Luigi I Gonzaga of Mantua; with him she founded the cadet Gonzaga line of Novellara and Bagnolo and became its lady consort.

Her son Guido (1340–1399) inherited Novellara in 1374 and married Ginevra Malatesta, while Guglielmo and Odoardo both joined the conspiracies of 1356 and 1376 against the Mantuan Gonzaga and fought as captains for Bologna.

Beatrice Gonzaga (c. 1301 – c. 1335) was a Mantuan noblewoman, the daughter of Guido Gonzaga and Agnese Pico. She married Nicolò I d'Este, who ruled Ferrara jointly with his brothers Rinaldo II and Obizzo III after the Este returned to power in 1317.

Her son Rinaldo d'Este (1333–1369) became a knight, and her daughter Jacopa married Trincia Trinci, signore of Foligno. Beatrice died at Ferrara around 1335, nine years before her husband.

Caterina Malatesta (c. 1300 – c. 1340) was an Italian noblewoman, the daughter of the condottiero Pandolfo I Malatesta, lord of Rimini, and Taddea da Rimini. After 1319 she became the second wife of Luigi I Gonzaga, first capitano del popolo of Mantua, tying his new signoria to the Malatesta lords of the Romagna.

Their four children were Corrado, founder of the cadet line later made marquises of Palazzolo, Alberto, Luigia, who married Azzo I da Correggio, and Federico, who died in 1376, long after Caterina's death at Mantua around 1340.

Corrado Gonzaga was an Italian condottiero born in Mantua, the son of Luigi I Gonzaga, the city's first capitano del popolo, and Caterina Malatesta. His father cut him out of the succession to Mantua, which passed through his brother's line.

In 1340 he married Verde Beccaria, daughter of Lodrisio Beccaria, a noble of Pavia. Their son Filippino carried on his branch, and Corrado is counted the founder of the cadet Gonzaga line whose descendants became marquises of Palazzolo in 1595.

Federico Gonzaga (died c. 1376) was a Mantuan condottiero, a son of Luigi I Gonzaga, the city's first capitano del popolo, and Caterina Malatesta of Rimini. In 1354 he joined the conspiracy that Fregnano della Scala raised against Cangrande della Scala, lord of Verona.

In 1376 he plotted again, this time against his own nephew Ludovico II Gonzaga of Mantua, together with Odoardo and Guglielmo Gonzaga. The courtier Guido Cavriani uncovered the scheme; Federico was condemned to death but escaped, dying around the same year.

en:
Feltrino Gonzaga (c. 1305–1374), third son of Mantua's first capitano del popolo Luigi I Gonzaga, founded the Gonzaga line of Novellara. In 1328 he helped drive the Bonacolsi from Mantua and married Antonia da Correggio. From 1335 he held Reggio Emilia, where he built a great citadel and in 1345 resisted Mastino della Scala.

In 1363 he led an anti-Visconti league to victory at Solara, and in 1366 Charles IV made him imperial vicar. His harsh rule had turned the Reggiani against him, and when Bernabò Visconti twice besieged the city in 1370–1371, his allies failed him.

Rather than yield to the Este, who had joined Bernabò, he surrendered to his old enemy and on 17 May 1371 sold Reggio for fifty thousand gold florins, keeping Novellara and Bagnolo. He spent his last years wandering northern Italy in poverty and died in Padua in 1374.

费尔特里诺·贡扎加（约1305—1374）是曼托瓦首位“人民首领”路易吉一世·贡扎加的第三子，诺瓦拉拉贡扎加家族旁支的始祖。1328年他参与将博纳科尔西家族逐出曼托瓦，并娶安东尼娅·达·科雷焦为妻。1335年起他领有雷焦艾米利亚，在当地修起一座雄伟的城堡，1345年又抵挡住马斯蒂诺·德拉·斯卡拉的进攻。

1363年他率领反维斯孔蒂联盟在索拉拉获胜，1366年被查理四世任命为帝国代理人。他的严苛统治使雷焦居民离心离德；1370至1371年贝尔纳博·维斯孔蒂两度围城，盟友纷纷背弃了他。

他不愿向与贝尔纳博联手的埃斯特家族屈膝，转而向宿敌投降，于1371年5月17日以五万金弗罗林出售雷焦，仅保留诺瓦拉拉和巴尼奥洛。晚年他漂泊于意大利北部，穷困潦倒，1374年卒于帕多瓦。

Filippino Gonzaga (died 5 April 1356) was a Mantuan condottiero and a son of Luigi I Gonzaga, Mantua's first capitano del popolo. His marriage in 1322 to Anna Dovara brought the Gonzaga the lands of Isola Dovarese and their first foothold in the Cremonese region. In 1328 he and his brothers helped their father drive out Rinaldo Bonacolsi.

In 1342 he married his daughter to Matteo II Visconti of Milan and then fought for the Visconti against the della Scala. Widowed in 1354, he married Verena of Habsburg-Laufenburg. He died in Mantua in 1356 and was buried in its cathedral.

Gigliola Gonzaga, also called Egidiola (c. 1325 – c. 1377), was the eldest daughter of the Mantuan condottiero Filippino Gonzaga and Anna Dovara. In 1342 her father married her to Matteo II Visconti, and as his wife she was a co-consort of Milan.

Her daughters were Caterina, who later married Ugolino Gonzaga, and Andreola, who became a nun. Widowed in 1355 when Matteo died, probably poisoned by his brothers, she returned to Mantua and disputed her mother's Cremonese border lands with her Gonzaga kinsmen until the family absorbed them.

吉廖拉·贡扎加（约1325—约1377），一作埃吉迪奥拉，是曼托瓦雇佣兵首领菲利皮诺·贡扎加与安娜·多瓦拉的长女。1342年，父亲将她嫁给马泰奥二世·维斯孔蒂；作为马泰奥之妻，她是米兰的共同领主夫人之一。

两个女儿中，卡泰丽娜后来嫁给乌戈利诺·贡扎加，安德莱奥拉成为修女。1355年马泰奥疑被众兄弟毒杀，吉廖拉寡居后返回曼托瓦，为继承母亲的克雷莫纳边境领地与贡扎加亲族长期争执，这些土地最终被家族吞并。

en:
Guido Corradi da Gonzaga, also called Corrado (died Mantua, 1318), was an Italian landowner of the Corradi-Gonzaga family, from which came the Gonzaga lords of Mantua. A friend of Mantua's Bonacolsi rulers, he raised his house's standing through pacts with the cities neighboring Mantua.

By his first wife Estrambina di San Martino he had several children, including Luigi (1268–1360), who after Guido's death became the first Gonzaga captain of the people of Mantua and founded the dynasty that ruled from 1328.

en:
Guido Gonzaga (1290–1369) was the eldest son of Ludovico I Gonzaga, who made the family masters of Mantua. Podestà of Mantua in 1328 and later of Reggio Emilia, he became lord of the latter in 1335.

He reached the head of Mantua only in 1360 as its second capitano del popolo, ruling beside his son Ugolino, who likely held the real power until two of Guido's other sons, Francesco and Ludovico, murdered him in 1362.

In 1368 Barnabò Visconti occupied Mantua until Emperor Charles IV intervened to free it; the Peace of Bologna then added other lands. Guido died in 1369 and was succeeded by his son Ludovico II, whose mother was Beatrice of Bar.

zh:
圭多·贡扎加（1290—1369）是卢多维科一世的长子，其父使贡扎加家族成为曼托瓦之主。他于1328年任曼托瓦行政长官，后任雷焦艾米利亚行政长官，1335年成为后者的领主。

直到1360年，他才作为曼托瓦第二位“人民首领”执掌该城，与儿子乌戈利诺共同统治，实权可能掌握在乌戈利诺手中，直到后者于1362年被圭多的另外两个儿子弗朗切斯科和卢多维科刺杀。

1368年贝尔纳博·维斯孔蒂占领曼托瓦，直至皇帝查理四世干预解围；随后签订的《博洛尼亚和约》将若干土地划入。圭多于1369年去世，其子卢多维科二世继位，后者的母亲是巴尔的贝亚特丽切。

en:
Ludovico II Gonzaga (1334–1382) was the third capitano del popolo of Mantua. A son of Guido Gonzaga and Beatrice of Bar, on 14 October 1362 he and his brother Francesco murdered their elder brother Ugolino at a dinner; Francesco died in mysterious circumstances in 1368, leaving Ludovico sole heir.

Succeeding in 1369, he allied Mantua with Bernabò Visconti, married Alda d'Este of Ferrara, wedded his son Francesco to Visconti's daughter Agnese, opened trade with Venice and strengthened his fortresses. He survived noble plots in 1373 and 1376 and died on 4 October 1382.

en:
Ludovico I Gonzaga (1268–1360) founded Gonzaga rule in Mantua. A son of Guido Corradi, in 1328 he drove out Rinaldo Bonacolsi with Ghibelline troops lent by Cangrande I della Scala and the help of his father-in-law. Mantua's citizens then elected him capitano del popolo. In 1329 Emperor Louis IV named him imperial vicar, and in 1335 he became lord of Reggio Emilia.

He backed the Visconti at Parabiago in 1339 and hosted Petrarch in Mantua in 1349. In his later years he fought Bernabò Visconti. He died in 1360 and was succeeded in Mantua by his son Guido, while another son, Feltrino, held Reggio Emilia.

卢多维科一世·贡扎加（1268—1360）是在曼托瓦建立贡扎加家族统治的意大利贵族。他是圭多·科拉迪之子，1328年借助坎格兰德一世·德拉·斯卡拉的吉伯林军队与岳父的帮助，驱逐里纳尔多·博纳科尔西，随后被曼托瓦市民选为“人民首领”。1329年皇帝路德维希四世任命他为帝国代理人，1335年他又成为雷焦艾米利亚领主。

1339年他支持维斯孔蒂家族打赢帕拉比亚戈战役，1349年在曼托瓦接待来访的诗人彼特拉克。晚年他与贝尔纳博·维斯孔蒂交战。1360年他去世，其子圭多在曼托瓦继位，另一子费尔特里诺则掌管雷焦艾米利亚。

en:
Margherita Gonzaga was a Mantuan noblewoman, the daughter of Guido Gonzaga, capitano del popolo of Mantua, and Beatrice of Bar. In 1353 she became the second wife of Jacopino da Carrara, signore of Padua, who ruled the city jointly with his nephew Francesco I da Carrara. In October 1354 Jacopino and Francesco led a Venetian league against the Visconti of Milan.

Rivalry over the succession ended in 1355 when Francesco uncovered a plot and jailed Jacopino. Margherita fled to Mantua with her son Jacopo, who died in Puglia in 1385.

Petronio Corradi, also called Piergiovanni or Petrozzano, was a son of the Mantuan landowner Guido Corradi, known as Corrado, and Estrambina di San Martino, and a younger brother of Luigi I Gonzaga, the first Gonzaga lord of Mantua.

He became a cleric: in 1288 he was a canon of Como Cathedral, and in 1339 he served as vicar of Mantua Cathedral. He had three natural sons, and his grandson Andrea Corradi was a notary who acted for the Gonzaga in legal cases. Petronio died in 1348.

Her son Guido became the second captain of Mantua and Feltrino founded the Gonzaga branch of Novellara. She brought the Gonzaga estates in Brescia and Ferrara, and died in Mantua in 1319, before her husband.

Tommasina Gonzaga was a Mantuan noblewoman, the daughter of Luigi I Gonzaga, Mantua's first capitano del popolo, and Richilda Ramberti. In 1319 she married Guglielmo Azzone Castelbarco, a condottiero serving the della Scala of Verona, who in 1328 led Veronese troops that helped expel the Bonacolsi from Mantua and bring the Gonzaga to power.

In 1333 the couple hosted Charles IV of Luxembourg, the future emperor, at their castle of Avio. She died in 1372, leaving six children.

en:
Ugolino Gonzaga (1320–1362), a Mantuan condottiero, was the son of Guido Gonzaga, Mantua's second capitano del popolo. He was the Gonzaga who bound the family to Milan.

In 1340 he married Verde della Scala, daughter of Mastino II, yet in 1342–1343 he fought beside the Milanese against the Scaligers. After Verde's death he married twice more, wedding Caterina Visconti, daughter of Matteo II Visconti and niece of Bernabò, in 1349. That Visconti alliance lasted into the early sixteenth century.

From 1360 he governed Mantua with his aged father, most likely as its real ruler. Venice disliked the alliance and backed a plot, and on 13 October 1362 his brothers Francesco and Ludovico murdered him.

乌戈利诺·贡扎加（1320—1362）是曼托瓦雇佣兵首领，曼托瓦第二位“人民首领”圭多·贡扎加之子，也是把贡扎加家族与米兰绑在一起的人。

1340年他娶马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉之女维尔德为妻，1342至1343年却随米兰军与斯卡拉家族作战。维尔德去世后他又两度续弦，1349年娶马泰奥二世·维斯孔蒂之女、贝尔纳博的侄女卡泰丽娜。这一与维斯孔蒂家族的同盟一直延续到16世纪初。

1360年起，他与年迈的父亲共同治理曼托瓦，很可能才是实际的统治者。威尼斯不喜欢这一同盟，支持了一场阴谋：1362年10月13日，乌戈利诺被兄弟弗朗切斯科和卢多维科刺杀。

en:
Rinchen, also called Lhachen Rinchan Bhoti, was a Ladakhi Buddhist nobleman. After his father and kinsmen were murdered by the Kalamanya clan, he feigned peace to avenge them before seeking his fortune in Kashmir. In the chaos after a Mongol invasion he seized the Kashmir throne in 1320, founding the Kashmir Sultanate.

He later converted to Islam under the influence of the Sufi Bulbul Shah, becoming the valley's first Muslim ruler and taking the name Sadr al-Din Shah. He built the Big Mosque and died on 25 November 1323, leaving his son Haidar Khan to Shah Mir's care.

仁钦，一称拉钦·仁钦·波提，是拉达克的佛教贵族。父亲与亲族被卡拉曼亚氏族害死后，他假意讲和、设计复仇，随后前往克什米尔谋求发展。趁蒙古入侵后的乱局，他于1320年夺取克什米尔王位，开创克什米尔苏丹国。

en:
Marc-Pierre de Voyer de Paulmy, comte d'Argenson (1696–1764), was Louis XV's reforming war minister and a figure well regarded by the philosophes.

Made war minister in 1743 during the War of the Austrian Succession, he reorganized the army after consulting Marshal Saxe, revived local militias to aid recruitment, and founded the École royale du génie at Mézières for military engineers. After the war he standardized the artillery and founded an officer school.

He also laid out the Place de la Concorde. Dismissed after the 1757 Damiens plot against the king, he died in 1764, days after returning from exile.

马克-皮埃尔·德·瓦耶·德·波尔米，阿尔让松伯爵（1696—1764），是路易十五手下锐意改革的陆军大臣，也受到启蒙哲士的好感。

1743年奥地利王位继承战争期间他被任命为陆军大臣，征询萨克森元帅后整顿军队，恢复地方民兵协助征募，并在梅济耶尔创办王家工兵学校培养军事工程师。战后他统一炮兵制度，创办军官学校。

他还主持规划了协和广场。1757年达米安刺杀国王未遂后他被解职，1764年在流放归来数日后去世。

en:
Martin Luther (1483–1546), born at Eisleben, was a German friar and theologian whose protest against indulgences split Western Christianity. After lightning struck near him in 1505 he vowed to become a monk, entered a monastery and from 1512 taught theology at Wittenberg, arguing that sinners are justified by faith alone.

In 1517 he issued the Ninety-five Theses against indulgence preaching; translated into German, they spread within weeks. Excommunicated in 1521, he refused to recant at Worms before Emperor Charles V and was outlawed. Hidden in Wartburg by his Saxon protector, he translated the New Testament into German; the full Bible appeared in 1534.

In 1525 he urged the nobles to crush the rebel peasants and married former nun Katharina von Bora, making clerical marriage respectable; his catechisms and hymns spread his teaching. His late writings against Jews called for burning synagogues. He died at Eisleben in 1546, still excommunicate.

马丁·路德（1483—1546）生于艾斯莱本，是德意志修士、神学家，对赎罪券的抗议令西方基督教分裂。1505年遭闪电惊吓后许愿做修士，入院修道，1512年起在维滕贝格教神学，主张因信称义。

1517年他发表反对赎罪券的《九十五条论纲》，译成德语后数周传遍德意志。1521年他被革除教籍，在沃尔姆斯议会当着皇帝查理五世拒绝撤回，被宣布为不法之徒。萨克森保护人将他藏入瓦尔特堡，译出德语《新约》，全本《圣经》1534年问世。

1525年呼吁贵族镇压农民起义，并娶还俗修女卡塔琳娜·冯·博拉，使教士结婚得以体面；教理问答与赞美诗传播了新教义。晚年反犹著作主张焚烧犹太会堂。1546年卒于艾斯莱本，至死未复教籍。

en:
Matteo Ricci (1552–1610) was an Italian Jesuit and a founder of the Jesuit China mission. At the Roman College he studied mathematics and astronomy under Christopher Clavius. He sailed from Lisbon in 1578 and reached Goa that year.

He reached Macau in 1582, mastered Chinese, and settled at Zhaoqing with Michele Ruggieri in 1583, where he made his first Chinese world map in 1584. Moving north, he entered Beijing in 1601 and served the Wanli Emperor as astronomer and cartographer, publishing the enlarged Kunyu Wanguo Quantu in 1602.

He stressed parallels between Catholicism and Confucian teaching and worked with Xu Guangqi to translate Euclid's Elements into Chinese. He died in Beijing in 1610.

利玛窦（1552—1610）是意大利籍耶稣会士，耶稣会在华传教事业的奠基人之一。他在罗马学院师从克里斯托弗·克拉维乌斯学习数学和天文学，1578年从里斯本乘船出发，同年抵达果阿。

1582年他抵达澳门，熟习汉语，1583年与罗明坚定居肇庆，并于1584年绘制了第一幅中文世界地图。此后他北上，1601年进入北京，以天文、制图之学侍奉万历帝，1602年刊行了增订的《坤舆万国全图》。

他着力阐明天主教与儒家义理的相通之处，并与徐光启合作将欧几里得《几何原本》译成中文。1610年，利玛窦在北京去世。

en:
Maximilien de Béthune, first Duke of Sully (1560–1641), was a Huguenot nobleman born near Mantes who became Henry of Navarre's closest counselor from 1571. During the St Bartholomew's Day Massacre in 1572, he escaped by carrying a Catholic book of hours.

He fought through the Wars of Religion and was wounded at Ivry in 1590, advising Henry's conversion to Catholicism while refusing his own. From 1596 he reformed royal finances, becoming superintendent in 1601 and balancing the budget while promoting agriculture, roads and the Canal de Briare.

Made a duke and peer in 1606, he resigned after Henry IV's assassination in 1610. Named a marshal in 1634, he died in 1641.

第一代叙利公爵马克西米连·德·贝蒂讷（1560—1641）是胡格诺派贵族，生于芒特附近，自1571年起追随纳瓦拉的亨利，成为他最亲信的谋臣。1572年圣巴托罗缪大屠杀期间，他携带天主教祈祷书躲过追杀。

宗教战争期间他为亨利率军作战，1590年在伊夫里战役负伤；他劝说亨利改宗天主教，自己却始终拒绝改宗。1596年起他整顿王室财政，1601年出任财政总监，在实现收支平衡的同时推动农业、道路建设和布里亚尔运河工程。

1606年他受封公爵和法兰西重臣。1610年亨利四世遇刺后他便辞职；1634年获授法国元帅衔，1641年去世。

en:
Casimir I of Kuyavia (c. 1211–1267) was a Piast prince, second son of Konrad I of Masovia. He received Kuyavia from his father in 1233 and Ląd on his marriage to Constance, and after Konrad's death in 1247 seized Sieradz-Łęczyca and Dobrzyń from his brothers. His bid to Christianize the Yotvingians failed amid Teutonic opposition, so he settled Templars at Łuków.

A coalition led by Bolesław the Pious forced him to cede Ląd in 1261. His third wife, Euphrosyne of Opole, bore Władysław I the Elbow-high, the future king of reunited Poland. Casimir died in 1267.

库亚维的卡齐米日一世（约1211—1267）是皮亚斯特王公，马佐夫舍的康拉德一世次子。1233年父亲把库亚维封给他，他又因与康斯坦丝的婚姻得到隆德；1247年康拉德死后，他从兄弟手中夺取谢拉兹—文奇察和多布任。他试图使雅特维格人皈依基督教，因条顿骑士团反对而失败，于是在武库夫安置圣殿骑士团。

虔诚者波列斯瓦夫率领的联军最终于1261年迫使他割让隆德。第三任妻子奥波莱的尤弗罗西娜为他生下后来重新统一波兰的国王瓦迪斯瓦夫一世“矮子”。卡齐米日于1267年去世。

en:
Konrad I (c. 1187–1247), youngest son of Casimir II the Just, was duke of Masovia from 1194 and Kuyavia from 1205. In 1205 he and his brother Leszek the White defeated Roman the Great of Galicia–Volhynia at Zawichost, where Roman was killed. His repeated campaigns against pagan Prussia failed amid border raids.

In 1226 he invited the Teutonic Order to conquer Chełmno Land and subdue the Prussians, and the order's rights were confirmed when Frederick II issued the Golden Bull of Rimini. He seized the Kraków seniorate as high duke in 1229–1232 and again in 1241–1243, and died in 1247.

康拉德一世（约1187—1247）是“正义者”卡齐米日二世的幼子，自1194年任马佐夫舍公爵，1205年起兼领库亚维亚。1205年，他与兄长“白者”莱谢克在扎维霍斯特击败加利西亚-沃里尼亚的罗曼大帝，罗曼战死。他多次征伐异教普鲁士，都在边境袭扰中失败。

en:
Hugo V was Count of Montfort-Bregenz, the son of Count Ulrich I, who died in 1287. He began ruling Bregenz in 1294 and acquired the Bregenzerwald as a pledge in 1307. In 1311 he bought Staufen Castle in the Upper Allgäu and founded its collegiate chapter.

He secured a market privilege for Bregenz in 1330. When he died on 26 July 1338, the Montfort-Bregenz line became extinct, and the Bregenz lands were divided among the surviving branches of the Montfort counts.

雨果五世是蒙特福特-布雷根茨伯爵，1287年去世的乌尔里希一世之子。他于1294年开始统治布雷根茨，1307年取得布雷根茨森林的质押权。1311年，他购得上阿尔高的施陶芬城堡，并创立了施陶芬法政牧师团。

en:
Ulrich I, Count of Montfort-Bregenz (died 1287), was a Swabian nobleman of the Montfort house, a cadet line of the counts palatine of Tübingen, and ruled the Bregenz lands in Vorarlberg. He was the second son of Count Hugo II and Elisabeth of Burgau.

Before 1272 he married Agnes of Helfenstein, who bore him his successor Hugo V (died 1338), and he also left an illegitimate daughter, Katharina.

en:
Brian Bóruma, known as Brian Boru (c. 941–23 April 1014), made himself king of Munster by 978, then subdued Dublin, Leinster and the northern Uí Néill. In 1002 his rival acknowledged him high king of Ireland, ending the Uí Néill hold on the high kingship.

In 1014 his army met the Norsemen of Dublin and their Leinster allies at Clontarf: Brian's forces won, but the elderly king was killed. He founded the O'Brien dynasty.

Cormac MacCarthy Mor (1271–1359) of the MacCarthy dynasty ruled as Prince of Desmond from 1325 until his death. In that same year Diarmaid Óg MacCarthy was murdered in the courtroom at Tralee by Maurice FitzMaurice, 4th Baron Kerry, who was attainted by the Dublin parliament and forfeited his lands.

Cormac's sons included Donal Og MacCarthy Mor, who succeeded him and ruled Desmond until 1391. Dermot MacCarthy was the first Lord of Muskerry (1340–1381).

en:
Diarmait Ua Briain (c. 1060–1118) was a son of Toirdelbach Ua Briain, king of Munster. After their father died in 1086 his brother Muirchertach drove him into exile, and he is thought to have led an Irish fleet to victory at the Battle of Mynydd Carn.

Reconciled in 1093, he ruled Waterford, and in 1114 took the kingship of Munster when Muirchertach fell ill, triggering four years of civil war. He died at Cork in 1118, after which Toirdelbach Ua Conchobair invaded and partitioned Munster.

en:
Donnchad mac Briain (died 1064) was a son of Brian Boru and a Leinster king's daughter. He survived the Battle of Clontarf in 1014, where his father and half-brother Murchad were killed, and made himself king of Munster; his rival half-brother Tadc was assassinated in 1023, reportedly on his order.

He later fought Diarmait of Leinster and his nephew Toirdelbach Ua Briain, who in 1058 helped drive him from Limerick. Deposed in 1063, he went on pilgrimage to Rome, died in 1064, and was buried at Santo Stefano al Monte Celio.

en:
Muirchertach Ua Briain (c. 1050–1119), son of Toirdelbach, ruled Dublin for his father and succeeded him as king of Munster in 1086. In 1101 he declared himself high king of Ireland and presided over a Church reform synod at Cashel.

He fought the Northern Uí Néill to a stalemate, while his fleets intervened in Wales and faced Norway's Magnus Barefoot in the Irish Sea. In 1114 illness let his brother Diarmait seize power; his nephew Toirdelbach partitioned Munster in 1118. He died at Lismore in 1119.

By his wife Mór he fathered Toirdelbach Ua Briain, who later became king of Munster and one of Ireland's most powerful kings. Tadc was assassinated in 1023 at Donnchad's instigation.

en:
Toirdelbach Ua Briain (1009–14 July 1086), grandson of Brian Bóruma, was king of Munster and effectively high king of Ireland. His father Tadc was killed in 1023, probably on the orders of his half-brother Donnchad, who seized Munster.

Allied from the 1050s with Diarmait of Leinster, he wore Donnchad down and in 1063 drove him into exile to Rome. After Diarmait's death he became Ireland's master, installing his sons Muirchertach in Dublin and Diarmait in Waterford and making and unmaking kings of Connacht. He died at Kincora in 1086, leaving Muirchertach his successor.

en:
Toirdhealbhach mac Diarmada Ua Briain (died 1167), a son of Diarmait Ua Briain, was king of Munster from 1142. His brother Tadhg deposed him in 1151, but he recovered the kingship after Tadhg's death in 1154.

In 1157 high king Muirchertach Mac Lochlainn drove him out and divided Munster, until Ruaidrí of Connacht restored him in North Munster. His own son Muirchertach deposed him in 1165, and he died in 1167. His sons included Domnall Mór Ua Briain.

en:
Wudayy ibn Jammaz was one of the twelve sons of Jammaz ibn Shihah, long-ruling emir of Medina from the Banu Muhanna, descendants of the Prophet through Husayn. The quarrel over his father's inheritance shaped his life.

Around 1301 he opposed the succession of the chosen heir, Mansur. Cairo had by then claimed the right to appoint Medina's emir, and Wudayy seized the city by force in 1316/7 and again in 1326/7.

He was acknowledged as co-emir in 1335 and from 1336 ruled as sole emir until his death in 1342/3. His rule was one of the few breaks in the hold of Mansur's descendants, who retook the emirate after him.

en:
Abu Bakr ibn Shaikh 'Umar was the Somali sultan ruling Mogadishu when the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta reached the city in 1331, at the height of its medieval prosperity. Ibn Battuta called him a Barbara, the medieval term for native Somalis.

He described Mogadishu as an exceedingly large city of wealthy merchants, famed for high-quality fabrics exported as far as Mamluk Egypt. The sultan spoke Somali and fluent Arabic alike, and kept a court of viziers, legal scholars, commanders and royal eunuchs.

en:
Ludwig von Braunschweig-Lüneburg (c. 1300–1346) was a Welf prince, a son of Duke Otto II the Strict, and from 1324 Bishop of Minden, the first of several Welf bishops there. Elected over the city's own candidate, he kept the see only through arbitration by his brother Duke Otto III.

His election was meant to bring Minden into step with the duchy against the Counts of Hoya, but it failed: Hoya troops destroyed his Neuhaus castle in 1335, and he quarrelled with the city's citizens. To defend against Hoya he built Schlüsselburg, granting the cathedral chapter and the city joint rights over it to pay for construction.

His finances never recovered, and in 1339 he placed the bishopric under his ducal brothers' guardianship, which lasted until 1348. He died at Walsrode in 1346.

路德维希·冯·不伦瑞克-吕讷堡（约1300—1346）是韦尔夫家族王公，公爵奥托二世（严苛者）之子，1324年起任明登主教，是明登数位韦尔夫出身主教中的第一位。他击败明登城自行推举的候选人当选，最终靠兄长奥托三世公爵仲裁才坐稳主教之位。

推举他本是希望明登与公国携手对抗霍亚伯爵，结果并未如愿：霍亚军队1335年摧毁了他的诺伊豪斯城堡，他还与明登市民纷争不断。为抵御霍亚，他修建施吕塞尔堡，并为筹措建费，给予主教座堂参议会和明登城共同处置权。

他的财政始终没有好转，1339年将主教区置于诸公爵兄弟的监护之下，监护持续到1348年。1346年，他在瓦尔斯罗德去世。

Wilhelm IV von Manderscheid was a lord of Manderscheid in the Eifel, the son of Wilhelm III von Manderscheid and Jutta von Reuland, who later married Johann I von der Fels in Luxembourg.

en:
Ajlan ibn Rumaythah (c. 1307–1375) became Emir of Mecca in 1343 or 1344, when he and his brother Thaqabah bought the emirate from their father Rumaythah for sixty thousand dirhams without the Mamluk sultan's approval. Thaqabah went to Egypt for recognition, but the sultan had him arrested and ordered Rumaythah restored.

Ajlan fled to Yemen, then returned in 1345 with a sultan's decree and took office without bloodshed. Thaqabah deposed him several times, and he spent 1359–1361 in a Cairene prison.

Restored in 1361, he made his son Ahmad coregent and in 1362 conquered Haly Ibn Yaqub, a feat no emir of Mecca had managed since Abu al-Futuh. He handed Mecca to Ahmad in 1372 and died in 1375, still named in the sermon.

阿杰兰·伊本·鲁迈萨（约1307—1375）于1343或1344年成为麦加埃米尔：他与兄弟塞格拜未经马穆鲁克苏丹许可，以6万迪拉姆从父亲鲁迈萨手中买下埃米尔之位。塞格拜赴埃及请求承认，苏丹却将他拘捕并下令恢复鲁迈萨的职位。

阿杰兰逃往也门，1345年携苏丹敕令返回，兵不血刃地接任。塞格拜数度将他废黜，1359至1361年他被囚禁于开罗。

1361年复位后，他立儿子艾哈迈德为共同埃米尔，1362年攻取哈利·伊本·叶尔孤卜，这是自阿布·法图赫以来没有一位麦加埃米尔做到过的事。1372年他将麦加交给艾哈迈德，1375年去世，聚礼讲道中仍保留其名。

en:
Muhammad Abu Numayy I (c. 1232–1301) was Emir of Mecca from 1250, ruling first with his father Abu Sa'd and then his uncle Idris ibn Qatadah. In 1269 he submitted to the Mamluk sultan Baybars, who invested him, and in 1270 he defeated and beheaded Idris at Khulays and began to rule alone.

In 1271 Jammaz ibn Shihah of Medina captured Mecca, but Abu Numayy defeated him and retook the city after forty days, and later fought off further seizures by him. On 6 October 1301 he abdicated in favour of his sons Humaydah and Rumaythah and died two days later.

en:
Asad al-Din Rumaythah, a son of Abu Numayy I, was Emir of Mecca seven times between 1301 and 1345, and each time the sultans in Cairo had the last word. Proclaimed joint emir with his brother Humaydah in October 1301, he was arrested after the hajj of 1302 and taken to Cairo in chains, then restored in 1305.

He spent decades feuding with Humaydah and later another brother, deposed, jailed and reinstated by Cairo in turn. From 1321 he openly backed Zaydi Shi'ism in Mecca. In 1343 or 1344 his sons Thaqabah and Ajlan forced him to abdicate for sixty thousand dirhams; the sultan reversed it, but in October 1345 he formally yielded Mecca to Ajlan at the dome over Zamzam.

He died on 3 March 1346. At his funeral the Shafi'i chief qadi stopped the Zaydi imam from leading the prayer.

阿萨德丁·鲁迈萨是阿布·努米一世之子，1301至1345年间七度成为麦加埃米尔，每一次都由开罗的苏丹说了算。1301年10月，他与兄弟胡迈达并立为埃米尔；1302年朝觐后被拘捕，戴镣押往开罗，1305年复位。

此后他与胡迈达、后来又与另一兄弟争斗数十年，被开罗轮番废黜、囚禁又复立。1321年起，他公开支持麦加的栽德派什叶教义。1343或1344年，儿子塞格拜和阿杰兰以6万迪拉姆逼他退位；苏丹推翻了这一安排，但1345年10月，他仍在渗渗泉圆顶屋前正式把麦加让给阿杰兰。

1346年3月3日他去世。葬礼上，沙斐仪派的首席法官不许栽德派伊玛目带领祷告。

en:
Albert II, called the Degenerate (c. 1240–1314), of the House of Wettin, ruled Meissen and Thuringia. In 1255 he married Margaret of Sicily, daughter of the Emperor Frederick II, but his affair with Kunigunde of Eisenberg drove Margaret from the Wartburg in 1270.

When he favoured the sons of his second marriage, his elder sons Frederick and Diezmann made war on him; Frederick captured Albert, and the Treaty of Rochlitz in 1289 cost him most of his lands. In 1293 he sold Thuringia to King Adolf of Nassau.

阿尔布雷希特二世，绰号“堕落者”（约1240—1314），出身韦廷家族，统治迈森与图林根。1255年他迎娶皇帝腓特烈二世之女西西里的玛格丽塔，却与艾森贝格的库妮贡德私通，迫使玛格丽塔于1270年离开瓦特堡。

en:
Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750) was a German composer and organist of the late Baroque. Orphaned at ten, he lived five years with brother Johann Christoph and from 1700 studied at St Michael’s School. In 1705 he travelled to Lübeck, reportedly on foot, to hear Dieterich Buxtehude play.

He married Maria Barbara in 1707, became Konzertmeister at Weimar in 1714, and in 1717 was hired by Prince Leopold of Anhalt-Köthen as Kapellmeister. Leopold wanted no elaborate church music, so Bach wrote mostly secular works, among them the Brandenburg Concertos.

In 1723 he became Thomaskantor at Leipzig, responsible for four churches’ music. The St Matthew Passion followed in 1727, and his last years were given to the Mass in B minor and The Art of Fugue. He died in 1750 after unsuccessful eye surgery, his grave unmarked for 150 years. Felix Mendelssohn’s 1829 St Matthew Passion performance began the Bach Revival.

约翰·塞巴斯蒂安·巴赫（1685—1750）是巴洛克晚期的德意志作曲家和管风琴家。他十岁成了孤儿，随长兄约翰·克里斯托夫生活五年，1700年起在圣米迦勒学校学习。1705年他相传徒步前往吕贝克，聆听迪特里希·布克斯特胡德的演奏。

1707年他与玛丽亚·芭芭拉结婚，1714年在魏玛升任乐队首席，1717年被安哈尔特-克滕亲王利奥波德聘为乐长。利奥波德不要繁复的教堂音乐，巴赫在那里多写世俗作品，包括《勃兰登堡协奏曲》。

1723年他出任莱比锡圣托马斯学校乐监，负责四座教堂的音乐。《马太受难曲》于1727年首演，晚年致力于《b小调弥撒》和《赋格的艺术》。1750年他在失败的眼科手术后去世，坟墓近150年没有标记。1829年费利克斯·门德尔松重演《马太受难曲》，掀起了巴赫复兴。

en:
Balthasar (1336–1406) of the House of Wettin was Margrave of Meissen and Landgrave of Thuringia. The second son of Margrave Frederick II, he was born at Weißenfels; after his father's death in 1349, his elder brother Frederick III acted as regent and guardian until Balthasar and their brother William came of age and ruled jointly with him.

In 1374 he married Margaret, daughter of Burgrave Albert of Nuremberg; their son Frederick IV succeeded him. In 1382 the Division of Chemnitz ended a quarrel with Frederick III's sons by assigning Balthasar the Landgraviate of Thuringia. He died at the Wartburg in 1406.

巴尔塔萨（1336—1406）是韦廷家族的迈森藩侯兼图林根领地伯爵。他是藩侯腓特烈二世的次子，生于魏森费尔斯；1349年父亲去世后，兄长腓特烈三世摄政并担任监护人，直到巴尔塔萨与弟弟威廉成年后同他共同执政。

1374年，他娶纽伦堡城堡伯爵阿尔布雷希特之女玛格丽特为妻，儿子腓特烈四世后来继承了他的爵位。1382年，《开姆尼茨分割协议》结束了他与腓特烈三世诸子的争端，将图林根领地伯国划归巴尔塔萨。1406年他在瓦特堡去世。

Elisabeth of Meissen (1329–1375), born at the Wartburg, was the daughter of Margrave Frederick II of Meissen and Mathilde of Bavaria. In 1356 she married at Jena Frederick V, Burgrave of Nuremberg, and became Burgravine of Nuremberg when he succeeded to the title in 1357.

Of her nine children, her younger son Frederick, born in 1371, became the first Hohenzollern Elector of Brandenburg, while her daughter Elisabeth married Rupert of Germany. She died in 1375 aged forty-five.

Elisabeth of Lobdeburg-Arnshaugk (1286–1359) was the last heiress of the Arnshaugk branch of the lords of Lobdeburg in Thuringia. In 1300 she married Margrave Frederick I of Meissen at Gotha, bringing her family's Thuringian claims to the Wettins.

After her husband suffered a stroke in 1321 she took over the government, and from his death in 1323 she ruled as regent for her underage son Frederick II until 1329. She remained an adviser to three generations of Wettin rulers and died at Gotha in 1359.

en:
Frederick II the Earnest (1310–1349) was Margrave of Meissen and Landgrave of Thuringia from 1323, ruling first under the guardianship of his mother Elisabeth of Lobdeburg-Arnshaugk until he came of age in 1329. His declaration of a public peace in 1338 curtailed noble privileges and provoked the Thuringian Count's War of 1342–1346, when rebel lords gathered at Arnstadt.

After Emperor Louis IV died in 1347 he declined the German crown and supported Charles IV, whom he met at Bautzen in 1348. He died at the Wartburg.

en:
Frederick III the Strict (1332–1381) of the House of Wettin was Margrave of Meissen and Landgrave of Thuringia. Born at Dresden, he took over the government after his father Frederick II died in 1349, initially ruling on behalf of his brothers William, Balthasar and Louis; from 1368 the brothers ruled jointly, exercising authority in two-year rotations, and in 1379 their lands were permanently divided.

He married Catherine of Henneberg, heiress to Coburg and other estates, and his son by her became Elector Frederick I of Saxony. Frederick died at Altenburg in 1381.

Frederick I, called the Brave or the Bitten (1257–1323), Margrave of Meissen, was the son of Albert the Degenerate and Margaret of Sicily, grandson of Emperor Frederick II. Legend says his mother bit his cheek when she fled the Wartburg in 1270, giving him his nickname.

With his brother Diezmann he warred on their father, was captured in 1281 and reconciled in 1289. His victory over King Albert I at Lucka in 1307 secured Thuringia. Paralyzed by a stroke in 1321, he died at Eisenach in 1323.

en:
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832) was a poet, playwright, novelist, scientist and statesman, and the most influential writer in the German language. He studied law at Leipzig and Strasbourg, where Herder turned him toward Shakespeare, and led the Sturm und Drang movement. In 1774 his novel The Sorrows of Young Werther made him famous.

In 1775 the duke invited him to Weimar, where he sat on the privy council from 1776 and was ennobled in 1782, ran the Weimar theatre from 1791, and from 1794 worked with Schiller until his death in 1805.

In 1806 Napoleon’s soldiers quartered in his house; days later he married Christiane Vulpius, companion of eighteen years. Of their five children only August reached adulthood. The first part of Faust appeared in 1808 and his Theory of Colours in 1810. Goethe died at Weimar in 1832, perhaps saying ‘More light’, though the report is disputed.
en_rich:
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832) was a poet, playwright, novelist, scientist and statesman, and the most influential writer in the German language. He studied law at [ShowLocationName('leipzig')] and [ShowLocationName('strasbourg')], where Herder turned him toward Shakespeare, and led the Sturm und Drang movement. In 1774 his novel The Sorrows of Young Werther made him famous.

In 1775 the duke invited him to [ShowLocationName('weimar')], where he sat on the privy council from 1776 and was ennobled in 1782, ran the Weimar theatre from 1791, and from 1794 worked with Schiller until his death in 1805.

In 1806 Napoleon’s soldiers quartered in his house; days later he married Christiane Vulpius, companion of eighteen years. Of their five children only August reached adulthood. The first part of Faust appeared in 1808 and his Theory of Colours in 1810. Goethe died at Weimar in 1832, perhaps saying ‘More light’, though the report is disputed.

约翰·沃尔夫冈·冯·歌德（1749—1832）是诗人、剧作家、小说家、科学家和政治家，也是最具影响力的德语作家。他先后在莱比锡和斯特拉斯堡学习法律，在那里赫尔德引导他走向莎士比亚，并领导狂飙突进运动。1774年的小说《少年维特之烦恼》使他一举成名。

1775年公爵邀他前往魏玛，他此后一直住在那里。1776年起他进入公爵的枢密院，1782年被封为贵族，1791年起主持魏玛剧院。1794年席勒与他结交，两人合作直至1805年席勒去世。

1806年拿破仑的士兵住进他在魏玛的家中；几天后他与相伴十八年的克里斯蒂安娜·武尔皮乌斯成婚，两人的五个孩子中只有奥古斯特长大成人。《浮士德》第一部于1808年问世，《色彩学》于1810年出版。歌德1832年在魏玛去世，一说他最后的话是“再多一点光”，但这一说法有争议。

en:
Margaret of Sicily (c. 1237–1270) was a Hohenstaufen princess born in Foggia, daughter of Emperor Frederick II and Isabella of England. She married Albert “the Degenerate”, heir to Meissen, in 1255, bringing the Pleissnerland as her dowry, and bore him five children at the Wartburg. In 1265 Albert became Landgrave of Thuringia.

After her nephew Conradin was executed in 1268, she inherited the Hohenstaufen claim to Sicily and Swabia. In June 1270, discovering Albert’s adultery, she fled to Frankfurt am Main, where the citizens supported her, and died there on 8 August. Legend says she bit her son Frederick’s cheek, earning him the nickname “the Bitten”.

西西里的玛格丽塔（约1237—1270）是霍恩施陶芬家族的公主，生于福贾，为皇帝腓特烈二世与英格兰的伊莎贝拉之女。1255年她嫁给迈森藩侯国继承人“堕落者”阿尔布雷希特，以普莱斯纳兰为嫁妆，在瓦尔特堡生下五名子女。1265年阿尔布雷希特成为图林根领地伯爵。

1268年侄子康拉丁被处决后，她继承了霍恩施陶芬家族对西西里与士瓦本的权利。1270年6月，她发现阿尔布雷希特通奸后逃往美因河畔法兰克福，得到市民支持，于8月8日在那里去世。相传她曾咬了儿子腓特烈的面颊，后者因而得到“被咬者”的绰号。

en:
Matilda of Bavaria (1313–1346) was the eldest daughter of the Wittelsbach emperor Louis IV and his first wife, Beatrice of Silesia. In 1323 she married Frederick II, Margrave of Meissen, at Nuremberg, binding the Wettin margrave to her father's imperial court.

Of her nine children, six survived infancy, among them the future margraves Frederick III, Balthasar and William I, and Elisabeth, wife of the Burgrave of Nuremberg. Matilda died at Meissen in 1346, three years before her husband.

巴伐利亚的玛蒂尔达（1313—1346）是维特尔斯巴赫家族的神圣罗马帝国皇帝路德维希四世与第一任妻子西里西亚的贝翠丝的长女。1323年，她在纽伦堡嫁给迈森藩侯腓特烈二世，使韦廷家族的藩侯与父皇的宫廷结盟。

她生有九名子女，其中六人活过幼年，包括后来的藩侯腓特烈三世、巴尔塔萨和威廉一世，以及嫁给纽伦堡城堡伯爵的伊丽莎白。1346年，玛蒂尔达在迈森去世，比丈夫早三年。

en:
Ahmet Bey, called Ahmed Gazi, was a son of the Menteşeid ruler İbrahim Bey. After İbrahim's death in the mid-fourteenth century, Ahmet and his brothers Musa and Mehmet divided the Menteşe beylik between them. After Musa died before 1375, Ahmet succeeded him and also ruled Milas and Beçin.

He commissioned a medrese at Beçin in 1375–1376 and died in 1391. His tombstone there gives his lineage as Ahmed Gazi, son of İbrahim, son of Orhan, son of Mesut — the chief written source for the Menteşeid dynasty's ancestry.

艾哈迈德贝伊人称艾哈迈德·加齐，是门泰谢统治者易卜拉欣贝伊之子。易卜拉欣于14世纪中叶去世后，艾哈迈德与兄弟穆萨、穆罕默德瓜分门泰谢贝伊国。穆萨于1375年前去世，艾哈迈德继承其位，也统治米拉斯和贝琴。

他于1375—1376年在贝琴兴建经学院，1391年去世。他在经学院的墓碑写明其谱系为艾哈迈德·加齐——易卜拉欣之子——奥尔汗之孙——梅苏德曾孙，这也是记载门泰谢王朝世系的主要文字史料。

İbrahim Bey was the fourth ruler of the Menteşeid beylik of southwestern Anatolia, succeeding his father Orhan Bey. After a crusader fleet took İzmir from Aydın in 1344, the Menteşeids joined Aydın in attacking Crete.

As İbrahim prepared in 1350 to march on İzmir, Venice threatened the harbour and compelled him to sign a treaty disarming the beylik. He died around 1355, and his lands passed to his sons Musa, Mehmet and Ahmet.

en:
Mehmet Bey was a son of the Menteşeid ruler İbrahim Bey of Milas. After İbrahim's death, the beylik was divided between Mehmet and his brothers Musa and Ahmet, with Mehmet ruling Muğla and Çine. He and his son İlyas joined an alliance against the Ottomans, who seized Menteşeid lands, and both fled to Timur.

In 1402, after Timur defeated the Ottomans at Ankara, Mehmet visited Timur near Denizli to seek the return of his family's lands. He died in early 1403.

en:
Menteşe Bey (died c. 1295) founded the Anatolian beylik that bore his name, with its capital at Milas. Leading Oghuz Turks pushed west by Mongol pressure, he seized Byzantine lands around Muğla, and in 1276–1277 joined the Jimri rebellion.

Around 1282 he captured Tralles and Nyssa, and in 1291 coins struck at Milas acknowledged Seljuk suzerainty. After he seized Miletus, the Byzantine general Philanthropenos defeated and killed him near Priene in 1295. His son Mesut succeeded him.

en:
Mesut Bey (died c. 1319) was the second ruler of the Menteşe beylik in southwestern Anatolia, succeeding his father Menteşe Bey. In 1300 his forces seized a large part of Rhodes.

The Hospitaller knights conquered Rhodes in 1308; in 1311 the Genoese allied with Mesut against them after the knights seized their goods. At Beçin Castle Mesut received Ulu Arif Çelebi, a travelling Mevlevi teacher and grandson of Rumi. On his death he was succeeded by his son Orhan.

zh: 穆萨贝伊是门泰谢贝伊国第四代统治者、驻跸米拉斯的易卜拉欣贝伊之子。易卜拉欣于14世纪中叶去世后，门泰谢贝伊国由穆萨与兄弟穆罕默德、艾哈迈德瓜分，三人各自治理自己的领地。

en:
Orhan Bey, also called Şücaüddin Orhan, was the third ruler of the Menteşeid Turks in southwestern Anatolia, succeeding his father Mesut Bey at Milas shortly before 1320. That year he sent a fleet against Rhodes in a failed attempt to take the island back from the Hospitallers.

When Ibn Battuta passed through the region in 1333, he visited Orhan at Beçin and called him the sultan of Milas. Orhan was followed by his son İbrahim.

en:
Hammir Singh (1302–1364) was a Rajput chief of the Sisodia branch of the Guhila dynasty, which had lost Chittor to Alauddin Khalji's invasion of Mewar. As Rana of Sisoda he campaigned for years to recover his ancestral lands, finally taking Chittorgarh and expelling the Delhi Sultanate's Chauhan vassal.

Rajput chronicles record that he defeated a Delhi army at Singoli and made Mewar independent. Crowned Maharana in 1326, he founded the ruling Sisodia line, built temples at Chittor, and died in 1364.

哈米尔·辛格（1302—1364）是古希拉王朝西索迪亚支系的拉杰普特首领，其家族在梅瓦尔遭阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉入侵时失去了吉多尔。他身为西索达的拉纳，为收复祖业征战多年，终于攻下吉多尔加尔，驱逐了德里苏丹国的乔汉人附庸。

拉杰普特编年史记载，他在辛戈利击败德里的军队，使梅瓦尔赢得独立。他于1326年加冕为大拉纳，开创西索迪亚统治世系，在吉多尔修建神庙，1364年去世。

en:
Aleramo (died before 991) was the Frankish founder of the Aleramici dynasty and marquis of western Liguria. He appears in 933, when King Hugh enfeoffed him near Vercelli, and in 958 Berengar II, whose daughter Gerberga he married, named him marquis. He then sided with Emperor Otto I, who confirmed his march in 967.

His sons Anselm and Otto founded the Savona and Monferrato lines. Legend makes him elope with Otto’s daughter Adelasia on a white and a red horse, winning the land he could ride without rest and naming it Monferrato.

阿莱拉莫（991年前去世）是法兰克人，阿莱拉莫家族的始祖，也是西利古里亚边区的侯爵。他在933年见于记载，意大利国王于格在韦尔切利附近封给他一块采邑；958年，贝伦加尔二世封他为侯爵，他娶了贝伦加尔的女儿格贝尔加。此后他倒向皇帝奥托一世，后者于967年确认了他的边区。

他的儿子安塞尔姆和奥托分别开创萨沃纳与蒙费拉托支系。相传他与奥托的女儿阿德拉西娅分别骑着红马和白马私奔，赢得自己策马不休所能跑遍的土地，并将其命名为蒙费拉托。

en:
Anselm I (died 998) was the eldest surviving son of the Frankish marquis Aleramo, by his first wife Adelasia. Succeeding his father as marquis of the whole Aleramic march, he held Savona and Montferrat before the latter passed to his brother Otto. A placitum of 983 records him as marquis at Otto III’s court in Ravenna, under Empress Adelaide’s regency.

He married Gisla of Milan and founded the Anselmian line of the Aleramici, whose branches included Savona, Del Vasto and Sezzadio; his son Anselm II inherited Savona.

安塞尔姆一世（998年卒）是法兰克侯爵阿莱拉莫与第一任妻子阿德拉西娅所生的在世长子。他承袭父亲成为整个阿莱拉莫边区的侯爵，领有萨沃纳和蒙费拉托，后来蒙费拉托转入其弟奥托之手。983年拉文纳宫廷的裁判文书已称他为侯爵，当时奥托三世年幼，由皇太后阿德莱德摄政。

en:
Argentina Spinola (1294–1337) was the daughter of Opizzino Spinola, captain of the people of Genoa, and Violante of Saluzzo. In October 1307 she married in Constantinople Theodore Palaiologos, son of the Byzantine emperor Andronikos II and heir to the March of Montferrat; with her father's backing the couple seized power at Casale.

While Theodore was absent in Constantinople from 1325, Argentina governed Montferrat as regent until his return in 1328. She died at Casale early in 1337, leaving a son, the future Marquess John II.

en:
Beatrice of Castile (1254–1286) was a daughter of Alfonso X of Castile and Violant of Aragon, born at Valladolid. Alfonso first betrothed her to John II, Margrave of Brandenburg, to win Brandenburg's support for his claim to the German crown, but the engagement was broken off. In August 1271 she married at Murcia William VII, Marquess of Montferrat, becoming his third wife.

Her children included Yolande, who took the name Irene and married the Byzantine emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos, and John I, who succeeded William as marquess. She died in 1286, six years before her husband.

en:
Boniface II “the Giant” (July 1202–1253) was Marquis of Montferrat from 1225, son of William VI and Berta di Clavesana. Taking power in 1226, he joined the Lombard League against Frederick II, and Alessandria defeated him in 1230. His wife Margaret of Savoy, married in 1235, bore William VII and Alessia.

Reconciled with the emperor in 1239, he received Thessalonica and became its titular king, but in 1245 submitted to Frederick at Turin. In 1253 Conrad IV granted him Casale Monferrato; days later, on 12 May, he died at Moncalvo.

“巨人”波尼法乔二世（1202年7月—1253年）自1225年起任蒙费拉托侯爵，是古列尔莫六世与克拉韦萨纳的贝尔塔之子。1226年亲政后，他加入伦巴第同盟与腓特烈二世为敌，1230年被亚历山德里亚击败。1235年他娶萨伏依的玛格丽特，生下古列尔莫七世和阿莱西娅。

en:
Cécile de Comminges (c. 1300–1354) was the youngest daughter of Bernard VII, Count of Comminges, and Laure de Montfort. She was married first to Amanieu, heir to the county of Astarac, who died in 1326.

When her son Centule IV succeeded as count in 1330, Cécile governed Astarac as regent. In 1337 she married the 16-year-old John II Palaiologos, Marquess of Montferrat. The marriage was childless and she died at Casale Monferrato in 1354.

zh:
塞茜尔·德·科曼日（约1300—1354）是科曼日伯爵贝尔纳七世与洛尔·德·蒙福尔的幼女。她先嫁给阿斯塔拉克伯国继承人阿马尼厄，后者于1326年去世。

1330年她的儿子桑蒂勒四世继位，塞茜尔以摄政身份治理阿斯塔拉克。1337年她再嫁16岁的蒙费拉托侯爵乔瓦尼二世·帕里奥洛加斯。这段婚姻没有子女，她于1354年在卡萨莱蒙费拉托去世。

en:
Henry (c. 1020–1045) was the younger son of Marquis William III of Montferrat and Waza. Around 1041 he married Adelaide, daughter of Margrave Ulric Manfred II of Turin and heiress of the March of Turin.

When William III died in 1042, Henry ruled the March of Montferrat jointly with his elder brother Otto II; a charter of 1042 records him granting lands to the church of Turin. His joint rule ended with his early death in 1045.

恩里科（约1020—1045）是蒙费拉托侯爵古列尔莫三世与瓦扎的幼子。约1041年，他娶都灵边疆伯奥尔德里克·曼弗雷迪二世之女、都灵边疆区女继承人阿德莱德为妻。

1042年古列尔莫三世去世后，他与兄长奥托二世共同治理蒙费拉托边疆区；1042年的一份特许状记载他向都灵教会赠与土地。1045年他早逝，共同执政随之结束。

en:
John I, called the Just (c. 1277–1305), was the last Aleramici marquis of Montferrat, the only son of William VII and Beatrice of Castile. Guarded as a boy by the rulers of Saluzzo and Naples, he later fought to recover his towns from Asti and Alessandria.

In 1296 he married Margaret of Savoy but had no children. His league drove Matteo Visconti from Milan in 1302 and Asti submitted in 1303. Dying in 1305, he made his nephew Theodore Palaiologos his heir, bringing the Palaiologoi to Montferrat.

乔瓦尼一世，人称“公正者”（约1277—1305），是末代阿莱拉莫家族蒙费拉托侯爵，为古列尔莫七世与卡斯蒂利亚的贝阿特丽斯的独子。少年时他受萨卢佐和那不勒斯统治者的庇护，后来作战试图从阿斯蒂和亚历山德里亚手中收复城镇。

1296年他娶萨伏依的玛格丽塔为妻，但没有子嗣。他组织的联盟于1302年将马泰奥·维斯孔蒂逐出米兰，1303年阿斯蒂臣服。1305年他临终前立外甥狄奥多尔·巴列奥略为继承人，巴列奥略家族由此入主蒙费拉托。

en:
John II Palaiologos (1321–1372) was Marquis of Montferrat from 1338 and spent his reign pushing the march's borders against its neighbours. The son of Theodore I, he shared in government from 1336 and succeeded at seventeen. With help from his cousin Otto of Brunswick-Grubenhagen he turned on the Angevins of Naples.

He used King Robert's death in 1343 to take Alessandria, Asti and Tortona by 1344, and in 1345 defeated their vicar at Gamenario. With Visconti's tacit backing he added Alba, Bra and Valenza, and in 1355 he escorted Charles IV and received Cherasco, Novara and Pavia.

His 1358 marriage to Isabella, titular queen of Majorca, cost him imperial favour and brought war with the Visconti, and he gave back the Pavia lands for Visconti ones near Asti. He died in 1372, and three of his sons succeeded him in turn.

zh:
乔瓦尼二世·巴列奥略（1321—1372）自1338年起任蒙费拉托侯爵，在位期间一直向外推进侯国边界。他是提奥多罗一世之子，1336年起参预政事，十七岁继位。他在堂兄弟不伦瑞克-格鲁本哈根的奥托帮助下，对那不勒斯的安茹家族开战。

他利用国王罗贝托1343年去世的机会，到1344年攻占亚历山德里亚、阿斯蒂和托尔托纳，1345年在加梅纳里奥击败安茹总督。在维斯孔蒂家族的默许下，他又夺得阿尔巴、布拉和瓦伦扎；1355年他护送查理四世，获授凯拉斯科、诺瓦拉和帕维亚。

1358年他娶马略卡名义女王伊莎贝尔为妻，这桩婚事使他失去皇帝宠信，招来与维斯孔蒂家族的战争，他以帕维亚的土地换回对方在阿斯蒂附近的领地。他于1372年去世，三个儿子先后继位。

en:
William III (c. 970–1042) was the third Marquis of Montferrat from 991, succeeding his father Otto I. He founded Spigno monastery and made donations to regional abbeys, but abandoned the imperial cause, allying with Ulric Manfred II of Turin and Bishop Leo of Vercelli. The allies soon quarrelled, and after Leo besieged him at Santhià, William burned Vercelli in revenge.

Peace with Manfred was sealed by marrying his son Henry to Manfred’s daughter Adelaide. He resisted Conrad II until the emperor destroyed his Orba valley fortress, and dying in 1042 he left the marquisate to Otto II.

zh:
古列尔莫三世（约970—1042）是第三代蒙费拉托侯爵，991年继承父亲奥托一世。他修建斯皮尼奥修道院，并向各地修道院捐赠土地，但后来背弃亲皇帝的立场，与都灵的乌尔里克·曼弗雷迪二世和韦尔切利主教利奥结盟。盟友不久反目，利奥把他围困在桑蒂亚之后，古列尔莫焚毁韦尔切利作为报复。

他与曼弗雷德议和，让儿子恩里科娶曼弗雷德的女儿阿德尔海德为妻，以此巩固和约。他坚持抵抗康拉德二世，直到皇帝摧毁了他在奥尔巴河谷的堡垒。1042年他去世，把侯爵领地传给奥托二世。

en:
William IV (c. 1030–1100) of the Aleramici dynasty was Marquis of Montferrat from 1084, the eldest son of Marquis Otto II and Constance of Savoy. He first appears in a 1059 document at Savona, where he limited his powers over the city, probably at the citizens’ request.

In 1093 he attended Emperor Henry IV’s donation of the monastery of Breme to the church of Pavia. His successor Rainier was born of his second wife, Otta di Aglié, and William died in 1100.

en:
William V “the Old” (c. 1115–1191) ruled Montferrat from 1135, the son of Marquis Renier I and Gisela of Burgundy. By Judith of Babenberg he had five sons, including Conrad, later King of Jerusalem, and Boniface, founder of the Kingdom of Thessalonica. A Second Crusade veteran, he backed Frederick Barbarossa against the Lombard League, then allied with Byzantine Emperor Manuel I Komnenos and married his son Renier to Manuel’s daughter Maria.

In 1183 he joined his grandson Baldwin V in the Holy Land. Saladin captured him at Hattin in 1187; freed in 1188, he died at Tyre in 1191.

en:
William VI (c. 1173–1226), son of Marquis Boniface I and Elena del Bosco, ruled Montferrat from 1207. On his father’s death in the Fourth Crusade, he kept Montferrat while his half-brother Demetrius inherited Thessalonica. He abandoned the Guelph emperor Otto IV for Frederick II, escorting Frederick from Genoa in 1212.

en:
William VII (c. 1240–1292), called the Great Marquis, ruled Montferrat from 1253 as son of Boniface II and Margaret of Savoy, with his mother governing as regent until 1257. Once a Guelph ally of Charles I of Naples, he allied with Alfonso X of Castile and married Alfonso’s daughter Beatrice in 1271, routing Charles’s forces in 1274.

He led a Lombard league and briefly ruled Milan until Ottone Visconti expelled him in 1281. His daughter Yolande, renamed Irene, married Byzantine Emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos.

In 1290 he entered Alessandria to make peace, but the citizens seized and caged him. He died on 6 February 1292, caged eighteen months, probably starved; Dante numbers him among the negligent princes in Purgatory.

“伟大侯爵”古列尔莫七世（约1240—1292）是波尼法乔二世与萨伏依的玛格丽特之子，1253年起统治蒙费拉托，由母亲摄政至1257年。他本是那不勒斯的查理一世的圭尔夫派盟友，后来与卡斯蒂利亚的阿方索十世结盟，1271年迎娶阿方索之女贝阿特丽斯，1274年击败查理的军队。

他曾统领伦巴第城市同盟，短暂统治米兰，1281年被奥托内·维斯孔蒂逐出。女儿约兰达改名伊琳娜，嫁给拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡二世·巴列奥略。

1290年他进入亚历山德里亚议和，却被市民抓住关入笼中。1292年2月6日，他在被囚禁十八个月后去世，可能是被饿死；但丁在《炼狱篇》中把他列入疏于职守的君主之列。

Margaret of Savoy (1225–c. 1264) was a daughter of Count Amadeus IV of Savoy. In 1228 she was betrothed to Boniface II, Marquess of Montferrat, and they married around 1235; she became the mother of his heir William VII.

When Boniface died in 1253, his testament named Margaret guardian and regent for the underage William, and she ruled Montferrat for about two years until he came of age. Her aunt Beatrice mentioned her in a testament dated 14 January 1264.

Otto I (died 991) was the third son of Aleram, founder of the Aleramici dynasty, and a younger brother of Anselm of Savona. He first appears in 961, in the charter founding Grazzano Abbey.

After Aleram died around 969 the family march passed to Anselm; Otto is recorded beside him as marquis only in 991 and died in that same year. His short co-rule began the Ottonian branch from which the marquises of Montferrat descended.

He married Constance of Savoy, who bore him three sons. His long rule left little other record. Otto died in 1084 and was followed by his son William IV.

Rainier (1075–1137), son of Marquis William IV of Montferrat, ruled the marquisate from 1100. A charter of March 1111 names him Raynerius de Monteferrato Marchio, the first surviving document to call a lord of Montferrat marquis.

He founded the abbey of Santa Maria di Lucedio and steered his house toward the imperial court. In 1105 he married Gisela of Burgundy, and on his death in 1137 their only son succeeded him as William V.

en:
Theodore I Palaiologos (c. 1290–1338) was Marquis of Montferrat from 1306 and founder of its Palaiologan line. The second son of Emperor Andronikos II and Irene of Montferrat, he was born in Constantinople as a porphyrogennetos. When his uncle John I, last of the Aleramici marquises, died heirless in 1305, the march passed to Irene's children.

The patriarch of Constantinople blocked the claim of Theodore's elder brother John, so Theodore sailed to Genoa in 1306 and in 1307 married Argentina Spinola. Manfred IV of Saluzzo had occupied much of the march, and other rivals also wanted a share.

Backed by the Spinola and local supporters, Theodore won back the lost lands within a few years and in 1310 received investiture from Henry VII. He died in 1338, succeeded by his son John II.

泰奥多罗一世·巴列奥略（约1290—1338）自1306年起任蒙费拉托侯爵，是该侯国巴列奥略支系的开创者。他是拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡二世与蒙费拉托的伊琳娜的次子，生于君士坦丁堡，拥有“紫衣贵族”身份。1305年，舅舅、阿莱拉米奇家族末代侯爵约翰一世无嗣而终，侯国由伊琳娜的子女继承。

君士坦丁堡牧首阻止泰奥多罗的长兄约翰继承，泰奥多罗于1306年渡海前往热那亚，1307年与阿尔真蒂娜·斯皮诺拉成婚。萨卢佐的曼弗雷迪四世已占据侯国大部分土地，其他竞争者也想分一杯羹。

借助斯皮诺拉家族和本地支持者，泰奥多罗数年内收复失地，1310年获皇帝亨利七世册封。他于1338年去世，其子乔瓦尼二世继位。

As countess she bore Amadeus VI, later called the Green Count, and Bianca, who married Galeazzo II Visconti of Milan. She died at Chambéry in 1342 giving birth to her last child.

薇尔兰特·巴列奥洛加（1318年6月—1342年12月24日）又称维奥兰特，是蒙费拉托侯爵泰奥多罗一世·巴列奥略与热那亚贵妇阿尔真蒂娜·斯皮诺拉之女。1330年5月1日，她嫁给萨伏依伯爵艾蒙，为蒙费拉托与萨伏依之间新达成的和平缔约。

en:
Burchard III, also numbered Burchard IV, was Count of Mansfeld-Querfurt, the line founded when the lords of Querfurt inherited Mansfeld in 1229. He first appears as count in 1273, while still under age. Before 20 December 1286 he married Sophie of Lüchow.

In 1287 he held Seeburg Castle, and in 1301 he is named as lord of Bornstedt. His children included Burchard V, Oda and Albert. He died between 2 October 1310 and 28 October 1311.

en:
Burchard V was Count of Mansfeld from the Querfurt line, the son of Count Burchard IV and husband of Oda of Wernigerode. He is documented from 1291 and steadily built up his lordship at the foot of the Harz, holding Allstedt, Hedersleben, Schraplau and Helfta.

Of his many sons, Burchard VI succeeded him as count, Gebhard married Luitgard of Valkenstein in 1327, and Ruprecht served the Hospitallers as a commander. Burchard died between 1354 and 1358 and was buried at Eisleben.

Gebhard III of Mansfeld was a son of Count Burchard V of Mansfeld-Querfurt and Oda of Wernigerode, first documented in 1314. On 21 October 1327 he obtained a papal dispensation at Avignon to marry Luitgard of Valkenstein, who bore him two sons, Albert and Gebhard.

He died young, between November 1332 and June 1335, while his sons were still children. His son Albert was a count in 1353, and Gebhard followed as count in 1362.

en:
Hugh II (c. 1195 – 11 August 1260) was Count of Montfort in Swabia, of the house founded by the Counts Palatine of Tübingen. On his father Hugh I's death in 1228 he inherited with his brother Rudolf I and ruled the county from 1234.

He married Elizabeth of Burgau. Their sons divided the inheritance, founding the Montfort lines of Bregenz under Ulrich I, Feldkirch under Rudolf II and Tettnang under Hugh.

Rudolf IV of Montfort-Feldkirch was the fourth son of Count Hugo IV and Anna of Veringen. Left underage at his father's death in 1310, he grew up under the regency of his uncles, including Rudolf, bishop of Constance.

en:
Michel Le Tellier (1603–1685) was the French statesman who built Louis XIV's army. Born in Paris, he became maître des requêtes in 1631 and intendant of justice for the French army in Piedmont in 1640. Through Cardinal Mazarin's favour he became Secretary of State for War in 1643, remaining loyal to Mazarin through the Fronde.

Over three decades he and his son Louvois turned the royal armies into a disciplined professional force. As Chancellor from 1677 he strengthened royal authority over military appointments and discipline, and in 1679 restored the teaching of civil law at the University of Paris.

A fierce enemy of the Huguenots, he helped persuade the king to revoke the Edict of Nantes and died at Versailles in 1685, days after signing it.

米歇尔·勒泰利耶（1603—1685）是为路易十四打造新式军队的法国政治家。他生于巴黎，1631年出任审查官，1640年任驻皮埃蒙特法军司法总监。借马扎然枢机的赏识，他于1643年任战争大臣，在投石党之乱中始终效忠马扎然。

此后三十余年间，他与儿子卢福瓦侯爵把王室军队改造成纪律严明的职业化军队。1677年出任法国首席大法官后，他强化了国王对军官任免与军纪的掌控，并于1679年恢复巴黎大学的民法教学。

他敌视胡格诺派，力劝路易十四废除《南特敕令》，1685年在敕令签署十几天后于凡尔赛去世。

en:
Michelangelo (1475–1564) was a sculptor, painter, architect and poet of the High Renaissance, raised in Florence. Apprenticed at thirteen to Domenico Ghirlandaio, he studied from 1490 in the circle of Lorenzo de' Medici. In Rome he carved the Pietà, his only signed work, and in Florence finished the David in 1504, before turning thirty.

In 1505 Pope Julius II recalled him to Rome to build a tomb with forty statues. It followed him for forty years and gave the world the Moses. Julius then set him to paint the Sistine Chapel ceiling (1508–1512), over 300 figures.

For the Medici he built the Medici Chapel. After the Florentine republic fell in 1530 he was condemned to death and later pardoned. He painted The Last Judgment (1534–1541), and in 1546 took over St Peter's and designed its dome, completed after his death. He died in Rome in 1564.

米开朗基罗（1475—1564）是盛期文艺复兴的雕塑家、画家、建筑师和诗人，在佛罗伦萨长大。十三岁时他拜多梅尼科·吉兰达约为师，1490年起在洛伦佐·德·美第奇身边的圈子里学习。他在罗马雕成《哀悼基督》，这是他唯一签名的作品；1504年在佛罗伦萨完成《大卫》，当时还不到三十岁。

1505年教皇尤利乌斯二世把他召回罗马，建造一座有四十尊雕像的陵墓。这项工程跟了他四十年，留下了《摩西》。尤利乌斯随即命他绘制西斯廷礼拜堂天顶画（1508—1512），画面有300多个人物。

他为美第奇家族建造美第奇礼拜堂。1530年佛罗伦萨共和国倒台后，他被判死刑，后来获赦免。他绘制了《最后的审判》（1534—1541）；1546年他接手圣伯多禄大教堂，设计了在他身后完工的穹顶。1564年，他在罗马去世。

en:
Berengaria of Navarre (c. 1165–1170 – 23 December 1230), queen of England, was the eldest daughter of King Sancho VI of Navarre and Sancha of Castile. Eleanor of Aquitaine arranged her marriage to Richard the Lionheart. Berengaria joined Richard on the Third Crusade; when her ship was imperilled off Cyprus, he conquered the island and married her at Limassol on 12 May 1191.

The marriage was childless, she saw Richard little and lived mostly in his lands in France, never visiting England. As a widow she gave to the church, although she struggled to collect her pension from John.

纳瓦拉的贝伦加丽亚（约1165—1170年—1230年12月23日）是英格兰王后，纳瓦拉国王桑乔六世与卡斯蒂利亚的桑查的长女。阿基坦的埃莉诺促成了她与狮心王理查的婚事。贝伦加丽亚随理查参加第三次十字军东征；她的座船在塞浦路斯附近遇险，理查遂征服该岛，并于1191年5月12日在利马索尔与她成婚。

John I of Beaumont (c. 1253–1306), also called John of Brienne-Beaumont, was viscount of Beaumont in Maine and lord of Sainte-Suzanne. The son of Louis of Acre and Agnes of Beaumont, he inherited the viscounty on his mother's death around 1301 and kept her name of Beaumont rather than Brienne.

By his first wife Jeanne de la Guerche he fathered his heir Robert. He died in 1306 and was buried at Étival Abbey.

Louis of Brienne, called Louis of Acre (c. 1230–after 1285), was a younger son of John of Brienne, king of Jerusalem and Latin emperor of Constantinople, and Berengaria of León. As a boy he left Constantinople with his brothers for the court of their cousin Louis IX of France, whose crusade he joined in Egypt.

Around 1253 he married Agnes of Beaumont, heiress to the viscounty of Beaumont in Maine, holding Beaumont, Fresnay and Sainte-Suzanne in her right. His sons included his heir John, Henry de Beaumont, and Louis, bishop of Durham; his daughter Margaret married Bohemond VII of Tripoli.

The son of Jean II de Beaumont and #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('mie_margarida_poitiers').GetID],X #L Marguerite de Poitiers#!#!, he descended from #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('lat_jean_i_brienne').GetID],X #L John of Brienne#!#!, king of Jerusalem, and inherited his father's lands around 1355.

In May 1364 Charles V sent him with Bertrand du Guesclin against the Navarrese, and he fell at Cocherel on 23 May 1364 as the French won a decisive victory. His lands passed to his half-sister Marie.

路易二世·德·博蒙（1330年后生，1364年卒）是博蒙子爵，兼领曼恩的圣苏珊娜、勒吕德和拉弗莱什。他是让二世·德·博蒙与玛格丽特·德·普瓦捷之子，先祖为耶路撒冷国王布里耶纳的约翰，约1355年继承父亲的领地。

1364年5月，法王查理五世派他随贝特朗·杜·盖克兰征讨纳瓦拉派；5月23日，法军在科什雷勒取得决定性胜利，他却在此役阵亡。死后领地传给同父异母的姐姐玛丽。

en:
Robert of Beaumont, also called Robert of Brienne-Beaumont (after 1285 – 20 September 1327), was viscount of Beaumont in Maine and lord of Sainte-Suzanne. The son of John I of Beaumont and Jeanne de la Guerche, and a great-grandson of Emperor John of Brienne, he succeeded his father to the viscounty in 1306.

He died on 20 September 1327 and was probably buried at Étival Abbey beside his father. His eldest son John II succeeded him.

en:
Qutb al-Din Muhammad (died 1346) was the Mihrabanid malik of Sistan from December 1330, raised to power after his uncle Nusrat al-Din Muhammad died. A deeply religious man, he patronized Sistan's religious figures, fed travelers and the poor, and distributed its fortresses among his family.

The collapse of Ilkhanid rule spared Sistan most of the wars ravaging Persia, though a Kartid army invaded in 1333 at the bidding of his opponents before withdrawing. Qutb al-Din died of plague in 1346, and his son Taj al-Din succeeded him.

库特卜丁·穆罕默德（1346年卒）于1330年12月成为米赫拉班王朝的锡斯坦马利克，在叔父努斯拉特丁·穆罕默德死后被拥立继位。他笃信宗教，优待锡斯坦的宗教人士，赈济旅人和贫民，并把城堡分封给族人。

伊利汗国中央政权崩溃，使锡斯坦大体避开了肆虐波斯的战乱；只有一支卡尔提德军队应其政敌之请于1333年来侵，随后退兵。1346年库特卜丁死于瘟疫，其子塔吉丁继位。

Taj al-Din ibn Qutb al-Din (died 1351) was Mihrabanid malik of Sistan from 1346 to 1350. As his father's governor of the town of Uq, he succeeded in 1346 despite a rival claim by a cousin; he was well-intentioned but weak.

In 1350 a conspiracy in Shahr-i Sistan drove him out and enthroned Jalal al-Din Mahmud. Fleeing to Herat, he won Kartid malik Mu'izz al-Din Husayn's backing for his restoration, and in 1351 he fell defending Herat against a Chagatai coalition under Amir Qazaghan.

en:
Mikołaj Rej (1505–1569) was a Polish nobleman, politician and writer, the first major author to write entirely in Polish. After one year at the Kraków Academy he largely educated himself through Latin literature and served voivode Andrzej Tęczyński at Sandomierz from about 1524. In 1543 he made his name with the verse dialogue A Brief Discussion between a Lord, a Bailiff and a Priest.

A convert to Calvinism in 1541 or 1548, he attended synods, founded Protestant schools and communities on his lands, and sat in the sejms. He founded Rejowiec in 1547 and died there in 1569, remembered as a father of Polish literature.

米科瓦伊·芮伊（1505—1569）是波兰贵族、政治家和作家，也是第一位完全以波兰语写作的重要作家。他在克拉科夫学院只读了一年，之后主要通过研读拉丁文学自学，约1524年起在桑多梅日为总督安杰伊·滕琴斯基效力。1543年，他以诗体对话《地主、村长与神父的短论》一举成名。

他于1541年或1548年皈依加尔文宗，出席宗教会议，在自己的领地上创办新教学校和教会，参加各级瑟姆。1547年他兴建雷伊奥维茨城，1569年在那里去世，被视为波兰文学之父。
