en:
Anne Robert Jacques Turgot (1727–1781) was a French economist and Controller-General of Finances to Louis XVI. After serving in the Parlement of Paris, he met the economists Quesnay and Vincent de Gournay, and in 1754 wrote in support of religious tolerance. He spent thirteen years as intendant of Limoges from 1761, reforming the land tax and writing his Reflections on the Formation and Distribution of Wealth.

In 1774 he became navy minister and then controller-general. He freed the grain trade, and in 1776 issued the Six Edicts abolishing the royal corvée and the guilds. Aristocratic and parlementary opposition forced his dismissal in 1776; he died in Paris in 1781.

安·罗伯特·雅克·杜尔哥（1727—1781）是法国经济学家、法王路易十六的财政总监。他早年在巴黎高等法院任职，结识了经济学家魁奈和樊尚·德·古尔奈，1754年撰文支持宗教宽容。1761年他出任利摩日总督，在任十三年间改革土地税，并写下《关于财富的形成和分配的考察》。

1774年他先任海军大臣，旋即改任财政总监，放开谷物贸易；1776年颁布六项敕令，废除王室徭役和行会制度。贵族与高等法院群起反对，他于1776年被迫去职，1781年在巴黎去世。

en:
Gleb Vseslavich (died September 13, 1119), a son of Vseslav of Polotsk, received Minsk when the Polotsk lands were divided in 1101 and founded the Minsk line of the Rurikids. In 1104 his Minsk withstood a siege by Monomakh's allies.

After he burned Slutsk in 1116, Vladimir Monomakh took Orsha and Drutsk and forced terms on him. Gleb resumed war in 1119, was captured by Mstislav, and died a prisoner in Kiev that September.

Rostislav Glebovich (died 1165) succeeded his father Gleb Vseslavich as prince of Minsk in 1146. In 1151 the Polotsk citizens expelled Rogvolod Borisovich and invited Rostislav, who left Minsk to his brother Volodar.

In 1158 Rogvolod seized Drutsk and drove out Rostislav's son Gleb, then returned to Polotsk; he made peace with Rostislav after a ten-day siege of Minsk. The war over Drutsk and Iziaslavl dragged on until 1161, and Rostislav died holding Minsk in 1165.

罗斯季斯拉夫·格列波维奇（？—1165）是明斯克王公格列布·弗谢斯拉维奇之子，1146年袭任明斯克王公。1151年，波洛茨克人驱逐罗格沃洛德·鲍里索维奇，迎立罗斯季斯拉夫，他把明斯克交给弟弟沃洛达里。

1158年罗格沃洛德夺取德鲁茨克，逐走罗斯季斯拉夫之子格列布，随后重返波洛茨克；他围攻明斯克十日不克，与罗斯季斯拉夫议和。此后围绕德鲁茨克与伊贾斯拉夫尔的战事一直持续到1161年。1165年，罗斯季斯拉夫卒于明斯克任上。

en:
Vladimir of Polotsk (c. 1140s–1216) ruled the city from about 1184; Henry of Livonia's chronicle styles him the great king of Polotsk. In 1203 he invaded Livonia and forced the Livs to resume tribute before defeat at Holme.

In 1212 he recognized Bishop Albert's rule in exchange for free trade on the Dvina. In 1216 the Estonians called him to march on Riga, but he died suddenly aboard ship.

Volodar Glebovich (c. 1090s–after 1167), son of Gleb Vseslavich, took Minsk in 1151 when his brother Rostislav moved to Polotsk, and was prince of Minsk again from 1165.

Around 1135 he married Richeza of Poland, daughter of Boleslaw III and widow of Magnus the Strong; the marriage soon ended in divorce, and their daughter Sophia married Valdemar I of Denmark. In 1167 he defeated Vseslav Vasilkovich and briefly held the Polotsk throne.

en:
Albert II of Mecklenburg (c. 1318 – 18 February 1379), born in Schwerin, was a son of Henry II the Lion and Anna of Saxe-Wittenberg, succeeding his father as Lord of Mecklenburg in 1329. In 1336 he married Euphemia, granddaughter of King Haakon V of Norway, through whom he gained estates in Sweden.

In 1348 Emperor Charles IV raised Mecklenburg to a duchy, making Albert and his younger brother John its first dukes. When Swedish nobles turned on his brother-in-law, King Magnus IV, Albert put forward his own son Albert as their candidate, meaning to rule through him; the younger Albert deposed Magnus.

He also married his eldest son Henry to the eldest daughter of Valdemar IV of Denmark and offered their infant son as heir to Denmark in vain. The Swedes called him the Fox of Mecklenburg for his scheming and avarice, and he died in 1379.

阿尔布雷希特二世（约1318—1379年2月18日）生于什未林，是“狮子”海因里希二世与萨克森-维滕贝格的安娜之子，1329年继父之位成为梅克伦堡领主。1336年他娶欧菲米亚——挪威国王哈康五世的外孙女，借此在瑞典获得产业。

1348年，皇帝查理四世将梅克伦堡升格为公国，他与弟弟约翰成为首任公爵。瑞典贵族与他的妻兄国王马格努斯四世反目时，他推出同名的儿子阿尔布雷希特作为贵族一方的人选，打算幕后掌权；小阿尔布雷希特后来废黜了马格努斯。

他还安排长子海因里希娶丹麦国王瓦尔德马四世的长女，并把两人的幼子推举为丹麦继承人，未能如愿。瑞典人因他的算计与贪婪，称他为“梅克伦堡的狐狸”；他于1379年去世。

en:
Anna of Saxe-Wittenberg (c. 1290–1327) was a German noblewoman of the House of Ascania, the daughter of Duke Albert II of Saxony and Agnes of Austria, herself a daughter of King Rudolf I of Germany. On 6 July 1315 she married Henry II the Lion, Lord of Mecklenburg, as his second wife.

Her children included Albert II the Great, the first Duke of Mecklenburg, and John I of Mecklenburg-Stargard. She died in November 1327.

en:
Beatrix of Mecklenburg, also called Beate (1324 – 5 August 1399), was the youngest daughter of Henry II the Lion and Anna of Saxe-Wittenberg. In March 1325 she was betrothed to Jaromar, only son of Prince Wizlaw III of Rügen. Jaromar died that May and Wizlaw in November, ending the princely house of Rügen.

She was instead given to the Poor Clare convent her father had founded at Ribnitz, taking the habit there aged five in 1329. On 20 May 1349, with a papal dispensation for her youth, she was elected abbess, the first princely abbess of Ribnitz.

The convent church was built in her lifetime, and its chronicle praises her piety and charity. She resigned through illness in 1398 and is venerated as a Blessed.

zh:
梅克伦堡的贝娅特丽克丝，又名贝娅特（1324—1399年8月5日），是“狮子”海因里希二世与萨克森-维滕贝格的安娜最小的女儿。1325年3月，她与吕根亲王维斯拉夫三世的独子雅罗马订亲；雅罗马当年5月去世，维斯拉夫也在11月去世，吕根亲王家族遂告绝嗣。

她改而被送进父亲在里布尼茨创办的贫穷修女会修道院，1329年年仅五岁便在那里穿上会衣。1349年5月20日，教廷因她年轻特准，她当选为院长，成为里布尼茨第一位出身诸侯家的女院长。

修院教堂建于她生前，院史称颂她虔诚、乐善好施。她于1398年因病辞职，被天主教会尊为真福者。

Elizabeth of Mecklenburg was one of the three documented children of John II, Lord of Mecklenburg, alongside a sister Luitgard and a brother John who died young.

She entered Rehna Abbey in Mecklenburg, in her day a house of Premonstratensian canonesses regular, and the abbey's list of prioresses records her in office from 1352 to 1359, where all trace of her ends.

en:
Euphemia Eriksdotter (c. 1317–1363/1370) was a Swedish princess, daughter of Duke Eric Magnusson of Södermanland and Ingeborg of Norway, and younger sister of King Magnus Eriksson. She married Albert II of Mecklenburg at Rostock in 1336, becoming duchess consort.

She kept real political weight in Sweden, and in 1340–1341 persuaded Magnus to renew Norwegian trading privileges for Rostock and Wismar. In 1357 she gave estates to Skänninge Abbey, and her son Albert became king of Sweden in 1364.

欧菲米亚·埃里克斯多塔（约1317—1363/1370）是瑞典公主，南曼兰公爵埃里克·马格努松与挪威的英格堡格之女，瑞典国王马格努斯·埃里克松之妹。1336年她在罗斯托克与梅克伦堡的阿尔布雷希特二世成婚，成为公爵夫人。

en:
Henry Borwin I (c. 1150–1227) ruled as Lord of Mecklenburg from 1178, succeeding his father Pribislav after his tournament death at Lüneburg, and married Matilda, daughter of Henry the Lion. From 1183 to 1185 he warred on his cousin Nicholas I; King Canute VI of Denmark captured him and forced him to cede Rostock and accept Canute as his liege, though Rostock returned to him as a Danish fief in 1200.

He fought for Denmark at the Battle of Stellau and received Gadebusch. He refounded Rostock and Wismar and founded Dobbertin Abbey.

海因里希·鲍尔温一世（约1150—1227年）自1178年起任梅克伦堡领主。父亲普里比斯拉夫在吕讷堡的比武中伤死后他继任，并娶狮子亨利之女玛蒂尔德为妻。1183至1185年他与堂兄尼古劳斯一世交战，丹麦国王克努特六世乘机将他俘获，迫使他割让罗斯托克并承认克努特为宗主；1200年罗斯托克作为丹麦封邑归还给他。

他站在丹麦一方参加施特劳战役，获得加德布施作封邑。他重建罗斯托克和维斯马，创立多贝尔廷修道院，1227年去世。

en:
Henry Borwin II (c. 1170–5 June 1226) of the Nikloting dynasty ruled Mecklenburg from 1219 and added Rostock in 1225. The son of Henry Borwin I, he backed Count Henry I of Schwerin against King Valdemar II of Denmark; victory at Mölln in 1225 and the Treaty of Bardowick freed Mecklenburg from Danish overlordship.

In 1200 he married Christina, said to be a daughter of King Sverker II of Sweden. He died at Güstrow in 1226, leaving four sons who in 1234 divided Mecklenburg into Werle, Parchim-Richenberg, Rostock and Mecklenburg.

海因里希·鲍尔温二世（约1170—1226年6月5日）是尼克洛特家族的王公，1219年起统治梅克伦堡，1225年又领有罗斯托克。他是海因里希·鲍尔温一世之子，曾支持什未林伯爵海因里希一世对抗丹麦国王瓦尔德马二世；1225年默尔恩之战获胜后，借《巴多维克条约》使梅克伦堡摆脱了丹麦的宗主权。

en:
Henry I of Mecklenburg, called the Pilgrim (c. 1230 – 2 January 1302), was the eldest son of John I the Theologian and ruled Mecklenburg from 1264.

In 1270 he crusaded against pagan Lithuania, and in 1271 he went on pilgrimage to the Holy Land, only to be captured and held by the Mamluks in Cairo for 27 years. His brothers John II and Nicholas III ruled as regents after a dispute with their cousins over the guardianship of his children.

He returned via Morea and Rome in 1298, resumed power in 1299 but left government to his son Henry II, and died in 1302, buried at Doberan Minster.

en:
Henry II of Mecklenburg, called the Lion (after 14 April 1266 – 21 January 1329), was the son of Henry I the Pilgrim and ruled Mecklenburg from 1302, after regency years during his father's captivity. Around 1299 he acquired Stargard from his father-in-law Albert III. In 1304 he fought for King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia against Emperor Albert I, earning his nickname.

He fought Wismar and Rostock, taking Rostock in 1312. When Brandenburg reclaimed Stargard, Henry defeated Margrave Waldemar at Gransee in 1316 and secured it in the Treaty of Templin in 1317. He died in 1329.

en:
Henry III (c. 1337–1383) was the eldest son of Duke Albert II of Mecklenburg and Euphemia of Sweden, and the heir to his father's Scandinavian ambitions. In 1362 he married Ingeborg, eldest daughter and potential heiress of King Valdemar IV of Denmark.

Their infant son was offered, unsuccessfully, as heir to Denmark against Valdemar's youngest daughter Margaret. After Ingeborg's death Henry married Matilda of Werle in 1377, and in 1379 he succeeded his father as duke of Mecklenburg.

He died at Schwerin on 24 April 1383 from a tournament accident at Wismar; his brother Magnus I and his son Albert IV took up joint rule.

en:
John I of Mecklenburg, called the Theologian (c. 1211 – 1 August 1264), was the eldest son of Henry Borwin II and ruled as Lord of Mecklenburg from 1234. He fought at Bornhöved in 1227, where the Danish defeat freed his land from Danish suzerainty.

He had ruled jointly with his brothers before the division of 1234, when he kept the ancestral lands. In 1255, after his brother Pribislaw I lost his lordship, John received Sternberg in the ensuing division.

He promoted the Church and German settlement in Mecklenburg, where Slavs still predominated, and in 1262 allied with the Guelphs against Denmark. He was buried in Doberan Minster.

He fought at Bornhöved in 1227, where the Danish defeat freed his land from Danish suzerainty.

He had ruled jointly with his brothers before the division of 1234, when he kept the ancestral lands. In 1255, after his brother Pribislaw I lost his lordship, John received [ShowLocationName('torzym')] in the ensuing division.

He promoted the Church and German settlement in Mecklenburg, where Slavs still predominated, and in 1262 allied with the Guelphs against [GetCountry('DAN').GetName]. He was buried in Doberan Minster.
zh:
约翰一世（约1211—1264年8月1日），绰号“神学家”，是海因里希·鲍尔温二世的长子，1234年起任梅克伦堡领主。1227年他参加博恩赫费德战役，丹麦战败使梅克伦堡摆脱了丹麦的宗主权。

他原与诸弟共同统治，1234年分家时保留祖业。1255年弟弟普里比斯拉夫一世失去领地后，约翰在随后的分割中得到施滕贝格。

他扶持教会、鼓励德意志人移居，当时梅克伦堡仍以斯拉夫人为主；1262年他与韦尔夫家族结盟对抗丹麦，死后葬于多伯兰大教堂。

en:
John I of Mecklenburg-Stargard (1326 – 1392/93) was the youngest son of Henry II the Lion and Anna of Saxe-Wittenberg. His father died in 1329, and John remained under guardianship until 1344. In 1348 Emperor Charles IV raised him and his brother Albert II to ducal rank.

The brothers first backed the False Waldemar against Margrave Louis V of Bavaria, making peace in 1350 when the emperor withdrew his support. In the division of Mecklenburg on 25 November 1352 John received Stargard and Sternberg, founding the Mecklenburg-Stargard line.

He backed his nephew Albert III's bid for the Swedish throne. By February 1393 his sons John II and Ulrich I were ruling in his place.

zh:
约翰一世（1326—1392/1393年）是“狮子”海因里希二世与萨克森-维滕贝格的安娜最小的儿子。父亲1329年去世，他受监护直到1344年。1348年，皇帝查理四世将他与哥哥阿尔布雷希特二世一同升为公爵。

兄弟二人起初支持“假瓦尔德马”，对抗巴伐利亚藩侯路德维希五世；1350年皇帝撤回支持后，他们与路德维希和解。1352年11月25日梅克伦堡分家，他分得施塔加德和施滕贝格，开创梅克伦堡-施塔加德支系。

他支持侄子阿尔布雷希特三世争取瑞典王位。1393年2月前，他的儿子约翰二世和乌尔里希一世已接位统治。

en:
John II (c. 1250–1299) was the youngest son of John I of Mecklenburg. After his father died he ruled Mecklenburg from 1264 jointly with his brothers.

When his elder brother Henry I was taken captive while on pilgrimage in 1275, John and his brother Nicholas III took over the regency and the guardianship of Henry's sons. From 1283 he is recorded as lord of Gadebusch, probably his apanage. John died on 12 October 1299.

约翰二世（约1250—1299）是梅克伦堡领主约翰一世的幼子。父亲去世后，他自1264年起与诸兄弟共同统治梅克伦堡。

1275年兄长海因里希一世在朝圣途中被俘，约翰遂与兄弟尼古拉斯三世共同摄政，监护海因里希诸子。1283年起，史料称他为加德布施领主，该地可能是他分得的封邑。约翰于1299年10月12日去世。

en:
John III (after 1266–1289) was a son of Henry I of Mecklenburg and Anastasia of Pomerania. From 1287 he ruled Mecklenburg jointly with his elder brother Henry II, while their uncle Nicholas III acted as regent. On 3 November 1288 he married Helena, daughter of Wizlaw II of Rügen.

His rule was short. On 27 May 1289 he drowned off the island of Poel and was buried in the Franciscan monastery at Wismar.

en:
Niklot (c. 1090 – August 1160) was a pagan prince of the Slavic Obotrites, ruling their confederacy from 1130/1131 as lord of Schwerin. He resisted Saxon princes for nearly thirty years. After the Wendish Crusade of 1147 he became a tributary vassal of Henry the Lion, in whose service he crushed a tribal rising in 1151.

In 1160 Henry and Valdemar the Great of Denmark attacked him, and Niklot was killed at Burg Werle. His death ended Slavic rule in Mecklenburg; he was ancestor of the House of Mecklenburg.

zh:
尼克洛特（约1090—1160年8月）是斯拉夫奥博特人的异教首领，1130至1131年间成为奥博特里特部落联盟的首领，领有什未林。他在近三十年里抵抗撒克逊诸侯，1147年文德十字军东征后沦为狮子亨利的纳贡附庸，1151年为其镇压部落起义。

1160年，狮子亨利与丹麦国王瓦尔德马一世联手进攻，尼克洛特在维尔勒城堡被杀。他的死终结了梅克伦堡的斯拉夫人统治；他是梅克伦堡家族的先祖。

en:
Nicholas I, Lord of Mecklenburg (died 25 May 1200), was a son of Wertislaw, Obotrite prince of Rostock, and governed Mecklenburg from 1178. Between 1183 and 1185 he warred against his cousin Henry Borwin I with Danish backing; in 1185 both cousins had to acknowledge King Canute VI of Denmark as their liege lord, who enfeoffed Nicholas with Rostock. He also campaigned with the Danes and Emperor Frederick I against Henry the Lion.

At Waschow in May 1200 the Mecklenburgers defeated Count Adolf III of Holstein, securing southwestern Mecklenburg, but Nicholas fell in the battle.

尼古拉斯一世（？—1200年5月25日）是罗斯托克的奥博德里特王公弗拉季斯拉夫之子，自1178年起统治梅克伦堡。1183至1185年间，他在丹麦支持下与堂亲海因里希·鲍尔温一世交战；1185年，两人被迫承认丹麦国王克努特六世为宗主，克努特随即将罗斯托克封给尼古拉斯。他还曾随丹麦人与皇帝腓特烈一世讨伐狮子亨利。

1200年5月，梅克伦堡军队在瓦绍击败荷尔斯泰因伯爵阿道夫三世，巩固了梅克伦堡西南部，但尼古拉斯一世战死阵中。

en:
Nicholas III of Mecklenburg (after 1230 – 8 June 1289 or 1290) was a younger son of John I the Theologian and an ecclesiastic: in 1266 he became canon of Lübeck Cathedral and from 1269 served as a priest in Wismar.

When his brother Henry I the Pilgrim was captured on pilgrimage, Nicholas and his brother John II acted as regents for Henry's underage sons. He is last attested in 1289.

en:
Pribislav (c. 1132 – 30 December 1178), son of the Obotrite prince Niklot, was the first Prince of Mecklenburg. After Niklot fell in 1160, he and his brother Wertislav led the revolt of 1163 against Henry the Lion; defeated at Verchen in 1164, with Wertislav hanged, Pribislav fled to Pomerania.

A Cistercian monk persuaded him to side with the Christians, and in 1167 Henry restored him as Prince of Mecklenburg, founding a dynasty that ruled until 1918. He died in 1178 of wounds from a tournament at Lüneburg, succeeded by his son Henry Borwin I.

梅克伦堡的普里比斯拉夫（约1132—1178年12月30日）是奥博特里特王公尼克洛特之子，也是第一任梅克伦堡亲王。1160年尼克洛特战死后，他与兄弟弗拉季斯拉夫于1163年起兵反抗狮子亨利；1164年在费尔兴战败，弗拉季斯拉夫被绞死，普里比斯拉夫逃奔波美拉尼亚。

一位西多会修士劝他与基督徒结盟，1167年狮子亨利恢复他的地位，封他为梅克伦堡亲王，由此开创的王朝一直延续到1918年。1178年他在吕讷堡的一次比武中因伤而死，其子海因里希·鲍尔温一世继立。

en:
Wertislaw (c. 1130 – May or June 1164) was a son of the Obotrite prince Niklot and brother of Prince Pribislav. After Niklot was killed fighting Henry the Lion in 1160, the brothers waged a guerrilla war from Pomerania against the German vassals installed in the Obotrite lands. Defending Burg Werle in 1163, he was captured by Henry's troops.

When Pribislav renewed the revolt in summer 1164, Henry had Wertislaw hanged near Malchow. His son Nicholas I later became Lord of Mecklenburg.

en:
Hualani, whose name means “heavenly fruit,” was in Hawaiian tradition a ruling high chiefess of Molokaʻi. She was the daughter of Chiefess Kamauliwahine and Laniaiku, and genealogies trace her line back to the voyager chief Maweke, giving her both Molokaʻi and Oʻahu descent.

Tradition relates that Kanipahu, a Pili-line chief of Hawaiʻi Island who ruled until c. 1245, was living concealed on Molokaʻi when Hualani learned his rank and took him as her husband. Their son was Kalahumoku I, ancestor of later Molokaʻi chiefs.

en:
Kamauaua was, in Hawaiian chants and genealogies, the first named high chief of Molokaʻi, though tradition notes that he was probably not the island's first ruler. His wife was the chiefess Hinakeha, who bore him four sons: Kaupeʻepeʻe-nui-kauila, Keʻoloʻewa, Haili and Uli-hala-nui.

The eldest son refused the rule, so Keʻoloʻewa succeeded him. His line later gave Molokaʻi three ruling chiefesses, Kapau-a-Nuʻakea, Kamauliwahine and Hualani, who married the Hawaiʻi Island chief Kanipahu, ruler until c. 1245.

en:
Kamauliwahine, whose name means “woman,” was a ruling chiefess of Molokaʻi in Hawaiian tradition. She was the only recorded child of Lanileo and the chiefess Kapau-a-Nuʻakea, whom she succeeded as aliʻi nui, or supreme chief, of the island.

Her partner was Laniaiku, and their daughter Hualani inherited the rule after her death. Hualani married Kanipahu, a Hawaiʻi Island chief of the Pili line whose reign ended c. 1245.

Kapau-a-Nuʻakea, whose name means “Kapau child of Nuʻakea,” was in Hawaiian genealogies a ruling chiefess of Molokaʻi. She was the only recorded child of High Chief Keʻoloʻewa and his Oʻahu-born wife Nuʻakea.

en:
Nuʻakea was, in Hawaiian tradition, a high chiefess born on Oʻahu, the daughter of Keaunui of ʻEwa and granddaughter of the Tahitian-born wizard chief Māweke, whom chants place in the eleventh century. She was named after the goddess of milk and lactation.

She went to Molokaʻi and married its high chief Keʻoloʻewa, bearing his successor Kapau-a-Nuʻakea. The scholar Martha Beckwith held that the historical chiefess was later deified as the goddess Nuʻakea. Her great-granddaughter Hualani married the Hawaiʻi Island chief Kanipahu, ruler until c. 1245.

据夏威夷传说，努阿凯阿是出生于瓦胡的高阶女酋长，父亲是埃瓦的凯亚乌努伊，祖父是出生于塔希提、擅行法术的酋长马韦凯——歌谣称马韦凯生活在11世纪。她的名字取自司掌乳汁与哺乳的女神。

后来她前往莫洛凯，嫁给当地高阶酋长凯奥洛埃瓦，生下继位者卡帕乌阿努阿凯阿。学者玛莎·贝克威思认为，这位真实存在过的女酋长后来被神化为女神努阿凯阿。她的曾孙女华拉妮嫁给了统治至约1245年的夏威夷岛酋长卡尼帕胡。

en:
Abraham Cresques (1325–1387) was a Jewish cartographer born in Palma, the leading master of the Majorcan cartographic school. Besides maps he made clocks, compasses and other nautical instruments.

Together with his son Jehuda Cresques he produced the Catalan Atlas in 1375, a set of chart-tablets commissioned by the Crown of Aragon and one of the most celebrated mappae mundi of the later Middle Ages, blending Mediterranean portolan knowledge with reports from Asia and Africa.

zh:
亚伯拉罕·克雷斯克斯（1325—1387）是生于帕尔马的犹太地图学家，马略卡制图学派的核心大师。除绘制地图外，他还制作时钟、罗盘等航海仪器。

1375年，他与儿子耶胡达·克雷斯克斯合作完成《加泰罗尼亚地图集》。这套受阿拉贡王室委托绘制的挂图是中世纪晚期最负盛名的世界地图之一，将地中海波托兰海图的传统与来自亚洲、非洲的见闻融为一体。

en:
Constance of Aragon (1318–1346) was the eldest daughter of King Alfonso IV of Aragon and Teresa d'Entença, and sister of Peter IV. To seal friendship with Aragon, King James III of Majorca married her at Perpignan in September 1336.

When James refused fealty to her brother in 1342, Peter IV invaded and in the war of 1343–1344 drove James from Majorca and annexed the Balearic Islands. Mother of the pretender James IV, she died in exile at Montpellier in 1346.

康斯坦丝（1318—1346）是阿拉贡国王阿方索四世与特蕾莎·德·恩滕萨的长女，佩德罗四世的姐姐。为与阿拉贡修好，马略卡国王海梅三世于1336年9月在佩皮尼昂与她成婚。

1342年海梅拒绝向她的弟弟宣誓效忠，佩德罗四世遂发兵入侵，在1343—1344年的战争中将海梅逐出马略卡，吞并巴利阿里群岛。她是王位觊觎者海梅四世的母亲，1346年在流亡中死于蒙彼利埃。

en:
Esclaramunda of Foix (c. 1255–1315) was queen consort of Majorca, wife of James II. Daughter of Count Roger IV of Foix, she married the infante James, younger son of James I of Aragon, at Perpignan in October 1275. When James inherited Majorca in 1276, she became queen and bore six children, including Sancho, James II's successor.

She tutored her grandson James III and protected the Order of Mercy. She died at Perpignan in 1315, five years after her husband.

en:
Ferdinand of Majorca (1278–1316), born at Perpignan, was the third son of King James II and Viscount of Aumelas from 1311. Frederick III of Sicily sent him to command the Catalan Company, but its leader rebuffed him, and Venetians captured him on his return.

Through his wife Isabella of Sabran he claimed Achaea, seizing Clarenza in June 1315. His rival Matilda of Hainaut returned with Venetian and Burgundian forces, and Ferdinand was killed at the Battle of Manolada on 5 July 1316. His son by Isabella became King James III of Majorca.

费尔南多·德·马略卡（1278—1316）生于佩皮尼昂，是马略卡国王海梅二世的第三子，1311年起任欧梅拉斯子爵。西西里国王腓特烈三世派他统率加泰罗尼亚佣兵团，却遭佣兵团首领拒绝；他在归途中被威尼斯人俘虏。

他娶伊莎贝拉·德·萨布朗为妻，借此主张亚该亚亲王国的继承权，于1315年6月攻占克拉伦扎。竞争对手埃诺的玛蒂尔达带着威尼斯和勃艮第援军返回，1316年7月5日，费尔南多在马诺拉达战役中阵亡。他与伊莎贝拉的儿子后来成为马略卡国王海梅三世。

en:
Ferdinand the Younger (1316–1342) was born in Nicosia, Cyprus, a posthumous son. His father, Infante Ferdinand of Majorca, had been killed at Manolada while trying to settle in Achaea. He grew up at the Angevin court of Naples under his aunt Sancha, so steeped in Franciscan ideals that he took some vows.

King Sancho's will made him heir to the Majorcan crown after his half-brother James III, who granted him an income in 1326, later replaced by the viscounty of Aumelas.

About 1338 he married Esquiva of Lusignan, and they had a daughter, Alicia. His relations with his father-in-law deteriorated, and in 1341 he was imprisoned; only papal intervention freed him. He returned alone to Majorca and died there in 1342.

小费尔南多（1316—1342）生于塞浦路斯尼科西亚，是遗腹子：父亲马略卡王子费尔南多为在亚该亚立足，战死于马诺拉达。他在那不勒斯的安茹宫廷由姑母桑查抚养长大，深受方济各会理想影响，以至发过部分修道誓愿。

按国王桑乔的遗嘱，他是继异母兄海梅三世之后的马略卡王位继承人；海梅于1326年赐他年金，后来改封欧梅拉斯子爵领。

约1338年，他娶埃斯基瓦·德·吕西尼昂，两人有一女阿莉西亚。他与岳父的关系恶化，1341年被囚禁，经教皇斡旋才得以脱身。他独自返回马略卡，1342年在当地去世。

Isabella de Sabran (1297 – 7 May 1315) was the daughter of Isnard de Sabran and Margaret of Villehardouin, heiress to the Principality of Achaea. In 1314 she married Ferdinand of Majorca, a son of King James II; her mother made over to the couple her claim to Achaea.

She gave birth to James III of Majorca on 5 April 1315 at Catania and died a month later. Ferdinand took up the Achaean claim in the name of their infant son.

en:
Isabella of Ibelin (1300–after 1342) was a Cypriot noblewoman, daughter of Philip of Ibelin, seneschal of Cyprus, and Maria Embriaco. In October 1315 she married by proxy Ferdinand of Majorca, claimant to the Principality of Achaea, and the wedding in person followed at Glarentza in the Morea the next year. Weeks later Ferdinand was defeated and beheaded after the Battle of Manolada.

Returning to Cyprus widowed, she married the titular Count of Jaffa, Hugh of Ibelin, in 1320. She was later accused of sorcery by King Hugh IV.

en:
James II of Majorca (1243–1311), second son of James I of Aragon, inherited Mallorca, Ibiza and Formentera with Roussillon, Cerdanya and Montpellier in 1276. By the 1279 Treaty of Perpignan he became a vassal of the Crown of Aragon.

France and Aragon contested Sicily, and James made an agreement with France. After he sided with France against his nephew Alfonso III, the Balearics were annexed but restored under the 1295 Treaty of Anagni.

He then reformed the currency and economy and built Bellver Castle and Palma Cathedral. He was succeeded in 1311 by his son Sancho.

马略卡国王海梅二世（1243—1311）是阿拉贡国王海梅一世的次子，1276年继承马略卡、伊维萨和福门特拉，以及鲁西永、塞尔达尼亚和蒙彼利埃。1279年他据《佩皮尼昂条约》承认自己是阿拉贡王室的封臣。

法国与阿拉贡争夺西西里时，海梅与法国达成协议。他曾联法对抗外甥阿方索三世，巴利阿里群岛一度被吞并，1295年凭《阿纳尼条约》收复。

此后他改革币制与经济，修建贝尔韦尔城堡和帕尔马主教座堂，1311年由儿子桑乔继位。

en:
James III of Majorca (1315–1349), called the Rash, was born at Catania. His father Ferdinand was killed at Manolada in 1316 trying to seize Achaea from the Angevins, and his mother Isabella of Sabran died soon after the birth; the orphan was declared Prince of Achaea. In 1324 he succeeded his uncle Sancho as King of Majorca.

Majorcan kings swore fealty to Aragon, but James argued that no king could hold authority over another, and jurists of Montpellier backed him. In 1337 he issued the Leges palatinae, the first code of its kind for a royal court.

In 1342 he refused fealty to his cousin Peter IV of Aragon, who conquered Majorca in 1344. James died at the Battle of Llucmajor on 25 October 1349, trying to recover it.

海梅三世，绰号“鲁莽者”（1315—1349），生于卡塔尼亚。1316年，父亲费尔南多为从安茹家族手中夺取亚该亚，在马诺拉达战死；母亲伊莎贝拉·德·萨布朗在他出生后不久也已去世，孤儿被宣布为亚该亚亲王。1324年，他继叔父桑乔之后成为马略卡国王。

马略卡国王历来要向阿拉贡国王宣誓效忠，海梅却主张国王不应受另一位国王管辖，蒙彼利埃的法学者为他辩护。1337年，他颁布《宫廷法》，这是同类宫廷法典中的首创。

James IV of Majorca (c. 1336 – 20 January 1375) was the son of James III and Constance of Aragon. After his father fell at Llucmajor in 1349 trying to reconquer the island, James was captured by his uncle Peter IV of Aragon and caged in Barcelona until 1362.

Escaping to Naples, he married Queen Joanna I in 1363 as king consort without power. He fought for the Black Prince at Nájera and twice attacked Roussillon, dying defeated at Soria in 1375; his claim passed to his sister Isabella.

en:
Sancho I (c. 1277 – 4 September 1324), called the Pacific, was King of Majorca from 1311 until his death. Succeeding his father James II, he kept the realm at peace. His marriage was childless, and in 1322 he made a will settling the crown on his nephew James, son of his late brother Ferdinand, and set up a regency council, forestalling annexation by Aragon.

He aided James II of Aragon's conquest of Sardinia. He spent time in the uplands because of his asthma and died at Formiguères in 1324.

en:
Albert Azzo II (1009–1097), Margrave of Milan and Liguria, was a powerful nobleman in the Holy Roman Empire. From around 1029 he enlarged his inherited estates in northern Italy.

Around 1073 he made the castle of Este his residence, giving the House of Este its name; before his building project Este had been little more than a village. In the Investiture Controversy he first mediated between Henry IV and Pope Gregory VII, then sided with the pope.

His son by Kunigunde of Altdorf, Welf I of Bavaria, founded the Guelph line; Fulco I, his son by Garsende of Maine, began the Italian branch. Azzo died in 1097, aged 88.

约1073年，他将埃斯泰城堡定为居所，埃斯特家族由此得名；在他的建造工程之前，埃斯泰不过是个小村庄。主教叙任权之争期间，他先试图在皇帝亨利四世与教皇格列高利七世之间调停，后转而支持教皇。

en:
Azzo V d'Este (1125–1193) was an Italian nobleman, the son of Margrave Obizzo I. In 1176 he married Marchesella Adelardi, heiress of the Adelardi, the leading Guelph family of Ferrara; the marriage brought the Este large estates and leadership of its Guelph party, opening the road to the later Este lordship of Ferrara.

He died prematurely in 1193, shortly before Obizzo I, so he never reigned. The succession passed to his son Azzo VI.

阿佐五世·德斯特（1125—1193）是意大利贵族，藩侯奥皮佐一世之子。1176年，他娶费拉拉首要圭尔夫家族阿德拉尔迪家的女继承人马尔凯塞拉·阿德拉尔迪为妻；这场婚姻为埃斯特家族带来费拉拉的大片地产和当地圭尔夫派的领导权，为日后统治费拉拉铺平了道路。

他于1193年先于父亲早逝，终未继位。家族由其子阿佐六世继承。

en:
Azzone Visconti (7 December 1302 – 16 August 1339) was born at Ferrara, where his parents Galeazzo I and Beatrice d'Este had taken refuge after the Torriani drove his grandfather Matteo out of Milan; he was their only legitimate son.

After King Louis IV jailed the family in Monza castle in 1327, he sold Azzone the imperial vicariate of Milan in 1329 for sixty thousand florins. Azzone fortified the city against Louis' return; after his uncle Marco, who coveted the lordship, was found dead, the council in 1330 made him lord of Milan for life.

He rebuilt Visconti power, taking Bergamo in 1332 and Cremona in 1334, followed by Como, Lodi, Piacenza and Brescia. Crippled by gout, he gave Luchino the army that crushed Lodrisio at Parabiago early in 1339, and died that August.

阿佐内·维斯孔蒂（1302年12月7日—1339年8月16日）生于费拉拉：托里亚尼家族把他的祖父马泰奥赶出米兰后，父母加莱亚佐一世与贝阿特丽切·德斯特避居此地。他是二人唯一的嫡子。

1327年，国王路德维希四世把维斯孔蒂一家关进蒙扎城堡，1329年却以六万弗罗林把米兰皇帝代理人的头衔卖给阿佐内。阿佐内加固米兰以防路德维希卷土重来；觊觎领主之位的叔父马尔科被发现死去后，1330年议会推举他为米兰终身领主。

他重建家族势力：1332年取得贝加莫，1334年取得克雷莫纳，随后又取得科莫、洛迪、皮亚琴察和布雷西亚。他因痛风行动不便，1339年初把军队交给卢基诺，后者在帕拉比亚戈击溃洛德里西奥；同年8月阿佐内去世。

en:
Beatrice d'Este (1268–1334), daughter of Obizzo II d'Este, marquis of Ferrara, married first Nino Visconti, judge of Gallura, and bore him a daughter Joanna in 1291. Widowed in 1296, she returned to Ferrara, and in 1300 married Galeazzo I Visconti, becoming lady of Milan; their son was Azzone Visconti.

Beatrice shared the Visconti exile of 1302–1311 and later fled Piacenza with Azzone. After Emperor Louis the Bavarian deposed Galeazzo in 1327 and he died in exile in 1328, Azzone became lord of Milan in 1329. Dante alludes to her in Purgatorio, and she died in Milan in 1334.

贝阿特丽切·德斯特（1268—1334）是费拉拉侯爵奥比佐二世·埃斯特之女。她嫁给加卢拉法官尼诺·维斯孔蒂，1291年生下女儿乔万娜；1296年丧夫后返回费拉拉，1300年改嫁加莱亚佐一世·维斯孔蒂，成为米兰领主夫人，生子阿佐内·维斯孔蒂。

1302—1311年贝阿特丽切随维斯孔蒂家族流亡，后来又与阿佐内逃离皮亚琴察。皇帝路德维希四世于1327年废黜加莱亚佐，后者1328年死于流放，阿佐内遂于1329年成为米兰领主。但丁在《神曲·炼狱篇》中影射过她。1334年她卒于米兰。

en:
Benedetto da Asinago (c. 1273–1339) was a Lombard friar whom Pope John XXII appointed Bishop of Como in 1328. Como's clergy had instead elected Valeriano Rusca, Emperor Louis the Bavarian's candidate, so for years the city had two rival bishops, one papal and one imperial, fighting over the see.

In 1335 Benedetto attacked Como to drive Rusca out. The hard-pressed Rusca family then offered Azzone Visconti of Milan the lordship of Como in return for Bellinzona.

Azzone entered with an army on 25 July, installed Benedetto as lawful bishop and made peace between the city's Guelphs and Ghibellines, keeping the lordship for himself. Benedetto held the see until his death in October 1339.

贝内代托·达西纳戈（约1273—1339）是伦巴第修士，1328年被教皇约翰二十二世任命为科莫主教。但科莫教士另选了皇帝路德维希四世属意的瓦莱里亚诺·鲁斯卡，于是城里多年并存两位对立主教，一位由教皇任命，一位由皇帝任命，为教区争战不休。

1335年，贝内代托攻打科莫，要赶走鲁斯卡。招架不住的鲁斯卡家族遂向米兰的阿佐内·维斯孔蒂开出条件：以贝林佐纳换取科莫的统治权。

7月25日，阿佐内率军进城，扶立贝内代托为合法主教，调停当地圭尔夫派与吉伯林派，统治权则归他自己。贝内代托一直担任主教，直到1339年10月去世。

en:
Bernabò Visconti (1323 – 19 December 1385), son of Stefano Visconti, lived in exile after a plot against his uncle Luchino, until Archbishop Giovanni recalled him to Milan in 1349. In 1354 he inherited Milan with Matteo II and Galeazzo II and took the eastern lands facing the Scaligeri: Bergamo, Brescia and Cremona. Matteo died in 1355, rumoured poisoned by his brothers.

Bernabò fought almost constant wars against Pope Urban V, Florence, Venice and Savoy; in 1363 the pope declared him a heretic and proclaimed a crusade, and the 1364 peace cost him Bologna but brought half a million florins and lifted his excommunication.

His rule ended on 6 May 1385, when his nephew Gian Galeazzo seized him and took power. He died in Trezzo castle that December, apparently poisoned.

贝尔纳博·维斯孔蒂（1323—1385年12月19日）是斯特凡诺·维斯孔蒂之子。他因参与谋害叔父卢基诺的阴谋而流亡，直到1349年乔瓦尼大主教将他召回米兰。1354年，他与马泰奥二世、加莱亚佐二世共同继承米兰，分得与斯卡拉家族接壤的东部领地：贝加莫、布雷西亚和克雷莫纳。1355年马泰奥暴卒，传闻遭兄弟毒杀。

贝尔纳博几乎连年与教皇乌尔班五世及佛罗伦萨、威尼斯、萨伏依交战；1363年教皇宣布他为异端并发起十字军，1364年和约令他交出博洛尼亚，换得五十万弗罗林并解除绝罚。

1385年5月6日，侄子吉安·加莱亚佐将他拘捕夺权。12月即死于特雷佐城堡，疑为中毒。

en:
Bernardino Corio (1459–c. 1519) was a Milanese humanist historian from a family that had served the Sforza for two and a half centuries. A chamberlain to Galeazzo Maria Sforza from 1474, he witnessed the duke's murder in 1476 and later entered Ludovico Sforza's circle. Backed by Ludovico, who wanted to justify Sforza rule, he began around 1485 a history of Milan from its origins to 1499. In 1497 the duke ordered archives opened to him.

Corio left Milan after Ludovico's fall. Printed in 1503, his Patria historia was the first scholarly history of an Italian city written in the vernacular rather than Latin.

贝尔纳迪诺·科里奥（1459—约1519）是米兰人文主义历史学家，其家族效忠斯福尔扎家族已逾两个半世纪。1474年起他任加莱亚佐·马利亚·斯福尔扎的侍从，亲历1476年公爵遇刺，后进入卢多维科·斯福尔扎的圈子。约1485年，他在希望为斯福尔扎统治辩护的卢多维科支持下，开始撰写一部从米兰起源写到1499年的史书。1497年公爵下令向他开放档案。

卢多维科倒台后，科里奥离开米兰。1503年刊行的《祖国史》是第一部用意大利俗语而非拉丁语写成的意大利城市学术史著作。

卢多维科倒台后，科里奥离开米兰。1503年刊行的《祖国史》是第一部用意大利俗语而非拉丁语写成的意大利城市学术史著作。

en:
Catherine of Savoy-Vaud (1324 – 18 June 1388) was the daughter of Louis II of Savoy, Baron of Vaud. In 1330 she married Azzone Visconti, lord of Milan, becoming a childless widow in 1339. After her brother fell at the Battle of Laupen, a privilege made her Louis's heir, and she ruled Vaud from 1349.

Her second husband, Raoul II de Brienne, was beheaded in 1350; in 1352 she married William I of Namur. In 1359 she sold Vaud to Amadeus VI of Savoy.

zh:
卡特琳·德·萨伏依-沃（1324—1388年6月18日）是沃男爵路易二世·德·萨伏依之女。1330年她嫁给米兰领主阿佐内·维斯孔蒂，1339年丈夫去世，未留子嗣。弟弟在劳彭战役阵亡后，凭借一项特权她被立为父亲的继承人，1349年起统治沃。

她的第二任丈夫拉乌尔二世·德·布里耶纳于1350年被斩首，1352年她改嫁那慕尔侯爵威廉一世。1359年，她把沃卖给萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥六世。

Caverno della Torre, also recorded as Caverna, was a Lombard nobleman and condottiero of the Guelph della Torre family of Milan and a son of Pagano della Torre, count of Valsassina and podestà of Brescia, who died in 1241.

His brothers included Napoleone della Torre, the Guelph ruler of Milan until his defeat at Desio in 1277, and Raimondo della Torre, patriarch of Aquileia from 1273.

卡韦尔诺·德拉·托雷（亦作卡韦尔纳）是米兰归尔甫派德拉·托雷家族的伦巴第贵族、佣兵队长，为瓦尔萨西纳伯爵、布雷西亚执政官帕加诺·德拉·托雷（1241年卒）之子。

en:
Ermanno della Torre, also called Alemanno, was the eldest son of Pagano della Torre and elder brother of Napoleone, ruler of Milan. He made his career as a foreign podestà: in 1253 the Bolognese chose him to replace Pietro Grillo, and he made peace with Ravenna.

He was podestà of Florence from 1255 to 1256, leading the Guelph cause in Tuscany: he forced Count Guido Guerra to readmit the exiles of Arezzo, marched against the Pisans and routed them on the Serchio, and in 1256 helped relieve famine in Florence and Lucca.

Of his sons, Lombardo perished in the iron cage of Castel Baradello in 1280 after the Torriani defeat at Desio in 1277, while Erreco and Goffredo took refuge with their uncle the patriarch. His descendants carried the family into Friuli as the Duino line. His death is placed in 1265, though his Milan tomb inscription gave 1272.

埃尔曼诺·德拉·托雷（亦称阿莱曼诺）是帕加诺·德拉·托雷的长子，米兰统治者纳波莱奥内的兄长。他以外来执政官为业：1253年博洛尼亚人选他接替彼得罗·格里洛，他与拉文纳订立和约。

1255至1256年他任佛罗伦萨执政官，领导托斯卡纳的归尔甫派事业：迫使圭多·圭拉伯爵重新接纳阿雷佐的流亡者，进军抗击比萨人并在塞尔基奥河将其击溃，1256年又赈济了佛罗伦萨与卢卡的饥荒。

他的儿子中，伦巴多在1277年托里亚尼家族于代西奥战败后被囚，1280年死于巴拉德罗城堡的铁笼，埃雷科与戈弗雷多则投奔任宗主教的叔父。他的后代把家族带到弗留利，形成杜伊诺一支。他约于1265年去世，但其米兰墓碑铭文作1272年。

en:
Filippo della Torre (early 13th century – 24 September 1265) was a Milanese Guelph noble, son of Iacopo, count of Valsassina, and brother of Martino, first signore of Milan. Made podestà of Genoa in 1256, he provoked a popular revolt, then returned to Milan and succeeded Martino as lord on 18 December 1263.

He brought Novara, Lodi, Vercelli and Bergamo under his sway, bloodily subdued Como, and in 1264 expelled the Ghibelline Oberto Pallavicino. In 1265 he supported the passage of Charles I of Anjou's troops, then died on 24 September.

菲利波·德拉·托雷（13世纪初—1265年9月24日）是米兰圭尔夫派贵族，瓦尔萨西纳伯爵贾科莫之子、米兰首任领主马蒂诺之弟。1256年他被任命为热那亚波德斯塔，任内引发民众暴动；回到米兰后，他于1263年12月18日继马蒂诺之后成为米兰领主。

他使诺瓦拉、洛迪、韦尔切利和贝加莫臣服，血腥镇压科莫，1264年驱逐皇帝派首领奥贝托·帕拉维奇诺。1265年他支持安茹的查理一世的军队借道，同年9月24日去世。

en:
Fulco I d'Este (c. 1070–c. 1134) founded the Italian branch of the House of Este. A younger son of Margrave Albert Azzo II, he inherited the family's Italian estates when his father died in 1097, while his elder half-brother Welf took the lands north of the Alps. Welf disputed the partition in vain, and his Bavarian descendants only dropped their claim in 1154.

Fulco was the first to forge ties with the nobility of Ferrara, later ruled by his descendants. His son Obizzo I succeeded him.

富尔科一世·德斯特（约1070—约1134）是埃斯特家族意大利支的始祖。他是藩侯阿尔贝托·阿佐二世的幼子之一，1097年父亲去世后继承家族在意大利的领地，异母长兄韦尔夫则分得阿尔卑斯山以北的土地。韦尔夫不服分割而未果，他在巴伐利亚的后代直到1154年才放弃主张。

富尔科是家族中率先与费拉拉贵族结交的人，其后代后来统治了费拉拉。其子奥皮佐一世继位。

en:
Francesco della Torre was a Milanese Guelph noble, son of Pagano I della Torre and brother of Napoleone, who ruled Milan from 1265. He held the lordship of Seprio. When Archbishop Ottone Visconti attacked the della Torre by night at Desio, Francesco was killed in the battle on 21 January 1277.

His son Guido was captured with his uncle Napoleone and imprisoned at Castel Baradello in Como. The Visconti became masters of Milan.

en:
Francesco Pecorari was an architect from Cremona, active in the first half of the fourteenth century. An inscription on the octagonal bell tower of Milan's church of San Gottardo, raised between 1330 and 1336 to carry the city's first public clock, names him in Latin as Magister Franciscus de Pecoraris de Cremona.

He is also credited with the octagonal tower of Chiaravalle Abbey near Milan, dated 1329–1340, and with work on the Torrazzo bell tower of his native Cremona.

弗朗切斯科·佩科拉里是克雷莫纳建筑师，活跃于14世纪上半叶。米兰圣戈塔尔多教堂的八角形钟楼建于1330—1336年，用来安放全城第一座公共时钟，塔上铭文以拉丁文称他为“克雷莫纳的弗朗切斯科·德·佩科拉里斯大师”。

米兰附近基亚拉瓦莱修道院的八角形塔楼（1329—1340年）也出自他之手，他还参与了故乡克雷莫纳托拉佐钟楼的工程。

en:
Galeazzo I Visconti (1277–1328), son of Matteo I Visconti, married Beatrice d'Este on 24 June 1300 and shared the long Visconti exile. Named capitano del popolo of Milan in 1322, he succeeded his father as lord and defeated a Papal–Angevin army at Bassignana, earning excommunication from Pope John XXII in March 1323.

With Emperor Louis IV he routed another papal army near Monza, but the emperor imprisoned him there in 1327 on his brother Marco's accusations. Freed in March 1328, he took shelter with Castruccio Castracani and died at Pescia on 6 August; his son Azzone succeeded him.

加莱亚佐一世·维斯孔蒂（1277—1328）是马泰奥一世·维斯孔蒂之子。1300年6月24日他娶贝阿特丽切·德斯特为妻，并随家族度过长期流亡。1322年他被任命为米兰人民统帅，继任其父为领主，在巴西尼亚纳击败教皇与安茹的联军，1323年3月被教皇约翰二十二世开除教籍。

他借助皇帝路德维希四世在蒙扎附近再破教皇军，却于1327年因弟弟马可的指控被皇帝囚禁于蒙扎。1328年3月获释后，他投奔卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼，8月6日卒于佩夏；其子阿佐内继位。

en:
Galeazzo II Visconti (c. 1320 – 4 August 1378), son of Stefano Visconti and Valentina Doria, was exiled in 1346 by his uncle Luchino and returned after Luchino died. In 1354 he inherited Milan with his brothers Bernabò and Matteo II and took the western lands facing Savoy. In 1356 the Visconti army beat an invading league at Casorate.

Galeazzo took Pavia in 1359, founded its university in 1361 and invited Petrarch there, and in 1365 moved his court to the city's finished castle, leaving Milan to Bernabò. He married his son Gian Galeazzo to Isabelle of Valois, the French king's sister, for half a million florins.

He joined the War of the Eight Saints in 1375 and died on 4 August 1378, three years later. His son Gian Galeazzo succeeded him.

加莱亚佐二世·维斯孔蒂（约1320—1378年8月4日）是斯特凡诺·维斯孔蒂与瓦伦蒂娜·多里亚之子。1346年叔父卢基诺将他放逐，卢基诺去世后他才回到米兰。1354年，他与兄弟贝尔纳博、马泰奥二世共同继承米兰，分得毗邻萨伏依的西部领地。1356年维斯孔蒂军队在卡索拉泰击败来犯的联盟。

1359年他攻取帕维亚，1361年在当地创办大学并邀请彼特拉克前来；1365年城堡竣工，他把宫廷迁往帕维亚，将米兰留给贝尔纳博。他花五十万弗罗林，让儿子吉安·加莱亚佐迎娶法国国王的妹妹瓦卢瓦的伊莎贝拉。

1375年他加入八圣之战，三年后的1378年去世。其子吉安·加莱亚佐继位。

en:
Galvano Fiamma (1283–1344) was a Milanese Dominican. He entered the monastery of Sant'Eustorgio, taught theology at Pavia from 1308 to 1313, and later lectured in Milan.

His many chronicles, above all the Chronicon maius, trace Milan's history, and he drew a map of the city. In 1339 Giovanni Visconti made him his chaplain, and he has been called the first Mediterranean writer to describe lands across the Atlantic.

加尔瓦诺·菲亚马（1283—1344）是米兰多明我会修士。他入圣欧斯托焦修道院，1308—1313年在帕维亚教授神学，后回米兰讲学。

他著有《大编年史》等多部史书，记述米兰历史，并绘制过一幅米兰地图。1339年，乔瓦尼·维斯孔蒂任命他为专职神父。他还被认为是最早记述大西洋彼岸陆地的地中海地区作家。

en:
Gianfrancesco da Correggio (born c. 1320), also called Cagnolo, was the son of Simone da Correggio, who had made himself lord of Parma with his brothers in 1341 and died in 1344. That year Azzo gave the city up to Este, and his uncles quarrelled over the sale.

Gianfrancesco first backed Azzo, then shifted between the great lords contending for the Po valley, and never regained the Parma his father had held. He served at the Visconti court and then at the Este court in Ferrara.

After siding with the Ghibellines he fled Ferrara, but was caught and brought back. Obizzo d'Este took San Quirico from him, and he gained his freedom only by ceding Gualtieri as well.

詹弗朗切斯科·达·科雷焦（约1320年生），通称卡尼奥洛，是西莫内·达·科雷焦之子；西莫内1341年与兄弟们夺得帕尔马，1344年去世。同年阿佐把这座城让给了埃斯特家族，叔父们为这笔出售起了争执。

詹弗朗切斯科先支持阿佐，随后在争夺波河流域的各大领主之间反复投靠，始终未能夺回父亲曾拥有的帕尔马。他先后在维斯孔蒂家族的宫廷和费拉拉的埃斯特宫廷任职。

他站在皇帝派一边后逃离费拉拉，却被追回。奥比佐·德斯特夺走他的圣奎里科，他又割让瓜尔蒂耶里才重获自由。

en:
Giovanni di Balduccio (c. 1300 – c. 1365) was a Pisan sculptor. Trained in Pisa's cathedral workshop, he signed work at Sarzana in 1327 and at San Casciano in 1330–1331 before Azzone Visconti called him to Milan around 1334.

There his signed marble shrine of Saint Peter Martyr in Sant'Eustorgio, dated 1339, is his masterpiece. He declined the mastership of Pisa Cathedral in 1349, and some scholars also credit him with the Arca di Sant'Agostino at Pavia, built 1362–1365.

en:
Giovanni Visconti (1290–1354), son of Matteo I Visconti, was an archbishop who led armies and held cities by force. Elected archbishop of Milan in 1317, he was refused confirmation by Pope John XXII, who installed Aicardo da Camodeia and excommunicated him for heresy in 1323; the antipope Nicholas V made him a cardinal.

He became bishop and lord of Novara in 1331 and entered Milan in triumph in 1339, only confirmed in 1342. With his brother Luchino he bought the co-lordship of Milan from the pope for half a million florins, and after 1349 he ruled alone. He gained Bologna in 1350 and Genoa in 1353.

When Florence organized an alliance against him, he tortured leading Bolognese until they confessed to a plot with Florence, and used it to justify war. Giovanni died on 5 October 1354.

佛罗伦萨组织联盟对抗他时，他拷问博洛尼亚显要，逼出通敌佛罗伦萨的供词，借此开战。1354年10月5日他去世。

en:
Isabella Fieschi (fl. 1331–1356), daughter of the Genoese noble Carlo Fieschi, was a great-niece of Pope Adrian V. In 1331 she married Luchino Visconti in Milan, a match arranged to seal an alliance between Genoa and Milan. She became lady of Milan in 1339, when Luchino took power after the death of his nephew Azzone.

She was known for her beauty and her lovers. An official visit to Venice in 1347 turned scandalous over her affairs, and Luchino swore to punish her cruelly; he died shortly after, in 1349, rumoured to have been poisoned by her.

Her son was forced to give up his rights to power in Milan and she was placed under house arrest. In 1356 she escaped and reportedly returned to her family in Savignone.

伊莎贝拉·菲耶斯基（活跃于1331—1356年）是热那亚贵族卡洛·菲耶斯基之女，教皇阿德里安五世的侄孙女。1331年她在米兰嫁给卢基诺·维斯孔蒂，这桩婚事是为了缔结热那亚与米兰的联盟。1339年，卢基诺在侄子阿佐内死后掌权，她成为米兰领主夫人。

她的儿子被迫放弃在米兰掌权的权利，她本人遭软禁。1356年她逃出米兰，据称回到萨维尼奥内的家族中。

en:
Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519) was an Italian polymath of the High Renaissance, known as a painter but also an engineer, anatomist and architect. Born out of wedlock near Vinci, he wrote left-handed in mirror script and about fourteen entered Verrocchio's Florence workshop.

About 1482 he went to Milan, offering Duke Ludovico Sforza his engineering skills. There he painted the Virgin of the Rocks and The Last Supper and modelled the giant equestrian Gran Cavallo, whose bronze became cannon in 1494. After the French overthrew Ludovico in 1500 he returned to Florence, served Cesare Borgia as a military engineer and in 1503 began the Mona Lisa.

In 1516 Francis I gave him the use of Clos Lucé at Amboise, and he died there in 1519. His pupil Francesco Melzi inherited his paintings and library; his thousands of notebook pages on anatomy, flight and water stayed unpublished, little influencing later science.

列奥纳多·达·芬奇（1452—1519）是意大利盛期文艺复兴博学者，以画家闻名，兼为工程师、解剖学家、建筑师。他为托斯卡纳芬奇镇附近的私生子，左手镜像写字，十四岁入韦罗基奥的佛罗伦萨作坊。

1482年赴米兰，向公爵卢多维科·斯福尔扎自荐工程本领。画下《岩间圣母》《最后的晚餐》，为巨型骑马像“大骏马”制模，青铜1494年铸成大炮。1500年法军推翻卢多维科后返佛罗伦萨，为切萨雷·波吉亚当军事工程师，1503年始画《蒙娜丽莎》。

1516年法王弗朗索瓦一世赐居昂布瓦斯的克洛·吕斯庄园，1519年卒于该处。学生弗朗切斯科·梅尔齐继承其画作与藏书；数千页解剖、飞行、水利笔记生前未出版，对后世科学几无影响。

Leonardo Visconti (died c. 1376) was the natural son of Giovanni Visconti, archbishop and co-lord of Milan. In 1352 he served as podestà of Novara, but a quarrel with his father drove him from Visconti territory, and he took shelter at Viazalla castle in the Vercelli country with his wife.

He then entered the service of John II, Marquess of Montferrat, and helped the marquess acquire Alba, Asti and Cuneo, setting himself against his Milanese Visconti kinsmen. He died around 1376.

en:
Lodrisio Visconti (c. 1280–1364), son of Pietro Visconti, was a Milanese condottiero who fought both for and against his own house. He first backed Matteo Visconti in winning Milan from the Torriani, then helped his cousin Marco arrest Galeazzo I at Monza. He fled to his Seprio fief, but Azzone destroyed it, and he took service with Mastino II della Scala.

In 1339, backed by Mastino, he raised the Compagnia di San Giorgio, remembered as the first mercenary company led by an Italian. He invaded the Milanese and was defeated and captured at Parabiago in February. With his son Ambrogio he spent ten years in an iron cage in San Colombano castle, until Archbishop Giovanni freed him.

He later led troops for Galeazzo II and fought in the 1356 victory over the anti-Visconti league. He died in 1364.

洛德里西奥·维斯孔蒂（约1280—1364）是彼得罗·维斯孔蒂之子，米兰籍雇佣兵首领，在家族内斗中既帮本家也反本家。起初他支持马泰奥·维斯孔蒂从托里亚尼家族手中夺回米兰，后来协助堂兄马可在蒙扎拘捕加莱亚佐一世。他逃到塞普里奥封地，阿佐内将其摧毁，他转而投靠马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉。

1339年，他在马斯蒂诺支持下组建圣乔治佣兵团，被视为意大利人统领的第一支佣兵团。他入侵米兰领地，2月在帕拉比亚戈战败被俘，与儿子安布罗焦一同被关在圣科隆巴诺城堡的铁笼里达十年，直到大主教乔瓦尼将他释放。

他后来为加莱亚佐二世统兵，参加了1356年击败反维斯孔蒂同盟的战役。1364年他去世。

Lombardo della Torre (c. 1231–1280) was a Milanese nobleman, son of Ermanno della Torre. He fought valiantly alongside his kinsmen in wars against Archbishop Ottone Visconti and was among the sixty della Torre who charged at the battle of Desio on 21 January 1277.

Captured in the defeat, he was thrown into the iron cage of Castel Baradello above Como, where he perished in 1280. His sons carried on the family line in Friuli.

en:
Luchino Visconti (1287 or 1292 – 24 January 1349), son of Matteo I Visconti, was left out of the succession and chose a soldier's life. In 1339 he led Milan's army to victory at Parabiago over Lodrisio's mercenaries, and when Azzone died that August he and his brother Archbishop Giovanni were chosen lords of Milan, with Luchino holding real power.

He took Bellinzona in 1340 and Locarno in 1341 and in 1346 forced the Este to sell him Parma. His rule was harsh: a noble's plot ended with the plotter and his sons beheaded, and he later exiled his three nephews.

When plague reached Milan in 1348 he had the first infected houses walled up, and the city was spared the worst. In January 1349, after reportedly threatening his wife Isabella Fieschi with burning at the stake, he died of poison.

卢基诺·维斯孔蒂（1287或1292—1349年1月24日）是马泰奥一世·维斯孔蒂之子，被排除在继承之外，转而投身军旅。1339年，他统率米兰军队在帕拉比亚戈击败族人洛德里西奥的雇佣军；同年8月阿佐内去世，他与兄弟乔瓦尼大主教被推举为米兰领主，实权掌握在他手里。

1340年他攻取贝林佐纳，1341年攻取洛迦诺，1346年迫使埃斯特家族把帕尔马卖给他。他的统治严厉：一名贵族谋反败露，与其子一同被斩首；他后来又放逐了三个侄子。

1348年瘟疫传入米兰，他下令把最早出现病例的几户人家封死，米兰躲过了最惨重的灾难。1349年1月，相传他扬言要把妻子伊莎贝拉·菲耶斯基烧死，随后中毒身亡。

en:
Marco Visconti, nicknamed Balatrone (c. 1289–1329), was a Ghibelline condottiero and son of Matteo I Visconti. He fought for Henry VII from 1310, taking Alessandria and ousting Archbishop Cassone della Torre from Milan; he later served noble factions in Genoa and was excommunicated.

He fought for Pisa at Montecatini in 1315. In 1327, with Lodrisio, he accused Galeazzo of treason and established a pro-imperial government.

In Tuscany in 1329 he seized Lucca with the Company of the Ceruglio and sold it for thirty thousand florins. On his return to Milan on 5 September 1329, he was strangled and his body thrown from a window; his nephew Azzone and Luchino were said to have taken part.

马可·维斯孔蒂，绰号巴拉特罗内（约1289—1329），是吉伯林派雇佣兵首领、马泰奥一世·维斯孔蒂之子。他自1310年为亨利七世作战，攻占亚历山德里亚，把大主教卡索内·德拉·托雷逐出米兰；后来为热那亚贵族派系效力，并被开除教籍。

1315年他为比萨参加蒙泰卡蒂尼战役。1327年，他与洛德里西奥一同控告加莱亚佐叛国，建立亲帝国政府。

1329年他在托斯卡纳率切鲁利奥佣兵团夺取卢卡，以三万弗罗林售出。1329年9月5日他回到米兰后被勒死，尸体被掷出窗外；据称侄子阿佐内与鲁吉诺参与了杀害。

en:
Martino della Torre (died 20 November 1263), son of Iacopo della Torre and nephew of Pagano I, led Milan's popular party. An elder of the Credenza di Sant'Ambrogio from 1247, he continued the land survey begun by Pagano.

In April 1259 he became capitano del popolo and then the first signore of Milan. With Oberto Pallavicino he defeated the Ghibelline Ezzelino III da Romano at Cassano d'Adda in 1259, and later appointed Pallavicino commander-general.

He fought Pope Urban IV's appointment of Ottone Visconti as archbishop and was excommunicated. Made podestà of Novara in June 1263, he died at Lodi that November and was buried at Chiaravalle.

马蒂诺·德拉·托雷（1263年11月20日卒）是贾科莫·德拉·托雷之子、帕加诺一世之侄，米兰平民派的领袖。1247年起任圣安布罗斯公社会长老，继续帕加诺开始的土地清丈。

他抵制教皇乌尔班四世任命奥托内·维斯孔蒂为大主教，因而被绝罚。1263年6月他出任诺瓦拉的波德斯塔，同年11月在洛迪病逝，葬于基亚拉瓦莱修道院。

en:
Matteo I Visconti, called the Great (1250–1322), son of Teobaldo Visconti, was named capitano del popolo by his great-uncle Archbishop Ottone in 1287, succeeding as lord of Milan in 1295. He was driven into exile in 1302 by a league led by the Della Torre.

In 1311, after years sheltering with the Scala family at Nogarola, Henry VII sold him the title of imperial vicar of Milan. His sons extended Ghibelline power and took Pavia in 1315.

Excommunicated by Pope John XXII, condemned for necromancy and threatened with a crusade, he abdicated in 1322 and died on 24 June, leaving Milan to his son Galeazzo I.

Matteo II Visconti (c. 1319–1355) was the eldest son of Stefano Visconti and Valentina Doria. In 1342 he married Egidiola Gonzaga of Mantua. After plotting against his uncle Luchino Visconti he was exiled to Montferrat in 1346 and recalled in 1349.

When his uncle Giovanni Visconti died in 1354, Matteo and his brothers Galeazzo II and Bernabò divided the Visconti domains. He died at Saronno in September 1355 after dinner, almost certainly poisoned on his brothers' orders.

en:
Corrado della Torre, known as Mosca (c. 1251–1307), was a son of Napoleone della Torre, Guelph lord of Milan. He fought at Desio in 1277, was captured with his father and held in the Baradello tower.

He later governed Istria and served as podestà of Trieste in 1293 and Bergamo in 1304. He also obtained permission to draw water from the Brembo, beginning an irrigation system for the fields around Treviglio.

In 1307 a plot by Matteo Visconti against him and his cousin Guido failed. Corrado died in Milan on 24 October 1307 and was buried at San Francesco Grande.

en:
Oberto I Pallavicino, nicknamed Pelavicino (1080–1148), was a Lombard feudatory of Busseto, near Parma; his nickname became the family name Pallavicino. In 1116 he courted Emperor Henry V when the emperor entered Italy to claim Matilda of Canossa's inheritance.

From 1124 he held Fontanellato castle and the former Este lands around Soragna. In 1136 he helped found the Cistercian abbey of Chiaravalle della Colomba.

After feuding with his son Delfino, he submitted lands in the Parma region to Piacenza in 1145 and received them back as fiefs in return for homage. War broke out between Parma and Piacenza, and Delfino sided with Parma against him. Oberto died at Busseto in 1148.

奥贝托一世·帕拉维奇诺，绰号佩拉维奇诺（1080—1148），是帕尔马附近布塞托的伦巴第封臣；他的绰号后来演变为家族姓氏帕拉维奇诺。1116年皇帝亨利五世进入意大利索取卡诺莎的玛蒂尔达的遗产时，奥贝托向他示好。

1124年起，他领有丰塔内拉托城堡以及原属德斯特家族的索拉尼亚一带土地。1136年，他参与创建熙笃会的基阿拉瓦莱-德拉科隆巴修道院。

后来他与儿子德尔菲诺反目，于1145年将帕尔马地区的土地交给皮亚琴察，以效忠换取这些封地。帕尔马与皮亚琴察爆发战争，德尔菲诺联合帕尔马对抗父亲。奥贝托于1148年卒于布塞托。

en:
Obizzo I d'Este (c. 1100–1193) succeeded his father Folco I as marquis of Este and reunited his grandfather Albert Azzo II's Italian lands. He kept on good terms with both emperor and pope.

In 1163 he aided Frederick Barbarossa against Verona and Padua, yet in 1167 joined the Lombard League against the emperor; he attended the Peace of Venice in 1177 and was named podestà of Padua the same year.

In Ferrara he led the Guelph Adelardi faction, preparing his family's rise in the city. His son Azzo V died in 1193, and when Obizzo died on Christmas Day that year, his grandson Azzo VI succeeded him.

In Ferrara he led the Guelph Adelardi faction, preparing his family's rise in the city. His son Azzo V died in 1193, and when Obizzo died on Christmas Day that year, his grandson Azzo VI succeeded him.
zh:
奥比佐一世·埃斯特（约1100—1193）继承父亲富尔科一世成为埃斯特藩侯，把祖父阿尔贝托·阿佐二世曾拥有的意大利领地重新统一。他与皇帝和教皇都保持良好关系。

1163年，他协助腓特烈一世攻打维罗纳和帕多瓦，却在1167年加入反对皇帝的伦巴第同盟；1177年他出席威尼斯和会，同年被任命为帕多瓦的波德斯塔。

在费拉拉，他领导归尔夫派阿代拉尔迪一派，为家族日后在该城的崛起铺平道路。儿子阿佐五世于1193年去世，奥比佐同年圣诞节去世后，由孙子阿佐六世继位。

en:
Ottone Visconti (1207–1295), a churchman, became the first Visconti lord of Milan. In 1262 Pope Urban IV named him archbishop over the candidate of the Guelph Della Torre, who opposed his appointment. Their occupation of Milan Cathedral began a long war between the families, in which his nephew Teobaldo was beheaded in 1276.

Ottone defeated Napoleone della Torre at Desio and entered Milan as its ruler on 22 January 1277. Victor again at Vaprio d'Adda in 1281, he made his grand-nephew Matteo I capitano generale in 1287, then retired to religious affairs and died at Chiaravalle Abbey in 1295.

奥托内·维斯孔蒂（1207—1295）出身教士，是维斯孔蒂家族首任米兰领主。1262年，教皇乌尔班四世越过归尔甫派德拉·托雷家族推举的人选，任命他为米兰大主教，该家族反对这一任命。德拉·托雷家族占据米兰主教座堂，两家由此展开长期战争，他的侄子泰奥巴尔多于1276年被斩首。

奥托内在代西奥击败拿波列奥内·德拉·托雷，于1277年1月22日以统治者身份进入米兰。1281年他又在阿达河畔瓦普里奥获胜，1287年任命侄孙马泰奥一世·维斯孔蒂为统帅，此后退居教务，1295年卒于基阿拉瓦莱修道院。

en:
Pagano della Torre, Count of Valsassina from 1216, was a Guelph noble and son of Iacopo della Torre. Named podestà of Brescia in 1227 as the second Lombard League formed, feuding noble families later forced him to flee the city.

After the imperial victory at Cortenuova in 1237, he gathered the broken Milanese army at Pontida and sheltered its men in Valsassina, caring for the wounded.

Milan made him an elder of the Credenza di Sant'Ambrogio in 1240, where he promoted a land survey that lowered taxes. He died on 6 January 1241 and was buried at Chiaravalle.

帕加诺·德拉·托雷是1216年起受封的瓦尔萨西纳伯爵，教皇派贵族，贾科莫·德拉·托雷之子。1227年第二次伦巴第同盟组建时，他被任命为布雷西亚的波德斯塔，后因贵族家族争斗被迫逃离。

Pietro Azario (1312 – after 1367) was a notary born in Novara. By 1347 he was serving the Visconti at Borgomanero, and from about 1362 he acted as chancellor to the podestà of Tortona.

There he compiled his Liber Gestorum in Lombardia, a chronicle of Milan under the Visconti from 1250 to 1362. A copy survives in Milan's Biblioteca Ambrosiana; his death is unrecorded, though he was alive in 1367.

en:
Francesco Sforza (1401–1466) was the Italian condottiero who founded the Sforza dynasty in Milan. Born at Cigoli in Tuscany, illegitimate son of condottiero Muzio Sforza, he fought from his teens in his father's company and served in turn Naples, the papacy, Florence, Venice and the Visconti.

In 1433–1435 he attacked the Papal States for Milan, then changed sides after taking Ancona and became its papal vicar. In 1441 he married Bianca Maria Visconti, daughter of Duke Filippo Maria. After 1447 he first served, then besieged the Ambrosian Republic, entering Milan as duke in 1450.

He improved irrigation canals, reorganised the administration and helped broker the Treaty of Lodi in 1454. He ruled until his death, succeeded by his son Galeazzo Maria.

弗朗切斯科·斯福尔扎（1401—1466）是在米兰建立斯福尔扎王朝的意大利雇佣兵首领。他生于托斯卡纳的奇戈利，是佣兵队长穆齐奥·斯福尔扎的私生子，少年起便随父征战，先后受雇于那不勒斯、教皇国、佛罗伦萨、威尼斯和维斯孔蒂家族。

1433—1435年他为米兰攻打教皇国，攻占安科纳后转变阵营，获教皇任命为该城代牧。1441年他与米兰公爵菲利波·马利亚之女比安卡·马利亚·维斯孔蒂成婚。1447年维斯孔蒂家族绝嗣后，他先效力继而围攻安布罗斯共和国，1450年入主米兰成为公爵。

他改善灌溉水道、重组行政，并于1454年促成《洛迪和约》。他统治直至1466年去世，其子加莱亚佐·马利亚继位。

en:
Simone della Torre (c. 1278–1324) was the son of Guido della Torre, the Guelph lord of Milan. To seal an alliance between the rival houses, he married Antiochia, daughter of Pietro Visconti. After his father was driven from Milan by the Emperor Henry VII in 1311, Simone fought in the Della Torre and papal league against the Visconti.

He helped capture Monza in 1323. On 28 February 1324 the league was routed at Vaprio d'Adda, where Simone was killed.

en:
Stefano Visconti (1288–4 July 1327), lord of Arona, was son of Matteo I Visconti and Bonacossa Borri. In 1318 he married Valentina Doria, sealing a Ghibelline alliance against the Genoese Guelphs. Their sons later shared rule of Milan.

Stefano died after serving as taster at Louis the Bavarian's coronation banquet in July 1327. Suspected of a poisoning plot, his brothers Galeazzo, Giovanni and Luchino and his nephew Azzone were imprisoned at Monza, triggering a crisis with the Empire.

Teobaldo Visconti (1230–1276) was a Milanese nobleman and soldier, son of Andreotto Visconti and nephew of Archbishop Ottone Visconti. His son was Matteo I, later called the Great, who became lord of Milan.

The Della Torre opposed Ottone's appointment as archbishop, and the families fought for Milan. After Napoleone della Torre exiled opposing noble families, they formed a coalition in Novara and Pavia. With their support, Teobaldo led an army and occupied Castelseprio, but was defeated near Gallarate; captured, he was beheaded there in 1276 on Napoleone's orders.

en:
Uberto Visconti (c. 1170–1248) was a Lombard nobleman, son of Ruggero Visconti, consul of Milan. He held the fiefs of Massino, Albizzate and Besnate and is regarded as progenitor of the Visconti lords and dukes of Milan.

By his wife Berta Pirovano he had six sons, the most famous being Ottone, later archbishop of Milan; the rival Torriani family challenged Ottone's election by citing Uberto's reputed lack of piety. He died in 1248, before his son made the family masters of Milan.

Valentina Doria (1290 – 27 August 1359) was a Genoese noblewoman, daughter of Bernabò Doria. In 1318 she married Stefano Visconti, son of Milan's lord Matteo I, a match meant to bind the Ghibelline Visconti to her father against Genoa's Guelphs. She bore four children, among them Matteo II, Galeazzo II and Bernabò, who later shared rule of Milan.

Widowed when Stefano died in 1327, she was laid beside him in Sant'Eustorgio. Bonino da Campione carved their joint tomb in 1359.

瓦伦蒂娜·多里亚（1290—1359年8月27日）是热那亚贵族女子，贝尔纳博·多里亚之女。1318年，她嫁给米兰领主马泰奥一世之子斯特凡诺·维斯孔蒂，这桩婚事意在使吉伯林派的维斯孔蒂家族与其父结盟，共同对付热那亚的圭尔夫派。她生有四个子女，包括后来分治米兰的马泰奥二世、加莱亚佐二世和贝尔纳博。

1327年斯特凡诺去世后她守寡，身后葬于圣欧斯托焦教堂，与丈夫合葬。博尼诺·达·坎皮奥内于1359年为二人雕刻了合葬墓。

en:
Si Kefa, also called Hso Hkan Hpa (1294–1369), was the Tai ruler of Möng Mao who founded the Luchuan state, succeeding around 1335. Tai chronicles say he built a new capital at Selan and won the submission of neighbouring Tai states. The Yuan court sent four expeditions against him, and all failed.

Fearing more attacks, he sent his heir to nominally acknowledge Yuan authority; amid the Red Turban rebellions the Yuan could only name him Pingmian Pacification Commissioner in 1355. He then turned west: his brother conquered Assam without a fight, but Hkan Hpa suspected him of plotting and poisoned him on his return.

In 1364 his forces sacked the Burmese kingdoms of Sagaing and Pinya and carried the king of Pinya back to Möng Mao. He died in 1369, succeeded by his son Si Bingfa.

思可法，傣语名思翰法（1294—1369），是麓川（勐卯）君主、麓川思氏政权的缔造者，约1335年继位。傣族编年史记载，他修筑新都色兰，使周边傣族邦国臣服。元朝先后四次发兵讨伐，均告失败。

他担心再遭进攻，派继承人赴元廷名义上表示归附；红巾起义爆发后，元朝只能在1355年封他为平缅宣慰使。随后他转向西方：其弟攻下阿萨姆，对方未作抵抗，但思可法疑心弟弟图谋不轨，在他返回时将其毒杀。

1364年，他的军队攻陷并劫掠缅甸的实皆与彬牙两个王国，把彬牙国王带回勐卯。1369年他去世，其子思并发继位。

en:
Corrado del Carretto (c. 1250–1316/1319) was the son of Giacomo del Carretto and Caterina da Marano, an illegitimate daughter of Emperor Frederick II.

After his father died the family lands were divided in 1268 into three shares, and Corrado received Millesimo in the Bormida valley, becoming the first marchese di Millesimo and founder of the Aleramici line. He was invested with the marquisate in 1269. His son Franceschino continued the Millesimo branch.

en:
Ma Xiuying (1332–1382), better known as Empress Ma, was the principal wife of the Ming founder Zhu Yuanzhang. Orphaned young, she was adopted by Red Turban leader Guo Zixing and married to his officer Zhu in 1352.

When Guo suspected Zhu of betrayal during a famine, she secretly brought him food. She accompanied him on campaign, and at the Battle of Lake Poyang in 1363 supplied troops and treasure against Chen Youliang.

When Zhu became the Hongwu Emperor in 1368 she was made empress. Admired for her frugality and for refusing to advance her relatives, she remained his close adviser until her death in 1382.

饥荒时郭子兴怀疑朱元璋叛变，马氏偷偷给丈夫送食物。她随军征战，1363年鄱阳湖水战期间供给军需、散发金帛，对抗陈友谅。

en:
Zhu Yuanzhang (1328–1398), the Hongwu Emperor, was a peasant's son who founded the Ming dynasty. After plague killed his family in 1344, he lived as a monk until 1352, when Yuan troops burned his monastery and he joined the Red Turban rebels. He took Nanjing in 1356.

In 1363 he defeated Chen Youliang's larger force at Lake Poyang. He became King of Wu in 1364 and took Suzhou in 1367, ending Zhang Shicheng. In 1368 he proclaimed the Ming dynasty and his armies took Dadu as the Yuan emperor fled north.

He issued the Great Ming Code. After executing Hu Weiyong in 1380 he abolished the chancellors and founded the Embroidered Uniform Guard in 1382; his purges killed tens of thousands under a strict sea ban. He died in 1398 and his grandson Jianwen succeeded him, until his fourth son Zhu Di seized power in 1402 as Yongle Emperor.

朱元璋（1328—1398），即洪武帝，是农家子出身的明朝开国皇帝。1344年瘟疫夺走他的家人，此后他做游方僧人，靠化缘度日；1352年元军烧毁他所在的寺庙，他于是投奔红巾军。1356年他攻占南京。

1363年，他在鄱阳湖水战中击败兵力占优的陈友谅；1364年称吴王；1367年攻下苏州，消灭张士诚。1368年他称帝建立明朝，大军攻占大都，元朝皇帝逃往北方。

他颁行《大明律》。1380年诛杀胡惟庸后废除丞相，1382年设锦衣卫，历次整肃杀人数以万计，又推行严厉海禁。1398年他去世，孙子建文帝继位；1402年第四子朱棣夺位，是为永乐帝。

Mikhail Davidovich was the first appanage prince of Mologa, a younger son of David Fyodorovich, prince of Yaroslavl. In 1321 he and his elder brother Vasily divided the principality: Vasily kept Yaroslavl, while Mikhail took the Mologa river basin, where the town of Mologa arose.

In 1362 he travelled to the Golden Horde with Grand Prince Dmitry Ivanovich. Under him a trade fair flourished at Kholopy Gorodok. He died around 1362, leaving three sons.

Amaury I of Montfort (died 1053) was the second lord of Montfort-l'Amaury in the Île-de-France, succeeding his father Guillaume, who had raised the first wooden castle on the mound that gave the lordship its name. Amaury rebuilt the castle in stone and enclosed the town with fortifications.

Around 1028 he married Bertrade, traditionally assigned to the house of Gometz, who bore him his successor Simon I. He died in 1053.

en:
Amaury III of Montfort (died 1137), a son of Simon I, succeeded his brother Simon II as lord of Montfort in 1101 and claimed the county of Évreux in 1118 when his uncle died. After Henry I annexed Évreux, Amaury formed a coalition with the French king and Norman barons.

He seized the town in 1118 and his supporters held its citadel after Henry burned it in 1119; at the council of Reims Henry granted him the county in exchange for the keep. Taxation disputes drove him to revolt again in 1123.

Captured at Bourgtheroulde in 1124, he was freed when his captor defected and later recovered the county. By Agnès de Garlande he left sons Simon III and Amaury IV, and he died in 1137.

en:
Amaury VI de Montfort (1192–1241) was the eldest son of Simon IV de Montfort. Knighted in 1213, he fought under his father in the Albigensian Crusade and succeeded to the claim on Toulouse in 1218.

In 1224 he ceded his Languedoc lands to Louis VIII, who raised Montfort-l'Amaury into a county. Appointed Constable of France in 1230, he yielded the earldom of Leicester to his brother Simon in 1239.

Captured at Gaza on the Barons' Crusade, he spent eighteen months in Cairo. Released in 1241, he died at Otranto on his way home and was buried in Rome.

Beatrice de Montfort (c. 1248–1311) inherited the county of Montfort-l'Amaury as an infant in 1249, when her father John I died in Cyprus on the Seventh Crusade. In 1260 she married Robert IV, Count of Dreux, who became count of Montfort by right of his wife and ruled alongside her.

Her daughter Yolande married King Alexander III of Scotland and later Arthur II, Duke of Brittany; through Yolande she was ancestress of the Montfort dukes of Brittany. Her son John II became Count of Dreux, and Beatrice died on 9 March 1311.

en:
John of Montfort (1294–1345), son of Arthur II of Brittany and Yolande of Dreux, inherited the county of Montfort-l’Amaury from his mother in 1322. When Duke John III died in 1341, he claimed Brittany against his niece Joan of Penthièvre and her husband Charles of Blois, beginning the War of the Breton Succession.

Said to have been urged on by his wife, he rode to Nantes, where the townsmen swore loyalty, and was recognised as duke in May, though the great vassals kept away. Edward III promised military aid.

In September the peers awarded Brittany to Charles, and Philip VI confiscated Montfort-l’Amaury. Nantes fell in November and John was taken to the Louvre. He died in 1345; his wife Joanna of Flanders kept up the fight, and his son John IV later won the duchy.

en:
Joan of Flanders, called Jeanne la Flamme (c. 1295–1374), was the daughter of Louis I, Count of Nevers, and in 1329 married John of Montfort, claimant to Brittany. The childless death of Duke John III in 1341 sparked a succession dispute, with England supporting the Montfort claim and France backing Charles of Blois.

When Philip VI imprisoned her husband, Joan took command of the Montfort cause herself. At the 1342 siege of Hennebont she fought in armour, led three hundred men out to burn Charles of Blois's camp and held the town until English relief arrived.

She later took refuge in England, where Edward III confined her at Tickhill Castle, for reasons historians dispute. She died in September 1374; her son John IV later became Duke of Brittany.

en:
Richard of Montfort (died 1092) was the fifth lord of Montfort-l'Amaury, a son of Simon I and Agnès d'Évreux, who succeeded his half-brother Amaury II in 1089. His reign was consumed by a family feud: his uncle William, count of Évreux, and Raoul II of Tosny ravaged each other's lands after their wives fell out.

Richard took the count's side and was killed by an arrow at the siege of Conches in 1092. His death led both sides to negotiate a truce. He died unmarried, and his brother Simon II succeeded him.

Simon I of Montfort (died 1087) was the third lord of Montfort-l'Amaury, succeeding his father Amaury I. He continued the family's building programme, founding the church of Saint-Pierre. By his first wife Isabelle he had Amaury II and Guillaume, later bishop of Paris.

After Isabelle died, Simon sought Agnès d'Évreux, but her father refused; her half-brother Raoul de Tosny carried her off to Montfort to become his second wife. Agnès bore Richard, Simon II, Amaury III and Bertrade, who married Fulk IV of Anjou and then King Philip I of France.

西蒙一世·德·蒙福尔（1087年卒）是蒙福尔拉莫里的第三位领主，继其父阿马尔里克一世之位。他延续家族的营建工程，修建了圣彼得教堂。他先娶伊莎贝尔，生下阿马尔里克二世与后来出任巴黎主教的纪尧姆。

Simon II of Montfort (died 1101) was the sixth lord of Montfort-l'Amaury, a son of Simon I and Agnès d'Évreux, who succeeded his brother Richard after Richard was killed at Conches in 1092.

In 1098 William II Rufus of England, ruling Normandy while Duke Robert Curthose was on crusade, besieged Montfort, but Simon repulsed the attack. He died unmarried in 1101 and the lordship passed to his younger brother Amaury III.

en:
Simon III of Montfort, called the Bald (1117–1181), was count of Évreux from 1140 and lord of Montfort-l'Amaury from 1137, younger son of Amaury III. His father had divided his lands between his sons, but the death of Amaury IV reunited Évreux and Montfort under Simon.

For Montfort the family owed allegiance to the French king, and for Évreux to the English king, placing it amid their rivalry. Simon sided with Henry II of England and surrendered his fortresses to him. He later reconciled with Louis VII. Simon died in 1181.

en:
Simon IV de Montfort (c. 1175–1218) was lord of Montfort-l'Amaury from 1188 and, through his mother, Earl of Leicester in England. He joined the Fourth Crusade in 1199 but refused to share in the sack of Zara and left rather than march on Constantinople.

After the siege of Carcassonne in 1209, he was elected leader of the Albigensian Crusade in Languedoc. In 1210 he burned 140 Cathars at Minerve, and in 1213 he routed Peter II of Aragon at Muret.

He received the county of Toulouse in 1215 and was killed in June 1218 at the siege of Toulouse, struck in the head by a stone from a mangonel.

Yolande of Dreux (c. 1269–1322) was the daughter of Robert IV of Dreux and Beatrice of Montfort. In October 1285 she married Alexander III of Scotland, who died in March 1286; her pregnancy did not result in a living child and she returned to France. In 1294 she married Arthur of Brittany, Duke Arthur II from 1305.

She inherited Montfort-l'Amaury from her mother in 1311. After disputes with her stepson John III, she died on 2 August 1322, leaving it to her son John.

Mengu-Timur (died 1280), a son of Toqoqan and grandson of Batu, was khan of the Golden Horde from 1266 to 1280. He struck silver coins in his own name without the great khan's and declined to visit Kublai, making the Horde effectively independent.

He exchanged embassies with the Mamluk sultan Baybars and aided Kaidu against the Chagatai khan Baraq. He died soon after an unsuccessful campaign against Poland in 1280, and his son Toqta later ruled the Horde.

Abd al-Haqq I (1147–1217), son of the Marinid chief Muhyu, was the first leader of the Marinid dynasty, a Zenata Berber noble. After Muhyu died of wounds fighting for the Almohads at Alarcos in 1195, he took command of the Banu Marin.

After the Almohad disaster at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212, he led his tribe into north-eastern Morocco in 1213 or 1214, occupying the Rif. In 1217 an Almohad army defeated and killed him, and his son Uthman I succeeded.

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Uthman (c. 1297–1351) became Marinid sultan of Morocco in 1331. His dark complexion, inherited from a sub-Saharan mother, earned him the name Black Sultan. He married the Hafsid ruler's daughter Fatima, sealing an alliance against Zayyanid Tlemcen.

In 1333 he took Gibraltar from Castile and in 1337 seized Tlemcen, though his attack on Tarifa ended in disaster in 1339. Turning back to the Maghreb, he conquered Hafsid Ifriqiya in 1347, briefly reuniting the region as the Almohads had.

He then overreached with the Arab tribes, who defeated him near Kairouan in 1348, and his son Abu Inan Faris, governor of Tlemcen, proclaimed himself sultan at Fes. A tempest wrecked his fleet off Bougie and Abu Inan defeated him in 1350. Broken, he abdicated in the High Atlas and died there in 1351.

阿布·哈桑·阿里·本·奥斯曼（约1297—1351）于1331年即位为摩洛哥马林王朝苏丹。他的深色肤色得自撒哈拉以南出身的母亲，因此被称为“黑苏丹”。他娶哈夫斯王朝统治者之女法蒂玛，结盟对抗宰扬王朝的特莱姆森。

1333年他从卡斯蒂利亚手中夺取直布罗陀，1337年攻占特莱姆森，但1339年进攻塔里法惨败。随后他转回马格里布，1347年吞并哈夫斯王朝治下的伊夫里奇亚，一度像穆瓦希德王朝那样重新统一了这片地区。

随后他对阿拉伯部落操之过急，1348年在凯鲁万附近被击败，任特莱姆森总督的儿子阿布·伊南·法里斯在非斯自立为苏丹。他的舰队在贝贾亚近海被风暴摧毁，1350年又被阿布·伊南击败。他在大阿特拉斯山区退位，1351年死在那里。

Abu al-Rabi Sulayman (March 1289–23 November 1310) succeeded his brother Abu Thabit Amir as Marinid sultan in July 1308, while Ceuta was held by a Nasrid-backed pretender. When Nasr of Granada abandoned the pretender, Marinid and Granadan forces retook Ceuta in July 1309.

He sent a fleet that raised the Castilian siege of Algeciras in January 1310. His Granadine bride brought Algeciras and Ronda as dowry, but he died of illness without sons in November 1310, and his uncle Abu Sa'id Uthman II succeeded him.

en:
Abu Ali Omar was the Marinid prince who threatened to split Morocco in two. A designated heir of Sultan Abu Sa'id Uthman II, he rebelled in 1315 and entrenched himself in Fez; when he fell ill the sultan besieged the city and forced his surrender.

He lost the succession to his brother Abu al-Hasan and received an appanage centred on the Saharan trading city of Sijilmasa. In 1320 he rose again and seized much of southern Morocco, Marrakesh included, until defeated in 1322, when he was again allowed to keep Sijilmasa.

He then allied with the Zayyanid sultan Abu Tashufin of Tlemcen, the Marinids' enemy. In 1332 Abu al-Hasan, by then sultan, took Sijilmasa and had his brother put to death.

阿布·阿里·欧麦尔是险些把摩洛哥一分为二的马林王朝王子。他是苏丹阿布·赛义德·奥斯曼二世之子并曾被立为储君，1315年起兵反叛，据守非斯；他患病后，苏丹围攻非斯，迫使他投降。

阿布·阿里失去继承权，让位于兄弟阿布·哈桑，获封以撒哈拉商城西吉勒马萨为中心的封邑。1320年他再度起事，夺取包括马拉喀什在内的摩洛哥南部大片土地，1322年兵败，再次获准保有西吉勒马萨。

他与马林王朝的敌人、特莱姆森的扎扬王朝苏丹阿布·塔什芬结盟。1332年，已经继位的阿布·哈桑攻克西吉勒马萨，将兄长处死。

en:
Abu Inan Faris (1329–1358), son of the Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan Ali, was governing Tlemcen when Arab tribes routed his father at Kairouan in 1348. He returned to Fes and declared himself sultan, while Tlemcen and the central Maghreb rose in revolt.

After his father died in 1351 he retook Tlemcen in 1352 and Béjaïa in 1353. Granada, fearing an invasion, sponsored a short-lived revolt by his brother Abu al-Fadl. He took Tunis in 1357, becoming master of Ifriqiya, until intrigues forced him to retreat.

He built madrasas at Meknes and Fes, from which the Bou Inania madrasas take their name, and commissioned Ibn Juzayy to record Ibn Battuta's travels, finished in 1355. He fell ill in 1357, and as he recovered his vizier had him strangled in January 1358.

阿布·伊南·法里斯（1329—1358）是马林王朝苏丹阿布·哈桑·阿里之子。1348年阿拉伯部落在凯鲁万击溃其父时，他正担任特莱姆森总督，随即返回非斯自立为苏丹，特莱姆森与马格里布中部则趁机叛乱。

1351年父亲死后，他于1352年重克特莱姆森，1353年攻取贝贾亚。格拉纳达担心他入侵，资助他的兄弟阿布·法德勒发动了短暂的叛乱。1357年他占领突尼斯，成为伊夫里奇亚之主，随后因朝中阴谋被迫退兵。

他在梅克内斯和非斯修建经学院，布·伊纳尼亚经学院即以他命名；又命伊本·朱扎伊记录伊本·白图泰的游历，该书于1355年完成。1357年他一病不起，渐渐康复时于1358年1月被维齐尔派人勒死。

en:
Abu Malik Abd al-Wahid (died 1339), also called Abomelique, was a son of the Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan Ali and his foremost general in Al-Andalus. Though he had lost an eye, he governed Algeciras and in 1333 took Gibraltar from Castile, then fought against rebels at Tlemcen in 1334.

When the truce expired in 1338, he returned to Ronda with a large force sent by his father. Castile, Aragon and Portugal joined against the threat and blockaded the Strait, while Alfonso XI raided deep into Marinid territory.

In 1339 he invaded, besieging Jerez de la Frontera without taking it. On the way back his loot-laden army was ambushed and destroyed, some 10,000 men killed or captured. Caught without armour or a horse, he hid by a stream and feigned death, but a Castilian soldier saw him move and killed him with a spear.

1339年，阿布·马利克以入侵作答，围攻赫雷斯-德拉弗龙特拉而未能攻克。满载战利品回师途中，他的军队遭到伏击而覆没，约一万人被杀或被俘。阿布·马利克未披甲、无坐骑，藏在溪边装死，却被一名卡斯蒂利亚士兵发现动弹，用长矛刺死。

en:
Abu Sa'id Uthman II (December 1276–August 1331), a younger son of Abu Yusuf Yaqub, succeeded his nephew Abu al-Rabi Sulayman as Marinid sultan in November 1310. Pious and peace-loving, he returned Algeciras and Ronda to Granada in 1313 to end Iberian entanglements.

His son Abu Ali rebelled in Fez in 1315; Uthman removed him from the succession and named Abu al-Hasan heir, then pardoned him after a second rebellion years later. He adorned Fez with the Al-Attarine and other madrasas, and died near Taza in 1331.

阿布·赛义德·奥斯曼·本·雅各布（1276年12月—1331年8月），即奥斯曼二世，为阿布·优素福·雅各布的幼子之一，1310年11月继侄儿阿布·拉比·苏莱曼之位，成为马林王朝苏丹。他虔诚而喜好和平，1313年将阿尔赫西拉斯与龙达归还格拉纳达，以了结伊比利亚半岛的纠葛。

en:
Abu Thabit Amir (1284–28 July 1308) became Marinid sultan in May 1307 after his father Abu Yaqub Yusuf was assassinated at the long siege of Tlemcen. With several rivals challenging him and a Nasrid-backed pretender holding Ceuta, he defeated his rivals, negotiated the lifting of the siege and hurried north.

To direct operations he founded a town south of Ceuta, Tetouan, but fell ill and died there in July 1308 after a year's reign, leaving the throne to his brother Abu al-Rabi Sulayman.

阿布·萨比特·阿米尔（1284—1308年7月28日）于1307年5月即位为马林王朝苏丹，此前他的父亲阿布·雅各布·优素福·纳赛尔在对特莱姆森的长期围城战中遇刺。当时多名觊觎者与他争位，格拉纳达支持的僭位者据有休达。他击败对手，又达成协议、有序解围，随即挥师北返。

为统筹战事，他在休达以南修筑城镇得土安，但仅在位一年便染病，于1308年7月死于得土安，王位由其弟阿布·拉比·苏莱曼继承。

en:
Abu Yahya ibn Abd al-Haqq (died 1258) was a Marinid ruler, a son of Abd al-Haqq I who succeeded his brother Muhammad I in 1244. He seized Meknes, but an Almohad counter-offensive drove him back into eastern Morocco.

When the Almohad caliph was killed attacking Tlemcen in 1248, Abu Yahya destroyed the remnants of his army, made himself master of eastern Morocco and captured Fez. By his death in 1258, the Almohads had been reduced to southern Morocco.

阿布·叶海亚·本·阿卜杜勒-哈克（？—1258）是马林王朝首领，阿卜杜勒-哈克一世之子，1244年继其兄穆罕默德一世之位。他攻占梅克内斯，却因穆瓦希德人的反攻而退回摩洛哥东部。

1248年，穆瓦希德哈里发在进攻特莱姆森时兵败被杀，阿布·叶海亚随即歼灭其残军，控制整个摩洛哥东部，并攻克非斯。到1258年他去世时，穆瓦希德人已退守摩洛哥南部。

en:
Abu Yaqub Yusuf an-Nasr (c. 1230–13 May 1307) succeeded his father as Marinid sultan in 1286, and faced revolts including from his own son Abu Amir. After Castile took Tarifa in 1292 he failed to recover it, and in 1295 ceded Algeciras to Granada, abandoning Spain.

He then turned on Tlemcen, besieging it from 1299 at al-Mansura. On 13 May 1307, as the city neared surrender, a eunuch killed him in his camp, and the siege ended under his successor Abu Thabit.

阿布·雅各布·优素福·纳赛尔（约1230—1307年5月13日）于1286年继其父之位成为马林王朝苏丹，在位期间遭遇多次叛乱，亲生儿子阿布·阿米尔也曾起兵反叛。1292年卡斯蒂利亚夺取塔里法，他反攻不克，1295年将阿尔赫西拉斯割给格拉纳达，退出伊比利亚半岛。

en:
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq (c. 1212–20 March 1286), fourth son of Marinid founder Abd al-Haqq I, was governor of Taza when his brother Abu Yahya died in 1258; he displaced his nephew and seized power. He retook Salé in 1260 and entered Marrakesh in 1269, extinguishing the Almohad Caliphate and unifying Morocco around Fez; he founded New Fez in 1276.

From 1275 he repeatedly crossed to Spain to aid Granada against Castile, winning at Écija. He died at Algeciras in March 1286 and was buried at Chellah.

en:
Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abi Zar al-Fasi (died between 1310 and 1320) was a Moroccan historian and scholar of Fes, the presumed author of the Rawd al-Qirtas. Written for Marinid sultan Abu Sa'id Uthman II, it chronicles the kings of the Maghreb and the history of Fes from Idris I in 788 down to the Marinids.

Divided into four parts, it became one of the most widely circulated medieval Maghrebi histories. Its authorship was long debated.

阿布·哈桑·阿里·伊本·阿比·扎尔·法西（1310至1320年间去世）是摩洛哥史学家、非斯学者，被认为是《罗乌德·吉尔塔斯》的作者。该书奉马林王朝苏丹阿布·赛义德·奥斯曼二世之命而作，记述788年伊德里斯一世以来至马林王朝的马格里布诸王史与非斯城史。

全书分为四部分，是中世纪流传最广的马格里布史书之一，其作者归属曾长期存在争议。

en:
Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Battuta (1304–1368/69) was a Berber Muslim scholar and the most widely travelled man of the pre-modern world. Born in Tangier to a family of qadis, he left in 1325 for the pilgrimage to Mecca, not returning for twenty-four years, wandering the Somali and Swahili coasts, Anatolia and the Golden Horde.

In 1333 he reached Delhi, where Muhammad bin Tughluq made him a judge, spending six years between favour and suspicion. In 1341 he led a mission to China, and bandits nearly killed him on the way. He became chief judge in the Maldives, reached China, and crossed the Sahara to Mali.

Back in Morocco in 1354, he dictated his travels to Ibn Juzayy for Sultan Abu Inan, completed in 1355 as the Rihla. By one estimate he covered 117,000 km, farther than Zheng He or Marco Polo; nearly all we know comes from it. He died in 1368 or 1369.

艾布·阿卜杜拉·穆罕默德·伊本·白图泰（1304—1368或1369）是柏柏尔穆斯林学者，也是前现代世界走得最远的人。他生于丹吉尔的教法法官世家，1325年启程前往麦加朝觐，此后二十四年未归，足迹遍及索马里与斯瓦希里海岸、安纳托利亚和金帐汗国。

1333年他抵达德里，穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克任命他为法官，此后六年他在恩宠与谋反嫌疑之间起落。1341年他率团出使中国，途中遭强盗袭击险些丧命。他在马尔代夫任首席法官，随后抵达中国，后来又穿越撒哈拉前往马里。

1354年返回摩洛哥后，他奉苏丹阿布·伊南之命向伊本·朱扎伊口述经历，1355年成书，即《游记》。据一种估算，他的行程约11.7万公里，超过郑和和马可·波罗，而其生平几乎全靠这部书流传。他在1368或1369年去世。

en:
Ibrahim ibn Ali, known as Abu Salim and by the regnal title al-Musta'in billah, was a Marinid sultan and a son of Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Uthman. Born around 1335, he took the throne at Fes in 1359 after Abu Bakr ibn Faris, in the unsettled years following Abu Inan Faris's murder.

As ruler he named Ibn Khaldun as his judge of mazalim. After two years and three months, civilian and military officials overthrew him in the autumn of 1361, and Tashfin ibn Ali succeeded him.

易卜拉欣·本·阿里，又称阿布·萨利姆，王号“穆斯塔因·比拉”，马林王朝苏丹，阿布·哈桑·阿里·本·奥斯曼之子，约生于1335年。1359年，他在阿布·伊南·法里斯遇刺后的动荡岁月中，于阿布·伯克尔·本·法里斯之后在非斯登上王位。

en: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Haqq (1202–1244) was a Marinid ruler, a son of Abd al-Haqq I and younger brother of Uthman I, whom he succeeded in 1240. He continued fighting the Almohad Caliphate, especially around Meknes. On 12 November 1244 he fell in battle against the Almohads, killed by Juan Gaitan, an officer of Christian mercenaries.
