Tashfin ibn Ali, known by the kunya Abu Umar, was a Marinid sultan and a son of Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Uthman. In 1361 he succeeded Ibrahim ibn Ali at Fes, amid the succession turmoil after Abu Inan Faris's murder in 1358.

Tashfin was a figurehead in the grip of his vizier Umar ibn Abd Allah. After a three-month reign the vizier deposed him around December 1361, and he died soon afterwards. Muhammad II ibn Faris then succeeded him.

Abram Petrovich Gannibal (c. 1696–1781) was a Russian military engineer and general of African origin. Captured as a child and taken to Constantinople, he was brought to Moscow in 1704 as a gift for Peter the Great, who became his godfather. He accompanied Peter on campaigns and studied engineering abroad.

After Peter's death he was exiled to Siberia in 1727 and built fortifications there. Pardoned in 1730, he continued to serve in Siberia until 1733.

Under Empress Elizabeth he rose to chief military engineer in 1756 and general-in-chief in 1759. One of his great-grandsons was the poet Alexander Pushkin.

阿布拉姆·彼得罗维奇·汉尼拔（约1696—1781）是非洲裔俄国军事工程师、上将。他幼年被俘带往君士坦丁堡，1704年作为礼物被送到莫斯科献给彼得大帝，彼得成为他的教父。他随彼得出征，并在国外学习工程。

en:
Afanasy Lavrentievich Ordin-Nashchokin (1605–1680) was a Russian statesman and diplomat under Tsar Alexis. Born to a poor landowning family near Pskov, he distinguished himself in the Pskov uprising of 1650 and the Russo-Swedish War of 1656–1658.

As head of the Posolsky Prikaz from 1667, he negotiated the Truce of Andrusovo with Poland-Lithuania, abolished tolls, set up a postal service and promoted shipbuilding on the Dvina and Volga.

The first junior noble to reach boyar rank through merit rather than family connections, he was dismissed in 1671, took monastic vows and died in 1680.

阿法纳西·拉夫连季耶维奇·奥尔金-纳晓金（1605—1680）是沙皇阿列克谢麾下的政治家与外交家。他出身普斯科夫附近的贫寒地主家庭，在1650年普斯科夫起义和1656—1658年俄瑞战争中崭露头角。

1667年起他执掌使节衙门，与波兰立陶宛联邦谈判达成《安德鲁索沃停战协定》，废除关税，兴办邮政，并推动西德维纳河与伏尔加河上的造船业。

他是俄国第一位凭功绩而非家族关系晋封波雅尔的低级贵族，1671年被解职后出家修道，1680年去世。

Alexander Peresvet (died 8 September 1380) was a Russian monk-warrior famed for the Battle of Kulikovo. Probably from Bryansk, he was tonsured at the Boris and Gleb Monastery in Rostov and later followed Sergius of Radonezh at the Trinity Lavra.

In 1380, as Dmitry Donskoy marched against the Tatar warlord Mamai, Sergius of Radonezh blessed the campaign and sent Peresvet and Rodion Oslyabya with the army.

At the opening of the battle Peresvet met the Golden Horde champion Chelubey in single combat, and the two killed each other at the first charge. Legend says he alone kept his saddle.

Prince Alexey Mikhailovich Lvov (1580s–1653) was a Russian statesman. He was voivode at Nizhny Novgorod in 1610, fought with Dmitry Pozharsky's militia in 1612, and in 1613 signed the charter electing Mikhail Romanov tsar.

After embassies to Denmark and Poland, where he helped conclude the Peace of Polyanovka in 1634, he headed the Grand Palace Office from 1627 to 1647 and effectively led the government in Mikhail's final years. He retired in 1652 and died in 1653.

Andrei Rublev (c. 1360–c. 1430) was the greatest master of medieval Russian icon and fresco painting. First recorded in 1405, he joined Theophanes the Greek in painting the Cathedral of the Annunciation in the Moscow Kremlin.

In 1408 he and Daniel Chorny decorated the Dormition Cathedral in Vladimir, and from 1425 to 1427 the Trinity Cathedral at the Trinity Lavra. His only fully authenticated work is the icon of the Trinity of about 1410.

At Moscow's Andronikov Monastery he painted the Saviour Cathedral and died. In 1551 a church council made his style a model for church painting; he was canonized in 1988.

Antonio Possevino (1533–1611) was a Mantuan-born Jesuit and papal diplomat. He joined the Society of Jesus in 1559 and founded Jesuit schools in Savoy.

As envoy of Pope Gregory XIII from 1578, he led missions across northern and eastern Europe: he received King John III of Sweden into the Catholic Church and travelled to Moscow to negotiate with Ivan the Terrible.

Mediating between Ivan and Stephen Báthory of Poland, he secured the Truce of Jam Zapolski in 1582, ending the war between Russia and Poland-Lithuania. He later wrote an account of Russia and died in Ferrara in 1611.

他在伊凡与波兰的斯特凡·巴托里之间斡旋，促成1582年的《亚姆·扎波尔斯基停战协定》，结束了俄国与波兰立陶宛之间的战争。他晚年著有俄国见闻录，1611年在费拉拉去世。

en:
Antonio Rinaldi (1709–1794) was an Italian architect from Palermo who worked most of his life in Russia. In 1751 Hetman Kirill Razumovsky summoned him to decorate his residences in what is now Ukraine.

From 1754 he served as chief architect of the young court of Peter III and Catherine II at Oranienbaum, where he built Peter III's palace and the Chinese Palace.

In the 1770s, as Grigory Orlov's architect, he designed the Marble Palace in Saint Petersburg and the vast Gatchina Castle, along with monuments at Tsarskoe Selo. In 1784 poor health took him back to Italy, and he died in Rome.

安东尼奥·里纳尔迪（1709—1794）是巴勒莫出身的意大利建筑师，大半生在俄国工作。1751年，盖特曼基里尔·拉祖莫夫斯基召他到今乌克兰境内装饰自己的府邸。

1754年起，他担任彼得三世与叶卡捷琳娜二世年轻宫廷的首席建筑师，在奥拉宁鲍姆修建了彼得三世宫与中国宫。

1770年代，他作为格里戈里·奥尔洛夫的建筑师，设计了圣彼得堡的大理石宫和宏伟的加特契纳宫，以及皇村的纪念建筑。1784年他因健康恶化返回意大利，后在罗马去世。

Aigusta Anastasia (c. 1320–1345), most likely a daughter of Lithuania's Grand Duke Gediminas, was baptized Orthodox as Anastasia to marry Prince Simeon of Moscow in 1333. The match promised better relations between them, but war resumed in 1335.

Her sons died in infancy, and her daughter Vasilisa married Prince Mikhail Vasilevich of Kashin in 1350. She took the veil shortly before her death on 11 March 1345 and was buried in a Kremlin church she had founded.

Bogdan Matveyevich Khitrovo (c. 1615–1680) was a Russian boyar and statesman under Tsars Alexis and Feodor III. As governor of Temnikov in the 1640s he founded a chain of forts on the Volga, including Simbirsk.

From 1654 until his death he headed the Kremlin Armoury, putting the tsar's icon painters under his patronage. Despite the opposition of Avvakum, he encouraged Simon Ushakov and others to absorb Western naturalism.

In his last sixteen years he administered the Kremlin palaces and other state estates. He died in March 1680, leaving books and icons to monasteries and freeing his slaves in his will.

波格丹·马特维耶维奇·希特罗沃（约1615—1680）是沙皇阿列克谢和费奥多尔三世两朝的波雅尔与重臣。1640年代他任捷姆尼科夫总督，在伏尔加河沿线修建一系列堡垒，辛比尔斯克即出自其手。

1654年至去世他长期主持克里姆林兵器库，沙皇家的圣像画家因而受其庇护。他不顾大司祭阿瓦库姆的反对，鼓励西蒙·乌沙科夫等人吸收西方的写实技法。

生命的最后16年，他管理克里姆林宫殿及其他国有地产。他于1680年3月去世，遗嘱将书籍和圣像赠予修道院，并释放自己的奴仆。

Boris Feodorovich Godunov (1552–1605) rose at the court of Ivan the Terrible as an oprichnik and married the daughter of Malyuta Skuratov; his sister Irina wed the heir Feodor in 1580, making Boris the future tsar's brother-in-law.

From Feodor I's accession in 1584 he was the de facto ruler of Russia. When Feodor died childless in 1598, Boris had himself elected tsar by the Zemsky Sobor and was crowned.

He imported foreign teachers and made peace with Sweden in 1595. In 1600 he moved against the rival Romanov family, forcing Feodor Romanov into a monastery. Boris died in April 1605 during the Time of Troubles.

Daniil Aleksandrovich (1261–5 March 1303), known as Daniel of Moscow, was the youngest son of Alexander Nevsky and the first prince of Moscow, enfeoffed on Nevsky's death in 1263 and ruling only from 1282. A peacemaker among the Rus princes, he took Kolomna from Ryazan in 1301 and received Pereslavl-Zalessky in 1302.

He founded Moscow's Danilov Monastery and died in monastic vows on 5 March 1303, having never held Vladimir's grand princely throne. He was the forefather of the Daniilovichi line.

Dmitry Gerasimov (c. 1465 – after 1535) was a Russian translator, diplomat and philologist, probably born in Novgorod. After learning Latin and German in Livonia, he served as interpreter on Vasily III's embassies, including the mission to Emperor Maximilian I.

In 1525 Vasily III sent him as envoy to Pope Clement VII in Rome to discuss an anti-Ottoman league. There he described Russia's geography to Paolo Giovio, who compiled the information in a book; Battista Agnese then mapped it, providing a pattern for most sixteenth-century maps of Muscovy.

Gerasimov also translated religious works and Donatus's grammar. Comparing Latin with Church Slavonic, he proposed terms for Slavic grammar and collaborated with Maximus the Greek.

德米特里·格拉西莫夫（约1465—1535年后）是俄国翻译家、外交官与语言学者，可能出生于诺夫哥罗德。他在利沃尼亚学会拉丁语和德语，此后在瓦西里三世的使团中担任译员，曾随团出使皇帝马克西米利安一世。

1525年，瓦西里三世派他为使节前往罗马觐见教皇克雷芒七世，商谈结成反对奥斯曼的联盟。他在罗马向保罗·乔维奥讲述俄国地理，乔维奥将这些信息汇编成书，巴蒂斯塔·阿涅塞随后据此绘制地图，成为16世纪多数莫斯科维亚地图的范本。

格拉西莫夫还翻译宗教著作和多纳图斯的语法书。他比较拉丁语与教会斯拉夫语，为斯拉夫语语法提出术语，并与马克西姆·格列克合作。

Domenico Trezzini (c. 1670–1734) was a Swiss-Italian architect from Ticino who became the first architect of St Petersburg. After training in Italy and working in Copenhagen, he was recruited by Peter I and reached the new capital in 1704.

He contributed to major projects including the Peter and Paul Fortress and its cathedral (1712–1733), the Summer Palace, the Twelve Collegia and the Alexander Nevsky Monastery. He founded a school on the European model, helped define the Petrine Baroque and trained Mikhail Zemtsov and other Russian architects, dying in St Petersburg in 1734.

多梅尼科·特列齐尼（约1670—1734）是瑞士提契诺出身的意大利裔建筑师，圣彼得堡的第一位建筑师。他在意大利学艺，后在哥本哈根工作，受彼得一世招募，1704年来到新都。

Elena Vasilyevna Glinskaya (c. 1510–1538), daughter of a Lithuanian prince, became the second wife of Grand Prince Vasili III in 1526, after he set aside his first consort amid opposition from the boyars and the Church. In 1530 she bore Ivan, the future Ivan the Terrible, and on Vasili's death in 1533 she became Russia's first female regent, ruling for her three-year-old son.

Her government fought Lithuania to an armistice in 1537 and carried out the currency reform of 1535, which introduced the kopek and unified the coinage. She died suddenly in April 1538, amid rumours of poisoning.

en:
Fyodor Apraksin (1661–1728) was one of Russia's first admirals and a lifelong friend of Peter the Great. After his sister married Tsar Feodor III in 1681 he became a stolnik, and in 1692 he was appointed governor of Arkhangelsk. From 1697 he supervised the building of the first Russian fleet at Voronezh.

He fought at the Azov siege of 1696, became the first governor of Azov in 1700 and general-admiral in 1708. He led Russian squadrons in the Great Northern War, including an expedition into the Gulf of Bothnia in 1719. He headed the Admiralty from 1717 and commanded the Baltic Fleet from 1723, and died in Moscow in 1728.

en:
Feodor Nikitich Romanov (1553–1633), first of the Romanov surname, served Tsar Feodor I against Sweden. A popular candidate for the throne in 1598, he was forced by Boris Godunov in 1600 to take monastic vows as Filaret.

The False Dmitry made him metropolitan of Rostov in 1605, and he was imprisoned in Poland from 1610 to 1618 for rejecting Sigismund III as tsar. Freed after the Truce of Deulino, he was enthroned Patriarch of Moscow in 1619 and co-ruled Russia with his son Tsar Michael until his death in 1633.

He reformed tax assessment and collection and encouraged theological publishing. He also reorganized the army with the help of foreign officers.

他改革税额评定与征收，鼓励出版神学著作。他还借助外国军官整顿军队。

en:
Francesco Bartolomeo Rastrelli (1700–1771) was an Italian architect born in Paris, where his Florentine father Carlo Rastrelli worked as a sculptor. In 1716 he accompanied his father to Saint Petersburg at Peter I's invitation and trained in his workshop.

Appointed senior court architect in 1730, he served Empresses Anna and Elizabeth, creating the opulent Late Baroque of the Winter Palace, the Catherine Palace at Tsarskoye Selo and the Smolny Convent. Elizabeth's death in 1762 left his planned bell tower at Smolny unfinished.

Under Catherine II he retired to Courland, where he supervised the completion and decoration of the ducal palaces. He died in 1771, shortly after joining the Imperial Academy of Arts.

叶卡捷琳娜二世时期他退隐库尔兰，监督公爵宫殿的竣工和装饰。1771年他去世，此前不久刚入选帝国艺术学院。

François Le Fort (1656–1699) was a Genevan adventurer who became Peter the Great's favourite and Russia's first general-admiral. He entered Russian service as a captain in 1678.

From 1690 he was the tsar's closest companion, organizing the toy-army manoeuvres and the All-Joking, All-Drunken Synod of Fools and Jesters, and rose to general by 1693.

In 1695 he took naval command in the Azov campaigns, and in 1696 jointly led Peter's Grand Embassy to Western Europe. He died in Moscow in March 1699, mourned by Peter as his one trusty man.

Elena Alexandrovna (died 1 March 1331), possibly a daughter of Prince Alexander Glebovich of Smolensk, was the first wife of Ivan I Kalita of Moscow; neither her birth date nor the year of the marriage is recorded.

She bore Ivan four sons and four daughters, among them Simeon the Proud and Ivan II, both later grand princes of Moscow, and Maria, married in 1328 to a prince of Rostov.

On her deathbed in the Spassky Monastery she took the veil under the name Solomonida, leaving three young sons then aged thirteen, five and three. She was buried in the monastery cathedral in the Moscow Kremlin, the first tomb in Moscow's grand-princely mausoleum.

en:
Ivan Bolotnikov (1565–1608) led a great peasant uprising during the Time of Troubles. A slave of Prince Andrei Teliatevsky, he fled to the Cossacks, was captured by Crimean Tatars and sold as a helmsman on a Turkish galley, then freed by German ships and carried to Venice.

Returning through Poland, he heard tales of Tsar Dmitri and met Mikhail Molchanov. In 1606 Molchanov sent him to Putivl. There he raised rebels, defeated the tsar's troops at Kromy and besieged Moscow.

Driven back to Kaluga and then Tula, he surrendered to Vasily Shuisky in October 1607 after a long siege. He was taken to Kargopol, blinded and drowned in 1608.

Ivan Fyodorov (c. 1510–1583) was the first printer of Muscovy. He became a deacon in the Moscow Kremlin and in 1564 set up the Moscow Print Yard with Pyotr Mstislavets, issuing the Apostol, the first dated printed book in Russia.

Persecuted by scribes and forced to flee after his workshop burned, he found refuge with Hetman Hrehory Chodkiewicz in Lithuania, printing the Didactic Gospel at Zabłudów in 1569. From 1572 he worked in Lviv.

In the service of Prince Konstanty Wasyl Ostrogski, he established a press at Ostrog and printed the first complete Church Slavonic Bible in 1581. He died in Lviv in 1583.

Ivan Gramotin (d. 1638) was a Russian diplomat and head of the Posolsky Prikaz through the Time of Troubles. First appointed its head in 1605 under False Dmitry I, he negotiated with Polish envoys in 1606, then served False Dmitry II and King Sigismund III, who restored him to the post.

Sent to Poland in 1612 over Wladislaus's claim to the throne, he befriended Filaret, later patriarch. After returning to Moscow in 1618 he handled Turkish and English negotiations.

Exiled at Filaret's insistence in 1626 for his intrigues, he returned in 1634. He died a monk at the Trinity Lavra in 1638.

en:
Ivan I Danilovich, nicknamed Kalita (Moneybag) (c. 1288–1340), was the fourth son of Daniel of Moscow and a grandson of Alexander Nevsky. He became Prince of Moscow in 1325, after his brother Yury was murdered by Dmitry of Tver, and won the khan's favour over its rival Tver. Metropolitan Peter made Moscow his residence, and in 1326 Ivan laid the foundation of the first stone church.

When Tver rose against the Mongols in 1327, Özbeg Khan sent him with a Tatar army to crush it. The khan divided the grand principality between him and Alexander of Suzdal in 1328; after Alexander's death in 1331, Ivan became sole Grand Prince of Vladimir.

He collected the khan's tribute and spent it on Moscow. In 1339 his rival Alexander of Tver was executed at the Horde, ending a struggle of thirty-five years. Ivan died in 1340, and his son Simeon succeeded him.

伊凡一世·丹尼洛维奇，绰号“卡利塔”（钱袋）（约1288—1340），是莫斯科王公丹尼尔的第四子，亚历山大·涅夫斯基之孙。1325年，兄长尤里被特维尔的德米特里杀害，他继任莫斯科王公，在汗廷宠遇中胜过宿敌特维尔。都主教彼得选定莫斯科为驻地，1326年，伊凡为第一座石造教堂奠基。

1327年特维尔爆发反蒙古起义，月即别汗派他率军镇压。1328年，大汗把大公国分给他与苏兹达尔的亚历山大；1331年亚历山大死后，伊凡独任弗拉基米尔大公。

他替大汗征收各王公的贡赋，并用在莫斯科身上。1339年，他的对手特维尔的亚历山大在金帐汗国被处死，三十五年的争斗就此结束。伊凡于1340年去世，其子谢苗继位。

Ivan II Ivanovich, called the Fair (30 March 1326 – 13 November 1359), was a son of Ivan I Kalita. After his brother Simeon died of the Black Death in 1353, he succeeded as prince of Moscow and grand prince of Vladimir.

A passive ruler, he let Algirdas of Lithuania take Bryansk and Oleg of Riazan raid his lands; yet aided by Metropolitan Alexius he annexed Borovsk and Vereya. His second wife bore him Dmitry Donskoy, and he died in 1359.

en:
Ivan IV, known as the Terrible (1530–1584), was Grand Prince of Moscow from 1533 and in 1547 became the first Tsar of all Russia. His father died when he was three and his regent mother in 1538, leaving him to feuding boyar families. With his Chosen Council he revised the law code and created the streltsy, Russia's first standing army.

Kazan fell in 1552, and he marked the victory with St Basil's Cathedral on Red Square; further campaigns took Astrakhan, giving Russia the whole Volga. He dismissed the council and launched the Livonian War (1558–1583), which failed to win Livonia.

His oprichniki, Russia's first political police, purged the nobility and massacred Novgorod's people. He is believed to have killed his heir, Ivan Ivanovich, in anger. His son Feodor succeeded him in 1584; Feodor's childless death in 1598 ended the Rurik dynasty and led into the Time of Troubles.

伊凡四世，史称伊凡雷帝（1530—1584），1533年起为莫斯科大公，1547年成为首位全俄罗斯沙皇。他三岁丧父，摄政的母亲于1538年去世，在波雅尔家族的争斗中长大。他与选拔会议一道修订法典，建立俄国第一支常备军射击军。

1552年喀山陷落，他在红场修建圣瓦西里大教堂纪念胜利；此后的战役攻取阿斯特拉罕，整个伏尔加河归俄国所有。他后来解散选拔会议，发动利沃尼亚战争（1558—1583），最终未能夺得利沃尼亚。

他的特辖军是俄国第一支政治警察，清洗贵族，屠杀诺夫哥罗德居民。据信他在盛怒之下杀死了继承人伊凡·伊凡诺维奇。费奥多尔1584年继位，1598年无嗣去世，留里克王朝终结，进入混乱时期。

Ivan Viskovatyi (c. 1510s–1570) was the first head of the Posolsky Prikaz, the foreign office of Ivan the Terrible. Given charge of diplomacy in 1549, he directed Russian foreign policy through the 1550s, when Kazan and Astrakhan were conquered, and in 1555 negotiated privileges for the English Muscovy Company. He also organised the diplomatic archive and formal registers of embassies.

In 1561 he became Keeper of the Seal and entered the Boyar Duma, later leading an embassy to Denmark. During the oprichnina he was accused of treason after the sack of Novgorod and publicly executed in Moscow on 25 July 1570.

伊万·维斯科瓦季（约1510年代—1570）是伊凡雷帝外交衙门的首任长官。1549年他受命掌管外交，在1550年代喀山和阿斯特拉罕被征服的十年间主持俄国外交，1555年谈成给予英国莫斯科公司的贸易特权。他还整理外交档案，正式编纂使节簿。

James Bruce (1669–1735) was a Russian field marshal and scientist of Scottish descent, and one of Peter the Great's ablest lieutenants. He rebuilt the artillery lost at Narva in 1700 and commanded the guns at Poltava in 1709.

One of the most learned men in Russia, he opened its first observatory in 1701, and his library of over fifteen hundred volumes later passed to the Academy of Sciences.

He headed the mining and manufacturing collegiums from 1717 and became one of Russia's first counts in 1721. Muscovites rumoured him a magician.

Jean-Baptiste Le Blond (1679–1719) was a French architect and garden designer, known in Paris for his hôtels particuliers and for a seminal treatise on formal gardens in 1709.

Invited by Peter the Great, he arrived at St Petersburg in 1716 with the title of Architect-General. He laid out workshops and nurseries along the Neva, introduced oil-lantern lighting for the main streets, and drew up an unexecuted grid plan centred on Vasilievsky Island. He helped plan the first palace and cascades at Peterhof in 1717. He died of smallpox there in 1719.

Joseph Volotsky (1439–1515) was a Russian Orthodox monk and theologian. About 1459 he entered a monastery at Borovsk and in 1477 became its hegumen, but in 1479 left to found the Joseph-Volokolamsk Monastery.

In his book The Enlightener he attacked the Judaizer heresy, demanding death for unrepentant heretics, and at the councils of 1503–1504 led the Possessors, defending monastic landownership against the Non-Possessors. He also taught that the tsar held autocratic power. He died in 1515 and was canonized in 1579.

约瑟夫·沃洛茨基（1439—1515）是俄罗斯正教会修士与神学家。约1459年他进入博罗夫斯克的修道院，1477年成为院长，1479年离开并创立约瑟夫—沃洛科拉姆斯克修道院。

Marco Ruffo, known in Russian chronicles as Mark Fryazin, was an Italian architect active in Moscow in the late fifteenth century. His Italian name remains uncertain; Ruffo was a nineteenth-century conjecture.

In 1484 he built a treasury for Ivan III in the Kremlin, followed in 1487 by the Small Embankment Palace. His surviving work is the Beklemishevskaya tower, and he also worked on the Kremlin's Spasskaya and Nikolskaya towers, later completed by Solari.

He began the Palace of Facets in 1487, completed by Solari in 1491. Chronicles last mention him in 1491; his later fate is unknown.

1487年他开始建造多棱宫，1491年由索拉里完成。编年史对他的最后记载是1491年，此后下落不明。

en:
Maria Yaroslavna of Borovsk (c. 1420–1485), daughter of the prince of Borovsk, became grand princess of Moscow on marrying Vasily II in 1433. During the civil war she was exiled to Galich when Dmitry Shemyaka seized Moscow, and in 1446 was captured and sent to Uglich with her husband.

Mother of Ivan III, she granted tax exemptions to the Trinity Lavra in 1450 and the Kirillo-Belozersky Monastery in 1471, and after her husband's death inherited Rostov.

In 1480 she blessed her son's campaign against Ahmed Khan. She took the veil as Marfa in 1482 and died in 1485.

en:
Alexius (before 1296–1378) was Metropolitan of Kiev and all Rus' from 1354 and a patron saint of Moscow. The son of a Chernigov boyar, he became a monk around 1313 and Bishop of Vladimir in 1352 before his election as metropolitan.

As spiritual tutor of the young Dmitry Donskoy, he led the Muscovite government as regent and backed Dmitry against Tver and Nizhny Novgorod. In 1357 the Golden Horde khan Jani Beg summoned him to cure his blind mother.

He founded the Andronikov and Chudov monasteries. He tried in vain to persuade Sergius of Radonezh to succeed him, and was canonized in 1448.

阿列克塞（1296年前—1378年）1354年起任基辅及全罗斯都主教，是莫斯科的主保圣人之一。他出身切尔尼戈夫的波雅尔家庭，约1313年出家，1352年成为弗拉基米尔主教，此后被选为都主教。

他创立了安德罗尼科夫修道院和丘多夫修道院。他曾试图说服拉多涅茨的谢尔盖继任但未成功，1448年被封圣。

en:
Natalya Naryshkina (1651–1694) was raised in the household of Moscow boyar Artamon Matveyev and became Tsar Alexis's second wife in 1671, and in 1672 she bore the future Peter the Great. As tsaritsa she broke with terem custom, becoming the first Russian woman to attend a theatre.

She was made regent for the young Peter in 1682 but was ousted by her stepdaughter Sophia amid the Streltsy revolt, which killed two of her brothers and Matveyev.

Under Sophia's regency Natalya lived with Peter at Preobrazhenskoe. Restored after Peter seized power in 1689, she ruled until her death in 1694.

Patrick Gordon (1635–1699) was a Scottish soldier who became a Russian general. Born in Aberdeenshire, he served Sweden and Poland before joining the Russian army in 1661.

A major-general by 1678 and commander at Kiev, in 1689 his troops turned the Moscow coup in Peter the Great's favour against Sophia, and his movable rampart helped take Azov in 1696. Peter made him a trusted adviser and organizer of his Western-style army, and Gordon secured Muscovy's first permanent Catholic church. He died in Moscow, leaving a detailed diary.

en:
Peter I, called the Great (1672–1725), was tsar of Russia from 1682 and its first emperor from 1721, the ruler who forced Russia toward Europe. Chosen tsar at ten, he first ruled with Ivan V under Sophia's regency, overthrowing her in 1689. He ruled alone from 1694 and took Azov in 1696.

In 1697 he travelled incognito and worked as a shipwright at Zaandam and Amsterdam. He ordered beards cut, dress worn and the new year moved to 1 January in 1699. Beaten by Charles XII at Narva in 1700, he rebuilt his army, founded Saint Petersburg in 1703 and crushed the Swedes at Poltava in 1709; the 1721 Treaty of Nystad gave Russia Ingria, Estonia and Livonia.

He created the Senate, Table of Ranks and Academy of Sciences. In 1718 his son Alexei, suspected of plotting, died under torture; Peter died in February 1725, aged fifty-two.

彼得一世，史称彼得大帝（1672—1725），1682年起任俄国沙皇，1721年成为首位皇帝，是用强力把俄国拉向欧洲的统治者。十岁继位后先与伊凡五世共治，由索菲娅摄政，1689年推翻她。1694年起独自掌权，1696年夺取亚速。

1697年微服游历，在赞丹和阿姆斯特丹当造船工。他下令剃须易服，1699年将新年改至1月1日。1700年纳尔瓦败于查理十二世后，他重建军队，1703年营建圣彼得堡，1709年在波尔塔瓦击溃敌军；1721年《尼斯塔德条约》为俄国赢得英格里亚、爱沙尼亚和利沃尼亚。

他设立元老院、官秩表与科学院。1718年儿子阿列克谢涉嫌谋反，受酷刑而死；1725年2月他去世，终年52岁。

en:
Postnik Yakovlev was a Russian architect from Pskov, active in the mid-sixteenth century. He helped erect the Cathedral of Saint Basil the Blessed on Red Square in 1555–1560 to mark the conquest of Kazan.

Barma, also associated with the building, may have been his nickname or an assistant's. In 1561–1562 he designed the walls of the Kazan Kremlin and its Annunciation Cathedral, and in 1588 added a chapel to Saint Basil's.

Legend claims Ivan the Terrible blinded him so he could never build anything more beautiful. His later works, however, suggest the story is a myth.

Ridolfo Fioravanti, nicknamed Aristotele, was born in Bologna about 1415 into a family of architects and engineers, and won fame for the devices he used to rebuild noble towers there. He worked in Florence, Milan and Hungary before Ivan III invited him to Moscow in 1475.

From 1475 to 1479 he built the Kremlin's Dormition Cathedral on the model of the older cathedral in Vladimir, introducing new architectural influences.

One account says he later served as a military engineer in Ivan's campaigns; another says he died in captivity after asking to return to Italy. He died around 1486.

en:
Sergius of Radonezh (1314–1392) was a Russian Orthodox monk and monastic reformer. With his brother he built a hermitage and a church of the Trinity near Radonezh, which grew into the Trinity Lavra of St. Sergius, Russia's most revered monastery.

After his brother left, he lived as a hermit until monks gathered and persuaded him to become abbot. He insisted that monks live by their own labor, and his disciples founded some forty monasteries across Russia.

In 1380 he blessed Dmitry Donskoy before Kulikovo. His relics were found in 1422, and he is venerated as one of Russia's greatest saints.

兄长离开后，他独居修行，直到修士们聚集并说服他担任院长。他坚持修士须靠自己的劳作生活，弟子们在俄罗斯各地创办了约四十座修道院。

Simeon Ivanovich, nicknamed the Proud (7 September 1317 – 27 April 1353), was the eldest son of Ivan I Kalita, succeeding him as prince of Moscow and grand prince of Vladimir in 1340. He traveled to the Golden Horde and secured his investiture from Uzbeg Khan, outbidding his Tver and Suzdal rivals.

That year he also forced Novgorod to surrender Torzhok's tax revenues. He had married the Lithuanian princess Aigusta Anastasia in 1333. Simeon and his sons died of the Black Death in 1353.

en:
Symeon of Polotsk (1629–1680) was a Belarusian-born churchman, poet and educator. Educated at the Kiev Mohyla College, he presented panegyric verses to Tsar Alexis during the tsar's visit to Polotsk in 1656, and moved to Moscow in 1664, where he taught Latin.

From 1667 he served as court poet. He also tutored the tsar's children, including the young Peter. His Baroque plays, among them a comedy of the Prodigal Son, were gathered into published collections. He died in Moscow in 1680.

en:
Simon Ushakov (c. 1626–1686) was the leading Russian icon painter of the seventeenth century. Around 1648 he joined the Silver Chamber, and his bright-coloured, proto-Baroque icons brought him to the notice of Patriarch Nikon and Tsar Alexis, who assigned him to the Kremlin Armoury in 1664.

That same year he published a treatise on icon painting. Drawing on Western naturalism, he pioneered secular portraits, or parsuna, and book engravings, while conservatives led by Archpriest Avvakum denounced his saints as fleshly and unorthodox. He trained many pupils, and some of his icons reached Western Europe. He died in Moscow in 1686.

en:
Zoe Palaiologina (c. 1449–1503), known in Russia as Sophia Fominichna, was a Byzantine princess, niece of the last emperor Constantine XI and daughter of Thomas Palaiologos. After the Ottoman conquest of the Morea in 1460 she was raised in Rome under papal protection. In 1472 she married Grand Prince Ivan III of Moscow.

In 1502 she saw her son Vasily III made co-ruler after the downfall of the rival heir Dmitry. She died in Moscow in 1503.

en:
Stephen of Perm (c. 1340–1396) was a Russian Orthodox missionary, bishop and painter who converted the Komi peoples. Born in Ustyug, he became a monk in Rostov and around 1370 devised a distinct alphabet for the Komi language, the Old Permic script.

From 1376 he worked along the Vychegda and Vym rivers, destroying pagan shrines as he won converts. In 1383 he was consecrated the first bishop of Perm.

His new see threatened Novgorod's control of the region's tribute and, aided by Ustyug, defeated a Novgorodian army in 1385. He died in Moscow in 1396 and was canonized in 1549.

Tikhon Nikitich Streshnev (1644?–1719) was a Russian boyar and one of Peter the Great's most trusted statesmen. With his uncle Rodion he mentored the young Peter, becoming a boyar in 1688 and head of the military chancellery in 1690.

en:
Yury Danilovich (1281–21 November 1325), eldest son of Daniel of Moscow, ruled Moscow from 1303 and contested Vladimir's grand princely throne with his uncle Mikhail of Tver. After submitting to Tver, Yury went to the Horde, married Uzbeg Khan's sister Konchaka and won the khan's favour.

When Konchaka died in Tverite captivity he accused Mikhail of poisoning her; the khan executed Mikhail in 1318 and made Yury grand prince. Mikhail's son Dmitry seized the title in 1322 and slew him at Sarai in 1325.

尤里·丹尼洛维奇（1281—1325年11月21日）是莫斯科的丹尼尔的长子，1303年起任莫斯科王公，与叔父特维尔的米哈伊尔争夺弗拉基米尔大公之位。向特维尔屈服后，尤里前往金帐汗国，娶月即别汗之妹康查卡为妻，赢得汗王欢心。

康查卡在特维尔的囚禁中死去，尤里控告米哈伊尔毒杀其妻，汗王遂于1318年处死米哈伊尔，立尤里为大公。1322年米哈伊尔之子德米特里夺得大公之位，并于1325年在萨莱将他杀死。

Frédéric III, also called Werric, was the thirty-first regular abbot of Notre-Dame de Mouzon, succeeding Lambert d'Yvois in 1345. On 21 December 1345 he swore fealty to Archbishop Jean de Vienne of Reims and appears in acts of 1346.

Mouzon's necrology records his death on 24 October, and by August 1347 Pierre II Hazard had succeeded him. Abbot lists gave him the arms of the châtelains of Yvois, possibly marking kinship with Lambert.

en:
Jean de Saint-Avit was the thirty-sixth regular abbot of Notre-Dame de Mouzon, a Benedictine born at Châteaudun. Already head of the Meuse-side abbey in 1361, he swore fealty to the church of Reims, and in 1364 he confirmed Thomas de Châlons in the priory of Thin.

In 1374 he settled a sharp dispute with his monks over the monastic pittance. In January 1378 he was transferred to Saint-Médard de Soissons, resigning Mouzon to Avignon pope Clement VII, and on 7 October 1391 he was appointed bishop of Avranches.

He was one of the few bishops to speak in Joan of Arc's defence at her trial at Rouen in 1431, and he died there on 22 July 1442.

en:
Lambert d'Epargnemaille, called d'Yvois, was the thirtieth regular abbot of Notre-Dame de Mouzon. When his predecessor Pierre I de Fismes resigned to Guillaume de Trie, archbishop of Reims, in April 1332, the abbey on the Meuse stayed vacant until 6 January 1333, when Trie, by compromise, appointed Lambert, a kinsman of the châtelains of Yvois. Accused of simony over his promotion, he cleared himself and was solemnly blessed by Trie.

His seal of 1334, a silver sun-shaped vessel and a chalice he gave the house all bore the arms of the châtelains of Yvois. A charter of 1339 still names him living, and he had died by 1345.

Pierre II Hazard, called Perinet, became the thirty-second regular abbot of Notre-Dame de Mouzon in 1347 and swore his fealty to Jean de Vienne, archbishop of Reims, on 20 August.

Soon afterwards he issued a formal acknowledgement that the right of presentation to the churches of Pure and Clémency belonged in alternation to the abbess of Juvigny and to his own abbey. He died on 17 April 1348, after only eight months in office, as the Black Death was reaching the Ardennes.

en:
Pierre IV d'Essone was the thirty-seventh regular abbot of Notre-Dame de Mouzon. A monk of Saint-Médard de Soissons, he was provided to Mouzon by the Avignon pope Clement VII after Jean de Saint-Avit's resignation, swearing fealty to the church of Reims on 18 March 1379. In 1381 the king of France named him a councillor.

He bought an estate with his monks and made it all over to them, on condition they remember him at the Monday Mass of Prime. In 1391 he returned to Saint-Médard de Soissons, dying there on 10 January.

John Randolph, 3rd Earl of Moray (1306 – 17 October 1346), was the second son of Thomas Randolph, Robert the Bruce's comrade, and inherited the earldom after his brother fell at Dupplin Moor in 1332. He served as joint Guardian of Scotland with Robert Stewart from 1334.

In 1335 he defeated Edward III's Flemish mercenaries at Boroughmuir but was captured soon after and spent five years in prisons. Exchanged in 1341, he fell commanding the right wing at Neville's Cross on 17 October 1346.

In 1335 he defeated Edward III's Flemish mercenaries at Boroughmuir but was captured soon after and spent five years in prisons. Exchanged in 1341, he fell commanding the right wing at Neville's Cross on 17 October 1346.

约翰·伦道夫，第三代马里伯爵（1306—1346年10月17日），是罗伯特·布鲁斯的战友托马斯·伦道夫的次子，1332年兄长在杜普林沼泽战死后袭爵。1334年，他与罗伯特·斯图亚特共同出任苏格兰护国主。

1335年，他在巴勒缪尔击败爱德华三世的佛兰德雇佣军，但旋即被俘，在监狱中度过五年。1341年他通过交换获释，1346年10月17日在内维尔十字之战指挥右翼时阵亡。

Gebhard von Schrapelau (died 1340), a son of Burchard I of the Schraplau branch of the counts of Querfurt, became provost of Magdeburg Cathedral in 1314 and custodian of Hildesheim Cathedral before his election as bishop of Merseburg in 1320.

He governed Merseburg until 1340. His constant feuds left the bishopric in disorder and debt for his successor, Heinrich V zu Stolberg, to repair.

Aldebert II of La Marche (died 1088), son of Bernard I and Amélie de Montignac, first appears as count on 16 June 1047. Early in his rule he burned Lesterps Abbey to flush out an enemy sheltering there, then compensated the monks with his rights over the town's free men.

Lay defender of Charroux Abbey, he long served Duke William VIII of Aquitaine. By Ponce he fathered Boso III and Almodis I. The Chronicle of Saint-Maixent dates his death to 1088.

Almodis I of La Marche (c. 1062–by 1129), daughter of Aldebert II and Ponce, married Roger le Poitevin of Montgommery. After her brother Boso III died childless in 1091, her uncle Eudes I took the county, but in 1098 she issued her first charter as countess, confirming her father's gift to Lesterps Abbey.

With the Count of Angoulême's help she held Charroux against Hugh of Lusignan. In 1115 she and her sons founded a Fontevrist priory at Châtain; she was dead by 1129.

Bernard I of La Marche (c. 991–1047), son of Aldebert I, was passed over as a boy in favour of his uncle Boso II. Around 1008 Duke William V of Aquitaine detached La Marche from Périgord and invested Bernard, but the abbot of Le Dorat held the county during his minority. Bernard appears as count by 1023.

By that year he had also feuded with Hugh of Lusignan over Civray. He died before June 1047, and by Amélie de Montignac left the counts Aldebert II and Eudes I.

Boso III of La Marche (died 1091), son of Aldebert II and Ponce, was count from 1088. In 1071, in his father's lifetime, he already bore the comital title in Duke William VIII of Aquitaine's following, and he later endowed Le Dorat Abbey.

He was killed in 1091 while besieging Confolens. Married but childless, he was succeeded by his uncle Eudes I over his sister Almodis I's claims.

Eudes I of La Marche (born c. 1028), younger son of Bernard I and Amélie de Montignac, gave property to Nouaillé Abbey with his brother Aldebert II by 1048, and appears with his nephew Boso III in ducal acts. When Boso died childless at Confolens in 1091, Eudes took the county despite claims from his niece Almodis I and her husband Roger de Montgommery.

His own charter confirms the succession. His last recorded acts appear to date to no later than 1095, and by December 1098 Almodis had succeeded him.

en:
Guy I of Lusignan (1269–1308), also called Guiard, was the younger son of Hugh XII of Lusignan. His brother Hugh XIII disinherited him in 1297, but after Hugh's death in 1303 Guy claimed La Marche and Angoulême; King Philip IV backed him and the Parlement of Paris confirmed them in 1304.

He fought for the king at Mons-en-Pévèle the same year, but in 1305 he made terms with the English at Saintes, ceding Cognac and Merpins for the seneschalship of Saintonge.

Accused before Philip in 1308 for homage to the English king, he died childless that November before trial, ending the senior male line of Lusignan.

en:
Hugh IX, called le Brun or the Brown (before 1151–1219), was a Poitevin lord of Lusignan who followed Richard the Lionheart on the Third Crusade. He followed Richard to Sicily in 1190 and to the siege of Acre the next year.

In December 1199 he detained Eleanor of Aquitaine and in return secured the county of La Marche. When King John married Isabella of Angoulême, his appeal to Philip Augustus helped bring the 1202 sentence against John's French fiefs.

Reconciled in 1214, he fought beside John at La Roche-aux-Moines. He joined the Fifth Crusade and died at the siege of Damietta on 11 August 1219.

1199年12月，他在阿基坦的埃莉诺途经时将其扣留，以此换得拉马什伯国。英王约翰娶走昂古莱姆的伊莎贝拉后，于格向法王腓力二世·奥古斯都申诉，促成1202年宣判没收约翰在法兰西的领地。

1214年双方和解，他随约翰参加罗什欧穆瓦讷之战。后来他加入第五次十字军东征，1219年8月11日死于杜姆亚特围城战。

en:
Hugh X of Lusignan (c. 1182–1249) succeeded his father Hugh IX as count of La Marche in 1219. In 1220 he married Isabella of Angoulême, widow of John of England, becoming count of Angoulême.

He used the conflict between Capetians and Plantagenets to strengthen his authority in Aquitaine. He wavered between the two courts until 1241, when he defied Louis IX and Alphonse of Poitiers and raised Poitou in revolt. The rising collapsed with the royal victory at Taillebourg in 1242.

In 1248 he joined Louis IX's Seventh Crusade. He was killed outside Damietta on 5 June 1249, where his father had died in 1219.

zh:
吕西尼昂的于格十世（约1182—1249）于1219年继其父于格九世成为拉马什伯爵。1220年，他迎娶英格兰国王约翰的遗孀昂古莱姆的伊莎贝拉，借此成为昂古莱姆伯爵。

他利用卡佩与金雀花两朝的纷争加强自己在阿基坦的权势，在两个朝廷之间摇摆。1241年他公然对抗路易九世和普瓦捷的阿方斯，煽动普瓦图贵族反叛；1242年，叛乱随着王军在塔耶堡之战获胜而瓦解。

1248年他随路易九世参加第七次十字军东征。1249年6月5日他战死在杜姆亚特城外，他的父亲正是1219年在同一座城下丧生。

en:
Hugh XI of Lusignan (c. 1221–1250), called the Brown, was the eldest son of Hugh X of Lusignan and Isabelle of Angoulême. Betrothed in 1224 and 1227, he married neither; in 1236 he married Yolande, daughter of Peter I of Brittany.

He inherited Angoulême from his mother in 1246 and La Marche from his father in 1249. That year he agreed to serve the count of Poitiers for a year on the crusade.

He joined Louis IX on the Seventh Crusade and was killed on 6 April 1250 at the Battle of Fariskur in Egypt. His son Hugh XII succeeded him.

于格十一世·德·吕西尼昂（约1221—1250），绰号“棕发”，是于格十世与昂古莱姆的伊莎贝尔的长子。他曾于1224年、1227年两度订婚但均未成婚；1236年，他与布列塔尼公爵皮埃尔一世之女约兰德结婚。

他随路易九世参加第七次十字军东征，1250年4月6日在埃及的法里斯库尔战役中阵亡，其子于格十二世继位。

en:
Hugh XII of Lusignan (c. 1238–1270) succeeded his father Hugh XI, killed at Fariskur in 1250, as Count of La Marche and Angoulême, ruling under the regency of his mother Yolande of Brittany. In 1254 he married Jeanne, heiress of Fougères, who bore him six children including Hugh XIII and Guy I.

He is the likeliest author behind the trouvère known as the Conte de la Marche. In 1270 he joined Louis IX's crusade and died in its early fighting at Tunis, whereupon Hugh XIII succeeded him.

Hugh XIII of Lusignan (25 June 1259 – 1 November 1303) was the eldest son of Hugh XII and Jeanne de Fougères. A boy of eleven when his father died on crusade at Tunis in 1270, he inherited the counties of La Marche and Angoulême. In 1276 he married Beatrice of Burgundy, but the marriage was childless.

Hugh died at Cognac on 1 November 1303. His brother Guy I claimed the two counties, ending the direct line of his branch.

en:
Yolande of Brittany (1218–1272), also called Yolande de Dreux, was the only daughter of Alix of Thouars and Peter I of Brittany. As a child she was thrice betrothed, including to Henry III of England, but married none; in 1236 she wed Hugh XI of Lusignan, bringing him the Breton counties of Penthièvre and Porhoët.

When Hugh was killed at Fariskur in 1250, she ruled La Marche and Angoulême as regent for her son Hugh XII until 1256. She died on 10 October 1272.

en:
Davyd, or David, Yurievich (c. 1163–1228) became prince of Murom after his elder brother Vladimir died in 1205. A steady ally of Vsevolod the Big Nest of Vladimir, he joined the 1207 siege of Pronsk and briefly held the town before being expelled. He fought at Lipitsa in 1216 for Grand Prince Yuri Vsevolodovich, and in 1220 sent his son against the Volga Bulgars.

He died on 2 April 1228. Some scholars identify him and his wife with the saints Peter and Fevronia of Murom.

en:
Gleb Vladimirovich (baptized David, c. 987–1015), a son of Vladimir the Great, was prince of Murom from about 1013 and younger brother of Boris of Rostov. After Vladimir's death in 1015 their half-brother Sviatopolk seized Kiev and had Boris murdered, then summoned Gleb from Murom.

Sviatopolk's men overtook him near Smolensk despite a warning from Yaroslav the Wise, and on 9 September 1015 his own cook cut his throat on their order. In 1019 Yaroslav buried him beside Boris, and the Church canonized the brothers as Saints Boris and Gleb.

格列布·弗拉基米罗维奇（教名大卫，约987—1015）是弗拉基米尔大帝之子，约1013年受封穆罗姆王公，罗斯托夫王公鲍里斯之弟。1015年父亲死后，异母兄斯维亚托波尔克占据基辅并杀害鲍里斯，随后召格列布从穆罗姆前来。

尽管智者雅罗斯拉夫派人报信示警，斯维亚托波尔克的追兵仍在斯摩棱斯克附近赶上了他：1015年9月9日，他的厨师奉追兵首领之命割断了他的喉咙。1019年雅罗斯拉夫将他与鲍里斯合葬，教会将兄弟二人册封为圣鲍里斯与圣格列布。

en:
Vladimir Svyatoslavich (died 1161), son of Sviatoslav Yaroslavich, was prince of Murom in 1147–1149 and 1155–1161 and prince of Ryazan from 1153. He first appears in 1146 in the wars of the southern princes, then fleeing his lands to Novgorod-Seversk.

On 4 April 1147 he was among the princes whom Yuri Dolgorukiy received at Moscow, in the town's first chronicle mention. At his death in 1161 his cousin Gleb Rostislavich took Ryazan.

弗拉基米尔·斯维亚托斯拉维奇（？—1161）是斯维亚托斯拉夫·雅罗斯拉维奇之子，1147—1149年及1155—1161年任穆罗姆王公，1153年起兼领梁赞。1146年他首次见于记载，卷入南方王公的战争，后弃地逃往诺夫哥罗德—谢韦尔斯克。

en:
Yaroslav Svyatoslavich (baptized Pankraty, c. 1071–1129) was the youngest son of Grand Prince Sviatoslav II of Kiev and founder of the Murom-Ryazan line. He first appears in 1096 fighting for his brother Oleg against Vladimir Monomakh; after defeat he withdrew to Murom and made peace. At the 1097 Lyubech congress the Murom-Ryazan land was assigned to him.

In 1123 he moved to rule Chernigov, but his nephew Vsevolod Olgovich drove him out in 1127, and Kiev refused to restore him. He died in Murom in 1129.

en:
Yaroslav Yurievich was prince of Murom from 1237, the only son of Yuri Davidovich, who may have fallen fighting Batu's Mongols on the Voronezh river. Almost nothing is recorded of his rule. In 1239 the Mongols overran the Mordvin lands and burned Murom, and his principality passes from the chronicles.

In 1248 he is named once more, marrying his daughter Maria to Prince Boris Vasilkovich of Rostov. After 1248 the Murom princes vanish from the sources for nearly a century, until 1345.

en:
Yuri Davidovich (died c. 1237) became prince of Murom in 1228 after his elder brother died before their father Davyd. He joined Grand Prince Yuri Vsevolodovich of Vladimir on campaigns against the Mordvins in 1229 and 1232.

In autumn 1237, when Batu's Mongols reached the southern Ryazan borders, he joined the Ryazan princes in battle on the Voronezh. Yuri most likely fell there, though sources never confirm it. His son Yaroslav succeeded to a Murom sacked the following winter.

尤里·达维多维奇（？—约1237）在兄长先于父亲达维德去世后，于1228年成为穆罗姆王公。1229年和1232年，他两度参加弗拉基米尔大公尤里·弗谢沃洛多维奇征讨莫尔多瓦人的远征。

en:
Yuri Vladimirovich (c. 1140–1174) succeeded his father Vladimir Svyatoslavich as prince of Murom in 1161, and Murom then stayed with his own line of the dynasty.

An ally of Andrei Bogolyubsky of Vladimir, he sent troops against the Volga Bulgars in 1164 and again in winter 1172, and joined Andrei's later campaigns against Novgorod and the Smolensk Rostislavichi. He died on 19 January 1174 and was buried at the Saviour Church in Murom, which the chronicles say he had himself built.

en:
Yuri, or Georgy, Yaroslavich was prince of Murom from 1345 to 1354, succeeding Vasily. In 1351 he rebuilt long-deserted Murom: he set up his court there, settlers followed, and he restored the churches.

In 1354 Fyodor Glebovich, backed by the Golden Horde, drove him out. They pleaded their claims before the Horde's princes; Fyodor won and imprisoned Yuri, who died in prison the same year. He is venerated as a local saint of Murom.

en:
Gaucher de Châtillon, called Gaucher de Nevers (c. 1221–1250), was the only son of Guy II, Count of Saint-Pol, and Agnès de Donzy, heiress of Nevers. His mother died in 1225 and his father was killed at the siege of Avignon the following year; he and his sister Yolande were raised by their grandmother.

In 1236 he married Jeanne, daughter of Count Philip Hurepel of Clermont. He fought the English in La Marche in 1242 and joined Louis IX's Seventh Crusade in 1248.

He was killed at Fariskur in Egypt after Mansurah, defending the approach to the village where the sick king had stopped. His sister inherited his counties.

戈谢·德·沙蒂永，人称“讷韦尔的戈谢”（约1221—1250），是圣波勒伯爵居伊二世与讷韦尔女继承人阿涅斯·德·栋济的独子。他的母亲于1225年去世，父亲次年死于阿维尼翁围城战；他与姐姐约兰德由外祖母抚养。

1236年，他娶克莱蒙伯爵腓力·于雷佩尔之女让娜。1242年他在拉马什与英格兰人作战，1248年参加路易九世的第七次十字军东征。

曼苏拉之战后，他在埃及法里斯库尔保卫染病国王驻足的村庄入口时战死，他的姐姐继承了各伯国。

en:
Jeanne de Clermont (1219–1252) was a French Capetian noblewoman, a granddaughter of King Philip II Augustus through his son Philip Hurepel, Count of Clermont. On her father's death in 1234 she inherited claims to lands including Clermont, and in 1236 she married Gaucher de Châtillon, heir to lands including Nevers and Auxerre.

Gaucher died on the Seventh Crusade in Egypt in April 1250, and their marriage was childless. Jeanne died in January 1252, her estates reverting to the royal domain.

en:
Rao Asthan (died 15 April 1291) was the second Rathore Rao, succeeding his father Sheoji in 1273. He conquered Khed from the Guhila Rajputs, and his descendants took the name Khedecha Rathores; he also granted Idar to his younger brother Sonag, ancestor of the Idariya Rathores.

When Jalaluddin Khalji's army attacked Pali in 1291, Asthan marched from Khed to meet it and died in the fighting. His son Doohad succeeded him.

拉奥·阿斯唐（1291年4月15日卒）是第二代拉托尔拉奥，1273年继父亲谢奥吉之位。他从古希拉拉杰普特人手中夺取凯德，后裔由此被称为凯德查拉托尔人；他还把伊达尔封给弟弟索纳格，即伊达里雅拉托尔人的祖先。

1291年贾拉勒丁·卡尔吉的军队进攻帕利，阿斯唐从凯德驰援，战死阵中，其子杜哈德继位。

en:
Rao Chhada, also called Chhadaji, was a Rathore Rajput chief who ruled the Marwar lands from 1328 to 1344. The son of Rao Jalansi, he defeated the Sodha Rajputs and prevailed against Jaisalmer, Nagaur and Jalore.

Like nine of fifteen early Rathore chiefs, he fell in 1344 while fighting the Songara Chauhans. His son Rao Tida succeeded him and avenged his death by defeating the Songaras.

en:
Rao Doohad (died 1309) succeeded his father Asthan in 1291 as Rathore Rao, ruling from Pali and Khed. He is said to have added some 140 villages to his principality and to have built the Nagnechiya Mata temple at Nagana.

Doohad once seized Mandore, the Parihar Rajputs' capital, but soon lost it again, and was killed on his second attack in 1309. His son Raipal succeeded him.

en:
Rao Sheoji, held by Rathore chronicles to be a grandson of Jayachandra, last Gahadavala king of Kannauj, is said to have led his kin west into Marwar after the dynasty fell to the Ghurids. Invited to Pali by Brahmins harassed by local raiders, he defeated the local Mer chief and founded the first Rathore polity there around 1243, taking the title Rao.

His sons Asthan and Sonag became ancestors of the Khedecha and Idariya Rathores. The Bithoor inscription records his death in battle in 1273.

en:
Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka was a Telugu warrior and founding ruler of the Musunuri Nayaka line. After the Delhi Sultanate overthrew the Kakatiya kingdom of Warangal in 1323 and captured its king Prataparudra, his ministers rallied the scattered Telugu nayakas and chose Prolaya as their leader.

His Vilasa grant of 1330 presents him as having restored the order of Prataparudra's days. On his death his cousin Kapaya Nayaka carried on the revolt and took Warangal in 1336.

Beatrice Visconti was a daughter of Matteo I Visconti, lord of Milan. In 1310 she married the condottiero Spinetta Malaspina il Grande, lord of Fosdinovo; the match tied him to Milan's ruling house, and in 1314 Matteo made him podestà of Milan.

Her daughter Giovanna Novella married Ludovico I Gonzaga of Mantua in 1340. Spinetta left no legitimate sons, so on his death in 1352 his nephews succeeded him.

en:
Bernabò Malaspina was a younger son of Moroello II Malaspina, Marquis of Mulazzo in Lunigiana. In the division of the Spino Secco family lands made in 1390 he and his brother Galeazzo received shares of the Cantalupo feud in the Trebbia valley.

Genealogical tradition makes Bernabò the father of Moroello and Giovanni, founders of the Fabbrica and Ottone branches; their descendants sold both fiefs to the Fieschi of Genoa in 1540.

贝尔纳博·马拉斯皮纳是卢尼贾纳穆拉佐侯爵莫罗埃洛二世的幼子。在1390年的干刺支族家产分割中，他与兄弟加莱亚佐分得特雷比亚河谷坎塔卢波领地的份额。

后世谱系传统以贝尔纳博为莫罗埃洛和乔瓦尼之父，二人是法布里卡与奥托尼两支的始祖；两支后人于1540年把领地卖给热那亚的菲耶斯基家族。

en:
Corrado Malaspina, called l'Antico (c. 1180–after 1254), was an Italian marquis, son of Obizzo II, and founder of the Malaspinas' Spino Secco branch. In 1198 he confirmed ceding the Grondola hills to Piacenza, then made treaties with Genoa and Milan.

In 1220 Emperor Frederick II confirmed Corrado's and his cousin Opizzo's rights and possessions; the next year they made the first great division of their lands. In 1226 he escorted Frederick across the Apennines.

In 1246 he briefly sided with Milan and Piacenza against the emperor. A patron of Provençal troubadours, he is last documented in 1254.

科拉多·马拉斯皮纳，绰号“老者”（约1180—1254年以后），是意大利侯爵、奥比佐二世之子，也是马拉斯皮纳家族“枯棘”支系的始祖。1198年，他确认将格龙多拉诸丘割让给皮亚琴察，随后与热那亚、米兰缔结了一系列条约。

1220年，皇帝腓特烈二世确认了他和堂兄弟奥比佐的领地与权利；次年，两人完成家族领地的第一次大分封。1226年他护送腓特烈翻越亚平宁山脉。

1246年，他短暂支持米兰和皮亚琴察反对皇帝。他曾资助普罗旺斯行吟诗人，最后一次见于记载是1254年。

Federico I Malaspina was marquis of Villafranca in Lunigiana and son of Corrado Malaspina il Vecchio, who founded the family's Spino Secco branch. His son Corrado il Giovane was praised by Dante in the Purgatorio.

Federico died shortly before 1266, when the family estates were divided and his sons received lands including the Lunigiana territory centered on Villafranca and their Sardinian possessions. He founded the Villafranca line.

费代里科一世·马拉斯皮纳是卢尼贾纳的维拉弗兰卡侯爵，为马拉斯皮纳家族“干刺”支始祖科拉多·“老者”·马拉斯皮纳之子。他的儿子“青年”科拉多曾被但丁在《炼狱篇》中称颂。

en:
Franceschino Malaspina was marquis of Mulazzo in Lunigiana, the son of Moroello Malaspina. He took part in the wars of Guelfs and Ghibellines and several times hosted the exiled Dante Alighieri at Mulazzo.

In October 1306, at Sarzana, he gave Dante his general mandate to negotiate for the whole Ghibelline branch of the family; the poet concluded the Peace of Castelnuovo with the bishop of Luni that same morning. Franceschino died in 1319 and was succeeded by his son Moroello II.

弗兰切斯基诺·马拉斯皮纳是卢尼贾纳穆拉佐的侯爵，莫罗埃洛·马拉斯皮纳之子。他卷入圭尔夫派与吉伯林派的战争，并在穆拉佐多次接待流亡中的但丁·阿利吉耶里。

1306年10月，他在萨尔扎纳授予但丁全权委托，代表整个吉伯林派的马拉斯皮纳家族谈判；诗人当天上午便与卢尼主教订立了《卡斯特尔诺沃和约》。弗兰切斯基诺于1319年去世，其子莫罗埃洛二世继立。

Gabriele Malaspina was marquis of Verrucola near Fivizzano in Lunigiana, from the Malaspina family's Spino Fiorito branch. He was the son of Isnardo I Malaspina and Cubitosa d'Este, daughter of Azzo VII of Ferrara.

In 1269 the bishop of Luni invested him, together with his uncle Alberto and his cousins, with lands including Verrucola, Fivizzano and Fosdinovo. Gabriele died in 1289 and was succeeded by his son Spinetta, later called il Grande, the future lord of Fosdinovo.

Gabriele Malaspina (c. 1311–1359) was the eldest son of Azzolino II Malaspina and a nephew of Spinetta the Great. When his uncle died without heirs in 1352, Gabriele and his brothers inherited his uncle's lands, including Fosdinovo.

In 1355 Emperor Charles IV raised Fosdinovo to a marquisate, investing the brothers as marquises. A cleric, Gabriele became bishop of Luni. He died in 1359, his share of the lands passing to his brothers.

en:
Galeotto I Malaspina (died 15 March 1367) was a son of Azzolino II Malaspina and nephew of Spinetta the Great. In 1352 he and his brothers inherited their uncle's lordship of Fosdinovo, and in 1355 Emperor Charles IV raised Fosdinovo to a marquisate and invested the three as marquises.

After Gabriele died in 1359, the two surviving brothers divided the lands, Galeotto receiving Fosdinovo itself. From 1361 he ruled it unchallenged, making him the first marquis of Fosdinovo.

He had been a judge in Verona and a knight. He died at Fosdinovo in 1367 and was buried in the church of San Remigio, in a tomb built right after his death.

Guglielmo I Malaspina was a Lombard marquis, son of Moroello I Malaspina and a lady of the Roman Frangipane family. In 1200 he allied with Milan and Piacenza in their war against Parma and Pavia.

Like his uncle Alberto, he kept his court open to troubadours, and the troubadour Aimeric de Peguilhan sang his liberality; when he died in 1220 Aimeric composed a planh, or lament, in his memory. His son Opizzino succeeded him.

en:
Obizzo I Malaspina, called the Great, was a Lombard nobleman, the son of Adalberto Malaspina. In 1154 he fought at the siege of Tortona against Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, yet in 1164 he joined the emperor and rescued him from the men of Pontremoli.

He supported the Lombard League, and in 1172, with Pisan backing, he raised a fierce revolt against Genoa. He had three sons; the Fosdinovo line, including Spinetta the Great, descended from him.

Obizzo II Malaspina, called Obizzone, was a Lombard marquis and the elder son of Obizzo I Malaspina and Maria Bianco di Vezzano. In 1184 he and his father promised the commune of Piacenza the castle of Oramala, and in 1185 he sat as imperial judge at Lucca.

In 1189 he joined in selling the Val d'Enza and Val di Taro to Piacenza. He died in 1193, and his son Corrado il Vecchio led the Spino Secco branch.

en:
Opizzino Malaspina, also recorded as Obizzo I, was marquis of Villafranca in Lunigiana, a son of Federico I and brother of Corrado il Giovane and Tommaso. In the family partition of 1266 the three brothers received lands including the Lunigiana estates centered on Villafranca and a share of their Sardinian possessions.

In 1281 their uncle Alberto ceded them another third of his Sardinian lands, and in 1296 Opizzino arranged mutual succession to those estates with his cousin Moroello of Giovagallo. He died in 1301.

en:
Opizzo Malaspina, called Opizzino, was a Lombard marquis and the son of Guglielmo I Malaspina. He succeeded his father in 1220, and in 1221 he and Corrado il Vecchio divided the great Malaspina inheritance: Opizzino took the Lunigiana lands east of the Magra, with Filattiera, and became the forefather of the Spino Fiorito branch.

He served Emperor Frederick II, but from 1246 sided with Milan and Piacenza against him. He died in 1249 or 1254, leaving sons including Isnardo.

en:
Spinetta Malaspina, called the Great (1282–1352), was the son of Gabriele Malaspina of Verrucola and founder of the Malaspina lords of Fosdinovo. In 1311 Emperor Henry VII made him imperial vicar of Reggio, and in 1314 his father-in-law Matteo Visconti named him podestà of Milan.

In 1317 Castruccio Castracani seized Fosdinovo and other fiefs and drove him to Verona; with Cangrande's troops he recovered his lands in 1320, and the struggle ran on until Castruccio died in 1328.

In 1340 he bought out the local nobles and became undisputed lord of Fosdinovo, where he enlarged the castle. He died in 1352 without heirs, passing his state to his nephews. His heirs raised him a cenotaph in Verona, but his own tomb was never found.

斯皮内塔·马拉斯皮纳，绰号“伟大者”（1282—1352），是韦鲁科拉的加布里埃莱·马拉斯皮纳之子，也是福斯迪诺沃马拉斯皮纳统治者的开创者。1311年，皇帝亨利七世任命他为雷焦的帝国代理官；1314年，岳父马泰奥·维斯孔蒂任命他为米兰的最高行政长官。

1317年，卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼夺取福斯迪诺沃等领地，把他赶到维罗纳；1320年他借坎格兰德的军队收复领地，双方的争斗持续到卡斯特拉卡尼于1328年去世。

1340年，他买下当地贵族的权利，成为福斯迪诺沃无可争议的领主，并扩建了城堡。1352年他去世时没有继承人，领地传给侄子们。后人在维罗纳为他立了一座衣冠冢，但他自己的墓地始终没有找到。

Mikhail Rostislavich (died 1279) was a Rurikid prince of the Smolensk branch, a younger son of Prince Rostislav Mstislavich of Smolensk. From 1260 he ruled the appanage of Mstislavl, and in 1278, after his elder brother Gleb died, he succeeded as grand prince of Smolensk. He reigned there for only about a year and died in 1279.

After his death his brother Fyodor had the foremost claim to Smolensk, but during Fyodor's long absence their nephew Alexander Glebovich controlled it, and in 1297 Alexander proclaimed himself prince and openly fought his uncle.

Roman Glebovich (died after 1301) was a Rurikid prince of the Smolensk line, the younger son of Gleb Rostislavich, prince of Smolensk. From 1281 he held the appanage of Mstislavl, and he was prince of Novgorod. In 1293 he led Novgorodians against a fortress the Swedes had built in Karelian land, but a thaw and lack of fodder for the horses forced a retreat.

In 1300 he and his elder brother Alexander of Smolensk besieged Dorogobuzh, where their cousin Andrei Mikhailovich of Vyazma defeated them. He is last mentioned alive after 1301, and his son Dmitry later held Bryansk.

en:
Fredo Mulucci was the leading man of the Guelph Mulucci house that dominated Macerata from about 1325. The city was the seat of the papal rector of the March, and the popes backed the Mulucci to keep it obedient. Fredo ruled with his uncle Muluccio II.

In 1328 he joined the papal army's siege of Senigallia. A popular rising drove the family out in February 1335; they returned the next year with papal support. In August 1340 the guilds overthrew the signoria, and Fredo had to cede his rights over Casale to the commune.

In March 1353, allied with the Malatesta, he appeared among the witnesses of the Peace of Sarzana, which let Macerata's exiles return.

In 1328 he joined the papal army's siege of Senigallia. A popular rising drove the family out in February 1335; they returned the next year with papal support. In August 1340 the guilds overthrew the signoria, and Fredo had to cede his rights over Casale to the commune.

In March 1353, allied with the Malatesta, he appeared among the witnesses of the Peace of [ShowLocationName('sarzana')], which let Macerata's exiles return.

弗雷多·穆卢奇是约自1325年起主宰马切拉塔的圭尔夫派穆卢奇家族的头面人物。该城是教廷边区总督的驻地，教宗扶持穆卢奇家族，以保证城市顺服。弗雷多与叔父穆卢乔二世共掌权柄。

1328年，他参加教廷军队围攻塞尼加利亚。1335年2月民众起事将家族逐出，次年他们靠教廷支持返城。1340年8月行会推翻领主政权，弗雷多被迫把对卡萨莱的权利让给市镇。

1353年3月，他已与马拉泰斯塔家族结盟，名列《萨尔扎纳和约》的见证人，和约允许马切拉塔的流亡者返回。

en:
Guarnaccia Mulucci was a son of Bonleone of the Guelph Mulucci family, which had risen to dominate Macerata in the later thirteenth century through its lands and its loyalty to the pope.

Early in the fourteenth century the family split into two branches, Bonleone's and that of Guarnaccia's uncle Muluccio II. In 1306 Guarnaccia and Muluccio attended a settlement between Camerino and neighbouring communes, concluded in Macerata's communal palace under papal authority.

That same year he was among the guarantors for Macerata at the Church's provincial parliament at Montolmo. The family's offices usually lay within the Marches, but in 1309–1310 Guarnaccia served farther afield as captain of the people at Siena.

瓜尔纳恰·穆卢奇是圭尔夫派穆卢奇家族成员博恩莱奥内之子。该家族凭土地财富和对教宗的忠诚，在13世纪后半叶成为马切拉塔的主导者。

14世纪初，家族分成博恩莱奥内这一支与瓜尔纳恰的叔父穆卢乔二世一支。1306年，瓜尔纳恰与穆卢乔在马切拉塔市政宫出席卡梅里诺与邻近诸市镇在教廷主持下达成的和解。

en:
Muluccio, son of Mulo, was a leading figure of the Guelph Mulucci family of Macerata. In the struggle between papal and imperial supporters, he sided with the pope. He served as podestà of Montegiorgio in 1251 and, after Macerata returned to papal obedience in 1252, received compensation for his losses.

Exiled with his family during Manfred's reign, he led an attack on Montolmo and became podestà of Castelfidardo in 1269. The 1268 register recorded him as the city's largest landowner, and from 1281 he sat on Macerata's special council.

en:
Muluccio II Mulucci headed one of the two branches of the Guelph family that ruled Macerata under papal favour between 1320 and 1340. A paternal grandson of Muluccio I, he attended a settlement between neighbouring communes at Macerata in 1306.

He served as podestà of several communes, reaching the crowning post of his career at Siena in 1323. In 1328 he and his son Nucciarello took up arms at Montefano against Ghibellines from Osimo.

After the guilds overthrew the family, a papal inquiry in 1341 named him and his nephew Fredo as the rulers of the signoria, supported by Nucciarello. In 1345 his sons Vanni and Leone sold their houses in the city.

en:
Nucciarello Mulucci was a son of Muluccio II of the Guelph family that held Macerata with the backing of the papal rector. Like his father he served the papal cause in arms: in 1328 the two took the field at Montefano against Ghibellines from Osimo.

He was podestà of Cingoli twice, in 1333 and 1335. Rule was not free of friction with the citizens, and in January 1336 the rector summoned Nucciarello and his kinsmen to restore peace.

A papal inquiry of 1341, after the guilds overthrew the family in 1340, called him a supporter of the signoria led by his father and Fredo.

en:
Blessed Pietro Mulucci (c. 1257–1347) was a Franciscan friar of the Guelph Mulucci house of Macerata and brother of the city's lord Fredo. In 1320 Pope John XXII made the loyal city a diocese, and on 6 June 1323 named Pietro its second bishop.

In 1325 he attended the canonization inquiry for Nicholas of Tolentino, where witnesses named him as an eyewitness to a miracle. Learned tradition remembers him as a zealous bishop who promoted the cult of Our Lady of Loreto and had a church raised around the Holy House.

In 1320 he had appeared as a witness at an inquisitorial trial of Recanati rebels accused of heresy. He held the see through his family's signoria and its overthrow by the guilds in 1340, dying in office on 29 October 1347.

Vanni Mulucci, Giovanni by baptismal name, belonged to the Guelph family that dominated Macerata from about 1325, when the city was newly a bishopric and the seat of the papal rector of the March.

en:
Agnes of Montbéliard (died c. 1377), eldest daughter of Reginald of Burgundy, Count of Montbéliard, was the heiress through whom the county passed to her husband, Henry of Montfaucon. They married in 1320, and a 1332 treaty over her brother Othenin's inheritance made Henry count in her right.

Her county suffered the Black Death in 1349 and then a feud of over thirty years with Louis of Neufchâtel over the Val de Morteau, after Henry seized part of Louis's lands for lack of homage.

King John II twice summoned her with other Burgundian barons to serve against the English. Her son Stephen succeeded as count, and another son, Louis, became Archbishop of Besançon.

蒙贝利亚尔的阿涅丝（约1377年卒）是蒙贝利亚尔伯爵雷诺·德·勃艮第的长女，伯国正是经由她转到丈夫蒙福孔的亨利手中。两人于1320年成婚；1332年，一项处理其兄弟奥特南遗产的条约使亨利凭妻权成为蒙贝利亚尔伯爵。

伯国先在1349年遭黑死病蹂躏，又为莫尔托谷地同讷沙泰勒的路易缠斗三十多年；起因是亨利以对方未行臣服礼为由扣押其部分领地。

en:
Amadeus II of Montfaucon (c. 1130–1195) was Count of Montbéliard and lord of Montfaucon from 1163. The son of Richard II of Montfaucon and Sophie, daughter and heiress of Count Theodoric II of Montbéliard, he inherited the county through his mother.

A loyal supporter of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa while other Burgundian barons held aloof, he was rewarded in 1170 with a share of the lordship of Orbe, becoming lord of Montagny.

In 1195 Count Palatine Otto I of Burgundy had him assassinated. His son Richard III succeeded him; another son, Walter, later served as regent of Cyprus.

en:
Stephen of Montfaucon (1325–1397), son of Henry I and Agnes of Montbéliard, was Count of Montbéliard from 1367. In 1354 he married Margaret of Chalon-Arlay and governed the county during his father's later campaigns.

His heir Henry II fell fighting the Ottomans at Nicopolis in 1396; Stephen sent men to search for him in vain. All his children died before him, and by his 1397 will he left Montbéliard to his ten-year-old granddaughter Henriette, betrothed to Eberhard IV of Württemberg, so carrying the county into the House of Württemberg.

蒙福孔的艾蒂安（1325—1397）是亨利一世与蒙贝利亚尔的阿涅丝之子，1367年起任蒙贝利亚尔伯爵。1354年，他娶沙隆-阿尔莱的玛格丽特为妻，在父亲晚年征战期间主持伯国政务。

en:
Henry I of Montfaucon (died 1367) was a baron of the County of Burgundy who became Count of Montbéliard through his wife. As the eldest he took over the barony of Montfaucon after John II died, and in 1320 married Agnes, daughter of Reginald of Burgundy, who had governed Montbéliard.

Her brother Othenin, mentally disabled, was kept under guardianship; after his death Henry ruled the county, and Emperor Louis IV invested him on 23 January 1339. In March 1340 the townspeople of Montbéliard rose against him, and he ended the revolt with promises of pardon rather than bloodshed.

He campaigned for Philip VI, fighting the Flemings at Cassel in 1328 and later the English, and served with the Teutonic Knights in Prussia. In 1362 Charles IV named him imperial vicar in the County of Burgundy, and his son Stephen succeeded him.

蒙贝利亚尔的亨利一世（1367年卒）是勃艮第伯国的一位男爵，因婚姻成为蒙贝利亚尔伯爵。兄长让二世去世后，他以长兄的身份接掌蒙福孔男爵领；1320年，他娶曾执掌蒙贝利亚尔的勃艮第的雷诺之女阿涅丝。

阿涅丝的兄弟奥特南患有智力障碍，一直处在监护之下；他去世后，亨利统治该伯国，1339年1月23日皇帝路德维希四世正式册封他。1340年3月，蒙贝利亚尔市民起事，他以赦免的许诺而非流血平息了叛乱。

他曾于1328年随腓力六世在卡塞尔同佛兰德人作战，后来对英格兰人作战，还随条顿骑士团前往普鲁士。1362年，皇帝查理四世任命他为勃艮第伯国的帝国代理官。其子艾蒂安继位。

Louis de Montfaucon was a younger son of Henry I of Montfaucon, who became Count of Montbéliard in 1321 through his marriage to its heiress, Agnes of Burgundy. Louis chose an ecclesiastical career, serving as dean before becoming Archbishop of Besançon.

He died on 25 July 1362 during his father's lifetime, so he never held the county, which passed to his elder brother Stephen in 1367.

en:
Louis of Scarpone (c. 1015–1071/1076) was the son of Count Richwin of Scarpone and Matilda of Eguisheim, sister of Pope Leo IX. In 1038 Emperor Conrad II married him to Sophie of Bar, heiress of the dukes of Upper Lorraine. The marriage brought Louis the county of Bar, and in 1042 the emperor also gave him Montbéliard.

He repulsed Count Renaud I of Burgundy's siege in 1044. After Duke Gerard of Lorraine died in 1070, Louis claimed the duchy through Sophie, but Emperor Henry IV chose Gerard's son Theodoric II. Louis died soon afterwards; his own son Theodoric founded the comital house of Bar.

en:
Othenin, called the Mad (died 1338), was Count of Montbéliard but never governed it. The only son of Reginald of Burgundy and Guillemette de Neufchâtel, he was too mentally disabled to take part in the county's affairs and was placed under the tutelage of his uncle Hugh of Chalon, lord of Fraisans.

He lived shut away at the Château de Montfaucon near Besançon until his death in 1338. Emperor Louis IV named Henry I of Montfaucon, husband of Othenin's sister Agnes, as his successor.

en:
Reginald of Burgundy (c. 1260–1321), a son of Hugh of Chalon and Countess Adelaide I, married Guillemette de Neufchâtel in 1282 and ruled Montbéliard and Belfort as count by right of his wife, heiress to both counties. In 1318, when Duke Eudes IV acquired the County of Burgundy by marriage, Reginald became its lieutenant-general.

He died in 1321. His son Othenin succeeded as Count of Montbéliard under his uncle's guardianship; after Othenin's death in 1339, the county passed to Reginald's daughter Agnes and her husband Henry of Montfaucon.

勃艮第的雷诺（约1260—1321）是沙隆的于格与女伯爵阿德莱德一世之子，1282年同吉耶梅特·德·讷沙泰勒结婚，凭妻子的继承权成为蒙贝利亚尔和贝尔福伯爵。1318年，勃艮第公爵厄德四世通过婚姻取得勃艮第伯国，雷诺被任命为伯国的总代理官。

en:
Richard III of Montfaucon was Count of Montbéliard and lord of Montfaucon, the son of Amadeus II. In the German succession dispute he and Stephen II of Auxonne backed the Welf claimant Otto IV against Philip of Swabia. Richard and Walter captured the bishop of Besançon and were excommunicated; a settlement in 1199 lifted the sentence in return for abandoning claims in the Jorat.

Richard later joined Stephen's war against Otto of Merania. He also warred against Count Frederick II of Ferrette, and peace was sealed by the marriage of his son Theodoric III to Frederick's daughter Alix. Richard died in 1227.

蒙福孔的理查三世是蒙贝利亚尔伯爵、蒙福孔领主，阿梅代二世之子。德意志王位之争中，他与欧塞尔的艾蒂安二世支持韦尔夫家族的奥托四世，反对士瓦本的菲利普。理查与戈蒂埃囚禁贝桑松主教，因而被处绝罚；1199年他们放弃对若拉的主张，换取解除绝罚。

en:
Theodoric I (Thierry, c. 1045–1103) ruled as count of Montbéliard, Bar and Verdun and lord of Mousson. The son of Count Louis of Scarpone and Sophie of Bar, he claimed the Duchy of Lorraine after his father's death.

Emperor Henry IV rejected him; when he ravaged the Diocese of Metz in reprisal, he was defeated by Bishop Adalbéron III and Duke Theodoric II. Reconciled with the Church, he founded a Benedictine abbey at Walbourg in 1074.

He did not take the cross, sending his son Louis on crusade instead. After 1096 Bishop Richer granted him Verdun for life.

蒂埃里一世（约1045—1103）是蒙贝利亚尔、巴尔和凡尔登伯爵、穆松领主。他是斯卡尔波内的路易伯爵与巴尔的索菲之子。父亲死后，他要求继承洛林公爵领地。

皇帝亨利四世驳回了他的要求；他报复性地洗劫梅斯主教区，却被梅斯主教阿达尔贝龙三世和洛林公爵蒂埃里二世击败。与教会和解后，他于1074年在瓦尔堡修建本笃会修道院。

他没有亲自参加十字军，而是派儿子路易前往。1096年后，凡尔登主教里谢将伯国终身授予他。

en:
Theodoric II (c. 1078 – January 1163), son of Count Theodoric I, became count of Montbéliard in 1103. First given the family's Meuse lands, he was driven out by their people for his harsh temper before inheriting Montbéliard on his father's death. In favour with the emperors, he took part in the Concordat of Worms in 1122, and founded several monasteries.

His son Theodoric III predeceased him, so the county passed to his grandson Amadeus II of Montfaucon, son of his daughter Sophie and Richard II of Montfaucon.

Theodoric III of Montfaucon (1205–1283), called the Great Baron, was Count of Montbéliard from 1227, succeeding his father Richard III. In 1248 he founded Montbéliard's first hospital for the poor outside the city walls.

He married Alix, daughter of Count Frederick II of Ferrette. Their son Richard died before him in 1279, so in 1282 Theodoric settled the county on his great-granddaughter Guillemette de Neufchâtel; her marriage to Reginald of Burgundy carried Montbéliard into a new dynasty.

Congalach Cnogba (died 956), also called Congalach mac Máel Mithig, was a king of Brega of the Síl nÁedo Sláine and high king of Ireland from about 944. He was a grandson of Flann Sinna and sister's son of his predecessor Donnchad Donn.

The annals show him warring with most neighbours, now allying with, now fighting Amlaíb Cuarán, Norse king of Dublin. In 956 he was killed in an ambush at Dún Ailinne, County Kildare, fighting the Leinstermen and the Norse of Dublin.

en:
Donnchad Donn (died 944), son of Flann Sinna of Clann Cholmáin, twice rebelled against his father, in 904 and 915. When his brother Conchobar and brother-in-law Niall Glúndub fell fighting the Vikings at Dublin in 919, Donnchad took Mide and the high kingship. He blinded one brother, Áed, and killed another, Domnall.

He long fought his son-in-law Muirchertach of the Leather Cloaks, who raided Mide in 941 and fell in 943. On his death in 944 his nephew Congalach Cnogba succeeded him as king of Tara.

en:
Flann Sinna (847 – 25 May 916), son of Máel Sechnaill I of Clann Cholmáin, was king of Mide from 877 and high king from 879. He took hostages from Leinster, attacked Armagh with Irish and Norse allies in 882, and lost to the Vikings at the Battle of the Pilgrim in 887.

In 908 he routed the Munstermen at Bellaghmoon and killed King Cormac mac Cuilennáin. High crosses at Clonmacnoise named him king of Ireland. After his heir Óengus was killed in 915 and his sons revolted, Flann died on 25 May 916 near Mullingar; Niall Glúndub succeeded him.

In 908 he routed the Munstermen at Bellaghmoon and killed King Cormac mac Cuilennáin. High crosses at Clonmacnoise named him king of Ireland. After his heir Óengus was killed in 915 and his sons revolted, Flann died on 25 May 916 near [ShowLocationName('mullingar')]; #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('tyr_niall_glundub').GetID],X #L Niall Glúndub#!#! succeeded him.
zh:
弗兰·锡纳（847—916年5月25日）是麦尔·舍赫奈尔一世之子，877年起任米斯国王，879年成为爱尔兰至高王。他即位之初先向伦斯特索取人质，882年联合爱尔兰人与诺斯人进攻阿马，887年在朝圣者之战中被维京人击败。

908年，他在贝拉穆恩击溃芒斯特军队，击杀芒斯特国王科马克·麦克·奎莱南；克朗麦克诺伊斯的高十字架上刻有他作为爱尔兰国王的名号。915年继承人奥恩古斯被杀、诸子叛乱，他于916年5月25日在马林加附近去世，塔拉王位由尼尔·格伦杜布继承。

en:
Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill (949–1022), called Máel Sechnaill Mór, of Clann Cholmáin, became king of Mide and High King of Ireland in 980. That year he defeated Olaf Cuaran of Dublin at Tara, took the city and freed its slaves.

With Brian Boru he won the Battle of Glenmama in 999, but surrendered the high kingship to Brian in 1002. After Brian fell at Clontarf in 1014, Máel Sechnaill regained the high kingship and ruled until his death.

en:
Máel Sechnaill I (died 27 November 862) of Clann Cholmáin became king of Mide in 845 and king of Tara in 846. Late in 845 he captured the Viking leader Turgesius and drowned him in Lough Owel.

Acknowledged as high king by the Ulstermen, he took Munster hostages in repeated campaigns and in 859 detached Osraige from Munster. In 860 he marched against his northern rival Áed Findliath and beat off a night attack. His son Flann Sinna held the high kingship.

en:
Paul I Mataranga was an Albanian feudal lord of the Mataranga family who held the Byzantine title of sevastocrator and governed Gora near Lake Ohrid. In 1319 he joined a coalition of Albanian nobles rising against King Milutin of Serbia, and Pope John XXII counted him among the favoured lords of Albania.

Around 1328 his daughter Euphemia married Andrea II Muzaka, allying the Mataranga with the Muzaka family. He died around 1350.

en:
Blasius Mataranga was an Albanian nobleman of the Mataranga family who ruled the short-lived Principality of Mataranga from 1358 to 1367. Holding the Byzantine title of sevastokrator, he controlled the coast between Durrës and Vlorë and grew wealthy on the grain trade with Ragusa.

He fought the rival Thopia and Balsha families and died around 1367, possibly killed while held captive by the Balsha. His son Gjon survived him.

en:
Aymar Adhémar de Monteil de La Garde (c. 1299–1361) was born into a noble family of the Dauphiné and became archdeacon of Reims and dean of Toul before succeeding his uncle as bishop of Metz in 1327. As prince-bishop he warred against Duke Raoul of Lorraine until Philip VI mediated a peace, and fought at Crécy in 1346.

He later clashed with the regent Marie de Châtillon and Robert I of Bar, burning Château-Salins and invading the Barrois. He died at Metz on 12 May 1361.

Gérard IV of Metz, also called Gerard de Bouzonville (c. 993–c. 1045), was a Lotharingian count, the son of Count Adalbert II of Metz. In 1033 he succeeded his father as count of Metz and Bouzonville.

By his wife Gisela he left two sons, Adalbert and Gérard, who both became dukes of Upper Lorraine; the younger Gérard founded the ducal House of Lorraine, ancestor of the later Habsburg-Lorraine dynasty.

en:
Fa Ngum (1316–1393) founded the Lao kingdom of Lan Xang. Born in Muang Sua, he was the son of Prince Phi Fa, whom his grandfather Khamphong had exiled to Angkor in the 1320s. He grew up at the Khmer court and married a Khmer princess.

Backed by Jayavarman IX, he returned with an army, subdued Lao principalities from Champasak to the upper Mekong, and in 1353 was crowned at Luang Prabang. He named his realm Lan Xang Hom Khao, land of a million elephants and a white parasol, and brought Theravada Buddhism and the Phra Bang from Angkor.

At his Khmer queen's request he made Buddhism the state religion in 1359. In 1372 his nobles deposed him in favour of his son Samsenethai, and Fa Ngum died in exile.

法昂（1316—1393）是老挝澜沧王国的开国国王。他生于勐苏瓦，是王子披法之子；披法在1320年代被祖父坎蓬放逐到吴哥。法昂在高棉宫廷长大，并娶了一位高棉公主。

在阇耶跋摩九世支持下，他起兵返回，征服从占巴塞到湄公河上游的佬人诸邦，1353年在琅勃拉邦登基，国号“澜沧洪考”，意为百万大象与白伞之地。他又从吴哥引入上座部佛教，迎来帕邦佛像。

1359年，应高棉王后请求，他立佛教为国教。1372年贵族废黜法昂，拥立其子桑森泰，法昂最终死于流亡之中。

在#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('khm_jayavarman_ix').GetID],X #L 阇耶跋摩九世#!#!支持下，他起兵返回，征服从[ShowLocationName('champasak')]到湄公河上游的佬人诸邦，1353年在琅勃拉邦登基，国号“澜沧洪考”，意为百万大象与白伞之地。他又从吴哥引入[ShowReligionName('theravada')]，迎来帕邦佛像。

1359年，应高棉王后请求，他立佛教为国教。1372年贵族废黜法昂，拥立其子桑森泰，法昂最终死于流亡之中。

en:
Panya Khamphong, titled Phraya Khamphong, ruled the Lao principality of Muang Sua, on the site of later Luang Prabang, from 1316. His father Panya Lang had founded the panya dynasty in 1271, in a Mekong valley under strong Mongol influence after the fall of Dali in 1253.

In 1286 Khamphong took part in a coup, probably Mongol-inspired, that exiled his father. Between 1286 and 1297 his lieutenants, acting for the Mongols, pacified wide territories, and in 1308 he seized the ruler of Muang Phuan, which was his vassal by 1312.

After his son Phi Fa took one of Khamphong's wives as a lover, Khamphong drove Phi Fa and his young grandson Fa Ngum into exile at Angkor in the 1320s. Fa Ngum later returned and founded the kingdom of Lan Xang in 1353.

zh:
披耶坎蓬是佬人勐苏瓦（在今琅勃拉邦一带）政权的统治者，1316年起在位。他的父亲披耶朗1271年建立披耶王朝，当时1253年大理陷落之后，蒙古人对湄公河中游有着极大的影响力。

1286年，坎蓬参与了一场多半由蒙古人策动的政变，把父亲赶下台。1286至1297年间，他的部将替蒙古人平定了大片地区；1308年他擒获勐普安的统治者，到1312年该地已成勐苏瓦的属国。

后来其子披法与坎蓬的一名妻妾私通，坎蓬遂在1320年代把披法和年幼的孙子法昂放逐到吴哥。法昂后来重返故土，于1353年建立澜沧王国。

en:
Lao chronicles name Khun Phi Fa (died 1343) as ruler of Muang Sua. The eldest son of King Suvanna Kamphong, he was banished after an affair with one of his father's wives, and his name was changed from Yak Fa to Phi Fa, meaning demon.

He returned to take the throne after his father's death and died in 1343, when his brother Kham Hiao succeeded him. His son Fa Ngum became the founder-king of Lan Xang.

据老挝编年史记载，坤披法（？—1343）是勐苏瓦的统治者。他是国王披耶坎蓬的长子，因与父王妃嫔私通被驱逐，名字也由亚法改为披法，意为恶鬼。

父亲死后他回国登位，1343年去世，由弟弟琴俸继位。其子法昂后来成为澜沧王国的开国国王。

en:
Muhammad al-Jazuli (died 1465) was a Moroccan Sufi sheikh of the Berber Jazulin tribe in the Sous region, who claimed descent from the Prophet Muhammad. He studied at the Saffarin madrasa in Fez, then spent forty years travelling in Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem before returning to Fez.

There he completed the prayer collection Dala'il al-Khayrat, among the most popular devotional works in Sunni Islam. Initiated into the Shadhili order, he spent fourteen years in seclusion before gathering many followers at Safi.

The city's governor expelled and poisoned him in 1465. In 1541 his remains were moved to Marrakesh, where he is honoured among its seven saints.

穆罕默德·贾祖利（卒于1465年）是摩洛哥苏斯地区柏柏尔贾祖利部落的苏菲谢赫，自称是先知穆罕默德的后裔。他曾在非斯的萨法林经学院学习，随后在麦加、麦地那和耶路撒冷游学四十年，回到非斯。

他在那里编成祈祷文集《达拉伊勒·海拉特》，这部书后来成为逊尼派流传最广的虔修读物之一。他加入沙兹里教团，独修十四年后在萨菲聚集了大批弟子。

1465年，他被当地总督驱逐并毒杀。1541年，他的遗骸迁葬马拉喀什，被尊为该城七圣之一。

en:
Ludolf von Steinfurt was a noble lord of the Westphalian House of Steinfurt in the Bishopric of Münster. He held half of Bredevoort Castle, whose other share his kinsmen sold to the see of Münster in 1284.

In the feud against Bishop Otto III of Rietberg he alone fought on after the truce of 1303, and his coalition prevailed and secured the bishop's deposition in 1306. His son Rudolf later became a cathedral scholaster in Münster.

卢多尔夫·冯·施泰因富特是威斯特法伦施泰因富特家族的贵族领主，身处明斯特主教区。他持有布雷德福特城堡的一半份额，族人于1284年把另一半份额卖给了明斯特教会。

在与主教奥托三世·冯·里特贝格的争斗中，1303年停战后唯有他继续作战，其同盟最终取胜，于1306年迫使主教去职。他的儿子鲁道夫后来出任明斯特主教座堂学务长。

Ludwig of Hesse (1282 or 1283–1357), a son of Landgrave Henry I of Hesse, ruled as Bishop Ludwig II of Münster from 1310 until his death, the longest episcopate in the see's history. He curbed the estates and the nobility, bound castle lords to him through open houses, and granted town charters to Dülmen, Billerbeck, Ramsdorf and Rheine.

He founded collegiate churches and monasteries in his diocese and cared for the sick during plague and famine. He died on 18 August 1357.
