黑森的路易（1282或1283—1357）是黑森伯爵海因里希一世之子，1310年起以路德维希二世之号任明斯特主教，直至去世，是该主教区在位时间最长的主教。他压制贵族与等级会议，以“开放宅邸”体系将城堡领主笼络到自己麾下，并授予迪尔门、比勒贝克、拉姆斯多夫和赖讷城市特许状。

他在主教区内修建牧师会教堂与修道院，并在瘟疫与饥荒期间照料病患。1357年8月18日他去世。

Rudolf von Steinfurt, a son of Lord Ludolf VII of Steinfurt, was a cleric in the diocese of Münster. While serving as a chapel rector, he and his brother Baldewin asked Bishop Ludwig II to exchange their prebends, a swap that admitted Rudolf to the Münster cathedral chapter.

In 1364 he is first recorded as Domscholaster, the cathedral school's master, and in 1369 he served the bishop as Amtmann, or bailiff, in the Emsland.

Mutukan (died 1221), also spelled Mö'etüken, was the eldest son of Chagatai Khan and a favourite grandson of Genghis Khan. He took part in the Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire and was killed by an arrow shot from the walls during the siege of Bamiyan in September 1221.

In his fury Genghis Khan had the city destroyed and its whole population put to the sword after it fell. His descendants included the Chagatai khans Qara Hülëgü, his son, and Baraq, his grandson through Yesünto'a.

木阿秃干（？—1221年），又作木阿秃干、莫图根，是察合台的嫡长子，也是成吉思汗钟爱的孙子。他随蒙古大军西征花剌子模，1221年九月在围攻巴米扬时被城上射来的箭射死。

成吉思汗大怒，城破后下令将城池夷平、屠尽城中生灵。他的后裔中有察合台汗哈剌旭烈与八剌，前者是他的儿子，后者是他的儿子也孙脱所生的孙子。

en:
Edmond Albanach de Burgh (died 1375), called the Scot for the years he spent hostage there, was a son of William Liath de Burgh and founder of the Mayo Bourkes, the Mac William Íochtar. In 1332 his cousin the Earl of Ulster starved his elder brother Walter to death in prison; Edmond made himself lord of Mayo, and the earl was murdered the next year in revenge, leaving only an infant daughter.

In April 1338 Edmond and his brother Raymond seized their rival cousin Edmond de Burgh, who was later thrown into Lough Mask in a sack of stones; the killing ended English overlordship of Connacht.

The brothers hid on islands off the western coast until Edward III pardoned them in 1340. Edmond died in 1375 the strongest lord west of the Shannon.

埃德蒙·阿尔巴纳赫·德·伯格（?—1375），绰号“阿尔巴纳赫”（意为苏格兰人），得自他在苏格兰充当人质的岁月。他是“灰发”威廉·德·伯格之子，梅奥伯克家族（北麦克威廉）的奠基人。1332年，表亲阿尔斯特伯爵把他的兄长沃尔特囚禁饿死，埃德蒙自立为梅奥领主；次年伯爵遭人报复杀害，只留下一个年幼的女儿。

1338年4月，他与兄弟雷蒙德擒获身为政敌的堂亲埃德蒙·德·伯格，后者随后被装进石头袋子沉入马斯克湖；这桩命案终结了英格兰对康诺特的宗主权。

兄弟二人逃到西海岸的岛屿避难，1340年获英王爱德华三世赦免。1375年他去世时已是香农河以西最强的领主。

Thomas mac Edmond Albanach de Búrca (died 1402) was the second Mac William Íochtar, lord of Lower Connacht and Mayo. The son of Edmond Albanach de Burgh, founder of the Mayo Bourkes, and Sadhbh Ní Mháille, he succeeded his father as chieftain in 1375.

Three of his sons died in 1384. On his death in 1402 his son Walter mac Thomas succeeded him as third Mac William Íochtar.

en:
Mubariz al-Din Muhammad (1301–1363) founded Iran's Muzaffarid dynasty after Ilkhanid rule in central Iran dissolved. He inherited his father's Ilkhanid offices in 1314 and took Yazd from its Atabeg in 1319. After Abu Sa'id's death he made himself independent, seizing Kirman in 1339 or 1340 and Bam soon after.

The Injuids of Shiraz and Isfahan became his rivals; their ruler Abu Ishaq failed to take Yazd in 1350–1351. In 1353 Mubariz captured Shiraz, chased Abu Ishaq to Isfahan and executed him; Shiraz became his capital. He refused vassalage to the Golden Horde khan Jani Beg, and in 1357 briefly occupied Tabriz before the Jalayirids forced him out.

A harsh ruler, he was blinded and imprisoned by his son Shah Shuja in 1358 and died in prison in 1363.

穆巴里兹·丁·穆罕默德（1301—1363）是伊朗穆扎法尔王朝的开创者，在伊儿汗国于伊朗中部的统治瓦解后填补了权力真空。1314年他承袭父亲在伊儿汗国的官职，1319年从亚兹德阿塔贝格手中夺取亚兹德。不赛因死后，他自立门户，1339或1340年攻取克尔曼，随后拿下巴姆。

设拉子与伊斯法罕的因朱王朝成为他的对手，统治者阿布·伊沙克于1350—1351年围攻亚兹德未果。1353年穆巴里兹攻占设拉子，追击阿布·伊沙克至伊斯法罕并将其处死，设拉子成为都城。他拒绝向金帐汗札尼别称臣，1357年短暂进占大不里士，随后被札剌亦儿军队逼退。

他以严苛著称，1358年被儿子沙·舒贾刺瞎并囚禁，1363年死于狱中。

en:
Shah Shoja (1333–1384) took the Muzaffarid state of southern Iran to its widest reach. He seized power from his father Mubariz al-Din Muhammad: after stopping him from demolishing the poet Saadi's tomb, he blinded and imprisoned him in 1358 and took the throne.

His long reign was a running quarrel with his brothers. Shah Mahmud, backed by his Jalayirid father-in-law, seized Shiraz in 1364, and Shoja could not retake his capital until 1366; he occupied Isfahan after Mahmud's death. A well-educated prince who wrote verse, he was alluded to 39 times by Hafez.

In 1383, drunk, he blinded his own son Sultan Shebli and regretted it the next day. That year he wrote to the warlord Timur and entrusted his sons to him. He died in 1384, naming Zain al-Abidin his successor.

沙·舒贾（1333—1384）把伊朗南部的穆扎法尔王朝带到势力的顶点。他是踩着父亲上台的：穆巴里兹·丁·穆罕默德要毁掉诗人萨迪的陵墓，被他拦下；1358年他刺瞎并囚禁了父亲，夺取王位。

在位期间，他与兄弟们争斗不休。其兄沙·马哈茂德得到札剌亦儿岳父的支持，1364年攻占设拉子，舒贾直到1366年才收回都城；马哈茂德死后，他进占伊斯法罕。他学识渊博、自己也写诗，哈菲兹在诗中39次提到他。

1383年，他酒醉后刺瞎了亲生儿子苏丹·谢卜利，次日便后悔不已。同年，他致信统帅帖木儿，将儿子们托付给他。1384年他去世，遗命以扎因·阿比丁为继承人。

en:
Andrea I Muzaka (died 1319) was an Albanian lord who built the Muzaka family's power from its base at Berat. Holding the Byzantine title sebastokrator and the Angevin office of Marshal of Albania from 1280, he was a vassal of the Angevin kings of Naples, with lands including Myzeqe, Opar and Skrapar in central Albania.

In 1319 Pope John XXII sent confidential letters to Andrea and other Albanian nobles, seeking support for a crusade against the Serbian king Milutin. His son Theodore I inherited his lands.

en:
Andrea II Muzaka (c. 1318–1372) inherited the Muzaka principality from his father Theodore I about 1331 and carried it to its greatest extent. He rose against Byzantine rule in southern Albania in 1335–1341 and in 1336 swore fealty to the Angevin king of Naples, which recognized him as Despot of the Kingdom of Albania.

When Stefan Dušan's Serbia overran the country, he led the resistance and in 1350 retook Berat. After Dušan's empire collapsed, Andrea and King Vukašin both claimed Kastoria's lands; Andrea won at Pelister in 1369, and the Byzantine emperor named him Despot of Epirus.

He adopted a double-headed eagle under a star as his arms, and in 1371 seized Kastoria from Prince Marko. He died in 1372, ruling from the Adriatic to Kastoria.

安德烈亚二世·穆扎卡（约1318—1372）约1331年从父亲特奥多尔一世手中继承穆扎卡公国，并把它扩张到最大。1335—1341年，他在阿尔巴尼亚南部起兵反抗拜占庭统治；1336年他向安茹家族的那不勒斯国王效忠，安茹方面承认他为“阿尔巴尼亚王国专制君主”。

塞尔维亚席卷阿尔巴尼亚时，他领导抵抗，1350年收复培拉特。杜尚帝国崩溃后，安德烈亚与塞尔维亚国王武卡欣同时索要卡斯托里亚一带的土地；1369年他在佩利斯特获胜，拜占庭皇帝因此封他为“伊庇鲁斯专制君主”。

他改用星辰之下的双头鹰作纹章，1371年又从马尔科王子手中夺取卡斯托里亚。他于1372年去世，领地西起亚得里亚海、东至卡斯托里亚。

Her children included Gjin I and Teodor II Muzaka, and her daughter Comita married Balsha II. She and Andrea were buried together in Durrës.

en:
Gjin I Muzaka (1337–1389) was an Albanian prince of the Muzaka family, a son of Andrea II Muzaka and Euphemia Mataranga. In 1367 the Serbian governor Thomas Preljubović held him prisoner for a time in Ioannina.

When Andrea II died in 1372, his lands were divided among his three sons: Gjin received Tomorniza and the Devoll valleys, and after his brother Stoya died without heirs he also took Kastoria. He married Suina Arianiti and was probably buried at Korçë.

en:
Teodor I Muzaka was an Albanian nobleman, son of Andrea I Muzaka, who ruled the Lordship of Berat from 1319 until his death around 1331. His lands ran from Myzeqe and Berat south to Këlcyra, and he held the high Byzantine court title of protosebastos.

His reign was overshadowed by the advance of the Serbian king Stefan Uroš II Milutin and by Angevin claims to Albania. He was succeeded by his son Andrea II Muzaka.

特奥多尔·穆扎卡是阿尔巴尼亚贵族，安德烈亚一世·穆扎卡之子，自1319年至约1331年去世时统治培拉特领地。他的疆土从米泽切亚、培拉特向南延伸至克尔曲拉，并领有拜占庭高级宫廷头衔普罗托塞巴斯托斯。

en:
Teodor II Muzaka (1337–1389) was an Albanian prince of the House of Muzaka, second son of Despot Andrea II Muzaka and Euphemia Mataranga. When Andrea died in 1372, his lands were split among three sons: Gjin inherited the main holdings, Teodor received Berat and Myzeqe, and Stoya took Kastoria.

In 1383–1384 Teodor and Stoya founded an Orthodox church in Kastoria. Teodor fell in 1389 fighting the Ottomans at Kosovo under Prince Lazar of Serbia.

zh:
特奥多尔二世·穆扎卡（1337—1389）是阿尔巴尼亚穆扎卡家族贵族，专制君主安德烈亚二世·穆扎卡与埃菲米娅·马特兰加之次子。1372年父亲去世后，领地分给三个儿子：金继承主体领地，特奥多尔得到培拉特与穆泽切，斯托亚得到卡斯托里亚。

1383—1384年，特奥多尔与斯托亚在卡斯托里亚修建了一座东正教教堂。1389年，他在塞尔维亚公拉扎尔率领的反奥斯曼联军中战死于科索沃战役。

en:
Hasan II (died 1349), also called Fakhr al-Dawla Hasan, was the last ruler of the Bavand dynasty in Tabaristan. A son of Shah-Kaykhusraw, he succeeded his brother in 1334. In 1344 the Sarbadar leader Mas'ud occupied Amol, but Hasan retook Sari and, with the Paduspanid Eskandar II, annihilated the invaders.

In 1349 his execution of a powerful vassal provoked a noble revolt. He sought support, but the sons of Kiya Afrasiyab murdered him in his bath, ending Bavand rule.

en:
Elisabeth of Namur (c. 1329–1382) was the youngest daughter of John I, Count of Namur, of the Dampierre house. Her elder sister Blanche became queen of Sweden, and in 1350 Elisabeth married the Wittelsbach count palatine Rupert I, who secured the electoral dignity for the Palatinate under the Golden Bull of 1356. The marriage remained childless.

A patron of the Heidelberg Franciscans, she enlarged their friary and asked in her will to be buried in their church. She died at Heidelberg in 1382.

en:
Guy II of Namur (c. 1312–1336) was briefly margrave of Namur. The second son of John I and Marie of Artois, he succeeded his brother John II in 1335 and, for a pension, did homage to Edward III of England and joined his Scottish campaign.

At Boroughmuir the Scots surprised his rearguard and captured him. On his way home he was killed jousting in a tournament at Saint-Venant on 12 March 1336, leaving Namur to his brother Philip III.

en:
William I (1324–1391), called the Rich, ruled Namur from 1337. The fifth son of John I and Marie of Artois, he inherited after four elder brothers died childless, his mother acting as regent.

He joined the English side in the Hundred Years' War, though Namur saw only a weavers' revolt in 1351. With money from his mother and wife he bought more lands and promoted mining, metalworking and trade. In 1362 Emperor Charles IV made Namur directly subject to the Empire, ending its vassalage to Hainaut, and in 1371 William was captured at Baesweiler.

His first wife Jeanne of Hainault died of the plague two years after their wedding; in 1352 he married Catherine of Savoy, mother of William II and John III, the last Marquis of Namur.

威廉一世（1324—1391），人称“富有者”，自1337年起统治那慕尔。他是约翰一世与阿图瓦的玛丽的第五子，四位兄长先后无嗣而终，他因而继位，未成年时由母亲摄政。

他在百年战争中加入英格兰一方，那慕尔本土除1351年的织工起义外一直保持和平。他靠母亲和妻子的财富购置土地扩大疆域，并发展采矿、冶铁与贸易。1362年，皇帝查理四世下诏使那慕尔直属于帝国，不再向埃诺称臣；1371年威廉在巴斯韦勒战役中战败被俘。

第一任妻子埃诺的让娜婚后两年死于黑死病；1352年他改娶萨伏依的卡特琳，二人之子为威廉二世和约翰三世，后者是那慕尔的末代侯爵。

en:
Henry II of Courtenay (1206–1229) was margrave of Namur from 1226 until his death. The third son of Peter II of Courtenay and Yolanda of Flanders, he succeeded when his eldest brother Philip II fell heirless on the Albigensian Crusade in 1226; their second brother Robert already ruled the Latin Empire.

After Robert died in 1228, he waived his claim to Constantinople in favour of his brother Baldwin. He died in 1229, childless, and Namur passed to his sister Margaret.

en:
John I of Namur (1267–1330), son of Count Guy of Flanders and Isabelle of Luxembourg, governed Namur for his father from 1297 and succeeded as marquis in 1305. He fought at the Golden Spurs victory in 1302, was defeated at Mons-en-Pévèle in 1304 and made peace with France in 1307.

In 1308 the French king ruled in his favour against Charles of Valois's claim. The emperor's 1314 grant of Cambrai led to his excommunication, and he fought Liège's bishop from 1318 to 1322. With Marie of Artois he fathered later counts and Blanche, queen of Sweden, and died in 1330.

zh:
那慕尔的约翰一世（1267—1330）是佛兰德斯伯爵居伊与卢森堡的伊莎贝尔之子。他自1297年起代父治理那慕尔，1305年继任侯爵。他参加了1302年金马刺战役的胜利，但1304年在蒙斯昂佩韦勒战败，1307年与法国议和。

1308年瓦卢瓦的查理主张继承权，法国国王裁决约翰胜诉。1314年皇帝把康布雷封赐给他，他因此被开除教籍；1318—1322年他与列日主教交战。他与阿图瓦的玛丽生下后来几代那慕尔伯爵以及瑞典王后布兰卡，1330年去世。

en:
John II of Namur (c. 1311–1335) was margrave of Namur from 1330 until his death. The eldest son of John I and Marie of Artois, he succeeded in 1330.

In 1332 he joined a league of Low Countries princes against John III, Duke of Brabant, until Philip VI of France mediated an end to the conflict. He never married and died in 1335, leaving an illegitimate son Philip; his brother Guy II succeeded him.

en:
Louis of Namur (1325–between 1378 and 1386) was a younger son of John I, Marquis of Namur, and brother of the later marquises of Namur. He held the lordships of Peteghem and Bailleul, and in 1346 he accompanied his brother William to the Battle of Crécy.

He governed Namur during his brother's absence when unrest broke out in 1352, and later fought against the Duke of Brabant. In 1365 he married Isabelle de Pierrepont, heiress of Roucy. The marriage was childless, and Louis died between 1378 and 1386.

Margaret of Namur (c. 1323–13 September 1383) was a daughter of John I, Marquis of Namur, and Marie of Artois, and a sister of William I and Blanche, queen of Sweden and Norway.

She became a Poor Clare nun in the abbey of Sainte-Claire de Beaulieu at Peteghem-sur-l'Escaut in Flanders, founded in 1290 by her grandmother Isabelle of Luxembourg, and died there on 13 September 1383.

en:
Marie of Artois (1291–1365), daughter of Philip of Artois and sister of Robert III, married John I of Namur in 1310. He gave her Wijnendale Castle and lands in Flanders. While he was in Italy with Emperor Henry VII, a 1313 revolt at Namur shut her and her three children in Namur Castle until John had the Count of Looz put it down.

Widowed in 1330, she saw three sons succeed as margrave and die within seven years. Her relations with the first, John II, had already soured after she intervened at Sluis.

In 1337 her youngest son William inherited at fifteen, and she ruled Namur as regent until 1340. In 1342 she bought Poilvache from John the Blind of Luxembourg, giving it to William in 1353.

阿图瓦的玛丽（1291—1365）是阿图瓦的菲利普之女、罗贝尔三世的妹妹，1310年嫁给那慕尔的约翰一世。约翰把韦嫩达尔城堡和佛兰德的土地赐给她。约翰随皇帝亨利七世远征意大利时，1313年那慕尔爆发叛乱，她和三个孩子被困在那慕尔城堡，直到约翰说服洛斯伯爵平定叛乱。

en:
Philip II of Courtenay (1195–1226), called à la Lèvre, was Marquis of Namur, eldest son of the Latin Emperor Peter II of Courtenay. In 1212 his uncle Philip the Noble named him heir to Namur. He defended it against Waleran III of Limburg, whose wife held a hereditary claim, until peace at Dinant in 1222.

After his father's death in 1217 he refused the Latin imperial throne, which went to his brother Robert. In 1226 he joined Louis VIII's Albigensian Crusade at Avignon and died of illness. Unmarried, he left Namur to his brother Henry.

en:
Robert of Namur (1323–1391), a younger son of John I of Namur, tied his fortunes to England. As a young man he crusaded in Prussia and the Holy Land. In 1346 his uncle Robert III of Artois sent him to Edward III's camp at the Calais siege, where he made a good impression on the king.

In 1350 he commanded the flagship at Winchelsea; in 1354 he married Isabella of Hainault, sister of Queen Philippa, and became Edward's brother-in-law. He was made a Knight of the Garter in 1369. In 1371 he led troops for Wenceslaus of Brabant at Baesweiler, lost, and was ransomed.

He brought Jean Froissart to England; at his request Froissart wrote a history whose first book of 1373 was dedicated to him. Neither of his marriages produced children.

en:
Angelo Acciaiuoli (c. 1330–1380) was the son of Niccolò Acciaioli, grand seneschal of Naples, and inherited his father's titles in Italy and Greece. From 1358 he was count of Malta and Gozo, and he later became count of Melfi and grand seneschal of the kingdom of Sicily.

He ruled Corinth from 1365 until 1371, when his cousin Nerio I Acciaiuoli drove him out. He died at Messina around 1380.

en:
Beatrice of Sicily (c. 1252–1275), second daughter of Charles I of Anjou, king of Sicily, was betrothed under the Treaty of Viterbo in 1267 to Philip of Courtenay, heir to the Latin Empire. The wedding took place at Foggia on 15 October 1273.

Days later her father-in-law Baldwin II died, and Philip was proclaimed titular Latin emperor with Beatrice as his empress. Their only child, Catherine of Courtenay, was born in 1274. Beatrice died in late 1275.

Beatrice of Anjou (1295–1321), fourteenth child of Charles II of Naples and Mary of Hungary, was twice married for dynastic ends. In 1305 the aged Azzo VIII d'Este, lord of Ferrara, wed the ten-year-old princess; their son Fresco died in 1309, after Azzo himself.

en:
Bertrand III des Baux was born at Andria in 1295, the son of Bertrand II des Baux, and became count of Andria. A leading Neapolitan baron, he served as senator of Rome, captain-general of Tuscany and long as grand justiciar of the realm. In 1309 he married Beatrice of Anjou, daughter of King Charles II.

His second wife Marguerite was the mother of his heir Francis. Pope Clement VI charged him with punishing the killers of Andrew of Hungary, murdered in 1345. He died in Naples in 1347 or 1351.

en:
Bertrand des Baux (c. 1238–1305), youngest son of Barral des Baux and Sibylle d'Anduze, was the first Angevin count of Avellino. In 1265 he joined Charles of Anjou's conquest of the Kingdom of Sicily, and in 1268 Charles granted him the county of Avellino; he fought at Tagliacozzo the same year. In 1270–1271 he was Charles's vicar of Rome.

Avellino rebelled against his harsh rule in 1276. In 1287, commanding a fleet against Sicily, he was captured by the Aragonese near Augusta; after ransom he negotiated a two-year truce, and died in Provence in 1305.

en:
Charles, Duke of Calabria (1298–1328), son of Robert the Wise of Naples, became Duke of Calabria on his father's accession in 1309. After Castruccio Castracani won Altopascio in 1325, Florence elected Charles its signore for ten years in 1326. Then attempting to take Sicily, he sent Walter of Brienne as his deputy.

Charles's arrival checked Castracani, but his harsh taxes led to his recall in 1327, when Emperor Louis IV entered Italy. He died in 1328, before his father. His daughter by Marie of Valois inherited Robert's crown as Queen Joanna I, and a posthumous daughter, Maria, followed.

Carlo de' Cabanni (died by 1340) was the eldest son of Raimondo de' Cabanni, the freed slave who rose to the top of the Neapolitan royal household, and Philippa of Catania, a fisherman's daughter who had wet-nursed the royal children.

He served as royal chamberlain and married Margherita da Ceccano, of the high nobility; they had four children, including Sancia, a companion of Princesses Joanna and Maria.

Within five years of his death the family fell: in 1345 Sancia and Philippa were accused of murdering Andrew, Duke of Calabria, Queen Joanna I's husband. Philippa died in prison, Carlo's brother Roberto was executed, and Raimondello was declared innocent in 1346.

zh:
卡洛·德·卡巴尼（至迟于1340年去世）是拉伊蒙多·德·卡巴尼与卡塔尼亚的菲莉帕的长子。父亲是由奴隶升到那不勒斯王室内廷顶层的自由人，母亲是渔夫之女，曾做王室子女的奶妈。

他曾任王室内侍，娶出身高等贵族的切卡诺的玛格丽塔，两人育有四个子女，其中女儿桑恰是乔万娜、玛丽亚两位公主的女伴。

他去世后不到五年，家族便告覆灭：1345年，桑恰与菲莉帕被指控参与谋杀女王乔万娜一世的丈夫、卡拉布里亚公爵安德拉什。菲莉帕死于狱中，兄弟罗伯托被处决，拉伊蒙代洛则在1346年被宣告无罪。

en:
Charles II, called the Lame (1254–1309), King of Naples, was the son of Charles I of Anjou and Prince of Salerno from 1272. After the Sicilian Vespers, his father made him regent on the mainland in 1283.

Roger of Lauria captured him in 1284; he was still an Aragonese prisoner when his father died in 1285. Crowned by Pope Nicholas IV in 1289, he fought on for Sicily until the Peace of Caltabellotta in 1302, which recognized Frederick's rule for life and the island's return to the Angevins on his death.

His children by Maria of Hungary founded the Neapolitan and Hungarian lines, and he died in May 1309, succeeded by Robert the Wise.

1284年，罗杰·德·劳里亚将他俘获；1285年父亲去世时他仍被阿拉贡人囚禁。1289年，教皇尼古拉四世为他加冕。他继续争夺西西里，直至1302年签订《卡尔塔贝洛塔和约》，承认腓特烈终身统治该岛，其死后该岛归还安茹家族。

他与匈牙利的玛丽亚的子女开创了那不勒斯和匈牙利两支安茹世系。1309年5月，他去世，智者罗贝托继位。

Caterina de' Cabanni was a daughter of Roberto de' Cabanni, count of Eboli and grand seneschal of Naples, and Sichelgaita Filomarino. Through her grandmother Philippa of Catania she entered the Angevin court as a lady-in-waiting to the young princesses Joanna and Maria.

She was given in marriage to Niccolò d'Aquino, lord of Villamaina, becoming his first wife. She had died by 1370, when Niccolò married his second wife, Rosella Crispano.

en:
Charles I of Anjou (1227–1285), youngest son of Louis VIII of France, gained Anjou and Maine from his brother Louis IX and Provence by marrying Beatrice. He joined Louis's Seventh Crusade and in 1250 forced towns including Marseille and Avignon to acknowledge his suzerainty.

With papal support he took Sicily from the Hohenstaufens: crowned King of Sicily in 1266, he defeated Manfred at Benevento and the Hohenstaufen heir Conradin at Tagliacozzo in 1268.

He became King of Albania in 1272 and took Achaea in 1278. The Sicilian Vespers of 1282 cost him the island, but he kept mainland Naples; he died in 1285 preparing its reconquest.

安茹的查理（1227—1285）是法王路易八世的幼子，从兄王路易九世处获得安茹和曼恩，又因迎娶贝亚特丽斯得到普罗旺斯。他随路易参加第七次十字军，1250年迫使马赛、阿维尼翁等地承认他的宗主权。

在教廷支持下，他从霍亨斯陶芬家族手中夺取西西里。1266年他加冕为西西里国王，在贝内文托击败曼弗雷迪，1268年又在塔利亚科佐击败霍亨斯陶芬继承人康拉丁。

他于1272年成为阿尔巴尼亚国王，1278年成为亚该亚亲王。1282年西西里晚祷使他失去西西里岛，但他守住了半岛上的那不勒斯，1285年在筹备反攻时去世。

en:
Dominic Thopia (c. 1300s–1382) was born into the Thopia family of Durrës and made his career in the Church. Educated in Italy, he joined the Dominicans, and in 1336 King Robert of Naples made him court chaplain and adviser.

From 1345 he was the order's vicar for Dalmatia and Durrës and founded its house at Shkodër. Louis I of Hungary backed him as bishop of Ston and Korčula in 1350. His 1360 bid for Dubrovnik's vacant archbishopric collapsed when the council, fearing for the city's autonomy, expelled him.

As archbishop of Zadar from 1368 to 1376 he earned the name Father of the Poor by giving away his possessions, and he supported his nephew Karl Thopia's takeover of Durrës. Moved to Bosnia's bishopric in 1376, he died in 1382.

多米尼克·托皮亚（约1300年代—1382）出生于都拉斯的托皮亚家族，选择在教会中谋出路。他在意大利受教，加入多明我会，1336年那不勒斯国王罗贝托任命他为宫廷神父和顾问。

1345年起，他任多明我会驻达尔马提亚与都拉斯的总代理，并创建斯库台修院。匈牙利的拉约什一世支持他于1350年出任斯通与科尔丘拉主教。1360年他争取空缺的杜布罗夫尼克大主教职位失败，议会因担心城市自治受损而将他驱逐。

1368至1376年任扎达尔大主教期间，他把财物散给穷人，被称为“穷人之父”，还支持侄子卡尔·托皮亚夺取都拉斯。1376年他调任波斯尼亚主教，1382年去世。

en:
Elizabeth of Hungary (c. 1255–c. 1322), daughter of Stephen V, was raised in the Dominican monastery on Rabbits' Island. Her aunt Margaret lived there and wished Elizabeth to succeed her as head of the community, and Elizabeth was recorded as prioress in 1278.

In 1288 she was carried off by Bohemian magnate Záviš of Falkenstein, in a marriage unrecognised by the Hungarian Church; Záviš was executed in 1290. Her alleged marriage to Stefan Uroš II Milutin of Serbia remains disputed. By 1300 she retired to a Dominican convent in Naples, dying there honoured as Blessed Elizabeth the Widow.

en:
Elzéar of Sabran (1285–1323), count of Ariano, was a Provençal nobleman and Franciscan tertiary serving the Angevin kings of Naples. Educated at Marseille's Abbey of St. Victor under his uncle the abbot, he and his wife Delphine of Glandèves took vows of chastity and joined the Franciscan Third Order together.

He inherited Ariano on his father's death in 1309. In 1312 he led King Robert of Naples' army to Rome against Emperor Henry VII, and in 1317 became tutor to Robert's son Duke Charles.

In 1323 he went as ambassador to Paris to arrange Charles's marriage to Marie of Valois, and died there. He was canonised as a saint around 1371.

In 1323 he went as ambassador to [ShowLocationName('paris')] to arrange Charles's marriage to #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('nap_marie_valois').GetID],X #L Marie of Valois#!#!, and died there. He was canonised as a saint around 1371.

普罗旺斯贵族埃尔泽阿·达·萨布拉诺（1285—1323）是阿里亚诺伯爵、方济各第三会会士，效力于那不勒斯的安茹王朝。他在马赛圣维克多修道院受教，由身为院长的叔父教导。他与妻子格朗代沃的德尔菲娜立下守贞誓约，共同加入方济各第三会。

1309年父亲去世后，他继承阿里亚诺。1312年，他率领罗贝托国王的军队进军罗马，对抗皇帝亨利七世；1317年，他成为罗贝托之子查理公爵的导师。

1323年，他出使巴黎，为查理迎娶瓦卢瓦的玛丽议婚，后在巴黎去世。他约于1371年被册封为圣徒。

en:
Philip of Majorca (1288–c. 1343), youngest son of James II of Majorca, came from a pious family: his grandfather James I had given up his crowns to become a monk. At Avignon in 1308 he met the Spiritual Franciscan Angelo da Clareno, sheltering him at Perpignan from 1311.

Philip joined the Franciscan Third Order and held that all clergy should live in poverty, even after John XXII denounced the Spirituals as heretics in 1316. He made Majorca a haven for Beguines hunted in southern France, and vainly asked the pope to recognize his new order, the Brothers of the Poor Life.

After his brother King Sancho died in 1324 he regented for his nephew James III until 1329. From 1335 he lived at his sister Queen Sancia's Naples court, leading a Fraticelli brotherhood until death.

马略卡的腓力（1288—约1343）是马略卡国王海梅二世的幼子，家族素来虔信：祖父海梅一世曾放弃王位做了修士。1308年，腓力在阿维尼翁结识属灵派方济各会士安杰洛·达·克拉雷诺，自1311年起在佩皮尼昂庇护他。

他加入方济各第三会，主张所有神职人员恪守贫穷，1316年教皇约翰二十二世斥属灵派为异端之后仍不改初衷。他让马略卡成为法国南部受迫害的贝居安会士的避难所，又多次请求教皇认可新教团“贫苦生活弟兄”，始终未能如愿。

1324年其兄桑乔一世去世后，他为侄子海梅三世摄政，直至1329年。1335年起，他住在那不勒斯其姐桑查王后的宫廷，领导一个弗拉蒂切利团体，直至去世。

Philippa of Catania (c. 1250–1346), a laundress from a Catania fishmonger family, was chosen in 1298 as wet nurse to the infant son of Robert of Anjou. She followed the court to Naples and in 1305 married Raimondo de' Cabanni, a former Ethiopian slave turned commander.

She became the most influential woman at the Angevin court and nurse to Queen Joanna I. After Joanna's consort Andrew was killed in 1345, she was tortured on a charge of plotting and died in Castel dell'Ovo in 1346.

Philip II of Taranto (1329–1373) was the son of Philip I of Taranto and Catherine of Valois. After his cousin Charles of Durazzo was executed in 1348, he became lord of Albania, and in 1355 married Maria of Calabria, Joanna I's sister.

In 1364 he succeeded his brother Robert as Prince of Taranto and Achaea and titular Latin Emperor. All his legitimate children died young, so at his death in 1373 his heir was his nephew James of Baux.

Francis of Baux (c. 1330–1422) was the first duke of Andria and the first noble raised to ducal rank in the Kingdom of Naples. In 1348 he married Margaret of Taranto, sister-in-law of Queen Joanna I, and governed Naples when the queen fled to Provence.

From 1373 he waged civil war against Joanna over the Taranto inheritance; stripped of his lands, he took refuge at Avignon and was restored only in 1381 under Charles III. He died around 1422.

Gentile II Orsini (c. 1240–after 1314) was a Roman noble of the Orsini and grandson of Gentile I, founder of the Pitigliano line. He served as senator of Rome and as podestà of Florence, then again as senator of Rome in 1299 and 1300.

In 1314 he was Grand Justiciar of the Kingdom of Sicily. His son Romano's marriage to Anastasia de Montfort in 1293 brought the county of Nola into the house, making Gentile the ancestor of its Nola and Pitigliano counts.

en:
Giambattista della Porta (1535–1615) was a Neapolitan nobleman and polymath whose Naples home drew scholars across Europe. In 1558 he published Magia Naturalis (Natural Magic), a popular survey of natural phenomena that he expanded to twenty books in 1589 and which spread knowledge of the lens-equipped camera obscura. His 1563 treatise De Furtivis Literarum Notis described a digraphic substitution cipher, earning him regard as the foremost cryptographer of the Renaissance.

He founded the Academia Secretorum Naturae, but was examined by the Inquisition and forced to disband it. He also wrote some twenty comedies in the commedia erudita tradition.

吉安巴蒂斯塔·德拉·波尔塔（1535—1615）是那不勒斯贵族、百科全书式的学者，家中的学术沙龙吸引了欧洲各地的学者。1558年他出版《自然魔法》，汇编各种自然现象，风行一时；1589年扩为二十卷，书中对加装凸透镜之暗箱的介绍推动了相关知识传播。1563年，他在《论隐秘的文字符号》中记述了一种双字母替换密码，被视为文艺复兴时期最杰出的密码学家。

他创办了自然秘密研究院，却遭宗教裁判所审查，被迫将其解散。他还依博学喜剧的传统写了约二十部喜剧。

en:
Joanna I (December 1325 – 27 July 1382), elder surviving daughter of Charles, Duke of Calabria, and Marie of Valois, succeeded her grandfather Robert the Wise as queen of Naples and countess of Provence in 1343. Her first husband, Andrew of Hungary, was murdered at Aversa in 1345, bringing invasion by Louis I of Hungary.

She later married three more times. In the Western Schism she backed the Avignon antipope Clement VII, and Urban VI declared her deposed in 1380. Charles of Durazzo seized Naples and had her killed at Muro Lucano.

乔万娜一世（1325年12月—1382年7月27日）是卡拉布里亚公爵卡洛与瓦卢瓦的玛丽活至成年的长女，1343年继祖父罗贝托一世之位成为那不勒斯女王，兼普罗旺斯女伯爵。1345年，第一任丈夫匈牙利的安德拉什在阿韦尔萨遇害，引来匈牙利国王拉约什一世入侵。

en:
Giovanni Boccaccio (1313–1375) was a Florentine writer and humanist, ranked with Dante and Petrarch among the three crowns of Italian literature and best known for The Decameron. The son of a merchant, he moved to Naples in 1326, and at King Robert the Wise's court took up poetry, writing Il Filostrato and Teseida.

He returned to Florence in early 1341. The Black Death of 1348, which killed some three-quarters of Florence's people, frames The Decameron, a hundred tales told by ten young people, begun around 1349 and largely finished by 1352. He welcomed Petrarch to Florence in 1350 and called him his teacher.

His Genealogia deorum gentilium (1360) defended the study of pagan antiquity and long remained a standard mythology work. He lectured on Dante in 1373 and died at Certaldo in 1375, leaving his library to a Florentine monastery.

乔万尼·薄伽丘（1313—1375）是佛罗伦萨作家、人文主义者，与但丁、彼特拉克并称意大利文学三杰，以《十日谈》闻名。他出身商人家庭，1326年随家迁往那不勒斯，在罗贝托国王的宫廷开始诗歌创作，写下《菲罗斯特拉托》《苔塞伊达》。

1341年他回到佛罗伦萨。1348年黑死病夺走佛罗伦萨约四分之三人口，成为《十日谈》的背景：十名青年男女讲述一百个故事，他约1349年动笔、1352年前后基本完成。1350年他在佛罗伦萨迎接彼特拉克，此后称其为师。

他的《异教诸神谱系》初稿于1360年完成，为研读异教古典辩护，长期是古典神话的标准参考书。1373年他开设但丁讲座，1375年在切塔尔多去世，藏书遗赠给佛罗伦萨一座修道院。

Helen of Anjou (c. 1235–8 February 1314) married King Stefan Uroš I of Serbia around 1245–1250 and became his queen. Her two sons were the future kings Stefan Dragutin and Stefan Milutin.

After Uroš abdicated in 1276, she governed Zeta and Travunia as dowager-queen until 1308. She built Gradac Monastery and founded the first girls' school in Serbia. She died as a nun at Skadar and was canonized by the Serbian Orthodox Church as Saint Helen.

安茹的海伦（约1235—1314年2月8日）约1245至1250年间嫁给塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·乌罗什一世成为王后，所生二子即后来的国王斯特凡·德拉古廷与斯特凡·米卢廷。

1276年乌罗什退位后，王太后海伦管辖泽塔与特拉武尼亚直至1308年。她修建格拉达茨修道院，创办塞尔维亚第一所女子学校，最终以修女身份卒于斯库台，被塞尔维亚正教会封为圣海伦娜。

Hugh of Brienne (c. 1240–9 August 1296), second surviving son of Count Walter IV of Brienne, inherited the County of Brienne around 1260. After claiming the regency of Jerusalem in vain in 1264, he served Charles I of Naples and recovered the County of Lecce.

Captured at the Gulf of Naples in 1284 and the Battle of the Counts in 1287, he was bailli of the Duchy of Athens from 1291 and was killed at Brindisi in 1296.

en:
Hugues IV des Baux (died 1351) was a Provençal lord who became count of Avellino and admiral of Sicily. He was the son of Raymond III.

In Naples, Queen Joanna's husband Louis of Taranto had held the real power since 1348. In July 1350, with papal blessing, Hugues sailed from Marseille with six galleys to free the queen from him. The expedition succeeded, and he used the moment to marry his heir Robert to Maria, widow of Charles of Durazzo.

Then one of his captains betrayed him to Louis, who had him executed in 1351 and took back full power. Hugues's sons Robert, now count of Avellino, and Raymond were imprisoned.

于格四世·德·博（意大利语作乌戈内·德尔·巴尔佐，1351年卒）是拉伊蒙多三世之子，普罗旺斯领主，后来成为安茹系阿韦利诺伯爵、西西里海军统帅。

在那不勒斯，乔万娜女王之夫、塔兰托的路易吉自1348年起把持实权。1350年7月，于格在教皇祝福下率六艘桨帆船从马赛出发，要把女王从他手中解救出来。行动成功后，他趁机让继承人罗贝尔迎娶杜拉佐公爵卡洛的遗孀卡拉布里亚的玛丽亚。

随后，麾下一名队长把他出卖给路易吉；路易吉于1351年将他处死，重掌全部权力。于格的儿子，即已成为阿韦利诺伯爵的罗贝尔，和拉伊蒙多都被囚禁。

Catherine of Austria (October 1295–18 January 1323), daughter of Albert I of Germany and Elisabeth of Tyrol, saw her betrothal to Philip I of Piedmont come to nothing, while her brothers' plan to wed her to Emperor Henry VII ended with his death in 1313.

In 1316 she married Charles, Duke of Calabria, heir to the Kingdom of Naples. After seven childless years she died in Naples in 1323; Charles then married Marie of Valois, mother of the future Joanna I.

en:
Lorenzo Acciaiuoli, called Lorenzino (1329 – April 1353), was an Italian nobleman and soldier. He was a son of Niccolò Acciaiuoli, grand seneschal of Naples.

He served the Angevin court as royal lieutenant in Calabria and castellan of Naples. When Louis I of Hungary invaded in 1347 to avenge the murder of his brother Andrew, Lorenzo took part in the defence of Melfi.

He married a daughter of Tommaso Sanseverino but left no known children. He died after a short illness and on 7 April 1353 was buried in the Certosa di Firenze built by his father; his white marble tomb slab, showing him in arms, came from the workshop of Andrea Orcagna.

洛伦佐·阿恰约利，通称洛伦齐诺（1329—1353年4月），是意大利贵族与军人，那不勒斯大总管尼科洛·阿恰约利之子。

他效力于那不勒斯安茹王朝宫廷，曾任王室驻卡拉布里亚副官和那不勒斯城堡长官。1347年，匈牙利国王拉约什一世为弟安德烈被杀一事进兵，洛伦佐参加了梅尔菲保卫战。

他娶托马索·圣塞韦里诺之女为妻，没有留下已知子嗣。他在一场急病后去世，1353年4月7日葬于其父修建的佛罗伦萨卡尔特修道院；墓上的白色大理石浮雕刻他全身戎装，出自安德烈亚·奥尔卡尼亚的作坊。

他娶托马索·圣塞韦里诺之女为妻，没有留下已知子嗣。他在一场急病后去世，1353年4月7日葬于其父修建的佛罗伦萨卡尔特修道院；墓上的白色大理石浮雕刻他全身戎装，出自安德烈亚·奥尔卡尼亚的作坊。

en:
Lorenzo Valla (c. 1407–1457) was a Roman humanist, priest and rhetorician who taught at Pavia and, from 1435 to 1445, served Alfonso V of Aragon in Naples.

In 1440 he exposed the Donation of Constantine as a forgery, showing through its anachronisms and crude eighth-century Latin that the charter could not date from Constantine's time. Tried by the Inquisition in 1444, he was saved by Alfonso's protection.

His Elegantiae linguae Latinae became the standard guide to classical Latin. Recalled to Rome by Pope Nicholas V in 1447, he died as papal secretary in 1457.

洛伦佐·瓦拉（约1407—1457）是罗马的人文主义者、神父与修辞学家，曾在帕维亚任教，1435至1445年间在那不勒斯效力于阿拉贡国王阿方索五世。

1440年，他证明《君士坦丁赠礼》是伪造文书：其中的年代错误和8世纪的粗糙拉丁文表明，这份文件不可能出自君士坦丁时代。1444年他受宗教裁判所审判，靠阿方索庇护才得以脱险。

他的《拉丁语的优雅》成为古典拉丁语的权威指南。1447年教皇尼古拉五世将他召回罗马，1457年于罗马去世，时任教皇秘书。

en:
Lodovico, born before 1324, was a younger son of Tsar Michael Shishman of Bulgaria and his Serbian wife Ana, sister of King Stefan Dečanski. Michael divorced Ana in 1324, and she and her sons were kept from court until he died at Velbazhd in 1330.

The victor, Dečanski, made Lodovico's brother Ivan Stephen emperor, but a coup in 1331 put Ivan Alexander on the throne, and Lodovico apparently fled with his mother and brother to Dubrovnik. By 1338 he was in Naples, where King Robert granted him a pension. About 1342 he married Maria of Taranto, illegitimate daughter of Philip I, titular Latin emperor.

By 1357 he had become a Catholic and was styled titular Bulgarian emperor. He was last attested in 1363, when he was captured by Siena at Guardavalle with the Hat Company.

洛多维科（1324年之前出生）是保加利亚沙皇米哈伊尔·希什曼与塞尔维亚妻子安娜之子，在诸子中排行较幼，安娜是塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·德钱斯基的妹妹。1324年米哈伊尔与安娜离婚，安娜母子被逐出宫廷，直到他1330年在维尔巴日德战死。

获胜的德钱斯基立洛多维科的兄长伊凡·斯蒂芬为保加利亚皇帝，但1331年的政变把伊凡·亚历山大推上皇位，洛多维科似乎与母亲和兄长逃往杜布罗夫尼克。1338年他已身在那不勒斯，罗贝托国王赐给他年金。约1342年，他迎娶名誉拉丁皇帝腓力一世的私生女、塔兰托的玛丽亚。

到1357年，他已成为天主教徒，被称为名誉保加利亚皇帝。1363年他随帽子军团在瓜尔达瓦莱被锡耶纳人俘虏，这是他最后一次见于记载，此后下落不明。

en:
Louis of Durazzo (1324–1362), Count of Gravina, was the younger brother of Charles, Duke of Durazzo. Made Vicar- and Captain-General of Albania in 1337, he married Margaret of Sanseverino in 1343 and rose with the Durazzo faction at Joanna I's court.

In 1348 Louis I of Hungary invaded and had Charles executed; Louis was imprisoned with his younger brother Robert until 1352. He spent his remaining years stirring up revolts against Joanna in Apulia with Free Company mercenaries.

In 1360 Louis of Taranto crushed them and shut him in the Castel dell'Ovo at Naples, where he was poisoned on 22 July 1362. His son by Margaret became Charles III of Naples.

杜拉佐的路易吉（1324—1362），格拉维纳伯爵，是杜拉佐公爵卡洛之弟。1337年他被任命为阿尔巴尼亚副王兼总司令，1343年迎娶桑瑟韦里诺的玛格丽塔，并随杜拉佐一系在乔万娜一世的宫廷中崛起。

1348年匈牙利国王拉约什一世入侵，处决了卡洛，路易吉与弟弟罗贝托一同遭囚禁，直到1352年。此后他借助自由雇佣兵团，在阿普利亚煽动叛乱对抗乔万娜。

1360年，塔兰托的路易吉将叛乱镇压，把他关入那不勒斯蛋堡，1362年7月22日他在堡中被毒杀。他与玛格丽塔之子后来成为那不勒斯国王卡洛三世。

en:
Louis of Taranto (1320–1362), second son of Philip I of Taranto and Catherine of Valois, won the crown of Naples by marriage. In 1347 he wed his cousin, Queen Joanna I, two years after her husband Andrew was murdered in a conspiracy that may have involved them both.

When Louis I of Hungary invaded to avenge his brother, the couple fled to Avignon, where Joanna sold the city to Pope Clement VI; the Black Death forced the Hungarians out in 1348 and they returned. Louis took all real power from his wife and purged her supporters. Another Hungarian invasion in 1350 drove them to Gaeta.

In 1352 Clement recognized him as co-ruler, and they were crowned together. He died on 26 May 1362, and Joanna ruled alone again. Petrarch called him violent, deceitful and cruel; his best act was making Niccolò Acciaioli grand seneschal.

塔兰托的路易吉（1320—1362）是塔兰托亲王菲利波一世与瓦卢瓦的凯瑟琳的次子，靠婚姻得到了那不勒斯王冠。1347年，他迎娶表亲女王乔万娜一世；两年前，她的丈夫安德拉什在一场可能牵涉两人的阴谋中遇害。

匈牙利国王拉约什一世为给弟弟复仇入侵时，夫妇逃往阿维尼翁，乔万娜将该城卖给教皇克雷芒六世；1348年黑死病迫使匈牙利军队撤走，二人才返回。路易吉夺走妻子的全部实权，清除了她的支持者。1350年匈牙利再次入侵，夫妇被迫逃往加埃塔。

1352年，克雷芒承认他为共治国王，二人一同加冕。1362年5月26日他去世，乔万娜重新独自执政。彼特拉克称他暴戾、虚伪而残忍；他最好的一项作为，是任命尼科洛·阿恰约利为大总管。

en:
Margaret of Taranto (c. 1325–1380) was a Neapolitan princess, daughter of Philip I of Taranto and Catherine of Valois. Around 1331 she may have married the Scottish claimant Edward Balliol; it was annulled, childless, by 1332.

In 1348 she married Francesco del Balzo, first Duke of Andria. Her children were James of Baux, last titular Latin Emperor, and Antonia, queen of Frederick III of Sicily. Margaret died in prison in Naples in 1380.

en:
Maria of Calabria (6 May 1329 – 20 May 1366) was the posthumous daughter of Charles, Duke of Calabria, and Marie of Valois, and Queen Joanna I's sister. In 1343 she was abducted and married to Charles, Duke of Durazzo, who was beheaded at Aversa in 1348.

A second forced marriage, to Robert of Avellino, ended in 1353 when she had him killed. In 1355 she married Philip II of Taranto; all their sons died young. Her daughters inherited her claim to the Neapolitan throne, and she died aged 37.

卡拉布里亚的玛丽亚（1329年5月6日—1366年5月20日）是卡拉布里亚公爵卡洛与瓦卢瓦的玛丽的遗腹女、女王乔万娜一世的妹妹。1343年她被劫持嫁给杜拉佐公爵卡洛，后者于1348年在阿韦尔萨被斩首。

第二段被迫的婚姻嫁给阿韦利诺的罗伯特，1353年她命人将其杀死。1355年她改嫁塔兰托的菲利波二世，所生诸子均早夭。她的女儿们继承了她对那不勒斯王位的权利；她去世时年仅37岁。

Mary of Hungary (c. 1257–1323), an Árpád princess and daughter of Stephen V of Hungary and Elizabeth the Cuman, married the future Charles II of Naples in 1270, becoming queen of Naples and Albania.

When Charles was captured by Aragon in 1284, and again during his later absences, she governed as regent in Provence from 1290 to 1294 and repeatedly in Naples. Of her children, Robert I inherited Naples while Charles Martel claimed the Hungarian crown. She died in Naples in 1323.

匈牙利的玛丽亚（约1257—1323）是阿帕德王朝公主、匈牙利国王伊什特万五世与库曼的伊丽莎白之女。1270年她嫁给后来的卡洛二世，成为那不勒斯与阿尔巴尼亚王后。

1284年卡洛被阿拉贡俘虏后，她于1290—1294年任普罗旺斯摄政，并在丈夫外出时多次在那不勒斯摄政。她的子女中，罗贝托一世后来继承那不勒斯王位，卡洛·马特罗则名义上领有匈牙利王位。1323年她在那不勒斯去世。

en:
Maria of Taranto (1301/1304–1368) was a daughter of Philip I of Taranto by his first wife, Thamar Angelina Komnene, daughter of the despot of Epirus.

She became abbess of the Cistercian nunnery of San Benedetto at Conversano in Apulia, the so-called Monstrum Apuliae, a privileged abbey whose abbess was uniquely entitled to the mitre and crozier. She died in 1368 and was buried in the church of Montevergine in Naples.

Marie of Valois (1309–1331) was the eldest daughter of Charles of Valois. In 1323 she married Charles, Duke of Calabria, heir of Robert the Wise of Naples, whose first wife had died childless. In Florence she persuaded the duke to let gentlewomen dress as their means allowed.

Her children included Joanna I of Naples and Maria, Countess of Alba. Her husband died in 1328; she never remarried and died in 1331 during a pilgrimage to Bari.

en:
Tommaso Aniello (1620–1647), known as Masaniello, was a fisherman and smuggler in Spanish-ruled Naples. He sold fish to evade tax and was often imprisoned; his wife Bernardina was jailed for bringing untaxed flour into the city.

In July 1647 a new tax on fruit drove the vendors to rise; on 7 July he led the riot that burned the customs houses and forced the viceroy to flee his palace. Made captain-general of the people, he saw him swear to their demands on 13 July.

Accused of madness, he was murdered on 16 July in a monastery. The revolt he began led to the short-lived Neapolitan Republic that year.

托马索·阿涅洛（1620—1647），绰号马萨涅洛，是西班牙统治下那不勒斯的渔民兼走私者。他为逃税卖鱼，常被抓入狱；妻子贝尔纳迪娜也因夹带未缴税面粉入城而被囚。

1647年7月，新征的水果税把小贩逼反；7月7日，他率领暴动者焚毁税卡，迫使总督逃出官邸。他被任命为人民的统帅，7月13日总督宣誓接受民众的要求。

此后他被指精神失常，7月16日在一座修道院遇害。他掀起的起义在同年晚些时候催生了短命的那不勒斯共和国。

en:
Niccolò Acciaioli (1310–1365) was a Florentine banker's son who rose to be grand seneschal of the Angevin kingdom of Naples. Sent to Naples in 1331 on family business, he was knighted by King Robert and became the confidant of the exiled Latin empress Catherine of Valois, whose son Louis of Taranto he helped to reconquer Achaea; in 1358 he was made lord of Corinth.

The family bank collapsed in 1345, yet in 1348 he became grand seneschal. He arranged Louis's marriage to Queen Joanna I and, after Louis died in 1362, defended her against rebel barons.

A friend and patron of Petrarch and Boccaccio, he founded the Florence Charterhouse, where he was buried. He died in Naples on 8 November 1365.

zh:
尼科洛·阿恰约利（1310—1365）是佛罗伦萨银行家之子，后来做到那不勒斯安茹王国的大总管。1331年他被家族派往那不勒斯打理生意，获罗贝托国王册封为骑士，又成为流亡的拉丁女皇瓦卢瓦的卡特琳的心腹，助其子塔兰托的路易重新征服亚该亚，1358年受封科林斯领主。

1345年家族银行倒闭，1348年他却就任大总管。他促成路易与乔万娜一世女王的婚事，1362年路易死后又为女王抵御叛乱的男爵。

他是彼特拉克与薄伽丘的朋友和庇护者，修建了佛罗伦萨卡尔特修道院，死后葬于其中。1365年11月8日，他在那不勒斯去世。

en:
Nicola Orsini (1331–1399), count of Nola, inherited the Neapolitan counties of Nola and Soleto. A Guelph leader aligned with the Angevin crown, he was senator of Rome in 1356 and viceroy of the Abruzzo in 1359–1361, defeating Konrad von Landau's invading Great Company there in 1359.

He became Gonfalonier of the Church in 1365 and later rector of the Patrimony of Saint Peter. A friend of Boccaccio and Salutati, he rebuilt the cathedral of Nola in the Gothic style, a work that ran from 1370 to 1395.

诺拉伯爵尼古拉·奥尔西尼（1331—1399）继承了那不勒斯王国的诺拉和索莱托伯国。作为亲安茹王朝的归尔甫派领袖，他1356年任罗马元老，1359—1361年任阿布鲁佐总督，并于1359年击退康拉德·冯·兰道入侵的大佣兵团。

1365年他受任教会旗手，后来又任圣彼得遗产长官。他与薄伽丘、萨卢塔蒂交游，并主持重建哥特式的诺拉主教座堂，工程从1370年延续至1395年。

en:
Raimondello de' Cabanni was born in 1328, the grandson of the Neapolitan courtier Raimondo de' Cabanni and Philippa of Catania. King Robert of Naples marked his birth with the gift of a woollen cloak decorated with parrots, and he was still a minor in 1345.

After the murder of Andrew, Duke of Calabria, his grandmother died in prison and his uncle Roberto was executed. On 16 May 1346 the crown declared Raimondello innocent. He later held the lordship of Maenza through his mother.

en:
Raimondo de' Cabanni (died October 1334) was a Neapolitan knight of black African origin who rose from slavery to the highest office in the Angevin royal household. Boccaccio says the Ethiopian boy was sold by pirates to the provost of the royal kitchens, who freed and baptized him and made him his heir.

In 1304 or 1305 he married Philippa of Catania, wet nurse of the royal children, and rose to be chamberlain to Charles of Calabria, then seneschal of the royal hospice. He was buried in Santa Chiara, resting place of the Angevin kings, under an effigy of a knight at prayer.

His family's swift ruin is the theme of Boccaccio's tale: in 1345 Philippa and his son Roberto were accused of murdering Andrew, Duke of Calabria; Philippa died in prison and Roberto was executed.

拉伊蒙多·德·卡巴尼（1334年10月卒）是黑人出身的那不勒斯骑士，从奴隶一路升到安茹王室内廷的最高职位。薄伽丘记述，这名埃塞俄比亚少年被海盗卖给王室御厨总管，后者将他释放、为他施洗，并指定他继承财产与职务。

1304或1305年，他娶王室子女的奶妈卡塔尼亚的菲莉帕为妻，此后步步高升，成为卡拉布里亚公爵查理的内侍，最后出任王宫总管。他葬于安茹诸王安息之地圣基亚拉教堂，墓上雕像是一名祈祷的骑士。

薄伽丘的故事正是写他一家的迅速败落：1345年，菲莉帕与他的儿子罗伯托被指控谋杀卡拉布里亚公爵安德拉什；菲莉帕死于狱中，罗伯托被处决。

Raymond IV des Baux (died 1372), fifth count of Avellino and lord of Les Baux, was a son of Hugues IV des Baux. After his father's failed venture against Queen Joanna I, he and his brother Robert were held in the Castel dell'Ovo until 1354, when he succeeded Robert as count.

In 1355 Robert of Durazzo seized Les Baux until Pope Innocent VI paid to restore it. Raymond rebelled in 1357, plundering Provence with Gascon routiers, until Joanna pardoned him in 1363. He left a daughter, Alix.

雷蒙四世·德博（?—1372）为第五代阿韦利诺伯爵、莱博领主，是于格四世·德·博之子。父亲反对女王乔万娜一世的冒险失败后，他与兄长罗贝尔一同被囚于蛋堡，1354年才获释，随后继承伯爵之位。

en:
Raymond de Gramat was apostolic administrator of the Abbey of Monte Cassino from 9 April 1326 until his death on 26 July 1340, and his name survives chiefly through a book.

Around 1330 he probably commissioned a deluxe Vulgate of 507 folios, made in Naples, where Pietro Cavallini had been active since 1308. The more than 250 miniatures at the page bottoms are perhaps by Cavallini or his workshop. His library inventory called it a biblia pulcra, a beautiful bible.

After his death Pope Benedict XII acquired it and in 1341 sent it to the papal library at Avignon. After 1378 the antipope Clement VII painted over its original coat of arms with his own, and the manuscript is now known as the Clement Bible.

雷蒙德·德·格拉马于1326年4月9日至1340年7月26日担任卡西诺山修道院宗座管理者，直至去世，他的名字主要靠一部书流传下来。

约1330年，他很可能委托制作了一部豪华的武加大译本《圣经》，共507个对开页，在那不勒斯完成；彼得罗·卡瓦利尼自1308年起活跃于该城。页脚250余幅细密画可能出自卡瓦利尼或其画坊之手。他的藏书目录称它为“美丽的圣经”。

他去世后，教宗本笃十二世获得此书，并于1341年将它送入阿维尼翁的教宗图书馆。1378年之后，对立教宗克雷芒七世把原有纹章换成了自己的，这部抄本因此被称为《克莱门特圣经》。

Raimondo del Balzo (1264–1321), second Angevin count of Avellino, was the son of Bertrand des Baux. He was captured at Berat in 1281 fighting Byzantium, and again in June 1287, when Roger of Lauria crushed the Angevin fleet off Naples; he was held until 1290.

Charles II made him captain-general in 1294, and he fought in the 1299 Sicilian campaign. After the peace of 1302, he saw to his troubled estates in Provence and Italy, later serving as seneschal in both regions. In 1321, campaigning in Calabria with five hundred Provençal knights, he was killed at Grusana in a night attack, unrecognized, by his own soldiers.

拉伊蒙多·德尔·巴尔佐（法语作雷蒙·德·博，1264—1321）是安茹王朝第二代阿韦利诺伯爵，贝特朗·德·博之子。1281年他在培拉特与拜占庭作战时被俘；1287年6月，鲁杰罗·迪·劳里亚在那不勒斯湾击溃安茹舰队，他再次被俘，直到1290年才获释。

Robert des Baux was the eldest son of Hugues IV des Baux, count of Avellino and lord of Les Baux. In 1350 his father sailed from Marseille with six galleys to free Queen Joanna I from Louis of Taranto, and used the intervention to marry Robert to Maria of Calabria, the throne's designated heiress.

Handed to Louis, Hugues was executed in 1351 and Robert imprisoned, though he became count of Avellino. His forced marriage proved fatal: Maria had him killed in 1354.

en:
Robert of Anjou, the Wise (1276–1343), third son of Charles II of Naples, was the central figure of Italian politics. The War of the Sicilian Vespers shaped his youth: after his father's capture he went to Aragon as a hostage, and in 1298 he led the Angevin invasion of Sicily. The war ended in 1302, and the island was lost to the dynasty.

His elder brothers died or renounced their claims, and he became King of Naples on his father's death in 1309. Leader of the Italian Guelphs, he opposed Emperor Henry VII in 1311–1313.

He preached sermons, and Dante dismissed him as a ‘re di sermone’, a king of words, yet he patronized Giotto and Petrarch, who asked Robert to examine him before his coronation in 1341. His son Charles of Calabria died in 1328, so in 1343 the crown passed to his granddaughter Joanna I.

安茹的罗贝托，世称智者（1276—1343），是那不勒斯国王卡洛二世的第三子，也是当时意大利政坛的中心人物。西西里晚祷战争塑造了他的青年时代：父亲被俘后，他被送往阿拉贡充当人质；1298年，他统率安茹军队入侵西西里。战事于1302年收场，西西里岛从此脱离安茹家族。

兄长们或死或放弃继承权，1309年父亲去世后，他即位为那不勒斯国王。作为意大利圭尔夫派领袖，他于1311—1313年抵制皇帝亨利七世。

他登坛讲道，被但丁讥为“言辞之王”，却依旧赞助乔托与彼特拉克；1341年彼特拉克加冕前，请罗贝托主考。其子卡拉布里亚的卡洛于1328年先他而死，故1343年罗贝托去世后，王位传给孙女乔万娜一世。

After the murder of Andrew, Duke of Calabria, husband of Queen Joanna I, in 1345, he was accused of complicity. Arrested and tortured, he was publicly executed on 2 August 1346.

1345年女王乔万娜一世的丈夫、卡拉布里亚公爵安德拉什遇刺后，他被控同谋，遭逮捕刑讯，于1346年8月2日被当众处决。

en:
Robert of Durazzo (1326–1356) was the third son of John, Duke of Durazzo, and held lordships in the Kingdom of Naples. Captured at Aversa in 1350, he was held by King Louis I of Hungary until 1352, then took refuge at Avignon with his uncle Cardinal Talleyrand-Périgord.

In 1355 he seized the fortress of Les Baux, for which he was excommunicated and forced to surrender it. He fought for the French at Poitiers and was killed in the fighting.

en:
Roberto Orsini (1295–1345) was an Italian nobleman of the Orsini family and count of Nola, the eldest son of Romano Orsini and Anastasia de Montfort, heiress of Nola. He held the office of grand justiciar of the Kingdom of Naples.

He married Sveva del Balzo, daughter of the count of Soleto; their son Niccolò was born in 1331 and inherited Nola when Roberto died early in 1345.

Through Sveva, the Del Balzo inheritance of her brother Raimondo, including Soleto, later passed to Niccolò's son Raimondello, who took the name Orsini del Balzo and founded that line of the family.

罗贝托·奥尔西尼（1295—1345）是奥尔西尼家族的意大利贵族、诺拉伯爵，罗马诺·奥尔西尼与诺拉伯国女继承人阿纳斯塔西娅·德·蒙福尔的长子。他曾任那不勒斯王国大司法官。

他娶索莱托伯爵之女斯韦瓦·德尔·巴尔佐为妻，儿子尼科洛生于1331年。罗贝托于1345年初去世，诺拉由尼科洛继承。

凭借斯韦瓦的关系，其舅拉伊蒙多名下包括索莱托在内的德尔·巴尔佐遗产后来传给尼科洛之子拉伊蒙代洛；后者以奥尔西尼-德尔巴尔佐为姓，开创了该支系。

en:
Sancia of Majorca (c. 1281–1345) was queen of Naples as the wife of Robert the Wise. She married Robert, then heir to the throne, in 1304 and became queen when Charles II died in 1309.

Her court became a refuge for the Spiritual Franciscans. Her brother Philip of Majorca gathered Fraticelli there, and the couple asked Avignon for leave to house them at Santa Chiara, but Pope Benedict XII refused. She repeatedly petitioned for her marriage to be dissolved, to become a nun.

After Robert died in January 1343 she joined the regency council for his granddaughter Joanna I, but it proved ineffective and a papal legate took over. In January 1344 she resigned and entered the convent of Santa Maria della Croce, where she died in July 1345.

马略卡的桑查（约1281—1345）是那不勒斯国王智者罗贝托之妻、那不勒斯王后。1304年她与时为王位继承人的罗贝托成婚，1309年查理二世去世后成为王后。

她的宫廷成了方济各会属灵派的避难所。弟弟马略卡的腓力在这里聚起弗拉蒂切利团体，夫妇二人向阿维尼翁教廷申请让弟兄们入住圣基亚拉修道院，遭教皇本笃十二世拒绝。桑查本人则多次请求解除婚姻，想要成为修女。

1343年1月罗贝托去世后，她加入为其孙女乔万娜一世设立的摄政会议，但会议无力维持局面，教皇派出特使接管。1344年1月她辞去摄政，进入圣玛丽亚·德拉·克罗切修道院，1345年7月在院中去世。

en:
Sancia de' Cabanni was a granddaughter of Raimondo de' Cabanni and Philippa of Catania. Through Philippa's influence she became a lady-in-waiting at the Angevin court, attending the young princesses Joanna and Maria. Early in Joanna I's reign the queen gave her in marriage to the count of Morcone.

Accused with her family of complicity in the murder of Andrew, Duke of Calabria, in 1345, she confessed under torture and was executed on 31 December 1346.

Sveva del Balzo (1305–c. 1336) was an Italian noblewoman and sister of the prominent Angevin commander Raimondo del Balzo. In 1330 she married Roberto Orsini, eldest son of Romanello Orsini, third Count of Nola.

Their son Nicola (1331–1399), later Count of Nola, fathered Raimondello, who inherited the Del Balzo feudal estates from his great-uncle Raimondo and founded the Orsini del Balzo line. Sveva also bore two daughters and died around 1336.

Yolande of Aragon (1273–19 August 1302), daughter of Peter III of Aragon and Constance of Sicily, married in 1297 under the Treaty of Anagni and before Pope Boniface VIII Charles II of Naples' heir Robert, Duke of Calabria.

Her two sons were Charles (1298–1328), later Duke of Calabria, and Louis, who died in 1310. She died at Termini Imerese on 19 August 1302 while following Robert's army in Sicily, never becoming queen, and was buried in Marseille.

en:
Agnes of Navarre (1334–1396), a daughter of King Philip III and Queen Joan II, was raised at the French court as a pupil of the poet Guillaume de Machaut and, by tradition, heroine of his Voir Dit. In 1349 she married Gaston III Fébus, count of Foix, renouncing her Navarre rights.

The marriage was unhappy, and Froissart records how Fébus killed their son Gaston in 1381. Agnes then took refuge at the French court.

纳瓦拉的阿涅丝（1334—1396）是纳瓦拉国王腓力三世与女王胡安娜二世之女，在法兰西宫廷长大，师从诗人纪尧姆·德·马肖；相传她是马肖《真言》的女主人公。1349年，她嫁给富瓦伯爵加斯东三世·费比斯，并放弃纳瓦拉的继承权。

en:
Blanche of Navarre (c. 1331–1398), third daughter of Philip III and Joan II of Navarre, was famed for her beauty. Several betrothals came to nothing before she married King Philip VI of France in 1350. She was queen for only seven months: Philip died that year, and her posthumous daughter Joan was born in 1351.

She refused to marry Peter of Castile, mediated between her brother Charles II of Navarre and John II in 1354, and in 1389 organized Isabeau of Bavaria's coronation.

纳瓦拉的布兰卡（约1331—1398）是腓力三世与胡安娜二世的第三女，以美貌闻名。数次婚约均告落空后，她于1350年嫁给法兰西国王腓力六世；她仅做了七个月王后，腓力六世便于同年去世，遗腹女让娜于1351年出生。

她拒绝改嫁卡斯蒂利亚国王佩德罗，1354年在弟弟卡洛斯二世与法兰西国王约翰二世之间调停，1389年又主持了巴伐利亚的伊莎博的加冕典礼。

en:
Charles II, called the Bad (1332–1387), inherited Navarre from his mother Joan II in 1349 and held the county of Évreux in Normandy. Through his mother, a daughter of Louis X, he claimed the French crown, though the Valois outranked him.

He spent his reign almost entirely in France, treating Navarre as a source of manpower. Married to a daughter of John II, he kept changing sides between John and Edward III of England, using the threat of an English alliance to extract concessions. He had the Constable Charles de la Cerda murdered in January 1354, until John made peace with him at Mantes.

John arrested him at Rouen in 1356; he escaped in 1357 and in 1358 played both sides in Paris, suppressing the Jacquerie while bidding to become Captain of Paris. His plots collapsed in 1378. He died in 1387 after his linen wrappings caught fire.

恶人卡洛斯二世（1332—1387）于1349年继承母亲胡安娜二世的纳瓦拉王位，领有诺曼底的埃夫勒伯国。他通过母亲——法王路易十世之女——主张法国王位，但瓦卢瓦家的辈分压过了他。

他在位期间几乎都待在法国，把纳瓦拉当作兵源。他娶法王约翰二世之女为妻，却在约翰与英王爱德华三世之间反复倒戈，用结盟英国的威胁换取让步。1354年1月，他派人刺杀王室统帅夏尔·德·拉·塞尔达，直到约翰在芒特与他议和。

1356年，他在鲁昂被约翰拘捕，1357年越狱；1358年他在巴黎两面下注，一边镇压扎克雷起义，一边谋求出任巴黎统领。1378年，他的阴谋败露。1387年，他因缠裹身体的亚麻绷带起火而被烧死。

en:
Fortún Garcés, called the One-Eyed (died 922), was the last king of Pamplona of the Arista dynasty, ruling from 882 until 905. Captured at Milagro by Emir Muhammad I of Córdoba in 860, he spent twenty years in Córdoba.

He was allowed home after his father fell at Aibar. He then pursued a policy friendly to the Banu Qasi clan that angered the Pamplonese nobility.

In 905 the nobles replaced him with Sancho Garcés, supported by Alfonso III of Asturias and the counts of Aragon. Fortún withdrew to the monastery of Leyre, where he died in 922.

弗顿·加尔塞斯，绰号独眼者（922年卒），是阿里斯塔王朝最后一位潘普洛纳国王，882—905年在位。860年，他在米拉格罗被科尔多瓦埃米尔穆罕默德一世俘虏，在科尔多瓦被囚禁了二十年。

父亲在艾瓦尔战死后，他获许归国继位。他对巴努·卡西家族采取亲善政策，激起潘普洛纳贵族不满。

905年，贵族以桑乔·加尔塞斯取代了他；桑乔得到阿斯图里亚斯国王阿方索三世和阿拉贡伯爵们的支持。弗顿退隐雷伊雷修道院，于922年在那里去世。

en:
García Sánchez I (c. 919–970) became king of Pamplona in 925, at six years old, under the tutelage of his uncle Jimeno Garcés and his mother Toda Aznárez.

In 934, as a Cordoban army approached, Toda acknowledged Caliph Abd-ar-Rahman III as overlord at Calahorra, winning her son caliphal recognition. García later fought the Caliphate, joining Ramiro II of León at the victory of Simancas in 939.

By his marriage to Andregoto Galíndez, heiress of the County of Aragon, his son Sancho II added Aragon to the Pamplonese crown. García died in 970.

加西亚·桑切斯一世（约919—970）于925年六岁时即位为潘普洛纳国王，由叔父希梅诺·加尔塞斯和母亲托达·阿斯纳雷斯监护。

934年，科尔多瓦军队逼近潘普洛纳，托达在卡拉奥拉向哈里发阿卜杜勒-拉赫曼三世称臣，为儿子换得哈里发的承认。加西亚后来与哈里发国交战，于939年与莱昂国王拉米罗二世联手，在西曼卡斯之战中取胜。

他娶阿拉贡伯国女继承人安德蕾戈塔·加林德斯为妻，其子桑乔二世因此把阿拉贡并入潘普洛纳王权。加西亚于970年去世。

García Sánchez II (c. 964 – c. 1000), called the Tremulous, ruled as king of Pamplona and count of Aragon from 994, succeeding his father Sancho II. With his cousin Count Sancho García of Castile he tried to end his father's submission to Córdoba.

In 996 he was forced to sue for peace before Almanzor, and in 1000 he fought in the coalition defeat at the Battle of Cervera. He entrusted Aragon to his brother Gonzalo and married Jimena Fernández; their son became Sancho III the Great.

en:
García Sánchez III, called of Nájera (c. 1012–1054), succeeded his father Sancho III as king of Pamplona in 1035, ruling Álava and part of Castile as overlord to his brothers Ramiro and Gonzalo.

In 1037 García and his brother Ferdinand defeated and killed Bermudo III of León at Tamarón. He defeated Ramiro in 1043, fixing the eastern border, and took Calahorra in 1045 from the weakened Muslim taifa kingdoms.

His feud with Ferdinand, now king of León, over Castilian lands ended at the battle of Atapuerca, where García was killed on 1 September 1054.

en:
García Íñiguez (c. 810 – 870/882), son of Íñigo Arista, was the second king of Pamplona, succeeding his father in 851 or 852. Raised in Córdoba, he had become regent when his father was paralysed in 842.

In 843 he and his kinsman Musa ibn Musa rebelled against Córdoba, but the emir defeated him and killed his uncle Fortún. In 859 Vikings captured him for a ransom of some seventy thousand gold dinars, but he and Ordoño I of Asturias crushed Musa at Albelda later that year.

In 860 his heir Fortún was captured and held in Córdoba for twenty years. García probably fell in 882 at Aibar, fighting the emir's forces.

加西亚·伊尼格斯（约810—870或882）是伊尼戈·阿里斯塔之子，潘普洛纳第二任国王，于851或852年继位。他在科尔多瓦长大，842年父亲瘫痪后出任摄政。

843年，他与亲族穆萨·伊本·穆萨共同反抗科尔多瓦，遭埃米尔击败，叔父弗顿阵亡。859年，维京人俘虏了他，勒索约七万金第纳尔；同年晚些时候，他与阿斯图里亚斯国王奥多尼奥一世联手，在阿尔韦尔达之战中大破穆萨。

860年，他的继承人弗顿被俘，在科尔多瓦被囚禁了二十年。加西亚可能于882年在艾瓦尔与埃米尔军队作战时阵亡。

en:
García Ramírez, called the Restorer (c. 1112–1150), was lord of Monzón, son of Ramiro Sánchez and Cristina, El Cid's daughter. When Alfonso the Battler died childless in 1134, the Navarrese chose García as their king, restoring the kingdom's independence after fifty-eight years of union with Aragon.

The Aragonese nobles chose Alfonso's brother Ramiro instead. By the 1135 Pact of Vadoluengo García became the adoptive ‘son’ of Ramiro II, and he then did homage to Alfonso VII, gaining recognition of his kingship and Zaragoza as a fief.

He fought beside Alfonso at the capture of Almería in 1147. He died near Estella on 21 November 1150, and was succeeded by Sancho VI.

加西亚·拉米雷斯，绰号“复兴者”（约1112—1150），是蒙宗领主，拉米罗·桑切斯与熙德之女克里斯蒂娜之子。1134年“斗士”阿方索无嗣而终，纳瓦拉人推选加西亚为王，使王国在与阿拉贡联合58年后恢复独立。

阿拉贡贵族转而选择阿方索的弟弟拉米罗。1135年加西亚凭《巴多卢恩戈条约》成为拉米罗二世的“养子”，随后向阿方索七世行臣服礼，得到对其王位的承认，并受封萨拉戈萨。

1147年他随阿方索参加攻占阿尔梅里亚之役，1150年11月21日在埃斯特利亚附近去世，儿子桑乔六世继位。

en:
Henry I, called the Fat (c. 1244–1274), was the youngest son of Theobald I of Navarre and Margaret of Bourbon. He governed as regent during the absences of his childless brother Theobald II, whom he succeeded as king and count of Champagne in December 1270.

He swore to uphold the fueros at Pamplona in 1271 and did homage to Philip III for Champagne. In 1272 he arranged a marriage between his son Theobald and Violant, daughter of Alfonso X of Castile. Theobald died after a fall in 1273, and Henry died in July 1274, leaving his daughter Joan under Blanche of Artois's regency.

恩里克一世，绰号“胖子”（约1244—1274），是纳瓦拉国王特奥巴尔多一世与波旁的玛格丽特的幼子。无嗣的兄长特奥巴尔多二世外出期间，他曾代掌摄政之权，并于1270年12月兄长去世后继位为纳瓦拉国王兼香槟伯爵。

en:
Íñigo Arista (c. 790 – 851/852) was a Basque chieftain remembered as the first king of Pamplona and founder of Navarre. Chroniclers place his rise after the Frankish defeat at Pancorbo in 816 and a Carolingian rout in 824. He is first documented in 840, rising with his Banu Qasi half-brother Musa ibn Musa against the Emirate of Córdoba.

His brother Fortún fell against the emir's forces in 843, and after peace in 845 Pamplona backed Musa's renewed revolt in 850. Íñigo died in 851 or 852 and was succeeded by his son García Íñiguez.

en:
Joan II (1312–1349) was the only surviving child of Louis X of France, and the crowns that should have been hers went to her uncles. Salic Law passed the throne to Louis's brother Philip V in 1316. When Charles IV died in 1328, the Navarrese expelled the French governor and declared her queen.

Philip VI acknowledged her right to Navarre in exchange for her and her husband Philip of Évreux giving up Champagne and Brie for three counties. They were crowned at Pamplona in 1329 and funded irrigation around Tudela, though they lived mostly in France and left Navarre to governors.

In 1346, she granted Edward III's troops free passage through Angoulême in return for protection of her lands. She died of the Black Death in 1349, and her son Charles II succeeded her.

胡安娜二世（1312—1349）是法兰西国王路易十世唯一存活的女儿，本应属于她的王冠都落到了叔父们手里。依据萨利克法，王位在1316年传给路易的弟弟腓力五世。1328年查理四世去世，纳瓦拉人驱逐法兰西总督，宣布她为女王。

腓力六世承认她对纳瓦拉的权利，条件是她和丈夫埃夫勒的腓力放弃香槟和布里，换取三个伯国。夫妇二人于1329年在潘普洛纳加冕，并资助图德拉周边的灌溉工程；不过他们多半住在法国，纳瓦拉交由总督打理。

1346年，她允许爱德华三世的军队自由通过她的昂古莱姆伯国，换取自己领地的安全。1349年她死于黑死病，儿子卡洛斯二世继位。

en:
Joan of Navarre (c. 1326–1387) was the eldest child of King Philip III and Queen Joan II of Navarre. At her parents' accession in 1328 she became heir presumptive to the Navarrese crown, and in 1333 she was betrothed to Peter, heir to Aragon.

The marriage never took place: she was replaced by her younger sister Maria, renounced her succession rights, and in 1337 was veiled as a Poor Clare at the Abbey of Longchamp. She died in the convent in 1387.

en:
Juan Corbarán de Lehet (c. 1282–1355) was a Navarrese ricohombre from one of the kingdom's older noble houses. After the battle of Beotíbar in 1321 he became alférez of Navarre and held the post into the 1340s.

With Juan Martínez de Medrano he led an embassy to Paris to take the oath of Philip II of Navarre. His moment came in 1328: when Charles I died and the succession was in crisis, the Navarrese assembly named the two men regents.

In 1340 he treated with Peter IV of Aragon in Barcelona, and in 1350 Charles II confirmed his title as ricohombre. He died in 1355.

1328年2月卡洛斯一世去世后，纳瓦拉集会罢免法兰西总督，任命他与莱埃特为王国摄政。他们召路易十世之女胡安娜及其夫埃夫勒的腓力返回纳瓦拉，于1329年宣誓即位为国王与女王。梅德拉诺于1337或1338年去世。

en:
Maria of Navarre (c. 1329–1347) was a daughter of King Philip III and Queen Joan II of Navarre and a sister of Charles II the Bad. In 1338 she married Peter IV of Aragon, becoming his first wife and queen; barely ten at the wedding, she only began married life years later.

She died in childbirth at Valencia on 29 April 1347 and was buried at Poblet monastery. Peter IV remarried Eleanor of Portugal before the year ended.

纳瓦拉的玛丽亚（约1329—1347）是纳瓦拉国王腓力三世与女王胡安娜二世之女、“恶人”卡洛斯二世的姐姐。1338年她嫁给阿拉贡国王佩德罗四世，成为他的第一任妻子、阿拉贡王后，时年仅约十岁，数年后才圆房。

en:
Onneca Fortúnez (c. 848 – after 890) was a Pamplonese princess, daughter of King Fortún Garcés. Her father was captured by the forces of Córdoba at Milagro in 860 and held for twenty years. She married Abdullah, son of Emir Muhammad I and later emir himself, around 862; Muslim chroniclers call her Durr, or Pearl.

Her son Muhammad was the father of Abd-ar-Rahman III, making Onneca grandmother of the first Caliph of Córdoba. The Códice de Roda also records her marriage to her cousin Aznar Sánchez, by whom she mothered Toda Aznárez, queen of Pamplona.

zh:
奥内卡·弗顿内斯（约848—890年后）是潘普洛纳公主，国王弗顿·加尔塞斯之女。860年，她的父亲在米拉格罗被科尔多瓦军队俘虏，此后被囚禁二十年。她约于862年嫁给埃米尔穆罕默德一世之子、后来继位的阿卜杜拉；穆斯林编年史家称她为杜尔，意为珍珠。

她的儿子穆罕默德是阿卜杜勒-拉赫曼三世之父，奥内卡因此是科尔多瓦第一代哈里发的祖母。据《罗达抄本》记载，她还嫁给表亲阿斯纳尔·桑切斯，并生下后来的潘普洛纳王后托达·阿斯纳雷斯。

en:
Philip of Navarre (1336–1363), Count of Longueville, was a younger son of King Philip III and Queen Joan II and a loyal brother of Charles II the Bad. In 1353 he married Yolande of Flanders, widow of Henry IV of Bar; the marriage was childless. That same year he and Charles fought King John II of France.

In summer 1363 he joined Bertrand du Guesclin against routier garrisons near Bayeux and Caen in Normandy, caught a chill on campaign, and died that August.

纳瓦拉的腓力（1336—1363），隆格维尔伯爵，是纳瓦拉国王腓力三世与胡安娜二世的儿子、“恶人”卡洛斯二世忠实的弟弟。1353年，他娶巴尔伯爵亨利四世的遗孀佛兰德的约兰德为妻，婚姻没有子嗣；同年他与卡洛斯一同对法兰西国王约翰二世作战。

en:
Philip III of Évreux (1306–1343) came from a minor branch of the French royal house. In 1328 the French crown went to the Valois, but his wife Joan, daughter of Louis X, inherited Navarre and he became its king beside her, ending forty-four years of union with France.

Philip is credited with improving Navarre's legislature. He fought for his cousin Philip VI in the first campaigns of the Hundred Years' War, then turned Navarre toward Iberia, where war with Castile ended at Las Cuevas in 1336.

In July 1343 he joined the siege of Algeciras against Granada with troops and provisions, fell ill, withdrew, and died at Jerez de la Frontera on 16 September. Joan ruled alone until 1349.

zh:
埃夫勒的腓力三世（1306—1343）出身法国王室的一个小分支。1328年法国王位转入瓦卢瓦家，但他的妻子胡安娜，即路易十世之女，继承了纳瓦拉，他与她并肩为王，结束了纳瓦拉与法国长达四十四年的共主联合。

腓力以改进纳瓦拉的立法机构著称。他投身百年战争初期的战役，为堂兄腓力六世作战，随后把纳瓦拉的目光转向伊比利亚，与卡斯蒂利亚的战争于1336年以《拉斯奎瓦斯条约》结束。

1343年7月，他率军携补给赶到围攻格拉纳达的阿尔赫西拉斯前线，不久患病退出，9月16日在赫雷斯-德拉弗龙特拉去世。胡安娜独自执政到1349年。

en:
Sancho Garcés (c. 1038 – 1083) was an illegitimate son of King García Sánchez III of Pamplona, born before his father married Queen Stephanie. He held the lordships of Uncastillo and Sangüesa.

Before 1057 he married Constanza; their son Ramiro Sánchez, lord of Monzón, married a daughter of El Cid and fathered García Ramírez the Restorer, founder of a new Navarrese dynasty. Sancho was killed in 1083 at the treachery of Rueda, stoned with his half-brother Ramiro after entering the surrendered Muslim castle.

en:
Sancho I Garcés (c. 875–925), son of García Jiménez, was the first Jiménez king of Pamplona. He seized power backed by Alfonso III of Asturias, replacing Fortún Garcés in 905.

In 907 he killed his former ally Lubb ibn Muhammad, then crushed the Banu Qasi and annexed the County of Aragon. With Ordoño II of León he took Calahorra in 918, and founded the abbey of San Martín de Albelda in 924. He died by the Ebro on 10 December 925, leaving a young son García; his brother Jimeno Garcés succeeded him.

桑乔一世·加尔塞斯（约875—925）是加西亚·希梅内斯之子，潘普洛纳希梅纳王朝的第一位国王。他在阿斯图里亚斯国王阿方索三世的支持下夺权，于905年取代弗顿·加尔塞斯。

907年，他击杀旧日盟友卢布·伊本·穆罕默德，随后击垮卡希家族，吞并阿拉贡伯国。918年，他与莱昂国王奥多尼奥二世联手夺取卡拉奥拉；924年建立圣马丁·德·阿尔韦尔达修道院。925年12月10日他在埃布罗河畔去世，儿子加西亚年幼，由弟弟希梅诺·加尔塞斯继位。

en:
Sancho II Garcés, called Abarca (c. 938–994), inherited the County of Aragon through his mother in 948 and became king of Pamplona on his father's death in 970. He was the first to style himself king of Navarre.

In 976 the Codex Vigilanus, with the earliest Western Arabic numerals, was completed at Albelda in his reign. Later he suffered repeated defeats by Almanzor of Córdoba: after the battle of Rueda in 981 he submitted at Córdoba in person, giving his daughter to the Muslim ruler. Further raids led him to submit again in 992, and he died during another caliphal raid in 994.

zh:
桑乔二世·加尔塞斯，绰号阿瓦尔卡（约938—994），于948年通过母亲继承阿拉贡伯国，970年父亲去世后成为潘普洛纳国王。他是第一位自称纳瓦拉国王的君主。

976年，载有西方最早阿拉伯数字的《维希拉努斯抄本》在他治下的阿尔韦尔达修道院完成。他统治后期屡遭科尔多瓦的曼苏尔挫败：981年卢埃达之战后，他亲赴科尔多瓦称臣，并把女儿嫁给这位穆斯林统治者。此后入侵不断，他于992年再次称臣，并于994年在哈里发军队的又一次入侵期间去世。

en:
Sancho III Garcés, called the Great (born between 992 and 996, died 1035), inherited Pamplona as a child in 1004 and, through marriage and conquest, built the largest Christian power in Spain.

He added Sobrarbe in 1015 and Ribagorza in 1018, occupied Castile after the murder of its count in 1027 and gave it to his son Ferdinand, and in 1034 captured León.

A patron of Cluny who fostered the pilgrim road to Santiago, he divided his realms among his sons on his death in 1035, laying the foundations for the later kingdoms of Aragon and Castile.

zh:
桑乔三世·加尔塞斯，世称大帝（生于992至996年间，1035年卒），1004年幼年继承潘普洛纳，后凭借联姻与征战建成西班牙最强大的基督教政权。

他于1015年取得索布拉韦，1018年取得里瓦哥萨；1027年卡斯蒂利亚伯爵遇刺后出兵占领卡斯蒂利亚，交给儿子斐迪南，又于1034年攻占莱昂。

他庇护克吕尼教会，推动通往圣地亚哥的朝圣之路。1035年临终时，他把领地分给诸子，为日后阿拉贡与卡斯蒂利亚成为王国奠定了基础。

en:
Sancho IV, called of Peñalén (c. 1039–1076), was proclaimed king of Pamplona in 1054 after his father García III fell at Atapuerca, ruling under his mother Stephanie's regency. Many western lords went over to León at his accession, while his uncle Ramiro I of Aragon supported him.

A treaty with Ferdinand I in 1062 confirmed his rule in the Rioja, Álava and Biscay. In the War of the Three Sanchos (1067–1068) he lost Bureba, Alta Rioja and Álava to Sancho II of Castile.

On 4 June 1076 his siblings Ramón and Ermesinda had him thrown from a cliff at Peñalén. Aragon and León-Castile then divided Pamplona.

zh:
桑乔四世，绰号“佩尼亚伦的”（约1039—1076），1054年父亲加西亚三世在阿塔普埃尔卡战死后被拥立为潘普洛纳国王，由母亲斯特凡妮摄政。即位时许多西部领主倒向莱昂，叔父阿拉贡国王拉米罗一世则支持他。

1062年他与斐迪南一世缔约，确认了他在里奥哈、阿拉瓦和比斯开的统治。在“三桑乔战争”（1067—1068）中，他被卡斯蒂利亚的桑乔二世夺去布雷瓦、上里奥哈和阿拉瓦。

1076年6月4日，兄弟姐妹拉蒙和埃尔梅辛达在佩尼亚伦将他推下悬崖。此后阿拉贡与莱昂-卡斯蒂利亚瓜分了潘普洛纳。

en:
Sancho VI, called the Wise (1132–1194), succeeded his father García Ramírez in 1150, the first to style himself King of Navarre rather than of Pamplona. He inherited a weakened kingdom: Castile had agreed to partition it in the 1140 Treaty of Carrión.

In 1168 he and Alfonso II of Aragon partitioned Murcia at Sangüesa, and in 1181 he founded San Sebastián, Vitoria and Treviño on his western frontier to strengthen royal authority against Castilian expansion.

His daughter Berengaria married Richard I of England in 1191. He died in Pamplona on 27 June 1194 and was succeeded by Sancho VII.

桑乔六世，绰号“智者”（1132—1194），1150年继承父亲加西亚·拉米雷斯的王位，是第一位自称“纳瓦拉国王”而非“潘普洛纳国王”的君主。他继承的王国已然衰弱：卡斯蒂利亚曾在1140年的《卡里翁条约》中商定瓜分纳瓦拉。

他的女儿贝伦加丽亚于1191年嫁给英格兰国王理查一世。1194年6月27日桑乔在潘普洛纳去世，桑乔七世继位。

en:
Sancho VII, called the Strong (c. 1157–1234), the last king of the Jiménez dynasty, succeeded his father Sancho VI in 1194. He fell out with Alfonso VIII of Castile after Alarcos in 1195, and while he campaigned in Africa in 1198–1200 Castile and Aragon invaded Navarre; Castile seized Álava, Guipúzcoa and Biscay.

He distinguished himself at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212, breaking through to the Almohad caliph's tent, later linked with the chains on Navarre's arms.

Lamed by illness, he retired to Tudela and died there on 7 April 1234. The crown passed to his nephew Theobald of Champagne.

en:
Theobald I (1201–1253), called the Troubadour, was count of Champagne from birth and in 1234 succeeded his uncle Sancho VII as the first French king of Navarre. His claim to Champagne was contested by his cousin Philippa, until he paid her to relinquish her rights in 1222.

A gifted trouvère whose songs survive with their music, he led a crusade to the Holy Land in 1239–1240, where treaties he negotiated returned Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Nazareth and Galilee to the Kingdom of Jerusalem. In Navarre he codified local custom in the Fuero General. He died at Pamplona in July 1253, and the crown passed to his son Theobald II.

en:
Theobald II (1239–1270), called the Young, was king of Navarre and count of Champagne from 1253, succeeding his father Theobald I at fourteen. His mother Margaret of Bourbon and James I of Aragon acted as regents until 1256, after which he asserted royal power against the fueros-bound nobility.

He granted rights to towns, and in 1266 held Navarre's first census. In July 1270 he joined Louis IX's Eighth Crusade to Tunis. Louis died during the siege, and Theobald died childless at Trapani in December 1270; his brother Henry I succeeded him.

Toda Aznárez (c. 876 – 958) was queen of Pamplona, wife of King Sancho I Garcés. After the deaths of her husband and his brother King Jimeno, she ruled as regent from 931 for her young son García Sánchez I.

托达·阿斯纳雷斯（约876—958年）是潘普洛纳王后，国王桑乔·加尔塞斯一世之妻。丈夫及其弟希梅诺相继去世后，她自931年起为幼子加西亚·桑切斯一世摄政。

934年她向侄子、科尔多瓦哈里发阿卜杜勒-拉赫曼三世称臣，又把女儿们嫁入莱昂、卡斯蒂利亚和阿拉瓦的统治家族。958年，她亲赴科尔多瓦，为被废黜的外孙“胖子”桑乔求医，同年去世。

en:
Angelo Sanudo (died 1262), a son of Marco I Sanudo, succeeded his father in 1227 as the second duke of the Archipelago, the Venetian duchy centered on Naxos.

In 1235 he sent a naval squadron to defend Constantinople, where the Latin emperor John of Brienne was besieged by the forces of Nicaea and Bulgaria, and his further mediation produced a two-year truce between the two empires.

He married a daughter of Macaire de Sainte-Ménéhould. In 1261 she welcomed Emperor Baldwin II at Thebes after he fled Constantinople following its fall to the Byzantines. Their son Marco II succeeded Angelo.

1235年，他派出舰队援救君士坦丁堡：当时拉丁皇帝布里耶纳的约翰正遭尼西亚与保加利亚联军围攻，经他进一步斡旋，两国达成为期两年的停战。

en:
John I Sanudo, called Janulli (died 1362), a son of William I, succeeded his brother Nicholas I in 1341 as sixth duke of the Archipelago. In 1344 the Aydınid Turks occupied part of Naxos and carried off some six thousand islanders as slaves.

Backing Venice in her war with Genoa, he was captured and imprisoned at Genoa, and held there despite papal pleas until the peace settlement of 1355. By his wife Maria he left a daughter, Florence, who followed him as duchess of the Archipelago.

en:
Guglielmo I Sanudo (died c. 1323), son of Marco II, was the fourth duke of the Archipelago. In 1286, as lord of Syros, he bought a donkey stolen from the Ghisi family of Tinos; the Ghisi invaded Syros and besieged him in his castle, and the quarrel, called the War of the Donkey, ended only through Angevin intervention and Venetian arbitration.

In 1303 he inherited an intact duchy from his father. He ruled until his death, when his son Nicholas succeeded him.

en:
Marco Sanudo (c. 1153 – c. 1227) was a Venetian adventurer who founded the Duchy of the Archipelago. Maternal nephew of Doge Enrico Dandolo, he took part in the Fourth Crusade in 1204 and helped negotiate Venice's purchase of Crete. Between 1205 and 1207 he raised a fleet and conquered Naxos and other Cycladic islands. He built his capital of Kastro and kept the Greek archontes in possession of their lands and religion.

He became a vassal of the Latin Emperor Henry around 1210 or 1216 and fought the Empire of Nicaea for him. He died around 1227 and was succeeded by his son Angelo.

en:
Marco II Sanudo (died c. 1303), eldest son of Angelo Sanudo, succeeded as third duke of the Archipelago in 1262. Early in his reign the Byzantine admiral Licario, campaigning for Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos, seized most of the Cyclades from the Latins, and Marco lost many of his islands, holding little beyond Naxos and Paros.

About two decades later he recovered the islands. He left the duchy essentially intact to his son William I, who succeeded him.

en:
Nicholas II Sanudo, called Spezzabanda, was lord of Gridia on Andros and, from 1364 to 1371, eighth duke of the Archipelago, ruling as husband and co-ruler of his cousin Duchess Florence Sanudo. Florence, widowed in 1358, was twice barred by Venice from remarrying before the Republic took her to Crete and forced the match in 1364.

When Florence died in 1371 his own rule came to an end. By her he left two daughters: Maria, who inherited Andros, and Elisabetta.

en:
Nicholas I Sanudo (c. 1295–1341), son of William I, became fifth duke of the Archipelago in 1323. In 1311 he fought at Halmyros beside his brother-in-law Walter V of Brienne, duke of Athens, and was one of the few knights on the losing side to escape with life and freedom.

As a vassal of Achaea he joined John of Gravina's 1325 campaign in the Morea and fought at the futile siege of Karytaina. When John left in spring 1326, Nicholas took charge and beat a larger Byzantine army before leaving the Morea.

He married Joanna of Brienne. On his death his brother John I succeeded him, while another brother, Marco, was lord of Milos.

Nicholas I Sanudo (c. 1295–1341), son of William I, became fifth duke of the Archipelago in 1323. In 1311 he fought at Halmyros beside his brother-in-law #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('ath_gautier_v_brienne').GetID],X #L Walter V of Brienne#!#!, duke of [GetCountry('ATH').GetName], and was one of the few knights on the losing side to escape with life and freedom.

As a vassal of [GetCountry('ACH').GetName] he joined #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('alb_john_gravina').GetID],X #L John of Gravina#!#!'s 1325 campaign in the [GetCountry('MOE').GetName] and fought at the futile siege of Karytaina. When John left in spring 1326, Nicholas took charge and beat a larger Byzantine army before leaving the Morea.

He married #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('nax_joanna_brienne').GetID],X #L Joanna of Brienne#!#!. On his death his brother John I succeeded him, while another brother, Marco, was lord of Milos.
zh:
尼科洛一世·萨努多（约1295—1341）是古列尔莫一世之子，1323年成为第五代群岛公爵。1311年，他随内兄、雅典公爵戈蒂埃五世·德·布里耶纳参加阿尔米罗斯之战，战败后是少数既保住性命又未被俘的骑士之一。

作为亚该亚亲王国的藩属，他于1325年加入格拉维纳的乔凡尼的摩里亚远征，参与徒劳无功的卡里泰纳围城战。1326年春乔凡尼离开后由尼科洛接掌军事，他击败一支兵力占优的拜占庭军队，随后离开摩里亚。

他娶布里耶纳的让娜为妻。他死后由弟弟乔瓦尼一世继位，另一位兄弟马尔科为米洛斯岛领主。

en:
Michiel de Ruyter (1607–1676) was a Dutch naval commander, born at Vlissingen in Zeeland. He went to sea at eleven and became a merchant master at thirty, fought Spain in 1641, traded until the 1652 Anglo-Dutch War, and rose to vice admiral.

Made commander of the Dutch fleet in 1665, he won the Four Days' Battle in 1666 and in 1667 led the Raid on the Medway, burning English ships and towing off Royal Charles. In 1672–1673 he foiled an Anglo-French invasion at Solebay, Schooneveld and Texel. Mortally wounded at Augusta off Sicily, he died at Syracuse in 1676.

米希尔·德·鲁伊特（1607—1676）是荷兰海军将领，生于泽兰省弗利辛恩。他十一岁登船，三十岁成为商船船长，1641年参加对西班牙作战，后重操商船旧业，1652年英荷战争中晋升中将。

1665年他出任荷兰舰队总司令，1666年赢得四日海战，1667年奇袭梅德韦河，焚毁英格兰舰船并拖走旗舰“皇家查理号”。1672—1673年他在索莱湾、斯洪内费尔德与泰瑟尔诸役挫败英法联军入侵。1676年他在西西里附近的奥古斯塔海战受致命伤，卒于锡拉库萨。

Alberto da Verona was a Lombard nobleman of Negroponte, a son of Giberto da Verona, one of the three original triarchs. In the Venetian partition of 1216/17, the central triarchy was split between Alberto and his brother Guglielmo I, each holding a sixth of Euboea.

He died no later than 1255, and Guglielmo inherited his share before passing it to Alberto's son Grapello. In 1256, after the Lombard barons repudiated their prince, Grapello was named triarch in his place.

阿尔贝托·达·维罗纳是内格罗蓬特的伦巴第贵族，初代三执政之一吉贝尔托·达·维罗纳之子。在1216/17年威尼斯主持的分割中，中部三头领地由他与兄弟古列尔莫一世瓜分，二人各领埃维亚岛的六分之一。

他不迟于1255年去世，古列尔莫继承他的份额后，将其交给阿尔贝托之子格拉佩洛。1256年伦巴第男爵们宣布不臣服于他们的亲王后，格拉佩洛被推为三执政以继其位。

Alicia dalle Carceri (died 1313) was the daughter of the Negroponte triarch Narzotto dalle Carceri and Felisa da Verona. She held the southern triarchy, based at Karystos, as triarchissa from 1285 until her death.

Around 1299 she married Giorgio Ghisi I, lord of Tinos and Mykonos, who ruled her third until he fell against the Catalan Company at the Cephissos in 1311. Her son Bartolomeo Ghisi succeeded her in 1313.

en:
Andrea Cornaro (died 1323) was a Venetian noble and baron of Scarpanto. In 1306 he conquered Karpathos from the Byzantines.

In 1312 he married Maria dalle Carceri, heiress of a sixth of Euboea, and co-governed her share of the marquisate of Bodonitsa. The Hospitallers seized his islands in 1313 and he recovered them only in 1320. Under a 1319 treaty he paid the Catalans of Athens an annual tribute of four warhorses. He died in 1323, his sons succeeding to his fiefs.

安德烈亚·科尔纳罗（？—1323）是威尼斯贵族、斯卡尔潘托男爵。1306年，他从拜占庭手中征服卡尔帕索斯岛。

en:
Balzana Gozzadini was a Lombard noblewoman in Frankish Greece. Widowed by the baron of Arcadia in Achaea, she held half that barony and in 1324 married the Negroponte triarch Peter dalle Carceri, who through her became Baron of Arcadia and whose heir Giovanni she bore. When Peter died in 1340 leaving a young son, she ruled his two triarchies as regent.

In 1343 she joined other lords in arming a galley for the first Smyrniote crusade and fortified Euboea against Turkish raiders. She died after 1343.

巴尔扎娜·戈扎迪尼是法兰克希腊的伦巴第贵妇。她先嫁亚该亚的阿卡迪亚男爵，以遗孀身份领有半份男爵领地；1324年改嫁内格罗蓬特三执政彼得·达莱·卡尔切里，后者凭她成为阿卡迪亚男爵，她生下继承人乔瓦尼。1340年彼得去世、儿子年幼，她以摄政身份统治他的两个三主辖区。

1343年，她与其他领主合力装备一艘桨帆船参加第一次士麦那十字军，又加固埃维亚岛的工事抵御土耳其人袭扰。她于1343年之后去世。

en:
Bartholomew II Ghisi (c. 1300–1341) held his triarchy while Venice and the Catalan Company fought over Euboea. His father George I Ghisi fell to the Catalans in 1311, and his mother Alice governed until 1313. By 1315 he held Tinos, Mykonos and one of Euboea's triarchies, and in 1319 he signed the Venetian-brokered truce with the Catalans.

As Grand Constable of Achaea he was captured in 1320 by the Byzantine governor Andronikos Asen and held in Constantinople until 1325. In 1326/27 he made peace with the Catalans, marrying his son George to Simona, daughter of Alfonso Fadrique.

The dowry brought half the castellany of Saint Omer in Thebes, and Venice protested. In 1331/32 he backed Walter VI of Brienne's attempt on Athens. He died in 1341.
