en:
Beatrice da Verona (died 1328) ruled the central triarchy of Negroponte as its reigning baroness from 1285 until her death. A daughter of Giberto II da Verona and Maria Navigajoso, she spent much of her reign away from the island and left the government to her mother at Chalkis.

Her husband Jean de Noyers became her co-ruler in 1303. When she died in 1328, her son Pietro dalle Carceri succeeded to her third.

en:
Bertha dalle Carceri (died 1240) was a Lombard noblewoman of Negroponte, the daughter of Ravano dalle Carceri, sole lord of Euboea until his death in 1216. The Venetian bailo then divided the island into six hexarchies, and Bertha received the southern third of Karystos jointly with her mother Isabella.

Under the settlement, a dead hexarch's share passed to the other holder of their third, not to their heirs. She ruled her sixth until her death in 1240.

en:
Boniface of Verona (c. 1270–1317/18), a younger son of Francesco of Verona, sold his inheritance in 1287 to become a knight at the court of Athens, where Duke Guy II gave him thirteen castles. Through his wife he claimed Aegina and Karystos, and in 1296 he expelled the Byzantines from Euboea.

He regented Athens in 1308/09. Captured at Halmyros in 1311, he refused the Catalans' offer to lead them. In 1317 he married his daughter Marulla to Alfonso Fadrique and died soon after.

博尼法乔·达维罗纳（约1270—1317/18）是弗朗切斯科·达维罗纳的幼子。1287年他卖掉继承的城堡，置办装备前往雅典公国投身骑士生涯；雅典公爵居伊二世对他宠信有加，封给他十三座城堡。他凭妻子取得埃伊纳与卡里斯托斯的继承权，1296年把拜占庭人全部赶出埃维亚岛。

en:
Carintana dalle Carceri (died 1255) ruled the northern triarchy of Negroponte from Oreos from about 1220 until her death. She had succeeded her father, Rizzardo dalle Carceri, one of the Lombard hexarchs set up in 1216.

When she died childless in 1255, her kinsman Leone dalle Carceri claimed the inheritance against the other two triarchs and appealed to William II of Villehardouin. The quarrel grew into the War of the Euboeote Succession, drawing in Venice; Leone's son Grapella succeeded her.

Felisa da Verona was a Lombard noblewoman of Negroponte, daughter of Guglielmo I da Verona and sister of Giberto II. Her first husband was Narzotto dalle Carceri, triarch of the southern third, who died in 1264.

Afterwards Licario, a knight in her brother's service, wooed and secretly married her, but her relatives dissolved the match and drove him out. Licario then took service with Emperor Michael VIII and conquered most of Euboea for Byzantium.

Giberto da Verona (died c. 1208) was a Veronese nobleman of the dalle Carceri kindred and one of the first triarchs of Frankish Negroponte. In 1200 he and his kinsman Ravano joined the Fourth Crusade and fought at Constantinople's capture.

He then served Boniface of Montferrat, who enfeoffed him in August 1205 with the central third of Euboea around Chalkis. He died about 1208, leaving sons Guglielmo I and Alberto, who later held shares there.

Giberto II da Verona (died 1278) was triarch of the central third of Negroponte from 1275, second son of Guglielmo I da Verona. He succeeded after his elder brother Guglielmo II fell fighting the Byzantines amid Licario's reconquest of Euboea.

Giberto joined Marino II dalle Carceri in resisting the invasion, but in 1278 the two triarchs lost a decisive battle and perished or fled the island. Central Euboea then passed under Byzantine control.

en:
George I Ghisi (died 15 March 1311), son of the Venetian lord Bartholomew Ghisi, held the Achaean barony of Chalandritsa through his first wife. In 1292, as castellan of Kalamata, he attacked Roger of Lauria's fleet near Navarino, was captured, and freed only for a heavy ransom.

In Venice's war with Byzantium he helped seize Keos and Serifos, and in 1303 inherited Tinos and Mykonos. Through his second wife Alice dalle Carceri he became triarch of Negroponte, and fell against the Catalan Company at the Cephissos in 1311.

en:
George II Ghisi (c. 1318–1344/45), son of Bartholomew II Ghisi, was lord of Tinos and Mykonos and triarch of Negroponte. In 1326/27 his father married him to Simona of Aragon, daughter of Alfonso Fadrique, sealing peace with the Catalans; her dowry brought half the castellany of Saint Omer. He succeeded in 1341. At Clement VI's call in 1343 he armed a galley for the first Smyrniote crusade.

The crusade's leaders all died in the fighting, and George vanishes from the record after 1344/45, so he may have gone in person and fallen with them. His minor son Bartholomew III succeeded under Simona's regency.

乔治二世·吉西（约1318—1344/45）是巴尔托洛梅奥二世·吉西之子，领有蒂诺斯岛、米科诺斯岛，并任内格罗蓬特三主之一。1326/27年，父亲为他与阿方索·法德里克之女、阿拉贡的西莫娜成婚，以此同加泰罗尼亚人讲和；西莫娜的嫁妆是圣奥梅尔城堡领地的一半。1341年他继承父亲之位。1343年应教皇克雷芒六世号召，他装备一艘桨帆船参加第一次士麦那十字军。

这支十字军的统帅们先后战死，乔治在1344/45年之后也不再见于记载，可能亲赴战场，与他们一同阵亡。幼子巴尔托洛梅奥三世继位，由西莫娜摄政。

Giovanni dalle Carceri (c. 1330–1358) was central triarch of Negroponte from 1340 to 1358. The son of Peter dalle Carceri and Balzana Gozzadini, he inherited Chalkis in 1340 aged ten, under his mother's regency, until he came of age in 1349.

A planned sale of his claims to Duke John I Sanudo of Naxos instead became a marriage to his daughter Florence. From 1350 to 1352 he gave Venice help against Genoa, and on his death in 1358 his son Nicholas III succeeded.

乔瓦尼·达莱·卡尔切里（约1330—1358）是1340至1358年的内格罗蓬特中部三执政。他是彼得·达莱·卡尔切里与巴尔扎娜·戈扎迪尼之子，1340年年仅十岁便继承哈尔基斯，由母亲摄政，1349年成年亲政。

他曾打算把自己的权利卖给纳克索斯公爵乔瓦尼一世·萨努多，最终改为迎娶公爵之女菲奥伦扎。1350至1352年威尼斯对热那亚作战期间，他向威尼斯提供大量援助；1358年去世，其子尼科洛三世继位。

Grapella dalle Carceri (died 1264) was a Lombard triarch of Negroponte, son of Leone dalle Carceri and son-in-law of Guglielmo I da Verona. After Carintana dalle Carceri died childless in 1255, his family's claim to the northern triarchy helped provoke the War of the Euboeote Succession.

In the 1262 peace, William II recognized Grapella as one of the island's three triarchs. He ruled until his death in 1264.

en:
Grapozzo dalle Carceri was a Lombard nobleman of Frankish Euboea, or Negroponte. When the triarch Grapella died without children, Grapozzo and his brother Gaetano divided his third, and in 1264 Grapozzo received the northern sixth of the island, the barony of Oreos.

He married Beatrice, daughter of Giberto II da Verona, triarch of the central third; her brothers died young, so she was heiress of her father's third. Grapozzo lived chiefly at Naples, and a deputy governed his sixth.

He was dead by 1296, when Beatrice administered the northern sixth for their young son Pietro, who recovered his father's lands in 1323. Beatrice later remarried and died in 1328.

格拉波佐·达莱·卡尔切里是法兰克人治下埃维亚岛（内格罗蓬特）的伦巴第贵族。三主之一格拉佩拉死后无嗣，格拉波佐与兄弟加埃塔诺分割其三分之一辖区，1264年他分得该岛北部的六分之一，即奥雷奥斯男爵领。

他娶中部三主之一吉贝尔托二世·达·维罗纳之女贝亚特丽切为妻；贝亚特丽切的兄弟早夭，因而是其父辖区的女继承人。格拉波佐主要住在那不勒斯，由副手掌管其辖区。

1296年前他已去世，当时贝亚特丽切为年幼的儿子彼得代管北部辖区；彼得于1323年收回父亲的领地。贝亚特丽切后来改嫁，1328年去世。

Guglielmo I da Verona (died 1263) ruled the central third of Frankish Euboea around Chalkis as triarch from 1216. An infant when his father Giberto died, he received the family share in 1217 with his brother Alberto. Through his wife Elena of Montferrat he bore the title king of Thessalonica in 1243–1246.

In 1256 he and his son-in-law Narzotto opposed William II's seizure of a triarchy but were beaten at Karydi. He died in a Byzantine raid in 1263.

en:
Guglielmo II da Verona (died 1273/75) was a Lombard noble of Negroponte, the second son of Guglielmo I da Verona, triarch of the central third of Euboea. He married Catherine, a niece of Prince William II of Villehardouin, with whom he had no known children.

He joined the Latin lords' naval attack on the Byzantine fleet anchored at Demetrias: after an initial Lombard success, the despot John Palaiologos arrived through the night with reinforcements and routed the Latin fleet. Guglielmo was killed in the battle, while the Venetian commander Filippo Sanudo was captured.

Isabella dalle Carceri (died 1220) was a Lombard noblewoman who ruled Chalkis on Negroponte after her husband's death. Before 1212 Pope Innocent III let the Archbishop of Athens marry her to Ravano dalle Carceri, though she was another man's wife.

When Ravano died in 1216 the Venetian bailiff divided Euboea into sixths, assigning Isabella half of the central third around Chalkis, held until her death. She has sometimes been identified with the trobairitz Ysabella.

en:
Leone dalle Carceri (last attested 1259) was a Lombard baron of Negroponte and kinsman of Carintana dalle Carceri, the northern triarch of Oreos. When Carintana died childless in 1255 and the other two triarchs shut his family out, Leone appealed to William II of Villehardouin, the island's overlord.

William imprisoned the two triarchs and occupied Oreos, opening the War of the Euboeote Succession. Leone's son Grapella was recognized as triarch in the peace of 1262.

莱昂内·达莱·卡尔切里（1259年最后见载）是内格罗蓬特的伦巴第贵族，北区奥雷奥斯三执政卡林塔娜·达莱·卡尔切里的亲属。1255年卡林塔娜死后无嗣，另外两名三执政将他的家族排除在继承之外，莱昂内遂向埃维亚岛封君威廉二世·德·维尔阿杜安申诉。

威廉囚禁两名三执政并占领奥雷奥斯，埃维亚继承战争由此爆发。在1262年的和约中，莱昂内之子格拉佩拉被承认为三执政。

en:
Maria dalle Carceri (died 1323) was marchioness of Bodonitsa from 1311 until her death. Born to a Lombard family of Verona, she was the daughter of Gaetano and heiress to a sixth of Euboea.

Her first husband, Albert Pallavicini, was killed at the Battle of the Cephissus in 1311, and Maria succeeded him, dividing the march with their daughter Guglielma. She kept the Catalan Company from taking Bodonitsa but paid them a tribute of four warhorses, then married Andrea Cornaro for protection.

玛丽亚·达莱·卡尔切里（？—1323）自1311年起担任博多尼察女侯爵，直至去世。她出身维罗纳的伦巴第家族，是加埃塔诺之女，并继承了埃维亚岛六分之一的领地。

她的第一任丈夫阿尔贝托·帕拉维奇尼于1311年在凯菲索斯河战役中阵亡，玛丽亚继位，与女儿古列尔玛瓜分侯国。她使博多尼察免于被加泰罗尼亚佣兵团吞并，但须年年向其进贡四匹战马；随后她为求得庇护改嫁安德烈亚·科尔纳罗。

en:
Marino I dalle Carceri (died 1247) was a Lombard hexarch of Negroponte who ruled the northern triarchy from Oreos. Son of Redondello dalle Carceri and nephew of Ravano, he married Margherita, daughter of Pecoraro da Mercanuovo.

When Ravano died, the Venetian bailo split the island into six hexarchies; Marino took a northern share with his brother Rizzardo. He ruled until 1247, and his son Narzotto later became triarch of Chalkis.

马里诺一世·达莱·卡尔切里（？—1247）是内格罗蓬特的伦巴第六分领主，以奥雷奥斯为治所统治北区。他是雷东代洛·达莱·卡尔切里之子、拉瓦诺的侄子，娶佩科拉罗·达·梅尔卡诺沃的女儿玛格丽塔为妻。

en:
Marino II dalle Carceri (died 1278) was the son of the southern triarch Narzotto dalle Carceri and Felisa da Verona. On Narzotto's death in 1264 he inherited the southern triarchy based at Karystos while still a child, ruling under his mother's regency.

In 1268 he joined the peace between Venice and Byzantium, and in 1270 he allied with Guglielmo II against Byzantium. In 1278, the year of his death, Byzantine troops under Licario overran most of Euboea. His son Grapozzo later held the northern triarchy of Oreos.

en:
Narzotto dalle Carceri was a Lombard nobleman who ruled the southern triarchy of the Frankish island of Negroponte from 1247 until his death in 1264, holding the barony of Karystos. He married Felisa da Verona, daughter of William I of Verona, triarch of the central third.

In 1256, during the War of the Euboeote Succession, Narzotto and Guglielmo of Verona renounced their allegiance to William II of Villehardouin and placed themselves under Venice; William had the two triarchs arrested and seized Chalkis. After the defeat of their ally Guy I de la Roche of Athens at Karydi in 1258 and the peace of 1262, Narzotto was restored to his triarchy.

He died in 1264 leaving a young son, Marino II, under Felisa's regency. After his death Felisa was secretly married to Licario, but her family had the match annulled; Licario fled to Byzantine service and captured Karystos in 1276.

纳尔佐托·达莱·卡尔切里是伦巴第贵族，自1247年起统治法兰克人治下内格罗蓬特岛的南部三主辖区，领有卡里斯托男爵领，直至1264年去世。他娶中部三主古列尔莫一世·达·维罗纳之女费利萨·达·维罗纳为妻。

1256年埃维亚继承战争期间，纳尔佐托与古列尔莫·达·维罗纳不再臣服于威廉二世·德·维尔阿杜安，转而归附威尼斯；威廉下令将两名三主逮捕并攻占哈尔基斯。1258年盟友雅典的居伊一世·德·拉罗什在卡里迪战败，1262年议和后纳尔佐托复位。

他于1264年去世，幼子马里诺二世由费利萨摄政。他死后，费利萨曾与利卡里奥秘密成婚，但被家族废除；利卡里奥出逃投奔拜占庭，1276年攻陷卡里斯托。

en:
Peter dalle Carceri (died 1340) gathered most of Negroponte into one hand. Since the Fourth Crusade the island had been split into three thirds run by interrelated Lombard families under growing Venetian influence. Peter succeeded his father Grapozzo to a share of Oreos and inherited half of Chalkis from his mother Beatrice of Verona.

In 1328 he added the other half of Chalkis and succeeded Maria dalle Carceri to a share of Karystos, giving him two thirds of the island. By 1324 he also held half the Barony of Arcadia in Achaea, usually thought to have come through his second marriage to Balzana Gozzadini.

When Peter died in 1340, Chalkis passed to Giovanni, his only son by that marriage; the last triarchs would later leave the island to Venice.

彼得·达莱·卡尔切里（？—1340）把内格罗蓬特的大半收归一手。第四次十字军东征以来，埃维亚岛被分成三个三主辖区，由彼此联姻的伦巴第家族掌管，受威尼斯影响日增。彼得继承父亲格拉波佐在奥雷奥斯的份额，又从母亲贝亚特丽切·达·维罗纳处继承半个哈尔基斯。

1328年，他取得另外半个哈尔基斯，并继受玛丽亚·达莱·卡尔切里在卡里斯托的份额，据有全岛的三分之二。至1324年，他还持有亚该亚亲王国阿卡迪亚男爵领的一半，通常认为来自他与巴尔扎娜·戈扎迪尼的第二次婚姻。

彼得于1340年去世，哈尔基斯传给这次婚姻所生的独子乔瓦尼；末代三主后来把全岛留给了威尼斯。

Ravano dalle Carceri (died 1216) was a Veronese nobleman who joined the Fourth Crusade and helped conquer Euboea from the Byzantines in 1205. King Boniface of Thessalonica divided the island into three triarchies and probably granted him the central third.

In 1209, after the other triarchs died or left, Ravano seized the whole island, briefly defied the Latin Emperor Henry, then foiled a plot against the emperor's life and kept Negroponte until his death. In 1217 the Venetian bailiff split Euboea into sixths, his daughter Bertha sharing Chalkis with his widow.

拉瓦诺·达莱·卡尔切里（？—1216）是维罗纳贵族，参加第四次十字军，于1205年参与从拜占庭手中夺取埃维亚岛。萨洛尼卡国王博尼法乔将该岛分为三个三主领地，可能把中部三分之一封给了他。

1209年，在其他三主或死或离去后，拉万夺取全岛，一度抗拒拉丁皇帝亨利，随后又挫败了一起谋害皇帝的阴谋，至死保有内格罗蓬特。1217年，威尼斯派驻的政务官将埃维亚岛分为六份，其女贝尔塔与遗孀平分哈尔基斯。

en:
Rizzardo dalle Carceri (died 1220) was a Lombard hexarch of Negroponte. A son of Redondello dalle Carceri and nephew of Ravano, he received a share of the northern triarchy of Oreos in the Venetian bailo's partition, ruling it alongside his brother Marino I.

He died in 1220, and his daughter Carintana inherited his sixth. When she died childless in 1255, the dispute over her inheritance grew into the War of the Euboeote Succession.

en:
Simona of Aragon was a daughter of the Catalan vicar-general of Athens, Alfonso Fadrique, and Marulla da Verona. In 1326–1327 she was married to George II Ghisi, lord of Tinos and Mykonos, to seal peace between the Catalans and the Ghisi; her dowry was half the castellany of Saint Omer in Thebes.

After George II's death she became regent for their minor son Bartholomew III, governing Tinos, Mykonos and the Negroponte triarchy until he came of age in 1358.

阿拉贡的西莫娜是雅典加泰罗尼亚副王阿方索·法德里克与马鲁拉·达·维罗纳之女。1326至1327年，她嫁给蒂诺斯与米科诺斯领主乔治二世·吉西，以巩固加泰罗尼亚人与吉西家族之间的和约；她的嫁妆是底比斯圣奥梅尔城堡领地的一半。

en:
Amadeus of Neuchâtel (died 3 February 1288), son of Rudolph III and Sibylle de Montfaucon, was co-lord of Neuchâtel with his brothers Ulrich IV and Henry from their father's death in 1263. In 1270 his grandfather Theodoric III of Montbéliard arbitrated the succession: Amadeus, the elder brother, received Henry's liege homage for his share.

Later that year he married Jordane of La Sarraz. He ruled alone from Henry's death in 1283, and his son Rudolph IV, born in 1274, succeeded him.

en:
Berthold I of Neuchâtel (c. 1183–1259) was the son of Rodolphe II. In 1214, under his uncle Ulrich III's guardianship, a charter let burghers appeal to Lausanne's bishop against him.

After partitioning with Ulrich in 1218, Berthold took the title of lord and his uncle that of count; after Ulrich's death in 1225 he styled himself count. After Basel's bishop burned Neuchâtel in 1249, Berthold founded Nugerol in 1253 and set up a Three Estates court and town council. His son by Richenza of Frobourg was Rodolphe III.

en:
Louis I (1305–1373) ruled as count of Neuchâtel from 1325, the son of Count Rudolph IV and Eleanor of Savoy-Vaud. In 1343 he swore fealty to the Holy Roman Empire and granted liberties to the men of Boudry. Emperor Charles IV gave him in 1347 the right to mint coin and levy tolls.

He campaigned with Albert II of Austria against Zurich in 1351. His three sons predeceased him, so his daughters Isabella and Varenne inherited the county in 1373.

Rudolph III of Neuchâtel (died 1263), son of Count Berthold I and Richenza of Frobourg, was created the first count of Thielle. After fire destroyed the old castle in 1249, he built a new one in 1250.

From 1259 he ruled Neuchâtel until 1263, exceptionally styling himself count. In 1260 he granted Nugerol's suburbs franchises. He married Sibylle, daughter of Theodoric III of Montbéliard; their son Amadeus succeeded him.

Rudolph IV (1274–1343), called Rollin, succeeded his father Amadeus as lord of Neuchâtel in 1288; he lost imperial immediacy and received his lands as a fief from John I of Chalon-Arlay. He allied with Bern in 1308 and founded Le Landeron facing the Bishopric of Basel, and died in 1343, leaving the county to his son Louis I.

en:
Hervé IV of Donzy (1173–1222) was a powerful baron of the Nivernais. In 1199, in a feud over the castle of Gien, he defeated and captured his suzerain Peter II of Courtenay; a settlement followed, and in 1200 his marriage to Peter's daughter Mahaut de Courtenay made him Count of Nevers.

In 1204–1205 he supported the French against the English. He joined the Albigensian Crusade in 1209 and fought for King John of England at Bouvines in 1214, later winning Philip Augustus's pardon.

After Peter of Courtenay died in 1219 he also held Auxerre and Tonnerre. He died at Saint-Aignan in 1222, reputedly poisoned.

Louis I of Nevers (1272–22 July 1322), son of Robert III of Flanders and Yolande of Burgundy, succeeded his mother as count of Nevers in 1280. In 1290 he married Joan, countess of Rethel, and ruled Rethel jure uxoris until his death.

Their children were Joan, later wife of John of Brittany, and Louis de Crécy, born in 1304, later count of Flanders, Nevers and Rethel. Louis died in Paris two months before his father, so he never ruled Flanders.

en:
Matilda I of Nevers (1188–1257) was ruling countess of Nevers, Auxerre and Tonnerre. Only daughter of Peter II of Courtenay and Agnes I of Nevers, she married Hervé IV of Donzy in 1199, after he captured her father in war; the peace ceded him Nevers.

After her father's death, Matilda inherited Auxerre and Tonnerre; Hervé returned from the Fifth Crusade to take control of the counties. Widowed in 1222, she married Guigues IV of Forez in 1226.

In 1223 she granted Auxerre a charter of liberties, and in 1235 founded a Cistercian nunnery. She died at Coulanges-sur-Yonne, succeeded by her great-granddaughter Matilda II.

玛蒂尔达一世（1188—1257）是讷韦尔、欧塞尔和托内尔三个伯国的实际统治者，为库尔特奈的皮埃尔二世与讷韦尔的阿格尼丝一世的独女。1199年，她嫁给栋济的埃尔韦四世：此前埃尔韦在交战中俘获了她的父亲，议和条件是把讷韦尔伯国割让给他并成婚。

父亲去世后，玛蒂尔达继承欧塞尔和托内尔；埃尔韦从第五次十字军东征返回，接管这两个伯国。1222年她守寡，1226年改嫁福雷的吉格四世。

1223年，她向欧塞尔颁发自由特许状，1235年又创办一座西多会修女院。她在约讷河畔库朗日去世，由曾孙女玛蒂尔达二世继位。

Yolande of Burgundy (1247–2 June 1280), daughter of Odo of Burgundy and Countess Matilda II of Nevers, inherited Nevers, Tonnerre and Auxerre in 1262; a 1273 Parlement ruling left her Nevers. Her first husband, John Tristan, son of Louis IX, died at Tunis on the Eighth Crusade in 1270.

In 1272 she married Robert III of Flanders, and that year they claimed the Duchy of Burgundy, but Philip III awarded it to her uncle Robert II. Her son Louis was born the same year.

en:
Nicolas Fouquet (1615–1680) was a French financier born in Paris into a noblesse de robe family. Loyal to Cardinal Mazarin through the Fronde, he was made Superintendent of Finances in 1653 and amassed a vast fortune, buying Belle-Île and building the chateau of Vaux-le-Vicomte.

On 17 August 1661 he entertained Louis XIV there with a sumptuous fete, but the jealous king, urged on by Colbert, had him arrested by d'Artagnan at Nantes on 5 September 1661 on charges of embezzlement. After a three-year trial he was imprisoned for life and died in the fortress of Pignerol on 23 March 1680.

尼古拉·富凯（1615—1680）是法国财政官员，生于巴黎的一个穿袍贵族家庭。投石党运动期间他忠于枢机马萨林，1653年被任命为财政总监，积聚了巨额财富，买下贝勒岛并修建了沃勒维孔特城堡。

1661年8月17日，他在那里以奢华的盛宴款待路易十四，但心生猜忌的国王在柯尔贝尔怂恿下，于9月5日命达达尼昂在南特将他逮捕，罪名是侵吞公款。经过三年审讯，他被判处终身监禁，1680年3月23日死于皮内罗洛要塞。

en:
Engelbert I (died 1329), of the Ziegenhain comital house, ruled the County of Nidda from 1294, styling himself count of Ziegenhain. In 1294 he sold Neustadt castle and town to Archbishop Gerhard of Mainz. His feud with the Hospitallers ended only in 1315.

He married Heilwig of Isenburg-Büdingen in 1286, and their only child was Lukardis. In 1300 King Albert I allowed his fiefs to pass to her should he have no sons, and Engelbert died without male heir in 1329.

en:
Louis II (died after 1289) was Count of Nidda, succeeding his father Gottfried IV. In 1258 a partition mediated by the archbishop of Mainz separated Nidda from the County of Ziegenhain, leaving Louis with Nidda and Neustadt.

Drawn into the Thuringian-Hessian war of succession, he backed Mainz against the landgraves of Hesse: around 1270 he built Neustadt Castle, but Hessian troops took it in 1273. In 1279 he pledged the Fulda Vogtei. His son Engelbert I succeeded him.

en:
Lukardis (died 1333) was the only child and heiress of Count Engelbert I of Nidda. In 1311 she married Count John I of Ziegenhain, and on their wedding day the couple confirmed the town of Nidda's rights and freedoms.

In 1323 Emperor Louis IV enfeoffed John with Nidda castle and town as an imperial fief. After her father died in 1329, Lukardis nominally ruled the County of Nidda until her death in 1333, after which John united Nidda with Ziegenhain.

卢卡迪斯（卒于1333年）是尼达伯爵恩格尔贝特一世唯一的女儿和继承人。1311年，她嫁给齐根海因伯爵约翰一世；婚礼当天，夫妇二人确认了尼达城的权利与自由。

1323年，皇帝路德维希四世将尼达城堡与城镇作为帝国封地授予约翰。1329年父亲去世后，卢卡迪斯名义上统治尼达伯国，直至1333年离世，此后约翰将尼达与齐根海因合为一体。

en:
John II of Hoya (1319–1377) became ruling count in 1324 after his father Otto II's death, governing jointly with his brother Gerhard III. A former church canon, he married Helen of Saxony-Lauenburg in 1338. In 1345 the brothers divided their lands, John taking the Upper County and Gerhard the Lower County.

His rule saw the Hoya Feud against the city of Bremen, and late in life he joined Magnus II of Brunswick-Lüneburg in the Lüneburg War of Succession.

约翰二世（霍亚，1319—1377）在1324年父亲奥托二世去世后继任伯爵，与兄弟格哈德三世共同统治。他本是教会法政牧师，1338年娶萨克森-劳恩堡的海伦。1345年兄弟瓜分领地，约翰得到上伯国，格哈德得到下伯国。

他在位期间经历了与不来梅城为敌的霍亚之争，晚年又加入不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公爵马格努斯二世一方，卷入吕讷堡继承战争。

en:
Nimi a Nzima is named in Kongo oral tradition as the last ruler of Mpemba Kasi, a Bantu kingdom in the Vungu lands that was vast but not strong, remembered as the Mother of Kongo.

He married Lukeni lua Nsanze, daughter of Nsaku Lau, chief of the northern kingdom of Mbata, and the match bound the two states together. Around 1375 Mpemba Kasi and Mbata merged to form the Kingdom of Kongo.

Their son Lukeni lua Nimi is traditionally said to have conquered the country around Mbanza Kongo and become its first king. These traditions were written down in the seventeenth century.

尼米·阿·恩齐马在刚果口传传统中是姆彭巴·卡西的末代统治者。这个班图王国位于温古之地，疆域辽阔却不强盛，传统称之为“刚果之母”。

他娶北邻姆巴塔之主恩萨库·劳的女儿卢凯尼·卢安桑泽为妻，这场联姻把两国连在一起。约1375年，姆彭巴·卡西与姆巴塔合并，形成刚果王国。

他们的儿子卢凯尼·卢阿·尼米传统上被认为征服了姆班扎刚果一带，成为第一位国王。这些传统于17世纪被记录成文。

en:
Withego I von Ostrau (died 27 October 1348) was bishop of Naumburg from 1335. A son of Henning von Ostrau, he held church offices at Merseburg, Zeitz and Sulza, and the Naumburg chapter made him accept its first episcopal election capitulation.

He repaired relations with Margrave Frederick II of Meissen and stayed neutral in the Thuringian Count War. In 1347 he ended a feud against Poppo von Würzburg and his sons, and he probably died at Zeitz the next year.

en:
Bolesław the Elder (c. 1293 – c. 1365) was a Silesian Piast duke, eldest son of Bolko I of Opole. After his father's death in 1313 he ruled Wieluń and Niemodlin. Tied to the Luxembourg kings of Bohemia, war with Władysław I cost him Wieluń in 1326, and in 1327 he did homage to King John.

He joined John's 1328 crusade against Lithuania and in 1355 accompanied Charles IV to his imperial coronation in Rome. In 1325 he married Euphemia of Wrocław, by whom he had eight children.

波列斯瓦夫“长者”（约1293—约1365）是西里西亚皮亚斯特家族公爵，奥波莱公爵波尔科一世的长子。1313年父亲死后，他统治维隆与涅莫德林。他依附波希米亚的卢森堡诸王：与瓦迪斯瓦夫一世的战争使他于1326年失去维隆，1327年他向国王约翰行臣服礼。

en:
Euphemia of Wrocław (born c. 1312, died after 1384), also called Ofka, was the second daughter of Henry VI the Good, duke of Wrocław, and Anna of Austria. In 1324 or 1325 she married Bolesław the Elder, duke of Niemodlin; as the pair were distant cousins, the marriage required a papal dispensation.

Arranged by her father to build an alternative Piast succession line, the marriage gave her three sons and five daughters. In October 1383 Władysław Opolczyk confirmed her dower rights, and she died soon after.

en:
Nogai (died 1299 or 1300) was a Mongol general and kingmaker of the Golden Horde, a great-grandson of Jochi. He first appears as a young commander raiding Poland. After Berke died in 1266 he never claimed the khanate, but ruled the lands west of the Dnieper almost as an independent lord; after his raids on Bulgaria and Byzantium, Emperor Michael VIII gave him his daughter as a wife.

In 1280 Bulgarian rebel Ivaylo sought his help, and Nogai had him killed at a feast; he then made George Terter and later Smilets vassal tsars. In 1290 he lured the khan Talabuga to a meeting, had him ambushed and strangled, and put the young Tokhta on the throne.

In 1299 or 1300 Tokhta's larger army beat him at Kahamlyk. Wounded by a Russian soldier, he asked to be taken to Tokhta and was killed, and his sons were hunted down.

那海（？—1299/1300）是金帐汗国的蒙古将领和立汗者，术赤的曾孙。他最早作为年轻将领远征波兰。1266年别儿哥去世后，他从未谋求汗位，却以近乎独立领主的身份统治第聂伯河以西的土地；他劫掠保加利亚和拜占庭之后，拜占庭皇帝米哈伊尔八世把女儿许配给他。

1280年保加利亚起义者伊瓦伊洛前来求助，那海在宴席上将他处死，随后先后扶立乔治·泰尔特和斯米莱茨为附庸沙皇。1290年他诱使兀剌不花汗赴会，设伏将其勒死，扶立年轻的脱脱登上汗位。

1299/1300年，脱脱的大军在卡哈姆利克击败那海。那海被一名俄罗斯士兵刺伤，要求见脱脱，随即被杀，他的儿子们也被追捕处死。

en:
Agnes Haakonsdatter (1290–1319) was the elder daughter of King Haakon V of Norway, born before her parents' marriage. As she was illegitimate, the succession was settled in favour of her younger sister Ingeborg, with Agnes's descendants retaining a contingent claim.

In 1302 she married Baron Havtore Jonsson, governor of Romerike, whose estates included Borregård. Her sons Jon and Sigurd Havtoresson held leading roles in the Norwegian council under her nephew, King Magnus VII Eriksson.

阿涅丝·哈康斯多塔（1290—1319）是挪威国王哈康五世的长女，因出生时父母尚未正式成婚而被视为非婚生女儿，王位继承因此改由妹妹英格堡优先，她的后裔仅保留英格堡一系绝嗣后的候补继承权。

en:
Haakon V Magnusson (1270–1319) was the younger son of King Magnus the Lawmender and ruled Norway from the death of his brother Eric II in 1299. As Duke of Norway he had governed lands around Oslo and Stavanger from 1280.

He curbed his nobles, renewed the war against Denmark and made peace in 1309, while Oslo displaced Bergen as the kingdom's main seat; he built the Akershus and Bohus fortresses.

The last male king of the House of Sverre, he had no legitimate son. He married his daughter Ingeborg to the Swedish duke Erik Magnusson in 1312, and in 1319 was succeeded by their infant son Magnus Eriksson.

哈康五世·马格努松（1270—1319）是“修法王”马格努斯国王的幼子，1299年兄长埃里克二世去世后继任挪威国王。自1280年起，他作为挪威公爵统领奥斯陆和斯塔万格周边的土地。

他遏制贵族势力，重启对丹麦的战争并于1309年媾和；他在位时奥斯陆取代卑尔根成为王国主要的统治中心，阿克斯胡斯与布胡斯两座要塞也由他主持修建。

他是斯韦勒家族最后一位男系国王，没有合法的儿子。1312年他将女儿英格堡嫁给瑞典公爵埃里克·马格努松，1319年去世后由他们年幼的儿子马格努斯·埃里克松继位。

Havtore Jonsson (c. 1275–1320) was a Norwegian baron of the Sudrheim family on Romerike. In 1302 he was betrothed to Agnes Håkonsdatter, the illegitimate daughter of King Håkon V, whom he later married. A landowner with estates including Borregård, he served as sysselmann of Romerike.

In 1319, he joined other nobles at the dying Håkon's bedside in swearing to uphold the king's provisions for succession and government. His sons Jon and Sigurd later served Magnus Eriksson.

Ingeborg of Norway (1301–1361) was the only legitimate daughter of King Håkon V. In 1312 she married the Swedish duke Erik Magnusson. After Erik died in prison in 1318 and Håkon V in 1319, her young son Magnus inherited Norway and was elected king of Sweden, and Ingeborg participated in the regency governments, becoming Sweden's first female regent.

Her tie to Canute Porse and her independent rule led the nobility to remove her in 1326–1327. She later married Porse, duke of Halland, and died in 1361.

Jon Havtoresson (c. 1312–1395) belonged, with his brother Sigurd, to one of the most powerful families in Norway. His mother Agnes was an illegitimate daughter of King Haakon V Magnusson; his father, the knight Havtore Jonsson, came from the Sudrheim family. As probably the eldest son, Jon inherited the manor of Skea, with estates in Solør and Odalen, and held further lands in Østfold.

He governed Borgarsysla and advised both Magnus Eriksson and Haakon VI. His marriage to Birgitta Knutsdatter produced sons Ulv, Håkon and Brynjolv, all three members of the Council of the Realm; his daughter Cecilia married the Swedish knight Ulv Holmgeirsson.

Sigurd Havtoresson (c. 1315–c. 1390) was a grandson of King Haakon V Magnusson through his mother Agnes, his illegitimate daughter, and with his brother Jon belonged to the most powerful families in Norway. His father, the knight Havtore Jonsson, was of the Sudrheim family, and Sigurd held the family seat at Sudreim.

He held senior offices and a seat on the Council of the Realm, and became the largest private landowner in late medieval Norway. His daughter Agnes Sigurdsdatter was the mother of Sigurd Jonsson, who later became regent of Norway.

en:
Peter Wessel Tordenskiold (1690–1720) was a Norwegian naval officer in the Royal Dano-Norwegian fleet, born in Trondheim. He ran away to Copenhagen in 1704 and became a naval second lieutenant in 1711. During the Great Northern War he won fame attacking Swedish ships against the odds, and in 1712 helped destroy Swedish transports near Rügen. In 1716 Frederick IV ennobled him as Tordenskiold, meaning Thunder Shield, and at Dynekilen he destroyed nearly the entire Swedish transport fleet, forcing Charles XII's army out of Norway.

Promoted vice-admiral, he then took Marstrand and Carlsten fortress. He was killed in a duel near Hanover in November 1720.

Konstantin Vsevolodovich (1185–1218), surnamed the Wise, was the eldest son of Vsevolod the Big Nest of Vladimir. He ruled Novgorod from 1205 and received Rostov and Yaroslavl in 1208.

When Vsevolod left Vladimir to his son Yuri, Konstantin resisted, and at Lipitsa in 1216 he and Mstislav the Bold defeated Yuri, making Konstantin grand prince of Vladimir. He founded the Assumption Cathedral in Rostov and amassed a great library. He died in 1218, leaving Rostov to his son Vasilko; Yuri regained Vladimir.

Mstislav Izyaslavich (died 1069) was the eldest son of Grand Prince Iziaslav of Kiev. Iziaslav installed him in Novgorod, where he ruled around 1067.

In 1069 he returned to Rus from Poland with his exiled father and was sent to crush the Kiev uprising against Iziaslav, putting it down through mass executions and blindings. Later that year he defeated Prince Vseslav Briachislavich and took Polotsk, but died soon afterwards.

姆斯季斯拉夫·伊贾斯拉维奇（？—1069）是基辅大公伊贾斯拉夫一世的长子。伊贾斯拉夫将他安置到诺夫哥罗德，他约于1067年统治该城。

1069年他随遭放逐的父亲从波兰返回罗斯，随即受命镇压基辅人反抗大公的起义，以处死、剜目的暴烈手段平息叛乱。同年他击败波洛茨克王公弗谢斯拉夫·布里亚奇斯拉维奇，取得波洛茨克公位，不久后便去世。

en:
Sviatoslav III Vsevolodovich (1196–1252), a son of Vsevolod the Big Nest, was twice prince of Novgorod between 1200 and 1210. At the partition he received Yuriev-Polsky, where he built the Cathedral of St George in 1230–1234, and in 1220 he sacked Aşlı.

He fought the Mongols at the Battle of the Sit in 1238 and became grand prince of Vladimir with the Golden Horde's patent in 1246, only to be ousted by his nephew Mikhail Khorobrit in 1248. He died at Yuriev-Polsky in 1252.

斯维亚托斯拉夫三世·弗谢沃洛多维奇（1196—1252）是弗谢沃洛德三世（“大窝”）之子，曾在1200年至1210年间两度担任诺夫哥罗德王公。分封时他得到尤里耶夫-波利斯基，并于1230—1234年在当地修建圣格奥尔吉教堂；1220年他攻掠阿什雷。

1238年，他参加西蒂河战役，抗击拔都率领的蒙古大军。1246年，他凭金帐汗国的封诰成为弗拉基米尔大公，却于1248年被侄子米哈伊尔·霍罗布里特逐出弗拉基米尔。1252年他在尤里耶夫-波利斯基去世。

en:
Vladimir Yaroslavich (1020–1052) was prince of Novgorod from 1036 until his death. The eldest son of Yaroslav the Wise of Kiev by Ingegerd of Sweden, in 1043 he led the last Rus' expedition against Byzantium, where a storm wrecked much of his fleet, yet he defeated its pursuers.

He founded Novgorod's Cathedral of St Sophia in 1045 and was buried there when he died in 1052, two years before his father. Venerated as Saint Vladimir, he left a son Rostislav, whose line ruled Halych until 1199.

弗拉基米尔·雅罗斯拉维奇（1020—1052）于1036年起任诺夫哥罗德王公，直至去世。他是基辅大公智者雅罗斯拉夫与瑞典的因吉戈尔德的长子，1043年率领罗斯人最后一次远征拜占庭：船队遭遇风暴损失惨重，但他仍击败了前来追击的拜占庭战船。

1045年他在诺夫哥罗德修建圣索菲亚主教座堂，1052年先于父亲两年去世，葬于该堂。东正教会尊他为圣人。其子罗斯季斯拉夫的后裔后来统治哈利奇，直至1199年。

Vysheslav Vladimirovich (born c. 977) was the eldest son of Vladimir the Great of Kyiv, born to his first wife, the Varangian Olava. From about 988 he ruled as prince of Novgorod, the seat of the senior son.

One account places his death in Novgorod after 1010; the throne passed to his younger brother Yaroslav the Wise. A conflicting theory identifies him with the Rus prince Vissavald, whom the Norse sagas say Sigrid of Sweden burned around 995.

维谢斯拉夫·弗拉基米罗维奇（约977年生）是基辅的弗拉基米尔大帝与第一任妻子、瓦良格人奥拉娃所生的长子。约988年起他出镇诺夫哥罗德，那是长子的席位。

en:
Kongo oral tradition remembers Mpuku a Nsuku as the ruler of the small kingdom of Mbata around 1350 to 1375; his clan, the Nsaku Lau, provided Mbata's ruling line.

As Nimi a Nzima of Mpemba Kasi built up his power, Mpuku a Nsuku made a founding alliance with him in which the two rulers guaranteed each other's line of succession.

The pact was sealed by the marriage of Mpuku's sister Lukeni lua Nsanze to Nimi a Nzima, and their son Lukeni lua Nimi founded the Kingdom of Kongo around 1390. The descendants of the Nsaku Lau continued to rule Mbata under Kongo's protection.

en:
Aimery III (died 1239), son of the Castilian noble Pedro Manrique de Lara, held the viscounty of Narbonne from 1194, after his father seized it in 1192.

His reign was dominated by the Albigensian Crusade: he reluctantly served Simon de Montfort at Béziers in 1209 and Minerve in 1210, but after Muret in 1213 he refused Montfort entry to Narbonne. In 1223 he did homage to Raymond VII of Toulouse, and at his death in 1239 the viscounty passed to his son Amalric I.

艾默里三世（？—1239）是卡斯蒂利亚贵族佩德罗·曼里克·德·拉腊之子。其父于1192年夺取纳博讷后，他自1194年起担任纳博讷子爵。

任内正值阿尔比十字军肆虐：他不情愿地追随西蒙·德·蒙福尔，于1209年出现在贝济耶、1210年参加米内尔瓦围城战；但1213年米雷战役之后，他拒绝蒙福尔进入纳博讷。1223年他向图卢兹伯爵雷蒙七世行臣服礼，1239年去世时子爵之位传给儿子阿马尔里克一世。

en:
Aimery IV of Narbonne (c. 1245–1298) was viscount of Narbonne from 1270 and an Italian condottiero. Serving Charles I of Anjou, he commanded the Guelph army against the Ghibellines, and in 1289 won the Battle of Campaldino and overran the Aretine countryside to Arezzo's gates, and was feted in Florence.

The last great Occitan troubadour, Guiraut Riquier, served at his court. He married Sibylle, daughter of Count Roger IV of Foix, and died in 1298, leaving Narbonne to his son Amalric II.

en:
Aimery VI de Narbonne (c. 1328–1388) became viscount in 1341 under his mother's tutelage after his half-brother Amalric III died. The English captured him at Auberoche in 1345 and again, wounded, at Poitiers in 1356; in November 1355 he defended Narbonne against the Black Prince.

He was admiral of France from 1369 to 1373, and from 1381 he waged the brutal war of the viscount against Narbonne itself. He died in 1388, succeeded by his son William I.

en:
Amalric II (c. 1260–1328), eldest son of Aimery IV of Narbonne and Sibylle de Foix, was a French soldier. Captured at Perpignan on Philip III's Aragonese Crusade in 1285, he then served Charles II of Naples in Tuscany. Italian sources make him commander of the Florentine Guelph army at the Battle of Campaldino in 1289; he also stormed Rondine outside Arezzo.

He succeeded his father as viscount in 1298 and joined Philip IV's Flemish campaign in 1300. He died in 1328, succeeded by his son Aimery V.

en:
Amalric III de Narbonne was viscount of Narbonne from 1336 until his death at Montpellier on 8 February 1341. The eldest son of Aymeri V de Narbonne by his first wife Catherine de Poitiers, he succeeded his father in 1336.

Almost nothing is recorded of his five-year rule. He died without issue, so the viscounty passed to his half-brother Aimery VI, son of Tiburge de Son.

George Koriatovich (died 1375 or 1377) was the eldest son of the Lithuanian prince Karijotas. After the Battle of Blue Waters, he and his brothers received Podolia around 1363. He cooperated with Casimir III of Poland against his Lithuanian kinsmen in the Galicia–Volhynia struggles.

After being expelled around 1362 he fled to the Polish court. In 1374 he was elected voivode of Moldavia, where his Vlach subjects murdered him in 1375 or 1377.

en:
Alberic III of Dammartin (c. 1135–1200) is first recorded as count of Dammartin in a charter of 1162, confirming the possessions of Chaalis Abbey. In 1165 he married Mahaut, heiress of Clermont.

Serving Philip Augustus, he led a mission to the English king in 1180 and fought Philip of Flanders, who captured him at Dammartin in 1182.

Around 1187 he transferred to Henry II of England, receiving the Norman fief of Lillebonne. He later supported John Lackland against Philip Augustus, died at Lillebonne in 1200, and was buried at Jumièges Abbey. His sons Renaud and Simon both became counts.

en:
Anna of Nuremberg (died 1355) was the daughter of Burgrave Frederick III of Nuremberg of the Hohenzollern family and Helena of Saxony. In 1295 or 1296 she married Count Emich I of Nassau-Hadamar and bore him eight children, including his successor John and Emich II.

Widowed in 1334, she secured the imperial castle of Kammerstein as her dower in 1336, remained at Hadamar until 1349, then retired to Kammerstein, where she died in 1355. She supported Nuremberg's Poor Clares and Franciscans, helped found Bärbach Abbey, and was buried in the city's Franciscan Barfüsserkirche.

en:
Emich II of Nassau-Hadamar (died 1 March 1359) was the second son of Count Emich I and Anna of Nuremberg. He entered the Church and is attested as a canon of Mainz, but soon left the clergy and from 1337 shared rule with his brother John. He fought beside John in the Nassau-Dillenburg feud of 1350 and 1351.

He repeatedly seized revenues from monasteries and churches, but in his will ordered full restitution. He died unmarried in 1359, and John then ruled alone.

en:
Henry II the Rich (c. 1180–1250), Count of Nassau, was the eldest son of Walram I and ruled from 1198. He enlarged his domains around Wiesbaden through the imperial stewardship granted around 1214 and built several castles, including Dillenburg.

He married Matilda of Guelders in 1215 and joined Frederick II on the Sixth Crusade in 1228. His sons Walram II and Otto I divided Nassau in 1255, founding the dynasty's two lines.

en:
Margaret of Nuremberg (born c. 1316, died after 1382) was a daughter of Burgrave Frederick IV of Nuremberg and Margaret of Görz-Tyrol, and through marriage the progenitrix of the Nassau-Wiesbaden-Idstein line. In 1332 she married Count Adolf I of Nassau-Wiesbaden-Idstein, with whom she resided chiefly at Idstein.

In their joint testament of 1360 the couple endowed Klarenthal Abbey near Wiesbaden, Margaret leaving her gowns and mantle; Adolf died in 1370 and was buried there. Her own will, dated 13 November 1382, is the last record of her, and she was later buried at Klarenthal.

Of her many children, Gerlach II and Walram IV ruled Nassau-Wiesbaden-Idstein, while Adolf and John II became archbishop-electors of Mainz. Two daughters served as abbesses of Klarenthal.

纽伦堡的玛格丽特（约1316—1382年后）是纽伦堡城伯腓特烈四世与戈里齐亚-蒂罗尔的玛格丽特之女，因婚姻成为拿骚-威斯巴登-伊德施泰因支系的始祖母。1332年她嫁给拿骚-威斯巴登-伊德施泰因伯爵阿道夫一世，夫妇主要居于伊德施泰因。

1360年，二人在共同遗嘱中向威斯巴登附近的克拉伦塔尔修道院捐赠财物，玛格丽特留下自己的裙袍与披风；阿道夫于1370年去世，葬于该院。她本人的遗嘱订于1382年11月13日，是关于她最后的记载，身后亦葬于克拉伦塔尔。

她的众多子女中，格拉赫二世与瓦拉姆四世统治拿骚-威斯巴登-伊德施泰因，阿道夫与约翰二世则成为美因茨大主教兼选侯，还有两个女儿出任克拉伦塔尔修道院院长。

en:
Otto I (1224–1290), Count of Nassau, was a son of Henry II the Rich. With his brother Walram II he succeeded their father before 1251, and in 1255 they signed the Prima Divisio, partitioning Nassau along the Lahn; Otto took the north around Siegen.

His feuds with Rhenish lords and a quarrel over Teutonic Order estates brought him excommunication in 1285, settled the following year. By Agnes of Leiningen he left sons Henry, Emicho and John.

en:
Nsaku Lau was the ruler of the Bantu kingdom of Mbata in the later fourteenth century. Tradition holds that around 1375 he allied with Nimi a Nzima, ruler of Mpemba Kasi, and sealed the pact by marrying his daughter Lukeni lua Nsanze to him. Their son Lukeni lua Nimi led the expansion from which the Kingdom of Kongo took shape, and later Kilukeni rulers descended from him.

As Kongo centralized, Mbata lost influence; by 1620 it kept only the symbolic title Nkaka andi a Mwene Kongo, grandfather of the king of Kongo.

恩萨库·劳是14世纪后期班图人姆巴塔王国的统治者。传说约1375年他与姆彭巴·卡西的统治者尼米·阿·恩齐马结盟，并将女儿卢凯尼·卢安桑泽嫁给对方以巩固盟约。两人的儿子卢凯尼·卢阿·尼米领导了扩张，刚果王国由此成形，此后的基卢凯尼诸王都出自他的世系。

随着刚果集权加强，姆巴塔的影响力逐渐衰退；到1620年，它只保留了“刚果国王的外祖父”（恩卡卡·安迪·阿·姆韦内·刚果）这一象征性称号。

John (c. 1275–1328), third son of Count Otto I of Nassau, was destined for the Church and became a canon at Worms. After his mother's death in 1303 he left the clergy, receiving Nassau-Dillenburg in the brothers' partition.

He fought the long Dernbach feud against local lords and Hesse. In 1327 he captained the Mainz-Nassau army, winning at Seibertshausen, but fell against the Hessians near Wetzlar in 1328. Unmarried, his lands reverted to his brothers.

en:
John (died 1364 or 1365) was ruling count of Nassau-Hadamar from his father Emich I's death in 1334. He enlarged his lands by buying a share of Driedorf and taking the Amt Ellar in pledge in 1337. His later feuds drove him into debt: he backed Emperor Charles IV against Louis the Bavarian, and in 1351 was captured near Löhnberg and had to ransom himself.

He later sold his Frankish estates around Kammerstein to Burgrave Albert of Nuremberg. By Elisabeth of Waldeck he left his successor Henry.

en:
Adolph I (c. 1307–1370) was the eldest son of Count Gerlach I of Nassau and Agnes of Hesse. He and his brothers took full power when their father abdicated in 1344, ruling jointly until they partitioned the inheritance in 1355. Adolph thereby founded the Nassau-Wiesbaden-Idstein line and resided chiefly at Idstein, where he built the Hexenturm.

In imperial politics he supported Emperor Charles IV. In 1322 he married Margaret of Nuremberg, daughter of Burgrave Frederick IV.

en:
Gerlach I (c. 1285–1361), Count of Nassau and a younger son of King Adolf of Nassau, succeeded his elder brother Rupert in 1305 and ruled from Sonnenberg Castle near Wiesbaden. In 1309 he translated his father's body to Speyer Cathedral.

He escorted Henry VII to his imperial coronation in Rome in 1312 and only submitted to Louis the Bavarian after the battle of Mühldorf in 1322. Imperial Vogt of the Wetterau from 1326, he divided Nassau among his sons in 1344.

en:
Walram II (c. 1220–24 January 1276), Count of Nassau, was the second son of Henry II the Rich. He succeeded before 1251 with his brother Otto I, and the Prima Divisio of 1255 gave him the lands south of the Lahn: Wiesbaden, Idstein and Weilburg.

He served King Rudolf I as Hofmarschall and councillor, but lost Niederlahnstein and Vallendar to the Archbishop of Trier. In a fit of madness he burned his copy of the division treaty and allegedly died mentally deranged; his son Adolf became King of Germany.

Simeon (Semyon Alexandrovich) was prince of Novosil in the middle of the fourteenth century, reckoned by genealogies a son of Prince Alexander Semyonovich, who was killed in the Golden Horde in 1326. He ruled the small upper-Oka principality while its princes steered between Moscow, Lithuania and the Horde.

The testament of Grand Prince Simeon Ivanovich of Moscow, drawn up in 1353, records buying the village of Zabereg from him. His sons Ivan and Roman succeeded him as princes of Novosil.

en:
Henry I (c. 1270–1343), Count of Nassau-Siegen and eldest son of Count Otto I, succeeded his father in 1290. He backed his cousin Adolf of Nassau's election as German king in 1292, fighting for him in Thuringia and at Göllheim in 1298, where Adolf was killed. Adolf had pledged him the Ratzenscheid silver mines, the basis of the Nassau mining rights.

The 1303 partition of Nassau gave him Siegen, and in 1306 he gained Dillenburg. He died in 1343, succeeded by his son Otto II.

en:
Otto II (c. 1305–1350/51) succeeded his father Henry I as Count of Nassau-Siegen in 1343. The 1341 partition gave him the Siegerland and Dillenburg with the surrounding lands. His reign was spent in feuds and debt: he sold or pledged lands including Löhnberg, his half of Siegen and Haiger, and won Dillenburg its city rights from Emperor Louis the Bavarian.

He was killed in his feud with the Walderdorff brothers between late 1350 and early 1351. His son John I succeeded under the regency of his widow, Adelaide of Vianden.

en:
John I (1309–1371) was the second son of Count Gerlach I of Nassau. He took power with his elder brother Adolph in 1344, and in the 1355 partition received Weilburg on the Lahn, founding the Nassau-Weilburg line.

In 1356 he fought for France as a mercenary at Poitiers, where his half-brother Kraft was killed and John was captured but quickly released. Emperor Charles IV raised him to an Imperial Prince-Count in 1366. His marriages to Gertrude of Merenberg and Johanna of Saarbrücken brought him Merenberg, Gleiberg and the Saarbrücken inheritance. His son Philip I succeeded him in 1371.

约翰一世（1309—1371）是拿骚伯爵格拉赫一世的次子。1344年他与兄长阿道夫共同掌权，1355年分家时得到兰河畔的魏尔堡，开创拿骚-魏尔堡支系。

1356年他作为雇佣兵为法国一方参加普瓦捷战役，异母弟克拉夫特战死，他本人被俘但很快获释。1366年皇帝查理四世将他升为帝国诸侯级伯爵。他先后娶梅伦贝格的格特鲁德与萨尔布吕肯的约翰娜为妻，由此取得梅伦贝格、格莱贝格和萨尔布吕肯的继承权。1371年他在魏尔堡去世，子菲利普一世继位。

en:
Rappold von Külsheim, in contemporary charters Rapoto von Külsheim and called the Strong Knight, was a Franconian knight and vassal of the burgraves of Nuremberg; his family held the castle of Külsheim near Windsheim and estates around Fürth. He first appears in the burgraves' following in 1317 and numbered among the leading officials of their court from 1333, repeatedly named a judge of the imperial land court between 1337 and 1352, and recorded as Reichsschultheiß of Nuremberg in 1338.

In 1349 he held the castle of Atzenhof, and on his petition the church of St. Johannis at Burgfarrnbach was raised into an independent parish that same year.

He died at Fürth in 1355 or 1356 and was buried at Burgfarrnbach, where his grave slab shows the family stag. A later legend tells that he set up a roadside column after his daughter died in an accident.

拉波尔德·冯·屈尔斯海姆，在当时文书中作拉波托·冯·屈尔斯海姆，绰号“强壮的骑士”，是法兰克尼亚骑士、纽伦堡城伯的封臣；其家族据有温茨海姆附近的屈尔斯海姆城堡和菲尔特周边的地产。1317年他首次见于城伯的随从队伍，1333年起跻身城伯宫廷的首要官员，1337至1352年间多次出任帝国地方法院法官，纽伦堡法官名录则记他于1338年任城市帝国法官。

1349年他领有阿岑霍夫城堡；在他的请求下，布格法伦巴赫的圣约翰教堂于同年升为独立教区。

他于1355或1356年在菲尔特去世，葬于布格法伦巴赫，墓板上刻有家族的雄鹿。后世传说他在女儿意外身亡后竖立了一根路旁纪念柱。

en:
Euphrosyne Yaroslavna was a Galician princess, the daughter of Prince Yaroslav Osmomysl of Halych and Olga Yurievna of Suzdal. Her personal name is absent from the chronicles and the attribution remains uncertain. Around 1169 she married Prince Igor Svyatoslavich of Novgorod-Seversk and bore him six children.

She is famous as the Yaroslavna of The Lay of Igor's Campaign, about Igor's failed 1185 raid against the Polovtsians; her Yaroslavna's Lament, in which she pleads with the Dnieper for her husband's return, is one of the poem's most celebrated passages and made her the emblem of the faithful wife.

叶夫罗西尼娅·雅罗斯拉夫娜是哈利奇王公雅罗斯拉夫·奥斯莫梅斯尔与苏兹达尔的奥尔加·尤里耶夫娜之女。编年史没有记下她的名字，这一名字的归属仍有争议。约1169年，她嫁给诺夫哥罗德-谢韦尔斯基王公伊戈尔·斯维亚托斯拉维奇，为他生下六名子女。

en:
Nanker, born Jan Kołda around 1270 near Bytom, was a Polish cleric and supporter of King Władysław the Short. He was archdeacon of Sandomierz before studying canon law in Bologna, and later became dean of Kraków. Consecrated bishop of Kraków in 1320, he issued diocesan statutes and began the Gothic Wawel Cathedral.

Translated to Wrocław in 1326, he ruled the episcopal principality of Nysa and in 1337 excommunicated King John of Bohemia. He died at Nysa in 1341 and was buried in Wrocław Cathedral.

南克尔约1270年生于比托姆附近，本名扬·考达，是波兰教士，也是国王瓦迪斯瓦夫一世（矮子）的支持者。他先任桑多梅日总执事，后赴博洛尼亚研习教会法，再任克拉科夫座堂主任司铎。1320年他就任克拉科夫主教，颁布教区法规，并主持动工兴建哥特式的瓦维尔大教堂。

en:
Shōsatto, also read Ufusatu, founded Sannan (Nanzan), the southernmost of Okinawa's Three Kingdoms, in 1337. He had been aji of Ōzato and set his capital at Shimasoe-Ōzato Castle. The Ming Veritable Records record his tribute mission to China in 1383, and in 1385 the Hongwu Emperor invested him as King of Sannan with a gilded silver seal.

His kingdom soon came apart: in 1392 Shō Hashi of Sashiki seized his capital and he withdrew to Shimajiri-Ōzato. One account says that around 1396 his uncle Ō Eishi, allied with Hashi, defeated him and he fled.

Korean records tell of a Sannan king who fled to Korea in 1398; some take him for Shōsatto, though others think him another lord.

en:
Elepuʻukahonua was a high chief of ancient Oʻahu, remembered in Hawaiian chants as a son of Kumuhonua, a supreme chief of the island. On Kumuhonua's death he succeeded to the rule of Oʻahu; he may have been the eldest of four brothers, the others being Molohaia, Kahakuokane and Kukawaieakane.

He married Chiefess Hikilena. Their son Kahokupohakano and grandson Nāwele, who ruled around 1290, both carried on the dynasty of Māweke on Oʻahu.

en:
Kahokupohakano, also called Hoʻokupohokano, was a high chief of ancient Oʻahu, the son of Chief Elepuʻukahonua and Chiefess Hikilena.

After his father died he briefly held the title of aliʻi nui of Oʻahu, until his cousin Hoʻokamaliʻi, a descendant of the Kauaʻi chief Moʻikeha, usurped the throne. By his wife Kaumana II he fathered Nāwele, who around 1290 reconquered Oʻahu and restored the line of Māweke.

卡霍库波哈卡诺（又名霍奥库波哈卡诺）是古代瓦胡岛大酋长，为埃莱普乌卡霍努瓦与希基莱娜之子。

父亲死后，他短暂领有瓦胡阿利伊努伊之位，不久便被堂亲、考艾酋长莫伊凯哈的后裔霍奥卡马利伊篡位。他与妻子考马娜二世生下纳韦莱；约1290年，纳韦莱重新征服瓦胡，恢复了马韦凯一系的统治。

en:
Hawaiian chants name Keaunui, also called Keaunui-a-Maweke, as a high chief of the Nanaulu line who ruled Oʻahu's ʻEwa, Waiʻanae and Waialua districts. A son of the Tahitian-born ‘wizard’ chief Māweke and the high chiefess Naiolaukea, he was a brother of Mulielealiʻi and Kalehenui.

He married Chiefess Wehelani, who bore him Laakona of ʻEwa, Moʻi and Nuʻakea, chiefess of Molokaʻi. Tradition credits Keaunui with opening a navigable channel at Pearl Harbor.

夏威夷歌谣记载，凯亚乌努伊（又称凯亚乌努伊—阿—马韦凯）是纳纳乌鲁一系的高级酋长，统治瓦胡岛的埃瓦、怀阿奈和怀阿卢阿地区。他是出生于塔希提的‘巫师’酋长马韦凯与女酋长纳约劳凯娅之子，穆列莱亚利伊与卡莱赫努伊的兄弟。

en:
Hawaiian chants name Kumuhonua as an aliʻi nui, or supreme chief, of Oʻahu. He was the son of the high chief Mulielealiʻi and Chiefess Wehelani, and a grandson of Māweke, the Tahitian-born priest and wizard who came to Oʻahu and raised a temple to Kanaloa.

His siblings included Moʻikeha, chief of Kauaʻi, and Chiefess Hainakolo. Kumuhonua founded a dynasty on Oʻahu, was succeeded by his son Elepuʻukahonua, and his line still ruled the island in the time of his great-grandson Nāwele around 1290.

en:
Hawaiian chants name Māweke as a chief of the highest known rank and a kahuna, or priest, famed for his knowledge of black magic, who came to Hawaiʻi from Tahiti. They also name his famous ancestor Nanaulu.

On reaching Oʻahu he erected a temple to the god Kanaloa. He married the high chiefess Naiolaukea, who bore him the chiefs Mulielealiʻi, Keaunui and Kalehenui among other children, making him the ancestor of Oʻahu's ruling chiefs.

en:
Moʻikeha was a high chief of ancient Kauaʻi, celebrated in Hawaiian chants for the migration by sea from Kahiki, the Tahitian homeland, to the Hawaiian Islands; the wind god Laʻamaomao sailed with him and settled on Molokaʻi.

He was a son of the Oʻahu chief Mulielealiʻi and Wehelani, brother of Kumuhonua, a supreme chief of Oʻahu, and of ʻOlopana, who returned to Tahiti. His Kauaʻi line lasted two generations, and a descendant, Hoʻokamaliʻi, seized Oʻahu.

zh:
莫伊凯哈是古代考艾岛的大酋长，夏威夷歌谣传诵他率领族人从塔希提故土卡希基渡海迁居夏威夷，风神拉阿毛茅随行，后定居于莫洛凯岛。

他是瓦胡酋长穆列莱亚利伊与韦赫拉妮之子，与瓦胡最高酋长库穆霍努阿、返回塔希提的奥洛帕纳是兄弟。他开创的考艾王统延续两代；其后裔霍奥卡马利伊夺取了瓦胡。

en:
Hawaiian chants and the writings of Abraham Fornander name Mulielealiʻi, also called Miʻi-i-ele-aliʻi, as an ancient high chief of Oʻahu with the title aliʻi nui. A son of the Tahitian-born priest-chief Māweke and his wife Naiolaukea, he was a brother of Chief Keaunui of ʻEwa.

He married Chiefess Wehelani, who also married Keaunui and bore Mulielealiʻi Kumuhonua, later ruler of Oʻahu, the Kauaʻi chief Moʻikeha, ʻOlopana, who sailed to Tahiti, and Chiefess Hainakolo.

en:
Hawaiian genealogies name Nāwele as an aliʻi nui, or supreme chief, of Oʻahu around 1290. He was a descendant of the voyager chief Māweke and the son of Kahokupohakano.

Chants relate that after his cousin Kahaʻi, son of the usurper Hoʻokamaliʻi, held Oʻahu, Nāwele reconquered the island and ruled it. His wife was the chiefess Kalanimoeikawaikai, and his son Lakona succeeded him as aliʻi nui.

en:
Konrad I (c. 1294–1366) was a Silesian Piast duke, the second son of Henry III of Głogów. After his father died in 1309 he ruled with his brothers, receiving Oleśnica in the 1312 partition and holding it alone after his brother Bolesław died in 1321.

He made peace at Kraków in 1323, surrendering Namysłów to end Polish and Legnica raids, and paid homage to John of Bohemia in 1328. He repelled Casimir III's invasion in 1343, gained Koźle in 1355 and a share of Bytom in 1357. He died in 1366.

zh:
康拉德一世（约1294—1366）是西里西亚皮亚斯特家族公爵，格沃古夫公爵亨里克三世的次子。1309年父亲去世后他与诸兄弟共同统治，在1312年的分封中得到奥莱希尼察，1321年兄弟波列斯瓦夫死后独掌该公国。

为结束波兰与莱格尼察军队的袭扰，他于1323年在克拉科夫议和，放弃纳梅斯武夫，并于1328年向波希米亚国王约翰行臣服礼。1343年他击退卡齐米日三世的入侵，1355年取得科兹莱，1357年分得比托姆的一部分。他于1366年去世。

en:
Aruγ Temür (died 1361) was a Mongol prince of the House of Ögedei, descended from Ögedei's youngest son Melik, and inherited the title Prince of Yangi. In 1360, garrisoning the northern Mongolian lands amid the Red Turban wars, he raised an army in Lingbei, forced the northern princes to join him and demanded the imperial seal from Toghon Temür.

He routed the army sent against him, but in 1361 a second Yuan army aided by his brother Qutuq Temür defeated him. Seized by his own followers, he was sent to court and executed.

阿鲁辉帖木儿（？—1361）是窝阔台家族的蒙古宗王，窝阔台幼子灭里的后裔，袭封阳翟王。1360年红巾军之乱期间，他正屯守漠北，却在岭北举兵，胁迫北方诸王从叛，并要求元顺帝交出玉玺。

en:
Tuman was a Mongol prince of the House of Ögedei, descended from the khan's youngest son Melik, whose family roamed the Irtysh valley and had followed Kaidu. After Kaidu's death and the collapse of his ulus, the line submitted to the Yuan.

In 1308 Tuman presented the court with the jade seal of Ögedei long kept by his family, and the Yuan emperor invested him as Prince of Yangi with a golden seal. His son Küčün inherited the title.

en:
Adolf of Nassau (c. 1255–1298) succeeded his father Walram II as Count of Nassau around 1276. In May 1292 the prince-electors chose him as King of the Romans after Rudolf of Habsburg's death, preferring a pliable count to Rudolf's son Albert.

He soon struck out on his own, allying with Edward I of England against France in 1294 and buying the war-torn Landgraviate of Thuringia. The electors deposed him in June 1298 and raised Albert of Habsburg to the throne. Adolf fell at the Battle of Göllheim on 2 July 1298, never crowned emperor by the pope.

拿骚的阿道夫（约1255—1298）约在1276年继其父瓦拉姆二世之后成为拿骚伯爵。1292年5月，选帝侯们在哈布斯堡的鲁道夫去世后选他为罗马人的国王，宁可立这位小国伯爵，也不立鲁道夫之子阿尔布雷希特。

en:
Beatrice I (1143–1184) was the only child of Reginald III, Count of Burgundy, and inherited the county at his death in 1148. Her regent uncle William of Mâcon tried to seize her inheritance and imprisoned her; Frederick Barbarossa intervened and married her in 1156, ruling Burgundy jointly with her.

She accompanied Frederick on campaign and brought him Burgundian reinforcements at the siege of Crema in 1159. She was crowned empress in Rome by Antipope Paschal III in 1167, and queen of Burgundy at Vienne in 1178. She died in 1184; her son Otto I succeeded to her county.

贝亚特丽丝一世（1143—1184）是勃艮第伯爵瑞诺三世的独女，1148年父亲去世后继承伯国。担任摄政的叔父马孔伯爵威廉企图侵吞她的遗产并将她囚禁；皇帝腓特烈一世（巴巴罗萨）出面干预，于1156年与她成婚，此后与她共同统治勃艮第。

她随腓特烈征战，1159年率勃艮第援军驰援克雷马围城战。她于1167年在罗马由对立教宗巴斯加三世加冕为皇后，1178年在维埃纳加冕为勃艮第王后。她于1184年去世，勃艮第伯国由儿子奥东一世继承。

en:
Frederick I Barbarossa (1122–1190), of the Hohenstaufen family, was Holy Roman Emperor from 1155 until his death. The son of Duke Frederick II of Swabia and Judith, a Welf, he succeeded his father as duke of Swabia and in 1152 was elected king.

Six expeditions took him into Italy. He was crowned emperor in 1155, married Beatrice of Burgundy in 1156 and destroyed much of Milan in 1162. Backing antipopes brought him to the Lombard League, which beat him at Legnano in 1176, where he was wounded and thought dead; he made peace at Venice in 1177.

In 1180 he had his cousin Henry the Lion stripped of his lands. He took the cross in 1188 and led an army into Anatolia, where he drowned in the Saleph River on 10 June 1190. His body was divided among Antioch, Tyre and Tarsus, and his son Henry VI succeeded him.

腓特烈一世·巴巴罗萨（1122—1190）出身霍恩施陶芬家族，1155年起任神圣罗马皇帝直至去世。他是施瓦本公爵腓特烈二世与韦尔夫家族尤迪特之子，先继任施瓦本公爵，1152年当选国王。

他先后六次远征意大利。1155年加冕为帝，1156年迎娶勃艮第的贝亚特丽丝，1162年将叛乱的米兰大半摧毁。他因扶持对立教宗与伦巴第同盟交战，1176年在莱尼亚诺战败负伤，一度被传已死，1177年在威尼斯议和。

1180年他削夺表弟狮子亨利的领地。1188年他领十字率军进入安纳托利亚，1190年6月10日在萨列法河溺亡，遗体分葬安条克、泰尔和塔尔苏斯，儿子亨利六世继位。

en:
Frederick I (c. 1050–1105) was the first Duke of Swabia from the House of Hohenstaufen, from 1079 to 1105. The son of Count Frederick of Büren, he built Hohenstaufen Castle and founded Lorch Abbey.

During the Investiture Controversy he backed King Henry IV against the anti-king Rudolf; in 1079 Henry enfeoffed him with the duchy and betrothed him to his daughter Agnes. Rival claimants confined his rule to northern Swabia until a 1098 settlement recognized Berthold of Zähringen.

In his last years Frederick expanded northwards as protector of Weissenburg Abbey and the bishopric of Speyer. By Agnes he fathered Duke Frederick II and King Conrad III.

腓特烈一世（约1050—1105）是霍恩施陶芬家族首任施瓦本公爵，1079年至1105年在位。他是布伦伯爵腓特烈之子，修建了霍恩施陶芬城堡，并创立洛尔希修道院。

叙任权斗争期间，他支持亨利四世对抗对立国王鲁道夫；1079年国王将施瓦本公国封给他，并把女儿阿格妮丝许配给他。对手的争夺使他只能统治施瓦本北部，直到1098年与策林根的贝特霍尔德达成和解。

晚年他担任魏森堡修道院和施派尔主教区的保护人，将领地向北扩张。他与阿格妮丝生下了施瓦本公爵腓特烈二世和德意志国王康拉德三世。

叙任权斗争期间，他支持亨利四世对抗对立国王鲁道夫；1079年国王将施瓦本公国封给他，并把女儿阿格妮丝许配给他。对手的争夺使他只能统治施瓦本北部，直到1098年与策林根的贝特霍尔德达成和解。

晚年他担任[ShowLocationName('weissenburg')]修道院和[ShowLocationName('speyer')]主教区的保护人，将领地向北扩张。他与阿格妮丝生下了施瓦本公爵#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('ogk_friedrich_ii_swabia').GetID],X #L 腓特烈二世#!#!和德意志国王#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('ogk_konrad_iii_hohenstaufen').GetID],X #L 康拉德三世#!#!。

en:
Frederick II (1194–1250), called Stupor Mundi (Wonder of the World), was King of Sicily, King of the Germans and Holy Roman Emperor. The son of Emperor Henry VI and Constance of Sicily, he was crowned King of Sicily in 1198, went north as King of the Germans in 1212 and was crowned emperor in 1220.

He was excommunicated four times, yet his Sixth Crusade of 1228 recovered Jerusalem by treaty with Egypt. In Sicily he built an absolutist state: he founded the University of Naples in 1224 and issued the Constitutions of Melfi in 1231.

In Italy he fought the Lombard League, defeating it at Cortenuova in 1237, and Pope Innocent IV, who called him the forerunner of the Antichrist. He died of dysentery at Castel Fiorentino on 13 December 1250. His son Conrad IV died in 1254, the Hohenstaufen fell, and the Empire entered the Great Interregnum.

zh:
腓特烈二世（1194—1250）人称“世间奇人”，身兼西西里国王、德意志国王和神圣罗马皇帝。他是亨利六世与西西里的康斯坦丝之子，1198年加冕为西西里国王，1212年北上成为德意志国王，1220年加冕为皇帝。

他四次被开除教籍，但1228年的第六次十字军仍通过与埃及缔约收回耶路撒冷。他在西西里建立专制国家，1224年创办那不勒斯大学，1231年颁布《梅尔菲宪章》。

1237年他在科尔泰诺瓦击败伦巴第同盟，并与教宗英诺森四世对抗，后者称他是反基督的先驱。1250年12月13日他因痢疾卒于菲奥伦蒂诺堡；其子康拉德四世1254年去世，霍恩施陶芬家族失势，帝国进入大空位时代。

en:
Frederick II (1090–1147), called the One-Eyed, was the second Hohenstaufen Duke of Swabia, ruling from 1105. With his brother Conrad he enlarged the family lands, and in 1116 Henry V appointed the brothers regents during his Italian campaign.

After the Salian line ended in 1125 Frederick stood for the crown but lost to Lothair II; a feud over the Salian inheritance cost him an eye and his royal hopes. He fought Lothair until submitting at Bamberg in 1135.

After Conrad became king in 1138 he supported him against the Welfs. By Judith of Bavaria he fathered Frederick Barbarossa, and died at Alzey in 1147.

腓特烈二世（1090—1147），绰号“独眼”，是霍恩施陶芬家族第二代施瓦本公爵，1105年继位。他与弟弟康拉德一同扩张家族领地，1116年亨利五世远征意大利时，任命兄弟二人摄政。

1125年萨利安王朝绝嗣，他参选国王却败给洛泰尔二世；在争夺萨利安家族遗产的混战中失去一目，从此与王位无缘。他与洛泰尔交战多年，1135年在班贝格臣服。

1138年康拉德成为国王后，他支持康拉德对抗韦尔夫家族。他与巴伐利亚的尤迪特生下腓特烈一世，1147年卒于阿尔蔡。

en:
Henry Berengar (born 1136 or 1137, died 1150) was the eldest son of King Conrad III of Germany and Gertrude of Sulzbach, groomed for the succession. Before leaving on the Second Crusade, Conrad had the princes elect the ten-year-old Henry co-king at Regensburg in March 1147, and he was crowned at Aachen.

He led the royal army to victory over Welf VI and Welf VII at the Battle of Flochberg in 1150. He died later that year and was buried at Lorch, predeceasing his father.

海因里希·贝伦加尔（1136/1137年—1150年）是德意志国王康拉德三世与苏尔茨巴赫的格特鲁德的长子，自幼被定为继承人。1147年3月，康拉德三世出发参加第二次十字军东征前，在雷根斯堡让诸侯选举年仅十岁的海因里希为共治国王，随后在亚琛为他加冕。

1150年，他率军在弗洛希贝格之战击败韦尔夫六世与韦尔夫七世，同年晚些时候去世，葬于洛尔希修道院，先于其父而死。

en:
Henry I (919/921–955), second son of Henry the Fowler and younger brother of Otto the Great, twice rebelled against the king. Wounded at Birten in 939, he reconciled with Otto and received Lotharingia in 940. He plotted to kill Otto at Quedlinburg in 941 and was pardoned after imprisonment.

In 948 Otto enfeoffed him with Bavaria, where he married Judith. He fought the Magyars, joined the 951 Italian campaign and crushed his nephew Liudolf's revolt. He died at Pöhlde on 1 November 955, leaving a son, Henry the Wrangler.

亨利一世（919/921—955）是捕鸟者亨利的次子、奥托大帝的弟弟。他两度反叛兄长：939年在比尔滕负伤，940年与奥托和解并领有洛林。941年他在奎德林堡密谋刺杀奥托，事泄被囚，忏悔后获赦。

948年奥托将巴伐利亚封给他，他迎娶尤迪特为妻。他与马扎尔人作战，参加了951年的意大利远征，又镇压了侄子柳道尔夫的叛乱。955年11月1日他卒于珀尔德修道院，身后留下儿子“争吵者”亨利。

en:
Henry I, called the Fowler (c. 876–936), Duke of Saxony from 912, became the first non-Frankish king of East Francia in 919, elected at Conrad I's dying wish. He subdued Bavaria and Swabia and recovered Lotharingia in 925.

Buying a truce from the Magyars in 924, he built fortresses and cavalry that crushed them at the Riade in 933. He took Brandenburg from the Slavs in 929 and conquered Schleswig in 934. He died at Memleben on 2 July 936 and was buried at Quedlinburg; his son Otto the Great succeeded him.

en:
Henry II (973–1024), later Saint Henry, was the son of Duke Henry the Wrangler of Bavaria. Succeeding as duke in 995, he took the German crown after his cousin Otto III died childless in 1002, became King of Italy in 1004 and was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in Rome in 1014.

He founded the bishopric of Bamberg in 1007 and waged long wars against Poland, ending with the Peace of Bautzen in 1018. He died without an heir in 1024, the last Ottonian ruler, and was canonized in 1146.

en:
Henry III (1016–1056), the Salian emperor called the Pious, was the eldest son of Conrad II, who made him Duke of Bavaria in 1027 and had him elected co-king in 1028. He inherited Swabia and Burgundy in 1038 and succeeded his father as king in 1039.

At Sutri in 1046 he ended the papal schism by deposing three rival popes and was crowned in Rome by his nominee Clement II. He defeated a rebellion in Lorraine, but died at Bodfeld on 5 October 1056, leaving the crown to his five-year-old son Henry IV.

en:
Henry IV (1050–1106) was the Salian emperor at the centre of the Investiture Controversy. Succeeding his father Henry III at five in 1056, he clashed with Pope Gregory VII over the appointment of bishops. Excommunicated in 1076, he did penance barefoot at Canossa in January 1077, but the German princes raised rival kings against him.

In 1080 he installed the antipope Clement III, who crowned him emperor in Rome in 1084, only to be forced to abdicate in 1105 by his son Henry V. He died at Liège on 7 August 1106.

亨利四世（1050—1106）是萨利安王朝皇帝，一生处在主教叙任权之争的中心。1056年他五岁继其父亨利三世之位为王，围绕主教任命权与教宗格里高利七世发生冲突。1076年他被开除教籍，1077年1月在卡诺莎城堡赤足忏悔，然而德意志诸侯仍另立对立国王与他为敌。

1080年他扶立对立教宗克莱门特三世，后者于1084年在罗马为他加冕为帝。1105年他被儿子亨利五世逼迫退位，1106年8月7日卒于列日。

en:
Henry II the Wrangler (951–995) inherited Bavaria at four and married Gisela of Burgundy in 972. Under Otto II he fought the emperor over a bishopric and Swabia, and a plot of 974 landed him in prison at Ingelheim. He escaped in 976 and raised Bavaria in revolt, but Otto II took Regensburg, deposed him and carved Carinthia from Bavaria.

Freed in 983, he abducted the infant Otto III and had himself proclaimed king, but submitted in 985. He recovered Bavaria and later Carinthia, dying on 28 August 995; his son became Emperor Henry II.

zh:
亨利二世（951—995），绰号“争吵者”，四岁继承巴伐利亚公爵之位，972年与勃艮第的吉塞拉成婚。奥托二世在位时，他为主教任命和施瓦本继承权与皇帝对抗，974年密谋败露后被囚于英格尔海姆。976年他逃脱并在巴伐利亚举兵，奥托二世攻占雷根斯堡将他废黜，并从巴伐利亚划出克恩滕。

983年获释后，他劫持幼王奥托三世、自立为罗马人的国王，但于985年臣服。他后来收复巴伐利亚并得到克恩滕，995年8月28日去世，其子日后成为神圣罗马皇帝亨利二世。

en:
Henry V (1081–1125), last emperor of the Salian dynasty, was the younger son of Henry IV. Made co-king in 1099, he joined the reforming princes against his father and forced his abdication in 1105. At Rome in 1111 he imprisoned Pope Paschal II and wrung from him an imperial coronation and the right to invest bishops.

Renewed conflict ended only in 1122, when he and Pope Callixtus II concluded the Concordat of Worms, settling the Investiture Controversy. He died without legitimate heirs at Utrecht on 23 May 1125, and the princes elected Lothair in his place.

zh:
亨利五世（1081—1125）是萨利安王朝末代皇帝、亨利四世的幼子。1099年被立为共王后，他倒向主张教会改革的诸侯，于1105年逼迫父亲退位。1111年在罗马，他囚禁教宗帕斯加尔二世，迫使对方为他加冕为帝并承认其主教叙任权。

冲突重启后直到1122年，他才与教宗加里斯都二世订立《沃尔姆斯宗教协定》，为叙任权之争画上句号。1125年5月23日他卒于乌得勒支，没有嫡出继承人，诸侯随后选举洛泰尔继位。

en:
Henry VI (1165–1197) of the Hohenstaufen dynasty was elected King of the Romans in 1169, the son of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa. Educated in Roman and canon law, he patronized poets.

Crowned emperor in 1191, he claimed Sicily through his wife Constance: his first invasion failed at Naples, but in 1194, funded by Richard I of England's ransom, he conquered the kingdom and was crowned in Palermo. His plan to make the Empire hereditary failed with the princes. In 1197, after crushing a Sicilian revolt, he died of malaria at Messina, leaving the infant Frederick II.

zh:
亨利六世（1165—1197）出身霍恩施陶芬王朝，1169年被选为罗马人的国王，是皇帝腓特烈一世（巴巴罗萨）之子。他受过罗马法与教会法教育，资助诗人。

1191年加冕为皇帝后，他以妻子康斯坦丝的继承权主张西西里王位；首次远征在那不勒斯受挫，1194年他凭英格兰国王理查一世的赎金征服西西里王国并在巴勒莫加冕。他将帝国改为世袭制的计划遭诸侯反对。1197年镇压西西里叛乱后，他因疟疾死于墨西拿，继承人是尚在襁褓中的腓特烈二世。

en:
Conrad II (c. 990–1039), called the Elder, founded the Salian dynasty. A Franconian count, he was elected King of the Romans in 1024 after the last Ottonian, Henry II, died heirless. He crossed the Alps in 1026, took the Iron Crown at Milan, and was crowned emperor in Rome by Pope John XIX in March 1027.

After Rudolf III died in 1032, he claimed Burgundy, subsequently conquering it and joining it to the empire; his 1037 edict on Italian fiefs protected lesser vassals. He died at Utrecht on 4 June 1039 and was buried at Speyer, leaving it to his son Henry III.

康拉德二世（约990—1039），人称“长者”，是萨利安王朝的开创者。他本为法兰克尼亚伯爵，1024年末代奥托王朝君主亨利二世无嗣而终后，他被选为罗马人的国王。1026年他翻越阿尔卑斯山，在米兰戴上伦巴第铁王冠，1027年3月在罗马由教宗约翰十九世加冕为帝。

en:
Conrad III (1093 or 1094–1152) was the first Hohenstaufen King of the Romans. Younger son of Duke Frederick I of Swabia and Agnes, he became Duke of Franconia in 1116 and was elected anti-king in 1127, submitting to Lothair II in 1135.

Elected king in 1138, he dispossessed Henry the Proud, opening the Guelph–Ghibelline struggle. Before joining the Second Crusade he had his son Henry Berengar crowned king, but was routed at Dorylaeum in 1147. He died at Bamberg in 1152, and was succeeded by his nephew Frederick Barbarossa.

康拉德三世（1093或1094—1152）是霍恩施陶芬家族首位罗马人的国王。他是施瓦本公爵腓特烈一世与阿格妮丝的幼子，1116年成为法兰克尼亚公爵，1127年被推举为对立国王，1135年向洛泰尔二世臣服。

en:
Conrad IV (1228–1254), the only son of Emperor Frederick II and Isabella II of Jerusalem, inherited Jerusalem when his mother died giving him birth. Made Duke of Swabia in 1235, he was elected King of the Romans in 1237.

He fought Pope Innocent IV and rival kings, and after Frederick's death in 1250 ruled Sicily and seized Naples in 1253. Excommunicated in 1254, he died of malaria at Lavello on 21 May, leaving his son Conradin; his death opened the Interregnum.

en:
Lothair II of Supplinburg (1075–1137) was the only emperor of his house. Made Duke of Saxony in 1106, he was elected king at Mainz in 1125 after the childless Henry V. He fought the Staufer brothers and was beaten by the Bohemians at Chlumec in 1126.

Pope Innocent II crowned him emperor in 1133. His campaign of 1136–37 against Roger II of Sicily conquered Apulia, but he died on the march home at Breitenwang in 1137; his daughter Gertrude had married Henry the Proud.

en:
Otto II, called the Red (955–983), was the sole surviving son of Otto the Great and Adelaide. Crowned co-emperor in 967, he succeeded his father in 973 and married the Byzantine princess Theophanu.

He crushed a revolt by his Bavarian kinsman Henry the Wrangler, then campaigned in southern Italy, where he was disastrously defeated near Crotone in 982. In 983 a Slav rising drove the Empire back beyond the Elbe, and he died that December, aged twenty-eight, leaving the throne to his three-year-old son Otto III.

In 983 a Slav rising drove the Empire back beyond the Elbe, and he died that December, aged twenty-eight, leaving the throne to his three-year-old son #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('ogk_otto_iii_liudolfinger').GetID],X #L Otto III#!#!.
zh:
奥托二世（955—983），人称“红头发”，是奥托大帝与阿德莱德唯一存活的儿子。他于967年被加冕为共治皇帝，973年继承父位，并娶拜占庭公主赛奥法诺为妻。

他平定了巴伐利亚族人“强辩者”亨利的叛乱，随后南下意大利作战，于982年在克罗托内附近遭遇惨败。983年斯拉夫人起义，将帝国势力逐回易北河以西；同年12月他猝逝，年仅28岁，皇位传给3岁的儿子奥托三世。

en:
Otto III (980–1002), only son of Otto II and the Byzantine Theophanu, was crowned king at three in 983, ruling under the regency of his mother and grandmother.

Crowned emperor in Rome in 996, he installed his cousin as Pope Gregory V, the first German pope, and crushed a Roman revolt in 998. At Gniezno in 1000 he met Bolesław of Poland and backed Stephen I's coronation in Hungary, pursuing renewal of the Roman Empire. He died of fever near Rome in 1002, aged twenty-one and without an heir.

en:
Otto IV (1175–1218), third son of Henry the Lion of Saxony and Matilda of England, was raised at his grandfather Henry II's court. His uncle Richard I made him Count of Poitou in 1196 and backed his election as king in 1198, against Philip of Swabia; he was crowned at Aachen with replica regalia.

After Philip's murder in 1208, Otto was crowned emperor by Pope Innocent III in 1209, but his bid for Sicily brought excommunication in 1210. He was defeated at Bouvines in 1214, abandoned by his princes by 1215, and died near Brunswick in 1218.

en:
Otto I the Great (912–973), eldest son of Henry the Fowler and Matilda, was East Frankish king from 936 and Holy Roman Emperor from 962. Crowned at Aachen on 7 August 936 in Frankish dress as Charlemagne's successor, he tied the great duchies to his family by marriage. His brother Henry rebelled twice before becoming Duke of Bavaria in 948.

His destruction of the Magyars at the Lechfeld in 955 ended their raids on the west and earned him the name of saviour of Christendom. He married Adelaide, and on 2 February 962 Pope John XII crowned him emperor in Rome. When John XII plotted against him, Otto deposed him and installed Leo VIII.

He died at Memleben, his father's deathplace, on 7 May 973, and was buried beside his first wife Eadgyth at Magdeburg. Otto II succeeded, though the rebuilt empire was too large for its administration.

奥托一世（912—973）是捕鸟者亨利与玛蒂尔达的长子，936年起为东法兰克国王，962年起为神圣罗马皇帝。936年8月7日他在亚琛加冕，身穿法兰克服饰，以示自己是查理曼的继承人，并用联姻把各大公国与王室绑在一起。弟弟亨利两度叛乱，最终在948年成为巴伐利亚公爵。

955年他在莱希费尔德歼灭马扎尔人，终结了他们对西方的劫掠，被誉为基督教世界的救星。他迎娶阿德尔海德，962年2月2日教宗约翰十二世在罗马为他加冕为皇帝。约翰十二世密谋反对他，奥托将其废黜，另立利奥八世。

973年5月7日他卒于梅姆莱本，与首任妻子伊迪丝并葬马格德堡。奥托二世继位，但重建的帝国对当时的行政体制过于庞大。

en:
Philip of Swabia (1177–1208), youngest son of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, was raised for a church career but left the clergy in 1193 and inherited the Duchy of Swabia in 1196. In 1197 he married Irene Angelina, Isaac II's daughter.

After Henry VI died leaving an infant heir, Philip was elected King of the Romans in March 1198; the Welf Otto IV was elected a rival king three months later, opening the German throne dispute. By 1204 Philip held the upper hand, but in June 1208 he was murdered at Bamberg by count palatine Otto of Wittelsbach.

Christian IV (attested in charters 1302–1323) was Count of Oldenburg, eldest son of John II. In 1313 he promised to share rule with his infant half-brother Conrad I, and from 1316 he ruled jointly with his brother John III.

In 1317 the brothers styled themselves dukes of the Frisians, and in 1318 Christian alone called himself protector of the Frisians, pressing claims over Östringen and Rüstringen that never took effect. He left a daughter Jutta, and John III and Conrad I succeeded him.

en:
John II (first attested in 1272, died 1315) was Count of Oldenburg, succeeding his father Christian III in 1285 under the guardianship of his uncle Otto II until 1289. Around 1292–1293 he joined Otto's failed attack on the Stedinger lands of the Bremen archbishopric and waged feuds against the Stedinger peasants.

From 1301 he issued charters jointly with his brother Christian. He died in 1315, leaving his sons Christian IV and John III to succeed him.

en:
John III (documented 1302–1342) was Count of Oldenburg, the second son of Count John II and Elisabeth of Brunswick-Lüneburg. From 1316 he ruled jointly with his brother Christian IV, and from 1324 with his half-brother Conrad I. At his order the illuminated Rastede manuscript of the Sachsenspiegel, the medieval Saxon law book, was completed in 1336.

After Conrad's death in 1347 he ruled together with his cousin Conrad II. No marriage or children of his are recorded; he died on 6 October 1356, and the dynastic succession was continued by his cousin's descendants.

en:
Öljaitü (1282–1316), born Khar-banda and later called Muhammad Khodabandeh, was the eighth Ilkhan of Persia, ruling from 1304. The son of Arghun and brother of Ghazan, he eliminated rival princes, was crowned in 1304, and later led an unsuccessful invasion of Mamluk Syria.

Raised a Buddhist and briefly baptised a Christian, he ended as a Shia Muslim. With his vizier Rashid al-Din, compiler of the Jami al-Tawarikh, he built the new capital Soltaniyeh, where he died in 1316 and was succeeded by his son Abu Sa'id.

en:
Ontsifor Lukinich (died 1367) was a boyar of the Novgorod Republic from the Mishinichi clan. He used popular movements against the boyars to advance, and is first recorded in 1342 leading a city uprising for which he was exiled but soon returned.

In 1348 he led the Novgorod army that defeated King Magnus Eriksson of Sweden after the Swedes seized Oreshek fortress. He served as posadnik from 1350 to 1354 and in 1354 carried through the posadnik reform, creating six lifetime posadniki from the city's different ends, with a presiding one chosen each year; he himself declined that office.

Kameshwar Thakur was a Maithil Brahmin scholar of the Kashyap gotra, born at Oini, who served as chief priest and guru to Harisimhadeva, the last Karnat king of Mithila.

When the Karnat dynasty collapsed in 1324, he succeeded to the Mithila throne in 1325, becoming the first king of the Oiniwar (or Sugauna) dynasty. His accession opened nearly two centuries of Maithil Brahmin rule over Mithila, which lasted until 1526.

Bolko I of Opole (before 1258–1313), third son of Vladislaus I of Opole, ruled Opole from 1282, initially jointly with his brother Casimir, who took Bytom in 1284. An ally of Henry IV Probus of Wrocław, he was captured fighting at Siewierz in 1289 and ransomed a year later by Władysław I the Elbow-high.

In 1291 he did homage to Wenceslaus II of Bohemia, attended the king's coronations in 1297 and 1300, and was made starosta of Kraków. He died in 1313.

en:
Bolko II (before 1300–1356) was a Silesian Piast who inherited the Duchy of Opole in 1313, ruling with his brother Albert until they divided their lands in 1323. Through his marriage to Elisabeth of Świdnica he was briefly linked to King Władysław I of Poland, but on 5 April 1327 at Wrocław he paid homage to John of Bohemia, becoming the last Silesian duke to accept Bohemian vassalage.

He fostered trade and introduced German law in villages. He died on 21 June 1356 and was buried in Opole's Franciscan monastery.

en:
Przemysław of Racibórz (1258/1268–1306), son of Vladislaus I of Opole, became duke on his father's death in 1282, ruling jointly with his brother Mieszko I until they divided their lands in 1290 and Przemysław kept Racibórz. In 1285 he sheltered a bishop fleeing Henry IV Probus of Wrocław, whose army besieged and nearly destroyed Racibórz in 1287.

He paid homage to Wenceslaus II of Bohemia in 1291, and in 1299 granted Racibórz town rights and founded its Dominican monastery, where he was buried in 1306.

en:
Vladislaus II (c. 1332–1401), called Opolczyk, was the eldest son of Bolko II of Opole and became duke in 1356. He served Louis I of Hungary, becoming Count palatine (1367–1372), then governed Hungarian-ruled Ruthenia until 1378, and received Wieluń and Częstochowa for supporting Louis's Polish succession.

In 1382 he founded the Pauline monastery of Jasna Góra, bringing the Black Madonna icon there. After Louis's death he claimed the Polish crown, but his 1388 coup failed, and his Teutonic alliances cost him his Polish fiefs in 1392. He died at Opole on 18 May 1401.

瓦迪斯瓦夫二世（约1332—1401），绰号奥波尔奇克，是波尔科二世的长子，1356年成为奥波莱公爵。他效力于匈牙利国王拉约什一世，1367—1372年任匈牙利宫相，其后治理匈牙利治下的罗塞尼亚至1378年，并因支持拉约什继承波兰王位而获得维隆与琴斯托霍瓦。

en:
Vladislaus I of Opole (c. 1225–1282), second son of Casimir I of Opole, received Kalisz and Wieluń as his share in 1234 but lost both to Greater Poland by 1249. In 1246 he inherited Opole-Racibórz from his brother Mieszko II the Fat. He first sided with Hungary, then switched in 1255 to Ottokar II of Bohemia and fought for him in 1260.

His 1273 bid for the Kraków throne ended in defeat. He founded numerous monasteries and granted Magdeburg Law to the towns of his duchy.

en:
Anna of Racibórz (1292/98–1340) was a Silesian Piast princess, the daughter of Duke Przemysław of Racibórz and Anna of Masovia. In 1318 she married Nicholas II of Opava, an illegitimate grandson of King Ottokar II of Bohemia, and bore him six children, including Jan I, who inherited Racibórz.

When her brother Leszek died in 1336, King John of Bohemia awarded her husband the Duchy of Racibórz. Anna died in 1340 and was probably buried in Racibórz's Dominican monastery.

en:
John I of Opava-Ratibor (c. 1322–1380/82) was the only son of Nicholas II of Opava by his first wife, Anna of Racibórz, and through her became sole heir of Racibórz in 1365. From 1367 he ruled Opava jointly with his three half-brothers, and the partition of 1377 left him with Racibórz, Krnov and Bruntál.

In 1375 financial difficulties led him to sell Mikołów and Pless to Vladislaus of Opole. In 1361 he married Anna of Żagań, mother of his heir John II the Iron, and died in 1380 or 1382.

en:
Nicholas I of Opava (c. 1255–1318) was the natural son of King Ottokar II of Bohemia. Legitimated with papal consent and enfeoffed with Opava in 1269, he founded the Silesian Přemyslid line. He fought for Ottokar at the Marchfeld in 1278, was captured by the Hungarians, and recovered his duchy from Rudolf of Habsburg, whose niece he married in 1283.

After the Přemyslids died out in 1306 he had to accept the pledging of Opava, which John of Bohemia redeemed in 1318 for his son Nicholas II; Nicholas died the same year.
