en:
Nicholas II of Opava (1288–1365) was a prince of the Opava branch of the Přemyslid dynasty, son of Nicholas I and Adelheid of Habsburg. A loyal supporter of King John of Bohemia, he received Opava as an independent fief in 1318 and moved his residence there from Hradec nad Moravicí.

In 1318 he also married Anna of Racibórz, and when her brother Leszek died in 1336, King John invested him with Racibórz in 1337, uniting Opava and Racibórz under his rule. He died on 8 December 1365.

en:
Bertrand I of Baux (c. 1137–1181) was a younger son of Raymond of Baux. During his family's wars with the house of Barcelona, he helped the young Alfonso II of Aragon escape to Arles, helping reconcile the families.

In 1173 he married Thiburge II, heiress of Orange, and in 1175 began building the abbey church of Silvacane. In 1178 Emperor Frederick Barbarossa granted him at Arles the right to style himself Prince of Orange and to wear a closed crown.

On Easter Day 1181 he was killed in an ambush while marching on Montpellier, reportedly on Count Raymond V of Toulouse's orders, and was buried at Silvacane.

博的贝特朗一世（约1137—1181）是博的雷蒙的幼子。在家族与巴塞罗那家族的战争中，他帮助年幼的阿拉贡国王阿方索二世逃到阿尔勒，促成两家和解。

1173年他与奥朗日女继承人蒂比尔热二世结婚，1175年动工修建锡尔瓦卡内修道院教堂。1178年皇帝腓特烈一世（巴巴罗萨）在阿尔勒授予他奥朗日亲王的称号以及佩戴封闭王冠的权利。

1181年复活节，他在进军蒙彼利埃途中遇伏身亡，据传出自图卢兹伯爵雷蒙五世的授意，葬于锡尔瓦卡内修道院。

en:
Bertrand IV des Baux (c. 1240–1314) succeeded his father Raymond I as Prince of Orange in 1282. In 1288 he bought his cousin Bertrand III's share of the principality, becoming sole prince, and a charter of 1293 made Orange impartible, to pass to a single heir.

In 1309 he obtained Charles II of Naples's half of Orange by accepting vassalage to the counts of Provence. He fathered his successor Raymond IV and died in 1314.

贝特朗四世·德·博（约1240—1314）于1282年继父亲雷蒙德一世之后成为奥朗日亲王。1288年他买下堂兄弟贝特朗三世名下的亲王份额，成为唯一亲王；1293年他颁布文书，规定奥朗日不可分割，只能由单一继承人继承。

en:
William I of Baux (c. 1176–1218), Prince of Orange, was the son of Bertrand I of Baux and a troubadour poet like his parents, a few of whose poems survive. He succeeded his father as prince in 1182 and joined Simon de Montfort's Albigensian Crusade against Toulouse.

In 1215 Emperor Frederick II appointed him viceroy of the Kingdom of Arles. Captured by Toulouse's Avignonese allies in 1216, he was held at Avignon and killed there in 1218. Pope Honorius III called a crusade to avenge him, and his son Raymond I succeeded him.

en:
William II des Baux (died 1239), a younger son of Prince William I of Orange, became co-prince of Orange with his elder half-brother Raymond I after their father was killed by the Albigensians in 1218, and he founded the Baux-Orange line.

In alliance with the citizens of Marseille and his cousins, he warred against Count Raymond Berengar IV of Provence, and in 1233 joined the peace treaty ending the Provençal civil war. He died in 1239, leaving sons who included the later co-princes William III and Raymond II.

en:
Levi ben Gershom (1288–1344), known as Gersonides, was a Jewish philosopher, Talmudist, mathematician, physician and astronomer born at Bagnols-sur-Cèze in Languedoc, who lived at Avignon and Orange. His masterwork The Wars of the Lord, written in 1317–1329, defended strict Aristotelian positions and surveyed Arabic astronomy; part of it was translated into Latin for Pope Clement VI in 1342.

He is credited with inventing the Jacob's staff to measure stellar angles, used the camera obscura for eclipse observations, and pioneered mathematical induction. He died on 20 April 1344.

列维·本·格尔肖姆（1288—1344），以吉尔松尼德之名著称，是生于朗格多克塞兹河畔巴尼奥勒的犹太哲学家、塔木德学者、数学家、医师兼天文学家，曾生活在阿维尼翁与奥朗日。他的巨著《上主的战争》写于1317—1329年，坚持严格的亚里士多德立场，并综述阿拉伯天文学，其中一部分于1342年应教皇克雷芒六世之请译成拉丁文。

他被认为发明了用于测量星体角度的“雅各布杖”，利用暗箱观测日月食，并率先系统运用数学归纳法。1344年4月20日去世。

en:
Raymond I des Baux (died 1282) became Prince of Orange in 1218 after his father was killed by the Albigensians. He ruled jointly in turn with his brother, nephews and Bertrand III. In 1237 he received lands from Raymond VII of Toulouse, doing homage to Alphonse of Poitiers in 1253.

Captured by Orange townsmen in 1247, he made peace the same year. In 1257 he ceded his claims to the kingdom of Arles to Charles I of Anjou, and he left a son, Bertrand IV.

en:
Raymond IV des Baux (died 1340) was Prince of Orange from 1314, succeeding his father Bertrand IV. In 1317 he married Anne de Viennois, daughter of Guigues de la Tour du Pin, after a papal dispensation granted on 28 May. When Anne inherited the barony of Montauban in 1319, the couple sold it to Guigues VIII of Viennois.

He bought Condorcet castle in 1324 and received Puy as a fief in 1339. He died in 1340 and was succeeded by his son Raymond V.

Raymond V des Baux (died 1393) was the last Baux prince of Orange, ruling from 1340, first under his mother's regency. In 1358 he married Jeanne of Geneva, daughter of Count Amadeus III of Geneva and sister of Avignon Pope Clement VII.

In 1365 Pope Urban V granted privileges to Orange's school, and Emperor Charles IV, passing through the town, authorized studies in law, medicine and the liberal arts. In 1386 he betrothed his only daughter, Marie, to John III of Chalon-Arlay, granting Orange as her dowry. He died at Avignon on 10 February 1393, ending the Baux-Orange line.

雷蒙五世·德·博（？—1393）是博家族最后一位奥朗日亲王，1340年继位，初由母亲维埃努瓦的安娜摄政。1358年，他迎娶日内瓦伯爵阿梅迪奥三世之女、阿维尼翁教皇克雷芒七世的妹妹让娜。

1365年，教皇乌尔班五世赐予奥朗日学校特权；同年皇帝查理四世途经奥朗日，批准在此讲授法律、医学及博雅诸艺。1386年，他把独生女玛丽许配给沙隆-阿尔莱的让三世，并以奥朗日亲王国为嫁妆。1393年2月10日卒于阿维尼翁，博家族奥朗日支系至此终结。

en:
Eleanor de Bohun (1304–1363) was an English noblewoman, born at Knaresborough Castle, the daughter of Humphrey de Bohun, 4th Earl of Hereford, and Elizabeth of Rhuddlan, daughter of Edward I. Orphaned young, she was raised at Amesbury Priory under her aunt Mary of Woodstock.

In 1327 she married James Butler, 1st Earl of Ormond, and after his death married Thomas de Dagworth in 1343; Dagworth was killed in an ambush in Brittany in 1352. She died on 7 October 1363.

埃莉诺·德·博洪（1304—1363）是英格兰贵族女子，生于纳尔斯伯勒城堡，父亲是第四代赫里福德伯爵汉弗莱·德·博洪，母亲是爱德华一世之女鲁德兰的伊丽莎白。她幼年父母双亡，由姑母伍德斯托克的玛丽在埃姆斯伯里修道院抚养成人。

1327年她嫁给第一代奥蒙德伯爵詹姆斯·巴特勒；巴特勒死后，她于1343年改嫁托马斯·达格沃思，后者1352年在布列塔尼遭遇伏击身亡。她于1363年10月7日去世。

James Butler, 1st Earl of Ormond (1304–1338), was an Anglo-Irish noble, born at Arklow in County Wicklow, the son of Edmund Butler, Earl of Carrick. In 1325 he inherited his family's estates and the hereditary office of Chief Butler of Ireland.

In 1327 he married Eleanor de Bohun, a granddaughter of Edward I and cousin of Edward III, who created him Earl of Ormond in 1328 with palatine rights in Tipperary. He campaigned in Scotland in 1335 and died at Gowran, County Kilkenny, in January 1338.

James Butler, 2nd Earl of Ormond (1331–1382) was the son of the 1st Earl and Eleanor de Bohun, and a great-grandson of Edward I. After his father's death he was given in ward, and in 1346 he married Elizabeth Darcy.

He served repeatedly as Lord Justice of Ireland and from 1364 as deputy to Lionel of Antwerp, Duke of Clarence. In 1362 he defeated the MacMurroughs at Teigstaffen, killing six hundred. He died at Knocktopher Castle in October 1382 and was buried in St Canice's Cathedral, Kilkenny.

en:
Alexander Narimuntovich (born c. 1320) was a Lithuanian Gediminid prince, grandson of Gediminas and son of Narimantas. His career belongs to Lithuania's reach into Novgorod's northern lands.

In 1331 Gediminas detained Novgorod's archbishop-elect crossing Lithuania for consecration, releasing him only after the Novgorodians promised Narimantas several border towns. Around 1335 Narimantas left, and Alexander stayed on as his lieutenant until he was recalled in 1338 as Swedish attacks threatened the Neva.

He may have been captured by the Swedes in 1348 and may have died before the later fourteenth century. The Ruzhinsky princely family later claimed descent from him, a claim some modern researchers dispute.

亚历山大·纳里曼托维奇（约1320年生）是立陶宛格迪米纳斯家族王公，格迪米纳斯之孙、纳里曼塔斯之子。他的经历属于立陶宛势力伸入诺夫哥罗德北境的那段历史。

1331年，诺夫哥罗德当选大主教途经立陶宛受任圣职时被格迪米纳斯扣留，直到诺夫哥罗德人答应把数座边境城镇交给纳里曼塔斯才得放行。约1335年纳里曼塔斯离开，留下亚历山大在当地担任总督；1338年瑞典人进犯涅瓦河一带，他被召回。

他可能在1348年被瑞典俘虏，也可能在14世纪后半叶前去世。鲁任斯基王公家族后来自称是他的后裔，一些现代研究者对此存疑。

en:
Anangabhima Deva III ruled the Eastern Ganga empire of Orissa from 1211 to 1238, holding lands from the Ganga to the Godavari. He drove the Muslim rulers of Bengal from his kingdom. His Brahman general Vishnu captured the Kalachuri king Pratapmalla and won western lands, and Anangabhima married his daughter to the Kalachuri prince in alliance.

A devotee of Jagannath, he declared the god supreme ruler and himself the god's servant, and built a shrine at Srikurmam. He was succeeded by his son Narasimha Deva I.

Bhanu Deva II ruled the Eastern Ganga kingdom of Orissa from 1306 to 1328, succeeding Narasimha Deva II, as the Delhi Sultanate reached his borders. When Prince Ulugh Khan, the future Muhammad bin Tughlaq, destroyed the Kakatiya kingdom of Warangal in 1323, Bhanu backed its king.

In 1324 Ulugh Khan retaliated, raiding Jajnagar and capturing Rajamundry, routing Bhanu's army and carrying off forty or fifty war elephants to Delhi. Bhanu died in 1328 and was succeeded by his son Narasimha Deva III.

zh:
巴努·提婆二世于1306至1328年统治奥里萨的东恒伽王国，上接那罗辛哈·提婆二世，在位时德里苏丹国的势力已逼近边境。1323年，王子乌卢格汗（即后来的穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克）攻灭瓦朗加尔的卡卡提亚王国，巴努出兵支持卡卡提亚国王。

1324年乌卢格汗报复性入侵，劫掠贾杰纳加尔、夺取拉贾蒙德里，击溃巴努的军队，将四五十头战象掳往德里。巴努于1328年去世，其子那罗辛哈·提婆三世继位。

en:
Narasimha Deva I, known as Langula Narasimha, ruled the Eastern Ganga kingdom of Kalinga from 1238 to 1264, succeeding his father Anangabhima Deva III. He took the offensive against the Mamluk rulers of Bengal, drove the Muslim forces back to the Padma River and secured Orissa's northern frontier for a century, while in the south he humbled the Kakatiya king.

From 1246 he used the title Gajapati, lord of elephants. He built the Sun Temple at Konark, along with other temples and the great fort at Raibania.

那罗辛哈·提婆一世（别称朗古拉·那罗辛哈）于1238至1264年统治羯陵伽的东恒伽王国，继父阿南伽毗摩·提婆三世之位。他主动出击孟加拉的马木留克统治者，把穆斯林军队逐回博多河，使奥里萨北境安靖百年，在南方则使卡卡提亚国王屈服。

他自1246年起使用意为“象主”的加贾帕蒂称号，并修建了科纳克太阳神庙及其他寺院与赖巴尼亚大要塞。

en:
Narasimha Deva II ruled the Eastern Ganga kingdom of Kalinga from 1279 to 1306, succeeding his father Bhanu Deva I. Still a child at his accession, he reigned for about twelve years under the regency of the Vaishnava scholar and minister Narahari Tirtha.

Narahari Tirtha, a disciple of Madhvacharya, spread Dvaita teaching in Kalinga. Building work continued under Narasimha on the Atharanala bridge at Puri. His son Bhanu Deva II succeeded him.

en:
Malise V (Gaelic Maol Íosa, died c. 1357) was the last native Gaelic earl of Strathearn, succeeding his father Malise IV in 1329. After Earl Magnus died, he also inherited the Norwegian jarldom of Orkney, including Caithness.

He commanded the third division of the Scottish army against Edward Balliol at the Battle of Halidon Hill in 1333, and was afterwards forfeited, with Strathearn granted to the Earl of Surrey. Acquitted of treason in the 1340s, he never recovered the earldom, which David II gave to his nephew Maurice de Moravia in 1344.

马利兹五世（盖尔语作莫尔·伊奥萨，约1357年卒）是最后一位本土盖尔裔斯特拉森伯爵，1329年继承父亲马利兹四世之位。奥克尼伯爵马格努斯死后，他又继承了挪威的奥克尼雅尔领，辖地包括凯斯内斯。

1333年，他在哈里登山战役中指挥苏格兰军第三师抗击爱德华·巴里奥，战后被剥夺爵位，斯特拉森被封给萨里伯爵。1340年代他被判叛国罪名不成立，却未能取回伯爵领，大卫二世于1344年将其封给外甥莫里斯·德·莫里亚。

en:
Izz al-Din Gurdanshah, a grandson of the last king of Ormus's old dynasty, was placed on the throne in 1311 when Baha ud-Din Ayaz retired to Qalhat.

War followed with Izz ud-Din Abdul-Aziz, who claimed Ormus for the Ilkhan Öljeitü and besieged it. Seized during a parley and imprisoned in Kish, Gurdanshah escaped, bought peace with a tribute of thirty thousand dirhams, and ruled until his death in 1317. His sons Qutb al-Din Tahmtan and Nizam al-Din Kay Qubad later ruled Ormus.

伊兹丁·古尔丹沙是旧霍尔木兹王朝末代国王之孙，1311年巴哈丁·阿亚兹退居盖勒哈特时被扶上王位。

此后他卷入与伊兹丁·阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹的战争；阿齐兹在伊利汗完者都支持下宣称拥有霍尔木兹并围攻该岛。古尔丹沙在谈判时被擒、囚禁于基什，后成功脱逃，以三万迪拉姆银币换取和平，统治至1317年去世。其子库特卜丁·塔赫姆坦与尼扎姆丁·凯库巴德后来相继统治霍尔木兹。

en:
Qutb al-Din Tahamtan was sultan of Hormuz from 1319 to 1346, succeeding Izz al-Din Kurdan Shah over the island trading kingdom. Under him Hormuz remained the great emporium of the Persian Gulf, its markets linked by sea to India, China and East Africa.

Around 1330 the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta sailed from Oman to Hormuz and met Tahamtan, whom he calls king of the island. He died in 1346 and was followed on the throne by his son Turan Shah.

en:
Shanba ibn Kaiqubad was a prince of Hormuz and a nephew of Tahamtan II. His uncle gave him and his brother Shadi joint rule of Uwāl, but their conflicting interests drove Shanba to Fāl near Shiraz.

After Tahamtan's death in 1346, Shanba returned to Uwāl with an army and killed his nephew Fulan, who had been left to govern the island. The people of Uwāl rose against him, seized his castle and killed him.

en:
Turan Shah ruled the island kingdom of Hormuz as sultan from 1346 to 1377, succeeding his father Qutb al-Din Tahamtan over the Persian Gulf port whose ships traded with India and China.

In Shiraz the poet Hafez names both Tahamtan and his son Turan Shah among the Hormuzi rulers he praised. When Turan Shah died in 1377, after more than thirty years on the throne, the crown passed to his son.

en:
Gottfried von Arnsberg (c. 1285–1363), a younger son of Count Ludwig of Arnsberg, was a canon at Münster before his election as bishop of Osnabrück in 1321. In 1327 he renewed his predecessor's protection charter for Osnabrück's Jews.

In 1349 he left to claim the archbishopric of Bremen, contested by Moritz of Oldenburg in the Bremen Feud. Gottfried entered Bremen in 1350, and his rival's defeat in the Hoya Feud in July 1358 briefly left him unchallenged; he resigned the see in 1359 and died in 1363.

戈特弗里德·冯·阿恩斯贝格（约1285—1363）是阿恩斯贝格伯爵路德维希较年幼的儿子，原为明斯特的法政牧师，1321年当选奥斯纳布吕克主教。1327年，他延续前任的做法，向城中的犹太人重新签发保护文书。

1349年他离开奥斯纳布吕克，去争夺不莱梅大主教之位，与奥尔登堡的莫里茨陷入不莱梅大主教争端。他于1350年进入不莱梅；1358年7月对手在霍亚争端中战败，使他短暂确立权位。1359年他辞去大主教之职，1363年去世。

en:
Jan I the Scholastic (1308/10–1372) was duke of Oświęcim from 1324, only son of Duke Władysław and Euphrosyne of Masovia. Destined for the Church, he had held the scholastership of Kraków from 1321 but left his clerical career to succeed his father.

In February 1327 he did homage to John of Bohemia at Opava with the other Silesian Piasts, and in 1336 was forced to accept the annexation of Racibórz to Troppau. On his death in 1372 the duchy passed to his son Jan II.

扬一世（绰号“学者”，约1308—1372）1324年起任奥斯威辛公爵，是瓦迪斯瓦夫一世与马佐夫舍的欧芙洛齐娜的独子。他自幼被安排走教会道路，1321年受任克拉科夫的教堂司学，但为继承父爵放弃了教士生涯。

1327年2月，他与其他西里西亚皮亚斯特公爵一道在奥帕瓦向波希米亚国王约翰行臣服礼；1336年被迫接受拉齐布日并入奥帕瓦公国。1372年他去世，公爵之位传给儿子扬二世。

en:
Władysław of Oświęcim (1275/1280–1324) was the eldest son of Mieszko I, Duke of Cieszyn, who named him co-ruler in 1290. When Mieszko died in 1315, Władysław received not Cieszyn but the smaller Oświęcim, becoming its first duke and founding the Oświęcim branch of the Silesian Piasts.

He allied with his namesake Władysław the Elbow-high, king of Poland from 1320, and after his death in 1324 his son Jan the Scholastic succeeded him.

奥斯威辛的瓦迪斯瓦夫（1275/1280—1324）是切申公爵梅什科一世的长子，1290年被父亲立为共治者。1315年梅什科去世后，他得到的不是首府切申，而是较小的奥斯威辛，成为第一代奥斯威辛公爵，开创了西里西亚皮亚斯特王朝的奥斯威辛支系。

en:
Ajashiri was a Mongol noble of the Ötchigin lineage, descended from Temüge, youngest brother of Genghis Khan, who held the title Prince of Liao under the Northern Yuan. After Ming forces defeated the Northern Yuan in 1388, he submitted in 1389 and was made the first commander of the Taining Guard.

He later raided the Ming border, and Ming forces attacked the Three Uriankhai Guards in 1391. In 1392 Zhou Xing tried to secure his submission while returning from northern Mongolia.

en:
Jibügen (born c. 1190) was the eldest son of Temüge Otchigin, Genghis Khan's youngest brother, who held the great eastern appanage around the Khingan Mountains. Though expected to succeed his father as head of the Otchigin family, he died before him, around 1225.

His early death meant that when Temüge at last died in 1246, Jibügen's young son Taghachar inherited the appanage; Taghachar's half-brother tried to seize power, and the succession was only secured by the regent Töregene Khatun.

en:
Nayan (c. 1257–1287) was a Borjigin prince of the Yuan dynasty and great-great-grandson of Temüge, Genghis Khan's youngest brother. Lord of the family appanage in Manchuria, he led the eastern princes against Kublai Khan's centralizing reforms, and in 1287 rebelled and sought Kaidu's support.

Kublai, aged seventy-two, campaigned in person and routed Nayan's army on the Liao River. Captured, Nayan was executed without spilling his blood, wrapped in a carpet and trampled to death. A Nestorian, he bore the cross on his standard.

乃颜（约1257—1287）是元朝孛儿只斤氏宗王，成吉思汗幼弟铁木哥斡赤斤的玄孙，领有家族在满洲的封地。因不满忽必烈削弱东道诸王，他于1287年举兵反叛，并暗中联络海都。

七十二岁的忽必烈亲征，在辽河流域击溃乃颜的军队。乃颜被俘后，为不使宗王流血，被裹在毡毯中踩踏处死。他是景教徒，军旗上绘有十字架。

en:
Taghachar (c. 1210–after 1274) became the second prince of the Otchigin appanage in 1246, after the death of his grandfather Temüge, Genghis Khan's youngest brother. His father Jibügen had died earlier, and Töregene Khatun secured his succession against his half-brother's bid for power.

He backed Möngke after Güyük's death, and in 1257 Möngke made him commander against the Southern Song. In the Toluid civil war he was the first prince to hail Kublai as khan and helped rout Ariq Böke in 1261.

en:
Toqto'a (died 14 November 1328) was a Borjigin prince of the Otchigin lineage and a son of the rebel Nayan. After Nayan's fall in 1287 he headed the Otchigin house, and in 1316 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liao, the eastern princes' highest title.

After Gegeen Khan's murder in 1323, he killed more than a hundred kinsmen and seized their herds. In the 1328 succession war he enthroned the child Ragibagh at Shangdu; when the city fell, Toqto'a was put to death.

脱脱（？—1328年11月14日）是元朝孛儿只斤氏宗王，出自斡赤斤家族，是叛王乃颜之子。1287年乃颜败亡后，他继为斡赤斤家族之长，1316年受封辽王，这是东道诸王的最高封号。

en:
Yanashiri was a Mongol prince of the Ötchigin lineage, descended from Temüge, youngest brother of Genghis Khan, and son of Toqto'a, Prince of Liao. In 1329 the Yuan court enfeoffed him as Prince of Liao, heading the family's eastern appanage.

After the Yuan withdrew north in 1368, he and his kinsmen kept faith with the Northern Yuan khan, and in the 1380s he remained one of the most powerful princes in the khan's following.

en:
Tzompantzin was the last Otomi tlatoani (ruler) of Xaltocan, an island city-state in the lakes of the Valley of Mexico, reigning after Paintzin. Xaltocan had long warred with the Nahua city of Cuauhtitlan, until around 1395 its ruler Xaltemoctzin allied with Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco and his Mexica subjects of Tenochtitlan, and the island was conquered.

Tzompantzin fled the ruined city with his people and took refuge at Metztitlan to the north, where he fortified himself and held out against the Tepanecs. The refugees made Metztitlan an independent señorío, the direct successor of the Xaltocan kingdom.

en:
Alvise Forzatè (died 1374) came from one of Padua's leading families, whose rise rested on ties to the Carrara signori: his mother Cubitosa was a Carrara of the Papafava branch, and Giacomo II was his brother-in-law. After Giacomo's murder in 1350 he served his son Francesco I, in 1356 holding Valsugana castles against Louis of Brandenburg.

He sat on commissions handling Padua's border dispute with Venice, and in the war of 1372–1373 defended the Brenta line. After Padua accepted Venice's harsh peace terms, he joined his sons and a nephew in a plot to murder Francesco I and put Marsilio da Carrara in his place.

Betrayed, he was beheaded at the Palazzo della Ragione in January 1374; one source holds that he was innocent, condemned only for his friendship with Marsilio.

阿尔维塞·福尔扎泰（卒于1374年）出身帕多瓦最显赫的家族之一，家族的上升靠的是与卡拉拉僭主的关系：母亲库比托萨是卡拉拉家族帕帕法瓦支系的女儿，雅各布二世是他的内兄弟。1350年雅各布二世被杀后，他效力于其子弗朗切斯科一世，1356年受命镇守瓦尔苏加纳城堡，抵御勃兰登堡的路易。

他参加处理帕多瓦与威尼斯边界争端的委员会，1372至1373年的战争中守卫布伦塔河防线。帕多瓦接受威尼斯的严苛和约后，他与儿子们及一名侄子密谋刺杀弗朗切斯科一世、改立马尔西利奥·达·卡拉拉。

事泄被捕，他于1374年1月在法理宫被斩首；有一种记载认为他是无辜的，只因与马尔西利奥交好而获罪。

en:
Azzo I da Correggio (died 1400) was a condottiero, count of Casalpò from 1341 and lord of Guastalla, the son of Guido IV. He served the Visconti of Milan until he fell out with Luchino Visconti over Guastalla in 1346, and in 1354 led Guardasone in revolt against Milan.

Turning against the Este in 1357, he was imprisoned until 1372, when his son Guido seized Correggio. Gian Galeazzo Visconti took Casalpò in 1397 and destroyed his castle the next year; Azzo died there in 1400.

en:
Bertrando de' Rossi, called juniore (1336–1396), was a nobleman and diplomat of the Rossi family of Parma, son of Bertrando seniore. He led the house with his cousin Rolando, holding Felino, and inherited the family lands when Rolando died without male heirs in 1389.

His standing came from Gian Galeazzo Visconti, whose councillor and testamentary executor he was. He received Milanese citizenship after a diplomatic mission to the French court, and in 1388 the prince had his son Giacomo elected bishop of Verona.

He commissioned finely illuminated missals and books of hours from a Paris workshop; one shows him kneeling before the Virgin in the red of his house. He died at Pavia in 1396, leaving his property to his three sons.

小贝特朗·德·罗西（1336—1396）是帕尔马罗西家族的贵族与外交官，老贝特朗·罗西之子。他与堂兄弟罗兰多共同执掌家族，领有费利诺；1389年罗兰多无男嗣而终，家产尽归贝特朗。

他的地位来自吉安·加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂，既是其顾问，又是其遗嘱执行人。他曾出使法国宫廷并获得米兰公民身份，1388年亲王又促成他的儿子贾科莫当选维罗纳主教。

他向巴黎一间工坊订制装帧精美的弥撒经本与日课经，其中一部绘有他身着家族红色、跪在圣母面前的肖像。1396年他卒于帕维亚，将财产留给三个儿子。

Bertrando de' Rossi, called Senior, was a soldier of Parma's Rossi family, son of Rolando de' Rossi and Agnese Ruggeri. Exiled with his kin by Mastino della Scala at Azzo da Correggio's urging, he returned after Parma passed to the Este and took part in the revolt of 6 April 1345 against Este rule, hoping to give the city to Luchino Visconti.

Defeated, he fled to Milan and died at Cremona that October. By Sara da Camposampiero he left a son, Bertrando (born 1336), and a daughter Caterina.

Filippino (Filippo) Forzatè (born c. 1330) was a Paduan nobleman, son of Enrico Forzatè and nephew of Alvise Forzatè, whose family had risen through its ties to the Carrara lords of Padua. In September 1373 Padua accepted the harsh peace imposed by Venice.

Towards the end of that year he joined his uncle in a plot to murder Francesco I da Carrara and install Marsilio da Carrara. Betrayed by Pietro Salomoni, he was arrested in January 1374 and beheaded with his uncle at the Palazzo della Ragione on 24 January.

en:
Francesco I da Carrara, called il Vecchio (1325–1393), tried to build a state around Padua and lost it to Milan. He became lord in 1350 after his father Giacomo II was murdered, sharing power with his uncle Jacopino until he jailed him over a plot in 1355.

Imperial vicar from 1356, he gained Feltre and Valsugana from Louis I of Hungary in 1360. He lost the war with Venice in 1372–1373 and paid 280,000 ducats, backed Genoa in the War of Chioggia, and bought Treviso in 1384. In 1387 his army under John Hawkwood won Castagnaro against Verona.

But Gian Galeazzo Visconti kept Verona and Vicenza and in 1388 allied with Venice to break Padua. Francesco abdicated for his son Francesco Novello and died a prisoner at Monza in 1393. He gave Petrarch an estate at Arquà.

zh:
弗朗切斯科一世·达·卡拉拉，人称“老者”（1325—1393），试图以帕多瓦为中心建国却败给米兰。1350年父亲雅各布二世遇刺后，他与叔父雅各皮诺共同执政，1355年因阴谋将其下狱。

1356年他成为帝国代理人，1360年从匈牙利国王拉约什一世手中获得费尔特雷、瓦尔苏加纳等地。1372至1373年对威尼斯战败，赔款二十八万杜卡特；基奥贾战争中支持热那亚，1384年买下特雷维索。1387年他的军队在霍克伍德指挥下于卡斯塔尼亚罗战胜维罗纳。

但吉安·加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂独吞维罗纳、维琴察，1388年联合威尼斯瓦解帕多瓦。他退位给儿子弗朗切斯科·诺韦洛，1393年死于蒙扎的囚室。他赠彼特拉克阿尔夸田产。

1356年他成为帝国代理人，1360年从[GetCountry('HUN').GetName]国王拉约什一世手中获得[ShowLocationName('feltre')]、瓦尔苏加纳等地。1372至1373年对威尼斯战败，赔款二十八万杜卡特；[ShowLocationName('chioggia')]战争中支持热那亚，1384年买下[ShowLocationName('treviso')]。1387年他的军队在霍克伍德指挥下于卡斯塔尼亚罗战胜维罗纳。

但吉安·加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂独吞维罗纳、维琴察，1388年联合威尼斯瓦解帕多瓦。他退位给儿子弗朗切斯科·诺韦洛，1393年死于蒙扎的囚室。他赠彼特拉克阿尔夸田产。

en:
Jacopino da Carrara, also called Giacomino, was a Paduan nobleman of the imperial party. Around 1163 he married the wealthy heiress Speronella Dalesmanni; when the emperor's vicar Pagano della Torre abducted her, her kinsmen besieged the fortress and in 1164 defeated Barbarossa's representative, an episode seen as the birth of Padua's free commune.

Jacopino nevertheless stayed loyal to the emperor, and in 1174 he became podestà of Treviso before dying at Padua around 1190.

en:
Giacomo I da Carrara, called the Great (1264–1324), founded Carraresi rule over Padua. A Guelph, he led Padua's war against Verona over Vicenza in 1311. In 1318, under Ghibelline pressure and civic feuding, the aristocracy elected him defensor, protector and governor in perpetuity, making him the city's first signore; Ghibelline exiles returned, while he exiled the poet Albertino Mussato.

When Cangrande I della Scala besieged Padua in 1319, Giacomo temporarily yielded office to Frederick the Fair to save the city and keep it from the Scaligeri. He died in 1324 and was buried at the Church of the Eremitani, leaving one daughter, Taddea.

雅各布一世·达·卡拉拉，人称“伟大者”（1264—1324），是卡拉拉家族统治帕多瓦的开创者。作为圭尔夫派，他于1311年领导帕多瓦为维琴察的归属对维罗纳作战。1318年，面对吉伯林派压力与城内党争，帕多瓦贵族推举他为终身保卫者、保护者兼总督，他由此成为该城第一位僭主；吉伯林派流亡者返城，他则放逐了诗人阿尔贝蒂诺·穆萨托。

1319年坎格兰德一世·德拉·斯卡拉围攻帕多瓦，雅各布为保全城池暂时将职位让给美男子腓特烈，使城市免于落入斯卡拉家族之手。他于1324年去世，葬于埃雷米塔尼教堂，身后只留下女儿塔代娅。

en:
Giacomo II da Carrara (c. 1305–1350), son of Niccolò da Carrara, took Padua by murder. His father's pro-Scaliger coup failed in 1327 and he was captured and sent to Germany. Freed after two years but barred from Padua, he lived in exile until his cousin Ubertino let him return in 1340.

Ubertino, dying in 1345, named Marsilietto Papafava as lord and passed Giacomo over; on the night of 6 May Giacomo killed Marsilietto and was proclaimed signore next morning. He declared an amnesty and let exiles return, tied Padua to Venice, and joined its campaigns at Zara and Capodistria. In 1349 he brought Petrarch to Padua as a cathedral canon.

On 19 December 1350 Guglielmo, an illegitimate son of Giacomo I, stabbed him to death; he was buried in Sant'Agostino under a tomb with an epitaph by Petrarch.

雅各布二世·达·卡拉拉（约1305—1350）是尼科洛·达·卡拉拉之子，靠一场谋杀夺得了帕多瓦。1327年，他父亲支持斯卡拉家族的政变失败，他被俘送往德意志。两年后获释，却不得返回帕多瓦，过着流亡生活，直到1340年堂兄乌贝蒂诺准许他回城。

1345年乌贝蒂诺临终时指定马尔西列托·帕帕法瓦为领主，绕过了雅各布；5月6日夜里，雅各布杀死马尔西列托，次日清晨被宣布为领主。他宣布大赦，允许流亡者返乡，让帕多瓦与威尼斯结盟，并参加了威尼斯收复扎拉和科佩尔的战事。1349年他把彼特拉克请到帕多瓦担任大教堂法政牧师。

1350年12月19日，他被雅各布一世的私生子古列尔莫刺死，葬于圣阿戈斯蒂诺教堂，墓上刻着彼特拉克所作的铭文。

en:
Giberto IV da Correggio (c. 1320–1373) was a condottiero and signore of Correggio, a small lordship squeezed between Este Ferrara and Visconti Milan. In 1344 Obizzo III d'Este knighted him after he saved Obizzo's life against Feltrino Gonzaga, but in 1346 Luchino Visconti took Guastalla from him.

He came to terms with the Visconti in 1354, broke with them in 1361 and joined Charles IV's anti-Visconti league in 1368. In 1372, while Giberto was at Ferrara, his nephew Guido seized Correggio and imprisoned his sons.

Stripped of his lordship, Giberto became a general of Venice against the Carraresi of Padua. Beaten at Lova, he made up for it at Piove di Sacco by capturing Rizzardo di Sambonifacio, and died in Venice in 1373.

吉贝尔托四世·达·科雷焦（约1320—1373）是佣兵首领、科雷焦领主，领地夹在埃斯特的费拉拉与维斯孔蒂的米兰之间。1344年，他从费尔特里诺·贡扎加手下救了奥比佐三世·埃斯特一命，被后者册封为骑士；但1346年卢基诺·维斯孔蒂从他手中夺走瓜斯塔拉。

1354年他与维斯孔蒂和解，1361年又与之决裂，1368年加入查理四世的反维斯孔蒂联盟。1372年，吉贝尔托在费拉拉时，他的侄子圭多夺取科雷焦，囚禁了他的儿子们。

失去领地后，吉贝尔托出任威尼斯将领，对抗帕多瓦的卡拉拉家族。他在洛瓦战败，却在皮奥韦迪萨科俘获里扎尔多·迪·圣博尼法乔挽回颜面，1373年卒于威尼斯。

en:
Guglielmo de' Rossi (c. 1252–1339) was the Guelph soldier of Parma who spent half his life fighting to get back into the city. Son of Giacomo de' Rossi, he married Donella da Carrara of Padua in 1282, served as podestà of Modena, Milan and Lucca, and in 1293 drove the Sanvitale out of Parma.

After Giberto III da Correggio seized Parma in 1303, Guglielmo was repeatedly exiled. He routed Giberto's Ghibellines in 1308 before losing at Torrechiara, and when Giberto switched to the Guelphs without readmitting the exiles, united discontented exiles to take Borgo San Donnino. After Emperor Henry VII died he sought peace, and married his daughter Maddalena to Giberto.

In 1336 Mastino II della Scala's takeover of Parma drove him into exile again, and he died at the Carrara court in Padua in 1339.

古列尔莫·德·罗西（约1252—1339）是帕尔马的圭尔夫派军人，半生都在为重返这座城市而战。他是贾科莫·德·罗西之子，1282年娶帕多瓦的多内拉·达·卡拉拉，曾在摩德纳、米兰和卢卡出任波德斯塔，1293年将圣维塔莱家族逐出帕尔马。

1303年吉贝尔托三世·达·科雷焦夺取帕尔马后，古列尔莫屡遭流放。1308年他击败吉贝尔托的吉伯林派军队，随后在托雷基亚拉落败；吉贝尔托转投圭尔夫派却不让流亡者回城，古列尔莫便联合不满的流亡者夺取博尔戈圣多尼诺。皇帝亨利七世去世后他转而求和，把女儿马达莱娜嫁给吉贝尔托。

1336年马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉接管帕尔马，他再度流亡，1339年在帕多瓦的卡拉拉宫廷去世。

en:
Guido IV da Correggio (died 1345) was a condottiero and signore of Correggio, the son of Giberto III. His career was made in the service of the Scaligeri of Verona: he fought for Cangrande della Scala in the 1328 conquest of Padua, was elected podestà of Verona in 1331, and under Mastino II took Parma in 1335.

In 1341 he and his brother Azzo plotted to take Parma from the Scaligeri and hand it to the Visconti, but the scheme collapsed in a quarrel and Guido occupied Brescello.

He had earlier defended Brescia for the Scaligeri until driven out, and died in 1345. The next year Luchino Visconti took Guastalla from his son Giberto.

圭多四世·达·科雷焦（？—1345）是佣兵首领、科雷焦领主，吉贝尔托三世之子。他的仕途在维罗纳斯卡拉家族麾下起步：1328年随坎格兰德·德拉·斯卡拉参与征服帕多瓦，1331年当选维罗纳波德斯塔，又在马斯蒂诺二世麾下于1335年攻取帕尔马。

1341年，他与兄弟阿佐密谋从斯卡拉家族手中夺取帕尔马、交给维斯孔蒂家族，却因反目而失败，圭多转而占领布雷谢洛。

此前他还曾为斯卡拉家族镇守布雷西亚，直到被逐走。他于1345年去世，次年卢基诺·维斯孔蒂从他的儿子吉贝尔托手中夺走瓜斯塔拉。

en:
Guido da Lozzo was the son of Nicolò da Lozzo. His family held the castle of Lozzo in the Euganean hills.

In 1313 the magistrates of Padua condemned Guido for treason and ordered his image painted in the communal palace as a mark of infamy. The sentence may have followed his father's delivery of the family castle the previous year.

en:
Guidoriccio da Fogliano (c. 1290–1352), a condottiero from Reggio di Lombardia and son of Niccolò da Fogliano, is the rider portrayed in Simone Martini's fresco in Siena's Palazzo Pubblico. Siena hired him in 1327 to attack Pisa and the Aldobrandeschi in the Maremma.

In 1328 he besieged Montemassi, defended by Castruccio Castracani, and took it after seven months. He went on to capture several Sienese border towns and defeat the Pisans at Giuncarico, until the Sienese expelled him in 1333. He went to Reggio and, with his brother Giberto, ousted Azzo Manfredi; two years later the Gonzaga took it and the brothers moved to the Veneto.

He was podestà of Padua and later of Verona, returned to Siena in 1351, and died there the next year and was buried in San Domenico.

圭多里乔·达·福利亚诺（约1290—1352）是生于伦巴第雷焦的佣兵首领，尼科洛·达·福利亚诺之子；锡耶纳市政厅里西莫内·马蒂尼壁画所绘的骑马武将就是他。1327年锡耶纳雇用他，在马雷马进攻比萨和阿尔多布兰德斯基家族。

1328年他围攻由卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼防守的蒙特马西，七个月后攻克，随后又攻占数座边境城镇、在朱恩卡里科击败比萨人，直到1333年被锡耶纳人驱逐。他转往雷焦，与兄弟吉贝尔托赶走阿佐·曼弗雷迪；两年后贡扎加家族攻占该城，兄弟二人迁往威尼托。

他曾任帕多瓦和后来的维罗纳波德斯塔，1351年返回锡耶纳，次年卒于当地，葬于圣多梅尼科教堂。

en:
Anna Gradenigo, also called Isabetta or Elisabetta, was a daughter of the Venetian doge Pietro Gradenigo and Tommasina Morosini. She married Giacomo I da Carrara, the Guelph leader who became the first signore of Padua in 1318; the match won him Venetian citizenship and strengthened his hand in the city's factional strife.

Her daughter Taddea married Mastino II della Scala of Verona in Venice in 1328; a son, Milone, died young. Anna died in 1321, three years before her husband.

Jacopino da Carrara was a Paduan nobleman, the younger son of Niccolò da Carrara and Elena della Torre. In 1327 he was imprisoned for backing Cangrande della Scala of Verona against the Paduan lord Marsilio I. After his release he helped his brother Jacopo II govern.

When Jacopo II was assassinated in December 1350, Jacopino and his nephew Francesco were acclaimed joint lords of Padua. Rivalry over the succession led Francesco to imprison him in 1355, and he died in the fortress of Monselice in 1372.

en:
Marsilio da Carrara (1294–1338) was the Carrara lord who lost Padua to the Scaligeri and took it back. He succeeded his uncle Giacomo I, but when Niccolò da Carrara went over to the Scaliger of Verona, he had to surrender Padua to Cangrande della Scala in 1328. He kept the title of vicar and married Giacomo's daughter Taddea to Mastino II della Scala.

At war with the Papal States, he fought beside Mastino at Brescia in 1330–1331, took the city by treachery and governed it as vicar. In 1332 he had his wife Bartolomea Scrovegni poisoned on suspicion of adultery.

After Cangrande's death, Florence and Venice, worried by Scaliger power, backed him, and he retook Padua in 1337. He died in March 1338, succeeded by his cousin Ubertino.

马尔西利奥·达·卡拉拉（1294—1338）是先把帕多瓦丢给斯卡拉家族、后又夺回的卡拉拉领主。他继叔父雅各布一世成为僭主，但尼科洛·达·卡拉拉叛投维罗纳的斯卡拉家族后，他于1328年被迫把帕多瓦交给坎格兰德·德拉·斯卡拉。他保留代理人头衔，并将雅各布的女儿塔代娅嫁给马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉。

对教皇国作战时，他于1330至1331年与马斯蒂诺攻打布雷西亚，凭借内应夺取该城并出任当地代理人。1332年，他因怀疑妻子巴尔托洛梅亚·斯克罗韦尼不忠而将其毒杀。

坎格兰德死后，佛罗伦萨与担忧斯卡拉家族势力的威尼斯支持他，他于1337年收复帕多瓦。1338年3月他去世，堂弟乌贝蒂诺继位。

en:
Marsilietto Papafava da Carrara (died 1345) came from a minor branch of the Carrara family, nicknamed Papafava, and ruled Padua for only forty-one days. Son of Albertino, he was wounded in the anti-Carrarese revolt of 1325, and was exiled in 1328 on a charge of insulting the imperial vicar.

Recalled when Padua submitted to Cangrande della Scala later that year, he was knighted by Cangrande at Verona and fought at the siege of Monselice in 1337. On 27 March 1345 the dying signore Ubertino named him his heir, passing over Niccolò da Carrara's sons Giacomo and Giacomino, whose revenge Ubertino's vicar feared.

Marsilietto renewed the alliance with Venice on 20 April. On 6 May Giacomo II killed him and took the signoria, claiming it by right of succession.

马尔西列托·帕帕法瓦·达·卡拉拉（卒于1345年）出身卡拉拉家族绰号“帕帕法瓦”的旁支，只统治了帕多瓦四十一天。他是阿尔贝蒂诺之子，1325年在反对卡拉拉家族的暴动中受伤，1328年因被指辱骂帝国代理人而遭放逐。

同年晚些时候帕多瓦归附坎格兰德·德拉·斯卡拉，他被召回并在维罗纳受封骑士，1337年参加蒙塞利切围城战。1345年3月27日，临终的僭主乌贝蒂诺绕过尼科洛·达·卡拉拉的儿子雅各布和贾科米诺，指定他为继承人，乌贝蒂诺的代理人担心这两人报复。

马尔西列托于4月20日续订与威尼斯的同盟。5月6日，雅各布二世杀死了他，以继承权为由夺取僭主之位。

en:
Niccolò da Carrara (1282–1344), son of Ubertino il Vecchio, was a Paduan noble who bet on the Scaligeri of Verona against his own kinsmen who ruled Padua. He began on the other side: in 1320 he helped hold Padua against a Scaliger attack, and in 1322 he was podestà and captain of war at Bologna.

He then followed a pro-Scaliger policy and plotted against his kinsman Marsilio, lord of Padua, in 1327. Marsilio thwarted the plot, jailing Niccolò's friends but leaving him free, and in 1328 gave Padua up to Cangrande della Scala. In 1335 Niccolò became rector of the Guelph party at Parma.

He died at Chioggia in 1344 and was buried in Padua's Sant'Agostino church. His son Giacomo II took power in Padua a year later.

尼科洛·达·卡拉拉（1282—1344）是老者乌贝蒂诺之子，帕多瓦贵族，他把赌注押在维罗纳的斯卡拉家族身上，对抗执掌帕多瓦的亲族。他起初站在另一边：1320年协助抵御斯卡拉家族对帕多瓦的进攻，1322年出任博洛尼亚的波德斯塔兼战争统领。

此后他奉行亲斯卡拉政策，1327年策划反对同族的帕多瓦僭主马尔西利奥。马尔西利奥挫败阴谋，监禁其友人却放过了他，并于1328年把帕多瓦交给坎格兰德·德拉·斯卡拉。1335年，尼科洛成为帕尔马圭尔夫派首领。

1344年他卒于基奥贾，葬于帕多瓦的圣阿戈斯蒂诺教堂。一年后，儿子雅各布二世夺取帕多瓦政权。

en:
Ubertino da Carrara, called Novello or Ubertinello (c. 1301–1345), was Lord of Padua from 1338 until his death. In 1325 he murdered Guglielmo Dente, his family's rival, and after exile in Chioggia returned by force to drive the Dente faction out of Padua.

Succeeding his cousin Marsilio in 1338, he traded Treviso to Venice and was named papal vicar by Benedict XII in 1339. He fought the Scaligeri through shifting alliances, reformed Padua's finances and patronized its university. He died on 29 March 1345, naming Marsilietto Papafava his successor.

乌贝蒂诺·达·卡拉拉，人称“诺韦洛”或“乌贝尔蒂内洛”（约1301—1345），1338年起任帕多瓦领主，直至去世。1325年他刺杀卡拉拉家族的政敌古列尔莫·登特，被流放基奥贾后又武力返回，将登特派逐出帕多瓦。

1338年他继承堂兄马尔西利奥的权位，取得特雷维索后将其让给威尼斯，1339年被教皇本笃十二世任命为教廷代理人。他在不断变换的同盟中与斯卡拉家族作战，整顿帕多瓦财政，并扶持帕多瓦大学。他于1345年3月29日去世，指定马尔西列托·帕帕法瓦为继承人。

Adolf (1300–1327), called the Upright, was the second son of Rudolf I, Duke of Bavaria. After his father died in 1319 he was formally Count Palatine of the Rhine, but his uncle Emperor Louis IV occupied the Palatinate, so Adolf never exercised real rule.

In 1320 he married Irmengard of Oettingen, who bore his son Rupert II in 1325. Adolf died in 1327 and was buried at Schönau Abbey; the 1329 Treaty of Pavia restored the Palatinate to his brothers and son.

Agnes of Hohenstaufen (1176–1204) was the daughter and heiress of Conrad, Count Palatine of the Rhine. To reconcile Staufen and Welf, she was betrothed as a child to Henry, eldest son of Henry the Lion.

When Emperor Henry VI instead planned to wed her to King Philip II of France, her mother Irmengard married the pair in early 1194. From 1195 she ruled the Palatinate with Henry, and bore the future Count Palatine Henry VI and two daughters.

霍亨斯陶芬的阿格尼丝（1176—1204）是莱茵行宫伯爵康拉德的女儿和继承人。为弥合施陶芬与韦尔夫两大家族，她幼年即许配给狮子亨利的长子海因里希。

皇帝亨利六世一度想把她改嫁给法国国王腓力二世，其母伊尔门加德于1194年初为两人完婚。1195年起她与海因里希共同统治行宫领地，生下后来的行宫伯爵海因里希六世和两个女儿。

en:
Anna of Carinthia-Tyrol (c. 1300–1331) was a Meinhardiner princess, daughter of Otto III, Duke of Carinthia and Count of Tyrol, and Euphemia of Silesia-Liegnitz of the Piast dynasty. In 1328 she married Rudolf II, the Wittelsbach Count Palatine of the Rhine.

In September 1329 she gave birth to a daughter, also named Anna, who in 1349 married the future Emperor Charles IV and became queen of Bohemia. Anna died on 31 October 1331 and was buried at Schönau Cistercian Abbey; Rudolf remarried and died blind without a male heir in 1353.

Anne of the Palatinate (1329–1353) was the daughter of Count Palatine Rudolf II and Anna of Carinthia, born at Merano in 1329. On 11 March 1349 she married Charles IV at Bacharach on the Rhine as his second wife.

She was crowned Queen of the Romans at Aachen in July 1349 and later crowned Queen of Bohemia. Her only son Wenceslaus, born in 1350, died in 1351, and Anne herself died on 2 February 1353, aged twenty-three.

en:
Henry the Elder (c. 1173–1227), eldest son of Henry the Lion and Matilda of England, was raised in English exile. Returning in 1189, he defended Brunswick against King Henry VI's forces, and in 1193 married Agnes of Hohenstaufen.

Enfeoffed with the Rhine Palatinate in 1195, he founded the Welf Palatine line. He served Emperor Henry VI in the Sicilian campaign and on Crusade, then backed his brother Otto IV, though he briefly joined Philip of Swabia before returning to Otto.

He ceded the Palatinate to his son Henry in 1213; after his son's early death, he left his Welf hereditary lands to his nephew Otto the Child. He died in April 1227.

Henry VI the Younger of Brunswick (c. 1196–1214) was Count Palatine of the Rhine from 1212. The only son of Count Palatine Henry V and Agnes of Hohenstaufen, he was raised at the English court of his great-uncle King John. In 1212 his father abdicated and he married Mathilde of Brabant.

He backed his uncle Otto IV, then defected to Frederick II. He died childless in 1214 and was buried at Schönau Abbey, the Palatinate passing to Duke Louis I.

en:
Irmengard of Oettingen (c. 1304–1389) was a daughter of Count Louis VI of Oettingen and Agnes of Württemberg. In 1320 she married Adolf the Upright, nominal Count Palatine of the Rhine; his uncle Emperor Louis IV exercised the actual power of government, and Adolf died in 1327.

After his death she retired to the Dominican Liebenau monastery at Worms; the Treaty of Pavia in 1329 secured her young son Rupert II's succession to the Palatinate. She took the veil around 1347 and died at Liebenau in 1389.

en:
Conrad of Hohenstaufen (c. 1135–1195), younger half-brother of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, was the first hereditary Count Palatine of the Rhine. In 1156 Barbarossa granted him the count palatine's dignity, and from about 1160 he was married to Irmengard of Henneberg.

He clashed with the archbishops of Trier and Cologne. As his sons predeceased him, his lands passed through his daughter Agnes to her Welf husband Henry.

en:
Mechtild of Nassau (before 1280–1323) was the youngest daughter of Adolf, King of the Romans, and Imagina of Isenburg-Limburg. In 1294 she married Rudolf I of Bavaria, the Wittelsbach duke who became Count Palatine of the Rhine.

After Rudolf's death in 1319 and the long feud with his brother, Emperor Louis IV, her sons Rudolf II and Rupert I and her grandson Rupert II received the Palatinate under the Treaty of Pavia in 1329. She died at Heidelberg in 1323.

en:
Rudolf II, called the Blind (1306–1353), was Count Palatine of the Rhine. Born at Wolfratshausen to Rudolf I of Wittelsbach and Mechthild of Nassau, he grew up in a family war: after his father's death in 1319, his uncle Emperor Louis IV seized the Palatinate, and the fighting ended only in 1322.

Rudolf and his brother Ruprecht I reconciled with Louis after their mother's death in 1323, and by the Treaty of Pavia in 1329 took over the Palatinate, while Louis and his sons kept Upper Bavaria; Rudolf received Neustadt in the 1338 partition.

In 1349 the brothers backed Günther von Schwarzburg as anti-king, yet Rudolf married his daughter Anna to Charles IV, whom the Wittelsbachs recognized the next year. Illness led him to leave most government to his brother, and he died at Neustadt in 1353, blind in his last year.

鲁道夫二世，绰号“盲人”（1306—1353），是莱茵行宫伯爵。他生于沃尔夫拉茨豪森，是鲁道夫一世·维特尔斯巴赫与拿骚的梅希蒂尔德之子，童年笼罩在家族内战中：1319年父亲去世后，叔父皇帝路德维希四世夺取普法尔茨，战事直到1322年才结束。

1349年兄弟俩支持京特尔·冯·施瓦茨堡为对立国王，但鲁道夫却把女儿安娜嫁给查理四世，维特尔斯巴赫家族于次年承认查理。鲁道夫因病将大部分政务交给弟弟，1353年卒于诺伊施塔特，最后一年已经失明。

en:
Rupert II, called the Hard (1325–1398), was Elector Palatine of the Rhine. Born at Amberg, the elder son of Count Palatine Adolf and Irmengard of Oettingen, he was named heir to his childless uncles Rudolf II and Rupert I by the Treaty of Pavia in 1329 and succeeded Rupert I in 1390.

In 1391 he expelled the Jews from the Palatinate and seized their property, and in 1395 he issued the Rupertine Constitution keeping the Palatinate undivided. Married in 1345 to Beatrice of Sicily, he died at Amberg in 1398.

鲁普雷希特二世，绰号“严厉者”（1325—1398），莱茵普法尔茨选帝侯。他生于安贝格，是莱茵行宫伯爵阿道夫与厄廷根的伊尔门加德的长子；1329年的《帕维亚条约》指定他为无嗣的两位叔父鲁道夫二世与鲁普雷希特一世的继承人，1390年他继承鲁普雷希特一世成为选帝侯。

en:
Rupert I, called the Red (1309–1390), was Count Palatine of the Rhine and then the first Elector Palatine. A son of Rudolf I of Wittelsbach and Mechthild of Nassau, he lost his father at ten. In 1329 he and his brother Rudolf II won the Treaty of Pavia from their uncle Emperor Louis IV, which made the Palatinate a principality of its own; the brothers shared the electoral vote until Rupert became sole count in 1353.

Charles IV's Golden Bull of 1356 guaranteed the Palatinate's vote in imperial elections. In 1376 Rupert received several towns for voting Wenceslaus king.

He founded Heidelberg University in 1386, the third in the Holy Roman Empire. Neither of his two marriages produced an heir. He died at Neustadt in 1390, and his nephew Rupert II succeeded him.

鲁普雷希特一世，绰号“红发”（1309—1390），历任莱茵行宫伯爵、首任普法尔茨选帝侯。他是鲁道夫一世·维特尔斯巴赫与拿骚的梅希蒂尔德之子，十岁丧父。1329年，他与兄长鲁道夫二世从叔父皇帝路德维希四世手中争得《帕维亚条约》，使普法尔茨成为独立的公国；兄弟二人共享选帝侯票，1353年鲁普雷希特成为唯一的行宫伯爵。

查理四世1356年颁布的《金玺诏书》保障了普法尔茨的帝国选帝权。1376年，他因投票选举文策尔为国王而获赐数座城镇。

他于1386年创办海德堡大学，即神圣罗马帝国的第三所大学。他的两次婚姻均无继承人。1390年他卒于诺伊施塔特，由侄子鲁普雷希特二世继位。

Ottobuono de' Fieschi (c. 1205–1276), son of Tedisio Fieschi of Lavagna, became a papal chaplain and in 1251 was made Cardinal Deacon of San Adriano by his uncle Pope Innocent IV.

Clement IV sent him to England in 1265 to reconcile Henry III with his barons and preach the Crusades, and he stayed until 1268. In 1268 he issued canons that became a foundation of English church law.

Elected pope as Adrian V in July 1276 through Charles I of Anjou, he died at Viterbo that August, unordained, after only thirty-eight days, having suspended Gregory X's conclave rules. Dante places him among the avaricious in Purgatory.

奥托博诺·德·菲耶斯基（约1205—1276）是拉瓦尼亚的泰迪西奥·菲耶斯基之子，成为教宗随侍神父，1251年被叔父依诺增爵四世任命为圣亚德堂枢机执事。

克勉四世于1265年派他出使英格兰，调解亨利三世与贵族的纠纷并宣讲十字军，他一直留任到1268年。1268年他颁布教规，成为英格兰教会法的基础。

1276年7月经安茹的查理推动，他当选教宗，称阿德里安五世，但仅在位三十八天，尚未领受司铎圣职便在8月卒于维泰博，生前已暂停格列高利十世有关秘密会议的规章。但丁在《神曲·炼狱篇》中将他置于贪财者之中。

en:
Jacques Fournier (c. 1285–1342), born at Saverdun in the County of Foix, joined the Cistercians and became Abbot of Fontfroide in 1311. As Bishop of Pamiers from 1317 he hunted the last Cathars of Languedoc; his inquiry led to the burning of Guillaume Bélibaste in 1321, and his Montaillou inquiries filled the Fournier Register.

A cardinal from 1327, he kept wearing his Cistercian cowl and was nicknamed the white cardinal. Elected pope at Avignon in 1334 as Benedict XII, third of the Avignon popes, he could not move the court to Rome and built the great papal palace at Avignon instead.

He reformed the monastic orders, opposed nepotism and settled John XXII's beatific vision dispute with the bull Benedictus Deus, but could not bring Emperor Louis IV to terms. He died in April 1342 and was buried at Avignon.

雅克·富尼耶（约1285—1342）生于富瓦伯国的萨韦尔丹，加入西多会，1311年任丰特弗鲁瓦德修道院院长。1317年起任帕米耶主教，大力清剿朗格多克残余的清洁派；经他调查，纪尧姆·贝利巴斯特于1321年被火刑处死，他在蒙塔尤的调查则记满了《富尼耶登记册》。

1327年他升任枢机，仍穿着西多会会袍，得了“白衣枢机”的绰号。1334年他在阿维尼翁当选教宗，称本笃十二世，是第三任阿维尼翁教宗；他无法把教廷迁回罗马，便动工兴建阿维尼翁教皇宫。

他改革各修会、反对裙带关系，颁布《赞美天主》诏书了结若望二十二世的荣福直观之争，却没能与皇帝路德维希四世达成和解。1342年4月他去世，葬于阿维尼翁。

en:
Pope Benedict XI (1240–1304), born Niccolò Boccasini in Treviso, was a Dominican who studied in Venice and Milan. He was twice provincial prior of Lombardy, elected master general of the order in 1296 and made a cardinal in 1298.

He was at Pope Boniface VIII's side when French troops seized the pope at Anagni in 1303. Elected pontiff in October 1303, he lifted Boniface's excommunication of Philip IV but in June 1304 excommunicated Philip's minister Guillaume de Nogaret.

He had served as papal legate to Hungary and France, and brokered a French-English armistice. He died at Perugia in July 1304 after eight months as pope.

en:
Pedro Martínez de Luna (1328–1423), known as Papa Luna, was an Aragonese noble and canon lawyer, the last claimant of the Avignon papacy in the Western Schism. He studied law at Montpellier; Gregory XI made him a cardinal in 1375.

After Clement VII's death the Avignon cardinals elected him pope in 1394 as Benedict XIII. France withdrew obedience in 1398 and besieged him at Avignon for five years until his escape in 1403. He refused Gregory XII's proposal that both resign, and the 1409 Council of Pisa only added a third.

The Council of Constance deposed him in 1417, leaving only Aragon on his side. He held out in Peníscola castle until his death on 23 May 1423, still claiming the papacy.

佩德罗·马丁内斯·德·卢纳（1328—1423），人称“卢纳教皇”，是阿拉贡贵族、教会法学者，也是西方教会大分裂中阿维尼翁一系最后的重要教宗人选。他曾在蒙彼利埃学习法律，1375年被格列高利十一世任命为枢机。

克勉七世去世后，阿维尼翁的枢机们于1394年选举他为教皇，称本笃十三世。1398年法国撤回承认并围困阿维尼翁教皇宫五年，他于1403年逃脱。他拒绝格列高利十二世提出的双方同时退位之议，1409年比萨公会议反而又选出第三位教宗。

1417年康斯坦茨公会议废黜他，此时只有阿拉贡还支持他。他退守佩尼伊斯科拉城堡，1423年5月23日在那里去世，至死仍自称教皇。

en:
Gian Lorenzo Bernini (1598–1680) was the sculptor and architect who gave Rome its Baroque face, credited with creating the Baroque style. Born in Naples, he moved to Rome in 1606 with his father, Pietro Bernini, and under Cardinal Borghese made four masterpieces in 1619–1625, including Apollo and Daphne.

Urban VIII made him architect of St Peter's, where he raised the nearly 30-metre bronze Baldacchino over the tomb. When cracks appeared under the bell tower, enemies led by Borromini blamed him, and after Urban VIII's death Innocent X had it demolished in 1646; Bernini answered with the Four Rivers Fountain and Cornaro Chapel, where the Ecstasy of Saint Teresa is staged as theatre.

Under Alexander VII he built St Peter's Square colonnades, the Cathedra Petri and the Scala Regia. His 1665 Louvre designs were rejected; working until two weeks before a stroke, he was buried at Santa Maria Maggiore.

吉安·洛伦佐·贝尼尼（1598—1680）是雕塑家、建筑师，赋予罗马以巴洛克面貌，被认为创立了巴洛克风格。他生于那不勒斯，1606年随父亲彼得罗·贝尼尼迁居罗马，在博尔盖塞红衣主教庇护下于1619—1625年完成四件杰作，其中有《阿波罗与达芙妮》。

乌尔班八世任他为圣彼得大教堂建筑师，他在墓上立起近30米高的青铜华盖。钟楼出现裂缝后，以博罗米尼为首的对手归咎于他，乌尔班八世去世后英诺森十世于1646年下令拆除钟楼；贝尼尼以《四河喷泉》和科尔纳罗小堂作答，《圣特雷莎的狂喜》在其中如戏剧般上演。

亚历山大七世时期，他建造圣彼得广场的柱廊、圣彼得宝座和王室阶梯。1665年他的卢浮宫设计方案被否决；他一直工作到中风前两周，葬于圣母大殿。

乌尔班八世任他为圣彼得大教堂建筑师，他在墓上立起近30米高的青铜华盖。钟楼出现裂缝后，以博罗米尼为首的对手归咎于他，乌尔班八世去世后英诺森十世于1646年下令拆除钟楼；贝尼尼以《四河喷泉》和科尔纳罗小堂作答，《圣特雷莎的狂喜》在其中如戏剧般上演。

亚历山大七世时期，他建造圣彼得广场的柱廊、圣彼得宝座和王室阶梯。1665年他的卢浮宫设计方案被否决；他一直工作到中风前两周，葬于圣母大殿。

en:
Bertoldo Orsini was a Roman nobleman, brother of Matteo Rosso Orsini, who served as podestà of Viterbo in 1259, Lucca in 1262, Messina in 1269 and Orvieto in 1278.

In 1278 Pope Nicholas III named him count of Romagna and governor of Bologna. Hostile to the Annibaldeschi faction, he spent a period of exile at Palestrina, governed Spoleto from 1298 and died in 1319.

贝尔托尔多·奥尔西尼是罗马贵族，马泰奥·罗索·奥尔西尼之弟，曾先后任维泰博（1259年）、卢卡（1262年）、墨西拿（1269年）和奥尔维耶托（1278年）的长官。

1278年，教皇尼古拉三世任命他为罗马涅伯爵兼博洛尼亚总督。因与安尼巴尔代斯基家族为敌，他曾一度被逐，避居帕莱斯特里纳，1298年起任斯波莱托总督，1319年去世。

en:
Pope Boniface VIII (c. 1230–1303), born Benedetto Caetani, was pope from 1294 and put forward some of the strongest claims to temporal as well as spiritual power. A younger son of the baronial Caetani family, he entered the Curia in 1264, became a cardinal in 1281, and was elected after Celestine V abdicated. In 1297 he stripped the Colonna cardinals of their rank and excommunicated them, and by 1298 his troops had razed Palestrina.

In 1300 he proclaimed the first jubilee year in Rome. His quarrel with Philip IV of France over taxing the clergy began with Clericis laicos in 1296, and in 1302 he answered with Unam sanctam, declaring kings subject to the Roman pontiff.

On 7 September 1303 Nogaret and Sciarra Colonna attacked him at Anagni; Colonna allegedly slapped him, the schiaffo di Anagni. Freed after three days, he died in Rome on 11 October.

教皇卜尼法斯八世（约1230—1303），本名本尼狄克·卡埃塔尼，1294年起任教皇，对世俗与精神权力提出了教皇史上最强的主张。他是卡埃塔尼男爵家族的幼子，1264年进入教廷，1281年受任枢机，雷定五世退位后当选。1297年他革除科隆纳家族枢机的职位并处以绝罚，到1298年其军队已将帕莱斯特里纳夷为平地。

1300年他在罗马首创圣年。他与法王腓力四世围绕向教士征税的冲突始于1296年的《教士不纳税》谕令，1302年又以《唯一至圣》通谕作答，宣称君王都服从罗马教宗。

1303年9月7日，诺加雷与夏拉·科隆纳在阿纳尼袭击他，传说科隆纳掴了他一记耳光，史称“阿纳尼耳光”。三天后他获救，10月11日在罗马去世。

en:
Guy of Burgundy, son of Count William I of Burgundy, became archbishop of Vienne in 1088 and led French resistance to Emperor Henry V over lay investiture; his 1112 council at Vienne condemned the practice and excommunicated Henry.

Elected pope at Cluny in 1119 as Callixtus II, he issued the bull Sicut Judaeis in 1120, protecting the Jews from forced conversion and violence.

His chief achievement was ending the Investiture Controversy through the Concordat of Worms in 1122, confirmed at the First Lateran Council in 1123. He died in Rome on 13 December 1124.

勃艮第的居伊是勃艮第伯爵威廉一世之子，1088年出任维埃纳大主教，率领法国教士反抗皇帝亨利五世的俗人授职主张；1112年他在维埃纳召集的会议谴责俗人授职并将亨利逐出教会。

1119年他在克吕尼当选教皇，称加里斯都二世，1120年颁布《犹太人保护通谕》，禁止强迫犹太人改宗和施暴。

他最大的成就是1122年签订《沃尔姆斯宗教协定》结束叙任权之争，1123年第一次拉特朗大公会议予以确认。1124年12月13日他在罗马去世。

en:
Giacinto Bobone was born around 1106 into the noble Orsini branch of Rome's Bobone family. He studied under Peter Abelard and defended him at the 1140 Council of Sens, and became a cardinal deacon in 1144.

Elected pope in 1191 at about eighty-five, he took the name Celestine III and crowned Henry VI Holy Roman Emperor. In 1192 he confirmed the Teutonic Order, and in 1195 he quashed Philip II of France's repudiation of his wife Ingeborg. He died in 1198.

en:
Bertrand de Got (c. 1264–1314), born to a Gascon family, studied law and became Archbishop of Bordeaux in 1297. As archbishop he was an English subject but a friend of Philip IV of France.

Elected pope in 1305 as Clement V, he transferred the papal court from Rome to Avignon in 1309, opening the Avignon Papacy. Yielding to Philip IV, he moved against the Knights Templar, allowed the execution of many of its members and suppressed the order. He repressed the Dulcinians in Lombardy as heretics, issued the Clementine Constitutions in 1313 and died on 20 April 1314.

en:
Pierre Roger (1291–1352), born at Maumont in the Limousin, entered the Benedictine abbey of La Chaise-Dieu as a boy and became a theology master in Paris in 1323. He rose from Abbot of Fécamp in 1326 to Archbishop of Sens in 1329 and Archbishop of Rouen in 1330, and was made a cardinal in 1338, serving Philip VI as councillor and diplomat.

Elected pope at Avignon in May 1342, he took the name Clement VI and deepened French dominance of the Church. He added a chapel to the Papal Palace and kept composers such as Philippe de Vitry about him.

In 1348, as the Black Death struck, he condemned the pogroms against the Jews and granted remission of sins to plague victims. He died on 6 December 1352, remembered as a munificent prince, but no saint, and was buried at La Chaise-Dieu.

皮埃尔·罗歇（1291—1352）生于利穆赞的莫蒙，少年时进入本笃会的拉谢斯迪约修道院，1323年在巴黎成为神学硕士。他1326年任费康修道院院长，此后历任桑斯大主教（1329年）和鲁昂大主教（1330年），1338年受任枢机，以顾问和外交官身份效力于腓力六世。

1342年5月他在阿维尼翁当选教宗，称克雷芒六世，加深了法国对教会的支配。他在教宗宫增建一座礼拜堂，身边常有菲利普·德·维特里等作曲家。

黑死病袭来的1348年，他下诏谴责迫害犹太人的暴行，并为染疫而死者颁赐罪罚大赦。1352年12月6日他去世，人们记得他是一位慷慨的君侯，却算不上圣人，遗体安葬在拉谢斯迪约。

en:
Domenico Fontana (1543–1607) was born at Melide on Lake Lugano and settled in Rome in 1563, working his way up from plasterer to master builder. In 1584 Cardinal Montalto entrusted him with building the Chapel of the Manger in Santa Maria Maggiore.

When Montalto became Pope Sixtus V in 1585, Fontana was named architect of St Peter's and added the lantern to Michelangelo's dome. In 1586 he famously moved the ancient Vatican obelisk into St Peter's Square and re-erected three other Roman obelisks.

After Sixtus died he fell from favour and in 1592 moved to Naples, where he served the Spanish viceroy until his death on 28 June 1607.

多梅尼科·丰塔纳（1543—1607）生于卢加诺湖畔的梅利德，1563年定居罗马，从灰泥工一路做到营造师。1584年，蒙塔尔托红衣主教委托他在圣母大殿修建圣诞小堂。

蒙塔尔托于1585年成为教宗西斯都五世后，丰塔纳被任命为圣彼得大教堂建筑师，为米开朗基罗设计的穹顶加装灯笼顶。1586年，他将古老的梵蒂冈方尖碑迁至圣彼得广场，又在罗马城重新竖立另外三座方尖碑，轰动一时。

西斯都五世去世后他失宠，1592年前往那不勒斯为西班牙总督效力，1607年6月28日在当地去世。

en:
Francesco Petrarca (1304–1374), known as Petrarch, was an Italian poet and scholar and the first great figure of Renaissance humanism. Born at Arezzo, he grew up at Avignon, where his family followed the papal court. His father made him study law, but he cared only for writing and the classics.

In 1327 he saw a woman named Laura in the church of Sainte-Claire, beginning a lifelong love celebrated in the Canzoniere, whose sonnets were imitated across Europe. His Latin epic Africa made him a celebrity, and in 1341 he was crowned poet laureate in Rome, only the second since antiquity.

In 1345 at Verona he found Cicero's letters, credited with starting Renaissance humanism. He coined the idea of a “dark age” after antiquity, settled at Arquà about 1368 and died there in 1374. His will left Boccaccio fifty florins for a winter dressing gown.

弗朗切斯科·彼特拉克（1304—1374）是意大利诗人与学者，文艺复兴人文主义的第一位大家。他生于阿雷佐，在阿维尼翁长大，家人随教廷迁居。父亲逼他学法律，他却只爱写作和古典作品。

1327年，他在圣克莱尔教堂见到名叫劳拉的女子，由此开始贯穿一生的恋情，并写入《歌集》，其中的十四行诗被全欧洲仿效。拉丁语史诗《阿非利加》使他名声大噪，1341年他在罗马加冕为桂冠诗人，是古典时代以来第二位获此殊荣者。

1345年他在维罗纳发现西塞罗的书信，常被视为人文主义的起点。他提出古代与当世之间存在“黑暗时代”的看法，约1368年迁居阿尔夸，1374年在那里去世，遗嘱留给薄伽丘50弗罗林买一件暖和的冬睡袍。

en:
Gerald Odonis (1285–1349), born at Camboulit, joined the Franciscans at Figeac and taught theology at Toulouse and Paris. His order was split over poverty: John XXII had deposed Michael of Cesena in 1328, and in 1329 the Paris general chapter, siding with the pope, elected Gerald Minister General.

In 1331 he represented John at Naples, where King Robert and Queen Sancia protected the strict adherents of poverty. On 18 December 1333 he defended John's teaching on the beatific vision at Paris. In 1337 he pushed his Benedictine constitutions through the Cahors chapter, and kept sending missionaries to Persia, Malabar and China.

In 1342 Clement VI made him Patriarch of Antioch and Bishop of Catania. When the Black Death reached Messina in 1347, Catania would not let St Agatha's relics go, so he dipped them in water and carried the water there himself. He died of the plague in 1349.

杰拉尔德·奥多尼斯（1285—1349）生于康布利，在菲雅克加入方济各会，曾在图卢兹和巴黎教授神学。修会因贫穷之争分裂：若望二十二世1328年罢免切塞纳的米凯莱，1329年巴黎全体大会站在教宗一边，选举他为修会总会长。

1331年他代表教宗前往那不勒斯，国王罗贝托与王后桑查在当地庇护坚持严格守贫的一派。1333年12月18日他在巴黎为教宗的荣福直观主张辩护，1337年在卡奥尔大会上通过“本笃会宪”，并不断向波斯、马拉巴尔和中国派遣传教士。

1342年克雷芒六世任命他为安条克牧首兼卡塔尼亚主教。1347年黑死病传到墨西拿时，卡塔尼亚人不肯交出圣阿加莎的圣髑，他便把圣髑浸入水中，亲自将这水带往墨西拿，1349年他死于瘟疫。

en:
Gil de Albornoz (1302/1303–1367), born at Carrascosa del Campo, was a Castilian churchman and soldier. He studied law and became Archbishop of Toledo in 1338. He fought the Marinid invasion at Río Salado in 1340.

After Alfonso XI died in 1350 he left Castile and never returned; Clement VI made him a cardinal. Innocent VI named him grand penitentiary with the epithet 'Angel of Peace', a title his campaigns soon made ironic.

Sent to Italy in 1353 to restore papal authority, he led mercenary armies in two campaigns and extended the Papal States. His Constitutiones Sanctae Matris Ecclesiae regulated their administration until 1816, and he died in 1367.

en:
Giordano Orsini, called del Monte (died 1367), was a Roman baron of the Orsini di Monterotondo branch and lord of Monterotondo and Marino. He sat as senator of Rome repeatedly from 1339 to 1353, and in 1341 he crowned Petrarch with the laurel on the Capitol.

When Cola di Rienzo seized power in 1347, Giordano was almost the only Roman baron to back the tribune: he knighted him, was made console and patrician, and in the street fighting led his cavalry against the Colonna. He abandoned Cola in 1348 and was besieged by his troops at Marino.

From 1352 he served Cardinal Gil de Albornoz as rector of the Patrimonio, campaigning against the prefect Giovanni di Vico; he had forced Vico's surrender at Vetralla in 1347. He headed the Monte Giordano line, which tradition names as the source of the name of the Roman hill.

焦尔达诺·奥尔西尼，又称德尔蒙特（1367年卒），是奥尔西尼家族蒙特罗通多支系的罗马男爵，领有蒙特罗通多与马里诺。他于1339至1353年间多次出任罗马元老，1341年在卡皮托利尼为彼特拉克戴上桂冠。

1347年科拉·迪·里恩佐夺取政权时，焦尔达诺是几乎唯一支持这位护民官的罗马贵族：他册封科拉为骑士，受任执政官和贵族，并在巷战中率骑兵攻打科隆纳家族。1348年他背弃科拉，被其军队围困在马里诺。

1352年起，他任枢机吉尔·德·阿尔沃诺斯麾下的圣彼得遗产长官，征讨郡守乔瓦尼·迪·维科，1347年迫使维科在韦特拉拉投降。他是蒙特焦尔达诺支系的首领，传说罗马的蒙特焦尔达诺丘便因他得名。

en:
Pierre Roger de Beaufort (c. 1329–1378), born at Maumont in the Limousin, was the nephew of Pope Clement VI, who made him a cardinal in 1348 at about eighteen. He studied at Perugia and became a skilled canonist.

Elected pope at Avignon on 30 December 1370, he took the name Gregory XI and was the seventh and last Avignon pope. He waged the War of the Eight Saints against Florence, placing the city under interdict in March 1376.

Catherine of Siena came to Avignon to urge his return, and on 17 January 1377 he entered Rome, ending nearly seventy years of papal residence at Avignon. He died on 27 March 1378. Urban VI was elected to succeed him and a rival pope emerged at Avignon, beginning the Western Schism, not fully healed until the Council of Constance.

Elected pope at [ShowLocationName('avignon')] on 30 December 1370, he took the name Gregory XI and was the seventh and last Avignon pope. He waged the War of the Eight Saints against Florence, placing the city under interdict in March 1376.

Catherine of [ShowLocationName('siena')] came to Avignon to urge his return, and on 17 January 1377 he entered Rome, ending nearly seventy years of papal residence at Avignon. He died on 27 March 1378. Urban VI was elected to succeed him and a rival pope emerged at Avignon, beginning the Western Schism, not fully healed until the Council of Constance.

皮埃尔·罗歇·德·博福尔（约1329—1378）生于利穆赞的莫蒙，是教宗克雷芒六世的侄子，1348年约十八岁时被叔父册封为枢机。他在佩鲁贾求学，成为精通教会法的学者。

1370年12月30日他在阿维尼翁当选教宗，称格里高利十一世，是第七位也是最后一位阿维尼翁教宗。他对佛罗伦萨发动“八圣之战”，1376年3月对该城处以禁罚。

锡耶纳的凯瑟琳亲赴阿维尼翁促其返回罗马，1377年1月17日他进入罗马，结束了教廷居留阿维尼翁近七十年的历史。1378年3月27日他去世，乌尔巴诺六世当选后继任者，阿维尼翁出现对立教宗，西方教会大分裂就此开始，直到康斯坦茨公会议才完全解决。

en:
Gregory XII (c. 1327–1417), born Angelo Correr into a Venetian noble family, became bishop of Castello in 1380 and a cardinal in 1405.

Elected pope in 1406 at about eighty, he took office on condition he resign if the Avignon claimant Benedict XIII did the same, ending the schism that had split the Church since 1378. Talks with Benedict went nowhere, and in 1409 the Council of Pisa chose a third claimant; Gregory, holding Rome, recognised none.

In 1415 he freely resigned at the Council of Constance, the last pope to do so until Benedict XVI in 2013. The council made him a cardinal bishop and legate for life. He died at Recanati in 1417, the year Martin V was elected and the schism ended.

Guillaume Court (c. 1290–1361), born at Belpech, was a Cistercian theologian who received a doctorate in theology in 1319. He aided his uncle, the inquisitor Jacques Fournier, in the heresy trials at Montaillou.

When Fournier became Benedict XII, he made Court Bishop of Nîmes in 1337 and raised him to cardinal in 1338. Called the white cardinal, probably for the Cistercian robe he wore, he sat in the conclaves of 1342 and 1352 and served as legate in Lombardy.

In 1354 he headed the Avignon tribunal that cleared Joannes de Rupescissa, ordered to write the Book of Secret Events; two others were condemned and burned. He died at Avignon on 12 June 1361.

富尼耶成为本笃十二世后，1337年任命他为尼姆主教，1338年擢升他为枢机。他人称“白衣枢机”，大概因穿西多会会袍而得名，参加了1342年和1352年两次秘密会议，曾任伦巴第特使。

1354年他主持阿维尼翁宗教法庭，为曾奉命撰写《隐秘事件之书》的让·德·罗克塔亚德平反，另两人则被判有罪烧死。1361年6月12日，他卒于阿维尼翁。

en:
Hélie de Talleyrand-Périgord was born at Périgueux in 1301, the third son of Count Elias VII of Périgord, and was destined for the Church. He became a leading cardinal of the Avignon papacy: at the 1334 conclave he headed the French cardinals resolved to keep the Curia in Avignon, against Napoleone Orsini's party demanding a return to Rome, and the election went to Benedict XII.

Cardinal-bishop of Albano from 1348 and a papal diplomat in the Hundred Years' War, he became dean of the College of Cardinals in 1361. After Innocent VI died in 1362, the cardinals split between Hélie and Guy of Boulogne and settled on an outsider, who became Urban V.

In 1363 Urban named Hélie legate for the crusade against the Turks planned by John II of France and Peter I of Cyprus. He died in January 1364, before it set out.

埃利·德·塔列朗-佩里戈尔1301年生于佩里格，是佩里戈尔伯爵埃利七世的第三子，自幼被安排走上教会道路。他成为阿维尼翁教廷的核心枢机：1334年的教皇选举中，他率领法国枢机一派坚持把教廷留在阿维尼翁，对手是要求回归罗马的拿破仑·奥尔西尼一派，结果本笃十二世当选。

他1348年起任阿尔巴诺枢机主教，百年战争期间充当教皇的使节斡旋，1361年出任枢机团团长。1362年英诺森六世去世后，枢机们分成支持他和支持布洛涅的居伊的两派，最后选出局外人乌尔班五世。

1363年乌尔班任命他为十字军使节，这场对突厥人的远征由法王约翰二世与塞浦路斯的彼得一世筹划。1364年1月他在远征启程前去世。

Sinibaldo Fieschi (c. 1195–1254), son of Count Ugo Fieschi, was the pope who deposed Emperor Frederick II. He was made a cardinal in 1227. Elected pope in 1243 as Innocent IV, he inherited the dispute over lands Frederick had seized from the Church.

Talks collapsed in 1244 when a meeting at Narni looked like a trap; Innocent left Civitavecchia disguised as a soldier and made his way to Lyon. There the council that opened in June 1245 confirmed Frederick's excommunication and deposed him. In 1252 his bull Ad extirpanda authorised torture of heretics.

Frederick died in 1250, and Innocent returned to Italy in 1251 to face his sons Conrad IV and Manfred. In May 1254 he invested Edmund Crouchback, son of Henry III of England, with Sicily; Manfred submitted only to gain time. Innocent died at Naples on 7 December 1254 with Sicily still unsettled.

西尼巴尔多·菲耶斯基（约1195—1254）是乌戈·菲耶斯基伯爵之子，也是废黜皇帝腓特烈二世的教宗。他于1227年被任命为枢机。1243年他当选教宗，称英诺森四世，接手了教廷与腓特烈关于皇帝所占教会土地的争端。

1244年，纳尔尼会面看上去像是圈套，谈判随之破裂；英诺森乔装成士兵，从奇维塔韦基亚辗转到了里昂。1245年6月开幕的里昂会议重申了对腓特烈的绝罚，并宣布废黜他。1252年，他颁布《根除异端》诏书，准许对异端用刑。

腓特烈于1250年去世，英诺森1251年返回意大利，面对腓特烈的儿子康拉德四世和曼弗雷德。1254年5月，他把西西里王国册封给英格兰国王亨利三世之子埃德蒙·克罗奇贝克；曼弗雷德表示臣服，但只是为了争取时间。1254年12月7日，英诺森四世在那不勒斯去世，西西里的归属仍未解决。

Étienne Aubert, who became Pope Innocent VI (1282–1362), was the son of a Limousin lord and taught civil law at Toulouse before becoming a bishop and, from 1342, a cardinal under Clement VI.

In 1347 he took part in the peace mission that produced the Truce of Calais. Elected at Avignon in December 1352, he revoked a capitulation that placed the pope beneath the college of cardinals, reformed papal administration, and sent Cardinal Albornoz to restore order in Rome and the Papal States.

Plague and the Italian wars left the papacy short of money, so he cut the chapel staff and sold works of art. He died at Avignon on 12 September 1362, and Urban V succeeded him.

Innocent VII (c. 1336–1406), born Cosimo de' Migliorati at Sulmona in the Abruzzo, taught canon and civil law at Perugia and Padua before entering the papal Curia under Urban VI. He served ten years as papal collector in England, became archbishop of Ravenna in 1387 and a cardinal under Boniface IX in 1389.

Elected pope in October 1404 during the Western Schism, he faced Benedict XIII's court at Avignon. In August 1405 his nephew Ludovico Migliorati murdered eleven Romans, forcing him to flee to Viterbo; he returned in January 1406 and died in Rome on 6 November 1406.

en:
Jean-Raymond de Comminges (c. 1285–1348), a younger son of Count Bernard VII of Comminges, entered the Cistercians and became a canon at Narbonne. Elected Bishop of Maguelone in 1309, he attended the Council of Vienne and in 1317 became the first Archbishop of Toulouse.

In 1320, as the Shepherds' Crusade massacred Jews and Cagots in the region, he wrote to the pope for help. John XXII made him a cardinal in 1327.

In the 1334 conclave he refused election to the papacy, which then went to Benedict XII. He died at Avignon in 1348.

en:
Jacques Duèze (1244–1334), born at Cahors, taught law before becoming Bishop of Avignon in 1310 and a cardinal in 1312. After a two-year interregnum he was elected pope at Lyon in 1316 as John XXII, second of the Avignon popes, and centralized papal power and income.

He excommunicated Emperor Louis IV, who marched on Rome and enthroned the antipope Nicholas V in reply, and he condemned the Franciscan doctrine of absolute poverty.

In 1323 he canonized Thomas Aquinas. His beatific-vision teaching caused a scandal he retracted only on his deathbed at Avignon in December 1334.

en:
Manuele Fieschi was a Genoese priest of the powerful Fieschi family who served as a papal notary at Avignon. Around 1337 he wrote to Edward III of England claiming that Edward's father, Edward II, had not been murdered at Berkeley in 1327 but had escaped and lived in exile on the continent.

A copy found at Montpellier in 1878 began a debate that continues: some historians count the letter as evidence that Edward II survived, while others suspect a blackmail attempt. Fieschi later became bishop of Vercelli and died in 1349.

en:
Matteo Rosso Orsini, called the Great, was a Roman noble of the Orsini family, a friend of Saint Francis of Assisi and protector of the Franciscan order. In 1241 Pope Gregory IX named him senator of Rome, and during that year's sede vacante he was the city's effective lord, confining the cardinals in the Septizodium to force the papal election.

He opposed Emperor Frederick II's Italian campaigns and defeated him in 1243. He greatly enlarged the Orsini estates and died in 1246; his son became Pope Nicholas III.

en:
Napoleone Orsini (1263–1342) was a Roman cardinal of the family that had given the Church Pope Nicholas III, his uncle. He took holy orders in 1285, and in 1288 Nicholas IV named him cardinal deacon of Sant'Adriano. As legate to Spoleto and Ancona under Boniface VIII he retook rebellious Gubbio in 1301 and backed the pope's crusades against the Colonna.

In the Avignon years he reconciled with the Colonna and testified at Boniface's posthumous trial. In 1305 Clement V made him archpriest of St Peter's. He took a prominent part in the long conclave of 1314–1316, which elected John XXII after bitter quarrels among the cardinals.

As senior cardinal deacon he crowned Benedict XII in January 1335. Over his 54 years as a cardinal he sat in six conclaves. He died at Avignon in 1342.

拿破仑·奥尔西尼（1263—1342）是罗马枢机，出身奥尔西尼家族，叔父即教皇尼古拉三世。他1285年领受神职，1288年被尼古拉四世任命为枢机执事，领圣阿德里亚诺执事区。卜尼法斯八世在位时，他以驻斯波莱托与安科纳特使的身份于1301年收复反叛的古比奥，并支持教皇讨伐科隆纳家族的十字军。

1335年1月，他以资深枢机执事的身份为本笃十二世加冕。担任枢机的54年间，他共参与六次秘密会议，1342年卒于阿维尼翁。

en:
Nicola Caetani (c. 1310–1348) was count of Fondi from 1336, the son and successor of Roffredo III Caetani and Giovanna dell'Aquila, through whose marriage the county had returned to the Caetani.

A man of arms, in 1348 he took into his pay the German mercenary Werner von Urslingen and his Great Company, who on his orders ravaged the Roman Campagna and sacked Anagni after twelve of his envoys had been killed there. He married Giacoma Orsini and was succeeded by his son Onorato I.

en:
Giovanni Gaetano Orsini, eldest son of the Roman noble Matteo Rosso Orsini, was made cardinal deacon by Innocent IV in 1244. He served under eight popes, becoming protector of the Franciscans.

In November 1277 he was elected pope after a six-month vacancy, taking the name Nicholas III. In 1278 Rudolf of Habsburg recognized papal sovereignty over Romagna, the March of Ancona and Spoleto, and a new constitution ended Charles of Anjou's hold on the Roman senatorship.

In 1279 he issued Exiit qui seminat to settle the Franciscan poverty dispute. He was the first pope to reside permanently at the Vatican, and died of apoplexy on 22 August 1280.

1279年，他发布《出去播种》通谕，裁定方济各会的贫穷之争。他是首位常驻梵蒂冈的教皇，1280年8月22日中风而死。

en:
Onorato I Caetani (c. 1336–1400) was count of Fondi and a powerful baron of the Papal States and Naples. Succeeding his father around 1348, his rule was confirmed by Queen Joanna I in 1352.

In September 1378 he sheltered the French cardinals at Fondi, who elected Robert of Geneva as the antipope Clement VII, opening the Western Schism. He backed Anjou against Ladislaus; excommunicated by Boniface IX and defeated by papal and Neapolitan armies, he died at Fondi in April 1400.

en:
Orso di Bobone (c. 1136–1207) was a Roman politician regarded as the founder of the great Orsini house. The son of Bobone di Pietro, he was a nephew of Pope Celestine III and was counted among the senators of Rome before 1207.

He married Gaetana Caetani of Sermoneta, and through his son Giovanni, called Giangaetano, he was the great-grandfather of Pope Nicholas III. The main Orsini lines, including the lords of Pitigliano, descend from him.

en:
Rinaldo della Torre, called Passerino, was a Milanese nobleman and soldier of the Guelph Della Torre family, the son of Napo della Torre. After Emperor Henry VII's vicar was driven from Cremona in January 1312, the city made him its podestà.

With Giacomo Cavalcabò he led the Guelph army against the Visconti at the battle of Soncino on 16 March 1312, and in later campaigns against Galeazzo Visconti he stormed the castle of Tegnoso near Monza. He died around 1330.

en:
Raphael (1483–1520), born Raffaello Sanzio at Urbino, was an Italian painter and architect of the High Renaissance, ranked with Leonardo and Michelangelo. He was an orphan at eleven. He probably trained under Pietro Perugino, was described as a master in 1500, and worked in Florence from 1504 to 1508, absorbing Leonardo and Michelangelo.

In 1508 Julius II called him to Rome to redecorate the Vatican apartments, now the Raphael Rooms, of which the School of Athens is the best known. After Bramante died in 1514 he took over St Peter's, and his large workshop executed much late work from his drawings.

Raphael never married and died on Good Friday, 6 April 1520, after a fifteen-day illness, possibly on his 37th birthday. His will left his studio to Giulio Romano and Penni, and at his request he was buried in the Pantheon, under an epitaph by Pietro Bembo.

拉斐尔（1483—1520）原名拉法埃洛·圣齐奥，生于乌尔比诺，是意大利盛期文艺复兴的画家和建筑师，与达·芬奇、米开朗基罗并称。他十一岁成为孤儿。他很可能师从佩鲁吉诺，1500年已被称为大师，1504至1508年在佛罗伦萨吸收达·芬奇和米开朗基罗的作品。

1508年儒略二世召他到罗马重新装饰梵蒂冈的教皇寓所，即拉斐尔房间，其中最著名的是《雅典学院》。1514年伯拉孟特去世后，他接手圣彼得大教堂，他庞大的作坊根据他的草图完成许多晚期作品。

拉斐尔终身未婚，在病了十五天后于1520年4月6日耶稣受难日去世，那天可能正是他的三十七岁生日。遗嘱把作坊留给朱利奥·罗马诺和彭尼，他依遗愿安葬万神殿，墓志铭出自本博之手。

Rinaldo Orsini (1217–1286) was founder of the Orsini line of Monterotondo. The third son of Matteo Rosso Orsini and a brother of Pope Nicholas III, he served as podestà of Foligno in 1262.

When Henry of Castile entered Rome and joined the Ghibellines later that year, Rinaldo fled and fortified himself in Marino, returning only after Conradin's defeat in 1268. He died in 1286, leaving sons including the future cardinal Napoleone Orsini.

en:
Roffredo II Caetani (c. 1225–1296) was a nobleman of Anagni and brother of Pope Boniface VIII. In 1278 he bought land near Anagni on behalf of his brother, became podestà of Todi in 1282 and later served as senator of Rome.

In 1295 Charles II made him count of Caserta. He married Elisabetta Orsini; their son Francesco became cardinal in 1295, and Pietro II succeeded him after his death in 1296.

Roffredo III Caetani (c. 1270–1335) was a nobleman of the Kingdom of Naples, the son of Pietro II Caetani and a great-nephew of Pope Boniface VIII. In 1297 he married Margherita dell'Aquila, but later divorced her and wed Giovanna dell'Aquila, heiress of the county of Fondi.

Through this marriage Fondi passed to the Caetani in 1299 and Roffredo became its count. He died in 1335 and was succeeded by his son Nicola.

罗弗雷多三世·卡埃塔尼（约1270—1335）是那不勒斯王国贵族，彼得罗二世之子，教宗卜尼法斯八世的侄孙。1297年他娶玛格丽塔·德拉奎拉为妻，后与其离异，改娶丰迪伯国女继承人焦万娜·德拉奎拉。

en:
Simone Martini (c. 1284–1344) was the Sienese painter who gave Italian art its courtly Gothic grace. Probably a pupil of Duccio di Buoninsegna, he painted in the soft, flowing line of the Sienese tradition and drew on French illuminated manuscripts. His first documented work is the Maestà of 1315 in Siena's Palazzo Pubblico.

In 1317 King Robert of Anjou called him to Naples, where he painted Saint Louis of Toulouse crowning his brother Robert. With Lippo Memmi he painted the Annunciation of 1333 now in the Uffizi, and frescoed the San Martino Chapel at Assisi.

By 1335 he was at the Avignon papal court, where he befriended Petrarch, two of whose sonnets mention a portrait of Laura he is said to have painted. He died at Avignon in July 1344.

西莫内·马蒂尼（约1284—1344）是锡耶纳画家，为意大利艺术带来了宫廷式的哥特优雅。相传他师从杜乔·迪·博尼塞尼亚，承袭锡耶纳传统柔和流畅的线条，又吸收了法国手抄本插图的养分。他有纪年可考的最早作品，是1315年锡耶纳市政厅的《威严》湿壁画。

1317年，安茹的罗贝尔国王召他前往那不勒斯，他在那里画下图卢兹的圣路易为兄弟罗贝尔加冕的画面。他与利波·梅米合作完成今藏乌菲齐美术馆的1333年《天使报喜》，并在阿西西的圣马蒂诺礼拜堂绘制湿壁画。

约1335年他已身在阿维尼翁教廷，与彼特拉克结交；彼特拉克在两首十四行诗中提到一幅相传由马蒂尼所绘的劳拉肖像。1344年7月，他卒于阿维尼翁。

en:
Hugues Roger (1293–1363), the cardinal of Tulle, was a son of Guillaume Roger and Guillemette de Mestre, a brother of Pope Clement VI and an uncle of the future Gregory XI. A Benedictine monk of Tulle, he became abbot of Saint-Jean-d'Angély in 1341.

With his brother on the papal throne at Avignon, he rose fast: bishop of Tulle in July 1342, cardinal-priest of San Lorenzo in Damaso that September. In 1345 he bought the barony of Portes-Bertrand from the dauphin Humbert II for 62,000 gold florins, and later passed such estates to his nephew. He later served as abbot of Cluny and camerlengo of the cardinals.

Elected pope in the 1362 conclave with fifteen votes, he refused, and Urban V was chosen instead. He died in 1363 at the abbey of Mallast.

于格·罗歇（1293—1363），人称“蒂勒的枢机”，是纪尧姆·罗歇与纪耶梅特·德梅斯特尔之子，教皇克雷芒六世的兄弟，未来的格列高利十一世的叔父。他是蒂勒的本笃会修士，1341年出任圣让当热利修道院院长。

兄弟在阿维尼翁登上教皇宝座后，他的升迁很快：1342年7月任蒂勒主教，同年9月受任为达马苏斯圣老楞佐堂枢机司铎。1345年，他以62000金弗罗林向多芬安贝尔二世买下波尔特-贝尔特朗男爵领，后来又把这类产业转给侄子。他后来还出任克吕尼修道院院长和枢机团财务总长。

1362年教皇选举中，他得到十五票，却拒绝接受，乌尔班五世因而当选。1363年，他在马拉斯特修道院去世。

en:
Guillaume de Grimoard (1310–1370), a Benedictine canonist from Grizac near Mende, was neither bishop nor cardinal when he was elected pope at Avignon in 1362 as Urban V. He kept the Benedictine Rule and lived simply, which set him against luxury-loving cardinals, and he pressed monastic reform and sought reunion with the Greek Church.

His 1363 crusade call led Peter I of Cyprus to seize Alexandria in 1365. That November, free companies led by Bertrand du Guesclin threatened Avignon, and he paid them a ransom to leave the Rhône valley.

In 1367 he moved the curia back to Rome, the first Avignon pope to do so, but Italian unrest drove him back to Avignon in 1370, where he died on 19 December. Beatified in 1870, he is the only beatified Avignon pope.

纪尧姆·德·格里莫阿尔德（1310—1370）是芒德附近格里扎克出身的本笃会教会法学家，1362年在阿维尼翁当选教皇、称乌尔班五世时，既非主教也非枢机。他仍遵守本笃会戒规，生活简朴，与习于奢华的枢机们不和；他推行修道院改革，并谋求与希腊教会复合。

1363年他号召十字军，塞浦路斯国王彼得一世的军队于1365年攻占亚历山大。同年11月，贝特朗·迪·盖克兰率领的自由佣兵团逼近阿维尼翁，他付赎金让他们离开罗讷河谷。

1367年，他将教廷迁回罗马，是第一位这样做的阿维尼翁教皇；但意大利的乱局迫使他于1370年返回阿维尼翁，12月19日在那里去世。他于1870年被宣福，是唯一获此待遇的阿维尼翁教皇。

en:
Bartolomeo Prignano (c. 1318–1389), a Neapolitan canon lawyer, worked in the papal chancery at Avignon, where he was known for simplicity and frugality, and became archbishop of Bari in 1377. He was elected pope as Urban VI on 8 April 1378, the last candidate chosen from outside the College of Cardinals.

French cardinals rejected his reforms and at Fondi on 20 September 1378 elected Robert of Geneva as Clement VII. The resulting Western Schism split Christendom until 1417, with France and its allies backing the Avignon antipope.

He excommunicated Queen Joanna I of Naples and crowned her rival Charles III in 1381; besieged at Nocera in 1384, he executed his cardinal opponents. He died in Rome on 15 October 1389, likely from a fall from his mule.

巴尔托洛梅奥·普里尼亚诺（约1318—1389）是那不勒斯籍教会法学者，曾在阿维尼翁教廷秘书处任职，以朴素节俭著称，1377年成为巴里大主教。他于1378年4月8日当选教宗，称乌尔班六世，是最后一位从枢机团之外选出的教宗。

法兰西枢机反对他的改革，于1378年9月20日在丰迪推选日内瓦的罗贝尔为克雷芒七世。随之而来的西方教会大分裂使基督教世界分裂到1417年，法兰西及其盟友站在阿维尼翁的对立教宗一边。

他绝罚那不勒斯女王乔万娜一世，1381年为其政敌卡洛三世加冕；1384年被围困于诺切拉，事后处死了反对他的枢机。1389年10月15日，他在罗马去世，可能死于此前坠骡造成的伤势。

en:
Azzo da Correggio (1303–c. 1362) was an Italian condottiero born in Parma, son of Giberto III da Correggio, the Defender. Meant for the church, he turned to politics instead and set out to break the Rossi family's hold on Parma. In 1335, backed by the Della Scala of Verona, he succeeded and left them the lordship.

The next year they sent him to Avignon to plead their cause against the Rossi, and there he befriended Petrarch. In 1341 he took Parma from Mastino della Scala himself, with Petrarch at his side, and ruled it until 1344, when he ceded it to Obizzo III d'Este.

Petrarch stayed with him several times and dedicated several works to him. Azzo allied with the Visconti in 1347, hoping to regain Parma, and died at Milan in 1362 as Bernabò Visconti's guest.

阿佐·达·科雷焦（1303—约1362）是生于帕尔马的意大利雇佣军首领，为有“保卫者”之称的吉贝尔托三世·达·科雷焦之子。他本来走教会的路，后来转向政治，着手打破罗西家族对帕尔马的控制。1335年，他在维罗纳德拉·斯卡拉家族支持下得手，把领主之位让给了他们。

次年，斯卡拉家族派他去阿维尼翁，为对付罗西家族向教皇陈情，他在那里与彼特拉克结为好友。1341年，他在彼特拉克陪同下亲自从马斯蒂诺·德拉·斯卡拉手中夺取帕尔马，统治至1344年，随后将其让给费拉拉领主奥比佐三世·埃斯特。

彼特拉克数次在他那里作客，并把多部作品题献给他。1347年，阿佐为重夺帕尔马与维斯孔蒂家族结盟，1362年在米兰作为贝尔纳博·维斯孔蒂的客人去世。

en:
Guglielmo Pallavicini (twelfth century – 1217), called Guglielmo di Oberto, was a Lombard nobleman and ancestor of the Pallavicino Lombard branch. He held the castle of Scipione.

In 1198 he attacked Cardinal Pietro Capuano while the legate crossed his lands, and was excommunicated by Pope Innocent III. The ban was lifted only in 1205, when Guglielmo surrendered the fortress of Landasio to the Church. He died around 1217.

古列尔莫·帕拉维奇尼（12世纪—1217），又称古列尔莫·迪·奥贝托，是伦巴第贵族，帕拉维奇诺家族伦巴第支系的始祖，领有希皮奥内堡。

1198年，枢机主教皮埃特罗·卡普阿诺途经他的领地时，古列尔莫发兵袭击这位使节，被教宗依诺增爵三世处以绝罚。直到1205年，他把兰达肖要塞交给教会，绝罚才获解除。他约于1217年去世。

en:
Manfredino Pallavicini, known as the Pious (1254–1328), was a Lombard marchese in the Parma region and the only son and heir of the Ghibelline leader Oberto II. He rebuilt the family castle of Ravarano, destroyed by the Guelphs of Parma, and with Visconti help recovered Tabiano.

Driven from Ravarano by rival kinsmen, he won back the fortress after Parma made peace with Borgo San Donnino. In 1327 Emperor Louis the Bavarian confirmed his lands and privileges, and he died in 1328.

曼弗雷迪诺·帕拉维奇尼，人称‘虔诚者’（1254—1328），是伦巴第帕尔马一带的侯爵，吉伯林派领袖欧贝尔托二世的独子与继承人。他重建了被帕尔马圭尔夫派拆毁的家族城堡拉瓦拉诺，又在维斯孔蒂家族帮助下收复塔比亚诺。

他曾被对立的族人逐出拉瓦拉诺，待帕尔马与圣多尼诺堡议和后才收复该堡。1327年，皇帝路德维希四世（巴伐利亚人）确认了他的领地与特权，他于1328年去世。

en:
Oberto II Pallavicino, also called Pelavicino (1197–1269), was an Italian condottiere of the Lombard Pallavicino family, son of Guglielmo Pallavicino. An imperial vicar and Ghibelline leader, he backed Emperor Frederick II against Pope Gregory IX and the communes from 1234. From 1250, with Buoso da Dovara, he mastered Parma, Cremona, Piacenza, Pavia and Brescia.

He then turned on his former friend Ezzelino III da Romano and joined the Guelfs, helping the Lombard League win Cassano in 1259, and gained Milan and five other cities. He later fought Charles of Anjou in Lombardy without success and died at Gusaliggio on 8 May 1269.
