欧贝尔托二世·帕拉维奇诺，又称佩拉维奇诺（1197—1269），是帕拉维奇诺家族伦巴第支系的意大利雇佣军首领，古列尔莫·帕拉维奇诺之子。他身为帝国代理人和吉伯林派领袖，自1234年起支持皇帝腓特烈二世对抗教皇格列高利九世及诸城市公社。1250年起，他与博索·达·多瓦拉一道征服帕尔马、克雷莫纳、皮亚琴察、帕维亚和布雷西亚。

随后他与旧友埃泽利诺三世·达·罗马诺反目，加入圭尔夫派，帮助伦巴第联盟在1259年的卡萨诺战役中获胜，由此获得米兰等六座城市。后来他在伦巴第与入侵的安茹的查理作战，屡遭败绩，1269年5月8日卒于古萨利乔。

en:
Oberto, also called Uberto, Pallavicino was a Ghibelline marquis in the Parma region and a son of Manfredino 'il Pio' Pallavicino. When his father died in 1328 the family fiefs passed to Oberto and his brothers Federico and Donnino; in 1348, after Federico's death, he inherited Busseto and Solignano.

He later made himself lord of Ravarano. He founded the Ravarano branch of the dynasty and married Teresa de' Rossi, daughter of the Parmesan condottiero Marsilio de' Rossi.

en:
Pasquale Paoli (1725–1807) was the son of the Corsican patriot Giacinto Paoli and grew up exiled in Naples after 1739. Returning in 1755, he was elected general of the Corsicans and built the Corsican Republic, ruling from Corte with an elected diet and a written constitution while Genoa held the coast.

After Genoa transferred its rights over Corsica to France, his forces were beaten at Ponte Novu in 1769 and he fled to Britain. He returned with the French Revolution, then broke with France and helped found the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom of 1794–1796, dying in London in 1807.

帕斯夸莱·保利（1725—1807）是科西嘉爱国者贾钦托·保利之子，1739年后随父流亡那不勒斯并在那里长大。1755年他回到科西嘉，被推举为科西嘉人的将军，建立科西嘉共和国，以科尔特为首都，设立民选议会和成文宪法，热那亚则保有沿海地带。

热那亚将对科西嘉的权利转让给法国后，他的军队于1769年在蓬泰诺沃战败，他逃往英国。法国大革命爆发后他返回家乡，后来与法国决裂，参与建立1794至1796年的英属科西嘉王国，1807年在伦敦去世。

en:
William Frangipani (Guglielmo; died 1337) was a Roman Franciscan of the Frangipani family who held the see of Patras as Latin Archbishop from 1317 and ruled its barony as a virtually autonomous lord.

His ties ran to Venice: in 1321, as Byzantine forces pressed Achaea, he led a failed bid to hand the principality's remains to the Republic, and in 1336 he became a Venetian citizen. In 1329, when Prince John of Gravina left the Morea for Italy, he was named bailli, the first cleric to hold the post, and settled disputes between the feudal lords until 1331.

After 1330 he repeatedly excommunicated the Catalans of Athens. When Bertrand des Baux became bailli in 1336, William refused homage to the prince and relations soured. He died in 1337, and Bertrand's siege of Patras failed to bring the archbishopric back under control.

威廉·弗兰吉帕尼（意大利语名古列尔莫，1337年卒）是罗马弗兰吉帕尼家族的方济各会士，1317年起任帕特雷拉丁大主教，以近乎独立的领主身份统治帕特雷男爵国。

他与威尼斯关系密切：1321年，拜占庭军队进逼亚该亚亲王国，他带头试图把亲王国剩余的土地交给威尼斯共和国，但未成功；1336年，他成为威尼斯公民。1329年，亲王格拉维纳的乔凡尼离开摩里亚前往意大利，他被任命为巴伊略，是首位担任此职的教士，并在1331年前负责调解领主之间的纠纷。

1330年以后，他多次将雅典公国的加泰罗尼亚人开除教籍。1336年贝特朗·德博出任巴伊略，威廉拒绝再向亲王效忠，两人关系恶化。1337年他去世，贝特朗围攻帕特雷，未能使大主教区重新就范。

en:
Castellino Beccaria (born c. 1300, died 1358) was a Ghibelline nobleman of Pavia who succeeded his father Musso as signore of the city in 1343 and ruled until his death.

In 1346 he stood godfather to Luchino Novello, son of the Milanese lord Luchino Visconti. After Luchino's death his exiled nephews came to power in Milan, and Castellino joined a coalition against Galeazzo II Visconti alongside Ludovico I Gonzaga and John II of Montferrat.

He died at Pavia in 1358, leaving no children; the signoria passed to his brother Leodrisino. Guelfs then tried to found a republic, but the Visconti captured the city and added it to their domain.

卡斯泰利诺·贝卡里亚（约1300年生，1358年卒）是帕维亚的吉伯林派贵族，1343年继承父亲穆索成为该城领主，统治直至去世。

1346年，他为米兰领主卢基诺·维斯孔蒂之子卢基诺·诺韦洛充当教父。卢基诺死后，遭他放逐的侄子们在米兰掌权，卡斯泰利诺随后加入反对加莱亚佐二世·维斯孔蒂的联盟，盟友包括卢多维科一世·贡扎加和蒙费拉托侯爵乔瓦尼二世。

1358年他卒于帕维亚，没有子女，领主之位由其弟莱奥德里西诺继承。随后圭尔夫派试图建立共和国，但维斯孔蒂家族攻占该城，并入自己的领地。

en:
Fiorello Beccaria was a nobleman of Pavia, the younger son of the signore Musso Beccaria, and shared rule over the city with his brother Castellino. He married Filippina Sannazzaro and rebuilt the fortress of Rocca de' Giorgi, later called Roccafirella after him.

He founded the Beccaria di Messer Fiorello line; his son Galvagno received the fief of Pietra in 1405, and his descendants ruled there and held Castana castle until 1531.

菲奥雷洛·贝卡里亚是帕维亚贵族，城主穆索·贝卡里亚较年幼的儿子，与兄弟卡斯泰利诺共同统治该城。他娶菲利皮娜·桑纳扎罗为妻，重建了罗卡德乔治要塞，该要塞后来以他得名“菲奥雷洛岩”。

他开创了“菲奥雷洛先生的贝卡里亚”支系；其子加尔瓦尼奥于1405年受封彼得拉，后裔在当地统治并保有卡斯塔纳城堡直至1531年。

en:
Manfredo Beccaria (c. 1262–1322) led the Ghibelline popular party of Pavia. After serving as podestà of Vercelli and Novara, he became potestas of the People and the Merchants in Pavia in 1282. He oversaw the city's grain supply and drew support from merchants and guilds, building a popular regime against the Guelph nobles.

In 1289 William VII of Montferrat took Pavia and drove him into exile. Recalled in October 1290, he was confirmed ten-year podestà and ruled Pavia as its effective lord.

In 1299 he led an anti-Visconti league, taking Vercelli and Novara, but in 1300 the rival Langosco expelled him again. Imprisoned around 1311, he was freed when the Visconti entered Pavia in 1315, dying there on 22 March 1322.

曼弗雷多·贝卡里亚（约1262—1322）是帕维亚的吉伯林派领袖。他曾担任韦尔切利和诺瓦拉的波德斯塔，1282年起任帕维亚的“人民与商人长官”。他掌管城市粮食供应，依靠商人与行会，对抗归尔夫贵族并建立平民政权。

1289年蒙费拉侯爵古列尔莫七世攻占帕维亚，将他逐出。1290年10月他被召回，受任为期十年的波德斯塔，成为帕维亚事实上的领主。

1299年他领导反维斯孔蒂同盟，一度攻占韦尔切利和诺瓦拉，但1300年敌对的兰戈斯科家族再度将他赶走。约1311年他被囚禁，1315年维斯孔蒂军队进入帕维亚后获释，1322年3月22日在该城去世。

en:
Musso Beccaria (died 1343), son of Manfredo Beccaria, was a Ghibelline signore of Pavia from 1322 and a loyal servant of Milan's Visconti. The Guelfs expelled his family in 1300, and it returned in 1315 only after Matteo Visconti drove its rivals from the city.

In 1323 he was excommunicated after ignoring an inquisitorial summons. In 1328 he seized a papal convoy carrying sixty thousand gold gulden to the papal commander fighting the Visconti, who besieged Pavia and entered it on 8 June 1331, restoring Guelf rule.

After a November 1332 uprising toppled the papal governor, Musso returned with Visconti help and in 1333 allied with Robert of Naples against John of Bohemia. In 1342 he turned to Louis IV of Bavaria, but Luchino Visconti forced him to submit. He died in 1343, succeeded by his son Castellino.

zh:
穆索·贝卡里亚（1343年卒）是曼弗雷多·贝卡里亚之子，自1322年起任帕维亚的吉伯林派领主，也是米兰维斯孔蒂家族的忠实追随者。1300年圭尔夫派驱逐了他的家族，直到1315年马泰奥·维斯孔蒂把对手逐出帕维亚，家族才得以返回。

1323年，他无视宗教裁判所的传召，遭绝罚。1328年，他劫取教皇送往对维斯孔蒂作战的教皇军统帅处的六万金古尔登车队；那位统帅围困帕维亚，于1331年6月8日入城，恢复了圭尔夫派的统治。

1332年11月起义推翻教皇代理人后，穆索借维斯孔蒂之助复位，1333年又与那不勒斯国王罗贝托结盟对抗波希米亚国王约翰。1342年他转而投向巴伐利亚的路德维希四世，却被卢基诺·维斯孔蒂逼得投降。他于1343年去世，其子卡斯泰利诺继位。

en:
Bernard V of Lippe (1277–1341) was Prince-Bishop of Paderborn from 1321 until his death. A son of Simon I, Lord of Lippe, he was appointed provost of Paderborn in 1305 and governed the bishopric de facto under two earlier bishops before taking office.

In 1309 he established a council of canons, ministeriales and citizens, and in 1326 issued the Privilegium Bernhardi, binding himself to consult the Estates before taxation. He founded Dringenberg and Peckelsheim and is regarded as the founder of Paderborn's prince-bishopric.

利珀的伯恩哈德五世（1277—1341）自1321年起任帕德博恩采邑主教，直至去世。他是利珀领主西蒙一世之子，1305年被任命为帕德博恩教长，在就任前的两任主教任内已实际执掌主教区。

Francesco della Faggiola was a 14th-century Italian man-at-arms, the son of Ranieri della Faggiola, known as Neri, and grandson of Uguccione della Faggiola, who ruled Pisa and Lucca.

In 1336 his marriage to a daughter of Pier Saccone Tarlati, lord of Arezzo, sealed the peace between Tarlati and his father after years of war over the Massa Trabaria and Sansepolcro.

en:
Ranieri della Faggiola, called Neri (1290–1355), was a Ghibelline condottiero and imperial vicar, the son of Uguccione della Faggiola. In 1314 his father, then ruling Pisa and Lucca, made him vicar of Pisa, and at Montecatini in 1315 he commanded the infantry, becoming podestà of Lucca after the victory. In April 1316 he condemned Castruccio Castracani to death, but the Lucchese revolted and Castracani besieged him into surrender, sparing his life.

After his father's fall he kept the family's Apennine lordships, centred on Casteldelci, and remained close to the Visconti and a rival of Florence. From 1329 he fought Pier Saccone Tarlati of Arezzo, relieving Casteldelci in 1334 and recovering it in 1337.

The peace of 1336 was sealed by the marriage of his son Francesco to a daughter of Pier Saccone. A record of 1353 lists 72 castles and villages in his possession, and he died in 1355.

拉涅里·德拉·法焦拉，绰号“内里”（1290—1355），是吉伯林派将领、帝国代理人，乌古乔内·德拉·法焦拉之子。1314年其父统治比萨、卢卡期间，任命他为比萨代理人；1315年蒙特卡蒂尼战役中他指挥步兵，获胜后被任命为卢卡行政长官。1316年4月，他判处卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼死刑，但卢卡人起事，卡斯特鲁乔将他围困在堡垒中迫其投降，留他一命。

父亲倒台后，他保有家族在亚平宁的领地，以卡斯泰尔德尔奇为中心，始终亲维斯孔蒂、与佛罗伦萨为敌。1329年起他与阿雷佐领主皮尔·萨科内·塔拉蒂交战，1334年驰援卡斯泰尔德尔奇，1337年将其收复。

1336年议和，以其子弗朗切斯科迎娶皮尔·萨科内之女为盟。1353年的一份文书记载他名下有72座城堡与村镇，他于1355年去世。

en:
Philip I of Courtenay (1243–1283) was titular Latin Emperor of Constantinople from 1273, ruling in exile after the Greeks recovered the city in 1261. He was the son of Emperor Baldwin II; as a boy his father mortgaged him to Venetian merchants.

By the Treaty of Viterbo in 1267 he was betrothed to Beatrice, daughter of Charles I of Sicily, and they married in 1273. Philip held only the Latin lands in Greece and died in 1283, his claim inherited by his daughter Catherine.

库特奈的菲利普一世（1243—1283）于1273年成为君士坦丁堡拉丁帝国的挂名皇帝；1261年希腊人收复君士坦丁堡后，他只能在流亡中统治。他是皇帝鲍德温二世之子，幼年曾被父亲抵押给威尼斯商人。

en:
Pedro de Peralta y Ezpeleta, called the Younger (1421–c. 1492), was constable of Navarre and leader of the Agramont faction against the Beaumont party in the Navarrese Civil War of 1451–1455. John II made him first Count of Santisteban de Lerín and lord of Peralta, Falces and other towns.

He married Anne of Brabant, an illegitimate daughter of Anthony of Burgundy, in 1440, and Isabel de Foix in 1462. He later backed the Catholic Monarchs, receiving titles in return for supporting the marriage of Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon in 1469.

佩德罗·德·佩拉尔塔-埃斯佩莱塔，人称“小佩德”（1421—约1492），是纳瓦拉宫廷长，在1451—1455年的纳瓦拉内战中领导阿格拉蒙特派同博蒙特派作战。胡安二世封他为首任桑蒂斯特万-德·莱林伯爵，领有佩拉尔塔、法尔塞斯等城镇。

1440年他娶勃艮第的安东尼的私生女布拉班特的安妮，1462年续娶伊莎贝尔·德·富瓦。后来他支持天主教双王，因支持1469年卡斯蒂利亚的伊莎贝尔与阿拉贡的费尔南多联姻而获得封号。

en:
Binnya E Laung was the only known son of King Binnya E Law of Martaban and heir presumptive from his father's accession in 1330. When E Law was summoned to the throne by his half-sister Sanda Min Hla, he brought his son to Martaban.

His rival was his younger half-cousin Binnya U, son of Queen Sanda Min Hla, and E Law never formally named an heir apparent. In the 1340s, as the king's health failed, the two princes fought an elephant-back duel, which Binnya U won; the enraged king had U arrested until the queen secured his release. E Laung died of smallpox soon afterward, without taking the throne. Binnya U succeeded in 1348.

en:
Binnya E Law (1308–1348/1349), son of King Hkun Law and nephew of founder Wareru, ruled Martaban from 1330. He was three when his father was assassinated in a coup in 1311, but the children were spared. He won the trust of his cousin King Saw Zein, who made him governor of Sittaung and later Pegu.

In 1330 Saw Zein was assassinated, and King Saw E, set up by Queen Sanda Min Hla, was poisoned within 49 days. Sanda Min Hla, E Law's half-sister, then summoned him to Martaban. His armies defeated a Sukhothai invasion in 1330–1331, ending Martaban's tributary status to the Siamese kingdom, though the fighting brought famine.

In his later years his son Binnya E Laung and Sanda Min Hla's son Binnya U rivalled for the succession, once fighting an elephant-back duel that U won. E Law died in 1348/1349, and U succeeded him.

zh:
频耶埃劳（1308—1348/1349）是恭劳王之子、王朝创立者伐丽流之侄，1330年起为马达班国王。1311年他年仅三岁，父亲在政变中遇刺，但孩子们获免于难。他深得表兄修齐因王信任，先后出任锡当总督和勃固总督。

1330年，修齐因遇刺，由僧陀明罗王后扶立的国王修埃也在四十九天内被毒死。僧陀明罗是埃劳的异母姐，随后召他前往马达班。1330—1331年，他的军队大败素可泰王国的入侵，结束了马达班对暹罗的藩属地位，但战火引发饥荒。

他统治后期，其子频耶埃朗与僧陀明罗之子频耶宇争夺继承权，两人甚至骑象决斗，结果频耶宇获胜。埃劳于1348/1349年去世，频耶宇继位。

en:
Binnya U (1323–1384) took the throne of Martaban–Hanthawaddy in 1348 as Hsinbyushin, Lord of the White Elephant, succeeding his maternal uncle Binnya E Law. Son of Saw Zein and Sanda Min Hla, he held power only tenuously and bought the court's loyalty with marriages, taking three daughters of a minister himself.

In 1351–1352 he drove back a Lan Na invasion, leading the counterattack on his white elephant; in 1352–1353 he retook Pegu from his half-brother Min Linka. In 1362 he raised the Shwedagon Pagoda at Dagon to about 20 metres.

Then a coup by two brothers in 1363–1364 began the loss of Martaban, and by 1369 he held only Pegu province, which became his capital. Ailing, he made his sister Maha Dewi regent in 1383 and died in January 1384 amid the revolt of his eldest son Binnya Nwe, who became King Razadarit.

zh:
频耶宇（1323—1384）1348年继舅父频耶埃劳为马达班—汉达瓦底国王，号“辛骠信”，意为“白象之主”。他是修齐因王与僧陀明罗王后之子，起初权力并不稳固，靠联姻笼络宫廷，亲自娶了一位大臣的三个女儿。

1351—1352年，他骑白象率军反击，击退兰纳的入侵；1352—1353年，他攻克勃固，夺回被异母弟明林加占据的城池。1362年他在大光把大金塔加高到约20米。

1363—1364年，两兄弟发动政变，马达班自此逐步失守，到1369年他只剩勃固一省，便以勃固为都。他长年多病，1383年命姐姐摩诃提毗摄政，1384年1月在长子频耶努的叛乱中去世；频耶努即位，即亚扎底律。

en:
Hkun Law (27 March 1254 – March 1311), born Ma Gada at Donwun, was Wareru's younger brother and heir. When Wareru was assassinated in January 1307 without a male heir, Gada succeeded as king of Martaban, receiving recognition from his overlord Sukhothai and the regnal name Hkun Law.

He proved a weak ruler: Lan Na raiders struck as far south as Donwun and killed its governor, while the delta governor Min Bala, his brother-in-law, ruled like a sovereign. In March 1311 Min Bala seized Martaban while Law hunted near Moulmein. Returning to find the gates shut, he fled into the woods, where Bala's troops killed him; most later Wareru-dynasty kings descended from Law.

恭劳（1254年3月27日—1311年3月）本名马加答，出生于棠温，是伐丽流之弟与继承人。1307年1月伐丽流遇刺且无子，马加答继位为马达班国王，得到宗主素可泰承认并获王号恭劳。

他统治软弱：兰纳袭扰者长驱南下直抵棠温，杀死当地总督，而他的妹夫、三角洲总督敏巴拉形同独立之君。1311年3月，敏巴拉趁恭劳在毛淡棉附近狩猎时夺取马达班。恭劳返回时发现城门紧闭，逃入树林，却被敏巴拉的士兵追杀。后来伐丽流王朝的多数国王都是他的后裔。

en:
Hnin U Yaing (c. 1260s – 1310s) was a princess of Martaban, younger sister of the kingdom's founder Wareru. In 1285 her brother used her to lure Governor Aleimma: the governor fell in love with her and was killed at their wedding feast, letting Wareru seize Martaban.

She married Min Bala, whom Wareru made governor of Myaungmya, and joined her husband in the March 1311 coup against her brother Hkun Law. Bala's troops killed Law after he returned from a hunting trip and found the capital's gates shut.

She then stopped Bala from taking the crown himself, insisting that their eldest son Saw O be made king; her sons Saw O and Saw Zein both later reigned.

宁乌亚英（约1260年代—1310年代）是马达班公主，王朝开创者伐丽流的幼妹。1285年，兄长借她引诱总督阿梨摩：阿梨摩爱上她，却在婚宴上被杀，伐丽流由此夺取马达班。

她嫁给敏巴拉，丈夫被伐丽流任命为渺弥亚总督；1311年3月，她与丈夫发动政变推翻兄长恭劳。恭劳狩猎归来，发现首都城门紧闭，随后被敏巴拉的士兵杀害。

她阻止敏巴拉自立为王，坚持立长子修乌继位。她的两个儿子修乌和修齐因后来都做了国王。

en:
Maha Dewi (c. 1322–c. 1392), born Mwei Na, was a daughter of King Saw Zein and Queen Sanda Min Hla and elder sister of King Binnya U of Martaban.

From 1364 she governed Dagon, and after 1369 she was her ailing brother's closest adviser, ruling the kingdom in all but name by the early 1380s. A court faction led by the chief minister tried to undermine her with talk of an affair with her nephew-in-law Smin Maru.

In October 1383 Binnya U made her regent, but she could not put down the rebellion of her nephew and adopted son Binnya Nwe, secretly backed by the chief minister. When U died in January 1384 the court chose Nwe as King Razadarit, who sent her back to Dagon in a purely ceremonial role.

May Hnin Htapi was a daughter of King Loe Thai of Sukhothai, who in 1311 sent her to Martaban to marry the newly crowned King Saw O, when Martaban was Sukhothai's nominal vassal. As Saw O's chief queen she bore a son, Saw E, and a daughter.

After Saw O broke with Sukhothai and died in 1323, his successor Saw Zein made her his second-ranking queen; she bore Min Linka while Zein fought to restore his authority. When Zein was assassinated in 1330, Saw E reigned only 49 days before the chief queen Sanda Min Hla killed him, after which Htapi vanishes from the chronicles.

梅宁塔琵是素可泰国王乐泰之女。1311年，父亲将她送往马达班，嫁给新即位的国王修乌，当时马达班是素可泰名义上的属邦。她作为修乌的正宫王后，生下儿子修埃和一个女儿。

en:
Min Bala, also called Smim Myaungmya, was governor of the port of Myaungmya from the 1290s and husband of Hnin U Yaing, sister of King Wareru, founder of Hanthawaddy.

In March 1311 he seized the Martaban throne and killed Wareru's successor Hkun Law, but at his wife's insistence yielded the crown to their eldest son Saw O on 10 April 1311. Until his death in the later 1310s Bala was the power behind the throne, ruling from his own palace outside Martaban much as a sovereign; his son Saw Zein later reigned as king.

en:
Min Linka (c. 1327–1352/53) was a younger son of King Saw Zein of Martaban and half-brother of King Binnya U, who appointed him governor of Pegu in 1348 and married him to Mwei Daw, youngest daughter of Minister Than-Bon.

When Lan Na invaded in 1351–1352 and reached the outskirts of Martaban, Linka sent no help to his hard-pressed brother. After the invaders were repelled, Binnya U retook Pegu in 1352–1353; Linka was carried back to Martaban and executed, and Mwei Daw became one of U's queens.

明林加（约1327—1352/1353）是马达班国王修齐因之子、频耶宇王的异母弟。1348年，频耶宇任命他为勃固总督，并安排他迎娶大臣丹邦的幼女妙杜。

en:
Sanda Min Hla (c. early 14th century – 1363/1364), personal name Hnin An Po, was chief queen of three kings of Martaban and the real power behind its throne. A daughter of King Hkun Law and niece of the founder Wareru, she lost her father to a coup in 1311, when the usurpers married her to their son, her cousin Saw Zein.

By 1323 she was his chief queen and had borne Binnya U. After Zein's assassination in 1330 she put down the usurper Zein Pun within a week, then enthroned and married Saw E, grandson of Sukhothai's king, only to poison him after 49 days and place her half-brother Binnya E Law on the throne.

The killing brought a Sukhothai invasion in 1330–1331; E Law defeated it, ending Martaban's vassalage. She held power behind the throne until Binnya U succeeded in 1348.

僧陀明罗（约14世纪初—1363/1364年）本名宁安波，曾是马达班三位国王的正宫王后，也是王位背后的实际掌权者。她是国王恭劳之女、王朝开创者伐丽流的侄女，1311年父亲死于政变，夺位者随即将她嫁给自己的儿子、她的表兄修齐因。

1323年她成为正宫王后，生下后来的国王频耶宇。1330年修齐因遇刺后，她在一周内平定篡位者泽因榜，随即拥立素可泰国王的外孙修埃为王并嫁给他，49天后又将他毒杀，改立异母兄弟频耶埃劳。

素可泰因此于1330—1331年入侵，被频耶埃劳击败，马达班从此不再臣属素可泰。直到1348年儿子频耶宇继位，她始终是幕后掌权者。

en:
Saw Zein (19 May 1303 – c. April 1330), also titled Binnya Ran De, was king of Martaban and a son of Min Bala and Hnin U Yaing, succeeding his brother Saw O in September 1323.

His vassals revolted: he retook Pegu, Dagon and Dala, set up a temporary capital north of Pegu and gathered war elephants before forcing the delta lords of Myaungmya and Bassein to submit. He could not recover the Tenasserim coast from Sukhothai and made a truce as its nominal vassal. In April 1330 his officer Zein Pun murdered him at a housewarming feast; the usurper was killed a week later.

修齐因（1303年5月19日—约1330年4月）又号频耶兰岱，是马达班国王、敏巴拉与宁乌亚英之子，1323年9月继兄长修乌之后登位。

en:
Tala Shin Saw Bok was a queen of King Binnya E Law of Martaban, a daughter of King Hkun Law and younger full sister of the powerful queen Sanda Min Hla. She and her siblings were spared when their father was overthrown in 1311.

In about June 1330 her half-brother Binnya E Law, whom Sanda Min Hla had just placed on the throne, raised her as a principal queen.

In the 1340s she joined her sister in persuading the king to release the young prince Binnya U, arrested after an elephant-back duel with the king's own son Binnya E Laung. E Laung died of smallpox soon afterwards, and Binnya U succeeded as king in 1348.

en:
Wareru (20 March 1253 – c. 14 January 1307), founder of the Martaban Kingdom, was born Ma Gadu at Tagaw Wun near Thaton and served in the elephant stables of King Ram Khamhaeng of Sukhothai before returning home.

He seized the governorship of Martaban in 1285 and in 1287 declared independence from the collapsing Pagan Empire with Sukhothai's backing. In 1295–1296 he and Tarabya of Pegu crushed a Pagan invasion, then he eliminated Tarabya and united the three Mon provinces.

Recognized by Yuan China in 1298, he commissioned the Wareru Dhammathat law code, which influenced Burmese and Siamese law for centuries. In January 1307 he was assassinated by Tarabya's sons.

马达班王国的开创者伐丽流（1253年3月20日—约1307年1月14日）本名马加杜，出生于直通附近的棠温，曾在素可泰国王兰甘亨的象厩供职，后返回故乡。

1285年，他夺取马达班都督之位，1287年在素可泰支持下宣布脱离蒲甘王朝独立。1295—1296年，他与勃固的多罗跋联手击退蒲甘大军，随后除掉多罗跋，统一三个孟族地区。

en:
Adalbert I (c. 955–997), second son of Boso the Old of La Marche, was captured with his brother Hélie I by Guy I of Limoges in 974. Released around 977, he married Guy's sister Almodis and was recognised as count in La Marche in 988; he added Périgord after Hélie's death.

In 995 he and Boso II warred against William V of Aquitaine. He was killed by an arrow at the siege of Gençay in 997 and buried at Charroux.

zh:
阿达尔贝尔一世（约955—997）是马尔什的博松老者的次子。974年，他与兄长埃利一世被利摩日的居伊一世俘虏；约977年获释后，他娶居伊的妹妹阿尔莫迪斯为妻，988年被承认为马尔什伯爵，埃利死后又取得佩里戈尔。

995年，他与博松二世联合向阿基坦公爵威廉五世开战。997年，他在让塞围城战中中箭身亡，葬于沙鲁。

en:
Ali Qushji (1403–1474), born Ala al-Din Ali in Samarkand, was a Timurid astronomer and mathematician whose epithet means falconer, after his father who kept Ulugh Beg's birds. He joined Ulugh Beg's observatory in Samarkand, contributing to the Zij-i-Sultani star tables.

After Ulugh Beg's assassination he travelled west, and around 1470 reached Constantinople as the envoy of Uzun Hasan. Welcomed by Mehmed II, he stayed, helped found the Sahn-ı Seman madrasa, and taught there until his death in 1474, arguing for an astronomy independent of natural philosophy and discussing the rotation of the Earth.

阿里·库什吉（1403—1474），原名阿拉丁·阿里，生于撒马尔罕，是帖木儿王朝的天文学家、数学家；“库什吉”意为驯鹰人，得自他为乌鲁伯格养鹰的父亲。他进入撒马尔罕的乌鲁伯格天文台，参与编撰《苏丹历表》。

乌鲁伯格遇刺后，他辗转西行，约1470年作为乌尊·哈桑的使节抵达君士坦丁堡。穆罕默德二世对他礼遇有加，他便留下，参与创建萨恩-塞米安经学院，并在此任教，直至1474年去世。他主张天文学独立于自然哲学，并探讨地球自转。

en:
Archambaud II Talleyrand (c. 1185–1239), son of Hélie VII, was count of Périgord from about 1209. In 1212 he did homage to King Philip Augustus, confirming his father’s vassalage to the French crown; John Lackland recognized it only after his defeats in 1214.

In 1239 he joined the Barons’ Crusade under Theobald IV of Champagne and died the same year on the road to the Holy Land. His son Hélie VIII succeeded him.

阿尔尚博二世·塔列朗（约1185—1239）是埃利七世之子，约1209年起任佩里戈尔伯爵。1212年，他向法王腓力·奥古斯都行臣服礼，确认了其父开启的对法国王权的直接封臣关系；无地王约翰在1214年战败之后才予以承认。

1239年，阿尔尚博加入香槟伯爵蒂博四世率领的男爵十字军，同年死于前往圣地的途中。其子埃利八世继位。

en:
Archambaud III (c. 1237–c. 1295) succeeded his father Hélie VIII as count of Périgord in 1251, ruling as a child under the regency of his mother Gaillarde.

In 1277 he confirmed the lands of his cousin Hélie II de Talleyrand and released him from vassalage, from which the Talleyrand-Périgord line later grew. He married twice and was succeeded by his son Hélie IX.

阿尔尚博三世（约1237—约1295）于1251年继承父亲埃利八世之位，成为佩里戈尔伯爵，幼年由母亲加亚尔达摄政。

en:
Archambaud IV (c. 1300–1334) became count of Périgord in 1311 on the death of his father Hélie IX, ruling first under the regency of his mother Brunissende de Foix. In 1313 he married Jeanne, daughter of Renaud.

When Jeanne's childless brother Hélie Rudel died in 1334, Archambaud seized Bergerac; the widow Mathe d'Albret contested the inheritance and called in the English king. He died amid the quarrel childless, and his brother Roger-Bernard succeeded.

en:
Adalbert II, called Cadoirac (c. 1020–1072), was count of Périgord from 1044, succeeding his father Boson III. He feuded with Girard de Gordon, bishop of Périgueux, who until 1059 refused to authenticate coins struck by Adalbert’s predecessor Count Hélie II.

By his wife Asceline he left two sons, Hélie III and Adalbert III; the county passed first through Hélie’s line and then, in 1149, to Adalbert’s grandson Boson IV.

en:
Adalbert III (c. 1065–1116) was a son of Count Adalbert II Cadoirac of Périgord. After his brother Hélie III died in 1101 or 1104, he ruled the county jointly with Hélie’s sons: his nephew Guillaume III Talleyrand until 1115, then briefly Hélie Rudel in 1116.

Of his own sons, Boson IV later became count; Audebert held the lordship of Puyguilhem; and Raymond became bishop of Périgueux and later archbishop of Bordeaux.

阿达尔贝尔三世（约1065—1116）是佩里戈尔伯爵阿达尔贝尔二世·卡杜瓦拉克之子。兄长埃利三世于1101或1104年去世后，他与埃利的诸子共同执掌伯国：先与侄子纪尧姆三世·塔列朗共治至1115年，1116年又与埃利·吕德尔短暂共治。

他的儿子中，博松四世后来成为伯爵；奥德贝尔领有皮伊吉扬；雷蒙曾任佩里格主教，后升任波尔多大主教。

en:
The Chronicle of Saint-Maixent records Boso, called the Old, as the son of Sulpice. Around 950 he held the Limousin frontier march, building the castle of Bellac as its seat, and is regarded as the first count of La Marche.

Through his marriage to Emma of Périgord he also succeeded to the county of Périgord. From about 968 he warred with Géraud of Limoges and died soon after, dividing his lands among his three eldest sons, Hélie, Adalbert and Boso.

en:
Boso II, third son of Boso the Old, succeeded his brother Adalbert I as count of La Marche and Périgord in 997, despite the claims of Adalbert's young son Bernard. In 1000 he fought for his suzerain William V of Aquitaine against Adémar of Limoges.

The chronicler Adémar de Chabannes accused Boso's unnamed wife of poisoning him after his return from Rome. By William V's award of 1008, Périgord passed to Boso's son Hélie and La Marche to his nephew Bernard I.

en:
Boso III (c. 990–1031/1044), count of Périgord, was probably a younger son of Boso II. He succeeded his brother Hélie II around 1033, possibly after ruling at his side as co-count.

By his wife Contor he had his successor Hélie VI Talleyrand, two sons who became monks and another who became an abbot; his daughter Jourdaine married Archambaud V of Comborn.

en:
Brunissende of Foix (died September 1324), daughter of Roger-Bernard III, Count of Foix, and Margaret, Viscountess of Béarn, married Count Hélie IX of Périgord in 1298 with a dowry of six thousand livres. Widowed in 1311, she ruled the county as regent during the minority of her son Archambaud.

She was widely believed to hold great sway at the new Avignon curia; chroniclers even rumored she was the mistress of Pope Clement V, and she secured rich church benefices for her son Hélie, later an influential cardinal. Her sons Archambaud and Roger-Bernard each became Count of Périgord.

Guillaume III Talleyrand (c. 1080–1115), elder son of Hélie III, was count of Périgord from 1104. From 1104 or 1107 his charters name him with his uncle Adalbert III and brother Hélie Rudel.

He was only the second member of the dynasty to bear Talleyrand, originally a nickname that later became the family name. His son Hélie IV was still living in 1131, but the succession passed to his brother Hélie Rudel.

en:
Hélie I (died 976 or 977), eldest son of Boso the Old and Emma of Périgord, was count of La Marche and Périgord. In 974 he fought beside his father against Géraud of Limoges and succeeded to La Marche when Boso died. In 975 his uncle Ranulf Bompar, count of Périgord, was killed and Hélie inherited that county.

After he blinded Benedict, intended as bishop of Limoges, Guy I captured Hélie and Adalbert and imprisoned them at Montignac. He escaped for Rome to seek papal pardon but died on the way; Adalbert inherited Périgord.

en:
Hélie II, count of Périgord, was a son of Boso II. When Boso died, the two counties were meant to pass to his nephew Bernard, but William V of Aquitaine kept La Marche for Bernard and gave Périgord to the under-age Hélie, opening the line that held Périgord for four centuries.

He married Adèle and left sons including Aldebert II. He last appears in a papal letter of 1031 and probably died soon afterwards.

Hélie IX (c. 1261–1311) was Count of Périgord from 1294, son of Archambaud III. In 1276 he married Philippa, heiress of her brother Vézian III, Viscount of Lomagne and Auvillars; after Vézian's death in 1280 Mathe de Bordeaux disputed the claim before the English duke of Aquitaine, though he kept Lomagne until Philippa's death in 1286.

He married Brunissende of Foix in 1298. In 1301 he ceded both lands to Philip IV of France to keep them from English sway. He died in 1311, leaving Archambaud IV a minor under Brunissende's regency.

Hélie V, called Rudel (c. 1083–1149), the younger son of Hélie III, ruled Périgord from 1115, after years beside his brother Guillaume III and their uncle Adalbert III. His bitter war against Adémar le Barbu of Limoges cost the lives of his own sons.

en:
Hélie VI Talleyrand (c. 1136–1203) was count of Périgord from 1166, succeeding his father Boson IV. In 1181 he answered the troubadour Bertran de Born’s call and joined the Aquitanian lords’ revolt against Richard the Lionheart, submitting in 1182.

When Richard was imprisoned in 1192, he rebelled again, allied with King Philip Augustus and Count Raymond V of Toulouse, but ducal forces defeated him once more. His last charter dates to 1203–1204, and his son Hélie VII succeeded.

Hélie VII Talleyrand (c. 1150–c. 1209) succeeded his father Hélie VI as count of Périgord around 1203–1204. In 1204 he swore liege homage to King Philip Augustus of France, ending the county’s long vassalage to the dukes of Aquitaine; John Lackland accepted the change only in 1214.

He married Marguerite of Limoges, and their son Archambaud II did homage for the county to the French king in 1212.

Hélie VIII (c. 1210/1215–1247/1251) succeeded his father Archambaud II as count of Périgord in 1239. In 1245 he confirmed his father’s grant of Grignols to Boson Talleyrand, founder of the Talleyrand-Périgord line.

en:
Roger-Bernard (c. 1299–1361), a younger son of Count Hélie IX and Brunissende of Foix, became Count of Périgord in 1334 when his childless brother Archambaud IV died. Until 1340 he contested the lordship of Bergerac with Mathe d’Albret, the wife of his late brother.

With the Hundred Years’ War, Périgord came under repeated attack: the Earl of Derby raided it in 1345, and in 1356 the Black Prince entered Périgueux unopposed, on the ride that ended at Poitiers with King John II’s capture. The Treaty of Brétigny in 1360 put the county under English sovereignty. Roger-Bernard died the next year, and his son Archambaud V succeeded him.

Giovanni Malatesta, called Gianciotto the Lame (c. 1245–1304), was the second son of Malatesta da Verucchio of Rimini. From 1265 he fought in Romagna against Guido da Montefeltro's Ghibellines and helped rule papal Rimini.

In 1285 he found his wife Francesca da Polenta in the arms of his brother Paolo and killed them both, a murder Dante placed in Inferno. Expelled from Rimini with his family in 1288, he served five times as podestà of Pesaro, dying there in 1304.

en:
Philibert Orry, comte de Vignory (1689–1747), was a French administrator and the longest-serving finance minister of his century. Born in Troyes, the son of the economist Jean Orry, he was a cavalry captain in the War of the Spanish Succession before serving as an intendant.

Appointed controller-general in 1730, he restored the dixième tax, fostered textiles and porcelain manufacture, and balanced the budget in 1739–1740. From 1736 he also ran the king's buildings, founded the Paris Salon, and built France's road network through the corvée.

In 1738 he instructed intendants to require inhabitants to work two weeks a year on roads. Madame de Pompadour's hostility forced his resignation in 1745.

菲利贝尔·奥里，维尼奥里伯爵（1689—1747），是法国大臣，也是那个世纪在任最久的财政总监。他生于特鲁瓦，父亲是经济学家让·奥里，曾在西班牙王位继承战争中任骑兵上尉，之后担任地方督办。

1730年，他被任命为财政总监，恢复十分之一税，扶持纺织业和瓷器制造，并于1739—1740年实现预算平衡。1736年起他又兼管王室建筑，创立巴黎沙龙展，并以王家劳役修筑法国公路网。

1738年，他指示地方督办要求居民每年服役两周修路。在蓬帕杜夫人的敌视下，他于1745年去职。

en:
Philipp Apian (1531–1589), born Philipp Bienewitz in Ingolstadt, was a mathematician, physician and cartographer, the son of Peter Apian. He succeeded his father as professor of mathematics at Ingolstadt in 1552.

In 1554 Duke Albert V of Bavaria commissioned him to survey the duchy; after seven summers in the field he completed a huge map in 1563, followed in 1568 by the 24-sheet Bairische Landtafeln, the first detailed atlas of a European country. A Protestant, he left Ingolstadt in 1569 amid the Counter-Reformation and lost his Tübingen chair in 1583 for refusing to condemn Calvinism.

菲利普·阿皮安（1531—1589），本名菲利普·比内维茨，生于英戈尔施塔特，是数学家、医生与制图家，彼得·阿皮安之子。1552年他继父之位任英戈尔施塔特大学数学教授。

1554年，巴伐利亚公爵阿尔布雷希特五世委托他测绘公国；他用七个夏天实地勘测，于1563年绘成一幅巨型地图，又在1568年推出24幅分图组成的《巴伐利亚地图集》——欧洲第一部精确描绘单个国家的专用地图集。作为新教徒，他于1569年在反宗教改革中离开英戈尔施塔特，1583年因拒绝谴责加尔文宗而被解除蒂宾根大学的教职。

Catherine de la Tour du Pin (c. 1290–1337) was a daughter of Humbert I, Dauphin of Viennois. In 1312 she married Philip I of Savoy-Achaia, lord of Piedmont and prince of Achaea, and bore him eleven children. Her eldest son James succeeded Philip as lord of Piedmont in 1334.

Several sons entered the Church, among them Edward, Archbishop of Tarentaise, and Thomas, bishop of Turin. Her daughter Beatrice married Humbert VI of Thoire in 1334. Catherine died in 1337.

en:
Pierre Boaistuau (c. 1517–1566) was a French humanist writer, translator and compiler born in Nantes and trained in civil and canon law. Around 1550 he served the French ambassador Jean-Jacques of Cambrai and travelled through Italy and Germany, later visiting England and meeting Elizabeth I.

His Théâtre du monde appeared in 1558, and he was the first editor of Marguerite of Navarre's nouvelles, later the Heptaméron. His Histoires tragiques of 1559 translated six tales by Bandello, including Romeo and Juliet, which reached Shakespeare through English adaptations, and he introduced the tragic and prodigious tale as literary genres in France.

皮埃尔·博瓦斯蒂奥（约1517—1566）是法国人文主义作家、翻译家和编纂者，生于南特，受过民法与教会法训练。约1550年，他为法国使节让-雅克·德·康布雷效力，游历意大利和德意志，后来访问英格兰、觐见过伊丽莎白一世。

他的《世界剧场》于1558年问世，并首次编订了纳瓦拉的玛格丽特的短篇故事集，即后世所称的《七日谈》。1559年出版的《悲剧故事》翻译了班戴洛的六篇小说，其中包括《罗密欧与朱丽叶》；这一故事经英文改写传到了莎士比亚那里。博瓦斯蒂奥把悲剧故事和奇异故事两种文学体裁引入法国。

en:
Pietro Perugino (c. 1446–1523), born Pietro Vannucci at Città della Pieve, was the leading painter of the Umbrian Renaissance. Trained in Florence in Andrea del Verrocchio's workshop alongside Leonardo da Vinci, he was enrolled as a master by 1472.

Summoned to Rome in 1479, he led painters including Botticelli and Ghirlandaio in decorating the new Sistine Chapel from 1481, contributing the Delivery of the Keys. In Perugia he frescoed the Collegio del Cambio in 1496–1500 with planets, classical figures and his own portrait. He trained Raphael, his most famous pupil, and died of plague at Fontignano in 1523.

彼得罗·佩鲁吉诺（约1446—1523）原名彼得罗·万努奇，生于翁布里亚的皮耶韦城，是翁布里亚文艺复兴画派的代表画家。他在佛罗伦萨安德烈亚·德尔·韦罗基奥的作坊学艺，与列奥纳多·达·芬奇同窗，1472年已登记为画师。

1479年他应召前往罗马，1481年起率领波提切利、吉兰达约等画师装饰新建的西斯廷礼拜堂，《交付钥匙》即出自其手。1496至1500年，他在佩鲁贾为汇兑行会大厅绘制湿壁画，画中有行星、古代人物及他的自画像。他最著名的学生是拉斐尔，1523年他在丰蒂尼亚诺死于鼠疫。

Atula Maha Dhamma Dewi (born c. 1295), whose personal name was Saw Min Ya, was the chief queen consort of King Uzana I of Pinya. A daughter of King Kyawswa of Pagan, Pagan's last reigning king, and Queen Saw Soe, she was Uzana's half-sister by the same father.

When Uzana took the Pinya throne in 1325 she became his chief queen and held that position until 1340. Her two sons were princes of Pinya, and she was a paternal aunt of King Swa Saw Ke of Ava.

Atula Sanda Dewi, whose personal name was Nan Lon Me, was born a Pagan princess around 1312. Her grandfather Kyawswa, a king of Pagan, was forced to abdicate by the three Myinsaing brothers in December 1297, and her father Saw Hnit then governed Pagan for them as viceroy until 1325.

She became chief queen consort of Kyawswa I, who ruled Pinya from 1344 to 1350. Her three sons Uzana II, Kyawswa II and Narathu each succeeded to the Pinya throne and were the kingdom's last three kings before Pinya fell in 1364. She died around 1357, before the dynasty's end.

en:
Kyaswa (1198–1251) ruled the Pagan kingdom of Burma from 1235, succeeding his father Htilominlo. A devout Buddhist scholar, he left most administration to his son Uzana and devoted himself to religious writing and patronage of orthodox Theravada monks.

His peaceful reign saw the royal treasury drained by vast tax-free monastic estates; his attempt to reclaim land from forest-dwelling monks was reversed under public pressure. Kyaswa refused to use forced labour in building temples, so his Pyathada Temple at Pagan was smaller than many built by his predecessors.

In 1249 he had stone edicts erected in the empire's villages ordering humane punishments and banning the impaling of thieves. He died in 1251.

他在位时天下大体太平，但免税的寺院领地日广，王室府库空虚；他试图收回森林僧团的土地，却迫于舆论作罢。加苏瓦不愿征发劳役建寺，他在蒲甘修建的比亚达寺比许多前代寺庙规模都小。

1249年，他下令在帝国各村勒石立敕，规定宽和用刑，禁止将盗贼刺穿处死。加苏瓦于1251年去世。

en:
Kyawswa I (1299–1350), called Nga-zi Shin or Lord of the Five White Elephants, was king of Pinya from 1344 to 1350. The elder son of Thihathu and the Pagan princess Mi Saw U, he ranked second in line behind his half-brother Uzana.

Governor of Pinle, the family's base, from 1313, he was beaten back by Saw Yun at Sagaing in 1316; after Uzana took the throne in 1325 he built up his own power at Pinle. In 1340 he refused Uzana's demands for his five rare white elephants, and Uzana abdicated to become a monk. Kyawswa called himself king by 1342 and took over formally in 1344.

He raised cavalry and shield infantry and tended the Kyaukse granary, and his reign was largely peaceful. He died suddenly in 1350 and became the nat Nga-zi Shin.

en:
Kyawswa (1260–1299) became king of Pagan in 1289 with the support of the dowager queen Pwa Saw, after the collapse following his father Narathihapate's murder; he had governed Dala since 1285. His rule barely reached beyond Pagan city, while real power in the Kyaukse granary belonged to the three Myinsaing brothers, recognised by him as viceroys in 1293.

To counter them he sent his son Theingapati to the Yuan and received Mongol recognition as a vassal king in March 1297. That December the brothers invited him to a monastery dedication at Myinsaing, then seized him and forced him into monkhood. They executed him on 10 May 1299.

en:
Kyawswa II (1328–1359), Lord of the Four White Elephants after inheriting the animals from his father, was king of Pinya from December 1350. A younger son, he had been made heir over his elder brother Uzana, whose legs were paralysed. His authority scarcely reached beyond the Kyaukse granary; Prome and Toungoo were nearly independent.

Pressure from the north shaped his reign. Mong Mao, whose ruler Tho Kho Bwa had defeated three Mongol expeditions, was turning on Sagaing, and in 1351 Kyawswa accepted a truce proposed by envoys from Sagaing.

In 1358–59 Toungoo raided Kyaukse while Maw Shans broke through Sagaing's territory into Pinya. Kyawswa died in March 1359 during the raids, childless, and his brother Narathu succeeded him. A week earlier, on 12 March, he had issued a decree ordering checks on tax-free religious lands, Burma's earliest recorded land survey.

en:
Mi Saw U was a princess of Pagan, daughter of Narathihapate, the last sovereign king of that dynasty. She was first married to her half-brother Kyawswa of Pagan. In December 1297 Thihathu of Myinsaing overthrew Kyawswa and seized her, pregnant with Kyawswa's son Uzana, making her his chief queen.

Eager to pass as Pagan's rightful heir, Thihathu raised Uzana as his own child and named him heir apparent, while her son by Thihathu, Kyawswa, became governor of Pinle in 1313. Both sons went on to rule Pinya as kings. Her youngest son Nawrahta quarrelled with Kyawswa and defected to Sagaing around 1349.

en:
Narathihapate (1238–1287), last king of the Pagan Empire, reigned from 1256, when Minister Yazathingyan placed him over his half-brother Thihathu. He once exiled Yazathingyan, then recalled him to crush revolts in Martaban and Arakan. Growing tax-free religious estates had long drained the treasury, yet he built the Mingalazedi Pagoda with forced labour.

In the Mongol invasions of 1277–1287 he fled Pagan for Lower Burma in 1285, earning the byname 'Taruk-Pyay Min', king who fled the Chinese. He submitted to Kublai Khan in January 1287, and that July his son Thihathu, Viceroy of Prome, forced him to take poison, after which the empire broke apart.

那腊底哈勃德（1238—1287）是蒲甘王朝末代国王，1256年大臣耶娑梯犍撇开他的异母兄梯伽都，把他扶上王位。他曾流放耶娑梯犍，后来又召回他平定马都八与阿腊干的叛乱。不断扩大的免税宗教地产长期消耗着王室府库，那腊底哈勃德仍征发民力修建弥伽罗佛塔。

en:
Narathu (c. 1333–1364?) ruled Pinya from 1359, succeeding his brother Kyawswa II. Toungoo had rebelled and raided Kyaukse, and Narathu lacked the strength to control his vassals.

He abandoned Pinya's alliance with Sagaing and, after Mong Mao Shans raided deep into his lands in 1362–1363, took the junior role under their ruler Tho Kho Bwa in a joint attack on Sagaing. His blockade of the Irrawaddy failed, allowing Sagaing's royalty to escape when the Shans sacked the city in April 1364.

Tho Kho Bwa then sacked Pinya that May, carrying Narathu and his white elephants off to the Shan country. Narathu is remembered as Maw-Pa Min, the king taken to the Maw land.

en:
Nawrahta of Kanni (b. 1300) was the youngest son of King Thihathu of Pinya and his chief queen Mi Saw U. On 7 February 1313 his father enfeoffed him with the town of Shisha.

When the Myinsaing kingdom split into Pinya and Sagaing in 1315, he stayed with his father's Pinya side. In March 1344 his brother Kyawswa took the throne and made him governor of Pinle, the family's ancestral base, but the two soon became rivals.

In 1349 Nawrahta fled west to Sagaing, where his nephew Nawrahta Minye had just become king and made him governor of Kanni. Later chronicles trace King Bayinnaung of the Toungoo dynasty back to him as a maternal great-great-great-grandfather.

Saw Hnit (1283–1325) was viceroy of Pagan from 1297 to 1325 under the suzerainty of the Myinsaing kingdom. A son of King Kyawswa of Pagan, he was placed on the throne by the three Myinsaing brothers after they forced his father to abdicate in December 1297. Though styled king of Pagan, his authority reached only the lands around the city.

He gave his first audience on 8 May 1299, two days before the brothers executed Kyawswa. On his death in 1325 his son Uzana succeeded him.

en:
Saw Soe (1250–1334) was a principal queen consort of King Kyawswa of the Pagan dynasty of Burma. She was the daughter of Yazathingyan, chief minister and commander-in-chief of the Pagan army. The royal chronicles name her Kyawswa's chief queen, although modern historians give that position to Saw Thitmahti.

Her children included Saw Hnit, viceroy of Pagan, and Min Shin Saw, as well as queens of Pinya and Sagaing, and she was grandmother of King Swa Saw Ke of Ava.

en:
Sithu Min Oo (born c. late 1310s) was the elder son of King Uzana I of Pinya and a longtime claimant to its throne. When Uzana took the throne in 1325 Sithu was technically heir presumptive, but he may never have been proclaimed heir apparent, and the chronicles record no governorship for him, while his younger brother Thihapate ruled Yamethin.

He nonetheless survived the fall of Pinya in 1364 and the founding of Ava in 1365. King Swa Saw Ke of Ava, seeking his prestige, gave Sithu his daughter Minkhaung Medaw in marriage, and through that line Sithu became an ancestor of the Toungoo kings Mingyi Nyo, Tabinshwehti and Nanda.

en:
Tarabya I (1297–1339) was king of Sagaing in central Burma from 1327 to 1336. The son of Queen Yadanabon by her first husband, he was adopted by her consort King Thihathu of Pinya. When his half-brother Saw Yun founded Sagaing in 1315, Tarabya joined him as his deputy and succeeded him in 1327.

In 1336 his son Shwetaungtet deposed and imprisoned him. Tarabya escaped and had Shwetaungtet killed in 1339, but was himself executed by minister Nanda Pakyan.

德勒帕耶基（1297—1339）是缅甸实皆王国国王，1327至1336年在位。他是王后娅达娜邦与前夫之子，被娅达娜邦的丈夫、彬牙王梯诃都收为养子。1315年同母异父的弟弟苏云兴建实皆城时，他前往投奔，成为苏云的副手，并于1327年继位。

en:
The Burmese chronicles describe Theinkha Bo as a son of the sawbwa (chief) of Binnaka. After quarrelling with his elder brother, who had inherited the chieftainship, he left Binnaka and settled at Myinsaing, where in 1260 he married.

His three sons Athinkhaya, Yazathingyan and Thihathu became commanders relied on by King Narathihapate of Pagan, and in 1297 founded the Myinsaing dynasty that replaced Pagan rule. His descendants later ruled Pinya, Sagaing and Ava.

en:
Thihapate (c. 1318–c. 1351), also called Chauk-Hse Shin, the Lord of Sixty Elephants, was the second son of King Uzana I of Pinya. Uzana had held the throne since 1325 but never shook off his rival Kyawswa, and came to rely on this younger son.

In the late 1330s he made him governor of Yamethin, where Thihapate kept sixty war elephants and a large standing army. When Kyawswa I drove Uzana from power between 1340 and 1344, Thihapate weighed rebellion, but the governor of Nyaungyan would not join him, and he submitted after Kyawswa sent a rare black stallion from Onbaung.

The chronicles do not mention him again, and by 1351 Swa Saw Ke governed Yamethin, so Thihapate may have died or been removed from office.

1330年代末，他任命梯诃波帝为央米丁总督，梯诃波帝在当地常备六十头战象和大批兵马。1340至1344年间，觉苏瓦一世把乌兹那逐下王位，梯诃波帝考虑过起兵，良渊总督却不肯同行；觉苏瓦送来一匹出自翁榜的罕见黑色骏马示好，他便归顺。

此后编年史不再提及他。1351年央米丁已由斯伐修寄执掌，梯诃波帝可能已去世，或已被免职。

en:
Thihathu (1265–1325) was the founder of Burma's Pinya Kingdom. The youngest of three brothers from Myinsaing, he helped drive back Mongol invasions, and in 1298 the brothers overthrew King Kyawswa of Pagan, reducing it to a puppet state. After proclaiming himself king in 1309, he pushed aside his brother Yazathingyan after their eldest brother's death in 1310 and became sole ruler.

In 1313 he moved his capital to Pinya, styling himself Pagan's successor. His adoption of Kyawswa's son Uzana as heir drove his own son Saw Yun to found rival Sagaing in 1315, and when Thihathu died in 1325 Pinya and Sagaing became separate kingdoms.

en:
Uzana I (1298–c. 1357) was king of Pinya in central Burma from 1325 to 1340. He was born to King Kyawswa of Pagan and Mi Saw U six months after his father's overthrow, and was adopted at birth by the usurper Thihathu. At his coronation at Pinya in 1313, Thihathu named Uzana heir-apparent.

When Thihathu died in 1325 the kingdom split in two. Uzana kept Pinya but could not retake Sagaing in the north, and his southernmost vassals were practically independent. His real rival was his half-brother Kyawswa of Pinle, who held court nearby with his own army.

When Kyawswa twice refused to hand over five rare white elephants, Uzana abdicated in 1340 and spent his remaining years as a monk at Mekkhaya.

乌兹那一世（1298—约1357）是缅甸彬牙王国国王，1325至1340年在位。他是蒲甘王觉苏瓦与弥修乌之子，生于父亲被废黜半年之后，出生即被篡位者梯诃都收养。1313年梯诃都在彬牙加冕，立乌兹那为王储。

1325年梯诃都去世，王国一分为二。乌兹那据有彬牙，却无力收复北方的实皆，最南端的诸侯近乎独立。他真正的对手是同母异父弟觉苏瓦，后者据守邻近的宾里，拥有自己的军队。

觉苏瓦两次拒绝献上五头稀有的白象，乌兹那于1340年退位，晚年在梅卡亚出家为僧。

en:
Uzana (1213–1256) ruled the Pagan kingdom of Burma from 1251 to 1256, though he already held full authority under his devout father Kyaswa. He left government to his chief minister Yazathingyan, preferring to drink and hunt elephants.

In May 1256 he was accidentally trampled to death by an elephant while hunting near Dala. His death opened a succession struggle: his eldest son Thihathu claimed the throne, but Yazathingyan's court secured the crown for Narathihapate, Uzana's son by a concubine.

zh:
乌兹那（1213—1256）于1251年至1256年统治缅甸蒲甘王朝，而早在其父加苏瓦虔心礼佛之时，他便已总揽大权。他把治国实务交给首相耶娑梯犍，自己贪杯好猎象。

1256年5月，他在达拉附近猎象时意外被象踩踏身亡。他死后旋即爆发王位之争：长子梯诃都争位，耶娑梯犍为首的朝臣却把乌兹那庶妃所生之子那腊底哈勃德扶上王位。

en:
Uzana II (c. 1324–1364), called Pyaung, was the eldest son of King Kyawswa I of Pinya and spent his life in the shadow of his younger brothers. Because his legs were weak or crippled, his father chose his brother Kyawswa as heir; after Kyawswa became king, their brother Narathu ranked ahead of Uzana as well.

In May 1364 the Mong Mao Shans sacked Pinya and carried Narathu off, and in June the court elected the long-overlooked Uzana king. He ruled in name only for three months, with little authority even around the capital.

But his kinsman Thado Minbya, new king of ruined Sagaing, proved the abler leader. Seeing a chance to reunite central Burma, he crossed the Irrawaddy in September 1364, took Pinya without a fight and had Uzana put to death.

zh:
乌兹那比昂（约1324—1364）即乌兹那二世，是彬牙国王觉苏瓦一世的长子，一生都活在弟弟们的阴影里。由于他腿部无力或有残疾，父亲选了弟弟觉苏瓦为王储；觉苏瓦即位后，另一个弟弟那腊都又排在他之前。

1364年5月，麓川掸军攻破彬牙，掳走那腊都，6月朝廷推举久被忽视的乌兹那为王。他只做了三个月的名义国王，连都城周边也没有多少权威。

但他的亲族、已成废墟的实皆的新王德多明帕耶更有才干。德多明帕耶想趁机重新统一缅甸中部，1364年9月渡过伊洛瓦底江，兵不血刃攻取彬牙，随即将乌兹那处死。

en:
Yadanabon (c. 1280–?) was a queen of Thihathu, founder with his brothers of the Myinsaing kingdom and later ruler of Pinya in central Burma. The chronicles describe her as a commoner from the northern village of Linyin, a widow travelling south with her one-year-old child, whom Thihathu met on a hunting trip and took as a concubine.

She bore his first son Saw Yun, who founded the rival kingdom of Sagaing in 1315, and a daughter Saw Pale, and was then raised to Queen of the Northern Palace. Her line outlasted Pinya's: her descendants included Sagaing's later kings and Thado Minbya, founder of the Ava Kingdom.

zh:
娅达娜邦（约1280年生）是梯诃都的王后之一。梯诃都与兄弟一同建立敏象王国，后来成为缅甸中部彬牙王国的君主。编年史记载，她本是北方林因村的平民，身为寡妇的她带着一岁的孩子南行，遇上外出狩猎的梯诃都，被纳为妾。

她生下梯诃都的长子苏云——1315年他建立了与彬牙对峙的实皆王国——又生下女儿梭巴列，随后被立为北宫王后。她的血脉比彬牙存续得更久：后裔中有实皆后来的几位国王，以及阿瓦王国的建立者他拖弥婆耶。

en:
Andrea Gambacorta (c. 1290–1351), head of a leading Pisan family of popolani, traded woollen cloth in Pisa. In 1325 he proposed measures to protect Pisan merchants competing with Genoa for Florentine freight.

When Pisa's signore Ranieri Novello della Gherardesca died in 1347, the leading families split into two parties: the Bergolini, named from the young count's nickname Bergo, and their rivals, mocked as Raspanti for their greed. They fought in council and then in the streets, and Andrea, leader of the Bergolini, led the rising that drove the Raspanti chiefs out in December.

He then dominated Pisa and subject Lucca until his death in 1351, ruling through the Anziani with his nephew Francesco. His son Pietro ruled Pisa from 1369.

安德烈亚·甘巴科尔塔（约1290—1351）是比萨平民望族的族长，在比萨经营毛织品贸易。1325年他提出措施，保护与热那亚人竞争佛罗伦萨货运的比萨商人。

1347年比萨统治者拉涅里·诺韦洛·德拉·盖拉尔代斯卡去世后，城中望族分成两派：一派自称贝尔戈利尼，名字取自年轻伯爵的绰号“贝尔戈”；对手则被他们讥为拉斯潘蒂，意指其贪得无厌。双方先在议会中交锋，继而在街巷厮杀，贝尔戈利尼派首领安德烈亚于12月领导起义，将拉斯潘蒂派首领逐出城外。

此后他左右比萨及臣服的卢卡，直至1351年去世；他依靠长老会议与侄子弗朗切斯科执政。其子彼得罗于1369年起统治比萨。

en:
Buonaccorso Gambacorta, known as Coscio, was a Pisan merchant and politician, son of Vernaccio and brother of Gherardo. In 1295 he joined a trading partnership in Sardinia whose ships carried various goods. He first served among Pisa's elders in 1297 and held the office repeatedly until 1312.

In 1309 he joined an embassy to Barcelona that proposed placing Pisa under King James II of Aragon. He died in Pisa before 1330.

博纳科尔索·甘巴科尔塔，绰号“科肖”，是比萨商人兼政治家，韦尔纳乔之子、盖拉尔多的兄弟。1295年，他在撒丁岛加入贸易合伙，船只运载各类货物。他于1297年首次出任比萨长老，此后多次担任该职，直至1312年。

Eldizio Visconti was a 12th-century Pisan patrician, the son of Alberto Visconti and Aligarda, and served as consul of Pisa in 1184–1185. He married a daughter of Torchitorio III, judge of Cagliari, a match through which his sons could claim rights in Sardinia.

Emilia della Gherardesca was born in Pisa in the spring of 1328, the daughter of Bonifazio Novello della Gherardesca, called Fazio Novello, signore of Pisa, and his wife Bertecca Castracani.

She became the second wife of Ugolino Gonzaga, co-lord of Mantua, whose first wife Verde della Scala had died in 1340. Emilia herself died at Mantua in 1349 and was buried in the city's Cathedral of San Pietro.

en:
Bonifazio della Gherardesca, known as Fazio (c. 1250–1312), was a Pisan nobleman, a son of Gherardo della Gherardesca “il Vecchio” and Teodora of Montferrat.

After Pisa overthrew the giudicato of Cagliari in 1258, his father gained Sardinian territory including the curatorie of Sulcis, Nora and Decimo, which later passed to Bonifazio and his brother Ranieri. Their cousin Guelfo seized them, but Ranieri retook the region by storming Villa di Chiesa in 1295.

Bonifazio served as a Pisan admiral and fought at the battle of Meloria in 1284. His son Gherardo was the father of Fazio Novello, later lord of Pisa.

1258年比萨攻灭卡利亚里王国后，他的父亲获得撒丁岛上的领地，其中苏尔奇斯、诺拉和德奇莫辖区后来传给博尼法乔与兄弟拉涅里；堂亲圭尔福强占这些地方，1295年拉涅里攻破基耶萨镇，收复该地区。

博尼法乔曾任比萨海军将领，参加1284年的梅洛里亚海战。他的儿子盖拉尔多是后来的比萨领主法齐奥·诺韦洛之父。

en:
Bonifazio Novello della Gherardesca, known as Fazio Novello (c. 1305–1340), was the only son of Gherardo Gaddo, count of Donoratico. In 1327 he was among those who accepted Emperor Louis the Bavarian as lord of Pisa; when imperial rule bred discontent, he led the revolt of June 1329 that expelled the imperial vicar, Tarlato of Arezzo, and took power.

That August he made peace with Florence and returned Pisa to papal obedience. In 1332 he beat back a coup by exiles under the former bishop Gherardo Orlandi, and in 1335 he put down a rising of noble and popular houses, an event recalled by a victory tower at the Ponte di Spina.

The Studium Pisano was founded under his rule in 1338. He died on 22 December 1340, and his son Ranieri Novello took over Pisa.

博尼法齐奥·诺韦洛·德拉·盖拉尔代斯卡，人称“法齐奥·诺韦洛”（约1305—1340），是多诺拉蒂科伯爵盖拉尔多·加多的独子。1327年，他是同意奉皇帝巴伐利亚的路德维希为比萨之主的人之一；皇帝治下民怨渐深，1329年6月他领导公开起义，赶走皇帝的代理人阿雷佐的塔尔拉托，接掌大权。

同年8月，他与佛罗伦萨缔和，让比萨重新服从教皇。1332年他击退以前主教盖拉尔多·奥兰迪为首的流亡者发动的政变，1335年又镇压贵族与平民望族的联合叛乱，斯皮纳桥头的胜利塔便是为纪念此事而建。

比萨学园于1338年在他治下设立。他于1340年12月22日去世，儿子拉涅里·诺韦洛接掌比萨。

en:
Francesco Gambacorta (c. 1300–1355), son of Buonaccorso di Gherardo and nephew of Andrea, was a wealthy Pisan merchant who served five terms as an elder. In 1348 he helped design the Massa delle Prestanze, which consolidated the commune's debts at ten percent, secured by iron revenues from Pisan-held Elba.

After 1349 he oversaw the commune's mounted mercenaries, and when Andrea died in 1351 he inherited leadership of the Bergolini faction and shared power with his brothers.

In 1355 their opponents blamed them for a revolt against Emperor Charles IV. Francesco was arrested, tortured and condemned, and executed with his brothers on 26 May.

Gherardo Gambacorta, also known as Gaddo, was a Pisan merchant and brother of Buonaccorso, called Coscio. In 1294 he lent 262 ounces of gold to Charles II of Anjou for a journey to Rome. He served among the elders of Pisa in 1297, following his brother's election earlier that year.

The brothers held property around Pisa and in Sardinia and made loans together. Under Ranieri della Gherardesca's rule in 1321–1325, they were among the merchants charged with the largest forced loans.

en:
Gherardo della Gherardesca, called Gaddo or il Giovane (c. 1284–1320), son of Bonifazio di Gherardo, was the Pisan popular leader who helped overthrow Uguccione della Faggiola. In April 1316 Pisa's mercantile families, with his backing, revolted against Uguccione's harsh signoria and drove him out, and Gherardo held the post of capitano del popolo from April to June.

He then shaped city policy through the commissions of sapientes and commanded the commune's mounted mercenaries. In 1317 his government made peace with the Tuscan Guelf cities at Naples. He died suddenly in 1320; his uncle Ranieri Nieri took power and became guardian to Gherardo's underage son Bonifazio.

Gherardo della Gherardesca, called il Vecchio (1198–1268), was the tenth of his name in the great Ghibelline house of Pisa. He fought in Pisa's Sardinian war against the pro-Genoese giudicato of Cagliari and shared the partition after its capital Santa Igia fell in 1258, receiving several curatorie with his kinsman Ugolino.

He then followed Conradin of Hohenstaufen against Charles I of Anjou, was captured at Tagliacozzo in 1268, and beheaded in Naples on 29 October.

Gherardo della Gherardesca was the youngest son of Count Ranieri della Gherardesca, il Vecchio. On his brother Bernabò's death he inherited the title count of Donoratico and his family's Sulcis fiefs in Sardinia.

In September 1353, early in the Sardo-Catalan war, Arborean commanders captured him and Judge Mariano IV persuaded him to back Arborea. He died in Sardinia in January 1355, after which King Peter IV of Aragon sentenced him posthumously for treason and confiscated all his lands.

en:
Ranieri della Gherardesca, called Nieri (c. 1252–1325), was a son of Gherardo il Vecchio, beheaded at Naples with Conradin in 1268. Forced to leave Pisa for Sardinia in 1285, he returned to the island in 1294 to lead a Pisan expedition, defeating the sons of his rival Ugolino in 1295.

He hosted Emperor Henry VII at Pisa in 1313 and fought at Montecatini in 1315, where he had himself knighted over the body of Charles of Anjou, nephew of King Robert of Naples.

After his nephew Gherardo il Giovane died suddenly in 1320, Ranieri took charge of Pisa and ruled until his death on 13 December 1325.

1320年其侄盖拉尔多“年轻者”暴毙后，拉涅里接掌比萨，统治直至1325年12月13日去世。

en:
Pietro Gambacorti (1319–1392) was a Pisan nobleman, son of Andrea Gambacorta. In 1355 an uprising supported by Emperor Charles IV overthrew the regime of his kinsman Francesco, thought to lean too close to Florence, and the family was driven into exile.

Pietro returned to Pisa with his family in 1369 and, first as capitano delle masnade and then as doge, governed the republic until 1392. On 21 October 1392 he was assassinated by Jacopo d'Appiano, hungry for power and acting in agreement with Gian Galeazzo Visconti of Milan; his sons Lorenzo and Benedetto were killed in the same conspiracy. His daughter Chiara became a Dominican nun and was later beatified.

彼得罗·甘巴科尔塔（1319—1392）是比萨贵族，安德烈亚·甘巴科尔塔之子。1355年，一场得到皇帝查理四世支持的起义推翻了他的族人弗朗切斯科的政权，该政权被认为过于亲近佛罗伦萨，甘巴科尔塔家族被逐流亡。

彼得罗于1369年携家人返回比萨，先任佣兵队长，后任执政，统治比萨共和国直至1392年。1392年10月21日，他遭觊觎权位的雅各布·达皮亚诺暗杀，后者与米兰的詹·加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂暗中串通；其子洛伦佐与贝内代托也在同一阴谋中被杀。他的女儿基娅拉成为多明我会修女，后来受宣福。

Ranieri Novello della Gherardesca, also called Ranieri II, was the young son of Fazio Novello della Gherardesca, signore of Pisa. On his father's death he succeeded as count of Donoratico and ruled Pisa from 1341 to 1347 under the tutorship of Tinuccio della Rocca.

He was the last of the Donoratico lords. He died suddenly in 1347, after which Andrea Gambacorta took power in the city.

en:
Tinuccio della Rocca was a Pisan nobleman and a trusted agent of the counts of Donoratico. In 1326 he secured the Aragonese king's confirmation of the young count's Sardinian fiefs. After Bonifazio's death in 1340, Tinuccio became guardian to his son Ranieri Novello and governed Pisa in his name.

He helped capture Lucca in 1342, but a later Visconti war brought devastation and heavier taxes. Following Ranieri's sudden death in 1347, Tinuccio's opponents rose against him; his house was burned and he fled to Volterra.

She bore six children, including James Butler, 3rd Earl of Ormond, and Eleanor, wife of the Earl of Desmond. Widowed in 1382, she married Sir Robert de Hereford and died on 24 March 1390.

John Darcy, 2nd Baron Darcy de Knayth (c. 1317–1356), was the eldest son of the first baron and a northern English landowner. In the opening phase of the Hundred Years' War he commanded a company, fighting at Crécy in 1346 and the siege of Calais.

In 1347 he inherited his father's estates and the constableship of the Tower of London, and sat regularly in Parliament from 1348. In 1344 he married the heiress Elizabeth Meynell. He died at Notton on 5 March 1356.

John Darcy, 1st Baron Darcy de Knayth (c. 1290–1347), was an English peer and a trusted councillor of Edward III. Summoned to the barony in 1332, he served three terms as chief governor of Ireland from 1323 onward, and in 1324 presided over the witchcraft trial of Alice Kyteler.

He was the king's steward (1337–1340) and chamberlain (1342–1346), constable of the Tower of London, and fought at Crécy in 1346, carrying news of the victory back to Parliament. He died in 1347.

John de Burgh (1286–1313) was the eldest son and heir of Richard Óg de Burgh, the Red Earl of Ulster. On 30 September 1308 he married Elizabeth de Clare, sister of Gilbert de Clare, Earl of Gloucester; his own sister Maud married Gilbert the same year, sealing a double alliance.

Elizabeth joined him in Ireland in 1309 and on 17 September 1312 gave birth to William Donn, the future Earl of Ulster. John was killed in a minor skirmish at Galway on 18 June 1313, leaving the infant William as heir.

Sir John Morice (died 1362) was a Bedfordshire gentleman who spent most of his career in English Ireland, remembered for his keen, if not very successful, efforts to reform its government. He began in English noble service and sat for Bedfordshire in the Parliament of 1322.

In Ireland he was escheator from 1329 to 1336 and several times deputy justiciar. Charged with carrying out Edward III's reform ordinances of 1341, he governed as justiciar and was briefly lord chancellor, but his rule was judged inept and unpopular.

He was recalled in 1349 and died in England in 1362. His portrait in the Waterford Charter Roll is called the earliest of an Irish judge.

Richard Mór de Burgh (1194–1243), eldest son of William de Burgh, was a ward of the English crown after his father died in 1206 and came of age in 1214. Appointed seneschal of Munster in 1223, he claimed Connacht, his father's grant, and was confirmed in it in 1227. He served as justiciar of Ireland from 1228 to 1232.

In 1235 he drove Felim Ua Conchobair from Connacht with a feudal host, taking the title Lord of Connacht. In 1236 he built a castle at Loughrea and also founded Galway. He fell ill on a voyage to France and died in 1243.

Robert le Poer (died c. 1346) was an Irish judge and Crown official, possibly a younger son of Arnold le Poer, seneschal of Kilkenny. As a young man he served John Hastings and went with him to Gascony in 1307; by 1322 he was the Hastings family's bailiff in Ireland.

He became Chamberlain of North Wales in 1323, was appointed Lord High Treasurer of Ireland in 1327, and later served as Chief Baron of the Irish Exchequer.

Sir Walter Liath de Burgh was an Anglo-Irish noble, the eldest son of Sir William Liath de Burgh and Finola Ní Bhriain of Thomond. He is first recorded in 1326, when he and Sir Edmond de Burgh were named guardians of the peace and keepers of the late Earl of Ulster's lands in Connacht, Tipperary and Limerick.

He later quarrelled with the young Earl William Donn, who imprisoned him; Walter starved to death in the earl's castle in February 1332, a killing that led to the earl's own murder the following year.

William de Burgh (c. 1160–1205/1206) was an Anglo-Norman from Norfolk who went to Ireland with John, lord of Ireland, in 1185. Henry II made him governor of Limerick and granted him wide lands in Leinster and Munster, where he served as seneschal of Munster from 1201 to 1203. About 1193 he married a daughter of Domnall Mór Ó Briain, king of Thomond.

He campaigned in Desmond and Connacht and took the title Lord of Connacht in 1203. He died in winter 1205/1206 and was buried at Athassel Priory, which he had founded.

en:
Sir William Óg de Burgh was an Anglo-Irish noble and soldier, the third son of Richard Mor de Burgh, Lord of Connacht. He served in France under Henry III in 1245 and later fought in Scotland, before being drawn into the feudal wars of Ireland, where he killed the Lord of Desmond.

In 1270 he was killed fighting the Ua Conchobair kings of Connacht at the Battle of Áth an Chip. His son William Liath was an ancestor of the Mayo Burkes.

en:
Bolesław III of Płock (1322/1330–1351), son of Duke Wenceslaus and Elizabeth of Lithuania, inherited the duchy in 1336 under his uncles' regency and ruled from 1340. A Bohemian vassal who did homage to King John, he later drew close to Casimir III of Poland.

In 1351 he joined Casimir against his Lithuanian uncle Kęstutis, who accepted baptism and was placed in his custody; when Kęstutis escaped, Bolesław was killed pursuing him by an arrow at Mělník in August 1351. He died unmarried and lies in Płock Cathedral.

en:
Elizabeth Giedyminówna (c. 1301–1364) was a Lithuanian princess, the daughter of Grand Duke Gediminas. Around 1316 she married Wenceslaus, the Piast duke of Płock, and bore him two children, Anna and Bolesław III. After Wenceslaus died in 1336, she probably served as regent for her minor son until he came of age around 1340–1343.

In 1349 Bolesław granted her Wyszogród for life. She died on 2 June 1364 and was buried in Płock Cathedral.

en:
Wenceslaus of Płock (1293/1297–1336) was a Piast prince, son of Bolesław II of Płock and Kunigunde, and a grandson of Ottokar II of Bohemia. Inheriting Płock in 1313, he stayed neutral between Poland and the Teutonic Order, agreeing terms at Golub in 1321.

After Władysław I attacked Płock in 1325, he backed the Order in the war of 1326. Switching to Poland in 1329, he was invaded by King John of Bohemia and the Knights and forced to do homage to Bohemia. He died at Wyszogród in 1336, leaving a son, Bolesław III.

en:
Heinrich II, called the Bohemian (died 1302), was the eldest son of Heinrich I, Vogt of Plauen. First recorded in 1275 and knighted in 1289, he fought beside his father for King Adolf of Nassau against the Wettins.

In 1296 he became joint administrator of the fortress of Freyburg an der Unstrut, and in 1301 King Albert of Habsburg named him captain of Eger. He is last documented on 23 April 1302 and died soon afterwards, before his father; his son Heinrich III later held the Plauen lands.

Heinrich III of Plauen, called the Tall (c. 1284–1347/48), was Vogt of Plauen in the Vogtland. First documented in 1302, he was initially styled Heinrich of Seeberg after his wife Margarethe's family, and bore the nickname the Tall from 1312.

In March 1304 he submitted to King Albert I at Nuremberg, and later that year was appointed Landrichter of Eger. He died between February 1347 and May 1348.

en:
Demid Vladimirovich was a Pinsk prince of the Turov Izyaslavichi line, the middle of the three sons of Prince Vladimir Sviatopolkovich of Pinsk. In 1262 he and his brothers Fyodor and Yuri went to Nebl to congratulate the Galician-Volhynian prince Vasilko Romanovich on his victory over the Lithuanians near the town.

Demid outlived his brother Yuri, whom he mourned at his death around 1288–1292, and he then took over the Pinsk principality. He died after 1292.

Fyodor Vladimirovich was a Pinsk prince of the Turov Izyaslavichi line, the eldest of the three sons of Prince Vladimir of Pinsk. After the death of Mikhail of Pinsk he made himself ruler there.

1262年，他与兄弟杰米德、尤里一同向加利西亚—沃伦王公瓦西里科·罗曼诺维奇道贺，祝贺其在涅布利附近击败立陶宛人。一般认为他此时是平斯克诸王公中的最年长者，并曾纵容立陶宛人袭扰沃伦。1292年之后他仍在世。

en:
Mikhail Vladimirovich, called Mikhail of Pinsk, was a Rurikid prince of the Turov Izyaslavichi line, generally held to be a son of Vladimir Sviatopolkovich. He received the Pinsk principality from his uncle Rostislav Sviatopolkovich, who ruled it until 1232.

The Hypatian Chronicle places him at Pinsk in 1246–1247, when Daniel and Vasilko Romanovich fought the Lithuanian prince Lekovniy near the town; Mikhail tried to warn both sides. He died after 1247, and Pinsk passed to Fyodor Vladimirovich.

zh:
米哈伊尔·弗拉基米罗维奇，即平斯克的米哈伊尔，是留里克王朝图罗夫伊贾斯拉维奇一系的王公，一般认为是弗拉基米尔·斯维亚托波尔科维奇之子。他从叔父罗斯季斯拉夫·斯维亚托波尔科维奇手中接掌平斯克公国，后者统治当地至1232年。

《伊帕季耶夫编年史》在1246—1247年项下提到他：当时丹尼尔和瓦西里科·罗曼诺维奇兄弟在平斯克附近与立陶宛王公列科夫尼交战，米哈伊尔试图同时向双方示警。他在1247年后去世，平斯克随后转入费奥多尔·弗拉基米罗维奇之手。

en:
Rostislav Sviatopolkovich (died 1232), younger son of Sviatopolk Yurievich of Turov, was a prince of the Turov Izyaslavichi line. In 1228 he claimed Turov as senior of the dynasty, but it went to his cousin's son Yuri Andreevich; after his brother Vladimir died that year, their cousin Vladimir Glebovich took Pinsk, and Rostislav secured it only in 1229.

His sons seized Chartoryisk, but Daniel Romanovich of Galicia retook the town and captured them; in reply Rostislav sent troops to aid Vladimir of Kiev and Mikhail of Chernigov against Kamenets, without success. He ruled Pinsk until 1232.

罗斯季斯拉夫·斯维亚托波尔科维奇（卒于1232年）是图罗夫王公斯维亚托波尔克·尤里耶维奇的幼子，属图罗夫伊贾斯拉维奇一系。1228年，他以家族最年长者身份求领图罗夫，公位却归堂侄尤里·安德烈耶维奇；同年兄弟弗拉基米尔去世，堂兄弟弗拉基米尔·格列博维奇又占据平斯克，迟至1229年才取得该公国。

他的儿子们夺取恰尔托雷斯克后，加利西亚的丹尼尔·罗曼诺维奇收复该城并俘获他们；他遂发兵支援基辅的弗拉基米尔和切尔尼戈夫的米哈伊尔进攻卡缅涅茨，无功而返。他统治平斯克至1232年去世。

en:
Yaroslav Yurievich (1144–c. 1184) was a Rurikid prince of Pinsk, the son of Yuri Yaroslavich of Turov and Anna Vsevolodovna, and may have held Kletsk after his father's death.

He is found as prince of Pinsk in 1183, when he joined the campaign led by Grand Prince Sviatoslav Vsevolodovich of Kiev, alongside Mstislav of Goroden and Gleb of Dubrovitsa, which defeated the Polovtsian khan Konchak on the Orel river. Some historians infer that he died before 1190, when his brother Yaropolk is recorded holding Pinsk.

雅罗斯拉夫·尤里耶维奇（1144—约1184年）是留里克王朝的平斯克王公，图罗夫王公尤里·雅罗斯拉维奇与安娜·弗谢沃洛多芙娜之子，父亲死后可能领有克列茨克。

1183年，他以平斯克王公身份参加基辅大公斯维亚托斯拉夫·弗谢沃洛多维奇统率的远征，与戈罗杰茨王公姆斯季斯拉夫、杜布罗维察王公格列布等人在奥列尔河击败波洛伏齐汗康恰克。部分历史学家认为他在1190年前去世：1190年的记载中，平斯克已由其兄弟雅罗波尔克统治。

en:
Yuri, also called Georgy, Vladimirovich was prince of Pinsk, a member of the Turov Izyaslavichi line and a son of Prince Vladimir Sviatopolkovich. In 1262 he and his brothers Fyodor and Demid came to Nebl to congratulate Vasilko Romanovich of Volhynia on defeating the Lithuanians.

The chronicle praises him as a meek, humble and truthful prince; when he died, around 1288–1292, his widow, sons and brother Demid, and all the people mourned him with great lamentation. Demid then succeeded to Pinsk.

en:
Aimery IX (c. 1225–1256), viscount of Thouars in Poitou, was a son of Guy I of Thouars and Alix de Mauléon. In 1242 he submitted to King Louis IX rather than join the revolt of Hugh X of Lusignan. Succeeding his uncle Aimery VIII as viscount in 1246, he did homage to Alphonse of Poitiers, the king's brother.

He spent much of his time at Thouars, and in 1255 paid homage to Louis IX for the castles of Bugon and La Roche-sur-Yon, recovered through his Mauléon kin.

He died on 11 December 1256; by Poitevin custom the viscounty passed to his brother Renaud, not his son Guy.

艾默里克九世（约1225—1256）是普瓦图的图阿尔子爵，居伊一世·德·图阿尔与阿莉克丝·德·莫莱翁之子。1242年，他没有参加吕西尼昂的于格十世叛乱，而是归顺国王路易九世。1246年他继叔父艾默里克八世之后成为子爵，向国王之弟、普瓦捷的阿尔方斯行臣服礼。

他多居图阿尔，1255年凭莫莱翁亲族关系收回比贡和永河畔拉罗什城堡，为此向路易九世行臣服礼。

1256年12月11日他去世；按普瓦图习惯，子爵领传给弟弟雷诺，而非其子居伊。

en:
Alphonse of Poitiers (1220–1271) was a younger son of King Louis VIII of France and Blanche of Castile, and a brother of Louis IX. Granted Poitou and Auvergne as his appanage, he fought beside Louis IX at Taillebourg in 1242 against Henry III of England. By the 1229 Treaty of Paris he married Joan, only child of Count Raymond VII of Toulouse, and inherited Toulouse in 1249.

He and Charles of Anjou served as regents after Blanche's death in 1252. He joined the Eighth Crusade and died at Savona in 1271 without heirs, his lands reverting to the crown.

阿尔方斯·德·普瓦捷（1220—1271）是法兰西国王路易八世与卡斯蒂利亚的布兰卡之子、路易九世之弟。依照父亲遗嘱，他获得普瓦图和奥弗涅作为封禄，1242年在塔耶堡与路易九世并肩对抗英格兰国王亨利三世。根据1229年《巴黎条约》，他娶图卢兹伯爵雷蒙七世的独女让娜为妻，1249年继承图卢兹。

en:
Geoffrey IV of Thouars (c. 1125–1173), third son of Viscount Aimery V and Agnes of Poitiers, succeeded his brother William I as viscount in 1150. In 1156 he backed Geoffrey Plantagenet's claim to Anjou against Henry II of England and raided Henry's partisans.

In 1158 Henry besieged Thouars and stormed the supposedly impregnable castle in three days; Geoffrey fled, and the walls were dismantled at Eleanor of Aquitaine's request. He later recovered his lands, rebuilt the fortress and pilgrimaged to Santiago de Compostela. He died in 1173, and his son Aimery VII succeeded him.

Margaret of Lusignan (c. 1226–1288) was the daughter of Hugh X, count of La Marche, and Isabella of Angoulême, widow of King John of England, making her a half-sister of Henry III. In 1243 she married Raymond VII of Toulouse, but the Council of Lyons granted them a divorce in 1245.

She then wed Aimery IX, viscount of Thouars, and bore him Guy II. After Aimery died in 1256 she married Geoffrey VI of Châteaubriant. She died in 1288.

en:
Boris Davidovich was prince of Polotsk from after 1180 until around 1186, likely a son of the Vitebsk prince Davyd Sviatoslavich. His reign is known only from a Polotsk chronicle retold by Tatishchev: his second wife Sviatokhna, daughter of a Pomeranian prince, intrigued against his sons, including Vasilko, and forged a letter that had leading Polotsk boyars killed.

When Vasilko exposed the fraud, townsfolk rose at the veche bell, seized Sviatokhna and killed or expelled her Pomeranian followers. Boris died shortly after 1184.

en:
Bryachislav Iziaslavich (c. 997–1044) was prince of Polotsk from 1001, succeeding his father Iziaslav as a child. His line was excluded from the Kievan succession as izgoi, and he fought to keep Polotsk independent.

In 1020 he sacked Novgorod, but his uncle Yaroslav the Wise defeated him on the Sudoma River; he fled, leaving his prisoners and loot behind. In the peace of 1021 Yaroslav granted him only the cities of Vitebsk and Usvyat, yet their hostility continued for years. Bryachislav expanded his principality, founded Braslaw, and died in Polotsk in 1044. His son was Vseslav the Seer.

布里亚奇斯拉夫·伊贾斯拉维奇（约997—1044）自1001年起为波洛茨克王公，幼年继承父亲伊贾斯拉夫之位。其支系以“弃子”身份被排除在基辅继承之外，他力图维持波洛茨克独立。

1020年他洗劫诺夫哥罗德，但叔父智者雅罗斯拉夫在苏多马河将他击败；他丢下俘虏和战利品逃走。1021年的和约中雅罗斯拉夫只向他让出维捷布斯克和乌斯维亚特两城，此后双方仍敌对多年。布里亚奇斯拉夫扩大了公国疆域，建立布拉斯拉夫城，1044年死于波洛茨克。其子即“先知者”弗谢斯拉夫。

Briachislav Vasilkovich was a prince of the Vitebsk line of the Polotsk Rurikids, held to be a son of Vitebsk prince Vasilko Briachislavich. He succeeded his father in Vitebsk around 1221 and moved to the Polotsk throne around 1232, ruling there until after 1241.

In 1239 his daughter married Alexander Yaroslavich, the future Alexander Nevsky and grand prince of Vladimir. His death year is unknown, and a later prince of Polotsk, Konstantin the Armless, is regarded as his probable son.

en:
Iziaslav Vladimirovich (978–1001) was the son of Vladimir I of Kiev by Rogneda of Polotsk, and founder of the Polotsk branch of the Rurik dynasty, the Iziaslavichi. After Vladimir's conversion in 988, Rogneda was divorced and sent back with Iziaslav to Polotsk, where they ruled; Iziaslavl was named for him.

He was the first prince to make Polotsk autonomous from Kiev, passing the principality to his descendants. He died in 1001 before his father, barring his line from the Kievan succession under the rota system. His son Bryachislav continued the dynasty, which ruled Polotsk until 1222.

Jurgis Narimantaitis (c. 1326 – c. 1398) was a Lithuanian prince of the Gediminid dynasty, probably a son of Narimantas. He held Belz from 1352 against Louis I of Hungary and Chełm from 1359, and in 1366 became Casimir III of Poland's vassal.

After Casimir's death he raided Lesser Poland with Kęstutis in 1376, but lost his lands to Louis' counter-invasion the next year. In 1388 he joined the Teutonic Knights, but from 1392 served Vytautas, probably ending as prince of Pinsk.

尤尔吉斯·纳里曼塔伊蒂斯（约1326—约1398）是格迪米纳斯王朝的立陶宛王公，可能是纳里曼塔斯之子。1352年起他领有贝尔兹，抵御匈牙利国王拉约什一世，1359年起兼领海乌姆，1366年成为波兰国王卡齐米日三世的封臣。

1376年卡齐米日三世死后，他随科斯图提斯劫掠小波兰，但领地于次年被拉约什一世的反攻夺取。1388年他投奔条顿骑士团，1392年起转而为维陶塔斯效力，最后可能以平斯克王公身份终老。

en:
Konstantin, nicknamed the Armless, was prince of Polotsk in the 1250s and later prince of Vitebsk; one scholarly tradition makes him a son of Briachislav Vasilkovich. His nickname appears in the Instruction of Simeon, bishop of Polotsk. While ruling Polotsk he ceded Latgale lands to the Livonian Order, and late in the 1250s he lost the city to Tovtivil.

A possibly different Prince Konstantin campaigned against Yuryev in 1262 and Rakovor in 1268 and appears last in 1292, treating with the crusaders as an envoy of Grand Prince Dmitry of Vladimir.

zh:
绰号“无臂者”的康斯坦丁是1250年代的波洛茨克王公，后来任维捷布斯克王公，一种学术观点认为他是布里亚奇斯拉夫·瓦西里科维奇之子。他的绰号见于波洛茨克主教西缅的《训诫书》。统治波洛茨克期间，他把拉特加利亚的部分领地割让给利沃尼亚骑士团；1250年代末他失去波洛茨克，公位落入陶特维拉斯之手。

一位可能是另一人的康斯坦丁王公参加了1262年攻打尤里耶夫和1268年攻打拉科沃尔的战事；史料最后一次提到他是在1292年，当时他作为弗拉基米尔大公德米特里的使者与十字军谈判。

en:
Narimantas (died 2 February 1348), baptized Gleb, was a Lithuanian duke and the second son of Grand Duke Gediminas. He ruled Pinsk and Polotsk, and in 1333 Novgorod made him prince of its northern towns, the first Lithuanian service prince in Novgorod. His Orthodox baptism barred him from succeeding his father.

He backed his brother Jaunutis against Algirdas and fled to the Golden Horde, but after reconciling was killed fighting the Teutonic Knights at the Battle of Strėva on 2 February 1348.

纳里曼塔斯（洗礼名格列布，？—1348年2月2日）是立陶宛大公格迪米纳斯的次子，领有平斯克与波洛茨克。1333年，诺夫哥罗德立他为北方城镇的王公，他由此成为诺夫哥罗德第一位立陶宛籍附庸王公；皈依东正教也使他失去继承父亲大公爵位的资格。

他支持弟弟尧努蒂斯对抗阿尔吉尔达斯，一度逃奔金帐汗国，和解后于1348年2月2日在斯特雷瓦河战役中率军对阵条顿骑士团时战死。

en:
Rogvolod Vseslavich, baptized Boris (before 1054–1128), was the eldest son of Vseslav Briachislavich of Polotsk and ruled Polotsk after his father's death in 1101. Tatishchev says he founded Borisov in 1102 while returning from a campaign against the Yotvingians, and in 1106 he probably joined a failed expedition against the Semigallians.

Around 1120 he built a residence and the Boris and Gleb Monastery at Belchitsy near Polotsk, and the inscribed Boris Stones are linked with his reign. He died in early 1128 and was succeeded by his brother Davyd.

罗格沃洛德·弗谢斯拉维奇（教名鲍里斯，1054年前—1128年初）是波洛茨克王公弗谢斯拉夫·布里亚奇斯拉维奇的长子，1101年父亲死后登上波洛茨克公位。据塔季谢夫记载，1102年他在征讨雅特维格人返程时建立了鲍里索夫城；1106年，他可能参与了征讨泽姆加尔人的失败战事。

约1120年，他在波洛茨克附近的别利奇齐修建府邸与鲍里斯—格列布修道院，刻有铭文的“鲍里斯石”也与他的统治有关。他于1128年初去世，公位由弟弟达维德继承。

en:
Vainius, also called Voin, was the Lithuanian prince of Polotsk and a brother of Grand Duke Gediminas, held to be a son of Butvydas. First recorded in 1324, he already ruled Polotsk, and in 1326 joined Gediminas' embassy to Novgorod to make peace with the Novgorodians and the Livonian Order.

He probably died during the Order's campaigns against Polotsk in 1333–1334, and by 1338 Narimantas held the city. His only known son Liubartas was killed fighting the Order in 1342.

瓦伊纽斯（俄文称沃因）是立陶宛的波洛茨克王公、格迪米纳斯大公之弟，被认为是布特维达斯之子。1324年史籍首次提到他时，他已在统治波洛茨克；1326年，他随格迪米纳斯的使团前往诺夫哥罗德，与诺夫哥罗德人和利沃尼亚骑士团议和。

en:
Vasilko Sviatoslavich (died 1144), son of Sviatoslav Vseslavich of Vitebsk and grandson of Vseslav the Seer, was prince of Polotsk from 1132. In 1129 he was among the Polotsk princes exiled to Byzantium by Grand Prince Mstislav the Great, possibly serving Emperor John II Komnenos as a commander. He returned c. 1131, and in 1132 Polotsk expelled Sviatopolk Mstislavich and invited him to rule.

In 1138 he escorted Vsevolod Mstislavich, expelled from Novgorod, with honour and swore to him by kissing the cross. He held Polotsk until his death in 1144, at peace with the sons of Mstislav, and in 1143 married his daughter to Sviatoslav Vsevolodovich.

瓦西里科·斯维亚托斯拉维奇（?—1144）是维捷布斯克王公斯维亚托斯拉夫·弗谢斯拉维奇之子、“先知者”弗谢斯拉夫之孙，1132年起为波洛茨克王公。1129年基辅大公姆斯季斯拉夫大帝把一众波洛茨克王公掳往拜占庭，瓦西里科也在其中，可能曾在皇帝约翰二世·科穆宁麾下任将领。他约于1131年返回，1132年波洛茨克市民驱逐斯维亚托波尔克·姆斯季斯拉维奇，迎立他为主。

1138年，被逐出诺夫哥罗德的弗谢沃洛德·姆斯季斯拉维奇途经波洛茨克，他隆重护送并吻十字架向其立誓。他统治波洛茨克直至1144年去世，与姆斯季斯拉维奇兄弟保持和睦，1143年将女儿嫁给斯维亚托斯拉夫·弗谢沃洛多维奇。

en:
Vasilko Volodarevich was a Rurikid prince of the Polotsk land, a son of Volodar Glebovich, prince of Minsk and briefly prince of Polotsk in 1167, likely born of Volodar's short-lived marriage to Ryksa, daughter of Boleslaw III of Poland.

The Laurentian Chronicle names him as prince of Logoisk in 1186, when he campaigned against Polotsk together with the Novgorodians, a Smolensk force and the princes of Drutsk.

瓦西里科·沃洛达列维奇是波洛茨克地方的留里克王公，系明斯克王公、1167年还曾短暂据有波洛茨克的沃洛达里·格列波维奇之子，一般认为出自沃洛达里与波兰公爵波列斯瓦夫三世之女里克萨的短暂婚姻。

en:
Vseslav Bryachislavich, called the Seer (c. 1029–1101), was prince of Polotsk from 1044 and briefly grand prince of Kiev. Excluded from the Kievan succession as the only major Rurik prince not descended from Yaroslav the Wise, he raided the north.

After failing to take Pskov in 1065, he sacked Novgorod in 1066–1067, taking a bell from its cathedral to Polotsk. The three Yaroslavichi defeated him on the Nemiga in 1067 and seized him at peace talks.

Freed by the Kiev Uprising of 1068, he reigned in Kiev for seven months before securing Polotsk in 1071. He built Polotsk's Cathedral of Holy Wisdom and died on 24 April 1101.

弗谢斯拉夫·布里亚奇斯拉维奇，人称“先知者”（约1029—1101），自1044年起为波洛茨克王公，并曾短暂登上基辅大公之位。他是唯一不出于智者雅罗斯拉夫一脉的重要留里克王公，被排除在基辅继承之外，于是袭掠罗斯北方。

1065年他围攻普斯科夫受挫，1066—1067年冬洗劫诺夫哥罗德，将大教堂的一口钟带回波洛茨克。雅罗斯拉夫三王公于1067年在涅米加河将他击败，又在和谈时将他诱捕。

1068年基辅起义把他从狱中救出，他在基辅执政七个月，1071年重新稳固波洛茨克。他修建了波洛茨克圣索菲亚大教堂，于1101年4月24日去世。
