en:
Vseslav Iziaslavich (990s–1003) was prince of Polotsk from 1001, the probably elder son of Iziaslav Vladimirovich and a grandson of Vladimir the Great of Kyiv. He appears to have been the first Polotsk prince to inherit his throne rather than receive it by grant, marking the principality's emergence as a hereditary Rurikid domain.

The chronicles record only the year of his death. He likely died in childhood, and Polotsk passed to his brother Bryachislav.

弗谢斯拉夫·伊贾斯拉维奇（990年代—1003）自1001年起任波洛茨克王公，是伊贾斯拉夫·弗拉基米罗维奇可能的长子，也是基辅大公弗拉基米尔大帝之孙。他似乎是首位以继承而非受封方式获得公位的波洛茨克王公，标志着波洛茨克成为留里克家族的世袭领地。

编年史只留下他的卒年，他很可能幼年夭折，波洛茨克随后由其弟布里亚奇斯拉夫继承。

Aldona (baptized Anna; c. 1309 – 26 May 1339) was a Lithuanian princess, daughter of Grand Duke Gediminas, and from 1333 queen of Poland as the first wife of Casimir III. Their wedding in 1325 sealed the first Polish–Lithuanian alliance against the Teutonic Knights, and Gediminas released some twenty-five thousand Polish captives.

Remembered for her piety and the court musicians who accompanied her, she died suddenly in May 1339 and was buried in Kraków, leaving two daughters.

阿尔东娜（洗礼名安娜，约1309—1339年5月26日）是立陶宛大公格迪米纳斯之女，1333年成为波兰王后，即国王卡齐米日三世的第一任妻子。1325年的婚礼促成了波兰与立陶宛首次结盟，共同对付条顿骑士团，格迪米纳斯为此释放了约2.5万名波兰俘虏。

她以虔诚和宫廷乐师终日随行闻名，1339年5月突然去世，葬于克拉科夫，身后留下两个女儿。

en:
Bernardo Morando (c. 1540–1600) was an Italian architect, born in Padua or Venice in the Republic of Venice, who moved to Poland in 1569. In 1578 he signed an agreement with Great Crown Chancellor Jan Zamoyski to design the new foundation of Zamość, conceived as a Renaissance ideal city. He planned its layout, star-shaped fortifications and main buildings, from the Zamoyski Palace to the Town Hall and collegiate church, largely complete by 1598.

He also supervised burghers' houses and laid out other fortified towns. He served as mayor of Zamość in 1591–1593, was ennobled, and died there in 1600.

贝尔纳多·莫兰多（约1540—1600）是生于威尼斯共和国帕多瓦或威尼斯的意大利建筑师，1569年移居波兰。1578年，他与王国大总理扬·扎莫厄斯基签约，主持设计按文艺复兴“理想城市”理念兴建的新城扎莫希奇。他规划了城市布局、星形防御工事和扎莫伊斯基宫、市政厅、协同教堂等主要建筑，主体工程于1598年前基本完成。

莫兰多还监督市民住宅的修建，并规划了其他设防城镇。1591—1593年，他担任扎莫希奇市长，后受封贵族，1600年卒于当地。

en:
Bolesław III Wrymouth (1086–1138) was duke of Poland from 1107. The son of Władysław I Herman, he and his half-brother Zbigniew expelled the palatine Sieciech in 1101 and divided the realm on their father's death in 1102. He later blinded Zbigniew, then did public penance and pilgrimaged to Hungary.

Alliances with Hungary and Kievan Rus helped him repel an imperial invasion in 1109. From 1113 he conquered Pomerania in stages, incorporating Gdańsk Pomerania and supporting Otto of Bamberg's missions; in 1135 at the Congress of Merseburg he settled Pomerania's status with the Empire. His testament divided Poland among his sons, causing two centuries of fragmentation.

波列斯瓦夫三世，人称“歪嘴”（1086—1138），自1107年起为波兰公爵。他是瓦迪斯瓦夫一世·赫尔曼之子，1101年与异母兄兹比格涅夫联手逐走权臣谢切赫，1102年父亲死后两人瓜分国土。后来他弄瞎兹比格涅夫，随后公开忏悔并前往匈牙利朝圣。

他与匈牙利和基辅罗斯结盟，于1109年击退神圣罗马帝国的入侵。1113年起他分阶段征服波美拉尼亚，兼并格但斯克波美拉尼亚，并支持班贝格的奥托传教；1135年他在梅泽堡会议上与帝国敲定波美拉尼亚的地位。他的遗嘱把波兰分给诸子，导致近两百年的分裂。

en:
Bolesław the Pious (1224/27–1279) was a Piast duke of Greater Poland, the second son of Duke Władysław Odonic. From 1257 he ruled the whole duchy, succeeding his brother Przemysł I and guarding his infant nephew Przemysł II. In 1258 he married Jolenta, daughter of King Béla IV of Hungary, and in 1262–1264 he was regent of Masovia for Konrad II.

In 1264 he issued the Statute of Kalisz, the first written charter of privileges for the Jews of Greater Poland. On his death in 1279 his lands passed to Przemysł II.

虔诚者波列斯瓦夫（1224/27—1279）是皮雅斯特王朝的大波兰公爵，瓦迪斯瓦夫·奥多尼奇之次子。1257年其兄普热梅斯瓦夫一世去世后，他统治整个大波兰，并监护年幼的侄子普热梅斯瓦夫二世。1258年他娶匈牙利国王贝拉四世之女约伦塔为妻，1262—1264年为康拉德二世摄政马佐夫舍。

en:
Casimir III the Great (1310–1370), last Piast king of Poland, took the throne in 1333 over a small, ravaged realm. The Teutonic Order held Kuyavia. He chose treaties over war: at Visegrád in 1335 the arbitrators ordered Kuyavia and Dobrzyń returned, while he gave up Pomerania and the Chełmno Land to the Order; he also accepted the loss of Silesia.

Turning east, he annexed Red Ruthenia in 1340. His Statutes of Wiślica and Piotrków codified Polish law, earning him the name the Polish Justinian. Nearly thirty towns were walled and fifty castles built, and in 1364 he founded the University of Kraków.

He had also confirmed Jewish privileges in 1334 and encouraged settlement, yet he never had a legitimate son: in 1355 he named his nephew Louis I of Hungary as his heir should he die without one. When Casimir died on 5 November 1370, Louis took the crown and Piast rule ended.

卡齐米日三世，人称“大王”（1310—1370），是皮亚斯特王朝末代波兰国王，1333年即位时接手残破小国，条顿骑士团占据库亚维亚。他以条约代替战争，接受失去西里西亚，1335年在维谢格拉德把波美拉尼亚和海乌姆诺地让给骑士团，换回库亚维亚、多布任地。

他转向东方，1340年兼并红鲁塞尼亚。维希利察与彼得库夫法规统一了波兰法律，赢得“波兰的查士丁尼”之称。治下近三十座城镇筑城、约五十座城堡落成，1364年创立克拉科夫大学。

他还在1334年确认了犹太人特权并鼓励迁入，却始终没有嫡子：1355年，他指定外甥匈牙利国王拉约什一世在自己无子时继位。1370年11月5日卡齐米日去世，拉约什按约继承王位，皮亚斯特王朝由此告终。

en:
Clemente Molli (c. 1599–1664) was an Italian sculptor born near Bologna into a family from Russi in Romagna; contemporaries also knew him as an architect and man of letters. After studying humanities and philosophy he turned to sculpture, working across northern Italy on statues and marble groups before settling in Venice, where he joined the Accademia degli Incogniti.

Between 1644 and 1646 he carved in Warsaw the giant bronze statue of Sigismund III Vasa for Costante Tencalla's column. He died in Venice on 14 March 1664.

en:
Costante Tencalla (1593–1646) was a Swiss-Italian architect born at Bissone on Lake Lugano. Trained in Rome under the Baroque architect Carlo Maderno, he followed his uncle Matteo Castelli to the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and helped introduce early Roman Baroque architecture; Castelli became Poland's first royal architect.

After Castelli's death in 1632 he returned to Warsaw as royal architect to King Władysław IV Vasa. For the king he designed Sigismund's Column, erected in Warsaw in 1643–1644 with the sculptor Clemente Molli, and undertook buildings across the kingdom. He died in Warsaw in 1646.

科斯坦特·滕卡拉（1593—1646）是生于卢加诺湖畔比索内的瑞士籍意大利建筑师。他在罗马学艺，师从巴洛克建筑师卡洛·马代尔诺，后随叔父马泰奥·卡斯泰利前往波兰立陶宛联邦，将罗马早期巴洛克建筑引入当地；卡斯泰利成为波兰首位王室建筑师。

en:
Elizabeth of Poland (1326–1361) was the eldest daughter of Casimir III the Great of Poland and Aldona of Lithuania. Once betrothed to Louis VI the Roman, who instead married her younger sister Cunigunde, she married Bogislaw V, Duke of Pomerania, in 1343, sealing her father's anti-Teutonic agreement.

She lived mainly at Darłowo Castle and bore two children: Elizabeth of Pomerania, later wife of Emperor Charles IV, and Casimir (Kaźko). She died in 1361 at an Augustinian monastery and was buried there.

Elizabeth of Poland (1305–1380), daughter of Władysław I the Elbow-high and sister of Casimir III, became queen of Hungary by marriage to Charles I Robert. She founded a Poor Clares convent at Buda in 1334 and survived an assassination attempt that left her disabled.

After her son Louis I took the throne in 1342 she became queen mother. In 1343 she travelled to Naples with almost the whole royal treasure to win the crown for her son Andrew, husband of Queen Joanna, winning only a promise that he would be crowned as consort.

When Casimir died in 1370 and Louis inherited Poland, she governed there as regent until 1376, a regency that ended in violence. She spent her last years in a monastery outside Buda, and died on 29 December 1380.

1342年儿子拉约什一世继位后，她成为王太后。1343年，她带着几乎整个王室财库前往那不勒斯，为儿子安德拉什——乔万娜女王的丈夫——争取王冠，结果只得到他将以王夫身份加冕的允诺。

1370年卡齐米日三世去世、拉约什继承波兰王位，她出任波兰摄政至1376年，这段摄政以暴力收场。晚年她在布达城外的修道院度过，1380年12月29日去世。

en:
Euphrosyne of Opole (1228/30–1292) was a Piast duchess, the youngest daughter of Duke Casimir I of Opole. In 1257 she married her kinsman Casimir I of Kuyavia, bearing him four children, including Władysław I the Elbow-high, the future king who reunited Poland.

After Casimir's death in 1267 she ruled Kuyavia as regent until 1275, amid disputes with the Teutonic Order. That year she married Mestwin II, Duke of Pomerania; the childless marriage ended in divorce, and she died at Brześć Kujawski in 1292.

Hieronim Pinocci (1612–1676) was an Italian-born royal secretary, diplomat and writer, born at Lucca and active in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. He served King John II Casimir as envoy to the Dutch Republic in 1658 and to England in 1659.

In 1661 he edited the Merkuriusz Polski Ordynaryjny, the first Polish periodical newspaper, printed first in Kraków and then in Warsaw under royal sponsorship. The weekly covered European affairs and campaigns and promoted political reform and stronger royal authority. He died in Warsaw in 1676.

Jadwiga of Kalisz (1266 – 10 December 1339) was the daughter of Bolesław the Pious, duke of Greater Poland, and Yolanda of Hungary. In 1293 she married Władysław Łokietek, then fighting Wenceslaus II of Bohemia for control of Poland, and in 1300 she fled into hiding with her children.

She was crowned queen beside Władysław in Kraków in 1320 and took an active part in politics. Mother of Casimir III, she governed Stary Sącz as regent from 1334 and died in 1339.

en:
Jan Zamoyski (1542–1605) was a Polish nobleman, statesman and magnate, educated abroad and awarded a law doctorate at Padua. Returning to Poland in 1565, he rose through royal office to become Grand Chancellor of the Crown in 1578 and Great Hetman in 1581. After the Jagiellon dynasty died out in 1572, he helped secure all nobles the right to vote in royal elections.

A key adviser to Stephen Báthory, he led Polish forces in the Livonian campaigns, founded the city of Zamość and its academy, and in 1588 defeated the Habsburg claimant Maximilian III at Byczyna. He died on 3 June 1605.

en:
Casimir II the Just (1138–1194), a posthumous son of Bolesław III Wrymouth, received no land in his father's testament. In 1157 he was sent to Germany as a hostage for his brother's loyalty to Emperor Frederick Barbarossa.

He ruled Sandomierz from 1173, and in 1177, backed by nobles against his brother Mieszko III the Old, seized Kraków and became high duke of Poland. In 1184 he did homage to Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, and in 1186 inherited Masovia from his nephew Leszek, founding the Masovian Piast line. He ruled Kraków until his death in 1194, though Mieszko briefly displaced him; the Just is a 16th-century title.

en:
Kunigunde of Poland (c. 1328 – 26 April 1357) was the younger daughter of Casimir III the Great of Poland and Aldona of Lithuania. To block her match with the Wittelsbachs, John of Bohemia besieged Kraków in 1345 but failed to take the city, and that year she married Louis the Roman, son of Emperor Louis IV.

Her husband soon returned to Bavaria, leaving her in Kraków; she joined him in Berlin in 1356 and died on 26 April 1357. The marriage was childless.

波兰的库妮贡德（约1328—1357年4月26日）是波兰国王卡齐米日三世与立陶宛的阿尔东娜的幼女。为阻止她与维特尔斯巴赫家族联姻，波希米亚国王约翰于1345年围攻克拉科夫却未能破城；同年她嫁给神圣罗马帝国皇帝路德维希四世之子“罗马人”路德维希。

婚后不久丈夫便返回巴伐利亚，把她留在克拉科夫，她1356年才前往柏林与其团聚，1357年4月26日在当地去世，两人没有子女。

en:
Maciej, called Maćko, Borkowic (1298–1360) was voivode of Poznań from 1343 and a leader of Greater Poland's nobility. He campaigned in Red Ruthenia in 1340, and when Casimir III restored the general governorship in 1352 under Wierzbięta z Paniewic, Borkowic led the knightly confederation against the king; Greater Poland descended into civil war.

After killing the voivode of Kalisz he was exiled to Silesia, returned in 1356 and swore fealty at Sieradz in 1358. Arrested in 1360 and tried by the king, he was starved to death in Olsztyn castle tower.

马切伊（人称马奇科）·博尔科维奇（1298—1360）1343年起任波兹南总督，是大波兰贵族的领袖之一。1340年他出征红罗斯；1352年卡齐米日三世恢复总长官并授予帕涅维茨后，博尔科维奇领导骑士联盟起兵对抗国王，大波兰陷入内战。

他杀死卡利什总督后被逐往西里西亚，1356年回国，1358年在谢拉兹宣誓效忠。1360年他被捕，由国王亲自审判，最终在奥尔什丁城堡塔楼中饿死。

en:
Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636) was a Polish alchemist, philosopher and physician, born into a Polish noble family and educated at Kraków and several universities abroad.

In the 1590s he worked at Emperor Rudolf II's court in Prague, and around 1600 he entered the service of King Sigismund III Vasa, who experimented with him at Wawel Castle.

A chemistry pioneer, he devised ways of purifying acids and metals and wrote the influential treatise The New Chemical Light. He held that air contained a life-giving substance, identifying it with a gas released by heating saltpetre, and died in obscurity in 1636.

迈克尔·森达兹沃（1566—1636）是波兰炼金术士、哲学家与医生，出身贵族家庭，曾在克拉科夫及海外多所大学求学。

1590年代他在布拉格为鲁道夫二世宫廷效力，约1600年进入国王齐格蒙特三世·瓦萨的宫廷，国王曾与他一同在瓦维尔城堡做实验。

作为化学先驱，他改进了酸与金属的提纯方法，著有影响深远的《新化学之光》。他认为空气含有维持生命的物质，并认定它就是加热硝石时释放的气体。1636年，他在相对落寞中去世。

en:
Mieszko III the Old (c. 1122–1202) was a Piast duke, the fourth son of Bolesław III Wrymouth. His father's 1138 testament gave him Greater Poland. In 1173 he succeeded his brother Bolesław IV as high duke at Kraków, but his taxes and curbs on the nobility and clergy provoked a revolt that ousted him in 1177.

He retook Kraków in 1191 and after years of civil war recovered the high ducal title in 1198, holding it until his death at Kalisz in 1202, while keeping Greater Poland as his hereditary base.

梅什科三世“年老的”（约1122—1202）是皮亚斯特王朝王公，波列斯瓦夫三世“歪嘴”的第四子。按父亲1138年的遗嘱，他分得大波兰。1173年，他继兄长博莱斯瓦夫四世之后在克拉科夫就任大公，但他增收赋税、压制贵族与教会的举措激起叛乱，于1177年被赶下台。

他于1191年夺回克拉科夫，又经多年内战后在1198年重获大公称号，直至1202年在卡利什去世；大波兰则始终是他的世袭根基。

en:
Nicolaus Copernicus (1473–1543) was an astronomer who placed the Sun, not the Earth, at the centre of the universe. Born at Toruń, he was educated by his maternal uncle Lucas Watzenrode, later Bishop of Warmia. He studied at Kraków, Bologna and Padua, took a canon-law doctorate at Ferrara in 1503, and served his uncle as secretary and physician.

A canon of Warmia from 1497, before 1514 he circulated the Commentariolus, an outline of his heliocentric system. From 1516 to 1521 he ran Olsztyn and directed its castle's defence against the Teutonic Knights.

He hesitated to publish until 1539, when Georg Rheticus joined him and promoted his work. De revolutionibus orbium coelestium was printed at Nuremberg in 1543 with an unsigned preface calling its hypotheses mere calculation tools. He died on 24 May 1543, legend says with the finished book placed in his hands. It set off the Copernican Revolution.

尼古拉·哥白尼（1473—1543）是天文学家，主张太阳而非地球位于宇宙中心。他生于王家普鲁士的托伦，由舅父、后来的瓦尔米亚主教乌卡什·瓦岑罗德抚养教育。他在克拉科夫、博洛尼亚和帕多瓦求学，1503年在费拉拉获教会法博士学位，后担任舅父的秘书兼医生。

他自1497年起任瓦尔米亚教士，1514年之前已散发阐述日心体系的简短手稿《短论》。1516至1521年，他以管理者身份驻奥尔什丁，指挥城堡抵御条顿骑士团。

他一直犹豫是否出版，直到1539年数学家格奥尔格·雷蒂库斯前来师从并推动他的著作问世。《天体运行论》1543年在纽伦堡付印，书中附有一篇未署名序言，称其假说只是计算的工具。1543年5月24日哥白尼去世，相传成书当天送到他手中。这部书引发了哥白尼革命。

en:
Odon of Poznań (c. 1145–1194), or Odon Mieszkowic, was the eldest son of Mieszko III the Old and Elisabeth of Hungary. In 1177 he joined the revolt against his father, who had tried to force him into the priesthood and favored his half-brothers; backed by his uncle Casimir II he ruled Greater Poland in 1179–1181.

After Mieszko III's return he received Poznań in 1191 and Kalisz in 1193, where his mint struck coins reading Odon Dux. He died in 1194 and was buried at Poznań, leaving a young son, Władysław Odonic.

波兹南的奥东（约1145—1194），又称奥东·梅什科维奇，是梅什科三世“年老的”与匈牙利的伊丽莎白的长子。1177年，他参加反对父亲的叛乱：梅什科三世曾试图逼他出家为僧，又偏爱异母弟弟们；在叔父卡齐米日二世支持下，他于1179—1181年统治大波兰。

梅什科三世返国后，他在1191年得到波兹南，1193年又得到卡利什，并在当地开设造币厂，铸有“奥东公爵”字样的钱币。1194年他去世，葬于波兹南，留下年幼的儿子瓦迪斯瓦夫·奥多尼奇。

en:
Stanislaus of Szczepanów (1030–1079) was bishop of Kraków and one of the earliest native Polish bishops. Educated at Gniezno and probably Paris, he became a Kraków canon known for his preaching and was elected bishop in 1072, accepting only at the command of Pope Alexander II.

As advisor to Bolesław II he helped bring papal legates to Poland and restore the archiepiscopal see of Gniezno, a precondition of the 1076 coronation. After a conflict with Bolesław, he was executed in 1079. Canonized in 1253, he is a patron saint of Poland.

en:
Adalbert of Prague, born Vojtěch (c. 956–997), was bishop of Prague and a missionary martyr. Of the powerful Slavnik family of Bohemia, he studied at Magdeburg and became bishop in 982, while still under canonical age. Conflicts with Bohemian nobles drove him into retreat at Rome; after returning he founded Břevnov Abbey in 993.

Released from his see as a missionary bishop, he preached in Hungary and in March 997 joined Bolesław Chrobry at Gniezno before entering pagan Prussia, where tribesmen killed him on 23 April 997. Canonized in 999, he is a patron saint of Poland and Bohemia.

布拉格的亚德伯（约956—997），原名沃伊切赫，是布拉格主教和传教殉道者。他出身波希米亚权势显赫的斯拉夫尼克家族，在马格德堡求学，982年未满教会法定年龄便被推举为布拉格主教。他与波希米亚贵族屡次冲突，一度退隐罗马；返回后于993年创建布热夫诺夫修道院。

后来他获准以传教主教身份离开教区，赴匈牙利传教，997年3月在格涅兹诺投奔博莱斯瓦夫·赫罗布里，随后进入异教的普鲁士，997年4月23日在那里被普鲁士人杀害。他于999年被追封圣徒，是波兰和波希米亚的主保圣人。

en:
Wincenty Kadłubek (c. 1150–1223) was bishop of Kraków and the leading Polish scholar of his age. Educated at the Kraków cathedral school and then at Paris and Bologna, he was ordained before 1189 and served as provost of Sandomierz Cathedral. Consecrated bishop in 1208, he worked to reform the Kraków clergy.

He wrote the Chronica Polonorum, the first Polish history composed by a Pole and a cardinal source for early medieval Poland. In 1218 he resigned his see and retired to the Cistercian monastery at Jędrzejów, where he died in 1223. He was beatified in 1764.

en:
Wincenty of Kielcza (c. 1200–after 1262) was a Polish Dominican canon, poet, and the first Polish composer known by name. From about 1222 he served as chaplain to Bishop Iwo Odrowąż of Kraków, becoming a Kraków canon in 1257 and prior of the Dominican house at Racibórz in 1258–1260.

For the 1254 translation of Saint Stanislaus's relics he composed the liturgical office Historia gloriosissimi Stanislai, containing the hymn Gaude Mater Polonia, long sung by Polish knights after victory. He also wrote two lives of Saint Stanislaus.

en:
Władysław I the Elbow-high (c. 1260–1333) was the Piast duke who reunited Poland, the son of Casimir I of Kuyavia and Euphrosyne of Opole. In 1293 he married Hedwig, daughter of Bolesław the Pious. Driven into exile by Wenceslaus II of Bohemia, he recovered Kraków in 1306 after Wenceslaus III was murdered. With papal approval he was crowned king in January 1320, the first Polish coronation at Wawel Cathedral.

His later reign was dominated by war with the Teutonic Order. He died on 2 March 1333 and was succeeded by his son Casimir III the Great.

en:
Władysław Odonic, called the Spitter (c. 1190–1239), was a Piast duke of Greater Poland, son of Odon of Poznań. From 1206 he fought his uncle Władysław III Spindleshanks for his inheritance, in years of exile. With Pomeranian help he routed the high duke's army at Ujście in 1227 and seized most of Greater Poland.

At Gąsawa that November he was blamed for the ambush that killed Leszek the White. In 1229 he expelled his uncle and ruled all Greater Poland until 1234, when Henry I the Bearded took its southern and western lands. He died on 5 June 1239.

en:
Iaroslav Sviatopolkovich (c. 1072–1123) was a Rurikid prince, the second son of Sviatopolk II, Grand Prince of Kiev. In 1100 his father made him prince of Vladimir-in-Volhynia; in 1102 Novgorod refused to accept him as prince.

He strengthened ties with Hungary through marriage to a daughter of King Ladislaus I, and later wed Rogneda, daughter of Mstislav the Great. After he clashed with Vladimir Monomakh, who took Kiev in 1113, he sent Rogneda away and was driven from Volhynia in 1118.

He fled to Poland and Hungary. In 1123 he returned with their troops to besiege Vladimir-in-Volhynia, where he was killed.

en:
Barnim I the Good (c. 1217–1278), of the Griffin dynasty, ruled as duke of Pomerania from his father Bogislaw II's death in 1220, sharing power with his cousin Wartislaw III at Demmin. After German princes defeated Denmark at Bornhöved in 1227, Emperor Frederick II placed Pomerania under Brandenburg's suzerainty, and by the 1250 Treaty of Landin Barnim surrendered the Uckermark and accepted Ascanian overlordship.

In 1264 he inherited Wartislaw's lands and united the duchy. He promoted German settlement and granted rights to Stettin in 1243 and many other towns. He died on 13 November 1278.

Bogislaw IV (c. 1255–1309), of the Griffin dynasty, was the eldest son of Barnim I of Pomerania and served as co-ruler from 1276 before succeeding as duke in 1278. While his half-brothers were underage he ruled alone, and in the early 1280s intervened in the war over Brandenburg. After Barnim II died in 1295, Pomerania was partitioned and Bogislaw took Wolgast while Otto I received Szczecin.

He later allied with Władysław the Short of Poland and fought in the Brandenburg War. He was buried in Stettin's Marienkirche and succeeded by his son Wartislaw IV.

en:
Afonso I Henriques (1109–1185), called the Conqueror, was the son of Henry of Burgundy and Theresa of León, counts of Portugal. After Henry died in 1112, Theresa governed with a Galician noble; Portuguese nobles rallied around Afonso, who defeated her at the Battle of São Mamede in 1128 and ruled as count.

He crushed the Moors at Ourique in 1139 and proclaimed himself king of independent Portugal, defeating León to secure it. Second Crusaders helped him take Santarém and Lisbon in 1147, and a papal bull recognized the kingdom. When he died in 1185 he had doubled Portugal's size; his son Sancho I succeeded him.

en:
Afonso II (1185–1223), called the Fat, was third king of Portugal and eldest surviving son of Sancho I and Dulce of Aragon, succeeding in 1211. He opened his reign by exiling rebellious siblings. He kept peace with Castile while his nobles took Alcácer do Sal from the Moors.

He built up royal administration and issued Portugal's first written laws. He opened trade with northern Europe and in 1220 began the inquirições to recover crown land. His curbs on Church wealth led Pope Honorius III to excommunicate him. He died at Coimbra in 1223; his sons Sancho II and Afonso III later became kings.

阿方索二世（1185—1223），人称“胖子”，是葡萄牙第三位国王、桑乔一世与阿拉贡的杜尔塞存活的长子，1211年继位。他即位之初便放逐了叛乱的兄弟姐妹。他与卡斯蒂利亚保持和平，阿尔卡塞尔-杜萨尔则由贵族们从摩尔人手中攻取。

en:
Afonso III (1210–1279), called the Boulonnais, was the second son of Afonso II. In France he married Matilda II, Countess of Boulogne, in 1238 and ruled her county. In 1245 Pope Innocent IV declared his brother Sancho II deposed, and Afonso took Portugal, styling himself overseer and defender until Sancho died in 1248.

After Faro fell in 1249 he became the first king styled King of Portugal and the Algarve, completing the Reconquista. In 1253 he divorced Matilda and married Beatrice of Castile.

In 1254 he summoned the Cortes of Leiria, the first assembly with town representatives, and made Lisbon his capital. The 1267 Treaty of Badajoz fixed the Castilian frontier on the Guadiana.

en:
Afonso IV (1291–1357), called the Brave, was the only legitimate son of King Denis and Elizabeth of Aragon, but not his father's favourite: the old king preferred his bastard Afonso Sanches, and the half-brothers' rivalry several times ended in civil war. On succeeding in 1325 he exiled Sanches to Castile; after Sanches' failed invasions, their mother Elizabeth arranged a peace.

In 1340 Afonso joined Alfonso XI of Castile in defeating the Marinids at Salado. His long reign was mostly peaceful, and he funded a commercial fleet and ordered Portugal's first maritime explorations.

It ended in family tragedy. Alarmed by Castilian influence as the brothers of his son Peter's mistress Inês de Castro gained power at court, he had her murdered at Coimbra in 1355. Peter ravaged the north before father and son made peace in early 1357, and Afonso died that May.

阿方索四世（1291—1357），绰号“勇敢者”，是国王迪尼什与阿拉贡的伊莎贝尔唯一的嫡子，却不是父亲偏爱的儿子：老国王宠信私生子阿方索·桑切斯，两兄弟的积怨数次演变成内战。1325年继位后，他把桑切斯放逐到卡斯蒂利亚；桑切斯数次发兵入侵未果，最终在母亲伊莎贝尔的调解下议和。

晚年却以家庭悲剧收场：儿子佩德罗的情妇伊内斯·德·卡斯特罗的兄弟在朝中得势，他担心卡斯蒂利亚势力渗入，于1355年下令在科英布拉杀害伊内斯。佩德罗发兵蹂躏北方，直到1357年初父子和解，阿方索当年5月去世。

en:
Beatrice of Castile (1242/1244–1303) was an illegitimate daughter of Alfonso X of Castile and Mayor Guillén de Guzmán. In 1253 she married Afonso III of Portugal, in a settlement of Castile's claims over the Algarve. Afonso was still married to Matilda II of Boulogne, who accused him of bigamy; in 1258 the Pope condemned him for adultery.

As queen Beatrice promoted Portuguese-Castilian rapprochement. She inherited her mother's estates and protected the monastery of Santa Clara at Alcocer.

After Afonso's death she quarrelled with her son King Denis, returned to Castile in 1282, supported Alfonso X against her half-brother Sancho, and was at her father's deathbed in 1284. She died in 1303 and was buried at Alcobaça.

卡斯蒂利亚的比阿特丽斯（1242/1244—1303）是卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索十世与情妇玛约尔·纪廉·德·古斯曼的私生女。1253年她嫁给葡萄牙国王阿方索三世，以了结卡斯蒂利亚对阿尔加维的主权要求。阿方索当时仍与布洛涅的玛蒂尔达二世保持婚姻，玛蒂尔达控告他重婚，1258年教皇因通奸谴责他。

作为王后，比阿特丽斯推动葡萄牙与卡斯蒂利亚修好。她继承了母亲的产业，并庇护阿尔科塞尔的圣克拉拉修道院。

阿方索三世去世后，她与儿子迪尼什国王不和，1282年返回卡斯蒂利亚，支持父亲阿方索十世对抗异母弟桑乔，并在1284年为父亲送终。她于1303年去世，葬于阿尔科巴萨修道院。

en:
Beatrice of Castile (1293–1359), daughter of Sancho IV and María de Molina. The 1297 Treaty of Alcañices ended the war between Castile and Portugal and arranged marriages for two pairs of siblings, so at four she was betrothed to the Portuguese infante Afonso and sent to grow up at King Denis's court. After a papal dispensation they married in Lisbon in 1309.

Queen from 1325, she worked, like her mother-in-law Elizabeth of Aragon, as a mediator. When Afonso IV and her son-in-law Alfonso XI of Castile went to war in 1336, she crossed the border to ask for peace, in vain. In 1355 she helped reconcile her son Peter with his father after the murder of Inês de Castro.

After her daughter-in-law Constance died in 1345, she raised the future Ferdinand I. She died in 1359 and lies beside her husband in Lisbon Cathedral.

卡斯蒂利亚的比阿特丽斯（1293—1359）是桑乔四世与玛丽亚·德·莫利纳之女。1297年的《阿尔卡尼伊塞斯条约》结束了卡斯蒂利亚与葡萄牙之间的战事，并安排了两对兄妹的联姻，四岁的她因此许配给葡萄牙王子阿方索，被送到迪尼什国王宫中长大。获教皇特许后，两人于1309年在里斯本成婚。

1325年起她身为王后，像婆婆阿拉贡的伊莎贝尔一样充当调停人。1336年，丈夫阿方索四世与她的女婿卡斯蒂利亚的阿方索十一世开战，她越境求和，未能成功。1355年，儿子佩德罗因伊内斯·德·卡斯特罗被害与父亲决裂，她出面斡旋，促成和解。

1345年儿媳康斯坦丝去世后，她又抚养了后来的费尔南多一世。1359年她在里斯本去世，葬于里斯本大教堂，与丈夫相邻。

en:
Denis (1261–1325), called the Farmer King and the Poet King, was the eldest son of Afonso III and ruled Portugal from 1279. In 1290 he decreed Portuguese the language of the courts and founded the kingdom's first university in Lisbon. He promoted agriculture and ordered pine forests planted near Leiria to prevent soil erosion and supply ship timber.

In 1308 he signed Portugal's first commercial treaty with England, and in 1319 founded the Order of Christ to inherit the estates of the suppressed Templars. His poetry helped make Portuguese a literary language. His last years saw civil war between his heir Afonso and bastard son Afonso Sanches.

迪尼什（1261—1325），绰号“农夫国王”与“诗人国王”，是阿方索三世的长子，1279年起统治葡萄牙。1290年，他下令以葡萄牙语为法庭用语，并在里斯本创办国内第一所大学。他推动农业，下令在莱里亚附近营造松林，以防止土壤退化并为王室船只提供木材。

1308年他与英格兰签订葡萄牙第一个通商条约，1319年创立基督骑士团，接管被取缔的圣殿骑士团财产。他的诗作推动葡萄牙语成为文学语言。晚年，继承人阿方索与私生子阿方索·桑切斯之间爆发内战。

Eleanor of Portugal (1328 – 30 October 1348) was a Portuguese infanta, the youngest daughter of King Afonso IV and Beatrice of Castile, and sister of Peter I. In 1347 she married Peter IV of Aragon in Barcelona as his second wife, becoming the only Portuguese-born queen of Aragon.

Travelling the next year, she caught the Black Death at Teruel and died on 30 October 1348. Her remains were moved to Poblet Monastery in 1350.

Estêvão Gonçalves Leitão (c. 1290–1344) was the fourth master of the Order of Christ, elected in 1335 in succession to his brother Martim Gonçalves Leitão, holding office until death. King Afonso IV brought about his election, valuing the military record of his kin.

In the 1336–1339 war with Castile, his men joined the hosts of the bishops of Porto and Braga in routing a Castilian army under Fernando de Castro near Braga in 1337 and killing the commander's brother. He kept the Order's war against the Moors alive as vigorously as his predecessors.

Fernão Dias Pais Leme (c. 1608–1681) was a São Paulo bandeirante nicknamed the Emerald Hunter. From 1644 he led his own slave-raiding expeditions into the sertão.

Elected a local judge in 1651, he promoted reconciliation between settlers and Jesuits in 1653, yet in 1661 led another expedition against Jesuit missions to capture Indigenous people for enslavement.

In 1671 the governor commissioned him to find the emeralds of the legendary Serra da Sabarabuçu. Setting out in 1674, his bandeira spent years in the wilderness. He died of fever in 1681, believing the green stones he had sent south were emeralds; they were tourmalines.

费尔南·迪亚斯·派斯·莱梅（约1608—1681）是圣保罗的班德拉旗手，绰号“祖母绿猎手”。1644年起，他多次率领自己的旗队深入内陆掳掠印第安人为奴。

1651年他当选地方司法官，1653年促成定居者与耶稣会士和解，却又在1661年率队袭击耶稣会传教区，掳掠原住民为奴。

1671年，总督委托他寻找传说中的萨巴拉布苏山脉的祖母绿。1674年出发后，他的旗队在荒野中跋涉多年。1681年他死于热病，至死以为送出的绿色石头是祖母绿，其实是电气石。

Francisco Álvares (c. 1465–1536/1541) was a Portuguese priest and explorer. In 1515 he joined the Portuguese embassy to Emperor Lebna Dengel of Ethiopia; the mission reached the Ethiopian highlands only in 1520.

There Álvares met the long-settled Pêro da Covilhã, stayed six years and returned to Lisbon in 1526–1527. His report, A True Relation of the Lands of Prester John of the Indies, described his years in the Christian kingdom for European readers.

弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯（约1465—1536/1541）是葡萄牙神父与探险家。1515年，他加入前往埃塞俄比亚皇帝勒布纳·丹格尔宫廷的葡萄牙使团，使团迟至1520年才进入埃塞俄比亚高原。

Francisco de Arruda (died 1547) was a Portuguese architect and sculptor, younger brother of Diogo de Arruda. With his brother he helped forge the Manueline style, Portugal's exuberant late Gothic; his most famous work is the Belém Tower in Lisbon, commissioned by Manuel I to guard the mouth of the Tagus.

He repaired castles with semicircular artillery towers, worked on strongholds in Morocco and in 1520 designed Elvas Cathedral. After Diogo's death in 1531 his later buildings moved toward Renaissance forms. He died on 30 November 1547.

弗朗西斯科·德·阿鲁达（卒于1547年）是葡萄牙建筑师与雕塑家，迪奥戈·德·阿鲁达的弟弟。他与兄长一同塑造了曼努埃尔式——葡萄牙华丽的晚期哥特风格；其最著名的作品是里斯本的贝伦塔，由曼努埃尔一世下令修建，扼守塔霍河口。

他以半圆形炮台塔楼修缮城堡，参与摩洛哥要塞工程，1520年设计了埃尔瓦什大教堂。1531年迪奥戈去世后，他晚年建筑转向文艺复兴风格。1547年11月30日去世。

Elizabeth of Aragon (1271–1336), daughter of Peter III of Aragon, became queen of Portugal by marrying King Denis in 1288. She helped shape the Treaty of Alcañices between Denis and Castile in 1297. Her son Afonso accused Denis of favouring an illegitimate son, and civil war followed.

In 1323 Elizabeth rode a mule between the opposing armies to prevent battle; peace returned in 1324 when Afonso swore loyalty to his father. She gave alms to the poor and was linked with the miracle of the roses, died at Estremoz in 1336, and was canonized by Pope Urban VIII in 1625.

en:
John IV (1604–1656), eighth Duke of Braganza, succeeded his father Teodósio II in 1630. On 1 December 1640 the Forty Conspirators seized Lisbon and ended sixty years of Spanish rule; John was acclaimed king, opening the Portuguese Restoration War and founding the Braganza dynasty.

His troops beat Spain at Montijo in 1644, his fleets recovered Luanda in 1648 and northern Brazil from the Dutch by 1654. He was also a composer and writer on music.

en:
Luís Vaz de Camões (c. 1524–1580) was Portugal's greatest poet and author of its national epic Os Lusíadas. Probably born poor in Lisbon and likely educated by a clergyman uncle, he entered John III's court, served in Ceuta and lost his right eye in a Strait of Gibraltar battle.

Jailed for wounding a palace employee, he was pardoned in 1553 and went to serve in India. In the East he fought and was repeatedly imprisoned; tradition says he wrote part of the epic in a Macau cave and, shipwrecked near the Mekong, saved only himself and the manuscript.

He returned in 1570 so poor that friends paid his Mozambique debts. He recited it to young King Sebastian, who printed it in 1572 with a pension. He died in Lisbon on 10 June 1580, embittered by the defeat at Alcácer Quibir; that date is now Portugal's national day.

路易·瓦斯·德·贾梅士（约1524—1580）是葡萄牙诗人，被视为葡萄牙语最伟大的诗人、民族史诗《卢济塔尼亚人之歌》的作者。他出身破落贵族家庭，多半生于里斯本，可能受教于身为神职人员的叔父，后来出入若昂三世宫廷。他在休达从军，在直布罗陀海峡的海战中失去右眼。

他因刺伤王宫仆役入狱，1553年获准前往印度效力以代刑罚。在东方，他多次参战，数度入狱；相传他在澳门一处洞穴里写成史诗的一部分，又在湄公河口附近遇海难，只保住自己和手稿。

他1570年回国时穷困潦倒，靠朋友在莫桑比克替他还债才得以脱身。他向年轻的国王塞巴斯蒂安朗诵诗作，国王下令于1572年出版并赐他年金。1580年6月10日，他因阿尔卡塞尔基维尔战败而心灰意冷，在里斯本去世；这一天后来成为葡萄牙国庆日。

Luís de Meneses, 3rd Count of Ericeira (1632–1690), was a Portuguese nobleman, artillery general and historian who fought through the Restoration War, including the battles of Ameixial (1663) and Montes Claros (1665), and later wrote works on it.

He backed the party that deposed Afonso VI in 1667 and became finance minister under Pedro II. A Colbert-style mercantilist, he fostered Portuguese cloth and silk manufacture, settled foreign weavers in the interior, and secured protectionist sumptuary laws in 1677 and 1686. Troubled by melancholy, he killed himself at his Lisbon palace in May 1690.

他支持1667年废黜阿丰索六世的一派，在佩德罗二世治下担任财政总监。他是科尔贝式的重商主义者，扶持本国毛纺和丝织业，在内地安置外国织工，并推动1677年和1686年的保护主义禁奢法令。他长期受忧郁症困扰，1690年5月在里斯本宅邸自尽。

en:
Ferdinand Magellan (c. 1480–1521) was a Portuguese navigator who led the Spanish expedition that made the first circumnavigation. After service in India and Malacca, a 1513 wound at Azemmour left him lame, and a false trade charge cost him royal favour. When Manuel rejected his westward Spice Islands route, he won Charles I's backing in 1517.

As admiral he sailed in September 1519 with five ships and 270 men amid storms and mutinies. In November 1520 the fleet entered the strait that bears his name, christening the ocean beyond it the Mar Pacifico; the crossing took 98 days. In the Philippines he converted Humabon of Cebu, then attacked Lapulapu of Mactan on 27 April 1521 after he refused to convert.

He was killed in the fighting; Lapulapu refused to return his body. Only the Victoria, under Juan Sebastián Elcano, reached Spain in 1522 with some forty men, completing it.

斐迪南·麦哲伦（约1480—1521）是葡萄牙航海家，率领西班牙远征队完成人类首次环球航行。他曾在印度和马六甲服役，1513年在阿泽穆尔负伤致跛，又被诬非法贸易而失宠。曼努埃尔拒绝他西航香料群岛的计划后，1517年获西班牙国王卡洛斯一世支持。

受任将领后，1519年9月他率五船约270人出航，一路风暴与叛乱不断。1520年11月船队驶入以他命名的海峡，他把海峡外的大洋命名为“太平洋”，横渡耗时98天。在菲律宾他使宿务的胡马邦皈依，1521年4月27日进攻拒皈依的麦克坦酋长拉普拉普。

他战死沙场，拉普拉普拒绝交还他的遗体。只有埃尔卡诺率“维多利亚号”于1522年带约四十人返回西班牙，完成环球航行。

Pedro Afonso, Count of Barcelos (1287–1354), was the illegitimate son of King Denis of Portugal by Grácia Froes, and in 1314 his father gave him the town of Barcelos with the title of count. When Denis fell out with his heir Afonso, Pedro tried to hold a middle line until exiled to Castile in 1317, where he met the court culture of his great-grandfather Alfonso X the Wise.

Recalled in 1322, he sided with the heir in the civil war and regained his confiscated lands in 1324, after backing Queen Elizabeth's peacemaking. He fought beside Afonso IV at Salado in 1340.

A poet and troubadour like his father, he made his seat at Lalim near Lamego a cultural centre, and is credited with many major texts of medieval Portuguese literature. He died there in 1354 and was buried at Tarouca, under a tomb carved with boar-hunting scenes.

佩德罗·阿方索，巴塞卢什伯爵（1287—1354），是葡萄牙国王迪尼什与格拉西亚·弗罗埃斯的私生子，1314年父亲把巴塞卢什镇连同伯爵头衔赐给他。迪尼什与继承人阿方索失和时，他试图维持两边平衡，1317年被逐往卡斯蒂利亚，接触到曾祖父智者阿方索十世的宫廷文化。

1322年召回后他在内战中站到继承人一边，支持伊莎贝拉王后调停，于1324年夺回被没收的产业。1340年他随阿方索四世参加萨拉多战役。

他和父亲一样是诗人与游吟诗人，把拉梅古附近拉林的府邸经营成文化中心，中世纪葡萄牙文学的许多重要文本都归功于他。1354年他死于拉林，葬于塔鲁卡，墓上雕有猎野猪的场景。

en:
Peter I (1320–1367), called the Just, was the son of Afonso IV and Beatrice of Castile. In 1340 his wife Constanza Manuel arrived in Portugal with her lady-in-waiting Inês de Castro, and Peter fell in love with Inês, making her exiled brothers his closest advisers. This alarmed Afonso, who in 1355 had Inês beheaded at Coimbra.

Peter revolted, but in an August 1356 truce swore to obey his father and pardon the killers, and he became king in May 1357. Two killers who had fled to Castile were handed over and tried in 1361. Fernão Lopes says he tore out their hearts with his own hands.

Legend has it that he had Inês exhumed and crowned queen; certainly he moved her to Alcobaça, where their two tombs face each other to see each other at the Last Judgment. He died at Estremoz in 1367.

佩德罗一世（1320—1367），绰号“公正者”，是阿方索四世与卡斯蒂利亚的比阿特丽斯之子。他的妻子康斯坦莎·曼努埃尔于1340年抵达葡萄牙，侍女伊内斯·德·卡斯特罗随行入境，佩德罗爱上了伊内斯，并重用她流亡而来的兄弟。阿方索为此忧心，1355年下令在科英布拉将伊内斯斩首。

佩德罗起兵反叛，却在1356年8月的休战协议中发誓服从父亲、宽恕凶手，1357年5月登上王位。两名逃到卡斯蒂利亚的凶手被引渡回国，于1361年受审。费尔南·洛佩斯记载，他亲手掏出二人的心脏。

相传他掘出伊内斯的遗体，为她加冕为后；确凿的是他把她迁葬阿尔科巴萨，两座石棺相向而立，好让两人在最后审判时一睁眼就看见对方。1367年，他死于埃什特雷莫什。

Pêro da Covilhã (c. 1460–after 1526) was a Portuguese diplomat and explorer born at Covilhã in Beira. In 1487 he was sent on an overland mission to scout trade with India and Arabia. Travelling through Egypt and Arabia, he reached Calicut in India and Hormuz before making his way to Ethiopia, where he spent the rest of his life.

His detailed report was studied in Lisbon and, alongside Bartolomeu Dias's voyages, helped pave the way for Vasco da Gama's voyage of 1497, while his arrival opened Portugal's relations with Ethiopia.

Sancho I (1154–1211), called the Populator, was second king of Portugal and the only surviving legitimate son of Afonso I and Matilda of Savoy, crowned at Coimbra in 1185. As prince he married Dulce of Aragon in 1174, securing an alliance against Castile and León. With Third Crusade help he took Silves from the Moors in 1189 and styled himself king of Silves.

The Almohads invaded in 1190 and retook the city in 1191. He ended the wars on the Galician frontier, founded towns, settled remote northern areas, and promoted trade and learning. He died at Coimbra in 1211 and was succeeded by his son Afonso II.

桑乔一世（1154—1211），人称“殖民者”，是葡萄牙第二位国王，也是阿方索一世与萨伏依的玛蒂尔达唯一存活的合法儿子，1185年在科英布拉加冕。他为王子时于1174年娶阿拉贡的杜尔塞，巩固了两国对抗卡斯蒂利亚和莱昂的联盟。1189年他借第三次十字军之力从摩尔人手中夺取锡尔维什，自称锡尔维什国王。

穆瓦希德王朝于1190年和1191年两次入侵，并在第二次入侵时夺回该城。他结束了加利西亚边境的战事，兴建城镇，向偏远的北方地区移民，并鼓励贸易与学术。1211年他在科英布拉去世，儿子阿方索二世继位。

en:
Sancho II (1207–1248), nicknamed the Cowled, was born in Coimbra, the eldest son of Afonso II of Portugal and Urraca of Castile. He succeeded his father as king in 1223 amid a quarrel with the papacy over his father's excommunication, but largely ignored a ten-article treaty he signed with the Pope.

From 1236 he led Reconquista campaigns into the Alentejo and Algarve, taking several Muslim-held cities. His later reign was torn by civil war and Church opposition; in 1247 a Castilian intervention forced him into exile at Toledo, where he died in 1248. His brother Afonso III succeeded him.

桑乔二世（1207—1248），绰号“戴兜帽者”，生于科英布拉，是葡萄牙国王阿方索二世与卡斯蒂利亚的乌拉卡之长子。1223年他继位时，葡萄牙正因父亲被革除教籍而与教廷交恶；他与教皇签订了十条协议，却基本不予履行。

en:
Vasco da Gama (c. 1460s–1524) was a Portuguese mariner and nobleman who opened the first sea route from Europe to India. Born in Sines, he left Lisbon on 8 July 1497 with four ships and 170 men, swinging far into the South Atlantic and sighting no land for over three months, then the longest open-sea voyage.

At Christmas he named the coast Natal, took a Gujarati pilot at Malindi and reached Kozhikode on 20 May 1498. His gifts were trifling; the monsoon-battered return took over ninety days, scurvy killed about half the crew, and his brother Paulo died en route. He reached Lisbon in 1499 a hero.

In 1502 he returned with fifteen ships to avenge a Portuguese factory attack, burning the pilgrim ship Mirim with over 400 aboard and bombarding Kozhikode. Viceroy of India under John III from 1524, he died of malaria at Cochin on 24 December.

瓦斯科·达·伽马（约1460年代—1524）是葡萄牙航海家与贵族，开辟了从欧洲通往印度的第一条海上航路。他生于锡尼什，1497年7月8日率四艘船、170人从里斯本出发。他没有沿非洲海岸航行，而是远远驶入南大西洋，三个多月后才重新看到陆地，这是当时最长的一次不靠岸远航。

圣诞节前后，他把所经海岸命名为纳塔尔，在马林迪雇得一名古吉拉特领航员，1498年5月20日抵达科泽科德。他带去的礼物微不足道；回程逆季风横渡印度洋用了九十多天，坏血病夺去约半数船员，弟弟保罗也死在归途。1499年他回到里斯本，受到英雄般的欢迎。

1502年，他率十五艘船再赴印度，为葡萄牙商馆遇袭报复，烧死载有400多人的朝圣船“米里”号，又炮轰科泽科德。1524年，若昂三世任命他为印度总督，同年12月24日他在科钦死于疟疾。

en:
Alexander Mikhailovich (c. 1295–1340) was prince of Pronsk and the only son of Mikhail Yaroslavich. In 1340, while escorting tribute to the khan of the Golden Horde, he was seized on the road by his cousin Ivan Korotopol, grand prince of Ryazan, who carried him to Pereyaslavl-Ryazansky and had him killed.

His son Yaroslav, baptized Dmitry, succeeded as prince of Pronsk and, with Tatar backing, drove Ivan from Ryazan in 1342.

亚历山大·米哈伊洛维奇（约1295—1340）为普龙斯克王公，是米哈伊尔·雅罗斯拉维奇的独子。1340年，他押送贡赋前往金帐汗国汗廷，途中被堂兄、梁赞大公伊凡·科罗托波尔劫持，押到佩列亚斯拉夫尔-梁赞斯基后杀害。

en:
Mikhail Yaroslavich (died c. 1303) was possibly a prince of Pronsk, the second son of Yaroslav Romanovich, prince of Ryazan and Pronsk. The Laurentian Chronicle notes strife among the Ryazan princes in 1300, which scholars read as a quarrel with their uncle Konstantin Romanovich.

The Moscow campaign against Ryazan in 1301, which ended in the capture of the Ryazan prince, may have grown out of that feud. Mikhail's son Alexander Mikhailovich was prince of Pronsk and was killed in 1340.

en:
Rostislav Yaroslavich (died 1153) was a Rurikid prince, youngest son of Yaroslav Svyatoslavich of Murom. After his father died in 1129 he held Pronsk while his brother ruled Ryazan; he took Ryazan in 1143 and Murom in 1145.

He backed Iziaslav Mstislavich of Kiev against Yuri Dolgoruky, was driven out in 1146 and fled to the Cumans, recovering Murom in 1149 and Ryazan in 1151. In 1153 he founded Rostislavl and, with Cuman help, drove Andrei Bogolyubsky from Ryazan.

en:
Yaroslav Alexandrovich, in baptism Dmitry (1315/1320–1344), was prince of Pronsk from 1340 and grand prince of Ryazan from 1342, son of Alexander Mikhailovich, murdered by Ivan Korotopol of Ryazan in 1340. In 1342 Khan Janibek granted him the Ryazan throne, and with a Tatar army he took Pereyaslavl-Ryazansky, putting Ivan to flight.

Not daring to remain in the city taken with Tatar help, Yaroslav moved his court to Rostislavl-Ryazansky, ruling there until his death in 1344. He was ancestor of the princes of Pronsk.

Alfonso II (1180–1209) was the second son of Alfonso II of Aragon and Sancha of Castile, born in Barcelona. In 1185 his father took the County of Provence from his uncle Sancho and settled it on him.

In 1193 he married Garsenda of Sabran at Aix-en-Provence; she was heiress to the County of Forcalquier, and their son was Raymond Berengar. He died at Palermo in February 1209 while escorting his elder sister Constance to her wedding with Emperor Frederick II.

1193年，他在普罗旺斯地区艾克斯娶萨布朗的加尔森达为妻，她是福卡尔基耶伯国的女继承人，二人之子为拉蒙·贝伦格。1209年2月，他在护送姐姐康斯坦丝前往与皇帝腓特烈二世成婚的途中，死于巴勒莫。

en:
Antonio Grimaldi (c. 1269–1358) belonged to the Guelph Grimaldi, the Genoese house that stood with the Angevin kings of Naples against the Ghibelline houses. His father Gaspare, captain of the people in 1317, handed Genoa to Robert of Anjou the next year, and under Angevin rule the family dominated the city; Antonio raised armies and fleets for the Angevins.

When the doge Simone Boccanegra drove the Grimaldi into exile, Antonio bought up lands around Nice and Monaco. In 1332 he ravaged the Catalan coast.

In 1353 he commanded the Genoese navy against Venice and Aragon and was crushed at Alghero. He held Antibes and Cagnes, and his sons Luca and Marco founded the Antibes branch of the family in 1384.

安东尼奥·格里马尔迪（约1269—1358）出身教皇派的格里马尔迪家族，这个热那亚家族与那不勒斯的安茹国王结盟，对抗吉伯林派家族。他的父亲加斯帕尔1317年出任平民领袖，次年将热那亚交给安茹的罗贝尔，此后家族在安茹统治下称雄城中；安东尼奥则为安茹家族招兵组舰。

总督西蒙·博卡内格拉将格里马尔迪家族逼出热那亚后，他在尼斯和摩纳哥一带买下大片土地。1332年他袭扰加泰罗尼亚海岸。

1353年，他统率热那亚舰队对抗威尼斯与阿拉贡，却在阿尔盖罗惨败。他领有昂蒂布和卡涅，其子卢卡与马尔科于1384年开创家族的昂蒂布支系。

en:
Barral I des Baux (1217–1270), lord of Les Baux in Provence, succeeded his father Hugues III in 1240. As seneschal of the Comtat Venaissin for Raymond VII of Toulouse, he seized the Comtat and was excommunicated by the archbishop of Arles.

In 1249 he backed the citizens of Arles against their archbishop and was named podestà. When Arles was besieged in 1251 he concentrated on defending his own lands, and he later reconciled with the archbishop.

Reconciled with Charles of Anjou, count of Provence, he became grand justiciar of Sicily after Charles took Naples in 1266, holding the office until his death at Avignon in 1270.

巴拉尔一世·德博（1217—1270）是普罗旺斯的莱博领主，1240年继承父亲于格三世之位。他作为图卢兹伯爵雷蒙七世的沃奈桑伯爵领地总管，夺取沃奈桑，被阿尔勒大主教处以绝罚。

en:
Beatrice of Provence (c. 1229–1267) was ruling countess of Provence and Forcalquier, youngest daughter of Count Ramon Berenguer of Provence. Her father's will left her the two counties, and on his death in 1245 she succeeded him.

James I of Aragon invaded Provence, and Beatrice and her mother took refuge in a fortress and sought papal protection. In 1246 Pope Innocent IV and Louis IX arranged her marriage to the king's brother Charles of Anjou.

She helped raise the army that won Charles the Kingdom of Sicily and was crowned queen beside him in Rome in 1266. She died in 1267, leaving Provence to Charles.

普罗旺斯的贝亚特丽斯（约1229—1267）是普罗旺斯与福卡尔基耶的执政女伯爵，普罗旺斯伯爵拉蒙·贝伦格尔的幼女。父亲的遗嘱把两个伯国传给她，1245年父亲去世后她继位。

阿拉贡国王海梅一世入侵普罗旺斯，贝亚特丽斯与母亲躲进堡垒，向教皇寻求庇护。1246年，教皇英诺森四世与法王路易九世安排她嫁给国王之弟安茹的查理。

她协助筹集军队，助查理取得西西里王国，并于1266年在罗马与查理一同加冕为后。她于1267年去世，普罗旺斯由查理继承。

en:
Berenguer Ramon (1114–1144) was the younger son of Ramon Berenguer III, Count of Barcelona, and Douce I, Countess of Provence. On his father's death in 1131 he inherited his mother's county of Provence while his elder brother took Barcelona, and in 1132 he defeated Alfonso Jordan, Count of Toulouse, over Melgueil and married Beatrice, its heiress.

Much of his reign was spent warring against the house of Baux and against Genoa. He died at Melgueil in 1144 and was succeeded by his young son Raymond Berengar.

In 1286 his cousin enfeoffed him with Meyrargues and other lands, and in 1308 Charles II of Naples gave him rights over Muy and Angles. His son Bertrand III became count of Andria.

en:
Douce II (c. 1162–1172) was the only child of Ramon Berenguer II, Count of Provence, and Richeza of Poland. In 1165 she was betrothed to Raymond, heir of Count Raymond V of Toulouse, and when her father was killed at the siege of Nice in 1166 she inherited Provence.

Raymond V sought to marry her mother, but her cousin Alfonso II of Aragon intervened and made war over the county. Alfonso prevailed, and in 1168 granted it to his brother Ramon Berenguer III, leaving Douce only the title. She moved to her grandmother's court and died in 1172, shortly after being promised a share of Melgueil.

en:
Hugh III des Baux (1173/74–1239/40), seventh lord of Les Baux, was the eldest son of Bertrand I des Baux. In 1195 he married Barale, heiress of the viscount of Marseille, becoming his house's first viscount of Marseille and an Occitan troubadour.

He later joined the revolt of Marseille, Arles and Avignon. Captured by Ramon Berenguer IV in 1231, he was ransomed in 1233 and recovered his lands; his son Barral succeeded him.

zh:
于格三世·德·博（1173/74—1239/40）是第七代莱博领主，贝特朗一世·德·博的长子。1195年他娶马赛子爵之女兼继承人巴拉勒，成为本家族首任马赛子爵，同时也是一名奥克语游吟诗人。

后来他加入马赛、阿尔勒和阿维尼翁的反叛。1231年他被雷蒙-贝伦格尔四世俘获，1233年缴付赎金获释并收回领地，死后由儿子巴拉尔继位。

en: Luc Grimaldi was a Genoese Guelph nobleman, the son of Antoine Grimaldi, co-lord of Monaco and Genoese admiral against Venice and Aragon. With his brother Marc he founded the Provençal branch of the Grimaldi: the two took possession of Cagnes in 1371, acquired Menton in 1382, and obtained Antibes in 1384, which gave the line its name.

en:
Marco Grimaldi was a Genoese nobleman, son of the Guelph admiral Antonio Grimaldi and Argentina Malaspina. Driven out of Genoa by the feuds of the Guelphs and Ghibellines, Marco and his brother Luca rebuilt the family on the Provençal coast, taking Cagnes in 1371, Menton in 1382 and Antibes in 1384, where they founded the Grimaldi branch of Antibes.

The line outlasted the Genoese quarrels by centuries. Lambert of the branch became lord of Monaco by marriage in 1465, and Henry IV bought Antibes from the family in 1608.

马尔科·格里马尔迪是热那亚贵族，教皇派海军统帅安东尼奥·格里马尔迪与阿尔真蒂娜·马拉斯皮纳之子。格里马尔迪家族在教皇派与皇帝派的党争中被逐出热那亚，马尔科与兄弟卢卡在普罗旺斯海岸重建家业：1371年取得卡涅，1382年取得芒通，1384年取得昂蒂布，并在那里建立昂蒂布支系。

en:
Raymond des Baux-Meyrargues (c. 1193–1235/37) was the son of Bertrand II des Baux, lord of Berre. Succeeding at Meyrargues around 1201, he married Alazacie, daughter of the viscount of Marseille, through whom he held the viscounty as Raymond IV.

He warred on Ramon Berenguer IV of Provence, making peace in 1228, then joined his uncle Hugh III and Raymond VII of Toulouse in a fresh war that ended in 1233. After his death his sons divided his lands.

en:
Ramon Berenguer II (c. 1135–1166) was Count of Provence from 1144, succeeding his father Berenguer Ramon. His uncle, Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona, was regent until 1157 and in 1147 intervened militarily against the house of Baux; war with the Baux dragged on until 1162.

In 1161 he travelled to Turin to obtain Emperor Frederick I's confirmation of his rule in Provence, and there met Richeza, daughter of the Polish duke Ladislaus II, whom he married that November. He resumed the war against Genoa and was assassinated at the siege of Nice in 1166; his daughter Douce II succeeded him.

拉蒙·贝伦格二世（约1135—1166）1144年继父亲贝伦格-雷蒙之后成为普罗旺斯伯爵。他的叔父、巴塞罗那伯爵拉蒙·贝伦格尔四世担任摄政至1157年，并于1147年出兵对抗莱博家族；与莱博家族的战争一直持续到1162年。

en:
Ramon Berenguer III of Provence (c. 1158–1181), born Peter, was the third son of Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona and Petronilla of Aragon. He first held Cerdanya, but passed it to his younger brother Sancho in 1168, and in 1173 their elder brother King Alfonso II granted him Provence.

In 1176 he helped Sancho take Nice, then campaigned in Languedoc and against Toulouse. In 1181 he was assassinated near Montpellier, and Provence passed to Sancho.

普罗旺斯伯爵雷蒙-贝伦格尔三世（约1158—1181），原名彼得，是巴塞罗那的拉蒙·贝伦格尔四世与阿拉贡的佩德罗尼拉的第三子。他最初领有塞尔达尼亚，1168年将其让给弟弟桑乔；1173年，兄长阿拉贡国王阿方索二世把普罗旺斯封给他。

en:
Ramon Berenguer (1198–1245) of the House of Barcelona was count of Provence and Forcalquier, the first count to reside there in a century. After his father Alfonso II died in 1209 he was sent to the Templar castle of Monzón, returning in 1216 to claim his inheritance, and in 1219 he married Beatrice of Savoy.

From 1226 he reasserted his authority over Marseille; he and Beatrice also supported troubadours at their court. In 1234 he pledged castles to provide a dowry for their daughter Margaret.

His four daughters married rulers: Margaret wed Louis IX of France, Eleanor Henry III of England, Sanchia Richard of Cornwall, and Beatrice Charles I of Sicily. He died at Aix in 1245, leaving Provence to Beatrice.

zh:
拉蒙·贝伦格尔（1198—1245）出身巴塞罗那家族，是普罗旺斯与福卡尔基耶伯爵，也是一个世纪以来首位长居领地的伯爵。1209年父亲阿方索二世去世后，他被送往蒙宗的圣殿骑士城堡，1216年返回继承领地，1219年娶萨伏依的贝阿特丽切。

1226年起他重新确立对马赛的主权，并与妻子在宫廷资助游吟诗人。1234年，为筹措女儿玛格丽特的嫁妆，他抵押了几座城堡。

他的四个女儿都嫁给君主：玛格丽特嫁给法王路易九世，埃莉诺嫁给英王亨利三世，桑奇亚嫁给罗马人的国王理查，贝阿特丽切嫁给西西里国王查理一世。1245年他在艾克斯去世，普罗旺斯由贝阿特丽切继承。

en:
Sancho (1161–1223) was the youngest son of Count Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona and Queen Petronilla of Aragon. He inherited Provence after the assassination of Ramon Berenguer III in 1181, but Alfonso II deposed him in 1185 for allying with Toulouse and Genoa.

He served as regent of Provence from 1209 and, after Peter II fell at Muret in 1213, as regent of Aragon for the young James I from 1214. His regencies ended in 1218, when papal pressure forced him out for supporting Raymond VI of Toulouse against the Albigensian Crusade, and he died in 1223.

en:
Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) was the philosopher of Königsberg whose three Critiques made him a central Enlightenment thinker. From a Pietist harness-maker's household, he entered Königsberg University at sixteen and studied under Martin Knutzen. From 1746 he tutored in the countryside, then lectured from 1755 and wrote on science, proposing that the solar system formed from a nebula.

Made professor of logic and metaphysics in 1770, he published little for ten years, woken from his dogmatic slumber, he said, by David Hume. The Critique of Pure Reason (1781), over 800 dense pages, initially disappointed readers; after his 1783 Prolegomena he became the most famous philosopher of his day.

The Critiques of Practical Reason (1788) and Judgment (1790) followed. In 1794 a royal order barred him from writing or speaking publicly on religion. He never married; neighbours reportedly set their watches by his daily walk. He died in Königsberg in 1804.

zh:
伊曼努尔·康德（1724—1804）是柯尼斯堡的德国哲学家，以三大批判成为启蒙运动的核心思想家。他出身虔敬派马具匠家庭，十六岁进入柯尼斯堡大学，在马丁·克努岑门下研读哲学与科学。1746年，他到乡间做家庭教师，1755年起在大学授课并撰写科学著作，提出太阳系由星云形成。

1770年他出任逻辑学与形而上学教授，此后近十年几乎没有著作问世；他自称是大卫·休谟把他从独断论的迷梦中唤醒。1781年的《纯粹理性批判》长达800多页、文字艰涩，起初令读者失望，1783年他写出《未来形而上学导论》回应，不久便成为当时最有名的哲学家。

此后他又写出《实践理性批判》（1788）和《判断力批判》（1790）。1794年，一道王室命令禁止他公开写作或谈论宗教。他终身未婚，相传邻居按他每天散步的时间对表。1804年，他在柯尼斯堡去世。

en:
Mahmud Malik azh-Zahir was the third sultan of Samudera Pasai in northern Sumatra, succeeding his father Muhammad Malik azh-Zahir in 1326.

During his reign the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta spent fifteen days at his court in 1345 or 1346 and described him as a devout ruler of the Shafi'i school who spoke fluent Arabic, lived simply and led campaigns to subdue neighbouring regions, advised by a council of high officials and scholars.

en:
Aleksandr Mikhailovich (1301–1339) was the fugitive prince of Tver whom Pskov adopted after the Tver uprising against the Tatars in 1327. The city made him its prince and sheltered him against Moscow and the Golden Horde.

When Metropolitan Theognostos excommunicated him and all Pskov at Ivan of Moscow's bidding, Aleksandr left for Lithuania rather than bring ruin on the city, returning in 1331 or 1332. He left for Sarai in 1338 and was executed in 1339.

亚历山大·米哈伊洛维奇（1301—1339）是1327年特维尔反鞑靼起义后出逃的特维尔王公，被普斯科夫收留。市民拥戴他为本城王公，抗拒莫斯科与金帐汗国的追索。

在莫斯科的伊凡施压下，都主教费奥格诺斯特将他和全城革出教门；亚历山大不愿连累普斯科夫，遂出走立陶宛，1331或1332年返回。他1338年前往萨莱，1339年在该处被处死。

en:
Sudislav Vladimirovich (died 1063), youngest son of Vladimir the Great of Kiev, ruled as prince of Pskov from 1014. In 1036 his brother Yaroslav the Wise seized him, abolished his principality and imprisoned him in Kiev for twenty-three years to secure the succession for his sons.

In 1059 his nephews freed him after he swore to renounce the throne. He became a monk at Saint George's Monastery and died there in 1063, the first Rurikid prince recorded as a monk.

苏季斯拉夫·弗拉基米罗维奇（?—1063）是基辅大公弗拉基米尔一世的幼子，自1014年起任普斯科夫王公。1036年，兄长智者雅罗斯拉夫将他拘捕，废除普斯科夫公国，把他关押在基辅长达23年，以为儿子稳固继承权。

en:
Albert II of Saxe-Wittenberg (c. 1285–1342) was the third son of Duke Albert II of Saxe-Wittenberg and Agnes of Habsburg. Destined for the Church, he served as a canon of Mainz before Pope John XXII named him prince-bishop of Passau in 1320.

In the German throne dispute he backed his Habsburg cousin Frederick the Fair, fighting for him at Mühldorf in 1322. At Passau he sold the town hall back to the citizens, and he died there on 19 May 1342 and was buried in its cathedral.

en:
Guido Orsini (1305–1348), second son of Romano Orsini, count of Sovana, founded the Pitigliano line of the House of Orsini. In 1336 his father granted him Sovana, later called the county of Pitigliano after its unhealthy capital was abandoned. At the locals' call he warred on Ermanno Monaldeschi, lord of Orvieto.

He served Perugia as captain general from 1342, and in 1347 became lord and defender of Orvieto. He fled the plague and died in 1348, leaving sons Aldobrandino and Gentile.

Guido Orsini (1305–1348), second son of #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('ptg_romano_orsini').GetID],X #L Romano Orsini#!#!, count of Sovana, founded the Pitigliano line of the House of Orsini. In 1336 his father granted him Sovana, later called the county of Pitigliano after its unhealthy capital was abandoned. At the locals' call he warred on Ermanno Monaldeschi, lord of [ShowLocationName('orvietano')].

He served Perugia as captain general from 1342, and in 1347 became lord and defender of Orvieto. He fled the plague and died in 1348, leaving sons Aldobrandino and Gentile.
zh:
圭多·奥尔西尼（1305—1348）是索瓦纳伯爵罗马诺·奥尔西尼的次子，也是奥尔西尼家族皮蒂利亚诺支系的始祖。1336年，父亲将索瓦纳伯国封给他；后来因索瓦纳疫病流行、城池废弃，该伯国改称皮蒂利亚诺伯国。他应当地人之请，起兵征讨奥尔维耶托领主埃尔曼诺·莫纳尔德斯基。

1342年他出任佩鲁贾统帅，1347年被奥尔维耶托迎为城主与保护者。1348年他为躲避鼠疫离开该城，同年去世，留下阿尔多布兰迪诺和真蒂莱等子。

en:
Romano Orsini (c. 1270–1326) was an Italian condottiero and the fourth count of Sovana, son of Gentile Orsini. In 1293, backed by Cardinal Matteo Orsini and Charles II of Anjou, he married Anastasia de Montfort, heiress through her father to Nola and, through her mother, to Sovana and Pitigliano.

The marriage made him count of Nola and Sovana and began the Orsini line of Pitigliano. In 1297 Pope Boniface VIII sent him against the Colonna, and in 1325 he became senator of Rome.

zh:
罗马诺·奥尔西尼（约1270—1326）是意大利佣兵首领、第四代索瓦纳伯爵，为真蒂莱·奥尔西尼之子。1293年，在枢机主教马泰奥·奥尔西尼与安茹的查理二世支持下，他与阿纳斯塔西娅·德·蒙特福特成婚：她凭父系继承诺拉，又凭母系继承索瓦纳和皮蒂利亚诺。

这场婚姻使他成为诺拉伯爵兼索瓦纳伯爵，并开创了奥尔西尼家族的皮蒂利亚诺支系。1297年教皇卜尼法斯八世派他攻打科隆纳家族；1325年他出任罗马元老。

en:
Phaya Phanong, also known as Phaya Phakong the Elder, was a Khon Mueang ruler of Mueang Pua in the Phukha dynasty during the Sukhothai period. The Nan chronicles make him the son of Chao Kao Khuean, born Khun Sai, and a descendant of Phaya Phu Kha; his grandfather Khun Fong founded Pua.

He ruled Pua from 1320 to 1349. His sons Chao Sai and Chao Kan Mueang succeeded him, and his grandson Phaya Phakong the Younger later founded Nan.

帕亚帕农，又称长者帕亚帕空，是素可泰时期普卡王朝的磨城傣阮统治者。据《难府纪年》记载，他是昭九根之子，原名坤赛，为帕亚普卡的后裔，祖父坤丰出走另建磨城。

他于1320—1349年统治磨城，死后由儿子昭赛与昭干孟相继继位，其孙幼者帕亚帕空后来兴建了难城。

en:
Prithvi Malla was a king of the Khasa, or Yatse, kingdom, a Himalayan state ruled from Sinja in western Nepal. His father Punya Malla came from a Khas family of Purang royalty and governed the kingdom in 1336–1339.

His inscriptions date from 1354 to 1358, and the stone pillar he raised at Dullu in 1357 records his ten predecessors. After his rule the old Nagaraja line returned to power under Surya Malla, and the kingdom soon broke into small principalities.

普里特维·马拉是卡萨（又称亚泽）王国的国王，这个喜马拉雅王国以尼泊尔西部的辛贾为都。他的父亲普尼亚·马拉出身布让王族的卡斯人一支，于1336—1339年在位。

他留下的碑铭年代为1354—1358年，1357年在杜鲁竖立的石柱上刻有十位先王的名录。他之后，那加拉者旧族在苏利耶·马拉率领下重掌王权，王国随后分裂为诸小邦。

en:
Punya Malla, attested from 1336 to 1339, was a king of the Khasa Malla kingdom in the western Himalayas. Born Punya Pal, a chief of the Khas house of Purang in Tibet, he married a daughter of King Aditya Malla.

When the Nagaraja dynasty had no heir, he was called to the throne at Sinja and exchanged the title Pal for Malla. His inscriptions stress his double descent. He was succeeded by his son Prithvi Malla.

普尼亚·马拉于1336—1339年间有载，是喜马拉雅山西段卡萨马拉王国的国王。他原名普尼亚·帕尔，出身西藏布让的卡萨王族，后娶国王阿底提耶·马拉之女。

纳加拉杰旧王世系绝嗣后，他被迎往辛贾继位，并弃用帕尔称号、改称马拉。他在碑铭中强调自己兼具两系血统，王位后由其子普里特维·马拉继承。

en:
Qarachar Noyan (c. 1166–1243/44 or 1255/56) was a Mongol commander of the Barlas tribe and paternal ancestor of Timur. The Secret History records him leading a delegation to the 1190 assembly that proclaimed Temüjin ruler of the Mongols, and Rashid al-Din describes him as one of Chagatai Khan's military chiefs.

Timurid works such as the Zafarnama exalted him as hereditary head of the imperial guard and chief judge, assigned by Genghis Khan to Chagatai; Timur invoked this tradition to claim hereditary rule. His son Ichil succeeded him.

zh:
哈剌察儿那颜（约1166—1243/44或1255/56）是巴鲁剌思部的蒙古将领，也是帖木儿的父系先祖。《蒙古秘史》记载，他率代表团参加1190年推举铁木真为蒙古人首领的大会；拉施特丁《史集》称他是察合台汗麾下的一名军事长官。

帖木儿朝官史如《帖木儿武功记》把他抬高为大汗禁卫军的世袭统领和首席断事官，由成吉思汗指派侍奉察合台；帖木儿援引这一传统宣称世袭统治权。其子亦连吉儿承袭了他的职位。

en:
Ürüg Temür, also called Yulong Temür, was a Yuan Mongol prince and fifth-generation descendant of Qasar, Genghis Khan's brother. In 1319 he was enfeoffed as Prince of En, and in 1326 he succeeded as Prince of Qi with pastures on the Ergun and Hailar rivers.

During the succession war of 1328 he sided with Tugh Temür against Ragibagh: his troops besieged Shangdu, forced chancellor Dawlat Shah to surrender with the imperial seal and captured and killed Tokto, Prince of Liao. He died in 1329 and was succeeded by his son Shiremen.

月鲁帖木儿（又作玉龙帖木儿）是元朝蒙古宗王，为成吉思汗之弟合撒儿的五世孙。1319年他受封恩王，1326年嗣封齐王，封地在也里古纳河、海剌尔河一带。

1328年的帝位之争中，他站在图帖睦尔一边反对阿剌吉八：率兵围攻上都，迫使丞相倒剌沙奉玉玺出降，又擒杀辽王脱脱。1329年他去世，子失列门嗣爵。

en:
Shidur, also written Shidür, was a Yuan Mongol prince, the great-grandson of Qasar and grandson of Yesüngge. He inherited Yesüngge's appanage of pastures around the Argun and Hailar rivers and Hulun Lake.

In 1287 he answered Nayan's rebellion in Liaodong, in league with Qadan and in touch with Kaidu. Yuan forces under Prince Ayači and the Liaodong pacification commissioner Dachu defeated him; he surrendered and confessed, and Kublai Khan spared his life, though one account says he was executed.

势都儿（又译失都儿）是元朝蒙古宗王，为合撒儿曾孙、移相哥之孙。他承袭移相哥的封地，据有额尔古纳河、海拉尔河与呼伦湖一带。

1287年乃颜在辽东反叛，势都儿起兵响应，与哈丹秃鲁干结盟、与海都相约呼应。皇子爱牙赤与辽东道宣慰使塔出率军将他击败；势都儿认罪归降，忽必烈赦免其罪，一说终被处死。

en:
Yesüngge was a Mongol prince, the second son of Qasar, Genghis Khan's younger brother. Around 1225, after the Khwarazmian campaign, he hit a target at 335 paces before the Mongol nobility; his feat was commemorated on the Yesüngge Stone, the oldest surviving Mongolian-script inscription.

He supported the enthronements of Ögedei in 1229 and Möngke in 1251, and in 1260 led Kublai Khan's vanguard against Ariq Böke. He is said to have lived about seventy-five years.

移相哥是蒙古宗王，为成吉思汗之弟合撒儿的次子。约1225年西征花剌子模归来后，他在蒙古贵族面前于335步外射中靶心，其射艺被刻石纪念，即现存最早的畏兀字蒙文石刻“也松格碑”。

他曾于1229年拥戴窝阔台、1251年拥戴蒙哥即大汗位，1260年充任忽必烈汗的前锋讨伐阿里不哥。相传他享年约七十五岁。

en:
Jochi Qasar (1164–c. 1219), second son of Yesugei and brother of Genghis Khan, earned his nickname Khasar, after a fierce hunting dog, for bravery and archery. With Temüjin he killed half-brother Begter over hunting spoils. In 1203, after the defeat at Khalakhaljid Sands, a false surrender in his name lured the Kereite Ong Khan to ruin.

He commanded the centre against Naiman Tayang Khan and in 1206 received four thousand households on the Hulunbuir steppe. In 1213 he led the left wing against the Jin, taking Jizhou and other cities. His descendants became the Khorchin Mongols.

拙赤合撒儿（1164—约1219）是也速该次子、成吉思汗的同母弟，因勇武善射得绰号合撒儿，即一种猛犬之名。少年时他与铁木真合谋射杀异母兄别克帖儿。1203年合兰真沙陀战败后，一封以他名义送出的诈降书诱使克烈部王汗中计败亡。

他征讨乃蛮太阳汗时统领中军，1206年受封四千户，封地在呼伦贝尔草原。1213年他率左翼军攻金，攻取蓟州等地。他的后裔是科尔沁部蒙古人。

en:
Ürük Temür (c. 1318–1353) was a Uyghur idiqut, the hereditary ruler of the Qocho Uyghurs, also holding the Yuan title of Prince of Gaochang. The son of Taipinu, when he succeeded, the old Qocho lands around Turpan had fallen to the Chagatai Khanate and the idiqut family served the Yuan emperor in China.

He died on 14 July 1353 while with the Yuan army at Nanyang, and his son Sengge inherited his titles.

月鲁帖木儿（约1318—1353）是畏兀儿人，高昌回鹘的世袭亦都护，兼领元朝所封的高昌王爵。他是太平奴之子，继位时吐鲁番一带的高昌故地已沦入察合台汗国，亦都护一族迁居内地，为元朝效力。

1353年7月14日，他在南阳军中去世，其子桑哥承袭亦都护与高昌王爵位。

en:
Filippo Belegno (born 1265) was a Venetian patrician of the old Belegno family and a ducal councilor. During the Tiepolo conspiracy of June 1310, with Bajamonte Tiepolo's rebels holding the Rialto, Doge Pietro Gradenigo sent several envoys in vain.

Belegno at last persuaded Tiepolo at the last moment to lay down his arms, opening the way to the exile settlement approved by the Great Council. From 1337 to 1339 he served Venice as count, or rector, of Ragusa in Dalmatia.

菲利波·贝莱尼奥（1265年生）出身威尼斯古老的贝莱尼奥贵族世家，曾任公爵顾问。1310年6月的提埃波罗之乱中，巴亚蒙特·提埃波罗率叛军占据里亚尔托，总督彼得罗·格拉代尼戈接连派出的说客均无功而返。

en:
Ragibagh (1320–1328), remembered as the Tianshun Emperor, was the eldest son of Yesün Temür and was named crown prince in infancy in 1324. After his father died suddenly at Shangdu in August 1328, El Temür launched a coup at Dadu and raised Tugh Temür to the throne; the minister Dawlat Shah installed Ragibagh at Shangdu.

The War of the Two Capitals followed. Ragibagh's troops broke through the Great Wall but were routed, and Shangdu surrendered; Dawlat Shah was captured and executed, while Ragibagh vanished, evidently murdered, making him the shortest-reigning of Yuan emperors.

阿剌吉八（1320—1328），即天顺帝，也孙铁木儿长子，1324年尚在襁褓中即被立为皇太子。1328年8月父亲猝死于上都后，燕帖木儿在大都发动政变，拥立图帖睦尔；大臣倒剌沙则在上都拥立阿剌吉八。

两都之战随即爆发。阿剌吉八的军队虽突破长城，却遭惨败，上都投降；倒剌沙被俘处死，阿剌吉八本人下落不明，一般认为已遇害，他是元朝在位时间最短的皇帝。

en:
Bernardino I da Polenta (died 1359) succeeded his father Ostasio I as lord of Ravenna in 1346. In 1347 his brother Pandolfo imprisoned him, but Malatesta mediation won his release; later that year Bernardino locked up Pandolfo and their brother Lamberto at Cervia, where they died.

He kept Ravenna quiet with executions and exile, and the city knew his reign for war and crushing taxes. In 1354 Count Lando's Great Company sacked Ravenna and left the next month after Bernardino offered 12,000 florins, and in 1356 he became papal vicar of Ravenna for ten years in return for an annual payment.

A tax revolt in 1357 was crushed, with more than a hundred people arrested or killed. He died in 1359, and his son Guido III succeeded him.

贝尔纳迪诺一世·达·波伦塔（？—1359）1346年继父亲奥斯塔西奥一世之位成为拉韦纳领主。1347年，兄弟潘多尔福囚禁了他，经马拉泰斯塔家族调停后获释；同年晚些时候，贝尔纳迪诺将潘多尔福和另一名兄弟兰贝托囚禁于切尔维亚，二人死于狱中。

他以处决和流放压住拉韦纳的反对声音，治下城市以战乱和沉重赋税闻名。1354年兰多伯爵的大兵团洗劫拉韦纳，在贝尔纳迪诺许以12,000弗洛林后于次月撤走；1356年他获任拉韦纳教皇代理人，任期十年，须每年缴纳贡金。

1357年的赋税叛乱被他镇压，百余人被捕或被杀。他于1359年去世，儿子圭多三世继位。

en:
Bernardino da Polenta (died 1314) was an Italian condottiero of the da Polenta family and the son of Guido I of Ravenna. He was podestà of Cervia in 1283 and helped his father establish the family's control over the city.

He fought over Cesena in 1302–1303, and in 1306, as podestà of Bologna, he rescued the papal legate during a revolt. In the war of 1308 he and his brother Lamberto took Ferrara from the Venetians for the pope and Francesco d'Este.

In 1312 he joined the Tuscan Guelphs and Robert of Anjou against Emperor Henry VII. He died in Florence while serving as podestà.

en:
Caterina Malabocca was the daughter of the counts Malvicini of Bagnacavallo in the Romagna hinterland. Before March 1310 she married Guido Novello da Polenta, lord of Ravenna, a match linking the ruling Polentani to her family's inland lordship.

She bore him five children, among them Lamberto, Ostasio, Costanza, who married the Paduan nobleman Niccolò da Carrara, and Polentesia, who married Malatestino Novello Malatesta. She also used her right of church patronage to obtain benefices in Ravenna for Pietro Alighieri, the poet Dante's son. She died in 1327.

卡泰丽娜·马拉博卡出身罗马涅腹地巴尼亚卡瓦洛的马拉维奇尼伯爵家族。1310年3月之前，她嫁给拉文纳统治者圭多·诺韦洛·达·波伦塔，这桩联姻把当政的波伦塔家族与娘家在内地的领地联系在一起。

她生有五个子女，包括兰贝托、奥斯塔西奥、嫁给帕多瓦贵族尼科洛·达·卡拉拉的科斯坦扎，以及嫁给马拉泰斯蒂诺·诺韦洛·马拉泰斯塔的波伦泰西娅。她还以自己的教堂庇护权，为诗人但丁之子彼得罗·阿利吉耶里谋得拉文纳教堂的有俸圣职，1327年去世。

en:
Guido I da Polenta, called Guido the Old (died 1310), was the Guelph lord who made the da Polenta family masters of Ravenna. The son of Lamberto da Polenta, he seized the city in 1275 with Malatesta cavalry, founding a signoria that lasted until 1441.

He fought Guido Riccio da Polenta for power and allied with the Malatesta against Guido da Montefeltro. He married his daughter Francesca to Giovanni Malatesta and took Cervia in 1282.

He abdicated in 1297 in favour of his sons Lamberto and Bernardino. Francesca, murdered by her husband, was immortalised in Dante's Inferno, and his grandson Guido Novello hosted Dante in Ravenna.

圭多一世·达·波伦塔，人称“老圭多”（？—1310），是让达·波伦塔家族成为拉韦纳主人的教皇派领主。他是兰贝托·达·波伦塔之子，1275年凭借马拉泰斯塔家族的骑兵夺取拉韦纳，建立了一直延续到1441年的家族统治。

他与圭多·里乔·达·波伦塔争权，并与马拉泰斯塔家族结盟对抗圭多·达·蒙特费尔特罗。他将女儿弗朗切斯卡嫁给乔凡尼·马拉泰斯塔，1282年取得切尔维亚。

1297年他退位，由儿子兰贝托和贝尔纳迪诺继位。弗朗切斯卡被丈夫杀害，因但丁《神曲·地狱篇》的描写而不朽；他的孙子圭多·诺韦洛后来在拉韦纳接待了但丁。

en:
Guido Novello da Polenta (c. 1275–1333) was lord of Ravenna from 1316 to 1322 and a poet. Son of Ostasio da Polenta, he succeeded his uncle Lamberto I, sought peace and encouraged a literary circle in Ravenna.

He is remembered as Dante's patron: the exiled Florentine lived in Ravenna from 1318, and when Dante died in 1321 Guido gave him a solemn funeral.

In 1322 he was elected captain of the people at Bologna and left Ravenna to his brother Archbishop Rinaldo, whom their cousin Ostasio I murdered while seizing the city. Guido died in 1333, having failed to reconquer Ravenna.

圭多·诺韦洛·达·波伦塔（约1275—1333）1316至1322年任拉韦纳领主，本人也是诗人。他是奥斯塔西奥·达·波伦塔之子，继叔父兰贝托一世之位。他追求和平，扶持拉韦纳的文学圈。

他最知名的身份是但丁的庇护者：这位流亡的佛罗伦萨人自1318年起住在拉韦纳，1321年但丁去世后，圭多为他举行了隆重葬礼。

1322年，他当选博洛尼亚平民领袖，把拉韦纳交给任大主教的兄弟里纳尔多；堂亲奥斯塔西奥一世杀害里纳尔多并夺取城市。圭多于1333年去世，始终未能夺回拉韦纳。

en:
Lamberto I da Polenta (c. 1275–22 June 1316) was an Italian condottiero, eldest son of Guido da Polenta il Vecchio, who made the da Polenta masters of Ravenna. In 1301 his father named him successor and Lamberto took up the city's podestàship in perpetuity, founding the da Polenta signoria.

In 1312 he hosted Robert of Anjou in Ravenna during the king's war against Emperor Henry VII. He died in Ravenna on 22 June 1316 and was succeeded by his nephew Guido Novello.

兰贝托一世·达·波伦塔（约1275—1316年6月22日）是意大利佣兵首领，为带领达·波伦塔家族成为拉文纳之主的圭多·达·波伦塔（老圭多）的长子。1301年，父亲指定他为继承人，兰贝托永久执掌城市的波德斯塔一职，奠定了达·波伦塔家族僭主统治的基础。

1312年，他在拉文纳接待正与皇帝亨利七世作战的安茹的罗贝托。1316年6月22日他卒于拉文纳，由侄子圭多·诺韦洛继位。

Lamberto II da Polenta (died 1347) was a son of Ostasio I da Polenta, lord of Ravenna and Cervia. When Ostasio died in 1346, Lamberto inherited the lordships together with his brothers Bernardino I and Pandolfo.

Bernardino I soon made himself sole ruler and shut Lamberto and Pandolfo up at Cervia, where the two brothers were starved to death in 1347.

en:
Ostasio I da Polenta (died 1346) made himself lord of Ravenna by murder. The son of Bernardino da Polenta, lord of Cervia, in September 1322, with his cousin Guido Novello away serving at Bologna, he seized Ravenna and killed Archbishop Rinaldo da Polenta.

In 1326 he killed his uncle Bannino, who held Cervia, and took that lordship as well. A patron of letters, he had Giovanni Boccaccio at his court in 1345–1346.

Pope Benedict XII gave his rule legal standing by naming him papal vicar, but Ostasio died that November, allegedly murdered by his son Bernardino, who succeeded him.

奥斯塔西奥一世·达·波伦塔（？—1346）以谋杀夺得拉韦纳。他是切尔维亚领主贝尔纳迪诺·达·波伦塔之子。1322年9月，他趁堂亲圭多·诺韦洛赴博洛尼亚任职之机夺取拉韦纳，杀害大主教里纳尔多·达·波伦塔。

en:
Ostasio da Polenta (died 1297) was an Italian condottiero, a son of Guido da Polenta il Vecchio, founder of da Polenta rule in Ravenna. In 1282 he fought alongside the papal commander Giovanni d'Appia and helped storm Ghibelline Meldola, held by Guido da Montefeltro. He was elected podestà of Faenza in 1288 and podestà of Ravenna in 1290.

In 1297 he was joint podestà of Ravenna with his brother Lamberto, and died that year. His son Guido Novello ruled Ravenna as Dante's host.

奥斯塔西奥·达·波伦塔（?—1297）是意大利佣兵首领，为达·波伦塔家族在拉文纳统治的奠基者老圭多之子。1282年，他与教皇军将领乔瓦尼·达皮亚并肩作战，参与攻下圭多·达·蒙特费尔特罗占据的吉伯林派城市梅尔多拉。1288年他当选法恩扎的波德斯塔，1290年任拉文纳的波德斯塔。

1297年，他与兄弟兰贝托共同担任拉文纳波德斯塔，同年去世。其子圭多·诺韦洛后来统治拉文纳，曾庇护但丁。

en:
Siemowit II of Rawa (1283–1345), eldest son of Bolesław II of Płock, was a Piast duke who ruled central Masovia. He received Warsaw and Liw from his father in 1310, and after Bolesław died in 1313 made Rawa Mazowiecka his capital.

His long rule was spent maneuvering among Władysław I the Elbow-high, the Teutonic Order, Bohemia and Lithuania, repeatedly switching alliances to keep his duchy independent. He served as regent of Płock from 1336 to 1340 and welcomed the Peace of Kalisz between Poland and the Order in 1343.

拉瓦的谢莫维特二世（1283—1345）是普沃茨克公爵波列斯瓦夫二世的长子，皮亚斯特王朝治下统治马佐夫舍中部的公爵。1310年他先从父亲手中得到华沙与利夫，1313年父亲死后以马佐夫舍地区拉瓦为都城。

他在位期间长期周旋于瓦迪斯瓦夫一世“矮子”、条顿骑士团、波希米亚与立陶宛之间，屡次改换盟约，以维持公国独立。1336至1340年他担任普沃茨克摄政，1343年波兰与骑士团签订《卡利什和约》，使他得以安枕。

Frederick I, Count of Rietberg (died 5 July 1282), was the eldest son of Count Conrad I and Oda of Lippe. He married Beatrix of Horstmar. In 1264 his father, by then a Teutonic Knight, made the county over to him.

In 1267 Frederick fought for Archbishop Engelbert II of Cologne at the battle of Zülpich, was captured by Bishop Gerard of Münster, and spent a year and a half in prison. He died in 1282 and was buried at Marienfeld Abbey, succeeded by his son Conrad II.

en:
Conrad I, Count of Rietberg (born after 1203, died 1284–1294), was a son of Count Henry II of Arnsberg. In 1237 he and his brother Godfrey III divided Arnsberg: Godfrey kept Arnsberg while Conrad received the Rietberg lands on the upper Ems and the family's Dutch holdings, making Rietberg a territory in its own right.

In the same year he married Oda of Lippe. He later joined the Teutonic Order and in 1264, after Oda's death in 1262, made the county over to their son Frederick I.

Conrad II, Count of Rietberg (died 24 April 1313), was the son of Count Frederick I and Beatrix of Horstmar. He inherited the Westphalian county on his father's death in 1282. In 1302 he governed the county jointly with his brother Frederick II.

By his wife Mechthild, who died in 1304, he had nine children. When he died in 1313 his share passed to his son Otto I, who ruled until 1347. Conrad was buried at Marienfeld Abbey.

John I, Viscount of Rochechouart (died 19 September 1356), was a Limousin nobleman who held the castle of Rochechouart and the lordship of Tonnay-Charente. On 11 April 1336 he married Jeanne de Sully, daughter of Henry IV de Sully, grand butler and grand treasurer of France.

She brought him the lordships of Corbigny and Brion. He died at Poitiers on 19 September 1356. His grandson John II later held the viscounty.

en:
Jeanne de Sully (died 1385), lady of Corbigny and Brion, was a daughter of Henry IV de Sully, grand butler and grand treasurer of France under King Philip V, and Jeanne de Vendôme-Montoire. On 11 April 1336 she married John I, Viscount of Rochechouart and lord of Tonnay-Charente, carrying her estates at Corbigny and Brion into the Rochechouart family.

Her husband died at Poitiers on 19 September 1356, and she survived him by nearly thirty years. Their grandson John II became viscount.

en:
Singama I (ruled 1326–1361) was a Telugu Recherla Nayaka and founder of a Padmanayaka kingdom in Telangana. During the reign of the Kakatiya king Prataparudra II, he fought alongside his father in the Kanchi wars and received the title Ashitivarala Singama Nayaka. After the fall of the Kakatiyas, he joined Prolaya Nayaka in the struggle against the rulers from Delhi.

As independent kingdoms emerged in the Telugu country, Singama established his own at Amanagallu and opposed Kapaya Nayaka. He was succeeded by Anavota in 1361; Anavota moved the capital from Amanagallu to Rachakonda.

During the reign of the Kakatiya king Prataparudra II, he fought alongside his father in the Kanchi wars and received the title Ashitivarala Singama Nayaka. After the fall of the Kakatiyas, he joined Prolaya Nayaka in the struggle against the rulers from [ShowLocationName('delhi')].

As independent kingdoms emerged in the Telugu country, Singama established his own at Amanagallu and opposed Kapaya Nayaka. He was succeeded by Anavota in 1361; Anavota moved the capital from Amanagallu to [ShowLocationName('rachakonda')].
zh:
辛伽玛一世（1326—1361年在位）是泰卢固的隶契罗·那耶迦首领，在特伦甘纳建立了帕德马纳耶迦王国。卡卡蒂亚国王钵罗陀波楼陀罗二世在位时，他与父亲一同参加甘吉战争，获得阿什蒂瓦拉拉·辛伽玛·那耶迦的称号。卡卡蒂亚王国灭亡后，他与普罗拉亚·那耶迦共同抗击来自德里的统治者。

随着泰卢固地区出现多个独立王国，辛伽玛在阿马纳加卢建立自己的王国，并反对卡帕亚·那耶迦。1361年阿纳沃塔继位，将都城从阿马纳加卢迁至拉彻孔达。

en:
Prolaya Vema Reddi (died 1353), a commander of the Kakatiya empire, founded the Reddi Kingdom in 1325 after the dynasty fell to the Delhi Sultanate in 1323. Making Addanki his capital, he ruled from Kandukur to the Godavari coast.

He built an army of peasants and herdsmen and waged guerrilla war against the Turkish invaders, allying with Hoysala king Vira Ballala III and Kapaya Nayaka of Warangal. He built the hill forts of Kondapalli and Kondaveedu. At his court the poet Erranna completed the Andhra Mahabharatam.

普罗拉亚·吠摩·罗底（？—1353）原是卡卡提亚王朝的将领。1323年卡卡提亚王朝被德里苏丹国攻灭后，他于1325年建立罗底王朝，以阿登吉为都，疆域从坎杜库尔一直延伸到戈达瓦里海岸。

他征发农民和牧民组成军队，以游击战抗击突厥入侵者，并与曷萨拉国王维拉·巴拉拉三世及瓦朗加尔的卡帕亚·纳亚卡结盟。他修建了孔达帕利和孔达维杜两座山堡。诗人埃拉纳在他的宫廷中完成了《安得拉摩诃婆罗多》。

Heinrich Bullinger (1504–1575) was a Swiss Reformer, born at Bremgarten in Aargau. Studying at Cologne, he accepted Reformation teaching through the Bible and Luther's works. From 1523 he taught and preached at Kappel Abbey, where he introduced systematic Bible study.

Following Zwingli's death at Kappel in 1531, Bullinger succeeded him as the leading pastor of the Church of Zürich, holding the office for more than forty years.

He helped draft the First Helvetic Confession in 1536, joined John Calvin in a 1549 agreement on the Lord's Supper, and shaped the Second Helvetic Confession of 1566. He died at Zürich in 1575.

海因里希·布林格（1504—1575）是瑞士宗教改革家，生于阿尔高的布雷姆加滕。他在科隆求学期间通过圣经和马丁·路德的著作接受了宗教改革教义。1523年起，他到卡佩尔修道院任教、布道，推行系统的圣经研读。

1531年慈运理在卡佩尔战死后，布林格继任苏黎世教会首席牧师，任职四十余年。

1536年，他参与起草《第一海尔维第信纲》；1549年与约翰·加尔文就圣餐教义达成共识；1566年又主持完成《第二海尔维第信纲》。1575年，他在苏黎世去世。

en:
Guido de Bres (1522–1567) was a Walloon Reformed pastor and theologian, born at Mons in Hainaut. Trained as a glass painter, he embraced Protestantism in his youth and fled to England in 1548. He later studied under John Calvin in Geneva, returning around 1559 to the Low Countries as a travelling preacher.

In 1561 he drafted the Belgic Confession for the Spanish government and threw it over Tournai's castle wall to reach the governor. After the Siege of Valenciennes he was tried by the Spanish Inquisition and hanged in the city in May 1567.

en:
Justus Jonas (1493–1555) was a German Lutheran reformer and theologian, best known as the German translator of Luther and Melanchthon. Born at Nordhausen, he studied law at Erfurt and Wittenberg and became rector of Erfurt University in 1519.

He followed Luther to the 1521 Diet of Worms and helped translate Luther's German Bible as a Wittenberg professor. In 1531 he translated the Apology of the Augsburg Confession into German, and as superintendent he led Halle's Reformation.

He was at Luther's Eisleben deathbed in 1546 and preached his funeral sermon. Soon exiled, he died at Eisfeld in 1555.

尤斯图斯·约纳斯（1493—1555）是德国路德派改革家、神学家，尤以把路德和梅兰希通的著作译成德文闻名。他生于诺德豪森，曾在爱尔福特和维滕贝格学习法律，1519年任爱尔福特大学校长。

他追随路德出席1521年沃尔姆斯帝国会议，作为维滕贝格教授协助翻译路德的德文圣经。1531年他将《奥格斯堡信纲辩护书》译成德文，并以总监督身份主持哈雷的宗教改革。

1546年他在艾斯莱本陪伴路德临终，并为其葬礼讲道。不久他遭流放，1555年死于艾斯费尔德。

en:
Philipp Melanchthon (1497–1560), born Philipp Schwartzerdt, was Luther's closest collaborator and the first systematic theologian of the Reformation. His great-uncle Reuchlin suggested the Greek form of his surname, meaning black earth. Recommended by Reuchlin, he took Wittenberg's new Greek chair in 1518, aged twenty-one, and Luther called him the little Greek.

In 1519 he joined Luther at the Leipzig Disputation, and in 1521 published the Loci communes, the Wittenberg Reformation's first dogmatics. While Luther hid at the Wartburg, he stood in for him at the university. At the Diet of Augsburg in 1530 he wrote the Augsburg Confession, followed in 1531 by its Apology, authoritative confessions of the Lutheran church.

After the Schmalkaldic War defeat in 1547, his compromise over the Interim brought conflict with Matthias Flacius. He died in 1560 and was buried beside Luther in Wittenberg's Castle Church, bearing the title Praeceptor Germaniae, teacher of Germany.

菲利普·梅兰希通（1497—1560）原名菲利普·施瓦策尔特，是路德最亲密的合作者、宗教改革第一位系统神学家。叔祖罗伊希林建议他改用希腊文姓氏，意为黑土。经其举荐，1518年二十一岁的他出任维滕贝格希腊语教席，路德称他为“小希腊人”。

1519年随路德参加莱比锡辩论会，1521年发表《共同要义》，是维滕贝格改革第一部教义学著作。路德隐居瓦尔特堡期间，他在大学代行其职。1530年奥格斯堡议会上撰写《奥格斯堡信纲》，1531年写出《辩护书》，成为路德宗权威信条。

1547年施马尔卡尔登战争败后，他因《临时协定》的妥协与弗拉齐乌斯冲突。1560年去世，葬于维滕贝格城堡教堂路德墓旁，称号“德意志之师”。

en:
Nikolaus von Ybbs (c. 1275–1340) was a cleric from Ybbs an der Donau who probably studied law at Bologna and served in the royal chanceries of Albert I and Henry VII before his election as prince-bishop of Regensburg on 19 March 1313.

In the German throne dispute he backed Louis IV of Bavaria against Frederick the Fair, and his see was ravaged and later placed under interdict for supporting the excommunicated emperor.

He redeemed Donaustauf from pledge, and his diocese's first parish register was compiled around 1326 during his episcopate. He died at Oberalteich Abbey on 11 October 1340.

伊布斯的尼古劳斯（约1275—1340）是多瑙河畔伊布斯出身的教士，可能曾在博洛尼亚攻读法律，在阿尔布雷希特一世与亨利七世的王室中书省任职，1313年3月19日当选雷根斯堡采邑主教。

德意志王位之争中，他支持巴伐利亚的路德维希四世、与美男子腓特烈为敌，教区因此遭兵燹，后又因支持被绝罚的皇帝而被处禁行圣事令。

en:
Reinhard, Count of Solms-Lich (1491–1562), was a German commander and military engineer, born at Lich Castle. As a young man he fought in the 1534 siege of the Anabaptist regime at Münster.

He modernized the fortifications of Hanau and, between 1539 and 1542, built the bastions of the Bavarian fortress of Ingolstadt, where he moved his household out of an unsafe residence just before it collapsed. In Emperor Charles V's 1544 campaign against France he directed the bombardment and mining of Saint-Dizier. He became imperial field marshal in 1546 and later an imperial councillor, and died at Lich in 1562.
