Baltasar de Zúñiga y Velasco (1561–1622) was a Spanish nobleman and diplomat. After surviving the 1588 Armada, he served Philip III as ambassador in Brussels, Paris and Vienna.

Back in Madrid, he joined the Duke of Uceda in bringing down the Duke of Lerma in 1618 and took charge of foreign policy. In 1619 he persuaded the king to aid the Habsburg emperor in Bohemia, taking Spain into the Thirty Years War. In 1621 he secured the rise of his nephew Olivares as Philip IV's chief minister, and died the following year.

José Antonio de Gaztañeta e Iturribalzaga (c. 1656–1728) was a Basque naval officer and ship designer born at Mutriku. He sailed with his father from the age of twelve and joined the navy in 1684.

In the War of the Spanish Succession he founded the El Astillero shipyard and later directed shipbuilding in the Basque Country. Commanding the fleet, he was defeated and captured by the British at Cape Passaro in 1718, but soon returned to service.

Promoted lieutenant-general in 1720, he led the treasure fleet through the blockade of Porto Bello in 1727. He died in Madrid the following year.

Jorge Juan y Santacilia (1713–1773) was a Spanish naval officer, mathematician and astronomer, nicknamed the Spanish savant. He joined the French Geodesic Mission to the Equator in 1735, travelling Peru with Antonio de Ulloa; their measurements confirmed that the Earth flattens at the poles.

Back in Spain from 1746, he studied English shipbuilding in London and went on to reform Spanish naval construction and education. He later served as ambassador to Morocco and director of the Seminary of Nobles in Madrid, where he died in 1773.

Claudio Coello (1642–1693) was a Spanish Baroque painter born in Madrid to Portuguese parents. Trained under Francisco Rizi, he studied Titian, Rubens and van Dyck in the royal collection, worked in Rome, and painted frescoes in Madrid and Toledo with José Jiménez Donoso.

Named court painter to Charles II, he spent seven years on his masterpiece, the altarpiece of the Adoration of the Miraculous Host in the sacristy of San Lorenzo de El Escorial, with over fifty court portraits. Regarded as the last great Spanish painter of the century, he died in Madrid in 1693.

Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares (1587–1645), was born in Rome while his father served as Spain's ambassador there. From 1621 he was the chief minister and favourite of Philip IV, guiding Spain through the renewed Eighty Years' War and the Thirty Years' War.

He made the Netherlands his first priority, but his drive to centralize power and raise wartime taxes provoked the revolts of Catalonia and Portugal in 1640. He was dismissed in 1643 and died in retirement two years later.

Bartolomé Esteban Murillo (1618–1682) was a Spanish Baroque painter born in Seville, where he trained with his uncle Juan del Castillo. His first major commission was eleven canvases for Seville's San Francisco convent, painted between 1645 and 1648 and depicting stories of Franciscan saints.

In 1660 he co-founded Seville's Academy of Fine Arts. He became famous for luminous religious paintings, above all the Immaculate Conception, and warm scenes of street children.

He also painted genre works such as The Young Beggar. He died in 1682 after a fall from a scaffold while working at Cádiz.

他还绘有《小乞丐》等风俗画。他在加的斯作画时从脚手架坠落，于1682年去世。

Tomás de Mercado (c. 1525–1575) was a Spanish Dominican theologian and economist of the School of Salamanca. He joined the Dominicans in New Spain as a young man, then returned to study at Salamanca University, where he lectured in philosophy, moral theology and law.

He later worked at the Exchange House of Seville, a centre of Spain's international money flows. His Summa de tratos y contratos of 1571, a manual of deals and contracts, made him a founder of Iberian monetarism, and he died at sea returning to Mexico.

Leonardus Lessius (1554–1623) was a Jesuit theologian, jurist and economist of the School of Salamanca, born in Brabant. He entered the Jesuits in 1572, studied at the Roman College, and from 1585 taught theology at Leuven.

There he defended Luis de Molina's doctrine of grace despite censorship. Illness ended his teaching in 1600, and he then wrote De iustitia et iure, applying moral theology to banking and allowing interest when a lender bore risk or lost gain. Known as the oracle of the Low Countries, he died at Leuven in 1623.

Alejandro Malaspina (1754–1810), born at Mulazzo in Tuscany, was a Spanish naval officer and explorer. He joined the Spanish fleet in 1774 and circumnavigated the world on a royal commission in 1786–1788.

From 1789 to 1794 he led the Malaspina Expedition, surveying the American Pacific coast from Cape Horn to the Gulf of Alaska and crossing to the Philippines and Australia. His criticism of colonial rule and a plot against Manuel Godoy led to his arrest in 1795 and imprisonment; freed and exiled to Italy in 1802, he died in 1810.

Bernardo de Gálvez (1746–1786) was a Spanish general and colonial administrator born in Málaga province. As governor of Spanish Louisiana he backed the American revolutionaries, and after Spain entered the war in 1779 he led the campaigns of 1779–1781 that drove the British from West Florida, crowned by his victory at Pensacola.

Charles III added the motto Yo Solo, 'I alone', to his coat of arms. He later governed Cuba and succeeded his father as viceroy of New Spain, where he faced famine after poor harvests and died of typhus in 1786.

Cosme Damián de Churruca y Elorza (1761–1805) was a Basque Spanish Navy officer and hydrographer born at Mutriku in Gipuzkoa. He entered the naval academy at Cádiz in 1776, surveyed the Strait of Magellan in 1788–1789 and charted the Antilles on a royal cartographic expedition of 1792–1795.

Fausto Elhuyar (1755–1833) was a Spanish chemist born at Logroño. After studying in Paris with his brother Juan José, he taught mineralogy at Vergara in the Royal Basque Society, and in 1783 the two brothers first isolated tungsten there. In 1786 he was appointed director of mines in New Spain.

Juan José Elhuyar (1754–1796) was a Spanish chemist and mineralogist born at Logroño. From 1773 to 1777 he studied medicine and the natural sciences in Paris with his brother Fausto, and in 1781 he was sent to Sweden to work with leading chemists there.

Back in Spain, the brothers first isolated tungsten at the Royal Basque Society's laboratory in Vergara in 1783. Posted to New Granada in 1784, he improved the silver mines of Mariquita and died at Bogotá in 1796.

Francisco Javier de Balmis (1753–1819) was a Spanish physician born at Alicante. He trained as a military surgeon and served in New Spain, where he studied Mexican plants. As physician to Charles IV he persuaded the crown to back a vaccination mission.

In 1803 the Royal Philanthropic Expedition sailed carrying the smallpox vaccine to Spanish America, using orphan boys as live carriers. Balmis carried it through Venezuela, Cuba and New Spain and on to the Philippines and China, in history's first international vaccination campaign. He died in Madrid.

Pedro Rodríguez de Campomanes (1723–1802) was a Spanish statesman and economist born at Tineo in Asturias. After studying law, he won notice in Madrid with a 1747 work on the Knights Templar and became Minister of the Treasury in 1760. A chief reformist adviser to Charles III, he drove the expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767.

His essays of 1774–1775 urged the revival of Spanish crafts and denounced guild privileges. He presided over the Council of Castile from 1788 until Charles IV dismissed him in 1793, and died in 1802.

en:
Giulio Alberoni (1664–1752) was an Italian-born cardinal and chief minister of Philip V of Spain. A gardener's son from near Piacenza, he reached Spain in 1711 during the War of the Spanish Succession, arranged Philip's marriage to Elisabetta Farnese in 1714 and headed the government by 1715, becoming a cardinal in 1717. He abolished internal customs, promoted colonial trade and reorganized state finances.

His occupation of Sardinia in 1717 and invasion of Sicily in 1718 drew the Quadruple Alliance into war; after the British destroyed his fleet off Cape Passaro, he was dismissed in 1719 and returned to Italy.

Gaspar Melchor de Jovellanos (1744–1811) was an Asturian statesman and writer, a leading figure of the Spanish Enlightenment. Born at Gijón, he served as a judge in Seville and then in Madrid, and from 1790 to 1797 lived in virtual exile back at Gijón.

His Report on the Agrarian Law of 1795 attacked entailed and church estates and urged agricultural reform as the key to Spain's prosperity. He served as minister of justice and was imprisoned in Bellver Castle in Mallorca in 1801; freed after the French invasion of 1808, he refused to serve Joseph Bonaparte, joining the Supreme Central Junta before his death in 1811.

Alonso de Santa Cruz (1505–1567) was a Seville-born cartographer, cosmographer and historian. He served at the Casa de Contratación and the Council of the Indies, where he maintained the Padrón Real, the crown's secret master chart. In 1530 he produced the first map of magnetic variation from true north and designed new nautical instruments.

He believed magnetic variation could help determine longitude. At Philip II's request he compiled in 1542 the Islario general, a survey of the world's islands, and he also taught cosmography at the court of Charles V.

Álvaro de Bazán, first Marquis of Santa Cruz (1526–1588), was Spain's foremost sixteenth-century admiral. Born at Granada, he fought the Ottomans in the Mediterranean, helped relieve Malta in 1565 and at Lepanto in 1571 led the Christian reserve and restored the line when it was broken.

He crushed the French-backed fleet at Ponta Delgada in 1582, securing the Azores for Philip II, and in 1583 first proposed the invasion of England by sea. Appointed to command the Spanish Armada, he died at Lisbon in 1588 before it sailed, unbeaten in battle.

Andrés de Urdaneta (1508–1568) was a Basque explorer who became an Augustinian friar. Aged seventeen he joined the Loaísa expedition to the Spice Islands and spent over eight years in Asia before settling in New Spain and taking the Augustinian habit in 1552.

At Philip II's request he sailed with Legazpi to the Philippines in 1564, and in 1565 mapped the eastward return route across the Pacific to Acapulco. The tornaviaje became the path of the Manila galleons for more than two centuries. He reported on the voyage in Spain, and died in Mexico City in 1568.

José Moñino, Count of Floridablanca (1728–1808), was the reforming chief minister of Charles III of Spain. He became a criminal prosecutor in Castile in 1766 and investigated the Esquilache Riots. He backed the expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767 and, as envoy to Pope Clement XIV, secured the suppression of the Jesuits and his countship in 1773.

Chief minister from 1777, he freed colonial trade and founded the Bank of San Carlos in 1782, the year Spain recovered Menorca and Florida from Britain. Ousted in 1792, he was imprisoned until 1795. He died in 1808 heading the Supreme Central Junta against Napoleon.

Pedro Calderón de la Barca (1600–1681) was the last great dramatist of Spain's Golden Age. Born in Madrid, his first play was staged at the Royal Alcázar in 1623 during the Prince of Wales's visit. He served in the royal army in Italy and Flanders from 1625 to 1635.

After Lope de Vega died in 1635 he became Spain's foremost playwright, favoured by Philip IV; his masterpiece La vida es sueño explores free will against destiny. Ordained in 1651, he wrote autos sacramentales and palace plays, dying in 1681.

Félix Lope de Vega (1562–1635), born in Madrid, was the most prolific playwright of Spain's Golden Age. In 1583 he fought at Ponta Delgada in the Azores. Exiled from Castile for libel, he married Isabel de Urbina in May 1588 and sailed with the Armada, surviving its failure.

In Valencia and later Madrid he forged the comedia nueva that made theatre mass entertainment and defined Spanish Baroque drama. His output includes hundreds of plays, some three thousand sonnets and several novels. Ordained a priest in 1614, he served the Duke of Sessa until his death in Madrid.

Luis de Góngora y Argote (1561–1627) was a Spanish Baroque poet born in Córdoba, where he served as a canon of the cathedral. He took deacon's orders in 1586. Ordained priest around 1605, he became honorary chaplain to Philip III in 1617 through the Duke of Lerma.

His elaborate, Latinate style was known as culteranismo or Gongorismo. The style reached its peak in the Fable of Polyphemus and Galatea (1612) and the Soledades.

He feuded for decades with Francisco de Quevedo, champion of the rival conceptismo. Illness forced him back to Córdoba in 1626, and he died there in 1627.

路易斯·德·贡戈拉-阿尔戈特（1561—1627）是西班牙巴洛克诗人，生于科尔多瓦，曾任当地大教堂法政牧师。他于1586年受执事圣职，约1605年晋铎，1617年经莱尔马公爵安排成为腓力三世的荣誉圣堂牧师。

他繁复典雅、多用拉丁化句法的文风被称为“夸饰主义”，又称贡戈拉主义，代表作是《波吕斐摩斯与加拉特亚的寓言》（1612）和《孤独》。

他与对立风格“概念主义”的代表弗朗西斯科·德·克维多终生论战。1626年他因病返回科尔多瓦，次年在当地去世。

Juan de Mariana (1536–1624) was a Spanish Jesuit theologian and historian of the School of Salamanca. He studied at Alcalá de Henares and joined the Society of Jesus at seventeen. From 1561 he taught theology in Rome, and from 1569 lectured on Thomas Aquinas in Paris.

In poor health, he retired to Toledo in 1574 and spent the next fifty years in literary work. His treatise De rege et regis institutione (1599) argued that a people may depose, and even kill, a tyrant, numbering him among the Catholic Monarchomachs.

Qiu Ying (c. 1494–1552) was a Ming gongbi painter and one of the Four Masters of Ming. Born to a peasant family in Taicang, he moved to Suzhou and worked as a lacquer painter until Zhou Chen trained him.

Employed by Jiangnan collectors such as Xiang Yuanbian, he studied their Song and Yuan paintings and broadened his art. He copied old masters so faithfully that his versions could pass for originals, while forging his own style of fine-line figures and blue-and-green landscapes.

He remained a professional outsider to Suzhou's amateur Wu school. Yet he was ranked alongside Shen Zhou, Wen Zhengming and Tang Yin.

仇英（约1494—1552）是明代工笔画家，明四家之一。他出身农家，原籍太仓，后移居苏州，早年做过漆工，后得画家周臣传授画艺。

他长期受聘于项元汴等江南富藏家，得以接触他们收藏的宋元画作，拓展画艺。他临摹古画几可乱真，同时形成了自己精细人物与青绿山水的画风。

他始终是以卖画为生的职业画家，游离于苏州文人吴门画派之外，却仍与沈周、文徵明、唐寅并称。

Yun Shouping (1633–1690) was an early-Qing painter, calligrapher and poet born at Wujin, Changzhou, son of a Ming loyalist. In the Ming-Qing war he served with his father in the anti-Qing resistance, was separated and adopted into a Qing official's household, and met his father again at Hangzhou's Lingyin Temple.

His family could not afford the civil service examinations, and he devoted himself to art. He first painted landscape but, outshone by Wang Hui, turned to bird-and-flower painting, reviving the boneless mogu manner and founding the Changzhou school. He ranks among the Six Masters of the early Qing, and died poor in 1690.

恽寿平（1633—1690）是清初画家、书法家、诗人，常州府武进县人，明遗民之子。明清易代之际，他随父参加抗清，兵败失散，被清朝官员家中收养，后在杭州灵隐寺与父亲重逢。

家中无力供他参加科举，他便投身艺术。他早年画山水，因自以为不及好友王翚而改画花鸟，重振“没骨”画法，成为常州画派的创始人。他位列“清初六家”，晚年贫困，1690年去世。

Wu Li (c. 1632–1718) was a Chinese landscape painter, poet and Jesuit priest. Born at Changshu in Jiangsu, he studied painting under Wang Shimin and Wang Jian from 1646 and is counted among the Six Masters of the early Qing.

Wang Shimin (1592–1680) was a landscape painter of the late Ming and early Qing, born at Taicang, grandson of grand secretary Wang Xijue. As a youth he studied under Dong Qichang and copied the Song and Yuan masters in his family's collection.

He served by hereditary privilege as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He retired through illness in 1632 and refused Qing office after 1644.

He headed the Four Wangs and founded the influential Loudong landscape school. He taught Wang Hui and Wu Li and was the grandfather and teacher of Wang Yuanqi.

en:
Wang Yuanqi (1642–1715) was a Qing-dynasty court painter and official, born at Taicang and taught by his grandfather Wang Shimin. After the jinshi degree in 1670 he rose to vice minister of revenue and became curator of the Kangxi Emperor's collection.

In 1704 he joined the South Study, painting for the emperor. In 1705 he compiled the Peiwenzhai Catalogue of Painting and Calligraphy.

His dense abstract landscapes, modelled on Yuan master Huang Gongwang, made him the Orthodox school's later leader and one of the Four Wangs. He died in office in 1715.

王原祁（1642—1715），江苏太仓州人，清代宫廷画家与官员，祖父王时敏亲自教他作画。1670年中进士后，他官至户部左侍郎，后掌管康熙帝的御藏。

Wang Hui (1632–1717) was an early-Qing landscape painter born at Changshu into a family of painters. After studying with Zhang Ke, he was discovered by Wang Jian, who took him as a pupil, and later studied under Wang Shimin.

Blending the northern and southern manners, he was hailed as a sage of painting. In 1691 he was summoned to Beijing to direct the Kangxi Emperor's Southern Tour scrolls. He founded the Yushan school, was one of the Four Wangs, and died in 1717.

Fan Meng (died 1339) was a native of Bianliang, now Kaifeng in Henan, and a low-ranking clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs in Henan during the Yuan dynasty. In the eleventh month of 1339 he conspired with Huo Bashi and others to forge an edict bearing the imperial seal.

Claiming appointment as a secretary of the Henan provincial administration, he arrested the province's chief officials and put them to death, briefly controlling the Henan administration. Fan was soon seized, sent to Dadu, and executed by dismemberment for treason.

Tang Xianzu (1550–1616) was a Ming playwright born in Linchuan, Jiangxi. After passing the provincial exam, he twice failed the metropolitan test for refusing to help grand secretary Zhang Juzheng's sons, and became a jinshi only in 1583.

His memorials attacked corruption; a 1591 attack on court officials had him demoted to Guangdong. He later governed Suichang County but, frustrated by official constraints, retired to Linchuan in 1598.

His plays, known as the Four Dreams, include The Peony Pavilion, in which the love of Du Liniang and Liu Mengmei conquers death. He founded the Linchuan school.

汤显祖（1550—1616），江西临川人，明代戏曲家。他中举后，因不肯替首辅张居正的儿子们科举攀附，两次会试落第，直到1583年才中进士。

他上疏揭露弊政，1591年因抨击朝臣被贬广东。此后他出任遂昌知县，却因施政受掣肘，于1598年辞官回到临川。

他的传奇合称“临川四梦”，尤以《牡丹亭》最为著名，剧中杜丽娘与柳梦梅的爱情足以跨越生死；他还开创了戏曲史上的临川派。

George Macartney, 1st Earl Macartney (1737–1806), was a British diplomat born in Ireland to a Scottish family. After Trinity College Dublin, he negotiated an alliance with Catherine II as envoy to Russia in 1764 and became Chief Secretary for Ireland in 1768.

He later governed Grenada and Madras, concluding the Treaty of Mangalore in 1784. Created an earl in 1792, he led Britain's first embassy to Qing China, reaching the Qianlong Emperor's court in 1793, but returned in 1794 without trade concessions. He later governed the Cape Colony, dying in 1806.

第一代马戛尔尼伯爵乔治·马戛尔尼（1737—1806）是英国外交官，出生于爱尔兰，家族先世出自苏格兰。都柏林三一学院毕业后，1764年他出使俄国，与叶卡捷琳娜二世谈结盟约，1768年出任爱尔兰首席大臣。

Yang Shen (1488–1559) was a Ming-dynasty poet and scholar from Xindu in Sichuan and son of grand secretary Yang Tinghe. In 1511 he took first place in the palace examination, becoming zhuangyuan, and joined the Hanlin Academy.

In the Great Rites Controversy of 1524 he led officials weeping and protesting at the palace gate over the emperor's choice of imperial father. He was twice flogged and exiled to the Yongchang garrison in Yunnan.

There he spent more than thirty years. He produced many works on Yunnan's nature and history, including the lyric The Immortals by the River.

杨慎（1488—1559），四川新都人，明代诗人、学者，是内阁首辅杨廷和之子。1511年，他殿试第一，高中状元，入翰林院任修撰。

1524年大礼议中，他率众官在宫门伏阙哭谏，要求皇帝更改皇考，两遭廷杖，被贬往云南永昌卫戍边。

他在云南度过三十余年，写下大量以当地山川风物与历史文化为题的作品，其中包括词《临江仙》。

Qin Liangyu (1574–1648) was a female general of the late Ming. Born in Zhongzhou, Sichuan, in 1595 she married Ma Qiancheng, chieftain of Shizhu, and led 500 men against the 1599 Bozhou rebellion.

Her husband's death in prison in 1613 made her pacification commissioner; with her famed White Staff troops she fought the Later Jin and Zhang Xianzhong. Defeated by Zhang, she withdrew but kept her soldiers from surrendering.

The Longwu Emperor of Southern Ming made her a marquis. She died at Shizhu in 1648, the only woman listed among Ming generals in official history.

秦良玉（1574—1648）是明末女将，出生于四川忠州。1595年她嫁与石砫土司马千乘，1599年率五百人参与征讨播州叛乱。

1613年丈夫瘐死狱中后，她继任石砫宣抚使，率麾下著名的“白杆兵”抗击后金和张献忠的军队。她被张献忠击败后退守，但阻止了士兵投降。

南明隆武帝封她为侯爵。1648年她在石砫去世，是正史将领列传中唯一的女性。

Wang Zhenyi (1768–1797) was a Qing-dynasty astronomer, mathematician and poet from Jiangning. Her grandfather taught her astronomy, while her father taught her mathematics and medicine.

After her grandfather died in 1782, she spent years in Jilin reading his library and learning riding and archery. Largely self-taught in astronomy and mathematics, she taught male students after her marriage at twenty-five.

Her poetry argued that women were men's equals. Most of her writings were burned at her death; the survivors were compiled by Qian Yiji, who called her the greatest female scholar since Ban Zhao. She died aged twenty-nine.

王贞仪（1768—1797）是清朝江宁的天文学家、数学家与诗人。祖父教她天文，父亲则教她数学和医学。

1782年祖父去世后，她在吉林数年，遍读祖父的藏书，并学习骑射。她的天文、数学多靠自学，25岁出嫁后甚至教授男学生。

她在诗中主张女子可与男子比肩。她临终前焚毁大部分著作，残存文稿由钱仪吉辑录，钱仪吉称她为班昭之后第一女学者。她于1797年去世，年仅29岁。

Song Lian (1310–1381) was a historian and official of the early Ming dynasty, born in Pujiang, Zhejiang. A leading Neo-Confucian of the Jinhua school, he refused Yuan office before joining Zhu Yuanzhang, the future Hongwu Emperor, and tutoring the crown prince.

In 1369 he headed the Bureau of History and directed the compilation of the History of Yuan, completed in 1370. The commissioned official history became a major source for many peoples' histories.

He rose to chief minister of the Hanlin Academy, but after retiring in 1377 was implicated in the Hu Weiyong case through his grandson and died in exile at Kui Prefecture in 1381.

宋濂（1310—1381），字景濂，号潜溪，浙江金华浦江人，明初的政治家、文学家与史学家。他是元代金华学派的重要理学家，元末辞谢翰林院编修之召，后投奔朱元璋，为太子讲授经学。

1369年他出任总裁官，主持修纂《元史》，于1370年成书。这部奉敕编修的前朝正史，成为研究诸多民族历史的重要资料。

他后官至翰林学士承旨。1377年辞官归乡，却因长孙宋慎卷入胡惟庸案而受牵连，1381年死于流放途中的夔州。

en:
Liu Jin (1451–1510), a native of Xingping in Shaanxi, was the most powerful eunuch of the Zhengde Emperor's Ming court. Originally surnamed Tan, he castrated himself, entering palace service as a boy and becoming the crown prince's favourite attendant. At the emperor's accession in 1505, Liu led the eunuch Eight Tigers, headed the Directorate of Ceremonial, purged opposing officials and from 1508 ran a secret-police bureau.

His revenue reforms strengthened eunuchs over scholar-officials and provoked unrest. In 1510, after the Prince of Anhua rebelled against him, fellow Tiger Zhang Yong denounced him for treason, and he was seized and executed by slicing.

刘瑾（1451—1510），陕西兴平人，明武宗正德朝权势最盛的宦官。他本姓谈，少年时自宫入宫，成为太子最宠信的近侍。1505年新帝即位后，他统领宦官“八虎”，掌管司礼监，斥逐反对他的朝臣，1508年起自设内行厂特务机构。

他的财政改革扩大宦官权势、削弱士大夫，引发各地动荡。1510年安化王以讨伐他为名起兵，八虎之一的张永告发他谋反，刘瑾随即被捕，定罪后凌迟处死。

他的财政改革扩大宦官权势、削弱士大夫，引发各地动荡。1510年安化王以讨伐他为名起兵，八虎之一的张永告发他谋反，刘瑾随即被捕，定罪后凌迟处死。

en:
Michał Boym (c. 1612–1659) was a Polish Jesuit born in Lwów. He reached Macau about 1645 and opened a mission on Hainan, until the Manchu conquest drove him to Tonkin in 1647.

In 1650 the Southern Ming Yongli court sent him to seek papal aid. Under arrest in Goa, he escaped and reached Venice in 1652; Pope Alexander VII received him in 1655 but gave no aid.

His Flora Sinensis (1656), the first European survey of Chinese flora and fauna, brought Chinese natural history to Europe. He died on the Tonkin-Guangxi border in 1659.

卜弥格（约1612—1659）是生于利沃夫的波兰籍耶稣会士。约1645年他抵达澳门，在海南岛建立传教点，1647年满清攻取海南后避居东京（今越南北部）。

1650年，南明永历朝廷派他出使罗马求援。他在果阿遭软禁后逃脱，1652年抵达威尼斯；教宗亚历山大七世1655年接见他，却未给予实际援助。

他的《中国植物志》（1656年）是欧洲第一部系统介绍中国动植物的著作，把中国的博物学传入欧洲。1659年，他在交趾与广西边境去世。

en:
Cao Xueqin (c. 1715–1763/64) was a Qing novelist, born at Shangyuan near Nanjing into a bondservant family of the Plain White Banner, grandson of Jiangning textile commissioner Cao Yin.

In 1727 the Yongzheng Emperor seized the family's estates and jailed Cao Fu, forcing them to Beijing. Cao spent his later years poor in the western suburbs, selling paintings while labouring for a decade on Dream of the Red Chamber, a novel of a great family's rise and fall.

He died in 1763 or 1764. He left some eighty chapters, the core of one of China's Four Great Classical Novels.

曹雪芹（约1715—1763/1764），清代小说家，生于南京附近的上元，出身正白旗包衣世家，祖父曹寅曾任江宁织造。

1727年，雍正帝查抄曹家、将曹頫下狱，全家被迫迁往北京。曹雪芹晚年穷居北京西郊，卖画度日，以十年心血创作《红楼梦》，写一个大族的由盛转衰。

他于1763或1764年去世，留下约八十回书稿，成为中国四大古典名著之一的雏形。

en:
Huang Gongwang (1269–1354), born Lu Jian at Changshu, was the oldest of the Four Masters of Yuan literati painting. Only ten when the Song fell to the Mongols, he found his path to office severely restricted.

He served as a low-ranking Censorate clerk until jailed over a minister's case, and after his release became a Quanzhen Taoist hermit in the Fuchun Mountains near Hangzhou.

There, from 1347 to 1350, he painted his great handscroll Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains. Rejecting the landscape conventions of the academy of his day, he built up scenes with dry brushstrokes and light ink washes, creating influential models for later painters.

黄公望（1269—1354），本姓陆名坚，常熟人，是元代画坛“元四家”中年辈最长者。宋亡时他年仅十岁，后来仕途受限。

他在御史台任低级掾吏时因一桩大臣案入狱，获释后出家为全真道士，隐居杭州附近的富春山。

1347至1350年，他在此绘成长卷《富春山居图》。他反对当时院体山水的惯例，以干笔和淡墨层层构筑景致，为后世画家提供了影响深远的范本。

en:
Wu Zhen (1280–1354), art name the Taoist of the Plum Blossom, was a Yuan-dynasty painter born at Weitang near Jiaxing in Zhejiang, one of the Four Masters of the Yuan. Educated in philosophy and swordsmanship, he chose the quiet life of an artist.

His paintings initially sold poorly. He supported himself by fortune-telling while painter friends taught him their craft. He took the tenth-century monk Juran as his model and became a master of moist-ink landscape in long hemp-fibre strokes, as well as ink bamboo and pines; his bold, saturated ink style influenced later painters.

吴镇（1280—1354），号梅花道人，浙江嘉兴魏塘桥（今嘉善）人，元代画家，“元四家”之一。他虽治学兼习剑术，却选择清静的画家生活。

早年他的画作销路不佳，靠替人算命为生，并在画友指点下学画。他师法五代画僧巨然，以长披麻皴作水墨山水，兼擅墨竹与松石；其笔力雄劲、墨气沉厚的画风，深刻影响了后世画家。

en:
Ni Zan (1301–1374), art name Yunlin, was a Yuan painter and one of the Four Yuan Masters. He was born to a wealthy family in Wuxi.

In the 1340s famine and heavy taxation ruined it, and as rebellions spread he gave away his estates and lived twenty years on a houseboat, studying under Huang Gongwang.

After 1345 he developed his sparse ink landscapes of bare trees, empty water and distant banks with no human figures, painting ink bamboo to express spirit, not likeness. He returned to Wuxi in 1371, painting the Rongxi Studio the next year.

倪瓒（1301—1374），号云林，无锡人，元代画家，“元四家”之一，出身富庶之家。

1340年代饥荒与重税毁了当地，乱局蔓延时，他散尽田产，此后二十年间乘舟漂泊，并曾向黄公望学画。

1345年以后，他形成疏淡的水墨山水：枯树、空水、远岸，画面从不画人物；他画墨竹只为抒写逸气，不求形似。1371年他回到无锡，次年绘成《容膝斋图》。

en:
Wang Meng (c. 1308–1385) was a landscape painter of the late Yuan and early Ming and the youngest of the Four Masters of Yuan painting. Born in Wuxing in Zhejiang, he was a maternal grandson of the painter-calligrapher Zhao Mengfu.

After briefly holding office late in the Yuan, he withdrew for thirty years to Yellow Crane Mountain in Yuhang, styling himself its woodcutter; Ni Zan had urged him to value the pursuit of learning over rank and wealth.

Amid the end-of-Yuan wars he joined Zhang Shicheng and, after Zhang's defeat, went over to Zhu Yuanzhang. Under the Ming he became prefect of Tai'an in Shandong, but in 1385 he was implicated in Chancellor Hu Weiyong's treason case after viewing paintings at Hu's house, and died in prison.

王蒙（约1308—1385），号黄鹤山樵，浙江吴兴人，是元末明初的山水画家，也是元四家四人中最年轻的一位。他是书画家赵孟頫的外孙。

元末他曾短暂出仕，后弃官隐居余杭黄鹤山约三十年；画家倪瓒曾劝他重乐道而轻仕禄财富。

元末战乱中，他先投奔张士诚，张败后归附朱元璋。明朝建立后出任山东泰安知州，1385年因曾在丞相胡惟庸府中观画，受谋反案牵连，死于狱中。

en:
Shen Zhou (1427–1509), courtesy name Qinan, was a Ming painter. He was born into a scholarly landowning family at Xiangcheng near Suzhou.

After his father's death, he chose not to sit for the civil service examinations, devoting himself instead to his widowed mother and a reclusive life of poetry, calligraphy and painting; commoners who came to his door requesting works were never turned away. His wealth let him paint without relying on a patron.

He modeled his landscapes on the Four Masters of Yuan and founded the Suzhou-based Wu school of literati painting, which set personal expression against the academic Zhe school. He is ranked first among the Four Masters of Ming.

沈周（1427—1509），字启南，长洲相城（今江苏苏州）人，明代画家，出身书香富户。

父亲去世后，他选择不应科举，在家奉养寡母，过着吟诗作画的隐居生活；凡登门求画者，哪怕是贩夫牧童，他也从不拒绝。富足的家境使他作画不必依赖赞助人。

他的山水画取法元四家，在苏州创立了文人画的吴门画派，以抒写心性对抗浙派的院体画风，名列明四家之首。

en:
Wen Zhengming (1470–1559), born Wen Bi, took the art name Hengshan. He was a Suzhou painter, calligrapher and poet and one of the Four Masters of Ming painting. In 1489 he became a pupil of Shen Zhou, founder of the Wu school.

He failed the provincial examinations nine times before winning a Hanlin Academy post in 1523; he resigned in 1526 and spent the next thirty years leading the Wu school in Suzhou.

The Humble Administrator's Garden inspired his poems and paintings. Famed for his regular and running script, he died in 1559 while writing an epitaph.

文徵明（1470—1559），原名文璧，号衡山居士，苏州长洲（今江苏苏州）人，明代画家、书法家、诗人，明四家之一。1489年他拜吴门画派创始人沈周为师。

他九次参加乡试都未中举，直到1523年才入翰林院任待诏，1526年辞官归乡，此后三十年主持吴门画派。

拙政园曾激发他创作诗画。他的楷书与行书名扬天下，1559年在为人书写墓志时掷笔端坐而逝。

Tang Yin (1470–1524), courtesy name Bohu, was a Suzhou painter and poet, one of the Four Masters of Ming. Born into a tavern-keeper's family in Wuxian, he entered Suzhou's scholarly circles and befriended Wen Zhengming.

He took first place in the 1498 Nanjing provincial examinations, but a 1499 examination-leak scandal ended his official career. He refused a clerical post in Zhejiang and returned to Suzhou. There he built his Peach Blossom Hermitage and earned a living painting landscapes and figures.

In 1514 he briefly served the Prince of Ning at Nanchang. He feigned madness to escape after discovering the prince's treason.

1498年他在南京乡试高中第一名解元，1499年却因会试泄题案下狱，仕途尽毁；他拒绝浙江小吏之职，回到苏州筑桃花庵，以卖山水人物画为生。

1514年他曾短暂入南昌宁王幕府，察觉宁王谋反后，靠装疯才脱身归乡。

en:
Lê Lợi (1385–1433) was the Vietnamese leader who drove out the Ming occupation and founded the Later Lê dynasty. Born into a landed family at Lam Sơn in Thanh Hóa, he was imprisoned under the Ming after their 1407 conquest.

Held from 1413 to 1415, he raised revolt in 1418 as Prince of Pacification. He wore down Ming armies by guerrilla ambush.

In 1427 his forces destroyed Liu Sheng's army at Chi Lăng and took Xương Giang, forcing the Ming to withdraw. Enthroned in 1428 and recognized by the Ming in 1431, he died in 1433 as Lê Thái Tổ.

黎利（1385—1433）是驱逐明朝在越统治、建立后黎朝的越南民族领袖。他出身清化蓝山的豪强之家，1407年明朝征服安南后曾被明军囚禁。

他于1413至1415年被囚，1418年起兵自称平定王，以游击伏击消耗明军。

Giovanni de' Marignolli (fl. 1338–1353) was a Florentine Franciscan and papal legate to the Mongol Yuan court of China. In 1338 Pope Benedict XII sent him after Yuan envoys reached Avignon asking for a successor to Archbishop John of Montecorvino.

He reached Khanbaliq in 1342 and was received by Toghon Temür; his mission built a church and baptized converts at Almaliq. After three or four years he sailed home from Quanzhou by way of India and Persia, reaching Avignon in 1353 with the khan's letter. He later became bishop of Bisignano and chronicler to Emperor Charles IV in Prague.

Ivan Nelipić (died 1344) was a Croatian nobleman and Duke of Knin from the Nelipić family. A voivode of Mladen II Šubić, he turned against his lord and helped overthrow him at the Battle of Bliska in 1322.

Expelling the garrison from Knin, he made the city his seat. Between 1322 and 1344 he was the most powerful magnate in Croatia. He repelled King Charles I Robert's expeditions and defied Hungarian attempts to subdue him until his death in 1344; royal authority was re-established in Croatia the following year.

Francisco de Pina (1585–1625) was a Portuguese Jesuit missionary and interpreter, born at Guarda, who pioneered the romanization of Vietnamese. He entered the Jesuits in 1605 and studied at St Paul's College in Macau from 1611 to 1617.

In 1617 he arrived in Đàng Trong to work the missions at Hội An and Qui Nhơn. Drawing on João Rodrigues's Portuguese phonetic methods, used to transcribe Japanese, he devised the first Latin transcription of Vietnamese, the basis of the chữ Quốc ngữ alphabet. He drowned in December 1625 at Cửa Đại, rescuing guests from a wrecked boat.

en:
Christiern Pedersen (c. 1480–1554) was a Danish humanist, printer and translator, often called the father of Danish literature. Educated at Greifswald and Paris, he published a Latin-Danish dictionary in 1510 and the first printed edition of Saxo Grammaticus's Gesta Danorum in 1514.

Loyal to Christian II, he followed the exiled king to the Netherlands in 1526. He turned Lutheran in 1529 and issued his Danish translation of the New Testament.

After running a press in Malmø he completed the first full Danish Bible in 1543, printed in 1550. He died in 1554.

克里斯蒂安·佩德森（约1480—1554）是丹麦人文主义者、印刷商与翻译家，常被称为“丹麦文学之父”。他曾在格赖夫斯瓦尔德和巴黎求学，1510年出版拉丁语—丹麦语词典，1514年首次印行萨克索·格拉玛提库斯的《丹麦人的事迹》。

他曾在马尔默开办印刷所，后完成第一部丹麦语全本《圣经》，译稿1543年完成、1550年印行。他于1554年去世。

Hans Mikkelsen (died 1532) was a wealthy merchant who became a councillor in Malmö in 1503 and its burgomaster from 1508, and a trusted adviser of Christian II.

In 1520 he went to Stockholm to negotiate an alliance against the Hanseatic League. When Christian was driven from Denmark in 1523 he followed him, embracing Luther's teaching at Wittenberg.

He supervised the first Danish translation of the New Testament, printed in 1524, and himself translated the epistles of Paul. He followed the king to Norway in 1531 and died in 1532.

en:
Lorenz van Steenwinckel (1585–1619) was a Flemish-Danish architect and sculptor, son of Hans van Steenwinckel the Elder and brother of Hans the Younger. From 1613 he oversaw a series of building projects for Christian IV, including the king's chapel in Roskilde Cathedral and the Copenhagen Stock Exchange.

His contracts specified that he work from drawings supplied by the king, and art historians differ over whether he was a designer or chiefly a stonecutter.

He died suddenly in 1619 at only 34. His unfinished works, including the Børsen, were completed by his brother Hans.

Sir Andrew Sinclair of Ravenscraig (1555–1625), known in Denmark as Anders Sincklar, was a Scottish nobleman, a son of Henry, 6th Lord Sinclair. In 1589 he sailed with James VI to Norway for Anne of Denmark, staying on as hofjunker to Christian IV from 1591.

He married Kirsten Kaas in 1600. He held Scanian fiefs including Landskrona and began building Sinclairsholm. In the Kalmar War he fought at the capture of Öland and governed Kalmar. He ended as a Danish privy counsellor, colonel and envoy to England, dying in January 1625.

Falk Lykke (1583–1650) of Skovgaard and Bollerup was a Danish nobleman, lensmand and officer from Skåne. He served in the Kalmar War and in 1612 became lensmand of Christianopel.

In 1625 he became colonel of the Scanian Regiment and exchanged Christianopel for Gulland, governing Gotland until 1627, when he received Lund St. Peter's monastery. During the Torstenson War his regiment was long quartered at Helsingør, where he clashed severely with the townspeople. He helped compile the Gotland chronicle, was knighted in 1648 and died in July 1650.

en:
Lambert van Haven (1630–1695) was a Danish-Norwegian architect, master builder and painter, born in Bergen, the son of Salomon van Haven. Already a royal master builder in 1653, he spent fifteen years studying Baroque architecture in Italy, France and the Netherlands.

In 1671 Christian V named him Denmark-Norway's first General Building Master, overseeing all royal works; he redesigned the Nørreport gate and from 1682 built the Church of Our Saviour in Christianshavn, consecrated in 1696 after his death. As court painter he supervised the king's paintings and sculptures, and he introduced the European Baroque to Danish architecture.

1671年，克里斯蒂安五世任命他为丹麦-挪威首任总营造师，统管全部王室工程；他重新设计了北城门，并于1682年起在克里斯蒂安港修建救主堂，教堂在他去世后的1696年才落成祝圣。他还以宫廷画家身份监察国王的绘画和雕塑，并把欧洲巴洛克风格引入了丹麦建筑。

en:
Pieter Jansz. Liorne (1561–1620) was a merchant and ship-owner of Hoorn in Holland. He traded across the Baltic and with Italy and served his town as burgomaster and director of the Dutch East India Company's Hoorn chamber.

He is credited as the chief initiator of the lengthened fluyt, a cheap bulk cargo ship decisive for Dutch seaborne trade. In 1618 Stadholder Maurice dismissed him, probably for sympathising with the Remonstrants.

彼得·扬斯·利奥内（1561—1620）是荷兰霍伦的商人与船东。他经营波罗的海与意大利贸易，并担任家乡市长和荷兰东印度公司霍伦分会主管。

他被视为加长型福禄特帆船的主要推动者；这种造价低廉的散装货船成为荷兰海上贸易的关键。1618年，执政毛里茨亲王将他解职，原因可能是他同情抗辩派。

en:
Bahlul Khan Lodi (died 1489) was chief of the Afghan Lodi tribe. He began as a horse trader; fine horses sold to the Sayyid sultan Muhammad Shah earned him land, and he rose to govern Lahore, winning the title Khan-i-Khanan.

He twice failed to take Delhi, but when the last Sayyid sultan Alam Shah withdrew in 1448, his minister invited Bahlul to seize the throne. He ascended Delhi's throne in 1451 after the abdication and founded the Lodi dynasty. In 1479 he conquered the Jaunpur Sultanate. He died in 1489 and his son Sikandar Lodi succeeded him.

巴赫卢勒汗·洛迪（1489年卒）是阿富汗洛迪部落的酋长。他早年以贩马为业，把良马卖给赛义德王朝的穆罕默德沙后，凭一块封邑起家，最终领有拉合尔，赢得汗中之汗的称号。

他曾两度攻打德里未果；末代赛义德苏丹阿拉姆沙于1448年退隐后，其大臣邀请巴赫卢勒入主德里。阿拉姆沙退位后，巴赫卢勒于1451年登上德里王位，建立洛迪王朝。1479年，他攻灭江布尔苏丹国。1489年去世后，其子西坎达尔汗·洛迪继位。

Ismail Mukh, also known as Nasir-ud-din Ismail Shah, was an Afghan noble serving the Delhi Sultanate in the Deccan. In 1346 the Deccani amirs rebelled against Muhammad bin Tughluq and proclaimed him their leader.

The rebellion ended Delhi's control over the Deccan. After Zafar Khan defeated the sultan's armies, Ismail stepped aside in his favour in 1347, an act from which the Bahmani Sultanate was born.

Zafar Khan, enthroned as Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah, gave him lands and title Amir-ul-Umara. Ismail was later poisoned after a local chieftain turned him against the new sultan.

伊斯梅尔·穆赫（又名纳西尔丁·伊斯梅尔沙）是在德干为德里苏丹国效力的阿富汗贵族。1346年，德干埃米尔起兵反抗穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克，推举他为首领。

这场叛乱使德里失去了对德干的控制。扎法尔汗击败苏丹大军后，伊斯梅尔于1347年让位给他，巴赫马尼苏丹国由此诞生。

登基称阿拉丁·巴曼沙的扎法尔汗赐他封地与诸埃米尔之长的头衔。后来一名地方首领挑唆他与新苏丹反目，他随即被毒杀。

en:
Malik Maqbul, also titled Khan-i-Jahan, was a Telugu commander of the Kakatiya Empire named Gannama Nayaka, guarding Warangal Fort until Muhammad bin Tughluq conquered it in 1323. Captured and converted to Islam, he entered Delhi service. After Warangal fell to rebels, he governed Cambay.

He rose to become wazir under Firuz Shah Tughlaq, who called him brother and left all fiscal administration in his hands. While the sultan campaigned in Sindh, Maqbul held Delhi. He died in 1369, and his son Jauna Khan succeeded him.

马利克·马克布勒（称号汗·伊·贾汉）原是卡卡蒂亚王朝的泰卢固将领，名甘纳马·纳亚卡，镇守瓦朗加尔堡，直至1323年穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克将其攻占。他被俘后改宗伊斯兰教，转仕德里。瓦朗加尔被叛军夺取后，他出镇坎贝。

en:
Khizr Khan (c. 1361–1421) was governor of Multan under Firuz Shah Tughlaq and claimed descent from the Prophet Muhammad, a claim that gave his line the name Sayyid dynasty.

After Timur's invasion shattered Tughlaq power, he captured Delhi in 1414, imprisoned its ruler Daulat Khan Lodi, and reigned until 1421. Fearing Timur's heir Shah Rukh, he took no royal title and struck coins in former sultans' names, only winning leave in 1417 to add his own. He forced the ruler of Katehar to submit, and plundered and annexed Bayana and Gwalior. His son Mubarak Shah succeeded him.

en:
John Locke (1632–1704) was an English philosopher and physician, a founder of British empiricism, educated at Oxford. From 1666 he served Anthony Ashley Cooper, later Earl of Shaftesbury.

After Shaftesbury's fall he took refuge in the Netherlands in 1683. He returned only in 1689, after the Glorious Revolution.

His Letter Concerning Toleration appeared in 1689, followed by Two Treatises of Government and An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, arguing for natural rights, government by consent and the mind as a blank slate. He also defended the right to resist tyranny, and died in Essex in 1704.

约翰·洛克（1632—1704）是英格兰哲学家与医生，英国经验主义的奠基人之一，就读于牛津大学。1666年起他侍奉后来受封沙夫茨伯里伯爵的安东尼·阿什利·库珀。

沙夫茨伯里失势后，他于1683年流亡荷兰。直到光荣革命后的1689年他才返回英格兰。

同年他的《论宽容书》问世，随后出版《政府论》和《人类理解论》，主张自然权利与基于同意的政府，并提出心灵是一块白板。他还维护人民反抗暴政的权利，1704年在埃塞克斯去世。

en:
Edmund of Langley, 1st Duke of York (1341–1402), was the fifth son of Edward III. He campaigned in France, Portugal and Castile before Richard II made him Duke of York in 1385.

In 1370 he joined the Black Prince's campaign that sacked Limoges, and in 1381 he led an unsuccessful expedition to press his brother John of Gaunt's claim to Castile.

He served as Keeper of the Realm during Richard II's Irish expeditions. Left to guard England in 1399, he first resisted and then joined the returning Henry Bolingbroke, and was rewarded under the new Henry IV. Founder of the House of York, Edmund died in 1402.

兰利的埃德蒙，第一代约克公爵（1341—1402），是爱德华三世第五子。他曾在法兰西、葡萄牙和卡斯蒂利亚征战，1385年被理查二世封为约克公爵。

en:
John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster (1340–1399), was the fourth son of Edward III. He married Blanche of Lancaster and became one of England's richest landowners, fighting in France and Spain.

As his elder brother the Black Prince fell ill, John assumed much of the government. Through his second wife Constance he claimed the crown of Castile, and in 1386 he arranged the Anglo-Portuguese alliance.

He wielded great influence under Richard II and mediated between the king and rebellious nobles. After his death in 1399 the crown confiscated his estates; his son Henry Bolingbroke seized the throne as Henry IV, founding the House of Lancaster.

冈特的约翰，兰开斯特公爵（1340—1399），是爱德华三世第四子。他迎娶兰开斯特的布兰奇，成为英格兰最富有的大地主之一，在法兰西和西班牙征战。

兄长黑太子病重时，约翰承担了大量政务。他凭借第二任妻子康斯坦斯主张卡斯蒂利亚王位，1386年促成英葡同盟。

Henry Percy, 1st Earl of Northumberland (1341–1408), was one of the most powerful noblemen in northern England. He was appointed Warden of the Scottish Marches and created earl at Richard II's coronation in 1377.

With his son Harry 'Hotspur' Percy he backed Henry Bolingbroke's seizure of the throne in 1399 and became Constable of England. Father and son were tasked with subduing Owain Glyndŵr's Welsh rebellion.

The Percys rebelled in 1403 and Hotspur fell at Shrewsbury; in 1405 Henry fled to Scotland. Invading again in 1408, he was killed at Bramham Moor, his head displayed on London Bridge.

Abba Giyorgis of Segla (c. 1365–1425) was one of the most influential Ethiopian Orthodox theologians and Ge'ez writers of his age. He served as court chaplain to Emperor Dawit I and tutored royal princes.

His teaching on the Sabbath drew the hostility of Dawit I, who imprisoned him. He was released on the accession of Tewodros I and later flourished under Yeshaq I.

His best-known works are the Book of Hours (Sa'atat) and the theological treatise Book of the Mystery of Heaven and Earth, which shaped Ethiopian liturgy and calendars.

塞格拉的阿巴·吉约吉斯（约1365—1425）是当时最有影响的埃塞俄比亚正教神学家与吉兹语作家之一。他担任皇帝达维特一世的宫廷司铎，教导诸王子。

他关于安息日的主张触怒达维特一世而被监禁，直到特沃德罗斯一世即位才获释，其后在伊沙克一世朝继续著述。

他最著名的作品是《时辰书》（《萨阿塔特》）与神学著作《天地奥秘之书》，对埃塞俄比亚的礼仪和历书影响深远。

Masaccio (1401–1428), born Tommaso di Ser Giovanni di Simone near Arezzo, was the first great painter of the Florentine Quattrocento. Registered as a master in Florence's painters' guild in 1422, he worked with Masolino on the Brancacci Chapel frescoes, where his solid, lifelike figures and dramatic light set a new standard for realism.

His Trinity in Santa Maria Novella, painted around 1425–1427, applied Brunelleschi's linear perspective with rigorous precision. He died in Rome in the summer of 1428, aged twenty-six; later masters from Leonardo to Michelangelo studied his Brancacci figures.

Sir John Hawkwood (c. 1320–1394), born in Essex, became the most famous English condottiero in Italy. A longbowman in the Hundred Years' War, he joined the White Company after the Treaty of Brétigny in 1360 and entered Italy in 1361, becoming its captain two years later.

He served the pope, the Visconti of Milan and finally Florence, which made him a citizen. In 1377 he married an illegitimate daughter of Bernabò Visconti, and in 1387 won his finest victory at Castagnaro for Padua. He died in Florence in 1394 and was buried with honours in the Duomo.

Charles-Louis de Secondat, baron de Montesquieu (1689–1755), was a French political philosopher. Born near Bordeaux, he inherited in 1716 his family title and the office of président à mortier of the Bordeaux Parlement.

He won fame with the Persian Letters (1721), a satirical portrait of French society seen through Persian visitors, sold his judicial office in 1726, and entered the Académie Française in 1728. He then toured Europe, spending more than a year in England.

After years of travel and study he published The Spirit of the Laws (1748), which divided government into legislative, executive and judicial powers; the Church placed it on the Index in 1751.

夏尔·德·塞孔达，孟德斯鸠男爵（1689—1755），通称孟德斯鸠，是法国政治哲学家，生于波尔多附近。1716年他继承家族爵位和波尔多高等法院庭长之职。

1721年，他以借波斯访客的眼睛讽刺法国社会的《波斯人信札》一举成名；1726年卖掉司法官职，1728年入选法兰西学术院，同年开始游历欧洲，在英国逗留一年多。

经过多年游历与著述，他于1748年出版《论法的精神》，主张把政府权力划分为立法、行政、司法三权；1751年，教会将此书列入禁书目录。

Arrigo della Rocca (c. 1340–1401) was a Corsican noble of the Cinarchesi clan Banda dei Fuori. As a boy his father gave him to the Genoese as a hostage.

After fighting in Sambucuccio d'Alando's revolt he broke with Genoa and took refuge at the court of Aragon. He returned in 1373 with Aragonese backing, defeated the Genoese governor in 1375, and in 1376 was proclaimed count of Corsica under the Aragonese flag.

In 1393 the king of Aragon appointed him lieutenant in Corsica. He mastered the island for years, but died in June 1401, possibly poisoned by the Genoese.

en:
Sambucuccio d'Alando was a Corsican popular leader during the anti-feudal rising that broke out in 1357. An assembly of chiefs named him military commander, and the rebels razed the nobles' castles. Allied with Doge Simone Boccanegra, he helped bring Genoese rule to the island when a Corsican delegation made act of submission at Genoa in October 1358.

When the nobles counter-attacked, he secured Genoese aid and a governor, Tridano della Torre. After the popular camp split and Tridano was murdered in 1372, he again took arms and requested another governor, who arrived in 1373; after that year all trace of him disappears.

桑布库乔·达兰多是1357年科西嘉反封建起义中的平民领袖。起义首领集会推举他为军事指挥官，起义者夷平贵族城堡。他与热那亚总督西蒙·博卡内格拉结盟，1358年10月科西嘉代表团赴热那亚正式归顺，帮助热那亚确立对全岛的统治。

贵族反扑时，他求得热那亚援军和总督特里达诺·德拉·托雷。平民阵营分裂、特里达诺于1372年遇刺后，桑布库乔再次武装对抗贵族，并请求另派总督，新总督1373年到任；此后史料中再无他的记载。

Luiggi Giafferi (1668–1748) was born at Talasani in Corsica and captained in the Venetian army. Back home he entered the Noble Twelve and in 1706 went to Genoa as orator of Corsica pleading for reforms.

In the 1729–1730 anti-tax rising he helped turn the revolt into an armed political insurrection and became one of the first generals of the Nation. After imprisonment in the Savona fortress in 1732 he returned in 1734 to lead the second insurrection.

Under King Theodore he was prime minister in 1736 and then regent. French intervention forced him into exile in 1739.

路易吉·贾费里（1668—1748）生于科西嘉的塔拉萨尼，曾在威尼斯军队中任上尉。回到家乡后他入选“十二贵族”，1706年作为科西嘉演说者赴热那亚呼吁改革。

1729至1730年的抗税起义中，他帮助将反抗转变为武装政治起义，并成为最早的几位“民族将军”之一。1732年他被囚于萨沃纳要塞，1734年返回科西嘉领导第二次起义。

特奥多尔国王时期，他于1736年出任首相，随后担任摄政。1739年法国出兵，迫使他流亡。

en:
Galeazzo Alessi (1512–1572) was an Italian architect born in Perugia. There he trained and studied Roman ruins before moving to Genoa in 1548.

He modernized the harbour fortifications with the Porta del Molo and built palaces along the new Strada Nuova, designs later copied by the young Rubens. From 1549 he spent decades on the Basilica of Santa Maria in Carignano, modelled on Bramante's scheme for St Peter's. In Milan he designed Palazzo Marino. Around 1561 he returned to Perugia, where he died in 1572.

加莱亚佐·阿莱西（1512—1572）是生于佩鲁贾的意大利建筑师。他在当地学艺、研习古罗马建筑，1548年移居热那亚。

他主持整修港口防御，修建码头门，并在新辟的“新街”两侧设计多座宫殿，年轻的鲁本斯后来曾临摹这些建筑。1549年起他历时数十年营造卡里尼亚诺的圣母升天圣殿，设计参照布拉曼特改建圣彼得大教堂的方案。他在米兰设计了马里诺宫，约1561年返回佩鲁贾，1572年在当地去世。

en:
Bartolomeo Bianco (1590–1657) was the leading architect of the Genoese Baroque. Born near Como, he moved to Genoa with his architect father and became the favourite builder of the Balbi family.

From 1618 he laid out the new Via Balbi and lined it with palaces, including the Palazzo Balbi-Senarega, later published by Rubens. In 1626 he took charge of the city's New Walls.

From 1634 he built the Jesuit college, his masterpiece, now the seat of the University of Genoa. Its steep site inspired a dramatic arrangement of loggias and stairways. He died in Genoa during the plague of 1657.

1618年起他主持开辟巴尔比街，沿街修建包括巴尔比-塞纳雷加宫在内的多座宫殿，鲁本斯后来刊印了这些建筑。1626年他主持修建热那亚新城墙。

1634年起他建造耶稣会学院——这是他的杰作，后来成为热那亚大学的主楼。学院地势陡峭，他借此布置了富有戏剧效果的凉廊和阶梯。1657年他在鼠疫中病逝于热那亚。

Bernardo Strozzi (c. 1581–1644), called il Cappuccino and il Prete Genovese, was a Genoese Baroque painter and engraver of altarpieces, portraits, genre scenes and still lifes. He joined a Capuchin monastery in 1598, but left around 1608 to support his family through painting, winning patrons such as the Doria.

In 1630 his refusal to return to the monastery led to his imprisonment. He settled in Venice around 1632, where the doge and the Grimani family commissioned him. His glowing colour and broad brushwork helped found the Venetian Baroque style. He died in Venice in 1644.

Giovanni Benedetto Castiglione (1609–1664), called Il Grechetto, was a Genoese Baroque painter and printmaker. He trained in Genoa and studied the work of Rubens and Anthony van Dyck.

He lived in Rome from 1634 to about 1645 before returning to Genoa, and in 1651 moved to Mantua to become court artist to Duke Carlo II Gonzaga, where he died in 1664.

He painted rural scenes crowded with animals, notably Noah's Ark and other Old Testament subjects. He won lasting fame for his etchings and as the inventor of the monotype.

乔瓦尼·贝内代托·卡斯蒂廖内（1609—1664），人称“小希腊人”，是热那亚画派的巴洛克画家与版画家。他在热那亚学艺，研习鲁本斯和安东尼·凡·戴克的作品。

1634至约1645年他旅居罗马，后回到热那亚；1651年前往曼托瓦，担任卡洛二世·贡扎加公爵的宫廷画家，1664年在当地去世。

他擅长画动物成群的乡野场景，尤其喜爱挪亚方舟等旧约题材。其蚀刻画享有盛名，他也被视为独幅版画技法的发明者。

Valerio Castello (1624–1659) was a leading painter of the Genoese Baroque. The youngest son of the painter Bernardo Castello, he was apprenticed to Domenico Fiasella and Giovanni Andrea de' Ferrari, then studied in Milan and Parma, absorbing Rubens and van Dyck.

He painted cycles in Genoese churches and excelled in turbulent battle pieces and histories such as the Rape of the Sabines, his compositions full of Rubens-inspired movement. Between 1655 and 1659 he frescoed the vaults of the Palazzo Balbi-Senarega, his masterpiece, including a Chariot of Time. He died suddenly in Genoa in 1659, aged about thirty-five.

Alessandro Magnasco (1667–1749), called il Lissandrino, was a late-Baroque painter born in Genoa, son of Stefano Magnasco. He trained under Valerio Castello and then Filippo Abbiati in Milan, where he worked until 1735 apart from a Florentine stay in 1703–1711 serving Cosimo III.

He became famous for eerie, phantasmagoric genre scenes, monks' gatherings and stormy landscapes, built from flickering brushwork and small figures. His unusual subjects included inquisitorial torture and Jewish and Quaker religious ceremonies. He returned to Genoa in 1735 and died there in 1749.

en:
Giorgi Saakadze (c. 1570–1629) was a Georgian commander from Kartli's petty nobility. Appointed mouravi of Tbilisi in 1608, he destroyed an Ottoman invasion at Tashiskari in 1609. Forced into exile by intrigue in 1612, he served Shah Abbas I, aided his invasion of Georgia in 1614 and became de facto ruler of Kartli in 1619.

In 1625, learning Abbas planned to massacre armed Kartlians, he ambushed the Iranian army at Martqopi. After the Iranian victory at Marabda he withdrew to the mountains and led a guerrilla campaign. Defeated at Bazaleti in 1626, he took Ottoman service and was executed in Constantinople in 1629.

吉奥尔基·萨阿卡泽（约1570—1629）是出身卡特利低级贵族的格鲁吉亚军事统帅。1608年他被任命为第比利斯的穆拉维，1609年在塔什斯卡里歼灭一支奥斯曼入侵军。1612年遭宫廷倾轧被迫出逃后，他效力于沙阿阿拔斯一世，1614年协助其入侵格鲁吉亚，1619年成为卡特利的实际统治者。

Prince Sulkhan-Saba Orbeliani (1658–1725) was a Georgian writer, lexicographer and diplomat. Raised at the Kartli court, he wrote the fable collection A Book of Wisdom and Lies in his youth and took monastic vows in 1698. His Georgian Dictionary, combining a lexicon with an encyclopedia, helped standardize the literary Georgian language.

As tutor and envoy of King Vakhtang VI he travelled to Paris and Rome seeking aid against the Ottomans, but the mission came to nothing when Louis XIV died. He died in Moscow in 1725.

en:
Yahya ibn Umar ibn Rahhu was a Zenata Berber commander in Nasrid Granada and son-in-law of Uthman ibn Abi al-Ula, the Volunteers of the Faith's chief. In December 1326, amid civil war, the vizier named him rival commander of the Volunteers, drawing their troops from Uthman. Around 1340 Sultan Yusuf I made him chief.

After 1354 he governed for Muhammad V, maintaining peace with Castile and paying it tribute. When Ismail II seized power in 1359, Yahya stayed loyal and fled to Castile with two hundred horsemen, finding asylum in Cordoba before rejoining the exiled sultan in 1361.

叶海亚·伊本·奥马尔·伊本·拉胡是纳斯里德王朝格拉纳达的泽纳塔柏柏尔将领，是“信仰志愿军”首领乌斯曼·伊本·阿比·乌拉的女婿。内战期间的1326年12月，大维齐尔任命他为与乌斯曼分庭抗礼的志愿军统领，志愿军随之背离乌斯曼。约1340年，优素福一世苏丹任命他为志愿军首领。

1354年后，他辅佐穆罕默德五世治国，对卡斯蒂利亚维持和平并纳贡。1359年伊斯玛仪二世篡位，叶海亚仍忠于穆罕默德五世，率两百骑兵逃往卡斯蒂利亚，在科尔多瓦得到庇护，1361年重新与流亡苏丹会合。

en:
Thomas von Villach (1435/1440–1523/1529), born Thomas Artula at Thörl near Arnoldstein, was the leading late-Gothic painter in Carinthia. Probably trained by Friedrich von Villach, he worked in Villach from about 1455, painting frescoes and altarpieces that blended Italian and later Netherlandish influences.

Among his attributed works is the Landplagenbild of 1485 on Graz Cathedral, commemorating the plague, locusts and Ottoman siege of 1480. From 1520 he served as a city judge in Villach and died there between 1523 and 1529.

托马斯·冯·菲拉赫（1435/1440—1523/1529）本名托马斯·阿尔图拉，生于阿诺尔德施泰因附近的特尔尔，是克恩滕晚期哥特画派最重要的画家。他大概师从弗里德里希·冯·菲拉赫，约1455年起在菲拉赫创作湿壁画和祭坛画，融合意大利画风，后来又吸收尼德兰艺术。

归于他的作品包括1485年绘于格拉茨大教堂的《天灾图》，纪念1480年的瘟疫、蝗灾和奥斯曼人围攻。1520年起他出任菲拉赫城市法官，1523至1529年间在当地去世。

en: Leonhard Egkelzain was the mining judge, or Bergrichter, of Schladming in Styria, whose silver, lead and copper mines in the Schladminger Tauern gave work to as many as fifteen hundred miners. In 1408 he drew up the Schladminger Bergbrief, the Schladming Mining Letter, which set down in writing the procedural rules and customary rights of the town's miners.

en:
Kaspar Schlick (c. 1396–1449), born at Eger to a merchant councilor, studied at Leipzig and entered Sigismund's service. He rose from scribe in 1416 to royal secretary, vice-chancellor and, in 1433, imperial chancellor, its first lay commoner.

Knighted at Sigismund's coronation in Rome, he fought the Ottomans and Hussites and negotiated for the king in Prussia, Poland and Lithuania, being made a count in 1437–1438. He later served Albert II and Frederick III, patronised Enea Silvio Piccolomini, and died in Vienna in 1449.

卡斯帕尔·施利克（约1396—1449）生于海布，父亲是商人兼市议员。他就读莱比锡大学，后进入西吉斯蒙德麾下，从1416年的文书历任国王秘书、副首相，1433年成为帝国首相，是首位出任此职的在俗平民。

西吉斯蒙德加冕时他在罗马受封骑士，参加过对奥斯曼人和胡斯派的战争，代表国王在普鲁士、波兰和立陶宛谈判，1437至1438年受封伯爵。他先后效力阿尔布雷希特二世和腓特烈三世，资助过埃内亚·西尔维奥·皮科洛米尼，1449年卒于维也纳。

en:
Conrad Celtes (1459–1508), born Konrad Pickel near Schweinfurt in Franconia, was the foremost German humanist of his age. Educated at Cologne and Heidelberg, he published his Art of Writing Verses in 1486 and was crowned poet laureate by Emperor Frederick III at Nuremberg in 1487. He lectured across Germany and Italy and founded a chain of humanist literary societies.

In 1494 he rediscovered the plays of Hrotsvitha at Regensburg. Summoned to Vienna by Maximilian I in 1497, he founded the Collegium Poetarum there in 1502 and died in Vienna in 1508.

康拉德·策尔蒂斯（1459—1508）生于法兰克尼亚施韦因富特附近，本名康拉德·皮克尔，是当时首屈一指的德意志人文主义者。他在科隆和海德堡求学后，于1486年出版《作诗术》，1487年在纽伦堡被皇帝腓特烈三世加冕为桂冠诗人。他遍历德意志和意大利讲学，并创办了一系列人文主义文学会。

1494年，他在雷根斯堡重新发现了赫罗斯维塔的剧作。1497年他应马克西米利安一世之召前往维也纳，1502年在当地创立诗人学院，1508年于维也纳去世。

Johannes Cuspinian (1473–1529), born near Schweinfurt in Franconia, studied at Leipzig and Vienna, becoming professor of medicine and university rector in 1500. In 1493 Maximilian I crowned him poet laureate. A leading humanist in Conrad Celtes's Danubian circle, he edited classical and medieval historical texts and wrote Austria, a historical survey of Lower Austria.

As Maximilian's councillor and diplomat he negotiated the Habsburg–Jagiellonian double marriage alliance of 1515, which ultimately brought Bohemia and Hungary to the Habsburgs in 1526.

Wilhelm von Schröder (1640–1688) was a German mercantilist and cameralist at Emperor Leopold I's Vienna court. After studying law at Jena, he travelled in Holland and England, pursuing economics and the natural sciences, and joined the Royal Society in 1662.

He converted to Catholicism and entered Habsburg service in 1673, reporting on English economic innovations. In 1677 he took over Vienna's Kunst- und Werkhaus, a state model factory for wool, silk and glass.

The factory closed in 1681 and burned down in the 1683 Turkish siege. Schröder died at Eperies while serving as a treasury councillor in Hungary.

en:
Philipp Wilhelm von Hörnigk (1640–1714) was an Austrian cameralist and mercantilist writer. He took a law doctorate at Ingolstadt in 1661 and compiled trade statistics in Vienna from 1673.

After Vienna's 1683 Ottoman siege, his 1684 manifesto Austria over All argued that wealth rested on raw materials rather than trade, calling for protected mines and manufactures and an army of a hundred thousand men. Treating the Habsburg lands as one economic space, it dominated policy debate for a generation. Hörnigk died in 1714, and the book reached fifteen editions by 1784.

菲利普·威廉·冯·霍尼克（1640—1714）是奥地利官房学派学者、重商主义作家。他1661年在因戈尔施塔特获得法学博士学位，1673年起在维也纳编纂贸易统计。

1683年维也纳遭奥斯曼围攻之后，他在1684年发表纲领性著作《奥地利高于一切，只要它愿意》，主张国家财富建立在原料而非贸易之上，呼吁保护矿山和工场，并组建一支十万人的军队。该书把哈布斯堡各领地视为统一的经济区，主导了一代人的政策讨论。霍尼克1714年去世，该书到1784年共印行十五版。

en:
Ulrich von Eyczing (c. 1395–1460) was an Austrian baron who acquired Schrattenthal in 1434 and later enlarged his estates. He served Dukes Albert IV and Albert V against the Hussites and was raised to baronial rank in 1439.

After Albert II's death, in 1451 he formed the Mailberger Bund, uniting 250 nobles against the emperor's guardianship of Ladislaus Postumus. He sat on the regency council of 1453–1455 and became governor of Austria in 1457–1458.

Later imprisoned by Albert VI, he was freed through the emperor's intervention and tried without success to organise another league before his death in 1460.

乌尔里克·冯·艾青（约1395—1460）是奥地利男爵，1434年取得施拉滕塔尔，后来继续扩充地产。他先后效力公爵阿尔布雷希特四世和阿尔布雷希特五世，参加过抗击胡斯派的战争，1439年受封男爵。

阿尔布雷希特二世死后，他于1451年牵头结成有250名贵族参加的迈尔贝格联盟，反对皇帝监护拉斯洛。1453至1455年他任摄政会议成员，1457至1458年出任奥地利执政。

en:
Johannes Müller von Königsberg (1436–1476), known as Regiomontanus, was a German mathematician and astronomer born in Lower Franconia. He became Georg von Peuerbach's pupil at Vienna in 1451, and on his master's deathbed in 1461 promised to complete his abridgement of Ptolemy's Almagest. After four years in Italy with Cardinal Bessarion, he finished the Epitome.

He served Matthias Corvinus at Buda, building instruments and compiling trigonometrical tables. Settling in Nuremberg in 1471, he ran the first scientific printing press. Summoned to Rome by Sixtus IV, he died there in 1476.

Johann Faber (1478–1541), born in Swabia, studied theology and canon law and became vicar-general of Constance in 1517. Once sympathetic to Zwingli's reforms, he became their steadfast opponent, debating Zwingli at the First Zürich Disputation of 1523 and publishing his Malleus Haereticorum, or hammer of heretics.

As Archduke Ferdinand's confessor from 1524 and Bishop of Vienna from 1530, he helped draft the Catholic refutation of the Augsburg Confession and led the campaign against Protestant teaching in Austria.

He also undertook missions to Spain and England seeking aid against the Turks, and as bishop founded twelve scholarships for poor boys. He died at Baden near Vienna.

Melchior Khlesl (1552–1630) was an Austrian cardinal-statesman of the early Counter-Reformation. Born to Lutheran parents in Vienna, he converted under Jesuit influence and became Lower Austrian vicar general in 1581, leading its Protestant towns back to Catholicism.

He became Bishop of Vienna in 1602 and from 1609 was Matthias's chief minister, working for compromise between the camps, and was made cardinal in 1616. His moderation angered hardliners, and in 1618 Ferdinand II arrested him and held him in the Tyrol. Released in 1623, he resumed his diocese and died in 1630.

Prince Eugene of Savoy (1663–1736) was born in Paris, youngest son of the Count of Soissons and Olympia Mancini, raised at Louis XIV's court. Refused a French commission in 1683, he entered Emperor Leopold I's service and won fame at the relief of Vienna. A field marshal by 25, he crushed the Ottomans at Zenta in 1697.

With Marlborough he shared victories at Blenheim (1704), Oudenaarde (1708) and Malplaquet (1709), and won at Petrovaradin in 1716 before taking Belgrade in 1717. He served three emperors and collected art and books; his Vienna palaces include the Belvedere.

Johann Ribi von Lenzburg (1310s–1374), born at Seengen in Aargau, rose through Habsburg service. He became a notary in 1352 and chancellor of Duke Albert II in 1353.

From 1358 he headed Archduke Rudolf IV's chancellery, possibly helping to draft the Privilegium Maius. After failing to win the bishopric of Freising, he was appointed bishop of Gurk by the pope in 1359.

He served as governor of Carinthia in 1363–1365. Rudolf then secured his election as bishop of Brixen, confirmed by the pope in 1364, and Johann died at Brixen in 1374.

Wenzel Anton von Kaunitz (1711–1794) was a Habsburg statesman born in Vienna, one of nineteen children. Originally destined for the Church, he studied law and diplomacy after his elder brother died.

He secured Sardinian support for Maria Theresa at Turin in 1742, later served as minister in the Austrian Netherlands, and was sent as ambassador to Versailles in 1750.

As State Chancellor from 1753 he turned that diplomacy into the Treaty of Versailles of 1756, joining Austria to France against Prussia. He directed Habsburg foreign policy until 1792 and was made a prince of the Empire in 1764.

en:
Franz Anton von Raab (1722–1783) was an Austrian court official and agrarian reformer under Maria Theresa. Trained in law, he designed the land reform named after him, Raabization: from the 1770s, church and noble estates in the Bohemian and Austrian lands were split into small holdings sold to peasants on hereditary leases for cash payments replacing their compulsory robota labour.

Continued under Joseph II, the reform freed tenant farmers, founded new villages and raised state revenues. Knighted in 1755, Raab died in Vienna in 1783.

Adam František Kollár (1718–1783) was a Slovak scholar and a central intellectual of Maria Theresa's enlightened reforms. Educated by the Jesuits at Trnava and Vienna, he left the order afterwards. In 1748 he joined the Imperial Court Library and began teaching classical Greek, becoming chief librarian in 1774.

A linguist at home in more than twenty languages, he wrote works of history and law that underpinned the empress's centralizing policy; his arguments in 1772 for her apostolic rights over Hungary helped justify the Habsburg acquisition of Galicia. In 1783 he gave the first definition of the discipline he named ethnology.

Klemens von Metternich (1773–1859) was an Austrian statesman and diplomat, foreign minister and chancellor. Born in Koblenz and educated at Strasbourg and Mainz, he served Austria as envoy to Saxony, Prussia and Napoleonic France before becoming foreign minister in 1809.

He arranged Napoleon's marriage to Archduchess Marie Louise, then brought Austria into the War of the Sixth Coalition. He led the Austrian delegation at the Congress of Vienna in 1814–1815 and, as chancellor from 1821, shaped the conservative Concert of Europe.

Opposed to liberalism, he used censorship and spies to suppress unrest at home. The 1848 revolutions forced him from office; he returned from exile in 1851 and died in Vienna in 1859.

克莱门斯·冯·梅特涅（1773—1859）是奥地利政治家和外交家，曾任外交大臣与首相。他生于科布伦茨，曾在斯特拉斯堡和美因茨求学，后历任奥地利驻萨克森、普鲁士和拿破仑法国的使节，1809年出任外交大臣。

他一手安排了拿破仑与奥地利女大公玛丽·路易丝的婚事，随后又使奥地利加入第六次反法同盟。1814至1815年，他率领奥地利代表团出席维也纳会议；1821年起任首相，主导保守的欧洲协调体系。

他反对自由主义，在国内利用审查制度和间谍网络压制动荡。1848年革命迫使他下台；他于1851年结束流亡回国，1859年在维也纳去世。

Joseph Radetzky von Radetz (1766–1858) was a Bohemian-born Austrian field marshal. Orphaned young and schooled at Vienna's Theresa Academy, he entered the army as a cadet in 1784 and fought against the Ottomans and in the Napoleonic Wars.

As chief of the general staff he helped plan the allied victory at Leipzig in 1813 and later drove reforms of the Austrian army. In the 1848–1849 Italian war he defeated Sardinia-Piedmont at Custoza and Novara; his soldiers called him Father Radetzky, and Johann Strauss I wrote the Radetzky March to celebrate Custoza. He died in Milan in 1858.

约瑟夫·拉德茨基·冯·拉德茨（1766—1858）是生于波希米亚的奥地利陆军元帅。他自幼父母双亡，在维也纳特雷西亚军校学习，1784年以学员身份入伍，先后参加奥土战争与拿破仑战争。

Nicolò Pacassi (1716–1790) was an Italian-Austrian architect of the late Baroque and early classicism. Born in Wiener Neustadt to a merchant family from Gorizia, he succeeded Jean Nicolas Jadot as head of the court building office in 1753 and became Maria Theresa's chief court architect.

He led the remodelling of Schönbrunn Palace, designed the ballroom wing of the Vienna Hofburg and rebuilt parts of Prague Castle, with further commissions in Innsbruck, Buda and Gorizia. Knighted in 1764 and raised to baron in 1769, he left the building office at his own request in 1772 and remained an adviser until his death in Vienna.

尼科洛·帕卡西（1716—1790）是巴洛克晚期至早期古典主义时期的意大利裔奥地利建筑师。他生于维也纳新城，家族是来自戈里齐亚的商人家庭。1753年，他接替让·尼古拉·雅多出任宫廷营造署主管，成为玛丽亚·特蕾西亚的首席宫廷建筑师。

他主持改建美泉宫，设计维也纳霍夫堡的歌舞厅翼楼，并重建布拉格城堡的部分区域，还在因斯布鲁克、布达和戈里齐亚等地承接工程。他于1764年受封骑士，1769年晋封男爵，1772年应自己的请求离开营造署，此后担任顾问直至在维也纳去世。

John of Viktring (c. 1270–1345/1347) was elected abbot of the Cistercian monastery of Viktring near Klagenfurt in 1312. He served as chaplain and confidential secretary to Duke Henry of Carinthia, and in 1330 accompanied King John of Bohemia across the Brenner Pass to Trent. After Henry's death in 1335 he pleaded the claims of Margaret of Tyrol at Linz before Emperor Louis IV, only for the Habsburg dukes to seize Carinthia.

He then advised Dukes Albert II and Otto in Vienna until 1341, when he retired to his abbey and wrote the six-book chronicle Liber certarum historiarum, covering 1217–1343.

约翰·冯·维克特林（约1270—1345/1347）于1312年当选为克拉根福附近维克特林西多会修道院院长。他任克恩滕公爵亨利的宫廷神父与机要秘书，1330年随波希米亚国王约翰的军队翻越布伦纳山口，前往特伦托。1335年亨利去世后，他在林茨向皇帝路德维希四世陈情，为蒂罗尔的玛格丽特争取继承权，但克恩滕最终被哈布斯堡公爵夺取。

此后他在维也纳为阿尔布雷希特二世与奥托两位公爵顾问，直到1341年退回修道院，撰写六卷本编年史《确凿史事》，记述1217至1343年的史事。

Theophrastus von Hohenheim, called Paracelsus (1493–1541), was born at Einsiedeln in the Swiss canton of Schwyz, the son of a physician who taught him medicine and mineralogy. He took his doctorate at Ferrara around 1516 and travelled across Europe as an army surgeon.

In 1526 he was called to Basel to treat the printer Johann Froben. Appointed town physician in 1527, he lectured in German and publicly burned the medical texts of Avicenna.

Rejecting classical authority in favour of observation and experiment, he pioneered chemical remedies and the study of poisons, later writing the Great Surgery. He died at Salzburg in 1541, leaving a movement, Paracelsianism, that transformed Renaissance medicine.

特奥夫拉斯图斯·冯·霍恩海姆，人称帕拉塞尔苏斯（1493—1541），生于瑞士施维茨州的艾恩西德尔恩，父亲是医生，曾教他医学与矿物学。他约1516年在费拉拉取得医学博士学位，后在欧洲游历、充任军医。

1526年，他应召到巴塞尔为印刷商约翰·弗罗本治病。1527年他受聘为巴塞尔城市医生，用德语讲学，并当众焚毁阿维森纳的医学典籍。

他摒弃古典权威，主张观察与实验，首倡用化学药物治病、系统研究毒物，后著有《大外科》。1541年他卒于萨尔茨堡，其学说形成帕拉塞尔苏斯主义，深刻改变了文艺复兴时期的医学。

Oswald von Wolkenstein (1376/1377–1445), born at Pfalzen near Brixen in Tyrol, was one of the finest German poets and composers of the later Middle Ages. As a youth he served as a squire for fourteen years, travelling as far as Crete, Lithuania, Crimea, Turkey and the Holy Land, journeys he recalled in autobiographical songs.

After an inheritance quarrel with his brother, he received a share of Hauenstein Castle in 1407 but occupied the whole castle. From 1414 he served Emperor Sigismund as a diplomat, visiting England, Scotland and Portugal.

He married Margarete von Schwangau in 1417 and fought in Tyrol's noble wars against Duke Frederick IV, who held him captive in 1421–1422. He died at Meran in 1445.

Petrus Zwicker was a Celestine monk and inquisitor born at Wormditt in East Prussia. He served as school rector at Zittau until 1381, when he entered the Celestine monastery on the Oybin; by 1395 he was its prior and provincial of the Celestines in Germany.

From 1390 he was entrusted with pursuing heretics, and between 1391 and his death in Vienna in 1403 he directed one of the largest inquisitorial campaigns of the later Middle Ages, ranging through Austria, Pomerania, Brandenburg and Hungary and aimed almost entirely at the Waldensians.

en:
Niklas Türing the Elder was a late-Gothic stonemason, sculptor and master builder whose family came from Memmingen in Swabia. Around 1480 Duke Sigmund of Tyrol brought him from the Allgäu to Innsbruck, and Emperor Maximilian I later named him court master builder.

For Maximilian, who took over the Tyrolean regency in 1490, he and his son Gregor built the famous Golden Roof oriel in 1497–1500 and carved its figural and heraldic reliefs. He also made the castle giant Haidl for the Burgriesenhaus in Innsbruck. He died at Innsbruck in 1517.

老尼克拉斯·图林是哥特晚期的石匠、雕刻家兼建筑师，家族出自施瓦本的梅明根。约1480年，蒂罗尔公爵西吉斯蒙德把他从阿尔高召到因斯布鲁克，后来皇帝马克西米利安一世任命他为宫廷建筑总管。

马克西米利安于1490年接掌蒂罗尔的统治，图林与儿子格雷戈尔于1497至1500年为他建造了著名的“金屋顶”凸窗，并雕刻了上面的人物与纹章浮雕。他还为因斯布鲁克的城堡巨人屋制作了城堡巨人海德尔。1517年他在因斯布鲁克去世。

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina (c. 1525–1594) was an Italian composer, leading figure of the Roman School of Renaissance polyphony. Born near Rome in Palestrina, he served as organist at its cathedral from 1544 to 1551, when Pope Julius III made him maestro di cappella of the Cappella Giulia at St Peter's.

Dismissed in 1555 because, as a married layman, he could not serve in Paul IV's all-clerical choir, he directed music at St John Lateran and Santa Maria Maggiore before rejoining St Peter's in 1571.

By his death in 1594 he had written more than 105 masses and 250 motets. These works helped establish a model for later sacred counterpoint.

乔瓦尼·皮耶路易吉·达·帕莱斯特里纳（约1525—1594）是意大利作曲家，文艺复兴复调音乐罗马乐派的代表人物。他出生于罗马附近的帕莱斯特里纳，1544至1551年担任当地大教堂的管风琴师，此后教宗尤利乌斯三世任命他为圣彼得大教堂朱利亚礼拜堂乐长。

1555年，因身为已婚俗人，无法在教宗保禄四世只收神职人员的唱诗班任职，他被迫去职，此后先后主持拉特朗圣若望大殿和圣母大殿的音乐事务，1571年回到圣彼得大教堂。

到1594年去世时，他已作有超过105首弥撒曲和250首经文歌，这些作品成为后世宗教对位法的典范。

Pieter Bruegel the Elder (c. 1525–1569) was a leading Flemish painter and printmaker of the Northern Renaissance, celebrated for landscapes and peasant scenes. Born near Breda, he became an Antwerp guild master in 1551 and travelled to Italy, reaching Rome. Settling in Antwerp in 1555, he designed prints for the publisher Hieronymus Cock before turning to painting.

In 1563 he married Mayken Coecke and moved to Brussels, where he died in 1569, leaving two painter sons, Pieter and Jan. His Landscape with the Fall of Icarus (c. 1560) and The Hunters in the Snow (1565) remain among his celebrated works.

老彼得·勃鲁盖尔（约1525—1569）是北方文艺复兴时期杰出的佛兰德斯画家与版画家，以风景画和农民题材闻名。他出生于布雷达一带，1551年成为安特卫普画师行会的师傅，随后前往意大利游学，最远抵达罗马。1555年他定居安特卫普，为出版商希罗尼穆斯·科克设计版画，后来转向绘画。

1563年他与迈克·科克结婚，迁居布鲁塞尔，1569年在当地去世，两个儿子小彼得和扬后来都成为画家。《伊卡洛斯坠落的风景》（约1560）和《雪中猎人》（1565）是他的著名作品。

Martin Brenner (1548–1616) was prince-bishop of Seckau from 1585, who led the recatholicization of Styria during the Counter-Reformation. Born at Dietenheim in Württemberg and a doctor of theology from Pavia, he was appointed bishop by the Archbishop of Salzburg in 1585 and vicar general of Styria in 1591.

From 1600 he headed military-backed commissions that expelled Lutheran preachers, burned Protestant books and forced the people to swear Catholic oaths or emigrate. He reconverted all of Styria within half a year and was called the Apostle of Styria.

From 1602 he promoted catechism instruction in reconverted districts and in 1604 led a conversion campaign in Klagenfurt. He resigned his see in 1615 and died at Leibnitz in 1616.

马丁·布伦纳（1548—1616）1585年起任塞考采邑主教，是反宗教改革时期施蒂利亚重新天主教化的主导者。他出生于符腾堡的迪滕海姆，在帕维亚获得神学博士学位，1585年被萨尔茨堡大主教任命为主教，1591年出任施蒂利亚副主教。

1600年起，他率领有军队支持的宗教委员会，驱逐路德宗传教士、焚烧新教书籍，并强迫民众宣誓信奉天主教，否则必须移居。他在半年内完成了整个施蒂利亚的改宗，被称为“施蒂利亚使徒”。

1602年起他在重新天主教化的地区推行要理教育，1604年又在克拉根福主持改宗行动。1615年他辞去主教之职，1616年卒于莱布尼茨。

Maximilian von und zu Trauttmansdorff (1584–1650) was an Austrian statesman born in Graz. After studying law, he joined the Aulic Council in 1609 and became a key diplomat for Ferdinand II from 1618, arranging the emperor's alliance with Bavaria in 1619 and concluding the Peace of Nikolsburg with Gabriel Bethlen in 1621.

From 1633 he was Obersthofmeister and closest adviser to Ferdinand III, negotiating the Peace of Prague in 1635. As head of the imperial delegation at Westphalia, he was a chief architect of the Peace of Westphalia, and in 1648 persuaded Ferdinand to accept peace without Spain's involvement or military support.

马克西米利安·冯·特劳特曼斯多夫（1584—1650）是生于格拉茨的奥地利政治家。他曾学习法律，1609年进入帝国枢密院，1618年后成为斐迪南二世倚重的外交官，1619年促成皇帝与巴伐利亚的同盟，1621年与拜特伦·加博尔签订《尼科尔斯堡和约》。

1633年起他担任后来的斐迪南三世的宫廷总管兼首席顾问，1635年谈成《布拉格和约》。作为威斯特伐利亚和会上的帝国代表团团长，他是《威斯特伐利亚和约》的主要缔造者之一。1648年，他说服斐迪南在西班牙不参与、也不提供军事支持的情况下接受和约。

Franz Seraph von Dietrichstein (1570–1636) was a Habsburg cardinal, Bishop of Olomouc and the first Prince of Dietrichstein. Born in Madrid to an imperial diplomat, he was made cardinal in 1599 and, as Bishop of Olomouc from 1600, led the Counter-Reformation in Moravia. President of the Privy Council from 1607, he crowned Matthias and Ferdinand II kings of Bohemia in 1611 and 1617.

Exiled by the rebel estates in 1619, he returned after White Mountain as governor of Moravia and promoted its reconversion. Raised to hereditary imperial prince in 1624, he named his nephew Maximilian as his heir and died at Brno in 1636.

方济各·塞拉夫·冯·迪特里希施泰因（1570—1636）是哈布斯堡的枢机主教、奥洛穆茨主教，也是迪特里希施泰因家族的第一位亲王。他出生于马德里，父亲是帝国外交官，1599年受封枢机，1600年起任奥洛穆茨主教，领导摩拉维亚的反宗教改革。1607年起任枢密院主席，先后于1611年和1617年为马蒂亚斯和斐迪南二世加冕为波希米亚国王。

1619年他被叛乱的等级驱逐，白山战役后以摩拉维亚总督身份返回，推行当地的重新天主教化。1624年他被升为世袭帝国亲王，指定侄子马克西米利安为继承人，1636年卒于布尔诺。

Gerhard von Questenberg (c. 1586–1646) was an imperial diplomat and statesman of the Thirty Years' War, born in Cologne. A privy councillor to Ferdinand II and vice-president of the Court War Council, he bought confiscated lordships in Moravia and Bohemia and was made a baron in 1627.

One of the few councillors trusted by Wallenstein, he was chosen with Verda at the 1630 Regensburg Diet to deliver the general's dismissal at Memmingen. They negotiated his reinstatement in 1632; Questenberg mediated between him and the court until his murder in 1634. In 1636 he became imperial regent over the two Austrias and Hungary, dying in Vienna in 1646.

Johann Baptist Verda, Baron von Verdenberg from 1623 (c. 1582–1648), was an imperial diplomat, the first court chancellor for Upper, Inner and Lower Austria, and confidant of Ferdinand II. Educated by the Jesuits in Graz with a law doctorate from Pavia, he entered Ferdinand's service in 1607 and became court chancellor in 1619, helping draft Bohemia's absolutist constitution after White Mountain.

During the Thirty Years' War he negotiated with Wallenstein in 1630 and delivered his dismissal, later negotiating his reinstatement. He also helped negotiate with Saxony towards the Peace of Prague of 1635. Resigning at Ferdinand's death in 1637, he died in Vienna in 1648.

Nikolaus Esterházy de Galántha (1583–1645) was a Hungarian nobleman born at Galanta and the founder of the House of Esterházy. Raised a Protestant, he converted to Catholicism and became, with Cardinal Pázmány, a pillar of Habsburg rule in Hungary, fighting the Ottoman occupation and opposing the Protestant princes Gabriel Bethlen and George I Rákóczi.

His first marriage brought him wealth and the lordship of Munkács, which he surrendered to Bethlen under the Peace of Nikolsburg in 1622 in exchange for imperial compensation. Matthias II later made him a baron and then count of Bereg.

He defeated the Turks on the Nyitra in 1623, and in 1625 Ferdinand II named him Palatine of Hungary, the kingdom's highest office. He received the Golden Fleece in 1626.

加兰塔的米克洛什·埃施特哈齐（1583—1645）是匈牙利贵族，生于加兰塔，是埃施特哈齐家族的奠基人。他本在新教家庭长大，后改宗天主教，与彼得·帕兹曼尼枢机并立，成为哈布斯堡统治匈牙利的支柱：他抗击奥斯曼占领，并同新教诸侯拜特伦·加博尔、拉科齐·捷尔吉一世对抗。

第一段婚姻给他带来财富与蒙卡奇领地；依照《尼科尔斯堡和约》，他于1622年将蒙卡奇交给拜特伦，并从皇帝处得到补偿。马蒂亚斯后来先后封他为男爵和拜赖格伯爵。

1623年他在尼特拉河击败土耳其人，1625年斐迪南二世任命他为匈牙利帕拉蒂尼，即王国的最高官职。1626年他获颁金羊毛勋章。

Vilém Slavata of Chlum (1572–1652) was a Bohemian nobleman born near Kutná Hora. Raised in the Unity of the Brethren, he converted to Catholicism in 1597 and served Rudolf II and Matthias at court. A firm backer of Ferdinand II, he was the king's viceregent in Prague when Protestant nobles led by Thurn threw him and Jaroslav of Martinice from the castle windows on 23 May 1618.

He survived with severe injuries but was arrested. The next year he escaped to Saxony and then Passau. He returned after the White Mountain victory of 1620, became a leading figure in restoring Catholicism, and in 1628 became High Chancellor of Bohemia.

赫卢姆的维莱姆·斯拉瓦塔（1572—1652）是生于库特纳霍拉附近的波希米亚贵族。他在弟兄合一会的氛围中长大，1597年改宗天主教，曾在鲁道夫二世和马蒂亚斯朝中任职。作为斐迪南二世的坚定支持者，他担任国王在布拉格的摄政；1618年5月23日，图尔恩率领的新教贵族把他和马丁尼茨的雅罗斯拉夫从城堡窗口掷出。

他身负重伤却生还，随后被捕；次年他逃往萨克森，再前往帕绍。1620年白山战役获胜后他返回波希米亚，积极推动恢复天主教，1628年出任波希米亚最高大臣。

Antonio Cesti (1623–1669), baptised Pietro, was an Italian Baroque composer, tenor and organist, among the most celebrated musicians of his generation. Born at Arezzo, he joined the Franciscans in 1637 but turned to secular music at Volterra. His career as a singer and opera composer conflicted with his religious calling, and by 1650 he had been reprimanded.

His first operas appeared in Venice in 1651. From 1652 he served Archduke Ferdinand Charles at Innsbruck, where he gave L'Argia for Queen Christina of Sweden and premiered Orontea in 1656.

He entered the papal chapel in Rome in 1660 and became vice-Kapellmeister at Vienna in 1666, staging Il pomo d'oro for the court. He died in Florence in 1669.

安东尼奥·彻斯提（1623—1669），洗礼名彼得罗，是意大利巴洛克作曲家、男高音和管风琴师，也是他那一代最负盛名的音乐家之一。他出生于阿雷佐，1637年加入方济各会，后来在沃尔泰拉转向世俗音乐。他的歌唱与歌剧创作生涯和修士身份发生冲突，至1650年已受到训诫。

1651年他的首批歌剧在威尼斯上演。1652年起他在因斯布鲁克侍奉奥地利大公斐迪南·卡尔，在那里为瑞典女王克里斯蒂娜的到访演出《阿尔吉亚》，并于1656年首演《奥龙泰阿》。

1660年他进入罗马的教宗合唱团，1666年出任维也纳副乐长，为宫廷上演《金苹果》。1669年他在佛罗伦萨去世。

Franz Grillparzer (1791–1872) was an Austrian writer, born in Vienna and regarded as Austria's leading nineteenth-century dramatist. He studied law at the University of Vienna and, after his father's death, worked as a private tutor. From 1813 he earned his living as a civil servant, directing the Hofkammer archives from 1832 until his retirement in 1856.

His verse plays, shaped by classical drama and often staged at the Burgtheater, include Sappho, the Medea trilogy and his 1825 tragedy of the Bohemian king, König Ottokars Glück und Ende.

He wrote Beethoven's funeral oration in 1827 and Schubert's epitaph. After his only comedy was rejected by the public in 1840, he nearly passed from his contemporaries' memory.

弗朗茨·格里帕泽（1791—1872）是奥地利作家，生于维也纳，被视为19世纪奥地利首屈一指的剧作家。他曾在维也纳大学攻读法律，父亲去世后做过家庭教师。1813年起他以公务员为业，1832年任宫廷财务署档案主管，直至1856年退休。

他的诗剧受古典戏剧影响颇深，常在城堡剧院上演，代表作包括《萨福》、美狄亚三部曲以及1825年以波希米亚国王普热米斯尔·奥托卡二世为主角的悲剧《奥托卡王的兴衰》。

1827年他为贝多芬的葬礼撰写悼词，还为舒伯特撰写了墓志铭。1840年他唯一的喜剧遭观众冷遇后，他几乎被同时代人遗忘。
