Johann Anton von Pergen (1725–1814) was a Habsburg diplomat and statesman whose career spanned four monarchs. A Jesuit-educated lawyer, he served as imperial envoy at Mainz and administered the occupied western territories during the Seven Years' War. In 1766 he became a State Council vice-chancellor and Kaunitz's deputy, and in 1770 drafted an education reform proposing state control of schools and lay teachers in place of Jesuit teachers.

As a minister under Joseph II he centralized the police and built up a secret police to enforce the emperor's radical reforms; after 1792 he returned under Francis II to suppress opposition.

约翰·安东·冯·佩尔根（1725—1814）是历仕四位君主的哈布斯堡外交家与政治家。他早年受耶稣会教育、学习法律，曾任帝国驻美因茨使节，七年战争期间治理西部被占领的地区。1766年他出任国务院副首相兼考尼茨的副手，1770年起草教育改革方案，主张将学校置于国家管理之下，以世俗教师取代耶稣会士。

作为约瑟夫二世手下的大臣，他把警察系统中央集权化，并建立秘密警察以推行皇帝的激进改革；1792年后他在弗朗茨二世治下复出，负责镇压反对势力。

Primož Trubar (1508–1586) was born at Rašica in Carniola. After schooling in Salzburg and Trieste he served as a preacher in Ljubljana from 1530, gradually embracing Lutheran teaching until his expulsion in 1547.

In exile at Rothenburg he wrote the first books printed in Slovene, the Catechismus and Abecedarium of 1550, basing his written language on the speech of Ljubljana. As first superintendent of the Carniolan Protestant Church he published his Slovene New Testament in three parts by 1577. He wrote twenty-two books in Slovene and died in 1586, having helped establish the language's literary form.

普里莫日·特鲁巴尔（1508—1586）生于卡尼奥拉的拉希察，曾在萨尔茨堡和的里雅斯特求学。1530年起他在卢布尔雅那任布道神父，逐渐接受路德宗主张，1547年被逐出城。

流亡罗滕堡期间，他写成最早的斯洛文尼亚文印刷书籍，即1550年印行的《教理问答》和《识字课本》，并以卢布尔雅那口语为书面语基础。作为卡尼奥拉新教教会首任总监，他到1577年分三部分出齐斯洛文尼亚语《新约》译本。他一生著有二十二部斯洛文尼亚文著作，帮助奠定其书面语，1586年去世。

Johann Friedrich Böhmer (1795–1863) was a German historian and archivist born in Frankfurt am Main. After law studies at Heidelberg and Göttingen and time in Italy, he returned to Frankfurt and through Baron vom Stein became secretary to the Monumenta Germaniae Historica in 1824.

Appointed city archivist in 1825, he launched the Regesta Imperii, a calendar of charters issued by the German kings and emperors. The work made him a pioneer of diplomatics. He disliked Prussia and Protestantism and favoured Austria and Catholicism, though he was not a Catholic.

Johann Strauss I (1804–1849) was an Austrian composer born in Leopoldstadt. Orphaned young and apprenticed to a bookbinder, he learned the violin, played in Joseph Lanner's orchestra and founded his own band in 1825. His Little Doves Waltz established his reputation at the Vienna carnival in 1826.

His waltzes, polkas and galops made Vienna dance, and his tours took him across Germany, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Britain. With Lanner he transformed the waltz into a Viennese institution, earning the nickname Father of the Waltz and paving the way for his sons Johann, Josef and Eduard. His best-known work was the Radetzky March of 1848.

老约翰·施特劳斯（1804—1849）是奥地利作曲家，生于利奥波德城。他自幼父母双亡，曾给装订商当学徒，后学习小提琴，进入约瑟夫·兰纳的乐队，1825年自组乐队。1826年，他的《小鸽子圆舞曲》在维也纳狂欢节上赢得声誉。

他的圆舞曲、波尔卡和加洛普让整个维也纳翩然起舞，还率乐队巡演德国、法国、比利时、荷兰和英国。他与兰纳一道把圆舞曲发展成维也纳的标志，赢得‘圆舞曲之父’的称号，也为儿子小约翰、约瑟夫和爱德华开辟了道路。1848年的《拉德茨基进行曲》是他最著名的作品。

en:
Marianna Martines (1744–1812) was an Austrian composer, pianist and singer in Classical Vienna. She grew up in her family's Vienna home, where the poet Metastasio lived and oversaw an education more extensive than was customary for women of her class. She studied keyboard with the young Joseph Haydn, singing with Nicola Porpora and composition with Hasse and Bonno.

She performed often before Empress Maria Theresa, and her Italian-style masses, motets, cantatas and oratorios to Metastasio's texts won wide esteem. In 1773 she became the first woman admitted to Bologna's Accademia Filarmonica, and her later home concerts were attended by Haydn and Mozart.

玛丽安娜·马丁内斯（1744—1812）是维也纳古典主义时期的奥地利作曲家、钢琴家与歌唱家。她在维也纳的家中长大，诗人梅塔斯塔西奥与她家同住并督导她的教育，为她安排了超出同阶层女性通常程度的学业。她随年轻的海顿学键盘、随波尔波拉学声乐，并随哈塞与博诺学作曲。

她常为玛丽亚·特蕾西亚女皇演奏演唱，所作意大利风格的弥撒、经文歌、康塔塔及采用梅塔斯塔西奥脚本的清唱剧广受赞誉。1773年，她成为首位入选博洛尼亚爱乐学院的女性，晚年家中的音乐聚会常有海顿和莫扎特出席。

Antonio Salieri (1750–1825) was an Italian composer born in Legnago who spent his career in Habsburg Vienna. Taken there as an orphaned pupil of Florian Leopold Gassmann and later patronised by Gluck, he directed the court Italian opera from 1774 to 1792 and served as imperial Kapellmeister from 1788 to 1824, responsible for music at the court chapel.

His operas, written in Italian, French and German, were performed across Europe, and he taught Beethoven, Schubert, Liszt and Hummel. He wrote no operas after 1804, and vehemently denied rumours that he had poisoned Mozart.

安东尼奥·萨列里（1750—1825）是意大利作曲家，生于莱尼亚戈，一生事业都在维也纳度过。他幼年父母双亡，被加斯曼带到维也纳培养，后受格鲁克提携；1774至1792年主持宫廷意大利歌剧院，1788至1824年任宫廷乐长，负责宫廷礼拜堂的音乐。

他用意、法、德三种语言创作的歌剧曾在欧洲各地上演，学生包括贝多芬、舒伯特、李斯特和胡梅尔。1804年后他不再创作歌剧；关于他毒杀莫扎特的传闻，他本人坚决否认。

Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), born at Delft, was a Dutch humanist jurist and a child prodigy who entered Leiden University at eleven. He later became an advocate at The Hague.

His Mare Liberum of 1609 argued that the sea was open to all nations, challenging Portuguese claims to exclusive Asian trade. Drawn into the Republic's religious conflicts on the Arminian side, he was imprisoned in Loevestein Castle after 1618 and escaped in 1621 hidden in a chest of books.

In Paris he published De jure belli ac pacis in 1625, a foundation of modern international law. From 1634 he served Sweden as ambassador to France. After being shipwrecked he died at Rostock in 1645.

胡果·格劳秀斯（1583—1645）生于代尔夫特，是荷兰人文主义法学家，自幼有神童之名，十一岁便进入莱顿大学，后来成为海牙律师。

他在1609年发表的《海洋自由论》主张海洋向各国开放，挑战葡萄牙对亚洲贸易的独占主张。因卷入共和国的宗教冲突、站在阿民念派一边，他于1618年后被囚禁在勒文斯泰因城堡，1621年藏在书箱中逃脱。

他在巴黎于1625年出版《战争与和平法》，为现代国际法奠定了基础。1634年起他出任瑞典驻法国大使，后遇海难，1645年于罗斯托克去世。

Christiaan Huygens (1629–1695) was a Dutch mathematician, astronomer and physicist, born in The Hague, the son of Constantijn Huygens, adviser to the House of Orange. He studied law and mathematics at Leiden. Grinding lenses with his brother, he built powerful telescopes, discovered Saturn's largest moon, Titan, in 1655 and explained its appearance as a thin flat ring.

In 1657 he patented the pendulum clock. His Horologium Oscillatorium of 1673 laid the foundations of dynamics, and his Traité de la Lumière of 1690 set out the wave theory of light.

1657年他取得摆钟专利。1673年的《摆钟论》奠定动力学基础，1690年的《光论》提出光的波动说。

Gerardus Mercator (1512–1594), born Gerard de Kremer in Rupelmonde, Flanders, was a Flemish cartographer, globe-maker and cosmographer. Trained in Leuven by Gemma Frisius, he won fame with early maps of the Holy Land, the world and Flanders. Arrested for Protestant heresy in 1543, he was jailed seven months and in 1552 moved to tolerant Duisburg, where he became ducal cosmographer.

His world map of 1569 introduced the projection that bears his name, drawing constant compass bearings as straight lines for navigation. His Atlas was published posthumously in 1595.

格拉杜斯·墨卡托（1512—1594），本名赫拉德·德·克雷默，生于佛兰德斯的吕佩尔蒙德，是佛兰德斯地图学家、地球仪制作家和宇宙志学者。他在鲁汶随赫马·弗里修斯学艺，以圣地地图、世界地图和佛兰德斯地图成名。1543年他因新教异端入狱七个月，1552年迁居宗教宽容的杜伊斯堡，任公爵的宫廷宇宙志学者。

他1569年的世界地图采用至今以他命名的投影法，将恒定罗盘方位画为直线，便于航海。其《地图集》于1595年在他死后出版。

Johan de Witt (1625–1672) was a Dutch statesman born at Dordrecht. Trained in law at Leiden, he became Grand Pensionary of Holland in 1653 and dominated the Republic through its Stadtholderless Golden Age, opposing the House of Orange. In 1667 the Dutch raid on the Medway humiliated England, and he carried an act barring the House of Orange from the stadtholderate.

In the Rampjaar of 1672 the Republic suffered defeats and French armies invaded. De Witt was stabbed in June, resigned in August, and on the 20th was lynched with his brother Cornelis by an Orangist mob in The Hague.

约翰·德·维特（1625—1672）是荷兰政治家，生于多德雷赫特。他在莱顿学习法律，1653年出任荷兰省大议长，在无执政的黄金时代主导共和国政务，反对奥兰治家族。1667年，荷兰舰队突袭梅德韦河，羞辱了英国，他又推动通过法案，禁止奥兰治家族担任执政。

1672年的“灾难年”中，共和国连遭败绩，法军入侵。德·维特6月遇刺受伤，8月辞职，20日与兄长科内利斯一同在海牙被奥兰治派暴民私刑处死。

Anthonie Heinsius (1641–1720) was a Dutch statesman born at Delft. He became pensionary of Delft in 1679. Sent to Paris in 1682 to protest Louis XIV's seizure of Orange, he was threatened with the Bastille and returned an opponent of France. In 1689 he became Grand Pensionary of Holland and drove the anti-French coalition in the Nine Years' War.

After William III died in 1702, Heinsius became the Republic's main foreign policymaker. During the War of the Spanish Succession he helped direct alliance strategy with Marlborough and Prince Eugene, and died in office in 1720.

Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677) was a Dutch philosopher born in Amsterdam to a family of Portuguese-Jewish merchants. Raised in the city's Portuguese Jewish congregation, he challenged rabbinic authority and was expelled from it in 1656. He then lived quietly, earning a living by grinding lenses and publishing sparingly to avoid persecution.

His Tractatus Theologico-Politicus questioned the divine origin of the Hebrew Bible and defended freedom of thought, while his Ethics, identifying God with nature, appeared only after his death. He declined a chair at Heidelberg to guard his independence, and died at The Hague in 1677.

巴鲁赫·斯宾诺莎（1632—1677）是荷兰哲学家，生于阿姆斯特丹一个葡萄牙犹太商人家庭。他在当地葡萄牙犹太会社群中长大，因质疑拉比权威，于1656年被革出教门。此后他过着平静生活，以磨镜片为生，为避免迫害生前很少发表著作。

他的《神学政治论》质疑《希伯来圣经》的神圣来源，主张思想自由；《伦理学》将上帝等同于自然，在他去世后才出版。为保持独立，他拒绝了海德堡大学的教席，1677年在海牙去世。

Johannes Bogerman (1576–1637) was a Frisian Calvinist theologian, born at Upleward in East Frisia, the son of a preacher. From 1591 he studied at Franeker, Heidelberg, Geneva, Oxford and Cambridge, then held Reformed pastorates at Sneek, Enkhuizen and Leeuwarden, preaching against the Arminians.

He was appointed president of the Synod of Dort of 1618–1619, which issued the Canons of Dort and authorized a new Dutch Bible translated from the original languages. He later helped translate that Statenbijbel, took a theology chair at Franeker in 1636, and died there the following year.

en:
Lodewijk Elzevir (c. 1540–1617) was a printer and publisher born in Leuven. He began as a bookbinder in an Antwerp workshop and, after moves through Wesel and Douai, settled in Leiden before 1580. In 1583 he produced his first book there, founding the House of Elzevir.

Its books favoured legible type, often in small formats with narrow margins. After his death his sons and grandsons expanded the business, which published Galileo's Two New Sciences when its author could not publish in Italy. The family business continued until 1791.

Georg Giese (1497–1562) was a Hanseatic merchant of Danzig, the son of the city's mayor Albrecht Giese. His family maintained an office at the Steelyard in London. From the 1520s he spent at least twelve years in London managing that office, and became the Alderman's Deputy there in 1533.

In 1532 Hans Holbein the Younger painted his portrait amid the letters and seals of his counting house. He returned to Danzig in 1535, married the daughter of a leading merchant, and died there in 1562.

Heinrich Sudermann (1520–1591) was a lawyer from Cologne and the first Syndic of the Hanseatic League. The son of Cologne's mayor Hermann Sudermann, he was elected in 1556 to the newly created post as a permanent official with legal training.

He worked to protect and extend the diplomatic agreements of the League's member towns. Revised agreements in 1557 and 1579 set out the towns' obligations and made some progress towards that goal. Sudermann died in Lübeck in 1591.

en:
András Hess (c. 1450–c. 1473) was a printer of German origin who founded the first printing press in the Kingdom of Hungary. Summoned from Rome to Buda in 1471 or 1472 by Provost László Karai, he set up his press in 1472 with a grant of two thousand silver florins.

On 5 June 1473, the eve of Pentecost, he completed the Latin Chronica Hungarorum, or Buda Chronicle, the first book printed in Hungary. No trace of him or his press survives after 1473.

Baron Tamás Nádasdy (1498–1562), called the Great Palatine, was a Hungarian statesman educated at Graz, Bologna and Rome. Sent by Louis II to the Diet of Speyer in 1525 for help against the Turks, he returned to learn of the Mohács disaster. Appointed Ferdinand's commandant of Buda in 1527, he went over to John Zápolya and defended it against imperial troops in 1530.

He returned to Ferdinand in 1533 and later defended the southern frontier as Ban of Croatia-Slavonia. In 1540 he became Judge royal, and in 1559 was elected palatine at Pozsony. He founded a school and press at Újsziget and died in 1562.

男爵陶马什·纳道什迪（1498—1562）人称“伟大的总督”，是匈牙利政治家，曾在格拉茨、博洛尼亚和罗马求学。1525年，国王拉约什二世派他出席施派尔议会求援抵御奥斯曼人，他回国时得知摩哈赤惨败的消息。1527年，斐迪南任命他为布达城防司令；他后转投亚诺什·扎波尧伊，1530年守城抵御帝国军队。

1533年他重返斐迪南阵营，后任克罗地亚-斯拉沃尼亚总督，守卫南部边境。1540年他出任王国大法官，1559年在波若尼被推举为匈牙利总督。他在乌伊西格特创办学校与印刷所，1562年去世。

en:
Count Tamás Erdődy (1558–1624) was a Hungarian-Croatian magnate who became Ban of Croatia in 1583. After earlier victories over the Ottomans and a defeat at Brest in 1592, he helped crush the Ottoman army at Sisak in 1593, a battle that triggered the Long Turkish War; Pope Clement VIII sent him his congratulations.

After leaving the banate in 1595, he held senior court offices. From 1607 he was perpetual count of Varaždin, an office made hereditary in his family, and he held the banate again from 1608 to 1615. He died in 1624.

Janus Pannonius (1434–1472), born in Slavonia, was the leading Hungarian humanist poet of his age and Bishop of Pécs. Sent to Italy in 1447 by his uncle John Vitéz, he studied under Guarino da Verona and canon law at Padua, writing his first epigrams before he was fifteen. He returned to Hungary in 1458.

He became royal vice-chancellor and, in 1469, Ban of Slavonia, and kept ties with leading philosophers while assembling a major humanist library. He died at Medvedgrad in 1472.

Miklós Toldi (c. 1320–1390) was a Hungarian nobleman of Bihar County famed in folklore for superhuman strength. Long thought legendary, royal charters show he served Charles I and Louis I: in 1354 as viscount and castellan of Pozsony County, and in 1383 and 1385 as count of Szabolcs County.

As a mercenary captain in Louis the Great's Italian campaigns he brought two lion cubs back from Florence in 1359 at the king's request. He died in 1390.

Mark of Kalt (Hungarian: Márk Kálti; fl. 1336–1368) was a Hungarian Franciscan friar and chronicler born into the lesser nobility of Veszprém County. He was chaplain to Queen Elizabeth of Poland and later a parish priest in Buda and provost of Kő, before entering the service of Louis I.

For Louis I he wrote the Latin Chronicon Pictum in 1358, an illustrated history of Hungary whose 147 miniatures were finished between 1370 and 1373. He likely died before the manuscript was completed.

en:
Balázs Magyar (c. 1410–c. 1490) was a Hungarian general, a follower of John Hunyadi who became a leading captain of Matthias Corvinus's Black Army. From 1470 he guarded the southern marches and held senior commands, including Voivode of Transylvania in 1472–1475, supporting Moldavia against the Ottomans.

He fought the Hussites in Bohemia and helped take Veglia in 1479, though the island could not be held against the Venetian fleet. In 1480 he led a force to Italy that recaptured Otranto from the Turks.

He retired to western Hungarian estates and died at Kassa in 1490. His daughter Benigna and her husband Pál Kinizsi inherited his property.

鲍拉日·马扎尔（约1410—约1490）是匈牙利将领，早年追随匈雅提·亚诺什，后来成为马加什·科尔温黑军的主要统帅之一。1470年起他守卫南部边疆，历任要职，1472至1475年任特兰西瓦尼亚总督，支持摩尔达维亚抵御奥斯曼人。

他曾在波希米亚与胡斯派作战，1479年参加攻取克尔克岛，但该岛未能抵挡威尼斯舰队。1480年他率军前往意大利，从奥斯曼人手中收复奥特朗托。

晚年他退隐西匈牙利的庄园，1490年在考绍去世。他的女儿贝尼格纳与女婿保尔·基尼日继承了他的财产。

en:
Pál Kinizsi (1432–1494) was the most celebrated general of Matthias Corvinus's Black Army, of obscure origins, holder of Nagyvázsony castle from 1472. In October 1479 he and István Báthory won a decisive victory over an Ottoman invasion at the Battle of Breadfield in Transylvania.

From 1484 he was Count of Temes and Captain-General of the southern marches, and he never lost a battle in his career. After Matthias died in 1490 he backed Vladislas II and crushed the Black Army's mutinous remnants. He married Benigna, daughter of Blaise Magyar, suffered a stroke and died in 1494.

en:
Johannes Honterus (1498–1549) was a Transylvanian Saxon humanist and Protestant reformer born in Brassó. After taking his master of arts degree at Vienna in 1525, the Ottoman advance of 1529 drove him west to Kraków and Basel, where he published a Latin grammar and a cosmography manual, practiced wood engraving and printed the first published map of Transylvania, based on information gathered on visits home.

Back home from 1533, he ran a printing house and school in Brassó and led the Transylvanian Saxons into the Lutheran Reformation, organizing their Evangelical church.

en:
Adam František Kollár (1718–1783) was a Slovak jurist, historian and linguist. After joining the Jesuits and studying Eastern languages in Vienna he left the order, entered the Imperial-Royal Library as a scribe in 1748 and became its chief librarian in 1774.

As adviser to Empress Maria Theresa, he supplied historical arguments for her centralist reforms and, in 1772, for Habsburg claims to Galicia and Dalmatia. His writings on the monarchy's peoples gave ethnology its first formal definition in 1783, and he is counted among the earliest pan-Slavic writers. He died in Vienna that year.

Muhammad ibn Falah (1400–1461) was a Shi‘a theologian born in Wasit, Iraq, who founded the millenarian Musha‘sha‘iya sect. Educated at the Shia center of al-Hillah, he proclaimed himself the earthly representative of Imam Ali and the Mahdi and was denounced as an unbeliever; his Qur'an-style revelations were collected as the Kalam al-Mahdi.

In 1442 he established himself at Hoveizeh in Khuzestan. Claiming descent from Imam Musa al-Kazim, he died there in 1461 and was succeeded by his son.

Mirza Shah Hossein, in full Mirza Kamal al-Din Shah Hossein Isfahani (died 1523), was a Persian statesman of the early Safavid Empire and a native of Isfahan. Trained as an architect, in 1503 he became vizier to the Qizilbash governor Durmish Khan Shamlu.

After the Battle of Chaldiran in 1514, he found Shah Ismail I's favorite wife, lost in Azerbaijan, and the shah named him vakil (vicegerent) and vizier. In 1515 he protested the Portuguese conquest of Hormuz, seeking an alliance and gunners.

A close favorite of the withdrawn shah, he amassed power and in 1521 forced his old master Durmish Khan out to Herat. In April 1523 angry Qizilbash chiefs murdered him.

米尔扎·沙·侯赛因，全名米尔扎·卡迈勒丁·沙·侯赛因·伊斯法哈尼（卒于1523年），是萨法维帝国初期的波斯政治家，伊斯法罕本地人。他本是建筑师，1503年成为奇兹尔巴什总督杜尔米什汗·沙姆鲁的维齐尔。

1514年查尔迪兰战役后，他找到了沙阿伊斯梅尔一世在阿塞拜疆失散的宠妻，沙阿任命他为瓦基勒（副王）兼维齐尔。1515年，他向葡萄牙使节抗议葡萄牙占领霍尔木兹，同时寻求结盟并请求派来炮手。

他深为消沉退隐的沙阿宠信，借机揽权，1521年把旧主杜尔米什汗排挤到赫拉特。1523年4月，愤怒的奇兹尔巴什首领将他杀害。

Abdi Beg Shirazi (1513–1580), who wrote under the pen name Novidi, was a poet, historian and administrator of Safavid Iran. Although known as Shirazi, he was probably born and raised in Tabriz and served as a secretary and accountant (mostawfi) in the chancery of Shah Tahmasp I.

en:
Sir Anthony Shirley (1565–c. 1635) was an English adventurer and diplomat, second son of Sir Thomas Shirley. After fighting in the Netherlands and France, Henry IV made him a knight of St Michael in 1593, prompting Elizabeth I to investigate his foreign oath.

In 1598 he sailed with his younger brother Robert to Shah Abbas I's court, receiving the title Mirza Antonio. In 1599 Abbas sent him to Europe to seek an anti-Ottoman alliance; the embassy visited Moscow without result, and Elizabeth I barred his return to England.

He later served the Habsburgs and Spain as the self-styled Count of the East, and died in poverty in Madrid.

Robert Shirley (c. 1581–1628) was an English traveller and adventurer, third son of Thomas Shirley. In 1598 he went with his brother Anthony to Safavid Persia, where he trained Shah Abbas I's army and reorganized its artillery on the English model, helping Persia match the Ottomans in the war of 1603–1612. In 1607 he married the Circassian Sampsonia.

In 1608 Abbas sent him to seek a European alliance against the Ottomans. He visited Poland-Lithuania and Rome, and the emperor and pope made him a count. He returned to Persia in 1613 and died at Qazvin in 1628, soon after returning again with the English embassy.

Khvajeh Ali Safavi, also called Khvajeh Ali Siyahpush (c. 1370–1427), was the third head of the Safavid Sufi order at Ardabil, succeeding his father around 1391. Grandson of founder Safi al-Din Ardabili, he led it through the age of Timur.

Tradition credits him with saving Tatar tribes of Sham from Timur's vengeance; they became followers later known as the Qizilbash. Under him the order turned decisively to popular Shi'ism. He died in 1427 and was succeeded by his son Ibrahim Shah.

Iskandar Beg Munshi (1561/1562–1633/1634), whose name means Alexander Beg the Scribe, was an Iranian court chronicler of Safavid Iran. Born into a Turkoman clan of the Qizilbash, he and his elder brother chose the royal bureaucracy over the army.

He trained as a scribe in the later reign of Shah Tahmasp I. He is chiefly remembered for his history, the Tarikh-e Alam-ara-ye Abbasi, which narrates early Safavid rule, above all the reign of Shah Abbas I.

en:
William Adams (1564–1620) was an English navigator who reached Japan in April 1600 aboard the Liefde, the sole survivor of a five-ship Dutch expedition, and became the first Englishman in the country. At Limehouse he spent twelve years learning shipbuilding and navigation.

Summoned before Tokugawa Ieyasu, he became the shōgun's foreign-affairs adviser and built Japan's first Western-style sailing ship, completed in 1604. Granted samurai rank and an estate on the Miura Peninsula, he took the name Miura Anjin, led red-seal voyages to Siam and helped open the English factory at Hirado.

The Tokugawa authorities refused to let him leave for over a decade; when finally allowed to return to England, he stayed. He died at Hirado in 1620.

威廉·亚当斯（1564—1620）是英格兰航海家，1600年4月乘荷兰五船探险队中唯一幸存的“慈爱号”漂流到日本，成为最早抵达日本的英格兰人。他曾在莱姆豪斯学习造船与航海术达十二年。

他被德川家康召见后担任幕府的外交顾问，主持建造日本第一艘西式帆船，于1604年完工。他获赐武士身份与三浦半岛的领地，得名三浦按针，此后率领朱印船远航暹罗，并协助在平户开设英国商馆。

德川当局十余年间不许他离开日本；后来获准返回英格兰时，他选择留下。1620年，他卒于平户。

Gedeon Chetvertinsky (1634–1690) was a Ruthenian prince and Orthodox hierarch born in Volhynia. In 1659 he became bishop of Lutsk and Ostroh, but after clashing with the Uniate Church he fled to Baturyn in 1684 under Hetman Ivan Samoilovych's protection.

In 1685 a Kyiv synod proclaimed him metropolitan, and that October Patriarch Joachim of Moscow installed him as Metropolitan of Kyiv, Galicia and all Ruthenia. In 1686 Constantinople permitted Moscow to control Kyiv's metropolitans. After Samoilovych's fall, he lost the style of all Ruthenia in 1688, and he died at Kyiv in 1690.

Ivan Rutkovych (c. 1650–c. 1708) was a Ruthenian Baroque icon painter, born near Zolochiv in the Lviv region. He worked chiefly at Zhovkva and Univ and is regarded as founder of the Zhovkva school of icon painting and wood carving, making iconostases for village wooden churches with other masters.

His seven-row iconostasis for the Church of the Nativity in Zhovkva (1697–1699), now in the Lviv National Museum, is counted a masterpiece of Ukrainian art. Blending Byzantine tradition with secular, realistic European influences, he died between 1703 and 1708.

Phillippe de Longvilliers de Poincy (1584–1660) was a French nobleman and Bailiff Grand Cross of the Knights of Malta. In 1638 he sailed to the Caribbean as lieutenant governor of the French Isles of America, ruling Saint Christopher from 1639.

He ruled almost independently: he seized Saint-Barthélemy in 1648, occupied Saint-Martin, and refused entry to his appointed successor in 1644, eventually sending him back to France in chains. In 1651 he persuaded the Knights to buy the four islands. He built up Basseterre and the Château de la Montagne, and died on Saint Kitts in 1660.

Giovanni Paolo Lascaris (1560–1657) was an Italian nobleman of the Counts of Ventimiglia, related to the Lascaris emperors of Nicaea, and the 57th Grand Master of the Knights of Malta. He entered the Order of St John in 1584 and served as ambassador to Spain in 1632. In 1636 he became Grand Master.

He fortified Malta with the Lascaris coastal watchtowers (1637–1652), and in 1651 the Order bought four Caribbean islands. He guarded the Order's independence against Spain and France, and died on Malta in 1657 aged 97.

Giacomo Bosio (1544–1627) was an Italian knight of the Order of St John and its first historian. Born at Chivasso near Turin to a Milanese noble family long serving the Order, he went to Rome in 1587 as the Order's representative at the Holy See.

He wrote his forty-book history of the Hospitallers, from their origins to the siege era of Jean de la Valette in 1571, printed in three folio volumes in 1621, later translated into French and continued to 1688 by Bartolomeo dal Pozzo. He died at Rome in 1627.

He wrote his forty-book history of the Hospitallers, from their origins to the siege era of Jean de la Valette in 1571, printed in three folio volumes in 1621, later translated into French and continued to 1688 by Bartolomeo dal Pozzo. He died at Rome in 1627.
zh:
贾科莫·博西奥（1544—1627）是意大利的医院骑士团骑士，也是该修会最早的史家。他生于都灵附近的基瓦索，出身一个长期为骑士团效力的米兰贵族家庭，1587年作为骑士团驻教廷代表前往罗马。

他撰写了四十卷本的医院骑士团史，叙事起自修会起源，止于1571年让·德·拉瓦莱特的时代，于1621年以三卷对开本印行，后来被译成法语，并由巴尔托洛梅奥·达尔波佐续写至1688年。1627年他在罗马去世。

en:
Ch'oe Musŏn (1325–1395) was a Goryeo general and inventor who gave Korea its first domestic gunpowder. As wokou pirates raided Goryeo's coasts and inland, he traced the three ingredients of powder and, after years of failed experiments, bribed the Chinese merchant Li Yuan for the manufacturing secret, producing gunpowder between 1374 and 1376.

In 1377 the court set up an official firearms bureau, where he devised shipboard cannons, hand cannons and rocket arrows; in 1380 his guns helped sink over five hundred pirate ships at Jinpo. After the founding of Joseon he retired and died in 1395, and King Taejo granted him an honorary office posthumously.

崔茂宣（1325—1395）是高丽末年的将领与火器发明家，使朝鲜半岛第一次实现火药自产。当时倭寇劫掠沿海、深入内陆，他探明火药的三种原料，又在多年试验失败后贿赂中国商人李元，求得配制秘方，于1374至1376年间试制出火药。

1377年朝廷设立官方火器机构，他在其中研制出舰载火炮、手铳与火箭；1380年，他的火炮在镇浦协助击沉倭寇战船五百余艘。朝鲜王朝建立后，他退隐并于1395年去世，太祖在他身后追赠官职。

Mun Ik-chŏm (1329–1398) was a Goryeo civil official and Neo-Confucian scholar from Gangseong-hyeon near Jinju in Gyeongsang Province. After passing the civil service examination in 1360, he accompanied a diplomatic mission to Yuan China in 1363.

Although the Yuan banned the export of cotton seeds, he brought home cotton seed and, helped by a Chinese monk, began growing cotton, introducing cotton cultivation to Korea. He died in 1398; in 1440 King Sejong posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis Fumin.

当时元朝禁止棉种出境，他仍将棉花种子带回国内，并在一名汉僧帮助下开始植棉，棉花种植由此传入朝鲜半岛。他于1398年去世，1440年朝鲜世宗追封他为富民侯。

Heo Nanseolheon (1563–1589), personal name Cho-hui, was a Joseon poet and painter of the Yangcheon Heo clan in Gangneung. A child prodigy, her Chinese verse written at age eight was hailed as the work of an immortal maiden. Her elder brother Heo Bong and younger brother Heo Gyun, author of The Tale of Hong Gildong, guided her education.

She composed some two hundred poems in Chinese. Married to Kim Seongnip, she suffered an unhappy marriage and the death of both children, and died of illness on March 19, 1589, aged twenty-seven.

许兰雪轩（1563—1589），本名楚姬，是朝鲜王朝中期的女诗人、女画家，出身江陵的阳川许氏。她自幼有神童之名，八岁时写的汉文诗即被誉为仙女手笔。兄长许篈与弟弟许筠——《洪吉童传》的作者——先后指导她治学。

她留有约两百首汉文诗。她嫁给金成立后婚姻不幸，一子一女先后夭折，本人于1589年3月19日病逝，终年二十七岁。

Radvila Astikas (died 1477), baptized Nicholas, was a Lithuanian magnate and founder of the Radziwiłł family. Twice Grand Marshal of Lithuania and a leading member of the Council of Lords, he led embassies to the Teutonic Knights and the Golden Horde. In 1447 he received Kėdainiai from Casimir Jagiellon and developed it into a trading town.

In 1473 he joined negotiations defining Lithuania's border with Livonia, and later served as voivode of Trakai and castellan of Vilnius before his death in 1477.

拉德维拉·阿斯季卡斯（?—1477），洗礼名尼古拉斯，是立陶宛大贵族、拉齐维乌家族的始祖。他两度出任立陶宛大司马，是贵族会议的核心成员，多次受命出使条顿骑士团和金帐汗国。1447年他获卡齐米日·雅盖隆契克赐予凯代尼艾，并将其经营成通商市镇。

1473年他参与划定立陶宛与利沃尼亚边界的谈判，后来历任特拉凯总督和维尔纽斯城主，1477年去世。

en:
Jonas Goštautas (c. 1393–1458) was a magnate of the Goštautai family in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. He first served as a marshal under Vytautas the Great and became voivode of Trakai in 1433.

In 1440 he helped the Council of Lords proclaim Casimir Jagiellon Grand Duke of Lithuania against the wishes of Polish magnates, dissolving the personal union with Poland. As Chancellor from 1443, he held power beside the young Grand Duke.

He expanded the powers of the Council of Lords, but after a failed 1456 plot to replace Casimir with Simeon Olelkowicz he died in Vilnius in 1458.

约纳斯·戈什陶塔斯（约1393—1458）是立陶宛大公国戈什陶塔伊家族的大贵族。他早年任维陶塔斯大帝的典礼官，1433年成为特拉凯总督。

1440年，他协助贵族会议拥立卡齐米日·雅盖隆契克为立陶宛大公，违背波兰贵族的意愿，瓦解了两国的共主关系。1443年起他出任大公国宰相，在年幼的大公身边掌握实权。

他扩大了贵族会议的权力；1456年图谋以谢苗·奥列尔科维奇取代卡齐米日失败，1458年于维尔纽斯去世。

Martynas Mažvydas (1510–1563) was a Protestant writer who produced the first printed book in Lithuanian. Persecuted for his Lutheran beliefs, he entered the university in Königsberg in 1546 at Duke Albrecht of Prussia's invitation. In 1547 he and his collaborators published The Simple Words of Catechism, based on Martin Luther's Small Catechism.

From 1549 he served as priest and from 1554 as archdeacon of Ragainė, issuing further Lithuanian hymns and prayer books until his death in Königsberg in 1563.

Franciszek Smuglewicz (1745–1807) was a Polish-Lithuanian painter and founder of the Vilnius school of art. Born in Warsaw to painters, he trained in Rome from 1763 under Anton von Maron and adopted Neo-Classicism during twenty-one years in Italy. Returning to Warsaw in 1784, he opened a school and won fame with historical canvases such as The Meeting of the Four Years' Sejm (1793) and Kościuszko's Oath at Kraków (1797).

In 1797 he moved to Vilnius to lead the Institute of Sketch and Painting at the Vilnius Academy, teaching there until his death in 1807.

弗朗齐谢克·斯穆格莱维奇（1745—1807）是活跃于波兰与立陶宛的画家，维尔纽斯画派的奠基人。他生于华沙的绘画世家，1763年赴罗马师从安东·冯·马伦，在意大利的二十一年间接受了新古典主义风格。1784年回到华沙后，他开办学校，以《四年议会开会》（1793年）和《柯斯丘什科在克拉科夫宣誓》（1797年）等历史题材油画成名。

en:
Balthasar Russow (1536–1600) was a Livonian chronicler and Lutheran pastor, born in Reval, now Tallinn. Educated in Pomerania, he served from 1566 until his death as pastor of the Estonian congregation at the Holy Spirit Church in Reval.

He is famous for his Low German Chronica der Provinz Lyfflandt, which relates the decline of the Livonian Order and the Livonian War of 1558–1583. First printed at Rostock in 1578, the work denounces the immorality of the Livonian nobility and the superstitions of Estonian peasants, while praising Swedish rule.

en:
Maulana Malik Ibrahim, later known as Sunan Gresik, was the first of the Wali Songo, the nine missionaries credited with bringing Islam to Java. A native of Kashan in Persia, he preached for thirteen years in Champa, marrying a king's daughter and fathering Sunan Ampel. In the late fourteenth century he settled near Gresik in Majapahit Java.

His equal treatment of different castes won support among lower castes and led to conversions. He treated the sick and founded an Islamic boarding school after meeting the Majapahit ruler, and died at Gresik on 7 April 1419.

毛拉纳·马利克·易卜拉欣，后称苏南·锦石，是瓦利松戈九贤之首，相传正是这九位传教士将伊斯兰教传入爪哇。他生于波斯卡尚，先在占婆传教十三年，娶当地国王之女，生子苏南·安佩尔。14世纪末，他定居满者伯夷治下爪哇的锦石附近。

en:
James II (c. 1438–1473), called the Bastard, was the illegitimate son of King John II of Cyprus. He became Archbishop of Nicosia in 1456 but lost the see after killing the royal chamberlain. When John II died in 1458, the crown passed to James's half-sister Charlotte. In 1460, backed by the Egyptian Mamluk sultan, James invaded, blockaded Charlotte in Kyrenia for three years, and was crowned king by 1464.

Seeking Venetian support, he married Catherine Cornaro in 1468. James died in 1473 amid rumours of Venetian poisoning, leaving his pregnant wife as regent.

Amir Husain al-Kurdi, known to the Portuguese as Mirocem, was the leading Mamluk naval commander under Sultan Qansuh al-Ghuri and governor of Jeddah, whose fortifications he raised to secure the Red Sea pilgrimage route against the Portuguese.

In 1508 he joined the Gujarati admiral Malik Ayyaz to defeat and kill Lourenco de Almeida at Chaul. The next year Francisco de Almeida avenged his son by crushing Husain's fleet at Diu. In 1517 he helped an Ottoman squadron repel the Portuguese from Jeddah. He died later that same year.

en:
Shams al-Din al-Sakhawi (1428–1497) was a Shafi'i scholar of hadith and history, and the leading student of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, whose biography he later wrote. A prolific author, he compiled al-Daw' al-Lami, a vast biographical dictionary of the notable figures of his century, and added a supplement to al-Maqrizi's chronicle of the Mamluk sultans.

He recorded the marital histories of five hundred women in Egypt and observed that at least a third of women in Egypt and Syria married more than once. He died in Medina.

沙姆斯丁·萨哈维（1428—1497）是沙斐仪派圣训学者和史家，也是伊本·哈贾尔·阿斯卡拉尼的得意门生，后来还为其师撰写了传记。他著述宏富，编纂了收录同时代名人的大型传记辞典《灿烂之光》，并为塔基丁·马克里齐的马穆鲁克苏丹编年史撰写续编。

他在埃及记录了五百名女性的婚姻史，并观察到埃及和叙利亚至少三分之一的女性结过不止一次婚。他最终在麦地那去世。

en:
Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (1372–1449), born Ahmad ibn Ali in Cairo, was the foremost Shafi'i scholar and hadith master of his age. Orphaned in infancy, he was sent to study the Qur'an at five and had memorised it by nine. In 1397 he married Uns Khatun.

He produced roughly 150 works, above all Fath al-Bari, his classic commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari, which earned him the epithet Hafiz of the Time. When he died in Cairo in 1449, the Abbasid caliph led his funeral prayer and about fifty thousand mourners attended.

Jamal al-Din Yusuf, known as Ibn Taghribirdi (1411–1470), was an Egyptian historian born in Cairo into the Mamluk military elite; his father was a leading amir. He studied law and history under Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, while mastering horsemanship, poetry and Turkish. His wealth freed him from earning a living, and his connections with amirs and the court gave him access to information.

He wrote twelve historical works, above all the multi-volume annalistic chronicle al-Nujum al-zahira, which records Egypt's rulers from the Islamic conquest to 1467 with precise dates.

贾迈勒丁·优素福，世称伊本·塔格里比尔迪（1411—1470），是生于开罗的埃及史家，出身马穆鲁克军事权贵之家，父亲是高级埃米尔。他师从伊本·哈贾尔·阿斯卡拉尼学习教法与历史，同时精通骑术、诗歌与突厥语。他家境富有，无需为生计工作，与埃米尔和宫廷的交往让他得以获取史料。

他撰有十二部史书，代表作是多卷本编年史《灿烂星辰：埃及与开罗诸王志》，以精确日期记述自伊斯兰征服至1467年的历代埃及统治者。

Heshen (1750–1799), born Shanbao, was a Manchu official of the Niohuru clan in the Qing dynasty. He studied at the Xian'an Palace school, learning four languages. He entered palace service as an imperial guard in 1772 and caught the eye of the Qianlong Emperor, who promoted him into the Grand Council in 1776.

Over more than twenty years he amassed a vast fortune through bribes and married his son to the emperor's favourite daughter. Within days of Qianlong's death in 1799, the Jiaqing Emperor charged him with corruption, seized his wealth, and ordered him to strangle himself.

Heinrich von Brühl (1700–1763) was chief minister of Saxony and Poland under Augustus III. A page at the Dresden court from 1719, he won the elector's trust when Augustus II died in 1733 and raised the money that secured Frederick Augustus II's election as Polish king. After 1738 he served as sole minister, controlling access to the king.

His diplomacy shaped the Diplomatic Revolution of 1756, but his ruinous finances left Saxony helpless before Prussia in the Seven Years' War. He died at Dresden weeks after Augustus III in 1763.

Gottfried Silbermann (1683–1753), born at Kleinbobritzsch in Saxony, was the outstanding German organ builder of the Baroque. He learned the craft in Strasbourg from his brother Andreas after 1702. He returned to Saxony in 1710 and opened his workshop at Freiberg, completing the grand organ of Freiberg Cathedral in 1714.

Appointed court organ builder to the Saxon elector in 1723, he built some fifty organs. He also made fortepianos after Cristofori's design from 1732, selling several to Frederick the Great, and died at Dresden in 1753.

en:
Andreas Karlstadt (1486–1541), born Andreas Bodenstein, was a radical theologian of the early Reformation. A professor at the University of Wittenberg, he defended Luther against Johann Eck at the Leipzig Debate of 1519. While Luther was in hiding in 1521–1522, Karlstadt led reform in Wittenberg, celebrating Mass in German and removing images.

In 1522 he married, breaking with clerical celibacy. Later in conflict with Luther and expelled from Saxony, he served as a minister before taking a post at Basel in 1534, where he died of the plague in 1541.

Johann Eck (1486–1543), born Johann Maier, was the foremost Catholic theologian to oppose Martin Luther. Ordained in 1508, he became a professor at Ingolstadt in 1510. He attacked Luther's ninety-five theses and then debated Karlstadt and Luther at the Leipzig Disputation of 1519, where he pressed Luther to deny the authority of pope and councils.

He then went to Rome and brought back the bull Exsurge Domine (1520) condemning Luther's writings. In 1530 he helped draft the Catholic Confutatio at Augsburg, and died at Ingolstadt in 1543.

Lucas Cranach the Elder (1472–1553), born in Kronach, Franconia, was the leading German painter and printmaker of the early Reformation; he took his surname from his birthplace. In 1504 Elector Frederick the Wise of Saxony made him court painter at Wittenberg, where he served the Saxon electors for the rest of his life. A close friend of Martin Luther, he ran a workshop producing portraits of Protestant princes, altarpieces and woodcuts.

A wealthy Wittenberg burgher who served twice as burgomaster, he joined John Frederick I in captivity after Mühlberg (1547) and died at Weimar in 1553.

Johann Melchior Dinglinger (1664–1731), born at Biberach in Swabia, was the most celebrated goldsmith of the Baroque age. Apprenticed in Ulm and trained as a journeyman in Augsburg and other cities, he settled in Dresden in 1692 and became court jeweller to Augustus the Strong of Saxony in 1698.

With his brothers he ran a great workshop, creating the Golden Coffee Service of 1701 and the Court of Delhi on the Birthday of the Grand Mughal Aurangzeb (1701–1708), a tableau of 132 enamelled gold figures. Augustus continued to commission his work even in wartime. Dinglinger died in Dresden in 1731.

Abraham Gottlob Werner (1749–1817) was a German geologist born in Silesia. After studying mining at Freiberg and Leipzig, he published On the External Characters of Minerals in 1774, the first modern textbook of descriptive mineralogy, and in 1775 became teacher of mining and mineralogy at the Freiberg Mining Academy.

There he taught that all rocks had crystallized from a primordial ocean, a doctrine called Neptunism, which drew students from across Europe. His demonstration of chronological succession in rock strata earned him the title father of German geology. He died in Dresden in 1817.

Johann Adolph Hasse (1699–1783) was a German composer born near Hamburg, the leading master of opera seria in his age. He began as a tenor in 1718; his first opera, Antioco, appeared at Brunswick in 1721, and he spent the 1720s in Naples studying under Alessandro Scarlatti.

In 1730 he married Faustina Bordoni and was appointed Kapellmeister at Dresden, becoming Oberkapellmeister in 1747. He frequently set libretti by Pietro Metastasio. The Seven Years' War scattered the court, and after his patron Augustus III died in 1763 he worked in Vienna before ending his life in Venice.

Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1646–1716), born in Leipzig, was a German polymath, mathematician and philosopher. From age seven he used his late father's library, reading philosophy and theology widely. After studying mathematics in Paris from 1672, he entered the service of the Brunswick dukes at Hanover in 1676 as councillor.

Independently of Newton he developed the calculus, and devised binary arithmetic and a mechanical calculating machine. In his Théodicée and Monadology he argued that this is the best of all possible worlds. Out of favour with George I, he died neglected in Hanover in 1716.

Georg Bartisch (1535–1607), born in Saxony, was a barber-surgeon and pioneering eye specialist. Apprenticed at thirteen, he spent years as an itinerant surgeon before settling in Dresden as court oculist to the Saxon electors. Though he had no academic medical training, he became a skilled practitioner of eye surgery.

In 1583 he published Ophthalmodouleia, the first comprehensive German textbook of ophthalmology, with woodcuts of eye diseases and instruments and the first printed account of removing a diseased eyeball. Skilled but superstitious, he held that astrology, witchcraft and magic had a place in medicine.

Facino Cane da Casale (1360–1412), born Bonifacio Cane, was an Italian condottiero. After early service under Charles of Durazzo, he hired his company to Verona, Padua and other lords. Captured by Padua in 1387, he entered its service until his cruelty led the marquess to dismiss him in 1397.

He entered Visconti service in 1401 and gained Alessandria. After Duke Gian Galeazzo's death in 1402, Facino controlled Milan for the duke's young sons, and was made count of Biandrate in 1406.

He died at Pavia in 1412. His widow Beatrice married Filippo Maria Visconti, who inherited his cities, treasure and soldiers.

1401年他转投米兰维斯孔蒂家族，获得亚历山德里亚。吉安·加莱亚佐公爵于1402年去世后，法奇诺为公爵年幼的儿子们掌控米兰，1406年受封比安德拉泰伯爵。

en:
Simone da Orsenigo was a fourteenth-century Lombard architect and builder, probably a native of Orsenigo near Como. He is remembered for his work on Milan Cathedral, where a document of 1387 names him its first general engineer and master.

He initially raised the structure in brick in the Lombard style. Replaced as engineer by Nicolas de Bonaventure in 1389, he kept working at the cathedral until 1395.

Jacopo Dal Verme (1350–1409) was an Italian condottiero born at Verona, the son of condottiero Luchino Dal Verme. He began his career as a condottiero before serving the Visconti of Milan almost continuously from 1379, becoming Gian Galeazzo Visconti's captain general.

He helped capture Bernabò Visconti in 1385, obtained Padua's surrender in 1387 and routed Jean III of Armagnac's French invasion army at Alessandria in 1391. He also helped win the battle of Casalecchio in 1402.

After Gian Galeazzo's death he defeated Facino Cane at Binasco. He switched to Venice in 1407 and died there in 1409.

en:
Dragoș, called Vodă or the Founder, is traditionally regarded as the first voivode of Moldavia. Moldavian chronicles relate that he came from Maramureș chasing an aurochs across the Carpathians and dismounted by the Moldova River; this dismounting became the legendary symbol of the principality's foundation. Most chronicles date his arrival to 1359.

He headed a Hungarian border march after Hungary's 1345 victory over the Golden Horde. Early sources credit him with founding Baia and Siret and inviting Saxon settlers, who introduced viticulture. He was succeeded by his son Sas. His grandson Balc was later expelled by Bogdan of Cuhea.

德拉戈什，人称沃德或奠基者，被传统视为摩尔多瓦首任沃伊沃德。摩尔多瓦编年史记载，他从马拉穆列什出发，翻越喀尔巴阡山追逐一头原牛，在摩尔多瓦河畔下马；这次下马成为公国奠基的传奇象征。多数编年史将他的到来定在1359年。

1345年匈牙利击败金帐汗国后，他担任一处匈牙利边疆领地的首领。早期史料称巴亚与锡雷特两城由他建立，他还邀来撒克逊移民，引入葡萄种植。他死后儿子萨斯继位。孙子巴尔克后来被库赫亚的博格丹驱逐。

en:
Mohammed al-Shaykh (c. 1490–1557), son of a Saadi leader, became the first sultan of the Saadian dynasty. After his father died in 1517 he and his brother Ahmad led the war against the Portuguese, taking Marrakesh in 1524.

By the Treaty of Tadla in 1527 the Saadians and Wattasids divided their territories, but the brothers later fell into conflict. He captured Agadir in 1541, forcing the Portuguese from their coastal towns, then seized Fez in 1549 and overthrew the Wattasids.

He lost Fez in 1554 but retook it after defeating the Wattasids at Tadla. While preparing an alliance with Spain against the Ottomans, he was assassinated by their agents in 1557.

穆罕默德·谢赫（约1490—1557）是萨阿德家族首领之子，后来成为萨阿德王朝的第一位苏丹。1517年父亲去世后，他与兄弟艾哈迈德共同领导对葡萄牙人的战争，1524年攻占马拉喀什。

1527年的塔德莱条约划分了萨阿德人与瓦塔斯人的势力范围，但兄弟二人后来发生冲突。1541年他攻克阿加迪尔，迫使葡萄牙人撤出沿海据点；1549年又攻取非斯，攻灭瓦塔斯王朝。

1554年他失去非斯，后来在塔德莱击败瓦塔斯势力，收复该城。1557年，他正筹划联合西班牙对抗奥斯曼人，被奥斯曼刺客杀害。

Abu Zakariya Yahya ibn Ziyan al-Wattasi (died 1448) was a Wattasid strongman and vizier of Marinid Morocco. As governor of Salé, he seized power at Fez after Sultan Abu Sa'id Uthman III was assassinated in 1420, installed the infant Abd al-Haqq II as sultan and ruled as regent.

He kept power after the sultan came of age in 1436. When Henry the Navigator's Portuguese army besieged Tangier in 1437, Abu Zakariya starved it into surrender, securing a treaty promising the return of Ceuta. The victory won him widespread support. He ruled until his death, founding the Wattasid line of viziers and sultans.

Dmitry Yuryevich Krasny (died 1440) was the youngest son of Yury of Zvenigorod and grandson of Dmitry Donskoy, prince of Galich-Mersky. In the Great Feudal War he backed his father's moderate line, making peace with Vasily II in 1433 and receiving Bezhetsky Verkh, though joining the march on Moscow in 1434.

In 1437 he and his brother Dmitry Shemyaka led the army Khan Ulugh Muhammad routed at Belyov, and he governed Moscow in 1439. He died at Bezhetsky Verkh in 1440 after a strange, wasting illness; the chronicler's details suggest arsenic poisoning.

Vasily Yuryevich Kosoy (c. 1403–1448), nicknamed the Squint, was the eldest son of Yury of Zvenigorod and prince of Zvenigorod from 1421. Dmitry Donskoy had placed Yury after Vasily I in the succession, but Vasily I passed the claim to his own sons.

When his father seized Moscow from Vasily II and died in 1434, Kosoy proclaimed himself grand prince. His brother Dmitry Shemyaka rejected him, joined Vasily II and drove him from the city in 1435. In 1436 Kosoy was defeated in Rostov province, captured and blinded, and he died in captivity in 1448.

en:
Raja Todar Mal (1523/1524–1589) was Akbar's finance minister and one of the nine Navaratnas. Born into a Hindu family in Awadh, he began as a clerk and was entrusted by Sher Shah Suri with building the fort of Rohtas in Punjab. He entered Mughal service after the fall of the Sur dynasty, later governing Gujarat.

As Akbar's dewan he overhauled the empire's land revenue, introducing standard measurements, the zabt assessment and a ten-year settlement, and his 1582–1584 decrees made Persian the language of Mughal administration. He rebuilt the Kashi Vishwanath temple in 1585 and died at Lahore in 1589.

拉贾·托达尔·马尔（1523/1524—1589）是阿克巴的财政大臣，也是宫廷九宝之一。他生于阿瓦德一个印度教家庭，早年任文书，后受舍尔沙·苏利之命修筑旁遮普的罗赫塔斯堡。苏尔王朝覆亡后他转入莫卧儿效力，曾任古吉拉特总督。

en:
Ustad Ahmad Lahori, also called Ahmad Mi'mar, Ahmad the Architect (c. 1570–1649), was a Persian-speaking architect and engineer serving the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. The emperor's official chronicle names him with Ustad Hamid among the planners of the Red Fort at Delhi, built from 1639 to 1648 as the centre of the new capital Shahjahanabad.

Ahmad is widely credited with designing the Taj Mahal at Agra, the marble mausoleum for Shah Jahan's wife, though the only explicit evidence is a poem by his son Lutfullah Muhandis. His three sons also became architects. Ahmad died in 1649.

乌斯塔德·艾哈迈德·拉合里，又称建筑师艾哈迈德·艾马尔（约1570—1649），是效力莫卧儿皇帝沙贾汉的波斯语建筑师与工程师。皇帝的官方编年史将他与乌斯塔德·哈米德并列为德里红堡的设计者：红堡建于1639至1648年，是新都沙贾汉纳巴德的核心。

en:
Luigi Vanvitelli (1700–1773), born in Naples to the Dutch painter Caspar van Wittel, was Italy's leading architect of the mid-eighteenth century, bridging Late Baroque and Neoclassicism. He began as a history painter, worked at St Peter's in Rome from 1724, and from 1733 built the lazaretto at Ancona.

In 1750 Charles VII of Naples summoned him; his 1751 design for the Royal Palace of Caserta, with four courtyards, a grand staircase and a park axis, became the largest palace of its age and occupied him until his death in 1773. His son Carlo completed the work.

Antonio Corradini (1688–1752) was a Venetian Rococo sculptor celebrated for marble figures draped in veils so thin that the body beneath stays visible. He trained under Antonio Tarsia in Venice.

In 1716–1717 he carved eighteen busts and two statues for Peter the Great's summer garden, and from 1733 served as court sculptor to Emperor Charles VI in Vienna. In 1744 he settled in Naples, summoned by Raimondo di Sangro to decorate the Sansevero Chapel, where in 1750 he finished La Pudicizia, the veiled tomb of the prince's mother. He died in Naples in 1752. His bozzetti later guided Giuseppe Sanmartino's Veiled Christ.

1716至1717年，他为彼得大帝的夏园雕刻了十八座胸像和两座雕像，1733年起在维也纳担任皇帝查理六世的宫廷雕塑家。1744年，他应雷蒙多·迪·桑格罗之召定居那不勒斯，负责圣塞韦罗礼拜堂的雕塑装饰，并于1750年完成亲王母亲的披纱陵墓《羞怯》。1752年他卒于那不勒斯。他留下的草稿后来指引朱塞佩·圣马尔蒂诺完成了《蒙面基督》。

Charles d'Artois (c. 1300–1346) was the illegitimate son of Robert the Wise of Naples, raised at the royal court. On his deathbed in 1343 Robert named him and Queen Sancia guardians of his granddaughters Joanna and Maria. Joanna I made him Chancellor of the Realm and Count of Sant'Agata de' Goti in 1345.

A leading plotter in the murder that September of her husband Andrew, he was condemned to death and fled with his eldest son to his county. Captured by his enemies, he died at Melfi in 1346, of stress or poison.

Jan Adriaenszoon Leeghwater (1575–1650), born at De Rijp in North Holland, was a Dutch millwright and hydraulic engineer. In 1605 he patented a diving bell for underwater work. He helped drain the Beemster, completed in 1612, and later the Purmer, Wormer and Schermer lakes.

In 1629 he drained the marshes around besieged 's-Hertogenbosch for the Dutch army, and his 1641 book urged draining the Haarlemmermeer. He also improved the rotating-cap windmill and died in Amsterdam.

Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (1632–1723) was a Dutch scientist born at Delft. After an apprenticeship at a linen-draper's in Amsterdam, he opened his own shop in Delft in 1654 and became a land surveyor in 1669.

Largely self-taught, he took up lens grinding and in the 1670s built single-lens microscopes achieving magnifications far beyond earlier lenses. He was the first to describe bacteria, protozoa, sperm cells and blood corpuscles, reporting his findings in some 560 letters to the Royal Society. He died at Delft in 1723, a founder of microbiology.

Pierre Bayle (1647–1706) was a French Huguenot philosopher, the son of a Calvinist minister. He converted to Catholicism at Toulouse in 1669, soon returned to Calvinism and fled to Geneva, then held the chair of philosophy at the Protestant Academy of Sedan from 1675.

In 1681 he fled to the Dutch Republic, becoming professor of philosophy and history at Rotterdam, where he lost the chair in 1693. His Historical and Critical Dictionary, published from 1697, deployed skepticism in defence of toleration and shaped the Enlightenment. He died in Rotterdam in 1706.

Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), born at Delft, was a Dutch humanist and jurist, a Leiden-trained prodigy. In 1609 he published Mare Liberum (The Free Sea), arguing the sea belonged to no state and was open to all trade, against Portuguese monopoly.

Amid religious disputes in the Dutch Republic, he was seized in 1618 and jailed for life in Loevestein Castle, but escaped in 1621 hidden in a book chest and fled to Paris.

There in 1625 he issued De Jure Belli ac Pacis, a foundation of modern international law. Later Swedish ambassador in France, he died at Rostock in 1645.

Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn (1606–1669) was a Dutch painter and printmaker. Born in Leiden to a miller, he trained in Amsterdam and opened a Leiden studio in 1625. He moved to Amsterdam in 1631 and became its leading portraitist, marrying Saskia van Uylenburgh in 1634.

Between 1640 and 1642 he painted The Night Watch. Saskia died in 1642, and his passion for collecting art forced him to declare insolvency in 1656; his collection was sold.

Undiminished, he painted late masterpieces including The Jewish Bride before dying in Amsterdam in 1669. About three hundred paintings and three hundred etchings survive.

困境中他仍画出《犹太新娘》等晚期杰作，1669年卒于阿姆斯特丹。存世的油画与蚀刻画各约三百幅。

Menno van Coehoorn (1641–1704) was a Dutch officer and military engineer. Commissioned in 1657, he was wounded defending Maastricht in 1673 during the Franco-Dutch War. The fall of Dutch fortresses in 1672 had exposed their weak defences.

He redesigned Dutch fortifications for the low, waterlogged terrain, relying on multiple lines and water defences, and was ranked with the French engineer Vauban as the age's leading siege expert.

As inspector general of fortifications, he strengthened the Barrier towns after the 1697 Treaty of Ryswick. He took Venlo, Bonn and Huy in 1702–1703 and died at The Hague on 17 March 1704.

他针对低湿地形重新设计荷兰防御工事，依托多道防线与水上设防，与法国工程师沃邦并称当时首屈一指的攻城筑城专家。

作为防御工事总监，他在1697年《赖斯韦克条约》签订后主持加固屏障城镇，又于1702至1703年攻取芬洛、波恩和于伊，1704年3月17日在海牙去世。

Willem Barentsz (c. 1550–1597) was a Dutch cartographer and navigator who led three expeditions seeking a Northeast Passage to China, believing the summer sun would melt the ice north of Siberia and leave a trade route open.

In 1594 he mapped Novaya Zemlya's west coast before ice drove him back, and a follow-up expedition in 1595 also failed. In May 1596 he sailed again, discovering Bear Island and Spitsbergen, but his ship was trapped off Novaya Zemlya, where the sixteen men wintered in a driftwood lodge, Het Behouden Huys.

In June 1597 the survivors set out in open boats; Barentsz died at sea on 20 June. The Barents Sea bears his name.

威廉·巴伦支（约1550—1597）是荷兰制图师与航海家，曾三次率领探险队寻找通往中国的东北航道。他相信夏日的阳光会融化西伯利亚以北的海冰，开辟一条贸易航道。

1594年，他测绘了新地岛西海岸，终因海冰被迫返航；1595年的后续探险同样失败。1596年5月他再度出航，发现了熊岛和斯匹次卑尔根，但船只在新地岛外海被困，十六人在一座浮木小屋“得救之屋”中过冬。

1597年6月，幸存者乘敞篷小船启程，巴伦支于6月20日在海上去世。巴伦支海即以他命名。

Frederick Coyett (c. 1615–1687) was a Swedish nobleman who served the Dutch East India Company. Born in Stockholm, he joined the company in 1643 and twice headed its Dejima trading post in Japan, in 1647–1648 and 1652–1653. Ennobled by Queen Christina in 1649, he became governor of Formosa in 1656.

In 1661–1662 Zheng Chenggong's nine-month siege of Fort Zeelandia forced his surrender and ended Dutch rule. Exiled to the Banda Islands in 1665, he was ransomed and pardoned in 1674, and died in 1687.

Pieter Post (1608–1669) was a Dutch Golden Age architect, painter and printmaker, baptised at Haarlem. His father was a stained-glass painter. With his collaborator Jacob van Campen he created the Dutch Baroque style of architecture, and together they designed the Mauritshuis in The Hague.

As painter and architect to Stadtholder Frederik Hendrik, he oversaw additions to the Noordeinde Palace from 1640 and built Huis ten Bosch from 1645. He died at The Hague, where he was buried on 8 May 1669.

Sigurd Jonsson (1390s–1452) was a Norwegian nobleman and knight, descended through the Sudreim family from King Haakon V. After the council deposed King Erik in 1440, he ruled Norway as drottsete during the interregnum, until Christopher of Bavaria was crowned in 1442. He commanded Akershus Fortress and led Norway's anti-Hanseatic policies.

When Christopher died in 1448, he again guarded the realm, declined the crown himself, and backed Christian I. Part of the council crowned the Swedish king Karl Knutsson instead, but Sigurd resisted him in southern Norway; Karl abandoned his claim and Christian was crowned in 1450.

西古尔德·荣松（1390年代—1452）是挪威贵族与骑士，出身苏德尔海姆家族，为国王哈康五世的后裔。1440年政务会议废黜国王埃里克后，他在王位空悬期以摄政身份统治挪威，直到1442年巴伐利亚的克里斯托弗加冕。他担任阿克斯胡斯城堡指挥官，并主导挪威的反汉萨政策。

Cort Sivertsen Adeler (1622–1675) was a Norwegian-born seaman who entered the Dutch navy at fifteen and fought at the Battle of the Downs in 1639. From 1642 he served aboard a Dutch ship hired by Venice, becoming its captain in 1645 and flag captain in 1650.

On 13 May 1654 his ship broke the Turkish galley line near the Dardanelles and sank fifteen galleys; Tenedos surrendered to him the following day. Ennobled by Denmark in 1666, he led the Dano-Norwegian fleet until his death at Copenhagen in 1675.

Ingerd Ottesdotter Rømer (c. 1475–1555), lady of Austrått, was the wealthiest landowner in sixteenth-century Norway. Heiress of the noble Rømer family, she married Nils Henriksson, who became Chancellor and High Steward of Norway; her Austrått estate made her daughters sought-after brides. Widowed in 1523, she worked through her powerful sons-in-law and opposed Archbishop Olav Engelbrektsson.

Later, she sheltered a claimant calling himself Nils Sture and planned to marry her daughter Eline to him and place him on Sweden's throne. She and her family promoted the Lutheran Reformation, and she died in a shipwreck in 1555.

Niels Henrikssøn Gyldenløve (c. 1455–1523) was a Norwegian knight and landowner, the son of national counselor Henrik Jensson. By marrying Ingerd Ottesdotter Rømer, heiress of Austrått in the Trondheimsfjord, he settled an inheritance feud over the great manor and became one of Norway's largest landowners. He and Ingerd had five daughters.

He joined the Council of the Realm around 1483 and remained central to the government until his death, taking the honorific title of High Steward in 1514 or 1515.

Karp was a fourteenth-century deacon in Pskov whom the chronicles name as the founder of the Strigolniki sect. He rejected the church hierarchy, monasticism and the fees charged for the sacraments, and taught that laymen might preach and perform the rites.

His following first grew in Pskov and then spread to Novgorod. The chronicles record that in 1375 or 1376 the Novgorodians drowned Karp, the deacon Nikita and a third follower in the Volkhov River.

卡尔普是14世纪普斯科夫的一名执事，被编年史称为剪裁派的创始人。他反对教会等级制度、修道制度和圣事收费，主张俗人也有讲道和施行圣事的权利。

他的信众先在普斯科夫壮大，随后传入诺夫哥罗德。编年史记载，1375或1376年，诺夫哥罗德人把卡尔普、执事尼基塔和另一名信徒投入沃尔霍夫河溺死。

en:
Marfa Boretskaya, known as Marfa the Mayoress (d. after 1478), was one of the wealthiest landowners of late fifteenth-century Novgorod and widow of the posadnik Isaak Boretsky. In the 1470s she led the boyar faction resisting Moscow.

In 1471 she and her sons negotiated Novgorod's submission to Casimir IV of Lithuania and invited Mikhailo Olelkovich to rule, provoking Ivan III's campaign; after the Battle of Shelon, her son Dmitry was executed and Fyodor was exiled in 1475. She continued intriguing with Lithuania until Ivan III annexed Novgorod in 1478, when she was taken to Moscow and her estates were seized.

玛尔法·博列茨卡娅，人称“女行政长官玛尔法”（1478年后去世），是15世纪末诺夫哥罗德最富有的地主之一，行政长官伊萨克·博列茨基的遗孀。1470年代，她领导波雅尔贵族派抵抗莫斯科。

1471年，她与儿子们同立陶宛的卡齐米日四世谈判，谋图让诺夫哥罗德归附立陶宛，并迎立米哈伊洛·奥列尔科维奇为统治者，由此招致伊凡三世出兵；舍隆河战役战败后，儿子德米特里被处死，费奥多尔于1475年被流放。她继续借立陶宛周旋，直至1478年伊凡三世吞并诺夫哥罗德，被押往莫斯科，地产被没收。

en:
Sarala Dasa was an Odia poet of the fifteenth century, the age of Gajapati Kapilendra Deva (d. 1466), honoured as the Adi Kabi, or First Poet, of Odia literature. Born into a farming family with little formal schooling, tradition tells that the goddess Sarala heard him singing while ploughing his father's field and granted him the gift of poetry.

He was the first major writer to compose in Odia rather than Sanskrit, giving ordinary readers the Sarala Mahabharata, the Vilanka Ramayana and the Chandi Purana.

萨拉拉·达萨是15世纪的奥里亚语诗人，生活在加贾帕蒂国王卡皮伦德拉·代沃（卒于1466年）的时代，被尊为奥里亚文学的“最初诗人”（阿迪·卡比）。他出身农家，几乎没有受过正规教育。相传他耕种父亲的田地时唱歌，萨拉拉女神听见后赐予他作诗的才能。

他是最早以奥里亚语而非梵文进行创作的重要诗人，为普通读者写下《萨拉拉摩诃婆罗多》《维兰卡罗摩衍那》和《昌迪往世书》。

en:
Achyutananda Dasa was a sixteenth-century Odia poet, seer and Vaishnava saint, later called the Mahapurusa, or Great Person. Born into a Karana family, the son of an official of the Gajapati king Prataparudra Deva (r. 1497–1538), he formed the Panchasakha, five comrades who rendered Sanskrit scriptures into Odia for common readers.

The most prolific of the five, he composed the Harivamsa, Kaibarta Gita and Gurubhakti Gita, along with prophetic writings, and was believed to see past, present and future. His writings described contemporary society.

阿丘塔南达·达萨是16世纪的奥里亚语诗人、先知与毗湿奴派圣人，后世尊为“大士”（摩诃普鲁沙）。他出身卡拉纳家庭，父亲是加贾帕蒂国王普拉塔帕鲁德拉·代沃（1497—1538年在位）的属官。他与四位同道并称“五友”（潘查萨卡），将梵文经典译为奥里亚语，供平民诵读。

en:
Kapilendra Deva (died 25 November 1466) founded the Suryavamsa Gajapati Empire of Odisha. A commander under the last Eastern Ganga king, Bhanudeva IV, he took power as the dynasty collapsed and became Gajapati. He drove off invasions by the Jaunpur and Bengal sultanates and sent his son Hamvira south to extend Odisha's rule; under him the empire stretched from the Ganga to the Kaveri.

He reduced taxes and warned nobles against oppressing the people. A patron of Jagannath worship and Odia letters, he was succeeded by his youngest son Purushottama Deva, whose succession led to civil war with Hamvira.

卡皮伦德拉·代沃（卒于1466年11月25日）是奥里萨太阳族加贾帕蒂帝国的建立者。他本是东恒伽王朝末代国王巴努提婆四世麾下的将领，在王朝崩溃之际掌权，称“加贾帕蒂”。他击退江布尔与孟加拉苏丹国的入侵，又派儿子哈姆维拉南下开拓；在他治下，奥里萨疆域北起恒河、南至高韦里河。

他减轻赋税，告诫贵族不要压迫百姓。他崇奉贾格纳特、扶持奥里亚文学，去世后由幼子普鲁肖塔玛·代沃继位，继承问题引发了他与哈姆维拉之间的内战。

Purushottama Dasa (c. 1550–1600) was a sixteenth-century Odia poet and devotee of Jagannath, born into a Karana family in Puri district. A resident of Puri, he kept the accounts of the Jagannath temple and could describe its festivals from direct observation.

His poem Kanchi Kaveri, weaving King Purushottama Deva's Kanchi campaign and marriage together with legends of Jagannath, Krishna and Balarama, became a classic of Odia verse and was later translated into Bengali. He also wrote the puranic poem Ganga Mahatmya and several shorter devotional works.

他的长诗《甘吉—高韦里》把加贾帕蒂国王普鲁肖塔玛·代沃出征甘吉并迎娶公主的史事，与贾格纳特、黑天和大力罗摩的传说交织成篇，成为奥里亚语诗歌的经典，后来被译成孟加拉语。他还著有往世书题材的《恒河颂》及若干短篇虔诚诗作。

en:
Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522) was a German humanist and a distinguished Christian scholar of Greek and Hebrew. Born at Pforzheim, he learned Greek in Paris and lectured at Basel, later serving Count Eberhard of Württemberg as a diplomat. Ennobled in 1492, he learned Hebrew and published De Verbo Mirifico in 1494 and the kabbalistic dialogue De Arte Cabalistica.

When the Dominicans moved to destroy Jewish books, he defended Hebrew literature before the Inquisition. He later taught Hebrew at Ingolstadt and Tübingen and died at Stuttgart.

en:
Gian Pietro Carafa (1476–1559), of the Carafa family, was a rigid reforming churchman who became Pope Paul IV. As papal envoy in Spain he developed a hostility to Spanish rule that shaped his later policy.

Bishop of Chieti, he resigned in 1524 and founded the Theatine order with Saint Cajetan. A cardinal from 1536, he persuaded Pope Paul III in 1542 to establish the Roman Inquisition on the Spanish model.

Elected pope in 1555 over Charles V's opposition, he issued the first Index of Prohibited Books and, by the bull Cum nimis absurdum, ghettoized Rome's Jews. He died in 1559, hated by the Roman populace.

吉安·彼得罗·卡拉法（1476—1559）出身卡拉法家族，是作风强硬的改革派教士，后来成为教宗保罗四世。他担任教廷驻西班牙使节时形成了反对西班牙统治的立场，影响了日后的政策。

他曾任基耶蒂主教，1524年辞职，与圣嘉耶当共同创立戴蒂尼会。1536年他成为枢机，1542年劝说教宗保罗三世仿照西班牙宗教裁判所设立罗马宗教裁判所。

1555年他不顾查理五世反对当选教宗，任内发布第一部《禁书目录》，又颁行诏书将罗马的犹太人限制在隔都之中。1559年他去世时，罗马民众对他恨之入骨。

en:
Ignazio Danti (April 1536–1586), born in Perugia, came from a family of artists and scientists: his father, an architect and engineer, taught him painting and architecture. He entered the Dominican Order in 1555 and devoted himself to mathematics, astronomy and geography, teaching mathematics at Bologna before Pope Gregory XIII called him to Rome as pontifical mathematician.

Danti sat on the commission whose work produced the Gregorian calendar reform and supervised the forty frescoed regional maps of the Vatican's Gallery of Maps (1580–1581). In 1583 Gregory made him Bishop of Alatri, where he convoked a diocesan synod before his death on 10 October 1586.

伊尼亚齐奥·丹蒂（1536年4月—1586年）生于佩鲁贾，出身艺术与科学世家，父亲是建筑师兼工程师，教他绘画和建筑。1555年他加入多明我会，此后致力于数学、天文学与地理学，曾在博洛尼亚教授数学，后被教宗格列高利十三世召至罗马，任教宗数学家。

Giordano Bruno (February 1548–1600), born Filippo Bruno in Nola near Naples, entered the Dominican Order at seventeen and was ordained a priest in 1572. He demonstrated his famed mnemonic system before Pope Pius V.

Charged with heterodoxy, he fled Naples in 1576 and wandered Europe, teaching in Paris and London, where in 1584 he published Italian dialogues defending an infinite universe of suns circled by planets.

Denounced to the Venetian Inquisition in 1592, he was extradited to Rome in 1593 and tried for seven years. Refusing to recant, he was burned at the stake in the Campo de' Fiori on 17 February 1600.

焦尔达诺·布鲁诺（1548年2月—1600年）原名菲利波·布鲁诺，生于那不勒斯附近的诺拉，十七岁入多明我会，1572年受任神父。他曾在教宗庇护五世面前展示自己闻名的记忆体系。

1576年他因被控异端离开那不勒斯，辗转欧洲各地，曾在巴黎与伦敦讲学；1584年在伦敦出版意大利语对话集，主张宇宙无限、星辰皆是太阳并有行星环绕。

1592年他遭人告发，被威尼斯宗教裁判所逮捕，1593年引渡至罗马，受审七年。他拒绝放弃主张，1600年2月17日在罗马鲜花广场被处以火刑。

Gil Álvarez de Albornoz (1302/1303–1367) was a Castilian churchman and soldier, archbishop of Toledo from 1338. He fought against a Marinid invasion at the Battle of Río Salado in 1340. Made a cardinal in 1350, he was sent to Italy as legate by Pope Innocent VI in 1353, leading mercenary armies that reconquered most of the Papal States.

In 1357 he promulgated the Constitutiones Sanctæ Matris Ecclesiæ, which governed the Papal States until 1816. He founded Bologna's College of Saint Clement in 1364 and died in 1367.

Scipione Caffarelli-Borghese (1 September 1577–1633) was born in Artena. When his maternal uncle became Pope Paul V in 1605, Scipione was made a cardinal, granted the Borghese name, and as Cardinal Nephew ran the Vatican government and the family finances.

He amassed vast estates around Rome, his income reaching a hundred and forty thousand scudi by 1612. His use of papal funds for family investments caused resentment, and he often compelled owners to sell property at steep discounts.

A discerning patron, he championed Caravaggio and the young Bernini and built the Villa Borghese to hold his collection. He died in Rome on 2 October 1633.

他独具眼光，资助卡拉瓦乔与年轻的贝尼尼，并修建博尔盖塞别墅以陈列收藏。1633年10月2日他在罗马去世。

Iacopo Bussolari (1312–1380) was an Augustinian hermit friar born in Pavia. In 1356 he led a popular rising that drove the Beccaria family from the city, commanded the defence against Galeazzo II Visconti's siege, and set up a republican regime in Pavia.

When the Visconti took the city in 1359 he was imprisoned. Freed in 1373, he made his way to Ischia, where his brother was bishop, and died there in 1380.

Piotr Skarga (1536–1612) was born near Grójec in Mazovia and educated at the Kraków Academy. Ordained around 1564, he joined the Jesuits in Rome in 1569 and became a leading preacher of the Counter-Reformation in the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

After returning to Poland in 1571 he preached in several cities. In 1579 he became first rector of the Vilnius Academy, and his Lives of the Saints became one of the most-read Polish books. From 1588 he was first court preacher to King Sigismund III Vasa.

His Sejm Sermons of 1597 urged stronger royal power and reform, and he criticized religious tolerance and the power of the nobility. He died in Kraków in 1612.

《议会布道集》（1597年）呼吁强化王权、改革国政，也批评宗教宽容与贵族权力。1612年他在克拉科夫去世。

John III Sobieski (1629–1696) was born at Olesko to a Ruthenian voivode's family. He volunteered in 1648 to fight the Khmelnytsky Uprising.

He served through the Swedish Deluge and the wars against Muscovy and the Ottomans, rising to Grand Hetman of the Crown in 1668; his victory at Khotyn in 1673 made his name, and he was elected king in 1674.

In 1683 he led the Christian coalition that broke the siege of Vienna, earning the name Lion of Lechistan. His reign brought the Commonwealth stability after years of conflict. He died in 1696 and was buried at Wawel Cathedral.

他历经瑞典入侵的大洪水时代以及对莫斯科和奥斯曼的战争，1668年升任王冠大盖特曼，1673年在霍京大捷而声名大振，1674年被选为国王。

Bohdan Khmelnytsky (c. 1595–1657) was a Ruthenian noble probably born near Chyhyryn. After his father fell at the Battle of Cecora in 1620, he spent two years in Turkish captivity.

In 1648, with Crimean Tatar allies, he led the Zaporozhian Cossacks in a great uprising against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and created an independent Cossack hetmanate. In 1648–1649 his Cossacks massacred tens of thousands of Poles and Jews.

In 1654 he concluded the Treaty of Pereiaslav with the Russian tsar, placing Ukraine under Russian protection. He died at Chyhyryn on 6 August 1657.

Arend Dickmann (1572–1627) was a Dutch-born sailor, a native of Delft who from 1608 lived in Gdańsk as captain and owner of a merchant ship.

In 1626 he joined the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth navy in its war with Sweden, and on 24 November 1627 was made admiral and commander-in-chief. Four days later he led the fleet to victory at the Battle of Oliwa in Gdańsk Bay, his men boarding and capturing the Swedish galleon Tigern.

The battle also forced the Swedish ship Solen to be scuttled. Dickmann was killed on the Tigern's deck by a stray cannon shot, possibly from either side.

1626年波瑞战争期间，他加入波兰—立陶宛联邦海军，1627年11月24日获授海军上将军衔，出任舰队总司令。四天后，他率舰队在格但斯克湾的奥利瓦海战中取胜，部下跳帮俘获瑞典战船“虎号”。

Aleksander Józef Lisowski (c. 1580–1616) was a Polish noble whose family had settled in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. He first soldiered in the Moldavian wars, later joined the rokosz against King Sigismund III, and during Muscovy's Time of Troubles took service with False Dmitry II.

Georg Hewel was a wealthy Gdańsk merchant and shipowner who helped King Władysław IV build a royal fleet in the 1630s. He placed two of his own merchant ships at the king's disposal and bought others in his own name to conceal the king's plans.

Appointed the king's agent, he purchased ten more ships at royal expense. Together with his own vessels they formed the basis of the fleet, which later found a base on the Hel Peninsula.

en:
Esterka Małach, traditionally called Esterka, was a fourteenth-century Jewish woman whom the chronicler Jan Długosz, writing under the year 1356, named as the beloved mistress of King Casimir III the Great. Said to be the granddaughter of a merchant and physician of Opoczno, she was credited with prompting the king's favourable privileges for the Jews of Poland.

Długosz wrote that she bore the king two sons, Niemira and Pełka. In his chronicle Marcin Bielski wrote that Casimir set aside a Bohemian mistress and took Esterka in her place.

en:
Zawisza the Black of Garbów (c. 1379–1428) was a celebrated Polish knight who served Władysław II Jagiełło and Sigismund of Luxembourg as commander and diplomat. He fought at Grunwald in 1410 and won tournaments at Buda in 1412 and Perpignan in 1416.

At the Council of Constance he spoke in defence of Jan Hus. Captured at Kutná Hora in 1421, he was ransomed.

In 1428 he led a banner of 500 light horsemen in Sigismund's campaign against the Ottomans. At Golubac on the Danube his troops guarded the defeated army's retreat; he was killed in battle or executed in Ottoman captivity.

加尔博夫的黑扎维沙（约1379—1428）是当时享有盛誉的波兰骑士，以统帅和外交官身份效力于瓦迪斯瓦夫二世·雅盖沃和卢森堡的西吉斯蒙德。他1410年参加格伦瓦德之战，并在1412年布达和1416年佩皮尼昂的骑士比武中夺魁。

在康斯坦茨公会议上，他曾为扬·胡斯辩护。他于1421年在库特纳霍拉被俘，随后被赎出。

1428年他率领一支500人的轻骑兵队伍参加西吉斯蒙德对奥斯曼的战役，在多瑙河畔戈卢巴茨掩护败军撤退；他或战死沙场，或在奥斯曼囚禁中被处死。

en:
Zbigniew Oleśnicki (1389–1455) was Bishop of Kraków from 1423 and the most powerful churchman-statesman of fifteenth-century Poland. A royal secretary at twenty, he fought beside Władysław II Jagiełło at Grunwald in 1410.

He shaped crown policy under two Jagiellonian kings, governing as regent during Władysław III's minority and leading the legation to the Council of Basel in 1433. He opposed the Hussites, and in the 1430s a conflict led to a brief civil war. In 1439 he was made the first native Polish cardinal. He pressed Władysław III's Hungarian crusade, which ended at Varna in 1444. He died in 1455.

en:
Veit Stoss (before 1450–1533), in Polish Wit Stwosz, was a German sculptor probably born at Horb am Neckar, whose dramatic wood carvings stand between late Gothic and the Northern Renaissance. He settled in Nuremberg in 1473 and in 1477 moved to Kraków, where his workshop completed the huge altarpiece for St Mary's Basilica in 1489; he also made Casimir IV's tomb in Wawel Cathedral.

Back in Nuremberg from 1496, Stoss was branded for forgery in 1503 and pardoned by Emperor Maximilian in 1506. Vasari called his Florentine St Roch a miracle in wood.

en:
Martim Afonso de Sousa (c. 1500–1564) was a Portuguese nobleman born at Vila Viçosa and raised alongside the future John III. At court he studied mathematics, cosmography and geography.

In 1530 the king gave him command of an armada to drive the French from the Brazilian coast and begin permanent settlement. He patrolled against pirates, and in 1532 founded São Vicente, Brazil's first chartered town, becoming its first donatary captain.

Back in Portugal he led the home fleet, and from 1542 to 1545 served as governor of Portuguese India. He died in Lisbon on 21 July 1564.

John Methuen (1650–1706) was an English lawyer, member of Parliament and diplomat, born the son of a wealthy Wiltshire cloth merchant. Called to the Bar in 1674, he rose to be Master in Chancery and held office as both Lord Chancellor of Ireland and English ambassador to Portugal.

During the War of the Spanish Succession he negotiated the Methuen Treaty of 1703: English textiles were admitted into Portugal while Portuguese wines paid no more duty in England than French wine. The agreement bound the two economies for decades and made port an English staple.

Gaspar da Gama (c. 1444–c. 1510), also called Gaspar da Índia, was a Jewish merchant and linguist probably born in Poznań. In 1498 he boarded Vasco da Gama's returning fleet at Angediva Island. Suspected of being a spy, he was whipped and interrogated before being carried to Portugal and baptized with the admiral as his godfather.

Speaking Hebrew, Italian, Spanish and Indian tongues, he became an interpreter and guide to Portuguese fleets, sailing to India with Pedro Álvares Cabral in 1500 and again with Vasco da Gama in 1502.

en:
Fernão Lopes (c. 1385–after 1459) was Portugal's first royal chronicler and a founder of documentary historiography. Probably of humble Alentejo origins and self-educated, he was appointed head of the royal archives by John I in 1418, and in 1434 King Edward named him the realm's first cronista-mor, commissioning histories of the Portuguese kings.

His surviving chronicles cover the reigns of Peter I, Ferdinand I and John I, drawing on official documents rather than rhetoric. He completed the first two parts of John I's reign, leaving the third to his successor, and died sometime after 1459.

Bartolomeu Dias (c. 1450–1500) was a Portuguese mariner who in 1481 helped build the fort of São Jorge da Mina in the Gulf of Guinea.

Sent by John II to probe the southern African coast, he rounded the Cape of Good Hope in February 1488, becoming the first European known to sail from the Atlantic into the Indian Ocean.

He later helped design the ships used by Vasco da Gama in 1497. In 1500 he captained a vessel in Cabral's fleet, which reached Brazil, and drowned in a storm off the Cape on 29 May 1500.

巴尔托洛梅乌·迪亚士（约1450—1500）是葡萄牙航海家，1481年参与在几内亚湾修建圣若热·达米纳要塞。

受若昂二世派遣探查非洲南岸，他于1488年2月绕过好望角，成为已知第一个从大西洋驶入印度洋的欧洲人。

后来他参与设计了瓦斯科·达·伽马1497年使用的船只。1500年，他在卡布拉尔舰队中担任船长，随队抵达巴西，同年5月29日在好望角附近的风暴中溺亡。

António Raposo Tavares (1598–1658) was born in Alentejo and went to Brazil with his father in 1618, settling near São Paulo. In 1628 he led a bandeira of settlers and Tupi warriors against Jesuit-protected Guarani villages, taking thousands of captives and extending Portuguese rule east of the Uruguay River.

He fought the Dutch in the northeast in 1639–1642. His final bandeira, begun in 1648, covered more than ten thousand kilometres through the interior to Belém at the mouth of the Amazon. He returned to São Paulo and died in 1658.

en:
Nuno Álvares Pereira (1360–1431) was a Portuguese general, legitimized son of the prior of Crato. In the 1383 crisis he backed John, Master of Aviz, and after victory at Atoleiros in 1384 was made constable of Portugal, harassing the Castilian army besieging Lisbon until plague forced it to withdraw.

On 14 August 1385 he led an outnumbered army to decisive victory over Castile at Aljubarrota, securing the new Aviz dynasty, and won again at Valverde.

When hostilities ended he gave much of his wealth to veterans. After his wife died he entered a Carmelite convent as Frei Nuno de Santa Maria.

努诺·阿尔瓦雷斯·佩雷拉（1360—1431）是葡萄牙军事将领，为克拉托修道院长之子，后获承认为嫡出。1383年危机期间，他支持阿维什骑士团团长若昂；1384年阿托莱罗斯之战获胜后，他被任命为葡萄牙统帅，并袭扰围攻里斯本的卡斯蒂利亚军队，直到瘟疫迫使敌军撤退。

1385年8月14日，他率领兵力处于劣势的葡军在阿尔茹巴罗塔决战中决定性地击败卡斯蒂利亚军队，保住了新生的阿维什王朝，此后又在巴尔韦德再胜。

战争结束后，他将大部分财产赠予老兵。妻子去世后，他以“圣玛利亚的努诺”为名进入加尔默罗会修道院修道。

Nuno Gonçalves (c. 1425–c. 1491) was appointed court painter to King Afonso V of Portugal in 1450, knighted in 1470 and named official painter for Lisbon in 1471. His style shows the influence of Flemish masters such as Van Eyck and Van der Weyden.

His surviving masterpiece is the polyptych of the Saint Vincent Panels, a panorama of Portuguese society. He is regarded as the founder of painting in the Portuguese Renaissance.

Robert Burns (1759–1796), Scotland's national poet, was born at Alloway in Ayrshire, the son of a poor tenant farmer, and began writing songs while labouring on his family's farms. In July 1786, hoping to pay for passage to Jamaica, he published Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect at Kilmarnock; its success carried him to Edinburgh instead, where a second edition appeared in 1787.

He later farmed at Ellisland and worked as an exciseman in Dumfries, while composing and collecting songs such as Auld Lang Syne and Scots Wha Hae. He died at Dumfries in July 1796, aged 37.

David Beaton (c. 1494–1546) was the last Scottish cardinal before the Reformation and, from 1539, Archbishop of St Andrews. A trusted diplomat of James V, he led negotiations for the king's French marriages and championed the Auld Alliance against Henry VIII's pressure to break with Rome.

After James V's death in 1542 he claimed the regency for the infant Mary, Queen of Scots, on the basis of a will widely regarded as forged, but was imprisoned. In 1544 he became papal legate in Scotland, and in March 1546 he had the Protestant preacher George Wishart burned for heresy and was himself murdered in St Andrews Castle two months later.

en:
Sir George Bruce of Carnock (c. 1550–1625) was a Scottish merchant and mining engineer at Culross in Fife. He built Culross Palace and pioneered undersea coal mining at the Moat Pit, tunnelling under the Firth of Forth to the unheard-of depth of 40 fathoms, with drainage by a horse-driven chain of buckets. James VI visited in 1617 and emerged through a stone tower a quarter-mile offshore.

Bruce also ran salt pans exporting to England and Germany. The Moat Pit was flooded in March 1625, weeks before his death that May.

卡诺克的乔治·布鲁斯爵士（约1550—1625）是苏格兰商人、采矿工程师，在法夫的卡勒罗斯经营。他建造了卡勒罗斯宫，并首创海底采煤：坑井从陆地伸入福斯湾海底，深达此前闻所未闻的40英寻，并用马拉斗链排水。1617年詹姆斯六世亲临矿井，从离岸四分之一英里的一座石塔走出。

Dositej Obradović (1739–1811), born in Čakovo in the Banat, was a Serbian monk, writer and reformer. Taking the name Dositej at the Hopovo monastery in 1757, he left in 1760 and travelled widely across Europe and Asia Minor, where he encountered the German Enlightenment; his first book appeared in 1783.

Writing in the spoken vernacular instead of Church Slavonic, he became, with Vuk Karadžić, a father of modern Serbian literature. During the First Serbian Uprising he moved to Belgrade in 1807 as Serbia's first minister of education, founded the Velika škola in 1809, and died in Belgrade in 1811.

多西泰伊·奥布拉多维奇（1739—1811）出生在巴纳特的恰科沃，是塞尔维亚修士、作家与改革家。1757年他在霍波沃修道院出家，取法名多西泰伊，1760年离开修道院，游历欧洲和小亚细亚，接触到德国启蒙思想，1783年出版第一部著作。

他用民间口语而非教会斯拉夫语写作，与武克·卡拉季奇并称为现代塞尔维亚文学之父。第一次塞尔维亚起义期间，他于1807年前往贝尔格莱德出任塞尔维亚首任教育大臣，1809年创办大学校，1811年在贝尔格莱德去世。
