Palman (called Palman Bracht; c. 1290–after 1363) was a German knight born in Styria. After serving the Habsburgs, he set out for the Holy Land, entered Zeta and joined Stefan Dušan with his German followers, becoming captain of Dušan's Alemannic Guard of 300 men.

In 1331 he marched with Dušan from Skadar against Stefan Uroš III, and he later put down revolts in Zeta and northern Albania. He held Veria until John Cantacuzene retook it. He is last attested in 1363 and lives on in Serbian epic poetry.

帕尔曼（常称帕尔曼·布拉赫特，约1290—1363年后）是生于施蒂利亚的德意志骑士。他曾效力哈布斯堡家族，动身前往圣地途中进入泽塔，与德意志随从一同投效斯特凡·杜尚，成为杜尚麾下300人的阿勒曼尼卫队队长。

1331年，他随杜尚从斯库台出兵讨伐斯特凡·乌罗什三世，后来又平定泽塔和阿尔巴尼亚北部的叛乱。他据守韦里亚，直至约翰·坎塔库泽努斯夺回该城。史料最后于1363年提到他，他的形象也留存于塞尔维亚史诗中。

en:
Makarije Sokolović (16th century–1574) was the first patriarch of the restored Serbian Patriarchate of Peć. A kinsman of the Ottoman grand vizier Mehmed-paša Sokolović, he owed the patriarchate's 1557 restoration to the vizier's influence, after the see lapsed in 1463.

The sultan granted his patriarchate the rights of Constantinople; its jurisdiction extended beyond medieval Serbia into Bosnia and Dalmatia, with more than forty eparchies. His church renewed the Peć, Gračanica and Studenica monasteries. He resigned through illness in 1571 to his nephew Antonije and died in 1574; the Serbian Orthodox Church venerates him as a saint.

马卡里耶·索科洛维奇（16世纪—1574）是佩奇牧首区恢复后的首任塞尔维亚牧首。他是奥斯曼大维齐尔穆罕默德帕夏·索科洛维奇的亲属；1463年牧首区中断，1557年凭这位大维齐尔的影响得以恢复。

苏丹授予他的牧首区与君士坦丁堡同等的权利；辖区除中世纪塞尔维亚领土外，还包括波斯尼亚和达尔马提亚，下辖四十多个教区。他的教会重修了佩奇、格拉查尼察和斯图代尼察修道院。他因病于1571年让位给侄子安东尼耶，1574年去世，被塞尔维亚正教会尊为圣人。

Francesco di Giorgio Martini (1439–1501) was a Sienese painter, architect and military engineer, trained in Vecchietta's workshop. From the mid-1470s he served Federico da Montefeltro, Duke of Urbino, building nearly seventy fortifications, among the earliest star-shaped bastions, and designing Santa Maria delle Grazie church at Cortona.

His Trattato di architettura, completed after 1482, set out ideal-city plans and machines; Leonardo da Vinci owned and annotated a copy. He returned to Siena as city engineer in 1486, and in 1499 became capomaestro of Siena Cathedral.

弗朗切斯科·迪·乔治·马蒂尼（1439—1501）是锡耶纳画家、建筑师和军事工程师，学艺于韦基耶塔的作坊。从1470年代中期起，他为乌尔比诺公爵费德里科·达·蒙特费尔特罗效力，修筑近七十座防御工事，其中包括最早一批星形棱堡，并设计了科尔托纳的圣马利亚感恩教堂。

他的《建筑、工程与军事艺术论》在1482年后完成，绘有理想城市方案和机械图样，列奥纳多·达·芬奇曾收藏并批注过一个抄本。1486年他返回锡耶纳任城市工程师，1499年出任锡耶纳大教堂工程总监。

en:
Catherine of Siena (1347–1380), born Caterina di Jacopo di Benincasa, was the daughter of a Sienese cloth dyer who rejected marriage to join the Dominican mantellate as a mystic and ascetic. Her reputation gave her rare political weight: she helped persuade Pope Gregory XI to leave Avignon for Rome in 1376 and negotiated for peace between the papacy and Florence.

She dictated her major work, The Dialogue, in 1377–1378, then backed Urban VI in Rome during the Great Schism. She died in Rome in 1380 and was canonized in 1461.

锡耶纳的加大利纳（1347—1380），本名卡泰丽娜·迪·雅各波·迪·贝宁卡萨，是锡耶纳一名染工的女儿。她拒绝婚嫁，加入道明会的曼特拉特善会，过着神秘主义者的苦行生活。她的声望使她拥有罕见的政治影响力：1376年她帮助说服教宗格里高利十一世把教廷从法国亚维农迁回罗马，并受托为教廷与佛罗伦萨议和奔走。

1377至1378年她口授完成主要著作《对话录》，西方教会大分裂后又在罗马支持教宗乌尔巴诺六世。她于1380年在罗马去世，1461年被封圣。

en:
Pandolfo Petrucci (1452–1512) was the effective lord of Renaissance Siena. His family was exiled in 1456 after his uncle's failed plot and returned only in 1480. As captain of the city guard from 1495 he built his power, and after his brother's death in 1497 he eliminated his rivals, having his father-in-law killed in 1500, and ruled Siena as its undisputed master.

After plotting against Cesare Borgia he fled in 1503 and returned under French protection. In 1512 he ceded Montepulciano to Florence before dying, leaving Siena to his son Borghese.

潘多尔福·佩特鲁奇（1452—1512）是文艺复兴时期锡耶纳事实上的统治者。他的家族1456年因叔父的密谋败露而被放逐，1480年才返回。他自1495年起担任城防统领，借此积蓄权力；1497年继承兄长的官职后铲除异己，于1500年派人杀死岳父，成为锡耶纳无可争议的主人。

他因谋划反对切萨雷·博尔贾而于1503年出逃，后在法国保护下回国。1512年他将蒙特普尔恰诺割让给佛罗伦萨，同年去世，把锡耶纳留给儿子博格斯。

Abd al-Rahman al-Sa'di (1596 – c. 1656) was a West African jurist, imam and historian born in Timbuktu. He served as a notary in Djenné and from 1627 as imam of the Sankoré mosque, then returned to Timbuktu around 1637, where as kātib, or government secretary, he mediated between local Songhai rulers and the Moroccan Arma administration.

Around 1655 he began writing the Tarikh al-Sudan, an Arabic chronicle of the Songhai Empire down to the Moroccan invasion of 1591 and of Timbuktu under Moroccan rule, which remains a major source for Songhai history.

阿卜杜勒-拉赫曼·萨迪（1596—约1656）是生于廷巴克图的西非法学家、伊玛目和史学家。他在杰内做公证人，1627年起任桑科雷清真寺伊玛目，约1637年回到家乡廷巴克图，后担任书记官卡提卜，在桑海地方势力与摩洛哥阿尔马政权之间斡旋调停。

约1655年，他开始撰写阿拉伯文编年史《苏丹史》，记述桑海帝国直至1591年摩洛哥入侵以及入侵后廷巴克图的历史，是研究桑海历史的重要原始文献。

Askia Muhammad I, called Askia the Great (1443–1538), was born Muhammad Ture and rose as a general under the Songhai ruler Sunni Ali. In 1493 he overthrew Sunni Ali's successor, Sunni Baru, for failing to uphold Islam, and founded the Askia dynasty. He made the hajj to Mecca in 1496, whose prestige strengthened his position.

He extended Songhai from Taghaza to the Hausa cities, created a provincial bureaucracy, standardized taxes and trade, and made Islam the religion of the ruling class. His son Askia Musa deposed him in 1528, and he died in 1538.

Per Brahe the Younger (1602–1680) was a Swedish soldier, statesman and twice a regent. Grandson of Per Brahe the Elder, he fought in the Polish War and in Germany, and after Gustavus Adolphus's death in 1632 he was one of the regents during Queen Christina's minority. He negotiated the 1635 Truce of Stuhmsdorf with Poland.

As Governor-General of Finland in 1637–1640 and 1648–1654 he reformed administration, introduced a postal system, promoted commerce and education, founded ten towns and opened the Royal Academy of Turku in 1640. He was regent again after Charles X died in 1660, dying at Bogesund in 1680.

小佩尔·布拉赫（1602—1680）是瑞典军人、政治家，曾两度出任摄政。他是老佩尔·布拉赫之孙，曾在波兰战争和德意志作战；国王古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫于1632年阵亡后，他成为克里斯蒂娜女王幼年时的摄政之一。1635年他与波兰谈判达成《斯图姆斯多夫停战协定》。

Olaus Rudbeck (1630–1702) was a Swedish polymath and professor of medicine at Uppsala University. Born in Västerås, the son of Bishop Johannes Rudbeckius, he won fame at twenty-three by describing the lymphatic vessels, Sweden's first major medical discovery. In 1655 he founded Sweden's first botanical garden at Uppsala, and also worked as an architect, astronomer and musician.

His later years were devoted to Atland eller Manheim, a vast history arguing that Sweden was the lost Atlantis and the cradle of all civilization. During Uppsala's great fire of 1702 he directed firefighting from a roof while his house burned; many of his writings and botanical woodblocks were lost. He died in Uppsala shortly afterward.

Carl Michael Bellman (1740–1795) was Sweden's national poet-songwriter. After trying banking and study at Uppsala, debt drove him to Norway in 1763. From 1768, back in Stockholm, he composed a new kind of song, accompanying himself on the cittern in taverns and at court. King Gustav III called him a master improviser and became his patron.

His reputation rests on two collections, Fredman's Epistles and Fredman's Songs, published in 1790 and 1791, whose drinking-house characters and rococo allusions blend comedy, satire and melancholy. Bellman died in Stockholm in 1795.

卡尔·米凯尔·贝尔曼（1740—1795）是瑞典的民族诗人与歌曲作家。他曾尝试银行业和在乌普萨拉大学求学，后因债务所迫于1763年逃往挪威。回到斯德哥尔摩后，他从1768年起创作了一种全新的歌曲，在酒馆和宫廷中弹着西特恩琴自唱。国王古斯塔夫三世称他为即兴大师，成为他的庇护人。

en:
Jacob Johan Anckarström (1762–1792) was the Swedish captain who murdered King Gustav III. A former page and captain in the king's regiment, he was embittered by the Union and Security Act of 1789 stripping the nobles of privilege. With Counts Horn and Ribbing he conspired, and on 16 March 1792 shot the king at a masked ball in Stockholm's Royal Opera. The king had received an anonymous warning but attended anyway.

Gustav III died on 29 March. Anckarström confessed, was condemned to flogging, loss of his right hand and beheading, and was executed on 27 April 1792.

Per Brahe the Elder (1520–1590) was a Swedish statesman and Count of Visingsborg. His father Joakim Brahe died in the Stockholm Bloodbath of 1520, and his mother Margareta Eriksdotter Vasa was Gustav Vasa's sister, so Brahe was cousin to kings Eric XIV, John III and Charles IX. He joined the Privy Council in 1544.

In 1561 he was among Sweden's first counts at Eric XIV's coronation, receiving Visingsborg the following year, and under John III he became Lord High Justiciar (riksdrots). He died in 1590 at Stora Sundby; his grandson Per Brahe the Younger also became a statesman.

Klaus Störtebeker (c. 1360 – 1401) was a leader of the Likedeeler, or Victual Brothers, pirates hired as privateers for Albert of Sweden against Margaret of Denmark, then raiders of Hanseatic shipping. The name Likedeeler referred to their practice of sharing their spoils equally. Expelled from Visby on Gotland in 1398, they used Marienhafe in East Frisia as a base.

Captured near Heligoland by a Hamburg fleet on 22 April 1401, he and 72 companions were beheaded on Hamburg's Grasbrook that October. Legend says his headless body passed eleven men before the headsman stopped him.

Wizli Wisso (died 1350) was a knight of a Zurich ministerial family; his grandfather had died fighting for Habsburg at the Battle of Morgarten in 1315. After Rudolf Brun's guild revolution of 1336, Wizli joined the patrician exiles who sheltered in Rapperswil.

On the night of 23–24 February 1350 he took part in their attempt to seize Zurich and overthrow Brun, later called the Murder Night of Zurich. The coup failed and Wizli was killed in the fighting; Brun confiscated his estates.

Matthäus Schiner (c. 1465–1522), born at Mühlebach in the Valais, became bishop of Sion in 1499. A diplomat and commander, he forged the papal–Swiss alliance that gave rise to the Swiss Guard, and secured Bellinzona for the Confederacy in the Peace of Arona in 1503. Pope Julius II made him a cardinal in 1511.

As legate he led Swiss troops that drove the French from Milan and installed Maximilian Sforza as duke in 1512. He won Novara in 1513, then fought at Marignano in 1515. Driven from Sion in 1517, he supported Charles V's election in 1519 and advised him, and died of plague in 1522.

Johannes Hadlaub (fl. c. 1300, died before 1340) was a Zurich Minnesinger and one of the last poets of Middle High German courtly song. A citizen of Zurich, he is documented buying a house there in 1302. Fifty-one of his songs survive in the Codex Manesse.

His work included love songs, dawn songs and longer lyrical compositions. Because his verse seems to have shaped the collection, scholars commonly assume he helped compile it. Gottfried Keller later made him the hero of the novella Hadlaub, which strongly influenced later perceptions of the poet.

他的作品包括情歌、破晓歌和较长的抒情诗。由于他的诗作在抄本中地位特殊，学界普遍认为他参与了抄本编纂。戈特弗里德·凯勒后来以他为主人公写成中篇小说《哈德劳布》，深刻影响了后人对这位诗人的认识。

en:
Dorothea of Montau (1347–1394) was a Prussian visionary who practised ascetic disciplines from childhood. Married to a Danzig swordsmith, she bore nine children and soon had visions, though only one daughter survived.

In 1384 the couple sold their possessions and went on pilgrimage. After her husband died in 1390 during her pilgrimage to Rome, she settled at Marienwerder, and in 1391 escaped burning as a witch at Danzig through her confessor.

On 2 May 1393 she was enclosed in a cell built against the cathedral, receiving communion until her death the next year. Beatified in 1976, she is venerated as patroness of Prussia and the Teutonic Order.

蒙陶的多萝特（1347—1394）是普鲁士的神秘主义者，自幼便行苦修。她嫁给但泽的一名兵器匠，生有九个孩子，婚后不久便得见异象，其中只有一名女儿存活。

1384年夫妇二人变卖财产，踏上朝圣之路。1390年丈夫在她赴罗马朝圣期间去世，她此后迁居马林韦尔德；1391年她在但泽被控行巫、险遭火刑，全靠告解神父相救。

1393年5月2日，她被封入大教堂墙边的隐修小室，领受圣体直至次年去世。她于1976年受宣福，被尊为普鲁士与条顿骑士团的主保圣人。

Johann von Posilge (c. 1340–1405) was a Prussian cleric traditionally regarded as a chronicler of the Teutonic Order, probably an Old Prussian by birth. First documented in 1376, he served the bishop of Pomesania and later worked as a parish priest.

The chronicle traditionally attributed to him, whose authorship remains disputed, begins its account in 1360 and was later continued by other hands. Written in Latin but surviving only in German, it records the political and cultural life of the Order's state; above all it covers the Great War with Poland and Lithuania, and it ranks among the most valuable German chronicles of that state.

约翰·冯·普茨格（约1340—1405）是普鲁士教士，传统上被认为是条顿骑士团的编年史家，可能是古普鲁士人。他于1376年首次见于文献，曾任波梅萨尼亚主教的属员，后来出任本堂神父。

传统上归于他的编年史作者身份尚有争议，记事始于1360年，后来由他人续修；原以拉丁文写就，今仅存德文本，记载了骑士团国家的政治与文化生活，尤其记述了骑士团与波兰、立陶宛之间的“大战”，是该国最有价值的德语编年史之一。

Piotr of Grudziądz, or Petrus Wilhelmi de Grudencz (1392–c. 1480), was a composer and poet born at Graudenz (Grudziądz) in Prussia. He studied at the University of Kraków from 1418 and later worked in Vienna and near Basel.

In the 1440s he was chaplain to Emperor Frederick III in Vienna. In 1448 he served at the bishop's court in Wrocław and in 1452 travelled to Rome, spending his last years in Silesia.

Fewer than twenty of his works survive, identified by acrostics of his name; his songs and motets reflect the musical culture of medieval Central Europe.

格鲁琼兹的彼得（1392—约1480），拉丁名作彼得鲁斯·威廉米·德·格鲁登茨，是生于普鲁士格劳登茨（格鲁琼兹）的作曲家与诗人。他自1418年在克拉科夫大学学习，后来在维也纳和巴塞尔一带活动。

1440年代他在维也纳担任皇帝腓特烈三世的小堂神父。1448年他供职于弗罗茨瓦夫的主教宫廷，1452年前往罗马，晚年在西里西亚度过。

他的作品存世不足二十首，学者凭借其中暗藏其名字的离合诗确认作者身份；这些歌曲和经文歌体现了中世纪中欧的音乐文化。

en:
Fazlallah Astarabadi (1339/40–1394), pen name Naimi, was a Persian mystic born at Astarabad near the Caspian. As a child he inherited his father's position as judge. At eighteen, hearing a dervish recite a verse by Rumi brought him a religious experience.

He later abandoned his family and possessions to become a wandering dervish, teaching that God reveals himself through the letters of scripture, the doctrine at the heart of the Hurufi movement. His Javidan-namah, or Eternal Book, set out his teaching, and followers gathered across Khorasan, Azerbaijan and Shirvan, above all at Baku. Condemned as a heretic, he was imprisoned at Alinja near Nakhchivan and executed in 1394 by order of Miran Shah, son of Timur.

法兹拉拉·阿斯塔拉巴迪（1339/40—1394），笔名纳伊米，是生于里海沿岸阿斯塔拉巴德的波斯神秘主义者。他幼年继承父亲的法官职位，十八岁时听一名德尔维希吟诵鲁米的诗句，获得了一次宗教体验。

此后他舍弃家庭与财产，成为游方德尔维希，宣扬神借文字的字母显现自身，这一教义构成胡鲁非运动的核心。他的《贾维丹书》意为“永恒之书”，系统阐述其学说；信徒在呼罗珊、阿塞拜疆和希尔万各地聚集，以巴库为中心。他被定为异端，囚禁在纳希切万附近的阿林贾，1394年奉帖木儿之子米兰沙之命被处死。

en:
Gawhar Shad (died 1457) was the chief consort of the Timurid emperor Shah Rukh. Married around 1388, she bore Shah Rukh Ulugh Beg in 1394 and helped move the capital from Samarkand to Herat in 1405.

With her husband she patronized the arts and made Persian language and culture central to Timurid rule, funding Herat's Musalla complex and the Goharshad Mosque in Mashhad, begun in 1418.

After Shah Rukh died in 1447 she was de facto ruler for a favored grandson until Abu Sa'id seized power and had her, aged over eighty, executed on 19 July 1457.

高哈尔绍德（？—1457）是帖木儿帝国皇帝沙哈鲁的正宫皇后。约1388年出嫁，1394年为沙哈鲁生下兀鲁伯，1405年促成帝国都城从撒马尔罕迁至赫拉特。

她与丈夫共同资助艺术，使波斯语言文化成为帖木儿朝统治的核心，先后资助修建赫拉特的穆萨拉建筑群和1418年动工的马什哈德高哈尔绍德清真寺。

1447年沙哈鲁死后，她扶持宠孙继位，以摄政身份实际掌权；阿布·赛义德夺权后，年逾八旬的她于1457年7月19日被处死。

Ghiyath al-Din Jamshid al-Kashi (c. 1380–1429) was a Persian astronomer and mathematician born at Kashan. His early works included the Sullam al-sama, a treatise on celestial distances, and the Khaqani Zij, whose sine tables had unprecedented precision.

Invited to Samarkand by Ulugh Beg, who gathered scholars there, al-Kashi led work at the observatory, calculated pi to sixteen decimal places in 1424 and wrote the Key to Arithmetic using decimal fractions. He died at Samarkand in 1429; Ulugh Beg called him a scientist who could solve the hardest problems.

吉亚斯丁·贾姆希德·卡希（约1380—1429）是生于卡尚的波斯天文学家与数学家。他的早期著作包括探讨天体距离的《天梯》和《哈卡尼历表》，后者给出了精度空前的正弦函数表。

卡希受在撒马尔罕汇聚学者的兀鲁伯之邀前往该城，主持天文台的研究，1424年将圆周率算到小数点后十六位，并在《算术之钥》中运用十进小数。1429年他在撒马尔罕去世；兀鲁伯曾称赞他是一位能解开最艰深难题的杰出学者。

Ali-Shir Nava'i (1441–1501) was a Timurid poet, statesman and linguist born in Herat. His family fled the city after Shah Rukh's death in 1447 and later returned to Khorasan. A schoolmate of Sultan Husayn Bayqara, he entered Bayqara's service after the latter seized Herat in 1469, and in 1472 was made emir of the supreme council.

The greatest writer of Chagatai Turkic literature, he argued its superiority over Persian in Muhakamat al-Lughatayn and composed a Khamsa and four divans. He died unmarried in Herat on 3 January 1501.

阿里希尔·纳沃伊（1441—1501）是帖木儿王朝的诗人、政治家和语言学家，生于赫拉特。1447年沙哈鲁死后，他的家人逃离该城，后来返回呼罗珊。他与苏丹侯赛因·拜哈拉是同窗，1469年拜哈拉夺取赫拉特后入朝效力，1472年出任最高会议埃米尔。

他是察合台突厥语文学最伟大的代表，在《两种语言之辩》中主张察合台语优于波斯语，并著有《五卷诗》和四部诗集。他终身未娶，1501年1月3日在赫拉特去世。

en:
Qavam al-Din ibn Zayn al-Din Shirazi (died 1438) was a Persian architect of the Timurid period. A native of Shiraz, he served Shah Rukh at Herat as a master of engineering, design and building, and his activity was first recorded in 1410.

In an inscription of 1418 he called himself a worker in mud or clay. His monumental designs combined Iranian art with features of contemporary Central Asian buildings, and he pioneered a dome on intersecting arches.

For Queen Gawhar Shad he designed the Goharshad Mosque in Mashhad, begun in 1418, and the Musalla complex in Herat. He died in February 1438.

盖瓦姆丁·设拉齐（？—1438）是帖木儿王朝时期的波斯建筑师，生于设拉子，在赫拉特侍奉沙哈鲁，精通工程、设计与营造，其活动最早见于1410年的记载。

在一则1418年的铭文中，他自称泥工。他设计的大型建筑融合了伊朗艺术与当时中亚建筑的特色，并首创以交叉拱券承托穹顶的做法。

他为皇后高哈尔绍德设计了马什哈德的高哈尔绍德清真寺（1418年动工）和赫拉特的穆萨拉建筑群，1438年2月去世。

Hafiz-i Abru (died 1430), born Abd Allah al-Khwafi in Khorasan, was the leading Persian historian and geographer of the early Timurid court. He studied at Hamadan, joined Timur in the 1380s and accompanied the conqueror's campaigns from Transoxiana and Iran to Syria, gathering eyewitness geographical notes.

After Timur's death he served Shah Rukh at Herat, who in 1414 commissioned his universal history, the Majma al-tawarikh, or Collection of Histories. He also continued Shami's Zafarnama and wrote geographical works on Fars, Kirman and Khurasan, and he died in 1430.

Hafiz-i Abru (died 1430), born Abd Allah al-Khwafi in Khorasan, was the leading Persian historian and geographer of the early [GetCountry('TIM').GetName] court. He studied at Hamadan, joined Timur in the 1380s and accompanied the conqueror's campaigns from Transoxiana and Iran to Syria, gathering eyewitness geographical notes.

After Timur's death he served Shah Rukh at Herat, who in 1414 commissioned his universal history, the Majma al-tawarikh, or Collection of Histories. He also continued Shami's Zafarnama and wrote geographical works on Fars, Kirman and Khurasan, and he died in 1430.

哈菲兹·阿布鲁（？—1430）原名阿卜杜拉·哈瓦菲，生于呼罗珊，是帖木儿朝早期最重要的波斯语史学家与地理学家。他在哈马丹求学，1380年代进入帖木儿宫廷，随帖木儿大军从河中和伊朗一直征战到叙利亚，沿途记录亲身见闻。

帖木儿去世后，他在赫拉特侍奉沙哈鲁；1414年奉沙哈鲁之命编纂通史《历史总汇》。他还续成沙米的《武功记》，撰有法尔斯、克尔曼与呼罗珊的地理志，1430年去世。

en:
Ali Pasha of Ioannina (c. 1743–1822) was an Albanian ruler in the Ottoman Empire. Starting as leader of a band of Albanian brigands, he entered Ottoman service and in 1788 was appointed pasha of the Sanjak of Ioannina.

Through war and diplomacy he extended his control over much of Albania and mainland Greece, ruling his pashalik in all but complete independence from the Porte.

Declared a rebel in 1820, he was hunted down and killed by Ottoman troops in 1822; his revolt helped set the stage for the Greek Revolution of 1821.

约阿尼纳的阿里帕夏（约1743—1822）是奥斯曼帝国的阿尔巴尼亚族统治者。他早年为阿尔巴尼亚匪徒首领，后入仕奥斯曼，1788年被任命为约阿尼纳桑贾克的帕夏。

他凭借征战与外交，将势力扩展到阿尔巴尼亚和希腊大陆大部，其帕夏辖区实际上独立于伊斯坦布尔朝廷。

1820年他被宣布为叛臣，1822年被奥斯曼军队擒杀；他的起事客观上为1821年希腊革命铺平了道路。

Bekir Efendi, later known as Hacı Bekir, was an Ottoman confectioner from Araç in Kastamonu. He moved to Constantinople and in 1777 opened a small sweet shop at Bahçekapı, which became known for lokum, or Turkish delight, and akide candies.

After making the pilgrimage to Mecca between 1817 and 1820 he was known as Hacı Bekir. His shop supplied the Ottoman palace, earning him the title of chief confectioner, şekercibaşı, and both the business and the title passed to his son and grandson.

Ioannis Vlachos (1722 or 1730–1771), better known as Daskalogiannis, or John the Teacher, was a wealthy Cretan shipbuilder and shipowner. Born at Anopolis in Sfakia, he was educated abroad.

He owned four three-masted merchant ships sailing out of southern Crete and served as chairman of Sfakia from 1765. In 1770 he led the Sfakian revolt against Ottoman rule. The rising failed; Daskalogiannis surrendered at Frangokastello and was put to death on 17 June 1771, becoming a hero of Cretan folk song.

约安尼斯·弗拉霍斯（1722或1730年—1771），人称达斯卡洛扬尼斯，意为“教师约翰”，是克里特富有的造船主与船东。他生于斯法基亚的阿诺波利斯，曾被送往海外求学。

他拥有四艘从克里特南部出海的三桅商船，1765年出任斯法基亚地区的议长，并于1770年领导斯法基亚起义，反抗奥斯曼统治。起义失败后，达斯卡洛扬尼斯在弗兰戈卡斯特罗投降，于1771年6月17日被处死，成为克里特民歌中传颂的英雄。

Khayr al-Din Barbarossa (c. 1478–1546), born Hızır on Lesbos, was an Ottoman corsair and admiral. Sailing with his elder brother Oruç Reis, he helped seize Algiers from Spain in 1516, and after Oruç's death in 1518 inherited his command and the nickname Barbarossa and pledged Algiers to the Ottomans.

In 1533 Suleiman the Magnificent made him Kapudan Pasha, or grand admiral. He conquered Tunis in 1534 and crushed the Holy League at Preveza in 1538, securing Ottoman mastery of the Mediterranean. After campaigning with France in the 1540s he retired to Constantinople and died in 1546.

海雷丁·巴巴罗萨（约1478—1546），本名赫兹尔，生于莱斯沃斯岛，是奥斯曼帝国的私掠船长和海军将领。他随兄长奥鲁奇·雷斯出海，1516年兄弟二人从西班牙手中夺取阿尔及尔；1518年奥鲁奇战死后，他接掌部众，继承“巴巴罗萨”的绰号，并把阿尔及尔归附奥斯曼。

1533年，苏莱曼大帝任命他为卡普丹帕夏，即海军总司令。1534年他征服突尼斯，1538年在普雷韦扎大败神圣同盟，奠定奥斯曼在地中海的霸权。1540年代他与法国联合作战，此后退隐君士坦丁堡，1546年在当地去世。

Sedefkar Mehmed Agha (c. 1540–1617) built Istanbul's Sultan Ahmed Mosque, the Blue Mosque. He was brought to Istanbul through the devshirme in 1563 and worked for twenty years in mother-of-pearl inlay, earning the surname Sedefkâr. He became Mimar Sinan's pupil and assistant, and in 1606 became chief imperial architect.

Between 1609 and 1616 he built the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, its central dome buttressed by four semi-domes in a blend of Hagia Sophia and Sinan's style. He died in 1617.

Çandarlı Halil Pasha the Younger (d. 1453) was the fourth grand vizier from the Turkish Çandarlı family. He became grand vizier in 1439 under Murad II. Twice, in 1444 and 1446, he recalled the abdicated Murad to the throne, setting aside the young Mehmed II. When Murad died in 1451, Halil ensured the immediate transfer of power to Mehmed.

He opposed the siege of Constantinople and was suspected of taking Byzantine bribes. After Mehmed II conquered the city in 1453, Halil was dismissed and executed on 10 July.

Haji Bayram Veli (1352–1430), born Numan in Ankara, was an Ottoman Sufi poet and saint who founded the Bayramiyya dervish order. He made the pilgrimage to Mecca with his master, who continued to teach him on the journey.

Inheriting his master's authority in 1412, he returned to Ankara, where his preaching and hymns drew crowds. When the order's growth alarmed the authorities, he was sent to Murad II in Edirne, where the sultan let him lecture at court.

A later legend credits Bayram with foretelling Mehmed II's conquest of Constantinople. He died in Ankara in 1430, leaving the order to his disciple Akshamsaddin.

哈吉·巴伊拉姆·韦利（1352—1430），本名努曼，生于安卡拉，是奥斯曼苏菲派诗人与圣徒，拜拉姆苦行僧教团的创立者。他与师尊一同赴麦加朝觐，旅途中师尊继续教导他。

1412年继承师尊的权威后，他回到安卡拉，以讲道和赞诗吸引了大批信众。教团壮大引起地方官不安，他被送往埃迪尔内觐见穆拉德二世，苏丹允许他在宫廷讲道。

后世传说称巴伊拉姆曾预言穆罕默德二世将征服君士坦丁堡。1430年他在安卡拉去世，将教团传给弟子阿克谢姆塞丁。

en:
Meriwether Lewis (1774–1809) was an American explorer and soldier, born in Virginia. He joined the army, rose to captain, and in 1801 became Thomas Jefferson's secretary.

Chosen by Jefferson to lead an expedition across the Louisiana Purchase, he shared command with William Clark; from 1804 to 1806 the Corps of Discovery traveled up the Missouri, crossed the Rockies and reached the Pacific in November 1805, collecting scientific data along the way. Appointed governor of Upper Louisiana in 1806, he died of gunshot wounds in Tennessee on 11 October 1809, in circumstances still disputed.

他受杰斐逊挑选率领穿越路易斯安那购地的远征，与威廉·克拉克共同指挥；1804至1806年，“发现军团”溯密苏里河而上，翻越落基山脉，于1805年11月抵达太平洋，沿途收集科学资料。1806年他被任命为上路易斯安那总督，1809年10月11日在田纳西因枪伤身亡，究竟是他杀还是自杀至今没有定论。

William Clark (1770–1838) was an American explorer, soldier and territorial governor, born in Virginia. His family moved to Kentucky in 1785, and he served in the U.S. Army at the Battle of Fallen Timbers in 1794.

In 1803 his friend Meriwether Lewis invited him to share command of an expedition across the Louisiana Purchase; from 1804 to 1806 the Corps of Discovery followed the Missouri to the Pacific and back, mapping the American West.

Clark later governed the Missouri Territory and from 1822 was Superintendent of Indian Affairs in St. Louis, where he died in 1838.

In 1803 his friend Meriwether Lewis invited him to share command of an expedition across the Louisiana Purchase; from 1804 to 1806 the Corps of Discovery followed the Missouri to the Pacific and back, mapping the American West.

Clark later governed the Missouri Territory and from 1822 was Superintendent of Indian Affairs in St. Louis, where he died in 1838.

威廉·克拉克（1770—1838）是美国探险家、军人和领地总督，生于弗吉尼亚。1785年他的家人迁往肯塔基，他曾在美军服役，参加了1794年的鹿寨战役。

1803年，友人梅里韦瑟·刘易斯邀他共同率领一支穿越路易斯安那购地的远征队；1804至1806年，“发现军团”沿密苏里河抵达太平洋再返回，绘制了美国西部的地图。

他后来出任密苏里领地总督，1822年起在圣路易斯任印第安事务总监，1838年在当地去世。

Daniel Shays (1747–1825) was an American farmer and Continental Army captain, born in Hopkinton, Massachusetts, in 1747. He fought at Bunker Hill and Saratoga, but left the army unpaid and returned home to debts and tax foreclosures.

In 1786 he joined rural protesters shutting down county courts, and in January 1787 led hundreds of Regulators against the federal armory at Springfield, where militia grapeshot broke the assault.

Condemned for treason, Shays was pardoned in 1788. He later lived on a federal pension and a small plot of land, and died in New York in 1825.

Benjamin Franklin (1706–1790) was a Founding Father of the United States. He made his name in Philadelphia as a printer and publisher of Poor Richard's Almanack. His studies of electricity made him a leading scientist, and his inventions included the lightning rod.

As a colonial agent in London he helped secure repeal of the Stamp Act in 1766. He helped draft the Declaration of Independence in 1776, then as minister to France won the French alliance and the 1783 Treaty of Paris. He also helped found Philadelphia's first fire department. President of Pennsylvania from 1785, he signed the Constitution in 1787.

Tito Livio Burattini (1617–1681) was a Venetian inventor and scientist born in Agordo, near Belluno, who spent his career in Poland and Lithuania. In 1641 he was summoned to Warsaw by King Ladislaus IV.

In 1647 he built a model aircraft called the flying dragon, said to have lifted a cat in 1648 but never a man. His 1675 treatise Universal Measure first applied the name metre to a unit of length. He died in Kraków.

Claudio Monteverdi (baptized 1567–1643) was an Italian composer born in Cremona whose work marks the transition from Renaissance to Baroque music. He published his first book of madrigals in 1587 and entered the Gonzaga court in Mantua around 1590, defending his innovative techniques as a seconda pratica.

His opera L'Orfeo was performed at Mantua in 1607. In 1613 he became maestro di cappella at St Mark's Basilica in Venice, holding the post until his death, and in old age wrote The Return of Ulysses and The Coronation of Poppea for Venetian theatres.

Tiziano Vecellio, known as Titian (c. 1488/1490–1576), was the leading painter of the Venetian Renaissance, born at Pieve di Cadore near Belluno. Trained in Venice under Giovanni Bellini alongside Giorgione, he won fame with the Assumption of the Virgin for the Frari, completed in 1518.

Its agitated apostles broke with the meditative stillness of earlier Venetian painting. His patrons came to include Emperor Charles V and Philip II of Spain.

Equally master of portraits, mythologies and altarpieces, he defined Venetian colour and loose brushwork across nearly seventy years. He died in Venice in the plague of 1576.

提齐亚诺·韦切利奥，即提香（约1488/1490—1576），是威尼斯文艺复兴时期最杰出的画家，生于贝卢诺附近的皮耶韦-迪卡多雷。他在威尼斯随乔瓦尼·贝利尼学艺，与乔尔乔内同窗，1518年为弗拉里教堂完成《圣母升天》，一举成名。

画中激动的使徒打破了早期威尼斯绘画的沉静氛围。他的赞助人包括皇帝查理五世和西班牙国王腓力二世。

他兼擅肖像、神话题材与祭坛画，在近七十年的创作中确立了威尼斯画派的色彩风格与奔放笔法。他最终于1576年在威尼斯鼠疫中去世。

Lorenzo Marcello (1603–1656) was a Venetian admiral born into the patrician Marcello family. He entered the navy in 1618 and campaigned against Barbary pirates in the 1630s before joining the war against the Ottomans over Crete.

At Valona in 1638 he kept command after being wounded, earning the Senate's praise. In September 1655 he succeeded Francesco Morosini as Captain General of the Sea.

On 26 June 1656 he led the Venetian and Maltese fleet against the Ottoman navy at the Dardanelles, winning Venice's greatest victory since Lepanto; he was killed by a cannon shot leading the centre into battle. His lieutenant concealed his body to preserve the crews' morale.

1638年他在瓦罗纳负伤后继续指挥，受到元老院嘉奖。1655年9月，他接替弗朗切斯科·莫罗西尼出任海上总司令。

Adrian Willaert (c. 1490–1562) was a Flemish composer of the High Renaissance and the founder of the Venetian School. Born near Roeselare in Flanders, he went to Paris to study law but turned to music, and in 1515 entered the service of the Este family of Ferrara.

In 1527 Andrea Gritti helped secure his appointment as maestro di cappella of St Mark's Basilica in Venice, a post he held until his death. He transplanted Franco-Flemish polyphony to Italy and trained musicians from across Europe, including Gioseffo Zarlino.

Gioseffo Zarlino (1517–1590) was an Italian Franciscan composer and the most influential music theorist of the Renaissance, born at Chioggia near Venice. He entered the Franciscan order in 1532 and moved to Venice in 1541 to study with Adrian Willaert.

In 1565 he succeeded Cipriano de Rore as maestro di cappella of St Mark's, holding the post until his death. His writings founded the theory of tonal harmony in the major and minor modes, and his pupils included Claudio Merulo and Vincenzo Galilei.

Baldassare Donato (c. 1525/1530–1603) was an Italian composer and singer of the late Venetian school and a leading developer of the light secular villanella. First recorded as a singer at St Mark's Basilica in 1550, he was charged with training its choirboys in 1562.

When Gioseffo Zarlino became maestro di cappella in 1565 Donato was demoted to singer, and their feud ended in a brawl on the Feast of St Mark in 1569. He became Zarlino's deputy in 1588 and succeeded him at St Mark's in 1590, serving until his death.

Claudio Merulo (1533–1604), born at Correggio, was an Italian organist, composer and publisher of the late Venetian Renaissance, celebrated for pioneering keyboard music. After a year at Brescia Cathedral, he was appointed organist of St Mark's in 1557 and became its first organist in 1566.

He wrote festive music for Henry III of France's 1574 visit to Venice. In 1584 he left St Mark's for Parma's Farnese court; from 1587 he served Parma Cathedral and published his influential Toccate per organo. He died at Parma in 1604.

Giovanni Gabrieli (c. 1554/1557–1612) was an Italian composer and organist who brought the Venetian School to its peak at the turn to the Baroque. He probably studied in Venice with his uncle Andrea Gabrieli and in Munich with Orlando de Lassus.

In 1585 he succeeded Claudio Merulo as principal organist of St Mark's and served for life as organist of the Scuola Grande di San Rocco. His Sacrae symphoniae of 1597 spread the Venetian polychoral style across Europe, drawing pupils such as Heinrich Schütz. He died in Venice in 1612.

Pietro Loredan (1372–1438) was a Venetian nobleman and admiral of the Loredan family, whose father and grandfather had also commanded Venetian fleets. In 1412, as captain-general, he took Šibenik and helped defeat the troops of Sigismund of Hungary at the Battle of Motta, securing Dalmatia for Venice.

Sent against the Ottomans in 1416, he destroyed their fleet at the Battle of Gallipoli. He later campaigned against Genoa and Milan and was made Procurator of St Mark's in 1425. In 1423 he lost the doge's election to his rival Francesco Foscari; when Loredan died in 1438, Foscari was suspected of poisoning him.

彼得罗·洛雷丹（1372—1438）出身洛雷丹家族，是威尼斯贵族与海军统帅，他的父亲和祖父也曾统领威尼斯舰队。1412年他出任舰队统帅，攻取希贝尼克，并在莫塔战役中协助击败匈牙利国王西吉斯蒙德的军队，为威尼斯保住达尔马提亚。

Bartolomeo Bon (c. 1405–c. 1466) was a Venetian sculptor and architect whose career bridged Venetian Gothic and the early Renaissance. Trained by his father Giovanni Bon, he worked with him on the sculptural decoration of the Ca' d'Oro between 1424 and 1430.

Father and son also made the marble door of the Frari and were entrusted with the Porta della Carta (1438–1442), the rich marble gateway joining the Doge's Palace to St Mark's Basilica. Bartolomeo also worked independently on the portal of San Giovanni e Paolo.

Antonio Vivaldi (1678–1741), nicknamed the Red Priest, was a Venetian Baroque composer and violinist. Ordained in 1703, he was excused from saying Mass through ill health and instead worked at Venice's Ospedale della Pietà, where he taught violin and composed concertos for its orchestra of orphaned girls.

He consolidated the solo concerto form in hundreds of works, above all The Four Seasons. In 1740 he followed his patron Emperor Charles VI to Vienna, but the emperor died and Vivaldi died in poverty in 1741.

安东尼奥·维瓦尔第（1678—1741）是威尼斯巴洛克作曲家与小提琴家，绰号“红发神父”。他1703年受任神职，因体弱获准不主持弥撒，转而长年任职于威尼斯仁爱济贫院，在院里教授小提琴，并为孤女组成的乐团创作协奏曲。

Benedetto Marcello (1686–1739) was a Venetian nobleman, magistrate and Baroque composer. His father wanted him to pursue law, so he combined public service with music, holding office from the Council of Forty in 1711 to provincial governor at Pola while writing more than three hundred cantatas and four oratorios.

His masterpiece Estro poetico-armonico (1724–1727) set fifty psalms for voices and continuo and was admired across Europe by Goethe, Rossini and Verdi. In 1728 he secretly married his singing pupil Rosanna Scalfi, a commoner, and he died of tuberculosis at Brescia in 1739.

贝内代托·马切洛（1686—1739）是威尼斯贵族、法官与巴洛克作曲家。他的父亲希望他从事法律，他便在公职之余兼顾音乐，从1711年进入四十人团到出任波拉长官，公务之余创作了三百余首康塔塔和四部清唱剧。

其代表作《诗与和声的灵感》（1724—1727）将50首诗篇谱为人声与通奏低音的乐曲，在欧洲广受赞誉，歌德、罗西尼和威尔第都对其推崇备至。1728年他与平民出身的声乐学生罗桑娜·斯卡尔菲秘密成婚，1739年在布雷西亚因结核病去世。

Alessandro Leopardi (c. 1465–1522/1523) was a Venetian sculptor, bronze founder and architect, nicknamed del Cavallo after his most famous work. A master at the Venetian mint, he was exiled for fraud in 1487 but recalled in 1490 to cast the bronze equestrian statue of Bartolomeo Colleoni, left unfinished at Verrocchio's death. Verrocchio had made the clay model, but the Venetians chose Leopardi; casting was completed in 1492 and his pedestal in 1495.

He also designed and cast the three bronze flagpole bases in St Mark's Square between 1505 and 1506, and later oversaw fortifications at Padua and Treviso.

亚历山德罗·莱奥帕尔迪（约1465—1522/1523）是威尼斯雕塑家、青铜铸造师兼建筑师，因最著名的作品得到“德尔卡瓦洛”（铸马者）的绰号。他本是威尼斯造币厂的师傅，1487年因欺诈被流放，1490年被召回，负责铸造韦罗基奥去世时未完成的巴尔托洛梅奥·科莱奥尼青铜骑马像；韦罗基奥已制成泥模，威尼斯当局却选中莱奥帕尔迪，铜像1492年浇铸完成，基座1495年落成。

1505至1506年，他又设计并铸造了圣马可广场三座青铜旗杆基座，后来还主持过帕多瓦和特雷维索的防御工事。

en:
Paolo Sarpi (1552–1623) was a Venetian Servite friar, historian and canon lawyer who defended the Republic against the papacy. He entered the Servite Order in 1566 and later became the senate's canonist consultor.

When Pope Paul V laid Venice under interdict in 1606, Sarpi supplied the legal case for defiance; excommunicated in 1607, he survived a dagger attack by five assassins later that year. In 1619 his History of the Council of Trent was published and at once banned in Rome. A friend of Galileo, he died in Venice in 1623.

保罗·萨尔皮（1552—1623）是威尼斯圣母忠仆会修士、历史学家和教会法学家，曾为威尼斯共和国对抗教廷。他1566年加入圣母忠仆会，后来成为元老院的教会法顾问。

1606年教宗保罗五世对威尼斯颁布禁令，萨尔皮为共和国的反抗提供法理依据；1607年他被革除教籍，同年遭五名刺客持刀袭击，侥幸生还。1619年，他的《特伦托会议史》出版，随即被罗马列为禁书。他是伽利略的朋友，1623年在威尼斯去世。

Antonio Pigafetta (c. 1492–c. 1534) was a Venetian nobleman and explorer from Vicenza. He joined Ferdinand Magellan's Spanish expedition to the Spice Islands, serving as Magellan's assistant and keeping a precise journal of the voyage.

After Magellan's death in the Philippines in 1521, he was one of eighteen men, out of about 240 who had set out, who completed the entire voyage. Led by Juan Sebastián Elcano, they reached Spain in 1522 aboard the Victoria, completing the first circumnavigation of the globe.

After Magellan's death in the Philippines in 1521, he was one of eighteen men, out of about 240 who had set out, who completed the entire voyage. Led by Juan Sebastián Elcano, they reached Spain in 1522 aboard the Victoria, completing the first circumnavigation of the globe.

Francesco Foscari (1373–1457) was the 65th doge of Venice, elected in 1423 over Pietro Loredan after serving as ambassador and Procurator of St Mark's. His thirty-four-year reign was the longest in the republic's history. He led Venice through the Wars in Lombardy against Milan's Visconti, driving mainland expansion until Francesco Sforza forced a peace.

A patron of Renaissance art, he built the Ca' Foscari on the Grand Canal. His son Jacopo was tried and exiled, dying in Crete, and in 1457 the Council of Ten made Foscari abdicate; he died days later and received a state funeral.

Fra Mauro (c. 1400–1459) was a Camaldolese monk and cartographer at San Michele monastery on Murano. In his youth he travelled as a merchant and soldier and became familiar with the Middle East, and he later ran a mapmaking workshop, questioning returning merchants.

Around 1450 he finished his great circular world map, made for the rulers of Venice and Portugal. More than two metres across and covered with thousands of notes, it was the most detailed world map of its age and put accuracy above biblical geography, without Jerusalem at its centre.

Marino Sanuto the Younger (1466–1536) was a patrician, historian and diarist, the son of the senator Leonardo Sanuto. Elected to the Great Council at twenty and a senator from 1498, he kept a daily record of the republic's politics, diplomacy and news, granted access to the state's secret archives.

His Diarii filled fifty-eight volumes covering 1496 to 1533. Twice passed over for the post of official historian, he received a senate pension in 1531 and died in 1536.

Elena Cornaro Piscopia (1646–1684) was a Venetian noblewoman and philosopher, the daughter of Gianbattista Cornaro-Piscopia, Procurator of St Mark. A Benedictine oblate from 1665, she became president of Venice's Accademia dei Pacifici in 1670.

Cardinal Barbarigo refused her a theology degree but allowed her to study philosophy, and on 25 June 1678, in Padua Cathedral, she was proclaimed a doctor of philosophy after disputing Aristotle in Latin, the first woman to earn a doctorate in philosophy. She died of tuberculosis in Padua in 1684.

埃琳娜·科尔纳罗·皮斯科皮亚（1646—1684）是威尼斯贵族女性、哲学家，父亲是圣马可行政长官詹巴蒂斯塔·科尔纳罗-皮斯科皮亚。她1665年成为本笃会献修女，1670年出任威尼斯“和平学院”院长。

巴尔巴里戈枢机不准她攻读神学学位，只许她学习哲学。1678年6月25日，她在帕多瓦主教座堂用拉丁语就亚里士多德著作答辩，被授予哲学博士，成为第一位获得哲学博士学位的女性。1684年她因肺结核在帕多瓦去世。

Angelo Notari (1566–1663) was an Italian composer born in Padua and trained in Venice, who spent most of his career in England. From 1610 he served Henry, Prince of Wales, and from 1618 Prince Charles, later King Charles I, as a singer and lutenist.

His 1613 collection Prime musiche nuove, containing monodies and canzonettas, brought the latest Italian monodic style to the English court. He died in London in December 1663, aged about ninety-seven.

Benedetto Castelli (1578–1643), born Antonio Castelli in Brescia, was an Italian Benedictine monk, mathematician and physicist, and the closest pupil of Galileo Galilei. He assisted Galileo's study of sunspots and took part in discussions of Copernican theory.

In 1613 he took Galileo's old mathematics chair at the University of Pisa, and in 1625 Pope Urban VIII called him to teach at the Sapienza in Rome.

His studies of running water issued in the treatise On the Measurement of Running Waters, a foundation of modern hydraulics. His pupils included Torricelli, Borelli and Cavalieri. He died in Rome.

贝内代托·卡斯泰利（1578—1643）出生于布雷西亚，俗名安东尼奥，是意大利本笃会修士、数学家与物理学家，也是伽利略最亲近的弟子。他协助伽利略研究太阳黑子，参与讨论哥白尼学说。

1613年他在比萨大学接任伽利略的数学教席，1625年被教宗乌尔班八世召往罗马智慧大学任教。

他研究流水的运动与测量，所著《论流水的测量》奠定了现代水力学的基础。他的学生包括托里拆利、博雷利与卡瓦列里，最终在罗马去世。

Nicolò Minato (c. 1627–1698) was a Venetian poet, librettist and impresario born in Bergamo. He began writing for the Venetian stage in 1650 with Orimonte for Francesco Cavalli while still working as a lawyer, and from 1665 helped run the Teatro San Salvador.

In 1669 he moved to Vienna as court poet to Emperor Leopold I. Over his career he wrote more than 200 librettos, later revived by Handel and Telemann, and he died in Vienna on 28 February 1698.

Alberto Fortis (1741–1803) was an Augustinian abbot, naturalist and travel writer born in Padua. From 1765 he explored Veneto, Istria and Venetian Dalmatia, studying geology, antiquities and local folklore.

His Journey to Dalmatia (1774), translated into English, French and German, described the customs, costumes and epic songs of the Morlach highlanders and first printed the ballad Hasanaginica, drawing European attention to the Balkan hinterland and inspiring a literary fashion later called Morlachism.

In 1785 he became mineralogist to the Bourbon court of Naples, where he was tasked with reforming the saltpeter industry. He was elected to the Royal Society in 1795 and died in Bologna.

阿尔贝托·福尔蒂斯（1741—1803）是出生于帕多瓦的奥斯定会修士、博物学家与旅行作家。1765年起他在威尼托、伊斯特拉和威尼斯治下的达尔马提亚考察，研究地质、古物与当地民俗。

1774年出版的《达尔马提亚纪行》记述了莫拉克山民的风俗、服饰与史诗吟唱，并首次刊印民歌《哈桑阿吉尼察》；该书被译成英、法、德多种文字，使巴尔干腹地引起欧洲关注，催生了后来所称的“莫拉克主义”文学风尚。

1785年他出任那不勒斯波旁王室的矿物学家，受命改革当地硝石业。1795年他当选英国皇家学会会员，最终在博洛尼亚去世。

Rosalba Carriera (1673–1757) was a Venetian Rococo painter who began with portrait miniatures and then made her name with pastel portraits, a medium she popularized across eighteenth-century Europe. She painted miniatures for snuff-box lids and was among the first to use ivory rather than vellum for them.

Grand Tour travellers across Europe sought her work. In 1704 Rome's Accademia di San Luca made her a member. From 1720 to 1721 she worked in Paris, winning election to the Académie royale, and in 1730 she went to Vienna, where Charles VI collected over 150 of her pastels. She died blind in Venice.

罗萨尔巴·卡列拉（1673—1757）是威尼斯洛可可画家，早年绘制肖像细密画，后以色粉肖像闻名，把色粉笔画推广到整个18世纪的欧洲。她曾为鼻烟盒盖绘制细密画，也是最早以象牙代替羊皮纸作画的画家之一。

欧洲各地的壮游者争相求画。1704年罗马圣路加学院接纳她为院士。1720至1721年她在巴黎创作，入选皇家绘画雕塑学院；1730年她前往维也纳，皇帝查理六世收藏了她150多幅色粉画。她晚年双目失明，在威尼斯去世。

Giovanni Dondi dall'Orologio (c. 1330–1388) was a physician, astronomer and clockmaker born in Chioggia, the son of Jacopo Dondi, who had built the great astronomical clock in Padua in 1344. From 1348 to 1364 Giovanni designed and constructed his Astrarium, a complex astronomical clock and planetarium modelling the movements of the planets with mathematical precision.

He taught in Padua and served as ambassador to Venice in 1371. After the Paduan war he moved to the University of Pavia, where he worked as a diplomat and scholar until his death at Abbiategrasso in 1388.

乔瓦尼·唐迪（约1330—1388）是生于基奥贾的医生、天文学家与钟表匠，父亲是1344年在帕多瓦建造大型天文钟的雅各布·唐迪。1348至1364年间，他设计并制成了“星盘仪”，这是一座精密的天文钟兼行星仪，以数学精度模拟行星运行。

他曾在帕多瓦任教，1371年出任驻威尼斯使节。帕多瓦与威尼斯交战后他转往帕维亚大学，兼任外交与学术工作，1388年卒于阿比亚泰格拉索。

Vyasatirtha (1447–1539), born Yatiraja, was a Hindu philosopher and saint of Madhva's Dvaita school of Vedanta. Ordained in his youth, he succeeded Bramhanya Tirtha as pontiff at Abbur in 1478, then studied under Sripadaraja at Mulbagal.

As rajaguru of the Vijayanagara Empire he advised Kings Saluva Narasimha and Krishna Deva Raya, and was honoured as one of the three great saints of Dvaita. His works such as the Nyayamruta dissected rival philosophies.

He developed irrigation at Bettakonda and established temples in newly conquered regions. His Kannada and Sanskrit devotional songs such as Krishna Nee Begane shaped the Haridasa movement.

维亚萨提尔塔（1447—1539），本名亚蒂拉贾，是印度教摩陀婆二元论吠檀多学派的哲学家与圣徒。他少年出家，1478年继布拉曼亚·提尔塔出任阿布尔修道院住持，后在穆尔巴加尔师从斯里帕达拉贾。

作为毗奢耶那伽罗帝国的帝师，他侍奉萨卢瓦·纳拉辛哈与克里希纳·德瓦·拉亚两位国王，被尊为二元论三大圣徒之一。所著《逻辑甘露》等作品辩驳各派学说。

他在贝塔孔达兴修灌溉，并在新征服地区建立神庙。他以卡纳达语和梵语谱写的《克里希纳，快来吧》等虔诚歌影响了哈里达萨运动。

Nachana Somanatha was a Telugu poet of the Vijayanagara Empire in the fourteenth century. An inscription dated to 1344, though other readings give different dates, records that King Bukka Raya I granted him the village of Penchukaladinne, also called Bukka-raya-puram.

He translated the Sanskrit Harivamsa into Telugu as the Uttara-Harivamsamu and composed the Vasanta Vilasamu, an early prabandha work now lost. He helped shift Telugu verse from the Puranic manner toward the polished kavya style later perfected by Srinatha.

纳查纳·索马纳塔是14世纪毗奢耶那伽罗帝国的泰卢固语诗人。一说定为1344年（也有其他释读）的铭文记载，国王布卡一世将彭丘卡拉丁内村（又称布卡罗亚普兰）封赐给他。

他把梵语《诃利世系》译为泰卢固语的《乌塔拉诃利世系》，还创作了早期“普拉班达”诗体作品《瓦桑塔·维拉萨姆》，今已散佚。他推动泰卢固诗歌从往世书体转向精致的宫廷诗风，为后来斯里纳塔等人的创作开辟了道路。

Kanaka Dasa (c. 1508–1606), born Thimmappa Nayaka near Haveri, was a Haridasa saint, poet and musician of the Dvaita Vedanta school. Tradition relates that he served as an army commander until defeat in battle turned him to religious life, when he became a disciple of Vyasatirtha.

He composed keertanas and ugabhogas in simple Kannada using native metrical forms. With Purandara Dasa he contributed to the foundations of Carnatic music and became known as one of the twin poets of Haridasa devotional literature.

卡纳卡·达萨（约1508—1606），原名蒂马帕·纳亚卡，生于哈韦里一带，是信奉二元论吠檀多的哈里达萨圣徒、诗人与音乐家。相传他本是统兵将领，战败后弃武皈依，成为维亚萨提尔塔的弟子。

他用浅白的卡纳达语和本土韵律谱写克尔坦和乌加博加。他与普兰达拉·达萨共同奠定卡纳提克音乐的基础，并称哈里达萨虔诚文学的双星。

Kempe Gowda I (1510–1569) was chieftain of Yelahanka and a vassal of the Vijayanagara Empire. In 1526 he conquered Sivagange, and in 1537, with imperial permission, he built the fortified town of Bengaluru Pete and moved his capital there from Yelahanka. Within its eight gates, two main roads crossed and markets were set aside for different goods and trades.

He built the Gavi Gangadhareshwara temple and the great Bull Temple with its granite monolith of Nandi. Once imprisoned for years after a rival's complaint, he was restored to his lands and granted surrounding villages, dying in 1569.

肯佩·高达一世（1510—1569）是叶拉汉卡的首领、毗奢耶那伽罗帝国的封臣。1526年他征服锡瓦甘盖，1537年经皇帝准许修筑设防城镇班加罗尔佩特，将都城从叶拉汉卡迁此。城中有八座城门，两条主道交叉，不同货物与行当各有市场。

他修建加维·甘加达雷什瓦拉神庙以及供奉整块花岗岩南迪石像的大公牛神庙。他曾因邻邦首领告状被囚禁数年，获释后恢复领地并获赐周边村庄，1569年去世。

Atukuri Molla (1440–1530), known as Kummari Molla after her potter caste, was one of the earliest women to write poetry in Telugu. The daughter of a potter of Gopavaram near Nellore, she was named Molla, meaning jasmine.

She claimed Shiva as her guru and took the poet Pothana as her model. She rendered the Sanskrit Ramayana into plain Telugu as the Molla Ramayanam and recited it at the court of Krishnadevaraya.

Refusing to dedicate the work to any king, she entrusted it to temple authorities in her home village. She then went to Srisailam, where she practiced austerities and taught spiritual seekers before her death around 1530.

阿图库里·摩拉（1440—1530）因陶工种姓而被称为“陶工摩拉”，是最早的泰卢固语女诗人之一。她是内洛尔附近戈帕瓦拉姆村陶工之女，名字摩拉意为茉莉。

她奉湿婆为上师，以诗人波塔纳为楷模。她把梵语《罗摩衍那》译为浅白的泰卢固语，成《摩拉罗摩衍那》，并在克里希纳·德瓦·拉亚的宫廷中诵读。

她拒绝将诗作题献给任何国王，而把它托付给故乡的寺庙管理者。此后她前往斯里赛勒姆修行，向求道者讲学，约1530年在那里辞世。

Tallapaka Tirumalamma, popularly called Timmakka, was a Telugu poet of the fifteenth century and is regarded as the first woman to write poetry in Telugu. Born into a Niyogi Brahmin family, she became the first wife of the singer-poet Annamacharya.

Her surviving work, the Subhadra Kalyanam, is a dvipada kavya of some 1170 poems based on Nannaya's Telugu Mahabharata. It retells the marriage of Arjuna and Subhadra, filling the Sanskrit story with Telugu domestic life and humor.

塔拉帕卡·蒂鲁马拉马，通称蒂姆卡，是15世纪的泰卢固语女诗人，被视为第一位以泰卢固语创作诗歌的女性。她出身尼约吉婆罗门家庭，后成为吟唱诗人安纳马查里亚的元配。

她传世的作品《妙贤婚礼》是一部约1170首的双行体长诗，取材于南纳亚的泰卢固语《摩诃婆罗多》，重述阿周那与妙贤的姻缘，并在这一梵语故事中融入了泰卢固人的家庭生活与诙谐情趣。

Zacharias Kopystensky (died 21 March 1627), born in Przemyśl, was an Orthodox cleric and writer in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. Educated at the Ostroh Academy, he entered the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra and in 1624 succeeded Yelisey Pletenetsky as its archimandrite.

His chief work, Palinodiia (1621–1623), defended Eastern Orthodoxy against the Ruthenian Uniate Church, and he translated the Horologion and works of John Chrysostom. The Hustyn Chronicle, a history of the old Rus' lands to 1598, has also been attributed to him.

撒迦利亚·科佩斯坚斯基（？—1627），生于普热梅希尔，是波兰—立陶宛联邦的东正教神职人员与作家。他曾在奥斯特罗赫学院求学，后入基辅洞窟修道院，1624年继叶利谢·普列捷涅茨基出任院长。

其主要著作《翻案篇》（1621—1623）为东正教辩护，驳斥鲁塞尼亚合并派教会；他还翻译了《时祷书》和金口约翰的著作。记述古罗斯直至1598年历史的《古斯滕编年史》也被归于他的名下。

Shona tradition presents Nyatsimba Mutota (c. 1400–c. 1450), a royal prince of declining Great Zimbabwe, as the founder of the Mutapa Empire. Tradition relates that a salt shortage led him to lead his people north to Dande, where he set up a new dynasty.

Taking the title Mwene Mutapa, he also became high priest of Mwari. Around 1440 he opened campaigns along the Zambezi and conquered Great Zimbabwe itself.

He built the gold and ivory trade with Sofala. He was killed in war with a Tonga tribe about 1450 and succeeded by his son Matope.

He built the gold and ivory trade with [ShowLocationName('sofala')]. He was killed in war with a [GetCountry('TNA').GetName] tribe about 1450 and succeeded by his son Matope.

尼亚钦巴·穆托塔（约1400—约1450），据绍纳人传说，是日渐衰落的大津巴布韦的王族成员、穆塔帕帝国的创建者。相传因盐源匮乏，他率族人北迁至丹德，在那里建立新王朝。

他采用“姆韦尼穆塔帕”的称号，又成为姆瓦里大祭司。约1440年起，他沿赞比西河四处征战，一度征服大津巴布韦。

他发展与索法拉的黄金和象牙贸易。约1450年，他在与通加部落的战争中身亡，其子马托佩继位。

en:
Changamire Dombo (died c. 1696) was the Shona ruler who founded the Rozvi Empire on the Zimbabwean Plateau. Mutapa had become a Portuguese vassal earlier in the century, and Portuguese settlers raided its Shona subjects.

Dombo used royal cattle herds to build a following, defeated Portuguese and Mutapa forces in the 1670s and 1680s, and conquered the gold-rich kingdom of Butua about 1683.

In the 1690s, answering a Mutapa ruler's call for aid, he massacred Portuguese traders and drove every Portuguese off the plateau, later conquering Manyika before his death about 1696.

东博凭借王室牛群招揽部众，于1670至1680年代击败葡萄牙人与穆塔帕的军队，约1683年征服盛产黄金的布图阿王国。

en:
Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba (1453–1515), known as El Gran Capitán, was a Spanish general born at Montilla. He fought for Isabella of Castile in the civil war after 1474 and in 1479 took part in the final battle against Portugal.

He then campaigned in the conquest of Granada and in the Italian Wars, where he was the first European to use firearms decisively on the battlefield and reorganized infantry with pikes and guns.

He was made Duke of Terranova in 1502 and served as viceroy of Naples. He died on 2 December 1515.

en:
Benjamin Hornigold (c. 1680–1719) was an English pirate of the Bahamas. From 1713 he raided shipping off New Providence and helped make Nassau a self-styled Republic of Pirates.

By 1717 he commanded the thirty-gun sloop Ranger and had made Edward Teach, later Blackbeard, his second-in-command. After he refused to rob British ships, his crew voted him from command. In December 1718 he took the King's Pardon from Governor Woodes Rogers and hunted former comrades until a hurricane wrecked his ship on a reef in 1719.

en:
Henry Every (born 20 August 1659, vanished 1696) was an English pirate called the Arch Pirate. As first mate of the warship Charles II, he took command in a mutiny at Corunna in 1694, renamed her Fancy and was elected captain.

On 7 September 1695 he led a pirate squadron that captured the Grand Mughal's treasure ships Fateh Muhammed and Ganj-i-Sawai off India, seizing plunder worth up to six hundred thousand pounds, the richest prize of the pirate age.

The raid outraged the Mughal court; the Privy Council and East India Company offered a reward for Every, sparking a worldwide manhunt, but he eluded it and disappeared in 1696.

1695年9月7日，他率领海盗船队在印度外海截获莫卧儿大帝的宝船“法塔赫穆罕默德号”和“根杰伊萨瓦伊号”，掠走价值高达60万英镑的财物，是海盗时代最丰厚的一票。

en:
Thomas Tew (died September 1695), the Rhode Island Pirate, was an English privateer turned pirate. From Bermuda he sailed the sloop Amity in 1692 and, with his crew's consent, turned pirate in the Red Sea, seizing a Mughal treasure ship and returning rich to Newport; he pioneered the route called the Pirate Round.

On a second cruise beginning in November 1694 he joined Henry Every at the Mandab Strait and was killed in September 1695 attacking a Mughal ship believed to be the Fateh Muhammed. He was later said to be a founder of the legendary pirate colony Libertalia.

Jan Janszoon of Haarlem, known after his conversion as Murat Reis the Younger (c. 1570–c. 1641), was a Dutch seaman turned Barbary corsair. Captured by Algerian corsairs off Lanzarote in 1618, he converted to Islam and took the name Murad, thereafter raiding European shipping from Algiers and the Moroccan coast. He helped found the independent Republic of Salé and served as its first president and commander.

In 1622 he docked at Veere under the Moroccan flag; Dutch authorities brought his wife and children to persuade him to abandon piracy, but he refused. On 20 June 1631 he led the sack of Baltimore in Ireland, carrying much of its population away into slavery.

Jan Želivský (1380–9 March 1422) was a radical Hussite priest whose preaching helped spark the Hussite Wars. His fiery apocalyptic sermons drew large crowds.

On 30 July 1419 he led a procession past the New Town Hall; after councillors stoned his followers, they stormed the hall and hurled the councillors from the windows, the First Defenestration of Prague. He lost command after defeat at Brüx in 1421, and on 9 March 1422 the town council arrested and beheaded him.

Liu Ji (1311–1375), courtesy name Bowen and commonly called Liu Bowen, was a strategist, scholar and official of the late Yuan and early Ming, born in Qingtian, Zhejiang. After passing the Yuan jinshi examination he served the Mongol regime for 25 years before retiring from office.

In 1360 he joined the rebel leader Zhu Yuanzhang and advised him through the campaigns that overthrew the Yuan and founded the Ming in 1368. With Jiao Yu he compiled the military treatise Huolongjing, or Fire Dragon Manual. He later fell out with the chancellor Hu Weiyong and died in 1375, possibly poisoned.

刘基（1311—1375），字伯温，通常称刘伯温，浙江青田人，是元末明初的军事家、学者与官员。他考中元朝进士后为蒙古政权效力二十五年，最终辞官归隐。

1360年，他投奔起事首领朱元璋，为其出谋划策，辅佐推翻元朝，于1368年建立明朝。他与焦玉共同编纂兵书《火龙经》。后来他与丞相胡惟庸交恶，于1375年去世，相传可能是被毒杀。

Xu Pu (1429–1499) was a Ming dynasty grand secretary born in Yixing. He passed the palace examination in 1454 as second-ranked jinshi, or bangyan, and entered the Hanlin Academy. He joined the Grand Secretariat in 1487 and became senior grand secretary in 1492, serving for twelve years with a quiet, consensus-seeking style.

He urged the Hongzhi Emperor to curb the influence of Li Guang and the Daoists without success. In 1497 he was put in charge of compiling the Collected Statutes of the Ming Dynasty. After retiring because of failing eyesight he died in 1499, canonised as Wenjing.

en:
Wang Shouren (1472–1529), known as Wang Yangming, was a Ming statesman, general and Neo-Confucian philosopher born in Yuyao, Zhejiang. After banishment in 1506 for offending the eunuch Liu Jin, he later became governor of Jiangxi.

In 1517–1518 he suppressed peasant revolts in Jiangxi, Fujian and Guangdong, and in 1519 crushed Zhu Chenhao, Prince of Ning, capturing him before he could take Nanjing.

As a thinker he rejected Zhu Xi's dualism and taught innate knowing and the unity of knowledge and action, and is regarded as a founder of the School of the Mind. In 1584, after his death, he was enshrined in the Confucian Temple.

王守仁（1472—1529），号阳明，世称王阳明，浙江余姚人，是明代的政治家、军事家与理学家。1506年他因得罪宦官刘瑾被贬谪，后来出任江西巡抚。

1517至1518年，他平定江西、福建、广东的民众起事；1519年又迅速平定宁王朱宸濠叛乱，在叛军攻取南京前将朱宸濠俘获。

思想上，他反对朱熹的二元论，提出“致良知”与“知行合一”之说，被视为心学一派的开创者之一。1584年，他在身后被从祀孔子庙廷。

Muhammad Salih Thattvi was a seventeenth-century Mughal metallurgist, astronomer and craftsman from Thatta in Sindh, active at the Mughal court in the mid-seventeenth century. He cast seamless celestial globes by the lost-wax process, following a technique pioneered in Kashmir in 1589–1590.

His globe of AH 1070 (1659–1660), twenty-one centimetres across with silver dots marking about 1018 stars, is in Delhi's Red Fort Museum; another of 1663–1664 in the Khalili Collection carries Arabic and Sanskrit inscriptions. He also made at least four astrolabes dated between 1661 and 1667.

他在伊斯兰历1070年（1659—1660年）所铸的天球仪直径21厘米，以银点标示约1018颗星，现存德里红堡博物馆；1663—1664年的一件藏于哈利利收藏，带有阿拉伯语和梵语铭文。他还制作了至少四件署年在1661—1667年间的星盘。

Mian Mir (c. 1550–1635), born Mian Mir Muhammad Qadiri, was a Qadiri Sufi saint who lived in Lahore. Claiming descent from the Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab, he founded the Mian Khel branch of the Qadiri order and became the spiritual instructor of the Mughal prince Dara Shikoh, eldest son of Shah Jahan.

He died in August 1635, and his disciple Dara Shikoh read his funeral oration. His shrine southeast of Lahore draws Muslim and Sikh devotees, and Mullah Shah Badakhshi succeeded him.

米安·米尔（约1550—1635），本名米安·米尔·穆罕默德·卡迪里，是居于拉合尔的卡迪里教团苏菲圣徒。他自称是哈里发欧麦尔·本·赫塔卜的后裔，开创了卡迪里教团的米安海勒支派，并成为莫卧儿皇子、沙贾汗长子达拉·舒科的灵性导师。

Reza Abbasi (c. 1565–1635), earlier called Aqa Reza, was the leading Persian miniaturist of the Isfahan school and the last great master of the Persian miniature. He joined Shah Abbas I's royal workshop young, and the shah granted him the honorific Abbasi in 1603.

As book illustration gave way to albums, he made his name with single muraqqa leaves showing one or two elegant figures on a spare garden ground. His works ranged from pure pen drawings to fully coloured paintings, and his style shaped later painters such as Mo'en Mosavver.

礼萨·阿巴西（约1565—1635），早年称阿迦·礼萨，是伊斯法罕画派最重要的波斯细密画家，也被视为最后一位波斯细密画大师。他年轻时便加入沙阿阿拔斯一世的皇家画室，1603年获沙阿赐号“阿巴西”。

在书籍插图让位于画册的时代，他以穆拉卡单页画著称，常以素淡园林为背景，只画一两个姿态优雅的人物。他的作品既有纯线描，也有通幅设色的画作，画风影响了穆因·穆萨维尔等后世画家。

Bahāʾ al-Dīn al-ʿĀmilī (1547–1621), known as Sheikh Bahāʾī, was a Twelver Shia polymath in Safavid Iran. Born near Baalbek in Ottoman Syria to a family from Jabal ʿĀmil, he was brought to Iran as a boy and completed his studies in Isfahan.

Trusted by Shah Abbas I, he planned the new capital Isfahan, including Naqsh-e Jahan Square and the Shah Mosque, and wrote over a hundred Arabic and Persian treatises on law, mathematics and astronomy.

His Persian Tashrīḥ al-Aflāk argued for the possibility of the Earth's motion. He died in Isfahan and was buried at Mashhad.

巴哈丁·阿米利（1547—1621），通称谢赫·巴哈伊，是萨法维伊朗的十二伊玛目派什叶派通才学者。他出生于奥斯曼叙利亚的巴勒贝克附近，家族来自阿米勒山，幼年随家人迁居伊朗，在伊斯法罕完成学业。

他深受沙阿阿拔斯一世倚重，主持了新都伊斯法罕的城市规划，包括纳克什·贾汗广场和沙阿清真寺，并以阿拉伯语和波斯语写下百余部涉及教法、数学与天文的著作。

他的波斯语作品《天体解剖》提出了地球运动的可能性。他卒于伊斯法罕，葬于马什哈德。

en:
Şerafeddin Sabuncuoğlu (1385–1468) was an Ottoman surgeon and physician who spent his career at the Darüşşifa hospital in Amasya and directed it for fourteen years. He began studying medicine at seventeen, in a city that was a centre of commerce and culture in the early Ottoman Empire.

In 1465, aged about eighty, he completed the Cerrahiyyetü'l-Haniyye (Imperial Surgery), the first illustrated surgical atlas written in Turkish. Its three chapters carry his own miniatures, including the first depictions of female surgeons. Drawing on al-Zahrawi's al-Taṣrīf, he added his own techniques, among them ligating the temporal artery for migraine.

谢拉夫丁·萨本久奥卢（1385—1468）是奥斯曼外科医生兼内科医师，长期在阿马西亚的达尔什法医院行医，并担任院长十四年。他十七岁开始学医，当时阿马西亚是奥斯曼帝国早期的商业与文化中心。

1465年，年约八旬的他完成《帝王外科学》，这是第一部用土耳其语写成的插图外科图谱。全书三章，配有他亲手绘制的插图，其中最早出现了女性外科医生的画像。该书虽借鉴宰赫拉威的《医学宝鉴》，也记载了他自创的技法，例如结扎颞动脉治疗偏头痛。

ʿAbd al-ʿAlī al-Bīrjandī (died 1528) was a Persian astronomer, mathematician and physicist who worked in Birjand, in Khurasan; his birth date is unrecorded. He produced a string of technical commentaries, chief among them the Sharḥ al-Tadhkirah on Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's astronomical treatise, completed in 1507–1508.

In the commentary he tested the claim that a falling stone disproves the Earth's rotation, arguing that a stone dropping perpendicular to the horizon could remain compatible with a moving Earth.

Birjandi also wrote on astronomical instruments and on constructing almanacs. He died in 1528 and was buried at Bojd near Birjand.

阿卜杜勒·阿里·比里詹迪（?—1528）是波斯天文学家、数学家与物理学家，在呼罗珊的比尔詹德治学，生年不详。他留下多部专业注释，其中最重要的是为纳西尔丁·图西的天文学著作所作的《〈提要〉注》，于1507—1508年完成。

他在《〈提要〉注》中检验了“落石可证地球静止”的说法，认为石块沿垂直于地平线的方向落下仍可与地球运动相容。

比里詹迪还写过天文仪器和编制历书方面的著作。他于1528年去世，葬于比尔詹德附近的布季德村。

en:
Lin Daoqian was a 16th-century Chinese pirate of Teochew origin and a native of Huilai in Guangdong. From the 1560s he raided the coasts of Guangdong and Fujian; in 1566 he attacked Zhao'an with 50 ships and was driven off by the Ming navy under Yu Dayou, fleeing via Penghu to Taiwan.

Repeatedly pardoned and restive, he fled overseas in 1573 and in 1578 established a base with two thousand followers in Patani on the Malay Peninsula.

After 1581 he may have settled in Patani, where he served as customs chief and cast cannon for its queen. Patani tradition says he died testing one of them.

林道乾是16世纪的中国海盗，潮州人，广东惠来人。1560年代起，他袭扰广东、福建沿海；1566年率战船五十艘攻打诏安，被俞大猷率领的明军水师击退，经澎湖逃往台湾。

他屡受招安又再度反叛，1573年逃亡海外，1578年率部众两千人在马来半岛的北大年建立据点。

1581年后他可能在北大年定居，管理海关并为当地女王铸造大炮。北大年当地相传，他在试射其中一门炮时身亡。

Zhu Biao (1355–1392) was the eldest son of the Hongwu Emperor and the founding crown prince of the Ming dynasty. Born to Zhu Yuanzhang and Lady Ma, he became heir in 1364 and crown prince at the Ming proclamation in 1368.

Educated in Confucian statecraft by Song Lian, he took part in daily government from 1377 and was known for his humanity.

Sent to Shaanxi in 1391 to assess a capital move to Xi'an, he presented a map and a memorial on his return. He fell ill and died in May 1392. His son Zhu Yunwen later reigned as the Jianwen Emperor.

朱标（1355—1392）是洪武帝的长子，明朝的开国皇太子。他为朱元璋与马氏之子，1364年被立为世子，1368年明朝建立时成为皇太子。

他在宋濂教导下学习儒家治国之术，1377年起参与日常政务，以仁厚著称。

1391年他奉命巡视陕西，考察迁都西安之事，归来后呈上地图和奏疏。他随后患病，于1392年5月去世。其子朱允炆后来继位，即建文帝。

Khlopko Kosolap (died 1603) was an ataman of a robber band in Russia during the Time of Troubles. Amid the great famine of 1601–1603 he commanded the largest such detachment, with up to six hundred men, near Moscow; many of the rebels were kholopy who fled estates when their masters refused to feed them.

In August 1603 the government sent a hundred streltsy under Ivan Basmanov against Khlopko. The rebels ambushed the troops and killed Basmanov on 12 September, but were routed; the wounded Khlopko was captured and soon executed.

赫洛普科·科索拉普（1603年卒）是俄罗斯混乱时期的一名匪帮首领。1601—1603年大饥荒期间，他率领其中最大的一支队伍在莫斯科近郊活动，人数多达六百人，许多叛乱者是因主人拒绝供养而逃离庄园的奴仆。

Lennart Torstensson (1603–1651) was a Swedish field marshal of the Thirty Years' War. A page to Gustavus Adolphus, he led the Swedish artillery from 1629 and helped win Breitenfeld in 1631. Captured at Alte Veste, he was imprisoned at Ingolstadt.

In 1641 he succeeded Banér as generalissimo, crushed the Imperials at the second Breitenfeld in 1642, invaded Denmark in the war named after him of 1643–1645, and won at Jankau in 1645. Crippled by gout, he resigned in 1645, was made a count, and governed Sweden's western provinces.

伦纳特·托尔斯滕松（1603—1651）是三十年战争中的瑞典陆军元帅。他早年是古斯塔夫·阿道夫的侍童，1629年执掌瑞典炮兵，在1631年的布莱登菲尔德战役中立下战功。他在阿尔特韦斯特被俘，囚于因戈尔施塔特。

1641年他接替巴纳出任全军总司令，在1642年的第二次布莱登菲尔德战役击溃帝国军，随后入侵丹麦——这场1643—1645年的战争以他的名字命名，又在1645年的扬考战役克敌。他因痛风致残，1645年辞职，后受封伯爵，统辖瑞典西部诸省。

Count Gustav Horn (1592–1657) was a Swedish field marshal of the Thirty Years' War. He studied warfare under Maurice of Orange, was seriously wounded at the siege of Riga in 1621, and became a field marshal in 1628.

As Gustavus Adolphus's second-in-command, he stopped Tilly's flank attack at Breitenfeld in 1631 after the Saxon allies fled. After the king's death in 1632, Horn and John Banér took command of Swedish forces in Germany.

Captured at Nördlingen in 1634, he was held at Burghausen until exchanged in 1642. He conquered most of Scania in 1644, became Count of Björneborg in 1651, and later governed Livonia.

Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, Viscount of Turenne (1611–1675), known as Turenne, was one of France's greatest generals. He trained under his uncle Maurice of Nassau.

In the Thirty Years' War he took Breisach in 1638 and became Marshal of France in 1643. He initially supported the Fronde but returned to royal service in 1651, defeated the Spanish at Arras (1654) and the Dunes (1658), and became Marshal General in 1660.

He converted to Catholicism in 1668. In 1675 he won at Turckheim and maneuvered around the Vosges in winter, driving the Imperials from Alsace, before he was killed by a cannonball at Salzbach.

蒂雷纳子爵亨利·德·拉图尔多韦涅（1611—1675），通称蒂雷纳，是法国最伟大的将领之一。他早年在舅父拿骚的毛里茨麾下受训。

三十年战争中，他于1638年攻克布赖萨赫，1643年成为法国元帅。他最初支持投石党运动，1651年重返王室阵营，又在阿拉斯（1654）和沙丘（1658）战胜西班牙军，1660年成为法国大元帅。

他于1668年改宗天主教。1675年他在蒂尔凯姆取胜，并在冬季绕过孚日山脉，将帝国军逐出阿尔萨斯，最终在萨斯巴赫被炮弹炸死。

Johann von Aldringen (1588–1634) was an imperial field marshal born in the Duchy of Luxembourg who served Spain from 1606 before entering imperial service in 1618. He fought beside Wallenstein at the Dessau Bridge in 1626, helped negotiate the Peace of Lübeck in 1629, and grew rich at the sack of Mantua in 1630.

As Tilly's artillery commander he was wounded at the Lech in April 1632, then succeeded Tilly and became a field marshal. He joined the plot against Wallenstein and was shot while retreating across the Isar at Landshut on 22 July 1634.

Otto Heinrich Fugger, Count of Kirchberg and Weissenhorn (1592–1644), was born in Augsburg into his famous banking family and became a professional soldier. He fought at the White Mountain in 1620, then entered Bavarian service in 1631 and captured Fulda.

Promoted Feldzeugmeister in 1632, he supported Wallenstein with six thousand men at the Alte Veste. In 1634 he succeeded the fallen Aldringen as commander and distinguished himself at Nördlingen, gaining the Golden Fleece from Spain and an imperial countship.

Appointed governor of Augsburg in 1635, he was later dismissed over his policies favouring Catholics. He died there on 12 October 1644.

Gottfried Heinrich Graf zu Pappenheim (1594–1632), a Bavarian nobleman who converted to Catholicism in 1614, became an imperial cavalry general in the Thirty Years' War. He gained experience of cavalry warfare in Polish service and was left for dead at the White Mountain in 1620. He ruthlessly crushed the Upper Austrian peasant revolt in 1626.

Made an imperial count in 1628, he helped storm Magdeburg in 1631 and, after Breitenfeld, covered the imperial retreat. Recalled to Wallenstein's army, he fell mortally wounded leading his cavalry at Lützen on 16 November 1632 and died soon afterwards.

Charles Bonaventure de Longueval, Count of Bucquoy (1571–1621), was a general born at Arras in the Spanish Netherlands. He entered the Army of Flanders young, fought at Nieuwpoort in 1600 and the Siege of Ostend, and served as General of the Artillery under Ambrogio Spinola. In 1613 he became governor of Hainaut.

At the outbreak of the Bohemian Revolt in 1618, Emperor Matthias gave him command of the Imperial army. He was beaten by Thurn at Lomnice, defeated Mansfeld at Sablat in 1619, and with Tilly won the Battle of White Mountain in 1620. He was killed at the siege of Neuhäusel in July 1621.

Franz von Mercy (c. 1597–1645), born at Longwy in Lorraine, became a field marshal and commander-in-chief of the Bavarian army in 1643. Wounded at Breitenfeld in 1631, he was captured and exchanged in 1634, and defended Rheinfelden against a Swedish siege until its food ran out.

In 1641 he protected the Imperial Diet at Regensburg from Banér's Swedes. He destroyed a French army at Tuttlingen in 1643, held Freiburg in 1644, and routed Turenne at Herbsthausen in 1645. He was killed by a musket shot at Nördlingen on 3 August 1645.

Ambrogio Spinola (1569–1630), Marquess of Los Balbases, was a Genoese nobleman and one of the ablest generals in Spanish pay. He entered Spanish service in 1602, raising nine thousand men at his own expense, and forced the garrison of Ostend to surrender. As commander-in-chief in Flanders he seized Rhine towns from Maurice of Nassau, a campaign that ruined him financially.

He overran the Palatinate early in the Thirty Years' War and crowned his career by taking Breda in 1625. Undermined by Olivares, he left Flanders in 1628 and died at the Siege of Casale in 1630.

Tommaso Caracciolo, Duke of Roccarainola (1572–1631), was a Neapolitan aristocrat who served Spain as a professional soldier. He began as a common infantryman. After fighting at the Siege of Ostend in 1601, he led a tercio in the War of the Montferrat Succession.

In the Bohemian-Palatine War he played a decisive part at the Battle of the White Mountain in 1620, holding off Hungarian and Cossack cavalry. Philip IV made him Duke of Roccarainola in 1625; the same year the French captured him in Liguria and held him for ransom. He died in 1631 travelling to Genoa as governor-general.

Peter Ernst von Mansfeld (c. 1580–1626), commonly called Ernst, was an illegitimate son of the Spanish stadtholder Count Peter Ernst von Mansfeld and was raised a Catholic in Luxembourg. From about 1610 he served the Protestant princes and became a leading mercenary general of the early Thirty Years' War.

Sent to aid the Bohemian rebels in 1618, he took Pilsen but was defeated at Sablat in 1619. He held the Upper Palatinate against Tilly in 1621 and beat him at Wiesloch in 1622, then entered Dutch service. Wallenstein routed him at the Dessau Bridge in 1626; retreating through Bosnia, he died near Sarajevo that November.

Heinrich Matthias von Thurn (1567–1640) was a Bohemian Protestant noble and leader of the Bohemian Revolt. After imperial service against the Turks, he became marshal of the Protestant nobility. In 1617 he demanded religious freedom from Ferdinand, and in May 1618 helped lead the Defenestration of Prague, opening the Thirty Years' War.

He commanded the Bohemian army, backed Frederick V as king, and fought at White Mountain in 1620. Exiled, he lost his Bohemian estates and served Sweden under Gustavus Adolphus. Captured by Wallenstein in 1633 and ransomed, he retired to Swedish Estonia and died at Pärnu in 1640.

Johan Banér (1596–1641) was a Swedish field marshal born at Djursholm in Uppland; he was four when his father was executed in the Linköping Bloodbath of 1600. Joining up in 1615, he distinguished himself at Pskov and became one of Gustavus Adolphus's foremost generals, leading the Swedish cavalry at Breitenfeld in 1631.

After Nördlingen he took command in Germany and restored Sweden's cause with victories at Wittstock in 1636 and Chemnitz in 1639. His last exploit was a midwinter surprise march on Regensburg in 1641, but the thawing ice prevented its capture. He died at Halberstadt in May 1641.

Wolderich Lappe was a knight of the Lappe family, landed lords in Hadeln on the Lower Elbe and followers of the dukes of Saxe-Lauenburg. In 1324 Duke Eric I pledged him jurisdictional rights in the parishes of Wolde and Groden for 200 marks, securing him steady revenues around Ritzebüttel.

In 1325 he appears in the first surviving charter to name Ritzebüttel, promising in a treaty not to move against two lords. Later charters attest his leading position in Hadeln.

Albrecht VI (born 1330) was count of Lindow-Ruppin, succeeding his father Ulrich II. In 1370 he pledged the lordship of Lindau to Prince John II of Anhalt-Köthen for 1300 marks and was forced to sell further villages to meet his debts.

Liutgard of Mecklenburg (c. 1289–1352) was the only child of John III, lord of Mecklenburg, who drowned off Poel in 1289, and Helena of Rügen. In 1302 she married Count Gerhard II of Hoya, a childless union; Gerhard died in 1312 or 1313.

In 1312 she married Count Adolf of Holstein-Kiel, again without issue, and in 1315 Adolf was slain in his bed at the Siegesburg in Segeberg by his castellan Hartwig Reventlow. Liutgard died in 1352.

en:
Ulrich II (c. 1300–3 February 1356) was count of Lindow-Ruppin, succeeding his father Ulrich I in the Brandenburg march. He married Agnes of Anhalt-Zerbst, and their children included Albrecht, later Count Albrecht VI, and Agnes, wife of John I of Mecklenburg-Stargard.

In 1334 he had to surrender lands around Rathenow and Friesack, but the margrave confirmed his rights to Gransee and Wusterhausen in 1347, and these became Brandenburg fiefs in 1349. The same year he sold Fürstenberg and bought Havelland estates around Glien and Rhinow.

en:
Alexander Pushkin (1799–1837), born in Moscow into a noble family and descended through his mother from Abram Gannibal, Peter the Great's African godson, is regarded as Russia's greatest poet and founder of modern Russian literature. His first poem was printed in 1814, at fifteen.

In 1820 he published his first long poem, Ruslan and Ludmila; that year his verses brought exile under Alexander I to the south and then confinement at Mikhailovskoye. Under police surveillance he wrote Boris Godunov, and his novel in verse Eugene Onegin appeared from 1825 to 1832.

Nicholas I made him a kamer-junker in 1833, a rank for young men, and Pushkin was furious. By 1836 he was deep in debt and facing rumours over his wife and the French officer d'Anthès. In an 1837 pistol duel d'Anthès shot him; he died two days later, and Glinka, Mussorgsky and Tchaikovsky based operas on his works.

亚历山大·普希金（1799—1837）生于莫斯科的贵族家庭，母系先祖是彼得大帝的黑人教子阿布拉姆·汉尼拔，被视为俄国最伟大的诗人和现代俄国文学的奠基人。1814年，十五岁的他发表了第一首诗。

1820年他发表首部长诗《鲁斯兰与柳德米拉》；同年，他的诗篇使他被亚历山大一世流放南方，后来又被软禁在母亲的米哈伊洛夫斯科耶庄园。在警察监视下，他写出戏剧《鲍里斯·戈都诺夫》，诗体小说《叶甫盖尼·奥涅金》在1825至1832年间陆续发表。

1833年尼古拉一世授予他通常只给年轻人的侍从官头衔，普希金勃然大怒。到1836年，他债台高筑，又被妻子与法国军官丹特斯的传闻所困。1837年的手枪决斗中他被丹特斯击中，两天后去世。格林卡、穆索尔斯基和柴可夫斯基都曾据他的作品谱写歌剧。

en:
Alexander Radishchev (1749–1802) was a Russian writer and social critic. Sent to the University of Leipzig in the 1760s, he returned steeped in Enlightenment ideas and entered Catherine the Great's civil service. In 1790 he privately printed A Journey from St Petersburg to Moscow, a fierce attack on serfdom and autocracy that Catherine condemned as Jacobin sedition.

Arrested and sentenced to death, he was exiled instead to Ilimsk in Siberia until 1797. Pardoned under Alexander I, he briefly helped draft legal reforms but, broken by persecution, took his own life in 1802.

亚历山大·拉季舍夫（1749—1802）是俄国作家与社会批评家。1760年代他被派往莱比锡大学学习，回国时深受启蒙思想熏陶，进入叶卡捷琳娜二世的政府任职。1790年，他自费印行《从彼得堡到莫斯科旅行记》，尖锐抨击农奴制与专制制度，被叶卡捷琳娜斥为雅各宾式煽动。

他被捕并判处死刑，后改判流放西伯利亚伊利姆斯克，直到1797年才获释。亚历山大一世即位后，他一度参与起草法律改革，但终因迫害摧折，于1802年自杀。

Aleksey Fyodorovich Adashev (1510–1561) was a low-born Russian statesman who became the closest lay adviser of Tsar Ivan IV. After the Moscow fires of 1547 he and the priest Sylvester headed the reforming government of Ivan's early years: the new Sudebnik law code was confirmed in 1550, and Kazan and Astrakhan fell in 1552 and 1556.

As head of the Petition Office he also led Russian diplomacy. In 1560 he was exiled to Livonia, and he died imprisoned in Dorpat in 1561.

Boris Ivanovich Morozov (1590–1661) was a boyar who headed the Russian government in the early reign of Tsar Alexis, whose tutor he became in 1634. In 1648 he arranged Alexis's marriage to Maria Miloslavskaya and soon after married her sister Anna, becoming the tsar's brother-in-law.

He cut salaries and imposed a heavy salt tax, provoking the Salt Riot of 1648; the tsar saved him from the mob by a feigned exile to the Kirillo-Belozersky Monastery. Back in Moscow, he helped draft the 1649 legal code, the Sobornoye Ulozheniye, and continued to direct the government in the early 1650s.

Ernst Johann von Biron (1690–1772), a Courland nobleman, entered Anna Ivanovna's court and became her all-powerful favourite after she took the Russian throne in 1730; his dominance was dubbed the Bironovshchina. In 1737 he was elected Duke of Courland, ruling the duchy from Saint Petersburg.

Anna's will made him regent for the infant Ivan VI in October 1740, but within weeks Münnich's coup overthrew him and he spent 1740 to 1761 in exile. Peter III recalled him, and Catherine II restored him to Courland in 1763, which he passed to his son Peter in 1769.

en:
Fyodor Isakovich Baykov (c. 1612–c. 1663) was the first Russian ambassador sent to China. In 1654 Tsar Alexis dispatched him to the Shunzhi Emperor to establish regular trade between Moscow and Beijing. He travelled across Dzungaria and the Gobi, but was stopped at Kalgan, where officials mistook his advance messenger for the ambassador.

He reached the Forbidden City in March 1656. His refusal to kowtow except to the emperor himself and his insistence on presenting his credentials directly left negotiations deadlocked; after months of isolation the court expelled him. He returned to Moscow, leaving a detailed account of his journey.

en:
Grigory Orlov (1734–1783) was a Russian guards officer and favourite of Empress Catherine the Great. Wounded at Zorndorf in 1758, he became Catherine's lover and, with his brothers, led the coup of 1762 that deposed her husband Peter III and placed her on the throne. Made a count and then, in 1772, a prince of the Holy Roman Empire, he headed the Free Economic Society and organized Moscow's response to the plague of 1771.

He patronized scholars and painters and commissioned the Great Gatchina Palace. After failed peace talks at Focșani he lost favour and died in Moscow in 1783.

Ivan Ivanovich Betskoy (1704–1795), born in Stockholm to Field Marshal Prince Ivan Trubetskoy and his Swedish mistress, was Catherine II's chief adviser on education. He spent years in Paris among Enlightenment thinkers including Rousseau, helped Catherine seize power from Peter III in 1762, and in 1763 presented his Statute for the Education of the Youth of Both Sexes, inspired by Rousseau.

He oversaw the Smolny Institute for noble girls, founded foundling homes in Moscow in 1764 and Saint Petersburg in 1770, and served as president of the Imperial Academy of Arts from 1764 to 1794, building Russia's first unified public education system.

Ivan Ivanovich Shuvalov (1727–1797) was a Russian patron of education and the arts during the Enlightenment. A Moscow-born court page, he became Empress Elizabeth's favourite in 1749. With Mikhail Lomonosov he secured Elizabeth's approval in 1755 for Moscow University, becoming its first curator, and in 1757 he founded the Academy of the Three Noble Arts in his Saint Petersburg palace, serving as its first president.

From 1763 to 1777 he travelled Europe, corresponding with Voltaire and Diderot and buying art for the Academy and the Hermitage. Catherine II made him High Chamberlain in 1777.

Joseph Bové (1784–1834) was a neoclassical architect who rebuilt Moscow after the great fire of 1812. Born in St Petersburg to a Neapolitan painter, he trained in Moscow. In 1813 the Moscow Building Commission placed him in charge of façade design for the reconstructed city, approving new façades and enforcing the street lines of the rebuilding plan.

He laid out Red Square and Theatre Square, rebuilt the Manege, erected the Triumphal Arch at Tverskaya Zastava, and designed his most famous building, the Bolshoi Theatre, opened in 1825. He died in Moscow in 1834.

Grigory Lukyanovich Skuratov-Belsky, known as Malyuta Skuratov, was a leader of Ivan the Terrible's Oprichnina. He rose to prominence in 1569 through the trial and execution of Prince Vladimir of Staritsa, a possible claimant to the throne, and the same year strangled the former Metropolitan Philip II for denouncing the Oprichnina. His daughter Maria married Boris Godunov in 1570.

In January 1571 he led a punitive expedition against Novgorod, killing thousands suspected of treason. He was killed in 1573 storming Weissenstein in the Livonian War and buried at the Joseph-Volokolamsk Monastery.
