Michael Maddox (1747–1822) was an English showman and theatre manager who settled in Russia. After bringing a museum of mechanical curiosities to Russia in 1766, he returned to Moscow and in 1776 joined Prince Pyotr Urusov's theatre company.

When their wooden Znamensky Theatre burned down in 1780, Maddox bought Urusov's share and built the brick Petrovsky Theatre on Petrovka Street, Moscow's first permanent opera house and the direct predecessor of the Bolshoi Theatre. In 1792 financial troubles forced its transfer to the state, and he received a life pension from Empress Maria Feodorovna.

Prince Mikhail Shcherbatov (1733–1790) was a Russian statesman, historian and political thinker of an ancient boyar family. He defended serfdom and the nobility's old privileges, while holding up the British constitutional monarchy and separation of powers as an ideal. He represented the Yaroslavl nobility at Catherine II's Legislative Commission of 1767 and became imperial historiographer in 1768.

His seven-volume History of Russia from the Earliest Times appeared from 1771, followed by the utopian Journey to the Land of Ophir (1784). A founder of Russian conservatism, he attacked court morals in On the Corruption of Morals in Russia, published posthumously in 1797.

米哈伊洛·谢尔巴托夫王公（1733—1790）出身古老的波雅尔家族，是俄罗斯帝国的政治家、历史学家和政治思想家。他维护农奴制和贵族的古老特权，同时推崇英国的君主立宪与权力分立制度。他在1767年代表雅罗斯拉夫尔贵族出席叶卡捷琳娜二世召集的立法委员会，1768年出任帝国史官。

他的七卷本《俄罗斯远古史》自1771年起陆续刊行，此后又写成乌托邦作品《奥菲尔之地游记》（1784）。他是俄罗斯保守主义的奠基人之一，在身后于1797年出版的《论俄罗斯道德之败坏》中抨击宫廷风气。

Mikhail Vasilyevich Lomonosov (1711–1765) was Russia's first major natural scientist and a poet who shaped the modern Russian literary language. Born near Kholmogory, a fisherman's son, he left in 1730 with a fish convoy for Moscow, where he entered the Slavic Greek Latin Academy by posing as a nobleman's son.

He joined the Academy of Sciences in 1735, studied in Germany at Marburg and Freiberg from 1736, and reached St Petersburg in 1741. In 1745 he became professor of chemistry, the Academy's first Russian member in natural science. In 1748 he set up Russia's first chemistry laboratory, and in 1755 drew up the first plan for Moscow University.

On 26 May 1761 he watched Venus cross the Sun, saw an arc of light around it, and correctly concluded that Venus has an atmosphere. He died in St Petersburg in 1765, and in 1940 Moscow University was renamed for him.

Born near [ShowLocationName('kholmogory')], a fisherman's son, he left in 1730 with a fish convoy for Moscow, where he entered the Slavic Greek Latin Academy by posing as a nobleman's son.

He joined the Academy of Sciences in 1735, studied in Germany at Marburg and Freiberg from 1736, and reached St Petersburg in 1741. en:
Mikhail Speransky (1772–1839) was the chief reforming statesman of Alexander I's Russia. A village priest's son from Vladimir Province, he became the tsar's closest adviser after 1807. His plans produced the ministry system and, in 1810, the State Council, of which he became the first state secretary. Aristocratic opposition brought him dismissal and exile to Perm in 1812.

He later served as governor of Penza and governor-general of Siberia, returning to the State Council in 1821. Under Nicholas I, he directed the compilation of the Complete Collection of Laws, the basis of the Code of Laws of the Russian Empire, published in 1833. He was made count weeks before his death in 1839.

米哈伊尔·斯佩兰斯基（1772—1839）是亚历山大一世时期俄国最主要的改革派政治家。他是弗拉基米尔省乡村神父之子，1807年后成为沙皇最亲近的顾问。他主持的改革奠定了部制，并于1810年促成设立国务会议，本人出任首任国务秘书。1812年，因贵族反对，他被解职并流放彼尔姆。

en:
Nikon (1605–1681), born Nikita Minin to Mordvin peasants near Nizhny Novgorod, became the seventh Patriarch of Moscow and all Rus' in 1652. After his three children died, he became a monk and took the name Nikon.

A confidant of Tsar Alexis, he largely ruled Russia during the Polish campaigns. From 1654 he convened councils that corrected the service books after Greek models, splitting conservatives into the Old Believers' Raskol.

His assertion of church supremacy over the tsar alienated Alexis, and in December 1667 the Great Moscow Synod deposed and exiled him north, while confirming his reforms. He died returning from exile in 1681.

作为沙皇阿列克谢的密友，他在对波兰战争期间实际主持俄罗斯国政。1654年起，他接连召开宗教会议，仿照希腊经书修订礼仪书，反对派由此分裂出去，形成旧礼仪派的“大分裂”。

他主张教权高于沙皇，招致阿列克谢疏远；1667年12月，莫斯科大公会议将他罢黜并流放北方，同时认可了他的改革。1681年他在流放归来途中去世。

en:
Nikolay Novikov (1744–1818) was a Russian writer and publisher, often called the first Russian journalist and a leading voice of the Russian Enlightenment. He edited the Moscow Gazette and brought out satirical journals modelled on The Spectator, attacking serfdom and social abuses and even drawing printed replies from Catherine the Great.

Backed by his masonic network, his press issued roughly a third of all books published in Russia, and he promoted Shakespeare among Russian readers. In 1792 Catherine imprisoned him without trial in the Shlisselburg Fortress; Paul I freed him in 1796, but he never returned to public life.

Prince Sergei Trubetskoy (1790–1860) was a Russian guards colonel and a leader of the Decembrist revolt. A veteran of 1812–1814, he rose to colonel in 1821 and headed the reform-minded Northern Society.

Chosen the rebels' dictator for the Senate Square rising of December 1825, he lost his nerve and hid in the Austrian embassy instead. Arrested and sentenced to death, he was instead sent to lifelong hard labour in the Nerchinsk mines. His wife Ekaterina was the first Decembrist wife to follow him into exile. Amnestied in 1856, he died in Moscow in 1860.

en:
Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst (1729–1796), born at Stettin to a minor German princely family, became Catherine the Great, empress of Russia for thirty-four years. In 1744 she converted to Orthodoxy, taking the name Catherine, and in 1745 married Peter, grandson of Peter the Great. In July 1762, with the guards and the Orlov brothers, she overthrew her husband after a reign of seven months and was crowned in Moscow that September.

The Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774 opened the Black Sea and made Crimea a protectorate, which she annexed in 1783. She placed Stanisław Poniatowski on the Polish throne, and the partitions of 1793 and 1795 erased the Commonwealth from the map.

At home she issued charters to the nobility and towns in 1785, yet serfdom remained its basis, as Pugachev's rebellion of 1773–1775 showed. She died of a stroke in November 1796 and her son Paul succeeded.

1768—1774年的俄土战争打开了黑海通道，使克里米亚成为俄国保护国，1783年将其吞并。她把斯坦尼斯瓦夫·波尼亚托夫斯基扶上波兰王位，1793年和1795年的瓜分把波兰从地图上抹去。

国内，她于1785年颁布面向贵族和城市的特许状，但农奴制仍是国家的根基，1773—1775年的普加乔夫起义即其明证。1796年11月她死于中风，其子保罗继位。

Sylvester was a priest of Moscow's Cathedral of the Annunciation and, with Aleksey Adashev, the most powerful adviser to Tsar Ivan IV. After the great Moscow fire of 1547 he became the leading voice of the Chosen Council, shaping the government's church and administrative reforms until 1560.

Having lost Ivan's favour, he withdrew to monasteries in the north, where under the monastic name Spiridon he copied books. He is thought to have died around 1566.

Yemelyan Pugachev (c. 1742–1775) was a Don Cossack who led the greatest peasant uprising of Catherine the Great's reign. A veteran of the Seven Years' War and the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774, he deserted in 1770 and drifted among discontented Cossacks and Old Believers.

In 1773 he proclaimed himself the murdered tsar Peter III and promised an end to serfdom, drawing a huge rebel army that overran the Volga and Urals lands and burned Kazan in 1774. Defeated near Tsaritsyn, he was handed over by his own men and beheaded in Moscow in January 1775.

叶梅利扬·普加乔夫（约1742—1775）是顿河哥萨克，领导了叶卡捷琳娜二世时期规模最大的农民起义。他曾参加七年战争和1768—1774年的俄土战争，1770年逃离军队，在不满的哥萨克与旧礼仪派信徒中流亡。

1773年，他自称是已遇害的沙皇彼得三世，许诺废除农奴制，聚集起庞大的起义军，席卷伏尔加河与乌拉尔之间的土地，并于1774年焚毁喀山。他在察里津附近战败，被部下出卖，1775年1月在莫斯科被斩首。

en:
Yury Matveyevich Felten, born Georg Friedrich Veldten (1730–1801) to a German family in Russian service, was an architect favoured by Catherine the Great. From 1752 to 1762 he assisted Bartolomeo Rastrelli on the Winter Palace, then designed the Old Hermitage, the Zubov wing of the Catherine Palace and the Chesme Palace.

He built the lifting machine that moved the giant granite pedestal of the Bronze Horseman, and in 1783 completed the celebrated iron railing of the Summer Garden. He taught at the Imperial Academy of Arts from 1764 and directed it from 1789 until his death.

尤里·马特维耶维奇·费尔滕（1730—1801）原名格奥尔格·弗里德里希·费尔滕，出身于一个供职俄国的德意志家庭，是深受叶卡捷琳娜大帝信任的建筑师。1752至1762年，他作为巴尔托洛梅奥·拉斯特雷利的助手参与冬宫建造，此后设计了旧艾尔米塔什、叶卡捷琳娜宫祖博夫配楼和切什梅宫。

他还造出起重装置，搬运了青铜骑士雕像的巨型花岗岩基座；1783年完成了著名的夏花园铁栅栏。他自1764年起在帝国艺术学院任教，1789年出任院长，直至去世。

en:
Bernard of Ravensberg (died 1346) was a younger son of Count Otto III of Ravensberg and Hedwig of Lippe. He first followed a church career, as provost of Schildesche and a canon at Osnabrück and Münster, until his elder brother Otto IV died in 1328 and he succeeded to the county as the last male of the Ravensberg-Calvelage line.

He kept the county out of the great feuds of his day, and having no children arranged for his niece Margaret and her husband Gerhard of Jülich to inherit. He died in September 1346.

伯恩哈德·冯·拉芬斯贝格（？—1346）是拉芬斯贝格伯爵奥托三世与利珀的海德维希的幼子。他本走教会道路，曾任希尔德舍修道院院长、奥斯纳布吕克与明斯特的法政牧师，直到1328年兄长奥托四世去世，才继位为拉芬斯贝格伯爵，是拉芬斯贝格-卡尔费拉格家族的最后一位男嗣。

他使伯国避开当时的各大纷争，因无子嗣，安排侄女玛格丽特及其丈夫于利希的格哈德继承领地。他于1346年9月去世。

en:
Margaret of Ravensberg (c. 1320–1389) was the daughter of Count Otto IV of Ravensberg and Margaret of Berg-Windeck. When her uncle Bernard, the last male count, died without issue in 1346, she inherited Ravensberg; two years later the death of her maternal uncle Adolf IX of Berg brought her the County of Berg as well.

Through her marriage to Gerhard VI of Jülich, both counties passed to the House of Jülich. She was the mother of William, the first Duke of Berg, and died in February 1389.

玛格丽特·冯·拉芬斯贝格（约1320—1389）是拉芬斯贝格伯爵奥托四世与贝格-温德克的玛格丽特之女。1346年，她的叔叔、家族末代男嗣伯恩哈德无嗣而终，她由此继承拉芬斯贝格；两年后舅父贝格伯爵阿道夫六世去世，她又继承了贝格伯国。

Margaret of Berg-Windeck (c. 1285–1340) was the daughter of Henry of Berg, lord of Windeck, and Agnes of the Mark. In 1313 she married Count Otto IV of Ravensberg. Their daughters were Hedwig, wife of Duke William of Brunswick-Lüneburg, and Margaret, who in 1338 married Gerhard of Jülich.

When Otto died in 1328 Ravensberg passed to his brother Bernard, and the countess last appears in charters in 1339. Her daughter Margaret inherited Ravensberg in 1346 and the County of Berg in 1348.

Otto III (c. 1246–1306) was count of Ravensberg from 1249. As his father Louis died while he was a minor, Bernard III of Lippe held the regency and occupied Ravensberg Castle before Otto was installed. In 1267 he fought for Archbishop Engelbert II of Cologne at the Battle of Zülpich.

On 5 March 1271 he married Hedwig of Lippe, and in 1293 founded a canonry at Bielefeld, where he and his wife were buried. His son Otto IV succeeded him.

en:
Otto IV (c. 1276–1328) was count of Ravensberg from 1306 until his death, the son of Otto III and Hedwig of Lippe. Destined for the church, he became a canon at Osnabrück and Münster, but returned to secular life to succeed his father.

In 1313 he married Margaret of Berg-Windeck, who bore him only daughters and no son. Through his daughter Margaret's marriage to Gerhard of Jülich, Ravensberg later passed to the counts of Jülich.

en:
Gleb Rostislavich (died 30 June 1177) was prince of Ryazan and ancestor of its Rurikid branch, a son of Rostislav Yaroslavich. In 1145 his father sent him to rule Ryazan, but a Suzdalian siege drove him to the Polovtsians in 1146. He founded Glebov in 1159 and later secured Ryazan.

In 1176 he burned Moscow and sacked Bogolyubovo, but Vsevolod the Big Nest defeated him on the Koloksha in 1177, capturing him and his sons. Gleb died in prison at Vladimir after refusing freedom in exchange for Ryazan.

格列布·罗斯季斯拉维奇（？—1177年6月30日）是梁赞王公、留里克王朝梁赞支系的始祖，罗斯季斯拉夫·雅罗斯拉维奇之子。1145年父亲派他出镇梁赞，但1146年苏兹达尔军队围攻梁赞，迫使他投奔波洛伏齐人。1159年他建立格列博夫城，后来坐稳了梁赞公位。

1176年他焚毁莫斯科、洗劫博戈柳博沃，1177年却在科洛克沙河被弗谢沃洛德·大窝击败，与诸子一同被俘。格列布被押往弗拉基米尔入狱，因拒绝以放弃梁赞换取自由，于6月30日死于狱中。

en:
Igor Glebovich (died 1194) was a prince of Ryazan, the second son of Gleb Rostislavich. He fought beside his father at the Koloksha battle in 1177, where Vsevolod the Big Nest captured him, and after Gleb died in prison Ryazan was held jointly by Igor and his brothers Roman and Vladimir.

In 1180 he backed Roman in a feud against their other brothers, and in 1186 Vsevolod the Big Nest's intervention forced the Ryazan princes to swear submission. His son Ingvar later ruled Ryazan.

en:
Ingvar Igorevich, in baptism Kosma (died 1235), was prince of Ryazan from 1217. In 1207 he was among the Ryazan princes accused of treason and carried off to prison by Vsevolod the Big Nest of Vladimir, and he was released only in 1212. He escaped the congress at Isady in 1217, where his cousin Gleb Vladimirovich massacred his rivals and Ingvar's brothers died.

en:
Ivan II Ivanovich, called Korotopol (died 1343), was prince of Ryazan, son of Ivan Yaroslavich. He is thought to have succeeded in 1327 after his father was executed by Öz Beg Khan of the Golden Horde, and later campaigned with Moscow against Novgorod and with a Horde army against Smolensk.

On the Smolensk march he robbed his cousin Alexander of Pronsk, took him to Pereyaslavl and killed him there. In 1342 Alexander's son brought Tatar troops against him and besieged Pereyaslavl; Ivan resisted for a day, fled by night and died the following year.

Konstantin Romanovich (died 1306) was the youngest son of Grand Prince Roman Olgovich of Ryazan and ruled Ryazan from 1299. In autumn 1301 Prince Daniil Alexandrovich of Moscow invaded, defeated a Tatar force Konstantin had hired, and captured him through a ruse, reportedly the treachery of his own boyars.

Daniil planned to free him after peace but died in 1303, and his successor Yury Danilovich ordered Konstantin killed in 1306. His son Vasily succeeded in Ryazan.

en:
Oleg II Ivanovich (died 1402) was grand prince of Ryazan from about 1350 and a persistent rival of Moscow. In 1365 he defeated a raiding Horde army under Tagai, but in 1371 Dmitri of Moscow's troops routed him at Skornishchevo and drove him from the throne. In the 1380 Kulikovo campaign he negotiated with Mamai and Jogaila without joining the battle.

After seizing Kolomna in 1385, he made peace through the mediation of Sergius of Radonezh and in 1387 married his son Fyodor to Dmitri's daughter Sofia. He died in July 1402, later venerated as a Ryazan saint.

en:
Oleg Ingvarevich, called the Red or the Handsome (c. 1215–1258), was the only senior Ryazan prince to survive Batu's invasion of 1237–1238. Said to have been captured at Kolomna, he refused the khan's demand to convert and was spared for his rare beauty.

He returned to ruined Ryazan in 1243, the first Russian prince to visit Karakorum and return alive. Summoned and detained by the Horde in 1250, he was freed in 1252, took monastic vows, and died on 20 March 1258.

Roman Olgovich (1237–19 July 1270) was grand prince of Ryazan from 1258, only son of Oleg the Red. He inherited a principality recovering from the Mongol sack and for twelve years complied with the Horde to keep it from ruin.

A tax collector slandered him to Khan Mengu-Timur, who summoned him in 1270 and offered death or conversion. Roman refused, was tortured and mutilated, then executed, and is venerated as an Orthodox martyr. Before leaving he divided his lands among his sons, including Konstantin.

Svyatoslav Yaroslavich (died 1145) was a Rurikid prince of Ryazan and Murom, son of Yaroslav Svyatoslavich of Murom. On his father's death in 1129 the lands were divided: his elder brother Yury took Murom, while Svyatoslav and his younger brother Rostislav received the Ryazan region.

In 1143, after Yury's death, Svyatoslav moved to Murom's senior throne and ceded Ryazan to Rostislav. He died in Murom two years later. His son Vladimir later became grand prince of Ryazan.

en:
Fyodor Yuryevich (died 1348) was prince of Rzhev and Fomin, from the Smolensk branch of the Rurik dynasty, who served the princes of Moscow. In 1314 Yuri Danilovich of Moscow sent him with Prince Afanasy Danilovich to Novgorod to expel the governors of Grand Prince Mikhail Yaroslavich of Tver. They seized the city.

But after Mikhail defeated the Novgorodians near Torzhok in 1315, Fyodor was handed over and lost his Rzhev appanage. He kept part of Fomin, later served as the grand prince's namestnik in Novgorod, and died there on 1 December 1348.

en:
John I of Saarbrücken (c. 1260–1342) was count of Saarbrücken from 1308, the son of Count Simon IV and Margaret of Broyes. In 1285 he inherited part of the lordship of Commercy from his mother, and from 1297 served the dukes of Lorraine, campaigning in Flanders for France.

He joined King Henry VII's embassy to the papal court at Avignon in 1309 and fought with the emperor's auxiliaries in Italy in 1313, where he was captured. He granted town rights to Saarbrücken in 1322 and Commercy in 1324, and died on 23 January 1342.

John II of Saarbrücken (1310/1313–1381) was count of Saarbrücken from 1342. The son of Simon of Saarbrücken-Commercy and Margaret of Savoy, he received the county on his grandfather John I's death in 1342, while most of Commercy went to his cousin.

He fought for France and was captured with King John II at Poitiers in 1356, imprisoned in England until 1360. He later served France on embassies to the emperor and England and was made Grand Bouteiller in 1364. He died on 11 March 1381, leaving Saarbrücken to his daughter Johanna.

en:
Jean II de Sarrebruck-Commercy (died 1344) was a younger son of Jean I, count of Saarbrücken and lord of Commercy, and Mahaut d'Apremont. He inherited the castle of Commercy as sire of Commercy-Château-Haut, while his nephew Jean IV kept the county of Saarbrücken and the Château-Bas portion of the town. In 1324 he and his father granted Commercy its charter of franchises.

In 1331 he married Alix de Joinville, heiress of Briquenay and Vénizy, who brought him those Champagne lordships. Their sons Simon II and Jean III later ruled Commercy.

Simon IV of Saarbrücken-Commercy (c. 1244–1308) was count of Saarbrücken and lord of Commercy. Son of Countess Mathilde of Saarbrücken, he shared in governing from 1266, succeeded his mother in 1274, and bought off his half-brothers' claims.

He faced the bishop of Metz, who claimed the county as a lapsed fief; allied with Duke Frederick III of Lorraine, he won St. Wendel and in 1277 settled with the bishop to hold the county as his fief. By his wife Margaret he fathered Johann I.

Simon of Saarbrücken-Commercy (c. 1284–1325) was the eldest son of Count Johann I of Saarbrücken, marked out as sole heir to both Saarbrücken and Commercy. In 1309 he married Margaret of Savoy, daughter of Louis I, lord of Vaud, who bore him a son, Johann II, and daughters.

Simon died before his father in 1325, overturning the planned succession: his younger brother Johann was designated heir to Commercy, while his young son Johann was designated heir to Saarbrücken.

Shwetaungtet, also called Anawrahta I of Sagaing (1313–1339), ruled Sagaing as a usurper from 1335/36 to 1339. His father Tarabya had followed Saw Yun's revolt of 1315 and took over Sagaing after Saw Yun died in 1327, ruling for his infant sons. Shwetaungtet had the weaker claim but moved before the boys grew up: in 1335/36 he staged a palace coup and imprisoned his father.

He could not get hold of the boys. Queen Saw Hnaung and the minister Nanda Pakyan hid them at Mindon in Pinya and paid the minister to keep silent. In 1339 Shwetaungtet found them and led an expedition to bring them back.

His father's loyalists killed him at the palace soon afterwards. Nanda Pakyan won the fighting that followed, executed Tarabya and placed Kyaswa on the throne.

zh:
瑞当代，又称阿奴律陀一世（1313—1339），1335/36至1339年以篡位者的身份统治实皆。他的父亲答里必牙曾追随苏云在1315年起事，1327年苏云去世后执掌实皆，代管苏云的幼子们。瑞当代继承权更弱，于是趁王子们尚未成年下手，1335/36年发动宫廷政变，囚禁父王。

可是他抓不到那几个孩子——绍南王后与首相南达巴坚把他们藏在彬牙境内的敏东，并贿赂这位首相守口如瓶。1339年，瑞当代查出下落，率军前往带回诸王子。

不久他便在宫中被父王的党羽杀死。南达巴坚在随后的战斗中获胜，处死德勒帕耶基，扶立加苏瓦为王。

en:
Kyaswa (1323–1349), the eldest son of Sagaing's founder Saw Yun, was king from 1339 to 1349. He was not yet four when his father died in 1327 and his uncle Tarabya I took the throne. After Tarabya's son Shwetaungtet seized power in 1335/36, Kyaswa was hidden for three years at Mindon in Pinya.

In 1339 Chief Minister Nanda Pakyan crushed the coups, executed Tarabya and crowned the sixteen-year-old, then went on running the government himself. The reign was largely peaceful: Kyaswa kept the peace with Pinya by marrying Saw Pa Oh, daughter of King Uzana I, and it held even after Uzana lost his throne.

An inscription of 1343 or 1344 records his gifts of land and a monastery. He died around March 1349 without a male heir, and his brother succeeded him.

zh:
加苏瓦（1323—1349）是实皆开国君主苏云的长子，1339年至1349年在位。1327年父亲去世时他还不满四岁，叔父德勒帕耶基继位。1335/36年德勒帕耶基之子瑞当代篡位，加苏瓦被送到彬牙境内的敏东躲藏了三年。

1339年，首相南达巴坚平定政变、处死德勒帕耶基，拥立十六岁的加苏瓦为王，朝政仍由他自己主持。这一朝大体太平：加苏瓦迎娶彬牙国王乌兹那一世之女绍巴奥，稳住了与彬牙的关系，即便乌兹那后来失位，和平仍然维持。

1343或1344年的碑文记录了他捐出的土地与寺院。1349年3月前后，加苏瓦去世，没有留下男嗣，王位传给了他的弟弟。

en:
Nawrahta Minye (1326–1349), also called Anawrahta II, was king of Sagaing for just over seven months in 1349. In 1336 his cousin Shwetaungtet seized the throne, and he spent three years exiled at Mindon in Pinya before the family returned in 1339.

Chief Minister Nanda Pakyan then crowned his brother Kyaswa and ran the government, leaving Minye a nominal role. He came to the throne in 1349, when Kyaswa died without a male heir, taking the reign name Anawrahta. He found a white elephant and styled himself Hsinbyushin, Lord of the White Elephant.

He strained the peace with Pinya by sheltering Nawrahta, governor of Pinle, who had fled its king, though no war followed. He died in November 1349, childless, and his younger brother Tarabya II succeeded him.

zh:
瑙亚塔明耶（1326—1349），又称阿奴律陀二世，1349年为实皆国王，在位仅七个多月。1336年堂兄瑞当代篡位，他在彬牙的敏东流亡三年，1339年随家人返回实皆。

首相南达巴坚随即拥立他的兄长加苏瓦为王并掌理国政，明耶只有名义上的角色。1349年加苏瓦去世，没有男嗣，他继位为王，取王号阿奴律陀。他得到一头白象，遂自称辛标信，意为白象王。

宾里总督瑙亚塔出逃彬牙国王，他予以庇护，使对彬牙的和平关系趋于紧张，不过并未开战。1349年11月他去世，没有子嗣，由弟弟德勒帕耶艾继位。

en:
Saw Hnaung (1296–?), also called Kodawgyi, was the chief queen consort of the Sagaing kingdom in Upper Burma. A daughter of King Kyawswa of Pagan and Queen Saw Soe, she was chief queen to two kings of Sagaing, Saw Yun and Tarabya I.

Her sons Kyaswa, Nawrahta Minye and Tarabya II each reigned as king of Sagaing, while her daughter Soe Min Kodawgyi became the mother of Thado Minbya, founder of the Ava kingdom. Saw Hnaung was also a paternal aunt of King Swa Saw Ke of Ava.

绍南（1296—？），又称科道基，是上缅甸实皆王国的首席王后。她是蒲甘国王觉苏瓦与王后绍索之女，先后为实皆两位国王苏云与德勒帕耶基的首席王后。

en:
Saw Yun (c. 1299–5 February 1327) was the founder of the Sagaing kingdom in Upper Burma. The eldest son of King Thihathu of Myinsaing–Pinya and Queen Yadanabon, he was angered when his father named his adopted stepbrother Uzana I heir, and in 1315 crossed the Irrawaddy to build Sagaing, where he repelled two Pinya expeditions by 1317. He remained nominally loyal to his father while ruling Sagaing in practice.

In 1318 he formed the thousand-strong Sagaing cavalry regiment. After Thihathu's death in 1325 the two kingdoms split, and Saw Yun died in February 1327; his three sons all ruled Sagaing.

zh:
苏云（约1299—1327年2月5日）是上缅甸实皆王国的开创者。他是敏象—彬牙国王梯诃都与王后雅达娜邦的长子，父亲立养子、继兄乌兹那为王储，苏云心怀不满，于1315年渡过伊洛瓦底江前往实皆筑城，至1317年两次击退彬牙的讨伐。他名义上仍效忠父亲，实际上统治着实皆。

1318年他组建了千人规模的实皆骑兵团。1325年梯诃都死后，实皆与彬牙正式分裂，他于1327年2月去世；他的三个儿子后来都登上了实皆王位。

en:
Soe Min Kodawgyi (born 1322 or earlier) was the eldest daughter of Saw Yun, founder of Sagaing, and the mother of Thado Minbya, the future founder of Ava. In 1335–1336 she fled Sagaing with her husband Thado Hsinhtein when her cousin Shwetaungtet seized the throne. They spent three years at Mindon inside Pinya and returned in 1339, when her brother Kyaswa became king.

In February 1352 her brother Tarabya II died heirless, her husband also dead, so she became kingmaker: she married the court official Minbyauk Thihapate, who took the throne, and she became chief queen.

As Maw Shan raiders struck Sagaing in the 1350s she twice sought a Pinya alliance, but Pinya withdrew after a devastating raid in 1358–1359. In 1364 Thado Minbya overthrew her husband.

索敏（1322年或更早出生）是实皆开国君主苏云的长女，也是日后阿瓦王国的建立者德多明帕耶之母。1335至1336年间，堂兄瑞当代篡位，她与丈夫德多信滕逃离实皆，在彬牙境内的敏东住了三年，1339年弟弟加苏瓦即位后返回。

1352年2月，弟弟德勒帕耶艾死后无嗣，她的丈夫也已去世，她成了拥立新王的人：下嫁朝臣明波梯诃波帝，使其登基，自己成为王后。

1350年代，猛卯的掸人不断袭扰实皆，她两次寻求与彬牙结盟；1358至1359年掸人一次重创之后，彬牙退出了同盟。1364年，德多明帕耶推翻了她的丈夫。

en:
Tarabya II (1327–1352), the youngest son of Sagaing's founder Saw Yun, was born eight months after his father's death. After his cousin Shwetaungtet's coup in 1336 he spent three years in exile at Mindon in Pinya. On their return in 1339, Nanda Pakyan crowned his brother Kyaswa and ran the state, leaving Tarabya a nominal role.

Kyaswa and Nawrahta Minye both died within eight months in 1349, and Tarabya took the throne late that year. He inherited Nawrahta's white elephant and styled himself Hsinbyushin, Lord of the White Elephant.

Relations with Pinya were tense: in 1351 he sheltered Saw Ke, who had fled Kyawswa II. But he sent his sister Soe Min to negotiate a truce, and the peace held. He died in February 1352, and Soe Min's second husband Thihapate succeeded him.

zh:
德勒帕耶艾（1327—1352）是实皆开国君主苏云的幼子，生于父亲去世八个月后。1336年堂兄瑞当代篡位，他在彬牙的敏东流亡三年。1339年返回后，南达巴坚拥立他的兄长加苏瓦为王并主持国政，德勒帕耶艾只有名义上的角色。

1349年，加苏瓦与瑙亚塔明耶在八个月内相继去世，他在当年晚些时候登基，继承了瑙亚塔明耶的白象，自称辛标信，意为白象王。

en:
Azalaïs of Montferrat (1150–1232) was Marchioness of Saluzzo and later its regent. Daughter of William V of Montferrat and Judith of Babenberg, she married Marquis Manfred II of Saluzzo before 1182, and like her brother Boniface of Montferrat patronised troubadours; around 1192 she founded the church of San Lorenzo.

After her son Boniface died in 1212 and her husband in 1215, she ruled Saluzzo as regent for her grandson Manfred III until 1218, making treaties with Savoy and Asti. In 1224 she endowed the convent of Rifreddo, and she died in 1232 and was buried at Staffarda Abbey.

蒙费拉托的阿扎莱斯（1150—1232）是萨卢佐侯爵夫人，后为萨卢佐摄政。她是蒙费拉托侯爵古列尔莫五世与尤蒂特·冯·巴本贝格之女，1182年前嫁给萨卢佐侯爵曼弗雷迪二世；她和兄长博尼法乔一样庇护游吟诗人，约1192年修建圣洛伦佐教堂。

en:
Beatrix of Sicily (1260–1307) was a Hohenstaufen princess, the daughter of King Manfred of Sicily. After her father fell at Benevento in 1266, she was captured with her mother at Trani by Charles of Anjou and held from 1271 in Naples' Castel dell'Ovo, regaining her freedom in 1284 after an Aragonese naval victory.

In 1286 she married Manfred IV of Saluzzo, becoming marchioness consort on his succession in 1296. She was the mother of Frederick I of Saluzzo and died in 1307.

en:
Boniface of Saluzzo (1184–1212) was the eldest son and heir of Marquis Manfred II of Saluzzo. First documented in 1197, he ruled as marquess alongside his father and in 1202 married Maria, daughter of Comita I, judge of Torres in Sardinia, a match celebrated by a troubadour.

With his father he resisted the expansion of Count Thomas I of Savoy. Boniface died in 1212, three years before Manfred II, so his claims passed to his son Manfred III, who succeeded his grandfather in 1215.

欧斯塔基奥（1405年卒），又称欧斯塔基奥·迪·蒙特罗索，是萨卢佐侯爵托马索二世与里恰尔达·维斯孔蒂之子、费德里科二世的兄弟。

en:
Frederick I (1287–29 June 1336) was the eldest son of Manfred IV of Saluzzo by his first wife Beatrix of Sicily. Manfred IV favoured his second wife's son, and his exclusion from the succession sparked civil war in 1330.

With the intercession of the House of Savoy, Frederick made good his claim: a treaty of 1332 recognised him as sole marquess. He married Margaret, mother of his heir Thomas II. After a reign of only four years he died on 29 June 1336, and Thomas succeeded him.

en:
Frederick II (1332–1396) succeeded his father Thomas II as Marquess of Saluzzo in 1357, inheriting a marquisate weakened by civil war and on poor terms with Savoy. With enemies all around him in Piedmont, he looked to the French court for protection. In April 1375 he swore fealty to the Dauphin of France and placed the whole marquisate under him.

In 1376 he went to Paris and had the quarrel with Savoy heard before the Parlement. The fighting did not stop: in 1394 Savoyard troops captured his son Thomas and held him for almost two years.

It was the first step on a road that ended in the sixteenth century with Saluzzo absorbed into the French state. He married Beatrice of Geneva and was succeeded by his son Thomas III.

费德里科二世（1332—1396）于1357年继承父亲托马索二世的萨卢佐侯位，接手的是一个被内战削弱、与萨伏依关系紧张的侯国。他在皮埃蒙特四面受敌，转而向法兰西宫廷寻求庇护。1375年4月，他向法兰西王太子宣誓效忠，把整个侯国置于其下。

1376年他前往巴黎，使萨卢佐与萨伏依的争端在巴黎高等法院受审。但战事并未停止：1394年他的儿子托马索被萨伏依军队俘获，囚禁近两年。

这是后来16世纪萨卢佐被并入法兰西国家的第一步。他娶日内瓦的贝阿特丽切，儿子托马索三世继位。

en:
Isabella Doria (c. 1290–1353) was a Genoese noblewoman, daughter of Bernabò Doria and Eleonora Fieschi, and the second wife of Manfred IV, Marquess of Saluzzo, whom she married in 1307. She bore him four children, including Manfred V, Boniface and Theodore.

Under her influence Manfred granted most of his lands to her son Manfred in 1321 and disinherited his eldest son Frederick in 1323, provoking a civil war that ended with a treaty of 1332 confirming Frederick in Saluzzo. She died in 1353.

en:
Manfred V (1309–1392), son of Manfred IV of Saluzzo and his second wife Isabella Doria, was made his father's heir over his elder half-brother Frederick through her influence.

Civil war with Frederick began in 1330 and ended in 1332, when Manfred ceded the throne by the treaty of 29 July. When Frederick died in 1336, he saw a second chance and led an army of Angevin troops against his young nephew Thomas II. Saluzzo, besieged for a week in April 1341, surrendered, and Manfred let it be sacked: the city was set ablaze and its castle destroyed.

He held it only until 1342, when Visconti pressure forced him to hand it back to Thomas. He died in Pavia in 1392.

en:
Manfred I (died 1175), founder of the marquisate of Saluzzo, ruled from 1142 until his death. The eldest of seven sons of Bonifacio del Vasto, he founded Staffarda Abbey in 1127, and his brothers ruled jointly after their father's death.

At the family partition in 1142, he took the lands between the Alps, the Po and the Stura and made Saluzzo castle his seat. A loyal ally of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, he acknowledged him as overlord and sought peace between him and the Lombard cities.

He married Eleonora, daughter of Judge Gonario II of Arborea. When he died in 1175, his son Manfred II succeeded him.

en:
Manfred II (1140–1215) was the second marquess of Saluzzo, ruling from 1175. He established Saluzzo as permanent capital of the margravate and, before 1182, married Azalaïs of Montferrat, allying with one of northern Italy's most powerful dynasties.

He expanded the march and long fought the neighbouring counts of Savoy. The two sides made terms in 1213, and peace lasted for the rest of his life.

His eldest son Boniface died in 1212, so when Manfred died in February 1215 he was succeeded by his grandson Manfred III under the regency of Azalaïs. Azalaïs paid tribute on his behalf, and Saluzzo remained a vassal of Savoy for the next century.

曼弗雷迪二世（1140—1215）是萨卢佐第二任侯爵，1175年父亲死后继位。他把萨卢佐确立为侯国的永久都城，并于1182年前迎娶蒙费拉托的阿扎莱斯，与北意大利最有权势的家族之一结盟。

他扩张领地，长期与邻邦[GetCountry('SAV').GetName]伯爵作战。双方于1213年议和，此后和平持续到他去世。

长子博尼法乔已于1212年先他而死，故他1215年2月去世后由孙子#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('sal_manfredo_iii_del_vasto').GetID],X #L 曼弗雷德三世#!#!继位，由阿扎莱斯摄政。阿扎莱斯代表年幼的侯爵向萨伏依纳贡，萨卢佐此后一个世纪均为其附庸。

en:
Manfred II Lancia (c. 1190–c. 1257), eldest son of Manfred I, was margrave of Busca but made his career as Frederick II's commander. Imperial representative in Piedmont from 1216, he campaigned in Sicily and probably in Germany, and in 1238 became imperial vicar over Piedmont and Liguria.

Excommunicated with Frederick by Innocent IV in 1245, he fought at Parma and in 1248 defended Vittoria camp, nearly dying in a raid by the people of Parma. After Frederick's death in 1250, Conrad IV favoured Oberto Pelavicino and treated the Lancia family harshly.

Manfred joined the Guelphs in 1252 and in 1253 took charge of Milan. He died at Asti c. 1257 after losing Alessandria.

曼弗雷德二世·兰恰（约1190—约1257）是曼弗雷德一世的长子、布斯卡侯爵，一生主要作为皇帝腓特烈二世的将领征战。1216年起他任腓特烈在皮埃蒙特的代表，随军在西西里作战，可能还远征德意志，1238年出任统辖皮埃蒙特与利古里亚的帝国代牧。

1245年他与腓特烈一同被教皇英诺森四世开除教籍，后在帕尔马作战，1248年守卫维多利亚营地时险些死于帕尔马人的突袭。1250年腓特烈死后，康拉德四世偏用奥贝托·佩拉维奇诺，又苛待兰恰家族。

曼弗雷德于1252年转投归尔夫派，1253年执掌米兰。失去亚历山德里亚后，他约于1257年在阿斯蒂去世。

en:
Manfred III (1204–1244), third marquess of Saluzzo, reigned from 1215. As his father Boniface died before him, he succeeded his grandfather Manfred II, and his grandmother Azalaïs of Montferrat acted as regent until 1218, paying tribute to Count Thomas I of Savoy.

Once in power, Manfred defended the march against Savoyard expansion and made a non-aggression pact with his cousin Boniface II of Montferrat. In 1233 he married Beatrice, daughter of Amadeus IV of Savoy.

He died in 1244, leaving the march to his young son Thomas I. Boniface II of Montferrat acted as regent for the new marquess.

zh:
曼弗雷德三世（1204—1244）是萨卢佐第三任侯爵，1215年即位。因父亲博尼法乔先他而死，他继承祖父曼弗雷迪二世之位，由祖母蒙费拉托的阿扎莱斯摄政至1218年，其间向萨伏依伯爵托马索一世纳贡。

亲政后，曼弗雷德抵御萨伏依的扩张，并与表亲蒙费拉托侯爵波尼法乔二世订立互不侵犯条约。1233年他娶萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥四世之女贝阿特丽切。

1244年他去世，把侯国留给幼子托马索一世，由波尼法乔二世出任摄政。

en:
Manfred IV (1262–1340) succeeded his father Thomas I in 1296 as fifth Marquess of Saluzzo. The town was then a free commune run by a podestà, and he had the rules between marquess and town put into a contract. In 1322 he gained several castles by settling the Del Carretto debts.

His undoing was the succession. His first wife, Beatrix of Sicily, bore his heir Frederick, but his second, Isabella Doria, won him over to her own son Manfred, and in 1321 he gave Manfred most of his lands. When he disinherited Frederick in 1323, civil war followed.

Frederick and his allies occupied towns, and the Visconti joined in. The treaty of 29 July 1332 gave the throne to Frederick, and Manfred abdicated and withdrew to the Langhe, dying at Cortemilia in 1340.

zh:
曼弗雷迪四世（1262—1340）于1296年继承父亲托马索一世，成为第五代萨卢佐侯爵。此时的萨卢佐已是由波德斯塔治理的自由市镇，他把侯爵与市镇之间的关系准则订入契约。1322年，他替德尔卡雷托家族清偿债务，换得数座城堡。

他的祸根在继承人。原配西西里的贝阿特丽切生下继承人费德里科，继室伊莎贝拉·多里亚却让他偏向亲生的曼弗雷德：1321年他把大部分土地赠给曼弗雷德，1323年又剥夺费德里科的继承权，内战随之爆发。

费德里科及其盟友占领数处城镇，维斯孔蒂家族也卷入其中。1332年7月29日的条约将侯位归于费德里科，曼弗雷德退位，隐居朗格地区，1340年卒于科尔泰米利亚。

en:
Manfred I Lancia (fl. 1160–1214), second margrave of Busca, was first of his Aleramici line to take the surname Lancia. The second son of Guglielmo del Vasto, he inherited part of the county of Loreto and held Dogliani.

Plagued by debts, he sold Dogliani in 1187 and pawned his Loreto rights to Alba. In 1192 he joined Asti against Boniface of Montferrat, but in 1196 transferred his lands to Boniface for three thousand gold ounces.

Captured by Asti in 1198, he ceded Loreto to it in 1206. He wrote Occitan verse, exchanging sirventes with Peire Vidal, and died in 1214 or 1215.

zh:
曼弗雷德一世·兰恰（活跃于1160—1214年）是第二位布斯卡侯爵，也是阿莱拉莫家族支系中第一个采用“兰恰”姓氏的人。他是古列尔莫·德尔·瓦斯托的次子，分得洛雷托伯国的一部分，据守多利亚尼。

他债务缠身，1187年卖掉多利亚尼，又向阿尔巴抵押洛雷托的权益。1192年他与阿斯蒂共同对蒙费拉托的博尼法乔作战，1196年却以三千盎司黄金把领地转让给博尼法乔。

1198年他被阿斯蒂俘虏，1206年被迫把洛雷托割让给该城。他还创作奥克语诗歌，与游吟诗人佩尔·维达尔唱和，1214或1215年去世。

en:
Ricciarda Visconti (1304–1361) was a daughter of Galeazzo I Visconti, Lord of Milan, and Beatrice d'Este. She married Thomas II, Marquess of Saluzzo, whose Visconti marriage placed him on the Ghibelline side in the war against his uncle Manfred V, the candidate of the Angevin-backed Guelfs.

Her children included Frederick II, who succeeded Thomas in 1357, Azonne, lord of Monasterolo, and Eustacchio, count of Cervinasco. In the fresco cycle at Castello della Manta she is portrayed as the Amazon heroine Lampeto.

里恰尔达·维斯孔蒂（1304—1361）是米兰领主加莱亚佐一世·维斯孔蒂与贝阿特丽切·德斯特之女，嫁给萨卢佐侯爵托马索二世。这桩维斯孔蒂联姻使托马索在同叔父曼弗雷迪五世的战争中站在吉伯林派一边，与安茹王朝支持的归尔甫派为敌。

en:
Thomas II (1304–1357), son of Frederick I, became Marquess of Saluzzo in 1336 and lost his city five years later. His uncle Manfred V contested the succession with a Guelf army paid by Robert of Naples. Thomas could not hold Saluzzo, which fell on 13 April 1341 and was sacked the next day.

Rather than treat with his uncle, Thomas surrendered to the Angevin seneschal and was freed after about a year for eighty thousand florins' ransom. After the Angevin defeat at Gamenario, Manfred handed the throne back, and in August 1347 joined John II of Montferrat in conquering Angevin lands in northern Italy.

His later years were spent recovering land lost in the civil war, alternately allying and warring with Savoy and Achaea. By Ricciarda Visconti he left a son, Frederick II, his successor.

托马索二世（1304—1357）是费德里科一世之子，1336年成为萨卢佐侯爵，五年后却丢了自己的城市。叔父曼弗雷迪五世争夺继承权，所率归尔甫军队由那不勒斯国王罗贝托出资。1341年4月13日萨卢佐陷落，次日遭到洗劫。

托马索不肯向叔父妥协，向安茹派的司厩长投降，被囚禁约一年，以八万弗罗林赎金获释。安茹军队在加梅纳里奥战败后，曼弗雷德交还侯位，1347年8月托马索与蒙费拉托侯爵乔瓦尼二世联手攻占安茹派在北意大利的领地。

此后他一直设法收复内战中失去的领土，与萨伏依和阿凯亚时而结盟、时而交战。他娶里恰尔达·维斯孔蒂为妻，死后由儿子费德里科二世继位。

en:
Thomas I (1239–1296) became the fourth Marquess of Saluzzo in 1244, succeeding his father Manfred III at the age of five, and was raised at the court of Boniface II of Montferrat. He allied with Savoy against Turin and Asti, but his chief adversary was Charles of Anjou.

In 1267 Charles defeated him over the Valle Stura and forced his submission, but in 1277 Thomas joined the anti-Angevin league that routed Charles at Roccavione. He then sought an alliance with Aragon against Savoy, without success.

He took Cuneo in 1291, extended the march to Carmagnola and made Saluzzo a free commune ruled by a podestà. His wife was Luigia of Ceva, and their son Manfred IV succeeded him.

zh:
托马索一世（1239—1296）于1244年成为第四代萨卢佐侯爵，年仅五岁便继承父亲曼弗雷德三世，在蒙费拉托侯爵波尼法乔二世的宫廷长大。他与萨伏依结盟对抗都灵和阿斯蒂，但主要敌手是安茹的查理。

1267年，查理在斯图拉河谷之战中击败他，迫使他臣服；1277年，托马索加入反安茹联盟，在罗卡维奥内击溃查理的军队。他寻求同阿拉贡结盟对抗萨伏依，但未能成功。

他于1291年攻取库内奥，将领地扩展至卡尔马尼奥拉，并把萨卢佐改为由波德斯塔治理的自由市镇。他娶切瓦的路易贾为妻，由儿子曼弗雷迪四世继位。

en:
Sampiero Corso, born Sampiero da Bastelica in 1498, was a Corsican condottiero who left his native island young and made his fortune in the Italian Wars. From 1535 he served the French Valois, becoming colonel of the Corsican mercenary troops in 1547.

Backed by Catherine de' Medici, he invaded Corsica against Genoa in 1564, but lost French support. Ambushed by rival Corsicans in January 1567, he was killed and beheaded. Marshal of France Alphonse d'Ornano was his son.

Samuel de Champlain (possibly baptized 1574 – 1635) was a French explorer, cartographer and colonial administrator. A mariner's son from La Rochelle or Brouage, he reached North America in 1603 and on 3 July 1608 founded Quebec, base of New France.

He mapped the Atlantic coast and the Great Lakes using his own observations and Indigenous information, and allied with the Huron and other nations against the Iroquois from 1609. When the English seized Quebec in 1629 he was taken to France; he returned in 1633 and died there on 25 December 1635.

萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰（可能于1574年受洗—1635）是法国探险家、地图学家和殖民管理者，可能生于拉罗谢尔或布鲁阿日的一个航海者家庭。1603年他首次抵达北美，1608年7月3日建立魁北克，使之成为新法兰西长久的据点。

en:
Béatrix de Pierrepont (1310–1349), called de Roucy-Pierrepont, was the daughter of John V, Count of Roucy and Braine, and Marguerite de Beaumez, and inherited several seigneuries. On 8 July 1329 she married Louis II, Count of Sancerre, and bore him seven children, including John III, who succeeded him, and Louis, later marshal and constable of France.

Her husband and father were both killed at Crécy on 26 August 1346. As widowed countess she confirmed a customary right of the lord of Pesselières as marshal of the county in 1348, and died the next year.

en:
Stephen I (1133–1190/1191), third son of Count Theobald II of Champagne, received the new County of Sancerre in 1151 and founded the House of Sancerre. He granted its merchants the Customs of Lorris in 1155 and built a stone citadel.

In 1170 he went to Jerusalem as a proposed husband for King Amalric's daughter Sibylla, before refusing the marriage and returning home. He led the baronial revolt against Philip II in 1181–1185, and in 1184 the king defeated him.

He freed his serfs in 1190. He joined the Third Crusade and died at the Siege of Acre, succeeded by his son William I.

en:
Stephen II (1252–1306) was Count of Sancerre, eldest son of Count John I and Marie de Vierzon, inheriting the county around 1284. A noted tournament knight, he jousted at Cambrai in 1269 and faced Geoffrey of Apremont at Chauvency in 1285.

He served in the French army in the Flemish war of 1297–1302; after Courtrai he defended Lille against the Flemings. With no relief, he negotiated its surrender with John of Namur on 6 August 1302. He died childless in May 1306, and his brother John II succeeded him.

en:
William I (c. 1176–1217) succeeded his father Stephen I as Count of Sancerre in 1191, and in 1211 married Eustachie of Courtenay, sister of Peter of Courtenay. On 27 July 1214 he fought at the Battle of Bouvines in the army of Philip II, as lieutenant of his cousin Odo III of Burgundy.

In 1217 he accompanied his brother-in-law Peter II of Courtenay, newly elected Latin Emperor, toward Constantinople by land after the failed siege of Durazzo. In the Albanian mountains Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus ambushed and captured them, and William died in Epirote captivity. His son Louis I succeeded him.

en:
John I (c. 1235–c. 1280/1284), son of Louis I and Blanche of Courtenay, became Count of Sancerre in 1268. In 1259 he married Marie de Vierzon, adding her lands to the county, and he built the fortress of La Vieille-Ferté in 1266.

In 1267 he assigned his wife's dower lands to his brother and gave her Sagonne in compensation. He sought to prevent the county's division.

He also confirmed the privileges of the bourgeois of Meillant and struck deniers and oboles at Sancerre. On his death he was succeeded by his son Stephen II.

en:
John II (c. 1260–1327), second son of Count John I of Sancerre and Marie de Vierzon, succeeded his elder brother Stephen II as count in 1306; he was also lord of Meillant, whose fortress he built c. 1300. For an unauthorized duel at Saint-Verain in 1308 he was imprisoned for months in Melun tower by order of Philip IV.

In 1316 he answered a summons to Paris with thirty men-at-arms, and in 1318, as lieutenant of the seneschal of Beaucaire, he was barred from royal office for violence. He died in 1327 and was buried at Bourges with his wife.

en:
John III of Sancerre (1334–1402) became count in 1346 after his father Louis II fell at Crécy. Captured at Poitiers in 1356, he was named among the hostages for the Treaty of Brétigny in 1360, and in 1364 destroyed an English company near La Charité.

He married Marguerite de Marmande in 1357 and later Constance of Saluzzo. Counselor and chamberlain of Charles VI, he died in March 1402 leaving only daughters, ending the male line of the house of Blois-Champagne.

en:
Louis I (c. 1207–1267) inherited Sancerre in 1217, after his father William I died in Epirote captivity on the way to Constantinople. In 1225 he attended the Council of Bourges, called to deal with the Cathars, and in 1234 his overlord Theobald IV of Champagne sold the homage of Sancerre and Blois to Louis IX, after which the counts held their county directly of the French crown.

On 1 September 1238 he took the cross for the Sixth Crusade. He later acquired the barony of Charenton in exchange for La Ferté-Loupière, and when he died in 1267 his son John I succeeded him.

en:
Louis II (c. 1305–1346), Count of Sancerre, was the son of John II and Louise de Beaumez. On 8 July 1329 he married Béatrix de Roucy, daughter of Count John V of Roucy; of their seven children John III succeeded, and Louis de Sancerre rose to be Marshal and then Constable of France.

In summer 1346 he reportedly served in Normandy under Constable Raoul II de Brienne, and on 26 August he was killed at Crécy beside his father-in-law. By one account he was among the French captains who broke into the first English division under the young Prince of Wales.

In 1334 he reached an agreement with the lord of Sagonne over the inheritance of Thibaud, Bishop of Tournai. Edward III had his body recovered and buried at Maintenay abbey.

en:
Alfonso Fadrique (c. 1294–1338) was the eldest, illegitimate son of Frederick III of Sicily and Sibilla Sormella. In 1317 his father sent him to govern the Catalan Duchy of Athens as vicar general for his half-brother Manfred, but Manfred died before he landed, leaving another half-brother, William, as duke.

That year Alfonso married Marulla, daughter of Boniface of Verona, chief lord of Euboea, gaining rights to castles. He fought Venice and stormed Negroponte. When John II Ducas of Neopatras died in 1318, Alfonso invaded Thessaly, took Neopatras, Siderokastron and Pharsalus and styled himself its vicar general.

Relieved of his post in 1330, he received the counties of Malta and Gozo. He died in 1338, leaving five sons who founded the Fadrique house.

阿方索·法德里克（约1294—1338）是西西里国王腓特烈三世与西比拉·索尔梅拉的长子，为私生子。1317年，腓特烈派他出任雅典公国总代牧，代表异母弟弟曼弗雷德统治加泰罗尼亚人的公国；曼弗雷德在他登陆前已去世，公爵已是另一异母弟弟古列尔莫。

同年，他娶埃维亚岛首要领主维罗纳的博尼法乔之女马鲁拉，获得数座城堡的权利。他与威尼斯交战，并攻陷内格罗蓬特。1318年新帕特雷的约翰二世·杜卡斯去世，阿方索入侵色萨利，夺取新帕特雷、锡德罗卡斯特龙和法萨罗斯，自称新帕特雷公国总代牧。

1330年他被解职，改封马耳他与戈佐伯爵。1338年他去世，五个儿子建立了法德里克家族。

en:
Boniface Fadrique (died before 1380) was a Catalan nobleman, a son of Alfonso Fadrique, vicar general of Athens and Neopatras. In 1359 he left Sicily to claim his mother's barony of Karystos, which he sold to Venice in 1365.

When his brother James died in 1366, he inherited the County of Salona and its dependencies, becoming a leading Catalan lord. He fought his nephew Louis Fadrique, who defeated him after 1375, seized his lands and exiled his son Peter to Aragon.

博尼法西奥·法德里科（？—1380年前）是加泰罗尼亚贵族，雅典与新帕特拉斯摄政阿方索·法德里科之子。1359年他离开西西里，前来继承母亲的卡里斯托斯男爵领地，并于1365年将其卖给威尼斯。

1366年兄长海梅去世，他继承萨洛纳伯国及其属地，成为加泰罗尼亚领地最有权势的领主之一。后来他与侄子路易·法德里科交战，1375年后被路易击败，封地遭夺，儿子佩德罗被流放至阿拉贡。

en:
James Fadrique (died 1366) was a Catalan nobleman in Greece and Count of Salona, son of Alfonso Fadrique and Marulla of Verona. In December 1335 he was excommunicated with his father by the Latin archbishop of Patras, because the papacy backed Walter VI of Brienne's claim to Athens.

Before 1355 he inherited Salona, Loidoriki and Veteranitsa from his childless brother Peter. In 1361–1362 the vicar general Peter of Pou seized his castles, until Peter was killed in an uprising.

In 1365 James took Siderokastron from the marshal Ermengol de Novelles, declared a rebel for refusing to surrender it to the new vicar general, and kept it himself. He died in 1366, leaving his rights at Athens, including Salona, to his brother Boniface and Siderokastron to his son Louis.

zh:
海梅·法德里克（1366年卒）是在希腊活动的加泰罗尼亚贵族、萨洛纳伯爵，阿方索·法德里克与马鲁拉·达维罗纳之子。1335年12月，因教廷支持布里耶纳的戈蒂埃六世对雅典的权利主张，他与父亲一道被帕特雷的拉丁大主教处以绝罚。

1355年前，他从无子嗣的兄长彼得手中继承萨洛纳、洛伊佐里基和韦泰拉尼察。1361—1362年，总代牧彼得·德·普夺取他的城堡，至彼得在起义中被杀。

1365年元帅埃芒戈尔·德·诺韦勒斯因拒不交出锡德罗卡斯特龙被宣布为叛逆，海梅夺取这座要塞并据为己有。1366年他去世，把雅典公国的权利（包括萨洛纳）留给弟弟博尼法西奥，把锡德罗卡斯特龙留给儿子路易。

en:
John Fadrique (Catalan Joan Frederic d'Aragó; died 1366) was a Catalan nobleman in Frankish Greece. His father Alfonso Fadrique, vicar general of Athens and Neopatras, was the illegitimate son of Frederick II of Sicily, and his mother Marulla was the daughter and heiress of Boniface of Verona, a triarch of Euboea.

John is attested in 1350 as lord of the islands of Aegina and Salamis. His brothers held fiefs across the Catalan duchies, and his sister Simona married George II Ghisi.

en:
Marulla of Verona (died 1326) was Lady of Karystos, the southern triarchy of Euboea, from 1318 until her death. The daughter of Boniface of Verona, lord of Karystos, she married Alfonso Fadrique, the Catalan vicar-general of Athens and illegitimate son of Frederick II of Sicily, who had seized Karystos the year before.

Her sons Peter and James ruled as counts of Salona, William held Livadeia, and Boniface held Aigina and Karystos; her daughter Simona married George II Ghisi.

马鲁拉·达维罗纳（？—1326）于1318年至1326年担任埃维亚岛南区卡里斯托斯的女领主。她是卡里斯托斯领主博尼法乔·达维罗纳之女，嫁给雅典公国的加泰罗尼亚总督、西西里国王腓特烈二世的私生子阿方索·法德里克；阿方索已于前一年攻占卡里斯托斯。

en:
Peter Fadrique (died 1350–1355), Count of Salona, was the eldest son of Alfonso Fadrique, vicar general of the Catalan Duchies of Athens and Neopatras. In 1335 he and his father and brother were excommunicated by the Latin Archbishop of Patras for resisting Walter VI of Brienne's claim.

He succeeded his father around 1338, holding Salona and its dependencies. The Crown of Aragon confiscated his fiefs after 1350 and later restored them to his brother James.

en:
Sartaq Khan (died 1256 or 1257) was the eldest son of Batu Khan and succeeded his father as ruler of the Golden Horde in 1255 or 1256, confirmed by the great khan Möngke. A Nestorian Christian who kept Mongol shamanist customs, he had overseen Russian affairs under Batu.

Alexander Nevsky secured the grand principality of Vladimir through his judgment. Sartaq held his own horde west of the Volga and built a Nestorian church there, but died within a year of taking power.

撒里答（?—1256/1257）是拔都的长子，于1255/1256年奉大汗蒙哥册封，继其父为金帐汗国统治者。他是景教徒，同时保留蒙古萨满旧俗，拔都在世时即主管罗斯事务。

亚历山大·涅夫斯基正是经他裁决取得弗拉基米尔大公之位。撒里答在伏尔加河以西拥有自己的斡耳朵，并修建景教教堂，但即位不到一年便死去。

en:
Amadeus I (c. 1016–c. 1051), called the Tailed (la Coda), was an early count of the House of Savoy and probably the eldest son of Humbert I. First appearing in charters from 1022, he held the title count by 1030.

A later story has him refuse to enter Emperor Henry III's chamber at Verona in 1046 without his train of knights, his ‘tail’. Last recorded in 1051 as count of Belley, he was buried at Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne and succeeded by his brother Otto.

阿梅迪奥一世（约1016—约1051），绰号“有尾者”（拉科达），是萨伏依家族早期的伯爵，疑为翁贝托一世的长子。1022年的文书中首次出现他的名字，1030年他已使用伯爵头衔。

en:
Amadeus II (c. 1050–1080) ruled the County of Savoy from 1078, succeeding his father Otto I. His short reign is poorly documented and was overshadowed by his formidable mother, Adelaide of Susa, who held real power, though he kept good relations with papacy and emperor.

His wife, possibly a daughter of Count Gerold of Geneva, bore him his successor Humbert II. When Amadeus died on 26 January 1080, Adelaide took direct control of the Savoyard lands.

en:
Amadeus III (1095–1148) became Count of Savoy and Maurienne in 1103, ruling at first through a regent. In 1128 he enlarged his lands with the New Chablais, and he restored Saint-Maurice d'Agaune and founded Hautecombe Abbey.

After his men killed his wife's brother Guigues IV of Albon at Montmélian, he escaped French retaliation by promising to take the cross. He joined the Second Crusade in 1147 with Louis VII, led the vanguard in Anatolia, and died of exhaustion at Nicosia in Cyprus in April 1148. His son Humbert III succeeded him.

en:
Amadeus IV (1197–1253), eldest son of Thomas I, became Count of Savoy in 1233. He crushed a revolt by his brothers Peter and Aymon in the Aosta Valley with the help of his sons-in-law. In 1234 he settled the family at Chillon with a treaty assigning frontier lordships to his younger brothers.

Knighted by Frederick II at Turin in 1238, in 1244 he escorted Pope Innocent IV from Susa to Chambéry, and in 1246 granted passage rights through his lands to Henry III of England. He died on 11 June 1253; his young son Boniface succeeded under Thomas's regency.

Amadeus (French: Amé) of Savoy was a younger son of Thomas III, lord of Piedmont, and Guyonne of Burgundy. The will his father made on 14 May 1282 names him among the four younger sons who were to receive appanages from their eldest brother, Philip I of Piedmont.

Amadeus entered the Church and became archdeacon of Reims, an office he already held in 1320, and he is last recorded alive after 1340.

en:
Amadeus of Savoy-Achaea (c. 1321–1376) was a younger son of Philip I, lord of Piedmont, and Catherine de la Tour du Pin. The cadet branch of Savoy that held Piedmont put its younger sons into the church, and Pope Clement VI, who favoured the house of Savoy, obliged.

Amadeus, already promised prebends, was made Bishop of Maurienne on 2 April 1349 before he had taken even minor orders. Count Amadeus VI of Savoy later tried to exchange his see for Lausanne: both bishops agreed and resigned, but Innocent VI answered too slowly and the exchange failed.

His brother Thomas became Bishop of Turin in November 1348. Amadeus died at Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne on 6 June 1376 and seems to have been buried in its cathedral.

阿梅迪奥·德·萨伏依-亚该亚（约1321—1376）是皮埃蒙特领主腓力一世与卡特琳·德·拉图尔迪潘较年幼的儿子。萨伏依家族中掌有皮埃蒙特的这一支把幼子送入教会，倾向萨伏依家的教皇克雷芒六世也乐于成全。

阿梅迪奥早已获许在法国的几处教堂取得教士圣俸，1349年4月2日被任命为莫里耶讷主教，当时他连低级神品都尚未领受。萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥六世后来策划让他以莫里耶讷交换洛桑主教区，两位主教同意并各自辞任，但教皇英诺森六世答复太迟，交换未能成事。

他的兄弟托马索于1348年11月成为都灵主教。阿梅迪奥于1376年6月6日在圣让德莫里耶讷去世，似乎葬于当地主教座堂。

en:
Amadeus V (1249–1323), called the Great, was the son of Thomas II of Piedmont and Beatrice Fieschi. He served his cousin Edward I of England in the Welsh wars and inherited Savoy from his uncle Philip I in 1285. His younger brother Louis received the new Barony of Vaud.

Through his wife Sybille de Baugé he added Bugey and Bresse; in 1287 he occupied Geneva and imposed the Treaty of Annemasse. In 1312 he attended Henry VII's coronation in Rome and was made Imperial Vicar of Lombardy. He died at Avignon on 16 October 1323.

en:
Amadeus VI (1334–1383), the Green Count, inherited Savoy in 1343 at the age of nine. His father's will named two cousins as co-regents, neither able to decide anything major alone. In 1350 he married his sister Bianca to Galeazzo II Visconti of Milan and founded the Order of the Black Swan to honour the match.

His greatest undertaking was the Savoyard Crusade of 1366–1367, which he personally financed: he seized Gallipoli from the Ottomans and campaigned in Bulgaria to help the Byzantine emperor John V, though the Turks won back these gains within five years.

At Turin in 1381 he mediated peace between Genoa and Venice. He died in 1383 on campaign in the kingdom of Naples, leaving Savoy to his son Amadeus VII.

His greatest undertaking was the Savoyard Crusade of 1366–1367, which he personally financed: he seized Gallipoli from the [GetCountry('TUR').GetName] and campaigned in [GetCountry('BUL').GetName] to help the Byzantine emperor John V, though the Turks won back these gains within five years.

At [ShowLocationName('turin')] in 1381 he mediated peace between Genoa and Venice. He died in 1383 on campaign in the kingdom of Naples, leaving Savoy to his son Amadeus VII.
zh:
阿梅迪奥六世（1334—1383），绰号“绿衣伯爵”，1343年九岁继承萨伏依。父亲的遗嘱指定两位堂亲共同摄政，二人都不能单独作重大决定。1350年，他将妹妹比安卡嫁给米兰的加莱亚佐二世·维斯孔蒂，并为这桩婚事创立黑天鹅骑士团。

他最大的事业是1366至1367年的萨伏依十字军，军费由他亲自筹措：他从奥斯曼人手中夺取加里波利，又进军保加利亚援助拜占庭皇帝约翰五世，但这些战果在五年内又被土耳其人夺回。

1381年，他在都灵调停热那亚与威尼斯之间的和约。1383年他在那不勒斯王国作战期间去世，萨伏依传给其子阿梅迪奥七世。

en:
Margaret of Burgundy (1192–1243), called Anne by some sources, was the youngest daughter of Duke Hugh III of Burgundy and Béatrice of Albon. Around 1217 she married Amadeus of Savoy, bringing castles in the Dauphiné as her dowry.

When her husband succeeded as Count Amadeus IV in 1233, she became countess of Savoy. Her daughter Beatrice married Manfred III of Saluzzo and then King Manfred of Sicily. She died in 1243.

勃艮第的玛格丽特（1192—1243），部分史料称安娜，是勃艮第公爵于格三世与阿尔邦的贝娅特丽克丝最小的女儿。约1217年她嫁给萨伏依的阿梅迪奥，带来多菲内的城堡作嫁妆。

en:
Aymon (1291–1343), called the Peaceful, was a younger son of Amadeus V, destined for the church, and was at the papal court in Avignon when his brother Edward, Count of Savoy, died in 1329. His niece Joan claimed the county with her husband's backing, but Savoy had never had a female ruler; Aymon took it and paid her off.

His early reign passed in the old feud with the dauphins of Viennois, until Philip VI brokered a truce in 1333. Edward III of England and Philip VI both courted him; he held back until Philip settled a lasting peace with the Dauphiné in 1337, and later fought for France.

His nickname came from settling his disputes with Amadeus III of Geneva by negotiation. He died in 1343, leaving Savoy to his son Amadeus VI.

zh:
艾蒙（1291—1343），绰号“和平者”，是阿梅迪奥五世的幼子，本被安排进入教会。1329年兄长爱德华去世、萨伏依伯爵之位空出时，他正在阿维尼翁的教廷。侄女让娜在丈夫支持下也提出继承要求，但萨伏依从未有过女性统治者，艾蒙继位后出钱了结此事。

他执政之初仍陷在与维埃努瓦多芬之间的世仇里，直到1333年法王促成休战。英格兰国王爱德华三世与腓力六世都来拉拢他，他一直不肯表态，直到1337年腓力促成与多菲内的持久和平，此后便为法国作战。

“和平者”之名来自他以谈判而非战争解决了与日内瓦伯爵阿梅迪奥三世的争端。1343年他去世，萨伏依由其子阿梅迪奥六世继承。

en:
Aimone of Savoy-Achaea (born after June 1330, died shortly after 13 March 1398) was a younger son of Philip I of Piedmont and Catherine de la Tour du Pin. His father's codicil of 1334 left him the fief of Fiano, and he served the count of Savoy as lieutenant of the castle of Villafranca.

He joined his cousin Amadeus VI on the Savoyard crusade to the Balkans in 1366–1367. By 1385 he had married Mencia di Ceva, and he made his will at Villafranca on 13 March 1398 as a knight; he died without legitimate issue.

en:
Béatrice de Faucigny (1234–1310), called the Great Dauphine, was the only child of Peter II of Savoy and Agnès of Faucigny. She married Guigues VII, dauphin of Viennois, before 1253 and inherited Faucigny in 1268. Widowed in 1269, she ruled the Dauphiné as regent for her son Jean, and was captured with him and freed that November.

She married Gaston VII of Béarn in 1273. She later gave Faucigny to her grandson Hugues and died at Mélan in 1310.

Bianca of Savoy (1336–1387) was born at Chambéry, the only surviving daughter of Count Aimone of Savoy and Yolande Palaeologina of Montferrat. Orphaned before she turned seven, she grew up beside her brother Amadeus VI, the Green Count.

Marriage plans with England and the Dauphin both fell through, and in 1350 she married Galeazzo II Visconti, becoming lady of Milan. She was the mother of Gian Galeazzo Visconti, joined his 1385 coup against Bernabò Visconti, and died at Pavia in 1387.

Boniface (1 December 1244 – 7 June 1263), called Roland (Orlando) for his warlike spirit, was the only son of Count Amadeus IV of Savoy. He succeeded in 1253 under the regency of his mother and uncle Thomas II.

After Thomas's death in 1259 he ruled alone, allying with the Ghibellines against Asti and Charles of Anjou. Having beaten William VII of Montferrat at Rivoli in 1263, he was defeated and captured before Turin and died of his wounds. He was succeeded by his uncle Peter.

en:
Edward (1284–1329), called the Liberal, eldest son of Amadeus V, ruled Savoy from 1323. Young, he saved Philip IV of France while fighting the Flemings. His reign was spent at war: in 1325, besieging Varey, he was defeated by the Dauphin Guigues VIII of Viennois and barely escaped.

In 1327 he helped suppress the revolt of Maurienne's inhabitants against their bishop, on condition that he gain administrative control of the diocese. He died at Paris on 4 November 1329, leaving one daughter, Joan; his brother Aymon succeeded him.

en:
Edward of Savoy-Achaea (c. 1322–1395) was a younger son of Philip I, lord of Piedmont, and Catherine de la Tour du Pin. He became a Cluniac monk in 1346 and rose through church offices, becoming abbot of Saint-Just in 1366 and bishop of Belley in 1371.

In 1375, after the murder of Bishop Guichard Tavelli, he was moved to Sion, called the richest of the Savoyard sees. There his cousin Amadeus VI sold him most of the murderer's estates for 46,000 florins, leaving him deep in debt. The Valaisans rose against him, and Amadeus burned Sion and put him back on the throne.

He had served Pope Clement VI as honorary chaplain from 1347. In 1386 the pope named him archbishop-count of Tarentaise, where he died in 1395.

爱德华·德·萨伏依-亚该亚（约1322—1395）是皮埃蒙特领主腓力一世与卡特琳·德·拉图尔迪潘之子。他于1346年成为克吕尼修会修士，在教会中历任升迁，1366年任圣朱斯特修道院院长，1371年升任贝莱主教。

1375年，主教吉沙尔·塔韦利遇害后，他被调往有萨伏依最富教区之称的锡永。在那里，表亲阿梅迪奥六世以46000弗罗林把凶手的大部分产业卖给他，使他债台高筑。瓦莱人起而反抗，阿梅迪奥放火烧了锡永城，让他重回主教之位。

他自1347年起担任教皇克雷芒六世的荣誉司铎。1386年教皇任命他为塔朗泰斯大主教兼伯爵，他于1395年在任内去世。

Girard de Cossonay (died before 1369), a younger son of Louis I de Cossonay, held L'Isle in the Vaud as a knight. In 1355 he granted a long-term lease of its lands, a transaction his eldest brother John III formally ratified in 1362.

By his will he left rents to the church of Saint-Paul and the priory of Cossonay. He died before his brother John, who inherited his lands and charged his son Louis with honouring the bequest.

Guillaume de Joinville (c. 1256 – after 1324) was a son of Simon de Joinville and Léonète, heiress of Gex, and founder of the Joinville-Gex line. Already lord of Gex by 1287, he rendered liege homage to Count Amédée V of Savoy in 1289.

The town's franchises were sealed in 1292, and in 1305 he bought the tower of La Maladière and the castle of Tougins. By Jeanne de Savoie he left a son, Hugues, and a daughter, Éléonore, heiress of Gex.

Hugh de Joinville (died 1347), lord of Gex, was son of William de Joinville and Joan of Savoy-Vaud, daughter of Baron Louis I of Vaud. In 1334 he and the abbot of Saint-Claude settled their Mijoux valley dispute, declaring it common land and founding a pilgrim hospice.

He married Joan of Montbéliard but left no children. At his death Gex passed to his sister Eleanor, then by her second marriage to the Genevan lords, until Amadeus VI of Savoy conquered it in 1353–1355.

en:
Humbert I (c. 980 – c. 1047), called the White-Handed, was founder and first count of the House of Savoy. Of obscure origins, probably Burgundian, he held lands before acquiring Aosta and Valais. He served the emperors Henry II and Conrad II.

After Rudolf III of Burgundy died in 1032, he swore fealty to Conrad and backed him against his rivals. In return the emperor granted him Maurienne and Chablais, territories commanding Alpine passes into Italy. He died at Hermillon and was succeeded by his son Amadeus I.

en:
Humbert II, called the Fat (1065–1103), succeeded his father Amadeus II as Count of Savoy in 1080, ruling at first under his grandmother Adelaide of Susa, who governed the Italian possessions. After her death in 1091, Emperor Henry IV seized the March of Turin in 1092, leaving him only the Susa valley south of the Alps.

Humbert secured the Mont Cenis pass on the Via Francigena and founded the first Savoyard mint at Susa. He was the first count to call himself Marquis of Italy. He died at Moûtiers on 19 October 1103 and was succeeded by his son Amadeus III.

en:
Humbert III (1136–1189), called the Blessed, inherited the County of Savoy in 1148 at the age of twelve. Pious, he endowed Hautecombe Abbey and was later the first prince buried there. After his third wife died in 1173, he retired to Hautecombe, but the nobility persuaded him to marry again.

He backed the Guelph cause against Emperor Frederick Barbarossa; imperial troops burned Susa, and Henry VI later seized most of his lands, leaving him only the Susa and Aosta valleys. His fourth wife bore him his heir Thomas. Humbert died at Chambéry on 4 March 1189.

他支持圭尔夫派，与皇帝腓特烈一世为敌：帝国军队焚毁[ShowLocationName('susa')]，亨利六世后来又夺去他大部分领地，他只剩苏萨河谷与[ShowLocationName('aosta')]河谷。第四任妻子为他生下继承人托马索。1189年3月4日，翁贝托卒于[ShowLocationName('chambery')]。

en:
Isabelle de Chalon-Arlay (c. 1292–c. 1359) was the daughter of Jean I, lord of Chalon-Arlay, and Marguerite of Burgundy. In 1309 she married Louis II of Savoy, baron of Vaud, allying his house with the leading nobility of the Franche-Comté.

Her son Jean died fighting at Laupen in 1339, and her daughter Catherine was named Louis's heiress in his 1340 testament. When Louis died in 1349, Isabelle ruled the barony of Vaud jointly with Catherine.

伊莎贝尔·德·沙隆-阿莱（约1292—约1359）是沙隆-阿莱领主让一世与勃艮第的玛格丽特之女。1309年，她嫁给沃男爵萨伏依的路易二世，这桩婚姻使萨伏依家族与弗朗什-孔泰的上层贵族结盟。

她的儿子让于1339年在劳彭之战中阵亡；路易于1340年立遗嘱指定女儿卡特琳为继承人。1349年路易去世后，伊莎贝尔与卡特琳共同统治沃男爵国。

Isabelle de Grandson (born c. 1310) was the daughter of Peter II de Grandson, lord of Belmont, and Blanche of Savoy-Vaud. She married Louis I de Cossonay, lord of Cossonay in the Vaud, binding two leading Vaudois dynasties to Savoy.

Her children included John III, later lord of Cossonay, Louis III, the family's last male, and Girard of L'Isle. When Louis I died before 1333, their uncle Aymon tutored the children. Long widowed, she willed them her estates in 1366.

James of Savoy-Achaia (1315–1367) was born at Pinerolo, the eldest son of Philip I of Piedmont. Succeeding as Lord of Piedmont in 1334, he kept the title Prince of Achaea though Naples had seized the principality in 1307.

In 1347 he and his cousin Amadeus VI of Savoy retook Chieri from John II of Montferrat and other towns. Later warring with Amadeus, he was captured at Pinerolo and lost his lands, restored by treaty in 1362. He died there in 1367.

萨伏依-亚该亚的贾科莫（1315—1367）生于皮内罗洛，是皮埃蒙特领主腓力一世的长子。1334年他继父位为皮埃蒙特领主；尽管那不勒斯的安茹家族已于1307年夺取亚该亚亲王国，他仍自称亚该亚亲王。

1347年，他与表亲萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥六世一同从蒙费拉托侯爵乔瓦尼二世手中夺回基耶里等城镇。后来他与阿梅迪奥交战，在皮内罗洛被俘、领地被没收，1362年依条约复国，1367年卒于该地。

John III de Cossonay (died before 1369), lord of Cossonay and L'Isle, was the eldest son of Louis I de Cossonay and Isabelle de Grandson. Knighted young, he pilgrimaged to the Holy Land and in 1343 married Louise of Montbéliard, daughter of Count Henry.

In 1348 he signed a mutual inheritance treaty with his cousin the lord of Varembon, and in 1357 confirmed Cossonay's town franchises. He died before July 1369, leaving his son Louis II to succeed him.

John of Savoy (died 21 June 1339), lord of Visieu, was the only son of Baron Louis II of Vaud. He wed Marguerite of Chalon, daughter of the Count of Auxerre; the marriage remained childless.

During the war of Laupen he was sent to Bern and the opposing league's camp to seek mediation, but died in June 1339 before succeeding. His early death led Louis II to settle the barony of Vaud on his daughter Catherine in 1340.

Louis I de Cossonay (died 1333) was a baron of the pays de Vaud, succeeding his father Jean II as lord of Cossonay, Bercher and L'Isle. In 1311 he granted the town hospital to the priory of Cossonay, and he was knighted only in 1329.

By his wife Isabelle, daughter of Pierre II de Grandson and Blanche of Savoy, he left sons Jean III, Guillaume, Louis and Girard and a daughter Agnès.

en:
Louis I of Savoy (1253–1302), third son of Thomas II of Piedmont and Béatrice Fieschi, founded the Savoy-Vaud line. Destined for the Church, he chose arms instead. He founded Morges and defeated the lords of Cossonay-Prangins, seizing Nyon.

After disputing the county of Savoy with his brother Amadeus V, an arbitration in 1285 granted him the Pays de Vaud, where he built a semi-independent principality and secured the right to mint coins from the Holy Roman Emperor. He died in 1302 and was buried at Hautecombe, succeeded by his son Louis II.

en:
Louis II of Savoy (c. 1290–1349) headed the Vaud branch of the house of Savoy, succeeding his father Louis I as baron of Vaud around 1302. He gave up his claim to the county of Savoy in return for financial advantages for Vaud, and built up its administration.

In 1310 he joined Emperor Henry VII's expedition to Italy and was made a senator of Rome, and between 1314 and 1322 he led several campaigns against the Dauphiné. His daughter Catherine married Azzone Visconti, lord of Milan.

From 1343 he was co-regent of Savoy for the young Amadeus VI, and he fought for Philip VI of France in the Hundred Years' War. His only son died in 1339, so he left Vaud to Catherine, and he died in January 1349.

路易二世·德·萨伏依-沃（约1290—1349）是萨伏依家族沃一支的首领，约1302年继父亲路易一世成为沃男爵。他放弃对萨伏依伯国的主张，换得沃男爵领的财政利益，并着力完善行政。

1310年，他随皇帝亨利七世远征意大利，被封为罗马元老；1314至1322年间又多次率军征战多菲内。他的女儿卡特琳嫁给米兰领主阿佐内·维斯孔蒂。

1343年起，他与人共同摄政萨伏依，辅佐年幼的阿梅迪奥六世，并在百年战争中为法王腓力六世作战。独子于1339年先逝，他便安排女儿卡特琳继承领地，1349年1月去世。

1343年起，他与人共同摄政萨伏依，辅佐年幼的#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('sav_amedee_vi_savoy').GetID],X #L 阿梅迪奥六世#!#!，并在百年战争中为法王腓力六世作战。独子于1339年先逝，他便安排女儿卡特琳继承领地，1349年1月去世。

en:
Louis III de Cossonay, son of Louis I de Cossonay and Isabelle de Grandson, held Berchier as his appanage. A trusted servant of Amadeus VI, he executed his will in 1383 and served Amadeus VII as lieutenant-general and governor of Savoy in 1384.

When his nephew Louis II died in 1383, he inherited Cossonay. In 1391 he was made an adviser during Amadeus VIII's minority. He died in 1394 or 1395, the last male of his line, leaving his great-nieces as heirs.

Margaret of Savoy (c. 1274–1359) was the eldest daughter of Count Amadeus V of Savoy and Sibylle of Bâgé. A marriage plan with John II of Viennois was rejected by the Pope, and in 1296 she married John I the Just, marquess of Montferrat.

The marriage was childless, and when John died in 1305 she became dowager marchioness of Montferrat. She died in 1359 and was buried at Hautecombe Abbey.

Marguerite of Chalon (died 1378) was a daughter of John II, Count of Auxerre and Tonnerre, by his second wife Alix of Burgundy. By a marriage contract drawn up between 1333 and 1337 she wed John of Savoy, only son and heir of Baron Louis II of Vaud.

John died on 21 June 1339 during the war of Laupen, and their marriage was childless. She later took a second husband, Henri de Vienne, lord of Antigny in Burgundy.

en:
Marie of Brabant (1277/1280–1338), countess consort of Savoy, was a daughter of John I, Duke of Brabant, and Margaret of Flanders. Her marriage was alliance-making: after a papal dispensation, she wed Count Amadeus V at Chambéry in 1298, tying Savoy to Brabant.

Marie brought Brabantine artisans to the Savoyard court and acted there as a diplomat and political adviser. Her sister Margaret was the wife of Henry VII, elected king of Germany in 1308; in 1310 the couple visited Marie at Geneva, and Amadeus joined Henry's Italian campaign.

Widowed in 1323, when her stepson Edward succeeded, she died in 1338. Her daughter Anna married the Byzantine emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos.

布拉班特的玛丽亚（1277/1280—1338）是萨伏依伯爵夫人，布拉班特公爵让一世与当皮埃尔的玛格丽特之女。这桩婚姻是结盟的一环：教皇发出特许后，她于1298年在尚贝里嫁给萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥五世，萨伏依由此与布拉班特结盟。

她把布拉班特的工匠带到萨伏依宫廷，并在那里充当外交家与政治顾问。她的姐姐玛格丽特是亨利七世之妻，亨利于1308年当选德意志国王；1310年夫妇在日内瓦探望了玛丽亚，阿梅迪奥也随亨利出征意大利。

1323年她丧夫，继子爱德华继位；她于1338年去世。女儿安娜嫁给了拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡三世·巴列奥略。

Otto (c. 1023–1057/1060), also called Oddone, was Count of Savoy from about 1051, a younger son of Humbert the White-Handed and Ancilla of Lenzburg. In 1046 he married Adelaide, heiress of the march of Susa and the county of Turin, and thereafter administered her Italian lands.

Succeeding his brother Amadeus I, he joined the counties of Maurienne and Aosta to Turin and Susa, turning the House of Savoy toward Italy. In the 1050s he briefly minted coins at Aiguebelle until a papal complaint made him stop. His son Peter I succeeded him.

奥东（约1023—1057/1060），又称奥多内，约1051年起任萨伏依伯爵，是“白手”翁贝托一世与伦茨堡的安西拉所生的较年幼的儿子。1046年，他娶苏萨边疆区与都灵伯国的女继承人阿德莱德，此后管理她在意大利的领地。

他继兄长阿梅迪奥一世之后继位，将莫里耶讷、奥斯塔与都灵、苏萨的领地合为一体，使萨伏依家族转而面向意大利发展。1050年代，他曾短暂在艾格贝勒铸币，后因教皇方面申诉而作罢，其子彼得罗一世继位。

en:
Philip I (1207–1285), youngest son of Thomas I, was a churchman: Bishop of Valence from 1241 and Archbishop of Lyon from 1245, and in 1244 he escorted Pope Innocent IV to Lyon. When the Savoyard succession fell to him, he resigned his sees, married Adelaide of Burgundy in 1267, and succeeded his brother Peter II as count in 1268.

He acquired Bresse in 1272, but in 1282 faced a coalition led by King Rudolph I and Charles of Anjou. He died childless in Roussillon on 16 August 1285, and his nephew Amadeus V succeeded him.

en:
Philip I of Savoy-Achaea (1278–25 September 1334) was lord of Piedmont and founder of the Savoy-Achaea branch. Son of Thomas III of Piedmont, he was a ward of his uncle Amadeus V of Savoy, who held his inheritance until an arbitration gave him Piedmont as a Savoyard fief.

In 1301 he married Isabella of Villehardouin, Princess of Achaea, and ruled the Morea. His appointment of followers from Savoy and Piedmont aroused the local barons' resentment, and Charles II of Naples deposed him in 1307. By Catherine de la Tour du Pin he had his heir James. He died at Pinerolo.

菲利波一世·德·萨伏依-亚该亚（1278—1334年9月25日）是皮埃蒙特领主，萨伏依-亚该亚支系的开创者。他是托马索三世之子，幼年由叔父萨伏依伯爵阿梅迪奥五世监护，后者占据了他的遗产，直到仲裁裁定他以萨伏依封臣身份领有皮埃蒙特。

en:
Peter I (c. 1048–9 August 1078), eldest son of Otto of Savoy and Adelaide of Susa, was Count of Savoy and margrave of Turin from about 1060. He ruled only in name, since his mother kept real power. About 1065 he married Agnes of Aquitaine, leaving two daughters.

He issued donation charters with his mother and his brother Amadeus II, the last in July 1078 for the abbey of Novalesa, and joined Bishop Cunibert of Turin in action against the monks of San Michele della Chiusa. On his death the county passed to Amadeus II under Salic law.

He ruled only in name, since his mother kept real power. About 1065 he married Agnes of [GetCountry('AQN').GetName], leaving two daughters.

He issued donation charters with his mother and his brother #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('sav_amedee_ii_savoy').GetID],X #L Amadeus II#!#!, the last in July 1078 for the abbey of Novalesa, and joined Bishop Cunibert of Turin in action against the monks of San Michele della Chiusa. On his death the county passed to Amadeus II under Salic law.
zh:
彼得罗一世（约1048—1078年8月9日）是奥东与苏萨的阿德莱德的长子，约1060年成为萨伏依伯爵、都灵藩侯。他只是名义上的统治者，实权始终掌握在母亲手中，约1065年娶阿基坦的阿格尼丝，留下两个女儿。

他与母亲及弟弟阿梅迪奥二世共同颁发捐赠特许状，存世的最后一件在1078年7月，对象是诺瓦莱萨修道院；他还与都灵主教库尼贝尔特联手，对圣米凯莱-德拉基乌萨修道院的修士采取行动。他死后，依照萨利克法，伯国传给阿梅迪奥二世。

en:
Peter II (c. 1203–1268), called the Little Charlemagne, was a younger son of Count Thomas I. He carved out a lordship in Vaud, gained Faucigny by marrying Agnes in 1236, and rebuilt Chillon Castle. After his niece Eleanor of Provence married Henry III, he held the Honour of Richmond from 1240 and built the Savoy Palace in London.

In 1263 he returned to succeed his childless nephew Boniface as Count of Savoy and issued the first county-wide statutes. He died on 15 May 1268 without a male heir, was buried at Hautecombe, and was succeeded by his brother Philip.

en:
Simon de Joinville (died 1276) was a younger son of Simon, lord of Joinville, and Béatrice d'Auxonne. First lord of Marnay, he married Léonète in 1252, the eldest daughter and heir of Amédée II, lord of Gex, and through her acquired the barony of Gex.

In March 1258 he concluded an agreement with the convent of Saint-Victor at Geneva. His sons Pierre and Guillaume succeeded him, and Guillaume rendered liege homage to Count Amédée V of Savoy in 1289.

en:
Thomas I (c. 1178–1233) succeeded his father Humbert III as Count of Savoy in 1189, under his mother's regency until 1191. A supporter of the Hohenstaufen, he was named Imperial Vicar of Lombardy by Frederick II in 1226 and earned the nickname the Ghibelline.

In 1195 he ambushed Margaret of Geneva's escort on her way to marry Philip II of France and married her himself; in 1219 he married their daughter Beatrice to Count Ramon Berenguer IV of Provence. He granted the Aosta Valley a charter of autonomy, took Vaud, Bugey and Cavour, and routed Montferrat with Milan in 1215. He died on 1 March 1233.

Thomas II (c. 1199–1259) was a younger son of Count Thomas I of Savoy. A former cleric, he left the church and in 1233 received the lordship of Piedmont, which he raised to a county.

From 1237 to 1244 he was count of Flanders by his marriage to Countess Joanna. In 1253 he became regent of Savoy for his nephew Count Boniface. Captured by the men of Asti at Moncalieri in 1255, he was freed in 1256 after his brothers forced a settlement.

Thomas III (c. 1246–1282), lord of Piedmont, was the eldest son of Thomas II of Savoy. Succeeding his father in 1259, he claimed Savoy when his cousin Boniface died in 1263, but was twice bypassed for his uncles. In 1274 he married Guia of Burgundy; their son Philip founded the Savoy-Achaea line.

In 1280 he captured William VII of Montferrat and forced him to surrender Turin. Mortally wounded in a feud, he died in 1282.

en:
Thomas II of Savoy-Achaea (c. 1323–1362) was a younger son of Philip I, lord of Piedmont, and Catherine de la Tour du Pin, and a younger brother of James, the reigning prince of Piedmont. Like other cadets of the house, he was sent into the church and became a canon of Lyon.

In 1346 James tried to win him the see of Ivrea, but Clement VI refused because Thomas was only twenty-two. In 1348 the same pope named him bishop of Turin, and he was consecrated on 3 April 1351.

As bishop Thomas stood by James and the Achaea line and rebuilt the cathedral of Saint John in Turin. He died in Turin in 1362.

en:
Bernhard (c. 1140–1212), youngest son of Albert the Bear, inherited in 1170 the Ascanian estates that formed the nucleus of Anhalt. After Henry the Lion was outlawed in 1180, Emperor Frederick Barbarossa granted him the Duchy of Saxony, though only reduced lands around Wittenberg and Lauenburg remained.

He destroyed rebellious Lauenburg and moved his court to Wittenberg. He died on 2 February 1212; his sons Henry and Albert founded the Anhalt and Saxon lines of the Ascanians.

en:
Henry the Proud (c. 1108–1139) of the House of Welf became Duke of Bavaria in 1126 and in 1127 married Gertrude, heiress of King Lothair III of Germany.

He fought for Lothair against the Hohenstaufen and campaigned with him in Italy in 1136, winning Tuscany and Spoleto. Rewarded with the Duchy of Saxony, he was the leading candidate to succeed Lothair as king in 1138 but lost the election to Conrad III.

Conrad refused to invest him with Saxony, saying one man could not hold two duchies. Placed under the ban, Henry recovered Saxony by force in 1139, then died suddenly at Quedlinburg on 20 October while preparing to invade Bavaria.

骄傲者亨利（约1108—1139）出身韦尔夫家族，1126年成为巴伐利亚公爵，1127年娶德意志国王洛泰尔二世的继承人格特鲁德。

他为洛泰尔同霍亨斯陶芬家族作战，1136年随其远征意大利，获得托斯卡纳和斯波莱托。他又受封萨克森公国，是1138年继承王位的最有力人选，却在选举中败给康拉德三世。

康拉德拒绝将萨克森正式授予他，理由是一人不能兼有两个公国。亨利遭帝国放逐后，于1139年以武力收复萨克森，随后在准备进军巴伐利亚时，于10月20日猝死于奎德林堡。

Abang Kina, titled Kyai Agung Natanegara, is named by the royal genealogy of Selimbau as the fifteenth ruler of that Hindu kingdom in what is now Kapuas Hulu, West Kalimantan. The genealogy gives his reign as 1300 to 1380.

It makes him the successor of Suryanegara, who ruled from 1280 to 1300, and the predecessor of Abang Keladi, titled Kyai Agung Cakranegara. The genealogy numbers him among the Hindu rajas who reigned before the dynasty turned to Islam.

Ala al-Din Muhammad was an official of the Ilkhanid claimant Togha Temur, governing Sabzavar in Khurasan. His oppressive taxation drove the landowner Abd al-Razzaq to kill his nephew at Bashtin and raise the revolt that became the Sarbadar state.

The rebels seized Sabzavar in the summer of 1337. In 1340, after the khan's army was destroyed by the Sarbadars, he was killed fleeing toward Mazandaran with the khan's brother.

Adolph VI (1256–1315) was Count of Holstein-Pinneberg and Schaumburg and founder of the younger Schauenburg line. Third son of Gerhard I of Holstein-Itzehoe, he received Pinneberg and the ancestral county of Schauenburg at the 1290 partition, and ruled mostly south of the Elbe.

In 1302 he built the water castle at Bückeburg guarding the Hellweg trade road. He married Helen of Saxe-Lauenburg and died on 13 May 1315, leaving his son Adolph VII to succeed him.

Adolf VII (c. 1297–1354) was Count of Schauenburg and Holstein-Pinneberg from 1315, eldest son of Adolf VI and Helena of Saxe-Lauenburg. When John II of Holstein-Kiel died in 1316, Gerhard III of Rendsburg and John III of Plön seized his lands.

Adolf claimed a share and warred, only to lose at Bramstedt in 1317. He married Heilwig zur Lippe in 1322, and his sons included Adolf VIII and Otto I. He died in 1354.

He died on 13 October 1370 at Famagusta in Cyprus on that journey. He left no children, and his brother Otto I succeeded him.

John of Ścinawa (c. 1298–before 19 May 1365) was a Silesian Piast, the fourth son of Henry III, Duke of Głogów. After his father's death he ruled with his brothers, receiving Ścinawa and neighbouring lands as his duchy in 1317. In 1329 he paid homage to King John of Bohemia at Wrocław.

Dogged by debts, he sold or pledged parts of his duchy; in 1337 his brothers bought Ścinawa, though he kept sovereignty for life. He married Margaret of Pomerania and died childless by May 1365.
