Jean II de Roussillon was a Benedictine monk from the noble de Roussillon family of the Dauphiné, elected abbot of Saint-Claude (then called Saint-Oyend) in the Jura in 1328.

Early in his abbacy he settled the long feud with the Joinville lords of Gex over the upper Valserine valley, concluding a treaty that made the valley a shared possession with its revenues divided, and in 1334 the two sides founded a pilgrim hospice at Mijoux. He governed the abbey until 1348, when Guillaume IV de Beauregard was elected to succeed him on 12 September.

上任之初，他结束了修道院与茹安维尔家族热克斯领主们为上瓦尔瑟里讷河谷持续多年的冲突，缔约规定河谷由双方共有、收入平分；1334年双方又在米茹修建收容前往孔达圣徒陵墓朝圣者的济贫院。他掌院至1348年，同年9月12日纪尧姆四世·德·博勒加尔当选继任。

en:
Áed mac Cináeda (Anglicized Hugh, c. 840–878), son of Kenneth MacAlpin, became king of the Picts in 877 after the death of his brother Causantín. A later Gaelic poem, the Duan Albanach, gave him the epithet Fhionnscothach, ‘of the White Flowers’.

He ruled barely a year: the sources record him slain by kinsmen in 878, and later chroniclers blamed his successor Giric. His son Causantín reigned as Constantine II from 900.

艾德·麦克·肯尼思（约840—878）是肯尼思一世之子，877年其兄康斯坦丁一世死后即位为皮克特人国王。后世的盖尔语诗篇给他“白花”的绰号。

Alan fitz Walter (c. 1140–1204) succeeded his father Walter fitz Alan in 1178 as hereditary High Steward of Scotland, serving William the Lion until his death. Under him the family acquired the Isle of Bute, and Rothesay Castle was possibly built on his initiative.

Later accounts say he joined Richard the Lionheart on the Third Crusade. A patron of the Knights Templar, he expanded the order's Scottish holdings, and died in 1204, buried at Paisley Abbey.

en:
Alexander Comyn, second Earl of Buchan (c. 1217–1289), was a leading Scoto-Norman magnate and chief counsellor of King Alexander III. The son of William Comyn and Marjory of Buchan, he served as Justiciar of Scotia from 1258.

In 1284 he joined the nobles who recognised Margaret of Norway as heir, and after Alexander III's death he was one of the Guardians of Scotland from 1286 until he died in 1289. He left many children, including his heir John.

第二代巴肯伯爵亚历山大·科明（约1217—1289）是重要的苏格兰—诺曼大贵族，国王亚历山大三世的首席顾问。他是威廉·科明与巴肯的玛乔丽之子，1258年起任苏格兰司法官。

en:
Alexander Comyn (c. 1258–1308) was a younger son of Alexander Comyn, second Earl of Buchan. While the earldom passed to his elder brother John, he served as sheriff of Aberdeen from 1297 to 1304, during the First War of Scottish Independence.

He left two daughters, Alice and Margaret. He died in 1308, shortly before his childless brother John, and the title to the earldom of Buchan passed to his daughters.

en:
Alexander Bruce, Earl of Carrick (d. 19 July 1333), was an illegitimate son of Edward Bruce, Earl of Carrick, younger brother of King Robert I. During Edward Balliol's invasion he fought for the Bruce loyalists at Dupplin Moor in 1332, then defected to Balliol and was captured and nearly killed at Annan before rejoining the crown.

Married to Eleanor Douglas, daughter of the guardian Sir Archibald Douglas, he fell fighting for the young King David II at Halidon Hill in 1333.

亚历山大·布鲁斯，卡里克伯爵（1333年7月19日卒），是国王罗伯特一世之弟、卡里克伯爵爱德华·布鲁斯的私生子。爱德华·巴里奥入侵期间，他先于1332年在杜普林沼地为布鲁斯一方作战，随后倒向巴里奥，在安南被俘、险些被杀，之后又重归王党。

en:
Alexander I, called the Fierce (c. 1078–1124), was a son of Malcolm III and Saint Margaret and king of Scotland from 1107, when he succeeded his brother Edgar. He married Sybilla of Normandy, daughter of Henry I of England, but the marriage was childless.

After Moray rebels attacked his court at Invergowrie, he chased and defeated them at Stockford in Ross, earning his nickname. He founded the Augustinian priory at Scone around 1115, died at Stirling on 23 April 1124, and was succeeded by his brother David I.

亚历山大一世，绰号“猛烈的”（约1078—1124），是马尔科姆三世与圣玛格丽特之子，1107年继承兄长埃德加的王位。他娶英格兰国王亨利一世之女西比拉为妻，两人没有子女。

en:
Alexander II (1198–1249), son of William the Lion, succeeded his father in 1214 aged sixteen. In the First Barons’ War he supported John’s rebel barons and campaigned in northern England, then made peace with Henry III and married his sister Joan in 1221.

He crushed the MacWilliam risings and subdued Galloway, while the Treaty of York in 1237 fixed the Anglo-Scottish border much as it remains. After Joan’s death he married Marie de Coucy in 1239, mother of Alexander III. In 1249 he sailed to subdue the Hebrides but died on Kerrera.

zh:
亚历山大二世（1198—1249）是狮子王威廉之子，1214年十六岁时继承父位。第一次诸侯战争期间，他支持反叛约翰王的英格兰诸侯，在英格兰北部作战，随后与亨利三世议和，并于1221年娶亨利之妹琼为妻。

他镇压麦克威廉叛乱，平定加洛韦；1237年的《约克条约》划定了与英格兰的边界，其走向大体沿用至今。琼死后，他于1239年续娶库西的玛丽，即亚历山大三世之母。1249年他出征赫布里底群岛，却在克雷拉岛上去世。

en:
Alexander III (1241–1286), son of Alexander II and Marie de Coucy, succeeded in 1249 aged seven and was crowned at Scone. In 1251 he married Margaret, daughter of Henry III, but refused homage for Scotland. He claimed the Western Isles from Norway; Haakon IV invaded in 1263, but a storm damaged his ships and the Battle of Largs was indecisive.

By the Treaty of Perth in 1266 Scotland gained the Hebrides and Man. When his children died, his granddaughter Margaret, Maid of Norway, was named heir in 1284. He died in a riding fall at Kinghorn in 1286.

Alexander Stewart of Dundonald (c. 1214–1283) succeeded his father as hereditary High Steward of Scotland in 1241. He joined Louis IX of France on the Seventh Crusade, where his brother John was killed at Damietta in 1249. In 1255 he served as a regent during the minority of Alexander III.

In October 1263 he commanded the Scottish army at Largs, repelling the invasion of Haakon IV of Norway. Under him the Stewarts gained the Cowal peninsula and Dunoon Castle. He died in 1283.

Alice Comyn (1289–1349) was the eldest daughter of Alexander Comyn, Sheriff of Aberdeen, and niece and heiress of John Comyn, Earl of Buchan. In 1310 she married the English baron Henry de Beaumont, who claimed the earldom in her right; his long struggle to secure Buchan helped cause the Second War of Scottish Independence.

Through her daughter Isabel she was great-grandmother of Henry IV. She died on 3 July 1349, when the Comyn line of Buchan came to an end.

Alpín mac Echdach (died 834) is the king of Dál Riata remembered as father of Kenneth MacAlpin, founder of the ruling line of Alba. He appears only in later chronicles, which give him a three-year reign from 831, spent warring against the Picts who had overrun his kingdom.

Later accounts tell of an initial victory near Angus, in which the Pictish king fell, followed by Alpín's defeat and death in Galloway in 834, reportedly beheaded after capture. His son Kenneth succeeded him.

阿尔平·麦克·埃赫达（?—834）是后世谱系中的达尔里阿达国王，被记为阿尔巴王族开创者肯尼思一世之父。后世编年史记载他于831年继位，在位三年，不断与侵占其国土的皮克特人交战。

en:
Sir Andrew Murray (1298–1338) was the posthumous son of Andrew Moray, commander at Stirling Bridge, and held the lordships of Avoch, Petty and Bothwell. When Robert I's regent Thomas Randolph died in 1332 and his successor, the Earl of Mar, was killed at Dupplin Moor nine days after being chosen, Edward Balliol was crowned and David II's supporters named Murray Guardian; they chose him again in 1335.

Taken prisoner in 1333, he refused to yield to anyone but the English king and was carried to Durham. Freed in 1334, he forced Henry de Beaumont out of Dundarg Castle by cutting its water pipes.

In 1335 he marched north to relieve Kildrummy, held by his wife Christina Bruce, sister of Robert I, and killed David of Strathbogie at Culblean. He fell ill besieging Edinburgh Castle, went home to Avoch and died in 1338; he lies at Dunfermline Abbey.

安德鲁·默里爵士（1298—1338）是斯特灵桥之战指挥官安德鲁·默里的遗腹子，据有阿沃赫、佩蒂和博斯韦尔领地。1332年，罗伯特一世指定的摄政托马斯·伦道夫去世，继任的马尔伯爵当选九天后便在达普林荒原战死，爱德华·巴里奥加冕，大卫二世的支持者推举默里为护国官，1335年再度推举他。

1333年他被俘，坚称只向英格兰国王投降，被押往达勒姆。1334年获释后，他切断敦达格城堡的水管，迫使亨利·德·博蒙出降。

1335年，他北上解救基尔德拉米城堡，守城的是他的妻子克里斯蒂娜·布鲁斯；他在库尔布伦杀死了大卫·斯特拉斯博吉。他在围攻爱丁堡城堡时染病，回到阿沃赫，1338年去世，葬于邓弗姆林修道院。

Sir Archibald Douglas (before 1298–1333) was the younger son of William le Hardi and half-brother of the Good Sir James. When Edward Balliol invaded with English backing in 1332, Douglas surprised him in a night attack at Annan and drove him back to England.

He was appointed Guardian of Scotland in March 1333. In July he marched to relieve besieged Berwick and was killed leading the uphill assault at the Battle of Halidon Hill on 19 July 1333.

en:
Archibald Douglas, called the Grim (c. 1330–1400), was the illegitimate son of Sir James the Black Douglas, Robert the Bruce's lieutenant. In 1342 he was named an heir to the Douglas lands.

In 1362 he married Joanna de Moravia, heiress of Bothwell, whose estates he took. As Lord of Galloway he was the Black Douglases' chief magnate. After his kinsman James, 2nd Earl, fell at Otterburn without legitimate issue, Archibald inherited as 3rd Earl of Douglas. He died at Threave Castle in 1400 and was buried at Bothwell.

Agnes Randolph, called Black Agnes for her dark complexion, was the daughter of Thomas Randolph, Earl of Moray, and in 1324 married Patrick, Earl of Dunbar and March.

While her husband was away in 1338, she took command of Dunbar Castle and held it for months against an English army, forcing the besiegers to abandon the blockade during the Second War of Scottish Independence. She died in 1369 and was buried near Mordington.

Christina Bruce (c. 1278–1356/57), sister of King Robert I of Scots, married Sir Christopher Seton in 1301; he was executed by the English in 1306. Captured after Kildrummy Castle fell, she spent eight years confined in a Lincolnshire nunnery and was freed in 1314 in a prisoner exchange after Bannockburn.

In 1326 she married Sir Andrew Murray, Guardian of Scotland. In 1335 she held Kildrummy Castle against David of Strathbogie until Murray's victory at Culblean. She died in 1356 or 1357.

克里斯蒂娜·布鲁斯（约1278—1356/1357）是苏格兰国王罗伯特一世的妹妹。1301年她嫁给克里斯托弗·西顿爵士，后者于1306年被英格兰人处决。基尔德鲁米城堡陷落后她被俘，在林肯郡的一所修女院被关押八年，1314年在班诺克本战役后的一次俘虏交换中获释。

en:
Sir Colin Og Campbell of Lochawe (died 1340) was the eldest son of Sir Neil Campbell and stepson of Mary Bruce, sister of Robert the Bruce. In 1316 the king granted him Lochawe and Ardscotnish as a free barony, in return for troops and a forty-oared galley when required.

He campaigned with Bruce in Ireland in 1315–1318 and later supported David II against Edward Balliol. By his wife Helena he left a son Archibald, ancestor of the Earls of Argyll.

en:
Causantín mac Cináeda, counted as Constantine I (c. 836–877), was a son of Kenneth MacAlpin who succeeded his uncle Domnall as king of the Picts in 862. His reign was dominated by Viking attacks: in 870 Norse leaders sacked Dumbarton Rock, stronghold of Alt Clut.

Two years later Causantín had its fugitive king Artgal killed. After a defeat near Dollar in 875, he fell fighting Vikings in Fife in 877, reportedly beheaded, and was buried on Iona.

康斯坦丁一世（盖尔语名考桑廷·麦克·基纳达，约836—877）是肯尼思一世之子，862年叔叔唐纳德去世后继任皮克特人国王。他在位时维京人连年进犯：870年诺斯人攻陷不列颠人王国阿尔特克鲁德的要塞邓巴顿岩。

en:
Causantín mac Áeda, anglicised Constantine II (died 952), son of Áed and grandson of Kenneth MacAlpin, ruled Alba from 900 to 943, the longest reign of any early Scottish king. He spent it containing the Uí Ímair Vikings and the ambitions of Wessex.

After Æthelstan invaded Alba in 934, he allied with the kings of Dublin and Strathclyde, but was defeated at Brunanburh in 937, where his son Cellach fell. In 943 he abdicated to the Culdee monastery at St Andrews and died there in 952; his reign saw Pictland remade as the Gaelic kingdom of Alba.

Causantín mac Cuiléin, anglicised as Constantine III and called Constantine the Bald, was a son of King Cuilén and ruled the kingdom of Alba from 995 to 997. He is portrayed as conspiring against Kenneth II, who was killed at Fettercairn in 995, after which Constantine seized the crown.

His reign was a struggle with Kenneth II's son Malcolm and Malcolm's uncle Kenneth. In 997 he was killed in battle at Rathinveramon near Perth, and Kenneth III succeeded him.

Cuilén mac Ilduilb, anglicised Colin (died 971), son of Indulf and nicknamed An Fionn, ‘the White’, ruled Alba from 967. After challenging Dub he was defeated in 965, but Dub was expelled and killed in 967.

en:
David I (c. 1084–1153), youngest son of Malcolm III and Saint Margaret, entered the court of Henry I as a young man before succeeding his brother Alexander I as king of Scots in 1124. He spent a decade subduing rivals such as Óengus of Moray.

Backing his niece Matilda against Stephen, he invaded England, was defeated at the Battle of the Standard in 1138, yet secured Northumberland and Cumbria. His reign brought the Davidian Revolution of burghs, monasteries and feudal tenure. He died at Carlisle in 1153, venerated as a saint.

en:
David II (1324–1371), son of Robert the Bruce, became king of Scots in 1329 and was crowned at Scone in 1331, the first anointed Scottish king. Married to Joan of the Tower, he fled to France after Halidon Hill in 1333 and returned in 1341.

Captured at Neville's Cross in 1346, he was held eleven years until the 1357 Treaty of Berwick fixed his ransom at one hundred thousand merks. The last male Bruce, he died childless in 1371, and his nephew Robert II succeeded.

en:
Sir David II Strathbogie (died 28 December 1326) was Earl of Atholl, the son of Earl John Strathbogie and Marjory, daughter of the Earl of Mar. A prisoner in England in 1300, he succeeded his father in 1306 and recovered the Atholl estates in 1307, then rebelled against Robert the Bruce and was banished, forfeiting his Scottish lands.

Serving the English crown, he received three Norfolk manors in compensation and the barony of Chilham in Kent in 1321, became warden of Northumberland in 1322, and commanded English troops in Gascony in 1325.

en:
David III Strathbogie (1309–1335) was the son of David II Strathbogie, Earl of Atholl, whose title was forfeited after he defected to England. In 1327 David served with Edward III on the Weardale campaign in Scotland, and in 1332 joined the disinherited lords who backed Edward Balliol.

He fought at Dupplin Moor, where Balliol restored him as Earl of Atholl, and at Halidon Hill in 1333. He changed sides twice during the wars that followed, returning to Balliol in 1335. On 30 November 1335 he was killed at Culblean fighting the guardian Andrew Murray's army. His son David IV never reclaimed Atholl.

en:
David IV Strathbogie (c. 1332–1369) was an Anglo-Scottish noble who inherited the barony of Strabolgi and the forfeited, titular earldom of Atholl as a small child, after his father David III was killed fighting for Edward Balliol at the Battle of Culblean in 1335.

He married Elizabeth Ferrers and was summoned among the English barons. He died in 1369 leaving only two daughters, so his barony fell into abeyance and his estates were divided between them.

en:
Donald I, Domnall mac Ailpín (812–862), followed his brother Kenneth MacAlpin as king of the Picts in 858 and ruled for four years. The Chronicle of the Kings of Alba records that in his reign the Gaels and their king established the rights and laws of the kingdom, the laws of Áed, at Forteviot.

He died on 13 April 862 and was buried on Iona. The kingship passed to his nephew Constantine, son of Kenneth.

Donald II (c. 862–900), son of Constantine I, took power in 889 after the fall of Giric, who had killed his uncle Áed, and was nicknamed Dásachtach, ‘the Madman’. Irish annals style him king of Alba, not king of the Picts.

He spent his reign fighting Vikings: he defeated the Danes at Innisibsolian, then died at Norse hands when Dunnottar was sacked in 900. He was succeeded by his cousin Constantine II; his son later reigned as Malcolm I.

Donald III, or Donald the Fair (c. 1032–1099), second son of Duncan I, spent his youth in Irish exile after Macbeth killed his father in 1040. When his brother Malcolm III fell at Alnwick in 1093, Donald seized the crown and expelled the English courtiers and Margaret's sons.

His nephew Duncan II displaced him with English backing in 1094, but Duncan's murder later that year restored him. In 1097 another nephew, Edgar, overthrew him with English aid; Donald was blinded and died in prison in 1099.

Dub (c. 928–967), son of Malcolm I, became king of Alba in 962 after Indulf's death; his Gaelic name meant ‘the Black’. He spent his reign fighting Indulf's son Cuilén, defeating him at the ridge of Crup, yet was later driven from the kingdom.

He was killed by the Scots themselves in 967; later legend said he was murdered at Forres and his body hidden under Kinloss bridge. His son Kenneth III later reigned.

Duncan I (c. 1001–1040), nicknamed An t-Ilgarach, the Sick, was king of Alba from 1034. A grandson of King Malcolm II, he succeeded his grandfather unopposed that year.

In 1039 he besieged Durham and was routed. The next year he marched into Moray, the domain of his war leader Macbeth, and was killed near Elgin in 1040, opening the way for Macbeth's kingship. He was the historical King Duncan of Shakespeare's Macbeth.

Duncan II (c. 1060–1094) was the eldest son of Malcolm III. Handed to William the Conqueror as a hostage in 1072, he grew up a knight at the Norman court. After his uncle Donald III seized the throne in 1093, Duncan invaded with troops lent by William II, won and was crowned at Scone in 1094.

Once he dismissed his foreign soldiers he was ambushed and killed by Donald's men on 12 November 1094, after less than seven months as king.

en:
Edgar, called Probus (c. 1074–1107), was the fourth son of Malcolm III and Saint Margaret and ruled Scotland from 1097. After Duncan II was murdered in 1094, he claimed the crown with English backing, and in 1097 English forces defeated Donald III and Edmund and set him on the throne.

His peaceful reign saw him recognize Magnus Barefoot's hold on the Hebrides and Kintyre. He died unmarried at Edinburgh in 1107 and was succeeded by his brother Alexander.

en:
Edward Balliol (c. 1283–1364) was the eldest son of John Balliol, the Scottish king who abdicated in 1296, and was held in the Tower of London until 1299. When Robert I died in 1329, leaving an infant heir, Balliol joined the Disinherited, English magnates who had lost Scottish lands in the peace.

In 1332, with covert English backing, they invaded, won at Dupplin Moor and had him crowned at Scone, but he was soon driven out and turned to Edward III. Edward's army won at Halidon Hill in 1333 and set him on the throne again, in return for much of southern Scotland; in 1334 Balliol ceded Lothian and did homage.

Forces loyal to David II regained the country, and defeats in 1335 unravelled his cause. The Scots never accepted him. In 1356 he surrendered his claim to Edward III for a pension and died childless in 1364.

爱德华·巴里奥（约1283—1364）是苏格兰国王约翰·巴里奥的长子，其父于1296年退位，他本人被囚于伦敦塔，直到1299年获释。1329年罗伯特一世去世、留下年幼的继承人，巴里奥加入“被剥夺继承权者”的行列，这是一批在和约中失去苏格兰领地的英格兰贵族。

1332年，他们在英格兰暗中支持下入侵苏格兰，在杜普林沼泽取胜，并让他在斯昆加冕；但他很快被逐出，转而求助爱德华三世。1333年英军在哈利顿山获胜，把他重新扶上王位，代价是苏格兰南部大片土地；1334年他割让洛锡安并向英王行臣服礼。

支持大卫二世的势力逐步收复全国，1335年的连番挫败使他的事业瓦解。苏格兰人始终没有接受他。1356年，他以年金为条件把王位要求让给爱德华三世，1364年无嗣而终。

en:
Edward Bruce (c. 1280–1318), Earl of Carrick, was Robert the Bruce's younger brother and a chief captain in the Scottish wars of independence. He fought at Bannockburn in 1314, and in 1315 landed at Larne in Ulster to open a second front against England; with Irish backing he was proclaimed High King of Ireland and crowned the next year.

His three-year campaign ended in defeat and death at the Battle of Faughart on 14 October 1318. His illegitimate son Alexander later inherited Carrick.

Elizabeth de Burgh (c. 1289–1327) was the second wife and queen of King Robert I of Scots. Daughter of Richard Óg de Burgh, Earl of Ulster, she married Robert in 1302 and was crowned beside him at Scone in March 1306.

Captured with the Bruce women by the Earl of Ross after Methven and handed to England, she remained a prisoner until her exchange in 1314 after Bannockburn. She bore the future David II and died in 1327 after falling from her horse at Cullen.

Elizabeth de Comyn (1299–1372) was the daughter of John Comyn of Badenoch, murdered by Robert Bruce at Dumfries in 1306. After her uncle Aymer de Valence, Earl of Pembroke, died in 1324, she inherited Goodrich, but the Despensers imprisoned her and forced her to surrender her estates.

Released in 1325, she secretly married Richard Talbot, who retook Goodrich after Queen Isabella's invasion in 1326. Their son Gilbert later became third Baron Talbot. Widowed in 1356, she remarried and died in 1372.

Elizabeth Mure was the daughter of Sir Adam Mure of Rowallan. Around 1336 she entered a secular marriage with Robert Stewart, High Steward of Scotland, which contemporaries criticized as uncanonical; after a papal dispensation in 1347 the couple remarried in 1349.

She bore Robert at least ten children, including the future Robert III and the Duke of Albany, but died before 1355, long before her husband took the throne as Robert II in 1371.

伊丽莎白·缪尔是罗阿兰的亚当·缪尔爵士之女。约1336年，她与苏格兰王室总管罗伯特·斯图亚特按世俗婚姻结合，时人批评这桩婚姻不合教规；1347年教皇特许颁布后，两人于1349年重新成婚。

她为罗伯特产下至少十个子女，包括后来的罗伯特三世和奥尔巴尼公爵，但她在1355年前便已去世，远早于丈夫1371年登基为罗伯特二世。

en:
Eochaid ab Rhun (fl. 853–889) was the son of Rhun, British king of Strathclyde, by a daughter of Cináed mac Ailpín, king of the Picts. After Áed mac Cináeda was killed by Giric in 878, sources link Eochaid with rule over the Picts, perhaps reigning alongside Giric while he retained Strathclyde.

In 889 Eochaid and Giric were driven out; their successor, the Alpínid Domnall mac Custantín, may have been responsible. Nothing more is recorded of Eochaid.

奥凯德·阿普·伦（853—889年间有载）是不列颠人的斯特拉斯克莱德国王伦之子，母亲是皮克特王辛纳德·麦克埃尔平（即肯尼思一世）之女。878年艾德·麦克辛纳德被吉里克所杀后，据史籍记载，奥凯德与皮克特人的王位联系在一起，可能与吉里克共治，同时仍领有斯特拉斯克莱德。

889年，奥凯德与吉里克被驱逐，继位的阿尔平家族成员多姆纳尔·麦克君士坦丁可能是驱逐他们的人。此后奥凯德再无记载。

Gilbert Talbot, 3rd Baron Talbot (c. 1332–1387) was an English nobleman and soldier, succeeding his father Richard as baron in 1356. He fought in France under the Black Prince, and in 1381 campaigned in Portugal and Spain under the Earl of Cambridge and took part in the capture of Higuera la Real.

He returned to Spain in 1386 with John of Gaunt, who was pressing his claim to Castile, and died there of the plague in 1387, leaving heavy debts. His son Richard succeeded him.

第三代塔尔博特男爵吉尔伯特·塔尔博特（约1332—1387）是英格兰贵族、军人，1356年继承父亲理查德的男爵爵位。他随黑太子在法兰西作战，1381年随剑桥伯爵征战葡萄牙与西班牙，参与攻占伊格拉拉雷亚尔。

1386年，他随正主张卡斯蒂利亚王位的冈特的约翰再赴西班牙，1387年死于当地鼠疫，身后留下沉重债务，儿子理查德继位。

en:
Henry de Beaumont (1280–1340) was an English baron, son of Louis of Brienne, and a leader of the Disinherited, the nobles whose Scottish lands Robert I had forfeited. A household knight of Edward I, he fought at Falkirk, where Wallace's spearmen killed his horse under him.

By 1310 he had married Alice Comyn, heiress of the earldom of Buchan, and claimed it in her right. In 1331 he persuaded Edward Balliol to come to England and helped plan the invasion of 1332, which won Dupplin Moor and Balliol's crown at Scone.

After Halidon Hill he returned to Buchan and rebuilt Dundarg Castle, where Andrew Murray besieged him and forced his surrender on 23 December 1334. He followed Edward III to the Low Countries in 1338 and died there in 1340. His son John never claimed Buchan, and the Comyn line of Buchan ended with Alice's death in 1349.

亨利·德·博蒙（1280—1340）是英格兰男爵，布里耶纳的路易之子，也是苏格兰领地被罗伯特一世没收的“被剥夺者”首领之一。他是爱德华一世的宫廷骑士，在福尔柯克被华莱士的长枪方阵刺死坐骑。

1310年前后，他娶巴肯伯爵领地继承人爱丽丝·科明，以妻权主张该领地。1331年他说服爱德华·巴里奥来到英格兰，参与筹划1332年的入侵，杜普林沼泽一战获胜，巴里奥在斯昆加冕。

哈利顿山之战后，他回到巴肯重建敦达格城堡，安德鲁·默里围攻此地，迫使他于1334年12月23日投降。1338年他随爱德华三世前往低地国家，1340年死于当地。其子约翰从未主张巴肯伯爵之位；1349年爱丽丝去世后科明一脉断绝。

Indulf (c. 927–962), son of Constantine II, ruled Alba from 954 to 962 and was nicknamed An Ionsaighthigh, ‘the Aggressor’. In his day oppidum Eden, usually identified as Edinburgh, was abandoned to the Scots, marking their advance into Lothian.

In 962 he fell fighting Vikings near Cullen at the Battle of Bauds. He was buried on Iona and succeeded by Dub; his own sons Cuilén and Amlaíb both later reigned.

英多尔夫（约927—962）是康斯坦丁二世之子，954—962年为阿尔巴国王，绰号“侵略者”。他在位时，通常被认为即今爱丁堡的“伊甸城”被弃守给苏格兰人，标志着盖尔势力进入洛锡安。

962年，他在卡伦附近的鲍兹战役中与维京人作战阵亡，葬于艾奥纳岛，由杜夫继位；他的亲子科林与安拿比后来都登上了王位。

en:
Isabella de Warenne (c. 1253–before 1292) was the daughter of John de Warenne, sixth Earl of Surrey, and Alice de Lusignan, half-sister of Henry III of England. In 1281 she married John Balliol, head of the powerful Balliol house and a future claimant to the Scottish throne.

The marriage linked the Balliols to the English court and produced Edward Balliol, later himself a pretender to the Scottish crown. Isabella is thought to have died before 1292, when her husband was chosen king, so she was probably never queen.

伊莎贝拉·德·瓦伦（约1253—1292年前）是第六代萨里伯爵约翰·德·瓦伦与艾丽斯·德·吕西尼昂之女，其母是英格兰国王亨利三世同母异父的妹妹。约1281年，她嫁给巴利奥尔家族首领约翰·巴里奥——一个有权问鼎苏格兰王位的人。

这桩婚姻把巴利奥尔家族与英格兰宫廷联结起来，她生下爱德华·巴里奥，后者后来也成为苏格兰王位的觊觎者。一般认为她在1292年丈夫被推举为国王之前便已去世，很可能从未成为王后。

en:
Iye Mackay, 4th of Strathnaver, was chief of Clan Mackay in the Highlands, succeeding his father Donald Mackay, 3rd of Strathnaver. His long feud with the Earl of Sutherland ended in 1370, when he and his eldest son and heir Donald were murdered at Dingwall Castle by the earl's party.

His daughter Mariota married Alexander Stewart, Earl of Buchan, the Wolf of Badenoch. Since Donald died with him, the chiefship passed to his grandson Angus Mackay.

第四代斯特拉思纳弗首领伊耶·麦凯是高地麦凯氏族的首领，继承了父亲第三代首领唐纳德·麦凯之位。他与萨瑟兰伯爵长期结仇，1370年，他与长子兼继承人唐纳德在丁沃尔城堡被伯爵一方杀害。

他的女儿玛丽奥塔嫁给了巴肯伯爵亚历山大·斯图亚特（“巴德诺赫之狼”）。由于唐纳德与他同时遇害，首领之位传给了孙子安格斯·麦凯。

en:
Sir James Douglas, called the Black Douglas (c. 1286–1330), was Robert the Bruce's most feared lieutenant in the Scottish Wars of Independence. He retook Douglas Castle in the 1307 massacre remembered as the Douglas Larder, seized Roxburgh Castle in 1314 and fought at Bannockburn.

His raids into England helped force the 1328 Treaty of Northampton. After Bruce died he carried the king's heart to Spain and was killed fighting the Moors at Teba on 25 August 1330.

詹姆斯·道格拉斯爵士，绰号“黑道格拉斯”（约1286—1330），是苏格兰独立战争中罗伯特·布鲁斯麾下最令敌人胆寒的将领。1307年，他以被称作“道格拉斯储藏室”的屠杀夺回家族的道格拉斯城堡，1314年攻取罗克斯堡城堡，并参加班诺克本战役。

他深入英格兰的奔袭促成了1328年的《诺咸顿条约》。布鲁斯死后，他携国王的心脏前往西班牙，1330年8月25日在特瓦战役与摩尔人作战时阵亡。

en:
James Stewart (c. 1260–1309) was the fifth High Steward of Scotland. In 1286 he became one of the six Guardians ruling during the interregnum. He first supported William Wallace and, after the defeat at Falkirk in 1298, transferred his backing to Robert Bruce.

Sent to France in 1302, he nevertheless swore fealty to Edward I in 1306, then returned to the Scottish cause. He died in Bruce's service in 1309, leaving a son Walter, the sixth High Steward.

詹姆斯·斯图亚特（约1260—1309）是第五代苏格兰王室总务官。1286年，他成为王位空悬期间六位护国官之一。他起初支持威廉·华莱士，1298年福尔柯克战败后转而支持罗伯特·布鲁斯。

1302年他奉命出使法国寻求援助，1306年却向爱德华一世宣誓效忠，随后又回归苏格兰阵营。1309年，他在效力布鲁斯期间去世，生子沃尔特，即第六代总务官。

en:
John de Balliol (before 1208 – 1268) was an Anglo-Scottish baron of Barnard Castle. In 1223 he married Dervorguilla of Galloway, whose wealthy inheritance funded his career. On Henry III's instruction he served as a joint protector of the young Alexander III of Scotland and was a leading counsellor of Henry from 1258 to 1265.

Captured at the Battle of Lewes in 1264, he escaped and rejoined Henry. After a dispute with the bishop of Durham, he supported scholars at Oxford from around 1263; Dervorguilla's later endowments helped establish Balliol College. He died in 1268; his son John was chosen king of Scots in 1292.

约翰·德·巴利奥尔（1208年以前—1268）是领有巴纳德城堡的英苏贵族。1223年，他娶加洛韦的德沃尔吉拉为妻，妻子丰厚的遗产资助了他的仕途。他奉亨利三世之命担任年幼的苏格兰国王亚历山大三世的共同保护人，并在1258至1265年间任亨利的主要顾问之一。

1264年他在刘易斯战役中被俘，随后逃脱并重新投奔亨利。与达勒姆主教发生争执后，他从约1263年起资助牛津的学者；德沃尔吉拉后来的捐赠促成了巴利奥尔学院的建立。他于1268年去世，其子约翰于1292年被推举为苏格兰国王。

en:
John Balliol (c. 1249–1314), derisively called Toom Tabard, meaning Empty Coat, was King of Scots from 1292 to 1296. Edward I of England chose him as king, but treated Scotland as an English vassal.

In 1295 Balliol renounced his fealty and concluded the Auld Alliance with France. Edward invaded, and after the defeat of 1296 Balliol abdicated and was imprisoned in the Tower of London. He later retired to France and died there in 1314; his son Edward Balliol revived the claim.

约翰·巴里奥（约1249—1314）被讥称为“空外套”（图姆·塔巴德），1292至1296年任苏格兰国王。英格兰国王爱德华一世选中巴里奥为王，却把苏格兰当作英格兰的附庸。

1295年，巴里奥宣布不再效忠爱德华，并与法国缔结“老同盟”。爱德华随即发兵入侵，1296年苏格兰战败后，巴里奥退位并被囚禁于伦敦塔。他后来退隐法兰西，1314年在那里去世；其子爱德华·巴里奥后来重新提出王位主张。

en:
John de Beaumont (1318–1342), second Baron Beaumont, was the son of Henry de Beaumont and Alice Comyn, heiress of Buchan. His family was the English branch of the French house of Brienne. Where his father had claimed the Scottish earldom of Buchan through his wife, John never used the title.

His marriage tied him to the house of Lancaster: on 6 November 1330 he married Eleanor of Lancaster, sister of Henry of Grosmont. In 1338 John and Eleanor, a lady-in-waiting to Queen Philippa, accompanied the queen to Ghent, where his son Henry was born in 1340.

After his father's death in 1340 he returned to England and took his seat in parliament. He died on 14 April 1342 of wounds from a tournament, leaving the infant Henry as baron.

约翰·德博蒙特（1318—1342），第二代博蒙特男爵，是亨利·德·博蒙与巴肯女继承人爱丽丝·科明之子。他的家族是法国布里耶纳家族的英格兰支系。父亲曾凭妻子的权利主张苏格兰的巴肯伯爵头衔，约翰却从未使用这一头衔。

婚姻把他与兰开斯特家族联在一起：1330年11月6日，他娶格罗斯蒙特的亨利之妹兰开斯特的埃莉诺为妻。1338年，约翰与担任菲利帕王后侍女的埃莉诺随王后前往低地国家的根特，儿子亨利于1340年在那里出生。

1340年父亲去世后，他返回英格兰，进入议会就任男爵。1342年4月14日，他因比武大会受伤而死，留下年幼的亨利继承爵位。

en:
John Comyn I (c. 1215–c. 1275) succeeded his uncle Walter as Lord of Badenoch in 1258 and served as Justiciar of Galloway. During Alexander III's minority the Comyns dominated Scotland from 1249 until ousted by rivals, returning in 1257–58.

He fought for Henry III of England at the Battle of Lewes in 1264 and was captured. In 1275 he helped lead the expedition that crushed the Manx revolt. His son was the Black Comyn.

en:
John Comyn II, the Black Comyn (c. 1250–1302), was Lord of Badenoch and head of Scotland's most powerful baronial house. After Alexander III's death he became one of the six guardians for the infant queen Margaret, and later put forward a claim to the crown in the Great Cause.

He married Eleanor de Balliol, sister of King John Balliol, allying the two houses. He died in 1302 and was succeeded by his son John, the Red Comyn.

en:
John Comyn III, the Red Comyn (c. 1274–1306), was the leading noble of the Balliol party. Son of the Black Comyn and nephew of King John Balliol, he served as Guardian after Balliol's 1296 abdication, commanding resistance to the English.

On 10 February 1306 he met Robert the Bruce at a church in Dumfries, where Bruce stabbed him to death before the high altar. The murder cleared Bruce's path to the crown and began a Comyn blood feud.

en:
John Comyn IV (c. 1294–1314) was the only son of the Red Comyn, who was killed at Dumfries in 1306. Sent to England by his mother, he saw his Badenoch lordship forfeited, probably at Robert Bruce's St Andrews parliament of 1309. He married Margaret Wake, by whom he had a son Aymer, who died in infancy in 1316.

Comyn returned to Scotland in the English army and was killed leading a cavalry charge against the Scottish schiltrons on the main day of the Battle of Bannockburn, 24 June 1314.

en:
Katherine de Beaumont (died 1368) was the daughter of Henry de Beaumont, Earl of Buchan, and his wife Alice Comyn. She married David III Strathbogie, titular Earl of Atholl and a leading supporter of Edward Balliol.

David was killed at the Battle of Culblean in 1335, after which the Scottish Guardian Andrew Moray besieged her in Lochindorb Castle; Edward III relieved her there in 1336. Her son David later claimed the earldom of Atholl, and she died in 1368.

凯瑟琳·德·博蒙（？—1368）是巴肯伯爵亨利·德·博蒙与妻子爱丽丝·科明之女。她嫁给名义上的阿索尔伯爵、爱德华·巴里奥的主要支持者大卫三世·斯特拉斯博吉。

1335年，大卫在卡尔布兰战役中阵亡，苏格兰护国官安德鲁·默里随即把她围困在洛欣多布城堡；1336年爱德华三世发兵将她救出。她的儿子大卫后来继续宣称阿索尔伯爵之位，她于1368年去世。

en:
Kenneth de Moravia (died 19 July 1333) was the fourth Earl of Sutherland and chief of Clan Sutherland in the Scottish Highlands. The second son of William de Moravia, second Earl of Sutherland, he inherited the earldom after the death of his brother William, the third earl.

He married Mary, daughter of Domhnall I, Earl of Mar, and their son William succeeded as the fifth earl. Kenneth was killed fighting the English at the Battle of Halidon Hill on 19 July 1333.

肯尼思·德·莫拉维亚（?—1333）是第四代萨瑟兰伯爵、苏格兰高地上萨瑟兰氏族的首领。他是第二代萨瑟兰伯爵威廉·德·莫拉维亚的次子，在兄长第三代伯爵威廉死后继承伯爵之位。

en:
Kenneth I, called Kenneth MacAlpin (c. 810–858), was king of the Picts. Tradition holds that he succeeded his father Alpín as king of Dál Riada around 841 and conquered the Picts between 843 and 850, after which he was hailed as founder of Scotland, or Alba, and surnamed the Conqueror.

He warred against the Britons of Strathclyde and Viking raiders, and moved the Stone of Scone and other relics from Iona into his kingdom. He died on 13 February 858 and was succeeded by his brother Donald.

肯尼思一世（约810—858），即肯尼思·麦克·亚尔宾，是皮克特人之王。传统记载称他约841年继承父亲阿尔平的达尔里阿达王位，又于843—850年征服皮克特人，后世因此奉他为苏格兰（盖尔语称阿尔巴）的开国君主，绰号“征服者”。

他一生与斯特拉斯克莱德的不列颠人及维京入侵者作战，并把斯昆石等圣物从爱奥那岛迁回自己的王国。他于858年2月13日去世，弟弟唐纳德继立。

en:
Cináed mac Maíl Coluim, anglicised Kenneth II (932–995), son of Malcolm I, became king of Alba in 971. He defeated northern rivals and raided northern England, and tradition says King Edgar recognised his rule over Lothian after his submission in 973.

In 995 he was ‘deceitfully killed’ at Fettercairn, and legend blamed Finnguala, who lured him into a booby-trapped cottage to avenge her son. Buried on Iona, he was succeeded by Constantine III; his son Malcolm II later became king.

肯尼思二世（盖尔语名基纳达·麦克·马尔·科卢姆，932—995）是马尔科姆一世之子，971年成为阿尔巴国王。他平定北方的争位者，又不断侵袭英格兰北部；传说他于973年向英王埃德加臣服，后者承认他对洛锡安的统治。

995年，他在费特凯恩被“背信弃义地杀害”，传说指使者是芬瓜拉，她为给儿子报仇，把他诱入设有弩机陷阱的小屋。他葬于艾奥纳岛，康斯坦丁三世继位；其子马尔科姆二世后来也成为国王。

en:
Cináed mac Duib, anglicised as Kenneth III and nicknamed An Donn, the Chief, ruled the Gaelic kingdom of Alba as king from 997 until 1005. A son of King Dub, he came to the throne after the death of Constantine III.

His reign is poorly recorded. Around 25 March 1005 he was defeated and killed at the battle of Monzievaird in Strathearn by his rival Máel Coluim, who ruled as Malcolm II.

Lulach mac Gille Coemgáin (c. 1032–1058), son of Gille Coemgáin, Mormaer of Moray, and Gruoch, was the stepson of Macbeth. After Macbeth fell at Lumphanan in 1057, his supporters placed him on the throne; he was inaugurated at Scone, the first Scottish king whose coronation details are recorded.

He ruled barely seven months, earning the nicknames the Unfortunate and the Simple, before Malcolm III killed him in 1058 and seized the crown. He was buried on Iona, and his son Máel Snechtai became Mormaer of Moray.

en:
Mac Bethad mac Findláich, known as Macbeth (c. 1005–1057), son of Findláech of Moray, became Mormaer of Moray in 1032 and married Gruoch. After Duncan I invaded Moray in 1040 and fell to his men, Macbeth took the throne of Alba.

His seventeen-year reign was largely peaceful: in 1050 he made a pilgrimage to Rome, scattering alms to the poor. In 1054 Siward of Northumbria invaded and fought a bloody battle at Dunsinane, and in 1057 Macbeth was killed at Lumphanan by men loyal to Malcolm III and buried on Iona.

麦克贝斯·麦克芬莱克，通称麦克白（约1005—1057），是莫里统治者芬莱克之子，1032年成为莫里总督，并娶格鲁赫为妻。1040年邓肯一世入侵莫里、死于其部众之手后，麦克白登上阿尔巴王位。

en:
Máel Coluim mac Domnaill, anglicised Malcolm I (c. 897–954), son of Donald II, became king of Alba in 943 when his cousin Constantine II abdicated into a monastery. In 945 Edmund I of England, after ravaging Cumbria, commended Strathclyde to Malcolm in return for an alliance.

Malcolm later raided Northumbria as far south as the River Tees and campaigned in Moray. He was killed in 954 and buried on Iona. His sons Dub and Kenneth II later reigned.

马尔科姆一世（盖尔语名梅尔·科卢姆·麦克·多姆纳尔，约897—954）是唐纳德二世之子，943年堂兄康斯坦丁二世退位为僧后成为阿尔巴国王。945年，英格兰国王埃德蒙一世劫掠坎布里亚后，将斯特拉斯克莱德“托付”给马尔科姆，以换取结盟。

Máel Coluim mac Cináeda, anglicised Malcolm II (c. 954–1034), son of Kenneth II, won the kingship of Alba in 1005 by killing Kenneth III at Monzievaird. In 1018, with his ally Owain Foel of Strathclyde, he crushed the Northumbrians at Carham and secured Lothian for the Scots.

He married his daughters into neighbouring dynasties: Bethóc wed Crínán of Dunkeld and bore the future Duncan I. Malcolm died at Glamis in 1034, and his grandson Duncan succeeded him.

马尔科姆二世（盖尔语名梅尔·科卢姆·麦克·基纳达，954—1034）是肯尼思二世之子，1005年杀死肯尼思三世，夺得阿尔巴王位。1018年，他联合盟友斯特拉斯克莱德国王欧文·福尔，在卡拉姆大败诺森布里亚人，为苏格兰人确立了对洛锡安的统治。

en:
Malcolm III, called Canmore or Great Chief (1031–1093), was the eldest son of Duncan I and ruled Scotland for thirty-five years. Exiled as a child after Macbeth killed his father in 1040, he slew Macbeth at Lumphanan in 1057 and killed his successor Lulach the next year to seize the crown.

In 1070 he married Margaret of Wessex, later Saint Margaret, mother of several future kings. After repeated raids into northern England, he was killed at the First Battle of Alnwick in 1093.

马尔科姆三世，绰号“大头”，意为伟大的首领（1031—1093），是邓肯一世的长子，统治苏格兰三十五年。1040年麦克白杀死其父后，他幼年流亡；1057年在隆发南击杀麦克白，次年又杀死其继承者卢拉赫，夺得王位。

en:
Malcolm IV (1141–1165), the Maiden, succeeded his grandfather David I and was inaugurated at Scone in May 1153 aged twelve. In 1157 he did homage to Henry II of England and surrendered Cumbria and Northumbria in return for the earldom of Huntingdon.

He faced revolts by his earls, campaigned in Galloway and Moray, and in 1164 saw Somerled of Argyll killed at Renfrew. He died unmarried at Jedburgh in 1165 aged twenty-four.

Margaret Bruce (born between 1315 and 1322, died c. 1346) was probably the eldest daughter of King Robert I of Scots by his second wife Elizabeth de Burgh. In 1324, during peace talks, Scottish envoys proposed her marriage to the English heir Edward, but the negotiations came to nothing.

In 1345 she married William de Moravia, 5th Earl of Sutherland. She died giving birth to her only child, John, Master of Sutherland.

en:
Marjorie Bruce (c. 1296–1316 or 1317) was the eldest daughter of King Robert I of Scots, born of his first wife Isabella of Mar. Captured with the queen and other Bruce women after her father's coronation in 1306, she spent years in captivity before her release after Bannockburn. In 1315 she married Walter Stewart, High Steward of Scotland.

Tradition says her son Robert was born after she fell from her horse near Paisley, though the fall may have occurred after his birth. He succeeded to the throne as Robert II in 1371, making Marjorie the ancestress of the House of Stewart.

en:
Mary Bruce (c. 1282–1323) was a younger sister of King Robert I of Scots. After her brother claimed the crown in 1306, she was handed to the English by the Earl of Ross. Edward I ordered her displayed in a cage at Roxburgh Castle, where she was held for about four years.

Moved to better confinement in 1310, she was freed in 1314 in exchange for English nobles captured at Bannockburn. She married Sir Neil Campbell.

en:
Sir Niall mac Cailein, also called Neil or Nigel Campbell (d. 1316), was a son of Cailean Mór and a lifelong warrior in the service of Robert the Bruce. One of Bruce's earliest adherents in 1306, he stood by him after the defeats at Methven and Dalrigh and fought the English and the MacDougalls.

He negotiated with the English crown in 1309 and 1314, and married the king's sister Mary Bruce. His service to the king elevated the Campbells in the Scottish nobility.

en:
Patrick Dunbar, Earl of March (c. 1285–1369), was a leading Scottish magnate under Robert the Bruce and David II, succeeding his father in 1309. He changed sides several times before finally supporting the Scottish cause; in 1338 his wife Agnes Randolph, the famed Black Agnes, defended Dunbar Castle against an English siege.

When his brother-in-law John Randolph fell at Neville's Cross in 1346, Dunbar took the Earl of Moray title. He backed a revolt against David II in 1363 and died in 1369.

en:
Sir Richard de Brus (died 1287), Lord of Writtle, was a younger son of Robert de Brus, fifth Lord of Annandale, and Isabella de Clare. An English household knight of Edward I, he may have accompanied the king on crusade and fought in Edward's conquest of Wales.

In 1286 he signed the Turnberry Band, the bond of Scottish and Anglo-Irish nobles sealed at Turnberry Castle. He died unmarried in 1287, and his estates reverted to his father.

en:
Richard Talbot, 2nd Baron Talbot (c. 1306–1356) was an English nobleman and soldier who in 1326 married Elizabeth de Comyn, heiress to the forfeited Comyn estates in England and Scotland. As one of the Disinherited he fought for Edward Balliol at Dupplin Moor in 1332 and was made Lord of Mar, but was captured in 1334 and ransomed in 1335.

Edward III made him captain of Berwick in 1337, and he fought at Crécy. He inherited his barony in 1346 and died in 1356, succeeded by his son Gilbert.

第二代塔尔博特男爵理查德·塔尔博特（约1306—1356）是英格兰贵族、军人，1326年娶被没收的科明家族在英格兰与苏格兰地产的女继承人伊丽莎白·德·科明。作为“被剥夺继承权者”之一，他于1332年在杜普林沼地之战中为爱德华·巴里奥效力，受封马尔勋爵；1334年被俘，1335年缴纳赎金获释。

en:
Robert de Brus (c. 1078–1141), first Lord of Annandale, was a Norman knight from Brix who came to England with King Henry I and founded Gisborough Priory in 1119.

His friendship with David I brought him the lordship of Annandale in 1124, but when David invaded England in support of Empress Matilda, Robert renounced his homage and fought for Stephen at the Battle of the Standard in 1138. He died in 1141, founder of the Bruce dynasty in Scotland.

en:
Robert de Brus, called le Meschin, second Lord of Annandale (died c. 1194), was a younger son of the first lord. When his father renounced David I before the Battle of the Standard in 1138, Robert fought for the Scots; tradition says his own father captured him and gave him to King Stephen.

He retained the family's Scottish lands while the Yorkshire estates went to his elder brother Adam, and made Lochmaben the centre of the lordship. He was succeeded by his son William.

Robert de Brus, called the Noble, was the fourth Lord of Annandale (c. 1195–1245), son of William de Brus. About 1219 he married Isobel of Huntingdon, daughter of the Earl of Huntingdon and a descendant of King David I.

The match brought him Essex manors including Writtle, and later supplied his great-grandson Robert the Bruce with his claim to the Scottish crown. He died in 1245 and was buried at Gisborough Priory, succeeded by his son Robert.

en:
Robert de Brus, fifth Lord of Annandale, called the Competitor (c. 1215–1295), was a Scottish magnate and regent during Alexander III's minority. A great-great-grandson of David I, he claimed the crown after the Maid of Norway died in 1290, but Edward I awarded the throne to his rival John Balliol in 1292.

Robert then resigned Annandale and his claim to his eldest son. He died at Lochmaben in 1295 and was buried at Gisborough Priory, his grandson becoming King Robert I.

Robert de Brus (1243–1304), sixth Lord of Annandale, became Earl of Carrick by his marriage in 1271 to Marjorie, the Carrick heiress, whom legend says kept him captive at Turnberry until he consented. A cross-border baron, he later wavered between Edward I and the Scots in the Wars of Independence.

His father passed his throne claim to him after the judgment of 1292, and when he died in 1304 it passed to his eldest son, the future Robert the Bruce.

en:
Robert II (1316–1390), born Robert Stewart, was the son of Walter Stewart, High Steward of Scotland, and Marjorie Bruce, daughter of Robert the Bruce. As High Steward he guarded Scotland during David II's exile in France and again after David's capture at Neville's Cross in 1346.

When David died childless in 1371, Robert became the first Stewart king, crowned at Scone. From 1384 power passed to his sons, first John, later Robert III. He died at Dundonald Castle in 1390.

Robert I, known as Robert the Bruce (1274–1329), was King of Scots from 1306 and leader of Scotland's war of independence against England. After killing his rival John Comyn in 1306 he was crowned at Scone, but defeat at Methven drove him into hiding until victory in 1307 began his comeback.

His triumph at Bannockburn in 1314 re-established Scottish independence, and in 1328 England renounced its claim to sovereignty in the Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton. He died in 1329 and was buried at Dunfermline Abbey, succeeded by his son David II.

en:
Thomas Randolph (c. 1285–1332), nephew of Robert the Bruce, was made Earl of Moray in 1312 and became a chief lieutenant of the king. In 1314 he retook Edinburgh Castle by a secret path and commanded a schiltron at Bannockburn that June.

He helped take Berwick in 1318 and won the Battle of Myton in 1319. He served as regent for the child David II from 1329 and died at Musselburgh in July 1332 while marching against Edward Balliol.

托马斯·伦道夫（约1285—1332）是罗伯特·布鲁斯的外甥，1312年受封莫里伯爵，成为国王最倚重的将领之一。1314年，他率部沿一条秘密小径攀崖，从英格兰人手中夺回爱丁堡城堡；同年6月在班诺克本之战中指挥一个长枪方阵。

en:
Walter fitz Alan (c. 1106/1110–1177), younger son of the Anglo-Norman baron Alan fitz Flaad, entered David I of Scotland’s service around 1136 and became royal steward around 1150, serving David, Malcolm IV and William the Lion. He received western lordships and in 1163 founded Paisley Priory.

He may have commanded when Somerled was slain near Renfrew in 1164. He died at Melrose in 1177 and was buried at Paisley; his son Alan inherited his office, from which the royal House of Stewart took its name.

沃尔特·菲茨艾伦（约1106/1110—1177）是盎格鲁—诺曼贵族艾伦·菲茨弗拉德较年幼的儿子之一，约1136年投效苏格兰国王大卫一世，约1150年成为王室总管，先后侍奉大卫一世、马尔科姆四世和狮子王威廉。他受封西部领地，1163年创立佩斯利修道院。

Walter Stewart of Dundonald (c. 1180–1246) was the third hereditary High Steward of Scotland and Justiciar of Scotia. The eldest son of Alan fitz Walter, he was the first of his line to use Stewart as a family name.

As seneschal and justiciar he witnessed charters of Alexander II, and around 1213 gave timber for Paisley Priory. By his wife Beatrix, daughter of the Earl of Angus, he fathered Alexander Stewart, the fourth High Steward, and died in 1246.

邓唐纳德的沃尔特·斯图亚特（约1180—1246）是第三代世袭苏格兰王室总务官，兼任苏格兰司法长。他是艾伦·菲茨沃尔特的长子，也是家族中第一个以斯图亚特为姓氏的人。

en:
Walter Stewart (c. 1296–1327), sixth hereditary High Steward of Scotland, fought at Bannockburn in 1314. In 1315 he married Marjorie Bruce, daughter of Robert I, who died giving birth in 1316 to their son Robert, the future Robert II and first Stewart king.

As Warden of the Western Marches he helped govern and defend the borders during Bruce's Irish campaign, and held Berwick against Edward II's siege in 1319. He died at Bathgate Castle on 9 April 1327.

William Comyn (1163–1233) was a Scottish noble who became Lord of Badenoch and, by marrying Marjory, Countess of Buchan, the first Comyn earl of Buchan. The son of Richard Comyn, he served William the Lion and rose to Justiciar of Scotia in 1205.

He campaigned against the rebel Meic Uilleim, beheading Gofraid mac Domnaill in 1213 and crushing their power by 1229, when he was granted Badenoch. His rise opened a century of Comyn dominance in Scotland, and he died in 1233.

William de Brus, third Lord of Annandale (died 1212), succeeded his father Robert in 1194 after his elder brother predeceased him. He held large estates across northern England, where King John granted him a weekly market at Hartlepool.

He witnessed a charter of William the Lion of Scotland. By his wife Christina mac Uhtred he left three sons and was succeeded by the eldest, Robert, whose marriage to Isobel of Huntingdon later gave the Bruces their claim to the Scottish throne.

en:
William de Moravia, 5th Earl of Sutherland and chief of Clan Sutherland, succeeded his father Kenneth in 1333 and was a loyal supporter of David II in the wars against England. In 1345 he married Margaret Bruce, daughter of Robert the Bruce; their son John of Sutherland was once regarded as an heir to the crown but died of plague in London.

After Margaret's death he married Joanna Menteith in 1346, by whom he had Robert, later 6th Earl. William last appears on record in 1370 and was certainly dead before 1389.

William Douglas le Hardi (1243–1298), Lord of Douglas, was a Scottish border baron and the father of the Black Douglas. By his first wife Elizabeth Stewart, daughter of the High Steward of Scotland, he had his heir James; in 1288 he abducted the wealthy widow Eleanor de Lovaine and made her his second wife.

He joined William Wallace's rising after the English conquest, was captured in 1297 and imprisoned in the Tower of London. There he died from ill treatment in January 1298.

en:
William Douglas, 1st Earl of Douglas (c. 1323–1384), son of Sir Archibald Douglas, killed at Halidon Hill, and nephew of Bruce's lieutenant Sir James the Good, was raised in France as ward of the Knight of Liddesdale. He returned in 1348, drove the English from Douglasdale, then killed Liddesdale in a 1353 feud and in 1354 gained a charter of all the Douglas lands.

He married Margaret of Mar in 1357 and was created first Earl of Douglas in 1358; his son James became 2nd Earl. He died in 1384.

William, Lord of Douglas, was a son of the Black Douglas, James, and inherited the Douglas lands as a child after his father was killed in Spain in 1330. His uncle, Sir Archibald Douglas, guarded his inheritance.

William the Lion (c. 1142–1214), younger brother of Malcolm IV, inherited Northumbria but lost it to Henry II in 1157 and became king in 1165. He made Scotland’s first treaty with France in 1168, and while backing a revolt against Henry II was captured at Alnwick in 1174.

The Treaty of Falaise made him Henry’s vassal until Richard I released those terms in 1189. In 1186 he married Ermengarde de Beaumont, mother of Alexander II; he founded Arbroath Abbey and died in 1214.

狮子王威廉（约1142—1214）是马尔科姆四世之弟，原领有诺森布里亚，1157年被亨利二世夺走，1165年即位为苏格兰国王。1168年他缔结苏格兰与法国之间的第一个同盟，后因支持反对亨利二世的叛乱，于1174年在阿尼克被俘。

en:
Hans Jakob Christoffel von Grimmelshausen (1621/22–1676) was a German novelist of the Thirty Years' War. Born at Gelnhausen, he was about ten when Hessian soldiers seized him; he grew up amid its armies, enlisted in the Imperial forces in 1639 and later worked as a regimental clerk.

At the war's close he entered the service of the bishop of Strasbourg. In 1665 he became magistrate at Renchen, where he turned to writing. His picaresque novel Simplicius Simplicissimus, published in 1669, drew on his wartime experiences and became the age's most famous German novel. He died at Renchen in 1676.

en:
Hans Tausen (1494–1561), called the Danish Luther, was the leading theologian of the Danish Reformation. A Hospitaller monk who studied with Luther at Wittenberg from 1523, he preached the new doctrine at Viborg under the townspeople's protection, and in 1526 King Frederick I made him a chaplain. He was the first Danish priest to marry and the first reformer to conduct services in Danish instead of Latin.

He went to preach in Copenhagen in 1529. In 1535 he printed the first Danish Pentateuch, and in 1542 became Bishop of Ribe, holding the see until his death in 1561.

en:
John Knox (c. 1514–1572) was the leading Reformer of Scotland. Born at Haddington and ordained a priest, he embraced Protestant teaching through George Wishart. After Cardinal Beaton's murder in 1546, French forces captured Knox and sent him to the galleys; released in 1549, he served Edward VI in England before fleeing under Mary I to Geneva, where he studied with John Calvin.

Returning to Scotland in 1559, he led the Reformation that overthrew the regent Mary of Guise, helped frame the Kirk's 1560 confession and Presbyterian order, and challenged Mary, Queen of Scots. He died at Edinburgh in 1572.

Przemysł of Inowrocław (c. 1278–1338/39), a Piast and the second son of Ziemomysł of Kuyavia, inherited his father's duchy in 1287. He submitted to Wenceslaus II of Bohemia in 1300, but from 1306 served his uncle Władysław I Łokietek as governor of Gdańsk Pomerania until the Teutonic Order seized it in 1309.

He recovered Inowrocław after his brother Leszek abdicated, and in 1327 or 1328 exchanged it for Sieradz. He died unmarried in late 1338 or early 1339.

Alexander Komnenos Asen was a Bulgarian noble in the Serbian Empire, the son of Despot John Komnenos Asen and nephew of Tsar Ivan Alexander. On his father's death, probably in 1363, he succeeded as sebastos and lord of Kanina and Valona on the Adriatic coast.

He soon lost both cities to the Albanian lord Andrea II Muzaka. He is thought to have fallen at the Battle of the Maritsa on 26 September 1371, and by 1372 his lands belonged to Balša II.

en:
Ana-Neda (fl. 1323–1357) was a Serbian princess, daughter of King Stefan Uroš II Milutin. Her husband Michael Shishman became emperor of Bulgaria in 1323 but divorced her in 1324 to marry a Byzantine princess, imprisoning her and their sons.

After Michael died at Velbazhd in 1330, her brother Stefan Uroš III placed her son Ivan Stephen on the Bulgarian throne, and she may have ruled as regent. Deposed in 1331, she took refuge in Dubrovnik; she was venerated as Saint Jelena.

安娜-内达（活跃于1323—1357年）是塞尔维亚内马尼奇王朝的公主，国王斯特凡·乌罗什二世·米卢廷之女。她的丈夫米哈伊尔·希什曼于1323年成为保加利亚皇帝，却在1324年为迎娶拜占庭公主而与她离婚，并囚禁了她和几个儿子。

en:
Andronikos Angelos Palaiologos (c. 1282–1328) was a Byzantine aristocrat, grandson of Michael II of Epirus through his father Demetrios Koutroules and of Emperor Michael VIII through his mother Anna. By 1326 he was protovestiarios and protosebastos, and in 1327–28 he governed Velegrada.

In the civil war between Andronikos II and Andronikos III he first backed the grandson, then changed sides. When Andronikos III won in 1328, his family was seized and his Macedonian estates confiscated; he fled to Serbia and died in exile at Prilep the same year. His daughter Anna became queen consort of Epirus.

安德洛尼卡·安格洛斯·巴列奥略（约1282—1328）是拜占庭贵族：通过父亲德米特里·库特鲁莱斯为伊庇鲁斯统治者米海尔二世之孙，通过母亲安娜为皇帝米海尔八世的外孙。到1326年，他已身兼御衣总管和首席至尊者之职，1327—1328年出守韦莱格拉达（今培拉特）。

在安德罗尼科斯二世与安德罗尼科斯三世的内战中，他先支持皇孙，后又倒戈。1328年安德罗尼科斯三世获胜后，他的家人被捕、马其顿地产被没收，他逃往塞尔维亚，同年死于流亡地普里莱普。其女安娜后来成为伊庇鲁斯王后。

en:
Anna Dandolo (died c. 1258) was a Venetian noblewoman of the powerful Dandolo family, daughter of Vice-Doge Rainero Dandolo and granddaughter of Doge Enrico Dandolo. Her father was killed fighting the Genoese in Crete in 1209.

Around 1217 she married Stefan, Grand Prince of Serbia, at Venice, and was crowned beside him the same year when he became the first crowned king of Serbia; the marriage drew Venetian artisans and Latin influence into the kingdom. Their son Stefan Uroš I succeeded to the throne in 1243. Long outliving her husband, Anna died around 1258 and was buried at Sopoćani Monastery.

安娜·丹多洛（约1258年卒）出身威尼斯权贵丹多洛家族，是威尼斯副总督拉伊纳罗·丹多洛之女、总督恩里科·丹多洛的孙女。她的父亲于1209年在克里特与热那亚人的战斗中阵亡。

Đorđe Nemanjić was the eldest son of Vukan Nemanjić and ruled Zeta as the heir of his branch of the Nemanjići. After his father's death he styled himself king of Duklja, and about 1208 accepted Venice's suzerainty to shield his ports and independence from his uncle Stefan the First-Crowned.

By 1216 Stefan had conquered Zeta and ended its independence, though Đorđe kept a regional lordship as prince of Duklja. He appears in sources for the last time in 1242.

en:
Dmitar Nemanjić, also called Dimitrije, was a son of Grand Prince Vukan Nemanjić and nephew of Stefan the First-Crowned. As župan of Polimlje, using masons from Dubrovnik he built the Davidovica Monastery near Brodarevo, completed by August 1281.

Late in life he took monastic vows as the monk David, and in 1286 went on pilgrimage to Jerusalem. His son Vratislav was grandfather of Princess Milica of Serbia, and the Orthodox Church venerates him as Saint David.

en:
George (Đurađ I) Balšić (died 1378) was lord of Zeta from 1362, eldest son of Balša I, whose family dominated the coastal Serbian lands after Stefan Dušan's death. He warred on Karl Thopia of Albania, who held him captive from 1364 to his Ragusan-mediated release in 1366; he besieged Kotor and converted to Catholicism in 1369. Venice also complained about his ships in the Adriatic.

After the Battle of Maritsa in 1371 he made Zeta independent, taking Prizren and Peć from King Marko. He died at Skadar in January 1378, leaving Zeta to Balša II.

en:
Helena of Bulgaria (c. 1315 – 7 November 1374), born Elena Sratsimir, was a Bulgarian princess and empress consort of Stefan Dušan of Serbia. Daughter of despot Sratsimir of Kran and sister of Tsar Ivan Alexander, she married Dušan in 1332 to seal the Bulgarian-Serbian peace, bearing him Stefan Uroš V.

After Dušan's death in 1355 she was regent for her son and ruled a principality around Serres. She took the veil as Elizabeth in 1359, governed Serres until 1365, and was canonized as Saint Elizabeth.

海伦娜（约1315—1374年11月7日），本名埃莱娜·斯拉齐米尔，是保加利亚公主，塞尔维亚皇帝斯特凡·杜尚的皇后。她是克兰专制公斯拉齐米尔之女、沙皇伊凡·亚历山大的姐妹，1332年依据保加利亚—塞尔维亚和约嫁给杜尚，生下斯特凡·乌罗什五世。

1355年杜尚死后，她代子摄政，统治以塞雷为中心的领地。1359年她出家为修女，法名伊丽莎白，统治塞雷至1365年，身后被东正教会尊为圣伊丽莎白。

en:
Helena Doukaina Angelina was a Greek noblewoman of Thessaly, daughter of its sebastokrator John I Doukas. Around 1273 to 1276 she married Stefan Uroš II Milutin of Serbia, who became king in 1282.

Milutin abandoned her around 1283. She may have been the mother of Stefan Konstantin, later a claimant to the Serbian throne, and seems to have returned to Greece.

海伦娜·杜卡伊娜·安格利娜是色萨利的希腊贵族女子，父亲是色萨利至尊者约翰一世·杜卡斯。约1273至1276年间，她嫁给塞尔维亚的斯特凡·乌罗什二世·米卢廷，米卢廷于1282年成为国王。

米卢廷在约1283年将她遗弃。她可能是后来争夺塞尔维亚王位的斯特凡·康斯坦丁之母，此后似乎返回了希腊。

en:
Hrelja, also called Stefan Dragovol or Hrelja Ohmućević (died 27 December 1342), was a Serbian lord whose domain around Štip, and later Strumica, lay where Serbia, Bulgaria and Byzantium met. He served three Serbian kings, and in the 1320s led a Serbian detachment to help Andronikos II in a Byzantine civil war.

In 1334–1335 he rebuilt Rila Monastery's church and raised Hrelja's Tower, inscribed with Dušan's name. By the late 1330s he had broken away and ruled from Strumica, nominally under Byzantium. In the next civil war he backed John VI Kantakouzenos, who gave him Melnik and the title protosebastos.

In summer 1342 Kantakouzenos gave him up to win Serbian help: Hrelja acknowledged Dušan again and ceded Melnik. He became the monk Hariton and died at Rila that December, said by Bulgarian sources to have been killed on Dušan's orders.

zh:
赫雷利亚，又名斯特凡·德拉戈沃尔、赫雷利亚·奥赫穆切维奇（？—1342年12月27日），是塞尔维亚领主，领地以什蒂普为中心，后来又纳入斯特鲁米察，正处在塞尔维亚、保加利亚与拜占庭的交界处。他曾效力于三位塞尔维亚国王，1320年代曾率塞尔维亚分队在拜占庭内战中援助安德洛尼卡二世。

1334—1335年，他重建里拉修道院的教堂，并修起刻有杜尚名字的赫雷利亚塔。1330年代末他脱离塞尔维亚，以斯特鲁米察为都，名义上臣属拜占庭。下一次拜占庭内战中他支持约翰六世·坎塔库泽努斯，获封梅尔尼克和首席至尊者头衔。

1342年夏，坎塔库泽努斯为换取塞尔维亚支持而舍弃了他：赫雷利亚重新承认杜尚的宗主权，交出梅尔尼克。他在里拉修道院出家，法名哈里顿，同年12月去世，据保加利亚方面的记载，他是奉杜尚之命被害。

en:
John Palaiologos (1288/89–1326) was a Byzantine aristocrat of the Palaiologos dynasty, the son of the general Constantine Palaiologos and grandson of Emperor Michael VIII. By 1325 he was governor of Thessalonica.

In 1326 he rebelled against his uncle, Emperor Andronikos II, and joined the Serbian king Stefan Dečanski in raiding Byzantine Macedonia as far as Serres. Offered the title of Caesar, he submitted, but fell ill and died at Skopje the same year. His daughter Maria became Dečanski's queen.

约翰·巴列奥略（1288/89—1326）是拜占庭巴列奥略王朝贵族，将军君士坦丁·巴列奥略之子、皇帝米哈伊尔八世之孙，1325年前后任塞萨洛尼基总督。

1326年他反叛伯父安德洛尼卡二世皇帝，投奔塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·德钱斯基，随其洗劫拜占庭属马其顿，兵锋远至塞雷。皇帝以凯撒头衔相诱，他于是归顺，却在同年病卒于斯科普里，其女玛丽亚后来成为德钱斯基的王后。

en:
Ivan Dragushin (fl. 1299–1340) was a Bulgarian nobleman, the son of Despot Aldimir of Kran from the Cuman Terter dynasty and Marina Smilets, daughter of Tsar Smilets. After Aldimir was possibly killed around 1305, he and his mother took refuge in Constantinople and then in Serbia, where his aunt Teodora was queen to Stefan Dečanski.

His cousin Stefan Dušan enfeoffed him with lands around the Crna River in Macedonia. With his mother he founded the Pološko Monastery, where he was buried before 1340.

伊万·德拉古申（活跃于1299—1340年）是保加利亚贵族，克兰专制公阿尔迪米尔与沙皇斯米莱茨之女玛丽娜·斯米莱茨之子，父系出自库曼人的捷尔捷尔家族。约1305年阿尔迪米尔可能遇害后，他随母亲先逃往君士坦丁堡，再转赴塞尔维亚，投奔姨母、斯特凡·德钱斯基的王后狄奥多拉。

表兄斯特凡·杜尚将马其顿境内茨尔纳河一带封给他。他与母亲共同修建了波洛什科修道院，1340年之前葬于该院。

en:
Jefimija (1349–1405), secular name Jelena, was the daughter of Caesar Vojihna of Drama and the wife of Despot Jovan Uglješa Mrnjavčević. She is honoured as the first female poet of medieval Serbia: her Lament for a Dead Son was engraved on the back of a diptych after her infant son died, and her Encomium of Prince Lazar is another landmark of old Serbian literature.

She was also a skilled needlewoman and engraver. She lived her later years as a nun and died in 1405.

耶菲米娅（1349—1405），俗名耶莱娜，是德拉马凯撒沃伊赫纳之女、专制公约万·乌格列沙·姆尔尼亚夫切维奇之妻，被尊为中世纪塞尔维亚第一位女诗人。幼子夭折后，她把《悼亡子》刻在一座双联圣像的背面；另一篇《拉扎尔颂》也是古塞尔维亚文学的名篇。

她还是技艺精湛的刺绣与雕刻匠人。她晚年出家为尼，1405年去世。

en:
Jelena Nemanjić Šubić was a daughter of King Stefan Uroš III Dečanski by Maria Palaiologina and a half-sister of Stefan Dušan. She married the Croatian magnate Mladen III Šubić and ruled with him from Klis. Widowed in 1348, she held Klis and Skradin for her son Mladen IV, pressed by Venice and Louis I of Hungary.

In 1355 she refused Venice's offer to buy the towns and called on Dušan for aid. After his death that December, Skradin passed to Venice and Klis to Hungary; Palman led her away, leaving Mladen IV a hostage.

耶莱娜·内马尼奇·舒比奇是塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·乌罗什三世·德钱斯基与玛丽亚·巴列奥略之女、斯特凡·杜尚的异母妹妹。她嫁给克罗地亚大贵族姆拉登三世·舒比奇，与丈夫同以克利斯为治所。1348年姆拉登死后，她代儿子姆拉登四世坚守克利斯和斯克拉丁，承受威尼斯与匈牙利国王拉约什一世的压力。

1355年她拒绝威尼斯购城之议，向杜尚求援。杜尚于12月死后，斯克拉丁归于威尼斯，克利斯落入匈牙利之手，帕尔曼带她离开，姆拉登四世被留作人质。

en:
Elizabeth of Serbia (Jelisaveta Nemanjić, fl. 1270–1331) was the daughter of King Stefan Dragutin of Syrmia and Catherine of Hungary. After 1283 she married Stephen I Kotromanić, ban of Bosnia, a match arranged to win her father's alliance; Stephen ruled under Dragutin's influence.

After he died in 1314 she was briefly regent for her young son Stephen II, then took refuge in Ragusa, where she died about 1331. Through her, her grandson Tvrtko I later claimed the Serbian throne.

塞尔维亚的伊丽莎白（耶丽萨维塔·内马尼奇，活跃于1270—1331年）是斯雷姆国王斯特凡·德拉古廷与匈牙利的卡塔琳娜之女。1283年后，她嫁给波斯尼亚班斯捷潘一世·科特罗马尼奇，这场婚姻意在换取其父的同盟，斯捷潘也在德拉古廷的影响下统治。

1314年丈夫死后，她一度为年幼的儿子斯捷潘二世摄政，随后避居拉古萨，约1331年在那里去世。她的孙子特夫尔特科一世后来正是凭借她的血统主张塞尔维亚王位。

en:
Lazar Hrebeljanović (c. 1329–15 June 1389) began as a stavilac, a court cupbearer, to Tsar Stefan Dušan, and married Princess Milica around 1353. After Dušan died in 1355 the Serbian Empire broke into magnates' domains, and by 1371 Lazar held Rudnik as knez, or prince.

That year the Ottomans destroyed the Mrnjavčević brothers at the Maritsa and the Nemanjić dynasty ended with Tsar Uroš. Lazar took Priština and Novo Brdo, and in 1373, with Tvrtko of Bosnia, defeated Nikola Altomanović. His Moravian Serbia became the largest Serbian state, and with the Church's backing he sought to restore the empire, though the nobility never accepted him as supreme ruler.

On 15 June 1389 he led the Christian army against Sultan Murad I on Kosovo Polje. Both rulers died in a battle tactically a draw but ruinous for the Serbs, and the Church later venerated Lazar as a martyr and saint.

拉扎尔·赫雷别利亚诺维奇（约1329—1389年6月15日）起初是沙皇斯特凡·杜尚宫廷里的侍饮官，约1353年娶米莉察公主为妻。1355年杜尚去世后，塞尔维亚帝国分裂为各地大贵族的领地；到1371年，拉扎尔已占有鲁德尼克，称王公（克涅兹）。

同年奥斯曼人在马里查河击溃姆尔尼亚夫切维奇兄弟，乌罗什皇帝去世，内马尼奇王朝绝嗣。拉扎尔夺取普里什蒂纳和新布尔多，1373年又与波斯尼亚的特夫尔特科联手击败尼古拉·阿尔托马诺维奇。他的摩拉瓦塞尔维亚成为最大的塞尔维亚国家；他在教会支持下试图重建帝国，但贵族始终不承认他为最高统治者。

1389年6月15日，他率基督教联军在科索沃平原迎战苏丹穆拉德一世。双方统帅都阵亡，此役战术上是平局，却使塞尔维亚元气大伤；教会后来尊拉扎尔为殉道者和圣徒。

en:
Maria Palaiologina (died 1355) was queen consort of Serbia as the second wife of King Stefan Uroš III Dečanski, whom she married in 1324. The daughter of John Palaiologos, Byzantine governor of Thessaloniki, and a great-niece of Emperor Andronikos II, she bore Dečanski a son, Simeon Uroš, and daughters Jelena and Teodora.

After Stefan Dušan deposed Dečanski, who was killed at Zvečan in 1331–1332, Maria sought Byzantine backing to place Simeon on the throne, in vain. She took the veil as Marta and died in 1355.

玛丽亚·巴列奥略（逝于1355年）是塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·乌罗什三世·德钱斯基的第二任王后，两人于1324年成婚。她是拜占庭塞萨洛尼基总督约翰·巴列奥略之女、皇帝安德洛尼卡二世的侄孙女，与德钱斯基育有一子西美翁·乌罗什以及耶莱娜、狄奥多拉两女。

1331—1332年斯特凡·杜尚废黜德钱斯基、后者在兹韦钱被杀后，玛丽亚寻求拜占庭支持以拥立西美翁继位，未能成功。她出家为修女，法名玛尔塔，1355年去世。

en:
Marina Smilets (before 1292 – 7 April 1355) was a Bulgarian princess, the eldest daughter of Tsar Smilets and his Byzantine wife. She married Aldimir, the Terterid despot of Kran, and bore him a son, Ivan Dragushin. After Aldimir was possibly killed around 1305, she fled with the boy to Serbia, where her sister Teodora was the first wife of King Stefan Dečanski.

As the maternal aunt of Stefan Dušan she remained close to the Serbian court, and her donor portrait survives at the Pološko Monastery near Kavadarci.

玛丽娜·斯米莱茨（1292年前—1355年4月7日）是保加利亚公主，沙皇斯米莱茨与他的拜占庭妻子的长女。她嫁给克兰的专制公、捷尔捷尔家族的阿尔迪米尔，生子伊万·德拉古申。约1305年阿尔迪米尔可能遇害后，她携幼子逃往塞尔维亚，因为她的妹妹狄奥多拉正是国王斯特凡·德钱斯基的第一任王后。

作为斯特凡·杜尚的姨母，她长期居于塞尔维亚宫廷；她的捐献者画像现存于卡瓦达尔齐附近的波洛什科修道院。

en:
Milica (c. 1335–1405), daughter of Prince Vratko of a collateral branch of the Nemanjić dynasty, married Prince Lazar Hrebeljanović. When Lazar fell at Kosovo Polje in 1389, she ruled Serbia as regent for their son Stefan Lazarević until he came of age in 1393.

The first months were the worst: Sigismund's Hungarians took northern fortresses and reached Kragujevac, Vuk Branković tried to unseat her, and when the Ottomans reached her border in the summer of 1390 she accepted their suzerainty and let them pass freely through her lands.

She founded Ljubostinja monastery about 1390 and took the veil there around 1393 as the nun Eugenia. In 1403 she went to the sultan at Serres to argue for Stefan in a dispute between her sons and Branković. She died on 11 November 1405, was buried at Ljubostinja and was canonised.

米莉察（约1335—1405）是内马尼奇王朝旁系的弗拉特科亲王之女，嫁给拉扎尔·赫雷别利亚诺维奇大公。1389年拉扎尔在科索沃平原战死，她代儿子斯特凡·拉扎列维奇摄政塞尔维亚，直到1393年他成年。

最难的是头几个月：西吉斯蒙德的匈牙利军攻占北部要塞，打到克拉古耶瓦茨；武克·布兰科维奇谋求推翻她；1390年夏天奥斯曼人兵临边境，她接受奥斯曼宗主权，允许他们自由通过领地。

约1390年她修建柳博斯蒂尼亚修道院，约1393年在那里出家，法名叶夫根尼娅。1403年她前往塞雷斯面见苏丹，在儿子们与布兰科维奇的纷争中为斯特凡辩护。她于1405年11月11日去世，葬于柳博斯蒂尼亚，后被封圣。

en:
Pribac Hrebeljanović (c. 1300–1362) was a Serbian nobleman who backed Stefan Dušan's rise and whose son Lazar would become prince of Serbia as the empire fell apart. His father Hrebljan, a merchant who rose in the army of Stefan Milutin, became governor of Stalać.

Pribac commanded a thousand men under the Dečani edict of 1330 and fought at Velbazhd and in the capture of Prilep and Ohrid. When Dušan revolted against his father Stefan of Dečani, Pribac gave him full support and was rewarded with Kosovo estates and the title of logothete.

He held Prilepac and Prizrenac and organized royal feasts, weddings and meetings. When the empire took shape and other nobles gained titles and land, none was offered to him. He died at Ferizaj in 1362; Lazar fell fighting the Ottomans at Kosovo in 1389.

皮里巴茨·赫雷别利亚诺维奇（约1300—1362）是塞尔维亚贵族，支持斯特凡·杜尚崛起，他的儿子拉扎尔后来在塞尔维亚帝国瓦解之际成为塞尔维亚王公。其父赫雷布良是在斯特凡·米卢廷军中发迹的商人，后任斯塔拉奇长官。

皮里巴茨曾按1330年的德查尼敕令统领千人，参加韦尔巴日德战役以及攻取普里莱普和奥赫里德的战事。杜尚反叛其父斯特凡·德查尼时，他全力支持，因而得到科索沃的封地与书记官头衔。

他拥有普里莱帕茨和普里兹雷纳茨，负责组织王室宴会、婚礼和会议。帝国形成时，其他贵族纷纷获得头衔和土地，他却一无所得。1362年他在费里扎伊去世；拉扎尔于1389年在科索沃与奥斯曼人作战时阵亡。

en:
Simeon Uroš, nicknamed Siniša (c. 1326–1370), was a son of King Stefan Dečanski of Serbia by the Byzantine princess Maria Palaiologina, and half-brother of Emperor Dušan. Dušan named him despot in 1346 and governor of Epirus and Acarnania in 1347; he won over the local aristocracy by marrying Thomais Orsini, daughter of the former ruler John II Orsini.

When Dušan died in 1355 and his son Stefan Uroš V took the throne, Simeon tried to make himself co-ruler and master of the empire's southern provinces. In 1356 he came into conflict with his nephew while trying to take Thessaly and Macedonia.

He then proclaimed himself emperor of the Serbs and Greeks and ruled a separate state centred on Thessaly and Epirus, splitting the south away from the empire, until his death in 1370. His son Jovan Uroš succeeded him.

西美翁·乌罗什，绰号西尼沙（约1326—1370），是塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·德钱斯基与拜占庭公主玛丽亚·巴列奥略之子，皇帝杜尚的异母弟。1346年，杜尚封他为专制公，1347年任命他为伊庇鲁斯和阿卡纳尼亚总督；他迎娶旧统治者约翰二世·奥尔西尼之女托马伊斯·奥尔西尼，争取到当地贵族。

1355年杜尚去世，其子斯特凡·乌罗什五世继位，西缅谋求成为共治者，并掌控帝国的南方诸省。1356年，他试图夺取色萨利和马其顿，与侄子发生冲突。

此后他自称塞尔维亚人与希腊人的皇帝，在色萨利和伊庇鲁斯另立一国，使帝国南部脱离出去，直至1370年去世。其子约万·乌罗什继位。

en:
Simonida (c. 1294 – after 1336), born Simonis Palaiologina, was a Byzantine princess and queen consort of King Stefan Milutin of Serbia. A daughter of Emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos, she was promised to him in 1298 to seal peace after a Byzantine defeat, and married him in spring 1299, aged five.

Her Greek entourage brought Byzantine court ceremony, titles and law to Serbia. She appears in a celebrated fresco at Gračanica monastery. After Milutin's death in 1321 she returned to Constantinople and became a nun.

西莫妮达（约1294—1336年后），原名西莫妮斯·巴列奥略，是拜占庭公主，后成为塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·米卢廷的王后。她是拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡二世之女；1298年拜占庭战败后被许配给米卢廷以巩固和约，1299年春两人成婚，时年五岁。

她带来的希腊随从将拜占庭宫廷礼仪、头衔与法律引入塞尔维亚。格拉查尼察修道院中她的壁画像极为著名。1321年米卢廷死后，她回到君士坦丁堡，成为修女。

en:
Stefan Uroš I, Uroš the Great (c. 1223–1 May 1277), was the youngest son of Stefan the First-Crowned and Anna Dandolo, granddaughter of the Venetian doge Enrico Dandolo. Chosen by the nobility, he replaced his half-brother Stefan Vladislav in 1243 after a brief succession war and ruled until 1276.

He gave Vladislav the administration of Zeta and married Helen, with whom he had sons Dragutin and Milutin. His long reign brought a mining boom that laid the groundwork for later Serbian expansion; he was also the first Serbian ruler to wear the full ceremonial vestments of Byzantine emperors. In 1276 conflict with his son Stefan Dragutin forced him to abdicate, and he died on 1 May 1277.

斯特凡·乌罗什一世，世称乌罗什大帝（约1223—1277年5月1日），是‘首任加冕者’斯特凡与威尼斯总督恩里科·丹多洛的孙女安娜·丹多洛的幼子。他受贵族拥立，在一场短暂的王位战争后于1243年取代异母兄斯特凡·弗拉迪斯拉夫，统治塞尔维亚至1276年。

他把泽塔交给弗拉迪斯拉夫治理，并娶海伦为妻，育有德拉古廷和米卢廷两个儿子。他在位长久，矿业与经济兴盛，为日后塞尔维亚的扩张奠定基础；他也是第一位采用拜占庭皇帝全套礼服的塞尔维亚统治者。1276年，与儿子斯特凡·德拉古廷的冲突迫使他退位，他于1277年5月1日去世。

en:
Stefan Uroš III, called Dečanski (c. 1276–1331), was king of Serbia from 1322. The son of Stefan Milutin, he spent his youth as a hostage at the court of Nogai Khan and governed Zeta. After Milutin died in 1321, Stefan was crowned in January 1322 and then defeated the rival claimants Konstantin and Stefan Vladislav II, the latter in 1324.

In 1330 Bulgaria and Byzantium planned an invasion of Serbia, but Stefan defeated the Bulgarians at Velbazhd, where Tsar Michael Asen III was killed. He founded Visoki Dečani monastery, which gave him his name. In 1331 his son Stefan Dušan deposed him; he died at Zvečan on 11 November and was canonised.

斯特凡·乌罗什三世，世称德钱斯基（约1276—1331），自1322年起任塞尔维亚国王。他是斯特凡·米卢丁之子，年轻时曾作为人质留在那海汗的宫廷，后来出统泽塔。1321年米卢丁去世后，他于1322年1月加冕，随后击败争位者康斯坦丁和堂兄斯特凡·弗拉迪斯拉夫二世，后者于1324年败北。

1330年保加利亚和拜占庭计划入侵塞尔维亚，但斯特凡在维尔巴日德击败保加利亚军，沙皇米哈伊尔·阿森三世战死。他修建了维索基德查尼修道院，并由此得名。1331年，其子斯特凡·杜尚将他废黜，他于11月11日死于兹韦查恩堡，后来被封圣。

en:
Stefan Dragutin (c. 1244–12 March 1316) was the eldest son of King Stefan Uroš I. Married to Catherine of Hungary and already titled young king, he rebelled with Hungarian help and forced his father to abdicate in 1276, ruling Serbia until 1282.

After a riding accident he handed the crown to his brother Milutin but kept the northern lands; in 1284 he received Hungarian border banates and became the first Serbian ruler of Belgrade, unofficially styled king of Syrmia. Their conflicts became open war in 1301; defeated by Milutin's mercenaries in 1311 or 1312, Dragutin made peace and died as a monk in 1316.

斯特凡·德拉古廷（约1244—1316年3月12日）是国王斯特凡·乌罗什一世的长子。他娶匈牙利的卡塔琳为妻并受封“年轻国王”，1276年借匈牙利援军起兵，逼迫父亲退位，统治塞尔维亚至1282年。

en:
Stefan Uroš IV Dušan (c. 1308–1355), called the Mighty, made medieval Serbia the leading power of the Balkans. He made his name at Velbazhd against Bulgaria in 1330, and when nobles wanting to expand south resented his father Dečanski for not pressing the victory on Byzantium, Dušan in 1331 besieged him at Nerodimlje, had him imprisoned, and was crowned king in September.

From 1342 he exploited the Byzantine civil war to take Byzantine lands as far as Kavala. On 16 April 1346 he was crowned emperor of the Serbs and Greeks at Skopje by the Serbian patriarch. He took Epirus in 1347 and Thessaly in 1348, ruling from the Danube to the Gulf of Corinth, and proclaimed his Code on 21 May 1349.

He died at Prizren on 20 December 1355 while preparing a campaign against the Turks, and his empire fell apart under his son Stefan Uroš V.

zh:
斯特凡·乌罗什四世·杜尚（约1308—1355），世称“强者”杜尚，使中世纪塞尔维亚成为巴尔干首强。1330年，他在对保加利亚的维尔巴日德之战中崭露头角。想向南扩张的贵族不满其父德钱斯基不乘胜进攻拜占庭；1331年，杜尚在内罗迪姆列围困父亲，将其囚禁，9月加冕为国王。

1342年起，他趁拜占庭内战夺取直到卡瓦拉的拜占庭领土。1346年4月16日，塞尔维亚牧首在斯科普里为他加冕，称塞尔维亚人与希腊人的皇帝。1347年他攻取伊庇鲁斯，1348年攻取色萨利，疆域北起多瑙河、南抵科林斯湾；1349年5月21日，他颁布《杜尚法典》。

1355年12月20日，他在筹划讨伐土耳其人时卒于普里兹伦，其子斯特凡·乌罗什五世继位后，帝国随即瓦解。

en:
Stefan Konstantin (c. 1283–1322) ruled as king of Serbia from his father Stefan Milutin's death in 1321 until the spring of 1322. The younger son of Milutin, probably born to his Greek wife Helena, he held the appanage of Zeta and became heir after his elder brother Stefan was exiled.

He then faced his brother Stefan, returned from exile. Rejecting a power-sharing offer, he was defeated and killed in battle below Zvečan fortress, leaving Stefan to rule as Dečanski.

en:
Stefan Uroš II Milutin (c. 1253–1321), youngest son of Stefan Uroš I and Helen of Anjou, became king when his brother Dragutin abdicated in 1282. He immediately invaded Byzantium, seizing northern Macedonia including Skoplje, which he made his capital.

By 1284 he held northern Albania and Durrës, and the peace of 1299 let him keep his conquests as the dowry of Simonis, daughter of Emperor Andronikos II.

His reign brought a mining boom, including the silver works at Novo Brdo, and churches such as Our Lady of Ljeviš in Prizren. He died in 1321 and was venerated as a saint.

斯特凡·乌罗什二世·米卢廷（约1253—1321）是斯特凡·乌罗什一世与安茹的海伦的幼子，1282年其兄德拉古廷退位后成为塞尔维亚国王。他即位后随即入侵拜占庭，夺取包括斯科普里在内的马其顿北部并以此为都。

到1284年，他已控制阿尔巴尼亚北部与都拉斯；1299年双方议和，他以皇帝安德洛尼卡二世之女西蒙尼斯的嫁妆为名保留了征服所得。

他在位时矿业兴盛，新布尔多发展为重要银矿产区，还兴建了普里兹伦的列维什圣母教堂等教堂。他于1321年去世，后被尊为圣徒。

en:
Stefan Nemanja (c. 1113–1199), youngest son of the Zachlumian prince Zavida, was Grand Prince of Raška from 1166 to 1196. He united the neighbouring Serb lands, broke free of Byzantine overlordship around 1180, and founded Studenica Monastery.

In 1196 he abdicated in favour of his son Stefan and withdrew to Mount Athos as the monk Simeon, where with his son Saint Sava he restored the Hilandar Monastery. He died in 1199 and was canonised as Saint Simeon the Myroblyte.

en:
Stefan Nemanjić, known as the First-Crowned (c. 1165–1228), was the second son of Grand Prince Stefan Nemanja and succeeded as Grand Prince of Serbia in 1196. After civil war and exile in his struggle with his elder brother Vukan, he regained power and brought Zeta and Hum under his control.

In 1217 he obtained a crown from Pope Honorius III and became Serbia's first crowned king. Two years later his brother Saint Sava secured autocephaly for the Serbian Church.

Around 1217 he married the Venetian noblewoman Anna Dandolo. He took monastic vows shortly before his death in 1228 and was buried at Sopoćani.

1217年，他从教宗洪诺留三世处取得王冠，成为第一位受加冕的塞尔维亚国王；两年后，其弟圣萨瓦为塞尔维亚教会争取到自治地位。

Stefan Radoslav (c. 1192–after 1235) was the eldest son of Stefan the First-Crowned and Eudokia Angelina. He succeeded as king of Serbia in 1228 and was crowned at Žiča by his uncle Archbishop Sava.

His marriage to Anna, daughter of Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus, gave his court a Greek flavour and alienated the Serbian nobility. In autumn 1233 the nobles rose and replaced Radoslav with his brother Vladislav. He fled to Dubrovnik, later returning to Serbia as the monk Jovan.

en:
Stefan Uroš V (1336–1371), called the Weak, was the only son of Stefan Dušan and Helena of Bulgaria. Crowned co-ruler in 1346, he succeeded as Serbian emperor in 1355, under whom the empire broke apart: his uncle Simeon Uroš proclaimed himself tsar, his mother Helena held Serres, and magnates such as Nikola Altomanović ruled on their own.

In 1365 Vukašin Mrnjavčević became co-ruler and in 1369 made his son Marko heir. After the Maritsa disaster of 1371, Uroš died childless that December, ending Nemanjić rule; he was canonised.

Stefan Vladislav (c. 1198–after 1264) was a son of Stefan the First-Crowned. In 1234 the Serbian nobility, hostile to his brother King Radoslav's Greek tilt, raised Vladislav to the throne. He married Beloslava, daughter of Ivan Asen II of Bulgaria.

When his uncle Archbishop Sava died in Bulgaria in 1235, Vladislav buried his relics in the Mileševa Monastery. After the Mongol devastation of the Balkans, the nobles deposed him in 1243 for his brother Uroš I, and he kept Zeta as governor.

zh:
斯特凡·弗拉迪斯拉夫（约1198—1264年后）是“首任国王”斯特凡之子。1234年，塞尔维亚贵族不满其兄国王拉多斯拉夫的亲希腊倾向，拥立弗拉迪斯拉夫登位；他娶保加利亚皇帝伊凡·阿森二世之女贝洛斯拉娃为妻。

1235年叔父大主教萨瓦在保加利亚去世，弗拉迪斯拉夫迎回其遗骨，安葬在米莱舍瓦修道院。蒙古人蹂躏巴尔干后，贵族于1243年废黜他，改立其弟乌罗什一世，他仍以泽塔长官的身份留在当地。

en:
Stefan Vladislav II (c. 1270–after 1326) was the eldest son of King Stefan Dragutin of Serbia and Catherine of Hungary. When Dragutin abdicated to his brother Stefan Milutin in 1282, the succession right of one of his sons was acknowledged. He inherited his father's northern realm of Syrmia in 1316 but was defeated and imprisoned by Milutin.

Freed after Milutin's death in 1321, he claimed the Serbian crown with Hungarian and Bulgarian backing, was beaten by Stefan Dečanski, and retired to Hungary in 1324.

zh:
斯特凡·弗拉迪斯拉夫二世（约1270—1326年后）是塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·德拉古廷与匈牙利的凯瑟琳的长子。1282年德拉古廷让位给弟弟斯特凡·米卢廷时，他其中一个儿子的继承权得到确认。1316年他继承父亲在北方的斯雷姆领地，却被米卢廷击败囚禁。

1321年米卢廷死后获释，他在匈牙利和保加利亚支持下争夺塞尔维亚王位，被斯特凡·德钱斯基击败，于1324年退入匈牙利。

en:
Theodora Nemanjić (1330 – after 1381) was the youngest daughter of King Stefan Uroš III Dečanski and Maria Palaiologina, and a half-sister of Stefan Dušan. In 1347 she married Despot Dejan, whom Dušan made sebastokrator, and bore him Jovan Dragaš and Constantine Dragaš, who ruled the eastern marches after Maritsa, and a daughter, Teodora.

Long widowed, she became a nun as Evdokija. Through Constantine's daughter Helena Dragaš she was the great-grandmother of the last Byzantine emperors John VIII and Constantine XI.

狄奥多拉·内马尼奇（1330—1381年以后）是国王斯特凡·乌罗什三世·德钱斯基与玛丽亚·巴列奥略最小的女儿、斯特凡·杜尚的异母妹妹。1347年她嫁给专制公德扬，杜尚封他为至尊者；她生下约万·德拉加什和康斯坦丁·德拉加什——兄弟二人在马里查战役后割据东部边疆——另有一女狄奥多拉。

寡居多年后她出家为尼，法名叶夫多基娅。通过康斯坦丁之女海伦娜·德拉加什，她是拜占庭末代皇帝约翰八世和君士坦丁十一世的曾祖母。

en:
Theodora, second daughter of Tsar Smilets of Bulgaria and Smiltsena Palaiologina, married the Serbian crown prince Stefan Uroš III, later Stefan Dečanski, in 1296. She was the mother of Stefan Dušan, the future emperor. When Milutin drove her husband into exile at Constantinople in 1314, she followed him and remained there until their return in 1320.

In 1322 she attended the assembly where Dušan was crowned young king; she and Dečanski soon divorced. A patron of literature and the arts, she died around 1322–1323 and was buried at Banjska.

Urošica (fl. 1285 – before 1316) was a Serbian prince of the Nemanjić dynasty, the younger son of King Stefan Dragutin and Catherine of Hungary. Renouncing political life, he took monastic vows as the monk Stefan and died before 1316, before his brother Vladislav inherited Syrmia.

He was buried in the church of Saint Achillius at Arilje, his father's endowment. The Serbian Orthodox Church venerates him as a saint.

乌罗什察（活跃于1285年—1316年前）是尼曼雅王朝的塞尔维亚王公，国王斯特凡·德拉古廷与匈牙利的凯瑟琳的幼子。他弃俗出家，取法名斯特凡，于1316年之前去世，未能见到兄长弗拉迪斯拉夫继承斯雷姆。

en:
Vojihna (c. 1298–1360) was a Serbian nobleman of a collateral Nemanjić line who became one of Stefan Dušan's leading commanders. Appointed governor of Drama before 1345, he was raised to the rank of caesar before 1348.

In 1356 he defeated and captured the Byzantine pretender Matthew Kantakouzenos near Serres, later handing him to Emperor John V Palaiologos for ransom. He died around 1360 and was buried at Hilandar; his daughter Jefimija married Despot Jovan Uglješa, who inherited his Drama lands.

沃伊赫纳（约1298—1360）出身内马尼奇王朝旁支，是斯特凡·杜尚麾下最主要的将领之一。1345年前他被任命为德拉马总督，1348年前获封凯撒。

1356年他在塞雷附近击败并俘获拜占庭帝位觊觎者马修·坎塔库泽努斯，随后将其交给皇帝约翰五世·巴列奥略以换取赎金。他约于1360年去世，葬于希兰达尔修道院；其女耶菲米娅嫁给专制公约万·乌格列沙，后者继承了他在德拉马的领地。
