en:
Vratislav Nemanjić was a Serbian župan of the Nemanjić dynasty and the only named son of Prince Dmitar Nemanjić. His father mentioned his heirs in a charter of 1286, while a grave slab at Davidovica Monastery calls him grand župan.

Serbian genealogies make him the father of the nobleman Vratko, sung in epic poetry as Jug Bogdan, and the grandfather of Princess Milica, wife of Prince Lazar. A Ragusan document of 1319 mentions another son, Radoslav.

en:
Vratko Nemanjić (fl. 1325–1355) was a Serbian nobleman of the Nemanjić dynasty's Vukan branch, the son of grand župan Vratislav and great-grandson of Vukan Nemanjić. A companion of Stefan Dušan, in 1342 he and vojvoda Oliver led a Serbian army against Serres in support of John VI Kantakouzenos, but the siege collapsed when dysentery killed some 1500 of their men.

His daughter Milica married Prince Lazar around 1353. Serbian epic poetry remembers him as Jug Bogdan, the aged hero of the Kosovo cycle.

en:
Vukan Nemanjić was the eldest son of Grand Prince Stefan Nemanja. Around 1190 his father gave him the lands centred on Zeta; an inscription of 1195 calls him king of Duklja. When Nemanja abdicated in 1196 the throne went to his younger brother Stefan.

In 1202 Vukan overthrew Stefan with troops from King Emeric of Hungary, whose vassal he became, promising to convert his people to Catholicism if the pope granted him a royal title. After a Bulgarian invasion in 1203 Stefan returned and deposed him in 1204. Reconciled through Saint Sava, he kept Zeta until his death soon after 1207.

武坎·内马尼奇是大茹潘斯特凡·尼曼雅的长子。约1190年，父亲把以泽塔为中心的领地封给他，1195年的一段铭文已称他为杜克里亚国王。1196年尼曼雅退位时，王位传给了他的弟弟斯特凡。

1202年，武坎在匈牙利国王伊姆雷的军队帮助下推翻斯特凡，成为匈牙利封臣，并许诺若教宗授予王号就让臣民改宗天主教。1203年保加利亚入侵后，斯特凡于1204年回国将他废黜。经圣萨瓦调解，兄弟和解，武坎保留泽塔直到1207年后不久去世。

en:
John Komnenos Asen (c. 1305–1363) was a Bulgarian nobleman, son of the despot Stracimir of Kran and brother-in-law of the Serbian tsar Stefan Dušan, whose court he joined. Dušan made him despot and put him in charge of his lands in southern Albania.

From about 1345 he ruled the Principality of Valona, at first as a Serbian vassal. Around 1350–1355 he married Anna Palaiologina, widow of the Epirote despot John II Orsini, which legitimised his standing. After Dušan died in 1355 he sided with the failed Simeon Uroš, yet with Venetian help kept Valona effectively independent.

He had become a Venetian citizen in 1353 and traded with Venice and Ragusa. He probably died of the plague in 1363 and was succeeded by Alexander, likely his son.

约翰·科穆宁·阿森（约1305—1363）是保加利亚贵族，为克兰专制公斯拉齐米尔之子，也是塞尔维亚沙皇斯特凡·杜尚的姻亲，后前往杜尚的宫廷。杜尚封他为专制公，让他掌管阿尔巴尼亚南部的领地。

约1345年起，他统治发罗拉公国，起初是塞尔维亚的封臣。约1350—1355年，他娶伊庇鲁斯专制君主约翰二世·奥尔西尼的遗孀安娜·巴列奥略吉娜为妻，这桩婚姻巩固了他的地位。1355年杜尚死后，他站在失败的西美翁·乌罗什一边，却靠威尼斯的帮助保住了发罗拉事实上的独立。

他1353年成为威尼斯公民，并与威尼斯和拉古萨通商。他很可能于1363年死于瘟疫，由很可能是其子的亚历山大继位。

en:
Sesshū Tōyō (c. 1420–1506) was the greatest Japanese ink painter of his age. Born into a samurai family in Bitchū Province, he became a Zen monk at Kyoto's Shōkoku-ji and studied for twenty years under Tenshō Shūbun. After leaving Kyoto he painted at a provincial Zen temple in western Japan.

In 1467 he sailed to Ming China with a Japanese envoy and studied Chinese landscape masters directly. He fused their realism with Japanese Zen sensibility in works such as his Winter Landscape and Four Landscape Scrolls of the Seasons. He died at Masuda in 1506, and later Japanese painting schools claimed him as founder.

雪舟（约1420—1506）是当时日本最伟大的水墨画家。他出身备中国的武士家庭，少年时入京都相国寺为禅僧，随天章周文学画二十年。离开京都后，他在日本西部的地方禅寺作画。

1467年，他随日本遣明使船前往明朝中国，亲炙中国山水画名家。他把中国画的写实笔法与日本禅宗意趣融为一体，代表作有《冬景山水图》与《四季山水图卷》等。1506年他在益田去世，后世日本众多画派都奉他为开山之祖。

en:
Shaikh Ali ibn Ali Qushji was an Ilkhanid administrator in Khurasan, its governor under Abu Sa'id Bahadur Khan. After Abu Sa'id's death in 1335, Qushji put forward the Genghisid prince Togha Temür as Ilkhan, persuading the amirs of Khurasan to have the Friday prayer read and coins struck in his name.

On Togha Temür's 1337 campaign the army was routed near Sultaniya by the Jalayirid Hasan Buzurg. Qushji fled, was seized at Bistam by Arghun Shah's men, and was executed, his head sent to Hasan Buzurg.

en:
Bahram Khan, also called Tatar Khan (died 1337), was a general of the Delhi Sultanate and governor of Sonargaon in Bengal. Chronicle accounts make him the infant son of a defeated ruler of Khorasan, adopted and raised by Sultan Ghiyath al-Din Tughlaq after a night attack near Multan.

Appointed governor of Satgaon in 1324, he was transferred to Sonargaon in 1328 and ruled there until his death. When he died in 1337 his armour keeper Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah seized power and founded the independent sultanate of Sonargaon.

en:
Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah (r. 1338–1349) was the founder of the independent sultanate of Sonargaon. A Bengali Muslim who rose as armour-bearer to the Delhi governor Bahram Khan, he seized power after Bahram died in 1337 and made Sonargaon his capital. After Qadar Khan of Lakhnauti occupied the city, Fakhruddin lured his troops amid a dispute over the spoils, killed Qadar Khan and recovered Sonargaon.

He then conquered Comilla, Noakhali and Sylhet, and in 1340 became the first Muslim ruler to take Chittagong. He died in 1349 and was succeeded by Ikhtiyaruddin Ghazi Shah.

法赫尔丁·穆巴拉克沙（1338—1349年在位）是独立的索纳尔冈苏丹国的建立者。他出身孟加拉穆斯林，在德里任命的索纳尔冈总督巴赫拉姆汗麾下担任掌甲侍从。1337年巴赫拉姆汗死后，他夺取政权，以索纳尔冈为都城。拉克瑙提的卡达尔汗一度攻占索纳尔冈，法赫尔丁趁敌军因分赃内讧之际诱使对方，杀死卡达尔汗并收复城池。

此后他征服库米拉、诺阿卡利和锡尔赫特，又于1340年成为首位拿下吉大港的穆斯林统治者。他于1349年去世，由伊赫提亚鲁丁·加齐沙继位。

en:
Shidibala (1302–1323), titled Gegeen Khan and Emperor Yingzong of Yuan, was the eldest son of Ayurbarwada, succeeding him in 1320. His early reign was overshadowed by his grandmother Dagi and her councillor Temuder, but he raised the Jalayir noble Baiju against them, and after the two died in 1322 he took full power.

With Baiju he carried out Confucian reforms, recalled Chinese scholar-officials and in 1323 promulgated the Da Yuan Tong Zhi code. That September, Temuder's faction and the Alan guard murdered him at Nanpo, the first violent overthrow of a Yuan emperor.

硕德八剌（1302—1323），号格坚汗，庙号英宗，爱育黎拔力八达长子，1320年继位。即位之初，朝政受制于祖母答己及其宠臣铁木迭儿；他提拔札剌亦儿贵族拜住以相制衡，1322年答己与铁木迭儿相继死去后，他全面亲政。

他与拜住推行儒治改革，起用汉族士大夫，并于1323年颁行《大元通制》。同年九月，铁木迭儿党羽联合阿速卫兵在南坡发动政变，将他弑杀，这是元朝首次以暴力更迭皇帝。

en:
Shikellamy (died 1748), also called Swatana, was an Oneida chief and overseer for the Haudenosaunee Confederacy, supervising the Shawnee and Lenape along Pennsylvania's Susquehanna River and protecting the confederacy's southern border. In 1742 he settled at Shamokin at the river's forks.

For two decades he was the chief go-between linking the Pennsylvania government with the confederacy council at Onondaga, guiding colonial envoys through Iroquois country and helping keep the frontier at peace. He died at Shamokin in December 1748.

希凯拉米（卒于1748年），又名斯瓦塔纳，是奥奈达酋长兼豪德诺索尼联盟的督办，负责监管宾夕法尼亚萨斯奎哈纳河沿岸的肖尼人与莱纳佩人，并保卫联盟南部边界。1742年他迁居萨斯奎哈纳河两河交汇处的沙莫金。

约二十年间，他是宾夕法尼亚殖民政府与奥农达加联盟议事会之间最主要的中间人，曾为殖民地使节穿越易洛魁地区引路，帮助维持边疆和平。1748年12月，他在沙莫金去世。

en:
Adolph IX (c. 1327–1390), numbered Adolf VII in the Kiel tradition, was the only son of Count John III the Mild of Holstein-Kiel, whom he succeeded in 1359 as count of Holstein-Kiel and Holstein-Plön. In 1362 he married Anna of Mecklenburg-Schwerin.

His long reign was mostly peaceful: in 1375 Archbishop Albert II of Bremen mortgaged him the Haseldorf Marsh, which was never redeemed and so stayed with Holstein. He died heirless in January 1390, after which the Rendsburg counts occupied his lands.

阿道夫九世（约1327—1390，按基尔谱系又称阿道夫七世）是荷尔斯泰因-基尔伯爵“温和者”约翰三世的独子，1359年继位，领有荷尔斯泰因-基尔与荷尔斯泰因-普伦。1362年他娶梅克伦堡-什未林的安娜为妻。

en:
Gerhard I (1232–1290) was Count of Holstein-Itzehoe, the second son of Count Adolf IV. From 1238 he ruled jointly with his elder brother John I under the guardianship of Duke Abel of Schleswig. In 1261 the brothers divided the county, Gerhard receiving Itzehoe with Stormarn and Plön.

He won the Battle of Loh Moor in 1262 and, after John's death in 1263, governed Kiel as regent for his nephews. He died in December 1290; his sons partitioned Itzehoe into Plön, Pinneberg and Rendsburg.

en:
Gerhard II, called the Blind (1254 – 28 October 1312), was count of Holstein-Plön from 1290. The second son of Gerhard I of Holstein-Itzehoe, he received Plön when his father's county was divided among the brothers in 1290.

In 1275 he married Ingeborg, daughter of the king of Sweden; their son Gerhard IV succeeded at Plön. In 1293 he married Agnes of Brandenburg, widow of King Eric V of Denmark, by whom he had John III, who ruled Holstein-Kiel from 1312.

en:
Gerhard III (c. 1292–1340), called the Great or the Bald Count, inherited Holstein-Rendsburg young and built it into a strong north German principality. In 1326 he helped depose King Christopher II of Denmark and set his nephew Valdemar on the throne, ruling Denmark as regent and detaching Schleswig through the Constitutio Valdemariana.

From 1332 he was the effective ruler of Jutland and Funen, his regime weighed down by debt and peasant revolts. On 1 April 1340 he was slain in his bedroom at Randers by the Danish squire Niels Ebbesen, ending Holstein rule in Denmark.

格哈德三世（约1292—1340），绰号“大帝”或“秃头伯爵”，年轻时继承荷尔斯泰因-伦茨堡，将其经营成北德意志的强大邦国。1326年他参与废黜丹麦国王克里斯托弗二世，把外甥瓦尔德马扶上丹麦王位，自己以摄政身份统治丹麦，并通过《瓦尔德马宪章》使石勒苏益格脱离丹麦。

1332年起，他成为日德兰和菲英的实际统治者，政权却深陷债务与农民起义。1340年4月1日，他在兰讷斯被丹麦乡绅尼尔斯·艾布森闯入睡房杀死，荷尔斯泰因人对丹麦的统治就此终结。

en:
Gerhard IV (c. 1277–1323) was Count of Holstein-Plön from 1312, the eldest son of Count Gerhard II and Ingeborg of Sweden. In 1313 he married Anastasia, daughter of Nicholas I of Schwerin.

Soon after succeeding, in 1314 he sold almost all of his inheritance to his younger brother John III, keeping little beyond the comital title. He died around 1323, leaving a son Gerhard V, a Lübeck canon, and a daughter Ingeborg, who married Count Conrad I of Oldenburg and mothered Christian V of Oldenburg.

en:
Gerhard V of Holstein-Plön (c. 1315–1350) was the only son of Count Gerhard IV and Anastasia of Schwerin. About 1323, aged eight, he inherited Holstein-Plön on his father's death, but he never formally ruled the county and lived as a landowner and a canon and provost of Lübeck Cathedral.

He died on 22 September 1350, unmarried and without children, leaving Holstein-Plön to his uncle John III of Kiel, who thus reunited Plön with Kiel.

en:
Henry I (1258–1304) was the first Count of Holstein-Rendsburg and a son of Gerhard I of Holstein-Itzehoe. In 1285 he persuaded King Eric V of Denmark to release Duke Valdemar IV of Schleswig from captivity. After Gerhard died in 1290, the surviving sons partitioned Holstein-Itzehoe and Henry received the Rendsburg portion.

He waged repeated wars against the Ditmarschen and, shortly before he died on 5 August 1304, introduced a toll on imported goods; Hamburg received half the proceeds.

en:
Henry II (c. 1317–c. 1384), called Iron Henry, was the elder son of Count Gerhard III of Holstein-Rendsburg and Sophia of Werle. After his father's murder in 1340 he ruled the county jointly with his younger brother Nicholas, pressing their claims in Schleswig against Denmark.

A famed mercenary captain, in 1367 he commanded a Hanseatic League fleet and in 1368 captured Copenhagen. By his second wife Ingeborg he fathered Gerhard VI, later Duke of Schleswig.

海因里希二世（约1317—约1384），绰号“铁人海因里希”，是荷尔斯泰因-伦茨堡伯爵格哈德三世与韦尔勒的索菲的长子。1340年父亲遇刺后，他与弟弟尼库劳斯共同统治伯国，在石勒苏益格与丹麦相争。

作为著名的雇佣军首领，1367年他统率汉萨同盟舰队，1368年攻占哥本哈根。他与第二任妻子英格堡生有格哈德六世，后者后来成为石勒苏益格公爵。

en:
John III, called the Mild (c. 1297–1359), was a count of Holstein-Plön and Holstein-Kiel, son of Gerhard II the Blind and Agnes of Brandenburg, and half-brother of Kings Eric VI and Christopher II. In 1312 he succeeded in Plön and inherited Kiel in 1316.

A chief creditor of Denmark, from 1332 to 1340 he and Count Gerhard III of Rendsburg guarded Schleswig. He died in 1359 and was succeeded by his son Adolphus.

en:
Nicholas, also called Claus of Holstein (1321–1397), was the second son of Count Gerhard III and Sophia of Werle. From 1340 he co-ruled Holstein-Rendsburg, first with his brother Henry II and later with his nephews.

In 1375 he became co-ruler of Schleswig, ruling alone after Henry's death until in 1386 he yielded it to Henry's son Gerhard VI. In 1390 he inherited Holstein-Kiel with his nephews, uniting nearly all Holstein. He died at Itzehoe on 8 May 1397.

en:
Sophia of Werle (d. after 1339) was a daughter of Lord Nicholas II of Werle and Richeza, daughter of King Eric V of Denmark. In 1310 her uncle King Eric VI betrothed her to Duke Erik of Södermanland and sent her to Sweden, but Erik married another in 1312 and she returned home.

Around 1315 she married Count Gerhard III of Holstein-Rendsburg, later ruler of Denmark. Her sons Henry II and Nicholas succeeded as counts, and through Henry she was an ancestress of the House of Oldenburg.

zh:
韦尔勒的索菲（1339年后在世）是韦尔勒领主尼古拉二世与丹麦国王埃里克五世之女里基莎的女儿。1310年，她的舅舅丹麦国王埃里克六世将她许配给南曼兰公爵埃里克，并把她送往瑞典；但埃里克于1312年另娶他人，索菲只好返回韦尔勒。

约1315年，她嫁给后来统治丹麦的荷尔斯泰因-伦茨堡伯爵格哈德三世。儿子海因里希二世和尼库劳斯后来继任伯爵；通过海因里希，她成为奥尔登堡家族的先祖之一。

en:
Princess Shouning was a Yuan imperial princess, the daughter of Gammala, Prince of Jin, and elder sister of Yesün Temür, the future Taiding Emperor; her grandfather was Crown Prince Zhenjin and her great-grandfather Kublai Khan. She married into the Naiman clan.

When her cousin's son Emperor Yingzong took the throne, he granted her seventy-five thousand guan, and after her brother seized power in 1323 she received a hundred qing of land and further gifts. Her daughter Babusha married Khutughtu Khan and bore the future Emperor Ningzong; another daughter, Sadabala, entered the Taiding Emperor's harem in 1326.

en:
Nusrat al-Din Hasan (died 1277) was a son of the Seljuk vizier Sahib Ata Fakhr al-Din Ali. In 1275 his father secured Karahisar-i Sahib (Afyonkarahisar) as a family holding for Hasan and his brother Taj al-Din Husayn, founding the Sahib Ataid beylik under their joint rule.

When the Karamanid Mehmed Bey and the Seljuk pretender Cimri seized Konya in 1277, the brothers marched against them and both fell at the Battle of Değirmençayı. Hasan's son Shams al-Din Mehmed succeeded as bey.

en:
Shams al-Din Mehmed (died 1287) was the second bey of the Sahib Ataids. His father Nusrat al-Din Hasan and his uncle Taj al-Din Husayn, joint founders of the beylik, both fell fighting the Karamanids at the Battle of Değirmençayı in 1277, and Mehmed succeeded to the rule of Karahisar-i Sahib (Afyonkarahisar).

In 1287 he led his forces to repel an attack by the neighbouring Germiyanids and was killed in the fighting. His son Nusrat al-Din Ahmed succeeded him.

舍姆塞丁·穆罕默德（？—1287年）是萨希布-阿塔的第二代贝伊。1277年，贝伊里克的共同创建者——他的父亲努斯拉丁·哈桑与叔父塔杰丁·侯赛因在代伊尔门恰伊战役中同卡拉曼人作战时双双阵亡，穆罕默德遂继领萨希布-卡拉希萨尔（阿菲永卡拉希萨尔）。

1287年，他率军抵御邻邦格尔米扬的进攻，战死沙场。其子努斯拉丁·艾哈迈德继位。

en:
Nusreddin Ahmed was the third bey of the Sahib Ataid principality centered on Karahisar-i Sahib. In 1287 he succeeded his father, killed fighting a Germiyanid attack.

When the Ilkhanid governor Temürtaş besieged Karahisar, Ahmed took refuge with the Germiyanids. The siege was abandoned in 1327 after Temürtaş's father was killed by the Ilkhan, and Ahmed returned to rule as a Germiyanid vassal. He died in 1343 and his lands were absorbed into the Germiyanid beylik.

努斯雷丁·艾哈迈德是以萨希卜卡拉希萨尔为中心的萨希布-阿塔贝伊国第三代贝伊。1287年，其父在抵御格尔米扬进攻的战斗中身亡，艾哈迈德继位。

伊利汗国安纳托利亚长官帖木儿塔什围攻卡拉希萨尔时，他逃往格尔米扬避难。1327年帖木儿塔什之父被伊利汗处死后，他撤围而去，艾哈迈德得以归国，作为格尔米扬的附庸继续统治。他于1343年去世，领土随后被并入格尔米扬贝伊国。

en:
Fakhr al-Din Ali, known as Sâhib Ata, was grand vizier of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum. First recorded in 1249 as amir-i dad, the chief justiciar, he held the regency in 1258 when Kaykawus II joined the Ilkhanid campaign against Baghdad, received the title sahib in 1260, and became grand vizier in 1261.

After the Mongols executed Mu'in al-Din Parwana in 1277, he was the dominant ruler of the sultanate. His sons Husayn and Hasan founded the Sahip Ataid principality. A great architectural patron, he died in 1288 after returning ill from the Ilkhanid court at Tabriz.

法赫尔丁·阿里，通称萨希布·阿塔，是罗姆塞尔柱苏丹国的大维齐尔。史籍中他最早于1249年以司法长官“埃米尔·达德”身份出现；1258年凯考斯二世随伊儿汗大军出征巴格达期间，他以摄政留守，1260年获赐“萨希布”称号，1261年出任大维齐尔。

1277年穆因丁·佩瓦内被蒙古人处死后，他成为罗姆苏丹国最有权势的执政者。其子侯赛因与哈桑开创萨希布·阿塔侯国。他大兴土木、广建慈善机构，1288年在大不里士觐见伊儿汗后抱病返回，不久便去世。

en:
Dietrich I (documented 1209–1249) was Count of Hohnstein, a Harz comital dynasty, and Vogt, or lay protector, of Homburg monastery on the Unstrut. Before 1231 he married Hedwig, daughter of Count Frederick II of Brehna.

In 1231 he attended the imperial court assembly at Worms. He is last recorded in 1249 and died on 23 July that year. His son Henry I succeeded him in the county and added the Klettenberg lordship in 1253.

en:
Dietrich II (c. 1245–1309) was Count of Hohnstein-Klettenberg, the son of Count Henry I. Made a knight in 1275, he became junior head of the dynasty in 1279 and steadily widened its Thuringian holdings: Arnsberg in 1293 and Sondershausen by 1295.

He held Voigtstedt, Artern and the Vogtei of Dietenborn, and in 1307 he became senior of the house. He married Sophie of Anhalt-Bernburg and died between 28 May and 11 August 1309.

迪特里希二世（约1245—1309）是霍恩施泰因-克莱滕贝格伯爵，海因里希一世之子。1275年受封骑士，1279年成为家族的年少领主，并不断扩大在图林根的领地，1293年取得阿恩斯贝格，1295年前取得松德斯豪森。

en:
Henry I (c. 1225–1284/93) was Count of Hohnstein, succeeding his father Dietrich I in 1249. In 1253 he took over Klettenberg, and over the following decades he built up a Thuringian lordship piecemeal: half of Kirchberg Castle and Ehrich in 1259, Greußen in 1260, and Spatenberg Castle, enfeoffed to him by Landgrave Albert in 1263.

Sömmerda followed in 1268. He married Mechthild of Regenstein before 1253, became senior of the house in 1280, and died on 24 January, between 1284 and 1293.

en:
Heinrich II (IV), Count of Honstein, was born around 1275, the son of Count Dietrich II and Sophie of Anhalt-Bernburg. Through his marriage before 1302 to Irmgard, heiress of Arnstadt, he inherited Arnstadt in 1302, became head of the house in 1305 and ruled its Klettenberg lands from 1309.

In 1327 he built Heringen Castle, and he founded the Klettberg line of the family. He is last documented in 1342 and died before 1344.

en:
Henry III of Honstein (c. 1256–1305) was a count of the Honstein dynasty who ruled its southern Harz lands around Honstein, Arnstadt and Sondershausen. He was the son of Count Henry I of Honstein and Mechtild of Regenstein. Before 1282 he married Jutta, daughter of Count Otto II of Ravensberg.

His son Henry V kept Sondershausen after him, and another son, Dietrich IV, also ruled there as count. Henry III died in 1305, and Jutta died shortly before him.

Henry V (III) of Honstein (c. 1290–1356) was count of Honstein-Sondershausen in the Thuringian Harz, son of Count Henry III and Jutta of Ravensberg. He ruled Sondershausen from 1312 and around 1319 married Matilda of Brunswick-Göttingen.

He also held several pledged Thuringian lordships. His daughters Agnes and Elizabeth married Schwarzburg counts, and leaving no son, Henry died after 24 April 1356, whereupon Sondershausen passed to the Schwarzburgs.

亨利希五世（又编号为三世）·冯·霍恩施泰因（约1290—1356）是图林根哈茨山区霍恩施泰因-松德斯豪森伯爵，伯爵亨利希三世与拉文斯贝格的尤塔之子。他1312年起统治松德斯豪森，约1319年娶不伦瑞克-哥廷根的玛蒂尔达。

他还受领多处抵押领地。女儿阿格妮丝与伊丽莎白嫁入施瓦茨堡家族；他没有儿子，1356年4月24日之后去世，松德斯豪森随之转入施瓦茨堡家族之手。

en:
Antoni de Vilaragut i Visconti (1336–1400) was a Catalan nobleman, son of Ramon de Vilaragut and Diana Visconti. He went from Valencia to Sicily at sixteen and, captaining ships defending the island against Naples, received the barony of Tripi from John, duke of Athens.

Peter IV made him castellan of Xàtiva in 1375, and John I named him majordomo in 1388. He died in 1400 leaving one of Valencia's greatest estates; the Seneca translations once credited to him may have been made by his grandson.

en:
Beatrice of Sicily (1326–1365) was a princess of the House of Barcelona, daughter of King Peter II of Sicily and Elisabeth of Carinthia, born in Palermo. In 1335 she was betrothed to her cousin John Henry IV of Gorizia, but the match was broken off when his mother allied the county with the Habsburgs.

In 1345 she married Rupert, Count Palatine of the Rhine. Her son Rupert became King of Germany, and she died in 1365.

en:
Beatrice of Savoy (born before 4 March 1223) was the elder daughter of Count Amadeus IV of Savoy. In March 1233 she married Manfred III, marquess of Saluzzo, and on his death in 1244 she held the regency for their young son Thomas, until Boniface II of Montferrat forced her aside.

In March 1247 she married by proxy Manfred, son of Emperor Frederick II, sealing the Savoy-Hohenstaufen alliance. Their daughter Constance married Peter III of Aragon. Beatrice died in 1258 or 1259, just as her husband seized the crown of Sicily.

en:
Bianca Lancia (c. 1210–c. 1248) was an Italian noblewoman of the Lancia family of Piedmont, who spent much of her life at the family seat of Brolo. She became the mistress of Emperor Frederick II, probably meeting him in Sicily between 1226 and 1230, and bore him three children.

Constance married the Nicaean emperor John III Vatatzes in 1244; Manfred later became king of Sicily; and Violante wed Richard Sanseverino. Chroniclers record a deathbed marriage to Frederick around 1247, which legitimized Manfred but was never recognized by the Church.

As Pietro left no sons, the County of Caltanissetta passed to John through this marriage. Her son Frederick succeeded his father as duke when John died of plague in 1348.

en:
Catherine of Sicily (1320–1342) was a daughter of King Frederick III of Sicily and Eleanor of Anjou. She was professed a Poor Clare at the royal convent of Santa Chiara in Messina, a house closely patronised by her mother, and became its first abbess.

She died there on 18 February 1342 with a reputation for sanctity, and was succeeded as abbess by her niece Constance, daughter of her brother King Peter II.

en:
Conradin (1252–1268), the last heir of the Hohenstaufen dynasty, was the son of King Conrad IV and Elisabeth of Bavaria. In 1254 he inherited the Duchy of Swabia and his family's claim to Sicily, and he was raised in Bavaria.

After Charles of Anjou seized southern Italy, he crossed the Alps in 1267 to answer the Ghibelline call and entered Rome in July 1268. Charles crushed his army at Tagliacozzo on 23 August 1268.

Betrayed while trying to sail to Sicily, he was captured and taken to Naples. There Conradin was beheaded on 29 October 1268, aged sixteen, ending the Hohenstaufen male line.

Constance of Sicily (1304/1306 – after 1344), born at Palermo, was a daughter of Frederick III of Sicily and Eleanor of Anjou. She was betrothed to a son of Philip IV of France until the boy died in 1308, then married King Henry II of Cyprus in 1317 and was widowed in 1324.

In 1331 she married Leo IV of Cilician Armenia; the marriage aroused anti-Western sentiment in Armenia. After Leo was murdered in 1341, she married John of Lusignan in 1343 and died after 1344.

Constance of Sicily (1324–1355) was a daughter of King Peter II and Elisabeth of Carinthia. Unmarried, she was an abbess at Messina and educated her brothers Louis and Frederick. After her mother died in 1352, Constance took over the regency for King Louis.

She ruled a kingdom torn by baronial feuds and the Black Death. Louis died of the plague in October 1355, and Constance followed him days later; their sister Euphemia then became regent for Frederick.

en:
Conrad of Antioch (born 1240/1241, died after 1312) was the eldest son of Frederick of Antioch, grandson of Emperor Frederick II and nephew of King Manfred. In 1258 he was made captain of Abruzzo.

He fought for Manfred to restore Hohenstaufen rule in central Italy, but the Angevin conquest drove him into exile; his cousin Conradin then made him prince of Abruzzo. He joined Conradin's invasion of 1267–1268, fought at Tagliacozzo, and was a prisoner until 1272.

He later raided Angevin Abruzzo without success, then retired to Anticoli. In May 1312 he led fifty knights to Rome to greet Henry VII.

他为曼弗雷迪征战，试图恢复霍恩施陶芬家族在意大利中部的统治，却在安茹家族征服王国后被迫流亡，流亡期间堂弟康拉丁授予他阿布鲁佐亲王头衔。1267—1268年，他加入康拉丁收复王国的进军，在塔利亚科佐参战，被俘后关押至1272年。

后来他多次袭扰安茹家族治下的阿布鲁佐，均未得手，此后退居安蒂科利。1312年5月，他还率五十名骑士赴罗马迎接亨利七世。

en:
Corrado Lancia, known as Corrado di Castromainardo, was a Sicilian nobleman, founder of the Lancia branch of Sicily. His father Galeotto was executed by the Angevins after Tagliacozzo in 1268, and the family took refuge in Aragon, returning under Aragonese rule. In 1302 the crown granted him baronies including Longi and Ficarra together with Brolo castle; he later served as justiciar of Palermo.

In 1312 he led 2200 men to Djerba and defeated its rebel Moors, and in 1314 he negotiated the truce of Trapani with Robert of Anjou. He died around 1328.

en:
Constance II of Sicily (c. 1249–1302) was the only daughter of Manfred, King of Sicily, and Beatrice of Savoy. On 13 June 1262 she married Peter, eldest son of James I of Aragon.

After Manfred fell to Charles of Anjou at Benevento in 1266, she inherited the Hohenstaufen claim to Sicily. Queen consort of Aragon from 1276, she ruled Sicily alongside Peter after the Sicilian Vespers of 1282 until his death in 1285.

Peter and then their sons claimed Sicily in her right in the ensuing war, which divided the kingdom between their heirs and those of Charles. She died as a nun in Barcelona on 9 April 1302.

en:
Demetrius of Montferrat (1205–1230) was king of Thessalonica from 1207. Born in the city and named after its patron Saint Demetrius, he was the son of Marquis Boniface I of Montferrat and Margaret of Hungary. After his father fell fighting the Bulgarians, Latin Emperor Henry of Flanders overawed the Lombard barons and crowned the boy king on 6 January 1209.

When Theodore of Epirus took Thessalonica in 1224, Demetrius fled to Frederick II, joined his crusade, ceded him his claims to the kingdom and died at Amalfi in 1230.

en:
Eleanor of Anjou (1289–1341), third daughter of Charles II of Naples and Mary of Hungary, was a bride whose wedding helped end a war. Her childhood marriage to Philippe II de Toucy was dissolved by the pope in 1300 because the two were related.

On 17 May 1302 she married Frederick III, King of Sicily, whom her father had long fought. The wedding was part of the diplomacy behind the Peace of Caltabellotta later that year, which gave Frederick the island and her father the mainland kingdom.

She bore Frederick nine children, including his successor Peter II and sons who held the duchy of Athens. Widowed in 1337, she died at a monastery in Catania on 9 August 1341.

zh:
安茹的埃莉诺（1289—1341）是那不勒斯国王卡洛二世与匈牙利的玛丽亚的第三个女儿，她的婚礼促成了一场战争的结束。她幼年与菲利普二世·德·图西的婚姻因两人有亲属关系，于1300年被教皇解除。

1302年5月17日，她嫁给西西里国王腓特烈三世，而她的父亲一直为西西里与他交战。这场婚礼是同年《卡尔塔贝洛塔和约》背后外交努力的一部分：和约把西西里岛划给腓特烈，大陆王国归她的父亲。

她为腓特烈生下九个子女，包括继位的皮埃特罗二世和曾任雅典公爵的几个儿子。1337年守寡后，她于1341年8月9日在卡塔尼亚的一座修道院去世。

Eleanor (1325–1375) was a Sicilian princess, daughter of King Peter II of Sicily and Elisabeth of Carinthia. In 1349 she married King Peter IV of Aragon as his third wife, becoming its queen consort and holding strong influence at court.

In 1357 she backed an unsuccessful plan to send Aragonese aid to her brother Frederick IV of Sicily in exchange for the Duchy of Neopatras. Her sons John I and Martin I both became kings of Aragon, and she died in 1375.

Elizabeth of Carinthia (1298?–1352) was the daughter of Otto III of Carinthia of the House of Gorizia. In 1323 she married King Peter II of Sicily and became queen, bearing the future kings Louis and Frederick IV.

When Peter died in 1342, her brother-in-law John of Randazzo ruled as regent for Louis; after John's death from plague in 1348 Elizabeth took the regency herself and steered the crown through feuding noble factions until her own death, probably of plague, in 1352.

en:
Euphemia of Sicily (1330–1359) was a princess of the House of Barcelona, daughter of King Peter II of Sicily and Elisabeth of Carinthia. When her brother King Louis and her regent sister Constance both died of plague in 1355, the crown passed to her brother Frederick IV, and Euphemia was named vicar.

She ruled through feuds between rival noble factions, favouring one side until Frederick removed her from the vicariate, though she directed the regency until 1357. She never married and died in 1359.

en:
Frederick of Antioch (c. 1223–1255/56) was an illegitimate son of Emperor Frederick II by Matilda of Antioch. From 1246 to 1250 he served his father as imperial vicar of Tuscany.

He ruled Florence as podestà and drove out the Guelph leaders in 1248. After a Florentine rebellion in 1250 and the emperor's death that December, his Tuscan regime collapsed. He then joined his half-brother Conrad IV and backed Manfred against the papacy. He died of plague during the siege of Foggia in 1255 or 1256.

en:
Frederick III of Sicily (1272–1337) was the third son of Peter III of Aragon and Constance II. In 1291 he became regent of Sicily for his brother James II. When James handed the island to the Church and the Angevins in 1295, the Sicilians refused to go back to French rule and crowned Frederick king at Palermo in 1296.

He held out against Angevin and papal armies, defeating an invasion in 1299. The Peace of Caltabellotta in 1302 recognised him as king for life and married him to Eleanor of Anjou, though the crown was nominally to return to the Angevins.

He strengthened the Sicilian parliament and renewed the war with Naples in 1313 with Emperor Henry VII's backing. He died at Paternò in 1337, and his son Peter II succeeded him regardless.

他强化了西西里议会，1313年在皇帝亨利七世支持下再度对那不勒斯开战。他于1337年卒于帕泰尔诺，儿子皮埃特罗二世仍继承了王位。

en:
Galeotto Lancia was a son of Galvano Lancia, grand marshal of the Kingdom of Sicily, by his second wife Margherita of Ocre, and held the title count of Atti. He married Cubitosa d'Aquino.

In 1268 Galeotto and his father joined Conradin of Hohenstaufen's expedition against Charles I of Anjou. Both were captured at the Battle of Tagliacozzo on 23 August.

His son Corrado later served the crown of Aragon as a lord in Sicily. Galeotto was beheaded in the market square of Naples on 29 October 1268, immediately after Conradin.

Galvano Lancia (before 1220–1268) was an Italian noble and commander of the Lancia family. Emperor Frederick II made him justiciar of Sicily in 1240, but Conrad IV expelled him in 1252; he then became Manfred's chief lieutenant and organized an army in Apulia in 1254.

In 1256 he was named prince of Salerno and grand marshal of Sicily. He joined Conradin against Charles of Anjou and was captured at Tagliacozzo on 23 August 1268. His career ended on the scaffold. He was beheaded at Naples on 29 October 1268.

en:
Walter III of Brienne (French: Gautier, c. 1166–1205), eldest son of Count Erard II, succeeded as count of Brienne in Champagne in 1191. In 1200 he married Elvira, daughter of the deposed Sicilian king Tancred, and prepared an army to press her claim to Sicily.

Having taken the cross for the Fourth Crusade, he recruited crusaders for his Italian campaign. Pope Innocent III refused Elvira's claim to the throne but recognised the couple's rights to Taranto and Lecce; Walter won battles at Capua and Cannae in 1201.

In June 1205 he was stabbed in his camp at Terracina and died of his wounds. His posthumous son was Walter IV.

布里耶纳的戈蒂埃三世（法语名戈蒂埃，约1166—1205）是埃拉尔二世伯爵的长子，1191年袭任香槟地区的布里耶纳伯爵。1200年，他娶被废黜的西西里国王坦克雷迪之女埃尔薇拉为妻，筹备军队为她争夺西西里王位。

他参加第四次十字军，招募十字军战士加入他的意大利远征。教皇英诺森三世拒绝承认埃尔薇拉的王位主张，却承认夫妻二人对塔兰托和莱切的权利；1201年戈蒂埃在卡普阿和坎尼连获胜仗。

1205年6月，他在泰拉奇纳的营寨中遇刺，伤重身亡。其遗腹子即戈蒂埃四世。

en:
John of Randazzo (1317–1348) was the fourth son of Frederick III of Sicily and Eleanor of Anjou, and the most powerful nobleman in Sicily under his brother Peter II and his nephew Louis. In 1338 he received the duchy of Randazzo, and he also held the duchies of Athens and Neopatria and the county of Malta.

When Peter II died in 1342, John became regent for the young Louis. He favoured the Catalan party over the local Italian nobility, yet kept the kingdom at peace, and named the Catalan Blasco II de Alagona to succeed him.

He married Cesarea, daughter of the count of Castalnasetta, and their son Frederick became Duke of Athens after him. John died of the Black Death in 1348 and was buried beside his father and nephew in Catania cathedral. War broke out upon his death.

兰达佐的乔瓦尼（1317—1348）是西西里国王腓特烈三世与安茹的埃莉诺的第四子，在兄长皮埃特罗二世和侄子路易两朝都是岛上最有权势的贵族。1338年，他受封兰达佐公爵，并领有雅典与新帕特雷公爵领地及马耳他伯国。

1342年皮埃特罗二世去世后，他为年幼的路易摄政西西里。他相较本地意大利贵族更倚重加泰罗尼亚派，却维持了王国的和平，并指定加泰罗尼亚人布拉斯科二世·德·阿拉戈纳接任。

他娶卡斯塔尔纳塞塔伯爵之女切萨雷娅，儿子费德里科后来继任雅典公爵。1348年他死于黑死病，与父亲和侄子一同葬在卡塔尼亚大教堂。他一死，战争就爆发了。

en:
Henry (VII) (1211–1242) was the eldest son of the Emperor Frederick II and Constance of Aragon. Crowned king of Sicily in 1212, he was elected king of the Romans in 1220 and took personal rule of Germany in 1228. His pro-city policy angered the princes, forcing the Statutum in favorem principum at Worms in 1231.

Rebelling against his father, he surrendered in 1235 and was deposed and imprisoned. He died on 12 February 1242 after a fall from his horse.

en:
Helena Angelina Doukaina (c. 1242–1271) was a Byzantine princess, daughter of Michael II Komnenos Doukas, despot of Epirus. In 1259 she married King Manfred of Sicily, sealing an Epirote-Sicilian alliance; her dowry brought him Durazzo, Corfu and other Albanian towns.

After Manfred was killed at the Battle of Benevento in 1266, she tried to flee with her children but was seized by the Angevins. Charles I of Anjou imprisoned her at Nocera Inferiore, where she died in 1271.

Elisabeth of Sicily (c. 1310–1349) was a princess of the Sicilian House of Barcelona, daughter of King Frederick III and Eleanor of Anjou. In 1328 she was married to the underage Wittelsbach prince Stephen II of Bavaria, sealing her father's alliance with Emperor Louis IV.

Her four children included three sons who became dukes of Bavaria and a daughter who married King James I of Cyprus. When Stephen began ruling in 1347 she became duchess, but she died at Landshut in 1349.

Isabella II (1212–1228) was queen of Jerusalem from birth. Her mother died after she was born, and her father John of Brienne ruled during her minority. In 1225 she was crowned and married by proxy to the Emperor Frederick II, then joined him in Italy as empress and queen of Sicily.

Frederick at once claimed Jerusalem and excluded her from power. She died aged fifteen, days after bearing her only son Conrad.

en:
Conrad of Bavaria (Italian: Corrado di Baviera; c. 1105–17 March 1126) was a younger son of Duke Henry the Black of Bavaria and Wulfhilde of Saxony, born at the Welf castle of Ravensburg. He studied theology at Cologne before the preaching of Arnold the German drew him to the Cistercian Order at Morimond.

Arnold planned to found a monastery in the Holy Land but died in 1125, so Conrad continued alone, hoping to live as a hermit there. He settled instead in a cave at Modugno near Bari.

His holiness drew local followers before his death in 1126. His cult was confirmed by beatification in 1832, and he is patron of Molfetta.

阿诺德计划在圣地建立修道院，却于1125年去世，康拉德便独自继续前行，希望在圣地隐修。他最终在巴里附近莫杜尼奥的一处洞穴定居。

他以圣洁赢得当地人追随，于1126年去世。1832年他获宣福，是莫尔费塔的主保圣人。

en:
Manfred (1232–1266) was the last Hohenstaufen king of Sicily, the natural son of Emperor Frederick II and Bianca Lancia. He took the regency for his nephew Conradin in 1254.

After negotiating with Pope Innocent IV, he fled to Lucera and, with Muslim allies, defeated a papal army at Foggia that December. Excommunicated by successive popes, he had himself crowned king at Palermo in 1258 and championed the Ghibellines.

Pope Urban IV called in Charles of Anjou. Charles defeated and killed Manfred at the Battle of Benevento on 26 February 1266, seizing Sicily.

与教皇英诺森四世谈判后，他逃往卢切拉，同年12月在穆斯林盟友协助下于福贾击败教皇军队。他接连被数任教皇开除教籍，1258年在巴勒莫自行加冕为王，力挺吉伯林派。

en:
Margaret of Sicily (1331–1377) was a daughter of King Frederick III of Sicily and Eleanor of Anjou, born in Palermo. In 1348 she married the widowed Count Palatine Rudolf II of the Rhine, known as the Blind after eye disease left him sightless. The marriage was childless.

Rudolf withdrew in favour of his brother Rupert I, who gained the Palatinate's electoral dignity in 1356. Margaret survived him by over two decades and died at Neustadt an der Weinstraße in 1377.

en:
Marie of Brienne (c. 1224–1275), also called Marie d'Acre, was the daughter of John of Brienne, king of Jerusalem and Latin emperor of Constantinople, and Berengaria of León. In 1234 she married Baldwin II of Courtenay, her father's junior co-emperor, becoming Latin empress at about ten.

She governed Constantinople as regent during Baldwin's long fundraising journeys in the West in 1237–1239 and again from 1243, and later defended the Courtenay lands at Namur.

Her son Philip was born in 1243. She died in exile in 1275 after Constantinople fell to the Nicaeans in 1261.

In 1331 he led the duchies in their war against Walter VI of Brienne, who sought to reconquer Athens, and he held the vicariate until about 1335.

en:
Peter II of Sicily (1305–1342), eldest son of Frederick III and Eleanor of Anjou, was recognized as heir by the Sicilian parliament in 1314 and associated with his father's throne in 1321. He married Elisabeth of Carinthia in 1322 and ruled alone after Frederick died in 1337.

His reign saw feuds with leading baronial families and a naval defeat at Lipari against the Neapolitans in 1339. He died in 1342, leaving the crown to his son Louis.

Pietro Lancia was the second count of Caltanissetta in Aragonese Sicily. In 1299 he succeeded to the fiefs of his uncle Corrado Lancia, and grew into one of the island's richest feudatories, drawing more than a thousand ounces of gold a year from his lands.

By his wife, of the Alagona family, he had a daughter Cesarea, who married John, duke of Randazzo, in 1324. When he died in 1335 without a male heir, his county passed to the duke of Randazzo.

他娶阿拉戈纳家族之女为妻，女儿切萨雷亚于1324年嫁给兰扎佐公爵乔瓦尼。1335年他去世时没有男性继承人，伯爵领地遂归兰扎佐公爵所有。

en:
Raimondo Peralta (in Catalan Ramon de Peralta; c. 1292–1349) was a Sicilian nobleman and admiral in Aragonese service. He fought in the conquest of Sardinia in 1323; in 1325 he replaced Francesco Carroz as land commander, but the two hated each other and the king removed both. From 1326 he served his cousin King Frederick of Sicily against the Angevins.

Made grand admiral of Aragon in 1335, he defended Sardinia against Genoa and kept the Angevins from landing at Palermo. In 1338 he was invested with Caltabellotta as first count, and in 1340 became grand chancellor of Sicily.

In 1347 he invaded Naples and made peace with Queen Joanna I. He died at Palermo in 1349, while Latins and Catalans fought for control of Sicily.

拉伊蒙多·佩拉尔塔（加泰罗尼亚语作拉蒙·德·佩拉尔塔，约1292—1349）是为阿拉贡效力的西西里贵族与海军将领。1323年他参加阿拉贡征服撒丁岛之役；1325年接替弗朗切斯科·卡罗兹统率陆军，但两人互相敌视，国王遂免去二人的职务。1326年起他追随表亲西西里国王费德里科，对抗安茹家族。

1335年他出任阿拉贡海军元帅，率舰队保卫撒丁岛、抵御热那亚，并阻止安茹军队在巴勒莫登陆。1338年他受封卡尔塔贝洛塔，成为首任伯爵，1340年升任西西里大法官。

1347年他攻入那不勒斯王国，与女王乔万娜一世议和。1349年他卒于巴勒莫，当时拉丁人与加泰罗尼亚人正为控制西西里而争斗。

en:
Ramón de Vilaragut y Sarriá (c. 1295–c. 1359) was a Catalan noble of the Crown of Aragon who rose from Valencian squire to command Sicily's army and navy. About 1333 he married Grandiana, daughter of Stefano Visconti of Milan; their son Antonio was born in 1336.

In 1342 his brother Berenguer granted him Valencian lordships including Sollana. In 1344 John, Duke of Randazzo, regent for the young King Louis I of Sicily, gave him Tripi castle and barony.

In 1345 he became captain general and admiral of Sicily. He died around 1359, by which time Sollana belonged to his son Antonio.

拉蒙·德·维拉古特-萨里亚（约1295—约1359）是阿拉贡联合王国的加泰罗尼亚贵族，出身巴伦西亚侍从骑士，后来升任西西里的军队统帅兼海军司令。约1333年，他娶米兰贵族斯特凡诺·维斯孔蒂之女格兰迪亚娜为妻，1336年生子安东尼奥。

1342年，其兄贝伦格尔将包括索利亚纳在内的巴伦西亚领地封赐给他。1344年，年幼的西西里国王路易一世的摄政、兰达佐公爵乔万尼把特里皮城堡与男爵领赐给他。

1345年，他出任西西里军队统帅兼海军司令。约1359年去世，此时索利亚纳已归其子安东尼奥所有。

Rinaldo d'Este (1230–1251) was the only son of Azzo VII d'Este, Guelph lord of Ferrara. In 1239 his father gave him to the Emperor Frederick II as a hostage in pledge of loyalty. When Azzo joined the papal side, Rinaldo was imprisoned in Apulia, where he died, probably poisoned, in 1251.

His illegitimate son Obizzo was born around 1247 to a Neapolitan laundress. The boy was legitimised by Pope Innocent IV in 1252 and inherited Ferrara in 1264.

里纳尔多·德斯特（1230—1251年）是费拉拉的圭尔夫派领主阿佐七世·埃斯特的独子。1239年，父亲将他交予皇帝腓特烈二世作为效忠的人质。阿佐倒向教廷后，里纳尔多被囚禁于普利亚，1251年遇害，很可能死于毒杀。

他与一名那不勒斯洗衣女工所生的私生子奥比佐约生于1247年。这个孩子1252年获教宗英诺森四世承认为合法子嗣，1264年继承费拉拉。

en:
Ugo Lancia, also called Ugone (born c. 1299), was a Sicilian baron in the Messina area, son of Corrado Lancia di Castromainardo, founder of the Sicilian Lancia branch. Succeeding his father around 1328, he held the baronies of Ficarra and Longi, the castle of Brolo and other lordships.

In 1335 he held a fief near Piazza, and in 1340 he served as strategot, or royal governor, of Messina. His sons Blasco, Corrado and Nicola carried on the family's branches.

乌戈·兰恰又称乌戈内（约1299年生），是墨西拿地区的西西里男爵，为兰恰家族西西里支系始祖科拉多·兰恰·迪·卡斯特罗马伊纳尔多之子。约1328年袭爵后，他领有菲卡拉与隆吉男爵领地、布罗洛城堡及其他庄园。

en:
Sidi Ahmed Ou Moussa (c. 1460–1563) was a Moroccan Sufi sheikh of the Jazula confederation in the Anti-Atlas mountains of the Sous. He studied Islam in Marrakesh and travelled widely in the east before returning in 1521 to Tazerwalt, where he founded a zawiya that drew hundreds of disciples and gave rise to the Tazerwalt dynasty.

Keeping good relations with the ruling Saadian dynasty, he turned his religious authority into an enclave of power. He died in 1563, and his tomb in the zawiya became a pilgrimage site; his descendants inherited much of his wealth and standing.

西迪·艾哈迈德·乌·穆萨（约1460—1563）是摩洛哥苏斯地区反阿特拉斯山区贾祖拉部落联盟的苏菲谢赫。他早年在马拉喀什学习伊斯兰教，又长期游学东方，1521年返回塔泽尔瓦勒特定居，在那里建立扎维叶道堂，吸引了数百名弟子，塔泽尔瓦勒特王朝由此兴起。

他与当朝萨阿德王朝保持良好关系，凭宗教威望开辟出一片势力之地。他于1563年去世，道堂中的陵墓成为朝谒之地，子孙继承了他的大部分财富与地位。

en:
Jacopo Casali was the eldest-listed son of Ranieri II Casali, the first signore of Cortona, and is recorded as a condottiere. When his younger brother Bartolomeo succeeded to the signoria in 1351, Jacopo appears at first to have shared power with him before being pushed aside.

He then led a conspiracy against Bartolomeo, but the rising was crushed with considerable bloodshed; it was the last revolt against the Casali lords of Cortona in Bartolomeo's lifetime.

en:
Bolesław I the Tall (1127–1201), eldest son of Władysław II the Exile, fled to Germany when his father was driven from Poland in 1146. In 1163, through Frederick Barbarossa's intervention, he and his brother Mieszko Tanglefoot received Silesia, and Bolesław established himself at Wrocław. A 1172 revolt by Mieszko and his son forced him to divide the duchy and cede Opole.

He founded Lubiąż Abbey and was buried there after his death in 1201. His son Henry I the Bearded inherited Wrocław.

en:
Henry II the Pious (1196–1241), son of Henry I the Bearded and Saint Hedwig, married Anne, daughter of King Ottokar I of Bohemia, in 1218. He ruled during his father's 1229 captivity, became co-ruler in 1234, and in 1238 succeeded to Silesia, Kraków and the high-ducal title.

On 9 April 1241, at the Battle of Legnica, he led a Silesian and Greater Polish coalition against the Mongol invaders and was defeated and killed. His death undid his father's project of Piast reunification.

亨里克二世（“虔诚者”，1196—1241）是亨里克一世“大胡子”与圣海德维希之子，1218年娶波希米亚国王奥托卡一世之女安娜为妻。他在父亲1229年被囚期间代理政务，1234年成为共治者，1238年继位，领有西里西亚、克拉科夫与波兰大公头衔。

1241年4月9日，他率领西里西亚与大波兰联军在莱格尼察迎战蒙古大军，兵败战死。他的死使父亲统一皮亚斯特诸领地的事业付诸东流。

en:
Henry I the Bearded (c. 1165–1238), son of Bolesław I the Tall, ruled Silesia from Wrocław after 1201. In 1202 his uncle Mieszko Tanglefoot seized Opole, but Henry consolidated Lower Silesia, promoting mining and settlement; in 1211 Złotoryja became the first chartered town in Poland.

Married to Hedwig of Andechs, he took Kraków in 1232 amid the Piast succession wars and ruled as high duke of Poland. He died in 1238, leaving his realms to his son Henry II the Pious.

亨里克一世（“大胡子”，约1165—1238）是波列斯瓦夫一世（高个子）之子，1201年起以弗罗茨瓦夫为都统治西里西亚。1202年叔父梅什科“绊脚”夺取奥波莱，但亨里克巩固了下西里西亚，发展矿业并招徕移民；1211年兹沃托雷亚成为波兰第一座获得特许状的城市。

他娶安德希斯的海德维希为妻，乘皮亚斯特继承权战乱于1232年攻取克拉科夫，成为波兰大公。1238年他去世，领地由其子亨里克二世（“虔诚者”）继承。

en:
Casimir I of Opole (c. 1178–1230), only son of Mieszko IV Tanglefoot, ruled Opole and Racibórz from his father's death in 1211. He joined the junior Piast coalition, and in 1215 granted wide privileges to the Church. He later drew close to his cousin Henry I the Bearded, supporting his 1225 expedition against Kraków.

Casimir moved his residence to Opole and promoted German settlement under town law, chartering several towns including Leśnica in 1217. He died in May 1230.

卡齐米日一世（奥波莱的，约1178—1230）是梅什科四世“绊脚”的独子，1211年父亲去世后统治奥波莱与拉齐布日。他起初加入皮亚斯特少壮派同盟，1215年向教会授予广泛特权，后来与堂兄亨里克一世“大胡子”接近，支持其1225年征讨克拉科夫。

en:
Mieszko IV Tanglefoot (c. 1130–1211) was the second son of Władysław II the Exile and grew up in exile after 1146. The brothers recovered Silesia through Frederick Barbarossa's intervention in 1163 and ruled it jointly until 1173, when Mieszko took Racibórz as his duchy.

He added Opole in 1202, founding the Opole line of the Silesian Piasts. In 1210 he captured Kraków and assumed the high-ducal title of Poland, and died there in 1211, leaving Opole-Racibórz to his son Casimir I.

en:
Władysław II the Exile (1105–1159), eldest son of Bolesław III Wrymouth, was high duke of Poland and duke of Silesia from 1138 under his father's settlement. His bid to centralize power brought war with his younger half-brothers; after he blinded their ally, the brothers expelled him from Poland in 1146.

He took refuge with his wife's imperial kindred and died in exile in 1159. His sons recovered Silesia in 1163, becoming the founders of the Silesian Piasts.

en:
Simon Le Moyne (1604–1665), a Jesuit born at Beauvais, reached New France in 1638 and worked among the Wendat until their dispersal drove him back to Quebec in 1650. Fluent in Wendat and Haudenosaunee, he became New France's chief peace envoy to the Iroquois.

In 1653 he travelled to Onondaga Lake, founded the Sainte Marie de Gannentaha mission and discovered the Onondaga salt springs. He negotiated with the Mohawks and returned in 1662 with nineteen freed captives, and died of fever near Trois-Rivières in 1665.

西蒙·勒穆瓦纳（1604—1665）是出生于博韦的耶稣会士，1638年抵达新法兰西，多年在休伦人地区传教；1650年休伦联盟覆灭后，他退回魁北克。他精通休伦语与易洛魁语，成为新法兰西派往易洛魁联盟的首席和平使节。

en:
Simon Stevin (1548–1620) was a Flemish mathematician and engineer, born probably in Bruges. After working as a clerk in Bruges, he moved north in 1581 and enrolled at Leiden University in 1583. At Leiden he befriended Maurice of Nassau and became his tutor and principal adviser, director of the Dutch water works from 1592 and quartermaster-general of the States-General's army.

He coined a native Dutch word for mathematics and translated other scientific terms into Dutch, proved the law of equilibrium on the inclined plane, and built a wind-driven land carriage that outran horses on the coastal sands.

西蒙·斯泰芬（1548—1620）是弗拉芒数学家与工程师，可能生于布鲁日。他在布鲁日做过书记员，1581年北上，1583年入读莱顿大学。他在莱顿结识拿骚的莫里斯，后来成为他的教师和首席顾问，1592年起主管荷兰的水利事务，并任联省军队的军需总监。

他用荷兰语本族词为数学命名，也将其他科学术语译成荷兰语；他还证明了斜面上的平衡定律，造出一辆风力陆地车，在海滩上跑得比马还快。

Aymon de Châtillon (c. 1260–1323) was a Valdostan cleric of a cadet branch of the Challant lords. A canon of Aosta and Sion, he was elected bishop of Sion in 1308 after his cousin Boniface de Challant, becoming a prince of the Empire and count of the Valais.

In December 1308 he exchanged homages with the count of Savoy, and he defeated Bernese Oberland lords who had invaded the Upper Valais. He died at Sion on 19 July 1323.

en:
Aymon de La Tour, called Aymon IV of Châtillon (d. 1338), was a Valais cleric of a baronial family, son of Pierre IV de La Tour. Pope John XXII named him bishop of Sion in 1323, and the next year he sold Laupen to Bern.

He defended his see's autonomy against the counts of Savoy, allying with the Dauphin Guigues VIII in 1327 before rendering only limited homage on the Morge. He died at Sion in April 1338.

en:
Boniface de Challant (c. 1240–1308) was a Valdostan cleric of the Challant family, appointed bishop of Sion by the pope in 1289 and consecrated in 1290. He ruled the see like a fief, building Tourbillon above Sion, and in 1293 demanded liege homage from Count Amadeus V of Savoy for Chillon.

From 1294 he warred on his neighbors, razing Riddes before making peace with Savoy in 1301. He founded the hospice of Brigue in 1304 and died at Sion in June 1308.

1294年起他接连与邻邦交战，荡平里德斯要塞，最终于1301年与萨伏依议和。他1304年创办布里格救济院，1308年6月在锡永去世。

en:
Skanderbeg, born Gjergj Kastrioti (c. 1405–1468), was the Albanian nobleman who led the longest resistance to the Ottomans in the Balkans. Sent as a hostage to the Ottoman court, he served Sultan Murad II for twenty years. The Turks called him İskender Bey, a comparison with Alexander the Great. In 1443 he deserted, seized Krujë and returned to Christianity.

In 1444 he gathered the Albanian houses at Lezhë into the League of Lezhë. That summer, on the plain of Torvioll, hidden cavalry encircled Ali Pasha's army, one of the few Ottoman defeats in a pitched battle on European soil. For twenty-five years he fought using the mountains for hit-and-run raids, and the sieges of Krujë failed in 1450 and 1466.

He fell ill in January 1468, probably of malaria, and died. Krujë starved and surrendered to Mehmed II in 1478, and Naples gave his family lands in southern Italy.

斯坎德培（约1405—1468），本名杰尔吉·卡斯特里奥蒂，是巴尔干地区抵抗奥斯曼时间最长的阿尔巴尼亚贵族。他少年时作为人质送入奥斯曼宫廷，为苏丹穆拉德二世效力二十年。土耳其人称他伊斯肯德尔贝伊，意即把他比作亚历山大大帝。1443年他叛逃、夺取克鲁亚并重新皈依基督教。

1444年他在莱什召集阿尔巴尼亚各家族组成莱什联盟。同年夏天在托尔维奥尔平原，伏兵骑兵合围阿里帕夏的军队，这是奥斯曼在欧洲土地上少有的阵地战败仗之一。二十五年间他利用山地打游击战，克鲁亚在1450年和1466年的大围攻中坚守不失。

1468年1月他病倒，可能是疟疾，不久去世。克鲁亚后来在饥饿中于1478年向穆罕默德二世投降，那不勒斯则把意大利南部的土地赐给了他的家族。

en:
Zayd, known as al-Aṣghar (the Younger) and styled ʿIzz al-Dīn, was a son of the Hasanid Emir of Mecca, Abu Numayy I. Medieval Arab genealogical and chronicle sources record him as sultan of Suakin on the African shore of the Red Sea, then as a naqib, or head, of the Talibid sayyids in Iraq.

In 698 AH, that is 1298–1299, he travelled there from the Hijaz. The ruling sultan granted him a landed estate at al-Hilla.

小扎伊德，尊号伊兹丁，是麦加哈桑系埃米尔阿布·努米一世之子。据阿拉伯谱系与编年史文献记载，他先在红海非洲沿岸的萨瓦金称苏丹，后来前往伊拉克，出任塔利卜家族圣裔的纳基卜（首领）。

伊斯兰历698年（1298—1299年）他从汉志抵达伊拉克，当政的苏丹把希拉的一处田庄封赐给他。

en: Ban Sen (born 1301) was the twelfth raja of Suket in the Punjab Hills. Born posthumously after his father Kranchan Sen died fighting Kullu, he was adopted by his maternal grandfather and ruled 1301–1346. Tradition credits him with the Parashara temple at Prashar Lake.

en: Dmitry Fyodorovich (d. 1354) was the fifth appanage prince of Starodub-on-the-Klyazma and a Rurikid, the eldest son of Prince Fyodor Ivanovich. He succeeded in 1330 after his father was killed in the Golden Horde and ruled until 1354 or the following year. He was buried at Starodub, and left sons Semyon Krapiva and Fyodor, ancestor of the Mikitinichi-Ryapolovsky princes.

en:
Fyodor Ivanovich, called the Pious, was the fourth prince of Starodub-on-the-Klyazma, succeeding his father Ivan Mikhailovich in 1315. The chronicles record only one event of his life: in 1330 he was killed at the court of the Golden Horde, under unknown circumstances.

Venerated as a martyr for the Orthodox faith, he was canonized as a holy prince and buried at Aleksino, where his relics were said to heal the sick.

en:
Ivan Mikhailovich, known as Kalistrat, was the third appanage prince of Starodub-on-the-Klyazma. The only son of Mikhail Ivanovich, he inherited the appanage from his father in 1281 and ruled until about 1315.

The chronicles record almost nothing of his reign and disagree on the date of his death. His only son Fyodor Ivanovich, later canonized as a holy prince, succeeded him.

Ivan Vsevolodovich, nicknamed Kasha, was the youngest son of Vsevolod the Big Nest, grand prince of Vladimir. After Batu's invasion, Grand Prince Yaroslav in 1238 granted him the devastated Starodub as his appanage, making him its first prince.

In 1246 he accompanied Yaroslav to the Golden Horde, and he died in 1247, leaving Starodub to his son Mikhail; he was buried in the Dormition Cathedral at Vladimir.

Mikhail Ivanovich was the second appanage prince of Starodub, succeeding his father Ivan Vsevolodovich Kasha. In 1281 he answered the summons of Andrey Alexandrovich, who with Tatar support advanced on Murom to seize Vladimir from his elder brother Dmitry.

Mikhail joined Andrey's brutal campaign against Pereyaslavl-Zalessky and probably died during it; the Nikon chronicle gives 1281 as his death year. His son Ivan Kalistrat carried on the Starodub line.

米哈伊尔·伊万诺维奇是第二代斯塔罗杜布藩王，继父亲伊凡·弗谢沃洛多维奇·卡沙之后统治。1281年，安德烈·亚历山德罗维奇在鞑靼人支持下进兵穆罗姆，要从兄长德米特里手中夺取弗拉基米尔，米哈伊尔响应其征召。

他加入了安德烈攻打佩列亚斯拉夫尔-扎列斯基的残酷征战，很可能就死在这场兵乱之中；《尼康编年史》系其卒年于1281年。其子伊凡·卡利斯特拉特延续了斯塔罗杜布世系。

en:
Vladimir Vsevolodovich (1192–1227), baptized Dmitry, was a son of Vsevolod the Big Nest of Vladimir and prince first of Pereyaslavl and then of Starodub. In the brothers' war after 1212 he held Moscow for Konstantin against Yuri, then withdrew to Pereyaslavl, where he married a Chernigov princess.

Captured by the Cumans in 1215, he was freed in 1218 and received Starodub. He died in January 1227 after taking the schema, and Starodub then reverted to Vladimir's grand princes.

Simon I ruled as Count of Upper Salm from 1332. He was the son of Count John I of Salm and Jeanne de Joinville, and in 1334, at Commercy, he married Mathilde of Saarbrücken, daughter of Count Simon V of Saarbrücken-Commercy.

Their son John, born around 1335, later ruled as Count John II of Salm. Simon was killed at the Battle of Crécy in France in 1346.

en:
John II (German: Johann II; c. 1335–c. 1400) was Count of Upper Salm in the Vosges and of Chiny, succeeding his father Simon I, who fell fighting for the French at Crécy in 1346. In May 1355 he married Philippa of Heinsberg-Valkenburg.

Their children included Simon II, lord of Born, who married Marie of Luxembourg and died in 1397, and two daughters, Odile and Mathilda, who married into the Wassenaar-Polanen and Hunolstein families.

His son John later succeeded as count of Upper Salm and fell at the Battle of Bulgnéville in 1431. John II himself died between 1386 and 1400.

en:
Hugo von Dürrach was Schultheiss (chief magistrate) of the imperial city of Solothurn for the office years 1335/36 and 1346/47, alternating in the post with his kinsman Konrad von Dürrach.

The Dürrach knights were one of the city's leading families and followed a broadly pro-Bern policy; Johann, Konrad II and Henmann von Dürrach all later served as Schultheiss, and in 1347 the family acquired the Vogtei over Derendingen.

en:
Konrad von Dürrach was Schultheiss (chief magistrate) of the imperial city of Solothurn in 1328/29–1333/34 and again in 1336/37–1339/40, when the office was a pawned imperial fief before passing to election by the citizenry around 1344. Other members of the Dürrach family held the same office down to 1411 and led the city's pro-Bern party.

During Konrad's second tenure Solothurn troops marched in Bern's relief army and fought at Laupen on 21 June 1339, when the allies raised the eleven-day siege by the army of Freiburg, the bishop of Basel and the Burgundian lords.

Friedrich von Leibnitz (died 30 March 1338), from a Salzburg ministerial family, was cathedral provost when elected Prince-Archbishop of Salzburg in 1315; he was consecrated at Avignon in 1316.

He allied Salzburg with Austria against Bavaria, and at the Battle of Mühldorf in 1322 Duke Frederick of Austria and many Salzburg knights were captured; Salzburg paid heavy reparations. In 1328 he issued Salzburg's first provincial ordinance and ruled until his death in 1338.

Jam Unar (died 1352) was the founder of the Samma dynasty and the first sultan of Sindh. In 1333 he rebelled against Malik Rattan, governor of Sehwan, killed him in single combat and seized the city, though Delhi soon retook it.

In 1351 he joined the Soomra rulers against Muhammad bin Tughluq, then expelled the last Soomra, Hamir, and was elected ruler of Sindh by the Samma and Soomra chiefs. He died the next year.

en:
Hrelja, known in Balkan epic as Relja Krilatica, the Winged One (died 1342), was a Serbian magnate who served kings Milutin, Dečanski and Dušan from Štip and Strumica. In 1334–1335 he rebuilt the church of Rila Monastery, adding the defensive tower named after him.

In the late 1330s, from a border domain between Serbia, Bulgaria and Byzantium, he broke away and ruled from Strumica, formally recognising Byzantine authority. In the next Byzantine civil war he backed John VI Kantakouzenos, who gave him Melnik and the title protosebastos. When Kantakouzenos fled to Dušan's court in 1342 and gave up his ally for Serbian help, Hrelja submitted to Dušan again and ceded Melnik.

He died at Rila on 27 December 1342, tonsured as the monk Hariton and buried in the church he had rebuilt; Bulgarian tradition blames Serb mercenaries hired by Dušan.

zh:
赫雷利亚（？—1342）在巴尔干史诗中被称为“翼人”雷利亚·克里拉蒂察，是塞尔维亚大贵族，以什蒂普和斯特鲁米察一带为领地，先后效力于米卢丁、德钱斯基和杜尚三位国王。1334—1335年，他重修里拉修道院的教堂，增建了以他名字命名的防御塔楼。

1330年代末，他凭借夹在塞尔维亚、保加利亚与拜占庭之间的边境领地脱离塞尔维亚，以斯特鲁米察为中心统治，名义上承认拜占庭权威。下一场拜占庭内战中，他支持约翰六世·坎塔库泽努斯，获封梅尔尼克和“首席塞巴斯托斯”头衔。1342年坎塔库泽努斯逃到杜尚的宫廷，为换取塞尔维亚援助舍弃盟友，赫雷利亚只得重新臣服杜尚并交出梅尔尼克。

同年12月27日，他在里拉修道院去世，不久前出家，法名哈里顿，葬在他重修的教堂里；保加利亚的说法是，他死于杜尚雇来的塞尔维亚雇佣兵之手。

1330年代末，他凭借夹在塞尔维亚、[GetCountry('BUL').GetName]与[GetCountry('BYZ').GetName]之间的边境领地脱离塞尔维亚，以斯特鲁米察为中心统治，名义上承认拜占庭权威。下一场拜占庭内战中，他支持#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('byz_john_kantakouzenos').GetID],X #L 约翰六世·坎塔库泽努斯#!#!，获封梅尔尼克和“首席塞巴斯托斯”头衔。1342年坎塔库泽努斯逃到杜尚的宫廷，为换取塞尔维亚援助舍弃盟友，赫雷利亚只得重新臣服杜尚并交出梅尔尼克。

同年12月27日，他在里拉修道院去世，不久前出家，法名哈里顿，葬在他重修的教堂里；保加利亚的说法是，他死于杜尚雇来的塞尔维亚雇佣兵之手。

en:
Beka I Jaqeli (c. 1242–1308) succeeded his father Sargis I in 1285 as prince of Samtskhe, the Jaqeli domain in southern Georgia. A vassal of the Mongol Il-Khans, he paid them tribute while ruling independently of the Georgian crown and fending off Turkish raids.

He married his daughter Jiajak to the Trapezuntine emperor Alexios II, and another daughter, Natela, to King Demetrius II of Georgia; Natela's son George V was raised at Beka's court after the Mongols executed Demetrius.

zh:
贝卡一世·贾克利（约1242—1308）于1285年继承父亲萨尔吉斯一世，成为格鲁吉亚南部萨姆茨赫的贾克利领地王公。他向蒙古伊尔汗国称臣纳贡，同时脱离格鲁吉亚王权独立统治，还击退了土耳其人的袭扰。

他把女儿贾贾克嫁给特拉比松皇帝阿莱克修斯二世，另一个女儿娜特拉嫁给格鲁吉亚国王德米特里二世；蒙古人处死德米特里后，娜特拉之子吉奥尔基五世在贝卡的宫廷中长大。

en:
Beka II Jaqeli (1332–1391) became atabeg of Samtskhe in 1361, succeeding his father Qvarqvare I, and was confirmed in office by his kinsman King Bagrat V of Georgia. From 1372 he ruled Meskheti jointly with his brother Shalva, until Shalva's death in 1389.

During Timur's invasions of Georgia Beka's authority collapsed, and he abandoned Bagrat and surrendered to Timur. He died in 1391, leaving the throne to his son Ivane II.

en:
Jiajak Jaqeli was a Georgian princess, daughter of Beka I Jaqeli, the atabeg of Samtskhe, and empress consort of Alexios II of Trebizond. They married around 1300, although the Byzantine emperor Andronikos II, Alexios's guardian, pressed the patriarch to annul the match; the patriarch refused, as Jiajak was already reported to be pregnant.

Her sons Andronikos III and Basil both became Trapezuntine emperors, and her daughter Anna Anachoutlou ruled Trebizond in 1341–1342. Alexios died in 1330; her own death date is unrecorded.

贾贾克·贾克利是格鲁吉亚公主，萨姆茨赫阿塔贝格贝卡一世·贾克利之女，特拉比松皇帝阿历克塞二世的皇后。两人约于1300年成婚；阿历克塞的监护人、拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡二世要求牧首宣布婚姻无效，但牧首以贾贾克据称已有身孕为由拒绝。

en:
Natela Jaqeli was a princess of Samtskhe, a daughter of Prince Beka I Jaqeli, and queen consort of Georgia as the wife of King Demetrius II. She gave birth to George, the future King George V, later called the Brilliant.

After the Mongols executed Demetrius in 1289, the young boy was raised at his grandfather Beka I's court in Samtskhe, and he later returned from there to rule Georgia. Natela died after 1289.

en:
Qvarqvare I Jaqeli (1298–1361) was a Georgian prince and atabeg of Samtskhe. He was the son of Atabeg Sargis II and a grandson of Beka I Jaqeli.

When his father died in 1334, he submitted to George V the Brilliant and received Samtskhe as atabeg, ending its separation from the Georgian crown under Ilkhanid rule since 1266. He ruled until his death in 1361, when his son Beka II succeeded him.

en:
Sargis I Jaqeli (died 1285) was the first sovereign prince of Samtskhe and founder of the Jaqeli principality. As spasalar of Samtskhe he served King David VII and in 1260 led rebels against Mongol general Arghun Aqa.

In 1266 Samtskhe gained crown-land status under direct Mongol suzerainty, virtually detaching it from the Georgian crown, and Sargis became its sovereign prince in 1268. Late in life he took the monastic name Saba and was succeeded by his son Beka I.

萨尔吉斯一世·贾克利（1285年卒）是萨姆茨赫第一位独立王公，也是贾克利政权的奠基人。他曾任萨姆茨赫军事长官，效力于大卫七世国王，1260年率起义军迎战蒙古将领阿儿浑·阿合。

en:
Sargis II Jaqeli (1271–1334) was prince of Samtskhe from 1308 until his death, the son of Beka I Jaqeli. During his father's reign he commanded the Samtskhe army against Anatolian Turkoman raiders, checking them near Vashlovani in the 1290s and expelling them around 1303.

After Beka's death in 1308 he succeeded to the principality, and his nephew King George V the Brilliant of Georgia named him Amirspasalar and Atabeg of the kingdom. His son Qvarqvare succeeded him.

en:
Alexander Glebovich (died 1313), eldest son of Gleb Rostislavich, was grand prince of Smolensk. He held Mstislavl from 1278 and may have ruled Smolensk while his uncle Fyodor the Black tarried in the Golden Horde; in 1297 the townsmen enthroned him, and Fyodor failed to dislodge him the next year.

In 1300 he and his brother Roman were defeated at Dorogobuzh by their cousin Andrey Mikhailovich, and one of his sons was killed. After Oleg of Bryansk died, he installed his son Vasily there. He died in 1313, succeeded by his son Ivan.

en:
Davyd Rostislavich (1140–1197), fourth son of Rostislav Mstislavich, was prince of Smolensk from 1180 until his death. After holding towns including Vyshhorod from 1167, he fought in the 1169 sack of Kiev and the nine-week defence of Vyshhorod in 1173. In 1176 the Cumans defeated him near Rostovets, a reverse recalled in The Tale of Igor's Campaign.

His Smolensk reign brought campaigns against the Cumans and the Olgovichi and defeat near Vitebsk in 1196. He died a monk in April 1197.

In 1176 the Cumans defeated him near Rostovets, a reverse recalled in The Tale of Igor's Campaign.

His Smolensk reign brought campaigns against the Cumans and the Olgovichi and defeat near Vitebsk in 1196. He died a monk in April 1197.

en:
Davyd Igorevich (c. 1058–1112) was a Volhynian prince, son of Igor Yaroslavich and grandson of Yaroslav the Wise. Left fatherless as an izgoi, he seized Tmutarakan in 1081, then blockaded the Dnieper mouth until Vsevolod granted him Dorogobuzh in 1084; he received Volhynia in 1086.

The 1097 Liubech congress confirmed Volhynia to him, but for arresting and blinding Prince Vasilko the 1100 Uvetichi congress deprived him of Vladimir. He founded Davyd-Gorodok and died at Dorogobuzh in 1112.

en:
Gleb Rostislavich (died 1278) was prince of Smolensk from the 1240s, a son of Rostislav Mstislavich, considered the ancestor of the later Smolensk princely line. He probably succeeded around 1249 after Vsevolod Mstislavich died. In 1270 he campaigned against Novgorod with Yaroslav Yaroslavich of Vladimir.

In 1274 he joined a Golden Horde campaign against Lithuania organized by Khan Mengu-Timur, then marched on Tatar orders against Galicia; the campaign marked Smolensk's submission to the Horde, and the first Tatar census followed in 1275. Gleb died in 1278 and was succeeded by his brother Mikhail.

en:
Igor Yaroslavich (c. 1036–1060) was a younger son of Yaroslav the Wise. Under his father's testament of 1054 he received the Volhynian principality, but in 1057, after his brother Vyacheslav died in Smolensk, the senior Yaroslavichi transferred Igor to the Smolensk throne and gave Volhynia to their nephew Rostislav Vladimirovich.

He died in 1060 aged twenty-four, leaving the young sons Davyd and Vsevolod, who were ruled izgoi and barred from succeeding him.

Ivan Aleksandrovich (died 1359) was grand prince of Smolensk, succeeding his father Alexander Glebovich in 1313. His brother Dmitry of Bryansk disputed the throne and besieged Smolensk with Tatar aid in 1334 before making peace.

In 1339 he allied with Gediminas of Lithuania and stopped paying tribute to the Golden Horde, and in 1340 Öz Beg Khan's army failed to storm Smolensk. In 1348 Smolensk regiments fought for Lithuania, but a campaign from Moscow in 1351 forced him to renounce the alliance. He died in 1359.

Konstantin Davidovich (c. 1184–1218) was a Smolensk Rurikid, the younger son of Davyd Rostislavich. When his father died in 1197, he was entrusted to his uncle Rurik Rostislavich in the Kyiv land, who presumably granted him an appanage, though no chronicle names his throne.

Polish chronicles record that he joined a campaign against Lithuania in 1207. He died in 1217 or 1218, and later genealogical tradition makes him ancestor of the princes of Fomin and Berezuysk.

Mstislav Davidovich (baptized Fyodor; died 1230) was prince of Smolensk from 1219, the son of Davyd Rostislavich. He campaigned against Lithuania in 1207 and in 1217 defeated Lithuanian raiders near Polotsk. In 1219, when Vladimir Rurikovich moved to Ovruch, he took the Smolensk throne.

Smolensk regiments fought at the Kalka River in 1223, and his reign brought a trade treaty with Riga and Gotland. He died in 1230 and was succeeded by his son Rostislav, though two years later his cousin's son Sviatoslav Mstislavich seized the city with Polotsk aid.

en:
Rostislav Mstislavich (born 1189; died in or after 1240/1249) was a Smolensk Rurikid, son of Mstislav Davidovich and ancestor of the later Smolensk princely line. He took the Smolensk throne after his father's death in 1230 but was expelled in 1232 by his cousin Sviatoslav Mstislavich with an army of Polotsk princes.

He may be the Rostislav who entered Kiev in 1239 during the Mongol invasion, after Mikhail Vsevolodovich fled to Hungary, and claimed the grand-princely title. Daniel of Galicia soon drove the claimant out and installed his voivode Dmytro there. Rostislav's sons Gleb, Mikhail and Fyodor the Black later all ruled Smolensk.

罗斯季斯拉夫·姆斯季斯拉维奇（1189年生，卒于1240/1249年或之后）是斯摩棱斯克系留里克王公、姆斯季斯拉夫·达维多维奇之子，是后世斯摩棱斯克王公一系的始祖。1230年父亲死后他继位，1232年被堂亲斯维亚托斯拉夫·姆斯季斯拉维奇借波洛茨克军队驱逐。

有说法认为他就是1239年蒙古入侵、米哈伊尔·弗谢沃洛多维奇逃往匈牙利后进入基辅自称大公的罗斯季斯拉夫。加利西亚的丹尼尔很快赶走争位者，以长官德米特里镇守基辅。其子格列布、米哈伊尔和“黑者”费奥多尔后来都统治过斯摩棱斯克。

en:
Stanislav Vladimirovich (c. 984/987–probably before 1015) was a younger son of Vladimir the Great of Kyiv. The later Nikon Chronicle records that around 988 he received Smolensk as his appanage, making him its first Rurikid prince; he is also the only pre-Mongol Rurikid known to have borne the name Stanislav.

Chronicles mention him solely in lists of Vladimir's sons, third from the last, and preserve no deeds of his. He probably died before his father, who died in 1015.

史书只在弗拉基米尔诸子名单中提到他，列倒数第三，没有留下任何事迹。他很可能先于1015年去世的父亲而亡。

Vyacheslav Yaroslavich (1036–1057) was a younger son of Yaroslav the Wise of Kyiv. On Yaroslav's death in 1054 he received the Principality of Smolensk in the division of the lands, but he ruled there for only three years before he died. Almost nothing else is recorded of him.

He left a son, Boris Vyacheslavich, who in 1077 laid claim to the Principality of Chernigov during the wars between Yaroslav's sons and was killed fighting in 1078.

维亚切斯拉夫·雅罗斯拉维奇（1036—1057）是基辅大公“智者”雅罗斯拉夫的幼子之一。1054年雅罗斯拉夫去世、诸子分割领地时，他分得斯摩棱斯克公国，但仅统治三年便去世。史籍对他的其他事迹几乎毫无记载。

en:
Johann Clare (died 5 May 1344), born to a burgher family of Thorn in Prussia, was a Teutonic Order priest who became a Samland canon in 1294 and cathedral dean in 1301.

After Bishop Siegfried of Regenstein died in 1310 the chapter unanimously elected him, but quarrels with Riga's archbishop and the Curia delayed his appointment until Pope John XXII gave him the see in 1319.

From 1320 he sought to recover church rights and lands seized by the order, securing only part of his claims. He oversaw construction of the new Königsberg Cathedral until his death in 1344.

约翰·克拉雷（？—1344年5月5日）出身于普鲁士托伦老城的市民家庭，是条顿骑士团神父，1294年成为萨姆兰教士团成员，1301年任主教座堂总铎。

1310年主教西格弗里德·冯·雷根施泰因去世后，教士团一致推选克拉雷接任，但他与里加大主教及教廷的争执使任命久拖不决，直到1319年教皇约翰二十二世才正式将教区授予他。

1320年起，他向骑士团追讨被侵占的教会权利与地产，只实现了部分诉求。他主持修建新的柯尼斯堡主教座堂，1344年卒于柯尼斯堡。

en:
Rajanarayana Sambuvarayar was a Tamil chief of the Sambuvarayar family who became an independent ruler of Tondaimandalam as the Hoysala and Pandya kingdoms crumbled. From 1337 he issued records in his own regnal years and held Kanchi with his fortress at Padaiveedu.

Around 1350 a Vijayanagara army led by Vira Savanna defeated him, then restored him as a vassal. He died around 1362, after which renewed Vijayanagara campaigns destroyed his power and annexed Tondaimandalam.

罗阇那罗延·三补缚罗耶尔是三补缚罗耶尔家族的泰米尔首领，在曷萨拉与潘地亚王国衰微之际成为通达曼达拉姆的独立统治者。自1337年起，他以自己的王年发布铭文，领有甘吉布勒姆，并以波代维杜为要塞。

约1350年，维拉·萨万纳率领毗奢耶那伽罗军队将他击败，随后又扶他复位，作为附庸。他约于1362年去世，此后毗奢耶那伽罗再度用兵，消灭其势力，吞并通达曼达拉姆。

en:
Sang Nila Utama, a prince of Palembang, is portrayed in the Malay Annals as the founder of the Kingdom of Singapura. He spotted Temasek across the sea; in 1299, sailing there, he was caught in a storm and cast his crown into the sea before reaching the island. There his minister identified a beast as a lion, an omen that led him to build a city and name the island Singapura, Sanskrit for Lion City.

He took the title Sri Tri Buana and ruled Singapura until his death in 1347. His son Sri Wikrama Wira succeeded him.

桑·尼拉·乌他玛原是巨港的王子，《马来纪年》称他为新加坡王国的建立者。他望见海对面的淡马锡；1299年前往该岛途中遭遇风暴，将王冠投入大海后才得以登陆。岛上大臣把一头异兽指认为狮子，他视为吉兆，便在此筑城，并以梵语“狮子城”之意将岛屿命名为新加坡拉。

他采用室利·特里·布瓦纳的尊号，统治新加坡拉至1347年去世，其子斯里·维克拉玛·维拉继位。

en:
Sri Wikrama Wira, eldest son of Sang Nila Utama, was the second Raja of Singapura, ruling from 1347 to 1362. He married Nila Panjadi, a princess from India.

His reign saw the first Siamese attempt to subdue the island: as the Malay Annals relate, a fleet of seventy junks besieged it, an episode recorded by the Chinese traveller Wang Dayuan in 1349. The fortified city held out until Chinese ships appeared and the Siamese withdrew.

The next threat came from Majapahit. In 1350 its king sent an envoy demanding submission; Sri Wikrama Wira refused, threatening to shave the king's head if he came. The Javanese fleet of 180 warships met 400 Singaporean ships, and after three days of fighting the inexperienced Javanese were routed.

斯里·维克拉玛·维拉是桑·尼拉·乌他玛的长子，新加坡王国第二任拉惹，1347至1362年在位。他娶印度公主尼拉·潘贾迪为妻。

他在位时，暹罗首次试图征服该岛：据《马来纪年》记载，一支拥有70艘大船的舰队围攻此地，中国旅行家汪大渊于1349年记录了此事。设防坚固的城池坚守不退，直到中国船只出现，暹罗人才撤围。

接着，满者伯夷成了下一个威胁。1350年其国王派使者要求新加坡臣服；斯里·维克拉玛·维拉拒绝，还回话威胁说，如果爪哇王敢来，就剃光他的头。爪哇的180艘战舰与新加坡的400艘战船交锋三日，不谙水战的爪哇人溃败而逃。

en:
The Malay Annals call Wan Sri Bini the daughter of the widowed Queen Permaisuri Iskandar Syah of Bentan on Bintan Island.

The queen married her to the Palembang prince Sang Nila Utama, giving the groom a golden crown set with gems and a royal signet ring; by the marriage he became raja of Bentan before founding Singapura. She bore his sons Raja Kechil-Besar, who ruled as Sri Wikrama Wira, and Raja Kechil-Muda, the kingdom's chief minister.

据《马来纪年》记载，宛·室利·比妮是宾坦岛本坦国寡居女王伊斯干达沙的女儿。

女王将她嫁给巨港王子桑·尼拉·乌他玛，随婚赐给女婿镶宝金冠与王印戒指；他由此成为本坦之主，此后才建国新加坡拉。她生下拉惹·吉兹尔-贝萨尔和拉惹·吉兹尔-穆达两子，前者以斯里·维克拉玛·维拉之名统治新加坡拉，后者出任首席大臣。

en:
Sogai (died 1296) was a Mongol prince of the Ilkhanate, the son of Hulagu's son Yoshmut. In 1295 he commanded an army of his cousin Ghazan in the campaign that overthrew Ilkhan Baydu and placed Ghazan on the throne.

When the Chagatai khan Duwa invaded Khorasan late that year, Sogai was sent against him but deserted, convinced the expedition was a plot by the emir Nawruz. He was seized and executed on Ghazan's orders in 1296.

唆海（？—1296）是伊儿汗国的蒙古宗王，为旭烈兀之子玉疏木忒之子。1295年，堂兄合赞起兵推翻伊儿汗拜都，唆海统领一军助合赞夺取汗位。

同年末，察合台汗笃哇入侵呼罗珊，唆海奉命迎击，却因怀疑此行是异密捏吾鲁兹设下的圈套而弃军逃走。1296年，合赞下令将他处死。

Blas de Lezo (1689–1741) was a Spanish admiral born near San Sebastián. Entering the navy in 1701, he lost his left leg at Vélez-Málaga in 1704, his left eye at the defence of Toulon in 1707 and the use of his right arm at the Siege of Barcelona in 1714. He served in the Pacific and helped recapture Oran in 1732.

In 1741 he defended Cartagena de Indias with a few thousand men against Edward Vernon's British fleet of nearly 200 ships and 27 thousand troops, forcing the British to withdraw. He died of typhus four months after the victory.

布拉斯·德莱索（1689—1741）是出生于圣塞瓦斯蒂安附近的西班牙海军上将。他1701年入伍，1704年在贝莱斯-马拉加海战中失去左腿，1707年守卫土伦时失去左眼，1714年在巴塞罗那围城战中右臂致残。他曾在太平洋服役，1732年协助收复奥兰。

1741年，他以数千之众守卫卡塔赫纳-德印第亚斯，抵御爱德华·弗农麾下近200艘舰船、2.7万人的英国舰队，迫使英军撤退。获胜四个月后，他死于斑疹伤寒。

en:
Francisco de Goya (1746–1828) was a Spanish painter and printmaker, often called the last of the Old Masters and the first of the moderns. Born at Fuendetodos in Aragon, he worked in Madrid and became a court painter in 1786 and Primer Pintor de Cámara in 1799. He painted Charles IV and His Family and the daring Naked Maja.

A severe illness in 1793 left him deaf, and his work grew darker; the Caprichos etchings dwell on madness, witches and corruption. He stayed in Madrid through Napoleon's 1807 invasion, and his Disasters of War prints and the 1814 painting The Third of May 1808 show war without heroism.

From 1819, living in isolation at the Quinta del Sordo, he painted the Black Paintings. In 1824 he left Spain for Bordeaux, where he died in 1828 aged 82. His work recorded his era's upheavals and influenced major later painters.

弗朗西斯科·德·戈雅（1746—1828）是西班牙画家和版画家，常被称为最后一位古典大师和第一位现代画家。他生于阿拉贡的丰德托多斯，在马德里从事创作，1786年成为宫廷画家，1799年升为首席宫廷画家。他画有《查理四世一家》和大胆的《裸体的马哈》。

1793年一场重病使他失聪，作品随之转向阴暗，《奇想集》蚀刻版画描绘疯狂、女巫与腐败。拿破仑1807年入侵时他留在马德里，《战争的灾难》版画和1814年的《1808年5月3日》展现了没有英雄色彩的战争。

1819年起他与世隔绝地住在“聋人之家”，画下《黑色绘画》。1824年他离开西班牙前往波尔多，1828年在那里去世，终年八十二岁。他的作品记录了所处时代的动荡，影响了后世许多重要画家。

en:
Ignatius of Loyola (1491–1556) was the Spanish priest and former soldier who founded the Society of Jesus. Born Íñigo López, youngest of thirteen children of a Basque family, he soldiered until a cannonball broke his right leg at Pamplona in 1521 and lamed him for life.

At Loyola he read the lives of Christ and the saints, finding dreams of sainthood left him at peace but dreams of glory left him empty. In 1522 he hung his sword at Montserrat and went to Manresa, where he begged, prayed in a cave and drafted the Spiritual Exercises, published in 1548.

After studies at Alcalá, Salamanca and Paris he gathered six companions, among them Francis Xavier, and in 1541 became first Superior General of the Society of Jesus, whose fourth vow of papal obedience made it a Counter-Reformation force. He died in Rome in 1556 and was canonized in 1622.

依纳爵·罗耀拉（1491—1556）是西班牙神父，出身军人，创立了耶稣会。他本名伊尼戈·洛佩斯，是巴斯克家庭十三个孩子中最小的一个，从军期间于1521年在潘普洛纳战役被一发炮弹打断右腿，从此终身跛足。

在罗耀拉养伤期间，他读起基督与圣徒的传记，发现梦想成圣使他平静，梦想荣耀却让他空虚。1522年他把佩剑挂在蒙塞拉特，前往马纳雷萨，在那里乞讨、在山洞祈祷，并起草《神操》，该书于1548年出版。

在阿尔卡拉、萨拉曼卡和巴黎求学后，他聚集了六名同伴，方济各·沙勿略便是其中之一，1541年出任耶稣会首任总会长；会士另发服从教宗的第四愿，耶稣会由此成为反宗教改革的力量。1556年他在罗马去世，1622年被封圣。

John of the Cross (1542–1591), born Juan de Yepes y Álvarez, was a Spanish Carmelite friar and mystic poet, and with Teresa of Ávila a founder of the Discalced Carmelites. He entered the Carmelite Order in 1563 and studied at Salamanca.

Ordained in 1567, he joined Teresa of Ávila's reform, and in 1568 opened the first reformed house at Duruelo, taking the name John of the Cross. In 1577 unreformed Carmelites seized him and carried him to Toledo; in a cell barely ten feet by six he was lashed weekly, yet composed much of the Spiritual Canticle and escaped through a window in 1578.

He became Vicar Provincial of Andalusia in 1585 and founded monasteries, but was later removed, and died in 1591. His works, including Dark Night of the Soul, are classics of Spanish mysticism; he was canonized in 1726 and named Doctor of the Church in 1926.

十字若望（1542—1591）原名胡安·德·耶佩斯·阿尔瓦雷斯，是西班牙加尔默罗会修士和神秘主义诗人，与阿维拉的德兰共同创立赤脚加尔默罗会。1563年他加入加尔默罗会，在萨拉曼卡求学。

1567年晋铎后，他加入德兰的改革，1568年在杜鲁埃洛开办第一座改革派修院，改名十字若望。1577年未改革的会士将他押到托莱多；在一间仅十英尺乘六英尺的囚室里他每周受鞭笞，却写成《灵歌》的大部分，1578年从窗口逃出。

1585年他出任安达卢西亚代理省会长，创建修院，后被免职，1591年去世。他的著作包括《心灵的黑夜》，是西班牙神秘文学的经典；1726年被封圣，1926年被列为教会圣师。

Miguel de Cervantes (1547–1616) was the Spanish soldier and writer who wrote Don Quixote, widely regarded as the first modern novel. Born at Alcalá de Henares, he left Spain in 1569.

In 1571 he fought at Lepanto, where he took three wounds, one leaving his left hand useless, and was nicknamed the one-handed man of Lepanto. In 1575 corsairs captured his ship, and he spent almost five years captive in Algiers, making four escape attempts, until the Trinitarians ransomed him in 1580. Back in Spain he published La Galatea in 1585 and was briefly jailed over his accounts.

Part One of Don Quixote appeared in 1605, written to undermine empty chivalric romances, and was an instant success. The Novelas ejemplares followed in 1613; when an unauthorised Avellaneda sequel appeared in 1614, Cervantes answered with Part Two in 1615. He died in Madrid in 1616.

米格尔·德·塞万提斯（1547—1616）是西班牙军人和作家，写下被广泛视为第一部现代小说的《堂吉诃德》。他生于埃纳雷斯堡，1569年离开西班牙。

1571年他参加勒班陀海战，身中三处伤，其中一处使左手残废，人称“勒班陀的独臂人”。1575年海盗劫船，他在阿尔及尔做了近五年俘虏，四次尝试逃跑，直到1580年三一会将他赎回。回到西班牙后，1585年出版《伽拉泰亚》，还曾因账目问题短期入狱。

《堂吉诃德》第一部于1605年问世，旨在打击空洞的骑士传奇，书一出便大受欢迎。1613年《训诫小说集》出版。1614年阿维亚内达出版未经授权的续集，塞万提斯1615年写出自己的第二部。1616年他在马德里去世。

Francisco de Quevedo (1580–1645) was a Spanish nobleman, politician and writer of the Baroque, and with Góngora one of the great poets of his age. Orphaned by six, lame from a club foot and short-sighted, the pince-nez he always wore gave Spanish the word quevedos.

The picaresque novel El Buscón made him famous. His style, conceptismo, stood against the ornate culteranismo of Góngora, whom he lampooned in the sonnet A una nariz for his nose. He took refuge with the Duke of Osuna, whom he served as secretary in Italy from 1613.

Osuna's fall in 1620 sent Quevedo into exile on his estate, where he wrote some of his best poetry. Back at court under Philip IV, he became royal secretary in 1632. In 1639 he was arrested and taken to the convent of San Marcos in León until 1643. He died on 8 September 1645.

弗朗西斯科·德·戈维多（1580—1645）是西班牙巴洛克时期的贵族、政治人物和作家，与贡戈拉并称当世大诗人。他六岁成了孤儿，有先天足畸形，又近视；他终日戴着夹鼻眼镜，西班牙语里夹鼻眼镜的名称就取自他的姓氏。

流浪汉小说《骗子外传》使他声名大噪。他的“概念派”文风与贡戈拉的华饰派针锋相对，他在十四行诗《致一只鼻子》里拿对方的鼻子开玩笑。他躲到奥苏纳公爵处避难，从1613年起任奥苏纳在意大利的秘书。

1620年奥苏纳失势，戈维多被放逐到自己的庄园，在那里写下一些最好的诗。腓力四世在位期间他重返宫廷，1632年成为国王秘书。1639年他被捕，押往莱昂的圣马可修道院，直到1643年才获释。1645年9月8日他去世。

流浪汉小说《骗子外传》使他声名大噪。他的“概念派”文风与贡戈拉的华饰派针锋相对，他在十四行诗《致一只鼻子》里拿对方的鼻子开玩笑。他躲到[ShowLocationName('osuna')]公爵处避难，从1613年起任奥苏纳在意大利的秘书。

1620年奥苏纳失势，戈维多被放逐到自己的庄园，在那里写下一些最好的诗。腓力四世在位期间他重返宫廷，1632年成为国王秘书。1639年他被捕，押往[ShowLocationName('leon')]的圣马可修道院，直到1643年才获释。1645年9月8日他去世。

en:
Teresa of Ávila (1515–1582) was a Spanish Carmelite nun, mystic and reformer of the Counter-Reformation. At seven she ran away to seek martyrdom among the Moors. In 1534 she entered the Carmelite Convent of the Incarnation; her zeal for mortification made her ill, and she spent almost a year in bed.

Raptures and visions followed; in the best known, a seraph drives a golden lance through her heart, a scene Bernini later carved in Rome. She founded the convent of Saint Joseph in Ávila in 1562 and won papal approval for absolute poverty. With John of the Cross she opened the first Discalced friary at Duruelo in 1568.

In 1580 a papal decree separated the Discalced Carmelites. She wrote The Interior Castle, whose seven mansions mark the soul's progress. She died in October 1582, was canonised in 1622, and in 1970 became the first woman Doctor of the Church.

亚维拉的德兰（1515—1582）是西班牙加尔默罗会修女，也是反宗教改革时期的神秘主义者和修会改革者。七岁时她曾逃出家门，想去摩尔人那里殉道。1534年她进入加尔默罗会降生修院，因苦行过度病得几乎卧床一年。

此后神魂超拔与异象接踵而来；最著名的一次，是一位炽天使用金矛刺穿她的心，贝尼尼后来在罗马把这一幕雕了出来。1562年她在阿维拉创立圣若瑟隐修院，并得到教宗对绝对贫穷的认可。1568年她与十字若望在杜鲁埃洛开办了第一所赤足会男修院。

1580年教宗诏书使赤足加尔默罗会独立。她写有《灵心城堡》，以七重居所描绘灵魂的进程。1582年10月她去世，1622年被封圣，1970年成为首位女性教会圣师。
