en:
Túpac Amaru II (1738–1781), born José Gabriel Condorcanqui near Cusco, was an indigenous kuraca and mule trader who claimed descent from the last Incas of Vilcabamba. He inherited his father's chieftainship. When the colonial authorities ignored his petitions against indigenous tribute and the mining mita, he seized and executed the corregidor Antonio de Arriaga in November 1780.

His rebellion spread from Peru into Upper Peru, and on 16 November he decreed the abolition of slavery, the first such measure in Spanish America. Betrayed after failing to take Cusco, he was beheaded and quartered in the main square on 18 May 1781.

图帕克·阿马鲁二世（1738—1781）原名何塞·加夫列尔·孔多尔坎基，生于库斯科附近，是土著酋长兼赶骡商人，自称是比尔卡班巴末代印加王的后裔，后来继承了父亲的酋长职位。殖民当局对他反对土著贡赋和矿山米塔劳役制的请愿置之不理，他遂于1780年11月逮捕并处死地方长官安东尼奥·德·阿里亚加。

他发动的起义从秘鲁蔓延到上秘鲁；11月16日他颁布废除奴隶制的法令，为西属美洲首例。攻打库斯科失败后他被部下出卖，1781年5月18日在库斯科武器广场被斩首并肢解。

en:
Diego Velázquez (baptized 6 June 1599 – 6 August 1660) was the leading painter at the court of Philip IV and of the Spanish Golden Age. Born in Seville, he was apprenticed in 1611 to Francisco Pacheco, whose daughter Juana he married in 1618. His first pictures were kitchen scenes, among them The Waterseller of Seville.

Philip IV sat for him on 30 August 1623, and Velázquez entered royal service. He spent 1629–1631 in Italy, then painted The Surrender of Breda (1634–1635) for the Buen Retiro palace. The Rokeby Venus, his only surviving female nude, dates from the 1640s.

On a second Italian trip in 1649–1651 he painted Pope Innocent X and Juan de Pareja, whom he freed in 1650. He painted Las Meninas in 1656, and received the Order of Santiago three years later. He fell ill in 1660 and died in Madrid.

迭戈·委拉斯开兹（1599年6月6日受洗—1660年8月6日）是腓力四世宫廷里的首席画师，也是西班牙黄金时代最杰出的画家。他生于塞维利亚，1611年师从弗朗西斯科·帕切科，1618年娶老师的女儿胡安娜。他最初画厨房场景，其中有《塞维利亚的卖水人》。

腓力四世于1623年8月30日坐下让他画像，他由此入宫供职。1629至1631年他在意大利停留，回国后为丽池宫画了《布雷达之降》（1634—1635）。《镜前的维纳斯》作于1640年代，是他仅存的女性裸体画。

1649至1651年第二次赴意大利，他画下教宗英诺森十世和胡安·德·帕雷哈的肖像，后者在1650年被他解除奴籍。1656年他画成《宫娥》，三年后获圣地亚哥骑士团勋章。1660年他发病，在马德里去世。

en:
Welf VI (1115–1191), third son of Duke Henry IX of Bavaria, inherited the Welf family lands in Swabia around Ravensburg while his elder brothers took Bavaria and the church.

In 1152 his nephew, Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, enfeoffed him with the duchy of Spoleto and the margraviate of Tuscany, founding the Italian line of the Welf dynasty. He campaigned with Barbarossa in Italy; his only son Welf VII died of epidemic illness at Siena during the retreat in 1167. He later surrendered his Italian states to the emperor and was buried at Steingaden Abbey, which he had founded.

韦尔夫六世（1115—1191）是巴伐利亚公爵亨利九世的第三子，继承了家族在施瓦本以拉芬斯堡为中心的领地，长兄们则分得巴伐利亚或进入教会。

1152年，他的外甥、皇帝腓特烈一世将斯波莱托公国和托斯卡纳藩侯领地封给他，由此开创韦尔夫家族的意大利支系。他随腓特烈一世出征意大利，独子韦尔夫七世于1167年撤军途中染疫病死于锡耶纳。他后来将意大利领地交还皇帝，死后葬于他本人创建的施泰因加登修道院。

en:
Welf VII (c. 1135–1167), only son of Welf VI and Uta of Calw, managed the family's Italian domains while his father remained in Swabia. From 1154 he accompanied his cousin Emperor Frederick Barbarossa on his Italian campaigns, and in 1160 the emperor made him duke of Spoleto.

In 1167 he took part in Barbarossa's siege of Rome against Pope Alexander III; after the city fell a devastating epidemic swept the imperial army, and he died of it at Siena on 12 September. He was buried at Steingaden Abbey in Bavaria.

en:
Khun Luang Pha Ngua, King Borommarachathirat I (c. 1311–1388), was a lord of the Suphannaphum clan and elder brother of King Ramathibodi I's queen. When Ramathibodi founded Ayutthaya in 1351, he appointed Pha Ngua to rule Suphan Buri.

After Ramathibodi died in 1369 his son Ramesuan took the throne, but within a year Pha Ngua forced him to abdicate and was crowned himself. He died in 1388; his young son Thong Lan ruled barely a week before Ramesuan returned from Lavo and seized power.

波隆摩罗阇一世（约1311—1388），即坤銮帕娃，是素攀那蓬家族的领主，也是拉玛铁菩提一世王后的兄长。1351年拉玛铁菩提建立阿瑜陀耶后，派他出镇素攀武里。

1369年拉玛铁菩提去世，王子拉梅萱继位，不到一年便被他逼迫退位，他由此加冕称王。他于1388年去世；幼子东兰继位仅一周，拉梅萱便从华富里返回，夺回王位。

en:
John I, called the Lame (c. 1245–1290), was count of the Further County of Sponheim, ruling from Kreuznach. He succeeded his father Simon I in 1265 and married Adelaide of Leiningen. He later had to partition the inheritance with his brothers Henry and Eberhard, and mediation settled the division in 1277.

A feud followed when Henry sold Böckelheim Castle to the archbishop of Mainz against John's pre-emption right, and in 1279 John was defeated at Sprendlingen. He was buried at Pfaffen-Schwabenheim.

zh:
约翰一世，绰号“瘸子”（约1245—1290），是前施蓬海姆伯国伯爵，以克罗伊茨纳赫为统治中心。1265年父亲西蒙一世去世后他继位，并于同年娶莱宁根的阿德海德为妻。后来他不得不与弟弟亨利和埃伯哈德分割祖产，分割于1277年经调解达成。

此后亨利不顾他的先买权，把伯克尔海姆城堡卖给美因茨大主教，双方结仇；1279年，约翰在施普伦德林根战败。他葬于普法芬-施瓦本海姆。

en:
John II, called the Lame (c. 1270–1340), was a count of the Sponheim-Kreuznach line. From 1290 he ruled the front County of Sponheim jointly with his brother Simon II, and by 1300 they had divided it along the Soonwald forest, John keeping the southern part around Bad Kreuznach.

He backed anti-king Frederick the Fair and feuded with Archbishop Baldwin of Trier. He died on 11 March 1340 and was buried at Pfaffen-Schwabenheim, his lands passing to his nephew Walram.

约翰二世，绰号“跛子”（约1270—1340），是施蓬海姆家族克罗伊茨纳赫支系的伯爵。1290年起，他与兄长西蒙二世共同统治前施蓬海姆伯国；约1300年，兄弟二人以索恩瓦尔德为界瓜分伯国，约翰领有以巴特克罗伊茨纳赫为中心的南部。

他支持对立国王美男子腓特烈，与特里尔大主教巴尔杜因·冯·卢森堡结仇交战。1340年3月11日他去世，葬于普法芬-施瓦本海姆，领地传给侄子瓦尔拉姆。

en:
Simon II (c. 1270–1336) was a count of the Sponheim-Kreuznach line. After his father John I died in 1290, he ruled the front County of Sponheim with his brother John II; around 1300 they divided it, Simon taking the north around Kastellaun.

He granted Kastellaun city rights in 1305. His feud with Archbishop Baldwin of Trier dominated his later years: Baldwin captured Sprendlingen and besieged Kastellaun in 1320–1321. Simon died in 1336 and was buried at Kastellaun, succeeded by his son Walram.

zh:
西蒙二世（约1270—1336）是施蓬海姆家族克罗伊茨纳赫支系的伯爵。1290年父亲约翰一世去世后，他与弟弟约翰二世共同统治前施蓬海姆伯国；约1300年两人瓜分伯国，西蒙分得卡斯特劳恩一带的北部。

他于1305年授予卡斯特劳恩城市权。他晚年与特里尔大主教巴尔杜因·冯·卢森堡连年结仇：1320至1321年，巴尔杜因攻占施普伦德林根并围攻卡斯特劳恩。1336年西蒙二世去世，葬于卡斯特劳恩，儿子瓦尔拉姆继位。

en:
Simon III (born after 1330; died 30 August 1414) was the last ruling count of the Sponheim-Kreuznach line and, through marriage, count of Vianden. The only son of Walram, he married Maria of Vianden in 1348, bringing the county of Vianden to his house.

In 1371 he was captured and held for years until a heavy ransom freed him. His son Walram died in 1382, and the male line of the Kreuznach counts ended with Simon's death in 1414.

西蒙三世（1330年后生，1414年8月30日卒）是施蓬海姆家族克罗伊茨纳赫支系的末代执政伯爵，并因婚姻得到菲安登伯爵头衔。作为伯爵瓦尔拉姆的独子，他于1348年娶菲安登的玛丽亚，菲安登城与伯国由此并入克罗伊茨纳赫支系。

1371年他兵败被俘，囚禁数年，靠支付巨额赎金才获释。其子瓦尔拉姆1382年早逝，克罗伊茨纳赫支系男嗣在他1414年去世后断绝。

en:
Walram (c. 1305–1380) was a count of the Sponheim-Kreuznach line, the eldest son of Simon II. In 1330 he married Elisabeth of Katzenelnbogen. He first inherited his father's northern half of the divided county, and when his uncle John II died without legitimate issue in 1340, Walram reunited the whole county and made Kreuznach his residence.

His rule saw many feuds with neighbouring lords. He died early in 1380 and was buried at Pfaffen-Schwabenheim, succeeded by his only son, Simon III.

zh:
瓦尔拉姆（约1305—1380）是施蓬海姆家族克罗伊茨纳赫支系的伯爵，西蒙二世的长子。1330年他娶卡岑埃尔恩博根的伊丽莎白为妻。他最初继承父亲分得的伯国北半部；1340年叔父约翰二世无嫡子而终，瓦尔拉姆重新统一整个伯国，并以克罗伊茨纳赫为居所。

en:
Gerhard von Ehrenberg (d. 1363), born into a Kraichgau knightly family, served in Emperor Louis IV's chancellery before being elected bishop of Speyer in 1336. Gerhard supported Louis militarily, switching to Charles IV only after Louis died.

He rebuilt Speyer's Augustinian monastery and freed the bishopric from debt, although he could not prevent the Jewish pogroms of 1349. He died in 1363 and was buried in the cathedral.

格哈德·冯·埃伦贝格（？—1363）出身克莱希高的骑士家族，曾在皇帝路德维希四世的官厅任职，1336年当选施派尔主教。格哈德以军事支持路德维希，直到路德维希去世后才转而效忠查理四世。

en:
Abd al-Razzaq ibn Fazlallah was a landowner of Bashtin near Sabzavar in Khurasan who founded the Sarbadar state. Oppressed by the taxes of Ala al-Din Muhammad, governor under Togha Temur, he killed an official in 1337 and revolted.

His followers defeated government forces and seized Sabzavar in 1337. He ruled with the title of amir and struck coins in his own name, but in 1338 he was stabbed to death by his brother Wajih al-Din Masud, who succeeded him.

阿卜杜勒-拉扎克·伊本·法兹卢拉是呼罗珊萨卜泽瓦尔附近巴什廷的地主，也是萨尔毕道朗政权的建立者。脱合帖木儿派总督阿拉丁·穆罕默德横征暴敛，他于1337年杀死一名税官起事。

部众击败官军，于1337年攻占萨卜泽瓦尔。他以埃米尔之号统治，并用自己的名字铸币；1338年，他被兄弟瓦吉赫丁·马斯乌德刺死，马斯乌德随即继位。

en:
Fakhr al-Din Ilyas Bey (d. 1362) succeeded his father Sarukhan as the second ruler of the Saruhanid beylik in 1345, ruling from Manisa. He stayed on good terms with the neighboring beyliks and the Genoese port of Phocaea.

In 1358, during the Byzantine siege of Phocaea, Ilyas feigned aid to the emperor while plotting to seize him at a hunt, but was arrested instead; his wife paid a ransom to free him. He died in 1362 and was succeeded by his son Ishak.

法赫尔丁·伊利亚斯贝伊（？—1362）于1345年继承父亲萨鲁汗贝伊之位，是萨鲁汗侯国第二代贝伊，以马尼萨为都。他与邻近的诸贝伊国以及热那亚人占据的福西亚港大体保持友好。

1358年拜占庭围攻福西亚期间，伊利亚斯佯装出兵相助皇帝，却密谋在一次狩猎中将其拘捕；结果反被拿下，最后由他的妻子支付赎金才得获释。他于1362年去世，儿子伊沙克继位。

en:
İshak Bey, honorifically Muzafferüddin İshak, was the third ruler of the Saruhanid beylik at Manisa. The son of Fahrüddin İlyas Bey, he succeeded his father after 1362 and reigned until his death in 1388.

In 1366 he ordered the building of Manisa's Great Mosque, with a madrasa added beside it in 1378. On his death his son Hızır Şah took the throne, while his other son Orhan took refuge with the Ottomans.

伊沙克贝伊，尊号穆扎费鲁丁·伊沙克，是定都马尼萨的萨鲁汗贝伊国第三位统治者。他是法赫鲁丁·伊利亚斯贝伊之子，1362年之后继位，统治到1388年去世。

en:
Sarukhan Bey (c. 1300–1346) was the Turkmen founder of the Saruhanid principality centered on Manisa. A former emir under the Seljuk sultans, he campaigned against Byzantine lands and in 1313 seized Thyatira and then Manisa.

In 1336 he allied with Emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos and supported him at the sieges of Mytilene and Phocaea, but in 1341 his fleet was repulsed while raiding toward Constantinople. He died in 1345 or 1346, soon after his eldest son Suleyman died of illness in 1345.

萨鲁汗贝伊（约1300—1345/1346）是土库曼出身的萨鲁汗侯国开国君主，立国于马尼萨。他原在塞尔柱苏丹麾下任埃米尔，后进攻拜占庭领土，于1313年攻占推雅推喇，随后又取马尼萨。

1336年他与拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡三世·巴列奥略结盟，出兵协助围攻米蒂利尼和福西亚；1341年他派舰队奔袭君士坦丁堡，却被击退。1345年长子苏莱曼病逝后，他也在1345或1346年离世。

en:
Suleyman Bey was the eldest son of Sarukhan Bey, founder of the Saruhanid principality at Manisa. In 1345 he answered the call of the Byzantine emperor John VI Kantakouzenos and, together with the Aydinid ruler Umur Bey, crossed into Thrace on the emperor's side.

He fought in the campaign that crushed the Bulgarian warlord Momchil near Didymoteicho in June 1345. Soon after that battle Suleyman fell ill and died; his father died the next year, grief-stricken at his loss.

en:
Hushang (r. 1372–1382) was the last Shirvanshah of the Kasranid line, succeeding his father Kavus, under whom Shirvan had become a Jalayirid vassal. Raised a hostage at the court of the Jalayirid sultan Shaykh Uways and released on his father's death, he kept minting coins in his overlords' names.

When Shah Mansur invaded Shirvan in 1375, Hushang avoided battle. The poet Arif Ardabili dedicated a masnavi to him. In 1382 Hushang was killed by his subjects; his cousin Ibrahim I succeeded him, opening the Darbandi line.

胡尚（1372—1382年在位）是科斯兰支系的末代希尔万沙，继父亲卡夫斯而立；在卡夫斯治下，希尔凡已沦为札剌亦儿王朝的属国。胡尚自幼在札剌亦儿苏丹谢赫·乌韦斯的宫廷中当人质，父亲去世后才获释，继续以宗主的名义铸币。

1375年沙·曼苏尔进攻希尔凡时，胡尚避不决战。诗人阿里夫·阿尔达比勒曾将一部玛斯纳维叙事诗献给他。1382年胡尚被臣民所杀，堂弟易卜拉欣一世继位，开启了德尔本特支系。

en:
Kavus I was the 32nd Shirvanshah, ruling first alongside his father Kayqubad I and alone from about 1348. He defied the Chobanid Malek Ashraf and in 1347 took shelter in Shirvan's castles; he then invited the Golden Horde khan Jani Beg, who captured Tabriz and killed Malek Ashraf.

Kavus twice occupied Tabriz, but after the Jalayirid Shaykh Uways besieged Shamakhi he accepted vassalage and left his son Hushang a hostage until 1372. Kavus died in 1372.

卡夫斯一世是第32代希尔万沙，先与父亲凯库巴德一世共治，约1348年起独掌大权。他抗拒楚邦的马立克·阿什拉夫，1347年退入希尔凡的城堡；随后请来金帐汗札尼别，札尼别攻占大不里士并杀死马立克·阿什拉夫。

卡夫斯曾两度占领大不里士；但札剌亦儿的谢赫·乌韦斯围攻沙马基后，他被迫称臣，把儿子胡尚留作人质直到1372年。卡夫斯于1372年去世。

en:
Kayqubad I was the 31st Shirvanshah, a son of Farrukhzad II, whose long reign was spent under Chobanid overlordship. When the Chobanid ruler Malek Ashraf demanded a daughter of the Shirvanshah in marriage, Kayqubad's son and co-ruler Kavus refused.

After Malek Ashraf invaded in winter 1347, the pair took shelter in Shirvan's strong castles. Kayqubad disappears from the sources soon afterwards and probably died between 1348 and 1356. The Keygubad Mosque is held to have been built on his order.

凯库巴德一世是第31代希尔万沙，法鲁赫扎德二世之子，在位时间很长，长期处于楚邦王朝的宗主权之下。楚邦统治者马立克·阿什拉夫求娶希尔万沙的女儿，凯库巴德之子、共治者卡夫斯予以拒绝。

en:
Cho Ton (趙暾, 1307–1380) was a Goryeo civil official born at Yongjin, a son of Cho Yanggi, the second Ssangsŏng commandant, and uncle of the fourth commandant, Cho Sosaeng. He had submitted to Goryeo under King Ch'ungsuk.

When Goryeo retook Ssangsŏng in 1356, his nephew detained him, but Ton escaped, joined Yu In-u, and with Yi Cha-ch'un opened the gates to the Goryeo army. In 1359 his mission to coax Sosaeng into surrender failed.

赵暾（1307—1380）是高丽后期文臣，龙津人，第二代双城总管赵良琪之子、第四代总管赵小生的叔父。忠肃王时他归附高丽。

1356年高丽收复双城时，侄子赵小生将他拘押，赵暾逃脱后投奔柳仁雨，并与李子春等从内部打开城门，引高丽军入城。1359年他招抚赵小生失败。

en:
Cho Hwi (died 1273), a local strongman on Goryeo's northeastern frontier, rebelled against Goryeo in 1258 when the Mongols invaded the Hwaju region. With T'ak Ch'ŏng he killed the frontier military commissioner Sin Chipp'yŏng, surrendered the lands north of Hwaju, and in 1259 was made General Superintendent of the new Mongol Ssangsŏng Prefecture.

He led Mongol attacks on Goryeo forts until his death, when his son Cho Yanggi succeeded him; his heirs held Ssangsŏng until Goryeo retook it in 1356.

zh:
赵晖（？—1273）是高丽东北边境的土著豪强。1258年蒙古军侵袭和州地区时，他与卓青一同起兵叛离高丽，杀害东北面兵马使慎执平，献出和州以北土地，1259年被蒙古任命为新设双城总管府的总管。

en:
Cho Inbyŏk (1330–1393) was a military commander of the late Goryeo dynasty from the Hanyang Cho clan, whose forebears had governed Ssangseong for the Yuan. In 1356 he and his father Cho Ton helped Goryeo retake Ssangseong. He fought Red Turban invaders in 1361 and helped crush Kim Yong's rebellion in 1363.

In 1372 he ambushed Japanese pirates near Hamju, beheading at least seventy men. Married to a sister of Yi Sŏng-gye, he became Internal Prince Yongwŏn after the Joseon founding in 1392.

en:
Cho Sosaeng (趙小生, died 1362) was the fourth hereditary commandant of the Yuan Ssangsŏng Prefecture at Hwaju. When Goryeo sent Yu In-u against Ssangsŏng in 1356, Sosaeng detained his uncle Cho Ton and resisted with the chiliarch Tak To-gyŏng. After Ton escaped and the townspeople surrendered, he fled to the Jurchen lands.

In 1362 Sosaeng brought in the Yuan general Naghachu; Yi Sŏng-gye routed them at Taltan-dong, and later that year the Jurchen darughachi and commandant killed Sosaeng and Tak To-gyŏng.

en:
Cho Yanggi (1260–?) succeeded his father Cho Hwi as the second General Superintendent of Mongol-ruled Ssangsŏng Prefecture in northeastern Goryeo. In 1281 he sailed as a deputy commander under Kim Panggyŏng in the Yuan invasion of Japan; he then campaigned against the Hamdan people and sent his captives to the Yuan court.

His daughter became the later wife of Yi Ch'un, grandfather of Yi Sŏnggye, founder of Joseon. His elder son Cho Rim inherited Ssangsŏng, while his second son, Cho Ton, sided with Goryeo when it retook the prefecture in 1356.

en:
Barnim III (c. 1300–1368) was a Griffin duke of Pomerania-Stettin. He became his father Otto I's co-regent in 1320 and fought Brandenburg, beating its forces near Prenzlau in 1329. Emperor Louis IV recognized Pomerania-Stettin's imperial immediacy in 1338 and Charles IV confirmed it in 1348.

In 1348 Barnim conquered the eastern Uckermark backing the False Waldemar, and in 1351 he defeated the Mecklenburgers at Schoppendamm. He was also the first Griffin to style himself Duke of the Kashubians. He ruled alone from 1344 until 1368.

en:
Otto I (1279–1344) was the youngest, posthumous son of Duke Barnim I of Pomerania. His half-brother Bogislaw IV ruled during his minority; after their brother Barnim II died, the Treaty of Stettin in 1295 split the duchy, leaving Otto with Pomerania-Stettin and Bogislaw with Pomerania-Wolgast.

Otto drew close to Brandenburg, occupying much of the Uckermark during the Brandenburg succession crisis after 1319. From 1320 he ruled with his son Barnim III, and in 1338 Emperor Louis IV recognized Pomerania-Stettin's imperial immediacy. He died in 1344.

en:
Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah was of Sistani origin. He served the Delhi Sultanate and became governor of Satgaon. After 1338 he ruled Satgaon independently, then took Lakhnauti in 1342 and Sonargaon in 1352, unifying Bengal into an independent sultanate with its capital at Pandua.

His armies raided Nepal in 1346 and sacked Kathmandu, then invaded Orissa and Kamarupa. When Firuz Shah Tughluq invaded in 1353, he withstood a siege at Ekdala. He died in January 1358 and was buried at Hajipur, founding the Ilyas Shahi dynasty.

en:
Alonso Meléndez de Guzmán (c. 1300–1342) was a Leonese noble and brother of Eleanor of Guzmán, Alfonso XI's mistress. Knighted in the Order of the Banda at the king's coronation in 1332, he was imposed as master of the Order of Santiago in 1338 by Alfonso XI's intervention, setting aside the order's election to hold the post for his infant nephew Fadrique Alfonso.

He relieved Siles in 1339, fought at Río Salado in 1340 and was entrusted with the defence of the frontier in 1341. He died of illness during the siege of Algeciras on 14 September 1342.

Agnes II of Donzy (c. 1205–1225) was the daughter of Hervé IV of Donzy and Mahaut de Courtenay, heiress to Nevers, Auxerre and Tonnerre. In 1217 she was married to Philip, eldest son of Louis VIII, who died the next year.

He served Philip Augustus in Normandy, on the Albigensian Crusade and at the Battle of Bouvines in 1214, where his charges through the enemy line were celebrated by chroniclers. He died at the siege of Toulouse in 1219.

In 1226 he joined Louis VIII's Albigensian Crusade and led the main assault on Avignon, where a stone from the walls killed him. The county reverted to his mother.

Guy III of Châtillon, Count of Saint-Pol (born after 1226, died 1289), was the second son of Count Hugh I of Blois. He received Saint-Pol in 1248, while his elder brother John took Blois. In 1255 he married Matilda of Brabant, and governed Artois as regent until 1265, when his stepson came of age.

He joined Louis IX on the Eighth Crusade in 1270 and Philip III's Aragón Crusade in 1284–1285. At Worringen in 1288 he captured the Count of Guelders and the archbishop of Cologne. He was buried at Cercamp Abbey.

Guy IV of Châtillon-Saint-Pol (born after 1254, died 1317), second son of Count Guy III and Matilda of Brabant, received the County of Saint-Pol from his brother Hugh II in 1292. Philip the Fair made him grand butler of France in 1296, and as governor of Flanders he commanded the rearguard at Courtrai in 1302.

At Mons-en-Pévèle in 1304 he shared in the victory and was credited with saving the king's life; both Philip IV and Louis X made him a testamentary executor. He married Marie of Brittany in 1292 and was buried at Cercamp Abbey in 1317.

en:
Guy V of Châtillon, Count of Saint-Pol from 1344 to 1360, was the son of John of Saint-Pol and Jeanne de Fiennes. He married Jeanne of Luxembourg. A commander in the Hundred Years' War, he served as royal lieutenant against the English in Picardy and fought at Crécy in 1346 beside his uncle Robert de Fiennes.

In 1358 he helped suppress the Jacquerie and campaigned against the partisans of Charles the Bad of Navarre, taking part in the eight-month siege that recovered Saint-Valery from the Navarrese.

The 1360 Treaty of Brétigny freed King John II after four years in London but required hostages for his ransom. Guy was one of them, and by one account died of plague soon after reaching London. He left no children, so his sister Mathilde inherited Saint-Pol.

沙蒂永的居伊五世于1344至1360年任圣波勒伯爵，是圣波勒伯爵让与让娜·德·菲耶讷之子，娶卢森堡的让娜为妻。作为百年战争中的将领，他以王室代理官的身份在皮卡第同英军作战，1346年与舅父罗贝尔·德·菲耶讷一同参加克雷西战役。

1358年，他参与镇压扎克雷起义，并同纳瓦拉国王恶人查理的党羽作战，参加了历时八个月的圣瓦勒里围城战，从纳瓦拉人手中收复该城。

en:
John of Châtillon, Count of Saint-Pol (died 1344), was the eldest son of Guy IV of Châtillon and Marie of Brittany, and held the county from 1317. He was a first cousin of Duke John III of Brittany and Queen Joan I of Navarre.

In 1329 he married Jeanne de Fiennes, whose brother Robert de Fiennes later became constable of France. He served Philip VI of Valois against Edward III of England at the outset of the Hundred Years' War.

When John died the county passed to his son Guy V; after Guy died without children it went through John's daughter Mathilde to the Luxembourg-Ligny family.

en:
Marie de St Pol, Countess of Pembroke (c. 1303–1377), was a daughter of Guy IV of Châtillon, Count of Saint-Pol, and a great-granddaughter of Henry III. In 1321 she married Aymer de Valence, Earl of Pembroke, and was widowed in June 1324; the marriage was childless. She founded Pembroke College, Cambridge.

Edward III exempted her from the 1337 seizure of alien lands, but Charles V confiscated her French estates in 1372. She died in March 1377 and was buried at Denny Abbey in the habit of a Franciscan nun.

Marie of Brittany (1268–1339), also called Marie de Dreux, was the daughter of John II, Duke of Brittany, and Beatrice of England, and a granddaughter of King Henry III. In 1292 she married Guy IV of Châtillon, Count of Saint-Pol.

Her son John succeeded as Count of Saint-Pol; her daughter Mahaut married Charles of Valois; and another daughter, Marie, Countess of Pembroke, founded Pembroke College, Cambridge. Marie died in May 1339.

en:
Albert of Strzelce (born after 1300, died c. 1370–1375) was the youngest son of Bolko I, Duke of Opole. After their father died in 1313, Albert and his brother Bolko II ruled Opole jointly until 1323, when Albert received Strzelce. In 1326 he granted town rights to Strzelce, and from 1327 his duchy was held as a fief of the Bohemian crown.

In 1347 he married Agnes, daughter of Burgrave Burchard I of Magdeburg; their only child Elisabeth married Władysław the White. He was buried at Jemielnica.

Ban Mueang was the second king of Sukhothai and a son of its founder Si Inthrathit and Queen Sueang. He succeeded his father around 1270, and the Ram Khamhaeng Inscription, carved in 1292, describes him as the elder brother whom Ram Khamhaeng served faithfully before inheriting the throne.

He died around 1279 or 1280 and was succeeded by Ram Khamhaeng. A chronicle records his son Ngua Nam Thum, who later ruled Sukhothai.

en:
Li Thai, known posthumously as Maha Thammaracha I, was king of Sukhothai from about 1347 until his death in 1368. The son of King Loe Thai, he ruled Si Satchanalai as viceroy before taking the throne.

A devout Theravada Buddhist, he built Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat at Phitsanulok and wrote the Trai Phum Phra Ruang, on Buddhist cosmology and a righteous king's duties, the first major Buddhist text composed in Thai. He was succeeded by his son Lue Thai.

en:
Loe Thai was the fourth king of Sukhothai, succeeding his father Ram Khamhaeng around 1298. The tributaries his father had won broke away, including Uttaradit, Luang Prabang and Vientiane, and Hanthawaddy in 1319, while U Thong rose in the south. Around 1312 he launched an expedition against Champa.

A devout Buddhist, he reproduced Sri Lankan Buddha footprints and bore the title Dhammaraja. He died in 1323, and the throne passed to his cousin Ngua Nam Thum.

zh:
乐泰是素可泰帕銮王朝第四代国王，约1298年继承其父兰甘亨的王位。父亲征服的属国相继叛离：程逸以及琅勃拉邦、万象脱离，1319年勃固独立，乌通在南方崛起。约1312年他远征占城。

乐泰笃信佛教，仿制了数个锡兰佛足印，因而有“法王”达磨罗阇的称号。他于1323年去世，王位落入堂兄弟威南童之手。

en:
Ngua Nam Thum was a king of Sukhothai of the House of Phra Ruang. The Jinakalamali chronicle makes him a son of King Ban Mueang, nephew of Ram Khamhaeng and cousin of Loe Thai, whom he followed on the throne around 1323.

Around 1340 he named Loe Thai’s son Li Thai his heir and ruler of Si Satchanalai. In 1347 or 1348, the Wat Pa Mamuang inscriptions record, Li Thai marched on the capital, killed his enemies and took the throne as Mahathammaracha I.

One historian has suggested that Ngua Nam Thum died that same year and that Li Thai seized the throne before the late king’s son could succeed him.

zh:
威南童是素可泰王国帕銮王朝的国王。据《胜者纪年》记载，他为国王班孟之子、兰甘亨的侄子、乐泰的堂兄，约于1323年继乐泰之后即位。

约1340年，他立乐泰之子立泰为王储，由立泰兼领是塞差那莱。据帕玛蒙寺碑铭记载，1347或1348年立泰率军进逼王都素可泰，诛杀仇敌后登基，称摩诃昙摩罗阇一世。

一位历史学者认为，威南童在同年去世，立泰在其子继位之前夺取了王位。

en:
Ram Khamhaeng the Great (c. 1239–1298) was the third king of Sukhothai, which he ruled from about 1279 at the height of its prosperity, and the king traditionally credited with giving the Thais their alphabet. Son of the kingdom's founder Si Inthrathit, he bore a name meaning ‘brave Rama’.

His campaigns are thought to have carried Sukhothai's influence to Vientiane, Nakhon Si Thammarat and the Mon lands, and in 1295 the Yuan court told him to stop attacking Malayu. From 1282 he sent embassies to Yuan China.

In 1283 he created the Thai script from Khmer and related alphabets and made Theravada Buddhism the state religion. A bell in Sukhothai let subjects summon him, and the 1292 stele, traditionally his, is the earliest Thai text. The Yuan History says he died in 1298; tradition says he was lost in the rapids at Sawankhalok. His son Loe Thai succeeded him.

zh:
兰甘亨大帝（约1239—1298）是素可泰第三代国王，约1279年起在位，素可泰在他治下最为繁荣，传统上认为是他给了泰人自己的文字。他是王国创建者室利膺陀罗铁之子，名字意为“勇敢的罗摩”。

有人推测他的征战使素可泰势力远及万象、洛坤和孟人之地；1295年元廷告谕他不要攻打末罗瑜。1282年起他多次遣使元朝。

1283年，他参照高棉文等文字创制泰文字母，又确立上座部佛教为国教。素可泰悬有一口大钟，百姓可敲钟求见；1292年的石碑传统上认为出自其手，是最早的泰文文献。《元史》记载他死于1298年，传说他消失在宋加洛的激流之中。其子乐泰继位。

en:
Si Inthrathit (1188–1270), born Bang Klang Hao, was the founder and first king of the Sukhothai Kingdom. As chief of Bang Yang, he joined Khun Pha Mueang in rebelling against Angkor in 1238, defeating the Khmer general Khlon Lamphong and seizing Sukhothai.

Crowned under the Sanskrit name Si Inthrathit, he was honoured as Phra Ruang, a title borne by his dynasty. His son Ram Khamhaeng defeated a Khmer prince in elephant combat. On his death in 1270 his second son Ban Mueang succeeded him.

zh:
室利膺陀罗铁（1188—1270）原名邦克朗豪，是素可泰王国的开国君主。他原是邦扬的首领，1238年与坤波孟起兵反抗吴哥，击败高棉大将柯伦喃蓬，夺取素可泰。

他登位后取梵语王号室利膺陀罗铁，获帕銮称号，其王朝遂称帕銮王朝。其子兰甘亨曾骑象击败高棉王子。1270年他去世后，次子班孟继位。

en:
Prabu Ajiguna Wisesa, also named Sang Mokteng Kiding, was a maharaja of the united Sunda and Galuh realm in western Java. As the son-in-law of King Prabu Lingga Dewata, he succeeded to the throne in 1333 and ruled from Kawali until about 1340.

He moved the royal court from Pakuan, now Bogor, to Kawali in the Ciamis region, which remained the kingdom's capital until 1482. Sundanese chronicles record that his son Prabu Ragamulya Luhur Prabawa followed him as king.

阿吉古纳维塞萨，又名桑·莫克滕·基丁，是西爪哇巽他与加卢统一王国的摩诃罗阇。他是国王普拉布·林加·德瓦塔的女婿，于1333年继位，在卡瓦利统治至约1340年。

他将王庭从帕库安（今茂物）迁至查米斯地区的卡瓦利，此后卡瓦利作为王国都城一直沿用到1482年。巽他编年史记载，其子普拉布·拉加穆利亚·卢胡尔·普拉巴瓦随后继位。

en:
Suqu Sechen was a 12th-century Mongol of the Barlas tribe and a paternal ancestor of Timur. The Secret History of the Mongols mentions him once: in 1190 he and his son Qarachar led one of two Barlas delegations to the assembly that proclaimed Temüjin ruler of the Mongols.

Later Timurid works made him a great-grandson of Tumanay Khan and a trusted adviser of Yesugei who foretold the infant Temüjin's greatness and died days after Yesugei in 1171, conflicting with the Secret History's 1190 assembly.

zh:
速忽赤臣是12世纪巴鲁剌思部的蒙古人，也是征服者帖木儿的父系先祖。《蒙古秘史》只提到他一次：1190年，他与儿子哈剌察儿率领巴鲁剌思人的两支代表团之一，参加推举铁木真为蒙古人首领的部落大会。

后世帖木儿朝著作称他是屯必乃汗的曾孙、也速该信任的谋臣，曾预言襁褓中的铁木真前途无量，于1171年也速该死后数日去世，与《秘史》所载他出席1190年大会相矛盾。

en:
Hajji Taghay was the second ruler of the Sutayids, a Mongol dynasty founded by his father, Emir Sutay, a commander of Ilkhan Ghazan that held Diyar Bakr and the Jazira. When Sutay died in 1332, Hajji Taghay inherited his fiefs around Amid.

He led the dynasty through the collapse of Ilkhanate rule, repeatedly fighting the Oirat tribes and allying himself with the Jalayirids. In 1343 he was killed by his own nephew, Ibrahimshah, who rose against him with Chupanid backing.

zh:
哈吉·塔盖是速台王朝的第二代统治者；这个蒙古王朝由其父、伊儿汗合赞麾下的异密速台建立，领有迪亚巴克尔与杰济拉。1332年速台去世，哈吉·塔盖继承了他在阿米德一带的封地。

在伊儿汗国统治瓦解之际，他屡次与卫拉特诸部交战，并与札剌亦儿王朝结盟。1343年，他被自己的侄子易卜拉欣沙杀害，后者是在楚邦王朝支持下起兵反叛的。

en:
Ibrahimshah was the third ruler of the Sutayid Mongols of Diyar Bakr. In 1343, with Chupanid support, he killed his uncle Hajji Taghay and seized the family's fiefs around Amid. He first served the Chupanid Malek Ashraf, but switched to rival Ilkhanid claimants in 1345.

Malek Ashraf defeated him at Aladagh, yet he held power until his death from a stroke in 1350, after which the Sutayids lost their Iraqi lands.

zh:
易卜拉欣沙是迪亚巴克尔速台蒙古人的第三代统治者。1343年，他在楚邦王朝支持下杀死叔父哈吉·塔盖，夺取了阿米德一带的家族封地。他起初依附楚邦王朝的马立克·阿什拉夫，1345年转而效忠与之对立的伊儿汗位争夺者。

马立克·阿什拉夫在阿拉达格将他击败，但他仍掌握政权，直至1350年中风而死；此后速台人丧失了他们在伊拉克的领地。

en:
Sutay (died 1332) was a Mongol emir and former stable master who rose under Ghazan fighting Nawruz's revolt from 1289 to 1294. He helped crush Sulamish's rebellion in Anatolia, winning the decisive battle near Akşehir in 1299.

He fought in Öljaitü's Gilan campaign of 1307 and in 1312 was appointed viceroy of Diyar Bakr. Dismissed in 1316, he was restored in 1319 after keeping clear of Irinjin's revolt, and held Diyar Bakr until his death in 1332. His descendants, the Sutayids, made their rule there hereditary after the Ilkhanate dissolved.

zh:
速台（？—1332）是蒙古异密，原为掌管马厩的侍从，在合赞汗麾下因1289至1294年征讨纳兀鲁思之乱而起家。他参与平定阿纳托利亚的苏拉米什叛乱，1299年在阿克谢希尔附近赢得决战。

他随完者都参加1307年的吉兰战役，1312年被任命为迪亚巴克尔总督。1316年他被解职，1319年因没有卷入伊林真叛乱而官复原职，一直领有迪亚巴克尔直到1332年去世。伊儿汗国解体后，他的后裔速台王朝使对该地的统治变为世袭。

en:
Hasso von Wedel-Schivelbein, called Hasso the Elder (died 1352 or 1354), was a Pomeranian noble and Vogt of the Neumark. Succeeding his father Wedego von Wedel as lord of Schivelbein in 1324, he is attested in that office in 1327 and represented Margrave Louis in 1345.

As lord of Schivelbein he raised the town walls, built the castle mill and founded the church of Saint Mary in 1338. During the conflict with the False Waldemar he apparently sympathized with the pretender, and was succeeded by his underage son Hans.

哈索·冯·魏德尔-希费尔拜因，人称“老哈索”（1352或1354年卒），是波美拉尼亚贵族、诺伊马克（新马尔克）的地方长官（福格特）。1324年，他继父亲韦德戈·冯·魏德尔之后成为希维德温领主；1327年已在该任上见于记载，1345年代表藩侯路德维希行事。

作为希维德温领主，他加高城墙、修建城堡磨坊，并于1338年兴建圣母教堂。在与“伪瓦尔德马”的纷争中，他似乎同情这位僭位者，死后由年幼的儿子汉斯继位。

en:
Wedego von Wedel (died 1324) was a Pomeranian knight and court marshal of the Wedel family. He served Margrave Waldemar of Brandenburg from 1304 and fought at the 1308 capture of Danzig, then from 1317 to 1322 was court marshal to Wartislaw IV of Pomerania.

At Pentecost 1319 he bought Schivelbein in the Neumark from Waldemar, with high and low justice. In 1324 he submitted with the Neumark estates to Margrave Louis of Wittelsbach and died that year at Uchtenhagen, leaving Schivelbein to his son Hasso.

韦德戈·冯·魏德尔（？—1324）是魏德尔家族出身的波美拉尼亚骑士和宫廷元帅。1304年起侍奉勃兰登堡侯爵瓦尔德马，参加1308年攻占但泽之役，1317至1322年改任波美拉尼亚公爵瓦季斯瓦夫四世的宫廷元帅。

1319年五旬节，他从瓦尔德马手中购得新马克的希维德温领地，享有高低裁判权。1324年他随新马克各等级归顺维特尔斯巴赫家族的路德维希侯爵，同年卒于乌希滕哈根，希维德温由其子哈索继承。

en:
Agnes of Habsburg (1257–1322), born at Rheinfelden, was a daughter of King Rudolph I of Germany and Gertrude of Hohenberg. On 24 October 1273, her father's coronation day at Aachen, she married Duke Albert II of Saxony, who had cast his vote for Rudolph, sealing the Ascanian–Habsburg alliance.

When Saxony was partitioned in 1296 she became Duchess of Saxe-Wittenberg, and after Albert's death in 1298 she was regent for her minor son Rudolf I until 1302. She died at Wittenberg on 11 October 1322.

哈布斯堡的阿格尼丝（1257—1322）生于莱茵费尔登，是德意志国王鲁道夫一世与霍恩堡的格特鲁德之女。1273年10月24日，即父亲在亚琛加冕之日，她嫁给萨克森公爵阿尔布雷希特二世，后者刚在选举中投票支持鲁道夫，这桩婚事就此结成阿斯坎尼家族与哈布斯堡家族的同盟。

1296年萨克森瓜分后，她成为萨克森—维滕贝格公爵夫人；1298年丈夫去世后，她为年幼的儿子鲁道夫一世摄政，直到1302年。1322年10月11日，她在维滕贝格去世。

en:
Agnes of Lindow-Ruppin (18 December 1314 – 9 May 1343) was the daughter of Count Ulrich I of Lindow-Ruppin and Adelheid of Schladen. After the death in 1329 of her first husband, Lord Henry II of Mecklenburg, she married Duke Rudolf I of Saxe-Wittenberg as his third wife in 1333.

She bore Rudolf's youngest son and successor Wenceslas I, later Elector of Saxony, and a daughter Helena. Agnes died at Wittenberg in 1343.

en:
Albert I (c. 1175–1260), younger son of Duke Bernhard III of Saxony, inherited the Saxon duchy in 1212 when his father's lands were divided, while his elder brother Henry took Anhalt.

He supported Emperor Otto IV against the Hohenstaufen and on 22 July 1227 commanded the imperial left flank at the Battle of Bornhöved, confirming his lordship over the counts of Holstein. Albert died at Lehnin Abbey on 7 October 1260; in 1296 his son Albert II and the three sons of his late son John I partitioned Saxony into Lauenburg and Wittenberg.

en:
Albert II (c. 1250–1298), a son of Duke Albert I of Saxony and Helen of Brunswick, ruled the Duchy of Saxony jointly with his elder brother John I from 1260 and later with John's sons. At the 1273 royal election he supported Rudolph of Habsburg and married Rudolph's daughter Agnes.

In 1292 he cast the Saxon vote for Adolf of Nassau. The partition of 1296 left him Saxe-Wittenberg, founding the Wittenberg Ascanian line, and he died near Aken on 25 August 1298.

en:
Kunigunde of Poland (c. 1295–1331 or 1333) was a Piast princess, daughter of Władysław I the Elbow-high, crowned King of Poland in 1320; her siblings included Casimir III the Great.

She first married Bernard, Duke of Świdnica, bearing him five children, among them Bolko II. Left a widow in 1326, she married secondly, in 1328, Rudolf I, Duke of Saxe-Wittenberg and future Elector of Saxony. She died at Wittenberg on 9 April 1331 or 1333.

波兰的库妮根德（约1295—1331或1333年）是皮亚斯特家族的公主，1320年加冕的波兰国王“矮子”瓦迪斯瓦夫一世之女，卡齐米日大帝的姐妹。

en:
Rudolf I (c. 1284–1356) ruled Saxe-Wittenberg from 1298, under his mother Agnes of Habsburg's regency until 1302. As Saxon elector he backed Frederick the Fair in the double election of 1314; after Frederick's defeat at Mühldorf in 1322 he reconciled with Emperor Louis IV.

The only elector at Charles IV's 1346 coronation, he received the Altmark in 1347; the Golden Bull of 1356 confirmed him as Elector of Saxony. He founded Wittenberg's All Saints' Monastery and died on 12 March 1356.

zh:
鲁道夫一世（约1284—1356）自1298年起统治萨克森-维滕贝格，1302年之前由母亲哈布斯堡的阿格尼丝摄政。作为萨克森选帝侯，他在1314年双重选举中支持表亲美男子腓特烈；1322年腓特烈在米尔多夫战败后，他与皇帝路德维希四世和解。

他是唯一出席1346年查理四世加冕礼的选帝侯，1347年获封阿尔特马克；1356年《金玺诏书》确认他为萨克森选帝侯。他在维滕贝格创立诸圣修道院，1356年3月12日去世。

en:
Rudolf II (c. 1307–1370), eldest son of Rudolf I, was Elector of Saxony from 1356. He fought at Crécy in 1346, leading the German auxiliaries after John of Bohemia fell, and received a thorn said to be from Christ's Crown of Thorns for Wittenberg's All Saints' Church.

He upheld his electorate against Saxe-Lauenburg claims, while the 1369 award of Lüneburg to his nephew Albert opened the Lüneburg War of Succession. Nearly blind late in life, he died in December 1370 without sons and was succeeded by his brother Wenceslas I.

zh:
鲁道夫二世（约1307—1370）是鲁道夫一世的长子，1356年起任萨克森选帝侯。1346年他在克雷西作战，波希米亚国王约翰战死后接统德意志援军，并获赠一根据称取自基督荆棘冠冕的荆棘，安置于维滕贝格诸圣堂。

en:
Wenceslas I (c. 1337–1388), son of Rudolf I, succeeded his brother Rudolf II as Duke and Elector of Saxe-Wittenberg in 1370. As elector he helped elect Wenceslas IV of Bohemia King of the Romans in 1376 and stood by Charles IV.

Charles IV invested Wenceslas and his nephew Albert with Brunswick-Lüneburg, but their claim failed in the Lüneburg War of Succession, and Wenceslas was defeated in 1388. He died on 15 May 1388 during the siege of Celle, amid rumours of poison.

zh:
文策尔一世（约1337—1388）是鲁道夫一世之子，1370年继兄长鲁道夫二世之后成为萨克森-维滕贝格公爵兼选帝侯。作为选帝侯，他在1376年参与选立波希米亚的瓦茨拉夫四世为罗马人的国王，始终站在皇帝查理四世一边。

查理四世将不伦瑞克-吕讷堡封授给他和侄子阿尔布雷希特，但他们的主张在吕讷堡继承战争中失败，文策尔于1388年兵败。1388年5月15日，他在策勒围城战期间去世，时人怀疑他是被毒杀。

en:
Agnes of Austria (c. 1315/1322–1392) was the second daughter of Duke Leopold I of Austria and Catherine of Savoy. After her father died in 1326 she grew up under the guardianship of her uncles. In 1338 she married Bolko II the Small, Duke of Świdnica, a match directed against the Luxembourg kings of Bohemia; the marriage was childless.

When Bolko died in 1368, his will left her his lands as her dower. She ruled them until her death at Świdnica on 2 February 1392, after which the duchies passed to the Bohemian crown.

奥地利的阿格尼丝（约1315/1322—1392）是奥地利公爵利奥波德一世与萨伏依的卡特琳的次女。1326年父亲去世后，她由叔父们监护长大。1338年，她嫁给希维德尼察公爵波尔科二世（“小个子”），这场联姻针对波希米亚的卢森堡王室，两人没有子女。

1368年波尔科去世，依遗嘱将希维德尼察等领地作为遗孀产留给她。她统治这些领地至1392年2月2日在希维德尼察去世，此后这些公国并入波希米亚。

en:
Bernard of Świdnica (c. 1291–1326), a son of Bolko I the Strict and Beatrix of Brandenburg, succeeded his father in 1301 under a regency that lasted until 1305. After partitions with his brothers he kept Świdnica for himself in 1322.

In 1310 he married Kunigunde, daughter of Władysław I the Elbow-high of Poland. He fought at Mühldorf in 1322 and joined the Teutonic Knights against Lithuania, then died on 6 May 1326. His son Bolko II the Small succeeded.

希维德尼察的伯纳德（约1291—1326）是“严厉者”波尔科一世与勃兰登堡的贝娅特丽克丝之子，1301年父亲去世后继位，由摄政团治理至1305年。经过与诸弟的几次瓜分，他在1322年独占希维德尼察。

en:
Bolko II the Small (c. 1312–1368) ruled Świdnica from 1326, the last independent Silesian duke of the Piast dynasty. When King John of Bohemia forced the other Silesian Piasts to pay homage in 1329–1331, Bolko refused and preserved his sovereignty through Poland, Hungary and the Habsburgs.

He married Agnes of Austria in 1338 and helped form the anti-Bohemian league of 1345. He gained Jawor in 1346 and Lusatia in 1364. Bolko died in 1368; his widow held the lands until 1392, when they passed to Bohemia.

波尔科二世（“小个子”，约1312—1368）自1326年起统治希维德尼察，是皮亚斯特王朝最后一位独立的西里西亚公爵。1329至1331年波希米亚国王约翰迫使其他西里西亚皮亚斯特王公效忠，波尔科拒不臣服，借波兰、匈牙利与哈布斯堡保住主权。

他于1338年娶奥地利的阿格尼丝，并参与促成1345年的反波希米亚同盟。他于1346年取得雅沃尔，1364年取得卢萨蒂亚。波尔科于1368年去世，遗孀领有这些领地直至1392年并入波希米亚。

en:
Anund Gårdske, or Anund from Russia, is known only from Adam of Bremen's chronicle, which names him king of part of Sweden around 1070. Summoned from Garðaríki, the Scandinavian name for Kievan Rus', he was a Christian.

He refused to perform the public sacrifice to the Norse gods, presumably at Uppsala, and was deposed at the thing. One of several claimants after King Stenkil, he left the assembly rejoicing to be found worthy of disgrace for Christ.

阿农德·戈尔德斯克意为“来自罗斯的阿农德”，仅见于亚当·冯·不来梅的教会史。据该书记载，约1070年他在瑞典一部分地区称王。他从加尔达里克——斯堪的纳维亚人对基辅罗斯的称呼——被召回瑞典，是一名基督徒。

en:
Anund Jacob (c. 1008–c. 1050), son of Olof Skötkonung, was made co-ruler c. 1019 and sole king in 1022, taking the Norse name Anund in place of his baptismal name Jakob. Surnamed Kolbränna, the Coal-burner, for burning opponents' houses, he promoted Christianity with missionaries from Hamburg-Bremen and minted coin at Sigtuna.

To check Danish hegemony he backed Norway's Olaf II against Cnut the Great and fought at the sea battle of Helgeå in 1026. He died c. 1050, leaving the throne to his half-brother Emund the Old.

en:
Axel Oxenstierna (1583–1654) was Sweden's Lord High Chancellor from 1612 to 1654 and architect of its modern state. He joined the Privy Council in 1609 and on taking office faced wars against Denmark, Poland-Lithuania and Russia, making peace with Denmark in 1613. As Gustavus Adolphus's chief minister he governed Livonia and Swedish-held Prussia, securing the Truce of Altmark in 1629.

After the king fell at Lützen in 1632, he led Sweden's war effort in Germany as head of Queen Christina's regency and framed the Instrument of Government of 1634. He also created Sweden's county administration, dying in office in 1654.

埃克塞尔·乌克森谢纳（1583—1654）自1612年至1654年任瑞典首相，是瑞典现代国家体制的缔造者。他1609年进入枢密院，就任时面临与丹麦、波兰立陶宛和俄国的战争，1613年与丹麦议和。作为古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫的首席大臣，他治理利沃尼亚和瑞典占领的普鲁士，1629年达成《阿尔特马克停战协定》。

1632年国王在吕岑阵亡后，他作为克里斯蒂娜女王摄政政府的首脑主持瑞典在德意志的战事，并制定1634年的《政府约法》。他还创立了瑞典的郡级行政体系，1654年卒于任上。

en:
Birger Jarl (c. 1210–1266), jarl of Sweden and head of the House of Bjälbo, married Ingeborg, sister of King Erik Eriksson, and received the title of jarl in 1248. Russian chronicles name him as the commander defeated by Alexander Nevsky at the Battle of the Neva in 1240.

He led the Second Swedish Crusade into Finland, probably around 1249–1250. He subdued the Tavastians and forced their conversion to Christianity.

When his young son Valdemar was elected king in 1250, Birger governed the kingdom as regent. Tradition credits him with founding Stockholm in 1252. He died in 1266.

en:
Birger Magnusson (c. 1280–1321) became King of Sweden in 1290 at the age of ten, when his father Magnus Ladulås died; Torkel Knutsson served as regent.

His reign was torn by feud with his brothers Erik and Valdemar, who imprisoned him at the Håtuna games in 1306. Released in 1308, he sought Danish aid but had to surrender the royal domain in exchange for other territories. At the Nyköping Banquet of 1317 he seized the dukes, whom Erik's Chronicle says were starved to death in Nyköping Castle.

The dukes' supporters drove him into Danish exile in 1318. His son Magnus was executed in 1320, and Birger died in Denmark after 31 May 1321.

比尔耶尔·马格努松（约1280—1321）于1290年十岁时成为瑞典国王，父亲马格努斯·拉杜洛斯去世后由托克尔·克努特松摄政。

他的统治被与弟弟埃里克、瓦尔德马尔的争斗撕裂，1306年他在“霍图纳游戏”中被两弟囚禁。1308年获释后，他向丹麦求援，却不得不放弃王室领地以换取其他地区。1317年的尼雪平宴会上，他拘捕两位公爵，二人据《埃里克编年史》记载在尼雪平城堡被饿死。

公爵们的支持者于1318年将他逐往丹麦流亡。他的儿子马格努斯于1320年被处决，比尔耶尔则于1321年5月31日之后在丹麦去世。

en:
Blanche of Namur (1320–1363), daughter of John I, Marquis of Namur, and Marie of Artois, became queen of Sweden and Norway through her marriage to King Magnus Eriksson. Magnus travelled to Namur to propose in June 1334, and the wedding followed in October or November 1335, possibly at Bohus Castle; she was crowned in Stockholm in July 1336.

She received Tunsberg in Norway and Lödöse in Sweden as wedding fiefs, exchanging Tunsberg for Bohus in 1353. Active and conspicuous in politics as well as at court, she became one of the best-known medieval queens of Sweden and Norway.

Many stories and songs attached to her; the Swedish nursery rhyme about a horse named Blanka is remembered as hers. Her sons were Eric XII of Sweden and Haakon VI of Norway, and she died in 1363.

那慕尔的布兰卡（1320—1363）是那慕尔侯爵约翰一世与阿图瓦的玛丽之女，因嫁给国王马格努斯·埃里克松成为瑞典与挪威王后。1334年6月马格努斯亲赴那慕尔求婚，婚礼于1335年10月或11月举行，地点可能是布胡斯城堡；1336年7月她在斯德哥尔摩加冕。

她得到挪威的滕斯贝格和瑞典的勒德瑟作为婚后封地，1353年又用滕斯贝格换取布胡斯。她在朝堂与政治中都十分活跃，成为瑞典与挪威中世纪最知名的王后之一。

许多故事与歌谣围绕她流传，瑞典那首讲小马名叫布兰卡的童谣据传与她有关。她的儿子是瑞典的埃里克十二世和挪威的哈康六世，她于1363年去世。

en:
Canute I, born Knut Eriksson (before 1150–1195/96), was son of the murdered Saint Erik. After his father's murder in 1160 he fled, returning to slay King Karl Sverkersson at Visingsö on 12 April 1167. He defeated rival claimants Kol and Burislev by c. 1173 and ruled all Sweden, aided by jarl Birger Brosa.

After c. 1180 he minted Sweden's first coinage in generations and made a trade treaty with Henry the Lion. He died in 1195/96 and was buried at Varnhem Abbey.

en:
Canute II, called Knut the Tall (Knut Långe, died 1234), was a Swedish noble of the House of Bjälbo and a councillor to the young Eric XI. After Eric was overthrown following the Battle of Olustra in 1229, Canute became king and was recognized by 1231.

Laws from his reign barred creditors from entering debtors' homes without an official and required the king to hold judicial reviews at least every third year. He died in 1234 and was buried at Sko Abbey; Eric XI then regained the throne.

en:
Charles VII (Karl Sverkersson, c. 1130–1167), son of Sverker the Elder, held Götaland after his father's murder in 1156 while Eric IX ruled in Svealand. In 1161 he killed his rival Magnus II at Örebro and was recognized as king of Sweden.

His short reign saw the first Swedish archbishopric established at Uppsala, Stefan becoming its first archbishop. On 12 April 1167 he was slain on Visingsö by backers of Knut Eriksson, who took the throne; his son Sverker later became king.

en:
Emund the Old, also called the Bad (died c. 1060), was a son of Olof Skötkonung by his Slavic co-wife Edla and succeeded his half-brother Anund Jacob c. 1050. Baptized but lukewarm in the faith, he defied the Archbishopric of Bremen by keeping his own bishop, Osmundus, consecrated in Poland.

His son Anund perished on an eastern expedition, and drought brought famine in 1056. Emund died c. 1060, the last king of the old Swedish dynasty; Stenkil, possibly his son-in-law, succeeded him.

en:
Eric IX, called Saint Erik (c. 1125–1160), ruled Sweden from about 1156 as founder of the House of Erik. Legend credits him with leading the first Swedish crusade to Finland and codifying the laws known as King Erik's Law.

On Ascension Day, 18 May 1160, after hearing Mass near Uppsala, he was set upon by rebels backing the Danish prince Magnus Henriksson, stabbed and beheaded. Venerated as a martyr, he became Sweden's patron saint; his son Canute I took the throne in 1167.

en:
Erik Magnusson (c. 1282–1318) was the second son of King Magnus Ladulås. He was Duke of Södermanland and rival of his brother King Birger.

In 1306 he helped force the execution of Torkel Knutsson and seized Birger at the Håtuna games. In 1309 he fought the kings of Norway and Denmark, until the peace of Helsingborg divided Sweden and gave Erik several provinces.

In 1312 he married Ingeborg of Norway; their son Magnus later ruled both Sweden and Norway. At the Nyköping Banquet of 1317 Birger seized him and his brother Valdemar; both died in Nyköping Castle's dungeon, apparently starved.

en:
Eric the Victorious (Erik Segersäll, c. 945–c. 995) was the first independently attested Swedish king, ruling in Uppland from c. 970. His epithet comes from the Battle of Fýrisvellir near Uppsala, where saga tradition says he defeated his nephew Styrbjörn the Strong, who invaded with Danish and Jomsviking support.

The chronicler Adam of Bremen wrote that Eric invaded Denmark, drove out Sweyn Forkbeard and briefly ruled there. Baptized in Denmark but later back among the old gods, he probably founded Sigtuna and died c. 995, leaving his son Olof Skötkonung the throne.

Eric X (Erik Knutsson, c. 1180–1216), son of Canute I, claimed the Swedish throne against Sverker Karlsson. Three brothers fell at Älgarås in 1205; Eric fled to Norway, returned in 1208 and defeated Sverker at Lena, then slew him at Gestilren in July 1210.

Later that year he married Rikissa, sister of Valdemar II of Denmark, and in November became the first Swedish king known to be crowned. He died suddenly on Visingsö on 10 April 1216; his posthumous son later ruled as Eric XI.

埃里克十世（本名埃里克·克努特松，约1180—1216）是克努特一世之子，向斯渥克尔二世争夺瑞典王位。1205年，他的三个兄弟战死在艾尔加罗斯，埃里克逃往挪威；1208年他回国，在莱纳击败斯渥克尔，又于1210年7月在耶斯蒂尔伦将其击杀。

同年晚些时候，他迎娶丹麦国王瓦尔德马二世的妹妹里基莎，11月成为第一位有记载的受加冕瑞典国王。1216年4月10日他在维辛瑟岛暴卒，遗腹子后来继位为埃里克十一世。

en:
Eric XI (Erik Eriksson, 1216–1250), surnamed the Lisp and Lame, was the posthumous son of Eric X and Rikissa of Denmark. He became king at six in 1222, was overthrown by Knut Långe at Olustra in 1229 and fled to Denmark, returning after Knut's death in 1234.

He ruled in the shadow of his jarls Ulf Fase and brother-in-law Birger Jarl. In 1247 a Folkung rising was crushed at Sparrsätra. Eric died on 2 February 1250, the last of the House of Erik; Birger Jarl's son Valdemar became king.

en:
Håkan the Red (Swedish: Håkan Röde) was a Swedish king who ruled for roughly five years in the second half of the 11th century, one of the rival claimants after the death of Stenkil. Later tradition makes him a son of Stenkil, born and buried at Levene in Västergötland.

Sources place him variously after Halsten and beside the short-reigned Anund Gårdske. When he died around 1079, Halsten and Inge the Elder emerged as rulers.

en:
Halsten Stenkilsson, son of Stenkil, was king of Sweden for a few years after 1067, after the civil war of 1066 left the two Erics dead. Adam of Bremen says he was soon driven out in favour of the Christian Anund Gårdske.

He may later have ruled Västergötland with his brother Inge the Elder, since a papal letter of 1081 addresses two kings, A and I. The Westrogothic law's king list calls him courteous and a fair judge, and he was the father of Philip and Inge the Younger.

en:
Bridget of Sweden (c. 1303–1373) was a Swedish mystic and founder of the Bridgettine Order. Born Birgitta Birgersdotter to a noble family of Uppland, she married Ulf Gudmarsson in 1316 and bore eight children. After her husband died in 1344 she devoted herself to visions. From 1350 she lived in Rome, seeking papal approval for a new order and the pope's return from Avignon, and Urban V confirmed its rule in 1370 for Vadstena Convent.

She urged church reform and died after her Jerusalem pilgrimage, was canonized in 1391 by Boniface IX, and became a patron saint of Europe.

瑞典的彼济达（约1303—1373）是瑞典神秘主义者、彼济达修会的创办人。她本名贝尔吉塔·比耶尔斯多特，出身乌普兰贵族家庭，1316年嫁给乌尔夫·古德马尔松，生下八个子女。1344年丈夫去世后，她潜心于神视异象。1350年她定居罗马，为新修会寻求教廷批准，并呼吁教宗从阿维尼翁返回；1370年教宗乌尔班五世批准了瓦斯泰纳修会的会规。

她呼吁教会改革，在赴耶路撒冷朝圣后去世，1391年由教宗卜尼法斯九世封圣，后成为欧洲的主保圣人之一。

en:
Inge the Elder, son of Stenkil, was king of Sweden from before 1080 until his death around 1110. A stern Christian, he refused to perform the pagan blót at Uppsala and was driven into exile, the Swedes choosing Blot-Sweyn as king.

After three winters he returned, surprised Sweyn in his house and slew him, restoring Christianity. Around 1100 he founded Vreta Abbey near Linköping, Sweden's first nunnery, with Queen Helena. He died about 1110 and was followed by his nephews Philip and Inge the Younger.

en:
Inge the Younger, son of Halsten and nephew of Inge the Elder, was king of Sweden from about 1110, ruling with his brother Philip until 1118 and then alone. He may already have died when Sigurd the Crusader invaded Småland in the Kalmar Crusade of 1123.

He is said to have died in Östergötland by a poisoned drink, a tale later attached to his queen. With his death around 1125 the House of Stenkil ended, and the crown passed to Sverker the Elder.

en:
Johan Anders Jägerhorn (1757–1825) was a Finnish nobleman and major in the Swedish army, born near Helsinki when Finland belonged to Sweden. He founded and led the secret Walhalla order at the Suomenlinna fortress. In 1788 he joined the Anjala conspiracy, a group of officers opposing Gustav III's war with Russia; Jägerhorn himself advocated Finnish sovereignty. Condemned to death for treason, he was exiled to Hamburg, where he put Irish rebels in touch with France before the 1798 rising.

After two years in the Tower of London (1799–1801), he returned home and sat as a noble delegate at the 1809 Porvoo Diet that established the autonomous Grand Duchy of Finland.

en:
Johan Sverkersson, or John I (c. 1201–1222), was the son of King Sverker II and Ingegerd Birgersdotter. While still an infant in 1202, his father gave him his grandfather's title. After Erik Knutsson died in 1216, the Swedish aristocracy made the teenage Johan king against the Pope's wishes.

Crowned in 1219, he confirmed and enlarged his father's privileges for the bishops. A Swedish expedition against the Estonians ended in disaster, and he died unmarried and childless of illness on Visingsö on 10 March 1222.

While still an infant in 1202, his father gave him his grandfather's title. en:
Jöran Persson (c. 1530–1568), King Eric XIV of Sweden's most trusted counselor, was the Sala-born son of a priest. After studying at Wittenberg in the 1550s he served Gustav I and then Prince Eric, and was raised to the nobility when Eric took the throne in 1560.

He headed the king's network of spies and was widely resented for his influence over Eric. As prosecutor and the king's representative in the royal court he had a role in sentencing; the court passed some 300 death sentences while he served.

In 1563 he crushed the revolt of Duke John of Finland and confined him at Gripsholm, and after the Sture murders of 1567 he defended the killings. After Eric's deposition in 1568 he was arrested and executed.

约兰·佩尔松（约1530—1568）是瑞典国王埃里克十四世最信任的谋臣，生于萨拉，父亲是当地牧师。1550年代他在维滕贝格求学，回国后先后效力古斯塔夫一世与埃里克王子，1560年埃里克即位时被封为贵族。

他掌管国王的间谍网络，因对埃里克的影响力而广遭反感。他在王室法庭兼任检察官和国王代表，参与量刑；他任职期间，法庭判处约300人死刑。

1563年他镇压芬兰公爵约翰的叛乱，将其囚禁于格里普斯科尔摩城堡；1567年斯图雷谋杀案后，他又为这些杀戮开脱。1568年埃里克被废黜后，他被捕并处决。

en:
Knut Jonsson (died between 1345 and 1347) was a Swedish knight of the Aspenäs family, the son of Johan Filipsson. Appointed lawspeaker of Östergötland in 1310, he kept the post for nearly four decades and sat on the council of Birger Magnusson and then of Magnus Eriksson, eventually rising to drots, the highest secular office in the realm.

He is last attested in 1345 and was dead by 1347. Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century writers sometimes called him Knut Jonsson Blå, tying him to the legendary Joar Blå, a descent no source supports.

en:
Magnus Gabriel De la Gardie (1622–1686) was a Swedish statesman and soldier, the son of Field Marshal Jacob De la Gardie. He became Queen Christina's favorite, married the future Charles X Gustav's sister and joined the Privy Council in 1647. He lost Christina's favor in 1653 but returned when his brother-in-law became king in 1654.

He held three great offices: Treasurer, Chancellor and Steward. As Lord High Chancellor from 1660 he led Charles XI's regency and championed the French alliance. The defeat at Fehrbellin in 1675 and the Great Reduction of 1680 destroyed his power; he died in 1686.

en:
Magnus Eriksson (1316–1374) was three years old when Swedish nobles elected him king at Mora in July 1319 to bar his uncle Birger Magnusson from returning to power. In August Norway acknowledged him too, as the grandson of Haakon V, and two crowns sat on one child.

His declaration of majority in 1331 provoked a Norwegian noble rising. In 1332 he bought Scania from Duke Johan of Holstein, raising taxes and eventually sparking war with Denmark; in 1335 he outlawed thralldom for Christian-born children, and his reign gave Sweden its first countryside law code and mining charters. Critics such as Bridget of Sweden called him weak and ruled by favourites, and Denmark retook Scania in 1360.

In 1364 Swedish nobles brought in Albert of Mecklenburg, who was crowned king. Magnus withdrew to Norway, where his son Haakon had reigned since 1355, and drowned in a shipwreck in 1374.

1364年瑞典贵族引来梅克伦堡的阿尔布雷希特并将其加冕为王。马格努斯退居挪威，其子哈康自1355年起在那里为王；1374年他在一场海难中溺亡。

Magnus I, called the Strong (Magnus Nilsson, c. 1106–1134), was the son of Denmark's King Niels and Margaret, daughter of Sweden's Inge the Elder. After his cousin Inge the Younger died in the 1120s, he claimed Sweden through his mother and won recognition from the Geats after King Ragnvald Knaphövde was murdered.

In 1127 he married Richeza of Poland. In 1131 he had Canute Lavard killed, sparking civil war in Denmark, and he fell to Eric Emune at Fotevik on 4 June 1134.

en:
Magnus Ladulås (c. 1240–1290), second son of Birger Jarl, was King of Sweden from 1275 until his death. On his father's death in 1266 he inherited the title Duke of Sweden.

In 1275, backed by King Eric Klipping of Denmark, he rebelled with his brother Erik against their elder brother King Valdemar and defeated him at the Battle of Hova, being elected king at the Stones of Mora the following month.

He lost provinces in Götaland to Valdemar in 1277, recovered them around 1278 and added the title King of the Goths. He died in 1290, leaving his ten-year-old son Birger to rule under the regency of Torkel Knutsson.

en:
Mikael Agricola (c. 1510–1557) was a Finnish Lutheran clergyman and reformer, regarded as the father of literary Finnish. Born at Pernå in Swedish-ruled Finland, he studied at Viborg and became a scribe in the bishop's office at Turku.

From 1536 he studied at Wittenberg under Martin Luther and Philipp Melanchthon. He began translating the New Testament into Finnish in 1537 and returned to Turku as rector of the cathedral school in 1539. His New Testament, Se Wsi Testamenti, appeared in 1548; his prayer books and hymns also helped establish written Finnish.

In 1554 he was consecrated bishop of Turku without papal approval. He died in 1557 while returning from Moscow, where he had helped negotiate the Treaty of Novgorod.

米卡埃尔·阿格里科拉（约1510—1557）是芬兰路德宗神职人员和宗教改革家，被誉为芬兰书面语之父。他生于当时属瑞典的芬兰佩尔诺，在维堡求学后到图尔库的主教办事处任书记。

1536年起，他在维滕贝格师从马丁·路德与菲利普·梅兰希通。1537年他开始将《新约》译成芬兰语，1539年返回图尔库担任座堂学校校长。他的《新约》译本于1548年刊行，祈祷书与赞美诗也帮助奠定了芬兰语的书面规范。

1554年，他未经教皇批准被祝圣为图尔库主教。1557年，他在赴莫斯科协助谈判《诺夫哥罗德条约》返程途中去世。

en:
Olof Skötkonung (c. 980–1022), son of Eric the Victorious, succeeded his father as king of Sweden around 995. He is the first Swedish king known to have ruled both the Swedes and the Geats, and he minted Sweden's first coins at Sigtuna. Baptized in 1008, he fostered Christianity but tolerated the pagan cult.

In 1000 he and Sweyn Forkbeard of Denmark destroyed Olaf Tryggvason's fleet at the Battle of Svolder and divided Norway. He died in 1022, leaving the crown to his son Anund Jacob.

en:
Philip Halstensson, son of Halsten and nephew of Inge the Elder, was king of Sweden from about 1105 or 1110 until 1118, ruling jointly with his younger brother Inge the Younger after their uncle's death. The Westrogothic law's regnal list calls him a good king, but almost nothing else is recorded of his reign.

The Hervarar saga says he ruled only briefly and married Ingegerd, daughter of the Norwegian king Harald Hardrada. He was probably buried beside his brother at Vreta Abbey near Linköping.

en:
Stenkil (died 1066) became king of Sweden around 1060, succeeding the childless Emund the Old, whose daughter he married, and founding the dynasty that bears his name. Probably rooted in Västergötland, he was a devout Christian who worked with bishops from Hamburg and Bremen, yet forbade them to destroy the pagan temple at Uppsala for fear of revolt.

His reign saw fighting against Harald Hardrada of Norway. When he died in 1066, about the time of Hastings, his sons Halsten and Inge the Elder later held the throne.

en:
Sverker the Elder (c. 1100–1156), of non-royal birth, became king of Sweden around 1130 after Stenkil's line ended and founded the House of Sverker, rival of the House of Erik for the next century. In 1142 a Swedish fleet entered the Gulf of Finland, breaking the long peace with Novgorod.

When Sweyn III of Denmark invaded Småland in 1153, Sverker avoided battle until winter and peasant resistance forced the Danes out. On Christmas Day 1156 he was murdered at Alebäck bridge near Alvastra; his son Charles later became king of Sweden.

en:
Sverker the Younger, or Sverker II (before 1167–1210), was the son of King Karl Sverkersson of Sweden and grew up in Denmark after his father was killed in 1167. Chosen king in 1196, he issued a charter of church privileges in 1200, Sweden's oldest surviving document, and married Ingegerd, Jarl Birger Brosa's daughter.

In 1205 he defeated the sons of Knut Eriksson at Älgarås, but in 1208 Erik Knutsson overthrew him at the Battle of Lena. Sverker was killed at the Battle of Gestilren on 17 July 1210.

en:
Valdemar Birgersson (1239–1302), eldest son of Birger Jarl, was elected King of Sweden in 1250 after his uncle Erik Eriksson died, and crowned at Linköping in 1251. Birger Jarl ruled as regent until 1266. Valdemar married Sofia of Denmark in 1260, but his affair with her sister Jutta in 1272 forced a pilgrimage to Rome.

On 14 June 1275 his brother Magnus Ladulås defeated and deposed him at Hova. He was imprisoned in Nyköping Castle in 1288 and died on 26 December 1302.

en:
Valdemar Magnusson (c. 1282–1318), third son of King Magnus Ladulås, was made Duke of Finland at his brother Birger's coronation in 1302. With his brother Erik he warred against King Birger: the Håtuna capture of 1306 and the Peace of Helsingborg in 1310 left the realm divided between the king and the two dukes, and in 1315 Valdemar took the east, including Stockholm.

In 1312 he married Ingeborg of Norway in Oslo. Seized with Erik at the Nyköping Banquet on 10 December 1317, he died in Nyköping Castle in 1318.

en:
Huldrych Zwingli (1484–1531) was the Zurich priest who began the Reformation in German-speaking Switzerland. He studied at Vienna and Basel and pastored at Glarus and Einsiedeln, where he read Erasmus. In 1519 he became people’s priest of the Grossmünster in Zurich and preached through the Gospel of Matthew instead of the Sunday readings, and nearly died in that year’s plague.

In 1522 he and others ate smoked sausages in Lent; the Affair of the Sausages is counted as the start of the Swiss Reformation. After the 1523 disputations images were removed, and on 13 April 1525 he celebrated communion with wooden cups and a German liturgy.

At Marburg in 1529 he and Luther agreed on fourteen of fifteen articles, but parted over the Eucharist. In 1531 the Catholic Five States routed Zurich’s 3500 men near Kappel, and Zwingli was among about 500 dead. Heinrich Bullinger succeeded him.

乌利希·慈运理（1484—1531）是在德语区瑞士发起宗教改革的苏黎世神父。他曾在维也纳和巴塞尔求学，先后任格拉鲁斯和艾因西德伦的堂区牧师，在艾因西德伦读到了伊拉斯谟。1519年他出任苏黎世格罗斯明斯特教堂的民众神父，不依周日读经而逐章讲解《马太福音》，同年还在鼠疫中险些丧命。

1522年大斋期间，他与一些人分吃熏香肠，这起“香肠事件”被视为瑞士宗教改革的开端。1523年的辩论会后圣像被撤去；1525年4月13日，他用木杯和德语礼仪主持圣餐。

1529年的马尔堡会谈上，他与路德在十五条中有十四条达成一致，却在圣餐中基督是否临在上分歧不下。1531年天主教五州在卡佩尔附近击溃苏黎世的3500人，慈运理也在约500名阵亡者之中。海因里希·布林格随后接任。

en:
Theophrastus Bombast von Hohenheim (1493–1541), known as Paracelsus, was a physician and philosopher of the German Renaissance who staked medicine on observation rather than inherited authority. Born at Einsiedeln, Schwyz, he learned medicine from his father, took his doctorate at Ferrara in 1515 or 1516, and served as an army surgeon.

In 1526 he reportedly cured the Basel printer Johann Froben. In 1527 he became city physician of Basel, lecturing at the university in German rather than Latin, and on 23 June burned Avicenna's Canon of Medicine in the market square, telling students that ‘the patients are your textbook’.

His attacks on other physicians drove him from Basel in 1528. In Nuremberg he called guaiac wood useless against syphilis, and the Leipzig faculty banned his book on the disease. He published his Great Surgery Book in 1536 and died at Salzburg in September 1541.

特奥夫拉斯图斯·邦巴斯特·冯·霍恩海姆（1493—1541），人称帕拉塞尔苏斯，是德意志文艺复兴时期的医生与哲学家，主张医学应建立在观察之上，而不是承袭旧权威。他生于施维茨州的艾恩西德恩，从父亲那里学医，1515或1516年在费拉拉获得博士学位，后来当了军医。

1526年，据传他治好了巴塞尔印刷商约翰·弗罗本。1527年他出任巴塞尔城市医生，在大学用德语而非拉丁语讲课，并于6月23日在集市广场烧掉阿维森纳的《医典》，对学生说“病人就是你们的教科书”。

他对其他医生的抨击迫使他于1528年离开巴塞尔。在纽伦堡，他称愈创木对梅毒无效，莱比锡医学院随即禁止了他论此病的著作。1536年他出版《大外科学》，1541年9月在萨尔茨堡去世。

en:
Gunzelin III (died 1274) inherited the County of Schwerin in 1228 from his father Henry I, ruling under his mother Audacia's regency. After Bornhöved, the captive Duke Otto I of Brunswick confirmed the fiefs Schwerin held from him. In 1230 he was betrothed to Margaret of Mecklenburg, and married her in 1241.

With his mother he founded Zarrentin Abbey in 1246. On his death in 1274, his sons Helmold III and Niklot I split the county into Schwerin and Wittenburg lines.

贡采林三世（？—1274）于1228年继承父亲亨利一世的什未林伯国，由母亲奥达恰摄政。博恩赫沃德之战后，被俘的不伦瑞克公爵奥托一世确认了什未林从不伦瑞克领受的封地。1230年他与梅克伦堡的玛格丽特定亲，1241年成婚。

en:
Henry III of Schwerin (died 1344), son of Count Helmold III, was born no earlier than 1289. Until 1307–1310 he ruled jointly with his elder brother Gunzelin V, whose childless death left Henry the greater part of the county, while kinsmen held its outlying lands.

In 1316 he married Elisabeth of Holstein-Schauenburg. Henry died in 1344 without children, the last of the elder line of Schwerin counts, and his lands passed to Nicholas II and Otto I.

en:
Helmold III (before 1228 – c. 1296) was the son of Count Gunzelin III of Schwerin and Margaret of Mecklenburg. On his father's death in 1274 he inherited the Schwerin portion of the divided county. He married three times, taking Margaret of Schleswig as his wife in 1264.

His son by the first marriage, Gunzelin V, succeeded him in 1296, while Henry III, his son by Margaret, later held Boizenburg and Crivitz. Helmold last appears in a charter of 25 August 1295 and was dead by May 1296.

en:
Niklot I (c. 1250–1323) was the youngest son of Count Gunzelin III of Schwerin and Margaret of Mecklenburg. When his father died in 1274, the brothers divided the county and Niklot received Wittenburg, founding the Schwerin-Wittenburg line. He married Elisabeth of Holstein-Kiel, and after her death Miroslawa of Pomerania.

His son Gunzelin VI succeeded as count at Wittenburg, while his daughter Anastasia married Duke Waldemar IV of Schleswig. Niklot died in 1323.

en:
Elisabeth of Hohnstein (c. 1302–1380) was the daughter of Count Henry IV of Hohnstein-Klettenberg. By 9 September 1331 she was married to Count Günther XXI of Schwarzburg-Blankenburg, the future anti-king, and bore him a son, Henry XIII, and four daughters.

When Günther died at Frankfurt in June 1349 after renouncing the crown, Elisabeth survived him by more than thirty years as countess dowager. She died around 4 April 1380.

霍恩施泰因的伊丽莎白（约1302—1380）是霍恩施泰因-克莱滕贝格伯爵海因里希四世之女。1331年9月9日之前，她已嫁给施瓦茨堡-布兰肯堡伯爵、后来的对立国王京特尔二十一世，生下儿子海因里希十三世和四个女儿。

1349年6月京特尔放弃王位后在法兰克福去世，伊丽莎白作为伯爵遗孀又活了三十多年，于1380年4月4日前后亡故。

en:
Elisabeth of Weimar-Orlamünde (c. 1308–1363) was the daughter of Count Otto IV of Weimar-Orlamünde and Catherine of Hesse. Before 5 June 1321 she married Count Henry VII (X) of Schwarzburg-Blankenburg, who ruled Blankenburg and half of Arnstadt; their children included Henry IX and Günther XI.

Her husband died on pilgrimage to Jerusalem before March 1338, leaving her a dowager countess. She died in 1363 and was buried at Saalfeld.

en:
Günther von Schwarzburg (1304–1349), count of Schwarzburg-Blankenburg, was a younger son of Count Henry VII. By 1331 he had married Elisabeth of Hohnstein and had five children. A diplomat of Emperor Louis IV, he led the Wittelsbach party after Louis's death in 1347.

On 30 January 1349 four electors chose him anti-king against Charles IV, whose army routed his forces at Eltville. By the Treaty of Eltville he renounced the crown; he died at Frankfurt on 14 June 1349 and was buried in Frankfurt Cathedral.

施瓦茨堡的京特尔（1304—1349），施瓦茨堡-布兰肯堡伯爵，是伯爵海因里希七世较年幼的儿子。1331年他已与霍恩施泰因的伊丽莎白成婚，两人育有五个子女。作为皇帝路德维希四世麾下的外交官，他在1347年路德维希死后成为维特尔斯巴赫一派的领袖。

Gunther XI of Schwarzburg-Blankenburg (9 September 1331 - 6 June 1368) was a son of Count Henry VII, who died on pilgrimage to Jerusalem in 1338, and Elizabeth of Weimar-Orlamunde. Before June 1347 he married Elizabeth of Hohnstein-Sondershausen.

He ruled half of Arnstadt and, from 1356, Sondershausen, and in June 1367 he held Belitz as a pledge lord. He died in 1368 and was buried in the Liebfrauenkirche at Arnstadt, leaving sons Henry XIV and Gunther XVI.

en:
Henry VI, also numbered Henry VII (before 1285–1324), ruled Schwarzburg-Blankenburg, which he inherited from his father Count Henry V; his mother was Sophie of Halych. In 1290 he received Blankenburg, adding Wachsenburg and Stadtilm in 1306 and Saalfeld in 1323.

His son by Christina of Gleichen, Günther XXI, was elected King of Germany at Frankfurt in 1349 against Charles IV. Henry died on 11 November 1324 on campaign in Brandenburg and was buried in Berlin's Grey Monastery.

en:
Henry VII (X), count of Schwarzburg-Blankenburg (c. 1298–1338), was the elder son of Count Henry VI and Christine von Gleichen, and elder brother of the anti-king Günther XXI. From his father's death in 1324 he ruled Blankenburg, and he held half of Arnstadt from 1326.

Before 5 June 1321 he married Elisabeth, daughter of Count Otto IV of Weimar-Orlamünde; their children included Henry IX, Günther XI and Jutta. He died on pilgrimage to Jerusalem before March 1338, and his widow survived until 1363.

en:
Henry IX (XII), called the Younger (c. 1325–1372/73), was the elder son of Count Henry VII (X) of Schwarzburg-Blankenburg and Elisabeth of Weimar-Orlamünde. In 1338 he married Agnes of Hohnstein-Sondershausen.

He later held a cluster of Schwarzburg lordships: Schlotheim, Rudolstadt, Frankenhausen, half of Arnstadt, Blankenburg, Saalfeld, Sondershausen and Ehrenstein. He sat as imperial judge in 1363–1365 and served as captain of the Altmark in 1366, and died between 1372 and 1373.

Sophie of Schwarzburg-Blankenburg was the daughter of Count Gunther IX, who was elected anti-king against Charles IV in January 1349 and died at Frankfurt that June, and Elizabeth of Hohnstein. In November 1353 she married Count George of Kafernburg, a union dissolved despite a papal dispensation.

Before November 1357 she married Frederick of Orlamunde-Lauenstein, later Count Henry XI of Stolberg, and finally John II of Schwarzburg-Wachsenburg. She is last documented in 1394 and 1395.

His wife Matilda of the Mark died before 1327, and Godfrey himself died on 18 October that year, after only three years ruling alone.

Burtel Orbelian, called the Long-Lived, ruled the Orbelian principality of Syunik from about 1300 to 1349, succeeding his father Elikum. He reunited the divided Orbelian lands and served as commander-in-chief of the Armenian and Georgian armies.

Syunik prospered under him: the architect Momik built the churches of Areni and Spitakavor and the Burtelashen mausoleum church at Noravank. In the 1340s the Ilkhanids made him governor-amir of Sultaniya and Tabriz. After his death around 1349, succession strife weakened Syunik.

Aleksandr Vasilyevich (died 1331) was Prince of Suzdal from 1309, when he succeeded his father Vasily, and Grand Prince of Vladimir from 1328. In 1327 he joined Ivan I of Moscow in Ozbeg Khan's punitive expedition against Tver after its anti-Tatar uprising, and the city was sacked.

The khan rewarded him in 1328 with the grand princely title, shared with Ivan: Aleksandr received Vladimir while Ivan took Novgorod and Kostroma. He died in 1331 and his brother Konstantin inherited Suzdal.

Konstantin Vasilyevich (died 1355), a younger son of Prince Vasily of Suzdal, succeeded his brother as prince of Suzdal in 1331. Exploiting strife at the Golden Horde capital Sarai, he secured Nizhny Novgorod and Gorodets, and in 1350 moved his seat there as grand prince of Nizhny Novgorod-Suzdal.

After Simeon of Moscow died in 1353, he contested the throne with Ivan II, backed by Novgorod, but the khan granted the patent to Ivan. He made peace with Moscow in 1355 and died the same year.

Gabriele Tadino (c. 1476–1543) was an Italian soldier and military engineer born near Bergamo. He entered Venetian service in 1508 and in 1513 took charge of Crema's fortifications. In 1522 he helped defend Rhodes against the Ottomans as superintendent of the Order's fortresses, losing his right eye to an arquebus shot while inspecting them.

In 1532 he commanded imperial artillery at Vienna when Suleiman's army turned back. Titian portrayed him in 1538 in the black robe of a Hospitaller knight. He died at Venice in 1543.

1532年他指挥帝国炮兵驻守维也纳，苏莱曼的大军最终撤退。1538年提香为他画像，画中他身着医院骑士的黑袍。1543年他在威尼斯去世。

en:
Tariácuri (fl. c. 1350–1390), whose name means 'strong wind' in Purépecha, is traditionally hailed as the founder of the Purépecha state, credited with raising it from a single city-state to the dominant power of the region. The son of Pauacume II, lord of Pátzcuaro, he was born into the powerful uacúsecha clan.

Tradition tells that the sun god Curicaueri, the clan's patron, sent him in a dream to build a unified state. He allied the neighbouring towns and expanded to the southwest and across the Pátzcuaro basin, though enemies from Curinguaro once drove his nephews to flight before he overcame the setback.

After his death the domain was divided: his son Hiquingaje took Pátzcuaro, while his nephews Tangaxoan and Hiripan took Tzintzuntzan and Ihuatzio and kept up his alliance and his expansion.

塔里亚库里（约1350—1390年在世）的普雷佩查语名字意为“强风”，相传为普雷佩查国家的缔造者，把一座城邦发展成称霸一方的势力。他是帕茨夸罗首领保阿库梅二世之子，出身湖盆地区权势显赫的瓦库塞查氏族。

传说氏族的守护神太阳神库里考埃里在梦中派他建立统一的普雷佩查国家。他联合邻近诸城，再向西南扩张，进而控制整个帕茨夸罗湖盆地；来自库林瓜罗的敌人曾迫使他的侄子们出逃，但他最终克服了这一挫折。

他去世后疆土分给后人：儿子伊金加赫得帕茨夸罗，侄子坦加肖安和伊里潘分得钦聪灿与伊瓦齐奥，他们保持联盟并继续扩张。

en:
Gunzelin VI of Schwerin (died 1327) was the eldest son of Count Nikolaus I of Schwerin-Wittenburg. He once held a canon's post at Schwerin Cathedral but had returned to secular life by 1312, and after his father's death he was named ruling count at Wittenburg in 1323.

He married Richardis, heiress of Count Otto IV of Tecklenburg; their son Nikolaus thereby inherited the County of Tecklenburg. Gunzelin died in 1327, succeeded by his son Otto I.

他娶泰克伦堡伯爵奥托四世的女继承人里查迪斯为妻，他们的儿子尼古劳斯因此继承了泰克伦堡伯国。贡采林于1327年去世，由其子奥托一世继位。

en:
Nicholas I (c. 1300–c. 1368), son of Gunzelin VI of Schwerin and Richardis of Tecklenburg, inherited Tecklenburg-Ibbendüren and other lands from his uncle Otto V in 1328, founding the Tecklenburg-Schwerin line.

He campaigned against the Frisians and rival knights, lost territory to the bishop of Osnabrück in 1350 but took Iburg in 1354. After inheriting Schwerin in 1357, he sold it to Mecklenburg in 1358. Pope Urban V excommunicated him in 1364.

en:
Taj al-Din Chelebi was the founder and first bey of the Taceddinid principality at Niksar in northeastern Anatolia. He inherited his lands from his father Doghan Shah in 1346 or 1348, at first ruling under Eretnid suzerainty.

In 1379 he repelled attacks on Niksar by the Eretnid vizier Kadi Burhan al-Din and ceased tribute; that year he married Eudokia, daughter of the Trebizond emperor Alexios III. Defeated by him in 1381, he died fighting in October 1386 and was succeeded by his son Mahmud.

1379年，他击退埃雷特纳维齐尔卡迪·布尔汉丁对尼克萨尔的进攻，停止纳贡；同年与特拉布宗皇帝阿历克塞三世之女埃夫多基亚成婚。1381年他被布尔汉丁击败，1386年10月战死，其子马哈茂德继位。

en:
Muhammad Bey (died c. 1328) was a son of Yunus Bey, founder of the Teke beylik at Antalya. In 1317 he supported the Ilkhanid commander Demirtaş in seizing and executing his uncle Dündar Bey, and received Antalya as his reward.

After Yunus died he ruled Antalya as the senior Teke bey while his brother Hızır governed Korkuteli. When Ibn Battuta visited Antalya in 1332, Hızır had already succeeded to the city.

穆罕默德·贝伊（约1328年卒）是据有安塔利亚的泰凯贝伊国开国者尤努斯·贝伊之子。1317年，他支持伊儿汗国将领德米尔塔什擒杀伯父敦达尔贝伊，并因此受封安塔利亚。

尤努斯死后，他作为长支泰凯贝伊统治安塔利亚，弟弟赫泽尔治理科尔库泰利。1332年伊本·白图泰到访安塔利亚时，赫泽尔已继位。

en:
Sinanüddin Hızır Bey was the Antalya ruler of the Teke branch of the Hamidid dynasty, a son of its founder Yunus Bey. Under his father and elder brother Mahmud he governed Korkuteli, building the Emir Sinaneddin Medrese there in 1319.

After Mahmud handed their uncle Dündar to the Chobanid Timurtash and fled to Cairo c. 1327, Hızır restored the Antalya beylik. In 1332 Doria found him holding twelve cities, twenty-five towers and eight thousand cavalry, and Ibn Battuta visited the ailing sultan there. His son Dadı Bey succeeded him.

锡南丁·赫泽尔贝伊是哈米德王朝泰凯支系统治安塔利亚的贝伊，为支系开创者尤努斯贝伊之子。父亲与兄长马哈茂德在位时，他出镇科尔库泰利，并于1319年在当地修建埃米尔·锡南丁经学院。

约1327年，马哈茂德把叔父丁达尔交给楚班家族的帖木儿塔什后逃奔开罗，赫泽尔于是复兴了安塔利亚贝伊国。1332年，多里亚见到他治下有十二座城池、二十五座塔楼和八千骑兵，伊本·白图泰也曾在当地拜访患病的他。他死后由其子达迪贝伊继位。

en:
Yunus Bey was a younger son of İlyas Bey, founder of the Hamidid beylik, and brother of Dündar. After the Hamidids seized Antalya, Dündar enfeoffed him with the city, and Yunus ruled as its emir, becoming the first prince of the Teke beylik, conventionally dated to 1321.

An inscription of 1319 places his son Hızır at Korkuteli. Yunus had died by 1324, when his son Mahmud Bey succeeded him in Antalya.

尤努斯贝伊是哈米德贝伊国建立者伊利亚斯贝伊较年幼的儿子之一、丁达尔之弟。哈米德家族夺取安塔利亚后，丁达尔将该城封给他，尤努斯遂以埃米尔身份统治此城，成为通常认定始建于1321年的泰凯贝伊国第一代君主。

1319年的一处铭文显示其子赫泽尔当时在科尔库特利。尤努斯于1324年前去世，其子马哈茂德贝伊在安塔利亚继位。

en:
Temüge Otchigin (c. 1168–1246), youngest brother of Genghis Khan, bore the title Otchigin, guardian of the family hearth. With his mother Hö'elün he ruled the Mongol heartland, and in 1206 they received the largest share of land and people. Genghis authorised him to kill the shaman Teb Tengri in a wrestling match.

After Ögedei died in 1241, Temüge tried to seize the throne while Güyük was away on campaign, but Töregene blocked him. When Güyük was elected in 1246, Temüge was executed.

铁木哥斡赤斤（约1168—1246）是成吉思汗的幼弟，拥有“斡赤斤”称号，意为家业与炉灶的守护者。他与母亲诃额仑主持蒙古腹地，1206年分得的土地与属民最多。成吉思汗授意他在一场角抵中杀死萨满帖卜腾格里。

1241年窝阔台死后，他乘贵由出征在外之机企图夺取汗位，被脱列哥那阻止；1246年贵由当选大汗后，铁木哥被处死。

en:
Temür Buqa was a Yuan imperial prince, a grandson of Kublai Khan and son of Aurughchi, Prince of Xiping. In the last Zhiyuan years, unrest in Ü-Tsang took him there with Mongol and Tibetan troops; he set up seven postal stations in Ü and four in Tsang to secure the roads.

In 1296 he crushed a rising at Jiezhou in the Yuan region of Tibet, and in 1297 he was enfeoffed as Prince Zhenxi Wujing with a gilded silver camel-seal, holding the Tibetan lands as his hereditary appanage.

铁木儿不花是元朝宗室，忽必烈之孙、西平王奥鲁赤之子。至元末年乌思藏不宁，他率蒙古军与吐蕃军前往讨伐，并在乌思设立七个驿站、后藏设立四个驿站，以保障道路安全。

en:
Temür (1265–1307), called Öljeyitü Khan, was a grandson of Kublai Khan and the third son of Crown Prince Zhenjin. In 1287 he campaigned with his grandfather against the rebel prince Nayan, and in 1293 he was put in charge of the Karakorum region. After Kublai's death he was enthroned in 1294 as the second Yuan emperor.

His reign brought nominal suzerainty over the rival Mongol khanates and respect for Confucian scholarship. He died in 1307 without a surviving heir.

en:
Tenshō Shūbun was a Zen monk and the founding master of Chinese-style suiboku ink painting in Muromachi Japan. Active in Kyoto from around 1403, he studied under the émigré Josetsu and modelled his landscapes on the Song masters Xia Gui and Ma Yuan.

His style bridged close imitation of Chinese models and the Japanese style that later artists developed. He directed the Ashikaga shoguns' court painting bureau and in 1423 joined the mission to Joseon Korea.

In the 1440s he taught the young Sesshū, his most celebrated pupil. His best-known painting was Reading in a Bamboo Grove, and he died around 1444–1450.

天章周文是日本室町时代的禅僧，也是日本汉派水墨山水画的奠基者。他约于1403年起在京都作画，师从渡日画僧如拙，山水取法宋代夏圭、马远。

他的画风上承对中国范本的紧密模仿，下启后来画家发展出的日本风格。他主持足利幕府的画院，并于1423年随使团出使李氏朝鲜。

1440年代，他收少年雪舟为徒，雪舟后来成为他最负盛名的弟子。他最著名的作品是《竹斋读书图》，约于1444至1450年间去世。

en:
Acolnahuacatl (died 1366), also called Acolnahuacatzin, was the Tepanec tlatoani of Azcapotzalco, probably a son of King Xiuhtlatonac. He married Cuetlaxochitzin, daughter of the Chichimec leader Xolotl, and their son was Tezozomoc, the future master of the Valley of Mexico.

The chronicler Chimalpain dates his rule from 1302 to 1366. In 1318 his Tepanecs attacked the Mexica of Chapultepec and raised their tribute.

en:
In the native chronicles, Cuetlaxochitzin was a daughter of Xolotl, the Chichimec leader who founded Tenayuca about 1224. She was married to Acolnahuacatl, king of the Tepanec city of Azcapotzalco, and later tradition remembered the pair as founders of the city; the marriage produced six children.

The best remembered was Tezozomoctli, who as the aged king Tezozomoc ruled Azcapotzalco from 1367 to 1426 and made it the leading power in the Valley of Mexico. Through him Cuetlaxochitzin was grandmother of Ayauhcihuatl, whom Tezozomoc married to the Mexica king Huitzilihuitl in 1403.

据本土编年史记载，奎特拉索奇钦是约1224年建立特纳尤卡的奇奇梅克首领索洛特尔之女。她嫁给特帕内克城邦阿斯卡波察尔科国王阿科尔纳瓦卡特尔，后世传说把二人奉为该城的奠基者；这场婚姻共育有六名子女。

其中最著名的是特索索莫克特利，即长寿的特索索莫克，他于1367—1426年统治阿斯卡波察尔科，将其建成墨西哥谷的首要强权。阿亚乌奇瓦特尔是她的孙女，1403年特索索莫克把阿亚乌奇瓦特尔嫁给墨西卡国王维齐利维特尔。

其中最著名的是特索索莫克特利，即长寿的特索索莫克，他于1367—1426年统治[ShowLocationName('azcapotzalco')]，将其建成墨西哥谷的首要强权。阿亚乌奇瓦特尔是她的孙女，1403年特索索莫克把阿亚乌奇瓦特尔嫁给墨西卡国王维齐利维特尔。

en:
Tezozomoc Yacateteltetl (c. 1320–1426) ruled the Tepanec city-state of Azcapotzalco from around 1370 until his death and built it into the dominant power in the Valley of Mexico. A son of King Acolnahuacatl and Cuetlaxochitzin, he set his own sons on the thrones of neighbouring cities.

In 1403 he approved the election of Tenochtitlan's king Huitzilihuitl and gave him his daughter Ayauhcihuatl in marriage, over his son Maxtla's opposition. Defeated by Texcoco's ruler, he made peace but later defeated its new ruler in 1419 and seized the city.

A colonial chronicler called him a cruel tyrant, so old that he was carried about swaddled in feathers and slept between two braziers. After he died in 1426 his son Tayatzin succeeded him, but Maxtla seized power.
