特索索莫克·亚卡特特尔特尔（约1320—1426）自约1370年起统治特帕内克城邦阿斯卡波察尔科，直至去世，将其建成墨西哥谷的霸主。他是国王阿科尔纳瓦卡特尔与奎特拉索奇钦之子，把自己的儿子安插到邻近城市的王位上。

1403年，他认可维奇利维特尔当选特诺奇蒂特兰国王，并不顾儿子马克斯特拉反对，将女儿阿约西瓦特尔嫁给他。他被特斯科科之主击败后求和，后来又击败其继任者，于1419年夺取该城。

殖民时期的编年史家称他为残酷的暴君，说他年老到要用羽毛包裹着抬来抬去，睡在两个大火盆之间。他1426年死后儿子塔亚钦继位，但马克斯特拉夺取了权力。

en:
The Ternatan chronicle recorded by François Valentijn makes Boheyat I the eldest son of Kolano Sidang Arif and ruler of Ternate from 1347 to 1350. He succeeded after Tolu-ma-lamo's death and was remembered as good-natured and mild.

In the second year of his reign he went blind, and in 1350 he died of illness after only three years on the throne, leaving a son born to a Javanese woman. His brother Ngolo-ma-Caya then succeeded him.

据法兰坦记录的特尔纳特编年史，博赫亚特一世是科拉诺西丁·阿里夫的长子，1347—1350年为特尔纳特统治者。他在托卢·马拉莫死后继位，史称性情温厚、为政宽和。

即位第二年他双目失明，1350年病死，在位仅三年，留下一子，为一名爪哇女子所生。其弟恩戈洛·玛·卡亚随后继位。

en:
Gapi Baguna I was the youngest son of Kolano Sidang Arif and kolano of Ternate from 1372 to 1377. The chronicle of François Valentijn depicts him as a peacemaker who settled the feuds of the Malukan kingdoms through marriage alliances.

His son married a daughter of the king of Jailolo and later inherited it, while his two daughters married at Tidore, one to its ruler and the other to his brother. He died in 1377.

加皮·巴古纳一世是科拉诺西丁·阿里夫的幼子，1372—1377年任特尔纳特的科拉诺。法兰坦的编年史把他描绘成议和者，以联姻平息马鲁古诸国的仇怨。

他的儿子娶贾伊洛洛国王之女，后来并继承了贾伊洛洛；两个女儿则嫁往蒂多雷，一个嫁国王，一个嫁国王之弟。他于1377年去世。

en:
Gapi-ma-lamo, the fourth son of Kolano Sidang Arif, became kolano of Ternate in 1359 after his brother Momole. He was a warlike ruler, fighting long wars against Jailolo and Tidore and later falling out with Bacan.

Though he conquered no new lands, his standing among the Malukan kings was high and he kept every enemy at bay. After a thirteen-year reign he died in 1372, and his youngest brother Gapi Baguna succeeded him.

zh:
加皮·马拉莫是科拉诺西丁·阿里夫的第四子，1359年继其兄莫莫勒成为特尔纳特的科拉诺。他生性好战，长期与贾伊洛洛、蒂多雷交战，后来又同巴占反目。

他虽然没有开拓新土，但在马鲁古诸王中威望很高，令敌国不敢来犯。他在位十三年，1372年去世，幼弟加皮·巴古纳继位。

en:
Ternatan tradition names Kalabata the fourth Kolano of Ternate, succeeding his father Siale in 1298. A weak and pleasure-loving king, he kept his throne through his brothers, who fought his enemies for him. He later feared their prowess and poisoned the three ablest; the survivors fled to Tidore.

Two died in exile and the rest returned only when Kalabata died in 1304. He left sons including Komalo and Patsaranga-ma-lamo.

特尔纳特传说称卡拉巴塔是第四任科拉诺，1298年继其父西亚勒即位。他为人软弱、贪图享乐，全靠诸弟替他征战才保住王位。后来他忌惮诸弟的勇武，毒杀了其中最出色的三人，余者逃往蒂多雷。

en:
The Ternatan chronicle makes Momole the second son of Kolano Sidang Arif and an elder brother of Ngolo-ma-Caya. He was brought up by the grandees of the kingdom and succeeded Ngolo-ma-Caya as kolano in 1357.

His short reign saw no recorded wars or deeds, for he was sickly and died in 1359 after only two years. Some accounts said a Makassarese concubine had poisoned him, and his brother Gapi-ma-lamo then took the throne.

en:
Ngolo-ma-Caya, a son of Kolano Sidang Arif, ruled Ternate as kolano from 1350 to 1357. Valentijn's chronicle describes him as a brave warrior who learned some Arabic through an Arab settler and was reputed a holy man able to summon spirits and angels who bathed with him in the Ake-Sibu stream.

The Arab also taught the Ternatans to build better ships; with these Ngolo-ma-Caya sailed to the Sula Islands, subdued them and placed his son Hamed over Taliabu. He died in 1357.

恩戈洛·玛·卡亚是科拉诺西丁·阿里夫之子，1350—1357年任特尔纳特的科拉诺。法兰坦的编年史称他作战勇猛，随一名阿拉伯侨民学了些阿拉伯语，并被视为能役使精灵与天使的圣人，相传精灵与天使曾与他在阿克-西布溪中沐浴。

那阿拉伯人还教特尔纳特人造出更好的船；恩戈洛·玛·卡亚率船队远征苏拉群岛并将其征服，以其子哈米德镇守塔利阿布。他于1357年去世。

en:
Patsaranga-ma-lamo, a son of Kalabata, succeeded his brother Komalo as Kolano of Ternate in 1317. The Ternatan grandees first made him promise that the throne would pass to a brother. Mild and well liked, he conquered two villages on Makian Island in 1321.

When he tried to make his son Komalo Bangsa heir despite his oath, the Ternatans deposed him in 1322 and placed his sister's son Sidang Arif Malamo on the throne.

帕察兰加-马拉莫是卡拉巴塔之子，1317年继其兄科马洛之位成为特尔纳特科拉诺。特尔纳特贵族先要他许诺，王位今后传给兄弟。他性情温和、颇受爱戴，并于1321年攻取马基安岛上的两座村庄。

en:
Sidang Arif Malamo (died 1331), a nephew of Patsaranga-ma-lamo, was made Kolano of Ternate after the deposition of 1322. His reign drew Javanese and Arab merchants to the island for the clove trade.

The four rulers of Maluku met on Moti Island and swore a bond, ranking Jailolo first and Ternate second. Through his friendship with foreign traders he gained wide knowledge, earning the name Sidang Arif, meaning wise master. He died in 1331.

西丁·阿里夫·马拉莫（1331年卒）是帕察兰加-马拉莫的外甥，1322年帕察兰加被废后被拥立为特尔纳特科拉诺。他在位期间，许多爪哇人和阿拉伯人为丁香贸易而来。

en:
The Ternatan chronicle preserved by François Valentijn names Syah Alam as kolano of Ternate from 1332 to 1343. A son of Patsaranga-ma-lamo, he was enthroned after his cousin Paji-ma-lamo was murdered.

Around 1334, when the people of Makian killed two Ternatan seafarers, Syah Alam invaded the island, subdued it and kept it under Ternatan rule. He died in 1343 and was succeeded by his brother Tolu-ma-lamo.

en:
Tolu-ma-lamo, a son of Patsaranga-ma-lamo, became kolano of Ternate in 1343 after his brother Syah Alam. Valentijn's chronicle calls him a troublesome ruler, the first to break the peace bond of the four kings.

Nuruddin of Tidore and Sidang Hasan of Bacan then attacked and took Makian, but in 1346 Tolu-ma-lamo recovered the island and wounded Nuruddin, who later died of it, before raiding Bacan's coasts. He later took to opium and died in 1347, leaving a son Komalo Pulu.

en:
Bolesław of Cieszyn (c. 1331/32–1356) was a Piast prince, the second son of Casimir I, Duke of Cieszyn, and Euphemia. Destined for the Church to avoid dividing the small duchy, he joined the Kraków cathedral chapter in 1349 and later became a canon of Wrocław.

In 1353 Emperor Charles IV made him his chaplain and provost of All Saints' Church at Prague Castle. He died in Prague on 23 July 1356.

en:
Casimir I (1280/1290–1358), second son of Mieszko I, became Duke of Cieszyn in 1315. At first close to King Władysław I of Poland, he switched sides after Lithuanian raids and swore homage to John of Bohemia at Opava in 1327, holding Cieszyn as a hereditary fief.

He secured half of Bytom in 1357, ringed Cieszyn with walls and promoted town life. He married Euphemia of Masovia, who bore him nine children, and died in 1358.

en:
Mieszko I (1252/1256–1314/1315), eldest son of Władysław of Opole-Racibórz, was the first Piast duke of Cieszyn. In the 1290 partition he received Cieszyn, Oświęcim and Zator, and promoted colonization by granting the towns their rights.

He tied his fate to Bohemia, swearing homage to Wenceslaus II in 1292 and attending his coronation in 1300. His daughter Viola Elisabeth married Wenceslaus III in 1305, but the young king's murder in 1306 ended his ambitions, and his sons took over the duchy.

en:
Przemyslaus I Noszak (1334–1410) was a Piast duke who ruled Cieszyn from 1358, after his elder brothers' early deaths made him Casimir I's chief heir. He served Emperor Charles IV at Prague and became a leading diplomat, helping arrange Anne of Bohemia's marriage to Richard II of England.

Under Wenceslaus IV he governed Bohemia in 1386 and acted as vicar in Germany. His eldest son was murdered in 1406 in a noble feud, and Przemyslaus died in 1410.

en:
Dietrich von Altenburg was the 19th Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights, leading the Order from 1335 until his death in 1341. He joined in 1307 and became Grand Marshal in 1331, reviving the war with Władysław I of Poland; after the Battle of Płowce the Order held Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land.

The 1335 Congress of Visegrád gave Poland Kuyavia and Dobrzyń while the Order kept Pomerelia, over Polish protests; a 1339 Curia order to surrender the disputed lands was never approved by the Pope.

As Grand Master he rebuilt the Order's castles and, at Marienburg, the church and its main tower, finishing the Chapel of Saint Anne. He died of illness at Thorn in October 1341 on his way to negotiate with Poland, the first Grand Master buried in the chapel; peace came only in 1343.

迪特里希·冯·阿尔滕堡是条顿骑士团第19任大团长，1335年至1341年去世前在任。他1307年加入骑士团，1331年出任大统帅，重启与波兰国王瓦迪斯瓦夫一世的战事；普沃夫采战役后，骑士团占有库亚维亚和多布任地区。

1335年的维谢格拉德会议商定：波兰收回库亚维亚和多布任，骑士团保留波美雷利亚，引发波兰方面抗议。1339年罗马教廷判令骑士团交出争议土地，但教皇没有批准判决。

出任大团长后，他修建骑士团的城堡，在马林堡重建圣母教堂及主塔，建成圣安娜礼拜堂。1341年10月他在赴波兰谈判途中病逝于托伦，成为首位葬于该礼拜堂的大团长；和平直到1343年才实现。

en:
Luther von Braunschweig (c. 1275–1335), a younger son of Duke Albert I of Brunswick-Lüneburg, was the 18th Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights from 1331 until his death. First recorded as a Teutonic Knight in 1295, he held several commandries and founded the town of Gilgenburg in 1326.

Elected Grand Master in 1331 while the Polish–Teutonic War continued, with the Battle of Płowce fought that September, he promoted settlement and church-building and extended Marienburg Castle. A patron of letters, he had Peter of Dusburg's chronicle translated into German, and died on 18 April 1335.

en:
Peter of Dusburg (died after 1326) was a priest-brother of the Teutonic Order and its foremost chronicler. In 1324 Grand Master Werner von Orseln commissioned him, probably in Königsberg, to write the Order's history; the resulting Chronicon terrae Prussiae described the Order and the Old Prussians in the 13th and early 14th centuries.

Completed by 1326 and later revised to include events through 1330, it expanded on a Latin author's now-lost account of the early Prussian Crusade. From 1331 to 1335 his chronicle was translated into Middle High German for Grand Master Luther von Braunschweig.

杜伊斯堡的彼得（1326年后去世）是条顿骑士团的神父修士，也是该团最重要的编年史家。1324年，他可能在柯尼斯堡受大团长维尔纳·冯·奥瑟尔恩委托撰写骑士团历史，成书《普鲁士土地编年史》，记述13世纪及14世纪初的骑士团和古普鲁士人。

该书在一位拉丁文作者现已佚失的早期普鲁士十字军记述基础上扩写，1326年前完成，后来又增补至1330年的事件。1331至1335年，此书受大团长路德·冯·不伦瑞克之命被译成中古高地德语。

en:
Werner von Orseln (c. 1280–1330) served the Teutonic Order in senior posts, becoming Grand Komtur at Malbork in 1314. Exiled with his patron, Grand Master Karl von Trier, during an internal coup, he returned in 1319 and restored discipline. On 6 July 1324 the chapter elected him Grand Master.

He set up the Grand Master's chancellery, commissioned Peter von Dusburg's chronicle and fought Poland over Pomerelia, ordering further conquests in 1327. In November 1330 the brother Johann von Endorf stabbed him to death after a reprimand.

en:
Diethelm I of Toggenburg (c. 1150–1205/1207) is the earliest count of the dynasty whose line can be traced. He may have married Guta of Rapperswil, though she may instead have been the wife of the next Diethelm. If she was his wife, she brought the county of Uznach and the upper March around Grynau into the marriage.

Around 1200 the couple shared in the inheritance of several neighbouring lordships while pressed by St. Gallen Abbey and neighbouring lords. His sons Diethelm II and Friedrich I survived him, and the comital title is documented from 1209.

Diethelm II of Toggenburg (c. 1180–1235) succeeded his father Diethelm I as count. St. Gallen chronicles accuse him of having his younger brother Friedrich I murdered in 1226, in order to seize the town Wil and Alt-Toggenburg.

In the ensuing conflict with St. Gallen Abbey the Toggenburgs lost several estates, including Wil and Alt-Toggenburg. Between 1226 and 1228 he founded the Hospitaller commandery of Tobel, later the family burial place. His son Kraft I succeeded him.

en:
Frederick IV (before 1286 – 15 November 1315) ruled as count of Toggenburg from 1309. In 1313 he bought Wildenburg Castle near Baar. He married Ita von Homberg, who bore him sons Frederick V and Diethelm V.

In November 1315 he rode with Duke Leopold I of Habsburg against the Swiss Confederates and was killed on 15 November at the Battle of Morgarten, when men of Schwyz ambushed Leopold's column beside Lake Ägeri.

en:
Kraft I of Toggenburg, son of Diethelm II, spent his years as count trying to recover the rights and estates his family had lost to St. Gallen Abbey after the feud of 1226. He also fought in campaigns as far afield as Lyon and Alsace. He is probably the minnesinger Count Kraft of Toggenburg whose songs were preserved in the Codex Manesse.

He was reportedly killed in 1254 by a retainer named Locher, because Kraft had allegedly slain Locher's brother. His son Friedrich III succeeded him.

en:
Boniface I of Montferrat (c. 1150–1207) became marquis in 1192, after his brother Conrad, king of Jerusalem, was killed. He fought the neighbouring communes, helped lead Emperor Henry VI's 1194 expedition to Sicily, and kept a court known for its patronage of troubadours.

In 1201 he took over leadership of the Fourth Crusade. Diverted to Constantinople, the army sacked the city in 1204; the Venetians blocked his election as Latin emperor, so he founded the Kingdom of Thessalonica and was crowned king in 1205.

On 4 September 1207 he died in a Vlach ambush. His severed head was sent as a trophy to Tsar Kaloyan of Bulgaria.

蒙费拉托的波尼法乔一世（约1150—1207）在其兄、耶路撒冷国王康拉德遇害后，于1192年继任侯爵。他与邻近的城邦交战，1194年协助统率皇帝亨利六世的西西里远征，宫廷还以赞助吟游诗人闻名。

1201年他接掌第四次十字军。十字军转攻君士坦丁堡，于1204年洗劫该城；威尼斯人阻挠他当选拉丁皇帝，他便于1205年建立帖撒罗尼迦王国并加冕为王。

1207年9月4日，他在弗拉赫人的伏击中身亡。他的首级被作为战利品送往保加利亚沙皇卡洛扬处。

en:
Demetrios Angelos Doukas (born c. 1220) was the youngest son of Theodore Komnenos Doukas. On his brother John's death in 1244 he succeeded as ruler of Thessalonica, and the Nicaean emperor John III confirmed him with the title of Despot.

Young and dissolute, he won little loyalty from its leading families, who conspired to hand Thessalonica to Nicaea. In 1246 Nicaean troops were admitted through a gate and annexed the city. Demetrios surrendered through his sister Irene's intercession and was exiled to Lentiana, where he probably died.

德米特里奥斯·安格洛斯·杜卡斯（约1220年生）是狄奥多尔·科穆宁·杜卡斯的幼子。1244年其兄约翰去世，他继位统治塞萨洛尼基，尼西亚皇帝约翰三世确认他的继承权并授予“专制君主”头衔。

他年少放荡，不受名门拥戴，后者密谋把塞萨洛尼基献给尼西亚。1246年，尼西亚军队经内应开门入城吞并此城；德米特里奥斯经姐姐伊琳娜求情投降，后被流放至伦蒂亚纳，可能在那里去世。

en:
John Komnenos Doukas (c. 1214–1244), eldest son of Theodore Komnenos Doukas, was captured by Tsar Ivan Asen II at Klokotnitsa in 1230 and freed in 1237 after his sister Irene married the tsar. His blinded father then ousted Manuel from Thessalonica and installed John as ruler.

In 1239 Manuel returned with Nicaean support and took Thessaly, which Theodore and John accepted. John used the imperial title by 1241, when Ivan Asen's death ended Bulgarian protection of Thessalonica; in 1242 the Nicaean emperor John III Vatatzes marched on the city and forced him to drop the title and accept the rank of despot under Nicaean suzerainty.

He showed little talent for governing and was said to wish to become a priest. On his death in 1244 his brother Demetrios succeeded him.

约翰·科穆宁·杜卡斯（约1214—1244）是狄奥多尔·科穆宁·杜卡斯的长子。1230年他在科洛特尼察战役中被保加利亚沙皇伊凡·阿森二世俘虏，1237年因姐姐伊琳娜嫁给沙皇而获释。失明的父亲随后从叔父曼努埃尔手中夺取帖撒罗尼迦，立约翰为统治者。

1239年曼努埃尔在尼西亚支持下返回并占领色萨利，狄奥多尔和约翰接受了这一损失。约翰至迟1241年使用帝号，当年伊凡·阿森去世使帖撒罗尼迦失去保加利亚的庇护；1242年尼西亚皇帝约翰三世·瓦塔策斯进军该城，迫使他放弃帝号，以专制公身份承认尼西亚的宗主权。

他缺乏治理才能，据称希望成为神父。约翰于1244年去世，其弟季米特里奥斯继位。

en:
Theodore Komnenos Doukas (born 1180–1185, died c. 1253) was a Greek prince of imperial descent who took power in Epirus after his half-brother Michael I died in 1215. He had served Theodore I Laskaris in Nicaea before joining Michael in Epirus.

He captured Latin emperor Peter of Courtenay in 1217 and took Thessalonica in 1224, crowning himself emperor there. In 1230 Bulgaria's Tsar Ivan Asen II defeated and captured him at Klokotnitsa, and Theodore was blinded in captivity.

Freed in 1237, he ruled Thessalonica through his sons until Nicaea annexed the city in 1246, and he died in Nicaean exile around 1253.

狄奥多尔·科穆宁·杜卡斯（1180—1185年生，约1253年卒）是出身科穆宁皇室的希腊王公，1215年在同父异母兄长米哈伊尔一世死后接管伊庇鲁斯。他此前曾在尼西亚为狄奥多尔一世·拉斯卡里斯效力，后来到伊庇鲁斯投奔米哈伊尔。

1217年他俘获拉丁皇帝库特奈的彼得，1224年攻取帖撒罗尼迦并在此加冕为帝。1230年，保加利亚沙皇伊凡·阿森二世在科洛特尼察战役中将他击败俘获，他在囚禁期间被刺瞎双目。

1237年获释后，他借儿子之名统治帖撒罗尼迦，直到1246年尼西亚吞并该城；约1253年，他死于尼西亚的流放之中。

en:
Brian Ruadh Ó Briain (died 1277), a younger son of Conor na Siudane, succeeded his father as King of Thomond in 1268. In 1270 he attacked the Anglo-Norman colonists and stormed Clare Castle. In 1275 his nephew Toirdhealbhach drove him from Clonroad, and Brian allied himself with Thomas de Clare, to whom the English crown had granted all Thomond.

Defeated by Toirdhealbhach in 1277, he was hanged by de Clare at Bunratty. His sons Donnchadh and Domnall carried on his Clann Briain line.

en:
Conor na Siudane Ua Briain (died 1268), son of Donnchadh Cairbreach, ruled Thomond as English colonisation advanced: the castles of Clare and Bunratty were built in 1249–1253. Through yearly tribute he kept the rest of his kingdom, and in 1257 he and his son Tadhg nearly expelled the English.

In 1268 he was slain fighting Conor Carrach O'Loughlin at the wood of Siudan, the place that gave him his epithet. Buried at Corcomroe Abbey, where his stone effigy survives, he was succeeded by his son Brian Ruadh.

Domnall Mór Ua Briain (died 1194), third son of Toirdhealbhach mac Diarmada, became King of Thomond in 1168 after his brother's death. He submitted to Henry II of England in 1171 but kept fighting the Norman invaders of Ireland, crushing a Cambro-Norman army at Thurles in 1175 and retaking Limerick in 1176. In 1185 he defeated Prince John's forces.

He founded Holy Cross Abbey and Kilcooly Abbey, both Cistercian, and died in 1194, regarded as the last king of Munster.

Donnchadh Cairbreach Ó Briain (died 1242), a son of Domnall Mór, became King of Thomond after his father's sons fought over the succession. In the 1210s he founded Ennis Friary as penance for his feud with his brother.

When rival clans revolted, he crushed them with Norman help from his brother-in-law de Burgh, paying for it by granting Limerick and surrounding lands to the colonists; Thomond was reduced to the area of modern County Clare behind the Shannon. He died in 1242.

Donnchad mac Briain Ó Briain (died 1284), eldest son of Brian Ruadh, claimed Thomond after his father's execution by Thomas de Clare in May 1277. In 1278 they raided de Clare's lands, but civil war with their cousin Toirdhealbhach Mór forced them back into de Clare's alliance. In 1280 de Clare partitioned Thomond between the rivals, and fighting soon resumed.

In 1284 Donnchad was betrayed by his own men and killed while bathing in the Fergus near Clare Castle. His son was Diarmait Cléirech Ó Briain.

en:
Tadhg Cael Uisce Ó Briain (c. 1230–1259) was the eldest son of Conor na Siudane Ua Briain and tánaiste, or heir-designate, of Thomond. He took his byname from the conference of Cael Uisce, where as his father's representative he refused to acknowledge Brian Ua Néill as High King of Ireland.

He died in 1259 before his father, leaving a young son, Toirdhealbhach Mór, whose descendants led the Clann Tadhg claim to Thomond.

en:
Toirdhealbhach Maol Ó Briain was a son of Muircheartach, king of Thomond. After his brother Mathghamhain's death in 1369 he claimed the kingship against his nephew Brian Sreamhach, ruling in rivalry for decades.

In 1375, allied with Ulick Burke of Clanricard, he briefly drove Brian out of Thomond and occupied the kingship, but Brian recovered his lands the same year. Toirdhealbhach then retired under English protection in the Pale, where he died of plague in 1398.

托伊尔德巴赫·麦尔·奥布赖恩是托蒙德国王穆尔切尔特赫之子。1369年其兄马特加曼死后，他与侄子布莱恩·斯雷瓦赫争夺王位，对峙长达数十年。

en:
Toirdhealbhach Mór Ó Briain (c. 1250–1306), son of Tadhg Cael Uisce, made himself King of Thomond by deposing his uncle Brian Ruadh in 1276. When Brian returned with Thomas de Clare's backing, he rallied his cousin William de Burgh and overthrew their army in 1277.

His long struggle with de Clare, who then backed Brian's son Donnchadh until he drowned in 1284, became the subject of the epic Caithréim Thoirdhealbhaigh. He ruled until his death in 1306, when his son Donnchadh succeeded him.

en:
Andrea I Thopia (died c. 1340 at Naples) belonged to the Thopia, an Albanian family that by 1340 held much of the land between the Mati and Shkumbin rivers. In 1338 he inherited the County of Mat from Tanush Thopia.

His fall came through a marriage. King Robert of Naples had promised a natural daughter to a ruler in the Morea and sent her to Greece by way of Durrës; in the port she met Andrea, and the two married without the king's consent, which Robert never forgave.

Years later he invited the couple to Naples on a pretext of reconciliation and had them executed. Their two sons, George and Karl, survived in Albania; Karl rose to be Prince of Albania, yet fought the Angevins all his life, unable to forgive his parents' killing.

安德烈亚一世·托皮亚（约1340年卒于那不勒斯）出身阿尔巴尼亚的托皮亚家族，该家族到1340年已控制马蒂河与什昆宾河之间的大片土地。1338年他从塔努什·托皮亚手中继承马蒂伯国。

他的败亡源于一桩婚事。那不勒斯国王罗贝托曾把一个私生女许给摩里亚的一位统治者，送她取道都拉斯前往希腊；她在港口遇到安德烈亚，两人未经国王同意便成婚，罗贝托始终不肯原谅。

数年后他以和解为借口邀请夫妇二人前往那不勒斯，并处决了他们。两个儿子乔治和卡尔留在阿尔巴尼亚幸免于难；卡尔后来成为阿尔巴尼亚亲王，却终生与安茹王朝为敌，无法原谅父母被杀。

en:
Karl Thopia (c. 1339–1388) was the son of Andrea I Thopia and Hélène, an illegitimate daughter of King Robert of Naples; Robert had his parents executed, and Karl and his brother George grew up at Krujë. In 1358 he won a great victory at Acheloos over Nikephoros II Orsini, Despot of Epirus, who fell in the battle, after which he styled himself Princeps Albaniae.

He took Angevin Durrës in 1368, lost it in 1376 and recovered it in 1383, and the Pope named him Grand Count of Albania in 1374. A trilingual inscription of 1381 has him claim descent from a French king's blood.

When his rival Balsha II seized Durrës in 1385, Thopia and other nobles called in Ottoman troops, who killed Balsha at Savra. He died in January 1388, leaving the princedom to his son Gjergj.

en:
Tanusio Thopia was an Albanian count under the Angevins, holding lands in the Mat region. His family, one of the most powerful in Angevin Albania, vanishes from the record after 1274 until 1329, when Tanusio appears as one of the counts of Albania; in 1338 Angevin records call him Count of Matia.

He served the Angevin Princes of Taranto and Dukes of Durazzo. The Thopia, who had turned from Orthodoxy to Catholicism, held much of the land between the Mati and Shkumbin rivers by 1340.

A later tradition makes Andrea I Thopia his son or brother: Andrea abducted and married a natural daughter of King Robert of Naples and was executed with her. That would make Tanusio the grandfather or great-uncle of Karl Thopia, later Prince of Albania.

塔努西奥·托皮亚是安茹王朝治下的阿尔巴尼亚伯爵，领地在马蒂地区。他的家族是安茹治下阿尔巴尼亚势力最大的家族之一，1274年后便不见于记载，直到1329年塔努西奥作为阿尔巴尼亚众伯爵之一出现；1338年安茹档案称他为马蒂伯爵。

他效力于安茹王朝的塔兰托亲王与都拉斯公爵。托皮亚家族由东正教改宗天主教，到1340年已控制马蒂河与什昆宾河之间的大片土地。

后世传说称安德烈亚一世·托皮亚是他的儿子或兄弟：安德烈亚劫走并娶了那不勒斯国王罗贝托的一个私生女，最终与她一同被处死。这样塔努西奥便是后来的阿尔巴尼亚亲王卡尔·托皮亚的祖父或伯祖父。

en:
John I Doukas (c. 1231–1289) was an illegitimate son of Michael II Komnenos Doukas, Despot of Epirus, who ruled Thessaly from 1268 until his death. In 1259 he led Vlach troops before defecting to Michael VIII Palaiologos at Pelagonia, helping the Nicaeans crush the allies; he then returned to help his family recover Epirus and Thessaly.

He became the emperor's foremost Greek opponent, rejecting the Union of the Churches, sheltering its enemies and allying with Athens and Charles of Anjou; imperial armies never subdued him. Made sebastokrator around 1272, he died in 1289, leaving Thessaly to his sons Constantine and Theodore.

zh:
约翰一世·杜卡斯（约1231—1289）是伊庇鲁斯专制君主米海尔二世·科穆宁·杜卡斯的私生子，约1268年起统治色萨利直至去世。1259年他率领瓦拉几亚军队，随后在佩拉戈尼亚战役中倒戈投奔米海尔八世·巴列奥略，帮助尼西亚军队击溃联军，此后又回到父兄一边，协助收复伊庇鲁斯和色萨利。

他成为皇帝最主要的希腊人对手：抵制东西方教会联合，庇护联合派的敌人，与雅典公国和安茹的查理结盟，帝国军队始终无法征服他。约1272年米海尔八世授予他“至尊者”头衔。1289年他去世，把色萨利留给儿子君士坦丁和狄奥多尔。

en:
John II Doukas (c. 1293–1318) ruled Thessaly from 1303 until his death. Succeeding his father Constantine Doukas young, he was given Guy II de la Roche of Athens as regent by the Thessalian magnates.

From 1306 the Catalan Company ravaged Thessaly for three years, but on coming of age in 1308 John rejected Athenian overlordship. Guy's successor Walter hired the Catalans against John, but they turned on Walter and killed him in 1311.

In 1315 he married Irene Palaiologina, an illegitimate daughter of Emperor Andronikos II, and drew closer to Byzantium. He died in 1318 without heirs, and the Catalans and local magnates divided his lands.

en:
Constantine Doukas (c. 1276–1303) was the second son of John I Doukas, sebastokrator of Thessaly. He succeeded his father around 1289 while still underage, ruling under the regency of Anna Palaiologina Kantakouzene and sharing power with his brother Theodore Angelos until Theodore's death around 1299.

Invested as sebastokrator around 1295, he fought Nikephoros of Epirus and the Angevins, seizing fortresses in 1295 and losing most of them in a 1296 truce. He died in 1303 and was succeeded by his son John II Doukas.

Manuel Komnenos Doukas (c. 1187–c. 1241) was a son of the sebastokrator John Doukas and brother of Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus. After Theodore's defeat and capture at Klokotnitsa in 1230, Ivan Asen II of Bulgaria allowed Manuel to rule Thessalonica as despot. In 1235 he joined the siege of Constantinople.

He was driven from Thessalonica in 1237 and fled to Nicaea, but returned with Nicaean support in 1239 to rule Thessaly until his death around 1241.

en:
Stephen Gabrielopoulos (died 1332/1333) was a Byzantine magnate and semi-independent ruler in western Thessaly. After John II Doukas died without a male heir in 1318, Byzantine troops occupied northern Thessaly and the Catalans entered the south.

Amid the collapse of the principality he turned to Constantinople, acknowledging the emperor's suzerainty and receiving the title sebastokrator. As the emperor's governor he ruled a broad domain from Trikala to Kastoria. After his death his heirs quarrelled, drawing in Byzantine and Epirote armies. His lands soon passed under direct imperial rule.

Theodore Angelos (c. 1278–c. 1299) was the third son of John I Doukas, sebastokrator of Thessaly. When his father died around 1289 he and his older brother Constantine were still underage and ruled under the tutelage of Anna Palaiologina Kantakouzene, Theodore serving as Constantine's co-ruler. In 1295 the Byzantine emperor granted him the title sebastokrator.

A planned marriage alliance came to nothing, and he was defeated in battle by Byzantine forces. He died around 1299.

en:
Khatsun Namkha Lekpa Gyaltsen (1305–1343) was a Sakya ruler of the Khon family under the Yuan dynasty, holding the seat just as the school's hold on Tibet began to loosen. His father Zangpo Pal, a nephew of Phagpa, had presided over Sakya rule at its height.

After Zangpo Pal died in 1324, the imperial preceptor Kunga Lotro Gyaltsen, Namkha Lekpa's elder brother, divided the brothers among four palace branches, and Namkha Lekpa headed the Zhitog. Made State Preceptor (guoshi) in 1325, he kept the post until 1341.

Under him Sakya failed to put down revolts, and the rival Phagmodrupa gained control of much of the plateau. He died in 1343 and was succeeded by his brother Jamyang Donyo Gyaltsen; his son Kunga Rinchen later became the sixteenth Sakya Trizin.

阔尊南喀勒贝洛追坚赞（1305—1343），通称囊卡来巴，是元朝昆氏家族的萨迦派法主；他接掌法座时，萨迦对西藏的统治正开始松动。其父达尼钦波桑波贝是八思巴的侄子，在位时萨迦的统治达到鼎盛。

1324年桑波贝去世，囊卡来巴的兄长、帝师贡噶洛追坚赞把诸弟分为四个拉章，囊卡来巴领细脱拉章。1325年他受封“国师”，任职至1341年。

他在位期间，萨迦未能有效平定叛乱，敌对的帕木竹巴掌握了高原上的大片地区。1343年他去世，法主之位由弟弟嘉央屯月坚赞继承；其子衮噶仁钦后来成为第十六代萨迦法王。

en:
Zangpo Pal (1261–1323) was abbot-ruler of Sakya, the leading Tibetan see under the Yuan. A nephew of Phagpa, he was exiled by Kublai Khan after his legitimacy was questioned.

When his cousin died in 1287, Kublai gave the Sakya estates to the Sharpa family instead. Temür Khan recalled him in 1296, and he took full abbot-ruler power in 1306.

Named State Preceptor in 1311, he fathered thirteen sons; his reign was peaceful, but in 1322 his sons were split into four palace branches, sowing rivalries that weakened Sakya before his death in 1323.

达尼钦波桑波贝（1261—1323）是元朝治下西藏首席教派萨迦派的法王。他是八思巴的侄子，因身世受质疑被忽必烈汗流放。

1287年堂兄去世后，忽必烈把萨迦领地交给夏尔巴家族，而没有让他继承。1296年铁穆耳汗将他召回，他于1306年接掌法王全权。

1311年他受封“国师”，共育有十三子；他在位时藏地大体安定，但1322年儿子们被划分为四个拉章支系，埋下内争的种子，削弱了萨迦，他于1323年去世。

Adelaide of Brunswick-Grubenhagen (1285–18 August 1320) was the daughter of Duke Henry I of Brunswick-Grubenhagen and Agnes of Meissen. On 15 September 1315 she married at Innsbruck Henry of Carinthia, the deposed king of Bohemia, who sought an heir and stronger alliances.

She bore the empty title of queen of Bohemia but never visited the kingdom. Her daughter Margaret, born in Tyrol in 1318, became the future Countess of Tyrol. Adelaide died in 1320 without producing a male heir.

en:
Agnes of Hohenberg was the daughter of Count Albert II of Hohenberg-Rotenburg, a Swabian Minnesänger known as Albert of Haigerloch, by his first wife, whose name is unrecorded.

In 1281 she was betrothed to Albert of Gorizia-Tirol, son of Count Meinhard II of Tyrol, and married him after 1282. Her husband, set to share the family inheritance, died before his father in April 1292.

King Adolf confirmed her dower in July 1293, the last record of her alive. Her only child Margaret married Burgrave Frederick IV of Nuremberg and died in 1348.

Albert II of Gorizia-Tyrol (c. 1266–30 April 1292) was a son of Count Meinhard II of Gorizia-Tyrol and Elisabeth of Bavaria. His father entrusted him with duties as vogt and marked him out to share the family's Tyrolean and Carinthian inheritance with his brothers. Around 1281 he married Agnes of Hohenberg.

Their daughter Margaret married the Burgrave of Nuremberg. Albert died before his father in late April 1292, so he never took part in the joint rule that began in 1295.

en:
Henry (c. 1265–1335) of the House of Gorizia was the younger son of Count Meinhard II of Tyrol. He inherited Tyrol and Carinthia in 1295, at first ruling with his brothers.

After marrying the Přemyslid princess Anne in 1306 he was elected king of Bohemia, but Habsburg troops drove him out. He was elected again in 1307 after Rudolf of Habsburg died.

In 1310 John of Luxembourg invaded and took Prague, forcing Henry back to his Alpine lands. His daughter by Adelaide of Brunswick was Margaret Maultasch; when Henry died in 1335 the Habsburgs seized Carinthia.

Charles IV then enfeoffed him with Moravia, where as margrave he founded the Moravian line of the House of Luxembourg. A loyal imperial diplomat, he died at Brno in 1375.

Louis of Gorizia-Tyrol (c. 1268–1305) was a son of Duke Meinhard of Carinthia and Elisabeth of Bavaria, and a younger brother of Otto III. On Meinhard's death in 1295 he inherited the Duchy of Carinthia and the County of Tyrol jointly with his brothers, and was appointed Vogt of the Bishops of Trent.

He died in 1305, before his brother Otto, and the joint rule passed to Otto and their youngest brother Henry VI.

格尔茨—蒂罗尔的路易（约1268—1305）是克恩滕公爵迈因哈德与巴伐利亚的伊丽莎白之子，奥托三世的弟弟。1295年迈因哈德去世后，他与兄弟们共同继承克恩滕公国和蒂罗尔伯国，并被任命为特伦托主教的福格特。

他于1305年先于其兄奥托去世，共治之责落到奥托与幼弟亨利六世身上。

en:
Margaret, called Maultasch (1318–1369), was the last Countess of Tyrol from the House of Gorizia and the only surviving child of Duke Henry of Carinthia. In 1330 she married John Henry of Luxembourg; the two disliked each other from the start.

Habsburgs and Wittelsbachs had agreed to carve up Tyrol, but the Tyroleans refused; only the Peace of Enns in 1336 let her enter her inheritance. On the night of 1 November 1341 she and her councillors barred the gates of Tyrol Castle against her husband, back late from a hunt.

In 1342 she married Margrave Louis of Brandenburg without a divorce, and was excommunicated by Pope Clement VI. When her son Meinhard III died in 1363, she ceded Tyrol to Rudolf IV and retired to Vienna, dying in 1369 after the Wittelsbachs abandoned their claim.

绰号“莫尔塔施”的玛格丽特（1318—1369）是格尔茨家族末代蒂罗尔女伯爵，也是克恩滕公爵亨利唯一活下来的孩子。1330年她嫁给卢森堡的约翰·海因里希，两人从一开始就互相厌恶。

哈布斯堡家与维特尔斯巴赫家本已议定瓜分蒂罗尔，但蒂罗尔人不肯，直到1336年恩斯和约后她才得以接掌领地。1341年11月1日夜里，丈夫打猎晚归，她与顾问们把蒂罗尔城堡的大门关在他面前。

1342年，她在未离婚的情况下改嫁勃兰登堡藩侯路德维希，被教皇克雷芒六世处以绝罚。1363年儿子迈因哈德三世去世，她将蒂罗尔让给鲁道夫四世，退居维也纳。1369年维特尔斯巴赫家放弃对蒂罗尔的要求后不久，她去世。

en:
Meinhard II (c. 1238–1295) of the House of Gorizia ruled Gorizia and Tyrol with his brother Albert from 1258, taking Tyrol when they divided their lands in 1271. As boys the brothers had been hostages at Hohenwerfen until their father's death.

By marrying Elisabeth of Bavaria, widow of Conrad IV, he became stepfather of Conradin. He allied with Rudolf of Habsburg, fought at the Marchfeld against Ottokar II in 1278 and received Carinthia in fief in 1286.

He built up Tyrol, founding Stams Abbey, minting the Groschen and issuing a vernacular Landrecht. He died in 1295; his daughter Elisabeth became German queen and his son Henry succeeded him.

格尔茨家族的迈因哈德二世（约1238—1295）自1258年起与弟弟阿尔贝特共同统治格尔茨和蒂罗尔，1271年瓜分领地时分得蒂罗尔。兄弟二人幼时曾在霍亨韦尔芬被扣为人质，直到父亲去世。

他娶了康拉德四世的遗孀、巴伐利亚的伊丽莎白，因此成为康拉丁的继父。他与哈布斯堡的鲁道夫结盟，1278年在马希费尔德之战中对抗奥托卡二世，1286年受封克恩滕公国。

他经营蒂罗尔，创立施塔姆斯修道院，铸造格罗申银币，颁布方言写成的《蒂罗尔邦法》。他于1295年去世；女儿伊丽莎白成为德意志王后，儿子亨利继位。

en:
Otto III of Carinthia (c. 1265–25 May 1310) was a son of Duke Meinhard of Carinthia and Elisabeth of Bavaria. When Meinhard died in 1295, Otto inherited the Duchy of Carinthia and the County of Tyrol, ruling jointly with his brothers Louis and Henry VI. In 1305 he expanded the market at Gries against bishop-controlled Bolzano.

In 1297 he married Euphemia of Legnica, who bore him four daughters. He died without male issue and was succeeded by Henry VI.

en:
Abu Hammu Musa I (died 1318), fourth Zayyanid sultan of Tlemcen and son of Sultan Abu Said Uthman, succeeded his brother Abu Zayyan I in 1308, when the kingdom was exhausted by a long Marinid siege of its capital.

Continuing his brother's work, he pacified restive tribes and re-established control over Bejaia and Constantine. He strengthened the fortifications and halted Marinid expansion near Oujda.

He kept a strong army but cared little for his subjects. His harsh treatment of his son Abu Tashufin proved fatal: in 1318 the prince had him assassinated and seized the throne.

阿布·哈穆·穆萨一世（？—1318）是特莱姆森第四任宰扬王朝苏丹，苏丹阿布·赛义德·奥斯曼之子。1308年他继兄长阿布·扎扬一世即位，当时王国正因首都长期遭马林王朝围攻而疲敝。

他延续兄长的恢复事业，平定不服的部落，重新控制贝贾亚和君士坦丁。他还加固城防，并在乌季达一带遏制了马林王朝的扩张。

他维持强大的军队，却很少关心臣民。他苛待儿子阿布·塔舒芬，最终招来杀身之祸：1318年，王子派人将他刺杀并夺取王位。

en:
Abu Tashufin I (c. 1295–1337), born Abd al-Rahman, was the Zayyanid sultan of Tlemcen, who in 1318 took the throne by overthrowing and killing his father Abu Hammu Musa I.

In 1329 he marched east into Ifriqiya, captured Algiers, defeated the Hafsids at er-Rais and occupied their capital Tunis. A Marinid–Hafsid alliance then turned against him and besieged Tlemcen from 1335; Abu Tashufin was killed in the siege in 1337.

The Marinid Abu al-Hasan held the city until 1348, when Abu Tashufin's sons retook it. In his capital he founded the Tashfiniya Madrasa, among the best-known schools of the Zayyanids, who were the first to patronise madrasas in that part of the Maghreb.

阿布·塔舒芬一世（约1295—1337）本名阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼，是特莱姆森的宰扬王朝苏丹，1318年废杀父亲阿布·哈穆·穆萨一世夺取王位。

1329年他东征伊夫里奇亚，攻占阿尔及尔，在赖斯击败哈夫斯王朝并占领其首都突尼斯。随后马林与哈夫斯两王朝结盟反目，从1335年起围攻特莱姆森，阿布·塔舒芬于1337年在围城期间被杀。

马林苏丹阿布·哈桑占据该城至1348年，才被阿布·塔舒芬的儿子们夺回。他曾在都城修建塔舒芬尼亚经学院，是宰扬王朝资助的最著名学府之一；宰扬王朝是马格里布这一带最早资助经学院的王朝。

en:
The Tlaxcalan chronicles recorded by Diego Muñoz Camargo make Culhuatecuhtli Quanez the founding lord of Tepeticpac, first and oldest of the four señoríos of Tlaxcallan. He led the Teochichimeca migrants who, carrying the cult of their god Camaxtli out of Chicomóztoc, entered the Texcalla valley, defeating and expelling its local lords and settling the heights of Tepeticpac.

Muñoz Camargo relates that he gave his younger brother Teyohualminqui half the province and part of Camaxtli's ashes, from which grew the lordship of Ocotelulco, and granted lands to refugees who then founded Quiahuiztlán.

Both reign lists in the Historia de Tlaxcala begin with him; modern scholars place his floruit in the thirteenth or fourteenth century, dating the founding to 1228 by the native year 9 Técpatl, or to the early 1300s on archaeological grounds.

据迭戈·穆尼奥斯·卡马戈笔录的特拉斯卡拉编年史，库尔瓦特库特利·卡内斯是特佩蒂克帕克的开国之君，特佩蒂克帕克是特拉斯卡拉四大城邦中最早的一个。他率特奥奇奇梅卡移民携卡马斯特利信仰离开奇科莫斯特克，进入特克斯卡拉谷地，击败并驱逐当地首领，在高地建立特佩蒂克帕克。

他还记述，库尔瓦特库特利把半壁疆土和一份卡马斯特利骨灰分给弟弟特约瓦尔明基，奥科特洛尔科城邦由此发展壮大；他又把土地授予一批难民，这些人后来建立了基亚维斯特兰。

《特拉斯卡拉史》保存的两份统治者世系都以他为始祖；现代学者或将建城系于本土历9燧石年折合的1228年，或据考古置于1300年前后，其活跃年代有13、14世纪两说。

en:
Kayin Ba (1253–1342) was a commoner who made himself master of Toungoo. Born an athi, he joined Toungoo's founders in 1279 and rose from prison keeper to mayor, winning his name by adopting a Karen orphan girl.

In 1317 he backed Thawun Nge's seizure of the governorship, and Toungoo survived a siege by its overlord Pinya. After Thawun Nge's death in 1324 his powers were curtailed, but when Pinya's king died the next year and his sons fought over the throne, the seventy-two-year-old killed Governor Saw Hnit and seized power; Pinya did not intervene.

迦因拔（1253—1342）是一名平民，最终成了东吁的主人。他出身阿梯家庭，1279年投效东吁的建立者，从狱吏一路升任市长，并因收养一名克伦族孤女而得名。

1317年，他支持苏温恩格夺取总督之位，东吁挺过了宗主彬牙的围攻。1324年苏温恩格去世后他权力被削；次年彬牙国王去世、诸子争位，七十二岁的迦因拔杀死总督苏涅夺权，彬牙未加干涉。

此后十七年，他像独立君主般统治东吁，修治水利、招徕移民，坐拥150头战象。1342年他去世，享年八十九岁，编年史尊他为“敏”，即主公。他的女婿继任，东吁于1358年脱离彬牙。

en:
Maravarman Kulasekara Pandyan I (r. 1268–1308) succeeded his father Sundara Pandya as the paramount king of the Pandya realm, sharing rule with kinsmen; Marco Polo, who visited his wealthy country, called him the eldest of five brother kings. In 1279 he overthrew Rajendra III, the last Chola, ending Chola rule.

His four decades brought peace and prosperity, temple building, and flourishing port trade. Muslim chroniclers say his son Sundara Pandya killed him, opening the Pandyan civil war of 1308–1323.

摩拉跋摩·俱罗施佉罗·潘地亚一世（1268—1308年在位）继承其父孙陀罗·潘地亚，成为潘地亚的最高国王，并与王族成员共同治国；曾到访其富庶国土的马可·波罗称他为“五兄弟王中最年长者”。1279年，他攻灭末代朱罗王拉金德拉三世，终结了朱罗王朝。

他在位约四十年，国泰民安、广建寺庙，港口贸易繁盛。据穆斯林史家记载，他最终被儿子孙陀罗·潘地亚所弑，随后爆发1308—1323年的潘地亚内战。

en:
Sundara Pandya was the legitimate younger son of the Pandya emperor Maravarman Kulasekhara I at Madurai. When their father died in 1308 his half-brother Vira took the throne, but Sundara seized it in 1309, opening civil war.

In 1311 Malik Kafur of Delhi overran the kingdom, Sundara avoiding battle and losing Madurai. Restored in 1312 but defeated again, from 1314 he held the south-east with Delhi troops as a vassal. In 1323 he was beaten by Ulugh Khan, and he died around 1327.

孙陀罗·潘地亚是定都马杜赖的潘地亚皇帝摩拉跋摩·俱罗施佉罗一世的嫡出幼子。1308年父王死后，庶兄毗罗继位，孙陀罗于1309年夺位，内战由此爆发。

1311年德里大将马利克·卡富尔大举来犯，孙陀罗避不决战，马杜赖失守。他一度于1312年复位，旋即战败；1314年借德里军队占据王国东南部，向德里称藩。1323年他被乌卢格汗击败；约1327年，孙陀罗去世。

en:
Vira Pandya was the favoured illegitimate elder son of the Pandya emperor Maravarman Kulasekhara I. He succeeded around 1308 but was overthrown by his half-brother Sundara in 1309, and the brothers' war split the Pandya kingdom.

In 1311 Malik Kafur's Delhi army reached his headquarters at Birdhul, destroyed a temple and raided Madurai. Vira gained the upper hand while Sundara held the south-east. From 1325 he warred on the new Ma'bar Sultanate, lost Madurai in 1335, and was defeated and killed around 1345.

毗罗·潘地亚是潘地亚皇帝摩拉跋摩·俱罗施佉罗一世得宠的庶长子。约1308年继位，1309年被异母弟孙陀罗推翻，兄弟内战使潘地亚王国分裂。

1311年，马利克·卡富尔的德里军队抵达他的大本营比尔杜尔，摧毁一座寺庙，又攻入马杜赖。毗罗逐渐占得上风，孙陀罗则保有东南一隅。1325年起他同新兴的马巴尔苏丹国交战，1335年丢失马杜赖，约1345年兵败身亡。

en:
Guglielmo Azzone Castelbarco, often called Azzone, was a fourteenth-century condottiero of the Castelbarco family, vassals of the bishop of Trent, and lord of lands in the Vallagarina. The son of Federico Castelbarco, he married Tommasina Gonzaga in 1319.

A loyal follower of the Scaligeri, on 16 August 1328 he led Veronese troops in the expulsion of the Bonacolsi from Mantua. In 1333 he hosted the future Emperor Charles IV at Avio Castle.

古列尔莫·阿佐内·卡斯泰尔巴科（常称阿佐内）是14世纪的雇佣军将领，出身特伦托主教的封臣卡斯泰尔巴科家族，领有拉加里纳山谷的领地。他是费代里科·卡斯泰尔巴科之子，1319年娶托马西娜·贡扎加为妻。

en:
Azzone Francesco Castelbarco (c. 1327–1410) was the last lord of the Dossomaggiore branch of his house, holding Avio, Ala and Brentonico. In 1388, after the Rovione line died out, Bishop Albert enfeoffed him with Castel San Giorgio.

In 1410, the year of his death, he willed at Avio that if his only heir Ettore died, the vicariates would pass to Venice. When Ettore died in 1411 Venice occupied the lands, beginning the era of the Four Vicariates.

en:
Guglielmo Azzone Castelbarco (born c. 1301) was lord of Ala, Avio and Brentonico in the bishopric of Trent and a condottiero loyal to the Scaligeri of Verona. He was nephew of the condottiero Guglielmo Castelbarco il Grande (died 1320).

In 1319 he married Tommasina Gonzaga, daughter of Ludovico I, first lord of Mantua and a key Scaligeri ally. On 16 August 1328 he led armed Veronese into Mantua and took part in expelling the Bonacolsi, helping bring the Gonzaga to power.

Faithful to the imperial cause, in 1333 he hosted Charles of Luxembourg, emperor from 1355, in his castle of Avio. He and Tommasina had six children. His tomb, first set in the castle's chapel of Sant'Antonio Abate, now stands in the church at Loppio.

古列尔莫·阿佐内·卡斯泰尔巴科（约1301年生）是特伦托主教区阿拉、阿维奥和布伦托尼科的领主，也是效忠维罗纳斯卡利杰里家族的雇佣兵首领。他是雇佣兵首领“大”古列尔莫·卡斯泰尔巴科（卒于1320年）的侄子。

1319年，他迎娶托马西娜·贡扎加，她是首任曼托瓦统治者卢多维科一世之女，而贡扎加家族是斯卡利杰里家族的重要盟友。1328年8月16日，他率领维罗纳武装进入曼托瓦，参与驱逐博纳科尔西家族，助贡扎加家族上台。

他忠于神圣罗马帝国，1333年在阿维奥城堡接待了卢森堡的查理，此人1355年成为皇帝。他与托马西娜生有六名子女。他的墓椁最初安放在城堡的圣安东尼·阿巴特礼拜堂，现存于洛皮奥的教堂。

en:
Nicolò da Bruna (Nikolaus von Brünn), born in Brno, was prince-bishop of Trent from 1338 to 1347. As chancellor to Charles, Margrave of Moravia, he followed him to the Tyrol in 1336, when Charles became guardian of the young counts John Henry and Margaret.

After Bishop Henry of Metz died that October, Charles had Nicolò named his successor, confirmed by the pope in 1338. As bishop he ended feuds among the valley nobility, recovered fiefs usurped by the Castelbarco and commissioned an enlarged Codex Wangianus.

Habsburg schemes then wrecked his position: in 1341 Margaret repudiated her husband, who fled with Nicolò to Aquileia, and in 1342 married Louis of Bavaria, whose imperial father took control of the bishopric. Charles, now emperor, recovered Trent in 1347, but Nicolò died in Moravia that November without returning.

尼科洛·达·布鲁纳（德语称尼古劳斯·冯·布林）生于布尔诺，1338至1347年任特伦托采邑主教。他原是藩侯查理的掌玺官，1336年随查理前往蒂罗尔，当时查理任年少伯爵约翰·海因里希和玛格丽特的监护人。

同年10月主教梅斯的亨利去世，查理让尼科洛接任，1338年获教皇确认。任内他平息河谷贵族争斗，收回卡斯泰尔巴科家族侵占的封地，并主持编纂增补版《万吉安努斯法典》。

随后哈布斯堡的图谋毁了他的地位：1341年玛格丽特拒绝丈夫，后者与尼科洛逃往阿奎莱亚；1342年她改嫁巴伐利亚的路德维希，路德维希的皇帝父亲夺取了主教领地。已成皇帝的查理1347年夺回特伦托，尼科洛却于同年11月在摩拉维亚去世，未能回去。

en:
Tode Mongke (died 1287) was a son of Toqoqan and a grandson of Batu Khan who ruled the Golden Horde from 1280 to 1287. After Berke's death in 1267 he was a candidate, but the Jochid elite chose his brother Mengu-Timur; he only took the throne with the backing of the powerful commander Nogai.

He converted to Islam in 1283 and left warfare to Nogai, while backing Andrey of Vladimir against Dmitry. In 1287 Nogai forced him to abdicate in favor of Talabuga, and he died the same year.

脱脱蒙哥（?—1287）是托托罕之子、拔都汗之孙，1280至1287年为金帐汗国的汗。1267年别儿哥死后他本是汗位候选人之一，但术赤系贵族选择了他的兄弟忙哥帖木儿；后来凭借权臣那海的支持，他才得以称汗。

他于1283年皈依伊斯兰教，战事多委于那海，在罗斯诸公国问题上与那海对立，支持弗拉基米尔的安德烈反对德米特里。1287年那海迫使他退位，改立兀剌不花，他本人也于同年死去。

en:
Toghrilcha was a Mongol prince of the Golden Horde, a son of the khan Mengu-Timur. He was among the princes who deposed the khan Tode-Mengu in 1287.

Later he fell out with Toqta, who had seized the throne in 1291; Toqta had him executed, married his widow, and drove his young son Öz Beg into exile. That son returned after Toqta's death to rule the Golden Horde as Öz Beg Khan from 1313 to 1341.

秃黑里勒察是金帐汗国的蒙古宗王，汗王忙哥帖木儿之子。他参与了1287年推翻汗王脱脱蒙哥的行动。

后来他与1291年夺取汗位的脱脱反目，被脱脱处死；脱脱纳娶他的遗孀，并将他年幼的儿子月即别放逐。月即别在脱脱死后归来，于1313至1341年统治金帐汗国。

en:
Talabuga (died 1291), son of Tartu and great-grandson of Batu, was khan of the Golden Horde from 1287 to 1291. In 1285 he joined Nogai's disastrous raid on Hungary, afterwards plundering the allied Galician lands.

Backed by Nogai, he deposed Tode Mongke in 1287 and took the throne; his reign saw raids on Poland and border clashes with the Ilkhanate. In 1291 Nogai lured him into an ambush and had him strangled, raising Toqta to the throne.

en:
Tolui (c. 1191–1232), youngest son of Genghis Khan and Börte, was reckoned the finest warrior of the four brothers and the father of two great khans. From 1211 he fought the Jin, and in 1221 Genghis sent him to subdue Khorasan with perhaps seven thousand men.

Merv surrendered on promise of fair treatment, but he broke his word and put its people to the sword. Nishapur, where Genghis's son-in-law Toquchar was killed, was stormed and nearly all slain; at Herat he killed only the garrison.

After Genghis died in 1227 he inherited most of his army and was regent, swearing allegiance to Ögedei in 1229. He routed the Jin at Sanfeng in 1230–1232 and died late that year: officially he drank a shaman's cursed potion to save Ögedei; others blamed drink or poison. His wife Sorghaghtani Beki raised Möngke and Kublai; Möngke took the throne in 1251.

拖雷（约1191—1232）是成吉思汗与孛儿帖的幼子，被视为四兄弟中最善战的一个，也是两位大汗的父亲。1211年起他率军攻金，1221年成吉思汗派他以约七千人平定呼罗珊。

木鹿城在对方承诺公平对待后投降，他却背弃诺言，把居民屠杀。成吉思汗的女婿脱忽察儿在你沙不儿被杀，该城随后被攻破，几乎全城被杀；而在也里，他只杀了守军。

成吉思汗1227年去世后，他继承了父亲的大部分军队并监国，1229年向窝阔台宣誓效忠。1230至1232年他在三峰山大破金军，同年年末死去：官方说法是他饮下巫师施咒的水代窝阔台受死，另有说法称死于酗酒或遭毒杀。妻子唆鲁禾帖尼抚养了蒙哥、忽必烈，1251年蒙哥即位。

en:
Jeanne I of Chalon-Tonnerre (1300–1360) was countess of Tonnerre, daughter of William of Chalon, count of Auxerre and heir of Tonnerre, and Eleanor of Savoy. After her father died in 1304, her mother became regent of the property of Jeanne and her brother John.

In 1321 she married Robert of Burgundy, but the marriage was childless and Robert died in 1334. Dying in an epidemic, she left Tonnerre to her brother by will.

沙隆-托内尔的让娜一世（1300—1360）是托内尔女伯爵，为欧塞尔伯爵、托内尔指定继承人沙隆的纪尧姆与萨伏依的埃莉诺之女。其父1304年去世后，母亲摄政管理她与弟弟让的财产。

en:
Margaret of Burgundy (1250–1308), second daughter of Odo, Count of Nevers, and Maud of Dampierre, inherited Tonnerre in 1262. In 1268 she married Charles of Anjou, king of Sicily; she became queen of Albania in 1272 and titular queen of Jerusalem in 1277.

The Sicilian Vespers of 1282 left her queen only of Naples. Widowed in 1285, she withdrew to her castle of Tonnerre with two noble companions, where they lived in prayer and charity, and she founded the Hospice of the Fontenilles.

She died on 4 September 1308 and was buried in the hospice. Her lands passed to her great-nephew John II of Chalon-Auxerre.

zh:
勃艮第的玛格丽特（1250—1308）是讷韦尔伯爵厄德与当皮埃尔的莫德的次女，1262年继承托内尔伯国。1268年她嫁给西西里国王安茹的查理，1272年成为阿尔巴尼亚王后，1277年又成为名义上的耶路撒冷王后。

1282年西西里晚祷之后，她的头衔只剩下那不勒斯王后。1285年守寡后，她与两名贵族女伴退居托内尔城堡，以祈祷和施舍度日，并创立了丰特尼耶济贫院。

她于1308年9月4日去世，葬在济贫院内，领地留给侄孙沙隆-欧塞尔的约翰二世。

en:
Toqoqan (c. 1220s–1256/1259) was a Mongol prince of the Golden Horde, a son of its founder Batu Khan and great-grandson of Genghis Khan. He held his own appanage as the Ulus of Jochi took shape after the Mongol campaign in the west.

Though Toqoqan never reigned, his sons by Köchü Khatun, Mengu-Timur and Tode Mongke, both became khans of the Golden Horde, while his eldest son Tartu was the father of Khan Talabuga.

托托罕（约1220年代—1256/1259）是金帐汗国的蒙古宗王，为汗国建立者拔都之子、成吉思汗曾孙。蒙古西征之后术赤兀鲁思形成之际，他领有自己的份地。

en:
Toqta (died 1312), a son of Mengu-Timur and great-grandson of Batu, was khan of the Golden Horde from 1291 to 1312. Placed on the throne by Nogai after Talabuga's fall, he at first ruled as Nogai's client, then rebelled; defeated in 1297, he crushed Nogai around 1300 and reunited the steppe.

Angered by the Genoese slave trade, he arrested Italian merchants at Sarai and besieged Caffa, whose defenders burned the city in 1308. He died in 1312 preparing a campaign against Russia.

en:
Torquemada names Catoxcan as the eighth of nine semi-legendary lords who, after the Totonacs settled at Mizquihuacan about 690, ruled in nine ages of eighty years each. He governed in peace and, like his predecessors, was said to have reigned eighty years before dying.

His two sons, Nahuacatl and Ixquahuitl, succeeded jointly; Torquemada presents their feud as the turning point that ended the long Totonac peace, split the nation and let the Chichimec Xihuitlpopoca make the Totonacs his vassals.

en:
Torquemada records Ixquahuitl as the younger son of the Totonac lord Catoxcan of Mizquihuacan, who in the ninth age after the settlement of about 690 inherited rule jointly with his elder brother Nahuacatl.

Both were married and neither would yield precedence, so they betrayed each other and the people split into factions. Defeated, Ixquahuitl abandoned Mizquihuacan for Ocotlán, where he married and had children, then moved on to Xoxopanco, married again and ruled that people for the rest of his life. He left the lordship to his son Quatemazatl. Their divided lands then fell to the Chichimec Xihuitlpopoca.

en:
Torquemada makes Nahuacatl, elder son of Catoxcan, the last of the nine semi-legendary lords of the Totonacs of Mizquihuacan, in the ninth age after the settlement of about 690. He and his brother Ixquahuitl inherited jointly; both married, neither acknowledged the other's precedence, and their treason split the town into warring bands.

Nahuacatl finally abandoned his people for another province, where he submitted to its lord, married and ended his days, leaving one son. With both lords gone, the Chichimec Xihuitlpopoca entered the masterless country and made the Totonacs his vassals.

en:
Alexios I Megas Komnenos (c. 1182–1222) founded the Empire of Trebizond with his brother David. A grandson of Emperor Andronikos I, he seized Trebizond in April 1204 with his aunt Queen Tamar of Georgia's support, as the Fourth Crusade took Constantinople.

While David conquered the western Pontic lands, Alexios held Trebizond against a Seljuk siege. In 1214 the Turks captured him defending Sinope; he was freed after the city surrendered on becoming the vassal of Sultan Kaykaus I.

Sinope's loss isolated Trebizond from the other Greek lands. He died on 1 February 1222, leaving the throne to his son-in-law Andronikos.

阿历克塞一世·梅加斯·科穆宁（约1182—1222）与弟弟大卫共同建立了特拉比松帝国。他是拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡一世之孙，1204年4月趁第四次十字军攻占君士坦丁堡之际，在姨母格鲁吉亚女王塔玛尔支持下夺取特拉比松。

大卫征服了本都西部的土地，阿历克塞则顶住塞尔柱人的围攻。1214年，他在保卫锡诺普时被突厥人俘虏，直到该城投降、他向苏丹凯考斯一世称臣后才获释。

锡诺普的失陷使特拉比松与其他希腊地区隔绝。他于1222年2月1日去世，女婿安德洛尼卡继位。

Alexios II Megas Komnenos (1282–1330), elder son of John II and Eudokia Palaiologina, became emperor of Trebizond in 1297 at fourteen, ruling at the empire's peak. Around 1300 he married Jiajak Jaqeli, daughter of the atabeg of Samtskhe, without the consent of his guardian and uncle Andronikos II.

In 1301–1302 he routed Turkoman raiders who had sacked Kerasous and captured their general. He later checked the Genoese by treaties and granted Venice equal privileges.

After Sinopite pirates burned Trebizond, he built the harbour sea walls in 1324. He died of plague on 3 May 1330, succeeded by Andronikos III.

阿历克塞二世·梅加斯·科穆宁（1282—1330）是约翰二世与欧多基娅·巴列奥略吉娜的长子，1297年十四岁时成为特拉比松皇帝，在位时帝国正值鼎盛。约1300年，他未经监护人兼舅父安德洛尼卡二世同意，迎娶萨姆茨赫阿塔贝格之女贾贾克·贾克利。

Alexios III Megas Komnenos (1338–1390) ruled Trebizond from 1349 until his death. The son of Emperor Basil and Irene, he was raised at the Byzantine court until John VI Kantakouzenos sent him to Trebizond in 1349 to replace the deposed Michael.

Crowned in 1350, he married Theodora Kantakouzene in 1351, defeated the rebel Niketas Scholares, and survived an ambush in 1363. Marriage alliances with Turkmen neighbors and Georgia secured his reign; he died in 1390 and was succeeded by his son Manuel III.

en:
Andronikos I Gidos (died 1235) ruled the Empire of Trebizond from 1222, the only emperor unrelated by blood to its founder Alexios I, whose daughter he married.

After a Seljuk raid on Trapezuntine territory, Andronikos sent a fleet against Sinope. In 1224 he led the defense of Trebizond against a Seljuk siege until a storm scattered the attackers; the captured sultan agreed to end Trebizond's vassalage, tribute and military obligations.

After Andronikos backed the Khwarazmshah Jalal al-Din against the Seljuks in 1230, Trebizond became a vassal once more. He died in 1235 and John I succeeded him.

Andronikos II Megas Komnenos (c. 1240–1266), eldest son of the Trapezuntine emperor Manuel I by Anna Xylaloe, succeeded his father as emperor in 1263. The chronicler Panaretos records that Manuel had chosen him and that he reigned for three years.

The chief event of his rule was the loss of Sinope to the Seljuk Turks under Mu'in al-Din Suleyman in 1265, giving the Turks a major Black Sea port. He died prematurely in 1265 or 1266.

Andronikos III Megas Komnenos (died 8 January 1332), eldest son of Alexios II and Jiajak Jaqeli, was emperor of Trebizond from October 1330 after a five-month interregnum following his father's death. Panaretos gives his reign fifteen months.

One of his first acts was to kill his two younger brothers George Azachoutlou and Michael Achpougas; another brother, Basil, escaped to Constantinople. Like his father, he died of bubonic plague, on 8 January 1332, and his young son Manuel II succeeded him.

en:
Anna Anachoutlou (died 3 September 1342), eldest daughter of Alexios II, spent most of her life as a nun while two brothers and a nephew reigned in quick succession. After Basil's death in 1340 his widow Irene Palaiologina, an outsider to the Grand Komnenos line, took the throne.

In July 1341 Anna escaped her convent and rallied the provinces: Laz and Zan tribesmen and Georgian soldiers. On 17 July she entered Trebizond unopposed and was crowned empress, Irene having abdicated days earlier.

Nobles who preferred a male heir turned to her uncle Michael, but when he landed with Byzantine troops the Laz beat them and Anna imprisoned him. Yet the Scholarioi clan and other nobles deposed and strangled her on 3 September 1342, and Michael's son John III took the city next day.

安娜·阿纳卓特鲁（？—1342）是阿历克塞二世的长女，大半生在修道院中度过，其间两位兄弟和一个侄子先后短暂在位。1340年瓦西里去世后，他的遗孀艾琳·巴列奥略吉娜这个大科穆宁家族的外人登上皇位。

1341年7月，安娜逃出修道院，召集各地的拉兹人、赞人和格鲁吉亚士兵。7月17日，她兵不血刃进入特拉比松，加冕为女皇，艾琳数日前已退位。

一些贵族更愿拥立男性继承人、她的叔父米哈伊尔，但米哈伊尔带着拜占庭军队登陆后，被拉兹人击败，安娜将他囚禁。斯科拉里奥伊家族等贵族仍将她废黜，于9月3日勒死；次日米哈伊尔之子约翰三世占领该城。

en:
Basil Megas Komnenos (died 6 April 1340), younger son of Alexios II and Jiajak Jaqeli, ruled Trebizond from 1332 amid a long civil war among its great nobles. When his brother Andronikos III took the throne in 1330 and killed two of their brothers, Basil was in Constantinople and escaped.

Invited home after Andronikos's death, he deposed the child Manuel II in 1332. A revolt in Manuel's favour was crushed and Manuel was killed in 1333, probably on Basil's orders. The city came to hate Basil: when a solar eclipse was read as divine wrath, the crowd forced him into the citadel.

In 1334 he married Irene Palaiologina, illegitimate daughter of the Byzantine emperor, but took a mistress also named Irene, marrying her around 1339. He died on 6 April 1340, apparently poisoned by his wife, who at once seized the throne.

1334年他迎娶拜占庭皇帝的私生女伊琳娜·巴列奥略，但又纳了一位同名的情妇，约1339年与她结婚。1340年4月6日他死去，疑遭妻子毒杀，后者随即夺取皇位。

Eudokia Palaiologina (c. 1265–1302), third daughter of Michael VIII Palaiologos, married John II Megas Komnenos in 1282 and bore him two sons, Alexios II and Michael.

After John died she returned in 1298 to her brother Andronikos II's court with Michael. Andronikos planned to wed her to Stefan Uroš II Milutin of Serbia as a peace bargain, but she refused. Andronikos also wanted Alexios to annul his Georgian marriage.

In 1301 Eudokia won leave for Trebizond, supposedly to make Alexios II annul his marriage; instead she told him to keep his wife. She died on 18 September 1302.

en:
George Megas Komnenos (c. 1255 – after 1284), elder son of Manuel I and Irene Syrikaina, succeeded his half-brother Andronikos as emperor of Trebizond in 1266 and ruled fourteen years. A boy at his accession, he first ruled through a regent and was the first Trapezuntine emperor styled Megas Komnenos.

After Michael VIII Palaiologos accepted church union at Lyons in 1274, anti-unionist refugees cast George as Orthodoxy's champion and pressed him to seek the throne of Constantinople. In June 1280 his officials betrayed him and captured him. In 1284 he failed to seize Trebizond from his brother John II, then vanished from the sources.

Helen Megale Komnene (died 1366) was a Trapezuntine princess, probably a daughter of Emperor Basil of Trebizond, and the first wife of King Bagrat V of Georgia. She bore Bagrat two sons, the future king George VII and a David otherwise unknown.

She died in 1366 during a plague outbreak, likely a recurrence of the Black Death, that swept Georgia. A year later Bagrat married Anna, a daughter of Alexios III of Trebizond.

en:
John I Komnenos Axouch (c. 1214–1238) was Emperor of Trebizond from 1235, the eldest son of the founder Alexios I and Theodora Axouchina. When Alexios died in 1222 the crown first passed to his son-in-law Andronikos I Gidos, whom John succeeded in 1235.

In 1238 he died playing tzykanion, the Byzantine polo-like game, after falling from his horse and being trampled. His heir Ioannikios was confined to a monastery, and his brother Manuel I became emperor.

en:
John II Megas Komnenos (c. 1262–1297), youngest son of Manuel I and Irene Syrikaina, became emperor of Trebizond in June 1280 after his brother George was seized by his officials. In 1281 he rejected Michael VIII Palaiologos' demand to abandon the title Emperor of the Romans.

After Papadopoulos revolted, seized the citadel and held John prisoner, he married Michael's daughter Eudokia Palaiologina. He retained the imperial dignity, but replaced the Roman title with Emperor and Autocrat of all the East.

In 1284 he foiled George's attempt to regain the throne. John died on 16 August 1297 and was succeeded by Alexios II.

en:
John III Megas Komnenos (c. 1321–1362) was emperor of Trebizond from 1342 to 1344. Son of Michael Megas Komnenos, he was raised in Constantinople, where Niketas Scholares brought him to claim the throne. With Genoese galleys he stormed Trebizond in September 1342, and the deposed empress Anna Anachoutlou was strangled after his coronation.

His dissolute reign ended in May 1344, when Niketas freed his captive father and deposed him. Exiled to Adrianople, he escaped about 1357 and died at Sinope in 1362.

en:
Irene Palaiologina (c. 1315 – after 1341) was an illegitimate daughter of the Byzantine emperor Andronikos III. In 1335 she married Emperor Basil of Trebizond, who divorced her in 1339 for a mistress also named Irene.

On 6 April 1340 she probably had Basil poisoned and seized the throne, becoming Trebizond's second reigning empress. Her position was insecure, since she was not a member of the ruling Komnenos dynasty; she sent Basil's second wife and sons to Constantinople.

Civil war followed, and rumours of a lover sparked rioting. On 17 July 1341 Anna Anachoutlou took Trebizond; Irene was deposed and sent to Constantinople.

伊琳娜·巴列奥略（约1315—1341年后）是拜占庭皇帝安德洛尼卡三世的私生女，1335年嫁给特拉比松皇帝瓦西里。瓦西里后来与同名情人相好，于1339年与她离婚。

1340年4月6日，她疑似毒杀瓦西里，夺取皇位，成为特拉比松帝国第二位女皇帝。她并非统治特拉比松的科穆宁家族成员，地位不稳，便把瓦西里的第二任妻子和儿子送往君士坦丁堡。

随后内战爆发，她有情人的传闻又引起骚乱。1341年7月17日，安娜·阿纳卓特鲁攻占特拉比松，伊琳娜被迫退位，被送回君士坦丁堡。

en:
Irene of Trebizond (died c. 1382) rose from Emperor Basil's mistress to bigamous wife, and then to power behind a boy emperor. She bore Basil two sons, Alexios and John, before he married her in 1339, though the Patriarch of Constantinople protested the marriage.

Basil died in April 1340, and rumour blamed the discarded empress Irene Palaiologina, who seized power at once and sent Irene and her sons to Constantinople. When John VI Kantakouzenos won the Byzantine civil war, he and Niketas Scholares backed John's bid, and in 1349 the thirteen-year-old took the throne as Alexios III.

Irene ran the regency against the Doranites family, whose revolt failed within six months. She was last recorded at a great-grandson's baptism in 1382.

特拉比松的伊琳娜（约1382年卒）从皇帝瓦西里的情妇做到重婚的妻子，又成为少年皇帝背后的掌权者。1339年瓦西里娶她之前，她已为他生下阿历克塞和约翰两个儿子，君士坦丁堡牧首对这桩婚姻提出抗议。

1340年4月瓦西里去世，传言说是被弃的皇后艾琳·巴列奥略吉娜所害；她随即夺权，把艾琳母子送往君士坦丁堡。约翰六世·坎塔库泽努斯赢得拜占庭内战后，与尼基塔斯·斯科拉里斯一同支持约翰争位，十三岁的约翰于1349年登基，即阿历克塞三世。

艾琳主持摄政，对付多拉尼特家族，该家族的叛乱在半年内即告失败。她最后一次见于记载是1382年出席曾孙的洗礼。

1340年4月瓦西里去世，传言说是被弃的皇后艾琳·巴列奥略吉娜所害；她随即夺权，把艾琳母子送往君士坦丁堡。#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('byz_john_kantakouzenos').GetID],X #L 约翰六世·坎塔库泽努斯#!#!赢得拜占庭内战后，与尼基塔斯·斯科拉里斯一同支持约翰争位，十三岁的约翰于1349年登基，即#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('tre_alexios_komnenos').GetID],X #L 阿历克塞三世#!#!。

艾琳主持摄政，对付多拉尼特家族，该家族的叛乱在半年内即告失败。她最后一次见于记载是1382年出席曾孙的洗礼。

en:
Manuel I Megas Komnenos (died March 1263), a son of Alexios I, succeeded his elder brother John I in 1238 and ruled Trebizond over a strip of the southern Black Sea coast. The chronicler Michael Panaretos praised him as his line's greatest and most fortunate general.

In 1254 he retook Sinope from the Sultanate of Rum, and between 1250 and 1260 rebuilt the Hagia Sophia monastery in Trebizond. After Michael VIII Palaiologos recovered Constantinople in 1261, Manuel refused to renounce the imperial title. He died in March 1263; four of his children later ruled Trebizond.

曼努埃尔一世·梅加斯·科穆宁（？—1263）是阿历克塞一世之子，1238年继兄长约翰一世之后统治特拉比松，领有黑海南岸的狭长地带。编年史作家帕纳雷托斯盛赞他是家族中最伟大、最幸运的统帅。

1254年，他从罗姆苏丹国手中收复锡诺普，并于1250至1260年间在特拉比松重建圣索菲亚修道院。1261年米海尔八世·巴列奥略收复君士坦丁堡后要求他放弃皇帝头衔，被他拒绝。1263年3月他去世，其四名子女后来先后统治特拉比松。

en:
Manuel II Megas Komnenos (c. 1324–1333), the son of Andronikos III, became emperor of Trebizond at the age of eight in January 1332. In August 1332 his army defeated an invasion by Bayram Beg, Emir of Chalybia, at Asomatos.

Three weeks later his uncle Basil returned from Constantinople and deposed him after eight months. A failed revolt in February 1333 prompted Basil to order the boy's execution, making Manuel the only deposed Trapezuntine emperor to be put to death.

曼努埃尔二世·梅加斯·科穆宁（约1324—1333）是安德洛尼卡三世之子，1332年1月八岁时成为特拉比松皇帝。同年8月，他的军队在阿索马托斯击败哈利比亚埃米尔巴伊拉姆贝伊的入侵。

en:
Michael Megas Komnenos (c. 1288–after 1355) was a younger son of Emperor John II of Trebizond and Eudokia. Raised in Constantinople, he married Acropolitissa and fathered John III. In 1341 he claimed Trebizond's throne but nobles imprisoned him.

Freed by Niketas Scholares, he was crowned emperor in 1344, deposed his son John III, and reigned until he was toppled in 1349. Forced into a monastery and exiled to Constantinople, he was released in 1355, failed to regain it and died soon after.

米哈伊尔·梅加斯·科穆宁（约1288—1355年后）是特拉比松皇帝约翰二世与欧多基娅较年幼的儿子。他在君士坦丁堡长大，娶阿克罗波利提莎为妻，生子约翰三世。1341年他前往特拉比松争位，却被贵族囚禁。

后来他被尼基塔斯·斯霍拉里斯释放，1344年加冕为帝，废黜儿子约翰三世，统治到1349年被推翻。他被迫出家，随后被流放至君士坦丁堡，1355年获释后试图夺回特拉比松未果，不久去世。

Theodora Megale Komnene (before 1253 – after 1285) was a daughter of the Trapezuntine emperor Manuel I by Rusudan, a Georgian princess. In 1284, backed by David VI Narin of Imereti, she seized the crown from her half-brother John II and ruled as empress for about a year.

She struck her own silver and bronze coins, the only reigning empress of Trebizond to do so. John II soon defeated her and recovered the throne, and she went into exile in her mother's Georgia.

Syed Shah Nasiruddin was a Sufi saint and military commander who helped spread Islam in Bengal. He left Baghdad after the Mongols sacked it in 1258, settled in Bengal, joined the Suhrawardiyya order, and rose to be Sipah Salar of Sultan Shamsuddin Firoz Shah.

In 1303 he led the third expedition against Gour Govinda of Sylhet, which triumphed after Shah Jalal joined. Dispatched against neighboring Taraf, whose ruler had executed a qadi, he occupied it and became governor, founding a hereditary ruling line.

赛义德·沙阿·纳西尔丁是推动伊斯兰教在孟加拉传播的苏非圣徒与军事统帅。1258年蒙古人攻陷巴格达后他离开该城，辗转来到孟加拉，加入苏哈拉瓦迪教团，后来成为苏丹沙姆斯丁·菲鲁兹沙的军队统帅。

1303年，他率军第三次征讨锡尔赫特的高尔·戈宾达，在沙阿·贾拉勒加入后攻克其地。随后他被派往邻邦塔拉夫——其统治者处死了一名卡迪——占领该国并受任总督，其家族此后世袭统治当地。

en:
Baldwin of Luxembourg (c. 1285–1354) was the youngest son of Count Henry VI of Luxembourg. In 1307 Trier's cathedral chapter elected him archbishop, and Pope Clement V consecrated him in 1308. He inherited a debt-laden see and steadied it with a French-style administration and tolls granted by his brother Henry.

He helped win the crown of the Romans for Henry VII in 1308 and went with him to Rome for the imperial coronation of 1312. He later backed his great-nephew Charles IV in 1346, and held that the electors alone choose the king, a principle the Golden Bull of 1356 later fixed in law.

In 1328 troops of Loretta of Sponheim captured him, and he was freed only after paying ransom. He built the Balduinbrücke at Koblenz and ruled Trier until his death.

鲍德温·冯·卢森堡（约1285—1354）是卢森堡伯爵亨利六世的幼子。1307年特里尔主教座堂会议选他为大主教，1308年由教皇克雷芒五世为他祝圣。他接手的是一个负债累累的大主教区，靠仿照法国的官署制度和兄长亨利授予的关税收入稳住了局面。

他在1308年促成兄长亨利七世当选罗马人的国王，并随其前往罗马参加1312年的皇帝加冕礼。后来他扶持1346年的侄孙查理四世，并主张只有选帝侯才有权选出国王，这一原则后来被1356年的《金玺诏书》写入法律。

1328年，施蓬海姆的洛雷塔派兵俘获他，他付出赎金后才获释。他在科布伦茨修建了鲍德温桥，统治特里尔直至去世。

en:
Anton von Turn was the last baron of the Valais house of Turn, holding Frutigen. Succeeding his father Peter III around 1356, he clashed with Bishop Tavelli of Sion: he seized Granges Castle in 1364, and in 1375 his men murdered the bishop.

The upper Valais districts rose and drove his family into exile in Savoy, which bought his estates. He sold his Lauterbrunnen lands in 1395 and Frutigen to Bern in 1400, and died in 1405, the last of his line.

Aymon II von Turn, also spelled Aymo (c. 1240–1276), was a baron of the leading Valais noble house seated at the Gestelnburg above Niedergesteln, and the son of Gerold I. On his father's death he inherited the vicedominatus, the bishop's temporal advocacy, of Conthey.

His sister Nantelma, widow of Rudolf von Raron, brought the family her late husband's estates at St. Niklaus and Zermatt. Aymon headed the house from 1265 until his death in 1276, when his son Peter II succeeded him.

Aymon II von Turn, also spelled Aymo (c. 1240–1276), was a baron of the leading Valais noble house seated at the Gestelnburg above Niedergesteln, and the son of Gerold I. On his father's death he inherited the vicedominatus, the bishop's temporal advocacy, of Conthey.

His sister Nantelma, widow of Rudolf von Raron, brought the family her late husband's estates at St. Niklaus and Zermatt. Aymon headed the house from 1265 until his death in 1276, when his son Peter II succeeded him.

en:
Johann I von Turn (c. 1280–1324), son of Peter II, ruled the Valais barony from the Gestelnburg. By his marriage to Elisabeth von Wädenswil he acquired the Bernese Oberland lordships of Frutigen and Mülenen.

He served in turn as imperial vicar of Como in 1311, Landvogt of the bishop of Sion from 1315 to 1317, and imperial governor at Milan in 1322. Johann died in 1323 or 1324, and his son Peter III succeeded him.

en:
Peter II von Turn (c. 1260–1308), son of Aymon II, was the first of his house to style himself baron of Niedergesteln at the Gestelnburg in the Valais. In 1291 he served the counts of Savoy as Landvogt of the Waadt.

He led the Valais nobility in revolt against Bishop Boniface de Challant of Sion, but after defeat at the Sustmatten in 1296 he made peace with the bishop in 1299. He ruled until his death in 1308 and was followed by his son Johann.

en:
Peter III von Turn headed the leading Valais noble house from the Gestelnburg, with estates in the Bernese Oberland. Succeeding Johann I around 1324, he sold off lands: Laupen to Bern, his Mülenen rights in 1341, and Lauterbrunnen tenants to Interlaken Abbey in 1346.

In 1349 his family feuded with that of Bishop Tavelli of Sion; the war drew in Count Amadeus VI of Savoy, whose troops burned Sion in 1353. Peter died about 1356 and was followed by his son Anton.

en:
Muhammad ibn Thabit was a head of the Banu Thabit, the clan ruling fourteenth-century Tripoli. Ibn Khaldun records that after townspeople killed the Hafsid governor, he was set over Tripoli in 1326 or 1327 and ruled on his own account for about twenty years; the Hafsids of Tunis kept only the right to name its qadi.

His domains ran from Tripoli to Gabes and Jabal Nafusa. He also annexed Jerba, retaken by the Hafsids in 1347 or 1348.

Thābit ibn Muḥammad was a ruler of the Banū Thābit, the dynasty that governed fourteenth-century Tripoli. An Arabic account names him its first ruler after the townspeople expelled the Ḥafṣid governor in 1323.

The Banū Thābit continued to recognize Ḥafṣid suzerainty while acting as autonomous lords over Tripolitania, with power stretching from Tripoli toward Gabès and the Nafusa Mountains. In 1354–1355 the Genoese seized Tripoli, and Thābit died in 1355.

Yury Mikhailovich, known in genealogies as Yury of Tarusa, is the semi-legendary progenitor of the Tarusa branch of the princes of Chernigov. Pedigrees name him a son of Mikhail Vsevolodovich, the grand prince of Kiev executed by the Mongols in 1246, and prince of Tarusa on the Oka.

Princely houses including the Obolensky, Volkonsky and Dolgorukov descended from his sons. Modern scholarship, judging from his descendants' dates, places him in the first half of the fourteenth century.

Biaquino II da Camino (c. 1180 – by 1227) was an Italian nobleman and soldier of the Trevisan da Camino family, the son of Gabriele II da Camino and Engelenda. Left fatherless as a child, he and his brothers were raised by guardians. In 1218 he appears as podestà of Belluno.

He then joined the Fifth Crusade, fitting out at his own expense a galley named the Biaquina. He sailed from Venice and died in the Holy Land before 1227, never returning home.

en:
Biaquino III da Camino (c. 1205 – July 1274) was a Trevisan noble, son of Guecellone IV and father of Gherardo III da Camino. A supporter of the Guelphs, he lost his family's lands in 1233 over the murder of the podestà Marino Dandolo. With Alberico da Romano he helped subdue Treviso in 1239 and served as its podestà in 1241–1243.

He fought the Ghibelline Ezzelino da Romano and Frederick II, helping defend Parma against the emperor in 1247. After reconciling his kin in 1259, he joined Treviso's Council of Three Hundred in 1263, paving the way for his son's signoria.

en:
Biaquino VI da Camino (1269 or 1270 – before 1317) was the second son of Guecellone VI and Beatrice Bonaparte of the da Camino house. Left fatherless in 1272, he grew up beside his elder brother Tolberto III, with whom he received the seignory of Oderzo in 1285.

In 1291 the brothers conspired against their cousin Gherardo III and, on failing, fled to Venice. In 1312 Biaquino led troops for Padua against Cangrande della Scala; he and Tolberto probably helped organise the December revolt that ended da Camino rule in Treviso. His only surviving son Guecellone VIII is named in Tolberto's 1317 will.

en:
Gabriele II da Camino (1145–1186) was an Italian nobleman of the Marca Trevigiana, son of Guecellone II and Sofia di Colfosco. He fought in Frederick Barbarossa's imperial coalition, and in 1177 joined his father at Venice for the peace with the Lombard League.

After the coalition's defeat he had to acknowledge the communes' authority, taking citizenship at Conegliano in 1179 and at Treviso in 1183. He died around 1186 at about forty, shortly after his father, leaving young sons led by Guecellone IV.

en:
Gherardo III da Camino (c. 1240 – 1306), son of Biaquino and India da Camposampiero, was the most outstanding lord of the Trevisan da Camino family. He received the seignory of Feltre and Belluno from their bishop in 1266. He expelled the Ghibellines from Treviso on 15 November 1283, after which he was elected capitano generale.

A tyrannical but efficient ruler, he boosted Treviso's economy and patronised arts and feasts, hosting Dante Alighieri at his court. His later years saw repeated plots, the last in 1305 by his son Rizzardo, and he died in 1306.

en:
Guecellone IV da Camino (c. 1177–c. 1236), eldest son of Gabriele II, was orphaned at nine and raised under guardians. In 1191 he swore loyalty to Treviso's podesta Ezzelino II da Romano, as the Guelph da Camino and Ghibelline da Romano rivaled over the Marca Trevigiana.

In 1195 the patriarch of Aquileia invested him and his brothers with several castles, and in 1211 they bought further lordships from the bishop of Belluno. Regarded as ancestor of the family's upper branch, he was long believed to have divided the lands with his brother Biaquino in 1233, though modern historians call that division fictitious.

Guecellone VI da Camino (1243–1272), son of Tolberto II, was an Italian nobleman of the da Camino family. The commune of Treviso, urged on by Ezzelino III da Romano, disputed his possession of the family fortress as it sought influence along the Piave.

Little inclined to war, Guecellone negotiated a settlement: he kept the castle, while its keep became a Trevisan garrison. He died at Treviso in 1272. In 1285 his widow Beatrice Bonaparte recovered confiscated fiefs and redeemed the county of Castelnuovo for their son Tolberto.

Guecellone VII da Camino (died August 1324), son of Gherardo III and Chiara della Torre, was the last da Camino lord of Treviso. Destined for the Church, he took power when his brother Rizzardo IV was assassinated in April 1312. He restored Guelph policy and reinstated his father's abolished communal institutions.

He allied with Padua against Cangrande della Scala, then defected to him. On 14–15 December 1312 the Trevisans revolted and sacked his palace; Guecellone escaped over the walls to Serravalle. His attempts to recover Treviso failed, and he died at Serravalle in 1324.

en:
Rizzardo IV da Camino (1274–1312) was an Italian condottiero and lord of Treviso. Knighted in 1295 by Azzo VIII d'Este, he succeeded his father Gherardo III in 1306. He long led the family's expansion into Friuli: in 1309 he escorted the patriarch of Aquileia home and extorted the title of captain general, only to be driven out by a citizen uprising.

In 1311 he joined the Ghibellines and became imperial vicar under Henry VII, alienating Venice. In April 1312 he was stabbed at chess in his palace and died a week later.

en:
Tolberto II da Camino (1218–1256), son of Biaquino II, belonged to the lower branch of the da Camino lords of Treviso. His father died in the Holy Land on the Fifth Crusade; left fatherless in infancy, he and his elder brother Guecellone were raised by their uncle Tolberto and forced from the city after the rise of Ezzelino III da Romano.

While his brother sided with Alberico da Romano, Tolberto joined Ezzelino and married his kinswoman Agnese de' Guidotti. He later defrauded the nephews under his guardianship, though his descendants carried on the line.

Niall kept disputing the lordship until his brother Maghnus killed him in 1348, securing Aonghus's rule. On his death in 1352, his uncle Feidhlimidh and brother Seán fought over the succession.

en:
Pace da Vedano, also called Pasquale, was a Dominican friar who served as bishop of Trieste from 18 May 1330 until his death on 12 August 1341. On 17 May 1332 he performed the first documented consecration of Trieste's basilica of San Silvestro.

His see's Istrian holdings were a standing source of trouble. One of them, Sipar castle, had been occupied by the Bratti family, who sought Capodistria's protection.

In 1333 Pace enfeoffed it to Andrea Dandolo. Dandolo handed it back to the Bratti, reigniting the dispute, which ended only when Pope Innocent VI ordered the castle restored to the Trieste church.

该教区在伊斯特拉的领地一向纠纷不断。其中的西帕尔城堡被布拉蒂家族占据，这个家族还寻求卡波迪斯特里亚的庇护。

1333年，帕切把城堡封授给安德烈亚·丹多洛。丹多洛却把城堡交还布拉蒂家族，争端再起，直到教皇英诺森六世下令把城堡归还的里雅斯特教会才告结束。

该教区在伊斯特拉的领地一向纠纷不断。其中的西帕尔城堡被布拉蒂家族占据，这个家族还寻求卡波迪斯特里亚的庇护。

1333年，帕切把城堡封授给安德烈亚·丹多洛。丹多洛却把城堡交还布拉蒂家族，争端再起，直到教皇#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('pap_innocenzo_vi').GetID],X #L 英诺森六世#!#!下令把城堡归还的里雅斯特教会才告结束。

en:
Quinatzin, also called Quinatzin Tlaltecatzin (traditional dates 1252–1331), is named in the native annals preserved by Alva Ixtlilxochitl and the Codex Xolotl as the first tlatoani of the Acolhua city of Texcoco, and the fourth holder of the Chichimec title Chichimecateuctli, 'lord of the Chichimecs'.

His forebears had ruled from Tenayuca; once elected, Quinatzin moved the seat to Texcoco, leaving Tenayuca a place of secondary importance and making Texcoco the centre of Acolhua power. By his wife Cuauhcihuatzin, a noblewoman of Huexotla, he fathered his successor Techotlalatzin and was grandfather of Ixtlilxochitl I.

基纳特辛（全名基纳特辛·特拉尔特卡钦，传世生卒1252—1331）据阿尔瓦·伊斯特利尔索奇特尔所录本地编年史与《索洛特尔法典》记载，是阿科尔瓦城邦特斯科科的第一位特拉托阿尼，也是第四位拥有奇奇梅卡首领称号奇奇梅卡特库特利（“奇奇梅卡人之主”）的统治者。

先辈都在特纳尤卡执政；他当选后把都城迁往特斯科科，让特纳尤卡退居次要，使特斯科科成为阿科尔瓦人的权力中心。他的妻子是韦克索特兰贵族妇女夸乌齐瓦钦，生子继承人特乔特拉拉特辛，孙子即伊斯特利尔索奇特尔一世。

en:
Techotlalatzin (c. 1323–1409) was tlatoani of the Acolhua city-state of Texcoco from 1357 or 1377 until his death, succeeding his father Quinatzin. The native annals gathered by Torquemada and Alva Ixtlilxochitl present him as the first Acolhua ruler to embrace the culture of the Valley of Mexico, adopting Nahuatl at his court.

He built a small Acolhua domain on the eastern shore of Lake Texcoco, though within the orbit of Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco, the Tepanec ruler whose city dominated the Valley. His son Ixtlilxochitl I inherited the throne and the quarrel: Tezozomoc defeated and killed him in 1419 and seized Texcoco.

特乔特拉拉特辛（约1323—1409）是阿科尔瓦城邦特斯科科的特拉托阿尼，1357年或1377年继承父亲基纳特辛之位，统治直至1409年去世。托尔克马达与阿尔瓦·伊斯特利尔索奇特尔等人辑录的本地编年史把他记作首位接纳墨西哥谷地文化的阿科尔瓦统治者，他在宫廷中采用纳瓦特尔语。

他在特斯科科湖东岸建起一块不大的阿科尔瓦领地，但始终处在阿斯卡波察尔科的特帕内克首领特索索莫克的势力笼罩之下，后者的城邦称雄谷地。他的儿子伊斯特利尔索奇特尔一世继承了王位，也继承了这场争端：1419年，特索索莫克击败并杀死了他，夺取特斯科科。

en:
Godfrey II (died 1369) was Count Palatine of Tübingen, son of William II and Heilika of Eberstein. Deep in debt and at odds with Count Ulrich of Württemberg, he was forced by Emperor Louis IV to sell Tübingen to Ulrich for twenty thousand gold hellers on 5 December 1342.

In 1357 he sold Böblingen and his remaining estates to Ulrich's sons. Through his wife Clara of Freiburg he inherited the lordship of Lichteneck and founded the Tübingen-Lichteneck line of counts.

戈特弗里德二世（1369年去世）是蒂宾根行宫伯爵，威廉二世与艾伯施泰因的海莉卡之子。他负债累累，又与符腾堡伯爵乌尔里希交恶，在皇帝路德维希四世的责令下，于1342年12月5日以两万金赫勒把蒂宾根卖给乌尔里希。

1357年，他又将伯布林根及其余地产卖给乌尔里希的儿子们。他凭借妻子弗赖堡的克拉拉继承了利希特内克领地，开创了蒂宾根-利希特内克伯爵支系。

en:
Tugh Temür (1304–1332), Jayaatu Khan or Emperor Wenzong of Yuan, was the second son of Külüg Khan. Banished to Hainan in 1320, he later became Prince of Huai. After Yesün Temür's death El Temür enthroned him at Dadu in October 1328, and he won the War of the Two Capitals.

In February 1329 he abdicated for his elder brother Kusala, regaining the throne that September after Kusala's suspicious death. A poet and calligrapher, he founded the Kuizhangge Academy while El Temür held real power. He died in 1332.

图帖睦尔（1304—1332），号札牙笃汗，庙号文宗，曲律汗次子。1320年他被流放海南岛，后来受封怀王。1328年泰定帝死后，燕帖木儿在大都拥立他为帝，他在两都之战中获胜。

1329年2月他让位于长兄和世㻋，同年9月和世㻋暴死后重新登基。他擅长诗文书法，开设奎章阁学士院，但实权掌握在燕帖木儿手中。他于1332年去世。

en:
Tumbinai, called Tumbinai Setsen, was khan of the Borjigin Mongols at the turn of the twelfth century. He was the son of Baishinkhur Dogshin. Faced with the strength of the Khitan-led Liao dynasty of northern China, he acknowledged its overlordship and paid tribute to the Liao emperor.

On his death around 1130 his son Khabul succeeded him, united the tribes into the Khamag Mongol confederation and became its first khan. Another son, Khaduli, was the ancestor, through the Barlas line, of Timur.

敦必乃（又称敦必乃薛禅）是12世纪之交的蒙古孛儿只斤氏可汗，拜姓忽儿之子。面对中国北方契丹人所建辽朝的威势，他向辽帝称臣纳贡。

en:
Abu Hafs Umar II was a son of the Hafsid caliph Abu Yahya Abu Bakr II. In 1342 the old caliph had named another son, Ahmad, as his heir and secured the backing of his son-in-law, the Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan. When the caliph died in October 1346, Umar had himself proclaimed caliph first.

Ahmad marched from the south and took the city, but Umar killed him, and his other brothers too. In spring 1347 Abu al-Hasan invaded Ifriqiya and met almost no resistance.

Accounts of Umar's end differ: one says he fled Tunis, was captured near Gabès and executed in August 1347, while others place his death in 1349.

阿布·哈夫斯·欧麦尔二世是哈夫斯王朝哈里发阿布·叶海亚·阿布·伯克尔二世之子。1342年，老哈里发指定另一个儿子艾哈迈德为继承人，并取得女婿、马林王朝苏丹阿布·哈桑的支持。1346年10月哈里发去世时，欧麦尔抢先自立为哈里发。

艾哈迈德从南方进军，夺取了突尼斯城，却被欧麦尔杀死，其他兄弟也未能幸免。1347年春，阿布·哈桑入侵伊夫里奇亚，几乎未遇抵抗。

关于欧麦尔之死，记载并不一致：一种说法称他逃出突尼斯，在加贝斯附近被俘，于1347年8月处决，另一些记载则称他死于1349年。
