en:
Abu Ishaq Ibrahim II (1336–1369), a son of Abu Yahya Abu Bakr II, was Hafsid caliph of Tunis from 1350 to 1369. In 1350 the chamberlain Ibn Tafragin overthrew Ibrahim's brother al-Fadl and placed the thirteen-year-old prince on the throne, holding real power for fourteen years.

Rival Hafsid branches controlled Constantine and Béjaïa. The Marinid sultan Abu Inan Faris seized Tunis in 1357 and Ibrahim fled, until Arab revolts drove the Moroccans out and he returned. Only Ibn Tafragin's death in 1364 let him rule for himself.

He died in 1369, aged thirty-two. His son Khalid II, a boy of ten or twelve, inherited the throne, and in 1370 the Hafsid ruler of Constantine occupied Tunis.

阿布·易司哈格·易卜拉欣二世（1336—1369）是阿布·叶海亚·阿布·伯克尔二世之子，1350—1369年担任突尼斯的哈夫斯王朝哈里发。1350年，宫廷总管伊本·塔夫拉金推翻他的兄弟法德勒，将年仅十三岁的他扶上王位，此后十四年独掌实权。

哈夫斯家族的敌对支系分别控制君士坦丁和贝贾亚。马林王朝苏丹阿布·伊南·法里斯于1357年攻占突尼斯，易卜拉欣出逃，直到阿拉伯部落起义把马林人赶走后才返回。直到1364年塔夫拉金去世他才得以亲政。

他于1369年去世，终年三十二岁。继位的儿子哈立德二世只有十岁或十二岁，1370年君士坦丁的哈夫斯统治者占领了突尼斯。

en:
Abu al-Abbas Ahmad I al-Fadl was a son of the Hafsid caliph Abu Yahya Abu Bakr II, who appointed him governor of Bona. He came to power after the dynasty had lost Tunis.

In 1347 the Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan invaded Ifriqiya, ending the brief reign of Ahmad's brother Umar II. An Arab tribal revolt defeated the Marinid army in 1348, and further rebellions forced Abu al-Hasan to withdraw westward.

In December 1349 Hafsid nobles led by the sheikh Ibn Tafragin proclaimed Ahmad caliph, restoring Hafsid rule in Tunis. It lasted only months: Ibn Tafragin deposed him in 1350 in favour of his younger brother Abu Ishaq Ibrahim II, and Ahmad died the same year.

阿布·阿拔斯·艾哈迈德一世·法德勒是哈夫斯王朝哈里发阿布·叶海亚·阿布·伯克尔二世之子，父亲在世时他担任博纳总督。他是在王朝丢掉突尼斯之后上台的。

1347年，马林王朝苏丹阿布·哈桑入侵伊夫里奇亚，终结了艾哈迈德之兄欧麦尔二世数月的统治。1348年阿拉伯部落起义击败马林军队，各地叛乱接连而起，迫使阿布·哈桑向西撤退。

1349年12月，谢赫伊本·塔夫拉金率领哈夫斯贵族拥立艾哈迈德为哈里发，在突尼斯恢复哈夫斯王朝的统治。这只维持了数月：1350年塔夫拉金将他废黜，改立其弟阿布·易司哈格·易卜拉欣二世，艾哈迈德于同年死去。

en:
Abu-l-Baqa Khalid an-Nasr (1283–1311) was a Hafsid prince who ruled Béjaïa after his father Abu Zakariyya Yahya III. In 1307 the scholar Ramon Llull was imprisoned by the qadi before Abu-l-Baqa released and expelled him.

He agreed with Abu Asida Muhammad II of Tunis that the survivor would inherit the other's realm. When Abu Asida died in 1309, however, the sheikhs raised Abu Yahya Abu Bakr ash-Shahid instead. Abu-l-Baqa crushed his rival in seventeen days and seized Tunis.

Revolts followed in Constantine, led by his cousin and then his brother. His harsh rule cost him the support of the notables, and in 1311 he surrendered to his brother and was assassinated.

阿布·巴卡·哈立德·纳绥尔（1283—1311）是哈夫斯王朝王公，继其父阿布·扎卡里亚·叶海亚三世成为贝贾亚统治者。1307年，学者拉蒙·柳利被卡迪囚禁，随后阿布·巴卡将他释放并驱逐出境。

他与突尼斯的阿布·阿西达·穆罕默德二世约定，两人中后死者继承对方的领地。但1309年阿布·阿西达死后，城内谢赫却另立阿布·叶海亚·阿布·伯克尔·沙希德。阿布·巴卡用十七天击溃对手、攻占突尼斯。

君士坦丁随即爆发叛乱，先由他的堂亲、后由其兄弟领导。他统治严苛，失去显贵的支持；1311年他向兄弟投降，仍遭刺杀。

en:
Ibn Tafragin (died 1364) was an Almohad sheikh and chamberlain who dominated the Hafsid state in the mid-fourteenth century. Around 1330 he reached high office under Caliph Abu Yahya Abu Bakr II, and as chief chamberlain from 1343 he pushed for closer ties with the Marinids of Fez.

A succession struggle in 1346 cost him his office, but he backed the Marinid invasion of 1347. Abu al-Hasan's mistakes in governing forced the Marinids out in 1349, and power passed to the Almohad sheikhs, of whom Ibn Tafragin was the most influential.

In December 1349 he raised Abu al-Abbas Ahmad al-Fadl to the caliphate, fell out with him and deposed him the next year. He installed the child Abu Ishaq Ibrahim II and ruled in his name until his death in 1364.

伊本·塔夫拉金（？—1364）是穆瓦希德派谢赫、宫廷总管，在14世纪中叶掌控哈夫斯朝政。约1330年，他在哈里发阿布·叶海亚·阿布·伯克尔二世治下升任要职，1343年起任首席宫廷总管，力主与非斯的马林王朝加强关系。

1346年的继位之争使塔夫拉金丢了官职，但他仍支持1347年马林人的入侵。1349年阿布·哈桑因治理失当被迫撤出，权力落入穆瓦希德谢赫们手中，塔夫拉金是其中最有势力的一个。

1349年12月，他拥立阿布·阿拔斯·艾哈迈德·法德勒为哈里发，却与其不和，次年将其废黜。他改立年幼的阿布·易司哈格·易卜拉欣二世，以其名义执政，直至1364年去世。

en:
Abu Yahya Abu Bakr II (died 19 October 1346) was the Hafsid caliph of Ifriqiya from 1318, son of Abu Zakariyya Yahya III of Béjaïa. He seized Béjaïa in 1312 and entered Tunis in 1318 after the fall of al-Lihyani.

He put down revolts until 1332 and ended Zayyanid raids from Tlemcen by allying with the Marinids of Fez, whose heir married his daughter. In 1335 he retook Djerba and built corsair fleets. His son Abu Hafs Umar succeeded him.

en:
Abu Zakariya Yahya III (c. 1260–1301) was the Hafsid emir who made Béjaïa independent of Tunis. A son of the caliph Abu Ishaq Ibrahim I, he fled to Tlemcen after his family's overthrow in 1283 but established himself at Béjaïa soon after. In 1285 he revolted with Arab tribal support and seized the western Hafsid lands including Constantine.

In 1286 he attacked Tunis itself; repulsed, he fled south. In 1300 he repulsed a Marinid siege of Béjaïa. He died in 1301 and was succeeded by his son Abu-l-Baqa Khalid.

Early in 1350 Hafsid notables proclaimed him caliph at Béjaïa. His reign lasted only months: in July the chamberlain Ibn Tafragin raised Ibrahim II in his place and put him to death, then governed in the young Ibrahim's name.

en:
Muhammad Abu al-Dhahab (c. 1735–1775), whose name means father of gold, was a Circassian-born mamluk emir and chief general of Ali Bey al-Kabir, strongman of Ottoman Egypt. In 1769 he crushed a revolt in Upper Egypt, in 1770 seized the Hejaz, and with Zahir al-Umar conquered much of Syria and took Damascus.

He then turned against Ali Bey, overthrew him in 1773, and ruled Egypt as regent. In 1775 he campaigned again in Palestine but died suddenly of the plague, leaving power to his mamluks Murad Bey and Ibrahim Bey.

穆罕默德·阿布·扎哈卜（约1735—1775），名字意为“黄金之父”，是出身切尔克斯的马木留克埃米尔，后成为奥斯曼埃及强人阿里贝伊麾下的首席将领。1769年他镇压上埃及的叛乱，1770年攻取汉志，又与扎希尔·欧麦尔联手，征服叙利亚大部并拿下大马士革。

随后他回师反对阿里贝伊，于1773年将其推翻，以摄政身份统治埃及。1775年他再度出征巴勒斯坦，却猝死于鼠疫，权力由他的马木留克穆拉德贝伊和易卜拉欣贝伊继承。

en:
Aşıkpaşazade (c. 1400–after 1484), born Dervish Ahmed near Amasya, pen name Aşıkî, was an early Ottoman historian and a dervish of the Vefai order. The great-grandson of the poet Aşık Pasha, he grew up in a Sufi lodge, made the hajj in 1437 and spent time in Egypt. He campaigned with the Ottoman army in the Balkans, fighting at Kosovo in 1448 and at the conquest of Constantinople.

Late in life he wrote the Tevarih-i Al-i Osman, a vernacular chronicle of the Ottoman dynasty drawing heavily on his own experience; he was still writing in 1484.

阿什克帕夏扎德（约1400—1484年后），本名德尔维什·艾哈迈德，笔名阿什基，生于阿马西亚附近，是奥斯曼早期历史学家、韦法伊教团的苦行僧。他是诗人阿什克帕夏的曾孙，自幼在道堂长大，1437年赴麦加朝觐，并在埃及停留。此后他随军征战巴尔干，参加了1448年的科索沃之战和君士坦丁堡攻城战。

晚年他撰写《奥斯曼家族编年史》，以亲身经历为基础，用通俗土耳其语记述奥斯曼王朝，1484年仍在写作。

en:
Ahmed Karamanli (1686–1745) was an Ottoman cavalry officer of Janissary origin who founded the Karamanli dynasty of Tripolitania. As Ottoman control weakened, he murdered the Ottoman governor in the 1711 coup and seized power.

He persuaded the Porte to confirm him as pasha and make the governorship hereditary, and Tripoli thereafter acted as an effectively independent kingdom, paying only nominal tribute. He enriched it through corsair raids on Mediterranean shipping and tribute from states seeking protection, and extended his rule over Fezzan and Cyrenaica before his death in 1745.

艾哈迈德·卡拉曼利（1686—1745）是奥斯曼骑兵军官，出身耶尼切里，建立了的黎波里塔尼亚的卡拉曼利王朝。随着奥斯曼控制力减弱，他在1711年的政变中杀死奥斯曼总督、夺取政权。

他随后说服高门承认他为帕夏，并将总督之位改为家族世袭；此后的黎波里仅在名义上纳贡，实际已是独立王国。他靠地中海海盗劫掠和求保护国家的贡金充实财源，在1745年去世前把统治扩展到费赞和昔兰尼加。

en:
Nedîm (c. 1681–1730), pen name of Ahmed Efendi, was the most celebrated Ottoman lyric poet of the Tulip Period, favored at Ahmed III's court. Rejecting the didactic style of the Nabi school, he wrote fresh, vernacular, often playful love lyrics and brought folk song forms into Divan poetry, founding the manner called Nedîmâne.

He taught at madrasas, served as chief librarian and the sultan's boon companion, and died in 1730; accounts differ, but one says he fell from his roof while fleeing the Patrona Halil rebellion.

奈迪姆（约1681—1730），本名艾哈迈德埃芬迪，是郁金香时期最负盛名的奥斯曼抒情诗人，受知于艾哈迈德三世的宫廷。他反对纳比一派说教式的诗风，以清新、口语化、时而戏谑的爱情诗闻名，并把民间歌谣体裁引入迪万诗歌，开创了“奈迪姆风格”。

他曾在经学院执教，担任首席图书馆长和苏丹的清客，于1730年去世，死因众说纷纭；一种说法称他在躲避帕特罗纳·哈利尔叛乱时从自家屋顶坠亡。

en:
Alaeddin Pasha (c. 1281–1331) was a son of Osman I, founder of the Ottoman beylik, and a half-brother of Orhan. Orhan, the better warrior, took the leadership, and while later Ottoman princes would fight over succession, Alaeddin submitted without dispute; the brothers stayed on good terms for life.

Orhan trusted him as an adviser trained in state affairs. In 1328 or 1329 he proposed three reforms: silver coinage in the sultan's name, an official dress with a cap of white felt, and an army divided into commanded units with a wartime infantry levy. The infantry scheme failed because the soldiers lacked training.

He lived piously and founded mosques, including the Alaeddin Bey Cami in Bursa, finished in 1335. He died in 1331 and lies in Osman I's tomb there.

阿拉丁帕夏（约1281—1331）是奥斯曼贝伊国创立者奥斯曼一世之子、奥尔汗的异母兄弟。善战的奥尔汗接过了领导权；后来的奥斯曼王子常为继承权相争，阿拉丁却毫无争议地臣服，兄弟终生和睦。

他受过政务训练，是奥尔汗信任的谋臣。1328或1329年，他提出三项改革：以苏丹名义铸造银币、为官员规定配白毡帽的统一官服、将军队改编为由军官统辖的分队并设立战时步兵征召。由于士兵缺乏训练，步兵方案最终失败。

他生活虔诚，修建多座清真寺，包括1335年落成的布尔萨阿拉丁贝伊清真寺。1331年他去世，葬于布尔萨的奥斯曼一世陵中。

en:
Ali Bey al-Kabir (1728–1773), known in Turkish as Bulutkapan, the Cloud-Catcher, was a mamluk of Georgian origin who became shaykh al-balad, the effective strongman of Ottoman Egypt. He held the office in 1760–1766, survived exile, and returned to power in 1767.

In 1769 he openly defied Istanbul, striking coins in his own name, ending the annual tribute, and conquering the Hejaz and Syria in 1770–1771. His revolt collapsed when his trusted general Abu al-Dahab turned against him; he was defeated near Cairo and died in captivity in May 1773.

阿里贝伊（1728—1773），土耳其语绰号“捕云者”，是出身格鲁吉亚的马木留克，最终以“城市长老”之位成为奥斯曼埃及的实际强人。他于1760—1766年担任此职，遭流放后又在1767年重新掌权。

en:
Asporça Hatun (died after 1362) was a Byzantine Greek noblewoman and first legal wife of Sultan Orhan. She married Orhan around 1310 and bore two sons, including Ibrahim Bey, and two daughters. Osman I esteemed her and granted her village revenues.

In September 1323 she founded a waqf endowing her lands to descendants, the oldest surviving Ottoman document. Her son Ibrahim was executed by Murad I in 1362, and she was buried in Orhan's Bursa tomb.

阿斯波尔恰可敦（1362年后去世）是拜占庭希腊贵族女子，也是苏丹奥尔汗的第一位正妻。她约在1310年嫁给奥尔汗，生下易卜拉欣贝伊等两个儿子和两个女儿。奥斯曼一世很看重她，把村庄的收入赐给她。

1323年9月她设立瓦克夫，把自己土地的收入留给后代，这是现存最早的奥斯曼文书。1362年她的儿子易卜拉欣被穆拉德一世处死，她本人死后葬于布尔萨的奥尔汗陵墓。

en:
Cinci Hoca, meaning the hoca of jinn, was the epithet of Karabaşzade Hüseyin Efendi, an Ottoman witch doctor born in Safranbolu. Kösem Sultan brought him to the palace to treat the mentally troubled Sultan Ibrahim, and the sultan's favor raised him high: in 1643 he became kadi of Galata and in 1644 kazasker of Anatolia, enraging the ulama.

After Ibrahim was deposed in 1648, Grand Vizier Sofu Mehmed Pasha seized his fortune and exiled him toward Damascus; when he railed against the vizier on the road, he was arrested and executed at Mihalcık.

金吉·霍贾（意为“精灵的霍贾”）是卡拉巴什扎德·侯赛因埃芬迪的绰号，他是出生于萨夫兰博卢的奥斯曼巫医。柯塞姆苏丹把他召入宫中，为精神失常的易卜拉欣苏丹治病；凭借苏丹宠信，他于1643年出任加拉塔卡迪，1644年升任安纳托利亚军政法官，激起乌理玛阶层强烈不满。

1648年易卜拉欣被废后，大维齐尔索菲·穆罕默德帕夏抄没其家产，将他流放大马士革；途中他抨击大维齐尔，随即在米哈尔哲克被捕处死。

en:
Çoban Bey (1283–1337) was an Ottoman prince, a son of Osman I, founder of the Ottoman state. He fought in the long campaign that ended with the conquest of Bursa in 1326.

He built a mosque in the captured city. His tomb lies in Bursa's Umurbey quarter, named after him, where the ruins of a madrasa endowed in his name also survive.

乔班·贝伊（1283—1337）是奥斯曼王子，奥斯曼国家开国者奥斯曼一世之子。他参加了1326年攻克布尔萨的长期战事。

en:
Enderûnlu Fâzıl (c. 1757–1810) was a poet born Hüseyin in Acre or Safed, a grandson of the Palestinian strongman Ẓāhir al-ʿUmar. After his family's revolt collapsed in 1776, he was schooled in Constantinople's Enderun academy, from which he was expelled in 1783, possibly over love affairs.

Years of poverty ended when Sultan Selim III made him a bey and waqf administrator. His satirical verse brought exile to Rhodes in 1799, where he went blind; allowed back, he wrote poetry for the imperial elite.

He is remembered for two erotic poetry books, Hubanname and Zenanname, the latter banned in the empire. He died in 1810 and was buried in Eyüp.

恩德伦卢·法齐勒（约1757—1810）是诗人，原名侯赛因，生于阿卡或萨法德，是巴勒斯坦强人扎希尔·欧麦尔的孙子。1776年家族叛乱失败后，他被带往君士坦丁堡，在恩德伦宫廷学校受训，1783年被逐，可能与风流韵事有关。

数度贫困之后，塞利姆三世封他为贝伊、任命为瓦合甫管理人。讽刺诗作使他于1799年被流放罗得岛，并在那里失明；获准返回后，他为帝国精英写诗。

他以色情诗集《美少年书》和《女子书》闻名，后者在帝国境内遭禁。1810年他去世，葬于埃于普。

en:
Ertuğrul Gazi (died c. 1280) was a Turkish marcher lord on the Byzantine frontier and father of Osman I, founder of the Ottoman dynasty. Little about his life is certain. An undated coin of Osman names him as Osman's father; the chronicles of his life were written a century or more later.

The chronicles differ over his father, but the official version names Suleyman Shah of the Kayı tribe. In that tradition the Kayı fled the Mongols westward, and after Suleyman Shah drowned in the Euphrates the tribe split; Ertuğrul went west with his followers. He served the Seljuk sultan Kayqubad I of Rum, receiving Karaca Dağ and later conquering Söğüt.

Besides Osman, tradition gives him two other sons. He died at Söğüt around 1280, and the town became the first Ottoman capital under Osman. Like his son, he was remembered as a ghazi, a warrior of the faith.

埃尔图鲁尔加齐（?—约1280）是拜占庭边境上的突厥边疆领主，也是奥斯曼王朝创立者奥斯曼一世之父。他的生平少有确凿之处。奥斯曼时期一枚无年份钱币称奥斯曼为埃尔图鲁尔之子，而他生平的编年史都写于一个多世纪之后。

诸书对他的父亲说法不一，正统说法作卡耶部的苏莱曼沙赫。依这一传说，卡耶人为躲避蒙古人西迁，苏莱曼沙赫渡幼发拉底河时溺亡，部落随之分裂，埃尔图鲁尔带着族人西行。他投效鲁姆塞尔柱苏丹凯库巴德一世，获赐卡拉贾达格，后来又攻取瑟于特村。

除奥斯曼外，传说他还有两个儿子。约1280年他卒于瑟于特，这座城镇在奥斯曼治下成为奥斯曼人最初的都城。他和儿子一样被尊为加齐，即为信仰而战的勇士。

en:
Esmâ Ibret Hanim (1780 – c. 1830) was an Ottoman calligrapher and poet, born in Istanbul, the daughter of palace official Ahmed Ağa. Her father showed her early writing to friends, astonished that his daughter had produced it.

From the age of ten she trained at the Sheikh Murad Dervish Lodge, mastering the sülüs-nesih script in the tradition of Hâfiz Osman, and received the title İbret at sixteen. Her master Mahmud Celaleddin Efendi, at first unwilling to teach a woman, accepted her after seeing her work and married her. A hilye she presented to Sultan Selim III and his mother earned her a grant of 500 kuruş.

埃斯玛·伊布雷特·哈内姆（1780—约1830）是奥斯曼女书法家、诗人，生于伊斯坦布尔，是宫廷官员艾哈迈德阿加之女。父亲曾将她早年的字迹展示给友人，众人惊讶于这些字出自其女之手。

她十岁起在谢赫·穆拉德德尔维希道堂习字，宗法哈菲兹·奥斯曼的苏鲁斯—纳西赫字体，十六岁获“伊布雷特”称号。她的老师马哈茂德·贾拉莱丁·埃芬迪起初不愿收女弟子，见到她的作品后改变主意，后来与她成婚。她进献给塞利姆三世及其母亲的一幅希利耶为她赢得500库鲁什的赏金。

en:
Fitnat Hanım (died 1780) was the pen name of Zübeyde, regarded as the foremost woman poet of the Ottoman Divan school. Born in Istanbul into a family of religious scholars, she was the daughter of Ebu İshakzade Mehmet Esad Efendi, şeyhülislam under Mahmud I.

Her marriage to Derviş Mehmet Efendi, a kazasker of Rumeli, proved unhappy and stifled her writing. Admired in the capital's literary circles, she exchanged poems with Grand Vizier Koca Ragıp Pasha; some of her poems were translated into Western languages in the nineteenth century, when she was called the queen of poets.

菲特娜特·哈内姆（？—1780）是女诗人祖贝达的笔名，被视为奥斯曼迪万诗派最重要的女诗人。她生于伊斯坦布尔的宗教学者世家，父亲是马哈茂德一世时期的谢赫伊斯兰埃布·伊沙克扎德·穆罕默德·埃萨德埃芬迪。

François Baron de Tott (1733–1793) was a French officer of Hungarian descent who became a key Ottoman military reformer. He went to Constantinople in 1755 as secretary to the French ambassador, learning Turkish and gathering information on the Crimean Khanate, and served as consul in Crimea from 1767.

During the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774 the Porte tasked him with defending the Dardanelles. He built a howitzer foundry and artillery units, fortified the Bosphorus, and began the naval science course that grew into the Ottoman naval school. 弗朗索瓦·德·托特男爵（1733—1793）是匈牙利裔法国军官，曾受奥斯曼政府聘请改革军队。他1755年担任法国大使秘书前往君士坦丁堡，学习土耳其语并搜集克里米亚汗国的情报，1767年起任驻克里米亚领事。

1768—1774年俄土战争期间，奥斯曼政府委托他防守达达尼尔海峡。他修建榴弹炮铸造厂、组建炮兵部队，加固博斯普鲁斯海峡防务，并开设海军科学课程，为后来的奥斯曼海军学校奠定基础。法国大革命后他回到匈牙利，于1793年在那里去世。

en:
Hâfiz Osman (1642–1698), born in Istanbul, was one of the most celebrated Ottoman calligraphers. Trained in the tradition of Şeyh Hamdullah, he belonged to the Sünbüliye dervish order.

He revitalised Ottoman calligraphic scripts and created the classical layout for the hilye, a calligraphic depiction of the Prophet based on the hadith, which became the empire-wide standard. He taught penmanship to the future sultans Mustafa II and Ahmed III. His Qur'ans and hilyes survive in the Topkapı Palace collections, and he died in Istanbul on 3 December 1698.

哈菲兹·奥斯曼（1642—1698），生于伊斯坦布尔，是奥斯曼帝国最负盛名的书法家之一。他上承谢赫·哈姆杜拉的传统，属于苏恩布利耶托钵僧教团。

他革新了奥斯曼书法字体，还为“希利耶”——依据圣训以书法表现先知穆罕默德的图样——确立了经典版式，成为通行全帝国的标准。他曾教授后来成为苏丹的穆斯塔法二世与艾哈迈德三世书法。他抄写的《古兰经》和希利耶作品现藏于托普卡帕宫，他本人于1698年12月3日在伊斯坦布尔去世。

en:
Halil Bey (c. 1347–1362) was an Ottoman prince, the only son of Sultan Orhan by his Byzantine wife Theodora Kantakouzene. In 1357 pirates seized him near İzmit and carried him to Phocaea, where he was held for a ransom of a hundred thousand hyperpyra.

Orhan paid the ransom in 1358 and promised to end his raids on Byzantine lands. In 1359 Halil married his cousin Irene, daughter of Emperor John V Palaiologos. After Orhan's death, his half-brother Murad I had him executed in 1362.

哈利勒贝伊（约1347—1362）是奥斯曼王子，为奥尔汗贝伊与拜占庭公主狄奥多拉·坎塔库泽努斯唯一的儿子。1357年，海盗在伊兹密特附近将他掳走，押到福西亚扣押，索要10万枚海佩伦金币赎金。

1358年，奥尔罕付清赎金，并承诺停止袭掠拜占庭领土。1359年，哈利勒迎娶表亲——皇帝约翰五世·巴列奥略之女伊琳娜。奥尔罕死后，他于1362年被异母兄穆拉德一世处死。

en:
Ḥassan Pasha (1657–1723) was a Georgian-origin Ottoman commander who founded the Mamluk dynasty of Iraq. A veteran of the wars against Iran, he was appointed vali of Baghdad in 1704 with a mandate to restore order. He subdued the unruly Arab and Kurdish tribes, curbed the Janissaries by raising Georgian and Circassian Mamluk troops, and remitted regular revenues to Istanbul.

In 1705 he had Karbala's channels cleaned and restored a caravanserai on the road to Najaf, and he also built schools and mosques. After his death in 1723 his son Ahmad Pasha succeeded him, and the Mamluk regime lasted until 1831.

哈桑帕夏（1657—1723）是格鲁吉亚裔奥斯曼将领，伊拉克马穆鲁克政权的建立者。他曾在对伊朗的战争中长期征战，1704年被任命为巴格达总督，受命恢复秩序。他平定作乱的阿拉伯和库尔德部落，编练格鲁吉亚和切尔克斯马穆鲁克军队以压制耶尼切里，按时向伊斯坦布尔解缴税款。

1705年他下令清理卡尔巴拉的水渠，并修复通往纳杰夫路上的商队驿站，还兴建学校与清真寺。他1723年去世，其子艾哈迈德帕夏继任，开创的马穆鲁克政权一直延续到1831年。

İbrahim Bey (c. 1310–1362) was the eldest son of Sultan Orhan by his Byzantine-born wife Asporça Hatun. In the waqf his mother founded in September 1323, the oldest surviving Ottoman document, he was named administrator of her landed endowments.

He later served as governor of Eskişehir. After Orhan's death in 1362, he and his sons were put to death on the order of his half-brother, the new sultan Murad I, and he was buried in Osman I's tomb in Bursa.

en:
İbrahim Müteferrika (1674–1745) was an Ottoman diplomat, scholar and printer. Born into a Hungarian Unitarian family in Kolozsvár in Transylvania, he converted to Islam and served the Sublime Porte. In 1726 he petitioned Sultan Ahmed III for leave to print non-religious books in Arabic script.

With the court's firman he opened Istanbul's first Muslim-run press using movable Arabic type. Over two decades he issued twenty-three volumes, including a Turkish-Arabic dictionary, an atlas and works of history and science. He died in 1745.

易卜拉欣·穆特费里卡（1674—1745）是奥斯曼帝国的外交官、学者与印刷家。他出生于特兰西瓦尼亚科洛兹堡的一个匈牙利人一位论派家庭，后改宗伊斯兰教，在高门任职。1726年他奏请艾哈迈德三世苏丹准许以阿拉伯字母印制非宗教书籍。

en:
Imadaddin Nasimi (c. 1369–c. 1419) was an Azerbaijani Turkic poet and the foremost voice of Hurufi mysticism. In Tabriz he became a disciple and successor of Fazlallah Astarabadi, founder of the Hurufi movement. After Astarabadi was executed, Nasimi carried the doctrine through Anatolia, rejected at Bursa and by the Sufi Haji Bayram Veli, before settling in Aleppo.

There his divans won him many followers and the hostility of Sunni ulama; around 1418–19 the Mamluk sultan al-Mu'ayyad Shaykh had him executed as a heretic. His poetry conveyed Hurufi teachings, in which the divine was revealed in the human face.

伊马达丁·纳西米（约1369—约1419）是阿塞拜疆突厥裔诗人，胡鲁菲神秘主义最重要的代言人。他在大不里士成为胡鲁菲运动创始人法兹拉拉·阿斯塔拉巴迪的弟子和继承人。阿斯塔拉巴迪被处死后，纳西米辗转安纳托利亚传播其教义，在布尔萨和苏菲圣徒哈吉·巴伊拉姆·韦利处都遭拒绝，最后落脚阿勒颇。

en:
Kadızade Mehmed Efendi (1582–1635) was an Ottoman Islamic preacher born in Balıkesir and the founder of the Kadızadeli movement. As a young man he tried to join a Sufi brotherhood but rejected its teachings and turned to preaching. In 1631 he was appointed preacher at the Hagia Sophia mosque, where he blamed the empire's disorders on deviation from the Sharia and roused crowds against the Sufi orders.

He backed Murad IV's tobacco ban; when challenged that God had not forbidden tobacco, he argued the ruler's prohibition was sufficient. He died in 1635, leaving a movement that shaped Ottoman religious politics.

卡迪扎德·穆罕默德埃芬迪（1582—1635）是奥斯曼帝国的伊斯兰宣教师，生于巴勒克埃西尔，为卡迪扎德派运动的创始人。他年轻时曾试图加入苏菲教团，却因反对其教义转而从事宣教。1631年他被任命为圣索菲亚清真寺的宣教师，在任上将帝国的乱象归咎于背离沙里亚法，并煽动信众反对苏菲教团。

en:
Kemal Reis (c. 1451–1511), born Ahmed Kemaleddin in Manisa, was an Ottoman privateer and admiral, and uncle of the cartographer Piri Reis. In 1487 Bayezid II sent him to support the Nasrid emir of Granada; he raided Málaga and the Andalusian coast and between 1490 and 1492 ferried fleeing Muslims and Jews to Ottoman lands.

He later commanded fleets against Venice and the Knights of St. John, and in 1507 carried oars and cannon to Egypt for the Mamluk sultan. In early 1511, while escorting a supply convoy to Egypt, he perished with twenty-seven ships in a Mediterranean storm.

凯末尔·雷斯（约1451—1511），本名艾哈迈德·凯末尔丁，生于马尼萨，是奥斯曼帝国的私掠船长与海军将领，也是制图师皮瑞·雷斯的叔父。1487年，巴耶济德二世派他支援格拉纳达的纳斯尔王朝埃米尔，他袭击马拉加和安达卢西亚海岸，并在1490至1492年间把出逃的穆斯林和犹太人运往奥斯曼领土。

此后他率舰队同威尼斯和圣约翰骑士团作战，1507年将船桨和火炮运到埃及交予马穆鲁克苏丹。1511年初，他在护送补给船队前往埃及时，与27艘船一同葬身于地中海风暴。

en:
Kemankeş Kara Mustafa Pasha (1592–1644) was an Ottoman commander and grand vizier. Born to an Albanian family at Vlorë, he rose through the Janissary corps and was famed as an archer; his epithet Kemankeş means bow-puller. He became Agha of the Janissaries in 1635 and Kapudan Pasha, the grand admiral.

He fought at the capture of Baghdad in 1638, and after the grand vizier died during the siege, Murad IV appointed him as his successor. Under Sultan Ibrahim he concentrated power, until a palace faction led by Kösem Sultan secured his dismissal and execution in 1644.

凯曼凯什·卡拉·穆斯塔法帕夏（1592—1644）是奥斯曼帝国的军事统帅与大维齐尔。他出身于发罗拉的阿尔巴尼亚人家庭，在禁卫军中崛起，以箭术闻名，绰号“凯曼凯什”意为拉弓手。他1635年升任禁卫军阿迦，同年出任卡普丹帕夏，即海军大元帅。

他参加了1638年攻取巴格达之役，大维齐尔在围城期间阵亡后，穆拉德四世任命他继任。在易卜拉欣苏丹在位期间他总揽朝政，最终以柯塞姆苏丹为首的宫廷派系促成他被解职，并于1644年被处决。

en:
Koca Mehmet Ragıp Pasha (1698–1763) was an Ottoman statesman, diplomat and poet. His epithet Koca meant great or giant.

After serving as a treasury official in Baghdad he joined the delegation that made the Treaty of Belgrade in 1739, became reis ül-küttab in 1740, and governed Egypt from 1744 to 1748, when local troops forced him to step down.

Appointed grand vizier in 1757, he served Sultans Osman III and Mustafa III for six years, reforming finance and administration and keeping the empire neutral in the Seven Years' War. He married Princess Saliha Sultan, exchanged verses with the poetess Fıtnat Hanım, and died in 1763.

科贾·穆罕默德·拉格普帕夏（1698—1763）是奥斯曼帝国的政治家、外交官与诗人，绰号“科贾”意为伟大或巨人。

他曾在巴格达担任财政官，1739年作为代表团成员参与签订《贝尔格莱德条约》，1740年升任帝国首席文书“雷斯·库塔布”，1744至1748年出任埃及总督，后因当地军队的压力而卸任。

1757年他被任命为大维齐尔，侍奉奥斯曼三世与穆斯塔法三世两任苏丹达六年，整顿财政与行政，并使帝国在七年战争期间保持中立。他娶萨利哈苏丹公主为妻，曾与女诗人菲特娜特·哈内姆唱和，于1763年去世。

Mahmud Celaleddin Efendi (c. 1750–1829) was an Ottoman calligrapher. Born in Dagestan in the Caucasus, he moved to Istanbul as a boy. After a disagreement over style he left his teacher and taught himself by studying the master Hâfiz Osman, developing his own versions of the sülüs and naskh scripts.

He left monumental inscriptions at the Eyüp Sultan imaret and the tomb of Mihrişah Sultan, and Sultan Abdülmecid was his pupil. At first doubting that the young Esmâ Ibret Hanim had written the samples shown to him, he accepted her after investigating and later married her. He died in 1829.

马哈茂德·杰拉勒丁埃芬迪（约1750—1829）是奥斯曼帝国书法家。他生于高加索的达吉斯坦，幼年迁居伊斯坦布尔。他因风格不合中止了从师学业，此后靠研习大师哈菲兹·奥斯曼的作品自学，形成了自己的苏卢斯与纳斯赫字体风格。

他为艾郁普苏丹清真寺的施粥场和米赫丽莎苏丹陵留下了多处纪念性铭文，苏丹阿卜杜勒-迈吉德也曾是他的学生。他起初怀疑呈给他的书法样本并非年轻的埃斯玛·伊卜雷特·哈内姆所写，经查证后收她为徒，后来与她成婚。他于1829年去世。

Malhun Hatun (died after 1326), also called Mal Hatun, was the first wife of Osman I, founder of the Ottoman dynasty, and the mother of his successor, Orhan. Long tradition made her the daughter of Sheikh Edebali, but a 1324 endowment deed issued by Orhan names his mother as Mal Hatun, daughter of an Umar or Ömer Bey.

She lived into the late 1320s and was probably buried in the family mausoleum around Osman's tomb at Bursa, in one of its unidentified sarcophagi.

Sedefkar Mehmed Agha (c. 1540–1617) was an Ottoman architect and the last pupil of the master builder Mimar Sinan. Recruited through the devshirme in 1563, he spent twenty years working mother-of-pearl inlay, which earned him the name Sedefkar, before joining Sinan's architectural office.

In 1606 he was appointed chief imperial architect, and from 1609 to 1616 he built his masterpiece, the Sultan Ahmed Mosque in Istanbul, known as the Blue Mosque. He died there in 1617.

en:
Mehmed Tahir Ağa was an Ottoman architect and chief imperial architect, mimarbaşı, under Mustafa III. At twelve he accompanied his father on campaigns against Russia and Austria, and in 1761 he was first appointed chief architect, heading the palace builders three times between 1761 and 1784 as one of the masters of the Ottoman baroque style.

During Mustafa III's great Istanbul building campaign he led the reconstruction of the Fatih Mosque and planned mosques and fortress repairs across the empire. In 1788, under Abdülhamid I, he supervised bridge works on the Austrian campaign and died the same year.

穆罕默德·塔希尔阿迦是奥斯曼帝国建筑师，穆斯塔法三世时期的首席宫廷建筑师，即米马尔巴舍。他12岁便随父参加对俄国和奥地利的战役，1761年首次出任首席建筑师，此后至1784年间三度担任此职，是奥斯曼巴洛克风格的代表建筑师之一。

在穆斯塔法三世于伊斯坦布尔大兴土木期间，他主持重建法提赫清真寺，并筹划帝国各地的清真寺与要塞修缮。1788年，他在阿卜杜勒-哈米德一世治下督办对奥地利战争中的桥梁工程，同年去世。

en:
Melek Hatun was a daughter of the Ottoman prince Melik Bey, a son of Osman I. Historian Vedat Turgut identified her as the Paşa-Melek Hatun who married Orhan's son Murad, and suggested her father was known as Kızıl Murad.

Orhan gave the villages of Koçi and Adaöyük to Kızıl Murad's son, and they passed to Paşa-Melek. She made them a family waqf and later directed their revenues to the Gazi Murad hospice. Her grandson Murad held the property before it passed out of family control.

梅莱克·哈屯是奥斯曼王子梅利克贝伊之女，其父是奥斯曼一世之子。历史学家韦达特·图尔古特认为她就是嫁给奥尔汗苏丹之子穆拉德的帕夏-梅莱克·哈屯，并推测其父又称克孜勒·穆拉德。

奥尔汗把科奇和阿达厄于克两村赐给克孜勒·穆拉德之子，两村后来转到帕夏-梅莱克名下。她将其立为家族瓦克夫，后来规定收入拨归加齐·穆拉德济贫院。她的孙子穆拉德曾掌管这份产业，后来产业脱离家族控制。

en:
Mihrî Hatun (1456/1460–c. 1506), born Mihrünnisa in Amasya, was one of the earliest Turkish women poets whose name survives. Her father was a qadi who wrote verse; she spent most of her life near Amasya and joined the literary circle of Şehzade Ahmed, son of Bayezid II.

She was reputed to have fallen in love several times, though her loves were said to have been chaste, and she never married. Her witty, polished qasidas and ghazals of love and gallantry won renown in her lifetime, and later readers called her the Sappho of the Ottomans.

米赫里·哈屯（1456/1460—约1506），本名米赫伦尼萨，生于阿马西亚，是名字流传至今的最早一批土耳其女诗人之一。她的父亲是一名会写诗的卡迪；她一生大部分时间住在阿马西亚或附近，加入了巴耶济德二世之子艾哈迈德王子的文学圈子。

相传她曾多次坠入爱河，但这些感情都纯洁无果，她终身未嫁。她所作的颂诗和加泽尔情诗机智而精巧，在世时即享有盛名，后世读者称她为奥斯曼人的萨福。

en:
Mimar Sinan (c. 1488/1490–1588), son of a stonemason born at Ağırnas near Kayseri, was the greatest architect of classical Ottoman architecture and chief royal architect to three sultans, from Suleiman the Magnificent to Murad III. Conscripted in 1512, he trained as a Janissary officer and military engineer, building fortifications, roads, bridges and aqueducts; in 1535 he built ships for the army to cross Lake Van.

After Lütfi Pasha made him Architect of the Abode of Felicity in 1539, commissions followed, including the Şehzade Mosque in the 1540s. Around fifty he became chief royal architect, a post he held for nearly fifty years. Over three hundred major buildings are credited to him, including the Süleymaniye Mosque.

Aged over eighty, he completed the Selimiye Mosque at Edirne, which he called his masterpiece. He died in 1588; his pupil Davud Agha succeeded him. He is often compared with his contemporary Michelangelo.

米马尔·希南（约1488/1490—1588）是石匠之子，生于开塞利附近的阿伊尔纳斯，是奥斯曼古典建筑最伟大的建筑师，曾任苏莱曼大帝至穆拉德三世三朝的皇家首席建筑师。1512年他被征召，接受耶尼切里军官和军事工程师训练，修筑工事、道路、桥梁和渡槽；1535年造船供军队横渡凡湖。

1539年吕特菲帕夏任命他为“幸福之门建筑师”后，1540年代建成王子清真寺。约五旬时他出任皇家首席建筑师，在任近五十年。他名下有三百多座重要建筑，包括苏莱曼尼耶清真寺。

八十多岁时，他完成了埃迪尔内的塞利米耶清真寺，并称之为自己的杰作。他于1588年去世，弟子达乌德阿迦接任，史家常把他与同时代的米开朗基罗相比。

en:
Mimar Sinan (c. 1488/1490–1588), called Koca Sinan, was chief architect of the Ottoman Empire under Suleiman the Magnificent, Selim II and Murad III. The son of a stonemason from Ağırnas near Kayseri, he was conscripted in 1512 and trained as a Janissary officer.

In 1539 Lütfi Pasha made him Architect of the Abode of Felicity, and around fifty he became chief royal architect, a post he kept for almost fifty years. In 1543 he built the Şehzade Mosque for Suleiman's son Mehmed, dead at twenty-two, his first masterpiece. His most famous work is the Süleymaniye, and he also designed the Sulaymaniyya Takiyya in Damascus, introducing the Ottoman style.

In the Selimiye Mosque at Edirne, his masterpiece, he set an octagonal dome 31.28 metres wide on eight piers and claimed it surpassed Hagia Sophia. He died in 1588 and lies in a tomb of his own design.

米马尔·希南（约1488/1490—1588），人称“大师希南”，是苏莱曼大帝、塞利姆二世和穆拉德三世三朝的首席建筑师。他是开塞利附近阿伊尔纳斯的石匠之子，1512年被征召入耶尼切里受训。

1539年吕特菲帕夏任他为“幸福之门建筑师”，约五旬时出任皇家首席建筑师，任职近五十年。1543年，他为苏莱曼二十二岁夭折的儿子穆罕默德修建王子清真寺，是他首件杰作。最著名的作品是苏莱曼尼耶清真寺；大马士革苏莱曼尼耶建筑群把奥斯曼风格引入该城。

在他自称毕生杰作的埃迪尔内塞利米耶清真寺里，他以八根巨柱撑起31.28米宽的八角形穹顶，并宣称它超过圣索菲亚大教堂。1588年他去世，葬在自己设计的陵墓中。

en:
Moses Hamon (c. 1490–1554), born in Granada, fled with his father Joseph to Constantinople, where he became personal physician to Suleiman the Magnificent, accompanying the sultan on every campaign. Versed in Arabic, Turkish and Persian, he patronised Jewish learning and printed Hebrew books in Constantinople as early as 1515, founding a school there.

After a blood libel against the Jews of Amasya around 1545, he persuaded Suleiman to reserve such charges for the royal court. In 1546 he paid for printing Persian and Arabic translations of the Pentateuch, and often settled disputes within the empire's Jewish communities.

摩西·哈蒙（约1490—1554）生于格拉纳达，随父亲约瑟夫逃到君士坦丁堡，后来成为苏莱曼大帝的贴身御医，随苏丹参加每一次远征。他通晓阿拉伯语、土耳其语和波斯语，襄助犹太学术，早在1515年便在君士坦丁堡印制希伯来文书籍，并创办了一所学校。

约1545年阿马西亚的犹太人遭血祭诬陷后，他促使苏莱曼下令此类指控只能由御前法庭审理。1546年，他出资印行《摩西五经》的波斯语和阿拉伯语译本，还常受委托调处帝国犹太人社群内部的纠纷。

en:
Köprülü Mehmed Pasha (c. 1575–1661) was an Albanian-born Ottoman statesman and founder of the Köprülü dynasty of grand viziers. He rose through imperial service to pasha rank, holding several provincial governorships, until in September 1656 Valide Sultan Turhan appointed him grand vizier amid naval defeat and court plots and granted him sweeping powers.

The Venetian blockade of the Dardanelles had cut off supplies to Ottoman forces in Crete. In 1657 he suppressed a cavalry revolt in Constantinople and broke the blockade; he then purged corrupt officials and campaigned in Transylvania in 1658. He died in Edirne in 1661, having secured the vizierate for his son Fazıl Ahmed.

科普鲁律·穆罕默德帕夏（约1575—1661）是阿尔巴尼亚裔奥斯曼政治家，科普鲁律大维齐尔世家的开创者。他在帝国体制内升迁至帕夏，历任多个行省总督；1656年9月，皇太后图尔汗在海军惨败、宫廷谋叛之际任命他为大维齐尔，授以全权。

当时威尼斯对达达尼尔海峡的封锁已切断克里特的补给。1657年，他镇压君士坦丁堡的骑兵叛乱，又打破海峡封锁，随后整肃贪官，1658年出征特兰西瓦尼亚。1661年他卒于埃迪尔内，死前把大维齐尔之位传给儿子法兹尔·艾哈迈德。

en:
Murad I (1326–1389), called Hüdavendigâr, the ‘sovereign’, was the third Ottoman ruler, who turned a frontier principality into a Balkan power. Son of Orhan, he was proclaimed ruler in 1362 while campaigning in Rumelia. That year he crushed revolts and had two brothers strangled.

In 1361 his forces took Adrianople, which Murad made his European capital; he also formed the Janissary corps. His raiders routed Hungarian-led crusaders on the Maritsa in 1364, and his forces crushed a Serbian army at Çirmen in 1371. Bulgaria submitted in 1368, the Byzantine emperor agreed to pay tribute in 1373 and Serbia followed in 1374.

When his son Savcı rebelled in 1373, Murad had him blinded and executed. In 1389 at Kosovo he met Lazar's coalition and died, by one account stabbed by Serbian knight Miloš Obilić. His son Bayezid took command and had his brother Yakub strangled. Murad was buried at Bursa.

[GetCountry('BUL').GetName] submitted in 1368, the Byzantine emperor agreed to pay tribute in 1373 and [GetCountry('SER').GetName] followed in 1374.

When his son Savcı rebelled in 1373, Murad had him blinded and executed. In 1389 at Kosovo he met Lazar's coalition and died, by one account stabbed by Serbian knight Miloš Obilić. His son Bayezid took command and had his brother Yakub strangled. Murad was buried at [ShowLocationName('bursa')].
zh:
穆拉德一世（1326—1389），绰号许达文迪加尔，意为“君主”，是奥斯曼第三位统治者，把一个边境小邦推成了巴尔干强国。他是奥尔汗之子，1362年在鲁米利亚出征时被拥立为君主，当年便平定内乱，绞死了两个兄弟。

1361年，他的军队攻克阿德里安堡，穆拉德把它定为欧洲方面的都城；他还组建了禁卫军。1364年，他的袭击部队在马里查河击溃匈牙利人率领的十字军；1371年，他的军队在奇尔门大破塞尔维亚军队。保加利亚于1368年臣服，拜占庭皇帝于1373年同意纳贡，塞尔维亚于1374年随之称臣。

1373年儿子萨夫奇叛乱，穆拉德下令先刺瞎其双眼，再处死。1389年他在科索沃迎战拉扎尔的联军，死于阵中，一说是被塞尔维亚骑士米洛什·奥比利奇刺杀。其子巴耶济德接掌军队，勒死了弟弟雅库布。穆拉德葬于布尔萨。

Murad Arslan, also recorded as Melik Bey (c. 1290–1336), was a son of the Ottoman founder Osman I. Melik, meaning king, may have been a title, since sources variously call him Arslan or Murad Arslan.

On 12 March 1324 he was listed among the witnesses of his brother Orhan's Mekece endowment charter, one of the oldest surviving Ottoman documents. He had a daughter, Melek Hatun.

穆拉德·阿尔斯兰，亦称马利克·贝伊（约1290—1336），是奥斯曼开国者奥斯曼一世之子。“马利克”源自阿拉伯语“国王”，可能只是称号，故史料中他的名字又作阿尔斯兰或穆拉德·阿尔斯兰。

en:
Nilüfer Hatun (died around 1363 or around 1380) was a Greek-born concubine of Sultan Orhan and the mother of Murad I. She entered Orhan's harem in 1325, converted to Islam and received the name Nilüfer, and in 1326 gave birth to Murad. After 1331 she moved with her son to Iznik.

When Murad succeeded in 1362, she became the Ottoman Empire's first Valide Hatun. She commissioned an imaret, a hammam and a caravanserai, and was buried in Orhan's tomb in Bursa; Murad built the Nilüfer Hatun Imaret at Iznik in 1388.

尼吕费尔可敦（约1363年或约1380年去世）是苏丹奥尔汗的希腊裔妾室，穆拉德一世之母。她于1325年进入奥尔汗后宫，皈依伊斯兰教并得名尼吕费尔，1326年生下穆拉德，1331年后随儿子迁居伊兹尼克。

1362年穆拉德继位后，她成为奥斯曼帝国第一位瓦利德可敦，即太后。她下令修建了施粥所、浴场和商队客栈，死后葬于布尔萨的奥尔汗陵墓；1388年穆拉德在伊兹尼克为纪念她修建了尼吕费尔可敦施粥所。

en:
Orhan Ghazi (c. 1281–1362), son of Osman I, was the second Ottoman ruler and the man who turned a frontier principality into a state. He succeeded in 1323/24, and Bursa surrendered in 1326 after its Byzantine commander went over to him; it became his capital.

In 1329 Andronikos III was routed at Pelekanon and never again fought the Ottomans in the field; Nicaea fell in 1331. In 1345 he annexed the Turkish emirate of Karesi, and Ottoman tradition credits him with founding the Janissaries, drawn from boys of conquered Christian families.

The Byzantine civil wars worked in his favour: in 1346 the regent John VI Kantakouzenos gave him his daughter Theodora and used Ottoman warriors. In 1354 his son Süleyman Pasha occupied Gallipoli, securing a bridgehead in Europe. Orhan died at Bursa in March 1362, and Murad I succeeded him.

zh:
奥尔汗·加齐（约1281—1362）是奥斯曼一世之子，奥斯曼第二位统治者，也是把边境侯国建成正式国家的人。他于1323/24年继位；布尔萨在1326年因拜占庭守将倒戈而献城，成为他的都城。

1329年，安德洛尼卡三世在佩勒卡农被击溃，此后再未与奥斯曼人野战；尼西亚于1331年陷落。1345年，他吞并突厥人的卡勒西侯国；奥斯曼传统还把耶尼切里的创立归于他，这支部队从被征服基督徒家庭的男孩中招募。

拜占庭内战对他有利：1346年，摄政约翰六世·坎塔库泽努斯把女儿狄奥多拉嫁给他，并调用奥斯曼战士。1354年，其子苏莱曼帕夏占领加里波利，为奥斯曼人在欧洲取得桥头堡。1362年3月奥尔汗卒于布尔萨，穆拉德一世继位。

en:
Osman I (c. 1254–1323/1324), called Osman Ghazi, was the founder of the Ottoman dynasty and the Ottomans' first bey. Born at Söğüt, he succeeded his father Ertuğrul around 1281 in Bithynia. He came under the Sufi Sheikh Edebali, whose daughter Rabia Bala he married, and another wife, Malhun Hatun, bore his successor Orhan.

As the Seljuk Sultanate of Rûm collapsed, he made himself an independent ruler in Bithynia, traditionally from 1299. His victory over the Byzantines at Bapheus in 1302 laid open the Bithynian countryside, and he laid siege to Bursa. A tale first recorded by Neşri has him shoot his uncle Dündar for opposing an attack on Bilecik.

Gout troubled him in his last years. Bursa fell to Orhan in 1326, and in some accounts Osman heard the news on his deathbed; Orhan carried his body to Bursa. The dynasty he founded ruled for more than six centuries.

奥斯曼一世（约1254—1323/1324），人称加齐·奥斯曼，是奥斯曼王朝的创建者、奥斯曼人的第一任贝伊。他生于瑟于特，约1281年在比提尼亚继承父亲埃尔图鲁尔之位。他受苏菲谢赫艾德巴利影响，娶了其女拉比娅·巴拉，另一位妻子玛尔可敦生下继承人奥尔汗。

随着鲁姆塞尔柱苏丹国瓦解，他在比提尼亚自立为独立统治者，传统上以1299年为建国之年。1302年他在巴菲乌斯击败拜占庭军队，使比提尼亚乡村门户大开，随后围困布尔萨。内沙里最先记下一则传说：叔父敦达尔反对进攻比莱吉克，被他射杀。

他晚年饱受痛风之苦。布尔萨于1326年被奥尔汗攻克，有的记载说奥斯曼在病榻上听到捷报；奥尔汗把他的遗体迁到布尔萨安葬。他创建的王朝延续了六个多世纪。

en:
Osmanzâde Tâib (c. 1659–1724), real name Ahmed, was an Ottoman Divan poet born in Istanbul, son of a Süleymaniye foundation official. He served as teacher and judge but won fame for his satires and odes, and Sultan Ahmed III granted him the title reîs-i şâirân, head of the poets. Influenced by the poet Nabi, he also wrote works on the grand viziers and on the Ottoman sultans.

His sharp tongue proved fatal: for a jest mocking the governor of Egypt, he was poisoned on the governor's orders in Cairo on 25 May 1724. He also wrote a history of the first twenty-four Ottoman sultans.

奥斯曼扎德·塔伊布（约1659—1724），本名艾哈迈德，是出生于伊斯坦布尔的奥斯曼迪万诗人，父亲是苏莱曼尼耶基金会的文书。他曾任教师和卡迪，尤以讽刺诗与颂诗闻名，艾哈迈德三世授予他“诗人之首”的称号。受诗人纳比影响，他还撰有记述历代大维齐尔和奥斯曼苏丹生平的两部传记。

en:
Patrona Halil (c. 1690–1730) was an Albanian-born Janissary from a village near Bitola and a veteran of the Niš and Vidin mutinies; he led the Vidin mutiny in 1720, and in the capital he lived by petty trade and bathhouse work.

In September 1730, angered by new taxes, wartime shortages and the extravagance of the Tulip Period court, he rallied artisans, shopkeepers and Janissaries at Bayezid Square. The revolt forced Sultan Ahmed III to execute Grand Vizier Ibrahim Pasha and then abdicate in favour of Mahmud I. Halil dominated the capital for weeks, but on 25 November 1730 the new sultan had him murdered at the palace, and his followers were then massacred.

帕特罗纳·哈利尔（约1690—1730）是出生于比托拉附近村庄的阿尔巴尼亚裔耶尼切里，曾参加尼什和维丁兵变，并于1720年领导后者。后来他在首都做小买卖，也在浴室当差。

1730年9月，出于对新税、战时物资匮乏和郁金香时期宫廷奢靡之风的愤怒，他在巴耶济德广场召集手工业者、小商贩和耶尼切里起事。叛乱迫使艾哈迈德三世处死大维齐尔易卜拉欣帕夏，随后退位，由马哈茂德一世继位。哈利尔一度控制首都数周，但1730年11月25日被新苏丹在宫中诱杀，追随者随后遭屠戮。

en:
Piri Reis (c. 1465/1470–1553), born Muhiddin Piri at Gallipoli, was an Ottoman corsair, admiral and cartographer. He sailed with his uncle Kemal Reis on coastal raids and in the Ottoman–Venetian wars, and after his uncle's death drew his celebrated world map of 1513.

He blockaded Alexandria during the 1517 conquest of Egypt and presented the map to Selim I, while his nautical atlas the Kitab-ı Bahriye was dedicated to Suleiman the Magnificent. As Indian Ocean fleet commander he fought the Portuguese in the Red Sea, but after retreating from the siege of Hormuz he was beheaded in 1553.

皮瑞·雷斯（约1465/1470—1553），本名毛希丁·皮里，生于加里波利，是奥斯曼帝国的私掠船长、海军将领和制图师。他早年随叔父凯末尔·雷斯出海劫掠，并在奥斯曼—威尼斯战争中作战，叔父死后绘出著名的1513年世界地图。

1517年征服埃及时，他封锁亚历山大港，并将地图献给塞利姆一世；他的航海图集《航海书》则题献给苏莱曼大帝。晚年他任印度洋舰队总司令，在红海同葡萄牙人作战，但在围攻霍尔木兹撤退后，于1553年被斩首。

en:
Rabia Bala Hatun (died 1324) was the second wife of Osman I, founder of the Ottoman dynasty, and the daughter of Sheikh Edebali, the influential Sufi sheikh who was Osman's mentor and girded him with the sword of a gazi. Her marriage to Osman bound the brotherhood of the Akhıs to his rising beylik.

She was the mother of Alaeddin Ali Pasha, an adviser to Orhan. She died at Bilecik in January 1324 and was buried beside her father in the tomb complex built there by Orhan.

拉比娅·巴拉·哈通（?—1324）是奥斯曼王朝创立者奥斯曼一世的第二位妻子，为有影响力的苏菲谢赫埃德巴利之女；埃德巴利是奥斯曼的导师，曾为他佩上加齐之剑。这场婚姻使阿赫兄弟会与新兴的奥斯曼侯国结成一体。

她是阿拉丁·阿里帕夏的生母，阿里帕夏后来担任奥尔汗的谋臣。1324年1月她在比莱吉克去世，葬在当地奥尔汗所建、其父谢赫·埃德巴利的陵寝建筑群内，与父亲相伴。

en:
Sheikh Celal, called Bozoklu from his native Bozok, later Yozgat, was an Ottoman Alevi preacher in Anatolia who gave his name to the Celali rebellions. In 1519, under Selim I, he led a revolt of hard-pressed peasants and dispossessed soldiery around Tokat.

He drew support from Turkmen stirred by Safavid agitation. The rising, the first Celali rebellion, was bloodily suppressed within the year, and later writers gave Celal's name to the Anatolian rebel movements that followed.

en:
Süleyman Pasha (c. 1306–1357) was Orhan's son and the commander who carried the Ottomans across into Europe, earning the title Ghazi and the name Conqueror of Rumelia. In Anatolia he led the capture of Nicaea in 1331, the Karasid principality in 1335 and Nicomedia in 1337, and became governor of the conquered lands.

The turning point came after the earthquake of 1354 wrecked Gallipoli and he occupied it. In 1355 he crossed the Dardanelles and seized Bolayır, Tekirdağ and other towns, planting settlements that became bases for further conquest in Thrace.

He built mosques, madrasas, caravanserais and schools in his lands. He died in 1357 after falling from his horse while hunting with a falcon, and was buried at Bolayır, though he had already built a mausoleum near Bursa.

苏莱曼帕夏（约1306—1357）是奥尔汗之子，也是率领奥斯曼人渡海进入欧洲的统帅，因战功被尊为加齐，号称“鲁米利亚的征服者”。在安纳托利亚，他率军于1331年攻取尼西亚、1335年攻灭卡勒西贝伊国、1337年攻取尼科米底亚，并出任征服地总督。

转折出现在1354年：地震重创加里波利，他随即占领该城。1355年他渡过达达尼尔海峡，攻占博拉伊尔、泰基尔达等城镇，建立的定居点成为进一步征服色雷斯的基地。

他在辖地修建清真寺、经学院、商队驿站和学校。1357年他架鹰狩猎时坠马而死，葬于博拉伊尔，尽管他早已在布尔萨附近修好陵墓。

en:
Taqi al-Din Muhammad ibn Ma'ruf (1526–1585), born in Damascus, was an Ottoman astronomer and polymath. After studying theology and the rational sciences in Damascus and Cairo, he held teaching and judicial posts; in 1551 he described a steam-driven device for turning a roasting spit. He later settled in Constantinople, becoming the sultan's chief astronomer in 1571.

Under Murad III he built the Constantinople observatory, using instruments including mechanical clocks to observe the great comet of 1577. Completed in 1579, it was demolished only months later. He wrote more than ninety works on astronomy, optics, clocks and mechanics and died in 1585.

塔基丁·穆罕默德·伊本·马鲁夫（1526—1585）生于大马士革，是奥斯曼帝国的天文学家和博学家。他在大马士革和开罗研习经学与理性科学，后担任教职和卡迪；1551年，他记述了一种用蒸汽带动烤肉叉转动的装置。此后他定居君士坦丁堡，1571年成为苏丹的首席天文学家。

在穆拉德三世治下，他主持修建君士坦丁堡天文台，用机械钟等仪器观测了1577年的大彗星。天文台1579年建成，仅数月后即被拆毁。他著有九十多部关于天文、光学、钟表和机械的著作，于1585年去世。

en:
Yusuf Ağa (died 1691) was the Kızlar Ağası, chief black eunuch of the imperial harem, under Sultan Mehmed IV and one of the palace's most powerful figures. His office supervised the imperial religious endowments for Mecca and Medina and had close ties to Egypt.

After the failed Siege of Vienna in 1683 he joined the enemies of Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha, helping bring about his downfall and execution. When Mehmed IV was deposed in 1687, Yusuf Ağa's estates were seized and he was exiled to Egypt, where he died in 1691.

优素福·阿迦（？—1691）是穆罕默德四世在位时的吉兹拉阿迦，即帝国后宫的黑人宦官总管，也是宫中最有权势的人物之一。该职位负责监督麦加和麦地那的帝国宗教基金，并与埃及有密切联系。

1683年维也纳之围失败后，他加入大维齐尔卡拉·穆斯塔法帕夏的政敌之列，促成其倒台并处决。1687年穆罕默德四世被废黜后，优素福·阿迦的家产被抄没，本人被流放埃及，最终于1691年死于该地。

en:
Zahir al-Umar al-Zaydani (1689/1690–1775) was the sheikh of the Arab Zayadina clan who became the effectively independent ruler of northern Palestine under Ottoman suzerainty. He took Tiberias in 1730, added Safed and Nazareth by around 1740, and in 1750 made Acre his capital, growing rich on the cotton trade with France. He invited Christian and Jewish immigrants, helping his towns to grow.

Allied with Ali Bey of Egypt, he seized Sidon and Jaffa in 1771, at his peak holding the coast from Jaffa to Sidon. Driven from Acre in March 1775, he soon returned, but an Ottoman fleet took the city and killed him that August.

扎希尔·欧麦尔·扎伊达尼（1689/1690—1775）是阿拉伯扎伊达纳部族的谢赫，在奥斯曼宗主权下成为北巴勒斯坦事实上的独立统治者。他1730年夺取太巴列，约1740年拿下萨法德与拿撒勒，1750年定都阿卡，靠与法国的棉花贸易致富。他招引基督徒和犹太移民，促进辖下城镇发展。

他与埃及的阿里贝伊结盟，1771年攻取西顿和雅法，极盛时控制从雅法到西顿的海岸。1775年3月他被逐出阿卡，不久便重返该城；8月奥斯曼舰队攻陷阿卡并将他杀死。

Andrei Ivanovich (died 1223) was a prince of Turov from the Turov line of the Rurik dynasty, son of Prince Ivan Yuryevich. He married a daughter of Mstislav Romanovich, grand prince of Kiev.

In 1223 he marched with the allied Rus princes against the Mongols at the Kalka River. The fortified camp where he stood was taken, and he was captured together with his father-in-law. The Mongols crushed the captive princes beneath the planks of their victory feast, and Andrei perished there.

Danylo Ostrozky was a Ruthenian knyaz, probably prince of Turaŭ, who became the first prince of Ostroh and founder of the Ostrozky house. In 1344 he called in Tatars to fight for Galicia during the Galicia–Volhynia Wars.

Later he joined Liubartas of Galicia–Volhynia, received Ostroh and rebuilt its ruined castle. He was prince of Kholm in 1352–1366, signed the Liubartas–Polish boundary charter in 1366 and died before 1376.

达尼洛·奥斯特罗兹基是罗斯王公，相传受封图罗夫，是见于史籍的第一位奥斯特罗格王公、奥斯特罗兹基家族始祖。1344年，在加利西亚-沃伦战争中，他召来鞑靼人为争夺加利西亚而战。

后来他投奔加利西亚-沃伦的柳巴尔塔斯，受封奥斯特罗格并重建被毁的城堡。1352—1366年他任海乌姆王公，1366年在柳巴尔塔斯与波兰的划界文书上署名，1376年前去世。

en:
Gleb Yuryevich (c. 1150–1195) was a son of Yuri Yaroslavich of Turov and Anna Vsevolodovna. The chronicles call him prince of Dubrovitsa from 1182. In 1183 he took part in Grand Prince Sviatoslav Vsevolodovich's victorious Polovtsian campaign.

When his elder brother Sviatopolk died in 1190, Gleb succeeded to the Turovo-Pinsk principality. He ruled it until his own death five years later.

Ivan Yuryevich was a prince of Turov, a son of Yuri Yaroslavich of Turov and Anna, daughter of Prince Vsevolodko of Goroden. The chronicles first name him in 1167–1168, when he joined the other princes of Rus in campaigns against the Polovtsians, and he campaigned against them again in 1170.

That same year he helped Mstislav Izyaslavich recover the Kievan throne from which Andrey Bogolyubsky had expelled him. His later fate is unrecorded.

en:
Sviatopolk Yuryevich (c. 1144–1190), son of Yuri Yaroslavich of Turov and Anna Vsevolodovna, was prince of Pinsk from 1168 and prince of Turov from 1170, when he succeeded his elder brother Ivan.

He joined the great Polovtsian campaign of 1168, backed Mstislav Izyaslavich against Andrey Bogolyubsky and changed sides in 1173. He ruled Turov for twenty years and was followed by his brother Gleb; his sons Vladimir and Rostislav later held Pinsk.

Vladimir Sviatopolkovich (died 1228) was a Rurikid prince, the eldest son of Sviatopolk Yuryevich of Turov. First recorded as prince of Pinsk in 1204, he joined Vsevolod Chermny's alliance against Rurik Rostislavich in 1207.

After his cousin Andrei Ivanovich of Turov was killed at the Kalka River in 1223, Vladimir united the Turov and Pinsk thrones and ruled Turov until his death. When he died in 1228, Andrei's son Yuri took Turov, while Vladimir's brother Rostislav received Pinsk.

en:
Yaropolk Iziaslavich (died 22 November 1086) was a son of Grand Prince Iziaslav I of Kiev. During his father's exile in the 1070s he sought support at the courts of the German emperor and the Pope, returning with him to Kiev in 1077.

In 1078 his uncle Grand Prince Vsevolod made him prince of Turov and Volhynia. Having fallen out with Vsevolod and his son Vladimir Monomakh, he fled to Poland in 1085, returned the next year and was reconciled with Vladimir.

In November 1086 he was murdered on a journey to Zvenigorod by a retainer named Neradets and was buried in the church of Saint Peter in Kiev, which he had endowed.

Yuri Andreevich (died late in the thirteenth century) was prince of Turov, a son of Andrei Ivanovich, who was killed at the Kalka River in 1223. Still underage then, he let Vladimir Sviatopolkovich rule Turov until 1228, when he took the throne.

Lithuania and Galicia-Volhynia pressed his borders, and in the winter of 1241 the Mongols sacked and destroyed Turov. After a battle against the Mongols in 1246 he kept his throne, though the principality slipped into vassalage. His son Semyon succeeded him.

en:
Yury Yaroslavich (born before 1112, died c. 1168), a son of Yaroslav Sviatopolkovich of Volhynia, founded the Turov-Pinsk branch of the Rurikids. From about 1142 he ruled Pinsk and Turov, and in 1157 he seized Turov from Yuri Dolgorukiy's son Boris after Dolgorukiy's death.

Grand Prince Izyaslav Davydovich besieged Turov in 1157 and again in 1159, allied with Mstislav of Volhynia, but failed to take it. In 1162 Grand Prince Rostislav of Kiev made peace with Yury. At his death his sons split the Turov-Pinsk principality into appanages.

Aleksandr Mikhailovich (1301–1339), son of Mikhail of Tver, became prince of Tver and grand prince of Vladimir in 1326. After Tver's citizens massacred the Tatar retinue of baskak Shevkal in 1327, Özbeg Khan sent Ivan I of Moscow to sack the city, and Aleksandr lost his throne.

After years of exile in Pskov and Lithuania he was pardoned at Sarai and returned to Tver in 1338, but in 1339 Özbeg had him and his son Fyodor executed, ending his 35-year struggle with Moscow for the grand principality of Vladimir.

en:
Konstantin Mikhailovich (1306–1346) ruled Tver in the years when it lost its long contest with Moscow. The third son of Mikhail of Tver, he was held captive in Sarai after the Mongols executed his father in 1318, until he was ransomed for 2000 rubles; in 1320 he married Sophia, daughter of Yury of Moscow.

When the 1327 uprising drove his brother Aleksandr out, he returned to a devastated Tver and began gathering its people. In 1328 he obtained the khan's yarlyk and ruled quietly under the close watch of his wife's uncle, Ivan I of Moscow.

After Aleksandr was executed in 1339, Konstantin ruled again. A quarrel with Aleksandr's son Vsevolod took him to the Horde for judgment, but he died in 1346 before the trial began, and Vsevolod took the throne.

Mikhail Aleksandrovich (1333–1399) was a son of Aleksandr Mikhailovich of Tver and grew up in Pskov after his father's flight in 1327. He became prince of Tver in 1368 and, allied with his brother-in-law Algirdas of Lithuania, was the last Tver ruler seriously to challenge Moscow for leadership of the Russian lands.

Three times between 1370 and 1375 he obtained a yarlyk as grand prince of Vladimir, but Dmitry Donskoy defeated him in 1375 and forced him to recognize Moscow's supremacy. He ruled Tver until his death in 1399.

米哈伊尔·亚历山德罗维奇（1333—1399）是特维尔大公亚历山大·米哈伊洛维奇之子，1327年其父流亡后在普斯科夫长大。1368年他成为特维尔统治者，与姐夫立陶宛大公阿尔吉尔达斯结盟，是最后一位能与莫斯科争夺罗斯领袖地位的特维尔王公。

他于1370至1375年间三次取得弗拉基米尔大公告令，却始终压不垮德米特里·顿斯科伊；1375年德米特里兵临特维尔，他被迫承认莫斯科的领袖地位。他统治特维尔直至1399年去世。

en:
Mikhail Yaroslavich (1271–1318) became prince of Tver in 1285 and was named grand prince of Vladimir in 1304 after receiving his patent from the khan of the Golden Horde. His reign was dominated by his feud with Yury of Moscow.

In December 1317 he defeated Yury at Bortenevo and captured his wife, a sister of Uzbeg Khan; when she died in custody, he was charged with her murder. Summoned to Sarai, he was executed on 22 November 1318. The Russian Church later canonized him for meeting certain death meekly.

米哈伊尔·雅罗斯拉维奇（1271—1318）于1285年成为特维尔王公，1304年获金帐汗国可汗颁授诰命，成为弗拉基米尔大公。他统治的主线是与莫斯科王公尤里的长期争斗。

1317年12月他在博尔捷涅沃击败尤里，俘获的尤里之妻是乌兹别克汗的妹妹；她在拘押中死去，米哈伊尔因此被控谋杀。米哈伊尔被召往萨莱，于1318年11月22日被处死。俄罗斯东正教会后来追封他为圣徒，以嘉其坦然赴死。

en:
Uliana Aleksandrovna (c. 1325–1391) was a princess of Tver, the daughter of Aleksandr Mikhailovich and Anastasia of Galicia. After her father and brother were executed at the Golden Horde in 1339, she grew up at the court of her brother-in-law Simeon of Moscow. In 1349 she married Grand Duke Algirdas of Lithuania as his second wife.

She bore him many children, including Jogaila, the future king of Poland, and in 1370 persuaded Algirdas to campaign against Moscow for her brother Mikhail of Tver. After Algirdas died in 1377 she held Vitebsk under his will.

乌莉安娜·亚历山德罗芙娜（约1325—1391）是特维尔公主，亚历山大·米哈伊洛维奇与加利西亚的阿纳斯塔西娅之女。1339年父亲和兄长在金帐汗国被处死后，她在姐姐玛丽亚的丈夫、莫斯科的谢苗宫廷中长大。1349年，她嫁给立陶宛大公阿尔吉尔达斯，成为其第二任妻子。

她生下众多子女，包括后来的波兰国王约盖拉；1370年，她说服阿尔吉尔达斯出兵，帮助兄长米哈伊尔对抗莫斯科。阿尔吉尔达斯于1377年去世后，她按其遗嘱领有维捷布斯克。

en:
Áed Findliath, the fair-grey (died 20 November 879), son of Niall Caille, was king of Ailech and became high king of Ireland in 862. He defeated the Norse at Glenn Foichle in 856 and burned their northern longphorts while Amlaíb and Auisle campaigned in Scotland.

In 868 he routed the men of Brega, Leinster and the foreigners at Cell Ua nDaigri, where Flann of Brega fell. He invaded Leinster in 870 and 874, died at Druim Inasclainn in 879, and left a son Niall Glúndub, ancestor of the O'Neills.

en:
Áed in Macáem Tóinlesc (died 1177) founded O'Neill power in Tír Eogain. After High King Muirchertach Mac Lochlainn was killed in 1166, Áed was proclaimed king of Tír Eogain with the backing of Donnchad Ua Cerbaill.

In 1167 High King Ruaidrí Ua Conchobair divided the province between Áed and Niall Mac Lochlainn. As Ruaidrí's vassal Áed brought three thousand men to the 1174 siege of Norman-held Trim. He was killed by Máel Sechlainn Mac Lochlainn in 1177, leaving his son Áed Méith to entrench O'Neill rule.

艾德·安·马凯姆·托因莱斯克（？—1177）奠定了奥尼尔家族在蒂尔欧文的势力。1166年爱尔兰高王穆尔切赫塔赫·麦克·洛克林败亡后，他在邓查德·乌阿·采尔拜尔支持下被拥立为蒂尔欧文国王。

1167年，高王罗艾德里·奥康却拜尔将蒂尔欧文分给他和尼亚尔·麦克洛克林。作为罗艾德里的封臣，他于1174年率三千人参与围攻诺曼人占据的特里姆。1177年他被梅尔·塞克兰·麦克洛克林杀害，其子艾德·梅思后来巩固了奥尼尔家族的统治。

en:
Aodh Méith Ó Néill (died 1230), son of Áed in Macáem Tóinlesc, made himself king of Tír Eoghain amid the chaos after the Norman conquest of eastern Ulster. From 1199 he raided John de Courcy's port of Larne and forced the Fir Manach and Cenél Conaill to submit.

He weathered invasions by Hugh de Lacy and Gall-Gaidhil forces, brought aid to King John at Carrickfergus in 1210, and in 1224 blocked a royal army in Armagh. He died in 1230 with O'Neill power entrenched; the Clandeboye O'Neills descend from him.

en:
Hugh Boy Ó Néill, called the Fair (died 1283), son of Domhnall Óg, was the last king of Ailech and eponym of the Clandeboye O'Neills. After Brian Chatha an Dúna fell in 1260 he took the kingship, expelling his brother Niall Cúlanch.

He married Eleanor, cousin of Earl Walter de Burgh, whom he acknowledged as overlord in 1269. In 1281 he killed Donnell Óg O'Donnell, and in 1283 was himself killed by Brian MacMahon and Gilla Ísa O'Reilly.

en:
Aodh Reamhar (Hugh the Stout) was king of Tír Eoghain in 1345–1364. The fourth son of Domhnall O'Neill, he came forward after three of his brothers were killed between 1318 and 1325. In 1339 he led a great army into Tír Chonaill, and in 1345 a fleet on Lough Neagh and the aid of the justiciar let him overcome his Clandeboye rival and seize the kingship.

He defeated Oriel and Fermanagh in 1354. When he died in 1364 the Four Masters called him the best of the Irish of his age, and his son Niall Mór succeeded him.

He defeated [GetCountry('OIL').GetName] and [GetCountry('FMA').GetName] in 1354. When he died in 1364 the Four Masters called him the best of the [ShowCultureName('irish')] of his age, and his son Niall Mór succeeded him.
zh:
艾·鲁尔（绰号“壮汉休”）在1345—1364年间任蒂尔埃奥甘国王。他是多姆纳尔·奥尼尔的第四子，三个兄弟在1318至1325年间先后被杀后，他崭露头角。1339年他率军攻入蒂尔康奈；1345年，他凭借内伊湖舰队与爱尔兰总督的援助，击败克兰德博伊的对手，夺得王位。

1354年他击败奥里尔与弗马纳的人马。1364年他去世时，《四大师编年史》称他为同时代爱尔兰人中最杰出者，其子尼尔·莫尔继位。

Brian Ó Néill, called Brian Chatha an Dúna (c. 1220–1260), ruled Tír Eoghain from 1238 and was acknowledged high king of Ireland in 1258. The son of Niall Ruadh, he crushed the Meic Lochlainn at Camergi in 1241, ending their long rivalry with the O'Neills.

In 1258 he was inaugurated King of the Gael. In 1260 he attacked the Normans at Downpatrick and fell at the battle of Drumderg; his head was sent to Henry III.

Brian Ó Néill (c. 1265–1295) was a king of Tír Eoghain and the son of Hugh Boy Ó Néill. In 1291, after his uncle Niall Cúlánach was killed by Donnell Ó Néill, Brian secured the kingship with Norman aid from the vassals of Earl Richard Óg de Burgh.

He ruled with Norman backing until 1295, when Donnell defeated and killed him at the battle of Creeve. His son Henry later became king and founded the lordship of Clandeboye.

Conchobar Beg (died 1201) was a Mac Lochlainn claimant to the kingship of Tír Eoghain. In 1201 the Cenél nEógain deposed their king Áed Méith Ó Néill and elected Conchobar in his stead.

He went to war with Eignechán Ua Domnaill of Tír Conaill. In the fighting his horse was wounded under him; unhorsed, he was killed by the Cenél Conaill, who held him to account for plundering the shrine of Saint Colum Cille.

Domnall Mac Lochlainn (died 1241) was the last Mac Lochlainn king of Tír Eoghain. In 1234 he killed the reigning king, Domnall Óc Ó Néill, and seized the kingship, but was deposed in 1238. He won power back after the battle of Carnteel in 1239.

In 1241 Brian Ó Néill and his allies defeated and killed him at Caimeirge; ten of his kindred died with him, and the kingship passed permanently to the Ó Néill.

en:
Domnall Ua Lochlainn (1048–1121), son of Ardgar, became king of Ailech in 1083 as leader of the Cenél nEógain, opening his reign with the traditional inaugural cattle-raid. From 1101 to 1119 he contested the high kingship of Ireland with his great southern rival, Muirchertach Ua Briain of Munster.

His jurists argued that a king who could lead his army through all Ireland unbeaten was high king despite opposition. He died at Derry in 1121, and the northern annals styled him over-king of Ireland.

Domnall ua Néill (c. 920–980) was High King of Ireland from 956. A grandson of Niall Glúndub of the northern Uí Néill, he became king of Ailech on his father's death in 943 and took the high kingship in 956.

A ruler credited with military reforms later associated with Brian Boru, he long warred against Amlaíb Cuarán, the Norse king of Dublin. In 980 he abdicated into Armagh monastery, where he died soon after, the last of his line to hold the high kingship.

en:
Donnell Ó Néill (c. 1245–1325), son of Brian Chatha an Dúna, was king of Tír Eoghain on and off from 1283. Earl Richard Óg de Burgh twice deposed him, but in 1295 Donnell slew Brian at Creeve and retook the kingship.

In 1314 he invited Edward Bruce to Ireland, and in 1317 urged Pope John XXII to denounce English rule and hail Bruce king of Ireland. Deposed after Bruce's defeat, he regained power and died in 1325.

Muirchertach Mac Lochlainn (died 1166), grandson of Domnall Ua Lochlainn, was king of Tír Eoghain and high king of Ireland from about 1156. He saw off a bid to overthrow him in 1159, but never broke the resistance of the Cenél Conaill and the Ulaid.

In 1166 he swore to the Bishop of Armagh to keep a truce with Ulaid, then seized and blinded its king. His allies deserted him, and he was cut down with sixteen followers; contemporaries read his death as Saint Patrick's vengeance.

Niall Cúlánach Ó Néill (c. 1231–1291), whose nickname means of the long back hair, was a son of Domhnall Óg and three times king of Tír Eoghain. In 1261 he took the kingship from his brother Hugh Boy but was defeated by Donnell Óg O'Donnell and expelled in 1262.

In 1286 Earl Richard Óg de Burgh installed him after deposing Donnell Ó Néill; Niall lost power and was restored before Donnell killed him in 1291. De Burgh then enthroned Hugh Boy's son Brian.

Niall Glúndub mac Áeda (died 919) was king of the Cenél nEógain and, from 916, High King of Ireland. A son of Áed Findliath, his mother was Máel Muire, daughter of Kenneth MacAlpin, king of Scots. He succeeded his brother as king of Ailech in 911.

Niall Mór O'Neill was king of Tír Eoghain in 1364–1397, succeeding his father Aodh Reamhar. In 1375 he crushed the Anglo-Irish at Downpatrick, reducing the Earldom of Ulster to the country around Carrickfergus and restoring O'Neill power east of the Bann.

In 1395 he did homage to Richard II during the king's Irish expedition. A patron of poets who hailed him as king of Tara, he abdicated in 1397 and died in 1398. The Annals of Ulster style him high-king of Ulster and claimant to the kingship of Ireland.

en:
Albert I Wittelsbach (1336–1404), third son of Emperor Louis IV, was a younger son expecting at best an appanage, yet came to rule Holland, Hainaut, Zeeland and Bavaria-Straubing. When his brother William went mad, Albert became regent in 1358, though the Hook and Cod factions simmered. He succeeded William as count in 1389, having married his daughter Margaret to John the Fearless of Burgundy.

The worst crisis of his reign began with a murder: his mistress Aleid van Poelgeest, a Cod partisan resented for her influence, was killed at The Hague in 1392 by Hook nobles. Albert hunted down the Hooks with sword and fire, and his son William fled to Hainaut.

His last years went to campaigns against the Frisians, never fully conquered. After he died in 1404 the Burgundian match brought his lands to Margaret's son Philip.

阿尔布雷希特一世·维特尔斯巴赫（1336—1404）是皇帝路德维希四世的第三子，本是至多指望分得一份附属领地的幼子，后来却统治荷兰、埃诺、泽兰和巴伐利亚-施特劳宾。兄长威廉发疯后，他于1358年出任摄政，鱼钩派与鳕鱼派的纷争仍未平息。1389年他继威廉为伯爵，此前已将女儿玛格丽特嫁给勃艮第的无畏者约翰。

他在位期间最严重的危机始于一桩谋杀：情妇阿莱德·范·普尔赫斯特属鳕鱼派，因影响力招致怨恨，1392年在海牙被鱼钩派贵族杀害。阿尔布雷希特以刀火追剿鱼钩派，其子威廉出走埃诺。

晚年他连年征讨弗里斯兰人，始终未能完全征服。1404年他去世，勃艮第联姻最终使他的领地归入玛格丽特之子腓力名下。

Beatrice of Świdnica (1290–1322) was a Piast princess, daughter of Duke Bolko I of Jawor-Świdnica and Beatrice of Brandenburg. After her father died in 1301 she was raised under guardianship until her brother Bernard arranged her marriage to Louis IV of Upper Bavaria in 1308.

She bore six children, three surviving to adulthood. In 1314 Louis was elected German king in rivalry with Frederick of Austria, making Beatrice a rival queen to Frederick's wife. She died in Munich in 1322.

en:
Dietrich von Parsberg was a Bavarian nobleman of the Parsberg ministerial family, whose seat was Parsberg Castle in the Upper Palatinate. Around 1300 his brother Konrad, protonotary of Duke Rudolf I of Upper Bavaria, secured for Dietrich and their brother Heinrich the two offices of Viztum, the duke's deputies who each administered roughly half of Upper Bavaria.

When Rudolf I lost his struggle with Louis IV, the Parsberg brothers lost their positions after 1310. Dietrich then served the victorious Louis IV.

迪特里希·冯·帕尔斯贝格出身巴伐利亚侍臣贵族帕尔斯贝格家族，家族居城是上普法尔茨的帕尔斯贝格城堡。约1300年，他的兄长、上巴伐利亚公爵鲁道夫一世的首席书记官康拉德，安排迪特里希与兄弟海因里希出任公爵治下仅有的两名代理人，两人分管上巴伐利亚约一半的领地。

鲁道夫一世在与路德维希四世的争斗中失败后，帕尔斯贝格兄弟于1310年后失去要职，迪特里希此后转而为获胜的路德维希四世效力。

en:
Elisabeth of Bavaria (1329–1402) was a daughter of Emperor Louis IV and Margaret II of Hainaut. In 1350 she married Cangrande II della Scala, who became lord of Verona in 1352; the marriage was childless, and in 1359 Cangrande was murdered by his brother Cansignorio.

In 1362 she married Ulrich, son and heir of Count Eberhard II of Württemberg, by whom she had the future Count Eberhard III. Ulrich fell at the Battle of Döffingen in 1388 before he could succeed. Elisabeth died in Stuttgart in 1402.

巴伐利亚的伊丽莎白（1329—1402）是皇帝路德维希四世与埃诺女伯爵玛格丽特二世之女。1350年，她嫁给坎格兰德二世·德拉·斯卡拉，后者于1352年成为维罗纳领主；这段婚姻没有子嗣，1359年坎格兰德被其兄弟坎西尼奥里奥刺杀。

1362年，她改嫁符腾堡伯爵埃伯哈德二世之子兼继承人乌尔里希，生下后来的伯爵埃伯哈德三世。乌尔里希于1388年在德芬根战役中阵亡，未能继位。伊丽莎白1402年卒于斯图加特。

en:
Johannes Hake, called Johann von Göttingen (c. 1280–1349), was one of the most famous physicians of his age. After studying medicine in Paris and teaching it at Montpellier, he served as doctor to rulers including Emperor Louis IV and Pope Benedict XII, and in 1331 wrote a treatise on poison.

Made bishop of Verden in 1331 and translated to Freising in 1341, he spent his later years at the papal court in Avignon, where he probably died in 1349 and was buried.

约翰内斯·哈克，人称“哥廷根的约翰”（约1280—1349），是当时最负盛名的医生之一。他在巴黎学医、在蒙彼利埃教授医学，曾为皇帝路德维希四世、教皇本笃十二世等显贵诊治，1331年撰写了一部论述毒物防备的专著。

他1331年出任费尔登主教，1341年调任弗赖辛主教，晚年多在阿维尼翁教廷度过，可能于1349年在当地去世并安葬。

Jutta of Świdnica (1285/1287–1320) was a Piast princess, eldest daughter of Duke Bolko I of Świdnica and Beatrix of Brandenburg. Around 1297 she married Duke Stephen I of Lower Bavaria, remaining in Silesia for two years because of her youth.

Stephen died at Landshut in 1310, leaving her with five children; their sons Henry XIV and Otto IV succeeded as dukes. Jutta died in 1320 and was buried beside her husband in Seligenthal Abbey at Landshut.

希维德尼察的尤塔（1285/1287—1320）是皮亚斯特家族的公主，希维德尼察公爵波尔科一世与勃兰登堡的贝娅特丽克丝的长女。约1297年她嫁给下巴伐利亚公爵施特凡一世，因年幼在西里西亚又留了两年。

施特凡1310年死于兰茨胡特，留给她五个孩子；儿子亨利十四世和奥托四世后来成为公爵。尤塔于1320年去世，葬在兰茨胡特的塞利根塔尔修道院，与丈夫合葬。

en:
Louis II Wittelsbach (1229–1294) ruled Upper Bavaria and the Rhenish Palatinate from the 1255 partition that left Lower Bavaria to his brother Henry XIII. In 1256 he had his wife Maria of Brabant beheaded for suspected adultery and founded Fürstenfeld Abbey in expiation.

During the Interregnum he backed the Hohenstaufen Conradin: excommunicated in 1266, he escorted him as far as Verona in 1267 and inherited Swabian lands after Conradin's execution in 1268.

He helped elect Rudolf of Habsburg in 1273 and fought beside him when Ottokar was defeated and killed at Dürnkrut in 1278. He died at Heidelberg in 1294.

路德维希二世·维特尔斯巴赫（1229—1294）在1255年家族领地分割后获得上巴伐利亚和莱茵行宫伯爵领，其弟亨利十三世分得下巴伐利亚。1256年他以涉嫌通奸为由将妻子布拉班特的玛丽亚斩首，后修建菲斯滕费尔德修道院赎罪。

大空位时期他支持霍亨斯陶芬家族的康拉丁，1266年被开除教籍，1267年护送康拉丁至维罗纳，1268年康拉丁被处死后继承了他在施瓦本的部分领地。

他于1273年助力选出哈布斯堡的鲁道夫，并于1278年在迪恩克鲁特战役中与鲁道夫并肩作战，奥托卡战败身亡。1294年，他卒于海德堡。

en:
Louis IV Wittelsbach (1282–1347), called the Bavarian, was Holy Roman Emperor from 1328 and the last Bavarian to wear the German crown until 1742. Elected King of the Romans in 1314 in a disputed double election against his Habsburg cousin Frederick the Fair, he defeated and captured Frederick at Mühldorf in 1322; the rivals later reconciled.

Pope John XXII excommunicated him for ruling without papal approval, so Louis marched to Rome, was crowned emperor in 1328 and backed an antipope. His Munich court sheltered Franciscan dissidents fleeing Avignon, William of Ockham among them.

Across his reign he expanded his dynasty's domains, securing Brandenburg in 1323, Lower Bavaria in 1340, and Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland through his wife Margaret in 1345, before dying on 11 October 1347.

路德维希四世·维特尔斯巴赫（1282—1347），绰号“巴伐利亚人”，1328年起任神圣罗马皇帝，也是直到1742年为止最后一位登上德意志王位的巴伐利亚人。1314年他在与哈布斯堡表亲美男子腓特烈的双重选举争议中当选罗马人的国王，1322年在米尔多夫战役击败并俘获腓特烈，二人后来和解。

教皇约翰二十二世因他不经教皇认可便行使皇权而开除其教籍，路德维希遂进军罗马，于1328年加冕为帝，并拥立对立教皇。他在慕尼黑的宫廷成了逃离阿维尼翁的方济各会异见者的庇护所，奥卡姆的威廉便是其中之一。

在位期间他不断拓展家族领地：1323年取得勃兰登堡，1340年并入下巴伐利亚，1345年又由妻子玛格丽特继承埃诺、荷兰和泽兰，直至1347年10月11日去世。

en:
Louis VI (1328–1365) was called the Roman because he was born in Rome in 1328, while his father, Louis IV, was there to be crowned emperor. He became Duke of Upper Bavaria in 1347. Expecting the Polish crown through his marriage to Cunigunde, daughter of Casimir III, he yielded Holland and Hainaut to his brothers William and Albert in 1349.

In 1351 he took Brandenburg from his half-brother Louis V in exchange for sole rule of Upper Bavaria. There he faced the False Waldemar, an impostor backed by several cities and by Charles IV until the Wittelsbachs came to terms with the emperor. The Golden Bull of 1356 confirmed him as prince-elector.

Childless and at odds with his brother Stephen II over the Bavarian inheritance, he and Otto V promised Brandenburg to Charles IV in 1364. He died in Berlin in 1365.

zh:
路德维希六世·维特尔斯巴赫（1328—1365）绰号“罗马人”，因1328年生于罗马、时值其父路德维希四世在那里加冕为皇帝而得名。1347年起他任上巴伐利亚公爵。他期望通过与卡齐米日三世之女昆尼贡德的婚姻取得波兰王位，于1349年将荷兰和埃诺让给弟弟威廉和阿尔布雷希特。

1351年，他以单独统治上巴伐利亚为条件，从异母兄路德维希五世手中换得勃兰登堡。在那里他遭到伪瓦尔德马的挑战，这个冒名者得到若干城市和皇帝查理四世的支持，直到维特尔斯巴赫家族与皇帝达成和解。1356年的《金玺诏书》确认其选帝侯地位。

他没有子嗣，又与兄弟斯特凡二世为巴伐利亚继承权失和，遂与奥托五世于1364年允诺由查理四世继承勃兰登堡。1365年他卒于柏林。

en:
Margaret II of Avesnes (1311–1356), daughter of Count William I of Hainaut, married Emperor Louis IV of Bavaria in 1324 and was crowned Holy Roman Empress in Rome in 1328. When her brother William II fell at Warns in 1345, Louis declared Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland his wife's possessions, and she won over their doubtful towns with economic privileges.

After seven months she was called back to Germany, and when Louis died in 1347 she resigned her lands to her son William for an allowance. He withheld it, she took back her rights in 1350, and the Hook and Cod wars began between her supporters and his.

Edward III won a naval battle for her off Veere in 1351, but weeks later her side was crushed at Vlaardingen. In 1354 she settled, keeping Hainaut for life, and on her death in 1356 William inherited the whole.

玛格丽特二世·德·阿韦讷（1311—1356）是埃诺伯爵威廉一世之女，1324年嫁给皇帝巴伐利亚人路德维希四世，1328年在罗马加冕为神圣罗马帝国皇后。1345年，其兄威廉二世在瓦恩斯战死，路德维希宣布埃诺、荷兰与泽兰是妻子的领地；她便授予存疑的城镇经济特权以赢得支持。

七个月后，她被召回德意志，1347年路德维希去世，她让位于儿子威廉以换取津贴。威廉拒付，1350年她收回权位，支持她的“鱼钩派”与支持威廉的“鳕鱼派”由此爆发内战。

1351年，爱德华三世在费勒外海为她赢得一场海战，数周后她这一方却在菲拉尔丁根惨败。1354年双方议和，她保留埃诺至终老，1356年去世后遗产全归威廉。

Margaret of Bavaria (1325–1374) was the eldest daughter of Emperor Louis IV and Margaret II, Countess of Hainaut. In 1351 she married Stephen, Duke of Slavonia, youngest son of King Charles I of Hungary. When Stephen died in 1354, she ruled Slavonia, Croatia and Dalmatia as regent for their infant son John, the heir presumptive to Hungary and Poland.

She remarried Gerlach von Hohenlohe in 1356, but in that year's war with Venice the Hungarian crown ended the duchy's autonomy and removed her from power. John died in 1360, and Margaret died in 1374.

Matilda of Habsburg (1253–1304) was the eldest daughter of King Rudolf I of Germany. In 1273 at Aachen she became the third wife of Louis II the Strict, Duke of Upper Bavaria; the marriage linked the rising Habsburgs with the Wittelsbach dynasty.

Her children included Rudolf I of Bavaria and the future Emperor Louis IV. After Louis II died in 1294, she ruled Upper Bavaria as regent for her young son until 1301, and died at Munich in 1304.

en:
Michael of Cesena (c. 1270–1342) was the Franciscan minister general whose defense of apostolic poverty broke with Pope John XXII and carried him into the emperor's camp. Born at Cesena, he studied theology in Paris before his election as minister general in 1316.

At first he sided with the pope in suppressing the Spiritual Franciscans, but in 1322 the Perugia chapter endorsed his teaching that Christ and the apostles owned no property, and John XXII condemned it. Summoned to Avignon in 1327 and forbidden to leave, Michael fled in 1328 with William of Ockham to Pisa, where Emperor Louis IV, himself in conflict with the pope, protected him.

Excommunicated and deposed by the Paris chapter in 1329, he was expelled by the Perpignan chapter in 1331 and stayed in Munich until his death in 1342; he was rehabilitated in 1359.

切塞纳的米凯莱（约1270—1342）是方济各会总会长，因捍卫使徒守贫而与教皇约翰二十二世决裂，最终投奔皇帝一方。他生于切塞纳，在巴黎研习神学，1316年当选总会长。

起初他站在教皇一边压制灵修派，但1322年佩鲁贾总会通过了他的主张，认定基督与使徒不蓄私产，约翰二十二世则谴责这一教义。1327年他被召至阿维尼翁并被禁止离开，1328年与奥卡姆的威廉一同出逃至比萨，在同样与教皇对立的皇帝路德维希四世处得到庇护。

他被开除教籍，1329年被巴黎总会免职，1331年又被佩皮尼昂总会逐出修会，此后一直留在慕尼黑，1342年死于当地，1359年获平反。

Rudolf I Wittelsbach (1274–1319) succeeded his father Louis II in 1294 as Duke of Upper Bavaria and Count Palatine of the Rhine and married Mechtild, daughter of King Adolf of Nassau. He supported Adolf at Göllheim in 1298, where the king was killed.

His reign was overshadowed by his brother Louis IV: besieged at Heidelberg in 1301, Rudolf accepted Louis as co-regent. The brothers fought a civil war and made peace at Munich in 1313.

He voted for the Habsburg Frederick the Fair in 1314 and yielded rule to Louis in 1317. The 1329 Treaty of Pavia granted the Palatinate to his sons and established their branch of the dynasty.

Stephen II (1319–1375), second son of Emperor Louis IV, ruled as duke of Bavaria from 1347. After the 1349 partition he governed Holland and Lower Bavaria-Landshut with his brothers, keeping only the latter after 1353.

He joined Charles IV's Italian expedition in 1354, inherited Upper Bavaria in 1363 and invaded Tyrol, then renounced it to the Habsburgs at the Peace of Schärding in 1369. His feud with Louis VI the Roman helped lose the Wittelsbachs Brandenburg. He died at Landshut in 1375 and was buried in Munich's Frauenkirche.

en:
Stephen III (1337–1413), called the Magnificent, was the eldest son of Duke Stephen II of Bavaria and Elizabeth of Sicily. From 1375 he ruled Bavaria jointly with his brothers, until the 1392 partition gave him Bavaria-Ingolstadt, where he founded the Ingolstadt line.

He repeatedly fought his brothers and nephews over their shares, supported King Rupert against the Luxemburgs, and backed the failed Munich citizens' uprising of 1403. His daughter Isabeau married Charles VI of France. A final bid to reconquer Tyrol in 1410 failed, and he died at Niederschönenfeld in 1413.

斯特凡三世（1337—1413），人称“豪华者”，是巴伐利亚公爵斯特凡二世与西西里的伊丽莎白的长子。1375年起他与兄弟共同统治巴伐利亚；1392年公国分裂，他分得巴伐利亚-因戈尔施塔特，开创因戈尔施塔特支系。

他为领地份额一再与兄弟和侄子交战，支持国王鲁普雷希特对抗卢森堡家族，并支持1403年失败的慕尼黑市民起义。其女伊萨博嫁给法国国王查理六世。1410年他最后一次试图夺回蒂罗尔，仍告失败，1413年死于尼德舍嫩费尔德。

en:
William Wittelsbach (1330–1389), second son of Emperor Louis IV and Margaret of Hainaut, was Duke of Bavaria-Straubing and Count of Holland, Hainaut and Zeeland. His rule began as a war with his own mother: when the nobles of Holland called Margaret back in 1350, the Cod and Hook leagues formed and civil war followed.

Edward III came to her aid, yet William won at Zwartewaal in 1351 after losing the naval battle of Veere. In 1354 she recognised him as Count of Holland and Zeeland, and her death in 1356 left him Hainaut as well.

He lost his reason after returning from England in 1357 and killed his knight Gerard van Wateringe. His brother Albert became regent in 1358, and William spent his last three decades confined at Le Quesnoy.

威廉·维特尔斯巴赫（1330—1389）是皇帝路德维希四世与埃诺的玛格丽特的次子，任巴伐利亚-施特劳宾公爵，兼荷兰、埃诺和泽兰伯爵。他的统治从与亲生母亲的战争开始：1350年荷兰贵族请玛格丽特回国，鳕鱼派与鱼钩派相继结盟，内战爆发。

爱德华三世出面相助，但1351年威廉在费勒海战失利后，又在兹瓦尔特瓦尔获胜。1354年母亲承认他为荷兰和泽兰伯爵，1356年她去世，埃诺也归他所有。

1357年他从英格兰返回后精神失常，杀死骑士赫拉德·范·瓦特灵厄。1358年起由弟弟阿尔布雷希特摄政，威廉余生的三十年被囚禁在勒凯努瓦城堡。

en:
William of Ockham (c. 1287–1347) was an English Franciscan friar and theologian, and to the nominalists one of the founders of their movement. He joined the Franciscans young, studied at the London school and Oxford, and never held a master’s chair, so was known as the ‘venerable beginner’. His Sentences lectures of 1317–1319 were followed by commentaries on Aristotle and Summary of Logic.

His razor tells thinkers to prefer fewest assumptions; the Latin wording, ‘entities must not be multiplied beyond necessity’, he never used. In 1324 John XXII summoned him to Avignon. A committee of theologians reviewed suspect passages without verdict.

Michael of Cesena asked him to study the bulls; he found them heretical. He slipped out of Avignon in May 1328, was excommunicated, and took refuge in Munich with Emperor Louis IV. He wrote political writings and died in April 1347 before the Black Death reached Munich.

奥卡姆的威廉（约1287—1347）是英格兰方济各会修士、神学家，唯名论者把他视为本派的奠基人之一。他年轻时加入方济各会，先后在会里的伦敦学校和牛津求学，却从未出任正式讲席教授，因此长期被称为“可敬的初学者”。约1317—1319年他讲授《箴言书》，其后写下对亚里士多德的评注以及《逻辑大全》。

以他命名的“剃刀”要求思想者选取假设最少的解释；其拉丁文表述“如无必要，勿增实体”，他本人从未用过。1324年，约翰二十二世召他到阿维尼翁，神学家委员会审查了可疑段落，却始终没有作出结论。

他为切塞纳的米凯莱研究教皇约翰二十二世的诏书，在其中看出许多异端之处。1328年5月他逃离阿维尼翁，被开除教籍，遂在慕尼黑受皇帝路德维希四世庇护。此后他转而撰写政治论著，1347年4月死于黑死病传到慕尼黑之前不久。

en:
Albert II of Hohenlohe-Uffenheim (c. 1250–1312) was a Franconian nobleman, lord of Hohenlohe and Uffenheim-Speckfeld, and the eldest son of Godfrey of Hohenlohe-Uffenheim and Elisabeth of Zollern. In 1289 he married Adelaide of Berg-Schelklingen.

At a Nuremberg tournament in 1290 his lance struck Louis of Bavaria, who died of the wound ten days later. Albert ruled the Uffenheim line until 1312; his son Louis succeeded him, and two younger sons became bishops of Bamberg and Würzburg.

阿尔布雷希特二世·冯·霍恩洛厄-乌芬海姆（约1250—1312年）是法兰克尼亚贵族、霍恩洛厄与乌芬海姆-施佩克费尔德领主，为乌芬海姆的戈特弗里德与伊丽莎白·冯·措伦的长子。1289年，他娶阿德尔海德·冯·贝格-舍尔克林根为妻。

1290年在纽伦堡的骑士比武中，他的长矛刺中巴伐利亚的路德维希，后者十天后伤重而死。阿尔布雷希特统治乌芬海姆支系直至1312年，子路德维希继位，另有两个幼子分别成为班贝格与维尔茨堡主教。

en:
Godfrey I of Hohenlohe (c. 1190–1254 or 1255) was a Franconian nobleman, knight and poet in Staufer service. Eldest son of Henry of Hohenlohe, he ruled the family lands around Weikersheim from about 1215 and joined Emperor Frederick II's court in 1220.

Rewarded for loyalty against the rebel King Henry VII, he received Langenburg Castle in 1235 and the county of Romagna. From 1237 to 1246 he led young King Conrad IV's privy council, effectively governing the empire north of the Alps.

Kraft I of Hohenlohe-Weikersheim (c. 1240–1313) was a Franconian nobleman and knight, a son of Godfrey I through whom all Hohenlohe lines living after 1412 descend. First documented in 1256, he consolidated the family estates around Weikersheim and Langenburg.

During the Interregnum he served the bishop of Würzburg. From 1273 he served King Rudolf of Habsburg, joining his 1276 Vienna campaign and fighting in Rudolf's 1278 victory over Ottokar of Bohemia on the Marchfeld.

en:
Ulaghchi Khan (died 1257) was the third ruler of the Golden Horde, succeeding Sartaq Khan for less than a year in 1257. A direct descendant of Batu, he was either Sartaq's son or younger brother. The great khan Möngke nominated him while he was still a child, and Batu's senior widow Boraqchin governed as regent.

Ulaghchi died before he could rule in person, and the throne passed to Batu's brother Berke. Berke later had Boraqchin executed for treason after she sought Hulagu's protection.

乌剌黑赤汗（？—1257）是金帐汗国第三位统治者，1257年继撒里答之位，在位不足一年。他是拔都的直系后裔，或为撒里答之子，或为其弟。大汗蒙哥册立他时，他年纪尚幼，由拔都的长妻博剌克真摄政。

en:
Ulman Stromer (1329–1407) was a Nuremberg merchant and councillor, son of the trader Heinrich Stromer. Trained in Barcelona, Genoa, Milan and Kraków, he began recording family, business and political events in his notebook in 1360, and in 1370 took over the family wholesale house, running a trade network from Barcelona to Riga and the Sea of Azov.

A councillor from 1371, in the Cities' War of 1387 to 1389 he brought Nuremberg into the Swabian-Rhenish League. In 1390 he converted the Gleissmühle into the first paper mill north of the Alps, bringing Italian papermakers north. He died of plague in 1407.

en:
Elizabeth de Burgh (1332–1363), fourth Countess of Ulster, was born at Carrickfergus Castle, the only child of William Donn de Burgh, Earl of Ulster. Her father's murder in 1333 left her countess at eleven months, while de Burgh kinsmen seized the Irish lands in the Burke Civil War.

She married Edward III's son Lionel of Antwerp at the Tower of London in 1342; Geoffrey Chaucer was her page. Their daughter Philippa, born in 1355, inherited Ulster and married Edmund Mortimer. She died in Dublin in 1363 and was buried at Bruisyard Abbey.

伊丽莎白·德·伯格（1332—1363）是第四代阿尔斯特女伯爵，生于卡里克弗格斯城堡，为第三代阿尔斯特伯爵威廉·唐·德·伯格的独女。1333年父亲遇刺后，年仅11个月的她继承伯爵爵位，而德·伯格亲族趁伯格内战实际占有了爱尔兰的领地。

1342年她在伦敦塔嫁给爱德华三世之子安特卫普的莱昂内尔，杰弗里·乔叟曾做她的侍童。独女菲莉琶1355年出生，后继承阿尔斯特并嫁给埃德蒙·莫蒂默。1363年她在都柏林去世，葬于布鲁西亚德修道院。

Richard Óg de Burgh, 2nd Earl of Ulster, called the Red Earl, was the most powerful Anglo-Norman noble in Ireland of his age, succeeding his father Walter in 1271. In 1294 the Earl of Kildare imprisoned him until parliament procured his release.

Although his daughter Elizabeth married Robert the Bruce, he campaigned in Scotland for Edward I. He was defeated by Edward Bruce at Connor in 1315, but recovered Ulster after Bruce fell at Faughart in 1318. He died in 1326.

Walter de Burgh, 1st Earl of Ulster (c. 1210–1271), was an Irish peer of the House of Burgh and the second son of Richard Mór de Burgh, Lord of Connacht. He succeeded to his father's Connacht lands in 1243, and in 1263 was created Earl of Ulster.

In 1270 he and the justiciar were defeated at Áth an Chip by Aedh mac Felim Ua Conchobair. He died in 1271 and was succeeded by his son Richard Óg, the Red Earl.

William Donn de Burgh (1312–1333), grandson of Richard Óg de Burgh, inherited the earldom of Ulster and was also lord of Connacht. He became Lieutenant of Ireland in 1331, and the next year had his cousin Walter Liath de Burgh starved to death at Greencastle.

Walter's kin took revenge: in 1333 they murdered William near Carrickfergus, led by Richard de Mandeville. His death plunged the de Burghs into the Burke Civil War. His infant daughter Elizabeth by Maud of Lancaster later married Lionel of Antwerp.
