en:
Domnall Ruadh Ó Máille (died 11 November 1337) ruled Umaill, the Ó Máille seafaring kingdom around Clew Bay in modern County Mayo, during the 1330s. A son of Brian mac Domnall, he had at least three sons, Cormac, Brian and Tadhg.

The Burke Civil War brought warfare to Connacht, and on St Martin's Night 1337 he and his son Cormac were slain by Clann-Merrick and other Englishmen. His own line soon lost the chiefship to the descendants of his nephew Eoghan mac Diarmait.

Eoghan mac Diarmait Ó Máille was a fourteenth-century member of the Ó Máille family, son of Diarmait and nephew of Domnall Ruadh Ó Máille, King of Umaill.

en:
Bonconte I da Montefeltro (c. 1170–1241/2) was an imperial nobleman of the House of Montefeltro and its first count of Urbino. In 1226 Emperor Frederick II, with Pope Honorius III's agreement, made Bonconte and his brother Taddeo counts of Urbino. A staunch Ghibelline, he attended the imperial diet at Ravenna that year, though Urbino did not accept its new counts until 1233–1234.

He aided Ravenna against Faenza of the Lombard League in 1235–1236 and served repeatedly as podestà of Città di Castello, apparently seeking to become its effective lord. He was at the siege of Faenza in December 1240 and died the next year or in early 1242.

布翁孔特一世·达·蒙特费尔特罗（约1170—1241/1242）是蒙特费尔特罗家族的帝国贵族，也是该支系首任乌尔比诺伯爵。1226年，皇帝腓特烈二世在教宗洪诺留三世同意下，册封布翁孔特及其兄弟塔代奥为乌尔比诺伯爵。作为坚定的吉伯林派，他于同年出席拉文纳帝国议会，但乌尔比诺直到1233—1234年才接受新伯爵。

1235—1236年他协助拉文纳对抗伦巴第同盟城市法恩扎，并多次出任卡斯泰洛城的行政长官，显然意图成为该城的实际领主。1240年12月他随军围攻法恩扎，于次年或1242年初去世。

en:
Federico I da Montefeltro (c. 1250–1322) was a Ghibelline condottiere and count of Urbino, eldest son of Guido I. As podestà of Arezzo he defeated the Guelphs of Florence and Siena at Cennina in 1303, and in 1305 formed the League of the Friends of the March.

He defeated the Malatesta in 1307 and conquered Ancona as podestà of Pisa in 1309; in 1310 Emperor Henry VII named him captain-general of the imperial army's Italian troops. He retook Urbino and Fano from the papalists in 1317, but in a popular revolt in Urbino he surrendered and begged for mercy, and he and his son Guido were killed on 26 April 1322.

Federico II Paolo Novello da Montefeltro (died c. 1370) was count of Urbino from 1364 until his death. He was the son of Nolfo da Montefeltro and Margherita Gabrielli, daughter of Cante Gabrielli, lord of Gubbio.

In 1360 he fought against the papal army led by Anichino di Bongardo. He married Teodora Gonzaga, daughter of the condottiero Ugolino Gonzaga, and had four sons; his son Antonio II succeeded him as count of Urbino.

en:
Guido I da Montefeltro (1223–1298), nicknamed the Old, was a Ghibelline military leader and count of Montefeltro, son of Montefeltrano II. In 1275 he led the Romagna Ghibellines to victory over the Guelphs and drove the Malatesta of Rimini from Cesena. As captain of Forlì he directed the city's defence against the papal siege of 1282–1283.

Forlì eventually fell and Guido accepted Pope Honorius IV's authority in 1286. Excommunicated in 1288, he captained Pisa's Ghibellines against Florence; reconciled in 1296, he joined the Franciscans and died at Ancona in 1298.

Guido II da Montefeltro, known as Novello, was a Ghibelline condottiero and count of Urbino, son of Count Federico I. When his father was killed in the Urbino revolt of 26 April 1322, he took refuge in Gubbio; in 1323 he returned to Urbino after two years of papal rule.

He ruled as count of Urbino from 1324 to 1360 and in 1341 served the Florentines against Lucca. He married Gentile Brancaleoni, who bore him no children.

en:
Montefeltrano II da Montefeltro (died 1255) was an Italian condottiero of the Ghibelline House of Montefeltro and the son of Bonconte I, first count of Urbino. He fought for Philip of Swabia in Sicily and was rewarded by Philip and Emperor Frederick II; in 1216 his possession of Montefeltro was confirmed.

From his father's death in 1242 he ruled Urbino as its lord and held the county of Montefeltro. He died in 1255 and was succeeded by his son Guido I.

Paolo Montefeltro was a son of Galasso Montefeltro, imperial vicar of Urbino, and belonged to the Guelph party. In 1364 he was associated in the government of Urbino together with his cousins Galasso, Antonio II and Nolfo II, ruling with them until 1369.

en:
Nolfo da Montefeltro (born Sighinolfo; c. 1290–1364), son of Federico I, was count of Montefeltro from 1323 to 1360. In 1323, as a Ghibelline leader in the Marche, he defeated a papal army and retook Urbino; his first act as lord was to have his father's enemies killed. In 1333 he became an adviser to John of Bohemia and a captain of the papal army.

He took the fortress of San Leo and occupied Lucca for Pisa in 1342. In 1348 he commanded Venice's army against Gorizia and was made imperial vicar of Urbino; in 1351 Giovanni Visconti of Milan hired him and he took Cagli the next year.

Then the papal commander Albornoz pushed him back in 1354. Nolfo made peace and ruled as papal vicar until his death.

Guy of Avesnes (c. 1253–1317), younger son of John I of Avesnes, was bishop of Utrecht from 1301 to 1317, appointed through his brother John II, count of Hainaut and Holland.

In 1304, while leading Flemish troops against his brother, he was captured at the Battle of Duiveland; in his absence the Fresingen seized power in Utrecht with guild support. He subdued the city in 1305 and granted town privileges to Amsterdam in 1306, attended the Council of Vienne in 1311 and was buried in Utrecht Cathedral after his death on 23 May 1317.

en:
Jan van Diest (died 1340) was bishop of Utrecht from 1322 to 1340. Born into a noble Brabantine family, he became provost of Cambrai before William III of Holland and Reginald II of Guelders backed him for the see; when the Utrecht chapters elected someone else, Pope John XXII annulled the election and consecrated him at Avignon.

His rule was marked by debt, nepotism and dependence on the two counts, who in 1331 even planned to partition the Sticht until local resistance saved the independence of the see. He was buried in the Dom Church of Utrecht.

Basalawarmi (died January 6, 1382), Prince of Liang, was the son of Bolot and a great-great-grandson of Kublai Khan. He held Yunnan for the Yuan; after the court fled north in 1368 he stayed loyal to the Northern Yuan.

In 1364 Dali troops helped him repel an invasion from the Ming Xia state, and in 1374 he executed a Ming envoy. In 1381 the Hongwu Emperor sent an army against him and crushed his forces. On January 6, 1382, he had his wife drowned in Dian Lake and killed himself.

en:
Sébastien Le Prestre de Vauban (1633–1707) was the foremost military engineer of Louis XIV's France. After serving the prince of Condé during the Fronde he was captured in 1653, joined the royal army and became ingénieur du roi in 1655, later fortifying newly acquired towns including Dunkirk.

He directed the sieges of Maastricht (1673) and Luxembourg (1684), remodelled more than a hundred fortresses and girdled France's northern frontier with his ceinture de fer. Louis XIV made him a marshal of France in 1703, the first engineer so honoured. His last tract, La Dîme royale, proposed a single tax on all estates and was destroyed by royal decree.

Sébastien Le Prestre de Vauban (1633–1707) was the foremost military engineer of Louis XIV's France. After serving the prince of Condé during the Fronde he was captured in 1653, joined the royal army and became ingénieur du roi in 1655, later fortifying newly acquired towns including Dunkirk.

He directed the sieges of [ShowLocationName('maastricht')] (1673) and [ShowLocationName('luxembourg')] (1684), remodelled more than a hundred fortresses and girdled [GetCountry('FRA').GetName]'s northern frontier with his ceinture de fer. Louis XIV made him a marshal of France in 1703, the first engineer so honoured. His last tract, La Dîme royale, proposed a single tax on all estates and was destroyed by royal decree.
zh:
塞巴斯蒂安·勒普雷斯特·德·沃邦（1633—1707）是路易十四时代法国首屈一指的军事工程师。投石党乱期间，他先在孔代亲王麾下效力，1653年被俘后转入王军，1655年成为国王御用工程师，战后加固了包括敦刻尔克在内的新占城镇。

他指挥了1673年马斯特里赫特围城战和1684年卢森堡围城战，改建了上百座要塞，并以“铁腰带”堡垒群拱卫法国北部边境。1703年，路易十四封他为法国元帅，他也是首位获此殊荣的工程师。晚年所著《王家什一税》主张向所有等级征收统一赋税，后来被王室下令销毁。

en:
Algirdas (c. 1296–1377), a son of Gediminas, became prince of Vitebsk through his marriage to its ruling princess, Maria. In 1345 he and his brother Kęstutis deposed their brother Jaunutis, and Algirdas became grand duke of Lithuania, ruling the east while Kęstutis guarded the west.

In 1362 he shattered the Golden Horde at the Battle of Blue Waters and extended Lithuanian rule to the Black Sea. He marched on Moscow three times between 1368 and 1372 without taking the city. He died in 1377 and was cremated with his horses in pagan rites, leaving the throne to Jogaila.

en:
Andrei of Polotsk (c. 1325–1399), eldest son of Grand Duke Algirdas and Maria of Vitebsk, ruled Polotsk from 1342 and Pskov until 1348. He campaigned against the Livonian Order and joined his father's marches on Moscow in 1368 and 1370. When Algirdas died in 1377, the throne passed to his half-brother Jogaila.

Andrei contested it, fighting for Dmitry of Moscow at Kulikovo in 1380 and later allying with the Teutonic Order against the Union of Krewo. Captured at Polotsk in 1387, he was imprisoned in Poland and later fell fighting the Tatars at the Vorskla River in 1399.

波洛茨克的安德烈（约1325—1399）是立陶宛大公阿尔吉尔达斯与维捷布斯克的玛丽亚的长子，1342年起统治波洛茨克，并领有普斯科夫至1348年。他长年在西疆与利沃尼亚骑士团作战，又在1368和1370年随父亲进军莫斯科。1377年阿尔吉尔达斯去世后，大公之位传给了他的异母弟约盖拉。

安德烈起兵争位，1380年在库里科沃之战中投身莫斯科的德米特里一方，后来又联合条顿骑士团反对克雷沃联合。1387年他在波洛茨克被俘，囚禁于波兰，获释后于1399年在沃尔斯克拉河与鞑靼人作战时阵亡。

en:
Briachislav Vasilkovich (died after 1241) was a Vitebsk-line prince who ruled Vitebsk from about 1221 and Polotsk from about 1232, probably a son of Vasilko Bryacheslavich and a daughter of Davyd of Smolensk.

Tradition credits him with founding three churches in Polotsk in 1203, dedicated to Holy Wisdom, Saints Boris and Gleb, and Paraskeva Pyatnitsa. In 1239 the chronicles show the future Alexander Nevsky marrying his daughter at Polotsk. He was still ruling Polotsk after 1241.

en:
Bryachislav Vasilkovich (died after 1186) was a Polotsk-branch Rurikid who held Iziaslavl and twice ruled Vitebsk. Around 1159 Prince Rogvolod Borisovich of Polotsk granted him Iziaslavl, which he held with his brother Volodsha, until the Glebovichi princes of Minsk captured the brothers; Rogvolod freed Bryachislav in 1160.

In 1162 he joined the Polotsk princes' campaign to Slutsk against Dorogobuzh, and in 1180, ruling Vitebsk, he fought at Drutsk for the Kiev prince Svyatoslav Vsevolodovich.

en:
Constantine (died c. 1390), by tradition a son of Algirdas of Lithuania, was a Gediminid prince and founder of the Czartoryski family. He led a Lithuanian banner at the Battle of Blue Waters in 1362, which broke the Golden Horde and won Podolia for Lithuania. Made the first prince of Podolia and ruling from Smotrych, he struck his own coinage bearing Saint George.

After Jogaila accepted the Union of Krewo in 1385, Constantine withdrew to Hungary, where he died between 1388 and 1392. His sons founded the Czartoryski line.

康斯坦丁（约1390年卒）按传统说法是立陶宛的阿尔吉尔达斯之子，格迪米纳斯家族王公，恰尔托雷斯基家族的始祖。1362年，他率领一支立陶宛部队参加蓝水之役，此战击溃金帐汗国，为立陶宛夺得波多利亚。他成为首任波多利亚王公，驻跸斯莫特里奇，并铸造了带有圣乔治像的钱币。

en:
Dmitry of Bryansk, or Dmitry the Elder (1327–1399), was the second son of Algirdas of Lithuania and Maria of Vitebsk. In 1356 his father took Bryansk from Smolensk and enfeoffed him with it. He repulsed Dmitry Donskoy's attack in 1370.

After Algirdas died in 1377, he backed his brother Andrei of Polotsk against Jogaila, withdrew to Moscow in 1379 and fought at Kulikovo in 1380. Reconciled with Jogaila in 1388, he returned to Bryansk and fell beside Andrei at the Vorskla River in 1399. His son Michael founded the Trubetskoy family.

en: Iziaslav Bryachislavich (died c. 1264) was a Vitebsk-line Rurikid, a son of Bryachislav Vasilkovich of Polotsk. Vitebsk prince lists suggest that he ruled from 1232 to 1262 and again in 1264, after Konstantin Bezruky's brief tenure. His son Iziaslav died in 1265.

en:
Maria of Vitebsk (c. 1300–c. 1346), also called Maria Yaroslavna, was the only child and heir of Yaroslav Vasilkovich, the last prince of Vitebsk. Around 1318 she married Algirdas, a son of Grand Duke Gediminas of Lithuania, and through her inheritance the Principality of Vitebsk passed to the Gediminids.

She bore Algirdas at least five sons, among them Andrei of Polotsk, Dmitry of Bryansk and Constantine, all baptized in the Orthodox rite, and their descendants included several princely houses. After her death Algirdas took as his second wife Uliana of Tver.

zh:
维捷布斯克的玛丽亚（约1300—约1346），又称玛丽亚·雅罗斯拉夫娜，是维捷布斯克末代王公雅罗斯拉夫·瓦西里科维奇的独女与继承人。约1318年，她嫁给立陶宛大公格迪米纳斯之子阿尔吉尔达斯，维捷布斯克公国也因她的继承关系转入格迪米纳斯家族手中。

她为阿尔吉尔达斯生下至少五个儿子，其中包括波洛茨克的安德烈、布良斯克的德米特里和康斯坦丁，诸子皆受东正教洗礼，后裔中包括多个王公世家。她去世后，阿尔吉尔达斯续娶特维尔的乌莉安娜。

en:
Mikhail Konstantinovich was prince of Vitebsk from the 1270s to the 1280s. He was a son of Konstantin Bezruky, prince of Polotsk and Vitebsk, and a brother of Yuri, prince of Rzhev, Fominsk and Berezuy.

In an undated letter written between 1271 and 1289, the aldermen and citizens of Riga accused him of unfair judgments against Riga merchants and of coercive dealings with them. Mikhail died before 1307.

米哈伊尔·康斯坦丁诺维奇于1270年代至1280年代任维捷布斯克王公，是波洛茨克兼维捷布斯克王公无臂者康斯坦丁之子，尔热夫、福明斯克与别列祖伊王公尤里的兄弟。

en:
Svyatoslav Vseslavich (Christian name Georgy; died after 1129) was a Rurikid prince of Polotsk, one of the younger sons of Vseslav Briachislavich. When the Polotsk land was divided on his father's death in 1101, he may have received Vitebsk, as historians infer from his grandsons' rule there. His daughter Predslava became the monastic saint Euphrosyne of Polotsk.

In 1129 Mstislav Vladimirovich of Kiev campaigned against Polotsk, captured Svyatoslav and exiled him to Constantinople, where all trace of him is lost.

斯维亚托斯拉夫·弗谢斯拉维奇（教名格奥尔基，1129年后去世）是波洛茨克的留里克王公，弗谢斯拉夫·布里亚奇斯拉维奇的幼子之一。1101年父亲去世后波洛茨克领地被诸子瓜分，他可能分得维捷布斯克，历史学家根据他的孙辈曾在此统治作出这一推断。他的女儿普列德斯拉瓦出家后成为波洛茨克的圣欧福新。

1129年，基辅的姆斯季斯拉夫·弗拉基米罗维奇征讨波洛茨克，将他俘获并流放君士坦丁堡，此后便下落不明。

en:
Vasilko Bryacheslavich (died after 1209, around 1221 by tradition) was prince of Vitebsk from 1186, a son of Bryachislav Vasilkovich. In 1180 he fought beside his father at the Olegovichi siege of Drutsk, and in 1186 took the Vitebsk throne with backing from his father-in-law Davyd of Smolensk.

In 1209 Grand Prince Vsevolod the Big Nest of Vladimir married Vasilko's daughter Liubava as his second wife. His son Bryachislav succeeded him.

en:
Vyacheslav, called Vyachko, Sviatoslavich (died 1167 or 1173) was a prince of Vitebsk, the son of Svyatoslav Vseslavich and Sofia Vladimirovna. In 1129 the grand prince of Kiev exiled the Polotsk princes to Byzantium; Vyachko and his kinsman Vasilko returned only in 1131 or 1132. He occupied the Vitebsk throne in 1162.

Around 1167 he escorted his sister Euphrosyne of Polotsk on her pilgrimage, and she tonsured his two daughters. His last chronicle appearance found him aiding Novgorod in 1167.

维亚切斯拉夫（昵称维亚奇科）·斯维亚托斯拉维奇（1167或1173年卒）是维捷布斯克王公，斯维亚托斯拉夫·弗谢斯拉维奇与索菲娅·弗拉基米罗芙娜之子。1129年基辅大公将波洛茨克诸王公放逐到拜占庭，维亚奇科与同族瓦西里科直到1131或1132年才返回。他于1162年登上维捷布斯克公位。

en:
Vseslav Vasilkovich (died c. 1186) was a Polotsk-branch Rurikid prince who held Vitebsk from 1132 and Polotsk. In 1162, after the prince of Drutsk fled his defeat by Minsk, the Polotsk veche invited Vseslav to rule. Married to a daughter of the prince of Smolensk, he leaned on Smolensk support and handed Vitebsk to Davyd Rostislavich in 1164.

Volodar drove him out in 1167, but Smolensk intervention restored him. He campaigned against Novgorod in 1170 and against Drutsk around 1180.

弗谢斯拉夫·瓦西里科维奇（约1186年卒）是留里克王朝波洛茨克支系王公，1132年起领有维捷布斯克，亦曾统治波洛茨克。1162年，德鲁茨克王公被明斯克击败出逃，波洛茨克韦彻遂邀请弗谢斯拉夫入主。他娶斯摩棱斯克王公之女，倚仗斯摩棱斯克支持，1164年把维捷布斯克交给达维德·罗斯季斯拉维奇。

1167年他被沃洛达里逐走，靠斯摩棱斯克出兵复位；1170年随军征讨诺夫哥罗德，约1180年合攻德鲁茨克。

en:
Yaroslav Vasilkovich is a putative prince named in the Genealogy of the Princes of Vitebsk as the last appanage prince of Vitebsk, who died in 1320. The chronicle, compiled no earlier than the sixteenth century, relates that he had no sons and in 1318 married his daughter Maria to the Lithuanian prince Algirdas.

The marriage legitimized Lithuanian rule over Vitebsk. The principality gradually lost its independence and in 1393 became the Vitebsk Voivodeship of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

雅罗斯拉夫·瓦西里科维奇是一位存在存疑的王公，《维捷布斯克王公谱系》记他为维捷布斯克末代封邑王公，卒于1320年。这部不早于16世纪编成的谱系称，他没有儿子，便于1318年将女儿玛丽亚嫁给立陶宛王公阿尔吉尔达斯。

这一联姻使立陶宛对维捷布斯克的统治获得合法性。维捷布斯克公国逐渐失去独立，于1393年成为立陶宛大公国的维捷布斯克省。

en:
Alix of Brittany (1297–1377) was a daughter of Arthur II, Duke of Brittany, and Yolande de Dreux. In 1320 she married Bouchard VI of the House of Montoire, count of Vendôme and Castres, and was his countess until his death in 1354.

Their children included John VI, who succeeded to Vendôme, Peter, killed at Poitiers in 1356, Bouchard, lord of Segré, and Eleanor, who married the count of Périgord. Alix then lived another twenty-three years as dowager countess, until her death in 1377, outliving her son John and seeing the county pass to her granddaughter Catherine.

zh:
布列塔尼的阿莉克丝（1297—1377）是布列塔尼公爵阿蒂尔二世与德勒的约朗德之女。1320年，她嫁给蒙图瓦尔家族的旺多姆兼卡斯特尔伯爵布沙尔六世，在1354年丈夫去世前一直担任伯爵夫人。

她的子女包括承袭旺多姆的约翰六世、1356年战死于普瓦捷的皮埃尔、塞格雷领主布沙尔，以及嫁给佩里戈尔伯爵的埃莱奥诺尔。此后她作为伯爵遗孀又度过了二十三年，1377年去世，历经儿子约翰六世早逝，看着伯国传到孙女凯瑟琳手中。

Bouchard of Vendôme, lord of Segré, was a younger son of Count Bouchard VI of Vendôme and Alix of Brittany. While his brother John VI inherited the county, he received Segré and other Angevin border lordships.

Around 1350 he married Marguerite of Beaumont-Brienne, heiress of Le Lude and Martigné-Ferchaud, which she brought to him. Their son John carried on the Vendôme-Segré line, which kept Le Lude until 1429.

en:
Bouchard V de Vendôme (c. 1230–1271) ruled the county of Vendôme from 1249 as head of the Montoire-Vendôme dynasty, succeeding his father Peter. He married Marie de Roye, who bore him his heir Jean V.

A loyal vassal of Charles I of Anjou, king of Naples, he fought in Charles's campaigns before joining Louis IX on the crusade to Tunis in 1270. He died there of plague in 1271 and was buried at Vendôme in the collegiate church of Saint-Georges.

en:
Bouchard VI de Vendôme (c. 1290–1354), count of Vendôme and lord of Castres, was the son of John V and Eleanor of Montfort. He married Alice, daughter of Duke Arthur II of Brittany, and their son John VI succeeded him.

In 1320 he sold his minting rights to King Philip V, and in 1329 a treaty with the count of Blois fixed their border and reduced its enclaves. He was sent on a military mission to Flanders in 1353 and a diplomatic mission to Charles the Bad of Navarre the next winter, but died on 26 February 1354 and was buried in the collegiate church of Saint-Georges at Vendôme.

en:
Éléonore de Montfort was the daughter of Philippe II de Montfort, lord of Castres, and Jeanne de Lévis-Mirepoix. Around 1285 she married Jean V, Count of Vendôme, bringing him the lordship of Castres in Albigeois; Jean preferred to reside there, and the counts of Vendôme thereafter held Castres.

Her children included Bouchard VI, who succeeded his father in Vendôme and Castres in 1315, and Jeanne, who married Henri IV de Sully. She was still living after 1338.

en:
Guy de Montfort (died 31 January 1228) was a French crusader and lord of Castres, younger son of Simon III de Montfort. He took part in the Third Crusade and joined the Fourth in 1202, but after Zara refused the Byzantine bargain and sailed to the Holy Land, where he married Helvis of Ibelin in 1204 and ruled Sidon as regent until 1210.

Back in France he fought in the Albigensian Crusade, notably at Muret in 1213. Wounded at Toulouse in 1218, he saw his brother Simon killed coming to his aid, and Guy himself was killed at the siege of Varilhes in 1228.

居伊·德·蒙福尔（1228年1月31日卒）是法兰西十字军将领、卡斯特尔领主，西蒙三世·德·蒙福尔较年幼的儿子之一。他参加第三次十字军东征，1202年又参加第四次东征；在扎拉之后，他拒绝拜占庭方面的交易，自行渡海前往圣地，1204年娶伊贝林的埃尔维斯为妻，并摄政西顿领地直至1210年。

回到法兰西后，他投入阿尔比十字军，1213年在米雷作战。1218年在图卢兹他负伤，兄长西蒙前来救援时阵亡；居伊本人于1228年在围攻瓦里勒时阵亡。

en:
Helvis of Ibelin (after 1178–1214) was the elder daughter of Balian of Ibelin and Maria Komnene, widow of King Amalric of Jerusalem, and half-sister of Queen Isabella I.

During Saladin's siege of Jerusalem in 1187 she was escorted to safety in Tripoli. After her father negotiated the city's surrender the family went to Tyre, where they supported Conrad of Montferrat.

In 1190 she married Reginald, lord of Sidon; they had a son Balian, and she was widowed in 1202. In 1204 she married Guy of Montfort, and their son Philip became lord of Tyre.

埃尔维斯·德·伊贝林（1178年后—1214）是伊贝林的巴利安与耶路撒冷前王后玛丽亚·科穆宁娜的长女，也是女王伊莎贝拉一世同母异父的妹妹。

1187年萨拉丁围攻耶路撒冷时，她被送往的黎波里避难。父亲谈判交出耶路撒冷后，全家前往提尔，支持蒙费拉的康拉德。

1190年，她嫁给西顿领主雷纳德，生子巴利安，并于1202年丧夫。1204年她改嫁蒙福尔的居伊，二人的儿子腓力后来成为提尔领主。

en:
John IV of Montoire (Jean IV de Vendôme; died 1240) was a French baron who became the first count of Vendôme from the House of Montoire-Vendôme. He inherited Montoire and succeeded as count of Vendôme in 1217, ruling until 1239 or 1240.

The son of Peter II of Montoire and Agnes of Vendôme, John married Eglantine, by whom he had several children, including Peter, who succeeded him as count, and Geoffrey, lord of Lavardin.

en:
John V de Vendôme (c. 1260–1315) of the House of Montoire inherited the county of Vendôme from his father Bouchard V in 1271. In 1282 he campaigned in Apulia in the service of Charles I of Anjou.

Through his marriage to Eleanor of Montfort, daughter of the lord of Castres, he inherited Castres in 1300 along with the county of Squillace, and spent most of the rest of his life at Castres. He split the Vendômois into Upper and Lower Vendôme, making Montoire chief town of the latter, and his son Bouchard VI succeeded him.

en:
John VI of Vendôme (died 1364), son of Bouchard VI and Alix of Brittany, succeeded as count of Vendôme and Castres in 1354. He lived chiefly at Castres, raised to a county by King John II in 1356 for his loyalty to the Valois. He fought and was captured at Poitiers the same year.

In 1362 English and Gascon routiers seized Vendôme and captured his wife Joan of Ponthieu; he paid a ransom to recover the town. He died in February 1364 famed for his sanctity. By Joan he left Bouchard VII and Catherine, who brought Vendôme to the Bourbons.

zh:
旺多姆的约翰六世（1364年卒）是布沙尔六世与布列塔尼的阿莉克丝之子，1354年承袭旺多姆与卡斯特尔伯爵之位。他主要住在卡斯特尔，因效忠瓦卢瓦王室，卡斯特尔于1356年被法王约翰二世升格为伯国；同年他在普瓦捷战役中被俘。

1362年，英格兰与加斯科涅流兵攻占旺多姆，俘虏了他的妻子蓬蒂约的让娜；他支付赎金收回了城池。1364年2月他去世，时人以圣徒之名相称。他与让娜留下布沙尔七世和女儿凯瑟琳，凯瑟琳后来把旺多姆带入波旁家族。

en:
Philip II of Montfort (1225–1270) was a French nobleman, the son of Philip I of Montfort, lord of Tyre. He joined Charles of Anjou's conquest of the Kingdom of Sicily and shared command of the first battalion at the Battle of Benevento in 1266.

Afterwards he protected the Papal States with his forces, then led Angevin troops into Sicily and crushed the revolt that ended in the sack of Augusta. Created count of Squillace, he inherited Castres on his father's death in March 1270, then joined Louis IX's Eighth Crusade and died at Tunis on 24 September 1270.

菲利普二世·德·蒙福尔（1225—1270）是法兰西贵族，为提尔领主菲利普一世·德·蒙福尔之子。他参加安茹的查理征服西西里王国的战争，1266年在贝内文托战役中共同指挥前锋营。

战后他受命率军保护教宗国，继而率安茹军队进入西西里岛镇压叛乱，最终洗劫奥古斯塔。他受封斯奎拉切伯爵，1270年3月父亲死后继承卡斯特尔，随后加入路易九世的第八次十字军东征，1270年9月24日死于突尼斯。

en:
Peter of Vendôme (c. 1200–1249) was count of Vendôme from 1240 until his death, the son of Count John IV and Eglantine of Palluau. He married Joan of Mayenne and had four children, including his successor Burchard V and Geoffrey, lord of La Chartre-sur-le-Loir; another son entered the Church and died young while studying at Bologna.

Peter joined King Louis IX on the Seventh Crusade and died in Cyprus on 25 March 1249, before the campaign reached Egypt. His body was taken home and buried in the collegiate church of Saint-Georges at Vendôme.

旺多姆的皮埃尔（约1200—1249）是1240年至去世时的旺多姆伯爵，伯爵约翰四世与帕吕奥的埃格朗蒂娜之子。他娶马耶讷的让娜为妻，生有四个子女，包括继任伯爵的布沙尔五世和卢瓦河畔拉沙特尔领主若弗鲁瓦；另一个儿子进入教会，在博洛尼亚求学时早逝。

en:
Jean III de Sarrebruck-Commercy (died 1384 or 1385) was a son of Jean II and Alix de Joinville and sire of Commercy-Château-Haut. He had first chosen the Church and in 1352 is styled a canon of Toul and Verdun, but inherited Commercy when his brother Simon II died childless in 1355.

In 1358 he married Marie d'Arcelles, lady of Méry-sur-Seine. Their sons were Simon III, sire of Commercy, Jean, a bishop, and Amé I, ancestor of the later Saarbrücken-Commercy line.

en:
Simon II (or V) de Sarrebruck-Commercy (died 1355) was a son of Jean II and Alix de Joinville and held Commercy-Château-Haut as sire of Commercy.

In 1344 he settled with his cousin Jean IV the long-delayed partition of the inheritance of Jean I, taking the keep of Commercy, half the town and many villages, mills and woods, while justice and the town walls remained shared. He died without children in 1355 and his lands passed to his brother Jean III.

en:
Emicho was a Rhineland count of the Emichones kindred, holding Kyrburg and Schmidtburg and attested in charters from 1086 to 1113. Genealogies name him the father of Gerlach I, first count of Veldenz.

He may have been the same man as Emich of Flonheim, who raised a host for the People's Crusade in 1096 and led the massacre of the Jewish community of Mainz, the worst of the Rhineland massacres. His army marched on toward Hungary but broke up in clashes there, and he returned home in disgrace.

en:
Georg I von Veldenz (died 1347), son of Heinrich I von Hohengeroldseck and Agnes von Veldenz, inherited the County of Veldenz in 1298 through his mother's line. From 1309 he served the Empire as royal Landvogt in the Speyergau, and from 1321 held an imperial castle-fief at Kaiserslautern.

In 1315 King Louis IV allowed him to fortify Meisenheim and grant it town rights, and he enlarged Schloss Veldenz. He married Agnes von Leiningen; their son Heinrich II succeeded him, while another son, Friedrich I, died as early as 1327.

en:
Heinrich II von Veldenz (c. 1300–1378) was the second son of Count Georg I and Agnes von Leiningen. In 1330 he married Agnes von Sponheim, daughter of Count Simon II von Sponheim-Kreuznach. His elder brother Friedrich I died in 1327, and Heinrich inherited the County of Veldenz after Georg I died in 1347.

When Friedrich's unmarried son Georg II died in 1377, most of his branch's property passed to Heinrich. Heinrich died in 1378 and was succeeded by his son Heinrich III.

en:
Heinrich I von Geroldseck (c. 1252, died 1296–1298) was a son of Walter I von Geroldseck. When the Veldenz comital family died out in the male line with Count Gerlach V around 1259, Heinrich married Gerlach's heiress Agnes von Veldenz, and from 1270 styled himself count of Veldenz, founding the Geroldseck dynasty of the county.

By Agnes he fathered Georg I, who succeeded him, and Walram, bishop of Speyer from 1328. His own brother Walter served as bishop of Strasbourg.

en:
Almorò Gradenigo, also called Ermolao, was a Venetian nobleman and a son of Doge Bartolomeo Gradenigo. In 1339 an agreement among leading families secured Bartolomeo's election, and at the Giants' Staircase Almorò, youngest of the ducal councillors, placed the crown on his father's head and, as a laudatory biography tells it, wept with emotion.

After the doge's death in 1342, the Major Council barred a living doge's brothers, sons and nephews from public office, ending the favours Bartolomeo had arranged for his sons.

In the autumn of 1350 Almorò was one of five patricians who escorted and watched over King Louis I of Hungary, Venice's rival for Dalmatia, as he crossed Venetian territory returning from Naples. In 1356 he sat among the forty-one electors who chose Giovanni Dolfin as doge.

阿尔莫罗·格拉代尼戈（又名埃尔莫拉奥）是威尼斯贵族，总督巴托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈之子。1339年，几大家族达成协议促成巴托洛梅奥当选；在巨人阶梯上，作为最年轻的总督顾问，阿尔莫罗亲手为父亲戴上冠冕，据一部颂扬性传记记载，他当时感动落泪。

1342年总督去世后，大议会禁止在任总督的兄弟、儿子和侄子担任公职，巴托洛梅奥为诸子谋官的好处就此终止。

1350年秋，阿尔莫罗是五名贵族之一，在威尼斯在达尔马提亚的对手、匈牙利国王拉约什一世从那不勒斯返程途经威尼斯领土时，护送并监视其行程。1356年，他跻身选举乔瓦尼·多尔芬为总督的四十一名选举人之列。

en:
Alvica Gradenigo was a Venetian noblewoman, a granddaughter of Doge Pietro Gradenigo and the daughter of Nicolo Gradenigo; she is named in her grandfather's will of 1309. By 1335 she had married Marino Falier as his second wife, becoming dogaressa when he took office in 1354.

After Falier was executed for his coup attempt in 1355, the Council of Ten cleared her of complicity and returned her dowry of 4000 lire. During a long widowhood she traded and lent money, dying in 1387 or 1388 as one of the richest women in Venice.

en:
Andrea Contarini (c. 1300–1382) had twice avoided the dogeship before being chosen as Venice's sixtieth doge on 20 January 1368; he accepted only when told refusal meant perpetual exile and confiscation of his goods.

His dogeship was defined by the War of Chioggia against Genoa. After the defeat off Pola on 7 May 1379 the Genoese seized Chioggia; Contarini liquidated his fortune to fund the war and, though nearly eighty, took command of some of the ships. The imprisoned admiral Vettor Pisani was released with the last forty galleys, and Chioggia was retaken on 24 June 1380. The Peace of Turin in 1381 cost Venice Dalmatia, Treviso and Tenedos, and Contarini died on 5 June 1382.

安德烈亚·孔塔里尼（约1300—1382）曾两度躲过总督之位，1368年1月20日才当选威尼斯第六十任总督；他得知拒绝的代价是终身流放和没收家产，方才接受任命。

他任内的决定性事件是对热那亚的基奥贾战争。1379年5月7日威尼斯舰队在波拉外海战败，热那亚人攻占基奥贾；孔塔里尼变卖家产充作军饷，年近八旬仍亲自统率部分战船。被囚的海军将领维托尔·皮萨尼获释，受命指挥最后的四十艘桨帆船，1380年6月24日基奥贾收复。1381年《都灵和约》使威尼斯丢掉达尔马提亚、特雷维索和泰内多斯，他于1382年6月5日去世。

en:
Andrea Dandolo (30 April 1306 – 7 September 1354) was a Venetian noble from one of the republic's oldest families, which had already given it three doges. He probably studied law at Padua and became procurator of St Mark's around 1328, then was elected the fifty-fourth doge on 4 January 1343.

A friend and correspondent of Petrarch, he had the Pala d'Oro of St Mark's restored in 1343–1345, gathered the republic's treaties into the Liber Albus and Liber Blancus, and wrote the Chronica Extensa, a chronicle of Venice from its origins to 1280.

The Black Death of 1348 may have taken half of Venice; Zara revolted and a war with Genoa filled his last four years. He died in 1354, before it ended, and was buried in St Mark's Baptistery.

zh:
安德烈亚·丹多洛（1306年4月30日—1354年9月7日）出身威尼斯最古老的家族之一，该家族已出过三位总督。他可能在帕多瓦学习过法律，约1328年出任圣马可行政长官，1343年1月4日当选第五十四任总督。

他是彼特拉克的朋友和通信对象；1343—1345年主持修复圣马可大教堂的黄金祭坛屏，把共和国的条约汇编为《白皮书》与《白册》，并撰写了记述威尼斯起源至1280年历史的《详编编年史》。

1348年的黑死病可能夺走了威尼斯一半的人口，扎拉起兵叛乱，对热那亚的战争则占据了他生命的最后四年。他于1354年去世，战争尚未结束，葬于圣马可洗礼堂。

en:
Antonio Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman and one of at least eight sons of Doge Bartolomeo Gradenigo. In 1348 he held office as Venetian count of Arbe, an island in Dalmatia, the coast over which King Louis I of Hungary was then quarrelling with Venice.

His father had sought offices and favours for his sons so flagrantly that after the doge's death in December 1342 the Major Council denied office to a living doge's kin and banned the ducal family from private trade.

en:
Antonio Venier (c. 1330–1400), son of Nicolò Venier, came from a recently ennobled family with no famous ancestors or allies. He made his name in the wars against Genoa, serving around 1380 as provveditore of the Tenedos fortress and in 1381, on the eve of his election, as captain in Crete.

In October 1382 he became the 62nd Doge of Venice and held office until his death. He had a name as a rigid judge, and his reign bore it out: he was famed for incorruptibility and strict discipline.

In his eighteen years the economy recovered and flourished, alliances extended Venetian rule into the Veneto hinterland, and in his last years Venice first clashed with the Ottoman Empire. He died on 23 November 1400 and was buried at Santi Giovanni e Paolo.

安东尼奥·韦涅尔（约1330—1400）是尼科洛·韦涅尔之子，出身新晋贵族之家，没有显赫祖先或有力的政治盟友。他在对热那亚的战争中崭露头角，约1380年镇守特内多斯要塞，1381年当选总督前夕被派往克里特担任指挥官。

1382年10月，他成为第六十二任威尼斯总督，直至去世。他以断案严苛闻名，任期也印证了这一点：他以清廉和纪律严明著称。

十八年间，威尼斯经济复苏并趋于繁荣，结盟政策使统治扩展到威尼托内陆；任期最后几年，威尼斯与奥斯曼帝国首次发生冲突。他于1400年11月23日去世，葬于圣乔凡尼保罗大教堂。

en:
Antonio Zeno (c. 1330 – c. 1403) was a Venetian nobleman, brother of the navigator Nicolò Zeno and of Admiral Carlo Zeno. His fame rests on the Zeno narrative.

In 1558 their descendant Nicolò Zeno the Younger published a map and letters claiming that in the 1390s Antonio and Nicolò sailed the North Atlantic at the bidding of a prince named Zichmni. The map was adopted by Gerardus Mercator, and modern scholarship generally regards the documents as a sixteenth-century forgery.

安东尼奥·泽诺（约1330—约1403）是威尼斯贵族，航海家尼科洛·泽诺与海军将领卡洛·泽诺的兄弟。他的名声来自“泽诺兄弟航行记”。

1558年，他们的后裔小尼科洛·泽诺公布了一幅地图和若干信件，声称1390年代安东尼奥与尼科洛奉一位名为齐赫姆尼的亲王之命航行北大西洋。该地图曾被格拉杜斯·墨卡托采用，而现代学界普遍认为这些文献是16世纪的伪作。

en:
Bartolomeo Gradenigo (1263–1342) was the 53rd Doge of Venice, elected in November 1339. Born into an ancient noble family, he grew rich in Eastern trade, served as a podestà abroad and procurator in Venice, and was known for his love of luxury, likely spending part of his fortune to win goodwill before the election.

His three years were quiet: rapprochement with Genoa, a revolt in Crete, Turkish raids. Nicknamed ‘the wheeler-dealer doge’ for using his influence to enrich himself and his family, he saw the ducal councillors forbid the practice shortly before his death.

Legend ties his reign to a storm in 1340, calmed by Saints Mark, George and Nicholas, whom a poor fisherman ferried across the lagoon; they left him a ring for the doge. He died on 28 December 1342.

巴托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈（1263—1342）是威尼斯第五十三任总督，1339年11月当选，在任直至去世。他出身古老的贵族家庭，靠东方贸易发家，曾在外邦担任波德斯塔、在威尼斯担任检察官，以酷爱奢华著称；他很可能在选举前拿出一部分家财笼络人心。

他在位三年相当平静：与热那亚逐步修好，只有克里特叛乱和土耳其人的袭扰。他因利用影响力为自己和家族敛财，得了“爱钻营的总督”的绰号，去世前不久，总督顾问便禁止此类滥权行为。

传说1340年的一场大风暴与他的任期相连：圣马可、圣乔治和圣尼古拉由一名贫苦渔夫载过潟湖，平息了风浪，并留给渔夫一枚戒指转交总督。他于1342年12月28日去世。

en:
Benedetto Dolfin was a Venetian patrician, the son of Enrico Dolfin, born into one of the wealthiest houses of the Venetian nobility. He was active in politics after the closing of the Great Council in 1297 and became procurator of St Mark's de supra in 1300.

He foiled a conspiracy led by Marin Bocconio. His son Giovanni Dolfin, probably born around 1303, was elected doge of Venice in 1356.

Bernardo de' Rossi is recorded as a knight (cavaliere), the only son among the six children of the Parmese condottiero Pietro de' Rossi and Ginella Fieschi of Calestano.

en:
Carlo Zeno (1333–1418) was a Venetian admiral and hero of the war against Genoa. He served as a mercenary before entering Venetian service, and in 1380 brought eighteen galleys back to Venice in time to win the decisive Battle of Chioggia.

He defeated the Genoese at Modon in 1403 and overthrew Padua's Carraresi in 1405. Later convicted of treason by the Council of Ten, he lost his offices, spent a year in prison, and died in Venice in 1418, honoured with a public funeral.

卡洛·泽诺（1333—1418）是威尼斯海军将领，也是对热那亚战争中的英雄。他曾以雇佣军身份服役，后来进入威尼斯军队；1380年他率十八艘桨帆船赶回威尼斯，及时赢得决定性的基奥贾战役。

en:
Domenico I Contarini (c. 1008–1071), the first doge from the great Contarini family, ruled Venice from 1041 until his death. In 1044 his support helped the patriarchate of Grado win papal recognition of its independence from Aquileia.

He strengthened ties with Constantinople, receiving the Byzantine title of imperial patrician and becoming the first doge to hold the title of magister. Venice also reconquered Zadar and parts of Dalmatia from the Croatian kingdom, and in 1063 he began rebuilding St Mark's Basilica and founded San Nicolò al Lido, where he was buried after his death in 1071.

Domenico Dandolo (fl. 1085–1130s) was a Venetian merchant and head of the patrician Dandolo family. In 1085 he led an embassy to Constantinople, where Emperor Alexios I Komnenos issued a chrysobull granting the doge the title of protosebastos and the heritable rank of duke of Venice, Dalmatia and Croatia.

After Pietro Polani became doge in 1130, Dandolo served at the ducal court as judge and gastald. His son Vitale was a Venetian ambassador and fathered Doge Enrico Dandolo.

en:
Domenico Morosini (died 1156) was doge of the Republic of Venice from 1148 until his death. He first won distinction at the siege of Tyre in 1124. In 1147, as ambassador to Constantinople, he negotiated with Emperor Manuel I Komnenos an alliance against the Normans who had seized Corfu, securing renewed and expanded trading privileges for Venice.

Succeeding Pietro Polani as doge, he reconciled the patrician factions that had long divided the city. His reign brought peace and renewed prosperity, and he died in February 1156.

en:
Enrico Dandolo (c. 1107–1205), a blind Venetian nobleman, was elected doge in 1192. After Byzantium imprisoned thousands of Venetians in 1171, he joined the 1172 expedition that collapsed of plague. He later joined embassies to Constantinople and helped restore the Venetian quarter there in 1184.

In old age he led Venice into the Fourth Crusade: his fleet sacked rebellious Zara in 1202 and stormed Constantinople on 12 April 1204, winning Venice a vast colonial empire. He took the title of despot and died there in 1205, buried in Hagia Sophia.

恩里科·丹多洛（约1107—1205）是双目失明的威尼斯贵族，1192年当选总督。拜占庭于1171年囚禁数千名威尼斯人后，他参加了1172年那场因瘟疫瓦解的远征。此后他出使君士坦丁堡，于1184年促成拜占庭恢复威尼斯侨民区。

晚年他率领威尼斯投身第四次十字军东征：他的舰队1202年洗劫了反叛的扎拉，1204年4月12日攻陷君士坦丁堡，为威尼斯夺得了幅员辽阔的殖民帝国。他接受“专制君主”头衔，1205年死于当地，葬于圣索菲亚大教堂。

en:
Federico Cornaro (died 1382) was a Venetian patrician, merchant and diplomat. Trade with Cyprus made his fortune: King Peter I granted him the fief of Episkopi, which he made a major sugar plantation, and in 1365 he lent the king sixty thousand ducats. By 1379 he was the richest man in Venice.

In the War of Chioggia he secured Bernabò Visconti's alliance. In 1377 he married his son Pietro to Maria of Enghien, heiress of Argos and Nauplia, and ruled the lordship in the couple's name until his death. He was buried beside his brother Marco in the Frari church.

费德里科·科尔纳罗（1382年卒）是威尼斯贵族、商人兼外交官。对塞浦路斯的贸易成就了他的家产：塞浦路斯国王彼得一世将埃皮斯科皮采邑封给他，他把这里建成大型甘蔗种植园，1365年又向国王放贷6万杜卡特。到1379年，他已是威尼斯首富。

基奥贾战争期间，他争取到贝尔纳博·维斯孔蒂的同盟。1377年，他安排儿子彼得罗迎娶阿尔戈斯与纳夫普利翁的女继承人昂吉安的玛丽亚，并以这对夫妇的名义统治该领地，直至去世。他葬在弗拉里圣母堂兄弟马可的墓旁。

en:
Francesco Dandolo (c. 1258–1339), one of Venice's ablest diplomats, was ambassador at Avignon to Popes Clement V and John XXII. He won the nickname Cane, or dog, by appearing before the pope in a chain to plead for lifting Venice's excommunication.

Elected the fifty-second doge on 4 January 1329, he fought Mastino II della Scala of Verona for the Veneto trade routes, allying Venice with Florence and other cities against Verona's grip on river traffic.

The peace of 1337 to 1339 brought Treviso and Mestre under Venetian rule and launched Venice's expansion on the Italian mainland. Dandolo died on 1 November 1339 and was buried in the Frari.

弗朗切斯科·丹多洛（约1258—1339）是威尼斯最干练的外交家之一，曾出使阿维农，先后面见教皇克雷芒五世和约翰二十二世。他颈缠锁链出现在教皇面前，恳求解除对威尼斯的绝罚，由此得到“狗”的绰号。

1329年1月4日，他当选第五十二任总督，为控制威尼托商路同维罗纳领主马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉开战，并促成威尼斯与佛罗伦萨等城市结盟，对抗维罗纳对河运的把持。

1337至1339年达成的和约使特雷维索和梅斯特雷归入威尼斯，开启了威尼斯在意大利本土的扩张。他于1339年11月1日去世，葬于弗拉里荣耀圣母堂。

en:
Fresca de' Rossi was one of the six children of the Parmese condottiero Pietro de' Rossi and Ginella Fieschi of Calestano, who married in 1328.

Her sisters were Luchina, Teodora, Isabella and Luigia, and her only brother was the knight Bernardo. Her father, captain of Venice's anti-Scaliger league, was killed at the siege of Monselice in August 1337, when his children were still young.

en:
Giberto Dandolo (1220–1279) was a Venetian admiral of the San Moisè branch of the Dandolo family. In the spring of 1263 he led thirty-two galleys to Negroponte, threatened by Byzantine emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos, and off Settepozzi defeated a Genoese squadron, capturing four ships and killing its admiral.

From 1264 he served two years as captain and bailo at Negroponte, later sat six times in the Greater Council, and in 1278 was ambassador to Pope Nicholas III. He died in 1279, leaving a son Giovanni, who became doge in 1280.

吉尔贝托·丹多洛（1220—1279）是威尼斯海军将领，出身丹多洛家族的圣莫伊塞支系。1263年春，因内格罗蓬特受到拜占庭皇帝米海尔八世·巴列奥略的威胁，他率领三十二艘桨帆船驰援，并在塞特波齐击败一支热那亚舰队，俘获敌船四艘，击杀敌军将领。

1264年起，他以内格罗蓬特统领兼巴约的身份驻守两年，后来又六度进入大议会，1278年出使教皇尼古拉三世。他于1279年去世，其子乔瓦尼于1280年当选总督。

en:
Giovanni Cornaro (c. 1210 – after 1291) was a Venetian nobleman and diplomat of the Cornaro family. First recorded in 1238 as envoy to Pope Gregory IX over disputes with Genoa, he later served at Emperor Frederick II's court and helped elect Marino Morosini doge in 1249.

In 1274 he attended the Second Council of Lyon, and in 1291 led an embassy to his grandnephew King Andrew III of Hungary. His son Marco was grandfather of Doge Marco Cornaro.

en:
Giovanni Dandolo (c. 1240–1289), son of the admiral Giberto Dandolo, was elected the forty-eighth doge of Venice on 31 March 1280 while campaigning against Istria and Trieste. He had previously been podestà of Bologna and Padua and commanded Venetian naval forces.

His reign saw wars against Aquileia, the papal states and Ancona, and a Cretan revolt backed by Emperor Michael VIII. When Venice refused a papal attack on Sicily, Martin IV excommunicated the Republic, until Honorius IV lifted the sentence in 1285. In 1284 Dandolo issued Venice's first gold ducat. He died in 1289 and was buried at San Zanipolo.

en:
Giovanni Dolfin (c. 1303–1361) was the 57th Doge of Venice, elected on 13 August 1356 while defending Treviso against a besieging Hungarian army. Refused safe conduct, he broke through the encirclement to reach Venice for his enthronement.

As doge he kept fighting Louis I of Hungary, but defeat at Nervesa in 1358 forced the Treaty of Zadar, by which Venice lost Dalmatia, Zara and Split while keeping naval predominance in the Adriatic.

In 1358–1359 Padua forced Venice to stop trading with Egypt, deepening an economic crisis. Dolfin had lost one eye in battle, and he died in 1361 and was buried in San Giovanni e Paolo.

乔瓦尼·多尔芬（约1303—1361）是威尼斯第五十七任总督。1356年8月13日当选时，他正指挥守卫被匈牙利军队围困的特雷维索；敌人拒绝给予安全通行，他便突围返回威尼斯就任。

任内他继续与匈牙利国王拉约什一世作战，但1358年在内尔韦萨战败，被迫签订《扎达尔条约》，威尼斯丧失达尔马提亚、扎拉和斯普利特，仅保住亚得里亚海的海军优势。

1358—1359年，帕多瓦迫使威尼斯停止与埃及通商，加剧了经济危机。多尔芬曾在战斗中失去一只眼睛，他于1361年去世，葬于圣乔凡尼保罗大教堂。

en:
Giovanni Gradenigo (c. 1279–1356), nicknamed Nason for his large nose, became the 56th Doge of Venice on 21 April 1355, in the wake of Marino Falier's execution for treason. He was the son of Marino Gradenigo, duke of Candia, who died in Crete.

Gruff and austere, a man many avoided, he was known as fiercely loyal to the Republic after a career as a podestà on the mainland. In June, with the city frightened by conspiracies, he made peace with Genoa, ending a long, losing war, and tackled the Republic's money troubles.

War broke out again in 1356, a conflict his successor Giovanni Dolfin would end on bad terms at Zadar. Gradenigo died in August 1356, with little mark left on the state.

乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈（约1279—1356）因鼻子硕大得到绰号“大鼻子”，1355年4月21日在前任马里诺·法列罗因叛国被处斩之后，当选威尼斯第五十六任总督。他是马里诺·格拉代尼戈之子，父亲任康迪亚公爵时死于克里特。

他性情严厉粗粝，许多人对他避之不及，却以对共和国忠心耿耿著称；在大陆历任波德斯塔之后，这份忠诚成了他当选的最大筹码。6月，国内阴谋频发，人心惶惶，他与热那亚媾和，结束了长期而不利的战争，并着手应对共和国的财政困难。

1356年战火重燃，这场战争要到继任者乔瓦尼·多尔芬手里才以不利的条件在扎拉收场。格拉代尼戈于1356年8月去世，没有在国政上留下多少印记。

en:
Giovanni Gradenigo was one of at least eight sons of Doge Bartolomeo Gradenigo (r. 1339–1342), probably born to the doge's first wife from the Cappello family.

Barbaro's genealogy records for him a successful career in political, military and diplomatic offices. His brothers held posts from rector of Chioggia to count of Traù, and such nepotism led the Great Council after 1342 to bar future doges from appointing their sons.

en:
Giovanni Soranzo (c. 1245–1328), a former admiral and diplomat, was elected the 51st Doge of Venice on 13 July 1312. In 1296, during the war with Genoa, he led a fleet to the Bosphorus, captured an enemy galley and raided Caffa in Crimea.

As podestà of Ferrara in 1308–1309 he faced Pope Clement V, who placed Venice under interdict before taking the city, and he failed to recover the lower Po. In 1310, after the failed Tiepolo conspiracy, he negotiated Baiamonte Tiepolo's surrender. His dogate repaired relations with the papacy, and he received Dante in Venice in 1321.

乔瓦尼·索兰佐（约1245—1328）曾任舰队司令与外交官，1312年7月13日当选第五十一任威尼斯总督。1296年对热那亚作战期间，他率舰队驶向博斯普鲁斯海峡，俘获一艘敌舰，并劫掠了克里米亚的卡法。

1308至1309年他出任费拉拉长官，与教皇克雷芒五世对峙；教皇先对威尼斯施以禁罚，随后夺取该城，他收复波河下游的尝试也告失败。1310年蒂耶波洛阴谋失败后，他与巴亚蒙特·蒂耶波洛谈判，促成其投降。他任内修复了威尼斯与教廷的关系，并于1321年在威尼斯接待了但丁。

en:
Isabella de' Rossi was one of the six children of the Parmese condottiero Pietro de' Rossi and Ginella Fieschi of Calestano, who married in 1328.

Her siblings were Luchina, Teodora, Fresca and Luigia, and one brother, the knight Bernardo. Pietro de' Rossi, then captain of the Venetian anti-Scaliger league, was killed at the siege of Monselice in August 1337 while Isabella and her sisters were still children.

en:
Jacopo Contarini (c. 1193–1280), the 47th doge of Venice, was born into the Contarini family. In 1265 he negotiated at Constantinople with Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos a truce Venice never ratified. Elected doge in September 1275, he was already in his eighties.

He let the councils rule through famine, plague and the wars with Ancona and Capodistria; a truce with Byzantium followed in 1278. He abdicated in March 1280, retired to a monastery and died in April, leaving sons by his wife Jacobina.

雅各布·孔塔里尼（约1193—1280）是威尼斯第四十七任总督，出身孔塔里尼家族。1265年，他在君士坦丁堡与皇帝米海尔八世·巴列奥略议定一项停战，威尼斯却始终未予批准。1275年9月，已年逾八旬的他当选总督。

任内他把政务交给诸委员会，威尼斯连遭饥荒、瘟疫，又与安科纳和卡波迪斯特里亚交战，1278年与拜占庭达成停战。他于1280年3月退位，退隐修道院，4月去世，与妻子雅各比娜生有子嗣。

任内他把政务交给诸委员会，威尼斯连遭饥荒、瘟疫，又与[ShowLocationName('ancona')]和卡波迪斯特里亚交战，1278年与[GetCountry('BYZ').GetName]达成停战。他于1280年3月退位，退隐修道院，4月去世，与妻子雅各比娜生有子嗣。

en:
Jacopo Tiepolo (c. 1170–1249) served as Doge of Venice from 1229 until his abdication in May 1249. He became the first Venetian Duke of Crete (1209–1214), enlisting Marco Sanudo to suppress the Greek revolt of 1211.

He was twice Podestà of Constantinople, signing treaties with Nicaea and the Sultanate of Rum. As doge he codified civil law and established the Venetian Senate.

From 1237 he fought Emperor Frederick II: his son Pietro was captured at Cortenuova and executed in 1240, when Venice also seized Ferrara. Tiepolo reconquered Pula in 1242, abdicated in 1249 and died two months later.

zh:
雅科波·提埃坡罗（约1170—1249）1229年出任威尼斯总督，直至1249年5月退位。他成为首任由威尼斯人担任的克里特公爵（1209—1214），并请马尔科·萨努多协助镇压1211年的希腊人起义。

他还两度出任君士坦丁堡长官，与尼西亚和鲁姆苏丹国签订条约。任总督期间，他主持编纂民法、设立威尼斯元老院。

1237年起他与皇帝腓特烈二世交战：其子彼得罗在科尔泰诺瓦被俘，1240年被处死，同年威尼斯攻占费拉拉。提埃坡罗于1242年收复普拉，1249年退位，两个月后去世。

en:
Leonardo Dandolo (1326–1406) was the younger son of Doge Andrea Dandolo and Francesca Morosini, named in the doge's will of 1354. A knight, he served from 1362 as duke of Candia, Venice's governor of Crete.

In August 1363, when Latin feudatories resisted a new Senate port tax, Dandolo refused to suspend it; on 9 August the rebels stormed the ducal palace, seized him and raised the banner of Saint Titus under Marco Gradenigo the Elder. A Venetian army led by Luchino dal Verme retook Candia in May 1364.

Around 1367 he was one of four Averroist-leaning patricians whose verdict that Petrarch was a good man but unlettered provoked the tract On His Own Ignorance. He later held senior offices and died on 16 January 1406.

莱奥纳尔多·丹多洛（1326—1406）是威尼斯总督安德烈亚·丹多洛与弗兰切斯卡·莫罗西尼的幼子，在父亲1354年的遗嘱中得到安排。他受封骑士，1362年起任干地亚公爵，即威尼斯在克里特的总督。

1363年8月，岛上的拉丁封建主抵制元老院新开的港口税，他拒绝缓征；8月9日起义者攻入公爵宫，将他逮捕，拥立长者马可·格拉代尼戈，竖起圣提多旗帜。卢基诺·达尔韦尔梅率领的威尼斯军队于1364年5月收复干地亚。

约1367年，他是四名倾向阿威罗伊学说的威尼斯贵族之一，四人称彼得拉克为人虽好却无学问，促使对方写下《论本人及众人之无知》。他后来历任要职，于1406年1月16日去世。

en:
Lorenzo Celsi (1310–1365) was a naval commander and diplomat from a family that had stayed out of public life, so his election as the 58th doge of Venice on 16 July 1361 came as a surprise. Deadlocked electors settled on him for his victories over the Genoese.

As captain of the sea in 1353 he took Genoese ships. From 1359 he was ambassador to Emperor Charles IV, seeking recognition of Venetian rule over Treviso.

His reign saw a feud over the ruling oligarchy and the Cretan revolt of 1363, whose suppression he celebrated lavishly. His style was sovereign: a servant walked before him with a rod like a sceptre. The Council of Ten put him on trial around his death in July 1365; he left only daughters and was buried at Santa Maria della Celestia.

洛伦佐·切尔西（1310—1365）是海军将领与外交官，出身的家族一向置身公共事务之外，所以1361年7月16日他当选威尼斯第五十八任总督，实属意外。僵持不下的选举人最后看中他对热那亚人的战绩。

1353年他任海上统帅，俘获多艘热那亚船只。1359年起，他出使神圣罗马帝国皇帝查理四世，寻求皇帝承认威尼斯对特雷维索的统治。

他任内，统治寡头集团内部争斗不休，1363年又爆发克里特岛起义，镇压成功后他大肆庆贺。他的排场如同君主：仆人手持权杖般的短杖走在他前面。十人议会在他1365年7月去世前后对他提起审判；他只留下女儿，葬于切莱斯蒂亚圣母堂。

en:
Lorenzo Tiepolo (died 16 August 1275), son of Doge Jacopo Tiepolo, was Doge of Venice from 23 July 1268 until his death. A commander in the War of Saint Sabas against Genoa, he broke the siege of the Venetian quarter at Acre and in 1258 drove the Genoese from the city.

In 1262 he took part in peace negotiations with William of Villehardouin, Prince of Achaea. He was elected doge with 25 of 41 votes, and as doge made peace with Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos and, at Cremona in 1270, with Genoa.

A trade war with Bologna and its allies from 1270 ended in 1273 with Venice confirmed in control of the Po.

洛伦佐·提埃坡罗（1275年8月16日卒）是总督雅科波·提埃坡罗之子，1268年7月23日当选威尼斯总督，在任直至去世。对热那亚的圣萨巴战争中，他率军解除了热那亚人对阿卡威尼斯街区的围困，并于1258年将热那亚人逐出该城。

1262年他参加了与亚该亚亲王纪尧姆·德·维勒阿杜安的和谈。他以41票中的25票当选总督，任内与皇帝米海尔八世·巴列奥略媾和，又于1270年在克雷莫纳与热那亚议和。

1270年起与博洛尼亚及其盟邦的贸易战于1273年结束，威尼斯对波河的控制权得到确认。

en:
Marco Cornaro (c. 1286–1368) came from one of Venice's old, rich families and made his fortune in the Egypt trade. In 1337, in the war against the Scaligeri, he became podestà of Padua after its negotiated handover.

As count of Zara he took refuge in the citadel when the city rose against Venice in May 1345, and was rescued; he later served as duke of Candia. In April 1355 patricians met in his house to answer Faliero's coup, and Cornaro headed the Republic between Faliero's execution on 17 April and Giovanni Gradenigo's election four days later.

His second wife Caterina's low birth hindered his election. Elected doge on 21 July 1365, he presided over economic growth overshadowed by losses to Genoa and the Ottomans, and died in January 1368.

马可·科尔纳罗（约1286—1368）出身威尼斯古老而富有的家族，财富来自对埃及的贸易。1337年，在对斯卡拉家族的战争中，帕多瓦经谈判交出后，他出任该城行政长官。

身为扎达尔伯爵，1345年5月城中反叛威尼斯时，他退守城堡，后获救；后来他还出任干地亚公爵。1355年4月，贵族们聚在他家应对法列罗的政变，在4月17日法列罗被处决到四天后乔万尼·格拉代尼戈当选之间，由他执掌共和国。

他的第二任妻子卡泰丽娜出身低微，使他的总督选举遇到阻力。1365年7月21日他当选总督，任内经济有所增长，但领地被热那亚和奥斯曼人蚕食；他于1368年1月去世。

en:
Marco Gradenigo (c. 1224–c. 1274) was a Venetian noble and naval commander. In 1255 he took Negroponte after a thirteen-month siege; as bailo from 1256 he united the Latin Greek lords against William of Villehardouin, who defeated him at Karydi in 1258.

As Podestà of Constantinople, his fleet was attacking Daphnousia in July 1261 when Nicaean troops retook the city, and he evacuated the Latin emperor Baldwin II to Negroponte. He later fought in the victory over Genoa at Trapani in 1266 and commanded Venetian forces in the war with Bologna in 1270.

马可·格拉代尼戈（约1224—约1274）是威尼斯贵族与海军将领。1255年他经十三个月围城夺取内格罗蓬特；1256年起出任巴伊洛，联合希腊的拉丁诸领主对抗纪尧姆·德·维勒阿杜安，却于1258年在卡里迪之战中被击败。

担任君士坦丁堡波德斯塔期间，1261年7月他的舰队正在出击达夫努西亚，尼西亚军队趁机收复君士坦丁堡，他只得将拉丁皇帝鲍德温二世撤至内格罗蓬特。此后他参加1266年大胜热那亚的特拉帕尼海战，并于1270年在对博洛尼亚的战争中指挥威尼斯军队。

en:
Marino Dandolo (died before 1243) was a Venetian nobleman who became the first Latin ruler of the island of Andros. In 1207 he joined Marco Sanudo's conquest of the Aegean islands and received Andros as a fief of the new Duchy of Naxos.

Around 1239 Geremia Ghisi, lord of the northern Aegean islands, expelled him from Andros. Marino died in exile before August 1243. His wife Felicia kept half the island and later married Jacopo Querini.

en:
Marino Falier (c. 1274–1355) was the 55th Doge of Venice, born into one of its oldest patrician houses. He had headed the Council of Ten and served as bailo of Negroponte before his election as doge on 11 September 1354, at about eighty, while ambassador to Pope Innocent VI at Avignon.

He came home to a Republic at war with Genoa, and on 4 November the Genoese destroyed the Venetian fleet at Sapienza. By April 1355 he was plotting with commoners to cut down the patricians and rule as prince.

Tradition traces his grievance to a Carnival slight. Betrayed on 14 April, he was beheaded on 17 April. In 1366 the Council of Ten had his portrait effaced and an inscription recording his treason put in its place.

马里诺·法列罗（约1274—1355）是威尼斯第五十五任总督，出身威尼斯最古老的贵族世家之一。他曾出任十人团首领和内格罗蓬特巴伊洛，1354年9月11日当选总督时已年约八旬，正以使节身份在阿维尼翁觐见教皇英诺森六世。

他回到威尼斯时，共和国正与热那亚交战，11月4日热那亚人在萨皮恩扎歼灭了威尼斯舰队。至1355年4月，他已在与平民密谋铲除贵族、自立为君。

传统上认为，他的怨恨起于狂欢节上受到的冒犯。阴谋于4月14日败露，他于4月17日被斩首。1366年，十人团下令抹去他的肖像，并在原处写上记录其叛国之罪的铭文。

Marino Gradenigo (c. 1250–c. 1283) was a Venetian noble, a son of the admiral Marco Gradenigo and brother of Doge Pietro Gradenigo. He sat several times in the Minor Council and Senate, and was twice Duke of Candia, in 1278–1280 and 1282–1283.

He died on Crete during his second term and was buried in the church of San Marco at Candia. With his wife Maria Dandolo, said to be a daughter of Doge Giovanni Dandolo, he left at least four sons; one of them, Giovanni, was elected doge in 1355.

en:
Marino Morosini (1181–1253) was doge of Venice from June 1249 until his death. Of the Morosini dalla Tressa branch, he had held senior offices, and his election was the first by forty-one electors.

His short reign brought prudent commercial policy and new trade treaties. When Louis IX crusaded against Egypt, Venice stayed neutral to safeguard its trade with the sultan. He admitted an inquisition court but reserved appointment of its judges, and created the Signori di Notte. He died in 1253 and was buried in Saint Mark's.

en:
Marino Zorzi (c. 1238–1312) was the 50th doge of Venice, elected in August 1311. He had been ambassador to Pope Benedict XI in 1303 and was nicknamed ‘il Santo’ for his piety.

Elected after the Tiepolo conspiracy of 1310 and the papal interdict over Ferrara, he failed to repair relations with Rome. A campaign against rebellious Zara ended in defeat, while a 1312 treaty with Padua settled Brenta navigation disputes. His reign lasted less than eleven months; he died in July 1312.

马里诺·佐尔齐（约1238—1312）是第50任威尼斯总督，1311年8月当选。他1303年曾出使觐见教皇本笃十一世，因虔诚被称为‘圣人’。

他在1310年蒂耶波洛阴谋和费拉拉战争引发的教皇禁令之后上台，却未能修复与罗马的关系。威尼斯征讨叛乱的扎拉失利，而1312年与帕多瓦签订的条约解决了布伦塔河航运争端。他在位不足11个月，于1312年7月去世。

en:
Marsilio de' Rossi (1287–1337) was the soldier of the brothers who ran Parma, an Emilian condottiero and son of Guglielmo de' Rossi. In Carrara service he was captured by Cangrande della Scala at Vicenza in 1314, and back in Parma from 1323 he joined his brother Rolando in driving out the Sanvitale.

When Emperor Louis IV came down into Italy he sided with the Empire, and became imperial vicar of Parma and then of Lombardy. He took power in Parma himself when Rolando was arrested at Bologna in 1329.

When the Rossi fell in 1335 he fled to Venice and led one of its three armies against the Scaligers. He died on 16 August 1337, a week after his brother Pietro, who had held the supreme command.

马尔西利奥·德·罗西（1287—1337）是执掌帕尔马的罗西兄弟中的武将，艾米利亚佣兵将领，帕尔马的古列尔莫·德·罗西之子。他为卡拉拉家族效力，1314年在维琴察被坎格兰德·德拉·斯卡拉俘获；1323年回到帕尔马后，与兄长罗兰多一道逐走圣维塔莱家族。

皇帝路德维希四世南下意大利后，他倒向帝国一方，受任帕尔马、继而伦巴第的帝国代理人。1329年罗兰多在博洛尼亚被捕，他接掌了帕尔马的大权。

1335年罗西家族失势，他逃往威尼斯，统领威尼斯三支大军之一对斯卡拉家族作战。1337年8月16日，他在曾任威尼斯军队最高统帅的弟弟彼得罗去世一周后病逝。

Michele Morosini was a Venetian nobleman of the Morosini dalla Sbarra, a son of the statesman Albertino Morosini and his wife Marchesina. His daughter Constanza, born around 1275, married the Serbian prince Stefan Vladislav II of Syrmia in 1293.

The match ended the support Vladislav's father Stefan Dragutin had given the Angevin claimant against King Andrew III of Hungary, Michele's cousin. Michele's brother Marino had died by the time Albertino drew up his last will in November 1305.

en:
Michele Morosini (1308–1382) was doge of Venice for only four months in 1382. Born into one of the city's most important families, he was extremely wealthy and made his name in trade.

During the gruelling War of Chioggia against Genoa (1378–1381), he bought houses cheaply while the city struggled and ended among the richest men in Venice. Opinion of him divided between a noble merchant who served the state faithfully and a ruthless speculator.

Elected after Andrea Contarini's death, he died of the plague and was buried at San Zanipolo, the traditional resting place of the doges. His wife was Cristina Condulmer.

Michele Morosini (1308–1382) was doge of Venice for only four months in 1382. Born into one of the city's most important families, he was extremely wealthy and made his name in trade.

During the gruelling War of Chioggia against Genoa (1378–1381), he bought houses cheaply while the city struggled and ended among the richest men in Venice. Opinion of him divided between a noble merchant who served the state faithfully and a ruthless speculator.

Elected after #TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('ven_andrea_contarini').GetID],X #L Andrea Contarini#!#!'s death, he died of the plague and was buried at San Zanipolo, the traditional resting place of the doges. His wife was Cristina Condulmer.
zh:
米凯莱·莫罗西尼（1308—1382）1382年担任威尼斯总督仅四个月。他出身威尼斯最显赫的家族之一，家财万贯，以经商闻名。

1378至1381年威尼斯与热那亚进行惨烈的基奥贾战争，城中艰难，他趁机低价买下大量房产，战争结束时已跻身威尼斯最富有的人之一。世人对他评价不一：有人视他为忠心事国的贵族商人，也有人视他为不择手段的投机客。

他在安德烈亚·孔塔里尼去世后当选总督，不久死于瘟疫，葬于历代总督传统的安葬地圣若望及保禄堂。妻子是克里斯蒂娜·孔杜尔梅。

en:
Michele Steno (c. 1331–1413) was the doge under whom Venice began to expand onto the Italian mainland. In 1354 he was jailed for insulting Doge Marino Faliero; legend later made the jibe the spark of Faliero's conspiracy. Blamed in part for the defeat at Pula in the War of Chioggia (1379), he recovered and in 1386 became Procurator of Saint Mark.

In 1398–1400 he negotiated peace with Gian Galeazzo Visconti, and on 1 December 1400 he was elected doge. After Visconti's death in 1402, Vicenza, Verona and other Veneto towns submitted to Venice, and the war of 1404–1405 ended Carrara rule in Padua.

Dalmatia returned in 1409, bought from Naples. The last of the Steno line, he died on 26 December 1413 and was buried at Santa Marina.

米凯莱·斯泰诺（约1331—1413）是威尼斯总督，威尼斯向意大利大陆扩张就始于他任内。1354年他因侮辱总督马里诺·法列罗被判入狱；后世传说把这句嘲讽说成法列罗密谋的导火索。1379年基奥贾战争中，他因普拉战败负有部分责任，但仕途随后恢复，1386年出任圣马可行政长官。

1398至1400年他与詹加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂议和，1400年12月1日当选总督。维斯孔蒂于1402年去世后，维琴察、维罗纳等威尼托城镇陆续归附威尼斯，1404至1405年的战争又终结了帕多瓦卡拉雷西家族的统治。

1409年达尔马提亚从那不勒斯手中买回。作为斯泰诺家族的最后一人，他于1413年12月26日去世，葬于圣玛丽娜教堂。

en:
Nicolò Gradenigo, called Nicoletto (c. 1267–c. 1317), was a Venetian noble, a son of Doge Pietro Gradenigo and Tommasina Morosini.

Genealogists name Bertucci, Giacomo and Paolo as his brothers, but only Nicolò and Marco survived their father, and the two were the sole fidecommissari, the trustees of the family inheritance, named in the doge's will in 1311; no public office of his is recorded.

en:
Nicolò Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman and a son of Doge Bartolomeo Gradenigo. Bartolomeo advanced his many sons through widely resented favouritism, until the Major Council, soon after his death in 1342, barred public office to the relatives of a living doge and forbade the ducal family to trade.

In 1348 Nicolò was sent as ambassador to King Louis I of Hungary, who was disputing Dalmatia with Venice, and he later served several times among the Savi.

尼科洛·格拉代尼戈是威尼斯贵族，总督巴托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈之子。巴托洛梅奥凭恃广受非议的偏私为诸子谋求前程，1342年他去世后不久，大议会便立法禁止在任总督的亲属担任公职，并禁止总督家族经商。

1348年，尼科洛受命出使正与威尼斯争夺达尔马提亚的匈牙利国王拉约什一世，后来又多次出任共和国的高级咨议官职“贤人”。

en:
Nicolò Soranzo was a Venetian nobleman and a son of Doge Giovanni Soranzo, by Francesca Molin or by an otherwise unknown earlier wife.

He had already died when the doge made his will on 8 August 1321, which names him as the deceased son among six children, with Marino, Antonio called Belello, Soranza, Elena and Fontana; he thus predeceased his father, who died in office in 1328, by more than seven years.

en:
Ordelaffo Falier was a Venetian nobleman of the ancient Falier family, the son of Jacopo Falier and Beriola Loredan, and a brother of Doge Marino Faliero, sharing his name with an earlier doge of the early twelfth century.

In 1344, while Marino was on an embassy to Avignon, Ordelaffo served in his place as podestà of Chioggia until his return. Ordelaffo died during the Black Death in 1348.

en:
Pietro Gradenigo (1251–1311), 49th Doge of Venice from 1289 until his death, was elected while podestà of Capodistria. In February 1297 he carried through the Serrata del Maggior Consiglio, restricting access to the Great Council and helping to form a hereditary oligarchy.

His reign saw defeat by Genoa at Curzola in 1298 and, from 1308, war over Ferrara that brought excommunication from Clement V. After Bajamonte Tiepolo's failed coup of June 1310, the Council of Ten was created. Gradenigo died on 13 August 1311 and, Venice being under interdict, was buried in an unmarked grave on Murano.

彼得罗·格拉代尼戈（1251—1311）是威尼斯第四十九任总督，1289年起任职直至去世，当选时正在卡波迪斯特里亚担任波德斯塔。1297年2月，他推动通过大议会封闭令，限制进入大议会的资格，促成世袭寡头政体的形成。

任内威尼斯1298年在库尔佐拉海战中败于热那亚，1308年起因费拉拉与教皇国交战，被教皇克雷芒五世处以绝罚。1310年6月巴亚蒙特·蒂耶波洛政变失败后，十人团应运而生。1311年8月13日格拉代尼戈去世，由于威尼斯正受绝罚禁令，他被葬于穆拉诺岛的无名墓地。

en:
Pietro Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman and a son of Doge Bartolomeo Gradenigo. He and his brothers owed their advancement to their father's determined lobbying while he was doge, which so angered Venetian opinion that after Bartolomeo's death in 1342 the Major Council banned grants of office to a living doge's relatives.

In 1355 Pietro served the Republic as count of Traù, on the Dalmatian coast that King Louis I of Hungary was contesting with Venice. In 1361, after Doge Giovanni Dolfin's death, he stood for the dogeship himself, but the election went to Lorenzo Celsi.

彼得罗·格拉代尼戈是威尼斯贵族，总督巴托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈之子。他和兄弟们的晋升都靠父亲任总督期间大力安插；这些做法激起公愤，巴托洛梅奥于1342年去世后，大议会遂立法禁止向在任总督的亲属授予公职。

1355年，彼得罗代表威尼斯共和国出任特拉乌伯爵，所在的达尔马提亚海岸，正是匈牙利国王拉约什一世与威尼斯相争之地。1361年总督乔瓦尼·多尔芬去世后，他亲自参选总督，但最终由洛伦佐·切尔西当选。

en:
Pietro de' Rossi (1303–1337) was the Emilian condottiero Venice set against the Scaligers. A son of Guglielmo de' Rossi of Parma, he had fought for the future Emperor Charles IV and held Lucca in vicariate until the Scaligers drove him out in 1334.

In 1336 Doge Francesco Dandolo hired him and his brothers Rolando and Marsilio, naming Pietro commander of the anti-Scaliger league's troops. He razed the Saline castle at Chioggia, and on 3 August 1337 Padua surrendered to him through his uncle Marsilio da Carrara; Alberto II della Scala was captured.

Five days later, in the first assault on Monselice, a Monselice peasant killed Pietro with a lance. He was buried in the Basilica of Saint Anthony at Padua.

彼得罗·德·罗西（1303—1337）是艾米利亚的佣兵将领，威尼斯用他来对付斯卡拉家族。他是帕尔马的古列尔莫·德·罗西之子，曾追随后来成为皇帝的查理四世作战，并以代理人身份领有卢卡，直到1334年被斯卡拉家族赶走。

1336年，总督弗朗切斯科·丹多洛雇用了他和兄弟罗兰多、马西利奥，任命彼得罗为反斯卡拉联盟军队的统帅。他摧毁了基奥贾的萨利内城堡；1337年8月3日，帕多瓦通过他的舅父马西利奥·达·卡拉拉向他投降，阿尔贝托二世·德拉·斯卡拉被俘。

五天后，在对蒙塞利切的首次强攻中，一名当地农民用长矛刺死了彼得罗。他葬于帕多瓦圣安多尼圣殿。

en:
Pietro Zeno (died 1345) was a Venetian commander. As captain and bailiff of Negroponte, he bought off a 380-ship Aydinid fleet under Umur Bey that raided the island in 1332.

That July Doge Francesco Dandolo charged him with arranging an anti-Turkish alliance, formally established as the Naval League by year's end. Zeno led its twenty galleys to victory over the emir of Karasi off Adramyttion on 14 September 1334.

In 1343 the Grand Council sent him to join the Smyrniote crusade. After Smyrna fell, he was killed in an ambush by Umur Bey's forces while attempting to celebrate mass on 17 January 1345.

彼得罗·泽诺（1345年卒）是威尼斯将领。他任内格罗蓬特指挥官兼行政长官期间，1332年乌穆尔贝伊率艾登王朝380艘战船袭掠该岛，他献贡金将其劝退。

同年7月，总督弗朗切斯科·丹多洛命他筹组反土耳其同盟，年底海上同盟正式成立。1334年9月14日，他率同盟二十艘桨帆船在阿德拉米蒂翁湾外击败卡拉西埃米尔的舰队。

1343年，大议会派他参加士麦那十字军。攻克士麦那后，1345年1月17日他试图举行弥撒时遭乌穆尔贝伊部下伏击身亡。

en:
Bartolomeo Platina (1421–1481), born Bartolomeo Sacchi at Piadena near Cremona, was an Italian humanist writer. After soldiering and tutoring the Gonzaga sons in Mantua, he studied Greek in Florence and entered papal service in Rome. Under the anti-humanist Paul II he was imprisoned in 1464 after losing his papal office, and again in 1468 over the Roman Academy affair, under torture.

Sixtus IV made him the first Vatican librarian in 1475. His De honesta voluptate et valetudine became the first printed cookbook, and his Lives of the Popes appeared in 1479, depicting Paul II harshly.

巴托洛米奥·普拉蒂纳（1421—1481），本名巴托洛梅奥·萨基，生于克雷莫纳附近的皮亚德纳，是意大利人文主义作家。他早年从军，后在曼托瓦担任贡扎加家族子弟的教师，又赴佛罗伦萨学习希腊语，随后到罗马为教廷效力。敌视人文主义的教皇保罗二世在位时，他因失去教廷职位于1464年被囚，1468年又因罗马学院事件再次入狱，受酷刑审讯。

1475年，西斯都四世任命他为首任梵蒂冈图书馆馆长。他的《论正当的享乐与健康》是第一部付印的烹饪书，1479年问世的《教皇传》则尖锐地描写了保罗二世。

en:
Raniero Dandolo (died 1209) was a Venetian admiral and statesman, the only confirmed son of Doge Enrico Dandolo. From 1202 to 1205 he governed Venice as vice-doge during his father's absence on the Fourth Crusade, corresponding with Pope Innocent III over the installation of Tommaso Morosini as Latin patriarch of Constantinople, and he also legislated as vice-doge.

After his father's death he led the Venetian conquest of Crete against the Genoese, and after subduing most of the island he was killed there by an arrow in 1209. His daughter Anna married King Stefan Nemanjić of Serbia.

拉伊纳罗·丹多洛（1209年卒）是威尼斯海军将领与政治家，也是总督恩里科·丹多洛唯一可考的儿子。1202至1205年，父亲参加第四次十字军远征在外，他以副总督身份主持威尼斯政务，就托马索·莫罗西尼出任君士坦丁堡拉丁牧首一事与教皇英诺森三世通信，并以副总督身份立法。

父亲死后，他率军同热那亚人争夺并征服克里特，在基本平定全岛后于1209年中箭身亡。他的女儿安娜嫁给了塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·尼曼伊奇。

en:
Reniero Zeno (c. 1200–1268), son of Pietro Zeno, was the 45th Doge of Venice from January 1253 until his death. He served as podestà of Pola, Verona and other Italian cities, retook rebellious Zara in 1242 and became captain-general of the Sea in 1244.

Elected doge while podestà of Fermo, he backed Pope Alexander IV against Ezzelino da Romano in 1256–1259 and fought the War of Saint Sabas against Genoa, winning at Settepozzi in 1263.

His reign enacted Venice's 129-article maritime code and made a five-year truce with Byzantium in 1268. He died on 7 July 1268.

雷涅罗·泽诺（约1200—1268）是彼得罗·泽诺之子，1253年1月起出任第四十五任威尼斯总督，在任直至去世。他曾出任普拉、维罗纳等意大利城市的长官，1242年收复反叛的扎拉，1244年受任为海军统帅。

en:
Rolando de' Rossi (c. 1285–1345) tried to make Parma his family's lordship while papal, Scaliger and Visconti power pressed on Emilia. In 1322 he imprisoned his rival Sanvitale, and in 1325 the legate made him captain of the Church. In 1328 he expelled the papal government, allied with Cangrande della Scala and was given supreme power by the general council, becoming Parma's effective signore.

The legate arrested him at Bologna in 1329. Freed in 1331, he submitted Parma to John of Bohemia and was made a count. With no help from Avignon or the Visconti, Parma surrendered to the Scaligers in June 1335, ending its self-rule.

In exile he commanded Venice's army against them until the 1339 peace, which restored his estates but not his city. He died at Padua in May 1345.

罗兰多·德·罗西（约1285—1345）试图把帕尔马变成自家的领地，而教廷、斯卡拉和维斯孔蒂家族都在向艾米利亚伸手。1322年，他囚禁政敌桑维塔莱；1325年，教皇使节任命他为教会队长。1328年，他驱逐教廷政府，与坎格兰德·德拉·斯卡拉结盟，总议会授予他最高权力，他成为帕尔马事实上的领主。

1329年他在博洛尼亚被捕。1331年获释后，他将帕尔马献给波希米亚国王约翰，受封伯爵。由于阿维尼翁和维斯孔蒂都不肯援手，1335年6月帕尔马向斯卡拉家族投降，自治就此终结。

流亡中，他统率威尼斯军队对抗斯卡拉家族，直到1339年和约；和约归还了他的产业，却没有归还帕尔马。1345年5月，他在帕多瓦去世。

en:
Jacopo Sansovino (1486–1570), born Jacopo Tatti in Florence, took the name of his master Andrea Sansovino and became the defining architect of Venetian Renaissance classicism. A sculptor in Florence and Rome, where Raphael judged his wax copy of the Laocoön the best, he fled to Venice after the Sack of Rome in 1527.

From 1529, as chief architect to the Procurators of St Mark, he reshaped the area around St Mark's Square, building the Biblioteca Marciana, his masterpiece, the Zecca mint and the Loggetta of the Campanile; in the library he combined classical architecture with Venetian decorative tastes. He died in Venice in 1570.

雅各布·桑索维诺（1486—1570），本名雅各布·塔蒂，生于佛罗伦萨，后随恩师安德烈亚·桑索维诺改姓，是威尼斯文艺复兴古典主义建筑的奠基者。他早年在佛罗伦萨和罗马从事雕塑，复制的《拉奥孔》蜡模曾被拉斐尔评为第一；1527年罗马之劫后他避居威尼斯。

1529年起，他担任圣马可行政长官的首席建筑师，重塑了圣马可广场一带的面貌，代表作有圣马可图书馆、造币厂和钟楼旁的小敞廊；他在图书馆的设计中将古典建筑与威尼斯的装饰趣味结合。1570年他在威尼斯去世。

en:
Simone Dandolo was a Venetian nobleman of the San Luca branch, the son of Fantino Dandolo and brother of Doge Andrea Dandolo. In 1345 he served as provveditore, supply commissioner, with the Venetian army fighting around the rebellious city of Zara in Dalmatia.

The revolt threatened Venice's hold on the coast. He afterwards became podestà of Treviso, and later sat as one of the judges of Doge Marino Falier.

en:
Stephen the Posthumous (1236–1271) was the posthumous son of King Andrew II of Hungary and Beatrice d'Este, born after his mother fled King Béla IV. Béla, his half-brother, disputed his paternity and denied him a king's son's revenues.

Raised from 1243 at the Ferrara court of Marquis Azzo VII d'Este, he married Tomasina Morosini of Venice. His mother sought Venetian support for his claims, but Venice promised Béla in its 1244 peace treaty not to support them.

He styled himself Duke of Slavonia and pressed his Hungarian claims without success. He died in Venice after making his will on 10 April 1271. His son by Tomasina became King Andrew III, the last Árpád ruler.

遗腹子伊什特万（1236—1271）是匈牙利国王安德烈二世与埃斯特的贝亚特里切的遗腹子。母亲逃离国王贝拉四世后生下他，同父异母的兄长贝拉质疑他的血统，拒绝给予他王子应得的收入。

自1243年起，他在费拉拉侯爵阿佐七世·埃斯特的宫廷长大，娶威尼斯的托马西娜·莫罗西尼为妻。母亲曾寻求威尼斯支持他的权利主张，但威尼斯在1244年的和约中向贝拉承诺不予支持。

他自称斯拉沃尼亚公爵，一再争取匈牙利的权益却始终无果。1271年4月10日立遗嘱后他在威尼斯去世。他与托马西娜所生之子后来成为匈牙利国王安德拉什三世，即阿帕德王朝末代君主。

en:
Jacopo Robusti, known as Tintoretto (1518–1594), was a Renaissance painter whose furious speed and bold brushwork earned him the nickname il Furioso. The son of a dyer, whence his name, he was dismissed from Titian's studio after a few days, reportedly out of jealousy, and taught himself drawing after Michelangelo day and night.

His 1548 Miracle of the Slave brought commissions. When Paolo Veronese took the prestigious commissions he wanted in 1551, he offered the Madonna dell'Orto two colossal 14.5-metre canvases.

In 1564, asked for ceiling sketches by the Scuola Grande di San Rocco, he secretly installed a finished painting as a gift it could not refuse, later painting fifty works there. After Veronese died in 1588 the Doge's Palace Paradise commission passed to him, finished with his son Domenico. His daughter Marietta died in 1590; he died in May 1594 and was buried beside her.

雅各布·罗布斯蒂，即丁托列托（1518—1594），是文艺复兴画家，作画速度迅疾、笔触大胆，因而得名“狂热者”。他是染匠之子，绰号意即“小染匠”；他在提香的作坊只待了几天就被辞退，据传出于嫉妒，此后便对着仿米开朗基罗的模型夜以继日地自学绘画。

他1548年的《奴隶的奇迹》大获成功，带来委托。1551年保罗·委罗内塞拿走了他渴望的重要委托，他便向果园圣母堂提出绘制两幅14.5米高的巨幅画布。

1564年圣洛克大会堂征集天花板草图，他偷偷把一幅完成的画安装上去，作为会堂无法拒收的赠礼，后来又为该会堂绘制五十幅作品。委罗内塞1588年去世后，总督宫《天堂》的委托转给了他，由儿子多梅尼科协助完成。女儿玛丽埃塔1590年去世，他于1594年5月去世，与女儿合葬。

雅各布·罗布斯蒂，即丁托列托（1518—1594），是文艺复兴画家，作画速度迅疾、笔触大胆，因而得名“狂热者”。他是染匠之子，绰号意即“小染匠”；他在提香的作坊只待了几天就被辞退，据传出于嫉妒，此后便对着仿米开朗基罗的模型夜以继日地自学绘画。

他1548年的《奴隶的奇迹》大获成功，带来委托。1551年保罗·委罗内塞拿走了他渴望的重要委托，他便向果园圣母堂提出绘制两幅14.5米高的巨幅画布。

1564年圣洛克大会堂征集天花板草图，他偷偷把一幅完成的画安装上去，作为会堂无法拒收的赠礼，后来又为该会堂绘制五十幅作品。委罗内塞1588年去世后，总督宫《天堂》的委托转给了他，由儿子多梅尼科协助完成。女儿玛丽埃塔1590年去世，他于1594年5月去世，与女儿合葬。

Tommasina Morosini (born in the 1260s) was a Venetian noblewoman who married Pietro Gradenigo, later doge of Venice. When he took office in 1289 she became dogaressa until her death before 1309. She was a niece of Tomasina Morosini, queen of Hungary and mother of Andrew III.

She bore Gradenigo at least ten children, including Nicolò, who served as a Venetian envoy to Treviso in 1314, and Isabetta, who married the Paduan lord Giacomo I da Carrara.

托马西娜·莫罗西尼（1260年代生）是威尼斯贵族女子，嫁给后来的威尼斯总督彼得罗·格拉代尼戈。1289年丈夫就任，她成为总督夫人，直至1309年以前去世。她是匈牙利王后、安德拉什三世之母托马西娜的侄女。

en:
Tommaso Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman, one of the five sons of Doge Giovanni Gradenigo and his second wife Felipa.

On 7 January 1353 his father, about to take up the rectorship of Capodistria, made his will and named Tommaso an executor with his mother, his sister Caterina and his brothers Marino, Orso and Luca; the brother Pietro was already dead and went unmentioned. Like his brothers, Tommaso never reached high office.

en:
Ugolino de' Rossi (c. 1300–1377) was bishop of Parma for fifty-four years, longer than anyone before or after him. The Rossi, now the city's masters, had the legate name him bishop; Pope John XXII ratified it in June 1323, when Ugolino held only minor orders.

He was caught between his brothers' politics and the papacy: he fled to Corniglio when Louis IV showed interest in Parma in 1329, and to Avignon when the Scaligers took it in 1334.

Back in 1341, he found his castles ruined and borrowed more than ten thousand gold florins from his brother Rolando. Unable to repay, he ceded chapter lands to his nephews. The Visconti, now lords of Parma, later called him to Milan, where he died on 28 April 1377, a friend and admirer of Petrarch.

乌戈利诺·德·罗西（约1300—1377）担任帕尔马主教长达54年，前后无人在任更久。罗西家族成为城中主宰后，让使节指定他出任主教；1323年6月教皇约翰二十二世批准任命，当时乌戈利诺只领有低级神品。

他夹在兄弟们的政治与教廷之间：1329年路德维希四世对帕尔马表现出兴趣时，他逃往科尔尼廖；1334年斯卡拉家族夺取帕尔马后，他又逃往阿维尼翁。

1341年返回时，他发现城堡尽毁，向兄长罗兰多借了一万多金弗罗林。因无力偿还，他把教区议事会的土地让给侄子们。后来他被已成为帕尔马新主人的维斯孔蒂家族召往米兰，1377年4月28日在当地去世，生前是彼特拉克的朋友与仰慕者。

en:
Vitale Dandolo was a Venetian jurist and a powerful member of the ducal court, head of the Dandolo of San Luca when his family rose to the front rank of Venetian politics.

After Doge Vitale II Michiel was murdered in front of San Zaccaria in 1172, Vitale was among the electors who chose Sebastiano Ziani as doge. Ziani sent him to Constantinople to negotiate peace with Emperor Manuel I Komnenos after the mass arrest of Venetians.

He died in 1174, in his nineties; only then did his son Enrico Dandolo, already about sixty-seven, become head of the family and begin his own public career.

维塔莱·丹多洛是威尼斯法学家、总督府的有权势成员，也是丹多洛家族圣卢卡支的家长，当时该家族正跻身威尼斯政坛前列。

1172年总督维塔莱二世·米基耶尔在圣扎卡里亚教堂前遇刺后，维塔莱参与推举塞巴斯蒂亚诺·齐亚尼为新总督。齐亚尼派他前往君士坦丁堡，就威尼斯人遭大规模逮捕一事与曼努埃尔一世·科穆宁皇帝议和。

他于1174年以九十多岁高龄去世，至此他年约六十七岁的儿子恩里科·丹多洛才成为家长，开始自己的公共生涯。

Alberto II della Scala (1306–1352) was the elder son of Alboino I della Scala. After Cangrande I died in 1329, he became lord of Verona, ruling with his younger brother Mastino II, who held the real power. In 1335 he took Parma and Reggio, handing Reggio to the Gonzaga.

The Scaligeri lost Padua in 1338 and further lands in 1339, and his 1341 attempt to retake Reggio from the Gonzaga failed. He died in Verona in 1352, and Mastino's sons succeeded him.

阿尔贝托二世·德拉·斯卡拉（1306—1352）是阿尔博伊诺一世·德拉·斯卡拉的长子。1329年坎格兰德一世去世后，他成为维罗纳领主，与弟弟马斯蒂诺二世共同执政，但实权掌握在马斯蒂诺手中。1335年他取得帕尔马和雷焦，随后把雷焦交给贡扎加家族。

en:
Alberto I della Scala (c. 1245–1301) was the son of Jacopino della Scala and a trusted lieutenant of his elder brother Mastino I. After Mastino's murder, the Veronese assembly elected him lifelong Captain and Rector on 27 October 1277.

He made Verona a true signoria, requiring oaths of allegiance, building a bureaucracy and personal guard, and repelling a Guelph assault in 1278–1279. Treaties with Mantua and Venice consolidated his position.

His daughter Costanza married Obizzo II d'Este, Marquis of Ferrara. He died on 3 September 1301 and was succeeded by his son Bartolomeo; Alboino and Cangrande ruled after him.

阿尔贝托一世·德拉·斯卡拉（约1245—1301）是雅各皮诺·德拉·斯卡拉之子，也是兄长马斯蒂诺一世信任的副手。马斯蒂诺遇刺后，维罗纳议会于1277年10月27日推举他为终身领袖与执政。

他把维罗纳建成真正的世袭领邦，要求官员宣誓效忠，设立官僚机构和私人卫队，并于1278至1279年击退圭尔夫派的进攻。与曼托瓦和威尼斯订立的条约帮助他巩固地位。

他的女儿科斯坦扎嫁给费拉拉侯爵奥比佐二世·埃斯特。他于1301年9月3日去世，其子巴尔托洛梅奥继位，此后阿尔博伊诺和坎格兰德也相继统治维罗纳。

他把维罗纳建成真正的世袭领邦，要求官员宣誓效忠，设立官僚机构和私人卫队，并于1278至1279年击退圭尔夫派的进攻。与曼托瓦和威尼斯订立的条约帮助他巩固地位。

他的女儿科斯坦扎嫁给费拉拉侯爵#TOOLTIP:CHARACTER,[GetCharacter('fer_obizzo_ii_este').GetID],X #L 奥比佐二世·埃斯特#!#!。他于1301年9月3日去世，其子巴尔托洛梅奥继位，此后阿尔博伊诺和坎格兰德也相继统治维罗纳。

en:
Alboino I della Scala (1284–1311), second son of Alberto I, became Lord of Verona after his brother Bartolomeo died in March 1304. In 1298 he married Caterina Visconti, daughter of Matteo I Visconti of Milan, and from 1308 he ruled alongside his younger brother Cangrande.

When the Emperor Henry VII entered Italy in 1311, he named the two brothers imperial vicars of Verona and its territory. Alboino died on 29 November 1311, leaving Cangrande to rule alone.

en:
Arrigo Castracani degli Antelminelli, called the Duchino (c. 1304–1357), was the eldest son and designated heir of the Lucchese condottiero Castruccio Castracani, the Ghibelline strongman who beat the Florentines at Altopascio in 1325 and was named duke of Lucca by Emperor Louis IV.

In 1325 Arrigo became Lucca's captain general and rector for life. Castruccio died of fever in 1328 while preparing to fight Florence again, and Louis IV then took Pisa and Lucca from his son. Arrigo repeatedly tried to recover his family's rule: in 1331 he briefly seized Lucca, only to be driven out by King John of Bohemia.

He later fought alongside Pisa but was again denied control of Lucca. Accused of conspiracy against Giovanni da Oleggio, he was executed at Bologna in 1357.

阿里戈·卡斯特拉卡尼·德利·安泰尔米内利，绰号“小公爵”（约1304—1357），是卢卡佣兵将领卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼的长子和指定继承人。卡斯特鲁乔是吉伯林派强人，1325年在阿尔托帕肖击败佛罗伦萨人，并被皇帝路德维希四世封为卢卡公爵。

1325年阿里戈获任卢卡终身总队长兼行政长官。1328年卡斯特鲁乔在筹备再战佛罗伦萨时病逝，路德维希四世随即从其子手中夺走比萨和卢卡。阿里戈屡次试图恢复家族统治：1331年他一度夺取卢卡，旋即被波希米亚国王约翰赶走。

他后来与比萨并肩作战，却再度未能掌控卢卡，因被指控密谋反对乔瓦尼·达·奥莱焦，于1357年在博洛尼亚被处决。

en:
Bailardino Nogarola (c. 1270–1340) was a Veronese nobleman, diplomat and condottiero who spent his life in the service of the della Scala lords of Verona. He joined them young and was knighted in 1295 together with Bartolomeo and Cangrande, sons of Lord Alberto I della Scala.

For the family he served as podestà of several cities, and in 1311 went to Milan as Scaliger ambassador to meet Emperor Henry VII.

When Cangrande died on 22 July 1329, Bailardino managed the passing of power to his nephews Mastino II and Alberto II della Scala. He died at Nogarole Rocca on 24 October 1340 and was given a solemn funeral.

巴伊拉尔多·诺加罗拉（约1270—1340）是维罗纳贵族、外交官与雇佣兵首领，一生效力于统治维罗纳的德拉·斯卡拉家族。他年轻时便投身该家族，1295年与维罗纳领主阿尔贝托一世·德拉·斯卡拉之子巴尔托洛梅奥和坎格兰德一同受封骑士。

他为家族出任数座城市的最高行政官，1311年作为斯卡拉家族的使节赴米兰觐见皇帝亨利七世。

1329年7月22日坎格兰德去世，他主持权力交接，由坎格兰德的侄子马斯蒂诺二世和阿尔贝托二世接掌。1340年10月24日，他卒于诺加罗莱罗卡，获隆重葬礼。

Bartolomeo I della Scala (1270–1304), eldest son of Alberto I and Verde di Salizzole, ruled Verona as lord from 1301. On succeeding he stripped the guilds' council of its remaining authority.

In 1291 he married Costanza di Antiochia. He sheltered the exiled Dante at his court, and Dante later praised him as il gran Lombardo in Paradise XVII. Bartolomeo died on 7 March 1304 and was succeeded by his brother Alboino.

Beatrice da Camino (died 1388) was the daughter of Rizzardo VI da Camino, lord of Serravalle, and Verde della Scala of Verona. When her father died in 1335 without a son, she was pushed aside in the succession struggle over the family fiefs. In 1351 she married Aldobrandino III d'Este of Ferrara.

She later joined the conspiracy of her son Obizzo IV against Alberto V d'Este; when it failed, she was beheaded with him at Ferrara in 1388.

en:
Beatrice Regina della Scala (1333–1384) was the youngest daughter of Mastino II della Scala, lord of Verona, and Taddea da Carrara. In 1350 she married Bernabò Visconti in Verona, a match sealing peace between the Scaligeri and expansionist Milan. When Bernabò took power as lord of Milan in 1354, she became lady of the city and his political adviser.

She was the mother of numerous children, whose marriages linked Milan to ruling houses across Europe. She died in 1384.

Cagnolo Nogarola was a Veronese nobleman of the French-descended Nogarola family, the son of Bailardino Nogarola, a condottiero and ambassador for the della Scala lords.

He is remembered as a resident of the medieval brick house near the Scaliger tombs in Verona that later tradition identified as Romeo's home. Cagnolo died in 1359 without children, and under his father's will his entire patrimony passed to the della Scala.

en:
Cangrande II della Scala (1332–1359) was the eldest son of Mastino II della Scala and Taddea da Carrara. In 1350 he married Elizabeth, daughter of Emperor Louis IV, and in 1351 inherited the lordship of Verona and Vicenza, at first under the regency of his uncle Alberto II.

Nicknamed Can Rabbioso, the Raging Dog, he governed harshly with Brandenburg mercenaries and built Castelvecchio and its fortified bridge as a refuge. In 1359 his brother Cansignorio, aided by the Carraresi of Padua, assassinated him.

坎格兰德二世·德拉·斯卡拉（1332—1359）是马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉与塔代亚·达·卡拉拉的长子。1350年他迎娶皇帝路德维希四世之女伊丽莎白，1351年继承维罗纳与维琴察领主之位，起初由叔父阿尔贝托二世摄政。
