en:
Cangrande I della Scala (9 March 1291 – 22 July 1329), third son of Alberto I and Verde di Salizzole, was nicknamed Cangrande, the great dog. He ruled Verona jointly with his brother Alboino from 1308 and alone from 1311, when Henry VII named him imperial vicar.

As leader of the Ghibellines he took Vicenza from Padua, seized Padua in 1328 and entered Treviso in 1329. He was the chief patron of the exiled Dante.

Cangrande died at Treviso on 22 July 1329, his illness attributed to polluted spring water. His nephews Mastino II and Alberto II succeeded him.

坎格兰德一世·德拉·斯卡拉（1291年3月9日—1329年7月22日）是阿尔贝托一世与维尔德·迪·萨利佐莱的第三子，绰号“坎格兰德”，意为“大狗”。1308年起他与兄长阿尔博伊诺共同统治维罗纳，1311年亨利七世任命他为帝国代理官后独掌大权。

作为吉伯林派的领袖，他从帕多瓦手中夺得维琴察，1328年攻占帕多瓦，1329年7月入主特雷维索。他也是流亡诗人但丁最主要的庇护人。

1329年7月22日，他在特雷维索去世；同时代记载称他的病是饮用受污染的泉水所致。侄辈马斯蒂诺二世与阿尔贝托二世继位。

Catherine da Camino was the daughter of the Trevisan noble Rizzardo VII da Camino. In 1331 her father made peace with the della Scala of Verona by betrothing her, still a child, to a natural son of Alberto II della Scala.

The match did not take place, and in 1339 she became the second wife of Bertoldo I d'Este, marquis of Este. She was widowed when Bertoldo died in 1343.

Caterina Visconti (1282–1311) was a Milanese noblewoman, the daughter of Matteo I Visconti, lord of Milan, and Bonacossa Borri. In 1298 she married Alboino della Scala, who became lord of Verona in 1304, linking the rising Visconti and Scaliger houses.

The marriage produced daughters, among them Alboina, who became abbess of San Michele in Campagna near Verona. Caterina died in Verona in 1311, the year Alboino and his brother Cangrande were named imperial vicars.

en:
Fregnano della Scala (c. 1331–1354) was a natural son of Mastino II, the lord who in 1339 had been cut back to Verona and Vicenza; his half-brother Cangrande II now held Verona. Fregnano began as a soldier in 1350, sent to help the papal rector of Romagna against the Manfredi lords of Faenza.

In 1354, while Cangrande was away at Bolzano, he joined a revolt backed by the Gonzaga of Mantua, named Paolo Pico podestà and proclaimed himself lord. Cangrande rushed back and on 25 February fought him at the Ponte Navi, where Fregnano fell into the Adige. His body was fished out and hung for days in the Piazza delle Erbe with other rebels.

1354年，趁坎格兰德二世前往博尔扎诺，他在曼托瓦贡扎加家族支持下参与叛乱，任命保罗·皮科为最高行政长官，并自立为领主。坎格兰德火速赶回，2月25日在纳维桥与他交战，弗雷尼亚诺坠入阿迪杰河。他的尸体被捞起，与其他叛乱者一起吊在百草广场示众多日。

en:
Gherardo V da Camino (1290s–1349) was a nobleman of the March of Treviso, of the family's lower branch, the son of Guecellone VIII da Camino. From the 1320s he and his brother Rizzardo VII fought the della Scala of Verona in alliance with Venice.

After the senior branch's Rizzardo VI died without male heirs in 1335, they seized Serravalle in 1337, but Venice eventually annexed the fortress. The brothers divided their fiefs in 1340, and Gherardo died around 1349, leaving a young son, Guecellone IX.

盖拉尔多五世·达·卡米诺（1290年代—1349）是特雷维索边区贵族，属达·卡米诺家族的“下支”，为圭切洛内八世·达·卡米诺之子。从1320年代起，他与兄弟里扎尔多七世联合威尼斯对抗维罗纳的德拉·斯卡拉家族。

1335年长支的里扎尔多六世去世且无男嗣，二人于1337年夺取塞拉瓦莱，但威尼斯最终吞并了这座要塞。1340年兄弟瓜分封地；盖拉尔多约于1349年去世，留下幼子圭切洛内九世。

Giacomo de' Rossi (died c. 1370) was the son of Rolando de' Rossi and Agnese Ruggeri. After his father's bid to rule Parma had failed, the Rossi settled for a much smaller lordship, and Giacomo became its first count.

With his brother Bertrando he lent the debt-ridden cathedral chapter of Parma large sums, and in 1365 the chapter gave the brothers the lands of San Secondo in compensation. In 1367, after Bertrando died, Giacomo was enfeoffed with San Secondo; the next year its inhabitants swore him fealty, a sign that Rossi power there was already rooted.

In his will of August 1370 he left the county to his nephew Bertrando the younger, though his own son Rolando held it de facto until 1389.

贾科莫·德·罗西（？—约1370）是罗兰多·德·罗西与阿涅塞·鲁杰里之子。父亲统治帕尔马的计划落空后，罗西家族退而经营一块小得多的领地，贾科莫成了这块领地的首任伯爵。

他与兄弟贝特朗多次向债台高筑的帕尔马主教座堂教务会借款，1365年教务会把圣塞孔多的土地抵给兄弟二人作补偿。1367年贝特朗去世后，贾科莫受封圣塞孔多；次年当地臣民向他宣誓效忠，可见罗西家族的权力在当地早已扎根。

1370年8月他立下遗嘱，把伯国传给侄子小贝特朗，但他自己的儿子罗兰多实际统治该地直到1389年。

Giberto da Fogliano (c. 1280–c. 1372), son of Niccolò da Fogliano and Caterina della Scala, was a condottiero who spent much of his life trying to retake Reggio nell'Emilia. In 1328 his family drove out the city's papal governor, and he sided with the Ghibellines under Louis the Bavarian, becoming imperial vicar of Reggio.

In 1335 the city passed to the Gonzaga, and he withdrew to Verona to serve the Scaligeri. Captured defending Treviso for Mastino II in 1336, he was freed three years later. A siege of Reggio in 1344 ended in his capture, and the Gonzaga tore down his buildings in revenge; a 1354 attempt also failed.

He then backed the Visconti, but their truce of 1369 again went against him, and he was imprisoned with his family, probably dying in 1372.

吉贝托·达·福利亚诺（约1280—约1372）是雇佣兵首领，尼科洛·达·福利亚诺与卡泰丽娜·德拉·斯卡拉之子，一生大半在设法夺回雷焦艾米利亚。1328年，福利亚诺家族把雷焦的教皇总督逐走；巴伐利亚人路德维希南下意大利时，吉贝托站到吉伯林派一边，出任雷焦的皇帝代理人。

1335年雷焦转入贡扎加家族之手，他退居维罗纳，效力于斯卡拉家族。1336年他为马斯蒂诺二世防守特雷维索时被俘，三年后获释。1344年他围攻雷焦，再度被俘，贡扎加家族为泄愤拆毁了他的许多建筑；1354年他再度尝试，仍告失败。

此后他倒向维斯孔蒂家族，但1369年的休战对他不利，他与家人一同被囚，约1372年去世。

Joanna of Swabia (c. 1280–1352) was the daughter of Conrad of Antiochia, grandson of Emperor Frederick II, by Beatrice Lancia. While travelling to Germany to marry a nobleman she had never met, she stopped at Verona as guest of her sister Constance, wife of Bartolomeo I della Scala.

Cangrande I della Scala fell in love with her and married her in 1308. The marriage was childless, though Cangrande left several illegitimate children. She died in 1352.

施瓦本的乔万娜（约1280—1352）是安条克的康拉德之女；康拉德是皇帝腓特烈二世的孙子，母亲为贝亚特里切·兰恰。她在前往德意志、准备嫁给一位素未谋面的贵族途中，在维罗纳停留，做客于姊妹科斯坦扎家中，科斯坦扎是巴尔托洛梅奥一世·德拉·斯卡拉之妻。

Giovanni II Castracani (born c. 1337) was a son of Valeriano Castracani, lord of Monteriggioni, and a grandson of Castruccio Castracani, the Ghibelline duke of Lucca.

He grew up while his family, dispossessed of Lucca, lived the life of exiled condottieri: in 1356 his father commanded about a thousand horsemen for Bernabò Visconti in the Reggio country and fought at Casorate, and he died around 1362. No public career of Giovanni's own is recorded.

Giovanni da Correggio (died c. 1363) was a nobleman and condottiero, son of Giberto III da Correggio of Parma. In 1341 he was captured at Parma when his brothers drove out the Scaligeri. After quarrelling with his brother Guido he was forced to cede Castelnuovo in 1344.

He then entered Este service, was captured by Feltrino Gonzaga, and was released only in 1345. He died around 1363, leaving a son Antonio, a Visconti knight.

en:
Guecello Tempesta (c. 1288–1338) was a Trevisan noble and leader of the city's pro-Scaliger faction. In 1327, after two years in exile, he survived an assassination attempt at a wedding in Treviso, raised mercenaries at Noale and seized the city, executing his rivals.

He surrendered Treviso to Cangrande I della Scala in 1329 and served the Scaligeri as podestà of Verona. Switching sides in 1337, he took a Venetian command, but died in 1338, after which Venice dismantled his signoria.

Guecellone VIII da Camino (after 1285–1332) was a knight, the son of Biaquino VI da Camino. In 1315 he served the commune of Treviso, and from 1318 he served Venice for a thousand ducats a year, becoming lord of Oderzo. He fought the Scaligeri expanding into the March of Treviso and was imprisoned in Verona.

In 1326 he tried to seize Motta and Camino from his cousin Biaquino VII. He died in January or February 1332, leaving sons Gherardo V and Rizzardo VII by Beatrice da Prata.

zh:
圭切洛内八世·达·卡米诺（1285年后—1332）是一名骑士，比亚奎诺六世·达·卡米诺之子。1315年他效力于特雷维索公社，1318年起为威尼斯服役，年俸一千达克特，并成为奥德尔佐领主。他抵抗斯卡拉家族向特雷维索边区扩张，曾被俘虏关押在维罗纳。

1326年，他试图从堂兄弟比亚奎诺七世手中夺取莫塔和卡米诺城堡。他于1332年1月或2月去世，与妻子贝阿特丽切·达·普拉塔生有儿子格拉尔多五世和里扎尔多七世。

Guido Savina da Fogliano was a son of Giberto da Fogliano, who long fought for the lordship of Reggio Emilia. He married Camilla da Canossa, and their son Carlo, born around 1350, became a prominent condottiero in the wars over Reggio.

In 1373 Guido Savina made a pact with Bernabò Visconti, lord of Milan, who confirmed his jurisdiction over his lands. He died in 1379.

圭多·萨维纳·达·福利亚诺是吉贝托·达·福利亚诺之子，其父长期争夺雷焦艾米利亚的统治权。他娶卡米拉·达·卡诺萨为妻；儿子卡洛约生于1350年，后来成为争夺雷焦战事中的著名将领。

en:
Jacopino della Scala (12th century–after 1248) was a Veronese wool merchant and politician, father of the first Scaliger lords of Verona. A grandson of Balduino della Scala, he held no noble titles and no great fortune, but was known as an able, peace-loving politician.

He served as imperial vicar of Ostiglia. By his first wife Margherita Giustiniani he had a son Manfredo, later bishop of Verona, and by his second wife Elisa Superbi he fathered Mastino I and Alberto I, the first Scaliger lords.

雅各皮诺·德拉·斯卡拉（12世纪—1248年后）是维罗纳的羊毛商人与政治家，斯卡拉家族最早几代维罗纳之主的父亲。作为巴尔杜伊诺·德拉·斯卡拉之孙，他没有贵族头衔，也无丰厚家产，却是一位有才干、有威望且倾向和平的政治家。

他出任过奥斯蒂利亚的皇帝代理人。他与第一任妻子玛格丽塔·朱斯蒂尼亚尼生有曼弗雷多，后者曾任维罗纳主教；与第二任妻子埃莉萨·苏佩尔比生有马斯蒂诺一世和阿尔贝托一世，二人后来成为斯卡拉家族最早的维罗纳之主。

Maddalena de' Rossi was a Parmese noblewoman, daughter of Guglielmo de' Rossi and Donella da Carrara of Padua. She married Gherardo V da Camino, a lord of the feudal family of the March of Treviso.

en:
Mastino I della Scala, born Leonardino, was the son of Jacopino della Scala and founder of Scaliger rule in Verona. A Ghibelline, he became podestà of Verona in 1259 and capitano del popolo from 1262, controlling the commune through its offices without a lordly title.

In 1264 his troops took Lonigo and Montebello and he won Veronese trading rights on the Adige from Venice. He also made peace with Mantua.

Backing Conradin in 1267 earned him excommunication, lifted after Cathars were burned in the Arena. He was assassinated in Verona in October 1277 and succeeded by his brother Alberto I.

马斯蒂诺一世·德拉·斯卡拉本名莱奥纳尔迪诺，是雅各皮诺·德拉·斯卡拉之子，也是斯卡拉家族在维罗纳统治的奠基人。作为吉伯林派成员，他于1259年成为维罗纳最高行政长官，1262年起任人民领袖，不靠单一领主头衔而通过多个官职控制全城。

1264年，他的军队攻取洛尼戈和蒙特贝洛，又从威尼斯争取到维罗纳人在阿迪杰河的通商权。他还与曼托瓦议和。

1267年他支持康拉丁而被开除教籍，后来在竞技场烧死清洁派信徒后才解除。1277年10月他在维罗纳遇刺，其弟阿尔贝托一世继位。

en:
Mastino II della Scala (1308–1351), son of Alboino I and Beatrice da Correggio, ruled Verona jointly with his brother Alberto II after Cangrande I died in 1329, but held the real power. He gave up his father's cautious balancing for conquest: he fought John of Bohemia in 1332, took Brescia that year, and won Parma and Lucca in 1335.

Florence, Venice and other cities formed a league against him, and by 1337 Milan under the Visconti and the Papal States had joined it. In 1338 he stabbed his cousin Bartolomeo, bishop of Verona.

In 1339 the mercenaries he backed against Milan lost at Parabiago, and Emperor Louis IV mediated a peace that left him only Verona and Vicenza. He died in Verona on 3 June 1351 and lies in the Scaliger Tombs by Santa Maria Antica.

马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉（1308—1351）是阿尔博伊诺一世与贝阿特丽切·达·科雷焦之子。1329年坎格兰德一世去世后，他与兄长阿尔贝托二世共同执掌维罗纳，实权却在他手里。他抛开父亲谨慎的均势政策转向扩张：1332年与波希米亚的约翰作战，同年夺取布雷西亚，1335年又拿下帕尔马和卢卡。

佛罗伦萨、威尼斯等城市结盟对付他，到1337年，米兰的维斯孔蒂和教皇国也加入同盟。1338年，他刺死堂兄弟、维罗纳主教巴尔托洛梅奥。

1339年，他支持的雇佣兵在帕拉比亚戈战败，皇帝路德维希四世出面调停，他只保住维罗纳和维琴察。1351年6月3日他在维罗纳去世，葬于老圣玛利亚教堂旁的斯卡拉陵墓。

en:
Orlando Castracani was a son of the Lucchese condottiero Arrigo Castracani (1304–1357), eldest son and heir of Duke Castruccio Castracani, and of Costanza de' Rossi, whom Arrigo married at Parma in 1334. He grew up in exile while his father fought for Venice, the Scaligeri and the Visconti.

Bolognese records give him four sons: Castruccio, Enrico, Francesco and Rolando. His son Francesco, called Fibbia, fled to Bologna early in the fifteenth century, took service with the Bentivoglio as a commander, and gave his descendants the name Fibbia.

奥兰多·卡斯特拉卡尼是卢卡雇佣军首领阿里戈·卡斯特拉卡尼（1304—1357）与科斯坦扎·德·罗西之子；阿里戈是卢卡公爵卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼的长子，1334年在帕尔马娶了科斯坦扎。奥兰多在流亡中长大，父亲先后为威尼斯、斯卡利杰家族和维斯孔蒂家族作战。

据博洛尼亚史料记载，奥兰多有卡斯特鲁乔、恩里科、弗朗切斯科、罗兰多四个儿子；其子弗朗切斯科绰号菲比亚，15世纪初流亡博洛尼亚，投靠本蒂沃利奥家族担任军队统帅，后裔从此以菲比亚为姓。

据博洛尼亚史料记载，奥兰多有卡斯特鲁乔、恩里科、弗朗切斯科、罗兰多四个儿子；其子弗朗切斯科绰号菲比亚，15世纪初流亡博洛尼亚，投靠本蒂沃利奥家族担任军队统帅，后裔从此以菲比亚为姓。

en:
Pietro Dal Verme (c. 1300–1357) was a Veronese condottiero and diplomat, the founder of his family's fortunes, who rose with the Scaligers. A trusted officer of Cangrande della Scala, he was knighted after the taking of Padua in 1328.

From 1329 to 1337 he governed newly won Treviso as podestà, a hard post of strained relations with Venice. In 1337 the Venetian–Florentine league overran the Scaliger strongholds one by one; he held Monselice, the last of them, for a year, and his garrison killed the league's commander. In August 1338 he surrendered the starving town, riding out armed under Scaliger banners with his men and townspeople unharmed.

Captured when Lucca fell to Pisa in 1342, he backed Fregnano della Scala's failed coup in 1354 and was exiled with his sons. He died at Brescia in 1357, and the break left his house free to build its own power.

彼得罗·达尔·韦尔梅（约1300—1357）是维罗纳的雇佣兵首领与外交官，随斯卡拉家族崛起，奠定了达尔·韦尔梅家族的基业。作为坎格兰德·德拉·斯卡拉信任的将领，他在1328年攻占帕多瓦后受封骑士。

1329—1337年，他出任新攻占的特雷维索的最高行政官，应付与威尼斯的紧张关系。1337年威尼斯与佛罗伦萨的联盟接连攻克斯卡拉家族的据点，他守住最后一处蒙塞利切达一年，守军还杀死了联盟统帅。1338年8月，他交出饥饿的城镇，全副武装、打着斯卡拉旗号骑马出城，部下和居民安然无恙。

1342年卢卡落入比萨之手时他被俘；1354年他支持弗雷尼亚诺·德拉·斯卡拉的未遂政变，与儿子们一同被放逐。他于1357年卒于布雷西亚，这次决裂也让他的家族得以自立门户。

Pietro della Scala (c. 1330–1393) was an illegitimate son of Mastino II della Scala, lord of Verona. In 1350 he was consecrated bishop of his native city, where he restored the property and rights Cansignorio della Scala had taken from the clergy.

After the Scaligeri lost Verona in 1387, Gian Galeazzo Visconti persuaded Pope Urban VI to move him to Lodi. Driven from Lodi in 1390, he took refuge in Mantua and died there in 1393, leaving three natural sons.

en:
Redondello dalle Carceri, also called Rotondello, was a Veronese nobleman, brother of Ravano dalle Carceri, triarch of Negroponte. He is recorded as podestà of Verona in 1210.

His sons Marino, Rizzardo and Nicolò sought their fortunes in Frankish Euboea; Ravano had adopted Marino and Rizzardo before his own marriage, and when he died in 1216 the Venetian bailo partitioned the island in 1217, assigning the northern triarchy of Oreoi to the two brothers. Marino wed Margherita, daughter of the former northern triarch, and Rizzardo died in 1220, leaving a daughter, Carintana.

雷东代洛·达莱·卡尔切里（一作罗通代洛）是维罗纳贵族，内格罗蓬特三头统治者拉瓦诺·达莱·卡尔切里的兄弟。史料载他1210年出任维罗纳波德斯塔。

他的儿子马里诺、里扎尔多和尼科洛前往法兰克人治下的优卑亚岛谋生；拉万在婚前已收养马里诺与里扎尔多。1216年拉万去世后，威尼斯巴约于1217年主持瓜分该岛，两兄弟分得首府在奥雷伊的北部三分之一。马里诺娶了原北部三头统治者的女儿玛格丽塔，里扎尔多于1220年去世，遗有一女卡林塔纳。

Rizzardo VI da Camino, called Rizzardo Novello (late 13th century – 12 September 1335), was an Italian condottiero, the son of Guecellone VII da Camino. Under an accord with the Scaligeri he married Verde, daughter of Alboino della Scala. After the Scaligeri occupied Serravalle in 1324, he recovered his domains in 1329.

He later invaded western Friuli and took Sacile in 1333, but Patriarch Bertrando of Aquileia defeated him and revoked his fiefs. Mortally wounded, he died at Serravalle, leaving three daughters.

里扎尔多六世·达·卡米诺，人称‘小里扎尔多’（13世纪末—1335年9月12日），是意大利佣兵首领，圭切洛内七世·达·卡米诺之子。根据家族与斯卡拉家族的协议，他娶了阿尔博伊诺·德拉·斯卡拉之女维尔德。1324年斯卡拉家族占领塞拉瓦莱后，他于1329年收复领地。

en:
Rizzardo VII da Camino (1290s–before 1358), son of Guecellone VIII and Beatrice da Prata, belonged to the lower branch of the Caminesi feudal family of the Trevisan March. With his brother he stood high at Treviso, and after 1327 they drifted from the Scaligeri towards Venice.

When Rizzardo VI died in 1335 without male heirs, the brothers claimed his inheritance against his widow Verde della Scala and in 1337 occupied Serravalle. The alarmed bishop of Ceneda offered the family's fiefs to Venice on forged documents. His plot against the bishop failed in 1340, and the brothers divided their lands.

In 1345, with Venice mediating, the bishop invested them at Ceneda and they entered the Venetian patriciate. He left a son Tolberto IV and a daughter Caterina, wed to Bertoldo I d'Este.

里扎尔多七世·达·卡米诺（1290年代—1358年前）是圭切洛内八世与贝阿特丽切·达·普拉塔之子，属于特雷维索边区卡米诺封建家族的“下支”。他与兄弟在特雷维索颇有声望，1327年之后两人渐渐疏远斯卡拉家族、靠近威尼斯。

1335年，里扎尔多六世去世，没有男性继承人，兄弟二人便与其遗孀维尔德·德拉·斯卡拉争夺遗产，1337年占领塞拉瓦莱。忌惮他们崛起的切内达主教随即凭伪造文书把该家族的封地献给威尼斯。1340年，他反对主教的密谋失败，兄弟二人瓜分了领地。

1345年，在威尼斯斡旋下，主教在切内达册封兄弟二人，他们也进入威尼斯贵族阶层。他留有儿子托尔贝托四世和嫁与贝特霍尔德一世·埃斯特的女儿卡特琳娜。

Simon da Correggio (died 1344) was an Emilian condottiero, son of Giberto III da Correggio. In 1323 he took the Guelph side when Piacenza was seized from the Visconti, then changed sides and fought for Cangrande I della Scala against Padua.

Driven out of Parma by the Rossi in 1329, he returned with Scaliger help in 1331 and in 1341 made himself, with his brothers, lord of Parma. He died in 1344, leaving a daughter Jacopina, wife of Ubertino da Carrara of Padua.

Taddea da Carrara (c. 1304–1375) was the daughter of Jacopo I da Carrara, lord of Padua, and Elisabetta Gradenigo. In 1328 she married Mastino II della Scala, lord of Verona and Lucca, sealing the Scaliger-Carrara alliance, and bore him seven children.

Her sons Cangrande II, Cansignorio and Paolo Alboino each ruled Verona, while her daughters married into the Visconti and the Este of Ferrara. She died in 1375.

Tolberto IV da Camino (died 1360) was a nobleman of the March of Treviso, the son of Rizzardo VII da Camino. While he and Leonardina della Torre were still children, their marriage was arranged to reconcile his father with her kinsman, the patriarch of Aquileia.

By 1358 he was lord of Solighetto, his family having recovered part of the lands lost in quarrels with Venice and Ceneda's bishop. That year Treviso's Council of Three Hundred called him as a judge. He died in 1360.

Uguccione della Faggiola (c. 1250–1319) was a Ghibelline condottiero who became virtual lord of Pisa and Lucca. A former imperial vicar, he took power in Pisa in 1313 and sacked Lucca in 1314 with his protégé Castruccio Castracani.

In August 1315 he crushed the Florentine Guelphs and their Angevin allies at Montecatini. Driven out of Pisa in 1316 over his authoritarian rule and heavy taxes, he served Cangrande I della Scala as podestà of Vicenza and died of malaria on 1 November 1319 during the siege of Padua.

乌古乔内·德拉·法焦拉（约1250—1319）是吉伯林派雇佣兵首领，曾实际统治比萨与卢卡。他曾任皇帝代理人，1313年入主比萨，1314年在门生卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼协助下洗劫卢卡。

Valeriano Castracani was a son of Castruccio Castracani, lord of Lucca. Still a boy when his father died in 1328, he was driven from Lucca after the Guelf restoration and became a condottiero.

In 1356 he led a thousand cavalry for Bernabò Visconti against the anti-Visconti league, but was beaten at San Polo d'Enza in February. Later that year he led Milanese skirmishers whose feigned retreat drew Count Lando's company into the trap at Casorate, giving the Visconti a decisive victory.

Verde della Scala was the daughter of Alboino I della Scala, lord of Verona, by his first wife Caterina Visconti. In 1316 she married Rizzardo VI da Camino, lord of Treviso, and bore him three daughters: Caterina, Ricciarda and Beatrice, who married into the Pepoli of Bologna and the Este.

After Rizzardo's death she was married again in 1340, to Ugolino Gonzaga, future co-lord of Mantua. She died in Mantua that same year without children by Gonzaga, and was buried in the cathedral of St Peter.

en:
Veronica Franco (c. 1546–1591) was a Venetian poet and a cortigiana onesta, an honoured courtesan whose humanist learning gave her access to Venice's leading literary circles. As a girl she received a humanist education from her brother's tutor.

Briefly married as a teenager, she was listed among Venice's leading courtesans in 1565 and joined Domenico Venier's salon. She published two books, of verse in 1575 and of letters in 1580.

After she left Venice during the plague of 1575, her home and possessions were looted and she lost much of her wealth. Charged with witchcraft before the Inquisition in 1577, she successfully defended herself, but died in poverty in 1591.

韦罗妮卡·佛朗哥（约1546—1591）是威尼斯诗人，也是一名“体面的交际花”，凭借人文修养出入威尼斯的上流文学圈。她年幼时便从兄弟的家庭教师那里接受人文教育。

她十几岁时曾短暂嫁人，1565年被列入威尼斯名妓名录，后加入多梅尼科·韦涅尔的沙龙。她于1575年和1580年分别出版了一部诗集和一部书信集。

1575年鼠疫期间她离开威尼斯，住宅和财物遭劫，损失了大部分财富。1577年她被宗教裁判所以施行巫术的罪名起诉，亲自辩护后指控被撤销，最终于1591年在贫困中去世。

en:
Henry II of Vianden (died 1337) was the last male of his house. Son of Count Philip II, he held the county from 1315 or 1316 jointly with his sister Adelaide, and in 1335 or 1336 he married Marie of Namur.

In 1337 he set out for the Holy Land by way of Cyprus with his brother-in-law Philip III of Namur, but at Famagusta their conduct was so dissolute that the townspeople killed them and their companions. Both were buried in the town's Franciscan church.

Henry's infant daughter Marie inherited Vianden; in 1417 her daughter Elisabeth gave up her rights to Engelbert I of Nassau-Dillenburg, a grandson of Adelaide, who became Count of Vianden.

en:
Maria of Vianden (1337–1400) was the posthumous daughter and heiress of Count Henry II, who was killed at Famagusta in Cyprus in September 1337; she inherited Vianden as an infant.

Her mother, Marie of Namur, married again around 1340, and in 1348 (or in 1346) Maria was married to Simon III, Count of Sponheim-Kreuznach, who ruled Vianden in her right and from 1357 also held other Luxembourg fiefs. Simon was taken prisoner in 1371 and freed after several years and a heavy ransom.

Her son Walram died in 1382 and her daughter Maria in 1373; her surviving daughter Elisabeth, twice widowed and childless, surrendered Vianden in 1417 to Engelbert I of Nassau-Dillenburg.

菲安登的玛丽（1337—1400）是伯爵亨利二世的遗腹女和继承人：1337年9月，亨利于塞浦路斯的法马古斯塔被杀，她在襁褓中即继承菲安登。

母亲那慕尔的玛丽约在1340年改嫁，玛丽本人则于1348年（一说1346年）嫁给斯蓬海姆-克罗伊茨纳赫伯爵西蒙三世，由后者以妻权统治菲安登，并自1357年起另领有多处卢森堡封邑。1371年西蒙被俘，数年后才以重金赎出。

她的儿子瓦勒拉姆于1382年去世，女儿玛丽于1373年去世；在世的女儿伊丽莎白两度丧夫且无子嗣，于1417年将菲安登交给拿骚-迪伦堡的恩格尔贝特一世。

en:
Marie de Namur (1322 – before 1353) was a daughter of John I, Marquis of Namur, and Marie of Artois, and a sister of Blanche of Namur, queen of Sweden.

In 1335 or 1336 she married Count Henry II of Vianden, who was murdered at Famagusta in September 1337; their daughter Maria inherited Vianden and married Simon III of Sponheim. In 1340 Marie married Theobald of Bar, lord of Pierrepont, by whom she had two more daughters, Yolande and Elisabeth.

en:
Bhavana Sangama, also called simply Sangama, was a chieftain of a pastoralist shepherd community in the Karnataka country, remembered above all as the father of the founders of the Vijayanagara Empire.

He married Maravve Nayakiti, daughter of Kampili Deva Raya, king of Kampili, and elder sister of Prince Kumara Rama. His five sons were Harihara, Bukka, Kampa, Marappa and Muddappa; the eldest two, Harihara and Bukka, went on to found Vijayanagara in 1336.

巴瓦纳·桑迦摩又简称桑迦摩，是卡纳塔克地区一个游牧牧人社群的首领，最主要的身份是毗奢耶那伽罗帝国开创者们的父亲。

他娶剑毕离国王坎皮利·提婆·罗耶之女、库马拉·拉马王子的姐姐马拉夫·那雅吉蒂为妻。他有五个儿子：哈里哈拉、布卡、坎帕、马拉帕和穆达帕；其中长子哈里哈拉与布卡后来于1336年开创了毗奢耶那伽罗帝国。

en:
Bukka Raya I (died 1377), a son of Bhavana Sangama, ruled the Vijayanagara Empire from 1356, succeeding his brother Harihara I. By 1360 he had conquered the Shambuvaraya kingdom of Arcot and the Reddis of Kondavidu, and in 1371 his son Kumara Kampana overthrew the Sultanate of Madurai.

By 1374 Bukka held the upper hand against the Bahmani Sultanate, took Goa, and forced Jaffna to pay tribute. He died in February 1377 and was followed by his son Harihara II.

en:
Harihara I (1306–1355), also called Hakka, was the eldest son of Bhavana Sangama and founder of the Vijayanagara Empire, ruling from 1336 until his death. One theory holds that he and his brother Bukka served the Kakatiya king of Warangal, were carried to Delhi after its fall, escaped and returned to Hinduism under sage Vidyaranya.

By 1339 inscriptions show him governing northern Karnataka from Gooty. When Veera Ballala III died fighting the Sultan of Madurai in 1343, Harihara took over all Hoysala territories and extended his rule to parts of the Konkan and Malabar coasts. Kannada inscriptions call him ‘fire to enemy kings’.

A 1346 Sringeri monastery grant calls him ruler of the country between the eastern and western seas, with Vidya Nagara as capital. He died on 20 November 1355 and was succeeded by Bukka, who moved the capital from Anegondi to Vijayanagara. The empire lasted until 1646.

zh:
哈里哈拉一世（1306—1355）又名哈卡，是巴瓦纳·桑迦摩的长子、毗奢耶那伽罗帝国的开创者，自1336年起统治该国，直至去世。据一种说法，他与弟弟布卡原本效力于瓦朗加尔的卡卡提亚国王，瓦朗加尔陷落后二人被押往德里，逃脱后在圣者维迪亚兰尼亚的影响下重新皈依印度教。

铭文显示，1339年他已在古蒂治理卡纳塔克北部。1343年，维拉·巴拉拉三世在对马杜赖苏丹的战争中阵亡，哈里哈拉接管了霍伊萨拉的全部领土，并把统治扩展到孔卡纳和马拉巴尔海岸的一部分。卡纳达语铭文称他是“敌王之火”。

1346年一份赐给斯林盖里寺院的文书称他统治着东西两洋之间的国土，以维迪亚纳伽拉为都城。1355年11月20日他去世，由布卡继位，布卡把都城从阿讷贡迪迁到毗奢耶那伽罗。这个帝国一直延续到1646年。

en:
Kampilideva was the second and last king of the Kampili kingdom, succeeding his father Singeya Nayaka III in 1300. With his son Kumara Rama he fought wars against the Kakatiyas, the Hoysalas and the Delhi Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

In 1327/1328 Tughlaq's armies invaded the kingdom. When defeat became certain the royal women performed jauhar, and Kampilideva and Kumara Rama fell fighting. Its fall preceded the rise of the Vijayanagara Empire under Harihara and Bukka.

坎比梨德瓦是剑毕离王国第二任也是末代国王，1300年继承父亲辛吉亚·纳亚卡三世。他与王子库马拉·罗摩连年征战，对手包括卡卡提耶王朝、曷萨拉王朝和德里苏丹穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克。

en:
Vittorino da Feltre (1378–1446), born Vittorino Rambaldoni in Feltre, was an Italian humanist and celebrated Renaissance teacher. After studying and teaching at Padua, he was summoned by Gianfrancesco I Gonzaga, marquis of Mantua, to educate his children, and founded the boarding school La Casa Gioiosa.

There noble children and poor pupils taught free of charge studied Greek, Latin, mathematics and music alongside physical exercise. He lived with his students, adapted teaching to their abilities and added field trips to the curriculum; his methods made the school a model copied across Europe. He died in Mantua in 1446.

费尔特雷的维多里诺（1378—1446），本名维多里诺·兰巴尔多尼，生于费尔特雷，是意大利人文主义者、文艺复兴时期最负盛名的教师之一。他在帕多瓦求学并任教，后应曼托瓦侯爵詹弗朗切斯科一世·贡扎加之聘教导其子女，并创办寄宿学校“欢乐之家”。

贵族子女与免收学费的贫家子弟在那里同堂学习希腊文、拉丁文、数学、音乐及体育。他与学生共同生活，按学生能力调整教学，并加入实地游学；其教学法使学校成为全欧效仿的典范。1446年他卒于曼托瓦。

贵族子女与免收学费的贫家子弟在那里同堂学习希腊文、拉丁文、数学、音乐及体育。他与学生共同生活，按学生能力调整教学，并加入实地游学；其教学法使学校成为全欧效仿的典范。1446年他卒于曼托瓦。

en:
Aymar I of Poitiers (c. 1115–1163) was the first count of Valentinois from the Poitiers dynasty. Around 1135 he acquired the county through his marriage to Rixende, possibly the sister or natural daughter of Eustache, bishop of Valence.

In 1157 the Emperor Frederick Barbarossa granted temporal lordship over thirteen parishes to the bishop of Valence, Odon de Crussol, who then also claimed the comital title. Aymar's son William I succeeded him around 1160.

普瓦捷的艾马尔一世（约1115—1163）是普瓦捷王朝的首任瓦朗蒂努瓦伯爵。约1135年，他通过与里克桑德联姻取得伯国；里克桑德可能是瓦朗斯主教厄斯塔什的姊妹或私生女。

1157年，皇帝腓特烈一世把十三个堂区的世俗管辖权授予瓦朗斯主教奥东·德·克吕索勒，后者遂也自称伯爵。约1160年，其子威廉一世继位。

en:
Aymar II de Poitiers (c. 1180–1250) was count of Valentinois. Son of William I, he succeeded around 1189 and that year received the Diois in fief from Raymond V of Toulouse. Around 1195 he joined an Occitan poetic debate with troubadour Raimbaut de Vaqueiras.

He backed Toulouse in the Albigensian Crusade; in 1217 de Montfort's crusaders invaded the Valentinois and besieged Crest, which Aymar defended before making peace. He married Philippa de Fay, who brought wide Vivarais lands. His son William predeceased him, and his grandson Aymaret, the future Aymar III, ran the county from 1239.

en:
Aymar III de Poitiers, called Aymaret (1226–1277), was count of Valentinois and Diois, son of William II of Poitiers and grandson of Aymar II. His father's 1226 death sparked a guardianship feud between his mother and Aymar II. He ran the county from 1239 but took the comital title only in 1250.

A land exchange with the lords of Pouzin brought conflict with his grandfather in 1239. He repeatedly fought the bishop of Valence over tolls at Crest, joined Louis IX's Eighth Crusade in 1270, and died in 1277 at Rochemaure, succeeded by his son Aymar IV.

en:
Aymar IV of Poitiers (c. 1250–1329), count of Valentinois and Diois, was the son of Aymar III. A minor in 1277, he inherited the Vivarais castles.

In 1280 he did homage to King Philip III for the county of Die, and in 1326 acknowledged the Vivarais castles as fiefs of King Charles IV. His first wife, Hippolyte of Burgundy, married in 1270, bore his successor Aymar V; his second wife Marguerite of Geneva mothered Anne and Catherine. He died in October 1329.

en:
Aymar VI de Poitiers, called le Gros (1322–1374 or 1376), inherited Valentinois after his father Louis I fell at Auberoche in 1345. As governor of the Dauphiné from 1349 to 1355 he handled the cession of Faucigny to the Count of Savoy.

In 1369 he held Taulignan for four months against Olivier du Guesclin's Bretons. Childless, he made his cousin Louis II his heir in 1371, and in 1372 Pope Gregory XI named him rector of the Comtat Venaissin.

en:
Aymar VI de Poitiers, called the Fat (1322–1374 or 1376), was count of Valentinois and Diois, son of Louis I of Poitiers. He was lieutenant of the last independent dauphin of Viennois, then governed the Dauphiné for France from 1349 to 1355; the new dauphin, Charles, disliked the cession of Faucigny to Savoy and had him fined.

Seeking some independence between the Empire and the French crown, he won from Emperor Charles IV the honorary title of imperial vicar-general in the kingdom of Arles. In 1369 his town of Taulignan withstood a four-month siege.

He married Alix Roger de Beaufort, niece of Clement VI, and in 1372 her brother Gregory XI made him rector of the Comtat Venaissin, hoping the childless count's lands might pass to the Church. Aymar had so willed them in 1366, but in 1371 he named his cousin Louis II instead.

艾马尔六世·德·普瓦捷，绰号“胖子”（1322—1374/1376），是瓦朗蒂努瓦与迪瓦伯爵，路易一世·德·普瓦捷之子。他曾任最后一位独立的维埃纳王太子的代理人，1349至1355年又代表法国治理多菲内；新任王太子查理不满福西尼割让给萨瓦一事，判他缴纳罚金。

他想在帝国与法国王室之间保持一点独立，便从皇帝查理四世那里得到阿尔勒帝国代理总督的荣誉头衔。1369年，他的托利尼昂城顶住长达四个月的围攻。

他娶克雷芒六世的侄女阿莉克斯·罗歇·德·博福尔为妻，1372年其妻之弟格里高利十一世任命他为沃奈桑伯爵领地行政长官，期望这位没有子嗣的伯爵的领地日后归于教会。艾马尔1366年的遗嘱确实这样安排，但1371年他改立堂弟路易二世为继承人。

en:
Aymar V de Poitiers (c. 1271–1339/40), count of Valentinois and Diois, was the eldest son of Aymar IV and Hippolyte of Burgundy. He succeeded in 1329 at about sixty, and a later historian judged him weak and fond of pleasure.

He did not carry on the old fight with the bishop of Valence: he made peace at Avignon in 1332, ending his family's long quarrel with the Church. His last years went on the Clérieu inheritance, which his brother and Humbert II, dauphin of Viennois, also claimed.

Arbitration favored Aymar in 1336, but the dauphin would not accept it, and after a suit reaching the pope, Aymar did liege homage to him at Chabeuil in 1338. His will of 1339 named his son Louis heir; he died soon after at Baix, in 1339 or 1340.

艾马尔五世·德·普瓦捷（约1271—1339/1340）是瓦朗蒂努瓦与迪瓦伯爵，艾马尔四世与勃艮第的伊波利特的长子。1329年继位时他已年近六十，后世一位史家说他性格软弱、耽于享乐。

他没有延续同瓦朗斯主教的旧争，而是于1332年在阿维尼翁议和，结束了家族与教会的长期纷争。晚年的大事是克莱里约的继承权，他的弟弟和维埃纳王太子安贝尔二世也主张权利。

1336年的仲裁对艾马尔有利，但王太子拒不接受；官司打到教宗面前，1338年艾马尔在沙伯伊向王太子行了效忠臣服礼。1339年的遗嘱立其子路易为继承人，不久后他于1339年底或1340年初在拜克斯去世。

en:
Charles de Poitiers (1330/1331–after 18 March 1410), eighth son of Count Aymar V of Valentinois and Sibylle des Baux, was seigneur of Saint-Vallier. In 1358 his nephew Count Aymar VI enfeoffed him with Saint-Vallier.

When his brother Henri, bishop of Troyes, died in 1370, Charles claimed to be the natural heir to Valentinois and long disputed the county with his nephew Louis II. By his wife Simone de Méry he founded the Saint-Vallier line from which Diane de Poitiers later descended; his son Louis succeeded him in 1410.

夏尔·德·普瓦捷（1330/1331—1410年3月18日后）是瓦朗蒂努瓦伯爵艾马尔五世与西比勒·德·博的第八子，圣瓦利耶领主。1358年，其侄伯爵艾马尔六世将圣瓦利耶封赐给他。

1370年其兄特鲁瓦主教亨利去世，夏尔自称瓦朗蒂努瓦的天然继承人，与侄儿路易二世长期争夺伯国。他与妻子西蒙娜·德·梅里开创圣瓦利耶支系，迪安娜·德·普瓦捷即出自该支；1410年其子路易继其位。

en:
Henry of Poitiers was the fighting bishop of the Poitiers-Valentinois house, son of Count Aymar V of Valentinois and Sibylle des Baux. Appointed bishop of Gap in 1349, he was driven out in 1350 after a Poitiers bastard murdered a kinsman of the previous bishop and angry townspeople sacked his palace; a settlement let him return.

Clement VI transferred him to Troyes in 1353, where he proved a brave warrior. Robert Knolles had burned the castle of Aix-en-Othe and was about to seize Troyes when Henry routed him.

In 1358–1359 he defeated and captured Eustace d'Aubrecicourt on the plain of Nogent-sur-Seine, where the captain had been plundering a country Froissart called his ‘chamber’. Henry died at Troyes on 25 August 1370.

普瓦捷的亨利是普瓦捷-瓦朗蒂努瓦家族的善战主教，瓦朗蒂努瓦伯爵艾马尔五世与西比勒·德·博之子。1349年他被任命为加普主教，1350年因普瓦捷家族一名私生子杀死前任主教的亲属，愤怒的市民洗劫了他的宫邸，他被逐出该城；双方达成协议后他得以返回。

1353年克雷芒六世将他调往特鲁瓦，他在那里以勇武著称。罗伯特·诺尔烧毁艾克斯昂奥特城堡、正要夺取特鲁瓦时，被他击溃。

1358—1359年，他在塞纳河畔诺让的平原上击败并俘虏了厄斯塔什·多布雷西古，这名队长一直在当地劫掠，傅华萨称那片地方是他的“房间”。1370年8月25日，亨利卒于特鲁瓦。

en:
Eustache was bishop of Valence from 1107 and, in the charters, bishop and count of Valentinois, probably a kinsman of the rising house of Poitiers-Valentinois. That year he attended Pope Paschal II's synod at Lyon and received the pope at Valence.

Bernard of Clairvaux denounced his conduct in letter 185, accusing him of oppressing the faithful and squandering his church's wealth, and on 30 May 1135 Pope Innocent II deposed him at the council of Pisa. Eustache refused to submit, and Valence lay under interdict for seven years.

A charter of March 1138 styles him Eustachius episcopus et comes Valentinensis. He was driven from Valence by force around Easter 1141, and his death is placed after 1148 or 1154.

zh:
厄斯塔什自1107年起任瓦朗斯主教，特许状称他为瓦朗蒂努瓦主教兼伯爵，学者认为他与兴起中的普瓦捷-瓦朗蒂努瓦家族有亲。同年他出席教皇帕斯夏二世在里昂召开的主教会议，并在瓦朗斯迎候教皇。

明谷的贝尔纳在第185封书信中斥责他品行不端、压迫信徒、挥霍教产；1135年5月30日，教皇英诺森二世在比萨宗教会议上将他废黜。他拒不从命，瓦朗斯城因此被停圣事长达七年。

1138年3月的特许状称他为瓦朗蒂努瓦主教兼伯爵。约1141年复活节时他被武力逐出瓦朗斯，史料把他的卒年定在1148年或1154年之后。

en:
William I of Poitiers (Guillaume de Poitiers) was the son of Count Aymar I. Around 1155 he married Beatrice, daughter of Guigues IV, count of Albon, allying his house with the Dauphins of Vienne, and he is first attested as count of Valentinois in 1158. In 1163 he did homage to the bishop of Die for Suze and Gigors in the Diois.

At Arles on 30 June 1178 he attended the coronation of Frederick Barbarossa, winning imperial privileges including the Rhône toll between Valence and Montélimar. He died after 4 May 1187 and was succeeded by his son Aymar II.

纪尧姆·德·普瓦捷是艾马尔一世伯爵之子。约1155年，他娶阿尔邦伯爵吉格四世之女贝阿特丽切，与维埃纳的太子家族结盟；1158年，他首次以瓦朗蒂努瓦伯爵身份见于记载。1163年，他为迪瓦境内的叙兹和日戈尔城堡向迪城主教行臣服礼。

en:
William II of Poitiers (31 January 1202 – c. 1227) was the only son and heir of Aymar II, count of Valentinois. In 1217 his father made peace with Simon de Montfort during the Albigensian Crusade and promised William to Simon's daughter Amicie, but the marriage never took place.

Around 1224 he married Flotte de Royans, heiress of Saint-Nazaire-en-Royans, who bore his successor Aymar III. He died before his father, leaving a disputed guardianship over the infant heir.

en:
William of Poitiers (1309–1374) was destined for the Church, one of three sons of Count Aymar V of Valentinois and Sibylle des Baux who became bishops. A Cluniac monk, he became prior of La Charité-sur-Loire in 1339 and was elected bishop of Langres in 1345.

He served in King John II's army in 1353. The next year armed captains appeared before Langres to seize the city, and the bishop was accused of conspiring with them to hand it to the English; he obtained absolution.

While still a monk he had fathered several children by different women, and as bishop he legitimized four of them. He died on 6 September 1374.

普瓦捷的纪尧姆（1309—1374）自幼被安排走教会的道路，是瓦朗蒂努瓦伯爵艾马尔五世与西比勒·德·博三个出任主教的儿子之一。他本是克吕尼派修士，1339年任卢瓦尔河畔拉沙里泰修道院长，1345年当选朗格勒主教。

1353年他随法王约翰二世的军队作战。次年佣兵队长带兵兵临朗格勒，意图夺城，主教被控与他们勾结、企图把城献给英格兰人，后来获得赦免。

他当修士期间与多名女子生有子女，成为主教后把其中四人合法化。1374年9月6日去世。

en:
Hippolyte of Burgundy (c.1254–1283), also called Polie, was lady of Saint-Vallier and the daughter of Hugh of Chalon, Count of Burgundy, and Adelaide I. In 1270 she married Aymar IV de Poitiers, Count of Valentinois and Diois.

Her sons included Aymar V, who succeeded as count in 1329, Guillaume and Louis, bishop of Metz. She made her will on 28 September 1283 and died soon after.

en:
Louis I de Poitiers (died 21 October 1345), son of Count Aymar V of Valentinois and Sibylle des Baux, succeeded his father as count of Valentinois in 1339. In the 1345 Gascon campaign he led seven thousand French troops and besieged the English garrison of Auberoche.

On 21 October Henry of Grosmont surprised his camp at supper and routed the French army; Louis died of his wounds. By his wife Marguerite de Vergy he left a son, Aymar VI, and a daughter, Marguerite.

en:
Otto of Poitiers was a son of Count Aymar V of Valentinois and Sibylle des Baux, whose father meant him for the Church. The will of 1339 left him Montmeyran Castle only until he held benefices worth 500 livres a year, and in 1342 he ceded his rights to his brother Louis, their father's successor.

After serving as abbot of Saint-Pierre de Châlons, he was elected bishop of Verdun in 1350 and held the see only about fifteen months. In 1351 contagious disease killed many in Verdun and left him disgusted with the bishopric.

He resigned it to Hugues de Bar for a pension of 1300 florins and returned to the papal court at Avignon. He died around 1352.

普瓦捷的奥托是瓦朗蒂努瓦伯爵艾马尔五世与西比勒·德·博之子，父亲有意让他走教会的道路。1339年的遗嘱把蒙梅朗城堡留给他，条件是等他领到年收入500里弗尔的圣职后就要归还；1342年他把权利让给兄长路易，也就是父亲的继承人。

他曾任沙隆圣伯多禄修道院院长，1350年当选凡尔登主教，在任仅约十五个月。1351年传染病在凡尔登夺去许多人的生命，他因此厌倦了这个主教职位。

他以1300弗罗林年金为条件把职位让给于格·德·巴尔，回到阿维尼翁教廷，约1352年去世。

Sibylle des Baux (died 1360) was the daughter of Bertrand des Baux, Angevin count of Avellino, and married Aymar V de Poitiers, count of Valentinois and Diois, as his second wife; the two were first cousins. Her husband dowered her with castles in the Vivarais and Upie in the Valentinois.

She bore his heir Louis I, the bishops Guillaume of Langres, Henri of Troyes and Otton of Verdun, and other children. Widowed in 1339 or 1340, she died in 1360.

en:
Andrey II Yaroslavich (c. 1222–1264) was a son of Yaroslav II Vsevolodovich of Vladimir. In 1242 he fought beside his brother Alexander Nevsky at the Battle on the Ice. In 1249 he became grand prince of Vladimir under a Mongol jarlig.

Refusing to renew his investiture at Sarai, he challenged the Golden Horde and was routed by Sartak's general Nevryuy in 1252, fleeing to Sweden. Pardoned in 1255, he held Suzdal until his death, and the Shuysky princely house descended from him.

en:
John Tristan (8 April 1250 – 3 August 1270) was a Capetian prince, the fourth son of King Louis IX of France. He was born at Damietta during the Seventh Crusade, and his mother named him Tristan amid the crisis of Louis's capture by the Egyptians.

He married Yolande of Burgundy, countess of Nevers, in 1266, ruling Nevers in her right, and in 1268 received Valois as his appanage. He died of dysentery at Tunis on the Eighth Crusade, childless; Valois reverted to the crown.

en:
Benedetto Belforti was a cleric of Volterra, the son of Ottaviano and nephew of Bishop Ranieri Belforti, and served as pleban of Castelfalfi. When Ranieri died in 1320 he sought the cathedral chapter's leave to administer the diocese during the vacancy, but secured only custody of Berignone castle, the bishops' residence and archive.

In December 1320 the chapter elected his cousin Rainuccio Allegretti, whose election John XXII confirmed in February 1321. Pressed by his father, Benedetto refused to surrender Berignone and the episcopal archives.

In the ensuing factional fighting the Belforti were defeated and exiled, and on 22 July 1321 father and son induced the Berignone garrison to submit to the Commune rather than to the bishop.

贝内德托·贝尔福蒂是沃尔泰拉的教士，奥塔维亚诺之子、主教拉涅里·贝尔福蒂之侄，任卡斯泰尔法尔菲的本堂神父。1320年拉涅里去世后，他争取教区会许可在主教出缺期间管理教区，却只得到贝里尼奥内城堡——主教官邸兼档案存放地——的看管权。

1320年12月教区会选出他的表亲拉伊努乔·阿莱格雷蒂，选举于1321年2月获教皇约翰二十二世批准。在父亲催促下，贝内德托拒绝交出贝里尼奥内城堡和主教档案。

随后的党争中贝尔福蒂家族战败流亡，1321年7月22日父子二人策动贝里尼奥内守军向公社而非主教投降。

Bernardo Belforti was a Guelph nobleman of Volterra, a son of Belforte di Ranieri and brother of Bishop Ranieri and signore Ottaviano Belforti. After Ottaviano died in the Black Death summer of 1348, three Belforti designated by him were entrusted on 4 August with urgent measures after many officials died.

The three were Bernardo, Ottaviano's son Roberto, and their cousin Franco di Dino. The arrangement gave way to the ascendancy of Ottaviano's sons.

en:
Bocchino Belforti (Paolo Belforti, called Bocchino), eldest son of Ottaviano, became co-lord of Volterra in 1348 and soon ruled alone. He had fought beside his father at the 1340 siege of Berignone and shared his excommunication, and the chronicler Matteo Villani called his harsh rule tyranny.

Volterra lay between Guelph Florence and Ghibelline Pisa, and Bocchino balanced the two: he married Bandecca de' Rossi of a leading Florentine family, allied with Pisa's anti-Florentine faction, and in May 1349 repulsed a surprise Pisan night assault.

In 1361 a feud with the sons of his cousin Francesco over Monteveltraio fortress brought Florentine soldiers against him. Judging Florence the stronger, he secretly agreed to sell the signory to Pisa for thirty-two thousand gold florins; the citizens rose and seized him on 5 September, and he was beheaded in the Piazza dei Priori on 10 October 1361.

博基诺·贝尔福蒂本名保罗·贝尔福蒂，是奥塔维亚诺的长子，1348年成为沃尔泰拉的共同领主，很快独掌大权。1340年他曾随父亲围攻贝里尼奥内，并与父亲一同遭到绝罚；编年史家马泰奥·维拉尼称其苛政为暴政。

沃尔泰拉夹在圭尔夫派的佛罗伦萨与吉伯林派的比萨之间，博基诺在两者间周旋：他娶佛罗伦萨名门之女班代卡·德·罗西，与比萨的反佛罗伦萨派结盟，1349年5月击退比萨人的夜间突袭。

1361年，他因蒙特韦尔特拉约要塞与堂兄弟弗朗切斯科的儿子们争斗，招来佛罗伦萨士兵。他自忖不敌，暗中同意以三万二千金弗罗林把领主权卖给比萨；市民起兵于9月5日将他抓获，1361年10月10日他在执政官广场被斩首。

en:
Filippo Belforti (1319–1358), son of Ottaviano Belforti, became bishop of Volterra in 1348, the year his brothers became the city's lords, and held the see until his death. The bishops' old imperial powers had become theoretical, and the diocese was poor. After consecration at Avignon he returned in 1350 to nearly exhausted silver mines and a shortage of priests, and taxed his clergy.

In 1352 he sold the disputed castle of Montecastelli to the commune for sixteen thousand livres. In 1355 he attended Emperor Charles IV's coronation in Rome and won confirmation of the see's jurisdiction and privileges, and he protested when Volterra's envoys swore allegiance to the emperor, a right he claimed for the bishop.

Even so, no real temporal power returned. He held a diocesan synod in 1356, issued synodal constitutions, completed the city hospital, and died at Volterra on 20 August 1358.

菲利波·贝尔福蒂（1319—1358）是奥塔维亚诺·贝尔福蒂之子，1348年出任沃尔泰拉主教，同年其兄弟成为城市领主，他任主教直至去世。主教得自皇帝的统治权此时只剩名义，教区也很穷。他在阿维尼翁晋牧，1350年返回时银矿几近枯竭、神父短缺，只得向神职人员征税。

1352年他把争议中的蒙特卡斯泰利城堡以一万六千里弗尔卖给公社。1355年他赴罗马参加皇帝查理四世加冕礼，使教区管辖权与特权获确认；沃尔泰拉使者向皇帝宣誓效忠时，他提出抗议，主张这项权利属于主教。

即便如此，主教并未重获实际的世俗权力。1356年他召开教区会议、颁布教区会宪，又建成城市医院，1358年8月20日在沃尔泰拉去世。

en:
Ottaviano Belforti (c. 1275–1348), son of Belforte Belforti, was a nobleman of Volterra, a commune long split between his family and the Allegretti faction. He backed his brother Bishop Ranieri against the Allegretti, and when Rainuccio Allegretti became bishop, the Belforti lost the fight and fled the city.

After years in exile he was podestà of Bologna in 1337–1338. Returning in 1340, he won a civil war against Rainuccio and besieged him in a castle; when it fell, Ottaviano and his family were excommunicated. He ruled Volterra as capitano generale until the city gave itself to Walter of Brienne in 1342.

When Walter fled Florence, Ottaviano regained power in August 1343 and reshaped the government so that a Belforti sat on its supreme council by right. In 1348 he secured the bishopric for one son and the signory for two others, dying that July.

奥塔维亚诺·贝尔福蒂（约1275—1348）是沃尔泰拉贵族，贝尔福泰·贝尔福蒂之子；这座公社长期分裂为他的家族与阿莱格雷蒂派两方。他支持担任主教的兄弟拉涅里对抗阿莱格雷蒂派，拉伊努乔·阿莱格雷蒂出任主教后，贝尔福蒂家族败北，逃出城去。

流亡多年后，他于1337至1338年任博洛尼亚的最高行政官。1340年他返回沃尔泰拉，在内战中击败拉伊努乔并将其围困在一座城堡中；城堡陷落后，奥塔维亚诺及其家族遭到绝罚。他以军事统帅身份统治沃尔泰拉，1342年城市归顺布里耶纳的戈蒂埃。

戈蒂埃逃离佛罗伦萨后，奥塔维亚诺于1343年8月重新掌权，改组政府，使贝尔福蒂家族在最高议事机构中拥有当然席位。1348年，他使一个儿子出任主教、另两个儿子获得领主地位，同年7月去世。

en:
Rainuccio degli Allegretti (died 1348), of one of Volterra's leading families, was bishop of Volterra from 1321. Once parish priest at Morba and, from 1315, vicar-general to Bishop Ranieri Belforti, he was elected by the cathedral chapter in December 1320 and confirmed by John XXII in February 1321.

He set out at once to win back church lands that private holders had usurped. The commune answered by exiling his father and condemning other relatives. In 1322 he withdrew to Casole d'Elsa, opened a mint and excommunicated the Volterrans who had sent troops against Berignone castle.

He was back in the city by late 1323 and held a pastoral visitation of his diocese in 1325–1328, among the earliest in Tuscany. In 1340 Ottaviano Belforti took power in Volterra and expelled him and his family, and he spent his last years in the castles he still controlled, dying in 1348.

拉伊努乔·德利·阿莱格雷蒂（卒于1348年）出身沃尔泰拉名门，1321年起任沃尔泰拉主教。他曾任莫尔巴的本堂神父，1315年起担任主教拉涅里·贝尔福蒂的副主教，1320年12月由座堂会议选为继任者，1321年2月获约翰二十二世批准。

上任后他着手收回被私人侵占的教会地产。公社的回应是流放其父、定罪其亲属。1322年他避居卡索莱代尔萨，开设造币厂，并对派兵围攻贝里尼奥内城堡的沃尔泰拉人处以绝罚。

1323年底回城，于1325—1328年巡视教区，是托斯卡纳最早的牧区视察之一。1340年奥塔维亚诺·贝尔福蒂掌握沃尔泰拉的权力，将他及其家人驱逐；此后辗转于仍控制的城堡之间，1348年去世。

en:
Ranieri Belforti (c. 1278–1320) was bishop of Volterra from a Guelph noble family, son of Belforte and brother of Ottaviano, the city's future lord. A cathedral canon, he was made bishop by Pope Boniface VIII on 22 December 1301 and consecrated the following January. He worked to rebuild the diocese's estates, bargained with the commune and Florence, and in 1305 became counselor to Robert of Anjou to settle diocesan debts, leaving a vicar to administer the diocese for three years.

Opposing Emperor Henry VII of Luxembourg, he lost his imperial fiefs. In 1319 factional strife drove the Belforti into exile, and he died in Florence on 26 November 1320.

拉涅里·贝尔福蒂（约1278—1320）出身圭尔夫派贵族家庭，曾任沃尔泰拉主教，是贝尔福泰之子、沃尔泰拉未来统治者奥塔维亚诺之兄。他本是大教堂法政牧师，1301年12月22日被教皇卜尼法斯八世任命为主教，次年1月接受祝圣。他致力于重建教区产业，与公社和佛罗伦萨方面谈判，1305年为解决教区债务出任罗贝尔·德·安茹的顾问，任职期间由一名代理人管理教区三年。

他与皇帝亨利七世对立，被剥夺全部帝国封地。1319年党争把贝尔福蒂家族放逐，1320年11月26日他卒于佛罗伦萨。

en:
Roberto Belforti was a son of Ottaviano Belforti, the first signore of Volterra. A former podestà of Perugia (1345), he was knighted in February 1346 and married Gemma, daughter of Gaddo Cavalcanti.

On 4 August 1348, amid the plague, Roberto, Bernardo and Franco Belforti were entrusted with urgent measures after many officials died. Roberto and his brothers Bocchino and Filippo came to exercise power, and after a long pilgrimage to the Holy Land he led Volterra's homage to Emperor Charles IV at Pisa in 1355.

en:
Bernard de Ventadour (c. 1293–c. 1384) succeeded his father Eble VIII as viscount of Ventadour in 1329 and became count in 1350. From 1339 he served in Philip VI's wars under the Duke of Normandy and the Count of Armagnac, and in 1346 obtained the châtellenies of Croc and Saint-Agnan for a small payment.

That year the countess Joan of Dreux died aged nine months, and he seized Montpensier and Aigueperse; the king recognised him as heir for ten thousand florins. From 1355, under John II, he sat on the royal council at a yearly salary of two thousand livres.

In 1382, with the consent of his son Robert, he sold Montpensier to the king's son John, Duke of Berry.

贝尔纳·德·旺塔杜尔（约1293—约1384）1329年继承父亲埃布勒八世，任旺塔杜尔子爵，1350年升为伯爵。1339年起，他在诺曼底公爵和阿马尼亚克伯爵麾下参加腓力六世的战争，1346年以少量代价取得克罗克和圣阿尼昂城堡区。

同年，年仅九个月的德勒女伯爵让娜夭折，他夺取蒙庞西耶和艾格佩尔斯，并向国王支付一万弗罗林，换得国王承认他为继承人。1355年起他在约翰二世治下入御前会议，年俸两千里弗尔。

1382年，他经儿子罗贝尔同意，把蒙庞西耶卖给国王之子贝里公爵约翰。

en:
Ebles I of Ventadour (c. 1034–1096) was a younger son of Archambaud II, viscount of Comborn. Around 1059–1060 the partition of the Comborn inheritance gave him the eastern lands that became the viscounty of Ventadour, and he was the first of his line to settle there, building the castle of Ventadour and founding several priories.

By his wife Almodie of Montberon he was the father of Ebles II, called the Singer, himself a troubadour. Ebles I died in 1096.

en:
Eble II of Ventadorn (after 1086–1155) was viscount of Ventadour in the Limousin, son of Eble I and Almodis de Montberon. The chronicler Geoffrey of Vigeois praised him as Ebolus cantator, a singer who gave great pleasure with his songs, and although none of his verses survive he is often called the first Provençal troubadour, influencing William IX of Aquitaine and Bernart de Ventadorn.

By his wife Alix, daughter of Guillaume de Montluçon, he fathered Eble III and Guillaume. He died at Montecassino in 1155.

en:
Eble III of Ventadorn (died 1170) was viscount of Ventadour in the Limousin, son of Eble II, the singer, and Agnes de Montluçon. He is remembered as the patron and protector of the troubadour Bernart de Ventadorn.

In 1148 he married Marguerite de Turenne, daughter of Viscount Raymond of Turenne, by whom he had a daughter, Matabrune; the marriage ended before 1150. He then married Alais, daughter of William VI of Montpellier, who bore him his heir Eble IV. He died in 1170.

Eble IV, also called Archambaud I, was viscount of Ventadour in the Limousin. He was the son of Eble III of Ventadour and Adelaide, daughter of William VI of Montpellier.

Eble married Sybille de la Faye, daughter of Raoul de Châtellerault, grand seneschal of Aquitaine. The marriage produced eight children, and their son Eble V succeeded him as viscount. Eble IV died after 1214.

1186年，他续娶蒂雷纳的玛格丽特，即以女游吟诗人和游吟诗人保护者闻名的旺塔杜尔的玛丽亚；其子埃布勒六世后来继承子爵之位。埃布勒五世于1236年后不久去世。

en:
Eble VI of Ventadour (c. 1210–before 1260) was viscount of Ventadour in the Limousin, the son of Eble V and the trobairitz Marie de Ventadour. In May 1221 he and his brother Raymond appear in the charters by which their father retired as a monk to Grandmont, and in November 1245, as lord of Carlux, he was named an executor of Raymond VI of Turenne's testament.

In 1247 he did homage to Louis IX, and in 1249 he joined the king's crusade. His last known charter, dated September 1256, records homage to the abbey of Tulle for his castle of Molceon.

By 1260 his widow Dauphine, daughter of Bernard III de La Tour, was acting for the viscounty with their son Hélie, who succeeded as Eble VII.

埃布勒六世·德·旺塔杜尔（约1210—1260年前）是利穆赞的旺塔杜尔子爵，埃布勒五世与女特罗巴杜尔玛丽·德·旺塔杜尔之子。1221年5月，他与兄长雷蒙出现在父亲退入格朗蒙修道院为僧的特许状中；1245年11月，身为卡吕领主的他被蒂雷纳的雷蒙六世遗嘱指定为执行人。

1247年他向路易九世行臣服礼，1249年参加国王发动的十字军。他存世的最后一份特许状是1256年9月为莫尔塞翁城堡向蒂勒修道院行臣服礼。

到1260年，遗孀德尔菲娜——拉图尔的贝尔纳三世之女——已与儿子埃利共同署理子爵领，埃利后以埃布勒七世之号继位。

en:
Hélie de Ventadour, also numbered Eble VIII, was viscount of Ventadour from about 1297, the son of Eble VII and Blanche de Châteauneuf. In 1290 he married Marguerite de Beaujeu, daughter of Louis de Beaujeu, seigneur of Montferrand, a match that gave his descendants claims to the Montpensier inheritance.

Of their seven children, the eldest, Ebles, married Mathe de Comborn by contract of November 1314 and succeeded as viscount; the second son Bernard became viscount in 1329 and the first count of Ventadour in 1350, seizing Montpensier in 1346; Guy became bishop of Cambrai and then of Vabres, and Blanche married into the Comborn family. Hélie died in 1321.

en:
Andrew (died 1323), son of King Yuri I of Galicia, ruled Galicia-Volhynia jointly with his brother Lev II from 1308, holding Volodymyr while Lev sat in Halych. The brothers fought Grand Duke Gediminas of Lithuania over Berestia while allying with King Władysław I of Poland.

In 1320 he exempted merchants from tolls in Ruthenian lands. He and Lev died in 1323 fighting the Lithuanians or Mongol-Tatars, ending the Romanovichi line; his daughter Euphemia married Gediminas's son Liubartas.

en:
Bolesław Jerzy II, also called Yuri II Boleslav (c. 1305–1340), was the Piast son of Trojden I and Maria of Galicia. In 1323–1325 he succeeded his Rurikid maternal uncles as ruler of Galicia and Volhynia.

Born a Catholic, he adopted Orthodoxy to win over his boyars, granted city rights to Volodymyr and Sanok, and in 1327 allied with the Teutonic Order. In 1331 he married a daughter of Gediminas. Poisoned by boyars in April 1340 without an heir, his death opened the Galicia–Volhynia Wars.

博莱斯瓦夫·耶日二世，又称尤里二世·博莱斯拉夫（约1305—1340），是特洛杰登一世与加利奇的玛丽亚之子，属皮亚斯特家族。1323—1325年，他继留里克家族的舅父之后成为加利奇和沃伦的统治者。

Daniel Romanovich (1201–1266) was the son of Roman the Great. Only four when his father died in 1205, he was exiled and raised at the Hungarian court.

He fought the Mongols at the Kalka River in 1223 and saw Kiev fall in 1240. He reunited Galicia after his victory at Yaroslav in 1245, and in 1246 had to accept Golden Horde overlordship at Sarai. In 1253 he was crowned king of Ruthenia. In 1256 he founded Lviv, named after his son Lev.

en:
Dmytro Dedko (died 1349) was a Galician boyar who emerged as ruler of Ruthenia after Bolesław Jerzy II died in 1340. At first he acknowledged Casimir the Great of Poland as overlord and ruled as starosta, but soon turned against the Polish garrisons and, with Lithuanian and Tatar support, raided Lublin in the winter of 1340–1341 until defeated on the Vistula.

In 1341 he wrote to Toruń to restore trade with Halych. He died in 1349, after which Casimir occupied Halych.

德米特罗·德科（？—1349）是加利西亚的波雅尔显贵，1340年博莱斯瓦夫·耶日二世死后成为罗斯的实际统治者。他起初承认波兰国王卡齐米日大帝的宗主权，以地方长官身份执政，但很快起兵反对波兰驻军，并在立陶宛和鞑靼人支持下于1340—1341年冬攻入卢布林，最终在维斯瓦河战败。

Mstislav Sviatopolkovich was a Rurikid prince, apparently the eldest son of Sviatopolk II of Kiev, born to a mistress. In 1099 his father seized Volodymyr-Volynskyi from David Igorevich and installed Mstislav as its prince.

David returned and besieged the town, and on 12 June 1099 Mstislav was struck by an arrow on the city walls and died. Kyiv Caves Monastery accounts portray his death as vengeance for monks he had killed over Varangian treasure.

Roman Mstislavich, called the Great (1152–1205), son of the Kyivan prince Mstislav Iziaslavich, ruled Novgorod and then inherited Volhynia. He seized Halych in 1188 but was driven out by Béla III of Hungary; in 1199 he took Galicia again, uniting it with Volhynia.

He curbed the Galician boyars, defeated the Cumans and captured Kyiv. In 1205 he invaded Poland and was killed at Zawichost by Leszek the White, leaving his young sons Daniel and Vasylko.

en:
Rostislav Vladimirovich (c. 1038–1066), baptized Mikhail, was a landless Rurikid izgoi prince, son of Vladimir of Novgorod and grandson of Yaroslav the Wise. His father died before Yaroslav, costing Rostislav his claim to Kiev, and he had no appanage for five years after Vladimir's death.

He held Volhynia and Galicia from 1057, and tradition makes his wife Anna a daughter of King Béla I of Hungary. In 1064, aided by Vyshata, he seized Tmutarakan on the Black Sea, was expelled by Svyatoslav of Chernigov, and then returned to subdue the Circassian Kasogi.

Alarmed by his rise, Byzantine Chersonesos had him poisoned on 3 February 1066. He left three sons, Rurik, Volodar and Vasilko.

罗斯季斯拉夫·弗拉基米罗维奇（约1038—1066），教名米哈伊尔，是留里克王朝的无地王公（伊兹戈伊），诺夫哥罗德王公弗拉基米尔·雅罗斯拉维奇之子、智者雅罗斯拉夫之孙。父亲先于雅罗斯拉夫去世，使罗斯季斯拉夫失去了基辅继承权；父亲死后五年间，他没有得到采邑。

1057年起他领有沃伦和加利奇亚，相传妻子安娜是匈牙利国王贝拉一世之女。1064年他在维沙塔帮助下夺取黑海之滨的特穆塔拉干，先被切尔尼戈夫的斯维亚托斯拉夫逐走，随后回城，征服了切尔克斯人的卡索格部。

克森尼索的希腊人忌惮他坐大，派使者于1066年2月3日将他毒杀。他留下留里克、沃洛达尔和瓦西里科三个儿子。

Yuri I (24 April 1252–1308), son of Leo I of Galicia, was prince of Belz from 1264 until he succeeded his father in 1301, reuniting all the lands of Galicia-Volhynia. His long reign was mostly peaceful and prosperous, though Poland retook Lublin and Hungary seized part of Transcarpathia.

He married Euphemia of Kuyavia, sister of Władysław I of Poland, and in 1303 secured from Constantinople the creation of the Orthodox Metropolis of Halych. His sons Andrew and Leo II succeeded jointly.

Johannes Hake, called John of Göttingen (c. 1280–1349), was a German physician and churchman from a Göttingen council family. He taught medicine at Montpellier from 1314 and served as physician to Emperor Louis the Bavarian, King John of Bohemia and Pope Benedict XII; in 1331 he dedicated his treatise on poisons to John.

The same year the pope named him the first directly appointed bishop of Verden, though he stayed at Avignon and ruled through vicars. Transferred to Freising in 1341, he died at Avignon in 1349.

He taught medicine at Montpellier from 1314 and served as physician to Emperor Louis the Bavarian, King John of [GetCountry('BOH').GetName] and Pope Benedict XII; in 1331 he dedicated his treatise on poisons to John.

The same year the pope named him the first directly appointed bishop of [ShowLocationName('verden')], though he stayed at [ShowLocationName('avignon')] and ruled through vicars. Transferred to [ShowLocationName('freising')] in 1341, he died at Avignon in 1349.
zh:
约翰内斯·哈克，人称哥廷根的约翰（约1280—1349），出身哥廷根的市政官家族，是德意志医生兼教士。他自1314年起在蒙彼利埃教授医学，曾任皇帝路德维希四世、波希米亚国王约翰和教皇本笃十二世的御医；1331年，他把论述毒物的专著题献给约翰。

同年，教皇直接任命他为费尔登主教，他是当地首位由教皇直接任命的主教，但他留居阿维尼翁，靠代牧治理教区。1341年他被调往弗赖辛，1349年在阿维尼翁去世。

en:
Conrad of Brunswick-Lüneburg (c. 1246 – 15 September 1300) was the youngest son of Duke Otto the Child and a Welf prince who became bishop of Verden. After his father's death in 1257 he first ruled jointly with his brothers Albert and John.

Provost of Bremen Cathedral from 1259, he became cathedral custodian at Hildesheim in 1266 or 1267. He was postulated to the see of Verden in 1269 and confirmed as bishop in 1285.

He rebuilt the fire-damaged Verden Cathedral and prevailed over his brother in a dispute over the Lüneburg saltworks. From 1277 he guarded Welf interests as guardian of his nephew Otto the Strict. In 1288 Duke Albert II of Saxony granted counties to his bishopric, enlarging it considerably.

康拉德·冯·不伦瑞克-吕讷堡（约1246—1300年9月15日）是韦尔夫家族诸侯、公爵“孩童”奥托的幼子，后来成为费尔登主教。1257年父亲去世后，他先与兄长阿尔布雷希特和约翰共同执政。

他自1259年起任不来梅大教堂主祷司铎，1266年或1267年成为希尔德斯海姆座堂司库；1269年被推举为费尔登主教，1285年获确认。

他重建了毁于火灾的费尔登主教座堂，在吕讷堡盐场的争执中胜过兄长。1277年起，他担任侄子“严厉者”奥托的监护人，维护韦尔夫家族利益；1288年萨克森公爵阿尔布雷希特二世将数处伯国转交其教区，使领地大为扩张。

en:
Jeanne de Montfort (c. 1255–1293), daughter of Philip II of Montfort, Lord of Castres, and Jeanne de Lévis, was twice married into princely houses. In 1268 she wed her cousin Guigues VI of Albon, Count of Forez, and after his death in 1278 ruled Forez as regent for their three-year-old son John I until 1290. Her donations to religious orders and distribution of food to the poor won her esteem as regent.

In 1283 she married Louis of Savoy, Baron of Vaud, becoming baroness of Vaud and bearing ten children, including Louis II. She was buried at Hautecombe Abbey.

让娜·德·蒙福尔（约1255—1293）是卡斯特尔领主菲利普二世·德·蒙福尔与让娜·德·莱维之女，两度嫁入望族。1268年她嫁给表兄、福雷伯爵吉格六世·达尔邦；1278年丈夫去世后，她为年仅三岁的儿子让一世摄政，直到1290年。她向修会捐赠、向贫民分发粮食，因而作为摄政者受到称道。

en:
Fyodor Svyatoslavich (c. 1300 – c. 1356), son of the Bryansk prince Svyatoslav Glebovich, was a Rurikid prince who held Rzhev and ruled Vyazma from about 1339 to 1341. He first served Yury Danilovich of Moscow and twice led Muscovite troops against Tver, later serving Gediminas as envoy to Novgorod in 1326.

After Algirdas's campaign of 1341 he lost Vyazma, entered Moscow service as governor of Volok, and in 1345 married his daughter Eupraxia to Prince Simeon the Proud.

费奥多尔·斯维亚托斯拉维奇（约1300—约1356）是布良斯克王公斯维亚托斯拉夫·格列博维奇之子，属留里克王朝，领有勒热夫，并于约1339至1341年统治维亚济马。他早年在莫斯科王公尤里·达尼洛维奇麾下效力，曾两次率军进攻特维尔，此后转投格迪米纳斯，1326年作为其使节前往诺夫哥罗德。

en:
Basarab I, called the Founder (c. 1270–1352), was the voivode who took Wallachia out of Hungarian overlordship. A charter of 1324 names him a vassal of Charles I of Hungary, but by 1325 another calls him disloyal, and he raided Hungary.

In July 1330 he marched to help Bulgaria's Michael Shishman against Serbia and shared the defeat at Velbazhd. Charles then invaded to take back the border lands Basarab held and refused his offer of tribute and a son sent to court. But the king's army, starving, had to accept an armistice.

On 9–12 November 1330 the Wallachians shot arrows and hurled rocks from the cliffs of a narrow Carpathian pass, nearly annihilating the king's army; Charles barely escaped. Hungarian suzerainty ended. Basarab moved his seat to Câmpulung, and his dynasty ruled Wallachia for two centuries.

巴萨拉布一世（约1270—1352），绰号“开创者”，是使瓦拉几亚摆脱匈牙利宗主权的沃伊沃德。1324年的一份特许状称他是匈牙利国王查理一世的臣属，1325年的另一份特许状已称他背弃王权，他还袭扰匈牙利。

1330年7月，他出兵援助保加利亚的米哈伊尔·希什曼进攻塞尔维亚，在维尔巴日德一同战败。查理随即入侵，要收回巴萨拉布占据的边境领地，拒绝了他提出的岁贡和送一子入宫的条件。国王的大军饥饿难行，被迫休战。

1330年11月9日至12日，瓦拉几亚人在喀尔巴阡山的狭窄隘口从崖上射箭投石，几乎将王军全歼，查理仅以身免。匈牙利的宗主权就此终结。巴萨拉布把驻地迁往肯普隆格，王朝统治瓦拉几亚达两个世纪。

Marghita, or Margareta, was the wife of Basarab I, the voivode whose victory at the Battle of Posada in 1330 made Wallachia independent. Local tradition tells of a Margareta who built a church at Câmpulung and drowned herself after her husband, the legendary Radu Negru, destroyed it.

Her name survives in a Câmpulung diptych commemorating Voivode Io Basarab and his wife. She was the mother of Basarab's successor Nicholas Alexander and of Theodora, wife of Ivan Alexander of Bulgaria.

玛尔吉塔（又作玛格丽塔）是瓦拉几亚督军巴萨拉布一世之妻；巴萨拉布在1330年的波萨达之战中获胜，使瓦拉几亚赢得独立。当地传说称一位玛格丽塔在肯普隆格修建教堂，教堂被其丈夫、传说中的黑公拉杜拆毁后投水自尽。

肯普隆格的一份追思名簿记有督军伊万·巴萨拉布与其妻玛尔吉塔，她的名字因此留存。她是继位者尼古拉·亚历山大之母，女儿狄奥多拉嫁给了保加利亚的伊凡·亚历山大。

Maria Lackfi (died before 1343) was the first wife of Nicholas Alexander, voivode of Wallachia, and probably came from a Bosnian or Balkan Orthodox elite family.

She was the mother of Vladislav I, called Vlaicu, who ruled Wallachia from 1364, of Voislav (died 1366), and of Elisabeth (died 1370), who married Ladislaus of Opole. She was probably buried at Câmpulung.

en:
Nicholas Alexander (c. 1300–1364), son of Basarab I, was the second voivode of Wallachia and is best known for founding the Orthodox Metropolis of Ungro-Wallachia in 1359.

He became his father's co-ruler about 1344 and swore loyalty to Louis I of Hungary to head off an invasion, ruling alone after Basarab's death in 1351 or 1352. At first he resisted Hungarian pressure, but in 1354, threatened by the Golden Horde, he recognised Louis's suzerainty and admitted Catholic missions and Saxon merchants; in 1359 he cast off Hungarian overlordship.

He died on 16 November 1364 and was buried at Câmpulung, his epitaph calling him the great and sole ruler, son of great Basarab. His son Vladislav I succeeded him.

zh:
尼古拉·亚历山大（约1300—1364）是巴萨拉布一世之子，瓦拉几亚第二任沃伊沃德，最为人知的事迹是1359年创立东正教的温格罗-瓦拉几亚都主教区。

约1344年他开始与父亲共同执政，并向匈牙利国王拉约什一世宣誓效忠，以免匈牙利出兵瓦拉几亚；1351或1352年巴萨拉布去世后，他独自执政。他起初抵制匈牙利的压力，但1354年在金帐汗国威胁下承认拉约什的宗主权，允许天主教会传教和萨克森商人通行，1359年又摆脱匈牙利宗主权。

1364年11月16日他去世，葬于肯普隆格，墓志铭称他为伟大的唯一统治者、伟大巴萨拉布之子。儿子弗拉迪斯拉夫一世继位。

en:
Thocomerius, also called Tihomir, was the father of Basarab I, the first independent voivode of Wallachia; a 1332 charter of King Charles I of Hungary names Basarab as his son. Romanian scholars make him a local ruler south of the Carpathians from about 1290 to 1310, possibly Bărbat's successor in Oltenia.

The chronicler Ottokar may describe him as the Wallachian lord who in 1307 imprisoned King Otto of Hungary and then fell ill; Basarab may have succeeded him as a local ruler around 1310.

en:
Vlad III (1428/31–1476/77), called the Impaler and also Dracula after his father Vlad II Dracul, was three times voivode of Wallachia. From 1442 he and Radu were Ottoman hostages. After his father and eldest brother were murdered, he invaded in 1448 with Ottoman support but was expelled, returning in 1456 with Hungarian backing to purge the boyars who killed his kin.

He impaled captives from the Transylvanian Saxons, giving him his epithet. In 1462 he raided south of the Danube, claiming over twenty-three thousand enemy dead. When Mehmed II invaded, Vlad night-attacked his Târgoviște camp to kill the sultan but missed his tent.

The Ottomans withdrew, but many Wallachians joined Radu, the sultan's new prince. Imprisoned in Hungary from 1463 to 1475, he retook Wallachia after his release in November 1476 and fell near Snagov before 10 January 1477. German pamphlets made his cruelty a bestseller.

弗拉德三世（1428/31—1476/77）绰号“穿刺公”，因父亲弗拉德二世·德拉库尔之名也称德古拉，曾三度出任瓦拉几亚大公。1442年起，他与弟弟拉杜一同作为奥斯曼人质。父亲和兄长遇刺后，他于1448年在奥斯曼支持下攻入瓦拉几亚，被逐出；1456年在匈牙利支持下重返，清洗了杀害亲人的波雅尔贵族。

他将特兰西瓦尼亚撒克逊人的俘虏处以穿刺之刑，绰号由此而来。1462年他突袭多瑙河以南，称杀敌两万三千多人。穆罕默德二世来攻，弗拉德夜袭其特尔戈维什泰营地，意在刺杀苏丹，却未能找到苏丹的营帐。

奥斯曼军撤走，但许多瓦拉几亚人投奔苏丹所立的新大公拉杜。弗拉德被囚禁在匈牙利，从1463年关到1475年；获释后于1476年11月夺回瓦拉几亚，1477年1月10日以前在斯纳戈夫附近战死。描写他残暴的德语小册子成为畅销书。

en:
Vladislav I, called Vlaicu Vodă, was voivode of Wallachia from 1364 until his death in 1377, succeeding his father Nicholas Alexander. Around 1365 he became the first Wallachian ruler to mint silver coins. In 1366 he accepted Louis I of Hungary as overlord and received Severin and Făgăraș.

He later fought the Hungarians and occupied Vidin in 1369 before submitting to Louis again. In 1369 he defeated a Turkish army allied with Bulgaria, securing its Danube frontier. He also backed the Vodița and Tismana monasteries.

en:
Otto II von Wolfskeel (died 23 August 1345) was prince-bishop of Würzburg from 1333. Born in Würzburg into a Franconian ministerialis family, the son of a commander of Marienberg Fortress, he faced a cathedral chapter split in 1333 between himself and Emperor Louis IV's secretary Hermann von Lichtenberg.

Otto sought Pope John XXII's backing and fled to Metz, returning after Lichtenberg's death in 1335, when he was elected. He added Kitzingen and Gemünden to the bishopric, ringed Marienberg with a new wall, founded thirteen parishes and created the office of vicar general.

奥托二世·冯·沃尔夫斯克尔（1345年8月23日卒）1333年起任维尔茨堡采邑主教。他生于维尔茨堡的法兰克尼亚武士家族，父亲曾执掌马林贝格要塞；1333年，主教座堂议会在他与皇帝路德维希四世的秘书赫尔曼·冯·利希滕贝格之间分裂。

奥托求得教皇约翰二十二世支持并避走梅斯，1335年利希滕贝格死后才返回并获推举。他为教区取得基青根和格明登，为马林贝格修筑新城墙，还设立十三座新堂区并首创副主教一职。

en:
Adolf I (died 3 October 1270) founded the County and House of Waldeck. A younger son of Count Henry I of Waldeck-Schwalenberg, he was a cleric until his uncle Hermann I left him Waldeck in 1224; after ruling jointly with his brother Volkwin IV, he took the Eder lands in the 1228 partition.

He secured Korbach and backed the anti-king William of Holland against the Hohenstaufen. His son Henry predeceased him, so his grandson Adolf II succeeded.

en:
Adolf II (c. 1258–1302), eldest son of Count Henry III of Waldeck, succeeded his grandfather Adolf I as ruling count in 1270. After he failed to marry Sophia of Hesse, a family treaty of 1275 gave the county to his brother Otto I, and Adolf entered the Church, holding posts in Liège, Trier and Utrecht.

In 1301 he was appointed prince-bishop of Liège, where he reconciled clergy and burghers. He died in December 1302, rumoured poisoned by the moneylenders he had persecuted.

en:
Dietrich von Waldeck (c. 1316–25 June 1355) was a son of Count Henry IV of Waldeck and Adelaide of Cleves who followed a clerical career. He studied canon law at Orléans, held prebends at Cologne from 1336 and Münster from 1338, and became cantor at Münster in 1344.

After resigning in 1346 he was reinstated by Pope Clement VI, and in 1348 was sworn in as cathedral provost of Münster, an office he held until 1353.

Elisabeth of Waldeck (c. 1309 – before 22 June 1385) was a daughter of Count Henry IV of Waldeck and Adelaide of Cleves. By 1331 she was married to Count John of Nassau-Hadamar, who ruled from 1334 until his death early in 1365.

She bore John ten children, including his successors as counts Henry and Emich III, Anna, and Elisabeth, abbess of Essen abbey. She died before 22 June 1385.

en:
Henry III of Waldeck (c. 1225–1267), eldest son of Count Adolf I, co-ruled Waldeck in his father's lifetime. With his father he backed Landgrave Henry I of Hesse against the bishop of Paderborn and Corvey Abbey in their dispute over the north Hessian borderlands.

He married Mechtild of Cuyk-Arnsberg, heiress of Wewelsburg. He died in 1267, three years before his father; his sons Adolf II and Otto I succeeded as counts.

en:
Henry IV (c. 1282–1348) ruled Waldeck from 1305 to 1344. Son of Count Otto I and Sophie of Hesse, he served the Archbishops of Mainz as Amtmann in northern Hesse and the Eichsfeld.

From 1306 his building of Wetterburg Castle caused a long feud with Archbishop Henry II of Cologne until both sides accepted joint ownership in 1325. In 1315 Emperor Louis IV made him protector of Dortmund. He retired in 1344 after arranging an undivided succession and died in 1348.

en:
Otto I (c. 1262–1305), youngest son of Henry III of Waldeck, inherited the county in 1275–1276 by marrying Sophia of Hesse, displacing his elder brother Adolf II. He fought for John I of Brabant in the Limburg Succession War and shared the victory at Worringen in 1288.

The victory brought him lands including Volksmarsen and Canstein Castle. He was captured in a feud near Heiligenstadt in 1305 and strangled.

en:
Otto II (before 1307–1369) was Count of Waldeck from 1344 until his death, having co-ruled with his father Henry IV since 1332. Around 1339 he married Matilda, daughter of Duke Otto III of Brunswick-Lüneburg.

In 1349 Emperor Charles IV enfeoffed him with Waldeck as an imperial county. When his father-in-law died without male heirs, Otto claimed Lüneburg, but the emperor awarded only a heavy indemnity that was never paid. He died in 1369 amid war with Mainz and Hesse.

en:
Albert I, Count of Werdenberg-Heiligenberg (died c. 1365), was the youngest son of Count Hugo II and Euphemia of Ortenburg. He was named by Emperor Louis the Bavarian imperial bailiff around Lake Constance and over Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden.

In 1344 and 1347 advocacies over the future Appenzell, the neighbourhood of Saint Gall Abbey and the Rhine Valley were pledged to him. After feuds with Austria in 1355 and Montfort-Feldkirch in 1360, the latter settled through his son Albert II's coup on Lake Constance, he died around 1365.

en:
Hugo II (died 1305 or 1309), called the One-Eyed, was count of Werdenberg-Heiligenberg and a loyal follower of the Habsburgs. In April 1292 he relieved Winterthur for Duke Albert I and then helped storm Wil after a two-month siege, where Albert knighted him.

He fought at Göllheim in 1298, when Albert took the crown from Adolf of Nassau. Married to Euphemia of Ortenburg, he is last documented in July 1305.

雨果二世（卒于1305或1309年），绰号“独眼”，是韦尔登贝格—海利根贝格伯爵，也是哈布斯堡家族的忠实追随者。1292年4月，他替公爵阿尔布雷希特一世解救温特图尔之围，随后参与围攻维尔，在两个月后将其攻克，并在当地受封骑士。

1298年他参加格尔海姆战役，阿尔布雷希特在此从拿骚的阿道夫手中夺得王冠。他娶奥滕堡的尤菲米娅为妻，1305年7月最后一次见于记载。

en:
Albert I is the first attested count of Wernigerode. He first appears in 1103 near Hildesheim, and on 18 October 1121 witnessed a charter of the bishop of Halberstadt as count of Wernigerode. He also held the advocacy of Ilsenburg Abbey.

On 13 November 1130 King Lothar III made him Vogt, or advocate, of Drübeck Abbey. He is last recorded on 5 December 1141 and left two sons, Bertold and Ludolf.

阿尔布雷希特一世是见于记载的第一代韦尼格罗德伯爵。他于1103年首次出现在希尔德斯海姆附近，1121年10月18日以韦尼格罗德伯爵身份在哈尔伯施塔特主教的特许状上联署，还兼任伊尔森堡修道院的保护官。

en:
Albert II was count of Wernigerode, attested from 1134 to 1165. The son of Count Bertold, who died in 1126, he was a grandson of Albert I, the family's first count.

With his wife Adelaide of Lüchow he had one son, Albert III, who appears as count from 1173 and held the advocacy of Drübeck Abbey. Albert II was still living after 1179.

en:
Albert III ruled as count of Wernigerode from 1173 until after 1214 and, like his predecessors, served as Vogt of Drübeck Abbey. The only son of Count Albert II, he married a daughter of the burgrave of Magdeburg.

His sons divided the family lands: Conrad I held the Ambergau with the Drübeck advocacy and Gebhard I the Derlingau and Nordthüringgau. A daughter, Kunigunde, married Count Bernard II of Wölpe.

en:
Albert V (also numbered IV), born around 1244, was count of Wernigerode from 1268 to 1319, ruling a county held as a fief of the margraves of Brandenburg. He was the son of Conrad II and Oda of Regenstein.

By his first, unnamed wife he had his heir Conrad III and a daughter Oda, who married a count of Mansfeld. His second wife came from the house of Barby, and Albert is last documented after 8 June 1320.

en:
Gebhard I, third son of Count Albert III of Wernigerode, is attested from 1217 as count in the Derlingau and Nordthüringgau, ruling the Wernigerode lands until 1269. In 1268 the county lost its imperial immediacy and became a fief of the margraves of Brandenburg, seeking protection against the dukes of Brunswick.

By his wife Luitgard he had his successor, Conrad II, and a daughter Hedwig, who became a prioress near Helmstedt. Gebhard died after 14 July 1270.

en:
Conrad III, Count of Wernigerode, ruled the Harz county from 1297, initially alongside his father Albert V, until his death in 1339. He married Helen, a daughter of Duke John I of Brunswick-Lüneburg.

In 1338 he granted land at Neustadt whose income was to maintain the chaplain of the chapel on the Harzburg. With his son Conrad IV he bound himself by a service treaty to Bishop Henry III of Hildesheim, in the bishop's long conflict over the Hildesheim see.

韦尼格罗德伯爵康拉德三世自1297年起统治哈茨山区的韦尼格罗德伯国，最初与父亲阿尔布雷希特五世共治，直至1339年去世。他娶不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公爵约翰一世之女海伦为妻。

en:
Conrad IV, Count of Wernigerode (c. 1306 – after 24 June 1373), was the son of Count Conrad III and Helen of Brunswick-Lüneburg and is documented as count from 1325. Around the middle of the century he founded in Wernigerode the Hospital of Saint George, whose chapel was first documented in 1347.

Like his father he served Bishop Henry III of Hildesheim by treaty. His wife Elisabeth of Hohnstein was mother of Henry IV, the last count.

en:
Francis Kübel was a Cistercian monk from Eger who had studied in Paris and served as abbot of Waldsassen Abbey from 1337 to 1349. His abbacy was marked by the decline and indebtedness of the house: in 1341 he sold the town of Redwitz to the city of Eger.

After dissident monks elected Nikolaus Heckel as a rival abbot, a visitor from Morimond annulled the election, but Kübel himself had to resign in 1349. He died about twenty years later.

en:
Sir Edmund Mortimer (1376–1409), a younger son of the Earl of March and great-grandson of Edward III through Lionel of Antwerp, held a crown claim. He supported Henry Bolingbroke despite his elder brother Roger's stronger claim, and after Roger's death in 1398 protected his young nephew's interests.

Fighting for Henry IV against Owain Glyndŵr, he was captured at Bryn Glas in June 1402. When the king forbade his ransom and seized his estates, Mortimer turned rebel, marrying Glyndŵr's daughter Catrin that November and promising to restore Richard II or crown his nephew.

In 1405 he joined the Tripartite Indenture with Glyndŵr and Northumberland. He died in the siege of Harlech Castle in 1409.

埃德蒙·莫蒂默爵士（1376—1409）是马奇伯爵的幼子，通过安特卫普的莱昂内尔为爱德华三世曾孙，本人拥有英格兰王位继承权。尽管兄长罗杰的继承权更强，他仍支持亨利·博林布鲁克；1398年罗杰阵亡后，他维护年幼侄子的利益。

他为亨利四世征讨欧文·格兰道尔，1402年6月在布林格拉斯之战中被俘。国王禁止为他赎身并没收其地产，莫蒂默于是转投叛军，同年11月娶格兰道尔之女卡特琳为妻，许诺复辟理查二世或拥立其侄为王。

1405年他与格兰道尔、诺森伯兰共同订立三分契约。1409年，他在哈莱克城堡围城期间死去。

Goronwy Fychan ap Tudur (died 22 March 1382) was a soldier and administrator, the eldest son of Tudur ap Goronwy and a leading man of the Tudors of Penmynydd on Anglesey. He married Myfanwy Fychan, heroine of a famous Welsh love poem.

Four days after he was made constable of Beaumaris Castle, one of the few Welshmen to hold the post, he and his brother Ednyfed drowned crossing a river in Kent. He was buried at Llanfaes friary.

Goronwy ap Tudur Hen (died 1331) was Lord of Penmynydd in Anglesey and the son of Tudur Hen. He served the English crown, fighting in Edward II's Scottish campaigns, including the defeat at Bannockburn in 1314. He remained loyal until Edward II's murder in 1327 and served as forester of Snowdon.

He died in 1331 and was buried at Llanfaes Friary near Bangor. Through his son Tudur he was a forebear of Owen Tudor and the royal House of Tudor.

en:
Hawys Gadarn, Hawys the Strong (c. 1291–c. 1350), was the heiress of the Welsh marcher lordship of Powys, daughter of Owain ap Gruffudd. When her brother Gruffudd ab Owain died in 1309, she inherited the lordship and within weeks married John Charlton, a Shropshire knight.

Her uncle Gruffudd ap Gruffudd challenged her claim under Welsh custom, and in 1312 besieged the couple in Welshpool castle; the quarrel lasted until his death in 1332. Sixteenth-century antiquaries first recorded her epithet.

en:
Owain Glyndŵr (c. 1354–c. 1416) was a Welsh nobleman descended from the princes of Powys. A dispute with his English neighbour sparked a rising in 1400, and he was acclaimed Prince of Wales. English penal laws widened support for his revolt.

By 1404 he controlled most of Wales, held parliament at Machynlleth and won French aid; his 1406 Pennal Letter planned Welsh universities and laws. After Harlech and Aberystwyth fell in 1409, he refused two pardons and fought on as a guerrilla until vanishing from the record in 1412. Never captured, he died in hiding about 1416, a Welsh folk hero.

en:
Rhys ap Tudur (died 1412) was a Welsh nobleman of the Penmynydd family who twice served as sheriff of Anglesey under Richard II and joined his 1398 Irish expedition. In 1400 he backed his cousin Owain Glyndŵr's revolt against Henry IV.

With his brother Gwilym he infiltrated and seized Conwy Castle in 1401. Outlawed in 1406, Rhys was captured and executed at Chester in 1412. The bard Gruffydd Gryg mourned his death.

en:
Tudur ap Goronwy, called Tudur Fychan (c. 1310–1367), was a Welsh landowner and royal officer on Anglesey, head of the Tudors of Penmynydd. He served Edward III in the French campaign of 1337.

In 1345 he led the men who killed Henry Shalford, the Prince of Wales's representative in North Wales. Both brothers were jailed, but released without charge and held their lands again by 1352. He was buried at Llanfaes friary. His son Maredudd was Owen Tudor's father.

Tudur Hen, also called Tudur ap Goronwy (died 1311), was a Welsh landowner of Penmynydd in Anglesey, son of Goronwy ab Ednyfed. After Edward I's conquest of Wales he held lands granted by the English crown, yet joined a revolt in 1294, submitting only after it failed.

He restored the Franciscan friary at Bangor and was buried there in 1311. Through his son Goronwy he was an ancestor of Owen Tudor and of the House of Tudor.

Frederick I (died 25 July 1365) was Count of Weimar-Orlamünde of the Ascanian line, son of Count Herman IV. In 1322 he married Elisabeth, daughter of Friedrich Klemm and widow of Otto II of Anhalt.

He was the last count to rule the county in his own right; his successor and brother Hermann VI held it as a fief of the Wettin margraves of Meissen. His son was Frederick III the Younger.

en:
Helene of Nuremberg (c. 1307 – after 1374) was a Hohenzollern burgravine, the eldest daughter of Burgrave Frederick IV of Nuremberg and Margaret of Görz-Tyrol, and sister of Burgrave John II. About 1321 she married Count Otto of Weimar-Orlamünde, bearing him a son, Frederick of Orlamünde, and a daughter, also named Helene.

After Otto's death she married, between 1341 and 1346, Count Henry of Schwarzburg-Blankenburg, by whom she had Henry and Sophie. Through both marriages she held the rank of countess.

海伦·冯·纽伦堡（约1307年—1374年后）是霍亨索伦家族的城堡伯爵之女，纽伦堡城堡伯爵腓特烈四世与戈里齐亚-蒂罗尔的玛格丽特的长女，也是城堡伯爵约翰二世的姐姐。约1321年，她嫁给魏玛-奥拉明德伯爵奥托，生有儿子奥拉明德的腓特烈和同名女儿海伦。

en:
Herman II (c. 1184–1247) was the son of Siegfried III and ruled Weimar-Orlamünde jointly with his brother Albert II after 1206. His feud with the Ludovingian landgraves of Thuringia went badly: Landgrave Herman I captured him at Weimar Castle in 1214, and Louis IV later took up arms against the brothers.

He refounded Weimar as a town and established the Cistercian nunnery at Oberweimar. He married Beatrix of Andechs-Merania, heiress of Plassenburg, and died on 27 December 1247.

In his feud with Landgrave Louis III of Thuringia, Weimar Castle was destroyed in 1174. He died on 19 October 1176, and his son Siegfried III succeeded him.

en:
Otto VI (1297–1340) was the last Ascanian count of Weimar-Orlamünde at the Plassenburg, son of Count Otto IV and Adelheid of Kevernburg. He married Kunigunde of Leuchtenberg, but the marriage remained childless; legend nevertheless made her the model of the Hohenzollern White Lady who killed her two children.

In 1337 Otto made an inheritance agreement with Burgrave John of Nuremberg. By his death in 1340, he had borrowed four thousand pounds from John against the Plassenburg, which passed to the Hohenzollern burgraves.
