en:
Siegfried III (c. 1155–1206) ruled as count of Weimar-Orlamünde from 1172. The son of Herman I and grandson of Albert the Bear, he backed the Hohenstaufen emperors and stood with the princes against Henry the Lion until the Welf duke's overthrow in 1180.

He married Sophie, a daughter of King Valdemar I of Denmark, and spent long periods at the Danish court. He died in 1206, leaving two sons, Albert II and Herman II.

zh:
西格弗里德三世（约1155—1206）自1172年起统治魏玛-奥拉明德伯国。他是赫尔曼一世之子、大熊阿尔布雷希特之孙，支持霍亨斯陶芬皇朝的皇帝，与众诸侯共同敌对狮子亨利，直到1180年这位韦尔夫公爵被推翻。

en:
Barnim IV (1325 – 22 August 1365) was a duke of Pomerania-Wolgast, the second son of Duke Wartislaw IV. He was barely a year old when his father died in 1326, and he and his brothers Bogislaw V and Wartislaw V ruled jointly, first under guardianship and from 1341 in person.

In 1348 Emperor Charles IV granted him imperial immediacy. His sons Wartislaw VI and Bogislaw VI took part in the 1368 partition of Pomerania-Wolgast after his death.

en:
Bogislaw V (c. 1318–1374), called the Great, was the eldest son of Duke Wartislaw IV of Pomerania-Wolgast. He and his brothers, including Barnim IV, succeeded in 1326 and ruled jointly from 1341. In 1343 he married Elisabeth, daughter of Casimir III of Poland, allying with Poland against the Teutonic Order.

His daughter Elisabeth became the wife of Emperor Charles IV in 1363. The 1368 partition after Barnim's death gave Bogislaw Farther Pomerania around Stolp, now Słupsk, thereafter Pomerania-Stolp.

Borko of Łobez (died probably 1287) was a Pomeranian magnate of the noble house of Borcke and served as castellan of Kołobrzeg from 1251 to 1255. Before 1271 he came to the lands along the middle Rega with his sons John, James and Nicholas.

Between 1260 and 1270 James commissioned a castle on the Rega at Resko. In 1280 Borko and his sons established Resko under Magdeburg law.

en:
Wartislaw IV (before 1290–1326), son of Bogislaw IV, succeeded as duke of Pomerania-Wolgast in 1309. In 1317 Waldemar of Brandenburg enfeoffed him with Schlawe and Stolp, and after Waldemar's death in 1319 he guarded the heir Henry II and sought to hold Brandenburg, until Emperor Louis IV granted it to his son in 1323.

A 1321 inheritance treaty with his uncle Wizlaw III of Rügen brought the principality to Wolgast in 1325, sparking a war with Mecklenburg that ended in 1328, after Wartislaw's death.

瓦季斯瓦夫五世（约1326年11月1日—1390）是波美拉尼亚-沃尔加斯特公爵瓦季斯瓦夫四世的遗腹子和最年幼的儿子。自1341年起，他与兄长波吉斯瓦夫五世、巴尔宁四世共同执政，但始终处在两位兄长的阴影之下。

1365年巴尔宁死后，继承权之争演变为内战，皇帝查理四世也介入调停；1368年和1372年的分割使瓦季斯瓦夫分得诺伊施泰丁（今什切青内克）领地。他于1390年去世，终身未娶。

en:
Matthias Gallas (1588–1647) was born in Trento and first served Spain and the Catholic League, fighting at Stadtlohn in 1623. In the Mantuan War he won at Villabuona and sacked Mantua in 1630, then became one of Wallenstein's foremost generals and helped remove him in 1634.

He was chief architect of the Imperial victory at Nördlingen and three times served as acting supreme commander. In 1637 he drove the Swedes to the Baltic coast, but in 1644 they cut off his supplies and he lost almost his entire army. He died in Vienna in April 1647 after a failed operation.

马蒂亚斯·加拉斯（1588—1647）生于特伦托，早年先后为西班牙和天主教联盟作战，参加了1623年的施塔特洛恩战役。曼图亚继承战争期间，他于1630年在维拉布奥纳获胜并纵兵洗劫曼图亚，此后成为华伦斯坦麾下最重要的将领之一，参与策划了1634年罢黜华伦斯坦的行动。

他是帝国军在讷德林根取胜的主要谋划者，曾三次代理帝国军队最高统帅。1637年他将瑞典军队逼退至波罗的海沿岸；1644年瑞军切断他的补给，他几乎损失整支军队。1647年4月，他在维也纳因手术失败去世。

en:
Ottavio Piccolomini (1599–1656), of the Sienese Piccolomini, enlisted as a Spanish pikeman and rose to imperial field marshal in the Thirty Years' War. He fought at the White Mountain in 1620 and captained Wallenstein's personal guard from 1627.

During the Mantuan War he was held hostage at Ferrara to 1631. At Lützen in 1632 five horses were shot under him, and he helped overthrow Wallenstein in 1634.

He earned his marshal's baton at Nördlingen, defeated the French at Thionville in 1639 and became Duke of Amalfi, and helped make the Peace of Westphalia in 1648. He died in Vienna in 1656 after falling from a horse.

奥塔维奥·皮科洛米尼（1599—1656）出身锡耶纳的皮科洛米尼家族，少年时加入西班牙军队当长矛兵，后在三十年战争中官至帝国陆军元帅。他参加1620年的白山战役，1627年成为华伦斯坦的亲卫队长。

曼图亚战争期间，他在费拉拉被扣为人质，直至1631年。1632年他在吕岑奋战，座骑五次被击毙，1634年参与推翻华伦斯坦的密谋。

他在讷德林根赢得元帅权杖，1639年在蒂永维尔击败法军，受封阿马尔菲公爵，1648年参与斡旋威斯特伐利亚和约。1656年他在维也纳坠马后去世。

en:
Albrecht von Wallenstein (1583–1634) was a Bohemian nobleman and, after converting to Catholicism in 1606, supreme commander of Emperor Ferdinand II's armies in the Thirty Years' War. A wealthy widow's marriage and confiscated Bohemian rebel lands brought him estates. In 1625 he raised fifty thousand men at his own expense, routed the Protestants at Dessau Bridge in 1626 and became Duke of Friedland.

Dismissed in 1630, he was recalled after Swedish victories and checked Gustavus Adolphus at the Alte Veste in 1632. Secret peace talks in 1633 made the emperor brand him a traitor, and in February 1634 he was murdered at Eger.

阿尔布雷希特·冯·华伦斯坦（1583—1634）是波希米亚贵族，1606年改宗天主教，后成为皇帝斐迪南二世军队的最高统帅，是三十年战争中的核心人物。与富孀结婚以及没收自波希米亚叛军的土地给他带来大批地产。1625年他自筹军费组建五万人的大军，1626年在德绍桥击溃新教军队，受封弗里德兰公爵。

1630年他被解职，在瑞典接连取胜后又被起用，1632年在阿尔特韦斯特阻击古斯塔夫二世。1633年他秘密议和，被皇帝宣布为叛贼，1634年2月在埃格尔遇刺身亡。

en:
Bernard II (c. 1320–1382) was the youngest son of John II, Lord of Werle-Güstrow, and Matilda of Brunswick-Grubenhagen. After their father's death in 1337 his elder brother Nicholas III ruled alone, but from 1339 to 1347 the brothers governed Werle jointly.

By the partition of 1347 Bernard received Werle-Waren, which he ruled until his death. When John IV of Werle-Goldberg died in 1374, Bernard also took over that lordship, joining Werle-Waren and Werle-Goldberg under his hand. He is last attested alive in 1382.

Adelheid of Wittgenstein (died between 1357 and 1362) was the daughter of Count Siegfried III of Wittgenstein and Margareta von Schönecken. In 1359 her brother Count Werner IV and then her father died, ending the male line of the Wittgenstein counts and leaving Adelheid as heiress of the county.

She was married to Salentin von Sayn-Homburg, who took possession of Wittgenstein in 1361 and founded the House of Sayn-Wittgenstein. Her son John IV later ruled the county.

en:
Siegfried II of Wittgenstein (died c. 1360) ruled the County of Wittgenstein from 1312 and was a sought-after mediator between Hesse, the archbishops of Mainz and the Nassau counts. In 1319 he married Margarethe von Schöneck; in 1322 he gained a share in Berleburg and entered the fief service of Mainz.

He enlarged his county with estates. His only son Werner IV died childless before him, so the county passed through his daughter Adelheid, wife of Salentin von Sayn, founding the House of Sayn-Wittgenstein.

en:
Eberhard II the Quarrelsome (1315–1392), eldest son of Ulrich III, was Count of Württemberg from 1344. He ruled jointly with his brother Ulrich IV until he defeated Ulrich's push to partition the county, and Ulrich renounced power in 1362.

Eberhard spent his reign fighting the Swabian Free Imperial Cities; at Döffingen in 1388 his son Ulrich was killed. The wars confirmed the cities' independence, yet he added Böblingen and Calw to his lands. He died in Stuttgart in 1392.

埃伯哈德二世（1315—1392），绰号“争吵者”，是乌尔里希三世的长子，1344年起任符腾堡伯爵。他先与弟弟乌尔里希四世共同执政，乌尔里希要求瓜分伯国未果，于1362年放弃权位。

埃伯哈德在位期间长期与施瓦本的帝国自由城市作战，1388年德芬根一役中他的儿子乌尔里希战死。战争虽确认了城市的独立地位，他仍为符腾堡夺得伯布林根和卡尔夫。1392年，他卒于斯图加特。

en:
Eberhard I (1265–1325), posthumous son of Count Ulrich I, succeeded his half-brother Ulrich II as count of Württemberg in 1279. He resisted Rudolph I's attempt to rebuild the Duchy of Swabia and defeated the Hohenbergs after 1291.

In 1298 Albert I made him vogt of Lower Swabia, and after the 1314 double election he played Louis IV and Frederick the Fair against each other to buy Swabian towns. He made Stuttgart his capital and was buried in its Stiftskirche.

zh:
埃伯哈德一世（1265—1325）出生时父亲乌尔里希一世已去世。1279年他继异母兄乌尔里希二世之后成为符腾堡伯爵。他抵制鲁道夫一世重建施瓦本公国的企图，1291年鲁道夫死后对霍亨贝格家族作战获胜。

1298年，阿尔布雷希特一世任命他为下施瓦本地方长官。1314年双重国王选举后，他在路德维希四世与美男子腓特烈之间周旋，购入施瓦本的城镇。他定斯图加特为都城，死后葬于当地的协同教堂。

en:
Ulrich III (1286/1291–1344) was Count of Württemberg from 1325 until his death. He steered the county through the rivalry between King Frederick the Fair and Emperor Louis IV, binding Württemberg closely to the Empire.

Through pacts and purchases he enlarged his lands, notably acquiring Tübingen in 1342. He married Sophie of Pfirt and died in Alsace in 1344, leaving two sons, Eberhard II and Ulrich IV, who succeeded him.

zh:
乌尔里希三世（1286/1291—1344）自1325年起担任符腾堡伯爵，直至去世。他在国王“美男子”腓特烈与皇帝路德维希四世的争斗中周旋，使符腾堡与帝国紧密结盟。

他通过盟约与购地扩张领地，最著名的是1342年取得蒂宾根。他娶普菲尔茨的索菲为妻，1344年卒于阿尔萨斯，儿子埃伯哈德二世与乌尔里希四世继位。

en:
Ulrich IV (after 1315–1366) was Count of Württemberg in name from 1344, ruling jointly with his elder brother Eberhard II after their father Ulrich III's death. Overshadowed by Eberhard, he pressed from 1352 to divide the county, possibly urged by his wife Katharina of Helfenstein.

Charles IV backed Eberhard and confirmed Württemberg indivisible, and Ulrich renounced the government on 1 May 1362 in return for castles. He died childless at Hohenneuffen on 24 or 26 July 1366.

zh:
乌尔里希四世（1315年后—1366）在父亲乌尔里希三世于1344年去世后，名义上与兄长埃伯哈德二世共同担任符腾堡伯爵。他在兄长面前相形见绌，自1352年起谋求瓜分伯国，这或许是受妻子黑尔芬施泰因的卡塔琳娜怂恿。

查理四世却支持埃伯哈德，确认符腾堡不可分割；乌尔里希遂于1362年5月1日退出执政，换取若干城堡。1366年7月24或26日，他在霍恩诺伊芬城堡去世，没有子嗣。

en:
Zhang Shicheng (1321–1367) was a salt shipper from northern Jiangsu who became the richest warlord of the late Yuan and a chief rival of Zhu Yuanzhang. In 1353 he led a salt workers' revolt and took Gaoyou with his brothers. In 1354 he proclaimed the state of Zhou and styled himself King Cheng.

That year the Yuan chancellor Toqto'a was dismissed while besieging Gaoyou. In 1356 he made Suzhou his capital and ruled the Yangtze delta, producing over half of China's salt. In 1357 he submitted to the Yuan; in 1363 he declared himself King of Wu.

Zhu Yuanzhang crushed Chen Youliang before turning on him. His brother Zhang Shide died in 1366; Zhu took Gaoyou and surrounded Suzhou, which fell on 1 October 1367. He tried to hang himself on the boat to Nanjing but was cut down; the Ming History says he hanged himself there.

zh:
张士诚（1321—1367），苏北盐贩出身，在元末群雄中以富庶著称，是朱元璋的主要对手之一。1353年盐工推举他为首领起兵，他与弟弟们攻下高邮。1354年他建立周国，自称诚王。

同年元朝丞相脱脱在围攻高邮时被罢免。1356年他以苏州为都，统治出产全国一半以上食盐的长江三角洲。1357年他向元朝投降；1363年他自称吴王。

朱元璋先灭陈友谅，再转而对付他。他的弟弟张士德于1366年去世；朱元璋攻取高邮并包围苏州，苏州于1367年10月1日陷落。他在押往南京的船上试图上吊被救下，《明史》则记载他在南京自缢而死。

en:
David Fyodorovich was prince of Yaroslavl from 1299 until his death in 1321, a son of Prince Fyodor Rostislavich the Black. He divided his lands between his sons Vasily, called the Terrible, who took Yaroslavl, and Mikhail, who received Mologa.

The Russian Orthodox Church venerates him among the pious princes: his relics, with those of his father and his brother Konstantin, were discovered under the last ruling prince of Yaroslavl and laid in the Spassky Monastery.

大卫·费奥多罗维奇是雅罗斯拉夫尔王公，1299年至1321年去世时在位，为费奥多尔·罗斯季斯拉维奇（绰号“黑人”）之子。他把封邑分给两个儿子：绰号“威严者”的瓦西里得到雅罗斯拉夫尔，米哈伊尔分得莫洛加。

俄罗斯正教会将他尊为虔诚王公圣徒：他的遗骨与父亲及弟弟康斯坦丁的遗骨在雅罗斯拉夫尔末代当政王公时期被一同发现，安奉于雅罗斯拉夫尔的救世主修道院。

en:
Fyodor Rostislavich, called the Black (1233–1299), was a son of Rostislav Mstislavich and prince of Smolensk and Yaroslavl. Around 1260 he married Anastasia of Yaroslavl, and after her death a khan's daughter at the Golden Horde, returning with a yarlyk to rule Yaroslavl.

He took Smolensk in 1279 and joined Dyuden's 1293 Tatar raid that ravaged northeastern Rus cities. He died a monk at Yaroslavl in 1299 and was canonized in 1467 with his sons David and Konstantin, the first Yaroslavl saints.

费奥多尔·罗斯季斯拉维奇，绰号“黑者”（1233—1299），是罗斯季斯拉夫·姆斯季斯拉维奇之子，曾任斯摩棱斯克与雅罗斯拉夫尔王公。约1260年他娶雅罗斯拉夫尔的阿纳斯塔西娅，妻子去世后在金帐汗国续娶汗王之女，带着汗王敕书返回执政。

1279年他取得斯摩棱斯克，1293年参加图丹统率的鞑靼入侵，东北罗斯诸城遭劫掠。1299年他在雅罗斯拉夫尔出家后去世；1467年与儿子大卫、康斯坦丁一同封圣，是雅罗斯拉夫尔最早的圣徒。

en:
Vasily Davidovich, called the Fearsome Eyes, ruled as Prince of Yaroslavl from 1321 until his death in 1345, succeeding his father. After marrying Yevdokiya, daughter of Ivan Kalita of Moscow, in 1330, he nonetheless rejected Moscow's overlordship and styled himself grand prince of Yaroslavl.

In 1339 he fought off a five-hundred-man detachment Kalita sent to seize him. In 1340 the khan awarded the title to Simeon of Moscow and Vasily had to submit; after his death Yaroslavl fell under Muscovite control.

en:
Yevdokiya Ivanovna (died 1342) was a daughter of Ivan I Kalita, prince of Moscow, and his first wife Helena of Smolensk. In 1330 her father married her to Vasily Davidovich, the prince of Yaroslavl known as the Fearsome Eyes.

The match did not win Kalita a loyal vassal: Vasily continued to challenge Moscow for years. Yevdokiya bore him three sons, Vasily, Gleb and Roman, and died in 1342, three years before her husband.

en:
Al-Afdal al-Abbas (r. 1363–1377) was a Rasulid sultan of Yemen who succeeded his father al-Mujahid Ali. He moved against extortion by port officials: he gave robes of honour to ship captains and abolished new tax levies, and merchants spread word of his justice.

A scholar-ruler, he compiled a multilingual dictionary in Arabic, Persian, Turkic, Greek, Armenian and Mongolian. He died in 1377 and his son al-Ashraf Isma'il succeeded him.

en:
Al-Malik al-Ashraf Umar II (c. 1242–1296) was the third Rasulid sultan of Yemen and a scholar of mathematics, astronomy, agriculture and medicine. The eldest son of al-Muzaffar Yusuf I, he raided Hajjah in 1266 and governed al-Mahjam and Sanaa.

He succeeded his father in 1295 but reigned for only 21 months before his death in 1296, leaving the throne to his younger brother al-Mu'ayyad Da'ud.

en:
Al-Mansur Umar, born Umar ibn Ali ibn Rasul, founded the Rasulid Sultanate of Yemen. In 1229 the last Ayyubid prince entrusted him with the government of Yemen. He ruled at first in the Ayyubids' name, until the Abbasid caliph recognized him as sultan in 1235.

Coins were struck and Friday prayers said for him across Yemen. From Ta'izz he campaigned into the Hijaz, took Mecca and extended his sway to Hadhramaut. In 1249 he was killed by his mamluks at al-Janad and succeeded by his son Yusuf.

Al-Malik al-Mu'ayyad Da'ud ibn Yusuf was the fourth Rasulid sultan of Yemen. A younger son of al-Muzaffar Yusuf I, he came to the throne in 1296 after the death of his brother al-Ashraf Umar II and ruled until 1321.

Two daughters of Umar II were married to sons of Da'ud, binding the two branches of the ruling house. On his death in 1321 he was succeeded by his own son.

en:
Al-Mujahid Ali was the fifth Rasulid sultan of Yemen, ruling from 1321 to 1363 after his father al-Mu'ayyad Dawud. In 1324 the Zaydi imams seized Sanaa, confining Rasulid power to the southern highlands and the Tihamah.

In 1350, while on pilgrimage at Mecca, he was seized by the Egyptian Mamluks and held captive for a year. He reformed taxation, assessing land tax on the average yield of several years, and died in 1363, succeeded by his son al-Afdal Abbas.

en:
Al-Muzaffar Yusuf I (1222–1295) was the second Rasulid sultan of Yemen. Born in Mecca, he succeeded his assassinated father al-Mansur Umar in 1249. During his 46-year reign the sultanate reached its apogee: he secured the Tihamah and southern highlands, defeated the Zaydi imams and briefly occupied Sanaa, and made Taiz a second seat.

He built Red Sea trade, and after the fall of Baghdad in 1258 claimed the caliphal title through his hold on Mecca. His son Umar II succeeded him.

en:
Yesugei (c. 1134–1171), called Baghatur, was a Borjigin chieftain of the Khamag Mongol confederation and father of Genghis Khan. A grandson of Khabul Khan, he ruled the confederation in all but name after Hotula Khan died. He abducted Hö'elün from her Merkit husband; she bore Temüjin, Qasar, Hachiun and Temüge.

In 1171, after betrothing the nine-year-old Temüjin to Börte of the Khongirad, Tatars poisoned him at a wayside feast, and he died at home three days later.

en:
Yesün Temür (1293–1328), the Taiding Emperor, was the son of Gammala and a great-grandson of Kublai Khan. In 1302 he succeeded his father as Prince of Jin. After the 1323 Nanpo coup killed Emperor Yingzong, he was enthroned that October and then executed the conspirators who had elevated him.

He honoured Confucianism publicly while entrusting government to Muslim and steppe officials, and barred Tibetan lamas from China proper. He died at Shangdu in August 1328; his young son Ragibagh was overthrown within months.

He honoured Confucianism publicly while entrusting government to Muslim and steppe officials, and barred Tibetan lamas from China proper. He died at Shangdu in August 1328; his young son Ragibagh was overthrown within months.

en:
Yesünto'a (died 1251) was a son of Mutukan and a grandson of Chagatai Khan. He represented the Chagatai family at Güyük Khan's coronation in 1246.

After Möngke seized the great khanate in 1251, he joined Ögedeid princes in a plot to resist the new khan; the conspiracy was broken by the chief judge Mengeser, and Yesünto'a was seized, tried and executed. His son Baraq ruled the Chagatai ulus from 1266 to 1271, and Baraq's son Duwa later became khan.

en:
Yi Bang-gwa (1357–1419), posthumously King Jeongjong, was the second king of Joseon and the second son of its founder, Yi Seong-gye. A career officer from the last Goryeo campaigns, he took the throne in 1398 after Yi Bang-won's coup in the First Strife of Princes killed the crown prince and Jeong Do-jeon and drove Taejo to abdicate.

Bang-won had promoted him, the eldest surviving son, as successor, and he moved the court back to Gaegyeong the same year. After Bang-won won the Second Strife of Princes in 1400, Jeongjong named him crown prince and abdicated months later. He died in 1419.

en:
Yi Seong-gye (1335–1408), founder of the Joseon dynasty, came from a family that served the Mongol Yuan before defecting to Goryeo in 1356. He helped retake Gaegyeong from the Red Turbans in 1361 and later fought off Mongol remnants and pirates.

His faction rivalled General Choe Yeong's. In 1388 Choe urged invading Liaodong over a Ming demand, and the opposing Yi was made commander. At Wihwa Island he turned back, seized Gaegyeong, dethroned King U and killed Choe, ruling four years through puppet kings.

In 1392 his son Yi Bang-won killed Jeong Mong-ju; Yi forced Gongyang to abdicate and took the throne, ending 475 years of Goryeo. In 1398 Yi Bang-won killed Jeong Dojeon, and Yi abdicated to Hamhung. The tale that he killed his son's envoys gave Korean ‘Hamhung envoy’, though recent studies disagree. Yi Bang-won became Taejong in 1400; Yi died in 1408.

李成桂（1335—1408），朝鲜王朝的开国君主，家族曾效力蒙古元朝，1356年举家转投高丽。1361年他协助从红巾军手中夺回开京，后来又把蒙古残余势力和倭寇逐出半岛。

朝廷分裂为他的一派与将军崔莹一派。1388年因明朝的要求，崔莹主张进攻辽东，反对的李成桂被任命为统帅。他在威化岛回师，攻入开京，废黜禑王，除掉崔莹，此后四年通过傀儡国王掌权。

1392年，他的儿子李芳远杀死郑梦周，李成桂逼恭让王退位，自立为王，结束了高丽475年的统治。1398年李芳远杀死郑道传，李成桂退位，退居咸兴。传说他杀了儿子派来的使者，由此产生“咸兴差使”一词，不过近年研究认为并无此事。李芳远1400年即位为太宗，他1408年去世。

en:
Yi Sun-sin (1545–1598) was the Joseon admiral undefeated in at least twenty-three Imjin War sea battles against Japan. Born in Seoul to an uninfluential family, he passed the military exam in 1576. Jealous superiors had him cashiered and tortured, but he returned, taking naval command at Yeosu in 1591 and building the turtle ship.

When Hideyoshi's invasion reached Seoul in nineteen days, Yi won early victories. At Hansan Island in August 1592 his ‘crane wing’ enclosed the Japanese and destroyed or captured 59 ships. In 1597 intrigue had him arrested and demoted, and his successor lost the fleet at Chilcheollyang.

With only 13 ships, Yi lured the enemy into Myeongnyang Strait and routed over 130 warships without loss. Hit by a stray bullet at Noryang on 16 December 1598, he ordered his death hidden until victory. His diary, the Nanjung Ilgi, joined UNESCO's Memory of the World.

李舜臣（1545—1598），是朝鲜王朝的水军名将，在壬辰倭乱中至少打了二十三场海战，战无不胜。他生于汉城，家族没有势力，1576年才武科及第。嫉妒的上司将他革职拷打，他却重新崛起，1591年在丽水出任水军将领，并督造了龟船。

丰臣秀吉的入侵十九天就打到汉城，李舜臣初战告捷。1592年8月在闲山岛，他以鹤翼阵合围日军，击毁或俘获日船59艘。1597年宫廷谗言使他再次被捕降职，接任者在漆川梁葬送了舰队。

复职时他只剩13艘战船，把日军引入鸣梁海峡，击溃130多艘战舰，己方无一损失。1598年12月16日，他在露梁被流弹击中，临终下令在胜利前隐瞒死讯。他的日记《乱中日记》入选联合国教科文组织的世界记忆项目。

en:
Yoshmut (c. 1234–1271) was an Ilkhanate prince, a son of Hulagu by his Khitan concubine Nogachin Aghachi. From 1253 he accompanied his father and brother Abaqa on the campaign that destroyed the Nizari state, and afterwards governed Arran and Azerbaijan as viceroy.

He was remembered for a fiery temper that made him unpopular with the army, and he died on 18 July 1271; his descendant Ilyas later reigned briefly as Ilkhan Suleiman Khan.

玉疏木忒（约1234—1271）是伊儿汗国宗王，旭烈兀与契丹妾室诺嘎真·阿合赤之子。1253年起，他随父亲和阿八哈参加攻灭尼扎里耶派政权的战事，后来出任阿兰与阿塞拜疆总督。

Dmitry Svyatoslavich (before 1228–1269) was prince of Yuryev-Polsky from 1252 to 1267 and the only son of Grand Prince Svyatoslav Vsevolodovich of Vladimir. The chronicles first mention him in 1238 among the princes who survived Batu's invasion.

In 1250 he accompanied his father to the Golden Horde, and in 1255 joined Alexander Nevsky's campaign against Novgorod. He took monastic vows in 1267 and died in 1269, buried in the Archangel Monastery at Yuryev.

Babusha (died 1330) was a Naiman princess, the daughter of Princess Shouning and wife of Khutughtu Khan Kusala, Emperor Mingzong of Yuan, whom she married before he took the throne; their son Rinchinbal briefly reigned as emperor in 1332. She is recorded as endorsing Hu Sihui's dietary compendium Yinshan Zhengyao.

After her husband's death she accused Empress Budashiri, wife of Jayaatu Khan Tugh Temür, of plotting against him. In retaliation Budashiri had her executed later that year.

八不沙（？—1330）出身乃蛮部，是寿宁公主之女，在元明宗和世㻋（忽都笃汗）即位前嫁给他为妻，二人的儿子懿璘质班曾在1332年短暂登基。据载她曾赞许忽思慧的饮食著作《饮膳正要》。

en:
Bayan Khutugh (1324–1365) was a Khongirad noblewoman, the daughter of Bolod Temür, who became the second empress of Toghon Temür, last Yuan emperor. His first empress, Danashiri, was deposed and put to death in 1335 for her part in her brother's failed rebellion.

Only in 1337 did the emperor marry again, and Bayan Khutugh was enthroned as empress at the age of thirteen. The History of Yuan praises her as frugal, free of jealousy and strict in observing ritual, in pointed contrast to the favoured concubine Lady Ki, who overshadowed her.

She died on 8 September 1365 aged forty-two. Lady Ki looked over the plain, worn clothes left among her things and laughed, asking how an empress could wear such dress.

伯颜忽都（1324—1365）出身弘吉剌部，是孛罗帖木儿之女，元朝末帝妥懽帖睦尔的第二任皇后。皇帝的第一任皇后答纳失里1335年因其兄谋反失败而被废处死。

直到1337年，皇帝才再次成婚，伯颜忽都册立为后，时年十三岁。《元史》称她节俭、不妒忌、谨守礼法，与深受宠爱的奇氏形成鲜明对照，奇氏在宫中盖过了皇后的风头。

1365年9月8日伯颜忽都去世，终年四十二岁；奇氏翻看她遗物中朴素破旧的衣服，笑着问皇后怎能穿这样的衣服。

en:
Bayan of the Merkid (1280–1340) was a Mongol general and the dominant minister of the late Yuan court. He won distinction campaigning against Kaidu and the title Baturu in 1307, and as governor of Henan he helped enthrone Tugh Temür in 1328, becoming left chancellor.

After supporting Toghon Temür's accession in 1333, he had the sons of his rival El Temür executed in 1335 and placed his nephew Toqto'a to watch the emperor. He became grand chancellor in 1339, abolished the Confucian examinations and curtailed Han officials.

He is said to have once urged the emperor to kill Han bearing the five commonest surnames. In 1340 Toqto'a ousted him with the emperor's backing while he was hunting, and Bayan died on his way into exile that same year.

伯颜（1280—1340）是元朝后期权倾一时的蒙古蔑儿乞部将领与大臣。他随军讨伐海都，以军功于1307年获“拔都儿”称号；1328年任河南行省平章政事时全力迎立怀王图帖睦尔（元文宗），升任中书左丞相。

1333年他拥立妥懽帖睦尔（元顺帝）即位，1335年奏诛政敌燕铁木儿诸子，任用侄子脱脱等亲信，并派脱脱监视皇帝。1339年他进大丞相，废除科举、排挤汉官。

相传他还曾建议皇帝杀掉五大姓氏的汉人。1340年，脱脱趁他出猎时奉皇帝之旨将他罢黜，他同年死于流放途中。

Empress Gi (1315–1369), born in Haengju, Goryeo, was sent to the Yuan court as a tribute girl in 1333 and became the favoured consort of Toghon Temür. After bearing the future Ayushiridara in 1339, she was made secondary empress in 1340 and wielded real power through her eunuch.

When King Gongmin of Goryeo killed her brother in 1356, her punitive army was routed at the Yalu. She became primary empress in 1365, fled the Ming advance in 1368, and died at Yingchang in 1369.

奇皇后（1315—1369）出生于高丽幸州（今韩国高阳），1333年作为贡女被送入元朝宫廷，成为妥懽帖睦尔（元顺帝）宠爱的妃子。1339年她生下后来的爱猷识理答腊，1340年被立为第二皇后，通过宦官掌握了朝廷的实权。

Jinzhier was a Merkid Mongol officer of the early Yuan dynasty, from a family that for three generations supplied officers of the imperial kesig guard. His father, a centurion, was killed campaigning with Möngke Khan against the Southern Song in Sichuan, and Jinzhier himself commanded the imperial guard in the Longfu palace of Empress Dowager Kökejin, widow of Crown Prince Zhenjin.

He was the father of Bayan (1280–1340), grand councillor at Toghon Temür's court, and of Majartai (1285–1347), father of the minister-historian Toqto'a. Jinzhier was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng and given the posthumous name Zhongyi.

en:
Khutughtu Khan Kusala (1300–1329), temple name Emperor Mingzong, was the eldest son of Khayishan, Emperor Wuzong. Khayishan had made his brother Ayurbarwada heir on condition that he later pass the succession to Kusala. Instead, Ayurbarwada made his son Shidebala heir, and in 1316 Kusala was relegated to Yunnan; after a failed revolt he fled to the Chagatai Khanate.

After the War of the Two Capitals in 1328 he returned with Chagatayid backing and enthroned himself north of Karakorum in 1329; his brother Tugh Temür abdicated in his favour, and Kusala made Tugh Temür his heir. Four days after a banquet with Tugh Temür he died suddenly, widely believed poisoned by the strongman El Temür.

忽都笃汗和世㻋（1300—1329），庙号明宗，是元武宗海山的长子。海山曾立弟弟爱育黎拔力八达为储君，条件是他日后传位和世㻋。爱育黎拔力八达却改立己子硕德八剌为储君，1316年将和世㻋徙往云南；和世㻋举事失败后西逃察合台汗国。

1328年两都之战后，他借察合台系宗王之力东归，于1329年在和林之北即位，其弟图帖睦尔让位，和世㻋立图帖睦尔为皇储。然而与图帖睦尔宴饮相见仅四天后，他便暴卒，世人多认为是权臣燕帖木儿将他毒死。

en:
Mailaiti (died 3 June 1320) was a noblewoman of the Qarluq people around Almaliq, descended from the Qarluq ruler Arslan Khan; her father was Temuder. In 1316 the Mongol prince Qoshila, later Khutughtu Khan and Emperor Mingzong, fled west after his failed uprising and passed through her lands. She became his wife.

She died on 3 June 1320 after giving birth to her son Toghon Temür, the future last Yuan emperor. In 1336 her son posthumously honoured her as Empress Zhenyu Huïsheng.

en:
Majartai (1285–1347), a Merkid Mongol, was the younger brother of the grand councillor Bayan and the father of Toqto'a. He held civil and military posts after serving Emperor Wuzong and the future Renzong.

In 1327, in Shaanxi, he gave his own wealth to feed the poor in a famine. In 1328 he raised troops for the Shangdu court against Emperor Wenzong; Shangdu lost, and only Bayan's merits saved him from punishment. In 1337, with Bayan dominating the court, he declined a princely title and went to guard the northern frontier.

After Bayan's fall in 1340 he became right chancellor but resigned the same year; in 1341 he was made prince of Zhong while his son Toqto'a took the chancellorship. Slandered in 1347, he was exiled to Gansu and died there.

1327年在陕西适逢饥荒，他捐出私财赈济贫民。1328年他起兵响应上都一方，对抗元文宗；上都兵败，他获罪，因兄长伯颜有功才得免。1337年伯颜专权，他辞谢王爵，出镇北边。

Rinchinbal (1326–1332), temple name Emperor Ningzong, was the second son of Khutughtu Khan Kusala, Emperor Mingzong, and a younger brother of Toghon Temür. After his father's death in 1329 he was made Prince of Fu and kept at court by his uncle Tugh Temür, Emperor Wenzong.

When Wenzong died in 1332 his widow Budashiri, honouring his deathbed wish to restore Kusala's line, had the six-year-old boy enthroned rather than recall the exiled Toghon Temür. Rinchinbal reigned barely seven weeks and died that December.

en:
Toghon Temür (1320–1370), temple name Emperor Huizong, was the last Yuan emperor to rule China and the first of the Northern Yuan. Eldest son of Emperor Mingzong, he was born in exile and, after his father's suspicious death, was banished to Goryeo and then Guangxi. In 1332, on his brother Rinchinbal's death, El Temür delayed his enthronement until 1333. In 1340, helped by Bayan's nephew Toqto'a, he removed Bayan.

The official histories of the Liao, Jin and Song were finished in 1345. Floods and famine then undermined the court, and the Red Turban Rebellion of 1351 broke Yuan power; the emperor dismissed Toqto'a in 1354 and withdrew from governing.

He fled Dadu at midnight in September 1368 as Xu Da's Ming army closed in. Mongolian chronicles preserve a poem in which he mourns the lost capital. He died at Yingchang in 1370 and was succeeded by his son Ayushiridara.

妥懽帖睦尔（1320—1370），庙号惠宗，是元朝在中原的末代皇帝，也是北元的第一位皇帝。他是元明宗的长子，生于父亲流亡期间；父亲死因可疑，随后他先后被流放高丽和广西。1332年弟弟懿璘质班去世，燕帖木儿把他的即位拖延到1333年。1340年，他借伯颜之侄脱脱之力罢黜了权臣伯颜。

1345年辽、金、宋三史修成。此后水患、饥荒动摇了朝廷，1351年红巾军起义打垮了元朝的统治；1354年皇帝罢免脱脱，此后不再亲理朝政。

1368年9月徐达的明军逼近，他在半夜出大都北逃。蒙古编年史保存着一首他哀悼失去都城的诗。他于1370年卒于应昌，由儿子爱猷识理达腊继位。

en:
Toqto'a (1314–1356) was a Merkid aristocrat, nephew of the all-powerful minister Bayan, and the dominant statesman of the late Yuan court. In March 1340 he joined his father Majartai and the emperor Toghon Temür in shutting the palace gates while Bayan was out hunting; Bayan was arrested and exiled.

That November Toqto'a became grand councillor and reversed Bayan's policies: examinations returned and taxes were eased. From 1343 he directed the compilation of the histories of the Liao, Jin and Song, treating all three as legitimate dynasties.

In 1351 he put 150,000 labourers and 20,000 soldiers to work on the Yellow River to reopen the Grand Canal. When the Red Turbans rose he retook Xuzhou in 1352 and ordered it massacred. In 1354 he was close to taking Zhang Shicheng's Gaoyou when court rivals had him dismissed; he was exiled to Yunnan and poisoned in January 1356.

脱脱（1314—1356），蔑儿乞氏，是权臣伯颜的侄子，也是元朝末年的执政重臣。1340年3月，他与父亲马札儿台一同协助元顺帝，趁伯颜出城打猎时关闭宫门，伯颜随即被捕流放。

同年11月，脱脱接任中书右丞相，推翻伯颜的旧政：恢复科举，减轻赋税。1343年起，他主持纂修辽、金、宋三史，把三朝并列为正统。

1351年，他征发民夫15万、军士2万治理黄河，意在重开大运河。红巾军起事后，1352年他收复徐州并下令屠城。1354年他围攻张士诚占据的高邮，眼看就要攻下，却被朝中政敌罢黜；他流放云南，1356年1月被毒杀。

en:
Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Muzni was the last emir of Biskra in the Zab, the eastern Algerian oasis state ruled by his Banu Muzni family since 1279. His father Yusuf and grandfather Mansur had governed the region under loose Hafsid suzerainty.

Ahmad fought repeated wars against the Hafsid sultans. In 1371–1372 Ibn Khaldun stayed at Biskra as the guest of its Muzni lord. Finally the Hafsid sultan Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz II destroyed the emirate in 1402.

艾哈迈德·本·优素福·穆兹尼是扎卜地区比斯克拉的最后一位埃米尔。自1279年起，他的巴努·穆兹尼家族便统治着阿尔及利亚东部这片绿洲；他的父亲优素福和祖父曼苏尔曾在哈夫斯王朝松散的宗主权下管治当地。

艾哈迈德在位期间屡次与哈夫斯苏丹交战。1371至1372年，史学家伊本·赫勒敦曾在比斯克拉居留，受到穆兹尼统治者的款待。最终哈夫斯苏丹阿布·法里斯·阿卜杜勒·阿齐兹二世于1402年攻灭这个埃米尔国。

Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAlī ibn Muznī was an Arab chieftain of the Banu Muzni, a Hilali tribe of the Zab. He backed the Hafsid prince Abū Isḥāq against his brother the caliph and followed him into exile in al-Andalus.

After Abū Isḥāq seized power, al-Faḍl in 1279 became ruler of Biskra and the Zab, founding the Muzni emirate. In 1284 or 1285 he left Biskra and was killed, and his son Manṣūr succeeded him.

Manṣūr ibn al-Faḍl succeeded his murdered father as emir of Biskra and the Zab in 1284 or 1285. He ruled the oasis city with the backing of the Hafsid sultans of Béjaïa against the bedouin tribes of the region.

From 1318 to 1337 the Dhawawida and Riyāḥ Arabs, backed by Tlemcen, waged a long rising against him, and in 1329 the Banu Muzni again swore allegiance to the Hafsids. His son Yūsuf succeeded him.

Henry IV the Faithful (c. 1292–1342), eldest son of Henry III of Głogów, ruled Żagań from 1309, first with his brothers. In 1310 he married Matilda of Brandenburg, but the alliance did not save the family's Greater Poland lands, which Władysław I had largely seized by 1314.

The 1321 partition made him sole duke of Żagań, and in 1329 he had to do homage to John of Luxembourg. He died in 1342 and was succeeded by his son Henry V of Iron.

Henry V the Iron (c. 1319–1369), the only son of Henry IV the Faithful, became duke of Żagań in 1342 and spent his reign recovering lands lost by his father. In 1344 he accepted Bohemian vassalage from King John of Luxembourg in exchange for half of Głogów.

He attended Emperor Charles IV's Roman coronation in 1355 and in 1356 went on pilgrimage to Palestine. In 1363 his daughter Hedwig married King Casimir III of Poland. He went blind in 1367 and died in 1369.

en:
Abu al-Muzaffar al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman, called Abu al-Mawahib (father of gifts), ruled the Kilwa Sultanate from 1310 until his death in 1333. A grandson of al-Hasan ibn Talut, founder of the Yemeni Mahdali dynasty, he was studying in Aden when his father died, so his brother Daud held the throne for two years before yielding it to him.

His reign made Kilwa prosperous: he expanded copper coinage, uniquely minted gold coins, built the Husuni Kubwa palace and reconquered Mafia island from the Shirazi.

Ibn Battuta visited Kilwa during his reign. The traveller recorded his generosity, including a gift of his own robes to a poor man.

阿布·穆扎法尔·哈桑·伊本·苏莱曼，绰号阿布·穆瓦希布（意为“馈赠之父”），1310年至1333年去世时统治基尔瓦苏丹国。他是也门裔马赫达利王朝建立者哈桑·伊本·塔卢特之孙；父亲去世时他正在亚丁求学，其弟达乌德先继位，两年后让位给他。

他在位期间基尔瓦臻于富庶：推广铜币，也是唯一铸造过金币的基尔瓦统治者；修建胡苏尼库布瓦宫，并从设拉子王朝手中收复马菲亚岛。

伊本·白图泰曾在他在位时到访。这位旅行家记下了他的慷慨，包括他将自己的衣袍赠给穷人。

en:
Al-Hasan ibn Talut al-Mahdali was the founder of the Mahdali dynasty of Yemeni Arab sayyids who ruled the Kilwa Sultanate. In 1277 he seized power, overthrowing Kilwa's Shirazi rulers, and reigned for about eighteen years, earning a reputation as an excellent knight.

He began the minting of copper coins at Kilwa, and during his rule his grandson al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman was sent to study in Aden. He died around 1294 and was succeeded by his son Suleiman.

en:
Daud ibn Suleiman, son of Sultan Suleiman ibn al-Hasan of the Mahdali dynasty, was twice sultan of Kilwa. When his father was murdered in 1308, his brother al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman had already been proclaimed ruler but was away on pilgrimage in Mecca; Daud held the throne in his brother's name for two years.

He then stepped down voluntarily on his brother's return. After al-Hasan died in 1333, Daud ascended again, ruling in his own right for about twenty-four years, until around 1357.

Daud ibn Sulaiman was a sultan of Kilwa from the Yemeni Mahdali dynasty, a son of Sultan Sulaiman ibn al-Hasan and brother of al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman, called Abu al-Mawahib, the father of gifts.

When their father died around 1308 while al-Hasan was away on pilgrimage to Mecca, Daud was placed on the Kilwa throne. He ruled for two years, then voluntarily stood down when his brother returned.

Al-Hasan's reign made Kilwa rich: he minted gold coins, began building the palace of Husuni Kubwa and earned the traveller Ibn Battuta's praise for his generosity. When al-Hasan died in 1333, Daud became sultan a second time.

Sulaiman ibn Dawud was a sultan of Kilwa from the Yemeni Mahdali dynasty, a son of Sultan Dawud ibn Sulaiman. On his father's death in 1356 Sulaiman succeeded to the throne but ruled for only twenty days before being deposed by his uncle Hussein al-Mat'un.

After intervening reigns, including that of his brother Talut ibn Dawud from 1362, Sulaiman regained the throne in 1364 and held it for two years and four months, until he was deposed in 1366 by Suleiman ibn Suleiman ibn Hussein.

Suleiman ibn al-Hasan, called al-Mat'un, was sultan of Kilwa from 1294 to 1308, succeeding his father al-Hasan ibn Talut, founder of the Mahdali dynasty. The Kilwa chronicle gives him a reign of fourteen years, ending when conspirators murdered him as he came out of a mosque.

His partisans proclaimed his son al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman sultan, but as the heir was away on pilgrimage in Mecca, the throne was held by his son Daud until al-Hasan returned.

Huijatoo, painted in the Mixtec codices under his calendar name Eleven Water 'Stone Rain' and also recorded as Cosiioeza I, was king of Zaachila from 1361 to 1386. He succeeded his father Ozomatli and ruled jointly with his sister-wife Eight Movement 'Fire Serpent'.

By his other wife Thirteen Serpent 'Plumed Serpent', a princess of Cacaxtli, he had six children, including his successor Six Water 'Cracked Boards'. Huijatoo died at Zaachila in 1386.

Ozomatli, painted in the Mixtec codices under his calendar name Three Alligator 'Smooth Eagle', was king of Zaachila from 1328 until his death in 1361. He was the son of Five Flower 'Xipe', king of Zaachila, and of Four Rabbit 'Quetzal' of Teozacoalco.

His two wives bore him five children, among them Eleven Water 'Stone Rain', called Huijatoo, who succeeded him. His genealogy and reign are recorded in the Codex Zouche-Nuttall.

Zhenjin (1243–1286), son of Kublai Khan and Chabi Khatun, was the Yuan dynasty's first crown prince. The monk Haiyun named him, meaning true gold. Made Prince of Yan in 1261, he was named heir in 1273. Tutored by Han Confucian scholars, he befriended the Tibetan lama Phagpa.

In 1285 a censor proposed Kublai abdicate in his favour, enraging the old emperor; Zhenjin died fearful and ill in January 1286, before ever reigning. His son Temür succeeded Kublai and posthumously honoured him as Emperor Yuzong.

真金（1243—1286）是忽必烈与察必皇后之子，元朝首位皇太子。他由僧人海云取名，意为“真金”。1261年受封燕王，1273年册立为皇太子。他由汉族儒士教导，又与吐蕃喇嘛八思巴交好。

1285年，有御史上奏请忽必烈禅位于真金，忽必烈大怒，真金忧惧成疾，于1286年1月去世，终生未及即位。其子铁穆耳继位后追尊他为裕宗皇帝。

en:
Bolko II of Ziębice (1300–1341), fourth son of Bolko I the Strict, rejected a Church career and received Ziębice as an independent duchy from his brother Bernard in 1322.

He robbed local monasteries and was excommunicated in 1329 for attacking a papal legate's suite. In 1335 he defeated a Bohemian force, but in 1336 did homage to the king of Bohemia. Debt forced him to pledge town after town, until only Ziębice remained, where he died in 1341.

波尔科二世（津比采，1300—1341）是波尔科一世（严厉者）的第四子，起初被安排走教会道路，但1322年从兄长伯纳德手中分得津比采，成为独立公爵。

他劫掠当地修道院，1329年又因袭击教皇使节随从而被开除教籍。1335年他击败一支波希米亚军队，但1336年仍向波希米亚国王称臣。债务迫使他逐座抵押城镇，最后只剩津比采本城，1341年在此去世。

en:
Bonne, also called Guta or Judith (died 1342), was duchess of Ziębice as the wife of Bolko II. She may have been of Savoyard origin and the widow of a Hungarian magnate of the Csák family. By 1321 she had married Bolko.

She bore him his heir Nicholas the Small and a daughter Margareta, later a nun at Strzelin. She died in 1342 and was buried beside her husband in the Cistercian abbey at Henryków.

en:
Adelheid of Ziegenhain (died 1388), a daughter of Count John I, married Count Henry II of Truhendingen in 1333. The marriage was dissolved before 1360, and she entered the collegiate foundation at Kaufungen as a canoness; in 1360 she renounced her parental inheritance in favour of her brother Gottfried VII.

She became provost in 1374 and was elected abbess in 1378. During her term the cloister and south transept of the collegiate church were renewed around 1379. She died in 1388.

阿德尔海德·冯·齐根海恩（?—1388）是齐根海恩伯爵约翰一世之女，1333年嫁给特鲁亨丁根伯爵海因里希二世。这段婚姻在1360年前以离婚告终，阿德尔海德遂进入考夫恩根女子教士团，成为女教士；1360年，她放弃应继承的父母遗产，让与兄长戈特弗里德七世。

1374年她任修院教长，1378年当选院长。在她任内，约1379年修院回廊和教堂南侧耳堂得到翻修。她于1388年去世。

en:
Engelbert II of Ziegenhain (1329–1341) was a younger son of Count John I of Ziegenhain and Nidda and of Lukardis, heiress of the County of Nidda. He was married to Isengard of Eppstein and was intended to inherit Nidda.

But his early death in 1341 at about the age of twelve prevented it. His elder brother Gottfried VII, who had first been destined for the church, eventually succeeded to both Ziegenhain and Nidda when John I died in 1359.

en:
Godfrey VI (1262–1304) became Count of Ziegenhain in 1272, first under his mother Hedwig's regency. In 1274 he was betrothed to Mechthild, daughter of Henry I of Hesse, whom he married in 1282. As a Mainz burgmann at Amöneburg he fought his future father-in-law and was defeated at Fritzlar in 1280.

In 1288 he fought for the Duke of Brabant at the Battle of Worringen against Cologne. He died on 30 November 1304, leaving his son John under Mechthild's regency until 1309.

en:
Gottfried VII (died 1372), eldest son of Count John I, ruled Ziegenhain and Nidda from 1359, having already received Nidda as co-ruler under his father.

Like earlier counts he tacked between Hesse and Mainz: in 1344 he and his father sold the archbishopric a quarter of the castle and town of Nidda, then allied with Hesse months later. He reorganized the county into six administrative offices.

In 1370 he became captain of the League of the Star, a coalition against Hessian expansion, and died in 1372 during the ensuing Star War. His son Gottfried VIII succeeded him.

en:
John I (died 1359) was count of Ziegenhain from 1304. In 1311 he married Lukardis, heiress of Count Engelbert I of Nidda, and in 1333, after her line ended, he merged Nidda with Ziegenhain, reuniting the counties divided in 1258.

Caught between Hesse and the archbishopric of Mainz, he steered a careful balancing course; in 1323 the future Emperor Louis IV enfeoffed him with the castle and town of Nidda as an imperial fief. He secured his lands by building or extending castles, and under him the county reached its greatest prosperity.

en: Zeyd, also called Zeydo, was a Kurdish chieftain and a grandson of Sheikh Hasan Zerraki. In 1335 he captured the castle of Buat near Farqin, the ancient Mayyafariqin, and founded the Kurdish Principality of Zirqan in the hills north of Mardin.

en:
Rudolf Brun (1290s–1360) led Zürich's guild revolution of 1336 and became the city's first independent mayor. Zürich had long been ruled by an aristocratic council, whose mayor was named by the abbess of the Fraumünster. Brun, a councillor from 1332, overthrew it in June 1336 with the craftsmen's help. His constitution balanced old and new: twenty-six councillors, thirteen patricians and thirteen guild masters, with the mayoralty reserved to him for life.

In 1349 he led a massacre of Zürich's Jews. In 1350 he crushed a noble coup, arrested Count Johann II of Rapperswil and destroyed Rapperswil Castle, and the next year Zürich joined the Swiss Confederacy.

His regime curbed the Grossmünster and Fraumünster monasteries, which had dominated the city throughout the Middle Ages, and he ruled the council until his death.

鲁道夫·布伦（1290年代—1360）领导了1336年的苏黎世行会革命，成为这座城市第一位独立市长。苏黎世长期由贵族议会统治，市长由圣母大教堂女院长任命。布伦1332年起任议员，1336年6月借手工业者之力推翻该议会。新宪法兼顾新旧势力：议会二十六席，旧贵族与行会会长各占十三席，市长由他终身担任。

1349年，他主导了对苏黎世犹太人的屠杀。1350年，他镇压贵族政变，逮捕其首领拉珀斯维尔伯爵约翰二世，摧毁拉珀斯维尔城堡；次年苏黎世加入瑞士邦联。

他的统治削弱了大教堂与圣母大教堂两座修道院的影响，它们在整个中世纪一直主宰着这座城市；他掌控市议会直至去世。

en:
Simon II (died 1311 or 1312) was Count of Zweibrücken from December 1308, when he succeeded his father Count Walram I, whose eldest son he was by Agnes of Vaudémont.

He was married to Agnes of Saarbrücken, who bore him two children, Walram and Agnes. He died between autumn 1311 and summer 1312, leaving a small son, Walram II, whose mother acted as regent until about 1327.

西蒙二世（？—1311或1312）于1308年12月继父亲瓦拉姆一世之位成为茨魏布吕肯伯爵，他是瓦拉姆一世与沃代蒙的阿格尼丝的长子。

他娶萨尔布吕肯的阿格尼丝为妻，生有瓦拉姆与阿格尼丝两个孩子。他在1311年秋至1312年夏之间去世，幼子瓦尔拉姆二世继位，由其母摄政至约1327年。

en:
Walram II (c. 1298–1366) was count of Zweibrücken and imperial governor in Lorraine. His father Simon II died young, so his mother was regent until about 1327. In 1333 he settled his inheritance dispute with Zweibrücken-Bitsch in a final partition treaty.

He backed Charles IV against a rival king, and the king made Zweibrücken a town in 1352 and in 1356 named Walram imperial governor in Lorraine. He enlarged the county; his son Eberhard II was its last count.

瓦尔拉姆二世（约1298—1366）是茨魏布吕肯伯爵，兼任皇帝驻洛林的帝国长官。其父西蒙二世早逝，母亲摄政至约1327年。1333年，他以一份最终分割条约解决了与茨魏布吕肯-比奇一系的继承争端。

他支持查理四世对抗对立国王，查理遂于1352年将茨魏布吕肯升格为城市，又于1356年任命他为驻洛林的帝国长官。他扩大了伯国领地；其子埃伯哈德二世是末代茨魏布吕肯伯爵。

en: Najm al-Din, called Bashak, was amir of the Zarzariyya, a Kurdish tribe between Hakkari and Lake Urmia that was most likely a branch of the Hadhbani. Around the mid-fourteenth century al-Umari names him the tribe's ruling amir, holding Mazkard district and the heights above Ushnu.

zh: 纳杰姆丁，人称巴沙克，是泽尔扎里部的埃米尔。该库尔德部族居于哈卡里与乌尔米耶湖之间，很可能是赫兹班尼部的一支。14世纪中叶欧麦里记载，他是该部在位的埃米尔，领有马兹卡德与俯瞰乌什努的高地。
